children.translated_text: An ascetic devoted to austerity and sacred recitation, the best among masters of speech,
<s>Vālmīki</s> asked <s>Nārada</s>, the eminent sage.

children.text: ko nv asmin sāmprataṃ loke guṇavān kaś ca vīryavān
children.translated_text: Who, now in this world, is virtuous, and who is valiant?

children.text: dharmajñaś ca kṛtajñaś ca satyavākyo dṛḍhavrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Who knows <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), is grateful, truthful in speech, and firm in vows?

children.text: cāritreṇa ca ko yuktaḥ sarvabhūteṣu ko hitaḥ
children.translated_text: Who is endowed with good conduct, and who is benevolent toward all beings?

children.text: vidvān kaḥ kaḥ samarthaś ca kaś caikapriyadarśanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Who is learned, who is capable, and who is also always pleasing to behold?
Who is self-possessed, who has conquered anger, who is wise, and who is free from envy?

children.text: kasya bibhyati devāś ca jātaroṣasya saṃyuge ||
children.translated_text: When his wrath is aroused in battle, of whom are even the gods afraid?

children.text: etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me
children.translated_text: I wish to hear this, for I have the greatest curiosity.

children.text: maharṣe tvaṃ samartho 'si jñātum evaṃvidhaṃ naram ||
children.translated_text: O great seer, you are able to know such a man.

children.text: śrutvā caitat trilokajño vālmīker nārado vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing these words of <s>Vālmīki</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, knower of the three worlds,

children.text: śrūyatām iti cāmantrya prahṛṣṭo vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: invited him, saying, 'Listen,' and, delighted, spoke these words.

children.text: bahavo durlabhāś caiva ye tvayā kīrtitā guṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Many and hard to find are the qualities that you have named.

children.text: mune vakṣyāmy ahaṃ buddhvā tair yuktaḥ śrūyatāṃ naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: O sage, I shall speak, having understood; listen to the man endowed with them.
Born from the line of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, known among people by the name <s>Rāma</s>,
he is self-restrained, very powerful, radiant, steadfast, and master of himself.
Intelligent, skilled in polity, eloquent, fortunate, and destroyer of enemies,
he has broad shoulders, mighty arms, a conch-like neck, and a great jaw.
Broad-chested, a great archer, with hidden collarbones, he is a subduer of foes.
His arms reach to his knees; his head is well formed, his forehead fine, and his stride excellent.
He is well proportioned, with limbs evenly formed, a smooth complexion, and great majesty.
Deep-chested and large-eyed, he is possessed of beauty and auspicious marks.

children.text: dharmajñaḥ satyasaṃdhaś ca prajānāṃ ca hite rataḥ
children.translated_text: He knows <s>dharma</s>, is true to his promises, and is devoted to the welfare of his subjects.
Famous, endowed with knowledge, pure, obedient, and composed in mind,
he is the protector of the world of living beings and the guardian of <s>dharma</s>.
He knows the truth of the <s>Veda</s> and the <s>Vedāṅgas</s>, and is firmly grounded in <s>dhanurveda</s> (the science of archery).
He knows the true meaning of all śāstras, is mindful, and is quick-witted.
Beloved by all people, good, with an undepressed spirit, he is discerning.
He is always approached by the good, as the ocean is approached by rivers.
Noble and impartial toward all, he is always pleasant to behold.
Endowed with every virtue, he increases the joy of <s>Kauśalyā</s>.

children.text: samudra iva gāmbhīrye dhairyeṇa himavān iva ||
children.translated_text: In depth he is like the ocean, and in firmness like the <s>Himavān</s>.
In valor he is like <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and in appearance pleasing like the moon.
In anger he is like the fire at the end of time, and in patience equal to the earth.

children.text: dhanadena samas tyāge satye dharma ivāparaḥ
children.translated_text: In generosity he is equal to <s>Dhanada</s>, and in truth he is like another <s>Dharma</s>.
That <s>Rāma</s>, endowed with such qualities and of true prowess,

children.text: jyeṣṭhaṃ śreṣṭhaguṇair yuktaṃ priyaṃ daśarathaḥ sutam
children.translated_text: his eldest son, joined with the highest virtues and dear to him, <s>Daśaratha</s>
the lord of the earth, out of affection, wished to install as heir-apparent.
But seeing the preparations for his consecration, his wife <s>Kaikayī</s>,

children.text: pūrvaṃ dattavarā devī varam enam ayācata
children.translated_text: the queen to whom boons had formerly been granted, asked for this boon:
the banishment of <s>Rāma</s> and the consecration of <s>Bharata</s>.
Bound by the truth of his word and restrained by the bond of <s>dharma</s>,
King <s>Daśaratha</s> sent his beloved son <s>Rāma</s> into exile.

children.text: sa jagāma vanaṃ vīraḥ pratijñām anupālayan
children.translated_text: The hero went to the forest, upholding his pledge,
at his father's command and in order to do what was pleasing to <s>Kaikayī</s>.

children.text: taṃ vrajantaṃ priyo bhrātā lakṣmaṇo 'nujagāma ha
children.translated_text: His dear brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> followed him as he went,
out of affection, endowed with humility, increasing <s>Sumitrā</s>'s joy.
Perfect in every auspicious mark, the best bride among women,

children.text: sītāpy anugatā rāmaṃ śaśinaṃ rohiṇī yathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s> too followed <s>Rāma</s>, as <s>Rohiṇī</s> follows the moon.

children.text: paurair anugato dūraṃ pitrā daśarathena ca
children.translated_text: Followed far by the citizens and by his father <s>Daśaratha</s>,
at <s>Śṛṅgaverapura</s>, on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, he dismissed the charioteer.

children.text: te vanena vanaṃ gatvā nadīs tīrtvā bahūdakāḥ
children.translated_text: Passing from forest to forest and crossing rivers full of water,
they reached <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, according to the instruction of <s>Bharadvāja</s>.

children.text: ramyam āvasathaṃ kṛtvā ramamāṇā vane trayaḥ
children.translated_text: Making a charming dwelling, the three delighted in the forest,
and there they lived happily, resembling gods and gandharvas.
When <s>Rāma</s> had gone to <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, the king, then afflicted by grief for his son,

children.text: rājā daśarathaḥ svargaṃ jagāma vilapan sutam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Daśaratha</s>, lamenting for his son, went to heaven.

children.text: mṛte tu tasmin bharato vasiṣṭhapramukhair dvijaiḥ
children.translated_text: When he had died, <s>Bharata</s>, urged by brahmins headed by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>
to accept the kingdom, did not desire the kingdom, mighty though he was.
The hero went to the forest to win the favor of <s>Rāma</s>'s feet.

children.text: pāduke cāsya rājyāya nyāsaṃ dattvā punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having given <s>Rāma</s>'s sandals again and again as a pledge for the kingship,
the elder brother of <s>Bharata</s> then turned <s>Bharata</s> back.
Without obtaining his wish, he touched <s>Rāma</s>'s feet,
and in <s>Nandigrāma</s> he ruled, longing for <s>Rāma</s>'s return.

children.text: rāmas tu punar ālakṣya nāgarasya janasya ca
children.translated_text: But <s>Rāma</s>, seeing again that the townspeople
were intent on coming there, entered the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest.

children.text: virādhaṃ rākṣasaṃ hatvā śarabhaṅgaṃ dadarśa ha
children.translated_text: After killing the rākṣasa <s>Virādha</s>, he saw <s>Śarabhaṅga</s>,

children.text: sutīkṣṇaṃ cāpy agastyaṃ ca agastyabhrātaraṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: and also <s>Sutīkṣṇa</s>, <s>Agastya</s>, and likewise <s>Agastya</s>'s brother.
At <s>Agastya</s>'s word, greatly pleased, he took up <s>Indra</s>'s bow,
as well as a sword and two quivers with inexhaustible arrows.

children.text: vasatas tasya rāmasya vane vanacaraiḥ saha
children.translated_text: While that <s>Rāma</s> was dwelling in the forest with forest-dwellers,
all the seers came to him for the destruction of asuras and rākṣasas.
While he was living there, the rākṣasī <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>, dwelling in <s>Janasthāna</s>,
a shape-shifting demoness, was disfigured.
Then, because of <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>'s words, all the rākṣasas who had set out,

children.text: kharaṃ triśirasaṃ caiva dūṣaṇaṃ caiva rākṣasam ||
children.translated_text: including the rākṣasa <s>Khara</s>, <s>Triśiras</s>, and <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>,

children.text: nijaghāna raṇe rāmas teṣāṃ caiva padānugān
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> killed in battle, along with their followers.
Fourteen thousand <s>rākṣasas</s> were slain.
Then, hearing of the slaughter of his kinsmen, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, overcome with anger,
chose as his helper a <s>rākṣasa</s> named <s>Mārīca</s>.
Though that <s>Rāvaṇa</s> was repeatedly restrained by <s>Mārīca</s>,

children.text: na virodho balavatā kṣamo rāvaṇa tena te ||
children.translated_text: saying, "Opposition to one who is strong is not fitting for you, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,"

children.text: anādṛtya tu tad vākyaṃ rāvaṇaḥ kālacoditaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, driven on by Time, disregarded that speech,
and then went with <s>Mārīca</s> to that hermitage.
By that illusionist the two princes were drawn far away,

children.text: jahāra bhāryāṃ rāmasya gṛdhraṃ hatvā jaṭāyuṣam ||
children.translated_text: and, after killing the vulture <s>Jaṭāyuṣ</s>, he carried off <s>Rāma</s>'s wife.

children.text: gṛdhraṃ ca nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā hṛtāṃ śrutvā ca maithilīm
children.translated_text: Seeing the vulture slain and hearing that <s>Maithilī</s> had been carried away,
<s>Rāghava</s>, scorched by grief, lamented with his senses distraught.

children.text: tatas tenaiva śokena gṛdhraṃ dagdhvā jaṭāyuṣam
children.translated_text: Then, in that very grief, after cremating the vulture <s>Jaṭāyuṣ</s>,

children.text: mārgamāṇo vane sītāṃ rākṣasaṃ saṃdadarśa ha ||
children.translated_text: while searching for <s>Sītā</s> in the forest, he saw a <s>rākṣasa</s>.
He was named <s>Kabandha</s>, deformed in shape and terrible to behold.

children.text: taṃ nihatya mahābāhur dadāha svargataś ca saḥ ||
children.translated_text: The mighty-armed one killed him and burned him, and he went to heaven.
And he told him of <s>Śabarī</s>, the righteous ascetic woman,
saying, "Go to that female renunciant, skilled in <s>dharma</s> (righteous conduct), O <s>Rāghava</s>."
The great-splendored destroyer of foes went to <s>Śabarī</s>.
Properly honored by <s>Śabarī</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>,
met on the bank of <s>Pampā</s> with the monkey <s>Hanumat</s>.
And through <s>Hanumat</s>'s words he met with <s>Sugrīva</s>.

children.text: sugrīvāya ca tat sarvaṃ śaṃsad rāmo mahābalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Mighty <s>Rāma</s> told <s>Sugrīva</s> all of that.
Then, in return, the king of the monkeys told of his enmity,
and all was reported to <s>Rāma</s> by him, afflicted and acting from affection.

children.text: vālinaś ca balaṃ tatra kathayāmāsa vānaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: There the monkey also described the strength of <s>Vālin</s>.

children.text: pratijñātaṃ ca rāmeṇa tadā vālivadhaṃ prati
children.translated_text: At that time <s>Rāma</s> promised to kill <s>Vālin</s>,

children.text: sugrīvaḥ śaṅkitaś cāsīn nityaṃ vīryeṇa rāghave ||
children.translated_text: but <s>Sugrīva</s> remained doubtful about <s>Rāghava</s>'s valor.

children.text: rāghavaḥ pratyayārthaṃ tu dundubheḥ kāyam uttamam
children.translated_text: So <s>Rāghava</s>, to inspire confidence, took the huge body of <s>Dundubhi</s>
and with the big toe of his foot hurled it a full ten yojanas.

children.text: bibheda ca punaḥ sālān saptaikena maheṣuṇā
children.translated_text: And again, with a single great arrow, he pierced seven śāla trees,

children.text: giriṃ rasātalaṃ caiva janayan pratyayaṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: a mountain, and the netherworld too, thereby producing confidence.

children.text: tataḥ prītamanās tena viśvastaḥ sa mahākapiḥ
children.translated_text: Then that great monkey, pleased in mind and trusting in him,

children.text: kiṣkindhāṃ rāmasahito jagāma ca guhāṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: went together with <s>Rāma</s> to <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, to the cave at that time.
Then <s>Sugrīva</s>, the best of monkeys, golden-brown in color, roared.
At that great sound the lord of monkeys came out.
Then, at <s>Sugrīva</s>'s word, after killing <s>Vālin</s> in battle,

children.text: sugrīvam eva tad rājye rāghavaḥ pratyapādayat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> installed <s>Sugrīva</s> himself in that kingdom.

children.text: sa ca sarvān samānīya vānarān vānararṣabhaḥ
children.translated_text: And that bull among monkeys gathered all the monkeys together,
and, wishing to see the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, sent them out to the directions.

children.text: tato gṛdhrasya vacanāt sampāter hanumān balī
children.translated_text: Then, on the word of <s>Sampāti</s>, the powerful <s>Hanumān</s>
leapt across the salt ocean, which stretched a hundred yojanas.
There, reaching <s>Laṅkā</s>, the city protected by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
he saw <s>Sītā</s>, absorbed in thought, in the aśoka grove.
After presenting the token and reporting the news,
and after reassuring <s>Vaidehī</s>, he smashed the gateway.

children.text: pañca senāgragān hatvā sapta mantrisutān api
children.translated_text: Having killed five army commanders and also seven sons of ministers,

children.text: śūram akṣaṃ ca niṣpiṣya grahaṇaṃ samupāgamat ||
children.translated_text: and having crushed the brave <s>Akṣa</s>, he submitted to capture.
Knowing himself to be released from the weapon by the boon of the grandsire,

children.text: marṣayan rākṣasān vīro yantriṇas tān yadṛcchayā ||
children.translated_text: the hero tolerated those <s>rākṣasas</s> who bound him, as if by chance.

children.text: tato dagdhvā purīṃ laṅkām ṛte sītāṃ ca maithilīm
children.translated_text: Then, after burning the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>, but sparing <s>Sītā Maithilī</s>,

children.text: rāmāya priyam ākhyātuṃ punar āyān mahākapiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the great monkey returned to tell <s>Rāma</s> the welcome news.
Approaching the great-souled <s>Rāma</s> and circumambulating him,
the immeasurable one reported truly, "<s>Sītā</s> has been seen."
Then, together with <s>Sugrīva</s>, he went to the shore of the great ocean,
and with arrows like the sun he agitated the sea.
The ocean, lord of rivers, then revealed himself,
and by the ocean's instruction he had <s>Nala</s> build a bridge.

children.text: tena gatvā purīṃ laṅkāṃ hatvā rāvaṇam āhave
children.translated_text: Crossing by that bridge to the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>, and killing <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle,
he consecrated <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>, in <s>Laṅkā</s>.
By that great deed, the three worlds, with all that moves and does not move,
together with the hosts of gods and seers, were pleased with the great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>.
Likewise, honored by all the gods, who were supremely satisfied,

children.text: kṛtakṛtyas tadā rāmo vijvaraḥ pramumoda ha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, having accomplished his purpose and freed from feverish distress, rejoiced then.

children.text: devatābhyo varān prāpya samutthāpya ca vānarān
children.translated_text: Having received boons from the deities and raised up the monkeys,

children.text: puṣpakaṃ tat samāruhya nandigrāmaṃ yayau tadā ||
children.translated_text: he mounted the <s>Puṣpaka</s> and then went to <s>Nandigrāma</s>.
At <s>Nandigrāma</s>, the sinless one, together with his brothers, put aside his matted hair,

children.text: rāmaḥ sītām anuprāpya rājyaṃ punar avāptavān ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Rāma</s>, reunited with <s>Sītā</s>, regained the kingdom.
The people, delighted and joyful, were satisfied, prosperous, and firmly devoted to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order).
They were free from affliction and disease, and devoid of the fear of famine.

children.text: na putramaraṇaṃ kecid drakṣyanti puruṣāḥ kvacit
children.translated_text: Men anywhere would never see the death of a son,
and women would always be unwidowed and devoted to their husbands.

children.text: na vātajaṃ bhayaṃ kiṃcin nāpsu majjanti jantavaḥ
children.translated_text: There would be no fear at all born of wind, nor would creatures sink in water,

children.text: na cāgrijaṃ bhayaṃ kiṃcid yathā kṛtayuge tathā ||
children.translated_text: and there would be no fear at all born of fire, just as in the <s>Kṛtayuga</s>.
Having sacrificed with hundreds of horse-sacrifices and likewise with many gifts of gold,
and having duly given ten billion cows to the learned,
<s>Rāghava</s> will establish royal lineages a hundredfold,

children.text: cāturvarṇyaṃ ca loke 'smin sve sve dharme niyokṣyati ||
children.translated_text: and in this world he will set the four social orders each in its own <s>dharma</s> (duty).
For ten thousand years and for ten hundreds of years besides,
<s>Rāma</s>, after ruling the kingdom, will go to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: idaṃ pavitraṃ pāpaghnaṃ puṇyaṃ vedaiś ca saṃmitam
children.translated_text: This is purifying, destroying sin, meritorious, and equal in authority to the Vedas.
Whoever recites the deeds of <s>Rāma</s> is released from all sins.

children.text: etad ākhyānam āyuṣyaṃ paṭhan rāmāyaṇaṃ naraḥ
children.translated_text: A man who recites this life-giving narrative, the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>,
together with his sons, grandsons, and attendants, is honored in heaven after death.

children.text: paṭhan dvijo vāgṛṣabhatvam īyāt syāt kṣatriyo bhūmipatitvam īyāt
children.translated_text: A twice-born man who recites it may attain excellence as a speaker; a kṣatriya may attain lordship of the earth.

children.text: vaṇigjanaḥ paṇyaphalatvam īyāj janaś ca śūdro 'pi mahattvam īyāt ||
children.translated_text: A merchant may obtain the fruit of merchandise, and even a śūdra may attain greatness.

children.text: nāradasya tu tad vākyaṃ śrutvā vākyaviśāradaḥ
children.translated_text: But when the eloquent one had heard those words of <s>Nārada</s>,
the righteous great sage, together with his disciples, honored him.

children.text: yathāvat pūjitas tena devarṣir nāradas tadā
children.translated_text: Then the divine seer <s>Nārada</s>, duly honored by him,
took leave, received permission, and went up into the sky.

children.text: sa muhūrtaṃ gate tasmin devalokaṃ munis tadā
children.translated_text: When he had gone for a while toward the world of the gods, the sage then
went to the bank of the <s>Tamasā</s>, not far from the <s>Jāhnavī</s>.

children.text: sa tu tīraṃ samāsādya tamasāyā mahāmuniḥ
children.translated_text: Having reached the bank of the <s>Tamasā</s>, the great sage

children.text: śiṣyam āha sthitaṃ pārśve dṛṣṭvā tīrtham akardamam ||
children.translated_text: saw that bathing-place free from mud and spoke to the disciple standing at his side.
"Look, <s>Bharadvāja</s>: this bathing-place is free from mud,
beautiful, with clear water, like the mind of a good person.

children.text: nyasyatāṃ kalaśas tāta dīyatāṃ valkalaṃ mama
children.translated_text: Set down the water-pot, dear child; give me my bark garment.
I shall bathe in this very excellent bathing-place of the <s>Tamasā</s>."
Thus addressed by the high-souled <s>Vālmīki</s>,

children.text: prāyacchata munes tasya valkalaṃ niyato guroḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bharadvāja</s>, restrained and obedient to his teacher, gave that sage the bark garment.
Taking the bark garment from his disciple's hand, the sage with controlled senses

children.text: vicacāra ha paśyaṃs tat sarvato vipulaṃ vanam ||
children.translated_text: walked about, looking at the broad forest on every side.
Near that place he saw a pair moving together, inseparable,
a lovely-voiced pair of <s>krauñca</s> birds.

children.text: tasmāt tu mithunād ekaṃ pumāṃsaṃ pāpaniścayaḥ
children.translated_text: But from that pair, one male bird
was killed, while the sage watched, by a niṣāda, a sinner whose mind was set on evil and whose nature was hostility.
Seeing him, his limbs covered with blood, writhing on the ground,

children.text: bhāryā tu nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā rurāva karuṇāṃ giram ||
children.translated_text: his mate cried out with a piteous voice when she saw him slain.

children.text: tathā tu taṃ dvijaṃ dṛṣṭvā niṣādena nipātitam
children.translated_text: Then, seeing that bird struck down by the niṣāda,
compassion arose in that righteous seer.
Then, because he was pierced by pity, the twice-born sage thought, "This is <s>adharma</s> (wrongdoing),"

children.text: niśāmya rudatīṃ krauñcīm idaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: and, hearing the female <s>krauñca</s> lamenting, he spoke these words:

children.text: mā niṣāda pratiṣṭhāṃ tvam agamaḥ śāśvatīṃ samāḥ
children.translated_text: "Niṣāda, may you find no lasting standing for endless years,
because you killed one bird from the <s>krauñca</s> pair while it was overcome with desire."

children.text: tasyaivaṃ bruvataś cintā babhūva hṛdi vīkṣataḥ
children.translated_text: As he spoke in this way, a thought arose in his heart while he looked on:

children.text: śokārtenāsya śakuneḥ kim idaṃ vyāhṛtaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: "What is this that I have uttered, grieving for this bird afflicted by sorrow?"

children.text: cintayan sa mahāprājñaś cakāra matimān matim
children.translated_text: Reflecting, that very wise and thoughtful sage formed an understanding,

children.text: śiṣyaṃ caivābravīd vākyam idaṃ sa munipuṃgavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and that foremost of sages spoke these words to his disciple:
"Bound in metrical feet, with an equal number of syllables, and joined to the rhythm of a stringed instrument,

children.text: śokārtasya pravṛtto me śloko bhavatu nānyathā ||
children.translated_text: this utterance that arose from my grief shall be a <s>śloka</s> (verse), and nothing else."

children.text: śiṣyas tu tasya bruvato muner vākyam anuttamam
children.translated_text: As the sage was speaking, his disciple received
that unsurpassed statement with delight, and his teacher was pleased with him.

children.text: so 'bhiṣekaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā tīrthe tasmin yathāvidhi
children.translated_text: Then, after performing his ablution at that bathing-place according to rule,

children.text: tam eva cintayann artham upāvartata vai muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: the sage returned, still contemplating that very meaning.

children.text: bharadvājas tataḥ śiṣyo vinītaḥ śrutavān guroḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Bharadvāja</s>, his disciplined and learned disciple,
took up the filled water-pot and followed behind his teacher.
Entering the hermitage together with his disciple, that knower of <s>dharma</s> (right order),

children.text: upaviṣṭaḥ kathāś cānyāś cakāra dhyānam āsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: sat down, turned to meditation, and spoke of other matters as well.
Then <s>Brahmā</s>, self-luminous maker of the worlds, arrived,
four-faced and greatly radiant, to see that foremost of sages.

children.text: vālmīkir atha taṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasotthāya vāgyataḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vālmīki</s>, seeing him, suddenly rose, restrained in speech,
and stood with joined palms, composed, and filled with supreme wonder.
He honored the god with water for the feet, arghya, a seat, and reverential greetings,
bowing to him according to rule and asking after his unfailing well-being.
Then the blessed one sat down on the supremely honored seat,
and after that he assigned a seat to the great seer <s>Vālmīki</s>.
When the very grandsire of the worlds had sat down there in person,

children.text: tad gatenaiva manasā vālmīkir dhyānam āsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vālmīki</s>, with his mind still fixed on that event, entered meditation.
"A cruel act was done by that sinful one, whose mind was intent on enmity,

children.text: yas tādṛśaṃ cāruravaṃ krauñcaṃ hanyād akāraṇāt ||
children.translated_text: who would kill such a beautifully calling <s>krauñca</s> without cause."

children.text: śocann eva muhuḥ krauñcīm upaślokam imaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Still grieving for the female <s>krauñca</s>, again and again
he sang that very verse, inwardly absorbed and given over to sorrow.

children.text: tam uvāca tato brahmā prahasan munipuṃgavam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s>, smiling, said to the foremost of sages:

children.text: śloka eva tvayā baddho nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: "It is indeed a <s>śloka</s> that you have composed; no reflection need be made about this.

children.text: macchandād eva te brahman pravṛtteyaṃ sarasvatī
children.translated_text: By my will alone this speech of yours has arisen, O brahman.

children.text: rāmasya caritaṃ kṛtsnaṃ kuru tvam ṛṣisattama ||
children.translated_text: Compose the entire life of <s>Rāma</s>, best of seers:
the story of righteous, virtuous, wise <s>Rāma</s> in the world,

children.text: vṛttaṃ kathaya dhīrasya yathā te nāradāc chrutam ||
children.translated_text: the steadfast one's history, just as you heard it from <s>Nārada</s>.

children.text: rahasyaṃ ca prakāśaṃ ca yad vṛttaṃ tasya dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: What happened to that wise one, in secret and in public,

children.text: rāmasya saha saumitre rākṣasānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and everything concerning <s>Rāma</s> together with <s>Saumitri</s>, and concerning the rākṣasas,

children.text: vaidehyāś caiva yad vṛttaṃ prakāśaṃ yadi vā rahaḥ
children.translated_text: and what happened to <s>Vaidehī</s>, whether in public or in secret,

children.text: tac cāpy aviditaṃ sarvaṃ viditaṃ te bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: all that too, though unknown, will become known to you.

children.text: na te vāg anṛtā kāvye kācid atra bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: No word of yours in this poem shall be false here."
Compose the blessed, delightful story of <s>Rāma</s>, bound in <s>śloka</s> (verse).

children.text: yāvat sthāsyanti girayaḥ saritaś ca mahītale
children.translated_text: As long as mountains and rivers shall remain on the surface of the earth,
so long will the story of the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s> circulate among the worlds.

children.text: yāvad rāmasya ca kathā tvatkṛtā pracariṣyati
children.translated_text: And as long as the story of <s>Rāma</s>, made by you, shall circulate,

children.text: tāvad ūrdhvam adhaś ca tvaṃ mallokeṣu nivatsyasi ||
children.translated_text: so long will you dwell above and below in my worlds.
Having spoken thus, the blessed <s>Brahmā</s> disappeared right there.

children.text: tataḥ saśiṣyo vālmīkir munir vismayam āyayau ||
children.translated_text: Then the sage <s>Vālmīki</s>, together with his disciples, was filled with wonder.

children.text: tasya śiṣyās tataḥ sarve jaguḥ ślokam imaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Thereafter all his disciples sang this verse again,

children.text: muhur muhuḥ prīyamāṇāḥ prāhuś ca bhṛśavismitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, delighted again and again, they spoke, greatly amazed:

children.text: samākṣaraiś caturbhir yaḥ pādair gīto maharṣiṇā
children.translated_text: That grief, sung by the great seer in four equal-syllabled feet,
through repeated utterance has again become <s>śloka</s> (metrical verse).

children.text: tasya buddhir iyaṃ jātā vālmīker bhāvitātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Then this thought arose in the mind of <s>Vālmīki</s>, whose self was disciplined:

children.text: kṛtsnaṃ rāmāyaṇaṃ kāvyam īdṛśaiḥ karavāṇy aham ||
children.translated_text: I shall make the whole <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s> as a <s>kāvya</s> (poem) in verses like these.

children.text: udāravṛttārthapadair manoramais tadāsya rāmasya cakāra kīrtimān
children.translated_text: Then that renowned sage, with noble meter, meaning, and words, delightful in form, made

children.text: samākṣaraiḥ ślokaśatair yaśasvino yaśaskaraṃ kāvyam udāradhīr muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: a fame-bringing <s>kāvya</s> for the glorious <s>Rāma</s>, in hundreds of equal-syllabled verses.

children.text: śrutvā vas tu samagraṃ tad dharmātmā dharmasaṃhitam
children.translated_text: But after hearing all that complete account, that righteous sage, full of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),

children.text: vyaktam anveṣate bhūyo yad vṛttaṃ tasya dhīmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: clearly investigated further what had happened to that wise one.
Sipping water, composed, and standing with folded hands, the sage
on darbha grass whose tips pointed east, investigated by <s>dharma</s> the course of events:
the great birth of <s>Rāma</s>, his valor, his kindness to all,
his being beloved by the world, his forbearance, gentleness, and truthfulness;
the many varied stories during his journey with <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,

children.text: jānakyāś ca vivāhaṃ ca dhanuṣaś ca vibhedanam ||
children.translated_text: the marriage of <s>Jānakī</s>, and the breaking of the bow;
the dispute between <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāma</s>, and likewise the virtues of <s>Daśaratha</s>'s son;
the consecration of <s>Rāma</s>, and the wicked disposition of <s>Kaikeyī</s>;
the obstruction of the consecration and the banishment of <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: rājñaḥ śokaṃ vilāpaṃ ca paralokasya cāśrayam ||
children.translated_text: the king's grief and lamentation, and his resort to the next world;
the sorrow of the subjects and the dismissal of the subjects,
the conversation with the lord of the <s>Niṣādas</s>, and the charioteer's return;
the crossing of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the meeting with <s>Bharadvāja</s>,
and, with <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s permission, the sight of <s>Citrakūṭa</s>;
the establishing of the dwelling by proper rites, and <s>Bharata</s>'s arrival,

children.text: prasādanaṃ ca rāmasya pituś ca salilakriyām ||
children.translated_text: the appeasing of <s>Rāma</s>, and the water-offering rite for his father;
the consecration of the sandals as foremost, and the dwelling at <s>Nandigrāma</s>;
the journey to the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest and the meeting with <s>Sutīkṣṇa</s>;
the affair of <s>Anasūyā</s> and the gift of cosmetic ointment;
the conversation with <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>, and likewise her disfigurement;
the killing of <s>Khara</s> and <s>Triśiras</s>, and the rising up of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>;

children.text: mārīcasya vadhaṃ caiva vaidehyā haraṇaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: the killing of <s>Mārīca</s>, and also the abduction of <s>Vaidehī</s>;
<s>Rāghava</s>'s lamentation and the slaying of the king of vultures;
the sight of <s>Kabandha</s>, and then also the sight of <s>Pampā</s>;
the meeting with <s>Śabarī</s>, and likewise the meeting with <s>Hanūmat</s>;
and the lamentation of the great-souled <s>Rāghava</s> at <s>Pampā</s>;
the journey to <s>Ṛṣyamūka</s> and the meeting with <s>Sugrīva</s>;
the production of trust, the friendship, and the conflict between <s>Vālin</s> and <s>Sugrīva</s>;
the crushing of <s>Vālin</s>, and the establishment of <s>Sugrīva</s>;
the time of <s>Tārā</s>'s lamentation and the residence through the rainy nights;
the anger of the lion-like <s>Rāghava</s> and the gathering of the forces;

children.text: diśaḥ prasthāpanaṃ caiva pṛthivyāś ca nivedanam ||
children.translated_text: the sending forth to the quarters, and the report concerning the earth;
the giving of the signet-ring and the sight of the cave of the bear;
the fasting unto death, and also the meeting with <s>Sampāti</s>;
the ascent of the mountain and the crossing of the ocean;
the entry into <s>Laṅkā</s> at night, and his reflection though he was alone;
the going to the drinking-ground and the sight of the inner apartments;
the going to the <s>Aśoka</s> grove, and also the sight of <s>Sītā</s>;
the giving of the token of recognition, and also the speech of <s>Sītā</s>;
the threatening by the rākṣasī women, and the sight of <s>Trijaṭā</s>'s dream;
the giving of the jewel by <s>Sītā</s>, and likewise the breaking of the trees;
the routing of the rākṣasī women, and the slaying of the servants;
the capture of the son of the Wind, and the burning of <s>Laṅkā</s> with roaring;
then the return-leap, and likewise the taking of the honey;
the reassuring of <s>Rāghava</s>, and likewise the handing over of the jewel;

children.text: saṃgamaṃ ca samudrasya nalasetoś ca bandhanam ||
children.translated_text: the meeting with the ocean, and the construction of <s>Nala</s>'s bridge;
the crossing of the ocean, and the siege of <s>Laṅkā</s> at night;
the association with <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, and the explanation of the means of killing;
the death of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> and the slaying of <s>Meghanāda</s>;

children.text: rāvaṇasya vināśaṃ ca sītāvāptim areḥ pure ||
children.translated_text: the destruction of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, and the recovery of <s>Sītā</s> in the enemy's city;
the consecration of <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, and the sight of the <s>Puṣpaka</s>;
the journey to <s>Ayodhyā</s>, and the meeting with <s>Bharata</s>;
the fortunate rise of <s>Rāma</s>'s consecration, and the dismissal of the whole army;
the delighting of his own kingdom, and also the dismissal of <s>Vaidehī</s>;

children.text: anāgataṃ ca yat kiṃcid rāmasya vasudhātale
children.translated_text: and whatever future event of <s>Rāma</s> on the surface of the earth there was,

children.text: tac cakārottare kāvye vālmīkir bhagavān ṛṣiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the blessed seer <s>Vālmīki</s> made that in the later <s>kāvya</s>.
The blessed seer <s>Vālmīki</s>, possessed of himself, composed
the entire life-story of <s>Rāma</s> after he had gained the kingdom, in words of varied beauty.

children.text: kṛtvā tu tan mahāprājñaḥ sabhaviṣyaṃ sahottaram
children.translated_text: Having composed that, including what was future and including the sequel, that very wise one...

children.text: cintayāmāsa ko nv etat prayuñjīyād iti prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The lord reflected, "Who indeed might put this to use?"
While that great seer, whose self was disciplined, was thinking,
then <s>Kuśa</s> and <s>Lava</s>, dressed as ascetics, took hold of his feet.
But <s>Kuśa</s> and <s>Lava</s>, knowers of <s>dharma</s> (right order), glorious princes,
brothers endowed with fine voices, he saw dwelling in the hermitage.

children.text: sa tu medhāvinau dṛṣṭvā vedeṣu pariniṣṭhitau
children.translated_text: Seeing the two intelligent boys, fully grounded in the Vedas,
the lord made them learn it for the sake of strengthening the Veda.

children.text: kāvyaṃ rāmāyaṇaṃ kṛtsnaṃ sītāyāś caritaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: The whole poem called the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>, the great story of <s>Sītā</s>,
he, firm in his vows, composed also as "The Slaying of the Descendant of <s>Pulastya</s>."

children.text: pāṭhye geye ca madhuraṃ pramāṇais tribhir anvitam
children.translated_text: Sweet in recitation and in song, furnished with the three measures,
joined with the seven musical modes and accompanied by string and rhythm,
with the comic, erotic, pathetic, furious, heroic, and terrible moods,
and with the disgusting and other <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic flavors), they sang this poem.
Those two, knowers of the principles of <s>gāndharva</s> music and skilled in pitch and modulation,
brothers endowed with fine voices, were like gandharvas in embodied form.
Endowed with beauty and auspicious marks, speaking in sweet voices,
they were like two images drawn from an image, as if taken also from <s>Rāma</s>'s own body.

children.text: tau rājaputrau kārtsnyena dharmyam ākhyānam uttamam
children.translated_text: Those two princes, having mastered in full the excellent righteous narrative,

children.text: vāco vidheyaṃ tat sarvaṃ kṛtvā kāvyam aninditau ||
children.translated_text: and having made the entire poem obedient to their speech, were beyond reproach.

children.text: ṛṣīṇāṃ ca dvijātīnāṃ sādhūnāṃ ca samāgame
children.translated_text: At gatherings of seers, twice-born men, and good people,
the two, knowing the truth, sang it attentively just as they had been instructed.
They were great-souled, greatly fortunate, and marked by every auspicious sign.
Once, near a gathering of seers whose minds were disciplined,
as they sat close by, the two sang this poem.
Hearing it, all the sages, their eyes clouded with tears,

children.text: sādhu sādhv iti tāv ūcatuḥ paraṃ vismayam āgatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: said to the two, "Well done, well done," overcome with supreme wonder.
All those sages, their minds pleased and devoted to <s>dharma</s>,
praised <s>Kuśa</s> and <s>Lava</s>, who were worthy of praise as they sang.

children.text: aho gītasya mādhuryaṃ ślokānāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: "Ah, the sweetness of the song, and especially of the verses!

children.text: ciranirvṛttam apy etat pratyakṣam iva darśitam ||
children.translated_text: Though this happened long ago, it has been shown as if before our eyes."

children.text: praviśya tāv ubhau suṣṭhu tadā bhāvam agāyatām
children.translated_text: Both of them entered fully into its feeling then and sang it well,
together, sweetly, with passion, complete in richness of voice.
Thus praised by the great seers, praiseworthy for their austerity,
the two sang even more deeply moved, exceedingly sweetly.

children.text: prītaḥ kaścin munis tābhyāṃ saṃsthitaḥ kalaśaṃ dadau
children.translated_text: One sage, pleased with them, standing there, gave them a water-pot;

children.text: prasanno valkalaṃ kaścid dadau tābhyāṃ mahāyaśāḥ ||
children.translated_text: another, a very famous one, delighted, gave them bark garments.
"This narrative proclaimed by the sage is a wonder,

children.text: paraṃ kavīnām ādhāraṃ samāptaṃ ca yathākramam ||
children.translated_text: the supreme support of poets, and completed in proper sequence."
As the two singers were praised everywhere, once, there,
<s>Bharata</s>'s elder brother saw them in the streets and on the royal roads.
Then, bringing the two brothers, <s>Kuśa</s> and <s>Lava</s>, to his own palace,
<s>Rāma</s>, destroyer of enemies, honored them, for they were worthy of honor.

children.text: āsīnaḥ kāñcane divye sa ca siṃhāsane prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: The lord, scorcher of foes, sat on a divine golden throne,
with ministers and his brothers seated close around him.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tu rūpasampannau tāv ubhau vīṇinau tataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, seeing those two handsome boys carrying vīṇās,

children.text: uvāca lakṣmaṇaṃ rāmaḥ śatrughnaṃ bharataṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> spoke to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and also to <s>Śatrughna</s> and <s>Bharata</s>:
"Let this narrative of these two, who shine like gods, be heard,
as they sing properly, in sweet voices, with varied words and meanings.

children.text: imau munī pārthivalakṣmaṇānvitau kuśīlavau caiva mahātapasvinau
children.translated_text: These two sages, endowed with royal marks, <s>Kuśa</s> and <s>Lava</s>, great ascetics,

children.text: mamāpi tad bhūtikaraṃ pracakṣate mahānubhāvaṃ caritaṃ nibodhata ||
children.translated_text: proclaim even my own fortunate and mighty story; listen to it."

children.text: tatas tu tau rāmavacaḥ pracoditāv agāyatāṃ mārgavidhānasampadā
children.translated_text: Then those two, impelled by <s>Rāma</s>'s words, sang with the excellence of the proper method,

children.text: sa cāpi rāmaḥ pariṣadgataḥ śanair bubhūṣayāsaktamanā babhūva ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Rāma</s> too, seated in the assembly, gradually became absorbed in mind with the wish to hear.

children.text: sarvāpūrvam iyaṃ yeṣām āsīt kṛtsnā vasuṃdharā
children.translated_text: From ancient times this whole earth had belonged to those
victorious kings, beginning with <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: yeṣāṃ sa sagaro nāma sāgaro yena khānitaḥ
children.translated_text: Among them was one named <s>Sagara</s>, by whom the ocean was dug out,
and whom sixty thousand sons surrounded as he went.

children.text: ikṣvākūṇām idaṃ teṣāṃ rājñāṃ vaṃśe mahātmanām
children.translated_text: In the lineage of those great-souled kings of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s>s,

children.text: mahad utpannam ākhyānaṃ rāmāyaṇam iti śrutam ||
children.translated_text: this great narrative arose, known as the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: tad idaṃ vartayiṣyāmi sarvaṃ nikhilam āditaḥ
children.translated_text: I shall now set it forth from the beginning, entirely and without omission;
joined with <s>dharma</s> (right order), <s>kāma</s> (desire), and <s>artha</s> (purpose), it should be heard without envy.

children.text: kosalo nāma muditaḥ sphīto janapado mahān
children.translated_text: There was a joyful, flourishing, great country named <s>Kosala</s>,
settled on the bank of the <s>Sarayū</s>, rich in abundant wealth and grain.
There stood a city named <s>Ayodhyā</s>, renowned throughout the world,

children.text: manunā mānavendreṇa yā purī nirmitā svayam ||
children.translated_text: a city built by <s>Manu</s> himself, lord of humankind.

children.text: āyatā daśa ca dve ca yojanāni mahāpurī
children.translated_text: That great city extended twelve yojanas in length,
and was three yojanas broad, prosperous, with its great roads well laid out.
It was adorned by a broad, well-divided royal road,
strewn with loose flowers and always sprinkled with water.
King <s>Daśaratha</s>, increaser of his great kingdom,
made that city his dwelling, like the lord of the gods in heaven.
It had gates and archways, and its inner markets were well arranged;
it possessed every kind of engine and weapon, and was attended by craftsmen of every craft.
Crowded with sūtas and māgadhas, splendid and of unequaled radiance,
it had high watchtowers and banners, and was filled with hundreds of <s>śataghnī</s> weapons.
On every side the city was joined with companies of women and performers.
Endowed with pleasure gardens and mango groves, great, and girdled by śāla trees,
with difficult fortifications and a deep moat, hard for others to approach,
filled with horses and elephants, and also with cows, camels, and asses,
surrounded by assemblies of neighboring kings and by offerings of tribute,
and beautified by merchants dwelling there from many countries,
adorned with palaces fashioned with jewels, like mountains,
and filled with lofty mansions, like <s>Indra</s>'s <s>Amarāvatī</s>,
varied in appearance, laid out like an aṣṭāpada board, and filled with groups of excellent women,
strewn with every kind of jewel and splendid with aerial mansions and houses,
dense with houses, without gaps, and established on level ground,
full of śāli rice grain and with water sweet as sugarcane juice,

children.text: dundubhībhir mṛdaṅgaiś ca vīṇābhiḥ paṇavais tathā
children.translated_text: with kettledrums, mṛdaṅgas, vīṇās, and paṇavas,

children.text: nāditāṃ bhṛśam atyarthaṃ pṛthivyāṃ tām anuttamām ||
children.translated_text: that unsurpassed city on earth was made to resound very loudly indeed.
It was like the celestial vehicle of the siddhas, attained in heaven through ascetic power,
with its houses well laid out at the edges, and filled with the best of men.

children.text: ye ca bāṇair na vidhyanti viviktam aparāparam
children.translated_text: Those who do not shoot with arrows at one isolated man after another,
but who are swift-handed experts in striking an extended target by sound,
killers in the forest of roaring, maddened lions, tigers, and boars,

children.text: hantāro niśitaiḥ śastrair balād bāhubalair api ||
children.translated_text: with sharp weapons and also by force through the strength of their arms,
with thousands of such great chariot-warriors
King <s>Daśaratha</s> then caused that city to be inhabited.

children.text: tām agnimadbhir guṇavadbhir āvṛtāṃ dvijottamair vedaṣaḍaṅgapāragaiḥ
children.translated_text: That city was surrounded by the best of twice-born men who maintained sacred fires, were virtuous, and had mastered the Veda with its six limbs,

children.text: sahasradaiḥ satyaratair mahātmabhir maharṣikalpair ṛṣibhiś ca kevalaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: by great-souled men who gave thousands, were devoted to truth, and were like great seers, and by pure ṛṣis.
In that city, <s>Ayodhyā</s>, there was a knower of the Veda, one who gathered all together,
far-seeing, very powerful, and dear to townsmen and country people.
Among the <s>Ikṣvākus</s> he was a great chariot-warrior, a sacrificer, devoted to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), and self-controlled,
a royal seer like a great ṛṣi, famed in the three worlds.
He was strong, had slain his enemies, possessed friends, and had conquered his senses,
and in wealth and other stores he was like <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>.
As the very powerful <s>Manu</s> was protector of the world,

children.text: tathā daśaratho rājā vasañ jagad apālayat ||
children.translated_text: so King <s>Daśaratha</s>, dwelling there, protected the world.
By him, who was pledged to truth and observed the three aims of life,
that excellent city was protected like <s>Amarāvatī</s> by the lord of the gods.

children.text: tasmin puravare hṛṣṭā dharmātmanā bahu śrutāḥ
children.translated_text: In that best of cities, ruled by the righteous king, the people were joyful and very learned;

children.text: narās tuṣṭādhanaiḥ svaiḥ svair alubdhāḥ satyavādinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the men were content with their own wealth, free from greed, and speakers of truth.
In that best city there was no one with meager possessions,
no householder who lacked success or was without cows, horses, wealth, and grain.

children.text: kāmī vā na kadaryo vā nṛśaṃsaḥ puruṣaḥ kvacit
children.translated_text: Nowhere in <s>Ayodhyā</s> could a lustful, miserly, or cruel man be seen,

children.text: draṣṭuṃ śakyam ayodhyāyāṃ nāvidvān na ca nāstikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor anyone unlearned, nor any atheist.

children.text: sarve narāś ca nāryaś ca dharmaśīlāḥ susaṃyatāḥ
children.translated_text: All men and women were devoted to <s>dharma</s> and well restrained,
joyful in conduct and character, stainless like great seers.
There was no one without earrings, without a diadem, without a garland, or with scant enjoyment,
nor anyone unwashed, with limbs unanointed, or lacking fragrance.
No one ate unclean food, no one failed to give, and no one was without armlets and gold necklaces;
nor was anyone seen without ornaments on the hands, or without self-control.
In <s>Ayodhyā</s> there was no brahmin who did not maintain sacred fires, perform sacrifices, or give by the thousand,

children.text: kaścid āsīd ayodhyāyāṃ na ca nirvṛttasaṃkaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor was there anyone of mixed and improper conduct.
The brahmins were always intent on their own duties and had conquered their senses,
devoted to giving and study, and restrained in accepting gifts.

children.text: na nāstiko nānṛtako na kaścid abahuśrutaḥ
children.translated_text: At that time there was no atheist, no liar, and no one without broad learning;

children.text: nāsūyako na cāśakto nāvidvān vidyate tadā ||
children.translated_text: no envious man, no incapable man, and no unlearned man existed.

children.text: na dīnaḥ kṣiptacitto vā vyathito vāpi kaścana
children.translated_text: There was not any man who was poor, distracted in mind, or distressed,

children.text: kaścin naro vā nārī vā nāśrīmān nāpy arūpavān
children.translated_text: nor any man or woman who lacked prosperity or beauty,
nor anyone in <s>Ayodhyā</s> who was not devoted to the king.
Among the foremost four varṇas, all people honored deities and guests;

children.text: dīrghāyuṣo narāḥ sarve dharmaṃ satyaṃ ca saṃśritāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all men were long-lived and relied upon <s>dharma</s> and truth.

children.text: kṣatraṃ brahmamukhaṃ cāsīd vaiśyāḥ kṣatram anuvratāḥ
children.translated_text: The kṣatriya order had the brahmins foremost, and the vaiśyas followed the kṣatriyas;
the śūdras were intent on their own <s>dharma</s> and served the three varṇas.
That city was well protected by that lord of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s>,
just as in former times it had been protected by wise <s>Manu</s>, lord of men.
It was filled with warriors like fire, skilled and intolerant of insult,
fully trained in all knowledge, like lions in a cave.
It was filled with excellent horses born in the <s>Kāmboja</s> region and in <s>Vāhlīka</s>,
as well as forest-bred and river-born horses, equal to <s>Hari</s>'s own steeds.
It was filled with maddened elephants born in the <s>Vindhya</s> mountains and also in the <s>Himavat</s>,
intoxicated with rut, exceedingly strong, and like mountains.

children.text: añjanād api niṣkrāntair vāmanād api ca dvipaiḥ
children.translated_text: That city had elephants descended from <s>Añjana</s> and also from <s>Vāmana</s>,

children.text: bhadramandrair bhadramṛgair mṛgamandraiś ca sā purī ||
children.translated_text: with bhadramandra, bhadramṛga, and mṛgamandra breeds of elephants.
It was always full of ever-maddened elephants resembling immovable mountains.

children.text: sā yojane ca dve bhūyaḥ satyanāmā prakāśate ||
children.translated_text: Extending for two yojanas and more, it shone forth as truly named.

children.text: tāṃ satyanāmāṃ dṛḍhatoraṇārgalām gṛhair vicitrair upaśobhitāṃ śivām
children.translated_text: That rightly named, auspicious city <s>Ayodhyā</s>, with firm gateways and bars, and adorned with varied houses,

children.text: purīm ayodhyāṃ nṛsahasrasaṃkulāṃ śaśāsa vai śakrasamo mahīpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: crowded with thousands of men, was ruled by the lord of the earth, equal to <s>Śakra</s>.
In it the hero had eight famous ministers,
pure and devoted, constantly engaged in the affairs of the king.
<s>Dhṛṣṭi</s>, <s>Jayanta</s>, <s>Vijaya</s>, <s>Siddhārtha</s>, and <s>Arthasādhaka</s>
<s>Aśoka</s>, <s>Mantrapāla</s>, and <s>Sumantra</s> was the eighth.
His two approved officiating priests were those two best of sages,

children.text: vasiṣṭho vāmadevaś ca mantriṇaś ca tathāpare ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and <s>Vāmadeva</s>; and there were also other ministers.
They were prosperous, high-souled, learned in the śāstras, and firm in valor,
renowned, attentive, and acting according to the king's command.
They had attained splendor, forbearance, and fame, and they spoke with a smile before their words;

children.text: krodhāt kāmārthahetor vā na brūyur anṛtaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: through anger, desire, or the pursuit of wealth they would not utter a false word.

children.text: teṣām aviditaṃ kiṃcit sveṣu nāsti pareṣu vā
children.translated_text: There was nothing, among their own people or among others, that was unknown to them,
whether it was being done, had been done, or was even intended, through their spies.
They were skilled in public dealings and tested in friendship;

children.text: prāptakālaṃ yathā daṇḍaṃ dhārayeyuḥ suteṣv api ||
children.translated_text: at the proper time they would impose the due <s>daṇḍa</s> (punishment), even upon their sons.
They were engaged in gathering the treasury and in maintaining the army;

children.text: ahitaṃ cāpi puruṣaṃ na vihiṃsyur adūṣakam ||
children.translated_text: yet they would not harm even a hostile man who had committed no offense.
They were heroic, constant in effort, and followed the science of kingship;
they were always protectors of the pure inhabitants of the realm.
Without injuring the Brahmin or Kṣatriya orders, they filled the treasury;
their punishments were very sharp after they had considered a man's strength and weakness.
Among all those pure, single-minded, and fully discerning people,

children.text: nāsīt pure vā rāṣṭre vā mṛṣāvādī naraḥ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: there was no man anywhere in the city or in the kingdom who spoke falsely.

children.text: kaścin na duṣṭas tatrāsīt paradāraratir naraḥ
children.translated_text: There was no wicked man there, nor any man attached to another's wife;

children.text: praśāntaṃ sarvam evāsīd rāṣṭraṃ puravaraṃ ca tat ||
children.translated_text: the whole kingdom, and that excellent city, was entirely at peace.

children.text: suvāsasaḥ suveśāś ca te ca sarve suśīlinaḥ
children.translated_text: They were finely clothed and well adorned, and all of them were of good conduct,
wakeful for the welfare of the king, with the eye of policy.

children.text: gurau guṇagṛhītāś ca prakhyātāś ca parākramaiḥ
children.translated_text: They were esteemed by their elders for their virtues and famed for their prowess;
even in foreign lands they were known everywhere for the firmness of their judgment.

children.text: īdṛśais tair amātyais tu rājā daśaratho 'naghaḥ
children.translated_text: Endowed with such ministers, rich in virtues, the blameless king <s>Daśaratha</s>
ruled the earth.
Watching his subjects through spies and delighting them through <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),

children.text: nādhyagacchad viśiṣṭaṃ vā tulyaṃ vā śatrum ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he found no enemy superior to himself, or even equal to him.

children.text: tair mantribhir mantrahitair niviṣṭair vṛto 'nuraktaiḥ kuśalaiḥ samarthaiḥ
children.translated_text: Surrounded by those ministers, devoted to counsel, loyal, skillful, and capable,

children.text: sa pārthivo dīptim avāpa yuktas tejomayair gobhir ivodito 'rkaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that king shone brightly, like the sun risen with rays full of light.
But for him, of such power, knower of <s>dharma</s>, high-souled as he was,
tormented by longing for sons, there was no son to continue the lineage.
As that great-souled king was thinking in this way, the thought arose in him:

children.text: sutārthaṃ vājimedhena kimarthaṃ na yajāmy aham ||
children.translated_text: “For the sake of sons, why should I not sacrifice with a horse sacrifice?”

children.text: sa niścitāṃ matiṃ kṛtvā yaṣṭavyam iti buddhimān
children.translated_text: Having formed a firm resolve that the sacrifice should be performed, the wise one,

children.text: mantribhiḥ saha dharmātmā sarvair eva kṛtātmabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the righteous-souled king, consulted with all his self-controlled ministers.
Then the king said this to <s>Sumantra</s>, the best of ministers:

children.text: śīghram ānaya me sarvān gurūṃs tān sapurohitān ||
children.translated_text: “Quickly bring me all those elders, together with the family priests.”

children.text: etac chrutvā rahaḥ sūto rājānam idam abravīt
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the charioteer spoke these words to the king in private:
“I once heard this ancient account, taught by officiating priests.
The blessed <s>Sanatkumāra</s> formerly told a story

children.text: ṛṣīṇāṃ saṃnidhau rājaṃs tava putrāgamaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: in the presence of the sages, O king, concerning the coming of sons to you.

children.text: kāśyapasya tu putro 'sti vibhāṇḍaka iti śrutaḥ
children.translated_text: There is a son of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, known as <s>Vibhāṇḍaka</s>;

children.text: ṛṣyaśṛṅga iti khyātas tasya putro bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: his son will be famed as <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s>.

children.text: sa vane nityasaṃvṛddho munir vanacaraḥ sadā
children.translated_text: He, a sage always dwelling in the forest, will be continually raised in the forest;
that best of Brahmins will know no one else, always obedient to his father.
The twofold nature of that great one's <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate discipline)

children.text: lokeṣu prathitaṃ rājan vipraiś ca kathitaṃ sadā ||
children.translated_text: will be famous among the worlds, O king, and always recounted by Brahmins.
As he lives in this way, time will pass for him,
while he tends the sacred fire and his famous father.

children.text: etasminn eva kāle tu romapādaḥ pratāpavān
children.translated_text: At that very time the powerful <s>Romapāda</s>,
a renowned king among the <s>Aṅgas</s>, will be mighty.
Because of that king's transgression there will be a very dreadful
and terrible drought, causing fear to all beings.
When the drought has occurred, the king, filled with sorrow,
will gather Brahmins grown old in learning and will speak:
“You are learned in <s>dharma</s> and know conduct in the world;
prescribe the observance by which there may be atonement.”
Those Brahmins, who have crossed to the far shore of the Vedas, will say to the ruler of the earth:
“O king, bring here <s>Vibhāṇḍaka</s>'s son by every means.
And after bringing <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s>, well honored, O ruler of the earth,

children.text: prayaccha kanyāṃ śāntāṃ vai vidhinā susamāhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: give him the maiden <s>Śāntā</s> according to rule, with full attention.”

children.text: teṣāṃ tu vacanaṃ śrutvā rājā cintāṃ prapatsyate
children.translated_text: Having heard their words, the king will fall into anxious thought:

children.text: kenopāyena vai śakyam ihānetuṃ sa vīryavān ||
children.translated_text: “By what means can that mighty one be brought here?”

children.text: tato rājā viniścitya saha mantribhir ātmavān
children.translated_text: Then the self-possessed king, having decided, together with his ministers,
will send his priest and ministers, treating them with honor.

children.text: te tu rājño vacaḥ śrutvā vyathitāvanatānanāḥ
children.translated_text: But when they hear the king's command, distressed and with downcast faces,

children.text: na gacchema ṛṣer bhītā anuneṣyanti taṃ nṛpam ||
children.translated_text: they will entreat that king: “We will not go, for we are afraid of the sage.”

children.text: vakṣyanti cintayitvā te tasyopāyāṃś ca tān kṣamān
children.translated_text: After reflecting, they will tell him those suitable means

children.text: āneṣyāmo vayaṃ vipraṃ na ca doṣo bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: by which they say, “We shall bring the Brahmin, and no fault will arise.”
Thus, by the lord of <s>Aṅga</s> himself, through courtesans, the sage's son
was brought; the god rained, and <s>Śāntā</s> is given to him.

children.text: ṛṣyaśṛṅgas tu jāmātā putrāṃs tava vidhāsyati
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s>, as your son-in-law, will provide sons for you.
This much, as told by <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, has been spoken by me.”
Then the delighted <s>Daśaratha</s> addressed <s>Sumantra</s>:
"Tell me in detail how <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s> was brought here."

children.text: sumantraś codito rājñā provācedaṃ vacas tadā
children.translated_text: Urged by the king, <s>Sumantra</s> then spoke these words:

children.text: yatharṣyaśṛṅgas tv ānītaḥ śṛṇu me mantribhiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: "Hear from me, together with the ministers, how <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s> was brought.
The priest, along with the ministers, said this to <s>Romapāda</s>:
"This harmless means has been thought out by us.
<s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s>, who lives in the forest, is devoted to austerity and recitation of sacred study;

children.text: anabhijñaḥ sa nārīṇāṃ viṣayāṇāṃ sukhasya ca ||
children.translated_text: he has no knowledge of women, of sensual objects, or of pleasure.
With desirable objects of the senses, which disturb the minds of men,
we shall quickly bring him to the city; let this be resolved upon at once.
Let courtesans go there, beautiful and well adorned;
honored here, they will entice him by various means and bring him.

children.text: śrutvā tatheti rājā ca pratyuvāca purohitam
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the king replied to the priest, "So be it,"

children.text: purohito mantriṇaś ca tathā cakruś ca te tadā ||
children.translated_text: and the priest and the ministers then acted accordingly.

children.text: vāramukhyās tu tac chrutvā vanaṃ praviviśur mahat
children.translated_text: But when the chief courtesans heard that, they entered the great forest;
not far from the hermitage they made an effort to appear before him,
the formidable son of the seer, who always dwelt in the hermitage.
Always content with his father, he did not go beyond the hermitage.
Since his birth that ascetic had never before seen

children.text: strī vā pumān vā yac cānyat sattvaṃ nagararāṣṭrajam ||
children.translated_text: a woman, a man, or any other being born in a city or kingdom.

children.text: tataḥ kadācit taṃ deśam ājagāma yadṛcchayā
children.translated_text: Then, one day, by chance, the son of <s>Vibhāṇḍaka</s> came to that place,
and there he saw those excellent women.
Those women, dressed in varied garments and singing with sweet voices,
approached the seer's son and all said these words:

children.text: kas tvaṃ kiṃ vartase brahmañ jñātum icchāmahe vayam
children.translated_text: "Who are you, brahmin, and what are you doing? We wish to know.

children.text: ekas tvaṃ vijane ghore vane carasi śaṃsa naḥ ||
children.translated_text: You wander alone in this desolate, terrible forest; tell us."

children.text: adṛṣṭarūpās tās tena kāmyarūpā vane striyaḥ
children.translated_text: Since he had never seen such forms before, those women in the forest seemed lovely to him.

children.text: hārdāt tasya matir jātā ākhyātuṃ pitaraṃ svakam ||
children.translated_text: Out of affection his mind arose to tell them about his own father:
"Our father is <s>Vibhāṇḍaka</s>, and I am his legitimate son.

children.text: ṛṣyaśṛṅga iti khyātaṃ nāma karma ca me bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: My name, famous on earth, is <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s>, as is my observance.
Our hermitage is here nearby, auspicious-looking ladies.

children.text: kariṣye vo 'tra pūjāṃ vai sarveṣāṃ vidhipūrvakam ||
children.translated_text: There I shall perform worship for all of you according to rule."

children.text: ṛṣiputravacaḥ śrutvā sarvāsāṃ matir āsa vai
children.translated_text: Hearing the words of the seer's son, the thought arose in all of them

children.text: tad āśramapadaṃ draṣṭuṃ jagmuḥ sarvāś ca tena ha ||
children.translated_text: to see that hermitage, and they all went there with him.

children.text: gatānāṃ tu tataḥ pūjām ṛṣiputraś cakāra ha
children.translated_text: When they had arrived, the seer's son then offered them hospitality:

children.text: idam arghyam idaṃ pādyam idaṃ mūlaṃ phalaṃ ca naḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Here is arghya water; here is water for washing the feet; here are our roots and fruits."

children.text: pratigṛhya tu tāṃ pūjāṃ sarvā eva samutsukāḥ
children.translated_text: After accepting that worship, all of them, greatly eager

children.text: ṛṣer bhītāś ca śīghraṃ tu gamanāya matiṃ dadhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: and afraid of the seer, quickly set their minds on departing.

children.text: asmākam api mukhyāni phalānīmāni vai dvija
children.translated_text: "We too have these excellent fruits, brahmin;

children.text: gṛhāṇa prati bhadraṃ te bhakṣayasva ca māciram ||
children.translated_text: take them, may good fortune be yours, and eat them without delay."

children.text: tatas tās taṃ samāliṅgya sarvā harṣasamanvitāḥ
children.translated_text: Then all of them, filled with delight, embraced him

children.text: modakān pradadus tasmai bhakṣyāṃś ca vividhāñ śubhān ||
children.translated_text: and gave him sweet cakes and various fine foods.

children.text: tāni cāsvādya tejasvī phalānīti sma manyate
children.translated_text: Tasting them, the brilliant one thought they were fruits,
things never before tasted by those who always lived in the forest.

children.text: āpṛcchya ca tadā vipraṃ vratacaryāṃ nivedya ca
children.translated_text: Then, taking leave of the brahmin and declaring their religious observance,

children.text: gacchanti smāpadeśāt tā bhītās tasya pituḥ striyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: those women departed under a pretext, afraid of his father.
When all of them had gone, the brahmin son of <s>Kāśyapa</s>
became troubled at heart and kept turning over his sorrow.

children.text: tato 'paredyus taṃ deśam ājagāma sa vīryavān
children.translated_text: Then on the following day that mighty one came to the place

children.text: manojñā yatra tā dṛṣṭā vāramukhyāḥ svalaṃkṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: where he had seen those charming, well-adorned courtesans.

children.text: dṛṣṭvaiva ca tadā vipram āyāntaṃ hṛṣṭamānasāḥ
children.translated_text: As soon as they saw the brahmin coming, their minds were delighted;

children.text: upasṛtya tataḥ sarvās tās tam ūcur idaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then all of them approached him and said these words:

children.text: ehy āśramapadaṃ saumya asmākam iti cābruvan
children.translated_text: "Come, gentle one, to our hermitage," they said.

children.text: tatrāpy eṣa vidhiḥ śrīmān viśeṣeṇa bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: "There too this splendid rite will be performed in a special way."

children.text: śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tāsāṃ sarvāsāṃ hṛdayaṃgamam
children.translated_text: Hearing the pleasing words of all of them,

children.text: gamanāya matiṃ cakre taṃ ca ninyus tadā striyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he set his mind on going, and the women then led him away.

children.text: tatra cānīyamāne tu vipre tasmin mahātmani
children.translated_text: And while that great-souled brahmin was being brought there,

children.text: vavarṣa sahasā devo jagat prahlādayaṃs tadā ||
children.translated_text: the god of rain suddenly poured down, gladdening the world at that time.
The lord of men, seeing that the brahmin had come into his own realm just through the rain,

children.text: pratyudgamya muniṃ prahvaḥ śirasā ca mahīṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: went out to meet the sage, bowed low, and touched the earth with his head.

children.text: arghyaṃ ca pradadau tasmai nyāyataḥ susamāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Calm and attentive, he duly offered him arghya

children.text: vavre prasādaṃ viprendrān mā vipraṃ manyur āviśet ||
children.translated_text: and begged a favor from the best of brahmins, so that anger would not enter the brahmin.
Entering the inner apartments, and giving him his daughter

children.text: śāntāṃ śāntena manasā rājā harṣam avāpa saḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śāntā</s> according to rule, the king obtained joy with a peaceful mind.

children.text: evaṃ sa nyavasat tatra sarvakāmaiḥ supūjitaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus the greatly brilliant <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s> lived there,
well honored with every desired thing, together with his wife <s>Śāntā</s>.

children.text: bhūya eva ca rājendra śṛṇu me vacanaṃ hitam
children.translated_text: Again, O king, hear my beneficial words,
as that wise, excellent divine being once told them.
"In the family of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s> there will be born a very righteous king,
glorious, true to his promise, named <s>Daśaratha</s>.

children.text: aṅgarājena sakhyaṃ ca tasya rājño bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: That king will have friendship with the king of <s>Aṅga</s>,

children.text: kanyā cāsya mahābhāgā śāntā nāma bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: and he will have a highly fortunate daughter named <s>Śāntā</s>.

children.text: putras tv aṅgasya rājñas tu romapāda iti śrutaḥ
children.translated_text: The son of the king of <s>Aṅga</s> will be known as <s>Romapāda</s>;

children.text: taṃ sa rājā daśaratho gamiṣyati mahāyaśāḥ ||
children.translated_text: to him the very famous king <s>Daśaratha</s> will go.

children.text: anapatyo 'smi dharmātmañ śāntā bhāryā mama kratum
children.translated_text: "I am without offspring, righteous one; <s>Śāntā</s> is my wife, and the sacrifice..."
At your command he will bring him for the sake of offspring and of the family line.

children.text: śrutvā rājño 'tha tad vākyaṃ manasā sa vicintya ca
children.translated_text: Then, having heard that speech of the king and reflected on it in his mind,
the self-possessed one will hand over <s>Śāntā</s>'s husband, who can bring sons.

children.text: pratigṛhya ca taṃ vipraṃ sa rājā vigatajvaraḥ
children.translated_text: And having received that brahmin, that king, freed from distress,
will undertake that sacrifice with a delighted heart.

children.text: taṃ ca rājā daśaratho yaṣṭukāmaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: And King <s>Daśaratha</s>, desiring to sacrifice, with joined palms,
will choose the best of twice-born men, <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s>, knowing <s>dharma</s> (righteous order).

children.text: yajñārthaṃ prasavārthaṃ ca svargārthaṃ ca nareśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: For the sake of the sacrifice, for the sake of progeny, and for the sake of heaven, that lord of men

children.text: labhate ca sa taṃ kāmaṃ dvijamukhyād viśāṃpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: will obtain that desire from the foremost brahmin, O lord of the people.
And four sons of immeasurable valor will be born to him,
establishers of his lineage and renowned in all the worlds.

children.text: evaṃ sa devapravaraḥ pūrvaṃ kathitavān kathām
children.translated_text: Thus that excellent god once told this story before,
the blessed lord <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, long ago in the age of the gods.

children.text: sa tvaṃ puruṣaśārdūla tam ānaya susatkṛtam
children.translated_text: Therefore, bull among men, bring him here, having honored him well,
going yourself, great king, together with your army and vehicles.

children.text: anumānya vasiṣṭhaṃ ca sūtavākyaṃ niśamya ca
children.translated_text: Having obtained <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s consent and heard the charioteer's words,

children.text: sāntaḥpuraḥ sahāmātyaḥ prayayau yatra sa dvijaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he set out, with his women of the inner palace and his ministers, to where that twice-born man was.

children.text: vanāni saritaś caiva vyatikramya śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: Passing slowly, slowly through forests and rivers,

children.text: abhicakrāma taṃ deśaṃ yatra vai munipuṃgavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he approached that country where the foremost sage was.
On reaching that best of twice-born men, who was near <s>Romapāda</s>,
he first saw the seer's son, blazing like fire.

children.text: tato rājā yathānyāyaṃ pūjāṃ cakre viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Then the king, in the proper manner, performed worship for him especially,
with a delighted heart because of his friendship with that king.
And when <s>Romapāda</s> had explained to the wise seer's son

children.text: sakhyaṃ sambandhakaṃ caiva tadā taṃ pratyapūjayat ||
children.translated_text: their friendship and family connection, he then honored him in return.
Thus well honored by him, the bull among men, the king, stayed with him
for seven or eight days, and then spoke these words to the king:

children.text: śāntā tava sutā rājan saha bhartrā viśāṃpate
children.translated_text: Your daughter <s>Śāntā</s>, O king, together with her husband, O lord of the people,

children.text: madīyaṃ nagaraṃ yātu kāryaṃ hi mahad udyatam ||
children.translated_text: should go to my city; for a great undertaking has been set in motion.

children.text: tatheti rājā saṃśrutya gamanaṃ tasya dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that the wise king's departure was agreed to, that king said, 'So be it,'

children.text: uvāca vacanaṃ vipraṃ gaccha tvaṃ saha bhāryayā ||
children.translated_text: and spoke this word to the brahmin: 'Go, you, together with your wife.'

children.text: ṛṣiputraḥ pratiśrutya tathety āha nṛpaṃ tadā
children.translated_text: The seer's son accepted and then said to the king, 'So be it';
permitted by the king, he set out together with his wife.

children.text: tāv anyonyāñjaliṃ kṛtvā snehāt saṃśliṣya corasā
children.translated_text: The two made añjalis to each other and, out of affection, embraced breast to breast;
<s>Daśaratha</s> and the powerful <s>Romapāda</s> rejoiced.
Then, having taken leave of his friend, the delight of the <s>Raghus</s> set out,
and he sent swift-going messengers to the citizens:

children.text: kriyatāṃ nagaraṃ sarvaṃ kṣipram eva svalaṃkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: 'Let the whole city quickly be made beautifully adorned.'

children.text: tataḥ prahṛṣṭāḥ paurās te śrutvā rājānam āgatam
children.translated_text: Then those delighted citizens, hearing that the king had arrived,

children.text: tathā pracakrus tat sarvaṃ rājñā yat preṣitaṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: did everything just as the king had ordered at that time.

children.text: tataḥ svalaṃkṛtaṃ rājā nagaraṃ praviveśa ha
children.translated_text: Then the king entered the well-adorned city,
placing the eminent brahmin before him amid the sounds of conches and kettledrums.

children.text: tataḥ pramuditāḥ sarve dṛṣṭvā vai nāgarā dvijam
children.translated_text: Then all the townspeople were very joyful when they saw the brahmin
being brought in with honor by the king, whose deeds were like <s>Indra</s>'s.

children.text: antaḥpuraṃ praveśyainaṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā tu śāstrataḥ
children.translated_text: Having led him into the inner palace and performed worship according to rule,
he then considered himself successful because he had brought him there.
All the women of the inner palace, seeing <s>Śāntā</s> arrived in that way,
the wide-eyed woman together with her husband, came to loving joy.

children.text: pūjyamānā ca tābhiḥ sā rājñā caiva viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Honored by them and especially by the king himself,

children.text: uvāsa tatra sukhitā kaṃcit kālaṃ saha dvijā ||
children.translated_text: she stayed there happily for some time together with the brahmin.
Then after much time had passed, on a certain very pleasant occasion,
when spring had fully arrived, the king's mind turned to sacrificing.

children.text: tataḥ prasādya śirasā taṃ vipraṃ devavarṇinam
children.translated_text: Then, bowing his head and propitiating that brahmin, who shone like a god,
he chose him for the sacrifice, for the sake of offspring and of the family line.

children.text: tatheti ca sa rājānam uvāca ca susatkṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: 'So be it,' he, well honored, said to the king,

children.text: sambhārāḥ saṃbhriyantāṃ te turagaś ca vimucyatām ||
children.translated_text: 'Let your materials be gathered, and let the horse be released.'
Then the king spoke these words to <s>Sumantra</s>, the best of ministers:
'<s>Sumantra</s>, quickly summon the officiating priests, the expounders of brahman.'
Then <s>Sumantra</s>, swift in action, quickly went

children.text: samānayat sa tān viprān samastān vedapāragān ||
children.translated_text: and brought together all those brahmins, masters of the Veda:

children.text: suyajñaṃ vāmadevaṃ ca jābālim atha kāśyapam
children.translated_text: <s>Suyajña</s>, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, and then <s>Jābāli</s> and <s>Kāśyapa</s>,

children.text: purohitaṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ ca ye cānye dvijasattamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the family priest <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, and the other excellent twice-born men.

children.text: tān pūjayitvā dharmātmā rājā daśarathas tadā
children.translated_text: Having honored them, righteous King <s>Daśaratha</s> then
spoke this gentle word, joined with <s>dharma</s> and practical purpose:

children.text: mama lālapyamānasya putrārthaṃ nāsti vai sukham
children.translated_text: 'For me, who am yearning for sons, there is indeed no happiness.
For that purpose my thought is: I shall sacrifice with a horse sacrifice.

children.text: tad ahaṃ yaṣṭum icchāmi śāstradṛṣṭena karmaṇā
children.translated_text: Therefore I wish to sacrifice by a rite seen in the śāstra (authoritative rule),
and through the power of the seer's son I too shall obtain my desires.'

children.text: tataḥ sādhv iti tad vākyaṃ brāhmaṇāḥ pratyapūjayan
children.translated_text: Then the brahmins, all headed by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, approved that word as good,
fallen from the mouth of the earthly king.
And with <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s> at their head they then replied to the lord of men:

children.text: sambhārāḥ saṃbhriyantāṃ te turagaś ca vimucyatām ||
children.translated_text: 'Let your materials be gathered, and let the horse be released.
In every way you will obtain four sons of immeasurable valor,

children.text: yasya te dhārmikī buddhir iyaṃ putrārtham āgatā ||
children.translated_text: since this righteous intention of yours has arisen for the sake of sons.'

children.text: tataḥ prīto 'bhavad rājā śrutvā tad dvijabhāṣitam
children.translated_text: Then the king became pleased on hearing that speech of the brahmins.
And the king, filled with joy, said these auspicious words to his ministers:

children.text: gurūṇāṃ vacanāc chīghraṃ sambhārāḥ saṃbhriyantu me
children.translated_text: "By the command of the venerable teachers, let the necessary materials be gathered for me quickly.
And let the horse, overseen by competent men and accompanied by its ritual teacher, be released.
Let the sacrificial ground be laid out on the northern bank of the <s>Sarayū</s>,
and let rites for appeasement and prosperity be performed according to rule and according to prescription.

children.text: śakyaḥ kartum ayaṃ yajñaḥ sarveṇāpi mahīkṣitā
children.translated_text: This sacrifice can be performed even by every protector of the earth,

children.text: nāparādho bhavet kaṣṭo yady asmin kratusattame ||
children.translated_text: but no grievous fault must occur in this best of rites.
For learned <s>brahmarākṣasas</s> (brahmin-demons) look for an opening here;
the performer of a sacrifice lacking proper rule perishes at once.

children.text: tad yathāvidhi pūrvaṃ me kratur eṣa samāpyate
children.translated_text: Therefore, so that this rite of mine may be completed according to rule from the beginning,
let the proper arrangement be made; you are capable in these matters."

children.text: tatheti ca tataḥ sarve mantriṇaḥ pratyapūjayan
children.translated_text: Then all the ministers approved, saying, "So be it,"
and carried out the command of that lord of kings just as it had been ordered.

children.text: tato dvijās te dharmajñam astuvan pārthivarṣabham
children.translated_text: Then those twice-born men praised the bull among kings, who knew <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),

children.text: anujñātās tataḥ sarve punar jagmur yathāgatam ||
children.translated_text: and, having been dismissed, they all went back the way they had come.

children.text: gatānāṃ tu dvijātīnāṃ mantriṇas tān narādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: When the twice-born men had gone, the lord of men
dismissed those ministers and entered his own palace, radiant with great splendor.

children.text: punaḥ prāpte vasante tu pūrṇaḥ saṃvatsaro 'bhavat
children.translated_text: But when spring came again, a full year had passed.

children.text: abhivādya vasiṣṭhaṃ ca nyāyataḥ pratipūjya ca ||
children.translated_text: After greeting <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and duly honoring him,
he spoke respectful words to that best of twice-born men for the sake of obtaining offspring:

children.text: yajño me kriyatāṃ vipra yathoktaṃ munipuṃgava ||
children.translated_text: "Let my sacrifice be performed, brahmin, just as it was prescribed, O foremost sage.

children.text: yathā na vighnaḥ kriyate yajñāṅgeṣu vidhīyatām
children.translated_text: Arrange it so that no obstruction is made in the parts of the sacrifice.

children.text: bhavān snigdhaḥ suhṛn mahyaṃ guruś ca paramo bhavān ||
children.translated_text: You are affectionate toward me, you are my friend, and you are my supreme guru.

children.text: voḍhavyo bhavatā caiva bhāro yajñasya codyataḥ
children.translated_text: This burden of the sacrifice that has been undertaken must indeed be borne by you."

children.text: tatheti ca sa rājānam abravīd dvijasattamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that best of twice-born men said to the king, "So be it.

children.text: kariṣye sarvam evaitad bhavatā yat samarthitam
children.translated_text: I will do all this that has been proposed by you."
Then he spoke to the elder twice-born men established in sacrificial rites,
and also to the elder, supremely righteous men skilled in architecture,
to work supervisors, craftsmen, carpenters, and diggers,
to calculators, artisans, actors, and dancers as well,
and also to pure men, learned in the śāstras and very well taught:
"At the king's command, you must set about the sacrificial work.
Let many thousands of bricks be brought quickly.
Let temporary lodgings, furnished with many amenities, be made for kings,
and hundreds of fine dwellings must also be made for brahmins,
well appointed with abundant food to eat, cooked rice, and drink.
