Likewise, broad lodgings must be made for the townspeople too,
with abundant food and supplied with every desired thing.
And for the people from the countryside also, something very splendid must be provided.

children.text: dātavyam annaṃ vidhivat satkṛtya na tu līlayā
children.translated_text: Food is to be given according to rule, with honor, and not carelessly.
Let people of all varṇas receive honor when they have been well received.
No contempt is to be shown, even under the sway of desire or anger.
Those men who are undistracted in the sacrificial tasks, and the artisans as well,

children.text: teṣām api viśeṣeṇa pūjā kāryā yathākramam
children.translated_text: must be honored especially, each in proper order.

children.text: yathā sarvaṃ suvihitaṃ na kiṃcit parihīyate ||
children.translated_text: Act so that everything is well arranged and nothing at all is left deficient.
Do this with a mind affectionate and pleased."

children.text: tataḥ sarve samāgamya vasiṣṭham idam abruvan ||
children.translated_text: Then they all assembled and said this to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>:

children.text: yathoktaṃ tat kariṣyāmo na kiṃcit parihāsyate
children.translated_text: "We shall do just as it has been said; nothing at all will be neglected."

children.text: tataḥ sumantram āhūya vasiṣṭho vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> summoned <s>Sumantra</s> and spoke these words:

children.text: nimantrayasva nṛpatīn pṛthivyāṃ ye ca dhārmikāḥ
children.translated_text: "Invite the kings on earth who are righteous,

children.text: brāhmaṇān kṣatriyān vaiśyāñ śūdrāṃś caiva sahasraśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and bring brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras by the thousands.
Bring people from all regions, honoring them properly.
Bring the heroic lord of <s>Mithilā</s>, <s>Janaka</s>, whose valor is true,
who is established in all the śāstras and likewise established in the Vedas.

children.text: tam ānaya mahābhāgaṃ svayam eva susatkṛtam
children.translated_text: Bring that illustrious man yourself, after honoring him well.

children.text: pūrvasambandhinaṃ jñātvā tataḥ pūrvaṃ bravīmi te ||
children.translated_text: Knowing him to be related from before, I mention him to you first.
Likewise, bring the lord of <s>Kāśi</s> yourself, affectionate and always speaking kindly,
of good conduct and godlike in appearance.
Likewise bring the king of the <s>Kekayas</s>, aged and supremely righteous,
the father-in-law of the lion among kings, together with his son.
Bring the greatly fortunate lord of <s>Aṅga</s>, <s>Romapāda</s>, after honoring him well,
the glorious friend of the lion among kings.
Bring the eastern kings, the kings of <s>Sindhu-Sauvīra</s>, and the rulers of <s>Saurāṣṭra</s>,

children.text: dākṣiṇātyān narendrāṃś ca samastān ānayasva ha ||
children.translated_text: and bring all the southern lords of men as well.

children.text: santi snigdhāś ca ye cānye rājānaḥ pṛthivītale
children.translated_text: And whatever other affectionate kings there are on the surface of the earth,
bring them here as quickly as possible, with their attendants and relatives."

children.text: vasiṣṭhavākyaṃ tac chrutvā sumantras tvaritas tadā
children.translated_text: Hearing that word of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Sumantra</s> then hurried

children.text: vyādiśat puruṣāṃs tatra rājñām ānayane śubhān ||
children.translated_text: and appointed excellent men there for the bringing of the kings.

children.text: svayam eva hi dharmātmā prayayau muniśāsanāt
children.translated_text: And that righteous <s>Sumantra</s> himself, by the sage's command, set out,
hurrying to assemble the guardians of the earth.

children.text: te ca karmāntikāḥ sarve vasiṣṭhāya ca dhīmate
children.translated_text: And all those work supervisors reported to wise <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>

children.text: sarvaṃ nivedayanti sma yajñe yad upakalpitam ||
children.translated_text: everything that had been prepared for the sacrifice.

children.text: tataḥ prīto dvijaśreṣṭhas tān sarvān punar abravīt
children.translated_text: Then the best of twice-born men, pleased, spoke again to them all:

children.text: avajñayā na dātavyaṃ kasyacil līlayāpi vā
children.translated_text: "Nothing is to be given to anyone with contempt, nor even carelessly."

children.text: avajñayā kṛtaṃ hanyād dātāraṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A thing done with contempt would destroy the giver; there is no doubt about this.
Then, after some days and nights, the rulers of the earth arrived,

children.text: bahūni ratnāny ādāya rājño daśarathasya ha ||
children.translated_text: bringing many jewels for King <s>Daśaratha</s>.

children.text: tato vasiṣṭhaḥ suprīto rājānam idam abravīt
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, very pleased, said this to the king:
"Tiger among men, the kings have arrived at your command.
All those excellent kings have also been honored by me according to their rank.

children.text: yajñiyaṃ ca kṛtaṃ rājan puruṣaiḥ susamāhitaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And, O king, what is needed for the sacrifice has been prepared by well-composed men.

children.text: niryātu ca bhavān yaṣṭuṃ yajñāyatanam antikāt
children.translated_text: Let your majesty now set out from nearby to perform the sacrifice at the sacrificial ground,
which is furnished on every side with all desired offerings that have been brought."
Then, at the word of both <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s>,
on an auspicious day and under an auspicious constellation, the lord of the earth set out.
Then all the best twice-born men, with <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> at their head,
placed <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s> in front and then began the sacrificial rite.

children.text: atha saṃvatsare pūrṇe tasmin prāpte turaṃgame
children.translated_text: Then, when the full year had passed and that horse had returned,
the king's sacrifice proceeded on the northern bank of the <s>Sarayū</s>.
With <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s> in front, the bull-like twice-born men performed the rite
in the great sacrifice of aśvamedha (horse sacrifice) for that very great-souled king.
The officiating priests, who had mastered the Veda, performed the rite according to rule;
according to prescription, according to proper order, and by the śāstra, they went through it.
After performing the pravargya according to śāstra, and likewise the upasad, the twice-born men

children.text: cakruś ca vidhivat sarvam adhikaṃ karma śāstrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: performed all the additional ritual work properly, according to śāstra.

children.text: abhipūjya tato hṛṣṭāḥ sarve cakrur yathāvidhi
children.translated_text: Then, having paid honor and being delighted, all those eminent sages performed, according to rule,
the rites beginning with the morning pressing.

children.text: na cāhutam abhūt tatra skhalitaṃ vāpi kiṃcana
children.translated_text: There was nothing there that had not been offered, nor anything at all that had slipped from rule.

children.text: dṛśyate brahmavat sarvaṃ kṣemayuktaṃ hi cakrire ||
children.translated_text: Everything was seen to be as if filled with sacred power, for they performed it with welfare secured.

children.text: na teṣv ahaḥsu śrānto vā kṣudhito vāpi dṛśyate
children.translated_text: On those days no one was seen to be wearied or hungry,
nor was there an unlearned brahmin there, nor one without a hundred attendants.

children.text: brāhmaṇā bhuñjate nityaṃ nāthavantaś ca bhuñjate
children.translated_text: Brahmins ate constantly, and those with protectors ate;

children.text: tāpasā bhuñjate cāpi śramaṇā bhuñjate tathā ||
children.translated_text: ascetics ate as well, and mendicants likewise ate.

children.text: vṛddhāś ca vyādhitāś caiva striyo bālās tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: The old and the sick, women and children likewise,
though eating continually, were not found to be satiated.

children.text: dīyatāṃ dīyatām annaṃ vāsāṃsi vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: "Give, give food, and various garments too";

children.text: iti saṃcoditās tatra tathā cakrur anekaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: thus urged there, they did so many times over.
Many heaps of food were seen there, resembling mountains,

children.text: divase divase tatra siddhasya vidhivat tadā ||
children.translated_text: prepared properly day after day at that time.

children.text: annaṃ hi vidhivat svādu praśaṃsanti dvijarṣabhāḥ
children.translated_text: The bull-like twice-born men praised the tasty food as properly prepared,

children.text: aho tṛptāḥ sma bhadraṃ te iti śuśrāva rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Rāghava</s> heard, "Ah, we are satisfied; good fortune to you."
Well-adorned men served the brahmins,
and others, wearing finely polished jewel earrings, attended upon them.

children.text: karmāntare tadā viprā hetuvādān bahūn api
children.translated_text: At intervals in the ritual, the eloquent and steadfast brahmins
stated many reasoned arguments as well, desiring to defeat one another.

children.text: divase divase tatra saṃstare kuśalā dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: Day after day there, skilled twice-born men on the sacrificial ground
performed all the rites as enjoined according to śāstra.
There was no member of that king's assembly there who did not know the six auxiliaries, who lacked vows, or who was not widely learned;

children.text: sadasyas tasya vai rājño nāvādakuśalo dvijaḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor was any twice-born man unskilled in debate.

children.text: prāpte yūpocchraye tasmin ṣaḍ bailvāḥ khādirās tathā
children.translated_text: When the raising of the sacrificial posts had arrived, six were of bilva wood and likewise of khadira wood;
as many again were made together with bilva, and others were of parṇin wood.
One was prescribed as made of śleṣmātaka wood, and likewise one of devadāru;
just those two were appointed there, each of a girth that could be embraced with outstretched arms.
All these were made by men who knew the śāstra and were expert in sacrifice;
for the beauty of that sacrifice they were adorned with gold.

children.text: vinyastā vidhivat sarve śilpibhiḥ sukṛtā dṛḍhāḥ
children.translated_text: All were set in place according to rule, well made and firm by the craftsmen,
all eight-sided and endowed with a smooth form.

children.text: ācchāditās te vāsobhiḥ puṣpair gandhaiś ca bhūṣitāḥ
children.translated_text: Covered with cloths and adorned with flowers and perfumes,
they shone like the radiant Seven Seers in heaven.

children.text: iṣṭakāś ca yathānyāyaṃ kāritāś ca pramāṇataḥ
children.translated_text: And bricks were made according to proper order and in due measure.
There the fire was piled by brahmins skilled in the work of the śulba rules.

children.text: sa cityo rājasiṃhasya saṃcitaḥ kuśalair dvijaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: That fire-altar of the lion-like king was built up by skilled twice-born men.
It was indeed in the form of <s>Garuḍa</s>, with golden wings, threefold and consisting of eighteen parts.

children.text: niyuktās tatra paśavas tat tad uddiśya daivatam ||
children.translated_text: Animals were assigned there, each with reference to its particular deity.
Serpents and birds too were assigned as enjoined according to śāstra,

children.text: śāmitre tu hayas tatra tathā jalacarāś ca ye ||
children.translated_text: and at the śāmitra place the horse was assigned there, as also the aquatic creatures.

children.text: ṛtvigbhiḥ sarvam evaitan niyuktaṃ śāstratas tadā
children.translated_text: All this was then assigned by the officiating priests according to śāstra.

children.text: paśūnāṃ triśataṃ tatra yūpeṣu niyataṃ tadā
children.translated_text: Three hundred animals were then fastened there to the sacrificial posts,
along with the finest jewel of a horse belonging to that King <s>Daśaratha</s>.

children.text: kausalyā taṃ hayaṃ tatra paricarya samantataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kausalyā</s>, after attending to that horse there on every side,
struck it with three knives, with the greatest joy.

children.text: patatriṇā tadā sārdhaṃ susthitena ca cetasā
children.translated_text: Then, together with that winged one, and with a well-composed mind,
<s>Kausalyā</s>, desiring dharma, stayed for one night alone.
The hotṛ, the adhvaryu, and likewise the udgātṛ joined the chief queen with the horse,
and then the parivṛktī, the vāvātā, and the other wife in turn.
Having cut out the omentum of that winged one, the self-controlled
officiating priest of the highest accomplishment cooked it according to śāstra.

children.text: dhūmagandhaṃ vapāyās tu jighrati sma narādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: The lord of men smelled the smoky scent of the omentum,
at the proper time and in the proper way, driving away sin from himself.

children.text: hayasya yāni cāṅgāni tāni sarvāṇi brāhmaṇāḥ
children.translated_text: And whatever limbs of the horse there were, all those the brahmins
All the sixteen officiating priests will duly cast them into the fire.
For other sacrifices the oblation is placed on branches of the plakṣa tree;
but for this single <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice), a portion of reed-wood is prescribed.
The <s>Aśvamedha</s> is reckoned by the brahmins, according to the <s>kalpasūtra</s> (ritual manual), as lasting three days.
Its first day is laid down as a <s>catuṣṭoma</s> rite.
The second is counted as an <s>ukthya</s>, and the following one as an <s>atirātra</s>.
Many rites prescribed there were performed, in accordance with what is seen in the śāstra.
The <s>jyotiṣṭoma</s> and the <s>āyuṣṭoma</s>, and also two <s>atirātras</s>, were carried out.
The <s>abhijit</s>, the <s>viśvajit</s>, and the great rite called <s>aptoryāma</s> were also performed.

children.text: prācīṃ hotre dadau rājā diśaṃ svakulavardhanaḥ
children.translated_text: The king, increaser of his own lineage, gave the eastern quarter to the <s>hotṛ</s> priest,

children.text: adhvaryave pratīcīṃ tu brahmaṇe dakṣiṇāṃ diśam ||
children.translated_text: the western quarter to the <s>adhvaryu</s>, and the southern quarter to the <s>brahman</s> priest.
Likewise he gave the northern quarter to the <s>udgātṛ</s>; this was the sacrificial fee that had been ordained.
In the great sacrifice of the <s>Aśvamedha</s>, it had been so prescribed of old by <s>Svayambhū</s>.

children.text: kratuṃ samāpya tu tadā nyāyataḥ puruṣarṣabhaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, having duly completed the sacrifice, that bull among men,

children.text: ṛtvigbhyo hi dadau rājā dharāṃ tāṃ kratuvardhanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king, promoter of the rite, gave that earth to the officiating priests.

children.text: ṛtvijas tv abruvan sarve rājānaṃ gatakalmaṣam
children.translated_text: But all the officiating priests said to the king, who was free from stain:

children.text: bhavān eva mahīṃ kṛtsnām eko rakṣitum arhati ||
children.translated_text: "You alone are fit to protect the whole earth.

children.text: na bhūmyā kāryam asmākaṃ na hi śaktāḥ sma pālane
children.translated_text: We have no use for land, for we are not capable of governing it.

children.text: ratāḥ svādhyāyakaraṇe vayaṃ nityaṃ hi bhūmipa
children.translated_text: We are always devoted to the performance of sacred recitation, O protector of the earth.

children.text: niṣkrayaṃ kiṃcid eveha prayacchatu bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore let Your Majesty grant us some substitute payment here."

children.text: gavāṃ śatasahasrāṇi daśa tebhyo dadau nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: The king gave them ten hundred-thousands of cows,
ten crores of gold, and four times as much silver.

children.text: ṛtvijas tu tataḥ sarve pradaduḥ sahitā vasu
children.translated_text: Then all the officiating priests together handed over the wealth
to the sage <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s> and to wise <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.

children.text: tatas te nyāyataḥ kṛtvā pravibhāgaṃ dvijottamāḥ
children.translated_text: Then those best of twice-born men, having made a fair division according to rule,
all replied, their minds well pleased and greatly delighted.

children.text: tataḥ prītamanā rājā prāpya yajñam anuttamam
children.translated_text: Then the king, glad at heart after obtaining that unsurpassed sacrifice,
which removes sin, leads to heaven, and is hard for the best of kings to accomplish,
then <s>Daśaratha</s> the king spoke at that time to <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s>:

children.text: kulasya vardhanaṃ tat tu kartum arhasi suvrata ||
children.translated_text: "O you of excellent vow, you should now perform what will increase my lineage."

children.text: tatheti ca sa rājānam uvāca dvijasattamaḥ
children.translated_text: "So be it," that best of twice-born men said to the king.

children.text: bhaviṣyanti sutā rājaṃś catvāras te kulodvahāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Four sons will be born to you, O king, upholders of your lineage."

children.text: medhāvī tu tato dhyātvā sa kiṃcid idam uttamam
children.translated_text: Then the intelligent one, having meditated for a while on this excellent matter,

children.text: labdhasaṃjñas tatas taṃ tu vedajño nṛpam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: and then regaining full awareness, the knower of the Veda spoke to the king:
"I shall perform for you a son-producing <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering rite), for the sake of sons,
made effective according to rule by the mantras taught in the <s>Atharvaśiras</s>."

children.text: tataḥ prākramad iṣṭiṃ tāṃ putrīyāṃ putrakāraṇāt
children.translated_text: Then he began that son-producing <s>iṣṭi</s>, for the sake of sons,
and the brilliant one offered oblations in the fire by a rite seen by the mantras.

children.text: tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the gods, together with the gandharvas, the siddhas, and the supreme seers,
assembled according to rule in order to receive their portions.

children.text: tāḥ sametya yathānyāyaṃ tasmin sadasi devatāḥ
children.translated_text: Having assembled properly in that sacrificial session, those deities
spoke a weighty word to <s>Brahmā</s>, the maker of the worlds:
"Blessed lord, through your favor a rākṣasa named <s>Rāvaṇa</s>

children.text: sarvānno bādhate vīryāc chāsituṃ taṃ na śaknumaḥ ||
children.translated_text: oppresses all of us by his might, and we cannot restrain him.

children.text: tvayā tasmai varo dattaḥ prītena bhagavan purā
children.translated_text: A boon was formerly given to him by you when you were pleased, blessed lord;

children.text: mānayantaś ca taṃ nityaṃ sarvaṃ tasya kṣamāmahe ||
children.translated_text: and, continually honoring that boon, we endure everything from him.

children.text: udvejayati lokāṃs trīn ucchritān dveṣṭi durmatiḥ
children.translated_text: That evil-minded one agitates the three worlds and hates those who are exalted.
He wishes to assault <s>Śakra</s>, the king of the thirty gods.

children.text: ṛṣīn yakṣān sagandharvān asurān brāhmaṇāṃs tathā
children.translated_text: The irresistible one transgresses against seers, yakṣas, gandharvas,
asuras, and brahmins as well, deluded by the granting of the boon.

children.text: nainaṃ sūryaḥ pratapati pārśve vāti na mārutaḥ
children.translated_text: The sun does not burn him, and the wind does not blow beside him.

children.text: calormimālī taṃ dṛṣṭvā samudro 'pi na kampate ||
children.translated_text: Even the ocean, garlanded with moving waves, does not tremble when it sees him.

children.text: tan manan no bhayaṃ tasmād rākṣasād ghoradarśanāt
children.translated_text: Therefore great fear has come upon us from that terrifying rākṣasa.

children.text: vadhārthaṃ tasya bhagavann upāyaṃ kartum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: Blessed lord, you should devise a means for his destruction."

children.text: evam uktaḥ suraiḥ sarvaiś cintayitvā tato 'bravīt
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by all the gods, he thought for a while and then spoke:
"Ah, a means has been ordained for the killing of that evil-souled one.
He declared, 'I am not to be killed by gandharvas, yakṣas, gods,

children.text: avadhyo 'smīti vāg uktā tathety uktaṃ ca tan mayā ||
children.translated_text: dānavas, or rākṣasas,' and I said to him, 'So be it.'

children.text: nākīrtayad avajñānāt tad rakṣo mānuṣāṃs tadā
children.translated_text: Out of contempt, that rākṣasa did not mention human beings then.

children.text: tasmāt sa mānuṣād vadhyo mṛtyur nānyo 'sya vidyate ||
children.translated_text: Therefore he is killable by a human; no other death is found for him."

children.text: etac chrutvā priyaṃ vākyaṃ brahmaṇā samudāhṛtam
children.translated_text: Hearing this pleasing word spoken by <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: devā maharṣayaḥ sarve prahṛṣṭās te 'bhavaṃs tadā ||
children.translated_text: the gods and all the great seers became delighted then.
Meanwhile <s>Viṣṇu</s>, of great splendor, arrived,

children.text: brahmaṇā ca samāgamya tatra tasthau samāhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, meeting with <s>Brahmā</s>, stood there composed.

children.text: tam abruvan surāḥ sarve samabhiṣṭūya saṃnatāḥ
children.translated_text: All the gods addressed him, bowing down after praising him:
"We shall appoint you, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, because we desire the welfare of the worlds.
O lord, of King <s>Daśaratha</s>, ruler of <s>Ayodhyā</s>,
who knows <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), who is generous, and whose splendor equals that of the great seers,
among his three wives, who are like modesty, prosperity, and fame,

children.text: tatra tvaṃ mānuṣo bhūtvā pravṛddhaṃ lokakaṇṭakam
children.translated_text: there become human, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and in battle kill <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: avadhyaṃ daivatair viṣṇo samare jahi rāvaṇam ||
children.translated_text: that grown thorn of the worlds, who is invulnerable to the deities.

children.text: sa hi devān sagandharvān siddhāṃś ca ṛṣisattamān
children.translated_text: For that foolish rākṣasa <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, swollen with the arrogance of his strength,
oppresses the gods together with the gandharvas, the siddhas, and the best of seers.

children.text: tad uddhataṃ rāvaṇam ṛddhatejasaṃ pravṛddhadarpaṃ tridaśeśvaradviṣam
children.translated_text: Therefore that arrogant <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, rich in growing power, swollen with pride, and hostile to the lord of the thirty gods...

children.text: virāvaṇaṃ sādhu tapasvikaṇṭakaṃ tapasvinām uddhara taṃ bhayāvaham ||
children.translated_text: Destroy <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the thorn of ascetics, the fearsome one who afflicts ascetics.
Then <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, appointed by the best of the gods,

children.text: jānann api surān evaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: though he knew the gods' intent, spoke these smooth words to them:

children.text: upāyaḥ ko vadhe tasya rākṣasādhipateḥ surāḥ
children.translated_text: "What is the means, gods, for killing that lord of rākṣasas,

children.text: yam ahaṃ taṃ samāsthāya nihanyām ṛṣikaṇṭakam ||
children.translated_text: by resorting to which I may slay that thorn of sages?"

children.text: evam uktāḥ surāḥ sarve pratyūcur viṣṇum avyayam
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, all the gods replied to imperishable <s>Viṣṇu</s>:

children.text: mānuṣīṃ tanum āsthāya rāvaṇaṃ jahi saṃyuge ||
children.translated_text: "Assume a human body and kill <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle.

children.text: sa hi tepe tapas tīvraṃ dīrghakālam ariṃdama
children.translated_text: For he performed fierce austerity for a long time, subduer of foes,
by which <s>Brahmā</s>, maker of the worlds and honored by the worlds, became pleased.

children.text: saṃtuṣṭaḥ pradadau tasmai rākṣasāya varaṃ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: Pleased, the lord granted that rākṣasa a boon:
freedom from fear from various kinds of beings, but not from human beings.
In granting the boon, he formerly disregarded humans,

children.text: tasmāt tasya vadho dṛṣṭo mānuṣebhyaḥ paraṃtapa ||
children.translated_text: therefore his death is seen to come from humans, scorcher of foes."

children.text: ity etad vacanaṃ śrutvā surāṇāṃ viṣṇur ātmavān
children.translated_text: Having heard this statement of the gods, self-possessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>
then chose king <s>Daśaratha</s> as his father.

children.text: sa cāpy aputro nṛpatis tasmin kāle mahādyutiḥ
children.translated_text: And that king too, greatly radiant, was without sons at that time;
desiring sons, the destroyer of foes performed the sacrifice for obtaining sons.
Then from the fire of the sacrificer there appeared
a great being of incomparable radiance, great in heroism and great in strength,
dark, wearing red garments, red-faced, with a voice like a kettledrum,
with tawny hair, fine moustache and beard, and excellent locks,
endowed with auspicious marks and adorned with divine ornaments,
as lofty as a mountain peak, with the stride of a proud tiger,
like the sun in appearance, like a blazing flame of fire,
holding a vessel made of heated jāmbūnada gold, with silver-edged covering,
filled with divine pāyasa, dear as a wife,

children.text: pragṛhya vipulāṃ dorbhyāṃ svayaṃ māyāmayīm iva ||
children.translated_text: grasping it in his broad arms as though he himself were fashioned by magic.
Looking upon king <s>Daśaratha</s>, he spoke these words:

children.text: prājāpatyaṃ naraṃ viddhi mām ihābhyāgataṃ nṛpa ||
children.translated_text: "Know me, king, as a man of <s>Prajāpati</s>, come here to you.

children.text: tataḥ paraṃ tadā rājā pratyuvāca kṛtāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: Then the king, with joined palms, replied at once:

children.text: bhagavan svāgataṃ te 'stu kim ahaṃ karavāṇi te ||
children.translated_text: "Blessed one, welcome to you. What may I do for you?"

children.text: atho punar idaṃ vākyaṃ prājāpatyo naro 'bravīt
children.translated_text: Thereupon the man of <s>Prajāpati</s> again spoke these words:

children.text: rājann arcayatā devān adya prāptam idaṃ tvayā ||
children.translated_text: "King, by worshiping the gods today you have obtained this.
This, tiger among men, is pāyasa made by the gods;
take it, for it produces offspring, is fortunate, and increases health.
Give it to your worthy wives, saying, 'Eat this.'

children.text: tāsu tvaṃ lapsyase putrān yadarthaṃ yajase nṛpa ||
children.translated_text: From them you will obtain sons, the very purpose for which you sacrifice, king."

children.text: tatheti nṛpatiḥ prītaḥ śirasā pratigṛhya tām
children.translated_text: Saying "So be it," the pleased king received on his head
that golden vessel, filled with the divine food and given by the gods.

children.text: abhivādya ca tad bhūtam adbhutaṃ priyadarśanam
children.translated_text: After bowing to that wondrous being, lovely to behold,
he joyfully circumambulated him with supreme delight.
Then <s>Daśaratha</s>, having obtained the pāyasa made by the gods,
became supremely pleased, like a poor man who has gained wealth.
Then that being, wondrous in appearance and supremely radiant,
having completed that act, disappeared right there.
His inner palace shone with rays of joy,
like the charming autumn sky with the rays of the moon.
Entering the inner palace, he said this to <s>Kausalyā</s>:

children.text: pāyasaṃ pratigṛhṇīṣva putrīyaṃ tv idam ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Receive this pāyasa, for it is meant to give you sons."
The lord of men then gave half of the pāyasa to <s>Kausalyā</s>,

children.text: ardhād ardhaṃ dadau cāpi sumitrāyai narādhipaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the king gave half of that half to <s>Sumitrā</s>.
He gave the remaining half to <s>Kaikeyī</s> for the sake of obtaining sons,
and he gave the remaining half of the nectar-like pāyasa
after deliberation to <s>Sumitrā</s> again, the lord of the earth.

children.text: evaṃ tāsāṃ dadau rājā bhāryāṇāṃ pāyasaṃ pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: Thus the king gave the pāyasa separately to his wives.

children.text: tās tv etat pāyasaṃ prāpya narendrasyottamāḥ striyaḥ
children.translated_text: Having received that pāyasa, all those foremost women of the king
regarded it as a high honor, their hearts lifted with joy.

children.text: putratvaṃ tu gate viṣṇau rājñas tasya mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Viṣṇu</s> had entered the state of being a son of that great-souled king,

children.text: uvāca devatāḥ sarvāḥ svayambhūr bhagavān idam ||
children.translated_text: the blessed self-born lord spoke this to all the deities:
"Create strong helpers for <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who is true to his promise, heroic,
and seeks the welfare of us all, helpers able to assume forms at will.
Make them skilled in magic and brave, equal to the wind in speed and swiftness,
knowers of policy, endowed with intelligence, equal to <s>Viṣṇu</s> in valor,
unconquerable, skilled in stratagems, endowed with divine bodily strength,
possessed of every excellence in weapons, as if they had drunk nectar.

children.text: apsaraḥsu ca mukhyāsu gandharvīṇāṃ tanūṣu ca
children.translated_text: Among the chief apsarases and in the bodies of gandharvī women,
among yakṣa and nāga maidens, and among female bears and vidyādharīs,

children.text: kiṃnarīṇāṃ ca gātreṣu vānarīṇāṃ tanūṣu ca
children.translated_text: in the bodies of kiṃnarī women and in the bodies of vānarī women,
beget sons in monkey form, equal in valor."

children.text: te tathoktā bhagavatā tat pratiśrutya śāsanam
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the blessed lord, they accepted that command,
and in that way they begot sons in the form of vānaras.
The great-souled sages too, siddhas, vidyādharas, and serpents,

children.text: cāraṇāś ca sutān vīrān sasṛjur vanacāriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the cāraṇas created heroic sons, forest-ranging beings.
Those heroes were created by the many thousands, intent on killing <s>Daśagrīva</s>,
of immeasurable strength, bold, and able to assume forms at will.
They were handsome and very strong, resembling elephants and mountains.
Bears, monkeys, and cow-tailed apes were born very quickly.

children.text: yasya devasya yad rūpaṃ veṣo yaś ca parākramaḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever form, appearance, and valor each god possessed,

children.text: ajāyata samastena tasya tasya sutaḥ pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: from each of them a separate son was born, fully matching him.
Some, of approved prowess, were born among the long-tailed apes,

children.text: ṛkṣīṣu ca tathā jātā vānarāḥ kiṃnarīṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: and likewise monkeys were born among she-bears and among female kinnaras.
All had rocks for missiles; all fought with trees.
All had claws and fangs for weapons, and all were skilled in every weapon.
They could shake great mountains and split firm trees.

children.text: kṣobhayeyuś ca vegena samudraṃ saritāṃ patim ||
children.translated_text: With their speed they could churn up the ocean, lord of rivers.
They could tear the earth with their feet and leap across the great ocean.

children.text: nabhastalaṃ viśeyuś ca gṛhṇīyur api toyadān ||
children.translated_text: They could enter the expanse of the sky and even seize the clouds.

children.text: gṛhṇīyur api mātaṃgān mattān pravrajato vane
children.translated_text: They could even seize rutting elephants roaming in the forest,
and by their roar they could make crying birds fall down.
Of such monkeys, able to assume any form at will, were born
hundreds of hundreds of thousands of high-souled troop-leaders.
They became the best of troop-leaders and begot heroic monkeys.
Some, by the thousands, occupied the slopes of <s>Ṛkṣavat</s>.

children.text: anye nānāvidhāñ śailān kānanāni ca bhejire ||
children.translated_text: Others resorted to various mountains and forests.

children.text: sūryaputraṃ ca sugrīvaṃ śakraputraṃ ca vālinam
children.translated_text: And all those monkey-lords attended upon <s>Sugrīva</s>, son of the Sun, and <s>Vālin</s>, son of <s>Śakra</s>,

children.text: bhrātarāv upatasthus te sarva eva harīśvarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the two brothers, every one of them.
By those monkey troop-protectors, whose bodies were like masses of clouds or mountains and whose strength was great,
the earth became covered with forms of fearsome bodies, for the sake of aiding <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: nirvṛtte tu kratau tasmin hayamedhe mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: But when that rite, the horse-sacrifice of the high-souled king, had been completed,
the gods, having received their shares, returned as they had come.
The king, his consecration vows completed, accompanied by his wives,
entered the city with his servants, army, and vehicles.

children.text: yathārhaṃ pūjitās tena rājñā vai pṛthivīśvarāḥ
children.translated_text: The lords of the earth, honored by that king as each deserved,
departed joyfully to their own lands after bowing to the foremost sage.
When the rulers of the earth had gone, the illustrious king <s>Daśaratha</s>
again entered the city, placing the best of brahmins before him.
<s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s>, highly honored, departed together with <s>Śāntā</s>,
being escorted by the wise king with his retinue.
<s>Kausalyā</s> bore <s>Rāma</s>, endowed with divine marks,
a greatly fortunate son, the delight of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> line, half of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
<s>Kausalyā</s> shone with that son of immeasurable splendor,
as <s>Aditi</s> shone with <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the best of the gods.
In <s>Kaikeyī</s> was born one named <s>Bharata</s>, whose valor was true,

children.text: sākṣād viṣṇoś caturbhāgaḥ sarvaiḥ samudito guṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the very quarter of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, endowed with all virtues together.
Then <s>Sumitrā</s> bore two sons, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and <s>Śatrughna</s>,
heroes skilled in every weapon, possessed together of half of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: rājñaḥ putrā mahātmānaś catvāro jajñire pṛthak
children.translated_text: Thus four high-souled sons were born separately to the king,
virtuous, suited to him, and pleasing, like the Proṣṭhapadā constellation.
When eleven days had passed, he then performed the naming rite:
the eldest, the high-souled <s>Rāma</s>, and <s>Bharata</s>, son of <s>Kaikeyī</s>.

children.text: saumitriṃ lakṣmaṇam iti śatrughnam aparaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Sumitrā</s> he named <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and the other <s>Śatrughna</s>.
At that time <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, greatly pleased, gave them their names,
and he caused all their birth rites and other ceremonies to be performed.

children.text: teṣāṃ ketur iva jyeṣṭho rāmo ratikaraḥ pituḥ
children.translated_text: Among them <s>Rāma</s>, the eldest, like a banner, brought delight to his father;

children.text: babhūva bhūyo bhūtānāṃ svayambhūr iva saṃmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: he became still more esteemed among beings, like <s>Svayambhū</s> himself.

children.text: sarve vedavidaḥ śūrāḥ sarve lokahite ratāḥ
children.translated_text: All were knowers of the Vedas and heroes; all were devoted to the welfare of the world.
All were endowed with knowledge, and all were furnished with virtues.
But among them the greatly radiant <s>Rāma</s>, whose prowess was true,
was dearly loved by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, increaser of prosperity, from childhood onward.
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> was always dear to <s>Rāma</s>, his elder brother who delighted the world,
doing everything pleasing for him, and to <s>Rāma</s> he was like his own body.
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, endowed with prosperity, was like another life-breath outside him.

children.text: na ca tena vinā nidrāṃ labhate puruṣottamaḥ
children.translated_text: Without him that best of men could not obtain sleep,

children.text: mṛṣṭam annam upānītam aśnāti na hi taṃ vinā ||
children.translated_text: nor would he eat fine food brought to him without him.

children.text: yadā hi hayam ārūḍho mṛgayāṃ yāti rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: For whenever <s>Rāghava</s>, mounted on a horse, went hunting,
then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> followed behind him with bow in hand, guarding him.
And <s>Śatrughna</s>, younger than <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, belonged similarly to <s>Bharata</s>;

children.text: prāṇaiḥ priyataro nityaṃ tasya cāsīt tathā priyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he was always dearer than life to him, and <s>Bharata</s> was likewise dear to him.

children.text: sa caturbhir mahābhāgaiḥ putrair daśarathaḥ priyaiḥ
children.translated_text: With those four greatly fortunate beloved sons, <s>Daśaratha</s>
became supremely delighted, like <s>Pitāmaha</s> with the gods.

children.text: te yadā jñānasampannāḥ sarve samuditā guṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: When they all were endowed with understanding and furnished with virtues,
modest, famous, all-knowing, and far-sighted,

children.text: atha rājā daśarathas teṣāṃ dārakriyāṃ prati
children.translated_text: then righteous king <s>Daśaratha</s>, regarding their marriages,
began to think, together with his preceptor and kinsmen.
While that high-souled king was reflecting in the midst of his ministers,
the great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, of immense splendor, arrived.

children.text: sa rājño darśanākāṅkṣī dvārādhyakṣān uvāca ha
children.translated_text: Desiring to see the king, he said to the door-keepers,

children.text: śīghram ākhyāta māṃ prāptaṃ kauśikaṃ gādhinaḥ sutam ||
children.translated_text: "Quickly announce that I, <s>Kauśika</s>, son of <s>Gādhi</s>, have arrived."

children.text: tac chrutvā vacanaṃ tasya rājaveśma pradudruvuḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing his words, they ran to the royal palace,
all with minds agitated, impelled by that statement.

children.text: te gatvā rājabhavanaṃ viśvāmitram ṛṣiṃ tadā
children.translated_text: Having gone then to the royal residence, they reported that the sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>
had arrived to the king, the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> ruler.

children.text: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā sapurodhāḥ samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing those words of theirs, together with his purohita and with collected mind,
he went forth delighted to meet him, as <s>Vāsava</s> would meet <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: sa dṛṣṭvā jvalitaṃ dīptyā tāpasaṃ saṃśitavratam
children.translated_text: Seeing the ascetic blazing with radiance, firm in his severe vows,
the king, his face joyful, then presented him with arghya.
Having received the arghya from the king according to the rite prescribed by śāstra,
he asked the lord of men about his welfare and freedom from decline.
And after meeting <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, that foremost of sages

children.text: ṛṣīṃś ca tān yathā nyāyaṃ mahābhāgān uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: addressed those greatly fortunate ṛṣis in due order.

children.text: te sarve hṛṣṭamanasas tasya rājño niveśanam
children.translated_text: All of them, their minds delighted, entered that king's residence,

children.text: viviśuḥ pūjitās tatra niṣeduś ca yathārthataḥ ||
children.translated_text: honored there, and sat down as was proper.
Then the king, glad at heart, addressed the great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,
most generous and delighted, honoring him.
"As the obtaining of nectar, as rain in a waterless place,
as the birth of a son to a childless man from a worthy wife,

children.text: pranaṣṭasya yathā lābho yathā harṣo mahodaye ||
children.translated_text: as the recovery of what was lost, as joy at a great rise of fortune,

children.text: kaṃ ca te paramaṃ kāmaṃ karomi kim u harṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: so is your arrival. What supreme desire of yours shall I fulfill, and why am I so delighted?

children.text: pātrabhūto 'si me vipra diṣṭyā prāpto 'si dhārmika
children.translated_text: You are a worthy recipient for me, O brahmin; by good fortune you have come, righteous one.

children.text: adya me saphalaṃ janma jīvitaṃ ca sujīvitam ||
children.translated_text: Today my birth is fruitful, and my life has been well lived.
Formerly, by the word 'royal sage,' with your splendor made manifest through austerity,
you attained the state of a brahmarṣi; therefore you are to be honored by me in many ways.

children.text: tad adbhutam idaṃ vipra pavitraṃ paramaṃ mama
children.translated_text: This, O brahmin, is wondrous and supremely purifying for me,
and I have come into an auspicious field through the sight of you, lord.

children.text: brūhi yat prārthitaṃ tubhyaṃ kāryam āgamanaṃ prati
children.translated_text: Tell me what desired business has brought you here.
I wish, having been favored by you, to bring about your purpose.

children.text: kāryasya na vimarśaṃ ca gantum arhasi kauśika
children.translated_text: You should not go into deliberation about the matter, O <s>Kauśika</s>;

children.text: kartā cāham aśeṣeṇa daivataṃ hi bhavān mama ||
children.translated_text: I will accomplish it completely, for you are a deity to me."

children.text: iti hṛdayasukhaṃ niśamya vākyaṃ śrutisukham ātmavatā vinītam uktam
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech, pleasing to the heart and pleasing to the ear, spoken humbly by the self-controlled king,

children.text: prathitaguṇayaśā guṇair viśiṣṭaḥ parama ṛṣiḥ paramaṃ jagāma harṣam ||
children.translated_text: the supreme ṛṣi, famous for his virtues and glory and distinguished by virtues, entered supreme joy.
Having heard the wondrous and expansive words of that lion among kings,
the greatly radiant <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, with his hair bristling in joy, replied:
"O tiger among kings, this is fitting for you, and for no other on earth,
born in a great lineage and instructed by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.

children.text: yat tu me hṛdgataṃ vākyaṃ tasya kāryasya niścayam
children.translated_text: But as for the speech that lies in my heart, make a firm decision
about that matter, O tiger among kings; be true to your promise.
I have undertaken a vow for its accomplishment, O bull among men;

children.text: tasya vighnakarau dvau tu rākṣasau kāmarūpiṇau ||
children.translated_text: but two rākṣasas, able to assume forms at will, obstruct it.

children.text: vrate me bahuśaś cīrṇe samāptyāṃ rākṣasāv imau
children.translated_text: When my vow has been practiced many times and is near completion, these two rākṣasas,

children.text: mārīcaś ca subāhuś ca vīryavantau suśikṣitau
children.translated_text: <s>Mārīca</s> and <s>Subāhu</s>, powerful and well trained,
rain upon that altar with a flood of flesh and blood.
When the rite fixed by that vow has thus been defiled,
my labor is wasted, I lose heart, and I withdraw from that place.

children.text: na ca me krodham utsraṣṭuṃ buddhir bhavati pārthiva
children.translated_text: Nor, O king, does my mind turn to releasing anger;

children.text: tathābhūtā hi sā caryā na śāpas tatra mucyate ||
children.translated_text: for that practice is such that no curse may be uttered there.
O tiger among kings, you should give me your own son <s>Rāma</s>, whose valor is true,

children.text: kākapakṣadharaṃ śūraṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ me dātum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: the heroic eldest boy who still wears side-locks.

children.text: śakto hy eṣa mayā gupto divyena svena tejasā
children.translated_text: For he, protected by me and by his own divine splendor, is able

children.text: rākṣasā ye vikartāras teṣām api vināśane ||
children.translated_text: to destroy those rākṣasas who are disfiguring the rite.

children.text: śreyaś cāsmai pradāsyāmi bahurūpaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: And I shall bestow many kinds of benefit upon him; there is no doubt,

children.text: trayāṇām api lokānāṃ yena khyātiṃ gamiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: by which he will attain renown throughout all three worlds.

children.text: na ca tau rāmam āsādya śaktau sthātuṃ kathaṃcana
children.translated_text: Those two, having encountered <s>Rāma</s>, will not be able to stand in any way,

children.text: na ca tau rāghavād anyo hantum utsahate pumān ||
children.translated_text: and no man other than the <s>Rāghava</s> is able to kill them.

children.text: vīryotsiktau hi tau pāpau kālapāśavaśaṃ gatau
children.translated_text: For those two sinners, swollen with valor, have come under the noose of time;
they are no match for great-souled <s>Rāma</s>, O tiger among kings.

children.text: na ca putrakṛtaṃ snehaṃ kartum arhasi pārthiva
children.translated_text: You should not act from affection for your son, O king.

children.text: ahaṃ te pratijānāmi hatau tau viddhi rākṣasau ||
children.translated_text: I promise you: know those two rākṣasas to be already slain.
I know great-souled <s>Rāma</s>, whose valor is true,

children.text: vasiṣṭho 'pi mahātejā ye ceme tapasi sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: as does the greatly radiant <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, and these others established in austerity.

children.text: yadi te dharmalābhaṃ ca yaśaś ca paramaṃ bhuvi
children.translated_text: If you desire the gain of <s>dharma</s> and supreme fame on earth,

children.text: sthiram icchasi rājendra rāmaṃ me dātum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: firm and lasting, O lord of kings, you should give <s>Rāma</s> to me.

children.text: yady abhyanujñāṃ kākutstha dadate tava mantriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: If your ministers, all headed by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,
grant their approval, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, then send <s>Rāma</s> forth.
You should give your son, unattached and intended for my purpose,
the lotus-eyed <s>Rāma</s>, for the ten nights of the sacrifice.

children.text: nātyeti kālo yajñasya yathāyaṃ mama rāghava
children.translated_text: Let the time of my sacrifice not pass away, O <s>Rāghava</s>;

children.text: tathā kuruṣva bhadraṃ te mā ca śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: act in such a way. May it be well with you, and do not set your mind on grief."

children.text: ity evam uktvā dharmātmā dharmārthasahitaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken words joined with <s>dharma</s> and practical purpose,
the righteous, greatly radiant great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s> fell silent.

children.text: iti hṛdayamanovidāraṇaṃ munivacanaṃ tad atīva śuśruvān
children.translated_text: Hearing that sage's word, which tore at his heart and mind,

children.text: narapatir agamad bhayaṃ mahad vyathitamanāḥ pracacāla cāsanāt ||
children.translated_text: the king went into great fear; distressed in mind, he trembled from his seat.
Hearing that utterance of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, O tiger among kings,

children.text: muhūrtam iva niḥsaṃjñaḥ saṃjñāvān idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: he was as if senseless for a moment; then, regaining consciousness, he said this:
"My lotus-eyed <s>Rāma</s> is not yet sixteen years old.

children.text: na yuddhayogyatām asya paśyāmi saha rākṣasaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: I do not see his fitness for battle with rākṣasas.

children.text: iyam akṣauhiṇī pūrṇā yasyāhaṃ patir īśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Here is a full akṣauhiṇī army, of which I am the master and lord."

children.text: anayā saṃvṛto gatvā yoddhāhaṃ tair niśācaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Going there surrounded by this force, I myself shall fight those night-wanderers.

children.text: ime śūrāś ca vikrāntā bhṛtyā me 'straviśāradāḥ
children.translated_text: And these brave and valiant servants of mine are skilled in weapons.

children.text: yogyā rakṣogaṇair yoddhuṃ na rāmaṃ netum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: They are fit to fight the hosts of rākṣasas; you should not take <s>Rāma</s>.
I myself, bow in hand, will be the protector at the forefront of battle.

children.text: yāvat prāṇān dhariṣyāmi tāvad yotsye niśācaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: As long as I hold my life, so long will I fight the night-wanderers.
That excellent vow of yours will be free from obstruction and well protected.

children.text: ahaṃ tatra gamiṣyāmi na rāma netum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: I shall go there; you should not take <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: bālo hy akṛtavidyaś ca na ca vetti balābalam
children.translated_text: For he is a boy, untrained, and he does not know strength and weakness.
He is not endowed with the power of weapons, nor is he skilled in war.

children.text: na cāsau rakṣasāṃ yogyaḥ kūṭayuddhā hi te dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: He is not fit to face the rākṣasas, for they certainly fight by deceit.

children.text: viprayukto hi rāmeṇa muhūrtam api notsahe
children.translated_text: Separated from <s>Rāma</s>, I cannot bear to live even for a moment,

children.text: jīvituṃ muniśārdūla na rāmaṃ netum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: tiger among sages; you should not take <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: yadi vā rāghavaṃ brahman netum icchasi suvrata
children.translated_text: Or if, O brahman of good vows, you wish to take the descendant of <s>Raghu</s>,

children.text: caturaṅgasamāyuktaṃ mayā saha ca taṃ naya ||
children.translated_text: then take him together with me and with a fourfold army.
Sixty thousand years have passed since I was born, O <s>Kauśika</s>,

children.text: duḥkhenotpāditaś cāyaṃ na rāmaṃ netum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: and this child was begotten with difficulty; you should not take <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: caturṇām ātmajānāṃ hi prītiḥ paramikā mama
children.translated_text: Among my four sons, my highest affection is indeed

children.text: jyeṣṭhaṃ dharmapradhānaṃ ca na rāmaṃ netum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: for the eldest, who is devoted above all to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order); you should not take <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: kiṃvīryā rākṣasās te ca kasya putrāś ca ke ca te
children.translated_text: What is the valor of those rākṣasas? Whose sons are they, and who are they?
What is their measure of strength, and who protects them, bull among sages?

children.text: kathaṃ ca pratikartavyaṃ teṣāṃ rāmeṇa rakṣasām
children.translated_text: How should <s>Rāma</s> act against those rākṣasas,

children.text: māmakair vā balair brahman mayā vā kūṭayodhinām ||
children.translated_text: or how should my forces, O brahman, or I myself act against those deceitful fighters?

children.text: sarvaṃ me śaṃsa bhagavan kathaṃ teṣāṃ mayā raṇe
children.translated_text: Tell me everything, blessed one: how must I stand against them in battle,
those wicked-minded ones? For the rākṣasas are swollen with valor.
Hearing that speech of his, <s>Viśvāmitra</s> replied:
"There is a rākṣasa named <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, born from the lineage of <s>Pulastya</s>.

children.text: sa brahmaṇā dattavaras trailokyaṃ bādhate bhṛśam
children.translated_text: Having received a boon from <s>Brahmā</s>, he greatly afflicts the three worlds,
mighty and very heroic, surrounded by many rākṣasas.
Indeed <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the lord of rākṣasas, is heard to be of great valor,
the very brother of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> and son of the sage <s>Viśravas</s>.

children.text: yadā svayaṃ na yajñasya vighnakartā mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: When that mighty one does not himself obstruct the sacrifice,

children.text: tena saṃcoditau tau tu rākṣasau sumahābalau
children.translated_text: then, urged on by him, those two very powerful rākṣasas,

children.text: mārīcaś ca subāhuś ca yajñavighnaṃ kariṣyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mārīca</s> and <s>Subāhu</s>, will bring about the obstruction of the sacrifice."

children.text: ity ukto muninā tena rājovāca muniṃ tadā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by that sage, the king then said to the sage:

children.text: na hi śakto 'smi saṃgrāme sthātuṃ tasya durātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "I am not able to stand in battle against that evil-minded one.

children.text: sa tvaṃ prasādaṃ dharmajña kuruṣva mama putrake
children.translated_text: Therefore, knower of <s>dharma</s>, show favor to my little son.
Gods, dānavas, gandharvas, yakṣas, birds, and serpents

children.text: na śaktā rāvaṇaṃ soḍhuṃ kiṃ punar mānavā yudhi
children.translated_text: are not able to withstand <s>Rāvaṇa</s>; how much less human beings in battle?

children.text: sa hi vīryavatāṃ vīryam ādatte yudhi rākṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For that rākṣasa draws away the valor of the valorous in battle.

children.text: tena cāhaṃ na śakto 'smi saṃyoddhuṃ tasya vā balaiḥ
children.translated_text: Because of him, I am not able to fight him or his forces,

children.text: sabalo vā muniśreṣṭha sahito vā mamātmajaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether with my army, best of sages, or together with my sons.
In no way will I give my little son, godlike but unskilled in battles,

children.text: bālaṃ me tanayaṃ brahman naiva dāsyāmi putrakam ||
children.translated_text: my child, O brahman, to you.
And those two sons of <s>Sunda</s> and <s>Upasunda</s>, like death in battle,

children.text: yajñavighnakarau tau te naiva dāsyāmi putrakam ||
children.translated_text: who obstruct your sacrifice: to them I will certainly not give my little son.

children.text: mārīcaś ca subāhuś ca vīryavantau suśikṣitau
children.translated_text: <s>Mārīca</s> and <s>Subāhu</s> are valorous and well trained;
against either of them I would become a fighter, together with my circle of friends."
Hearing that speech of his, its syllables confused by affection,
<s>Kauśika</s>, angry, answered the lord of the earth with these words:

children.text: pūrvam arthaṃ pratiśrutya pratijñāṃ hātum icchasi
children.translated_text: "Having first promised this matter, you now wish to abandon your pledge.
This reversal is unworthy of the family of the descendants of <s>Raghu</s>.

children.text: yad idaṃ te kṣamaṃ rājan gamiṣyāmi yathāgatam
children.translated_text: If this is what seems proper to you, king, I shall go as I came.
False to your promise, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, be happy with your kinsmen."
As the wise <s>Viśvāmitra</s> was overcome with anger,

children.text: cacāla vasudhā kṛtsnā viveśa ca bhayaṃ surān ||
children.translated_text: the whole earth trembled, and fear entered the gods.

children.text: trastarūpaṃ tu vijñāya jagat sarvaṃ mahān ṛṣiḥ
children.translated_text: Perceiving that the whole world was terrified, the great sage,

children.text: nṛpatiṃ suvrato dhīro vasiṣṭho vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: the firm and true-vowed <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, spoke to the king:

children.text: ikṣvākūṇāṃ kule jātaḥ sākṣād dharma ivāparaḥ
children.translated_text: "Born in the family of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s>, like another <s>Dharma</s> embodied,

children.text: dhṛtimānsuvrataḥ śrīmān na dharmaṃ hātum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: steadfast, true-vowed, and glorious, you should not abandon <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: triṣu lokeṣu vikhyāto dharmātmā iti rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: The descendant of <s>Raghu</s> is famed in the three worlds as righteous-souled;
therefore take up your own <s>dharma</s>; you should not bear unrighteousness.
For one who has promised, 'I will do thus,' and then does not do it, O descendant of <s>Raghu</s>,
there would be destruction of sacrifices and meritorious works. Therefore send <s>Rāma</s> forth.

children.text: kṛtāstram akṛtāstraṃ vā nainaṃ śakṣyanti rākṣasāḥ
children.translated_text: Whether he has mastered weapons or not, the rākṣasas will not be able to overcome him,
protected by the son of <s>Kuśika</s>, just as nectar is protected by fire.

children.text: eṣa vigrahavān dharma eṣa vīryavatāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: He is <s>dharma</s> in embodied form; he is the best of the valorous.

children.text: eṣa buddhyādhiko loke tapasaś ca parāyaṇam ||
children.translated_text: He is superior in wisdom in the world, and the supreme goal of austerity.
He knows the various weapons in the three worlds, with all that moves and does not move.

children.text: nainam anyaḥ pumān vetti na ca vetsyanti kecana ||
children.translated_text: No other man knows them, nor will any know them.

children.text: na devā narṣayaḥ kecin nāsurā na ca rākṣasāḥ
children.translated_text: Not the gods, nor any seers, nor the asuras, nor the rākṣasas,
nor the foremost gandharvas and yakṣas, together with kiṃnaras and great serpents, know them.
All the weapons, the sons of the highly righteous <s>Kṛśāśva</s>,

children.text: kauśikāya purā dattā yadā rājyaṃ praśāsati ||
children.translated_text: were formerly given to <s>Kauśika</s> when he was ruling his kingdom.
Those sons of <s>Kṛśāśva</s> too, born from the daughter of a son of <s>Prajāpati</s>,
are of manifold forms, very powerful, blazing, and bringers of victory."

children.text: jayā ca suprabhā caiva dakṣakanye sumadhyame
children.translated_text: <s>Jayā</s> and <s>Suprabhā</s>, O fair-waisted one, were daughters of <s>Dakṣa</s>.
They bore a hundred astras and śastras, supremely radiant.

children.text: pañcāśataṃ sutāṃl lebhe jayā nāma varān purā
children.translated_text: In ancient times the one named <s>Jayā</s> obtained fifty excellent sons,
immeasurable, able to assume forms at will, for the destruction of the armies of the asuras.
<s>Suprabhā</s> also again gave birth to fifty sons,
called the <s>Saṃhāras</s>, hard to assail, hard to overpower, and mighty.

children.text: tāni cāstrāṇi vetty eṣa yathāvat kuśikātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: This son of <s>Kuśika</s> knows those astras exactly as they are,

children.text: apūrvāṇāṃ ca janane śakto bhūyaś ca dharmavit ||
children.translated_text: and, knowing <s>dharma</s>, he is also able to generate unprecedented ones besides.
Such is the power, great splendor, and great austerity of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>;

children.text: na rāmagamane rājan saṃśayaṃ gantum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: therefore, O king, you should have no doubt about <s>Rāma</s>'s going.

children.text: tathā vasiṣṭhe bruvati rājā daśarathaḥ sutam
children.translated_text: When <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> had spoken in this way, king <s>Daśaratha</s>
called his son <s>Rāma</s>, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, his face bright with joy.
His mother, his father <s>Daśaratha</s>,
and the family priest <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> had performed rites of blessing for him and consecrated him with auspicious formulas.

children.text: sa putraṃ mūrdhny upāghrāya rājā daśarathaḥ priyam
children.translated_text: King <s>Daśaratha</s> smelled his dear son's head
and, with his inmost heart well pleased, handed him over to the son of <s>Kuśika</s>.

children.text: tato vāyuḥ sukhasparśo virajasko vavau tadā
children.translated_text: Then a dustless wind, pleasant to the touch, blew at that time,
when it saw lotus-eyed <s>Rāma</s> gone to <s>Viśvāmitra</s>.
There was a great shower of flowers and the sound of divine drums,
and the blare of conches and kettledrums as the great-souled one set out.

children.text: viśvāmitro yayāv agre tato rāmo mahāyaśāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Viśvāmitra</s> went in front; then the greatly renowned <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: kākapakṣadharo dhanvī taṃ ca saumitrir anvagāt ||
children.translated_text: wearing side-locks like crow's wings and bearing a bow, followed him, and <s>Saumitri</s> followed as well.
The two, with quivers and bows in hand, made the ten directions shine.
They followed the great-souled <s>Viśvāmitra</s> like two three-headed serpents,
unwearied, as the two <s>Aśvins</s> might follow the grandsire.
Wearing iguana-hide finger-guards and bearing swords, the two were of great brilliance,

children.text: sthāṇuṃ devam ivācintyaṃ kumārāv iva pāvakī ||
children.translated_text: like the inconceivable god <s>Sthāṇu</s>, or like the two sons of <s>Pāvaka</s>.
After going a yojana and a half on the southern bank of the <s>Sarayū</s>,
<s>Viśvāmitra</s> addressed him in sweet speech: "<s>Rāma</s>!"

children.text: gṛhāṇa vatsa salilaṃ mā bhūt kālasya paryayaḥ
children.translated_text: "Take water, child; let there be no lapse of the proper time.

children.text: mantragrāmaṃ gṛhāṇa tvaṃ balām atibalāṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: Receive the whole body of mantras, namely <s>Balā</s> and <s>Atibalā</s>.

children.text: na śramo na jvaro vā te na rūpasya viparyayaḥ
children.translated_text: There will be no fatigue for you, no fever, and no disfigurement of your beauty;

children.text: na ca suptaṃ pramattaṃ vā dharṣayiṣyanti nairṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor will the rākṣasas overpower you, whether asleep or heedless.

children.text: na bāhvoḥ sadṛśo vīrye pṛthivyām asti kaścana
children.translated_text: On earth there is no one equal to the strength of your arms,

children.text: triṣu lokeṣu vā rāma na bhavet sadṛśas tava ||
children.translated_text: and, <s>Rāma</s>, in the three worlds there will be none like you.

children.text: na saubhāgye na dākṣiṇye na jñāne buddhiniścaye
children.translated_text: In good fortune, in courtesy, in knowledge, and in firm judgment,
no one in the world, O faultless one, is to be understood as your equal.

children.text: etadvidyādvaye labdhe bhavitā nāsti te samaḥ
children.translated_text: When you have obtained this pair of vidyās, there will be no one equal to you;
<s>Balā</s> and <s>Atibalā</s> are indeed the mothers of all knowledge.

children.text: kṣutpipāse na te rāma bhaviṣyete narottama
children.translated_text: Hunger and thirst will not arise for you, <s>Rāma</s>, best of men,

children.text: balām atibalāṃ caiva paṭhataḥ pathi rāghava
children.translated_text: as you recite <s>Balā</s> and <s>Atibalā</s> on the road, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: vidyādvayam adhīyāne yaśaś cāpy atulaṃ bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: While you study this pair of vidyās, incomparable fame too will be yours on earth.
For these two vidyās, radiant with power, are daughters of the grandsire;

children.text: pradātuṃ tava kākutstha sadṛśas tvaṃ hi dhārmika ||
children.translated_text: you are worthy, righteous <s>Kākutstha</s>, that I should give them to you.

children.text: kāmaṃ bahuguṇāḥ sarve tvayy ete nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: All these many virtues surely already exist in you; there is no doubt about that.
Yet these two, accumulated through austerity and manifold in form, will become yours."

children.text: tato rāmo jalaṃ spṛṣṭvā prahṛṣṭavadanaḥ śuciḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s>, having touched water, pure and with a joyful face,
received those two vidyās from the great seer whose self was disciplined.
United with the vidyās, mighty <s>Rāma</s> shone brightly.
Having entrusted all duties owed to a teacher to the son of <s>Kuśika</s>,

children.text: ūṣus tāṃ rajanīṃ tatra sarayvāṃ susukhaṃ trayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the three spent that night there on the <s>Sarayū</s> very happily.
When the night had dawned, the great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>
addressed <s>Kākutstha</s>, who was lying on a bed of leaves:

children.text: kausalyā suprajā rāma pūrvā saṃdhyā pravartate
children.translated_text: "O <s>Rāma</s>, good son of <s>Kausalyā</s>, the early twilight is beginning.
Arise, tiger among men; the divine morning rite must be performed."
Hearing that most noble speech of the seer, the two princes

children.text: snātvā kṛtodakau vīrau jepatuḥ paramaṃ japam ||
children.translated_text: bathed, made their water offerings, and the heroes recited the supreme prayer.
Having completed their daily rites, the mighty heroes bowed to <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, rich in austerity,
and, delighted, stood near him ready to go.

children.text: tau prayāte mahāvīryau divyaṃ tripathagāṃ nadīm
children.translated_text: As those two mighty heroes proceeded, they then saw there

children.text: dadṛśāte tatas tatra sarayvāḥ saṃgame śubhe ||
children.translated_text: the divine river that flows in three paths, at the auspicious confluence with the <s>Sarayū</s>.
There was a holy hermitage of sages of fierce splendor,
who for many thousands of years had practiced supreme austerity.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā paramaprītau rāghavau puṇyam āśramam
children.translated_text: Seeing that holy hermitage, the two <s>Rāghavas</s> were deeply pleased,

children.text: ūcatus taṃ mahātmānaṃ viśvāmitram idaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and they spoke these words to the great-souled <s>Viśvāmitra</s>:

children.text: kasyāyam āśramaḥ puṇyaḥ ko nv asmin vasate pumān
children.translated_text: "Whose holy hermitage is this? What man lives here?

children.text: bhagavañ śrotum icchāvaḥ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi nau ||
children.translated_text: Blessed lord, we wish to hear, for we have the highest curiosity."

children.text: tayos tad vacanaṃ śrutvā prahasya munipuṃgavaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing their words, the foremost of sages smiled

children.text: abravīc chrūyatāṃ rāma yasyāyaṃ pūrva āśramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and said, "Listen, <s>Rāma</s>, whose former hermitage this was.

children.text: kandarpo mūrtimān āsīt kāma ity ucyate budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kandarpa</s> once had a body; the wise call him <s>Kāma</s>.
Here, as <s>Sthāṇu</s> was practicing austerity, disciplined and absorbed,
and as the lord of gods, already married, was going with the hosts of <s>Maruts</s>,
that fool assailed him, and he was met by a hum from the great-souled one.
When he was burned by the fierce eye of that great lord, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>,
all the limbs of that evil-minded one fell apart from his own body.

children.text: tasya gātraṃ hataṃ tatra nirdagdhasya mahātmanā
children.translated_text: His body was destroyed there, burned away by the great-souled lord;

children.text: aśarīraḥ kṛtaḥ kāmaḥ krodhād deveśvareṇa ha ||
children.translated_text: indeed <s>Kāma</s> was made bodiless by the anger of the lord of gods."

children.text: anaṅga iti vikhyātas tadā prabhṛti rāghava
children.translated_text: He has been known as <s>Anaṅga</s> from that time onward, O <s>Rāghava</s>;

children.text: sa cāṅgaviṣayaḥ śrīmān yatrāṅgaṃ sa mumoca ha ||
children.translated_text: and that glorious district of <s>Aṅga</s> is where he cast off his body.

children.text: tasyāyam āśramaḥ puṇyas tasyeme munayaḥ purā
children.translated_text: This is his holy hermitage, and these sages here were formerly

children.text: śiṣyā dharmaparā vīra teṣāṃ pāpaṃ na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: his disciples, devoted to <s>dharma</s> (righteous conduct), O hero; no sin exists among them.
Let us spend this night here, O <s>Rāma</s>, handsome one;

children.text: puṇyayoḥ saritor madhye śvas tariṣyāmahe vayam ||
children.translated_text: tomorrow we shall cross over, between the two sacred rivers.

children.text: teṣāṃ saṃvadatāṃ tatra tapo dīrgheṇa cakṣuṣā
children.translated_text: As they were conversing there, through vision extended by long austerity,
the sages, knowing of them, became greatly delighted and came in joy.
Offering arghya, water for the feet, and hospitality to the son of <s>Kuśika</s>,
they afterwards performed the rites of hospitality for <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
After receiving that honor, and delighting them with stories,
they stayed very happily there then at the site of <s>Kāma</s>'s hermitage.
Then, at clear daybreak, when the two subduers of foes had performed their daily rites,
they placed <s>Viśvāmitra</s> before them and came to the riverbank.

children.text: te ca sarve mahātmāno munayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ
children.translated_text: And all those great-souled sages, firm in their vows,
brought up a fine boat and then said to <s>Viśvāmitra</s>:
'Let your honor board the boat, with the princes before you;

children.text: ariṣṭaṃ gaccha panthānaṃ mā bhūt kālasya paryayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: go on an unharmed path; let there be no passing away of the time.'

children.text: viśvāmitras tathety uktvā tān ṛṣīn abhipūjya ca
children.translated_text: <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, saying 'So be it,' honored those ṛṣis,

children.text: tatāra sahitas tābhyāṃ saritaṃ sāgaraṃ gamām ||
children.translated_text: and, together with the two of them, crossed the river that goes to the ocean.
Then <s>Rāma</s>, in the middle of the river, asked the foremost of sages:

children.text: vāriṇo bhidyamānasya kim ayaṃ tumulo dhvaniḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'What is this tumultuous sound of the water being broken apart?'
Hearing the <s>Rāghava</s>'s question, which was filled with curiosity,
the righteous one explained the true cause of that sound to him.
'On Mount <s>Kailāsa</s>, O <s>Rāma</s>, there is a lake fashioned by the mind
of <s>Brahmā</s>, O tiger among men; therefore this is Lake <s>Mānasa</s>.
From that lake the river flowed forth, and it embraces <s>Ayodhyā</s>;
the sacred <s>Sarayū</s>, arising from a lake, has descended from <s>Brahmā</s>'s lake.
As it turns toward the <s>Jāhnavī</s>, this incomparable sound of it
is born from the churning of the waters, O <s>Rāma</s>; with discipline, make obeisance.'

children.text: tābhyāṃ tu tāv ubhau kṛtvā praṇāmam atidhārmikau
children.translated_text: After those two very righteous ones had made obeisance to the two rivers,
they reached the southern bank and went on with swift strides.
Seeing a forest with a dreadful appearance, the son of the best of kings,
the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> prince, asked the foremost of sages about that unbroken wilderness:
'Ah, this forest is hard to pass, sounding with hosts of crickets,
filled with fearsome beasts of prey and with birds of terrible cries.
It is filled with many kinds of birds crying out with fearsome sounds,
and is also adorned with lions, tigers, boars, and elephants.
It is crowded with dhava, aśvakarṇa, kakubha, bilva, tinduka, and pāṭala trees,

children.text: saṃkīrṇaṃ badarībhiś ca kiṃ nv idaṃ dāruṇaṃ vanam ||
children.translated_text: and with badarī trees as well. What is this dreadful forest?'
The greatly radiant great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s> said to him:

children.text: śrūyatāṃ vatsa kākutstha yasyaitad dāruṇaṃ vanam ||
children.translated_text: 'Listen, child of the <s>Kākutsthas</s>, to whom this dreadful forest belonged.

children.text: etau janapadau sphītau pūrvam āstāṃ narottama
children.translated_text: Formerly these two flourishing countries existed, O best of men,
<s>Malada</s> and <s>Karūṣa</s>, fashioned by divine construction.
Long ago, after the slaying of <s>Vṛtra</s>, O <s>Rāma</s>, when <s>Brahmahatyā</s> (the sin of killing a brahmin)
entered the thousand-eyed one, who was overwhelmed by impurity and hunger,

children.text: tam indraṃ snāpayan devā ṛṣayaś ca tapodhanāḥ
children.translated_text: the gods and the ascetic-rich ṛṣis bathed that <s>Indra</s>,
bathing him with jars and releasing his impurity.

children.text: iha bhūmyāṃ malaṃ dattvā dattvā kāruṣam eva ca
children.translated_text: Having placed here upon the earth the impurity and also the bodily kāruṣa
of great <s>Indra</s>, they then attained joy.

children.text: nirmalo niṣkarūṣaś ca śucir indro yadābhavat
children.translated_text: When <s>Indra</s> had become stainless, free from kāruṣa, and pure,

children.text: dadau deśasya suprīto varaṃ prabhur anuttamam ||
children.translated_text: the lord, greatly pleased, gave that land an unsurpassed boon:

children.text: imau janapadau sphītau khyātiṃ loke gamiṣyataḥ
children.translated_text: "These two flourishing countries shall become famous in the world,
<s>Malada</s> and <s>Karūṣa</s>, bearers of the impurity from my limbs."

children.text: sādhu sādhv iti taṃ devāḥ pākaśāsanam abruvan
children.translated_text: '"Well done, well done," the gods said to <s>Pākaśāsana</s>,

children.text: deśasya pūjāṃ tāṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛtāṃ śakreṇa dhīmatā ||
children.translated_text: seeing that honor for the land performed by wise <s>Śakra</s>.
For a long time, O subduer of foes, those two flourishing countries,

children.text: maladāś ca karūṣāś ca muditau dhanadhānyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Malada</s> and <s>Karūṣa</s>, rejoiced in wealth and grain.

children.text: kasyacit tv atha kālasya yakṣī vai kāmarūpiṇī
children.translated_text: But then, after some time, there was a yakṣī able to assume forms at will,

children.text: balaṃ nāgasahasrasya dhārayantī tadā hy abhūt ||
children.translated_text: possessing the strength of a thousand elephants.

children.text: tāṭakā nāma bhadraṃ te bhāryā sundasya dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: Her name was <s>Tāṭakā</s>, may it be well with you; she was the wife of wise <s>Sunda</s>.
Her son was the rākṣasa <s>Mārīca</s>, equal to <s>Śakra</s> in prowess.
This <s>Tāṭakā</s>, of wicked conduct, constantly destroys these two countries, O <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: maladāṃś ca karūṣāṃś ca tāṭakā duṣṭacāriṇī ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Maladas</s> and the <s>Karūṣas</s>.
She dwells blocking the road, at a distance of one and a half yojanas;

children.text: ata eva ca gantavyaṃ tāṭakāyā vanaṃ yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore one must go from here by the way where <s>Tāṭakā</s>'s forest lies.
Relying on the strength of your own arms, kill this woman of wicked conduct;

children.text: manniyogād imaṃ deśaṃ kuru niṣkaṇṭakaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by my command, make this land free of thorns again.

children.text: na hi kaścid imaṃ deśaṃ śaknoty āgantum īdṛśam
children.translated_text: For no one is able to come into a country such as this,
O <s>Rāma</s>; it has been laid waste by that terrible, unbearable yakṣiṇī.

children.text: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yathaitad dāruṇaṃ vanam
children.translated_text: All this has been told to you: how this forest became dreadful,

children.text: yakṣyā cotsāditaṃ sarvam adyāpi na nivartate ||
children.translated_text: and how everything was laid waste by the yakṣī; even now she does not desist.'
Then, hearing the excellent words of that immeasurable sage,
the tiger among men replied with auspicious speech:
'Since yakṣas are heard to possess little valor, O foremost of sages,
how does a woman hold the strength of a thousand elephants?'
<s>Viśvāmitra</s> spoke these words: 'Hear by what means she is superior in strength.'
She bears strength and power produced by the granting of a boon, though she is a weak woman.

children.text: pūrvam āsīn mahāyakṣaḥ suketur nāma vīryavān
children.translated_text: Formerly there was a great yakṣa, powerful, named <s>Suketu</s>.

children.text: anapatyaḥ śubhācāraḥ sa ca tepe mahat tapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He was childless and of pure conduct, and he performed great austerity.

children.text: pitāmahas tu suprītas tasya yakṣapates tadā
children.translated_text: Then the Grandsire, greatly pleased with that lord of yakṣas at that time,

children.text: kanyāratnaṃ dadau rāma tāṭakāṃ nāma nāmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: gave him a jewel of a daughter, O <s>Rāma</s>, named <s>Tāṭakā</s>.
And the Grandsire gave her the strength of a thousand elephants,

children.text: na tv eva putraṃ yakṣāya dadau brahmā mahāyaśāḥ ||
children.translated_text: but glorious <s>Brahmā</s> did not give the yakṣa a son.
When she had been born and was growing up, endowed with beauty and youth,
he gave the famous woman as wife to <s>Sunda</s>, son of <s>Jambha</s>.

children.text: kasyacit tv atha kālasya yakṣī putraṃ vyajāyata
children.translated_text: Then, after some time, the yakṣī gave birth to a son,

children.text: mārīcaṃ nāma durdharṣaṃ yaḥ śāpād rākṣaso 'bhavat ||
children.translated_text: named <s>Mārīca</s>, hard to assail, who became a rākṣasa through a curse.

children.text: sunde tu nihate rāma agastyam ṛṣisattamam
children.translated_text: But when <s>Sunda</s> had been slain, O <s>Rāma</s>, she wished to overpower
<s>Agastya</s>, the best of sages, together with her son.
Deeply enraged, <s>Agastya</s> said to <s>Mārīca</s>, "Take on rākṣasa-hood,"
and he also cursed <s>Tāṭakā</s>.
"O great yakṣī, man-eating, hideous, with a deformed face,

children.text: idaṃ rūpam apahāya dāruṇaṃ rūpam astu te ||
children.translated_text: having cast off this form, let a dreadful form be yours."
She, filled with resentment caused by that curse, <s>Tāṭakā</s>, overwhelmed by anger,
is laying waste this auspicious land once inhabited by <s>Agastya</s>.
O <s>Rāghava</s>, for the welfare of cows and Brahmins, kill this ill-conducted yakṣī,
this utterly dreadful one whose prowess is evil.

children.text: na hy enāṃ śāpasaṃsṛṣṭāṃ kaścid utsahate pumān
children.translated_text: For no man in the three worlds is able to kill her,

children.text: nihantuṃ triṣu lokeṣu tvām ṛte raghunandana ||
children.translated_text: defiled by the curse as she is, except you, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>.

children.text: na hi te strīvadhakṛte ghṛṇā kāryā narottama
children.translated_text: You should not feel pity because of killing a woman, O best of men.
For the welfare of the four social orders, it must be done by a prince.
This is the eternal <s>dharma</s> of those appointed to bear the burden of kingship.

children.text: adharmyāṃ jahi kākutstha dharmo hy asyā na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Kākutstha</s>, kill the unrighteous woman; for no <s>dharma</s> exists in her.

children.text: śrūyate hi purā śakro virocanasutāṃ nṛpa
children.translated_text: For it is heard that formerly <s>Śakra</s>, O king,
slew <s>Mantharā</s>, daughter of <s>Virocana</s>, who wished to destroy the earth.

children.text: viṣṇunā ca purā rāma bhṛgupatnī dṛḍhavratā
children.translated_text: And formerly, O <s>Rāma</s>, by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the firm-vowed wife of <s>Bhṛgu</s>,
the mother of <s>Kāvya</s>, who desired a world without <s>Indra</s>, was slain.
By these and by many other great-souled princes,
women devoted to unrighteousness have been killed by the best of men.
Hearing the sage's manly word, the son of the best of men,
<s>Rāghava</s>, firm in his vow, joined his palms and replied:
"By my father's verbal instruction and out of reverence for my father's word,
the word of <s>Kauśika</s> must be carried out without hesitation.
In <s>Ayodhyā</s>, among my elders, I was instructed by the great-souled

children.text: pitrā daśarathenāhaṃ nāvajñeyaṃ ca tad vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: father <s>Daśaratha</s>; that word of his is not to be disregarded.

children.text: so 'haṃ pitur vacaḥ śrutvā śāsanād brahmavādinaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore I, having heard my father's word and by the command of this speaker of sacred truth,
will perform the excellent slaying of <s>Tāṭakā</s>; there is no doubt.
For the welfare of cows and Brahmins, and for the happiness of this country,
I am ready to carry out your command too, you who are immeasurable."

children.text: evam uktvā dhanurmadhye baddhvā muṣṭim ariṃdamaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the subduer of foes grasped the middle of his bow with his fist

children.text: jyāśabdam akarot tīvraṃ diśaḥ śabdena pūrayan ||
children.translated_text: and made a sharp twang of the bowstring, filling the quarters with the sound.
By that sound the dwellers in <s>Tāṭakā</s>'s forest were terrified,

children.text: tāṭakā ca susaṃkruddhā tena śabdena mohitā ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Tāṭakā</s> too became greatly enraged and bewildered by that sound.
Fixing on that sound, the rākṣasī, overcome by anger,

children.text: śrutvā cābhyadravad vegād yataḥ śabdo viniḥsṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: heard it and rushed swiftly toward the place from which the sound had issued.

children.text: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā rāghavaḥ kruddhāṃ vikṛtāṃ vikṛtānanām
children.translated_text: Seeing her angry, deformed, with a deformed face,
and of exceedingly huge measure, <s>Rāghava</s> addressed <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:

children.text: paśya lakṣmaṇa yakṣiṇyā bhairavaṃ dāruṇaṃ vapuḥ
children.translated_text: "Look, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, at the terrifying, dreadful body of the yakṣiṇī.

children.text: bhidyeran darśanād asyā bhīrūṇāṃ hṛdayāni ca ||
children.translated_text: At the sight of her, the hearts of the fearful would split apart.
See this hard-to-assail one, endowed with the power of illusion.
Today I shall turn her back, with the tips of her ears and nose cut off.

children.text: na hy enām utsahe hantuṃ strīsvabhāvena rakṣitām
children.translated_text: For I do not wish to kill her, protected as she is by the nature of womanhood.

children.text: vīryaṃ cāsyā gatiṃ cāpi haniṣyāmīti me matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: My intention is to destroy her strength and also her power of movement."

children.text: evaṃ bruvāṇe rāme tu tāṭakā krodhamūrchitā
children.translated_text: But while <s>Rāma</s> was speaking thus, <s>Tāṭakā</s>, overcome by anger,
raising her arms and roaring, charged straight at <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: tām āpatantīṃ vegena vikrāntām aśanīm iva
children.translated_text: As she rushed on with speed, advancing like a thunderbolt,
