children.text: śareṇorasi vivyādha sā papāta mamāra ca ||
children.translated_text: he pierced her in the breast with an arrow; she fell and died.

children.text: tāṃ hatāṃ bhīmasaṃkāśāṃ dṛṣṭvā surapatis tadā
children.translated_text: Seeing her slain, terrible in appearance, the lord of the gods then

children.text: sādhu sādhv iti kākutsthaṃ surāś ca samapūjayan ||
children.translated_text: and the gods praised <s>Kākutstha</s>, saying, "Well done, well done!"
Greatly delighted, the thousand-eyed <s>Puraṃdara</s> spoke,

children.text: surāś ca sarve saṃhṛṣṭā viśvāmitram athābruvan ||
children.translated_text: and all the gods, filled with joy, then said to <s>Viśvāmitra</s>:

children.text: mune kauśike bhadraṃ te sendrāḥ sarve marudgaṇāḥ
children.translated_text: "O sage <s>Kauśika</s>, may it be well with you; all the hosts of <s>Maruts</s>, together with <s>Indra</s>,
are pleased by this deed. Show affection toward <s>Rāghava</s>.
O Brahmin, present to <s>Rāghava</s> the sons of <s>Prajāpati</s> <s>Bhṛśāśva</s>,
true in valor and sustained by the power of austerity.

children.text: pātrabhūtaś ca te brahmaṃs tavānugamane dhṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: O Brahmin, he is a fit recipient, resolved to follow you,

children.text: kartavyaṃ ca mahat karma surāṇāṃ rājasūnunā ||
children.translated_text: and a great deed of the gods is to be done by this prince."

children.text: evam uktvā surāḥ sarve hṛṣṭā jagmur yathāgatam
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, all the gods, delighted, went as they had come.
After honoring <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, then twilight set in.
Then the best of sages, pleased and satisfied by the slaying of <s>Tāṭakā</s>,

children.text: mūrdhni rāmam upāghrāya idaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: smelled <s>Rāma</s>'s head and spoke these words:
"O <s>Rāma</s>, fair to behold, let us stay here tonight.

children.text: śvaḥ prabhāte gamiṣyāmas tad āśramapadaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: Tomorrow at dawn we shall go to that hermitage-place of mine."

children.text: atha tāṃ rajanīm uṣya viśvāmitro mahāyaśāḥ
children.translated_text: Then, having spent that night, the greatly renowned <s>Viśvāmitra</s>
smiled and spoke to <s>Rāghava</s> words of sweet syllables:
"I am pleased; may it be well with you, O greatly renowned prince.

children.text: prītyā paramayā yukto dadāmy astrāṇi sarvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Filled with the highest affection, I shall give you all the weapons.
Even hosts of gods and asuras, together with gandharvas and serpents,
with these you will overpower, bring under control, and conquer as enemies in battle.

children.text: tāni divyāni bhadraṃ te dadāmy astrāṇi sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Those divine weapons, may it be well with you, I shall give you in full.

children.text: daṇḍacakraṃ mahad divyaṃ tava dāsyāmi rāghava ||
children.translated_text: I shall give you the great divine <s>Daṇḍacakra</s>, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: dharmacakraṃ tato vīra kālacakraṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Then, O hero, the <s>Dharmacakra</s> and likewise the <s>Kālacakra</s>,

children.text: viṣṇucakraṃ tathātyugram aindraṃ cakraṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: and the exceedingly fierce <s>Viṣṇucakra</s>, and likewise the <s>Aindra</s> disc.

children.text: vajram astraṃ naraśreṣṭha śaivaṃ śūlavaraṃ tathā
children.translated_text: The weapon called the thunderbolt, O best of men, and the excellent <s>Śaiva</s> trident,

children.text: astraṃ brahmaśiraś caiva aiṣīkam api rāghava ||
children.translated_text: and the <s>Brahmaśiras</s> weapon, as well as the <s>Aiṣīka</s>, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: dadāmi te mahābāho brāhmam astram anuttamam
children.translated_text: I give you, O mighty-armed one, the unsurpassed <s>Brāhma</s> weapon,

children.text: gade dve caiva kākutstha modakī śikharī ubhe ||
children.translated_text: and the two maces, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, both <s>Modakī</s> and <s>Śikharī</s>.
Blazing ones, O tiger among men, I hand over to you, O son of a king.

children.text: dharmapāśam ahaṃ rāma kālapāśaṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: I give you, O <s>Rāma</s>, the <s>Dharmapāśa</s>, and likewise the <s>Kālapāśa</s>,

children.text: vāruṇaṃ pāśam astraṃ ca dadāny aham anuttamam
children.translated_text: and I give the noose-weapon of <s>Varuṇa</s>, the unsurpassed one.
I present two thunderbolts, the dry and the wet, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>.

children.text: dadāmi cāstraṃ painākam astraṃ nārāyaṇaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: And I give the <s>Paināka</s> weapon, as well as the <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> weapon,

children.text: āgneyam astraṃ dayitaṃ śikharaṃ nāma nāmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the beloved fiery weapon, named <s>Śikhara</s> by name.

children.text: vāyavyaṃ prathamaṃ nāma dadāmi tava rāghava
children.translated_text: I give you, O <s>Rāghava</s>, the wind-weapon named <s>Prathama</s>,

children.text: astraṃ hayaśiro nāma krauñcam astraṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: the weapon named <s>Hayaśiras</s>, and likewise the <s>Krauñca</s> weapon.

children.text: śaktidvayaṃ ca kākutstha dadāmi tava cānagha
children.translated_text: And I give you two spears, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, O sinless one,

children.text: kaṅkālaṃ musalaṃ ghoraṃ kāpālam atha kaṅkaṇam ||
children.translated_text: the dreadful <s>Kaṅkāla</s> and <s>Musala</s>, then <s>Kāpāla</s> and <s>Kaṅkaṇa</s>.

children.text: dhārayanty asurā yāni dadāmy etāni sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: All these which the asuras bear, I give in their entirety.

children.text: vaidyādharaṃ mahāstraṃ ca nandanaṃ nāma nāmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the great <s>Vaidyādhara</s> weapon, named <s>Nandana</s> by name,
and the jewel of swords I give, O mighty-armed son of the best of kings.

children.text: gāndharvam astraṃ dayitaṃ mānavaṃ nāma nāmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The beloved <s>Gāndharva</s> weapon, named <s>Mānava</s> by name,
the sleep-inducing and pacifying weapons, and I give the <s>Saura</s> weapon, O <s>Rāghava</s>.
The <s>Darpaṇa</s> and <s>Śoṣaṇa</s>, and the tormenting and lamentation-causing weapons,
and the hard-to-resist <s>Madana</s>, as well as the beloved weapon of <s>Kandarpa</s>,

children.text: paiśācam astraṃ dayitaṃ mohanaṃ nāma nāmataḥ
children.translated_text: the beloved <s>Paiśāca</s> weapon, named <s>Mohana</s> by name:
receive them, O tiger among men, O greatly renowned prince.
The <s>Tāmasa</s>, O tiger among men, and the very mighty <s>Saumana</s>,

children.text: saṃvartaṃ caiva durdharṣaṃ mausalaṃ ca nṛpātmaja ||
children.translated_text: and the hard-to-resist <s>Saṃvarta</s>, and the <s>Mausala</s>, O son of a king;

children.text: satyam astraṃ mahābāho tathā māyādharaṃ param
children.translated_text: the <s>Satya</s> weapon, O mighty-armed one, and the supreme <s>Māyādhara</s>,
the dreadful one called <s>Tejaḥprabha</s>, which draws away another's splendor;

children.text: somāstraṃ śiśiraṃ nāma tvāṣṭram astraṃ sudāmanam
children.translated_text: the moon-weapon named <s>Śiśira</s>, and the <s>Tvāṣṭra</s> weapon <s>Sudāmana</s>,

children.text: dāruṇaṃ ca bhagasyāpi śīteṣum atha mānavam ||
children.translated_text: and the fierce weapon of <s>Bhaga</s>, then <s>Śīteṣu</s> and <s>Mānava</s>.
These, O mighty-armed one, are by name able to take whatever forms they wish and are very powerful.
Take them, most noble and exalted, at once, O son of a king."

children.text: sthitas tu prāṅmukho bhūtvā śucir nivaratas tadā
children.translated_text: Then, standing facing east, pure and restrained,
he joyfully gave to <s>Rāma</s> the unsurpassed collection of mantras.

children.text: japatas tu munes tasya viśvāmitrasya dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: As that wise sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s> was reciting them,
all the most precious weapons presented themselves before <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: ūcuś ca muditā rāmaṃ sarve prāñjalayas tadā
children.translated_text: And then all of them, delighted and with joined palms, said to <s>Rāma</s>:

children.text: ime sma paramodāra kiṃkarās tava rāghava ||
children.translated_text: "Here we are, most noble one; we are your servants, O <s>Rāghava</s>."

children.text: pratigṛhya ca kākutsthaḥ samālabhya ca pāṇinā
children.translated_text: Having received them, <s>Kākutstha</s> touched them with his hand,

children.text: manasā me bhaviṣyadhvam iti tāny abhyacodayat ||
children.translated_text: and directed them: "Be present to me in thought."
Then <s>Rāma</s>, glad at heart, bowed to the great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,
and, greatly radiant, prepared to depart.
Then, having received the weapons, with joyful face and purified,

children.text: gacchann eva ca kākutstho viśvāmitram athābravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kākutstha</s>, even as he was going, spoke to <s>Viśvāmitra</s>:
"I have received the weapons, venerable sir; I am hard to assail even by the gods.

children.text: astrāṇāṃ tv aham icchāmi saṃhāraṃ munipuṃgava ||
children.translated_text: But I wish to know the withdrawal of the weapons, O bull among sages."
When <s>Kākutstha</s> spoke thus, the great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,
steadfast, true to his vows, and pure, then uttered the withdrawals:

children.text: satyavantaṃ satyakīrtiṃ dhṛṣṭaṃ rabhasam eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Satyavant</s>, <s>Satyakīrti</s>, <s>Dhṛṣṭa</s>, and likewise <s>Rabhasa</s>,
the one called <s>Pratihāratara</s>, <s>Parāṅmukha</s>, and <s>Avāṅmukha</s>;
<s>Lakṣākṣa</s> and <s>Viṣama</s>, and both <s>Dṛḍhanābha</s> and <s>Sunābha</s>,
<s>Daśākṣa</s> and <s>Śatavaktra</s>, and <s>Daśaśīrṣa</s> and <s>Śatodara</s>;
<s>Padmanābha</s> and <s>Mahānābha</s>, <s>Dundunābha</s> and <s>Sunābhaka</s>,
<s>Jyotiṣa</s> and <s>Kṛśana</s>, and both <s>Nairāśya</s> and <s>Vimala</s>;
<s>Yaugandhara</s> and <s>Haridra</s>, and likewise the two crushings of daityas,
<s>Pitrya</s> and <s>Saumanasa</s>, and both <s>Vidhūta</s> and <s>Makara</s>;
<s>Karavīrakara</s>, and <s>Dhanadhānya</s>, O <s>Rāghava</s>,
<s>Kāmarūpa</s>, <s>Kāmaruci</s>, <s>Moha</s>, and <s>Āvaraṇa</s>;
<s>Jṛmbhaka</s>, <s>Sarvanābha</s>, and <s>Saṃtāna</s> and <s>Varaṇa</s>;
these shining sons of <s>Bhṛśāśva</s>, O <s>Rāma</s>, able to take forms at will.

children.text: pratīccha mama bhadraṃ te pātrabhūto 'si rāghava
children.translated_text: Receive them from me; may it be well with you. You are a worthy vessel, O <s>Rāghava</s>."
With divine, radiant bodies, embodied and bestowing ease,
they stood with joined palms before <s>Rāma</s> and spoke sweetly:

children.text: ime sma naraśārdūla śādhi kiṃ karavāma te ||
children.translated_text: "Here we are, O tiger among men; command us. What shall we do for you?"

children.text: gamyatām iti tān āha yatheṣṭaṃ raghunandanaḥ
children.translated_text: "Go as you wish," the delight of the <s>Raghus</s> said to them.
"When tasks arise, you shall give me assistance mentally."

children.text: atha te rāmam āmantrya kṛtvā cāpi pradakṣiṇam
children.translated_text: Then, after addressing <s>Rāma</s> and making a circumambulation,

children.text: evam astv iti kākutstham uktvā jagmur yathāgatam ||
children.translated_text: they said to <s>Kākutstha</s>, "So be it," and went away as they had come.

children.text: sa ca tān rāghavo jñātvā viśvāmitraṃ mahāmunim
children.translated_text: And that <s>Rāghava</s>, noticing them, addressed the great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,

children.text: gacchann evātha madhuraṃ ślakṣṇaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: speaking a sweet and gentle word as they went along:
"What indeed is this, cloud-like and not far from the mountain?

children.text: vṛkṣaṣaṇḍam ito bhāti paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me ||
children.translated_text: From here a cluster of trees shines forth; I am filled with great curiosity.
It is beautiful to see, full of deer, and exceedingly charming,
adorned with many kinds of birds speaking in pleasant voices.
We have come out, O best of sages, from the wilderness that made one's hair stand on end;
but from this I understand the pleasantness of the country.

children.text: sarvaṃ me śaṃsa bhagavan kasyāśramapadaṃ tv idam
children.translated_text: Tell me everything, blessed one: whose hermitage is this,

children.text: samprāptā yatra te pāpā brahmaghnā duṣṭacāriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: where those sinful, wicked brahmin-killers have come?"
Then, when that immeasurable one asked about that forest,
the greatly radiant <s>Viśvāmitra</s> began to explain:
"This, O <s>Rāma</s>, is the former hermitage of the great-souled <s>Vāmana</s>;

children.text: siddhāśrama iti khyātaḥ siddho hy atra mahātapāḥ ||
children.translated_text: it is famed as <s>Siddhāśrama</s>, for here the great ascetic attained success.

children.text: etasminn eva kāle tu rājā vairocanir baliḥ
children.translated_text: At that very time king <s>Bali</s>, son of <s>Virocana</s>,
having conquered the hosts of gods together with <s>Indra</s> and the companies of <s>Maruts</s>,

children.text: kārayāmāsa tad rājyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: ruled the kingdom that was renowned in the three worlds.
But while <s>Bali</s> was performing a sacrifice, the gods, with <s>Agni</s> at their head,

children.text: samāgamya svayaṃ caiva viṣṇum ūcur ihāśrame ||
children.translated_text: assembled and themselves spoke to <s>Viṣṇu</s> here in this hermitage:

children.text: balir vairocanir viṣṇo yajate yajñam uttamam
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Bali</s>, son of <s>Virocana</s>, is performing an excellent sacrifice.
Before that rite is completed, let your own purpose be accomplished.

children.text: ye cainam abhivartante yācitāra itas tataḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever petitioners approach him from here and there,

children.text: yac ca yatra yathāvac ca sarvaṃ tebhyaḥ prayacchati ||
children.translated_text: and whatever they ask, wherever and in whatever manner, he gives everything to them.
Therefore, for the welfare of the gods, resorting to the power of māyā (illusion),

children.text: vāmanatvaṃ gato viṣṇo kuru kalyāṇam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: take on dwarfhood, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and perform the highest good.

children.text: ayaṃ siddhāśramo nāma prasādāt te bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: By your favor this will become the hermitage called <s>Siddhāśrama</s>.

children.text: siddhe karmaṇi deveśa uttiṣṭha bhagavann itaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the work is accomplished, O lord of gods, arise from here, blessed one.'
Then the greatly radiant <s>Viṣṇu</s> was born from <s>Aditi</s>;
assuming the form of <s>Vāmana</s>, he approached the son of <s>Virocana</s>.

children.text: trīn kramān atha bhikṣitvā pratigṛhya ca mānataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, having begged for three steps and received them with due honor,
the soul of the worlds, devoted to the welfare of all beings, strode over the worlds.

children.text: mahendrāya punaḥ prādān niyamya balim ojasā
children.translated_text: Restraining <s>Bali</s> by his power, he gave the three worlds back to great <s>Indra</s>;

children.text: trailokyaṃ sa mahātejāś cakre śakravaśaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that greatly radiant one again placed the triple world under <s>Śakra</s>'s control.
Because this hermitage, which removes weariness, was formerly occupied by him,
I too, out of devotion, make use of this hermitage of that <s>Vāmana</s>.
To this hermitage come rākṣasas (demons) who cause obstruction.
Here, O tiger among men, those wicked ones must be killed.
Today, O <s>Rāma</s>, we shall go to unsurpassed <s>Siddhāśrama</s>.

children.text: tad āśramapadaṃ tāta tavāpy etad yathā mama ||
children.translated_text: That hermitage, dear child, belongs to you also, just as it belongs to me."
Seeing him, all the sages who dwelt in <s>Siddhāśrama</s>
leapt up again and again and at once honored <s>Viśvāmitra</s>.
They performed due worship for wise <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,
and likewise rendered guest-honor to the two princes.
Then, after the two princes, subduers of foes, had rested for a while,
the two descendants of <s>Raghu</s>, with joined palms, spoke to the tiger among sages:

children.text: adyaiva dīkṣāṃ praviśa bhadraṃ te munipuṃgava
children.translated_text: "Enter upon your consecration this very day. May it be well with you, O bull among sages.

children.text: siddhāśramo 'yaṃ siddhaḥ syāt satyam astu vacas tava ||
children.translated_text: Let this <s>Siddhāśrama</s> become truly successful; may your word be true."
Thus addressed, the greatly radiant great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>
then entered upon his consecration, restrained and with his senses controlled.

children.text: kumārāv api tāṃ rātrim uṣitvā susamāhitau
children.translated_text: The two youths also spent that night in deep composure,
and, rising at daybreak, paid homage to <s>Viśvāmitra</s>.
Then the two princes, subduers of foes, who knew place and time,

children.text: deśe kāle ca vākyajñāv abrūtāṃ kauśikaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and knew what should be said in the proper place and time, spoke these words to <s>Kauśika</s>:

children.text: bhagavañ śrotum icchāvo yasmin kāle niśācarau
children.translated_text: "Blessed one, we wish to hear at what time the two night-roamers
must be guarded against, O brahmin, so that that moment may not pass by."
As the two <s>Kākutsthas</s> spoke in this way, hastening in their desire to fight,

children.text: sarve te munayaḥ prītāḥ praśaśaṃsur nṛpātmajau ||
children.translated_text: all those sages, pleased, praised the sons of the king.

children.text: adya prabhṛti ṣaḍrātraṃ rakṣataṃ rāghavau yuvām
children.translated_text: "From today onward, O <s>Rāghavas</s>, you two must guard for six nights.

children.text: dīkṣāṃ gato hy eṣa munir maunitvaṃ ca gamiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: For this sage has entered consecration, and he will take up silence."

children.text: tau tu tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rājaputrau yaśasvinau
children.translated_text: Hearing that statement, the two glorious princes
kept sleepless watch over the ascetic grove for six days and nights.
The two heroes, alert and bearing excellent bows, attended there;
the subduers of foes guarded the best of sages, <s>Viśvāmitra</s>.

children.text: atha kāle gate tasmin ṣaṣṭhe 'hani samāgate
children.translated_text: Then, when that time had passed and the sixth day had arrived,

children.text: saumitram abravīd rāmo yatto bhava samāhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> said to <s>Saumitri</s>, "Be alert and composed."
As <s>Rāma</s>, eager in his desire to fight, was speaking thus,
the altar, together with the preceptor and officiating priest, blazed forth.
With mantras and according to rule, that sacrifice proceeded,

children.text: ākāśe ca mahāñ śabdaḥ prādurāsīd bhayānakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and in the sky there arose a great and terrible sound.

children.text: āvārya gaganaṃ megho yathā prāvṛṣi nirgataḥ
children.translated_text: Just as a cloud, spread over the sky, appears in the rainy season,
so the two rākṣasas, creating illusion, rushed forward.

children.text: mārīcaś ca subāhuś ca tayor anucarās tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Mārīca</s> and <s>Subāhu</s>, together with their followers,
came there, terrifying in appearance, and poured down streams of blood.
Seeing those two suddenly rushing down, the lotus-eyed one,

children.text: lakṣmaṇaṃ tv abhisamprekṣya rāmo vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, looking toward <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, spoke these words:
"Look, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, at these wicked rākṣasas, eaters of flesh,
shaken by the <s>Mānava</s> missile like clouds by the wind."
The greatly enraged <s>Rāghava</s> hurled the supremely noble, exceedingly radiant <s>Mānava</s> missile
at the chest of <s>Mārīca</s>.
Struck by that supreme missile, the <s>Mānava</s>,
he was flung a full hundred <s>yojanas</s> into the ocean's flood.
Seeing <s>Mārīca</s> unconscious, reeling, and crushed by the force of the cold missile,

children.text: nirastaṃ dṛśya mārīcaṃ rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: cast away, <s>Rāma</s> said to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:
'Look, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, at this cold missile, the <s>Mānava</s>, joined with <s>dharma</s> (righteous order).

children.text: mohayitvā nayaty enaṃ na ca prāṇair viyujyate ||
children.translated_text: It carries him off after stupefying him, and yet it does not part him from his life.
But these others too I shall kill: merciless, evil-acting
rākṣasas, established in sinful deeds, destroyers of sacrifice and eaters of blood.'
Then the delight of the <s>Raghus</s>, taking up the very great fiery missile,

children.text: subāhūrasi cikṣepa sa viddhaḥ prāpatad bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: hurled it at <s>Subāhu</s>'s chest; pierced by it, he fell to the ground.
Taking the <s>Vāyavya</s> missile, the greatly renowned one struck down the rest.
The supremely noble <s>Rāghava</s> brought joy to the sages.

children.text: sa hatvā rākṣasān sarvān yajñaghnān raghunandanaḥ
children.translated_text: After killing all the rākṣasas, the destroyers of sacrifice,

children.text: ṛṣibhiḥ pūjitas tatra yathendro vijaye purā ||
children.translated_text: the delight of the <s>Raghus</s> was honored there by the ṛṣis, as <s>Indra</s> had once been honored in victory.

children.text: atha yajñe samāpte tu viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ
children.translated_text: Then, when the sacrifice was completed, the great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,

children.text: nirītikā diśo dṛṣṭvā kākutstham idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: seeing the quarters free from calamity, said this to the <s>Kākutstha</s> prince:
'I have accomplished my purpose, mighty-armed one; your teacher's command has been fulfilled by you.

children.text: siddhāśramam idaṃ satyaṃ kṛtaṃ rāma mahāyaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Siddhāśrama</s> has truly been made successful, O greatly renowned <s>Rāma</s>.'

children.text: atha tāṃ rajanīṃ tatra kṛtārthau rāmalakṣmaṇau
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, having fulfilled their purpose, spent that night there,
those two joyful heroes, delighted in their inner hearts.
When the night had dawned and they had performed their morning rites,
the two went together to <s>Viśvāmitra</s> and the other ṛṣis.
Having bowed to the best of sages, blazing like fire,
the two sweet-spoken heroes spoke a sweet and noble sentence:
'Here we two servants of yours stand ready, O tiger among sages.

children.text: ājñāpaya yatheṣṭaṃ vai śāsanaṃ karavāva kim ||
children.translated_text: Command us as you wish; what order shall we carry out?'

children.text: evam ukte tatas tābhyāṃ sarva eva maharṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: When the two had spoken thus, all the great ṛṣis,
placing <s>Viśvāmitra</s> at their head, said these words to <s>Rāma</s>:
'O best of men, there will be a most righteous sacrifice
of <s>Janaka</s>, the <s>Maithila</s>; we shall go there.
And you too, tiger among men, should go with us.

children.text: adbhutaṃ ca dhanūratnaṃ tatra tvaṃ draṣṭum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: There you deserve to see a wondrous jewel of a bow.

children.text: taddhi pūrvaṃ naraśreṣṭha dattaṃ sadasi daivataiḥ
children.translated_text: For that bow, O best of men, was formerly given by the gods in an assembly,
a terrible weapon of immeasurable strength, supremely radiant at the sacrifice.

children.text: nāsya devā na gandharvā nāsurā na ca rākṣasāḥ
children.translated_text: Neither gods, nor gandharvas, nor asuras, nor rākṣasas,

children.text: kartum āropaṇaṃ śaktā na kathaṃcana mānuṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor in any way human beings, are able to string it.

children.text: dhanuṣas tasya vīryaṃ hi jijñāsanto mahīkṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: Kings, wishing to test the strength of that bow,
and mighty princes have not been able to string it.
That bow belongs to the great-souled <s>Maithila</s>, O tiger among men.
There, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, you will see it, and also a sacrifice wondrous to behold.
For that excellent bow was requested by that <s>Maithila</s>
as the fruit of a sacrifice, O tiger among men, from all the gods, fair-naved and splendid.

children.text: evam uktvā munivaraḥ prasthānam akarot tadā
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the excellent sage then set out,
with the company of ṛṣis and with the <s>Kākutstha</s> prince, after taking leave of the forest deities:

children.text: svasti vo 'stu gamiṣyāmi siddhaḥ siddhāśramād aham
children.translated_text: 'May there be well-being for you. Having achieved my aim, I shall go from <s>Siddhāśrama</s>
to the northern bank of the <s>Jāhnavī</s>, toward the rocky mass of <s>Himavant</s>.'
Then, having circumambulated the unsurpassed <s>Siddhāśrama</s>,
he began to set out, directing himself toward the northern quarter.
As that excellent sage was going, there followed him, among his attendants,
a train of about a hundred carts on the journey of the brahma-teaching ascetics.
And the groups of animals and birds dwelling in <s>Siddhāśrama</s>
followed the great-souled great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>.

children.text: te gatvā dūram adhvānaṃ lambamāne divākare
children.translated_text: After they had gone a long distance, as the sun was hanging low,
the groups of sages, composed and attentive, made camp on the bank of the <s>Śoṇā</s>.
When the sun had set, they bathed, offered oblations into the fire,
and, placing <s>Viśvāmitra</s> at their head, those men of boundless vigor sat down.

children.text: rāmo 'pi sahasaumitrir munīṃs tān abhipūjya ca
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> too, together with <s>Saumitri</s>, honored those sages
and then sat down in front of wise <s>Viśvāmitra</s>.
Then greatly radiant <s>Rāma</s> asked the great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,
that tiger among sages, filled with curiosity:

children.text: bhagavan ko nv ayaṃ deśaḥ samṛddhavanaśobhitaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Revered sir, what is this region, adorned with the beauty of prosperous forests?

children.text: śrotum icchāmi bhadraṃ te vaktum arhasi tattvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: I wish to hear; may it be well with you. You should tell it as it truly is.'
Prompted by <s>Rāma</s>'s words, the well-vowed ascetic,
the great penitent, told the whole story of that region in the midst of the ṛṣis.

children.text: brahmayonir mahān āsīt kuśo nāma mahātapāḥ
children.translated_text: There was a great ascetic named <s>Kuśa</s>, born from <s>Brahmā</s>,
and by a woman of <s>Vidarbha</s> he begot four sons like himself:
<s>Kuśāmba</s>, <s>Kuśanābha</s>, <s>Ādhūrtarajasa</s>, and <s>Vasu</s>,
endowed with brilliance and great energy. Wishing them to perform the <s>kṣatra-dharma</s> (duty of rulers),

children.text: tān uvāca kuśaḥ putrān dharmiṣṭhān satyavādinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kuśa</s> spoke to those sons, most righteous and truthful.
Hearing <s>Kuśa</s>'s word, the four men honored by the world,

children.text: niveśaṃ cakrire sarve purāṇāṃ nṛvarās tadā ||
children.translated_text: all those best of kings then founded settlements for cities.

children.text: kuśāmbas tu mahātejāḥ kauśāmbīm akarot purīm
children.translated_text: Greatly radiant <s>Kuśāmba</s> made the city <s>Kauśāmbī</s>.

children.text: kuśanābhas tu dharmātmā paraṃ cakre mahodayam ||
children.translated_text: Righteous <s>Kuśanābha</s> established the supreme city <s>Mahodaya</s>.
<s>Ādhūrtarajasa</s>, O <s>Rāma</s>, the lord of the earth, made <s>Dharmāraṇya</s>,

children.text: cakre puravaraṃ rājā vasuś cakre girivrajam ||
children.translated_text: and King <s>Vasu</s> made the excellent city <s>Girivraja</s>.

children.text: eṣā vasumatī rāma vasos tasya mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: This earth, O <s>Rāma</s>, was the dwelling of that great-souled one;
these five excellent mountains shine on every side.
The lovely river <s>Sumāgadhī</s>, famed among the <s>Māgadhas</s>, flowed there;
like a garland she shines in the midst of the five chief mountains.

children.text: saiṣā hi māgadhī rāma vasos tasya mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Indeed this is the <s>Māgadhī</s>, O <s>Rāma</s>, the dwelling of that great-souled one;
formerly frequented, O <s>Rāma</s>, with good fields and garlanded with crops.
But the royal seer <s>Kuśanābha</s>, righteous in soul, begot an unsurpassed hundred daughters
upon <s>Ghṛtācī</s>, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>.
Those young women, endowed with youth, beautiful and finely adorned,
came to the garden ground like a hundred flashes of lightning in the rainy season.

children.text: gāyantyo nṛtyamānāś ca vādayantyaś ca rāghava
children.translated_text: Singing, dancing, and playing instruments, O <s>Rāghava</s>,
they reached supreme delight, adorned with excellent ornaments.
Then those women, lovely in every limb and unequaled on earth in beauty,
having come to the garden ground, were like stars among clouds.
Seeing them, all endowed with every virtue and joined with beauty and youth,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā sarvātmako vāyur idaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vāyu</s>, who pervades all beings, spoke these words:

children.text: ahaṃ vaḥ kāmaye sarvā bhāryā mama bhaviṣyatha
children.translated_text: "I desire all of you. You shall become my wives.

children.text: mānuṣas tyajyatāṃ bhāvo dīrgham āyur avāpsyatha ||
children.translated_text: Give up the human state, and you will obtain long life."

children.text: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā vāyor akliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that statement of <s>Vāyu</s>, whose acts are unwearied,
the hundred maidens then laughed and spoke these words:

children.text: antaś carasi bhūtānāṃ sarveṣāṃ tvaṃ surottama
children.translated_text: "You move within all beings, O best of gods,

children.text: prabhāvajñāś ca te sarvāḥ kim asmān avamanyase ||
children.translated_text: and all of us know your power. Why do you slight us?
All of us, the daughters of <s>Kuśanābha</s>, are capable, O best of gods,

children.text: sthānāc cyāvayituṃ devaṃ rakṣāmas tu tapo vayam ||
children.translated_text: of dislodging you, a god, from your station; but we protect our tapas.

children.text: mā bhūt sa kālo durmedhaḥ pitaraṃ satyavādinam
children.translated_text: Let that time not come, O dull-minded one. Our father is truthful;
do not treat him with contempt. In accordance with <s>dharma</s> we await the svayaṃvara.

children.text: pitā hi prabhur asmākaṃ daivataṃ paramaṃ hi saḥ
children.translated_text: For our father is our lord, and he is indeed our highest deity.

children.text: yasya no dāsyati pitā sa no bhartā bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: The man to whom our father gives us will be our husband."

children.text: tāsāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā vāyuḥ paramakopanaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech of theirs, the exceedingly wrathful <s>Vāyu</s>,
the blessed and mighty lord, entered all their limbs and broke them.

children.text: tāḥ kanyā vāyunā bhagnā viviśur nṛpater gṛham
children.translated_text: Those maidens, broken by <s>Vāyu</s>, entered the king's house.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā bhagnās tadā rājā saṃbhrānta idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Seeing them deformed then, the king, alarmed, said this:

children.text: kim idaṃ kathyatāṃ putryaḥ ko dharmam avamanyate
children.translated_text: "Tell me, daughters, what is this? Who disregards <s>dharma</s>?

children.text: kubjāḥ kena kṛtāḥ sarvā veṣṭantyo nābhibhāṣatha ||
children.translated_text: By whom have you all been made hunchbacked? You writhe and do not speak."

children.text: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā kuśanābhasya dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech of wise <s>Kuśanābha</s>,
the hundred maidens touched his feet with their heads and spoke:
"<s>Vāyu</s>, who pervades all beings, O king, wished to violate us;

children.text: aśubhaṃ mārgam āsthāya na dharmaṃ pratyavekṣate ||
children.translated_text: taking up an evil path, he did not look to <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: pitṛmatyaḥ sma bhadraṃ te svacchande na vayaṃ sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: We have a father; may it be well with you. We are not standing in independence.

children.text: pitaraṃ no vṛṇīṣva tvaṃ yadi no dāsyate tava ||
children.translated_text: Ask our father for us, and if he gives us to you, we shall be yours.
Because of that sinful attachment, when we did not accept his words,

children.text: evaṃ bruvantyaḥ sarvāḥ sma vāyunā nihatā bhṛśam ||
children.translated_text: as we were all speaking thus, we were violently struck down by <s>Vāyu</s>."
Hearing that statement of theirs, the supremely righteous king,
the greatly radiant one, replied to the unsurpassed hundred maidens:

children.text: kṣāntaṃ kṣamāvatāṃ putryaḥ kartavyaṃ sumahat kṛtam
children.translated_text: "You have shown forbearance, daughters; a very great deed, proper for the forbearing, has been done.
Coming to one mind, you have also regarded my family.

children.text: alaṃkāro hi nārīṇāṃ kṣamā tu puruṣasya vā
children.translated_text: For forbearance is the ornament of women, and also of a man.

children.text: duṣkaraṃ tac ca vaḥ kṣāntaṃ tridaśeṣu viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: What you have forgiven is difficult to bear, especially among the thirty gods.

children.text: yādṛśīr vaḥ kṣamā putryaḥ sarvāsām aviśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Such is the forbearance in all of you without distinction, daughters.

children.text: kṣamā dānaṃ kṣamā yajñaḥ kṣamā satyaṃ ca putrikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Forbearance is giving; forbearance is sacrifice; forbearance is truth, little daughters.

children.text: kṣamā yaśaḥ kṣamā dharmaḥ kṣamāyāṃ viṣṭhitaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: Forbearance is fame; forbearance is <s>dharma</s>; the world is established in forbearance.
After dismissing the maidens, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, the king, whose prowess equaled that of the gods,
skilled in counsel, deliberated with his ministers about giving them away.
He considered the fitting bestowal of them, in the proper place and time.

children.text: etasminn eva kāle tu cūlī nāma mahāmuniḥ
children.translated_text: At that very time there was a great sage named <s>Cūlī</s>,
chaste, of pure conduct, who undertook brahmanic austerity.

children.text: tapyantaṃ tam ṛṣiṃ tatra gandharvī paryupāsate
children.translated_text: As that seer practiced austerity there, a gandharvī served him,

children.text: somadā nāma bhadraṃ te ūrmilā tanayā tadā ||
children.translated_text: named <s>Somadā</s>, may it be well with you, the daughter of <s>Ūrmilā</s>.

children.text: sā ca taṃ praṇatā bhūtvā śuśrūṣaṇaparāyaṇā
children.translated_text: She, having bowed to him and devoted herself to service,

children.text: uvāsa kāle dharmiṣṭhā tasyās tuṣṭo 'bhavad guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: dwelt there for a time, most righteous; and her teacher became pleased with her.

children.text: sa ca tāṃ kālayogena provāca raghunandana
children.translated_text: In due course he spoke to her, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>,

children.text: parituṣṭo 'smi bhadraṃ te kiṃ karomi tava priyam ||
children.translated_text: "I am pleased; may it be well with you. What dear thing shall I do for you?"
Knowing the sage to be pleased, the sweet-voiced gandharvī,
greatly delighted, skilled in speech, spoke to that master of speech:
"You are united with brahmanic splendor, become like Brahman, and are of great tapas.

children.text: brāhmeṇa tapasā yuktaṃ putram icchāmi dhārmikam ||
children.translated_text: I desire a righteous son endowed through brahmanic austerity.

children.text: apatiś cāsmi bhadraṃ te bhāryā cāsmi na kasyacit
children.translated_text: I am without a husband, may it be well with you, and I am no man's wife.

children.text: brāhmeṇopagatāyāś ca dātum arhasi me sutam ||
children.translated_text: Since I have approached you in a brahmanic way, you ought to give me a son."

children.text: tasyāḥ prasanno brahmarṣir dadau putram anuttamam
children.translated_text: Pleased with her, the brahmarṣi gave her an unsurpassed son,

children.text: brahmadatta iti khyātaṃ mānasaṃ cūlinaḥ sutam ||
children.translated_text: known as <s>Brahmadatta</s>, the mind-born son of <s>Cūlī</s>.

children.text: sa rājā brahmadattas tu purīm adhyavasat tadā
children.translated_text: That king <s>Brahmadatta</s> then dwelt in the city

children.text: kāmpilyāṃ parayā lakṣmyā devarājo yathā divam ||
children.translated_text: of <s>Kāmpilyā</s> with supreme splendor, as the king of the gods dwells in heaven.

children.text: sa buddhiṃ kṛtavān rājā kuśanābhaḥ sudhārmikaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the very righteous king <s>Kuśanābha</s> formed the intention,
O <s>Kākutstha</s>, to give the hundred maidens to <s>Brahmadatta</s>.
Calling that greatly radiant <s>Brahmadatta</s>, the lord of the earth,
the king, well pleased in his heart, gave him the hundred maidens.
Then, O <s>Raghunandana</s>, in due order he took their hands in marriage,
<s>Brahmadatta</s>, the king, lord of the earth, like the husband of the gods.
Then, as soon as their hands were touched, they were no longer bent and were free from distress;

children.text: yuktāḥ paramayā lakṣmyā babhuḥ kanyāśataṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: at that time the hundred maidens became endowed with supreme beauty.

children.text: sa dṛṣṭvā vāyunā muktāḥ kuśanābho mahīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that they had been released from <s>Vāyu</s>, King <s>Kuśanābha</s>,

children.text: babhūva paramaprīto harṣaṃ lebhe punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: became exceedingly pleased and felt joy again and again.
Then the lord of the earth sent off King <s>Brahmadatta</s>, whose marriage had been performed,
together with his wives and with the company of his priests.
<s>Somadā</s> too, greatly delighted at the fitting rite performed by her son,

children.text: yathānyāyaṃ ca gandharvī snuṣās tāḥ pratyanandata ||
children.translated_text: being a <s>Gandharvī</s>, duly welcomed those daughters-in-law.

children.text: kṛtodvāhe gate tasmin brahmadatte ca rāghava
children.translated_text: When that <s>Brahmadatta</s>, after the wedding had been performed, had departed, O <s>Rāghava</s>,
the sonless king arranged a sacrifice for the obtaining of a son.
While the sacrifice was in progress, then,
<s>Kuśa</s>, son of <s>Brahmā</s>, exceedingly pleased, spoke to King <s>Kuśanābha</s>.

children.text: putras te sadṛśaḥ putra bhaviṣyati sudhārmikaḥ
children.translated_text: 'My son, a son equal to you will be born to you, very righteous;

children.text: gādhiṃ prāpsyasi tena tvaṃ kīrtiṃ loke ca śāśvatīm ||
children.translated_text: through him, <s>Gādhi</s>, you will obtain everlasting fame in the world.'

children.text: evam uktvā kuśo rāma kuśanābhaṃ mahīpatim
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, O <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Kuśa</s> addressed King <s>Kuśanābha</s>,
entered the sky, and went to the eternal world of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: kasyacit tv atha kālasya kuśanābhasya dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after some time had passed for wise <s>Kuśanābha</s>,

children.text: jajñe paramadharmiṣṭho gādhir ity eva nāmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: there was born a supremely righteous son, known by the name <s>Gādhi</s>.

children.text: sa pitā mama kākutstha gādhiḥ paramadhārmikaḥ
children.translated_text: That most righteous <s>Gādhi</s> is my father, O <s>Kākutstha</s>;
I was born from the lineage of <s>Kuśa</s>, O <s>Raghunandana</s>, and so I am <s>Kauśika</s>.

children.text: pūrvajā bhaginī cāpi mama rāghava suvratā
children.translated_text: And I had an elder sister, O <s>Rāghava</s>, a woman of excellent vows;
by name she was called <s>Satyavatī</s>, and she was given to <s>Ṛcīka</s>.
Following her husband, she went bodily to heaven;
that supremely noble <s>Kauśikī</s> came forth as a great river.
Divine, with holy waters, lovely, and resting upon <s>Himavant</s>,
my sister flowed forth for the purpose of benefiting the world.
Therefore I dwell happily on the slopes of <s>Himavat</s>, self-restrained,
joined by affection for my sister <s>Kauśikī</s>, O <s>Raghunandana</s>.

children.text: sā tu satyavatī puṇyā satye dharme pratiṣṭhitā
children.translated_text: That holy <s>Satyavatī</s>, established in truth and in <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),
devoted to her husband and greatly fortunate, is <s>Kauśikī</s>, best of rivers.

children.text: ahaṃ hi niyamād rāma hitvā tāṃ samupāgataḥ
children.translated_text: I, O <s>Rāma</s>, because of my vow, left her and came here;
having reached <s>Siddhāśrama</s>, I have attained success through your splendor.

children.text: eṣā rāma mamotpattiḥ svasya vaṃśasya kīrtitā
children.translated_text: This, O <s>Rāma</s>, is my origin, and that of my own lineage, as I have recounted it,

children.text: deśasya ca mahābāho yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi ||
children.translated_text: and also of the country, O mighty-armed one, about which you asked me.
Half the night has passed, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, while I have been telling these tales;

children.text: nidrām abhyehi bhadraṃ te mā bhūd vighno 'dhvanīha naḥ ||
children.translated_text: go to sleep. May it be well with you; let no obstacle befall our journey here.
All the trees are motionless, and the beasts and birds have settled down;

children.text: naiśena tamasā vyāptā diśaś ca raghunandana ||
children.translated_text: the quarters too are covered by the darkness of night, O <s>Raghunandana</s>.

children.text: śanair viyujyate saṃdhyā nabho netrair ivāvṛtam
children.translated_text: The twilight slowly fades away, and the sky, as if covered with eyes,
thick with constellations and stars, shines with lights.
And the cool-rayed moon rises, the dispeller of the world's darkness,

children.text: hlādayan prāṇināṃ loke manāṃsi prabhayā vibho ||
children.translated_text: gladdening the minds of living beings in the world with its radiance, O lord.
Then all creatures of the night move about here and there,
as do hosts of <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s>, fierce flesh-eaters.
Having spoken thus, the great sage, mighty in splendor, fell silent;

children.text: sādhu sādhv iti taṃ sarve munayo hy abhyapūjayan ||
children.translated_text: and all the sages honored him, saying, 'Good, good!'
<s>Rāma</s> too, together with <s>Saumitri</s>, touched with some wonder,
praised the tiger among sages and went to sleep.
Having spent the rest of the night on the bank of the <s>Śoṇa</s> with the great seers,
when the night had become bright morning, <s>Viśvāmitra</s> spoke.

children.text: suprabhātā niśā rāma pūrvā saṃdhyā pravartate
children.translated_text: 'The night has dawned well, O <s>Rāma</s>; the early twilight is beginning.
Rise, rise. May it be well with you; prepare yourself for the journey.'

children.text: tac chrutvā vacanaṃ tasya kṛtvā paurvāhṇikīṃ kriyām
children.translated_text: Hearing his words and performing the morning rite,

children.text: gamanaṃ rocayāmāsa vākyaṃ cedam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: he approved the journey and then spoke these words:
'This <s>Śoṇa</s> has lovely water, is shallow, and is adorned with sandbanks;
by which path, O brāhman, shall we cross it?'

children.text: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa viśvāmitro 'bravīd idam
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Viśvāmitra</s> said this:

children.text: eṣa panthā mayoddiṣṭo yena yānti maharṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'This is the path pointed out by me, by which the great seers go.'

children.text: te gatvā dūram adhvānaṃ gate 'rdhadivase tadā
children.translated_text: After they had gone a long distance, when half the day had passed,
they saw the <s>Jāhnavī</s>, best of rivers, frequented by sages.
Seeing that river with holy waters, attended by swans and cranes,
all the sages, together with <s>Rāghava</s>, became joyful,

children.text: tasyās tīre tataś cakrus te āvāsaparigraham ||
children.translated_text: and then on its bank they chose a place to stay.
Then, bathing according to rule and satisfying the ancestors and deities,
offering the <s>agnihotra</s> (fire oblations), and partaking of the oblation as if it were nectar,
they entered a pure place on the bank of the <s>Jāhnavī</s>, their minds delighted,
surrounding the great-souled <s>Viśvāmitra</s> on every side.
Then <s>Rāma</s>, his mind filled with joy, said to <s>Viśvāmitra</s>:

children.text: bhagavañ śrotum icchāmi gaṅgāṃ tripathagāṃ nadīm
children.translated_text: 'Venerable sir, I wish to hear about the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, who goes in three paths;
how did she, having traversed the three worlds, go to the lord of rivers and streams?'
Prompted by <s>Rāma</s>'s words, the great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>

children.text: vṛddhiṃ janma ca gaṅgāyā vaktum evopacakrame ||
children.translated_text: began to tell of the growth and birth of <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

children.text: śailendro himavān nāma dhātūnām ākaro mahān
children.translated_text: There is a lord of mountains named <s>Himavān</s>, a great storehouse of minerals;
he had two daughters, O <s>Rāma</s>, matchless in beauty upon the earth.

children.text: yā meruduhitā rāma tayor mātā sumadhyamā
children.translated_text: Of those two, O <s>Rāma</s>, the mother was the slender-waisted daughter of <s>Meru</s>.

children.text: nāmnā menā manojñā vai patnī himavataḥ priyā ||
children.translated_text: By name she was <s>Menā</s>, charming indeed, the beloved wife of <s>Himavat</s>.

children.text: tasyāṃ gaṅgeyam abhavaj jyeṣṭhā himavataḥ sutā
children.translated_text: In her <s>Gaṅgā</s> was born, the elder daughter of <s>Himavat</s>;

children.text: umā nāma dvitīyābhūt kanyā tasyaiva rāghava ||
children.translated_text: and a second daughter of that very one, O <s>Rāghava</s>, was named <s>Umā</s>.
Then all the gods, wishing to accomplish the purpose of the deities,
asked the lord of mountains for <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the river that goes in three paths.
<s>Himavat</s>, according to <s>dharma</s> (right order), gave his daughter, the purifier of the worlds,
<s>Gaṅgā</s>, who moves by paths of her own choosing, desiring the welfare of the three worlds.
Having received <s>Gaṅgā</s> for the sake of the three worlds, those who work for the welfare of the three worlds
took her and went away, inwardly fulfilled in their purpose.
And that other daughter of the mountain, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>,

children.text: ugraṃ sā vratam āsthāya tapas tepe tapodhanā ||
children.translated_text: undertook a fierce vow and practiced austerity, rich in tapas.

children.text: ugreṇa tapasā yuktāṃ dadau śailavaraḥ sutām
children.translated_text: The excellent mountain gave his daughter, endowed with fierce austerity,
<s>Umā</s>, honored by the world, to incomparable <s>Rudra</s>.
These are the two daughters of the mountain-king, honored by the world:

children.text: gaṅgā ca saritāṃ śreṣṭhā umā devī ca rāghava ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gaṅgā</s>, best of rivers, and the goddess <s>Umā</s>, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: etat te dharmam ākhyātaṃ yathā tripathagā nadī
children.translated_text: This sacred account has been told to you: how the river that goes in three paths

children.text: khaṃ gatā prathamaṃ tāta gatiṃ gatimatāṃ vara ||
children.translated_text: first went to the sky, dear one, O best of those who have a course.
When that sage had spoken, both heroes, <s>Rāghava</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
praised the story and spoke to the bull among sages:

children.text: dharmayuktam idaṃ brahman kathitaṃ paramaṃ tvayā
children.translated_text: "This supreme, dharma-filled tale has been told by you, O brahman.
You should tell further about the elder daughter of the mountain-king.
You know the full extent of things, both divine and human in origin.

children.text: trīn patho hetunā kena pāvayel lokapāvanī ||
children.translated_text: For what reason does the purifier of the worlds purify the three paths?
How is <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the best of rivers, famed as the one who goes in three paths,

children.text: triṣu lokeṣu dharmajña karmabhiḥ kaiḥ samanvitā ||
children.translated_text: and with what deeds is she connected in the three worlds, O knower of <s>dharma</s>?"
As <s>Kākutstha</s> spoke in this way, <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, rich in tapas,
set forth the whole story completely among the sages.
"Long ago, O <s>Rāma</s>, the great ascetic <s>Śitikaṇṭha</s>, after he was married,
looked upon the goddess with desire and began to approach her for union.
A hundred divine years passed for the god <s>Śitikaṇṭha</s>,

children.text: na cāpi tanayo rāma tasyām āsīt paraṃtapa ||
children.translated_text: but still no son was born from her, O <s>Rāma</s>, tormentor of foes.
Then the gods, with the Grandfather at their head, became deeply anxious:

children.text: yad ihotpadyate bhūtaṃ kas tat pratisahiṣyate ||
children.translated_text: "If a being is produced here, who will be able to withstand it?"
All the gods approached, bowed down, and said this:
"God of gods, <s>Mahādeva</s>, devoted to the welfare of this world,
because of the gods' prostration you ought to show favor.

children.text: na lokā dhārayiṣyanti tava tejaḥ surottama
children.translated_text: The worlds will not be able to bear your fiery energy, O best of gods.

children.text: brāhmeṇa tapasā yukto devyā saha tapaś cara ||
children.translated_text: Joined with brahmanic austerity, practice tapas together with the goddess.
For the desired welfare of the three worlds, contain your fiery energy within fiery energy.

children.text: rakṣa sarvān imāṃl lokān nālokaṃ kartum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: Protect all these worlds; you ought not to make them worldless."
Hearing the words of the deities, the great lord of all the worlds

children.text: bāḍham ity abravīt sarvān punaś cedam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: said to them all, "So be it," and then again spoke these words:

children.text: dhārayiṣyāmy ahaṃ tejas tejasy eva sahomayā
children.translated_text: "I shall contain the fiery energy within fiery energy itself, together with <s>Umā</s>.
Let the thirty gods and the earth obtain relief.

children.text: yad idaṃ kṣubhitaṃ sthānān mama tejo hy anuttamam
children.translated_text: But this unsurpassed fiery energy of mine, stirred from its place,

children.text: dhārayiṣyati kas tan me bruvantu surasattamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: who will bear it for me? Tell me, best of gods."

children.text: evam uktās tato devāḥ pratyūcur vṛṣabhadhvajam
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, the gods then answered the bull-bannered one:

children.text: yat tejaḥ kṣubhitaṃ hy etat tad dharā dhārayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: "This fiery energy of yours that has been stirred, the earth will bear it."
Thus addressed, the lord of the gods released it upon the surface of the earth;
by that fiery energy the earth, with its mountains and forests, was pervaded.

children.text: tato devāḥ punar idam ūcuś cātha hutāśanam
children.translated_text: Then the gods again spoke these words to <s>Hutāśana</s>, fire:
"Enter, you of great splendor, the fierce energy, joined with <s>Vāyu</s>."

children.text: tad agninā punar vyāptaṃ saṃjātaḥ śvetaparvataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, pervaded again by fire, the white mountain arose,
and also a divine reed-thicket, resembling fire and the sun,
where the greatly radiant <s>Kārttikeya</s>, born from fire, came into being.

children.text: athomāṃ ca śivaṃ caiva devāḥ sarṣigaṇās tadā
children.translated_text: Then the gods, together with the hosts of sages, at that time
worshiped <s>Umā</s> and <s>Śiva</s> exceedingly, their minds very pleased.

children.text: atha śailasutā rāma tridaśān idam abravīt
children.translated_text: Then the mountain's daughter, O <s>Rāma</s>, spoke this to the thirty gods;
angry, with eyes reddened by wrath, she cursed them all:
"Because I was restrained when I had united with him in desire for a son,
you shall not be able to beget offspring in your own wives.

children.text: adya prabhṛti yuṣmākam aprajāḥ santu patnayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From this day onward, let your wives be without children."

children.text: evam uktvā surān sarvāñ śaśāpa pṛthivīm api
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, she cursed all the gods and also the earth:
"O earth, you shall have many forms and many husbands.
And, stained by my anger,

children.text: prāpsyasi tvaṃ sudurmedhe mama putram anicchatī ||
children.translated_text: you shall not obtain the joy that comes from a son, foolish one, since you did not wish for my son."

children.text: tān sarvān vrīḍitān dṛṣṭvā surān surapatis tadā
children.translated_text: Seeing all those gods ashamed, the lord of the gods then
began to go toward the direction guarded by <s>Varuṇa</s>.

children.text: sa gatvā tapa ātiṣṭhat pārśve tasyottare gireḥ
children.translated_text: Having gone there, <s>Maheśvara</s> undertook austerity on the northern side of that mountain,
on a peak born of <s>Himavat</s>, together with the goddess.

children.text: eṣa te vistaro rāma śailaputryā niveditaḥ
children.translated_text: This full account of the mountain's daughter has been told to you, O <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: gaṅgāyāḥ prabhavaṃ caiva śṛṇu me sahalakṣmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now hear from me, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the origin of <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

children.text: tapyamāne tapo deve devāḥ sarṣigaṇāḥ purā
children.translated_text: Long ago, while the god was practicing austerity, the gods together with the hosts of sages,
desiring a commander of the army, approached the Grandfather.
Then all the gods, with <s>Indra</s> and with fire at their head,
bowed down and spoke an auspicious speech to the blessed Grandfather:

children.text: yo naḥ senāpatir deva datto bhagavatā purā
children.translated_text: "O god, that commander of our army who was formerly granted by the Blessed One...

children.text: sa tapaḥ param āsthāya tapyate sma sahomayā ||
children.translated_text: He undertook supreme austerity and performed tapas together with <s>Umā</s>.
Whatever further action is to be done here, out of a desire for the welfare of the worlds,

children.text: saṃvidhatsva vidhānajña tvaṃ hi naḥ paramā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: arrange it, you who know proper ordinance; for you are our supreme refuge.
Having heard the words of the gods, the grandsire of all the worlds,

children.text: sāntvayan madhurair vākyais tridaśān idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: comforting the thirty gods with sweet words, spoke this to them:

children.text: śailaputryā yad uktaṃ tanna prajāsyatha patniṣu
children.translated_text: What the daughter of the mountain said, that you would have no offspring in your wives,

children.text: tasyā vacanam akliṣṭaṃ satyam eva na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: her unwearied word is indeed true; there is no doubt.

children.text: iyam ākāśagā gaṅgā yasyāṃ putraṃ hutāśanaḥ
children.translated_text: This sky-going <s>Gaṅgā</s> is the one in whom <s>Hutāśana</s> (Fire)
will beget a son, the enemy-subduing commander of the gods' army.
The elder daughter of the lord of mountains will honor that son;

children.text: umāyās tad bahumataṃ bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that will be highly approved by <s>Umā</s>, without doubt.

children.text: tac chrutvā vacanaṃ tasya kṛtārthā raghunandana
children.translated_text: Hearing that word of his, O <s>Raghunandana</s>, the gods, their purpose fulfilled,
all bowed down and honored the Grandsire.

children.text: te gatvā parvataṃ rāma kailāsaṃ dhātumaṇḍitam
children.translated_text: Then, O <s>Rāma</s>, all the gods went to the metal-rich mountain <s>Kailāsa</s>
and appointed <s>Agni</s> for the sake of obtaining a son.
O god <s>Hutāśana</s>, accomplish this work of the gods;
O greatly radiant one, cast your seed into <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the daughter of the mountain.
Having promised the gods, <s>Pāvaka</s> (Fire) approached <s>Gaṅgā</s>:

children.text: garbhaṃ dhāraya vai devi devatānām idaṃ priyam ||
children.translated_text: 'O goddess, bear the embryo; this is dear to the gods.'

children.text: ity etad vacanaṃ śrutvā divyaṃ rūpam adhārayat
children.translated_text: Hearing this word, she assumed a divine form;

children.text: sa tasyā mahimāṃ dṛṣṭvā samantād avakīryata ||
children.translated_text: and he, seeing her greatness, was scattered all around.
Then <s>Pāvaka</s> entered the goddess from every side,
and all the streams of <s>Gaṅgā</s> were filled, O <s>Raghunandana</s>.
Then <s>Gaṅgā</s> said to him, the priest of all the gods:

children.text: aśaktā dhāraṇe deva tava tejaḥ samuddhatam
children.translated_text: 'O god, I am unable to bear your overbearing energy,
for I am being burned by that fire and my mind is greatly shaken.'
Then <s>Hutāśana</s>, belonging to all the gods, said this to <s>Gaṅgā</s>:
'Let this embryo be deposited here at the foot of <s>Himavat</s>.'

children.text: śrutvā tv agnivaco gaṅgā taṃ garbham atibhāsvaram
children.translated_text: But hearing <s>Agni</s>'s word, <s>Gaṅgā</s>, greatly radiant,
released that exceedingly bright embryo from her streams then, O sinless one.
What came forth from her, because it had the brilliance of heated jāmbūnada gold,

children.text: kāñcanaṃ dharaṇīṃ prāptaṃ hiraṇyam amalaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: became gold when it reached the earth, pure and auspicious gold.
Copper and black iron also arose from its sharpness;

children.text: malaṃ tasyābhavat tatra trapusīsakam eva ca ||
children.translated_text: its impurity there became tin and lead.

children.text: tad etad dharaṇīṃ prāpya nānādhātur avardhata ||
children.translated_text: Having reached the earth, that became manifold ore and grew.
As soon as the embryo was deposited, colored by its radiance,
the whole forest adjoining the mountain became golden.

children.text: jātarūpam iti khyātaṃ tadā prabhṛti rāghava
children.translated_text: From then on, O <s>Rāghava</s>, gold, radiant like <s>Hutāśana</s>,
became known as jātarūpa, O tiger among men.

children.text: taṃ kumāraṃ tato jātaṃ sendrāḥ sahamarudgaṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Then, when that boy had been born, the gods together with <s>Indra</s> and the hosts of <s>Maruts</s>
appointed the <s>Kṛttikās</s> for the purpose of nurturing him with milk.

children.text: tāḥ kṣīraṃ jātamātrasya kṛtvā samayam uttamam
children.translated_text: They made an excellent agreement about milk for the newborn:

children.text: daduḥ putro 'yam asmākaṃ sarvāsām iti niścitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'This son belongs to all of us,' they decided, and gave it.

children.text: tatas tu devatāḥ sarvāḥ kārttikeya iti bruvan
children.translated_text: Then all the gods said, 'As <s>Kārttikeya</s>,
this son will become famous in the three worlds; there is no doubt.'

children.text: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā skannaṃ garbhaparisrave
children.translated_text: Hearing that word of theirs, because he had been poured forth in the outflow of the embryo,
they bathed him, splendid with supreme beauty and blazing like fire.

children.text: skanda ity abruvan devāḥ skannaṃ garbhaparisravāt
children.translated_text: Because he had been poured forth from the outflow of the embryo, the gods called him <s>Skanda</s>,
the greatly fortunate <s>Kārttikeya</s>, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, resembling flame.
Then the unsurpassed milk of the <s>Kṛttikās</s> appeared;

children.text: ṣaṇṇāṃ ṣaḍānano bhūtvā jagrāha stanajaṃ payaḥ ||
children.translated_text: becoming six-faced for the six of them, he took the breast-born milk.
Having taken the milk, then, in a single day, with a tender body,
the powerful one conquered by his own valor the hosts of armies of the Daityas.
Then the assembled hosts of gods, with <s>Agni</s> at their head,
consecrated that spotless-radiant one as lord of the hosts of the gods' army.

children.text: eṣa te rāma gaṅgāyā vistaro 'bhihito mayā
children.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Rāma</s>, I have told you the full account of <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: kumārasambhavaś caiva dhanyaḥ puṇyas tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: and also the birth of <s>Kumāra</s>, blessed and holy as well.

children.text: tāṃ kathāṃ kauśiko rāme nivedya madhurākṣaram
children.translated_text: Having related that story, sweet in syllables, to <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>

children.text: punar evāparaṃ vākyaṃ kākutstham idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: again spoke this further statement to <s>Kākutstha</s>:
Formerly there was a heroic king, lord of <s>Ayodhyā</s>,

children.text: sagaro nāma dharmātmā prajākāmaḥ sa cāprajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: named <s>Sagara</s>, righteous, desiring offspring, but childless.
O <s>Rāma</s>, the daughter of <s>Vidarbha</s>, named <s>Keśinī</s>,
was the elder wife of <s>Sagara</s>, very righteous and truthful.
The daughter of <s>Ariṣṭanemi</s>, matchless in beauty on earth,
was <s>Sagara</s>'s second wife, known by the name <s>Sumati</s>.

children.text: tābhyāṃ saha tadā rājā patnībhyāṃ taptavāṃs tapaḥ
children.translated_text: Together with those two wives, the king then practiced austerity,
having reached <s>Himavant</s>, on the mountain at <s>Bhṛguprasravaṇa</s>.
Then, when a hundred years had been completed, the sage, satisfied by his austerity,

children.text: sagarāya varaṃ prādād bhṛguḥ satyavatāṃ varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhṛgu</s>, best of truthful men, gave a boon to <s>Sagara</s>:
'A very great gain of offspring will be yours, O sinless one,
and you will attain incomparable fame in the world, O bull among men.

children.text: ekā janayitā tāta putraṃ vaṃśakaraṃ tava
children.translated_text: One wife, dear one, will bear you a son who will continue your lineage;
the other will give birth to sixty thousand sons.'
While that tiger among men was speaking, the two queens, having propitiated him,
then said, with joined palms, filled with supreme joy:

children.text: ekaḥ kasyāḥ suto brahman kā bahūñ janayiṣyati
children.translated_text: 'Which of us, O brahman, will have the one son, and which will give birth to many?

children.text: śrotum icchāvahe brahman satyam astu vacas tava ||
children.translated_text: We wish to hear it, O brahman. Let your word be true.'

children.text: tayos tad vacanaṃ śrutvā bhṛguḥ paramadhārmikaḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard those words of the two women, the most righteous <s>Bhṛgu</s>
spoke this supreme utterance: 'Let free choice be made here.

children.text: eko vaṃśakaro vāstu bahavo vā mahābalāḥ
children.translated_text: Let there be either one son who continues the lineage, or many mighty sons,

children.text: kīrtimanto mahotsāhāḥ kā vā kaṃ varam icchati ||
children.translated_text: famed and full of great energy; which woman desires which boon?'

children.text: munes tu vacanaṃ śrutvā keśinī raghunandana
children.translated_text: Hearing the sage's words, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>, <s>Keśinī</s>
chose a son who would continue the lineage, O <s>Rāma</s>, in the king's presence.
Then the sister of <s>Suparṇa</s>
<s>Sumati</s> chose sixty thousand sons, greatly energetic and famous.
Having circumambulated the sage and bowed down with his head,
the king went to his own city with his wives, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>.

children.text: atha kāle gate tasmiñ jyeṣṭhā putraṃ vyajāyata
children.translated_text: Then, when that time had passed, the elder wife gave birth to a son,
known as <s>Asamañja</s>, <s>Keśinī</s>'s son by <s>Sagara</s>.
But <s>Sumati</s>, tiger among men, gave birth to a gourd-like womb,
and sixty thousand sons came forth when the gourd split open.
Nurses raised them in jars filled with ghee,
and in the course of a long time they all reached youth.
Then after a long time, endowed with beauty and youth,
there were then sixty thousand sons of <s>Sagara</s>.
And that eldest one, best of men, born from <s>Sagara</s>'s own self,

children.text: bālān gṛhītvā tu jale sarayvā raghunandana
children.translated_text: would take children in the waters of the <s>Sarayū</s>, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>,

children.text: prakṣipya prahasan nityaṃ majjatas tān nirīkṣya vai ||
children.translated_text: throw them in and, constantly laughing, watch them as they sank.
Thus evil in conduct and a harasser of good people,

children.text: paurāṇām ahite yuktaḥ pitrā nirvāsitaḥ purāt ||
children.translated_text: intent on the townspeople's harm, he was banished from the city by his father.
<s>Asamañja</s> had a son named <s>Aṃśumān</s>, mighty in valor,
approved by all the world and pleasant-spoken to everyone.
Then after a long time a thought arose
in <s>Sagara</s>, best of men: 'I should perform a sacrifice'; so he resolved.

children.text: sa kṛtvā niścayaṃ rājā sopādhyāyagaṇas tadā
children.translated_text: Having made that decision, the king, together with his groups of priests,
learned in the Veda, began to perform the sacrificial rite.
Having heard <s>Viśvāmitra</s>'s words at the end of the tale, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>,
he, greatly pleased, addressed the sage, who blazed like fire:

children.text: śrotum icchāmi bhadraṃ te vistareṇa kathām imām
children.translated_text: 'I wish to hear this story in detail; may it be well with you.

children.text: pūrvako me kathaṃ brahman yajñaṃ vai samupāharat ||
children.translated_text: How, brahman, did my ancestor undertake that sacrifice?'

children.text: viśvāmitras tu kākutstham uvāca prahasann iva
children.translated_text: Then <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, smiling as it were, said to <s>Kākutstha</s>:
'Listen, <s>Rāma</s>, to the full account of great-souled <s>Sagara</s>.
There is the unsurpassed mountain <s>Himavān</s>, known as the father-in-law of <s>Śaṃkara</s>,
and the <s>Vindhya</s> mountain; they stand facing one another.

children.text: tayor madhye pravṛtto 'bhūd yajñaḥ sa puruṣottama
children.translated_text: Between those two that sacrifice proceeded, O best of men,

children.text: sa hi deśo naravyāghra praśasto yajñakarmaṇi ||
children.translated_text: for that region, tiger among men, is praised for sacrificial rites.
While its horse was being guarded, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, the firm-bowed great chariot-warrior

children.text: aṃśumān akarot tāta sagarasya mate sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aṃśumān</s>, dear one, acted in accordance with <s>Sagara</s>'s intention.

children.text: tasya parvaṇi taṃ yajñaṃ yajamānasya vāsavaḥ
children.translated_text: At a parvan of that sacrifice of the sacrificer,
<s>Vāsava</s>, assuming the body of a rākṣasī, carried off the sacrificial horse.

children.text: hriyamāṇe tu kākutstha tasminn aśve mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: When that horse of the great-souled one was being carried away, O <s>Kākutstha</s>,
all the groups of priests then said to the sacrificer:
'At this parvan the sacrificial horse is being taken away swiftly.
Strike down the thief, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, and let the horse be brought back.

children.text: yajñacchidraṃ bhavaty etat sarveṣām aśivāya naḥ
children.translated_text: This becomes a flaw in the sacrifice, bringing misfortune to us all;

children.text: tat tathā kriyatāṃ rājan yathācchidraḥ kratur bhavet ||
children.translated_text: therefore act so, O king, that the rite may be without flaw.'
Having heard the priests' words in that sacrificial assembly, the king

children.text: ṣaṣṭiṃ putrasahasrāṇi vākyam etad uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: then spoke this sentence to his sixty thousand sons:

children.text: gatiṃ putrā na paśyāmi rakṣasāṃ puruṣarṣabhāḥ
children.translated_text: 'My sons, bulls among men, I do not see the course of the rākṣasas,
for this great rite has been undertaken by great ones purified by mantras.

children.text: tad gacchata vicinvadhvaṃ putrakā bhadram astu vaḥ
children.translated_text: So go, search it out, dear sons; may there be welfare for you.
Go over the whole earth girdled by the ocean.
Each one of you, sons, should advance over a breadth of one yojana;
until the horse is seen, keep digging up the earth.
By my command, seeking that very thief of the horse,
I, consecrated, together with my grandson and groups of priests,

children.text: iha sthāsyāmi bhadraṃ vo yāvat turagadarśanam
children.translated_text: will remain here, blessed be you, until the horse is seen.'
Having been addressed thus, the mighty princes, joyful at heart,
went to the surface of the earth, O <s>Rāma</s>, constrained by their father's command.
Each one, over a breadth of a yojana, the ground
they split, O tiger among men, with arms equal to the touch of thunderbolts,

children.text: śūlair aśanikalpaiś ca halaiś cāpi sudāruṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and with spears like thunderbolts, and also with very terrible ploughs.
As the earth was being split, it resounded, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>;
as nāgas and asuras were being slain, O <s>Rāghava</s>,
and rākṣasas too, an irresistible cry arose from the beings.
For sixty thousand yojanas, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>,
the heroes split the earth down to the unsurpassed <s>Rasātala</s>.
Thus the princes, in mountain-crowded <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>,
digging, O tiger among kings, went around it on every side.
Then the gods, together with gandharvas, asuras, and pannagas,
all with agitated minds, approached <s>Pitāmaha</s>.
Having propitiated the great-souled one, then with dejected faces,
they, exceedingly terrified, said these words to <s>Pitāmaha</s>:
'Revered one, the whole earth is being dug up by the sons of <s>Sagara</s>.'
And many great-souled aquatic beings are being slain.
"This destroyer of our sacrifice is carrying off our horse."
Thus the sons of <s>Sagara</s> were killing all creatures.

children.text: devatānāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā bhagavān vai pitāmahaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing the words of the gods, the blessed Grandfather
answered those greatly terrified ones, who were bewildered by the power of fate:
"This whole earth belongs to wise <s>Vāsudeva</s>;

children.text: kāpilaṃ rūpam āsthāya dhārayaty aniśaṃ dharām ||
children.translated_text: having assumed the form of <s>Kapila</s>, he continually upholds the earth.

children.text: pṛthivyāś cāpi nirbhedo dṛṣṭa eva sanātanaḥ
children.translated_text: The splitting open of the earth has indeed been seen as an ancient event,
and so too the destruction of <s>Sagara</s>'s short-lived sons."
Hearing the Grandfather's words, the thirty-three gods, O subduer of foes,
rejoicing greatly, went back as they had come.

children.text: sagarasya ca putrāṇāṃ prādur āsīn mahātmanām
children.translated_text: As the earth was being split open, there arose among the great-souled sons of <s>Sagara</s>
a sound like a thunderclap.

children.text: tato bhittvā mahīṃ sarvāṃ kṛtvā cāpi pradakṣiṇam
children.translated_text: Then, after breaking open the whole earth and circling around it,

children.text: sahitāḥ sagarāḥ sarve pitaraṃ vākyam abruvan ||
children.translated_text: all the <s>Sagaras</s> together spoke these words to their father:

children.text: parikrāntā mahī sarvā sattvavantaś ca sūditāḥ
children.translated_text: "The whole earth has been traversed, and powerful beings have been slain,
gods, dānavas, rākṣasas, piśācas, serpents, and kiṃnaras.

children.text: na ca paśyāmahe 'śvaṃ tam aśvahartāram eva ca
children.translated_text: But we do not see that horse, nor the thief of the horse.

children.text: kiṃ kariṣyāma bhadraṃ te buddhir atra vicāryatām ||
children.translated_text: What shall we do? May it be well with you; let your judgment be considered in this matter."

children.text: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā putrāṇāṃ rājasattamaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that statement of his sons, the best of kings,
<s>Sagara</s>, angry, spoke these words, O joy of the <s>Raghus</s>:

children.text: bhūyaḥ khanata bhadraṃ vo nirbhidya vasudhātalam
children.translated_text: "Dig again, may it be well with you, splitting through the surface of the earth.
When you have found the thief of the horse and accomplished your purpose, return."
Accepting the command of their father, the great-souled <s>Sagara</s>,
the sixty thousand sons rushed toward <s>Rasātala</s>.
Then, while that place was being dug, they saw, like a mountain,
the directional elephant <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, holding up the surface of the earth.
The whole earth, with its mountains and forests, O joy of the <s>Raghus</s>,
the great elephant <s>Virūpākṣa</s> held upon his head.
Whenever, at a lunar juncture, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, the great elephant

children.text: khedāc cālayate śīrṣaṃ bhūmikampas tadā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: moves his head from weariness in order to rest, then an earthquake occurs.

children.text: taṃ te pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā diśāpālaṃ mahāgajam
children.translated_text: They circumambulated that great directional elephant,

children.text: mānayanto hi te rāma jagmur bhittvā rasātalam ||
children.translated_text: and, honoring him, O <s>Rāma</s>, they went on, breaking open <s>Rasātala</s>.

children.text: tataḥ pūrvāṃ diśaṃ bhittvā dakṣiṇāṃ bibhiduḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after splitting open the eastern quarter, they again split open the southern one.

children.text: dakṣiṇasyām api diśi dadṛśus te mahāgajam ||
children.translated_text: In the southern quarter too they saw a great elephant,
the great-souled <s>Mahāpadma</s>, like an enormous mountain;

children.text: śirasā dhārayantaṃ te vismayaṃ jagmur uttamam ||
children.translated_text: seeing him holding up the earth with his head, they were filled with supreme wonder.
Then, after circumambulating him, the sixty thousand sons
of great-souled <s>Sagara</s> split open the western quarter.
In the western quarter too those mighty ones saw
the great directional elephant <s>Saumanasa</s>, resembling a mountain.

children.text: taṃ te pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā pṛṣṭvā cāpi nirāmayam
children.translated_text: They circumambulated him and asked after his welfare;
then they set about digging toward the quarter belonging to <s>Soma</s>.
In the north, O best of the <s>Raghus</s>, they saw the snow-white

children.text: bhadraṃ bhadreṇa vapuṣā dhārayantaṃ mahīm imām ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhadra</s>, bearing this earth with his auspicious body.

children.text: samālabhya tataḥ sarve kṛtvā cainaṃ pradakṣiṇam
children.translated_text: Then all of them touched him respectfully and circumambulated him;
the sixty thousand sons split open the surface of the earth.

children.text: tataḥ prāguttarāṃ gatvā sāgarāḥ prathitāṃ diśam
children.translated_text: Then, having gone to the famed northeastern quarter,
all the sons of <s>Sagara</s>, in anger, dug into the earth.
There they saw <s>Kapila</s>, eternal <s>Vāsudeva</s>,

children.text: hayaṃ ca tasya devasya carantam avidūrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the horse of that god grazing not far away.
Knowing him to be the destroyer of the sacrifice, their eyes confused by anger,
they rushed upon him, enraged, and cried, "Stand! Stand!"

children.text: asmākaṃ tvaṃ hi turagaṃ yajñiyaṃ hṛtavān asi
children.translated_text: "You have indeed stolen our sacrificial horse.

children.text: durmedhas tvaṃ hi samprāptān viddhi naḥ sagarātmajān ||
children.translated_text: Know, fool, that we sons of <s>Sagara</s> have arrived."

children.text: śrutvā tad vacanaṃ teṣāṃ kapilo raghunandana
children.translated_text: Hearing those words of theirs, <s>Kapila</s>, O joy of the <s>Raghus</s>,
possessed by great anger, uttered a roar of "hum" then.
Then by that immeasurable great-souled <s>Kapila</s>,
all the sons of <s>Sagara</s> were reduced to heaps of ash, O <s>Kākutstha</s>.
Knowing that his sons had been gone a long time, O joy of the <s>Raghus</s>,
King <s>Sagara</s> spoke to his grandson, who shone with his own splendor:

children.text: śūraś ca kṛtavidyaś ca pūrvais tulyo 'si tejasā
children.translated_text: "You are heroic and learned, and equal to your forefathers in splendor.
Seek the fate of your ancestors, and by whom the horse was carried away.
The beings beneath the earth are powerful and mighty;

children.text: teṣāṃ tvaṃ pratighātārthaṃ sāsiṃ gṛhṇīṣva kārmukam ||
children.translated_text: to repel them, take up a sword and bow.
Having honored those who should be honored, and having slain any makers of obstacles,
return with your purpose accomplished, carrying my sacrifice through to completion."
Thus properly addressed by great-souled <s>Sagara</s>, <s>Aṃśumān</s>

children.text: dhanur ādāya khaḍgaṃ ca jagāma laghuvikramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: took up his bow and sword and went swiftly.

children.text: sa khātaṃ pitṛbhir mārgam antarbhaumaṃ mahātmabhiḥ
children.translated_text: He entered the underground path dug by his great-souled fathers,
O best of men, urged on by that king.
The greatly radiant one saw the directional elephant
being honored by daityas, dānavas, rākṣasas, piśācas, birds, and serpents.

children.text: sa taṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā pṛṣṭvā caiva nirāmayam
children.translated_text: He circumambulated him and also asked after his welfare;

children.text: pitṝn sa paripapraccha vājihartāram eva ca ||
children.translated_text: then he asked him about his ancestors and the thief of the horse.

children.text: diśāgajas tu tac chrutvā prītyāhāṃśumato vacaḥ
children.translated_text: When the directional elephant heard that, he joyfully spoke these words to <s>Aṃśumān</s>:
O son of <s>Asamañja</s>, having accomplished your purpose, you will quickly come back with the horse.

children.text: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā sarvān eva diśāgajān
children.translated_text: Having heard that speech of his, he then began
to question all the elephants of the quarters in order and according to rule.

children.text: taiś ca sarvair diśāpālair vākyajñair vākyakovidaiḥ
children.translated_text: Honored by all those guardians of the directions, who knew speech and were skilled in speech,
and urged on with the horse, he was told, "You will go on."

children.text: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā jagāma laghuvikramaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech of theirs, he of swift stride went
to the place where his <s>Sāgara</s> ancestors had been reduced to heaps of ashes.

children.text: sa duḥkhavaśam āpannas tv asamañjasutas tadā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Asamañja</s>'s son, fallen under the power of grief,

children.text: cukrośa paramārtas tu vadhāt teṣāṃ suduḥkhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: cried out, deeply afflicted and terribly pained by their death.

children.text: yajñiyaṃ ca hayaṃ tatra carantam avidūrataḥ
children.translated_text: There, not far away, he saw the sacrificial horse
grazing, that tiger among men, filled with sorrow and grief.
The tiger among men, wishing to perform the water rite, looked about;
the greatly radiant one sought water, but saw no reservoir.
Then, spreading his keen gaze, he saw the lord of birds,
the maternal uncle of his ancestors, O <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Suparṇa</s>, like the wind.

children.text: sa cainam abravīd vākyaṃ vainateyo mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: And mighty <s>Vainateya</s> spoke this word to him:
"Do not grieve, tiger among men. This death is approved by the worlds.
For these mighty ones were burned by immeasurable <s>Kapila</s>.

children.text: salilaṃ nārhasi prājña dātum eṣāṃ hi laukikam ||
children.translated_text: Wise one, you should not give them ordinary worldly water.
<s>Gaṅgā</s>, the eldest daughter of <s>Himavat</s>, O bull among men,
the purifier of the worlds, can purify these who have been reduced to heaps of ashes.

children.text: tayā klinnam idaṃ bhasma gaṅgayā lokakāntayā
children.translated_text: When this ash is moistened by her, by <s>Gaṅgā</s>, beloved of the worlds,
she will lead the sixty thousand sons to the world of heaven.
Go, fortunate one, take the horse, O bull among men;
hero, you should complete your grandfather's sacrifice."
Having heard <s>Suparṇa</s>'s words, the very powerful <s>Aṃśumān</s>,

children.text: tvaritaṃ hayam ādāya punar āyān mahāyaśāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the greatly famous one, quickly took the horse and came back.
Then, coming to the consecrated king, O joy of the <s>Raghus</s>,
