he reported what had happened, and also <s>Suparṇa</s>'s words.

children.text: tac chrutvā ghorasaṃkāśaṃ vākyam aṃśumato nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing from <s>Aṃśumān</s> that word of dreadful appearance, the king
completed the sacrifice according to rule and according to ordinance.
The glorious king, having performed the sacrifice, returned to his own city;
but the king did not reach a decision about the coming of <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

children.text: agatvā niścayaṃ rājā kālena mahatā mahān
children.translated_text: Without reaching a decision, the great king, after a long time,
having ruled the kingdom for thirty thousand years, went to heaven.
When <s>Sagara</s> had gone the way of time, O <s>Rāma</s>, the people of the realm
chose the very righteous <s>Aṃśumān</s> as king.

children.text: sa rājā sumahān āsīd aṃśumān raghunandana
children.translated_text: That king <s>Aṃśumān</s> was very great, O joy of the <s>Raghus</s>;

children.text: tasya putro mahān āsīd dilīpa iti viśrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he had a great son, famed by the name <s>Dilīpa</s>.
Having installed <s>Dilīpa</s> in the kingdom, O joy of the <s>Raghus</s>,
he practiced very severe tapas on a lovely peak of <s>Himavat</s>.
For thirty-two thousand years the king of great fame
stayed in the ascetic grove, rich in tapas, and obtained heaven.

children.text: dilīpas tu mahātejāḥ śrutvā paitāmahaṃ vadham
children.translated_text: But greatly radiant <s>Dilīpa</s>, hearing of the destruction of his forefathers,
with his mind stricken by sorrow, did not reach a decision.
"How can there be the descent of <s>Gaṅgā</s>? How can their water rite be performed?
How may I rescue them?" Thus he remained absorbed in thought.
While he, self-controlled and known through dharma, was constantly thinking,
a son named <s>Bhagīratha</s>, supremely righteous, was born to him.

children.text: dilīpas tu mahātejā yajñair bahubhir iṣṭavān
children.translated_text: Greatly radiant <s>Dilīpa</s> had worshiped with many sacrifices,
and the king ruled the kingdom for thirty thousand years.

children.text: agatvā niścayaṃ rājā teṣām uddharaṇaṃ prati
children.translated_text: Without reaching a decision concerning their deliverance,
the tiger among men met the law of time through disease.
The king went to <s>Indra</s>'s world by his own earned karma,
after anointing his pleasing son <s>Bhagīratha</s>, O bull among men.
But the royal seer <s>Bhagīratha</s>, righteous, O joy of the <s>Raghus</s>,
was without a son; greatly radiant, desiring offspring, he was still childless.

children.text: sa tapo dīrgham ātiṣṭhad gokarṇe raghunandana
children.translated_text: He undertook long tapas at <s>Gokarṇa</s>, O joy of the <s>Raghus</s>,
with arms raised, amid the five fires, eating only once a month, his senses conquered.
As he stood for a thousand years in terrible tapas,

children.text: suprīto bhagavān brahmā prajānāṃ patir īśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: the blessed <s>Brahmā</s>, lord and master of creatures, became well pleased.
Then the Grandfather, coming with the hosts of gods,
spoke to the great-souled <s>Bhagīratha</s> as he was practicing austerity:
"Greatly fortunate <s>Bhagīratha</s>, lord of men, I am pleased with you

children.text: tapasā ca sutaptena varaṃ varaya suvrata ||
children.translated_text: and with your well-practiced tapas. Choose a boon, good-vowed one."
The greatly radiant, greatly fortunate <s>Bhagīratha</s>, standing with joined palms,
said to the Grandfather of all the worlds:

children.text: yadi me bhagavān prīto yady asti tapasaḥ phalam
children.translated_text: "If the Blessed One is pleased with me, and if there is fruit from my tapas,
may all the sons of <s>Sagara</s> receive water from me.
When the ashes of these great-souled ones are moistened by the water of <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: svargaṃ gaccheyur atyantaṃ sarve me prapitāmahāḥ ||
children.translated_text: may all my great-grandfathers go completely to heaven.

children.text: deyā ca saṃtatir deva nāvasīdet kulaṃ ca naḥ
children.translated_text: And let offspring be granted, O god, so that our line may not sink down.

children.text: ikṣvākūṇāṃ kule deva eṣa me 'stu varaḥ paraḥ ||
children.translated_text: O god, let this be my supreme boon in the line of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s>."
To the king who had spoken these words, the Grandfather of all the worlds
replied with auspicious speech, sweet and sweetly syllabled:
"This wish is a great one, O mighty-charioted <s>Bhagīratha</s>.
So let it be. Good fortune to you, increaser of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> line."

children.text: iyaṃ haimavatī gaṅgā jyeṣṭhā himavataḥ sutā
children.translated_text: This <s>Gaṅgā</s>, daughter of <s>Himavat</s>, born in the Himalaya, is his eldest daughter.

children.text: tāṃ vai dhārayituṃ rājan haras tatra niyujyatām ||
children.translated_text: Let <s>Hara</s> be appointed there, O king, to bear her indeed.

children.text: gaṅgāyāḥ patanaṃ rājan pṛthivī na sahiṣyate
children.translated_text: The earth will not be able to endure the fall of <s>Gaṅgā</s>, O king.

children.text: tau vai dhārayituṃ vīra nānyaṃ paśyāmi śūlinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: To bear them, O hero, I see no one else but the trident-bearing one.

children.text: tam evam uktvā rājānaṃ gaṅgāṃ cābhāṣya lokakṛt
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to the king, and having addressed <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the maker of the worlds

children.text: jagāma tridivaṃ devaḥ saha sarvair marudgaṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the god went to heaven, together with all the hosts of the <s>Maruts</s>.
When that god of gods had gone, he pressed the earth with the tip of his big toe,
and, O <s>Rāma</s>, he remained in attendance for a year.
Then, when the year was complete, the lord of <s>Umā</s>, honored by all the worlds,
<s>Paśupati</s>, spoke these words to the king:

children.text: prītas te 'haṃ naraśreṣṭha kariṣyāmi tava priyam
children.translated_text: I am pleased with you, best of men; I shall do what is dear to you.
I myself shall bear on my head the daughter of the mountain-king.
Then the eldest daughter of <s>Himavat</s>, honored by all the worlds,

children.text: tadā sātimahad rūpaṃ kṛtvā vegaṃ ca duḥsaham
children.translated_text: having then assumed an exceedingly great form and an unbearable speed,

children.text: ākāśād apatad rāma śive śivaśirasy uta ||
children.translated_text: fell from the sky, O <s>Rāma</s>, upon auspicious <s>Śiva</s>, upon <s>Śiva</s>'s head.
She found no outlet at all, bewildered in the mass of his matted hair;
there the goddess wandered about for many groups of years.
By this he was exceedingly pleased, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>,

children.text: visasarja tato gaṅgāṃ haro bindusaraḥ prati ||
children.translated_text: and then <s>Hara</s> released <s>Gaṅgā</s> toward <s>Bindusaras</s>.
From the sky, from <s>Śaṃkara</s>'s head, she then came to the earth,
and the water spread there, preceded by a tremendous sound.
Then divine seers, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and hosts of <s>Siddhas</s> as well

children.text: vyalokayanta te tatra gaganād gāṃ gatāṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: looked on there at that time as she went from the sky to the earth.
In aerial cars shaped like cities, and on horses and excellent elephants,
and also moving through the air, the deities stood there.
Desiring to see that most wonderful event in the world, the supreme descent of <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
the hosts of gods of immeasurable power assembled.
With the hosts of gods flying together, and with the brilliance of their ornaments,
the sky, freed of clouds, shone as if with a hundred suns.
With hosts of porpoises and serpents, and with restless fish too,

children.text: vidyudbhir iva vikṣiptair ākāśam abhavat tadā ||
children.translated_text: the sky then seemed as though scattered with flashes of lightning.
With pale surges of water being scattered in a thousand ways,
the sky was filled as if with autumn clouds and flocks of swans.

children.text: kvacid drutataraṃ yāti kuṭilaṃ kvacid āyatam
children.translated_text: In one place she went very swiftly, in another crookedly, in another broadly extended;

children.text: vinataṃ kvacid uddhūtaṃ kvacid yāti śanaiḥ śanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: in one place bent low, in another tossed upward, and in another she went very slowly.
In one place water was again struck by water itself;

children.text: muhur ūrdhvapathaṃ gatvā papāta vasudhāṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: again and again, after going along an upward path, it fell back to the earth.
That water, fallen from <s>Śaṃkara</s>'s head and fallen again upon the surface of the earth,
then shone forth, stainless, pure, and free from defilement.
There the hosts of seers and <s>Gandharvas</s> dwelling on the surface of the earth
touched the water that had fallen from <s>Bhava</s>'s body, thinking it holy.

children.text: śāpāt prapatitā ye ca gaganād vasudhātalam
children.translated_text: And those who, because of a curse, had fallen from the sky to the surface of the earth,
after bathing there, became free from defilement.
Then, their sins washed away by that radiant water,

children.text: punar ākāśam āviśya svāṃl lokān pratipedire ||
children.translated_text: they entered the sky again and returned to their own worlds.

children.text: mumude mudito lokas tena toyena bhāsvatā
children.translated_text: The delighted world rejoiced in that shining water;
bathed in <s>Gaṅgā</s>, it became free from weariness.
The royal seer <s>Bhagīratha</s> too, mounted on a divine chariot,

children.text: prāyād agre mahātejās taṃ gaṅgā pṛṣṭhato 'nvagāt ||
children.translated_text: went ahead, greatly radiant, and <s>Gaṅgā</s> followed after him.
The gods, together with all the hosts of seers, <s>Daityas</s>, <s>Dānavas</s>, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>,
the chief <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Yakṣas</s>, together with <s>Kiṃnaras</s> and great serpents,
and all the <s>Apsarases</s>, O <s>Rāma</s>, following <s>Bhagīratha</s>'s chariot,

children.text: gaṅgām anvagaman prītāḥ sarve jalacarāś ca ye ||
children.translated_text: gladly followed <s>Gaṅgā</s>, along with all creatures that live in water.

children.text: yato bhagīratho rājā tato gaṅgā yaśasvinī
children.translated_text: Wherever King <s>Bhagīratha</s> went, there the glorious <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
best of rivers and destroyer of all sins, went as well.

children.text: sa gatvā sāgaraṃ rājā gaṅgayānugatas tadā
children.translated_text: Having gone to the ocean then, the king, followed by <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: praviveśa talaṃ bhūmer yatra te bhasmasātkṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: entered the lower region of the earth, where they had been reduced to ashes.

children.text: bhasmany athāplute rāma gaṅgāyāḥ salilena vai
children.translated_text: Then, when the ashes were flooded by the water of <s>Gaṅgā</s>, O <s>Rāma</s>,
<s>Brahmā</s>, lord of all the worlds, spoke these words to the king:

children.text: tāritā naraśārdūla divaṃ yātāś ca devavat
children.translated_text: They have been carried across, tiger among men, and have gone to heaven like gods:
the sixty thousand sons of great-souled <s>Sagara</s>.

children.text: sāgarasya jalaṃ loke yāvat sthāsyati pārthiva
children.translated_text: As long as the water of the ocean shall remain in the world, O king,
so long shall <s>Sagara</s>'s sons remain in heaven like gods.

children.text: iyaṃ ca duhitā jyeṣṭhā tava gaṅgā bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: And this <s>Gaṅgā</s> will become your eldest daughter;

children.text: tvatkṛtena ca nāmnā vai loke sthāsyati viśrutā ||
children.translated_text: by a name derived from your deed she will remain famous in the world.

children.text: gaṅgā tripathagā nāma divyā bhāgīrathīti ca
children.translated_text: The divine <s>Gaṅgā</s> will be named <s>Tripathagā</s> and <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>;
because she makes the three paths flourish, she is remembered as <s>Tripathagā</s>.
For all your forefathers, O lord of men, here
perform the water-offering, O king, and lay aside your vow.

children.text: pūrvakeṇa hi te rājaṃs tenātiyaśasā tadā
children.translated_text: For by your ancestor, that king of surpassing fame at that time,
the foremost among the righteous, this desire was not attained.
Likewise by <s>Aṃśumat</s>, dear one, of incomparable splendor in the world,
though he prayed to lead <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the vow was not fulfilled.
And by the virtuous royal seer, equal in splendor to a great seer,
equal to me in austerity and established in the <s>kṣatriya-dharma</s> (warrior's duty),
by greatly blessed <s>Dilīpa</s>, your father of surpassing splendor,

children.text: punar na śaṅkitā netuṃ gaṅgāṃ prārthayatānagha ||
children.translated_text: though he prayed, O sinless one, the bringing of <s>Gaṅgā</s> was not undertaken again.
But by you that vow has been surpassed and fulfilled, bull among men.
You have attained supreme fame in the world, held in the highest esteem.

children.text: yac ca gaṅgāvataraṇaṃ tvayā kṛtam ariṃdama
children.translated_text: And since the descent of <s>Gaṅgā</s> was accomplished by you, O subduer of foes,

children.text: anena ca bhavān prāpto dharmasyāyatanaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: by this you have reached a great abode of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order).
Bathe yourself, O best of men, in the water that is always fitting for rites,
O tiger among men; become pure and possessed of holy fruit.
Perform the water-rite for all your forefathers.

children.text: svasti te 'stu gamiṣyāmi svaṃ lokaṃ gamyatāṃ nṛpa ||
children.translated_text: May there be welfare for you. I shall go to my own world; you too may go, O king.
Having spoken thus, the lord of gods, the grandsire of all worlds,
the greatly renowned one went back to the world of the gods just as he had come.
The royal sage <s>Bhagīratha</s> too, having made that excellent libation of water
for the renowned sons of <s>Sagara</s>, in due order and according to rule,

children.text: kṛtodakaḥ śucī rājā svapuraṃ praviveśa ha ||
children.translated_text: the king, purified after offering the water, entered his own city.
His purpose fulfilled, O best of men, he ruled his own kingdom.

children.text: pramumoda ca lokas taṃ nṛpam āsādya rāghava
children.translated_text: The people rejoiced on obtaining that king, O <s>Rāghava</s>;
their grief was gone, their aims fulfilled, and they became free from distress.

children.text: eṣa te rāma gaṅgāyā vistaro 'bhihito mayā
children.translated_text: This full account of <s>Gaṅgā</s> has been told to you by me, O <s>Rāma</s>.
May you prosper, and may good be yours; the time of twilight is passing.

children.text: dhanyaṃ yaśasyam āyuṣyaṃ svargyaṃ putryam athāpi ca
children.translated_text: This tale is blessed, fame-giving, life-giving, heavenly, and also productive of sons.
I have recounted this narrative, the descent of <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
Having heard <s>Viśvāmitra</s>'s words, <s>Rāghava</s>, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
was filled with the greatest wonder and then spoke to <s>Viśvāmitra</s>:

children.text: atyadbhutam idaṃ brahman kathitaṃ paramaṃ tvayā
children.translated_text: This is exceedingly marvelous, brahman, as it has been told by you,
the holy descent of <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the filling of the ocean of <s>Sagara</s>.

children.text: tasya sā śarvarī sarvā saha saumitriṇā tadā
children.translated_text: For him, then, that whole night, together with <s>Saumitri</s>,
passed while he pondered <s>Viśvāmitra</s>'s auspicious story.
Then in the clear morning, to the great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,
<s>Rāghava</s>, subduer of foes, having completed his morning rites, spoke these words:

children.text: gatā bhagavatī rātriḥ śrotavyaṃ paramaṃ śrutam
children.translated_text: The blessed night has passed; what was to be heard was most excellent.
That night, O great ascetic, has passed as though it were only a moment

children.text: imāṃ cintayataḥ sarvāṃ nikhilena kathāṃ tava ||
children.translated_text: for me as I pondered this entire story of yours in full.

children.text: tarāma saritāṃ śreṣṭhāṃ puṇyāṃ tripathagāṃ nadīm
children.translated_text: Let us cross the best of rivers, the holy river that goes in three paths.

children.text: naur eṣā hi sukhāstīrṇā ṛṣīṇāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām
children.translated_text: For this boat has been well spread out and prepared by the sages of holy deeds,

children.text: bhagavantam iha prāptaṃ jñātvā tvaritam āgatā ||
children.translated_text: who, knowing that your reverence had arrived here, came quickly.

children.text: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech of the great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>,
he, together with the company of seers and with <s>Rāghava</s>, had the crossing made.
Having reached the northern bank and likewise honored the hosts of seers,

children.text: gaṅgākūle niviṣṭās te viśālāṃ dadṛśuḥ purīm ||
children.translated_text: they settled on the bank of <s>Gaṅgā</s> and saw the city <s>Viśālā</s>.
Then the best of sages quickly went, together with <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: viśālāṃ nagarīṃ ramyāṃ divyāṃ svargopamāṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: to the lovely city <s>Viśālā</s>, divine and like heaven.
Then the very wise <s>Rāma</s>, having folded his hands,

children.text: papraccha prāñjalir bhūtvā viśālām uttamāṃ purīm ||
children.translated_text: asked the great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s> about the excellent city <s>Viśālā</s>:
What royal dynasty is this in <s>Viśālā</s>, O great sage?

children.text: śrotum icchāmi bhadraṃ te paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me ||
children.translated_text: I wish to hear it; may it be well with you, for I have supreme curiosity.

children.text: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rāmasya munipuṃgavaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech of <s>Rāma</s>, the bull among sages
began to recount the ancient story of <s>Viśāla</s>.

children.text: śrūyatāṃ rāma śakrasya kathāṃ kathayataḥ śubhām
children.translated_text: Listen, <s>Rāma</s>, as I tell the auspicious story of <s>Śakra</s>;

children.text: asmin deśe hi yad vṛttaṃ śṛṇu tattvena rāghava ||
children.translated_text: hear truly what happened in this region, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: pūrvaṃ kṛtayuge rāma diteḥ putrā mahābalāḥ
children.translated_text: Formerly, in the <s>Kṛta</s> age, O <s>Rāma</s>, the sons of <s>Diti</s> were very powerful,
and the sons of <s>Aditi</s> were greatly fortunate, heroic, and very righteous.

children.text: tatas teṣāṃ naraśreṣṭha buddhir āsīn mahātmanām
children.translated_text: Then, O best of men, this thought arose among those great-souled ones:

children.text: amarā nirjarāś caiva kathaṃ syāma nirāmayāḥ ||
children.translated_text: How might we become immortal, undecaying, and free from disease?

children.text: teṣāṃ cintayatāṃ rāma buddhir āsīd vipaścitām
children.translated_text: As those wise ones reflected, O <s>Rāma</s>, the thought arose in them:

children.text: kṣīrodamathanaṃ kṛtvā rasaṃ prāpsyāma tatra vai ||
children.translated_text: Having churned the milk ocean, surely we shall obtain the essence there.

children.text: tato niścitya mathanaṃ yoktraṃ kṛtvā ca vāsukim
children.translated_text: Then, having resolved on churning, and having made <s>Vāsuki</s> the rope,
and <s>Mandara</s> the churning-stick, those of immeasurable splendor churned.

children.text: atha dhanvantarir nāma apsarāś ca suvarcasaḥ
children.translated_text: Then one named <s>Dhanvantari</s>, and radiant apsarases,

children.text: apsu nirmathanād eva rasāt tasmād varastriyaḥ
children.translated_text: excellent women, arose from that essence just by the churning of the waters,
O best of men; from that they became apsarases.
There were sixty crores of those radiant apsarases,

children.text: asaṃkhyeyās tu kākutstha yās tāsāṃ paricārikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and countless, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, were their attendants.

children.text: na tāḥ sma pratigṛhṇanti sarve te devadānavāḥ
children.translated_text: All those gods and dānavas did not accept them;
and because they were not accepted, they are remembered as common to all.
Then <s>Varuṇa</s>'s daughter <s>Vāruṇī</s>, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>,
greatly fortunate, arose, seeking someone to accept her.

children.text: diteḥ putrā na tāṃ rāma jagṛhur varuṇātmajām
children.translated_text: The sons of <s>Diti</s>, O <s>Rāma</s>, did not take that daughter of <s>Varuṇa</s>;

children.text: adites tu sutā vīra jagṛhus tām aninditām ||
children.translated_text: but <s>Aditi</s>'s sons, O hero, accepted that blameless one.

children.text: asurās tena daiteyāḥ surās tenāditeḥ sutāḥ
children.translated_text: For that reason the <s>Daiteyas</s> were asuras, and <s>Aditi</s>'s sons were suras;
the suras were delighted and rejoiced because they had accepted <s>Vāruṇī</s>.
<s>Uccaiḥśravas</s>, the best of horses, and the jewel-gem <s>Kaustubha</s>
arose, O best of men, and likewise the supreme amṛta (nectar of immortality).

children.text: atha tasya kṛte rāma mahān āsīt kulakṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, for the sake of that, O <s>Rāma</s>, there was a great destruction of clans.

children.text: adites tu tataḥ putrā diteḥ putrān asūdayan ||
children.translated_text: Thereafter <s>Aditi</s>'s sons slew the sons of <s>Diti</s>.

children.text: aditer ātmajā vīrā diteḥ putrān nijaghnire
children.translated_text: The heroic offspring of <s>Aditi</s> struck down the sons of <s>Diti</s>
in that terrible great battle between the <s>Daiteyas</s> and the <s>Ādityas</s>.

children.text: nihatya ditiputrāṃs tu rājyaṃ prāpya puraṃdaraḥ
children.translated_text: Having slain the sons of <s>Diti</s> and obtained the kingdom, <s>Puraṃdara</s>,
delighted, ruled the worlds together with the companies of seers and cāraṇas.
When those sons had been slain, <s>Diti</s> was overcome with the deepest grief.

children.text: mārīcaṃ kāśyapaṃ rāma bhartāram idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Rāma</s>, she spoke these words to her husband, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, descendant of <s>Marīci</s>:
Blessed lord, I have been deprived of my sons by your mighty sons.
I desire a son, won by long austerity, who will slay <s>Śakra</s>.

children.text: sāhaṃ tapaś cariṣyāmi garbhaṃ me dātum arhasi
children.translated_text: I shall practice austerity; you should grant me a pregnancy.
You should permit me to have such a son, a slayer of <s>Śakra</s>.

children.text: tasyās tadvacanaṃ śrutvā mārīcaḥ kāśyapas tadā
children.translated_text: Hearing those words of hers, the radiant <s>Kāśyapa</s>, descendant of <s>Marīci</s>, then
replied to <s>Diti</s>, who was utterly grief-stricken:

children.text: evaṃ bhavatu bhadraṃ te śucir bhava tapodhane
children.translated_text: So be it. Blessings on you. Be pure, O rich in austerity.
You shall give birth to a son who will slay <s>Śakra</s> in battle.

children.text: pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu śucir yadi bhaviṣyasi
children.translated_text: But when a thousand years are complete, if you remain pure,
then from me you shall give birth to a son who will destroy the three worlds.

children.text: evam uktvā mahātejāḥ pāṇinā sa mamārja tām
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the great radiant one stroked her with his hand.

children.text: samālabhya tataḥ svastīty uktvā sa tapase yayau ||
children.translated_text: After touching her and saying, 'May it be well,' he went away to perform austerity.
When he had gone, best of men, <s>Diti</s>, filled with supreme joy,
reached <s>Kuśaplavana</s> and practiced exceedingly severe austerity.

children.text: tapas tasyāṃ hi kurvatyāṃ paricaryāṃ cakāra ha
children.translated_text: While she was practicing austerity there, O best of men,
the thousand-eyed one served her with the highest excellence of conduct.

children.text: agniṃ kuśān kāṣṭham apaḥ phalaṃ mūlaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Fire, kuśa grass, wood, water, fruit, roots, and likewise

children.text: nyavedayat sahasrākṣo yac cānyad api kāṅkṣitam ||
children.translated_text: whatever else was desired, the thousand-eyed one provided.
By massaging her limbs and by removing her fatigue as well,

children.text: śakraḥ sarveṣu kāleṣu ditiṃ paricacāra ha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> served <s>Diti</s> at all times.
Then, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>, when only ten years remained of the thousand years,
<s>Diti</s>, exceedingly pleased, then spoke to the thousand-eyed one:

children.text: tapaś carantyā varṣāṇi daśa vīryavatāṃ vara
children.translated_text: O best of the strong, of the years during which I have been practicing austerity,

children.text: avaśiṣṭāni bhadraṃ te bhrātaraṃ drakṣyase tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: only ten remain. Blessings on you; after that you will see your brother.

children.text: tam ahaṃ tvatkṛte putra samādhāsye jayotsukam
children.translated_text: For your sake, my son, I shall establish him, eager for victory,
and you, my son, will share with him the conquest of the three worlds, free from distress.

children.text: evam uktvā ditiḥ śakraṃ prāpte madhyaṃ divākare
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to <s>Śakra</s>, when the sun had reached midday,
the goddess was overcome by sleep and placed her feet where her head should be.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tām aśuciṃ śakraḥ pādataḥ kṛtamūrdhajām
children.translated_text: Seeing her impure, with the hair of her head placed at her feet,

children.text: śiraḥsthāne kṛtau pādau jahāsa ca mumoda ca ||
children.translated_text: and her feet placed where her head should be, <s>Śakra</s> laughed and rejoiced.
Then <s>Purandara</s> entered an opening in her body,

children.text: garbhaṃ ca saptadhā rāma bibheda paramātmavān ||
children.translated_text: and, self-possessed, O <s>Rāma</s>, he split the embryo into seven parts.
Then, as the embryo was being split by the thunderbolt with a hundred joints,

children.text: ruroda susvaraṃ rāma tato ditir abudhyata ||
children.translated_text: it cried out with a clear sound, O <s>Rāma</s>; then <s>Diti</s> awoke.

children.text: mā rudo mā rudaś ceti garbhaṃ śakro 'bhyabhāṣata
children.translated_text: 'Do not cry, do not cry,' <s>Śakra</s> said to the embryo,

children.text: bibheda ca mahātejā rudantam api vāsavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the great radiant <s>Vāsava</s> split it even as it cried.

children.text: na hantavyo na hantavya ity evaṃ ditir abravīt
children.translated_text: 'He must not be killed, he must not be killed!' <s>Diti</s> said in this way,
and then <s>Śakra</s> came out, out of respect for his mother's words.
With joined palms and with the thunderbolt in hand, <s>Śakra</s> addressed <s>Diti</s>:
O goddess, you slept in an impure state, with the hair of your head at your feet.
Having found that opportunity, O goddess, I split into seven parts

children.text: abhindaṃ saptadhā devi tan me tvaṃ kṣantum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: the one who would have slain <s>Śakra</s> in battle. You should forgive me for that.

children.text: saptadhā tu kṛte garbhe ditiḥ paramaduḥkhitā
children.translated_text: When the embryo had been made sevenfold, <s>Diti</s>, utterly grief-stricken,
spoke a conciliatory sentence to the unassailable thousand-eyed one:
Through my own fault this embryo has been rendered fruitless in seven parts.
There is no fault of yours here, lord of gods, O <s>Balasūdana</s>.

children.text: priyaṃ tu kṛtam icchāmi mama garbhaviparyaye
children.translated_text: But in the reversal of my pregnancy I wish this kindness to be done for me:

children.text: marutāṃ sapta saptānāṃ sthānapālā bhavantv ime ||
children.translated_text: let these become guardians of the stations of the seven sevens of <s>Maruts</s>.

children.text: vātaskandhā ime sapta carantu divi putrakāḥ
children.translated_text: Let these seven groups of wind range through heaven, my little sons;
let my children, divine in form, be renowned as <s>Mārutas</s>.
Let one range in <s>Brahmaloka</s>, and another likewise in <s>Indraloka</s>;

children.text: divi vāyur iti khyātas tṛtīyo 'pi mahāyaśāḥ ||
children.translated_text: let a third also, of great fame, be known in heaven as <s>Vāyu</s>.

children.text: catvāras tu suraśreṣṭha diśo vai tava śāsanāt
children.translated_text: But four, O best of gods, by your command, through the directions
shall move about. Blessings on you; my sons have become divine beings,

children.text: tvatkṛtenaiva nāmnā ca mārutā iti viśrutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and by a name caused by you they shall be famous as <s>Mārutas</s>.
Hearing those words of hers, the thousand-eyed <s>Purandara</s>,
<s>Balaniṣūdana</s>, with joined palms, spoke these words to <s>Diti</s>:

children.text: sarvam etad yathoktaṃ te bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: All this shall be exactly as you have said; there is no doubt.
Blessings on you. Your sons, having become divine beings, shall move about.

children.text: evaṃ tau niścayaṃ kṛtvā mātāputrau tapovane
children.translated_text: Having thus made their agreement in the ascetic grove, mother and son

children.text: jagmatus tridivaṃ rāma kṛtārthāv iti naḥ śrutam ||
children.translated_text: went to the third heaven, O <s>Rāma</s>, their purpose accomplished; so we have heard.

children.text: eṣa deśaḥ sa kākutstha mahendrādhyuṣitaḥ purā
children.translated_text: This is that country, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, once inhabited by <s>Mahendra</s>,

children.text: ditiṃ yatra tapaḥ siddhām evaṃ paricacāra saḥ ||
children.translated_text: where he served <s>Diti</s> in this way while her austerity had succeeded.
But, tiger among men, there was a supremely righteous son of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>,
born of <s>Alambuṣā</s>, who was renowned as <s>Viśāla</s>.

children.text: tena cāsīd iha sthāne viśāleti purī kṛtā ||
children.translated_text: By him the city named <s>Viśālā</s> was made here in this place.
O <s>Rāma</s>, the son of <s>Viśāla</s> was mighty <s>Hemacandra</s>;
after <s>Hemacandra</s>, <s>Sucandra</s> became renowned.
O <s>Rāma</s>, the son of <s>Sucandra</s> was known as <s>Dhūmrāśva</s>,
and <s>Sṛñjaya</s> too was born as the son of <s>Dhūmrāśva</s>.
The son of <s>Sṛñjaya</s> was glorious and powerful <s>Sahadeva</s>;
<s>Kuśāśva</s>, supremely righteous, was the son of <s>Sahadeva</s>.
The son of <s>Kuśāśva</s> was the greatly radiant and powerful <s>Somadatta</s>;

children.text: somadattasya putras tu kākutstha iti viśrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the son of <s>Somadatta</s>, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, was known as <s>Kākutstha</s>.

children.text: tasya putro mahātejāḥ sampraty eṣa purīm imām
children.translated_text: His greatly radiant son now dwells in this city...
there dwells, godlike and unconquerable, a king named <s>Sumati</s>.

children.text: ikṣvākos tu prasādena sarve vaiśālikā nṛpāḥ
children.translated_text: And by the favor of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, all the kings of <s>Vaiśālī</s>
are long-lived, great-souled, powerful, and most righteous.

children.text: ihādya rajanīṃ rāma sukhaṃ vatsyāmahe vayam
children.translated_text: Here today, <s>Rāma</s>, we shall spend the night comfortably;

children.text: śvaḥ prabhāte naraśreṣṭha janakaṃ draṣṭum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: tomorrow at dawn, best of men, you should go to see <s>Janaka</s>.
But mighty <s>Sumati</s>, hearing that <s>Viśvāmitra</s> had arrived,
that most excellent of royal men, greatly renowned, came forth to meet him.

children.text: pūjāṃ ca paramāṃ kṛtvā sopādhyāyaḥ sabāndhavaḥ
children.translated_text: After offering him the highest honor, together with his priests and kinsmen,
he stood with joined palms, asked <s>Viśvāmitra</s> of his welfare, and then spoke:

children.text: dhanyo 'smy anugṛhīto 'smi yasya me viṣayaṃ mune
children.translated_text: I am blessed; I have been favored, O sage, since you

children.text: samprāpto darśanaṃ caiva nāsti dhanyataro mama ||
children.translated_text: have come to my realm and granted me your sight; no one is more blessed than I.
When they had asked after one another's welfare there at their meeting,
at the end of the conversation <s>Sumati</s> addressed these words to the great sage:
These two princes, may it be well with you, are equal to gods in valor,
heroic, with the gait of elephants and lions, and like tigers and bulls.
They have broad eyes like lotus petals and bear swords, quivers, and bows;
like the <s>Aśvins</s> in beauty, they have just reached youth.
As if by chance they have come to earth like immortals from the world of gods.

children.text: kathaṃ padbhyām iha prāptau kimarthaṃ kasya vā mune ||
children.translated_text: How have they come here on foot? For what purpose, and whose sons are they, O sage?
They adorn this country as the moon and sun adorn the sky,
each like the other in stature, bearing, and movements.

children.text: kimarthaṃ ca naraśreṣṭhau samprāptau durgame pathi
children.translated_text: For what purpose have these best of men come along a difficult road,
these heroes bearing excellent weapons? I wish to hear the truth.

children.text: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā yathāvṛttaṃ nyavedayat
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech of his, he related everything just as it had happened,
including their stay at <s>Siddhāśrama</s> and the slaying of the <s>Rākṣasas</s>.
Hearing <s>Viśvāmitra</s>'s words, the king was exceedingly delighted.

children.text: atithī paramau prāptau putrau daśarathasya tau
children.translated_text: Those two sons of <s>Daśaratha</s> had come as supreme guests;
he honored the mighty pair according to rule, for they deserved hospitality.
Then the two <s>Rāghavas</s>, having received the highest honor from <s>Sumati</s>,

children.text: uṣya tatra niśām ekāṃ jagmatur mithilāṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: spent one night there and then went on to <s>Mithilā</s>.

children.text: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā munayaḥ sarve janakasya purīṃ śubhām
children.translated_text: Seeing that auspicious city of <s>Janaka</s>, all the sages

children.text: sādhu sādhv iti śaṃsanto mithilāṃ samapūjayan ||
children.translated_text: praised <s>Mithilā</s>, saying, "Excellent, excellent," and paid it honor.
There, in a grove near <s>Mithilā</s>, <s>Rāghava</s> saw a hermitage,
ancient, deserted, and lovely, and asked the foremost of sages:
This seems like a splendid hermitage; why is it without sages?

children.text: śrotum icchāmi bhagavan kasyāyaṃ pūrva āśramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I wish to hear, venerable sir, whose former hermitage this was.
Hearing the words spoken by <s>Rāghava</s>, the eloquent,
greatly radiant great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s> replied:

children.text: hanta te kathayiṣyāmi śṛṇu tattvena rāghava
children.translated_text: Come, <s>Rāghava</s>, I shall tell you; listen to the truth
about the one whose hermitage-site this is, cursed in anger by the great-souled man.
Formerly, best of men, it was the hermitage of great-souled <s>Gautama</s>,
divine in appearance and highly honored even by the gods.

children.text: sa ceha tapa ātiṣṭhad ahalyāsahitaḥ purā
children.translated_text: Long ago he practiced austerity here together with <s>Ahalyā</s>,
for many groups of years, O royal prince of great fame.
But knowing of an opportunity, the thousand-eyed lord of <s>Śacī</s>,
wearing the form of the sage, said these words to <s>Ahalyā</s>:
Those who seek fulfillment do not wait for the proper season, O well-composed lady;

children.text: saṃgamaṃ tv aham icchāmi tvayā saha sumadhyame ||
children.translated_text: I desire union with you, O slender-waisted one.
Recognizing the thousand-eyed one in a sage's disguise, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>,
the foolish woman formed an intention out of curiosity about the king of the gods.
Then, inwardly satisfied because her aim was achieved, she said to the best of gods:

children.text: kṛtārtho 'si suraśreṣṭha gaccha śīghram itaḥ prabho
children.translated_text: Your aim has been achieved, best of gods; go quickly from here, lord.

children.text: ātmānaṃ māṃ ca deveśa sarvadā rakṣa mānadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Always protect both yourself and me, lord of gods, giver of honor.

children.text: indras tu prahasan vākyam ahalyām idam abravīt
children.translated_text: But <s>Indra</s>, laughing, spoke these words to <s>Ahalyā</s>:
Fair-hipped one, I am satisfied; I shall go back as I came.

children.text: evaṃ saṃgamya tu tayā niścakrāmoṭajāt tataḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus united with her, he then went out from the hut,

children.text: sa sambhramāt tvaran rāma śaṅkito gautamaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: but in confusion he hurried, O <s>Rāma</s>, anxious about <s>Gautama</s>.
Then he saw the great sage <s>Gautama</s> entering,
unassailable by gods and demons, endowed with the power of austerity,
wet with sacred water and blazing like fire.
Seeing him, the lord of the gods became terrified and downcast in face.
Then the sage, seeing the thousand-eyed one wearing a sage's form,
the virtuous man spoke in anger to the ill-behaved one:

children.text: mama rūpaṃ samāsthāya kṛtavān asi durmate
children.translated_text: Taking on my form, evil-minded one, you have done

children.text: akartavyam idaṃ yasmād viphalas tvaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: this thing that should not be done; therefore you shall become fruitless.
When the great-souled <s>Gautama</s>, full of anger, had spoken thus to him,
the testicles of the thousand-eyed one fell to the ground at that very moment.

children.text: tathā śaptvā sa vai śakraṃ bhāryām api ca śaptavān
children.translated_text: Having cursed <s>Śakra</s> in that way, he also cursed his wife:
For many thousands of years you shall dwell here.
Living on air, without food, performing austerity, and lying in ashes,
invisible to all beings, you shall dwell in this hermitage.

children.text: yadā caitad vanaṃ ghoraṃ rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: And when <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, irresistible in might,
comes to this dreadful forest, then you shall become purified.
Through hospitality to him, wicked woman, freed from greed and delusion,

children.text: matsakāśe mudā yuktā svaṃ vapur dhārayiṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: joyfully in my presence you shall assume your own body.
Having spoken thus, greatly radiant <s>Gautama</s>
abandoned this hermitage, which was frequented by <s>Siddhas</s> and <s>Cāraṇas</s>.
He, great in austerity, practiced austerity on the lovely peak of <s>Himavat</s>.

children.text: aphalas tu tataḥ śakro devān agnipurogamān
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, bereft of his testicles, said to the gods headed by <s>Agni</s>,
with a frightened face, together with hosts of seers and <s>Cāraṇas</s>:
By obstructing the austerity of great-souled <s>Gautama</s>,

children.text: krodham utpādya hi mayā surakāryam idaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and provoking his anger, I have done this work of the gods.

children.text: aphalo 'smi kṛtas tena krodhāt sā ca nirākṛtā
children.translated_text: Through his anger I have been made testicleless, and she has been rejected;
by a great release from the curse, his austerity has been taken away by me.

children.text: tan māṃ suravarāḥ sarve sarṣisaṃghāḥ sacāraṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, all you best of gods, with the hosts of seers and the <s>Cāraṇas</s>,
ought to make me, who have helped the gods, possessed of testicles again.
Hearing the words of <s>Śatakratu</s>, the gods, with <s>Agni</s> at their head,
approached the <s>Pitṛ</s>-gods and spoke, together with all the hosts of <s>Maruts</s>:

children.text: ayaṃ meṣaḥ savṛṣaṇaḥ śakro hy avṛṣaṇaḥ kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: This ram has testicles; <s>Śakra</s> has indeed been made without testicles.
Take the two testicles of the ram and quickly give them to <s>Śakra</s>.

children.text: aphalas tu kṛto meṣaḥ parāṃ tuṣṭiṃ pradāsyati
children.translated_text: The ram, though made testicleless, will give supreme satisfaction

children.text: bhavatāṃ harṣaṇārthāya ye ca dāsyanti mānavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for your delight, and so will those men who offer it.

children.text: agnes tu vacanaṃ śrutvā pitṛdevāḥ samāgatāḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Agni</s>'s words, the assembled <s>Pitṛ</s>-gods
tore out the ram's testicles and presented them to the thousand-eyed one.
From that time onward, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, the assembled <s>Pitṛ</s>-gods

children.text: aphalān bhuñjate meṣān phalais teṣām ayojayan ||
children.translated_text: eat testicleless rams and assign the fruits to those who offer them.

children.text: indras tu meṣavṛṣaṇas tadā prabhṛti rāghava
children.translated_text: And from that time onward, O <s>Rāghava</s>, <s>Indra</s> had the testicles of a ram,
through the power of <s>Gautama</s> and of the great-souled sage's austerity.
Therefore come, greatly radiant one, to the hermitage of that man of holy deeds;
deliver this greatly blessed, godlike <s>Ahalyā</s>.
Hearing <s>Viśvāmitra</s>'s words, <s>Rāghava</s>, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
placing <s>Viśvāmitra</s> before him, entered the hermitage.
And he saw the greatly blessed woman, her radiance made bright by austerity,
difficult to behold even when approached by the worlds together with gods and asuras.

children.text: prayatnān nirmitāṃ dhātrā divyāṃ māyāmayīm iva
children.translated_text: as if divine and made of illusion, fashioned by the Creator with effort,
her form enveloped in smoke, like the radiance of the full moon,
like the brightness of the full moon covered with frost and veiled by cloud,
like blazing sunlight in the midst of the waters, hard to assail.

children.text: sā hi gautamavākyena durnirīkṣyā babhūva ha
children.translated_text: For by <s>Gautama</s>'s word she had become hard to behold

children.text: trayāṇām api lokānāṃ yāvad rāmasya darśanam ||
children.translated_text: even for the three worlds, until <s>Rāma</s> should see her.

children.text: rāghavau tu tatas tasyāḥ pādau jagṛhatus tadā
children.translated_text: Then the two <s>Rāghavas</s> at that time clasped her feet,

children.text: smarantī gautamavacaḥ pratijagrāha sā ca tau ||
children.translated_text: and she, remembering <s>Gautama</s>'s words, received the two of them.
With full composure she offered water for the feet, arghya, and hospitality,
and <s>Kākutstha</s> accepted them by the rite prescribed in rule.
There was a great shower of flowers, with the sounds of divine drums,
and there was a great gathering of <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Apsarases</s>.

children.text: sādhu sādhv iti devās tām ahalyāṃ samapūjayan
children.translated_text: The gods honored that <s>Ahalyā</s>, saying, "Good, good!"
her body purified by the power of austerity, obedient to <s>Gautama</s>'s will.
<s>Gautama</s> too, greatly radiant and happy together with <s>Ahalyā</s>,

children.text: rāmaṃ sampūjya vidhivat tapas tepe mahātapāḥ ||
children.translated_text: honored <s>Rāma</s> according to rule and practiced great austerity.
<s>Rāma</s> too, having duly received supreme honor

children.text: sakāśād vidhivat prāpya jagāma mithilāṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: from <s>Gautama</s> the great sage, then went to <s>Mithilā</s>.

children.text: tataḥ prāguttarāṃ gatvā rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha
children.translated_text: Then, going toward the northeast, <s>Rāma</s> with <s>Saumitri</s>,
placing <s>Viśvāmitra</s> before them, approached the sacrificial enclosure.
<s>Rāma</s>, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, said to the tiger among sages:
Great indeed is the prosperity of the sacrifice of great-souled <s>Janaka</s>.
Here are many thousands of Brahmins dwelling in various lands,
greatly blessed and devoted to study of the <s>Veda</s>.
Hermitages of seers are seen, crowded with hundreds of carts.

children.text: deśo vidhīyatāṃ brahman yatra vatsyāmahe vayam ||
children.translated_text: O brahman, let a place be assigned where we may stay.
Hearing <s>Rāma</s>'s words, <s>Viśvāmitra</s> the great sage
made a lodging in a secluded place supplied with water.

children.text: viśvāmitraṃ muniśreṣṭhaṃ śrutvā sa nṛpatis tadā
children.translated_text: When that king heard that <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, best of sages, had come,
placing before him <s>Śatānanda</s>, his faultless family priest,

children.text: ṛtvijo 'pi mahātmānas tv arghyam ādāya satvaram
children.translated_text: the great-souled officiating priests too quickly took up the arghya,
and duly gave it to <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, preceded by mantras.

children.text: pratigṛhya tu tāṃ pūjāṃ janakasya mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Having accepted that honor from great-souled <s>Janaka</s>,

children.text: papraccha kuśalaṃ rājño yajñasya ca nirāmayam ||
children.translated_text: he asked about the king's welfare and the sacrifice's freedom from trouble.

children.text: sa tāṃś cāpi munīn pṛṣṭvā sopādhyāyapurodhasaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, having inquired after those sages too, along with their teachers and priests,
he joyfully met with all of them according to proper order.
Then the king, with joined palms, addressed the best of sages:
Let the Blessed One sit on the seat together with these excellent sages.
Hearing <s>Janaka</s>'s words, the great sage sat down,

children.text: purodhā ṛtvijaś caiva rājā ca saha mantribhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: as did the family priest, the officiating priests, and the king with his ministers.
When he saw them seated everywhere on the seats in due order,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā sa nṛpatis tatra viśvāmitram athābravīt ||
children.translated_text: the king there then spoke to <s>Viśvāmitra</s>:

children.text: adya yajñasamṛddhir me saphalā daivataiḥ kṛtā
children.translated_text: Today the prosperity of my sacrifice has been made fruitful by the gods;
today I have obtained the fruit of the sacrifice through seeing your blessed self.
I am fortunate; I am favored, O foremost of sages,
because you, O brahman, have come with the sages to my sacrificial session.

children.text: dvādaśāhaṃ tu brahmarṣe śeṣam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The wise say, O <s>Brahmarṣi</s>, that twelve days remain;

children.text: tato bhāgārthino devān draṣṭum arhasi kauśika ||
children.translated_text: after that, O <s>Kauśika</s>, you should see the gods, who desire their shares.
Having said this to the tiger among sages, then, with a delighted face,

children.text: punas taṃ paripapraccha prāñjaliḥ prayato nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the attentive king again questioned him with joined palms.
These two youths, may it be well with you, have valor equal to the gods;
they are heroes with the gait of elephants and lions, like a tiger and a bull.
Their eyes are broad like lotus petals; they bear swords, quivers, and bows.
In beauty they are like the <s>Aśvins</s>, and their youth has just come upon them.
They seem to have reached the earth by chance, like immortals from the world of the gods.

children.text: kathaṃ padbhyām iha prāptau kimarthaṃ kasya vā mune ||
children.translated_text: How have they come here on foot, and for what purpose, and whose are they, O sage?
Holding excellent weapons, these two heroes: whose sons are they, great sage,
as they adorn this land like the moon and sun adorning the sky?
They resemble one another in stature, gestures, and movements;
these heroes wear side-locks like crow's wings. I wish to hear the truth about them.
Hearing that statement of the high-souled <s>Janaka</s>,
he explained that the two high-souled ones were the sons of <s>Daśaratha</s>.
He told of their stay at <s>Siddhāśrama</s> and likewise the killing of the <s>Rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: tac cāgamanam avyagraṃ viśālāyāś ca darśanam ||
children.translated_text: their untroubled arrival there and the sight of <s>Viśālā</s>,
the sight of <s>Ahalyā</s> and their meeting with <s>Gautama</s>,
and their coming in order to investigate the great bow.
Having reported all this to the high-souled <s>Janaka</s> of great splendor,
the great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s> then fell silent.
Hearing that speech of wise <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,
the greatly radiant <s>Śatānanda</s>, whose hairs stood on end, the great ascetic,
the eldest son of <s>Gautama</s>, his brilliance made luminous by austerity,
came to supreme wonder merely from seeing <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: sa tau niṣaṇṇau samprekṣya sukhāsīnau nṛpātmajau
children.translated_text: Looking at the two princes seated there, sitting comfortably,
<s>Śatānanda</s> then spoke to <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, best of sages:

children.text: api te muniśārdūla mama mātā yaśasvinī
children.translated_text: O tiger among sages, was my renowned mother,
who has undertaken long austerity, shown to the prince by you?

children.text: api rāme mahātejo mama mātā yaśasvinī
children.translated_text: O greatly radiant one, did my renowned mother, before <s>Rāma</s>,
offer worship with forest things to him who is worthy of worship by all embodied beings?
O greatly radiant one, was the ancient event, just as it happened, told to <s>Rāma</s>,
the difficult deed done wrongly by the god toward my mother?

children.text: api kauśika bhadraṃ te guruṇā mama saṃgatā
children.translated_text: O <s>Kauśika</s>, may it be well with you; did my mother meet with my teacher,
best of sages, after the sight of <s>Rāma</s>?

children.text: api me guruṇā rāmaḥ pūjitaḥ kuśikātmaja
children.translated_text: O son of <s>Kuśika</s>, was <s>Rāma</s> honored by my teacher,
and has the greatly radiant one come here after receiving honor from the high-souled sage?

children.text: api śāntena manasā gurur me kuśikātmaja
children.translated_text: O son of <s>Kuśika</s>, was my teacher, with a peaceful mind,
respectfully greeted by <s>Rāma</s>, who came here disciplined and attentive?

children.text: tac chrutvā vacanaṃ tasya viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech of his, the great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,
knower of speech, replied to <s>Śatānanda</s>, skilled in speech:

children.text: nātikrāntaṃ muniśreṣṭha yat kartavyaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: Best of sages, what had to be done was not neglected; I have done it.
The wife was reunited with the sage, as <s>Reṇukā</s> was with the descendant of <s>Bhṛgu</s>.

children.text: tac chrutvā vacanaṃ tasya viśvāmitrasya dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that statement of wise <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,
the greatly radiant <s>Śatānanda</s> spoke these words to <s>Rāma</s>:

children.text: svāgataṃ te naraśreṣṭha diṣṭyā prāpto 'si rāghava
children.translated_text: Welcome to you, best of men; by good fortune you have arrived, O <s>Rāghava</s>,
placing before you the invincible great seer <s>Viśvāmitra</s>.
His deeds are inconceivable; by austerity he is a <s>brahmarṣi</s> (Brahman-seer) of boundless splendor.

children.text: viśvāmitro mahātejā vetsy enaṃ paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: Greatly radiant <s>Viśvāmitra</s> will know this supreme course.

children.text: nāsti dhanyataro rāma tvatto 'nyo bhuvi kaścana
children.translated_text: There is no one on earth, O <s>Rāma</s>, more fortunate than you,

children.text: goptā kuśikaputras te yena taptaṃ mahat tapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for the son of <s>Kuśika</s>, who has performed great austerity, is your protector.
Listen, and I shall tell, according to my ability, the story of the high-souled <s>Kauśika</s>,

children.text: yathābalaṃ yathāvṛttaṃ tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: just as it happened; hear it as I relate it.
This subduer of foes was once a righteous king for a long time,

children.text: dharmajñaḥ kṛtavidyaś ca prajānāṃ ca hite rataḥ ||
children.translated_text: knower of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), learned, and devoted to the welfare of his subjects.

children.text: prajāpatisutas tv āsīt kuśo nāma mahīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Prajāpati</s> was a lord of the earth named <s>Kuśa</s>;
<s>Kuśa</s>'s son was the powerful and very righteous <s>Kuśanābha</s>.

children.text: kuśanābhasutas tv āsīd gādhir ity eva viśrutaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kuśanābha</s>'s son was famed precisely as <s>Gādhi</s>;
<s>Gādhi</s>'s son was the greatly radiant great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>.
Greatly radiant <s>Viśvāmitra</s> protected the earth;
as king he ruled the kingdom for many thousands of years.
Once the greatly radiant one, having set his army in motion,
surrounded by an <s>akṣauhiṇī</s> (great battle formation), roamed over the earth.

children.text: nagarāṇi ca rāṣṭrāṇi saritaś ca tathā girīn
children.translated_text: Cities and kingdoms, rivers likewise and mountains,

children.text: āśramān kramaśo rājā vicarann ājagāma ha ||
children.translated_text: the king visited in order, and he came to hermitages as he wandered.
He came to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s hermitage-place, with trees bearing many kinds of flowers and fruits,
filled with groups of many kinds of deer, attended by perfected beings and <s>Cāraṇas</s>,
adorned by gods, <s>Dānavas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and <s>Kiṃnaras</s>,
filled with peaceful deer and frequented by assemblies of twice-born men,
crowded with hosts of <s>brahmarṣis</s> and attended by hosts of divine seers,
by great-souled ones, like fires, perfected through the practice of austerity,
always thronged and splendid with great-souled ones like <s>Brahmā</s>,
with those who lived on water, those who lived on air, and those who ate withered leaves,
with self-controlled eaters of fruits and roots, who had conquered anger and mastered their senses,
with seers and <s>Vālakhilyas</s> devoted to recitation and oblation.
<s>Viśvāmitra</s>, mighty and best of conquerors, saw <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s hermitage-place,
like another world of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Seeing it, mighty <s>Viśvāmitra</s> was exceedingly pleased;

children.text: praṇato vinayād vīro vasiṣṭhaṃ japatāṃ varam ||
children.translated_text: the hero bowed with humility to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, best of those devoted to recitation.

children.text: svāgataṃ tava cety ukto vasiṣṭhena mahātmanā
children.translated_text: Being told, 'Welcome to you,' by the high-souled <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,

children.text: āsanaṃ cāsya bhagavān vasiṣṭho vyādideśa ha ||
children.translated_text: blessed <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> assigned him a seat.
And then, when wise <s>Viśvāmitra</s> had sat down,
The best of sages duly brought fruits and roots.

children.text: pratigṛhya ca tāṃ pūjāṃ vasiṣṭhād rājasattamaḥ
children.translated_text: And having received that honor, the best of kings, from <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,
asked after the welfare of his austerities, agnihotra, and disciples.
The greatly radiant <s>Viśvāmitra</s> also asked about the hosts of forest trees,
and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> told the best of kings that all was well everywhere.
When the king <s>Viśvāmitra</s> was comfortably seated, the great ascetic,

children.text: papraccha japatāṃ śreṣṭho vasiṣṭho brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, best of mutterers of sacred formulas, son of <s>Brahmā</s>, asked him:

children.text: kaccit te kuśalaṃ rājan kaccid dharmeṇa rañjayan
children.translated_text: "Is it well with you, O king? O righteous king, do you, gladdening them by <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),
protect your subjects in the conduct proper to a king?

children.text: kaccit te subhṛtā bhṛtyāḥ kaccit tiṣṭhanti śāsane
children.translated_text: Are your servants well maintained? Do they remain under command?

children.text: kaccit te vijitāḥ sarve ripavo ripusūdana ||
children.translated_text: Have all your enemies been conquered, O subduer of foes?

children.text: kaccid bale ca kośe ca mitreṣu ca paraṃtapa
children.translated_text: Is all well with your army and treasury and allies, O scorcher of enemies?
Is all well with your sons and grandsons, O tiger among men, O sinless one?"
The greatly radiant king <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, filled with humility,
answered <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> that all was well everywhere.

children.text: kṛtvobhau suciraṃ kālaṃ dharmiṣṭhau tāḥ kathāḥ śubhāḥ
children.translated_text: After both very righteous men had spent a long time telling

children.text: mudā paramayā yuktau prīyetāṃ tau parasparam ||
children.translated_text: those auspicious stories, endowed with supreme joy, the two delighted in one another.
Then, O <s>Raghunandana</s>, at the end of their conversation, the blessed <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>

children.text: viśvāmitram idaṃ vākyam uvāca prahasann iva ||
children.translated_text: spoke these words to <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, as if smiling:
"O mighty one, I wish to offer hospitality to this army
and also to your immeasurable self; please accept it from me as is fitting.

children.text: satkriyāṃ tu bhavān etāṃ pratīcchatu mayodyatām
children.translated_text: Let your lordship accept this reception prepared by me.
O king, you are the foremost of guests and should be honored with care."
Thus addressed by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, the wise <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,

children.text: kṛtam ity abravīd rājā pūjāvākyena me tvayā ||
children.translated_text: the king, said, "It has already been done by you, through your words of honor to me.
O blessed one, with the fruits and roots that are found in your hermitage,
with water for the feet, water for sipping, and the sight of your venerable self,
in every way, O very wise one, I have been well honored by one worthy of honor.
I shall go; reverence to you. Look upon me with a friendly eye."

children.text: evaṃ bruvantaṃ rājānaṃ vasiṣṭhaḥ punar eva hi
children.translated_text: But as the king spoke in this way, righteous <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,
noble-minded, invited him again and again.

children.text: bāḍham ity eva gādheyo vasiṣṭhaṃ pratyuvāca ha
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Gādhi</s> then replied to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, "Certainly.
Let it be as your reverence wishes, O best of sages."

children.text: evam ukto mahātejā vasiṣṭho japatāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, the greatly radiant <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, best of those who mutter sacred formulas,
then, pleased, called <s>Kalmāṣī</s>, he who had shaken off impurity.

children.text: ehy ehi śabale kṣipraṃ śṛṇu cāpi vaco mama
children.translated_text: "Come, come quickly, O <s>Śabalā</s>, and hear my word.
I have resolved to provide a reception for this royal seer's army,
so arrange for me an honor-feast with very costly food.
Whatever is desired by each man, well honored among the six flavors,

children.text: tat sarvaṃ kāmadhug divye abhivarṣakṛte mama ||
children.translated_text: all that, O divine wish-milking one, shower forth for me.
Together with sauces, cooked rice, drink, foods to be licked and sucked,

children.text: annānāṃ nicayaṃ sarvaṃ sṛjasva śabale tvara ||
children.translated_text: create every heap of food, O <s>Śabalā</s>; be swift."
Thus addressed by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, O subduer of foes,

children.text: vidadhe kāmadhuk kāmān yasya yasya yathepsitam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śabalā</s>, the wish-giving cow, supplied desires for each one just as each wished.

children.text: ikṣūn madhūṃs tathā lājān maireyāṃś ca varāsavān
children.translated_text: Sugarcanes, honeys, parched grains, maireya drinks, and excellent wines,

children.text: pānāni ca mahārhāṇi bhakṣyāṃś coccāvacāṃs tathā ||
children.translated_text: very costly drinks, and foods of many high and low kinds appeared.
There were heaps like mountains of hot, sumptuous rice,

children.text: mṛṣṭānnāni ca sūpāś ca dadhikulyās tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: sweet dishes, soups, and likewise streams of curds.
And vessels completely filled with sauces of many sweet flavors,
and preparations of jaggery, were there by the thousands.
Everything was perfectly satisfying, crowded with people delighted and well nourished;
O <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Viśvāmitra</s>'s army had been fully gratified by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.
The royal seer <s>Viśvāmitra</s> too was then delighted and well nourished;
the king, together with the best of his inner apartments and with the brahmins and priests,
together with his ministers and counselors and servants, having then been honored,

children.text: yuktaḥ pareṇa harṣeṇa vasiṣṭham idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: was filled with supreme joy and spoke this to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>:
"O brahmin, I have been honored by you, who are worthy of honor, and well received.
Listen; I shall speak a statement, O expert in speech.
Let <s>Śabalā</s> be given to me for a hundred thousand cows.

children.text: ratnaṃ hi bhagavann etad ratnahārī ca pārthivaḥ
children.translated_text: For this, O blessed one, is a jewel, and a king is a taker of jewels.

children.text: tasmān me śabalāṃ dehi mamaiṣā dharmato dvija ||
children.translated_text: Therefore give <s>Śabalā</s> to me; by right she is mine, O twice-born one."

children.text: evam uktas tu bhagavān vasiṣṭho munisattamaḥ
children.translated_text: But thus addressed by <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, the blessed <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, best of sages,
righteous in nature, replied to the lord of the earth:
"I shall not give <s>Śabalā</s>, O king, for a hundred thousand cows,

children.text: rājan dāsyāmi śabalāṃ rāśibhī rajatasya vā ||
children.translated_text: nor even for a hundred crores of cows, nor for heaps of silver.
O subduer of foes, I could not abandon her from my side;

children.text: śāśvatī śabalā mahyaṃ kīrtir ātmavato yathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śabalā</s> is eternally mine, like the fame of a self-possessed man.

children.text: asyāṃ havyaṃ ca kavyaṃ ca prāṇayātrā tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: In her depend the offerings to the gods, the offerings to the ancestors, and the sustaining of life itself;

children.text: āyattam agnihotraṃ ca balir homas tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: the agnihotra (fire oblation), bali (offering), and homa (sacrifice) likewise depend on her.
The exclamations svāhā and vaṣaṭ, and various branches of knowledge as well,

children.text: āyattam atra rājarṣe sarvam etan na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: depend on her, O royal seer; all this is so, without doubt.

children.text: sarvasvam etat satyena mama tuṣṭikarī sadā
children.translated_text: In truth, she is all my wealth and always brings me satisfaction.

children.text: kāraṇair bahubhī rājan na dāsye śabalāṃ tava ||
children.translated_text: For many reasons, O king, I shall not give <s>Śabalā</s> to you."
But when <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> had spoken thus, <s>Viśvāmitra</s> then,
the expert in speech, spoke a much more impassioned statement:
"I give you fourteen thousand elephants with golden girths and neck ornaments,
adorned with golden goads."
and eight hundred golden chariots, yoked with four white horses,
adorned with little bells, I give to you.
Of horses born in good regions, of noble stock and great vigor,

children.text: sahasram ekaṃ daśa ca dadāmi tava suvrata ||
children.translated_text: I give one thousand and ten to you, O well-vowed one.
And of cows, divided into many colors and likewise in the prime of age,

children.text: dadāmy ekāṃ gavāṃ koṭiṃ śabalā dīyatāṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: I give one crore; let <s>Śabalā</s> be given to me."

children.text: evam uktas tu bhagavān viśvāmitreṇa dhīmatā
children.translated_text: But the blessed one, thus addressed by wise <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,

children.text: na dāsyāmīti śabalāṃ prāha rājan kathaṃcana ||
children.translated_text: said, "I shall not give <s>Śabalā</s>, O king, by any means.

children.text: etad eva hi me ratnam etad eva hi me dhanam
children.translated_text: She alone is my jewel; she alone is my wealth.

children.text: etad eva hi sarvasvam etad eva hi jīvitam ||
children.translated_text: She alone is my whole possession; she alone is my life.

children.text: darśaś ca pūrṇamāsaś ca yajñāś caivāptadakṣiṇāḥ
children.translated_text: The new-moon and full-moon rites, and sacrifices with due gifts,

children.text: etad eva hi me rājan vividhāś ca kriyās tathā ||
children.translated_text: she alone is these for me, O king, and various other rites as well.

children.text: adomūlāḥ kriyāḥ sarvā mama rājan na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: All my rites have her as their root, O king; there is no doubt.

children.text: bahūnāṃ kiṃ pralāpena na dāsye kāmadohinīm ||
children.translated_text: Why say much? I shall not give the wish-milking cow."

children.text: kāmadhenuṃ vasiṣṭho 'pi yadā na tyajate muniḥ
children.translated_text: When the sage <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> would not give up the <s>kāmadhenu</s> (wish-cow),
then, O <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Viśvāmitra</s> dragged away his <s>Śabalā</s>.

children.text: nīyamānā tu śabalā rāma rājñā mahātmanā
children.translated_text: As <s>Śabalā</s> was being led away, O <s>Rāma</s>, by the great king,
she was miserable and reflected, weeping and wasted by grief:
"Have I been abandoned by great-souled <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,
that I, wretched, am being carried off by the king's servants, afflicted with intense sorrow?
What offense have I committed against that great seer of purified self,

children.text: yan mām anāgasaṃ bhaktām iṣṭāṃ tyajati dhārmikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that righteous man, so that he abandons me, innocent, devoted, and dear?"

children.text: iti sā cintayitvā tu niḥśvasya ca punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having reflected in this way, and sighing again and again,
she then went swiftly to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, the supremely powerful one.

children.text: nirdhūya tāṃs tadā bhṛtyāñ śataśaḥ śatrusūdana
children.translated_text: Having shaken off those servants by the hundreds, O subduer of foes,
she went with the speed of the wind to the feet of the great-souled sage.

children.text: śabalā sā rudantī ca krośantī cedam abravīt
children.translated_text: That <s>Śabalā</s>, weeping and crying out, said this,
standing before <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, with a voice like a thundercloud and drum:

children.text: bhagavan kiṃ parityaktā tvayāhaṃ brahmaṇaḥ suta
children.translated_text: "Blessed one, son of <s>Brahmā</s>, why have I been abandoned by you,

children.text: yasmād rājabhṛtā māṃ hi nayante tvatsakāśataḥ ||
children.translated_text: since the king's servants are taking me away from your presence?"

children.text: evam uktas tu brahmarṣir idaṃ vacanam abravīt
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, the brahmarṣi spoke this word
to her whose heart was scorched by grief and who was sorrowful like a sister:

children.text: na tvāṃ tyajāmi śabale nāpi me 'pakṛtaṃ tvayā
children.translated_text: "I do not abandon you, O <s>Śabalā</s>, nor have you done me any wrong.

children.text: eṣa tvāṃ nayate rājā balān matto mahābalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This mighty king is taking you away from me by force.

children.text: na hi tulyaṃ balaṃ mahyaṃ rājā tv adya viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: For my power is not equal to his; today the king is especially strong.

children.text: balī rājā kṣatriyaś ca pṛthivyāḥ patir eva ca ||
children.translated_text: The king is powerful, a kṣatriya, and indeed lord of the earth.
This full <s>akṣauhiṇī</s> (army division), crowded with horses and chariots,
and filled with elephants and banners, makes him the stronger."
Thus addressed by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, she replied respectfully,
she who knew speech, to the brahmarṣi of immeasurable splendor:
"They do not call a kṣatriya's power true power; the brahmin is stronger.

children.text: brahman brahmabalaṃ divyaṃ kṣatrāt tu balavattaram ||
children.translated_text: O brahmin, divine brahminical power is stronger than kṣatriya power.
Your power is immeasurable; no one is stronger than you.
<s>Viśvāmitra</s> is of great heroism, but your fiery energy is unassailable.
Command me, O greatly radiant one, me who am filled with your brahminical power;

children.text: tasya darpaṃ balaṃ yat tan nāśayāmi durātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall destroy the pride and the power of that wicked man."

children.text: ity uktas tu tayā rāma vasiṣṭhaḥ sumahāyaśāḥ
children.translated_text: When she had spoken thus, O <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> of very great fame
then said, "Create a force that crushes the enemy's army."
From her bellowing hum there came forth <s>Pahlavas</s> by the hundreds, O king,
and they destroyed all of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>'s army as he looked on.
That king, exceedingly enraged, his eyes widened with anger,
destroyed the <s>Pahlavas</s> with weapons of every high and low kind.
Seeing the hundreds of <s>Pahlavas</s> crushed by <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,
she again created terrible <s>Śakas</s> mixed with <s>Yavanas</s>.

children.text: tair āsīt saṃvṛtā bhūmiḥ śakair yavanamiśritaiḥ
children.translated_text: The earth was covered by those <s>Śakas</s> mixed with <s>Yavanas</s>,
resplendent, greatly heroic, and resembling golden filaments.
Bearing long swords and spears, clad in garments of golden color,

children.text: nirdagdhaṃ tad balaṃ sarvaṃ pradīptair iva pāvakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: that whole army was burned up by them as if by blazing fires.
Then the greatly radiant <s>Viśvāmitra</s> released his missiles.
Then, seeing them bewildered, confused by <s>Viśvāmitra</s>'s missiles,
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s> urged the wish-milking cow, "Create by your power."
From her bellowing hum were born <s>Kāmbojas</s> like the sun,

children.text: ūdhasas tv atha saṃjātāḥ pahlavāḥ śastrapāṇayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and from her udder then arose <s>Pahlavas</s> with weapons in hand.

children.text: yonideśāc ca yavanaḥ śakṛddeśāc chakās tathā
children.translated_text: From the region of her womb came a <s>Yavana</s>, and from the region of her dung <s>Śakas</s> likewise;
from her hair-pores came <s>Mlecchas</s>, <s>Harītas</s>, and <s>Kirātas</s> too.

children.text: tais tan niṣūditaṃ sainyaṃ viśvamitrasya tatkṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: By them that army of <s>Viśvāmitra</s> was cut down in an instant,
with its infantry, elephants, horses, and chariots, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>.
Seeing the army destroyed by great-souled <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,
the hundred sons of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, bearing weapons of many kinds,
ran in great anger against <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, the best of those who mutter prayers.

children.text: huṃkāreṇaiva tān sarvān nirdadāha mahān ṛṣiḥ ||
children.translated_text: With a mere hum the great seer burned them all up.
They, together with horses, chariots, and infantry, by great-souled <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>
were reduced to ashes in a moment, those sons of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā vināśitān putrān balaṃ ca sumahāyaśāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing his sons destroyed, and his army too, the very famous
<s>Viśvāmitra</s> then became ashamed and absorbed in thought.
Like an ocean stilled, like a serpent with broken fangs,
like the sun in eclipse, he at once lost his splendor.
Bereft of sons and army, wretched, like a bird whose wings have been cut off,
his pride destroyed and his energy destroyed, he fell into despondency.

children.text: sa putram ekaṃ rājyāya pālayeti niyujya ca
children.translated_text: Having appointed his one son, saying, "Protect the kingdom,"
he, in accordance with the <s>kṣatra-dharma</s> (warrior's law), went away from the earth to the forest.
Going to the side of <s>Himavat</s>, frequented by kinnaras and serpents,
that great ascetic performed austerities in order to win the favor of <s>Mahādeva</s>.

children.text: kenacit tv atha kālena deveśo vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after some time, the lord of the gods, whose banner bears the bull,
the giver of boons, showed himself to the great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>.

children.text: kimarthaṃ tapyase rājan brūhi yat te vivakṣitam
children.translated_text: "For what purpose are you practicing austerity, O king? Tell me what you wish to say.

children.text: varado 'smi varo yas te kāṅkṣitaḥ so 'bhidhīyatām ||
children.translated_text: I am a giver of boons; let the boon desired by you be stated."

children.text: evam uktas tu devena viśvāmitro mahātapāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the god, the greatly ascetic <s>Viśvāmitra</s>
bowed down to <s>Mahādeva</s> and spoke these words:
"If you are pleased, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, O sinless one, let the dhanurveda be given to me,
complete with its limbs, subsidiary limbs, secret teaching, and mysteries.
And whatever weapons exist among gods, among demons, and among great seers,
among gandharvas, yakṣas, and rākṣasas, let them become manifest to me, O sinless one.
By your grace, O god of gods, let what I desire come to pass."

children.text: evam astv iti deveśo vākyam uktvā divaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: "So be it," said the lord of the gods, and, having spoken that word, he went to heaven.
Having obtained the weapons, the royal seer <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, mighty in strength,
was then joined with great arrogance and became filled with pride.
Growing in valor like the ocean on a full-moon day,

children.text: hatam eva tadā mene vasiṣṭham ṛṣisattamam ||
children.translated_text: he then thought the best of seers, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, already slain.
Then the king went to the hermitage and released the weapons,

children.text: yais tat tapovanaṃ sarvaṃ nirdagdhaṃ cāstratejasā ||
children.translated_text: by whose fiery weapon-power that entire ascetic grove was burned up.
Seeing that weapon of the wise <s>Viśvāmitra</s> being discharged,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā vipradrutā bhītā munayaḥ śataśo diśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the terrified brahmins fled in hundreds to the quarters.

children.text: vasiṣṭhasya ca ye śiṣyās tathaiva mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: And <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s disciples, as well as the deer and birds,
fled in fear, terrified, in thousands toward various directions.
The hermitage of the great-souled <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> became empty,
and for a moment it was silent, like a barren waste.

children.text: vadato vai vasiṣṭhasya mā bhaiṣṭeti muhur muhuḥ
children.translated_text: As <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> kept saying again and again, "Do not be afraid,

children.text: nāśayāmy adya gādheyaṃ nīhāram iva bhāskaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall destroy the son of <s>Gādhi</s> today, like the sun destroying mist,"

children.text: evam uktvā mahātejā vasiṣṭho japatāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: the greatly radiant <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, best of those who mutter sacred formulas,

children.text: viśvāmitraṃ tadā vākyaṃ saroṣam idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: then angrily spoke these words to <s>Viśvāmitra</s>:
"Since you have destroyed this hermitage, long brought to prosperity,

children.text: durācāro 'si yan mūḍha tasmāt tvaṃ na bhaviṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: you are ill-conducted, O fool; therefore you shall not exist."

children.text: ity uktvā paramakruddho daṇḍam udyamya satvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Having said this, extremely enraged, he quickly raised his staff,
like the smokeless fire of time, like another staff of <s>Yama</s>.
Thus addressed by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, mighty <s>Viśvāmitra</s>

children.text: āgneyam astram utkṣipya tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt ||
children.translated_text: lifted up the āgneya weapon and said, "Stand! Stand!"

children.text: vasiṣṭho bhagavān krodhād idaṃ vacanam abravīt
children.translated_text: The blessed <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, in anger, spoke these words:

children.text: kṣatrabandho sthito 'smy eṣa yad balaṃ tad vidarśaya ||
children.translated_text: "O mere kinsman of kṣatriyas, I stand here; show whatever strength you have.

children.text: nāśayāmy eṣa te darpaṃ śastrasya tava gādhija
children.translated_text: I shall destroy this pride of yours in your weapon, O son of <s>Gādhi</s>.

children.text: kva ca te kṣatriyabalaṃ kva ca brahmabalaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: What is your kṣatriya strength, and what is the great strength of brahman?
See my divine brahman-strength, O disgrace of kṣatriyas."
The terrible and excellent āgneya weapon of that son of <s>Gādhi</s>

children.text: brahmadaṇḍena tac chāntam agner vega ivāmbhasā
children.translated_text: was calmed by the brahmadaṇḍa, like the force of fire by water.

children.text: vāruṇaṃ caiva raudraṃ ca aindraṃ pāśupataṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: And he hurled the vāruṇa, the raudra, the aindra, and likewise the pāśupata weapon,
and, enraged, the delight of <s>Gādhi</s> also cast the aiṣīka weapon.

children.text: mānavaṃ mohanaṃ caiva gāndharvaṃ svāpanaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: He cast the mānava and the mohana, and also the gāndharva and the svāpana,
the jṛmbhaṇa and again the mohana, the saṃtāpana and vilāpana,

children.text: śoṣaṇaṃ dāraṇaṃ caiva vajram astraṃ sudurjayam ||
children.translated_text: the śoṣaṇa and dāraṇa, and the vajra weapon, very hard to conquer.

children.text: brahmapāśaṃ kālapāśaṃ vāruṇaṃ pāśam eva ca
children.translated_text: He cast the brahma-pāśa, the kāla-pāśa, and the vāruṇa noose as well,

children.text: pinākāstraṃ ca dayitaṃ śuṣkārdre aśanī tathā ||
children.translated_text: the beloved pināka weapon, and the dry and wet thunderbolts too,

children.text: daṇḍāstram atha paiśācaṃ krauñcam astraṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: then the daṇḍa weapon, the paiśāca, and likewise the krauñca weapon,
the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, the wheel of Time, and likewise the wheel of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: vāyavyaṃ mathanaṃ caiva astraṃ hayaśiras tathā
children.translated_text: the vāyavya and the mathana weapon, and likewise the weapon called hayaśiras,

children.text: śaktidvayaṃ ca cikṣepa kaṅkālaṃ musalaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: and he hurled the two śaktis, the kaṅkāla, and the musala as well,

children.text: vaidyādharaṃ mahāstraṃ ca kālāstram atha dāruṇam
children.translated_text: the great vaidyādhara weapon and then the dreadful kāla weapon,

children.text: triśūlam astraṃ ghoraṃ ca kāpālam atha kaṅkaṇam ||
children.translated_text: the terrible trident weapon, and then the kāpāla and the kaṅkaṇa.
He hurled all these weapons, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>,

children.text: vasiṣṭhe japatāṃ śreṣṭhe tad adbhutam ivābhavat ||
children.translated_text: against <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, best of those who mutter sacred formulas; then it was as if a marvel occurred.

children.text: tāni sarvāṇi daṇḍena grasate brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Brahmā</s> swallowed all of them with his staff.
When those were calmed, the delight of <s>Gādhi</s> cast the brahmāstra.

children.text: tad astram udyataṃ dṛṣṭvā devāḥ sāgnipurogamāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that weapon raised, the gods, with <s>Agni</s> at their head,
and the divine seers, alarmed, together with the gandharvas and great serpents, trembled.
The three worlds were terrified when the brahmāstra was discharged.

children.text: tad apy astraṃ mahāghoraṃ brāhmaṃ brāhmeṇa tejasā ||
children.translated_text: That weapon too, very terrible and brahmanical, by brahmanical splendor,
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s> swallowed completely with the brahmadaṇḍa, O <s>Rāghava</s>.
As the great-souled <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> was swallowing the brahmāstra,
his fierce form, bewildering the three worlds, became exceedingly dreadful.
From every pore of the great-souled <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>
rays shot forth like fire-flames confused with smoke.
And <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s brahmadaṇḍa, raised in his hand, blazed up,
like the smokeless fire of time, like another staff of <s>Yama</s>.
Then the hosts of sages praised <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, best of those who mutter sacred formulas.

children.text: amoghaṃ te balaṃ brahmaṃs tejo dhāraya tejasā
children.translated_text: Your power is unfailing, O brahmin; hold your fiery energy by means of your spiritual energy.
O brahmin, the greatly austere <s>Viśvāmitra</s> has been restrained by you.

children.text: prasīda japatāṃ śreṣṭha lokāḥ santu gatavyathāḥ
children.translated_text: Be gracious, O best of those who mutter sacred formulas; let the worlds be free from distress.

children.text: evam ukto mahātejāḥ śamaṃ cakre mahātapāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, the greatly radiant and greatly austere sage became calm.
<s>Viśvāmitra</s> too, humiliated, sighed and said this:
"Shame on the strength of a kṣatriya; the strength of brahmanical splendor is true strength.
By one brahma-staff all my weapons have been destroyed.
Having considered this, with my senses and mind made clear,
