children.text: tapo mahat samāsthāsye yad vai brahmatvakārakam ||
children.translated_text: I shall undertake great tapas, which indeed brings about brahminhood."
Then, his heart burning as he remembered his own defeat,
sighing again and again, he made enmity with that great-souled one.

children.text: sa dakṣiṇāṃ diśaṃ gatvā mahiṣyā saha rāghava
children.translated_text: He went to the southern quarter with his chief queen, O <s>Rāghava</s>,
and the greatly austere <s>Viśvāmitra</s> practiced exceedingly terrible austerity there.
Eating fruits and roots, self-controlled, he performed supreme tapas.
Then sons were born to him, devoted to truth and dharma:
<s>Haviṣyanda</s>, <s>Madhuṣyanda</s>, and <s>Dṛḍhanetra</s>, a great chariot-warrior.
When a thousand years had been completed, <s>Brahmā</s>, the grandsire of the worlds,
spoke sweet words to <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, whose wealth was tapas:
"The worlds of the royal sages have been won by you through tapas, O son of <s>Kuśika</s>.

children.text: anena tapasā tvāṃ hi rājarṣir iti vidmahe ||
children.translated_text: For by this tapas we recognize you as a royal seer."

children.text: evam uktvā mahātejā jagāma saha daivataiḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the greatly radiant lord, together with the gods,
went to the heavenly Brahma-world, he who is the supreme lord of the worlds.

children.text: viśvāmitro 'pi tac chrutvā hriyā kiṃcid avāṅmukhaḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, hearing that, lowered his face somewhat in shame,
and, overcome by great sorrow and angered, said this:

children.text: tapaś ca sumahat taptaṃ rājarṣir iti māṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: "I have performed very great tapas, yet they know me only as a royal seer.

children.text: devāḥ sarṣigaṇāḥ sarve nāsti manye tapaḥphalam ||
children.translated_text: All the gods together with the hosts of seers think so; I suppose there is no fruit of tapas."

children.text: evaṃ niścitya manasā bhūya eva mahātapāḥ
children.translated_text: Having resolved this in his mind, the greatly austere one again,
O <s>Kākutstha</s>, self-possessed, practiced the highest tapas.

children.text: etasminn eva kāle tu satyavādī jitendriyaḥ
children.translated_text: At this very time there was a truth-speaking, self-controlled king,
famous as <s>Triśaṅku</s>, delight of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> line.

children.text: tasya buddhiḥ samutpannā yajeyam iti rāghava
children.translated_text: This thought arose in him, O <s>Rāghava</s>: "I would perform a sacrifice,
and with this very body I would go to the supreme goal of the gods."
He summoned <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and told him what he had in mind,

children.text: aśakyam iti cāpy ukto vasiṣṭhena mahātmanā ||
children.translated_text: but the great-souled <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> told him, "It is impossible."

children.text: pratyākhyāto vasiṣṭhena sa yayau dakṣiṇāṃ diśam
children.translated_text: Rejected by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, he went to the southern quarter,

children.text: vasiṣṭhā dīrghatapasas tapo yatra hi tepire ||
children.translated_text: where the long-austere sons of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> were practicing tapas.
The very radiant <s>Triśaṅku</s> saw a hundred of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s sons,
most brilliant, famed, and engaged in austerity.

children.text: so 'bhigamya mahātmanaḥ sarvān eva guroḥ sutān
children.translated_text: Approaching all those great-souled sons of his guru,
and bowing to them in order, his face somewhat lowered in shame,
the very radiant king spoke to them all with joined palms:
"I come to you for refuge; I am one seeking refuge among those worthy of refuge.
Good fortune to you; I have been rejected by the great-souled <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.
I desire to perform a great sacrifice; you ought to authorize it.
Having bowed to all the sons of my guru, I seek to win your favor.

children.text: śirasā praṇato yāce brāhmaṇāṃs tapasi sthitān
children.translated_text: With my head bowed, I ask you brahmins who are established in tapas:

children.text: te māṃ bhavantaḥ siddhyarthaṃ yājayantu samāhitāḥ
children.translated_text: let your honors, concentrated, officiate for me for the sake of success,
so that I may obtain the world of the gods with my body intact.
Rejected by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, O ascetics rich in tapas, I see no other course

children.text: guruputrān ṛte sarvān nāhaṃ paśyāmi kāñcana ||
children.translated_text: apart from all the sons of my guru, none at all.

children.text: ikṣvākūṇāṃ hi sarveṣāṃ purodhāḥ paramā gatiḥ
children.translated_text: For the household priest of all the <s>Ikṣvākus</s> is their supreme refuge.

children.text: tasmād anantaraṃ sarve bhavanto daivataṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, after him, you all are my divinity."
Then, hearing <s>Triśaṅku</s>'s words, filled with anger,
O <s>Rāma</s>, the hundred sons of the seer said this to the king:
"Wicked-minded one, you have been rejected by your guru, who speaks truth.
How have you overstepped him and approached another branch?

children.text: ikṣvākūṇāṃ hi sarveṣāṃ purodhāḥ paramā gatiḥ
children.translated_text: For the household priest of all the <s>Ikṣvākus</s> is their supreme refuge,
and the word of one who speaks truth cannot be transgressed.

children.text: aśakyam iti covāca vasiṣṭho bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
children.translated_text: The blessed seer <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> has said, 'It is impossible.'

children.text: taṃ vayaṃ vai samāhartuṃ kratuṃ śaktāḥ kathaṃ tava ||
children.translated_text: How, then, can we undertake your sacrifice?

children.text: bāliśas tvaṃ naraśreṣṭha gamyatāṃ svapuraṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: You are childish, O best of men; go back to your own city.
O king, the blessed one is able to officiate even for the three worlds."
Hearing their speech, its syllables confused by anger,

children.text: sa rājā punar evaitān idaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: the king then again spoke this statement to them:
"I have been rejected by my guru, and likewise by the sons of my guru.

children.text: anyāṃ gatiṃ gamiṣyāmi svasti vo 'stu tapodhanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall go to another refuge. May there be well-being for you, O ascetics rich in tapas."

children.text: ṛṣiputrās tu tac chrutvā vākyaṃ ghorābhisaṃhitam
children.translated_text: But when the sons of the seer heard that statement, charged with a terrible intent,
they became supremely enraged and cursed him: "You shall become a caṇḍāla."

children.text: evam uktvā mahātmāno viviśus te svam āśramam ||
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, those great-souled ones entered their own hermitage.

children.text: atha rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ rājā caṇḍālatāṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, when the night had passed, the king had become a caṇḍāla:
clad in blue garments, dark in color, rough, with his hair ruined,
wearing garlands and unguents from the funeral ground, and adorned with iron ornaments.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā mantriṇaḥ sarve tyaktvā caṇḍālarūpiṇam
children.translated_text: Seeing him in the form of a caṇḍāla, all his ministers abandoned him,
and together, O <s>Rāma</s>, the townspeople who had followed him fled.

children.text: eko hi rājā kākutstha jagāma paramātmavān
children.translated_text: Alone, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, the self-possessed king went
to <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, rich in tapas, burning day and night with anguish.

children.text: viśvāmitras tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā rājānaṃ viphalīkṛtam
children.translated_text: But <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, seeing that king made unsuccessful,
in the form of a <s>caṇḍāla</s>, O <s>Rāma</s>, the sage was moved to compassion.
Out of compassion, that greatly radiant and supremely righteous one

children.text: idaṃ jagāda bhadraṃ te rājānaṃ ghoradarśanam ||
children.translated_text: spoke this word, 'May it be well with you,' to the king, terrible to behold:
'What is the purpose of your coming, O mighty prince,
O hero, lord of <s>Ayodhyā</s>, who through a curse have become a <s>caṇḍāla</s>?'

children.text: atha tad vākyam ākarṇya rājā caṇḍālatāṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, hearing that speech, the king who had become a <s>caṇḍāla</s>
spoke with joined palms, a speaker skilled in speech to one expert in speech:
'I have been rejected by my guru and likewise by the guru's sons;

children.text: anavāpyaiva taṃ kāmaṃ mayā prāpto viparyayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: without obtaining that desire, I have instead met with reversal.

children.text: saśarīro divaṃ yāyām iti me saumyadarśanam
children.translated_text: That I might go to heaven with my body: this, O gentle-looking one,

children.text: mayā ceṣṭaṃ kratuśataṃ tac ca nāvāpyate phalam ||
children.translated_text: was desired by me through a hundred sacrifices, but that fruit is not obtained.

children.text: anṛtaṃ noktapūrvaṃ me na ca vakṣye kadācana
children.translated_text: Never before have I spoken falsehood, nor shall I ever speak it,

children.text: kṛcchreṣv api gataḥ saumya kṣatradharmeṇa te śape ||
children.translated_text: even when fallen into difficulties, O gentle one; I swear this to you by the <s>kṣatriya-dharma</s>.

children.text: yajñair bahuvidhair iṣṭaṃ prajā dharmeṇa pālitāḥ
children.translated_text: I have sacrificed with many kinds of sacrifices; my subjects have been protected according to <s>dharma</s>;
and the great-souled gurus have been satisfied by my conduct and character.
Yet while I strive in <s>dharma</s> and wish to undertake a sacrifice,
the gurus do not become satisfied, O bull among sages.

children.text: daivam eva paraṃ manye pauruṣaṃ tu nirarthakam
children.translated_text: I consider fate alone supreme, and human effort useless;

children.text: daivenākramyate sarvaṃ daivaṃ hi paramā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: everything is overpowered by fate, for fate is the highest course.
For me, who am in extreme distress and desire your favor,
you ought to act, may it be well with you, since my undertaking has been struck down by fate.

children.text: nānyāṃ gatiṃ gamiṣyāmi nānyaḥ śaraṇam asti me
children.translated_text: I shall go to no other refuge; there is no other shelter for me.
You ought to turn back fate by human effort.'
When the king had spoken his words, <s>Kuśika</s>'s son, out of pity,
spoke a sweet word to him, though visibly in the form of a <s>caṇḍāla</s>:

children.text: ikṣvāko svāgataṃ vatsa jānāmi tvāṃ sudhārmikam
children.translated_text: 'Welcome, O child of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>; I know you to be very righteous.

children.text: śaraṇaṃ te bhaviṣyāmi mā bhaiṣīr nṛpapuṃgava ||
children.translated_text: I shall be your refuge; do not fear, O best of kings.
I shall invite all the great seers of meritorious deeds,
helpers in the sacrifice, O king; then you will sacrifice free from anxiety.

children.text: guruśāpakṛtaṃ rūpaṃ yad idaṃ tvayi vartate
children.translated_text: This form that exists in you, produced by your guru's curse,
with this very form, with your body, you shall go to heaven.

children.text: hastaprāptam ahaṃ manye svargaṃ tava nareśvara
children.translated_text: I consider heaven already within your grasp, O lord of men,

children.text: yas tvaṃ kauśikam āgamya śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: since you have come to <s>Kauśika</s>, a refuge, and taken refuge.'
Having spoken thus, the greatly radiant one
instructed his supremely righteous and very wise sons to gather the materials for the sacrifice.

children.text: sarvāñ śiṣyān samāhūya vākyam etad uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: After summoning all his disciples, he spoke this word:
'Children, by my command bring all the best of seers,
together with their disciples and friends, and with learned officiating priests.
Whatever word anyone else may speak, compelled by the force of my command,
all that, even if disrespectful, must be reported to me fully as it was said.'

children.text: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā diśo jagmus tadājñayā
children.translated_text: Hearing that word of his, they went to the quarters by his command,
and then speakers of brahman came from all countries.

children.text: te ca śiṣyāḥ samāgamya muniṃ jvalitatejasam
children.translated_text: Those disciples, having assembled before the sage of blazing splendor,

children.text: ūcuś ca vacanaṃ sarve sarveṣāṃ brahmavādinām ||
children.translated_text: all spoke the word of all the speakers of brahman:

children.text: śrutvā te vacanaṃ sarve samāyānti dvijātayaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Having heard your word, all the twice-born are coming together;
from every region they are coming, except for <s>Mahodaya</s>.
That whole hundred of <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, their speech disturbed by anger,

children.text: yad āha vacanaṃ sarvaṃ śṛṇu tvaṃ munipuṃgava ||
children.translated_text: said these words; hear it all, O bull among sages.
When a <s>kṣatriya</s> is officiating priest, especially for a <s>caṇḍāla</s>,

children.text: kathaṃ sadasi bhoktāro havis tasya surarṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: how will gods and seers be eaters of his oblation in the sacrificial assembly?
Or how will great-souled brahmins, having eaten a <s>caṇḍāla</s>'s food,
go to heaven, protected by <s>Viśvāmitra</s>?
This cruel statement they uttered, their eyes reddened,
the <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, O tiger among sages, all together with <s>Mahodaya</s>.'
Hearing that statement of theirs, the bull among sages,
his eyes reddened with anger, angrily spoke this:

children.text: yad dūṣayanty aduṣṭaṃ māṃ tapa ugraṃ samāsthitam
children.translated_text: 'Since they reproach me, who am not to be reproached, while I stand firm in fierce austerity,
those evil-minded men shall become ashes; there is no doubt.
Today, led by the noose of Time to the abode of <s>Vaivasvata</s>,
let them all become corpse-drinkers for seven hundred births.
With dog flesh as their fixed food, pitiless ones called <s>Muṣṭikas</s>,

children.text: vikṛtāś ca virūpāś ca lokān anucarantv imān ||
children.translated_text: deformed and ugly, let them wander through these worlds.

children.text: mahodayaś ca durbuddhir mām adūṣyaṃ hy adūṣayat
children.translated_text: And ill-minded <s>Mahodaya</s> has reproached me, who am not to be reproached;
disgraced in all the worlds, he shall fall into the state of a <s>Niṣāda</s>.
Devoted to the killing of living beings, having become merciless,
for a long time, because of my anger, he shall live in an evil state.'
Having spoken only so much of this statement, the greatly ascetic <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,
the great sage of mighty splendor, fell silent in the midst of the seers.
Having made the <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s> and <s>Mahodaya</s> struck down by the power of his austerity,
the greatly radiant <s>Viśvāmitra</s> spoke in the midst of the seers:
'This is <s>Triśaṅku</s>, famed as the heir of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>;

children.text: dharmiṣṭhaś ca vadānyaś ca māṃ caiva śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: he is most righteous and generous, and he has come to me for refuge,
with the wish to conquer the world of the gods in this body of his.
So that this man may go to the world of the gods in his own body,

children.text: tathā pravartyatāṃ yajño bhavadbhiś ca mayā saha ||
children.translated_text: let the sacrifice be set in motion by you together with me.'
Hearing <s>Viśvāmitra</s>'s word, all the great seers
The dharma-knowing sages, assembled together, spoke to him who was joined to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order):
"This sage, the descendant of <s>Kuśika</s>, is exceedingly prone to anger.

children.text: yad āha vacanaṃ samyag etat kāryaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever word he has spoken, that must properly be done; there is no doubt.

children.text: agnikalpo hi bhagavāñ śāpaṃ dāsyati roṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: For the blessed one is like fire; if angered, he will give a curse.

children.text: tasmāt pravartyatāṃ yajñaḥ saśarīro yathā divam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore let the sacrifice be set in motion, so that, in his body, to heaven
the descendant of <s>Ikṣvāku</s> may go by the splendor of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>.
Then let the sacrifice proceed; all of you preside over it together."

children.text: evam uktvā maharṣayaḥ saṃjahrus tāḥ kriyās tadā
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the great seers then carried out those rites,
and the greatly radiant <s>Viśvāmitra</s> became the officiating priest in the sacrifice.
The officiants, in due order, knowing the mantras and possessed of the mantras,
performed all the acts according to the ritual rule and according to the prescribed manner.
Then, after a long time, <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, great in austerity,
there invoked all the gods for the sake of their portions.
But when summoned at that time, all the gods did not come for their portions.
Then the great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s> was filled with anger.

children.text: sruvam udyamya sakrodhas triśaṅkum idam abravīt
children.translated_text: Raising the sruva-ladle angrily, he said this to <s>Triśaṅku</s>:

children.text: paśya me tapaso vīryaṃ svārjitasya nareśvara ||
children.translated_text: "Behold the power of my austerity, earned by myself, O lord of men.

children.text: eṣa tvāṃ svaśarīreṇa nayāmi svargam ojasā
children.translated_text: Now, by my strength, I shall bring you to heaven in your own body.
Go to heaven, hard to attain in one's own body, O lord of men.

children.text: svārjitaṃ kiṃcid apy asti mayā hi tapasaḥ phalam
children.translated_text: Indeed, if there is even some fruit of austerity earned by me,

children.text: rājaṃs tvaṃ tejasā tasya saśarīro divaṃ vraja ||
children.translated_text: O king, by the splendor of that, go bodily to heaven."
When that sage had spoken, the lord of men, in his own body,

children.text: divaṃ jagāma kākutstha munīnāṃ paśyatāṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: went to heaven, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, while the sages were watching.
Seeing <s>Triśaṅku</s> gone to the world of the gods, <s>Pākaśāsana</s>,

children.text: saha sarvaiḥ suragaṇair idaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: together with all the hosts of gods, spoke this word:

children.text: triśaṅko gaccha bhūyas tvaṃ nāsi svargakṛtālayaḥ
children.translated_text: "<s>Triśaṅku</s>, go back again; you are not one who has made a dwelling in heaven.
Struck by your guru's curse, fool, fall to the earth head downward."

children.text: evam ukto mahendreṇa triśaṅkur apatat punaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by mighty <s>Indra</s>, <s>Triśaṅku</s> fell again,
crying out, "Protect me!" to <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, rich in austerity.

children.text: tac chrutvā vacanaṃ tasya krośamānasya kauśikaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that word of his as he cried out, <s>Kauśika</s>

children.text: roṣam āhārayat tīvraṃ tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt ||
children.translated_text: summoned up fierce anger and said, "Stay! Stay!"
That radiant one, in the midst of the seers, like another <s>Prajāpati</s>,
then created another set of Seven Seers stationed on the southern path.
Bewildered by anger, he created another garland of constellations,
taking his stand in the southern quarter, the highly renowned one among the sages.
And having created a lineage of stars, tainted by anger,

children.text: anyam indraṃ kariṣyāmi loko vā syād anindrakaḥ
children.translated_text: he said, "I shall make another <s>Indra</s>, or the world shall be without <s>Indra</s>."

children.text: daivatāny api sa krodhāt sraṣṭuṃ samupacakrame ||
children.translated_text: In anger, he even set about creating gods.
Then the excellent gods, together with assemblies of seers, became exceedingly alarmed,
and spoke a conciliatory word to great-souled <s>Viśvāmitra</s>:
"This king, O greatly fortunate one, has been afflicted by his guru's curse.

children.text: saśarīro divaṃ yātuṃ nārhaty eva tapodhana ||
children.translated_text: He is certainly not worthy to go bodily to heaven, O treasure of austerity."
Hearing that word of the gods, the bull among sages
<s>Kauśika</s> spoke a very weighty statement to all the gods:

children.text: saśarīrasya bhadraṃ vas triśaṅkor asya bhūpateḥ
children.translated_text: "Blessings to you: having promised the bodily ascent of this king <s>Triśaṅku</s>,
I cannot make it false.
Let there be an eternal creation for this <s>Triśaṅku</s> in his body,

children.text: nakṣatrāṇi ca sarvāṇi māmakāni dhruvāṇy atha ||
children.translated_text: and let all these stars of mine be fixed.

children.text: yāval lokā dhariṣyanti tiṣṭhantv etāni sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: As long as the worlds shall endure, let all these remain,

children.text: matkṛtāni surāḥ sarve tad anujñātum arhatha ||
children.translated_text: made by me. All you gods should approve this."

children.text: evam uktāḥ surāḥ sarve pratyūcur munipuṃgavam ||
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, all the gods replied to the bull among sages:

children.text: evaṃ bhavatu bhadraṃ te tiṣṭhantv etāni sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: "So be it; welfare to you. Let all these remain entirely,
many in the sky, outside the path of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.
O best of sages, among those lights and stars, blazing,
let <s>Triśaṅku</s>, head downward, remain like an immortal."
But righteous <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, praised by all the gods,

children.text: ṛṣibhiś ca mahātejā bāḍham ity āha devatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and by the seers, the greatly radiant one, said firmly, "Yes," to the deities.

children.text: tato devā mahātmāno munayaś ca tapodhanāḥ
children.translated_text: Then the great-souled gods and the sages rich in austerity
all went as they had come at the end of the sacrifice, O best of men.

children.text: viśvāmitro mahātmātha prasthitān prekṣya tān ṛṣīn
children.translated_text: Then great-souled <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, seeing those seers set out,
said to all those forest-dwellers, O tiger among men:
"A great obstacle has arisen, occupying the southern quarter.

children.text: diśam anyāṃ prapatsyāmas tatra tapsyāmahe tapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: We shall resort to another direction; there we shall practice austerity.
In the broad western region, at <s>Puṣkara</s>, O great-souled ones,

children.text: sukhaṃ tapaś cariṣyāmaḥ paraṃ taddhi tapovanam ||
children.translated_text: we shall happily practice supreme austerity, for that is a forest of austerity."
Having spoken thus, the greatly radiant great sage, at <s>Puṣkara</s>,
performed fierce, unassailable austerity, living on roots and fruits.

children.text: etasminn eva kāle tu ayodhyādhipatir nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: At just that time, the king who was lord of <s>Ayodhyā</s>,
renowned as <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, set about performing a sacrifice.

children.text: tasya vai yajamānasya paśum indro jahāra ha
children.translated_text: While he was sacrificing, <s>Indra</s> carried off the sacrificial animal.

children.text: pranaṣṭe tu paśau vipro rājānam idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: When the animal had disappeared, the brahmin said this to the king:

children.text: paśur adya hṛto rājan pranaṣṭas tava durnayāt
children.translated_text: "The animal has today been carried off, O king, lost through your bad policy.
Faults strike down a king who does not protect, O lord of men.

children.text: prāyaścittaṃ mahaddhy etan naraṃ vā puruṣarṣabha
children.translated_text: This indeed is a great expiation: bring a man instead, O bull among men,

children.text: ānayasva paśuṃ śīghraṃ yāvat karma pravartate ||
children.translated_text: or quickly bring the sacrificial animal, while the rite is still proceeding."
Hearing the preceptor's words, that king, O bull among men,
The great-minded one searched for the sacrificial animal, along with thousands of cows.

children.text: deśāñ janapadāṃs tāṃs tān nagarāṇi vanāni ca
children.translated_text: He searched those various regions and countries, and cities and forests,
and holy hermitages too, as the lord of the earth sought it.
O dear one, O <s>Raghunandana</s>, he saw him together with his sons and his wife,
he saw <s>Ṛcīka</s> seated at <s>Bhṛgutunda</s>.
The one of great splendor bowed to him, won his favor, and spoke to him,
the royal sage of immeasurable radiance addressing the brahmarṣi blazing with tapas,

children.text: pṛṣṭvā sarvatra kuśalam ṛcīkaṃ tam idaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: after asking <s>Ṛcīka</s> about his welfare in every respect, these words:
"If you will sell your son for a hundred thousand cows,
then, O greatly blessed <s>Bhārgava</s>, I shall have fulfilled my purpose regarding the victim.

children.text: sarve parisṛtā deśā yajñiyaṃ na labhe paśum
children.translated_text: I have traversed all regions, but I do not find an animal fit for sacrifice.

children.text: dātum arhasi mūlyena sutam ekam ito mama ||
children.translated_text: You ought to give me one son from here for a price."

children.text: evam ukto mahātejā ṛcīkas tv abravīd vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, the very radiant <s>Ṛcīka</s> replied with these words:
"O best of men, I would never sell my eldest son in any way."

children.text: ṛcīkasya vacaḥ śrutvā teṣāṃ mātā mahātmanām
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Ṛcīka</s>'s words, the mother of those great-souled sons,
the ascetic woman, said to <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, tiger among men:

children.text: mamāpi dayitaṃ viddhi kaniṣṭhaṃ śunakaṃ nṛpa ||
children.translated_text: "Know, O king, that the youngest, <s>Śunaka</s>, is dear to me as well.

children.text: prāyeṇa hi naraśreṣṭha jyeṣṭhāḥ pitṛṣu vallabhāḥ
children.translated_text: For generally, O best of men, eldest sons are dear to fathers,

children.text: mātṝṇāṃ ca kanīyāṃsas tasmād rakṣe kanīyasam ||
children.translated_text: and younger sons to mothers; therefore I protect the youngest."

children.text: uktavākye munau tasmin munipatnyāṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: When the sage had spoken, and the sage's wife likewise,

children.text: śunaḥśepaḥ svayaṃ rāma madhyamo vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Śunaḥśepa</s>, the middle son, himself spoke these words:

children.text: pitā jyeṣṭham avikreyaṃ mātā cāha kanīyasam
children.translated_text: "My father says the eldest is not to be sold, and my mother says the youngest is not.

children.text: vikrītaṃ madhyamaṃ manye rājan putraṃ nayasva mām ||
children.translated_text: I consider the middle son sold, O king; take me away."
Then the lord of men, for a hundred thousand cows,
took <s>Śunaḥśepa</s> and, supremely pleased, departed, O <s>Raghunandana</s>.

children.text: ambarīṣas tu rājarṣī ratham āropya satvaraḥ
children.translated_text: But the royal sage <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, that greatly renowned one, quickly mounted him on the chariot,
and swiftly went away with the very radiant <s>Śunaḥśepa</s>.
Having taken <s>Śunaḥśepa</s>, O best of men, the greatly renowned one
rested at midday at <s>Puṣkara</s>, O <s>Raghunandana</s>.
While he was resting, the greatly renowned <s>Śunaḥśepa</s>,

children.text: puṣkaraṃ śreṣṭham āgamya viśvāmitraṃ dadarśa ha ||
children.translated_text: having reached excellent <s>Puṣkara</s>, saw <s>Viśvāmitra</s> there.

children.text: viṣaṇṇavadano dīnas tṛṣṇayā ca śrameṇa ca
children.translated_text: With dejected face, wretched from thirst and fatigue,

children.text: papātāṅke mune rāma vākyaṃ cedam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: he fell into the sage's lap, O <s>Rāma</s>, and spoke these words:

children.text: na me 'sti mātā na pitā jñātayo bāndhavāḥ kutaḥ
children.translated_text: "I have no mother and no father; how could I have kinsmen or relatives?

children.text: trātum arhasi māṃ saumya dharmeṇa munipuṃgava ||
children.translated_text: You ought to save me according to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), O gentle bull among sages.

children.text: trātā tvaṃ hi muniśreṣṭha sarveṣāṃ tvaṃ hi bhāvanaḥ
children.translated_text: For you are a savior, O best of sages, and you are the benefactor of all.

children.text: rājā ca kṛtakāryaḥ syād ahaṃ dīrghāyur avyayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The king would have his purpose accomplished, and I would live long, uninjured.

children.text: svargalokam upāśnīyāṃ tapas taptvā hy anuttamam
children.translated_text: Having practiced unsurpassed tapas, I would attain the world of heaven.

children.text: sa me nātho hy anāthasya bhava bhavyena cetasā
children.translated_text: With a kindly mind, become the protector of me who have no protector.

children.text: piteva putraṃ dharmātmaṃs trātum arhasi kilbiṣāt ||
children.translated_text: O righteous one, like a father saving his son, you ought to save me from sin."
Hearing that speech of his, <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, great in tapas,

children.text: sāntvayitvā bahuvidhaṃ putrān idam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: comforted him in many ways and then said this to his sons:
"That purpose for which parents beget sons, desiring what is good,
for the sake of benefit in the next world, the time for that has now come.

children.text: ayaṃ munisuto bālo mattaḥ śaraṇam icchati
children.translated_text: This young son of a sage seeks refuge from me.
By the mere gift of his life, my sons, do what is pleasing for him.
You are all doers of meritorious deeds, all devoted to <s>dharma</s>.
Become the king's victims and give satisfaction to Agni.

children.text: nāthavāṃś ca śunaḥśepo yajñaś cāvighnato bhavet
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śunaḥśepa</s> would have a protector, and the sacrifice would proceed without obstacle;

children.text: devatās tarpitāś ca syur mama cāpi kṛtaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the deities would be satisfied, and my word too would be fulfilled."

children.text: munes tu vacanaṃ śrutvā madhuṣyandādayaḥ sutāḥ
children.translated_text: But hearing the sage's words, his sons, beginning with <s>Madhuṣyanda</s>,
spoke this with pride and disdain, O best of men:
"How, lord, can you abandon your own sons and save another's son?

children.text: akāryam iva paśyāmaḥ śvamāṃsam iva bhojane ||
children.translated_text: We see this as something improper, like eating dog's meat."

children.text: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā putrāṇāṃ munipuṃgavaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech of his sons, the bull among sages,
his eyes reddened with anger, began to utter a curse:

children.text: niḥsādhvasam idaṃ proktaṃ dharmād api vigarhitam
children.translated_text: "This has been spoken without fear, condemned even by <s>dharma</s>,
transgressing my word, cruel and causing the hair to stand on end.
All of you shall become eaters of dog's meat, like the <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, among degraded births,
and you shall dwell on earth for a full thousand years."
Then, having made his sons subject to the curse, the best of sages
spoke to the afflicted <s>Śunaḥśepa</s>, after securing faultless protection for him:
"Bound with sacred cords, adorned with red garlands and unguents,

children.text: vaiṣṇavaṃ yūpam āsādya vāgbhir agnim udāhara ||
children.translated_text: approaching the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> sacrificial post, invoke Agni with your words.

children.text: ime tu gāthe dve divye gāyethā muniputraka
children.translated_text: Sing these two divine verses, O son of a sage,
at this sacrifice of <s>Ambarīṣa</s>; then you will attain success."

children.text: śunaḥśepo gṛhītvā te dve gāthe susamāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śunaḥśepa</s>, composed in mind, took those two verses,

children.text: tvarayā rājasiṃhaṃ tam ambarīṣam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: and in haste spoke to that lion among kings, <s>Ambarīṣa</s>:
"O lion among kings, great-hearted one, let us go quickly to the sacrificial assembly.
Return, O king of kings, and undertake the consecration."

children.text: tad vākyam ṛṣiputrasya śrutvā harṣaṃ samutsukaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech of the seer's son, the king, eager with joy,
went swiftly and diligently to the sacrificial enclosure.
With the approval of the officiants, the king marked the victim with purifying signs,

children.text: paśuṃ raktāmbaraṃ kṛtvā yūpe taṃ samabandhayat ||
children.translated_text: clothed him in red garments, and bound him to the sacrificial post.

children.text: sa baddho vāgbhir agryābhir abhituṣṭāva vai surau
children.translated_text: Bound there, the son of the sage praised the two gods with excellent words,
<s>Indra</s> and <s>Indra</s>'s younger brother, exactly as prescribed.
Then <s>Sahasrākṣa</s>, pleased and satisfied by the secret hymn,

children.text: dīrgham āyus tadā prādāc chunaḥśepāya rāghava ||
children.translated_text: Then he granted long life to <s>Śunaḥśepa</s>, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: sa ca rājā naraśreṣṭha yajñasya ca samāptavān
children.translated_text: And that king, O best of men, completed the sacrifice,
receiving abundant fruit produced by the favor of the thousand-eyed one.
Righteous <s>Viśvāmitra</s> too again practiced great austerity,
at <s>Puṣkara</s>, O best of men, for ten hundreds of years.
When a thousand years had been completed, the great sage, bathed after his vow,
was approached by all the gods, wishing to grant the fruit of his austerity.
Greatly radiant <s>Brahmā</s> spoke pleasing words:

children.text: ṛṣis tvam asi bhadraṃ te svārjitaiḥ karmabhiḥ śubhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: "You are a seer; welfare to you, by the auspicious deeds you have won for yourself."

children.text: tam evam uktvā deveśas tridivaṃ punar abhyagāt
children.translated_text: Having spoken to him in this way, the lord of the gods went back to heaven.

children.text: viśvāmitro mahātejā bhūyas tepe mahat tapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And greatly radiant <s>Viśvāmitra</s> again practiced great austerity.
Then, after a long time, the supreme apsaras <s>Menakā</s>
began to bathe at <s>Puṣkara</s>, O best of men.
The greatly radiant son of <s>Kuśika</s> saw her there, <s>Menakā</s>,
unmatched in beauty, like lightning in a cloud.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā kandarpavaśago munis tām idam abravīt
children.translated_text: Seeing her, the sage, brought under the power of desire, said this to her:

children.text: apsaraḥ svāgataṃ te 'stu vasa ceha mamāśrame
children.translated_text: "Apsaras, welcome to you. Stay here in my hermitage,
and favor me; welfare to you. I have been deeply bewildered by <s>Madana</s>."

children.text: ity uktā sā varārohā tatrāvāsam athākarot
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, that woman of lovely hips then made her dwelling there.
For a great obstacle to austerity had come upon <s>Viśvāmitra</s>.

children.text: tasyāṃ vasantyāṃ varṣāṇi pañca pañca ca rāghava
children.translated_text: While she was living there, five and five years, O <s>Rāghava</s>,
passed happily in <s>Viśvāmitra</s>'s hermitage, gentle one.

children.text: atha kāle gate tasmin viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ
children.translated_text: Then, when that time had passed, the great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>
became as if ashamed, given over to anxiety and grief.
An indignant thought arose in the sage, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>:
"All this is the work of the gods, a great theft of my austerity.
Ten years have passed under the guise of days and nights;
this obstacle has arisen for me, overcome by infatuation through desire."
The best of sages sighed deeply, distressed by remorse.

children.text: bhītām apsarasaṃ dṛṣṭvā vepantīṃ prāñjaliṃ sthitām
children.translated_text: Seeing the frightened apsaras standing with joined palms and trembling,
the son of <s>Kuśika</s> dismissed <s>Menakā</s> with gentle words,

children.text: uttaraṃ parvataṃ rāma viśvāmitro jagāma ha ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Viśvāmitra</s> went to the northern mountain, O <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: sa kṛtvā naiṣṭhikīṃ buddhiṃ jetukāmo mahāyaśāḥ
children.translated_text: Having formed a fixed resolve, the greatly renowned one, desiring to conquer,
reached the bank of the <s>Kauśikī</s> and practiced exceedingly terrible austerity.

children.text: tasya varṣasahasraṃ tu ghoraṃ tapa upāsataḥ
children.translated_text: While he was engaged in terrible austerity for a thousand years,

children.text: uttare parvate rāma devatānām abhūd bhayam ||
children.translated_text: on the northern mountain, O <s>Rāma</s>, fear arose among the gods.
All the gods, together with the hosts of seers, assembled and conferred:
"Let this son of <s>Kuśika</s> properly obtain the title of great seer."
Hearing the words of the gods, the grandsire of all the worlds
spoke a sweet word to <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, rich in austerity:
"Welcome, great seer, my child. I am pleased by your fierce austerity.
I grant you greatness and the status of foremost among seers, O <s>Kauśika</s>."

children.text: brahmaṇaḥ sa vacaḥ śrutvā viśvāmitras tapodhanaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that word of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, rich in austerity,
with joined palms and having bowed down, replied to the grandsire:
"If the blessed one calls me by the unequalled title of brahmin-seer,

children.text: yadi me bhagavān āha tato 'haṃ vijitendriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: through my own auspicious deeds, then I am one who has conquered his senses."

children.text: tam uvāca tato brahmā na tāvat tvaṃ jitendriyaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s> said to him, "You have not yet conquered your senses.

children.text: yatasva muniśārdūla ity uktvā tridivaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Strive on, tiger among sages." Having said this, he went to heaven.
When the gods had departed, the great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,
with arms raised, without support, living on air, practiced austerity.
In the hot season he became one practicing the five fires; in the rainy season he stayed exposed to the sky;
in winter he remained in water by night and day, rich in austerity.

children.text: evaṃ varṣasahasraṃ hi tapo ghoram upāgamat
children.translated_text: In this way he undertook terrible austerity for a thousand years.
But while the great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s> was thus heating himself in austerity,

children.text: sambhramaḥ sumahān āsīt surāṇāṃ vāsavasya ca
children.translated_text: a very great agitation arose among the gods and among <s>Vāsava</s>.

children.text: rambhām apsarasaṃ śakraḥ saha sarvair marudgaṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s>, together with all the hosts of <s>Maruts</s>, addressed the apsaras <s>Rambhā</s>,
speaking words beneficial to himself and harmful to <s>Kauśika</s>:

children.text: surakāryam idaṃ rambhe kartavyaṃ sumahat tvayā
children.translated_text: "This very great task of the gods must be done by you, <s>Rambhā</s>:
the seduction here of <s>Kauśika</s>, joined with desire and delusion."
Thus addressed, O <s>Rāma</s>, by the wise thousand-eyed one, that apsaras,
ashamed and with joined palms, replied to the lord of the gods:
"This great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s> is terrible, O lord of the gods.

children.text: krodham utsrakṣyate ghoraṃ mayi deva na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: He will unleash terrible anger against me, O god; there is no doubt.

children.text: tato hi me bhayaṃ deva prasādaṃ kartum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: Therefore I am afraid, O god. You ought to show me favor."
The thousand-eyed one said to her, as she trembled with joined palms:

children.text: mā bhaiṣī rambhe bhadraṃ te kuruṣva mama śāsanam ||
children.translated_text: "Do not be afraid, <s>Rambhā</s>; welfare to you. Carry out my command.
As a heart-captivating cuckoo amid beautiful trees in spring,
I shall stand beside you together with <s>Kandarpa</s>.

children.text: tvaṃ hi rūpaṃ bahuguṇaṃ kṛtvā paramabhāsvaram
children.translated_text: You, having made your form rich in many charms and supremely radiant,

children.text: tam ṛṣiṃ kauśikaṃ rambhe bhedayasva tapasvinam ||
children.translated_text: must break that ascetic seer <s>Kauśika</s>, O <s>Rambhā</s>."

children.text: sā śrutvā vacanaṃ tasya kṛtvā rūpam anuttamam
children.translated_text: Hearing his word, she made her form unsurpassed,
and the graceful one with a bright smile tempted <s>Viśvāmitra</s>.

children.text: kokilasya tu śuśrāva valgu vyāharataḥ svanam
children.translated_text: He heard the sweet sound of the cuckoo calling pleasantly,
and then, with a delighted mind, he looked toward her.

children.text: atha tasya ca śabdena gītenāpratimena ca
children.translated_text: Then, because of that sound, and because of the incomparable song,

children.text: darśanena ca rambhāyā muniḥ saṃdeham āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and because of the sight of <s>Rambhā</s>, the sage fell into suspicion.
Recognizing that deed as the work of the thousand-eyed one, the bull among sages
Filled with anger, the son of <s>Kuśika</s> cursed <s>Rambhā</s>.
"Because you tempt me, <s>Rambhā</s>, when I seek victory over desire and anger,
for ten thousand years you shall remain as stone, unfortunate one.
A brahmin of very great brilliance, endowed with the power of austerity,
will release you, <s>Rambhā</s>, who have been stained by my anger."
Having spoken thus, the greatly brilliant great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>
was unable to hold back his anger and fell into burning distress.

children.text: tasya śāpena mahatā rambhā śailī tadābhavat
children.translated_text: By that great curse of his, <s>Rambhā</s> then became stone,

children.text: vacaḥ śrutvā ca kandarpo maharṣeḥ sa ca nirgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, hearing the great seer's words, <s>Kandarpa</s> too departed.
Because his austerity had been diminished through anger, that greatly brilliant one,

children.text: indriyair ajitai rāma na lebhe śāntim ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: with his senses unconquered, O <s>Rāma</s>, did not obtain peace within himself.

children.text: atha haimavatīṃ rāma diśaṃ tyaktvā mahāmuniḥ
children.translated_text: Then, O <s>Rāma</s>, leaving the Himalayan quarter, the great sage

children.text: pūrvāṃ diśam anuprāpya tapas tepe sudāruṇam ||
children.translated_text: reached the eastern quarter and practiced very terrible austerity.
Having undertaken a silence of a thousand years, an unsurpassed vow,
he performed matchless austerity, O <s>Rāma</s>, exceedingly hard to carry out.
But when the thousand years were complete, the great sage had become like a log;

children.text: vighnair bahubhir ādhūtaṃ krodho nāntaram āviśat ||
children.translated_text: though shaken by many obstacles, anger found no opening in him.
Then the gods, together with gandharvas, serpents, asuras, and rākṣasas,
were bewildered by the power of his austerity, their rays grown dim,
and all, overcome by faintness, then spoke to the Grandfather.
"O god, though the great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>
has been tempted and angered in many ways, he grows still greater through austerity.

children.text: na hy asya vṛjinaṃ kiṃcid dṛśyate sūkṣmam apy atha
children.translated_text: No fault at all is seen in him now, not even the slightest one.

children.text: na dīyate yadi tv asya manasā yad abhīpsitam
children.translated_text: But if what he desires in his mind is not granted to him,
he will destroy the three worlds, with all that moves and does not move, by his austerity.

children.text: sāgarāḥ kṣubhitāḥ sarve viśīryante ca parvatāḥ
children.translated_text: All the oceans are agitated, and the mountains are breaking apart;

children.text: prakampate ca pṛthivī vāyur vāti bhṛśākulaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the earth trembles, and the wind blows in great disorder.

children.text: buddhiṃ na kurute yāvan nāśe deva mahāmuniḥ
children.translated_text: Before the great sage forms the thought of destruction, O god,
the blessed one, fire-formed and of great radiance, should be propitiated.
As once before, the whole three worlds are being burned by the fire of time.

children.text: devarājye cikīrṣeta dīyatām asya yan matam ||
children.translated_text: If he should wish to make himself king of the gods, let what he intends be given to him."
Then all the hosts of gods, with the Grandfather at their head,
spoke a sweet word to great-souled <s>Viśvāmitra</s>:

children.text: brahmarṣe svāgataṃ te 'stu tapasā sma sutoṣitāḥ
children.translated_text: "Welcome to you, brahmarṣi. We are well pleased by your austerity.
Through your fierce austerity you have attained brahminhood, O <s>Kauśika</s>.

children.text: dīrgham āyuś ca te brahman dadāmi samarudgaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: And I, together with the Marut hosts, grant you long life, O brahmin.

children.text: svasti prāpnuhi bhadraṃ te gaccha saumya yathāsukham ||
children.translated_text: May there be well-being for you; blessings on you. Go, gentle one, as you please."
Hearing the words of the Grandfather and of all the dwellers in heaven,
the great sage made obeisance and, delighted, spoke out:

children.text: brāhmaṇyaṃ yadi me prāptaṃ dīrgham āyus tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: "If brahminhood has been attained by me, and long life likewise,

children.text: oṃkāro 'tha vaṣaṭkāro vedāś ca varayantu mām ||
children.translated_text: then let the syllable Om, the vaṣaṭ-call, and the Vedas acknowledge me.
Let the foremost knower of the kṣatra-veda and also of the brahma-veda,

children.text: brahmaputro vasiṣṭho mām evaṃ vadatu devatāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, son of <s>Brahmā</s>, say this of me, O deities.

children.text: yady ayaṃ paramaḥ kāmaḥ kṛto yāntu surarṣabhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: If this highest desire has been fulfilled, then let the bulls among gods go."

children.text: tataḥ prasādito devair vasiṣṭho japatāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, best of those who recite, was propitiated by the gods;

children.text: sakhyaṃ cakāra brahmarṣir evam astv iti cābravīt ||
children.translated_text: the brahmarṣi made friendship and said, "So be it."

children.text: brahmarṣitvaṃ na saṃdehaḥ sarvaṃ sampatsyate tava
children.translated_text: "Your brahmarṣihood is beyond doubt; everything will be accomplished for you."

children.text: ity uktvā devatāś cāpi sarvā jagmur yathāgatam ||
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, all the deities too went away as they had come.
Righteous <s>Viśvāmitra</s> also, having obtained supreme brahminhood,
honored the brahmarṣi <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, best of those who recite.

children.text: kṛtakāmo mahīṃ sarvāṃ cacāra tapasi sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Having fulfilled his desire, he wandered over the whole earth, established in austerity.

children.text: evaṃ tv anena brāhmaṇyaṃ prāptaṃ rāma mahātmanā ||
children.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Rāma</s>, brahminhood was obtained by this great-souled one.

children.text: eṣa rāma muniśreṣṭha eṣa vigrahavāṃs tapaḥ
children.translated_text: This, O <s>Rāma</s>, is the best of sages; this is austerity embodied.

children.text: eṣa dharmaḥ paro nityaṃ vīryasyaiṣa parāyaṇam ||
children.translated_text: This is supreme eternal dharma; this is the final refuge of heroic power."
Hearing <s>Śatānanda</s>'s words in the presence of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
<s>Janaka</s>, with joined palms, spoke this word to the son of <s>Kuśika</s>:
"I am blessed; I have been favored, O bull among sages,

children.text: yajñaṃ kākutstha sahitaḥ prāptavān asi dhārmika ||
children.translated_text: since you, righteous one, have come to my sacrifice together with <s>Kākutstha</s>.
I have been purified by you, O brahmin, by your sight, O great sage;

children.text: guṇā bahuvidhāḥ prāptās tava saṃdarśanān mayā ||
children.translated_text: through seeing you I have obtained many kinds of virtues.

children.text: vistareṇa ca te brahman kīrtyamānaṃ mahat tapaḥ
children.translated_text: Your great austerity, O brahmin, as it has been recounted in detail,

children.text: śrutaṃ mayā mahātejo rāmeṇa ca mahātmanā ||
children.translated_text: has been heard by me, O greatly brilliant one, and by great-souled <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: sadasyaiḥ prāpya ca sadaḥ śrutās te bahavo guṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And after reaching the assembly, the members of the assembly have heard your many virtues.

children.text: aprameyaṃ tapas tubhyam aprameyaṃ ca te balam
children.translated_text: Your austerity is immeasurable, and your power too is immeasurable;

children.text: aprameyā guṇāś caiva nityaṃ te kuśikātmaja ||
children.translated_text: your virtues also are always immeasurable, O son of <s>Kuśika</s>.

children.text: tṛptir āścaryabhūtānāṃ kathānāṃ nāsti me vibho
children.translated_text: There is no satiety for me in these wondrous tales, O lord;
but the time for the rite is passing, O best of sages, and the sun's disk is hanging low.

children.text: śvaḥ prabhāte mahātejo draṣṭum arhasi māṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Tomorrow at daybreak, O greatly brilliant one, you should see me again.

children.text: svāgataṃ tapatāṃ śreṣṭha mām anujñātum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: Welcome to you, best of ascetics; you should permit me to depart."
Having spoken thus to the best of sages, the <s>Vaideha</s>, lord of <s>Mithilā</s>,
quickly circumambulated him, together with his preceptor and his kinsmen.
Righteous <s>Viśvāmitra</s> too, together with <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
went to his own enclosure, honored by the great seers.
Then, on the clear morning, the king, having performed his duties,
summoned great-souled <s>Viśvāmitra</s> together with <s>Rāghava</s>.
Having honored him, righteous one, with a rite prescribed by śāstra (scriptural rule),

children.text: rāghavau ca mahātmānau tadā vākyam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: And then he spoke these words to the two great-souled descendants of <s>Raghu</s> as well:

children.text: bhagavan svāgataṃ te 'stu kiṃ karomi tavānagha
children.translated_text: "Blessed sir, welcome to you. What may I do for you, sinless one?

children.text: bhavān ājñāpayatu mām ājñāpyo bhavatā hy aham ||
children.translated_text: Let your honor command me; for I am one to be commanded by you."

children.text: evam uktaḥ sa dharmātmā janakena mahātmanā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by great-souled <s>Janaka</s>, that righteous one,
the sage skilled in speech replied to the heroic king with these words:
"These two are the sons of <s>Daśaratha</s>, kṣatriyas renowned in the world.

children.text: draṣṭukāmau dhanuḥ śreṣṭhaṃ yad etat tvayi tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: They wish to see that excellent bow which is kept with you.

children.text: etad darśaya bhadraṃ te kṛtakāmau nṛpātmajau
children.translated_text: Show it to them. May there be good fortune for you. The princes will have their desire fulfilled,
and after seeing this bow they will go back as they please."

children.text: evam uktas tu janakaḥ pratyuvāca mahāmunim
children.translated_text: But when he had been addressed in this way, <s>Janaka</s> replied to the great sage:

children.text: śrūyatām asya dhanuṣo yad artham iha tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: "Listen for what reason this bow remains here.

children.text: devarāta iti khyāto nimeḥ ṣaṣṭho mahīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: A king named <s>Devarāta</s>, the sixth from <s>Nimi</s>, was renowned.

children.text: nyāso 'yaṃ tasya bhagavan haste datto mahātmanā ||
children.translated_text: Blessed sir, this deposit was placed in that great-souled king's hand.
Long ago, at the destruction of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s sacrifice, the mighty <s>Rudra</s>,

children.text: rudras tu tridaśān roṣāt salilam idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: having strung the bow in anger, spoke these words to the thirty gods:

children.text: yasmād bhāgārthino bhāgān nākalpayata me surāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Because, seeking shares, you gods did not allot my shares to me,
I shall cut off your noble, precious limbs with this bow.'

children.text: tato vimanasaḥ sarve devā vai munipuṃgava
children.translated_text: Then all the gods became dejected, O bull among sages,
and propitiated the lord of gods; <s>Bhava</s> became pleased with them.

children.text: prītiyuktaḥ sa sarveṣāṃ dadau teṣāṃ mahātmanām ||
children.translated_text: Being pleased, he gave it to all those great-souled gods.
This, then, is the jeweled bow of the great-souled god of gods.

children.text: nyāsabhūtaṃ tadā nyastam asmākaṃ pūrvake vibho ||
children.translated_text: It was then deposited as a trust with our ancestor, O lord.

children.text: atha me kṛṣataḥ kṣetraṃ lāṅgalād utthitā mama
children.translated_text: Then, while I was ploughing a field, there arose from my ploughshare

children.text: kṣetraṃ śodhayatā labdhvā nāmnā sīteti viśrutā ||
children.translated_text: one found by me as I was purifying the field, renowned by the name <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: bhūtalād utthitā sā tu vyavardhata mamātmajā
children.translated_text: She, arisen from the surface of the earth, grew up as my daughter.
This womb-born-from-no-womb maiden of mine has been established as one whose bride-price is valor.

children.text: bhūtalād utthitāṃ tāṃ tu vardhamānāṃ mamātmajām
children.translated_text: As that daughter of mine, arisen from the surface of the earth, was growing up,
kings came and sought her in marriage, O bull among sages.
When all those rulers of the earth were seeking the maiden,

children.text: vīryaśulketi bhagavan na dadāmi sutām aham ||
children.translated_text: I did not give my daughter, blessed sir, saying, 'Her bride-price is valor.'
Then all the kings assembled, O bull among sages,
and came to <s>Mithilā</s>, wishing then to test their valor.
For those who wished to test their valor, the bow was brought out.

children.text: na śekur grahaṇe tasya dhanuṣas tolane 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: They were not able either to grasp that bow or even to lift it.

children.text: teṣāṃ vīryavatāṃ vīryam alpaṃ jñātvā mahāmune
children.translated_text: Knowing the valor of those valorous kings to be slight, O great sage,
I rejected the kings. Understand that, O treasure of austerity.
Then, in supreme anger, the kings, O bull among sages,
all besieged <s>Mithilā</s>, having fallen into doubt about their valor.
Knowing themselves to have been slighted, O bull among sages,
they were filled with great anger and oppressed the city of <s>Mithilā</s>.

children.text: tataḥ saṃvatsare pūrṇe kṣayaṃ yātāni sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, when a full year had passed, all my resources,
O best of sages, were utterly exhausted; thereafter I was deeply distressed.
Then by austerity I propitiated all the hosts of gods,
and the gods, exceedingly pleased, gave me a fourfold army.

children.text: tato bhagnā nṛpatayo hanyamānā diśo yayuḥ
children.translated_text: Then the kings were broken, and, being struck down, fled to the quarters,
their valor gone, uncertain of their valor, together with their ministers, those evil-doers.
This, then, O tiger among sages, is that supremely radiant bow.
I shall show it also to <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, O you of good vows.

children.text: yady asya dhanuṣo rāmaḥ kuryād āropaṇaṃ mune
children.translated_text: If <s>Rāma</s> should string this bow, O sage,

children.text: sutām ayonijāṃ sītāṃ dadyāṃ dāśarather aham ||
children.translated_text: I shall give my womb-born-from-no-womb daughter <s>Sītā</s> to the son of <s>Daśaratha</s>."
Hearing <s>Janaka</s>'s words, the great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>

children.text: dhanur darśaya rāmāya iti hovāca pārthivam ||
children.translated_text: said to the king, "Show the bow to <s>Rāma</s>."

children.text: tataḥ sa rājā janakaḥ sacivān vyādideśa ha
children.translated_text: Then that king <s>Janaka</s> instructed his ministers:
"Let the divine bow, adorned with perfumes and garlands, be brought."
Commanded by <s>Janaka</s>, the ministers entered the city,

children.text: tad dhanuḥ purataḥ kṛtvā nirjagmuḥ pārthivājñayā ||
children.translated_text: and, placing that bow before them, came out by the king's command.
Five thousand men, broad and great-souled,

children.text: mañjūṣām aṣṭacakrāṃ tāṃ samūhus te kathaṃcana ||
children.translated_text: somehow drew along that eight-wheeled chest.

children.text: tām ādāya tu mañjūṣām āyatīṃ yatra tad dhanuḥ
children.translated_text: Taking that long chest in which the bow was kept,
the king's ministers, like gods, spoke to <s>Janaka</s>:
"Here is the excellent bow, O king, honored by all kings,
O lord of <s>Mithilā</s>, great king, if you wish it to be seen."

children.text: teṣāṃ nṛpo vacaḥ śrutvā kṛtāñjalir abhāṣata
children.translated_text: Hearing their words, the king, with joined palms, addressed
the great-souled <s>Viśvāmitra</s> and those two, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:
"This is the excellent bow, O brahmin, worshiped by the <s>Janakas</s>,

children.text: rājabhiś ca mahāvīryair aśakyaṃ pūrituṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: and then impossible to bend by kings of great valor.

children.text: naitat suragaṇāḥ sarve nāsurā na ca rākṣasāḥ
children.translated_text: Not all the hosts of gods, nor the asuras, nor the rākṣasas,
nor the chief gandharvas and yakṣas together with kinnaras and great serpents,

children.text: kva gatir mānuṣāṇāṃ ca dhanuṣo 'sya prapūraṇe
children.translated_text: can succeed with this bow; what then of human beings
in stringing it, fitting it, bending it, or even lifting it?

children.text: tad etad dhanuṣāṃ śreṣṭham ānītaṃ munipuṃgava
children.translated_text: This best of bows has now been brought, O bull among sages.
O greatly fortunate one, show it to these two princes."
Righteous <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, hearing what <s>Janaka</s> had said,

children.text: vatsa rāma dhanuḥ paśya iti rāghavam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: said to the descendant of <s>Raghu</s>, "Child <s>Rāma</s>, look at the bow."

children.text: maharṣer vacanād rāmo yatra tiṣṭhati tad dhanuḥ
children.translated_text: At the great seer's word, <s>Rāma</s> went to where that bow stood,

children.text: mañjūṣāṃ tām apāvṛtya dṛṣṭvā dhanur athābravīt ||
children.translated_text: opened that chest, and, having seen the bow, then said:
"O brahmin, I shall touch this excellent bow here with my hand."

children.text: yatnavāṃś ca bhaviṣyāmi tolane pūraṇe 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: "And I shall make an effort in lifting it, or even in drawing it to full tension."

children.text: bāḍham ity eva taṃ rājā muniś ca samabhāṣata
children.translated_text: The king and the sage both said to him simply, "Very well."

children.text: līlayā sa dhanur madhye jagrāha vacanān muneḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the sage's word, he playfully grasped that bow in the middle.
While many thousands of men looked on, O descendant of <s>Raghu</s>,

children.text: āropayat sa dharmātmā salīlam iva tad dhanuḥ ||
children.translated_text: that righteous one strung the bow as if in sport.
Having set the bowstring on it, the heroic one drew it fully;

children.text: tad babhañja dhanur madhye naraśreṣṭho mahāyaśāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the best of men, greatly renowned, broke that bow in the middle.
Its sound was tremendous, like the crash of a thunderbolt,
and there was a very great shaking of the earth, as if a mountain were splitting apart.

children.text: nipetuś ca narāḥ sarve tena śabdena mohitāḥ
children.translated_text: All the men fell down, stunned by that sound,

children.text: varjayitvā munivaraṃ rājānaṃ tau ca rāghavau ||
children.translated_text: except for the best of sages, the king, and the two <s>Rāghavas</s>.
When the people had recovered, the king, freed from fear,
with joined palms spoke these words to the foremost of sages, he who knew how to speak:
"Blessed one, the valor of <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, has been seen by me.

children.text: atyadbhutam acintyaṃ ca atarkitam idaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: This is most marvelous, inconceivable, and something I had not imagined.

children.text: janakānāṃ kule kīrtim āhariṣyati me sutā
children.translated_text: My daughter will bring fame to the family of the <s>Janakas</s>
when <s>Sītā</s> obtains <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, as her husband.

children.text: mama satyā pratijñā ca vīryaśulketi kauśika
children.translated_text: And my vow, O <s>Kauśika</s>, that she has valor as her bride-price, is true.

children.text: sītā prāṇair bahumatā deyā rāmāya me sutā ||
children.translated_text: My daughter <s>Sītā</s>, greatly valued by me as my very life, is to be given to <s>Rāma</s>.
With your approval, O brahmin, let my ministers go quickly,

children.text: mama kauśika bhadraṃ te ayodhyāṃ tvaritā rathaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Kauśika</s>, good fortune to you, swiftly by chariots to <s>Ayodhyā</s>.

children.text: rājānaṃ praśritair vākyair ānayantu puraṃ mama
children.translated_text: Let them bring the king to my city with respectful words,
and let them tell in every detail of the gift in which valor is the bride-price.

children.text: muniguptau ca kākutsthau kathayantu nṛpāya vai
children.translated_text: Let them tell the king that the two <s>Kākutsthas</s> are protected by the sage;
and let those very swift messengers bring the delighted king here."

children.text: kauśikaś ca tathety āha rājā cābhāṣya mantriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kauśika</s> said, "So be it," and the king, having addressed his ministers,
the righteous one, once the command had been given, sent them to <s>Ayodhyā</s>.
Those messengers, instructed by <s>Janaka</s>, though their mounts were weary,

children.text: trirātram uṣitvā mārge te 'yodhyāṃ prāviśan purīm ||
children.translated_text: stayed three nights on the road and then entered the city of <s>Ayodhyā</s>.
Those messengers, at the king's command, were admitted into the royal palace,
and they saw the aged king <s>Daśaratha</s>, who was like a god.
All the messengers, with the hollows of their hands joined, free from fear,
reverently spoke to the king a speech sweet in syllables:
"King <s>Janaka</s> of <s>Mithilā</s>, with the agnihotra placed foremost,
asks again and again after your welfare and imperishable well-being, together with your teachers and priests.
With sweet words joined with affection, again and again,
<s>Janaka</s> asks about you, great king, together with all who are before you.
After asking calmly about your welfare, <s>Vaideha</s>, lord of <s>Mithilā</s>,
with <s>Kauśika</s>'s approval, spoke this message to you:
'My former vow is known: my daughter has valor as her bride-price.
The kings, angry though they were, were turned away, powerless.
This daughter of mine, O king, has been won by your sons, heroes
who arrived by chance with <s>Viśvāmitra</s> before them.

children.text: tac ca rājan dhanur divyaṃ madhye bhagnaṃ mahātmanā
children.translated_text: And that divine bow, O king, was broken in the middle by the great-souled one,
by <s>Rāma</s>, great king, in a great assembly of people.

children.text: asmai deyā mayā sītā vīryaśulkā mahātmane
children.translated_text: I must give <s>Sītā</s>, whose bride-price is valor, to this great-souled man.

children.text: pratijñāṃ tartum icchāmi tad anujñātum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: I wish to cross over my vow; therefore you ought to give your permission.
Together with your teachers, O great king, and with your priests before you,

children.text: śīghram āgaccha bhadraṃ te draṣṭum arhasi rāghavau ||
children.translated_text: come quickly; good fortune to you. You ought to see the two <s>Rāghavas</s>.

children.text: prītiṃ ca mama rājendra nirvartayitum arhasi
children.translated_text: And you ought to bring about joy for me, O king of kings;

children.text: putrayor ubhayor eva prītiṃ tvam api lapsyase ||
children.translated_text: you too will obtain joy in both your sons.'
Thus the lord of <s>Videha</s> spoke that sweet message,
with <s>Viśvāmitra</s>'s approval and standing by the counsel of <s>Śatānanda</s>."

children.text: dūtavākyaṃ tu tac chrutvā rājā paramaharṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that message of the envoys, the king was supremely delighted,

children.text: vasiṣṭhaṃ vāmadevaṃ ca mantriṇo 'nyāṃś ca so 'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: and he spoke to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, and his other ministers:
"Protected by the son of <s>Kuśika</s>, he who increases <s>Kausalyā</s>'s joy

children.text: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā videheṣu vasaty asau ||
children.translated_text: is dwelling among the <s>Videhas</s> together with his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
The valor of the <s>Kākutstha</s> has been seen by the great-souled <s>Janaka</s>,

children.text: sampradānaṃ sutāyās tu rāghave kartum icchati ||
children.translated_text: and he wishes to make the formal gift of his daughter to the <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: yadi vo rocate vṛttaṃ janakasya mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: If this conduct of the great-souled <s>Janaka</s> is pleasing to you,

children.text: purīṃ gacchāmahe śīghraṃ mā bhūt kālasya paryayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: let us go quickly to the city; let there be no passing away of time."

children.text: mantriṇo bāḍham ity āhuḥ saha sarvair maharṣibhiḥ
children.translated_text: The ministers, together with all the great seers, said, "Very well,"

children.text: suprītaś cābravīd rājā śvo yātreti sa mantriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the king, highly pleased, told the ministers, "The journey is tomorrow."
The ministers of the lord of men, greatly honored for the night,

children.text: ūṣuḥ pramuditāḥ sarve guṇaiḥ sarvaiḥ samanvitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all stayed there, delighted and endowed with every virtue.
Then, when the night had passed, the joyful king <s>Daśaratha</s>,

children.text: rājā daśaratho hṛṣṭaḥ sumantram idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: together with his teachers and kinsmen, spoke this to <s>Sumantra</s>:

children.text: adya sarve dhanādhyakṣā dhanam ādāya puṣkalam
children.translated_text: "Today let all the treasurers take abundant wealth
and, well arranged, go in front, furnished with many kinds of jewels.
Let the fourfold army also set out quickly in its entirety,
and at the very time of my command let the unsurpassed vehicles and teams be ready.

children.text: vasiṣṭho vāmadevaś ca jābālir atha kāśyapaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, <s>Jābāli</s>, and then <s>Kāśyapa</s>,

children.text: mārkaṇḍeyaś ca dīrghāyur ṛṣiḥ kātyāyanas tathā ||
children.translated_text: long-lived <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> the seer, and <s>Kātyāyana</s> too,

children.text: ete dvijāḥ prayāntv agre syandanaṃ yojayasva me
children.translated_text: let these twice-born men go in front; harness my chariot,

children.text: yathā kālātyayo na syād dūtā hi tvarayanti mām ||
children.translated_text: so that there may be no loss of time, for the messengers are urging me on."

children.text: vacanāc ca narendrasya sā senā caturaṅgiṇī
children.translated_text: And at the command of the lord of men, that fourfold army...
He followed behind the king as he went together with the seers.
After traveling four days on the road, he approached the <s>Videhas</s>.

children.text: rājā tu janakaḥ śrīmāñ śrutvā pūjām akalpayat ||
children.translated_text: But the glorious king <s>Janaka</s>, hearing of it, arranged honors.

children.text: tato rājānam āsādya vṛddhaṃ daśarathaṃ nṛpam
children.translated_text: Then, coming up to the aged king, the ruler <s>Daśaratha</s>,

children.text: janako mudito rājā harṣaṃ ca paramaṃ yayau
children.translated_text: king <s>Janaka</s>, delighted, reached supreme joy,
and that best of men spoke to the best of men, who was filled with gladness:

children.text: svāgataṃ te mahārāja diṣṭyā prāpto 'si rāghava
children.translated_text: "Welcome to you, great king; by good fortune you have arrived, O <s>Rāghava</s>.
You will obtain joy in both your sons, won by valor.

children.text: diṣṭyā prāpto mahātejā vasiṣṭho bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
children.translated_text: By good fortune the greatly radiant venerable seer <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> has arrived,

children.text: saha sarvair dvijaśreṣṭhair devair iva śatakratuḥ ||
children.translated_text: together with all the best twice-born men, like <s>Śatakratu</s> with the gods.

children.text: diṣṭyā me nirjitā vighnā diṣṭyā me pūjitaṃ kulam
children.translated_text: By good fortune my obstacles have been overcome; by good fortune my lineage has been honored,
through alliance with the great-souled <s>Rāghavas</s>, foremost in prowess.
Tomorrow morning, O lord of kings, you should be pleased to complete,
at the end of the sacrifice, O best of men, the wedding approved by the seers."
Hearing that speech of his, the lord of men, in the midst of the seers,
the king, best of those skilled in speech, replied to the ruler:

children.text: pratigraho dātṛvaśaḥ śrutam etan mayā purā
children.translated_text: "The receiving of a gift depends on the giver; I heard this long ago.

children.text: yathā vakṣyasi dharmajña tat kariṣyāmahe vayam ||
children.translated_text: As you say, knower of <s>dharma</s> (righteous law), so we shall do."

children.text: tad dharmiṣṭhaṃ yaśasyaṃ ca vacanaṃ satyavādinaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that most righteous and glorious speech of the truthful king,
the lord of the <s>Videhas</s> was filled with supreme wonder.
Then all the groups of sages, in their meeting with one another,

children.text: harṣeṇa mahatā yuktās tāṃ niśām avasan sukham ||
children.translated_text: filled with great joy, passed that night happily.

children.text: rājā ca rāghavau putrau niśāmya pariharṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: And the king, seeing his two <s>Rāghava</s> sons, was delighted;
supremely pleased and well honored by <s>Janaka</s>, he spent the night there.
<s>Janaka</s> too, greatly radiant and knowing reality, performed the rite according to <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: yajñasya ca sutābhyāṃ ca kṛtvā rātrim uvāsa ha ||
children.translated_text: both for the sacrifice and for his daughters, and then spent the night.
Then in the morning <s>Janaka</s>, having completed his duties with the great seers,
skilled in speech, spoke these words to his priest <s>Śatānanda</s>:
"My younger brother is greatly radiant and exceedingly righteous;

children.text: kuśadhvaja iti khyātaḥ purīm adhyavasac chubhām ||
children.translated_text: known as <s>Kuśadhvaja</s>, he dwells in an auspicious city,
bounded by <s>Vāryāphalaka</s>, drinking from the river <s>Ikṣumatī</s>,
in <s>Sāṃkāśyā</s>, auspicious in appearance, like the aerial palace <s>Puṣpaka</s>.

children.text: tam ahaṃ draṣṭum icchāmi yajñagoptā sa me mataḥ
children.translated_text: I wish to see him; I consider him the protector of my sacrifice.

children.text: prītiṃ so 'pi mahātejā imāṃ bhoktā mayā saha ||
children.translated_text: That greatly radiant one too will enjoy this joy together with me."
At the king's command, they set out with swift horses
to bring that tiger among men, as <s>Viṣṇu</s> was brought at <s>Indra</s>'s command.
And by the king's command <s>Kuśadhvaja</s> came.
He saw the great-souled <s>Janaka</s>, devoted to <s>dharma</s>,
and, having saluted <s>Śatānanda</s> and also the righteous king,
he mounted a supreme, divine seat worthy of a king.

children.text: upaviṣṭāv ubhau tau tu bhrātarāv amitaujasau ||
children.translated_text: Then those two brothers, both of boundless energy, sat down.
The two heroes sent the best of ministers, <s>Sudāman</s>:
"Go quickly, chief minister, and bring the immeasurably splendid <s>Ikṣvāku</s>,
unassailable, together with his sons and his ministers."

children.text: aupakāryāṃ sa gatvā tu raghūṇāṃ kulavardhanam
children.translated_text: Going to the guest quarters of the <s>Raghus</s>,
he saw the increaser of the lineage and, saluting him with his head, said this:
"Heroic lord of <s>Ayodhyā</s>, the <s>Vaideha</s>, lord of <s>Mithilā</s>,
has resolved to see you together with your preceptors and priests."
Hearing the words of the best of ministers, the king, with the groups of seers,

children.text: sabandhur agamat tatra janako yatra vartate ||
children.translated_text: went there with his kinsmen, where <s>Janaka</s> was.
That king, accompanied by ministers, preceptors, and relatives,

children.text: vākyaṃ vākyavidāṃ śreṣṭho vaideham idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: best of those skilled in speech, said this to the <s>Vaideha</s>:
"Well known to you, great king, is the revered seer <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,

children.text: vaktā sarveṣu kṛtyeṣu vasiṣṭho bhagavān ṛṣiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the sacred authority of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> lineage and the speaker in all undertakings.
With <s>Viśvāmitra</s>'s permission, together with all the great seers,

children.text: eṣa vakṣyati dharmātmā vasiṣṭho me yathākramam ||
children.translated_text: this righteous <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> will speak for me in due order."
When <s>Daśaratha</s> had become silent, the venerable seer <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,
skilled in speech, spoke these words to the <s>Vaideha</s> together with his priests:
"<s>Brahmā</s>, whose origin is unmanifest, is eternal, constant, and imperishable.

children.text: tasmān marīciḥ saṃjajñe marīceḥ kaśyapaḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From him <s>Marīci</s> was born, and <s>Kaśyapa</s> was the son of <s>Marīci</s>.

children.text: vivasvān kaśyapāj jajñe manur vaivasvataḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vivasvān</s> was born from <s>Kaśyapa</s>; <s>Manu Vaivasvata</s> is remembered.

children.text: manuḥ prajāpatiḥ pūrvam ikṣvākus tu manoḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Manu</s> was formerly the lord of creatures, and <s>Ikṣvāku</s> was <s>Manu</s>'s son.

children.text: tam ikṣvākum ayodhyāyāṃ rājānaṃ viddhi pūrvakam
children.translated_text: Know that <s>Ikṣvāku</s> to have been the first king in <s>Ayodhyā</s>.

children.text: ikṣvākos tu sutaḥ śrīmān vikukṣir udapadyata ||
children.translated_text: From <s>Ikṣvāku</s> the glorious son <s>Vikukṣi</s> was born.

children.text: vikukṣes tu mahātejā bāṇaḥ putraḥ pratāpavān
children.translated_text: From <s>Vikukṣi</s> came the greatly radiant and mighty son <s>Bāṇa</s>.
And <s>Bāṇa</s>'s son was the greatly radiant and mighty <s>Anaraṇya</s>.

children.text: anaraṇyāt pṛthur jajñe triśaṅkus tu pṛthoḥ sutaḥ
children.translated_text: From <s>Anaraṇya</s> <s>Pṛthu</s> was born, and <s>Triśaṅku</s> was <s>Pṛthu</s>'s son.
From <s>Triśaṅku</s> there was a son, the greatly renowned <s>Dhundhumāra</s>.
From <s>Dhundhumāra</s> came the greatly radiant great chariot-warrior <s>Yuvanāśva</s>.
<s>Yuvanāśva</s>'s son was the glorious lord of the earth, <s>Māndhātṛ</s>.

children.text: māndhātus tu sutaḥ śrīmān susaṃdhir udapadyata
children.translated_text: From <s>Māndhātṛ</s> the glorious son <s>Susaṃdhi</s> was born.

children.text: susaṃdher api putrau dvau dhruvasaṃdhiḥ prasenajit ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Susaṃdhi</s> had two sons, <s>Dhruvasaṃdhi</s> and <s>Prasenajit</s>.

children.text: yaśasvī dhruvasaṃdhes tu bharato nāma nāmataḥ
children.translated_text: The famous son of <s>Dhruvasaṃdhi</s> was named <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: bharatāt tu mahātejā asito nāma jāyata ||
children.translated_text: From <s>Bharata</s> the greatly radiant one named <s>Asita</s> was born.

children.text: saha tena gareṇaiva jātaḥ sa sagaro 'bhavat
children.translated_text: Together with that very poison, he was born; he became <s>Sagara</s>."
But <s>Asamañjas</s> was the son of <s>Sagara</s>, and then from <s>Asamañjas</s> came <s>Aṃśumān</s>.
<s>Dilīpa</s> was the son of <s>Aṃśumān</s>, and <s>Bhagīratha</s> was the son of <s>Dilīpa</s>.

children.text: bhagīrathāt kakutsthaś ca kakutsthasya raghus tathā ||
children.translated_text: From <s>Bhagīratha</s> came <s>Kakutstha</s>, and likewise from <s>Kakutstha</s> came <s>Raghu</s>.

children.text: raghos tu putras tejasvī pravṛddhaḥ puruṣādakaḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Raghu</s>'s son was the radiant <s>Pravṛddha</s>, a devourer of men.

children.text: kalmāṣapādo hy abhavat tasmāj jātas tu śaṅkhaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He indeed became <s>Kalmāṣapāda</s>; from him <s>Śaṅkhaṇa</s> was born.
<s>Sudarśana</s> was the son of <s>Śaṅkhaṇa</s>, and <s>Agnivarṇa</s> came from <s>Sudarśana</s>.

children.text: śīghragas tv agnivarṇasya śīghragasya maruḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śīghraga</s> was the son of <s>Agnivarṇa</s>, and <s>Maru</s> was the son of <s>Śīghraga</s>.

children.text: maroḥ praśuśrukas tv āsīd ambarīṣaḥ praśuśrukāt
children.translated_text: From <s>Maru</s> came <s>Praśuśruka</s>, and <s>Ambarīṣa</s> came from <s>Praśuśruka</s>.
The son of <s>Ambarīṣa</s> was <s>Nahuṣa</s>, lord of the earth.

children.text: nahuṣasya yayātis tu nābhāgas tu yayātijaḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Yayāti</s> was the son of <s>Nahuṣa</s>, and <s>Nābhāga</s> was born from <s>Yayāti</s>.
From <s>Nābhāga</s> came <s>Aja</s>, and from <s>Aja</s> came <s>Daśaratha</s>.
From that <s>Daśaratha</s> were born the two brothers, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
For the sake of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, born in the family of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>,
of kings pure from the beginning of their line, supremely righteous, heroic, and truthful,
O king, I ask for your daughters.
O best of men, you should give the two fitting girls to these two fitting bridegrooms.
<s>Janaka</s>, with folded hands, answered him as he spoke in this way:

children.text: śrotum arhasi bhadraṃ te kulaṃ naḥ kīrtitaṃ param
children.translated_text: "You should hear, and may it be well with you, our supreme lineage as it is proclaimed.
For at the giving away of a bride, O best of sages, one's lineage must be told
without remainder by one born in a noble family. Learn it, O great sage.

children.text: rājābhūt triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ svena karmaṇā
children.translated_text: There was a king, renowned in the three worlds by his own deeds,
<s>Nimi</s>, whose self was supremely righteous, the best of all beings.

children.text: tasya putro mithir nāma janako mithiputrakaḥ
children.translated_text: His son was named <s>Mithi</s>; <s>Janaka</s> was <s>Mithi</s>'s son.

children.text: prathamo janako nāma janakād apy udāvasuḥ ||
children.translated_text: He was the first named <s>Janaka</s>, and from <s>Janaka</s> came <s>Udāvasu</s>.

children.text: udāvasos tu dharmātmā jāto vai nandivardhanaḥ
children.translated_text: From <s>Udāvasu</s> was born the righteous <s>Nandivardhana</s>.
And the son of <s>Nandivardhana</s> was named <s>Suketu</s>.
From <s>Suketu</s> too came the righteous and very powerful <s>Devarāta</s>.
The son of the royal sage <s>Devarāta</s> is remembered as <s>Bṛhadratha</s>.
The son of <s>Bṛhadratha</s> was the heroic <s>Mahāvīra</s>, great in valor and majesty.
From <s>Mahāvīra</s> came steadfast <s>Sudhṛti</s>, whose prowess was true.
From <s>Sudhṛti</s> too came the righteous <s>Dhṛṣṭaketu</s>, very devoted to <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: dhṛṣṭaketos tu rājarṣer haryaśva iti viśrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the son of the royal sage <s>Dhṛṣṭaketu</s> is renowned as <s>Haryaśva</s>.

children.text: haryaśvasya maruḥ putro maroḥ putraḥ pratīndhakaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Maru</s> was the son of <s>Haryaśva</s>, and <s>Pratīndhaka</s> was the son of <s>Maru</s>.
The righteous king <s>Kīrtiratha</s> was the son of <s>Pratīndhaka</s>.
The son of <s>Kīrtiratha</s> is also remembered as <s>Devamīḍha</s>.
From <s>Devamīḍha</s> came <s>Vibudha</s>, and from <s>Vibudha</s> came <s>Mahīdhraka</s>.
King <s>Kīrtirāta</s>, very powerful, was the son of <s>Mahīdhraka</s>.
From the royal sage <s>Kīrtirāta</s> was born <s>Mahāromā</s>.
From <s>Mahāromā</s> was born the righteous <s>Svarṇaromā</s>.
From the royal sage <s>Svarṇaromā</s> was born <s>Hrasvaromā</s>.
To him, the great-souled knower of <s>dharma</s>, two sons were born:

children.text: jyeṣṭho 'ham anujo bhrātā mama vīraḥ kuśadhvajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I am the elder, and my younger brother is the heroic <s>Kuśadhvaja</s>.

children.text: māṃ tu jyeṣṭhaṃ pitā rājye so 'bhiṣicya narādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: Then my father, the lord of men, consecrated me, the elder, in the kingdom,

children.text: kuśadhvajaṃ samāveśya bhāraṃ mayi vanaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: entrusted <s>Kuśadhvaja</s> to me as a charge, and went to the forest.

children.text: vṛddhe pitari svaryāte dharmeṇa dhuram āvaham
