children.translated_text: When my aged father had gone to heaven, I bore the burden according to <s>dharma</s>,
lovingly watching over my brother <s>Kuśadhvaja</s>, who was like a god.

children.text: kasyacit tv atha kālasya sāṃkāśyād agamat purāt
children.translated_text: Then, after some time, from the city of <s>Sāṃkāśya</s>
the powerful king <s>Sudhanvan</s> came and besieged <s>Mithilā</s>.

children.text: sa ca me preṣayāmāsa śaivaṃ dhanur anuttamam
children.translated_text: He also sent me this message: 'Let the incomparable bow of <s>Śiva</s>

children.text: sītā kanyā ca padmākṣī mahyaṃ vai dīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: and the lotus-eyed maiden <s>Sītā</s> be given to me.'

children.text: tasyāpradānād brahmarṣe yuddham āsīn mayā saha
children.translated_text: Because she was not given to him, O brahmin seer, there was war between him and me.

children.text: sa hato 'bhimukho rājā sudhanvā tu mayā raṇe ||
children.translated_text: Facing me in battle, king <s>Sudhanvan</s> was slain by me.
After killing that lord of men <s>Sudhanvan</s>, O best of sages,
I consecrated my heroic brother <s>Kuśadhvaja</s> in <s>Sāṃkāśya</s>.

children.text: kanīyān eṣa me bhrātā ahaṃ jyeṣṭho mahāmune
children.translated_text: This is my younger brother; I am the elder, O great sage.
With the greatest joy, O bull among sages, I give you the two brides.

children.text: sītāṃ rāmāya bhadraṃ te ūrmilāṃ lakṣmaṇāya ca
children.translated_text: May it be well with you: <s>Sītā</s> to <s>Rāma</s>, and <s>Ūrmilā</s> to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
My daughter <s>Sītā</s>, like a daughter of the gods, has heroism as her bride-price.

children.text: dvitīyām ūrmilāṃ caiva trir vadāmi na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: And also the second, <s>Ūrmilā</s>: I say it three times; there is no doubt.
With the greatest joy, O delighter of the <s>Raghus</s>, I give you the two brides.
O king, have the cow-gift performed for <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: pitṛkāryaṃ ca bhadraṃ te tato vaivāhikaṃ kuru ||
children.translated_text: May it be well with you; perform the ancestral rite, and then carry out the marriage ceremony.

children.text: maghā hy adya mahābāho tṛtīye divase prabho
children.translated_text: For today is <s>Maghā</s>, O mighty-armed lord; on the third day,

children.text: phalgunyām uttare rājaṃs tasmin vaivāhikaṃ kuru
children.translated_text: O king, under <s>Uttarā Phalgunī</s>, perform that marriage ceremony.
For <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, a gift should be made, bringing forth happiness."
When the <s>Vaideha</s> had said this, the great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,
together with <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, spoke a brave word to the king:
"O bull among men, the lineages of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s> and the <s>Videhas</s>
are inconceivable and immeasurable; there is no one equal to them.
O king, the bond of <s>dharma</s> is fitting, and so is the abundance of beauty
for <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, together with <s>Sītā</s> and <s>Ūrmilā</s>.

children.text: vaktavyaṃ na naraśreṣṭha śrūyatāṃ vacanaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: There is something to be said, O best of men; hear my words.

children.text: bhrātā yavīyān dharmajña eṣa rājā kuśadhvajaḥ
children.translated_text: This younger brother, the knower of <s>dharma</s>, is king <s>Kuśadhvaja</s>.
O king, this righteous man has, in beauty unequaled on earth,
two daughters, O best of men; we ask for them as wives
for prince <s>Bharata</s> and for wise <s>Śatrughna</s>."

children.text: varayema sute rājaṃs tayor arthe mahātmanoḥ ||
children.translated_text: O king, let us ask for the two daughters on behalf of those two great-souled ones.
These sons of <s>Daśaratha</s> are endowed with beauty and youth;
all are like guardians of the world, and equal to the gods in valor.
O lord of kings, let the untroubled house of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>
be bound by kinship with both of you, who perform meritorious deeds.
Then, hearing the words of <s>Viśvāmitra</s> and with <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s approval,
<s>Janaka</s>, with joined palms, spoke these words to the two foremost sages:
"The family alliance that you yourselves command is fitting.

children.text: evaṃ bhavatu bhadraṃ vaḥ kuśadhvajasute ime
children.translated_text: So be it. Blessings to you. These two daughters of <s>Kuśadhvaja</s>
let <s>Śatrughna</s> and <s>Bharata</s> together take as their wives.
On a single day, O great sage, let the four mighty princes
take the hands of the four princesses.
On the following day, O brahmin, under the two <s>Phalgunī</s> lunar mansions, the wise
commend marriage rites, when <s>Bhaga</s> is the presiding <s>Prajāpati</s>."

children.text: evam uktvā vacaḥ saumyaṃ pratyutthāya kṛtāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken this gracious speech, the king <s>Janaka</s> rose with joined palms

children.text: ubhau munivarau rājā janako vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: and addressed both excellent sages with these words:

children.text: paro dharmaḥ kṛto mahyaṃ śiṣyo 'smi bhavatoḥ sadā
children.translated_text: "The highest <s>dharma</s> has been done for me; I am always your disciple.
Let the two foremost sages sit on these chief seats.
Just as this city of <s>Ayodhyā</s> belongs to <s>Daśaratha</s>, so too it is mine;

children.text: prabhutve nāsīt saṃdeho yathārhaṃ kartum arhathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there is no doubt about your authority. You should act as is proper."
When <s>Janaka</s> the <s>Vaideha</s> was speaking in this way, the delight of the <s>Raghus</s>,
king <s>Daśaratha</s>, delighted, replied to the ruler of the earth:
"You two brothers, lords of <s>Mithilā</s>, possess countless virtues.
The seers and the assemblies of kings have been honored by you both.

children.text: svasti prāpnuhi bhadraṃ te gamiṣyāmi svam ālayam
children.translated_text: May you attain well-being. Blessings to you. I shall go to my own lodging,
and I shall perform all the ancestral rites," he said.

children.text: tam āpṛṣṭvā narapatiṃ rājā daśarathas tadā
children.translated_text: Having taken leave of that ruler, king <s>Daśaratha</s> then,
placing the two lordly sages before him, quickly departed, greatly renowned.

children.text: sa gatvā nilayaṃ rājā śrāddhaṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ
children.translated_text: After going to his residence, the king performed the ancestral rite according to rule;

children.text: prabhāte kālyam utthāya cakre godānam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: rising early at dawn, he made an excellent gift of cows.
The lord of men, the king, gave hundreds of thousands of cows

children.text: ekaikaśo dadau rājā putrān uddiśya dharmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: to the brahmins, one by one, with righteous intent for the sake of his sons.
They were complete, with golden horns, with calves, and with bronze milking vessels:
four hundred thousand cows, O bull among men.

children.text: vittam anyac ca subahu dvijebhyo raghunandanaḥ
children.translated_text: And the descendant of <s>Raghu</s>, loving his sons, gave very much other wealth
to the twice-born, with the cow-gift intended for his sons.

children.text: sa sutaiḥ kṛtagodānair vṛtaś ca nṛpatis tadā
children.translated_text: Then that king, surrounded by his sons who had performed the cow-gift,
shone like gentle <s>Prajāpati</s> surrounded by the guardians of the world.

children.text: yasmiṃs tu divase rājā cakre godānam uttamam
children.translated_text: But on the day when the king made that excellent gift of cows,

children.text: tasmiṃs tu divase śūro yudhājit samupeyivān ||
children.translated_text: the heroic <s>Yudhājit</s> arrived.
He was the son of the king of the <s>Kekayas</s>, indeed <s>Bharata</s>'s maternal uncle;

children.text: dṛṣṭvā pṛṣṭvā ca kuśalaṃ rājānam idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: after seeing the king and asking after his welfare, he spoke these words:
"The king, lord of the <s>Kekayas</s>, affectionately asked about your welfare.
Those whose welfare you desire are at present free from illness.
O lord of kings, O ruler of the earth, wishing to see my sister's son,
I came to <s>Ayodhyā</s> for that purpose, O descendant of <s>Raghu</s>.

children.text: śrutvā tv aham ayodhyāyāṃ vivāhārthaṃ tavātmajān
children.translated_text: But I heard that your sons had gone from <s>Ayodhyā</s> for the sake of marriage,

children.text: mithilām upayātās tu tvayā saha mahīpate ||
children.translated_text: and had come to <s>Mithilā</s> together with you, O ruler of the earth.
In haste I have come here, wishing to see my sister's son."
Then king <s>Daśaratha</s>, seeing his dear guest arrived,
honored him, who deserved honor, with the highest acts of hospitality.

children.text: tatas tām uṣito rātriṃ saha putrair mahātmabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, having spent that night together with his great-souled sons,
he placed the seers before him and went to the sacrificial enclosure.
At the fitting victorious moment, with all ornaments adorning them,
<s>Rāma</s>, whose auspicious wedding rites had been performed, came together with his brothers.

children.text: vasiṣṭhaṃ purataḥ kṛtvā maharṣīn aparān api ||
children.translated_text: He placed <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> before him, and the other great seers as well.
O king, king <s>Daśaratha</s>, with his sons whose auspicious wedding rites had been performed,
O best of noble men, waited for the giver of the brides.
For all purposes are accomplished through giver and receiver.
Undertake your own <s>dharma</s>, having made this excellent marriage rite."
Thus addressed by the supremely generous, great-souled <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,
the greatly radiant knower of the highest <s>dharma</s> replied with this speech:

children.text: kaḥ sthitaḥ pratihāro me kasyājñā sampratīkṣyate
children.translated_text: "What doorkeeper of mine is standing here? Whose command is being awaited?

children.text: svagṛhe ko vicāro 'sti yathā rājyam idaṃ tava ||
children.translated_text: What hesitation is there in one's own house? This kingdom is as much yours.
My daughters, for whom all auspicious wedding preparations have been made, have come to the foot of the altar,

children.text: mama kanyā muniśreṣṭha dīptā vahner ivārciṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O best of sages, shining like the flames of fire.
I am ready, waiting for you, established at this altar.

children.text: avighnaṃ kurutāṃ rājā kimarthaṃ hi vilambyate ||
children.translated_text: Let the king act without obstruction. Why indeed is there delay?"
Then <s>Daśaratha</s>, hearing that statement spoken by <s>Janaka</s>,
had all his sons enter, and the hosts of seers as well.
King <s>Janaka</s> spoke to the one who increased <s>Kausalyā</s>'s joy:

children.text: iyaṃ sītā mama sutā sahadharmacarī tava
children.translated_text: "This is <s>Sītā</s>, my daughter, your partner in <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: pratīccha caināṃ bhadraṃ te pāṇiṃ gṛhṇīṣva pāṇinā ||
children.translated_text: Accept her. Blessings to you. Take her hand with your hand.

children.text: lakṣmaṇāgaccha bhadraṃ te ūrmilām udyatāṃ mayā
children.translated_text: Come, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>; blessings to you. Accept <s>Ūrmilā</s>, offered by me.

children.text: pratīccha pāṇiṃ gṛhṇīṣva mā bhūt kālasya paryayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Take her hand. Let there be no passing of the appointed time."

children.text: tam evam uktvā janako bharataṃ cābhyabhāṣata
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to him, <s>Janaka</s> also addressed <s>Bharata</s>:
"Take <s>Māṇḍavī</s>'s hand with your hand, O descendant of <s>Raghu</s>."
And the righteous lord of <s>Janaka</s> also said to <s>Śatrughna</s>:
"Mighty-armed one, take <s>Śrutakīrti</s>'s hand with your hand.

children.text: sarve bhavantaḥ saumyāś ca sarve sucaritavratāḥ
children.translated_text: All of you are gentle, and all are of well-practiced vows.

children.text: patnībhiḥ santu kākutsthā mā bhūt kālasya paryayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let the <s>Kākutsthas</s> be joined with their wives; let there be no passing of the appointed time."

children.text: janakasya vacaḥ śrutvā pāṇīn pāṇibhir aspṛśan
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Janaka</s>'s words, they touched hands with hands,

children.text: catvāras te catasṛṇāṃ vasiṣṭhasya mate sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the four of them with the four maidens, standing in accordance with <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s counsel.

children.text: agniṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā vediṃ rājānam eva ca
children.translated_text: Having circumambulated the fire, the altar, and the king,
and the great-souled seers, the best of the <s>Raghus</s>, together with their wives,
performed the marriage according to rule, just as it had been prescribed.
There was a great shower of flowers, very bright, from the sky,
with the sound of divine kettledrums and the resonance of song and instruments.

children.text: nanṛtuś cāpsaraḥsaṃghā gandharvāś ca jaguḥ kalam
children.translated_text: Hosts of apsarases danced, and the gandharvas sang sweetly.
At the marriage of the foremost <s>Raghus</s>, that seemed a wonder.
While such a thing was taking place, amid the roar of trumpets and drums,

children.text: trir agniṃ te parikramya ūhur bhāryā mahaujasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: those men of great splendor, having circled the fire three times, took their wives.
Then the sons of <s>Raghu</s>, with their wives, went to the guest quarters,
and the king too followed, looking on, together with the company of seers and his kinsmen.
Then, when the night had passed, the great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,
after taking leave of the two kings, went to the northern mountain.
When <s>Viśvāmitra</s> had gone, the king, having taken leave of the <s>Vaideha</s>, lord of <s>Mithilā</s>,
then quickly set out for his city, King <s>Daśaratha</s>.

children.text: atha rājā videhānāṃ dadau kanyādhanaṃ bahu
children.translated_text: Then the king of the <s>Videhas</s>, the lord of <s>Mithilā</s>, gave much bridal wealth:
many hundreds of thousands of cows,
and foremost blankets, and garments of fine linen and silk by the crore,
elephants, horses, chariots, and infantry, splendid in form and well adorned.
The father of those maidens gave an unsurpassed retinue of female and male servants,
and also gold, refined gold, pearls, and coral.
Greatly delighted, he gave unsurpassed bridal wealth.
Having given abundant wealth and having dismissed the king,
the lord of <s>Mithilā</s> entered his own abode, <s>Mithilā</s>.
And the king, lord of <s>Ayodhyā</s>, together with his great-souled sons,
placing all the seers in front, went forth with his army and followers.
But as that tiger among men was going, together with the company of seers and the descendants of <s>Raghu</s>,

children.text: ghorāḥ sma pakṣiṇo vāco vyāharanti tatas tataḥ
children.translated_text: terrible birds uttered dreadful cries here and there,

children.text: bhaumāś caiva mṛgāḥ sarve gacchanti sma pradakṣiṇam ||
children.translated_text: while all the earth-roaming animals passed on the right.
Seeing them, the tiger among kings asked <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>:

children.text: asaumyāḥ pakṣiṇo ghorā mṛgāś cāpi pradakṣiṇāḥ
children.translated_text: "The birds are inauspicious and terrible, yet the animals are passing on the right.

children.text: kim idaṃ hṛdayotkampi mano mama viṣīdati ||
children.translated_text: What is this that shakes my heart? My mind sinks down."

children.text: rājño daśarathasyaitac chrutvā vākyaṃ mahān ṛṣiḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing this statement of King <s>Daśaratha</s>, the great seer

children.text: uvāca madhurāṃ vāṇīṃ śrūyatām asya yat phalam ||
children.translated_text: spoke in a sweet voice: "Listen to what its result will be.

children.text: upasthitaṃ bhayaṃ ghoraṃ divyaṃ pakṣimukhāc cyutam
children.translated_text: A terrible divine danger is at hand, fallen from the mouths of the birds.

children.text: mṛgāḥ praśamayanty ete saṃtāpas tyajyatām ayam ||
children.translated_text: These animals are calming it; let this anxiety be abandoned."

children.text: teṣāṃ saṃvadatāṃ tatra vāyuḥ prādurbabhūva ha
children.translated_text: While they were speaking together there, a wind arose,

children.text: kampayan medinīṃ sarvāṃ pātayaṃś ca drumāñ śubhān ||
children.translated_text: shaking the whole earth and felling fine trees.

children.text: tamasā saṃvṛtaḥ sūryaḥ sarvā na prababhur diśaḥ
children.translated_text: The sun was covered by darkness; none of the directions shone forth.

children.text: bhasmanā cāvṛtaṃ sarvaṃ saṃmūḍham iva tad balam ||
children.translated_text: Everything was covered with ash, and that army was as if bewildered.

children.text: vasiṣṭha ṛṣayaś cānye rājā ca sasutas tadā
children.translated_text: <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, the other seers, and the king with his sons at that time

children.text: sasaṃjñā iva tatrāsan sarvam anyad vicetanam ||
children.translated_text: remained there as if still conscious; all the rest were senseless.

children.text: tasmiṃs tamasi ghore tu bhasmacchanneva sā camūḥ
children.translated_text: In that dreadful darkness, with that army as if covered by ash,
he saw one of fearful appearance, wearing a mass of matted hair:

children.text: kailāsam iva durdharṣaṃ kālāgnim iva duḥsaham
children.translated_text: as unassailable as <s>Kailāsa</s>, as unbearable as the fire of time,
as if blazing with splendors, impossible for ordinary people to look upon.
He had slung an axe upon his shoulder and held a bow like a mass of lightning,

children.text: pragṛhya śaramukhyaṃ ca tripuraghnaṃ yathā haram ||
children.translated_text: and grasped a foremost arrow, like <s>Hara</s>, the destroyer of <s>Tripura</s>.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmasaṃkāśaṃ jvalantam iva pāvakam
children.translated_text: Seeing him, fearful in appearance and blazing like fire,
the brahmins headed by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, devoted to recitation and oblation,

children.text: saṃgatā munayaḥ sarve saṃjajalpur atho mithaḥ ||
children.translated_text: all the gathered sages then spoke among themselves:
"Surely, angry over his father's killing, he will not destroy the kṣatriyas?
Having formerly slaughtered the kṣatriyas, his anger gone and his fever passed,

children.text: kṣatrasyotsādanaṃ bhūyo na khalv asya cikīrṣitam ||
children.translated_text: surely he does not wish again to exterminate the kṣatriya class."
Having spoken thus and taken up the arghya, the honor offering, for the fearsome-looking <s>Bhārgava</s>,

children.text: ṛṣayo rāma rāmeti madhurāṃ vācam abruvan ||
children.translated_text: the seers addressed him with sweet speech, saying, "<s>Rāma</s>, <s>Rāma</s>."

children.text: pratigṛhya tu tāṃ pūjām ṛṣidattāṃ pratāpavān
children.translated_text: Then the powerful one, receiving that worship given by the seers,
<s>Rāma Jāmadagnya</s> addressed <s>Rāma Dāśarathi</s>:

children.text: rāma dāśarathe vīra vīryaṃ te śrūyate 'dbhutam
children.translated_text: "<s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, hero, your astonishing valor is heard of,

children.text: dhanuṣo bhedanaṃ caiva nikhilena mayā śrutam ||
children.translated_text: and I have heard fully of the breaking of the bow.

children.text: tad adbhutam acintyaṃ ca bhedanaṃ dhanuṣas tvayā
children.translated_text: That breaking of the bow by you was wondrous and inconceivable.

children.text: tac chrutvāham anuprāpto dhanur gṛhyāparaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: Hearing of it, I have come here, taking up another fine bow.

children.text: tad idaṃ ghorasaṃkāśaṃ jāmadagnyaṃ mahad dhanuḥ
children.translated_text: This is that great bow of the son of <s>Jamadagni</s>, terrible in appearance.
Fit it with an arrow, and show your own strength.

children.text: tad ahaṃ te balaṃ dṛṣṭvā dhanuṣo 'sya prapūraṇe
children.translated_text: Having seen your strength in the fitting of this bow,
I shall grant you a duel, one worthy of being praised for valor."

children.text: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rājā daśarathas tadā
children.translated_text: Hearing that statement of his, King <s>Daśaratha</s> then,
with a downcast face and distressed, spoke with joined palms:
"You have become pacified from anger against kṣatriyas, O brahmin of great fame,

children.text: bālānāṃ mama putrāṇām abhayaṃ dātum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: You ought to grant fearlessness to my young sons.
You were born in the family of the <s>Bhārgavas</s>, men devoted to recitation and vows;
after making a promise before thousand-eyed <s>Indra</s>, you laid down your weapon.

children.text: sa tvaṃ dharmaparo bhūtvā kāśyapāya vasuṃdharām
children.translated_text: Then, being devoted to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), you gave the earth to <s>Kāśyapa</s>,
went to the forest, and made your dwelling on <s>Mahendra</s>.
O great sage, you have come here for the complete destruction of me and mine;

children.text: na caikasmin hate rāme sarve jīvāmahe vayam ||
children.translated_text: for if <s>Rāma</s> alone is slain, none of us will remain alive.
While <s>Daśaratha</s> was speaking in this way, the powerful <s>Jāmadagnya</s>,
disregarding that speech entirely, addressed <s>Rāma</s> alone.

children.text: ime dve dhanuṣī śreṣṭhe divye lokābhiviśrute
children.translated_text: These are the two best bows, divine and renowned throughout the worlds,
firm, strong, foremost, and well made by <s>Viśvakarman</s>.
One was assigned by the gods to <s>Tryambaka</s>, who wished to fight;

children.text: tripuraghnaṃ naraśreṣṭha bhagnaṃ kākutstha yat tvayā ||
children.translated_text: that destroyer of <s>Tripura</s>, O best of men, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, is the one you broke.

children.text: idaṃ dvitīyaṃ durdharṣaṃ viṣṇor dattaṃ surottamaiḥ
children.translated_text: This second, hard to assail, was given to <s>Viṣṇu</s> by the highest gods,

children.text: samānasāraṃ kākutstha raudreṇa dhanuṣā tv idam ||
children.translated_text: and this bow, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, is equal in essence to the bow of <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: tadā tu devatāḥ sarvāḥ pṛcchanti sma pitāmaham
children.translated_text: Then all the deities questioned <s>Pitāmaha</s>
in order to examine the relative strength and weakness of <s>Śitikaṇṭha</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Knowing the intention of the deities, <s>Pitāmaha</s>,
best of truth-speakers, produced a conflict between those two.

children.text: virodhe ca mahad yuddham abhavad romaharṣaṇam
children.translated_text: And when the conflict arose, there was a great battle, making the hair stand on end,
between <s>Śitikaṇṭha</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, each seeking victory over the other.

children.text: tadā taj jṛmbhitaṃ śaivaṃ dhanur bhīmaparākramam
children.translated_text: Then that fearsome and powerful bow of <s>Śiva</s> was made to gape and slacken;
and <s>Mahādeva</s>, the three-eyed one, was checked by a mere hum.
Then the gods, together with hosts of seers and with the <s>Cāraṇas</s>, assembled

children.text: yācitau praśamaṃ tatra jagmatus tau surottamau ||
children.translated_text: and entreated them; thereupon those two highest gods came to peace.

children.text: jṛmbhitaṃ tad dhanur dṛṣṭvā śaivaṃ viṣṇuparākramaiḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that bow of <s>Śiva</s> disabled by the powers of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: adhikaṃ menire viṣṇuṃ devāḥ sarṣigaṇās tadā ||
children.translated_text: the gods, together with the hosts of seers, then considered <s>Viṣṇu</s> superior.

children.text: dhanū rudras tu saṃkruddho videheṣu mahāyaśāḥ
children.translated_text: But glorious <s>Rudra</s>, enraged, gave that bow among the <s>Videhas</s>,
together with its arrow, into the hand of the royal seer <s>Devarāta</s>.

children.text: idaṃ ca vaiṣṇavaṃ rāma dhanuḥ parapuraṃjayam
children.translated_text: And this Vaiṣṇava bow, O <s>Rāma</s>, conqueror of enemy cities,

children.text: ṛcīke bhārgave prādād viṣṇuḥ sa nyāsam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> gave to <s>Ṛcīka</s> the <s>Bhārgava</s> as an excellent deposit.
The greatly radiant <s>Ṛcīka</s> gave the divine bow to his son,

children.text: pitur mama dadau divyaṃ jamadagner mahātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: to my father, the great-souled <s>Jamadagni</s>, against whom no act could prevail.
When my father, endowed with the power of austerity, had laid down his weapons,

children.text: arjuno vidadhe mṛtyuṃ prākṛtāṃ buddhim āsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Arjuna</s>, adopting a base intention, brought death upon him.

children.text: vadham apratirūpaṃ tu pituḥ śrutvā sudāruṇam
children.translated_text: Hearing of the terrible and unfitting slaughter of my father,

children.text: kṣatram utsādayan roṣāj jātaṃ jātam anekaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I, out of anger, repeatedly destroyed the <s>kṣatra</s> (warrior order) as soon as it was born.
And after gaining the entire earth, O <s>Rāma</s>, at the end of a sacrifice
I gave it as sacrificial fee to great-souled <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the doer of holy deeds.
Then, dwelling on <s>Mahendra</s> and endowed with the power of austerity,

children.text: śrutavān dhanuṣo bhedaṃ tato 'haṃ drutam āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: I heard of the breaking of the bow, and for that reason I came swiftly.

children.text: tad idaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ rāma pitṛpaitāmahaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: Therefore take up this great Vaiṣṇava bow, O <s>Rāma</s>, inherited from my father and grandfather;
keeping <s>kṣatra-dharma</s> (the warrior's duty) before you, take this excellent bow.
Fit an arrow to the best of bows, O conqueror of enemy cities,

children.text: yadi śaknosi kākutstha dvaṃdvaṃ dāsyāmi te tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: if you are able, O <s>Kākutstha</s>; then I shall give you single combat.

children.text: śrutvā taj jāmadagnyasya vākyaṃ dāśarathis tadā
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech of <s>Jāmadagnya</s>, the son of <s>Daśaratha</s> then,
restraining his words out of respect for his father, addressed <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: śrutavān asmi yat karma kṛtavān asi bhārgava
children.translated_text: I have heard of the deed that you performed, O <s>Bhārgava</s>;
O brahmin, we approve of you, since you stood upon the repayment of your debt to your father.
But, O <s>Bhārgava</s>, as though I were without valor and incapable according to <s>kṣatra-dharma</s>,

children.text: avajānāmi me tejaḥ paśya me 'dya parākramam ||
children.translated_text: you disparage my energy; behold my prowess today.

children.text: ity uktvā rāghavaḥ kruddho bhārgavasya varāyudham
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the angry <s>Rāghava</s>, swift in valor,
took from <s>Bhārgava</s>'s hand both the excellent weapon and the arrow.

children.text: āropya sa dhanū rāmaḥ śaraṃ sajyaṃ cakāra ha
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> set the arrow on that bow and made it strung;

children.text: jāmadagnyaṃ tato rāmaṃ rāmaḥ kruddho 'bravīd vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then the angry <s>Rāma</s> spoke these words to <s>Rāma</s> the <s>Jāmadagnya</s>.
Because you are a brahmin, you are worthy of honor from me, and also because of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>;

children.text: tasmāc chakto na te rāma moktuṃ prāṇaharaṃ śaram ||
children.translated_text: therefore, O <s>Rāma</s>, though I am able, I will not release this life-taking arrow against you.
But this power of movement of yours, O <s>Rāma</s>, won by the power of austerity,

children.text: lokān apratimān vāpi haniṣyāmi yad icchasi ||
children.translated_text: or else your incomparable worlds, I shall destroy; choose which you wish.

children.text: na hy ayaṃ vaiṣṇavo divyaḥ śaraḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ
children.translated_text: For this divine Vaiṣṇava arrow, O conqueror of enemy cities,
does not fall in vain by its force, destroying the pride born of strength.
To see <s>Rāma</s> bearing the excellent weapon, the gods with the hosts of seers,
placing <s>Pitāmaha</s> at their head, assembled there in groups.
And <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Apsarases</s>, <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Cāraṇas</s>, and <s>Kiṃnaras</s>,

children.text: yakṣarākṣasanāgāś ca tad draṣṭuṃ mahad adbhutam ||
children.translated_text: as well as <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and <s>Nāgas</s>, came to see that great wonder.
When the world was stunned and <s>Rāma</s> was holding the excellent bow,
that powerless <s>Jāmadagnya Rāma</s> looked upon <s>Rāma</s>.
Deprived of strength by his splendors and made inert, <s>Jāmadagnya</s>

children.text: rāmaṃ kamalapattrākṣaṃ mandaṃ mandam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: slowly, very slowly, spoke to lotus-petal-eyed <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: kāśyapāya mayā dattā yadā pūrvaṃ vasuṃdharā
children.translated_text: When the earth was formerly given by me to <s>Kāśyapa</s>,

children.text: viṣaye me na vastavyam iti māṃ kāśyapo 'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kāśyapa</s> said to me, 'You must not dwell in my domain.'

children.text: so 'haṃ guruvacaḥ kurvan pṛthivyāṃ na vase niśām
children.translated_text: So, carrying out my guru's command, I do not stay a night upon the earth;

children.text: iti pratijñā kākutstha kṛtā vai kāśyapasya ha ||
children.translated_text: such indeed was the promise made to <s>Kāśyapa</s>, O <s>Kākutstha</s>.

children.text: tad imāṃ tvaṃ gatiṃ vīra hantuṃ nārhasi rāghava
children.translated_text: Therefore, O hero, O <s>Rāghava</s>, you ought not to destroy this power of movement of mine;
I shall go, with the speed of thought, to <s>Mahendra</s>, best of mountains.

children.text: lokās tv apratimā rāma nirjitās tapasā mayā
children.translated_text: But incomparable worlds, O <s>Rāma</s>, have been won by me through asceticism;

children.text: jahi tāñ śaramukhyena mā bhūt kālasya paryayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: strike them with your foremost arrow; let there be no passing of the appointed moment.
I know you as the imperishable slayer of <s>Madhu</s>, the lord of the gods;
from your handling of this bow, may there be welfare for you, O scorcher of foes.
All these hosts of gods have assembled and are watching
you, whose deeds are unmatched, who have no rival in battle.

children.text: na ceyaṃ mama kākutstha vrīḍā bhavitum arhati
children.translated_text: And this, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, should not become a shame for me,
that I have been turned away by you, the lord of the three worlds.

children.text: śaram apratimaṃ rāma moktum arhasi suvrata
children.translated_text: Release the incomparable arrow, O <s>Rāma</s>, O man of good vows;
when the arrow has been released, I shall go to <s>Mahendra</s>, the best of mountains.

children.text: tathā bruvati rāme tu jāmadagnye pratāpavān
children.translated_text: As <s>Rāma</s> <s>Jāmadagnya</s> was speaking thus, the powerful

children.text: rāmo dāśarathiḥ śrīmāṃś cikṣepa śaram uttamam ||
children.translated_text: illustrious <s>Rāma</s> <s>Dāśarathi</s> loosed the excellent arrow.

children.text: tato vitimirāḥ sarvā diśaḥ copadiśas tathā
children.translated_text: Then all the quarters and the intermediate quarters became free from darkness,
and the gods, together with the hosts of seers, praised <s>Rāma</s>, who had raised his weapon.

children.text: rāmaṃ dāśarathiṃ rāmo jāmadagnyaḥ praśasya ca
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> <s>Jāmadagnya</s>, after praising <s>Rāma</s> <s>Dāśarathi</s>,
then circumambulated him and, the lord, went to his own destined course.

children.text: gate rāme praśāntātmā rāmo dāśarathir dhanuḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāma</s> had gone, peaceful-souled <s>Rāma</s> <s>Dāśarathi</s>
gave the bow, together with the arrow, into the hand of immeasurable <s>Varuṇa</s>.
Then <s>Rāma</s>, having bowed to the sages headed by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,
saw his father distraught, and the delight of <s>Raghu</s> spoke:
<s>Rāma</s> <s>Jāmadagnya</s> has gone. Let the fourfold army proceed,
facing toward <s>Ayodhyā</s>, protected by you as its lord.

children.text: rāmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā rājā daśarathaḥ sutam
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Rāma</s>'s words, king <s>Daśaratha</s>
embraced his son with both arms and smelled <s>Rāghava</s>'s head.

children.text: gato rāma iti śrutvā hṛṣṭaḥ pramudito nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that <s>Rāma</s> had gone, the king was delighted and overjoyed;

children.text: codayāmāsa tāṃ senāṃ jagāmāśu tataḥ purīm ||
children.translated_text: he urged on that army and then quickly went to the city.
The king entered the lovely city, adorned with banners and standards and resounding with the sound of musical instruments,
with its royal roads sprinkled and beautiful, strewn with masses of flowers,
with citizens favorable to the royal entry and uttering auspicious words,
filled and adorned with crowds of people.

children.text: kausalyā ca sumitrā ca kaikeyī ca sumadhyamā
children.translated_text: <s>Kausalyā</s>, <s>Sumitrā</s>, and the slender-waisted <s>Kaikeyī</s>,
intent on receiving the brides, and the other royal women as well,

children.text: tataḥ sītāṃ mahābhāgām ūrmilāṃ ca yaśasvinīm
children.translated_text: then received greatly fortunate <s>Sītā</s> and famed <s>Ūrmilā</s>,
and also both daughters of <s>Kuśadhvaja</s>; the king's wives took them in.
Adorned with auspicious greetings and clothed in linen garments,
all those women quickly worshiped the shrines of the deities.
Having paid reverence to all who deserved reverence, all the royal daughters then

children.text: remire muditāḥ sarvā bhartṛbhiḥ sahitā rahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: rejoiced happily in private, together with their husbands.
Married, trained in weapons, with wealth and with friends,
those bull-like men lived attending upon their father.
Among them <s>Rāma</s>, very famous in the world and true in valor,
became the most endowed with virtues, like <s>Svayambhū</s> among beings.

children.text: rāmas tu sītayā sārdhaṃ vijahāra bahūn ṛtūn
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, together with <s>Sītā</s>, enjoyed himself through many seasons,

children.text: manasvī tadgatas tasyā nityaṃ hṛdi samarpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: high-minded, his mind fixed on her, and always lodged in her heart.

children.text: priyā tu sītā rāmasya dārāḥ pitṛkṛtā iti
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s> was dear to <s>Rāma</s> because she was a wife given by his father;

children.text: guṇād rūpaguṇāc cāpi prītir bhūyo vyavardhata ||
children.translated_text: because of her qualities and because of the qualities of her beauty, his love grew still more.

children.text: tasyāś ca bhartā dviguṇaṃ hṛdaye parivartate
children.translated_text: And her husband moved twofold within her heart;

children.text: antarjātam api vyaktam ākhyāti hṛdayaṃ hṛdā ||
children.translated_text: even what is born within, the heart makes clear to the heart.
For him, especially, <s>Maithilī</s>, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,

children.text: devatābhiḥ samā rūpe sītā śrīr iva rūpiṇī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s>, equal to goddesses in beauty, was like <s>Śrī</s> embodied.
Joined with her, that son of a royal seer, with the charming and deeply loving daughter of a supreme king,

children.text: atīva rāmaḥ śuśubhe 'tikāmayā vibhuḥ śriyā viṣṇur ivāmareśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> shone exceedingly, like mighty <s>Viṣṇu</s>, lord of the immortals, with <s>Śrī</s>.

children.text: kasyacit tv atha kālasya rājā daśarathaḥ sutam
children.translated_text: Then, after some time, king <s>Daśaratha</s>
said to his son <s>Bharata</s>, <s>Kaikeyī</s>'s son, O delight of <s>Raghu</s>:
This son of the king of the <s>Kekayas</s> is staying here, my son;

children.text: tvāṃ netum āgato vīra yudhājin mātulas tava ||
children.translated_text: your maternal uncle <s>Yudhājit</s> has come to lead you away, O hero.
Hearing this from <s>Daśaratha</s>, <s>Bharata</s>, <s>Kaikeyī</s>'s son,
then prepared to go, together with <s>Śatrughna</s>.
Taking leave of his father, and of <s>Rāma</s> whose actions were unwearied,
and of his mothers too, that best of men went together with <s>Śatrughna</s>.
<s>Yudhājit</s>, having obtained <s>Bharata</s> together with <s>Śatrughna</s>, was delighted;

children.text: svapuraṃ prāviśad vīraḥ pitā tasya tutoṣa ha ||
children.translated_text: the hero entered his own city, and his father was pleased.

children.text: sa tatra nyavasad bhrātrā saha satkārasatkṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: He lived there with his brother, honored with due honors,
fondled with a son's affection by his maternal relative <s>Aśvapati</s>.

children.text: tatrāpi nivasantau tau tarpyamāṇau ca kāmataḥ
children.translated_text: Although the two were dwelling there and were satisfied as they wished,

children.text: bhrātarau smaratāṃ vīrau vṛddhaṃ daśarathaṃ nṛpam ||
children.translated_text: the heroic brothers remembered the aged king <s>Daśaratha</s>.

children.text: rājāpi tau mahātejāḥ sasmāra proṣitau sutau
children.translated_text: The greatly radiant king too remembered his sons who were away,
both <s>Bharata</s> and <s>Śatrughna</s>, comparable to <s>Mahendra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>.

children.text: sarva eva tu tasyeṣṭāś catvāraḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ
children.translated_text: All four bull-like men were dear to him,
like four arms sprung from his own body.

children.text: teṣām api mahātejā rāmo ratikaraḥ pituḥ
children.translated_text: Yet among them mighty <s>Rāma</s>, who brought delight to his father,
became the most endowed with virtues, like <s>Svayambhū</s> among beings.

children.text: gate ca bharate rāmo lakṣmaṇaś ca mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Bharata</s> had gone, <s>Rāma</s> and mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>
then honored their father, who was like a god.
Putting their father's command foremost, righteous-souled <s>Rāma</s>

children.text: cakāra rāmo dharmātmā priyāṇi ca hitāni ca ||
children.translated_text: did all the affairs of the citizens, and things both dear and beneficial.
Toward his mothers, highly self-controlled, he performed the duties owed to mothers.
At the proper times he attended to the weighty duties owed to his elders.

children.text: evaṃ daśarathaḥ prīto brāhmaṇā naigamās tathā
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Daśaratha</s> was pleased, as were the brahmins and the townsmen,
and all the inhabitants of the realm were pleased by <s>Rāma</s>'s character and conduct.

children.text: sa hi nityaṃ praśāntātmā mṛdupūrvaṃ ca bhāṣate
children.translated_text: For he was always tranquil in spirit and spoke gently first;
even when addressed harshly, he did not give a harsh reply.
He was satisfied by even a single service rendered in some way,

children.text: na smaraty apakārāṇāṃ śatam apy ātmavattayā ||
children.translated_text: and through self-mastery he did not remember even a hundred offenses.
With good men mature in conduct, mature in knowledge, and mature in age,

children.text: kathayann āsta vai nityam astrayogyāntareṣv api ||
children.translated_text: he constantly conversed, even in the intervals of weapons practice.
He was of auspicious lineage, virtuous, not low-spirited, truthful in speech, and upright,
and he had been well disciplined by elders and by twice-born men who understood <s>dharma</s> and advantage.
He knew the true nature of <s>dharma</s>, advantage, and desire; he was mindful and possessed of ready intelligence.
He was fully trained and expert in worldly convention and customary conduct.
He knew the śāstras, was grateful, and understood distinctions among men,
and he was discerning in restraint and favor, each according to justice.
He knew the means in matters of revenue, and he understood the proper handling of expenditure once examined.
He had attained excellence among bodies of śāstra, even among mixed and varied disciplines.

children.text: arthadharmau ca saṃgṛhya sukhatantro na cālasaḥ
children.translated_text: Having mastered advantage and <s>dharma</s>, he was not ruled by pleasure and was not idle.
He understood the divisions of meaning in the arts of recreation.
He was skilled in the mounting and training of elephants and horses,
foremost among knowers of the <s>Dhanurveda</s>, and in the world regarded as an eminent chariot-warrior.
He was one who could march against an enemy and strike, and he was expert in leading an army.

children.text: apradhṛṣyaś ca saṃgrāme kruddhair api surāsuraiḥ
children.translated_text: In battle he could not be overpowered, even by gods and asuras enraged.

children.text: anasūyo jitakrodho na dṛpto na ca matsarī
children.translated_text: He was free from envy, had conquered anger, was not arrogant, and was not jealous.

children.text: na cāvamantā bhūtānāṃ na ca kālavaśānugaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He did not show contempt for beings, nor was he one who merely followed the sway of time.

children.text: evaṃ śreṣṭhair guṇair yuktaḥ prajānāṃ pārthivātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: Endowed with such excellent qualities, the king's son was beloved of the subjects.
He was esteemed in the three worlds, and in forbearance he had the qualities of the earth.
In intelligence he was equal to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, and in valor also to the lord of <s>Śacī</s>.
Thus, by qualities dear to all subjects and producing his father's affection,

children.text: guṇair viruruce rāmo dīptaḥ sūrya ivāṃśubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> shone forth, radiant like the sun with its rays.
The earth desired him as her lord, one endowed with such conduct,
with unassailable prowess and like the guardians of the worlds.

children.text: etais tu bahubhir yuktaṃ guṇair anupamaiḥ sutam
children.translated_text: Seeing his son endowed with these many incomparable qualities,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā daśaratho rājā cakre cintāṃ paraṃtapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: king <s>Daśaratha</s>, scorcher of foes, gave thought to the matter.

children.text: eṣā hy asya parā prītir hṛdi samparivartate
children.translated_text: This supreme delight revolved in his heart:

children.text: kadā nāma sutaṃ drakṣyāmy abhiṣiktam ahaṃ priyam ||
children.translated_text: "When indeed shall I see my dear son consecrated?
He desires the growth of the world and has compassion for all beings;

children.text: mattaḥ priyataro loke parjanya iva vṛṣṭimān ||
children.translated_text: he is dearer than I am in the world, like a rain-bringing cloud.
In valor he is equal to <s>Yama</s> and <s>Śakra</s>, and in judgment equal to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>;
in firmness he is equal to a mountain, and he is richer in virtues than I am.

children.text: mahīm aham imāṃ kṛtsnām adhitiṣṭhantam ātmajam
children.translated_text: May I, at this age, see my own son ruling

children.text: anena vayasā dṛṣṭvā yathā svargam avāpnuyām ||
children.translated_text: this entire earth, so that I may attain heaven."

children.text: taṃ samīkṣya mahārājo yuktaṃ samuditair guṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: Having considered him, endowed with the qualities gathered together in him,
the great king, deciding together with his ministers, regarded him as yuvarāja.
The lord of the earth summoned leading men from the earth,
residents of many cities and also separate provincial peoples.
Then, on the various seats provided by the king,
the disciplined kings sat down facing the king himself.

children.text: sa labdhamānair vinayānvitair nṛpaiḥ purālayair jānapadaiś ca mānavaiḥ
children.translated_text: Surrounded by honored and modest kings, and by men of the city and countryside

children.text: upopaviṣṭair nṛpatir vṛto babhau sahasracakṣur bhagavān ivāmaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: who sat near him, the king shone like the blessed thousand-eyed one surrounded by the immortals.
Then the lord of the earth addressed the entire assembly
and spoke these beneficial, gladdening, incomparable words.
With a great voice, deep and resonant, like the sound of a war-drum,

children.text: svareṇa mahatā rājā jīmūta iva nādayan ||
children.translated_text: the king made it resound like a rain-cloud as he spoke:
"This whole world, guarded by the former <s>Ikṣvāku</s> kings,
is worthy of happiness, and I wish to join it with welfare.
I too have followed the path practiced by my forefathers,
tirelessly protecting the subjects at all times as far as I was able.

children.text: idaṃ śarīraṃ kṛtsnasya lokasya caratā hitam
children.translated_text: This body of mine, while acting for the welfare of the whole world,
has grown old beneath the shade of this white parasol.
Having lived through many thousands of years of life,
I desire rest for this old body.
For I am weary from carrying the heavy burden of <s>dharma</s> for the world,
a burden attended by royal power and hard for men of unconquered senses to bear.

children.text: so 'haṃ viśramam icchāmi putraṃ kṛtvā prajāhite
children.translated_text: Therefore I wish for rest, after appointing my son to the welfare of the subjects,
with the approval of all these assembled foremost twice-born men.

children.text: anujāto hi me sarvair guṇair jyeṣṭho mamātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: For my eldest son, <s>Rāma</s>, has taken after me in all qualities,
equal to <s>Purandara</s> in valor and conqueror of enemy cities.

children.text: taṃ candram iva puṣyeṇa yuktaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ varam
children.translated_text: That bull among men, best of upholders of <s>dharma</s>, like the moon joined with <s>Puṣya</s>,
I shall gladly join to the office of yuvarāja.

children.text: anurūpaḥ sa vo nātho lakṣmīvāṃl lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ
children.translated_text: He is a suitable lord for you, fortunate and the elder brother of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>;

children.text: trailokyam api nāthena yena syān nāthavattaram ||
children.translated_text: with him as lord, even the three worlds would be better provided with a lord.

children.text: anena śreyasā sadyaḥ saṃyojyāham imāṃ mahīm
children.translated_text: By immediately joining this earth with this welfare,

children.text: gatakleśo bhaviṣyāmi sute tasmin niveśya vai ||
children.translated_text: and entrusting it to that son, I shall become free from toil."

children.text: iti bruvantaṃ muditāḥ pratyanandan nṛpā nṛpam
children.translated_text: As the king spoke thus, the delighted rulers applauded the king,
like peacocks greeting a great rain-cloud as it thunders with rain.
Knowing fully the intention of him who understood <s>dharma</s> and material welfare,

children.text: ūcuś ca manasā jñātvā vṛddhaṃ daśarathaṃ nṛpam ||
children.translated_text: and understanding it in their minds, they spoke to the aged King <s>Daśaratha</s>:
"You are aged, O king, after many thousands of years.
Therefore consecrate <s>Rāma</s>, the prince, as heir-apparent, O lord of the earth."

children.text: iti tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rājā teṣāṃ manaḥpriyam
children.translated_text: Hearing that statement of theirs, pleasing to his mind,

children.text: ajānann iva jijñāsur idaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: the king, as if not knowing it and wishing to find out more, spoke these words:

children.text: kathaṃ nu mayi dharmeṇa pṛthivīm anuśāsati
children.translated_text: "When I am ruling the earth according to <s>dharma</s>,
why do you wish to see my son as heir-apparent?"

children.text: te tam ūcur mahātmānaṃ paurajānapadaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Together with the townsmen and country people, they said to that great-souled one:

children.text: bahavo nṛpa kalyāṇā guṇāḥ putrasya santi te ||
children.translated_text: "Many auspicious virtues, O king, belong to your son.
<s>Rāma</s>, equal to <s>Śakra</s> in divine qualities and true in valor,

children.text: ikṣvākubhyo hi sarvebhyo 'py atirakto viśāṃ pate ||
children.translated_text: is dearer than all the <s>Ikṣvākus</s>, O lord of the people.
<s>Rāma</s> is a true man in the world, devoted to truth and <s>dharma</s>.
He knows <s>dharma</s>, keeps his promises, is virtuous in conduct, and free from envy.
He is patient, conciliatory, gentle, grateful, and master of his senses.

children.text: mṛduś ca sthiracittaś ca sadā bhavyo 'nasūyakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is mild, firm-minded, always worthy, and without malice.

children.text: priyavādī ca bhūtānāṃ satyavādī ca rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> speaks kindly to living beings and speaks the truth.
He attends upon learned, aged brahmins.

children.text: tenāsyehātulā kīrtir yaśas tejaś ca vardhate
children.translated_text: Because of him, incomparable fame, glory, and splendor increase for you here.
He is skilled in all weapons used by gods, asuras, and men.

children.text: yadā vrajati saṃgrāmaṃ grāmārthe nagarasya vā
children.translated_text: When he goes to battle for the sake of a village or a city,
he goes with <s>Saumitri</s> and does not return without victory.

children.text: saṃgrāmāt punar āgamya kuñjareṇa rathena vā
children.translated_text: After coming back from battle, whether on an elephant or in a chariot,
he always asks the citizens about their welfare as if they were his own people.
About their sons, sacred fires, wives, and groups of servants and pupils,
he asks fully and in order, like a father asking about his own sons.

children.text: śuśrūṣante ca vaḥ śiṣyāḥ kaccit karmasu daṃśitāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Do your pupils serve you? Are they diligent in their duties?'
Thus <s>Rāma</s>, tiger among men, always speaks to us.
In people's misfortunes he becomes deeply sorrowful,
and at all festivals he rejoices like a father.
Truth-speaking, a great archer, devoted to serving elders, and self-controlled,

children.text: vatsaḥ śreyasi jātas te diṣṭyāsau tava rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: that dear son of yours was born for welfare; fortunate indeed are you, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: diṣṭyā putraguṇair yukto mārīca iva kaśyapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Fortunately you have a son endowed with virtues, as <s>Kaśyapa</s> had <s>Mārīca</s>.

children.text: balam ārogyam āyuś ca rāmasya viditātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: All the people wish for strength, health, and long life

children.text: āśaṃsate janaḥ sarvo rāṣṭre puravare tathā ||
children.translated_text: for wise <s>Rāma</s>, throughout the kingdom and likewise in the best of cities.

children.text: abhyantaraś ca bāhyaś ca paurajānapado janaḥ
children.translated_text: The people inside and outside, the townsmen and country folk,

children.text: striyo vṛddhās taruṇyaś ca sāyamprātaḥ samāhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: women, old people, and young women, intent at evening and morning,
bow to all the gods for the sake of glorious <s>Rāma</s>.
May what they have prayed for, O lord, be fulfilled through your favor.
May we see <s>Rāma</s>, dark as a blue lotus and destroyer of all enemies,
your son, O best of kings, established in the office of heir-apparent.

children.text: taṃ devadevopamam ātmajaṃ te sarvasya lokasya hite niviṣṭam
children.translated_text: Your son, comparable to the lord of gods and devoted to the good of the whole world,

children.text: hitāya naḥ kṣipram udārajuṣṭaṃ mudābhiṣektuṃ varada tvam arhasi ||
children.translated_text: you ought, O giver of boons, swiftly and joyfully to consecrate for our welfare, he who is cherished by the noble."
The king received all their lotus-like joined hands,
and spoke to them words pleasing and beneficial:
"Ah, I am supremely pleased, and my greatness is unequaled,

children.text: yan me jyeṣṭhaṃ priyaṃ putraṃ yauvarājyastham icchatha ||
children.translated_text: since you wish my eldest, beloved son to be established as heir-apparent."

children.text: iti pratyarcya tān rājā brāhmaṇān idam abravīt
children.translated_text: Having honored them in return, the king spoke these words to the brahmins,
to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and <s>Vāmadeva</s>, while those very men were listening:

children.text: caitraḥ śrīmān ayaṃ māsaḥ puṇyaḥ puṣpitakānanaḥ
children.translated_text: "This is the splendid month of <s>Caitra</s>, holy, with the forests in flower.
Let everything be prepared for <s>Rāma</s>'s heir-apparent consecration."

children.text: kṛtam ity eva cābrūtām abhigamya jagatpatim
children.translated_text: Approaching the lord of the world, the two best of twice-born sages, delighted and filled with joy,
said simply, "It is done," according to the words that had been spoken.

children.text: tataḥ sumantraṃ dyutimān rājā vacanam abravīt
children.translated_text: Then the radiant king spoke a command to <s>Sumantra</s>:

children.text: rāmaḥ kṛtātmā bhavatā śīghram ānīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "Let <s>Rāma</s>, whose self is disciplined, be brought quickly by you."
Promising, "So be it," <s>Sumantra</s>, by the king's command,
brought <s>Rāma</s> there by chariot, that best of chariot-warriors.

children.text: atha tatra samāsīnās tadā daśarathaṃ nṛpam
children.translated_text: Then the kings seated there at that time around King <s>Daśaratha</s>,

children.text: prācyodīcyāḥ pratīcyāś ca dākṣiṇātyāś ca bhūmipāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those from the east, north, west, and south,

children.text: mlecchāś cāryāś ca ye cānye vanaśailāntavāsinaḥ
children.translated_text: mlecchas, āryas, and others who dwelt at the edges of forests and mountains,

children.text: upāsāṃcakrire sarve taṃ devā iva vāsavam ||
children.translated_text: all attended upon him as the gods attend upon <s>Vāsava</s>.

children.text: teṣāṃ madhye sa rājarṣir marutām iva vāsavaḥ
children.translated_text: In their midst that royal seer, like <s>Vāsava</s> among the <s>Maruts</s>,
standing in the palace, saw his son coming in a chariot.
He was like a king of gandharvas, with his manliness famed in the world,
long-armed, great in spirit, and walking like an intoxicated elephant.
King <s>Daśaratha</s> was not satisfied, as he watched <s>Rāma</s> approaching,
with a face lovely as the moon and exceedingly pleasing to behold, stealing men's eyes and minds by his beauty, nobility, and virtues,
delighting his subjects like rain-clouds refreshing those scorched by heat.
The lord of men was never sated as he looked upon him coming near.
Having helped that <s>Rāghava</s> down from the excellent chariot, <s>Sumantra</s>
followed behind with joined palms as he went toward his father.
That <s>Rāghava</s>, bull among men, ascended the palace,

children.text: āruroha nṛpaṃ draṣṭuṃ saha sūtena rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: which resembled a peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>, together with the charioteer, in order to see the king.

children.text: sa prāñjalir abhipretya praṇataḥ pitur antike
children.translated_text: Approaching with joined palms, <s>Rāma</s> bowed down near his father,

children.text: nāma svaṃ śrāvayan rāmo vavande caraṇau pituḥ ||
children.translated_text: announced his own name, and paid homage to his father's feet.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā praṇataṃ pārśve kṛtāñjalipuṭaṃ nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing him bowed at his side, with his hands joined in reverence,
the king drew him up by his cupped hands and embraced his beloved son.
And for him the illustrious king indicated a raised seat, adorned with jewels and gold,
a splendid and beautiful supreme seat for <s>Rāma</s>.
Having taken that excellent seat, <s>Rāghava</s> made it shine,

children.text: svayeva prabhayā merum udaye vimalo raviḥ ||
children.translated_text: as the spotless sun at its rising lights up <s>Meru</s> with its own radiance.
Illuminated by him there, that assembly shone brightly,
like the autumn sky with its clear planets and stars, illuminated by the moon.

children.text: taṃ paśyamāno nṛpatis tutoṣa priyam ātmajam
children.translated_text: As the king watched his dear son, he was delighted,
as though seeing his own adorned self standing on the surface of a mirror.

children.text: sa taṃ sasmitam ābhāṣya putraṃ putravatāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the king, best of those who have sons, addressed that smiling son,

children.text: uvācedaṃ vaco rājā devendram iva kaśyapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and spoke these words, like <s>Kaśyapa</s> speaking to <s>Devendra</s>.

children.text: jyeṣṭhāyām asi me patnyāṃ sadṛśyāṃ sadṛśaḥ sutaḥ
children.translated_text: "You were born from my eldest queen, one worthy of me, a son like myself;

children.text: utpannas tvaṃ guṇaśreṣṭho mama rāmātmajaḥ priyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: you, <s>Rāma</s>, are my dear son, best in virtues.

children.text: tvayā yataḥ prajāś cemāḥ svaguṇair anurañjitāḥ
children.translated_text: Since these subjects have been won over by your own virtues,
therefore, under the conjunction with <s>Puṣya</s>, obtain the office of <s>yuvarāja</s> (heir apparent).

children.text: kāmatas tvaṃ prakṛtyaiva vinīto guṇavān asi
children.translated_text: Certainly, by your very nature you are disciplined and virtuous,

children.text: guṇavaty api tu snehāt putra vakṣyāmi te hitam ||
children.translated_text: yet, though you are virtuous, out of affection, my son, I shall tell you what is beneficial.

children.text: bhūyo vinayam āsthāya bhava nityaṃ jitendriyaḥ
children.translated_text: Taking on still greater humility, always be one whose senses are mastered,
and abandon the vices that arise from desire and anger.
Conducting yourself both through what is unseen and through what is plainly visible,
win the affection of all the ministers and the other constituent powers of the realm.
The man who rules the earth with his subjects satisfied and attached to him,
his friends rejoice, like immortals who have obtained nectar;

children.text: tasmāt putra tvam ātmānaṃ niyamyaiva samācara ||
children.translated_text: therefore, my son, restrain yourself and act accordingly.

children.text: tac chrutvā suhṛdas tasya rāmasya priyakāriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Rāma</s>'s friends, who wished to do what was pleasing to him,
quickly and hastily came to <s>Kausalyā</s> and reported it.

children.text: sā hiraṇyaṃ ca gāś caiva ratnāni vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kausalyā</s>, foremost of women, ordered gold, cows,
and various jewels to be given to those who brought the pleasing news.
Then <s>Rāghava</s> bowed to the king, mounted his chariot,

children.text: yayau svaṃ dyutimad veśma janaughaiḥ pratipūjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and went to his own radiant mansion, honored by crowds of people.

children.text: te cāpi paurā nṛpater vacas tacchrutvā tadā lābham iveṣṭam āpya
children.translated_text: And those citizens too, hearing that word of the king and then gaining it as though it were a desired profit,

children.text: narendram āmantrya gṛhāṇi gatvā devān samānarcur atīva hṛṣṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: took leave of the lord of men, went to their houses, and worshipped the gods, exceedingly delighted.

children.text: gateṣv atha nṛpo bhūyaḥ paureṣu saha mantribhiḥ
children.translated_text: After the citizens had gone, the king again, together with his ministers,

children.text: mantrayitvā tataś cakre niścayajñaḥ sa niścayam ||
children.translated_text: took counsel and then, knowing how to decide, made his decision.

children.text: śva eva puṣyo bhavitā śvo 'bhiṣecyeta tu me sutaḥ
children.translated_text: "Tomorrow indeed <s>Puṣya</s> will occur; tomorrow my son,
<s>Rāma</s>, lotus-red-eyed, should be consecrated to the office of <s>yuvarāja</s>," so the lord decided.
Then king <s>Daśaratha</s> entered the inner apartments at that time,
and commanded the charioteer, "Bring <s>Rāma</s> here again."

children.text: pratigṛhya sa tadvākyaṃ sūtaḥ punar upāyayau
children.translated_text: Accepting that command, the charioteer again went

children.text: rāmasya bhavanaṃ śīghraṃ rāmam ānayituṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: swiftly to <s>Rāma</s>'s palace, to bring <s>Rāma</s> once more.
When <s>Rāma</s> heard from the doorkeepers that the charioteer had come again,

children.text: śrutvaiva cāpi rāmas taṃ prāptaṃ śaṅkānvito 'bhavat ||
children.translated_text: he at once became apprehensive at his arrival.

children.text: praveśya cainaṃ tvaritaṃ rāmo vacanam abravīt
children.translated_text: Having quickly admitted him, <s>Rāma</s> spoke these words:

children.text: yad āgamanakṛtyaṃ te bhūyas tad brūhy aśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Tell me completely the purpose for which you have come again."

children.text: tam uvāca tataḥ sūto rājā tvāṃ draṣṭum icchati
children.translated_text: Then the charioteer said to him, "The king wishes to see you.

children.text: śrutvā pramāṇam atra tvaṃ gamanāyetarāya vā ||
children.translated_text: Having heard this, the decision here is yours, whether to go or not."
Hearing the charioteer's words, <s>Rāma</s>, filled with haste,
set out for the royal palace to see the lord of men again.

children.text: taṃ śrutvā samanuprāptaṃ rāmaṃ daśaratho nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that <s>Rāma</s> had arrived, king <s>Daśaratha</s>,
wishing for privacy with his excellent beloved son, had him enter the house.

children.text: praviśann eva ca śrīmān rāghavo bhavanaṃ pituḥ
children.translated_text: As soon as the illustrious <s>Rāghava</s> entered his father's palace,
he saw his father from afar and bowed down with joined hands.
The lord of the earth raised him as he bowed, embraced him,

children.text: pradiśya cāsmai ruciram āsanaṃ punar abravīt ||
children.translated_text: assigned him a handsome seat, and then spoke again.

children.text: rāma vṛddho 'smi dīrghāyur bhuktā bhogā mayepsitāḥ
children.translated_text: "<s>Rāma</s>, I am old and have lived long; the enjoyments I desired have been enjoyed by me,
and a hundred sacrifices, rich in food and abundant gifts, have likewise been performed.

children.text: jātam iṣṭam apatyaṃ me tvam adyānupamaṃ bhuvi
children.translated_text: The desired offspring, you, unequaled today on earth, has been born to me;

children.text: dattam iṣṭam adhītaṃ ca mayā puruṣasattama ||
children.translated_text: I have given gifts, performed sacrifices, and studied, O best of men.

children.text: anubhūtāni ceṣṭāni mayā vīra sukhāni ca
children.translated_text: Desired pleasures and joys have been experienced by me, O hero,
and I am free from debt to gods, seers, ancestors, brahmins, and also to myself.
Nothing remains for me to do except your consecration;

children.text: ato yat tvām ahaṃ brūyāṃ tan me tvaṃ kartum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: therefore whatever I tell you, you ought to do for me.

children.text: adya prakṛtayaḥ sarvās tvām icchanti narādhipam
children.translated_text: Today all the constituent powers of the realm desire you as lord of men;
therefore, my dear son, I shall consecrate you as <s>yuvarāja</s>.

children.text: api cādyāśubhān rāma svapnān paśyāmi dāruṇān
children.translated_text: Moreover today, <s>Rāma</s>, I see inauspicious and dreadful dreams,
and great meteors with thunderclaps are falling here with a mighty sound.

children.text: avaṣṭabdhaṃ ca me rāma nakṣatraṃ dāruṇair grahaiḥ
children.translated_text: My birth-star, <s>Rāma</s>, is beset by terrible planets;
the astrologers report it as afflicted by <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Aṅgāraka</s>, and <s>Rāhu</s>.
For when omens of such a kind generally arise,

children.text: rājā vā mṛtyum āpnoti ghorāṃ vāpadam ṛcchati ||
children.translated_text: a king either meets death or falls into a dreadful calamity.

children.text: tad yāvad eva me ceto na vimuhyati rāghava
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Rāghava</s>, only so long as my mind does not become confused,

children.text: tāvad evābhiṣiñcasva calā hi prāṇināṃ matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: only so long should you be consecrated; for the minds of living beings are unstable.

children.text: adya candro 'bhyupagataḥ puṣyāt pūrvaṃ punar vasum
children.translated_text: Today the moon has entered <s>Punarvasu</s>, which comes before <s>Puṣya</s>;
tomorrow those who ponder the divine signs will certainly declare the conjunction with <s>Puṣya</s>."
"Under <s>Puṣya</s>, then, have yourself consecrated; my mind seems to hurry me on.
Tomorrow I shall consecrate you in the office of <s>yuvarāja</s>, scorcher of foes.
Therefore tonight you must remain under vows, self-restrained,
fasting together with your wife and lying on a spread of darbha grass.

children.text: suhṛdaś cāpramattās tvāṃ rakṣantv adya samantataḥ
children.translated_text: Let your attentive friends guard you today on every side,
for undertakings of this kind are beset with many obstacles.

children.text: viproṣitaś ca bharato yāvad eva purād itaḥ
children.translated_text: And while <s>Bharata</s> is away from the city,

children.text: tāvad evābhiṣekas te prāptakālo mato mama ||
children.translated_text: that very time I consider the proper time for your consecration.

children.text: kāmaṃ khalu satāṃ vṛtte bhrātā te bharataḥ sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Indeed, your brother <s>Bharata</s> abides in the conduct of the good,
obedient to his elder, righteous, compassionate, and self-controlled.

children.text: kiṃ tu cittaṃ manuṣyāṇām anityam iti me matiḥ
children.translated_text: Yet the mind of human beings is inconstant: such is my opinion,

children.text: satāṃ ca dharmanityānāṃ kṛtaśobhi ca rāghava ||
children.translated_text: and, <s>Rāghava</s>, even of the good who are constant in <s>dharma</s>, it is adorned by what has been done.
Thus addressed and given leave regarding the consecration that was to take place tomorrow,
<s>Rāma</s>, having bowed to his father when told, 'Go,' went to his house.
Having entered his own dwelling after the king had appointed the consecration,

children.text: tasmin kṣaṇe vinirgatya mātur antaḥpuraṃ yayau ||
children.translated_text: he immediately came out and went to his mother's inner apartment.

children.text: tatra tāṃ pravaṇām eva mātaraṃ kṣaumavāsinīm
children.translated_text: There he saw his mother, just then bowed down, clad in linen,
restrained in speech in the shrine, praying for prosperity.

children.text: prāg eva cāgatā tatra sumitrā lakṣmaṇas tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Sumitrā</s> had already come there, and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> as well,
and <s>Sītā</s>, summoned after hearing the welcome news of <s>Rāma</s>'s consecration.

children.text: tasmin kāle hi kausalyā tasthāv āmīlitekṣaṇā
children.translated_text: At that time <s>Kausalyā</s> stood with eyes half closed,
attended by <s>Sumitrā</s>, by <s>Sītā</s>, and by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Having heard that, under <s>Puṣya</s>, her son's consecration as <s>yuvarāja</s> would occur,
she was meditating on the divine person <s>Janārdana</s> through breath-control.
Approaching her just so, still under observance, and bowing to her,

children.text: uvāca vacanaṃ rāmo harṣayaṃs tām idaṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> then spoke these words, gladdening her:
"Mother, I have been appointed by father to the task of guarding the subjects.

children.text: bhavitā śvo 'bhiṣeko me yathā me śāsanaṃ pituḥ ||
children.translated_text: Tomorrow my consecration will take place, according to my father's command to me.
<s>Sītā</s> too must fast together with me this night;

children.text: evam ṛtvigupādhyāyaiḥ saha mām uktavān pitā ||
children.translated_text: so father told me, together with the officiating priests and teachers.

children.text: yāni yāny atra yogyāni śvobhāviny abhiṣecane
children.translated_text: Whatever auspicious rites are fitting here for tomorrow's consecration,

children.text: tāni me maṅgalāny adya vaidehyāś caiva kāraya ||
children.translated_text: have those blessings performed today for me and for <s>Vaidehī</s> as well."
Hearing this long-desired news, <s>Kausalyā</s>
spoke these words to <s>Rāma</s>, her voice choked with tears of joy:

children.text: vatsa rāma ciraṃ jīva hatās te paripanthinaḥ
children.translated_text: "Child <s>Rāma</s>, live long; may your enemies be destroyed.

children.text: jñātīn me tvaṃ śriyā yuktaḥ sumitrāyāś ca nandaya ||
children.translated_text: Endowed with royal fortune, bring joy to my kinsmen and to those of <s>Sumitrā</s>.

children.text: kalyāṇe bata nakṣatre mayi jāto 'si putraka
children.translated_text: Surely, my little son, you were born to me under an auspicious constellation,

children.text: yena tvayā daśaratho guṇair ārādhitaḥ pitā ||
children.translated_text: since through your virtues your father <s>Daśaratha</s> has been won over.

children.text: amoghaṃ bata me kṣāntaṃ puruṣe puṣkarekṣaṇe
children.translated_text: Surely my endurance with regard to the lotus-eyed person has not been fruitless,
since this royal fortune of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> line will take refuge in you, my son."

children.text: ity evam ukto mātredaṃ rāmo bhāratam abravīt
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by his mother, <s>Rāma</s> spoke this to his brother,

children.text: prāñjaliṃ prahvam āsīnam abhivīkṣya smayann iva ||
children.translated_text: looking at him as he sat with joined palms, bowed low, and seeming to smile:

children.text: lakṣmaṇemāṃ mayā sārdhaṃ praśādhi tvaṃ vasuṃdharām
children.translated_text: "<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, rule this earth together with me.

children.text: dvitīyaṃ me 'ntarātmānaṃ tvām iyaṃ śrīr upasthitā ||
children.translated_text: This royal fortune has come to you, who are like my second inner self.

children.text: saumitre bhuṅkṣva bhogāṃs tvam iṣṭān rājyaphalāni ca
children.translated_text: Son of <s>Sumitrā</s>, enjoy the pleasures you desire and the fruits of kingship.

children.text: jīvitaṃ ca hi rājyaṃ ca tvadartham abhikāmaye ||
children.translated_text: For I desire both life and kingdom for your sake."

children.text: ity uktvā lakṣmaṇaṃ rāmo mātarāv abhivādya ca
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and having bowed to his mothers,

children.text: abhyanujñāpya sītāṃ ca jagāma svaṃ niveśanam ||
children.translated_text: and having taken leave of <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Rāma</s> went to his own residence.
After instructing <s>Rāma</s> regarding the consecration to take place tomorrow,
the king summoned the household priest <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and said this:
"Go, treasure of austerity, and have <s>Kākutstha</s> undertake the fast today,
together with his wife, with controlled vow, for the gain of prosperity, fame, and kingdom."

children.text: tatheti ca sa rājānam uktvā vedavidāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: Saying "So be it" to the king, that best of knowers of the Veda,
the blessed <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> himself went to <s>Rāma</s>'s residence.
Reaching <s>Rāma</s>'s house, which had the splendor of a mass of white cloud,
the best of sages entered three courtyards in his chariot.

children.text: tam āgatam ṛṣiṃ rāmas tvarann iva sasaṃbhramaḥ
children.translated_text: When the sage arrived, <s>Rāma</s>, as if hastening in agitation,
came out from his residence to honor that one worthy of honor.
Approaching quickly to the side of the wise man's chariot,
he himself helped him down from the chariot, taking hold of him.

children.text: sa cainaṃ praśritaṃ dṛṣṭvā sambhāṣyābhiprasādya ca
children.translated_text: Seeing him respectful, and having greeted and graciously received him,

children.text: priyārhaṃ harṣayan rāmam ity uvāca purohitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the priest gladdened <s>Rāma</s>, who deserved affection, and spoke thus:

children.text: prasannas te pitā rāma yauvarājyam avāpsyasi
children.translated_text: "Your father is pleased with you, <s>Rāma</s>; you will obtain the office of <s>yuvarāja</s>.

children.text: upavāsaṃ bhavān adya karotu saha sītayā ||
children.translated_text: Today you should observe a fast together with <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: prātas tvām abhiṣektā hi yauvarājye narādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: For in the morning the lord of men will consecrate you as <s>yuvarāja</s>,

children.text: pitā daśarathaḥ prītyā yayātiṃ nahuṣo yathā ||
children.translated_text: your father <s>Daśaratha</s> doing so with affection, as <s>Nahuṣa</s>'s son did <s>Yayāti</s>."

children.text: ity uktvā sa tadā rāmam upavāsaṃ yatavratam
children.translated_text: Having thus addressed <s>Rāma</s>, the sage then, with mantras,
caused him, together with <s>Vaidehī</s>, to undertake the disciplined vow of fasting.

children.text: tato yathāvad rāmeṇa sa rājño gurur arcitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, duly honored by <s>Rāma</s>, the king's guru
took leave of <s>Kākutstha</s> and departed from <s>Rāma</s>'s residence.

children.text: suhṛdbhis tatra rāmo 'pi tān anujñāpya sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> too, there with his friends, gave them leave in every way,
and, after being honored, entered inside, having given them leave in every way.
Then <s>Rāma</s>'s house, filled with joyful women and men, shone forth
like a lake with blooming lotuses and flocks of intoxicated birds.
From that residence of <s>Rāma</s>, famed like a royal palace,
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s> went out and saw the road crowded with people.
In <s>Ayodhyā</s>, on every side, the royal roads, with crowd after crowd,
became tightly thronged, surrounded by curious people.
Then, from the jostling of waves of masses of people, with a joyful sound,
there arose the roar of the royal road, like the roar of the ocean.
For on that day the roads had been sprinkled and swept, and the city <s>Ayodhyā</s>, garlanded with forest-flowers,
stood with the banners of its lofty houses raised high.
At that time the people dwelling in <s>Ayodhyā</s>, with women, children, and the weak,
were longing for <s>Rāma</s>'s consecration, longing for the rising of the sun.
The people were eager to see that great festival of <s>Ayodhyā</s>,
which was an ornament to the subjects and increased the joy of the populace.
Thus the purohita (domestic priest), along the royal road crowded with people,

children.text: vyūhann iva janaughaṃ taṃ śanai rājakulaṃ yayau ||
children.translated_text: slowly went to the royal palace, as though parting that flood of people.
Having ascended the palace, resembling a peak of a white cloud,
he met with the king, like <s>Bṛhaspati</s> with <s>Śakra</s>.

children.text: tam āgatam abhiprekṣya hitvā rājāsanaṃ nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing him arrived, the king left his royal seat,

children.text: papraccha sa ca tasmai tat kṛtam ity abhyavedayat ||
children.translated_text: and questioned him; he reported to him that the matter had been done.

children.text: guruṇā tv abhyanujñāto manujaughaṃ visṛjya tam
children.translated_text: Then, permitted by his guru, dismissing that throng of men,
the king entered the inner apartments, like a lion entering a mountain cave.
The royal residence, filled with women in splendid attire and resembling the dwelling of <s>Mahendra</s>,

children.text: vidīpayaṃś cāru viveśa pārthivaḥ śaśīva tārāgaṇasaṃkulaṃ nabhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king entered, making it shine beautifully, like the moon entering the sky filled with hosts of stars.
When the purohita had gone, <s>Rāma</s>, bathed and with disciplined mind,
approached <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> together with his wide-eyed wife.

children.text: pragṛhya śirasā pātrīṃ haviṣo vidhivat tadā
children.translated_text: Then, holding the vessel of oblation on his head according to rule,
he offered the ājya (clarified butter) to the great deity in the blazing fire.

children.text: śeṣaṃ ca haviṣas tasya prāśyāśāsyātmanaḥ priyam
children.translated_text: Having eaten the remainder of that oblation and wished for what was dear to himself,
meditating on the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, on a well-spread bed of kuśa grass,
silent, together with <s>Vaidehī</s>, and with mind restrained,
the prince, best of men, lay down in the splendid shrine of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
When one watch of the night remained, he awoke,
and had the entire procedure of adorning the house performed.
There, listening to the pleasant words of charioteers, bards, and panegyrists,
he attended the morning twilight and recited with controlled mind.
He praised <s>Madhusūdana</s>, bowing with his head,
and, clothed in pure linen, had the twice-born recite.
Then their deep and sweet proclamation of an auspicious day
filled <s>Ayodhyā</s>, echoed by the sound of musical instruments.

children.text: kṛtopavāsaṃ tu tadā vaidehyā saha rāghavam
children.translated_text: Hearing that <s>Rāghava</s> was then observing a fast together with <s>Vaidehī</s>,
all the people living in <s>Ayodhyā</s> rejoiced.
Then all the townspeople, hearing of <s>Rāma</s>'s consecration,

children.text: prabhātāṃ rajanīṃ dṛṣṭvā cakre śobhāṃ parāṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and seeing the night grown light, once more made supreme splendor.
On temples resembling peaks of white clouds,
at crossroads, on streets, at shrines, and on watchtowers,
in merchants' shops rich with many wares,
and in the wealthy, splendid houses of householders,

children.text: sabhāsu caiva sarvāsu vṛkṣeṣv ālakṣiteṣu ca
children.translated_text: in all assembly halls and on trees marked out for the purpose,

children.text: dhvajāḥ samucchritāś citrāḥ patākāś cābhavaṃs tadā ||
children.translated_text: bright banners were raised high, and flags appeared then.
From troops of actors and dancers, and from singers singing,

children.text: manaḥkarṇasukhā vācaḥ śuśruvuś ca tatas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: words pleasant to mind and ear were heard on every side.

children.text: rāmābhiṣekayuktāś ca kathāś cakrur mitho janāḥ
children.translated_text: People spoke with one another of stories connected with <s>Rāma</s>'s consecration,
in the squares and in their houses, when <s>Rāma</s>'s consecration had drawn near.
Even children playing in groups at the doors of houses
spoke with one another only of matters connected with <s>Rāma</s>'s consecration.
The royal road, provided with offerings of flowers and perfumed with incense and fragrance,
was made splendid by the citizens for <s>Rāma</s>'s consecration.
And, to give light because they feared the coming of night,

children.text: dīpavṛkṣāṃs tathā cakrur anu rathyāsu sarvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: they set up tree-like lamps everywhere along the streets.
Having thus adorned the city, the inhabitants of that city,
longing for <s>Rāma</s>'s consecration as yuvarāja (crown prince),

children.text: sametya saṃghaśaḥ sarve catvareṣu sabhāsu ca
children.translated_text: all gathering in groups in the squares and assembly halls,
conversed with one another there and praised the lord of the people.
"Ah, this king is great-souled, the delight of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> line,

children.text: jñātvā yo vṛddham ātmānaṃ rāmaṃ rājye 'bhiṣekṣyati ||
children.translated_text: who, knowing himself to be old, will consecrate <s>Rāma</s> in the kingdom.

children.text: sarve hy anugṛhītāḥ sma yan no rāmo mahīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: We are all favored, since <s>Rāma</s> will be our lord of the earth,
a protector for a long time, one who has seen the near and far of the world.
He has an unarrogant mind, is learned, righteous, and affectionate to his brothers;

children.text: yathā ca bhrātṛṣu snigdhas tathāsmāsv api rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as <s>Rāghava</s> is loving toward his brothers, so he is also toward us.
May the righteous, blameless king <s>Daśaratha</s> live long,
by whose favor we shall see <s>Rāma</s> consecrated.
At that time the citizens were speaking in this way,
and people from the country, having heard the news even from the quarters, arrived.

children.text: te tu digbhyaḥ purīṃ prāptā draṣṭuṃ rāmābhiṣecanam
children.translated_text: Those country people, having come from the quarters to the city to see <s>Rāma</s>'s consecration,
filled <s>Rāma</s>'s city.

children.text: janaughais tair visarpadbhiḥ śuśruve tatra nisvanaḥ
children.translated_text: From those floods of people spreading about there, a sound was heard,
like the roar of the ocean with its tide swollen at the lunar junctures.

children.text: tatas tad indrakṣayasaṃnibhaṃ puraṃ didṛkṣubhir jānapadair upāgataiḥ
children.translated_text: Then that city, resembling the abode of <s>Indra</s>, was approached by country people who had come, desirous of seeing...

children.text: samantataḥ sasvanam ākulaṃ babhau samudrayādobhir ivārṇavodakam ||
children.translated_text: On every side it appeared noisy and crowded, like ocean water filled with sea creatures.

children.text: jñātidāsī yato jātā kaikeyyās tu sahoṣitā
children.translated_text: A maidservant born in her family, who had been living with <s>Kaikeyī</s>,
by chance climbed a palace shining like the moon.
