From that palace <s>Mantharā</s> looked out over all <s>Ayodhyā</s>, whose royal roads had been sprinkled and were strewn with lotuses and blue lotuses,
from that palace <s>Mantharā</s> looked out over <s>Ayodhyā</s>.
It was adorned with excellent banners and flags,
sprinkled with sandal-water and filled with people whose heads had been freshly bathed.

children.text: avidūre sthitāṃ dṛṣṭvā dhātrīṃ papraccha mantharā
children.translated_text: Seeing a nurse standing not far away, <s>Mantharā</s> asked her,
eager for the matter and filled with great joy:

children.text: rāmamātā dhanaṃ kiṃ nu janebhyaḥ samprayacchati
children.translated_text: "Why is <s>Rāma</s>'s mother giving wealth to the people?

children.text: atimātraṃ praharṣo 'yaṃ kiṃ janasya ca śaṃsa me
children.translated_text: Why is there this excessive rejoicing among the people? Tell me,
and what will the delighted king do?"
Then the nurse, bursting with joy and the highest delight,
told the hunchback of <s>Rāghava</s>'s great prosperity:
"Tomorrow, under <s>Puṣya</s>, King <s>Daśaratha</s>
will consecrate the anger-conquering, sinless <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Rāghava</s>, as heir-apparent."

children.text: dhātryās tu vacanaṃ śrutvā kubjā kṣipram amarṣitā
children.translated_text: But when the hunchback heard the nurse's words, she quickly became enraged
and descended from the palace, which resembled a peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>.
Burning with anger, sinful-minded <s>Mantharā</s>

children.text: śayānām etya kaikeyīm idaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: came to <s>Kaikeyī</s> as she lay sleeping and spoke these words:

children.text: uttiṣṭha mūḍhe kiṃ śeṣe bhayaṃ tvām abhivartate
children.translated_text: "Get up, fool! Why are you lying there? Danger is coming upon you.
Why do you not realize that you are being overwhelmed by a mighty flood of disaster?
Though what is harmful has the appearance of good fortune, you boast of your luck;

children.text: calaṃ hi tava saubhāgyaṃ nadyāḥ srota ivoṣṇage ||
children.translated_text: for your good fortune is unstable, like the current of a river in the hot season."

children.text: evam uktā tu kaikeyī ruṣṭayā paruṣaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed harshly by the angry hunchback,
the sinful-minded woman, <s>Kaikeyī</s> fell into deep distress.

children.text: kaikeyī tv abravīt kubjāṃ kaccit kṣemaṃ na manthare
children.translated_text: But <s>Kaikeyī</s> said to the hunchback, "All is well, is it not, <s>Mantharā</s>?
For I see that your face is downcast and that you are deeply pained."

children.text: mantharā tu vacaḥ śrutvā kaikeyyā madhurākṣaram
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Kaikeyī</s>'s sweet-syllabled words,
<s>Mantharā</s>, skilled in speech, replied with words joined to anger.

children.text: sā viṣaṇṇatarā bhūtvā kubjā tasyā hitaiṣiṇī
children.translated_text: Becoming still more despondent, the hunchback, seeking her welfare,
spoke, distressing her and setting her against <s>Rāghava</s>:
"A very great danger has arisen, O queen, one that will destroy you:
King <s>Daśaratha</s> will consecrate <s>Rāma</s> as heir-apparent.
I am sunk in unfathomable fear, filled with sorrow and grief,
and, as if burning with fire, I have come here for your good.

children.text: tava duḥkhena kaikeyi mama duḥkhaṃ mahad bhavet
children.translated_text: Through your sorrow, O <s>Kaikeyī</s>, my sorrow would be great,

children.text: tvadvṛddhau mama vṛddhiś ca bhaved atra na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and in your advancement lies my advancement too; there is no doubt about this.
You were born in a royal family and are the king's chief queen;

children.text: ugratvaṃ rājadharmāṇāṃ kathaṃ devi na budhyase ||
children.translated_text: how, O queen, do you not understand the stern ways of kingship?

children.text: dharmavādī śaṭho bhartā ślakṣṇavādī ca dāruṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Your husband speaks of <s>dharma</s> but is deceitful, smooth-spoken yet cruel;
in your pure-heartedness you do not know that you have been deceived by him in this way.
Using useless conciliation toward you when the moment has arrived,
your husband today will give the real advantage to <s>Kausalyā</s> alone.

children.text: apavāhya sa duṣṭātmā bharataṃ tava bandhuṣu
children.translated_text: Having sent <s>Bharata</s> away among your relatives, that wicked-hearted man
will tomorrow install <s>Rāma</s> in a kingdom with its thorns removed.
An enemy under the name of husband, like a venomous snake in your lap,
has been held by you, foolish girl, as though by a mother wishing his good.

children.text: yathā hi kuryāt sarpo vā śatrur vā pratyupekṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: Just as a snake or an enemy would act if disregarded,

children.text: rājñā daśarathenādya saputrā tvaṃ tathā kṛtā ||
children.translated_text: so King <s>Daśaratha</s> has acted today toward you and your son.
By sinful and false conciliation, O child always accustomed to comfort,

children.text: rāmaṃ sthāpayatā rājye sānubandhā hatā hy asi ||
children.translated_text: you and your dependents have indeed been ruined by his placing <s>Rāma</s> on the throne.

children.text: sā prāptakālaṃ kaikeyi kṣipraṃ kuru hitaṃ tava
children.translated_text: Therefore, O <s>Kaikeyī</s>, now that the proper time has come, quickly do what is good for you.

children.text: trāyasva putram ātmānaṃ māṃ ca vismayadarśane ||
children.translated_text: Save your son, yourself, and me too, O woman of wondrous beauty."

children.text: mantharāyā vacaḥ śrutvā śayanāt sa śubhānanā
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Mantharā</s>'s words, that fair-faced woman from her couch

children.text: evam ābharaṇaṃ tasyai kubjāyai pradadau śubham ||
children.translated_text: gave that hunchback a fine ornament.

children.text: dattvā tv ābharaṇaṃ tasyai kubjāyai pramadottamā
children.translated_text: Having given the ornament to that hunchback, the best of women,

children.text: kaikeyī mantharāṃ hṛṣṭā punar evābravīd idam ||
children.translated_text: the delighted <s>Kaikeyī</s> again said this to <s>Mantharā</s>:

children.text: idaṃ tu manthare mahyam ākhyāsi paramaṃ priyam
children.translated_text: "This, <s>Mantharā</s>, that you have told me is supremely dear to me.

children.text: etan me priyam ākhyātuḥ kiṃ vā bhūyaḥ karomi te ||
children.translated_text: What more shall I do for you, who have told me this dear news?

children.text: rāme vā bharate vāhaṃ viśeṣaṃ nopalakṣaye
children.translated_text: I perceive no difference between <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Bharata</s>;

children.text: tasmāt tuṣṭāsmi yad rājā rāmaṃ rājye 'bhiṣekṣyati ||
children.translated_text: therefore I am pleased that the king will consecrate <s>Rāma</s> in the kingdom.

children.text: na me paraṃ kiṃcid itas tvayā punaḥ priyaṃ priyārhe suvacaṃ vaco varam
children.translated_text: No dearer, more pleasing, excellent word than this has ever been spoken to me by you, O deserving of dear things;

children.text: tathā hy avocas tvam ataḥ priyottaraṃ varaṃ paraṃ te pradadāmi taṃ vṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: for you have spoken something still dearer than that, so I grant you an excellent boon: choose it."

children.text: mantharā tv abhyasūyyainām utsṛjyābharaṇaṃ ca tat
children.translated_text: But <s>Mantharā</s>, indignant at her, threw away that ornament
and then spoke these words, filled with anger and sorrow:

children.text: harṣaṃ kim idam asthāne kṛtavaty asi bāliśe
children.translated_text: "Why have you indulged in this joy at the wrong time, foolish woman?
You do not understand that you stand in the middle of an ocean of grief.
Fortunate indeed is <s>Kausalyā</s>, whose son will be consecrated
tomorrow under <s>Puṣya</s> by the best of twice-born men to the great office of heir-apparent.

children.text: prāptāṃ sumahatīṃ prītiṃ pratītāṃ tāṃ hatadviṣam
children.translated_text: She has attained very great joy, secure and with her enemies struck down;
you will attend upon that <s>Kausalyā</s> like a maidservant, standing with joined palms.

children.text: hṛṣṭāḥ khalu bhaviṣyanti rāmasya paramāḥ striyaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>'s chief wives will surely be delighted,
while your daughters-in-law will be joyless at <s>Bharata</s>'s downfall."

children.text: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā paramaprītāṃ bruvantīṃ mantharāṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Mantharā</s>, who was speaking and was supremely delighted,

children.text: rāmasyaiva guṇān devī kaikeyī praśaśaṃsa ha ||
children.translated_text: Queen <s>Kaikeyī</s> then praised the virtues of <s>Rāma</s> himself.

children.text: dharmajño gurubhir dāntaḥ kṛtajñaḥ satyavāk śuciḥ
children.translated_text: "<s>Rāma</s> knows <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), is restrained by his elders, grateful, truthful in speech, and pure;

children.text: rāmo rājñaḥ suto jyeṣṭho yauvarājyam ato 'rhati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, the king's eldest son, therefore deserves the heir-apparentship.

children.text: bhrātṝn bhṛtyāṃś ca dīrghāyuḥ pitṛvat pālayiṣyati
children.translated_text: Long-lived, he will protect his brothers and servants like a father.
Why, hunchback, do you grieve on hearing of <s>Rāma</s>'s consecration?

children.text: bharataś cāpi rāmasya dhruvaṃ varṣaśatāt param
children.translated_text: And <s>Bharata</s> too, surely after <s>Rāma</s> and after a hundred years,
will obtain the kingdom of his fathers and grandfathers, that bull among men.

children.text: sā tvam abhyudaye prāpte vartamāne ca manthare
children.translated_text: When prosperity has arrived, <s>Mantharā</s>, and is now present,
and when good fortune is still to come, for what reason do you grieve?

children.text: kausalyāto 'tiriktaṃ ca sa tu śuśrūṣate hi mām ||
children.translated_text: For he attends upon me even more than upon <s>Kausalyā</s>."
Hearing <s>Kaikeyī</s>'s words, <s>Mantharā</s>, deeply distressed,

children.text: dīrgham uṣṇaṃ viniḥśvasya kaikeyīm idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: sighed a long, hot sigh and said this to <s>Kaikeyī</s>:
"Seeing no danger, through foolishness you do not understand your own situation,
as you sink in an ocean of suffering spread wide with grief and calamity.

children.text: bhavitā rāghavo rājā rāghavasya ca yaḥ sutaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> will become king, and then whichever son belongs to <s>Rāghava</s>,
while <s>Bharata</s>, O <s>Kaikeyī</s>, will be excluded from the royal line.

children.text: na hi rājñaḥ sutāḥ sarve rājye tiṣṭhanti bhāmini
children.translated_text: For not all the king's sons stand in the kingship, fair lady;
if all were installed, a very great disorder would arise.

children.text: tasmāj jyeṣṭhe hi kaikeyi rājyatantrāṇi pārthivāḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, O <s>Kaikeyī</s>, kings place the reins of rule in the eldest,
even when the others are faultless and virtuous, faultless-limbed one.
That son of yours will be utterly crushed,

children.text: anāthavat sukhebhyaś ca rājavaṃśāc ca vatsale ||
children.translated_text: like one without a protector, cut off from pleasures and from the royal lineage, tender lady.

children.text: sāhaṃ tvadarthe samprāptā tvaṃ tu māṃ nāvabudhyase
children.translated_text: I have come for your sake, but you do not understand me,

children.text: sapatnivṛddhau yā me tvaṃ pradeyaṃ dātum icchasi ||
children.translated_text: you who wish to give me a gift at the rise of your co-wife.

children.text: dhruvaṃ tu bharataṃ rāmaḥ prāpya rājyam akaṇṭakam
children.translated_text: Surely <s>Rāma</s>, after obtaining the kingdom free of rivals, will take <s>Bharata</s>
and have him sent to another country, or even to the next world.

children.text: bāla eva hi mātulyaṃ bharato nāyitas tvayā
children.translated_text: For <s>Bharata</s>, while still a child, was taken by you to his maternal uncle's home;

children.text: saṃnikarṣāc ca sauhārdaṃ jāyate sthāvareṣv api ||
children.translated_text: from nearness affection arises even among immovable things.

children.text: goptā hi rāmaṃ saumitrir lakṣmaṇaṃ cāpi rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Saumitri</s> will protect <s>Rāma</s>, and <s>Rāghava</s> will protect <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>;

children.text: aśvinor iva saubhrātraṃ tayor lokeṣu viśrutam ||
children.translated_text: like that of the <s>Aśvins</s>, the brotherly love of those two is famed in the worlds.

children.text: tasmān na lakṣmaṇe rāmaḥ pāpaṃ kiṃcit kariṣyati
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>Rāma</s> will do no harm at all to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: rāmas tu bharate pāpaṃ kuryād iti na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but <s>Rāma</s> would do harm to <s>Bharata</s>; of this there is no doubt.

children.text: tasmād rājagṛhād eva vanaṃ gacchatu te sutaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore let your son go to the forest straight from <s>Rājagṛha</s>;

children.text: etaddhi rocate mahyaṃ bhṛśaṃ cāpi hitaṃ tava ||
children.translated_text: this pleases me, and it is also greatly beneficial to you.

children.text: evaṃ te jñātipakṣasya śreyaś caiva bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: In this way the welfare of your kinsmen's side too will come about,

children.text: yadi ced bharato dharmāt pitryaṃ rājyam avāpsyati ||
children.translated_text: if <s>Bharata</s> obtains his paternal kingdom by right.

children.text: sa te sukhocito bālo rāmasya sahajo ripuḥ
children.translated_text: That boy of yours, accustomed to happiness, is <s>Rāma</s>'s natural enemy;
with his own prosperity destroyed, how will he live under the control of one whose aims are fulfilled?
Like the lord of an elephant herd attacked in the forest by a lion,
you ought to protect <s>Bharata</s>, who is being overwhelmed by <s>Rāma</s>.
Previously, through pride in your good fortune, you rejected

children.text: rāmamātā sapatnī te kathaṃ vairaṃ na yātayet ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>'s mother, your co-wife; how would she not take revenge?

children.text: yadā hi rāmaḥ pṛthivīm avāpsyati dhruvaṃ pranaṣṭo bharato bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: For when <s>Rāma</s> obtains the earth, <s>Bharata</s> will surely be ruined;

children.text: ato hi saṃcintaya rājyam ātmaje parasya cādyaiva vivāsakāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: therefore think now of the kingdom for your son, and this very day of a cause for the other's banishment."

children.text: evam uktā tu kaikeyī krodhena jvalitānanā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Kaikeyī</s>, her face blazing with anger,

children.text: dīrgham uṣṇaṃ viniḥśvasya mantharām idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: sighed a long, hot sigh and said this to <s>Mantharā</s>:

children.text: adya rāmam itaḥ kṣipraṃ vanaṃ prasthāpayāmy aham
children.translated_text: "Today I shall quickly send <s>Rāma</s> from here to the forest;
I shall quickly consecrate <s>Bharata</s> with the heir-apparentship.

children.text: idaṃ tv idānīṃ saṃpaśya kenopāyena manthare
children.translated_text: But now consider this, <s>Mantharā</s>: by what means

children.text: bharataḥ prāpnuyād rājyaṃ na tu rāmaḥ kathaṃcana ||
children.translated_text: may <s>Bharata</s> obtain the kingdom, and not <s>Rāma</s> under any circumstances?"

children.text: evam uktā tayā devyā mantharā pāpadarśinī
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by that queen, <s>Mantharā</s>, seeing evil,
and injuring <s>Rāma</s>'s interest, said this to <s>Kaikeyī</s>:

children.text: hantedānīṃ pravakṣyāmi kaikeyi śrūyatāṃ ca me
children.translated_text: "Come, now I shall explain, O <s>Kaikeyī</s>; listen to me,

children.text: yathā te bharato rājyaṃ putraḥ prāpsyati kevalam ||
children.translated_text: how your son <s>Bharata</s> alone will obtain the kingdom."

children.text: śrutvaivaṃ vacanaṃ tasyā mantharāyās tu kaikayī
children.translated_text: Hearing this speech of <s>Mantharā</s>,

children.text: kiṃcid utthāya śayanāt svāstīrṇād idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kaikeyī</s> rose a little from her well-spread bed and said this:
"Tell me the means, <s>Mantharā</s>,

children.text: bharataḥ prāpnuyād rājyaṃ na tu rāmaḥ kathaṃcana ||
children.translated_text: by which <s>Bharata</s> may obtain the kingdom, and not <s>Rāma</s> in any way."

children.text: evam uktā tayā devyā mantharā pāpadarśinī
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by that queen, <s>Mantharā</s>, seeing evil,
the hunchback, injuring <s>Rāma</s>'s interest, spoke these words:

children.text: tava devāsure yuddhe saha rājarṣibhiḥ patiḥ
children.translated_text: "In the war between the gods and the asuras, your husband, together with royal seers,
went, taking you along, to aid the king of the gods.

children.text: diśam āsthāya kaikeyi dakṣiṇāṃ daṇḍakān prati
children.translated_text: Taking the southern direction, O <s>Kaikeyī</s>, toward the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> region,

children.text: vaijayantam iti khyātaṃ puraṃ yatra timidhvajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he went to the city known as <s>Vaijayanta</s>, where <s>Timidhvaja</s> was.

children.text: sa śambara iti khyātaḥ śatamāyo mahāsuraḥ
children.translated_text: He, known as <s>Śambara</s>, the great asura of a hundred illusions,
gave battle to <s>Śakra</s>, unconquered by the hosts of gods.

children.text: tasmin mahati saṃgrāme rājā daśarathas tadā
children.translated_text: In that great battle, King <s>Daśaratha</s> then,
having lost consciousness, was drawn away from the battle by you, O queen.

children.text: tatrāpi vikṣataḥ śastraiḥ patis te rakṣitas tvayā
children.translated_text: There too, wounded by weapons, your husband was protected by you;

children.text: tuṣṭena tena dattau te dvau varau śubhadarśane ||
children.translated_text: pleased, he gave you two boons, fair one.

children.text: sa tvayoktaḥ patir devi yadeccheyaṃ tadā varau
children.translated_text: You said to your husband, O queen, 'Whenever I should wish, then those boons

children.text: gṛhṇīyām iti tat tena tathety uktaṃ mahātmanā
children.translated_text: I shall take'; and that high-souled one said to that, 'So be it.'

children.text: anabhijñā hy ahaṃ devi tvayaiva kathitaṃ purā ||
children.translated_text: For I did not know of this, O queen; it was you yourself who told it before."
Ask your husband for those two boons: the consecration of <s>Bharata</s>

children.text: pravrājanaṃ ca rāmasya tvaṃ varṣāṇi caturdaśa ||
children.translated_text: and the banishment of <s>Rāma</s> for fourteen years.
Daughter of <s>Aśvapati</s>, enter the anger chamber today, as though enraged,
and lie on the ground, hidden away, wearing soiled clothes.

children.text: mā smainaṃ pratyudīkṣethā mā cainam abhibhāṣathāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Do not look toward him at all, and do not speak to him.

children.text: dayitā tvaṃ sadā bhartur atra me nāsti saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: You are always dear to your husband; in this I have no doubt.

children.text: tvatkṛte ca mahārājo viśed api hutāśanam ||
children.translated_text: For your sake the great king would even enter the fire.

children.text: na tvāṃ krodhayituṃ śakto na kruddhāṃ pratyudīkṣitum
children.translated_text: He is unable to anger you, or to look at you when you are angry.

children.text: tava priyārthaṃ rājā hi prāṇān api parityajet ||
children.translated_text: For the king would give up even his life for what is dear to you.

children.text: na hy atikramituṃ śaktas tava vākyaṃ mahīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: The lord of the earth is not able to transgress your word.
Woman of foolish nature, recognize the strength of your own good fortune.
Gems, pearls, gold, and various jewels

children.text: dadyād daśaratho rājā mā sma teṣu manaḥ kṛthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Daśaratha</s> may give you; do not set your mind on them.

children.text: yau tau devāsure yuddhe varau daśaratho 'dadāt
children.translated_text: Those two boons that <s>Daśaratha</s> gave in the war between gods and demons,

children.text: tau smāraya mahābhāge so 'rtho mā tvām atikramet ||
children.translated_text: remind him of those, highly fortunate one; let that purpose not pass you by.

children.text: yadā tu te varaṃ dadyāt svayam utthāpya rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: But when the <s>Rāghava</s>, raising you himself, grants you a boon,

children.text: vyavasthāpya mahārājaṃ tvam imaṃ vṛṇuyā varam ||
children.translated_text: after binding the great king by his word, choose this boon:

children.text: rāmaṃ pravrājayāraṇye nava varṣāṇi pañca ca
children.translated_text: "Send <s>Rāma</s> into exile in the forest for nine years and five,
and let <s>Bharata</s> be made king on earth, bull among kings."
And once <s>Rāma</s> has thus been sent away, he will become no delight,

children.text: bharataś ca hatāmitras tava rājā bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Bharata</s>, with enemies destroyed, will become your king.

children.text: yena kālena rāmaś ca vanāt pratyāgamiṣyati
children.translated_text: By the time when <s>Rāma</s> returns from the forest,

children.text: tena kālena putras te kṛtamūlo bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: by that time your son will have taken firm root,
having gathered men around him, self-possessed and together with friends.

children.text: prāptakālaṃ tu te manye rājānaṃ vītasādhvasā
children.translated_text: I think the proper time has come for you, fearless one,
to check the king's intention for <s>Rāma</s>'s consecration and turn it back.

children.text: anartham artharūpeṇa grāhitā sā tatas tayā
children.translated_text: Then she, having been made by her to grasp a calamity in the form of a benefit,

children.text: hṛṣṭā pratītā kaikeyī mantharām idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: delighted and confident, <s>Kaikeyī</s> said this to <s>Mantharā</s>:
"Hunchback, I know no one better than you, who speak what is best.
Among the hunchbacks on earth you are supreme in firmness of judgment.

children.text: tvam eva tu mamārtheṣu nityayuktā hitaiṣiṇī
children.translated_text: You alone are always engaged in my affairs, seeking my welfare.
Hunchback, I would not have understood what the king intended to do.
There are hunchbacks who are ill-formed, crooked, and exceedingly wicked;

children.text: tvaṃ padmam iva vātena saṃnatā priyadarśanā ||
children.translated_text: but you, bent like a lotus by the wind, are lovely to behold.

children.text: uras te 'bhiniviṣṭaṃ vai yāvat skandhāt samunnatam
children.translated_text: Your chest, projecting, is raised up as far as the shoulder,

children.text: adhastāc codaraṃ śāntaṃ sunābham iva lajjitam ||
children.translated_text: and below, your belly is calm, with a beautiful navel, as though bashful.
Your hips are prominent, adorned with a girdle-chain,

children.text: jaṅghe bhṛśam upanyaste pādau cāpy āyatāv ubhau ||
children.translated_text: your thighs are very well set, and both your feet are long.
With those long thighs, <s>Mantharā</s>, clothed in linen,
as you walk before me, you shine like a royal swan.

children.text: tavedaṃ sthagu yad dīrghaṃ rathaghoṇam ivāyatam
children.translated_text: This long hump of yours, extended like a chariot's pole,

children.text: matayaḥ kṣatravidyāś ca māyāś cātra vasanti te ||
children.translated_text: contains your thoughts, kṣatriya science, and stratagems.

children.text: atra te pratimokṣyāmi mālāṃ kubje hiraṇmayīm
children.translated_text: On this I will fasten a golden garland for you, hunchback,

children.text: abhiṣikte ca bharate rāghave ca vanaṃ gate ||
children.translated_text: when <s>Bharata</s> is consecrated and the <s>Rāghava</s> has gone to the forest.
And with native gold, well refined, beautiful one,

children.text: labdhārthā ca pratītā ca lepayiṣyāmi te sthagu ||
children.translated_text: having obtained my purpose and being satisfied, I will plate your hump.

children.text: mukhe ca tilakaṃ citraṃ jātarūpamayaṃ śubham
children.translated_text: And on your face I will have made a variegated, auspicious tilaka of gold,

children.text: kārayiṣyāmi te kubje śubhāny ābharaṇāni ca ||
children.translated_text: and auspicious ornaments for you, hunchback.
Wearing beautiful garments, you will go about like a goddess,
with a face that seems to call the moon, peerless-faced one;
you will move with the finest gait, making hostile people swell with envy.
Other hunchback women too, adorned with every ornament,

children.text: pādau paricariṣyanti yathaiva tvaṃ sadā mama ||
children.translated_text: will attend on your feet, just as you always attend on mine."

children.text: iti praśasyamānā sā kaikeyīm idam abravīt
children.translated_text: Thus being praised, she said this to <s>Kaikeyī</s>,

children.text: śayānāṃ śayane śubhre vedyām agniśikhām iva ||
children.translated_text: who was lying on the fine couch like a flame of fire on the altar:
"When the water has gone, auspicious lady, a bridge-dam is not built.
Rise; do what is beneficial, and show yourself to the king."

children.text: tathā protsāhitā devī gatvā mantharayā saha
children.translated_text: Thus urged, the queen, going with <s>Mantharā</s>,
large-eyed and proud with the intoxication of her good fortune, entered the anger chamber.
The lovely woman took off her pearl necklace worth many hundreds of thousands,
and her fine ornaments worthy of the highest honor.

children.text: tato hemopamā tatra kubjā vākyavaśaṃ gatā
children.translated_text: Then there, goldlike <s>Kaikeyī</s>, brought under the hunchback's word,

children.text: saṃviśya bhūmau kaikeyī mantharām idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: lay down on the ground and said this to <s>Mantharā</s>:

children.text: iha vā māṃ mṛtāṃ kubje nṛpāyāvedayiṣyasi
children.translated_text: "Either here, hunchback, you will report me dead to the king,

children.text: vanaṃ tu rāghave prāpte bharataḥ prāpsyati kṣitim ||
children.translated_text: or, when the <s>Rāghava</s> has gone to the forest, <s>Bharata</s> will obtain the earth."

children.text: athaitad uktvā vacanaṃ sudāruṇaṃ nidhāya sarvābharaṇāni bhāminī
children.translated_text: Then, having spoken this extremely cruel speech, the beautiful woman laid aside all her ornaments,

children.text: asaṃvṛtām āstaraṇena medinīṃ tadādhiśiśye patiteva kiṃnarī ||
children.translated_text: and lay down then on the uncovered earth, without a covering, like a fallen <s>kiṃnarī</s>.
Her face covered by the darkness of rising agitation, and her finest garlands and ornaments cast off,

children.text: narendrapatnī vimanā babhūva sā tamovṛtā dyaur iva magnatārakā ||
children.translated_text: that king's wife became despondent, like the sky covered by darkness with its stars submerged.
But the great king, after ordering <s>Rāghava</s>'s consecration,
entered the inner palace, self-controlled, to tell pleasant news to one deserving of affection.

children.text: tāṃ tatra patitāṃ bhūmau śayānām atathocitām
children.translated_text: There he saw her, fallen on the ground, lying in a way unbefitting her,
and the lord of the world was as if scorched with sorrow.

children.text: sa vṛddhas taruṇīṃ bhāryāṃ prāṇebhyo 'pi garīyasīm
children.translated_text: The old man saw his young wife, dearer even than his life-breaths,
he, sinless, saw her whose intention was sinful, on the floor.

children.text: kareṇum iva digdhena viddhāṃ mṛgayuṇā vane
children.translated_text: Like a female elephant in the forest, pierced by a hunter with a poisoned weapon,
he caressed her out of affection, like a great elephant in the wilderness.
And after stroking her with his hands, his mind greatly alarmed,
the loving man spoke these words to the lotus-petal-eyed woman:

children.text: na te 'ham abhijānāmi krodham ātmani saṃśritam
children.translated_text: "I do not recognize any anger of yours directed against me.
O queen, by whom have you been assailed, or by whom have you been insulted?

children.text: yad idaṃ mama duḥkhāya śeṣe kalyāṇi pāṃsuṣu
children.translated_text: Since, to my sorrow, you lie like this in the dust,

children.text: bhūmau śeṣe kimarthaṃ tvaṃ mayi kalyāṇacetasi
children.translated_text: why do you lie on the ground, fair one, when I am kindly disposed toward you?
You are tormenting my heart, as if your own mind had been struck by spirits.

children.text: santi me kuśalā vaidyā abhituṣṭāś ca sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: I have skilled physicians, fully satisfied in every way;

children.text: sukhitāṃ tvāṃ kariṣyanti vyādhim ācakṣva bhāmini ||
children.translated_text: they will make you well. Tell me the illness, lovely one.

children.text: kasya vā te priyaṃ kāryaṃ kena vā vipriyaṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: Whose pleasure is to be served, or by whom has displeasure been caused to you?

children.text: kaḥ priyaṃ labhatām adya ko vā sumahad apriyam ||
children.translated_text: Who is to receive favor today, or who some very great disfavor?

children.text: avadhyo vadhyatāṃ ko vā vadhyaḥ ko vā vimucyatām
children.translated_text: What man not deserving death is to be killed, or what man deserving death is to be released?

children.text: daridraḥ ko bhavatv āḍhyo dravyavān vāpy akiñcanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What poor man is to become wealthy, or what man of property is to become destitute?

children.text: ahaṃ caiva madīyāś ca sarve tava vaśānugāḥ
children.translated_text: I myself, and all that is mine, are all obedient to your control.

children.text: na te kaṃcid abhiprāyaṃ vyāhantum aham utsahe ||
children.translated_text: I am not able to thwart any intention of yours.
Tell me what you desire in your mind, even at the cost of my own life.

children.text: yāvad āvartate cakraṃ tāvatī me vasuṃdharā ||
children.translated_text: As far as the royal wheel turns, so far extends my earth."

children.text: tathoktā sā samāśvastā vaktukāmā tad apriyam
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, she took courage, wishing to speak that unwelcome thing,
and began again to torment her husband.

children.text: nāsmi viprakṛtā deva kenacin na vimānitā
children.translated_text: "I have not been wronged by anyone, lord, nor have I been insulted.

children.text: abhiprāyas tu me kaścit tam icchāmi tvayā kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: But I have a certain intention, and I wish it to be carried out by you.

children.text: pratijñāṃ pratijānīṣva yadi tvaṃ kartum icchasi
children.translated_text: Make a promise, if you wish to do it;

children.text: atha tad vyāhariṣyāmi yad abhiprārthitaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: then I shall declare what has been requested by me."

children.text: evam uktas tayā rājā priyayā strīvaśaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by his beloved, the king, brought under a woman's power,
the greatly radiant one, spoke to that <s>Kaikeyī</s> with a slight smile:

children.text: avalipte na jānāsi tvattaḥ priyataro mama
children.translated_text: "Proud woman, do you not know? Other than <s>Rāma</s>, tiger among men,

children.text: manujo manujavyāghrād rāmād anyo na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: there is no human being dearer to me than you.

children.text: bhadre hṛdayam apy etad anumṛśyoddharasva me
children.translated_text: Good lady, even after considering this heart of mine, tear it out.

children.text: etat samīkṣya kaikeyi brūhi yat sādhu manyase ||
children.translated_text: Reflecting on this, <s>Kaikeyī</s>, say what you think proper.

children.text: balam ātmani paśyantī na māṃ śaṅkitum arhasi
children.translated_text: Seeing my power within myself, you should not suspect me.

children.text: kariṣyāmi tava prītiṃ sukṛtenāpi te śape ||
children.translated_text: I shall do what pleases you; I swear to you even by my good deed."

children.text: tena vākyena saṃhṛṣṭā tam abhiprāyam ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Delighted by that speech, she declared that intention of her own,
most terrible, like death itself arrived before him:

children.text: yathākrameṇa śapasi varaṃ mama dadāsi ca
children.translated_text: "Since you swear in due order and grant me my boon,
let the thirty-three gods, with <s>Indra</s> at their head, hear this.

children.text: candrādityau nabhaś caiva grahā rātryahanī diśaḥ
children.translated_text: Let the moon and sun, the sky, the planets, night and day, and the quarters,

children.text: jagac ca pṛthivī caiva sagandharvā sarākṣasā ||
children.translated_text: and the world and the earth, together with gandharvas and rākṣasas,
the night-roaming beings, the beings in houses, and the household deities,

children.text: yāni cānyāni bhūtāni jānīyur bhāṣitaṃ tava ||
children.translated_text: and whatever other beings there are, know what you have said.
This truth-keeping, greatly radiant, dharma-knowing, well-composed man

children.text: varaṃ mama dadāty eṣa tan me śṛṇvantu devatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: is granting me a boon. Let the deities hear this from me."
Thus the queen took hold of the great archer and bound him by oath;
then she spoke these further words to the boon-giver, who was deluded by desire:

children.text: varau yau me tvayā deva tadā dattau mahīpate
children.translated_text: "Those two boons which were then given to me by you, lord, king of the earth,

children.text: tau tāvad aham adyaiva vakṣyāmi śṛṇu me vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall now state them both at once; hear my words.
The preparation for <s>Rāghava</s>'s consecration has been arranged;
with this very consecration let my <s>Bharata</s> be consecrated.

children.text: nava pañca ca varṣāṇi daṇḍakāraṇyam āśritaḥ
children.translated_text: For fourteen years, dwelling in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest,
wearing bark, deerskin, and matted hair, let <s>Rāma</s> become an ascetic.
Let <s>Bharata</s> today enjoy the office of <s>yuvarāja</s>, free of obstruction,

children.text: adya caiva hi paśyeyaṃ prayāntaṃ rāghavaṃ vane ||
children.translated_text: and this very day I must see <s>Rāghava</s> setting out for the forest."

children.text: tataḥ śrutvā mahārāja kaikeyyā dāruṇaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, O great king, hearing <s>Kaikeyī</s>'s dreadful words,

children.text: vyathito vilavaś caiva vyāghrīṃ dṛṣṭvā yathā mṛgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he was shaken and powerless, like a deer seeing a tigress.
Sitting on the bare ground, sighing deeply,

children.text: aho dhig iti sāmarṣo vācam uktvā narādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: the lord of men, angry, said, "Ah, shame!"
and again fell into unconsciousness, his mind struck down by grief.

children.text: cireṇa tu nṛpaḥ saṃjñāṃ pratilabhya suduḥkhitaḥ
children.translated_text: After a long time the king regained consciousness, deeply distressed,

children.text: kaikeyīm abravīt kruddhaḥ pradahann iva cakṣuṣā ||
children.translated_text: and angrily spoke to <s>Kaikeyī</s>, as if burning her with his eyes:
"Cruel woman, of evil conduct, destroyer of this family,

children.text: kiṃ kṛtaṃ tava rāmeṇa pāpe pāpaṃ mayāpi vā ||
children.translated_text: what wrong has <s>Rāma</s> done to you, wicked one, or what wrong have even I done?

children.text: sadā te jananītulyāṃ vṛttiṃ vahati rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> always conducts himself toward you as toward his mother.
For what reason are you now intent on bringing harm to that very man?
You were admitted by me into my own house for my own destruction,
unknowingly, princess, like a female snake with sharp poison.
Since the whole living world here sings the praise of <s>Rāma</s>'s virtues,

children.text: aparādhaṃ kam uddiśya tyakṣyāmīṣṭam ahaṃ sutam ||
children.translated_text: on account of what offense shall I abandon my beloved son?

children.text: kausalyāṃ vā sumitrāṃ vā tyajeyam api vā śriyam
children.translated_text: I might abandon <s>Kausalyā</s>, or <s>Sumitrā</s>, or even royal fortune,

children.text: jīvitaṃ vātmano rāmaṃ na tv eva pitṛvatsalam ||
children.translated_text: or my own life, but never <s>Rāma</s>, who is devoted to his father.

children.text: parā bhavati me prītir dṛṣṭvā tanayam agrajam
children.translated_text: My joy becomes supreme when I see my eldest son;

children.text: apaśyatas tu me rāmaṃ naṣṭā bhavati cetanā ||
children.translated_text: but when I do not see <s>Rāma</s>, my consciousness is lost.

children.text: tiṣṭhel loko vinā sūryaṃ sasyaṃ vā salilaṃ vinā
children.translated_text: The world might stand without the sun, or crops without water,

children.text: na tu rāmaṃ vinā dehe tiṣṭhet tu mama jīvitam ||
children.translated_text: but without <s>Rāma</s> my life would not remain in my body.

children.text: tad alaṃ tyajyatām eṣa niścayaḥ pāpaniścaye
children.translated_text: So enough. Let this resolve be abandoned, woman of evil resolve.

children.text: api te caraṇau mūrdhnā spṛśāmy eṣa prasīda me ||
children.translated_text: I even touch your feet with my head. Be gracious to me."

children.text: sa bhūmipālo vilapann anāthavat striyā gṛhīto hṛdaye 'timātrayā
children.translated_text: That ruler of the earth, lamenting like one without a protector, seized in his heart beyond measure by the woman,

children.text: papāta devyāś caraṇau prasāritāv ubhāv asaṃspṛśya yathāturas tathā ||
children.translated_text: Like a sick man, he fell down without touching the queen's two outstretched feet.
The great king, undeserving of that, lay there in a manner wholly unfitting,
like <s>Yayāti</s>, fallen from the world of the gods when his merit was spent.
She whose very form was calamity, whose purpose was already accomplished, fearless though she showed fear,

children.text: punar ākārayāmāsa tam eva varam aṅganā ||
children.translated_text: that woman again called up that very boon.
"You boast, great king, that you are truthful and firm in your vows;

children.text: mama cemaṃ varaṃ kasmād vidhārayitum icchasi ||
children.translated_text: why then do you wish to withhold this boon of mine?

children.text: evam uktas tu kaikeyyā rājā daśarathas tadā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Kaikeyī</s>, King <s>Daśaratha</s> then

children.text: pratyuvāca tataḥ kruddho muhūrtaṃ vihvalann iva ||
children.translated_text: answered her angrily, as if bewildered for a moment:

children.text: mṛte mayi gate rāme vanaṃ manujapuṃgave
children.translated_text: "When I am dead and <s>Rāma</s>, bull among men, has gone to the forest,
alas, ignoble woman, my enemy, <s>Rāma</s> will have been banished to the forest.

children.text: yadi satyaṃ bravīmy etat tad asatyaṃ bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: If I declare this to be true, then it will become false;

children.text: akīrtir atulā loke dhruvaṃ paribhavaś ca me ||
children.translated_text: immeasurable disgrace in the world and humiliation for me are certain."
As he lamented so, with his mind reeling,
the sun went down, and night drew on.
That night, adorned with the disk of the moon, did not shine
for the king, who suffered in this way and lamented through its three watches.
Then the aged King <s>Daśaratha</s>, sighing hotly again and again,
lamented in misery, like one afflicted, his eyes fixed on the sky:
"I do not wish for dawn; I have formed this supplicating añjali.

children.text: athavā gamyatāṃ śīghraṃ nāham icchāmi nirghṛṇām
children.translated_text: Or else go quickly away; I do not wish to see the merciless,

children.text: nṛśaṃsāṃ kaikeyīṃ draṣṭuṃ yatkṛte vyasanaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: cruel <s>Kaikeyī</s>, for whose sake this great calamity has arisen."

children.text: evam uktvā tato rājā kaikeyīṃ saṃyatāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the king, with folded hands toward <s>Kaikeyī</s>,
again tried to appease <s>Kaikeyī</s> and said this:
"O queen, show favor especially to this king, who has lived righteously,

children.text: prasādaḥ kriyatāṃ devi bhadre rājño viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: who is wretched, devoted to you, and whose life is spent, O gracious lady.
Surely this has been uttered by me from an empty heart, fair-hipped one;

children.text: kuru sādhu prasādaṃ me bāle sahṛdayā hy asi ||
children.translated_text: grant me kind favor, young woman, for you are compassionate."
Though the king was pure in feeling, she was evil in feeling; his eyes were copper-red and full of tears.

children.text: śrutvā vicitraṃ karuṇaṃ vilāpaṃ bhartur nṛśaṃsā na cakāra vākyam ||
children.translated_text: Hearing her husband's varied and piteous lament, the cruel woman made no reply.

children.text: tataḥ sa rājā punar eva mūrchitaḥ priyām atuṣṭāṃ pratikūlabhāṣiṇīm
children.translated_text: Then that king fainted once more, seeing his beloved dissatisfied and speaking against him,

children.text: samīkṣya putrasya vivāsanaṃ prati kṣitau visaṃjño nipapāta duḥkhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, distressed at the thought of his son's banishment, he fell senseless on the ground.
The wicked woman saw him, stricken by grief for his son, fallen senseless on the earth,
and, watching that scion of <s>Ikṣvāku</s> writhing there, she said this:

children.text: pāpaṃ kṛtveva kim idaṃ mama saṃśrutya saṃśravam
children.translated_text: "Why, after promising me the promise, do you lie on the ground as if you had committed a sin?

children.text: śeṣe kṣititale sannaḥ sthityāṃ sthātuṃ tvam arhasi ||
children.translated_text: You are sunk down; you ought to stand firm in your resolve.

children.text: āhuḥ satyaṃ hi paramaṃ dharmaṃ dharmavido janāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who know <s>dharma</s> say that truth is the highest <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: satyam āśritya hi mayā tvaṃ ca dharmaṃ pracoditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and relying on truth, I have urged you too toward <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: saṃśrutya śaibyaḥ śyenāya svāṃ tanuṃ jagatīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Having promised himself to the hawk, King <s>Śaibya</s>, lord of the earth,

children.text: pradāya pakṣiṇo rājañ jagāma gatim uttamām ||
children.translated_text: gave his own body to the bird, O king, and went to the highest state.

children.text: tathā hy alarkas tejasvī brāhmaṇe vedapārage
children.translated_text: So too the fiery <s>Alarka</s>, when a Veda-knowing brahmin
begged from him, plucked out his own eyes and gave them without distress.

children.text: saritāṃ tu patiḥ svalpāṃ maryādāṃ satyam anvitaḥ
children.translated_text: The lord of rivers, joined to truth, keeps even a slight boundary;
out of regard for truth, at the proper time he does not overstep his own shore.

children.text: samayaṃ ca mamāryemaṃ yadi tvaṃ na kariṣyasi
children.translated_text: And if you, noble one, do not fulfill this agreement of mine,
then, abandoned before your very eyes, I shall abandon my life.
Thus pressed by fearless <s>Kaikeyī</s>, the king

children.text: nāśakat pāśam unmoktuṃ balir indrakṛtaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: could not loosen the noose, like <s>Bali</s> bound by <s>Indra</s>.
His heart was distraught, and his face became colorless;

children.text: sa dhuryo vai parispandan yugacakrāntaraṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: the bearer of the yoke trembled like a draft animal between the wheels.

children.text: vihvalābhyāṃ ca netrābhyām apaśyann iva bhūmipaḥ
children.translated_text: With eyes confused, the lord of the earth seemed not to see;

children.text: kṛcchrād dhairyeṇa saṃstabhya kaikeyīm idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: with difficulty he steadied himself by firmness and said this to <s>Kaikeyī</s>:

children.text: yas te mantrakṛtaḥ pāṇir agnau pāpe mayā dhṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: "That hand of yours, sinful woman, which I ritually took in the fire with mantras,

children.text: taṃ tyajāmi svajaṃ caiva tava putraṃ saha tvayā ||
children.translated_text: I renounce, along with the son born of you, your son, together with you."
Then <s>Kaikeyī</s>, whose conduct was wicked, again
spoke a harsh speech to the king; she knew how to speak, but was stupefied by anger:

children.text: kim idaṃ bhāṣase rājan vākyaṃ gararujopamam
children.translated_text: "Why do you say this, O king, a speech like the pain of poison?
You ought to have your unwearied son <s>Rāma</s> brought here.

children.text: sthāpya rājye mama sutaṃ kṛtvā rāmaṃ vanecaram
children.translated_text: After installing my son in the kingdom and making <s>Rāma</s> a forest-dweller,

children.text: niḥsapatnāṃ ca māṃ kṛtvā kṛtakṛtyo bhaviṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: and after making me free of rivals, you will have accomplished your task."

children.text: sa nunna iva tīkṣṇeṇa pratodena hayottamaḥ
children.translated_text: Like a noble horse struck by a sharp goad,
the king, repeatedly driven on, said this to <s>Kaikeyī</s>:

children.text: dharmabandhena baddho 'smi naṣṭā ca mama cetanā
children.translated_text: "I am bound by the bond of <s>dharma</s>, and my consciousness is lost;

children.text: jyeṣṭhaṃ putraṃ priyaṃ rāmaṃ draṣṭum icchāmi dhārmikam ||
children.translated_text: I wish to see my eldest, beloved, righteous son <s>Rāma</s>."

children.text: iti rājño vacaḥ śrutvā kaikeyī tadanantaram
children.translated_text: Hearing the king's words, <s>Kaikeyī</s> immediately

children.text: svayam evābravīt sūtaṃ gaccha tvaṃ rāmam ānaya ||
children.translated_text: herself said to the charioteer, "Go; bring <s>Rāma</s>."

children.text: tataḥ sa rājā taṃ sūtaṃ sannaharṣaḥ sutaṃ prati
children.translated_text: Then that noble, righteous king, his joy concerning his son crushed,
looked up at the charioteer with eyes reddened by grief and spoke.

children.text: sumantraḥ karuṇaṃ śrutvā dṛṣṭvā dīnaṃ ca pārthivam
children.translated_text: <s>Sumantra</s>, hearing the piteous words and seeing the king wretched,
with folded hands withdrew a little from that place.

children.text: yadā vaktuṃ svayaṃ dainyān na śaśāka mahīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: When the lord of the earth, from misery, could not speak himself,

children.text: tadā sumantraṃ mantrajñā kaikeyī pratyuvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: then <s>Kaikeyī</s>, skilled in counsel, addressed <s>Sumantra</s>:

children.text: sumantra rāmaṃ drakṣyāmi śīghram ānaya sundaram
children.translated_text: "<s>Sumantra</s>, I wish to see beautiful <s>Rāma</s>; bring him quickly."

children.text: sa manyamānaḥ kalyāṇaṃ hṛdayena nananda ca ||
children.translated_text: Thinking this auspicious, he rejoiced in his heart.
<s>Sumantra</s>, urged on quickly by her, reflected:
"Clearly <s>Rāma</s>, who knows <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), will come here for the sake of the consecration."

children.text: iti sūto matiṃ kṛtvā harṣeṇa mahatā punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having formed this thought, the greatly radiant charioteer again, with great joy,
went out, wishing to see <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: tataḥ purastāt sahasā vinirgato mahīpatīn dvāragatān vilokayan
children.translated_text: Then, suddenly coming out in front and looking at the kings standing at the gate,

children.text: dadarśa paurān vividhān mahādhanān upasthitān dvāram upetya viṣṭhitān ||
children.translated_text: he saw various wealthy townsmen who had come to the gate and were standing there.

children.text: te tu tāṃ rajanīm uṣya brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ
children.translated_text: Those Brahmins, versed in the Veda, after spending that night,
came to the attendance-hall together with the royal priests.

children.text: amātyā balamukhyāś ca mukhyā ye nigamasya ca
children.translated_text: The ministers, the chiefs of the army, and the leading men of the guilds,
all delighted, had assembled for <s>Rāghava</s>'s consecration.
When the spotless sun had risen and the day under <s>Puṣya</s> had arrived,
everything had been prepared by the foremost twice-born men for <s>Rāma</s>'s consecration:
golden water-jars and a well-adorned auspicious seat,
and the seat for <s>Rāma</s>, properly spread with a shining tiger-skin.
Water had been brought from the holy confluence of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and <s>Yamunā</s>,

children.text: yāś cānyāḥ saritaḥ puṇyā hradāḥ kūpāḥ sarāṃsi ca ||
children.translated_text: and from other holy rivers, lakes, wells, and ponds.
From rivers flowing eastward, upward, and crosswise, carefully gathered,

children.text: tābhyaś caivāhṛtaṃ toyaṃ samudrebhyaś ca sarvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: water had likewise been brought from them, and from all the oceans.

children.text: kṣaudraṃ dadhighṛtaṃ lājā darbhāḥ sumanasaḥ payaḥ
children.translated_text: There were honey, curds, ghee, parched grain, darbha grass, flowers, and milk.
Pitchers of gold and silver, together with parched grain and covered with milky branches,
shone adorned with lotuses and blue lotuses, filled with the finest water.
White, jewel-adorned, and resembling moonbeams expanded in brightness,
the excellent yak-tail fan for <s>Rāma</s> stood ready.
A white parasol, like the disk of the moon,
stood ready, radiant and splendid, set before the consecration.

children.text: pāṇḍuraś ca vṛṣaḥ sajjaḥ pāṇḍurāśvaś ca susthitaḥ
children.translated_text: A white bull was ready, and a white horse stood well prepared.

children.text: prasrutaś ca gajaḥ śrīmān aupavāhyaḥ pratīkṣate ||
children.translated_text: A splendid rutting elephant, fit for riding, waited.
Eight auspicious maidens, adorned with every ornament,

children.text: vāditrāṇi ca sarvāṇi bandinaś ca tathāpare ||
children.translated_text: and all the musical instruments, the bards, and others likewise were there.
Just as a consecration should be assembled for the kingdom of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s>,
so they had brought every such kind of material for the consecration of the prince.
Those men, assembled there at the king's command,

children.text: apaśyanto 'bruvan ko nu rājño naḥ prativedayet ||
children.translated_text: not seeing the king, said, "Who now will announce us to the king?

children.text: na paśyāmaś ca rājānam uditaś ca divākaraḥ
children.translated_text: We do not see the king, and the sun has risen.
The consecration of wise <s>Rāma</s> as heir-apparent is ready."
As they were speaking thus among the sovereign kings,

children.text: abravīt tān idaṃ sarvān sumantro rājasatkṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sumantra</s>, honored by the king, said this to them all:

children.text: ayaṃ pṛcchāmi vacanāt sukham āyuṣmatām aham
children.translated_text: "At the word of your long-lived lordships, I shall ask
whether the king has awakened, and the reason for your coming."
Having said this, the knower of ancient lore came to the door of the inner apartments
and praised the <s>Rāghava</s> with blessings endowed with virtue.
"The blessed night has passed; an auspicious day has arrived.
Awake, tiger among kings, and then perform the task.

children.text: brāhmaṇā balamukhyāś ca naigamāś cāgatā nṛpa
children.translated_text: The Brahmins, the chiefs of the army, and the guildsmen have come, O king.
They desire your audience; awake, O <s>Rāghava</s>."

children.text: stuvantaṃ taṃ tadā sūtaṃ sumantraṃ mantrakovidam
children.translated_text: While the charioteer <s>Sumantra</s>, skilled in counsel, was praising him in this way,

children.text: pratibudhya tato rājā idaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: the king then woke and spoke these words:

children.text: na caiva saṃprasupto 'ham ānayed āśu rāghavam
children.translated_text: "I am certainly not asleep. Bring <s>Rāghava</s> quickly."

children.text: iti rājā daśarathaḥ sūtaṃ tatrānvaśāt punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus King <s>Daśaratha</s> again instructed the charioteer there.

children.text: sa rājavacanaṃ śrutvā śirasā pratipūjya tam
children.translated_text: Hearing the king's command and honoring him with bowed head,
he went out from the royal residence, thinking that a great joy was at hand.
Having entered the royal road, adorned with flags and banners,

children.text: sa sūtas tatra śuśrāva rāmādhikaraṇāḥ kathāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the charioteer heard there stories concerning <s>Rāma</s>.
Then <s>Sumantra</s> saw the delightful house of <s>Rāma</s>, shining like <s>Kailāsa</s>,
equal in splendor to the dwelling of <s>Śakra</s>.
It was closed with great doors and adorned with hundreds of balconies,
with golden images at the front and gateways of jewels and coral.
It was like a mass of autumn clouds, blazing, and like a cave of <s>Meru</s>,
adorned with very great strings of excellent garlands.

children.text: sa vājiyuktena rathena sārathir narākulaṃ rājakulaṃ vilokayan
children.translated_text: The charioteer, in a chariot yoked with horses, looked upon the royal compound crowded with people;

children.text: tataḥ samāsādya mahādhanaṃ mahat prahṛṣṭaromā sa babhūva sārathiḥ ||
children.translated_text: then, approaching that great and very wealthy place, the charioteer's hair stood on end.
The charioteer entered, unimpeded, that place resembling mountain peaks and moving clouds, with clusters of great palaces and excellent mansions,

children.text: avāryamāṇaḥ praviveśa sārathiḥ prabhūtaratnaṃ makaro yathārṇavam ||
children.translated_text: rich in abundant jewels, like a makara entering the ocean.
Passing beyond that door of the inner apartments, crowded with people,
the knower of ancient lore then reached a secluded courtyard.
It was occupied by young men bearing spears and bows, with polished earrings,
alert, intent, and deeply devoted.
There he saw old men wearing ocher garments, cane in hand and well adorned,
standing at the doorway, supervisors of the women's quarters, very attentive.
Seeing him coming, they, wishing to do what was dear to <s>Rāma</s>,
quickly reported it to <s>Rāma</s> together with his wife.
Knowing that the charioteer from his father had been announced,
<s>Rāghava</s>, with kindly intent, had him brought inside at that very place.
him, resembling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, seated and well adorned
The charioteer saw him on a golden couch with its upper covering,
anointed with excellent sandalwood, pure and fragrant,
like the blood of a boar, that scorcher of foes.
At his side stood <s>Sītā</s>, holding a yak-tail fan,

children.text: upetaṃ sītayā bhūyaś citrayā śaśinaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: attending him again, like the moon with <s>Citrā</s>.
The disciplined court bard, knowing proper conduct, bowed respectfully
to him, who blazed like the sun and was endowed with his own splendor.
With joined palms, after asking about his well-being in pleasure, recreation, bed, and seat,
<s>Sumantra</s>, honored by the king, said this to the prince:

children.text: kausalyā suprabhā deva pitā tvāṃ draṣṭum icchati
children.translated_text: "O son of <s>Kausalyā</s>, good morning, lord. Your father wishes to see you;

children.text: mahiṣyā saha kaikeyyā gamyatāṃ tatra māciram ||
children.translated_text: go there at once, where he is with Queen <s>Kaikeyī</s>."

children.text: evam uktas tu saṃhṛṣṭo narasiṃho mahādyutiḥ
children.translated_text: When this was said, that lion among men, of great radiance, was delighted.

children.text: tataḥ saṃmānayāmāsa sītām idam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: Then he honored <s>Sītā</s> and spoke these words:

children.text: devi devaś ca devī ca samāgamya madantare
children.translated_text: "Lady, the lord and the queen, meeting in my absence,
are surely discussing something connected with my consecration.
Having discerned his intention, that skillful woman, desiring what is dear to me,
the wine-eyed one, is urging the king on for my sake.

children.text: yādṛśī pariṣat tatra tādṛśo dūta āgataḥ
children.translated_text: As is the council there, so is the messenger who has come.
Surely today itself the king will consecrate me as <s>yuvarāja</s>.

children.text: hanta śīghram ito gatvā drakṣyāmi ca mahīpatim
children.translated_text: Come then, after going quickly from here, I shall see the lord of the earth.

children.text: saha tvaṃ parivāreṇa sukham āssva ramasva ca ||
children.translated_text: You remain happily here with your retinue, and take your ease."
Honored by her husband, dark-eyed <s>Sītā</s>
followed her husband as far as the doorway, meditating on auspicious blessings.

children.text: sa sarvān arthino dṛṣṭvā sametya pratinandya ca
children.translated_text: Seeing all the petitioners, meeting them and greeting them in return,
he then mounted the finest chariot, shining like fire.
It seemed to steal the eyes with its radiance and had a golden brilliance,
and it was yoked with excellent horses like young elephants.
Like thousand-eyed <s>Indra</s> with his bay-horse chariot,

children.text: prayayau tūrṇam āsthāya rāghavo jvalitaḥ śriyā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s>, blazing with majesty, mounted the swift chariot and quickly set out.
Like a thundercloud resounding in the sky,

children.text: niketān niryayau śrīmān mahābhrād iva candramāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the glorious one came out from his dwelling like the moon from a great cloud.
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, <s>Rāghava</s>'s younger brother, held the umbrella and fly-whisk,

children.text: jugopa bhrātaraṃ bhrātā ratham āsthāya pṛṣṭhataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the brother protected his brother from behind, having mounted the chariot.
Then a tumultuous cry arose on every side
from the crowd of people as he was coming out.

children.text: sa rāghavas tatra kathāpralāpaṃ śuśrāva lokasya samāgatasya
children.translated_text: There <s>Rāghava</s> heard the talk and conversation of the assembled people,

children.text: ātmādhikārā vividhāś ca vācaḥ prahṛṣṭarūpasya pure janasya ||
children.translated_text: and the various words, touching their own concerns, of the delighted people of the city:

children.text: eṣa śriyaṃ gacchati rāghavo 'dya rājaprasādād vipulāṅgam iṣyan
children.translated_text: "This <s>Rāghava</s> today goes toward royal fortune, about to attain vast prosperity by the king's favor.

children.text: ete vayaṃ sarvasamṛddhakāmā yeṣām ayaṃ no bhavitā praśāstā
children.translated_text: We are people whose desires are fully fulfilled, since he will be our ruler.

children.text: lābho janasyāsya yad eṣa sarvaṃ prapatsyate rāṣṭram idaṃ cirāya ||
children.translated_text: It is the gain of this people that he will obtain this whole kingdom for a long time."

children.text: sa ghoṣavadbhiś ca hayaiḥ sanāgaiḥ puraḥsaraiḥ svastikasūtamāgadhaiḥ
children.translated_text: With noisy horses and elephants, with auspicious heralds, charioteers, and panegyrists going before him,

children.text: mahīyamānaḥ pravaraiś ca vādakair abhiṣṭuto vaiśravaṇo yathā yayau ||
children.translated_text: honored by the best musicians and praised in song, he went like <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>.
<s>Rāma</s> saw the lovely great road, crowded with female elephants, elephants, chariots, and horses,

children.text: prabhūtaratnaṃ bahupaṇyasaṃcayaṃ dadarśa rāmo ruciraṃ mahāpatham ||
children.translated_text: its crossroads filled with great crowds, rich in jewels and piled with many wares.
Mounted on the chariot, with his friends rejoicing,
glorious <s>Rāma</s> looked upon the city crowded with many kinds of people.
<s>Rāma</s> went along the royal road, adorned with white houses like clouds,
and perfumed through its middle with agarwood incense.
That excellent royal road was beautiful and unobstructed,

children.text: saṃvṛtaṃ vividhaiḥ paṇyair bhakṣyair uccāvacair api ||
children.translated_text: covered with various goods and with foods of high and low kinds.
Hearing many blessings uttered by his friends,

children.text: yathārhaṃ cāpi sampūjya sarvān eva narān yayau ||
children.translated_text: and honoring all people according to their due, he went on.
"Take up today that path practiced by our grandfathers
and likewise by our great-grandfathers; consecrated, protect us.

children.text: yathā sma lālitāḥ pitrā yathā pūrvaiḥ pitāmahaiḥ
children.translated_text: As we were cherished by your father, and as by the grandfathers before him,

children.text: tataḥ sukhataraṃ sarve rāme vatsyāma rājani ||
children.translated_text: so, with <s>Rāma</s> as king, we shall all live still more happily.

children.text: alam adya hi bhuktena paramārthair alaṃ ca naḥ
children.translated_text: Enough for us today of food, and enough of the highest gains,

children.text: yathā paśyāma niryāntaṃ rāmaṃ rājye pratiṣṭhitam ||
children.translated_text: since we see <s>Rāma</s> going forth, established in the kingdom.

children.text: ato hi na priyataraṃ nānyat kiṃcid bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: For there will be nothing dearer than this, nothing else at all,
namely the consecration to kingship of <s>Rāma</s>, whose splendor is immeasurable."

children.text: etāś cānyāś ca suhṛdām udāsīnaḥ kathāḥ śubhāḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing these and other auspicious words of his well-wishers,
words that honored himself, <s>Rāma</s> went along the great road while remaining composed.

children.text: na hi tasmān manaḥ kaścic cakṣuṣī vā narottamāt
children.translated_text: No man could draw his mind or his eyes away
from that best of men, even after <s>Rāghava</s> had passed by.

children.text: sarveṣāṃ sa hi dharmātmā varṇānāṃ kurute dayām
children.translated_text: For that righteous one shows compassion to all the social classes,

children.text: caturṇāṃ hi vayaḥsthānāṃ tena te tam anuvratāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and to the four stages of life; therefore they were devoted to him.
Having reached the royal residence, like the palace of great <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: rājaputraḥ pitur veśma praviveśa śriyā jvalan ||
children.translated_text: the prince entered his father's dwelling, blazing with splendor.
The son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, passing beyond all the courtyards,
sent all the people back and approached the pure inner apartment.

children.text: tataḥ praviṣṭe pitur antikaṃ tadā janaḥ sa sarvo mudito nṛpātmaje
children.translated_text: Then, when the king's son had entered his father's presence, all those people, joyful at the prince,

children.text: pratīkṣate tasya punaḥ sma nirgamaṃ yathodayaṃ candramasaḥ saritpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: waited for his coming out again, as the ocean waits for the rising of the moon.

children.text: sa dadarśāsane rāmo niṣaṇṇaṃ pitaraṃ śubhe
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> saw his father seated on the fair seat,
together with <s>Kaikeyī</s>, wretched, his face dried up.

children.text: sa pituś caraṇau pūrvam abhivādya vinītavat
children.translated_text: First he bowed respectfully at his father's feet,
and then, with full composure, he bowed at <s>Kaikeyī</s>'s feet.
Saying only, "<s>Rāma</s>," his eyes clouded with tears,
the miserable king could neither look at him nor speak to him.

children.text: tad apūrvaṃ narapater dṛṣṭvā rūpaṃ bhayāvaham
children.translated_text: Seeing that unprecedented and fearsome condition of the king,

children.text: rāmo 'pi bhayam āpannaḥ padā spṛṣṭveva pannagam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> too became afraid, as if he had touched a serpent with his foot.
With his senses joyless, seeing that great king wasted by the burning pain of grief,
sighing, distressed, and confused in mind,
like the ocean, garlanded with waves and normally unshakable, becoming agitated,
like the sun eclipsed, like a sage who has spoken falsehood,

children.text: acintyakalpaṃ hi pitus taṃ śokam upadhārayan
children.translated_text: as he perceived that inconceivable grief of his father,
he became still more agitated, like the ocean at the full-moon tide.

children.text: cintayāmāsa ca tadā rāmaḥ pitṛhite rataḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s>, intent on his father's welfare, thought:

children.text: kiṃsvid adyaiva nṛpatir na māṃ pratyabhinandati ||
children.translated_text: "Why does the king not greet me today as before?

children.text: anyadā māṃ pitā dṛṣṭvā kupito 'pi prasīdati
children.translated_text: At other times, when my father sees me, even if angry, he becomes pleased.

children.text: tasya mām adya samprekṣya kimāyāsaḥ pravartate ||
children.translated_text: Why, on seeing me today, does distress arise in him?"
Then <s>Rāma</s>, as if humbled and afflicted with grief, the radiance of his face downcast,
after bowing to <s>Kaikeyī</s>, spoke these words:

children.text: kaccin mayā nāparādham ajñānād yena me pitā
children.translated_text: "Surely I have not committed some offense unknowingly, because of which my father

children.text: kupitas tan mamācakṣva tvaṃ caivainaṃ prasādaya ||
children.translated_text: is angry. Tell me that, and you yourself pacify him.

children.text: vivarṇavadano dīno na hi mām abhibhāṣate
children.translated_text: With his face discolored and miserable, he does not speak to me.

children.text: śārīro mānaso vāpi kaccid enaṃ na bādhate
children.translated_text: Surely no bodily or mental suffering is afflicting him?

children.text: saṃtāpo vābhitāpo vā durlabhaṃ hi sadā sukham ||
children.translated_text: Or is there some burning pain or fever? Happiness is indeed always hard to obtain.

children.text: kaccin na kiṃcid bharate kumāre priyadarśane
children.translated_text: Surely there is no misfortune concerning prince <s>Bharata</s>, dear to behold,

children.text: śatrughne vā mahāsattve mātṝṇāṃ vā mamāśubham ||
children.translated_text: or concerning mighty <s>Śatrughna</s>, or concerning my mothers?

children.text: atoṣayan mahārājam akurvan vā pitur vacaḥ
children.translated_text: If I were displeasing the great king or failing to do my father's command,

children.text: muhūrtam api neccheyaṃ jīvituṃ kupite nṛpe ||
children.translated_text: I would not wish to live even for a moment while the king was angry.
The person from whom a man sees the source of his own coming into being here,

children.text: kathaṃ tasmin na varteta pratyakṣe sati daivate ||
children.translated_text: how could he fail to act toward him as toward a manifest deity?

children.text: kaccit te paruṣaṃ kiṃcid abhimānāt pitā mama
children.translated_text: Surely my father has not, out of pride, said something harsh to you,

children.text: ukto bhavatyā kopena yatrāsya lulitaṃ manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or been addressed by you in anger, so that his mind has become disordered?

children.text: etad ācakṣva me devi tattvena paripṛcchataḥ
children.translated_text: Tell me this, O queen, truly, as I ask you:
What is the cause of this unprecedented change in the lord of men?

children.text: ahaṃ hi vacanād rājñaḥ pateyam api pāvake
children.translated_text: At the king's command I would even fall into fire,

children.text: bhakṣayeyaṃ viṣaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ majjeyam api cārṇave
children.translated_text: eat sharp poison, or plunge into the ocean,

children.text: niyukto guruṇā pitrā nṛpeṇa ca hitena ca ||
children.translated_text: if ordered by my elder, my father, the king, who wishes my good.

children.text: tad brūhi vacanaṃ devi rājño yad abhikāṅkṣitam
children.translated_text: Therefore tell me, O queen, the word desired by the king.

children.text: kariṣye pratijāne ca rāmo dvir nābhibhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: I shall do it, and I promise: <s>Rāma</s> does not speak twice."
To him, who was endowed with straightforwardness and spoke the truth, that ignoble woman
<s>Kaikeyī</s> spoke words exceedingly cruel:

children.text: purā devāsure yuddhe pitrā te mama rāghava
children.translated_text: "Long ago, in the battle between gods and asuras, O <s>Rāghava</s>, by your father,
whom I protected in the great battle when he was wounded, two boons were granted to me.
There I have asked the king for <s>Bharata</s>'s consecration,
and for your going to the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest this very day, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: yadi satyapratijñaṃ tvaṃ pitaraṃ kartum icchasi
children.translated_text: If you wish to make your father true to his promise,

children.text: ātmānaṃ ca naraśreṣṭha mama vākyam idaṃ śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: and yourself too, best of men, listen to this word of mine.

children.text: sa nideśe pitus tiṣṭha yathā tena pratiśrutam
children.translated_text: Stand under your father's command, just as he promised.

children.text: tvayāraṇyaṃ praveṣṭavyaṃ nava varṣāṇi pañca ca ||
children.translated_text: You must enter the forest for nine years and five.

children.text: sapta sapta ca varṣāṇi daṇḍakāraṇyam āśritaḥ
children.translated_text: For seven and seven years, dwelling in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest,
abandon this consecration and live wearing matted hair and bark garments.
Let <s>Bharata</s> rule this earth in the city of <s>Kosala</s>,
filled with many jewels and furnished with horses, chariots, and elephants."
Hearing that unwelcome word, like death itself, O slayer of foes,

children.text: śrutvā na vivyathe rāmaḥ kaikeyīṃ cedam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> was not disturbed, and he said this to <s>Kaikeyī</s>:

children.text: evam astu gamiṣyāmi vanaṃ vastum ahaṃ tv ataḥ
children.translated_text: "So be it. I shall go from here to dwell in the forest,
wearing matted hair and bark garments, upholding the king's promise.

children.text: idaṃ tu jñātum icchāmi kimarthaṃ māṃ mahīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: But I wish to know this: for what reason does the formidable king,
subduer of enemies, not greet me as before?

children.text: manyur na ca tvayā kāryo devi brūhi tavāgrataḥ
children.translated_text: You should not be angry, O queen. Speak in my presence.
I shall go to the forest wearing bark and matted hair; be well pleased.

children.text: hitena guruṇā pitrā kṛtajñena nṛpeṇa ca
children.translated_text: When ordered by a beneficent elder, a grateful father, and a king,

children.text: niyujyamāno viśrabdhaṃ kiṃ na kuryād ahaṃ priyam ||
children.translated_text: what beloved thing would I not confidently do?

children.text: alīkaṃ mānasaṃ tv ekaṃ hṛdayaṃ dahatīva me
children.translated_text: Yet one false thought burns my heart, as it were:

children.text: svayaṃ yan nāha māṃ rājā bharatasyābhiṣecanam ||
children.translated_text: that the king himself does not tell me of <s>Bharata</s>'s consecration.

children.text: ahaṃ hi sītāṃ rājyaṃ ca prāṇān iṣṭān dhanāni ca
children.translated_text: For I myself, delighted and unbidden, would give <s>Sītā</s>, the kingdom,
my dear life, and my wealth to my brother <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: kiṃ punar manujendreṇa svayaṃ pitrā pracoditaḥ
children.translated_text: How much more when I have been urged by the lord of men himself, my father,
and am upholding his promise for the sake of what is dear to you?

children.text: tad āśvāsaya hīmaṃ tvaṃ kiṃ nv idaṃ yan mahīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore reassure him. Why is it that the king,
his eyes fixed on the ground, slowly sheds tears?
And let messengers go today, on the king's command, with swift horses
to bring <s>Bharata</s> from his maternal relatives' house.
As for me, I am going from here at once to the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest,
without questioning my father's word, to dwell there for fourteen years."

children.text: sā hṛṣṭā tasya tadvākyaṃ śrutvā rāmasya kaikeyī
children.translated_text: Hearing that word of <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Kaikeyī</s> was delighted.
For, convinced of his departure, she hastened <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: evaṃ bhavatu yāsyanti dūtāḥ śīghrajavair hayaiḥ
children.translated_text: "So be it. Messengers, men with swift horses, will go
to bring <s>Bharata</s> back from his maternal relatives.

children.text: tava tv ahaṃ kṣamaṃ manye notsukasya vilambanam
children.translated_text: But I do not think delay is fitting for you, who are eager;

children.text: rāma tasmād itaḥ śīghraṃ vanaṃ tvaṃ gantum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: therefore, <s>Rāma</s>, you should go quickly from here to the forest.

children.text: vrīḍānvitaḥ svayaṃ yac ca nṛpas tvāṃ nābhibhāṣate
children.translated_text: And because the king, overcome with shame, does not speak to you himself,
that is nothing, best of men; let this resentment be put away.

children.text: yāvat tvaṃ na vanaṃ yātaḥ purād asmād abhitvaran
children.translated_text: Until you have gone to the forest, hastening from this city,

children.text: pitā tāvan na te rāma snāsyate bhokṣyate 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: your father, <s>Rāma</s>, will neither bathe nor even eat."

children.text: dhik kaṣṭam iti niḥśvasya rājā śokapariplutaḥ
children.translated_text: Sighing, "Alas, how painful!" the king, overwhelmed with grief,
fainted and fell upon that couch adorned with gold.
<s>Rāma</s> too, urged on by <s>Kaikeyī</s>, raised the king up,
and, like a horse struck by a whip, made haste to go to the forest.
Hearing that hateful speech of the ignoble woman, harsh at its core,

children.text: śrutvā gatavyatho rāmaḥ kaikeyīṃ vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, with distress gone, spoke these words to <s>Kaikeyī</s>:

children.text: nāham arthaparo devi lokam āvastum utsahe
children.translated_text: "I am not intent on wealth, O queen, nor do I desire to dwell in the world for its sake.

children.text: viddhi mām ṛṣibhis tulyaṃ kevalaṃ dharmam āsthitam ||
children.translated_text: Know me to be like the seers, devoted solely to <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: yad atrabhavataḥ kiṃcic chakyaṃ kartuṃ priyaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: Whatever pleasing thing can be done by me for his majesty,

children.text: prāṇān api parityajya sarvathā kṛtam eva tat ||
children.translated_text: even by abandoning my life, that has in every way already been done.

children.text: na hy ato dharmacaraṇaṃ kiṃcid asti mahattaram
children.translated_text: For there is no greater practice of <s>dharma</s> than this:

children.text: yathā pitari śuśrūṣā tasya vā vacanakriyā ||
children.translated_text: service to one's father, or the carrying out of his word.
Even though his majesty has not directly commanded me, at your word
I shall dwell here in the lonely forest for fourteen years.

children.text: na nūnaṃ mayi kaikeyi kiṃcid āśaṃsase guṇam
children.translated_text: Surely, <s>Kaikeyī</s>, you expect no virtue at all in me,

children.text: yad rājānam avocas tvaṃ mameśvaratarā satī ||
children.translated_text: since you spoke to the king, though you yourself have greater authority over me.

children.text: yāvan mātaram āpṛcche sītāṃ cānunayāmy aham
children.translated_text: Let me ask leave of my mother and persuade <s>Sītā</s>;
then today itself I shall go to the great forest of the <s>Daṇḍakas</s>.

children.text: bharataḥ pālayed rājyaṃ śuśrūṣec ca pitur yathā
children.translated_text: You must see that <s>Bharata</s> rules the kingdom and serves his father

children.text: tathā bhavatyā kartavyaṃ sa hi dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in the proper way, for that is the eternal <s>dharma</s>."

children.text: sa rāmasya vacaḥ śrutvā bhṛśaṃ duḥkhahataḥ pitā
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Rāma</s>'s words, his father, deeply struck by sorrow,
unable because of grief to restrain his tears, cried out loudly.

children.text: vanditvā caraṇau rāmo visaṃjñasya pitus tadā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s>, after bowing to the feet of his unconscious father,
and also to those of the ignoble <s>Kaikeyī</s>, went out, radiant with great splendor.

children.text: sa rāmaḥ pitaraṃ kṛtvā kaikeyīṃ ca pradakṣiṇam
children.translated_text: Having circumambulated his father and <s>Kaikeyī</s>,
<s>Rāma</s> left that inner chamber and saw his circle of friends.
Behind him followed <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, his eyes filled with tears,
extremely angry, the increaser of <s>Sumitrā</s>'s joy.
<s>Rāma</s> circumambulated the vessels prepared for the consecration
and went slowly, lingering there, not shifting his gaze from them.
The loss of the kingdom did not diminish his great splendor,
just as night does not diminish the loveliness of the cool-rayed moon.

children.text: na vanaṃ gantukāmasya tyajataś ca vasuṃdharām
children.translated_text: Though he wished to go to the forest and was abandoning the earth,
no alteration of mind was seen in him, as though he had passed beyond all worlds.

children.text: dhārayan manasā duḥkham indriyāṇi nigṛhya ca
children.translated_text: Bearing sorrow in his mind and restraining his senses,
self-possessed, he entered his mother's house to announce unwelcome news.

children.text: praviśya veśmātibhṛśaṃ mudānvitaṃ samīkṣya tāṃ cārthavipattim āgatām
children.translated_text: Entering the house, which was exceedingly full of joy, and seeing the ruin of that purpose now come about,

children.text: na caiva rāmo 'tra jagāma vikriyāṃ suhṛjjanasyātmavipattiśaṅkayā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> still underwent no change there, lest his friends suspect his own misfortune.

children.text: rāmas tu bhṛśam āyasto niḥśvasann iva kuñjaraḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Rāma</s>, greatly distressed and sighing like an elephant,

children.text: jagāma sahito bhrātrā mātur antaḥpuraṃ vaśī ||
children.translated_text: went, self-controlled and accompanied by his brother, to his mother's inner apartments.
There he saw an old man, highly honored,
seated at the doorway of the house, and many others standing nearby.

children.text: praviśya prathamāṃ kakṣyāṃ dvitīyāyāṃ dadarśa saḥ
children.translated_text: Entering the first chamber, he saw in the second
elderly Brahmins, learned in the Veda and honored by the king.

children.text: praṇamya rāmas tān vṛddhāṃs tṛtīyāyāṃ dadarśa saḥ
children.translated_text: After bowing to those elders, in the third chamber he saw

children.text: striyo vṛddhāś ca bālāś ca dvārarakṣaṇatatparāḥ ||
children.translated_text: old women and young girls intent on guarding the door.

children.text: vardhayitvā prahṛṣṭās tāḥ praviśya ca gṛhaṃ striyaḥ
children.translated_text: Those joyful women blessed him, then entered the house
and quickly announced that welcome news to <s>Rāma</s>'s mother.

children.text: kausalyāpi tadā devī rātriṃ sthitvā samāhitā
children.translated_text: Queen <s>Kausalyā</s> also, having spent the night collected in mind,

children.text: prabhāte tv akarot pūjāṃ viṣṇoḥ putrahitaiṣiṇī ||
children.translated_text: performed worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the morning, seeking her son's welfare.
Clad in linen, joyful, always devoted to vows,

children.text: agniṃ juhoti sma tadā mantravat kṛtamaṅgalā ||
children.translated_text: and having performed auspicious rites, she then offered into the fire with mantras.

children.text: praviśya ca tadā rāmo mātur antaḥpuraṃ śubham
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s> entered his mother's auspicious inner apartment
and saw his mother there offering oblations to the fire.
Seeing her son, the delight of his mother, arrived after so long,
she came toward him rejoicing, like a mare toward her young foal.

children.text: tam uvāca durādharṣaṃ rāghavaṃ sutam ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kausalyā</s>, out of motherly affection, spoke this dear and beneficial word
to her own son, the unassailable <s>Rāghava</s>:
"May you obtain the lifespan, fame, and <s>dharma</s>

children.text: prāpnuhy āyuś ca kīrtiṃ ca dharmaṃ copahitaṃ kule ||
children.translated_text: established in the family of aged, righteous, great-souled royal seers.
Go see your father, <s>Rāghava</s>, the king true to his promise;
for today that righteous man will consecrate you as heir-apparent."
<s>Rāghava</s> addressed his mother with folded hands slightly extended,

children.text: sa svabhāvavinītaś ca gauravāc ca tadānataḥ ||
children.translated_text: naturally humble and then bowed down out of reverence:

children.text: devi nūnaṃ na jānīṣe mahad bhayam upasthitam
children.translated_text: "O queen, surely you do not know that a great danger has arisen."

children.text: idaṃ tava ca duḥkhāya vaidehyā lakṣmaṇasya ca ||
children.translated_text: This will bring sorrow to you, to <s>Vaidehī</s>, and to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: caturdaśa hi varṣāṇi vatsyāmi vijane vane
children.translated_text: For fourteen years I shall dwell in the solitary forest,
living on honey, roots, and fruits, having given up meat like a sage.
The great king is granting the heir-apparency to <s>Bharata</s>;
but he is banishing me to <s>Daṇḍakāraṇya</s> as an ascetic.

children.text: tām aduḥkhocitāṃ dṛṣṭvā patitāṃ kadalīm iva
children.translated_text: Seeing her, unaccustomed to sorrow, fallen like a plantain tree,
<s>Rāma</s> raised up his mother, whose senses had left her.
