As she turned over and rose, miserable, like a mare beaten down,
her whole body covered with dust, he wiped her with his hand.
She, afflicted by unhappiness though accustomed to happiness, while <s>Rāghava</s> sat near her,
spoke to the tiger among men, with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> listening.

children.text: yadi putra na jāyethā mama śokāya rāghava
children.translated_text: If, my son <s>Rāghava</s>, you had not been born for my grief,

children.text: na sma duḥkham ato bhūyaḥ paśyeyam aham aprajā ||
children.translated_text: then, childless, I would not have seen a sorrow greater than this.

children.text: eka eva hi vandhyāyāḥ śoko bhavati mānavaḥ
children.translated_text: For a barren woman has only one grief, O man:

children.text: aprajāsmīti saṃtāpo na hy anyaḥ putra vidyate ||
children.translated_text: the torment, "I have no child"; no other exists, my son.

children.text: na dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ kalyāṇaṃ sukhaṃ vā patipauruṣe
children.translated_text: I have never before seen good fortune or happiness through my husband's power;

children.text: api putre vipaśyeyam iti rāmāsthitaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: thinking, "Perhaps I shall see it in my son," I placed my hope in <s>Rāma</s>.
I shall hear many unpleasant words that pierce the heart,

children.text: ahaṃ śroṣye sapatnīnām avarāṇāṃ varā satī
children.translated_text: from co-wives inferior to me, though I am the best of them;

children.text: ato duḥkhataraṃ kiṃ nu pramadānāṃ bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: what indeed could be more painful than this for women?

children.text: tvayi saṃnihite 'py evam aham āsaṃ nirākṛtā
children.translated_text: Even when you were present, I was thus disregarded;

children.text: kiṃ punaḥ proṣite tāta dhruvaṃ maraṇam eva me ||
children.translated_text: how much more when you are away, dear one; death alone is certain for me.

children.text: yo hi māṃ sevate kaścid atha vāpy anuvartate
children.translated_text: Whoever serves me, or whoever follows my wishes,

children.text: kaikeyyāḥ putram anvīkṣya sa jano nābhibhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: looking to <s>Kaikeyī</s>'s son, that person will not even speak to me.

children.text: daśa sapta ca varṣāṇi tava jātasya rāghava
children.translated_text: Seventeen years have passed since you were born, O <s>Rāghava</s>,
while I longed for the end of my sorrow.

children.text: upavāsaiś ca yogaiś ca bahubhiś ca pariśramaiḥ
children.translated_text: With fasts, disciplines, and many labors,

children.text: duḥkhaṃ saṃvardhito moghaṃ tvaṃ hi durgatayā mayā ||
children.translated_text: you were raised painfully and in vain by me, unfortunate as I am.

children.text: sthiraṃ tu hṛdayaṃ manye mamedaṃ yan na dīryate
children.translated_text: But I think this heart of mine is firm, since it does not split,
like the bank of a great river in the rainy season, struck by fresh water.

children.text: mamaiva nūnaṃ maraṇaṃ na vidyate na cāvakāśo 'sti yamakṣaye mama
children.translated_text: Surely death does not exist for me, and there is no place for me in <s>Yama</s>'s realm,

children.text: yad antako 'dyaiva na māṃ jihīrṣati prasahya siṃho rudatīṃ mṛgīm iva ||
children.translated_text: since the ender does not wish to seize me today by force, like a lion seizing a crying doe.

children.text: sthiraṃ hi nūnaṃ hṛdayaṃ mamāyasaṃ na bhidyate yad bhuvi nāvadīryate
children.translated_text: Surely my heart is firm and made of iron, since it neither breaks nor splits open on the ground,

children.text: anena duḥkhena ca deham arpitaṃ dhruvaṃ hy akāle maraṇaṃ na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: though my body has been consigned to this pain; indeed, untimely death surely does not exist.

children.text: idaṃ tu duḥkhaṃ yad anarthakāni me vratāni dānāni ca saṃyamāś ca hi
children.translated_text: But this is my sorrow: my vows, gifts, and restraints

children.text: tapaś ca taptaṃ yad apatyakāraṇāt suniṣphalaṃ bījam ivoptam ūṣare ||
children.translated_text: and the austerity practiced for the sake of a child are fruitless, like good seed sown in saline soil.

children.text: yadi hy akāle maraṇaṃ svayecchayā labheta kaścid guruduḥkhakarśitaḥ
children.translated_text: For if someone worn down by heavy sorrow could obtain death at will before his time,

children.text: gatāham adyaiva paretasaṃsadaṃ vinā tvayā dhenur ivātmajena vai ||
children.translated_text: I would go today to the assembly of the departed, without you, like a cow without her calf.

children.text: bhṛśam asukham amarṣitā tadā bahu vilalāpa samīkṣya rāghavam
children.translated_text: Then, exceedingly unhappy and unable to bear it, gazing at <s>Rāghava</s>, she lamented much,

children.text: vyasanam upaniśāmya sā mahat sutam iva baddham avekṣya kiṃnarī ||
children.translated_text: having perceived the great calamity, like a <s>kiṃnarī</s> seeing her son bound.

children.text: tathā tu vilapantīṃ tāṃ kausalyāṃ rāmamātaram
children.translated_text: To her, <s>Kausalyā</s>, the mother of <s>Rāma</s>, lamenting thus,

children.text: uvāca lakṣmaṇo dīnas tat kālasadṛśaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, distressed, spoke words suited to that moment.

children.text: na rocate mamāpy etad ārye yad rāghavo vanam
children.translated_text: I too do not approve this, noble lady: that <s>Rāghava</s> should go to the forest,

children.text: tyaktvā rājyaśriyaṃ gacchet striyā vākyavaśaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: abandoning the royal fortune, having come under the sway of a woman's words.

children.text: viparītaś ca vṛddhaś ca viṣayaiś ca pradharṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: Perverse, old, and overwhelmed by sense objects,

children.text: nṛpaḥ kim iva na brūyāc codyamānaḥ samanmathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: what would the king not say when driven on by passion?
I see no offense of his, nor any fault of such a kind,
by which <s>Rāghava</s> should be banished from the kingdom to live in the forest.

children.text: na taṃ paśyāmy ahaṃ loke parokṣam api yo naraḥ
children.translated_text: I do not see anywhere in the world a man, even one speaking behind his back,
who, though an enemy and though rejected, would declare a fault of his.

children.text: devakalpam ṛjuṃ dāntaṃ ripūṇām api vatsalam
children.translated_text: Godlike, upright, self-controlled, affectionate even toward enemies,

children.text: avekṣamāṇaḥ ko dharmaṃ tyajet putram akāraṇāt ||
children.translated_text: who, considering <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty), would abandon such a son without cause?

children.text: tad idaṃ vacanaṃ rājñaḥ punar bālyam upeyuṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore what son would take to heart this word of the king, who has returned to childishness,

children.text: putraḥ ko hṛdaye kuryād rājavṛttam anusmaran ||
children.translated_text: while remembering the conduct of kings?

children.text: yāvad eva na jānāti kaścid artham imaṃ naraḥ
children.translated_text: As long as no man knows this matter,

children.text: tāvad eva mayā sārdham ātmasthaṃ kuru śāsanam ||
children.translated_text: so long, together with me, make the royal command your own.

children.text: mayā pārśve sadhanuṣā tava guptasya rāghava
children.translated_text: With me at your side, armed with a bow, while you are protected, O <s>Rāghava</s>,
who is able to do anything more, when you stand like Fate itself?
This whole <s>Ayodhyā</s>, bull among men, I will make devoid of men

children.text: kariṣyāmi śarais tīkṣṇair yadi sthāsyati vipriye ||
children.translated_text: with sharp arrows, if it stands against your wish.

children.text: bharatasyātha pakṣyo vā yo vāsya hitam icchati
children.translated_text: And whoever is on <s>Bharata</s>'s side, or whoever wishes his welfare,

children.text: sarvān etān vadhiṣyāmi mṛdur hi paribhūyate ||
children.translated_text: all these I shall kill; for the gentle man is despised.

children.text: tvayā caiva mayā caiva kṛtvā vairam anuttamam
children.translated_text: Once you and I have made unsurpassed enmity,
who has the power to give sovereignty to <s>Bharata</s>, chastiser of foes?
O queen, I am by nature truly devoted to my brother;

children.text: satyena dhanuṣā caiva datteneṣṭena te śape ||
children.translated_text: by truth, by my bow, and by the gifts and sacrifices I have made, I swear to you.

children.text: dīptam agnim araṇyaṃ vā yadi rāmaḥ pravekṣyate
children.translated_text: If <s>Rāma</s> enters a blazing fire or the forest,

children.text: praviṣṭaṃ tatra māṃ devi tvaṃ pūrvam avadhāraya ||
children.translated_text: know, O queen, that I have entered there before him.

children.text: harāmi vīryād duḥkhaṃ te tamaḥ sūrya ivoditaḥ
children.translated_text: I shall remove your sorrow by my valor, as the risen sun removes darkness;

children.text: devī paśyatu me vīryaṃ rāghavaś caiva paśyatu ||
children.translated_text: let the queen see my valor, and let <s>Rāghava</s> himself see it.

children.text: etat tu vacanaṃ śrutvā lakṣmaṇasya mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: But having heard this speech of great-souled <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
<s>Kausalyā</s>, weeping and longing in grief, spoke to <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: bhrātus te vadataḥ putra lakṣmaṇasya śrutaṃ tvayā
children.translated_text: My son, you have heard your brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> speaking.

children.text: yad atrānantaraṃ tat tvaṃ kuruṣva yadi rocate ||
children.translated_text: What comes next here, do that, if it pleases you.

children.text: na cādharmyaṃ vacaḥ śrutvā sapatnyā mama bhāṣitam
children.translated_text: And, having heard the unrighteous word spoken by my co-wife,

children.text: vihāya śokasaṃtaptāṃ gantum arhasi mām itaḥ ||
children.translated_text: you should not leave me, scorched by grief, and go away from here.

children.text: dharmajña yadi dharmiṣṭho dharmaṃ caritum icchasi
children.translated_text: Knower of <s>dharma</s>, if you are most righteous and wish to practice <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: śuśrūṣa mām ihasthas tvaṃ cara dharmam anuttamam ||
children.translated_text: serve me while remaining here; practice the unsurpassed <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: śuśrūṣur jananīṃ putra svagṛhe niyato vasan
children.translated_text: My son, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, obediently serving his mother while dwelling restrained in his own house,

children.text: pareṇa tapasā yuktaḥ kāśyapas tridivaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: attained heaven, endowed with the highest austerity.

children.text: yathaiva rājā pūjyas te gauraveṇa tathā hy aham
children.translated_text: Just as the king is to be revered by you with honor, so indeed am I.

children.text: tvāṃ nāham anujānāmi na gantavyam ito vanam ||
children.translated_text: I do not give you leave; you must not go from here to the forest.

children.text: tvadviyogān na me kāryaṃ jīvitena sukhena vā
children.translated_text: Because of separation from you, I have no use for life or happiness.

children.text: tvayā saha mama śreyas tṛṇānām api bhakṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Better for me is even eating grass together with you.

children.text: yadi tvaṃ yāsyasi vanaṃ tyaktvā māṃ śokalālasām
children.translated_text: If you go to the forest, abandoning me when I am longing in grief,

children.text: ahaṃ prāyam ihāsiṣye na hi śakṣyāmi jīvitum ||
children.translated_text: I shall sit here fasting to death, for I shall not be able to live.

children.text: tatas tvaṃ prāpsyase putra nirayaṃ lokaviśrutam
children.translated_text: Then, my son, you will incur a hell famous in the world,
like the sin of killing a brāhmaṇa, from unrighteousness, as the ocean, lord of rivers, did.

children.text: vilapantīṃ tathā dīnāṃ kausalyāṃ jananīṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Then righteous-souled <s>Rāma</s> spoke a word joined with <s>dharma</s>
to his mother <s>Kausalyā</s>, who was lamenting in that way and wretched:

children.text: nāsti śaktiḥ pitur vākyaṃ samatikramituṃ mama
children.translated_text: I have no power to transgress my father's word.

children.text: prasādaye tvāṃ śirasā gantum icchāmy ahaṃ vanam ||
children.translated_text: I propitiate you with my head bowed; I wish to go to the forest.

children.text: ṛṣiṇā ca pitur vākyaṃ kurvatā vratacāriṇā
children.translated_text: By the sage <s>Kaṇḍu</s>, a knower of <s>dharma</s> and a wise vow-observer,

children.text: gaur hatā jānatā dharmaṃ kaṇḍunāpi vipaścitā ||
children.translated_text: a cow was killed while he was carrying out his father's word.

children.text: asmākaṃ ca kule pūrvaṃ sagarasyājñayā pituḥ
children.translated_text: And formerly in our family, at the command of their father <s>Sagara</s>,

children.text: khanadbhiḥ sāgarair bhūtim avāptaḥ sumahān vadhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a very great destruction was met by the sons of <s>Sagara</s> as they dug up the earth.
By <s>Rāma Jāmadagnya</s> himself, doing his father's word, his mother <s>Reṇukā</s>
was cut down with an axe in the forest.

children.text: na khalv etan mayaikena kriyate pitṛśāsanam
children.translated_text: This obedience to a father's command is certainly not being done by me alone.
This path, approved by the ancients, has been followed, and it is now to be followed.

children.text: tad etat tu mayā kāryaṃ kriyate bhuvi nānyathā
children.translated_text: Therefore this must be done by me; it is carried out on earth in no other way.

children.text: pitur hi vacanaṃ kurvan na kaścin nāma hīyate ||
children.translated_text: For no one at all declines by carrying out his father's word.

children.text: tām evam uktvā jananīṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ punar abravīt
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to his mother, he again addressed <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:

children.text: tava lakṣmaṇa jānāmi mayi sneham anuttamam
children.translated_text: I know, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, your unsurpassed affection for me,

children.text: abhiprāyam avijñāya satyasya ca śamasya ca ||
children.translated_text: but you do not understand the intention concerning truth and tranquility.

children.text: dharmo hi paramo loke dharme satyaṃ pratiṣṭhitam
children.translated_text: For <s>dharma</s> is supreme in the world; in <s>dharma</s> truth is established.

children.text: dharmasaṃśritam etac ca pitur vacanam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: And this excellent word of my father rests upon <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: saṃśrutya ca pitur vākyaṃ mātur vā brāhmaṇasya vā
children.translated_text: Having promised to fulfill the word of one's father, mother, or a brāhmaṇa,

children.text: na kartavyaṃ vṛthā vīra dharmam āśritya tiṣṭhatā ||
children.translated_text: a man who stands relying on <s>dharma</s>, O hero, must not make it futile.

children.text: so 'haṃ na śakṣyāmi pitur niyogam ativartitum
children.translated_text: So I shall not be able to overstep my father's injunction.

children.text: pitur hi vacanād vīra kaikeyyāhaṃ pracoditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For by my father's word, O hero, I have been urged by <s>Kaikeyī</s>.
Therefore abandon this ignoble intention that rests on warrior <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: dharmam āśraya mā taikṣṇyaṃ madbuddhir anugamyatām ||
children.translated_text: Take refuge in <s>dharma</s>; do not be harsh. Let my understanding be followed.

children.text: tam evam uktvā sauhārdād bhrātaraṃ lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken out of affection to his brother, the elder brother of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>
again spoke to <s>Kausalyā</s>, with joined palms and his head bowed:

children.text: anumanyasva māṃ devi gamiṣyantam ito vanam
children.translated_text: Give me leave, O goddess, as I go from here to the forest.

children.text: śāpitāsi mama prāṇaiḥ kuru svastyayanāni me
children.translated_text: You are adjured by my very life; perform rites of welfare for me.

children.text: tīrṇapratijñaś ca vanāt punar eṣyāmy ahaṃ purīm ||
children.translated_text: When my vow has been fulfilled, I shall return again from the forest to the city.

children.text: yaśo hy ahaṃ kevalarājyakāraṇān na pṛṣṭhataḥ kartum alaṃ mahodayam
children.translated_text: For merely for the sake of kingship I am not able to turn my great fame behind me.

children.text: adīrghakāle na tu devi jīvite vṛṇe 'varām adya mahīm adharmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this life, which is not long, O goddess, I do not choose today the inferior earth through unrighteousness.

children.text: prasādayan naravṛṣabhaḥ sa mātaraṃ parākramāj jigamiṣur eva daṇḍakān
children.translated_text: Thus propitiating his mother, that bull among men, wishing by his courage to go to the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest,

children.text: athānujaṃ bhṛśam anuśāsya darśanaṃ cakāra tāṃ hṛdi jananīṃ pradakṣiṇam ||
children.translated_text: then strongly instructed his younger brother and made a reverential circumambulation of his mother in his heart.

children.text: atha taṃ vyathayā dīnaṃ saviśeṣam amarṣitam
children.translated_text: Then, approaching <s>Saumitri</s>, who was wretched with anguish, especially indignant,
sighing like a great serpent, his eyes expanded with anger,

children.text: āsādya rāmaḥ saumitriṃ suhṛdaṃ bhrātaraṃ priyam
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, self-possessed and holding firmness by his courage,

children.text: uvācedaṃ sa dhairyeṇa dhārayan sattvam ātmavān ||
children.translated_text: spoke these words to his beloved friend and brother:
O <s>Saumitri</s>, the bustle of preparations that was for my consecration,
let that be a bustle of preparations for the cancellation of the consecration.
The one whose mind is tormented for the sake of my consecration,

children.text: mātā naḥ sā yathā na syāt saviśaṅkā tathā kuru ||
children.translated_text: act so that she, our mother, may not become full of suspicion.

children.text: tasyāḥ śaṅkāmayaṃ duḥkhaṃ muhūrtam api notsahe
children.translated_text: I cannot bear, even for a moment, to disregard
the sorrow born of suspicion that has arisen in her mind, O <s>Saumitri</s>.
Never here do I remember, whether intentionally or unintentionally,

children.text: mātṝṇāṃ vā pitur vāhaṃ kṛtam alpaṃ ca vipriyam ||
children.translated_text: having done even the slightest displeasing thing to my mothers or to my father.
My father is truthful, intent on truth, and always mighty through truth.
Let him, afraid of danger in the next world, become free from fear.

children.text: tasyāpi hi bhaved asmin karmaṇy apratisaṃhṛte
children.translated_text: For if this action were not carried through for him,

children.text: satyaṃ neti manastāpas tasya tāpas tapec ca mām ||
children.translated_text: the anguish in his mind, thinking 'it is not true,' would burn him, and that burning would burn me.
Therefore, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, having withdrawn the rite of consecration,

children.text: anvag evāham icchāmi vanaṃ gantum itaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I wish immediately thereafter to go from here again to the forest.
Because of my banishment today, the king's daughter, having accomplished her purpose,
will then calmly consecrate her son <s>Bharata</s>.
When I, wearing bark and antelope-skin and bearing a mass of matted locks,
have gone to the wilderness, there will be happiness in <s>Kaikeyī</s>'s mind.

children.text: buddhiḥ praṇītā yeneyaṃ manaś ca susamāhitam
children.translated_text: By whom this intention has been set forth, and whose mind is well composed,

children.text: tat tu nārhāmi saṃkleṣṭuṃ pravrajiṣyāmi māciram ||
children.translated_text: But I ought not to distress her; I shall go forth into exile without delay.

children.text: kṛtāntas tv eva saumitre draṣṭavyo matpravāsane
children.translated_text: Indeed, O <s>Saumitri</s>, fate alone must be seen as the cause of my banishment,

children.text: rājyasya ca vitīrṇasya punar eva nivartane ||
children.translated_text: and of the turning back again of the kingdom that had been bestowed.

children.text: kaikeyyāḥ pratipattir hi kathaṃ syān mama pīḍane
children.translated_text: For how could <s>Kaikeyī</s>'s course of action have arisen for the purpose of harming me,

children.text: yadi bhāvo na daivo 'yaṃ kṛtāntavihito bhavet ||
children.translated_text: if this condition were not divine, ordained by destiny?

children.text: jānāsi hi yathā saumya na mātṛṣu mamāntaram
children.translated_text: For you know, gentle one, that I have made no distinction among my mothers,

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ viśeṣo vā tasyā mayi sute 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: nor has there formerly been any difference in her attitude toward me or even toward her own son.
When I consider those hard-to-speak words of hers, aimed at stopping the consecration and bringing about exile,

children.text: ugrair vākyair ahaṃ tasyā nānyad daivāt samarthaye ||
children.translated_text: those fierce words, I can explain them by nothing other than fate.
How could a princess endowed with noble character and possessing such virtues,

children.text: brūyāt sā prākṛteva strī matpīḍāṃ bhartṛsaṃnidhau ||
children.translated_text: like an ordinary woman, speak of hurting me in her husband's presence?

children.text: yad acintyaṃ tu tad daivaṃ bhūteṣv api na hanyate
children.translated_text: But what is inconceivable is fate; it is not thwarted even among living beings.

children.text: vyaktaṃ mayi ca tasyāṃ ca patito hi viparyayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Clearly a reversal has fallen upon both me and her.

children.text: kaścid daivena saumitre yoddhum utsahate pumān
children.translated_text: What man, O <s>Saumitri</s>, is able to fight against fate,

children.text: yasya na grahaṇaṃ kiṃcit karmaṇo 'nyatra dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: when no means whatever of seizing its action is seen elsewhere?
Pleasure and pain, fear and anger, gain and loss, existence and nonexistence:

children.text: yasya kiṃcit tathā bhūtaṃ nanu daivasya karma tat ||
children.translated_text: whatever state of this kind there is, surely that is the work of fate.

children.text: vyāhate 'py abhiṣeke me paritāpo na vidyate
children.translated_text: Even though my consecration has been obstructed, I feel no grief.

children.text: tasmād aparitāpaḥ saṃs tvam apy anuvidhāya mām
children.translated_text: Therefore, being free from grief yourself too, follow my lead,
and quickly bring to a stop the rites connected with the consecration.

children.text: na lakṣmaṇāsmin mama rājyavighne mātā yavīyasy atiśaṅkanīyā
children.translated_text: O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, in this obstruction to my kingdom, my younger mother should not be greatly suspected.

children.text: daivābhipannā hi vadanty aniṣṭaṃ jānāsi daivaṃ ca tathāprabhāvam ||
children.translated_text: Those overcome by fate speak what is unwelcome; you know that fate has such power.

children.text: iti bruvati rāme tu lakṣmaṇo 'dhaḥśirā muhuḥ
children.translated_text: While <s>Rāma</s> was speaking thus, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, his head lowered again and again,
on hearing it, seemed in his mind to pass between sorrow and joy.

children.text: tadā tu baddhvā bhrukuṭīṃ bhruvor madhye nararṣabhaḥ
children.translated_text: Then that bull among men, knitting a frown between his brows,
breathed heavily like a great serpent angered inside its hole.
At that time, his face, hard to look upon with that frown,

children.text: babhau kruddhasya siṃhasya mukhasya sadṛśaṃ mukham ||
children.translated_text: shone like the face of an enraged lion.

children.text: agrahas taṃ vidhunvaṃs tu hastī hastam ivātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Shaking the tip of his hand as an elephant shakes its trunk,

children.text: tiryag ūrdhvaṃ śarīre ca pātayitvā śirodharām ||
children.translated_text: and bending his neck sideways, upward, and across his body,

children.text: agrākṣṇā vīkṣamāṇas tu tiryag bhrātaram abravīt
children.translated_text: he looked askance at his brother from the corner of his eye and said,

children.text: asthāne sambhramo yasya jāto vai sumahān ayam ||
children.translated_text: "This very great agitation of yours has arisen at an improper time.
On account of an attachment to a fault in <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty), and from an excessive fear of public opinion,

children.text: kathaṃ hy etad asambhrāntas tvadvidho vaktum arhati ||
children.translated_text: how can one such as you say this without being bewildered?
You are brave, a bull among kṣatriyas; why do you denounce this so-called fate,

children.text: kiṃ nāma kṛpaṇaṃ daivam aśaktam abhiśaṃsasi ||
children.translated_text: which is cowardly, pitiable, and powerless, as though it were strong?

children.text: pāpayos tu kathaṃ nāma tayoḥ śaṅkā na vidyate
children.translated_text: How is it that you have no suspicion of those two sinful people?

children.text: santi dharmopadhāḥ ślakṣṇā dharmātman kiṃ na budhyase ||
children.translated_text: There are smooth pretexts under the name of <s>dharma</s>; O righteous one, why do you not understand?
The consecration of someone other than you has been undertaken, hated by the people,

children.text: yeneyam āgatā dvaidhaṃ tava buddhir mahīpate
children.translated_text: and because of that your understanding, O lord of the earth, has fallen into this divided state.

children.text: sa hi dharmo mama dveṣyaḥ prasaṅgād yasya muhyasi ||
children.translated_text: That very <s>dharma</s> is hateful to me, by clinging to which you become deluded.

children.text: yady api pratipattis te daivī cāpi tayor matam
children.translated_text: Even if this is your understanding, and even if the opinion of those two is attributed to fate,

children.text: tathāpy upekṣaṇīyaṃ te na me tad api rocate ||
children.translated_text: still it ought not to be disregarded by you; and even that does not please me.

children.text: viklavo vīryahīno yaḥ sa daivam anuvartate
children.translated_text: One who is helpless and devoid of valor follows fate;
heroes who esteem themselves do not wait upon fate.
A man who is able to overpower fate by human effort,
when his purpose has been ruined by fate, does not sink down.

children.text: drakṣyanti tv adya daivasya pauruṣaṃ puruṣasya ca
children.translated_text: Today people shall see the manliness of fate and of a man;
today the distinction between divine force and human force will become clear.

children.text: adya matpauruṣahataṃ daivaṃ drakṣyanti vai janāḥ
children.translated_text: Today people shall indeed see fate struck down by my human effort,

children.text: yad daivād āhataṃ te 'dya dṛṣṭaṃ rājyābhiṣecanam ||
children.translated_text: since your royal consecration, seen today, has been struck down by fate.
Like an unrestrained elephant, arrogant with the strength of rut and beyond the goad,
I shall turn back fate as it charges forward, by human effort.
All those guardians of the world together could not obstruct <s>Rāma</s>'s consecration today,

children.text: na ca kṛtsnās trayo lokā vihanyuḥ kiṃ punaḥ pitā ||
children.translated_text: nor could all the three worlds; how much less, then, your father?

children.text: yair vivāsas tavāraṇye mitho rājan samarthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Those by whom your exile in the forest has been plotted together, O king,

children.text: araṇye te vivatsyanti caturdaśa samās tathā ||
children.translated_text: they shall live in the forest for fourteen years in the same way.

children.text: ahaṃ tadāśāṃ chetsyāmi pitus tasyāś ca yā tava
children.translated_text: I shall cut off that hope of your father and of her,
which, through the obstruction of your consecration, is directed toward her son's kingship.

children.text: madbalena viruddhāya na syād daivabalaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: The strength of fate will not be so able to bring pain to one opposed by my strength,
as my fierce human effort will prevail.
Only after the end of a thousand years, after you have protected the subjects without interruption,
will the noble princes undertake forest-dwelling when you have gone to the forest.
For forest-dwelling is prescribed according to the practice of royal sages of old,
after entrusting the subjects to sons for protection as if they were their own children.
But if, while the king's mind is divided, from fear of disorder in the kingdom,

children.text: naivam icchasi dharmātman rājyaṃ rāma tvam ātmani ||
children.translated_text: you do not desire the kingdom for yourself in this way, O righteous <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: pratijāne ca te vīra mā bhūvaṃ vīralokabhāk
children.translated_text: then I promise you, hero: may I never share the world of heroes

children.text: rājyaṃ ca tava rakṣeyam ahaṃ veleva sāgaram ||
children.translated_text: if I do not guard your kingdom like the shore guarding the ocean.

children.text: maṅgalair abhiṣiñcasva tatra tvaṃ vyāpṛto bhava
children.translated_text: Have yourself consecrated with auspicious rites; be occupied with that.

children.text: aham eko mahīpālān alaṃ vārayituṃ balāt ||
children.translated_text: I alone am sufficient to restrain the kings by force.

children.text: na śobhārthāv imau bāhū na dhanur bhūṣaṇāya me
children.translated_text: These two arms of mine are not for ornament, nor is my bow for decoration;
my sword is not for tying at my waist, nor are my arrows meant to stand idle as posts.
All this fourfold equipment of mine is for subduing enemies."

children.text: na cāhaṃ kāmaye 'tyarthaṃ yaḥ syāc chatrur mato mama ||
children.translated_text: Nor do I greatly desire that anyone whom I regard as my enemy should remain.
With a sword whose edge is sharp, flashing with the brilliance of lightning,

children.text: pragṛhītena vai śatruṃ vajriṇaṃ vā na kalpaye ||
children.translated_text: when it is grasped in my hand, I would not even reckon the wielder of the thunderbolt as an enemy.
Crushed by the blows of swords, the earth will become dense and hard for me to traverse,
covered with the hands, thighs, and heads of elephants, horses, and men.
Today elephants, struck by my sword-edge, like blazing mountains,

children.text: patiṣyanti dvipā bhūmau meghā iva savidyutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: will fall upon the earth like clouds accompanied by lightning.
When I stand with finger-guards of iguana-skin bound on and a bow grasped in hand,

children.text: kathaṃ puruṣamānī syāt puruṣāṇāṃ mayi sthite ||
children.translated_text: how could anyone who prides himself on being a man be counted a man among men?

children.text: bahubhiś caikam atyasyann ekena ca bahūñ janān
children.translated_text: Hurling many arrows at one man, and one arrow at many men,
I shall lodge my arrows in the vital spots of men, horses, and elephants.
Today the power of my missile-power will make its power manifest,

children.text: rājñaś cāprabhutāṃ kartuṃ prabhutvaṃ ca tava prabho ||
children.translated_text: able to make the king powerless and to establish your sovereignty, my lord.
Today these two arms, fit for sandalwood essence and for the loosening of armlets,

children.text: vasūnāṃ ca vimokṣasya suhṛdāṃ pālanasya ca ||
children.translated_text: and for the releasing of wealth and the protection of friends,

children.text: anurūpāv imau bāhū rāma karma kariṣyataḥ
children.translated_text: will perform a deed worthy of them, O <s>Rāma</s>,
in warding off those who have made an obstacle to your consecration.

children.text: bravīhi ko 'dyaiva mayā viyujyatāṃ tavāsuhṛt prāṇayaśaḥ suhṛjjanaiḥ
children.translated_text: Tell me: who today shall be deprived by me of life, fame, and friends as your enemy?

children.text: yathā taveyaṃ vasudhā vaśe bhavet tathaiva māṃ śādhi tavāsmi kiṃkaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Command me in such a way that this earth may come under your control; I am your servant.

children.text: vimṛjya bāṣpaṃ parisāntvya cāsakṛt sa lakṣmaṇaṃ rāghavavaṃśavardhanaḥ
children.translated_text: Wiping away his tears and repeatedly consoling <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, he, the increaser of the <s>Rāghava</s> line,

children.text: uvāca pitrye vacane vyavasthitaṃ nibodha mām eṣa hi saumya satpathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: spoke, firmly established in his father's command: "Understand me; this, dear one, is the true path."

children.text: taṃ samīkṣya tv avahitaṃ pitur nirdeśapālane
children.translated_text: But seeing him intent on carrying out his father's instruction,
<s>Kauśalyā</s>, choked with tears, spoke a most righteous word.
How shall one who has never seen suffering, righteous-souled, and pleasant-speaking to all beings,

children.text: mayi jāto daśarathāt katham uñchena vartayet ||
children.translated_text: born from <s>Daśaratha</s> through me, live by gleaning?

children.text: yasya bhṛtyāś ca dāsāś ca mṛṣṭāny annāni bhuñjate
children.translated_text: He whose servants and slaves eat fine foods,

children.text: kathaṃ sa bhokṣyate nātho vane mūlaphalāny ayam ||
children.translated_text: how will this lord eat roots and fruits in the forest?

children.text: ka etacchraddadhecchrutvā kasya vā na bhaved bhayam
children.translated_text: Who would believe this on hearing it, or who would not be afraid,

children.text: guṇavān dayito rājño rāghavo yad vivāsyate ||
children.translated_text: that virtuous <s>Rāghava</s>, dear to the king, is being banished?

children.text: tvayā vihīnām iha māṃ śokāgnir atulo mahān
children.translated_text: Here, when I am bereft of you, an incomparable, great fire of grief
will burn me as fire burns dry grass at winter's end.

children.text: kathaṃ hi dhenuḥ svaṃ vatsaṃ gacchantaṃ nānugacchati
children.translated_text: For how does a cow not follow her own calf as it goes away?
I shall follow you wherever you will go, my son.

children.text: tathā nigaditaṃ mātrā tad vākyaṃ puruṣarṣabhaḥ
children.translated_text: When his mother had spoken thus, the bull among men,
<s>Rāma</s>, hearing that speech, addressed his deeply sorrowing mother:

children.text: kaikeyyā vañcito rājā mayi cāraṇyam āśrite
children.translated_text: The king, deceived by <s>Kaikeyī</s>, with me having taken refuge in the forest,

children.text: bhavatyā ca parityakto na nūnaṃ vartayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: and abandoned by you as well, will surely not survive.

children.text: bhartuḥ kila parityāgo nṛśaṃsaḥ kevalaṃ striyāḥ
children.translated_text: Surely for a woman to abandon her husband is simply cruel;

children.text: sa bhavatyā na kartavyo manasāpi vigarhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that must not be done by you, for it is blameworthy even in thought.

children.text: yāvaj jīvati kākutsthaḥ pitā me jagatīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: So long as <s>Kākutstha</s>, my father, lord of the earth, lives,

children.text: śuśrūṣā kriyatāṃ tāvat sa hi dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so long service should be rendered to him; for that is the eternal <s>dharma</s> (duty).

children.text: evam uktā tu rāmeṇa kausalyā śubhadarśanā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Rāma</s>, fair-looking <s>Kauśalyā</s>
said, "So be it," well pleased with <s>Rāma</s>, who acted without weariness.

children.text: evam uktas tu vacanaṃ rāmo dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: When this word had been spoken, <s>Rāma</s>, best of those who uphold <s>dharma</s> (duty),

children.text: bhūyas tām abravīd vākyaṃ mātaraṃ bhṛśaduḥkhitām ||
children.translated_text: again spoke these words to his deeply sorrowing mother:

children.text: mayā caiva bhavatyā ca kartavyaṃ vacanaṃ pituḥ
children.translated_text: My father's word must be carried out by me and by you too;

children.text: rājā bhartā guruḥ śreṣṭhaḥ sarveṣām īśvaraḥ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king is husband, guru, the highest one, ruler and lord of all.

children.text: imāni tu mahāraṇye vihṛtya nava pañca ca
children.translated_text: But after dwelling in the great forest for these nine and five
years, I shall, supremely delighted, stand under your command.

children.text: evam uktā priyaṃ putraṃ bāṣpapūrṇānanā tadā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, then, with her face full of tears, to her beloved son
<s>Kauśalyā</s>, affectionate to her son, spoke in extreme distress:

children.text: āsāṃ rāma sapatnīnāṃ vastuṃ madhye na me kṣamam
children.translated_text: It is not possible for me, O <s>Rāma</s>, to live among these co-wives.

children.text: naya mām api kākutstha vanaṃ vanyāṃ mṛgīṃ yathā
children.translated_text: Take me too to the forest, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, like a wild doe,

children.text: yadi te gamane buddhiḥ kṛtā pitur apekṣayā ||
children.translated_text: if your mind is made up to go out of regard for your father.

children.text: tāṃ tathā rudatīṃ rāmo rudan vacanam abravīt
children.translated_text: To her weeping in that way, <s>Rāma</s>, weeping himself, spoke this word:

children.text: jīvantyā hi striyā bhartā daivataṃ prabhur eva ca
children.translated_text: For while a woman lives, her husband is her deity and her lord,

children.text: bhavatyā mama caivādya rājā prabhavati prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: and today the king is the lord with authority over you and me.
And righteous-souled <s>Bharata</s>, pleasant-speaking to all beings,

children.text: bhavatīm anuvarteta sa hi dharmarataḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: would follow your wishes, for he is always devoted to <s>dharma</s> (duty).

children.text: yathā mayi tu niṣkrānte putraśokena pārthivaḥ
children.translated_text: As, when I have gone forth, the lord of the earth

children.text: śramaṃ nāvāpnuyāt kiṃcid apramattā tathā kuru ||
children.translated_text: may suffer no distress at all from grief for his son, so act vigilantly.
A supremely excellent woman devoted to vows and fasts,

children.text: bhartāraṃ nānuvarteta sā ca pāpagatir bhavet ||
children.translated_text: if she did not attend upon her husband, would come to a sinful fate.

children.text: śuśrūṣām eva kurvīta bhartuḥ priyahite ratā
children.translated_text: She should simply perform service to her husband, delighting in his pleasure and welfare;

children.text: eṣa dharmaḥ purā dṛṣṭo loke vede śrutaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this <s>dharma</s> (duty) was seen of old in the world, heard and remembered in the <s>Veda</s>.

children.text: pūjyās te matkṛte devi brāhmaṇāś caiva suvratāḥ
children.translated_text: For my sake, O queen, brahmins of good vows should also be honored by you;
thus wait out the time, longing for my return.

children.text: prāpsyase paramaṃ kāmaṃ mayi pratyāgate sati
children.translated_text: You will obtain your highest desire when I have returned,
if the best of those who uphold <s>dharma</s> (duty) preserves his life.
Thus addressed by <s>Rāma</s>, her eyes troubled by tears,
<s>Kauśalyā</s>, afflicted by grief for her son, spoke this word to <s>Rāma</s>:

children.text: gaccha putra tvam ekāgro bhadraṃ te 'stu sadā vibho ||
children.translated_text: Go, my son, single-minded; may welfare always be yours, mighty one.

children.text: tathā hi rāmaṃ vanavāsaniścitaṃ samīkṣya devī parameṇa cetasā
children.translated_text: For, having looked upon <s>Rāma</s> as resolved on forest-dwelling, the queen, with the highest composure...

children.text: uvāca rāmaṃ śubhalakṣaṇaṃ vaco babhūva ca svastyayanābhikāṅkṣiṇī ||
children.translated_text: She spoke words to <s>Rāma</s>, marked with auspicious signs, and became intent on a blessing for his welfare.

children.text: sāpanīya tam āyāsam upaspṛśya jalaṃ śuci
children.translated_text: Having put away that weariness and sipped pure water,
the high-minded mother of <s>Rāma</s> performed auspicious rites.

children.text: svasti sādhyāś ca viśve ca marutaś ca maharṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: May the <s>Sādhyas</s>, the <s>Viśve Devas</s>, the <s>Maruts</s>, and the great seers grant you well-being.

children.text: svasti dhātā vidhātā ca svasti pūṣā bhago 'ryamā ||
children.translated_text: May <s>Dhātṛ</s> and <s>Vidhātṛ</s> grant well-being, and may <s>Pūṣan</s>, <s>Bhaga</s>, and <s>Aryaman</s> grant well-being.

children.text: ṛtavaś caiva pakṣāś ca māsāḥ saṃvatsarāḥ kṣapāḥ
children.translated_text: May the seasons, the fortnights, the months, the years, and the nights,

children.text: dināni ca muhūrtāś ca svasti kurvantu te sadā ||
children.translated_text: and the days and the muhūrtas, always bring you well-being.

children.text: smṛtir dhṛtiś ca dharmaś ca pāntu tvāṃ putra sarvataḥ
children.translated_text: May memory, firmness, and <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) protect you on every side, my son;

children.text: skandaś ca bhagavān devaḥ somaś ca sabṛhaspatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and may the blessed god <s>Skanda</s>, and <s>Soma</s> together with <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, protect you.

children.text: saptarṣayo nāradaś ca te tvāṃ rakṣantu sarvataḥ
children.translated_text: May the Seven Seers and <s>Nārada</s> protect you on every side.

children.text: nakṣatrāṇi ca sarvāṇi grahāś ca sahadevatāḥ
children.translated_text: May all the lunar mansions and the planets, together with their deities, protect you
as you wander the great forests in a sage's garb, wise one.

children.text: plavagā vṛścikā daṃśā maśakāś caiva kānane
children.translated_text: Leaping creatures, scorpions, gadflies, and mosquitoes in the forest,

children.text: sarīsṛpāś ca kīṭāś ca mā bhūvan gahane tava ||
children.translated_text: and reptiles and insects, may they not trouble you in the dense wilderness.

children.text: mahādvipāś ca siṃhāś ca vyāghrā ṛkṣāś ca daṃṣṭriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Great elephants, lions, tigers, tusked bears,

children.text: mahiṣāḥ śṛṅgiṇo raudrā na te druhyantu putraka ||
children.translated_text: and fierce horned buffaloes, may they not harm you, my little son.
Those fierce beings that feed on human flesh, and whatever other kinds of creatures there are,

children.text: mā ca tvāṃ hiṃsiṣuḥ putra mayā sampūjitās tv iha ||
children.translated_text: may they not injure you, my son, for they have been worshipped here by me.

children.text: āgamās te śivāḥ santu sidhyantu ca parākramāḥ
children.translated_text: May your journeys be auspicious, and may your heroic undertakings succeed.
May all prosperity be yours, <s>Rāma</s>; go blessed, my little son.

children.text: svasti te 'stv āntarikṣebhyaḥ pārthivebhyaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: May there be well-being for you again and again from beings of the mid-region and from beings of the earth,

children.text: sarvebhyaś caiva devebhyo ye ca te paripanthinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and from all the gods, and from those who stand in your way.
May <s>Brahmā</s>, lord of all worlds, the sustainer of beings, and the seers,

children.text: ye ca śeṣāḥ surās te tvāṃ rakṣantu vanavāsinam ||
children.translated_text: and whatever other gods remain, protect you as you dwell in the forest.

children.text: iti mālyaiḥ suragaṇān gandhaiś cāpi yaśasvinī
children.translated_text: Thus the renowned wide-eyed lady worshipped the hosts of gods with garlands
and with perfumes, and with fitting hymns of praise.
Whatever auspicious power came to the thousand-eyed one, honored by all the gods,

children.text: vṛtranāśe samabhavat tat te bhavatu maṅgalam ||
children.translated_text: at the destruction of <s>Vṛtra</s>, may that be an auspicious power for you.
Whatever auspicious power <s>Vinatā</s> once prepared for <s>Suparṇa</s>

children.text: amṛtaṃ prārthayānasya tat te bhavatu maṅgalam ||
children.translated_text: when he was seeking the nectar of immortality, may that be an auspicious power for you.
<s>Kausalyā</s> also prepared the effective herb <s>siddhārthā</s> and the blessed wound-healing herb,

children.text: cakāra rakṣāṃ kausalyā mantrair abhijajāpa ca ||
children.translated_text: made a protective charm, and recited mantras over it.
Bowing, smelling his head, and embracing him, the renowned lady

children.text: avadat putra siddhārtho gaccha rāma yathāsukham ||
children.translated_text: said, "My son, may your purpose be fulfilled; go, <s>Rāma</s>, as happily as you can.
May I see you healthy, your every aim accomplished, returned again to <s>Ayodhyā</s>,

children.text: paśyāmi tvāṃ sukhaṃ vatsa susthitaṃ rājaveśmani ||
children.translated_text: happy, dear child, securely established in the royal palace.
May the hosts of gods beginning with <s>Śiva</s>, worshipped by me, the great seers, beings, great asuras, and serpents,

children.text: abhiprayātasya vanaṃ cirāya te hitāni kāṅkṣantu diśaś ca rāghava ||
children.translated_text: and the directions wish what is beneficial for you as you set out to the forest for a long time, O <s>Rāghava</s>."

children.text: itīva cāśrupratipūrṇalocanā samāpya ca svastyayanaṃ yathāvidhi
children.translated_text: After speaking thus, her eyes filled with tears, and after completing the rite of blessing according to rule,

children.text: pradakṣiṇaṃ caiva cakāra rāghavaṃ punaḥ punaś cāpi nipīḍya sasvaje ||
children.translated_text: she circumambulated <s>Rāghava</s> and again and again embraced him tightly.

children.text: tathā tu devyā sa kṛtapradakṣiṇo nipīḍya mātuś caraṇau punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus circumambulated by the queen, he repeatedly pressed his mother's feet,

children.text: jagāma sītānilayaṃ mahāyaśāḥ sa rāghavaḥ prajvalitaḥ svayā śriyā ||
children.translated_text: and the greatly renowned <s>Rāghava</s>, blazing with his own splendor, went to <s>Sītā</s>'s dwelling.

children.text: abhivādya tu kausalyāṃ rāmaḥ samprasthito vanam
children.translated_text: Having bowed to <s>Kausalyā</s>, <s>Rāma</s> set out for the forest,
his mother having performed the blessing rite for him, and he stood firm on the most righteous path.
The king's son, making the royal road shine as it was filled with people,
seemed to churn the hearts of the people by the excellence of his virtues.

children.text: vaidehī cāpi tat sarvaṃ na śuśrāva tapasvinī
children.translated_text: But poor <s>Vaidehī</s> had not heard any of that whole matter;

children.text: tad eva hṛdi tasyāś ca yauvarājyābhiṣecanam ||
children.translated_text: in her heart there was only his consecration as crown prince.

children.text: devakāryaṃ sma sā kṛtvā kṛtajñā hṛṣṭacetanā
children.translated_text: After performing the worship of the gods, grateful and joyful at heart,
and knowledgeable in the duties of kings, she waited for the prince.
Then <s>Rāma</s> entered his own well-adorned house,
filled with delighted people, his face somewhat lowered from shame.

children.text: atha sītā samutpatya vepamānā ca taṃ patim
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sītā</s> sprang up, trembling, and looked at her husband,
burned by grief, his senses disturbed by anxiety.
Seeing his face discolored, seeing him sweating and unable to endure it,

children.text: āha duḥkhābhisaṃtaptā kim idānīm idaṃ prabho ||
children.translated_text: she, scorched by sorrow, said, "What is this now, my lord?

children.text: adya bārhaspataḥ śrīmān yuktaḥ puṣyo na rāghava
children.translated_text: Today, O <s>Rāghava</s>, the splendid <s>Puṣya</s> asterism, sacred to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, is in conjunction,

children.text: procyate brāhmaṇaiḥ prājñaiḥ kena tvam asi durmanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: so the wise Brahmins say; why then are you downcast?
Your lovely face is not shining, covered
by the hundred-ribbed umbrella that resembles water-foam.
Your face, with eyes like hundred-petaled lotuses, is not being fanned by two excellent fans,
bright as the moon and as swans.

children.text: vāgmino bandinaś cāpi prahṛṣṭās tvāṃ nararṣabha
children.translated_text: Eloquent bards too, joyful, O bull among men,
Sūtas and Māgadhas praising you with auspicious songs, are not seen today.

children.text: na te kṣaudraṃ ca dadhi ca brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ
children.translated_text: Brahmins who have mastered the Veda are not placing honey and curds
on your head according to rule, as one whose head has been consecrated.

children.text: na tvāṃ prakṛtayaḥ sarvā śreṇīmukhyāś ca bhūṣitāḥ
children.translated_text: All the subjects, the guild leaders adorned for the occasion,
and the townsmen and countryfolk do not wish to follow you.
Why does your chief <s>Puṣya</s> chariot, yoked with four swift horses

children.text: mukhyaḥ puṣyaratho yuktaḥ kiṃ na gacchati te 'grataḥ ||
children.translated_text: adorned with gold, not go before you?

children.text: na hastī cāgrataḥ śrīmāṃs tava lakṣaṇapūjitaḥ
children.translated_text: Nor is your splendid elephant, honored for its auspicious marks, seen ahead of you
on the procession, hero, shining like a dark cloud and a mountain."

children.text: na ca kāñcanacitraṃ te paśyāmi priyadarśana
children.translated_text: Nor, pleasant to behold, do I see for you the gold-decorated
auspicious seat placed in front, as you go with heroes before you.

children.text: abhiṣeko yadā sajjaḥ kim idānīm idaṃ tava
children.translated_text: When the consecration is ready, what is this state of yours now?

children.text: apūrvo mukhavarṇaś ca na praharṣaś ca lakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: Your complexion is changed in an unprecedented way, and no joy is seen.
To her as she was lamenting in this way, the delight of the <s>Raghu</s> line spoke:

children.text: sīte tatrabhavāṃs tātaḥ pravrājayati māṃ vanam ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Sītā</s>, our venerable father is sending me away to the forest.
Born in a great family, knower of <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty), follower of <s>dharma</s>,
hear, <s>Jānakī</s>, by what sequence this has come upon me.
By the king, my father <s>Daśaratha</s>, true to his promise,
two great boons had formerly been given to <s>Kaikeyī</s> with a pleased mind.
Today, when my consecration was ready and the king was undertaking it,
that appointed time was urged on by her, and he was overcome by <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: caturdaśa hi varṣāṇi vastavyaṃ daṇḍake mayā
children.translated_text: For fourteen years I must dwell in <s>Dandaka</s>;

children.text: pitrā me bharataś cāpi yauvarājye niyojitaḥ
children.translated_text: and by my father <s>Bharata</s> has been appointed to the office of heir apparent.

children.text: so 'haṃ tvām āgato draṣṭuṃ prasthito vijanaṃ vanam ||
children.translated_text: So I, setting out for the lonely forest, have come to see you.

children.text: bharatasya samīpe te nāhaṃ kathyaḥ kadācana
children.translated_text: In <s>Bharata</s>'s presence you should never speak of me;

children.text: ṛddhiyuktā hi puruṣā na sahante parastavam
children.translated_text: for men possessed of prosperity do not tolerate praise of another.

children.text: tasmān na te guṇāḥ kathyā bharatasyāgrato mama ||
children.translated_text: Therefore my virtues should not be spoken of by you before <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: nāpi tvaṃ tena bhartavyā viśeṣeṇa kadācana
children.translated_text: Nor should you ever be treated by him with special favor.
It will be possible to remain near him through compliance.

children.text: ahaṃ cāpi pratijñāṃ tāṃ guroḥ samanupālayan
children.translated_text: And I too, fully observing that promise of my elder,

children.text: vanam adyaiva yāsyāmi sthirā bhava manasvini ||
children.translated_text: will go to the forest this very day; be firm, high-minded one.

children.text: yāte ca mayi kalyāṇi vanaṃ muniniṣevitam
children.translated_text: And when I have gone, blessed one, to the forest frequented by sages,
you, faultless one, must be devoted to vows and fasts.

children.text: kālyam utthāya devānāṃ kṛtvā pūjāṃ yathāvidhi
children.translated_text: Rising early, after worshiping the gods according to rule,
you should bow to <s>Daśaratha</s>, my father, the lord of men.

children.text: mātā ca mama kausalyā vṛddhā saṃtāpakarśitā
children.translated_text: And my mother <s>Kausalyā</s>, aged and wasted by grief,

children.text: dharmam evāgrataḥ kṛtvā tvattaḥ sammānam arhati ||
children.translated_text: putting <s>dharma</s> foremost, deserves honor from you.

children.text: vanditavyāś ca te nityaṃ yāḥ śeṣā mama mātaraḥ
children.translated_text: And those others who are my mothers should be honored by you always;
by affection, intimacy, and enjoyment they are equal as my mothers.
And <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and <s>Śatrughna</s>, equal to brothers and sons, should be regarded with special care by you,
for they are dearer to me than life.

children.text: vipriyaṃ na ca kartavyaṃ bharatasya kadācana
children.translated_text: Nothing displeasing to <s>Bharata</s> should ever be done;

children.text: sa hi rājā prabhuś caiva deśasya ca kulasya ca ||
children.translated_text: for he is king and lord of both the country and the family.
Kings, when pleased by good conduct and carefully served with effort,
become gracious; in the opposite case they become angry.

children.text: aurasān api putrān hi tyajanty ahitakāriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: For kings abandon even sons born from their own body when they act against their welfare,
and they accept even other people when they are capable.

children.text: ahaṃ gamiṣyāmi mahāvanaṃ priye tvayā hi vastavyam ihaiva bhāmini
children.translated_text: I shall go to the great forest, dear one; you, beautiful woman, must stay right here.

children.text: yathā vyalīkaṃ kuruṣe na kasyacit tathā tvayā kāryam idaṃ vaco mama ||
children.translated_text: So that you do no wrong to anyone, this word of mine must be carried out by you."

children.text: evam uktā tu vaidehī priyārhā priyavādinī
children.translated_text: But <s>Vaidehī</s>, worthy of love and speaking lovingly, when addressed in this way,

children.text: praṇayād eva saṃkruddhā bhartāram idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: became angry out of affection itself and said this to her husband:

children.text: āryaputra pitā mātā bhrātā putras tathā snuṣā
children.translated_text: "Noble prince, father, mother, brother, son, and daughter-in-law

children.text: svāni puṇyāni bhuñjānāḥ svaṃ svaṃ bhāgyam upāsate ||
children.translated_text: enjoy their own merits and each attend upon their own fortune.

children.text: bhartur bhāgyaṃ tu bhāryaikā prāpnoti puruṣarṣabha
children.translated_text: But a wife alone obtains her husband's fortune, bull among men;

children.text: ataś caivāham ādiṣṭā vane vastavyam ity api ||
children.translated_text: and therefore I too am commanded: 'You must dwell in the forest.'

children.text: na pitā nātmajo nātmā na mātā na sakhījanaḥ
children.translated_text: Not father, not son, not self, not mother, not companions;

children.text: iha pretya ca nārīṇāṃ patir eko gatiḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: here and after death, for women the husband alone is always the way.

children.text: yadi tvaṃ prasthito durgaṃ vanam adyaiva rāghava
children.translated_text: If you have set out today for the difficult forest, <s>Rāghava</s>,
I shall go before you, trampling down the <s>kusa</s> grass and thorns.
Casting out jealousy and anger like water left over after drinking,

children.text: naya māṃ vīra viśrabdhaḥ pāpaṃ mayi na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: take me, hero, with confidence; there is no sin in me.
More than palace-tops, aerial mansions, or travel through the sky,
in every condition the shade of a husband's feet is superior.

children.text: anuśiṣṭāsmi mātrā ca pitrā ca vividhāśrayam
children.translated_text: I have been instructed by my mother and father in the many circumstances of life;

children.text: nāsmi samprati vaktavyā vartitavyaṃ yathā mayā ||
children.translated_text: I do not now need to be told how I must conduct myself.

children.text: sukhaṃ vane nivatsyāmi yathaiva bhavane pituḥ
children.translated_text: I shall live happily in the forest just as in my father's house,
not thinking of the three worlds, thinking only of the vow of devotion to my husband.
Serving you always, restrained and practicing chastity,

children.text: saha raṃsye tvayā vīra vaneṣu madhugandhiṣu ||
children.translated_text: I shall delight together with you, hero, in the honey-fragrant forests.

children.text: tvaṃ hi kartuṃ vane śakto rāma samparipālanam
children.translated_text: For you, <s>Rāma</s>, are able to give protection in the forest

children.text: anyasyāpi janasyeha kiṃ punar mama mānada ||
children.translated_text: even to another person here; how much more to me, giver of honor.
I shall always live on fruits and roots, without doubt;

children.text: na te duḥkhaṃ kariṣyāmi nivasantī saha tvayā ||
children.translated_text: living together with you, I shall cause you no suffering.

children.text: icchāmi saritaḥ śailān palvalāni vanāni ca
children.translated_text: I wish to see rivers, mountains, pools, and forests,

children.text: draṣṭuṃ sarvatra nirbhītā tvayā nāthena dhīmatā ||
children.translated_text: fearless everywhere with you, my wise lord.
Lotus ponds filled with geese and karandava ducks, well blossoming,

children.text: iccheyaṃ sukhinī draṣṭuṃ tvayā vīreṇa saṃgatā ||
children.translated_text: I would wish to see happily, joined with you, hero.
Together with you, wide-eyed one, I shall delight in the highest joy,

children.text: evaṃ varṣasahasrāṇāṃ śataṃ vāhaṃ tvayā saha ||
children.translated_text: even for a hundred thousand years together with you.

children.text: svarge 'pi ca vinā vāso bhavitā yadi rāghava
children.translated_text: And even if residence in heaven without you should come to be, <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: tvayā mama naravyāghra nāhaṃ tam api rocaye ||
children.translated_text: without you, tiger among men, I would not like even that.

children.text: ahaṃ gamiṣyāmi vanaṃ sudurgamaṃ mṛgāyutaṃ vānaravāraṇair yutam
children.translated_text: I shall go to the forest, very hard to traverse, filled with deer and joined with monkeys and elephants;

children.text: vane nivatsyāmi yathā pitur gṛhe tavaiva pādāv upagṛhya saṃmatā ||
children.translated_text: in the forest I shall live as in my father's house, holding only your feet and approved by you.

children.text: ananyabhāvām anuraktacetasaṃ tvayā viyuktāṃ maraṇāya niścitām
children.translated_text: me, single-minded, with a heart devoted to you, and resolved on death if separated from you

children.text: nayasva māṃ sādhu kuruṣva yācanāṃ na te mayāto gurutā bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Take me; kindly grant my request. After this, no burden will come to you because of me.

children.text: tathā bruvāṇām api dharmavatsalo na ca sma sītāṃ nṛvaro ninīṣati
children.translated_text: Although she was speaking in this way, the king, devoted to <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty), did not wish to take <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: uvāca caināṃ bahu saṃnivartane vane nivāsasya ca duḥkhitāṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: and he spoke many words to turn her back, addressing her as she was distressed about dwelling in the forest.

children.text: sa evaṃ bruvatīṃ sītāṃ dharmajño dharmavatsalaḥ
children.translated_text: To <s>Sītā</s>, who was speaking thus, he, knowing <s>dharma</s> and devoted to <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: nivartanārthe dharmātmā vākyam etad uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: that righteous-souled one then spoke these words for the sake of turning her back.

children.text: sīte mahākulīnāsi dharme ca niratā sadā
children.translated_text: "<s>Sītā</s>, you are born in a great family and are always intent on <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: ihācara svadharmaṃ tvaṃ mā yathā manasaḥ sukham ||
children.translated_text: Practice your own duty here, and not merely whatever is pleasing to your mind.

children.text: sīte yathā tvāṃ vakṣyāmi tathā kāryaṃ tvayābale
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s>, delicate one, you must act just as I shall tell you.

children.text: vane doṣā hi bahavo vadatas tān nibodha me ||
children.translated_text: For there are many faults in the forest; hear them from me as I describe them.
<s>Sītā</s>, let go of this resolve that is fixed on forest-dwelling.

children.text: bahudoṣaṃ hi kāntāraṃ vanam ity abhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: For a wilderness is called a forest because it is full of many faults.
This speech has indeed been spoken by me with a mind intent on your welfare.

children.text: sadā sukhaṃ na jānāmi duḥkham eva sadā vanam ||
children.translated_text: I do not know the forest as always happy; the forest is always suffering.
The sounds of lions, born among mountain torrents and dwelling in mountain caves,

children.text: siṃhānāṃ ninadā duḥkhāḥ śrotuṃ duḥkham ato vanam ||
children.translated_text: are painful to hear; for that reason the forest is painful.
One sleeps on beds of leaves, broken off by oneself, upon the ground,
exhausted by labor during the nights; therefore the forest is still more painful.
Fasting too must be undertaken according to one's strength, O <s>Maithilī</s>,
and a heavy mass of matted hair must be worn by one dressed in bark garments.

children.text: atīva vātas timiraṃ bubhukṣā cātra nityaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Here there is constant fierce wind, darkness, and hunger,

children.text: bhayāni ca mahānty atra tato duḥkhataraṃ vanam ||
children.translated_text: and great fears are here; therefore the forest is still more painful.

children.text: sarīsṛpāś ca bahavo bahurūpāś ca bhāmini
children.translated_text: Many creeping creatures, of many forms, O lovely one,

children.text: caranti pṛthivīṃ darpād ato duḥkhataraṃ vanam ||
children.translated_text: move over the earth in arrogance; therefore the forest is still more painful.
Snakes that dwell in rivers and move in winding river courses

children.text: tiṣṭhanty āvṛtya panthānam ato duḥkhataraṃ vanam ||
children.translated_text: stand blocking the path; therefore the forest is still more painful.

children.text: pataṃgā vṛścikāḥ kīṭā daṃśāś ca maśakaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Flying insects, scorpions, worms, biting flies, and mosquitoes

children.text: bādhante nityam abale sarvaṃ duḥkham ato vanam ||
children.translated_text: constantly afflict one, delicate one; therefore the forest is altogether painful.

children.text: drumāḥ kaṇṭakinaś caiva kuśakāśāś ca bhāmini
children.translated_text: There are thorny trees, and also kuśa and kāśa grasses, O lovely one,
with the tips of their branches tangled in the forest; because of that the forest is still more painful.

children.text: tad alaṃ te vanaṃ gatvā kṣamaṃ na hi vanaṃ tava
children.translated_text: So enough of your going to the forest; the forest is not suitable for you.
Considering it here, I see the forest as even more full of faults."

children.text: vanaṃ tu netuṃ na kṛtā matis tadā babhūva rāmeṇa yadā mahātmanā
children.translated_text: When the great-souled <s>Rāma</s> had not formed the resolve to take her to the forest then,

children.text: na tasya sītā vacanaṃ cakāra tat tato 'bravīd rāmam idaṃ suduḥkhitā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s> did not carry out that word of his; then, deeply distressed, she said this to <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: etat tu vacanaṃ śrutvā sītā rāmasya duḥkhitā
children.translated_text: Having heard this speech of <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Sītā</s>, distressed,
with her face wet with clinging tears, slowly spoke these words:

children.text: ye tvayā kīrtitā doṣā vane vastavyatāṃ prati
children.translated_text: "The faults you have mentioned regarding dwelling in the forest,

children.text: guṇān ity eva tān viddhi tava snehapuraskṛtān ||
children.translated_text: know those very things to be virtues, brought forward by your affection.

children.text: tvayā ca saha gantavyaṃ mayā gurujanājñayā
children.translated_text: I must go together with you, by the command of my elders.

children.text: tvadviyogena me rāma tyaktavyam iha jīvitam ||
children.translated_text: Through separation from you, O <s>Rāma</s>, my life must be abandoned here.

children.text: na ca māṃ tvatsamīpasthām api śaknoti rāghava
children.translated_text: Even the lord of the gods, <s>Śakra</s>, cannot, O <s>Rāghava</s>,
violate me by his power while I am standing near you.

children.text: patihīnā tu yā nārī na sā śakṣyati jīvitum
children.translated_text: But a woman without her husband will not be able to live.

children.text: kāmam evaṃvidhaṃ rāma tvayā mama vidarśitam ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, O <s>Rāma</s>, such a condition for me has been shown by you.

children.text: atha cāpi mahāprājña brāhmaṇānāṃ mayā śrutam
children.translated_text: And moreover, O very wise one, I formerly heard from brahmins

children.text: purā pitṛgṛhe satyaṃ vastavyaṃ kila me vane ||
children.translated_text: in my father's house that truly, they said, I was to dwell in the forest.
Having heard at home the words of twice-born men expert in signs,
I have always been eager for forest-dwelling, O mighty-armed one.

children.text: ādeśo vanavāsasya prāptavyaḥ sa mayā kila
children.translated_text: That injunction of forest-dwelling was indeed to be obtained by me.

children.text: sā tvayā saha tatrāhaṃ yāsyāmi priya nānyathā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore I shall go there with you, beloved, and not otherwise.
I shall be one for whom the injunction has been fulfilled; I shall go with you.

children.text: kālaś cāyaṃ samutpannaḥ satyavāg bhavatu dvijaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This time has arisen; let the brahmin be truthful in speech.

children.text: vanavāse hi jānāmi duḥkhāni bahudhā kila
children.translated_text: For I know that in forest-dwelling many sufferings, indeed,
are certainly met with by men who have not mastered themselves, O hero.

children.text: kanyayā ca pitur gehe vanavāsaḥ śruto mayā
children.translated_text: As a maiden in my father's house, I heard of forest-dwelling
from a mendicant woman of good conduct, here in the presence of my mother.

children.text: prasāditaś ca vai pūrvaṃ tvaṃ vai bahuvidhaṃ prabho
children.translated_text: And formerly, O lord, you were indeed entreated by me in many ways,

children.text: gamanaṃ vanavāsasya kāṅkṣitaṃ hi saha tvayā ||
children.translated_text: for I have desired the going to forest-dwelling together with you.

children.text: kṛtakṣaṇāhaṃ bhadraṃ te gamanaṃ prati rāghava
children.translated_text: I am ready for the time of departure, blessing to you, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: vanavāsasya śūrasya caryā hi mama rocate ||
children.translated_text: The way of life of heroic forest-dwelling is pleasing to me.
O pure-souled one, through the feeling of love I shall become free from stain,

children.text: bhartāram anugacchantī bhartā hi mama daivatam ||
children.translated_text: following my husband; for my husband is my deity.

children.text: pretyabhāve 'pi kalyāṇaḥ saṃgamo me saha tvayā
children.translated_text: Even in the state after death, O noble one, there will be union for me with you.

children.text: śrutir hi śrūyate puṇyā brāhmaṇānāṃ yaśasvinām ||
children.translated_text: For a holy tradition is heard among renowned brahmins:

children.text: iha loke ca pitṛbhir yā strī yasya mahāmate
children.translated_text: in this world, O great-minded one, whatever woman is given by her fathers to a man

children.text: adbhir dattā svadharmeṇa pretyabhāve 'pi tasya sā ||
children.translated_text: with water according to her own <s>dharma</s>, in the state after death too she is his.

children.text: evam asmāt svakāṃ nārīṃ suvṛttāṃ hi pativratām
children.translated_text: Thus, for what reason here do you not wish to take me,

children.text: nābhirocayase netuṃ tvaṃ māṃ keneha hetunā ||
children.translated_text: your own wife, well-conducted and faithful to her husband?

children.text: bhaktāṃ pativratāṃ dīnāṃ māṃ samāṃ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ
children.translated_text: Devoted, faithful to my husband, helpless, equal in pleasure and pain,
you ought to take me, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, one who shares the same pleasure and pain.

children.text: yadi māṃ duḥkhitām evaṃ vanaṃ netuṃ na cecchasi
children.translated_text: If you do not wish to take me, distressed in this way, to the forest,

children.text: viṣam agniṃ jalaṃ vāham āsthāsye mṛtyukāraṇāt ||
children.translated_text: I shall resort to poison, fire, or water as the cause of my death."

children.text: evaṃ bahuvidhaṃ taṃ sā yācate gamanaṃ prati
children.translated_text: Thus she begged him in many ways with regard to going,

children.text: nānumene mahābāhus tāṃ netuṃ vijanaṃ vanam ||
children.translated_text: but the mighty-armed one did not consent to take her to the lonely forest.

children.text: evam uktā tu sā cintāṃ maithilī samupāgatā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Maithilī</s> fell into thought.
as if bathing the earth with hot tears fallen from her eyes.

children.text: cintayantīṃ tathā tāṃ tu nivartayitum ātmavān
children.translated_text: As she was thinking in that way, the self-possessed one sought to turn her back;

children.text: krodhāviṣṭāṃ tu vaidehīṃ kākutstho bahv asāntvayat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kākutstha</s> tried at length to soothe the enraged <s>Vaidehī</s>.
But as she was being soothed by <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Maithilī</s>, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,
spoke these words to her husband on the matter of dwelling in the forest.
That <s>Sītā</s>, greatly agitated, addressed him, the broad-chested one,
and out of love and wounded pride reproached <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: kiṃ tvāmanyata vaidehaḥ pitā me mithilādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: What did my father, <s>Vaideha</s>, lord of <s>Mithilā</s>, think of you,
O <s>Rāma</s>, when he obtained as son-in-law a woman in a man's form?
This foolish world, through ignorance, will speak a falsehood,

children.text: tejo nāsti paraṃ rāme tapatīva divākare ||
children.translated_text: saying that there is no supreme splendor in <s>Rāma</s>, as if in the blazing sun.

children.text: kiṃ hi kṛtvā viṣaṇṇas tvaṃ kuto vā bhayam asti te
children.translated_text: What have you done that you are dejected? Or whence is there any fear for you,
that you wish to abandon me, who am devoted to no one else?
Know me, hero, to be like <s>Sāvitrī</s>, vowed to <s>Satyavant</s>, son of <s>Dyumatsena</s>,

children.text: sāvitrīm iva māṃ viddhi tvam ātmavaśavartinīm ||
children.translated_text: following the control of your own self.

children.text: na tv ahaṃ manasāpy anyaṃ draṣṭāsmi tvadṛte 'nagha
children.translated_text: Not even in thought shall I look upon another man apart from you, sinless one.
With you, O <s>Rāghava</s>, I would go; otherwise I would be like a woman who disgraces her family.

children.text: svayaṃ tu bhāryāṃ kaumārīṃ ciram adhyuṣitāṃ satīm
children.translated_text: Yet you wish to give me, your own wife, married as a maiden, long dwelling with you and faithful,

children.text: śailūṣa iva māṃ rāma parebhyo dātum icchasi ||
children.translated_text: to others, O <s>Rāma</s>, like an actor giving away a woman.

children.text: sa mām anādāya vanaṃ na tvaṃ prasthātum arhasi
children.translated_text: You ought not to set out for the forest without taking me.

children.text: tapo vā yadi vāraṇyaṃ svargo vā syāt saha tvayā ||
children.translated_text: Whether it is austerity, or the wilderness, or heaven, let it be together with you.

children.text: na ca me bhavitā tatra kaścit pathi pariśramaḥ
children.translated_text: There will be no weariness for me there on the road,
as I walk behind you, even as though on pleasure couches.
Kuśa grass, kāśa grass, reeds, rushes, and the thorny trees there
will feel to me on the path with you like cotton and deerskin.
The dust that a great wind, rising up, will scatter over me,

children.text: rajo ramaṇa tan manye parārdhyam iva candanam ||
children.translated_text: that, my beloved, I shall consider like the finest sandal paste.
When, moving in the forest at the forest's edge, I lie down on grassy ground,
what could be happier than that, even than beds spread with coverlets?

children.text: pattraṃ mūlaṃ phalaṃ yat tvam alpaṃ vā yadi vā bahu
children.translated_text: Whatever leaf, root, or fruit you yourself bring and give me,
whether little or much, that will be like the taste of nectar to me.

children.text: na mātur na pitus tatra smariṣyāmi na veśmanaḥ
children.translated_text: There I shall not remember my mother, nor my father, nor the house,

children.text: ārtavāny upabhuñjānā puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca ||
children.translated_text: as I enjoy seasonal flowers and fruits.

children.text: na ca tatra gataḥ kiṃcid draṣṭum arhasi vipriyam
children.translated_text: And once gone there, you should not see anything unpleasant,

children.text: matkṛte na ca te śoko na bhaviṣyāmi durbharā ||
children.translated_text: nor will there be sorrow for you on my account; I shall not be hard to maintain.

children.text: yas tvayā saha sa svargo nirayo yas tvayā vinā
children.translated_text: That which is with you is heaven; hell is that which is without you.

children.text: iti jānan parāṃ prītiṃ gaccha rāma mayā saha ||
children.translated_text: Knowing this supreme love, go, <s>Rāma</s>, together with me.

children.text: atha mām evam avyagrāṃ vanaṃ naiva nayiṣyasi
children.translated_text: But if you will not take me, unshaken as I am, to the forest,

children.text: viṣam adyaiva pāsyāmi mā viśaṃ dviṣatāṃ vaśam ||
children.translated_text: I shall drink poison this very day; do not let me fall into the power of enemies.

children.text: paścād api hi duḥkhena mama naivāsti jīvitam
children.translated_text: For afterward too, in sorrow, there is no life for me at all.

children.text: ujjhitāyās tvayā nātha tadaiva maraṇaṃ varam ||
children.translated_text: For one abandoned by you, lord, death at that very moment is better.

children.text: idaṃ hi sahituṃ śokaṃ muhūrtam api notsahe
children.translated_text: I cannot bear this grief even for a single moment;

children.text: kiṃ punar daśavarṣāṇi trīṇi caikaṃ ca duḥkhitā ||
children.translated_text: how much less for ten years, and three, and one, while suffering?

children.text: iti sā śokasaṃtaptā vilapya karuṇaṃ bahu
children.translated_text: Thus, burned by grief, after lamenting much and piteously,

children.text: cukrośa patim āyastā bhṛśam āliṅgya sasvaram ||
children.translated_text: she cried aloud to her husband, distressed, embracing him tightly with a ringing voice.

children.text: sā viddhā bahubhir vākyair digdhair iva gajāṅganā
children.translated_text: Pierced by many words, like a female elephant by poisoned shafts,
she released tears long restrained, as the fire-stick releases fire.
From her eyes there flowed water born of anguish,
clear as crystal, like water from two lotuses.

children.text: tāṃ pariṣvajya bāhubhyāṃ visaṃjñām iva duḥkhitām
children.translated_text: Then, embracing with his arms that sorrowing woman, almost unconscious,
<s>Rāma</s> spoke these words, reassuring her at that time.

children.text: na devi tava duḥkhena svargam apy abhirocaye
children.translated_text: Goddess, I would not desire even heaven if it caused you sorrow.

children.text: na hi me 'sti bhayaṃ kiṃcit svayambhor iva sarvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: For I have no fear from anywhere, like <s>Svayambhū</s>.
Not having fully understood all your intention, fair-faced one,

children.text: vāsaṃ na rocaye 'raṇye śaktimān api rakṣaṇe ||
children.translated_text: I did not favor your dwelling in the forest, though I am able to protect you.

children.text: yat sṛṣṭāsi mayā sārdhaṃ vanavāsāya maithili
children.translated_text: Since you were created for forest-dwelling together with me, <s>Maithilī</s>,

children.text: na vihātuṃ mayā śakyā kīrtir ātmavatā yathā ||
children.translated_text: you cannot be abandoned by me, just as fame cannot be abandoned by a self-possessed man.

children.text: dharmas tu gajanāsoru sadbhir ācaritaḥ purā
children.translated_text: But <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty), O lady with elephant-like thighs, was practiced by the good in ancient times;

children.text: taṃ cāham anuvarte 'dya yathā sūryaṃ suvarcalā ||
children.translated_text: and I follow it today, as <s>Suvarcalā</s> follows the sun.

children.text: eṣa dharmas tu suśroṇi pitur mātuś ca vaśyatā
children.translated_text: This, lovely-hipped one, is <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty): obedience to father and mother.

children.text: ataś cājñāṃ vyatikramya nāhaṃ jīvitum utsahe ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, having transgressed their command, I could not bear to live.

children.text: sa māṃ pitā yathā śāsti satyadharmapathe sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: As my father, standing on the path of truth and <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty), commands me,

children.text: tathā vartitum icchāmi sa hi dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
children.translated_text: so I wish to act; for that is the eternal <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty).
Follow me, timid one, and be my companion in <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty).

children.text: brāhmaṇebhyaś ca ratnāni bhikṣukebhyaś ca bhojanam
children.translated_text: Give jewels to the brahmins and food to the beggars;
give also to those who hope for gifts, and hurry; do not delay.

children.text: anukūlaṃ tu sā bhartur jñātvā gamanam ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, knowing that her own going was agreeable to her husband,
the joyful queen quickly began to give.

children.text: tataḥ prahṛṣṭā paripūrṇamānasā yaśasvinī bhartur avekṣya bhāṣitam
children.translated_text: Then the illustrious woman, delighted and with her heart fulfilled, having heard her husband's words,

children.text: dhanāni ratnāni ca dātum aṅganā pracakrame dharmabhṛtāṃ manasvinī ||
children.translated_text: the high-minded woman began to give away wealth and jewels to upholders of <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty).
Then the greatly radiant <s>Rāma</s> spoke to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
the hero standing before him, eager to go first, begging with joined palms.

children.text: mayādya saha saumitre tvayi gacchati tad vanam
children.translated_text: If you go today with me, O <s>Saumitri</s>, to that forest,

children.text: ko bhariṣyati kausalyāṃ sumitrāṃ vā yaśasvinīm ||
children.translated_text: who will support <s>Kausalyā</s>, or illustrious <s>Sumitrā</s>?

children.text: abhivarṣati kāmair yaḥ parjanyaḥ pṛthivīm iva
children.translated_text: He who showers desired things upon them, like <s>Parjanya</s> upon the earth...
That mighty-spirited king, the lord of the earth, has fallen under the snare of desire.

children.text: sā hi rājyam idaṃ prāpya nṛpasyāśvapateḥ sutā
children.translated_text: For she, having obtained this kingdom, the daughter of king <s>Aśvapati</s>,
will not act kindly toward the king's sorrowing co-wives.

children.text: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa lakṣmaṇaḥ ślakṣṇayā girā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Rāma</s> in gentle speech,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, skilled in speech, then replied to <s>Rāma</s>, the master of eloquence:
"By your own splendor, hero, <s>Bharata</s> will honor

children.text: kausalyāṃ ca sumitrāṃ ca prayato nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kausalyā</s> and <s>Sumitrā</s> with care; there is no doubt of this.

children.text: kausalyā bibhṛyād āryā sahasram api madvidhān
children.translated_text: Noble <s>Kausalyā</s> could support even a thousand men like me,
since she has received the livelihood of a thousand villages.
Taking a bow with arrows and carrying a spade and basket,
I shall go before you, showing the path.

children.text: āhariṣyāmi te nityaṃ mūlāni ca phalāni ca
children.translated_text: I shall always bring you roots and fruits,
and whatever other forest foods are suitable as the fare of ascetics.

children.text: bhavāṃs tu saha vaidehyā girisānuṣu raṃsyate
children.translated_text: But you, together with <s>Vaidehī</s>, will delight on the mountain slopes;

children.text: ahaṃ sarvaṃ kariṣyāmi jāgrataḥ svapataś ca te ||
children.translated_text: I shall do everything for you, whether you are awake or asleep."

children.text: rāmas tv anena vākyena suprītaḥ pratyuvāca tam
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, very pleased by this speech,
answered him: "Go, son of <s>Sumitrā</s>; take leave of all the friends.

children.text: ye ca rājño dadau divye mahātmā varuṇaḥ svayam
children.translated_text: And those two divine bows which the great <s>Varuṇa</s> himself gave
at <s>Janaka</s>'s great sacrifice, terrible to behold like <s>Rudra</s>,
and the two impenetrable divine armors, and the two quivers with inexhaustible arrows,
and both swords, clear as the sun and adorned with gold:
all this has been honorably deposited in the teacher's house.

children.text: sa tvam āyudham ādāya kṣipram āvraja lakṣmaṇa ||
