children.translated_text: So take the weapons and return quickly, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>."
He, resolved on forest-dwelling, took leave of the friends
and of the guru of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s>s, and took up the excellent weapons.
The son of <s>Sumitrā</s> showed to <s>Rāma</s>, tiger among kings,
all those divine weapons, honored and adorned with garlands and ornaments.

children.text: tam uvācātmavān rāmaḥ prītyā lakṣmaṇam āgatam
children.translated_text: Self-possessed <s>Rāma</s> spoke with affection to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, who had come:

children.text: kāle tvam āgataḥ saumya kāṅkṣite mama lakṣmaṇa ||
children.translated_text: "Gentle <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, you have come at the very time I desired.

children.text: ahaṃ pradātum icchāmi yad idaṃ māmakaṃ dhanam
children.translated_text: I wish to give away this wealth of mine
together with you, scorcher of foes, to Brahmins and ascetics.
The best twice-born men dwell here with firm devotion toward their teachers;

children.text: teṣām api ca me bhūyaḥ sarveṣāṃ copajīvinām ||
children.translated_text: for them too, and for all my dependents, let there be more from me.

children.text: vasiṣṭhaputraṃ tu suyajñam āryaṃ tvam ānayāśu pravaraṃ dvijānām
children.translated_text: Bring quickly noble <s>Suyajña</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s son, the foremost of Brahmins;

children.text: abhiprayāsyāmi vanaṃ samastān abhyarcya śiṣṭān aparān dvijātīn ||
children.translated_text: I shall go to the forest after honoring all the worthy ones and the other twice-born men."

children.text: tataḥ śāsanam ājñāya bhrātuḥ śubhataraṃ priyam
children.translated_text: Then, learning his brother's very auspicious and dear command,
he went and swiftly entered <s>Suyajña</s>'s dwelling.
Having bowed to that Brahmin, who was in the fire-sanctuary, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> said:
"Friend, come; see the house of him who performs difficult deeds."

children.text: tataḥ saṃdhyām upāsyāśu gatvā saumitriṇā saha
children.translated_text: Then, quickly completing his twilight worship, he went with the son of <s>Sumitrā</s>

children.text: juṣṭaṃ tat prāviśal lakṣmyā ramyaṃ rāmaniveśanam ||
children.translated_text: and entered <s>Rāma</s>'s charming dwelling, graced with prosperity.

children.text: tam āgataṃ vedavidaṃ prāñjaliḥ sītayā saha
children.translated_text: With folded hands, together with <s>Sītā</s>,
<s>Rāghava</s> approached the arrived <s>Suyajña</s>, knower of the Veda, like a worshipped fire.
With chief golden armlets and fine earrings,
with gems strung on gold threads, and also with bracelets and bangles,

children.text: anyaiś ca ratnair bahubhiḥ kākutsthaḥ pratyapūjayat
children.translated_text: and with many other jewels, <s>Kākutstha</s> honored <s>Suyajña</s>.
Then <s>Rāma</s>, prompted by <s>Sītā</s>, said to him:

children.text: hāraṃ ca hemasūtraṃ ca bhāryāyai saumya hāraya
children.translated_text: "Gentle friend, have this necklace and gold chain carried to your wife;

children.text: raśanāṃ cādhunā sītā dātum icchati te sakhe ||
children.translated_text: and now <s>Sītā</s> wishes to give you a girdle, friend.
<s>Vaidehī</s> also wishes to place upon you
an excellent couch with splendid covering, adorned with many jewels.

children.text: nāgaḥ śatruṃjayo nāma mātulo yaṃ dadau mama
children.translated_text: The elephant named <s>Śatruṃjaya</s>, which my maternal uncle gave me,
I give to you with a thousand elephants, best of the twice-born."

children.text: ity uktaḥ sa hi rāmeṇa suyajñaḥ pratigṛhya tat
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Suyajña</s> accepted it
and bestowed auspicious blessings on <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: atha bhrātaram avyagraṃ priyaṃ rāmaḥ priyaṃvadaḥ
children.translated_text: Then dear-speaking <s>Rāma</s> spoke this to his untroubled, beloved brother,
that son of <s>Sumitrā</s>, as <s>Brahmā</s> might speak to the lord of the gods:

children.text: agastyaṃ kauśikaṃ caiva tāv ubhau brāhmaṇottamau
children.translated_text: "<s>Agastya</s> and <s>Kauśika</s>, those two foremost Brahmins,
invite them and honor them with jewels, son of <s>Sumitrā</s>, as crops are honored by waters.

children.text: kausalyāṃ ca ya āśīrbhir bhaktaḥ paryupatiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: And the one who devotedly attends on <s>Kausalyā</s> with blessings,
the teacher of the <s>Taittirīya</s>s, handsome and learned in the Veda:

children.text: tasya yānaṃ ca dāsīś ca saumitre saṃpradāpaya
children.translated_text: give him vehicles and maidservants, son of <s>Sumitrā</s>,

children.text: kauśeyāni ca vastrāṇi yāvat tuṣyati sa dvijaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and silk garments, until that Brahmin is satisfied.
And the charioteer <s>Citraratha</s>, noble, a minister, long resident with us:

children.text: toṣayainaṃ mahārhaiś ca ratnair vastrair dhanais tathā ||
children.translated_text: satisfy him with very precious jewels, garments, and wealth as well.

children.text: śālivāhasahasraṃ ca dve śate bhadrakāṃs tathā
children.translated_text: And prepare a thousand loads of rice and two hundred excellent bulls,
and, for condiments, a thousand cows, son of <s>Sumitrā</s>."

children.text: tataḥ sa puruṣavyāghras tad dhanaṃ lakṣmaṇaḥ svayam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, tiger among men, himself
gave that wealth to the lords among Brahmins as prescribed, like the wealth-giver.
Then he spoke to the dependents standing with voices choked by tears,
after handing over abundant property to each dependent:

children.text: lakṣmaṇasya ca yad veśma gṛhaṃ ca yad idaṃ mama
children.translated_text: "<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s house, and this house of mine,
each one must be kept from being empty until my return."

children.text: ity uktvā duḥkhitaṃ sarvaṃ janaṃ tam upajīvinam
children.translated_text: Having said this to all those grieving dependents,
he said this to the treasurer: "Let the wealth be brought."
Then all his dependents brought all his wealth to him.

children.text: tataḥ sa puruṣavyāghras tad dhanaṃ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Then that tiger among men, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
had that wealth distributed to brāhmaṇas, to children and elders, and to the poor.

children.text: tatrāsīt piṅgalo gārgyas trijaṭo nāma vai dvijaḥ
children.translated_text: There was there a tawny <s>Gārgya</s>, a brāhmaṇa named <s>Trijaṭa</s>;

children.text: ā pañcamāyāḥ kakṣyāyā nainaṃ kaścid avārayat ||
children.translated_text: as far as the fifth courtyard no one stopped him.

children.text: sa rājaputram āsādya trijaṭo vākyam abravīt
children.translated_text: Having approached the prince, <s>Trijaṭa</s> said these words:
"I am poor and have many sons, prince of great fame;

children.text: uñchavṛttir vane nityaṃ pratyavekṣasva mām iti ||
children.translated_text: I live by gleaning in the forest always. Please look upon me."
Then <s>Rāma</s> said to him, with a playful tone:

children.text: gavāṃ sahasram apy ekaṃ na tu viśrāṇitaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: "Even one thousand cows have not yet been given away by me.
As far as you cast your staff, so much you shall obtain."

children.text: sa śāṭīṃ tvaritaḥ kaṭyāṃ saṃbhrāntaḥ pariveṣṭya tām
children.translated_text: Hastily wrapping his cloth around his waist in agitation,
he whirled the staff and hurled it with all his strength, driven by speed.

children.text: uvāca ca tato rāmas taṃ gārgyam abhisāntvayan
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s>, soothing that <s>Gārgya</s>, said to him:

children.text: manyur na khalu kartavyaḥ parihāso hy ayaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: "You must not be angry; this was only my joke."

children.text: tataḥ sabhāryas trijaṭo mahāmunir gavām anīkaṃ pratigṛhya moditaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the great sage <s>Trijaṭa</s>, with his wife, joyfully accepted the herd of cows,
and in return spoke blessings for that great-souled one, blessings that increased fame, strength, affection, and happiness.

children.text: dattvā tu saha vaidehyā brāhmaṇebhyo dhanaṃ bahu
children.translated_text: After giving much wealth, together with <s>Vaidehī</s>, to the brāhmaṇas,

children.text: jagmatuḥ pitaraṃ draṣṭuṃ sītayā saha rāghavau ||
children.translated_text: the two <s>Rāghavas</s> went with <s>Sītā</s> to see their father.
Then, when their weapons, hard to look upon, had been taken up,
the two shone, hung with garlands and wreaths and adorned along with <s>Sītā</s>.
Then the prosperous people climbed onto palaces, mansions,
and the peaks of aerial pavilions, and, sitting there, looked on.

children.text: na hi rathyāḥ sma śakyante gantuṃ bahujanākulāḥ
children.translated_text: For the streets could not be traveled, crowded as they were with many people;

children.text: āruhya tasmāt prāsādān dīnāḥ paśyanti rāghavam ||
children.translated_text: therefore the sorrowing people climbed onto palaces and looked at <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: padātiṃ varjitacchattraṃ rāmaṃ dṛṣṭvā tadā janāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Rāma</s> going on foot, deprived of the royal umbrella,
the people, their minds struck by grief, spoke many kinds of words:

children.text: yaṃ yāntam anuyāti sma caturaṅgabalaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: "He whom a great fourfold army used to follow as he went,

children.text: tam ekaṃ sītayā sārdham anuyāti sma lakṣmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: him only <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> now follows, together with <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: aiśvaryasya rasajñaḥ san kāmināṃ caiva kāmadaḥ
children.translated_text: Though he knows the savor of sovereignty and grants the desires of those who seek them,
he will not make his father false, out of reverence for <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: yā na śakyā purā draṣṭuṃ bhūtair ākāśagair api
children.translated_text: She who formerly could not be seen even by beings moving through the sky,

children.text: tām adya sītāṃ paśyanti rājamārgagatā janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Sītā</s> the people now see going along the royal road.
<s>Sītā</s>, accustomed to cosmetics and fond of red sandal paste,

children.text: varṣam uṣṇaṃ ca śītaṃ ca neṣyaty āśu vivarṇatām ||
children.translated_text: rain, heat, and cold will soon make pale.

children.text: adya nūnaṃ daśarathaḥ sattvam āviśya bhāṣate
children.translated_text: Surely today <s>Daśaratha</s> speaks as one possessed by some being;

children.text: na hi rājā priyaṃ putraṃ vivāsayitum arhati ||
children.translated_text: for the king ought not to banish a beloved son.
How could there be exile even for a son without virtues?

children.text: kiṃ punar yasya loko 'yaṃ jito vṛttena kevalam ||
children.translated_text: How much less for one by whose conduct alone this world has been won.

children.text: ānṛśaṃsyam anukrośaḥ śrutaṃ śīlaṃ damaḥ śamaḥ
children.translated_text: Non-cruelty, compassion, learning, good conduct, restraint, and calm:
these six virtues adorn <s>Rāghava</s>, the best of men.
Therefore, by the injury done to him, the subjects are deeply afflicted,
like aquatic creatures in summer from the dwindling of the water.

children.text: pīḍayā pīḍitaṃ sarvaṃ jagad asya jagatpateḥ
children.translated_text: The whole world of this lord of the world is afflicted by his pain,
like a tree laden with flowers and fruit when its root is injured.

children.text: te lakṣmaṇa iva kṣipraṃ sapatnyaḥ sahabāndhavāḥ
children.translated_text: Let us, with wives and kinsmen, quickly follow him as <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> does,
following <s>Rāghava</s> as he goes, wherever he goes.

children.text: udyānāni parityajya kṣetrāṇi ca gṛhāṇi ca
children.translated_text: Leaving gardens, fields, and houses behind,
sharing one sorrow and happiness, let us follow righteous <s>Rāma</s>.
Let <s>Kaikeyī</s> take possession of our homes, with their treasures dug up,
their courtyards ruined, their wealth and grain removed, and their substance wholly taken away,
strewn with dust and abandoned by the household deities,
those houses abandoned by us.

children.text: vanaṃ nagaram evāstu yena gacchati rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Let the forest become the city where <s>Rāghava</s> goes,

children.text: asmābhiś ca parityaktaṃ puraṃ saṃpadyatāṃ vanam ||
children.translated_text: and let the city, abandoned by us, become a forest.
Let all fanged beasts, and the deer and birds from dens and mountain slopes,
come to what has been abandoned by us and leave the places they now inhabit."
<s>Rāma</s> heard such varied words, uttered by many different people;

children.text: śuśrāva rāmaḥ śrutvā ca na vicakre 'sya mānasam ||
children.translated_text: and having heard them, his mind did not waver.
Waiting for those distressed people, while he himself appeared undistressed and almost smiling,

children.text: jagāma rāmaḥ pitaraṃ didṛkṣuḥ pitur nideśaṃ vidhivac cikīrṣuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> went, desiring to see his father and to carry out his father's command properly.

children.text: tat pūrvam aikṣvākasuto mahātmā rāmo gamiṣyan vanam ārtarūpam
children.translated_text: Then, before going to the forest, the great-souled son of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, seeing that sorrowful state,

children.text: vyatiṣṭhata prekṣya tadā sumantraṃ pitur mahātmā pratihāraṇārtham ||
children.translated_text: stood looking at <s>Sumantra</s>, so that he might be announced to his father.

children.text: pitur nideśena tu dharmavatsalo vanapraveśe kṛtabuddhiniścayaḥ
children.translated_text: By his father's command, loving <s>dharma</s>, with his decision firmly made to enter the forest,

children.text: sa rāghavaḥ prekṣya sumantram abravīn nivedayasvāgamanaṃ nṛpāya me ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Rāghava</s> looked at <s>Sumantra</s> and said, "Announce my arrival to the king."
The charioteer, sent by <s>Rāma</s>, quickly, his senses clouded by anguish,

children.text: praviśya nṛpatiṃ sūto niḥśvasantaṃ dadarśa ha ||
children.translated_text: entered and saw the king sighing.
Seeing him, greatly wise yet with mind utterly distraught,
grieving only for <s>Rāma</s>, the charioteer approached with joined palms.

children.text: ayaṃ sa puruṣavyāghra dvāri tiṣṭhati te sutaḥ
children.translated_text: "This son of yours, tiger among men, is standing at your door,
after giving wealth to the brāhmaṇas and to all his dependents.

children.text: sa tvā paśyatu bhadraṃ te rāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ
children.translated_text: May <s>Rāma</s> of true valor see you; welfare to you.

children.text: sarvān suhṛda āpṛcchya tvām idānīṃ didṛkṣate ||
children.translated_text: Having taken leave of all his friends, he now wishes to see you."
He will go to the great forest; look at him, lord of the earth,

children.text: vṛtaṃ rājaguṇaiḥ sarvair ādityam iva raśmibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: endowed with all royal virtues, like the sun with its rays.
He, a speaker of truth, righteous in spirit, like the ocean in depth,

children.text: ākāśa iva niṣpaṅko narendraḥ pratyuvāca tam ||
children.translated_text: stainless as the sky, the lord of men answered him.

children.text: sumantrānaya me dārān ye kecid iha māmakāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sumantra</s>, bring to me my wives, whoever of mine are here;

children.text: dāraiḥ parivṛtaḥ sarvair draṣṭum icchāmi rāghavam ||
children.translated_text: surrounded by all my wives, I wish to see <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: so 'ntaḥpuram atītyaiva striyas tā vākyam abravīt
children.translated_text: He, just after passing into the inner apartments, said this word to the women:

children.text: āryo hvayati vo rājā gamyatāṃ tatra māciram ||
children.translated_text: The noble king summons you; go there without delay.

children.text: evam uktāḥ striyaḥ sarvāḥ sumantreṇa nṛpājñayā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Sumantra</s> at the king's command, all the women

children.text: pracakramus tad bhavanaṃ bhartur ājñāya śāsanam ||
children.translated_text: set out for that palace, having learned their husband's order.
Those six hundred and fifty women, with copper-red eyes,
then surrounded <s>Kausalyā</s> and slowly went, firm in their vows.
When his wives had arrived, the lord of the earth looked upon them,

children.text: uvāca rājā taṃ sūtaṃ sumantrānaya me sutam ||
children.translated_text: and the king said to that charioteer, <s>Sumantra</s>, bring me my son.

children.text: sa sūto rāmam ādāya lakṣmaṇaṃ maithilīṃ tadā
children.translated_text: Then that charioteer, taking <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and <s>Maithilī</s>,
went swiftly toward the presence of the lord of the earth.

children.text: sa rājā putram āyāntaṃ dṛṣṭvā dūrāt kṛtāñjalim
children.translated_text: Seeing his son coming from afar with joined palms,
that king, afflicted and surrounded by the women, sprang quickly from his seat.
The lord of the people ran swiftly toward <s>Rāma</s> when he saw him,

children.text: tam asaṃprāpya duḥkhārtaḥ papāta bhuvi mūrchitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but, not reaching him, he fell unconscious on the ground, stricken with grief.

children.text: taṃ rāmo 'bhyapatat kṣipraṃ lakṣmaṇaś ca mahārathaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> quickly rushed toward him, and so did the great warrior <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: visaṃjñam iva duḥkhena saśokaṃ nṛpatiṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: toward the king who was as if senseless with grief and filled with sorrow at that time.
A cry of a thousand women arose in the king's palace,
suddenly crying, Ah, ah, <s>Rāma</s>!, mingled with the sound of ornaments.

children.text: taṃ pariṣvajya bāhubhyāṃ tāv ubhau rāmalakṣmaṇau
children.translated_text: Then those two, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, embraced him with their arms,
and, weeping, placed him on a couch together with <s>Sītā</s>.
Then, after a moment, <s>Rāma</s> addressed the lord of the earth,
who had regained consciousness and was overwhelmed by an ocean of grief, standing with joined palms:

children.text: āpṛcche tvāṃ mahārāja sarveṣām īśvaro 'si naḥ
children.translated_text: I take leave of you, great king; you are the lord of us all.

children.text: prasthitaṃ daṇḍakāraṇyaṃ paśya tvaṃ kuśalena mām ||
children.translated_text: See me as I set out for the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest, safe and well.

children.text: lakṣmaṇaṃ cānujānīhi sītā cānveti māṃ vanam
children.translated_text: And give permission to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>; <s>Sītā</s> too follows me to the forest.

children.text: kāraṇair bahubhis tathyair vāryamāṇau na cecchataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Though restrained by many sound reasons, these two do not wish to stay.

children.text: anujānīhi sarvān naḥ śokam utsṛjya mānada
children.translated_text: Give permission to all of us, giver of honor, putting aside your grief,

children.text: lakṣmaṇaṃ māṃ ca sītāṃ ca prajāpatir iva prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, to me, and to <s>Sītā</s>, as <s>Prajāpati</s> does to his creatures.
While <s>Rāghava</s>, calm and waiting for the lord of the earth's permission,
stood ready for forest-dwelling, the king looked at him and spoke:
O <s>Rāghava</s>, I have been deluded by the giving of boons to <s>Kaikeyī</s>.

children.text: ayodhyāyās tvam evādya bhava rājā nigṛhya mām ||
children.translated_text: Today you yourself become king of <s>Ayodhyā</s>, after restraining me.

children.text: evam ukto nṛpatinā rāmo dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the king, <s>Rāma</s>, best of those who uphold <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty),
skilled in speech, replied to his father with joined palms:
May you, lord of kings, be ruler of the earth for a thousand years.

children.text: ahaṃ tv araṇye vatsyāmi na me kāryaṃ tvayānṛtam ||
children.translated_text: But I shall dwell in the forest; I have no need for you to be false.
For your welfare, growth, and return again, dear father,
go unharmed, undisturbed, on a path free from danger on every side.

children.text: adya tv idānīṃ rajanīṃ putra mā gaccha sarvathā
children.translated_text: But today, now, my son, do not go this night in any way.

children.text: mātaraṃ māṃ ca saṃpaśyan vasemām adya śarvarīm
children.translated_text: Seeing your mother and me, stay for this night today.
Satisfied with every pleasure, you may set out tomorrow morning.

children.text: atha rāmas tathā śrutvā pitur ārtasya bhāṣitam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s>, having heard such speech from his afflicted father,

children.text: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā dīno vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: spoke these humble words together with his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:

children.text: prāpsyāmi yān adya guṇān ko me śvastān pradāsyati
children.translated_text: The goods that I would obtain today, who will give them to me tomorrow?
Therefore I choose departure itself over all pleasures.
This earth, with its kingdom, its people, and its abundance of wealth and grain,
has been relinquished by me; let it be given to <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: apagacchatu te duḥkhaṃ mā bhūr bāṣpapariplutaḥ
children.translated_text: Let your sorrow depart; do not be flooded with tears.

children.text: na hi kṣubhyati durdharṣaḥ samudraḥ saritāṃ patiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the unconquerable ocean, lord of rivers, is not disturbed.

children.text: naivāhaṃ rājyam icchāmi na sukhaṃ na ca maithilīm
children.translated_text: I desire neither the kingdom, nor pleasure, nor even <s>Maithilī</s>;

children.text: tvām ahaṃ satyam icchāmi nānṛtaṃ puruṣarṣabha ||
children.translated_text: I desire you to be truthful, not false, bull among men.

children.text: puraṃ ca rāṣṭraṃ ca mahī ca kevalā mayā nisṛṣṭā bharatāya dīyatām
children.translated_text: The city, the kingdom, and the whole earth have been relinquished by me; let them be given to <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: ahaṃ nideśaṃ bhavato 'nupālayan vanaṃ gamiṣyāmi cirāya sevitum ||
children.translated_text: Obeying your command, I shall go to the forest to dwell there for a long time.

children.text: mayā nisṛṣṭāṃ bharato mahīm imāṃ saśailakhaṇḍāṃ sapurāṃ sakānanām
children.translated_text: Let <s>Bharata</s> alone rule this earth relinquished by me, with its mountain tracts, its cities, and its forests,

children.text: śivāṃ susīmām anuśāstu kevalaṃ tvayā yad uktaṃ nṛpate yathāstu tat ||
children.translated_text: auspicious and well-bounded; let it be just as you have said, O king.

children.text: na me tathā pārthiva dhīyate mano mahatsu kāmeṣu na cātmanaḥ priye
children.translated_text: My mind, O king, is not set so much on great pleasures, nor on what is dear to myself,

children.text: yathā nideśe tava śiṣṭasaṃmate vyapaitu duḥkhaṃ tava matkṛte 'nagha ||
children.translated_text: as on your command, approved by the disciplined; let your grief on my account pass away, sinless one.

children.text: tad adya naivānagha rājyam avyayaṃ na sarvakāmān na sukhaṃ na maithilīm
children.translated_text: Therefore today, sinless one, I would choose neither imperishable kingship, nor all pleasures, nor happiness, nor <s>Maithilī</s>,

children.text: na jīvitaṃ tvām anṛtena yojayan vṛṇīya satyaṃ vratam astu te tathā ||
children.translated_text: nor life, if it would join you with falsehood; let truth be your vow accordingly.

children.text: phalāni mūlāni ca bhakṣayan vane girīṃś ca paśyan saritaḥ sarāṃsi ca
children.translated_text: Eating fruits and roots in the forest, and seeing mountains, rivers, and lakes,

children.text: vanaṃ praviśyaiva vicitrapādapaṃ sukhī bhaviṣyāmi tavāstu nirvṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall enter the forest with its varied trees and be happy; may contentment be yours.
Then the <s>Aikṣvāka</s> king, pained there by his promise,
sighing deeply with tears, said this again and again:
Charioteer, let an army, well filled with jewels and with the four kinds of forces,
be quickly arranged to accompany <s>Rāghava</s>.
Let well-adorned courtesans, and merchants of great wealth,
beautify the prince's army, well extended on its march.

children.text: ye cainam upajīvanti ramate yaiś ca vīryataḥ
children.translated_text: And those who live by him, and those with whom he takes delight in strength,

children.text: teṣāṃ bahuvidhaṃ dattvā tān apy atra niyojaya ||
children.translated_text: give them many kinds of gifts and appoint them also here.

children.text: nighnan mṛgān kuñjarāṃś ca pibaṃś cāraṇyakaṃ madhu
children.translated_text: Killing deer and elephants, drinking forest honey,

children.text: nadīś ca vividhāḥ paśyan na rājyaṃ saṃsmariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: and seeing many different rivers, he will not remember the kingdom.

children.text: dhānyakośaś ca yaḥ kaścid dhanakośaś ca māmakaḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever grain-treasury and money-treasury belong to me,

children.text: tau rāmam anugacchetāṃ vasantaṃ nirjane vane ||
children.translated_text: let both follow <s>Rāma</s> as he dwells in the lonely forest.
Sacrificing in holy places, distributing fitting gifts,

children.text: ṛṣibhiś ca samāgamya pravatsyati sukhaṃ vane ||
children.translated_text: and meeting with seers, he will dwell happily in the forest.
And mighty-armed <s>Bharata</s> shall rule <s>Ayodhyā</s>;

children.text: sarvakāmaiḥ punaḥ śrīmān rāmaḥ saṃsādhyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: but let illustrious <s>Rāma</s> be provided again with every pleasure.

children.text: evaṃ bruvati kākutsthe kaikeyyā bhayam āgatam
children.translated_text: As <s>Kākutstha</s> was speaking thus, fear came upon <s>Kaikeyī</s>;

children.text: mukhaṃ cāpy agamacchoṣaṃ svaraś cāpi nyarudhyata ||
children.translated_text: her face also became dry, and her voice too was choked.

children.text: sā viṣaṇṇā ca saṃtrastā kaikeyī vākyam abravīt
children.translated_text: Distressed and terrified, <s>Kaikeyī</s> spoke these words:

children.text: rājyaṃ gatajanaṃ sādho pītamaṇḍāṃ surām iva
children.translated_text: O good man, <s>Bharata</s> will not accept a kingdom emptied of people, like liquor whose clear essence has been drunk away,
most tasteless and empty.
As shameless <s>Kaikeyī</s> spoke this exceedingly cruel speech,
king <s>Daśaratha</s> addressed the wide-eyed woman with these words:

children.text: vahantaṃ kiṃ tudasi māṃ niyujya dhuri māhite ||
children.translated_text: Why do you torment me, already harnessed by you and bearing the burden, O hostile one?

children.text: kaikeyī dviguṇaṃ kruddhā rājānam idam abravīt
children.translated_text: Twice as angry, <s>Kaikeyī</s> said this to the king:

children.text: tavaiva vaṃśe sagaro jyeṣṭhaṃ putram upārudhat
children.translated_text: In your own lineage, <s>Sagara</s> confined his eldest son,

children.text: asamañja iti khyātaṃ tathāyaṃ gantum arhati ||
children.translated_text: known as <s>Asamañja</s>; likewise this one deserves to go.

children.text: evam ukto dhig ity eva rājā daśaratho 'bravīt
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, king <s>Daśaratha</s> said only, 'Shame!'

children.text: vrīḍitaś ca janaḥ sarvaḥ sā ca tan nāvabudhyata ||
children.translated_text: All the people were embarrassed, but she did not understand that.

children.text: tatra vṛddho mahāmātraḥ siddhārtho nāma nāmataḥ
children.translated_text: There an aged chief minister, pure and highly honored by the king,

children.text: śucir bahumato rājñaḥ kaikeyīm idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: named <s>Siddhārtha</s>, said this to <s>Kaikeyī</s>:

children.text: asamañjo gṛhītvā tu krīḍitaḥ pathi dārakān
children.translated_text: <s>Asamañja</s>, taking children playing in the road,

children.text: sarayvāḥ prakṣipann apsu ramate tena durmatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: would throw them into the waters of the <s>Sarayū</s>; that evil-minded man delighted in that.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā nāgarāḥ sarve kruddhā rājānam abruvan
children.translated_text: Seeing him, all the townspeople, angry, said to the king:
Choose either <s>Asamañja</s> alone, O increaser of the realm, or us.

children.text: tān uvāca tato rājā kiṃnimittam idaṃ bhayam
children.translated_text: Then the king said to them, 'What is the cause of this fear?'

children.text: tāś cāpi rājñā saṃpṛṣṭā vākyaṃ prakṛtayo 'bruvan ||
children.translated_text: And when questioned by the king, those subjects spoke these words:

children.text: krīḍitas tv eṣa naḥ putrān bālān udbhrāntacetanaḥ
children.translated_text: This one, deranged in mind, takes our young sons at play

children.text: sarayvāṃ prakṣipan maurkhyād atulāṃ prītim aśnute ||
children.translated_text: and, throwing them into the <s>Sarayū</s> out of folly, gains incomparable pleasure.

children.text: sa tāsāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā prakṛtīnāṃ narādhipa
children.translated_text: Hearing the words of those subjects, O ruler of men,
he abandoned that harmful son, wishing to do what was pleasing to them.

children.text: ity evam atyajad rājā sagaro vai sudhārmikaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus indeed did righteous king <s>Sagara</s> abandon him.

children.text: rāmaḥ kim akarot pāpaṃ yenaivam uparudhyate ||
children.translated_text: What sin has <s>Rāma</s> committed, that he should be confined in this way?
Hearing <s>Siddhārtha</s>'s words, the king, his voice still more exhausted,
spoke this to <s>Kaikeyī</s> in a voice stricken by grief:

children.text: anuvrajiṣyāmy aham adya rāmaṃ rājyaṃ parityajya sukhaṃ dhanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Today I shall follow <s>Rāma</s>, abandoning kingdom, comfort, and wealth.

children.text: sahaiva rājñā bharatena ca tvaṃ yathāsukhaṃ bhuṅkṣva cirāya rājyam ||
children.translated_text: Together with king <s>Bharata</s>, enjoy the kingdom as you please for a long time.
Then, hearing the chief minister's words, <s>Rāma</s>
answered <s>Daśaratha</s> with a statement, knowing proper conduct and speaking humbly:

children.text: tyaktabhogasya me rājan vane vanyena jīvataḥ
children.translated_text: O king, when I have given up enjoyments and live in the forest on forest fare,
what need have I of a retinue, having renounced every attachment?

children.text: yo hi dattvā dvipaśreṣṭhaṃ kakṣyāyāṃ kurute manaḥ
children.translated_text: For one who, after giving away the finest elephant, sets his mind on the girth-strap,
what use is affection for a rope when he is abandoning the best of elephants?

children.text: tathā mama satāṃ śreṣṭha kiṃ dhvajinyā jagatpate
children.translated_text: So too for me, best of the good, lord of the world, what use is an army?
I release them all; let them bring me bark garments alone.
Bring me both a digging tool and a basket as I go,

children.text: caturdaśa vane vāsaṃ varṣāṇi vasato mama ||
children.translated_text: for I am to dwell fourteen years in the forest.

children.text: atha cīrāṇi kaikeyī svayam āhṛtya rāghavam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kaikeyī</s> herself brought bark garments to <s>Rāghava</s>
and, shameless before the crowd of people, said, 'Put these on.'

children.text: sa cīre puruṣavyāghraḥ kaikeyyāḥ pratigṛhya te
children.translated_text: That tiger among men, receiving those bark garments from <s>Kaikeyī</s>,
cast off his fine clothing and put on the garments of ascetics.

children.text: lakṣmaṇaś cāpi tatraiva vihāya vasane śubhe
children.translated_text: And <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> too, right there, gave up his fine garments

children.text: tāpasāc chādane caiva jagrāha pitur agrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and took ascetic coverings in his father's presence.
Then <s>Sītā</s>, dressed in silk, looked at the bark garment

children.text: samīkṣya cīraṃ saṃtrastā pṛṣatī vāgurām iva ||
children.translated_text: meant for her own clothing, terrified like a doe at a snare.
Ashamed, as it were, and sorrowful, she took it,
and said this to her husband, who resembled the king of the <s>Gandharvas</s>:

children.text: kathaṃ nu cīraṃ badhnanti munayo vanavāsinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: How do forest-dwelling sages tie on a bark garment?

children.text: kṛtvā kaṇṭhe ca sā cīram ekam ādāya pāṇinā
children.translated_text: Placing one bark garment at her neck and taking another in her hand,

children.text: tasthau hy akuśalā tatra vrīḍitā janakātmajā ||
children.translated_text: the daughter of <s>Janaka</s> stood there, unskilled and embarrassed.

children.text: tasyās tat kṣipram āgamya rāmo dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: Quickly coming to her, <s>Rāma</s>, best of those who uphold <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty),
himself tied <s>Sītā</s>'s bark garment over her silk.
When she, though possessing a protector, was wearing bark like one without a protector,

children.text: pracukrośa janaḥ sarvo dhik tvāṃ daśarathaṃ tv iti ||
children.translated_text: all the people cried out, 'Shame on you, <s>Daśaratha</s>!'

children.text: sa niḥśvasyoṣṇam aikṣvākas tāṃ bhāryām idam abravīt
children.translated_text: The <s>Aikṣvāka</s> king sighed hotly and said this to that wife:

children.text: kaikeyi kuśacīreṇa na sītā gantum arhati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kaikeyī</s>, <s>Sītā</s> does not deserve to go in a garment of kuśa-bark.

children.text: nanu paryāptam etat te pāpe rāmavivāsanam
children.translated_text: Is this not enough for you, wicked woman, the exile of <s>Rāma</s>?

children.text: kim ebhiḥ kṛpaṇair bhūyaḥ pātakair api te kṛtaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Why have these further wretched sins also been committed by you?

children.text: evaṃ bruvantaṃ pitaraṃ rāmaḥ samprasthito vanam
children.translated_text: As his father was speaking thus, <s>Rāma</s>, setting out for the forest,
he spoke these words to him as he sat with his head bowed down:

children.text: iyaṃ dhārmika kausalyā mama mātā yaśasvinī
children.translated_text: This renowned <s>Kausalyā</s>, O righteous one, is my mother;

children.text: vṛddhā cākṣudraśīlā ca na ca tvāṃ devagarhite ||
children.translated_text: she is aged and of noble character, and she does not reproach you, O lord.
Deprived of me, O giver of boons, and plunged into an ocean of grief,
she has never before seen such misfortune; you ought to comfort her further.

children.text: imāṃ mahendropamajātagarbhiṇīṃ tathā vidhātuṃ jananīṃ mamārhasi
children.translated_text: You ought so to provide for my mother, whose womb bore one like <s>Mahendra</s>,

children.text: yathā vanasthe mayi śokakarśitā na jīvitaṃ nyasya yamakṣayaṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: that, when I am dwelling in the forest, she, wasted by grief, may not lay down her life and go to <s>Yama</s>'s abode.

children.text: rāmasya tu vacaḥ śrutvā muniveṣadharaṃ ca tam
children.translated_text: But when the king heard <s>Rāma</s>'s words, and saw him
wearing the dress of a sage, together with his wives, he lost consciousness.
Burning with grief, he did not look back at <s>Rāghava</s>,
nor, his mind distressed, did he answer him after looking at him.

children.text: sa muhūrtam ivāsaṃjño duḥkhitaś ca mahīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: For a moment the lord of the earth was as if unconscious and afflicted;
the great-armed king lamented, thinking only of <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: manye khalu mayā pūrvaṃ vivatsā bahavaḥ kṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Surely, I think, many living creatures were formerly made childless by me,

children.text: prāṇino hiṃsitā vāpi tasmād idam upasthitam ||
children.translated_text: or living beings were harmed; therefore this has come upon me.

children.text: na tv evānāgate kāle dehāc cyavati jīvitam
children.translated_text: Yet life does not fall from the body before the appointed time;

children.text: kaikeyyā kliśyamānasya mṛtyur mama na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: though I am tormented by <s>Kaikeyī</s>, death does not come to me.
For I see my son standing before me, shining like fire,
having cast off fine garments and taken on an ascetic covering.

children.text: ekasyāḥ khalu kaikeyyāḥ kṛte 'yaṃ kliśyate janaḥ
children.translated_text: For the sake of <s>Kaikeyī</s> alone, this people is suffering,

children.text: svārthe prayatamānāyāḥ saṃśritya nikṛtiṃ tv imām ||
children.translated_text: while she pursues her own interest and has resorted to this deceit.

children.text: evam uktvā tu vacanaṃ bāṣpeṇa pihitendriyaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken these words, his senses choked by tears,

children.text: rāmeti sakṛd evoktvā vyāhartuṃ na śaśāka ha ||
children.translated_text: after saying only once, '<s>Rāma</s>,' he could not utter anything more.

children.text: saṃjñāṃ tu pratilabhyaiva muhūrtāt sa mahīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after a moment, the lord of the earth regained consciousness,
and with both eyes filled with tears he spoke these words to <s>Sumantra</s>:

children.text: aupavāhyaṃ rathaṃ yuktvā tvam āyāhi hayottamaiḥ
children.translated_text: Yoke the carriage-chariot with the best horses and come here.
Convey this greatly blessed man beyond the boundary of the kingdom from here.

children.text: evaṃ manye guṇavatāṃ guṇānāṃ phalam ucyate
children.translated_text: This, I think, is said to be the fruit of the virtues of the virtuous:

children.text: pitrā mātrā ca yat sādhur vīro nirvāsyate vanam ||
children.translated_text: that a righteous hero is banished to the forest by his father and mother.
Having received the king's command, swift-moving <s>Sumantra</s>
yoked the chariot adorned with horses and came there.
With joined palms, the charioteer announced to the prince
that the gold-adorned chariot had been yoked with the finest steeds.
The king quickly summoned the man occupied with the treasury,
and, knowing place and time, spoke a firm command, pure in every respect:

children.text: vāsāṃsi ca mahārhāṇi bhūṣaṇāni varāṇi ca
children.translated_text: Bring costly garments and excellent ornaments,

children.text: varṣāṇy etāni saṃkhyāya vaidehyāḥ kṣipram ānaya ||
children.translated_text: quickly for <s>Vaidehī</s>, reckoning these years.

children.text: narendreṇaivam uktas tu gatvā kośagṛhaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the lord of men, he went then to the treasury,

children.text: prāyacchat sarvam āhṛtya sītāyai kṣipram eva tat ||
children.translated_text: and, bringing everything, quickly gave it to <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: sā sujātā sujātāni vaidehī prasthitā vanam
children.translated_text: The well-born <s>Vaidehī</s>, setting out for the forest,
adorned her well-formed limbs with those varied ornaments.
Finely adorned, <s>Vaidehī</s> made that house shine,
like the radiance of the radiant sun in the sky at the time of its rising.

children.text: tāṃ bhujābhyāṃ pariṣvajya śvaśrūr vacanam abravīt
children.translated_text: Her mother-in-law embraced her with both arms and spoke these words,
sniffing the head of <s>Maithilī</s>, who was not acting pitiably:
In this whole world, women, though constantly honored by their beloved ones, are untrue;
when their husband has fallen into misfortune, they do not stand by him.

children.text: sa tvayā nāvamantavyaḥ putraḥ pravrājito mama
children.translated_text: But this son of mine, sent into exile, must not be disrespected by you.

children.text: tava daivatam astv eṣa nirdhanaḥ sadhano 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: Whether poor or wealthy, let him be your deity.
Understanding that speech of hers, joined with <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty) and purpose, <s>Sītā</s>
stood facing her mother-in-law with joined palms and said this:

children.text: kariṣye sarvam evāham āryā yad anuśāsti mām
children.translated_text: I shall do everything, noble lady, just as you instruct me.

children.text: abhijñāsmi yathā bhartur vartitavyaṃ śrutaṃ ca me ||
children.translated_text: I know how one should conduct oneself toward a husband, and I have heard it taught.
You should not liken me, noble lady, to a wicked woman.

children.text: dharmād vicalituṃ nāham alaṃ candrād iva prabhā ||
children.translated_text: I am not able to turn away from <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty), any more than moonlight from the moon.

children.text: nātantrī vādyate vīṇā nācakro vartate rathaḥ
children.translated_text: A vīṇā is not played without strings; a chariot does not move without wheels;

children.text: nāpatiḥ sukham edhate yā syād api śatātmajā ||
children.translated_text: and a woman without a husband does not prosper happily, even if she should have a hundred sons.

children.text: mitaṃ dadāti hi pitā mitaṃ mātā mitaṃ sutaḥ
children.translated_text: A father gives in measure, a mother gives in measure, a son gives in measure;

children.text: amitasya hi dātāraṃ bhartāraṃ kā na pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: what woman would not honor a husband, the giver of what is immeasurable?
Therefore, being such as I am, noble and learned in the higher and lower teachings of <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty),

children.text: ārye kim avamanyeyaṃ strīṇāṃ bhartā hi daivatam ||
children.translated_text: why, noble lady, should I disrespect him? For a husband is the deity of women.
Hearing <s>Sītā</s>'s words, which went to her heart, <s>Kausalyā</s>,
of pure nature, suddenly shed tears born of sorrow and joy.
Then <s>Rāma</s>, most learned in supreme <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty), approached with joined palms
his mother, who was highly honored among the mothers, and spoke these words:

children.text: amba mā duḥkhitā bhūs tvaṃ paśya tvaṃ pitaraṃ mama
children.translated_text: Mother, do not be sorrowful. Look after my father.

children.text: kṣayo hi vanavāsasya kṣipram eva bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: For the end of my forest dwelling will come very quickly.

children.text: suptāyās te gamiṣyanti navavarṣāṇi pañca ca
children.translated_text: While you are as if asleep, nine years and five more will pass for you;

children.text: sā samagram iha prāptaṃ māṃ drakṣyasi suhṛdvṛtam ||
children.translated_text: then you will see me returned here safe and whole, surrounded by my friends.

children.text: etāvad abhinītārtham uktvā sa jananīṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: After saying to his mother this much speech with its meaning clearly expressed,
he looked around and saw his mothers, three hundred and fifty in number.

children.text: tāś cāpi sa tathaivārtā mātṝn daśarathātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: To those mothers too, who were afflicted in the same way, the son of <s>Daśaratha</s>
spoke this righteous word with joined palms:

children.text: saṃvāsāt paruṣaṃ kiṃcid ajñānād vāpi yat kṛtam
children.translated_text: Whatever harsh thing has been done by me through living together, or through ignorance,

children.text: tan me samanujānīta sarvāś cāmantrayāmi vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: forgive that of me. I take leave of you all.

children.text: jajñe 'tha tāsāṃ saṃnādaḥ krauñcīnām iva niḥsvanaḥ
children.translated_text: Then a clamor arose among those women, like the cry of female krauñca birds,
the wives of the lord of men, while <s>Rāghava</s> was speaking thus.
The house of <s>Daśaratha</s>, which formerly had been like the roar of muraja and paṇava drums and thunderclouds,
then became confused with lamentation and wailing, fallen into calamity and filled with great sorrow.

children.text: atha rāmaś ca sītā ca lakṣmaṇaś ca kṛtāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Sītā</s>, and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, with joined palms,
approached the king, saluted him, and, miserable, circumambulated him.

children.text: taṃ cāpi samanujñāpya dharmajñaḥ sītayā saha
children.translated_text: Having also taken leave of him, the knower of <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty), together with <s>Sītā</s>,
<s>Rāghava</s>, bewildered by grief, bowed to his mother.
Immediately after his brother, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> bowed to <s>Kausalyā</s>,

children.text: atha mātuḥ sumitrāyā jagrāha caraṇau punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and then again clasped the feet of his mother <s>Sumitrā</s>.

children.text: taṃ vandamānaṃ rudatī mātā saumitrim abravīt
children.translated_text: As he was bowing, his weeping mother spoke to <s>Saumitri</s>,
wishing his welfare, after smelling the head of mighty-armed <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
You have been appointed for forest-dwelling, deeply attached to your dear kin;

children.text: rāme pramādaṃ mā kārṣīḥ putra bhrātari gacchati ||
children.translated_text: do not be careless toward <s>Rāma</s>, my son, while your brother is going.

children.text: vyasanī vā samṛddho vā gatir eṣa tavānagha
children.translated_text: Whether he is afflicted or prosperous, he is your refuge, sinless one;

children.text: eṣa loke satāṃ dharmo yaj jyeṣṭhavaśago bhavet ||
children.translated_text: this is the <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty) of the good in the world: that one should be obedient to the eldest.

children.text: idaṃ hi vṛttam ucitaṃ kulasyāsya sanātanam
children.translated_text: For this conduct is fitting, the ancient custom of this family:

children.text: dānaṃ dīkṣā ca yajñeṣu tanutyāgo mṛdheṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: giving, consecration in sacrifices, and the abandonment of the body in battles.

children.text: rāmaṃ daśarathaṃ viddhi māṃ viddhi janakātmajām
children.translated_text: Know <s>Rāma</s> as <s>Daśaratha</s>; know the daughter of <s>Janaka</s> as me;

children.text: ayodhyām aṭavīṃ viddhi gaccha tāta yathāsukham ||
children.translated_text: know the forest as <s>Ayodhyā</s>; go, dear child, as happily as you can.

children.text: tataḥ sumantraḥ kākutsthaṃ prāñjalir vākyam abravīt
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sumantra</s>, with joined palms, spoke these words to <s>Kākutstha</s>,

children.text: vinīto vinayajñaś ca mātalir vāsavaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: humble and knowing humility, as <s>Mātali</s> would speak to <s>Vāsava</s>:

children.text: ratham āroha bhadraṃ te rājaputra mahāyaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Mount the chariot; may it be well with you, prince of great fame.

children.text: kṣipraṃ tvāṃ prāpayiṣyāmi yatra māṃ rāma vakṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: I shall quickly convey you, <s>Rāma</s>, wherever you tell me.

children.text: caturdaśa hi varṣāṇi vastavyāni vane tvayā
children.translated_text: For fourteen years you must dwell in the forest;
those years, which you have been ordered by the queen to undertake, must now be begun.

children.text: taṃ rathaṃ sūryasaṃkāśaṃ sītā hṛṣṭena cetasā
children.translated_text: With delighted mind <s>Sītā</s>, whose form was lovely,
mounted that chariot, shining like the sun, after adorning herself.
Likewise, the various weapons and the armors for the two brothers
were set on the platform of the chariot, together with the hide shields and leather guards.
Seeing them mounted, with <s>Sītā</s> as the third, he boldly urged on
the approved horses, equal to the wind in speed; <s>Sumantra</s> drove them forward.
When <s>Rāghava</s> had set out for the great forest for a long time,

children.text: babhūva nagare mūrchā balamūrchā janasya ca ||
children.translated_text: a faintness came over the city, and weakness over the people.
The city was then agitated and confused, with rutting elephants enraged,
filled with the neighing sounds of horses, a great uproar.
Then that city, with children and elders, greatly afflicted,
ran after <s>Rāma</s> alone, as one scorched by heat runs to water.
Hanging along his sides and behind him, their faces turned toward him,
all of them, their faces full of tears, spoke to him, overcome by intense sorrow:

children.text: saṃyaccha vājināṃ raśmīn sūta yāhi śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: Restrain the reins of the horses, charioteer; go slowly, slowly.

children.text: mukhaṃ drakṣyāmi rāmasya durdarśaṃ no bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Let us look upon <s>Rāma</s>'s face; soon it will be hard for us to see.
Surely the heart of <s>Rāma</s>'s mother is iron, without doubt,

children.text: yad devagarbhapratime vanaṃ yāti na bhidyate ||
children.translated_text: since, when one like the offspring of a god goes to the forest, it does not split.
<s>Vaidehī</s> has indeed fulfilled her duty, following her husband like a shadow;

children.text: na jahāti ratā dharme merum arkaprabhā yathā ||
children.translated_text: delighting in <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty), she does not leave him, as sunlight does not leave <s>Meru</s>.
Ah, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, you have attained your aim, since constantly
you will serve your dear-speaking brother, who is like a god.

children.text: mahaty eṣā hi te siddhir eṣa cābhyudayo mahān
children.translated_text: This is a great accomplishment for you; this is a great rise to prosperity;

children.text: eṣa svargasya mārgaś ca yad enam anugacchasi
children.translated_text: and this is the path to heaven, that you follow him.

children.text: evaṃ vadantas te soḍhuṃ na śekur bāṣpam āgatam ||
children.translated_text: Speaking thus, they could not hold back the tears that came.

children.text: atha rājā vṛtaḥ strībhir dīnābhir dīnacetanaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the king, surrounded by miserable women and miserable in mind,

children.text: nirjagāma priyaṃ putraṃ drakṣyāmīti bruvan gṛhāt ||
children.translated_text: went out from the house, saying, 'I will see my dear son.'
And ahead the loud sound of weeping women was heard,

children.text: yathā nādaḥ kareṇūnāṃ baddhe mahati kuñjare ||
children.translated_text: like the cry of female elephants when a great elephant has been bound.

children.text: pitā ca rājā kākutsthaḥ śrīmān sannas tadā babhau
children.translated_text: And the father, the splendid king <s>Kākutstha</s>, then appeared spent,
like the full moon at its season eclipsed by a planet.
Then a cry of tumult arose behind <s>Rāma</s>,
from the men, when they saw the king sinking, deeply afflicted with sorrow.

children.text: hā rāmeti janāḥ kecid rāmamāteti cāpare
children.translated_text: Some people cried, 'Alas, <s>Rāma</s>!' and others, 'O mother of <s>Rāma</s>!'
and the prosperous inner palace too wailed and lamented.
Looking back, <s>Rāma</s> saw the king,
despondent and bewildered in mind, and also his mother following along the road.
Bound tight by the noose of <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty), he did not look openly.
Seeing those two going on foot, though worthy of vehicles, undeserving of suffering, and accustomed to comfort,
he urged the charioteer, 'Go quickly.'

children.text: na hi tat puruṣavyāghro duḥkhadaṃ darśanaṃ pituḥ
children.translated_text: For that tiger among men was not able to endure

children.text: mātuś ca sahituṃ śaktas totrārdita iva dvipaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the sorrow-giving sight of his father and mother, like an elephant tormented by a goad.

children.text: tathā rudantīṃ kausalyāṃ rathaṃ tam anudhāvatīm
children.translated_text: Then, seeing <s>Kausalyā</s> weeping as she ran after that chariot,

children.text: krośantīṃ rāma rāmeti hā sīte lakṣmaṇeti ca
children.translated_text: crying '<s>Rāma</s>, <s>Rāma</s>!' and 'Alas, <s>Sītā</s>! <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>!',

children.text: asakṛt praikṣata tadā nṛtyantīm iva mātaram ||
children.translated_text: he looked again and again at his mother then, as if she were dancing.

children.text: tiṣṭheti rājā cukrośa yāhi yāhīti rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Stop!' the king cried; 'Go, go!' said <s>Rāghava</s>.
<s>Sumantra</s>'s mind was as if caught between the two wheels.
Even if reproached, you will say to the king, 'I did not hear,'

children.text: ciraṃ duḥkhasya pāpiṣṭham iti rāmas tam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: for lingering is most wicked in a time of sorrow; so <s>Rāma</s> said to him.

children.text: rāmasya sa vacaḥ kurvann anujñāpya ca taṃ janam
children.translated_text: Doing <s>Rāma</s>'s bidding and taking leave of that crowd,
even as they were departing, the charioteer quickly urged on the horses.

children.text: nyavartata jano rājño rāmaṃ kṛtvā pradakṣiṇam
children.translated_text: The king's people turned back, after circumambulating <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: manasāpy aśruvegaiś ca na nyavartata mānuṣam ||
children.translated_text: But in their hearts, and with floods of tears, that human throng did not turn back.

children.text: yam icchet punar āyāntaṃ nainaṃ dūram anuvrajet
children.translated_text: One whom one wishes to see returning again should not be followed far.

children.text: ity amātyā mahārājam ūcur daśarathaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus the ministers spoke these words to great king <s>Daśaratha</s>.
Hearing their words, well endowed with every good quality, his limbs sweating and his form dejected,

children.text: niśamya rājā kṛpaṇaḥ sabhāryo vyavasthitas taṃ sutam īkṣamāṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the pitiable king, together with his wives, remained standing, gazing at that son.
But as that tiger among men went out with joined palms,

children.text: ārtaśabdo hi saṃjajñe strīṇām antaḥpure mahān ||
children.translated_text: a great cry of distress arose among the women in the inner palace.
For this orphaned, weak, suffering people,

children.text: yo gatiḥ śaraṇaṃ cāsīt sa nāthaḥ kva nu gacchati ||
children.translated_text: he who was their course and refuge: where now is that protector going?
Even when reviled he does not grow angry, avoiding things that provoke anger;

children.text: kruddhān prasādayan sarvān samaduḥkhaḥ kva gacchati ||
children.translated_text: appeasing all who are angry and sharing every sorrow, where is he going?
As the greatly radiant one behaves toward <s>Kausalyā</s> as toward his mother,

children.text: tathā yo vartate 'smāsu mahātmā kva nu gacchati ||
children.translated_text: so that great-souled one behaves toward us also; where indeed is he going?
Driven to the forest by the king who was being tormented by <s>Kaikeyī</s>,

children.text: paritrātā janasyāsya jagataḥ kva nu gacchati ||
children.translated_text: where indeed is the protector of these people, of the world, going?
Ah, the king is senseless: the beloved of the living world,
<s>Rāma</s>, righteous and true to his vow, he is sending away to dwell in the forest.

children.text: iti sarvā mahiṣyas tā vivatsā iva dhenavaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus all those queens, like cows bereft of their calves,

children.text: ruruduś caiva duḥkhārtāḥ sasvaraṃ ca vicukruśuḥ ||
children.translated_text: wept, afflicted with grief, and cried out aloud.

children.text: sa tam antaḥpure ghoram ārtaśabdaṃ mahīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that terrible cry of distress in the inner palace,
the lord of the earth, scorched by grief for his son, became deeply sorrowful.
The <s>agnihotra</s> fire offerings were not offered, and the sun disappeared;

children.text: vyasṛjan kavalān nāgā gāvo vatsān na pāyayan ||
children.translated_text: elephants dropped their mouthfuls, and cows did not suckle their calves.
<s>Triśaṅku</s> and <s>Lohitāṅga</s>, and even <s>Bṛhaspati</s> and <s>Budha</s>,

children.text: dāruṇāḥ somam abhyetya grahāḥ sarve vyavasthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all the dreadful planets drew near the moon and stood there.
The constellations lost their rays, and the planets lost their splendor;

children.text: viśākhāś ca sadhūmāś ca nabhasi pracakāśire ||
children.translated_text: the stars of <s>Viśākhā</s>, smoky in appearance, shone in the sky.

children.text: akasmān nāgaraḥ sarvo jano dainyam upāgamat
children.translated_text: Suddenly all the city people fell into wretchedness;

children.text: āhāre vā vihāre vā na kaścid akaron manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: no one set his mind on food or recreation.
The people on the royal road had faces clouded with tears;

children.text: na hṛṣṭo lakṣyate kaścit sarvaḥ śokaparāyaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: no one was seen happy; everyone was given over to grief.

children.text: na vāti pavanaḥ śīto na śaśī saumyadarśanaḥ
children.translated_text: The wind did not blow cool, nor was the moon pleasant to behold;

children.text: na sūryas tapate lokaṃ sarvaṃ paryākulaṃ jagat ||
children.translated_text: the sun did not warm the world; the whole world was disturbed.

children.text: anarthinaḥ sutāḥ strīṇāṃ bhartāro bhrātaras tathā
children.translated_text: Sons were of no concern to women, nor husbands, nor brothers;
all, abandoning everything, thought only of <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: ye tu rāmasya suhṛdaḥ sarve te mūḍhacetasaḥ
children.translated_text: But all those who were <s>Rāma</s>'s friends were bewildered in mind;

children.text: śokabhāreṇa cākrāntāḥ śayanaṃ na jahus tadā ||
children.translated_text: overwhelmed by the weight of grief, they did not leave their beds then.

children.text: tatas tv ayodhyā rahitā mahātmanā puraṃdareṇeva mahī saparvatā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Ayodhyā</s>, deprived of that great-souled one, like the mountain-bearing earth deprived of <s>Purandara</s>,

children.text: cacāla ghoraṃ bhayabhārapīḍitā sanāgayodhāśvagaṇā nanāda ca ||
children.translated_text: shook terribly, oppressed by the weight of fear, and resounded with its elephants, warriors, horses, and troops.

children.text: yāvat tu niryatas tasya rajorūpam adṛśyata
children.translated_text: So long as the dust-cloud raised by his departure was visible,
so long the best of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s> did not withdraw his own eyes.

children.text: yāvad rājā priyaṃ putraṃ paśyaty atyantadhārmikam
children.translated_text: So long as the king saw his dear, supremely righteous son,
so long his sight of his son seemed to stretch out over the earth.

children.text: na paśyati rajo 'py asya yadā rāmasya bhūmipaḥ
children.translated_text: When the lord of the earth could no longer see even the dust of <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: tadārtaś ca viṣaṇṇaś ca papāta dharaṇītale ||
children.translated_text: then, distressed and despondent, he fell upon the ground.

children.text: tasya dakṣiṇam anvagāt kausalyā bāhum aṅganā
children.translated_text: <s>Kausalyā</s>, the lady, went to support his right arm,
and <s>Kaikeyī</s>, dear to <s>Bharata</s>, went to his left side.

children.text: tāṃ nayena ca sampanno dharmeṇa vinayena ca
children.translated_text: Endowed with justice, with <s>dharma</s>, and with humility,
the king, looking at <s>Kaikeyī</s> with senses shaken, spoke to her:

children.text: kaikeyi mā mamāṅgāni sprākṣīs tvaṃ duṣṭacāriṇī
children.translated_text: <s>Kaikeyī</s>, do not touch my limbs, you woman of wicked conduct.

children.text: na hi tvāṃ draṣṭum icchāmi na bhāryā na ca bāndhavī ||
children.translated_text: For I do not wish to see you; you are neither wife nor kinswoman.

children.text: ye ca tvām upajīvanti nāhaṃ teṣāṃ na te mama
children.translated_text: And those who depend on you: I am not theirs, nor are they mine.

children.text: kevalārthaparāṃ hi tvāṃ tyaktadharmāṃ tyajāmy aham ||
children.translated_text: For you, intent solely on gain and having abandoned <s>dharma</s>, I now abandon.

children.text: agṛhṇāṃ yac ca te pāṇim agniṃ paryaṇayaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: That I took your hand, and that I led you around the fire,

children.text: anujānāmi tat sarvam asmiṃl loke paratra ca ||
children.translated_text: all that I release, in this world and in the next.

children.text: bharataś cet pratītaḥ syād rājyaṃ prāpyedam avyayam
children.translated_text: And if <s>Bharata</s>, pleased after obtaining this imperishable kingdom,

children.text: yan me sa dadyāt pitrarthaṃ mā mā tad dattam āgamat ||
children.translated_text: should give me something for his father's sake, may that gift not come to me.
Then, having raised up that lord of men, who was covered with dust,
queen <s>Kausalyā</s>, wasted by grief, turned back at that time.

children.text: hatveva brāhmaṇaṃ kāmāt spṛṣṭvāgnim iva pāṇinā
children.translated_text: As if he had killed a Brahmin out of desire, or touched fire with his hand,
the righteous one was filled with remorse, thinking of his ascetic son.
Turning back again and again, sinking down on the chariot-road,
the king's form did not shine, like that of the sun when eclipsed.

children.text: vilalāpa ca duḥkhārtaḥ priyaṃ putram anusmaran
children.translated_text: Afflicted by grief, he lamented, remembering his dear son;
and realizing that his son had reached the edge of the city, he then said:

children.text: vāhanānāṃ ca mukhyānāṃ vahatāṃ taṃ mamātmajam
children.translated_text: Of the finest vehicles that were carrying my own son,

children.text: padāni pathi dṛśyante sa mahātmā na dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: the tracks are seen on the road, but that great-souled one is not seen.

children.text: sa nūnaṃ kvacid evādya vṛkṣamūlam upāśritaḥ
children.translated_text: Surely today, somewhere, he has taken shelter at the foot of a tree;

children.text: kāṣṭhaṃ vā yadi vāśmānam upadhāya śayiṣyate ||
children.translated_text: laying down a piece of wood, or perhaps a stone, he will sleep.
And, pitiable and covered with dust, he will rise from the ground,
sighing like a bull-elephant from among cow-elephants.
Surely forest-dwelling men will see long-armed <s>Rāma</s>,
lord of the world, rising and going through the forest like one without a protector.

children.text: sakāmā bhava kaikeyi vidhavā rājyam āvasa
children.translated_text: Have your desire fulfilled, <s>Kaikeyī</s>; live in the kingdom as a widow.

children.text: na hi taṃ puruṣavyāghraṃ vinā jīvitum utsahe ||
children.translated_text: For I cannot bear to live without that tiger among men.
Lamenting in this way, the king, surrounded by crowds of people,
entered the excellent city like one overtaken by an evil omen.
He saw it with its crossroads and inner houses empty, its shops and shrines closed,
weary, weak, afflicted with grief, and its great roads no longer crowded.

children.text: tām avekṣya purīṃ sarvāṃ rāmam evānucintayan
children.translated_text: Seeing that whole city, thinking only of <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: vilapan prāviśad rājā gṛhaṃ sūrya ivāmbudam ||
children.translated_text: the king entered the palace weeping, like the sun entering a cloud.
The house was like an unshaken great lake whose serpent had been carried off by <s>Suparṇa</s>,

children.text: rāmeṇa rahitaṃ veśma vaidehyā lakṣmaṇena ca ||
children.translated_text: bereft of <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Vaidehī</s>, and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: kausalyāyā gṛhaṃ śīghraṃ rāmamātur nayantu mām
children.translated_text: Take me quickly to the house of <s>Kausalyā</s>, <s>Rāma</s>'s mother,
and as the king spoke thus, the doorkeepers led him there.
Then, when he had entered <s>Kausalyā</s>'s dwelling there,
even after climbing onto the bed, his mind became agitated.

children.text: tac ca dṛṣṭvā mahārājo bhujam udyamya vīryavān
children.translated_text: Seeing that, the mighty great king raised his arm

children.text: uccaiḥ svareṇa cukrośa hā rāghava jahāsi mām ||
children.translated_text: and cried out in a loud voice, 'Ah, <s>Rāghava</s>, you are abandoning me!'

children.text: sukhitā bata taṃ kālaṃ jīviṣyanti narottamāḥ
children.translated_text: Happy indeed will be those best of men who live until that time,

children.text: pariṣvajanto ye rāmaṃ drakṣyanti punar āgatam ||
children.translated_text: who will see <s>Rāma</s> returned and will embrace him.

children.text: na tvāṃ paśyāmi kausalye sādhu māṃ pāṇinā spṛśa
children.translated_text: I do not see you, <s>Kausalyā</s>; gently touch me with your hand.

children.text: rāmaṃ me 'nugatā dṛṣṭir adyāpi na nivartate ||
children.translated_text: My sight has followed <s>Rāma</s>, and even now it does not turn back.

children.text: taṃ rāmam evānuvicintayantaṃ samīkṣya devī śayane narendram
children.translated_text: Seeing the lord of men on the bed, thinking only of that <s>Rāma</s>,
the queen sat down beside him, still more distressed in appearance, and, sighing, lamented painfully.

children.text: tataḥ samīkṣya śayane sannaṃ śokena pārthivam
children.translated_text: Then, seeing the king lying on the bed, sunk down by grief,
<s>Kausalyā</s>, afflicted by sorrow for her son, spoke to that lord of the earth.
O tiger among men, after casting out <s>Rāghava</s> like a two-tongued serpent its poison,
<s>Kaikeyī</s> will move about like a snake that has shed its skin.
Having exiled <s>Rāma</s>, fortunate, her wish gained and self-possessed,

children.text: trāsayiṣyati māṃ bhūyo duṣṭāhir iva veśmani ||
children.translated_text: that wicked woman will frighten me again like a poisonous snake in the house.

children.text: atha sma nagare rāmaś caran bhaikṣaṃ gṛhe vaset
children.translated_text: If <s>Rāma</s> were now to live in the city, going for alms from house to house,

children.text: kāmakāro varaṃ dātum api dāsaṃ mamātmajam ||
children.translated_text: it would be better, even if my son had to be given away as a slave.

children.text: pātayitvā tu kaikeyyā rāmaṃ sthānād yatheṣṭataḥ
children.translated_text: But after <s>Kaikeyī</s> made <s>Rāma</s> fall from his station as she wished,
he has been assigned as a portion for the rākṣasas, like an oblation by one who has kindled the sacred fire on a festival day.
The hero, with the gait of a lordly elephant, great-armed and bearing a bow,
is surely entering the forest with his wife and with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
For those who have never known suffering, abandoned for forest dwelling

children.text: tyaktānāṃ vanavāsāya kā nv avasthā bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: by you with <s>Kaikeyī</s>'s approval, what condition will there be?
Those pitiable young ones, deprived of jewels and banished in their prime,
how will they live, making fruits and roots their food?

children.text: apīdānīṃ sa kālaḥ syān mama śokakṣayaḥ śivaḥ
children.translated_text: Would that this auspicious time might now come, the end of my grief,

children.text: sabhāryaṃ yat saha bhrātrā paśyeyam iha rāghavam ||
children.translated_text: when I might see <s>Rāghava</s> here with his wife and with his brother.
When will <s>Ayodhyā</s>, hearing that the two heroes have arrived,
be glorious, its people joyful, adorned with raised banners and garlands?
When, seeing the two tigers among men returned from the forest,

children.text: nandiṣyati purī hṛṣṭā samudra iva parvaṇi ||
children.translated_text: will the delighted city rejoice like the ocean on a festival day?
When will the great-armed hero enter the city of <s>Ayodhyā</s>,

children.text: puraskṛtya rathe sītāṃ vṛṣabho govadhūm iva ||
children.translated_text: placing <s>Sītā</s> before him on the chariot, like a bull with his cow?
When will thousands of living beings on the royal road
scatter parched grain over my two sons, those subduers of foes, as they enter?

children.text: kadā sumanasaḥ kanyā dvijātīnāṃ phalāni ca
children.translated_text: When will joyful maidens, offering flowers and fruits to the twice-born,
make a circumambulation of the city?
When will he, mature in understanding and age, bright as moonlight,

children.text: abhyupaiṣyati dharmajñas trivarṣa iva māṃ lalan ||
children.translated_text: knower of <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty), approach me caressingly, as when he was three years old?

children.text: niḥsaṃśayaṃ mayā manye purā vīra kadaryayā
children.translated_text: Without doubt, I think, O hero, in a former life I was cruel,

children.text: pātu kāmeṣu vatseṣu mātṝṇāṃ śātitāḥ stanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the breasts of mothers were cut off by me while their calves wished to drink.

children.text: sāhaṃ gaur iva siṃhena vivatsā vatsalā kṛtā
children.translated_text: I, loving as a cow with her calf, have been made calf-less, like a cow by a lion,
by <s>Kaikeyī</s>, O tiger among men, forcibly, like a cow with a young calf.

children.text: na hi tāvad guṇair juṣṭaṃ sarvaśāstraviśāradam
children.translated_text: For, as a woman with one son, I cannot bear to live without that son,

children.text: ekaputrā vinā putram ahaṃ jīvitum utsahe ||
children.translated_text: endowed with virtues and skilled in all the śāstras.

children.text: na hi me jīvite kiṃcit sāmarthyam iha kalpyate
children.translated_text: No capacity for life at all is imagined for me here
while I do not see my dear son, great-armed and very strong.

children.text: ayaṃ hi māṃ dīpayate samutthitas tanūjaśokaprabhavo hutāśanaḥ
children.translated_text: This fire, arisen from grief for my son, has flared up and burns me,

children.text: mahīm imāṃ raśmibhir uttamaprabho yathā nidāghe bhagavān divākaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: as the blessed sun of highest radiance burns this earth with his rays in the hot season.

children.text: vilapantīṃ tathā tāṃ tu kausalyāṃ pramadottamām
children.translated_text: To <s>Kausalyā</s>, that best of women, lamenting in that way,

children.text: idaṃ dharme sthitā dharmyaṃ sumitrā vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sumitrā</s>, established in <s>dharma</s> (righteous conduct), spoke these righteous words.

children.text: tavārye sadguṇair yuktaḥ putraḥ sa puruṣottamaḥ
children.translated_text: Noble lady, your son, that best of men, is endowed with good qualities.

children.text: kiṃ te vilapitenaivaṃ kṛpaṇaṃ ruditena vā ||
children.translated_text: What use have you for such lamentation or for wretched weeping?

children.text: yas tavārye gataḥ putras tyaktvā rājyaṃ mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: Noble lady, your mighty son has gone, leaving the kingdom,
making his great-souled father, foremost of truth-speakers, righteous.

children.text: śiṣṭair ācarite samyak śaśvat pretya phalodaye
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> stands in <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty), rightly practiced by the virtuous

children.text: rāmo dharme sthitaḥ śreṣṭho na sa śocyaḥ kadācana ||
children.translated_text: and always yielding fruit after death; he is never to be mourned.
And sinless <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> follows an excellent course toward him.
He is compassionate toward all beings; he is a gain for that great-souled one.

children.text: araṇyavāse yad duḥkhaṃ jānatī vai sukhocitā
children.translated_text: Though she knows well the suffering in forest dwelling, she who is accustomed to comfort...
<s>Vaidehī</s> follows your righteous son.

children.text: kīrtibhūtāṃ patākāṃ yo loke bhrāmayati prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: He is the lord who makes a banner, which has become fame, move through the world.
Devoted to self-control, truth, and vows, what has your son not attained?

children.text: vyaktaṃ rāmasya vijñāya śaucaṃ māhātmyam uttamam
children.translated_text: Clearly recognizing <s>Rāma</s>'s purity and supreme greatness,

children.text: na gātram aṃśubhiḥ sūryaḥ saṃtāpayitum arhati ||
children.translated_text: the sun is not fit to scorch his body with its rays.
At all times, auspicious and issuing from the forests,
a pleasant wind, tempering cold and heat, will serve <s>Rāghava</s>.
As he sleeps at night, the moon, embracing the blameless one like a father,
will delight him, touching him with cool rays.

children.text: dadau cāstrāṇi divyāni yasmai brahmā mahaujase
children.translated_text: To that mighty one <s>Brahmā</s> gave divine weapons,
after seeing the son of <s>Timidhvaja</s>, lord of the Dānavas, slain in battle.

children.text: pṛthivyā saha vaidehyā śriyā ca puruṣarṣabhaḥ
children.translated_text: Together with the earth, with <s>Vaidehī</s>, and with royal fortune, that bull among men,
<s>Rāma</s>, will soon be consecrated together with these three.

children.text: duḥkhajaṃ visṛjanty asraṃ niṣkrāmantam udīkṣya yam
children.translated_text: The tear born of sorrow, which you shed as you watched him going away,
you will soon release from your eyes as water born of joy.
Seeing that son, together with his friends, greeting you respectfully,
you will soon shed tears of joy, like a rain-cloud streak in the rainy season.

children.text: putras te varadaḥ kṣipram ayodhyāṃ punar āgataḥ
children.translated_text: Your boon-giving son, having soon returned to <s>Ayodhyā</s>,
will press your feet with his soft, full hands.

children.text: niśamya tal lakṣmaṇamātṛvākyaṃ rāmasya mātur naradevapatnyāḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing those words of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s mother to <s>Rāma</s>'s mother, the wife of the king of men,

children.text: sadyaḥ śarīre vinanāśa śokaḥ śaradgato megha ivālpatoyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: grief at once vanished from her body like a cloud in autumn with little water.
The people, attached to great-souled <s>Rāma</s>, whose valor was true,
followed him as he set out for dwelling in the forest.

children.text: nivartite 'pi ca balāt suhṛdvarge ca rājani
children.translated_text: Even when the circle of friends and the king had been forcibly turned back,
they did not turn back, but followed <s>Rāma</s>'s chariot.
For to the men dwelling in <s>Ayodhyā</s>, that greatly famous one,
endowed with virtues, was dear like the full moon.

children.text: sa yācyamānaḥ kākutsthaḥ svābhiḥ prakṛtibhis tadā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kākutstha</s>, though entreated by his own subjects,
made his father truthful and proceeded only to the forest.
Looking at them affectionately, as if drinking them in with his eyes,

children.text: uvāca rāmaḥ snehena tāḥ prajāḥ svāḥ prajā iva ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> spoke with affection to those subjects, as to his own children.

children.text: yā prītir bahumānaś ca mayy ayodhyānivāsinām
children.translated_text: Whatever affection and great respect the residents of <s>Ayodhyā</s> have for me,
let that be placed especially in <s>Bharata</s>, for the sake of what is dear to me.
For he is of auspicious conduct and increases <s>Kaikeyī</s>'s joy.

children.text: kariṣyati yathāvad vaḥ priyāṇi ca hitāni ca ||
children.translated_text: He will duly do for you what is pleasing and beneficial.
Though young in age, he is mature in knowledge, gentle, and endowed with courage and virtue.

children.text: anurūpaḥ sa vo bhartā bhaviṣyati bhayāpahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He will be a fitting lord for you, removing fear.

children.text: sa hi rājaguṇair yukto yuvarājaḥ samīkṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: For he is endowed with royal virtues and has been chosen as crown prince.

children.text: api cāpi mayā śiṣṭaiḥ kāryaṃ vo bhartṛśāsanam ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, as instructed by me and by the elders, you must carry out the ruler's command.

children.text: na ca tapyed yathā cāsau vanavāsaṃ gate mayi
children.translated_text: And, while I have gone to dwell in the forest, you must act so that
the great king does not grieve, if you wish to do what is dear to me.
In whatever way <s>Dāśarathi</s> remained established in <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty),

children.text: tathā tathā prakṛtayo rāmaṃ patim akāmayan ||
children.translated_text: in that same way the subjects desired <s>Rāma</s> as their lord.

children.text: bāṣpeṇa pihitaṃ dīnaṃ rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, together with <s>Saumitri</s>, bound the wretched people, their faces covered with tears,

children.text: cakarṣeva guṇair baddhvā janaṃ punar ivāsanam ||
children.translated_text: as if with his virtues, and seemed to draw them back again.

children.text: te dvijās trividhaṃ vṛddhā jñānena vayasaujasā
children.translated_text: Those twice-born men were elders in three ways, by knowledge, age, and vigor;
their heads trembling with age, they spoke these words from afar:

children.text: vahanto javanā rāmaṃ bho bho jātyās turaṃgamāḥ
children.translated_text: O swift horses of noble breed, carrying <s>Rāma</s>, ho, ho!

children.text: nivartadhvaṃ na gantavyaṃ hitā bhavata bhartari
children.translated_text: Turn back. You must not go. Be well-disposed toward your master.

children.text: upavāhyas tu vo bhartā nāpavāhyaḥ purād vanam ||
children.translated_text: Your master is to be carried nearby, not carried away from the city to the forest.

children.text: evam ārtapralāpāṃs tān vṛddhān pralapato dvijān
children.translated_text: Seeing those old twice-born men lamenting such pained laments,

children.text: avekṣya sahasā rāmo rathād avatatāra ha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> suddenly descended from the chariot.
Then, with <s>Sītā</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, he went on foot alone,
<s>Rāma</s>, devoted to the forest, placing his steps close together.

children.text: dvijātīṃs tu padātīṃs tān rāmaś cāritravatsalaḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Rāma</s>, loving right conduct, could not, with compassionate eyes,

children.text: na śaśāka ghṛṇācakṣuḥ parimoktuṃ rathena saḥ ||
children.translated_text: leave those twice-born men who were on foot by going in the chariot.

children.text: gacchantam eva taṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmaṃ saṃbhrāntamānasāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Rāma</s> continuing on his way, their minds agitated,

children.text: ūcuḥ paramasaṃtaptā rāmaṃ vākyam idaṃ dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the deeply afflicted twice-born men spoke this sentence to <s>Rāma</s>:

children.text: brāhmaṇyaṃ kṛtsnam etat tvāṃ brahmaṇyam anugacchati
children.translated_text: All this Brahminhood follows you, who are devoted to Brahmins;
these sacred fires too, mounted on the shoulders of the twice-born, follow you.
Look at these umbrellas of ours, won from the <s>Vājapeya</s> sacrifice,
following behind like swans when the waters have passed away.
For you, who have obtained no parasol and are scorched by the sun's rays,

children.text: ebhiś chāyāṃ kariṣyāmaḥ svaiś chattrair vājapeyikaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: we shall make shade with these own umbrellas of ours from the <s>Vājapeya</s>.

children.text: yā hi naḥ satataṃ buddhir vedamantrānusāriṇī
children.translated_text: That understanding of ours, which always follows the Vedic mantras,
has, for your sake, dear child, been made to follow dwelling in the forest.

children.text: hṛdayeṣv avatiṣṭhante vedā ye naḥ paraṃ dhanam
children.translated_text: The Vedas, which are our highest wealth, remain in our hearts;

children.text: vatsyanty api gṛheṣv eva dārāś cāritrarakṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and our wives, protected by good conduct, will dwell at home alone.

children.text: na punar niścayaḥ kāryas tvadgatau sukṛtā matiḥ
children.translated_text: No further resolve need be made; our mind is firmly settled on going with you.

children.text: tvayi dharmavyapekṣe tu kiṃ syād dharmam avekṣitum ||
children.translated_text: But when you are intent on <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty), what else could there be for us to regard as <s>dharma</s>?
Asked by us, turn back, O restrained in conduct, by these heads
whose hairs are white as swans and which are dust-covered from falling on the earth.

children.text: bahūnāṃ vitatā yajñā dvijānāṃ ya ihāgatāḥ
children.translated_text: Many extended sacrifices of the twice-born men who have come here

children.text: teṣāṃ samāptir āyattā tava vatsa nivartane ||
children.translated_text: depend for their completion, dear child, on your turning back.
For beings, moving and unmoving, are devoted...

children.text: yācamāneṣu teṣu tvaṃ bhaktiṃ bhakteṣu darśaya ||
children.translated_text: As they beg you, show affection toward those devoted to you.
Unable to follow you, with their roots violently torn up,
the lofty trees, driven by the force of the wind, seemed to cry out.
The birds too, motionless, without eating or moving about, settled in one place on the trees,
implored him who had compassion for all beings.
As those twice-born birds cried out in this way for his return,
there the <s>Tamasā</s> was seen as if barring <s>Rāghava</s>'s way.

children.text: tatas tu tamasātīraṃ ramyam āśritya rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāghava</s>, taking refuge on the pleasant bank of the <s>Tamasā</s>,

children.text: sītām udvīkṣya saumitrim idaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: looked at <s>Sītā</s> and <s>Saumitri</s> and spoke these words:

children.text: iyam adya niśā pūrvā saumitre prasthitā vanam
children.translated_text: This, <s>Saumitri</s>, is now the first night since we have set out for the forest.

children.text: vanavāsasya bhadraṃ te sa notkaṇṭhitum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: May it be well with you; you should not give way to longing during our forest dwelling.
See the empty forests, seeming to weep on every side,
with the deer and birds gone to their proper lairs and hidden away.

children.text: adyāyodhyā tu nagarī rājadhānī pitur mama
children.translated_text: Today <s>Ayodhyā</s>, my father's royal capital,

children.text: sastrīpuṃsā gatān asmāñ śociṣyati na saṃśayaḥ ||
