children.translated_text: together with its women and men, will surely grieve for us who have gone.

children.text: bharataḥ khalu dharmātmā pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca me
children.translated_text: But righteous <s>Bharata</s> will surely console my father and my mother
with words joined to <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty), wealth, and desire.
Thinking again and again of <s>Bharata</s>'s kindness,
I do not grieve for my father or even for my mother, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: tvayā kāryaṃ naravyāghra mām anuvrajatā kṛtam
children.translated_text: O tiger among men, in following me you have done what had to be done.
For help must be sought for the sake of protecting <s>Vaidehī</s>.

children.text: adbhir eva tu saumitre vatsyāmy adya niśām imām
children.translated_text: With water alone, <s>Saumitri</s>, I shall spend this night tonight;

children.text: etaddhi rocate mahyaṃ vanye 'pi vividhe sati ||
children.translated_text: for this is what pleases me, even though there is various forest fare.

children.text: evam uktvā tu saumitraṃ sumantram api rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken to <s>Saumitri</s>, <s>Rāghava</s> also said to <s>Sumantra</s>,

children.text: apramattas tvam aśveṣu bhava saumyety uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: "Good sir, be vigilant with the horses."
When the sun had gone down, <s>Sumantra</s> restrained the horses,
gave them abundant fodder, and remained close at hand.

children.text: upāsyatu śivāṃ saṃdhyāṃ dṛṣṭvā rātrim upasthitām
children.translated_text: After performing the auspicious twilight observance and seeing that night had arrived,

children.text: rāmasya śayanaṃ cakre sūtaḥ saumitriṇā saha ||
children.translated_text: the charioteer, together with <s>Saumitri</s>, made <s>Rāma</s>'s bed.

children.text: tāṃ śayyāṃ tamasātīre vīkṣya vṛkṣadalaiḥ kṛtām
children.translated_text: Seeing that bed on the bank of the <s>Tamasā</s>, made from leaves of trees,

children.text: rāmaḥ saumitriṇā sārdhaṃ sabhāryaḥ saṃviveśa ha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, together with <s>Saumitri</s> and with his wife, lay down.

children.text: sabhāryaṃ saṃprasuptaṃ taṃ bhrātaraṃ vīkṣya lakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing his brother asleep with his wife, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>
told the charioteer of <s>Rāma</s>'s many virtues.

children.text: jāgrato hy eva tāṃ rātriṃ saumitrer udito raviḥ
children.translated_text: While <s>Saumitri</s> stayed awake through that very night, the sun rose
upon the charioteer on the bank of the <s>Tamasā</s>, as he spoke of <s>Rāma</s>'s virtues.
At a distance from the <s>Tamasā</s>, whose bank was crowded with herds of cattle,

children.text: avasat tatra tāṃ rātriṃ rāmaḥ prakṛtibhiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> spent that night there together with the people.

children.text: utthāya tu mahātejāḥ prakṛtīs tā niśāmya ca
children.translated_text: Then the greatly radiant one rose and, observing those people,
<s>Rāma</s> spoke to his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, marked with auspicious signs:
Look now, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, at these people, concerned for us, indifferent even to their own homes,
sleeping at the roots of trees.
From the resolve these citizens are keeping in not turning back from us,

children.text: api prāṇān asiṣyanti na tu tyakṣyanti niścayam ||
children.translated_text: they may even give up their lives, but they will not abandon their decision.

children.text: yāvad eva tu saṃsuptās tāvad eva vayaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: Therefore, while they are still asleep, let us quickly
mount the chariot and go along a road free from fear.
Otherwise the inhabitants of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>'s city, devoted to me,
would again from now on sleep, taking shelter at the roots of trees.

children.text: paurā hy ātmakṛtād duḥkhād vipramocyā nṛpātmajaiḥ
children.translated_text: For princes should free the citizens from suffering caused by themselves;

children.text: na tu khalv ātmanā yojyā duḥkhena puravāsinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: they should certainly not yoke the city-dwellers to suffering on their own account.

children.text: abravīl lakṣmaṇo rāmaṃ sākṣād dharmam iva sthitam
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> said to <s>Rāma</s>, who stood like <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) embodied:

children.text: rocate me mahāprājña kṣipram āruhyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "This pleases me, greatly wise one. Let the chariot be mounted at once."

children.text: sūtas tataḥ saṃtvaritaḥ syandanaṃ tair hayottamaiḥ
children.translated_text: Then the charioteer, in haste, yoked the carriage with those excellent horses
and, with joined palms, reported it to <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: mohanārthaṃ tu paurāṇāṃ sūtaṃ rāmo 'bravīd vacaḥ
children.translated_text: To bewilder the citizens, <s>Rāma</s> spoke these words to the charioteer:

children.text: udaṅmukhaḥ prayāhi tvaṃ ratham āsthāya sārathe ||
children.translated_text: "Facing north, drive the chariot, O charioteer.

children.text: muhūrtaṃ tvaritaṃ gatvā nirvartaya rathaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: After going quickly for a moment, turn the chariot back again.

children.text: yathā na vidyuḥ paurā māṃ tathā kuru samāhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Act attentively so that the citizens do not know where I am."

children.text: rāmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā tathā cakre sa sārathiḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Rāma</s>'s words, that charioteer did just so,
and, returning, presented the carriage to <s>Rāma</s>.
Mounting that carriage, <s>Rāghava</s>, together with his retinue,
crossed the swift-flowing <s>Tamasā</s> river, troubled with whirlpools.

children.text: sa saṃtīrya mahābāhuḥ śrīmāñ śivam akaṇṭakam
children.translated_text: Having crossed, the mighty-armed, illustrious one
entered the great road, auspicious, thornless, and safe for those who fear danger.

children.text: prabhātāyāṃ tu śarvaryāṃ paurās te rāghavaṃ vinā
children.translated_text: When the night had brightened into dawn, those citizens, without <s>Rāghava</s>,
became motionless from grief and stunned in mind.
Overwhelmed by tears born of sorrow, looking this way and that,

children.text: ālokam api rāmasya na paśyanti sma duḥkhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the grieving people did not see even a glimpse of <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: tato mārgānusāreṇa gatvā kiṃcit kṣaṇaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, following the road for a short while,
they were overcome by great despondency when the track disappeared.
With the chariot's track lost, those high-minded people turned back,

children.text: kim idaṃ kiṃ kariṣyāmo daivenopahatā iti ||
children.translated_text: saying, "What is this? What shall we do? We have been struck down by fate."
Then, with weary minds, by the very road by which they had come,
they all went to <s>Ayodhyā</s>, the city whose good people were distressed.
As the city-dwellers who had followed <s>Rāma</s> turned back,
the spirits of those downcast people seemed to have gone out of them.

children.text: svaṃ svaṃ nilayam āgamya putradāraiḥ samāvṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Having reached their own homes, surrounded by their sons and wives,
All shed tears, their faces covered with weeping.

children.text: na cāhṛṣyan na cāmodan vaṇijo na prasārayan
children.translated_text: They did not rejoice and took no pleasure; merchants did not display their goods,
wares did not shine, and householders did not cook.

children.text: naṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭvā nābhyanandan vipulaṃ vā dhanāgamam
children.translated_text: Seeing something lost, no one grieved; nor did they rejoice at a great gain of wealth.
Even a mother, having obtained a first-born son, did not rejoice.

children.text: gṛhe gṛhe rudantyaś ca bhartāraṃ gṛham āgatam
children.translated_text: In house after house, women, weeping when their husbands came home,

children.text: vyagarhayanta duḥkhārtā vāgbhis totrair iva dvipān ||
children.translated_text: tormented by sorrow, reviled them with words like goads striking elephants.

children.text: kiṃ nu teṣāṃ gṛhaiḥ kāryaṃ kiṃ dāraiḥ kiṃ dhanena vā
children.translated_text: What use have they for houses? What use for wives, or for wealth?

children.text: putrair vā kiṃ sukhair vāpi ye na paśyanti rāghavam ||
children.translated_text: What use for sons or even pleasures, for those who do not see <s>Rāghava</s>?

children.text: ekaḥ satpuruṣo loke lakṣmaṇaḥ saha sītayā
children.translated_text: In the world <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> alone is a good man, together with <s>Sītā</s>,
since he follows <s>Kākutstha</s>, serving <s>Rāma</s> in the forest.

children.text: āpagāḥ kṛtapuṇyās tāḥ padminyaś ca sarāṃsi ca
children.translated_text: Blessed are those rivers, lotus-ponds, and lakes,

children.text: yeṣu snāsyati kākutstho vigāhya salilaṃ śuci ||
children.translated_text: in whose pure water <s>Kākutstha</s> will plunge and bathe.
Forests with lovely groves will adorn <s>Kākutstha</s>,

children.text: āpagāś ca mahānūpāḥ sānumantaś ca parvatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: as will rivers with broad marshlands and mountains with peaks.

children.text: kānanaṃ vāpi śailaṃ vā yaṃ rāmo 'bhigamiṣyati
children.translated_text: Whatever woodland or mountain <s>Rāma</s> will approach,

children.text: priyātithim iva prāptaṃ nainaṃ śakṣyanty anarcitum ||
children.translated_text: they will not be able to fail to honor him, as one who has arrived as a dear guest.
Bearing clusters of varied flowers and many sprays,

children.text: akāle cāpi mukhyāni puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca
children.translated_text: even out of season, the mountains, from compassion,
will show their finest flowers and fruits to <s>Rāma</s> when he arrives.

children.text: vidarśayanto vividhān bhūyaś citrāṃś ca nirjharān
children.translated_text: Showing various waterfalls, and again others of wonderful beauty,
the trees on the mountain tops will delight <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: yatra rāmo bhayaṃ nātra nāsti tatra parābhavaḥ
children.translated_text: Where <s>Rāma</s> is, there is no fear; there is no defeat there.

children.text: sa hi śūro mahābāhuḥ putro daśarathasya ca ||
children.translated_text: For he is heroic, mighty-armed, and the son of <s>Daśaratha</s>.

children.text: purā bhavati no dūrād anugacchāma rāghavam
children.translated_text: Before he goes far from us, let us follow <s>Rāghava</s>.
The shade of the feet of such a great-souled lord is pleasant.

children.text: sa hi nātho janasyāsya sa gatiḥ sa parāyaṇam ||
children.translated_text: For he is the protector of these people; he is their refuge and their highest goal.

children.text: vayaṃ paricariṣyāmaḥ sītāṃ yūyaṃ tu rāghavam
children.translated_text: We shall attend upon <s>Sītā</s>, while you attend upon <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: iti paurastriyo bhartṝn duḥkhārtās tat tad abruvan ||
children.translated_text: Thus the women of the city, tormented by sorrow, spoke this and that to their husbands.
<s>Rāghava</s> will provide for your welfare and security in the forest,
and <s>Sītā</s> will provide for the welfare and security of these women.
Who indeed would be pleased by this unwelcome dwelling,
unlovely, filled with longing people, and with their minds carried away?

children.text: kaikeyyā yadi ced rājyaṃ syād adharmyam anāthavat
children.translated_text: If the kingdom should belong to <s>Kaikeyī</s>, unrighteous and as if without a protector,

children.text: na hi no jīvitenārthaḥ kutaḥ putraiḥ kuto dhanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: then life has no purpose for us; how much less sons, how much less wealth?

children.text: yayā putraś ca bhartā ca tyaktāv aiśvaryakāraṇāt
children.translated_text: She by whom son and husband alike were abandoned for the sake of sovereignty,

children.text: kaṃ sā parihared anyaṃ kaikeyī kulapāṃsanī ||
children.translated_text: whom else would that <s>Kaikeyī</s>, stain of her family, spare?

children.text: kaikeyyā na vayaṃ rājye bhṛtakā nivasema hi
children.translated_text: We would not live as servants in <s>Kaikeyī</s>'s kingdom

children.text: jīvantyā jātu jīvantyaḥ putrair api śapāmahe ||
children.translated_text: while she lives, so long as we live, even with our sons; by this we swear.
She who pitilessly sends into exile such a son of the lord of kings,

children.text: kas tāṃ prāpya sukhaṃ jīved adharmyāṃ duṣṭacāriṇīm ||
children.translated_text: who, obtaining that unrighteous woman of evil conduct, could live happily?

children.text: na hi pravrajite rāme jīviṣyati mahīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāma</s> has gone forth, the lord of the earth will not live.
When <s>Daśaratha</s> is dead, ruin will clearly follow immediately.
Those whose merit is exhausted and whose fate is very wretched should mix and drink poison,
or follow <s>Rāghava</s>, or else go to oblivion.
<s>Rāma</s> has been falsely exiled, together with his wife and with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: bharate saṃnisṛṣṭāḥ smaḥ saunike paśavo yathā ||
children.translated_text: We have been handed over to <s>Bharata</s> like animals to a slaughterer.

children.text: tās tathā vilapantyas tu nagare nāgarastriyaḥ
children.translated_text: As the city women lamented in that way in the city,
deeply tormented, they cried out as at the coming of the fear of death.

children.text: tathā striyo rāmanimittam āturā yathā sute bhrātari vā vivāsite
children.translated_text: Thus, distressed on account of <s>Rāma</s>, as when a son or brother has been exiled,

children.text: vilapya dīnā rurudur vicetasaḥ sutair hi tāsām adhiko hi so 'bhavat ||
children.translated_text: the women lamented, wretched and senseless, and wept; for to them he was dearer than their sons.
<s>Rāma</s> too, during the remainder of that night,
that tiger among men, went a great distance, remembering his father's command.

children.text: tathaiva gacchatas tasya vyapāyād rajanī śivā
children.translated_text: As he went on in that same way, the auspicious night passed away.

children.text: upāsya sa śivāṃ saṃdhyāṃ viṣayāntaṃ vyagāhata ||
children.translated_text: Having worshiped the auspicious twilight, he entered the edge of the country.

children.text: grāmān vikṛṣṭasīmāṃs tān puṣpitāni vanāni ca
children.translated_text: Seeing villages with their boundaries spread far apart and forests in bloom,

children.text: paśyann atiyayau śīghraṃ śarair iva hayottamaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: he swiftly passed beyond them with his excellent horses, as if with arrows.
He heard the words of men living in the settlements of the villages:

children.text: rājānaṃ dhig daśarathaṃ kāmasya vaśam āgatam ||
children.translated_text: Shame on King <s>Daśaratha</s>, who has come under the power of desire!
Ah, cruel <s>Kaikeyī</s> today, sinful and bound to sin,
harsh and breaking all bounds, is engaged in a harsh deed.

children.text: yā putram īdṛśaṃ rājñaḥ pravāsayati dhārmikam
children.translated_text: She sends into forest exile such a righteous son of the king,
a man of great wisdom, compassionate and untiring.
Hearing these words of men living in the settlements of the villages,
the hero, the lord of <s>Kosala</s>, passed beyond the <s>Kosala</s> lands.
Then, crossing the river named <s>Vedaśruti</s>, which carried auspicious waters,
he went forward facing the region inhabited by <s>Agastya</s>.

children.text: gatvā tu suciraṃ kālaṃ tataḥ śītajalāṃ nadīm
children.translated_text: After traveling for a very long time, he then came to the cool-watered river,
and crossed the <s>Gomatī</s>, with cattle-rich marshlands, flowing to the ocean.

children.text: gomatīṃ cāpy atikramya rāghavaḥ śīghragair hayaiḥ
children.translated_text: Having also passed beyond the <s>Gomatī</s>, <s>Rāghava</s>, with swift-going horses,
crossed the river <s>Syandikā</s>, resounding with peacocks and geese.

children.text: sa mahīṃ manunā rājñā dattām ikṣvākave purā
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> showed <s>Vaidehī</s> the flourishing land, surrounded by kingdoms,
which King <s>Manu</s> had formerly given to <s>Ikṣvāku</s>.

children.text: sūta ity eva cābhāṣya sārathiṃ tam abhīkṣṇaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Repeatedly addressing that charioteer simply as 'O charioteer,'
the splendid bull among men, whose voice was like the call of an intoxicated swan, spoke.

children.text: kadāhaṃ punar āgamya sarayvāḥ puṣpite vane
children.translated_text: When shall I come again and, in the flowering forest by the <s>Sarayū</s>,

children.text: mṛgayāṃ paryaṭiṣyāmi mātrā pitrā ca saṃgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: wander in the hunt, joined together with my mother and father?
I do not desire hunting in the <s>Sarayū</s> forest excessively;
for this delight is unequaled in the world and approved by groups of royal sages.

children.text: sa tam adhvānam aikṣvākaḥ sūtaṃ madhurayā girā
children.translated_text: The <s>Aikṣvāka</s>, with sweet speech, addressed that charioteer along the road,

children.text: taṃ tam artham abhipretya yayau vākyam udīrayan ||
children.translated_text: uttering words with this and that matter in view as he went.
Having passed through the broad, pleasant lands of <s>Kosala</s>, the elder brother of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
the mighty-armed one, arrived near <s>Śṛṅgaverapura</s>.
There <s>Rāghava</s> saw the divine <s>Gaṅgā</s>, flowing in three paths, with auspicious waters, free from moss,
holy and attended by sages.
It was resounding with flocks of swans and sārasas, and filled with the calls of cakravākas,

children.text: śiśumāraiś ca nakraiś ca bhujaṃgaiś ca niṣevitām ||
children.translated_text: and inhabited by river dolphins, crocodiles, and serpents.
Having looked upon her, turbid with waves and eddies, the great chariot-warrior
said to the charioteer <s>Sumantra</s>, "Let us stay right here today.
Not far from the river is this very great iṅgudī tree,
rich in many flowers and shoots; let us stay right here, charioteer."

children.text: lakṣmaṇaś ca sumantraś ca bāḍham ity eva rāghavam
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and <s>Sumantra</s> said to <s>Rāghava</s>, "Certainly,"
and then brought the horses near that iṅgudī tree.
<s>Rāma</s>, delight of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s>, approached that lovely tree,
and descended from that chariot with his wife and with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
<s>Sumantra</s> too, having descended at once and released the excellent horses,
stood before <s>Rāma</s>, who had gone to the foot of the tree, with joined palms.

children.text: tatra rājā guho nāma rāmasyātmasamaḥ sakhā
children.translated_text: There was a king named <s>Guha</s>, a friend of <s>Rāma</s> like his own self,
born among the Niṣādas, strong, and renowned as a chief.

children.text: sa śrutvā puruṣavyāghraṃ rāmaṃ viṣayam āgatam
children.translated_text: Hearing that <s>Rāma</s>, tiger among men, had come into his territory,
he came, surrounded by aged ministers and also by his kinsmen.
Then, seeing the lord of the Niṣādas standing at a distance,

children.text: saha saumitriṇā rāmaḥ samāgacchad guhena saḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, together with <s>Saumitri</s>, met with <s>Guha</s>.

children.text: tam ārtaḥ sampariṣvajya guho rāghavam abravīt
children.translated_text: Afflicted, <s>Guha</s> embraced <s>Rāghava</s> closely and said,

children.text: yathāyodhyā tathedaṃ te rāma kiṃ karavāṇi te ||
children.translated_text: "As <s>Ayodhyā</s> is yours, so is this place, <s>Rāma</s>. What may I do for you?"
Then, bringing various kinds of excellent food and drink,

children.text: arghyaṃ copānayat kṣipraṃ vākyaṃ cedam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: and quickly presenting water for respectful reception, he spoke these words:

children.text: svāgataṃ te mahābāho taveyam akhilā mahī
children.translated_text: "Welcome to you, mighty-armed one. This whole earth is yours.

children.text: vayaṃ preṣyā bhavān bhartā sādhu rājyaṃ praśādhi naḥ ||
children.translated_text: We are your servants; you are our lord. Rule this kingdom of ours well.

children.text: bhakṣyaṃ bhojyaṃ ca peyaṃ ca lehyaṃ cedam upasthitam
children.translated_text: Here are foods to be chewed, eaten, drunk, and licked, set before you,

children.text: śayanāni ca mukhyāni vājināṃ khādanaṃ ca te ||
children.translated_text: as well as fine beds and fodder for your horses."

children.text: guham eva bruvāṇaṃ taṃ rāghavaḥ pratyuvāca ha
children.translated_text: To <s>Guha</s>, who was speaking in this way, <s>Rāghava</s> replied,

children.text: arcitāś caiva hṛṣṭāś ca bhavatā sarvathā vayam ||
children.translated_text: "We have been honored and gladdened by you in every way.
By your coming on foot and by the display of affection,"
he said, pressing him with his well-formed arms.

children.text: diṣṭyā tvāṃ guha paśyāmi arogaṃ saha bāndhavaiḥ
children.translated_text: "By good fortune, <s>Guha</s>, I see you free from illness together with your kinsmen.

children.text: api te kuśalaṃ rāṣṭre mitreṣu ca dhaneṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: Is all well with your kingdom, your friends, and your wealth?

children.text: yat tv idaṃ bhavatā kiṃcit prītyā samupakalpitam
children.translated_text: But whatever has been prepared here by you out of affection,

children.text: sarvaṃ tad anujānāmi na hi varte pratigrahe ||
children.translated_text: I consent to all that, though I am not living in acceptance of gifts.
Know me, wearing kuśa grass, bark, and deerskin, and eating fruits and roots,
to be a forest-dwelling ascetic, devoted to <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty).
I have need of fodder for the horses, and of nothing else at all.
By this much from your honor, I shall be well worshiped here.

children.text: ete hi dayitā rājñaḥ pitur daśarathasya me
children.translated_text: For these horses are dear to the king, my father <s>Daśaratha</s>.

children.text: etaiḥ suvihitair aśvair bhaviṣyāmy aham arcitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With these horses well cared for, I shall be honored."

children.text: aśvānāṃ pratipānaṃ ca khādanaṃ caiva so 'nvaśāt
children.translated_text: He then instructed men there about watering and feeding the horses:

children.text: guhas tatraiva puruṣāṃs tvaritaṃ dīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Guha</s> said, "Let it be given quickly."
Then, with bark cloth as his upper garment, after performing the evening twilight rite,
he took only water as his meal, brought by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> himself.

children.text: tasya bhūmau śayānasya pādau prakṣālya lakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: After washing the feet of him who was lying on the ground,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> then came near him, with his wife, and stood leaning against a tree.
<s>Guha</s> too, conversing with <s>Saumitri</s> together with the charioteer,
kept watch over <s>Rāma</s> then, vigilant and holding his bow.

children.text: tathā śayānasya tato 'sya dhīmato yaśasvino dāśarather mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: And for that wise, famous, great-souled son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, as he lay there,

children.text: adṛṣṭaduḥkhasya sukhocitasya sā tadā vyatīyāya cireṇa śarvarī ||
children.translated_text: he who had not known sorrow and was accustomed to comfort, that night then passed slowly.

children.text: taṃ jāgratam adambhena bhrātur arthāya lakṣmaṇam
children.translated_text: To <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, who was keeping watch sincerely for his brother's sake,
<s>Guha</s>, tormented by grief, spoke words about <s>Rāghava</s>:

children.text: iyaṃ tāta sukhā śayyā tvadartham upakalpitā
children.translated_text: "Dear child, this comfortable bed has been prepared for you.
Take rest well on it, prince, at your ease.

children.text: ucito 'yaṃ janaḥ sarvaḥ kleśānāṃ tvaṃ sukhocitaḥ
children.translated_text: All these people are accustomed to hardships, while you are accustomed to comfort.
We shall keep watch through the night for the protection of <s>Kākutstha</s>.

children.text: na hi rāmāt priyataro mamāsti bhuvi kaścana
children.translated_text: For there is no one on earth dearer to me than <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: bravīmy etad ahaṃ satyaṃ satyenaiva ca te śape ||
children.translated_text: I say this truth, and by truth itself I swear to you.

children.text: asya prasādād āśaṃse loke 'smin sumahad yaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Through his favor I hope for very great fame in this world,

children.text: dharmāvāptiṃ ca vipulām arthāvāptiṃ ca kevalām ||
children.translated_text: and for abundant attainment of <s>dharma</s> (righteous merit) and complete attainment of wealth.

children.text: so 'haṃ priyasakhaṃ rāmaṃ śayānaṃ saha sītayā
children.translated_text: So I, bow in hand, together with all my kinsmen on every side,
will protect my dear friend <s>Rāma</s>, lying down with <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: na hi me 'viditaṃ kiṃcid vane 'smiṃś carataḥ sadā
children.translated_text: For there is nothing unknown to me as I am always moving in this forest.

children.text: caturaṅgaṃ hy api balaṃ sumahat prasahemahi ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, we could withstand even a very great fourfold army."
Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> said to him, "While we are being protected by you, sinless one,

children.text: nātra bhītā vayaṃ sarve dharmam evānupaśyatā ||
children.translated_text: Here we are not at all afraid, all of us, while you keep only <s>dharma</s> in view.

children.text: kathaṃ dāśarathau bhūmau śayāne saha sītayā
children.translated_text: How could sleep be obtained by me while the two sons of <s>Daśaratha</s> are lying on the ground with <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: śakyā nidrā mayā labdhuṃ jīvitaṃ vā sukhāni vā ||
children.translated_text: or life, or pleasures?

children.text: yo na devāsuraiḥ sarvaiḥ śakyaḥ prasahituṃ yudhi
children.translated_text: He whom all the gods and demons cannot overpower in battle,

children.text: taṃ paśya sukhasaṃviṣṭaṃ tṛṇeṣu saha sītayā ||
children.translated_text: look at him lying at ease on grass together with <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: yo mantratapasā labdho vividhaiś ca pariśramaiḥ
children.translated_text: He who was obtained by mantras, austerity, and many different exertions,
this one son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, bearing marks like his own,

children.text: asmin pravrajito rājā na ciraṃ vartayiṣyati
children.translated_text: when he has gone into exile, the king will not live long.

children.text: vidhavā medinī nūnaṃ kṣipram eva bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Surely the earth will very soon become widowed.
The women, after crying out with very loud cries, have ceased from weariness.
Dear one, I think the royal residence has fallen silent, its clamor stopped.

children.text: kausalyā caiva rājā ca tathaiva jananī mama
children.translated_text: <s>Kausalyā</s>, the king, and likewise my own mother,

children.text: nāśaṃse yadi jīvanti sarve te śarvarīm imām ||
children.translated_text: I do not expect that all of them are living through this night.

children.text: jīved api hi me mātā śatrughnasyānvavekṣayā
children.translated_text: My mother may perhaps live because she looks after <s>Śatrughna</s>;

children.text: tad duḥkhaṃ yat tu kausalyā vīrasūr vinaśiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: but that is the grief: <s>Kausalyā</s>, mother of a hero, will perish.
That city, filled with devoted people, pleasant to behold, bringing joy to those dear to it,
caught up in the king's calamity, will perish.
It is past, it is past: without attaining his heart's desire,

children.text: rājye rāmam anikṣipya pitā me vinaśiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: without installing <s>Rāma</s> in the kingdom, my father will perish.

children.text: siddhārthāḥ pitaraṃ vṛttaṃ tasmin kāle hy upasthite
children.translated_text: When that time has arrived, men whose purpose is fulfilled
will perform all the funeral rites for my dead father, the lord of the earth.
With lovely squares and courtyards, with great roads well laid out,
endowed with mansions and palaces, adorned by excellent courtesans,
crowded with chariots, horses, and elephants, resounding with the sound of instruments,
filled with every good thing, thronged with joyful and well-nourished people,
endowed with parks and gardens, splendid with assemblies and festivals,
they will move happily through my father's capital.
May we, together with the truthful one, safe and sound,
when this forest exile has ended, enter <s>Ayodhyā</s>.
For the great-souled prince, lamenting and afflicted with grief,
as he stood there, that night passed by.

children.text: tathā hi satyaṃ bruvati prajāhite narendraputre gurusauhṛdād guhaḥ
children.translated_text: While the prince of kings, speaking truth for the welfare of his subjects and out of affection for his elders, was saying this, <s>Guha</s>,

children.text: mumoca bāṣpaṃ vyasanābhipīḍito jvarāturo nāga iva vyathāturaḥ ||
children.translated_text: oppressed by distress, shed tears like a fever-stricken elephant tormented by pain.
But when the night had dawned, broad-chested and greatly renowned <s>Rāma</s>
spoke to <s>Saumitri</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> of auspicious marks:
This is the time of the sun's rising; the blessed night has gone.

children.text: asau sukṛṣṇo vihagaḥ kokilas tāta kūjati ||
children.translated_text: That very dark bird, dear one, the cuckoo, is calling.

children.text: barhiṇānāṃ ca nirghoṣaḥ śrūyate nadatāṃ vane
children.translated_text: And the cry of peacocks calling in the forest is heard.
Let us cross the swift-flowing <s>Jāhnavī</s>, which goes to the ocean, gentle one.
Understanding <s>Rāma</s>'s words, <s>Saumitri</s>, delighter of his friends,

children.text: guham āmantrya sūtaṃ ca so 'tiṣṭhad bhrātur agrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: summoned <s>Guha</s> and the charioteer and stood before his brother.

children.text: tataḥ kalāpān saṃnahya khaḍgau baddhvā ca dhanvinau
children.translated_text: Then, fastening on their quivers and tying on their swords, the two bowmen

children.text: jagmatur yena tau gaṅgāṃ sītayā saha rāghavau ||
children.translated_text: went toward the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the two <s>Rāghavas</s> together with <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: rāmam eva tu dharmajñam upagamya vinītavat
children.translated_text: Approaching <s>Rāma</s>, who knew <s>dharma</s>, in a humble manner,

children.text: kim ahaṃ karavāṇīti sūtaḥ prāñjalir abravīt ||
children.translated_text: the charioteer said with folded hands, 'What shall I do?'
'Turn back,' he said to him. 'This much has been done for me.

children.text: yānaṃ vihāya padbhyāṃ tu gamiṣyāmo mahāvanam ||
children.translated_text: Leaving the vehicle behind, we shall go on foot into the great forest.'

children.text: ātmānaṃ tv abhyanujñātam avekṣyārtaḥ sa sārathiḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing himself dismissed, the distressed charioteer,
<s>Sumantra</s>, spoke these words to the <s>Aikṣvāka</s>, the tiger among men:
No man in this world has ever undergone such a thing as this:
your dwelling in the forest like an ordinary man, with your brother and wife.

children.text: na manye brahmacarye 'sti svadhīte vā phalodayaḥ
children.translated_text: I do not think there is any arising of fruit from celibate discipline, or from Vedic study,

children.text: mārdavārjavayor vāpi tvāṃ ced vyasanam āgatam ||
children.translated_text: or even from gentleness and uprightness, if misfortune has come upon you.

children.text: saha rāghava vaidehyā bhrātrā caiva vane vasan
children.translated_text: Dwelling in the forest together with <s>Vaidehī</s> and your brother, O <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: tvaṃ gatiṃ prāpsyase vīra trīṃl lokāṃs tu jayann iva ||
children.translated_text: you will reach your destined course, hero, as if conquering the three worlds.

children.text: vayaṃ khalu hatā rāma ye tayāpy upavañcitāḥ
children.translated_text: We indeed are ruined, O <s>Rāma</s>, we who, deceived by her too,
will come under the power of sinful <s>Kaikeyī</s>, sharing in grief.

children.text: iti bruvann ātmasamaṃ sumantraḥ sārathis tadā
children.translated_text: Speaking thus then to one dear as his own self, <s>Sumantra</s>, the charioteer,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā dūragataṃ rāmaṃ duḥkhārto rurude ciram ||
children.translated_text: seeing <s>Rāma</s> going far away, afflicted with grief, wept for a long time.

children.text: tatas tu vigate bāṣpe sūtaṃ spṛṣṭodakaṃ śucim
children.translated_text: Then, when his tears had gone, to the charioteer who had touched water and was purified,

children.text: rāmas tu madhuraṃ vākyaṃ punaḥ punar uvāca tam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> again and again spoke a sweet word:
Among the <s>Ikṣvākus</s> I do not perceive a friend equal to you.

children.text: yathā daśaratho rājā māṃ na śocet tathā kuru ||
children.translated_text: Act so that King <s>Daśaratha</s> does not grieve for me.
The lord of the earth is old, his mind struck by sorrow,

children.text: kāmabhārāvasannaś ca tasmād etad bravīmi te ||
children.translated_text: and weighed down by the burden of desire; therefore I tell you this.

children.text: yad yad ājñāpayet kiṃcit sa mahātmā mahīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever that great-souled lord of the earth may command in any matter,
for the sake of doing what is dear and pleasing to <s>Kaikeyī</s>, that must be done without hesitation.
For this purpose kings rule kingdoms:

children.text: yad eṣāṃ sarvakṛtyeṣu mano na pratihanyate ||
children.translated_text: that their will may not be obstructed in all their undertakings.

children.text: tad yathā sa mahārājo nālīkam adhigacchati
children.translated_text: Therefore, in such a way that the great king does not incur falsehood,

children.text: na ca tāmyati duḥkhena sumantra kuru tat tathā ||
children.translated_text: and is not consumed by grief, <s>Sumantra</s>, do that.
After respectfully greeting the king, who has not known suffering, who is aged, noble, and self-controlled,

children.text: brūyās tvam abhivādyaiva mama hetor idaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: you should speak these words on my behalf:

children.text: naivāham anuśocāmi lakṣmaṇo na ca maithilī
children.translated_text: Neither I nor <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> nor <s>Maithilī</s> grieve

children.text: ayodhyāyāś cyutāś ceti vane vatsyāmaheti vā ||
children.translated_text: that we have been displaced from <s>Ayodhyā</s> or that we shall dwell in the forest.
When the fourteen years have passed, again and again...

children.text: lakṣmaṇaṃ māṃ ca sītāṃ ca drakṣyasi kṣipram āgatān ||
children.translated_text: You will soon see <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, me, and <s>Sītā</s> returned.

children.text: evam uktvā tu rājānaṃ mātaraṃ ca sumantra me
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken to the king and to my mother, O <s>Sumantra</s>,

children.text: anyāś ca devīḥ sahitāḥ kaikeyīṃ ca punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and to the other queens together, and to <s>Kaikeyī</s> again and again,
tell <s>Kausalyā</s> of our well-being, and then make obeisance at her feet

children.text: sītāyā mama cāryasya vacanāl lakṣmaṇasya ca ||
children.translated_text: on behalf of <s>Sītā</s>, myself, and noble <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: brūyāś ca hi mahārājaṃ bharataṃ kṣipram ānaya
children.translated_text: And say to the great king: "Bring <s>Bharata</s> quickly.

children.text: āgataś cāpi bharataḥ sthāpyo nṛpamate pade ||
children.translated_text: And when <s>Bharata</s> has come, he should be installed on the throne, as the king wishes.
Having embraced <s>Bharata</s> and consecrated him in the crown-princeship,
the sorrow born of distress over us will not overpower you."

children.text: bharataś cāpi vaktavyo yathā rājani vartase
children.translated_text: And <s>Bharata</s> too should be told: "As you conduct yourself toward the king,
so should you conduct yourself toward all the mothers, without distinction.

children.text: yathā ca tava kaikeyī sumitrā cāviśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: And just as <s>Kaikeyī</s> and <s>Sumitrā</s> are equally mothers to you,

children.text: tathaiva devī kausalyā mama mātā viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: so too is queen <s>Kausalyā</s>, especially, my mother."
As <s>Sumantra</s>, wasted by grief, was being turned back by <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: tat sarvaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā snehāt kākutstham abravīt ||
children.translated_text: he heard all that speech and, out of affection, said to the <s>Kākutstha</s>:

children.text: yad ahaṃ nopacāreṇa brūyāṃ snehād aviklavaḥ
children.translated_text: "If, from affection and without losing composure, I speak in a way lacking proper deference,

children.text: bhaktimān iti tat tāvad vākyaṃ tvaṃ kṣantum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: then, for now, you should forgive that speech of mine, thinking, 'He is devoted.'

children.text: kathaṃ hi tvadvihīno 'haṃ pratiyāsyāmi tāṃ purīm
children.translated_text: For how shall I return without you to that city,
which, dear child, through separation from you, will be distraught as if with sorrow for a son?

children.text: sarāmam api tāvan me rathaṃ dṛṣṭvā tadā janaḥ
children.translated_text: If the people were stricken even when they saw my chariot with <s>Rāma</s> in it,

children.text: vinā rāmaṃ rathaṃ dṛṣṭvā vidīryetāpi sā purī ||
children.translated_text: then, seeing the chariot without <s>Rāma</s>, that city might even burst apart.

children.text: dainyaṃ hi nagarī gacched dṛṣṭvā śūnyam imaṃ ratham
children.translated_text: The city would fall into misery on seeing this empty chariot,
like its own army in battle left only with the charioteer after its hero has been slain.
Though you will be living far away, you will stand before them in their minds;

children.text: cintayantyo 'dya nūnaṃ tvāṃ nirāhārāḥ kṛtāḥ prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: thinking of you today, the subjects have surely gone without food.

children.text: ārtanādo hi yaḥ paurair muktas tadvipravāsane
children.translated_text: The lament that was let loose by the townspeople when you were sent into exile,

children.text: rathasthaṃ māṃ niśāmyaiva kuryuḥ śataguṇaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: they would make a hundred times greater merely on seeing me seated in the chariot.

children.text: ahaṃ kiṃ cāpi vakṣyāmi devīṃ tava suto mayā
children.translated_text: And what shall I say to your queen? 'Your son has been taken by me

children.text: nīto 'sau mātulakulaṃ saṃtāpaṃ mā kṛthā iti ||
children.translated_text: to his maternal uncle's family; do not grieve'?

children.text: asatyam api naivāhaṃ brūyāṃ vacanam īdṛśam
children.translated_text: Even though untrue, I could never speak such a statement;

children.text: katham apriyam evāhaṃ brūyāṃ satyam idaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: how then could I speak this true word, which is wholly unpleasant?
As for those excellent horses in my charge, who carry your kinsmen,

children.text: kathaṃ rathaṃ tvayā hīnaṃ pravakṣyanti hayottamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: how will they draw the chariot when it is bereft of you?

children.text: yadi me yācamānasya tyāgam eva kariṣyasi
children.translated_text: If, though I am begging, you will simply abandon me,
then, with the chariot, I will enter fire the very moment I am abandoned here by you.
Whatever beings in the forest will obstruct your austerities,
I will ward off those creatures with the chariot, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: tvatkṛte na mayā prāptaṃ rathacaryākṛtaṃ sukham
children.translated_text: For your sake I have not obtained the pleasure produced by chariot-driving;
for your sake I hope to obtain the happiness produced by dwelling in the forest.
Be gracious. I wish to be immediately beside you in the wilderness.
I ask this out of affection: let me be your immediate attendant.

children.text: tava śuśrūṣaṇaṃ mūrdhnā kariṣyāmi vane vasan
children.translated_text: Dwelling in the forest, I will perform service to you with my head bowed;

children.text: ayodhyāṃ devalokaṃ vā sarvathā prajahāmy aham ||
children.translated_text: I abandon <s>Ayodhyā</s>, and even the world of the gods, in every way.

children.text: na hi śakyā praveṣṭuṃ sā mayāyodhyā tvayā vinā
children.translated_text: For I cannot enter that <s>Ayodhyā</s> without you,
just as one who has done evil cannot enter the capital of great <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: ime cāpi hayā vīra yadi te vanavāsinaḥ
children.translated_text: And these horses too, O hero, if, while you dwell in the forest,
they attend upon you, will attain the highest state.

children.text: vanavāse kṣayaṃ prāpte mamaiṣa hi manorathaḥ
children.translated_text: When the term of forest-dwelling has reached its end, this indeed is my wish:

children.text: yad anena rathenaiva tvāṃ vaheyaṃ purīṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that with this very chariot I may carry you back to the city.

children.text: caturdaśa hi varṣāṇi sahitasya tvayā vane
children.translated_text: For the fourteen years in the forest, if I am together with you,
will pass like a moment; otherwise they will become hundreds of times longer.
Affectionate to your servants, you should not abandon me, a servant who stands

children.text: bhaktaṃ bhṛtyaṃ sthitaṃ sthityāṃ tvaṃ na māṃ hātum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: on the path taken by my master's son, devoted and firm in loyalty.

children.text: evaṃ bahuvidhaṃ dīnaṃ yācamānaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: When he pleaded again and again in many such pitiable ways,

children.text: rāmo bhṛtyānukampī tu sumantram idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, compassionate toward his servants, said this to <s>Sumantra</s>:

children.text: jānāmi paramāṃ bhaktiṃ mayi te bhartṛvatsala
children.translated_text: "I know your supreme devotion to me, you who are devoted to your master;

children.text: śṛṇu cāpi yadarthaṃ tvāṃ preṣayāmi purīm itaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but hear also the reason for which I am sending you from here to the city.

children.text: nagarīṃ tvāṃ gataṃ dṛṣṭvā jananī me yavīyasī
children.translated_text: Seeing that you have gone to the city, my younger mother,

children.text: kaikeyī pratyayaṃ gacched iti rāmo vanaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kaikeyī</s>, would be convinced: '<s>Rāma</s> has gone to the forest.'

children.text: parituṣṭā hi sā devī vanavāsaṃ gate mayi
children.translated_text: For that queen, satisfied when I have gone to dwell in the forest,
would not much suspect the righteous king of speaking falsely.

children.text: eṣa me prathamaḥ kalpo yad ambā me yavīyasī
children.translated_text: This is my first plan: that my younger mother
should obtain prosperous kingship for her son, secured by <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: mama priyārthaṃ rājñaś ca sarathas tvaṃ purīṃ vraja
children.translated_text: For my sake, and for the king's sake, go to the city with the chariot;

children.text: saṃdiṣṭaś cāsi yānarthāṃs tāṃs tān brūyās tathātathā ||
children.translated_text: and, as you have been instructed about each matter, speak those things exactly as they are."

children.text: ity uktvā vacanaṃ sūtaṃ sāntvayitvā punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken to the charioteer and comforted him again and again,

children.text: guhaṃ vacanam aklībaṃ rāmo hetumad abravīt
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> spoke a firm, reasoned word to <s>Guha</s>:
"I shall go after making matted locks; bring the milk of the banyan tree."

children.text: tat kṣīraṃ rājaputrāya guhaḥ kṣipram upāharat
children.translated_text: <s>Guha</s> quickly brought that milk to the prince,
and with it <s>Rāma</s> made matted locks for <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and for himself.
Then the two, wearing bark garments and bearing coils of matted hair,
the brothers <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, shone like sages.
Then, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, having taken up the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> ascetic path,

children.text: vratam ādiṣṭavān rāmaḥ sahāyaṃ guham abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, having entered upon his vow, spoke to his ally <s>Guha</s>:

children.text: apramatto bale kośe durge janapade tathā
children.translated_text: "Be vigilant concerning the army, the treasury, the fort, and likewise the countryside

children.text: bhavethā guha rājyaṃ hi durārakṣatamaṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: Be vigilant, <s>Guha</s>; for a kingdom is regarded as exceedingly difficult to guard.
Then, having taken leave of that <s>Guha</s>, the delight of the Ikṣvākus
went quickly and untroubled, together with his wife and with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: sa tu dṛṣṭvā nadītīre nāvam ikṣvākunandanaḥ
children.translated_text: But when the delight of the Ikṣvākus saw the boat on the riverbank,

children.text: titīrṣuḥ śīghragāṃ gaṅgām idaṃ lakṣmaṇam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: desiring to cross the swift-flowing <s>Gaṅgā</s>, he said this to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:

children.text: āroha tvaṃ naravyāghra sthitāṃ nāvam imāṃ śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: Climb aboard this boat that stands here, tiger among men, slowly,
and help high-minded <s>Sītā</s> aboard after taking her by the arm.

children.text: sa bhrātuḥ śāsanaṃ śrutvā sarvam apratikūlayan
children.translated_text: Hearing his brother's command, and opposing none of it,
the self-possessed one first helped the <s>Maithilī</s> aboard, and then climbed aboard himself.
Then the radiant elder brother of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> climbed aboard himself;
after that <s>Guha</s>, lord of the Niṣādas, urged on his kinsmen.

children.text: anujñāya sumantraṃ ca sabalaṃ caiva taṃ guham
children.translated_text: And after taking leave of <s>Sumantra</s> and of <s>Guha</s> with his attendants,

children.text: āsthāya nāvaṃ rāmas tu codayāmāsa nāvikān ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, having mounted the boat, urged the boatmen onward.

children.text: tatas taiś coditā sā nauḥ karṇadhārasamāhitā
children.translated_text: Then that boat, driven by them, with the helmsman attentive,
struck by the speed of auspicious oars, quickly crossed the water.

children.text: madhyaṃ tu samanuprāpya bhāgīrathyās tv aninditā
children.translated_text: But when blameless <s>Vaidehī</s> had reached the middle of the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>,

children.text: vaidehī prāñjalir bhūtvā tāṃ nadīm idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: she joined her palms and spoke these words to that river:
This is the son of wise great king <s>Daśaratha</s>;
may he fulfill this command, <s>Gaṅgā</s>, protected by you.

children.text: caturdaśa hi varṣāṇi samagrāṇy uṣya kānane
children.translated_text: After dwelling in the forest for fourteen full years,

children.text: bhrātrā saha mayā caiva punaḥ pratyāgamiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: he will return again, together with his brother and with me.

children.text: tatas tvāṃ devi subhage kṣemeṇa punar āgatā
children.translated_text: Then, O fortunate goddess, having returned again safely,
I shall joyfully worship you, <s>Gaṅgā</s>, for the fulfilment of every desire.

children.text: tvaṃ hi tripathagā devi brahmalokaṃ samīkṣase
children.translated_text: For you, O goddess, move in the three paths and behold the world of <s>Brahmā</s>;
and in this world you are seen as the wife of the ocean-king.

children.text: sā tvāṃ devi namasyāmi praśaṃsāmi ca śobhane
children.translated_text: I bow to you, goddess, and praise you, O beautiful one,
when the tiger among men has regained his kingdom and returned again in safety.

children.text: gavāṃ śatasahasrāṇi vastrāṇy annaṃ ca peśalam
children.translated_text: Hundreds of thousands of cows, garments, and fine food
I shall give to brahmins, wishing to do what is dear to you.

children.text: tathā sambhāṣamāṇā sā sītā gaṅgām aninditā
children.translated_text: As blameless <s>Sītā</s> was speaking thus to the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
she, turning southward, very quickly reached the southern bank.

children.text: tīraṃ tu samanuprāpya nāvaṃ hitvā nararṣabhaḥ
children.translated_text: Having reached the bank and left the boat, the bull among men,

children.text: prātiṣṭhata saha bhrātrā vaidehyā ca paraṃtapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the scorcher of foes, set out with his brother and with <s>Vaidehī</s>.
Then the mighty-armed one said to the increaser of <s>Sumitrā</s>'s joy,

children.text: agrato gaccha saumitre sītā tvām anugacchatu ||
children.translated_text: Go ahead, <s>Saumitri</s>; let <s>Sītā</s> follow you.

children.text: pṛṣṭhato 'haṃ gamiṣyāmi tvāṃ ca sītāṃ ca pālayan
children.translated_text: I will go behind, protecting both you and <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: adya duḥkhaṃ tu vaidehī vanavāsasya vetsyati ||
children.translated_text: Today <s>Vaidehī</s> will know the hardship of forest-dwelling.

children.text: gataṃ tu gaṅgāparapāram āśu rāmaṃ sumantraḥ pratataṃ nirīkṣya
children.translated_text: But <s>Sumantra</s>, continually watching <s>Rāma</s> who had quickly gone to the far bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: adhvaprakarṣād vinivṛttadṛṣṭir mumoca bāṣpaṃ vyathitas tapasvī ||
children.translated_text: when his sight was cut off by the length of the road, shed tears, afflicted and miserable.

children.text: tau tatra hatvā caturo mahāmṛgān varāham ṛśyaṃ pṛṣataṃ mahārurum
children.translated_text: There they killed four great animals: a boar, an ṛśya deer, a pṛṣata deer, and a great ruru;

children.text: ādāya medhyaṃ tvaritaṃ bubhukṣitau vāsāya kāle yayatur vanaspatim ||
children.translated_text: hungry, they took the suitable meat and quickly went at evening to a forest tree for lodging.

children.text: sa taṃ vṛkṣaṃ samāsādya saṃdhyām anvāsya paścimām
children.translated_text: Having reached that tree and performed the western evening rite,

children.text: rāmo ramayatāṃ śreṣṭha iti hovāca lakṣmaṇam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, best of those who delight others, then spoke to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:

children.text: adyeyaṃ prathamā rātrir yātā janapadād bahiḥ
children.translated_text: Today this first night away from the settled country has arrived,

children.text: yā sumantreṇa rahitā tāṃ notkaṇṭhitum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: the one without <s>Sumantra</s>; you should not be anxious over it.
From today onward, during the nights, we two must keep watch without weariness,
for the security and welfare of <s>Sītā</s> rests with us, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Somehow, <s>Saumitri</s>, let us pass this night,
and lie down on the ground, spreading what we have gathered ourselves.
Then, lying down on the earth, though accustomed to a very costly bed,

children.text: imāḥ saumitraye rāmo vyājahāra kathāḥ śubhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> spoke these auspicious words to <s>Saumitri</s>:

children.text: dhruvam adya mahārājo duḥkhaṃ svapiti lakṣmaṇa
children.translated_text: Surely today the great king sleeps in sorrow, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>;

children.text: kṛtakāmā tu kaikeyī tuṣṭā bhavitum arhati ||
children.translated_text: but <s>Kaikeyī</s>, having gained her desire, ought to be satisfied.

children.text: sā hi devī mahārājaṃ kaikeyī rājyakāraṇāt
children.translated_text: For that queen <s>Kaikeyī</s>, for the sake of the kingdom,

children.text: api na cyāvayet prāṇān dṛṣṭvā bharatam āgatam ||
children.translated_text: may she not even drive the great king from his life when she sees <s>Bharata</s> returned.

children.text: anāthaś caiva vṛddhaś ca mayā caiva vinākṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: He is helpless, old, and deprived of me;

children.text: kiṃ kariṣyati kāmātmā kaikeyyā vaśam āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: what will the desire-bound king, fallen under <s>Kaikeyī</s>'s control, do?

children.text: idaṃ vyasanam ālokya rājñaś ca mativibhramam
children.translated_text: Seeing this calamity and the king's confusion of mind,

children.text: kāma evārdhadharmābhyāṃ garīyān iti me matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: I think desire is indeed stronger than wealth and <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: ko hy avidvān api pumān pramadāyāḥ kṛte tyajet
children.translated_text: For what man, even an ignorant one, would abandon for a woman's sake

children.text: chandānuvartinaṃ putraṃ tāto mām iva lakṣmaṇa ||
children.translated_text: a son obedient to his wishes, as father has abandoned me, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>?

children.text: sukhī bata sabhāryaś ca bharataḥ kekayīsutaḥ
children.translated_text: Happy indeed is <s>Bharata</s>, son of the Kekaya princess, together with his wife,

children.text: muditān kosalān eko yo bhokṣyaty adhirājavat ||
children.translated_text: who alone will enjoy the delighted <s>Kosalas</s> like an overlord.

children.text: sa hi sarvasya rājyasya mukham ekaṃ bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: For he will be the single face of the whole kingdom,

children.text: tāte ca vayasātīte mayi cāraṇyam āśrite ||
children.translated_text: with father overcome by age and with me gone to the forest.
One who abandons wealth and <s>dharma</s> and follows desire

children.text: evam āpadyate kṣipraṃ rājā daśaratho yathā ||
children.translated_text: quickly falls into such a disaster as king <s>Daśaratha</s> has.
I think <s>Kaikeyī</s>, gentle one, has obtained what leads to <s>Daśaratha</s>'s end,

children.text: kaikeyī saumya samprāptā rājyāya bharatasya ca ||
children.translated_text: to my banishment, and to the kingdom for <s>Bharata</s>.
May <s>Kaikeyī</s>, now deluded by the pride of good fortune,

children.text: kausalyāṃ ca sumitrāṃ ca samprabādheta matkṛte ||
children.translated_text: not oppress <s>Kausalyā</s> and <s>Sumitrā</s> on my account.

children.text: mā sma matkāraṇād devī sumitrā duḥkham āvaset
children.translated_text: May the queen <s>Sumitrā</s> not dwell in grief because of me;

children.text: ayodhyām ita eva tvaṃ kāle praviśa lakṣmaṇa ||
children.translated_text: therefore you, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, should enter <s>Ayodhyā</s> at the proper time.

children.text: aham eko gamiṣyāmi sītayā saha daṇḍakān
children.translated_text: I shall go alone with <s>Sītā</s> to the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forests;

children.text: anāthāyā hi nāthas tvaṃ kausalyāyā bhaviṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: for you will be the protector of helpless <s>Kausalyā</s>.

children.text: kṣudrakarmā hi kaikeyī dveṣād anyāyyam ācaret
children.translated_text: For petty-minded <s>Kaikeyī</s> might, out of hatred, do something unjust,

children.text: paridadyā hi dharmajñe bharate mama mātaram ||
children.translated_text: and might indeed hand my mother over to <s>Bharata</s>, O knower of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: nūnaṃ jātyantare kasmin striyaḥ putrair viyojitāḥ
children.translated_text: Surely, in some other birth, women have been separated from their sons;

children.text: jananyā mama saumitre tad apy etad upasthitam ||
children.translated_text: for this too has now befallen my mother, O <s>Saumitri</s>.
For by me, long nurtured by her and raised through hardship,

children.text: viprāyujyata kausalyā phalakāle dhig astu mām ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kausalyā</s> has been separated at the time of fruit. Shame on me!

children.text: mā sma sīmantinī kācij janayet putram īdṛśam
children.translated_text: May no married woman ever give birth to such a son

children.text: saumitre yo 'ham ambāyā dadmi śokam anantakam ||
children.translated_text: as I am, O <s>Saumitri</s>, who give endless grief to my mother.

children.text: manye prītiviśiṣṭā sā matto lakṣmaṇa śārikā
children.translated_text: I think, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, that śārikā bird is richer in affection than I,

children.text: yasyās tac chrūyate vākyaṃ śuka pādam arer daśa ||
children.translated_text: whose utterance is heard: "O parrot, bite the enemy's foot."
When that ill-fated woman is grieving, I do nothing to help her.

children.text: putreṇa kim aputrāyā mayā kāryam ariṃdama ||
children.translated_text: What use has one as good as sonless for a son like me, O subduer of foes?

children.text: alpabhāgyā hi me mātā kausalyā rahitā mayā
children.translated_text: For my mother <s>Kausalyā</s> is ill-fated, bereft of me;
afflicted by supreme sorrow, she lies fallen in an ocean of grief.

children.text: eko hy aham ayodhyāṃ ca pṛthivīṃ cāpi lakṣmaṇa
children.translated_text: I alone, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, when angry, could overcome <s>Ayodhyā</s> and the earth

children.text: tareyam iṣubhiḥ kruddho nanu vīryam akāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: with arrows; yet surely such valor serves no purpose.
But I am afraid of <s>adharma</s> and of the next world, O sinless one;
therefore, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, today I do not consecrate myself.

children.text: etad anyac ca karuṇaṃ vilapya vijane bahu
children.translated_text: Having lamented much in this and other piteous ways in the lonely place,
<s>Rāma</s>, his face full of tears, sat silent through the night.
When <s>Rāma</s> had ceased lamenting, like a fire whose flames had gone out,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> comforted him, like an ocean without motion.

children.text: dhruvam adya purī rāma ayodhyāyudhināṃ vara
children.translated_text: "Surely today, <s>Rāma</s>, the city <s>Ayodhyā</s>, O best of warriors,
with you gone forth, is without splendor, like a night whose moon has departed.

children.text: naitad aupayikaṃ rāma yad idaṃ paritapyase
children.translated_text: This is not fitting, <s>Rāma</s>, that you are grieving in this way;

children.text: viṣādayasi sītāṃ ca māṃ caiva puruṣarṣabha ||
children.translated_text: you make <s>Sītā</s> and me despondent too, O bull among men.

children.text: na ca sītā tvayā hīnā na cāham api rāghava
children.translated_text: Neither <s>Sītā</s>, bereft of you, nor I, O <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: muhūrtam api jīvāvo jalān matsyāv ivoddhṛtau ||
children.translated_text: could live even for a moment, like fish drawn out of water.

children.text: na hi tātaṃ na śatrughnaṃ na sumitrāṃ paraṃtapa
children.translated_text: Neither our father, nor <s>Śatrughna</s>, nor <s>Sumitrā</s>, O scorcher of foes,

children.text: draṣṭum iccheyam adyāhaṃ svargaṃ vāpi tvayā vinā ||
children.translated_text: nor even heaven would I wish to see today without you."

children.text: sa lakṣmaṇasyottamapuṣkalaṃ vaco niśamya caivaṃ vanavāsam ādarāt
children.translated_text: Having heard <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s excellent and ample speech, and accepting forest exile with reverence,

children.text: samāḥ samastā vidadhe paraṃtapaḥ prapadya dharmaṃ sucirāya rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the scorcher of foes, <s>Rāghava</s>, resorting to <s>dharma</s>, resolved to pass all the full years for a long time.

children.text: te tu tasmin mahāvṛkṣa uṣitvā rajanīṃ śivām
children.translated_text: After they had spent the auspicious night in that great tree,
when the spotless sun had risen, they set out from that place.
Where the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s> <s>Gaṅgā</s> approaches the <s>Yamunā</s>,

children.text: jagmus taṃ deśam uddiśya vigāhya sumahad vanam ||
children.translated_text: they went toward that place, plunging into a very great forest.

children.text: te bhūmim āgān vividhān deśāṃś cāpi manoramān
children.translated_text: Those famous ones, seeing various lands and delightful regions
never seen before, here and there, went on.

children.text: yathākṣemeṇa gacchan sa paśyaṃś ca vividhān drumān
children.translated_text: As he was going safely and seeing various trees,
just as the day had ended, <s>Rāma</s> said to <s>Saumitri</s>:

children.text: prayāgam abhitaḥ paśya saumitre dhūmam unnatam
children.translated_text: "Look near <s>Prayāga</s>, O <s>Saumitri</s>, at the high-rising smoke;

children.text: agner bhagavataḥ ketuṃ manye saṃnihito muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: I think it is the banner of the venerable fire. A sage must be close by.

children.text: nūnaṃ prāptāḥ sma sambhedaṃ gaṅgāyamunayor vayam
children.translated_text: Surely we have reached the confluence of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and <s>Yamunā</s>,

children.text: tathā hi śrūyate śabdo vāriṇo vārighaṭṭitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for the sound of water struck by water is heard in just that way.
Here are pieces of wood split by forest-born people who live from the forest,
and these various trees are seen at <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s āśrama."

children.text: dhanvinau tau sukhaṃ gatvā lambamāne divākare
children.translated_text: The two bowmen went happily while the sun was hanging low,
and reached the sage's dwelling at the junction of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and <s>Yamunā</s>.

children.text: rāmas tv āśramam āsādya trāsayan mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Rāma</s>, approaching the āśrama and startling the deer and birds,
went a short distance along the road and came to <s>Bharadvāja</s>.

children.text: tatas tv āśramam āsādya muner darśanakāṅkṣiṇau
children.translated_text: Then, having reached the sage's āśrama and desiring to see the sage,
the two heroes, accompanied by <s>Sītā</s>, stood at a distance.
Seeing the greatly fortunate sage after his agnihotra had been offered, <s>Rāma</s>, with joined palms,
together with <s>Saumitri</s> and <s>Sītā</s>, paid homage to him.
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s elder brother then made himself known to him:
"Reverend sir, we are the sons of <s>Daśaratha</s>, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
This auspicious <s>Vaidehī</s>, daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, is my wife;
the blameless one has followed me into the lonely ascetic forest.

children.text: pitrā pravrājyamānaṃ māṃ saumitrir anujaḥ priyaḥ
children.translated_text: As I was being sent into exile by my father, this beloved younger brother <s>Saumitri</s>

children.text: ayam anvagamad bhrātā vanam eva dṛḍhavrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: has followed me, my firm-vowed brother, to the forest itself.
Commissioned by our father, reverend sir, we shall enter the ascetic forest;
there, living on roots and fruits, we shall practice only <s>dharma</s>."
Hearing that speech of the wise prince,

children.text: upānayata dharmātmā gām arghyam udakaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the righteous one then had a cow, respectful water, and water brought near.
Seated with deer, birds, and sages all around,

children.text: rāmam āgatam abhyarcya svāgatenāha taṃ muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: the sage honored <s>Rāma</s> who had come and greeted him with words of welcome.

children.text: pratigṛhya ca tām arcām upaviṣṭaṃ sarāghavam
children.translated_text: After accepting that honor, and when <s>Rāma</s> with his companions had sat down,
<s>Bharadvāja</s> then spoke this word, joined with <s>dharma</s>:

children.text: cirasya khalu kākutstha paśyāmi tvām ihāgatam
children.translated_text: "After a long time indeed, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, I see you come here;

children.text: śrutaṃ tava mayā cedaṃ vivāsanam akāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: and I have heard of this groundless exile of yours.
This is a secluded space at the meeting of the two great rivers,

children.text: puṇyaś ca ramaṇīyaś ca vasatv iha bhavān sukham ||
children.translated_text: holy and delightful; may your lordship dwell here happily."

children.text: evam uktas tu vacanaṃ bharadvājena rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed with these words by <s>Bharadvāja</s>, <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: pratyuvāca śubhaṃ vākyaṃ rāmaḥ sarvahite rataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, devoted to the welfare of all, replied with auspicious words:
"Reverend sir, from here the people of the city and countryside are near;

children.text: āgamiṣyati vaidehīṃ māṃ cāpi prekṣako janaḥ
children.translated_text: the people will come as spectators to look at <s>Vaidehī</s> and me too.

children.text: anena kāraṇenāham iha vāsaṃ na rocaye ||
children.translated_text: For this reason I do not like dwelling here.
In a secluded place, reverend sir, see an excellent site for a hermitage,
where <s>Vaidehī</s>, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, who deserves comfort, may delight.

children.text: etac chrutvā śubhaṃ vākyaṃ bharadvājo mahāmuniḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing this auspicious speech, the great sage <s>Bharadvāja</s>
then spoke words to <s>Rāghava</s> that grasped his purpose:

children.text: daśakrośa itas tāta girir yasmin nivatsyasi
children.translated_text: Dear child, ten krośas from here is a mountain on which you may dwell,
holy, frequented by great seers, and pleasant to behold on every side.
It is roamed by golāṅgūlas and inhabited by monkeys and bears,
known as <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, resembling <s>Gandhamādana</s>.
So long as a man looks upon the peaks of <s>Citrakūṭa</s>,

children.text: kalyāṇāni samādhatte na pāpe kurute manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he gains auspicious things and does not set his mind on sin.

children.text: ṛṣayas tatra bahavo vihṛtya śaradāṃ śatam
children.translated_text: Many seers there, having dwelt for a hundred autumns,
ascended to heaven through asceticism, together with <s>Kapālaśiras</s>.

children.text: praviviktam ahaṃ manye taṃ vāsaṃ bhavataḥ sukham
children.translated_text: I think that dwelling is secluded and pleasant for you.

children.text: iha vā vanavāsāya vasa rāma mayā saha ||
children.translated_text: Or else, <s>Rāma</s>, stay here with me for your forest residence.

children.text: sa rāmaṃ sarvakāmais taṃ bharadvājaḥ priyātithim
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Bharadvāja</s>, knower of <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty), received <s>Rāma</s>, beloved guest and possessed of every desired virtue,

children.text: sabhāryaṃ saha ca bhrātrā pratijagrāha dharmavit ||
children.translated_text: together with his wife and with his brother.

children.text: tasya prayāge rāmasya taṃ maharṣim upeyuṣaḥ
children.translated_text: For <s>Rāma</s>, who had come to that great seer at <s>Prayāga</s>,

children.text: prapannā rajanī puṇyā citrāḥ kathayataḥ kathāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the blessed night passed as they told delightful stories.
When the night had dawned, he approached <s>Bharadvāja</s>,
and the tiger among men spoke to the sage of blazing splendor:
Reverend sir, true in conduct, this night today in your hermitage

children.text: uṣitāḥ smeha vasatim anujānātu no bhavān ||
children.translated_text: we have stayed here; now may your honor permit us to depart from this dwelling.

children.text: rātryāṃ tu tasyāṃ vyuṣṭāyāṃ bharadvājo 'bravīd idam
children.translated_text: When that night had passed, <s>Bharadvāja</s> said this:
Go to <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, furnished with honey, roots, and fruits.
There herds of elephants and herds of deer all around
wander in the forest borders; you will see them, <s>Rāghava</s>.
That auspicious mountain, resounding with the calls of delighted koyaṣṭikas and cuckoos,

children.text: mṛgaiś ca mattair bahubhiś ca kuñjaraiḥ suramyam āsādya samāvasāśramam ||
children.translated_text: and made most lovely by many rutting deer and elephants, reach it and settle in a hermitage.
After spending the night there, the two enemy-subduing princes

children.text: maharṣim abhivādyātha jagmatus taṃ giriṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: honored the great seer and then set out toward that mountain.

children.text: prasthitāṃś caiva tān prekṣya pitā putrān ivānvagāt
children.translated_text: Seeing them setting forth, he followed after them like a father after his sons,

children.text: tataḥ pracakrame vaktuṃ vacanaṃ sa mahāmuniḥ ||
children.translated_text: and then that great sage began to speak these words:
Then, having reached the <s>Kālindī</s>, a river with swift current,

children.text: tatra yūyaṃ plavaṃ kṛtvā taratāṃśumatīṃ nadīm ||
children.translated_text: there make a raft and cross the shining river.
Then, coming to a great banyan with green leaves,
grown large with many trees, dark, and attended by perfected beings,

children.text: krośamātraṃ tato gatvā nīlaṃ drakṣyatha kānanam
children.translated_text: after going about a krośa from there, you will see a dark-blue forest,
mixed with palāśa and badarī trees, <s>Rāma</s>, and with bamboos of the Yamunā region.

children.text: sa panthāś citrakūṭasya gataḥ subahuśo mayā
children.translated_text: That road to <s>Citrakūṭa</s> has been taken by me many times;
it is delightful, gentle, and free from forest fires.

children.text: iti panthānam āvedya maharṣiḥ sa nyavartata ||
children.translated_text: Having pointed out the road in this way, the great seer turned back.

children.text: upāvṛtte munau tasmin rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt
children.translated_text: When that sage had turned back, <s>Rāma</s> said to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: kṛtapuṇyāḥ sma saumitre munir yan no 'nukampate ||
children.translated_text: We are blessed, <s>Saumitri</s>, since the sage has compassion for us.
After those two tigers among men, thoughtful in mind, had thus consulted together,

children.text: sītām evāgrataḥ kṛtvā kālindīṃ jagmatur nadīm ||
children.translated_text: they placed <s>Sītā</s> in front and went to the river <s>Kālindī</s>.
Then the two made a very large raft from a collection of wood;

children.text: cakāra lakṣmaṇaś chittvā sītāyāḥ sukham āsanam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, cutting wood, made a comfortable seat for <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: tatra śriyam ivācintyāṃ rāmo dāśarathiḥ priyām
children.translated_text: There <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, placed his beloved, like inconceivable splendor itself,
her slightly embarrassed, upon the raft.
Then by the raft they crossed the swift, shining, wave-garlanded

children.text: tīrajair bahubhir vṛkṣaiḥ saṃterur yamunāṃ nadīm ||
children.translated_text: river <s>Yamunā</s>, with many trees growing on its banks.

children.text: te tīrṇāḥ plavam utsṛjya prasthāya yamunāvanāt
children.translated_text: Having crossed, released the raft, and set out from the <s>Yamunā</s> forest,
they came to the dark banyan, cool and green-leaved.

children.text: kausalyāṃ caiva paśyeyaṃ sumitrāṃ ca yaśasvinīm
children.translated_text: May I see <s>Kauśalyā</s> and also the glorious <s>Sumitrā</s>,
so saying, <s>Sītā</s>, with folded hands, circumambulated the tree.
After going about a krośa from there, the brothers <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: bahūn medhyān mṛgān hatvā ceratur yamunāvane ||
children.translated_text: having killed many pure game animals, wandered in the <s>Yamunā</s> forest.

children.text: vihṛtya te barhiṇapūganādite śubhe vane vāraṇavānarāyute
children.translated_text: Having wandered in that beautiful forest, resounding with flocks of peacocks and filled with elephants and monkeys,

children.text: samaṃ nadīvapram upetya saṃmataṃ nivāsam ājagmur adīnadarśanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: they reached together an approved dwelling near the river bank, their faces undismayed.
Then, when the night had passed, immediately after they had slept,
the delight of the <s>Raghu</s> line gently awakened <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: saumitre śṛṇu vanyānāṃ valgu vyāharatāṃ svanam
children.translated_text: <s>Saumitri</s>, listen to the sweet sound of the forest creatures as they call out.
Let us set out now; it is time for departure, scorcher of foes.

children.text: sa suptaḥ samaye bhrātrā lakṣmaṇaḥ pratibodhitaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, asleep, was awakened at the proper time by his brother,

children.text: jahau nidrāṃ ca tandrīṃ ca prasaktaṃ ca pathi śramam ||
children.translated_text: and he cast off sleep, drowsiness, and the weariness that had clung to him on the road.

children.text: tata utthāya te sarve spṛṣṭvā nadyāḥ śivaṃ jalam
children.translated_text: Then all of them rose and touched the auspicious water of the river,
and went along that road to <s>Citrakūṭa</s> pointed out by the seer.

children.text: tataḥ samprasthitaḥ kāle rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha
children.translated_text: Then, setting out at the proper time, <s>Rāma</s>, together with <s>Saumitri</s>,
spoke these words to lotus-petal-eyed <s>Sītā</s>:

children.text: ādīptān iva vaidehi sarvataḥ puṣpitān nagān
children.translated_text: <s>Vaidehī</s>, look at the kiṃśuka trees, flowering on all sides as if blazing,

children.text: svaiḥ puṣpaiḥ kiṃśukān paśya mālinaḥ śiśirātyaye ||
children.translated_text: garlanded with their own blossoms at the end of winter.
Look at the blooming bhallātaka trees, untouched by men,
bent down with fruits and leaves; surely I shall be able to live here.
Look, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, at the honeycombs hanging down, as large as a <s>droṇa</s> measure,
the honey gathered by the bees on tree after tree.

children.text: eṣa krośati natyūhas taṃ śikhī pratikūjati
children.translated_text: This <s>natyūha</s> bird cries out, and the peacock calls back to it
in a lovely stretch of forest, thick with a carpet of flowers.
Look at this mountain <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, frequented by herds of elephants and resounding with flocks of birds,
a mountain with lofty peaks.

children.text: tatas tau pādacāreṇa gacchantau saha sītayā
children.translated_text: Then the two, going on foot together with <s>Sītā</s>,
reached the delightful mountain <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, charming to the mind.
Having reached that mountain, filled with many flocks of birds, he said,

children.text: ayaṃ vāso bhavet tāvad atra saumya ramemahi ||
children.translated_text: "Let this be our dwelling for now; here, gentle one, we may take our pleasure.

children.text: lakṣmaṇānaya dārūṇi dṛḍhāni ca varāṇi ca
children.translated_text: Bring timbers, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, strong and excellent ones,
and make a dwelling, gentle one; my mind delights in living here."

children.text: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā saumitrir vividhān drumān
children.translated_text: Hearing that word of his, <s>Saumitri</s> brought many kinds of trees,
and then that subduer of enemies made a leaf-hut.
To him, attentive and eager to serve, he spoke this word:

children.text: aiṇeyaṃ māṃsam āhṛtya śālāṃ yakṣyāmahe vayam ||
children.translated_text: "Having brought antelope meat, we shall sacrifice for the hut."

children.text: sa lakṣmaṇaḥ kṛṣṇamṛgaṃ hatvā medhyaṃ pratāpavān
children.translated_text: Then mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, having killed a ritually fit black antelope,
<s>Saumitri</s> cast it into the kindled fire.

children.text: taṃ tu pakvaṃ samājñāya niṣṭaptaṃ chinnaśoṇitam
children.translated_text: Knowing it to be cooked, thoroughly roasted and drained of blood,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> then spoke to <s>Rāghava</s>, the tiger among men:

children.text: ayaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ samāptāṅgaḥ śṛtaḥ kṛṣṇamṛgo yathā
children.translated_text: "This black antelope, whole in all its limbs, has been cooked as a black antelope should be.

children.text: devatā devasaṃkāśa yajasva kuśalo hy asi ||
children.translated_text: O godlike one, O god, perform the sacrifice, for you are skilled."

children.text: rāmaḥ snātvā tu niyato guṇavāñ japyakovidaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s>, having bathed, self-restrained, virtuous, and skilled in recitation,
performed an excellent <s>bali</s> offering, one that quiets sin.

children.text: tāṃ vṛkṣaparṇacchadanāṃ manojñāṃ yathāpradeśaṃ sukṛtāṃ nivātām
children.translated_text: All of them together entered that charming hut, roofed with leaves, well made in a proper place and sheltered from the wind,

children.text: vāsāya sarve viviśuḥ sametāḥ sabhāṃ yathā devagaṇāḥ sudharmām ||
children.translated_text: for their dwelling, as the hosts of gods enter the <s>Sudharmā</s> assembly hall.
In that best of forests, crowded with many different beasts and birds, joined with trees bearing clusters of varied flowers,

children.text: vanottame vyālamṛgānunādite tathā vijahruḥ susukhaṃ jitendriyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and echoing with wild animals, they, with their senses mastered, passed their time very happily.

children.text: suramyam āsādya tu citrakūṭaṃ nadīṃ ca tāṃ mālyavatīṃ sutīrthām
children.translated_text: Having reached beautiful <s>Citrakūṭa</s> and that river <s>Mālyavatī</s>, rich in good fords,

children.text: nananda hṛṣṭo mṛgapakṣijuṣṭāṃ jahau ca duḥkhaṃ puravipravāsāt ||
children.translated_text: he rejoiced, delighted among the animals and birds, and gave up the sorrow caused by exile from the city.
After speaking for a long time with <s>Sumantra</s>, deeply afflicted with grief,
while <s>Rāma</s> remained on the southern bank, <s>Guha</s> went to his own home.
Then <s>Sumantra</s>, having been permitted to go and having yoked the best horses,
set out for the city <s>Ayodhyā</s>, deeply dejected in mind.

children.text: sa vanāni sugandhīni saritaś ca sarāṃsi ca
children.translated_text: Seeing fragrant forests, rivers, and lakes,

children.text: paśyann atiyayau śīghraṃ grāmāṇi nagarāṇi ca ||
children.translated_text: and also villages and cities, he passed quickly on.
Then, at evening time on the third day, the charioteer
reached <s>Ayodhyā</s> and saw it devoid of joy.

children.text: sa śūnyām iva niḥśabdāṃ dṛṣṭvā paramadurmanāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing it as if empty and silent, and being extremely downcast,
<s>Sumantra</s>, struck by the force of grief, began to think:

children.text: kaccin na sagajā sāśvā sajanā sajanādhipā
children.translated_text: "I hope this city, with its elephants and horses, with its people and its lord,
has not been burned by the fire of sorrow, through the anguish caused by <s>Rāma</s>."

children.text: iti cintāparaḥ sūtas tvaritaḥ praviveśa ha ||
children.translated_text: Thus absorbed in thought, the charioteer quickly entered.
As that <s>Sumantra</s> was approaching, hundreds and then thousands of men,

children.text: kva rāma iti pṛcchantaḥ sūtam abhyadravan narāḥ ||
children.translated_text: asking, "Where is <s>Rāma</s>?", ran up to the charioteer.

children.text: teṣāṃ śaśaṃsa gaṅgāyām aham āpṛcchya rāghavam
children.translated_text: He told them, "At the <s>Gaṅgā</s> I took leave of <s>Rāghava</s>;
permitted by that righteous, great-souled one, I have returned."

children.text: te tīrṇā iti vijñāya bāṣpapūrṇamukhā janāḥ
children.translated_text: Understanding that they had crossed over, the people, their faces filled with tears,

children.text: aho dhig iti niḥśvasya hā rāmeti ca cukruśuḥ ||
children.translated_text: sighed, "Ah, shame!", and cried out, "Alas, <s>Rāma</s>!"

children.text: śuśrāva ca vacas teṣāṃ vṛndaṃ vṛndaṃ ca tiṣṭhatām
children.translated_text: And he heard the words of those people standing group by group:

children.text: hatāḥ sma khalu ye neha paśyāma iti rāghavam ||
children.translated_text: "Surely we are ruined, since we do not see <s>Rāghava</s> here.
At gifts, sacrifices, weddings, and great assemblies,

children.text: na drakṣyāmaḥ punar jātu dhārmikaṃ rāmam antarā ||
children.translated_text: we shall never again behold righteous <s>Rāma</s> among us.

children.text: kiṃ samarthaṃ janasyāsya kiṃ priyaṃ kiṃ sukhāvaham
children.translated_text: Whatever was beneficial for this people, whatever was dear and conducive to happiness,
this city had been guarded by <s>Rāma</s> like a father."
And from the women standing at the windows and in the spaces between the shops,
women scorched by grief for <s>Rāma</s>, he heard their lamentation.
Then <s>Sumantra</s>, his face covered, went along the middle of the royal road

children.text: yatra rājā daśarathas tad evopayayau gṛham ||
children.translated_text: to that very palace where King <s>Daśaratha</s> was.

children.text: so 'vatīrya rathāc chīghraṃ rājaveśma praviśya ca
children.translated_text: Quickly descending from the chariot and entering the royal residence,
he passed through seven courtyards crowded with many people.
Then from the palaces of <s>Daśaratha</s>'s women, on every side,
he heard the low murmuring of those women, afflicted by grief for <s>Rāma</s>:

children.text: saha rāmeṇa niryāto vinā rāmam ihāgataḥ
children.translated_text: "He went out together with <s>Rāma</s> and has come here without <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: sūtaḥ kiṃ nāma kausalyāṃ śocantīṃ prativakṣyati ||
children.translated_text: What indeed will the charioteer say to grieving <s>Kausalyā</s>?

children.text: yathā ca manye durjīvam evaṃ na sukaraṃ dhruvam
children.translated_text: As I think, living is hard in such a case; surely it is not easy,

children.text: ācchidya putre niryāte kausalyā yatra jīvati ||
children.translated_text: when <s>Kausalyā</s> lives on after her son has gone away, torn from her."

children.text: satyarūpaṃ tu tadvākyaṃ rājñaḥ strīṇāṃ niśāmayan
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech of the king's women, true in its form,

children.text: pradīptam iva śokena viveśa sahasā gṛham ||
children.translated_text: he suddenly entered the palace, as if blazing with grief.

children.text: sa praviśyāṣṭamīṃ kakṣyāṃ rājānaṃ dīnam āturam
