children.translated_text: Entering the eighth court, he saw the king, wretched and afflicted,
wasted by grief for his son, in the pale royal house.

children.text: abhigamya tam āsīnaṃ narendram abhivādya ca
children.translated_text: Approaching that seated lord of men and saluting him,
<s>Sumantra</s> reported <s>Rāma</s>'s message exactly as it had been spoken.

children.text: sa tūṣṇīm eva tac chrutvā rājā vibhrāntacetanaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing it, the king remained silent, his mind bewildered;
oppressed by grief for <s>Rāma</s>, he fainted and fell to the ground.
Then, when the lord of the earth had fainted, the inner palace was thrown into agitation;

children.text: uddhṛtya bāhū cukrośa nṛpatau patite kṣitau ||
children.translated_text: when the king had fallen to the ground, it raised its arms and cried aloud.

children.text: sumitrayā tu sahitā kausalyā patitaṃ patim
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kauśalyā</s>, together with <s>Sumitrā</s>,
raised up her fallen husband and spoke these words:
Greatly blessed one, why do you not answer this messenger
who has come back from the forest-exile of that man who has performed a difficult deed?
Today, <s>Rāghava</s>, after causing this calamity, are you ashamed?

children.text: uttiṣṭha sukṛtaṃ te 'stu śoke na syāt sahāyatā ||
children.translated_text: Rise up; may good be yours. In grief there can be no help.

children.text: deva yasyā bhayād rāmaṃ nānupṛcchasi sārathim
children.translated_text: O lord, <s>Kaikeyī</s>, from fear of whom you do not question the charioteer about <s>Rāma</s>,
is not standing here; speak to him confidently.
Having thus addressed the great king, <s>Kauśalyā</s>, overcome with grief,
quickly fell upon the ground, her speech choked by tears.

children.text: evaṃ vilapatīṃ dṛṣṭvā kausalyāṃ patitāṃ bhuvi
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Kauśalyā</s> fallen on the ground and lamenting in this way,

children.text: patiṃ cāvekṣya tāḥ sarvāḥ sasvaraṃ ruruduḥ striyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and looking upon their husband, all those women wept aloud.

children.text: tatas tam antaḥpuranādam utthitaṃ samīkṣya vṛddhās taruṇāś ca mānavāḥ
children.translated_text: Then, seeing that cry of the inner palace arisen, the old men, the young men,

children.text: striyaś ca sarvā ruruduḥ samantataḥ puraṃ tadāsīt punar eva saṃkulam ||
children.translated_text: and all the women wept on every side, and that city once again became confused.

children.text: pratyāśvasto yadā rājā mohāt pratyāgataḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: When the king had recovered and returned again from his stupor,
then he summoned that charioteer in order to hear the news of <s>Rāma</s>.
The old man was deeply afflicted, like an elephant newly seized,
sighing, brooding, and like an elephant out of health.

children.text: rājā tu rajasā sūtaṃ dhvastāṅgaṃ samupasthitam
children.translated_text: But the king addressed the charioteer, who had come before him with limbs covered in dust,
his face full of tears, wretched, and in the highest distress:

children.text: kva nu vatsyati dharmātmā vṛkṣamūlam upāśritaḥ
children.translated_text: Where will the righteous one live, taking shelter at the foot of a tree?
Charioteer, what will that <s>Rāghava</s>, who was supremely accustomed to happiness, eat?
How does the son of the king lie on the ground like one without a protector?
He whom foot soldiers, chariots, and elephants used to follow when he went forth:

children.text: sa vatsyati kathaṃ rāmo vijanaṃ vanam āśritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: how will that <s>Rāma</s> live, resorting to a lonely forest?
A forest frequented by serpents and wild beasts, and inhabited by black snakes:

children.text: kathaṃ kumārau vaidehyā sārdhaṃ vanam upasthitau ||
children.translated_text: how have the two princes, together with <s>Vaidehī</s>, entered it?
With delicate, ascetic <s>Sītā</s>, O <s>Sumantra</s>,

children.text: rājaputrau kathaṃ pādair avaruhya rathād gatau ||
children.translated_text: how did the two royal sons go on foot after descending from the chariot?

children.text: siddhārthaḥ khalu sūta tvaṃ yena dṛṣṭau mamātmajau
children.translated_text: You, charioteer, are surely one whose purpose is fulfilled, since you saw my two sons

children.text: vanāntaṃ praviśantau tāv aśvināv iva mandaram ||
children.translated_text: entering the edge of the forest like the two <s>Aśvins</s> entering <s>Mandara</s>.

children.text: kim uvāca vaco rāmaḥ kim uvāca ca lakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: What words did <s>Rāma</s> say, and what did <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> say?

children.text: sumantra vanam āsādya kim uvāca ca maithilī
children.translated_text: O <s>Sumantra</s>, when they had reached the forest, what did <s>Maithilī</s> say?

children.text: āsitaṃ śayitaṃ bhuktaṃ sūta rāmasya kīrtaya ||
children.translated_text: Charioteer, tell me of <s>Rāma</s>'s sitting, sleeping, and eating.
Thus urged by the lord of men, the charioteer, with faltering
speech embraced by tears, addressed the king:
Great king, <s>Rāghava</s>, following <s>dharma</s> alone, spoke to me,
making an añjali and bowing his head in reverence:
Charioteer, by my words, of that father who knows himself,
of that great-souled one whose feet are to be honored with the head, honor those venerable feet.

children.text: sarvam antaḥpuraṃ vācyaṃ sūta madvacanāt tvayā
children.translated_text: The whole inner palace must be told by you, charioteer, in my words,
of my good health, and my greeting to each according to rank.

children.text: mātā ca mama kausalyā kuśalaṃ cābhivādanam
children.translated_text: And my mother <s>Kauśalyā</s> must be told of my welfare and given my greeting:

children.text: devi devasya pādau ca devavat paripālaya ||
children.translated_text: Lady, guard the lord's feet like those of a god.

children.text: bharataḥ kuśalaṃ vācyo vācyo madvacanena ca
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s> must be told of my welfare, and he must be told in my words:

children.text: sarvāsv eva yathānyāyaṃ vṛttiṃ vartasva mātṛṣu ||
children.translated_text: Conduct yourself properly toward all the mothers according to what is right.
And that mighty-armed delight of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> line must be told:
Standing in the rank of heir-apparent, protect your father established in the kingship.

children.text: ity evaṃ māṃ mahārāja bruvann eva mahāyaśāḥ
children.translated_text: Great king, while the greatly renowned one was speaking to me in just this way,
lotus-red-eyed <s>Rāma</s> shed tears profusely.

children.text: lakṣmaṇas tu susaṃkruddho niḥśvasan vākyam abravīt
children.translated_text: But <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, very angry and sighing, spoke this sentence:
For what offense has this royal son been banished?
If <s>Rāma</s> has been sent into exile because of an act done from greed,
or on account of the granting of boons, then in every way a wicked act has been done.

children.text: rāmasya tu parityāge na hetum upalakṣaye ||
children.translated_text: But I perceive no reason at all for the abandonment of <s>Rāma</s>.
Begun without proper consideration, contrary to reason, from lightness of judgment,
the banishment of <s>Rāghava</s> will produce outcry.
For my part, in the great king I do not perceive fatherhood.

children.text: bhrātā bhartā ca bandhuś ca pitā ca mama rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> is my brother, master, kinsman, and father.
Having abandoned one dear to all the world, devoted to the welfare of all the world,
how could all the world be attached to you by this deed?
But <s>Jānakī</s>, great king, the poor ascetic, sighing,
stood there bewildered, as if her mind had been struck by a spirit.
The glorious royal daughter, who had never before seen calamity,

children.text: tena duḥkhena rudatī naiva māṃ kiṃcid abravīt ||
children.translated_text: weeping from that sorrow, said nothing at all to me.
Looking up at her husband with a face dried up,

children.text: mumoca sahasā bāṣpaṃ māṃ prayāntam udīkṣya sā ||
children.translated_text: she suddenly shed tears when she saw me departing.
In just the same way <s>Rāma</s>, his face wet with tears and his hands joined, stood there, supported by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s arm;

children.text: tathaiva sītā rudatī tapasvinī nirīkṣate rājarathaṃ tathaiva mām ||
children.translated_text: in just the same way ascetic <s>Sītā</s>, weeping, kept looking at the royal chariot and at me.

children.text: mama tv aśvā nivṛttasya na prāvartanta vartmani
children.translated_text: But when I had turned back, my horses would not proceed on the road;

children.text: uṣṇam aśru vimuñcanto rāme samprasthite vanam ||
children.translated_text: they poured out hot tears when <s>Rāma</s> had set out for the forest.
Then, after making an añjali to both royal sons,

children.text: prasthito ratham āsthāya tad duḥkham api dhārayan ||
children.translated_text: I set out, mounting the chariot, though I was bearing that grief.

children.text: guhena sārdhaṃ tatraiva sthito 'smi divasān bahūn
children.translated_text: I remained there together with <s>Guha</s> for many days,

children.text: āśayā yadi māṃ rāmaḥ punaḥ śabdāpayed iti ||
children.translated_text: in the hope that <s>Rāma</s> might call me back again.
In your realm, great king, worn down by the calamity of <s>Rāma</s>,
even the trees, though bearing flowers, shoots, and buds, have withered.

children.text: na ca sarpanti sattvāni vyālā na prasaranti ca
children.translated_text: Creatures do not move about, and wild beasts do not range abroad.
Overcome by grief for <s>Rāma</s>, that forest became silent.
The lotus-ponds, lord of men, have withdrawn lotus leaves and turbid waters;
their lotuses are scorched, and their fish and birds are hidden away.

children.text: jalajāni ca puṣpāṇi mālyāni sthalajāni ca
children.translated_text: The water-born flowers, the garland-flowers growing on land,

children.text: nādya bhānty alpagandhīni phalāni ca yathā puram ||
children.translated_text: and the fruits, now faint in fragrance, do not shine as they did before.

children.text: praviśantam ayodhyāṃ māṃ na kaścid abhinandati
children.translated_text: As I entered <s>Ayodhyā</s>, no one welcomed me.

children.text: narā rāmam apaśyanto niḥśvasanti muhur muhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The men, not seeing <s>Rāma</s>, sigh again and again.

children.text: harmyair vimānaiḥ prāsādair avekṣya ratham āgatam
children.translated_text: Seeing from mansions, aerial chambers, and palaces that the chariot had arrived,
the women, wasted by not seeing <s>Rāma</s>, raised cries of grief.
With their long, clear eyes flooded by the rush of tears,
the women looked at one another, plainly still more afflicted.
Among enemies, friends, and indifferent people alike,
because of their distress, I perceive no difference in anyone.
With its people joyless, its elephants and horses dejected,
faded with cries of pain and resounding with sighs,
devoid of delight, great king, and afflicted by <s>Rāma</s>'s banishment,
<s>Ayodhyā</s> appears to me like <s>Kauśalyā</s> bereft of her son.
Hearing the charioteer's words, the king, in an exceedingly piteous voice,

children.text: bāṣpopahatayā rājā taṃ sūtam idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: choked with tears, said this to that charioteer:
Urged on by <s>Kaikeyī</s>, whose nature was born of evil lineage,

children.text: mayā na mantrakuśalair vṛddhaiḥ saha samarthitam ||
children.translated_text: I did not consult with elders skilled in counsel.

children.text: na suhṛdbhir na cāmātyair mantrayitvā na naigamaiḥ
children.translated_text: Without taking counsel with friends, ministers, or citizens,

children.text: mayāyam arthaḥ sammohāt strīhetoḥ sahasā kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: through delusion, for the sake of a woman, I have done this thing suddenly.

children.text: bhavitavyatayā nūnam idaṃ vā vyasanaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: Surely by the force of what had to be, this great calamity
has come by chance, charioteer, for the destruction of this family.

children.text: sūta yady asti te kiṃcin mayāpi sukṛtaṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: Charioteer, if any good deed has been done for you by me,

children.text: tvaṃ prāpayāśu māṃ rāmaṃ prāṇāḥ saṃtvarayanti mām ||
children.translated_text: bring me quickly to <s>Rāma</s>; my life-breaths are hurrying me on.

children.text: yad yad yāpi mamaivājñā nivartayatu rāghavam
children.translated_text: Let whatever command of mine there may be turn <s>Rāghava</s> back.

children.text: na śakṣyāmi vinā rāmaṃ muhūrtam api jīvitum ||
children.translated_text: I shall not be able to live even for a moment without <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: atha vāpi mahābāhur gato dūraṃ bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Or, if the mighty-armed one will have gone far away,

children.text: mām eva ratham āropya śīghraṃ rāmāya darśaya ||
children.translated_text: place me myself in the chariot and quickly show me to <s>Rāma</s>.
Where is that great archer, fine-toothed, the elder brother of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>?

children.text: yadi jīvāmi sādhv enaṃ paśyeyaṃ saha sītayā ||
children.translated_text: If I live, may I indeed see him together with <s>Sītā</s>.
If I do not see <s>Rāma</s>, red-eyed, mighty-armed,

children.text: rāmaṃ yadi na paśyāmi gamiṣyāmi yamakṣayam ||
children.translated_text: wearing jeweled earrings, I shall go to the abode of <s>Yama</s>.

children.text: ato nu kiṃ duḥkhataraṃ yo 'ham ikṣvākunandanam
children.translated_text: What, then, could be more painful than this, that I, in such a state,

children.text: imām avasthām āpanno neha paśyāmi rāghavam ||
children.translated_text: do not see here <s>Rāghava</s>, the delight of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s>s?

children.text: hā rāma rāmānuja hā hā vaidehi tapasvini
children.translated_text: Ah <s>Rāma</s>! Ah younger brother of <s>Rāma</s>! Ah, ah, ascetic <s>Vaidehī</s>!

children.text: na māṃ jānīta duḥkhena mriyamāṇam anāthavat
children.translated_text: You do not know that I am dying of grief like one without a protector.
O queen, this ocean of grief is hard for me, while living, to cross.

children.text: aśobhanaṃ yo 'ham ihādya rāghavaṃ didṛkṣamāṇo na labhe salakṣmaṇam
children.translated_text: It is an evil thing that, desiring to see <s>Rāghava</s> here today together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, I do not obtain him.

children.text: itīva rājā vilapan mahāyaśāḥ papāta tūrṇaṃ śayane sa mūrchitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Lamenting in this way, the king of great fame at once fell senseless upon his bed.

children.text: iti vilapati pārthive pranaṣṭe karuṇataraṃ dviguṇaṃ ca rāmahetoḥ
children.translated_text: As the lord of the earth lamented thus and lost consciousness, more pitiably and with doubled grief on account of <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: vacanam anuniśamya tasya devī bhayam agamat punar eva rāmamātā ||
children.translated_text: the queen, <s>Rāma</s>'s mother, hearing his words, became afraid once again.
Then, as if possessed by a spirit, trembling again and again,
<s>Kauśalyā</s>, as though bereft of life upon the ground, spoke to the charioteer:

children.text: naya māṃ yatra kākutsthaḥ sītā yatra ca lakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Take me where <s>Kākutstha</s> is, and where <s>Sītā</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> are.

children.text: tān vinā kṣaṇam apy atra jīvituṃ notsahe hy aham ||
children.translated_text: Without them I cannot bear to live here even for a moment.

children.text: nivartaya rathaṃ śīghraṃ daṇḍakān naya mām api
children.translated_text: Turn the chariot back quickly; take me too to the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest.
But if I do not follow them, I shall go to the abode of <s>Yama</s>.
With her voice checked by the rush of tears and faltering,

children.text: idam āśvāsayan devīṃ sūtaḥ prāñjalir abravīt ||
children.translated_text: the charioteer, consoling the queen, spoke these words with folded hands:

children.text: tyaja śokaṃ ca mohaṃ ca sambhramaṃ duḥkhajaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Give up grief, delusion, and the bewilderment born of sorrow.

children.text: vyavadhūya ca saṃtāpaṃ vane vatsyati rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Shaking off distress, <s>Rāghava</s> will dwell in the forest.

children.text: lakṣmaṇaś cāpi rāmasya pādau paricaran vane
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> too, serving <s>Rāma</s>'s feet in the forest,
righteous and self-controlled, is winning merit for the next world.

children.text: vijane 'pi vane sītā vāsaṃ prāpya gṛheṣv iva
children.translated_text: Even in the lonely forest, <s>Sītā</s>, having found dwelling there as though in her own homes,
gains confidence, unafraid, with her mind entrusted to <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: nāsyā dainyaṃ kṛtaṃ kiṃcit susūkṣmam api lakṣaye
children.translated_text: I observe that no wretchedness at all has been caused in her,
not even the slightest; <s>Vaidehī</s> seems to me as though accustomed to exile.

children.text: nagaropavanaṃ gatvā yathā sma ramate purā
children.translated_text: Just as she used to take pleasure in the past when she went to the city groves,

children.text: tathaiva ramate sītā nirjaneṣu vaneṣv api ||
children.translated_text: so <s>Sītā</s> takes pleasure even in deserted forests.
<s>Sītā</s>, whose face is like the young moon, takes delight like a child;

children.text: rāmā rāme hy adhīnātmā vijane 'pi vane satī ||
children.translated_text: that lovely woman has her self dependent on <s>Rāma</s>, though she is a virtuous woman in the lonely forest.

children.text: tadgataṃ hṛdayaṃ hy asyās tadadhīnaṃ ca jīvitam
children.translated_text: Her heart has gone to him, and her life depends upon him.

children.text: ayodhyāpi bhavet tasyā rāmahīnā tathā vanam ||
children.translated_text: Even <s>Ayodhyā</s>, without <s>Rāma</s>, would be for her just like the forest.

children.text: pathi pṛcchati vaidehī grāmāṃś ca nagarāṇi ca
children.translated_text: On the road <s>Vaidehī</s> asks about villages and cities,

children.text: gatiṃ dṛṣṭvā nadīnāṃ ca pādapān vividhān api ||
children.translated_text: and, seeing the course of rivers, about many kinds of trees too.
By the journey, by the force of the wind, by agitation, and by the heat,

children.text: na hi gacchati vaidehyāś candrāṃśusadṛśī prabhā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vaidehī</s>'s radiance, like moonbeams, does not fade.
It is like a hundred-petalled lotus, with a radiance like the full moon.
The face of that noble <s>Vaidehī</s> does not tremble.
Her two feet, appearing red with lac-dye though free of lac-dye,
even now shine like lotus buds.
The lovely woman walks playfully, as if with the graceful jingle of anklets;
even now <s>Vaidehī</s>, her love fixed on him, has laid aside her ornaments.

children.text: gajaṃ vā vīkṣya siṃhaṃ vā vyāghraṃ vā vanam āśritā
children.translated_text: When she sees an elephant, a lion, or a tiger in the forest where she dwells,
she feels no terror, for she clings to the arms of <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: na śocyās te na cātmā te śocyo nāpi janādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: They are not to be pitied, nor are you to be pitied, nor even the lord of men;

children.text: idaṃ hi caritaṃ loke pratiṣṭhāsyati śāśvatam ||
children.translated_text: for this deed will stand in the world forever.

children.text: vidhūya śokaṃ parihṛṣṭamānasā maharṣiyāte pathi suvyavasthitāḥ
children.translated_text: Having shaken off sorrow, with delighted minds, firmly set on the path trodden by great seers,

children.text: vane ratā vanyaphalāśanāḥ pituḥ śubhāṃ pratijñāṃ paripālayanti te ||
children.translated_text: delighting in the forest and eating forest fruits, they are fulfilling their father's auspicious promise.
Yet, though the charioteer restrained her with well-spoken words, she was wasted by grief for her son;

children.text: na caiva devī virarāma kūjitāt priyeti putreti ca rāghaveti ca ||
children.translated_text: the queen did not cease from crying out, 'Beloved!', 'My son!', and '<s>Rāghava</s>!'

children.text: vanaṃ gate dharmapare rāme ramayatāṃ vare
children.translated_text: When dharma-minded <s>Rāma</s>, best of those who bring delight, had gone to the forest,

children.text: kausalyā rudatī svārtā bhartāram idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kausalyā</s>, weeping and afflicted in herself, spoke these words to her husband:

children.text: yadyapi triṣu lokeṣu prathitaṃ te mahad yaśaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Although your great fame is renowned throughout the three worlds,

children.text: sānukrośo vadānyaś ca priyavādī ca rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and you, O <s>Rāghava</s>, are compassionate, generous, and gentle in speech,

children.text: kathaṃ naravaraśreṣṭha putrau tau saha sītayā
children.translated_text: how, best and foremost of men, will those two sons, together with <s>Sītā</s>,
raised in comfort and now distressed, endure hardship in the forest?

children.text: sā nūnaṃ taruṇī śyāmā sukumārī sukhocitā
children.translated_text: Surely that young, dark, delicate woman, accustomed to comfort,

children.text: katham uṣṇaṃ ca śītaṃ ca maithilī prasahiṣyate ||
children.translated_text: how will <s>Maithilī</s> bear heat and cold?
After eating fine food with soups and condiments, she of the wide eyes,
how will <s>Sītā</s> eat wild nivāra grain as her food?
After hearing the auspicious sound of song and instruments, that blameless woman,
how will she hear the dreadful cries of flesh-eaters and lions?
Where now does the mighty-armed one, like the banner of <s>Mahendra</s>, sleep,
the greatly powerful one laying down his arm, like an iron bar, as a pillow?
When shall I see <s>Rāma</s>'s face, lotus-colored, edged with fine hair,
excellent, lotus-fragrant, and lotus-eyed?

children.text: vajrasāramayaṃ nūnaṃ hṛdayaṃ me na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Surely my heart is made of the substance of the thunderbolt; there is no doubt,

children.text: apaśyantyā na taṃ yad vai phalatīdaṃ sahasradhā ||
children.translated_text: since, though I do not see him, it does not split here into a thousand pieces.

children.text: yadi pañcadaśe varṣe rāghavaḥ punar eṣyati
children.translated_text: If <s>Rāghava</s> returns in the fifteenth year,

children.text: jahyād rājyaṃ ca kośaṃ ca bharatenopabhokṣyate ||
children.translated_text: he may abandon the kingdom and the treasury, already enjoyed by <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: evaṃ kanīyasā bhrātrā bhuktaṃ rājyaṃ viśāṃ pate
children.translated_text: When the kingdom has thus been enjoyed by a younger brother, O lord of the people,

children.text: bhrātā jyeṣṭho variṣṭhaś ca kimarthaṃ nāvamaṃsyate ||
children.translated_text: why would the elder and superior brother not disdain it?

children.text: na pareṇāhṛtaṃ bhakṣyaṃ vyāghraḥ khāditum icchati
children.translated_text: A tiger does not wish to eat food brought by another;

children.text: evam eva naravyāghraḥ paralīḍhaṃ na maṃsyate ||
children.translated_text: in just the same way, the tiger among men will not value what has been licked by another.

children.text: havir ājyaṃ puroḍāśāḥ kuśā yūpāś ca khādirāḥ
children.translated_text: Oblations, ghee, sacrificial cakes, kuśa grass, and sacrificial posts of khadira wood,
when they have passed their proper time, are not used again in a sacrifice.

children.text: tathā hy āttam idaṃ rājyaṃ hṛtasārāṃ surām iva
children.translated_text: So too this kingdom, once taken, is like liquor whose essence has been removed;
<s>Rāma</s> cannot approve it, like a sacrifice whose soma has been lost.
<s>Rāghava</s> will not endure such an insult,
just as a powerful tiger will not endure the touching of its tail.
Such a man, lion-strong, bull-eyed, a bull among men,

children.text: svayam eva hataḥ pitrā jalajenātmajo yathā ||
children.translated_text: has himself been slain by his father, like an offspring by a water-born creature.
If this eternal <s>dharma</s>, practiced by the twice-born and seen in scripture, is yours,

children.text: yadi te dharmanirate tvayā putre vivāsite ||
children.translated_text: O you devoted to <s>dharma</s>, then by you your son has been exiled.

children.text: gatir ekā patir nāryā dvitīyā gatir ātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: For a woman, one refuge is her husband; a second refuge is her son;

children.text: tṛtīyā jñātayo rājaṃś caturthī neha vidyate ||
children.translated_text: her kinsmen are the third, O king; a fourth does not exist here.

children.text: tatra tvaṃ caiva me nāsti rāmaś ca vanam āśritaḥ
children.translated_text: Among these, you are no longer mine, and <s>Rāma</s> has taken to the forest.

children.text: na vanaṃ gantum icchāmi sarvathā hi hatā tvayā ||
children.translated_text: I do not wish to go to the forest; in every way I have been ruined by you.

children.text: hataṃ tvayā rājyam idaṃ sarāṣṭraṃ hatas tathātmā saha mantribhiś ca
children.translated_text: You have destroyed this kingdom together with its realm, and likewise yourself together with your ministers;

children.text: hatā saputrāsmi hatāś ca paurāḥ sutaś ca bhāryā ca tava prahṛṣṭau ||
children.translated_text: I am destroyed along with my son, the citizens are destroyed, while your son and wife are delighted.'

children.text: imāṃ giraṃ dāruṇaśabdasaṃśritāṃ niśamya rājāpi mumoha duḥkhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing this speech, filled with harsh sounds, the king too fainted in sorrow;

children.text: tataḥ sa śokaṃ praviveśa pārthivaḥ svaduṣkṛtaṃ cāpi punas tadāsmarat ||
children.translated_text: then the ruler entered into grief and again remembered his own evil deed.

children.text: evaṃ tu kruddhayā rājā rāmamātrā saśokayā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed with harsh words by <s>Rāma</s>'s mother,
who was angry and full of sorrow, the king thought in misery.
As he was thinking, his evil deed came back to him,

children.text: yad anena kṛtaṃ pūrvam ajñānāc chabdavedhinā ||
children.translated_text: what he had done long before, in ignorance, as an archer striking by sound.

children.text: amanās tena śokena rāmaśokena ca prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: His mind undone by that sorrow and by sorrow for <s>Rāma</s>, the lord,

children.text: dahyamānas tu śokābhyāṃ kausalyām āha bhūpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: burning with both griefs, said to <s>Kausalyā</s>:
'I seek to appease you, <s>Kausalyā</s>; this folded supplication has been made by me.

children.text: vatsalā cānṛśaṃsā ca tvaṃ hi nityaṃ pareṣv api ||
children.translated_text: For you are loving and compassionate always, even toward others.

children.text: bhartā tu khalu nārīṇāṃ guṇavān nirguṇo 'pi vā
children.translated_text: For women, whether he has virtues or even lacks virtues,
a husband, O queen, is a visible deity when they reflect upon <s>dharma</s>.
You are always devoted to <s>dharma</s> and have seen the higher and lower ways of the world;
though distressed, you should not speak what is painful to one who is already deeply distressed.'

children.text: tad vākyaṃ karuṇaṃ rājñaḥ śrutvā dīnasya bhāṣitam
children.translated_text: Hearing the king's compassionate words, spoken by that wretched man,
<s>Kausalyā</s> let her tears flow like a channel pouring fresh water.

children.text: sa mūrdhni baddhvā rudatī rājñaḥ padmam ivāñjalim
children.translated_text: Weeping, she placed upon her head her lotus-like folded hands before the king,
and, frightened in her agitation, spoke words with hurried syllables:

children.text: prasīda śirasā yāce bhūmau nipatitāsmi te
children.translated_text: 'Be gracious. With my head I beg you; I have fallen on the ground before you.'

children.text: yācitāsmi hatā deva hantavyāhaṃ na hi tvayā ||
children.translated_text: I have been entreated, my lord; I am stricken. I ought not to be slain by you.

children.text: naiṣā hi sā strī bhavati ślāghanīyena dhīmatā
children.translated_text: For a woman whom her husband must appease is not one praised by the wise,

children.text: ubhayor lokayor vīra patyā yā saṃprasādyate ||
children.translated_text: O hero, in either of the two worlds.

children.text: jānāmi dharmaṃ dharmajña tvāṃ jāne satyavādinam
children.translated_text: I know <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), O knower of <s>dharma</s>; I know you as a speaker of truth.

children.text: putraśokārtayā tat tu mayā kimapi bhāṣitam ||
children.translated_text: But, afflicted by grief for my son, I spoke something improper.

children.text: śoko nāśayate dhairyaṃ śoko nāśayate śrutam
children.translated_text: Grief destroys courage; grief destroys learning.

children.text: śoko nāśayate sarvaṃ nāsti śokasamo ripuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Grief destroys everything. There is no enemy equal to grief.
A blow fallen from an enemy's hand can be endured,

children.text: soḍhum āpatitaḥ śokaḥ susūkṣmo 'pi na śakyate ||
children.translated_text: but grief, once it has fallen, cannot be endured, even if it is very subtle.
Today five nights are counted for <s>Rāma</s>'s dwelling in the forest,
but for me, whose joy has been struck down by grief, they are like five years.

children.text: taṃ hi cintayamānāyāḥ śoko 'yaṃ hṛdi vardhate
children.translated_text: As I think of him, this grief grows in my heart,
like the great water of the ocean under the force of rivers.

children.text: evaṃ hi kathayantyās tu kausalyāyāḥ śubhaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: While <s>Kausalyā</s> was thus speaking auspicious words,
the sun became dim-rayed, and night came on.

children.text: atha prahlādito vākyair devyā kausalyayā nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the king, gladdened by the words of Queen <s>Kausalyā</s>,

children.text: śokena ca samākrānto nidrāyā vaśam eyivān ||
children.translated_text: yet overcome by grief, came under the power of sleep.
Awakened after a short while, his consciousness stricken by grief,

children.text: atha rājā daśarathaḥ sa cintām abhyapadyata ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Daśaratha</s> then fell into anxious reflection.
Because of the banishment of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, he, who was like <s>Vāsava</s>,
was entered by an affliction, as demonic darkness enters the sun.

children.text: sa rājā rajanīṃ ṣaṣṭhīṃ rāme pravrajite vanam
children.translated_text: On the sixth night after <s>Rāma</s> had gone forth to the forest,
at midnight <s>Daśaratha</s>, remembering an evil deed he had done,
spoke these words to <s>Kausalyā</s>, who was afflicted by grief for her son:

children.text: yad ācarati kalyāṇi śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham
children.translated_text: Whatever a doer does, O noble lady, whether good or bad,

children.text: tad eva labhate bhadre kartā karmajam ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that very result, born from his own act, he obtains, O blessed one.
One who, at the outset of actions, does not know the weight or lightness of aims,

children.text: doṣaṃ vā yo na jānāti sa bāla iti hocyate ||
children.translated_text: or their fruit or fault, is said to be a child.

children.text: kaścid āmravaṇaṃ chittvā palāśāṃś ca niṣiñcati
children.translated_text: Someone, after cutting down a mango grove, waters palāśa trees;

children.text: puṣpaṃ dṛṣṭvā phale gṛdhnuḥ sa śocati phalāgame ||
children.translated_text: greedy for fruit when he has seen the blossom, he grieves when fruit-time comes.

children.text: so 'ham āmravaṇaṃ chittvā palāśāṃś ca nyaṣecayam
children.translated_text: So I, after cutting down a mango grove, watered palāśa trees.

children.text: rāmaṃ phalāgame tyaktvā paścāc chocāmi durmatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having cast away <s>Rāma</s> at fruit-time, I grieve afterward, foolish-minded as I am.
O <s>Kausalyā</s>, when I was a young prince with a bow, famed for hitting by sound,

children.text: kumāraḥ śabdavedhīti mayā pāpam idaṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: this sin was committed by me, a youth called a sound-shooter.

children.text: tad idaṃ me 'nusaṃprāptaṃ devi duḥkhaṃ svayaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: That sorrow, O queen, self-made by me, has now come upon me.

children.text: sammohād iha bālena yathā syād bhakṣitaṃ viṣam
children.translated_text: As poison might be eaten here by a child through delusion,
so too, unrecognized by me, was this fruit made of shooting by sound.

children.text: devy anūḍhā tvam abhavo yuvarājo bhavāmy aham
children.translated_text: O queen, you were not yet married, and I was the crown prince.
Then the rainy season arrived, increasing intoxication and desire.

children.text: upāsya hi rasān bhaumāṃs taptvā ca jagad aṃśubhiḥ
children.translated_text: Having drawn up the earthly juices and heated the world with its rays,
the sun enters the fearful quarter trodden by the departed.

children.text: uṣṇam antardadhe sadyaḥ snigdhā dadṛśire ghanāḥ
children.translated_text: The heat at once disappeared; moist clouds were seen.
Then all the frogs, deer, and peacocks rejoiced.
Covered by fallen rain and by rain repeatedly falling,
the mountain, with its excited deer, shone like a mass of water.

children.text: tasminn atisukhe kāle dhanuṣmān iṣumān rathī
children.translated_text: In that very pleasant season, armed with bow and arrows and riding in a chariot,
I went along the river <s>Sarayū</s>, resolved on exercise.

children.text: nipāne mahiṣaṃ rātrau gajaṃ vābhyāgataṃ nadīm
children.translated_text: At night, at a drinking-place, I wished to kill a buffalo, or an elephant that had come to the river,

children.text: anyaṃ vā śvāpadaṃ kaṃcij jighāṃsur ajitendriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or some other wild beast; I was not master of my senses.

children.text: athāndhakāre tv aśrauṣaṃ jale kumbhasya pūryataḥ
children.translated_text: Then in the darkness I heard, in the water, the sound of a pot being filled,
a noise beyond the range of sight, like the roaring of an elephant.
Then, drawing out a blazing arrow like a venomous serpent,
I released the sharp shaft, like a venomous serpent.

children.text: tatra vāg uṣasi vyaktā prādurāsīd vanaukasaḥ
children.translated_text: There a clear voice of a forest-dweller arose, as at daybreak.

children.text: hā heti patatas toye vāg abhūt tatra mānuṣī
children.translated_text: As he fell into the water, a human voice there cried, "Ah! Alas!"

children.text: katham asmadvidhe śastraṃ nipatet tu tapasvini ||
children.translated_text: "How could a weapon fall upon an ascetic like me?
I came at night to this secluded river to draw water.

children.text: iṣuṇābhihataḥ kena kasya vā kiṃ kṛtaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: By whom have I been struck with an arrow? What have I done, and to whom?

children.text: ṛṣer hi nyastadaṇḍasya vane vanyena jīvataḥ
children.translated_text: For a seer who has laid aside violence and lives in the forest on forest fare,

children.text: kathaṃ nu śastreṇa vadho madvidhasya vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: how can death by a weapon be ordained for one such as I?
I wear a mass of matted hair and garments of bark and antelope skin.

children.text: ko vadhena mamārthī syāt kiṃ vāsyāpakṛtaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: Who could have any purpose in killing me? What wrong have I done to him?
This undertaking is fruitless and joined only with harm.

children.text: na kaścit sādhu manyeta yathaiva gurutalpagam ||
children.translated_text: No good person would approve it, just as no one would approve one who violates his teacher's bed.
I do not grieve so much over the loss of my own life;
I grieve for both my mother and my father, when one like me is gone.

children.text: tad etan mithunaṃ vṛddhaṃ cirakālabhṛtaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: That aged pair has long been supported by me.

children.text: mayi pañcatvam āpanne kāṃ vṛttiṃ vartayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: When I have gone to the state of the five elements, what livelihood will they follow?

children.text: vṛddhau ca mātāpitarāv ahaṃ caikeṣuṇā hataḥ
children.translated_text: My aged mother and father, and I too, have been slain by one arrow.
By whom have we all been killed, by an immature, uncontrolled boy?

children.text: tāṃ giraṃ karuṇāṃ śrutvā mama dharmānukāṅkṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that pitiful voice, I, who longed for <s>dharma</s> (righteous conduct),
was shaken, and the bow with its arrow fell from my hands to the ground.

children.text: taṃ deśam aham āgamya dīnasattvaḥ sudurmanāḥ
children.translated_text: Coming to that place, poor in spirit and deeply dejected,

children.text: apaśyam iṣuṇā tīre sarayvās tāpasaṃ hatam ||
children.translated_text: I saw an ascetic on the bank of the <s>Sarayū</s>, struck down by my arrow.

children.text: sa mām udvīkṣya netrābhyāṃ trastam asvasthacetasam
children.translated_text: Looking up at me with his eyes, as I trembled and my mind was unsettled,

children.text: ity uvāca vacaḥ krūraṃ didhakṣann iva tejasā ||
children.translated_text: he spoke this harsh speech, as if wishing to burn me with his splendor:

children.text: kiṃ tavāpakṛtaṃ rājan vane nivasatā mayā
children.translated_text: "What wrong have I done to you, O king, while living in the forest?

children.text: jihīrṣur ambho gurvarthaṃ yad ahaṃ tāḍitas tvayā ||
children.translated_text: Wishing to fetch water for my honored elders, I have been struck by you.

children.text: ekena khalu bāṇena marmaṇy abhihate mayi
children.translated_text: For with a single arrow I have been hit in a vital spot,

children.text: dvāv andhau nihatau vṛddhau mātā janayitā ca me ||
children.translated_text: and two blind old people have been slain: my mother and my father.

children.text: tau nūnaṃ durbalāv andhau matpratīkṣau pipāsitau
children.translated_text: Surely those two, weak and blind, waiting for me and thirsty,
will long sustain that painful thirst, their hope fixed on me.

children.text: na nūnaṃ tapaso vāsti phalayogaḥ śrutasya vā
children.translated_text: Surely there is no joining of fruit to austerity or to sacred learning,

children.text: pitā yan māṃ na jānāti śayānaṃ patitaṃ bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: since my father does not know that I am lying fallen on the ground.

children.text: jānann api ca kiṃ kuryād aśaktir aparikramaḥ
children.translated_text: And even if he knew, what could he do, powerless and without means?

children.text: bhidyamānam ivāśaktas trātum anyo nago nagam ||
children.translated_text: One helpless tree cannot save another tree that is being split.

children.text: pitus tvam eva me gatvā śīghram ācakṣva rāghava
children.translated_text: Go yourself quickly to my father and tell him, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: na tvām anudahet kruddho vanaṃ vahnir ivaidhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Otherwise, in anger, he may burn you like a blazing fire burning a forest.

children.text: iyam ekapadī rājan yato me pitur āśramaḥ
children.translated_text: This single footpath, O king, leads to my father's hermitage.

children.text: taṃ prasādaya gatvā tvaṃ na tvāṃ sa kupitaḥ śapet ||
children.translated_text: Go and appease him, so that he does not curse you in wrath.

children.text: viśalyaṃ kuru māṃ rājan marma me niśitaḥ śaraḥ
children.translated_text: Remove the barb from me, O king; the sharp arrow in my vital spot

children.text: ruṇaddhi mṛdu sotsedhaṃ tīram amburayo yathā ||
children.translated_text: blocks my tender, swollen wound as a rush of water blocks a bank.

children.text: na dvijātir ahaṃ rājan mā bhūt te manaso vyathā
children.translated_text: I am not a twice-born man, O king; let there be no anguish in your mind.
I was born from a <s>Vaiśya</s> father and a <s>Śūdra</s> mother, O lord of the land.
As he spoke thus with difficulty, his vital part struck by the arrow,

children.text: tasya tv ānamyamānasya taṃ bāṇam aham uddharam ||
children.translated_text: and as his body bent, I drew that arrow out of him.

children.text: jalārdragātraṃ tu vilapya kṛcchrān marmavraṇaṃ saṃtatam ucchvasantam
children.translated_text: After lamenting painfully over him, his body wet with water, continually gasping from the mortal wound,

children.text: tataḥ sarayvāṃ tam ahaṃ śayānaṃ samīkṣya bhadre subhṛśaṃ viṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I saw him lying there by the <s>Sarayū</s>, O fair lady, and became deeply despondent.

children.text: tad ajñānān mahat pāpaṃ kṛtvā saṃkulitendriyaḥ
children.translated_text: Having committed that great sin through ignorance, with my senses confounded,

children.text: ekas tv acintayaṃ buddhyā kathaṃ nu sukṛtaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: I alone reflected with my mind: how now could any good be done?

children.text: tatas taṃ ghaṭam ādāya pūrṇaṃ paramavāriṇā
children.translated_text: Then, taking up the pot filled with excellent water,

children.text: āśramaṃ tam ahaṃ prāpya yathākhyātapathaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: I went by the path he had described and reached that hermitage.
There I saw his parents, weak, blind, old, and without a guide,

children.text: apaśyaṃ tasya pitarau lūnapakṣāv iva dvijau ||
children.translated_text: like two birds whose wings had been cut off.
They were sitting there, unable to move, with conversations centered on him,

children.text: tām āśāṃ matkṛte hīnāv udāsīnāv anāthavat ||
children.translated_text: bereft, because of me, of that hope, sitting dejected like people without protectors.

children.text: padaśabdaṃ tu me śrutvā munir vākyam abhāṣata
children.translated_text: But when he heard the sound of my footsteps, the sage spoke these words:

children.text: kiṃ cirāyasi me putra pānīyaṃ kṣipram ānaya ||
children.translated_text: Why are you so long, my son? Bring the water quickly.

children.text: yannimittam idaṃ tāta salile krīḍitaṃ tvayā
children.translated_text: Whatever the reason, child, that you have been playing in the water,

children.text: utkaṇṭhitā te māteyaṃ praviśa kṣipram āśramam ||
children.translated_text: this mother of yours is anxious; enter the hermitage quickly.

children.text: yad vyalīkaṃ kṛtaṃ putra mātrā te yadi vā mayā
children.translated_text: Whatever wrong has been done, my son, by your mother or by me,

children.text: na tan manasi kartavyaṃ tvayā tāta tapasvinā ||
children.translated_text: you, child and ascetic, should not take it to heart.

children.text: tvaṃ gatis tv agatīnāṃ ca cakṣus tvaṃ hīnacakṣuṣām
children.translated_text: You are the refuge of those without refuge, and you are the eyes of those without eyes.

children.text: samāsaktās tvayi prāṇāḥ kiṃcin nau nābhibhāṣase ||
children.translated_text: Our lives are fastened upon you. Why do you not speak even a little to us?

children.text: munim avyaktayā vācā tam ahaṃ sajjamānayā
children.translated_text: Looking at that sage, in an indistinct voice,
stammering and lacking clear syllables, afraid as if made still more afraid, I spoke.
Steadying the strength of my speech with mind, action, and effort,

children.text: ācacakṣe tv ahaṃ tasmai putravyasanajaṃ bhayam ||
children.translated_text: I told him of the fearful calamity concerning his son.
I am a <s>kṣatriya</s>, <s>Daśaratha</s>; I am not the noble one's son.
This sorrow, condemned by the good and born of my own deed, has come upon me.
Blessed sir, bow in hand I had come to the bank of the <s>Sarayū</s>,

children.text: jighāṃsuḥ śvāpadaṃ kiṃcin nipāne vāgataṃ gajam ||
children.translated_text: intending to kill some wild animal, or an elephant that had come to the watering place.

children.text: tatra śruto mayā śabdo jale kumbhasya pūryataḥ
children.translated_text: There I heard in the water the sound of a jar being filled.

children.text: dvipo 'yam iti matvā hi bāṇenābhihato mayā ||
children.translated_text: Thinking, 'This is an elephant,' I struck it with an arrow.

children.text: gatvā nadyās tatas tīram apaśyam iṣuṇā hṛdi
children.translated_text: Then, going to the riverbank, I saw an ascetic on the ground, pierced in the heart by the arrow,
lying there, his life departed.
Blessed sir, aiming by sound and wishing to kill an elephant,

children.text: visṛṣṭo 'mbhasi nārācas tena te nihataḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I released a barbed arrow into the water, and by it your son was slain.

children.text: sa coddhṛtena bāṇena tatraiva svargam āsthitaḥ
children.translated_text: And when the arrow was drawn out, he went to heaven on that very spot,

children.text: bhagavantāv ubhau śocann andhāv iti vilapya ca ||
children.translated_text: lamenting for both you blessed ones and crying out that you were blind.
Through ignorance your son was suddenly struck by me.

children.text: śeṣam evaṃgate yat syāt tat prasīdatu me muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since this has happened, O sage, may what remains now be met with your favor.

children.text: sa tac chrutvā vacaḥ krūraṃ niḥśvasañ śokakarśitaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing those harsh words, he sighed, worn down by grief,
and the greatly radiant one spoke to me as I stood before him with folded hands:

children.text: yady etad aśubhaṃ karma na sma me kathayeḥ svayam
children.translated_text: If you had not yourself told me of this evil deed,

children.text: phalen mūrdhā sma te rājan sadyaḥ śatasahasradhā ||
children.translated_text: your head, O king, would at once have burst into a hundred thousand pieces.
A killing done by a <s>kṣatriya</s>, O king, especially against a forest hermit,

children.text: jñānapūrvaṃ kṛtaḥ sthānāc cyāvayed api vajriṇam ||
children.translated_text: if done knowingly, could dislodge even <s>Vajrin</s> from his station.

children.text: ajñānāddhi kṛtaṃ yasmād idaṃ tenaiva jīvasi
children.translated_text: Because this was done through ignorance, for that reason alone you live.

children.text: api hy adya kulaṃ na syād rāghavāṇāṃ kuto bhavān ||
children.translated_text: Otherwise, today even the line of the <s>Rāghava</s>s would not exist, much less you.

children.text: naya nau nṛpa taṃ deśam iti māṃ cābhyabhāṣata
children.translated_text: Take us to that place, O king, he said to me,

children.text: adya taṃ draṣṭum icchāvaḥ putraṃ paścimadarśanam ||
children.translated_text: for today we wish to see our son, the last sight of him.
His limbs are covered with blood, his antelope-skin garment is scattered,
and he lies on the ground unconscious, gone under the power of <s>Dharmarāja</s>.

children.text: athāham ekas taṃ deśaṃ nītvā tau bhṛśaduḥkhitau
children.translated_text: Then I alone led those two, deeply afflicted, to that place,

children.text: asparśayam ahaṃ putraṃ taṃ muniṃ saha bhāryayā ||
children.translated_text: and I made that sage and his wife touch their son.

children.text: tau putram ātmanaḥ spṛṣṭvā tam āsādya tapasvinau
children.translated_text: Those two ascetics, touching their own son when they reached him,
fell upon his body, and his father said this:

children.text: na nv ahaṃ te priyaḥ putra mātaraṃ paśya dhārmika
children.translated_text: Am I not dear to you, my son? Look at your mother, righteous one.

children.text: kiṃ nu nāliṅgase putra sukumāra vaco vada ||
children.translated_text: Why do you not embrace me, my son? Tender child, speak a word.
Whose heart-delighting voice shall I hear in the latter part of the night?
or, while I am reciting, some sweet śāstra, or some other text in particular?

children.text: ko māṃ saṃdhyām upāsyaiva snātvā hutahutāśanaḥ
children.translated_text: Who, after worshipping at twilight, bathing, and offering oblations into the fire,
will sit near me and praise me, afflicted as I am by grief and fear for my son?

children.text: kandamūlaphalaṃ hṛtvā ko māṃ priyam ivātithim
children.translated_text: Who, bringing bulbs, roots, and fruits, will feed me as a dear guest,
helpless, without means, and without a guide?

children.text: imām andhāṃ ca vṛddhāṃ ca mātaraṃ te tapasvinīm
children.translated_text: And this blind and aged mother of yours, an ascetic woman,
how, my son, shall I support her, wretched and longing for her son?

children.text: tiṣṭha mā mā gamaḥ putra yamasya sadanaṃ prati
children.translated_text: Stay; do not go, my son, to the abode of <s>Yama</s>.

children.text: śvo mayā saha gantāsi jananyā ca samedhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Tomorrow you shall go together with me and with your mother joined to us.

children.text: ubhāv api ca śokārtāv anāthau kṛpaṇau vane
children.translated_text: Both of us, too, stricken with grief, protectorless and wretched in the forest,

children.text: kṣipram eva gamiṣyāvas tvayā hīnau yamakṣayam ||
children.translated_text: will very soon go to <s>Yama</s>'s realm, bereft of you.

children.text: tato vaivasvataṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ pravakṣyāmi bhāratīm
children.translated_text: Then, seeing <s>Vaivasvata</s>, I shall speak this speech to him:

children.text: kṣamatāṃ dharmarājo me bibhṛyāt pitarāv ayam ||
children.translated_text: 'Let <s>Dharmarāja</s> forgive me; let this boy support his parents.'
You are sinless, my son, though slain by a sinner.

children.text: tena satyena gacchāśu ye lokāḥ śastrayodhinām ||
children.translated_text: By that truth, go swiftly to the worlds of those who fight with weapons.

children.text: yānti śūrā gatiṃ yāṃ ca saṃgrāmeṣv anivartinaḥ
children.translated_text: The goal which heroes attain, and those who do not turn back in battles,

children.text: hatās tv abhimukhāḥ putra gatiṃ tāṃ paramāṃ vraja ||
children.translated_text: that supreme goal, my son, attain, since you were struck facing your foe.

children.text: yāṃ gatiṃ sagaraḥ śaibyo dilīpo janamejayaḥ
children.translated_text: The goal which <s>Sagara</s>, <s>Śaibya</s>, <s>Dilīpa</s>, <s>Janamejaya</s>,

children.text: nahuṣo dhundhumāraś ca prāptās tāṃ gaccha putraka ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nahuṣa</s>, and <s>Dhundhumāra</s> attained, go to that, little son.

children.text: yā gatiḥ sarvasādhūnāṃ svādhyāyāt tapasā ca yā
children.translated_text: The destiny of all good men, and that which comes from <s>svādhyāya</s> (sacred recitation) and austerity,
and that of the giver of land, the keeper of the sacred fire, and the man vowed to one wife,
and that of givers of a thousand cows, and that also of those who serve their elders,

children.text: dehanyāsakṛtāṃ yā ca tāṃ gatiṃ gaccha putraka
children.translated_text: and that which belongs to those who lay down the body, go to that destiny, little son.

children.text: na hi tv asmin kule jāto gacchaty akuśalāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: For one born in this family does not go to an inauspicious destiny.
Thus he lamented there piteously, again and again.

children.text: tato 'smai kartum udakaṃ pravṛttaḥ saha bhāryayā ||
children.translated_text: Then, together with his wife, he began to perform the water rite for him.

children.text: sa tu divyena rūpeṇa muniputraḥ svakarmabhiḥ
children.translated_text: But the sage's son, by his own deeds assuming a divine form,

children.text: āśvāsya ca muhūrtaṃ tu pitarau vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: comforted his parents for a moment and spoke these words:

children.text: sthānam asmi mahat prāpto bhavatoḥ paricāraṇāt
children.translated_text: I have attained a great station through service to you both.

children.text: bhavantāv api ca kṣipraṃ mama mūlam upaiṣyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: And you two also will quickly come to my source.

children.text: evam uktvā tu divyena vimānena vapuṣmatā
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the self-controlled sage's son
quickly mounted to heaven in a radiant celestial chariot.

children.text: sa kṛtvā tūdakaṃ tūrṇaṃ tāpasaḥ saha bhāryayā
children.translated_text: After quickly performing the water rite, that ascetic, together with his wife,
of great splendor, spoke to me as I stood nearby with folded hands:

children.text: adyaiva jahi māṃ rājan maraṇe nāsti me vyathā
children.translated_text: Today itself kill me, O king; there is no pain for me in death,

children.text: yac chareṇaikaputraṃ māṃ tvam akārṣīr aputrakam ||
children.translated_text: since with an arrow you have made me, who had one son, sonless.

children.text: tvayā tu yad avijñānān nihato me sutaḥ śuciḥ
children.translated_text: Because my pure son has been killed by you in ignorance,
therefore I shall curse you with a grief most painful and extremely terrible.

children.text: putravyasanajaṃ duḥkhaṃ yad etan mama sāmpratam
children.translated_text: This grief born from the calamity of losing a son, which is now mine,

children.text: evaṃ tvaṃ putraśokena rājan kālaṃ kariṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: in just this way, O king, you too shall die from grief for your son.

children.text: tasmān mām āgataṃ bhadre tasyodārasya tadvacaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, O noble lady, that word of that magnanimous man has come upon me,

children.text: yad ahaṃ putraśokena saṃtyakṣyāmy adya jīvitam ||
children.translated_text: for today I shall give up my life through grief for my son.

children.text: yadi māṃ saṃspṛśed rāmaḥ sakṛd adyālabheta vā
children.translated_text: If <s>Rāma</s> were to touch me today, or speak to me even once,

children.text: na tan me sadṛśaṃ devi yan mayā rāghave kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: still, O queen, what I have done to <s>Rāghava</s> was not worthy of me.

children.text: cakṣuṣā tvāṃ na paśyāmi smṛtir mama vilupyate
children.translated_text: I do not see you with my eyes; my memory is failing.
These messengers of <s>Vaivasvata</s>, O <s>Kausalyā</s>, are hastening me on.

children.text: atas tu kiṃ duḥkhataraṃ yad ahaṃ jīvitakṣaye
children.translated_text: What then is more painful than this, that at the end of my life

children.text: na hi paśyāmi dharmajñaṃ rāmaṃ satyaparākramam ||
children.translated_text: I do not see righteous <s>Rāma</s>, whose valor is true?

children.text: na te manuṣyā devās te ye cāruśubhakuṇḍalam
children.translated_text: They are not men, they are gods, those who

children.text: mukhaṃ drakṣyanti rāmasya varṣe pañcadaśe punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: will see again in the fifteenth year the face of <s>Rāma</s>, beautiful with shining earrings.
The fortunate will see <s>Rāma</s>'s face, with eyes like lotus petals, fair-browed, fine-toothed, and lovely-nosed,
a face like the lord of stars.
The fortunate will see that fragrant face of my lord,

children.text: sugandhi mama nāthasya dhanyā drakṣyanti tanmukham ||
children.translated_text: like the autumn moon and like a blossoming lotus.
Happy people will see <s>Rāma</s> returned to <s>Ayodhyā</s>,

children.text: drakṣyanti sukhino rāmaṃ śukraṃ mārgagataṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: his forest exile ended, like <s>Śukra</s> moving on its path.

children.text: ayam ātmabhavaḥ śoko mām anātham acetanam
children.translated_text: This grief born from myself, finding me helpless and senseless,
is sweeping me away with force, as a river's current sweeps away a bank.
Ah, <s>Rāghava</s>, mighty-armed one! Ah, destroyer of my distress!
Thus king <s>Daśaratha</s>, grieving, reached the end of his life.

children.text: tathā tu dīnaṃ kathayan narādhipaḥ priyasya putrasya vivāsanāturaḥ
children.translated_text: So the lord of men, speaking piteously, tormented by the exile of his beloved son,

children.text: gate 'rdharātre bhṛśaduḥkhapīḍitas tadā jahau prāṇam udāradarśanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when midnight had passed, greatly oppressed by sorrow, then gave up his breath, noble in appearance.
Then, when the night had passed, early on the next day,
the bards attended upon that royal residence.
Then attendants pure in conduct and skilled in attendance,
mostly women and chamberlains, stood by as before.
Those who knew the rules of bathing brought water mixed with yellow sandalwood
in golden jars, at the proper time and according to rule.
Other women, with many maidens among them, brought auspicious objects to touch
and implements for things to be consumed.
Then those women who were nearest

children.text: tāḥ striyas tu samāgamya bhartāraṃ pratyabodhayan ||
children.translated_text: to the king of <s>Kosala</s>'s bed came together and awakened their lord.

children.text: tā vepathuparītāś ca rājñaḥ prāṇeṣu śaṅkitāḥ
children.translated_text: Trembling and fearing for the king's life,
they shook like the tips of grass against the current.

children.text: atha saṃvepamānānāṃ strīṇāṃ dṛṣṭvā ca pārthivam
children.translated_text: Then, as those women were trembling and had seen the king,

children.text: yat tad āśaṅkitaṃ pāpaṃ tasya jajñe viniścayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The evil that had been feared became certain for him.

children.text: tataḥ pracukruśur dīnāḥ sasvaraṃ tā varāṅganāḥ
children.translated_text: Then those noble women, wretched, cried out
in full voice, like she-elephants in the forest whose herd-leaders have fallen from their place.
By the sound of their wailing, suddenly roused to consciousness,

children.text: kausalyā ca sumitrā ca tyaktanidre babhūvatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kausalyā</s> and <s>Sumitrā</s> both awoke, their sleep abandoned.

children.text: kausalyā ca sumitrā ca dṛṣṭvā spṛṣṭvā ca pārthivam
children.translated_text: <s>Kausalyā</s> and <s>Sumitrā</s>, seeing and touching the king,
cried, "Ah, lord!" and fell upon the ground.
That daughter of the lord of <s>Kosala</s>, writhing on the earth,
did not shine, covered with dust, like a star fallen from the sky.
The palace of the lord of men who had reached his destined end became at once
terrified and confused, crowded with anxious people, filled on all sides with tumultuous crying, with kinsmen afflicted by grief,
its joy suddenly fallen away, and pitiful and distressed to behold.
Such became the dwelling of the king who had reached the end ordained by fate.

children.text: atītam ājñāya tu pārthivarṣabhaṃ yaśasvinaṃ saṃparivārya patnayaḥ
children.translated_text: Knowing that the glorious bull among kings had passed away, his wives surrounded him,

children.text: bhṛśaṃ rudantyaḥ karuṇaṃ suduḥkhitāḥ pragṛhya bāhū vyalapann anāthavat ||
children.translated_text: and, weeping bitterly, piteously, and in great sorrow, raised their arms and lamented like those without a protector.

children.text: tam agnim iva saṃśāntam ambuhīnam ivārṇavam
children.translated_text: Seeing that king gone to heaven, like a fire extinguished, like an ocean without water,
like the sun robbed of its splendor,
<s>Kausalyā</s>, her eyes full of tears and wasted by many kinds of grief,
embraced the king's head and spoke to <s>Kaikeyī</s>.

children.text: sakāmā bhava kaikeyi bhuṅkṣva rājyam akaṇṭakam
children.translated_text: "Have your desire fulfilled, <s>Kaikeyī</s>; enjoy a kingdom without rivals,
having abandoned the king, intent on that alone, cruel woman of wicked conduct.

children.text: vihāya māṃ gato rāmo bhartā ca svargato mama
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> has gone away, leaving me, and my husband has gone to heaven;
like a caravanless woman on a wrong road, I cannot bear to live.

children.text: bhartāraṃ taṃ parityajya kā strī daivatam ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Having lost that husband, what woman, whose husband is her own divinity,
would wish to live, except <s>Kaikeyī</s>, who has abandoned <s>dharma</s>?

children.text: na lubdho budhyate doṣān kiṃ pākam iva bhakṣayan
children.translated_text: The greedy person does not perceive faults, as one eating a poisonous fruit does not perceive its ripening consequence.
Because of the hunchback, <s>Kaikeyī</s> has destroyed the family of the <s>Rāghavas</s>.
When <s>Janaka</s> hears that the king, appointed to what was improper, has exiled <s>Rāma</s>

children.text: sabhāryaṃ janakaḥ śrutvā paritapsyaty ahaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: together with his wife, he will grieve just as I do.
<s>Rāma</s>, lotus-petal-eyed, has gone from here to the destruction of life;
and the daughter of the king of <s>Videha</s>, ascetic <s>Sītā</s>,
unaccustomed to suffering, will tremble at suffering in the forest.
At night, hearing the fearful cries
of roaring beasts and birds, surely terrified, she will take refuge in <s>Rāghava</s>.
And that aged king, with few sons, thinking of <s>Vaidehī</s>,
surely he too, overcome by grief, will give up his life."
Then the attendants, embracing that poor woman
<s>Kausalyā</s> as she lamented, led her away, deeply afflicted with sorrow.
Then the ministers placed the lord of the earth in a trough of oil,

children.text: rājñaḥ sarvāṇy athādiṣṭāś cakruḥ karmāṇy anantaram ||
children.translated_text: and afterward, as instructed, they performed all the rites for the king.

children.text: na tu saṃkālanaṃ rājño vinā putreṇa mantriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: But without his son, the ministers, though all-knowing,

children.text: sarvajñāḥ kartum īṣus te tato rakṣanti bhūmipam ||
children.translated_text: did not wish to perform the king's cremation; therefore they guarded the lord of the earth.

children.text: tailadroṇyāṃ tu sacivaiḥ śāyitaṃ taṃ narādhipam
children.translated_text: When that lord of men had been laid in the oil-trough by the ministers,

children.text: hā mṛto 'yam iti jñātvā striyas tāḥ paryadevayan ||
children.translated_text: those women, knowing, "Ah, he is dead," lamented around him.
Raising their arms, wretched, with faces streaming from their eyes,
weeping and scorched by grief, they lamented pitifully.
Like a night without stars, like a woman bereft of her husband,
the city of <s>Ayodhyā</s> did not shine, deprived of the great-souled king.
Its people were confused with tears, the women of its households cried "Alas!",
and its squares and house-courts were empty; it did not shine as before.

children.text: gataprabhā dyaur iva bhāskaraṃ vinā vyapetanakṣatragaṇeva śarvarī
children.translated_text: Like the sky bereft of the sun and stripped of its splendor, like a night whose host of stars has disappeared,

children.text: purī babhāse rahitā mahātmanā na cāsrakaṇṭhākulamārgacatvarā ||
children.translated_text: the city appeared bereft of the great-souled one, its roads and squares crowded with people whose throats were choked with tears.

children.text: narāś ca nāryaś ca sametya saṃghaśo vigarhamāṇā bharatasya mātaram
children.translated_text: Men and women gathered in groups, reproaching the mother of <s>Bharata</s>;

children.text: tadā nagaryāṃ naradevasaṃkṣaye babhūvur ārtā na ca śarma lebhire ||
children.translated_text: then, at the death of the king, they were afflicted in the city and found no happiness.
When the night had passed and the sun had risen,
the twice-born men who were makers of kings assembled and went to the council hall.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, <s>Maudgalya</s>, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>,

children.text: kātyāyano gautamaś ca jābāliś ca mahāyaśāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kātyāyana</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, and <s>Jābāli</s> of great fame,

children.text: ete dvijāḥ sahāmātyaiḥ pṛthag vācam udīrayan
children.translated_text: these brahmins, together with the ministers, each spoke their words
facing <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> himself, the foremost royal priest.

children.text: atītā śarvarī duḥkhaṃ yā no varṣaśatopamā
children.translated_text: "The night that was like a hundred years to us has passed in misery,
since this king reached the state of the five elements through grief for his son.

children.text: svargataś ca mahārājo rāmaś cāraṇyam āśritaḥ
children.translated_text: The great king has gone to heaven, and <s>Rāma</s> has taken refuge in the forest;

children.text: lakṣmaṇaś cāpi tejasvī rāmeṇaiva gataḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: the energetic <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> too has gone together with <s>Rāma</s> himself.
Both <s>Bharata</s> and <s>Śatrughna</s>, scorcher of foes, are among the <s>Kekayas</s>,
in the lovely city <s>Rājagṛha</s>, at their maternal grandfather's residence.
Let some king of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s> be appointed here this very day,

children.text: arājakaṃ hi no rāṣṭraṃ na vināśam avāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: so that our realm, being kingless, may not come to destruction.
In a kingless country, the thundercloud, garlanded with lightning and loud-sounding,
does not rain upon the earth with heavenly water.
In a kingless country, a handful of seed is not scattered;

children.text: nārājake pituḥ putro bhāryā vā vartate vaśe ||
children.translated_text: in a kingless country, a son is not obedient to his father, nor a wife to her husband.

children.text: arājake dhanaṃ nāsti nāsti bhāryāpy arājake
children.translated_text: In a kingless country there is no wealth; in a kingless country there is not even a wife.

children.text: idam atyāhitaṃ cānyat kutaḥ satyam arājake ||
children.translated_text: And this other great danger exists: how could there be truth in a kingless country?
In a kingless country, men do not convene an assembly.

children.text: udyānāni ca ramyāṇi hṛṣṭāḥ puṇyagṛhāṇi ca ||
children.translated_text: nor pleasant parks, nor joyful houses of merit.
In a kingless realm, twice-born men devoted to sacrifice
do not attend sacrificial sessions as self-controlled Brahmins of strict vows.
In a kingless realm, where actors and dancers are abundant,

children.text: utsavāś ca samājāś ca vardhante rāṣṭravardhanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: festivals and public gatherings, which make a kingdom prosper, do not flourish.
In a kingless realm, merchants whose aims have been achieved,
men fond of tales, are not delighted by stories told by lovers of stories.
In a kingless realm, men filled with desire do not go out

children.text: narā niryānty araṇyāni nārībhiḥ saha kāminaḥ ||
children.translated_text: with women in swift-moving vehicles to the forests.
In a kingless realm, wealthy men, secure and protected,
farmers and cowherds do not sleep with their doors open.
In a kingless realm, merchants who travel far,
richly endowed with merit, do not safely go along the road.
In a kingless realm, there is no place where a self-controlled sage, living alone, wanders,
cultivating himself by himself, and having whatever place he reaches at evening as his dwelling.
In a kingless realm, the securing and preservation of welfare does not proceed;

children.text: na cāpy arājake senā śatrūn viṣahate yudhi ||
children.translated_text: nor, in a kingless realm, can an army withstand enemies in battle.

children.text: yathā hy anudakā nadyo yathā vāpy atṛṇaṃ vanam
children.translated_text: For as rivers are without water, or as a forest is without grass,

children.text: agopālā yathā gāvas tathā rāṣṭram arājakam ||
children.translated_text: and as cows are without a cowherd, so is a kingdom without a king.
In a kingless realm, nothing belongs to anyone as his own;

children.text: matsyā iva narā nityaṃ bhakṣayanti parasparam ||
children.translated_text: like fish, men constantly devour one another.
Even those who have broken all bounds, who are atheists and have cut off all doubt,
become fit for good conduct when pressed by the king's punishment.

children.text: aho tama ivedaṃ syān na prajñāyeta kiṃcana
children.translated_text: Alas, this world would be like darkness; nothing at all would be discerned,

children.text: rājā cen na bhavel loke vibhajan sādhvasādhunī ||
children.translated_text: if there were no king in the world dividing the good from the bad.

children.text: jīvaty api mahārāje tavaiva vacanaṃ vayam
children.translated_text: Though the great king still lives, all of us do not transgress your word alone,
just as the ocean, having reached its shore, does not pass beyond it.

children.text: sa naḥ samīkṣya dvijavaryavṛttaṃ nṛpaṃ vinā rājyam araṇyabhūtam
children.translated_text: Therefore, considering the conduct of the best of the twice-born and this kingdom made like a wilderness without a ruler,

children.text: kumāram ikṣvākusutaṃ vadānyaṃ tvam eva rājānam ihābhiṣiñca ||
children.translated_text: do you yourself here consecrate as king the generous prince, the son of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>.

children.text: teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā vasiṣṭhaḥ pratyuvāca ha
children.translated_text: Having heard those words of theirs, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> replied

children.text: mitrāmātyagaṇān sarvān brāhmaṇāṃs tān idaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: to all the friends, ministers, and Brahmins with these words:

children.text: yad asau mātulakule pure rājagṛhe sukhī
children.translated_text: Since <s>Bharata</s> is living happily in his maternal uncle's city, in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>,
together with his brother <s>Śatrughna</s>,

children.text: tacchīghraṃ javanā dūtā gacchantu tvaritair hayaiḥ
children.translated_text: therefore let swift messengers quickly go with fast horses

children.text: ānetuṃ bhrātarau vīrau kiṃ samīkṣāmahe vayam ||
children.translated_text: to bring the two heroic brothers here. What are we waiting for?

children.text: gacchantv iti tataḥ sarve vasiṣṭhaṃ vākyam abruvan
children.translated_text: Then all said to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, "Let them go."

children.text: teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā vasiṣṭho vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Having heard those words of theirs, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> spoke these words:
Come, <s>Siddhārtha</s>, <s>Vijaya</s>, <s>Jayanta</s>, and <s>Aśokanandana</s>;

children.text: śrūyatām itikartavyaṃ sarvān eva bravīmi vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: listen to what is to be done. I am telling it to all of you.

children.text: puraṃ rājagṛhaṃ gatvā śīghraṃ śīghrajavair hayaiḥ
children.translated_text: Having gone to the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> quickly with horses of rapid speed,

children.text: tyaktaśokair idaṃ vācyaḥ śāsanād bharato mama ||
children.translated_text: free from any sign of grief, <s>Bharata</s> is to be told this by my command:

children.text: purohitas tvāṃ kuśalaṃ prāha sarve ca mantriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: "The priest asks after your welfare, and so do all the ministers.

children.text: tvaramāṇaś ca niryāhi kṛtyam ātyayikaṃ tvayā ||
children.translated_text: Set out in haste, for there is an urgent matter for you to attend to."

children.text: mā cāsmai proṣitaṃ rāmaṃ mā cāsmai pitaraṃ mṛtam
children.translated_text: But when you have gone, do not tell him that <s>Rāma</s> has gone into exile, nor that his father is dead,

children.text: bhavantaḥ śaṃsiṣur gatvā rāghavāṇām imaṃ kṣayam ||
children.translated_text: nor this destruction that has befallen the <s>Rāghavas</s>.

children.text: kauśeyāni ca vastrāṇi bhūṣaṇāni varāṇi ca
children.translated_text: Taking silken garments and excellent ornaments,

children.text: kṣipram ādāya rājñaś ca bharatasya ca gacchata
children.translated_text: go quickly for the king and for <s>Bharata</s>.
Permitted by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, the messengers set out in great haste.

children.text: te hastinapure gaṅgāṃ tīrtvā pratyaṅmukhā yayuḥ
children.translated_text: They crossed the <s>Gaṅgā</s> at <s>Hastinapura</s> and went westward,
reaching the land of the <s>Pāñcālas</s> through the middle of <s>Kurujāṅgala</s>.
With speed they approached the clear-watered, splendid <s>Śaradaṇḍā</s>,
served by many kinds of birds and crowded with people.
Reaching <s>Nikūlavṛkṣa</s>, the splendid place called <s>Satyopayācana</s>,
they approached and reverently saluted it, and then entered the city of <s>Kuliṅgā</s>.
Then, having come at the proper time, and having passed beyond the place where the sun's heat prevailed,

children.text: yayur madhyena vāhlīkān sudāmānaṃ ca parvatam
children.translated_text: they went through the middle of the <s>Vāhlīkas</s> and past Mount <s>Sudāman</s>,

children.text: viṣṇoḥ padaṃ prekṣamāṇā vipāśāṃ cāpi śālmalīm ||
children.translated_text: beholding <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s Footprint, and also the <s>Vipāśā</s> and <s>Śālmalī</s> rivers.

children.text: te śrāntavāhanā dūtā vikṛṣṭena satā pathā
children.translated_text: Those messengers, their mounts weary from a long road stretched far out,
quickly and directly reached <s>Girivraja</s>, the best of cities.

children.text: bhartuḥ priyārthaṃ kularakṣaṇārthaṃ bhartuś ca vaṃśasya parigrahārtham
children.translated_text: For the sake of their lord's dear purpose, for the protection of the family, and for the preservation of their lord's lineage,

children.text: aheḍamānās tvarayā sma dūtā rātryāṃ tu te tat puram eva yātāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the messengers, showing no disregard and acting with haste, entered that very city at night.

children.text: yām eva rātriṃ te dūtāḥ praviśanti sma tāṃ purīm
children.translated_text: On the very night on which those messengers entered that city,

children.text: bharatenāpi tāṃ rātriṃ svapno dṛṣṭo 'yam apriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s> too saw this unpleasant dream in that night.

children.text: vyuṣṭām eva tu tāṃ rātriṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ svapnam apriyam
children.translated_text: When that night had passed, after seeing that unpleasant dream,
the son of the emperor was extremely distressed.
Seeing that he was tormented, his companions, speakers of pleasant words,

children.text: āyāsaṃ hi vineṣyantaḥ sabhāyāṃ cakrire kathāḥ ||
children.translated_text: wishing to remove his weariness, began conversations in the assembly.

children.text: vādayanti tathā śāntiṃ lāsayanty api cāpare
children.translated_text: Some played music for calm, and others even made dancers perform;

children.text: nāṭakāny apare prāhur hāsyāni vividhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: others recited plays and various comic pieces.

children.text: sa tair mahātmā bharataḥ sakhibhiḥ priyavādibhiḥ
children.translated_text: But the noble <s>Bharata</s>, the <s>Rāghava</s>, did not rejoice
with those friends, speakers of pleasant words, as they made convivial jokes.

children.text: tam abravīt priyasakho bharataṃ sakhibhir vṛtam
children.translated_text: A dear friend, surrounded by companions and seated beside him with well-wishers,
said to <s>Bharata</s>, "Friend, why do you not take pleasure?"

children.text: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ suhṛdaṃ bharataḥ pratyuvāca ha
children.translated_text: To the friend who spoke thus, <s>Bharata</s> replied:

children.text: śṛṇu tvaṃ yannimittaṃ me dainyam etad upāgatam ||
children.translated_text: Listen to the reason why this dejection has come upon me.
In a dream I saw my father, soiled and with his hair loosened,
falling from a mountain peak into a foul lake of cow-dung.

children.text: plavamānaś ca me dṛṣṭaḥ sa tasmin gomayahrade
children.translated_text: And I saw him floating there in that lake of cow-dung,

children.text: pibann añjalinā tailaṃ hasann iva muhur muhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: drinking oil with cupped hands and laughing, as it were, again and again.

children.text: tatas tilaudanaṃ bhuktvā punaḥ punar adhaḥśirāḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after eating rice cooked with sesame, again and again with his head downward,
his whole body smeared with oil, he plunged into oil alone.

children.text: svapne 'pi sāgaraṃ śuṣkaṃ candraṃ ca patitaṃ bhuvi
children.translated_text: In the dream too I saw the ocean dried up and the moon fallen to the earth,
and the blazing fire suddenly extinguished.

children.text: avadīrṇāṃ ca pṛthivīṃ śuṣkāṃś ca vividhān drumān
children.translated_text: I see the earth split open, many kinds of trees dried up,

children.text: ahaṃ paśyāmi vidhvastān sadhūmāṃś caiva parvatān ||
children.translated_text: and mountains shattered and smoking.
And I saw him seated on an iron seat, dressed in black garments,
while women who were black and tawny laughed at the king.
The righteous one, hurrying, wearing red garlands and unguents,
went southward in a chariot yoked with donkeys.

children.text: evam etan mayā dṛṣṭam imāṃ rātriṃ bhayāvahām
children.translated_text: Such was the vision I saw in this dreadful night.

children.text: ahaṃ rāmo 'thavā rājā lakṣmaṇo vā mariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Either I, <s>Rāma</s>, the king, or <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> will die.

children.text: naro yānena yaḥ svapne kharayuktena yāti hi
children.translated_text: For a man who in a dream goes in a vehicle yoked with donkeys,
before long the smoking tip of his funeral pyre is seen.

children.text: etannimittaṃ dīno 'haṃ tan na vaḥ pratipūjaye ||
children.translated_text: Because of this omen I am dejected; therefore I have not honored you properly.

children.text: śuṣyatīva ca me kaṇṭho na svastham iva me manaḥ
children.translated_text: My throat seems to be drying up, and my mind seems unwell.

children.text: jugupsann iva cātmānaṃ na ca paśyāmi kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: It is as though I loathe myself, and yet I see no cause.

children.text: imāṃ hi duḥsvapnagatiṃ niśāmya tām anekarūpām avitarkitāṃ purā
children.translated_text: Having observed this course of evil dreams in the night, manifold and never imagined before,

children.text: bhayaṃ mahat taddhṛdayān na yāti me vicintya rājānam acintyadarśanam ||
children.translated_text: that great fear does not leave my heart as I think of the king and this inconceivable vision.

children.text: bharate bruvati svapnaṃ dūtās te klāntavāhanāḥ
children.translated_text: While <s>Bharata</s> was telling the dream, those messengers, their mounts exhausted,
entered the lovely city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, whose moat was hard to cross.

children.text: samāgamya tu rājñā ca rājaputreṇa cārcitāḥ
children.translated_text: After meeting with the king and being honored by the prince,

children.text: rājñaḥ pādau gṛhītvā tu tam ūcur bharataṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: they took the king's feet and then spoke these words to <s>Bharata</s>:

children.text: purohitas tvā kuśalaṃ prāha sarve ca mantriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The purohita reports your welfare, and so do all the ministers.

children.text: tvaramāṇaś ca niryāhi kṛtyam ātyayikaṃ tvayā ||
children.translated_text: Set out quickly and in haste; an urgent business must be attended to by you.

children.text: atra viṃśatikoṭyas tu nṛpater mātulasya te
children.translated_text: Here are twenty crores from the king, your maternal uncle,

children.text: daśakoṭyas tu sampūrṇās tathaiva ca nṛpātmaja ||
children.translated_text: and ten crores complete as well, O prince.

children.text: pratigṛhya ca tat sarvaṃ svanuraktaḥ suhṛjjane
children.translated_text: Receiving all that, and warmly attached to his friends,

children.text: dūtān uvāca bharataḥ kāmaiḥ sampratipūjya tān ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s> spoke to the messengers after honoring them with desired gifts.

children.text: kaccit sukuśalī rājā pitā daśaratho mama
children.translated_text: Is the king, my father <s>Daśaratha</s>, truly well?

children.text: kaccic cārogatā rāme lakṣmaṇe vā mahātmani ||
children.translated_text: And is all well, without illness, for noble <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>?
Is the noble lady devoted to <s>dharma</s>, knowing <s>dharma</s> and seeing <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: arogā cāpi kausalyā mātā rāmasya dhīmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kausalyā</s>, the mother of wise <s>Rāma</s>, also free from illness?

children.text: kaccit sumitrā dharmajñā jananī lakṣmaṇasya yā
children.translated_text: Is <s>Sumitrā</s>, who knows <s>dharma</s>, the mother of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: śatrughnasya ca vīrasya sārogā cāpi madhyamā ||
children.translated_text: and also of heroic <s>Śatrughna</s>, that middle queen, well and free from illness?
Self-interested, always fierce, irascible, and thinking herself wise,

children.text: arogā cāpi kaikeyī mātā me kim uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: is <s>Kaikeyī</s>, my mother, also free from illness, and what did she say?

children.text: evam uktās tu te dūtā bharatena mahātmanā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by great-souled <s>Bharata</s>,

children.text: ūcuḥ sampraśritaṃ vākyam idaṃ taṃ bharataṃ tadā
children.translated_text: the messengers then spoke this humble statement to <s>Bharata</s>:

children.text: kuśalās te naravyāghra yeṣāṃ kuśalam icchasi ||
children.translated_text: Those whose welfare you wish, O tiger among men, are well.

children.text: bharataś cāpi tān dūtān evam ukto 'bhyabhāṣata
children.translated_text: And <s>Bharata</s>, so addressed, spoke to those messengers:
I shall take leave of the great king; the messengers are hurrying me.

children.text: evam uktvā tu tān dūtān bharataḥ pārthivātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to the messengers, <s>Bharata</s>, the prince,

children.text: dūtaiḥ saṃcodito vākyaṃ mātāmaham uvāca ha ||
