children.translated_text: urged by the messengers, spoke these words to his maternal grandfather:
O king, urged on by the messengers, I shall go to my father's presence.

children.text: punar apy aham eṣyāmi yadā me tvaṃ smariṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: I shall come again whenever you remember me.

children.text: bharatenaivam uktas tu nṛpo mātāmahas tadā
children.translated_text: When <s>Bharata</s> had spoken thus, the king, his maternal grandfather,

children.text: tam uvāca śubhaṃ vākyaṃ śirasy āghrāya rāghavam ||
children.translated_text: smelled <s>Rāghava</s>'s head and spoke this auspicious word to him:

children.text: gaccha tātānujāne tvāṃ kaikeyī suprajās tvayā
children.translated_text: Go, dear child; I permit you. <s>Kaikeyī</s> is blessed with you as a son.

children.text: mātaraṃ kuśalaṃ brūyāḥ pitaraṃ ca paraṃtapa ||
children.translated_text: Tell your mother and your father that all is well, O scorcher of foes,

children.text: purohitaṃ ca kuśalaṃ ye cānye dvijasattamāḥ
children.translated_text: and also the purohita and whatever other best twice-born men there are,

children.text: tau ca tāta maheṣvāsau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau ||
children.translated_text: and those two great bowmen, dear child, the brothers <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: tasmai hastyuttamāṃś citrān kambalān ajināni ca
children.translated_text: For him <s>Kaikeya</s>, after honoring <s>Bharata</s>, gave wealth:
excellent variegated elephants, blankets, and antelope skins.
Two thousand gold niṣkas and sixteen hundred horses,
after honoring <s>Kaikeyī</s>'s son, the <s>Kekaya</s> ordered as wealth.
Likewise <s>Aśvapati</s> quickly gave chosen attendants,
trustworthy and endowed with virtues, as followers for <s>Bharata</s>.
His maternal uncle gave him handsome elephants called <s>Airāvatas</s> and <s>Aindraśiras</s>,

children.text: kharāñ śīghrān susaṃyuktān mātulo 'smai dhanaṃ dadau ||
children.translated_text: swift, well-harnessed donkeys, and wealth.
And as a present he gave dogs, greatly raised within the inner palace,
endowed with a tiger's courage and strength, armed with fangs, and huge-bodied.

children.text: sa mātāmaham āpṛcchya mātulaṃ ca yudhājitam
children.translated_text: Having taken leave of his maternal grandfather and of his maternal uncle <s>Yudhājit</s>,
<s>Bharata</s> mounted a chariot and set out together with <s>Śatrughna</s>.
After yoking well over a hundred chariots with round wheels,
servants followed <s>Bharata</s> as he went, with camels, cattle, horses, and donkeys.

children.text: balena gupto bharato mahātmā sahāryakasyātmasamair amātyaiḥ
children.translated_text: Protected by an army, great-souled <s>Bharata</s>, together with <s>Āryaka</s>'s ministers who were like himself,

children.text: ādāya śatrughnam apetaśatrur gṛhād yayau siddha ivendralokāt ||
children.translated_text: taking <s>Śatrughna</s> with him and free from enemies, went from the house like a perfected being from <s>Indra</s>'s world.
The mighty one, going out eastward from <s>Rājagṛha</s>,
toward the <s>Hrādinī</s>, hard to cross from afar, wave-filled and flowing westward,
The illustrious descendant of <s>Ikṣvāku</s> crossed the river <s>Śatadrū</s>.
Having crossed the river at <s>Elādhāna</s> and reached <s>Aparaparpaṭa</s>,
and having crossed <s>Śilā</s> and <s>Ākurvatī</s>, and the southeastern <s>Śalyakartana</s>,
the truthful, pure, illustrious prince, while looking upon <s>Śilāvahā</s>,

children.text: atyayāt sa mahāśailān vanaṃ caitrarathaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: passed beyond the great mountains toward the forest <s>Caitraratha</s>.
He also reached the swift river called <s>Kuliṅgā</s>, roaring and enclosed by mountains,

children.text: yamunāṃ prāpya saṃtīrṇo balam āśvāsayat tadā ||
children.translated_text: and, having reached and crossed the <s>Yamunā</s>, he then gave rest to the army.

children.text: śītīkṛtya tu gātrāṇi klāntān āśvāsya vājinaḥ
children.translated_text: After cooling their limbs and comforting the weary horses,

children.text: tatra snātvā ca pītvā ca prāyād ādāya codakam ||
children.translated_text: he bathed there, drank, took water with him, and set out again.
The royal prince, fortunate and travelling in a fine vehicle, passed through the great forest, rarely visited,

children.text: bhadro bhadreṇa yānena mārutaḥ kham ivātyayāt ||
children.translated_text: as the wind passes through the sky.
He approached <s>Jambūprastha</s> by the southern side of <s>Toraṇa</s>,

children.text: varūthaṃ ca yayau ramyaṃ grāmaṃ daśarathātmajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Daśaratha</s>'s son went on to the delightful village <s>Varūtha</s>.

children.text: tatra ramye vane vāsaṃ kṛtvāsau prāṅmukho yayau
children.translated_text: After spending the night in that pleasant forest, he went eastward,
to the grove of <s>Ujjihānā</s>, where priyaka trees stood.

children.text: sālāṃs tu priyakān prāpya śīghrān āsthāya vājinaḥ
children.translated_text: Having reached the śāla and priyaka trees, and having mounted swift horses,
<s>Bharata</s>, after dismissing the army, hurried on his way.

children.text: vāsaṃ kṛtvā sarvatīrthe tīrtvā cottānikāṃ nadīm
children.translated_text: After staying at <s>Sarvatīrtha</s>, crossing the river <s>Uttānikā</s>,

children.text: anyā nadīś ca vividhāḥ pārvatīyais turaṃgamaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and many other rivers with mountain-bred horses,
he reached <s>Hastipṛṣṭhaka</s> and passed beyond <s>Kuṭikā</s>.

children.text: tatāra ca naravyāghro lauhitye sa kapīvatīm
children.translated_text: Then the tiger among men crossed the <s>Kapīvatī</s> at <s>Lauhitya</s>,
and at <s>Ekasāla</s> the <s>Sthāṇumatī</s>, and at <s>Vinata</s> the river <s>Gomatī</s>.
Then, after reaching <s>Kaliṅganagara</s> too and the śāla forest,
<s>Bharata</s> came on swiftly, his mounts utterly exhausted.
Having quickly passed beyond the forest, at dawn after the night,

children.text: ayodhyāṃ manunā rājñā nirmitāṃ sa dadarśa ha ||
children.translated_text: he saw <s>Ayodhyā</s>, built by king <s>Manu</s>.
That tiger among men, who had spent seven nights on the road,

children.text: ayodhyām agrato dṛṣṭvā rathe sārathim abravīt ||
children.translated_text: seeing <s>Ayodhyā</s> before him, spoke to the charioteer in the chariot:
This famous <s>Ayodhyā</s>, with its holy gardens, does not seem joyful to me,
O charioteer; pale with dust, it is visible from afar.
It was formerly filled, for the most part, with prosperous brahmins endowed with virtues, sacrificers and masters of the <s>Veda</s>,
and protected by the best of royal seers.

children.text: ayodhyāyāṃ purā śabdaḥ śrūyate tumulo mahān
children.translated_text: In <s>Ayodhyā</s> formerly a great, tumultuous sound was heard,

children.text: samantān naranārīṇāṃ tam adya na śṛṇomy aham ||
children.translated_text: from men and women on every side; today I do not hear it.
In other days, in the evening, the gardens shone with people who had finished their play,
running about everywhere around them.
Today those same gardens seem to weep, abandoned by lovers;
the city appears to me like wilderness ground, O charioteer.

children.text: na hy atra yānair dṛśyante na gajair na ca vājibhiḥ
children.translated_text: For here the chief men are not seen as before, with vehicles, elephants, or horses,
either going out or coming in.

children.text: aniṣṭāni ca pāpāni paśyāmi vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: I see various inauspicious and evil things,

children.text: nimittāny amanojñāni tena sīdati me manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: unpleasant omens; therefore my mind sinks.
With his horses exhausted he entered through the <s>Vaijayanta</s> gate,

children.text: dvāḥsthair utthāya vijayaṃ pṛṣṭas taiḥ sahito yayau ||
children.translated_text: and, asked of his victory by the gatekeepers who rose up, he went on together with them.

children.text: sa tv anekāgrahṛdayo dvāḥsthaṃ pratyarcya taṃ janam
children.translated_text: But with his heart drawn in many directions, after honoring the gatekeeper and those people,

children.text: sūtam aśvapateḥ klāntam abravīt tatra rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Rāghava</s> spoke there to the tired charioteer of <s>Aśvapati</s>:

children.text: śrutā no yādṛśāḥ pūrvaṃ nṛpatīnāṃ vināśane
children.translated_text: The signs of which we formerly heard when kings perish,

children.text: ākārās tān ahaṃ sarvān iha paśyāmi sārathe ||
children.translated_text: all those signs I see here, O charioteer.
I see the people in the city, women and men alike, soiled, their eyes full of tears, wretched, absorbed in anxious thought, and emaciated,

children.text: sastrīpuṃsaṃ ca paśyāmi janam utkaṇṭhitaṃ pure ||
children.translated_text: and all of them longing and distressed.

children.text: ity evam uktvā bharataḥ sūtaṃ taṃ dīnamānasaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to that charioteer, <s>Bharata</s>, downcast in mind,

children.text: tāny aniṣṭāny ayodhyāyāṃ prekṣya rājagṛhaṃ yayau
children.translated_text: seeing those evil omens in <s>Ayodhyā</s>, went to the royal palace.
Seeing the city, whose crossroads, houses, and roads were empty, whose door panels and bolts were reddened with dust,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā purīm indrapurīprakāśāṃ duḥkhena sampūrṇataro babhūva ||
children.translated_text: the city that had once shone like <s>Indra</s>'s city, he became still more filled with sorrow.

children.text: bahūni paśyan manaso 'priyāṇi yāny anyadā nāsya pure babhūvuḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing many things unpleasant to his mind, things that had never before been in his city,

children.text: avākśirā dīnamanā na hṛṣṭaḥ pitur mahātmā praviveśa veśma ||
children.translated_text: the great-souled one, with head bowed, dejected and joyless, entered his father's house.

children.text: apaśyaṃs tu tatas tatra pitaraṃ pitur ālaye
children.translated_text: Then, not seeing his father there in his father's residence,

children.text: jagāma bharato draṣṭuṃ mātaraṃ mātur ālaye ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s> went to see his mother in her residence.

children.text: anuprāptaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā kaikeyī proṣitaṃ sutam
children.translated_text: When <s>Kaikeyī</s> saw her son returned from abroad,
she sprang up joyfully, leaving her golden couch.
As soon as righteous <s>Bharata</s> entered his own house, bereft of splendor,

children.text: bharataḥ prekṣya jagrāha jananyāś caraṇau śubhau ||
children.translated_text: he saw his mother and grasped her auspicious feet.
Smelling him on the head and embracing the famous <s>Bharata</s>,
she placed him on her lap and began to question him:
How many nights has it now been since you left your grandfather's house?
I hope the fatigue of the road has not quickly overcome you as you came by chariot.

children.text: āryakas te sukuśalī yudhājin mātulas tava
children.translated_text: Is your noble grandfather well, and your maternal uncle <s>Yudhājin</s>?

children.text: pravāsāc ca sukhaṃ putra sarvaṃ me vaktum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: And from your stay abroad, my son, you should tell me whether everything has been well.

children.text: evaṃ pṛṣṭas tu kaikeyyā priyaṃ pārthivanandanaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus questioned by <s>Kaikeyī</s>, the lotus-eyed <s>Bharata</s>, beloved son of the king,
told everything to his mother.
Today is the seventh night since I left my grandfather's house.

children.text: ambāyāḥ kuśalī tāto yudhājin mātulaś ca me ||
children.translated_text: My mother's father is well, and so is my maternal uncle <s>Yudhājin</s>.

children.text: yan me dhanaṃ ca ratnaṃ ca dadau rājā paraṃtapaḥ
children.translated_text: The wealth and jewels that the king, scorcher of foes, gave me

children.text: pariśrāntaṃ pathy abhavat tato 'haṃ pūrvam āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: became burdensome on the road; therefore I came on ahead.
I came because I was being hurried by messengers who carried the king's command.

children.text: yad ahaṃ praṣṭum icchāmi tad ambā vaktum arhati ||
children.translated_text: Mother should tell me what I wish to ask.
This couch of yours, adorned with gold, is empty;

children.text: na cāyam ikṣvākujanaḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ pratibhāti me ||
children.translated_text: and these <s>Ikṣvāku</s> people do not appear joyful to me.
The king is usually here in Mother's residence;

children.text: tam ahaṃ nādya paśyāmi draṣṭum icchann ihāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: I do not see him today, though I have come here wishing to see him.

children.text: pitur grahīṣye caraṇau taṃ mamākhyāhi pṛcchataḥ
children.translated_text: I will clasp my father's feet; tell me of him, since I ask.
Or is he, Mother, in the residence of the elder <s>Kausalyā</s>?

children.text: taṃ pratyuvāca kaikeyī priyavad ghoram apriyam
children.translated_text: To him <s>Kaikeyī</s> replied, speaking pleasantly what was terribly unpleasant,
knowing it while he did not know it, deluded by greed for the kingdom:

children.text: yā gatiḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ tāṃ gatiṃ te pitā gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Your father has gone to that state to which all beings go."
Hearing that statement, <s>Bharata</s>, pure and born of a righteous family,
suddenly fell to the ground, crushed by the force of grief for his father.
Then enveloped in sorrow, pained by his father's death,
the greatly radiant one lamented, his mind bewildered and agitated.

children.text: etat suruciraṃ bhāti pitur me śayanaṃ purā
children.translated_text: "Formerly this couch of my father looked very beautiful;

children.text: tad idaṃ na vibhāty adya vihīnaṃ tena dhīmatā ||
children.translated_text: but today, deprived of that wise man, it does not shine.

children.text: tam ārtaṃ devasaṃkāśaṃ samīkṣya patitaṃ bhuvi
children.translated_text: Seeing him distressed, godlike, fallen on the ground,
she raised him up, afflicted with sorrow, and said this word:
"Rise, rise! Why are you lying there, famous prince?

children.text: tvadvidhā na hi śocanti santaḥ sadasi saṃmatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For good men like you, esteemed in assemblies, do not grieve."

children.text: sa ruditvā ciraṃ kālaṃ bhūmau viparivṛtya ca
children.translated_text: After weeping for a long time and rolling on the ground,
he replied to his mother, enveloped by many sorrows:

children.text: abhiṣekṣyati rāmaṃ tu rājā yajñaṃ nu yakṣyati
children.translated_text: "The king will consecrate <s>Rāma</s>, or perhaps he will perform a sacrifice,

children.text: ity ahaṃ kṛtasaṃkalpo hṛṣṭo yātrām ayāsiṣam ||
children.translated_text: thinking thus, I set out on the journey with fixed resolve and joy.

children.text: tad idaṃ hy anyathā bhūtaṃ vyavadīrṇaṃ mano mama
children.translated_text: But this has turned out otherwise; my mind is split apart,

children.text: pitaraṃ yo na paśyāmi nityaṃ priyahite ratam ||
children.translated_text: because I do not see my father, who was always devoted to what was dear and beneficial.

children.text: amba kenātyagād rājā vyādhinā mayy anāgate
children.translated_text: Mother, by what illness did the king pass away while I was absent?

children.text: dhanyā rāmādayaḥ sarve yaiḥ pitā saṃskṛtaḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: Blessed are all, beginning with <s>Rāma</s>, by whom the rites for Father were performed in person.

children.text: na nūnaṃ māṃ mahārājaḥ prāptaṃ jānāti kīrtimān
children.translated_text: Surely the famed great king does not know that I have arrived;

children.text: upajighreddhi māṃ mūrdhni tātaḥ saṃnamya satvaram ||
children.translated_text: for Father would quickly bend down and smell my head.
Where is that hand of Father, pleasant to the touch, whose deeds were unwearied,

children.text: yena māṃ rajasā dhvastam abhīkṣṇaṃ parimārjati ||
children.translated_text: with which he often wiped me clean when I was covered with dust?

children.text: yo me bhrātā pitā bandhur yasya dāso 'smi dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: He who is my brother, father, and kinsman, whose servant I am, that wise one,
tell me quickly about that <s>Rāma</s> of unwearied deeds.

children.text: pitā hi bhavati jyeṣṭho dharmam āryasya jānataḥ
children.translated_text: For an elder brother is a father to a noble man who knows <s>dharma</s> (righteous order);

children.text: tasya pādau grahīṣyāmi sa hīdānīṃ gatir mama ||
children.translated_text: I will clasp his feet, for he is now my refuge.

children.text: ārye kim abravīd rājā pitā me satyavikramaḥ
children.translated_text: Noble lady, what did the king, my father of true valor, say?
I wish to hear the last good message intended for me."

children.text: iti pṛṣṭā yathātattvaṃ kaikeyī vākyam abravīt
children.translated_text: Thus asked, <s>Kaikeyī</s> told the matter as it was:

children.text: rāmeti rājā vilapan hā sīte lakṣmaṇeti ca
children.translated_text: The king, crying "<s>Rāma</s>!" and lamenting, "Ah <s>Sītā</s>! <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>!",

children.text: sa mahātmā paraṃ lokaṃ gato gatimatāṃ varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that great-souled one, best of those who go on, went to the highest world.

children.text: imāṃ tu paścimāṃ vācaṃ vyājahāra pitā tava
children.translated_text: "But your father uttered these last words,
overcome by the law of time, like a great elephant bound in nooses:

children.text: siddhārthās tu narā rāmam āgataṃ sītayā saha
children.translated_text: 'Men who have accomplished their purpose will see <s>Rāma</s> returned with <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahābāhuṃ drakṣyanti punar āgatam ||
children.translated_text: and mighty-armed <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> also come back again.'"
Hearing that, he sank down at once at this second report of something unwelcome;
with face dejected, he again asked his mother:
"And where now has that righteous-souled increaser of <s>Kausalyā</s>'s joy gone,

children.text: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā sītayā ca samaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: together with his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and with <s>Sītā</s>?"
Thus questioned, she began to relate the truth,
his mother, all at once speaking words unwelcome though she hoped they would be pleasing:

children.text: sa hi rājasutaḥ putra cīravāsā mahāvanam
children.translated_text: "For that prince, son, wearing bark garments, has gone to the great forest,
to the <s>Daṇḍakas</s>, with <s>Vaidehī</s>, followed by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>."

children.text: tac chrutvā bharatas trasto bhrātuś cāritraśaṅkayā
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Bharata</s> was alarmed, suspecting some fault in his brother's conduct;
because of the greatness of his own lineage, he began to question her:

children.text: kaccin na brāhmaṇadhanaṃ hṛtaṃ rāmeṇa kasyacit
children.translated_text: "Surely no brahmin's wealth was taken by <s>Rāma</s> from anyone?

children.text: kaccin nāḍhyo daridro vā tenāpāpo vihiṃsitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Surely no innocent rich or poor man was harmed by him?
Surely the prince did not desire another's wife?
Why has he been exiled to the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest like a slayer of an embryo?"

children.text: athāsya capalā mātā tat svakarma yathātatham
children.translated_text: Then his fickle mother began to tell that deed of her own just as it was,
in that very disposition of hers as a woman:
"No brahmin's wealth at all was taken by <s>Rāma</s> from anyone;

children.text: kaścin nāḍhyo daridro vā tenāpāpo vihiṃsitaḥ
children.translated_text: nor was any innocent rich or poor man harmed by him.

children.text: na rāmaḥ paradārāṃś ca cakṣurbhyām api paśyati ||
children.translated_text: Nor does <s>Rāma</s> even look with his eyes upon other men's wives.
But I, son, as soon as I heard of <s>Rāma</s>'s consecration,

children.text: yācitas te pitā rājyaṃ rāmasya ca vivāsanam ||
children.translated_text: asked your father for the kingdom and for <s>Rāma</s>'s exile.

children.text: sa svavṛttiṃ samāsthāya pitā te tat tathākarot
children.translated_text: Your father, keeping to his own conduct, did exactly that;

children.text: rāmaś ca sahasaumitriḥ preṣitaḥ saha sītayā ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Rāma</s> was sent away with <s>Saumitri</s> and with <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: tam apaśyan priyaṃ putraṃ mahīpālo mahāyaśāḥ
children.translated_text: Not seeing that dear son, the greatly famous protector of the earth,
wasted by grief for his son, reached the state of the five elements.

children.text: tvayā tv idānīṃ dharmajña rājatvam avalambyatām
children.translated_text: But now, knower of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), kingship should be taken up by you;

children.text: tvatkṛte hi mayā sarvam idam evaṃvidhaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: for all this of such a kind was done by me for your sake.

children.text: tat putra śīghraṃ vidhinā vidhijñair vasiṣṭhamukhyaiḥ sahito dvijendraiḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, son, quickly, together with the foremost brahmins headed by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, who know the rite,

children.text: saṃkālya rājānam adīnasattvam ātmānam urvyām abhiṣecayasva ||
children.translated_text: having duly performed the rites for the undaunted king, have yourself consecrated over the earth."

children.text: śrutvā tu pitaraṃ vṛttaṃ bhrātarau ca vivāsitau
children.translated_text: But hearing that his father was dead and that his two brothers had been exiled,
<s>Bharata</s>, scorched by grief, spoke these words:

children.text: kiṃ nu kāryaṃ hatasyeha mama rājyena śocataḥ
children.translated_text: What use is kingship here to me, as good as dead and grieving,

children.text: vihīnasyātha pitrā ca bhrātrā pitṛsamena ca ||
children.translated_text: now that I am bereft of my father and of my brother, who is equal to my father?

children.text: duḥkhe me duḥkham akaror vraṇe kṣāram ivādadhāḥ
children.translated_text: You have added sorrow to my sorrow, as one pours alkali on a wound,

children.text: rājānaṃ pretabhāvasthaṃ kṛtvā rāmaṃ ca tāpasam ||
children.translated_text: by bringing the king to the state of the dead and making <s>Rāma</s> an ascetic.
You have come for the destruction of the family like the night of doom.

children.text: aṅgāram upagūhya sma pitā me nāvabuddhavān ||
children.translated_text: My father did not realize that he had clasped a burning coal.
<s>Kausalyā</s> and <s>Sumitrā</s>, oppressed by grief for their sons,

children.text: duṣkaraṃ yadi jīvetāṃ prāpya tvāṃ jananīṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: will do a difficult thing if they live on, having you as my mother.

children.text: nanu tv āryo 'pi dharmātmā tvayi vṛttim anuttamām
children.translated_text: Surely even the noble, righteous <s>Rāma</s>, knowing the highest conduct toward you,
behaved as one behaves toward a mother, knowing the proper conduct toward an elder.

children.text: tathā jyeṣṭhā hi me mātā kausalyā dīrghadarśinī
children.translated_text: So too my eldest mother, far-seeing <s>Kausalyā</s>,

children.text: tvayi dharmaṃ samāsthāya bhaginyām iva vartate ||
children.translated_text: stands firm in <s>dharma</s> toward you and behaves as toward a sister.
Having sent her self-possessed son, clad in bark and strips of cloth,

children.text: prasthāpya vanavāsāya kathaṃ pāpe na śocasi ||
children.translated_text: to dwell in the forest, how, sinful woman, do you not grieve?
Having banished that blameless, heroic, self-mastered, famous man,

children.text: pravrājya cīravasanaṃ kiṃ nu paśyasi kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: clad in bark garments, what reason do you see for it?

children.text: lubdhāyā vidito manye na te 'haṃ rāghavaṃ prati
children.translated_text: Greedy as you are, I think you did not know how I stood toward <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: tathā hy anartho rājyārthaṃ tvayā nīto mahān ayam ||
children.translated_text: for this great disaster has been brought about by you for the sake of the kingdom.
For without seeing those two tigers among men, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
by what power or might shall I be able to protect the kingdom?

children.text: taṃ hi nityaṃ mahārājo balavantaṃ mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: For the great king, though himself very powerful, always relied on that strong one,
that righteous one, as <s>Meru</s> relies on the forest of <s>Meru</s>.
How then shall I bear this burden, raised up for a mighty draught-beast,

children.text: damyo dhuram ivāsādya saheyaṃ kena caujasā ||
children.translated_text: like a trainable animal that has come under the yoke? By what strength could I do so?

children.text: athavā me bhavec chaktir yogair buddhibalena vā
children.translated_text: Or even if strength should be mine through means or through the power of intellect,

children.text: sakāmāṃ na kariṣyāmi tvām ahaṃ putragardhinīm
children.translated_text: I will not fulfill your desire, greedy for your son as you are;
I will bring back from the forest my brother, beloved of his kinsmen.

children.text: ity evam uktvā bharato mahātmā priyetarair vākyagaṇais tudaṃs tām
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the noble <s>Bharata</s>, piercing her with clusters of unwelcome words,

children.text: śokāturaś cāpi nanāda bhūyaḥ siṃho yathā parvatagahvarasthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: though distressed by grief, roared again like a lion in a mountain cave.

children.text: tāṃ tathā garhayitvā tu mātaraṃ bharatas tadā
children.translated_text: Then, having reproached his mother in that way, <s>Bharata</s> at that time,
possessed by great anger, again spoke these words:
Fall away from the kingdom, <s>Kaikeyī</s>, cruel woman of evil conduct;

children.text: parityaktā ca dharmeṇa mā mṛtaṃ rudatī bhava ||
children.translated_text: abandoned by <s>dharma</s>, do not live to weep for me when I am dead.

children.text: kiṃ nu te 'dūṣayad rājā rāmo vā bhṛśadhārmikaḥ
children.translated_text: What offense did the king do to you, or <s>Rāma</s>, so deeply righteous,

children.text: yayor mṛtyur vivāsaś ca tvatkṛte tulyam āgatau ||
children.translated_text: that death for one and exile for the other have come alike because of you?
You have incurred the sin of embryo-killing by destroying this family;

children.text: kaikeyi narakaṃ gaccha mā ca bhartuḥ salokatām ||
children.translated_text: go to hell, <s>Kaikeyī</s>, and do not share your husband's world.

children.text: yat tvayā hīdṛśaṃ pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ ghoreṇa karmaṇā
children.translated_text: Since such a sin was done by you through a terrible act,
abandoning one dear to all the world, fear has been brought even upon me.

children.text: tvatkṛte me pitā vṛtto rāmaś cāraṇyam āśritaḥ
children.translated_text: Because of you my father is dead and <s>Rāma</s> has taken refuge in the forest;
and by you I have been brought into disgrace in the world of the living.
Enemy of mine in the form of a mother, cruel woman, desiring the kingdom,
you are not fit to be addressed by me, wicked woman, killer of your husband.

children.text: kausalyā ca sumitrā ca yāś cānyā mama mātaraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kausalyā</s> and <s>Sumitrā</s> and the other women who are my mothers
are overwhelmed by great sorrow because they have met you, defiler of the family.

children.text: na tvam aśvapateḥ kanyā dharmarājasya dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: You are not the daughter of <s>Aśvapati</s>, the wise king of righteousness;
you were born there as a rākṣasī, destroyer of your father's line.

children.text: yat tvayā dhārmiko rāmo nityaṃ satyaparāyaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Because righteous <s>Rāma</s>, ever devoted to truth,

children.text: vanaṃ prasthāpito duḥkhāt pitā ca tridivaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: was sent by you to the forest in sorrow, and my father has gone to heaven,

children.text: yatpradhānāsi tat pāpaṃ mayi pitrā vinākṛte
children.translated_text: that sin, of which you are the chief cause, rests on me, deprived of my father,
abandoned by my brothers and displeasing to all the world.
Having separated <s>Kausalyā</s>, joined to <s>dharma</s>, from her son, you whose resolve is sinful,

children.text: kṛtvā kaṃ prāpsyase tv adya lokaṃ nirayagāminī ||
children.translated_text: what world will you obtain today, you who are bound for hell?
Do you not understand, cruel woman, that attachment to kin is fixed,
and that <s>Rāma</s>, the eldest, equal to a father, is born from <s>Kausalyā</s>'s own self?
A son is born from every limb and sub-limb, and also from the heart;

children.text: tasmāt priyataro mātuḥ priyatvān na tu bāndhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore he is dearer to a mother, not merely a kinsman by being dear.
Once, they say, the righteous <s>Surabhi</s>, honored by the gods,
saw her two sons on the earth, bearing a load and exhausted.

children.text: tāv ardhadivase śrāntau dṛṣṭvā putrau mahītale
children.translated_text: Seeing her two sons on the ground, weary at midday,
she wept from grief for her sons, her eyes clouded with tears.
As she passed above that great-souled king of the gods,
fine drops, fragrant with <s>Surabhi</s>'s scent, fell on his body.
Seeing the glorious one burned by sorrow,
<s>Indra</s>, wielder of the thunderbolt, the king of the gods, anxious and with joined palms, spoke these words:

children.text: bhayaṃ kaccin na cāsmāsu kutaścid vidyate mahat
children.translated_text: Surely there is no great danger to us from any quarter?
What is the cause of your grief? Tell me, seeker of the good of all.

children.text: evam uktā tu surabhiḥ surarājena dhīmatā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the wise king of the gods,
steadfast <s>Surabhi</s>, skilled in speech, then replied with these words:

children.text: śāntaṃ pāpaṃ na vaḥ kiṃcit kutaścid amarādhipa
children.translated_text: Let evil be stilled; there is no danger to you from anywhere, lord of the immortals.

children.text: ahaṃ tu magnau śocāmi svaputrau viṣame sthitau ||
children.translated_text: But I grieve for my two sons, sunk down and placed in hardship.
Seeing these two oxen lean, wretched, scorched by the sun's rays,
tormented by a farmer, O lord of the gods,

children.text: mama kāyāt prasūtau hi duḥkhitau bhārapīḍitau
children.translated_text: for they were born from my body, distressed and oppressed by burdens.

children.text: yau dṛṣṭvā paritapye 'haṃ nāsti putrasamaḥ priyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing those two, I am scorched with grief; there is no beloved thing equal to a son.
Even the wish-granting cow, who has thousands of sons, grieves.

children.text: kiṃ punar yā vinā rāmaṃ kausalyā vartayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: How then will <s>Kausalyā</s>, deprived of <s>Rāma</s>, go on living?

children.text: ekaputrā ca sādhvī ca vivatseyaṃ tvayā kṛtā
children.translated_text: She is virtuous and has only one son; she has been made calf-less by you.

children.text: tasmāt tvaṃ satataṃ duḥkhaṃ pretya ceha ca lapsyase ||
children.translated_text: Therefore you will obtain constant suffering both after death and here in this world.

children.text: ahaṃ hy apacitiṃ bhrātuḥ pituś ca sakalām imām
children.translated_text: For I shall make this whole expiation toward my brother and my father,

children.text: vardhanaṃ yaśasaś cāpi kariṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and shall also increase their fame; there is no doubt of it.
Having brought back <s>Kausalyā</s>'s son, the one of great splendor,
I myself shall enter the forest frequented by sages.
Saying this, like an elephant in the forest driven by a lance and goad,

children.text: papāta bhuvi saṃkruddho niḥśvasann iva pannagaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he fell upon the ground in anger, sighing like a serpent.
Then, with reddened eyes, his garment loosened and all his ornaments shaken off, the subduer of foes

children.text: babhūva bhūmau patito nṛpātmajaḥ śacīpateḥ ketur ivotsavakṣaye ||
children.translated_text: lay fallen on the ground, like the banner of <s>Śacīpati</s> at the end of a festival.
While the great-souled <s>Bharata</s> was crying out in that way,

children.text: kausalyā śabdam ājñāya sumitrām idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kausalyā</s>, recognizing the sound, said this to <s>Sumitrā</s>:
<s>Bharata</s>, the son of <s>Kaikeyī</s> of cruel deeds, has come.

children.text: tam ahaṃ draṣṭum icchāmi bharataṃ dīrghadarśinam ||
children.translated_text: I wish to see that far-seeing <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: evam uktvā sumitrāṃ sā vivarṇā malināmbarā
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to <s>Sumitrā</s>, she, pale and in soiled garments,
set out, trembling and senseless, to where <s>Bharata</s> was.

children.text: sa tu rāmānujaś cāpi śatrughnasahitas tadā
children.translated_text: And <s>Bharata</s>, the younger brother of <s>Rāma</s>, together with <s>Śatrughna</s> at that time,
set out for the residence of <s>Kausalyā</s>.
Then <s>Śatrughna</s> and <s>Bharata</s>, seeing <s>Kausalyā</s> distressed,
embraced her, afflicted with grief, fallen down and unconscious.
<s>Kausalyā</s>, deeply afflicted with grief, said this to <s>Bharata</s>:

children.text: idaṃ te rājyakāmasya rājyaṃ prāptam akaṇṭakam
children.translated_text: This kingdom, desired by you, has now been obtained without obstacle.

children.text: samprāptaṃ bata kaikeyyā śīghraṃ krūreṇa karmaṇā ||
children.translated_text: Alas, it has been obtained by <s>Kaikeyī</s> swiftly through a cruel deed.
After sending away my son, clad in bark garments and dwelling in the forest,

children.text: kaikeyī kaṃ guṇaṃ tatra paśyati krūradarśinī ||
children.translated_text: what virtue does cruel-looking <s>Kaikeyī</s> see in that?

children.text: kṣipraṃ mām api kaikeyī prasthāpayitum arhati
children.translated_text: <s>Kaikeyī</s> ought quickly to send me away as well,
to where my son, the greatly renowned <s>Hiraṇyanābha</s>, stays.
Or else I myself, gladly accompanied by <s>Sumitrā</s>,
placing the <s>agnihotra</s> (sacred fire-oblation) before me, shall set out to where <s>Rāghava</s> is.

children.text: kāmaṃ vā svayam evādya tatra māṃ netum arhasi
children.translated_text: Or, if you wish, you yourself ought to lead me there today,

children.text: yatrāsau puruṣavyāghras tapyate me tapaḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: where that tiger among men, my son, is practicing austerity.
For this broad kingdom of yours, filled with wealth and grain,
full of elephants, horses, and chariots, has been handed over to you by her.

children.text: evaṃ vilapamānāṃ tāṃ bharataḥ prāñjalis tadā
children.translated_text: As she was lamenting in this way, <s>Bharata</s> then, with joined palms,
replied to <s>Kausalyā</s>, who was enveloped by many sorrows:

children.text: ārye kasmād ajānantaṃ garhase mām akilbiṣam
children.translated_text: Noble lady, why do you blame me, ignorant of this and free from guilt?

children.text: vipulāṃ ca mama prītiṃ sthirāṃ jānāsi rāghave ||
children.translated_text: You know my great and steady affection for <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: kṛtā śāstrānugā buddhir mā bhūt tasya kadācana
children.translated_text: May a mind guided by scripture never be formed in the man
by whose consent my noble brother, true to his word and best of the good, went away.

children.text: praiṣyaṃ pāpīyasāṃ yātu sūryaṃ ca prati mehatu
children.translated_text: May he go into servitude among the most sinful, and may he urinate facing the sun;

children.text: hantu pādena gāṃ suptāṃ yasyāryo 'numate gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: may he strike a sleeping cow with his foot, if my noble brother went away with his consent.

children.text: kārayitvā mahat karma bhartā bhṛtyam anarthakam
children.translated_text: When a master, after making a servant perform a great task, treats him as useless,

children.text: adharmo yo 'sya so 'syās tu yasyāryo 'numate gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: whatever <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) belongs to him, may that be his, if my noble brother went away with his consent.
May the sin of one who betrays a king while he protects beings like his sons

children.text: tatas tu druhyatāṃ pāpaṃ yasyāryo 'numate gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: belong to the man by whose consent my noble brother went away.
Whatever <s>adharma</s> belongs to a king who takes a sixth share as tax
but does not protect his subjects, may that be his, if my noble brother went away with his consent.

children.text: saṃśrutya ca tapasvibhyaḥ sattre vai yajñadakṣiṇām
children.translated_text: After promising sacrificial fees to ascetics at a sattra sacrifice,
may the sin of one who defrauds them of that be his, if my noble brother went away with his consent.
In battle crowded with elephants, horses, and chariots, and filled with weapons,

children.text: mā sma kārṣīt satāṃ dharmaṃ yasyāryo 'numate gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: may he fail to perform the <s>dharma</s> (duty) of the good, if my noble brother went away with his consent.
May that wicked-souled man destroy the scripture, subtle in meaning,
which has been carefully taught by a wise man, if my noble brother went away with his consent.

children.text: pāyasaṃ kṛsaraṃ chāgaṃ vṛthā so 'śnātu nirghṛṇaḥ
children.translated_text: May that merciless man eat sweet rice, rice-and-sesame gruel, and goat's meat in vain,
and may he also disrespect his elders, if my noble brother went away with his consent.

children.text: putrair dāraiś ca bhṛtyaiś ca svagṛhe parivāritaḥ
children.translated_text: Surrounded in his own house by sons, wives, and servants,

children.text: sa eko mṛṣṭam aśnātu yasyāryo 'numate gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: may he alone eat choice food, if my noble brother went away with his consent.
Whatever sin is said to lie in the killing of kings, women, children, and the aged,

children.text: bhṛtyatyāge ca yat pāpaṃ tat pāpaṃ pratipadyatām ||
children.translated_text: and whatever sin lies in abandoning servants, may he incur that sin.

children.text: ubhe saṃdhye śayānasya yat pāpaṃ parikalpyate
children.translated_text: Whatever sin is reckoned for one who sleeps through both twilights,

children.text: tac ca pāpaṃ bhavet tasya yasyāryo 'numate gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: may that sin be his, if my noble brother went away with his consent.

children.text: yad agnidāyake pāpaṃ yat pāpaṃ gurutalpage
children.translated_text: Whatever sin belongs to an arsonist, whatever sin to one who violates his teacher's bed,

children.text: mitradrohe ca yat pāpaṃ tat pāpaṃ pratipadyatām ||
children.translated_text: and whatever sin lies in betraying a friend, may he incur that sin.

children.text: devatānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca mātāpitros tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: May he not render service to the gods, the ancestors,

children.text: mā sma kārṣīt sa śuśrūṣāṃ yasyāryo 'numate gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor likewise to his mother and father, if my noble brother went away with his consent.

children.text: satāṃ lokāt satāṃ kīrtyāḥ sajjuṣṭāt karmaṇas tathā
children.translated_text: From the world of the good, from the fame of the good, and from deeds honored by the good,
may he fall quickly, this very day, if my noble brother went away with his consent.
Thus consoling <s>Kausalyā</s>, bereft of husband and son,

children.text: evam āśvāsayann eva duḥkhārto nipapāta ha ||
children.translated_text: the prince himself, afflicted with grief, fell down.

children.text: tathā tu śapathaiḥ kaṣṭaiḥ śapamānam acetanam
children.translated_text: Then, as he was swearing with harsh oaths and had lost consciousness,
<s>Kausalyā</s> spoke words to <s>Bharata</s>, who was scorched by grief.

children.text: mama duḥkham idaṃ putra bhūyaḥ samupajāyate
children.translated_text: My sorrow, my son, is now arising again.

children.text: śapathaiḥ śapamāno hi prāṇān uparuṇatsi me ||
children.translated_text: For, while swearing these oaths, you are choking off my very life-breaths.

children.text: diṣṭyā na calito dharmād ātmā te sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Fortunately your self, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, has not swerved from <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty).

children.text: vatsa satyapratijño me satāṃ lokān avāpsyasi ||
children.translated_text: My child, true to your promise, you will attain the worlds of the good.
As that great-souled one was lamenting in this way, afflicted by sorrow,

children.text: mohāc ca śokasaṃrodhād babhūva lulitaṃ manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: his mind became confused through bewilderment and the obstruction of grief.
While he babbled, senseless, his understanding lost, fallen on the ground,

children.text: muhur muhur niḥśvasataś ca dīrghaṃ sā tasya śokena jagāma rātriḥ ||
children.translated_text: and again and again breathed long sighs, that night passed for him in sorrow.
To <s>Bharata</s>, son of <s>Kaikeyī</s>, thus scorched by grief,

children.text: uvāca vadatāṃ śreṣṭho vasiṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhavāg ṛṣiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the sage <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, best of speakers and best in speech, said:

children.text: alaṃ śokena bhadraṃ te rājaputra mahāyaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Enough of grief. May it be well with you, prince of great fame.
Perform now the king's final departure rite, for its proper time has come.

children.text: vasiṣṭhasya vacaḥ śrutvā bharato dhāraṇāṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s words, <s>Bharata</s> regained steadiness,
and, knowing <s>dharma</s>, had all the rites for the dead performed.

children.text: uddhṛtaṃ tailasaṃkledāt sa tu bhūmau niveśitam
children.translated_text: The king was taken out from his soaking in oil and then placed on the ground,
his face yellowish in color, as if the lord of the earth were asleep.
After placing <s>Daśaratha</s> on an excellent couch adorned with many jewels,
his son, exceedingly sorrowful, then lamented over him.

children.text: kiṃ te vyavasitaṃ rājan proṣite mayy anāgate
children.translated_text: What did you resolve, O king, while I was away and had not yet returned,

children.text: vivāsya rāmaṃ dharmajñaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahābalam ||
children.translated_text: when you sent into exile <s>Rāma</s>, knower of <s>dharma</s>, and mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>?

children.text: kva yāsyasi mahārāja hitvemaṃ duḥkhitaṃ janam
children.translated_text: Where will you go, great king, abandoning this sorrowing people,
deprived of <s>Rāma</s>, that lion among men whose deeds are never wearisome?

children.text: yogakṣemaṃ tu te rājan ko 'smin kalpayitā pure
children.translated_text: Who, O king, will provide welfare and security in this city for you,

children.text: tvayi prayāte svas tāta rāme ca vanam āśrite ||
children.translated_text: when you have gone to heaven, father, and <s>Rāma</s> has taken refuge in the forest?

children.text: vidhavā pṛthivī rājaṃs tvayā hīnā na rājate
children.translated_text: Widowed, O king, the earth does not shine, deprived of you;
the city appears to me like a night without the moon.
As <s>Bharata</s>, wretched in mind, was lamenting in this way,

children.text: abravīd vacanaṃ bhūyo vasiṣṭhas tu mahān ṛṣiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the great sage <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> again spoke these words to him:
The rites for the dead that must be performed for this lord of the people,
let them be carried out calmly, mighty-armed one, without delay.
Saying, 'So be it,' <s>Bharata</s> honored that command of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,
and urged on the officiating priests, family priests, and teachers in every way.

children.text: ye tv agrato narendrasya agnyagārād bahiṣkṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Those fires of the king that had been carried out beforehand from the fire-house,

children.text: ṛtvigbhir yājakaiś caiva te hriyante yathāvidhi ||
children.translated_text: were borne away according to rule by the officiants and sacrificers.
Then the attendants lifted the lifeless king onto a palanquin,
and, their throats choked with tears and their minds dejected, carried him.

children.text: hiraṇyaṃ ca suvarṇaṃ ca vāsāṃsi vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: Scattering gold, refined gold, and various garments,

children.text: prakiranto janā mārgaṃ nṛpater agrato yayuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the people went before the king along the road.
Bringing sandalwood, aloe-resin, resinous pine, padmaka wood,
and deodar wood as well, others made the funeral pyre.

children.text: gandhān uccāvacāṃś cānyāṃs tatra dattvātha bhūmipam
children.translated_text: After placing there various kinds of perfumes and fragrant substances, and then the lord of the earth,
the priests then laid him in the middle of the pyre.

children.text: tathā hutāśanaṃ hutvā jepus tasya tadartvijaḥ
children.translated_text: Having offered the oblation into the fire in the proper way, those priests recited for him,

children.text: jaguś ca te yathāśāstraṃ tatra sāmāni sāmagāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the chanters of <s>Sāman</s> hymns sang the <s>Sāmans</s> there according to scripture.

children.text: śibikābhiś ca yānaiś ca yathārhaṃ tasya yoṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: In palanquins and vehicles, as was fitting, his women

children.text: nagarān niryayus tatra vṛddhaiḥ parivṛtās tadā ||
children.translated_text: then went out from the city, surrounded by elders.

children.text: prasavyaṃ cāpi taṃ cakrur ṛtvijo 'gnicitaṃ nṛpam
children.translated_text: The priests circumambulated the king, laid on the fire-built pyre, counterclockwise,
as did the women, scorched with grief, with <s>Kausalyā</s> at their head.

children.text: krauñcīnām iva nārīṇāṃ ninādas tatra śuśruve
children.translated_text: There was heard at that time a cry of women like female krauñca birds,
piteous, from thousands crying out in distress.

children.text: tato rudantyo vivaśā vilapya ca punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, weeping, helpless, and lamenting again and again,
the noble women descended from their vehicles to the bank of the <s>Sarayū</s>.

children.text: kṛtodakaṃ te bharatena sārdhaṃ nṛpāṅganā mantripurohitāś ca
children.translated_text: The king's women, ministers, and priests, together with <s>Bharata</s>, performed the water offering,

children.text: puraṃ praviśyāśruparītanetrā bhūmau daśāhaṃ vyanayanta duḥkham ||
children.translated_text: and, entering the city with eyes filled with tears, spent ten days on the ground in grief.
Then, when the ten days had passed and the prince had completed purification,
on the arrival of the twelfth day he had the <s>śrāddha</s> rites performed.

children.text: brāhmaṇebhyo dadau ratnaṃ dhanam annaṃ ca puṣkalam
children.translated_text: He gave jewels, wealth, and abundant food to the brahmins,

children.text: bāstikaṃ bahuśuklaṃ ca gāś cāpi śataśas tathā ||
children.translated_text: and many white goats, and also cows by the hundreds.

children.text: dāsīdāsaṃ ca yānaṃ ca veśmāni sumahānti ca
children.translated_text: Female slaves and male slaves, vehicles, and very large houses
the king's son gave to the brahmins as the rite for him after death.
Then at daybreak on the thirteenth day,
mighty-armed <s>Bharata</s>, overwhelmed by grief, lamented.
His throat muffled by sobbing, he had come for the rite of purification,

children.text: citāmūle pitur vākyam idam āha suduḥkhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and at the foot of his father's pyre, deeply sorrowful, he spoke these words:

children.text: tāta yasmin nisṛṣṭo 'haṃ tvayā bhrātari rāghave
children.translated_text: Father, when I had been entrusted by you to my brother <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: tasmin vanaṃ pravrajite śūnye tyakto 'smy ahaṃ tvayā ||
children.translated_text: and he has gone forth to the forest, I have been abandoned by you in emptiness.
That helpless mother, whose son has been banished to the forest, has no refuge;

children.text: tām ambāṃ tāta kausalyāṃ tyaktvā tvaṃ kva gato nṛpa ||
children.translated_text: abandoning her, father, abandoning <s>Kausalyā</s>, where have you gone, O king?
Seeing that circle of the place of burnt bones, reddened with ash,
and his father's body reduced to nothing, he groaned and sank down in despair.

children.text: sa tu dṛṣṭvā rudan dīnaḥ papāta dharaṇītale
children.translated_text: Seeing it, he, weeping and miserable, fell upon the surface of the earth,
while being lifted up, like <s>Śakra</s>'s mechanical banner that had fallen.
Then all his ministers hastened toward him, whose vows were pure,
as the seers once did to <s>Yayāti</s>, fallen at the end of his time.
And <s>Śatrughna</s> too, seeing <s>Bharata</s> overwhelmed by grief,
he fell unconscious upon the ground, remembering the lord of the earth.
Like a madman, senseless and deeply afflicted, he lamented,

children.text: smṛtvā pitur guṇāṅgāni tāni tāni tadā tadā ||
children.translated_text: again and again recalling those many virtues of his father.
The fierce ocean of grief, sprung from <s>Mantharā</s>, crowded with <s>Kaikeyī</s> as its sea-monster,
made of the granting of boons and impossible to withstand, drowned him.

children.text: sukumāraṃ ca bālaṃ ca satataṃ lālitaṃ tvayā
children.translated_text: Leaving <s>Bharata</s>, tender and young, always cherished by you,

children.text: kva tāta bharataṃ hitvā vilapantaṃ gato bhavān ||
children.translated_text: where, father, have you gone, while he laments?

children.text: nanu bhojyeṣu pāneṣu vastreṣv ābharaṇeṣu ca
children.translated_text: Surely in foods, drinks, garments, and ornaments

children.text: pravārayasi naḥ sarvāṃs tan naḥ ko 'dya kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: you used to satisfy us all; who will do that for us now?
Even at a time for splitting open, the earth does not split apart,

children.text: vihīnā yā tvayā rājñā dharmajñena mahātmanā ||
children.translated_text: though it is bereft of you, the king, the great-souled knower of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: pitari svargam āpanne rāme cāraṇyam āśrite
children.translated_text: When my father has gone to heaven and <s>Rāma</s> has resorted to the forest,
what power is there in life for me? I shall enter the fire.

children.text: hīno bhrātrā ca pitrā ca śūnyām ikṣvākupālitām
children.translated_text: Bereft of my brother and my father, I shall not enter <s>Ayodhyā</s>,
empty though guarded by the <s>Ikṣvākus</s>; I shall enter the ascetic grove.

children.text: tayor vilapitaṃ śrutvā vyasanaṃ cānvavekṣya tat
children.translated_text: Having heard the lament of those two and having considered that calamity,
all their followers became even more intensely afflicted again.

children.text: tato viṣaṇṇau śrāntau ca śatrughnabharatāv ubhau
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śatrughna</s> and <s>Bharata</s> both, dejected and exhausted,
writhed upon the ground like two bulls with broken horns.

children.text: tataḥ prakṛtimān vaidyaḥ pitur eṣāṃ purohitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, self-possessed and learned, the family priest of their father,

children.text: vasiṣṭho bharataṃ vākyam utthāpya tam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: raised <s>Bharata</s> up and spoke this word to him.
Three pairs of opposites have come into being among creatures without distinction;
since they are unavoidable, one should not behave in this way regarding them.
And <s>Sumantra</s>, too, raised <s>Śatrughna</s> and soothed him,
and, knowing reality, made him hear of the coming-to-be and passing-away of all beings.
When those two tigers among men had risen, the famous pair shone forth,
like two separate banners of <s>Indra</s>, weathered by rain and heat.
Wiping away their tears, red-eyed, and speaking pitifully,

children.text: amātyās tvarayanti sma tanayau cāparāḥ kriyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the ministers hastened the sons on to the remaining rites.
There <s>Śatrughna</s>, the younger brother of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, spoke this word
to <s>Bharata</s>, scorched by grief and intent on the journey.

children.text: gatir yaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ duḥkhe kiṃ punar ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: He who is the refuge of all beings in distress, how much more of his own people,

children.text: sa rāmaḥ sattvasampannaḥ striyā pravrājito vanam ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Rāma</s>, endowed with strength of character, has been sent to the forest by a woman.

children.text: balavān vīryasampanno lakṣmaṇo nāma yo 'py asau
children.translated_text: And that one named <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, strong and endowed with valor,

children.text: kiṃ na mocayate rāmaṃ kṛtvāpi pitṛnigraham ||
children.translated_text: why does he not free <s>Rāma</s>, even by restraining his father?

children.text: pūrvam eva tu nigrāhyaḥ samavekṣya nayānayau
children.translated_text: He should have been restrained at the very start, after considering right policy and wrong policy,

children.text: utpathaṃ yaḥ samārūḍho nāryā rājā vaśaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king who had mounted the wrong path and come under a woman's control.
While <s>Śatrughna</s>, the younger brother of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, was speaking thus,
the hunchback appeared then at the eastern gate, adorned with every ornament.
She was smeared with essence of sandalwood and wore royal garments,
with various girdle-strings, like a monkey tied with ropes.

children.text: tāṃ samīkṣya tadā dvāḥstho bhṛśaṃ pāpasya kāriṇīm
children.translated_text: Seeing her then, the doorkeeper, seeing the cruel hunchback who had done great evil,
seized the pitiless hunchback and reported her to <s>Śatrughna</s>.

children.text: yasyāḥ kṛte vane rāmo nyastadehaś ca vaḥ pitā
children.translated_text: For whose sake <s>Rāma</s> is in the forest and your father has laid down his body,

children.text: seyaṃ pāpā nṛśaṃsā ca tasyāḥ kuru yathāmati ||
children.translated_text: this is that wicked and cruel woman; do with her as you think fit.

children.text: śatrughnaś ca tad ājñāya vacanaṃ bhṛśaduḥkhitaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Śatrughna</s>, deeply distressed, learned that speech,
he, firm in his vow, spoke thus to all the attendants of the inner palace:

children.text: tīvram utpāditaṃ duḥkhaṃ bhrātṝṇāṃ me tathā pituḥ
children.translated_text: By whom fierce suffering has been produced for my brothers and also for my father,

children.text: yayā seyaṃ nṛśaṃsasya karmaṇaḥ phalam aśnutām ||
children.translated_text: let this woman now experience the fruit of her cruel deed.
When he had thus spoken, the hunchback, surrounded by her companions,

children.text: gṛhītā balavat kubjā sā tadgṛham anādayat ||
children.translated_text: was quickly seized with force and made that house resound with cries.
Then all her companions were extremely distressed,
and, knowing <s>Śatrughna</s> to be angry, they fled in every direction.
And the whole company of her companions conferred together:
As he has begun, he will make an end of us without remainder.

children.text: sānukrośāṃ vadānyāṃ ca dharmajñāṃ ca yaśasvinīm
children.translated_text: Let us go for refuge to <s>Kausalyā</s>, compassionate, generous,

children.text: kausalyāṃ śaraṇaṃ yāmaḥ sā hi no 'stu dhruvā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: a knower of <s>dharma</s> and renowned; may she be our sure refuge.

children.text: sa ca roṣeṇa tāmrākṣaḥ śatrughnaḥ śatrutāpanaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śatrughna</s>, the scorcher of foes, his eyes copper-red with rage,
dragged the hunchback, crying out, over the surface of the earth.

children.text: tasyā hy ākṛṣyamāṇāyā mantharāyās tatas tataḥ
children.translated_text: As that <s>Mantharā</s> was being dragged this way and that,

children.text: citraṃ bahuvidhaṃ bhāṇḍaṃ pṛthivyāṃ tad vyaśīryata ||
children.translated_text: many varied and splendid objects were shattered on the ground.
The splendid royal residence, strewn with those objects,

children.text: aśobhata tadā bhūyaḥ śāradaṃ gaganaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: then became still more beautiful, like the autumn sky.

children.text: sa balī balavat krodhād gṛhītvā puruṣarṣabhaḥ
children.translated_text: Powerful and foremost among men, he, with overpowering anger, seized her,
and after fiercely rebuking <s>Kaikeyī</s>, spoke harsh words.

children.text: tair vākyaiḥ paruṣair duḥkhaiḥ kaikeyī bhṛśaduḥkhitā
children.translated_text: By those harsh and painful words <s>Kaikeyī</s> was greatly afflicted,
and, terrified by fear of <s>Śatrughna</s>, she came to her son for refuge.

children.text: tāṃ prekṣya bharataḥ kruddhaṃ śatrughnam idam abravīt
children.translated_text: Seeing her, <s>Bharata</s> said this to the angry <s>Śatrughna</s>:
Women are not to be killed by any beings; let her be pardoned.

children.text: hanyām aham imāṃ pāpāṃ kaikeyīṃ duṣṭacāriṇīm
children.translated_text: I would kill this sinful <s>Kaikeyī</s>, whose conduct is wicked,

children.text: yadi māṃ dhārmiko rāmo nāsūyen mātṛghātakam ||
children.translated_text: if righteous <s>Rāma</s> would not censure me as a mother-killer.

children.text: imām api hatāṃ kubjāṃ yadi jānāti rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: If righteous <s>Rāghava</s> learns that this hunchback too has been killed,

children.text: tvāṃ ca māṃ caiva dharmātmā nābhibhāṣiṣyate dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: he certainly will not speak either to you or to me.
Hearing <s>Bharata</s>'s words, <s>Śatrughna</s>, the younger brother of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: nyavartata tato roṣāt tāṃ mumoca ca mantharām ||
children.translated_text: turned back then from his anger and released <s>Mantharā</s>.

children.text: sā pādamūle kaikeyyā mantharā nipapāta ha
children.translated_text: She, <s>Mantharā</s>, fell at the feet of <s>Kaikeyī</s>.
Breathing heavily and afflicted with great pain, she wailed piteously.
Seeing the hunchback, her consciousness bewildered by <s>Śatrughna</s>'s attack, <s>Bharata</s>'s mother

children.text: śanaiḥ samāśvāsayad ārtarūpāṃ krauñcīṃ vilagnām iva vīkṣamāṇām ||
children.translated_text: slowly comforted her, distressed as she was, looking like a trapped female krauñca bird.
Then at daybreak, on the fourteenth day,
the royal functionaries assembled and spoke these words to <s>Bharata</s>:

children.text: gato daśarathaḥ svargaṃ yo no gurutaro guruḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Daśaratha</s> has gone to heaven, he who was our teacher beyond all teachers,

children.text: rāmaṃ pravrājya vai jyeṣṭhaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahābalam ||
children.translated_text: after banishing eldest <s>Rāma</s> and mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: tvam adya bhava no rājā rājaputra mahāyaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Today be our king, O prince of great fame.
Because of circumstance, no fault attaches to taking this kingdom, which has no ruler.
Taking all this equipment for consecration, O <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: pratīkṣate tvāṃ svajanaḥ śreṇayaś ca nṛpātmaja ||
children.translated_text: your own people and the guilds await you, O son of the king.
Accept the great kingdom of your fathers and grandfathers, <s>Bharata</s>.
Consecrate yourself and protect us, bull among men.
After circumambulating all the vessels for consecration,

children.text: bharatas taṃ janaṃ sarvaṃ pratyuvāca dhṛtavrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s>, firm in his vow, answered all those people:

children.text: jyeṣṭhasya rājatā nityam ucitā hi kulasya naḥ
children.translated_text: Kingship always properly belongs to the eldest in our family.

children.text: naivaṃ bhavanto māṃ vaktum arhanti kuśalā janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: You wise people ought not speak to me in this way.

children.text: rāmaḥ pūrvo hi no bhrātā bhaviṣyati mahīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, our elder brother, will be lord of the earth.

children.text: ahaṃ tv araṇye vatsyāmi varṣāṇi nava pañca ca ||
children.translated_text: But I shall dwell in the forest for fourteen years.
Let a great army, powerful in its four divisions, be made ready.

children.text: ānayiṣyāmy ahaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ bhrātaraṃ rāghavaṃ vanāt ||
children.translated_text: I shall bring my eldest brother, <s>Rāghava</s>, back from the forest.
And taking before me all this prepared equipment for consecration,
I shall go toward the forest for the sake of <s>Rāma</s>.
There itself, after consecrating that tiger among men and placing him foremost,

children.text: āneṣyāmi tu vai rāmaṃ havyavāham ivādhvarāt ||
children.translated_text: I shall bring <s>Rāma</s> back, like the oblation-bearing fire from the sacrifice.

children.text: na sakāmāṃ kariṣyāmi svām imāṃ mātṛgandhinīm
children.translated_text: I shall not fulfill the desire of this woman who is a mother only in name.

children.text: vane vatsyāmy ahaṃ durge rāmo rājā bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: I shall dwell in the difficult forest; <s>Rāma</s> will be king.

children.text: kriyatāṃ śilpibhiḥ panthāḥ samāni viṣamāṇi ca
children.translated_text: Let a road be made by the craftsmen, through level places and uneven ones alike.
Let guards go along the route, inspecting its difficult stretches.
As the prince spoke thus for the sake of <s>Rāma</s>,
all the people answered him with splendid, unsurpassed words:

children.text: evaṃ te bhāṣamāṇasya padmā śrīr upatiṣṭhatām
children.translated_text: May lotus-like Fortune attend you as you speak in this way,

children.text: yas tvaṃ jyeṣṭhe nṛpasute pṛthivīṃ dātum icchasi ||
children.translated_text: you who wish to give the earth to the eldest prince.

children.text: anuttamaṃ tad vacanaṃ nṛpātmaja prabhāṣitaṃ saṃśravaṇe niśamya ca
children.translated_text: Hearing that unsurpassed speech proclaimed by the prince in the assembly,

children.text: praharṣajās taṃ prati bāṣpabindavo nipetur āryānananetrasambhavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: teardrops born of joy fell toward him from the eyes in the faces of the noble ones.

children.text: ūcus te vacanam idaṃ niśamya hṛṣṭāḥ sāmātyāḥ sapariṣado viyātaśokāḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard this speech, the delighted ministers, together with the council and freed from grief, said:

children.text: panthānaṃ naravarabhaktimāñ janaś ca vyādiṣṭas tava vacanāc ca śilpivargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By your word, the craftsmen's guild and the people devoted to the best of men have been ordered to make the road.
Then men who knew the lay of the land, skilled in measuring by cord,
devoted to their own work, brave diggers and workers with machines,
laborers, architects, men expert in machines,
and carpenters, road-makers, and tree-cutters as well,
well-diggers, plasterers, and workers in bamboo,

children.text: samarthā ye ca draṣṭāraḥ puratas te pratasthire ||
children.translated_text: and those capable supervisors, set out before them.

children.text: sa tu harṣāt tam uddeśaṃ janaugho vipulaḥ prayān
children.translated_text: That vast stream of people, going joyfully toward that place,
shone with great speed like the ocean at the full moon.
Those men skilled in roadwork, each taking up his assigned task,
set out in front, equipped with various tools.

children.text: latāvallīś ca gulmāṃś ca sthāṇūn aśmana eva ca
children.translated_text: Creepers, winding vines, thickets, stumps, and stones,

children.text: janās te cakrire mārgaṃ chindanto vividhān drumān ||
children.translated_text: those people cleared as they made the road, cutting down various trees.

children.text: avṛkṣeṣu ca deśeṣu kecid vṛkṣān aropayan
children.translated_text: In treeless places some planted trees.

children.text: kecit kuṭhāraiṣ ṭaṅkaiś ca dātraiś chindan kvacit kvacit ||
children.translated_text: Some cut here and there with axes, adzes, and sickles.
Other very strong men broke apart clumps of vīraṇa grass.

children.text: vidhamanti sma durgāṇi sthalāni ca tatas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here and there they broke up difficult and raised places.
Others filled holes and deep pits with earth.

children.text: nimnabhāgāṃs tathā kecit samāṃś cakruḥ samantataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Some made the low-lying places level all around.

children.text: babandhur bandhanīyāṃś ca kṣodyān saṃcukṣudus tadā
children.translated_text: They bound what had to be bound and crushed what had to be crushed then.

children.text: bibhidur bhedanīyāṃś ca tāṃs tān deśān narās tadā ||
children.translated_text: Those men split what had to be split in those various places.
In a very short time,
they made many water-filled channels, of many forms, many of them like seas,
and many kinds of wells encircled with platforms.
With a surface plastered smooth with lime, with trees in full flower,
resounding with flocks of exhilarated birds and adorned with banners,
sprinkled with sandal-water and ornamented with many kinds of flowers,
the army's road shone greatly, like a path to heaven.
Then, having given orders, those appointed men, engaged according to the command,
in pleasant regions abounding in sweet fruits,

children.text: yo niveśas tv abhipreto bharatasya mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: further beautified whatever encampment was intended
for great-souled <s>Bharata</s>, making it like an ornament adorned with ornaments.
At auspicious lunar mansions and at auspicious moments, those who knew such matters
established the encampment of great-souled <s>Bharata</s>.
There were also many heaps of earth, surrounded by moats,
like the stakes of <s>Indra</s>, splendid with excellent gateways,
furnished with rows of palaces and enclosed by mansions and ramparts.
All were adorned with banners, and their great roads were well constructed.
With upper mansions at the tops of balconies seeming to spread through the sky,
those lofty dwellings became like the city of <s>Śakra</s>.
And having reached the <s>Jāhnavī</s>, with her groves of various trees,
with cool, pure drinking water, and crowded with great fish,

children.text: sacandratārāgaṇamaṇḍitaṃ yathā nabhaḥ kṣapāyām amalaṃ virājate
children.translated_text: just as the stainless sky, adorned with the moon and hosts of stars, shines at night,

children.text: narendramārgaḥ sa tathā vyarājata krameṇa ramyaḥ śubhaśilpinirmitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so that royal road, lovely in its order and made by skilled craftsmen, shone.
Then, on the auspicious night, the charioteers and bards,
skilled in special forms of speech, praised <s>Bharata</s> with hymns joined to blessings.
The watch-drum, struck with golden-tipped beaters, gave forth its sound,

children.text: dadhmuḥ śaṅkhāṃś ca śataśo vādyāṃś coccāvacasvarān ||
children.translated_text: and they blew hundreds of conches and instruments of high and varied tones.

children.text: sa tūryaghoṣaḥ sumahān divam āpūrayann iva
children.translated_text: That very great sound of instruments seemed to fill the sky,
and pierced <s>Bharata</s>, already scorched by grief, with still more griefs.

children.text: tataḥ prabuddho bharatas taṃ ghoṣaṃ saṃnivartya ca
children.translated_text: Then <s>Bharata</s> woke up, stopped that noise,

children.text: nāhaṃ rājeti cāpy uktvā śatrughnam idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: and, saying, 'I am not the king,' spoke these words to <s>Śatrughna</s>:
See, <s>Śatrughna</s>, the great wrong <s>Kaikeyī</s> has done to the world.

children.text: visṛjya mayi duḥkhāni rājā daśaratho gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having cast sorrows upon me, King <s>Daśaratha</s> has departed.
The royal fortune of that great-souled king, a king of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),
whose foundation was <s>dharma</s>, is drifting about like a boat without a helmsman on the water.

children.text: ity evaṃ bharataṃ prekṣya vilapantaṃ vicetanam
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Bharata</s> thus lamenting, senseless,

children.text: kṛpaṇaṃ ruruduḥ sarvāḥ sasvaraṃ yoṣitas tadā ||
children.translated_text: all the women then wept piteously, crying aloud.
While he was lamenting in that way, the glorious <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, knower of royal duty,
entered the assembly hall of the lord of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s>.
It was charming, made of refined gold, and filled with jewels and gems;
the righteous man entered it with his attendants as though it were <s>Sudharmā</s> itself.
He sat upon a golden seat covered with a very costly spread,
and, knowing all the Vedas, he instructed the messengers:
Bring the brahmins, kṣatriyas, warriors, ministers, and beloved leaders

children.text: kṣipram ānayatāvyagrāḥ kṛtyam ātyayikaṃ hi naḥ ||
children.translated_text: quickly and without agitation, for our business is urgent.
Then a great tumultuous sound arose

children.text: rathair aśvair gajaiś cāpi janānām upagacchatām ||
children.translated_text: from the people approaching with chariots, horses, and elephants.
Then the subjects welcomed <s>Bharata</s> as he came,
just as the immortals welcomed <s>Śatakratu</s>, and just as they had welcomed <s>Daśaratha</s>.
Like a lake with still waters, filled with great fish and serpents, with jewels, shells, and gravel,

children.text: daśarathasutaśobhitā sabhā sadaśaratheva babhau yathā purā ||
children.translated_text: the assembly, graced by <s>Daśaratha</s>'s son, shone as if <s>Daśaratha</s> were there as before.
Wise <s>Bharata</s> saw that assembly filled with noble men and held in order,
like a night filled by the full moon.
As the noble men entered their seats according to rank,
it appeared like an autumn night with the full moon after the passing of clouds.

children.text: rājñas tu prakṛtīḥ sarvāḥ samagrāḥ prekṣya dharmavit
children.translated_text: Seeing all the king's estates assembled together, the priest, knower of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: idaṃ purohito vākyaṃ bharataṃ mṛdu cābravīt ||
children.translated_text: spoke these gentle words to <s>Bharata</s>:

children.text: tāta rājā daśarathaḥ svargato dharmam ācaran
children.translated_text: Dear child, King <s>Daśaratha</s> has gone to heaven, practicing <s>dharma</s>,
after giving you this flourishing earth, rich in wealth and grain.

children.text: rāmas tathā satyadhṛtiḥ satāṃ dharmam anusmaran
children.translated_text: And <s>Rāma</s>, firm in truth, remembering the <s>dharma</s> of the good,

children.text: nājahāt pitur ādeśaṃ śaśī jyotsnām ivoditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: did not abandon his father's command, as the risen moon does not abandon its moonlight.

children.text: pitrā bhrātrā ca te dattaṃ rājyaṃ nihatakaṇṭakam
children.translated_text: The kingdom has been given to you by your father and by your brother, free of thorns;
enjoy it, with your ministers rejoicing, and have yourself consecrated at once.

children.text: udīcyāś ca pratīcyāś ca dākṣiṇātyāś ca kevalāḥ
children.translated_text: Let the northern, western, and southern regions, all of them,
and the frontier and ocean-bordering lands bring jewels to you.
Hearing that speech, <s>Bharata</s>, flooded by grief,
went in his mind to <s>Rāma</s>, knowing <s>dharma</s> and longing for <s>dharma</s>.
The young man, with a voice choked by tears and sounding like a kalahaṃsa bird,
lamented in the middle of the assembly and reproached the priest.
What man like me would seize the kingdom from one who has practiced celibate discipline, completed his learning, and is wise,

children.text: dharme prayatamānasya ko rājyaṃ madvidho haret ||
children.translated_text: from one who is devoted to striving in <s>dharma</s>?
How could one born from <s>Daśaratha</s> become a usurper of the kingdom?

children.text: rājyaṃ cāhaṃ ca rāmasya dharmaṃ vaktum ihārhasi ||
children.translated_text: Both the kingdom and I belong to <s>Rāma</s>; you ought to speak <s>dharma</s> here.
The eldest, the best, righteous, and comparable to <s>Dilīpa</s> and <s>Nahuṣa</s>,

children.text: labdhum arhati kākutstho rājyaṃ daśaratho yathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kākutstha</s> deserves to obtain the kingdom, just as <s>Daśaratha</s> did.

children.text: anāryajuṣṭam asvargyaṃ kuryāṃ pāpam ahaṃ yadi
children.translated_text: If I were to commit a sin practiced by ignoble men and leading not to heaven,
I would become in the world the disgrace of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s>.

children.text: yaddhi mātrā kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ nāhaṃ tad abhirocaye
children.translated_text: I do not approve of the sin that was done by my mother.
Standing here, with joined palms, I bow to him who is in the difficult forest.

children.text: rāmam evānugacchāmi sa rājā dvipadāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: I will follow <s>Rāma</s> alone; he is the king, the best of two-footed beings.

children.text: trayāṇām api lokānāṃ rāghavo rājyam arhati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> deserves sovereignty even over the three worlds.

children.text: tad vākyaṃ dharmasaṃyuktaṃ śrutvā sarve sabhāsadaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech joined with <s>dharma</s>, all the members of the assembly,
their minds fixed on <s>Rāma</s>, shed tears of joy.

children.text: yadi tv āryaṃ na śakṣyāmi vinivartayituṃ vanāt
children.translated_text: But if I am not able to turn the noble one back from the forest,

children.text: vane tatraiva vatsyāmi yathāryo lakṣmaṇas tathā ||
children.translated_text: I will dwell there in the forest, just as noble <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> does.
I will employ every means to turn him back, even by force,
in the presence of the honorable noble men and the good men who follow virtue.

children.text: evam uktvā tu dharmātmā bharato bhrātṛvatsalaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, righteous <s>Bharata</s>, devoted to his brother,
said this to nearby <s>Sumantra</s>, skilled in counsel:

children.text: tūrṇam utthāya gaccha tvaṃ sumantra mama śāsanāt
children.translated_text: Rise quickly and go, <s>Sumantra</s>, at my command.

children.text: yātrām ājñāpaya kṣipraṃ balaṃ caiva samānaya ||
children.translated_text: Order the journey quickly, and assemble the army as well.

children.text: evam uktaḥ sumantras tu bharatena mahātmanā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by great-souled <s>Bharata</s>, <s>Sumantra</s>

children.text: prahṛṣṭaḥ so 'diśat sarvaṃ yathā saṃdiṣṭam iṣṭavat ||
children.translated_text: was delighted and gave all the orders exactly as instructed, as if it were his own cherished wish.

children.text: tāḥ prahṛṣṭāḥ prakṛtayo balādhyakṣā balasya ca
children.translated_text: Then the delighted citizens and the commanders of the army
heard that the march had been ordered for the return of <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: tato yodhāṅganāḥ sarvā bhartṝn sarvān gṛhe gṛhe
children.translated_text: Then all the wives of the warriors, in every house,
learning that the journey was to begin, joyfully hurried all their husbands on.

children.text: te hayair gorathaiḥ śīghraiḥ syandanaiś ca manojavaiḥ
children.translated_text: With horses, ox-carts, swift teams, and chariots as fast as thought,

children.text: saha yodhair balādhyakṣā balaṃ sarvam acodayan ||
children.translated_text: the army commanders, together with the warriors, set the whole army in motion.

children.text: sajjaṃ tu tad balaṃ dṛṣṭvā bharato gurusaṃnidhau
children.translated_text: But when <s>Bharata</s> saw that army ready, in the presence of his elders,
he said to <s>Sumantra</s> at his side, 'Hasten my chariot.'
Joyfully accepting that command of <s>Bharata</s>,
<s>Sumantra</s> took the chariot, yoked with excellent horses, and set out.

children.text: sa rāghavaḥ satyadhṛtiḥ pratāpavān bruvan suyuktaṃ dṛḍhasatyavikramaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Bharata</s>, a <s>Rāghava</s> of truthful resolve, mighty and speaking fitting words, firm in the valor of truth,

children.text: guruṃ mahāraṇyagataṃ yaśasvinaṃ prasādayiṣyan bharato 'bravīt tadā ||
children.translated_text: wishing to propitiate his renowned elder who had gone to the great forest, spoke at that time.

children.text: tūrṇaṃ samutthāya sumantra gaccha balasya yogāya balapradhānān
children.translated_text: 'Rise quickly, <s>Sumantra</s>, and go to the chief commanders for the mustering of the army.

children.text: ānetum icchāmi hi taṃ vanasthaṃ prasādya rāmaṃ jagato hitāya ||
children.translated_text: For the welfare of the world, I wish to bring back <s>Rāma</s>, who dwells in the forest, after winning his favor.'

children.text: sa sūtaputro bharatena samyag ājñāpitaḥ saṃparipūrṇakāmaḥ
children.translated_text: That son of a charioteer, properly instructed by <s>Bharata</s> and having his desire fully fulfilled,

children.text: śaśāsa sarvān prakṛtipradhānān balasya mukhyāṃś ca suhṛjjanaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: commanded all the leading citizens, the principal men of the army, and the circle of friends.

children.text: tataḥ samutthāya kule kule te rājanyavaiśyā vṛṣalāś ca viprāḥ
children.translated_text: Then, rising up in each family, the kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, śūdras, and brahmins

children.text: ayūyujann uṣṭrarathān kharāṃś ca nāgān hayāṃś caiva kulaprasūtān ||
children.translated_text: yoked camel-carts, donkeys, elephants, horses, and well-bred steeds.
Then <s>Bharata</s>, rising early in the morning and mounting the finest chariot,
set out quickly, longing to see <s>Rāma</s>.
Ahead of him went all the ministers and family priests,
mounted on chariots yoked with horses and resembling the chariot of the sun.
Nine thousand elephants, equipped according to rule,
followed <s>Bharata</s> as he went, the delight of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> line.
Sixty thousand chariots, with bowmen bearing various weapons,
followed <s>Bharata</s> as he went, the renowned prince.
A hundred thousand horses, with riders mounted upon them,
followed <s>Bharata</s> as he went, the renowned prince.

children.text: kaikeyī ca sumitrā ca kausalyā ca yaśasvinī
children.translated_text: <s>Kaikeyī</s>, <s>Sumitrā</s>, and renowned <s>Kausalyā</s>,
delighted at the bringing back of <s>Rāma</s>, went in a shining vehicle.
Groups of noble people also set out to see <s>Rāma</s> together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: tasyaiva ca kathāś citrāḥ kurvāṇā hṛṣṭamānasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: their minds joyful as they told wondrous stories about him alone.
'When shall we see <s>Rāma</s>, dark as a raincloud, mighty-armed, steady in nature, firm in his vow,
the remover of the world's sorrow?'

children.text: dṛṣṭa eva hi naḥ śokam apaneṣyati rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Merely by being seen, <s>Rāghava</s> will take away our grief,

children.text: tamaḥ sarvasya lokasya samudyann iva bhāskaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: like the rising sun taking away the darkness of the whole world.'

children.text: ity evaṃ kathayantas te samprahṛṣṭāḥ kathāḥ śubhāḥ
children.translated_text: Speaking in this way, telling auspicious tales, delighted and overjoyed,
the citizens then went, embracing one another.

children.text: ye ca tatrāpare sarve saṃmatā ye ca naigamāḥ
children.translated_text: And all the others there who were respected, and the guildsmen too,

children.text: rāmaṃ prati yayur hṛṣṭāḥ sarvāḥ prakṛtayas tadā ||
children.translated_text: all the people then went joyfully toward <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: maṇikārāś ca ye kecit kumbhakārāś ca śobhanāḥ
children.translated_text: All the jewelers and the fine potters,
the workers in thread, and those who lived by weapons,
the peacock-feather workers, sawyers, polishers, and piercers,
the ivory workers, plasterers, and those who lived by perfumes,
the renowned goldsmiths, and the washers of blankets,
bath attendants, clothiers, physicians, incense-makers, and liquor sellers,
washermen, tailors, and the elders of villages and cowherd settlements,

children.text: śailūṣāś ca saha strībhir yānti kaivartakās tathā ||
children.translated_text: actors with their women, and the fishermen and boatmen as well, all went.
Self-controlled brahmins, knowers of the <s>Veda</s>, esteemed for their conduct,
followed <s>Bharata</s> as he went, by the thousands, in ox-carts.
Well dressed, clothed in clean garments, and anointed with reddish, polished unguents,

children.text: sarve te vividhair yānaiḥ śanair bharatam anvayuḥ ||
children.translated_text: all of them followed <s>Bharata</s> slowly in various vehicles.
That army, joyful and glad, followed the son of <s>Kaikeyī</s>,
and that army of <s>Bharata</s>'s followers took up its positions.

children.text: nirīkṣyānugatāṃ senāṃ tāṃ ca gaṅgāṃ śivodakām
children.translated_text: Seeing the army following him, and seeing the <s>Gaṅgā</s> with her auspicious waters,
<s>Bharata</s>, skilled in speech, addressed all his ministers.
'Have my army encamped in every respect according to what is suitable.
When rested, we shall cross this great river tomorrow.
