children.text: dātuṃ ca tāvad icchāmi svargatasya mahīpateḥ
children.translated_text: And meanwhile I wish to descend into the river and offer water
for the sake of the rites after death for the departed king.'
As he spoke in this way, the ministers said, 'So be it,' and, attentive,

children.text: nyaveśayaṃs tāṃś chandena svena svena pṛthakpṛthak ||
children.translated_text: encamped them separately, each according to his own preference.

children.text: niveśya gaṅgām anu tāṃ mahānadīṃ camūṃ vidhānaiḥ paribarhaśobhinīm
children.translated_text: Having encamped the army along the great river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, splendid with its equipment and ordered arrangements,

children.text: uvāsa rāmasya tadā mahātmano vicintayāno bharato nivartanam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s> stayed there then, pondering how to bring back great-souled <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: tato niviṣṭāṃ dhvajinīṃ gaṅgām anvāśritāṃ nadīm
children.translated_text: Then the king of the <s>Niṣādas</s>, seeing the bannered army encamped by the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
quickly addressed his kinsmen as soon as he saw it.
'This great army appears from here like the ocean.
Even when considering it with my mind, I cannot grasp its end.'

children.text: sa eṣa hi mahākāyaḥ kovidāradhvajo rathe
children.translated_text: For this great-bodied man, whose chariot bears the banner of the kovidāra tree,

children.text: bandhayiṣyati vā dāśān atha vāsmān vadhiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: will either bind the <s>Dāśas</s> or else kill us.

children.text: atha dāśarathiṃ rāmaṃ pitrā rājyād vivāsitam
children.translated_text: Or <s>Bharata</s>, son of <s>Kaikeyī</s>, is approaching <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>,
who was banished from the kingdom by his father, in order to kill him.

children.text: bhartā caiva sakhā caiva rāmo dāśarathir mama
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, is both my lord and my friend.
Stand here equipped on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, desiring his welfare.

children.text: tiṣṭhantu sarvadāśāś ca gaṅgām anvāśritā nadīm
children.translated_text: Let all the <s>Dāśas</s> remain stationed along the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> at all times,
strong and serving as river guards, living on meat, roots, and fruits.

children.text: nāvāṃ śatānāṃ pañcānāṃ kaivartānāṃ śataṃ śatam
children.translated_text: For the five hundred boats, let a hundred <s>Kaivarta</s> boatmen for each

children.text: saṃnaddhānāṃ tathā yūnāṃ tiṣṭhantv ity abhyacodayat ||
children.translated_text: stand ready, armed and young: so he commanded them.

children.text: yadā tuṣṭas tu bharato rāmasyeha bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: But when <s>Bharata</s> is satisfied here toward <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: seyaṃ svastimayī senā gaṅgām adya tariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: this army, full of welfare, shall cross the <s>Gaṅgā</s> today.
Having spoken thus, and taking offerings, fish, meat, and honey,
<s>Guha</s>, lord of the <s>Niṣādas</s>, approached <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: tam āyāntaṃ tu samprekṣya sūtaputraḥ pratāpavān
children.translated_text: Seeing him coming, the powerful son of the charioteer
then informed <s>Bharata</s>, respectfully and with knowledge of proper conduct:
This chief is surrounded by a thousand kinsmen.

children.text: kuśalo daṇḍakāraṇye vṛddho bhrātuś ca te sakhā ||
children.translated_text: He is skilled in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest, elderly, and a friend of your brother.

children.text: tasmāt paśyatu kākutstha tvāṃ niṣādādhipo guhaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, let <s>Guha</s>, lord of the <s>Niṣādas</s>, see you.
Without doubt he knows where those two, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, are.

children.text: etat tu vacanaṃ śrutvā sumantrād bharataḥ śubham
children.translated_text: Hearing this auspicious speech from <s>Sumantra</s>,

children.text: uvāca vacanaṃ śīghraṃ guhaḥ paśyatu mām iti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s> quickly said these words: Let <s>Guha</s> see me.
Having received permission, delighted and surrounded by his kinsmen,

children.text: āgamya bharataṃ prahvo guho vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Guha</s> came to <s>Bharata</s>, bowed low, and spoke these words:

children.text: niṣkuṭaś caiva deśo 'yaṃ vañcitāś cāpi te vayam
children.translated_text: This place is a secluded tract, and we too are at your service.

children.text: nivedayāmas te sarve svake dāśakule vasa ||
children.translated_text: We all make this request to you: stay among your own household of servants.

children.text: asti mūlaṃ phalaṃ caiva niṣādaiḥ samupāhṛtam
children.translated_text: There are roots and fruits brought together by the <s>Niṣādas</s>,

children.text: ārdraṃ ca māṃsaṃ śuṣkaṃ ca vanyaṃ coccāvacaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: and fresh meat and dried meat, and much wild fare of many kinds.
I hope that your well-fed army will spend this night here.

children.text: arcito vividhaiḥ kāmaiḥ śvaḥ sasainyo gamiṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: Honored with various enjoyments, you will set out tomorrow with your army.

children.text: evam uktas tu bharato niṣādādhipatiṃ guham
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, wise <s>Bharata</s>
replied to <s>Guha</s>, lord of the <s>Niṣādas</s>, with a speech joined to reason and purpose:

children.text: ūrjitaḥ khalu te kāmaḥ kṛto mama guroḥ sakhe
children.translated_text: Your intention is indeed generous, O friend of my revered elder,

children.text: yo me tvam īdṛśīṃ senām eko 'bhyarcitum icchasi ||
children.translated_text: since you alone wish to honor such an army of mine.

children.text: ity uktvā tu mahātejā guhaṃ vacanam uttamam
children.translated_text: Having said this, illustrious <s>Bharata</s> of great splendor
again spoke an excellent word to <s>Guha</s>, lord of the <s>Niṣādas</s>:
By which way shall I go to the hermitage of <s>Bharadvāja</s>, O <s>Guha</s>?
This country along the <s>Gaṅgā</s> is very dense and hard to cross.
Hearing that speech of the wise prince,
<s>Guha</s>, who ranged through difficult terrain, spoke with joined palms:
Bow-bearing <s>Dāśas</s>, well composed, will accompany you,
and I too will accompany you, O prince of great fame.
I trust you are not going with evil intent toward <s>Rāma</s>, whose deeds are untroubled.

children.text: iyaṃ te mahatī senā śaṅkāṃ janayatīva me ||
children.translated_text: This great army of yours seems to raise suspicion in me.

children.text: tam evam abhibhāṣantam ākāśa iva nirmalaḥ
children.translated_text: To him who was speaking thus, <s>Bharata</s>, clear as the sky,

children.text: bharataḥ ślakṣṇayā vācā guhaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: spoke these words to <s>Guha</s> in a gentle voice:

children.text: mā bhūt sa kālo yat kaṣṭaṃ na māṃ śaṅkitum arhasi
children.translated_text: May there never be such a terrible time. You ought not suspect me.

children.text: rāghavaḥ sa hi me bhrātā jyeṣṭhaḥ pitṛsamo mama ||
children.translated_text: For that <s>Rāghava</s> is my elder brother, equal to my father.
I am going to bring back that <s>Kākutstha</s>, who dwells in the forest.

children.text: buddhir anyā na te kāryā guha satyaṃ bravīmi te ||
children.translated_text: You should not form any other thought, O <s>Guha</s>; I tell you the truth.
Hearing <s>Bharata</s>'s words, he, with a delighted face,

children.text: punar evābravīd vākyaṃ bharataṃ prati harṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: again spoke to <s>Bharata</s>, rejoicing:

children.text: dhanyas tvaṃ na tvayā tulyaṃ paśyāmi jagatītale
children.translated_text: Blessed are you. I see no one equal to you on the surface of the earth,

children.text: ayatnād āgataṃ rājyaṃ yas tvaṃ tyaktum ihecchasi ||
children.translated_text: since you wish to abandon a kingdom that came to you without effort.

children.text: śāśvatī khalu te kīrtir lokān anucariṣyati
children.translated_text: Surely your lasting fame will move through the worlds,

children.text: yas tvaṃ kṛcchragataṃ rāmaṃ pratyānayitum icchasi ||
children.translated_text: since you wish to bring back <s>Rāma</s>, who has fallen into hardship.
While <s>Guha</s> was conversing in this way with <s>Bharata</s> then,
the sun lost its radiance, and night came on.

children.text: saṃniveśya sa tāṃ senāṃ guhena paritoṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: Having encamped that army, and pleased by <s>Guha</s>,

children.text: śatrughnena saha śrīmāñ śayanaṃ punar āgamat ||
children.translated_text: the illustrious man returned to his bed together with <s>Śatrughna</s>.
A sorrow made wholly of thoughts of <s>Rāma</s> arose in great-souled <s>Bharata</s>,
though he did not deserve such grief, for he looked toward <s>dharma</s>.
Burning with an inner fire, it tormented the <s>Rāghava</s>,
like a hidden fire tormenting a tree scorched by a forest blaze.
Sweat, born from the fire of grief, streamed from all his limbs,
as <s>Himavān</s>, heated by the rays of the sun, streams with snow.
With caves of brooding, with mineral streams of sighs,
with masses of trees of despondency, with peaks of sorrow and exhaustion,
with endless creatures of bewilderment, and with bamboos that were herbs of anguish,
the son of <s>Kaikeyī</s> was overwhelmed by a great mountain of suffering.

children.text: guhena sārdhaṃ bharataḥ samāgato mahānubhāvaḥ sajanaḥ samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: High-minded <s>Bharata</s>, composed and accompanied by his people, had met with <s>Guha</s>.

children.text: sudurmanās taṃ bharataṃ tadā punar guhaḥ samāśvāsayad agrajaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Guha</s> again consoled that deeply dejected <s>Bharata</s> concerning his elder brother.
Then <s>Guha</s>, who ranged through difficult terrain, told
immeasurable <s>Bharata</s> the true disposition of great-souled <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:
how he stayed awake, endowed with virtues, bearing an excellent bow and arrows.
For the sake of protecting my brother, I spoke very earnestly to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:

children.text: iyaṃ tāta sukhā śayyā tvadartham upakalpitā
children.translated_text: Dear child, this comfortable bed has been prepared for your sake.
Take heart; sleep happily on it, delight of the <s>Raghus</s>.

children.text: ucito 'yaṃ janaḥ sarvo duḥkhānāṃ tvaṃ sukhocitaḥ
children.translated_text: All these people are accustomed to hardships, while you are accustomed to comfort.
Righteous one, for his protection we shall keep watch.

children.text: na hi rāmāt priyataro mamāsti bhuvi kaścana
children.translated_text: For there is no one on earth dearer to me than <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: motsuko bhūr bravīmy etad apy asatyaṃ tavāgrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Do not be anxious; I say this before you, and it is not false.

children.text: asya prasādād āśaṃse loke 'smin sumahad yaśaḥ
children.translated_text: By his favor I hope for very great fame in this world,

children.text: dharmāvāptiṃ ca vipulām arthāvāptiṃ ca kevalām ||
children.translated_text: and for abundant attainment of <s>dharma</s> and complete attainment of prosperity.

children.text: so 'haṃ priyasakhaṃ rāmaṃ śayānaṃ saha sītayā
children.translated_text: So I, with bow in hand, will guard my dear friend <s>Rāma</s>, sleeping together with <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: rakṣiṣyāmi dhanuṣpāṇiḥ sarvaiḥ svair jñātibhiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: along with all my own kinsmen.

children.text: na hi me 'viditaṃ kiṃcid vane 'smiṃś carataḥ sadā
children.translated_text: There is nothing unknown to me in this forest, since I am always moving about here.

children.text: caturaṅgaṃ hy api balaṃ prasahema vayaṃ yudhi ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, we could withstand even a fourfold army in battle.
When we had spoken thus, the great-souled <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
looking only to <s>dharma</s>, gently restrained us all.

children.text: kathaṃ dāśarathau bhūmau śayāne saha sītayā
children.translated_text: How could sleep be obtained by me, or life, or pleasures,

children.text: śakyā nidrā mayā labdhuṃ jīvitaṃ vā sukhāni vā ||
children.translated_text: while the two sons of <s>Daśaratha</s> lie on the ground together with <s>Sītā</s>?

children.text: yo na devāsuraiḥ sarvaiḥ śakyaḥ prasahituṃ yudhi
children.translated_text: He whom all the gods and asuras together cannot overcome in battle,

children.text: taṃ paśya guha saṃviṣṭaṃ tṛṇeṣu saha sītayā ||
children.translated_text: behold him, <s>Guha</s>, lying on grass together with <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: mahatā tapasā labdho vividhaiś ca pariśramaiḥ
children.translated_text: Won by great austerity and by many kinds of effort,
this one son of <s>Daśaratha</s> bears marks like his own.

children.text: asmin pravrājite rājā na ciraṃ vartayiṣyati
children.translated_text: When he has been banished, the king will not live long.

children.text: vidhavā medinī nūnaṃ kṣipram eva bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Surely the earth will very soon become widowed.
The women, after crying out with a very great wail, will be stilled by exhaustion.
Surely today the royal residence is silent, its noise brought to an end.

children.text: kausalyā caiva rājā ca tathaiva jananī mama
children.translated_text: <s>Kausalyā</s>, the king, and likewise my mother,

children.text: nāśaṃse yadi te sarve jīveyuḥ śarvarīm imām ||
children.translated_text: I do not expect that all of them will live through this night.

children.text: jīved api hi me mātā śatrughnasyānvavekṣayā
children.translated_text: My mother may perhaps live, out of regard for <s>Śatrughna</s>,

children.text: duḥkhitā yā tu kausalyā vīrasūr vinaśiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: but <s>Kausalyā</s>, distressed and mother of a hero, will perish.
With his cherished desire repeatedly passing beyond reach and remaining unattained,

children.text: rājye rāmam anikṣipya pitā me vinaśiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: my father will die without installing <s>Rāma</s> in the kingdom.

children.text: siddhārthāḥ pitaraṃ vṛttaṃ tasmin kāle hy upasthite
children.translated_text: When my father has passed away and that time has come, those whose purposes are fulfilled
will perform all the funeral rites for the king.
With charming squares and meeting places, with great roads well laid out,
endowed with mansions and palaces, adorned with every jewel,
crowded with elephants, horses, and chariots, resounding with the sound of instruments,
filled with every blessing, thronged with joyful and well-nourished people,
full of parks and gardens, rich in gatherings and festivals,
they will wander happily through my father's capital.
May we, together with him whose promise is true, safe and sound,

children.text: nivṛtte samaye hy asmin sukhitāḥ praviśemahi ||
children.translated_text: enter happily when this appointed time has ended.
As that great-souled prince stood there lamenting in this way,
that night passed by.

children.text: prabhāte vimale sūrye kārayitvā jaṭā ubhau
children.translated_text: In the clear morning, when the sun had risen, after having the two make matted locks,
I ferried them safely across here on this bank of the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>.
Those two mighty men, with matted hair, wearing bark and cloth, like leaders of elephant herds,

children.text: vareṣucāpāsidharau paraṃtapau vyavekṣamāṇau saha sītayā gatau ||
children.translated_text: bearing excellent arrows, bows, and swords, tormentors of foes, went on together with <s>Sītā</s>, looking about them.

children.text: guhasya vacanaṃ śrutvā bharato bhṛśam apriyam
children.translated_text: Having heard <s>Guha</s>'s words, deeply painful as they were, <s>Bharata</s>

children.text: dhyānaṃ jagāma tatraiva yatra tac chrutam apriyam ||
children.translated_text: fell into thought right there, where he had heard that painful news.
Delicate, of great strength, lion-shouldered and mighty-armed,
with eyes broad as lotuses, young and pleasant to behold,
after recovering himself for a moment, yet for a time exceedingly downcast,

children.text: papāta sahasā totrair hṛdi viddha iva dvipaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he suddenly fell like an elephant pierced in the heart by goads.
<s>Śatrughna</s>, standing beside <s>Bharata</s> in that condition,
embraced him and wept loudly, senseless and worn by grief.

children.text: tataḥ sarvāḥ samāpetur mātaro bharatasya tāḥ
children.translated_text: Then all those mothers of <s>Bharata</s> came together,
thin from fasting, wretched, and worn by their husband's calamity.

children.text: tāś ca taṃ patitaṃ bhūmau rudantyaḥ paryavārayan
children.translated_text: Weeping, they surrounded him as he lay fallen on the ground,
while <s>Kausalyā</s>, distressed, came after him and embraced him.

children.text: vatsalā svaṃ yathā vatsam upagūhya tapasvinī
children.translated_text: The suffering woman, affectionate, clasped him as a cow clasps her own calf,
and, weeping and overwhelmed by grief, questioned <s>Bharata</s>:

children.text: putra vyādhir na te kaccic charīraṃ paribādhate
children.translated_text: Son, surely no illness is afflicting your body?
For today the life of this royal family depends on you.

children.text: tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā putra jīvāmi rāme sabhrātṛke gate
children.translated_text: Seeing you, son, I live, now that <s>Rāma</s> has gone with his brother.

children.text: vṛtte daśarathe rājñi nātha ekas tvam adya naḥ ||
children.translated_text: With King <s>Daśaratha</s> dead, you alone are our protector today.

children.text: kaccin na lakṣmaṇe putra śrutaṃ te kiṃcid apriyam
children.translated_text: Surely, son, you have not heard anything painful about <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: putra vā hy ekaputrāyāḥ sahabhārye vanaṃ gate ||
children.translated_text: or about my son, the only son of a mother with one child, gone to the forest together with his wife?

children.text: sa muhūrtaṃ samāśvasya rudann eva mahāyaśāḥ
children.translated_text: After regaining his composure for a moment, the greatly renowned one, still weeping,
consoled <s>Kausalyā</s> and spoke these words to <s>Guha</s>:

children.text: bhrātā me kvāvasad rātriṃ kva sītā kva ca lakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Where did my brother spend the night? Where was <s>Sītā</s>, and where was <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>?

children.text: asvapac chayane kasmin kiṃ bhuktvā guha śaṃsa me ||
children.translated_text: On what bed did he sleep? What did he eat? Tell me, <s>Guha</s>.
Questioned in this way, <s>Guha</s>, lord of the <s>Niṣādas</s>, told <s>Bharata</s>
how he had acted toward <s>Rāma</s>, his dear and cherished guest.

children.text: annam uccāvacaṃ bhakṣāḥ phalāni vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: Food of many kinds, delicacies, and various fruits
had been brought by me in abundance for <s>Rāma</s> to eat.
<s>Rāma</s>, whose valor was true, consented to all that,

children.text: na hi tat pratyagṛhṇāt sa kṣatradharmam anusmaran ||
children.translated_text: for he did not accept it, remembering <s>kṣatradharma</s> (the duty of a warrior).

children.text: na hy asmābhiḥ pratigrāhyaṃ sakhe deyaṃ tu sarvadā
children.translated_text: "Friend, it is not to be accepted by us; rather, we must always give.

children.text: iti tena vayaṃ rājann anunītā mahātmanā ||
children.translated_text: Thus, O king, we were conciliated by that great-souled one.
After drinking the water brought by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the greatly renowned one
<s>Rāghava</s>, together with <s>Sītā</s>, observed that fast for the night.

children.text: tatas tu jalaśeṣeṇa lakṣmaṇo 'py akarot tadā
children.translated_text: Then, with the remaining water, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> also did so at that time.

children.text: vāgyatās te trayaḥ saṃdhyām upāsata samāhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Restraining their speech, those three attended the twilight worship with composed minds.

children.text: saumitris tu tataḥ paścād akarot svāstaraṃ śubham
children.translated_text: Then afterward <s>Saumitri</s> made an auspicious bed
by quickly bringing grasses himself for <s>Rāghava</s>'s sake.

children.text: tasmin samāviśad rāmaḥ svāstare saha sītayā
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> lay down on that bed together with <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: prakṣālya ca tayoḥ pādāv apacakrāma lakṣmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, after washing their feet, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> withdrew.

children.text: etat tad iṅgudīmūlam idam eva ca tat tṛṇam
children.translated_text: This is that root of the iṅgudī tree, and this indeed is that grass

children.text: yasmin rāmaś ca sītā ca rātriṃ tāṃ śayitāv ubhau ||
children.translated_text: on which both <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Sītā</s> slept that night.

children.text: niyamya pṛṣṭhe tu talāṅgulitravāñ śaraiḥ supūrṇāviṣudhī paraṃtapaḥ
children.translated_text: Fastening on his back the hand-guard and two quivers well filled with arrows, the scorcher of foes,

children.text: mahad dhanuḥ sajyam upohya lakṣmaṇo niśām atiṣṭhat parito 'sya kevalam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, taking up his great strung bow, stood through the night all around him, alone.

children.text: tatas tv ahaṃ cottamabāṇacāpadhṛk sthito 'bhavaṃ tatra sa yatra lakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Then I too, bearing an excellent bow and arrows, stood there where <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> was,

children.text: atandribhir jñātibhir āttakārmukair mahendrakalpaṃ paripālayaṃs tadā ||
children.translated_text: with watchful kinsmen holding bows, guarding him then as though he were great <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: tac chrutvā nipuṇaṃ sarvaṃ bharataḥ saha mantribhiḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard all that in detail, <s>Bharata</s>, together with his ministers,
came to the root of the iṅgudī tree and looked upon that bed of <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: abravīj jananīḥ sarvā iha tena mahātmanā
children.translated_text: He said to all his mothers, "Here by that great-souled one

children.text: śarvarī śayitā bhūmāv idam asya vimarditam ||
children.translated_text: the night was spent lying on the ground; this is where it was pressed down by him.
A man of such high fortune, noble birth, great blessedness, and wisdom,

children.text: jāto daśarathenorvyāṃ na rāmaḥ svaptum arhati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, born on earth from <s>Daśaratha</s>, does not deserve to sleep so.
Having slept on beds spread over with antelope skins and piled with fine coverings,
how does the tiger among men lie upon the surface of the earth?
In the upper palace pavilions and on balconies at all times,
on floors of gold and silver, furnished with fine bedding,
bright with heaps of flowers and fragrant with sandalwood and agaru,
shining like white clouds and sounding with flocks of parrots,
with the noise of singing and instruments and the jingling of fine ornaments,
and with the excellent sounds of mṛdaṅgas, he was constantly awakened.
At the proper time he was praised by many bards, sūtas, and māgadhas,
with fitting songs and hymns, that scorcher of foes.

children.text: aśraddheyam idaṃ loke na satyaṃ pratibhāti mā
children.translated_text: This is unbelievable in the world; it does not seem true to me.

children.text: muhyate khalu me bhāvaḥ svapno 'yam iti me matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: My mind is surely bewildered; I think this is a dream.

children.text: na nūnaṃ daivataṃ kiṃcit kālena balavattaram
children.translated_text: Surely there is no deity more powerful than Time,

children.text: yatra dāśarathī rāmo bhūmāv evaṃ śayīta saḥ ||
children.translated_text: since <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, should sleep thus on the ground.
And <s>Sītā</s>, daughter of the king of <s>Videha</s>, lovely to behold,

children.text: dayitā śayitā bhūmau snuṣā daśarathasya ca ||
children.translated_text: beloved and the daughter-in-law of <s>Daśaratha</s>, has lain on the ground.

children.text: iyaṃ śayyā mama bhrātur idaṃ hi parivartitam
children.translated_text: This is my brother's bed; here indeed is where he turned over.

children.text: sthaṇḍile kaṭhine sarvaṃ gātrair vimṛditaṃ tṛṇam ||
children.translated_text: On the hard bare ground, all the grass has been pressed by their limbs.

children.text: manye sābharaṇā suptā sītāsmiñ śayane tadā
children.translated_text: I think <s>Sītā</s>, adorned with ornaments, slept then on this bed,

children.text: tatra tatra hi dṛśyante saktāḥ kanakabindavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for here and there golden particles are seen clinging.
Clearly <s>Sītā</s>'s upper garment was caught here then,

children.text: tathā hy ete prakāśante saktāḥ kauśeyatantavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for these silk threads appear caught in just that way.

children.text: manye bhartuḥ sukhā śayyā yena bālā tapasvinī
children.translated_text: I think the bed was comfortable for her husband, because that young ascetic woman,

children.text: sukumārī satī duḥkhaṃ na vijānāti maithilī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Maithilī</s>, though tender and delicate, did not know pain.
Born in a line of universal emperors, bringing happiness to all people,
dear to all people, having abandoned his beloved and unsurpassed kingdom,
how has dark-blue, red-eyed, lovely-to-behold <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: sukhabhāgī ca duḥkhārhaḥ śayito bhuvi rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a sharer in happiness and undeserving of sorrow, lain upon the earth?

children.text: siddhārthā khalu vaidehī patiṃ yānugatā vanam
children.translated_text: <s>Vaidehī</s> has indeed fulfilled her purpose, since she followed her husband to the forest.

children.text: vayaṃ saṃśayitāḥ sarve hīnās tena mahātmanā ||
children.translated_text: We all are left in uncertainty, deprived of that great-souled one.
The earth, without a helmsman, appears to me as if empty,

children.text: gate daśarathe svarge rāme cāraṇyam āśrite ||
children.translated_text: with <s>Daśaratha</s> gone to heaven and <s>Rāma</s> taking refuge in the wilderness.

children.text: na ca prārthayate kaścin manasāpi vasuṃdharām
children.translated_text: And no one, even in thought, covets the earth
protected by the strength of his arms, even while he dwells in the forest.
Though it lacks enclosure and protection and its horses and elephants are uncontrolled,
though its city gates are open and the capital is unguarded,
though its army is cheerless, diminished, in difficulty, and exposed,
enemies do not set their minds on it, as on food made poisonous.

children.text: adya prabhṛti bhūmau tu śayiṣye 'haṃ tṛṇeṣu vā
children.translated_text: From today onward I shall sleep on the ground or on grass,
always eating fruits and roots, wearing matted hair and bark garments.

children.text: tasyārtham uttaraṃ kālaṃ nivatsyāmi sukhaṃ vane
children.translated_text: For his sake I shall dwell happily in the forest for the remaining time,

children.text: taṃ pratiśravam āmucya nāsya mithyā bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: taking on that pledge, so that his promise will not become false.
<s>Śatrughna</s> will follow me as I live there for my brother's sake,
while the noble one, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, will rule <s>Ayodhyā</s>.
The twice-born will consecrate <s>Kākutstha</s> in <s>Ayodhyā</s>.

children.text: api me devatāḥ kuryur imaṃ satyaṃ manoratham ||
children.translated_text: May the gods make this true wish of mine come to pass.

children.text: prasādyamānaḥ śirasā mayā svayaṃ bahuprakāraṃ yadi na prapatsyate
children.translated_text: If, though entreated by me myself with bowed head in many ways, he does not yield,

children.text: tato 'nuvatsyāmi cirāya rāghavaṃ vane vasan nārhati mām upekṣitum ||
children.translated_text: then I shall follow <s>Rāghava</s> for a long time; dwelling in the forest, he ought not disregard me.

children.text: vyuṣya rātriṃ tu tatraiva gaṅgākūle sa rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spent the night right there on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, that descendant of <s>Raghu</s>,

children.text: bharataḥ kālyam utthāya śatrughnam idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s>, rising early, said this to <s>Śatrughna</s>."
O <s>Śatrughna</s>, get up! Why are you lying asleep? <s>Guha</s>, lord of the <s>Niṣādas</s>,

children.text: śīghram ānaya bhadraṃ te tārayiṣyati vāhinīm ||
children.translated_text: bring him quickly; may good be yours. He will ferry the army across.
I am awake; I am not sleeping, for I am likewise thinking of the noble one.

children.text: ity evam abravīd bhrātrā śatrughno 'pi pracoditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Śatrughna</s> too, urged by his brother, replied.
While those two lions among men were thus speaking with one another,

children.text: āgamya prāñjaliḥ kāle guho bharatam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Guha</s> came at the proper time with joined palms and spoke to <s>Bharata</s>:
O <s>Kākutstha</s>, did you pass the night happily on the riverbank?

children.text: kaccic ca saha sainyasya tava sarvam anāmayam ||
children.translated_text: And is all well with your entire army?

children.text: guhasya tat tu vacanaṃ śrutvā snehād udīritam
children.translated_text: Hearing that word of <s>Guha</s>, spoken out of affection,
<s>Bharata</s> too, obedient to <s>Rāma</s>, said this sentence:

children.text: sukhā naḥ śarvarī rājan pūjitāś cāpi te vayam
children.translated_text: O king, the night was pleasant for us, and we have been honored by you.

children.text: gaṅgāṃ tu naubhir bahvībhir dāśāḥ saṃtārayantu naḥ ||
children.translated_text: But let the boatmen ferry us across the <s>Gaṅgā</s> with many boats.
Then <s>Guha</s>, having heard <s>Bharata</s>'s command, hurried
back into the town and spoke to his kinsmen:

children.text: uttiṣṭhata prabudhyadhvaṃ bhadram astu hi vaḥ sadā
children.translated_text: Rise up, wake up; may good always be yours.
Draw the boats together. We shall ferry the army across.
So addressed, they rose up quickly at the king's command

children.text: pañca nāvāṃ śatāny eva samāninyuḥ samantataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and brought five hundred boats from every side.
Other excellent boats, recognizable by the svastika mark and bearing great bells,
shone with banners, well rigged, and firmly joined together.
Then <s>Guha</s> brought forward a fine boat, recognizable by the svastika mark,
covered with pale blankets, auspicious, and ringing with a joyous sound.

children.text: tām āruroha bharataḥ śatrughnaś ca mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s> boarded it, and so did mighty <s>Śatrughna</s>,

children.text: kausalyā ca sumitrā ca yāś cānyā rājayoṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: along with <s>Kausalyā</s>, <s>Sumitrā</s>, and the other royal women.

children.text: purohitaś ca tat pūrvaṃ guravo brāhmaṇāś ca ye
children.translated_text: The priest went first, and then the elders and brahmins,
and after them the royal wives, as well as the carts and market goods.
As some set the camp alight and others plunged into the ford,
and as they took up the baggage, the clamor touched the heavens.

children.text: patākinyas tu tā nāvaḥ svayaṃ dāśair adhiṣṭhitāḥ
children.translated_text: Those bannered boats, piloted by the boatmen themselves,

children.text: vahantyo janam ārūḍhaṃ tadā saṃpetur āśugāḥ ||
children.translated_text: swiftly carried the people who had boarded them across at that time.

children.text: nārīṇām abhipūrṇās tu kāścit kāścit tu vājinām
children.translated_text: Some were filled with women, others with horses,

children.text: kāścit tatra vahanti sma yānayugyaṃ mahādhanam ||
children.translated_text: and others there carried vehicles, draught animals, and great wealth.

children.text: tāḥ sma gatvā paraṃ tīram avaropya ca taṃ janam
children.translated_text: After those boats had gone to the far bank and set the people down,
they returned, while the boatmen's kinsmen performed various feats with poles.
Elephants with victory banners, urged on by their riders,

children.text: tarantaḥ sma prakāśante sadhvajā iva parvatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: shone as they crossed, like mountains furnished with banners.

children.text: nāvaś cāruruhus tv anye plavais terus tathāpare
children.translated_text: Some others mounted boats; others crossed on rafts.

children.text: anye kumbhaghaṭais terur anye teruś ca bāhubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Some crossed with water jars and pots, and others crossed with their arms.

children.text: sā puṇyā dhvajinī gaṅgāṃ dāśaiḥ saṃtāritā svayam
children.translated_text: That holy bannered army, ferried across the <s>Gaṅgā</s> by the boatmen themselves,
set out at the <s>Maitra muhūrta</s> toward the excellent forest of <s>Prayāga</s>.

children.text: āśvāsayitvā ca camūṃ mahātmā niveśayitvā ca yathopajoṣam
children.translated_text: After reassuring the army and encamping it wherever suitable,

children.text: draṣṭuṃ bharadvājam ṛṣipravaryam ṛtvigvṛtaḥ san bharataḥ pratasthe ||
children.translated_text: great-souled <s>Bharata</s> set out, surrounded by officiating priests, to see <s>Bharadvāja</s>, the foremost sage.
When that bull among men saw <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s hermitage from a krośa away,

children.text: balaṃ sarvam avasthāpya jagāma saha mantribhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: he halted the whole army and went on with his ministers.
The knower of <s>dharma</s> went on foot alone, having laid aside his weapons and equipment,
wearing two linen garments and placing the family priest before him.
Then, at the sight of <s>Bharadvāja</s>, the <s>Rāghava</s>
left those ministers behind and followed after the priest.
As soon as the great ascetic <s>Bharadvāja</s> saw <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,

children.text: saṃcacālāsanāt tūrṇaṃ śiṣyān arghyam iti bruvan ||
children.translated_text: he rose quickly from his seat, telling his disciples, Bring the arghya offering.
Coming together with <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, and being greeted respectfully by <s>Bharata</s>,
the greatly radiant sage recognized him as that son of <s>Daśaratha</s>.

children.text: tābhyām arghyaṃ ca pādyaṃ ca dattvā paścāt phalāni ca
children.translated_text: Having given arghya and water for the feet to the two of them, and then fruits,

children.text: ānupūrvyāc ca dharmajñaḥ papraccha kuśalaṃ kule ||
children.translated_text: the knower of <s>dharma</s> asked in proper order about the welfare of the family.

children.text: ayodhyāyāṃ bale kośe mitreṣv api ca mantriṣu
children.translated_text: He asked about <s>Ayodhyā</s>, the army, the treasury, the allies, and the ministers;

children.text: jānan daśarathaṃ vṛttaṃ na rājānam udāharat ||
children.translated_text: but, knowing that <s>Daśaratha</s> had passed away, he did not mention the king.
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and <s>Bharata</s> in turn asked him about his well-being,
in body, in his sacred fires, in his trees, in his pupils, and among the deer and birds.
The great ascetic <s>Bharadvāja</s> answered, So it is,
and, bound by affection for <s>Rāghava</s>, said this to <s>Bharata</s>:

children.text: kim ihāgamane kāryaṃ tava rājyaṃ praśāsataḥ
children.translated_text: What purpose do you have in coming here, while you are ruling the kingdom?

children.text: etad ācakṣva me sarvaṃ na hi me śudhyate manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Tell me all this, for my mind is not clear about it.
He whom <s>Kausalyā</s> bore, the destroyer of foes and increaser of her joy,

children.text: bhrātrā saha sabhāryo yaś ciraṃ pravrājito vanam ||
children.translated_text: who with his brother and his wife was exiled to the forest for a long time,
that famous man who was ordered by a father ruled by a woman
to be a forest-dweller here, they say, for fourteen years,

children.text: kaccin na tasyāpāpasya pāpaṃ kartum ihecchasi
children.translated_text: surely you do not wish to do harm to that sinless one,
desiring to enjoy his kingdom, and his younger brother's, free of rivals?

children.text: evam ukto bharadvājaṃ bharataḥ pratyuvāca ha
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Bharata</s> replied to <s>Bharadvāja</s>,
his eyes filled with tears from grief and his speech faltering:

children.text: hato 'smi yadi mām evaṃ bhagavān api manyate
children.translated_text: I am ruined, if even the blessed one thinks of me in this way.

children.text: matto na doṣam āśaṅker naivaṃ mām anuśādhi hi ||
children.translated_text: Do not suspect fault in me; do not instruct me in this way.

children.text: na caitad iṣṭaṃ mātā me yad avocan madantare
children.translated_text: Nor was that desired by my mother, what she said when I was absent.

children.text: nāham etena tuṣṭaś ca na tad vacanam ādade ||
children.translated_text: I am not pleased with that, and I do not accept that command.

children.text: ahaṃ tu taṃ naravyāghram upayātaḥ prasādakaḥ
children.translated_text: Rather, I have come to that tiger among men to win his favor.
and to lead him back to <s>Ayodhyā</s> and bow down to his feet.

children.text: tvaṃ mām evaṃ gataṃ matvā prasādaṃ kartum arhasi
children.translated_text: You should be gracious to me, considering me to have come in this way.

children.text: śaṃsa me bhagavan rāmaḥ kva samprati mahīpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Tell me, reverend sir, where is the lord king <s>Rāma</s> at present?

children.text: uvāca taṃ bharadvājaḥ prasādād bharataṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Bharadvāja</s>, being favorably disposed, spoke these words to <s>Bharata</s>:
This is fitting in you, tiger among men, born in the line of <s>Rāghava</s>:
your conduct toward elders, self-restraint, and following after good men.

children.text: jāne caitan manaḥsthaṃ te dṛḍhīkaraṇam astv iti
children.translated_text: And I know this to be settled in your mind; let there be confirmation, I thought.
I questioned you for your own great advantage, increasing your fame.

children.text: asau vasati te bhrātā citrakūṭe mahāgirau
children.translated_text: That brother of yours dwells on the great mountain <s>Citrakūṭa</s>.

children.text: śvas tu gantāsi taṃ deśaṃ vasādya saha mantribhiḥ
children.translated_text: Tomorrow you will go to that region, after staying here together with your ministers.

children.text: etaṃ me kuru suprājña kāmaṃ kāmārthakovida ||
children.translated_text: Do this wish of mine, very wise one, you who know the objects of desire.

children.text: tatas tathety evam udāradarśanaḥ pratītarūpo bharato 'bravīd vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, saying 'So be it,' <s>Bharata</s>, of noble vision and gracious appearance, spoke in reply;

children.text: cakāra buddhiṃ ca tadā mahāśrame niśānivāsāya narādhipātmajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and then the prince resolved to spend the night in the great hermitage.

children.text: kṛtabuddhiṃ nivāsāya tathaiva sa munis tadā
children.translated_text: When he had likewise made up his mind to stay there, the sage at that time
invited <s>Bharata</s>, son of <s>Kaikeyī</s>, with hospitality.

children.text: abravīd bharatas tv enaṃ nanv idaṃ bhavatā kṛtam
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s> said to him, 'Surely this has already been done by you:

children.text: pādyam arghyaṃ tathātithyaṃ vane yad upapadyate ||
children.translated_text: water for the feet, arghya, and such hospitality as is possible in the forest.'
Then <s>Bharadvāja</s>, as if smiling, said to <s>Bharata</s>:

children.text: jāne tvāṃ prītisaṃyuktaṃ tuṣyes tvaṃ yena kenacit ||
children.translated_text: 'I know you to be joined with affection; you are pleased with anything whatever.

children.text: senāyās tu tavaitasyāḥ kartum icchāmi bhojanam
children.translated_text: But I wish to provide food for this army of yours.

children.text: mama prītir yathārūpā tvam arho manujarṣabha ||
children.translated_text: You are worthy, bull among men, of hospitality such as accords with my affection.

children.text: kimarthaṃ cāpi nikṣipya dūre balam ihāgataḥ
children.translated_text: And why, having left your forces far away, have you come here?
Why have you not approached here with your army, best of men?'
<s>Bharata</s>, with joined palms, answered this to that treasure of ascetic power:
'I did not approach with my army, reverend sir, out of fear of your reverence.

children.text: vājimukhyā manuṣyāś ca mattāś ca varavāraṇāḥ
children.translated_text: The foremost horses, the men, and the intoxicated excellent elephants,

children.text: pracchādya mahatīṃ bhūmiṃ bhagavann anuyānti mām ||
children.translated_text: covering the great earth, reverend sir, follow me.

children.text: te vṛkṣān udakaṃ bhūmim āśrameṣūṭajāṃs tathā
children.translated_text: They might damage the trees, the water, the ground,

children.text: na hiṃsyur iti tenāham eka evāgatas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also the huts in the hermitages; therefore I came from there alone.'
When the great seer commanded, 'Let the army be brought here,'

children.text: tathā tu cakre bharataḥ senāyāḥ samupāgamam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s> did accordingly, causing the army to come near.
Then, entering the fire-hall, drinking water, and purifying himself,
for the purpose of the act of hospitality he invoked <s>Viśvakarman</s>.

children.text: āhvaye viśvakarmāṇam ahaṃ tvaṣṭāram eva ca
children.translated_text: 'I invoke <s>Viśvakarman</s> and also <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>.

children.text: ātithyaṃ kartum icchāmi tatra me saṃvidhīyatām ||
children.translated_text: I wish to render hospitality; let arrangements for it be made for me there.

children.text: prāksrotasaś ca yā nadyaḥ pratyaksrotasa eva ca
children.translated_text: Let the rivers that flow eastward and those that flow westward,

children.text: pṛthivyām antarikṣe ca samāyāntv adya sarvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: on earth and in the atmosphere, all come together today from every side.

children.text: anyāḥ sravantu maireyaṃ surām anyāḥ suniṣṭhitām
children.translated_text: Let some flow with maireya liquor, others with well-prepared surā,
and still others with cool water like the juice of sugarcane stalks.
I invoke the divine gandharvas, <s>Viśvāvasu</s>, <s>Hāhā</s>, and <s>Hūhū</s>,
and likewise all the divine apsarases and gandharvī women.
<s>Ghṛtācī</s>, <s>Viśvācī</s>, <s>Miśrakeśī</s>, and <s>Alambusā</s>,

children.text: śakraṃ yāś copatiṣṭhanti brahmāṇaṃ yāś ca bhāminīḥ
children.translated_text: and the lovely women who attend <s>Śakra</s> and those who attend <s>Brahmā</s>,
all of them, with <s>Tumburu</s> and their attendants, I summon.

children.text: vanaṃ kuruṣu yad divyaṃ vāso bhūṣaṇapattravat
children.translated_text: The divine forest in the land of the <s>Kurus</s>, whose trees bear garments and ornaments as leaves,

children.text: divyanārīphalaṃ śaśvat tat kauberam ihaiva tu ||
children.translated_text: and always bear divine women as fruit, that forest of <s>Kubera</s> is to be right here.

children.text: iha me bhagavān somo vidhattām annam uttamam
children.translated_text: Here may venerable <s>Soma</s> provide excellent food for me:

children.text: bhakṣyaṃ bhojyaṃ ca coṣyaṃ ca lehyaṃ ca vividhaṃ bahu ||
children.translated_text: many varied things to be eaten, consumed as meals, sucked, and licked.
And varied garlands, some dropped from trees,

children.text: surādīni ca peyāni māṃsāni vividhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: and drinks such as surā, and many kinds of meat.'
Thus, endowed with concentration and with incomparable brilliance,
the sage spoke, with proper śikṣā (phonetic discipline) and intonation, and with ascetic power.
While he meditated mentally, facing east with joined palms,
all those divine beings arrived separately, one by one.
Then a wind that removed sweat, touching <s>Malaya</s> and <s>Dardura</s>,

children.text: upaspṛśya vavau yuktyā supriyātmā sukhaḥ śivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: blew appropriately, very pleasing, pleasant, and auspicious in nature.
Then divine clouds gathered, and showers of flowers fell,
and the sound of heavenly drums was heard in all directions.
Excellent breezes blew, and hosts of apsarases danced;
divine gandharvas sang, and vīṇās released their notes.

children.text: sa śabdo dyāṃ ca bhūmiṃ ca prāṇināṃ śravaṇāni ca
children.translated_text: That sound entered heaven and earth and the ears of living beings,
smoothly produced, even, and endowed with the quality of rhythm.

children.text: tasminn uparate śabde divye śrotrasukhe nṛṇām
children.translated_text: When that divine sound, pleasing to men's ears, had ceased,
the army of <s>Bharata</s> saw the arrangement made by <s>Viśvakarman</s>.

children.text: babhūva hi samā bhūmiḥ samantāt pañcayojanam
children.translated_text: For the ground became level all around for five yojanas,
covered with many grasses resembling blue beryl.

children.text: tasmin bilvāḥ kapitthāś ca panasā bījapūrakāḥ
children.translated_text: On it there appeared bilva trees, kapittha trees, jackfruit trees, and citron trees;

children.text: āmalakyo babhūvuś ca cūtāś ca phalabhūṣaṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: there were āmalakī trees and mango trees, adorned with fruit.
And from the northern <s>Kurus</s> came a forest rich in divine enjoyments;

children.text: ājagāma nadī divyā tīrajair bahubhir vṛtā ||
children.translated_text: a divine river came too, surrounded by many trees born on its banks.
There were bright four-sided halls and stables for elephants and horses,
clusters of mansions and palaces, and beautiful gateways.
There was also a royal dwelling like a white cloud, with fine gateways,
made to look as if formed of white garlands and sprinkled with divine fragrance.
It was square, spacious, and furnished with beds, seats, and vehicles.
furnished with divine things of every flavor, and provided with divine food and garments.
There every kind of food had been prepared, and the vessels had been washed clean,
splendid, with every seat arranged and with excellent beds well spread.
With the great sage's permission, the mighty-armed one entered
that house filled with jewels: <s>Bharata</s>, the son of <s>Kaikeyī</s>.

children.text: anujagmuś ca taṃ sarve mantriṇaḥ sapurohitāḥ
children.translated_text: All the ministers, together with the priests, followed him,

children.text: babhūvuś ca mudā yuktās taṃ dṛṣṭvā veśmasaṃvidhim ||
children.translated_text: and they were filled with delight when they saw the arrangement of the house.

children.text: tatra rājāsanaṃ divyaṃ vyajanaṃ chattram eva ca
children.translated_text: There were a divine royal seat, a fan, and a parasol,
and <s>Bharata</s>, together with the ministers, approached them like a king.
He honored the seat, bowing toward <s>Rāma</s>,
and, taking up the yak-tail fan, sat down on a minister's seat.
Then all the ministers and priests sat down in due order;

children.text: tataḥ senāpatiḥ paścāt praśāstā ca niṣedatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: after them the commander of the army and the governor also sat down.
Then, in a moment, rivers whose mud was milk-rice
stood before <s>Bharata</s> at <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s command.
On both banks of those rivers, smeared with white clay,

children.text: ramyāś cāvasathā divyā brahmaṇas tu prasādajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: there were pleasant, divine dwellings produced by <s>Brahmā</s>'s favor.
In that very moment, adorned with divine ornaments,
twenty thousand women came, sent by <s>Brahmā</s>.
Adorned with gold, jewels, pearls, and coral,
twenty thousand women came, sent by <s>Kubera</s>.

children.text: yābhir gṛhītaḥ puruṣaḥ sonmāda iva lakṣyate
children.translated_text: A man seized by them appeared as if mad with passion;
twenty thousand companies of apsarases came from <s>Nandana</s>.
<s>Nārada</s>, <s>Tumburu</s>, <s>Gopa</s>, <s>Parvata</s>, and <s>Sūryavarcas</s>,
these kings of the gandharvas sang before <s>Bharata</s>.
<s>Alambusā</s>, <s>Miśrakeśī</s>, <s>Puṇḍarīkā</s>, and <s>Vāmanā</s>
danced attendance on <s>Bharata</s> at <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s command.

children.text: yāni mālyāni deveṣu yāni caitrarathe vane
children.translated_text: The garlands that are among the gods, and those in <s>Caitraratha</s> forest,
appeared at <s>Prayāga</s> at <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s command.
Bilva trees became mṛdaṅga players, and vibhītaka trees became holders of clappers;
aśvattha trees became dancers, by <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s power.
Then sarala trees, palms, tilakas, and naktamālakas

children.text: prahṛṣṭās tatra saṃpetuḥ kubjā bhūtvātha vāmanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: joyfully gathered there, having become hunchbacks and dwarfs.

children.text: śiṃśapāmalakī jambūr yāś cānyāḥ kānane latāḥ
children.translated_text: Śiṃśapās, āmalakīs, jambūs, and whatever other creepers were in the forest
assumed the forms of women and stayed in <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s hermitage.

children.text: surāṃ surāpāḥ pibata pāyasaṃ ca bubhukṣitāḥ
children.translated_text: "Drink wine, you wine-drinkers, and rice-milk, you hungry ones;

children.text: māṃsāni ca sumedhyāni bhakṣyantāṃ yāvad icchatha ||
children.translated_text: eat pure, well-prepared meats as much as you wish."
The women scrubbed and bathed them on the lovely riverbanks,

children.text: apy ekam ekaṃ puruṣaṃ pramadāḥ sapta cāṣṭa ca ||
children.translated_text: seven or eight women attending each single man.
Beautiful-eyed women came up as they massaged them,
and, after wiping them properly, the lovely women gave them drink.

children.text: hayān gajān kharān uṣṭrāṃs tathaiva surabheḥ sutān
children.translated_text: They fed the horses, elephants, donkeys, camels, and likewise the offspring of <s>Surabhi</s>,

children.text: ikṣūṃś ca madhujālāṃś ca bhojayanti sma vāhanān
children.translated_text: and they gave sugarcanes and honeycombs to the riding animals,
while the mighty men urged on the best warriors of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s>.
No groom recognized his horse, and no elephant-keeper recognized his elephant;
that army shone there, intoxicated, careless, and delighted.
Satisfied with every desired thing and smeared with red sandalwood,
the soldiers, attended by companies of apsarases, raised their voices:
"We will not go to <s>Ayodhyā</s>; we will not go to the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forests.
May <s>Bharata</s> be well, and may <s>Rāma</s> likewise be happy."
Thus the foot soldiers, elephant riders, horsemen, and keepers

children.text: anāthās taṃ vidhiṃ labdhvā vācam etām udairayan ||
children.translated_text: uttered these words after receiving that provision, though they had been helpless.

children.text: samprahṛṣṭā vinedus te narās tatra sahasraśaḥ
children.translated_text: Those men, thousands of <s>Bharata</s>'s followers, were overjoyed and shouted there,
and they said, "This is heaven."

children.text: tato bhuktavatāṃ teṣāṃ tad annam amṛtopamam
children.translated_text: Then, although they had eaten that food like ambrosia,

children.text: divyān udvīkṣya bhakṣyāṃs tān abhavad bhakṣaṇe matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: when they saw those divine dainties, their minds turned again to eating.

children.text: preṣyāś ceṭyaś ca vadhvaś ca balasthāś cāpi sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Servants, maidservants, young women, and all who were in the army

children.text: babhūvus te bhṛśaṃ tṛptāḥ sarve cāhatavāsasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: became deeply satisfied, and all wore fresh garments.

children.text: kuñjarāś ca kharoṣṭraś ca go'śvāś ca mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Elephants, donkeys, camels, cattle, horses, deer, and birds

children.text: babhūvuḥ subhṛtās tatra nānyo hy anyam akalpayat ||
children.translated_text: were well nourished there, for no one had to provide for another.
There was no one there without white garments, nor anyone hungry or dirty,

children.text: rajasā dhvastakeśo vā naraḥ kaścid adṛśyata ||
children.translated_text: nor was any man seen with hair disheveled by dust.
With heaps of the finest sauces made from goats and boars,
and with soups prepared from masses of fruit, endowed with fragrance and flavor,
men saw there, with wonder, thousands of iron cauldrons

children.text: dadṛśur vismitās tatra narā lauhīḥ sahasraśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: filled all around with white rice and bearing banners of flowers.
At the sides of the forest there were wells whose mud was milk-rice;

children.text: tāś ca kāmadughā gāvo drumāś cāsan madhuścyutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there were wish-granting cows, and trees dripping with honey.
There were ponds full of maireya liquor, surrounded by heaps of choice meat,
and also hot cooking vessels with peacocks and fowl set along the road.
There were thousands of vessels, made of refined gold,

children.text: sthālyaḥ kumbhyaḥ karambhyaś ca dadhipūrṇāḥ susaṃskṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: and bowls, jars, and karambha-pots, well prepared and filled with curds
from young, fair cattle, fragrant with kapittha fruit.

children.text: hradāḥ pūrṇā rasālasya dadhnaḥ śvetasya cāpare
children.translated_text: There were lakes full of rasāla drink, and others full of white curd;
at the edge of the milk-rice there were heaps of sugar.

children.text: kalkāṃś cūrṇakaṣāyāṃś ca snānāni vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: There were pastes, powders, decoctions, and various kinds of baths.
The men saw vessels set out at the fords of the rivers,
and also heaps of white, shining tooth-cleaning sticks,
and white sandalwood pastes placed in boxes.

children.text: darpaṇān parimṛṣṭāṃś ca vāsasāṃ cāpi saṃcayān
children.translated_text: They saw polished mirrors and piles of garments,
and pairs of sandals and shoes there by the thousands,

children.text: āñjanīḥ kaṅkatān kūrcāṃś chattrāṇi ca dhanūṃṣi ca
children.translated_text: collyrium boxes, combs, brushes, parasols, and bows,
variegated armor, beds, and seats,
watering ponds filled for donkeys, camels, elephants, and horses,
and excellent bathing ponds full of blue and red lotuses.
They also saw soft heaps of barley fodder, colored like blue beryl,

children.text: nirvāpārthaṃ paśūnāṃ te dadṛśus tatra sarvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there everywhere, for the refreshment of the animals.

children.text: vyasmayanta manuṣyās te svapnakalpaṃ tad adbhutam
children.translated_text: Those men were amazed at that marvelous thing, like a dream,
when they saw such hospitality performed for <s>Bharata</s> by the great seer.

children.text: ity evaṃ ramamāṇānāṃ devānām iva nandane
children.translated_text: While they were thus enjoying themselves like gods in <s>Nandana</s>,
that night passed in <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s lovely hermitage.

children.text: pratijagmuś ca tā nadyo gandharvāś ca yathāgatam
children.translated_text: The rivers returned, and the <s>Gandharvas</s> also, just as they had come,

children.text: bharadvājam anujñāpya tāś ca sarvā varāṅganāḥ ||
children.translated_text: after taking leave of <s>Bharadvāja</s>, and so did all those beautiful women.

children.text: tathaiva mattā madirotkaṭā narās tathaiva divyāgurucandanokṣitāḥ
children.translated_text: The men were still intoxicated, excited with liquor, and sprinkled with divine aloe-wood and sandal,

children.text: tathaiva divyā vividhāḥ sraguttamāḥ pṛthakprakīrṇā manujaiḥ pramarditāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and likewise the excellent divine garlands of many kinds lay scattered separately, crushed by the men.

children.text: tatas tāṃ rajanīm uṣya bharataḥ saparicchadaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after spending that night, <s>Bharata</s>, together with his retinue,
having been received as a guest, approached <s>Bharadvāja</s> as he wished.

children.text: tam ṛṣiḥ puruṣavyāghraṃ prekṣya prāñjalim āgatam
children.translated_text: Seeing that tiger among men coming with folded hands,
<s>Bharadvāja</s>, who had performed the agnihotra offering, addressed <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: kaccid atra sukhā rātris tavāsmadviṣaye gatā
children.translated_text: Has this night here in my domain passed happily for you?

children.text: samagras te janaḥ kaccid ātithye śaṃsa me 'nagha ||
children.translated_text: Has all your company been satisfied with the hospitality? Tell me, sinless one.
Making a reverent gesture and bowing down, <s>Bharata</s> spoke to him,
to the sage of highest radiance who had come out from the hermitage.
I have spent the night happily, blessed sir, with my whole army and its vehicles intact;

children.text: tarpitaḥ sarvakāmaiś ca sāmātyo balavat tvayā ||
children.translated_text: with my ministers and forces, I have been satisfied by you with every desired thing.
Freed from weariness and distress, well fed and well sheltered,

children.text: api preṣyān upādāya sarve sma susukhoṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all of us, even including the servants, have spent the night very happily.
I take my leave of you now, blessed one, if you permit, best of sages.
I am setting out to my brother's presence; look on me with a friendly eye.
Knower of <s>dharma</s>, tell me the hermitage of that righteous, great-souled one,

children.text: ācakṣva katamo mārgaḥ kiyān iti ca śaṃsa me ||
children.translated_text: which road it is and how far it is; tell me this.
Thus asked by <s>Bharata</s>, who longed to see his brother,
the greatly radiant <s>Bharadvāja</s>, the great ascetic, replied:
Two and a half yojanas from here, <s>Bharata</s>, in an unpeopled forest,
there is the mountain <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, with lovely caves and woods.

children.text: uttaraṃ pārśvam āsādya tasya mandākinī nadī
children.translated_text: When one reaches its northern side, there is the river <s>Mandākinī</s>,
covered with flowering trees and lovely with blossoming groves.

children.text: anantaraṃ tat saritaś citrakūṭaś ca parvataḥ
children.translated_text: Immediately beyond that river is the mountain <s>Citrakūṭa</s>;

children.text: tayoḥ parṇakuṭī tāta tatra tau vasato dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: between those two, dear one, is a leaf-hut. There those two surely dwell.
By the southern road, keeping properly to left and right,
O lord of the army, lead the force crowded with elephants, horses, and chariots,
fortunate one; then you will see <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: prayāṇam iti ca śrutvā rājarājasya yoṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: When the wives of the king of kings heard, 'Departure,'
though worthy of riding in vehicles, they left their vehicles and surrounded the Brahmin.

children.text: vepamānā kṛśā dīnā saha devyā sumitrayā
children.translated_text: Trembling, thin, and wretched, together with queen <s>Sumitrā</s>,

children.text: kausalyā tatra jagrāha karābhyāṃ caraṇau muneḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kausalyā</s> there took the sage's feet in her hands.
With her desire unfulfilled, condemned by all the world,
<s>Kaikeyī</s> took his feet, filled with shame.
Having circumambulated the blessed great sage,
she then stood not far from <s>Bharata</s> himself, distressed in mind.
Then <s>Bharadvāja</s>, firm in his vow, asked <s>Bharata</s>,

children.text: viśeṣaṃ jñātum icchāmi mātṝṇāṃ tava rāghava ||
children.translated_text: I wish to know the distinction among your mothers, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: evam uktas tu bharato bharadvājena dhārmikaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Bharadvāja</s>, righteous <s>Bharata</s>,
skilled in speech, stood with folded hands and spoke these words:
This wretched woman, blessed sir, emaciated by grief and fasting,

children.text: pitur hi mahiṣīṃ devīṃ devatām iva paśyasi ||
children.translated_text: whom you see like a goddess, is my father's chief queen.
This <s>Kausalyā</s> gave birth to that tiger among men, who walks with a lion's stride,

children.text: kausalyā suṣuve rāmaṃ dhātāram aditir yathā ||
children.translated_text: to <s>Rāma</s>, just as <s>Aditi</s> gave birth to the Sustainer.

children.text: asyā vāmabhujaṃ śliṣṭā yaiṣā tiṣṭhati durmanāḥ
children.translated_text: The one who stands despondent, clinging to her left arm,
like a branch of a <s>karṇikāra</s> tree with its flowers fallen in the forest,

children.text: etasyās tau sutau devyāḥ kumārau devavarṇinau
children.translated_text: of that queen are those two sons, princes with the appearance of gods,
both <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and <s>Śatrughna</s>, heroes of true valor.

children.text: yasyāḥ kṛte naravyāghrau jīvanāśam ito gatau
children.translated_text: For whose sake those two tigers among men have gone from here toward the loss of life,

children.text: rājā putravihīnaś ca svargaṃ daśaratho gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and King <s>Daśaratha</s>, bereft of his sons, has gone to heaven,
that power-seeking <s>Kaikeyī</s>, ignoble though appearing noble,
know this mother of mine to be cruel and fixed upon evil,

children.text: yatomūlaṃ hi paśyāmi vyasanaṃ mahad ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: from whom as the root I see this great calamity of my own.
Having spoken thus, that tiger among men, with a voice choked by tears,

children.text: sa niśaśvāsa tāmrākṣo nāgaḥ kruddha ivāsakṛt ||
children.translated_text: red-eyed, sighed again and again like an angry serpent.

children.text: bharadvājo maharṣis taṃ bruvantaṃ bharataṃ tadā
children.translated_text: Then the great sage <s>Bharadvāja</s>, as <s>Bharata</s> was speaking in that way,
being very wise, answered him with these meaningful words:
You should not understand <s>Kaikeyī</s> as acting from fault, <s>Bharata</s>.
For this exile of <s>Rāma</s> will have happiness as its outcome.

children.text: abhivādya tu saṃsiddhaḥ kṛtvā cainaṃ pradakṣiṇam
children.translated_text: Then, after saluting him and, fully prepared, circumambulating him,

children.text: āmantrya bharataḥ sainyaṃ yujyatām ity acodayat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s> addressed the army and urged them, 'Let everything be yoked.'
Then, when the splendid chariots, adorned with gold, had been yoked with horses,
many people of many kinds, wishing to set out, mounted them.
Female elephants and male elephants too, with golden girths and bearing banners,
set out with a great roar, like rain clouds at the end of the hot season.

children.text: vividhāny api yānāni mahānti ca laghūni ca
children.translated_text: Various vehicles, both large and small,
very costly, went forth, while the foot-soldiers went on foot alone.
Then the women, with <s>Kausalyā</s> at their head, in excellent conveyances,
desiring to see <s>Rāma</s>, set out joyfully at that time.
And the illustrious <s>Bharata</s>, mounting a fine palanquin assigned to him,
shining like the young sun, set out together with his retinue.
That great army, filled with elephants, horses, and chariots, set out,
covering the southern quarter like a great cloud arisen,
and passing through forests inhabited by deer and birds.
There, <s>Bharata</s>'s army, with its delighted elephants, horses, and warriors, frightening flocks of deer and birds,

children.text: mahad vanaṃ tat pravigāhamānā rarāja senā bharatasya tatra ||
children.translated_text: shone as it plunged into that great forest.
Afflicted by that great marching, bannered army, the forest-dwelling
rutting herd-leaders fled in all directions together with their herds.

children.text: ṛkṣāḥ pṛṣatasaṃghāś ca ruravaś ca samantataḥ
children.translated_text: Bears, groups of spotted deer, and ruru deer on every side

children.text: dṛśyante vanarājīṣu giriṣv api nadīṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: were seen in the lines of forest, on the mountains, and also by the rivers.
Joyful, the righteous son of <s>Daśaratha</s> set out,
surrounded by a great, resounding fourfold army.
The army of great-souled <s>Bharata</s>, resembling a flood of the sea,
covered the earth as clouds cover the sky in the rainy season.
With masses of horses spread out and with elephants of great speed,

children.text: anālakṣyā ciraṃ kālaṃ tasmin kāle babhūva bhūḥ ||
children.translated_text: the earth became unrecognizable for a long time at that moment.
After traveling a long road, his mounts and vehicles thoroughly wearied,

children.text: uvāca bharataḥ śrīmān vasiṣṭhaṃ mantriṇāṃ varam ||
children.translated_text: the illustrious <s>Bharata</s> spoke to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, the foremost of ministers:

children.text: yādṛśaṃ lakṣyate rūpaṃ yathā caiva śrutaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: 'From the appearance that is seen, and just as I have heard,

children.text: vyaktaṃ prāptāḥ sma taṃ deśaṃ bharadvājo yam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: it is clear that we have reached the region of which <s>Bharadvāja</s> spoke.

children.text: ayaṃ giriś citrakūṭas tathā mandākinī nadī
children.translated_text: This mountain is <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, and that is the river <s>Mandākinī</s>;
this forest, dark as a blue cloud, is visible from afar.
The lovely ridges of <s>Citrakūṭa</s> mountain now
are being trampled by my mountain-like elephants.
These trees on the mountain ridges are letting fall their flowers,
like dense blue rain clouds pouring water when the heat has passed.
Look, <s>Śatrughna</s>, at the mountain, a region frequented by <s>Kiṃnaras</s>,

children.text: hayaiḥ samantād ākīrṇaṃ makarair iva sāgaram ||
children.translated_text: covered all around with horses like the ocean with makaras.
These herds of deer shine, swift in speed and driven onward,
like rows of clouds in the autumn sky, hurled by the wind.
These make fragrant crests of flowers upon their heads,
like men of the south with shields gleaming like clouds.
This forest, as though it had become silent and fearful to behold,
now appears to me like <s>Ayodhyā</s> crowded with people.

children.text: khurair udīrito reṇur divaṃ pracchādya tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: Dust stirred up by the hoofs stands covering the sky;

children.text: taṃ vahaty anilaḥ śīghraṃ kurvann iva mama priyam ||
children.translated_text: the wind carries it swiftly, as if doing something dear to me.
Look, <s>Śatrughna</s>, at these chariots furnished with horses,

children.text: etān saṃpatataḥ śīghraṃ paśya śatrughna kānane ||
children.translated_text: manned by chief charioteers, rushing swiftly together in the forest.
Look at these lovely peacocks, frightened,
entering this mountain, the dwelling place of birds.

children.text: atimātram ayaṃ deśo manojñaḥ pratibhāti mā
children.translated_text: This region appears to me exceedingly charming;
this abode of ascetics is plainly like the path to heaven.

children.text: mṛgā mṛgībhiḥ sahitā bahavaḥ pṛṣatā vane
children.translated_text: Many spotted deer in the forest, the males together with the females,
are seen in pleasing forms, as if variegated with flowers.

children.text: sādhu sainyāḥ pratiṣṭhantāṃ vicinvantu ca kānanam
children.translated_text: Good. Let the soldiers take their positions and search the forest,
so that those two tigers among men, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, may be seen.'
Hearing <s>Bharata</s>'s words, brave men with weapons in their hands

children.text: viviśus tad vanaṃ śūrā dhūmaṃ ca dadṛśus tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: entered that forest, and then they saw smoke.

children.text: te samālokya dhūmāgram ūcur bharatam āgatāḥ
children.translated_text: Having observed the tip of the smoke, they came back and said to <s>Bharata</s>:

children.text: nāmanuṣye bhavaty agnir vyaktam atraiva rāghavau ||
children.translated_text: 'There is no fire in a place without people; clearly the two <s>Rāghavas</s> are right here.
Or, if the two tigers among men, the princes who scorch their enemies, are not here,

children.text: anye rāmopamāḥ santi vyaktam atra tapasvinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then there are surely other ascetics here who are like <s>Rāma</s>.'

children.text: tac chrutvā bharatas teṣāṃ vacanaṃ sādhusaṃmatam
children.translated_text: Hearing that word of theirs, approved by the good,
<s>Bharata</s>, crusher of enemy forces, spoke to all those soldiers:

children.text: yattā bhavantas tiṣṭhantu neto gantavyam agrataḥ
children.translated_text: 'Let your honors stand attentive; no one should go farther from here.

children.text: aham eva gamiṣyāmi sumantro gurur eva ca ||
children.translated_text: I alone shall go, along with <s>Sumantra</s> and the venerable priest.'

children.text: evam uktās tataḥ sarve tatra tasthuḥ samantataḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, all of them then stood there on every side,

children.text: bharato yatra dhūmāgraṃ tatra dṛṣṭiṃ samādadhāt ||
children.translated_text: while <s>Bharata</s> fixed his gaze on the place where the tip of the smoke was.

children.text: vyavasthitā yā bharatena sā camūr nirīkṣamāṇāpi ca dhūmam agrataḥ
children.translated_text: That army, stationed by <s>Bharata</s> and gazing at the smoke in front,

children.text: babhūva hṛṣṭā nacireṇa jānatī priyasya rāmasya samāgamaṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: soon became thrilled, knowing then of the meeting with beloved <s>Rāma</s>.
Dwelling for a long time on that mountain, loving mountain and forest,

children.text: vaidehyāḥ priyamākāṅkṣan svaṃ ca cittaṃ vilobhayan ||
children.translated_text: wishing to please <s>Vaidehī</s> and to delight his own mind,
then the son of <s>Daśaratha</s> showed her lovely <s>Citrakūṭa</s>.
his wife, while he himself shone like an immortal, as <s>Purandara</s> does with <s>Śacī</s>.

children.text: na rājyād bhraṃśanaṃ bhadre na suhṛdbhir vinābhavaḥ
children.translated_text: O blessed lady, neither falling from the kingdom nor separation from friends

children.text: mano me bādhate dṛṣṭvā ramaṇīyam imaṃ girim ||
children.translated_text: troubles my mind when I see this delightful mountain.
Look, O blessed lady, at this immovable mountain, filled with flocks of many birds,
adorned with mineral-bearing peaks that seem to pierce the sky.
Some are like silver, some resemble blood,
some are yellow and madder-red in color, and some shine like excellent jewels.
Some have the radiance of flowers, arka, and ketaka, and some the glow of liquid light;
the regions of the lord of mountains, adorned with minerals, gleam forth.
Surrounded by herds of many animals, tigers, hyenas, bears, and groups of trees,
this harmless mountain shines, thronged with many birds.
With mangoes, rose-apples, asana trees, lodhra trees, priyāla trees, jackfruit trees, dhava trees,
aṅkola trees, bhavya trees, tiniśa trees, bilva trees, tinduka trees, and bamboos,
with kāśmarya, ariṣṭa, and varaṇa trees, madhūka trees, and tilaka trees too,
with jujube, āmalaka, nīpa, reeds, dhanvana, and bījaka trees,
flowering, bearing fruit, giving shade, and delightful,

children.text: evamādibhir ākīrṇaḥ śriyaṃ puṣyaty ayaṃ giriḥ ||
children.translated_text: this mountain, filled with such trees and others like them, nourishes its beauty.
On the lovely plateaus of the mountain, look at these beings who arouse desire and delight,
the high-spirited kiṃnaras, O blessed lady, sporting in pairs.

children.text: śākhāvasaktān khaḍgāṃś ca pravarāṇy ambarāṇi ca
children.translated_text: Look at the swords hung on branches, and the fine garments too;
see the charming playgrounds of the women of the vidyādharas.

children.text: jalaprapātair udbhedair nisyandaiś ca kvacit kvacit
children.translated_text: With waterfalls, springs, and streams here and there,

children.text: sravadbhir bhāty ayaṃ śailaḥ sravan mada iva dvipaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this mountain shines as it flows, like an elephant streaming with rut-fluid.
The wind from the caves, carrying scents born from many flowers,

children.text: ghrāṇatarpaṇam abhyetya kaṃ naraṃ na praharṣayet ||
children.translated_text: comes to satisfy the sense of smell; what man would it not gladden?
If I dwell here for many autumns together with you, O blameless one,

children.text: lakṣmaṇena ca vatsyāmi na māṃ śokaḥ pradhakṣyati ||
children.translated_text: and with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, grief will not burn me.
In this lovely place, rich in many flowers and fruits and filled with flocks of many birds,

children.text: vicitraśikhare hy asmin ratavān asmi bhāmini ||
children.translated_text: on this mountain of varied peaks, I am indeed delighted, O radiant lady.
Through this dwelling in the forest I have gained a twofold fruit:

children.text: pituś cānṛṇatā dharme bharatasya priyaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: freedom from debt to my father in respect to <s>dharma</s> (duty), and also what is dear to <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: vaidehi ramase kaccic citrakūṭe mayā saha
children.translated_text: Are you enjoying yourself, <s>Vaidehī</s>, on <s>Citrakūṭa</s> together with me,
seeing these various states of life, restrained in mind, speech, and body?

children.text: idam evāmṛtaṃ prāhū rājñāṃ rājarṣayaḥ pare
children.translated_text: The former royal seers, my great-grandfathers, declared this very thing to be nectar for kings:
forest dwelling, for the sake of welfare after death.
The broad rocks of the mountain shine by the hundreds all around,
abundant, with many colors: blue, yellow, white, and red.
At night, on the lord of mountains, they shine like flames of fire,
the herbs by their own splendor, gleaming in beauty by the thousands.
Some places look like dwellings, some like pleasure gardens,
and some parts of this mountain appear as a single mass of rock, O radiant lady.
<s>Citrakūṭa</s> shines as if it had split the earth and risen up;
that peak of <s>Citrakūṭa</s> is seen everywhere, auspicious.
Look at the lovers' own coverlets, with upper coverings of kuṣṭha, puṃnāga, tagara, and birch leaves,
spread with lotus petals.
Crushed and cast aside, lotus garlands are seen there;

children.text: kāmibhir vanite paśya phalāni vividhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: look, O woman, at the various fruits left by lovers as well.
That mountain <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, rich in roots, fruits, and water, seems to surpass
the lotus lake of <s>Vasvaukasārā</s> and even the <s>Uttara Kurus</s>.

children.text: imaṃ tu kālaṃ vanite vijahrivāṃs tvayā ca sīte saha lakṣmaṇena ca
children.translated_text: Having sported for this season here, O lady, together with you, <s>Sītā</s>, and with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: ratiṃ prapatsye kuladharmavardhinīṃ satāṃ pathi svair niyamaiḥ paraiḥ sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall attain a delight that increases the <s>dharma</s> (duty) of my lineage, standing on the path of the good through excellent restraints.
Then, coming down from the mountain, the lord of the <s>Kosalas</s>
showed the <s>Maithilī</s> the lovely river <s>Mandākinī</s>, with its auspicious waters.
And lotus-eyed <s>Rāma</s> spoke to the fair-hipped woman, whose face was like the lovely moon,
the daughter of the king of <s>Videha</s>:
Look at the lovely river <s>Mandākinī</s>, with its varied sandy banks, visited by haṃsas and sārasas,
rich with flowers.
It is surrounded by many kinds of trees growing on its banks, by trees bearing flowers and fruit,
and it shines on every side like the lotus lake of the king of kings.
Its charming fords, whose waters are now muddied by herds of deer drinking there,
produce delight in me.
At the proper time, sages wearing matted hair and antelope skins, with bark garments as their outer clothing,

children.text: ṛṣayas tv avagāhante nadīṃ mandākinīṃ priye ||
children.translated_text: bathe in the river <s>Mandākinī</s>, dear one.
Following their rule, they worship the sun with arms upraised;
here are other sages, broad-eyed one, of sharpened vows.
With treetops shaken by the wind, the mountain is as if dancing,
as the trees scatter leaves and flowers all around the river.
In places its water resembles jewels, in places it is rich with sandy banks;
in places it is crowded with perfected beings: look at the river <s>Mandākinī</s>.
See the heaps of flowers shaken loose by the wind and spread out,
and look at others floating in the middle of the water.
Those birds called rathāṅgas, with exceedingly lovely voices,
alight on them, O beautiful one, uttering auspicious cries.
The sight of <s>Citrakūṭa</s> and of the <s>Mandākinī</s>, O lovely one,

children.text: adhikaṃ puravāsāc ca manye ca tava darśanāt ||
children.translated_text: I consider greater than dwelling in the city, and still more because of the sight of you.
with perfected beings whose impurities have been shaken off, endowed with austerity, self-restraint, and calm;
enter, together with me, these waters that are always stirred.

children.text: sakhīvac ca vigāhasva sīte mandākinīm imām
children.translated_text: Like a companion, <s>Sītā</s>, enter this <s>Mandākinī</s>,
plunging among the lotuses and water-lilies, lovely lady.

children.text: tvaṃ paurajanavad vyālān ayodhyām iva parvatam
children.translated_text: Woman, regard the wild creatures as citizens, and the mountain as <s>Ayodhyā</s>,

children.text: manyasva vanite nityaṃ sarayūvad imāṃ nadīm ||
children.translated_text: and always regard this river as the <s>Sarayū</s>.
And righteous <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> remains obedient to my command;

children.text: tvaṃ cānukūlā vaidehi prītiṃ janayatho mama ||
children.translated_text: and you, <s>Vaidehī</s>, being favorable to me, both give me joy.
Touching water at the three daily times, eating honey, roots, and fruits,

children.text: nāyodhyāyai na rājyāya spṛhaye 'dya tvayā saha ||
children.translated_text: today I long neither for <s>Ayodhyā</s> nor for the kingdom, while I am with you.

children.text: imāṃ hi ramyāṃ gajayūthalolitāṃ nipītatoyāṃ gajasiṃhavānaraiḥ
children.translated_text: For this charming river, stirred by herds of elephants, whose water has been drunk by elephants, lions, and monkeys,

children.text: supuṣpitaiḥ puṣpadharair alaṃkṛtāṃ na so 'sti yaḥ syān na gatakramaḥ sukhī ||
children.translated_text: adorned with flowering trees heavy with blossoms: there is no one who would not become happy after coming to her.

children.text: itīva rāmo bahusaṃgataṃ vacaḥ priyāsahāyaḥ saritaṃ prati bruvan
children.translated_text: Speaking in this way many such words about the river, with his beloved as companion,

children.text: cacāra ramyaṃ nayanāñjanaprabhaṃ sa citrakūṭaṃ raghuvaṃśavardhanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, increaser of the <s>Raghu</s> line, wandered over lovely <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, dark as collyrium to the eyes.
While he was staying there in that way, as <s>Bharata</s> was drawing near,

children.text: sainyareṇuś ca śabdaś ca prādurāstāṃ nabhaḥspṛśau ||
children.translated_text: the dust of the army and its noise appeared, touching the sky.

children.text: etasminn antare trastāḥ śabdena mahatā tataḥ
children.translated_text: At that moment, frightened by the great sound,

children.text: arditā yūthapā mattāḥ sayūthā dudruvur diśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the rutting leaders of herds, distressed and with their herds, ran in all directions.

children.text: sa taṃ sainyasamudbhūtaṃ śabdaṃ śuśrava rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> heard that noise produced by the army,

children.text: tāṃś ca vipradrutān sarvān yūthapān anvavaikṣata ||
children.translated_text: and he looked at all those herd-leaders that had fled away.

children.text: tāṃś ca vidravato dṛṣṭvā taṃ ca śrutvā sa niḥsvanam
children.translated_text: Seeing them running off and hearing that roar,
<s>Rāma</s> spoke to <s>Saumitri</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> of blazing splendor:

children.text: hanta lakṣmaṇa paśyeha sumitrā suprajās tvayā
children.translated_text: 'Come, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, look here; <s>Sumitrā</s> is blessed with a good son in you.
A tumultuous sound is heard, deep as a terrible thunderclap.

children.text: rājā vā rājamātro vā mṛgayām aṭate vane
children.translated_text: Perhaps a king or a prince is roaming in the forest for the hunt,

children.text: anyad vā śvāpadaṃ kiṃcit saumitre jñātum arhasi
children.translated_text: or perhaps it is some other wild creature, <s>Saumitri</s>; you ought to find out.
You should soon learn all this exactly as it is.'

children.text: sa lakṣmaṇaḥ saṃtvaritaḥ sālam āruhya puṣpitam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> quickly climbed a flowering śāla tree,

children.text: prekṣamāṇo diśaḥ sarvāḥ pūrvāṃ diśam avaikṣata ||
children.translated_text: and, looking over all the directions, he gazed toward the eastern quarter.
Looking northward, he saw a great army,
crowded with chariots, horses, and elephants, joined by ready foot soldiers.
That army, filled with horses and elephants and adorned with chariot banners,

children.text: śaśaṃsa senāṃ rāmāya vacanaṃ cedam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: he reported to <s>Rāma</s>, and he spoke these words:
