children.text: agniṃ saṃśamayatv āryaḥ sītā ca bhajatāṃ guhām
children.translated_text: 'Let my noble brother put out the fire, and let <s>Sītā</s> go into a cave.

children.text: sajyaṃ kuruṣva cāpaṃ ca śarāṃś ca kavacaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: String your bow, and make ready your arrows and armor as well.'

children.text: taṃ rāmaḥ puruṣavyāghro lakṣmaṇaṃ pratyuvāca ha
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s>, tiger among men, replied to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:
'Look closely, <s>Saumitri</s>; whose army do you think this is?'

children.text: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa lakṣmaṇo vākyam abravīt
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> spoke this sentence,

children.text: didhakṣann iva tāṃ senāṃ ruṣitaḥ pāvako yathā ||
children.translated_text: angry like a fire blazing up, as if wishing to burn that army:

children.text: sampannaṃ rājyam icchaṃs tu vyaktaṃ prāpyābhiṣecanam
children.translated_text: 'Clearly <s>Bharata</s>, son of <s>Kaikeyī</s>, after obtaining consecration,

children.text: āvāṃ hantuṃ samabhyeti kaikeyyā bharataḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: desiring the prosperous kingdom, is coming here to kill us both.
There shines that very great and splendid tree,
the kovidāra banner on his chariot, radiant with its raised trunk.

children.text: bhajanty ete yathākāmam aśvān āruhya śīghragān
children.translated_text: These men, riding swift horses, serve him as they wish;

children.text: ete bhrājanti saṃhṛṣṭā gajān āruhya sādinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and these horsemen shine joyfully, mounted on elephants.
Taking up our bows, hero, let the two of us take refuge on the mountain.

children.text: api nau vaśam āgacchet kovidāradhvajo raṇe ||
children.translated_text: Perhaps the one with the kovidāra banner may come under our power in battle.

children.text: api drakṣyāmi bharataṃ yatkṛte vyasanaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: Perhaps I shall see <s>Bharata</s>, for whose sake this great calamity

children.text: tvayā rāghava samprāptaṃ sītayā ca mayā tathā ||
children.translated_text: has been reached by you, <s>Rāghava</s>, by <s>Sītā</s>, and by me as well.

children.text: yannimittaṃ bhavān rājyāc cyuto rāghava śāśvatāt
children.translated_text: For whose sake you, <s>Rāghava</s>, have been cast out from the eternal kingdom:

children.text: samprāpto 'yam arir vīra bharato vadhya eva me ||
children.translated_text: this enemy <s>Bharata</s> has arrived, hero, and he is fit to be slain by me.

children.text: bharatasya vadhe doṣaṃ nāhaṃ paśyāmi rāghava
children.translated_text: I see no fault, <s>Rāghava</s>, in killing <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: pūrvāpakāriṇāṃ tyāge na hy adharmo vidhīyate
children.translated_text: For no unrighteousness is prescribed in abandoning those who have first done harm;
when he is slain, rule the whole earth.

children.text: adya putraṃ hataṃ saṃkhye kaikeyī rājyakāmukā
children.translated_text: Today <s>Kaikeyī</s>, greedy for kingship, will see her son killed in battle

children.text: mayā paśyet suduḥkhārtā hastibhagnam iva drumam ||
children.translated_text: by me, stricken with great sorrow, like a tree broken by an elephant.
And I shall kill <s>Kaikeyī</s> too, along with her followers and relatives.
Let the earth today be freed from a great pollution.

children.text: adyemaṃ saṃyataṃ krodham asatkāraṃ ca mānada
children.translated_text: Today, giver of honor, this restrained anger and this insult
I shall release among the enemy troops like fire among dry thickets.
Today, splitting the bodies of enemies with sharp arrows,
I shall make this forest of <s>Citrakūṭa</s> sprinkled with blood.
Let wild beasts drag away elephants and horses whose hearts have been pierced by arrows,

children.text: śvāpadāḥ parikarṣantu narāṃś ca nihatān mayā ||
children.translated_text: and men too who have been slain by me.
In this great forest I shall have repaid my debt to my arrows and bow;

children.text: sasainyaṃ bharataṃ hatvā bhaviṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: after killing <s>Bharata</s> together with his army, I shall surely be so.'
But then <s>Rāma</s>, after calming <s>Saumitri</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, who was greatly enraged and overcome by anger,

children.text: rāmas tu parisāntvyātha vacanaṃ cedam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: spoke these words:

children.text: kim atra dhanuṣā kāryam asinā vā sacarmaṇā
children.translated_text: 'What need is there here for a bow, or for a sword and shield,
when mighty-armed and very wise <s>Bharata</s> has come himself?

children.text: prāptakālaṃ yad eṣo 'smān bharato draṣṭum icchati
children.translated_text: Since the time is right and this <s>Bharata</s> wishes to see us,

children.text: asmāsu manasāpy eṣa nāhitaṃ kiṃcid ācaret ||
children.translated_text: he would not do anything harmful to us even in thought.

children.text: vipriyaṃ kṛtapūrvaṃ te bharatena kadā na kim
children.translated_text: When has anything displeasing ever been done to you by <s>Bharata</s>?'

children.text: īdṛśaṃ vā bhayaṃ te 'dya bharataṃ yo 'tra śaṅkase ||
children.translated_text: What sort of fear is this that you now have, that you suspect <s>Bharata</s> here?

children.text: na hi te niṣṭhuraṃ vācyo bharato nāpriyaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: For <s>Bharata</s> must not be addressed harshly by you, nor with an unpleasant word.

children.text: ahaṃ hy apriyam uktaḥ syāṃ bharatasyāpriye kṛte ||
children.translated_text: For I myself would be the one spoken to unpleasantly, if something unpleasant were done to <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: kathaṃ nu putrāḥ pitaraṃ hanyuḥ kasyāṃcid āpadi
children.translated_text: How indeed could sons kill their father in some calamity?

children.text: bhrātā vā bhrātaraṃ hanyāt saumitre prāṇam ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or how could a brother kill his brother, O <s>Saumitri</s>, his very own life?

children.text: yadi rājyasya hetos tvam imāṃ vācaṃ prabhāṣase
children.translated_text: If you are saying this speech for the sake of the kingdom,

children.text: vakṣyāmi bharataṃ dṛṣṭvā rājyam asmai pradīyatām ||
children.translated_text: then, when I have seen <s>Bharata</s>, I shall say, 'Let the kingdom be given to him.'

children.text: ucyamāno hi bharato mayā lakṣmaṇa tattvataḥ
children.translated_text: For when <s>Bharata</s> is told by me truly, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: rājyam asmai prayaccheti bāḍham ity eva vakṣyati ||
children.translated_text: 'Give the kingdom to him,' he will say only, 'Certainly.'

children.text: tathokto dharmaśīlena bhrātrā tasya hite rataḥ
children.translated_text: When he had been addressed in this way by his righteous brother, who was devoted to his welfare,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, from shame, seemed to withdraw into his own limbs.

children.text: vrīḍitaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāghavaḥ pratyuvāca ha
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> ashamed, <s>Rāghava</s> spoke again:

children.text: eṣa manye mahābāhur ihāsmān draṣṭum āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: I think this mighty-armed one has come here to see us.
Thinking over our dwelling in the forest, he will take us back home,
or else he will take this <s>Vaidehī</s>, who is accustomed to the utmost happiness.
Those two are becoming visible, well-bred, delightful,
equal to the speed of the wind, O hero, swift, the finest of horses.
And there, at the head of the army, that very great-bodied elephant is shaking,

children.text: nāgaḥ śatruṃjayo nāma vṛddhas tātasya dhīmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: named <s>Śatruṃjaya</s>, the old elephant of my wise father.

children.text: avatīrya tu sālāgrāt tasmāt sa samitiṃjayaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, descending from the top of that sala tree, the conqueror in battle,

children.text: lakṣmaṇaḥ prāñjalir bhūtvā tasthau rāmasya pārśvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, with joined palms, stood at <s>Rāma</s>'s side.

children.text: bharatenātha saṃdiṣṭā sammardo na bhaved iti
children.translated_text: Then, instructed by <s>Bharata</s> that there should be no crowding,
he arranged the army's camp all around that mountain.
That army of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s>, extending a yojana and a half,
settled beside the mountain, surrounding it, crowded with elephants, horses, and chariots.

children.text: sā citrakūṭe bharatena senā dharmaṃ puraskṛtya vidhūya darpam
children.translated_text: On <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, that army, led by prudent <s>Bharata</s>, putting righteousness first and casting off pride,
shone forth for the purpose of winning the favor of the delight of the <s>Raghus</s>.

children.text: niveśya senāṃ tu vibhuḥ padbhyāṃ pādavatāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: After stationing the army, the lord, best of those who go on foot,
desired to approach <s>Kākutstha</s>, who was obedient to his elders.
When the army had just been stationed properly in its places, with discipline,

children.text: bharato bhrātaraṃ vākyaṃ śatrughnam idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s> spoke this word to his brother <s>Śatrughna</s>:

children.text: kṣipraṃ vanam idaṃ saumya narasaṃghaiḥ samantataḥ
children.translated_text: Quickly, dear one, you should search this forest on every side with groups of men,

children.text: lubdhaiś ca sahitair ebhis tvam anveṣitum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: together with these hunters as well.

children.text: yāvan na rāmaṃ drakṣyāmi lakṣmaṇaṃ vā mahābalam
children.translated_text: Until I see <s>Rāma</s>, or mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: vaidehīṃ vā mahābhāgāṃ na me śāntir bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: or the greatly fortunate <s>Vaidehī</s>, there will be no peace for me.

children.text: yāvan na candrasaṃkāśaṃ drakṣyāmi śubham ānanam
children.translated_text: Until I see the auspicious face of my brother, shining like the moon,

children.text: bhrātuḥ padmapalāśākṣaṃ na me śāntir bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: lotus-petal-eyed, there will be no peace for me.
Until I bear on my head my brother's feet, marked with the signs of sovereignty,

children.text: śirasā dhārayiṣyāmi na me śāntir bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: there will be no peace for me.

children.text: yāvan na rājye rājyārhaḥ pitṛpaitāmahe sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Until he who is worthy of kingship stands in the kingdom inherited from father and grandfather,
moistened with the waters of consecration, there will be no peace for me.
Highly blessed and fulfilled is <s>Vaidehī</s>, daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,
since she follows as husband the lord of the earth bounded by the ocean.
Fortunate is that <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, that mountain like the king of mountains,

children.text: yasmin vasati kākutsthaḥ kubera iva nandane ||
children.translated_text: where <s>Kākutstha</s> dwells like <s>Kubera</s> in <s>Nandana</s>.
This difficult forest, frequented by wild beasts, has achieved its purpose,

children.text: yad adhyāste mahātejā rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: because mighty <s>Rāma</s>, best of weapon-bearers, inhabits it.
Having spoken thus, the mighty <s>Bharata</s>, bull among men,

children.text: padbhyām eva mahātejāḥ praviveśa mahad vanam ||
children.translated_text: entered the great forest on foot alone, full of splendor.
He, the best of speakers, went through the middle of those clusters of trees
that had grown on the mountain slopes, their tops in blossom.

children.text: sa gireś citrakūṭasya sālam āsādya puṣpitam
children.translated_text: Coming to a flowering sala tree on <s>Citrakūṭa</s> mountain,
he saw the raised banner of the fire belonging to <s>Rāma</s>'s hermitage.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā bharataḥ śrīmān mumoda sahabāndhavaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing it, illustrious <s>Bharata</s> rejoiced along with his kinsmen;

children.text: atra rāma iti jñātvā gataḥ pāram ivāmbhasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: knowing, '<s>Rāma</s> is here,' he was like one who had reached the far shore of the water.

children.text: sa citrakūṭe tu girau niśāmya rāmāśramaṃ puṇyajanopapannam
children.translated_text: Then on <s>Citrakūṭa</s> mountain, perceiving <s>Rāma</s>'s hermitage, attended by holy people,

children.text: guhena sārdhaṃ tvarito jagāma punar niveśyaiva camūṃ mahātmā ||
children.translated_text: the great-souled one, after stationing the army again, went quickly with <s>Guha</s>.

children.text: niviṣṭāyāṃ tu senāyām utsuko bharatas tadā
children.translated_text: When the army had been encamped, eager <s>Bharata</s> then
went to see his brother, pointing the way to <s>Śatrughna</s>.

children.text: ṛṣiṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ saṃdiśya mātṝn me śīghram ānaya
children.translated_text: Instructing the sage <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, 'Bring my mothers quickly,'

children.text: iti tvaritam agre sa jagāma guruvatsalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he, devoted to his elders, went ahead in haste.

children.text: sumantras tv api śatrughnam adūrād anvapadyata
children.translated_text: <s>Sumantra</s> too followed <s>Śatrughna</s> from not far away;
the thirst born of seeing <s>Rāma</s> was his as it was <s>Bharata</s>'s.
Then, as he went, <s>Bharata</s> saw, standing in the ascetic settlement,

children.text: bhrātuḥ parṇakuṭīṃ śrīmān uṭajaṃ ca dadarśa ha ||
children.translated_text: his brother's leaf-hut, splendid, and the cottage as well.

children.text: śālāyās tv agratas tasyā dadarśa bharatas tadā
children.translated_text: Then in front of that hut <s>Bharata</s> saw
pieces of wood split apart and flowers gathered.

children.text: dadarśa ca vane tasmin mahataḥ saṃcayān kṛtān
children.translated_text: And in that forest he saw great heaps made
from the dung of deer and buffaloes, for the sake of warmth.

children.text: gacchan eva mahābāhur dyutimān bharatas tadā
children.translated_text: As he went, mighty-armed, radiant <s>Bharata</s> then,

children.text: śatrughnaṃ cābravīddhṛṣṭas tān amātyāṃś ca sarvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: delighted, spoke to <s>Śatrughna</s> and to all those ministers:

children.text: manye prāptāḥ sma taṃ deśaṃ bharadvājo yam abravīt
children.translated_text: I think we have reached the place of which <s>Bharadvāja</s> spoke.

children.text: nātidūre hi manye 'haṃ nadīṃ mandākinīm itaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For I think the river <s>Mandākinī</s> is not very far from here.

children.text: uccair baddhāni cīrāṇi lakṣmaṇena bhaved ayam
children.translated_text: And these bark-cloths tied high up must have been by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>...
The path had been marked with signs by one who wished to travel at an untimely hour.
And this is the track of lofty-tusked, powerful elephants,
traversed on the mountain-side as they roared at one another.

children.text: yam evādhātum icchanti tāpasāḥ satataṃ vane
children.translated_text: The fire which ascetics in the forest always wish to kindle,
its dense smoke is visible there, dark in its course.
Here, rejoicing, I shall see the tiger among men, who honors his elders,

children.text: āryaṃ drakṣyāmi saṃhṛṣṭo maharṣim iva rāghavam ||
children.translated_text: the noble <s>Rāghava</s>, like a great seer.

children.text: atha gatvā muhūrtaṃ tu citrakūṭaṃ sa rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after going for a short while to <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, that <s>Rāghava</s>

children.text: mandākinīm anuprāptas taṃ janaṃ cedam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: reached the <s>Mandākinī</s> and spoke these words to the people:
'The tiger among men, the lord of men, sits on the ground, delighting in a hero's posture;

children.text: janendro nirjanaṃ prāpya dhiṅme janma sajīvitam ||
children.translated_text: having come to a lonely place. Shame on my birth and my life.
On my account the lord of the world, of great splendor, has fallen into distress;

children.text: sarvān kāmān parityajya vane vasati rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: abandoning all pleasures, <s>Rāghava</s> dwells in the forest.
Reviled by the world for this, today, seeking favor at his feet,

children.text: rāmasya nipatiṣyāmi sītāyāś ca punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall fall again and again at the feet of <s>Rāma</s> and of <s>Sītā</s>.'

children.text: evaṃ sa vilapaṃs tasmin vane daśarathātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus lamenting in that forest, the son of <s>Daśaratha</s>
saw a great, holy, delightful leaf-hut.
It was covered with many leaves of sāla, tāla, and aśvakarṇa trees,
broad and strewn with soft kuśa grass, like an altar at a sacrifice.
It was adorned with bows resembling <s>Śakra</s>'s weapon, able to bear heavy strain,
gold-backed, very strong, and capable of afflicting enemies.
It was adorned with dreadful arrows kept in quivers, shining like rays of the sun,
like <s>Bhogavatī</s> with serpents whose faces blaze.
It shone with two swords in great silver sheaths,
and was adorned also with two shields variegated with spots of gold.
With fastened finger-guards of iguana-skin, variegated and ornamented with gold,
it was unassailable by hosts of foes, like a lion's cave by deer.
There in <s>Rāma</s>'s dwelling <s>Bharata</s> saw a broad, holy altar,
sloping east and north, with its fire blazing brightly.

children.text: nirīkṣya sa muhūrtaṃ tu dadarśa bharato gurum
children.translated_text: After looking for a moment, <s>Bharata</s> saw his revered elder,
<s>Rāma</s>, seated in the hut, wearing a mass of matted hair.
He saw <s>Rāma</s> seated there, wearing a black antelope-skin,
clothed in bark and bast garments, like a fire close at hand.
He had the shoulders of a lion, mighty arms, and eyes like lotuses;
he was the lord of the earth bounded by the oceans, walking in <s>dharma</s>.
The mighty-armed one sat like eternal <s>Brahmā</s>
on bare ground strewn with darbha grass, together with <s>Sītā</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Seeing him, illustrious <s>Bharata</s>, overwhelmed by grief and bewilderment,
rushed toward him, righteous <s>Bharata</s>, son of <s>Kaikayī</s>.
And seeing him, afflicted, he lamented in a voice choked with tears;
unable to maintain his composure, he spoke these words:

children.text: yaḥ saṃsadi prakṛtibhir bhaved yukta upāsitum
children.translated_text: 'He who should be attended in assembly by his ministers,

children.text: vanyair mṛgair upāsīnaḥ so 'yam āste mamāgrajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this elder brother of mine sits here attended by wild deer.
That great-souled one, who deserved garments worth many thousands,

children.text: mṛgājine so 'yam iha pravaste dharmam ācaran ||
children.translated_text: wears a deer-skin here, practicing <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: adhārayad yo vividhāś citrāḥ sumanasas tadā
children.translated_text: He who then wore many kinds of bright flowers,

children.text: so 'yaṃ jaṭābhāram imaṃ sahate rāghavaḥ katham ||
children.translated_text: how does this <s>Rāghava</s> endure this heavy mass of matted hair?

children.text: yasya yajñair yathādiṣṭair yukto dharmasya saṃcayaḥ
children.translated_text: He whose store of <s>dharma</s> was joined with sacrifices performed as prescribed
now seeks <s>dharma</s> born from bodily hardship.
He whose limbs were treated with costly sandal-paste,

children.text: malena tasyāṅgam idaṃ katham āryasya sevyate ||
children.translated_text: how are these limbs of the noble one now treated with dirt?

children.text: mannimittam idaṃ duḥkhaṃ prāpto rāmaḥ sukhocitaḥ
children.translated_text: Because of me, <s>Rāma</s>, who deserved happiness, has come to this sorrow.
Shame on my cruel life, condemned by the world.'
Thus lamenting, wretched, his lotus-face covered with sweat,

children.text: pādāv aprāpya rāmasya papāta bharato rudan ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s> fell down weeping before he could reach <s>Rāma</s>'s feet.
Scorched by grief, <s>Bharata</s>, the mighty royal prince,

children.text: uktvāryeti sakṛd dīnaṃ punar novāca kiṃcana ||
children.translated_text: said piteously once, 'Noble one!' and then said nothing more.
His throat was blocked by tears, and, looking at glorious <s>Rāma</s>,
he cried only, 'Noble one!' and after that could not speak.

children.text: śatrughnaś cāpi rāmasya vavande caraṇau rudan
children.translated_text: <s>Śatrughna</s> too, weeping, bowed to <s>Rāma</s>'s feet;

children.text: tāv ubhau sa samāliṅgya rāmo 'py aśrūṇy avartayat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> embraced them both and himself shed tears.

children.text: tataḥ sumantreṇa guhena caiva samīyatū rājasutāv araṇye
children.translated_text: Then the two royal sons came together in the forest with <s>Sumantra</s> and <s>Guha</s>,

children.text: divākaraś caiva niśākaraś ca yathāmbare śukrabṛhaspatibhyām ||
children.translated_text: like the sun and the moon in the sky together with <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

children.text: tān pārthivān vāraṇayūthapābhān samāgatāṃs tatra mahaty araṇye
children.translated_text: Seeing those princes, like leaders of elephant herds, gathered there in the great forest,

children.text: vanaukasas te 'pi samīkṣya sarve 'py aśrūṇy amuñcan pravihāya harṣam ||
children.translated_text: all the forest-dwellers too gave up joy and shed tears.

children.text: āghrāya rāmas taṃ mūrdhni pariṣvajya ca rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s>, that <s>Rāghava</s>, smelled him on the head and embraced him;
placing <s>Bharata</s> on his lap, composed, he questioned him:

children.text: kva nu te 'bhūt pitā tāta yad araṇyaṃ tvam āgataḥ
children.translated_text: 'What then has become of your father, dear boy, that you have come to the forest?

children.text: na hi tvaṃ jīvatas tasya vanam āgantum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: For while he is alive, you ought not to come to the forest.

children.text: cirasya bata paśyāmi dūrād bharatam āgatam
children.translated_text: After a long time indeed I see <s>Bharata</s>, come from afar;

children.text: duṣpratīkam araṇye 'smin kiṃ tāta vanam āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: hard to recognize in this forest. Why, dear boy, have you come to the forest?
Is King <s>Daśaratha</s>, true to his promise, in good health,
the performer of rājasūyas and aśvamedhas, firmly resolved in <s>dharma</s>?

children.text: sa kaccid brāhmaṇo vidvān dharmanityo mahādyutiḥ
children.translated_text: And is that learned brāhmaṇa, ever devoted to <s>dharma</s> and very splendid...
Dear one, is the preceptor of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s> honored as is proper?

children.text: tāta kaccic ca kausalyā sumitrā ca prajāvatī
children.translated_text: Dear one, are <s>Kausalyā</s> and <s>Sumitrā</s>, blessed with children, well?

children.text: sukhinī kaccid āryā ca devī nandati kaikayī ||
children.translated_text: And is the noble queen <s>Kaikayī</s> happy and rejoicing?
Is your priest disciplined, well-born, and very learned,
free from envy, watchful, and honored by you?

children.text: kaccid agniṣu te yukto vidhijño matimān ṛjuḥ
children.translated_text: Is the man appointed over your sacred fires knowledgeable in the rites, wise, and upright?

children.text: hutaṃ ca hoṣyamāṇaṃ ca kāle vedayate sadā ||
children.translated_text: Does he always inform you at the proper time of what has been offered and what is yet to be offered?
Dear one, do you esteem <s>Sudhanvan</s> as your instructor, endowed with the finest bows and missiles

children.text: sudhanvānam upādhyāyaṃ kaccit tvaṃ tāta manyase ||
children.translated_text: and thoroughly skilled in <s>arthaśāstra</s> (the science of policy and material welfare)?
Dear one, have you made men your ministers who are equal to yourself, heroic, learned, self-controlled,

children.text: kulīnāś ceṅgitajñāś ca kṛtās te tāta mantriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: of noble birth, and able to understand gestures and intentions?

children.text: mantro vijayamūlaṃ hi rājñāṃ bhavati rāghava
children.translated_text: For counsel, <s>Rāghava</s>, is the root of victory for kings,
when it is well guarded by ministers who keep counsel and know the śāstras.

children.text: kaccin nidrāvaśaṃ naiṣi kaccit kāle vibudhyase
children.translated_text: Do you not fall under the power of sleep, and do you wake at the proper time?
And in the later watches of the night, do you reflect on skill in affairs?

children.text: kaccin mantrayase naikaḥ kaccin na bahubhiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Do you not deliberate alone, and not together with too many?

children.text: kaccit te mantrito mantro rāṣṭraṃ na paridhāvati ||
children.translated_text: Once your plan has been deliberated, does it not run through the kingdom?
Having decided on an undertaking with small cost and great result,

children.text: kṣipram ārabhase kartuṃ na dīrghayasi rāghava ||
children.translated_text: do you begin it quickly, <s>Rāghava</s>, and not delay it?

children.text: kaccit tu sukṛtāny eva kṛtarūpāṇi vā punaḥ
children.translated_text: Do other kings learn only of your well-executed actions,

children.text: vidus te sarvakāryāṇi na kartavyāni pārthivāḥ ||
children.translated_text: or of those already brought into form, and not of what is still to be done?

children.text: kaccin na tarkair yuktvā vā ye cāpy aparikīrtitāḥ
children.translated_text: Dear one, is the counsel discussed by you or by your ministers not discovered

children.text: tvayā vā tava vāmātyair budhyate tāta mantritam ||
children.translated_text: through reasoning, inference, or by those who are otherwise unmentioned?

children.text: kaccit sahasrān mūrkhāṇām ekam icchasi paṇḍitam
children.translated_text: Do you prefer one wise man to a thousand fools?

children.text: paṇḍito hy arthakṛcchreṣu kuryān niḥśreyasaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: For a wise man, in difficulties involving interests, can bring about great welfare.

children.text: sahasrāṇy api mūrkhāṇāṃ yady upāste mahīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Even if a lord of the earth attends upon thousands of fools,
or even tens of thousands, there is no help among them.

children.text: eko 'py amātyo medhāvī śūro dakṣo vicakṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Even a single intelligent minister, heroic, capable, and discerning,

children.text: rājānaṃ rājamātraṃ vā prāpayen mahatīṃ śriyam ||
children.translated_text: can bring a king, or even one only nominally a king, to great prosperity.

children.text: kaccin mukhyā mahatsv eva madhyameṣu ca madhyamāḥ
children.translated_text: Are the chief servants assigned to the chief tasks, the middling to middling tasks,

children.text: jaghanyāś ca jaghanyeṣu bhṛtyāḥ karmasu yojitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the lowest servants to the lowest tasks?
Do you appoint ministers who have passed tests, who are pure, and whose fathers and grandfathers served before them,

children.text: śreṣṭhāñ śreṣṭheṣu kaccit tvaṃ niyojayasi karmasu ||
children.translated_text: the best men to the best duties?

children.text: kaccit tvāṃ nāvajānanti yājakāḥ patitaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: Do sacrificial priests not despise you as one fallen,
as they despise one who exacts harsh gifts or one who is excessively desirous of women?
Whoever does not kill a physician skilled in expedients, one who delights in corrupting servants,

children.text: śūram aiśvaryakāmaṃ ca yo na hanti sa vadhyate ||
children.translated_text: or a brave man who desires sovereignty, is himself killed.

children.text: kaccid dhṛṣṭaś ca śūraś ca dhṛtimān matimāñ śuciḥ
children.translated_text: Have you appointed as commander a man who is bold, heroic, steadfast, intelligent, pure,

children.text: kulīnaś cānuraktaś ca dakṣaḥ senāpatiḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: noble-born, loyal, and capable?

children.text: balavantaś ca kaccit te mukhyā yuddhaviśāradāḥ
children.translated_text: Are your leading warriors strong and skilled in battle,
men of proven achievements and valor, honored by you with proper respect?

children.text: kaccid balasya bhaktaṃ ca vetanaṃ ca yathocitam
children.translated_text: Do you give the army its rations and pay, as appropriate,
at the time when they are due, without delay?
For when the time for rations and wages is exceeded, servants

children.text: bhartuḥ kupyanti duṣyanti so 'narthaḥ sumahān smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: become angry with their master and turn hostile; that is remembered as a very great misfortune.
Are all the well-born men, especially the principal ones, attached to you?
Do they, intent upon your purposes, give up their very lives for your sake?
<s>Bharata</s>, have you appointed as your envoy a local man who is learned, courteous, quick-witted,

children.text: yathoktavādī dūtas te kṛto bharata paṇḍitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: wise, and one who speaks exactly as instructed?

children.text: kaccid aṣṭādaśāny eṣu svapakṣe daśa pañca ca
children.translated_text: Do you learn the offices among these eighteen on the enemy's side, and the fifteen on your own side,

children.text: tribhis tribhir avijñātair vetsi tīrthāni cārakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: through spies, three by three, who are unknown to one another?

children.text: kaccid vyapāstān ahitān pratiyātāṃś ca sarvadā
children.translated_text: Crusher of enemies, do you always keep watch over hostile men who have been driven away and have returned,
without despising them because they are weak?

children.text: kaccin na lokāyatikān brāhmaṇāṃs tāta sevase
children.translated_text: Dear one, do you not associate with <s>Lokāyatika</s> brahmins?
For these fools, imagining themselves learned, are skilled only in harm.
Though the principal <s>dharmaśāstras</s> (texts on sacred law) exist,

children.text: buddhimān vīkṣikīṃ prāpya nirarthaṃ pravadanti te ||
children.translated_text: those dull-witted men, having taken up dialectical reasoning, speak uselessly.

children.text: vīrair adhyuṣitāṃ pūrvam asmākaṃ tāta pūrvakaiḥ
children.translated_text: Dear one, do you protect <s>Ayodhyā</s>, truly named, formerly inhabited by our heroic ancestors,
with strong gates and filled with elephants, horses, and chariots?
It is surrounded by thousands of noble people, brahmins, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas,
always devoted to their own duties, self-controlled, and full of high energy.
It is encircled by palaces of many forms and crowded with physicians;
do you protect prosperous, thriving <s>Ayodhyā</s>?
Is your district adorned with hundreds of shrines, crowded with well-settled people,
and beautified with temples, water-stations, and ponds?
Is it graced by joyful men and women and by gatherings and festivals,
with well-ploughed boundaries, rich in cattle, and free from violence?
Is the countryside lovely, not dependent on rain alone, and free from wild beasts?
<s>Rāghava</s>, does the prosperous realm dwell in happiness?
Are all those dear to you who live by agriculture and cattle-keeping?

children.text: vārttāyāṃ saṃśritas tāta loko hi sukham edhate ||
children.translated_text: For the world, dear one, prospers happily when supported by <s>vārttā</s> (agriculture, cattle, and trade).

children.text: teṣāṃ guptiparīhāraiḥ kaccit te bharaṇaṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: Have you made provision for their maintenance through protection and relief from burdens?

children.text: rakṣyā hi rājñā dharmeṇa sarve viṣayavāsinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For all inhabitants of the realm must be protected by the king according to <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: kaccit striyaḥ sāntvayasi kaccit tāś ca surakṣitāḥ
children.translated_text: Do you conciliate women, and are they well protected?

children.text: kaccin na śraddadhāsyāsāṃ kaccid guhyaṃ na bhāṣase ||
children.translated_text: Do you not place trust in them, and do you not tell them secrets?

children.text: kaccin nāgavanaṃ guptaṃ kuñjarāṇāṃ ca tṛpyasi
children.translated_text: Is the elephant forest guarded, and are you attentive to the elephants?
Do you regularly show yourself, adorned, to the people,
rising early in the morning, O royal prince, on the great road?
Are all the forts fully supplied with wealth, grain, weapons, and water,
and also with engines, artisans, and archers?

children.text: āyas te vipulaḥ kaccit kaccid alpataro vyayaḥ
children.translated_text: Is your income abundant, and is your expenditure smaller?

children.text: apātreṣu na te kaccit kośo gacchati rāghava ||
children.translated_text: Does your treasury not go to unworthy recipients, O <s>Rāghava</s>?
Does your expenditure go for the gods, for the ancestors, and for brahmins and guests,

children.text: yodheṣu mitravargeṣu kaccid gacchati te vyayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and for warriors and groups of friends?
Is no noble man of pure character, untainted by the act of theft,

children.text: apṛṣṭaḥ śāstrakuśalair na lobhād badhyate śuciḥ ||
children.translated_text: bound through greed while innocent, without being examined by those skilled in the śāstras?

children.text: gṛhītaś caiva pṛṣṭaś ca kāle dṛṣṭaḥ sakāraṇaḥ
children.translated_text: And when a thief has been seized, questioned, and seen at the proper time with due cause,

children.text: kaccin na mucyate coro dhanalobhān nararṣabha ||
children.translated_text: is he not released through greed for money, bull among men?

children.text: vyasane kaccid āḍhyasya durgatasya ca rāghava
children.translated_text: In a misfortune involving a rich man or a destitute man, O <s>Rāghava</s>,
do your learned ministers view the matter without partiality?
The tears that fall from those who have been falsely accused, O <s>Rāghava</s>,
destroy the sons and cattle of a ruler who punishes for the sake of favor.

children.text: kaccid vṛddhāṃś ca bālāṃś ca vaidyamukhyāṃś ca rāghava
children.translated_text: Do you seek to support the old, the young, and the chief physicians, O <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: dānena manasā vācā tribhir etair bubhūṣase ||
children.translated_text: by these three: gift, thought, and speech?

children.text: kaccid gurūṃś ca vṛddhāṃś ca tāpasān devatātithīn
children.translated_text: Do you honor teachers, elders, ascetics, deities, guests,

children.text: caityāṃś ca sarvān siddhārthān brāhmaṇāṃś ca namasyasi ||
children.translated_text: all shrines, those who have attained their aims, and brahmins?

children.text: kaccid arthena vā dharmaṃ dharmaṃ dharmeṇa vā punaḥ
children.translated_text: Do you not obstruct <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) for the sake of wealth, or wealth again for the sake of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: ubhau vā prītilobhena kāmena na vibādhase ||
children.translated_text: or both of them through desire born of affection and greed?

children.text: kaccid arthaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca jayatāṃ vara
children.translated_text: O best of conquerors, do you attend to wealth, <s>dharma</s>, and desire,

children.text: vibhajya kāle kālajña sarvān bharata sevase ||
children.translated_text: dividing them by the proper time, O <s>Bharata</s>, knower of time?
Do the brahmins, learned in the meaning of all śāstras, wish you welfare,
O very wise one, together with the townspeople and countryfolk?
Atheism, falsehood, anger, negligence, procrastination,
failure to meet the wise, laziness, enslavement to the five senses,
thinking through matters alone, consulting with those who do not understand policy,
failing to begin what has been decided, failing to guard counsel,
failing to perform auspicious rites, and rising up against everything:

children.text: kaccit tvaṃ varjayasy etān rājadoṣāṃś caturdaśa ||
children.translated_text: do you avoid these fourteen faults of kings?

children.text: kaccit svādukṛtaṃ bhojyam eko nāśnāsi rāghava
children.translated_text: You do not eat well-prepared, tasty food alone, do you, O <s>Rāghava</s>?
Do you share it with friends who are hoping for it?

children.text: rāmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā bharataḥ pratyuvāca ha
children.translated_text: Having heard <s>Rāma</s>'s words, <s>Bharata</s> replied,

children.text: kiṃ me dharmād vihīnasya rājadharmaḥ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: What will royal duty do for me, who am bereft of <s>dharma</s>?
This is the eternal <s>dharma</s>, always established among us, bull among men:

children.text: jyeṣṭhaputre sthite rājan na kanīyān bhaven nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when the eldest son is living, O king, the younger must not become king.

children.text: sa samṛddhāṃ mayā sārdham ayodhyāṃ gaccha rāghava
children.translated_text: Therefore go to prosperous <s>Ayodhyā</s> together with me, O <s>Rāghava</s>,
and consecrate yourself for the welfare of this family and of us.

children.text: rājānaṃ mānuṣaṃ prāhur devatve saṃmato mama
children.translated_text: They call a king human, but he is regarded by me as divine
whose conduct, joined with <s>dharma</s> and wealth, they call superhuman.

children.text: kekayasthe ca mayi tu tvayi cāraṇyam āśrite
children.translated_text: While I was in the land of the <s>Kekayas</s> and you had gone to the forest,

children.text: divam ārya gato rājā yāyajūkaḥ satāṃ mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: O noble one, the king, devoted to sacrifice and honored by the good, went to heaven.
Rise, tiger among men; let the water-offering for our father be performed.

children.text: ahaṃ cāyaṃ ca śatrughnaḥ pūrvam eva kṛtodakau ||
children.translated_text: I and this <s>Śatrughna</s> have already offered the water before.

children.text: priyeṇa kila dattaṃ hi pitṛlokeṣu rāghava
children.translated_text: For they say that what is given in the world of the fathers by a beloved son, O <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: akṣayyaṃ bhavatīty āhur bhavāṃś caiva pituḥ priyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: becomes imperishable, and you were especially dear to our father.

children.text: tāṃ śrutvā karuṇāṃ vācaṃ pitur maraṇasaṃhitām
children.translated_text: Hearing those piteous words, bound up with his father's death,
spoken by <s>Bharata</s>, <s>Rāghava</s> lost consciousness.
When <s>Rāma</s>, scorcher of foes, received the thunderbolt of speech spoken by <s>Bharata</s>, painful to hear,

children.text: pragṛhya bāhū rāmo vai puṣpitāgro yathā drumaḥ
children.translated_text: he raised his arms, like a tree with a flowering top,

children.text: vane paraśunā kṛttas tathā bhuvi papāta ha ||
children.translated_text: and fell to the ground as if cut down by an axe in the forest.

children.text: tathā hi patitaṃ rāmaṃ jagatyāṃ jagatīpatim
children.translated_text: As <s>Rāma</s>, lord of the world, had fallen so upon the earth,
like an elephant asleep, exhausted after breaking down a riverbank,
his brothers, weeping on every side, together with <s>Vaidehī</s>,

children.text: rudantaḥ saha vaidehyā siṣicuḥ salilena vai ||
children.translated_text: sprinkled that great archer, wholly wasted by grief, with water.

children.text: sa tu saṃjñāṃ punar labdhvā netrābhyām āsram utsṛjan
children.translated_text: Then, regaining consciousness and shedding tears from his eyes,
<s>Kākutstha</s> began to speak at length in a piteous way.

children.text: kiṃ nu tasya mayā kāryaṃ durjātena mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: What use am I, ill-born as I am, to that great-souled one,

children.text: yo mṛto mama śokena na mayā cāpi saṃskṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: who died from grief for me and was not even given his rites by me?

children.text: aho bharata siddhārtho yena rājā tvayānagha
children.translated_text: Ah, <s>Bharata</s>, you are fortunate, sinless one, since through you
and through <s>Śatrughna</s> the king was honored in all the rites for the dead.
Even when my forest exile is ended, I do not have the heart to go to <s>Ayodhyā</s>,
bereft of its lord, distracted, and deprived of the king.
When I have completed my forest exile and my father has gone to the other world,

children.text: ko nu śāsiṣyati punas tāte lokāntaraṃ gate ||
children.translated_text: who, O scorcher of foes, will command me again in <s>Ayodhyā</s>?

children.text: purā prekṣya suvṛttaṃ māṃ pitā yāny āha sāntvayan
children.translated_text: Formerly, seeing me well behaved, my father would speak comforting

children.text: vākyāni tāni śroṣyāmi kutaḥ karṇasukhāny aham ||
children.translated_text: words; from where shall I now hear those pleasing words for the ear?

children.text: evam uktvā sa bharataṃ bhāryām abhyetya rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to <s>Bharata</s>, <s>Rāghava</s> approached his wife
and, afflicted with grief, spoke to her whose face was like the full moon:

children.text: sīte mṛtas te śvaśuraḥ pitrā hīno 'si lakṣmaṇa
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s>, your father-in-law is dead; <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, you are bereft of your father.
<s>Bharata</s> tells of this sorrow, that the lord of the earth has gone to heaven.

children.text: sāntvayitvā tu tāṃ rāmo rudantīṃ janakātmajām
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s>, after consoling that weeping daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,

children.text: uvāca lakṣmaṇaṃ tatra duḥkhito duḥkhitaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, distressed, he spoke these sorrowful words to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:
Bring the oil-cake of iṅgudī fruit, and bring the bark-cloth upper garment.
For the sake of the water-rite for my great-souled father, I shall go.

children.text: sītā purastād vrajatu tvam enām abhito vraja
children.translated_text: Let <s>Sītā</s> go in front, and you go close beside her.

children.text: ahaṃ paścād gamiṣyāmi gatir hy eṣā sudāruṇā ||
children.translated_text: I shall go behind; for this course is very terrible.
Then <s>Sumantra</s>, always attending upon them, self-possessed and very wise,

children.text: mṛdur dāntaś ca śāntaś ca rāme ca dṛḍhabhaktimān ||
children.translated_text: gentle, restrained, peaceful, and firmly devoted to <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: sumantras tair nṛpasutaiḥ sārdham āśvāsya rāghavam
children.translated_text: together with those royal sons, after comforting <s>Rāghava</s>,
led him down, supporting him, to the auspicious river <s>Mandākinī</s>.

children.text: te sutīrthāṃ tataḥ kṛcchrād upāgamya yaśasvinaḥ
children.translated_text: Then those illustrious men, with difficulty, approached the well-descended bathing place
on the beautiful river <s>Mandākinī</s>, whose groves were always in flower.
Having reached the auspicious, mudless ford with its swift current,

children.text: siṣicus tūdakaṃ rājñe tata etad bhavatv iti ||
children.translated_text: they sprinkled water for the king, saying, 'May this be for him.'
Then the lord of the earth, taking his joined palms filled with water,

children.text: diśaṃ yāmyām abhimukho rudan vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: faced the southern quarter and, weeping, spoke these words:

children.text: etat te rājaśārdūla vimalaṃ toyam akṣayam
children.translated_text: May this pure and unfailing water, O tiger among kings,
given today by me, reach you who have gone to the world of the ancestors.
Then that radiant <s>Rāghava</s>, having come back up from the bank of the <s>Mandākinī</s>,

children.text: pituś cakāra tejasvī nivāpaṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: made the <s>nivāpa</s> (funeral oblation) for his father together with his brothers.
On a spread of <s>darbha</s> grass he placed iṅgudī oil-cake mixed with jujube berries,

children.text: nyasya rāmaḥ suduḥkhārto rudan vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Rāma</s>, deeply afflicted with grief, wept and spoke these words:

children.text: idaṃ bhuṅkṣva mahārāja prīto yadaśanā vayam
children.translated_text: Eat this, great king, content with the food by which we ourselves live.

children.text: yadannaḥ puruṣo bhavati tadannās tasya devatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever food a man has, that same food belongs to his deities and ancestors.
Then, by that same path, having climbed back up from the riverbank,
the tiger among men ascended the mountain with its lovely slopes.
Then, reaching the doorway of the leaf-hut, the lord of the world
took both <s>Bharata</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> in his hands.

children.text: teṣāṃ tu rudatāṃ śabdāt pratiśrutkābhavad girau
children.translated_text: From the sound of their weeping there arose an echo on the mountain,

children.text: bhrātṝṇāṃ saha vaidehyā siṃhānāṃ nardatām iva ||
children.translated_text: as if of lions roaring, the brothers being together with <s>Vaidehī</s>.
Perceiving the tumultuous sound, <s>Bharata</s>'s frightened soldiers

children.text: abruvaṃś cāpi rāmeṇa bharataḥ saṃgato dhruvam
children.translated_text: said, '<s>Bharata</s> has surely met with <s>Rāma</s>;',

children.text: teṣām eva mahāñ śabdaḥ śocatāṃ pitaraṃ mṛtam ||
children.translated_text: 'That is the great sound of those very men grieving for their dead father.'

children.text: atha vāsān parityajya taṃ sarve 'bhimukhāḥ svanam
children.translated_text: Then all of them, leaving their quarters, turned toward that sound,
and, of one mind, they ran from their various places and went there.

children.text: hayair anye gajair anye rathair anye svalaṃkṛtaiḥ
children.translated_text: Some went by horses, some by elephants, and some by finely adorned chariots,

children.text: sukumārās tathaivānye padbhir eva narā yayuḥ ||
children.translated_text: while other delicate men went on foot alone.
All the people, eager to see <s>Rāma</s>, who had been away only a short time as though he had been gone long,
went suddenly to the hermitage.

children.text: bhrātṝṇāṃ tvaritās te tu draṣṭukāmāḥ samāgamam
children.translated_text: Those men, hastening and eager to see the meeting of the brothers,
went in many kinds of vehicles, amid the crush of hooves and wheel-rims.
That ground, struck by many vehicles and by hooves and wheel-rims,
sent up a tumultuous sound, like the sky at the gathering of clouds.
Frightened by that sound, elephants surrounded by cow-elephants,

children.text: āvāsayanto gandhena jagmur anyad vanaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: scenting the region with their odor, went from there to another forest.
Boars, deer, lions, buffaloes, bears, and monkeys,
together with tigers, gokarṇas, gavayas, and spotted deer, fled in terror.
Cakravāka birds, sāhvas, natyūhas, geese, kāraṇḍava ducks, and waterfowl,

children.text: tathā puṃskokilāḥ krauñcā visaṃjñā bhejire diśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and likewise male cuckoos and cranes, bewildered, took to the quarters of the sky.

children.text: tena śabdena vitrastair ākāśaṃ pakṣibhir vṛtam
children.translated_text: With birds terrified by that sound covering the sky,

children.text: manuṣyair āvṛtā bhūmir ubhayaṃ prababhau tadā ||
children.translated_text: and with men covering the earth, both regions shone forth then.
Then, seeing those men with eyes full of tears and deeply afflicted,

children.text: paryaṣvajata dharmajñaḥ pitṛvan mātṛvac ca saḥ ||
children.translated_text: he, knower of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), embraced them like a father and like a mother.

children.text: sa tatra kāṃścit pariṣasvaje narān narāś ca kecit tu tam abhyavādayan
children.translated_text: There he embraced some men, while certain men bowed to him.

children.text: cakāra sarvān savayasyabāndhavān yathārham āsādya tadā nṛpātmajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When they came to him, the prince treated them all, friends and kinsmen alike, as each deserved.

children.text: tataḥ sa teṣāṃ rudatāṃ mahātmanāṃ bhuvaṃ ca khaṃ cānuvinādayan svanaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the sound of those great-souled men as they wept, making the earth and sky resound,

children.text: guhā girīṇāṃ ca diśaś ca saṃtataṃ mṛdaṅgaghoṣapratimo viśuśruve ||
children.translated_text: was heard continuously in the caves, the mountains, and the quarters, like the beat of drums.

children.text: vasiṣṭhaḥ purataḥ kṛtvā dārān daśarathasya ca
children.translated_text: Placing <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> in front, along with the wives of <s>Daśaratha</s>,
he approached that place, longing for the sight of <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: rājapatnyaś ca gacchantyo mandaṃ mandākinīṃ prati
children.translated_text: As the king's wives went slowly toward the <s>Mandākinī</s>,
they saw there that bathing place used by <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
<s>Kausalyā</s>, her face dry and filled with tears,

children.text: sumitrām abravīd dīnā yāś cānyā rājayoṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: spoke in misery to <s>Sumitrā</s> and to the other royal women:
This is the hard-won, solitary ford in the forest of those orphaned ones,

children.text: vane prāk kevalaṃ tīrthaṃ ye te nirviṣayīkṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those men of blameless deeds who have been deprived of their kingdom.

children.text: itaḥ sumitre putras te sadā jalam atandritaḥ
children.translated_text: From here, <s>Sumitrā</s>, your son, tireless <s>Saumitri</s>,

children.text: svayaṃ harati saumitrir mama putrasya kāraṇāt ||
children.translated_text: always carries water himself for the sake of my son.
On the ground, on <s>darbha</s> grass with its tips turned south,
the long-eyed lady saw the iṅgudī oil-cake set down for his father.

children.text: taṃ bhūmau pitur ārtena nyastaṃ rāmeṇa vīkṣya sā
children.translated_text: Seeing that offering for his father placed on the ground by grief-stricken <s>Rāma</s>,
queen <s>Kausalyā</s> spoke to all the wives of <s>Daśaratha</s>:
Behold this food of the great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>, lord of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s>s,
properly given by <s>Rāghava</s> for his father.
For that great-souled king, equal to the gods,
I do not think this is fitting food, since he had enjoyed every pleasure.
Having enjoyed the earth bounded on four sides, that mighty lord, equal to <s>Mahendra</s>,
how does that ruler of the earth eat oil-cake of iṅgudī?

children.text: ato duḥkhataraṃ loke na kiṃcit pratibhāti mā
children.translated_text: Nothing in the world appears to me more painful than this,

children.text: yatra rāmaḥ pitur dadyād iṅgudīkṣodam ṛddhimān ||
children.translated_text: that prosperous <s>Rāma</s> should offer crushed iṅgudī to his father.
Seeing the iṅgudī oil-cake given by <s>Rāma</s> to his father,

children.text: kathaṃ duḥkhena hṛdayaṃ na sphoṭati sahasradhā ||
children.translated_text: how does my heart not burst into a thousand pieces from grief?

children.text: evam ārtāṃ sapatnyas tā jagmur āśvāsya tāṃ tadā
children.translated_text: Then those co-wives, having comforted her as she was thus afflicted, went on,

children.text: dadṛśuś cāśrame rāmaṃ svargāc cyutam ivāmaram ||
children.translated_text: and in the hermitage they saw <s>Rāma</s>, like an immortal fallen from heaven.
Seeing <s>Rāma</s> bereft of every enjoyment, the mothers,
afflicted and wasted by grief, shed tears aloud.

children.text: tāsāṃ rāmaḥ samutthāya jagrāha caraṇāñ śubhān
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> rose and grasped the auspicious feet
of all his mothers, that tiger among men, true to his pledge.
With hands pleasant to touch, with soft fingers and palms, auspicious,
those wide-eyed women wiped the dust from <s>Rāma</s>'s back.

children.text: saumitrir api tāḥ sarvā mātṝn samprekṣya duḥkhitaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Saumitri</s> too, distressed at seeing all those mothers,
after <s>Rāma</s>, gently saluted them with devotion.

children.text: yathā rāme tathā tasmin sarvā vavṛtire striyaḥ
children.translated_text: As they behaved toward <s>Rāma</s>, so all the women behaved toward him,
toward <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, born of <s>Daśaratha</s> and marked with auspicious signs.
<s>Sītā</s> too, sorrowful, clasping the feet of those
mothers-in-law, her eyes filled with tears, stood before them.

children.text: tāṃ pariṣvajya duḥkhārtāṃ mātā duhitaraṃ yathā
children.translated_text: Embracing her, stricken with grief, as a mother embraces a daughter,
<s>Kausalyā</s> spoke to her, wretched and made thin by dwelling in the forest:
The daughter of the king of <s>Videha</s> and daughter-in-law of <s>Daśaratha</s>,

children.text: rāmapatnī kathaṃ duḥkhaṃ samprāptā nirjane vane ||
children.translated_text: the wife of <s>Rāma</s>, how has she come to suffering in the lonely forest?
Like a lotus scorched by heat, like a blue lotus afflicted,

children.text: kāñcanaṃ rajasā dhvastaṃ kliṣṭaṃ candram ivāmbudaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: like gold ruined by dust, like the moon troubled by clouds,

children.text: mukhaṃ te prekṣya māṃ śoko dahaty agnir ivāśrayam
children.translated_text: seeing your face, <s>Vaidehī</s>, grief burns me like fire burns its fuel,
fiercely in my heart, born from the fire-sticks of calamity.
While his mother was speaking thus in distress, the elder brother of <s>Bharata</s>,

children.text: pādāv āsādya jagrāha vasiṣṭhasya sa rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Rāghava</s>, approached and grasped the feet of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.

children.text: purohitasyāgnisamasya tasya vai bṛhaspater indra ivāmarādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: Like <s>Indra</s>, lord of the immortals, before <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, he grasped the feet of that priest, fire-like and richly endowed with splendor,

children.text: pragṛhya pādau susamṛddhatejasaḥ sahaiva tenopaviveśa rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, having taken hold of those feet, <s>Rāghava</s> sat down together with him.

children.text: tato jaghanyaṃ sahitaiḥ sa mantribhiḥ purapradhānaiś ca sahaiva sainikaiḥ
children.translated_text: Then, last of all, together with his ministers, the city chiefs, and the soldiers,

children.text: janena dharmajñatamena dharmavān upopaviṣṭo bharatas tadāgrajam ||
children.translated_text: righteous <s>Bharata</s> sat near his elder brother, along with a people most knowledgeable in <s>dharma</s> (righteous order).

children.text: upopaviṣṭas tu tadā sa vīryavāṃs tapasviveṣeṇa samīkṣya rāghavam
children.translated_text: Then mighty <s>Bharata</s>, seated nearby, saw <s>Rāghava</s> in ascetic dress,

children.text: śriyā jvalantaṃ bharataḥ kṛtāñjalir yathā mahendraḥ prayataḥ prajāpatim ||
children.translated_text: shining with majesty, and sat with joined palms like <s>Mahendra</s>, reverent before <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: kim eṣa vākyaṃ bharato 'dya rāghavaṃ praṇamya satkṛtya ca sādhu vakṣyati
children.translated_text: What words will <s>Bharata</s> now say to <s>Rāghava</s>, after bowing and duly honoring him?

children.text: itīva tasyāryajanasya tattvato babhūva kautūhalam uttamaṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: Thus a supreme curiosity truly arose then among those noble people.

children.text: sa rāghavaḥ satyadhṛtiśca lakṣmaṇo mahānubhāvo bharataś ca dhārmikaḥ
children.translated_text: That <s>Rāghava</s>, steadfast in truth, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> of great power, and righteous <s>Bharata</s>,

children.text: vṛtāḥ suhṛdbhiś ca virejur adhvare yathā sadasyaiḥ sahitās trayo 'gnayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: surrounded by friends, shone in the rite like the three fires attended by officiants.

children.text: taṃ tu rāmaḥ samāśvāsya bhrātaraṃ guruvatsalam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s>, having reassured his brother, devoted to his elders,
began, together with his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, to question him:

children.text: kim etad iccheyam ahaṃ śrotuṃ pravyāhṛtaṃ tvayā
children.translated_text: I wish to hear what this is that has been spoken by you,

children.text: yasmāt tvam āgato deśam imaṃ cīrajaṭājinī ||
children.translated_text: why you have come to this region wearing bark-cloth, matted hair, and deer-skin.
For what reason have you entered this region, bearing black-antelope skin and matted hair,

children.text: hitvā rājyaṃ praviṣṭas tvaṃ tat sarvaṃ vaktum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: after leaving the kingdom? You should tell all of that.
Thus addressed by the high-souled <s>Kākutstha</s>, the son of <s>Kekayī</s>,

children.text: pragṛhya balavad bhūyaḥ prāñjalir vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: joining his hands again with intense feeling, spoke these words:

children.text: āryaṃ tātaḥ parityajya kṛtvā karma suduṣkaram
children.translated_text: Noble one, our father, abandoning you and doing a deed very hard to do,
has gone to heaven, mighty-armed one, crushed by grief for his son.

children.text: striyā niyuktaḥ kaikeyyā mama mātrā paraṃtapa
children.translated_text: Urged by a woman, by <s>Kaikeyī</s> my mother, scorcher of foes,
he committed this very great sin, destructive of his own fame.
She, not obtaining the fruit of kingship, widowed and wasted by grief,
my mother will fall into a most terrible hell.

children.text: tasya me dāsabhūtasya prasādaṃ kartum arhasi
children.translated_text: You should show favor to me, who am as your servant,
and be consecrated today itself to the kingship, like <s>Maghavan</s>.

children.text: imāḥ prakṛtayaḥ sarvā vidhavā mātaraś ca yāḥ
children.translated_text: All these subjects, and the widowed mothers who are here,
have come into your presence; you should show them favor.

children.text: tadānupūrvyā yuktaṃ ca yuktaṃ cātmani mānada
children.translated_text: Therefore, honorable one, what accords with due succession and what is fitting for yourself:

children.text: rājyaṃ prāpnuhi dharmeṇa sakāmān suhṛdaḥ kuru ||
children.translated_text: gain the kingdom according to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), and fulfill your friends' desires.

children.text: bhavatv avidhavā bhūmiḥ samagrā patinā tvayā
children.translated_text: Let the whole earth be no widow, with you as her husband,
like an autumn night with the stainless moon.

children.text: ebhiś ca sacivaiḥ sārdhaṃ śirasā yācito mayā
children.translated_text: Together with these ministers, I ask you with my head bowed;

children.text: bhrātuḥ śiṣyasya dāsasya prasādaṃ kartum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: you should show favor to your brother, pupil, and servant.

children.text: tad idaṃ śāśvataṃ pitryaṃ sarvaṃ sacivamaṇḍalam
children.translated_text: This entire council of ministers, ancient and inherited from our father,
honored, tiger among men, I am not able to overstep.
Having spoken thus, the mighty-armed son of <s>Kekayī</s>, filled with tears,

children.text: rāmasya śirasā pādau jagrāha bharataḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s> again grasped <s>Rāma</s>'s feet with his head.

children.text: taṃ mattam iva mātaṃgaṃ niḥśvasantaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: As he sighed again and again like a rut-maddened elephant,
<s>Rāma</s> embraced his brother <s>Bharata</s> and spoke these words:
You are noble-born, endowed with character, radiant, and faithful to your vow,

children.text: rājyahetoḥ kathaṃ pāpam ācaret tvadvidho janaḥ ||
children.translated_text: How could a person like you commit evil for the sake of kingship?

children.text: na doṣaṃ tvayi paśyāmi sūkṣmam apy arisūdana
children.translated_text: I see no fault in you, not even the slightest, O slayer of foes,

children.text: na cāpi jananīṃ bālyāt tvaṃ vigarhitum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: nor should you reproach your mother, for she acted from childishness.
As much respect as there is toward a father, O knower of <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty), honored by the world,

children.text: tāvad dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭha jananyām api gauravam ||
children.translated_text: so much respect, O best of those who uphold <s>dharma</s>, is also due toward a mother.
When these two righteous ones, my mother and father, said to me, 'Go to the forest,' O <s>Rāghava</s>,
how could I act otherwise?
You are to obtain the kingdom in <s>Ayodhyā</s>, honored by the world;
I, clad in bark garments, am to dwell in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest.
Having thus made the division in the presence of the people,

children.text: vyādiśya ca mahātejā divaṃ daśaratho gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and having given his command, the greatly radiant great king <s>Daśaratha</s> went to heaven.

children.text: sa ca pramāṇaṃ dharmātmā rājā lokagurus tava
children.translated_text: That righteous king, your teacher before the world, is authoritative;

children.text: pitrā dattaṃ yathābhāgam upabhoktuṃ tvam arhasi ||
children.translated_text: you ought to enjoy the share given by our father, according to its allotment.
For fourteen years, dear one, dwelling in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest,

children.text: upabhokṣye tv ahaṃ dattaṃ bhāgaṃ pitrā mahātmanā ||
children.translated_text: I too shall enjoy the share given by our great-souled father.

children.text: yad abravīn māṃ naralokasatkṛtaḥ pitā mahātmā vibudhādhipopamaḥ
children.translated_text: What my great-souled father, honored among men and equal to the lord of the gods, said to me,

children.text: tad eva manye paramātmano hitaṃ na sarvalokeśvarabhāvam avyayam ||
children.translated_text: that alone I consider beneficial to my highest self, not the imperishable condition of being lord of all the worlds.
Then, for those lions among men, surrounded by those groups of friends,
the night passed painfully while they were still grieving.
When the night had beautifully dawned, those brothers, surrounded by friends,

children.text: mandākinyāṃ hutaṃ japyaṃ kṛtvā rāmam upāgaman ||
children.translated_text: performed the oblation and recitation at the <s>Mandākinī</s> and approached <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: tūṣṇīṃ te samupāsīnā na kaścit kiṃcid abravīt
children.translated_text: They sat near him in silence; no one said anything.

children.text: bharatas tu suhṛnmadhye rāmaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: But <s>Bharata</s>, in the midst of his friends, spoke these words to <s>Rāma</s>:

children.text: sāntvitā māmikā mātā dattaṃ rājyam idaṃ mama
children.translated_text: My mother has been appeased, and this kingdom has been given to me;

children.text: tad dadāmi tavaivāhaṃ bhuṅkṣva rājyam akaṇṭakam ||
children.translated_text: I give it back to you alone. Enjoy the kingdom, free from obstruction.
Like a bridge broken by a great rush of water in the rainy season,
this great broken realm cannot be restrained by anyone other than you.
As a donkey cannot follow the speed of a horse, or a bird the flight of <s>Tārkṣya</s>,

children.text: anugantuṃ na śaktir me gatiṃ tava mahīpate ||
children.translated_text: so I have no power to follow your course, O lord of the earth.

children.text: sujīvaṃ nityaśas tasya yaḥ parair upajīvyate
children.translated_text: The life of one by whom others are supported is always easy to live;

children.text: rāma tena tu durjīvaṃ yaḥ parān upajīvati ||
children.translated_text: but, O <s>Rāma</s>, hard to live is the life of one who depends upon others.

children.text: yathā tu ropito vṛkṣaḥ puruṣeṇa vivardhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Just as a tree planted by a man and made to grow,
though now a great tree with a rooted trunk, may be too tall for that short man to climb,

children.text: sa yadā puṣpito bhūtvā phalāni na vidarśayet
children.translated_text: if, after flowering, it should not show fruit,

children.text: sa tāṃ nānubhavet prītiṃ yasya hetoḥ prabhāvitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then he would not enjoy the pleasure for the sake of which he nurtured it.

children.text: eṣopamā mahābāho tvam arthaṃ vettum arhasi
children.translated_text: This is the comparison, O mighty-armed one; you should understand its meaning:

children.text: yadi tvam asmān ṛṣabho bhartā bhṛtyān na śādhi hi ||
children.translated_text: if you, the bull among men, our master, do not rule us, your servants.

children.text: śreṇayas tvāṃ mahārāja paśyantv agryāś ca sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Let the guilds and all the foremost people see you, O great king,
standing in the kingdom, subduer of enemies, blazing like the sun.
When you set out, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, let intoxicated elephants trumpet;
let the women in the inner palace rejoice, fully composed in happiness.

children.text: tasya sādhv ity amanyanta nāgarā vividhā janāḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing the speech of <s>Bharata</s>, who was pleading again with <s>Rāma</s>,
the various townspeople approved it, thinking, 'Well said.'

children.text: tam evaṃ duḥkhitaṃ prekṣya vilapantaṃ yaśasvinam
children.translated_text: Seeing that illustrious <s>Bharata</s> thus distressed and lamenting,
self-possessed <s>Rāma</s>, master of himself, consoled him.
A man has no free power over himself; this person is not his own lord.
Fate drags him this way and that.
All accumulations end in destruction; all elevations end in falling;
unions end in separations, and life ends in death.

children.text: yathā phalānāṃ pakvānāṃ nānyatra patanād bhayam
children.translated_text: Just as ripe fruits have no fear except falling,

children.text: evaṃ narasya jātasya nānyatra maraṇād bhayam ||
children.translated_text: so a man who has been born has no fear except death.
Just as a house with firm pillars, after becoming old, sinks down,
so men sink down when they have come under the power of old age and death.
Days and nights pass here for all living beings,

children.text: āyūṃṣi kṣapayanty āśu grīṣme jalam ivāṃśavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: quickly wasting away their lifespans, like sunrays drying up water in summer.

children.text: ātmānam anuśoca tvaṃ kim anyam anuśocasi
children.translated_text: Grieve for yourself; why do you grieve for another?

children.text: āyus te hīyate yasya sthitasya ca gatasya ca ||
children.translated_text: Your own life diminishes, whether you are standing still or going.

children.text: sahaiva mṛtyur vrajati saha mṛtyur niṣīdati
children.translated_text: Death goes together with one; death sits down together with one;

children.text: gatvā sudīrgham adhvānaṃ saha mṛtyur nivartate ||
children.translated_text: after one has gone on a very long road, death returns together with one.

children.text: gātreṣu valayaḥ prāptāḥ śvetāś caiva śiroruhāḥ
children.translated_text: Wrinkles have appeared on the limbs, and the hairs of the head have turned white;

children.text: jarayā puruṣo jīrṇaḥ kiṃ hi kṛtvā prabhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: when a man has been worn out by old age, what can he do to prevail?

children.text: nandanty udita āditye nandanty astam ite ravau
children.translated_text: People rejoice when the sun has risen, and rejoice when the sun has set;
they do not understand the wasting away of their own lives.

children.text: hṛṣyanty ṛtumukhaṃ dṛṣṭvā navaṃ navam ihāgatam
children.translated_text: They are delighted when they see the beginning of a season newly and newly arrived here;
but through the turning of the seasons comes the dwindling of living beings' lives.

children.text: yathā kāṣṭhaṃ ca kāṣṭhaṃ ca sameyātāṃ mahārṇave
children.translated_text: Just as one piece of wood and another may meet in the great ocean,

children.text: sametya ca vyapeyātāṃ kālam āsādya kaṃcana ||
children.translated_text: and, having met, may separate after some time has come,

children.text: evaṃ bhāryāś ca putrāś ca jñātayaś ca vasūni ca
children.translated_text: so wives, sons, kinsmen, and possessions

children.text: sametya vyavadhāvanti dhruvo hy eṣāṃ vinābhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: come together and then run apart, for separation from them is certain.

children.text: nātra kaścid yathā bhāvaṃ prāṇī samabhivartate
children.translated_text: No living being here can proceed according to his own intention;

children.text: tena tasmin na sāmarthyaṃ pretasyāsty anuśocataḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore there is no power in lamenting for one who is dead.

children.text: yathā hi sārthaṃ gacchantaṃ brūyāt kaścit pathi sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: For just as someone standing on the road might say to a caravan going along,

children.text: aham apy āgamiṣyāmi pṛṣṭhato bhavatām iti ||
children.translated_text: 'I too will come after you,'

children.text: evaṃ pūrvair gato mārgaḥ pitṛpaitāmaho dhruvaḥ
children.translated_text: so this fixed path, trodden by those before us and by our fathers and grandfathers,

children.text: tam āpannaḥ kathaṃ śoced yasya nāsti vyatikramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: has been entered upon; how should one grieve over that from which there is no turning aside?
For life, as it passes, like a stream, does not return.

children.text: ātmā sukhe niyoktavyaḥ sukhabhājaḥ prajāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should direct oneself toward happiness; living beings are said to have happiness as their portion.

children.text: dharmātmā sa śubhaiḥ kṛtsnaiḥ kratubhiś cāptadakṣiṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: Our righteous father, by all auspicious sacrifices with abundant sacrificial gifts,

children.text: dhūtapāpo gataḥ svargaṃ pitā naḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: having shaken off sin, has gone to heaven, he who was lord of the earth.
Through properly supporting his servants, through protecting his subjects,

children.text: arthādānāc ca dhārmeṇa pitā nas tridivaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and through taking revenue according to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), our father has gone to the third heaven.

children.text: iṣṭvā bahuvidhair yajñair bhogāṃś cāvāpya puṣkalān
children.translated_text: Having sacrificed with many kinds of sacrifices and having obtained abundant enjoyments,

children.text: uttamaṃ cāyur āsādya svar gataḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and having reached an excellent span of life, the lord of the earth has gone to heaven.

children.text: sa jīrṇaṃ mānuṣaṃ dehaṃ parityajya pitā hi naḥ
children.translated_text: For our father, casting off this aged human body,
has attained divine prosperity, the kind that moves in <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: taṃ tu naivaṃvidhaḥ kaścit prājñaḥ śocitum arhati
children.translated_text: No wise man of such a kind ought to mourn him in this way,
one such as you, and one who is so learned and very intelligent.
These many kinds of grief, and lamenting and weeping likewise,
must be avoided in every condition by a steadfast and thoughtful man.

children.text: sa svastho bhava mā śoco yātvā cāvasa tāṃ purīm
children.translated_text: Therefore be composed; do not grieve. Go and dwell in that city,

children.text: tathā pitrā niyukto 'si vaśinā vadatāṃ vara ||
children.translated_text: for so you were commanded by our self-controlled father, best of speakers.
Where I too was commanded by that same man of meritorious deeds,
there I shall carry out the command of my noble father.

children.text: na mayā śāsanaṃ tasya tyaktuṃ nyāyyam ariṃdama
children.translated_text: It is not right for me to abandon his command, crusher of enemies;

children.text: tat tvayāpi sadā mānyaṃ sa vai bandhuḥ sa naḥ pitā ||
children.translated_text: and that command must always be honored by you too, for he is our kinsman and our father.

children.text: evam uktvā tu virate rāme vacanam arthavat
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāma</s> had spoken this meaningful speech and fallen silent,

children.text: uvāca bharataś citraṃ dhārmiko dhārmikaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s>, the righteous man, spoke a wondrous righteous speech to the righteous one.

children.text: ko hi syād īdṛśo loke yādṛśas tvam ariṃdama
children.translated_text: Who indeed in the world could be such as you are, crusher of enemies?

children.text: na tvāṃ pravyathayed duḥkhaṃ prītir vā na praharṣayet ||
children.translated_text: Suffering does not shake you, nor does affection or joy make you exult.

children.text: saṃmataś cāsi vṛddhānāṃ tāṃś ca pṛcchasi saṃśayān
children.translated_text: You are esteemed by the elders, and you ask them about doubtful matters;

children.text: yathā mṛtas tathā jīvan yathāsati tathā sati ||
children.translated_text: for you, the dead is as the living, and what does not exist is as what exists.

children.text: yasyaiṣa buddhilābhaḥ syāt paritapyeta kena saḥ
children.translated_text: When someone has gained such understanding, by what could he be tormented?

children.text: sa evaṃ vyasanaṃ prāpya na viṣīditum arhati ||
children.translated_text: Having met with such misfortune, he ought not to despond.
You are like an immortal in firmness, a great-souled man true to your pledge,

children.text: sarvajñaḥ sarvadarśī ca buddhimāṃś cāsi rāghava ||
children.translated_text: all-knowing, all-seeing, and wise, <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: na tvām evaṃ guṇair yuktaṃ prabhavābhavakovidam
children.translated_text: A grief that is most unbearable ought not to assail you,
endowed as you are with such virtues and skilled in discerning prosperity and ruin.

children.text: proṣite mayi yat pāpaṃ mātrā matkāraṇāt kṛtam
children.translated_text: The evil that my mother did for my sake while I was away,

children.text: kṣudrayā tad aniṣṭaṃ me prasīdatu bhavān mama ||
children.translated_text: that hateful act by that petty woman is abhorrent to me; let Your Lordship be gracious to me.
I am bound by the bond of <s>dharma</s> (duty); for that reason I do not here
kill this mother of mine with a severe punishment, though she deserves punishment and has done evil.
How could I, born from <s>Daśaratha</s>, whose lineage and deeds were pure,

children.text: jānan dharmam adharmiṣṭhaṃ kuryāṃ karma jugupsitam ||
children.translated_text: knowing <s>dharma</s>, perform a most unrighteous and detestable act?

children.text: guruḥ kriyāvān vṛddhaś ca rājā pretaḥ piteti ca
children.translated_text: Because he was a teacher, one who performed rites, an elder, a king, dead, and my father,

children.text: tātaṃ na parigarheyaṃ daivataṃ ceti saṃsadi ||
children.translated_text: I would not censure my father in an assembly, dear one, regarding him also as a deity.

children.text: ko hi dharmārthayor hīnam īdṛśaṃ karma kilbiṣam
children.translated_text: Who, desiring to please a woman, would do such a sinful act,

children.text: striyāḥ priyacikīrṣuḥ san kuryād dharmajña dharmavit ||
children.translated_text: devoid of <s>dharma</s> and advantage, O knower of <s>dharma</s>, O one who understands <s>dharma</s>?
At the time of death, beings become bewildered, so ancient sacred tradition says;

children.text: rājñaivaṃ kurvatā loke pratyakṣā sā śrutiḥ kṛtā ||
children.translated_text: by the king acting in this way, that tradition was made visible in the world.

children.text: sādhvartham abhisaṃdhāya krodhān mohāc ca sāhasāt
children.translated_text: Whatever transgression of our father occurred, from aiming at a good end, from anger, delusion, and rashness,

children.text: tātasya yad atikrāntaṃ pratyāharatu tad bhavān ||
children.translated_text: may Your Lordship draw that back.

children.text: pitur hi samatikrāntaṃ putro yaḥ sādhu manyate
children.translated_text: For when a son regards as good what his father has transgressed,

children.text: tad apatyaṃ mataṃ loke viparītam ato 'nyathā ||
children.translated_text: the world considers that offspring perverse; otherwise, the opposite.

children.text: tad apatyaṃ bhavān astu mā bhavān duṣkṛtaṃ pituḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore be a true son; let Your Lordship not approve our father's evil deed,
an act done in the world and condemned by the steadfast.

children.text: kaikeyīṃ māṃ ca tātaṃ ca suhṛdo bāndhavāṃś ca naḥ
children.translated_text: May Your Lordship protect <s>Kaikeyī</s>, me, our father, our friends and kinsmen,

children.text: paurajānapadān sarvāṃs trātu sarvam idaṃ bhavān ||
children.translated_text: all the city-dwellers and country people, and all this realm.

children.text: kva cāraṇyaṃ kva ca kṣātraṃ kva jaṭāḥ kva ca pālanam
children.translated_text: What has the forest to do with royal duty? What have matted locks to do with protection?

children.text: īdṛśaṃ vyāhataṃ karma na bhavān kartum arhati ||
children.translated_text: Your Lordship ought not to perform such a contradictory act.

children.text: atha kleśajam eva tvaṃ dharmaṃ caritum icchasi
children.translated_text: But if you wish to practice only a <s>dharma</s> born of hardship,

children.text: dharmeṇa caturo varṇān pālayan kleśam āpnuhi ||
children.translated_text: then incur hardship by protecting the four social classes according to <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: caturṇām āśramāṇāṃ hi gārhasthyaṃ śreṣṭham āśramam
children.translated_text: For the knowers of <s>dharma</s> say that, among the four <s>āśramas</s> (life-stages),

children.text: āhur dharmajña dharmajñās taṃ kathaṃ tyaktum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: the householder's state is the best life-stage; how can you abandon it, O knower of <s>dharma</s>?

children.text: śrutena bālaḥ sthānena janmanā bhavato hy aham
children.translated_text: In learning, age, station, and birth I am junior to Your Lordship;

children.text: sa kathaṃ pālayiṣyāmi bhūmiṃ bhavati tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: so how shall I rule the earth while Your Lordship is present?

children.text: hīnabuddhiguṇo bālo hīnaḥ sthānena cāpy aham
children.translated_text: I am deficient in intellect and virtues, young, and deficient in station as well;

children.text: bhavatā ca vinā bhūto na vartayitum utsahe ||
children.translated_text: and bereft of Your Lordship, I cannot manage to live.

children.text: idaṃ nikhilam avyagraṃ pitryaṃ rājyam akaṇṭakam
children.translated_text: Rule this entire inherited kingdom, untroubled and free of thorns,
according to your own <s>dharma</s>, O knower of <s>dharma</s>, together with your kinsmen.
Let the sacrificial priests, together with <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and your kinsmen,
consecrate you here with mantras, since they are skilled in mantras.

children.text: abhiṣiktas tvam asmābhir ayodhyāṃ pālane vraja
children.translated_text: Consecrated by us, go to <s>Ayodhyā</s> for its protection,

children.text: vijitya tarasā lokān marudbhir iva vāsavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: after conquering the worlds by force, like <s>Vāsava</s> with the Maruts.

children.text: ṛṇāni trīṇy apākurvan durhṛdaḥ sādhu nirdahan
children.translated_text: Clearing away the three debts, properly burning up your ill-wishers,

children.text: suhṛdas tarpayan kāmais tvam evātrānuśādhi mām ||
children.translated_text: and satisfying your friends with desired objects, you alone command me here.
Today, noble one, let your friends be joyful at your consecration;

children.text: adya bhītāḥ pālayantāṃ durhṛdas te diśo daśa ||
children.translated_text: today let your ill-wishers, afraid, keep watch over the ten directions.

children.text: ākrośaṃ mama mātuś ca pramṛjya puruṣarṣabha
children.translated_text: Wiping away the reproach against me and my mother, bull among men,

children.text: adya tatra bhavantaṃ ca pitaraṃ rakṣa kilbiṣāt ||
children.translated_text: today protect there both Your Lordship and our father from guilt.
With my head bowed I entreat you: show compassion to me,

children.text: bāndhaveṣu ca sarveṣu bhūteṣv iva maheśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and to all your kinsmen, as <s>Maheśvara</s> does toward beings.

children.text: athavā pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā vanam eva bhavān itaḥ
children.translated_text: Or else, having put me behind you, Your Lordship will go from here only to the forest;

children.text: gamiṣyati gamiṣyāmi bhavatā sārdham apy aham ||
children.translated_text: if you go, I too will go together with Your Lordship.

children.text: tathāpi rāmo bharatena tāmyatā prasādyamānaḥ śirasā mahīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Even so, though <s>Bharata</s>, distressed, was propitiating him with his head bowed, <s>Rāma</s>, the lord of the earth,

children.text: na caiva cakre gamanāya sattvavān matiṃ pitus tadvacane pratiṣṭhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: steadfast and established in that word of his father, did not form the intention to go.

children.text: tad adbhutaṃ sthairyam avekṣya rāghave samaṃ jano harṣam avāpa duḥkhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that wondrous firmness in <s>Rāghava</s>, the people, though grieved, gained an equal joy:

children.text: na yāty ayodhyām iti duḥkhito 'bhavat sthirapratijñatvam avekṣya harṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: they were grieved that he would not go to <s>Ayodhyā</s>, but delighted at seeing his firmness in his vow.

children.text: tam ṛtvijo naigamayūthavallabhās tathā visaṃjñāśrukalāś ca mātaraḥ
children.translated_text: The sacrificial priests, the leaders of the guilds and townsmen, and the mothers, senseless and shedding tears,

children.text: tathā bruvāṇaṃ bharataṃ pratuṣṭuvuḥ praṇamya rāmaṃ ca yayācire saha ||
children.translated_text: praised <s>Bharata</s> as he spoke thus, and, bowing to <s>Rāma</s>, entreated him together.

children.text: punar evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ tu bharataṃ lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ
