children.translated_text: Then the glorious elder brother of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, highly honored among his kinsmen,
replied to <s>Bharata</s>, who was speaking again in this way.

children.text: upapannam idaṃ vākyaṃ yat tvam evam abhāṣathāḥ
children.translated_text: This speech is fitting, in that you have spoken thus,
being a son born from <s>Daśaratha</s>, best of kings, in <s>Kaikeyī</s>.

children.text: purā bhrātaḥ pitā naḥ sa mātaraṃ te samudvahan
children.translated_text: Long ago, brother, when that father of ours married your mother,
he promised your maternal grandfather an unsurpassed bride-price: the kingdom.

children.text: devāsure ca saṃgrāme jananyai tava pārthivaḥ
children.translated_text: And in the battle between gods and asuras, the king,

children.text: samprahṛṣṭo dadau rājā varam ārādhitaḥ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: well pleased and satisfied, granted your mother a boon.

children.text: tataḥ sā saṃpratiśrāvya tava mātā yaśasvinī
children.translated_text: Then, having made him promise, your famous mother,
that lovely woman, asked the best of men for two boons.

children.text: tava rājyaṃ naravyāghra mama pravrājanaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Your kingdom, tiger among men, and likewise my banishment:

children.text: tac ca rājā tathā tasyai niyuktaḥ pradadau varam ||
children.translated_text: the king, bound by that charge, granted those boons to her accordingly.

children.text: tena pitrāham apy atra niyuktaḥ puruṣarṣabha
children.translated_text: Therefore I too, bull among men, have been enjoined here by that father
to dwell in the forest for fourteen years, as the gift of a boon.

children.text: so 'haṃ vanam idaṃ prāpto nirjanaṃ lakṣmaṇānvitaḥ
children.translated_text: So I have come to this deserted forest, accompanied by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
and by incomparable <s>Sītā</s>, standing firm in the truthfulness of my father's word.

children.text: bhavān api tathety eva pitaraṃ satyavādinam
children.translated_text: Your Lordship too ought likewise to make our truth-speaking father,
the lord of kings, true to his word, by quickly accepting consecration.

children.text: ṛṇān mocaya rājānaṃ matkṛte bharata prabhum
children.translated_text: Release the lord king from his debts on my account, <s>Bharata</s>;
protect our father, knower of <s>dharma</s> (duty), and gladden your mother.

children.text: śrūyate hi purā tāta śrutir gītā yaśasvinī
children.translated_text: For, dear one, an illustrious sacred saying is heard from of old,

children.text: gayena yajamānena gayeṣv eva pitṝn prati ||
children.translated_text: sung by <s>Gaya</s> as he sacrificed at <s>Gayā</s> concerning the ancestors:

children.text: puṃnāmnā narakād yasmāt pitaraṃ trāyate sutaḥ
children.translated_text: Because a son saves his father from the hell named <s>Puṃ</s>,

children.text: tasmāt putra iti proktaḥ pitṝn yat pāti vā sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore he is called <s>putra</s>; or because a son protects the ancestors.
Many sons should be desired, virtuous and deeply learned;

children.text: teṣāṃ vai samavetānām api kaścid gayāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: for among them, when gathered together, perhaps even one may go to <s>Gayā</s>.
All royal sages have understood it so, delight of kings;

children.text: tasmāt trāhi naraśreṣṭha pitaraṃ narakāt prabho ||
children.translated_text: therefore, best of men, lord, protect our father from hell.
Go to <s>Ayodhyā</s>, <s>Bharata</s>; win over the subjects,
hero, together with <s>Śatrughna</s> and with all the twice-born.
I too, without delay, shall enter <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest,

children.text: ābhyāṃ tu sahito rājan vaidehyā lakṣmaṇena ca ||
children.translated_text: king, accompanied by these two, <s>Vaidehī</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: tvaṃ rājā bhava bharata svayaṃ narāṇāṃ vanyānām aham api rājarāṇ mṛgāṇām
children.translated_text: You, <s>Bharata</s>, be king yourself of men; I too shall be king of the wild deer.

children.text: gaccha tvaṃ puravaram adya samprahṛṣṭaḥ saṃhṛṣṭas tv aham api daṇḍakān pravekṣye ||
children.translated_text: Go today, delighted, to the excellent city; delighted too, I shall enter the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> woods.

children.text: chāyāṃ te dinakarabhāḥ prabādhamānaṃ varṣatraṃ bharata karotu mūrdhni śītām
children.translated_text: Let the royal parasol, bright as the sun and warding off heat, make cool shade over your head, <s>Bharata</s>;

children.text: eteṣām aham api kānanadrumāṇāṃ chāyāṃ tām atiśayinīṃ sukhaṃ śrayiṣye ||
children.translated_text: I too shall happily take refuge in that far surpassing shade of these forest trees.

children.text: śatrughnaḥ kuśalamatis tu te sahāyaḥ saumitrir mama viditaḥ pradhānamitram
children.translated_text: <s>Śatrughna</s>, wise in good counsel, is your helper; <s>Saumitri</s> is known to me as my chief friend.

children.text: catvāras tanayavarā vayaṃ narendraṃ satyasthaṃ bharata carāma mā viṣādam ||
children.translated_text: We four excellent sons, <s>Bharata</s>, carry out the command of the king established in truth; do not grieve.
While he was consoling <s>Bharata</s>, <s>Jābāli</s>, the best of brahmins,

children.text: uvāca rāmaṃ dharmajñaṃ dharmāpetam idaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: spoke this word, contrary to <s>dharma</s> (duty), to <s>Rāma</s>, the knower of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: sādhu rāghava mā bhūt te buddhir evaṃ nirarthakā
children.translated_text: Enough, <s>Rāghava</s>; let such a useless notion not be yours,
as if it belonged to a common man, when you are noble-minded and ascetic.

children.text: kaḥ kasya puruṣo bandhuḥ kim āpyaṃ kasya kenacit
children.translated_text: Who is whose kinsman? What can anyone obtain from anyone,

children.text: yad eko jāyate jantur eka eva vinaśyati ||
children.translated_text: since a creature is born alone and perishes alone?

children.text: tasmān mātā pitā ceti rāma sajjeta yo naraḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Rāma</s>, the man who clings, saying 'mother' and 'father,'

children.text: unmatta iva sa jñeyo nāsti kāciddhi kasyacit ||
children.translated_text: should be known as like a madman; for nothing at all belongs to anyone.

children.text: yathā grāmāntaraṃ gacchan naraḥ kaścit kvacid vaset
children.translated_text: Just as some man, going to another village, may stay somewhere,
and, leaving that dwelling, set out on the next day,

children.text: evam eva manuṣyāṇāṃ pitā mātā gṛhaṃ vasu
children.translated_text: so too for human beings father, mother, house, and wealth,
descendant of <s>Kakutstha</s>, are only a lodging; good people do not cling to them.

children.text: pitryaṃ rājyaṃ samutsṛjya sa nārhati narottama
children.translated_text: Having abandoned your paternal kingdom, best of men, you ought not
to take to a wrong path, painful, rough, and full of many thorns.
Consecrate yourself in prosperous <s>Ayodhyā</s>;
for the city, wearing a single braid, is waiting for you.
Enjoying the very precious pleasures of kings, son of a king,

children.text: vihara tvam ayodhyāyāṃ yathā śakras triviṣṭape ||
children.translated_text: sport in <s>Ayodhyā</s> as <s>Śakra</s> does in <s>Triviṣṭapa</s>.

children.text: na te kaścid daśaratas tvaṃ ca tasya na kaścana
children.translated_text: <s>Daśaratha</s> is no one to you, and you are no one to him;

children.text: anyo rājā tvam anyaś ca tasmāt kuru yad ucyate ||
children.translated_text: one king is gone, and you are another; therefore do what is being said.

children.text: gataḥ sa nṛpatis tatra gantavyaṃ yatra tena vai
children.translated_text: That king has gone there where indeed he had to go.

children.text: pravṛttir eṣā martyānāṃ tvaṃ tu mithyā vihanyase ||
children.translated_text: Such is the course of mortals; but you are being harmed in vain.

children.text: arthadharmaparā ye ye tāṃs tāñ śocāmi netarān
children.translated_text: Those who are devoted to wealth and <s>dharma</s>, each one of them I pity, and no others;

children.text: te hi duḥkham iha prāpya vināśaṃ pretya bhejire ||
children.translated_text: for after obtaining suffering here, they met with destruction after death.
'The aṣṭakā rite is for the Fathers and the gods': so this belief has spread among people.

children.text: annasyopadravaṃ paśya mṛto hi kim aśiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: See the waste of food; for when a man is dead, what will he eat?

children.text: yadi bhuktam ihānyena deham anyasya gacchati
children.translated_text: If what is eaten here by one person goes to the body of another,

children.text: dadyāt pravasataḥ śrāddhaṃ na tat pathy aśanaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: one should offer a śrāddha for a man who is away on a journey; but that would not be food for the road.

children.text: dānasaṃvananā hy ete granthā medhāvibhiḥ kṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: These treatises, devised by clever men, are means for inducing gifts:

children.text: yajasva dehi dīkṣasva tapas tapyasva saṃtyaja ||
children.translated_text: 'Sacrifice, give, undertake initiation, practice austerity, renounce.'

children.text: sa nāsti param ity eva kuru buddhiṃ mahāmate
children.translated_text: There is no hereafter: set your mind on this alone, great-minded one.

children.text: pratyakṣaṃ yat tad ātiṣṭha parokṣaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ kuru ||
children.translated_text: Rely on what is directly perceived; put what is beyond sight behind your back.
Putting foremost the understanding of the good, which can discern all the world,
accept the kingdom, now offered to you by <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: jābāles tu vacaḥ śrutvā rāmaḥ satyātmanāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard the words of <s>Jābāli</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, best of those whose nature is truth,
spoke with supreme reasoning and with his own unimpaired understanding.

children.text: bhavān me priyakāmārthaṃ vacanaṃ yad ihoktavān
children.translated_text: The speech that Your Honor has spoken here for the sake of what you think dear and beneficial to me
is a thing not to be done though it looks like something to be done, unwholesome though it appears wholesome.
A man without bounds, joined to sinful conduct,
wins no honor among the good, for his character is seen to be broken.
Whether a man is noble-born or low-born, brave or proud of his manhood,

children.text: cāritram eva vyākhyāti śuciṃ vā yadi vāśucim ||
children.translated_text: conduct alone declares whether he is pure or impure.

children.text: anāryas tv āryasaṃkāśaḥ śaucāddhīnas tathā śuciḥ
children.translated_text: If a man is ignoble while seeming noble, deficient in purity while seeming pure,
marked as worthy while unworthy, and ill-conducted while seeming virtuous,
then if I should adopt this <s>adharma</s> clothed in the guise of <s>dharma</s>, this confusion of the world,
abandoning what is good and wholesome and lacking the rule of proper action,
what thoughtful man, skilled in discerning what should and should not be done,

children.text: bahu maṃsyati māṃ loke durvṛttaṃ lokadūṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: would esteem me in the world, as one of bad conduct and a corrupter of the people?

children.text: kasya yāsyāmy ahaṃ vṛttaṃ kena vā svargam āpnuyām
children.translated_text: Whose conduct shall I follow, and by what shall I attain heaven,
if I live by this way of life, one that betrays a low pledge?

children.text: kāmavṛttas tv ayaṃ lokaḥ kṛtsnaḥ samupavartate
children.translated_text: This entire world proceeds according to the conduct of those who act as they wish;

children.text: yadvṛttāḥ santi rājānas tadvṛttāḥ santi hi prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for whatever conduct kings have, that same conduct their subjects have.
Truth and non-cruelty are the eternal conduct of a king;

children.text: tasmāt satyātmakaṃ rājyaṃ satye lokaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore kingship is grounded in truth, and the world is established on truth.

children.text: ṛṣayaś caiva devāś ca satyam eva hi menire
children.translated_text: The seers and the gods indeed considered truth alone supreme;

children.text: satyavādī hi loke 'smin paramaṃ gacchati kṣayam ||
children.translated_text: for one who speaks truth in this world reaches the highest abode.
People recoil from a man who speaks falsehood, just as they recoil from serpents.

children.text: dharmaḥ satyaṃ paro loke mūlaṃ svargasya cocyate ||
children.translated_text: Truth is the highest <s>dharma</s> in the world, and it is called the root of heaven.

children.text: satyam eveśvaro loke satyaṃ padmā samāśritā
children.translated_text: Truth alone is lord in the world; prosperity rests upon truth.

children.text: satyamūlāni sarvāṇi satyān nāsti paraṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: All things are rooted in truth; there is no higher state than truth.

children.text: dattam iṣṭaṃ hutaṃ caiva taptāni ca tapāṃsi ca
children.translated_text: Gifts, sacrifices performed, offerings poured, and austerities practiced,
and the Vedas are founded on truth; therefore one should be devoted to truth.

children.text: ekaḥ pālayate lokam ekaḥ pālayate kulam
children.translated_text: One man protects the world; one man protects his family.

children.text: majjaty eko hi niraya ekaḥ svarge mahīyate ||
children.translated_text: One man sinks into hell, and one man is honored in heaven.

children.text: so 'haṃ pitur nideśaṃ tu kimarthaṃ nānupālaye
children.translated_text: Why then should I not obey my father's command,
true to my promise, truth itself, bound by truth?

children.text: naiva lobhān na mohād vā na cājñānāt tamo'nvitaḥ
children.translated_text: Neither through greed, nor through delusion, nor through ignorance wrapped in darkness
shall I break the bridge of truth, being true to the promise made to my elder.
Of a man who breaks his pledge, though seeming good, fickle and unstable in mind,

children.text: naiva devā na pitaraḥ pratīcchantīti naḥ śrutam ||
children.translated_text: neither gods nor Fathers accept the offerings: so we have heard.

children.text: pratyagātmam imaṃ dharmaṃ satyaṃ paśyāmy ahaṃ svayam
children.translated_text: I myself perceive this inward <s>dharma</s> as truth.
It is a burden borne by good men; for that reason it is rejoiced in.

children.text: kṣātraṃ dharmam ahaṃ tyakṣye hy adharmaṃ dharmasaṃhitam
children.translated_text: I shall abandon the kṣatriya's <s>dharma</s> if it is <s>adharma</s> joined with the name of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: kṣudrair nṛśaṃsair lubdhaiś ca sevitaṃ pāpakarmabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: practiced by petty, cruel, greedy men and by evil-doers.

children.text: kāyena kurute pāpaṃ manasā sampradhārya ca
children.translated_text: A man commits sin with his body and after resolving it with his mind,

children.text: anṛtaṃ jihvayā cāha trividhaṃ karma pātakam ||
children.translated_text: and he speaks falsehood with his tongue: sinful action is threefold.

children.text: bhūmiḥ kīrtir yaśo lakṣmīḥ puruṣaṃ prārthayanti hi
children.translated_text: The earth, fame, glory, and fortune seek out a man,

children.text: svargasthaṃ cānubadhnanti satyam eva bhajeta tat ||
children.translated_text: and they follow him even when he has reached heaven; therefore let him adhere to truth alone.

children.text: śreṣṭhaṃ hy anāryam eva syād yad bhavān avadhārya mām
children.translated_text: What Your Honor has determined about me would indeed be most ignoble,

children.text: āha yuktikarair vākyair idaṃ bhadraṃ kuruṣva ha ||
children.translated_text: when with arguments of reasoning you say, 'Do this beneficial thing.'

children.text: kathaṃ hy ahaṃ pratijñāya vanavāsam imaṃ guroḥ
children.translated_text: For how, after promising this forest-dwelling to my elder,

children.text: bharatasya kariṣyāmi vaco hitvā guror vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: shall I carry out <s>Bharata</s>'s word, abandoning my elder's word?
A firm promise was made by me in the presence of my elder,
and Queen <s>Kaikeyī</s> was then delighted in her heart.
Dwelling in the forest in this way, pure and restrained in food,

children.text: mūlaiḥ puṣpaiḥ phalaiḥ puṇyaiḥ pitṝn devāṃś ca tarpayan ||
children.translated_text: satisfying the Fathers and the gods with holy roots, flowers, and fruits,
I, with the five classes of beings contented, shall carry on the journey of life,
free from deceit, faithful, and skilled in discerning what should and should not be done.

children.text: karmabhūmim imāṃ prāpya kartavyaṃ karma yac chubham
children.translated_text: Having reached this land of action, the auspicious action that must be done should be done.

children.text: agnir vāyuś ca somaś ca karmaṇāṃ phalabhāginaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Fire, Wind, and Soma are sharers in the fruits of actions.

children.text: śataṃ kratūnām āhṛtya devarāṭ tridivaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: Having performed a hundred sacrifices, the king of the gods went to heaven;

children.text: tapāṃsy ugrāṇi cāsthāya divaṃ yātā maharṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and by undertaking fierce austerities, great seers went to heaven.

children.text: satyaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca parākramaṃ ca bhūtānukampāṃ priyavāditāṃ ca
children.translated_text: Truth, <s>dharma</s>, valor, compassion for beings, and pleasant speech,

children.text: dvijātidevātithipūjanaṃ ca panthānam āhus tridivasya santaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and honoring twice-born men, gods, and guests: the good call these the path to heaven.

children.text: dharme ratāḥ satpuruṣaiḥ sametās tejasvino dānaguṇapradhānāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who delight in <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), who are joined with good men, splendid, and foremost in the virtue of giving,

children.text: ahiṃsakā vītamalāś ca loke bhavanti pūjyā munayaḥ pradhānāḥ ||
children.translated_text: who are non-injuring and free from stain, become revered in the world, eminent sages.

children.text: kruddham ājñāya rāmaṃ tu vasiṣṭhaḥ pratyuvāca ha
children.translated_text: But, perceiving <s>Rāma</s> to be angry, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> answered:
<s>Jābāli</s> too knows the coming and going of this world;

children.text: nivartayitukāmas tu tvām etad vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: but wishing to turn you back, he spoke these words to you.
Now understand from me, O lord of the world, this origin of the world.

children.text: sarvaṃ salilam evāsīt pṛthivī yatra nirmitā
children.translated_text: All was water alone, where the earth was formed;

children.text: tataḥ samabhavad brahmā svayambhūr daivataiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: then <s>Brahmā</s>, the self-born, came into being with the deities.

children.text: sa varāhas tato bhūtvā projjahāra vasuṃdharām
children.translated_text: Then, becoming a boar, he lifted up the earth,

children.text: asṛjac ca jagat sarvaṃ saha putraiḥ kṛtātmabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and created the whole world, together with his self-controlled sons.
<s>Brahmā</s>, arisen from the ether, is eternal, constant, and imperishable;

children.text: tasmān marīciḥ saṃjajñe marīceḥ kaśyapaḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: from him <s>Marīci</s> was born, and <s>Kaśyapa</s> was the son of <s>Marīci</s>.

children.text: vivasvān kaśyapāj jajñe manur vaivasvataḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vivasvān</s> was born from <s>Kaśyapa</s>; <s>Manu</s>, called <s>Vaivasvata</s>,

children.text: sa tu prajāpatiḥ pūrvam ikṣvākus tu manoḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: was formerly a progenitor, and <s>Ikṣvāku</s> was the son of <s>Manu</s>.

children.text: yasyeyaṃ prathamaṃ dattā samṛddhā manunā mahī
children.translated_text: To whom this prosperous earth was first given by <s>Manu</s>,

children.text: tam ikṣvākum ayodhyāyāṃ rājānaṃ viddhi pūrvakam ||
children.translated_text: know that <s>Ikṣvāku</s> to have been the first king in <s>Ayodhyā</s>.

children.text: ikṣvākos tu sutaḥ śrīmān kukṣir eveti viśrutaḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Ikṣvāku</s>'s illustrious son was known as <s>Kukṣi</s>;
then from <s>Kukṣi</s> the heroic <s>Vikukṣi</s> was born.

children.text: vikukṣes tu mahātejā bāṇaḥ putraḥ pratāpavān
children.translated_text: From <s>Vikukṣi</s> came a greatly splendid, powerful son, <s>Bāṇa</s>;
from <s>Bāṇa</s> came mighty-armed <s>Anaraṇya</s>, of great fame.

children.text: nānāvṛṣṭir babhūvāsmin na durbhikṣaṃ satāṃ vare
children.translated_text: Under that best of the good, there was no drought
and no famine, nor any thief at all, when great king <s>Anaraṇya</s> ruled.

children.text: anaraṇyān mahābāhuḥ pṛthū rājā babhūva ha
children.translated_text: From <s>Anaraṇya</s> mighty-armed king <s>Pṛthu</s> came to be;
from that great king <s>Pṛthu</s>, <s>Triśaṅku</s> was born,

children.text: sa satyavacanād vīraḥ saśarīro divaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: a hero who, because of his truthful speech, went bodily to heaven.
From <s>Triśaṅku</s> came a son, <s>Dhundhumāra</s> of great fame;
from <s>Dhundhumāra</s> was born the greatly splendid <s>Yuvanāśva</s>.
The illustrious <s>Māndhātṛ</s> became the son of <s>Yuvanāśva</s>;
and from the greatly splendid <s>Māndhātṛ</s> was born <s>Susaṃdhi</s>.

children.text: susaṃdher api putrau dvau dhruvasaṃdhiḥ prasenajit
children.translated_text: <s>Susaṃdhi</s> had two sons, <s>Dhruvasaṃdhi</s> and <s>Prasenajit</s>;
from <s>Dhruvasaṃdhi</s> came the famous <s>Bharata</s>, destroyer of foes.

children.text: bharatāt tu mahābāhor asito nāma jāyata
children.translated_text: From mighty-armed <s>Bharata</s> was born one named <s>Asita</s>;
against him these rival kings arose as enemies,

children.text: haihayās tālajaṅghāś ca śūrāś ca śaśabindavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Haihayas</s>, the <s>Tālajaṅghas</s>, and the valiant <s>Śaśabindus</s>.

children.text: tāṃs tu sarvān prativyūhya yuddhe rājā pravāsitaḥ
children.translated_text: Having resisted them all in battle, the king was driven into exile;

children.text: sa ca śailavare ramye babhūvābhirato muniḥ
children.translated_text: and on a lovely, excellent mountain he dwelt content, like a sage.

children.text: dve cāsya bhārye garbhiṇyau babhūvatur iti śrutiḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is heard that he had two pregnant wives.
A Bhārgava sage named <s>Cyavana</s> was dwelling near <s>Himavant</s>;

children.text: tam ṛṣiṃ samupāgamya kālindī tv abhyavādayat ||
children.translated_text: approaching that seer, <s>Kālindī</s> paid homage to him.

children.text: sa tām abhyavadad vipro varepsuṃ putrajanmani
children.translated_text: The brahmin addressed her, as she desired a boon for the birth of a son;

children.text: tataḥ sā gṛham āgamya devī putraṃ vyajāyata ||
children.translated_text: then that queen returned home and gave birth to a son.

children.text: sapatnyā tu garas tasyai datto garbhajighāṃsayā
children.translated_text: But poison had been given to her by her co-wife, wishing to destroy the embryo;

children.text: gareṇa saha tenaiva jātaḥ sa sagaro 'bhavat ||
children.translated_text: because he was born together with that very poison, he became <s>Sagara</s>.

children.text: sa rājā sagaro nāma yaḥ samudram akhānayat
children.translated_text: That king named <s>Sagara</s> was the one who had the ocean dug out,

children.text: iṣṭvā parvaṇi vegena trāsayantam imāḥ prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: after performing sacrifice at the sacred season, swiftly terrifying these creatures.

children.text: asamañjas tu putro 'bhūt sagarasyeti naḥ śrutam
children.translated_text: <s>Asamañja</s> was a son of <s>Sagara</s>, so we have heard;

children.text: jīvann eva sa pitrā tu nirastaḥ pāpakarmakṛt ||
children.translated_text: while still alive, that evil-doer was cast out by his father.
A powerful son of <s>Asamañja</s> was named <s>Aṃśumān</s>;
<s>Dilīpa</s> was the son of <s>Aṃśumān</s>, and <s>Bhagīratha</s> of <s>Dilīpa</s>.

children.text: bhagīrathāt kakutsthas tu kākutsthā yena tu smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: From <s>Bhagīratha</s> came <s>Kakutstha</s>, from whom the <s>Kākutsthas</s> are remembered;

children.text: kakutsthasya tu putro 'bhūd raghur yena tu rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Kakutstha</s>'s son was <s>Raghu</s>, from whom the <s>Rāghavas</s> are so called.

children.text: raghos tu putras tejasvī pravṛddhaḥ puruṣādakaḥ
children.translated_text: The splendid son of <s>Raghu</s> was <s>Pravṛddha</s>, a man-eater,

children.text: kalmāṣapādaḥ saudāsa ity evaṃ prathito bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: known on earth as <s>Kalmāṣapāda</s> and <s>Saudāsa</s>.
<s>Kalmāṣapāda</s>'s son was <s>Śaṅkhaṇa</s>, so he is known;

children.text: yas tu tad vīryam āsādya sahaseno vyanīnaśat ||
children.translated_text: having attained that prowess, he destroyed <s>Sahasena</s>.

children.text: śaṅkhaṇasya tu putro 'bhūc chūraḥ śrīmān sudarśanaḥ
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Śaṅkhaṇa</s> was the heroic, illustrious <s>Sudarśana</s>;
from <s>Sudarśana</s> came <s>Agnivarṇa</s>, and from <s>Agnivarṇa</s>, <s>Śīghraga</s>.

children.text: śīghragasya maruḥ putro maroḥ putraḥ praśuśrukaḥ
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Śīghraga</s> was <s>Maru</s>, and <s>Praśuśruka</s> was the son of <s>Maru</s>;
from <s>Praśuśruka</s> was born <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, of great radiance.
The son of <s>Ambarīṣa</s> was <s>Nahuṣa</s>, true in valor;
and <s>Nahuṣa</s>'s son was <s>Nābhāga</s>, supremely righteous.

children.text: ajaś ca suvrataś caiva nābhāgasya sutāv ubhau
children.translated_text: <s>Aja</s> and <s>Suvrata</s> were both sons of <s>Nābhāga</s>;

children.text: ajasya caiva dharmātmā rājā daśarathaḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the righteous king <s>Daśaratha</s> was the son of <s>Aja</s>.

children.text: tasya jyeṣṭho 'si dāyādo rāma ity abhiviśrutaḥ
children.translated_text: You are his eldest heir, renowned as <s>Rāma</s>;

children.text: tad gṛhāṇa svakaṃ rājyam avekṣasva jagan nṛpa ||
children.translated_text: therefore take your own kingdom and look after the world, O king.

children.text: ikṣvākūṇāṃ hi sarveṣāṃ rājā bhavati pūrvajaḥ
children.translated_text: For among all the <s>Ikṣvākus</s>, the firstborn becomes king;
the younger son follows the elder, and the eldest is consecrated to the kingdom.

children.text: sa rāghavāṇāṃ kuladharmam ātmanaḥ sanātanaṃ nādya vihātum arhasi
children.translated_text: Therefore today you must not abandon your own eternal family <s>dharma</s> (law) of the <s>Rāghavas</s>;

children.text: prabhūtaratnām anuśādhi medinīṃ prabhūtarāṣṭrāṃ pitṛvan mahāyaśāḥ ||
children.translated_text: rule the earth rich in jewels and rich in realms, O greatly famous one, like your father.

children.text: vasiṣṭhas tu tadā rāmam uktvā rājapurohitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, the royal priest, having spoken thus to <s>Rāma</s>,
again spoke another speech joined with <s>dharma</s> (righteousness).
For a man born here there are three gurus (venerable teachers):

children.text: ācāryaś caiva kākutstha pitā mātā ca rāghava ||
children.translated_text: the teacher, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, and the father and mother, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: pitā hy enaṃ janayati puruṣaṃ puruṣarṣabha
children.translated_text: For the father begets this man, O bull among men,

children.text: prajñāṃ dadāti cācāryas tasmāt sa gurur ucyate ||
children.translated_text: and a teacher gives wisdom; therefore he is called a guru.

children.text: sa te 'haṃ pitur ācāryas tava caiva paraṃtapa
children.translated_text: I am that teacher of your father, and of you as well, O scorcher of foes.

children.text: mama tvaṃ vacanaṃ kurvan nātivarteḥ satāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: If you act according to my word, you will not overstep the path of the good.

children.text: imā hi te pariṣadaḥ śreṇayaś ca samāgatāḥ
children.translated_text: For these councils and guilds have assembled here for you.

children.text: eṣu tāta caran dharmaṃ nātivarteḥ satāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: Among them, dear child, while practicing <s>dharma</s> (duty), you will not overstep the path of the good.
You ought not to turn away from your aged mother, who is devoted to <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: asyās tu vacanaṃ kurvan nātivarteḥ satāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: If you act according to her word, you will not overstep the path of the good.
If you act according to the word of <s>Bharata</s>, who is beseeching you, O <s>Rāghava</s>,
you will not violate your own self, O you whose valor is truth and <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: evaṃ madhuram uktas tu guruṇā rāghavaḥ svayam
children.translated_text: Thus sweetly addressed by his guru, <s>Rāghava</s> himself,
that bull among men, replied to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, who was seated.

children.text: yan mātāpitarau vṛttaṃ tanaye kurutaḥ sadā
children.translated_text: Whatever conduct a mother and father always perform toward a son,

children.text: na supratikaraṃ tat tu mātrā pitrā ca yat kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: what is done by mother and father is not easy to repay.
By giving according to their ability, by bathing and clothing him,

children.text: nityaṃ ca priyavādena tathā saṃvardhanena ca ||
children.translated_text: by constant gentle speech, and likewise by raising him,

children.text: sa hi rājā janayitā pitā daśaratho mama
children.translated_text: that king <s>Daśaratha</s>, my begetter, is my father.

children.text: ājñātaṃ yan mayā tasya na tan mithyā bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: What I was commanded by him will not become false.

children.text: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa bharataḥ pratyanantaram
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāma</s> had spoken thus, immediately <s>Bharata</s>,
most noble and exceedingly dejected, said to the charioteer:

children.text: iha me sthaṇḍile śīghraṃ kuśān āstara sārathe
children.translated_text: Quickly spread kuśa grass for me here on the bare ground, charioteer.

children.text: āryaṃ pratyupavekṣyāmi yāvan me na prasīdati ||
children.translated_text: I shall sit in protest before my noble brother until he is gracious to me.
Without food, without light, and without wealth, like a brahmin,

children.text: śeṣye purastāc chālāyā yāvan na pratiyāsyati ||
children.translated_text: I shall lie before the hut until he returns.

children.text: sa tu rāmam avekṣantaṃ sumantraṃ prekṣya durmanāḥ
children.translated_text: But he, downcast, seeing <s>Sumantra</s> looking toward <s>Rāma</s>,
had a layer topped with kuśa grass brought and himself spread it on the ground.
Greatly radiant <s>Rāma</s>, the best of royal seers, said to him:

children.text: kiṃ māṃ bharata kurvāṇaṃ tāta pratyupavekṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: What are you making me do, <s>Bharata</s>, dear one, that you sit in protest against me?

children.text: brāhmaṇo hy ekapārśvena narān roddhum ihārhati
children.translated_text: For a brahmin may properly restrain men here by lying on one side,
but there is no rule for such protest-sitting among those anointed as kings.
Rise, tiger among men; abandon this dreadful vow.

children.text: puravaryām itaḥ kṣipram ayodhyāṃ yāhi rāghava ||
children.translated_text: Go quickly from here to the excellent city, <s>Ayodhyā</s>, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: āsīnas tv eva bharataḥ paurajānapadaṃ janam
children.translated_text: But <s>Bharata</s>, remaining seated, looked all around at the city and country people,

children.text: uvāca sarvataḥ prekṣya kim āryaṃ nānuśāsatha ||
children.translated_text: and said, Why do you not instruct my noble brother?

children.text: te tam ūcur mahātmānaṃ paurajānapadā janāḥ
children.translated_text: The city and country people said to that great-souled one:
We know this <s>Kākutstha</s>; <s>Rāghava</s> speaks rightly.

children.text: eṣo 'pi hi mahābhāgaḥ pitur vacasi tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: For this greatly fortunate one too stands firm in his father's word.

children.text: ata eva na śaktāḥ smo vyāvartayitum añjasā ||
children.translated_text: For that very reason we cannot turn him back directly.

children.text: teṣām ājñāya vacanaṃ rāmo vacanam abravīt
children.translated_text: Knowing their words, <s>Rāma</s> spoke these words:
Understand this speech of friends whose sight is <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: etac caivobhayaṃ śrutvā samyak saṃpaśya rāghava
children.translated_text: Having heard both sides, reflect on it properly, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: uttiṣṭha tvaṃ mahābāho māṃ ca spṛśa tathodakam ||
children.translated_text: Stand up, mighty-armed one, and touch me, and water as well.

children.text: athotthāya jalaṃ spṛṣṭvā bharato vākyam abravīt
children.translated_text: Then, having risen and touched water, <s>Bharata</s> spoke these words:

children.text: śṛṇvantu me pariṣado mantriṇaḥ śreṇayas tathā ||
children.translated_text: Let the assemblies, the ministers, and the guilds hear me.

children.text: na yāce pitaraṃ rājyaṃ nānuśāsāmi mātaram
children.translated_text: I did not ask father for the kingdom, nor do I command my mother.
I recognize <s>Rāghava</s> as noble and supremely learned in <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: yadi tv avaśyaṃ vastavyaṃ kartavyaṃ ca pitur vacaḥ
children.translated_text: But if he must necessarily dwell there and our father's word must be carried out,

children.text: aham eva nivatsyāmi caturdaśa vane samāḥ ||
children.translated_text: I myself shall dwell in the forest for fourteen years.

children.text: dharmātmā tasya tathyena bhrātur vākyena vismitaḥ
children.translated_text: Astonished by that truthful speech of his brother, righteous <s>Rāma</s>,
looking at the city and country people, said:

children.text: vikrītam āhitaṃ krītaṃ yat pitrā jīvatā mama
children.translated_text: What was sold, deposited, or bought by my father while he was alive

children.text: na tal lopayituṃ śakyaṃ mayā vā bharatena vā ||
children.translated_text: cannot be annulled either by me or by <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: upadhir na mayā kāryo vanavāse jugupsitaḥ
children.translated_text: No blameworthy substitution is to be made by me in the matter of dwelling in the forest.

children.text: yuktam uktaṃ ca kaikeyyā pitrā me sukṛtaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: What <s>Kaikeyī</s> said was fitting, and what my father did was well done.
I know <s>Bharata</s> to be patient and one who honors his elders.
Everything here is auspicious in this great-souled man who is true to his pledge.
When I have returned from the forest with this brother who is devoted to <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: bhrātrā saha bhaviṣyāmi pṛthivyāḥ patir uttamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall be, together with him, the excellent lord of the earth.

children.text: vṛto rājā hi kaikeyyā mayā tadvacanaṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: For the king was petitioned by <s>Kaikeyī</s>, and I have carried out that word of his,
thereby freeing that father of mine, the lord of the earth, from falsehood.
At that thrilling meeting of the two brothers of incomparable splendor,
the assembled great seers were amazed as they beheld the encounter.

children.text: antarhitās tv ṛṣigaṇāḥ siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: And the hidden hosts of seers, the perfected ones, and the supreme seers
praised those two great-souled <s>Kākutstha</s> brothers.

children.text: sa dhanyo yasya putrau dvau dharmajñau dharmavikramau
children.translated_text: Blessed is the one whose two sons know <s>dharma</s> and are mighty through <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: śrutvā vayaṃ hi sambhāṣām ubhayoḥ spṛhayāmahe ||
children.translated_text: Having heard the conversation of both, we feel longing and admiration for them.
Then the hosts of seers, desiring the death of <s>Daśagrīva</s>, quickly

children.text: bharataṃ rājaśārdūlam ity ūcuḥ saṃgatā vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: together addressed <s>Bharata</s>, the tiger among kings, with these words:
Born in a noble family, very wise, of great conduct and great fame,

children.text: grāhyaṃ rāmasya vākyaṃ te pitaraṃ yady avekṣase ||
children.translated_text: you should accept <s>Rāma</s>'s word, if you have regard for your father.

children.text: sadānṛṇam imaṃ rāmaṃ vayam icchāmahe pituḥ
children.translated_text: We wish this <s>Rāma</s> always to be free from debt to his father;
and because the debt to <s>Kaikeyī</s> has been discharged, <s>Daśaratha</s> has gone to heaven.
Having said this much, the <s>Gandharvas</s> together with the great seers,

children.text: rājarṣayaś caiva tathā sarve svāṃ svāṃ gatiṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and likewise the royal seers, all went each to his own course.
Gladdened by that auspicious speech, the handsome <s>Rāma</s>,
his face delighted, honored those seers.

children.text: srastagātras tu bharataḥ sa vācā sajjamānayā
children.translated_text: But <s>Bharata</s>, his limbs slackened, with his voice faltering,

children.text: kṛtāñjalir idaṃ vākyaṃ rāghavaṃ punar abravīt ||
children.translated_text: With joined palms he again spoke these words to <s>Rāghava</s>:
Considering royal <s>dharma</s> (duty) and the continuity of family <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: kartum arhasi kākutstha mama mātuś ca yācanām ||
children.translated_text: you ought, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, to carry out the request of me and of my mother.

children.text: rakṣituṃ sumahad rājyam aham ekas tu notsahe
children.translated_text: I alone am not able to protect this very great kingdom,
nor likewise to satisfy the city-dwellers and country people who are attached to you.

children.text: jñātayaś ca hi yodhāś ca mitrāṇi suhṛdaś ca naḥ
children.translated_text: For our relatives, warriors, friends, and well-wishers

children.text: tvām eva pratikāṅkṣante parjanyam iva karṣakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: await you alone, like farmers awaiting <s>Parjanya</s>.

children.text: idaṃ rājyaṃ mahāprājña sthāpaya pratipadya hi
children.translated_text: Take possession of this kingdom, great wise one, and establish it firmly;
you are capable, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, of protecting the world.

children.text: ity uktvā nyapatad bhrātuḥ pādayor bharatas tadā
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Bharata</s> then fell at his brother's feet,
and, speaking kindly, earnestly implored <s>Rāma</s> in this way.

children.text: tam aṅke bhrātaraṃ kṛtvā rāmo vacanam abravīt
children.translated_text: Placing his brother in his lap, <s>Rāma</s> himself spoke a word
to the dark-hued, lotus-petal-eyed one, whose voice was like that of a proud swan.

children.text: āgatā tvām iyaṃ buddhiḥ svajā vainayikī ca yā
children.translated_text: This understanding that has come to you is your own and born of discipline;

children.text: bhṛśam utsahase tāta rakṣituṃ pṛthivīm api ||
children.translated_text: dear one, you are fully capable of protecting even the earth.

children.text: amātyaiś ca suhṛdbhiś ca buddhimadbhiś ca mantribhiḥ
children.translated_text: With ministers, well-wishers, and wise counsellors,
after consulting on all affairs, even very great ones, have them carried out.

children.text: lakṣmīś candrād apeyād vā himavān vā himaṃ tyajet
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s> might depart from the moon, or <s>Himavān</s> might abandon snow,

children.text: atīyāt sāgaro velāṃ na pratijñām ahaṃ pituḥ ||
children.translated_text: or the ocean might cross beyond its shore, but I will not break my father's promise.

children.text: kāmād vā tāta lobhād vā mātrā tubhyam idaṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: Whether from desire, dear one, or from greed, this was done by your mother for your sake;

children.text: na tan manasi kartavyaṃ vartitavyaṃ ca mātṛvat ||
children.translated_text: that should not be held in your mind, and she should be treated as a mother.
As he was speaking thus, <s>Bharata</s> addressed the son of <s>Kausalyā</s>,
who shone like the sun in splendor and was lovely to behold like the moon of the first lunar day:
Mount, noble one, with your feet these sandals adorned with gold;
for these will provide the welfare and security of the whole world.

children.text: so 'dhiruhya naravyāghraḥ pāduke hy avaruhya ca
children.translated_text: Then that tiger among men mounted the sandals and, having stepped down,
the greatly radiant one handed them to great-souled <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: sa pāduke te bharataḥ pratāpavān svalaṃkṛte samparigṛhya dharmavit
children.translated_text: Then mighty <s>Bharata</s>, knower of <s>dharma</s> (duty), received those well-adorned sandals,

children.text: pradakṣiṇaṃ caiva cakāra rāghavaṃ cakāra caivottamanāgamūrdhani ||
children.translated_text: circumambulated <s>Rāghava</s>, and placed them on the head of an excellent elephant.

children.text: athānupūrvyāt pratipūjya taṃ janaṃ gurūṃś ca mantriprakṛtīs tathānujau
children.translated_text: Then, in proper order, having honored those people, the elders, the ministers and subjects, and likewise his younger brothers,

children.text: vyasarjayad rāghavavaṃśavardhanaḥ sthitaḥ svadharme himavān ivācalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the increaser of <s>Raghu</s>'s line dismissed them, standing firm in his own <s>dharma</s> (duty) like unmoving <s>Himavān</s>.

children.text: taṃ mātaro bāṣpagṛhītakaṇṭhyo duḥkhena nāmantrayituṃ hi śekuḥ
children.translated_text: His mothers, their throats choked with tears, were unable because of grief even to address him in farewell;

children.text: sa tv eva mātṝn abhivādya sarvā rudan kuṭīṃ svāṃ praviveśa rāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but <s>Rāma</s>, after saluting all his mothers, entered his own hut weeping.

children.text: tataḥ śirasi kṛtvā tu pāduke bharatas tadā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Bharata</s>, placing the sandals on his head,
gladly mounted the chariot together with <s>Śatrughna</s>.

children.text: vasiṣṭho vāmadevaś ca jābāliś ca dṛḍhavrataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, <s>Jābāli</s>, and <s>Dṛḍhavrata</s>
all set out in front, together with the ministers honored for counsel.

children.text: mandākinīṃ nadīṃ ramyāṃ prāṅmukhās te yayus tadā
children.translated_text: Facing east, they then went to the lovely river <s>Mandākinī</s>,
circumambulating the great mountain <s>Citrakūṭa</s>.
Seeing thousands of lovely mineral deposits of many kinds,

children.text: prayayau tasya pārśvena sasainyo bharatas tadā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s> then proceeded along its side with his army.
Not far from <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, <s>Bharata</s> then saw

children.text: āśramaṃ yatra sa munir bharadvājaḥ kṛtālayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the hermitage where the sage <s>Bharadvāja</s> had made his dwelling.

children.text: sa tam āśramam āgamya bharadvājasya buddhimān
children.translated_text: Having come to that hermitage of wise <s>Bharadvāja</s>,
the delight of his lineage descended from the chariot and bowed to his feet.

children.text: tato hṛṣṭo bharadvājo bharataṃ vākyam abravīt
children.translated_text: Then delighted <s>Bharadvāja</s> spoke a word to <s>Bharata</s>:

children.text: api kṛtyaṃ kṛtaṃ tāta rāmeṇa ca samāgatam ||
children.translated_text: Dear one, has the matter been accomplished, and has the meeting with <s>Rāma</s> taken place?

children.text: evam uktas tu bharato bharadvājena dhīmatā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by wise <s>Bharadvāja</s>,
<s>Bharata</s>, devoted to <s>dharma</s> (duty), replied to <s>Bharadvāja</s>:

children.text: sa yācyamāno guruṇā mayā ca dṛḍhavikramaḥ
children.translated_text: Though requested by the guru and by me, he of firm valor,
<s>Rāghava</s>, greatly pleased, spoke these words to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>:

children.text: pituḥ pratijñāṃ tām eva pālayiṣyāmi tattvataḥ
children.translated_text: I shall faithfully keep that very promise of my father,

children.text: caturdaśa hi varṣāṇi yā pratijñā pitur mama ||
children.translated_text: the promise of my father concerning fourteen years.

children.text: evam ukto mahāprājño vasiṣṭhaḥ pratyuvāca ha
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, the very wise <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> replied
with an important speech to <s>Rāghava</s>, who knew speech and was skillful in speech:
Joyfully give these sandals adorned with gold;
in <s>Ayodhyā</s>, great wise one, they will bring your welfare and security.

children.text: evam ukto vasiṣṭhena rāghavaḥ prāṅmukhaḥ sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Rāghava</s>, standing facing east,

children.text: pāduke hemavikṛte mama rājyāya te dadau ||
children.translated_text: gave those gold-wrought sandals to me for my kingship.
I have turned back, permitted by great-souled <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: ayodhyām eva gacchāmi gṛhītvā pāduke śubhe ||
children.translated_text: and I am going to <s>Ayodhyā</s>, taking the auspicious sandals.

children.text: etac chrutvā śubhaṃ vākyaṃ bharatasya mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing this auspicious statement of great-souled <s>Bharata</s>,
the sage <s>Bharadvāja</s> uttered an even more auspicious speech:
This is no wonder, tiger among men, best of those whose conduct is virtuous,

children.text: yad āryaṃ tvayi tiṣṭhet tu nimne vṛṣṭim ivodakam ||
children.translated_text: that nobility should abide in you, like rainwater in a low place.

children.text: amṛtaḥ sa mahābāhuḥ pitā daśarathas tava
children.translated_text: Your mighty-armed father <s>Daśaratha</s> is not dead,

children.text: yasya tvam īdṛśaḥ putro dharmātmā dharmavatsalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: since you are such a son, righteous and devoted to <s>dharma</s> (duty).

children.text: tam ṛṣiṃ tu mahātmānam uktavākyaṃ kṛtāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: Then, with joined palms, after the great-souled sage had said these words,
he began to take leave of him, grasping his feet.

children.text: tataḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā bharadvājaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, having circumambulated <s>Bharadvāja</s> again and again,

children.text: bharatas tu yayau śrīmān ayodhyāṃ saha mantribhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: splendid <s>Bharata</s> went toward <s>Ayodhyā</s> together with the ministers.

children.text: yānaiś ca śakaṭaiś caiva hayair nāgaiś ca sā camūḥ
children.translated_text: And that broad army following <s>Bharata</s>, with vehicles and carts,
with horses and elephants, turned back again.

children.text: tatas te yamunāṃ divyāṃ nadīṃ tīrtvormimālinīm
children.translated_text: Then, having crossed the divine river <s>Yamunā</s>, garlanded with waves,

children.text: dadṛśus tāṃ punaḥ sarve gaṅgāṃ śivajalāṃ nadīm ||
children.translated_text: all of them again saw that river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, with auspicious waters.
Having crossed her, full of lovely water, together with his kinsmen,
he entered the charming <s>Śṛṅgaverapura</s> with his army.
From <s>Śṛṅgaverapura</s> again he came in sight of <s>Ayodhyā</s>;
<s>Bharata</s>, scorched by grief, said this to the charioteer:

children.text: sārathe paśya vidhvastā ayodhyā na prakāśate
children.translated_text: Charioteer, look: devastated <s>Ayodhyā</s> does not shine;
it is formless, joyless, wretched, its sounds beaten down.
Approaching in a chariot with a smooth and deep rumble, the lord,
the greatly famed <s>Bharata</s>, quickly entered <s>Ayodhyā</s>.
It was haunted by cats and owls, its men and elephants withdrawn,
struck by darkness, black and unlit, like night.
Like <s>Rohiṇī</s>, the beloved wife of <s>Rāhu</s>'s foe, blazing with radiant splendor,
alone and oppressed by a planet that had risen against her.
Like a meager mountain stream, with scant warm and agitated water, its birds scorched by heat,
its fish, great fish, and crocodiles hidden away.
Like a golden, smokeless flame arisen from the sacrificial fire,
sprinkled afterward with oblation and gone out at its crest.
Like an army in a great battle, its armor shattered, its elephants, horses, chariots, and banners broken,
its chief warriors slain and itself fallen into distress.
Like a water-wave that had risen from the ocean, foamy and roaring,
then, when the wind had stilled, was tossed into silence.

children.text: tyaktāṃ yajñāyudhaiḥ sarvair abhirūpaiś ca yājakaiḥ
children.translated_text: Like an altar abandoned by all the sacrificial implements and by handsome priests,
after the time of the soma-pressing had passed, with its sound gone.

children.text: goṣṭhamadhye sthitām ārtām acarantīṃ navaṃ tṛṇam
children.translated_text: Like an anguished cow standing in the middle of the cowshed, not grazing on fresh grass,
a mate of the herd, longing after being abandoned by the bull.
Like a new necklace of pearls deprived of genuine jewels,

children.text: viyuktāṃ maṇibhir jātyair navāṃ muktāvalīm iva ||
children.translated_text: bright with smooth rays and excellent, as though blazing.

children.text: sahasā calitāṃ sthānān mahīṃ puṇyakṣayād gatām
children.translated_text: Like a star suddenly shaken from its place and fallen from heaven through the exhaustion of merit,
with the expanse of its radiance withdrawn.
Like a forest creeper laden with flowers at spring's end and rich with intoxicated bees,
weary after being scorched by sparks of a swift forest fire.
With all its commercial quarters bewildered and its markets and shops contracted,
like the sky covered by clouds, its moon and stars hidden.
Covered with broken cups from which the best drink had been exhausted,
like a disorderly drinking ground in the sky, bereft of its drinkers.
Its ground cut up and sunken, covered with broken vessels,
like a fallen water station, broken after its water had been used up.
Like a broad and stretched bowstring of forceful warriors, fitted with a loop,

children.text: bhūmau bāṇair viniṣkṛttāṃ patitāṃ jyām ivāyudhāt ||
children.translated_text: cut off by arrows and fallen from the weapon onto the ground.
Like a weak young mare suddenly driven by a battle-maddened horseman in war,
her gear thrown down and herself abandoned.
Like the splendor of the sun when, in the deep rainy season, he has entered a mass of clouds,
concealed by dark blue rain-clouds.

children.text: bharatas tu rathasthaḥ sañ śrīmān daśarathātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: But glorious <s>Bharata</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, standing in the chariot,
spoke these words to the charioteer who was driving the excellent chariot:

children.text: kiṃ nu khalv adya gambhīro mūrchito na niśamyate
children.translated_text: Why indeed today is the deep and swelling
sound of song and instruments in <s>Ayodhyā</s> not heard as before?
The fragrance of intoxication from vāruṇī wine and the fragrance of garlands,
and the scent of smoked agaru do not waft on every side.
The noise of splendid vehicles, the pleasing neigh of horses,
the cry of rutting elephants, and the great rumble of chariots

children.text: nedānīṃ śrūyate puryām asyāṃ rāme vivāsite ||
children.translated_text: are not now heard in this city, since <s>Rāma</s> has been exiled.
The great roads of <s>Ayodhyā</s> no longer shine with young men, handsomely dressed,
walking proudly and gathering together.

children.text: evaṃ bahuvidhaṃ jalpan viveśa vasatiṃ pituḥ
children.translated_text: Speaking in many ways like this, he entered his father's dwelling,

children.text: tena hīnāṃ narendreṇa siṃhahīnāṃ guhām iva ||
children.translated_text: deprived of that lord of men, like a cave deprived of a lion.

children.text: tato nikṣipya mātṝn sa ayodhyāyāṃ dṛḍhavrataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, having settled his mothers in <s>Ayodhyā</s>, firm in his vow,
<s>Bharata</s>, tormented by grief, then said this to the elders:
I shall go to <s>Nandigrāma</s>; today I take leave of all of you.

children.text: tatra duḥkham idaṃ sarvaṃ sahiṣye rāghavaṃ vinā ||
children.translated_text: There I shall endure all this sorrow without <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: gataś ca hi divaṃ rājā vanasthaś ca gurur mama
children.translated_text: For the king has gone to heaven, and my elder is dwelling in the forest.

children.text: rāmaṃ pratīkṣe rājyāya sa hi rājā mahāyaśāḥ ||
children.translated_text: I await <s>Rāma</s> for the kingship, for he is the greatly famed king.

children.text: etac chrutvā śubhaṃ vākyaṃ bharatasya mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing this auspicious speech of great-souled <s>Bharata</s>,

children.text: abruvan mantriṇaḥ sarve vasiṣṭhaś ca purohitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: all the ministers and the priest <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> said:

children.text: sadṛśaṃ ślāghanīyaṃ ca yad uktaṃ bharata tvayā
children.translated_text: Fitting and praiseworthy is the word you have spoken, <s>Bharata</s>;
it is truly appropriate to you, arising from affection for your brother.
Of you, always attached to your kinsman and standing firm in brotherly love,
who has entered the noble path, what man would not approve?
Having heard the ministers' words, pleasing and just as he desired,

children.text: abravīt sārathiṃ vākyaṃ ratho me yujyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: he said this to the charioteer: Let my chariot be yoked.
With joyful face, having respectfully greeted all his mothers,
that glorious one mounted the chariot together with <s>Śatrughna</s>.

children.text: āruhya tu rathaṃ śīghraṃ śatrughnabharatāv ubhau
children.translated_text: Having quickly mounted the chariot, both <s>Śatrughna</s> and <s>Bharata</s>,
exceedingly delighted, set out, surrounded by ministers and priests.
In front there were the elders, the twice-born headed by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.
All of them set out facing east, to where <s>Nandigrāma</s> was.
And that army, though not summoned, crowded with elephants, horses, and chariots,

children.text: prayayau bharate yāte sarve ca puravāsinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: set out when <s>Bharata</s> had gone, and so did all the residents of the city.

children.text: rathasthaḥ sa tu dharmātmā bharato bhrātṛvatsalaḥ
children.translated_text: But righteous <s>Bharata</s>, devoted to his brother, standing in his chariot,

children.text: nandigrāmaṃ yayau tūrṇaṃ śirasy ādhāya pāduke ||
children.translated_text: quickly went to <s>Nandigrāma</s>, placing the sandals upon his head.

children.text: tatas tu bharataḥ kṣipraṃ nandigrāmaṃ praviśya saḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Bharata</s> quickly entered <s>Nandigrāma</s>,

children.text: avatīrya rathāt tūrṇaṃ gurūn idam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: and, swiftly descending from the chariot, spoke these words to his elders:

children.text: etad rājyaṃ mama bhrātrā dattaṃ saṃnyāsavat svayam
children.translated_text: This kingdom has been given to me personally by my brother, as something deposited in trust.
And these gold-adorned sandals will carry its acquisition and protection;
I shall guard it until the coming of <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: kṣipraṃ saṃyojayitvā tu rāghavasya punaḥ svayam
children.translated_text: After quickly restoring them myself to <s>Rāghava</s> again,

children.text: caraṇau tau tu rāmasya drakṣyāmi sahapādukau ||
children.translated_text: I shall see those two feet of <s>Rāma</s> together with the sandals.
Then, my burden laid down, reunited with <s>Rāghava</s>,
and having handed the kingdom over to my elder, I shall devote myself to service of my elder.
Having given these excellent sandals, kept in trust, back to <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: rājyaṃ cedam ayodhyāṃ ca dhūtapāpo bhavāmi ca ||
children.translated_text: and this kingdom and <s>Ayodhyā</s> as well, I shall become cleansed of sin.
When <s>Kākutstha</s> is consecrated and the people are joyful and delighted,

children.text: prītir mama yaśaś caiva bhaved rājyāc caturguṇam ||
children.translated_text: my satisfaction and fame will become four times greater than from kingship.

children.text: evaṃ tu vilapan dīno bharataḥ sa mahāyaśāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus lamenting in misery, that greatly renowned <s>Bharata</s>
ruled at <s>Nandigrāma</s>, sorrowful, together with his ministers.
That lord, wearing bark garments and matted hair, dressed in the garb of an ascetic,
the heroic <s>Bharata</s>, stayed then at <s>Nandigrāma</s> with his army.
<s>Bharata</s>, devoted to his brother, longing for <s>Rāma</s>'s return,
obedient to his brother's command and steadfast in his vow at that time,
then consecrated the sandals and lived at <s>Nandigrāma</s>.
<s>Bharata</s> reported every act of rule to the sandals.
When <s>Bharata</s> had gone back, <s>Rāma</s>, dwelling in the ascetic grove,
then noticed the anxiety and uneasiness of the ascetics.
Those who were there in the ascetics' hermitage before <s>Citrakūṭa</s>,

children.text: rāmam āśritya niratās tān alakṣayad utsukān ||
children.translated_text: who had settled there relying on <s>Rāma</s>, he saw to be uneasy.

children.text: nayanair bhṛkuṭībhiś ca rāmaṃ nirdiśya śaṅkitāḥ
children.translated_text: With their eyes and brows they pointed to <s>Rāma</s>, apprehensive,

children.text: anyonyam upajalpantaḥ śanaiś cakrur mithaḥ kathāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, whispering to one another, they quietly held conversations among themselves.

children.text: teṣām autsukyam ālakṣya rāmas tv ātmani śaṅkitaḥ
children.translated_text: Perceiving their uneasiness, <s>Rāma</s>, suspecting some fault in himself,
then joined his palms and spoke these words to the sage, the head of the community:

children.text: na kaccid bhagavan kiṃcit pūrvavṛttam idaṃ mayi
children.translated_text: Surely, venerable sir, no earlier conduct of mine
is seen as improper, because of which the ascetics are disturbed?

children.text: pramādāc caritaṃ kaccit kiṃcin nāvarajasya me
children.translated_text: Surely nothing done through negligence by my younger brother
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> has been seen by the seers as somehow unworthy of him?
Surely <s>Sītā</s>, while wishing to serve you and devoted to serving me,

children.text: pramadābhyucitāṃ vṛttiṃ sītā yuktaṃ na vartate ||
children.translated_text: is not behaving in a manner more fitting for women and unsuitable here?

children.text: atharṣir jarayā vṛddhas tapasā ca jarāṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: Then the sage, aged with years and grown old through austerity,
as if trembling, spoke to <s>Rāma</s>, who was full of compassion for beings:
How could there be any wavering in <s>Vaidehī</s>, who has an auspicious nature
and is likewise devoted to what is auspicious, dear son, especially toward ascetics?

children.text: tvannimittam idaṃ tāvat tāpasān prati vartate
children.translated_text: For now this is happening toward the ascetics on your account.

children.text: rakṣobhyas tena saṃvignāḥ kathayanti mithaḥ kathāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Alarmed by the rākṣasas, they are therefore talking among themselves.
There is a certain rākṣasa here named <s>Khara</s>, younger brother of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
who has uprooted all the ascetics dwelling in <s>Janasthāna</s>.

children.text: dhṛṣṭaś ca jitakāśī ca nṛśaṃsaḥ puruṣādakaḥ
children.translated_text: Insolent, thinking himself victorious, cruel, and a devourer of men,

children.text: avaliptaś ca pāpaś ca tvāṃ ca tāta na mṛṣyate ||
children.translated_text: arrogant and evil, he does not tolerate you either, dear son.

children.text: tvaṃ yadā prabhṛti hy asminn āśrame tāta vartase
children.translated_text: From the time, dear son, that you began living in this hermitage,
from that time onward the rākṣasas have been tormenting the ascetics.

children.text: darśayanti hi bībhatsaiḥ krūrair bhīṣaṇakair api
children.translated_text: For with hideous, cruel, and terrifying forms,
and with various misshapen forms unpleasant to see, they show themselves.
After assailing the ascetics with inauspicious and impure things,

children.text: pratighnanty aparān kṣipram anāryāḥ purataḥ sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the ignoble ones, standing before them, quickly strike others down.

children.text: teṣu teṣv āśramasthāneṣv abuddham avalīya ca
children.translated_text: In one hermitage-site after another, hiding where they are not perceived,
those petty-minded ones take pleasure there, destroying the ascetics.
They throw away the ladles and vessels, and they sprinkle the fires with water.
They crush the water pots when the oblation is at hand.
Wishing to abandon the hermitages possessed by those evil-minded ones,
the seers today are urging me to go to another region.

children.text: tat purā rāma śārīrām upahiṃsāṃ tapasviṣu
children.translated_text: So, before those wicked ones inflict bodily injury

children.text: darśayanti hi duṣṭās te tyakṣyāma imam āśramam ||
children.translated_text: upon the ascetics, O <s>Rāma</s>, we shall leave this hermitage.
Not far from here is a beautiful forest rich in roots and fruits.
I, together with my group, shall again take refuge in that ancient hermitage.

children.text: kharas tvayy api cāyuktaṃ purā tāta pravartate
children.translated_text: Before <s>Khara</s> acts improperly even toward you, dear son,

children.text: sahāsmābhir ito gaccha yadi buddhiḥ pravartate ||
children.translated_text: go from here together with us, if your mind is so inclined.

children.text: sakalatrasya saṃdeho nityaṃ yat tasya rāghava
children.translated_text: Since there is constant danger for one with his wife from him, O <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: samarthasyāpi hi sato vāso duḥkham ihādya te ||
children.translated_text: even though you are capable, your dwelling here now is painful.

children.text: ity uktavantaṃ rāmas taṃ rājaputras tapasvinam
children.translated_text: When that ascetic had spoken thus, <s>Rāma</s>, the prince,
could not restrain him, eager as he was, with words in reply.
Having taken leave of <s>Rāghava</s>, having honored him, and having reassured him,

children.text: sa jagāmāśramaṃ tyaktvā kulaiḥ kulapatiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: the head of the community left the hermitage, together with his families.

children.text: rāmaḥ saṃsādhya tv ṛṣigaṇam anugamanād deśāt tasmāt kulapatim abhivādyarṣim
children.translated_text: But <s>Rāma</s>, having arranged matters with the group of seers and dissuaded the head of the community from accompanying him from that region, bowed to the sage.

children.text: samyakprītais tair anumata upadiṣṭārthaḥ puṇyaṃ vāsāya svanilayam upasaṃpede ||
children.translated_text: When they were fully pleased and had given their consent, he, having received instruction about his purpose, returned to his own blessed dwelling place.

children.text: āśramaṃ tv ṛṣivirahitaṃ prabhuḥ kṣaṇam api na jahau sa rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: But the lord <s>Rāghava</s> did not leave the hermitage, bereft of seers, even for a moment;

children.text: rāghavaṃ hi satatam anugatās tāpasāś cārṣacaritadhṛtaguṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for ascetics, bearing virtues grounded in the conduct of seers, constantly followed <s>Rāghava</s>.
But when the ascetics had departed, <s>Rāghava</s> reflected;

children.text: na tatrārocayad vāsaṃ kāraṇair bahubhis tadā ||
children.translated_text: for many reasons he then found no pleasure in dwelling there.

children.text: iha me bharato dṛṣṭo mātaraś ca sanāgarāḥ
children.translated_text: Here <s>Bharata</s> was seen by me, together with my mothers and the townspeople;

children.text: sā ca me smṛtir anveti tān nityam anuśocataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and that memory follows me, as I constantly grieve over them.
Because of the encampment of that great-souled one's army,
great trampling and damage were caused by the dung of horses and elephants.

children.text: tasmād anyatra gacchāma iti saṃcintya rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore let us go elsewhere, <s>Rāghava</s> thought;

children.text: prātiṣṭhata sa vaidehyā lakṣmaṇena ca saṃgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and he set out together with <s>Vaidehī</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: so 'trer āśramam āsādya taṃ vavande mahāyaśāḥ
children.translated_text: Having reached <s>Atri</s>'s hermitage, the greatly renowned one bowed to him;

children.text: taṃ cāpi bhagavān atriḥ putravat pratyapadyata ||
children.translated_text: and venerable <s>Atri</s> received him like a son.

children.text: svayam ātithyam ādiśya sarvam asya susatkṛtam
children.translated_text: After personally arranging hospitality, everything for him was duly honored;

children.text: saumitriṃ ca mahābhāgāṃ sītāṃ ca samasāntvayat ||
children.translated_text: and he comforted <s>Saumitri</s> and the greatly fortunate <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: patnīṃ ca samanuprāptāṃ vṛddhām āmantrya satkṛtām
children.translated_text: Then, summoning his wife, who had come near, aged and honored,
the knower of <s>dharma</s>, devoted to the welfare of all beings, spoke reassuringly.
To greatly fortunate <s>Anasūyā</s>, an ascetic woman practicing <s>dharma</s>,
the best of seers said, Receive <s>Vaidehī</s>.
And to <s>Rāma</s> he described that ascetic woman practicing <s>dharma</s>:

children.text: daśa varṣāṇy anāvṛṣṭyā dagdhe loke nirantaram ||
children.translated_text: During ten years of drought, when the world was continually scorched,

children.text: yayā mūlaphale sṛṣṭe jāhnavī ca pravartitā
children.translated_text: by her roots and fruits were created, and the <s>Jāhnavī</s> was set flowing;

children.text: ugreṇa tapasā yuktā niyamaiś cāpy alaṃkṛtā ||
children.translated_text: she was endowed with fierce asceticism and adorned with observances.
For ten thousand years she performed great austerity;
by the vows of <s>Anasūyā</s>, dear one, obstacles were warded off.
And for the sake of the gods' task, when she was hurrying,

children.text: daśarātraṃ kṛtvā rātriḥ seyaṃ māteva te 'nagha ||
children.translated_text: she made a single night into ten nights; she is like a mother to you, sinless one.
Let <s>Vaidehī</s> approach this famous woman, worthy of homage from all beings,
aged and always free from anger.

children.text: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ tam ṛṣiṃ tathety uktvā sa rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: When the seer spoke thus, <s>Rāghava</s> said, So be it,

children.text: sītām uvāca dharmajñām idaṃ vacanam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: and spoke these excellent words to <s>Sītā</s>, who knew <s>dharma</s>:

children.text: rājaputri śrutaṃ tv etan muner asya samīritam
children.translated_text: Princess, you have heard this uttered by this sage;
quickly approach the ascetic woman for your own welfare.

children.text: anasūyeti yā loke karmabhiḥ khyātim āgatā
children.translated_text: She who has become famous in the world by her deeds as <s>Anasūyā</s>,

children.text: tāṃ śīghram abhigaccha tvam abhigamyāṃ tapasvinīm ||
children.translated_text: quickly approach that approachable ascetic woman.

children.text: sītā tv etad vacaḥ śrutvā rāghavasya hitaiṣiṇī
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s>, seeking <s>Rāghava</s>'s good, heard this word of his;
and <s>Maithilī</s> went up to <s>Atri</s>'s wife, that knower of <s>dharma</s>.
She was loose-limbed, wrinkled, aged, her hair grey-white with old age,
her limbs constantly trembling like a plantain tree in the wind.

children.text: tāṃ tu sītā mahābhāgām anasūyāṃ pativratām
children.translated_text: But composed <s>Sītā</s> saluted that greatly fortunate <s>Anasūyā</s>,
the devoted wife, and stated her own name.

children.text: abhivādya ca vaidehī tāpasīṃ tām aninditām
children.translated_text: After saluting that blameless ascetic woman, <s>Vaidehī</s>,
with cupped joined hands, delighted, asked after her well-being.

children.text: tataḥ sītāṃ mahābhāgāṃ dṛṣṭvā tāṃ dharmacāriṇīm
children.translated_text: Then seeing greatly fortunate <s>Sītā</s>, that follower of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: sāntvayanty abravīd dhṛṣṭā diṣṭyā dharmam avekṣase ||
children.translated_text: she, delighted and consoling her, said, Fortunately you have regard for <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: tyaktvā jñātijanaṃ sīte mānam ṛddhiṃ ca mānini
children.translated_text: Leaving your kinsfolk, honor, and prosperity, O proud <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: avaruddhaṃ vane rāmaṃ diṣṭyā tvam anugacchasi ||
children.translated_text: fortunately you follow <s>Rāma</s>, confined to the forest.

children.text: nagarastho vanastho vā pāpo vā yadi vāśubhaḥ
children.translated_text: Whether he dwells in the city or in the forest, whether he is sinful or auspicious,

children.text: yāsāṃ strīṇāṃ priyo bhartā tāsāṃ lokā mahodayāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those women to whom their husband is dear have worlds of great prosperity.

children.text: duḥśīlaḥ kāmavṛtto vā dhanair vā parivarjitaḥ
children.translated_text: Whether he is ill-conducted, ruled by desire, or deprived of wealth,
for women of noble nature the husband is the supreme deity.

children.text: nāto viśiṣṭaṃ paśyāmi bāndhavaṃ vimṛśanty aham
children.translated_text: Reflecting on it, I see no kinsman superior to him,

children.text: sarvatra yogyaṃ vaidehi tapaḥ kṛtam ivāvyayam ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Vaidehī</s>, fit in all circumstances, like inexhaustible ascetic merit.

children.text: na tv evam avagacchanti guṇadoṣam asatstriyaḥ
children.translated_text: But false women do not understand merit and fault in this way,
whose hearts are ruled by the words of desire, though they live under a husband's protection.

children.text: prāpnuvanty ayaśaś caiva dharmabhraṃśaṃ ca maithili
children.translated_text: They incur both disgrace and a fall from <s>dharma</s>, O <s>Maithilī</s>,

children.text: akāryavaśam āpannāḥ striyo yāḥ khalu tadvidhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: women of that sort who have come under the sway of what should not be done.
But women like you, endowed with virtues and seeing both this world and the next,

children.text: striyaḥ svarge cariṣyanti yathā puṇyakṛtas tathā ||
children.translated_text: will move in heaven just as those who have performed meritorious acts do.

children.text: sā tv evam uktā vaidehī anasūyānasūyayā
children.translated_text: <s>Vaidehī</s>, thus addressed by <s>Anasūyā</s>, who was free from envy,
honored her words and began to speak softly:

children.text: naitad āścaryam āryāyā yan māṃ tvam anubhāṣase
children.translated_text: It is no wonder, noble lady, that you speak to me in this way;

children.text: viditaṃ tu mamāpy etad yathā nāryāḥ patir guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: for this too is known to me, that a woman's husband is her guru.

children.text: yady apy eṣa bhaved bhartā mamārye vṛttavarjitaḥ
children.translated_text: Even if this husband of mine, noble lady, were devoid of good conduct,

children.text: advaidham upacartavyas tathāpy eṣa mayā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: even then he would have to be served by me without duplicity.

children.text: kiṃ punar yo guṇaślāghyaḥ sānukrośo jitendriyaḥ
children.translated_text: How much more one who is praiseworthy for virtues, compassionate, self-controlled,
steadfast in affection, righteous, obedient to his mother, and dear to his father.

children.text: yāṃ vṛttiṃ vartate rāmaḥ kausalyāyāṃ mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: The conduct that mighty <s>Rāma</s> maintains toward <s>Kausalyā</s>,

children.text: tām eva nṛpanārīṇām anyāsām api vartate ||
children.translated_text: that same conduct he maintains toward the king's other wives as well.

children.text: sakṛd dṛṣṭāsv api strīṣu nṛpeṇa nṛpavatsalaḥ
children.translated_text: Toward women seen even once by the king, the hero, loving toward the king,

children.text: mātṛvad vartate vīro mānam utsṛjya dharmavit ||
children.translated_text: knowing <s>dharma</s>, conducts himself like a son toward a mother, setting aside pride.

children.text: āgacchantyāś ca vijanaṃ vanam evaṃ bhayāvaham
children.translated_text: And as I came to the deserted forest, so fearful,

children.text: samāhitaṃ hi me śvaśrvā hṛdaye yat sthitaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: my mother-in-law fixed in my heart what was already settled in me.

children.text: pāṇipradānakāle ca yat purā tv agnisaṃnidhau
children.translated_text: And at the time of the giving of my hand, formerly, in the presence of the fire...

children.text: anuśiṣṭā jananyāsmi vākyaṃ tad api me dhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: I have been instructed by my mother; and that command too has been retained by me.

children.text: navīkṛtaṃ tu tat sarvaṃ vākyais te dharmacāriṇi
children.translated_text: But all that has now been renewed by your words, O woman who practices <s>dharma</s>.
For a woman, no austerity other than service to her husband is prescribed.
<s>Sāvitrī</s>, having performed service to her husband, is honored in heaven;

children.text: tathāvṛttiś ca yātā tvaṃ patiśuśrūṣayā divam ||
children.translated_text: and you too, following that same conduct, have gone to heaven through service to your husband.

children.text: variṣṭhā sarvanārīṇām eṣā ca divi devatā
children.translated_text: This goddess too is the foremost of all women in heaven;

children.text: rohiṇī ca vinā candraṃ muhūrtam api dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Rohiṇī</s> is not seen even for a moment apart from the moon.
Such excellent women, firmly vowed to their husbands,
are honored in the world of the gods by their own meritorious deeds.
Then <s>Anasūyā</s>, delighted on hearing the speech spoken by <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: śirasy āghrāya covāca maithilīṃ harṣayanty uta ||
children.translated_text: smelled <s>Maithilī</s>'s head and spoke, gladdening her.

children.text: niyamair vividhair āptaṃ tapo hi mahad asti me
children.translated_text: By many observances I have gained great ascetic power;

children.text: tat saṃśritya balaṃ sīte chandaye tvāṃ śucivrate ||
children.translated_text: relying on that strength, O <s>Sītā</s> of pure vows, I invite you to choose a boon.

children.text: upapannaṃ ca yuktaṃ ca vacanaṃ tava maithili
children.translated_text: Your speech, O <s>Maithilī</s>, is proper and fitting;

children.text: prītā cāsmy ucitaṃ kiṃ te karavāṇi bravīhi me
children.translated_text: I am pleased. Tell me, what suitable thing may I do for you?
"It is already done," <s>Sītā</s> said to the woman endowed with ascetic power.

children.text: sā tv evam uktā dharmajñā tayā prītatarābhavat
children.translated_text: But when she had been addressed in this way by <s>Sītā</s>, that knower of <s>dharma</s> became still more pleased.

children.text: saphalaṃ ca praharṣaṃ te hanta sīte karomy aham ||
children.translated_text: Come then, O <s>Sītā</s>, I shall make this joy of yours fruitful.

children.text: idaṃ divyaṃ varaṃ mālyaṃ vastram ābharaṇāni ca
children.translated_text: Here is a divine boon: a garland, a garment, and ornaments,
and, O <s>Vaidehī</s>, a very precious body-coloring and unguent.

children.text: mayā dattam idaṃ sīte tava gātrāṇi śobhayet
children.translated_text: Given by me, O <s>Sītā</s>, this will adorn your limbs;
it will remain always fitting and unfaded.
With my limbs anointed by this divine cosmetic, O daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,

children.text: śobhayiṣyāmi bhartāraṃ yathā śrīr viṣṇum avyayam ||
children.translated_text: I shall make my husband shine, as <s>Śrī</s> adorns imperishable <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: sā vastram aṅgarāgaṃ ca bhūṣaṇāni srajas tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Maithilī</s> accepted the garment, the body-coloring,
the ornaments and the garlands, that unsurpassed gift of affection.

children.text: pratigṛhya ca tat sītā prītidānaṃ yaśasvinī
children.translated_text: Having accepted that gift of affection, illustrious <s>Sītā</s>,
steadfast, with the hollow of her joined palms clasped, attended upon the rich-in-austerity woman.
As <s>Sītā</s> sat attending upon her in that way, firm-vowed <s>Anasūyā</s>

children.text: vacanaṃ praṣṭum ārebhe kathāṃ kāṃcid anupriyām ||
children.translated_text: began to ask a question, a certain pleasing story.

children.text: svayaṃvare kila prāptā tvam anena yaśasvinā
children.translated_text: At a svayaṃvara, they say, you were won by this illustrious man,

children.text: rāghaveṇeti me sīte kathā śrutim upāgatā ||
children.translated_text: by <s>Rāghava</s>, O <s>Sītā</s>; that story has come to my hearing.

children.text: tāṃ kathāṃ śrotum icchāmi vistareṇa ca maithili
children.translated_text: I wish to hear that story in detail, O <s>Maithilī</s>;

children.text: yathānubhūtaṃ kārtsnyena tan me tvaṃ vaktum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: as you experienced it, in its entirety, you should tell it to me.

children.text: evam uktā tu sā sītā tāṃ tato dharmacāriṇīm
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Sītā</s> then said to that woman who practiced <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: śrūyatām iti coktvā vai kathayāmāsa tāṃ kathām ||
children.translated_text: "Listen," and then she told that story.
There was a heroic lord of <s>Mithilā</s>, named <s>Janaka</s>, a knower of <s>dharma</s>;
devoted to the <s>dharma</s> of warriors, he ruled the earth justly.
As he held a plough in his hand and was ploughing the circuit of a field,

children.text: ahaṃ kilotthitā bhittvā jagatīṃ nṛpateḥ sutā ||
children.translated_text: I, his daughter, arose, they say, breaking through the earth.
Seeing me, the king, intent on scattering the clods with his fist,
with all my limbs covered in dust, <s>Janaka</s> was amazed.

children.text: anapatyena ca snehād aṅkam āropya ca svayam
children.translated_text: Since he was childless, out of affection he himself lifted me onto his lap,

children.text: mameyaṃ tanayety uktvā sneho mayi nipātitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and saying, "This is my daughter," he placed his affection upon me.
And a voice in the sky, incomparable and superhuman, was uttered, they say:

children.text: evam etan narapate dharmeṇa tanayā tava ||
children.translated_text: "So it is, O king; by <s>dharma</s> she is your daughter."

children.text: tataḥ prahṛṣṭo dharmātmā pitā me mithilādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: Then my father, the righteous lord of <s>Mithilā</s>, was overjoyed;

children.text: avāpto vipulām ṛddhiṃ mām avāpya narādhipaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that king obtained abundant prosperity by obtaining me.
I was given, as he wished, to his eldest queen, that woman of meritorious acts,
and by her, affectionate with a mother's love, I was honored and cherished.

children.text: patisaṃyogasulabhaṃ vayo dṛṣṭvā tu me pitā
children.translated_text: But when my father saw that my age had become suitable for union with a husband,
he fell into anxious distress, like a poor man at the loss of wealth.

children.text: sadṛśāc cāpakṛṣṭāc ca loke kanyāpitā janāt
children.translated_text: In this world, from people equal or inferior to him, the father of a maiden
incurs humiliation, even if he is equal to <s>Śakra</s> on earth.
Seeing that humiliation close at hand in his own case, the king
entered an ocean of anxiety and found no far shore, like a man without a raft.

children.text: ayonijāṃ hi māṃ jñātvā nādhyagacchat sa cintayan
children.translated_text: Knowing that I was not born from a womb, the protector of the earth, while reflecting,

children.text: sadṛśaṃ cānurūpaṃ ca mahīpālaḥ patiṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: could not find a husband suitable and fitting for me.

children.text: tasya buddhir iyaṃ jātā cintayānasya saṃtatam
children.translated_text: As he continually reflected in this way, this thought arose in the wise king:
"I shall hold a svayaṃvara for my daughter."
At a great sacrifice of his at that time, by great-souled <s>Varuṇa</s>,
a choice bow was given with pleasure, along with two quivers of inexhaustible arrows.

children.text: asaṃcālyaṃ manuṣyaiś ca yatnenāpi ca gauravāt
children.translated_text: Because of its weight, that bow was unmovable by men even with effort;

children.text: tan na śaktā namayituṃ svapneṣv api narādhipāḥ ||
children.translated_text: kings were unable even in dreams to bend it.

children.text: tad dhanuḥ prāpya me pitrā vyāhṛtaṃ satyavādinā
children.translated_text: Having received that bow, my truth-speaking father declared,
in an assembly of kings, after first inviting the rulers:

children.text: idaṃ ca dhanur udyamya sajyaṃ yaḥ kurute naraḥ
children.translated_text: "The man who lifts this bow and strings it

children.text: tasya me duhitā bhāryā bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: will without doubt have my daughter as his wife."

children.text: tac ca dṛṣṭvā dhanuḥśreṣṭhaṃ gauravād girisaṃnibham
