children.translated_text: Seeing that best of bows, like a mountain because of its weight,

children.text: abhivādya nṛpā jagmur aśaktās tasya tolane ||
children.translated_text: the kings bowed and went away, unable to lift it.
But after a very long time, this greatly radiant <s>Rāghava</s>
came together with <s>Viśvāmitra</s> to see the sacrifice.
<s>Rāma</s>, whose valor is true, came with his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>;

children.text: viśvāmitras tu dharmātmā mama pitrā supūjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and righteous <s>Viśvāmitra</s> was highly honored by my father.
There he spoke to my father about the two brothers, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:
"These two are the sons of <s>Daśaratha</s>, desiring to see the bow."

children.text: ity uktas tena vipreṇa tad dhanuḥ samupānayat ||
children.translated_text: When thus addressed by that brahmin, he brought that bow near.
In only the interval of a blink, that mighty one bent it,
and, having quickly set the string on it, the mighty one drew it to full stretch.

children.text: tena pūrayatā vegān madhye bhagnaṃ dvidhā dhanuḥ
children.translated_text: As he drew it with force, the bow broke in the middle into two pieces.
Its dreadful sound was like that of a thunderbolt fallen to earth.
Then there I was made ready to be given to <s>Rāma</s> by my father, whose resolve was true,
after he had lifted up the excellent water vessel.

children.text: dīyamānāṃ na tu tadā pratijagrāha rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: But then <s>Rāghava</s> did not accept me as I was being given,
without knowing the wish of his father, the lord, the ruler of <s>Ayodhyā</s>.

children.text: tataḥ śvaśuram āmantrya vṛddhaṃ daśarathaṃ nṛpam
children.translated_text: Then, after my father had invited his father-in-law, the aged king <s>Daśaratha</s>,

children.text: mama pitrā ahaṃ dattā rāmāya viditātmane ||
children.translated_text: I was given by my father to wise <s>Rāma</s>.
And my virtuous younger sister <s>Ūrmilā</s>, lovely to behold,

children.text: bhāryārthe lakṣmaṇasyāpi dattā pitrā mama svayam ||
children.translated_text: was also given by my father himself for the purpose of being <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s wife.

children.text: evaṃ dattāsmi rāmāya tadā tasmin svayaṃvare
children.translated_text: Thus I was given to <s>Rāma</s> then at that svayaṃvara,

children.text: anuraktā ca dharmeṇa patiṃ vīryavatāṃ varam ||
children.translated_text: and, in accordance with <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty), I became devoted to my husband, the best of the valiant.

children.text: anasūyā tu dharmajñā śrutvā tāṃ mahatīṃ kathām
children.translated_text: But <s>Anasūyā</s>, knowing <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty), having heard that great tale,
embraced <s>Maithilī</s> with both arms and smelled her head in affection.
Your speech has been clear in syllable and word, wondrous and sweet,

children.text: yathā svayaṃvaraṃ vṛttaṃ tat sarvaṃ hi śrutaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: and I have heard in full how the svayaṃvara took place.

children.text: rame 'haṃ kathayā te tu dṛḍhaṃ madhurabhāṣiṇi
children.translated_text: I take deep delight in your tale, sweet-speaking one,

children.text: ravir astaṃ gataḥ śrīmān upohya rajanīṃ śivām ||
children.translated_text: but the glorious sun has set, bringing on an auspicious night.
Of the birds that were scattered through the day in search of food,
the sound is heard at twilight as they settle down for sleep.
And these sages too, wet from bathing and carrying cleansed fruits,
are returning together, their bark garments soaked with water.
When oblations have been offered according to rule in the sages' agnihotras,
smoke, dove-grey and reddish, is seen lifted by the wind.
For the trees, with few leaves, have grown dense all around,

children.text: viprakṛṣṭe 'pi ye deśe na prakāśanti vai diśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so that even in a distant region the directions no longer shine forth.
Night-roaming beings move about on every side,
and these deer of the ascetic grove lie down at the altar-banks.
Night has begun, <s>Sītā</s>, adorned with stars,
and the moon, with moonlight as its covering, is seen risen in the sky.
Go now; I give you leave. Be <s>Rāma</s>'s attendant,
for I have been satisfied by you as you spoke sweetly.

children.text: alaṃkuru ca tāvat tvaṃ pratyakṣaṃ mama maithili
children.translated_text: And for a while adorn yourself before my eyes, <s>Maithilī</s>;
dear child, gladden me, shining with divine ornaments.
Then <s>Sītā</s>, like a daughter of the gods, adorned herself,

children.text: praṇamya śirasā tasyai rāmaṃ tv abhimukhī yayau ||
children.translated_text: and, bowing her head to her, went toward <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: tathā tu bhūṣitāṃ sītāṃ dadarśa vadatāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāghava</s>, best of speakers, saw <s>Sītā</s> thus adorned,
and he rejoiced at the affectionate gift of the ascetic woman.

children.text: nyavedayat tataḥ sarvaṃ sītā rāmāya maithilī
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Maithilī</s>, reported everything to <s>Rāma</s>:
the ascetic woman's loving gift of garments, ornaments, and garlands.

children.text: prahṛṣṭas tv abhavad rāmo lakṣmaṇaś ca mahārathaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> was delighted, and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the great chariot-warrior, too,
seeing the honor shown to <s>Maithilī</s>, so hard to obtain among human beings.

children.text: tatas tāṃ śarvarīṃ prītaḥ puṇyāṃ śaśinibhānanaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, pleased, the moon-faced <s>Raghunandana</s> spent that sacred night,
honored by perfected ascetics.
When that night had passed, after the ablutions and fire offerings had been performed,
the two tiger-like men took leave of the ascetics who ranged in the forest.

children.text: tāv ūcus te vanacarās tāpasā dharmacāriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Those forest-dwelling ascetics, followers of <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty), said to the two of them
how to move through that forest, which was overrun by rākṣasas.

children.text: eṣa panthā maharṣīṇāṃ phalāny āharatāṃ vane
children.translated_text: This is the path of the great seers when they gather fruits in the forest;

children.text: anena tu vanaṃ durgaṃ gantuṃ rāghava te kṣamam ||
children.translated_text: by this route, <s>Rāghava</s>, it is proper for you to go into the difficult forest.

children.text: itīva taiḥ prāñjalibhis tapasvibhir dvijaiḥ kṛtasvastyayanaḥ paraṃtapaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, with auspicious rites performed by those ascetics, brahmins with joined hands, the scorcher of foes

children.text: vanaṃ sabhāryaḥ praviveśa rāghavaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ sūrya ivābhramaṇḍalam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> entered the forest with his wife and with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, like the sun entering a mass of clouds.
Having entered the great wilderness, the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest, self-possessed
and unassailable <s>Rāma</s> saw a circle of ascetic hermitages.
It was enclosed by kuśa grass and bark cloth and enveloped in brahmanical splendor,
like the blazing, unassailable orb of the sun in the sky.
It was a refuge for all beings, its courtyard always well swept,

children.text: pūjitaṃ copanṛttaṃ ca nityam apsarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: honored and continually danced around by groups of apsarases.
It was adorned with spacious fire-houses, ladles and vessels, antelope skins and kuśa grass,
with fuel sticks, water jars, fruits, and roots.

children.text: āraṇyaiś ca mahāvṛkṣaiḥ puṇyaiḥ svāduphalair vṛtam
children.translated_text: It was surrounded by great wild trees, holy and bearing sweet fruits,
holy, honored with bali offerings and homa rites, and resounding with Vedic recitation.

children.text: puṣpair vanyaiḥ parikṣiptaṃ padminyā ca sapadmayā
children.translated_text: It was strewn with forest flowers and had a lotus pond full of lotuses,
and was inhabited by self-controlled ascetics eating fruits and roots, clothed in bark and black antelope skins.
It was surrounded by ancient sages shining like the sun and fire,
and adorned by holy supreme seers whose food was regulated.
That place, like the abode of <s>Brahmā</s>, resounded with Vedic recitation,
and was beautified by greatly fortunate brahmins who knew brahman.
Seeing that circle of ascetic hermitages, glorious <s>Rāghava</s>

children.text: abhyagacchan mahātejā vijyaṃ kṛtvā mahad dhanuḥ ||
children.translated_text: approached, greatly radiant, after unstringing his great bow.
Those great seers, endowed with divine knowledge, seeing <s>Rāma</s>...

children.text: abhyagacchaṃs tadā prītā vaidehīṃ ca yaśasvinīm ||
children.translated_text: Then, pleased, they approached the famous <s>Vaidehī</s> as well.

children.text: te taṃ somam ivodyantaṃ dṛṣṭvā vai dharmacāriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Those followers of <s>dharma</s>, seeing him like Soma rising,
uttered auspicious words, and the firm-vowed ones received him.
The form, bodily build, beauty, delicacy, and fine attire
of <s>Rāma</s>, dwelling in the forest, they saw with expressions of wonder.

children.text: vaidehīṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ rāmaṃ netrair animiṣair iva
children.translated_text: With unwinking eyes, as it were, they looked upon <s>Vaidehī</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and <s>Rāma</s>,
and all those forest-dwellers beheld them as something marvelous.
There the greatly fortunate ones, intent on the welfare of all beings,
lodged <s>Rāghava</s> as a guest in a leaf-hut.
Then, after honoring <s>Rāma</s> according to rule, those greatly fortunate men,
followers of <s>dharma</s>, bright like fire, brought water.

children.text: mūlaṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ vanyam āśramaṃ ca mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Roots, flowers, forest fruits, and the hermitage of the great-souled sage
they presented, and then the knowers of <s>dharma</s> spoke with joined palms:
The king is the protector of this people, a refuge, greatly renowned,

children.text: pūjanīyaś ca mānyaś ca rājā daṇḍadharo guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: worthy of worship, worthy of honor, the bearer of the rod, and a guru.
Like a fourth portion of <s>Indra</s>, he protects his subjects, O <s>Rāghava</s>;

children.text: rājā tasmād varān bhogān bhuṅkte lokanamaskṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore the king, saluted by the world, enjoys excellent pleasures.
We, dwelling in your realm, are to be protected by you;

children.text: nagarastho vanastho vā tvaṃ no rājā janeśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether you are in the city or in the forest, you are our king, lord of men.
We have laid aside the rod, O king; we have conquered anger and conquered the senses;
we ascetics rich in tapas must always be protected by you, like unborn children.

children.text: evam uktvā phalair mūlaiḥ puṣpair vanyaiś ca rāghavam
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, with fruits, roots, and forest flowers,
and with other various foods, they worshiped <s>Rāghava</s> together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Likewise other perfected ascetics, bright like fire,
living by right conduct, satisfied that lord according to proper custom.
Then <s>Rāma</s>, having received hospitality, at the rising of the sun,

children.text: āmantrya sa munīn sarvān vanam evānvagāhata ||
children.translated_text: took leave of all the sages and entered the forest itself.
Filled with herds of many kinds of deer, frequented by tigers and wolves,
with trees, creepers, and thickets crushed, its waters difficult to see,
with many birds crying out and with swarms of crickets sounding,
<s>Rāma</s>, followed by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, saw the middle of the forest.
But in the middle of that forest, filled with terrible beasts, <s>Kākutstha</s>
saw a man-eater, loud-roaring, like a mountain peak.
Deep-eyed, huge-mouthed, misshapen, with an uneven belly,
hideous, deformed, tall, distorted, and terrible to behold,
wearing a tiger skin, wet with fat and sprinkled with blood,
frightening all beings, with gaping mouth like Death itself,

children.text: trīn siṃhāṃś caturo vyāghrān dvau vṛkau pṛṣatān daśa
children.translated_text: with three lions, four tigers, two wolves, ten spotted deer,

children.text: saviṣāṇaṃ vasādigdhaṃ gajasya ca śiro mahat ||
children.translated_text: and the great tusked head of an elephant, smeared with fat,
hung upon an iron spear, roaring with a great noise,

children.text: sa rāmaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ caiva sītāṃ dṛṣṭvā ca maithilīm ||
children.translated_text: he, seeing <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and <s>Sītā</s>, the <s>Maithilī</s>,
rushed at them, greatly enraged, like Death the destroyer at creatures.

children.text: sa kṛtvā bhairavaṃ nādaṃ cālayann iva medinīm ||
children.translated_text: Making a fearsome roar, as though shaking the earth,
he took <s>Vaidehī</s> in his arm, stepped away, and then said:
You two, wearing matted hair and bark garments, with a wife, have little life left,
having entered the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest, carrying arrows, bows, and swords.

children.text: kathaṃ tāpasayor vāṃ ca vāsaḥ pramadayā saha ||
children.translated_text: How can the two of you ascetics dwell with a woman?
Unrighteous and sinful, who are you two, defilers of sages?

children.text: ahaṃ vanam idaṃ durgaṃ virādho nāma rākṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I am a rākṣasa named <s>Virādha</s>; in this difficult forest
I roam always armed, eating the flesh of seers.

children.text: iyaṃ nārī varārohā mama bhāryā bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: This woman of fine hips will become my wife,

children.text: yuvayoḥ pāpayoś cāhaṃ pāsyāmi rudhiraṃ mṛdhe ||
children.translated_text: and I shall drink the blood of you two sinners in battle.
Hearing that bold, arrogant speech
of evil-souled <s>Virādha</s>, as he spoke thus, <s>Janaka</s>'s daughter was terrified;
<s>Sītā</s> trembled from distress like a plantain tree in a strong wind.

children.text: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā rāghavaḥ sītāṃ virādhāṅkagatāṃ śubhām
children.translated_text: Seeing fair <s>Sītā</s> held in <s>Virādha</s>'s grasp,
<s>Rāghava</s> spoke a word to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, his mouth dry:
Look, gentle one, at the self-born daughter of king <s>Janaka</s>,
my wife, of auspicious conduct, placed in <s>Virādha</s>'s grasp,
the renowned princess, raised in the utmost happiness.

children.text: yad abhipretam asmāsu priyaṃ varavṛtaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: Whatever she intended regarding us, and whatever cherished boon she chose,

children.text: kaikeyyās tu susaṃvṛttaṃ kṣipram adyaiva lakṣmaṇa ||
children.translated_text: that purpose of <s>Kaikeyī</s> has now quickly come to pass this very day, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: yā na tuṣyati rājyena putrārthe dīrghadarśinī
children.translated_text: She who, far-seeing for her son's sake, is not satisfied with the kingdom,
by whom I, a friend to all beings, was sent to the forest,

children.text: adyedānīṃ sakāmā sā yā mātā mama madhyamā ||
children.translated_text: now, today, she, my middle mother, has fulfilled her desire.

children.text: parasparśāt tu vaidehyā na duḥkhataram asti me
children.translated_text: For me there is no sorrow more painful than another's touch upon <s>Vaidehī</s>,
not even my father's death, O <s>Saumitri</s>, nor the loss of my own kingdom.
As <s>Kākutstha</s> was speaking thus, overwhelmed with tears and grief,

children.text: abravīl lakṣmaṇaḥ kruddho ruddho nāga iva śvasan ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, angry, spoke, breathing like a confined serpent:

children.text: anātha iva bhūtānāṃ nāthas tvaṃ vāsavopamaḥ
children.translated_text: You are the lord of beings, like <s>Vāsava</s>, though you speak as if without a protector;
with me as your servant, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, why do you grieve?
When the rākṣasa is struck down today by an arrow from me in anger,

children.text: virādhasya gatāsor hi mahī pāsyati śoṇitam ||
children.translated_text: the earth will drink the blood of lifeless <s>Virādha</s>.

children.text: rājyakāme mama krodho bharate yo babhūva ha
children.translated_text: The anger I had toward <s>Bharata</s>, who desired the kingdom,

children.text: taṃ virādhe vimokṣyāmi vajrī vajram ivācale ||
children.translated_text: that I will release upon <s>Virādha</s>, as the wielder of the thunderbolt releases his thunderbolt upon a mountain.

children.text: mama bhujabalavegavegitaḥ patatu śaro 'sya mahān mahorasi
children.translated_text: Driven by the force and speed of my arm, let my great arrow fall upon his mighty chest.

children.text: vyapanayatu tanoś ca jīvitaṃ patatu tataś ca mahīṃ vighūrṇitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let him remove life from the body, and then, reeling, let him fall to the earth.

children.text: athovāca punar vākyaṃ virādhaḥ pūrayan vanam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Virādha</s> spoke again, filling the forest with his words:

children.text: ātmānaṃ pṛcchate brūtaṃ kau yuvāṃ kva gamiṣyathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Tell me, who are you two, since I ask about you, and where will you go?

children.text: tam uvāca tato rāmo rākṣasaṃ jvalitānanam
children.translated_text: Then mighty <s>Rāma</s> spoke to that rākṣasa, whose face was blazing,
as he questioned him, declaring his own descent from the line of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>:
Know us to be two kṣatriyas, endowed with good conduct, wandering in the forest.

children.text: tvāṃ tu veditum icchāvaḥ kas tvaṃ carasi daṇḍakān ||
children.translated_text: But we wish to know you: who are you, roaming through the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forests?

children.text: tam uvāca virādhas tu rāmaṃ satyaparākramam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Virādha</s> spoke to <s>Rāma</s>, whose valor was true:

children.text: hanta vakṣyāmi te rājan nibodha mama rāghava ||
children.translated_text: Very well, I shall tell you, king; listen to me, <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: putraḥ kila jayasyāhaṃ mātā mama śatahradā
children.translated_text: I am said to be the son of <s>Jaya</s>; my mother is <s>Śatahradā</s>.

children.text: virādha iti mām āhuḥ pṛthivyāṃ sarvarākṣasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: All the rākṣasas on earth call me <s>Virādha</s>.

children.text: tapasā cāpi me prāptā brahmaṇo hi prasādajā
children.translated_text: By austerity I have obtained from <s>Brahmā</s>, born of his favor,
that in the world I cannot be killed by weapons, nor cut or split apart.
Abandon this woman and, taking no thought for her, go back the way you came.

children.text: tvaramāṇau pālayethāṃ na vāṃ jīvitam ādade ||
children.translated_text: Hurry away and preserve yourselves; otherwise I shall take your lives.
<s>Rāma</s>, his eyes reddened with anger, replied to him with these words,
to the rākṣasa <s>Virādha</s>, deformed in shape and evil in mind:

children.text: kṣudra dhik tvāṃ tu hīnārthaṃ mṛtyum anveṣase dhruvam
children.translated_text: Base creature, shame on you, worthless one; you are certainly seeking death.

children.text: raṇe samprāpsyase tiṣṭha na me jīvan gamiṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: Stand firm; you will meet it in battle, and you will not go away alive from me.

children.text: tataḥ sajyaṃ dhanuḥ kṛtvā rāmaḥ suniśitāñśarān
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s> strung his bow and, setting very sharp arrows to it very swiftly,
struck the rākṣasa down.
From his bow, fitted with string and cord, he released seven arrows,
gold-feathered, of great speed, moving like <s>Suparṇa</s> and the wind.
Having pierced the body of <s>Virādha</s>, who was clothed in a tiger-skin,
those fire-like arrows fell to the earth, smeared with blood.
He roared a great roar and, seizing a spear like <s>Śakra</s>'s banner,
then shone forth like Death with mouth agape.
That spear, like a thunderbolt and like fire blazing in the sky,

children.text: dvābhyāṃ śarābhyāṃ cicheda rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, best of weapon-bearers, cut apart with two arrows.

children.text: tasya raudrasya saumitrir bāhuṃ savyaṃ babhañja ha
children.translated_text: <s>Saumitri</s> broke the left arm of that fierce one,

children.text: rāmas tu dakṣiṇaṃ bāhuṃ tarasā tasya rakṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Rāma</s> swiftly broke the right arm of that rākṣasa.
With his arms broken and his senses shaken, the rākṣasa quickly fell
to the ground like a mountain, dark as a cloud, split by a thunderbolt,
and <s>Virādha</s> spoke these words to <s>Kākutstha</s>, the bull among men:

children.text: kausalyā suprajās tāta rāmas tvaṃ vidito mayā
children.translated_text: Dear son of <s>Kausalyā</s>, I have recognized you as <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: vaidehī ca mahābhāgā lakṣmaṇaś ca mahāyaśāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and this greatly fortunate lady as <s>Vaidehī</s>, and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> as the very renowned one.

children.text: abhiśāpād ahaṃ ghorāṃ praviṣṭo rākṣasīṃ tanum
children.translated_text: Because of a curse I entered this terrible rākṣasa body.

children.text: tumburur nāma gandharvaḥ śapto vaiśravaṇena hi ||
children.translated_text: I am the gandharva named <s>Tumburu</s>, cursed by <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>.

children.text: prasādyamānaś ca mayā so 'bravīn māṃ mahāyaśāḥ
children.translated_text: When I was seeking to appease him, that greatly renowned one said to me:

children.text: yadā dāśarathī rāmas tvāṃ vadhiṣyati saṃyuge ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, kills you in battle,

children.text: tadā prakṛtim āpanno bhavān svargaṃ gamiṣyati
children.translated_text: then, restored to your true nature, you shall go to heaven.

children.text: iti vaiśravaṇo rājā rambhāsaktam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: So king <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> said to me, who was attached to <s>Rambhā</s>.
Angry because I did not attend upon him, he pronounced this upon me.
By your favor I have been released from that very terrible curse.

children.text: bhavanaṃ svaṃ gamiṣyāmi svasti vo 'stu paraṃtapa ||
children.translated_text: I shall go to my own abode. May there be well-being for you, scorcher of foes.
From here the righteous and powerful <s>Śarabhaṅga</s> dwells,
dear one, a great seer like the sun, at a distance of one and a half yojanas.

children.text: taṃ kṣipram abhigaccha tvaṃ sa te śreyo vidhāsyati
children.translated_text: Go quickly to him; he will arrange what is best for you.

children.text: avaṭe cāpi māṃ rāma nikṣipya kuśalī vraja ||
children.translated_text: And, <s>Rāma</s>, after casting me into a pit, go on safely.
This is the ancient <s>dharma</s> (customary rule) for rākṣasas whose life has departed:

children.text: avaṭe ye nidhīyante teṣāṃ lokāḥ sanātanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those who are placed in a pit have everlasting worlds.

children.text: evam uktvā tu kākutsthaṃ virādhaḥ śarapīḍitaḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken to <s>Kākutstha</s>, <s>Virādha</s>, tormented by arrows,
reached heaven, the mighty one having laid aside his body.
Lifting up <s>Virādha</s>, slack-throated, spike-eared, and making a great noise,
he threw him into a chasm, as he roared with a dreadful sound.

children.text: tatas tu tau kāñcanacitrakārmukau nihatya rakṣaḥ parigṛhya maithilīm
children.translated_text: Then those two, with bows adorned with gold, having slain the rākṣasa and taken <s>Maithilī</s> with them,

children.text: vijahratus tau muditau mahāvane divi sthitau candradivākarāv iva ||
children.translated_text: wandered joyfully in the great forest like the moon and the sun standing in the sky.

children.text: hatvā tu taṃ bhīmabalaṃ virādhaṃ rākṣasaṃ vane
children.translated_text: After killing that rākṣasa <s>Virādha</s>, dreadful in strength, in the forest,

children.text: tataḥ sītāṃ pariṣvajya samāśvāsya ca vīryavān
children.translated_text: then mighty <s>Rāma</s> embraced <s>Sītā</s> and comforted her,
and spoke to his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, blazing with splendor:

children.text: kaṣṭaṃ vanam idaṃ durgaṃ na ca smo vanagocarāḥ
children.translated_text: This forest is hard and difficult, and we are not forest-dwellers.
Let us go quickly to the ascetic rich in tapas, <s>Śarabhaṅga</s>.
<s>Rāghava</s> went to the hermitage of <s>Śarabhaṅga</s>.
Near <s>Śarabhaṅga</s>, whose divine power was great and whose self was purified by austerity,
he saw a great marvel.
He saw the lord of the gods, shining with a body like the sun and the sacrificial fire,
not touching the earth.
He saw the god, radiant with splendid ornaments and wearing spotless garments,
being worshiped by many great-souled beings of the same kind.
He saw, not far from him, a chariot traveling through the mid-air, yoked with tawny horses,
resembling the young sun.
He saw a spotless parasol, like a mass of white cloud, like the disk of the moon,
adorned with variegated garlands,
and excellent yak-tail fans with costly golden handles.
as his head was held by the two forest women and was being shaken;
and many <s>Gandharvas</s>, immortals, <s>Siddhas</s>, and supreme seers
praised the god who was in the sky with excellent words.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā śatakratuṃ tatra rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Śatakratu</s> there, <s>Rāma</s> said to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:

children.text: ye hayāḥ puruhūtasya purā śakrasya naḥ śrutāḥ
children.translated_text: "The horses of <s>Puruhūta</s>, of <s>Śakra</s>, about which we formerly heard,

children.text: antarikṣagatā divyās ta ime harayo dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: divine and moving through the sky, these must surely be those bay steeds.

children.text: ime ca puruṣavyāghra ye tiṣṭhanty abhito ratham
children.translated_text: And these men, tiger among men, who stand on every side of the chariot,
a hundred and a hundred, wearing earrings, young, with swords in their hands,
all of them have necklaces on their breasts, like blazing fire,
and they bear, O <s>Saumitri</s>, the form of men twenty-five years old.

children.text: etaddhi kila devānāṃ vayo bhavati nityadā
children.translated_text: For this, they say, is always the age of the gods,
as these tigers among men appear, pleasing to behold.

children.text: ihaiva saha vaidehyā muhūrtaṃ tiṣṭha lakṣmaṇa
children.translated_text: Stay right here with <s>Vaidehī</s> for a moment, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: yāvaj jānāmy ahaṃ vyaktaṃ ka eṣa dyutimān rathe ||
children.translated_text: until I know clearly who this radiant one in the chariot is."

children.text: tam evam uktvā saumitrim ihaiva sthīyatām iti
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to <s>Saumitri</s>, saying, "Remain right here,"
<s>Kākutstha</s> went toward the hermitage of <s>Śarabhaṅga</s>.
Then, seeing <s>Rāma</s> approaching, the lord of <s>Śacī</s>,
after taking leave of <s>Śarabhaṅga</s>, spoke these words to the gods:

children.text: ihopayāty asau rāmo yāvan māṃ nābhibhāṣate
children.translated_text: "This <s>Rāma</s> is coming here; before he addresses me,

children.text: niṣṭhāṃ nayata tāvat tu tato māṃ draṣṭum arhati ||
children.translated_text: bring matters to completion for that time; afterward he is worthy to see me.

children.text: jitavantaṃ kṛtārthaṃ ca draṣṭāham acirād imam
children.translated_text: Soon I shall see this man victorious and fulfilled,

children.text: karma hy anena kartavyaṃ mahad anyaiḥ suduṣkaram ||
children.translated_text: for a great deed must be done by him, very difficult for others to accomplish."

children.text: iti vajrī tam āmantrya mānayitvā ca tāpasam
children.translated_text: Thus the wielder of the thunderbolt took leave of him and honored the ascetic,
and the subduer of foes went to heaven in a chariot yoked with bay horses.
When the thousand-eyed one had departed, <s>Rāghava</s>, together with his attendants,
approached <s>Śarabhaṅga</s>, who was sitting near the sacred fire.

children.text: tasya pādau ca saṃgṛhya rāmaḥ sītā ca lakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Sītā</s>, and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> took hold of his feet,
and, with his permission, invited and granted lodging, they sat down.

children.text: tataḥ śakropayānaṃ tu paryapṛcchat sa rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Then that <s>Rāghava</s> asked about <s>Śakra</s>'s arrival,

children.text: śarabhaṅgaś ca tat sarvaṃ rāghavāya nyavedayat ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Śarabhaṅga</s> reported all of it to <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: mām eṣa varado rāma brahmalokaṃ ninīṣati
children.translated_text: "O <s>Rāma</s>, this giver of boons wishes to lead me to <s>Brahmaloka</s>,
which has been won by severe austerity and is hard to attain for the unpurified.
But knowing, tiger among men, that you were present not far away,

children.text: brahmalokaṃ na gacchāmi tvām adṛṣṭvā priyātithim ||
children.translated_text: I do not go to <s>Brahmaloka</s> without having seen you, my dear guest.
After meeting you, I shall go to the third heaven, served by the gods.

children.text: akṣayā naraśārdūla jitā lokā mayā śubhāḥ
children.translated_text: Imperishable, auspicious worlds have been won by me, O tiger among men,

children.text: brāhmyāś ca nākapṛṣṭhyāś ca pratigṛhṇīṣva māmakān ||
children.translated_text: both those of <s>Brahmā</s> and those on the back of heaven; accept those of mine."
Thus addressed by the seer <s>Śarabhaṅga</s>, the tiger among men,
<s>Rāghava</s>, skilled in every śāstra (systematic teaching), spoke these words:
"I myself shall obtain all the worlds, great sage;

children.text: āvāsaṃ tv aham icchāmi pradiṣṭam iha kānane ||
children.translated_text: but I desire a dwelling place assigned here in the forest."
When <s>Rāghava</s>, equal to <s>Śakra</s> in strength, had spoken in this way,
the very wise <s>Śarabhaṅga</s> again said these words:

children.text: sutīkṣṇam abhigaccha tvaṃ śucau deśe tapasvinam
children.translated_text: "Go to <s>Sutīkṣṇa</s>, an ascetic, in a pure region;

children.text: ramaṇīye vanoddeśe sa te vāsaṃ vidhāsyati ||
children.translated_text: in a delightful part of the forest he will provide you a dwelling.

children.text: eṣa panthā naravyāghra muhūrtaṃ paśya tāta mām
children.translated_text: This is the path, tiger among men. Watch me for a moment, dear one,

children.text: yāvaj jahāmi gātrāṇi jīrṇāṃ tvacam ivoragaḥ ||
children.translated_text: until I cast off my limbs like a serpent its old skin."

children.text: tato 'gniṃ sa samādhāya hutvā cājyena mantravit
children.translated_text: Then, having kindled the fire and offered oblation with ghee, that knower of mantras,
the greatly radiant <s>Śarabhaṅga</s>, entered the sacrificial fire.

children.text: tasya romāṇi keśāṃś ca dadāhāgnir mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: The fire burned the hairs and locks of that great-souled one,

children.text: jīrṇāṃ tvacaṃ tathāsthīni yac ca māṃsaṃ ca śoṇitam ||
children.translated_text: and likewise his old skin, bones, flesh, and blood.
And he became a youth resembling fire,
and, rising up from that fire-altar, <s>Śarabhaṅga</s> shone forth.

children.text: sa lokān āhitāgnīnām ṛṣīṇāṃ ca mahātmanām
children.translated_text: Passing beyond the worlds of the maintainers of sacred fires, of the great-souled seers,
and of the gods, he ascended to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: sa puṇyakarmā bhuvane dvijarṣabhaḥ pitāmahaṃ sānucaraṃ dadarśa ha
children.translated_text: That bull among twice-born seers, rich in meritorious deeds, saw <s>Pitāmaha</s> with his attendants in the world,

children.text: pitāmahaś cāpi samīkṣya taṃ dvijaṃ nananda susvāgatam ity uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Pitāmaha</s>, seeing that twice-born sage, rejoiced and said, "Welcome indeed."
When <s>Śarabhaṅga</s> had gone to heaven, assemblies of sages came together
and approached <s>Kākutstha</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, blazing with radiance.
<s>Vaikhānasas</s>, <s>Vālakhilyas</s>, <s>Samprakṣālas</s>, and <s>Marīcipas</s>,

children.text: aśmakuṭṭāś ca bahavaḥ pattrāhārāś ca tāpasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: many stone-pounders and ascetics who lived on leaves,
those using their teeth as mortars, and likewise others who immersed themselves,
sages living on water, and still others feeding on air,
those dwelling in the open sky, and likewise those sleeping on bare ground,
self-controlled ones dwelling on high, and those wearing wet garments,
those engaged in recitation and constantly devoted to austerity, and likewise those practicing the five fires,
all endowed with brahmanic splendor and firmly absorbed in yoga,
the ascetics came to <s>Rāma</s> at <s>Śarabhaṅga</s>'s hermitage.

children.text: abhigamya ca dharmajñā rāmaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ varam
children.translated_text: Having approached <s>Rāma</s>, the knower of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), best of those who uphold <s>dharma</s>,
the assembled seers, composed in mind, spoke to that supreme knower of <s>dharma</s>:
"You are the great warrior of this line of <s>Ikṣvāku</s> and of the earth,

children.text: pradhānaś cāsi nāthaś ca devānāṃ maghavān iva ||
children.translated_text: and you are its chief and lord, like <s>Maghavan</s> among the gods.

children.text: viśrutas triṣu lokeṣu yaśasā vikrameṇa ca
children.translated_text: You are renowned in the three worlds for fame and valor,

children.text: pitṛvratatvaṃ satyaṃ ca tvayi dharmaś ca puṣkalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and in you are truth, devotion to your father's command, and abundant <s>dharma</s>.
Having reached you, a great-souled knower of <s>dharma</s> and lover of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: arthitvān nātha vakṣyāmas tac ca naḥ kṣantum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: because we are petitioners, O lord, we shall speak; and you ought to forgive us for that."

children.text: adharmas tu mahāṃs tāta bhavet tasya mahīpateḥ
children.translated_text: But great <s>adharma</s> would belong, dear one, to that king

children.text: yo hared baliṣaḍbhāgaṃ na ca rakṣati putravat ||
children.translated_text: who takes the sixth share as tax and does not protect his people as sons.

children.text: yuñjānaḥ svān iva prāṇān prāṇair iṣṭān sutān iva
children.translated_text: Applying his own life-breaths, as it were, for their lives, and cherishing them like beloved sons,
always engaged, always protecting all those who dwell in his realm,

children.text: prāpnoti śāśvatīṃ rāma kīrtiṃ sa bahuvārṣikīm
children.translated_text: he obtains, O <s>Rāma</s>, lasting fame extending through many years;

children.text: brahmaṇaḥ sthānam āsādya tatra cāpi mahīyate ||
children.translated_text: having reached the abode of <s>Brahmā</s>, he is honored even there.

children.text: yat karoti paraṃ dharmaṃ munir mūlaphalāśanaḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever supreme <s>dharma</s> an ascetic living on roots and fruits performs,

children.text: tatra rājñaś caturbhāgaḥ prajā dharmeṇa rakṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: a fourth share of that belongs to the king who protects his subjects according to <s>dharma</s>.
This great company of forest-dwellers, mostly brahmins,
though having you as protector, O <s>Rāma</s>, is being violently slain by rākṣasas as if without a protector.
Come, see the bodies of the many sages whose selves have been disciplined,

children.text: hatānāṃ rākṣasair ghorair bahūnāṃ bahudhā vane ||
children.translated_text: killed in many ways in the forest by terrible rākṣasas.
Of those dwelling by the <s>Pampā</s> river and also along the <s>Mandākinī</s>,
and of those dwelling at <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, a great slaughter is being made.

children.text: evaṃ vayaṃ na mṛṣyāmo viprakāraṃ tapasvinām
children.translated_text: Thus we cannot endure the outrage against the ascetics,
a terrible one being committed in the forest by rākṣasas of dreadful deeds.

children.text: tatas tvāṃ śaraṇārthaṃ ca śaraṇyaṃ samupasthitāḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore we have approached you for refuge, you who are a refuge;
protect us, O <s>Rāma</s>, as we are being killed by night-roamers.

children.text: etac chrutvā tu kākutsthas tāpasānāṃ tapasvinām
children.translated_text: Having heard this from the ascetics, from those ascetics rich in austerity,

children.text: idaṃ provāca dharmātmā sarvān eva tapasvinaḥ
children.translated_text: righteous <s>Kākutstha</s> said this to all the ascetics:

children.text: naivam arhatha māṃ vaktum ājñāpyo 'haṃ tapasvinām ||
children.translated_text: "You should not speak to me in this way; I am to be commanded by ascetics.
I have come by chance for the accomplishment of your purpose;

children.text: tasya me 'yaṃ vane vāso bhaviṣyati mahāphalaḥ
children.translated_text: this dwelling of mine in the forest will have great fruit.

children.text: tapasvināṃ raṇe śatrūn hantum icchāmi rākṣasān ||
children.translated_text: I wish to slay in battle the rākṣasa enemies of the ascetics."

children.text: dattvā varaṃ cāpi tapodhanānāṃ dharme dhṛtātmā saha lakṣmaṇena
children.translated_text: And after granting the boon to the ascetics, his mind fixed on <s>dharma</s>, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: tapodhanaiś cāpi sabhājyavṛttaḥ sutīkṣṇam evābhijagāma vīraḥ ||
children.translated_text: the hero, whose conduct was honored by the ascetics, went on to <s>Sutīkṣṇa</s> himself.

children.text: rāmas tu sahito bhrātrā sītayā ca paraṃtapaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s>, the scorcher of foes, accompanied by his brother and by <s>Sītā</s>,
went to <s>Sutīkṣṇa</s>'s hermitage together with those twice-born men.

children.text: sa gatvā dūram adhvānaṃ nadīs tīrtvā bahūdakāḥ
children.translated_text: Having gone a long road and crossed rivers rich in water,
he saw a broad mountain, lofty like a great cloud.

children.text: tatas tad ikṣvākuvarau satataṃ vividhair drumaiḥ
children.translated_text: Then those two best of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s>, the two <s>Rāghavas</s>,

children.text: kānanaṃ tau viviśatuḥ sītayā saha rāghavau ||
children.translated_text: entered that forest, thick with various trees, together with <s>Sītā</s>.
Having entered the dreadful forest, with trees full of many flowers and fruits,
he saw, in a secluded place, an āśrama adorned with garlands of bark-garments.
There, seated, bearing matted hair soiled with dirt and mud, was the ascetic;
<s>Rāma</s> addressed <s>Sutīkṣṇa</s>, grown old in austerity, according to rule:

children.text: rāmo 'ham asmi bhagavan bhavantaṃ draṣṭum āgataḥ
children.translated_text: "I am <s>Rāma</s>, blessed sir; I have come to see you.
Therefore greet me, O knower of <s>dharma</s>, great seer of true prowess."

children.text: sa nirīkṣya tato vīraṃ rāmaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ varam
children.translated_text: Then, looking upon the hero <s>Rāma</s>, the best of upholders of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: samāśliṣya ca bāhubhyām idaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: and embracing him with both arms, he spoke these words:

children.text: svāgataṃ khalu te vīra rāma dharmabhṛtāṃ vara
children.translated_text: "Welcome indeed to you, heroic <s>Rāma</s>, best of upholders of <s>dharma</s>.
Now this āśrama, entered by you, is as if it had a protector.
I have been waiting for you alone, O greatly famous hero;

children.text: devalokam ito vīra dehaṃ tyaktvā mahītale ||
children.translated_text: therefore I have not ascended to the world of the gods after abandoning my body here on earth.
I have heard that, beginning from <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, you have been deprived of the kingdom;
<s>Kākutstha</s>, <s>Śatakratu</s>, the king of the gods, came here

children.text: sarvāṃl lokāñ jitān āha mama puṇyena karmaṇā ||
children.translated_text: and said that all the worlds have been won by my meritorious deed.
In those worlds, frequented by divine seers and won by me through austerity,
by my grace enjoy yourself with your wife and with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>."
To that great seer, blazing with fierce austerity and speaking truth,
self-possessed <s>Rāma</s> replied, as <s>Vāsava</s> might to <s>Brahmā</s>:
"I myself shall win those worlds on my own, O great sage;

children.text: āvāsaṃ tv aham icchāmi pradiṣṭam iha kānane ||
children.translated_text: but I desire a dwelling-place appointed here in the forest.
You are skilled in every place and devoted to the welfare of all beings;
you were described by the great-souled <s>Śarabhaṅga Gautama</s>."

children.text: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa maharṣir lokaviśrutaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Rāma</s>, the great seer renowned in the world
spoke a sweet sentence, flooded with great joy:

children.text: ayam evāśramo rāma guṇavān ramyatām iha
children.translated_text: "This very āśrama, O <s>Rāma</s>, is excellent; take delight here.
It is frequented by companies of seers and is always supplied with roots and fruits.
Having come to this āśrama, O greatly famous one, herds of deer
wander about and go back, enticing us, fearless from every side."

children.text: tac chrutvā vacanaṃ tasya maharṣer lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that statement of the great seer, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s elder brother,

children.text: uvāca vacanaṃ dhīro vikṛṣya saśaraṃ dhanuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the steadfast one, drawing his bow with an arrow set, spoke these words:
"Those herds of deer, O greatly fortunate one, when they have gathered,
I might strike down with a sharp-edged arrow bright as lightning.

children.text: bhavāṃs tatrābhiṣajyeta kiṃ syāt kṛcchrataraṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Your reverence would be distressed over that; what could be more difficult than that?

children.text: etasminn āśrame vāsaṃ ciraṃ tu na samarthaye ||
children.translated_text: Therefore I do not consider a long residence in this āśrama possible."

children.text: tam evam uktvā varadaṃ rāmaḥ saṃdhyām upāgamat
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to that giver of boons, <s>Rāma</s> approached the twilight rite;

children.text: anvāsya paścimāṃ saṃdhyāṃ tatra vāsam akalpayat ||
children.translated_text: after attending upon the western twilight, he arranged to stay there.

children.text: tataḥ śubhaṃ tāpasabhojyam annaṃ svayaṃ sutīkṣṇaḥ puruṣarṣabhābhyām
children.translated_text: Then great-souled <s>Sutīkṣṇa</s> himself respectfully gave auspicious food fit for ascetics

children.text: tābhyāṃ susatkṛtya dadau mahātmā saṃdhyānivṛttau rajanīṃ samīkṣya ||
children.translated_text: to the two best of men, after the twilight rite was completed and seeing that night had come.
<s>Rāma</s>, together with <s>Saumitri</s>, honored by <s>Sutīkṣṇa</s>,
spent the night there and awoke in the morning.

children.text: utthāya tu yathākālaṃ rāghavaḥ saha sītayā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāghava</s>, rising at the proper time together with <s>Sītā</s>,
performed the water rite with very cool water fragrant with lotuses.

children.text: atha te 'gniṃ surāṃś caiva vaidehī rāmalakṣmaṇau
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vaidehī</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, having worshiped the fire and the gods
at dawn according to rule in the ascetics' shelter in the forest,
and seeing the sun rising, with their impurities gone,
approached <s>Sutīkṣṇa</s> and spoke this gentle word:

children.text: sukhoṣitāḥ sma bhagavaṃs tvayā pūjyena pūjitāḥ
children.translated_text: We have dwelt happily, blessed one, honored by you, who are worthy of honor.
We take leave; we shall set out. The sages are urging us on.
We are eager to see the whole circle of hermitages
of the virtuous seers who dwell in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest.
We wish to be permitted by you, together with these foremost sages,
who are constant in <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), restrained by tapas, and like fires without smoke.
While the sun has not yet become unbearable in heat and does not shine too intensely,
like wealth gained by an unworthy man through a wrong path,

children.text: tāvad icchāmahe gantum ity uktvā caraṇau muneḥ
children.translated_text: we wish to go. Having said this, at the feet of the sage
<s>Rāghava</s>, together with <s>Saumitri</s> and with <s>Sītā</s>, bowed down.
The foremost sage raised them up as they touched his feet,

children.text: gāḍham āliṅgya sasneham idaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: embraced them firmly and affectionately, and spoke this word:

children.text: ariṣṭaṃ gaccha panthānaṃ rāma saumitriṇā saha
children.translated_text: Go on an unharmed path, <s>Rāma</s>, together with <s>Saumitri</s>
and together with this <s>Sītā</s>, who follows you like a shadow.
Hero, see the lovely hermitage-sites of the dwellers in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest,
of these ascetics whose selves have been purified by tapas.
You will see forests rich in roots and fruits and full of blossoms,
with herds of deer at peace and flocks of birds at rest,
ponds and lakes with blooming masses of lotuses and clear waters,
strewn with kāraṇḍava ducks,
and mountain streams delightful to the eye.
You will see charming woodlands filled with the cries of peacocks.

children.text: gamyatāṃ vatsa saumitre bhavān api ca gacchatu
children.translated_text: Go, dear child <s>Saumitri</s>; and you too should go.

children.text: āgantavyaṃ ca te dṛṣṭvā punar evāśramaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: And when you have seen them, you must come back again to my hermitage.

children.text: evam uktas tathety uktvā kākutsthaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Kākutstha</s>, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, said, 'So be it,'
circumambulated the sage, and began to set out.
Then wide-eyed <s>Sītā</s> gave the two brothers their very auspicious quivers and bows,

children.text: dadau sītā tayor bhrātroḥ khaḍgau ca vimalau tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and then also their two spotless swords.

children.text: ābadhya ca śubhe tūṇī cāpau cādāya sasvanau
children.translated_text: Having fastened on the fine quivers and taken up the resonant bows,

children.text: niṣkrāntāv āśramād gantum ubhau tau rāmalakṣmaṇau ||
children.translated_text: the two, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, went out from the hermitage to depart.
When the delight of the <s>Raghu</s> line, permitted by <s>Sutīkṣṇa</s>, had set out,

children.text: vaidehī snigdhayā vācā bhartāram idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vaidehī</s> spoke this to her husband in an affectionate voice:

children.text: ayaṃ dharmaḥ susūkṣmeṇa vidhinā prāpyate mahān
children.translated_text: This great <s>dharma</s> (righteous conduct) is attained by a very subtle rule,

children.text: nivṛttena ca śakyo 'yaṃ vyasanāt kāmajād iha ||
children.translated_text: and here it can be practiced by one who has turned away from desire-born vice.

children.text: trīṇy eva vyasanāny atra kāmajāni bhavanty uta
children.translated_text: There are indeed three desire-born vices in this matter:
false speech is the worst, and the other two are still more serious than that,
approaching another's wife, and fierceness without enmity.

children.text: mithyāvākyaṃ na te bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati rāghava
children.translated_text: False speech has never been yours, <s>Rāghava</s>, nor will it be.
How could there be in you desire for others' women, the destroyer of <s>dharma</s>?

children.text: tac ca sarvaṃ mahābāho śakyaṃ voḍhuṃ jitendriyaiḥ
children.translated_text: All that, great-armed one, can be borne away by men whose senses are conquered,
and I know, handsome one, that your senses are under control.
But this third thing, this fierce harming of others' lives,

children.text: nirvairaṃ kriyate mohāt tac ca te samupasthitam ||
children.translated_text: done without hostility out of delusion: that has now presented itself to you.
For you have vowed, hero, on behalf of the dwellers in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest,
to kill the rākṣasas in battle for the protection of the seers.

children.text: etannimittaṃ ca vanaṃ daṇḍakā iti viśrutam
children.translated_text: And for this purpose you have set out into the forest famed as <s>Daṇḍaka</s>,
together with your brother, carrying arrows and bow.

children.text: tatas tvāṃ prasthitaṃ dṛṣṭvā mama cintākulaṃ manaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, seeing you setting out, my mind is filled with anxious thought;

children.text: tvadvṛttaṃ cintayantyā vai bhaven niḥśreyasaṃ hitam ||
children.translated_text: as I reflect on your conduct, what is ultimately best and beneficial comes to mind.

children.text: na hi me rocate vīra gamanaṃ daṇḍakān prati
children.translated_text: Hero, your going toward the <s>Daṇḍakas</s> does not please me.

children.text: kāraṇaṃ tatra vakṣyāmi vadantyāḥ śrūyatāṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: I shall tell the reason for this; listen to me as I speak.

children.text: tvaṃ hi bāṇadhanuṣpāṇir bhrātrā saha vanaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: For you, with bow and arrows in hand, have gone into the forest with your brother.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā vanacarān sarvān kaccit kuryāḥ śaravyayam ||
children.translated_text: Seeing all the forest-roaming beings, might you not spend your arrows?
For kṣatriyas here, the bow, and fuel for fire,
when standing nearby, greatly increase the power of their energy.

children.text: purā kila mahābāho tapasvī satyavāk śuciḥ
children.translated_text: Long ago, it is said, great-armed one, there was a pure ascetic, true in speech,
in a certain holy forest, delighting in deer and birds.

children.text: tasyaiva tapaso vighnaṃ kartum indraḥ śacīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: To make an obstacle to his tapas, <s>Indra</s>, husband of <s>Śacī</s>,
came to the hermitage with a sword in hand, taking the form of a soldier.
At that hermitage-site an excellent sword was then deposited.

children.text: sa nyāsavidhinā dattaḥ puṇye tapasi tiṣṭhataḥ ||
children.translated_text: It was given as a trust to him as he was engaged in holy tapas.
Having received that weapon, intent on guarding the deposit,

children.text: vane tu vicaraty eva rakṣan pratyayam ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he kept wandering in the forest, protecting the confidence placed in him.

children.text: yatra gacchaty upādātuṃ mūlāni ca phalāni ca
children.translated_text: Wherever he went to gather roots and fruits,

children.text: na vinā yāti taṃ khaḍgaṃ nyāsarakṣaṇatatparaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he did not go without that sword, intent on guarding the deposit.

children.text: nityaṃ śastraṃ parivahan krameṇa sa tapodhanaḥ
children.translated_text: Constantly carrying the weapon, in time that treasure of tapas

children.text: cakāra raudrīṃ svāṃ buddhiṃ tyaktvā tapasi niścayam ||
children.translated_text: made his own understanding cruel, abandoning his resolve upon tapas.
Then, devoted to cruelty, heedless, and dragged down by <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness),

children.text: tasya śastrasya saṃvāsāj jagāma narakaṃ muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: because of dwelling together with that weapon, the sage went to hell.

children.text: snehāc ca bahumānāc ca smāraye tvāṃ na śikṣaye
children.translated_text: Out of affection and respect I remind you; I do not instruct you.

children.text: na kathaṃcana sā kāryā gṛhītadhanuṣā tvayā ||
children.translated_text: In no way should that be done by you while you have taken up the bow.

children.text: buddhir vairaṃ vinā hantuṃ rākṣasān daṇḍakāśritān
children.translated_text: My thought is not to kill the rākṣasas who dwell in <s>Daṇḍaka</s> out of enmity,

children.text: aparādhaṃ vinā hantuṃ lokān vīra na kāmaye ||
children.translated_text: nor, O hero, do I wish you to kill beings without offense.
For heroic kṣatriyas, self-restrained in the forests,
the task of the bow is only this much: the protection of the distressed.

children.text: kva ca śastraṃ kva ca vanaṃ kva ca kṣātraṃ tapaḥ kva ca
children.translated_text: What has a weapon to do with the forest? What has kṣatriya conduct to do with austerity?

children.text: vyāviddham idam asmābhir deśadharmas tu pūjyatām ||
children.translated_text: This has been confused by us; let the <s>dharma</s> (proper order) of the place be honored.
Therefore, noble one, a tainted thought arises from the use of weapons.

children.text: punar gatvā tv ayodhyāyāṃ kṣatradharmaṃ cariṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: But after returning again to <s>Ayodhyā</s>, you will practice the <s>dharma</s> (duty) of a kṣatriya.

children.text: akṣayā tu bhavet prītiḥ śvaśrūśvaśurayor mama
children.translated_text: Unfailing love from my mother-in-law and father-in-law would be mine

children.text: yadi rājyaṃ hi saṃnyasya bhaves tvaṃ nirato muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: if, after renouncing the kingdom, you were devoted as a sage.

children.text: dharmād arthaḥ prabhavati dharmāt prabhavate sukham
children.translated_text: From <s>dharma</s> arises advantage; from <s>dharma</s> arises happiness.

children.text: dharmeṇa labhate sarvaṃ dharmasāram idaṃ jagat ||
children.translated_text: Through <s>dharma</s> one obtains everything; this world has <s>dharma</s> as its essence.

children.text: ātmānaṃ niyamais tais taiḥ karṣayitvā prayatnataḥ
children.translated_text: After carefully wearing down oneself by many kinds of restraints,

children.text: prāpyate nipuṇair dharmo na sukhāl labhyate sukham ||
children.translated_text: <s>dharma</s> is attained by the skillful; happiness is not gained from comfort.

children.text: nityaṃ śucimatiḥ saumya cara dharmaṃ tapovane
children.translated_text: Always pure in thought, gentle one, practice <s>dharma</s> in the ascetic grove.

children.text: sarvaṃ hi viditaṃ tubhyaṃ trailokyam api tattvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: For everything is known to you in truth, even the three worlds.

children.text: strīcāpalād etad udāhṛtaṃ me dharmaṃ ca vaktuṃ tava kaḥ samarthaḥ
children.translated_text: This has been said by me from a woman's fickleness; who is able to instruct you in <s>dharma</s>?

children.text: vicārya buddhyā tu sahānujena yad rocate tat kuru mācireṇa ||
children.translated_text: But, after considering with your intelligence together with your younger brother, do at once what pleases you.

children.text: vākyam etat tu vaidehyā vyāhṛtaṃ bhartṛbhaktayā
children.translated_text: Having heard this speech uttered by <s>Vaidehī</s>, devoted to her husband,

children.text: śrutvā dharme sthito rāmaḥ pratyuvācātha maithilīm ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, established in <s>dharma</s>, then answered the <s>Maithilī</s>:

children.text: hitam uktaṃ tvayā devi snigdhayā sadṛśaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: "What is beneficial has been spoken by you, goddess, a fitting word from one who is affectionate,
and from one who shows the nobility of her family, O knower of <s>dharma</s>, daughter of <s>Janaka</s>.

children.text: kiṃ tu vakṣyāmy ahaṃ devi tvayaivoktam idaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Yet I shall say this, goddess: this very statement has been spoken by you,

children.text: kṣatriyair dhāryate cāpo nārtaśabdo bhaved iti ||
children.translated_text: that the bow is carried by kṣatriyas so that there should be no cry of distress.
And those distressed sages in <s>Daṇḍakāraṇya</s>, firm in severe vows,

children.text: māṃ sīte svayam āgamya śaraṇyāḥ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Sītā</s>, came to me themselves and sought refuge with me as one fit to grant refuge.
Living in the forest, devoted to <s>dharma</s>, eating roots and fruits,

children.text: na labhante sukhaṃ bhītā rākṣasaiḥ krūrakarmabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: they do not find happiness, being frightened by rākṣasas of cruel deeds.

children.text: kāle kāle ca niratā niyamair vividhair vane
children.translated_text: At every appointed time, while intent on various observances in the forest,
they are eaten by dreadful rākṣasas who live on human flesh.
Those sages dwelling in <s>Daṇḍakāraṇya</s>, as they were being eaten,
said to me, 'Come to our aid,' O best of twice-born men.

children.text: mayā tu vacanaṃ śrutvā teṣām evaṃ mukhāc cyutam
children.translated_text: When I had heard that word fallen from their mouths in this way,
and had paid reverence to their feet, I spoke this statement:

children.text: prasīdantu bhavanto me hrīr eṣā hi mamātulā
children.translated_text: 'May you be gracious to me; this is an incomparable shame for me,
that I, who should be attended upon by such brahmins, am attended upon by them.

children.text: kiṃ karomīti ca mayā vyāhṛtaṃ dvijasaṃnidhau ||
children.translated_text: What shall I do?' Thus I spoke in the presence of the twice-born.

children.text: sarvair eva samāgamya vāg iyaṃ samudāhṛtā
children.translated_text: Then, after they had all assembled, this speech was uttered:
'By many rākṣasas in <s>Daṇḍakāraṇya</s>, able to assume forms at will,

children.text: arditāḥ sma bhṛśaṃ rāma bhavān nas trātum arhati ||
children.translated_text: we are sorely afflicted, O <s>Rāma</s>; you ought to protect us.
When the time of oblation arrives, and on festival days, sinless one,
the rākṣasas, hard to withstand and eaters of flesh, attack us.
For ascetics and practitioners of austerity attacked by rākṣasas,

children.text: gatiṃ mṛgayamāṇānāṃ bhavān naḥ paramā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and seeking a refuge, you are our highest refuge.
If we wished, by the power of austerity we could kill the night-roamers,

children.text: cirārjitaṃ tu necchāmas tapaḥ khaṇḍayituṃ vayam ||
children.translated_text: but we do not wish to destroy the austerity long accumulated by us.
A life of austerity has many obstacles and is very hard to practice, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: tena śāpaṃ na muñcāmo bhakṣyamāṇāś ca rākṣasaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore we do not release a curse, even while we are being eaten by rākṣasas.
Therefore, while we are being oppressed by rākṣasas dwelling in <s>Daṇḍakāraṇya</s>,

children.text: rakṣa nas tvaṃ saha bhrātrā tvannāthā hi vayaṃ vane ||
children.translated_text: protect us together with your brother, for in this forest we have you as our lord.'

children.text: mayā caitad vacaḥ śrutvā kārtsnyena paripālanam
children.translated_text: And when I had heard this entire statement, O daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,
complete protection of the seers in <s>Daṇḍakāraṇya</s> was promised by me.

children.text: saṃśrutya ca na śakṣyāmi jīvamānaḥ pratiśravam
children.translated_text: Having promised, while I live I cannot make otherwise

children.text: munīnām anyathā kartuṃ satyam iṣṭaṃ hi me sadā ||
children.translated_text: the pledge given to the sages, for truth is always dear to me.

children.text: apy ahaṃ jīvitaṃ jahyāṃ tvāṃ vā sīte salakṣmaṇām
children.translated_text: I might give up my life, or you, O <s>Sītā</s>, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: na tu pratijñāṃ saṃśrutya brāhmaṇebhyo viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: but not a vow after promising it, especially to brahmins.

children.text: tad avaśyaṃ mayā kāryam ṛṣīṇāṃ paripālanam
children.translated_text: Therefore protection of the seers must necessarily be done by me,

children.text: anuktenāpi vaidehi pratijñāya tu kiṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even if unbidden, O <s>Vaidehī</s>; how much more after I have made a promise?

children.text: mama snehāc ca sauhārdād idam uktaṃ tvayā vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Because of affection for me and friendship, this word has been spoken by you.

children.text: parituṣṭo 'smy ahaṃ sīte na hy aniṣṭo 'nuśiṣyate
children.translated_text: I am pleased, O <s>Sītā</s>, for one who is not beloved is not admonished.

children.text: sadṛśaṃ cānurūpaṃ ca kulasya tava śobhane ||
children.translated_text: And this is fitting and proper for your family, beautiful one."

children.text: ity evam uktvā vacanaṃ mahātmā sītāṃ priyāṃ maithilarājaputrīm
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken this statement to beloved <s>Sītā</s>, the daughter of the king of <s>Mithilā</s>,

children.text: rāmo dhanuṣmān saha lakṣmaṇena jagāma ramyāṇi tapovanāni ||
children.translated_text: great-souled <s>Rāma</s>, bearing his bow, went with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> to the lovely ascetic groves.

children.text: agrataḥ prayayau rāmaḥ sītā madhye sumadhyamā
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> went ahead; slender-waisted <s>Sītā</s> was in the middle,
and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, bow in hand, followed behind.

children.text: tau paśyamānau vividhāñ śailaprasthān vanāni ca
children.translated_text: The two, looking at various mountain plateaus and forests,

children.text: nadīś ca vividhā ramyā jagmatuḥ saha sītayā ||
children.translated_text: and many lovely rivers, traveled on together with <s>Sītā</s>.
They saw sārasas and cakravākas moving on the riverbanks,

children.text: sarāṃsi ca sapadmāni yutāni jalajaiḥ khagaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and lakes with lotuses, filled with water-born birds,
and spotted deer in herds, horned and maddened with rut,

children.text: mahiṣāṃś ca varāhāṃś ca gajāṃś ca drumavairiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and buffaloes, boars, and elephants, enemies of trees.

children.text: te gatvā dūram adhvānaṃ lambamāne divākare
children.translated_text: Having traveled a long road, as the sun was sinking,
they together saw a lovely lake, a yojana in length.
dense with lotus-clusters and adorned with herds of elephants,
crowded with sārasa cranes, swans, kādamba geese, and water birds.
In that lovely lake, with its clear water, he heard
the sound of singing and instruments, yet no one at all was seen.

children.text: tataḥ kautūhalād rāmo lakṣmaṇaś ca mahārathaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, out of curiosity, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, great chariot-warriors,
approached the sage, an upholder of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), to ask him.

children.text: idam atyadbhutaṃ śrutvā sarveṣāṃ no mahāmune
children.translated_text: Having heard this exceedingly wonderful thing, great sage, in all of us

children.text: kautūhalaṃ mahaj jātaṃ kim idaṃ sādhu kathyatām ||
children.translated_text: great curiosity has arisen; please tell us what this is.

children.text: tenaivam ukto dharmātmā rāghaveṇa munis tadā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed then by righteous <s>Rāghava</s>,
the sage began to describe the entire power of the lake.
This perennial pond is named <s>Pañcāpsaras</s>,
made through <s>tapas</s> (austerity), <s>Rāma</s>, by the sage <s>Māṇḍakarṇi</s>.

children.text: sa hi tepe tapas tīvraṃ māṇḍakarṇir mahāmuniḥ
children.translated_text: For that great sage <s>Māṇḍakarṇi</s> practiced severe <s>tapas</s> (austerity),
for ten thousand years, living on air and dwelling in water.
Then all the gods, with <s>Agni</s> at their head, became greatly disturbed,
and all, having gathered together, spoke this word to one another:

children.text: asmākaṃ kasyacit sthānam eṣa prārthayate muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: "This sage is seeking the station of one of us."

children.text: tataḥ kartuṃ tapovighnaṃ sarvair devair niyojitāḥ
children.translated_text: Then, to make an obstacle to his <s>tapas</s> (austerity), by all the gods were appointed
five foremost apsarases, flashing with the splendor of lightning.
Then, by those apsarases, the sage who had seen both higher and lower things
was brought under the power of love, for the accomplishment of the gods' purpose.

children.text: tāś caivāpsarasaḥ pañca muneḥ patnītvam āgatāḥ
children.translated_text: And those five apsarases became the sage's wives;

children.text: taṭāke nirmitaṃ tāsām asminn antarhitaṃ gṛham ||
children.translated_text: a hidden house was built for them here in the pond.
There those five apsarases, living just as they please,
delight the sage, who has assumed youth through the power of <s>tapas</s> (austerity).
This is the sound of instruments belonging to them as they play together,
mingled with ornaments; a charming sound of song is heard.
As wondrous, this speech of that disciplined sage
the greatly famous <s>Rāghava</s> accepted, together with his brother.
As he was speaking thus, he saw a circle of hermitages,
enclosed with kuśa grass and bark garments, covered with many trees.

children.text: praviśya saha vaidehyā lakṣmaṇena ca rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s>, together with <s>Vaidehī</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, entered

children.text: tadā tasmin sa kākutsthaḥ śrīmaty āśramamaṇḍale ||
children.translated_text: that splendid hermitage-cluster then, he, <s>Kākutstha</s>.
Having lived there very happily, honored by the great seers,
he went in turn to the hermitages of those ascetics,

children.text: yeṣām uṣitavān pūrvaṃ sakāśe sa mahāstravit
children.translated_text: near whom that knower of great missiles had stayed before,

children.text: kvacit paridaśān māsān ekaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: in one place for ten months, and in another for a year.

children.text: kvacic ca caturo māsān pañcaṣaṭ cāparān kvacit
children.translated_text: In one place he stayed four months, and in another five or six,
elsewhere still more months, and in one place more than a year and a half.

children.text: trīn māsān aṣṭamāsāṃś ca rāghavo nyavasat sukham
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> dwelt happily for three months and for eight months,

children.text: tathā saṃvasatas tasya munīnām āśrameṣu vai
children.translated_text: and while he was living thus in the hermitages of the sages,
and delighting there agreeably, ten years passed.

children.text: parisṛtya ca dharmajño rāghavaḥ saha sītayā
children.translated_text: Having traveled around, the knower of <s>dharma</s>, <s>Rāghava</s>, together with <s>Sītā</s>,
the illustrious one came again to <s>Sutīkṣṇa</s>'s hermitage.

children.text: sa tam āśramam āgamya munibhiḥ pratipūjitaḥ
children.translated_text: Having come to that hermitage and been honored by the sages,

children.text: tatrāpi nyavasad rāmaḥ kaṃcit kālam ariṃdamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, conqueror of enemies, stayed there also for some time.
Then, while living in the hermitage, at some time, out of humility,

children.text: upāsīnaḥ sa kākutsthaḥ sutīkṣṇam idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kākutstha</s>, sitting near that great sage <s>Sutīkṣṇa</s>, said this:
"Blessed sir, I have always heard, as people told stories,

children.text: vasatīti mayā nityaṃ kathāḥ kathayatāṃ śrutam ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Agastya</s>, the best of sages, lives in this forest.

children.text: na tu jānāmi taṃ deśaṃ vanasyāsya mahattayā
children.translated_text: But I do not know that place, because of the vastness of this forest,
where the holy hermitage-site of that wise great seer is.

children.text: prasādāt tatra bhavataḥ sānujaḥ saha sītayā
children.translated_text: By your favor, together with my younger brother and with <s>Sītā</s>,
I would go to <s>Agastya</s>, to pay homage to the sage.
This great desire keeps turning in my heart,

children.text: yad ahaṃ taṃ munivaraṃ śuśrūṣeyam api svayam ||
children.translated_text: that I might myself attend upon that best of sages."

children.text: iti rāmasya sa muniḥ śrutvā dharmātmano vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing this speech of righteous <s>Rāma</s>,
that sage <s>Sutīkṣṇa</s>, pleased, replied to the son of <s>Daśaratha</s>:

children.text: aham apy etad eva tvāṃ vaktukāmaḥ salakṣmaṇam
children.translated_text: "I too wished to tell you this very thing, along with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:
'Go to <s>Agastya</s>, <s>Rāghava</s>, together with <s>Sītā</s>.'

children.text: diṣṭyā tv idānīm arthe 'smin svayam eva bravīṣi mām
children.translated_text: Fortunately, just now, in this matter, you yourself speak to me.

children.text: aham ākhyāsi te vatsa yatrāgastyo mahāmuniḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall tell you, child, where the great sage <s>Agastya</s> is.

children.text: yojanāny āśramāt tāta yāhi catvāri vai tataḥ
children.translated_text: Dear one, from this hermitage go exactly four yojanas;
to the south is the great, splendid hermitage of <s>Agastya</s>'s brother.
In a stretch of forest mostly on firm ground, adorned with groves of pippalī,
lovely with many flowers and fruits, resounding with various birds,
there are various lotus ponds, with clear and auspicious water,
filled with swans and kāraṇḍava ducks, adorned with cakravākas.

children.text: tatraikāṃ rajanīm uṣya prabhāte rāma gamyatām
children.translated_text: After staying there one night, <s>Rāma</s>, in the morning you should go,
taking the southern direction, beside a section of forest.
After going one yojana farther, to <s>Agastya</s>'s hermitage-site,
in a delightful stretch of forest covered with many trees,

children.text: raṃsyate tatra vaidehī lakṣmaṇaś ca tvayā saha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vaidehī</s> will take delight there, and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> together with you.
For that woodland is lovely, crowded with many trees.

children.text: yadi buddhiḥ kṛtā draṣṭum agastyaṃ taṃ mahāmunim
children.translated_text: If your intention is fixed on seeing that great sage <s>Agastya</s>,
then choose the intention of going today itself, greatly renowned one."

children.text: iti rāmo muneḥ śrutvā saha bhrātrābhivādya ca
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāma</s> had heard this from the sage and, together with his brother, had bowed...
He set out, aiming for <s>Agastya</s>, together with his younger brother and with <s>Sītā</s>.
He saw varied forests and mountains resembling clouds,
and lakes and rivers along the road, following the course of the path.
Having gone comfortably by that path pointed out by <s>Sutīkṣṇa</s>,
he was greatly delighted and spoke these words to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:
Surely this is the hermitage-site of that great-souled one,
the meritorious brother of the sage <s>Agastya</s>; it is now visible.

children.text: yathā hīme vanasyāsya jñātāḥ pathi sahasraśaḥ
children.translated_text: For here, along the road, trees of this forest are seen by the thousand,
bent down by the weight of fruit and by the weight of flowers.

children.text: pippalīnāṃ ca pakvānāṃ vanād asmād upāgataḥ
children.translated_text: And from this forest comes the scent of ripe pippalī fruits,
lifted up by the wind, suddenly rising sharp and pungent.

children.text: tatra tatra ca dṛśyante saṃkṣiptāḥ kāṣṭhasaṃcayāḥ
children.translated_text: Here and there compact heaps of firewood are seen,

children.text: lūnāś ca pathi dṛśyante darbhā vaiḍūryavarcasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and along the path cut <s>darbha</s> grasses, shining like beryl, are seen.
And in the midst of the forest, like the peak of a dark cloud,
the tip of smoke from the fire in the hermitage is clearly visible.
At secluded bathing places, twice-born men who have bathed
make an offering of flowers with blossoms gathered by themselves.

children.text: tat sutīkṣṇasya vacanaṃ yathā saumya mayā śrutam
children.translated_text: Therefore, dear one, just as I heard <s>Sutīkṣṇa</s>'s words,
this must indeed be the hermitage of <s>Agastya</s>'s brother.
For the welfare of the worlds, he swiftly subdued death,

children.text: yasya bhrātrā kṛteyaṃ dik śaraṇyā puṇyakarmaṇā ||
children.translated_text: and by his meritorious brother this quarter was made a refuge.

children.text: ihaikadā kila krūro vātāpir api celvalaḥ
children.translated_text: Here once, it is said, cruel <s>Vātāpi</s> and also <s>Ilvala</s>,
two brothers together, dwelt as great <s>asuras</s>, killers of Brahmins.

children.text: dhārayan brāhmaṇaṃ rūpam ilvalaḥ saṃskṛtaṃ vadan
children.translated_text: Assuming the form of a Brahmin and speaking refined Sanskrit,

children.text: āmantrayati viprān sa śrāddham uddiśya nirghṛṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that pitiless <s>Ilvala</s> would invite Brahmins for a <s>śrāddha</s> rite.

children.text: bhrātaraṃ saṃskṛtaṃ bhrātā tatas taṃ meṣarūpiṇam
children.translated_text: Then the brother served his brother, prepared in the form of a ram,
to those twice-born men as food, according to the rite prescribed for <s>śrāddha</s>.
Then, when those Brahmins had eaten, <s>Ilvala</s> said,
speaking in a great voice, '<s>Vātāpi</s>, come out!'

children.text: tato bhrātur vacaḥ śrutvā vātāpir meṣavan nadan
children.translated_text: Then, hearing his brother's words, <s>Vātāpi</s>, bleating like a ram,
burst through the bodies of the Brahmins again and again and came out.
Thousands of Brahmins were destroyed by those shape-shifters
in this way, after being gathered together again and again by the flesh-eaters.
Then, at the request of the gods, by the great seer <s>Agastya</s>,

children.text: anubhūya kila śrāddhe bhakṣitaḥ sa mahāsuraḥ ||
children.translated_text: after he had taken part in the <s>śrāddha</s>, that great <s>asura</s> was eaten, it is said.

children.text: tataḥ sampannam ity uktvā dattvā hastāvasecanam
children.translated_text: Then, saying, 'It is completed,' and giving water for washing the hands,
<s>Ilvala</s> addressed him: 'Brother, come out!'

children.text: taṃ tathā bhāṣamāṇaṃ tu bhrātaraṃ vipraghātinam
children.translated_text: But to that Brahmin-slaying brother as he was speaking thus,
wise <s>Agastya</s>, best of sages, said with a laugh:

children.text: kuto niṣkramituṃ śaktir mayā jīrṇasya rakṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: 'How could the <s>rākṣasa</s> digested by me have the power to come out,
your brother who had the form of a ram and has gone to <s>Yama</s>'s abode?'

children.text: atha tasya vacaḥ śrutvā bhrātur nidhanasaṃśritam
children.translated_text: Then, hearing his words concerning his brother's death,
the night-roamer, out of anger, began to attack the sage.
He rushed upon that lord of twice-born men; by the sage of blazing splendor,
with an eye like fire, he was burned up and went to death.
This is the hermitage of his brother, adorned with ponds and woodland,
by whom this difficult deed was done out of compassion for Brahmins.
While <s>Rāma</s> was speaking in this way with <s>Saumitri</s>,
the sun set and the time of twilight came on.

children.text: upāsya paścimāṃ saṃdhyāṃ saha bhrātrā yathāvidhi
children.translated_text: Having performed the western twilight rite with his brother according to rule,
he entered the hermitage-site and paid homage to that seer.

children.text: samyak pratigṛhītas tu muninā tena rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Properly received by that sage, <s>Rāghava</s>

children.text: nyavasat tāṃ niśām ekāṃ prāśya mūlaphalāni ca ||
children.translated_text: stayed there for one night, eating roots and fruits.
When that night had passed and the sun's disk was clear,
<s>Rāghava</s> addressed that brother of <s>Agastya</s>:

children.text: abhivādaye tvā bhagavan sukham adhyuṣito niśām
children.translated_text: 'I bow to you, holy sir; I have spent the night happily.

children.text: āmantraye tvāṃ gacchāmi guruṃ te draṣṭum agrajam ||
children.translated_text: I take leave of you; I am going to see your venerable elder brother.'
Told by him, 'Go,' the delight of the <s>Raghu</s> line went on,
following the path as indicated and looking upon that forest.

children.text: nīvārān panasāṃs tālāṃs timiśān vañjulān dhavān
children.translated_text: Wild rice, jackfruit trees, palms, timiśas, vañjulas, dhavas,

children.text: ciribilvān madhūkāṃś ca bilvān api ca tindukān ||
children.translated_text: ciribilvas, madhūkas, bilvas, and tindukas too,
flowering trees entwined by creepers with flowering tips:
<s>Rāma</s> saw there hundreds of such trees of the wilderness,
trampled by elephants' trunks and adorned with monkeys,
and resounding hundreds of times with flocks of intoxicated birds.
Then lotus-eyed <s>Rāma</s> spoke to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, standing nearby,
the heroic increaser of prosperity, who had followed behind him:

children.text: snigdhapattrā yathā vṛkṣā yathā kṣāntā mṛgadvijāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Since the trees have glossy leaves, and since the deer and birds are calm,
the hermitage of the great seer of purified self is not very far away.

children.text: agastya iti vikhyāto loke svenaiva karmaṇā
children.translated_text: Known in the world as <s>Agastya</s> by his own deed,
his hermitage is visible, removing the fatigue of the weary.
Its forest is filled with abundant smoke and adorned with strings of bark garments,
with peaceful herds of deer and echoing with many kinds of birds.
He swiftly subdued death for the welfare of the worlds,

children.text: dakṣiṇā dik kṛtā yena śaraṇyā puṇyakarmaṇā ||
children.translated_text: and by that meritorious one the southern quarter was made a refuge.'
This is the hermitage of that one by whose power, because of the rākṣasas,

children.text: dig iyaṃ dakṣiṇā trāsād dṛśyate nopabhujyate ||
children.translated_text: this southern quarter is seen only with fear and is not occupied.
From the time when this quarter was taken possession of by that doer of holy deeds,
from that time onward the night-roamers have been without hostility and pacified.

children.text: nāmnā ceyaṃ bhagavato dakṣiṇā dik pradakṣiṇā
children.translated_text: And by the name of the blessed one this southern quarter is called auspiciously southern,
renowned in the three worlds and unassailable by those of cruel deeds.
Though the excellent mountain constantly sought to block the path of the sun,

children.text: saṃdeśaṃ pālayaṃs tasya vindhyaḥ śailo na vardhate ||
children.translated_text: Mount <s>Vindhya</s>, keeping his command, does not grow higher.
This is the splendid hermitage of long-lived <s>Agastya</s>,
whose deeds are famous in the world and which is frequented by tame deer.

children.text: eṣa lokārcitaḥ sādhur hite nityaṃ rataḥ satām
children.translated_text: This world-honored holy man, always devoted to the welfare of the good,
will join us, now that we have come here, with what is best.
Here I shall worship that great sage <s>Agastya</s>,

children.text: śeṣaṃ ca vanavāsasya saumya vatsyāmy ahaṃ prabho ||
children.translated_text: and, gentle lord, I shall spend the rest of my forest exile here.

children.text: atra devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: Here the gods together with the gandharvas, the siddhas, and the supreme seers
constantly attend on <s>Agastya</s>, whose food is restrained.

children.text: nātra jīven mṛṣāvādī krūro vā yadi vā śaṭhaḥ
children.translated_text: Here no liar would live, nor any cruel man or deceitful one,

children.text: nṛśaṃsaḥ kāmavṛtto vā munir eṣa tathāvidhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor a ruthless or lust-driven man; for this sage is of such a nature.

children.text: atra devāś ca yakṣāś ca nāgāś ca patagaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Here gods and yakṣas and nāgas, together with birds,
dwell with restrained diet, seeking to honor <s>dharma</s> (righteous order).
Here great-souled perfected supreme seers, in sun-like aerial cars,

children.text: tyaktvā dehān navair dehaiḥ svaryātāḥ paramarṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned their bodies and taken new bodies, have gone to heaven.

children.text: yakṣatvam amaratvaṃ ca rājyāni vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: Yakṣa-hood, immortality, and various kingdoms

children.text: atra devāḥ prayacchanti bhūtair ārādhitāḥ śubhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the gods grant here when worshiped by auspicious beings.
We have reached the hermitage, <s>Saumitri</s>; enter ahead of me

children.text: nivedayeha māṃ prāptam ṛṣaye saha sītayā ||
children.translated_text: and announce to the seer that I have arrived here together with <s>Sītā</s>.
Entering the hermitage, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the younger brother of <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: agastyaśiṣyam āsādya vākyam etad uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: approached a disciple of <s>Agastya</s> and spoke these words:

children.text: rājā daśaratho nāma jyeṣṭhas tasya suto balī
children.translated_text: There is a king named <s>Daśaratha</s>; his eldest son is the mighty

children.text: rāmaḥ prāpto muniṃ draṣṭuṃ bhāryayā saha sītayā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, who has come to see the sage together with his wife <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: lakṣmaṇo nāma tasyāhaṃ bhrātā tv avarajo hitaḥ
children.translated_text: I am his younger brother, named <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, well-disposed to him,

children.text: anukūlaś ca bhaktaś ca yadi te śrotram āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: agreeable and devoted, if this has come to your hearing.

children.text: te vayaṃ vanam atyugraṃ praviṣṭāḥ pitṛśāsanāt
children.translated_text: We have entered this extremely harsh forest by our father's command;
we all wish to see the blessed one. Please let this be reported.
Hearing that statement of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the ascetic rich in tapas
