said, 'So be it,' and entered the fire-sanctuary to make the announcement.
Having entered, he came before the best of sages, unassailable through tapas,
and, with joined palms, spoke plainly of <s>Rāma</s>'s arrival:

children.text: putrau daśarathasyemau rāmo lakṣmaṇa eva ca
children.translated_text: These two sons of <s>Daśaratha</s>, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
have entered the hermitage together with <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Rāma</s>'s wife.
The two subduers of foes have come to see you and to serve you;
please command what is proper immediately after this.

children.text: tataḥ śiṣyād upaśrutya prāptaṃ rāmaṃ salakṣmaṇam
children.translated_text: Then, hearing from his disciple that <s>Rāma</s> had arrived with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: vaidehīṃ ca mahābhāgām idaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: and that the greatly blessed <s>Vaidehī</s> had come too, he spoke these words:

children.text: diṣṭyā rāmaś cirasyādya draṣṭuṃ māṃ samupāgataḥ
children.translated_text: By good fortune, after a long time <s>Rāma</s> has come today to see me;

children.text: manasā kāṅkṣitaṃ hy asya mayāpy āgamanaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: for his arrival has been desired in my mind as well.
Go. Let <s>Rāma</s>, honored, together with his wife and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: praveśyatāṃ samīpaṃ me kiṃ cāsau na praveśitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: be brought into my presence. Why has he not already been admitted?

children.text: evam uktas tu muninā dharmajñena mahātmanā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the great-souled sage who knew <s>dharma</s>,
the disciple bowed and said, 'So be it,' his joined palms held in discipline.

children.text: tato niṣkramya saṃbhrāntaḥ śiṣyo lakṣmaṇam abravīt
children.translated_text: Then the disciple went out in haste and said to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: kvāsau rāmo muniṃ draṣṭum etu praviśatu svayam ||
children.translated_text: Where is <s>Rāma</s>? Let him come to see the sage; let him enter himself.
Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, going with the disciple to the hermitage grounds,
showed him <s>Kākutstha</s> and <s>Sītā</s>, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>.

children.text: taṃ śiṣyaḥ praśritaṃ vākyam agastyavacanaṃ bruvan
children.translated_text: Speaking <s>Agastya</s>'s message in humble words, the disciple
admitted the well-honored guest in due form for the sake of honoring him.
Then <s>Rāma</s> entered with <s>Sītā</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
looking upon the hermitage, filled with peaceful deer.

children.text: sa tatra brahmaṇaḥ sthānam agneḥ sthānaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: There he saw the place of <s>Brahmā</s> and likewise the place of <s>Agni</s>,

children.text: viṣṇoḥ sthānaṃ mahendrasya sthānaṃ caiva vivasvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the place of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the place of great <s>Indra</s>, and that of <s>Vivasvat</s>.

children.text: somasthānaṃ bhagasthānaṃ sthānaṃ kauberam eva ca
children.translated_text: the place of <s>Soma</s>, the place of <s>Bhaga</s>, and also the place of <s>Kubera</s>,

children.text: dhātur vidhātuḥ sthānaṃ ca vāyoḥ sthānaṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: the places of <s>Dhātṛ</s> and <s>Vidhātṛ</s>, and likewise the place of <s>Vāyu</s>.

children.text: tataḥ śiṣyaiḥ parivṛto munir apy abhiniṣpatat
children.translated_text: Then the sage too, surrounded by his disciples, came out.
<s>Rāma</s> saw him before him, blazing with splendor among the sages,
and the hero spoke these words to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, increaser of fortune:

children.text: eṣa lakṣmaṇa niṣkrāmaty agastyo bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
children.translated_text: This, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, is the blessed seer <s>Agastya</s> coming out;
by his noble bearing I recognize this treasure-house of tapas.
Having spoken thus, the great-armed scorcher of foes, delighted at heart,
grasped the feet of <s>Agastya</s>, who shone like the sun.

children.text: abhivādya tu dharmātmā tasthau rāmaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: Having bowed, righteous <s>Rāma</s> stood with joined palms,

children.text: sītayā saha vaidehyā tadā rāmaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then <s>Rāma</s>, with <s>Sītā</s> the <s>Vaidehī</s> and with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Receiving <s>Kākutstha</s> and honoring him with a seat and water,

children.text: kuśalapraśnam uktvā ca āsyatām iti so 'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: and after asking about his welfare, he said, 'Be seated.'

children.text: agniṃ hutvā pradāyārghyam atithiṃ pratipūjya ca
children.translated_text: Having made an offering into the fire, given arghya, and duly honored his guest,

children.text: vānaprasthena dharmeṇa sa teṣāṃ bhojanaṃ dadau ||
children.translated_text: he gave them food according to the <s>dharma</s> of a forest-dwelling ascetic.
Then, first sitting down, the knower of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), the foremost of sages,
spoke to <s>Rāma</s>, who was seated with joined palms and skilled in <s>dharma</s>.
"Otherwise indeed, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, an ascetic who behaves improperly

children.text: duḥsākṣīva pare loke svāni māṃsāni bhakṣayet ||
children.translated_text: would in the other world eat his own flesh, like a false witness.
A king, a great chariot-warrior who practices <s>dharma</s>, belongs to the whole world;

children.text: pūjanīyaś ca mānyaś ca bhavān prāptaḥ priyātithiḥ ||
children.translated_text: you are to be honored and respected, and you have arrived as a dear guest.

children.text: evam uktvā phalair mūlaiḥ puṣpaiś cānyaiś ca rāghavam
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, with fruits, roots, flowers, and other offerings he honored <s>Rāghava</s>
according to his desire, and then again he spoke further:
"This great divine bow, adorned with gold and diamond,
is Vaiṣṇava, O tiger among men, fashioned by <s>Viśvakarman</s>.
This unfailing best of arrows, radiant like the sun, was given by <s>Brahmā</s>;
and these two inexhaustible quivers were given to me by great <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: sampūrṇau niśitair bāṇair jvaladbhir iva pāvakaiḥ
children.translated_text: They are filled with sharp arrows blazing as if with fires;
and this sword, adorned with gold, has a great silver sheath.

children.text: anena dhanuṣā rāma hatvā saṃkhye mahāsurān
children.translated_text: With this bow, O <s>Rāma</s>, after slaying the great asuras in battle,

children.text: ājahāra śriyaṃ dīptāṃ purā viṣṇur divaukasām ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> of old won back the blazing fortune of the gods.

children.text: tad dhanus tau ca tūṇīrau śaraṃ khaḍgaṃ ca mānada
children.translated_text: That bow, those two quivers, the arrow, and the sword, O giver of honor,
accept for victory, as the wielder of the thunderbolt accepts the thunderbolt."

children.text: evam uktvā mahātejāḥ samastaṃ tad varāyudham
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the illustrious blessed <s>Agastya</s>, mighty in splendor,

children.text: dattvā rāmāya bhagavān agastyaḥ punar abravīt ||
children.translated_text: gave that entire excellent set of weapons to <s>Rāma</s> and again spoke:

children.text: rāma prīto 'smi bhadraṃ te parituṣṭo 'smi lakṣmaṇa
children.translated_text: "<s>Rāma</s>, I am pleased; welfare to you. I am satisfied, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: abhivādayituṃ yan māṃ prāptau sthaḥ saha sītayā ||
children.translated_text: that you two have come together with <s>Sītā</s> to pay homage to me.
Fatigue from the road, with abundant exertion, is troubling you both,
and clearly <s>Maithilī</s>, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, too is weary with longing.

children.text: eṣā hi sukumārī ca duḥkhaiś ca na vimānitā
children.translated_text: For she is delicate and has never been slighted by hardships;
yet, impelled by love for her husband, she has entered the forest, full of many faults.

children.text: yathaiṣā ramate rāma iha sītā tathā kuru
children.translated_text: See that this <s>Sītā</s> delights here, O <s>Rāma</s>, in whatever way she may;

children.text: duṣkaraṃ kṛtavaty eṣā vane tvām anugacchatī ||
children.translated_text: for she has done a hard thing, following you into the forest.

children.text: eṣā hi prakṛtiḥ strīṇām āsṛṣṭe raghunandana
children.translated_text: For this is the nature of women from creation onward, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>:
they are attached to one who is in prosperity, but abandon one who is in adversity.
Women follow the fickleness of lightning, likewise the sharpness of weapons,
and the swiftness of <s>Garuḍa</s> and the wind.

children.text: iyaṃ tu bhavato bhāryā doṣair etair vivarjitā
children.translated_text: But this wife of yours is free from those faults;

children.text: ślāghyā ca vyapadeśyā ca yathā devī hy arundhatī ||
children.translated_text: she is praiseworthy and worthy to be named, just like the goddess <s>Arundhatī</s>.

children.text: alaṃkṛto 'yaṃ deśaś ca yatra saumitriṇā saha
children.translated_text: And this region is adorned, O <s>Rāma</s>, subduer of foes,

children.text: vaidehyā cānayā rāma vatsyasi tvam ariṃdama ||
children.translated_text: where you will dwell with <s>Saumitri</s> and this <s>Vaidehī</s>."

children.text: evam uktas tu muninā rāghavaḥ saṃyatāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the sage, <s>Rāghava</s>, holding his hands joined in restraint,

children.text: uvāca praśritaṃ vākyam ṛṣiṃ dīptam ivānalam ||
children.translated_text: spoke a humble statement to the seer, who shone like fire:
"Blessed am I; I am favored, since the foremost sage, the granter of boons,
is pleased with my virtues, together with those of my brother and wife.

children.text: kiṃ tu vyādiśa me deśaṃ sodakaṃ bahukānanam
children.translated_text: But designate for me a place with water and many forests,
where, having made an hermitage, I may dwell happily, intent on my observance."
Then the best of sages, having heard <s>Rāma</s>'s speech, spoke;

children.text: dhyātvā muhūrtaṃ dharmātmā dhīro dhīrataraṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: after meditating for a moment, the righteous and steadfast one uttered words still more steadfast:
"From here, dear son, at a distance of two yojanas, rich in roots, fruits, and water,
there is a splendid region, full of many animals, renowned as <s>Pañcavaṭī</s>.
Going there, make an hermitage together with <s>Saumitri</s>,

children.text: ramasva tvaṃ pitur vākyaṃ yathoktam anupālayan ||
children.translated_text: and enjoy yourself while carrying out your father's command just as it was spoken.

children.text: vidito hy eṣa vṛttānto mama sarvas tavānagha
children.translated_text: For this whole matter of yours is known to me, sinless one,

children.text: tapasaś ca prabhāvena snehād daśarathasya ca ||
children.translated_text: both through the power of austerity and through affection for <s>Daśaratha</s>.

children.text: hṛdayasthaś ca te chando vijñātas tapasā mayā
children.translated_text: By austerity I have known the wish that rests in your heart:

children.text: iha vāsaṃ pratijñāya mayā saha tapovane ||
children.translated_text: you have promised to dwell here with me in this ascetic forest.

children.text: ataś ca tvām ahaṃ brūmi gaccha pañcavaṭīm iti
children.translated_text: Therefore I say to you: go to <s>Pañcavaṭī</s>.

children.text: sa hi ramyo vanoddeśo maithilī tatra raṃsyate ||
children.translated_text: That woodland is delightful, and <s>Maithilī</s> will delight there.

children.text: sa deśaḥ ślāghanīyaś ca nātidūre ca rāghava
children.translated_text: That region is praiseworthy and not very far away, O <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: godāvaryāḥ samīpe ca maithilī tatra raṃsyate ||
children.translated_text: and it is near the <s>Godāvarī</s>; <s>Maithilī</s> will delight there.
It has abundant roots and fruits and is filled with groups of many kinds of birds;

children.text: viviktaś ca mahābāho puṇyo ramyas tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: it is secluded, O mighty-armed one, holy and likewise delightful.

children.text: bhavān api sadāraś ca śaktaś ca parirakṣaṇe
children.translated_text: You also, together with your wife, are able to protect it,

children.text: api cātra vasan rāmas tāpasān pālayiṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: and moreover, while dwelling here, O <s>Rāma</s>, you will protect the ascetics.

children.text: etad ālakṣyate vīra madhūkānāṃ mahad vanam
children.translated_text: Here is seen, hero, a great forest of madhūka trees;
you should go to the north of it, approaching a banyan tree.
Then, climbing up to level ground not far from the mountain,
there is the place known simply as <s>Pañcavaṭī</s>, with woods always in flower."

children.text: agastyenaivam uktas tu rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Agastya</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, together with <s>Saumitri</s>,
honored and took leave of that truth-speaking seer.
The two, permitted by him and having bowed at his feet,
then went from that hermitage to <s>Pañcavaṭī</s> together with <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: gṛhītacāpau tu narādhipātmajau viṣaktatūṇī samareṣv akātarau
children.translated_text: The two princes, holding their bows, with quivers fastened on, fearless in battles,

children.text: yathopadiṣṭena pathā maharṣiṇā prajagmatuḥ pañcavaṭīṃ samāhitau ||
children.translated_text: went with collected minds to <s>Pañcavaṭī</s> by the path pointed out by the great seer.
Then, while going to <s>Pañcavaṭī</s>, the delight of the <s>Raghus</s>, on the way,
came upon a huge-bodied vulture of terrifying prowess.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā tau mahābhāgau vanasthaṃ rāmalakṣmaṇau
children.translated_text: Seeing him, the two greatly fortunate ones, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, dwelling in the forest,

children.text: menāte rākṣasaṃ pakṣiṃ bruvāṇau ko bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: thought the bird was a rākṣasa, and said, "Who are you?"

children.text: sa tau madhurayā vācā saumyayā prīṇayann iva
children.translated_text: He, as if gladdening the two of them with a sweet and gentle voice,

children.text: uvāca vatsa māṃ viddhi vayasyaṃ pitur ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He said: "Child, know me as the friend of your father.

children.text: sa taṃ pitṛsakhaṃ buddhvā pūjayāmāsa rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāghava</s> understood him to be his father's friend, he honored him,

children.text: sa tasya kulam avyagram atha papraccha nāma ca ||
children.translated_text: and then asked him calmly about his family and his name.

children.text: rāmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā kulam ātmānam eva ca
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Rāma</s>'s words about his family and himself,
the bird explained to him the lineage, and himself as well, beginning from the origin of all beings.
"In ancient time, mighty-armed one, there were <s>prajāpatis</s> (lords of creatures).

children.text: tān me nigadataḥ sarvān āditaḥ śṛṇu rāghava ||
children.translated_text: Hear all of them from the beginning as I name them to you, <s>Rāghava</s>.
<s>Kardama</s> was the first of them, and after him <s>Vikṛta</s>.

children.text: śeṣaś ca saṃśrayaś caiva bahuputraś ca vīryavān ||
children.translated_text: Then came <s>Śeṣa</s>, <s>Saṃśraya</s>, and the valiant <s>Bahuputra</s>.

children.text: sthāṇur marīcir atriś ca kratuś caiva mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sthāṇu</s>, <s>Marīci</s>, <s>Atri</s>, and mighty <s>Kratu</s>,

children.text: pulastyaś cāṅgirāś caiva pracetāḥ pulahas tathā ||
children.translated_text: and also <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Pracetā</s>, and likewise <s>Pulaha</s>.
<s>Dakṣa</s>, <s>Vivasvān</s> as another, and <s>Ariṣṭanemi</s>, <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: kaśyapaś ca mahātejās teṣām āsīc ca paścimaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and glorious <s>Kaśyapa</s> was the last of them.

children.text: prajāpates tu dakṣasya babhūvur iti naḥ śrutam
children.translated_text: Of the <s>prajāpati</s> <s>Dakṣa</s> there were born, so we have heard,
sixty daughters, <s>Rāma</s>, renowned and greatly famous.
<s>Kaśyapa</s> accepted eight of those lovely-waisted women:

children.text: aditiṃ ca ditiṃ caiva danum api ca kālakām ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aditi</s>, <s>Diti</s>, <s>Danu</s>, and also <s>Kālakā</s>,

children.text: tāmrāṃ krodhavaśāṃ caiva manuṃ cāpy analām api
children.translated_text: as well as <s>Tāmrā</s>, <s>Krodhavaśā</s>, <s>Manu</s>, and <s>Analā</s>.

children.text: tās tu kanyās tataḥ prītaḥ kaśyapaḥ punar abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kaśyapa</s>, pleased, again said to those maidens:
'You shall bear sons who uphold the three worlds, equal to me.'

children.text: aditis tanmanā rāma ditiś ca danur eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aditi</s> set her mind on that, <s>Rāma</s>, and so did <s>Diti</s> and <s>Danu</s>.

children.text: kālakā ca mahābāho śeṣās tv amanaso 'bhavan
children.translated_text: <s>Kālakā</s> too did so, mighty-armed one, but the remaining ones were not of that mind.
From <s>Aditi</s> were born the thirty-three gods, subduer of foes:

children.text: ādityā vasavo rudrā aśvinau ca paraṃtapa
children.translated_text: the <s>Ādityas</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, and the two <s>Aśvins</s>, scorcher of enemies.

children.text: ditis tv ajanayat putrān daityāṃs tāta yaśasvinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But <s>Diti</s> bore sons, child, the famous <s>Daityas</s>.
Formerly this earth, together with its forests and oceans, belonged to them.

children.text: danus tv ajanayat putram aśvagrīvam ariṃdama ||
children.translated_text: <s>Danu</s>, subduer of foes, bore the son <s>Aśvagrīva</s>.
<s>Kālakā</s> also gave birth to <s>Naraka</s> and <s>Kālaka</s>.

children.text: krauñcīṃ bhāsīṃ tathā śyenīṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrīṃ tathā śukīm ||
children.translated_text: <s>Krauñcī</s>, <s>Bhāsī</s>, <s>Śyenī</s>, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭrī</s>, and <s>Śukī</s>
were the five daughters whom <s>Tāmrā</s> bore, all famed in the world.

children.text: ulūkāñ janayat krauñcī bhāsī bhāsān vyajāyata ||
children.translated_text: <s>Krauñcī</s> produced owls, and <s>Bhāsī</s> gave birth to bhāsas.

children.text: śyenī śyenāṃś ca gṛdhrāṃś ca vyajāyata sutejasaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śyenī</s> gave birth to powerful hawks and vultures,

children.text: dhṛtarāṣṭrī tu haṃsāṃś ca kalahaṃsāṃś ca sarvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: while <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭrī</s> produced swans and all kinds of kalahaṃsas.

children.text: cakravākāṃś ca bhadraṃ te vijajñe sāpi bhāminī
children.translated_text: That beautiful one also bore cakravākas; may good be yours.

children.text: śukī natāṃ vijajñe tu natāyā vinatā sutā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śukī</s> gave birth to <s>Natā</s>, and <s>Vinatā</s> was <s>Natā</s>'s daughter.
<s>Krodhavaśā</s> too, <s>Rāma</s>, gave birth to ten daughters born from herself:

children.text: mṛgīṃ ca mṛgamandāṃ ca harīṃ bhadramadām api ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mṛgī</s>, <s>Mṛgamandā</s>, <s>Harī</s>, and also <s>Bhadramadā</s>,

children.text: mātaṃgīm atha śārdūlīṃ śvetāṃ ca surabhīṃ tathā
children.translated_text: then <s>Mātaṅgī</s>, <s>Śārdūlī</s>, <s>Śvetā</s>, and <s>Surabhī</s>,
as well as <s>Surasā</s>, endowed with every mark, and <s>Kadrukā</s>.

children.text: apatyaṃ tu mṛgāḥ sarve mṛgyā naravarottama
children.translated_text: All deer are the offspring of <s>Mṛgī</s>, best of men.

children.text: ṛkṣāś ca mṛgamandāyāḥ sṛmarāś camarās tathā ||
children.translated_text: From <s>Mṛgamandā</s> came bears, sṛmaras, and camaras.

children.text: tatas tv irāvatīṃ nāma jajñe bhadramadā sutām
children.translated_text: Then <s>Bhadramadā</s> bore a daughter named <s>Irāvatī</s>.

children.text: tasyās tv airāvataḥ putro lokanātho mahāgajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Her son was <s>Airāvata</s>, lord of the world, the great elephant.

children.text: haryāś ca harayo 'patyaṃ vānarāś ca tapasvinaḥ
children.translated_text: The offspring of <s>Harī</s> were lions and forest-dwelling monkeys.

children.text: golāṅgūlāṃś ca śārdūlī vyāghrāṃś cājanayat sutān ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śārdūlī</s> bore golāṅgūlas and tigers as her sons.

children.text: mātaṃgyās tv atha mātaṃgā apatyaṃ manujarṣabha
children.translated_text: From <s>Mātaṅgī</s> came elephants as offspring, bull among men.

children.text: diśāgajaṃ tu śvetākṣaṃ śvetā vyajanayat sutam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śvetā</s> gave birth to a son, the white-eyed elephant of the quarters.

children.text: tato duhitarau rāma surabhir devy ajāyata
children.translated_text: Then the goddess <s>Surabhī</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, bore two daughters,

children.text: rohiṇīṃ nāma bhadraṃ te gandharvīṃ ca yaśasvinīm ||
children.translated_text: one named <s>Rohiṇī</s>, may good be yours, and the renowned <s>Gandharvī</s>.

children.text: rohiṇy ajanayad gā vai gandharvī vājinaḥ sutān
children.translated_text: <s>Rohiṇī</s> bore cows, and <s>Gandharvī</s> bore horses as her sons.

children.text: surasājanayan nāgān rāma kadrūś ca pannagān ||
children.translated_text: <s>Surasā</s> gave birth to nāgas, <s>Rāma</s>, and <s>Kadrū</s> to serpents.
<s>Manu</s>, wife of great-souled <s>Kaśyapa</s>, bore human beings,

children.text: brāhmaṇān kṣatriyān vaiśyāñ śūdrāṃś ca manujarṣabha ||
children.translated_text: brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras, bull among men.

children.text: mukhato brāhmaṇā jātā urasaḥ kṣatriyās tathā
children.translated_text: Brahmins were born from the mouth, and kṣatriyas from the breast;

children.text: ūrubhyāṃ jajñire vaiśyāḥ padbhyāṃ śūdrā iti śrutiḥ ||
children.translated_text: vaiśyas were born from the thighs, and śūdras from the feet, so says the sacred tradition.
<s>Analā</s> also gave birth to all trees bearing blessed fruits.

children.text: vinatā ca śukī pautrī kadrūś ca surasā svasā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vinatā</s> was the granddaughter of <s>Śukī</s>, and <s>Kadrū</s> was the sister of <s>Surasā</s>.

children.text: kadrūr nāgaṃ sahasrāsyaṃ tu vijajñe dharaṇīdharam
children.translated_text: <s>Kadrū</s> gave birth to the thousand-headed nāga, the bearer of the earth.

children.text: dvau putrau vinatāyās tu garuḍo 'ruṇa eva ca ||
children.translated_text: But <s>Vinatā</s> had two sons, <s>Garuḍa</s> and <s>Aruṇa</s>.

children.text: tasmāj jāto 'ham aruṇāt sampātiś ca mamāgrajaḥ
children.translated_text: From <s>Aruṇa</s> I was born, and <s>Sampāti</s> is my elder brother.

children.text: jaṭāyur iti māṃ viddhi śyenīputram ariṃdama ||
children.translated_text: Know me as <s>Jaṭāyu</s>, the son of <s>Śyenī</s>, subduer of foes.
So, if you wish, I shall be your companion in dwelling here.

children.text: sītāṃ ca tāta rakṣiṣye tvayi yāte salakṣmaṇe ||
children.translated_text: And when you go away with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, dear child, I shall guard <s>Sītā</s>."

children.text: jaṭāyuṣaṃ tu pratipūjya rāghavo mudā pariṣvajya ca saṃnato 'bhavat
children.translated_text: After honoring <s>Jaṭāyu</s>, <s>Rāghava</s> joyfully embraced him and bowed respectfully.

children.text: pitur hi śuśrāva sakhitvam ātmavāñ jaṭāyuṣā saṃkathitaṃ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the self-possessed one had heard again and again the friendship with his father recounted by <s>Jaṭāyu</s>.

children.text: sa tatra sītāṃ paridāya maithilīṃ sahaiva tenātibalena pakṣiṇā
children.translated_text: There he entrusted <s>Sītā</s>, the <s>Maithilī</s>, to that very powerful bird,

children.text: jagāma tāṃ pañcavaṭīṃ salakṣmaṇo ripūn didhakṣañ śalabhān ivānalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, went to <s>Pañcavaṭī</s>, eager to burn his enemies like fire burning moths.
Then, having reached <s>Pañcavaṭī</s>, filled with many kinds of beasts and deer,
<s>Rāma</s> spoke to his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, who blazed with splendor:

children.text: āgatāḥ sma yathoddiṣṭam amuṃ deśaṃ maharṣiṇā
children.translated_text: "We have come, as directed by the great seer, to this region.
This is the region of <s>Pañcavaṭī</s>, gentle one, with its flowering forest.

children.text: sarvataś cāryatāṃ dṛṣṭiḥ kānane nipuṇo hy asi
children.translated_text: Let your gaze range in every direction through the forest, for you are skilled.

children.text: āśramaḥ katarasmin no deśe bhavati saṃmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: In which place would a hermitage be agreeable for us?"

children.text: ramate yatra vaidehī tvam ahaṃ caiva lakṣmaṇa
children.translated_text: Where <s>Vaidehī</s>, you, and I may delight, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
look for such a place, one close to a body of water.
where there is the charm of the forest and likewise the charm of water,
and where firewood, flowers, kuśa-grass, and water are close at hand.

children.text: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa lakṣmaṇaḥ saṃyatāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, with disciplined joined palms,
spoke these words to <s>Kākutstha</s> in the presence of <s>Sītā</s>:

children.text: paravān asmi kākutstha tvayi varṣaśataṃ sthite
children.translated_text: I am dependent on you, <s>Kākutstha</s>, even if you should remain here for a hundred years.

children.text: svayaṃ tu rucire deśe kriyatām iti māṃ vada ||
children.translated_text: Please tell me yourself, 'Build it in whatever place pleases you.'
Greatly pleased by that statement of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the greatly radiant one,
after considering, approved a place endowed with every good quality.

children.text: sa taṃ ruciram ākramya deśam āśramakarmaṇi
children.translated_text: Entering that lovely place for the work of the hermitage,

children.text: hastau gṛhītvā hastena rāmaḥ saumitrim abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, taking <s>Saumitri</s>'s hands in his own hand, said:

children.text: ayaṃ deśaḥ samaḥ śrīmān puṣpitais tarubhir vṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: This place is level and splendid, surrounded by flowering trees.
Here, gentle one, you should properly make a hermitage-site.
Not far away this lovely lotus-pond is seen,
adorned with lotuses fragrant in scent and shining like the sun.
As it was described by the sage <s>Agastya</s>, whose self is cultivated,

children.text: iyaṃ godāvarī ramyā puṣpitais tarubhir vṛtā ||
children.translated_text: this is the lovely <s>Godāvarī</s>, surrounded by flowering trees.
It is crowded with geese and kāraṇḍava birds and beautified by cakravākas,
neither too far nor too near, and frequented by herds of deer.
Lovely tall mountains, full of many caves and resounding with peacocks,

children.text: dṛśyante girayaḥ saumya phullais tarubhir āvṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: are seen, gentle one, covered with blossoming trees.

children.text: sauvarṇe rājatais tāmrair deśe deśe ca dhātubhiḥ
children.translated_text: With gold, silver, copper, and other minerals here and there,
they shine as though windowed, like elephants with supreme adornments.

children.text: sālais tālais tamālaiś ca kharjūraiḥ panasāmrakaiḥ
children.translated_text: They are adorned with śāla, palm, tamāla, date-palm, jackfruit, and mango trees,
with wild rice and timiśa trees, and also with puṃnāgas.

children.text: cūtair aśokais tilakaiś campakaiḥ ketakair api
children.translated_text: They are covered with mangoes, aśokas, tilakas, campakas, and ketakas too,
with various trees furnished with flowering shrubs and creepers.

children.text: candanaiḥ syandanair nīpaiḥ panasair lakucair api
children.translated_text: with sandal trees, syandanas, nīpas, jackfruits, and lakucas too,
with dhava, aśvakarṇa, khadira, śamī, kiṃśuka, and pāṭala trees.

children.text: idaṃ puṇyam idaṃ medhyam idaṃ bahumṛgadvijam
children.translated_text: This place is holy; this place is pure; this place has many deer and birds.

children.text: iha vatsyāma saumitre sārdham etena pakṣiṇā ||
children.translated_text: Here, <s>Saumitri</s>, we shall live together with this bird.

children.text: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, slayer of enemy heroes,
very mighty, soon made a hermitage for his brother.
There he made a very spacious leaf-hut, with a packed-clay structure,
well-pillared, beautifully made with long poles and well-thatched.

children.text: sa gatvā lakṣmaṇaḥ śrīmān nadīṃ godāvarīṃ tadā
children.translated_text: Then the splendid <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> went to the river <s>Godāvarī</s>;

children.text: snātvā padmāni cādāya saphalaḥ punar āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: having bathed, taken lotuses, and obtained fruits, he returned.

children.text: tataḥ puṣpabaliṃ kṛtvā śāntiṃ ca sa yathāvidhi
children.translated_text: Then, after making an offering of flowers and a rite of appeasement according to rule,
he showed <s>Rāma</s> the hermitage-site that had been made.

children.text: sa taṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛtaṃ saumyam āśramaṃ saha sītayā
children.translated_text: Seeing that gentle hermitage made, together with <s>Sītā</s>,
<s>Rāghava</s> felt supreme joy in the leaf-hut.
Greatly delighted, he then embraced <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> with both arms,

children.text: atisnigdhaṃ ca gāḍhaṃ ca vacanaṃ cedam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: and spoke this very affectionate and tender statement:

children.text: prīto 'smi te mahat karma tvayā kṛtam idaṃ prabho
children.translated_text: I am pleased with this great work you have done, my lord.

children.text: pradeyo yannimittaṃ te pariṣvaṅgo mayā kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For that reason, an embrace from me was due to you and has been given.
Knowing my feelings, grateful, and knowing <s>dharma</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: tvayā putreṇa dharmātmā na saṃvṛttaḥ pitā mama ||
children.translated_text: you, as a son, have prevented my righteous father from being lost to me.

children.text: evaṃ lakṣmaṇam uktvā tu rāghavo lakṣmivardhanaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, <s>Rāghava</s>, increaser of fortune,

children.text: tasmin deśe bahuphale nyavasat sa sukhaṃ vaśī ||
children.translated_text: self-controlled, lived happily in that place rich in fruit.

children.text: kaṃcit kālaṃ sa dharmātmā sītayā lakṣmaṇena ca
children.translated_text: For some time that righteous one lived there,
served by <s>Sītā</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, like an immortal in heaven.

children.text: vasatas tasya tu sukhaṃ rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: While the great-souled <s>Rāghava</s> was living happily there,
after autumn had passed, the welcome winter season began.
Then one morning, when the night had ended, <s>Raghunandana</s>
set out for his ablution to the lovely river <s>Godāvarī</s>.

children.text: prahvaḥ kalaśahastas taṃ sītayā saha vīryavān
children.translated_text: Following behind him, together with <s>Sītā</s>, bowing, and with a pitcher in his hand,
his heroic brother <s>Saumitri</s> spoke these words:

children.text: ayaṃ sa kālaḥ samprāptaḥ priyo yas te priyaṃvada
children.translated_text: This time has arrived, dear speaker of pleasant words, which is dear to you,
by which the auspicious year shines as though adorned.
The world is harsh with mist; the earth wears a garland of grain;
the waters are not fit to be enjoyed, but fire is delightful.
After worshiping the ancestors and deities with offerings of the new first-fruits,
good people, having performed the agrayaṇa rite at the proper time, are free from stain.
The countryside is rich in desired goods and abounds more fully in milk and curds;
kings who desire conquest wander out for campaigns.
When the sun steadily resorts to the quarter served by <s>Antaka</s>,
the northern direction does not shine, like a woman bereft of her forehead-mark.
Now naturally rich in stores of snow and far from the sun,
the mountain <s>Himavān</s> is plainly true to its name as 'snowy'.
The days are exceedingly pleasant for walking about, pleasant to the touch at midday,
with a beautiful sun, but unpleasant in shade and water.
The days now appear with a gentle sun, filled with mist, intensely cold, and windy,
with the forests empty and struck down by frost.
Now the nights, no longer suitable for sleeping under the open sky, reddened by frost and led on by Puṣya,
cold and grown longer in duration, pass by.
The moon's disk, its beauty transferred by the sun and reddened by dew,
The moon does not shine, like a mirror clouded by breath.
The moonlight, stained by frost, does not gleam on the full-moon night;

children.text: sīteva cātapaśyāmā lakṣyate na tu śobhate ||
children.translated_text: like <s>Sītā</s> darkened by the sun, it is visible but does not shine with beauty.
The western wind, naturally cool to the touch and now pierced by frost,
blows in season doubly cold.
The forests, veiled in mist, and the barley and wheat fields
shine when the sun has risen, with krauñca and sārasa cranes crying out.
With heads shaped like date-palm blossoms and filled with rice grains,
the rice plants shine, slightly drooping and golden in luster.
With rays creeping forward, enveloped in frost and fog,

children.text: dūram abhyuditaḥ sūryaḥ śaśāṅka iva lakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: the sun, risen far away, appears like the moon.
In the forenoon its heat is scarcely perceptible; at midday it is pleasant to the touch;

children.text: saṃraktaḥ kiṃcid āpāṇḍur ātapaḥ śobhate kṣitau ||
children.translated_text: somewhat red and somewhat pale, the sunlight shines upon the earth.
By the fall of dew the grass is somewhat damp,
and the forest ground shines, with tender sunlight resting on it.
Wrapped in the darkness of dew and covered by the gloom of mist,
the flowerless rows of forest trees appear as if asleep.
Their waters hidden by vapor, their sārasa cranes recognized by their cries,
the rivers now gleam with banks of sand wet from frost.
Because of the falling frost and the mildness of the sun,

children.text: śaityād agāgrastham api prāyeṇa rasavaj jalam ||
children.translated_text: and because of the cold, even water standing on the tips of grass is generally refreshing.
With leaves worn and broken by age, with filaments and seed-cups fallen away,
the lotus ponds, their stalks alone remaining and ruined by frost, do not shine.
But in this season, tiger among men, afflicted with sorrow,

children.text: tapaś carati dharmātmā tvadbhaktyā bharataḥ pure ||
children.translated_text: righteous <s>Bharata</s>, out of devotion to you, practices austerity in the city.

children.text: tyaktvā rājyaṃ ca mānaṃ ca bhogāṃś ca vividhān bahūn
children.translated_text: Having abandoned the kingdom, honor, and many various pleasures,
that ascetic, restrained in diet, sleeps on the cold ground.

children.text: so 'pi velām imāṃ nūnam abhiṣekārtham udyataḥ
children.translated_text: Surely he too, at this very hour, intent on his ritual bath,

children.text: vṛtaḥ prakṛtibhir nityaṃ prayāti sarayūṃ nadīm ||
children.translated_text: ever surrounded by his ministers, goes to the river <s>Sarayū</s>.
Raised in the utmost comfort, delicate, and tormented by the cold,
how does he plunge into the <s>Sarayū</s> in the last watches of the night?
Lotus-petal-eyed, dark, fortunate, slim-waisted, and great,
knowing <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), truthful, restrained by modesty, and master of his senses,
pleasant in speech, sweet, long-armed, subduer of enemies,
having given up various pleasures, he has taken refuge wholly in his noble elder brother.

children.text: jitaḥ svargas tava bhrātrā bharatena mahātmanā
children.translated_text: Heaven has been won by your brother, great-souled <s>Bharata</s>,

children.text: vanastham api tāpasye yas tvām anuvidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: who follows your ascetic way even while you dwell in the forest.

children.text: na pitryam anuvartante mātṛkaṃ dvipadā iti
children.translated_text: "People follow not the father but the mother," so humans say;
this well-known popular saying has been made false by <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: bhartā daśaratho yasyāḥ sādhuś ca bharataḥ sutaḥ
children.translated_text: She whose husband was <s>Daśaratha</s> and whose son is good <s>Bharata</s>,

children.text: kathaṃ nu sāmbā kaikeyī tādṛśī krūradarśinī ||
children.translated_text: how indeed can that mother <s>Kaikeyī</s> be so cruel-minded?

children.text: ity evaṃ lakṣmaṇe vākyaṃ snehād bruvati dhārmike
children.translated_text: As righteous <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, out of affection, was speaking such words,
<s>Rāghava</s>, unable to bear that reproach of his mother, said:

children.text: na te 'mbā madhyamā tāta garhitavyā kathaṃcana
children.translated_text: Dear one, your middle mother must never be blamed by you in any way;
speak instead of that very story of <s>Bharata</s>, lord of the Ikṣvākus.

children.text: niścitāpi hi me buddhir vanavāse dṛḍhavratā
children.translated_text: Though my resolve for forest-dwelling is fixed, firm in its vow,
it is again made childish, scorched by affection for <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: ity evaṃ vilapaṃs tatra prāpya godāvarīṃ nadīm
children.translated_text: Lamenting thus there, and having reached the river <s>Godāvarī</s>,
<s>Kākutstha</s> performed his ablution with his younger brother and with <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: tarpayitvātha salilais te pitṝn daivatāni ca
children.translated_text: Then with waters they satisfied the ancestors and the deities,

children.text: stuvanti smoditaṃ sūryaṃ devatāś ca samāhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, composed, praised the risen sun and the gods.

children.text: kṛtābhiṣekaḥ sa rarāja rāmaḥ sītādvitīyaḥ saha lakṣmaṇena
children.translated_text: After his ablution, <s>Rāma</s> shone, with <s>Sītā</s> as his companion and with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: kṛtābhiṣekas tv agarājaputryā rudraḥ sanandī bhagavān iveśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: like blessed <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, after ablution, with the mountain king's daughter and with <s>Nandin</s>.

children.text: kṛtābhiṣeko rāmas tu sītā saumitrir eva ca
children.translated_text: After <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Sītā</s>, and <s>Saumitri</s> had performed their ablutions,

children.text: tasmād godāvarītīrāt tato jagmuḥ svam āśramam ||
children.translated_text: then from that bank of the <s>Godāvarī</s> they went to their own hermitage.
Having approached that hermitage, <s>Rāghava</s>, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
performed the forenoon duty and entered the leaf-hut.

children.text: sa rāmaḥ parṇaśālāyām āsīnaḥ saha sītayā
children.translated_text: That <s>Rāma</s>, seated in the leaf-hut with <s>Sītā</s>,
the great-armed one shone like the moon with <s>Citrā</s>.

children.text: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā cakāra vividhāḥ kathāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Together with his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, he held various conversations.
While <s>Rāma</s> was seated there, his mind absorbed in conversation,

children.text: taṃ deśaṃ rākṣasī kācid ājagāma yadṛcchayā ||
children.translated_text: a certain rākṣasī (demoness) came by chance to that place.

children.text: sā tu śūrpaṇakhā nāma daśagrīvasya rakṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: She, named <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>, sister of the rākṣasa (demon) <s>Daśagrīva</s>,
came up to <s>Rāma</s> and saw him, like one of the gods.
lion-chested, great-armed, with eyes like lotus petals,
delicate, of great strength, endowed with marks of royalty.
Seeing <s>Rāma</s>, dark as a blue lotus and radiant like <s>Kandarpa</s>,
the rākṣasī (demoness) became deluded by desire for him, who was like <s>Indra</s>.
Foul-faced herself, she beheld fair-faced <s>Rāma</s>; pot-bellied, she beheld him slender-waisted;
misshapen-eyed, she saw him broad-eyed; copper-haired, she saw him fine-haired.
Deformed herself, she saw him lovely in form; harsh-voiced, she heard him sweet-voiced;
old and dreadful, she saw him young and gracious in speech.
Ill-conducted, she saw him just in conduct; ugly to behold, she saw him beloved,
and, possessed by bodily passion, the rākṣasī (demoness) spoke to <s>Rāma</s>:
Wearing matted hair in the guise of an ascetic, with a wife, carrying bow and arrows,

children.text: āgatas tvam imaṃ deśaṃ kathaṃ rākṣasasevitam ||
children.translated_text: how have you come to this region, which is frequented by rākṣasas (demons)?

children.text: evam uktas tu rākṣasyā śūrpaṇakhyā paraṃtapaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the rākṣasī <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>, the scorcher of foes
began, in his straightforwardness, to tell her everything.
There was a king named <s>Daśaratha</s>, equal in valor to the thirty gods.

children.text: tasyāham agrajaḥ putro rāmo nāma janaiḥ śrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I am his eldest son, known among people by the name <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: bhrātāyaṃ lakṣmaṇo nāma yavīyān mām anuvrataḥ
children.translated_text: This is my younger brother, named <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, devoted to following me.

children.text: iyaṃ bhāryā ca vaidehī mama sīteti viśrutā ||
children.translated_text: And this <s>Vaidehī</s> is my wife, famed as <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: niyogāt tu narendrasya pitur mātuś ca yantritaḥ
children.translated_text: Constrained by the command of the king, my father, and of my mother,

children.text: dharmārthaṃ dharmakāṅkṣī ca vanaṃ vastum ihāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and desiring <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty) for the sake of <s>dharma</s>, I have come here to dwell in the forest.

children.text: tvāṃ tu veditum icchāmi kathyatāṃ kāsi kasya vā
children.translated_text: But I wish to know you. Tell me who you are and whose you are.

children.text: iha vā kiṃnimittaṃ tvam āgatā brūhi tattvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or for what reason have you come here? Speak truthfully.
Hearing his words, the rākṣasī, afflicted by passion, said:

children.text: śrūyatāṃ rāma vakṣyāmi tattvārthaṃ vacanaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: Listen, <s>Rāma</s>; I shall tell you the true meaning of my words.
I am a rākṣasī named <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>, able to take any form at will.
I wander alone in this forest, a terror to all.

children.text: rāvaṇo nāma me bhrātā rākṣaso rākṣaseśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: My brother is the rākṣasa named <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas.
And <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, very mighty, is always grown heavy with sleep.

children.text: vibhīṣaṇas tu dharmātmā na tu rākṣasaceṣṭitaḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> is righteous in spirit, and does not behave like a rākṣasa.
And my brothers <s>Khara</s> and <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> are famous for their valor in battle.

children.text: tān ahaṃ samatikrāntā rāma tvā pūrvadarśanāt
children.translated_text: I have surpassed them all, <s>Rāma</s>, since first seeing you.
With desire I have come to you, the best of men, as a husband.

children.text: cirāya bhava bhartā me sītayā kiṃ kariṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: Be my husband for a long time. What will you do with <s>Sītā</s>?

children.text: vikṛtā ca virūpā ca na seyaṃ sadṛśī tava
children.translated_text: She is deformed and ugly; she is not suitable for you.

children.text: aham evānurūpā te bhāryā rūpeṇa paśya mām ||
children.translated_text: I alone am a wife fit for you. Look at me in my beauty.
This ugly, unchaste, grim woman with sunken belly

children.text: anena saha te bhrātrā bhakṣayiṣyāmi mānuṣīm ||
children.translated_text: I will eat, along with that brother of yours, this human woman.
Then, seeing mountain peaks and various forests,

children.text: paśyan saha mayā kānta daṇḍakān vicariṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: you, beloved, will wander through <s>Daṇḍaka</s> together with me.

children.text: ity evam uktaḥ kākutsthaḥ prahasya madirekṣaṇām
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Kākutstha</s> laughed at the woman with intoxicated eyes
and, skilled in speech, began to say these words.
Then <s>Rāma</s> addressed that <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>, who was ensnared by the noose of desire,
with a clear, smooth voice, smiling first.
Lady, I am already married; this is my beloved wife.
For women like you, sharing a husband with a co-wife is very painful.

children.text: anujas tv eṣa me bhrātā śīlavān priyadarśanaḥ
children.translated_text: But this younger brother of mine is virtuous and handsome,

children.text: śrīmān akṛtadāraś ca lakṣmaṇo nāma vīryavān ||
children.translated_text: the glorious, unmarried, and mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
He has no wife, desires a wife, is young and handsome,

children.text: anurūpaś ca te bhartā rūpasyāsya bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: and he will be a husband suited to this beauty of yours.

children.text: enaṃ bhaja viśālākṣi bhartāraṃ bhrātaraṃ mama
children.translated_text: Choose him, broad-eyed one, my brother, as your husband.
Then, shapely one, you will be without a co-wife, like sunlight upon <s>Meru</s>.

children.text: iti rāmeṇa sā proktā rākṣasī kāmamohitā
children.translated_text: So addressed by <s>Rāma</s>, the rākṣasī, bewildered by desire,

children.text: visṛjya rāmaṃ sahasā tato lakṣmaṇam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: at once left <s>Rāma</s> and then spoke to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: asya rūpasya te yuktā bhāryāhaṃ varavarṇinī
children.translated_text: I, a woman of excellent complexion, am the wife suited to this beauty of yours.

children.text: mayā saha sukhaṃ sarvān daṇḍakān vicariṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: Together with me you will happily roam all through <s>Daṇḍaka</s>.

children.text: evam uktas tu saumitrī rākṣasyā vākyakovidaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the rākṣasī, <s>Saumitri</s>, skilled in speech,

children.text: tataḥ śūrpaṇakhīṃ smitvā lakṣmaṇo yuktam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: then smiled and said what was fitting to <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>.

children.text: kathaṃ dāsasya me dāsī bhāryā bhavitum icchasi
children.translated_text: How do you wish to become the wife, a slave woman, of me, a slave?
For I am dependent on my noble brother, lotus-complexioned lady.
Broad-eyed, joyful, spotless-complexioned one, you should become the younger wife

children.text: āryasya tvaṃ viśālākṣi bhāryā bhava yavīyasī ||
children.translated_text: of my noble brother, whose aims are prosperous and fulfilled.
Abandoning this ugly, unchaste, grim wife with sunken belly,

children.text: bhāryāṃ vṛddhāṃ parityajya tvām evaiṣa bhajiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: this old wife, he will choose you alone.

children.text: ko hi rūpam idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ saṃtyajya varavarṇini
children.translated_text: For what discerning man, lovely-complexioned one, would abandon this supreme beauty
and set his affection among human women, shapely one?
Thus addressed by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the grim, sunken-bellied woman
thought his words true, not understanding the jest.
Deluded by desire, she spoke to <s>Rāma</s>, the scorcher of foes,
unassailable, seated in the leaf-hut with <s>Sītā</s>.
Clinging to this ugly, unchaste, grim, sunken-bellied,

children.text: vṛddhāṃ bhāryām avaṣṭabhya na māṃ tvaṃ bahu manyase ||
children.translated_text: old wife, you do not think much of me.
Today, while you watch, I will eat this human woman.
Then I will wander with you as I please, without a rival wife.
Having spoken thus, the woman whose eyes were like burning coals
rushed in great anger at the fawn-eyed woman, like a great meteor at <s>Rohiṇī</s>.
As she came rushing on, like the noose of death, the very mighty <s>Rāma</s>

children.text: nigṛhya rāmaḥ kupitas tato lakṣmaṇam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: restrained her, became angry, and then spoke to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
With cruel, ignoble people, <s>Saumitri</s>, joking

children.text: na kāryaḥ paśya vaidehīṃ kathaṃcit saumya jīvatīm ||
children.translated_text: must never be done. See, gentle one, <s>Vaidehī</s> is somehow still alive.
This ugly, unchaste, overly intoxicated, big-bellied
rākṣasī, tiger among men, you ought to disfigure.

children.text: ity ukto lakṣmaṇas tasyāḥ kruddho rāmasya paśyataḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, the mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, angry, while <s>Rāma</s> looked on,
drew his sword and cut off her ears and nose.

children.text: nikṛttakarṇanāsā tu visvaraṃ sā vinadya ca
children.translated_text: With her ears and nose cut off, she gave a discordant cry
and dreadful <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s> ran back into the forest the way she had come.
That rākṣasī, deformed, extremely dreadful, and sprinkled with blood,

children.text: nanāda vividhān nādān yathā prāvṛṣi toyadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: roared many kinds of roars, like a rain-cloud in the rainy season.
Dripping blood in many streams, terrible to behold,
she raised her arms, roared, and entered the great forest.

children.text: tatas tu sā rākṣasasaṃghasaṃvṛtaṃ kharaṃ janasthānagataṃ virūpitā
children.translated_text: Then she, disfigured, came to <s>Khara</s>, who was in <s>Janasthāna</s> surrounded by a host of rākṣasas,

children.text: upetya taṃ bhrātaram ugratejasaṃ papāta bhūmau gaganād yathāśaniḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, approaching that brother of fierce splendor, fell to the ground from the sky like a thunderbolt.

children.text: tataḥ sabhāryaṃ bhayamohamūrchitā salakṣmaṇaṃ rāghavam āgataṃ vanam
children.translated_text: Then, faint with fear and bewilderment, she told him that <s>Rāghava</s> had come to the forest with his wife and with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: virūpaṇaṃ cātmani śoṇitokṣitā śaśaṃsa sarvaṃ bhaginī kharasya sā ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Khara</s>'s sister, sprinkled with blood, recounted all the mutilation done to herself.

children.text: tāṃ tathā patitāṃ dṛṣṭvā virūpāṃ śoṇitokṣitām
children.translated_text: Seeing her fallen in that condition, disfigured and sprinkled with blood,
the rākṣasa <s>Khara</s>, burning with anger, questioned his sister.
"You are endowed with strength and valor, able to go where you wish and take whatever form you wish.

children.text: imām avasthāṃ nītā tvaṃ kenāntakasamā gatā ||
children.translated_text: By whom, one like Death, have you been brought to this condition?
Among gods, gandharvas, beings, and great-souled seers,

children.text: ko 'yam evaṃ mahāvīryas tvāṃ virūpāṃ cakāra ha ||
children.translated_text: who is this man of such great heroism who has made you disfigured?

children.text: na hi paśyāmy ahaṃ loke yaḥ kuryān mama vipriyam
children.translated_text: For I see no one in the world who would do me harm,
apart from the thousand-eyed <s>Mahendra</s>, the chastiser of <s>Pāka</s>.
Today with arrows that bring life to an end I shall take his breaths away,

children.text: salile kṣīram āsaktaṃ niṣpibann iva sārasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: like a sārasa bird drinking up milk mixed in water.
When he has been killed by me in battle, his vital parts cut by arrows,

children.text: saphenaṃ rudhiraṃ raktaṃ medinī kasya pāsyati ||
children.translated_text: whose red blood, foaming, will the earth drink?

children.text: kasya pattrarathāḥ kāyān māṃsam utkṛtya saṃgatāḥ
children.translated_text: Whose body will birds, having gathered, tear the flesh from,
and joyfully devour after he has been killed by me in battle?

children.text: taṃ na devā na gandharvā na piśācā na rākṣasāḥ
children.translated_text: Neither gods nor gandharvas, neither piśācas nor rākṣasas,
will be able to rescue that wretched man dragged down by me in the great battle.

children.text: upalabhya śanaiḥ saṃjñāṃ taṃ me śaṃsitum arhasi
children.translated_text: When you have slowly recovered consciousness, you should tell me

children.text: yena tvaṃ durvinītena vane vikramya nirjitā ||
children.translated_text: by what ill-conducted man you were overpowered and conquered in the forest."

children.text: iti bhrātur vacaḥ śrutvā kruddhasya ca viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard the words of her brother, especially as he was angry,

children.text: tataḥ śūrpaṇakhā vākyaṃ sabāṣpam idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s> then spoke these words with tears in her eyes:
"There are two young men, handsome in form, delicate, and very strong,
broad-eyed like lotuses, dressed in bark cloth and black antelope skins.
They resemble kings of the gandharvas and possess the marks of royal men.

children.text: devau vā mānuṣau vā tau na tarkayitum utsahe ||
children.translated_text: I cannot determine whether they are gods or human beings.
There I saw a young woman, beautiful in form, adorned with every ornament,

children.text: dṛṣṭā tatra mayā nārī tayor madhye sumadhyamā ||
children.translated_text: a slender-waisted woman standing between the two of them.

children.text: tābhyām ubhābhyāṃ sambhūya pramadām adhikṛtya tām
children.translated_text: Both of them joined together on account of that woman,
and I have been brought to this state, like an unprotected, helpless woman.

children.text: tasyāś cānṛjuvṛttāyās tayoś ca hatayor aham
children.translated_text: On the battlefield I wish to drink the foaming blood
of that crooked woman and of those two men when they have been killed.

children.text: eṣa me prathamaḥ kāmaḥ kṛtas tāta tvayā bhavet
children.translated_text: This first desire of mine, dear brother, should be fulfilled by you:

children.text: tasyās tayoś ca rudhiraṃ pibeyam aham āhave ||
children.translated_text: I would drink her blood and the blood of those two in battle."
While she was speaking thus, angry <s>Khara</s> ordered fourteen very powerful rākṣasas,
equal to Death itself.
"Two human beings, equipped with weapons and dressed in bark cloth and black antelope skins,
have entered the terrible <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest together with a woman.

children.text: tau hatvā tāṃ ca durvṛttām upāvartitum arhatha
children.translated_text: Kill those two and that wicked woman, and then you should return.

children.text: iyaṃ ca rudhiraṃ teṣāṃ bhaginī mama pāsyati ||
children.translated_text: This sister of mine will drink their blood.
This cherished wish of my sister, rākṣasas,

children.text: śīghraṃ saṃpadyatāṃ gatvā tau pramathya svatejasā ||
children.translated_text: must quickly be accomplished by going there and crushing those two with your own might."
Thus commanded in return, those fourteen rākṣasas

children.text: tatra jagmus tayā sārdhaṃ ghanā vāteritā yathā ||
children.translated_text: went there together with her, like clouds driven by the wind.
Then terrible <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s> came to <s>Rāghava</s>'s hermitage

children.text: rakṣasām ācacakṣe tau bhrātarau saha sītayā ||
children.translated_text: and pointed out the two brothers, together with <s>Sītā</s>, to the rākṣasas.
They saw mighty <s>Rāma</s> sitting in the leaf-hut,

children.text: dadṛśuḥ sītayā sārdhaṃ vaidehyā lakṣmaṇena ca ||
children.translated_text: together with <s>Sītā</s>, the <s>Vaidehī</s>, and with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: tān dṛṣṭvā rāghavaḥ śrīmān āgatāṃ tāṃ ca rākṣasīm
children.translated_text: Seeing them and that rākṣasī who had come, the splendid <s>Rāghava</s>,
<s>Rāma</s>, spoke to his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, blazing with splendor:
"For a moment, <s>Saumitri</s>, stay close beside <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: imān asyā vadhiṣyāmi padavīm āgatān iha ||
children.translated_text: I shall kill these men here, who have come on her track."

children.text: vākyam etat tataḥ śrutvā rāmasya viditātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing this statement of wise <s>Rāma</s>,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> honored <s>Rāma</s>'s command, saying, "So be it."
Righteous <s>Rāghava</s> then strung his great bow,

children.text: cakāra sajyaṃ dharmātmā tāni rakṣāṃsi cābravīt ||
children.translated_text: adorned with gold, and spoke to those rākṣasas:
"We are the two sons of <s>Daśaratha</s>, brothers, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Together with <s>Sītā</s> we have entered the hard-to-traverse <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest.
Living on fruits and roots, self-controlled ascetics who practice <s>dharma</s>,
we dwell in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest. Why do you seek to harm us?
At the command of the seers I have come, bow and arrows in hand,
to kill you sinful men who commit outrages in the great forest.
Remain here content, and do not come nearer.

children.text: yadi prāṇair ihārtho vo nivartadhvaṃ niśācarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: If you have any use for your lives here, turn back, night-roamers."

children.text: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rākṣasās te caturdaśa
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech of his, those fourteen rākṣasas,
slayers of brahmins, bearing spears, spoke words in great anger.
Their eyes were reddened and terrible, and they addressed <s>Rāma</s>, whose eye-corners too were red,
with harsh and unpleasant speech, though they were delighted at seeing his valor:

children.text: krodham utpādya no bhartuḥ kharasya sumahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: "Having aroused the anger of our lord, the very great-souled <s>Khara</s>,

children.text: tvam eva hāsyase prāṇān adyāsmābhir hato yudhi ||
children.translated_text: you alone will give up your life today, slain by us in battle.

children.text: kā hi te śaktir ekasya bahūnāṃ raṇamūrdhani
children.translated_text: What power do you, a single man, have to stand on the battlefield

children.text: asmākam agrataḥ sthātuṃ kiṃ punar yoddhum āhave ||
children.translated_text: before us, who are many, much less to fight in battle?"
With these iron clubs, spears, and paṭṭiśas hurled by our arms,

children.text: prāṇāṃs tyakṣyasi vīryaṃ ca dhanuś ca karapīḍitam ||
children.translated_text: you will give up your life, your valor, and the bow gripped in your hand.

children.text: ity evam uktvā saṃrabdhā rākṣasās te caturdaśa
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, those fourteen enraged rākṣasas
with weapons and swords raised rushed straight at <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: cikṣipus tāni śūlāni rāghavaṃ prati durjayam ||
children.translated_text: They hurled those spears at unconquerable <s>Rāghava</s>.
But <s>Kākutstha</s> cut all those fourteen spears apart
with just as many arrows, adorned with gold.
Then afterward the greatly radiant one, exceedingly angry,
took up fourteen stone-sharpened nārāca arrows, bright as the sun.

children.text: gṛhītvā dhanur āyamya lakṣyān uddiśya rākṣasān
children.translated_text: Taking his bow, drawing it, and aiming at the rākṣasas as his targets,

children.text: mumoca rāghavo bāṇān vajrān iva śatakratuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> released the arrows, like <s>Śatakratu</s> releasing thunderbolts.
The gold-feathered shafts, blazing and adorned with gold,
became in the sky equal in splendor to great meteors.

children.text: te bhittvā rakṣasāṃ vegād vakṣāṃsi rudhirāplutāḥ
children.translated_text: Having swiftly pierced the breasts of the rākṣasas, soaked with blood,
they flew out and then sank into the earth with a thunderbolt's sound.

children.text: te bhinnahṛdayā bhūmau chinnamūlā iva drumāḥ
children.translated_text: With their hearts split open, like trees whose roots had been cut,
they fell to the ground, their limbs wet with blood, deformed and lifeless.

children.text: tān bhūmau patitān dṛṣṭvā rākṣasī krodhamūrchitā
children.translated_text: Seeing them fallen on the ground, the rākṣasī, stupefied with anger

children.text: paritrastā punas tatra vyasṛjad bhairavaṃ ravam ||
children.translated_text: and terrified, once more let out a dreadful cry there.

children.text: sā nadantī mahānādaṃ javāc chūrpaṇakhā punaḥ
children.translated_text: Crying out with a great roar, <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s> again

children.text: upagamya kharaṃ sā tu kiṃcit saṃśuṣkaśoṇitā
children.translated_text: quickly approached <s>Khara</s>, somewhat dried of blood,
and again fell down in distress, like a creeper drained of sap.

children.text: nipātitān prekṣya raṇe tu rākṣasān pradhāvitā śūrpaṇakhā punas tataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, seeing the rākṣasas struck down in battle, <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s> ran back again,

children.text: vadhaṃ ca teṣāṃ nikhilena rakṣasāṃ śaśaṃsa sarvaṃ bhaginī kharasya sā ||
children.translated_text: and she, <s>Khara</s>'s sister, reported fully the slaughter of all those rākṣasas.

children.text: sa punaḥ patitāṃ dṛṣṭvā krodhācchūrpaṇakhāṃ kharaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Khara</s> saw <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s> fallen again,

children.text: uvāca vyaktayā vācā tām anarthārtham āgatām ||
children.translated_text: he spoke in a clear voice to her, who had come for a harmful purpose.

children.text: mayā tv idānīṃ śūrās te rākṣasā rudhirāśanāḥ
children.translated_text: Just now those heroic, blood-eating rākṣasas
were sent out by me for your sake; why are you crying again?

children.text: bhaktāś caivānuraktāś ca hitāś ca mama nityaśaḥ
children.translated_text: They are devoted, attached, and always beneficial to me.

children.text: ghnanto 'pi na nihantavyā na na kuryur vaco mama ||
children.translated_text: Even while killing, they were not to be killed; and they would certainly not disobey my word.

children.text: kim etacchrotum icchāmi kāraṇaṃ yatkṛte punaḥ
children.translated_text: I wish to hear what this reason is, because of which again

children.text: hā nātheti vinardantī sarpavad veṣṭase kṣitau ||
children.translated_text: you cry out 'Alas, protector!' and writhe on the ground like a serpent.

children.text: anāthavad vilapasi kiṃ nu nāthe mayi sthite
children.translated_text: Why do you lament like one without a protector, when I, your protector, am standing here?

children.text: uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha mā bhaiṣīr vaiklavyaṃ tyajyatām iha ||
children.translated_text: Get up, get up. Do not be afraid; let this distress be abandoned here.

children.text: ity evam uktā durdharṣā khareṇa parisāntvitā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed and comforted by <s>Khara</s>, the unassailable woman

children.text: vimṛjya nayane sāsre kharaṃ bhrātaram abravīt ||
children.translated_text: wiped her tearful eyes and spoke to <s>Khara</s>, her brother.

children.text: preṣitāś ca tvayā śūrā rākṣasās te caturdaśa
children.translated_text: Those fourteen heroic and dreadful rākṣasas sent by you
to kill <s>Rāghava</s> together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, for my sake,
though angry and holding spears and paṭṭiśas in their hands,
were all killed in battle by <s>Rāma</s> with arrows that pierced their vital spots.

children.text: tān bhūmau patitān dṛṣṭvā kṣaṇenaiva mahābalān
children.translated_text: When I saw those very mighty ones fallen on the ground in a single moment,

children.text: rāmasya ca mahat karma mahāṃs trāso 'bhavan mama ||
children.translated_text: and saw <s>Rāma</s>'s great deed, a great terror came over me.

children.text: sāsmi bhītā samudvignā viṣaṇṇā ca niśācara
children.translated_text: So I am frightened, shaken, and despondent, night-roamer.

children.text: śaraṇaṃ tvāṃ punaḥ prāptā sarvato bhayadarśinī ||
children.translated_text: Seeing fear on every side, I have come to you again for refuge.
Why do you not rescue me, sunk in this vast ocean of grief,

children.text: kiṃ māṃ na trāyase magnāṃ vipule śokasāgare ||
children.translated_text: inhabited by crocodiles of despair and garlanded with waves of terror?

children.text: ete ca nihatā bhūmau rāmeṇa niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
children.translated_text: And these rākṣasas, flesh-eaters who had reached my path,

children.text: ye ca me padavīṃ prāptā rākṣasāḥ piśitāśanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: lie killed on the ground by <s>Rāma</s> with sharp arrows.

children.text: mayi te yady anukrośo yadi rakṣaḥsu teṣu ca
children.translated_text: If you have compassion for me, and for those rākṣasas,

children.text: rāmeṇa yadi śaktis te tejo vāsti niśācara
children.translated_text: if you have the power or the energy against <s>Rāma</s>, night-roamer,
then kill that thorn of the rākṣasas who dwells in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest.

children.text: yadi rāmaṃ mamāmitram adya tvaṃ na vadhiṣyasi
children.translated_text: If today you do not kill <s>Rāma</s>, my enemy,
I, shameless, will give up my life right before you.

children.text: buddhyāham anupaśyāmi na tvaṃ rāmasya saṃyuge
children.translated_text: By my understanding I see that in battle
you are not able to stand face to face with <s>Rāma</s>, bow in hand, in a great fight.
You think yourself a hero, but you are no hero; your prowess has been falsely ascribed to you,

children.text: mānuṣau yan na śaknoṣi hantuṃ tau rāmalakṣmaṇau ||
children.translated_text: since you cannot kill those two humans, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Leave <s>Janasthāna</s> quickly, together with your kinsmen.

children.text: niḥsattvasyālpavīryasya vāsas te kīdṛśas tv iha ||
children.translated_text: What kind of dwelling here is there for one without strength and of little valor?
Overpowered by <s>Rāma</s>'s splendor, you will quickly perish.
For <s>Rāma</s>, the son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, is endowed with splendor,

children.text: bhrātā cāsya mahāvīryo yena cāsmi virūpitā ||
children.translated_text: as is his brother of great valor, by whom I have been disfigured.

children.text: evam ādharṣitaḥ śūraḥ śūrpaṇakhyā kharas tadā
children.translated_text: Thus insulted then by <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>, the hero <s>Khara</s>

children.text: uvāca rakṣasāṃ madhye kharaḥ kharataraṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: spoke, in the midst of the rākṣasas, words harsher than <s>Khara</s> himself.
This unequaled anger of mine, born from your humiliation,
cannot be held back, like briny water once risen.

children.text: na rāmaṃ gaṇaye vīryān mānuṣaṃ kṣīṇajīvitam
children.translated_text: I do not regard <s>Rāma</s> as powerful, a human whose life is exhausted,

children.text: ātmā duścaritaiḥ prāṇān hato yo 'dya vimokṣyati ||
children.translated_text: who today, slain by his own misdeeds, will release his life-breaths.

children.text: bāṣpaḥ saṃhriyatām eṣa sambhramaś ca vimucyatām
children.translated_text: Let these tears be restrained, and let this agitation be abandoned.

children.text: ahaṃ rāmaṃ saha bhrātrā nayāmi yamasādanam ||
children.translated_text: I will bring <s>Rāma</s>, together with his brother, to the abode of <s>Yama</s>.
Today, when feeble-breathed <s>Rāma</s> lies on the ground, struck down by an axe,

children.text: rāmasya rudhiraṃ raktam uṣṇaṃ pāsyasi rākṣasi ||
children.translated_text: you shall drink his red, warm blood, rākṣasī.

children.text: sā prahṛṣṭā vacaḥ śrutvā kharasya vadanāc cyutam
children.translated_text: Delighted on hearing the words that had fallen from <s>Khara</s>'s mouth,

children.text: praśaśaṃsa punar maurkhyād bhrātaraṃ rakṣasāṃ varam ||
children.translated_text: she, in her folly, again praised her brother, the best of rākṣasas.

children.text: tayā paruṣitaḥ pūrvaṃ punar eva praśaṃsitaḥ
children.translated_text: Having first reviled him, she then praised him once again.

children.text: abravīd dūṣaṇaṃ nāma kharaḥ senāpatiṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Khara</s> spoke to the general named <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>:
Fourteen thousand who follow my will,
rākṣasas of terrible speed who do not turn back in battles,
dark as blue rain-clouds, dreadful, cruel in action,
strong, fierce in splendor, delighting in harming the world,
with the pride of tigers, great-mouthed and very mighty,
gentle one, set all those rākṣasas in full readiness.

children.text: upasthāpaya me kṣipraṃ rathaṃ saumya dhanūṃṣi ca
children.translated_text: Quickly bring up my chariot, gentle one, and my bows,

children.text: śarāṃś ca citrān khaḍgāṃś ca śaktīś ca vividhāḥ śitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: variegated arrows, swords, and many kinds of sharpened spears.
I wish to march out at the head of the great-souled <s>Paulastyas</s>,
I, skilled in battle, for the killing of ill-conducted <s>Rāma</s>.
As he was speaking thus, <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> then showed him
a great chariot, sun-colored and yoked with fine dappled horses.
It was shaped like the peak of <s>Meru</s> and adorned with refined gold,
with golden wheels, spacious, and with a pole made of beryl.

children.text: matsyaiḥ puṣpair drumaiḥ śailaiś candrasūryaiś ca kāñcanaiḥ
children.translated_text: It was covered with golden fish, flowers, trees, mountains, moons, and suns,

children.text: māṅgalyaiḥ pakṣisaṃghaiś ca tārābhiś ca samāvṛtam ||
children.translated_text: with auspicious flocks of birds and with stars.
Furnished with a banner and sword and adorned with rows of little bells,
that chariot yoked with fine horses was mounted by <s>Khara</s> in rage.
Seeing him mounted on the chariot, the rākṣasas of terrible valor
stood surrounding him and mighty <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>.
But <s>Khara</s>, seeing all the rākṣasas, great archers with dreadful shields, weapons, and banners,
said from his chariot, 'March out!'
Then that rākṣasa army, with dreadful shields, weapons, and banners,
went out from <s>Janasthāna</s> with great noise and great speed,

children.text: mudgaraiḥ paṭṭiśaiḥ śūlaiḥ sutīkṣṇaiś ca paraśvadhaiḥ
children.translated_text: with clubs, paṭṭiśas, spears, and very sharp axes,

children.text: khaḍgaiś cakraiś ca hastasthair bhrājamānaiś ca tomaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: with swords, discus-weapons held in hand, and shining javelins,

children.text: śaktibhiḥ parighair ghorair atimātraiś ca kārmukaiḥ
children.translated_text: with spears, dreadful iron clubs, and bows of immense size,
and with maces, swords, pestles, and thunderbolts grasped, terrible to behold.
Fourteen thousand of the very dreadful rākṣasas,
following <s>Khara</s>'s will, marched out from <s>Janasthāna</s>.

children.text: tāṃs tv abhidravato dṛṣṭvā rākṣasān bhīmavikramān
children.translated_text: Seeing those rākṣasas of terrible valor rushing forward,
<s>Khara</s>'s chariot too went a little way after them.
Then those dappled horses adorned with refined gold,
understanding <s>Khara</s>'s intention, the charioteer urged on.

children.text: sa codito rathaḥ śīghraṃ kharasya ripughātinaḥ
children.translated_text: Urged on, the swift chariot of <s>Khara</s>, slayer of enemies,
filled the quarters and the intermediate quarters with its sound.

children.text: pravṛddhamanyus tu kharaḥ kharasvano ripor vadhārthaṃ tvarito yathāntakaḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Khara</s>, his anger swollen, harsh-voiced and hastening for the killing of his enemy like Death,

children.text: acūcudat sārathim unnadan punar mahābalo megha ivāśmavarṣavān ||
children.translated_text: again urged on the charioteer with a roar, mighty as a cloud raining stones.

children.text: tat prayātaṃ balaṃ ghoram aśivaṃ śoṇitodakam
children.translated_text: As that dreadful, inauspicious force set forth, with bloody water,
a great dense cloud, red as a donkey, rained down upon it.
His horses, yoked to the chariot and very swift, fell down
on level ground strewn with flowers, by chance, on the royal road.
A dark halo, edged with blood-red, appeared,
like a circle of firebrands, enclosing the sun.
Then a huge and extremely dreadful vulture came to the lofty banner
with its golden staff, climbed upon it, and stood there.
Near <s>Janasthāna</s>, gathering together with harsh cries,
carnivorous beasts and birds made many discordant sounds.

children.text: vyājahruś ca pradīptāyāṃ diśi vai bhairavasvanam
children.translated_text: In the blazing quarter, jackals uttered a terrifying cry,
inauspicious for the yātudhānas, dreadful and loud-sounding.
Terrible clouds, resembling split mountains and bearing dried-up water,

children.text: ākāśaṃ tad anākāśaṃ cakrur bhīmā balāhakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: made that sky seem no sky at all.
A dreadful darkness arose, dense and hair-raising,

children.text: diśo vā vidiśo vāpi suvyaktaṃ na cakāśire ||
children.translated_text: and neither the quarters nor the intermediate quarters shone clearly.
Though it was not twilight time, there appeared a glow like wet blood,

children.text: kharasyābhimukhaṃ nedus tadā ghorā mṛgāḥ khagāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and dreadful beasts and birds cried out facing <s>Khara</s>.
Jackals, always bringers of misfortune in battle and dreadful to behold,
howled facing the army with flame-spouting mouths.
A headless trunk, appearing like an iron club, was seen near the sun,
and <s>Svarbhānu</s>, the great seizer, seized the sun out of season.
The wind blew swiftly; the sun became without radiance,

children.text: utpetuś ca vinā rātriṃ tārāḥ khadyotasaprabhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and stars with the brightness of fireflies sprang up though it was not night.
The lotus ponds had their fish and birds withdrawn, and their lotuses closed in,

children.text: tasmin kṣaṇe babhūvuś ca vinā puṣpaphalair drumāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and at that moment the trees became without flowers and fruits.

children.text: uddhūtaś ca vinā vātaṃ reṇur jaladharāruṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Dust, red as a rain-cloud, was raised though there was no wind,
and there the mynas cried out, 'vīcīkūcī.'
Meteors too, dreadful to behold and accompanied by thunderous noise, fell down,
and the earth shook, together with its mountains, groves, and forests.
As discerning <s>Khara</s> stood on the chariot roaring,
his left arm trembled, and his voice caught.
His sight became tear-filled as he looked all around,

children.text: lalāṭe ca rujā jātā na ca mohān nyavartata ||
children.translated_text: and pain arose in his forehead; yet through delusion he did not turn back.
Having observed those great portents that had arisen, hair-raising as they were,

children.text: abravīd rākṣasān sarvān prahasan sa kharas tadā ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Khara</s>, laughing, spoke to all the rākṣasas:
All these great portents that have arisen, dreadful to behold,

children.text: na cintayāmy ahaṃ vīryād balavān durbalān iva ||
children.translated_text: I do not heed them, because of my valor, as a strong man does not heed weak men.

children.text: tārā api śarais tīkṣṇaiḥ pātayeyaṃ nabhastalāt
children.translated_text: With sharp arrows I could even bring down the stars from the vault of heaven,
and, enraged, I could subject Death itself to the condition of dying.

children.text: rāghavaṃ taṃ balotsiktaṃ bhrātaraṃ cāpi lakṣmaṇam
children.translated_text: That <s>Rāghava</s>, swollen with strength, and also his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
I cannot bear to turn back without killing them with sharp arrows.

children.text: sakāmā bhaginī me 'stu pītvā tu rudhiraṃ tayoḥ
children.translated_text: Let my sister have her desire fulfilled after drinking the blood of those two,
on whose account ruin has come upon <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: na kvacit prāptapūrvo me saṃyugeṣu parājayaḥ
children.translated_text: Never anywhere before has defeat in battle come to me;

children.text: yuṣmākam etat pratyakṣaṃ nānṛtaṃ kathayāmy aham ||
children.translated_text: this is evident to you, and I am not speaking falsely.
Even the king of the gods, mounted on rutting <s>Airāvata</s> in anger,

children.text: vajrahastaṃ raṇe hanyāṃ kiṃ punas tau ca mānuṣau ||
children.translated_text: with the thunderbolt in his hand, I would kill in battle; how much more those two humans?

children.text: sā tasya garjitaṃ śrutvā rākṣasasya mahācamūḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that roar of the rākṣasa, his great army
felt incomparable delight, though it was fast bound by the noose of death.
And the great-souled ones, eager to witness the battle, gathered together:

children.text: ṛṣayo devagandharvāḥ siddhāś ca saha cāraṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: seers, gods, gandharvas, siddhas, and cāraṇas as well.
Having assembled, those meritorious ones said together to one another:

children.text: svasti gobrāhmaṇebhyo 'stu lokānāṃ ye ca saṃmatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: May there be welfare for cows and brahmins, and for those honored among the worlds.
May <s>Rāghava</s> conquer in battle the <s>Paulastya</s> night-roamers,
as the discus-handed one conquered all the foremost asuras in battle.

children.text: etac cānyac ca bahuśo bruvāṇāḥ paramarṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: Saying this and much else again and again, the supreme seers
saw the army of those rākṣasas whose lives were already spent.

children.text: rathena tu kharo vegāt sainyasyāgrād viniḥsṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Khara</s>, with speed, drove out in his chariot from the front of the army,

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasaṃ bhūyo rākṣasāś ca viniḥsṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and seeing that rākṣasa, the rākṣasas came forth once more.
<s>Śyenagāmī</s>, <s>Pṛthugrīva</s>, <s>Yajñaśatru</s>, <s>Vihaṃgama</s>,
<s>Durjaya</s>, <s>Karavīrākṣa</s>, <s>Paruṣa</s>, and <s>Kālakārmuka</s>,
<s>Meghamālī</s>, <s>Mahāmālī</s>, <s>Sarpāsya</s>, and <s>Rudhirāśana</s>--
these twelve, of great valor, set out surrounding <s>Khara</s>.
<s>Mahākapāla</s>, <s>Sthūlākṣa</s>, <s>Pramāthī</s>, and also <s>Triśiras</s>--
these four leaders of the army followed behind <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>.
That army of rākṣasa heroes, terrible, very fierce, eager for battle and moving with dreadful speed,

children.text: tau rājaputrau sahasābhyupetā mālā grahāṇām iva candrasūryau ||
children.translated_text: rushed suddenly upon the two princes, like a ring of planets upon the moon and sun.
When <s>Khara</s>, whose prowess was harsh, was going toward the hermitage,

children.text: tān evautpātikān rāmaḥ saha bhrātrā dadarśa ha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, together with his brother, saw those very portents.
Seeing those very dreadful portents arisen, making the hair stand on end

children.text: prajānām ahitān dṛṣṭvā vākyaṃ lakṣmaṇam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: and hostile to living beings, he spoke these words to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:
See, mighty-armed one, these great portents that take away all beings,
arisen for the destruction of all the rākṣasas.
Those clouds in the sky, pouring down streams of blood
and making harsh sounds, whirl about, rough and donkey-red.

children.text: sadhūmāś ca śarāḥ sarve mama yuddhābhinandinaḥ
children.translated_text: All my arrows, smoky and rejoicing in battle,
and my gold-backed bows are twitching, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
From the way the forest-roaming birds cry here,

children.text: agrato no bhayaṃ prāptaṃ saṃśayo jīvitasya ca ||
children.translated_text: danger has come before us, and there is uncertainty about life.

children.text: samprahāras tu sumahān bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: A very great combat will take place, without doubt;

children.text: ayam ākhyāti me bāhuḥ sphuramāṇo muhur muhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: this arm of mine, throbbing again and again, announces it to me.

children.text: saṃnikarṣe tu naḥ śūra jayaṃ śatroḥ parājayam
children.translated_text: But near at hand for us, brave one, are victory and the enemy's defeat;

children.text: suprabhaṃ ca prasannaṃ ca tava vaktraṃ hi lakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: for your face is seen to be bright and serene.

children.text: udyatānāṃ hi yuddhārthaṃ yeṣāṃ bhavati lakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: For those who rise up for the sake of battle, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
when their faces become lusterless, their span of life is exhausted.
Provision for what has not yet come must be made by a man who desires good,
by a wise man who suspects danger.
Therefore, taking <s>Vaidehī</s>, with arrows in hand and bow in hand,
take refuge in a hard-to-reach cave of the mountain, crowded with trees.

children.text: pratikūlitum icchāmi na hi vākyam idaṃ tvayā
children.translated_text: I do not wish this command of mine to be opposed by you;

children.text: śāpito mama pādābhyāṃ gamyatāṃ vatsa māciram ||
children.translated_text: I adjure you by my feet: go, dear child, without delay.

children.text: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa lakṣmaṇaḥ saha sītayā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, together with <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: śarān ādāya cāpaṃ ca guhāṃ durgāṃ samāśrayat ||
children.translated_text: took his arrows and bow and sought shelter in the difficult cave.

children.text: tasmin praviṣṭe tu guhāṃ lakṣmaṇe saha sītayā
children.translated_text: When <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> had entered the cave with <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: hanta niryuktam ity uktvā rāmaḥ kavacam āviśat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, saying, 'Good, the arrangement is made,' put on his armor.
Adorned with that armor, which was like fire,
<s>Rāma</s> became like a smokeless fire arisen in the darkness.

children.text: sa cāpam udyamya mahac charān ādāya vīryavān
children.translated_text: Then the mighty one raised his great bow and took up arrows,
