and stood there, filling the quarters with the sounds of the bowstring.

children.text: tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāś ca saha cāraṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: Then the gods with the gandharvas, the siddhas with the cāraṇas,
and the guhyakas, greatly terrified, spoke among themselves:
There are fourteen thousand rākṣasas of dreadful deeds,

children.text: ekaś ca rāmo dharmātmā kathaṃ yuddhaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Rāma</s>, righteous-souled, is alone. How will the battle be?
Then the army of the yātudhānas, deep-resounding, dreadful with armor, weapons, and banners,
appeared on every side.
As they sent forth lion-roars and roared against one another,
as they twanged their bows and repeatedly gaped wide,
and as they beat their drums with loud, piercing sounds,

children.text: teṣāṃ sutumulaḥ śabdaḥ pūrayāmāsa tad vanam ||
children.translated_text: their exceedingly tumultuous noise filled that forest.
Frightened by that sound, the wild animals roaming in the forest
ran away to a silent place, not looking back behind them.

children.text: tat tv anīkaṃ mahāvegaṃ rāmaṃ samupasarpata
children.translated_text: But that army, with great speed, advanced upon <s>Rāma</s>,
holding many kinds of weapons, deep and like the ocean.
<s>Rāma</s> too, skilled in battle, moving his eyes on every side,
saw that army of <s>Khara</s>, raised up and facing him for battle.

children.text: vitatya ca dhanur bhīmaṃ tūṇyāś coddhṛtya sāyakān
children.translated_text: Stringing his terrible bow and drawing arrows from the quivers,
he summoned fierce anger for the killing of all the rākṣasas.

children.text: duṣprekṣyaḥ so 'bhavat kruddho yugāntāgnir iva jvalan
children.translated_text: When angry he became hard to look at, blazing like the fire at the end of an age;
seeing him possessed by splendor, the forest deities trembled.

children.text: tasya kruddhasya rūpaṃ tu rāmasya dadṛśe tadā
children.translated_text: Then the form of angry <s>Rāma</s> was seen
like that of <s>Pinākin</s>, ready to destroy <s>Dakṣa</s>'s sacrifice.
<s>Rāma</s>, standing firm with bow, angry and a slayer of enemies,
<s>Khara</s> saw when he came to the hermitage with his vanguard.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā saguṇaṃ cāpam udyamya kharaniḥsvanam
children.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Khara</s> raised his strung bow with a harsh sound
and urged his charioteer, saying, "Drive on facing <s>Rāma</s>."
At <s>Khara</s>'s command, that charioteer drove on the horses

children.text: yatra rāmo mahābāhur eko dhunvan dhanuḥ sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: to where mighty-armed <s>Rāma</s> stood alone, shaking his bow.

children.text: taṃ tu niṣpatitaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarve te rajanīcarāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing him rush forth, all those night-roaming rākṣasas,
roaring a great roar, surrounded him as his counselors.

children.text: sa teṣāṃ yātudhānānāṃ madhye rato gataḥ kharaḥ
children.translated_text: Having gone in a chariot into the midst of those yātudhānas, <s>Khara</s>
appeared like <s>Lohitāṅga</s> (Mars) risen among the stars.

children.text: tatas taṃ bhīmadhanvānaṃ kruddhāḥ sarve niśācarāḥ
children.translated_text: Then all the angry night-roamers
showered unconquerable <s>Rāma</s>, wielder of a terrible bow, with weapons of many kinds.

children.text: mudgarair āyasaiḥ śūlaiḥ prāsaiḥ khaḍgaiḥ paraśvadhaiḥ
children.translated_text: With iron clubs, spears, javelins, swords, and axes,
the rākṣasas, intent on rage, struck <s>Rāma</s> in battle.
Cloud-like, loud-roaring, and very strong,
they charged at <s>Kākutstha</s>, at <s>Rāma</s>, eager to kill him in battle.

children.text: te rāme śaravarṣāṇi vyasṛjan rakṣasāṃ guṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Those bands of rākṣasas loosed showers of arrows upon <s>Rāma</s>,
like rain-clouds raining streams upon a great mountain.

children.text: sa taiḥ parivṛto ghorai rāghavo rakṣasāṃ gaṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: Surrounded by those dreadful bands of rākṣasas, <s>Rāghava</s>

children.text: tithiṣv iva mahādevo vṛtaḥ pāriṣadāṃ gaṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: was like <s>Mahādeva</s> surrounded by hosts of attendants on the lunar days.

children.text: tāni muktāni śastrāṇi yātudhānaiḥ sa rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Those weapons released by the yātudhānas, <s>Rāghava</s>
received with arrows, as the ocean receives the torrents of rivers.

children.text: sa taiḥ praharaṇair ghorair bhinnagātro na vivyathe
children.translated_text: Though his body was pierced by those dreadful missiles, he did not tremble:

children.text: rāmaḥ pradīptair bahubhir vajrair iva mahācalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> was like a great mountain struck by many blazing thunderbolts.
Pierced and smeared with blood over all his limbs, <s>Rāghava</s>,
<s>Rāma</s>, became like the sun covered by twilight clouds.
The gods, gandharvas, siddhas, and supreme seers sank into distress

children.text: ekaṃ sahasrair bahubhis tadā dṛṣṭvā samāvṛtam ||
children.translated_text: when they saw one man surrounded then by many thousands.
Then <s>Rāma</s>, greatly enraged, making his bow into a circle,
released sharp arrows by the hundreds and then by the thousands.
Unstoppable, unbearable, like the nooses of Death in battle,
<s>Rāma</s> easily let fly straight-flying arrows feathered with vulture plumes.

children.text: te śarāḥ śatrusainyeṣu muktā rāmeṇa līlayā
children.translated_text: Those arrows, released with ease by <s>Rāma</s> into the enemy armies,

children.text: ādadū rakṣasāṃ prāṇān pāśāḥ kālakṛtā iva ||
children.translated_text: took away the lives of the rākṣasas like nooses made by Death.

children.text: bhittvā rākṣasadehāṃs tāṃs te śarā rudhirāplutāḥ
children.translated_text: Having pierced those rākṣasa bodies, those arrows, drenched with blood,
shone in the sky with splendor equal to blazing fire.
Countless arrows of <s>Rāma</s>, very fierce,
shot forth from the circle of his bow, taking away the lives of the rākṣasas.

children.text: tair dhanūṃṣi dhvajāgrāṇi varmāṇi ca śirāṃsi ca
children.translated_text: With them he cut down bows, the tips of banners, armor, and heads,
and many arms adorned with ornaments, and thighs like elephants' trunks.
Then, with nālīkas, nārācas, sharp-pointed arrows, and vikarṇis,
the night-roamers, being split apart, made a terrible, pained cry.

children.text: tat sainyaṃ niśitair bāṇair arditaṃ marmabhedibhiḥ
children.translated_text: That army, afflicted by sharp arrows that pierced vital points,

children.text: rāmeṇa na sukhaṃ lebhe śuṣkaṃ vanam ivāgninā ||
children.translated_text: found no ease from <s>Rāma</s>, like a dry forest from fire.

children.text: kecid bhīmabalāḥ śūrāḥ śūlān khaḍgān paraśvadhān
children.translated_text: Some night-roamers, heroic and of terrible strength,
in extreme anger hurled spears, swords, and axes at <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: tāni bāṇair mahābāhuḥ śastrāṇy āvārya rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Mighty-armed <s>Rāghava</s> warded off those weapons with arrows

children.text: jahāra samare prāṇāṃś cicheda ca śirodharān ||
children.translated_text: and in battle took away lives and cut off necks.

children.text: avaśiṣṭāś ca ye tatra viṣaṇṇāś ca niśācarāḥ
children.translated_text: The remaining night-roamers there, dejected
and tormented by arrows, ran straight to <s>Khara</s> for refuge.

children.text: tān sarvān punar ādāya samāśvāsya ca dūṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Gathering all of them again and reassuring them, <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>
rushed angrily at <s>Kākutstha</s>, like <s>Antaka</s> at <s>Rudra</s>.
Then all of them, having turned back and made fearless by relying on <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>,
charged again at <s>Rāma</s>, armed with sal trees, palm trees, and rocks.
That battle became astonishing, tumultuous, and hair-raising,

children.text: rāmasyāsya mahāghoraṃ punas teṣāṃ ca rakṣasām ||
children.translated_text: very dreadful, between this <s>Rāma</s> and those rākṣasas again.

children.text: tad drumāṇāṃ śilānāṃ ca varṣaṃ prāṇaharaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: That great, life-destroying shower of trees and rocks
righteous <s>Rāghava</s> received with sharp arrows.

children.text: pratigṛhya ca tad varaṃ nimīlita ivarṣabhaḥ
children.translated_text: Having received that excellent shower, the bull-like <s>Rāma</s>, as if with eyes closed,

children.text: rāmaḥ krodhaṃ paraṃ bheje vadhārthaṃ sarvarakṣasām ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> entered supreme anger for the killing of all the rākṣasas.
Then, filled with anger and as if blazing with splendor,
he scattered arrows against the army on every side, together with <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>.
Then the angry army-chief <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>, defiler of enemies,
He seized an iron club, mountain-peak-like and hair-raising,
wrapped with golden bands and able to crush the armies of the gods,
studded with sharp iron spikes and spattered with enemies' blood.
It felt like a thunderbolt or lightning strike, and could split open an enemy's gate-tower.
Taking up that iron club in battle, resembling a great serpent,
the night-roaming <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>, cruel in deed, rushed upon <s>Rāma</s>.
As that <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> was rushing toward him,
<s>Rāghava</s> cut off his two arms, still adorned with bracelets, with two arrows.
That great-bodied club, fallen from him, dropped at the front of the battlefield
like the banner of <s>Śakra</s>, after its wielder's hands had been cut off.

children.text: sa karābhyāṃ vikīrṇābhyāṃ papāta bhuvi dūṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> fell to the ground with his hands scattered apart,
like a proud great elephant with its two tusks shattered.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā taṃ patitaṃ bhūmau dūṣaṇaṃ nihataṃ raṇe
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> fallen on the ground, slain in battle,

children.text: sādhu sādhv iti kākutsthaṃ sarvabhūtāny apūjayan ||
children.translated_text: all beings honored <s>Kākutstha</s>, crying, "Well done, well done!"
At that moment three wrathful leaders of the army,
bound already by the noose of death, rushed together against <s>Rāma</s>:
<s>Mahākapāla</s>, <s>Sthūlākṣa</s>, and the very strong <s>Pramāthī</s>.
The rākṣasa <s>Mahākapāla</s> raised a huge spear,

children.text: sthūlākṣaḥ paṭṭiśaṃ gṛhya pramāthī ca paraśvadham ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sthūlākṣa</s> took up a paṭṭiśa spear, and <s>Pramāthī</s> an axe.

children.text: dṛṣṭvaivāpatatas tāṃs tu rāghavaḥ sāyakaiḥ śitaiḥ
children.translated_text: But when <s>Rāghava</s> saw them rushing on,
he received them with sharp-pointed arrows, as if they were guests who had arrived.
The delight of the Raghus cut off <s>Mahākapāla</s>'s head,
and with countless streams of arrows he crushed <s>Pramāthī</s>.
With keen shafts he filled <s>Sthūlākṣa</s>'s eyes,

children.text: sa papāta hato bhūmau viṭapīva mahādrumaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, slain, he fell upon the ground like a great tree with its branches.
Then the splendid hero, with arrows resembling fire
and adorned with gold and diamond, struck down the remainder of that army.

children.text: te rukmapuṅkhā viśikhāḥ sadhūmā iva pāvakāḥ
children.translated_text: Those gold-feathered arrows, like smoky fires,

children.text: nijaghnus tāni rakṣāṃsi vajrā iva mahādrumān ||
children.translated_text: struck down those rākṣasas like thunderbolts striking great trees.

children.text: rakṣasāṃ tu śataṃ rāmaḥ śatenaikena karṇinā
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> killed a hundred rākṣasas with a single hundred barbed arrows,
and a thousand with a thousand, on the front of the battlefield.
With their armor and ornaments split apart and their bows cut and broken,
the night-roamers, smeared with blood, fell upon the earth.
With those fallen warriors in battle, their hair loosened and their bodies sprinkled with blood,

children.text: āstīrṇā vasudhā kṛtsnā mahāvediḥ kuśair iva ||
children.translated_text: the whole earth was strewn as a great altar is strewn with kuśa grass.
In a moment that very terrible forest, its rākṣasas slain,
became like hell, muddy with flesh and blood.
Fourteen thousand rākṣasas of dreadful deeds
were slain by <s>Rāma</s> alone, a human being fighting on foot.

children.text: tasya sainyasya sarvasya kharaḥ śeṣo mahārathaḥ
children.translated_text: Of all that army there remained only the great chariot-warrior <s>Khara</s>,

children.text: rākṣasas triśirāś caiva rāmaś ca ripusūdanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the rākṣasa <s>Triśiras</s>, and <s>Rāma</s>, the slayer of foes.

children.text: tatas tu tad bhīmabalaṃ mahāhave samīkṣya rāmeṇa hataṃ balīyasā
children.translated_text: Then, seeing that dreadful force struck down in the great battle by the stronger <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: rathena rāmaṃ mahatā kharas tataḥ samāsasādendra ivodyatāśaniḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Khara</s> approached <s>Rāma</s> in his great chariot, like <s>Indra</s> with uplifted thunderbolt.
But as <s>Khara</s> was advancing toward <s>Rāma</s>,
a rākṣasa commander named <s>Triśiras</s> came up and said this:
"Appoint me, valiant one; turn back from this rash venture.
Watch mighty-armed <s>Rāma</s> brought down in battle.

children.text: pratijānāmi te satyam āyudhaṃ cāham ālabhe
children.translated_text: I pledge you the truth, and I touch my weapon as witness:
I shall kill <s>Rāma</s>, who deserves death at the hands of all rākṣasas.

children.text: ahaṃ vāsya raṇe mṛtyur eṣa vā samare mama
children.translated_text: Either I shall be his death in battle, or he will be mine in the fight.
Restrain your eagerness for battle for a moment and be a spectator.

children.text: prahṛṣṭo vā hate rāme janasthānaṃ prayāsyasi
children.translated_text: If <s>Rāma</s> is slain, you will go rejoicing to <s>Janasthāna</s>;
or, if I am slain, you will go forward to fight <s>Rāma</s>."
<s>Khara</s>, persuaded by that <s>Triśiras</s> through his longing for death,
gave him leave, saying, "Go, fight," and he advanced toward <s>Rāghava</s>.
<s>Triśiras</s>, in a bright chariot yoked with horses,

children.text: abhyadravad raṇe rāmaṃ triśṛṅga iva parvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: rushed upon <s>Rāma</s> in battle like a three-peaked mountain.
Releasing masses of arrow-showers like a great cloud,
he let out a roar like the sound of a water-soaked war drum.
Seeing the rākṣasa <s>Triśiras</s> coming on,
<s>Rāghava</s> met him with his bow, shaking loose sharp arrows.
A tremendous and mighty clash arose between <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Triśiras</s>,
two very powerful warriors, like the clash of a lion and an elephant.

children.text: tatas triśirasā bāṇair lalāṭe tāḍitas tribhiḥ
children.translated_text: Then, struck on the forehead by <s>Triśiras</s> with three arrows,

children.text: amarṣī kupito rāmaḥ saṃrabdham idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: indignant and enraged, <s>Rāma</s> spoke these words in fury:
"Ah, such is the strength of this rākṣasa, brave in prowess,

children.text: puṣpair iva śarair yasya lalāṭe 'smi parikṣataḥ
children.translated_text: by whose arrows I have been grazed on the forehead as though by flowers.
Now you too receive my arrows, released from the bowstring."

children.text: evam uktvā tu saṃrabdhaḥ śarān āśīviṣopamān
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, he angrily shot arrows like venomous snakes,
fourteen of them, into <s>Triśiras</s>'s chest.
With four arrows, their knots well bent,
the splendid hero brought down his four horses.
With eight shafts he felled the charioteer onto the floor of the chariot,

children.text: rāmaś cicheda bāṇena dhvajaṃ cāsya samucchritam ||
children.translated_text: and with one arrow <s>Rāma</s> cut down his lofty banner.
Then, as the night-roamer leapt from that chariot whose team had been killed,

children.text: bibheda rāmas taṃ bāṇair hṛdaye so 'bhavaj jaḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> pierced him in the heart with arrows, and he became senseless.
And with arrows the immeasurable-souled one, enraged at that rākṣasa,

children.text: śirāṃsy apātayat trīṇi vegavadbhis tribhiḥ śataiḥ ||
children.translated_text: struck down his three heads with three hundred swift shafts.
That night-roamer, vomiting blood and tormented by <s>Rāma</s>'s arrows,
fell to the ground together with his own heads that had already fallen.
Then the surviving rākṣasas, routed and dependent on <s>Khara</s>,

children.text: dravanti sma na tiṣṭhanti vyāghratrastā mṛgā iva ||
children.translated_text: fled and did not stand firm, like deer terrified by a tiger.

children.text: tān kharo dravato dṛṣṭvā nivartya ruṣitaḥ svayam
children.translated_text: Seeing them fleeing, <s>Khara</s> angrily turned them back himself,
and rushed straight at <s>Rāma</s>, as <s>Rāhu</s> rushes at the moon.

children.text: nihataṃ dūṣaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā raṇe triśirasā saha
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> slain in battle together with <s>Triśiras</s>,

children.text: kharasyāpy abhavat trāso dṛṣṭvā rāmasya vikramam ||
children.translated_text: even <s>Khara</s> felt fear when he saw <s>Rāma</s>'s valor.

children.text: sa dṛṣṭvā rākṣasaṃ sainyam aviṣahyaṃ mahābalam
children.translated_text: Seeing that mighty and irresistible rākṣasa army,

children.text: hatam ekena rāmeṇa dūṣaṇas triśirā api ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> and <s>Triśiras</s> too, slain by <s>Rāma</s> alone,

children.text: tad balaṃ hatabhūyiṣṭhaṃ vimanāḥ prekṣya rākṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: the rākṣasa looked upon that force, mostly destroyed, and grew dejected;

children.text: āsasāda kharo rāmaṃ namucir vāsavaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Khara</s> approached <s>Rāma</s> as <s>Namuci</s> approached <s>Vāsava</s>.
Drawing his strong bow, <s>Khara</s> took nārāca arrows that fed on blood,

children.text: kharaś cikṣepa rāmāya kruddhān āśīviṣān iva ||
children.translated_text: and, like angry venomous serpents, hurled them at <s>Rāma</s>.
Often shaking the bowstring and displaying his training in weapons,

children.text: cacāra samare mārgāñ śarai rathagataḥ kharaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Khara</s>, mounted on his chariot, moved through the battle paths with his arrows.

children.text: sa sarvāś ca diśo bāṇaiḥ pradiśaś ca mahārathaḥ
children.translated_text: That great chariot-warrior filled all the directions and intermediate directions with arrows;

children.text: pūrayāmāsa taṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmo 'pi sumahad dhanuḥ ||
children.translated_text: seeing him, <s>Rāma</s> too took up his very great bow.
With unbearable shafts, like fires sending out sparks,
he made the sky without an opening, like a rain cloud with showers.
The space around them became, through the sharp arrows released by <s>Khara</s> and <s>Rāma</s>,
no space at all, everywhere crowded with arrows.

children.text: śarajālāvṛtaḥ sūryo na tadā sma prakāśate
children.translated_text: The sun, covered by the net of arrows, did not shine then,
while the two warriors fought, intent on killing one another.
Then with nālīka and nārāca arrows, and with sharp-pointed vikarṇin shafts,

children.text: ājaghāna raṇe rāmaṃ totrair iva mahādvipam ||
children.translated_text: he struck <s>Rāma</s> in battle, as one strikes a great elephant with goads.
All beings saw that rākṣasa standing near, stationed on his chariot with bow in hand,
like Death with a noose in his hand.
Seeing him as bold as a lion and moving with a lion's stride,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā nodvijate rāmaḥ siṃhaḥ kṣudramṛgaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> was not shaken, as a lion is not shaken by a small beast.
Then <s>Khara</s>, in a great chariot shining like the sun,

children.text: āsasāda raṇe rāmaṃ pataṃga iva pāvakam ||
children.translated_text: approached <s>Rāma</s> in battle like a moth approaching fire.
Then, showing the swiftness of his hand, <s>Khara</s> cut
the great-souled <s>Rāma</s>'s bow, with its arrow, at the grip.

children.text: sa punas tv aparān sapta śarān ādāya varmaṇi
children.translated_text: Then again, in battle, the enraged one took seven other arrows
and struck his armor with them, blazing like <s>Śakra</s>'s thunderbolt.

children.text: tatas tat prahataṃ bāṇaiḥ kharamuktaiḥ suparvabhiḥ
children.translated_text: Then that armor of <s>Rāma</s>, radiant as the sun,
struck by the well-jointed arrows loosed by <s>Khara</s>, fell to the ground.

children.text: sa śarair arpitaḥ kruddhaḥ sarvagātreṣu rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Pierced by arrows on all his limbs, the angry <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: rarāja samare rāmo vidhūmo 'gnir iva jvalan ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, shone in battle like a smokeless blazing fire.
Then <s>Rāma</s>, destroyer of enemies, for the end of his foe

children.text: cakārāntāya sa ripoḥ sajyam anyan mahad dhanuḥ ||
children.translated_text: strung another great bow that gave a deep roar.

children.text: sumahad vaiṣṇavaṃ yat tad atisṛṣṭaṃ maharṣiṇā
children.translated_text: Raising that excellent, very great Vaiṣṇava bow, which had been given by the great seer,

children.text: varaṃ tad dhanur udyamya kharaṃ samabhidhāvata ||
children.translated_text: he rushed against <s>Khara</s>.
Then with arrows having golden shafts and well-bent joints,

children.text: cicheda rāmaḥ saṃkruddhaḥ kharasya samare dhvajam ||
children.translated_text: the enraged <s>Rāma</s> cut down <s>Khara</s>'s banner in battle.

children.text: sa darśanīyo bahudhā vicchinnaḥ kāñcano dhvajaḥ
children.translated_text: That beautiful golden banner, cut apart in many places,
went to the earth like the sun at the command of the gods.

children.text: taṃ caturbhiḥ kharaḥ kruddho rāmaṃ gātreṣu mārgaṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: Angry <s>Khara</s>, skilled in striking vital spots, pierced <s>Rāma</s>

children.text: vivyādha hṛdi marmajño mātaṃgam iva tomaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: in the limbs and in the heart with four arrows, like an elephant with lances.
Pierced by many arrows released from <s>Khara</s>'s bow,
<s>Rāma</s>, his limbs wet with blood, became exceedingly angry.

children.text: sa dhanur dhanvināṃ śreṣṭhaḥ pragṛhya paramāhave
children.translated_text: Then that best of bowmen, the supreme archer, grasped his bow
in the great battle and released six well-aimed arrows.

children.text: śirasy ekena bāṇena dvābhyāṃ bāhvor athārpayat
children.translated_text: With one arrow he struck him on the head, and with two he struck him on the arms;

children.text: tribhiś candrārdhavaktraiś ca vakṣasy abhijaghāna ha ||
children.translated_text: with three crescent-faced arrows he struck him in the chest.
Then afterward, the greatly splendid one, angry and wishing to kill the rākṣasa,
took thirteen nārāca arrows, like the sun and sharpened on stone.

children.text: tato 'sya yugam ekena caturbhiś caturo hayān
children.translated_text: Then with one he cut his yoke, with four his four horses,

children.text: ṣaṣṭhena ca śiraḥ saṃkhye cicheda kharasāratheḥ ||
children.translated_text: and with the sixth he cut off the head of <s>Khara</s>'s charioteer in the fight.

children.text: tribhis triveṇuṃ balavān dvābhyām akṣaṃ mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: With three arrows the strong, mighty one cut the triveṇu, and with two the axle;

children.text: dvādaśena tu bāṇena kharasya saśaraṃ dhanuḥ
children.translated_text: and with the twelfth arrow he cut <s>Khara</s>'s bow with its arrow.
Having cut it with a thunderbolt-like shaft, <s>Rāghava</s>, as if smiling,
with the thirteenth, equal to <s>Indra</s>, pierced <s>Khara</s> in battle.
His bow broken, his chariot gone, his horses killed, and his charioteer slain,

children.text: gadāpāṇir avaplutya tasthau bhūmau kharas tadā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Khara</s> then leapt down with mace in hand and stood on the ground.

children.text: tat karma rāmasya mahārathasya sametya devāś ca maharṣayaś ca
children.translated_text: The gods and great seers, having assembled, beheld that deed of <s>Rāma</s>, the great chariot-warrior,

children.text: apūjayan prāñjalayaḥ prahṛṣṭās tadā vimānāgragatāḥ sametāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, gathered on the fronts of their aerial cars, joyfully praised him with joined palms.

children.text: kharaṃ tu virathaṃ rāmo gadāpāṇim avasthitam
children.translated_text: But to <s>Khara</s>, who stood chariotless with mace in hand,
the greatly splendid <s>Rāma</s> spoke words, first gentle and then harsh:
While standing amid a great army crowded with elephants, horses, and chariots,
you have done a terribly cruel deed, detested by all the worlds.
You are a cause of terror to beings, cruel, and a doer of sinful deeds.

children.text: trayāṇām api lokānām īśvaro 'pi na tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: even if he is lord of all three worlds, does not remain standing.
But, night-roamer, when one performs an act opposed to the world,

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ sarvajano hanti sarpaṃ duṣṭam ivāgatam ||
children.translated_text: all people sharply strike him down, like a wicked snake that has come near.

children.text: lobhāt pāpāni kurvāṇaḥ kāmād vā yo na budhyate
children.translated_text: One who commits sins from greed, or from desire, and does not understand,

children.text: bhraṣṭaḥ paśyati tasyāntaṃ brāhmaṇī karakād iva ||
children.translated_text: fallen, sees the end of that deed, like a Brāhmaṇī plant from hail.
What fruit, <s>rākṣasa</s>, will you obtain

children.text: kiṃ nu hatvā mahābhāgān phalaṃ prāpsyasi rākṣasa ||
children.translated_text: by killing the greatly blessed ascetics dwelling in <s>Daṇḍakāraṇya</s> and practicing <s>dharma</s>?
Men of sinful deeds, cruel and despised by the world,

children.text: aiśvaryaṃ prāpya tiṣṭhanti śīrṇamūlā iva drumāḥ ||
children.translated_text: do not stand long after obtaining power, like trees with withered roots.

children.text: avaśyaṃ labhate kartā phalaṃ pāpasya karmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The doer inevitably receives the fruit of an evil deed,

children.text: ghoraṃ paryāgate kāle drumaḥ puṣpam ivārtavam ||
children.translated_text: terrible when the time has come round, as a tree receives its seasonal flower.

children.text: nacirāt prāpyate loke pāpānāṃ karmaṇāṃ phalam
children.translated_text: In the world the fruit of evil deeds is obtained before long,
night-roamer, like that of poisonous foods after they have been eaten.
While you were practicing terrible evil and wishing harm to the world,

children.text: aham āsādito rājā prāṇān hantuṃ niśācara ||
children.translated_text: you have come upon me, a king, night-roamer, for the taking of your life.

children.text: adya hi tvāṃ mayā muktāḥ śarāḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇāḥ
children.translated_text: For today the arrows released by me, adorned with gold,
will tear you open and fall upon you like snakes into an anthill.
Those who practiced <s>dharma</s> and were devoured by you in <s>Daṇḍakāraṇya</s>:
today, slain in battle together with your army, you will follow them.

children.text: adya tvāṃ nihataṃ bāṇaiḥ paśyantu paramarṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: Today let the supreme seers whom you injured before

children.text: nirayasthaṃ vimānasthā ye tvayā hiṃsitāḥ purā ||
children.translated_text: behold you, struck down by arrows, in hell, while they stand in heavenly cars.

children.text: prahara tvaṃ yathākāmaṃ kuru yatnaṃ kulādhama
children.translated_text: Strike as you wish; make your effort, vilest of your clan.

children.text: adya te pātayiṣyāmi śiras tālaphalaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: Today I shall make your head fall like a palm fruit.

children.text: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa kruddhaḥ saṃraktalocanaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Rāma</s>, enraged and with blood-red eyes,
he then replied to <s>Rāma</s>, laughing and stupefied with anger:
After killing common <s>rākṣasas</s> in battle, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>,
why do you, by yourself, praise yourself, who are not worthy of praise?

children.text: vikrāntā balavanto vā ye bhavanti nararṣabhāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who are truly valiant or powerful, bull among men,

children.text: kathayanti na te kiṃcit tejasā svena garvitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: say nothing, proud in their own splendor.
But common men, uncontrolled in themselves, dregs of kṣatriyas in the world,
boast uselessly, <s>Rāma</s>, just as you boast.
What hero in battle, naming his lineage,

children.text: mṛtyukāle hi samprāpte svayam aprastave stavam ||
children.translated_text: would utter praise of himself, out of place, when the time of death has arrived?

children.text: sarvathā tu laghutvaṃ te katthanena vidarśitam
children.translated_text: In every way your littleness has been shown by this bragging,
like gold's counterfeit nature by heated kuśa-grass fire.

children.text: na tu mām iha tiṣṭhantaṃ paśyasi tvaṃ gadādharam
children.translated_text: But you do not see me standing here, mace in hand,
unshakable like a mountain bearing the earth and streaked with minerals.

children.text: paryāpto 'haṃ gadāpāṇir hantuṃ prāṇān raṇe tava
children.translated_text: I, mace in hand, am enough to take your life in battle,
like <s>Antaka</s>, noose in hand, for even the three worlds.

children.text: kāmaṃ bahv api vaktavyaṃ tvayi vakṣyāmi na tv aham
children.translated_text: Though much could be said to you, I shall not say it;

children.text: astaṃ gaccheddhi savitā yuddhavighnas tato bhavet ||
children.translated_text: for the sun would set, and then there would be an interruption to the battle.
Fourteen thousand <s>rākṣasas</s> of mine have been killed by you.
Today, by your destruction, I shall wipe away their tears.

children.text: ity uktvā paramakruddhas tāṃ gadāṃ paramāṅgadaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, most enraged, wearing splendid armlets,

children.text: kharaś cikṣepa rāmāya pradīptām aśaniṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Khara</s> hurled that mace at <s>Rāma</s>, like a blazing thunderbolt.
That great blazing mace, released from <s>Khara</s>'s arm,

children.text: bhasma vṛkṣāṃś ca gulmāṃś ca kṛtvāgāt tatsamīpataḥ ||
children.translated_text: reduced trees and thickets to ash and came near him.
As that fiery mace, like the noose of death, came falling,
<s>Rāma</s> cut it into many pieces with arrows while it was in the air.

children.text: sā viśīrṇā śarair bhinnā papāta dharaṇītale
children.translated_text: Shattered and split by arrows, it fell upon the surface of the earth,
like a female serpent brought down by the power of spells and herbs.

children.text: bhittvā tu tāṃ gadāṃ bāṇai rāghavo dharmavatsalaḥ
children.translated_text: After breaking that mace with arrows, <s>Rāghava</s>, devoted to <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: smayamānaḥ kharaṃ vākyaṃ saṃrabdham idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: smiling, spoke this agitated speech to <s>Khara</s>:
This whole strength of yours has been displayed, lowest of <s>rākṣasas</s>.
You are far weaker than I; in vain you roar at me.
This mace, split apart by arrows, has gone to the surface of the earth,
destroying the confidence that came from your boastful speech.
As for what you said, 'I shall wipe away

children.text: rākṣasānāṃ karomīti mithyā tad api te vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the tears of the destroyed <s>rākṣasas</s>,' that word of yours too is false.
Of you, a low, petty-natured, false-conducted <s>rākṣasa</s>,
I shall carry off the life-breaths, as <s>Garuḍa</s> carried off the nectar.
Today, when your throat is split and you are torn open by my arrows,
the earth will drink your blood, adorned with foam and bubbles.
With all your limbs smeared with dust and both your arms fallen and cast aside,

children.text: svapsyase gāṃ samāśliṣya durlabhāṃ pramadām iva ||
children.translated_text: you will sleep embracing the earth, as if she were a woman hard to win.
When you, dregs of <s>rākṣasas</s>, lie in greatly deepened sleep,
these regions of <s>Daṇḍakāraṇya</s> will become a refuge for those without refuge.
In <s>Janasthāna</s>, made a place of slaughter by my arrows, <s>rākṣasa</s>,
the sages will wander everywhere in the forest without fear.
Today the <s>rākṣasa</s> women, deprived of their kinsmen, will scatter,
pitiful, their faces wet with tears, spreading fear because of their own fear.
Today, night-roamer, those wives of fitting families

children.text: anurūpakulāḥ patnyo yāsāṃ tvaṃ patir īdṛśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: will come to know the taste of grief, those whose husband is one such as you.
Cruel by nature, petty-souled, forever a thorn in the throats of Brāhmaṇas,

children.text: tvatkṛte śaṅkitair agnau munibhiḥ pātyate haviḥ ||
children.translated_text: because of you the oblation is cast into the fire by sages who are afraid.

children.text: tam evam abhisaṃrabdhaṃ bruvāṇaṃ rāghavaṃ raṇe
children.translated_text: To <s>Rāghava</s>, who was speaking thus in fury on the battlefield,
<s>Khara</s>, with a voice harsher than ever, angrily rebuked him:

children.text: dṛḍhaṃ khalv avalipto 'si bhayeṣv api ca nirbhayaḥ
children.translated_text: You are certainly deeply arrogant, and fearless even in the face of dangers.

children.text: vācyāvācyaṃ tato hi tvaṃ mṛtyuvaśyo na budhyase ||
children.translated_text: For that reason, being already subject to death, you do not understand what may and may not be said.
For men who are encircled by the noose of Time
and whose six senses are cast down do not know what should and should not be done.

children.text: evam uktvā tato rāmaṃ saṃrudhya bhrukuṭiṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to <s>Rāma</s>, the night-roamer then knit his brow
and saw a great śāla tree not far away.
Looking all around in battle for something to use as a weapon,
he saw it and uprooted it, baring his teeth.
Lifting it up with both arms and roaring, the mighty one

children.text: rāmam uddiśya cikṣepa hatas tvam iti cābravīt ||
children.translated_text: hurled it at <s>Rāma</s> and said, You are slain!

children.text: tam āpatantaṃ bāṇaughaiś chittvā rāmaḥ pratāpavān
children.translated_text: As it came flying toward him, mighty <s>Rāma</s> cut it apart with torrents of arrows

children.text: roṣam āhārayat tīvraṃ nihantuṃ samare kharam ||
children.translated_text: and summoned up fierce anger in order to kill <s>Khara</s> in battle.
Then <s>Rāma</s>, sweating and with the corners of his eyes reddened by anger,
pierced <s>Khara</s> in battle with a thousand arrows.

children.text: tasya bāṇāntarād raktaṃ bahu susrāva phenilam
children.translated_text: Much foaming blood flowed from the spaces between his arrow wounds,
like streams of water pouring from a mountain spring.

children.text: vihvalaḥ sa kṛto bāṇaiḥ kharo rāmeṇa saṃyuge
children.translated_text: Made reeling by <s>Rāma</s>'s arrows in the fight, <s>Khara</s>,
maddened by the smell of blood, rushed swiftly at him again.
As he charged in fury, trained in weapons and drenched in blood,
<s>Rāma</s> withdrew step by step, with somewhat rapid movement.
Then, for <s>Khara</s>'s death in battle, <s>Rāma</s> took up
an arrow blazing like fire, like another rod of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: sa tad dattaṃ maghavatā surarājena dhīmatā
children.translated_text: That arrow had been given by wise <s>Maghavan</s>, the king of the gods;

children.text: saṃdadhe ca sa dharmātmā mumoca ca kharaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: the righteous-souled one set it on the bow and released it toward <s>Khara</s>.
Released by <s>Rāma</s> as he raised his bow, that great arrow,
sounding like a thunderclap, fell upon <s>Khara</s>'s chest.

children.text: sa papāta kharo bhūmau dahyamānaḥ śarāgninā
children.translated_text: <s>Khara</s> fell to the ground, burning with the fire of the arrow,
like <s>Andhaka</s> burned up by <s>Rudra</s> in <s>Śvetāraṇya</s>.

children.text: sa vṛtra iva vajreṇa phenena namucir yathā
children.translated_text: Like <s>Vṛtra</s> by the thunderbolt, like <s>Namuci</s> by foam,
and like <s>Bala</s> struck by <s>Indra</s>'s bolt, <s>Khara</s> fell slain.
Then all the royal seers and the supreme seers gathered together,

children.text: sabhājya muditā rāmam idaṃ vacanam abruvan ||
children.translated_text: honored <s>Rāma</s> and joyfully spoke these words:
For this purpose the mighty <s>Mahendra</s>, the chastiser of <s>Pāka</s>,
<s>Puraṃdara</s>, came to the holy hermitage of <s>Śarabhaṅga</s>.

children.text: ānītas tvam imaṃ deśam upāyena maharṣibhiḥ
children.translated_text: You were brought to this region by the great seers through a stratagem
for the destruction of these cruel rākṣasas of sinful deeds.

children.text: tad idaṃ naḥ kṛtaṃ kāryaṃ tvayā daśarathātmaja
children.translated_text: That task of ours has now been accomplished by you, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>.
The great seers will happily practice <s>dharma</s> in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forests.

children.text: etasminn antare vīro lakṣmaṇaḥ saha sītayā
children.translated_text: Meanwhile the hero <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, together with <s>Sītā</s>,
came out from the mountain stronghold and happily entered the hermitage.

children.text: tato rāmas tu vijayī pūjyamāno maharṣibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Then victorious <s>Rāma</s>, honored by the great seers,
entered the hermitage, and the hero was greeted respectfully by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Seeing that slayer of enemies, the bringer of happiness to the great seers,
<s>Vaidehī</s> became delighted and embraced her husband.
Then <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>, seeing fourteen thousand
rākṣasas of dreadful deeds slain by <s>Rāma</s> alone,

children.text: dūṣaṇaṃ ca kharaṃ caiva hataṃ triśirasaṃ raṇe
children.translated_text: and seeing <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>, <s>Khara</s>, and <s>Triśiras</s> slain in battle,
again let out a great roar, like a rain cloud.

children.text: sā dṛṣṭvā karma rāmasya kṛtam anyaiḥ suduṣkaram
children.translated_text: Seeing the deed done by <s>Rāma</s>, very hard for others to do,
she went, deeply agitated, to <s>Laṅkā</s>, ruled by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
There, at the front of his palace, she saw <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, radiant with splendor,
seated with his ministers like <s>Vāsava</s> with the <s>Maruts</s>.
He sat on an excellent golden throne shining like the sun,
placed upon a golden dais, majestic and blazing like fire.
He was unconquerable in battle by gods, gandharvas, beings,
and great-souled seers; a hero, like Death with gaping mouth.
In the clashes of gods and asuras he had been wounded by thunderbolts and lightning missiles,
and his chest bore raised scars from the tips of <s>Airāvata</s>'s tusks.
He had twenty arms and ten necks, and his ornaments were splendid to behold.
He was broad-chested, heroic, and marked with the signs of royalty.
He shone like smooth vaidūrya, with earrings of heated gold,
fine-armed, white-toothed, great-mouthed, and mountain-like.
In battles with the gods his body had been struck hundreds of times
by the fall of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s discus and likewise by all the divine weapons.
He could disturb the unshakable oceans and was swift in action;
he hurled mountain peaks and crushed the gods.
He was a destroyer of dharmas and a violator of others' wives,
a wielder of every divine missile and always an interrupter of sacrifices.

children.text: purīṃ bhogavatīṃ gatvā parājitya ca vāsukim
children.translated_text: Having gone to the city <s>Bhogavatī</s> and defeated <s>Vāsuki</s>,

children.text: takṣakasya priyāṃ bhāryāṃ parājitya jahāra yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he conquered <s>Takṣaka</s> and carried off his dear wife.
Having gone to Mount <s>Kailāsa</s> and defeated <s>Naravāhana</s>,

children.text: vimānaṃ puṣpakaṃ tasya kāmagaṃ vai jahāra yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he carried off his Puṣpaka aerial car, which went wherever one wished.

children.text: vanaṃ caitrarathaṃ divyaṃ nalinīṃ nandanaṃ vanam
children.translated_text: The divine <s>Caitraratha</s> grove, the lotus pond <s>Nalinī</s>, and the <s>Nandana</s> forest--
in anger that powerful one would destroy the gardens of the gods.
The blessed moon and sun, scorchers of foes, as they rose,
he, like a mountain peak, would hold back with his arms.
Having practiced austerities for ten thousand years in the great forest,

children.text: purā svayambhuve dhīraḥ śirāṃsy upajahāra yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: who long ago, steadfast, offered his heads to <s>Svayambhū</s>.
By gods, dānavas, gandharvas, piśācas, birds, and serpents,

children.text: abhayaṃ yasya saṃgrāme mṛtyuto mānuṣād ṛte ||
children.translated_text: he had been granted freedom from fear in battle and from death, except at the hands of a human being.
The sacred soma, consecrated with mantras by twice-born priests at sacrifices,
that mighty one would destroy in the havirdhāna sheds.
Cruel, a taker of completed sacrifices, a slayer of brahmans, evil in conduct,
harsh, pitiless, intent on what was harmful to creatures,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, who brought fear to all beings and all worlds,

children.text: rākṣasī bhrātaraṃ krūraṃ sā dadarśa mahābalam
children.translated_text: the rākṣasī saw her cruel, mighty brother.
She saw that lord of rākṣasas, adorned with divine garments and ornaments,
resplendent with divine garlands, greatly fortunate, the delight of <s>Paulastya</s>'s line.
To him, after showing herself overcome with fear, bewilderment, and faintness, with blazing wide eyes,

children.text: sudāruṇaṃ vākyam abhītacāriṇī mahātmanā śūrpaṇakhā virūpitā ||
children.translated_text: the disfigured <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>, moving without fear, spoke a most terrible speech before that great-souled one.
Then wretched <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>, enraged, addressed <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, who made the world cry out,
and in the midst of his ministers she spoke harsh words.
Drunk with sensual pleasures, acting as you please, unchecked,
you do not perceive the dreadful danger that has arisen, though it should be understood.
Subjects do not highly regard a king attached to vulgar pleasures, ruled by desire,

children.text: lubdhaṃ na bahu manyante śmaśānāgnim iva prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and greedy, just as they do not value a funeral fire.

children.text: svayaṃ kāryāṇi yaḥ kāle nānutiṣṭhati pārthivaḥ
children.translated_text: A king who does not himself attend to affairs at the proper time

children.text: sa tu vai saha rājyena taiś ca kāryair vinaśyati ||
children.translated_text: perishes along with his kingdom and with those very affairs.
Men avoid from afar a ruler whose spies are not properly employed, who is hard to approach and not in control of himself,

children.text: varjayanti narā dūrān nadīpaṅkam iva dvipāḥ ||
children.translated_text: as elephants avoid the mud of a river.

children.text: ye na rakṣanti viṣayam asvādhīnā narādhipāḥ
children.translated_text: Kings who are not in control of themselves and do not protect their realm

children.text: te na vṛddhyā prakāśante girayaḥ sāgare yathā ||
children.translated_text: do not shine forth with prosperity, like mountains in the ocean.
Having made enemies of self-possessed gods, gandharvas, and dānavas,
with spies ill-employed and yourself fickle, how will you be a king?

children.text: yeṣāṃ cāraś ca kośaś ca nayaś ca jayatāṃ vara
children.translated_text: O best of conquerors, those kings whose spies, treasury, and policy

children.text: asvādhīnā narendrāṇāṃ prākṛtais te janaiḥ samāḥ ||
children.translated_text: are not under their control are equal to common people.

children.text: yasmāt paśyanti dūrasthān sarvān arthān narādhipāḥ
children.translated_text: Because kings see all matters, even those far away,
through spies, therefore kings are called long-eyed.

children.text: ayuktacāraṃ manye tvāṃ prākṛtaiḥ sacivair vṛtam
children.translated_text: I think your spies are ill-employed, and you are surrounded by ordinary ministers,

children.text: svajanaṃ ca janasthānaṃ hataṃ yo nāvabudhyase ||
children.translated_text: since you did not learn that your own people and Janasthāna had been destroyed.
Fourteen thousand rākṣasas of dreadful deeds

children.text: hatāny ekena rāmeṇa kharaś ca sahadūṣaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: have been slain by <s>Rāma</s> alone, and <s>Khara</s> together with <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>.

children.text: ṛṣīṇām abhayaṃ dattaṃ kṛtakṣemāś ca daṇḍakāḥ
children.translated_text: Safety has been given to the seers, and the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forests have been made secure;
Janasthāna has been overrun by <s>Rāma</s>, whose deeds are effortless.

children.text: tvaṃ tu lubdhaḥ pramattaś ca parādhīnaś ca rāvaṇa
children.translated_text: But you, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, are greedy, careless, and dependent on others,

children.text: viṣaye sve samutpannaṃ bhayaṃ yo nāvabudhyase ||
children.translated_text: since you do not perceive the danger that has arisen in your own domain.
All beings do not run to a king in calamity
if he is severe, gives little, is careless, arrogant, and deceitful.
Even his own people destroy in calamity a ruler
who is excessively proud, unapproachable, self-important, and wrathful.

children.text: nānutiṣṭhati kāryāṇi bhayeṣu na bibheti ca
children.translated_text: One who does not attend to affairs and does not fear dangers

children.text: kṣipraṃ rājyāc cyuto dīnas tṛṇais tulyo bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: will quickly be cast down from his kingdom, wretched, and become equal to straw.

children.text: śuṣkakāṣṭhair bhavet kāryaṃ loṣṭair api ca pāṃsubhiḥ
children.translated_text: Use may be made of dry wood, and even of clods and dust,

children.text: na tu sthānāt paribhraṣṭaiḥ kāryaṃ syād vasudhādhipaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: but no use can be made of kings who have fallen from their station.

children.text: upabhuktaṃ yathā vāsaḥ srajo vā mṛditā yathā
children.translated_text: As a garment that has been worn, or garlands that have been crushed,
so a man fallen from kingship is useless, even if capable.

children.text: apramattaś ca yo rājā sarvajño vijitendriyaḥ
children.translated_text: But the king who is vigilant, all-knowing, master of his senses,

children.text: kṛtajño dharmaśīlaś ca sa rājā tiṣṭhate ciram ||
children.translated_text: grateful, and established in <s>dharma</s>, that king remains long in power.
Though asleep with his eyes, he keeps awake through the eye of policy;

children.text: vyaktakrodhaprasādaś ca sa rājā pūjyate janaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: clear in anger and favor alike, that king is honored by the people.

children.text: tvaṃ tu rāvaṇa durbuddhir guṇair etair vivarjitaḥ
children.translated_text: But you, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, of wicked mind, are devoid of these virtues,

children.text: yasya te 'viditaś cārai rakṣasāṃ sumahān vadhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for this great slaughter of rākṣasas was unknown to you through your spies.
One who despises others, is attached to sensual domains, and does not know the true division of place and time,
whose judgment is misapplied in deciding merits and faults, will soon lose his kingdom and fall into ruin.

children.text: iti svadoṣān parikīrtitāṃs tayā samīkṣya buddhyā kṣaṇadācareśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: When the lord of night-roamers saw with his mind his own faults recited by her,

children.text: dhanena darpeṇa balena cānvito vicintayāmāsa ciraṃ sa rāvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, endowed with wealth, pride, and power, reflected for a long time.

children.text: tataḥ śūrpaṇakhāṃ kruddhāṃ bruvatīṃ paruṣaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, as angry <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s> spoke harsh words,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, enraged in the midst of his ministers, questioned her.

children.text: kaś ca rāmaḥ kathaṃvīryaḥ kiṃrūpaḥ kiṃparākramaḥ
children.translated_text: Who is <s>Rāma</s>? What is his strength? What is his form? What is his prowess?
For what purpose has he entered the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest, so difficult to traverse?

children.text: āyudhaṃ kiṃ ca rāmasya nihatā yena rākṣasāḥ
children.translated_text: What is <s>Rāma</s>'s weapon, by which the rākṣasas were slain,

children.text: kharaś ca nihataḥ saṃkhye dūṣaṇas triśirās tathā ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Khara</s> was killed in battle, as were <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> and <s>Triśiras</s>?
Thus addressed by the lord of rākṣasas, the rākṣasī, overcome with anger,
then began to describe <s>Rāma</s> properly.
Long-armed, broad-eyed, wearing bark cloth and a black antelope skin,
<s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, is equal in form to <s>Kandarpa</s>.
Drawing a bow like <s>Śakra</s>'s rainbow, with golden armlets flashing,

children.text: dīptān kṣipati nārācān sarpān iva mahāviṣān ||
children.translated_text: he shoots blazing iron arrows like serpents of deadly poison.

children.text: nādadānaṃ śarān ghorān na muñcantaṃ mahābalam
children.translated_text: In battle I do not see mighty <s>Rāma</s> taking up his terrible arrows,

children.text: na kārmukaṃ vikarṣantaṃ rāmaṃ paśyāmi saṃyuge ||
children.translated_text: nor releasing them, nor drawing his bow.

children.text: hanyamānaṃ tu tat sainyaṃ paśyāmi śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ
children.translated_text: But I see that army being struck down by showers of arrows,
like the finest crop battered by <s>Indra</s> with showers of hailstones.
Fourteen thousand rākṣasas of dreadful valor
were slain with sharp arrows by that single foot soldier.
In somewhat more than half a muhūrta, <s>Khara</s> too, together with <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>, was killed;

children.text: ṛṣīṇām abhayaṃ dattaṃ kṛtakṣemāś ca daṇḍakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: safety was given to the seers, and the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forests were made secure.
I alone was somehow spared, after being humiliated by the great-souled one,
by the self-knowing <s>Rāma</s>, who hesitated to kill a woman.
And his brother, greatly radiant, equal to him in qualities and valor,

children.text: anuraktaś ca bhaktaś ca lakṣmaṇo nāma vīryavān ||
children.translated_text: named <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, is devoted, loyal, and heroic.

children.text: amarṣī durjayo jetā vikrānto buddhimān balī
children.translated_text: Impatient of insult, hard to conquer, victorious, bold, intelligent, and strong,

children.text: rāmasya dakṣiṇo bāhur nityaṃ prāṇo bahiścaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: he is always <s>Rāma</s>'s right arm, his very life moving outside his body.
And <s>Rāma</s>'s broad-eyed lawful wife, famed,
is named <s>Sītā</s>, the lovely-hipped <s>Vaidehī</s> of slender waist.

children.text: naiva devī na gandharvī na yakṣī na ca kiṃnarī
children.translated_text: Neither goddess nor gandharvī, neither yakṣī nor kiṃnarī,
have I ever before seen such a woman on the surface of the earth.

children.text: yasya sītā bhaved bhāryā yaṃ ca hṛṣṭā pariṣvajet
children.translated_text: He whose wife <s>Sītā</s> might be, and whom she would joyfully embrace,

children.text: atijīvet sa sarveṣu lokeṣv api puraṃdarāt ||
children.translated_text: would surpass even <s>Puraṃdara</s> in all the worlds.
She is well-conducted, with a body worthy of praise, unequalled in beauty on earth;

children.text: tavānurūpā bhāryā sā tvaṃ ca tasyās tathā patiḥ ||
children.translated_text: she is a wife suited to you, and you likewise are a husband suited to her.
That fair-faced woman, with broad hips and full, high breasts,
I set out to bring here as a wife for you.
But when today you see that <s>Vaidehī</s>, whose face is like the full moon,

children.text: manmathasya śarāṇāṃ ca tvaṃ vidheyo bhaviṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: you will become subject to the arrows of <s>Manmatha</s>.

children.text: yadi tasyām abhiprāyo bhāryārthe tava jāyate
children.translated_text: If desire for her as a wife arises in you,

children.text: śīghram uddhriyatāṃ pādo jayārtham iha dakṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: quickly raise your right foot here for the sake of victory.

children.text: kuru priyaṃ tathā teṣāṃ rakṣasāṃ rākṣaseśvara
children.translated_text: Do what is pleasing also to those rākṣasas, O lord of rākṣasas,
through the killing of that cruel <s>Rāma</s>, the dweller in the hermitage.

children.text: taṃ śarair niśitair hatvā lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahāratham
children.translated_text: Killing him with sharpened arrows, and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> too, the great chariot-fighter,
you will duly and happily enjoy <s>Sītā</s>, deprived of her protectors.

children.text: rocate yadi te vākyaṃ mamaitad rākṣaseśvara
children.translated_text: If this word of mine pleases you, O lord of rākṣasas,
then carry out my command without hesitation, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: niśamya rāmeṇa śarair ajihmagair hatāñ janasthānagatān niśācarān
children.translated_text: Hearing that the night-roamers who dwelt in <s>Janasthāna</s> have been slain by <s>Rāma</s>'s straight-flying arrows,

children.text: kharaṃ ca buddhvā nihataṃ ca dūṣaṇaṃ tvam adya kṛtyaṃ pratipattum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: and knowing <s>Khara</s> and <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> slain, you ought today to set about the task.
Then, having heard that hair-raising speech of <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>,

children.text: sacivān abhyanujñāya kāryaṃ buddhvā jagāma ha ||
children.translated_text: he dismissed his ministers, understood the matter, and went away.

children.text: tat kāryam anugamyātha yathāvad upalabhya ca
children.translated_text: Then, following up that matter and learning it properly,

children.text: doṣāṇāṃ ca guṇānāṃ ca sampradhārya balābalam ||
children.translated_text: and weighing the strength and weakness of faults and advantages,

children.text: iti kartavyam ity eva kṛtvā niścayam ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: having made in his mind the decision, 'This is what must be done,'

children.text: sthirabuddhis tato ramyāṃ yānaśālāṃ jagāma ha ||
children.translated_text: with steady judgment he then went to the lovely carriage-house.
Having then gone secretly to the carriage-house, the lord of rākṣasas
urged his charioteer, saying, 'Let the chariot be yoked.'
Thus addressed, in a moment the swift-acting charioteer
yoked for him the excellent chariot he desired.
Mounting the golden chariot, wish-moving and adorned with jewels,
yoked with asses with faces like piśācas and golden ornaments,
with it, whose sound resembled a cloud, that younger brother of the wealth-giver,
the glorious lord of rākṣasas, went toward the lord of streams and rivers.
That ten-faced one, with white yak-tail fans and a white parasol,
lustrous like smooth vaidūrya and adorned with heated gold,
ten-mouthed, twenty-armed, with splendid accoutrements,
enemy of the thirty gods, slayer of foremost sages, like a ten-crested king of mountains,
having mounted the wish-moving chariot, the lord of rākṣasas shone
like a cloud in the sky encircled with lightning and accompanied by cranes.
The mighty one looked out over the coastal land with its mountains,
strewn by thousands with trees bearing various flowers and fruits;
surrounded on every side by lotus ponds with cool, auspicious water,
and by spacious hermitage grounds furnished with altars;
crowded with plantains and āḍhakī plants, adorned with coconuts,

children.text: sālais tālais tamālaiś ca tarubhiś ca supuṣpitaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and with śāla, palm, tamāla, and other trees in full bloom;
beautified by supreme seers of extremely regulated diet,

children.text: nāgaiḥ suparṇair gandharvaiḥ kiṃnaraiś ca sahasraśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and by nāgas, suparṇas, gandharvas, and kiṃnaras in thousands;

children.text: jitakāmaiś ca siddhaiś ca cāraṇaiś copaśobhitam
children.translated_text: adorned by siddhas who had conquered desire and by cāraṇas,
by ājas, vaikhānasas, māṣas, vālakhilyas, and marīcipas;
filled with thousands of apsarases of divine form, wearing divine ornaments and garlands,
skilled in the arts of play and love;
served by splendid wives of gods and surrounded by prosperity,
traversed by hosts of gods and dānavas who feed on nectar;
filled with haṃsas, krauñcas, and plavas, and resounding with sārasas;
lovely, with vaidūrya slabs, gleaming with the splendor of the ocean;
and on every side he saw pale, spacious aerial cars, furnished with divine garlands,
attended by instrumental music and song.
As the wish-moving cars of those who had conquered worlds by austerity descended,
the younger brother of the wealth-giver saw gandharvas and apsarases as well.
And he saw thousands of gentle sandalwood forests, rich in exudations, sap, and roots,
satisfying to the sense of smell.

children.text: agarūṇāṃ ca mukhyānāṃ vanāny upavanāni ca
children.translated_text: He looked upon forests and groves of the finest aloe trees,

children.text: takkolānāṃ ca jātyānāṃ phalānāṃ ca sugandhinām ||
children.translated_text: of takkola and jāti trees, and of fragrant fruits,

children.text: puṣpāṇi ca tamālasya gulmāni maricasya ca
children.translated_text: flowers of the tamāla and thickets of pepper plants,
and heaps of pearls drying along the shore;
beds of conches as well, and piles of coral,

children.text: kāñcanāni ca śailāni rājatāni ca sarvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and mountains of gold and silver everywhere;
lovely springs and clear lakes,
places endowed with wealth and grain and thronged with jewel-like women;
and cities crowded with elephants, horses, and chariots.
He looked upon that level region, smooth everywhere, with breezes soft to the touch,
the marshland of the ocean king, like the third heaven.

children.text: tatrāpaśyat sa meghābhaṃ nyagrodham ṛṣibhir vṛtam ||
children.translated_text: There he saw a banyan, cloud-like in appearance, surrounded by sages,

children.text: samantād yasya tāḥ śākhāḥ śatayojanam āyatāḥ
children.translated_text: whose branches stretched for a hundred yojanas on every side.

children.text: yasya hastinam ādāya mahākāyaṃ ca kacchapam
children.translated_text: Taking up an elephant and a huge tortoise,
the mighty <s>Garuḍa</s> had come to one of its branches for the sake of food.

children.text: tasya tāṃ sahasā śākhāṃ bhāreṇa patagottamaḥ
children.translated_text: Then suddenly, through the weight, that best of birds,
the mighty <s>Suparṇa</s>, broke that leaf-covered branch.
There were <s>Vaikhānasa</s> ascetics, <s>Māṣas</s>, <s>Vālakhilyas</s>, and <s>Marīcipas</s>,

children.text: ajā babhūvur dhūmrāś ca saṃgatāḥ paramarṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the supreme seers called <s>Ajas</s> and <s>Dhūmras</s> were gathered there.

children.text: teṣāṃ dayārthaṃ garuḍas tāṃ śākhāṃ śatayojanām
children.translated_text: Out of compassion for them, <s>Garuḍa</s> took up that hundred-yojana branch
and sped away, carrying also both the elephant and the tortoise.
Standing on one foot, that righteous one ate that flesh;
and after striking the Niṣāda territory with the branch, that best of birds
felt incomparable joy, having released the great sages.
By that very joy his valor was doubled,
and the wise one formed the intention of bringing away <s>amṛta</s>, the nectar of immortality.
Having crushed the iron lattices and broken into the excellent jewel-house,
he then carried off the nectar guarded in the palace of mighty <s>Indra</s>.
The younger brother of <s>Dhanada</s> saw that banyan, honored by hosts of great seers,
marked by <s>Suparṇa</s>, and known by the name <s>Subhadra</s>.

children.text: taṃ tu gatvā paraṃ pāraṃ samudrasya nadīpateḥ
children.translated_text: Then, going to the far shore of the ocean, lord of rivers,
he saw a hermitage in a solitary, holy, pleasant forest region.
There he saw the rākṣasa named <s>Mārīca</s>, wearing a black antelope skin,
bearing matted hair and bark garments, and restrained in diet.

children.text: sa rāvaṇaḥ samāgamya vidhivat tena rakṣasā
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, having met properly with that rākṣasa,

children.text: tataḥ paścād idaṃ vākyam abravīd vākyakovidaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then afterward, skilled in speech, spoke these words:

children.text: mārīca śrūyatāṃ tāta vacanaṃ mama bhāṣataḥ
children.translated_text: “<s>Mārīca</s>, dear one, listen to the words I am speaking.

children.text: ārto 'smi mama cārtasya bhavān hi paramā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: I am afflicted, and for me in distress you are the highest refuge.

children.text: jānīṣe tvaṃ janasthānaṃ bhrātā yatra kharo mama
children.translated_text: You know <s>Janasthāna</s>, where my brother <s>Khara</s> lived,

children.text: dūṣaṇaś ca mahābāhuḥ svasā śūrpaṇakhā ca me ||
children.translated_text: as did mighty-armed <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> and my sister <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>,
and the very splendid rākṣasa <s>Triśiras</s>, eater of flesh,

children.text: anye ca bahavaḥ śūrā labdhalakṣā niśācarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and many other heroic night-roamers skilled in hitting their marks.
At my command those rākṣasas made their dwelling there,
harassing in the great forest the sages who follow <s>dharma</s>.
Fourteen thousand rākṣasas of dreadful deeds,
heroes skilled in hitting their marks and obedient to <s>Khara</s>’s will,

children.text: te tv idānīṃ janasthāne vasamānā mahābalāḥ
children.translated_text: those mighty ones, dwelling then in <s>Janasthāna</s>,

children.text: saṃgatāḥ param āyattā rāmeṇa saha saṃyuge ||
children.translated_text: came together, fully engaged, in battle with <s>Rāma</s>.
By that <s>Rāma</s>, whose anger had arisen, at the forefront of battle,

children.text: anuktvā paruṣaṃ kiṃcic charair vyāpāritaṃ dhanuḥ ||
children.translated_text: without his saying anything harsh, the bow was set to work with arrows.
Fourteen thousand rākṣasas of dreadful deeds
were slain with sharp arrows by a human being fighting on foot.

children.text: kharaś ca nihataḥ saṃkhye dūṣaṇaś ca nipātitaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Khara</s> was killed in the fight, and <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> was struck down;

children.text: hatvā triśirasaṃ cāpi nirbhayā daṇḍakāḥ kṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and after killing <s>Triśiras</s> too, he made the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest fearless.
Cast out by his angry father, with his wife, his life nearly spent,

children.text: sa hantā tasya sainyasya rāmaḥ kṣatriyapāṃsanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Rāma</s>, disgrace of kṣatriyas, is the killer of that army.
He is ill-conducted, harsh, sharp, foolish, greedy, and uncontrolled in his senses;

children.text: tyaktadharmas tv adharmātmā bhūtānām ahite rataḥ ||
children.translated_text: he has abandoned <s>dharma</s>, is unrighteous in soul, and delights in harming beings.

children.text: yena vairaṃ vināraṇye sattvam āśritya kevalam
children.translated_text: Without any enmity, in the forest, relying only on strength,
he disfigured my sister by cutting off her ears and nose.
His wife <s>Sītā</s>, like a daughter of the gods, from <s>Janasthāna</s>

children.text: ānayiṣyāmi vikramya sahāyas tatra me bhava ||
children.translated_text: I shall carry off by force; be my helper in that.

children.text: tvayā hy ahaṃ sahāyena pārśvasthena mahābala
children.translated_text: For with you as my helper, standing at my side, mighty one,

children.text: bhrātṛbhiś ca surān yuddhe samagrān nābhicintaye ||
children.translated_text: and with my brothers, I do not take account even of all the gods together in battle.

children.text: tat sahāyo bhava tvaṃ me samartho hy asi rākṣasa
children.translated_text: Therefore be my helper. You are capable, rākṣasa;

children.text: vīrye yuddhe ca darpe ca na hy asti sadṛśas tava ||
children.translated_text: in valor, in battle, and in pride, there is no one equal to you.
For this purpose I have come near you, night-roamer.

children.text: śṛṇu tat karma sāhāyye yat kāryaṃ vacanān mama ||
children.translated_text: Hear what deed must be done in assistance, at my command.

children.text: sauvarṇas tvaṃ mṛgo bhūtvā citro rajatabindubhiḥ
children.translated_text: Become a golden deer, variegated with silver spots,

children.text: āśrame tasya rāmasya sītāyāḥ pramukhe cara ||
children.translated_text: and move about in front of <s>Sītā</s> at <s>Rāma</s>’s hermitage.

children.text: tvāṃ tu niḥsaṃśayaṃ sītā dṛṣṭvā tu mṛgarūpiṇam
children.translated_text: Seeing you in the form of a deer, <s>Sītā</s> will certainly
say to her husband and to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, ‘Let it be caught.’

children.text: tatas tayor apāye tu śūnye sītāṃ yathāsukham
children.translated_text: Then, when those two are away and <s>Sītā</s> is alone, at my pleasure,
unhindered, I shall carry her off, like <s>Rāhu</s> carrying off the moon’s radiance.
Afterward, when <s>Rāma</s> is tormented by the taking of his wife,
I shall strike him confidently, my inner purpose accomplished.”
When the great-souled <s>Mārīca</s> heard this account of <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: śuṣkaṃ samabhavad vaktraṃ paritrasto babhūva ca ||
children.translated_text: His mouth became dry, and he grew terrified.
Knowing <s>Rāma</s>'s prowess in the great forest, he was frightened and despondent at heart before <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: kṛtāñjalis tattvam uvāca vākyaṃ hitaṃ ca tasmai hitam ātmanaś ca ||
children.translated_text: With joined palms he spoke a truthful speech, beneficial to him and beneficial to himself.
Hearing that speech of the lord of rākṣasas, he who was skilled in speech
the very wise <s>Mārīca</s> answered the lord of rākṣasas.
Men who always speak what is pleasing are easy to find, O king,

children.text: apriyasya ca pathyasya vaktā śrotā ca durlabhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but one who speaks what is unpleasant yet wholesome, and one who listens to it, are hard to find.

children.text: na nūnaṃ budhyase rāmaṃ mahāvīryaṃ guṇonnatam
children.translated_text: Surely you do not understand <s>Rāma</s>, mighty in valor and exalted in virtues,
because your agents are unfit and you are fickle, though he is like <s>Mahendra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>.

children.text: api svasti bhavet tāta sarveṣāṃ bhuvi rakṣasām
children.translated_text: May there yet be well-being, dear one, for all rākṣasas on earth;

children.text: api rāmo na saṃkruddhaḥ kuryāl lokam arākṣasam ||
children.translated_text: may <s>Rāma</s>, if angered, not make the world devoid of rākṣasas.
May the daughter of <s>Janaka</s> not have arisen for the end of your life;

children.text: api sītā nimittaṃ ca na bhaved vyasanaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: may <s>Sītā</s> not become the cause of a great calamity.

children.text: api tvām īśvaraṃ prāpya kāmavṛttaṃ niraṅkuśam
children.translated_text: May <s>Laṅkā</s>, having obtained you as its lord, self-willed and unrestrained,

children.text: na vinaśyet purī laṅkā tvayā saha sarākṣasā ||
children.translated_text: not perish together with you and all its rākṣasas.
For a king like you, ruled by desire, ill-conducted, and advised by evil counsel,

children.text: ātmānaṃ svajanaṃ rāṣṭraṃ sa rājā hanti durmatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: being foolish, destroys himself, his own people, and his realm.

children.text: na ca pitrā parityakto nāmaryādaḥ kathaṃcana
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> was not cast off by his father, nor is he in any way lawless;

children.text: na lubdho na ca duḥśīlo na ca kṣatriyapāṃsanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he is not greedy, not of bad conduct, and not a disgrace to the kṣatriyas.
The increaser of <s>Kausalyā</s>'s joy is not lacking in dharmic virtues,

children.text: na ca tīkṣṇo hi bhūtānāṃ sarveṣāṃ ca hite rataḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor is he harsh toward beings; he is devoted to the welfare of all.
Seeing his truth-speaking father deceived by <s>Kaikeyī</s>,
that righteous one went forth to the forest, thinking, 'I will fulfill it.'
For the sake of <s>Kaikeyī</s>'s desired favor and of his father <s>Daśaratha</s>,

children.text: hitvā rājyaṃ ca bhogāṃś ca praviṣṭo daṇḍakāvanam ||
children.translated_text: he abandoned kingdom and pleasures and entered the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest.

children.text: na rāmaḥ karkaśas tāta nāvidvān nājitendriyaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> is not cruel, dear one, nor ignorant, nor uncontrolled in his senses;

children.text: anṛtaṃ na śrutaṃ caiva naiva tvaṃ vaktum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: you ought not to speak what is false or contrary to what is known.
<s>Rāma</s> is <s>dharma</s> embodied, virtuous and true in his valor;

children.text: rājā sarvasya lokasya devānām iva vāsavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he is king of the whole world, like <s>Vāsava</s> among the gods.

children.text: kathaṃ tvaṃ tasya vaidehīṃ rakṣitāṃ svena tejasā
children.translated_text: How do you wish to carry off by force that <s>Vaidehī</s>, protected by his own splendor,

children.text: icchasi prasabhaṃ hartuṃ prabhām iva vivasvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: as if one would seize the radiance of the sun?
You should not rashly enter in battle the blazing fire that is <s>Rāma</s>, whose flames are arrows,

children.text: rāmāgniṃ sahasā dīptaṃ na praveṣṭuṃ tvam arhasi ||
children.translated_text: unassailable, whose fuel is bow and sword.
With his bow drawn like a blazing mouth, with arrows as flames, intolerant of insult,
that hero bears bow and arrows and carries off the armies of his enemies.

children.text: rājyaṃ sukhaṃ ca saṃtyajya jīvitaṃ ceṣṭam ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Having abandoned your kingdom, happiness, and even the life dear to yourself,
you should not here draw too near to <s>Rāma</s>, who will be your death, dear one.

children.text: aprameyaṃ hi tattejo yasya sā janakātmajā
children.translated_text: Immeasurable is the splendor of him whose wife is that daughter of <s>Janaka</s>;

children.text: na tvaṃ samarthas tāṃ hartuṃ rāmacāpāśrayāṃ vane ||
children.translated_text: you are not able to carry her off in the forest while she is sheltered by <s>Rāma</s>'s bow.
His wife, always faithful, is dearer to him than his very breaths;
slender-waisted <s>Sītā</s> is like the flame of a blazing fire.

children.text: kim udyamaṃ vyartham imaṃ kṛtvā te rākṣasādhipa
children.translated_text: Why undertake this fruitless effort, lord of rākṣasas?

children.text: dṛṣṭaś cet tvaṃ raṇe tena tadantaṃ tava jīvitam
children.translated_text: If you are seen by him in battle, that will be the end of your life;

children.text: jīvitaṃ ca sukhaṃ caiva rājyaṃ caiva sudurlabham ||
children.translated_text: life, happiness, and kingdom alike will be very hard to obtain again.
Therefore, together with all your ministers, with <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> at their head,

children.text: mantrayitvā tu dharmiṣṭhaiḥ kṛtvā niścayam ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: after consulting with the most righteous and making your own decision,

children.text: doṣāṇāṃ ca guṇānāṃ ca sampradhārya balābalam
children.translated_text: after weighing the strength and weakness of faults and virtues,

children.text: ātmanaś ca balaṃ jñātvā rāghavasya ca tattvataḥ
children.translated_text: and knowing truly both your own strength and that of <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: hitaṃ hi tava niścitya kṣamaṃ tvaṃ kartum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: you should determine what is beneficial for you and do what is proper.

children.text: ahaṃ tu manye tava na kṣamaṃ raṇe samāgamaṃ kosalarājasūnunā
children.translated_text: But I think it is not proper for you to meet in battle the son of the king of <s>Kosala</s>.

children.text: idaṃ hi bhūyaḥ śṛṇu vākyam uttamaṃ kṣamaṃ ca yuktaṃ ca niśācarādhipa ||
children.translated_text: Hear further this excellent speech, lord of night-wanderers, both proper and well-reasoned.

children.text: kadācid apy ahaṃ vīryāt paryaṭan pṛthivīm imām
children.translated_text: Once, roaming over this earth by my valor,
bearing the strength of a thousand elephants and resembling a mountain,
dark like a blue rain cloud and wearing earrings of heated gold,
creating fear for the world, crowned and armed with an iron club,
I wandered through the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest, eating the flesh of seers.
Then the righteous great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, terrified of me,

children.text: svayaṃ gatvā daśarathaṃ narendram idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: went himself to King <s>Daśaratha</s> and said this:

children.text: ayaṃ rakṣatu māṃ rāmaḥ parvakāle samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Let this <s>Rāma</s>, attentive at the time of the sacred observance, protect me;

children.text: mārīcān me bhayaṃ ghoraṃ samutpannaṃ nareśvara ||
children.translated_text: a terrible fear of <s>Mārīca</s> has arisen for me, lord of men.'

children.text: ity evam ukto dharmātmā rājā daśarathas tadā
children.translated_text: When he had been addressed in this way, righteous King <s>Daśaratha</s> then
answered the illustrious great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>:
'This <s>Rāghava</s> is not yet sixteen years old and has not mastered weapons;

children.text: kāmaṃ tu mama yat sainyaṃ mayā saha gamiṣyati
children.translated_text: rather, whatever army is mine will go with me,
and I shall kill your enemy as you wish, best of sages.'

children.text: ity evam uktaḥ sa munī rājānaṃ punar abravīt
children.translated_text: Spoken to in this way, that sage again addressed the king:

children.text: rāmān nānyad balaṃ loke paryāptaṃ tasya rakṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'No force in the world other than <s>Rāma</s> is sufficient for that rākṣasa.

children.text: bālo 'py eṣa mahātejāḥ samarthas tasya nigrahe
children.translated_text: Though he is a boy, he is of great splendor and able to subdue him;

children.text: gamiṣye rāmam ādāya svasti te 'stu paraṃtapa ||
children.translated_text: I shall go taking <s>Rāma</s>. May there be well-being for you, scorcher of foes.'

children.text: ity evam uktvā sa munis tam ādāya nṛpātmajam
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the sage took that prince
and, greatly delighted, <s>Viśvāmitra</s> went to his own hermitage.

children.text: taṃ tadā daṇḍakāraṇye yajñam uddiśya dīkṣitam
children.translated_text: Then, in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest, when he had been consecrated for the sacrifice,
<s>Rāma</s> stood there, making his bow resound wondrously.
The glorious one, not yet showing signs of manhood, a boy, dark-hued and fair-eyed,
wearing a single garment, armed with a bow, with a topknot and a golden garland;
making the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest shine with his own blazing splendor,
then <s>Rāma</s> appeared like the young moon risen.
Then I, resembling a rain cloud and wearing earrings of heated gold,
strong, granted boons, came in arrogance to that hermitage.
Seen by him, I entered suddenly, with weapon raised;

children.text: māṃ tu dṛṣṭvā dhanuḥ sajyam asambhrāntaś cakāra ha ||
children.translated_text: but when he saw me, he calmly strung his bow.

children.text: avajānann ahaṃ mohād bālo 'yam iti rāghavam
children.translated_text: Disregarding <s>Rāghava</s> through delusion, thinking, "This is a boy,"
I rushed hastily upon that altar of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>.

children.text: tena muktas tato bāṇaḥ śitaḥ śatrunibarhaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Then by him a sharp arrow, destroyer of enemies, was released;
struck by it, I was hurled a hundred yojanas into the ocean.
Cast away by the speed of <s>Rāma</s>'s arrow, my mind bewildered,
I was then thrown down by him into the deep waters of the sea.

children.text: prāpya saṃjñāṃ cirāt tāta laṅkāṃ prati gataḥ purīm ||
children.translated_text: Regaining consciousness after a long time, dear one, I went toward the city <s>Laṅkā</s>.

children.text: evam asmi tadā muktaḥ sahāyās te nipātitāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus at that time I was released, while your companions were struck down
by <s>Rāma</s>, a boy not yet practiced in weapons, but unwearied in action.

children.text: tan mayā vāryamāṇas tvaṃ yadi rāmeṇa vigraham
children.translated_text: Therefore, if, though I am restraining you, you make

children.text: kariṣyasy āpadaṃ ghorāṃ kṣipraṃ prāpya naśiṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: hostility with <s>Rāma</s>, you will quickly meet dreadful disaster and perish.
To those skilled in the arts of sport and pleasure, flourishing in assemblies and festivals,
you will bring only torment and ruin upon the rākṣasas.
Crowded with mansions and palaces, adorned with many kinds of jewels,

children.text: drakṣyasi tvaṃ purīṃ laṅkāṃ vinaṣṭāṃ maithilīkṛte ||
children.translated_text: you will see the city <s>Laṅkā</s> destroyed for the sake of <s>Maithilī</s>.
Even those who commit no sins, though pure, through association with sinners
perish by the sins of others, like fish in a serpent's lake.
With limbs anointed with divine sandal paste and adorned with divine ornaments,

children.text: drakṣyasy abhihatān bhūmau tava doṣāt tu rākṣasān ||
children.translated_text: you will see the rākṣasas struck down on the ground because of your fault.

children.text: hṛtadārān sadārāṃś ca daśa vidravato diśaḥ
children.translated_text: Their wives carried off, or fleeing with their wives into the ten directions,
you will see the night-wanderers, the survivors of slaughter, helpless and without refuge.
Surrounded by a net of arrows, enveloped in flames of fire,
you will undoubtedly see <s>Laṅkā</s> with its buildings burned.
Thousands of women are in your possession, O king;
be devoted to your own wives and protect your own family, O rākṣasa.

children.text: mānaṃ vṛddhiṃ ca rājyaṃ ca jīvitaṃ ceṣṭam ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: If you wish to enjoy for a long time honor, prosperity, kingdom,

children.text: yadīcchasi ciraṃ bhoktuṃ mā kṛthā rāmavipriyam ||
children.translated_text: and your own cherished life, do not do what is hostile to <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: nivāryamāṇaḥ suhṛdā mayā bhṛśaṃ prasahya sītāṃ yadi dharṣayiṣyasi
children.translated_text: If, though strongly restrained by me as a friend, you forcibly violate <s>Sītā</s>,
your strength exhausted, together with your kinsmen, your life seized by <s>Rāma</s>'s arrow, you will go to <s>Yama</s>'s abode.

children.text: evam asmi tadā muktaḥ kathaṃcit tena saṃyuge
children.translated_text: Thus at that time I somehow escaped him in battle;

children.text: idānīm api yad vṛttaṃ tac chṛṇuṣva yad uttaram ||
children.translated_text: now hear also what happened afterward.

children.text: rākṣasābhyām ahaṃ dvābhyām anirviṇṇas tathā kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: I, not yet disillusioned, together with two rākṣasas,
accompanied by those two in deer form, entered the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest.
Flaming-tongued, huge-bodied, sharp-horned, and very strong,
I roamed the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest as a great beast feeding on flesh.
At sacrificial fires, at sacred fords, and at sacred trees, O <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
I roamed in utter terror, assaulting those ascetics.
Having killed ascetics who lived by <s>dharma</s> in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest,

children.text: rudhirāṇi pibaṃs teṣāṃ tathā māṃsāni bhakṣayan ||
children.translated_text: drinking their blood and likewise eating their flesh,
cruel, feeding on the flesh of seers, terrifying the forest-dwellers,
then, maddened with blood, I roamed the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest.
Then, roaming in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest as a corrupter of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: āsādayaṃ tadā rāmaṃ tāpasaṃ dharmam āśritam ||
children.translated_text: I came upon <s>Rāma</s>, an ascetic devoted to <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: vaidehīṃ ca mahābhāgāṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahāratham
children.translated_text: and upon noble <s>Vaidehī</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the great chariot-warrior,
an ascetic of controlled diet, devoted to the welfare of all beings.
Then I, despising mighty <s>Rāma</s> who had gone to the forest,
thinking, "This is an ascetic," and remembering our former enmity,
rushed upon him in great anger, sharp-horned and deer-shaped,
wishing to kill him, foolish, remembering that earlier blow.

children.text: tena muktās trayo bāṇāḥ śitāḥ śatrunibarhaṇāḥ
children.translated_text: By him three sharp arrows, destroyers of enemies, were released
as he drew his powerful bow, arrows moving like <s>Suparṇa</s> and the wind.
Those arrows, thunderbolt-like, very terrible, drinking blood,
all three came together, with well-set shafts.
Knowing <s>Rāma</s>'s valor, cunning and already acquainted with fear,

children.text: samutkrāntas tato muktas tāv ubhau rākṣasau hatau ||
children.translated_text: I sprang away and so escaped; but those two rākṣasas were killed.

children.text: śareṇa mukto rāmasya kathaṃcit prāpya jīvitam
children.translated_text: Having somehow escaped <s>Rāma</s>'s arrow and gained my life,
I have been driven here into exile, disciplined, an ascetic, self-collected.
