On every tree I see <s>Rāma</s>, clothed in bark and black antelope skin,
holding a bow, like <s>Antaka</s> with a noose in his hand.
Terrified, I see even thousands of <s>Rāma</s>s, O <s>Rāvaṇa</s>;

children.text: rāmabhūtam idaṃ sarvam araṇyaṃ pratibhāti me ||
children.translated_text: this whole forest appears to me as having become <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: rāmam eva hi paśyāmi rahite rākṣaseśvara
children.translated_text: In empty places I see only <s>Rāma</s>, lord of rākṣasas;
when I see <s>Rāma</s> in a dream, I start up, senseless.
For me, terror-stricken by <s>Rāma</s>, O <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, names beginning with the syllable ra

children.text: ratnāni ca rathāś caiva trāsaṃ saṃjanayanti me ||
children.translated_text: and even jewels and chariots give rise to fear.

children.text: ahaṃ tasya prabhāvajño na yuddhaṃ tena te kṣamam
children.translated_text: I know his power; battle with him is not fitting for you.

children.text: raṇe rāmeṇa yudhyasva kṣamāṃ vā kuru rākṣasa
children.translated_text: Fight with <s>Rāma</s> in battle, or else practice forbearance, O rākṣasa;

children.text: na te rāmakathā kāryā yadi māṃ draṣṭum icchasi ||
children.translated_text: you should not speak of <s>Rāma</s> to me if you wish to see me.

children.text: idaṃ vaco bandhuhitārthinā mayā yathocyamānaṃ yadi nābhipatsyase
children.translated_text: If you do not accept this speech, spoken by me as a kinsman seeking your welfare,

children.text: sabāndhavas tyakṣyasi jīvitaṃ raṇe hato 'dya rāmeṇa śarair ajihmagaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Together with your kinsmen you will abandon your life in battle, struck down today by <s>Rāma</s> with straight-flying arrows.

children.text: mārīcena tu tad vākyaṃ kṣamaṃ yuktaṃ ca rāvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Rāvaṇa</s> did not accept that speech of <s>Mārīca</s>,
though it was proper and reasonable, just as a man wishing to die does not accept medicine.
Then the lord of rākṣasas, driven on by fate,
spoke a harsh and improper word to <s>Mārīca</s>, who was speaking what was salutary and beneficial.

children.text: yat kilaitad ayuktārthaṃ mārīca mayi kathyate
children.translated_text: 'This speech that is being addressed to me, <s>Mārīca</s>, is indeed pointless,

children.text: vākyaṃ niṣphalam atyarthaṃ bījam uptam ivoṣare ||
children.translated_text: a wholly fruitless utterance, like seed sown on barren ground.

children.text: tvadvākyair na tu māṃ śakyaṃ bhettuṃ rāmasya saṃyuge
children.translated_text: By your words I cannot be turned away from battle with <s>Rāma</s>,
especially with that evil-natured, foolish human being.

children.text: yas tyaktvā suhṛdo rājyaṃ mātaraṃ pitaraṃ tathā
children.translated_text: He abandoned his friends, his kingdom, his mother,

children.text: strīvākyaṃ prākṛtaṃ śrutvā vanam ekapade gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and his father too, and, hearing the common words of a woman, went at once to the forest.

children.text: avaśyaṃ tu mayā tasya saṃyuge kharaghātinaḥ
children.translated_text: In battle I must by all means carry off <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: prāṇaiḥ priyatarā sītā hartavyā tava saṃnidhau ||
children.translated_text: dearer to him than life, the slayer of <s>Khara</s>, in your presence.

children.text: evaṃ me niścitā buddhir hṛdi mārīca vartate
children.translated_text: Such is my settled thought, <s>Mārīca</s>, remaining in my heart;

children.text: na vyāvartayituṃ śakyā sendrair api surāsuraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: it cannot be turned back even by the gods and asuras together with <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: doṣaṃ guṇaṃ vā saṃpṛṣṭas tvam evaṃ vaktum arhasi
children.translated_text: When asked, you may speak in this way about fault or merit,

children.text: apāyaṃ vāpy upāyaṃ vā kāryasyāsya viniścaye ||
children.translated_text: or about danger or means, in deciding this undertaking.
But when a wise minister is consulted,

children.text: udyatāñjalinā rājño ya icched bhūtim ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: if he desires prosperity for himself, he should speak to the king with folded hands raised.

children.text: vākyam apratikūlaṃ tu mṛdupūrvaṃ śubhaṃ hitam
children.translated_text: A king, lord of the earth, should be addressed with words not contrary to him,
gentle at the outset, auspicious, beneficial, and joined with courtesy.

children.text: sāvamardaṃ tu yad vākyaṃ mārīca hitam ucyate
children.translated_text: But a king worthy of honor does not welcome speech that is contemptuous,
even if it is called beneficial, <s>Mārīca</s>, when it is devoid of respect.
Kings of immeasurable might bear five forms:

children.text: agner indrasya somasya yamasya varuṇasya ca
children.translated_text: those of Agni, <s>Indra</s>, Soma, Yama, and Varuṇa,

children.text: auṣṇyaṃ tathā vikramaṃ ca saumyaṃ daṇḍaṃ prasannatām ||
children.translated_text: heat, valor, gentleness, punishment, and graciousness.

children.text: tasmāt sarvāsv avasthāsu mānyāḥ pūjyāś ca pārthivāḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore in all circumstances earthly rulers are to be honored and worshiped;

children.text: tvaṃ tu dharmam avijñāya kevalaṃ moham āsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but you, not understanding <s>dharma</s> (right order), have taken refuge only in delusion.
Out of wickedness you speak such harsh words to me when I have come to you.

children.text: guṇadoṣau na pṛcchāmi kṣamaṃ cātmani rākṣasa
children.translated_text: I am not asking about merits and faults, rākṣasa, nor about what is suitable for myself;

children.text: asmiṃs tu sa bhavān kṛtye sāhāyyaṃ kartum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: rather, in this task you ought to render assistance.

children.text: sauvarṇas tvaṃ mṛgo bhūtvā citro rajatabindubhiḥ
children.translated_text: Becoming a golden deer, variegated with spots of silver,
you may entice <s>Vaidehī</s> and then go wherever you wish.

children.text: tvāṃ tu māyāmṛgaṃ dṛṣṭvā kāñcanaṃ jātavismayā
children.translated_text: Seeing you as an illusory deer, golden and marvelous,

children.text: ānayainam iti kṣipraṃ rāmaṃ vakṣyati maithilī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Maithilī</s>, filled with wonder, will quickly say to <s>Rāma</s>, "Bring it here."

children.text: apakrānte ca kākutsthe lakṣmaṇe ca yathāsukham
children.translated_text: When <s>Kākutstha</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> have gone away,
I shall bring <s>Vaidehī</s> at ease, as the thousand-eyed one brought <s>Śacī</s>.

children.text: evaṃ kṛtvā tv idaṃ kāryaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ gaccha rākṣasa
children.translated_text: Having done this task, go wherever you wish, rākṣasa;
I shall give you half of my kingdom, <s>Mārīca</s>, good vowed one.

children.text: gaccha saumya śivaṃ mārgaṃ kāryasyāsya vivṛddhaye
children.translated_text: Go, gentle one, on an auspicious path for the success of this undertaking.

children.text: prāpya sītām ayuddhena vañcayitvā tu rāghavam
children.translated_text: Having obtained <s>Sītā</s> without battle and having deceived <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: laṅkāṃ prati gamiṣyāmi kṛtakāryaḥ saha tvayā ||
children.translated_text: I shall go back to <s>Laṅkā</s>, my purpose accomplished, together with you.

children.text: etat kāryam avaśyaṃ me balād api kariṣyasi
children.translated_text: You must do this task of mine, even by force.

children.text: rājño hi pratikūlastho na jātu sukham edhate ||
children.translated_text: For one who stands opposed to a king never prospers happily.

children.text: āsādya taṃ jīvitasaṃśayas te mṛtyur dhruvo hy adya mayā virudhya
children.translated_text: If you encounter him, your life is in doubt; but by opposing me, death today is certain.

children.text: etad yathāvat parigṛhya buddhyā yad atra pathyaṃ kuru tat tathā tvam ||
children.translated_text: Taking this properly into your understanding, do exactly what is salutary here.'
Ordered with words befitting a king, though they were hostile,
the night-roaming <s>Mārīca</s> spoke harsh words to the lord of rākṣasas:
'By what evil-doer was this destruction taught to you,
night-roamer, destruction for you together with your sons, kingdom, and ministers?

children.text: kas tvayā sukhinā rājan nābhinandati pāpakṛt
children.translated_text: What wicked man, when you were happy, did not rejoice in you, O king?
By whom was this doorway to death presented to you as a means?
Plainly your enemies, weak in valor, night-roamer,
wish you to be destroyed, hemmed in by one stronger than you.
By what low man, speaking what is harmful, was this advised to you,

children.text: yas tvām icchati naśyantaṃ svakṛtena niśācara ||
children.translated_text: one who wishes you to perish by your own act, night-roamer?

children.text: vadhyāḥ khalu na hanyante sacivās tava rāvaṇa
children.translated_text: Surely your ministers, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, deserve death, though they are not killed,

children.text: ye tvām utpatham ārūḍhaṃ na nigṛhṇanti sarvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for they do not restrain you in every way when you have mounted a wrong path.

children.text: amātyaiḥ kāmavṛtto hi rājā kāpatham āśritaḥ
children.translated_text: For a king ruled by desire, having taken to a bad road,

children.text: nigrāhyaḥ sarvathā sadbhir na nigrāhyo nigṛhyase ||
children.translated_text: must by all means be restrained by good ministers; though you should be restrained, you are not restrained.

children.text: dharmam arthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca yaśaś ca jayatāṃ vara
children.translated_text: Ministers, O best of conquerors, obtain <s>dharma</s> (right order), <s>artha</s> (advantage), <s>kāma</s> (desire),
and fame too, night-roamer, through the favor of their lord.

children.text: viparyaye tu tat sarvaṃ vyarthaṃ bhavati rāvaṇa
children.translated_text: But when the reverse occurs, all that becomes futile, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>;
other people meet calamity because of the defects of their lord.

children.text: rājamūlo hi dharmaś ca jayaś ca jayatāṃ vara
children.translated_text: For <s>dharma</s> (right order) and victory are rooted in the king, O best of conquerors;
therefore in all circumstances the ruler of men must be protected.

children.text: rājyaṃ pālayituṃ śakyaṃ na tīkṣṇena niśācara
children.translated_text: A kingdom cannot be protected by one who is harsh, night-roamer,
nor by one who is contrary, nor by one without discipline, rākṣasa.

children.text: ye tīkṣṇamantrāḥ sacivā bhajyante saha tena vai
children.translated_text: Ministers whose counsel is harsh are broken together with such a king,
just as chariots with poor charioteers quickly break on uneven ground.
Many good men in the world, established in fitting <s>dharma</s> (conduct),
have perished with their retinues through the offense of others.
Subjects protected by a lord who is contrary and harsh, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: rakṣyamāṇā na vardhante meṣā gomāyunā yathā ||
children.translated_text: do not prosper, like sheep guarded by a jackal.'
Inevitably, O <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, all the rākṣasas will perish,

children.text: yeṣāṃ tvaṃ karkaśo rājā durbuddhir ajitendriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: those for whom you are the harsh king, evil-minded and with unconquered senses.

children.text: tad idaṃ kākatālīyaṃ ghoram āsāditaṃ tvayā
children.translated_text: This terrible thing, like the chance fall of a crow and a palm fruit, has been encountered by you;

children.text: atra kiṃ śobhanaṃ yat tvaṃ sasainyo vinaśiṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: what good is there in this, that you will perish together with your army?

children.text: māṃ nihatya tu rāmo 'sau nacirāt tvāṃ vadhiṣyati
children.translated_text: But after killing me, that <s>Rāma</s> will soon kill you;

children.text: anena kṛtakṛtyo 'smi mriye yad ariṇā hataḥ ||
children.translated_text: by this I shall have fulfilled my purpose, since I die struck down by an enemy.

children.text: darśanād eva rāmasya hataṃ mām upadhāraya
children.translated_text: From the mere sight of <s>Rāma</s>, consider me already killed,

children.text: ātmānaṃ ca hataṃ viddhi hṛtvā sītāṃ sabāndhavam ||
children.translated_text: and know yourself too, with your kinsmen, to be killed, since you have carried off <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: ānayiṣyāmi cet sītām āśramāt sahito mayā
children.translated_text: If I bring <s>Sītā</s> from the hermitage, together with you,

children.text: naiva tvam asi naivāhaṃ naiva laṅkā na rākṣasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: then there will be neither you nor I, neither <s>Laṅkā</s> nor the rākṣasas.

children.text: nivāryamāṇas tu mayā hitaiṣiṇā na mṛṣyase vākyam idaṃ niśācara
children.translated_text: Though I, wishing your welfare, try to restrain you, you do not tolerate this speech, O night-wanderer.

children.text: paretakalpā hi gatāyuṣo narā hitaṃ na gṛhṇanti suhṛdbhir īritam ||
children.translated_text: For men who are as good as dead and whose lifespan is spent do not accept salutary advice spoken by friends.

children.text: evam uktvā tu paruṣaṃ mārīco rāvaṇaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken harshly to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
wretched <s>Mārīca</s> then said, 'Let us go,' out of fear of the lord of night-roamers.
And once I am again seen by him who bears arrows, bow, and sword,
with his weapon raised to kill me, my life is destroyed.

children.text: kiṃ tu kartuṃ mayā śakyam evaṃ tvayi durātmani
children.translated_text: But what can I do, since you, wicked-souled one, are set on this?

children.text: eṣa gacchāmy ahaṃ tāta svasti te 'stu niśācara ||
children.translated_text: So I go, dear one; may there be well-being for you, O night-wanderer.

children.text: prahṛṣṭas tv abhavat tena vacanena sa rākṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: The rākṣasa became delighted at that statement,
and, embracing him in a tight clasp, spoke these words:

children.text: etac chauṇḍīryayuktaṃ te macchandād iva bhāṣitam
children.translated_text: This speech of yours is endowed with boldness, as if spoken according to my wish;

children.text: idānīm asi mārīcaḥ pūrvam anyo niśācaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: now you are <s>Mārīca</s>; before, O night-wanderer, you were someone else.
Mount quickly this sky-going chariot, adorned with jewels,

children.text: mayā saha ratho yuktaḥ piśācavadanaiḥ kharaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: yoked for me with donkeys that have the faces of piśācas.

children.text: tato rāvaṇamārīcau vimānam iva taṃ ratham
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and <s>Mārīca</s> mounted that chariot, like an aerial car,
and quickly departed from that region of hermitages.

children.text: tathaiva tatra paśyantau pattanāni vanāni ca
children.translated_text: There, as they went, they saw towns and forests,

children.text: girīṃś ca saritaḥ sarvā rāṣṭrāṇi nagarāṇi ca ||
children.translated_text: and mountains, all the rivers, kingdoms, and cities.
Having reached the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest, then the lord of rākṣasas, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
together with <s>Mārīca</s>, saw the hermitage of <s>Rāghava</s>.
Then, descending from that gold-adorned chariot,

children.text: haste gṛhītvā mārīcaṃ rāvaṇo vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s> took <s>Mārīca</s> by the hand and spoke these words:
This is seen to be <s>Rāma</s>'s hermitage site, surrounded by plantains;

children.text: kriyatāṃ tat sakhe śīghraṃ yadarthaṃ vayam āgatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: quickly do that, my friend, for the sake of which we have come.

children.text: sa rāvaṇavacaḥ śrutvā mārīco rākṣasas tadā
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s words, the rākṣasa <s>Mārīca</s> then
became a deer and wandered at the entrance of <s>Rāma</s>'s hermitage.
The tips of his horns were excellent gems, and the form of his face was white and black;
his face was like a red lotus and blue lotus, and his ears were blue lotuses like sapphires.
His neck was slightly raised, his belly like a sapphire,
his flanks like madhūka flowers, and he resembled the filaments of a lotus.
His hooves shone like cat's-eye gems, his legs were slender, and he was compactly formed;
he was resplendent above with a tail colored like a rainbow.
Charming and glossy in color, covered with many kinds of jewels,
in an instant the rākṣasa had become a supremely beautiful deer.

children.text: vanaṃ prajvalayan ramyaṃ rāmāśramapadaṃ ca tat
children.translated_text: The rākṣasa, lighting up the lovely forest and that hermitage site of <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: manoharaṃ darśanīyaṃ rūpaṃ kṛtvā sa rākṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: having made a form lovely and beautiful to behold,
variegated with many minerals, for the purpose of tempting <s>Vaidehī</s>,
wandered about, going properly through the grassy places all around.
Having become variegated with hundreds of silvery spots and pleasing to see,
he wandered, breaking and eating the shoots of the trees.
Going to the plantain grove and then here and there to the karṇikāra trees,
moving slowly, he lingered there for the sight of <s>Sītā</s>.
That great deer, whose back was marked like lotuses, shone forth;
near <s>Rāma</s>'s hermitage he wandered at will.

children.text: punar gatvā nivṛttaś ca vicacāra mṛgottamaḥ
children.translated_text: Going again and turning back, that best of deer roamed about;
after going for a moment in haste, he would turn back again.

children.text: vikrīḍaṃś ca punar bhūmau punar eva niṣīdati
children.translated_text: Playing again on the ground, he would sit down again;
having come to the entrance of the hermitage, he would go toward the herds of deer.
Followed by the herds of deer, he would again turn back,
the rākṣasa who had assumed deerhood, desiring the sight of <s>Sītā</s>.
He wandered around, bounding in varied circles,

children.text: samudvīkṣya ca sarve taṃ mṛgā ye 'nye vanecarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and all the other forest-roaming deer, having looked closely at him,
approached, sniffed him, and fled in the ten directions.

children.text: rākṣasaḥ so 'pi tān vanyān mṛgān mṛgavadhe rataḥ ||
children.translated_text: That rākṣasa too, though intent on killing deer,
did not eat those wild deer when he touched them, in order to conceal his true nature.

children.text: tasminn eva tataḥ kāle vaidehī śubhalocanā ||
children.translated_text: Then at that very time fair-eyed <s>Vaidehī</s>,
busy gathering flowers, passed among the trees.

children.text: karṇikārān aśokāṃś ca cūtāṃś ca madirekṣaṇā ||
children.translated_text: The wine-eyed lady, gathering flowers, wandered among karṇikāras, aśokas, and mango trees,
plucking blossoms, she of lovely face.
She, the supreme woman, unfit for dwelling in the forest, saw that jewel-made deer,
its limbs variegated with pearls and gems.
With eyes wide open in wonder, she looked affectionately
at him, whose teeth and lips were beautiful, and whose body-hair was of silvery mineral hue.

children.text: sa ca tāṃ rāmadayitāṃ paśyan māyāmayo mṛgaḥ
children.translated_text: And that illusory deer, seeing <s>Rāma</s>'s beloved,

children.text: vicacāra tatas tatra dīpayann iva tad vanam ||
children.translated_text: wandered there then, as if setting that forest ablaze.
Seeing that deer, never seen before and made of many jewels,
<s>Sītā</s>, daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, fell into the highest wonder.

children.text: sā taṃ samprekṣya suśroṇī kusumāni vicinvatī
children.translated_text: As she was gathering flowers, the fair-hipped lady saw that deer,
adorned on its two flanks with the colors of gold and silver.
Delighted, faultless-limbed, and shining like polished gold,

children.text: bhartāram api cākrandal lakṣmaṇaṃ caiva sāyudham ||
children.translated_text: she cried out to her husband and also to armed <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Called by <s>Vaidehī</s>, those two tigers among men, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: vīkṣamāṇau tu taṃ deśaṃ tadā dadṛśatur mṛgam ||
children.translated_text: looked about that place and then saw the deer.

children.text: śaṅkamānas tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇo rāmam abravīt
children.translated_text: But <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, seeing it and becoming suspicious, said to <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: tam evainam ahaṃ manye mārīcaṃ rākṣasaṃ mṛgam ||
children.translated_text: "I think this very deer is the rākṣasa <s>Mārīca</s>.
While kings were roaming joyfully on the hunt in the forest,
they were killed by this evil shape-shifter through deceit, <s>Rāma</s>.
This form of a magical deer has been made by him, a knower of magic,
O radiant tiger among men, resembling a city of the gandharvas.

children.text: mṛgo hy evaṃvidho ratnavicitro nāsti rāghava
children.translated_text: For no deer of such a kind, variegated with jewels, exists, O <s>Rāghava</s>;

children.text: jagatyāṃ jagatīnātha māyaiṣā hi na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in the world, lord of the world, this is magic; there is no doubt."
Checking <s>Kākutstha</s> as he was speaking in this way, the pure-smiling lady
spoke, delighted, her mind carried away by the disguise:
"Noble prince, that lovely deer steals my heart.
Bring it here, mighty-armed one; it will be for our sport.
Here in the precinct of our hermitage many animals pleasant to behold

children.text: mṛgāś caranti sahitāś camarāḥ sṛmarās tathā ||
children.translated_text: move about together: camarā deer and sṛmaras too,

children.text: ṛkṣāḥ pṛṣatasaṃghāś ca vānarāḥ kiṃnarās tathā
children.translated_text: bears, herds of spotted deer, monkeys, and kinnaras as well;
they wander here, mighty-armed one, excellent in form and very strong.

children.text: na cāsya sadṛśo rājan dṛṣṭapūrvo mṛgaḥ purā
children.translated_text: But no deer like this, king, has ever been seen before,
in splendor, grace, and radiance, as this best of deer is.
With limbs variegated in many colors and covered with jewel-like spots,
it lights up the undisturbed forest and shines like the moon.

children.text: aho rūpam aho lakṣmīḥ svarasampac ca śobhanā
children.translated_text: Ah, its beauty! Ah, its grace! And its excellent voice is lovely.
This wondrous, many-colored deer seems to steal my heart.

children.text: yadi grahaṇam abhyeti jīvann eva mṛgas tava
children.translated_text: If this deer can be taken alive by you,
it will be a marvel and will produce amazement.
When our forest exile is finished and we are again established in the kingdom,
this deer will serve to adorn the inner palace.
For <s>Bharata</s>, noble prince, for my mothers-in-law, and for me, lord,
this divine deer-form will produce amazement.

children.text: jīvan na yadi te 'bhyeti grahaṇaṃ mṛgasattamaḥ
children.translated_text: If this best of deer cannot be taken alive by you,
then its beautiful hide will be mine, tiger among men.
On the gold-like skin of this creature when it has been killed,
spread over a prepared grass-seat, I wish to sit.

children.text: kāmavṛttam idaṃ raudraṃ strīṇām asadṛśaṃ matam
children.translated_text: This desire-driven impulse is thought harsh and unlike women,

children.text: vapuṣā tv asya sattvasya vismayo janito mama ||
children.translated_text: yet wonder has been stirred in me by the body of this creature."
And by that golden-haired deer, with horns like choice jewels,
colored like the young sun and shining like the path of the stars,
even <s>Rāghava</s>'s mind was filled with wonder.

children.text: evaṃ sītāvacaḥ śrutvā dṛṣṭvā ca mṛgam adbhutam
children.translated_text: Having heard <s>Sītā</s>'s words and seen the wondrous deer,

children.text: uvāca rāghavo hṛṣṭo bhrātaraṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the delighted <s>Rāghava</s> spoke these words to his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:

children.text: paśya lakṣmaṇa vaidehyāḥ spṛhāṃ mṛgagatām imām
children.translated_text: "Look, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, at this longing of <s>Vaidehī</s> directed toward the deer.

children.text: rūpaśreṣṭhatayā hy eṣa mṛgo 'dya na bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Because of its supreme beauty, no deer like this will be found today.
Not in the region of <s>Nandana</s>, nor in the resort of <s>Caitraratha</s>,

children.text: kutaḥ pṛthivyāṃ saumitre yo 'sya kaścit samo mṛgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: much less on earth, son of <s>Sumitrā</s>, is there any deer equal to this one.
The lovely rows of its hair, both against and with the grain,
shine on the deer's body, variegated with golden spots.
Look at its tongue, blazing like a flame of fire,

children.text: jihvāṃ mukhān niḥsarantīṃ meghād iva śatahradām ||
children.translated_text: coming out from its mouth like lightning from a cloud as it yawns.
Its face is like masāra and galvarka stones; its belly is like conch shell and pearls.

children.text: kasya nāmābhirūpo 'sau na mano lobhayen mṛgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whose mind would that handsome deer not entice?
Seeing this form, radiant like refined gold,

children.text: nānāratnamayaṃ divyaṃ na mano vismayaṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: divine and made of many jewels, whose mind would not fall into wonder?

children.text: māṃsahetor api mṛgān vihārārthaṃ ca dhanvinaḥ
children.translated_text: For the sake of meat and also for sport, kings armed with bows
kill deer, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, while hunting in the great forest.
Riches are sought out by exertion in the great forest,
and various ores too, jewels, gems, and gold.

children.text: tat sāram akhilaṃ nṝṇāṃ dhanaṃ nicayavardhanam
children.translated_text: That entire essence is men's wealth, increasing their stores;

children.text: manasā cintitaṃ sarvaṃ yathā śukrasya lakṣmaṇa ||
children.translated_text: all that is conceived in the mind is such wealth, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, as it was for <s>Śukra</s>.
The purpose for which a man seeking gain sets out without hesitation,

children.text: tam artham arthaśāstrajñaḥ prāhur arthyāś ca lakṣmaṇa ||
children.translated_text: that purpose the knowers of <s>arthaśāstra</s> and seekers of gain call <s>artha</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
On the very costly golden hide of this jewel among deer,
slender-waisted <s>Vaidehī</s> will sit together with me.

children.text: na kādalī na priyakī na praveṇī na cāvikī
children.translated_text: Neither kādalī, nor priyakī, nor praveṇī, nor woolen cloth

children.text: bhaved etasya sadṛśī sparśaneneti me matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: would be equal to this in touch; so I think.

children.text: eṣa caiva mṛgaḥ śrīmān yaś ca divyo nabhaścaraḥ
children.translated_text: This splendid deer, and that divine one that moves in the sky,
these two are both divine deer, the star-deer and the earth-deer.

children.text: yadi vāyaṃ tathā yan māṃ bhaved vadasi lakṣmaṇa
children.translated_text: Or if this is as you say to me, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
if this is the magic of a rākṣasa, then it must be killed by me.
For by this cruel and uncontrolled <s>Mārīca</s>,
while he formerly wandered in the forest, eminent sages were harmed.
Many lords of men too, rising up for the hunt,

children.text: nihatāḥ parameṣvāsās tasmād vadhyas tv ayaṃ mṛgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: great archers, were killed by him; therefore this deer deserves to be killed.
In former times here <s>Vātāpi</s>, having insulted ascetics,
While in the belly he kills the twice-born, like its own embryo a mule-mare.

children.text: sa kadācic cirāl loke āsasāda mahāmunim
children.translated_text: Once, after a long time in the world, he encountered a great sage,

children.text: agastyaṃ tejasā yuktaṃ bhakṣyas tasya babhūva ha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Agastya</s>, endowed with splendor, and he became food for him.

children.text: samutthāne ca tadrūpaṃ kartukāmaṃ samīkṣya tam
children.translated_text: Seeing him, when he rose up, wishing to assume that same form,

children.text: utsmayitvā tu bhagavān vātāpim idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: the blessed one smiled and said this to <s>Vātāpi</s>:
'Because you, <s>Vātāpi</s>, disregarded and overpowered through your splendor

children.text: jīvaloke dvijaśreṣṭhās tasmād asi jarāṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the best of the twice-born in the living world, therefore you have gone to digestion.'

children.text: evaṃ tan na bhaved rakṣo vātāpir iva lakṣmaṇa
children.translated_text: So that must not happen, rākṣasa, like <s>Vātāpi</s>, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
to one who would despise a man like me, steadfast in <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) and self-controlled.
This one would be slain, as <s>Vātāpi</s> was by <s>Agastya</s>, if he came against me.

children.text: iha tvaṃ bhava saṃnaddho yantrito rakṣa maithilīm ||
children.translated_text: Remain here armed and restrained; guard <s>Maithilī</s>.

children.text: asyām āyattam asmākaṃ yat kṛtyaṃ raghunandana
children.translated_text: On her depends whatever task is ours, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>.

children.text: aham enaṃ vadhiṣyāmi grahīṣyāmy athavā mṛgam ||
children.translated_text: I shall either kill this deer or capture it.

children.text: yāvad gacchāmi saumitre mṛgam ānayituṃ drutam
children.translated_text: While I go quickly, O <s>Saumitri</s>, to bring back the deer,
watch <s>Vaidehī</s>, who has become eager for the deer's skin.

children.text: tvacā pradhānayā hy eṣa mṛgo 'dya na bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: For today this deer, with its excellent hide, will cease to be.
You must be vigilant in the hermitage with <s>Sītā</s>

children.text: yāvat pṛṣatam ekena sāyakena nihanmy aham
children.translated_text: until I kill the spotted deer with a single arrow.

children.text: hatvaitac carma ādāya śīghram eṣyāmi lakṣmaṇa ||
children.translated_text: Having killed it and taken its hide, I shall return quickly, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: pradakṣiṇenātibalena pakṣiṇā jaṭāyuṣā buddhimatā ca lakṣmaṇa
children.translated_text: With the exceedingly strong bird <s>Jatāyus</s>, who is wise and moves auspiciously around us, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: bhavāpramattaḥ pratigṛhya maithilīṃ pratikṣaṇaṃ sarvata eva śaṅkitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: be alert, taking charge of <s>Maithilī</s>, suspicious at every moment on every side.

children.text: tathā tu taṃ samādiśya bhrātaraṃ raghunandanaḥ
children.translated_text: Having instructed his brother in that way, the delight of the <s>Raghus</s>,
the greatly splendid one fastened on his sword, whose hilt was made of refined gold.
Then, taking up the thrice-bent bow that adorned him,
and binding on two quivers, he set out with exalted valor.

children.text: taṃ vañcayāno rājendram āpatantaṃ nirīkṣya vai
children.translated_text: Seeing the king rushing toward him, the deer deceived him:
out of fear it vanished, and then it appeared again in sight.

children.text: baddhāsir dhanur ādāya pradudrāva yato mṛgaḥ
children.translated_text: With his sword fastened on and bow in hand, he ran toward the place where the deer was.

children.text: taṃ sa paśyati rūpeṇa dyotamānam ivāgrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: He saw it before him, shining in its form.
The bow-handed hero kept watching and watching as it ran through the great forest,
sometimes luring him on after it had passed beyond the fall of an arrow.
It was wary, bewildered, seeming to leap into the sky,
now visible and now invisible in certain new places.
Like the disk of the autumn moon veiled by broken clouds,

children.text: muhūrtād eva dadṛśe muhur dūrāt prakāśate ||
children.translated_text: it was seen in a moment, and again it shone from afar.
By appearing and disappearing in just this way, it drew <s>Rāghava</s> away.

children.text: āsīt kruddhas tu kākutstho vivaśas tena mohitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kākutstha</s> grew angry, helpless and deluded by it.
Then, very weary, it stopped, taking shelter in the shade on a grassy spot,
and was seen not far away, surrounded by wild deer.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā rāmo mahātejās taṃ hantuṃ kṛtaniścayaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing it, the greatly splendid <s>Rāma</s>, resolved to kill it,

children.text: saṃdhāya sudṛḍhe cāpe vikṛṣya balavad balī ||
children.translated_text: set an arrow on his firm bow and forcefully drew it back, strong as he was.

children.text: tam eva mṛgam uddiśya jvalantam iva pannagam
children.translated_text: Aiming at that very deer, he released a blazing, shining missile,
like a flaming serpent, a weapon fashioned by <s>Brahmā</s>.
That best of arrows, like a thunderbolt, pierced violently through
the heart of <s>Mārīca</s>, who had the form of a deer.
Then, leaping up the height of a palm tree, he fell, tormented by the arrow,
and, with little life left, uttered a terrifying cry on the ground.

children.text: mriyamāṇas tu mārīco jahau tāṃ kṛtrimāṃ tanum ||
children.translated_text: As he was dying, <s>Mārīca</s> abandoned that artificial body.

children.text: samprāptakālam ājñāya cakāra ca tataḥ svaram
children.translated_text: Knowing that the proper time had come, he then produced a voice

children.text: sadṛśaṃ rāghavasyaiva hā sīte lakṣmaṇeti ca ||
children.translated_text: exactly like <s>Rāghava</s>'s own: 'Ah, <s>Sītā</s>! <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>!'
Pierced in a vital spot by that incomparable arrow,

children.text: mṛgarūpaṃ tu tat tyaktvā rākṣasaṃ rūpam ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: he cast off the deer form and assumed his own rākṣasa form.

children.text: cakre sa sumahākāyo mārīco jīvitaṃ tyajan ||
children.translated_text: Thus huge-bodied <s>Mārīca</s> did so while abandoning his life.
Then, wearing varied armlets and adorned with every ornament,
garlanded with gold and having great fangs, he became a rākṣasa struck by an arrow.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā patitaṃ bhūmau rākṣasaṃ ghoradarśanam
children.translated_text: Seeing that terrifying-looking rākṣasa fallen on the ground,

children.text: jagāma manasā sītāṃ lakṣmaṇasya vacaḥ smaran ||
children.translated_text: he turned in his mind to <s>Sītā</s>, remembering <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s words.

children.text: hā sīte lakṣmaṇety evam ākruśya tu mahāsvaram
children.translated_text: 'This rākṣasa has died after crying loudly,

children.text: mamāra rākṣasaḥ so 'yaṃ śrutvā sītā kathaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: "Ah, <s>Sītā</s>! <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>!" How will <s>Sītā</s> be when she hears it?

children.text: lakṣmaṇaś ca mahābāhuḥ kām avasthāṃ gamiṣyati
children.translated_text: And to what condition will mighty-armed <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> come?'
Thinking thus, righteous <s>Rāma</s>'s body hair stood on end.

children.text: tatra rāmaṃ bhayaṃ tīvram āviveśa viṣādajam
children.translated_text: There an intense fear born of despondency entered <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: rākṣasaṃ mṛgarūpaṃ taṃ hatvā śrutvā ca tatsvaram ||
children.translated_text: after he had killed that rākṣasa in deer form and heard that voice.

children.text: nihatya pṛṣataṃ cānyaṃ māṃsam ādāya rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāghava</s>, having killed another spotted deer and taken its flesh,
hurried at that time toward <s>Janasthāna</s>.

children.text: ārtasvaraṃ tu taṃ bhartur vijñāya sadṛśaṃ vane
children.translated_text: But in the forest <s>Sītā</s> recognized that distressed cry as like her husband's voice,

children.text: uvāca lakṣmaṇaṃ sītā gaccha jānīhi rāghavam ||
children.translated_text: and said to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, 'Go; find out about <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: na hi me jīvitaṃ sthāne hṛdayaṃ vāvatiṣṭhate
children.translated_text: My life is not secure, nor does my heart remain steady,

children.text: krośataḥ paramārtasya śrutaḥ śabdo mayā bhṛśam ||
children.translated_text: for I have heard the voice of one crying out in extreme distress.

children.text: ākrandamānaṃ tu vane bhrātaraṃ trātum arhasi
children.translated_text: You ought to save your brother as he cries out in the forest.

children.text: taṃ kṣipram abhidhāva tvaṃ bhrātaraṃ śaraṇaiṣiṇam ||
children.translated_text: Run quickly to that brother, who seeks refuge,

children.text: rakṣasāṃ vaśam āpannaṃ siṃhānām iva govṛṣam
children.translated_text: fallen under the power of rākṣasas like a bull among lions.'

children.text: na jagāma tathoktas tu bhrātur ājñāya śāsanam ||
children.translated_text: But though addressed in that way, he did not go, because of his brother's command.

children.text: tam uvāca tatas tatra kupitā janakātmajā
children.translated_text: Then the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, angry there, said to him,

children.text: saumitre mitrarūpeṇa bhrātus tvam asi śatruvat ||
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Saumitri</s>, wearing the form of a friend, you are like an enemy toward your brother.'

children.text: yas tvam asyām avasthāyāṃ bhrātaraṃ nābhipadyase
children.translated_text: But you do not go to your brother in this condition,

children.text: icchasi tvaṃ vinaśyantaṃ rāmaṃ lakṣmaṇa matkṛte ||
children.translated_text: and you wish <s>Rāma</s> to perish for my sake, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: vyasanaṃ te priyaṃ manye sneho bhrātari nāsti te
children.translated_text: I think his misfortune is dear to you; you have no affection for your brother.

children.text: tena tiṣṭhasi viśrabdhas tam apaśyan mahādyutim ||
children.translated_text: For that reason you stand here unconcerned, not seeing that great-splendored one.

children.text: kiṃ hi saṃśayam āpanne tasminn iha mayā bhavet
children.translated_text: What doubt could there be for me here, when he has fallen into danger?

children.text: kartavyam iha tiṣṭhantyā yat pradhānas tvam āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: What should I do, standing here, since you have come with him as your chief concern?
As <s>Vaidehī</s> spoke thus, overwhelmed by tears and grief,

children.text: abravīl lakṣmaṇas trastāṃ sītāṃ mṛgavadhūm iva ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> spoke to the frightened <s>Sītā</s>, who was like a doe.
Lady, among gods and men, among <s>gandharvas</s> and birds,
among <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, <s>kiṃnaras</s>, and beasts,

children.text: dānaveṣu ca ghoreṣu na sa vidyeta śobhane
children.translated_text: and among the terrible <s>dānavas</s>, there is no one, fair lady,
who could fight against <s>Rāma</s> in battle, equal as he is to <s>Vāsava</s>.

children.text: avadhyaḥ samare rāmo naivaṃ tvaṃ vaktum arhasi
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> cannot be slain in battle; you should not speak in this way.

children.text: na tvām asmin vane hātum utsahe rāghavaṃ vinā ||
children.translated_text: I cannot bring myself to abandon you in this forest without <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: anivāryaṃ balaṃ tasya balair balavatām api
children.translated_text: His force cannot be checked even by the forces of the strong,

children.text: tribhir lokaiḥ samudyuktaiḥ seśvaraiḥ sāmarair api ||
children.translated_text: even if the three worlds, with their lords and the immortals, were arrayed against him.

children.text: hṛdayaṃ nirvṛtaṃ te 'stu saṃtāpas tyajyatām ayam
children.translated_text: Let your heart be at ease; abandon this distress.

children.text: āgamiṣyati te bhartā śīghraṃ hatvā mṛgottamam ||
children.translated_text: Your husband will come quickly, after killing the best of deer.

children.text: na sa tasya svaro vyaktaṃ na kaścid api daivataḥ
children.translated_text: Plainly that was not his voice, nor was it any deity.
That was the illusion of that <s>rākṣasa</s>, like a city of the <s>gandharvas</s>.
You are a trust, <s>Vaidehī</s>, entrusted to me by the great-souled

children.text: rāmeṇa tvaṃ varārohe na tvāṃ tyaktum ihotsahe ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, lovely-hipped lady; I cannot abandon you here.

children.text: kṛtavairāś ca kalyāṇi vayam etair niśācaraiḥ
children.translated_text: We have made enemies of these night-roamers, auspicious lady,
with respect to the killing of <s>Khara</s> and the slaughter at <s>Janasthāna</s>, lady.
<s>Rākṣasas</s>, by contrivance, send forth such voices in the great forest.
They take violence as sport, <s>Vaidehī</s>; you should not be anxious.
But when <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> had spoken in this way, she became angry, her eyes reddened,
and she spoke a harsh word to truthful <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:
Ignoble man, with compassion only as a beginning, cruel one, disgrace of your family,

children.text: ahaṃ tava priyaṃ manye tenaitāni prabhāṣase ||
children.translated_text: I think that I am dear to you; that is why you say these things.

children.text: naitac citraṃ sapatneṣu pāpaṃ lakṣmaṇa yad bhavet
children.translated_text: It is no wonder, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, that evil should arise among rivals,
among cruel men like you, who always move in secret.

children.text: suduṣṭas tvaṃ vane rāmam ekam eko 'nugacchasi
children.translated_text: Very wicked as you are, you alone follow <s>Rāma</s>, alone in the forest,

children.text: mama hetoḥ praticchannaḥ prayukto bharatena vā ||
children.translated_text: concealed on my account, or else sent by <s>Bharata</s>.
How could I, after taking as my husband <s>Rāma</s>, dark as a blue lotus,
with eyes like lotuses, desire some other ordinary man?

children.text: samakṣaṃ tava saumitre prāṇāṃs tyakṣye na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Before your very eyes, son of <s>Sumitrā</s>, I will give up my life, without doubt.

children.text: rāmaṃ vinā kṣaṇam api na hi jīvāmi bhūtale ||
children.translated_text: Without <s>Rāma</s>, I cannot live on earth even for a moment.

children.text: ity uktaḥ paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ sītayā romaharṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Sītā</s> with harsh, hair-raising words,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, with joined palms and senses mastered, said to <s>Sītā</s>:

children.text: uttaraṃ notsahe vaktuṃ daivataṃ bhavatī mama
children.translated_text: I cannot bring myself to speak an answer; you are a divinity to me.

children.text: vākyam apratirūpaṃ tu na citraṃ strīṣu maithili ||
children.translated_text: But improper speech is no wonder among women, <s>Maithilī</s>.

children.text: svabhāvas tv eṣa nārīṇām eṣu lokeṣu dṛśyate
children.translated_text: For this is seen to be the nature of women in these worlds:
women are free from <s>dharma</s> (right conduct), fickle, sharp, and divisive.
Let all the forest-dwellers hear me, becoming witnesses,

children.text: nyāyavādī yathā vākyam ukto 'haṃ paruṣaṃ tvayā ||
children.translated_text: how, though I spoke justly, I have been addressed harshly by you.

children.text: dhik tvām adya praṇaśya tvaṃ yan mām evaṃ viśaṅkase
children.translated_text: Shame on you today; may you perish, since you suspect me in this way,
because of the corrupt nature of womanhood, though I stand firm in my elder's command.

children.text: gamiṣye yatra kākutsthaḥ svasti te 'stu varānane
children.translated_text: I will go where <s>Kākutstha</s> is; may it be well with you, lovely-faced lady.
May all the forest deities protect you, wide-eyed one.

children.text: nimittāni hi ghorāṇi yāni prādurbhavanti me
children.translated_text: For terrible omens are appearing to me.

children.text: api tvāṃ saha rāmeṇa paśyeyaṃ punar āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: May I see you again, together with <s>Rāma</s>, when I have returned.
When <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> had spoken thus, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, weeping,
then replied with a fierce word, overwhelmed by tears:
I will enter the <s>Godāvarī</s> without <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>;
or I will hang myself, or cast off my body on rough ground.

children.text: pibāmi vā viṣaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ pravekṣyāmi hutāśanam
children.translated_text: Or I will drink sharp poison; I will enter the fire.

children.text: na tv ahaṃ rāghavād anyaṃ padāpi puruṣaṃ spṛśe ||
children.translated_text: But I will not touch any man other than <s>Rāghava</s>, even with my foot.
Having thus reviled <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, <s>Sītā</s>, filled with sorrow,

children.text: pāṇibhyāṃ rudatī duḥkhād udaraṃ prajaghāna ha ||
children.translated_text: struck her belly with both hands as she wept in grief.

children.text: tām ārtarūpāṃ vimanā rudantīṃ saumitrir ālokya viśālanetrām
children.translated_text: Seeing her, wide-eyed, distressed in appearance, dejected and weeping,

children.text: āśvāsayāmāsa na caiva bhartus taṃ bhrātaraṃ kiṃcid uvāca sītā ||
children.translated_text: the son of <s>Sumitrā</s> comforted her, but <s>Sītā</s> said nothing more to that brother of her husband.

children.text: tatas tu sītām abhivādya lakṣmaṇaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ kiṃcid abhipraṇamya
children.translated_text: Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, having saluted <s>Sītā</s>, with joined palms and a slight bow,

children.text: avekṣamāṇo bahuśaś ca maithilīṃ jagāma rāmasya samīpam ātmavān ||
children.translated_text: and looking back again and again at <s>Maithilī</s>, self-possessed, went to <s>Rāma</s>'s side.

children.text: tayā paruṣam uktas tu kupito rāghavānujaḥ
children.translated_text: Harshly addressed by her, the younger brother of <s>Rāghava</s> was angered,

children.text: sa vikāṅkṣan bhṛśaṃ rāmaṃ pratasthe nacirād iva ||
children.translated_text: and, greatly anxious for <s>Rāma</s>, he set out without delay.
Then <s>Daśagrīva</s>, quickly taking the opportunity that had arisen,
approached <s>Vaidehī</s>, assuming the form of a wandering ascetic.
Wrapped in smooth ocher garments, with a topknot, an umbrella, and sandals,
and having hung on his left shoulder a fine staff and water-pot,
he approached <s>Vaidehī</s> in the guise of a wandering ascetic.
That immensely strong one reached her in the forest, deprived of the two brothers,
like great darkness reaching twilight deprived of the sun and moon.

children.text: tām apaśyat tato bālāṃ rājaputrīṃ yaśasvinīm
children.translated_text: Then he saw that young, famous princess...
like <s>Rohiṇī</s> bereft of the moon, exceedingly dreadful as under an evil planet.
Seeing that fierce one of sinful deeds, the trees growing in <s>Janasthāna</s>

children.text: samīkṣya na prakampante na pravāti ca mārutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: did not tremble, and the wind did not blow.

children.text: śīghrasrotāś ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā vīkṣantaṃ raktalocanam
children.translated_text: And when the swift-flowing <s>Godāvarī</s> river saw him gazing about with blood-red eyes,

children.text: stimitaṃ gantum ārebhe bhayād godāvarī nadī ||
children.translated_text: from fear it began to move sluggishly, as though stilled.

children.text: rāmasya tv antaraṃ prepsur daśagrīvas tadantare
children.translated_text: But <s>Daśagrīva</s>, seeking an opening against <s>Rāma</s>, at that moment
approached <s>Vaidehī</s>; <s>Rāvaṇa</s> was in the form of a mendicant.
The unworthy one, in a worthy-looking form, came near <s>Vaidehī</s>
as she grieved after her husband, like <s>Śanaiścara</s> approaching fair <s>Citrā</s>.

children.text: sa pāpo bhavyarūpeṇa tṛṇaiḥ kūpa ivāvṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: That sinner, in a worthy-looking form, like a well covered over with grass,
stood there looking at <s>Vaidehī</s>, the famous wife of <s>Rāma</s>.
She was auspicious, with lovely teeth and lips, and a face like the full moon,
seated in the leaf-hut, oppressed by tears and grief.
That night-roaming rākṣasa (demon), evil-minded, approached
<s>Vaidehī</s>, lotus-petal-eyed and dressed in yellow silk.
Pierced by the arrows of <s>Manmatha</s>, yet uttering Vedic sounds,
the lord of rākṣasas spoke humble words in that lonely place.

children.text: tām uttamāṃ trilokānāṃ padmahīnām iva śriyam
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s> then praised her, the finest woman in the three worlds,
shining with her body like <s>Śrī</s> without her lotus.
"Who are you, golden-hued lady, dressed in yellow silk,

children.text: kamalānāṃ śubhāṃ mālāṃ padminīva ca bibhratī ||
children.translated_text: bearing, like a lotus-pond, a beautiful garland of lotuses?

children.text: hrīḥ śrīḥ kīrtiḥ śubhā lakṣmīr apsarā vā śubhānane
children.translated_text: Are you <s>Hrī</s>, <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Kīrti</s>, auspicious <s>Lakṣmī</s>, or an apsaras, fair-faced one?

children.text: bhūtir vā tvaṃ varārohe ratir vā svairacāriṇī ||
children.translated_text: Or are you <s>Bhūti</s>, fine-hipped lady, or <s>Rati</s> moving at will?

children.text: samāḥ śikhariṇaḥ snigdhāḥ pāṇḍurā daśanās tava
children.translated_text: Your teeth are even, pointed, smooth, and white;
your eyes are broad and clear, dark-pupiled with reddish corners.
Your hips are broad and full, and your thighs are like the trunks of young elephants;
these two rounded limbs are well developed, close-set, and splendid.
Your breasts, full and raised at the tips, lovely, like smooth palmyra fruits,
are charming, adorned with excellent jewels.
Lovely-smiling, lovely-toothed, lovely-eyed, playful lady,

children.text: mano harasi me rāme nadīkūlam ivāmbhasā ||
children.translated_text: you carry away my mind, O <s>Rāma</s>'s woman, as water carries away a riverbank.
You are slender enough to be measured by a handspan, with beautiful hair and compact breasts;

children.text: naiva devī na gandharvī na yakṣī na ca kiṃnarī ||
children.translated_text: you are no goddess, no gandharvī, no yakṣī, and no kiṃnarī.
Never before have I seen a woman of such form on earth;

children.text: iha vāsaś ca kāntāre cittam unmādayanti me ||
children.translated_text: your dwelling here in this wilderness drives my mind mad.

children.text: sā pratikrāma bhadraṃ te na tvaṃ vastum ihārhasi
children.translated_text: So go away from here; may it be well with you. You do not deserve to live here.
This is the dwelling-place of terrible rākṣasas who can assume forms at will.
Beautiful palace-tops and city pleasure-gardens,
prosperous and fragrant, are fitting for you to frequent.

children.text: varaṃ mālyaṃ varaṃ pānaṃ varaṃ vastraṃ ca śobhane
children.translated_text: Fine garlands, fine drink, and fine clothing, beautiful one,

children.text: bhartāraṃ ca varaṃ manye tvadyuktam asitekṣaṇe ||
children.translated_text: and a fine husband too, dark-eyed lady, I consider suited to you.

children.text: kā tvaṃ bhavasi rudrāṇāṃ marutāṃ vā śucismite
children.translated_text: Who are you among the <s>Rudras</s>, or among the <s>Maruts</s>, bright-smiling one?

children.text: vasūnāṃ vā varārohe devatā pratibhāsi me ||
children.translated_text: Or among the <s>Vasus</s>, fine-hipped lady? You appear to me to be a deity.

children.text: neha gacchanti gandharvā na devā na ca kiṃnarāḥ
children.translated_text: Gandharvas do not come here, nor gods, nor kiṃnaras;

children.text: rākṣasānām ayaṃ vāsaḥ kathaṃ nu tvam ihāgatā ||
children.translated_text: this is the dwelling-place of rākṣasas. How, then, have you come here?
Here there are branch-going animals, lions, leopards, tigers, and deer,

children.text: ṛkṣās tarakṣavaḥ kaṅkāḥ kathaṃ tebhyo na bibhyasi ||
children.translated_text: bears, hyenas, and vultures. How are you not afraid of them?
And of the terrible, swift elephants, intoxicated with rut,

children.text: katham ekā mahāraṇye na bibheṣi varānane ||
children.translated_text: how are you not afraid, lovely-faced one, alone in the great forest?

children.text: kāsi kasya kutaś ca tvaṃ kiṃnimittaṃ ca daṇḍakān
children.translated_text: Who are you, whose are you, and whence have you come? For what reason,
fair lady, do you wander alone in the dreadful <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest, haunted by rākṣasas?"
Thus praised by evil-minded <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, <s>Vaidehī</s>,

children.text: dvijātiveṣeṇa hi taṃ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇam āgatam
children.translated_text: seeing that <s>Rāvaṇa</s> had come in the guise of a twice-born man,
honored him with all the courtesies due to a guest, she of <s>Mithilā</s>.
First she brought him a seat and then respectfully offered water for his feet,

children.text: abravīt siddham ity eva tadā taṃ saumyadarśanam ||
children.translated_text: and said to that gentle-looking one, simply, "It is ready."

children.text: dvijātiveṣeṇa samīkṣya maithilī tam āgataṃ pātrakusumbhadhāriṇam
children.translated_text: When <s>Maithilī</s> saw him come in the guise of a twice-born man, carrying a bowl and ochre robe,

children.text: aśakyam udveṣṭum upāyadarśanān nyamantrayad brāhmaṇavad yathāgatam ||
children.translated_text: unable, through his show of proper conduct, to reject him, she invited him as a brāhmaṇa, just as he had come.

children.text: iyaṃ bṛsī brāhmaṇa kāmam āsyatām idaṃ ca pādyaṃ pratigṛhyatām iti
children.translated_text: "Here is a seat, brāhmaṇa; sit as you please, and accept this water for your feet,

children.text: idaṃ ca siddhaṃ vanajātam uttamaṃ tvadartham avyagram ihopabhujyatām ||
children.translated_text: and here is excellent food produced in the forest; partake of it here calmly, for your sake."
As he was being invited, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> looked closely at <s>Maithilī</s>, the king's wife, who spoke fully and courteously;

children.text: prahasya tasyā haraṇe dhṛtaṃ manaḥ samarpayāmāsa vadhāya rāvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: laughing, with his mind fixed on carrying her off, he consigned himself to his own destruction.

children.text: tataḥ suveṣaṃ mṛgayāgataṃ patiṃ pratīkṣamāṇā sahalakṣmaṇaṃ tadā
children.translated_text: Then, waiting for her well-dressed husband who had gone hunting, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: nirīkṣamāṇā haritaṃ dadarśa tan mahad vanaṃ naiva tu rāmalakṣmaṇau ||
children.translated_text: she looked out and saw that great green forest, but not <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: rāvaṇena tu vaidehī tadā pṛṣṭā jihīrṣuṇā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vaidehī</s>, questioned by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, who wished to carry her away,
while he was in the form of a wandering ascetic, told him about herself by herself.

children.text: brāhmaṇaś cātithiś caiṣa anukto hi śapeta mām
children.translated_text: "This man is a brāhmaṇa and a guest; if unaddressed, he may curse me,"

children.text: iti dhyātvā muhūrtaṃ tu sītā vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: so <s>Sītā</s> reflected for a moment and then spoke these words:
"I am the daughter of great-souled <s>Janaka</s>, king of <s>Mithilā</s>;

children.text: sītā nāmnāsmi bhadraṃ te rāmabhāryā dvijottama ||
children.translated_text: my name is <s>Sītā</s>; may it be well with you. I am <s>Rāma</s>'s wife, best of twice-born men.
For a year I lived in the dwelling of <s>Rāghava</s>,
enjoying human pleasures, endowed with the fulfillment of every desire.

children.text: tataḥ saṃvatsarād ūrdhvaṃ samamanyata me patim
children.translated_text: Then, after that year had passed, my husband was considered fit
to be consecrated as king, <s>Rāma</s>, together with the royal ministers."
But while preparations were being made for <s>Rāghava</s>'s consecration,

children.text: kaikeyī nāma bhartāraṃ mamāryā yācate varam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kaikeyī</s> by name, my noble mother-in-law, asked her husband for a boon.

children.text: pratigṛhya tu kaikeyī śvaśuraṃ sukṛtena me
children.translated_text: For <s>Kaikeyī</s>, having obtained a promise from my father-in-law through her former good deed,
asked for my husband's banishment and <s>Bharata</s>'s consecration
as two boons from her husband, the best of kings, who was steadfast in truth.

children.text: nādya bhokṣye na ca svapsye na pāsye 'haṃ kadācana
children.translated_text: 'Today I shall not eat, nor shall I sleep, nor shall I ever drink;

children.text: eṣa me jīvitasyānto rāmo yady abhiṣicyate ||
children.translated_text: this is the end of my life, if <s>Rāma</s> is consecrated.'

children.text: iti bruvāṇāṃ kaikeyīṃ śvaśuro me sa mānadaḥ
children.translated_text: As <s>Kaikeyī</s> spoke thus, my father-in-law, that giver of honor,

children.text: ayācatārthair anvarthair na ca yācñāṃ cakāra sā ||
children.translated_text: begged her with fitting arguments, but she did not grant his request.
My husband, of great splendor, was twenty-five years old;

children.text: rāmeti prathito loke guṇavān satyavāk śuciḥ
children.translated_text: known in the world as <s>Rāma</s>, he was virtuous, truthful in speech, and pure,
wide-eyed, mighty-armed, and devoted to the welfare of all beings.

children.text: abhiṣekāya tu pituḥ samīpaṃ rāmam āgatam
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāma</s> had come near his father for the consecration,

children.text: kaikeyī mama bhartāram ity uvāca drutaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kaikeyī</s> spoke these hurried words to my husband:

children.text: tava pitrā samājñaptaṃ mamedaṃ śṛṇu rāghava
children.translated_text: 'By your father this has been commanded; hear it from me, O <s>Rāghava</s>:
this kingdom, free of thorns, is to be given to <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: tvayā tu khalu vastavyaṃ nava varṣāṇi pañca ca
children.translated_text: But you must dwell for nine years and five
in the forest. Go into exile, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, and free your father from falsehood.'

children.text: tathety uvāca tāṃ rāmaḥ kaikeyīm akutobhayaḥ
children.translated_text: 'So be it,' <s>Rāma</s>, fearless on every side, said to <s>Kaikeyī</s>;

children.text: cakāra tadvacas tasyā mama bhartā dṛḍhavrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: my husband, firm in his vow, carried out her word.

children.text: dadyān na pratigṛhṇīyāt satyaṃ brūyān na cānṛtam
children.translated_text: He would give, not take; he would speak truth, not falsehood:

children.text: etad brāhmaṇa rāmasya vrataṃ dhruvam anuttamam ||
children.translated_text: this, O brāhmaṇa, is <s>Rāma</s>'s fixed and unsurpassed vow.

children.text: tasya bhrātā tu vaimātro lakṣmaṇo nāma vīryavān
children.translated_text: His half-brother, named <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, was powerful;
that tiger among men, destroyer of foes in battle, was <s>Rāma</s>'s helper.

children.text: sa bhrātā lakṣmaṇo nāma dharmacārī dṛḍhavrataḥ
children.translated_text: That brother named <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, righteous in conduct and firm in his vow,
followed with bow in hand when he went into exile together with me.

children.text: te vayaṃ pracyutā rājyāt kaikeyyās tu kṛte trayaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus the three of us, fallen from the kingdom because of <s>Kaikeyī</s>,
wander through the deep forest with courage, O best of twice-born men.

children.text: samāśvasa muhūrtaṃ tu śakyaṃ vastum iha tvayā
children.translated_text: Take comfort for a moment; it is possible for you to stay here.

children.text: āgamiṣyati me bhartā vanyam ādāya puṣkalam ||
children.translated_text: My husband will come, bringing abundant forest fare.

children.text: sa tvaṃ nāma ca gotraṃ ca kulam ācakṣva tattvataḥ
children.translated_text: So tell me truthfully your name, your <s>gotra</s> (lineage), and your family;

children.text: ekaś ca daṇḍakāraṇye kimarthaṃ carasi dvija ||
children.translated_text: and why do you wander alone in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest, O twice-born one?
When <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Rāma</s>'s wife, had spoken thus, the mighty one,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas, gave a fierce reply:
'I am he by whom the worlds, together with gods, asuras, and serpents, have been terrified;

children.text: ahaṃ sa rāvaṇo nāma sīte rakṣogaṇeśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: I am that one named <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, O <s>Sītā</s>, lord of the hosts of rākṣasas.
But seeing you, gleaming with a golden complexion and clothed in silk,
I find no delight in my own wives, O blameless one.
Among the many excellent women brought here and there,

children.text: sarvāsām eva bhadraṃ te mamāgramahiṣī bhava ||
children.translated_text: be my chief queen over them all. Fortune be yours.

children.text: laṅkā nāma samudrasya madhye mama mahāpurī
children.translated_text: In the middle of the ocean is my great city named <s>Laṅkā</s>,
surrounded by the sea and set upon the summit of a mountain.

children.text: tatra sīte mayā sārdhaṃ vaneṣu vicariṣyasi
children.translated_text: There, O <s>Sītā</s>, you will wander with me in the groves,
and you will not long for this dwelling in the forest, O lovely woman.
Five thousand maidservants, adorned with every ornament,

children.text: sīte paricariṣyanti bhāryā bhavasi me yadi ||
children.translated_text: will attend on you, O <s>Sītā</s>, if you become my wife.'
But when <s>Rāvaṇa</s> had spoken thus, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s> became angry;
the faultless-limbed woman, disregarding that rākṣasa, replied:
'I am devoted to my husband, unshakable like a great mountain and resembling <s>Mahendra</s>,
to <s>Rāma</s>, unperturbed like the great ocean.
I am devoted to <s>Rāma</s>, mighty-armed, broad-chested, moving with the stride of a lion,
a lion among men, like a lion in appearance.
I am devoted to <s>Rāma</s>, heroic, with a face like the full moon, royal, and self-controlled,
broad in fame and mighty-armed.

children.text: tvaṃ punar jambukaḥ siṃhīṃ mām ihecchasi durlabhām
children.translated_text: But you are a jackal, desiring me here, a lioness hard to obtain.

children.text: nāhaṃ śakyā tvayā spraṣṭum ādityasya prabhā yathā ||
children.translated_text: I cannot be touched by you, as the radiance of the sun cannot be touched.

children.text: pādapān kāñcanān nūnaṃ bahūn paśyasi mandabhāk
children.translated_text: Surely, poor fool, you think you see many golden trees,

children.text: rāghavasya priyāṃ bhāryāṃ yas tvam icchasi rāvaṇa ||
children.translated_text: since you desire <s>Rāghava</s>'s beloved wife, O <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
You wish to take a fang from the mouth of a hungry, impetuous lion, enemy of deer,
from the mouth of a venomous serpent.
You wish to carry off <s>Mandara</s>, best of mountains, with your hand,

children.text: kālakūṭaṃ viṣaṃ pītvā svastimān gantum icchasi ||
children.translated_text: and, after drinking the poison <s>Kālakūṭa</s>, you wish to go away unharmed.

children.text: akṣisūcyā pramṛjasi jihvayā lekṣi ca kṣuram
children.translated_text: You wipe your eye with a needle and lick a razor with your tongue;

children.text: rāghavasya priyāṃ bhāryām adhigantuṃ tvam icchasi ||
children.translated_text: you desire to possess <s>Rāghava</s>'s beloved wife.

children.text: avasajya śilāṃ kaṇṭhe samudraṃ tartum icchasi
children.translated_text: Fastening a stone to your neck, you wish to cross the ocean;
you wish to seize both the sun and the moon with your two hands,

children.text: yo rāmasya priyāṃ bhāryāṃ pradharṣayitum icchasi ||
children.translated_text: you who wish to violate <s>Rāma</s>'s beloved wife.
Seeing a blazing fire, you wish to carry it away in a cloth,

children.text: kalyāṇavṛttāṃ rāmasya yo bhāryāṃ hartum icchasi ||
children.translated_text: you who wish to carry off <s>Rāma</s>'s wife, whose conduct is noble.
You wish to walk on the points of iron-tipped spears,

children.text: rāmasya sadṛśīṃ bhāryāṃ yo 'dhigantuṃ tvam icchasi ||
children.translated_text: you who desire to obtain a wife equal to <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: yad antaraṃ siṃhaśṛgālayor vane yad antaraṃ syandanikāsamudrayoḥ
children.translated_text: As great as the difference in the forest between a lion and a jackal, as the difference between a river and the ocean,

children.text: surāgryasauvīrakayor yad antaraṃ tad antaraṃ dāśarathes tavaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: as the difference between excellent wine and sour gruel, such is the difference between <s>Daśaratha</s>'s son and you.

children.text: yad antaraṃ kāñcanasīsalohayor yad antaraṃ candanavāripaṅkayoḥ
children.translated_text: As great as the difference between gold, lead, and iron, as the difference between sandal-water and mud,

children.text: yad antaraṃ hastibiḍālayor vane tad antaraṃ dāśarathes tavaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: As great as the difference between an elephant and a cat in the forest, that is the difference between <s>Daśaratha</s>'s son and you.

children.text: yad antaraṃ vāyasavainateyayor yad antaraṃ madgumayūrayor api
children.translated_text: As great as the difference between a crow and <s>Vainateya</s>, and also the difference between a water-bird and a peacock,

children.text: yad antaraṃ sārasagṛdhrayor vane tad antaraṃ dāśarathes tavaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: as great as the difference between a crane and a vulture in the forest, that is the difference between <s>Daśaratha</s>'s son and you.
While <s>Rāma</s>, whose splendor is equal to the thousand-eyed god, stands there with bow and arrows in hand,

children.text: hṛtāpi te 'haṃ na jarāṃ gamiṣye vajraṃ yathā makṣikayāvagīrṇam ||
children.translated_text: even though I have been carried off by you, I shall not come to ruin, just as a thunderbolt is not harmed when swallowed by a fly.

children.text: itīva tad vākyam aduṣṭabhāvā sudṛṣṭam uktvā rajanīcaraṃ tam
children.translated_text: Having spoken that very statement plainly to that night-roaming being, she whose heart was undefiled

children.text: gātraprakampād vyathitā babhūva vātoddhatā sā kadalīva tanvī ||
children.translated_text: became distressed, her limbs trembling, slender as a plantain tree shaken by the wind.

children.text: tāṃ vepamānām upalakṣya sītāṃ sa rāvaṇo mṛtyusamaprabhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: Observing <s>Sītā</s> trembling, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, whose splendor was like death,

children.text: kulaṃ balaṃ nāma ca karma cātmanaḥ samācacakṣe bhayakāraṇārtham ||
children.translated_text: recounted his lineage, strength, name, and deeds, in order to cause fear.
As <s>Sītā</s> was speaking in this way, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, enraged, with harsh syllables,

children.text: lalāṭe bhrukuṭīṃ kṛtvā rāvaṇaḥ pratyuvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: knitted his brow upon his forehead and replied:
I am the brother of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, born of a rival wife, O fair-limbed one.

children.text: rāvaṇo nāma bhadraṃ te daśagrīvaḥ pratāpavān ||
children.translated_text: My name is <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, good fortune to you, the mighty ten-necked one.
From fear of me the gods, together with the gandharvas, piśācas, birds, and serpents,

children.text: vidravanti bhayād bhītā mṛtyor iva sadā prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: flee in terror, as creatures always flee from death.
Through my valor in battle, in anger over a certain cause, my half-brother <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>

children.text: dvaṃdvam āsāditaḥ krodhād raṇe vikramya nirjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: was brought to single combat and conquered.
Afflicted by fear of me, the man-borne one abandoned his own prosperous seat
and now dwells on <s>Kailāsa</s>, best of mountains.

children.text: yasya tat puṣpakaṃ nāma vimānaṃ kāmagaṃ śubham
children.translated_text: That beautiful aerial car named <s>Puṣpaka</s>, which goes wherever one wishes,

children.text: vīryād āvarjitaṃ bhadre yena yāmi vihāyasam ||
children.translated_text: was bent to my power, O noble lady, and by it I travel through the sky.
Merely seeing my face when anger has arisen in me, O <s>Maithilī</s>,
the gods, with <s>Śakra</s> at their head, flee away in terror.

children.text: yatra tiṣṭhāmy ahaṃ tatra māruto vāti śaṅkitaḥ
children.translated_text: Wherever I stand, the wind blows in dread,

children.text: tīvrāṃśuḥ śiśirāṃśuś ca bhayāt sampadyate raviḥ ||
children.translated_text: and from fear the sun of fierce rays becomes cool-rayed.
Trees have motionless leaves, and rivers have stilled waters

children.text: bhavanti yatra yatrāhaṃ tiṣṭhāmi ca carāmi ca ||
children.translated_text: wherever I stand and wherever I move.

children.text: mama pāre samudrasya laṅkā nāma purī śubhā
children.translated_text: Across the ocean from here is my splendid city named <s>Laṅkā</s>,
filled with terrible rākṣasas, like <s>Amarāvatī</s> of <s>Indra</s>.
It is surrounded by a rampart and shines white,
a lovely city with golden courts and gateways made of beryl.
It is crowded with elephants, horses, and chariots, and resounds with the sound of musical instruments.
It is adorned with crowded gardens full of trees that bear every desired fruit.

children.text: tatra tvaṃ vasatī sīte rājaputri mayā saha
children.translated_text: Dwelling there with me, O <s>Sītā</s>, princess,
you will no longer remember human women, O proud-minded one.

children.text: bhuñjānā mānuṣān bhogān divyāṃś ca varavarṇini
children.translated_text: Enjoying human pleasures and divine ones as well, O fair-limbed one,
you will not remember <s>Rāma</s>, a mere mortal whose life is spent.

children.text: sthāpayitvā priyaṃ putraṃ rājñā daśarathena yaḥ
children.translated_text: After the king <s>Daśaratha</s> had installed his beloved son,

children.text: mandavīryaḥ suto jyeṣṭhas tataḥ prasthāpito vanam ||
children.translated_text: that eldest son, weak in valor, was then sent away to the forest.
What will you do with that <s>Rāma</s>, deprived of his kingdom and bereft of sense,
O wide-eyed one, an ascetic, wretched with austerity?
I am the lord of all rākṣasas, come here of my own accord out of desire.
You ought not reject me, pierced as I am by the arrows of <s>Manmatha</s>.
For after rejecting me, timid woman, you will come to remorse,
like <s>Urvāśī</s> after striking <s>Purūravas</s> with her foot.

children.text: evam uktā tu vaidehī kruddhā saṃraktalocanā
children.translated_text: But when she had been addressed in this way, <s>Vaidehī</s>, angry and with reddened eyes,
spoke harsh words to the lord of rākṣasas in that lonely place.
How can you name as your brother the god <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, honored by all beings,

children.text: bhrātaraṃ vyapadiśya tvam aśubhaṃ kartum icchasi ||
children.translated_text: and yet desire to do an inauspicious deed?
Surely all the rākṣasas will perish, O <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: yeṣāṃ tvaṃ karkaśo rājā durbuddhir ajitendriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: since you are their harsh king, evil-minded and uncontrolled in your senses.

children.text: apahṛtya śacīṃ bhāryāṃ śakyam indrasya jīvitum
children.translated_text: One might live after abducting <s>Śacī</s>, the wife of <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: na tu rāmasya bhāryāṃ mām apanīyāsti jīvitam ||
children.translated_text: but after carrying me off, the wife of <s>Rāma</s>, there is no life for you.

children.text: jīvec ciraṃ vajradharasya hastāc chacīṃ pradhṛṣyāpratirūparūpām
children.translated_text: One might live long after violating <s>Śacī</s>, whose beauty is incomparable, from the hand of the wielder of the thunderbolt;

children.text: na mādṛśīṃ rākṣasa dharṣayitvā pītāmṛtasyāpi tavāsti mokṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but after violating one such as me, O rākṣasa, there is no release for you, even if you had drunk nectar.
Hearing the words of <s>Sītā</s>, the mighty ten-necked one

children.text: haste hastaṃ samāhatya cakāra sumahad vapuḥ ||
children.translated_text: struck hand against hand and made his body exceedingly large.

children.text: sa maithilīṃ punar vākyaṃ babhāṣe ca tato bhṛśam
children.translated_text: Then he spoke again to <s>Maithilī</s>, and very forcefully:
Madwoman, I think you have not heard of my heroic strength and prowess.

children.text: udvaheyaṃ bhujābhyāṃ tu medinīm ambare sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Standing in the sky, I could lift up the earth with my two arms,

children.text: āpibeyaṃ samudraṃ ca mṛtyuṃ hanyāṃ raṇe sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and I could drink up the ocean and slay death as he stood in battle.

children.text: arkaṃ rundhyāṃ śarais tīkṣṇair vibhindyāṃ hi mahītalam
children.translated_text: I could block the sun with sharp arrows and split the earth's surface.

children.text: kāmarūpiṇam unmatte paśya māṃ kāmadaṃ patim ||
children.translated_text: See me, madwoman: able to assume whatever form I wish, a husband who grants desire.
When <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, radiant like fire, had spoken in this way,
his eyes, red with anger and tawny at the edges, appeared.

children.text: sadyaḥ saumyaṃ parityajya bhikṣurūpaṃ sa rāvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: At once <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, abandoning the gentle form of a mendicant,
assumed his own form, like the form of death, that younger brother of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>.
With blood-red eyes, splendid, wearing earrings of heated gold,
the night-roaming being became ten-faced, bearing bow and arrows.
Abandoning that disguise of a wandering ascetic, his body huge,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of rākṣasas, entered into his own form.
Blood-red-eyed from anger, with the splendor of a mass of rain-clouds,
Wearing red garments, he stood gazing at <s>Maithilī</s>, that jewel among women.

children.text: sa tām asitakeśāntāṃ bhāskarasya prabhām iva
children.translated_text: Then, seeing her whose hair ended in dark locks, like the radiance of the sun,
that <s>Maithilī</s>, adorned with garments and ornaments, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> spoke to her:

children.text: triṣu lokeṣu vikhyātaṃ yadi bhartāram icchasi
children.translated_text: "If you desire a husband renowned in the three worlds,

children.text: mām āśraya varārohe tavāhaṃ sadṛśaḥ patiḥ ||
children.translated_text: take refuge in me, fair-hipped lady; I am a husband worthy of you.

children.text: māṃ bhajasva cirāya tvam ahaṃ ślāghyas tava priyaḥ
children.translated_text: Serve me for a long time; I will be praiseworthy and dear to you.

children.text: naiva cāhaṃ kvacid bhadre kariṣye tava vipriyam
children.translated_text: And never, my good lady, will I do anything displeasing to you.

children.text: tyajyatāṃ mānuṣo bhāvo mayi bhāvaḥ praṇīyatām ||
children.translated_text: Let this human feeling be abandoned; let affection be directed toward me.
By what virtues are you attached to <s>Rāma</s>, fallen from his kingdom, unsuccessful,
and of limited life, foolish woman who thinks herself wise?

children.text: yaḥ striyā vacanād rājyaṃ vihāya sasuhṛjjanam
children.translated_text: That evil-minded man, who at a woman's word abandoned his kingdom together with his friends
and lives in this forest haunted by beasts,

children.text: ity uktvā maithilīṃ vākyaṃ priyārhāṃ priyavādinīm
children.translated_text: having thus spoken this speech to <s>Maithilī</s>, who deserved gentle words and spoke gently,

children.text: jagrāha rāvaṇaḥ sītāṃ budhaḥ khe rohiṇīm iva ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s> seized <s>Sītā</s>, like <s>Budha</s> seizing <s>Rohiṇī</s> in the sky.

children.text: vāmena sītāṃ padmākṣīṃ mūrdhajeṣu kareṇa saḥ
children.translated_text: With his left hand he grasped lotus-eyed <s>Sītā</s> by the hair of her head,
and with his right hand he took hold of her thighs.
Seeing him, like a mountain peak, with sharp fangs and mighty arms,
the forest deities, stricken with fear, fled from him, who resembled death.

children.text: sa ca māyāmayo divyaḥ kharayuktaḥ kharasvanaḥ
children.translated_text: And there appeared the divine, magical great chariot of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
golden-bodied, yoked with asses, and harsh-sounding.

children.text: tatas tāṃ paruṣair vākyair abhitarjya mahāsvanaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, threatening her with harsh words, the loud-voiced one
took <s>Vaidehī</s> on his lap and at that time mounted her on the chariot.
When seized by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the glorious <s>Sītā</s>, distressed with grief,

children.text: rāmeti sītā duḥkhārtā rāmaṃ dūragataṃ vane ||
children.translated_text: cried out loudly, "<s>Rāma</s>!" calling to <s>Rāma</s>, who was far away in the forest.

children.text: tām akāmāṃ sa kāmārtaḥ pannagendravadhūm iva
children.translated_text: Then lust-tormented <s>Rāvaṇa</s> took her, unwilling and writhing,
like the wife of the lord of serpents, and flew up.
Then, as she was being carried through the air by the lord of rākṣasas,
she cried out intensely, like a maddened woman, her mind reeling as if afflicted.
"Ah, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, mighty-armed one, delighter of your elder's heart,
do you not know that I am being carried off by a shape-shifting rākṣasa?

children.text: jīvitaṃ sukham arthāṃś ca dharmahetoḥ parityajan
children.translated_text: Abandoning life, pleasure, and wealth for the sake of dharma,

children.text: hriyamāṇām adharmeṇa māṃ rāghava na paśyasi ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Rāghava</s>, do you not see me being carried away unlawfully?
Surely you are the chastiser of the undisciplined, scorcher of foes.

children.text: katham evaṃvidhaṃ pāpaṃ na tvaṃ śādhi hi rāvaṇam ||
children.translated_text: How then do you not punish <s>Rāvaṇa</s> for such a sin?
Surely the fruit of the act of an undisciplined man is seen at once;

children.text: kālo 'py aṅgī bhavaty atra sasyānām iva paktaye ||
children.translated_text: time too becomes a factor here, as it does in the ripening of crops.
He has done this act with his mind overcome by time;
may you, from <s>Rāma</s>, suffer a terrible calamity that ends your life.

children.text: hantedānīṃ sakāmā tu kaikeyī bāndhavaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Alas, now <s>Kaikeyī</s>, together with her kinsmen, will have her desire fulfilled,
since I, the lawful wife of the glorious lover of dharma, am being carried away.
I call upon <s>Janasthāna</s> and the flowering karṇikāra trees:

children.text: kṣipraṃ rāmāya śaṃsadhvaṃ sītāṃ harati rāvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: quickly tell <s>Rāma</s>, '<s>Rāvaṇa</s> is carrying off <s>Sītā</s>.'
I bow to <s>Mālyavant</s>, to the peaked mountain <s>Prasravaṇa</s>:

children.text: kṣipraṃ rāmāya śaṃsadhvaṃ sītāṃ harati rāvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: quickly tell <s>Rāma</s>, '<s>Rāvaṇa</s> is carrying off <s>Sītā</s>.'
I bow to the river <s>Godāvarī</s>, resounding with flocks of swans and cranes:

children.text: kṣipraṃ rāmāya śaṃsadhvaṃ sītāṃ harati rāvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: quickly tell <s>Rāma</s>, '<s>Rāvaṇa</s> is carrying off <s>Sītā</s>.'

children.text: daivatāni ca yānty asmin vane vividhapādape
children.translated_text: And whatever deities move in this forest with its varied trees,

children.text: namaskaromy ahaṃ tebhyo bhartuḥ śaṃsata māṃ hṛtām ||
children.translated_text: I bow to them; tell my husband that I have been carried away.

children.text: yāni kānicid apy atra sattvāni nivasanty uta
children.translated_text: Whatever beings dwell here at all,
I take refuge in them all, even the hosts of deer and birds.
Tell him that his beloved <s>Sītā</s>, dearer to her husband than life,
has been carried away, helpless and abducted by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
When mighty-armed, very powerful <s>Rāma</s> learns of me,
he will bring me back by his valor, even if I have been taken by <s>Vaivasvata</s> himself.

children.text: rāmāya tu yathātattvaṃ jaṭāyo haraṇaṃ mama
children.translated_text: O <s>Jaṭāyu</s>, the abduction of me must be told to <s>Rāma</s> exactly as it happened,

children.text: lakṣmaṇāya ca tat sarvam ākhyātavyam aśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and all of it, without remainder, must also be reported to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>."

children.text: taṃ śabdam avasuptasya jaṭāyur atha śuśruve
children.translated_text: Then <s>Jaṭāyu</s>, who had been sleeping, heard that sound.

children.text: niraikṣad rāvaṇaṃ kṣipraṃ vaidehīṃ ca dadarśa saḥ ||
children.translated_text: He quickly looked toward <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and saw <s>Vaidehī</s> as well.
Then that best of birds, splendid, with a sharp beak and resembling a mountain summit,
perched in a tree, uttered these auspicious words:
"O <s>Daśagrīva</s>, I stand in ancient dharma, founded on truth;
I am named <s>Jaṭāyu</s>, a mighty king of vultures.
<s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, is king of the whole world, equal to great <s>Indra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>,

children.text: lokānāṃ ca hite yukto rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and he is devoted to the welfare of the worlds.
This glorious woman is the lawful wife of that lord of the world,

children.text: sītā nāma varārohā yāṃ tvaṃ hartum ihecchasi ||
children.translated_text: named <s>Sītā</s>, fair-hipped, whom you wish to carry off from here.

children.text: kathaṃ rājā sthito dharme paradārān parāmṛśet
children.translated_text: How can a king established in dharma touch another man's wife?
A king's wife, mighty one, must be especially protected.
Turn back this base intention, this assault upon another's wife.

children.text: na tat samācared dhīro yat paro 'sya vigarhayet
children.translated_text: A wise man should not do what another would blame in him.
Others' wives, like one's own, must be protected from violation.

children.text: arthaṃ vā yadi vā kāmaṃ śiṣṭāḥ śāstreṣvanāgatam
children.translated_text: Whether for wealth or for desire, the well-bred determine as dharma, in accordance with the king,
what is not laid down in the śāstras, O descendant of <s>Pulastya</s>.

children.text: rājā dharmaś ca kāmaś ca dravyāṇāṃ cottamo nidhiḥ
children.translated_text: The king is dharma and kāma, and the highest treasury of riches;
