children.text: dharmaḥ śubhaṃ vā pāpaṃ vā rājamūlaṃ pravartate ||
children.translated_text: whether good or evil, conduct proceeds with the king as its root.

children.text: pāpasvabhāvaś capalaḥ kathaṃ tvaṃ rakṣasāṃ vara
children.translated_text: Being sinful by nature and fickle, how have you, O best of rākṣasas,
attained sovereignty, like a wrongdoer attaining a celestial vehicle?"

children.text: kāmasvabhāvo yo yasya na sa śakyaḥ pramārjitum
children.translated_text: Whatever one's own nature, ruled by desire, may be, it cannot be wiped away.

children.text: na hi duṣṭātmanām āryamāvasaty ālaye ciram ||
children.translated_text: For noble conduct does not dwell long in the house of the corrupt-hearted.

children.text: viṣaye vā pure vā te yadā rāmo mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: Since mighty <s>Rāma</s>, in your territory or in your city,
commits no offense, being righteous, how can you offend against him?
If <s>Khara</s>, who had gone to <s>Janasthāna</s> because of <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>,
had overstepped and was formerly killed by <s>Rāma</s>, whose deeds are unwearied,

children.text: atra brūhi yathāsatyaṃ ko rāmasya vyatikramaḥ
children.translated_text: then tell the truth here: what transgression has <s>Rāma</s> committed,

children.text: yasya tvaṃ lokanāthasya hṛtvā bhāryāṃ gamiṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: that you will go away after carrying off the wife of that lord of the world?

children.text: kṣipraṃ visṛja vaidehīṃ mā tvā ghoreṇa cakṣuṣā
children.translated_text: Release <s>Vaidehī</s> quickly, lest he burn you with a terrible gaze,
becoming fire itself, as <s>Indra</s>'s thunderbolt burned <s>Vṛtra</s>.
You have bound a venomous snake in the hem of your garment and do not understand it;

children.text: grīvāyāṃ pratimuktaṃ ca kālapāśaṃ na paśyasi ||
children.translated_text: and you do not see the noose of Death fastened around your neck.

children.text: sa bhāraḥ saumya bhartavyo yo naraṃ nāvasādayet
children.translated_text: Friend, that burden should be borne which does not sink a man;

children.text: tad annam upabhoktavyaṃ jīryate yad anāmayam ||
children.translated_text: that food should be eaten which digests without illness.

children.text: yat kṛtvā na bhaved dharmo na kīrtir na yaśo bhuvi
children.translated_text: What man would undertake an act by doing which there would be no <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), no renown, and no fame on earth,

children.text: śarīrasya bhavet khedaḥ kas tat karma samācaret ||
children.translated_text: but only distress for the body?
Sixty thousand years have passed since I was born, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
while I have duly upheld the kingdom inherited from my fathers and grandfathers.

children.text: vṛddho 'haṃ tvaṃ yuvā dhanvī sarathaḥ kavacī śarī
children.translated_text: I am old; you are young, an archer, with chariot, armor, and arrows;

children.text: tathāpy ādāya vaidehīṃ kuśalī na gamiṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: nevertheless, after taking <s>Vaidehī</s>, you will not go away unharmed.

children.text: na śaktas tvaṃ balāddhartuṃ vaidehīṃ mama paśyataḥ
children.translated_text: You are not able to carry off <s>Vaidehī</s> by force while I am watching,
any more than fixed Vedic revelation can be carried away by arguments joined with reasoning.

children.text: yudhyasva yadi śūro 'si muhūrtaṃ tiṣṭha rāvaṇa
children.translated_text: Fight, if you are a hero; stay a moment, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: śayiṣyase hato bhūmau yathāpūrvaṃ kharas tathā ||
children.translated_text: You will lie slain upon the ground, just as <s>Khara</s> did before.
By him who has repeatedly slain daityas and dānavas in battle,

children.text: nacirāc cīravāsās tvāṃ rāmo yudhi vadhiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: by <s>Rāma</s>, who wears bark garments, you will soon be killed in war.

children.text: kiṃ nu śakyaṃ mayā kartuṃ gatau dūraṃ nṛpātmajau
children.translated_text: What indeed can I do, when the two princes have gone far away?

children.text: kṣipraṃ tvaṃ naśyase nīca tayor bhīto na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Quickly you will perish, base man, through fear of those two; there is no doubt.

children.text: na hi me jīvamānasya nayiṣyasi śubhām imām
children.translated_text: While I am alive, you shall not carry off this auspicious woman,
<s>Sītā</s>, lotus-petal-eyed, <s>Rāma</s>'s dear queen.

children.text: avaśyaṃ tu mayā kāryaṃ priyaṃ tasya mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: But I must surely do what is dear to that great-souled one,
even with my life, for <s>Rāma</s> and also for <s>Daśaratha</s>.

children.text: tiṣṭha tiṣṭha daśagrīva muhūrtaṃ paśya rāvaṇa
children.translated_text: Stand, stand, ten-necked one; look for a moment, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
I shall offer you the hospitality of battle, according to my strength, night-roamer.

children.text: vṛntād iva phalaṃ tvāṃ tu pātayeyaṃ rathottamāt ||
children.translated_text: I would make you fall from your excellent chariot like a fruit from its stalk.
When <s>Rāvaṇa</s> had thus been addressed properly by <s>Jaṭāyus</s>,
all twenty eyes of the angry one shone like fire.
With eyes reddened by anger and earrings like heated gold,
the intolerant lord of rākṣasas rushed at the lord of birds.

children.text: sa samprahāras tumulas tayos tasmin mahāvane
children.translated_text: Then a tumultuous combat between the two arose in that great forest,
like that of two clouds in the sky driven up by the wind.
Then that battle between the vulture and the rākṣasa became wondrous,
like that of two great mountains, winged and garlanded.
Then with nālīka arrows, iron shafts, and sharp-pointed barbed arrows,
the mighty one showered the very terrible missiles upon the powerful king of vultures.
The vulture, lord of feathered chariots,
<s>Jaṭāyus</s>, received those nets of arrows, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s weapons, in battle.
Then with his two sharp-clawed feet,
the powerful best of birds made many wounds in his limbs.
Then, in anger, the ten-necked one grasped ten arrows,
terrible, like the rod of death, longing to crush his enemy.

children.text: sa tair bāṇair mahāvīryaḥ pūrṇamuktair ajihmagaiḥ
children.translated_text: With those fully drawn, straight-flying arrows, the very powerful one

children.text: bibheda niśitais tīkṣṇair gṛdhraṃ ghoraiḥ śilīmukhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: pierced the vulture with sharp, keen, terrible shafts.
Seeing <s>Jānakī</s> in the rākṣasa's chariot, her eyes full of tears,
he paid no heed to those arrows and rushed at the rākṣasa.
Then the lord of birds, very radiant,
broke with his feet his bow, together with its arrow, adorned with pearls and jewels.
And that blazing quiver of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, shining like fire,
the very radiant lord of birds shook away with his wings.
Strong in battle, he also slew those swift steeds of his,

children.text: tāṃś cāsya javasampannāñ jaghāna samare balī ||
children.translated_text: divine, with golden breast-plates and ghoul-like faces.
And he broke the great chariot, excellent, furnished with three poles, moving at will, gleaming like fire,
its body variegated with jewels and gold,
and the umbrella like the full moon, together with the fans.
With his bow broken, deprived of his chariot, his horses slain and his charioteer slain,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, taking <s>Vaidehī</s> in his lap, fell upon the ground.
Seeing <s>Rāvaṇa</s> fallen on the ground, his vehicle broken,

children.text: sādhu sādhv iti bhūtāni gṛdhrarājam apūjayan ||
children.translated_text: the beings honored the king of vultures, saying, "Well done, well done!"

children.text: pariśrāntaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā jarayā pakṣiyūthapam
children.translated_text: But seeing that chief of birds exhausted by old age,

children.text: utpapāta punar hṛṣṭo maithilīṃ gṛhya rāvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s> sprang up again in delight, seizing <s>Maithilī</s>.
When the king of vultures saw him delighted, holding the daughter of <s>Janaka</s> in his lap and going away,
<s>Jaṭāyus</s> flew up and said this:
"<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, small-minded one, in carrying off this wife of <s>Rāma</s>, whose arrows strike like thunderbolts,

children.text: alpabuddhe harasy enāṃ vadhāya khalu rakṣasām ||
children.translated_text: you are doing this indeed for the destruction of the rākṣasas.
Together with your friends, kinsmen, ministers, army, and retinue,
you are drinking this draught of poison like water when thirsty."
Not understanding the consequences of deeds, and undiscerning about actions,

children.text: śīghram eva vinaśyanti yathā tvaṃ vinaśiṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: men quickly perish, just as you will perish.

children.text: baddhas tvaṃ kālapāśena kva gatas tasya mokṣyase
children.translated_text: You are bound by the noose of Time; wherever you have gone, how will you be released from it?

children.text: vadhāya baḍiśaṃ gṛhya sāmiṣaṃ jalajo yathā ||
children.translated_text: You are like a water-born creature that has seized a baited hook for its own death.

children.text: na hi jātu durādharṣau kākutsthau tava rāvaṇa
children.translated_text: For the two <s>Kākutsthas</s>, hard to assail, O <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
the two <s>Rāghavas</s> will never pardon your violation of this hermitage.

children.text: yathā tvayā kṛtaṃ karma bhīruṇā lokagarhitam
children.translated_text: The deed you have done, cowardly and condemned by the world,
is the path followed by thieves; it is not practiced by heroes.

children.text: yudhyasva yadi śūro 'si muhūrtaṃ tiṣṭha rāvaṇa
children.translated_text: Fight, if you are a hero. Stand for a moment, O <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: śayiṣyase hato bhūmau yathā bhrātā kharas tathā ||
children.translated_text: Slain, you will lie on the ground, just as your brother <s>Khara</s> did.
At the time of death, whatever deed a man undertakes,
that unrighteous deed, leading to his own destruction, you have undertaken.

children.text: pāpānubandho vai yasya karmaṇaḥ ko nu tat pumān
children.translated_text: What man, indeed, would do an act whose consequence is sin,
even if he were the blessed self-born lord of the world?

children.text: evam uktvā śubhaṃ vākyaṃ jaṭāyus tasya rakṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken these excellent words to that rākṣasa,
the valiant <s>Jaṭāyu</s> fell violently upon the back of the ten-headed one.

children.text: taṃ gṛhītvā nakhais tīkṣṇair virarāda samantataḥ
children.translated_text: Seizing him with his sharp talons, he tore at him on every side,
like an elephant-rider mounted upon a vicious elephant.

children.text: virarāda nakhair asya tuṇḍaṃ pṛṣṭhe samarpayan
children.translated_text: He tore him with his claws, pressing his beak upon his back,
and with claws, wings, and beak as his weapons, he plucked out his hair.

children.text: sa tathā gṛdhrarājena kliśyamāno muhur muhuḥ
children.translated_text: That rākṣasa, tormented again and again by the king of vultures,
trembled, his lips quivering with anger and impatience.
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, holding <s>Vaidehī</s> close with his left flank,
struck <s>Jaṭāyu</s> with his palm, distressed and overcome by rage.
Then <s>Jaṭāyu</s>, lord of birds and subduer of enemies, surpassed him and with his beak
tore away his ten left arms at that moment.

children.text: tataḥ kruddho daśagrīvaḥ sītām utsṛjya vīryavān
children.translated_text: Then the mighty ten-headed one, enraged, released <s>Sītā</s>,
and battered the king of vultures with his fists and feet.
Then for a moment there was a battle between two beings of unequaled valor,

children.text: rākṣasānāṃ ca mukhyasya pakṣiṇāṃ pravarasya ca ||
children.translated_text: the chief of rākṣasas and the foremost of birds.
As he was struggling on behalf of <s>Rāma</s>, then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>

children.text: pakṣau pādau ca pārśvau ca khaḍgam uddhṛtya socchinat ||
children.translated_text: drew his sword and cut off his wings, feet, and sides.
With his wings cut off suddenly by the rākṣasa of cruel deed,
the slain vulture, with little life remaining, fell to the earth.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā patitaṃ bhūmau kṣatajārdraṃ jaṭāyuṣam
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Jaṭāyu</s> fallen on the ground, wet with blood,
the grieving <s>Vaidehī</s> ran to him as though to her own kinsman.
The lord of <s>Laṅkā</s> saw <s>Jaṭāyu</s> on the earth, resembling a dark raincloud, with a very pale breast and noble valor,

children.text: dadarśa laṅkādhipatiḥ pṛthivyāṃ jaṭāyuṣaṃ śāntam ivāgnidāvam ||
children.translated_text: like a forest fire that had been calmed.

children.text: tatas tu taṃ pattrarathaṃ mahītale nipātitaṃ rāvaṇavegamarditam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sītā</s>, daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, her face shining like the moon, again embraced that bird-chariot fallen on the ground,

children.text: punaḥ pariṣvajya śaśiprabhānanā ruroda sītā janakātmajā tadā ||
children.translated_text: crushed by the force of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, and wept.
The lord of rākṣasas saw that vulture, with little life left, twitching on the ground,
fallen near <s>Rāghava</s>'s hermitage.

children.text: sā tu tārādhipamukhī rāvaṇena samīkṣya tam
children.translated_text: But she, whose face was like the lord of stars, seeing that king of vultures
struck down by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lamented in deep sorrow.
Omens, knowledge of signs, and observation of birds' cries
surely appear before men in times of happiness and sorrow.

children.text: na nūnaṃ rāma jānāsi mahad vyasanam ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Surely, O <s>Rāma</s>, you do not know of this great calamity of your own.
Surely, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, the deer and birds are running for my sake.

children.text: trāhi mām adya kākutstha lakṣmaṇeti varāṅganā
children.translated_text: "Save me today, O <s>Kākutstha</s>! O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>!" the beautiful woman
cried out in great terror, as if they were within hearing nearby.
As <s>Vaidehī</s>, her garlands and ornaments disheveled, lamented like one without a protector,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of rākṣasas, rushed toward her.

children.text: tāṃ latām iva veṣṭantīm āliṅgantīṃ mahādrumān
children.translated_text: As she twined herself around great trees and embraced them like a vine,
the lord of rākṣasas said again and again, "Let go, let go."

children.text: krośantīṃ rāma rāmeti rāmeṇa rahitāṃ vane
children.translated_text: As she cried, "<s>Rāma</s>, <s>Rāma</s>!" bereft of <s>Rāma</s> in the forest,
he, resembling Death, seized her by the hair, for the end of her life.
When <s>Vaidehī</s> was violated, the whole world, with moving and unmoving beings,
became lawless, covered by blind darkness.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā sītāṃ parāmṛṣṭāṃ dīnāṃ divyena cakṣuṣā
children.translated_text: Seeing poor <s>Sītā</s> touched by force, with his divine eye,

children.text: kṛtaṃ kāryam iti śrīmān vyājahāra pitāmahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the glorious <s>Pitāmaha</s> said, "The task is accomplished."

children.text: prahṛṣṭā vyathitāś cāsan sarve te paramarṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: All those great seers dwelling in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest were both delighted and distressed,
seeing <s>Sītā</s> touched by force.

children.text: sa tu tāṃ rāma rāmeti rudantīṃ lakṣmaṇeti ca
children.translated_text: But <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of rākṣasas, took her as she wept, crying "<s>Rāma</s>, <s>Rāma</s>!" and "<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>!",
and went into the sky.
The princess, whose whole body was adorned with glowing ornaments and who wore yellow silk garments,

children.text: rarāja rājaputrī tu vidyut saudāmanī yathā ||
children.translated_text: shone like flashing lightning.

children.text: uddhūtena ca vastreṇa tasyāḥ pītena rāvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: And because of her yellow garment streaming upward, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>
shone still more, like a mountain blazing with fire.
The reddish and fragrant lotus petals
of supremely beautiful <s>Vaidehī</s> were scattered over <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Her silk garment, streaming upward in the sky and gleaming like gold,
shone like a coppery cloud in the heat, reddened by the sun.

children.text: tasyās tad vimalaṃ vaktram ākāśe rāvaṇāṅkagam
children.translated_text: That spotless face of hers, resting in <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s lap in the sky,

children.text: na rarāja vinā rāmaṃ vinālam iva paṅkajam ||
children.translated_text: did not shine without <s>Rāma</s>, like a lotus without its stalk.

children.text: babhūva jaladaṃ nīlaṃ bhittvā candra ivoditaḥ
children.translated_text: It was like the moon rising after breaking through a dark cloud.
with a fine forehead and beautiful hairline, like the interior of a lotus, without blemish,
adorned with white, very spotless teeth, radiant and shining.
Though she had wept and wiped away her tears, it was lovely to behold, like the moon,
with a fine nose and charming copper-red lips, gleaming in the sky like gold.
That lovely face of hers, shaken by the lord of the rākṣasas,

children.text: śuśubhe na vinā rāmaṃ divā candra ivoditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: did not shine without <s>Rāma</s>, like the moon risen by day.
Golden in color, <s>Maithilī</s> shone beside the dark-limbed lord of the rākṣasas,

children.text: śuśubhe kāñcanī kāñcī nīlaṃ maṇim ivāśritā ||
children.translated_text: like a golden girdle resting upon a blue jewel.
Lotus-fair and gold-bright, <s>Sītā</s>, daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,
adorned with heated-gold ornaments, shone as if lightning had entered a cloud.
Through the sound of the ornaments of <s>Vaidehī</s>, the lord of the rākṣasas

children.text: babhūva vimalo nīlaḥ saghoṣa iva toyadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: became bright and dark, like a thundering raincloud.
From her noble head a shower of flowers fell on every side;
as <s>Sītā</s> was being carried away, it dropped to the surface of the earth.
But that shower of flowers, shaken on every side by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s speed,
turned back again toward <s>Daśagrīva</s>.
The stream of flowers turned back upon the younger brother of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>,
pure as a garland of stars upon lofty Mount <s>Meru</s>.
From <s>Vaidehī</s>'s foot an anklet, adorned with jewels, slipped loose;
resembling a circle of lightning, it fell with a sweet sound.
Red as fresh shoots, <s>Vaidehī</s> made the dark-limbed lord of the rākṣasas
shine like a golden girth upon an elephant.
Blazing with her own splendor like a great meteor in the sky,
the younger brother of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> carried <s>Sītā</s> away, entering the sky.
Those fire-colored ornaments of hers upon the earth
were scattered with a sound, like exhausted stars from the firmament.
The necklace fallen from between <s>Vaidehī</s>'s breasts, bright as the lord of stars,

children.text: vaidehyā nipatan bhāti gaṅgeva gaganāc cyutā ||
children.translated_text: shone as it fell, like the <s>Gaṅgā</s> fallen from the sky.
The trees, struck by an ominous wind and filled with flocks of many birds,

children.text: mā bhair iti vidhūtāgrā vyājahrur iva pādapāḥ ||
children.translated_text: with their tops shaken, seemed to say, "Do not be afraid."
The lotus ponds, their lotuses crushed and their fish and water-creatures terrified,

children.text: sakhīm iva gatotsāhāṃ śocantīva sma maithilīm ||
children.translated_text: seemed to grieve for <s>Maithilī</s>, like a friend whose spirit had gone.
Rushing in from every side, lions, tigers, deer, and birds
then ran after her in anger, following <s>Sītā</s>'s shadow.
With waterfalls as tearful faces and peaks as upraised arms,
the mountains seemed to cry out while <s>Sītā</s> was being carried away.

children.text: hriyamāṇāṃ tu vaidehīṃ dṛṣṭvā dīno divākaraḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Vaidehī</s> being carried off, the wretched sun,
glorious though he was, had his radiance shattered and became pale in disk.

children.text: nāsti dharmaḥ kutaḥ satyaṃ nārjavaṃ nānṛśaṃsatā
children.translated_text: "There is no <s>dharma</s> (righteous order); how can there be truth? There is no honesty, no compassion,

children.text: yatra rāmasya vaidehīṃ bhāryāṃ harati rāvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: where <s>Rāvaṇa</s> carries off <s>Vaidehī</s>, the wife of <s>Rāma</s>."
Thus all beings lamented in groups;
terrified, with downcast faces, even the young deer wept.
Looking upward again and again, their eyes clouded by falling tears,
and their bodies trembling greatly, the forest deities stood there.

children.text: vikrośantīṃ dṛḍhaṃ sītāṃ dṛṣṭvā duḥkhaṃ tathā gatām
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Sītā</s> crying out loudly and reduced to such grief,

children.text: tāṃ tu lakṣmaṇa rāmeti krośantīṃ madhurasvarām ||
children.translated_text: crying in a sweet voice, "<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>! <s>Rāma</s>!",
and seeing <s>Vaidehī</s> again and again looking down at the surface of the earth,
with the ends of her hair disheveled and her forehead-mark rubbed away,
<s>Daśagrīva</s> carried that spirited woman away, to his own destruction.

children.text: tatas tu sā cārudatī śucismitā vinākṛtā bandhujanena maithilī
children.translated_text: Then that charming-toothed, pure-smiling <s>Maithilī</s>, separated from her kinsmen,
not seeing either <s>Rāghava</s> or <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, was pale-faced and oppressed by the weight of fear.

children.text: kham utpatantaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā maithilī janakātmajā
children.translated_text: Seeing him flying up into the sky, <s>Maithilī</s>, daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,
was distressed, deeply agitated, and caught in great fear.
With eyes reddened by anger and weeping, she addressed the fierce-eyed lord of the rākṣasas;
as she was being carried away, <s>Sītā</s>, weeping piteously, said this:
"Are you not ashamed, base <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, of this deed,

children.text: jñātvā virahitāṃ yo māṃ corayitvā palāyase ||
children.translated_text: that, knowing me to be alone, you steal me and flee?

children.text: tvayaiva nūnaṃ duṣṭātman bhīruṇā hartum icchatā
children.translated_text: Surely, evil-souled coward, because you wished to carry me off,
my husband was led away by you through magic in the form of a deer,

children.text: yo hi mām udyatas trātuṃ so 'py ayaṃ vinipātitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and this one too, who rose up to protect me, has been struck down.

children.text: paramaṃ khalu te vīryaṃ dṛśyate rākṣasādhama
children.translated_text: Great indeed is the valor you display, lowest of rākṣasas,

children.text: viśrāvya nāmadheyaṃ hi yuddhe nāsti jitā tvayā ||
children.translated_text: for you have not won me in battle after proclaiming your name.

children.text: īdṛśaṃ garhitaṃ karma kathaṃ kṛtvā na lajjase
children.translated_text: How are you not ashamed after doing such a censured act,

children.text: striyāś ca haraṇaṃ nīca rahite ca parasya ca ||
children.translated_text: the carrying off of a woman, base one, one who is alone and belongs to another?
People in the worlds will tell of this contemptible deed,
very cruel and most unrighteous, of you who pride yourself on heroism.

children.text: dhik te śauryaṃ ca sattvaṃ ca yat tvayā kathitaṃ tadā
children.translated_text: Shame on your courage and strength, which you boasted of then;

children.text: kulākrośakaraṃ loke dhik te cāritram īdṛśam ||
children.translated_text: shame on such conduct of yours, bringing reproach upon your family in the world.

children.text: kiṃ śakyaṃ kartum evaṃ hi yaj javenaiva dhāvasi
children.translated_text: What can be done, since you simply run with speed?

children.text: muhūrtam api tiṣṭhasva na jīvan pratiyāsyasi ||
children.translated_text: Stand still even for a moment; you will not return alive.

children.text: na hi cakṣuḥpathaṃ prāpya tayoḥ pārthivaputrayoḥ
children.translated_text: For once you have come within sight of those two princes,

children.text: sasainyo 'pi samarthas tvaṃ muhūrtam api jīvitum ||
children.translated_text: even with an army you will not be able to live for even a moment.

children.text: na tvaṃ tayoḥ śarasparśaṃ soḍhuṃ śaktaḥ kathaṃcana
children.translated_text: You will never be able to endure the touch of their arrows,
any more than a bird can endure the touch of fire blazing in the forest.

children.text: sādhu kṛtvātmanaḥ pathyaṃ sādhu māṃ muñca rāvaṇa
children.translated_text: Do what is good and wholesome for yourself; do well and release me, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: matpradharṣaṇaruṣṭo hi bhrātrā saha patir mama
children.translated_text: For my husband, enraged by your assault upon me, together with his brother,

children.text: vidhāsyati vināśāya tvaṃ māṃ yadi na muñcasi ||
children.translated_text: will ordain your destruction, if you do not release me.

children.text: yena tvaṃ vyavasāyena balān māṃ hartum icchasi
children.translated_text: The purpose by which you wish to carry me off by force,

children.text: vyavasāyaḥ sa te nīca bhaviṣyati nirarthakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that purpose of yours, base man, will become fruitless.

children.text: na hy ahaṃ tam apaśyantī bhartāraṃ vibudhopamam
children.translated_text: For when I do not see that husband of mine, equal to the gods,
I shall not be able, while fallen under an enemy's power, to sustain my life for long.

children.text: na nūnaṃ cātmanaḥ śreyaḥ pathyaṃ vā samavekṣase
children.translated_text: Surely you do not consider your own welfare or what is wholesome,
as a mortal at the time of death pursues what is contrary to his good.

children.text: mumūrṣūṇāṃ hi sarveṣāṃ yat pathyaṃ tan na rocate
children.translated_text: For what is wholesome for all who are about to die does not please them;
indeed, I seem to see you caught about the neck in the noose of Time.

children.text: yathā cāsmin bhayasthāne na bibheṣi daśānana
children.translated_text: And since in this place of danger you feel no fear, O <s>Daśānana</s>,

children.text: vyaktaṃ hiraṇmayān hi tvaṃ saṃpaśyasi mahīruhān ||
children.translated_text: it is clear that you are seeing golden trees.
You see the terrible river <s>Vaitaraṇī</s>, carrying a flood of blood,
and also the dreadful forest whose leaves are swords, O <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
And you will see the sharp śālmalī tree, with flowers like heated gold and excellent beryl leaves,

children.text: drakṣyase śālmalīṃ tīkṣṇām āyasaiḥ kaṇṭakaiś citām ||
children.translated_text: covered with iron thorns.

children.text: na hi tvam īdṛśaṃ kṛtvā tasyālīkaṃ mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: For after doing such a false wrong against that great-souled one,

children.text: dharituṃ śakṣyasi ciraṃ viṣaṃ pītveva nirghṛṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: you will not be able to live long, cruel man, like one who has drunk poison.
You are bound, O <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, by the noose of Time, impossible to ward off;

children.text: kva gato lapsyase śarma bhartur mama mahātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: where will you go and obtain safety from my great-souled husband?
Without his brother, in battle, in the space of a mere blink,
he slew fourteen thousand rākṣasas.

children.text: sa kathaṃ rāghavo vīraḥ sarvāstrakuśalo balī
children.translated_text: How then would heroic <s>Rāghava</s>, powerful and skilled in every missile,

children.text: na tvāṃ hanyāc charais tīkṣṇair iṣṭabhāryāpahāriṇam ||
children.translated_text: not kill you with sharp arrows, you who have stolen his beloved wife?

children.text: etac cānyac ca paruṣaṃ vaidehī rāvaṇāṅkagā
children.translated_text: This and other harsh speech <s>Vaidehī</s>, seated on <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s lap,
overcome by fear and grief, lamented piteously.

children.text: tathā bhṛśārtāṃ bahu caiva bhāṣiṇīṃ vilalāpa pūrvaṃ karuṇaṃ ca bhāminīm
children.translated_text: In that way the wicked one carried off the young woman, the king's daughter, who was deeply distressed, speaking much, formerly lamenting piteously, fair and struggling,

children.text: jahāra pāpas taruṇīṃ viveṣṭatīṃ nṛpātmajām āgatagātravepathum ||
children.translated_text: her limbs trembling as she came into his grasp.

children.text: hriyamāṇā tu vaidehī kaṃcin nātham apaśyatī
children.translated_text: But as <s>Vaidehī</s> was being carried away, seeing no protector at all,
she saw five foremost vānaras standing on a mountain peak.
Among them the wide-eyed, fair-hipped <s>Maithilī</s> let fall
her silk upper garment, shining like gold, and her auspicious ornaments,

children.text: mumoca yadi rāmāya śaṃseyur iti maithilī ||
children.translated_text: thinking, 'Perhaps they will report this to <s>Rāma</s>.'
After she had cast off the garment, placed among them together with the ornaments,

children.text: sambhramāt tu daśagrīvas tat karma na ca buddhavān ||
children.translated_text: <s>Daśagrīva</s>, in his agitation, did not notice that act.

children.text: piṅgākṣās tāṃ viśālākṣīṃ netrair animiṣair iva
children.translated_text: The tawny-eyed bulls among the vānaras saw with unblinking eyes
wide-eyed <s>Sītā</s> then crying out.

children.text: sa ca pampām atikramya laṅkām abhimukhaḥ purīm
children.translated_text: And the lord of rākṣasas, having passed beyond <s>Pampā</s> and facing the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>,
went on, holding the weeping <s>Maithilī</s>.

children.text: tāṃ jahāra susaṃhṛṣṭo rāvaṇo mṛtyum ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Exultant, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> carried her off as his own death,
like a serpentess in his lap, sharp-fanged and full of deadly poison.

children.text: vanāni saritaḥ śailān sarāṃsi ca vihāyasā
children.translated_text: Through the sky he quickly passed over forests, rivers, mountains,

children.text: sa kṣipraṃ samatīyāya śaraś cāpād iva cyutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and lakes, like an arrow released from a bow.
Then, reaching the inexhaustible abode of <s>Varuṇa</s>, haunt of timingilas and makaras,
the refuge of rivers, he crossed the ocean.
As <s>Vaidehī</s> was being carried away, the abode of <s>Varuṇa</s> became agitated, its waves turning about,
its fish and great serpents obstructed.
Then the Cāraṇas, moving in the sky, uttered words,
and the Siddhas then said, 'This is the end of <s>Daśagrīva</s>.'

children.text: sa tu sītāṃ viveṣṭantīm aṅkenādāya rāvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, taking struggling <s>Sītā</s> on his lap,

children.text: praviveśa purīṃ laṅkāṃ rūpiṇīṃ mṛtyum ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: entered the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>, death for himself in embodied form.
Having reached the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>, with its great avenues well laid out,
he entered his own inner palace, crowded with many enclosed chambers.
There <s>Rāvaṇa</s> placed <s>Sītā</s>, dark at the corners of her eyes and given over to grief and bewilderment,

children.text: nidadhe rāvaṇaḥ sītāṃ mayo māyām ivāsurīm ||
children.translated_text: as <s>Maya</s> might place an asuric illusion.
And <s>Daśagrīva</s> spoke to the piśācī women of dreadful appearance,

children.text: yathā naināṃ pumān strī vā sītāṃ paśyaty asaṃmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: saying, 'Let no man or woman see this <s>Sītā</s> without my consent.
Pearls, gems, gold, garments, and ornaments,

children.text: yad yad icchet tad evāsyā deyaṃ macchandato yathā ||
children.translated_text: whatever she may desire, let exactly that be given to her, according to my command.

children.text: yā ca vakṣyati vaidehīṃ vacanaṃ kiṃcid apriyam
children.translated_text: And any woman who says even one unpleasant word to <s>Vaidehī</s>,

children.text: ajñānād yadi vā jñānān na tasyā jīvitaṃ priyam ||
children.translated_text: whether from ignorance or knowingly, will not hold her life dear.'

children.text: tathoktvā rākṣasīs tās tu rākṣasendraḥ pratāpavān
children.translated_text: Having thus addressed those rākṣasīs, the mighty lord of rākṣasas,

children.text: niṣkramyāntaḥpurāt tasmāt kiṃ kṛtyam iti cintayan
children.translated_text: leaving that inner palace and thinking, 'What is to be done?',
saw eight rākṣasas of great valor, eaters of flesh.

children.text: sa tān dṛṣṭvā mahāvīryo varadānena mohitaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing them, he of great valor, deluded by the boon he had received,
spoke this speech to them, praising their strength and courage:
'With many kinds of weapons, go quickly from here, swiftly,
to <s>Janasthāna</s>, the place of slaughter, formerly the dwelling of <s>Khara</s>.
Stay there in <s>Janasthāna</s>, empty now and with its rākṣasas slain,

children.text: pauruṣaṃ balam āśritya trāsam utsṛjya dūrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: relying on your manliness and strength, casting fear far away.

children.text: balaṃ hi sumahad yan me janasthāne niveśitam
children.translated_text: For that very great force of mine which was stationed in <s>Janasthāna</s>,
together with <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> and <s>Khara</s>, was slain in battle by <s>Rāma</s>'s arrows.
Therefore an unprecedented anger in me grows above my firmness,

children.text: vairaṃ ca sumahajjātaṃ rāmaṃ prati sudāruṇam ||
children.translated_text: and a very great and exceedingly terrible enmity toward <s>Rāma</s> has arisen.

children.text: niryātayitum icchāmi tac ca vairam ahaṃ ripoḥ
children.translated_text: I wish to pay back that enmity against my foe,

children.text: na hi lapsyāmy ahaṃ nidrām ahatvā saṃyuge ripum ||
children.translated_text: for I shall not obtain sleep without killing my enemy in battle.'

children.text: taṃ tv idānīm ahaṃ hatvā kharadūṣaṇaghātinam
children.translated_text: But now, after killing that <s>Rāma</s>, the slayer of <s>Khara</s> and <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>,
I shall obtain happiness, like a penniless man after gaining wealth.

children.text: janasthāne vasadbhis tu bhavadbhī rāmam āśritā
children.translated_text: While you dwell in <s>Janasthāna</s> and keep watch on <s>Rāma</s>,
news must be brought truthfully: what is he doing?

children.text: apramādāc ca gantavyaṃ sarvair eva niśācaraiḥ
children.translated_text: And all you night-roamers must go with vigilance;

children.text: kartavyaś ca sadā yatno rāghavasya vadhaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: constant effort must be made toward the killing of <s>Rāghava</s>.
For I know your strength, many times over, on the front of battle;

children.text: ataś cāsmiñ janasthāne mayā yūyaṃ niyojitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore I have stationed you here in <s>Janasthāna</s>.

children.text: tataḥ priyaṃ vākyam upetya rākṣasā mahārtham aṣṭāv abhivādya rāvaṇam
children.translated_text: Then the eight rākṣasas accepted the welcome, weighty command and saluted <s>Rāvaṇa</s>;

children.text: vihāya laṅkāṃ sahitāḥ pratasthire yato janasthānam alakṣyadarśanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: leaving <s>Laṅkā</s> together, they set out for <s>Janasthāna</s>, invisible in appearance.

children.text: tatas tu sītām upalabhya rāvaṇaḥ susamprahṛṣṭaḥ parigṛhya maithilīm
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, having obtained <s>Sītā</s>, was greatly delighted and took hold of <s>Maithilī</s>;

children.text: prasajya rāmeṇa ca vairam uttamaṃ babhūva mohān muditaḥ sa rākṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, having deliberately made supreme enmity with <s>Rāma</s>, that rākṣasa became joyful through delusion.
Having instructed the eight dreadful rākṣasas of great strength,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, through failure of judgment, thought himself to have accomplished his aim.
Thinking of <s>Vaidehī</s>, pierced by the arrows of desire,

children.text: praviveśa gṛhaṃ ramyaṃ sītāṃ draṣṭum abhitvaran ||
children.translated_text: he entered his beautiful house, hurrying to see <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: sa praviśya tu tadveśma rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: And having entered that mansion, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas,
saw <s>Sītā</s> among the rākṣasī women, wholly given over to grief.
Her face was filled with tears, she was wretched, crushed by the burden of sorrow,
like a boat sinking in the ocean, battered by blasts of wind.
She was like a doe fallen away from the herd of deer and surrounded by dogs;
and the night-roamer approached her, downcast-faced and miserable.

children.text: tāṃ tu śokavaśāṃ dīnām avaśāṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the lord of the rākṣasas, to that helpless, miserable woman under the power of grief,
showed by force a house resembling the house of the gods.
It was crowded with mansions and palaces and served by thousands of women,
frequented by flocks of many kinds of birds and furnished with many kinds of jewels.

children.text: kāñcanais tāpanīyaiś ca sphāṭikai rājatais tathā
children.translated_text: With golden, refined-gold, crystal, and silver,
and with pillars variegated by diamonds and vaiḍūrya gems, charming to the eye,
resounding with divine kettledrums and having gateways of heated gold,

children.text: sopānaṃ kāñcanaṃ citram āruroha tayā saha ||
children.translated_text: he mounted a bright golden staircase together with her.
Ivory and silver windows, pleasing to behold,
and rows of palaces covered with golden latticework were there.
Floor-spaces everywhere were variegated with white plaster and jewels;
in his own palace the ten-necked one showed them to <s>Maithilī</s>.
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> showed long pools and lotus-ponds covered with various flowers
to <s>Sītā</s>, who was wholly given over to grief.

children.text: darśayitvā tu vaidehīṃ kṛtsnaṃ tad bhavanottamam
children.translated_text: And after showing <s>Vaidehī</s> that entire excellent palace,
the evil-minded <s>Rāvaṇa</s> spoke these words to the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>:
There are ten crores of rākṣasas, and twenty-two more besides,
apart from the old, the aged, and the young night-roamers.

children.text: teṣāṃ prabhur ahaṃ sīte sarveṣāṃ bhīmakarmaṇām
children.translated_text: I am the lord of all those dreadful workers, <s>Sītā</s>;
for each one, a thousand stand before me for my business.

children.text: yad idaṃ rājyatantraṃ me tvayi sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam
children.translated_text: This whole machinery of my kingdom is established upon you;

children.text: jīvitaṃ ca viśālākṣi tvaṃ me prāṇair garīyasī ||
children.translated_text: and my life too, wide-eyed one: you are dearer to me than my vital breaths.
That multitude of many thousands of women who are my wives,

children.text: tāsāṃ tvam īśvarī sīte mama bhāryā bhava priye ||
children.translated_text: be their mistress, <s>Sītā</s>; become my wife, dear one.

children.text: sādhu kiṃ te 'nyayā buddhyā rocayasva vaco mama
children.translated_text: Come now, what use have you for any other thought? Be pleased with my words.
Love me, who am tormented; you ought to show me favor.
This <s>Laṅkā</s>, a hundred yojanas across, is encircled by the ocean;

children.text: neyaṃ dharṣayituṃ śakyā sendrair api surāsuraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: it cannot be assaulted even by the gods and asuras together with <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: na deveṣu na yakṣeṣu na gandharveṣu narṣiṣu
children.translated_text: Among gods, yakṣas, gandharvas, or human sages,

children.text: ahaṃ paśyāmi lokeṣu yo me vīryasamo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: I see no one in the worlds who could be equal to my valor.
What will you do with <s>Rāma</s>, kingdomless, miserable, an ascetic, his life nearly spent,
a human being of little brilliance?

children.text: bhajasva sīte mām eva bhartāhaṃ sadṛśas tava
children.translated_text: Choose me alone, <s>Sītā</s>; I am a husband suited to you.

children.text: yauvanaṃ hy adhruvaṃ bhīru ramasveha mayā saha ||
children.translated_text: For youth is impermanent, timid one; enjoy yourself here with me.

children.text: darśane mā kṛthā buddhiṃ rāghavasya varānane
children.translated_text: Do not set your mind on seeing <s>Rāghava</s>, beautiful-faced one;

children.text: kāsya śaktir ihāgantum api sīte manorathaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: who has the power to come here, <s>Sītā</s>, even in imagination?

children.text: na śakyo vāyur ākāśe pāśair baddhaṃ mahājavaḥ
children.translated_text: The swift wind cannot be bound with snares in the sky,

children.text: dīpyamānasya vāpy agner grahītuṃ vimalāṃ śikhām ||
children.translated_text: nor can the spotless flame of blazing fire be grasped.

children.text: trayāṇām api lokānāṃ na taṃ paśyāmi śobhane
children.translated_text: In all the three worlds I do not see the one, lovely woman,
who by valor could take you away while you are protected by my arms.

children.text: laṅkāyāṃ sumahad rājyam idaṃ tvam anupālaya
children.translated_text: Rule this very great kingdom in <s>Laṅkā</s>;
drenched with consecration water and pleased, delight me.

children.text: duṣkṛtaṃ yat purā karma vanavāsena tad gatam
children.translated_text: Whatever evil deed there was formerly has been exhausted by forest-dwelling;

children.text: yaś ca te sukṛto dharmas tasyeha phalam āpnuhi ||
children.translated_text: and whatever dharma you have well performed, enjoy its fruit here.
Here are all garlands and divine fragrances, <s>Maithilī</s>,

children.text: bhūṣaṇāni ca mukhyāni tāni seva mayā saha ||
children.translated_text: and the finest ornaments; enjoy them with me.

children.text: puṣpakaṃ nāma suśroṇi bhrātur vaiśravaṇasya me
children.translated_text: Lovely-hipped one, the delightful aerial car named <s>Puṣpaka</s> belonged to my brother <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>;

children.text: vimānaṃ ramaṇīyaṃ ca tad vimānaṃ manojavam ||
children.translated_text: that aerial car moves at the speed of thought.

children.text: tatra sīte mayā sārdhaṃ viharasva yathāsukham
children.translated_text: There, <s>Sītā</s>, roam as you please together with me.
Your face, like a lotus, spotless and lovely to behold,

children.text: śokārtaṃ tu varārohe na bhrājati varānane
children.translated_text: does not shine while grief-stricken, fair-hipped, beautiful-faced one.
Enough of this bashfulness, <s>Vaidehī</s>, caused for you by a breach of dharma.
This is a destined current, sanctioned by the seers, which will come upon you.

children.text: etau pādau mayā snigdhau śirobhiḥ paripīḍitau ||
children.translated_text: These two feet of yours have been affectionately pressed by me with my heads.

children.text: prasādaṃ kuru me kṣipraṃ vaśyo dāso 'ham asmi te
children.translated_text: Show me favor quickly; I am submissive, your slave.

children.text: nemāḥ śūnyā mayā vācaḥ śuṣyamāṇena bhāṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These words of mine are not empty, spoken by me as I waste away.

children.text: na cāpi rāvaṇaḥ kāṃcin mūrdhnā strīṃ praṇameta ha
children.translated_text: Nor indeed would <s>Rāvaṇa</s> bow his head to any woman.
Having spoken thus to <s>Maithilī</s>, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, the ten-necked one,
fallen under the power of death, thought, 'She is mine.'

children.text: sā tathoktā tu vaidehī nirbhayā śokakarṣitā
children.translated_text: But <s>Vaidehī</s>, addressed in that way, fearless though worn down by grief,
placed a blade of grass between them and replied to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>:
There was a king named <s>Daśaratha</s>, firm as a bridge of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),

children.text: satyasaṃdhaḥ parijñāto yasya putraḥ sa rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: known as true to his promise; his son is that <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: rāmo nāma sa dharmātmā triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ
children.translated_text: That righteous-souled one, named <s>Rāma</s>, is renowned in the three worlds.

children.text: dīrghabāhur viśālākṣo daivataṃ sa patir mama ||
children.translated_text: Long-armed and broad-eyed, he, a divine being, is my husband.
Born in the line of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s>, lion-shouldered and greatly radiant,

children.text: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā yas te prāṇān hariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: together with his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, he will take your life.

children.text: pratyakṣaṃ yady ahaṃ tasya tvayā syāṃ dharṣitā balāt
children.translated_text: If I were violated by you by force in his very presence,

children.text: śayitā tvaṃ hataḥ saṃkhye janasthāne yathā kharaḥ ||
children.translated_text: you would lie slain in battle, as <s>Khara</s> did at <s>Janasthāna</s>.

children.text: ya ete rākṣasāḥ proktā ghorarūpā mahābalāḥ
children.translated_text: Those rākṣasas you have mentioned, terrible in form and very strong,

children.text: rāghave nirviṣāḥ sarve suparṇe pannagā yathā ||
children.translated_text: will all be without venom before <s>Rāghava</s>, like serpents before <s>Suparṇa</s>.
His arrows, released from the bowstring and adorned with gold,
will tear your body apart like waves tearing the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

children.text: asurair vā surair vā tvaṃ yady avadho 'si rāvaṇa
children.translated_text: Even if you are unslayable by asuras or by gods, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: utpādya sumahad vairaṃ jīvaṃs tasya na mokṣyase ||
children.translated_text: having raised such great enmity, you will not escape him while alive.
Powerful <s>Rāghava</s> will be the ender of what remains of your life.
Like an animal brought to the sacrificial post, your life will be hard to preserve.

children.text: yadi paśyet sa rāmas tvāṃ roṣadīptena cakṣuṣā
children.translated_text: If that <s>Rāma</s> should look at you with an eye blazing in anger,

children.text: rakṣas tvam adya nirdagdho gaccheḥ sadyaḥ parābhavam ||
children.translated_text: rākṣasa, burned up today, you would at once come to ruin.

children.text: yaś candraṃ nabhaso bhūmau pātayen nāśayeta vā
children.translated_text: The one who could cast the moon from the sky to the earth, or destroy it,

children.text: sāgaraṃ śoṣayed vāpi sa sītāṃ mocayed iha ||
children.translated_text: or dry up the ocean, could free <s>Sītā</s> here.
Your life is spent, your splendor gone, your strength gone, your senses gone.
<s>Laṅkā</s>, through your deed, will be filled with widowhood.

children.text: na te pāpam idaṃ karma sukhodarkaṃ bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: This sinful deed of yours will not end in happiness for you,

children.text: yāhaṃ nītā vinā bhāvaṃ patipārśvāt tvayā vanāt ||
children.translated_text: that I was carried off by you from the forest, against my will, from my husband's side.

children.text: sa hi daivatasaṃyukto mama bhartā mahādyutiḥ
children.translated_text: For my husband, greatly radiant and joined with divine power,

children.text: nirbhayo vīryam āśritya śūnye vasati daṇḍake ||
children.translated_text: fearless and relying on his valor, dwells in the desolate <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest.

children.text: sa te darpaṃ balaṃ vīryam utsekaṃ ca tathāvidham
children.translated_text: In battle he will strip from your limbs your pride, strength, valor,
and arrogance of that kind, by a shower of arrows.
When the destruction of beings is seen, driven on by time,

children.text: tadā kārye pramādyanti narāḥ kālavaśaṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: then men who have come under the power of time act heedlessly in what must be done.

children.text: māṃ pradhṛṣya sa te kālaḥ prāpto 'yaṃ rākṣasādhama
children.translated_text: By assaulting me, that time of yours has now arrived, lowest of rākṣasas,
for the killing of yourself, of the rākṣasas, and of your inner palace.
An altar standing in the midst of a sacrifice, adorned with ladles and vessels,
purified by the mantras of twice-born priests, cannot be trampled by a caṇḍāla.

children.text: idaṃ śarīraṃ niḥsaṃjñaṃ bandha vā ghātayasva vā
children.translated_text: This body is senseless; bind it or kill it.

children.text: nedaṃ śarīraṃ rakṣyaṃ me jīvitaṃ vāpi rākṣasa
children.translated_text: This body is not something I must protect, nor even life itself, rākṣasa,

children.text: na hi śakṣyāmy upakrośaṃ pṛthivyāṃ dātum ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for I cannot bring reproach upon myself on earth.

children.text: evam uktvā tu vaidehī krodhāt suparuṣaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken very harsh words from anger, <s>Vaidehī</s>,

children.text: rāvaṇaṃ maithilī tatra punar novāca kiṃcana ||
children.translated_text: <s>Maithilī</s>, said nothing more there to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Hearing <s>Sītā</s>'s harsh, hair-raising speech,
he then answered <s>Sītā</s> with words meant to show her fear:

children.text: śṛṇu maithili madvākyaṃ māsān dvādaśa bhāmini
children.translated_text: Listen to my words, <s>Maithilī</s>: twelve months, beautiful woman.
If within this time you do not come to me, lovely-smiling one,

children.text: tatas tvāṃ prātarāśārthaṃ sūdāś chetsyanti leśaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then the cooks will cut you into pieces for my morning meal.

children.text: ity uktvā paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ rāvaṇaḥ śatrurāvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken these harsh words, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, who makes his enemies cry out,

children.text: rākṣasīś ca tataḥ kruddha idaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: then, angry, said these words to the rākṣasīs:

children.text: śīghram evaṃ hi rākṣasyo vikṛtā ghoradarśanāḥ
children.translated_text: Quickly, rākṣasīs, deformed and terrible to behold,
you eaters of flesh and blood, remove her pride in this way.

children.text: vacanād eva tās tasya vikṛtā ghoradarśanāḥ
children.translated_text: At his very command, those deformed ones, terrible to behold,
folded their hands and surrounded <s>Maithilī</s>.

children.text: sa tāḥ provāca rājā tu rāvaṇo ghoradarśanaḥ
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, terrible to behold, spoke to them,
shaking the earth with the lifting and stamping of his feet, as if tearing it apart:
Let <s>Maithilī</s> be taken into the middle of the <s>Aśoka</s> grove.
There let her be guarded secretly, surrounded by you.

children.text: tatraināṃ tarjanair ghoraiḥ punaḥ sāntvaiś ca maithilīm
children.translated_text: There, with terrible threats and then again with conciliatory words,

children.text: ānayadhvaṃ vaśaṃ sarvā vanyāṃ gajavadhūm iva ||
children.translated_text: bring this <s>Maithilī</s> under control, all of you, like a wild cow-elephant.
Thus commanded by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, those rākṣasīs
went to the <s>Aśoka</s> grove, taking that <s>Maithilī</s> with them.
It was surrounded by trees yielding the fruits of every desire, and by trees with many kinds of flowers and fruits,
and it was frequented by birds intoxicated in every season.
But <s>Maithilī</s>, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, her body overcome by grief,
fell under the power of the rākṣasīs like a doe among tigresses.

children.text: na vindate tatra tu śarma maithilī virūpanetrābhir atīva tarjitā
children.translated_text: There <s>Maithilī</s> found no peace, fiercely threatened by women with deformed eyes.

children.text: patiṃ smarantī dayitaṃ ca devaraṃ vicetanābhūd bhayaśokapīḍitā ||
children.translated_text: Remembering her husband and her beloved brother-in-law, she became senseless, afflicted by fear and grief.
Having killed <s>Mārīca</s>, the rākṣasa who roamed in the form of a deer and could assume any shape,

children.text: nihatya rāmo mārīcaṃ tūrṇaṃ pathi nyavartata ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> quickly turned back along the path.
As he was hurrying, eager to see <s>Maithilī</s>,
Then a jackal with a harsh cry howled behind him.

children.text: sa tasya svaram ājñāya dāruṇaṃ romaharṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Recognizing its sound, dreadful and making the hairs stand on end,
he began to think, made apprehensive by the jackal's cry:

children.text: aśubhaṃ bata manye 'haṃ gomāyur vāśyate yathā
children.translated_text: "Alas, I think this is inauspicious, the way the jackal cries.

children.text: svasti syād api vaidehyā rākṣasair bhakṣaṇaṃ vinā ||
children.translated_text: May there be safety for <s>Vaidehī</s>, without her being devoured by rākṣasas.

children.text: mārīcena tu vijñāya svaram ālakṣya māmakam
children.translated_text: But if <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, knowing and recognizing my voice
cried out by <s>Mārīca</s> in the form of a deer, should hear it,

children.text: sa saumitriḥ svaraṃ śrutvā tāṃ ca hitvātha maithilīm
children.translated_text: that son of <s>Sumitrā</s>, having heard the voice and then leaving <s>Maithilī</s>,
sent by her herself, will quickly come here to my side.

children.text: rākṣasaiḥ sahitair nūnaṃ sītāyā īpsito vadhaḥ
children.translated_text: Surely the killing of <s>Sītā</s> is desired by the rākṣasas gathered together;

children.text: kāñcanaś ca mṛgo bhūtvā vyapanīyāśramāt tu mām ||
children.translated_text: and becoming a golden deer, they removed me from the hermitage.

children.text: dūraṃ nītvā tu mārīco rākṣaso 'bhūc charāhataḥ
children.translated_text: After leading me far away, <s>Mārīca</s>, the rākṣasa, struck by my arrow,

children.text: hā lakṣmaṇa hato 'smīti yad vākyaṃ vyājahāra ha ||
children.translated_text: uttered the words, 'Ah, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, I am slain!'

children.text: api svasti bhaved dvābhyāṃ rahitābhyāṃ mayā vane
children.translated_text: May there be safety for the two who are left without me in the forest.
For because of <s>Janasthāna</s> I have made enmity with the rākṣasas,

children.text: nimittāni ca ghorāṇi dṛśyante 'dya bahūni ca ||
children.translated_text: and today many terrible omens are being seen."

children.text: ity evaṃ cintayan rāmaḥ śrutvā gomāyuniḥsvanam
children.translated_text: Thinking thus, <s>Rāma</s>, having heard the jackal's cry,
and realizing that he had been drawn away by the rākṣasa in the form of a deer,
<s>Rāghava</s>, full of apprehension, came back to <s>Janasthāna</s>.
Animals and birds approached that great-souled one, whose mind was dejected and who was wretched,

children.text: savyaṃ kṛtvā mahātmānaṃ ghorāṃś ca sasṛjuḥ svarān ||
children.translated_text: keeping him on their left and uttering terrible cries.
Seeing those extremely dreadful omens, <s>Rāghava</s>
then saw <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> approaching, his brightness gone.
Then, not far away, that <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> met <s>Rāma</s>,
despondent with the despondent one, distressed with the one who shared his grief.

children.text: saṃjagarhe 'tha taṃ bhrātā jyeṣṭho lakṣmaṇam āgatam
children.translated_text: Then his elder brother reproached <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> when he had come,
after leaving <s>Sītā</s> in the deserted forest frequented by rākṣasas.

children.text: gṛhītvā ca karaṃ savyaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ raghunandanaḥ
children.translated_text: Taking <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s left hand, the delight of the <s>Raghu</s> line
spoke these harsh words, pained though sweet in their outcome:

children.text: aho lakṣmaṇa garhyaṃ te kṛtaṃ yat tvaṃ vihāya tām
children.translated_text: "Ah, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, what you have done is blameworthy, since, leaving her,

children.text: sītām ihāgataḥ saumya kaccit svasti bhaved iti ||
children.translated_text: leaving <s>Sītā</s>, you have come here, gentle one. I wonder whether there can be safety.

children.text: na me 'sti saṃśayo vīra sarvathā janakātmajā
children.translated_text: I have no doubt, hero: in every way the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>
has either perished or been devoured by rākṣasas who roam the forest.

children.text: aśubhāny eva bhūyiṣṭhaṃ yathā prādurbhavanti me
children.translated_text: Since mostly inauspicious signs are appearing to me,
may we, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, still find <s>Sītā</s> unharmed.

children.text: idaṃ hi rakṣo mṛgasaṃnikāśaṃ pralobhya māṃ dūram anuprayātam
children.translated_text: For this rākṣasa, resembling a deer, lured me and led me far away;

children.text: hataṃ kathaṃcin mahatā śrameṇa sa rākṣaso 'bhūn mriyamāṇa eva ||
children.translated_text: slain somehow with great effort, that rākṣasa became himself as he was dying.

children.text: manaś ca me dīnam ihāprahṛṣṭaṃ cakṣuś ca savyaṃ kurute vikāram
children.translated_text: My mind here is dejected and not joyful, and my left eye twitches.

children.text: asaṃśayaṃ lakṣmaṇa nāsti sītā hṛtā mṛtā vā pathi vartate vā ||
children.translated_text: Without doubt, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, <s>Sītā</s> is gone: she has been carried off, or is dead, or lies somewhere on the path.

children.text: sa dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇaṃ dīnaṃ śūnye daśarathātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> dejected and the place empty, the son of <s>Daśaratha</s>,
the righteous one, questioned him, since he had come without <s>Vaidehī</s>:

children.text: prasthitaṃ daṇḍakāraṇyaṃ yā mām anujagāma ha
children.translated_text: She who followed me when I set out for the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest,

children.text: kva sā lakṣmaṇa vaidehī yāṃ hitvā tvam ihāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: where is that <s>Vaidehī</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, whom you left and came here?
As I am fallen from my kingdom, miserable, wandering through the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> woods,

children.text: kva sā duḥkhasahāyā me vaidehī tanumadhyamā ||
children.translated_text: where is that slender-waisted <s>Vaidehī</s>, the companion of my sorrow?

children.text: yāṃ vinā notsahe vīra muhūrtam api jīvitum
children.translated_text: Without whom, hero, I cannot bear to live even for a moment,

children.text: kva sā prāṇasahāyā me sītā surasutopamā ||
children.translated_text: where is that <s>Sītā</s>, companion of my life-breaths, like a daughter of the gods?

children.text: patitvam amarāṇāṃ vā pṛthivyāś cāpi lakṣmaṇa
children.translated_text: Kingship over the immortals, or even over the earth, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
I would not desire without that daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, shining like gold.

children.text: kaccij jīvati vaidehī prāṇaiḥ priyatarā mama
children.translated_text: Is <s>Vaidehī</s> alive, she who is dearer to me than my life-breaths?

children.text: kaccit pravrājanaṃ saumya na me mithyā bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Gentle one, surely my exile will not become fruitless?

children.text: sītānimittaṃ saumitre mṛte mayi gate tvayi
children.translated_text: When I am dead on account of <s>Sītā</s>, and you too are gone, son of <s>Sumitrā</s>,

children.text: kaccit sakāmā sukhitā kaikeyī sā bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: will that <s>Kaikeyī</s> then be satisfied in her desire and happy?
Will poor <s>Kausalyā</s>, her son dead, attend upon <s>Kaikeyī</s>,

children.text: upasthāsyati kausalyā kaccit saumya na kaikayīm ||
children.translated_text: who has obtained her aim and has a kingdom for her son, gentle one?

children.text: yadi jīvati vaidehī gamiṣyāmy āśramaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: If <s>Vaidehī</s> is alive, I will go back to the hermitage.

children.text: suvṛttā yadi vṛttā sā prāṇāṃs tyakṣyāmi lakṣmaṇa ||
children.translated_text: If that well-conducted woman has died, I shall abandon my life-breaths, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
If <s>Vaidehī</s> does not speak to me when I have reached the hermitage,
if <s>Sītā</s> is not again smiling, I shall perish, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: brūhi lakṣmaṇa vaidehī yadi jīvati vā na vā
children.translated_text: Tell me, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, whether <s>Vaidehī</s> is alive or not,

children.text: tvayi pramatte rakṣobhir bhakṣitā vā tapasvinī ||
children.translated_text: or whether, through your negligence, that poor ascetic woman has been devoured by rākṣasas.

children.text: sukumārī ca bālā ca nityaṃ cāduḥkhadarśinī
children.translated_text: Tender, young, and always unacquainted with suffering,
<s>Vaidehī</s>, separated from me, is plainly grieving, downcast in mind.
In every way, by that crooked and very wicked rākṣasa,

children.text: vadatā lakṣmaṇety uccais tavāpi janitaṃ bhayam ||
children.translated_text: who loudly cried '<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>!', fear was produced in you too.

children.text: śrutaś ca śaṅke vaidehyā sa svaraḥ sadṛśo mama
children.translated_text: And I think that <s>Vaidehī</s> heard that voice resembling mine;

children.text: trastayā preṣitas tvaṃ ca draṣṭuṃ māṃ śīghram āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: you were sent by her in terror and have come quickly to see me.

children.text: sarvathā tu kṛtaṃ kaṣṭaṃ sītām utsṛjatā vane
children.translated_text: But in every way a grievous thing has been done by abandoning <s>Sītā</s> in the forest.
An opportunity has been given to the cruel rākṣasas to strike back.
The flesh-eating rākṣasas, distressed by the killing of <s>Khara</s>,

children.text: taiḥ sītā nihatā ghorair bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: will undoubtedly have slain <s>Sītā</s>, those dreadful ones.
Ah, I am sunk in calamity in every way, destroyer of foes.

children.text: kiṃ tv idānīṃ kariṣyāmi śaṅke prāptavyam īdṛśam ||
children.translated_text: What shall I do now? I fear that such a fate had to befall me."

children.text: iti sītāṃ varārohāṃ cintayann eva rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Rāghava</s> kept thinking of lovely-hipped <s>Sītā</s>.
He came swiftly to <s>Janāsthāna</s>, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: vigarhamāṇo 'nujam ārtarūpaṃ kṣudhā śramāc caiva pipāsayā ca
children.translated_text: Reproaching his younger brother, distressed in appearance because of hunger, weariness, and thirst,

children.text: viniḥśvasañ śuṣkamukho viṣaṇṇaḥ pratiśrayaṃ prāpya samīkṣya śūnyam ||
children.translated_text: sighing, dry-mouthed, and dejected, he reached the shelter and saw that it was empty.

children.text: svam āśramaṃ saṃpravigāhya vīro vihāradeśān anusṛtya kāṃścit
children.translated_text: The hero entered his own hermitage and followed some of the places of recreation;

children.text: etat tad ity eva nivāsabhūmau prahṛṣṭaromā vyathito babhūva ||
children.translated_text: saying, "This is that place," on the ground where they had dwelt, he became horrified, his hair standing on end.
Then, when he had turned back from the hermitage, the delight of the <s>Raghus</s>
<s>Rāma</s>, afflicted by grief, again questioned <s>Saumitri</s>:

children.text: tam uvāca kimarthaṃ tvam āgato 'pāsya maithilīm
children.translated_text: He said to him, "Why have you come, abandoning <s>Maithilī</s>,

children.text: yadā sā tava viśvāsād vane virahitā mayā ||
children.translated_text: when she had been left alone by me in the forest in reliance upon you?

children.text: dṛṣṭvaivābhyāgataṃ tvāṃ me maithilīṃ tyajya lakṣmaṇa
children.translated_text: Seeing you arrived here after leaving <s>Maithilī</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: śaṅkamānaṃ mahat pāpaṃ yat satyaṃ vyathitaṃ manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: my mind, truly troubled, suspects some great evil.

children.text: sphurate nayanaṃ savyaṃ bāhuś ca hṛdayaṃ ca me
children.translated_text: My left eye, my arm, and my heart are throbbing,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇa dūre tvāṃ sītāvirahitaṃ pathi ||
children.translated_text: as I see you, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, far off on the road, without <s>Sītā</s>."

children.text: evam uktas tu saumitrir lakṣmaṇaḥ śubhalakṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Saumitri</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> of auspicious marks,
again overwhelmed by grief, spoke to the grieving <s>Rāma</s>:

children.text: na svayaṃ kāmakāreṇa tāṃ tyaktvāham ihāgataḥ
children.translated_text: "I have not come here by my own will after abandoning her;
urged by her alone with harsh words, I have come here to your presence.

children.text: āryeṇeva parikruṣṭaṃ hā sīte lakṣmaṇeti ca
children.translated_text: A cry seemed to be shouted by you, noble one: 'Ah, <s>Sītā</s>! <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>!'

children.text: paritrāhīti yad vākyaṃ maithilyās tac chrutiṃ gatam ||
children.translated_text: and the words 'Save me!' reached the hearing of <s>Maithilī</s>.

children.text: sā tam ārtasvaraṃ śrutvā tava snehena maithilī
children.translated_text: Hearing that distressed voice, <s>Maithilī</s>, out of love for you,

children.text: gaccha gaccheti mām āha rudantī bhayavihvalā ||
children.translated_text: said to me, 'Go, go,' weeping and bewildered by fear.
When she repeatedly urged me, saying 'Go,'
I answered <s>Maithilī</s> with these words, filled with confidence in you:

children.text: na tat paśyāmy ahaṃ rakṣo yad asya bhayam āvahet
children.translated_text: 'I do not see any <s>rākṣasa</s> who could bring danger upon him.

children.text: nirvṛtā bhava nāsty etat kenāpy evam udāhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Be at ease. This is not so; someone else has uttered this.

children.text: vigarhitaṃ ca nīcaṃ ca katham āryo 'bhidhāsyati
children.translated_text: How could the noble one speak a contemptible and low word,

children.text: trāhīti vacanaṃ sīte yas trāyet tridaśān api ||
children.translated_text: saying, "Save me," O <s>Sītā</s>, he who could save even the gods?

children.text: kiṃnimittaṃ tu kenāpi bhrātur ālambya me svaram
children.translated_text: For what reason has someone, taking up my brother's voice,

children.text: visvaraṃ vyāhṛtaṃ vākyaṃ lakṣmaṇa trāhi mām iti
children.translated_text: uttered a discordant cry, "<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, save me"?
You should not give way to distress of the kind resorted to by ignoble women.

children.text: alaṃ vaiklavyam ālambya svasthā bhava nirutsukā
children.translated_text: Enough of taking up agitation; be steady and free from anxiety.

children.text: na cāsti triṣu lokeṣu pumān yo rāghavaṃ raṇe
children.translated_text: There is no man in the three worlds who, in battle, could defeat <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: jāto vā jāyamāno vā saṃyuge yaḥ parājayet ||
children.translated_text: whether he has been born already or is yet to be born.'
But <s>Vaidehī</s>, her mind overcome with delusion, when thus addressed,

children.text: uvācāśrūṇi muñcantī dāruṇaṃ mām idaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: spoke these cruel words to me, shedding tears:

children.text: bhāvo mayi tavātyarthaṃ pāpa eva niveśitaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Your feeling toward me has been fixed in utter evil.

children.text: vinaṣṭe bhrātari prāpte na ca tvaṃ mām avāpsyasi ||
children.translated_text: When your brother is destroyed and the occasion has come, still you will not obtain me.
By an agreement with <s>Bharata</s> you are following <s>Rāma</s>;
for though he cries out so violently, you do not come to his aid.
You are an enemy moving in concealment, following for my sake;
desiring an opening against <s>Rāghava</s>, you therefore do not go to him.'

children.text: evam ukto hi vaidehyā saṃrabdho raktalocanaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Vaidehī</s>, I was enraged, red-eyed,
my lips quivering with anger, and I came out from the hermitage."
To <s>Saumitri</s>, who was speaking in this way, <s>Rāma</s>, bewildered by anguish,

children.text: abravīd duṣkṛtaṃ saumya tāṃ vinā yat tvam āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: said, "You did wrong, gentle one, in that you came without her.

children.text: jānann api samarthaṃ māṃ rakṣasāṃ vinivāraṇe
children.translated_text: Although you knew that I am able to ward off the <s>rākṣasas</s>,
you came away because of this angry speech of <s>Maithilī</s>.

children.text: na hi te parituṣyāmi tyaktvā yad yāsi maithilīm
children.translated_text: I am not pleased with you, since you came after leaving <s>Maithilī</s>;

children.text: kruddhāyāḥ paruṣaṃ śrutvā striyā yat tvam ihāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: hearing the harsh words of an angry woman, you came here.

children.text: sarvathā tv apanītaṃ te sītayā yat pracoditaḥ
children.translated_text: In every way you acted wrongly: urged by <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: krodhasya vaśam āgamya nākaroḥ śāsanaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: you came under the power of anger and did not carry out my command.

children.text: asau hi rākṣasaḥ śete śareṇābhihato mayā
children.translated_text: For that <s>rākṣasa</s> lies there, struck down by my arrow,
the one by whom I was drawn away from the hermitage in the form of a deer.

children.text: vikṛṣya cāpaṃ paridhāya sāyakaṃ salīlabāṇena ca tāḍito mayā
children.translated_text: Drawing my bow and setting an arrow upon it, I struck him with an easy shot;

children.text: mārgīṃ tanuṃ tyajya ca viklavasvaro babhūva keyūradharaḥ sa rākṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: abandoning the body of a deer, that <s>rākṣasa</s>, wearing armlets, cried out in a faltering voice.

children.text: śarāhatenaiva tadārtayā girā svaraṃ mamālambya sudūrasaṃśravam
children.translated_text: By him, wounded by the arrow, with that pain-stricken voice, taking on my voice audible from far away,

children.text: udāhṛtaṃ tad vacanaṃ sudāruṇaṃ tvam āgato yena vihāya maithilīm ||
children.translated_text: that exceedingly cruel utterance was made, because of which you came, leaving <s>Maithilī</s>.
As he was hastening greatly, his lower left eye

children.text: prāsphurac cāskhalad rāmo vepathuś cāsya jāyate ||
children.translated_text: throbbed; <s>Rāma</s> stumbled, and trembling arose in him.
Observing those inauspicious omens again and again,

children.text: api kṣemaṃ tu sītāyā iti vai vyājahāra ha ||
children.translated_text: he said, "Is <s>Sītā</s> safe?"
Then, hurrying and longing to see <s>Sītā</s>, he went;
seeing the dwelling empty, his mind became anxious.
Like one whirling about in haste and casting his eyes around, the delight of the <s>Raghus</s>
looked everywhere, here and there, over the site of the hut.

children.text: dadarśa parṇaśālāṃ ca rahitāṃ sītayā tadā
children.translated_text: Then he saw the leaf-hut bereft of <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: śriyā virahitāṃ dhvastāṃ hemante padminīm iva ||
children.translated_text: bereft of beauty and ruined, like a lotus pond in winter.
It seemed to weep with its trees, its flowers, deer, and birds faded and dispirited;
deprived of beauty, devastated, abandoned by the forest deities.
Its antelope skins and <s>kuśa</s> grass were scattered; its reed-mats were thrown about.
Seeing the empty hut-site, he lamented again and again:

children.text: hṛtā mṛtā vā naṣṭā vā bhakṣitā vā bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: "She must have been carried off, or killed, or lost, or eaten;

children.text: nilīnāpy atha vā bhīrur atha vā vanam āśritā ||
children.translated_text: or perhaps the timid one has hidden, or else she has taken refuge in the forest."

children.text: gatā vicetuṃ puṣpāṇi phalāny api ca vā punaḥ
children.translated_text: She has gone to gather flowers, or fruits as well, perhaps,

children.text: atha vā padminīṃ yātā jalārthaṃ vā nadīṃ gatā ||
children.translated_text: or else she has gone to the lotus pond, or gone to the river for water.

children.text: yatnān mṛgayamāṇas tu nāsasāda vane priyām
children.translated_text: But though he searched carefully, he did not find his beloved in the forest;
with eyes reddened by grief, through grief he seemed like a madman.

children.text: vṛkṣād vṛkṣaṃ pradhāvan sa girīṃś cāpi nadīn nadīm
children.translated_text: Rushing from tree to tree, and from mountain to mountain, river to river,
<s>Rāma</s> kept lamenting, plunged in an ocean of the mire of grief.

children.text: asti kaccit tvayā dṛṣṭā sā kadambapriyā priyā
children.translated_text: Surely that dear one, fond of kadambas, has been seen by you?

children.text: kadamba yadi jānīṣe śaṃsa sītāṃ śubhānanām ||
children.translated_text: O kadamba, if you know, tell me of <s>Sītā</s>, the beautiful-faced one.
She who has the likeness of tender leaves and wears yellow silk,

children.text: śaṃsasva yadi vā dṛṣṭā bilva bilvopamastanī ||
children.translated_text: tell me, O bilva, if she has been seen, she whose breasts are like bilva fruits.

children.text: atha vārjuna śaṃsa tvaṃ priyāṃ tām arjunapriyām
children.translated_text: Or you, O arjuna tree, tell of that beloved, fond of arjunas;

children.text: janakasya sutā bhīrur yadi jīvati vā na vā ||
children.translated_text: whether the timid daughter of <s>Janaka</s> is alive or not.

children.text: kakubhaḥ kakubhoruṃ tāṃ vyaktaṃ jānāti maithilīm
children.translated_text: The kakubha surely knows that <s>Maithilī</s>, whose thighs are like the kakubha;
for this lord of trees shines, rich with creepers, shoots, and flowers.

children.text: bhramarair upagītaś ca yathā drumavaro hy ayam
children.translated_text: And since this excellent tree is sung around by bees,
this tilaka surely knows the woman who is fond of tilakas.
O aśoka, remover of grief, for me whose mind is stricken by grief,
quickly make your name true by showing me my beloved.
O tāla, if you have seen her, whose breasts are like ripe tāla fruits,

children.text: kathayasva varārohāṃ kāruṇyaṃ yadi te mayi ||
children.translated_text: tell of the fair-hipped woman, if you have compassion for me.

children.text: yadi dṛṣṭā tvayā sītā jambu jāmbūnadaprabhā
children.translated_text: O jambu, if <s>Sītā</s> has been seen by you, she who shines like jāmbūnada gold,

children.text: priyāṃ yadi vijānīṣe niḥśaṅkaṃ kathayasva me ||
children.translated_text: if you know my beloved, tell me without hesitation.

children.text: atha vā mṛgaśāvākṣīṃ mṛga jānāsi maithilīm
children.translated_text: Or, O deer, do you know <s>Maithilī</s>, the doe-eyed one?
The lovely woman with a deer's glance may be together with the does.

children.text: gaja sā gajanāsorur yadi dṛṣṭā tvayā bhavet
children.translated_text: O elephant, if she whose thighs are like an elephant's trunk has been seen by you,

children.text: tāṃ manye viditāṃ tubhyam ākhyāhi varavāraṇa ||
children.translated_text: I think she is known to you; tell me, best of elephants.

children.text: śārdūla yadi sā dṛṣṭā priyā candranibhānanā
children.translated_text: O tiger, if that beloved, with a face like the moon, has been seen,

children.text: maithilī mama viśrabdhaḥ kathayasva na te bhayam ||
children.translated_text: tell me about my <s>Maithilī</s> trustfully; there is no fear for you.

children.text: kiṃ dhāvasi priye nūnaṃ dṛṣṭāsi kamalekṣaṇe
children.translated_text: Why do you run, beloved? Surely I have seen you, lotus-eyed one.

children.text: vṛkṣeṇācchādya cātmānaṃ kiṃ māṃ na pratibhāṣase ||
children.translated_text: Why, hiding yourself behind a tree, do you not speak to me?

children.text: tiṣṭha tiṣṭha varārohe na te 'sti karuṇā mayi
children.translated_text: Stop, stop, fair-hipped one; you have no pity for me.
You are not so very given to laughter; why do you ignore me?
You have been revealed by your yellow silk garment, woman of excellent complexion;

children.text: dhāvanty api mayā dṛṣṭā tiṣṭha yady asti sauhṛdam ||
children.translated_text: even as you ran, I saw you. Stop, if there is affection.

children.text: naiva sā nūnam atha vā hiṃsitā cāruhāsinī
children.translated_text: Surely that is not she; or else the lovely-smiling woman has been harmed,

children.text: kṛcchraṃ prāptaṃ hi māṃ nūnaṃ yathopekṣitum arhati ||
children.translated_text: for how could she ignore me, surely, when I have come to such distress?

children.text: vyaktaṃ sā bhakṣitā bālā rākṣasaiḥ piśitāśanaiḥ
children.translated_text: Clearly that young beloved, separated from me, has been eaten by flesh-eating rākṣasas,
after they divided all her limbs.

children.text: nūnaṃ tac chubhadantauṣṭhaṃ mukhaṃ niṣprabhatāṃ gatam
children.translated_text: Surely that face, with its lovely teeth and lips, has lost its radiance;
and that neck, shining with the color of campaka and adorned with a necklace,

children.text: komalā vilapantyās tu kāntāyā bhakṣitā śubhā
children.translated_text: soft and beautiful, of my beloved as she cried out, has been eaten.
Surely those two arms, tender as shoots, being tossed about,
trembling at the tips, together with their hand-ornaments and armlets, have been eaten.

children.text: mayā virahitā bālā rakṣasāṃ bhakṣaṇāya vai ||
children.translated_text: The young woman, separated from me, has indeed become food for rākṣasas.
She of many kinsmen has been devoured, like one abandoned by a caravan.

children.text: hā lakṣmaṇa mahābāho paśyasi tvaṃ priyāṃ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: Ah, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, mighty-armed one, do you see my beloved anywhere?

children.text: hā priye kva gatā bhadre hā sīteti punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Ah beloved, where have you gone, gentle one? Ah <s>Sītā</s>! So he cried again and again.

children.text: ity evaṃ vilapan rāmaḥ paridhāvan vanād vanam ||
children.translated_text: Thus lamenting, <s>Rāma</s> ran from forest to forest.

children.text: kvacid udbhramate vegāt kvacid vibhramate balāt
children.translated_text: At times he wandered in agitation through his speed; at times he reeled helplessly;
at times he seemed like a madman, wholly intent on searching for his beloved.

children.text: sa vanāni nadīḥ śailān giriprasravaṇāni ca
children.translated_text: Through forests, rivers, mountains, and mountain streams,
and through woodlands he roamed swiftly, without steadiness.

children.text: tathā sa gatvā vipulaṃ mahad vanaṃ parītya sarvaṃ tv atha maithilīṃ prati
children.translated_text: Then, after he had gone through that broad, great forest, circling all around in search of <s>Maithilī</s>,

children.text: aniṣṭhitāśaḥ sa cakāra mārgaṇe punaḥ priyāyāḥ paramaṃ pariśramam ||
children.translated_text: with his hope unfulfilled, he again made the utmost effort in seeking his beloved.
Seeing the hermitage empty, <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>,

children.text: rahitāṃ parṇaśālāṃ ca vidhvastāny āsanāni ca ||
children.translated_text: and the leaf-hut deserted, and the seats overturned,

children.text: adṛṣṭvā tatra vaidehīṃ saṃnirīkṣya ca sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: not seeing <s>Vaidehī</s> there and looking all around,

children.text: uvāca rāmaḥ prākruśya pragṛhya rucirau bhujau ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> cried aloud, raising his beautiful arms, and said:

children.text: kva nu lakṣmaṇa vaidehī kaṃ vā deśam ito gatā
children.translated_text: Where, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, is <s>Vaidehī</s>? To what place has she gone from here?

children.text: kenāhṛtā vā saumitre bhakṣitā kena vā priyā ||
children.translated_text: By whom has my beloved been carried off, O son of <s>Sumitrā</s>, or by whom has she been eaten?

children.text: vṛkṣeṇācchādya yadi māṃ sīte hasitum icchasi
children.translated_text: If, <s>Sītā</s>, you wish to laugh at me while hiding behind a tree,

children.text: alaṃ te hasitenādya māṃ bhajasva suduḥkhitam ||
children.translated_text: enough of this laughter today; attend to me, who am in great misery.

children.text: yaiḥ saha krīḍase sīte viśvastair mṛgapotakaiḥ
children.translated_text: Those trusting little deer with whom you used to play, <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: ete hīnās tvayā saumye dhyāyanty asrāvilekṣaṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: bereft of you, gentle one, are brooding with tear-filled eyes.
Dead from the great grief born of <s>Sītā</s>'s abduction,

children.text: paraloke mahārājo nūnaṃ drakṣyati me pitā ||
children.translated_text: my father, the great king, will surely see me in the next world.

children.text: kathaṃ pratijñāṃ saṃśrutya mayā tvam abhiyojitaḥ
children.translated_text: 'After hearing the pledge, you were charged by me;
without completing that term, how have you come here into my presence?'

children.text: kāmavṛttam anāryaṃ māṃ mṛṣāvādinam eva ca
children.translated_text: 'You are ruled by desire, ignoble, and a liar as well;

children.text: dhik tvām iti pare loke vyaktaṃ vakṣyati me pitā ||
children.translated_text: fie on you!' my father will surely say in the next world.
Helpless, scorched by grief, miserable, with my desire shattered,

children.text: mām ihotsṛjya karuṇaṃ kīrtir naram ivānṛjum ||
children.translated_text: where are you going, leaving me here pitiably, like fame leaving an unrighteous man?

children.text: kva gacchasi varārohe mām utsṛjya sumadhyame
children.translated_text: Where are you going, fair-hipped, slender-waisted one, abandoning me?

children.text: tvayā virahitaś cāhaṃ mokṣye jīvitam ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Separated from you, I shall cast off my life.
Thus lamenting, longing for the sight of <s>Sītā</s>,
<s>Rāghava</s>, overwhelmed by great sorrow, did not see the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>.
As <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> saw that son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, unable to find <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: paṅkam āsādya vipulaṃ sīdantam iva kuñjaram
children.translated_text: like an elephant sinking after reaching a broad mire,
he spoke to <s>Rāma</s> with deep concern and with a desire for his welfare:

children.text: mā viṣādaṃ mahābāho kuru yatnaṃ mayā saha
children.translated_text: Do not give way to despair, mighty-armed one; make an effort together with me.

children.text: idaṃ ca hi vanaṃ śūra bahukandaraśobhitam ||
children.translated_text: For this forest too, hero, is adorned with many caves.
<s>Maithilī</s>, fond of wandering in beloved groves and intoxicated by the forest,

children.text: sā vanaṃ vā praviṣṭā syān nalinīṃ vā supuṣpitām ||
