children.translated_text: may have entered the forest, or a lotus-pond full of blossoms,
or she may have reached a river frequented by fish and vañjula reeds.

children.text: vitrāsayitukāmā vā līnā syāt kānane kvacit
children.translated_text: Or, wishing to frighten us, she may be hidden somewhere in the woodland,

children.text: jijñāsamānā vaidehī tvāṃ māṃ ca puruṣarṣabha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vaidehī</s> testing you and me, bull among men.

children.text: tasyā hy anveṣaṇe śrīman kṣipram eva yatāvahe
children.translated_text: In searching for her, splendid one, let us quickly make an effort.

children.text: vanaṃ sarvaṃ vicinuvo yatra sā janakātmajā
children.translated_text: Let us search the whole forest, wherever that daughter of <s>Janaka</s> may be.

children.text: manyase yadi kākutstha mā sma śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: If you think so, <s>Kākutstha</s>, do not set your mind on grief.
Thus addressed out of friendship by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the composed
<s>Rāma</s> began to search together with the son of <s>Sumitrā</s>.

children.text: tau vanāni girīṃś caiva saritaś ca sarāṃsi ca ||
children.translated_text: Those two sons of <s>Daśaratha</s> searched the forests, mountains,
rivers, and lakes completely, looking for <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: tasya śailasya sānūni guhāś ca śikharāṇi ca ||
children.translated_text: Searching completely the slopes of that mountain,
its caves and its peaks, they still did not come upon her.

children.text: vicitya sarvataḥ śailaṃ rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Having searched the mountain everywhere, <s>Rāma</s> said to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:

children.text: neha paśyāmi saumitre vaidehīṃ parvate śubhe
children.translated_text: Here on this beautiful mountain, <s>Saumitri</s>, I do not see <s>Vaidehī</s>.
Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, burned by sorrow, spoke these words
to his brother of blazing splendor as he wandered through the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest:
Greatly wise one, you will find <s>Maithilī</s>, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,

children.text: yathā viṣṇur mahābāhur baliṃ baddhvā mahīm imām
children.translated_text: just as mighty-armed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, after binding <s>Bali</s>, obtained this earth.

children.text: evam uktas tu vīreṇa lakṣmaṇena sa rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the heroic <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, that <s>Rāghava</s>
spoke in a mournful voice, his mind struck down by sorrow:
The whole forest has been well searched, and the lotus-ponds with blooming lotuses;
and this mountain too, greatly wise one, with its many caves and waterfalls.

children.text: na hi paśyāmi vaidehīṃ prāṇebhyo 'pi garīyasīm ||
children.translated_text: Yet I do not see <s>Vaidehī</s>, dearer to me even than my life.
Thus lamenting, <s>Rāma</s>, wasted by the abduction of <s>Sītā</s>,
wretched and filled with grief, became overwhelmed for a moment.
With all his limbs overcome, his understanding gone, and his senses lost,
he sank down, distressed and miserable, drawing a long, hot sigh.

children.text: bahuśaḥ sa tu niḥśvasya rāmo rājīvalocanaḥ
children.translated_text: Having sighed many times, lotus-eyed <s>Rāma</s>
cried out again and again, 'Ah, beloved!', his voice choked with tears.
Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, his dear kinsman, consoled him
in many ways; knowing <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), he stood humbly with folded hands.
But disregarding the words that had fallen from <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s lips,

children.text: apaśyaṃs tāṃ priyāṃ sītāṃ prākrośat sa punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: not seeing his beloved <s>Sītā</s>, he cried out again and again.

children.text: sa dīno dīnayā vācā lakṣmaṇaṃ vākyam abravīt
children.translated_text: Wretched, he spoke to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> in a mournful voice:

children.text: śīghraṃ lakṣmaṇa jānīhi gatvā godāvarīṃ nadīm
children.translated_text: Go quickly, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, to the river <s>Godāvarī</s> and learn

children.text: api godāvarīṃ sītā padmāny ānayituṃ gatā ||
children.translated_text: whether <s>Sītā</s> has gone to the <s>Godāvarī</s> to bring lotuses.

children.text: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa lakṣmaṇaḥ punar eva hi
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> once more
went with swift stride to the lovely river <s>Godāvarī</s>.

children.text: tāṃ lakṣmaṇas tīrthavatīṃ vicitvā rāmam abravīt
children.translated_text: After searching that river with its fords, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> said to <s>Rāma</s>:

children.text: naināṃ paśyāmi tīrtheṣu krośato na śṛṇoti me ||
children.translated_text: I do not see her at the fords, and though I call out she does not hear me.

children.text: kaṃ nu sā deśam āpannā vaidehī kleśanāśinī
children.translated_text: To what place, then, has <s>Vaidehī</s>, remover of distress, come?

children.text: na hi taṃ vedmi vai rāma yatra sā tanumadhyamā ||
children.translated_text: For I do not know, <s>Rāma</s>, where that slender-waisted woman is.
Hearing <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s words, wretched and bewildered by anguish,
<s>Rāma</s> himself approached the river <s>Godāvarī</s>.

children.text: sa tām upasthito rāmaḥ kva sītety evam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Standing before her, <s>Rāma</s> said just this: 'Where is <s>Sītā</s>?'
Though she had been carried off by the lord of rākṣasas, who deserved death,

children.text: na tāṃ śaśaṃsū rāmāya tathā godāvarī nadī ||
children.translated_text: the beings did not tell <s>Rāma</s> of her, nor did the river <s>Godāvarī</s>.

children.text: tataḥ pracoditā bhūtaiḥ śaṃsāsmai tāṃ priyām iti
children.translated_text: Then, urged on by the beings, 'Tell him of his beloved,'

children.text: na ca sābhyavadat sītāṃ pṛṣṭā rāmeṇa śocitā ||
children.translated_text: even when questioned by grieving <s>Rāma</s>, she did not speak of <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: rāvaṇasya ca tad rūpaṃ karmāṇi ca durātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Thinking of the form and deeds of wicked-souled <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: dhyātvā bhayāt tu vaidehīṃ sā nadī na śaśaṃsa tām ||
children.translated_text: that river, out of fear, did not tell him about <s>Vaidehī</s>.

children.text: nirāśas tu tayā nadyā sītāyā darśane kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Made hopeless by that river in his hope of seeing <s>Sītā</s>,
<s>Rāma</s>, wasted by not seeing <s>Sītā</s>, said to <s>Saumitri</s>:

children.text: kiṃ nu lakṣmaṇa vakṣyāmi sametya janakaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: What words, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, shall I speak when I meet <s>Janaka</s>,

children.text: mātaraṃ caiva vaidehyā vinā tām aham apriyam ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Vaidehī</s>'s mother too, without her, bearing bad news?

children.text: yā me rājyavihīnasya vane vanyena jīvataḥ
children.translated_text: She who removed all my grief when I was deprived of my kingdom,

children.text: sarvaṃ vyapanayacchokam vaidehī kva nu sā gatā ||
children.translated_text: living in the forest on forest fare: where has that <s>Vaidehī</s> gone?
Not seeing that princess, I am bereft of the side of my kinsmen.

children.text: manye dīrghā bhaviṣyanti rātrayo mama jāgrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: I think the nights will become long for me as I lie awake.
The <s>Godāvarī</s>, <s>Janasthāna</s>, and this <s>Prasravaṇa</s> mountain:

children.text: sarvāṇy anucariṣyāmi yadi sītā hi dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: I will roam through them all, if <s>Sītā</s> may be seen.

children.text: evaṃ sambhāṣamāṇau tāv anyonyaṃ bhrātarāv ubhau
children.translated_text: While those two brothers were speaking thus with one another,
they saw a path of flowers fallen on the earth.

children.text: tāṃ puṣpavṛṣṭiṃ patitāṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmo mahītale
children.translated_text: Seeing that shower of flowers fallen on the ground,

children.text: uvāca lakṣmaṇaṃ vīro duḥkhito duḥkhitaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the heroic <s>Rāma</s>, distressed, spoke distressed words to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:
I recognize these flowers, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>;
they were fastened on <s>Vaidehī</s>, given by me in the forest.
Having spoken thus, the mighty-armed one addressed <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, bull among men,

children.text: kruddho 'bravīd giriṃ tatra siṃhaḥ kṣudramṛgaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: and, enraged, spoke there to the mountain as a lion might to a small beast:

children.text: tāṃ hemavarṇāṃ hemābhāṃ sītāṃ darśaya parvata
children.translated_text: Show me golden-colored, golden-shining <s>Sītā</s>, mountain.

children.text: yāvat sānūni sarvāṇi na te vidhvaṃsayāmy aham ||
children.translated_text: until I have shattered all your peaks.
Burned by the fire of my arrows, you will become reduced to ashes,
always unfit to be inhabited, stripped of grass, trees, and shoots.

children.text: imāṃ vā saritaṃ cādya śoṣayiṣyāmi lakṣmaṇa
children.translated_text: Or else, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, today I shall dry up this river,

children.text: yadi nākhyāti me sītām adya candranibhānanām ||
children.translated_text: if it does not tell me today where <s>Sītā</s>, whose face is like the moon, is.

children.text: evaṃ sa ruṣito rāmo didhakṣann iva cakṣuṣā
children.translated_text: Thus angered, <s>Rāma</s>, as if wishing to burn it with his eyes,

children.text: dadarśa bhūmau niṣkrāntaṃ rākṣasasya padaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: saw on the ground the great footprint of a <s>rākṣasa</s> that had come out.

children.text: sa samīkṣya parikrāntaṃ sītāyā rākṣasasya ca
children.translated_text: Seeing the track traversed by <s>Sītā</s> and by the <s>rākṣasa</s>,
<s>Rāma</s>, his heart shaken, told his dear brother:
Look, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, at <s>Vaidehī</s>'s scattered golden drops,

children.text: bhūṣaṇānāṃ hi saumitre mālyāni vividhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: the ornaments, O son of <s>Sumitrā</s>, and the various garlands.
Look, O son of <s>Sumitrā</s>, at the whole surface of the earth, covered everywhere
with varied drops of blood that resemble drops of molten gold.
I think, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, that <s>Vaidehī</s> has been cut apart again and again

children.text: bhittvā bhittvā vibhaktā vā bhakṣitā vā bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: and divided up, or has been eaten by shape-shifting <s>rākṣasas</s>.
Because of <s>Vaidehī</s>, while two were contending,

children.text: babhūva yuddhaṃ saumitre ghoraṃ rākṣasayor iha ||
children.translated_text: there was a terrible battle here, O son of <s>Sumitrā</s>, between two <s>rākṣasas</s>.
Inlaid with pearls and jewels and adorned with gold,

children.text: dharaṇyāṃ patitaṃ saumya kasya bhagnaṃ mahad dhanuḥ ||
children.translated_text: whose great broken bow is this, fallen on the ground, gentle one?
Resembling the young sun, set with balls of beryl,

children.text: viśīrṇaṃ patitaṃ bhūmau kavacaṃ kasya kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: whose golden armor is this, shattered and fallen on the ground?
Whose parasol is this, with a hundred ribs, adorned with divine garlands,

children.text: bhagnadaṇḍam idaṃ kasya bhūmau saumya nipātitam ||
children.translated_text: its staff broken, lying here on the ground, gentle one?
And these asses, with golden breast-plates and faces like fiends,

children.text: bhīmarūpā mahākāyāḥ kasya vā nihatā raṇe ||
children.translated_text: terrible in form and huge in body, whose were they, slain in battle?
Whose war-chariot is this, bright and shining, with a battle-banner like blazing fire,

children.text: apaviddhaś ca bhagnaś ca kasya sāṃgrāmiko rathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: cast aside and broken?
Whose arrows are these, as large as chariot-axles, adorned with gold,
struck down and scattered, arrows of terrible action?
See, gentle one, this enmity against me, multiplied a hundredfold and ending in my life,
from the shape-shifting <s>rākṣasas</s> whose hearts are most dreadful.

children.text: hṛtā mṛtā vā sītā hi bhakṣitā vā tapasvinī
children.translated_text: For <s>Sītā</s>, the ascetic woman, has been carried off, or killed, or eaten.

children.text: na dharmas trāyate sītāṃ hriyamāṇāṃ mahāvane ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> (righteous order) does not protect <s>Sītā</s> as she is being abducted in the great forest.

children.text: bhakṣitāyāṃ hi vaidehyāṃ hṛtāyām api lakṣmaṇa
children.translated_text: If <s>Vaidehī</s> has been eaten, or even if she has been carried off, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: ke hi loke priyaṃ kartuṃ śaktāḥ saumya mameśvarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: who in the world, gentle one, what powerful beings, can do what is dear to me?
Even the maker of the worlds, heroic and sensitive to compassion,
all beings would despise out of ignorance, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Gentle, devoted to the welfare of the world, self-controlled, sensitive to compassion,

children.text: nirvīrya iti manyante nūnaṃ māṃ tridaśeśvarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: surely the lords of the Thirty think me powerless.

children.text: māṃ prāpya hi guṇo doṣaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ paśya lakṣmaṇa
children.translated_text: See, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>: in me virtue has become a fault.
This very day, for the destruction of all beings and of the <s>rākṣasas</s>,
I shall rise like the great sun, having drawn away the moonlight.

children.text: naiva yakṣā na gandharvā na piśācā na rākṣasāḥ
children.translated_text: Neither <s>yakṣas</s>, nor <s>gandharvas</s>, nor <s>piśācas</s>, nor <s>rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: kiṃnarā vā manuṣyā vā sukhaṃ prāpsyanti lakṣmaṇa ||
children.translated_text: nor <s>kiṃnaras</s>, nor human beings will attain happiness, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Look, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, at the sky filled with my missile-arrows.
Today I shall make it impassable for those who move through the three worlds.
With the hosts of planets obstructed and the moon covered over,
with fire, wind, and the sun's brilliance lost and enveloped,
with the peaks of mountains torn away, reservoirs drying up,
trees, creepers, and thickets destroyed, and the ocean ruined,

children.text: na tāṃ kuśalinīṃ sītāṃ pradāsyanti mameśvarāḥ
children.translated_text: if the mighty ones do not give back to me that unharmed <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: asmin muhūrte saumitre mama drakṣyanti vikramam ||
children.translated_text: then in this very moment, O son of <s>Sumitrā</s>, they will see my valor.
No beings at all will fly up into the sky, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
because of the unbroken nets of arrows released from my bowstring.
Today, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, see the world harried by my iron arrows, its beasts and birds driven into ruin and confusion,
thrown into turmoil and beyond all bounds.
For the sake of <s>Maithilī</s>, with arrows drawn fully to the ear and hard to ward off,
I shall make the world of living beings free of <s>piśācas</s> and free of <s>rākṣasas</s>.
Today the gods will see the power of my arrows, urged on by wrath,
released in anger and flying far.

children.text: naiva devā na daiteyā na piśācā na rākṣasāḥ
children.translated_text: Neither gods, nor <s>Daityas</s>, nor <s>piśācas</s>, nor <s>rākṣasas</s>
will remain when the three worlds have been destroyed by my anger.
The worlds of gods, <s>Dānavas</s>, and <s>yakṣas</s>, and those even of the <s>rākṣasas</s>,
will fall in many pieces, smashed to fragments by floods of arrows.

children.text: nirmaryādān imāṃl lokān kariṣyāmy adya sāyakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Today I shall make these worlds lawless, without boundaries, with my arrows.

children.text: yathā jarā yathā mṛtyur yathā kālo yathā vidhiḥ
children.translated_text: As old age, as death, as time, as destiny,
are never warded off among all beings, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
so I, joined with anger, am without doubt not to be restrained.

children.text: pureva me cārudatīm aninditāṃ diśanti sītāṃ yadi nādya maithilīm
children.translated_text: If today they do not give back to me <s>Sītā</s>, the lovely-toothed, blameless <s>Maithilī</s>, as she was before,
I shall overturn the world, with its gods, <s>gandharvas</s>, human beings, serpents, and mountains.
Seeing <s>Rāma</s> burning in this way, wasted by the abduction of <s>Sītā</s>,
intent on the destruction of the worlds, like the fire of dissolution,

children.text: vīkṣamāṇaṃ dhanuḥ sajyaṃ niḥśvasantaṃ muhur muhuḥ
children.translated_text: looking at his strung bow and sighing again and again,

children.text: hantukāmaṃ paśuṃ rudraṃ kruddhaṃ dakṣakratau yathā ||
children.translated_text: desiring to kill, like an enraged <s>Rudra</s> at <s>Dakṣa</s>'s sacrifice,

children.text: adṛṣṭapūrvaṃ saṃkruddhaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmaṃ sa lakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, seeing <s>Rāma</s> angry as never before,
With joined palms, his mouth dried up, he spoke these words:

children.text: purā bhūtvā mṛdur dāntaḥ sarvabhūtahite rataḥ
children.translated_text: Formerly you were gentle and self-controlled, devoted to the welfare of all beings;

children.text: na krodhavaśam āpannaḥ prakṛtiṃ hātum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: you, who have not fallen under the power of anger, ought not abandon your nature.

children.text: candre lakṣmīḥ prabhā sūrye gatir vāyau bhuvi kṣamā
children.translated_text: Beauty is in the moon, radiance in the sun, motion in the wind, and forbearance on the earth;

children.text: etac ca niyataṃ sarvaṃ tvayi cānuttamaṃ yaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: all this is fixed, and in you too there is unsurpassed fame.

children.text: na tu jānāmi kasyāyaṃ bhagnaḥ sāṃgrāmiko rathaḥ
children.translated_text: But I do not know whose war-chariot this is, broken apart,

children.text: kena vā kasya vā hetoḥ sāyudhaḥ saparicchadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or by whom, or for what reason, it was shattered, with its weapons and equipment.
This place, cut up by hooves and wheel-rims and sprinkled with drops of blood,
is a very terrible ground where the battle has ended, O prince.

children.text: ekasya tu vimardo 'yaṃ na dvayor vadatāṃ vara
children.translated_text: This crushing belongs to one person, not to two, O best of speakers;

children.text: na hi vṛttaṃ hi paśyāmi balasya mahataḥ padam ||
children.translated_text: for I do not see here the trace of a great army.

children.text: naikasya tu kṛte lokān vināśayitum arhasi
children.translated_text: You ought not destroy the worlds for the sake of one person;
for gentle and tranquil kings of the earth impose punishment in due measure.

children.text: sadā tvaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ śaraṇyaḥ paramā gatiḥ
children.translated_text: You are always the refuge of all beings, their supreme goal;

children.text: ko nu dārapraṇāśaṃ te sādhu manyeta rāghava ||
children.translated_text: who, <s>Rāghava</s>, would think the destruction caused by the loss of your wife a good thing?
Rivers, oceans, mountains, gods, gandharvas, and dānavas

children.text: nālaṃ te vipriyaṃ kartuṃ dīkṣitasyeva sādhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: are not able to do what is displeasing to you, as good men would not harm one who is consecrated.

children.text: yena rājan hṛtā sītā tam anveṣitum arhasi
children.translated_text: By whom, O king, <s>Sītā</s> has been carried off, him you ought to seek out,
with me as your second, bow in hand, together with your helpers, the great seers.

children.text: samudraṃ ca viceṣyāmaḥ parvatāṃś ca vanāni ca
children.translated_text: We shall search the ocean, the mountains, and the forests,

children.text: guhāś ca vividhā ghorā nalinīḥ pārvatīś ca ha ||
children.translated_text: and the various terrible caves, and the lotus-ponds among the mountains too.
We shall search, with collected minds, the worlds of gods and gandharvas,
until we discover the man who has carried off your wife.

children.text: na cet sāmnā pradāsyanti patnīṃ te tridaśeśvarāḥ
children.translated_text: If even the lords of the thirty gods will not give back your wife through conciliation,
then afterward, lord of <s>Kosala</s>, you will do what the time demands.

children.text: śīlena sāmnā vinayena sītāṃ nayena na prāpsyasi cen narendra
children.translated_text: If by character, conciliation, humility, and policy you do not obtain <s>Sītā</s>, O king,
then annihilate them with volleys of gold-feathered arrows resembling <s>Mahendra</s>'s thunderbolt.
To him, thus scorched by grief, lamenting like one without protection,
possessed by great delusion, wasted away and senseless,

children.text: tataḥ saumitrir āśvāsya muhūrtād iva lakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, son of <s>Sumitrā</s>, having consoled <s>Rāma</s> after a moment,
roused him to awareness while pressing his feet.

children.text: mahatā tapasā rāma mahatā cāpi karmaṇā
children.translated_text: By great austerity, <s>Rāma</s>, and by great action too,
you were obtained by King <s>Daśaratha</s>, like nectar by the immortals.

children.text: tava caiva guṇair baddhas tvadviyogān mahīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Bound by your very virtues and by separation from you, the lord of the earth,

children.text: rājā devatvam āpanno bharatasya yathā śrutam ||
children.translated_text: the king attained the state of a god, as was heard from <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: yadi duḥkham idaṃ prāptaṃ kākutstha na sahiṣyase
children.translated_text: If you, <s>Kākutstha</s>, will not endure this sorrow that has come upon you,

children.text: prākṛtaś cālpasattvaś ca itaraḥ kaḥ sahiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: what other ordinary man of little strength will endure it?

children.text: duḥkhito hi bhavāṃl lokāṃs tejasā yadi dhakṣyate
children.translated_text: For if you, being distressed, burn the worlds with your energy,

children.text: ārtāḥ prajā naravyāghra kva nu yāsyanti nirvṛtim ||
children.translated_text: where, O tiger among men, will afflicted creatures find relief?
This indeed is the nature of the world: <s>Yayāti</s>, son of <s>Nahuṣa</s>,

children.text: gataḥ śakreṇa sālokyam anayas taṃ samaspṛśat ||
children.translated_text: went to share <s>Śakra</s>'s world, yet calamity touched him.

children.text: maharṣayo vasiṣṭhas tu yaḥ pitur naḥ purohitaḥ
children.translated_text: And the great sage <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, who is our father's priest,

children.text: ahnā putraśataṃ jajñe tathaivāsya punar hatam ||
children.translated_text: begot a hundred sons in a day, and afterward they too were slain.

children.text: yā ceyaṃ jagato mātā devī lokanamaskṛtā
children.translated_text: And this goddess, mother of the world, revered by the worlds,

children.text: asyāś ca calanaṃ bhūmer dṛśyate satyasaṃśrava ||
children.translated_text: even of her, the earth, movement is seen, O truthful one.

children.text: yau cemau jagatāṃ netre yatra sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam
children.translated_text: And these two eyes of the worlds, on which everything is established,
the mighty sun and moon, have undergone eclipse.

children.text: sumahānty api bhūtāni devāś ca puruṣarṣabha
children.translated_text: Even very great beings, and the gods too, O bull among men,
all embodied beings do not escape fate.
Even among gods beginning with <s>Śakra</s>, right conduct and wrong conduct

children.text: śrūyete naraśārdūla na tvaṃ vyathitum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: are heard of, O tiger among men; you ought not be disturbed.

children.text: naṣṭāyām api vaidehyāṃ hṛtāyām api cānagha
children.translated_text: Though <s>Vaidehī</s> is lost, and though she has been carried off, sinless hero,

children.text: śocituṃ nārhase vīra yathānyaḥ prākṛtas tathā ||
children.translated_text: you ought not grieve as any ordinary man would.

children.text: tvadvidhā hi na śocanti satataṃ satyadarśinaḥ
children.translated_text: For men like you, constantly seeing the truth, do not grieve,
O <s>Rāma</s>; even in very great difficulties, their vision is not despairing.
Therefore, O best of men, reflect on the matter truly with understanding;
the very wise, joined with understanding, discern the good and the bad.
For actions whose virtues and faults have not been seen, and which have not been undertaken,

children.text: nāntareṇa kriyāṃ teṣāṃ phalam iṣṭaṃ pravartate ||
children.translated_text: their desired fruit does not arise apart from action.

children.text: mām eva hi purā vīra tvam eva bahuśo 'nvaśāḥ
children.translated_text: In the past, O hero, you yourself instructed me many times;

children.text: anuśiṣyāddhi ko nu tvām api sākṣād bṛhaspatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: who indeed could instruct you, even if it were <s>Bṛhaspati</s> himself in person?

children.text: buddhiś ca te mahāprājña devair api duranvayā
children.translated_text: Your understanding, O greatly wise one, is hard for even the gods to follow;
but since your knowledge has been lulled to sleep by grief, I am awakening it.

children.text: divyaṃ ca mānuṣaṃ caivam ātmanaś ca parākramam
children.translated_text: Considering your own divine and human power,
O bull of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s>, strive for the slaughter of your enemies.
What use is the destruction of all to you once it has been done, O bull among men?

children.text: tam eva tu ripuṃ pāpaṃ vijñāyoddhartum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: Rather, having identified that sinful enemy alone, you ought to root him out.
And the elder brother, merely addressed by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s well-spoken words,
<s>Rāghava</s>, grasping their essence, accepted their deeply significant meaning.
The mighty-armed <s>Rāma</s>, restraining the great growth of his own anger

children.text: avaṣṭabhya dhanuś citraṃ rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: and holding fast his splendid bow, spoke to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:

children.text: kiṃ kariṣyāvahe vatsa kva vā gacchāva lakṣmaṇa
children.translated_text: What shall we do, dear child, or where shall we go, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>?
By what means might I see <s>Sītā</s>? Consider this.

children.text: taṃ tathā paritāpārtaṃ lakṣmaṇo rāmam abravīt
children.translated_text: To <s>Rāma</s>, thus afflicted by anguish, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> said:

children.text: idam eva janasthānaṃ tvam anveṣitum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: You ought to search this very <s>Janasthāna</s>.
It is strewn with many rākṣasas and filled with many kinds of trees and creepers.
Here there are mountain strongholds, clefts, and caves.
There are also various terrible caverns, thronged with herds of many kinds of animals,
dwellings of kiṃnaras and abodes of gandharvas.

children.text: tāni yukto mayā sārdhaṃ tvam anveṣitum arhasi
children.translated_text: Together with me, you should properly search them.
Great-souled men like you, endowed with wisdom, O bull among men,
do not tremble in calamities, like mountains before the force of winds.

children.text: ity uktas tad vanaṃ sarvaṃ vicacāra salakṣmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: So addressed, <s>Rāma</s>, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, ranged through that whole forest.

children.text: kruddho rāmaḥ śaraṃ ghoraṃ saṃdhāya dhanuṣi kṣuram
children.translated_text: Angry, <s>Rāma</s> set a terrible razor-headed arrow on his bow.
Then he saw, like the peak of a mountain, the greatly fortunate best of birds,
<s>Jaṭāyuṣ</s>, fallen on the ground and wet with blood.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā giriśṛṅgābhaṃ rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt
children.translated_text: Seeing him, who resembled a mountain summit, <s>Rāma</s> said to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:

children.text: anena sītā vaidehī bhakṣitā nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Without doubt <s>Sītā</s> <s>Vaidehī</s> has been eaten by this one.

children.text: gṛdhrarūpam idaṃ vyaktaṃ rakṣo bhramati kānanam
children.translated_text: Clearly this rākṣasa, in the form of a vulture, roams the forest.
Having eaten wide-eyed <s>Sītā</s>, he now sits here at ease.

children.text: enaṃ vadhiṣye dīptāgrair ghorair bāṇair ajihmagaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall kill him with blazing-tipped, terrible, straight-flying arrows.

children.text: ity uktvābhyapatad gṛdhraṃ saṃdhāya dhanuṣi kṣuram
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, angry <s>Rāma</s> rushed upon the vulture, setting a razor-headed arrow on his bow,

children.text: kruddho rāmaḥ samudrāntāṃ cālayann iva medinīm ||
children.translated_text: as if shaking the earth as far as the ocean's edge.

children.text: taṃ dīnadīnayā vācā saphenaṃ rudhiraṃ vaman
children.translated_text: But the bird, vomiting foamy blood,
addressed <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, in a very pitiable voice:
Long-lived one, she whom you seek in this great forest, like a healing herb,

children.text: sā devī mama ca prāṇā rāvaṇenobhayaṃ hṛtam ||
children.translated_text: that lady, and my own life as well, both have been taken by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: tvayā virahitā devī lakṣmaṇena ca rāghava
children.translated_text: O <s>Rāghava</s>, the lady, separated from you and from <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
was seen by me being carried away by mighty <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: sītām abhyavapanno 'haṃ rāvaṇaś ca raṇe mayā
children.translated_text: I came to aid <s>Sītā</s>, and <s>Rāvaṇa</s> was struck down by me in battle,
his chariot and parasol shattered, fallen upon the ground.

children.text: etad asya dhanur bhagnam etad asya śarāvaram
children.translated_text: Here is his broken bow; here is his quiver.

children.text: ayam asya raṇe rāma bhagnaḥ sāṃgrāmiko rathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, O <s>Rāma</s>, is his war-chariot, broken in the fight.

children.text: pariśrāntasya me pakṣau chittvā khaḍgena rāvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: When I was exhausted, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> cut off my two wings with his sword,
and, taking <s>Sītā</s> <s>Vaidehī</s>, he flew up into the sky.

children.text: rakṣasā nihataṃ pūrvaṃ na māṃ hantuṃ tvam arhasi ||
children.translated_text: Since I was already struck down by the rākṣasa, you should not kill me.

children.text: rāmas tasya tu vijñāya sītāsaktāṃ priyāṃ kathām
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāma</s> understood from him the beloved tale concerning <s>Sītā</s>,
he embraced the king of vultures and wept together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Seeing him somehow breathing, alone in that difficult single path,

children.text: samīkṣya duḥkhito rāmaḥ saumitrim idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: grieving <s>Rāma</s> said this to <s>Saumitri</s>:

children.text: rājyād bhraṃśo vane vāsaḥ sītā naṣṭā hato dvijaḥ
children.translated_text: Loss of kingdom, dwelling in the forest, <s>Sītā</s> lost, and this bird slain:
such is my ill fortune that it could burn even fire.

children.text: sampūrṇam api ced adya pratareyaṃ mahodadhim
children.translated_text: If today I were to cross the great ocean, even when it was full,

children.text: so 'pi nūnaṃ mamālakṣmyā viśuṣyet saritāṃ patiḥ ||
children.translated_text: surely even that lord of rivers would dry up through my ill fortune.
In this world, with its moving and unmoving beings, there is no one more unfortunate than I,
since this great snare of calamity has come upon me.
This king of vultures, old and a friend of my father,
lies slain on the ground because of the reversal of my fortune.

children.text: ity evam uktvā bahuśo rāghavaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus again and again, <s>Rāghava</s>, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
touched <s>Jaṭāyuṣ</s>, showing a father's affection.

children.text: nikṛttapakṣaṃ rudhirāvasiktaṃ taṃ gṛdhrarājaṃ parirabhya rāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Embracing that king of vultures, his wings cut off and drenched in blood, <s>Rāma</s>

children.text: kva maithili prāṇasamā mameti vimucya vācaṃ nipapāta bhūmau ||
children.translated_text: cried out, 'Where is <s>Maithilī</s>, equal to my own life?' and fell upon the ground.

children.text: rāmaḥ prekṣya tu taṃ gṛdhraṃ bhuvi raudreṇa pātitam
children.translated_text: Seeing that vulture cast down on the earth by a terrible blow, <s>Rāma</s>
said these words to well-disposed <s>Saumitri</s>:
Surely this bird, striving on my behalf in my affairs,

children.text: rākṣasena hataḥ saṃkhye prāṇāṃs tyajati dustyajān ||
children.translated_text: has been killed in battle by the rākṣasa, and is giving up his life, hard to give up.

children.text: ayam asya śarīre 'smin prāṇo lakṣmaṇa vidyate
children.translated_text: O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, there is still life in this body of his;
yet he is voiceless and looks around in distress.

children.text: jaṭāyo yadi śaknoṣi vākyaṃ vyāharituṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: O <s>Jaṭāyuṣ</s>, if you can utter speech once more,

children.text: sītām ākhyāhi bhadraṃ te vadham ākhyāhi cātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: tell me of <s>Sītā</s>; may it be well with you, and tell me of your own killing.

children.text: kiṃnimitto 'harat sītāṃ rāvaṇas tasya kiṃ mayā
children.translated_text: For what reason did <s>Rāvaṇa</s> carry off <s>Sītā</s>? What offense was committed by me

children.text: aparāddhaṃ tu yaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇena hṛtā priyā ||
children.translated_text: against him, that, seeing it, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> took away my beloved?

children.text: kathaṃ tac candrasaṃkāśaṃ mukham āsīn manoharam
children.translated_text: How was that charming face of <s>Sītā</s>, shining like the moon,

children.text: sītayā kāni coktāni tasmin kāle dvijottama ||
children.translated_text: and what words were spoken by <s>Sītā</s> at that time, O best of birds?

children.text: kathaṃvīryaḥ kathaṃrūpaḥ kiṃkarmā sa ca rākṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: What is that rākṣasa's strength, what is his form, and what are his deeds?

children.text: kva cāsya bhavanaṃ tāta brūhi me paripṛcchataḥ ||
children.translated_text: And where is his dwelling, father? Tell me, as I ask you.
Then, looking upon him lamenting thus without cease,
the dejected <s>Jaṭāyuṣ</s> said this to <s>Rāma</s> in a voice very faint:
She was taken through the sky by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of rākṣasas,
after he had resorted to a vast illusion, crowded with storm and darkness.

children.text: pariśrāntasya me tāta pakṣau chittvā niśācaraḥ
children.translated_text: Father, when I was exhausted, the night-roamer cut off my wings,
and, taking <s>Sītā</s> <s>Vaidehī</s>, he went away facing south.

children.text: uparudhyanti me prāṇā dṛṣṭir bhramati rāghava
children.translated_text: My breaths are being obstructed, O <s>Rāghava</s>; my sight is whirling.
I see golden trees, with hair made of uśīra grass.

children.text: yena yāti muhūrtena sītām ādāya rāvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: In the muhūrta in which <s>Rāvaṇa</s> goes, taking <s>Sītā</s>,
lost wealth is quickly recovered by its owner.

children.text: vindo nāma muhūrto 'sau sa ca kākutstha nābudhat
children.translated_text: That muhūrta is named <s>Vinda</s>, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, but he did not know it.

children.text: jhaṣavad baḍiśaṃ gṛhya kṣipram eva vinaśyati ||
children.translated_text: Like a fish taking a hook, he will perish very quickly.

children.text: na ca tvayā vyathā kāryā janakasya sutāṃ prati
children.translated_text: And you should not feel distress concerning the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>.

children.text: vaidehyā raṃsyase kṣipraṃ hatvā taṃ rākṣasaṃ raṇe ||
children.translated_text: You will soon delight in <s>Vaidehī</s> after killing that rākṣasa in battle.
As the unbewildered vulture was answering <s>Rāma</s>,
bloody matter with flesh flowed from the mouth of the dying bird.

children.text: putro viśravasaḥ sākṣād bhrātā vaiśravaṇasya ca
children.translated_text: "He is the direct son of <s>Viśravas</s> and the brother of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>";

children.text: ity uktvā durlabhān prāṇān mumoca patageśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: having said this, the lord of birds gave up his hard-to-retain life.
As <s>Rāma</s>, with folded hands, kept saying, "Speak, speak!",

children.text: tyaktvā śarīraṃ gṛdhrasya jagmuḥ prāṇā vihāyasam ||
children.translated_text: the vulture's life-breaths left his body and went to the sky.

children.text: sa nikṣipya śiro bhūmau prasārya caraṇau tadā
children.translated_text: Then, laying his head upon the ground and stretching out his feet,

children.text: vikṣipya ca śarīraṃ svaṃ papāta dharaṇītale ||
children.translated_text: and casting his body down, he fell upon the surface of the earth.

children.text: taṃ gṛdhraṃ prekṣya tāmrākṣaṃ gatāsum acalopamam
children.translated_text: Seeing that copper-eyed vulture, lifeless and like an unmoving mountain,

children.text: rāmaḥ subahubhir duḥkhair dīnaḥ saumitrim abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, made wretched by many griefs, spoke to <s>Saumitri</s>:

children.text: bahūni rakṣasāṃ vāse varṣāṇi vasatā sukham
children.translated_text: For many years this bird lived happily among the dwellings of the rākṣasas,
wandering here in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest.
This one, who had lived for many years and stood firm for a long time,

children.text: so 'yam adya hataḥ śete kālo hi duratikramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: now lies slain today; for time is hard to overcome.

children.text: paśya lakṣmaṇa gṛdhro 'yam upakārī hataś ca me
children.translated_text: Look, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>: this vulture, my benefactor, has been killed

children.text: sītām abhyavapan no vai rāvaṇena balīyasā ||
children.translated_text: while trying to save <s>Sītā</s> from the stronger <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Abandoning the great vulture-kingdom inherited from his fathers and grandfathers,

children.text: mama hetor ayaṃ prāṇān mumoca patageśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: this lord of birds gave up his life for my sake.
Indeed, noble people who follow <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty) are seen everywhere,
brave and giving refuge, <s>Saumitri</s>, even among those born in animal wombs.

children.text: sītāharaṇajaṃ duḥkhaṃ na me saumya tathāgatam
children.translated_text: The grief born from <s>Sītā</s>'s abduction has not struck me so much, gentle one,

children.text: yathā vināśo gṛdhrasya matkṛte ca paraṃtapa ||
children.translated_text: as has the destruction of this vulture for my sake, scorcher of foes.

children.text: rājā daśarathaḥ śrīmān yathā mama mahāyaśāḥ
children.translated_text: As the glorious king <s>Daśaratha</s>, of great fame, was to me,

children.text: pūjanīyaś ca mānyaś ca tathāyaṃ patageśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: worthy of worship and worthy of honor, so too is this lord of birds.
<s>Saumitri</s>, bring wood; I shall kindle the fire by friction.
I wish to cremate the vulture king, who has met death for my sake.
I shall place this lord of the world of birds upon the funeral pyre;

children.text: imaṃ dhakṣyāmi saumitre hataṃ raudreṇa rakṣasā ||
children.translated_text: I shall burn him, <s>Saumitri</s>, slain by the fierce rākṣasa.

children.text: yā gatir yajñaśīlānām āhitāgneś ca yā gatiḥ
children.translated_text: The state attained by those devoted to sacrifice, and the state of those who maintain sacred fires,

children.text: aparāvartināṃ yā ca yā ca bhūmipradāyinām ||
children.translated_text: and that of those who do not return, and that of those who give land:

children.text: mayā tvaṃ samanujñāto gaccha lokān anuttamān
children.translated_text: with my permission, go to those unsurpassed worlds,

children.text: gṛdhrarāja mahāsattva saṃskṛtaś ca mayā vraja ||
children.translated_text: O vulture king, great being; ritually honored by me, depart.

children.text: evam uktvā citāṃ dīptām āropya patageśvaram
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Rāma</s> placed the lord of birds on the blazing pyre,

children.text: dadāha rāmo dharmātmā svabandhum iva duḥkhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, righteous-souled and grieving, burned him as though he were his own kinsman.

children.text: rāmo 'tha sahasaumitrir vanaṃ yātvā sa vīryavān
children.translated_text: Then powerful <s>Rāma</s>, together with <s>Saumitri</s>, went into the forest,

children.text: sthūlān hatvā mahārohīn anu tastāra taṃ dvijam ||
children.translated_text: killed large, well-grown <s>rohi</s> deer, and then spread offerings for that twice-born one.
Glorious <s>Rāma</s> took up the flesh of the <s>rohi</s> deer and made it into pieces,
and gave it for the bird on a lovely green meadow.

children.text: yat tat pretasya martyasya kathayanti dvijātayaḥ
children.translated_text: That rite which the twice-born declare to be for a dead mortal,

children.text: tat svargagamanaṃ tasya kṣipraṃ rāmo jajāpa ha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> then recited it for that one's swift ascent to heaven.
Then the two noble princes went to the river <s>Godāvarī</s>,

children.text: udakaṃ cakratus tasmai gṛdhrarājāya tāv ubhau ||
children.translated_text: and both performed the water offering for him, the vulture king.

children.text: sa gṛdhrarājaḥ kṛtavān yaśaskaraṃ suduṣkaraṃ karma raṇe nipātitaḥ
children.translated_text: That vulture king, struck down in battle after doing a fame-winning deed very hard to do,

children.text: maharṣikalpena ca saṃskṛtas tadā jagāma puṇyāṃ gatim ātmanaḥ śubhām ||
children.translated_text: and then honored by one like a great seer, went to a holy and blessed destiny of his own.

children.text: kṛtvaivam udakaṃ tasmai prasthitau rāghavau tadā
children.translated_text: Having thus made the water offering for him, the two <s>Rāghavas</s> set out then,

children.text: avekṣantau vane sītāṃ paścimāṃ jagmatur diśam ||
children.translated_text: looking for <s>Sītā</s> in the forest, and went toward the western direction.
Having gone to that southern direction, carrying bows, arrows, and swords,
the two <s>Ikṣvākus</s> took an unobstructed path.

children.text: gulmair vṛkṣaiś ca bahubhir latābhiś ca praveṣṭitam
children.translated_text: It was enveloped by thickets, many trees, and vines,
covered on every side, difficult to pass, dense, and terrible to behold.

children.text: vyatikramya tu vegena gṛhītvā dakṣiṇāṃ diśam
children.translated_text: But swiftly passing through and taking the southern direction,
the two mighty ones went across that exceedingly frightful great forest.

children.text: tataḥ paraṃ janasthānāt trikrośaṃ gamya rāghavau
children.translated_text: Then, going three krośas beyond <s>Janasthāna</s>, the two <s>Rāghavas</s>,
those two of great vigor, entered the dense <s>Krauñca</s> forest.
It resembled masses of various clouds and seemed delighted everywhere,
filled with beautiful flowers of many colors and with hosts of deer and birds.

children.text: didṛkṣamāṇau vaidehīṃ tad vanaṃ tau vicikyatuḥ
children.translated_text: Desiring to see <s>Vaidehī</s>, the two searched that forest,
stopping here and there, emaciated by the abduction of <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: lakṣmaṇas tu mahātejāḥ sattvavāñ śīlavāñ śuciḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, very radiant, strong in spirit, virtuous, and pure,
spoke a sentence with folded hands to his brother of blazing splendor:

children.text: spandate me dṛḍhaṃ bāhur udvignam iva me manaḥ
children.translated_text: My arm throbs strongly, and my mind seems disturbed;
and in general I perceive inauspicious omens.

children.text: tasmāt sajjībhavārya tvaṃ kuruṣva vacanaṃ hitam
children.translated_text: Therefore make yourself ready, noble one, and do what is beneficial according to my words.

children.text: mamaiva hi nimittāni sadyaḥ śaṃsanti sambhramam ||
children.translated_text: For these omens now announce danger to me.
This terrible bird named <s>Vañculaka</s>

children.text: āvayor vijayaṃ yuddhe śaṃsann iva vinardati ||
children.translated_text: is crying aloud as if proclaiming victory for the two of us in battle.

children.text: tayor anveṣator evaṃ sarvaṃ tad vanam ojasā
children.translated_text: As the two of them were thus searching that whole forest with vigor,

children.text: saṃjajñe vipulaḥ śabdaḥ prabhañjann iva tad vanam ||
children.translated_text: a great sound arose, as if splitting that forest apart.
The dense forest seemed to be wrapped about completely by the wind,

children.text: vanasya tasya śabdo 'bhūd divam āpūrayann iva ||
children.translated_text: and its sound seemed to fill the sky.

children.text: taṃ śabdaṃ kāṅkṣamāṇas tu rāmaḥ kakṣe sahānujaḥ
children.translated_text: Wishing to know the source of that sound, <s>Rāma</s>, with his younger brother, in the thicket
saw a huge-bodied rākṣasa with an enormous chest.

children.text: āsedatus tatas tatra tāv ubhau pramukhe sthitam
children.translated_text: Then the two of them approached him there, standing before them,
grown huge, without head or neck, with his mouth in his belly: <s>Kabandha</s>.
He stood towering like a great mountain, covered with dense, sharp hairs.
Dark like a blue cloud, dreadful, with a roar like thunderclouds,
with a great tawny eyelid, broad and long,
and with a single terrible eye in his chest, hard to look at,
endowed with great fangs, licking his huge mouth,
devouring most dreadful bears, lions, deer, and elephants,

children.text: ghorau bhujau vikurvāṇam ubhau yojanam āyatau
children.translated_text: brandishing two terrible arms, each extending a yojana,

children.text: karābhyāṃ vividhān gṛhya ṛkṣān pakṣigaṇān mṛgān ||
children.translated_text: grasping with his hands various bears, flocks of birds, and deer,
pulling in and dragging away many leaders of deer-herds,

children.text: sthitam āvṛtya panthānaṃ tayor bhrātroḥ prapannayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: standing there, blocking the path of the two brothers who had come upon it,
then, after going on for about a krośa, the two saw him:
a huge, cruel, fearsome <s>Kabandha</s>, enveloped by his arms.

children.text: sa mahābāhur atyarthaṃ prasārya vipulau bhujau
children.translated_text: That mighty-armed one, stretching out his two enormous arms very far,

children.text: jagrāha sahitāv eva rāghavau pīḍayan balāt ||
children.translated_text: seized the two <s>Rāghavas</s> together, crushing them by force.
Armed with swords, bearing firm bows, fierce in splendor and mighty-armed,
the two powerful brothers had fallen helpless, dragged along by him.
Then the mighty-armed <s>Kabandha</s>, best of <s>Dānavas</s>, said to them:
Who are you two, bull-shouldered men, bearing great swords and bows,

children.text: ghoraṃ deśam imaṃ prāptau mama bhakṣāv upasthitau
children.translated_text: who have come into this dreadful region and stand here before me as my food?

children.text: vadataṃ kāryam iha vāṃ kimarthaṃ cāgatau yuvām ||
children.translated_text: Tell me what business you have here, and for what purpose you two have come.
You have arrived in this region where I stand afflicted by hunger;
and, with arrows, bows, and swords, you are like two bulls with sharp horns.
Having come into my mouth, your life will be hard to regain.
Hearing that speech of wicked <s>Kabandha</s>,
<s>Rāma</s>, his mouth dried up, said to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:
After falling from hardship into a still greater hardship, terrible one, O true in valor,

children.text: vyasanaṃ jīvitāntāya prāptam aprāpya tāṃ priyām ||
children.translated_text: we have reached a calamity that ends in life itself, without having recovered that beloved one.
Great indeed is the power of Time over all beings, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: tvāṃ ca māṃ ca naravyāghra vyasanaiḥ paśya mohitau
children.translated_text: See, tiger among men, how you and I are bewildered by calamities.
There is no burden too heavy for fate among all beings, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: śūrāś ca balavantaś ca kṛtāstrāś ca raṇājire
children.translated_text: Even heroes who are strong and skilled in weapons on the battlefield,
when overtaken by Time, sink down like embankments of sand.

children.text: iti bruvāṇo dṛḍhasatyavikramo mahāyaśā dāśarathiḥ pratāpavān
children.translated_text: Thus speaking, the glorious son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, firm in truth and valor, powerful and renowned,

children.text: avekṣya saumitrim udagravikramaṃ sthirāṃ tadā svāṃ matim ātmanākarot ||
children.translated_text: looked at <s>Saumitri</s>, fierce in courage, and then steadied his own mind within himself.

children.text: tau tu tatra sthitau dṛṣṭvā bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
children.translated_text: Seeing the two brothers, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, standing there,
caught in the noose of his arms, <s>Kabandha</s> spoke these words:

children.text: tiṣṭhataḥ kiṃ nu māṃ dṛṣṭvā kṣudhārtaṃ kṣatriyarṣabhau
children.translated_text: Why do you stand there after seeing me, afflicted by hunger, O bulls among <s>kṣatriyas</s>?
You have been assigned by fate for my food, your minds gone astray.

children.text: tac chrutvā lakṣmaṇo vākyaṃ prāptakālaṃ hitaṃ tadā
children.translated_text: Hearing that timely and useful speech,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, overwhelmed by distress and resolved on valor, then said:

children.text: tvāṃ ca māṃ ca purā tūrṇam ādatte rākṣasādhamaḥ
children.translated_text: This lowest <s>rākṣasa</s> will soon quickly seize both you and me.

children.text: tasmād asibhyām asyāśu bāhū chindāvahai gurū ||
children.translated_text: Therefore let us at once cut off his massive arms with our swords.

children.text: tatas tau deśakālajñau khaḍgābhyām eva rāghavau
children.translated_text: Then the two <s>Rāghavas</s>, knowing place and time, with their swords alone,
joyfully cut off his arms at the shoulders.

children.text: dakṣiṇo dakṣiṇaṃ bāhum asaktam asinā tataḥ
children.translated_text: With his sword <s>Rāma</s> then swiftly cut off the right arm attached on the right,

children.text: cicheda rāmo vegena savyaṃ vīras tu lakṣmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: while heroic <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> cut off the left.
That mighty-armed one, his arms severed, fell with a great roar,

children.text: khaṃ ca gāṃ ca diśaś caiva nādayañ jalado yathā ||
children.translated_text: making the sky, the earth, and the quarters resound like a raincloud.
Seeing his two arms cut away and flooded with streams of blood,

children.text: dīnaḥ papraccha tau vīrau kau yuvām iti dānavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Dānava</s>, wretched, asked the two heroes, Who are you?
As he was speaking in this way, fair-marked <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
the mighty one, told <s>Kabandha</s> about <s>Kākutstha</s>.

children.text: ayam ikṣvākudāyādo rāmo nāma janaiḥ śrutaḥ
children.translated_text: This is <s>Rāma</s>, heir of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, known among men by name.

children.text: asyaivāvarajaṃ viddhi bhrātaraṃ māṃ ca lakṣmaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Know me to be his younger brother, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
While this man of divine power was dwelling in the lonely forest,
his wife was carried off by a <s>rākṣasa</s>; seeking her, we have come here.

children.text: tvaṃ tu ko vā kimarthaṃ vā kabandha sadṛśo vane
children.translated_text: But who are you, <s>Kabandha</s>, and for what reason, in this forest,
with a blazing mouth in your chest and with broken thighs, do you writhe about?

children.text: evam uktaḥ kabandhas tu lakṣmaṇenottaraṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed with an answering speech by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, <s>Kabandha</s>,
greatly pleased and remembering that word of <s>Indra</s>, said:

children.text: svāgataṃ vāṃ naravyāghrau diṣṭyā paśyāmi cāpy aham
children.translated_text: Welcome to you both, tigers among men; by good fortune I now see you.

children.text: diṣṭyā cemau nikṛttau me yuvābhyāṃ bāhubandhanau ||
children.translated_text: By good fortune these bonds of my arms have been cut away by you two.

children.text: virūpaṃ yac ca me rūpaṃ prāptaṃ hy avinayād yathā
children.translated_text: As for this deformed shape of mine, which I obtained through misconduct,

children.text: tan me śṛṇu naravyāghra tattvataḥ śaṃsatas tava ||
children.translated_text: listen to that truly, tiger among men, as I tell it to you.
Formerly, O mighty-armed <s>Rāma</s>, strong in great might and valor,

children.text: rūpam āsīn mamācintyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam
children.translated_text: I had an inconceivable form, renowned in the three worlds,

children.text: yathā somasya śakrasya sūryasya ca yathā vapuḥ ||
children.translated_text: like the body of <s>Soma</s>, of <s>Śakra</s>, and of the Sun.

children.text: so 'haṃ rūpam idaṃ kṛtvā lokavitrāsanaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: Then, making this form of mine, a great terror to the world,

children.text: ṛṣīn vanagatān rāma trāsayāmi tatas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: I used to frighten the sages who had gone into the forest, O <s>Rāma</s>, here and there.

children.text: tataḥ sthūlaśirā nāma maharṣiḥ kopito mayā
children.translated_text: Then a great seer named <s>Sthūlaśirā</s>, angered by me,
while gathering various forest produce, was assaulted by me in this form.
Looking at me, he spoke with words of a terrible curse:

children.text: etad eva nṛśaṃsaṃ te rūpam astu vigarhitam ||
children.translated_text: Let this very cruel and blameworthy form be yours.

children.text: sa mayā yācitaḥ kruddhaḥ śāpasyānto bhaved iti
children.translated_text: Though he was angry, I begged him that there might be an end to the curse,
and these words were spoken by him, the maker of the curse.

children.text: yadā chittvā bhujau rāmas tvāṃ dahed vijane vane
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāma</s> has cut off your two arms and burns you in a lonely forest,

children.text: tadā tvaṃ prāpsyase rūpaṃ svam eva vipulaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: then you will regain your own vast and auspicious form.

children.text: śriyā virājitaṃ putraṃ danos tvaṃ viddhi lakṣmaṇa
children.translated_text: Know me, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, as the son of <s>Danu</s>, radiant with splendor.

children.text: indrakopād idaṃ rūpaṃ prāptam evaṃ raṇājire ||
children.translated_text: Through <s>Indra</s>'s wrath I obtained this form in just this way on the battlefield.
For with fierce austerity I pleased the grandsire,

children.text: dīrgham āyuḥ sa me prādāt tato māṃ vibhramo 'spṛśat ||
children.translated_text: and he granted me a long life; after that delusion took hold of me.

children.text: dīrgham āyur mayā prāptaṃ kiṃ me śakraḥ kariṣyati
children.translated_text: I had obtained long life; what could <s>Śakra</s> do to me?

children.text: ity evaṃ buddhim āsthāya raṇe śakram adharṣayam ||
children.translated_text: Adopting just such a thought, I attacked <s>Śakra</s> in battle.
By his hundred-jointed thunderbolt, released from his arm,

children.text: sakthinī ca śiraś caiva śarīre saṃpraveśitam ||
children.translated_text: my thighs and head alike were driven into my body.

children.text: sa mayā yācyamānaḥ sann ānayad yamasādanam
children.translated_text: Though I begged him, he did not send me to the abode of <s>Yama</s>;

children.text: pitāmahavacaḥ satyaṃ tad astv iti mamābravīt ||
children.translated_text: he said to me, 'Let the grandsire's word be true.'
How, without food, with thighs, head, and mouth shattered,
struck by the thunderbolt, could I be able to live for a very long time?

children.text: evam uktas tu me śakro bāhū yojanam āyatau
children.translated_text: When I spoke thus, <s>Śakra</s> gave me arms a yojana long,

children.text: prādād āsyaṃ ca me kukṣau tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭram akalpayat ||
children.translated_text: and fashioned for me a sharp-fanged mouth in my belly.
So with my two long arms I drag in forest-roaming creatures,
lions, elephants, deer, and tigers, and devour them from every side.

children.text: sa tu mām abravīd indro yadā rāmaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Indra</s> said to me, 'When <s>Rāma</s> together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>

children.text: chetsyate samare bāhū tadā svargaṃ gamiṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: cuts off your two arms in battle, then you will go to heaven.'

children.text: sa tvaṃ rāmo 'si bhadraṃ te nāham anyena rāghava
children.translated_text: You are that <s>Rāma</s>; welfare to you, O <s>Rāghava</s>. I cannot

children.text: śakyo hantuṃ yathātattvam evam uktaṃ maharṣiṇā ||
children.translated_text: be killed by anyone else; so it was truly spoken by the great seer.
For I will act as a counselor for you, O best of men,
and I will point out a friend, once I have been purified by fire by you two.

children.text: evam uktas tu dharmātmā danunā tena rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāghava</s>, righteous in spirit, had been addressed thus by that son of <s>Danu</s>,
he spoke these words while <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> was listening:

children.text: rāvaṇena hṛtā sītā mama bhāryā yaśasvinī
children.translated_text: My famous wife <s>Sītā</s> has been carried off by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
after I had gone out from <s>Janasthāna</s> at ease together with my brother.

children.text: nāmamātraṃ tu jānāmi na rūpaṃ tasya rakṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: I know only the name of that rākṣasa;

children.text: nivāsaṃ vā prabhāvaṃ vā vayaṃ tasya na vidmahe ||
children.translated_text: we do not know his form, his dwelling, or his power.
For us, afflicted with grief, helpless, and running about in this way,

children.text: kāruṇyaṃ sadṛśaṃ kartum upakāre ca vartatām ||
children.translated_text: it is fitting to show compassion and to engage in helping us.

children.text: kāṣṭhāny ānīya śuṣkāṇi kāle bhagnāni kuñjaraiḥ
children.translated_text: Bringing dry pieces of wood, broken down in due course by elephants,

children.text: bhakṣyāmas tvāṃ vayaṃ vīra śvabhre mahati kalpite ||
children.translated_text: we will burn you, O hero, in a great pit that has been prepared.

children.text: sa tvaṃ sītāṃ samācakṣva yena vā yatra vā hṛtā
children.translated_text: So tell us about <s>Sītā</s>, by whom she was taken or where she was taken;

children.text: kuru kalyāṇam atyarthaṃ yadi jānāsi tattvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: do us the greatest good, if you know the truth.

children.text: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa vākyaṃ danur anuttamam
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Danu</s>'s son, skilled in speech,

children.text: provāca kuśalo vaktuṃ vaktāram api rāghavam ||
children.translated_text: spoke this excellent reply even to <s>Rāghava</s>, the speaker:

children.text: divyam asti na me jñānaṃ nābhijānāmi maithilīm
children.translated_text: I do not have divine knowledge; I do not know <s>Maithilī</s>.

children.text: yas tāṃ jñāsyati taṃ vakṣye dagdhaḥ svaṃ rūpam āsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When I have been burned and have assumed my own form, I will tell you the one who will know her.

children.text: adagdhasya hi vijñātuṃ śaktir asti na me prabho
children.translated_text: Unburned, O lord, I have no power to recognize

children.text: rākṣasaṃ taṃ mahāvīryaṃ sītā yena hṛtā tava ||
children.translated_text: that mighty rākṣasa by whom your <s>Sītā</s> was carried off.

children.text: vijñānaṃ hi mahad bhraṣṭaṃ śāpadoṣeṇa rāghava
children.translated_text: For my great knowledge has been lost through the fault of the curse, O <s>Rāghava</s>;
through my own deed I have obtained a form reviled by the world.

children.text: kiṃ tu yāvan na yāty astaṃ savitā śrāntavāhanaḥ
children.translated_text: But before the sun, whose steeds are wearied, goes to setting,

children.text: tāvan mām avaṭe kṣiptvā daha rāma yathāvidhi ||
children.translated_text: cast me into a pit and burn me according to rule, O <s>Rāma</s>.
When I have been burned by you in the pit according to proper rite, O <s>Raghunandana</s>,

children.text: vakṣyāmi tam ahaṃ vīra yas taṃ jñāsyati rākṣasam ||
children.translated_text: I will tell you, O hero, of the one who will know that rākṣasa.

children.text: tena sakhyaṃ ca kartavyaṃ nyāyyavṛttena rāghava
children.translated_text: With him you must make friendship, O <s>Rāghava</s>, acting according to what is right.
Pleased, that one of swift prowess will arrange assistance for you.

children.text: na hi tasyāsty avijñātaṃ triṣu lokeṣu rāghava
children.translated_text: For there is nothing unknown to him in the three worlds, O <s>Rāghava</s>;

children.text: sarvān parisṛto lokān purā vai kāraṇāntare ||
children.translated_text: in the past, for another reason, he ranged through all the worlds.

children.text: evam uktau tu tau vīrau kabandhena nareśvarau
children.translated_text: When the two heroes, those lords of men, had been addressed thus by <s>Kabandha</s>,
they reached a mountain cleft and set fire there.
Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, with great blazing firebrands all around,
kindled the pyre, and it flamed up on every side.
That great body of <s>Kabandha</s>, like a lump of ghee,
burned slowly in the fire as its fat was cooked.

children.text: sa vidhūya citām āśu vidhūmo 'gnir ivotthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, quickly shaking off the pyre, he rose up like a smokeless fire,

children.text: araje vāsasī bibhran mālāṃ divyāṃ mahābalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: mighty, wearing spotless garments and a divine garland.
Then, with speed, shining and clothed in stainless garments,
he sprang up from the pyre, delighted and adorned on every limb.
Standing in a radiant aerial car, drawn by swans and bestowing fame,

children.text: prabhayā ca mahātejā diśo daśa virājayan ||
children.translated_text: that greatly splendid one illumined the ten directions with his brilliance.
From the sky <s>Kabandha</s> spoke these words to <s>Rāma</s>:

children.text: śṛṇu rāghava tattvena yathā sīmām avāpsyasi ||
children.translated_text: Listen, O <s>Rāghava</s>, truly, how you will obtain <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: rāma ṣaḍ yuktayo loke yābhiḥ sarvaṃ vimṛśyate
children.translated_text: O <s>Rāma</s>, in the world there are six expedients by which everything is examined.
One who has been tested by a condition of fortune is to be served according to his share of that condition.
You, O <s>Rāma</s>, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, have fallen into a reduced condition,

children.text: yat kṛte vyasanaṃ prāptaṃ tvayā dārapradharṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: since, because of it, the calamity of the seizure of your wife has befallen you.

children.text: tad avaśyaṃ tvayā kāryaḥ sa suhṛt suhṛdāṃ vara
children.translated_text: Therefore you must certainly make that one your friend, O best of friends;

children.text: akṛtvā na hi te siddhim ahaṃ paśyāmi cintayan ||
children.translated_text: thinking it over, I do not see success for you unless you do so.

children.text: śrūyatāṃ rāma vakṣyāmi sugrīvo nāma vānaraḥ
children.translated_text: Listen, O <s>Rāma</s>; I shall tell you. There is a vānara named <s>Sugrīva</s>,
cast out by his angry brother <s>Vālin</s>, the son of <s>Śakra</s>.
He is on excellent <s>Ṛṣyamūka</s> mountain, made lovely by the edge of <s>Pampā</s>.

children.text: nivasaty ātmavān vīraś caturbhiḥ saha vānaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The self-possessed hero dwells there with four <s>vānaras</s>.

children.text: vayasyaṃ taṃ kuru kṣipram ito gatvādya rāghava
children.translated_text: Go from here today at once, O <s>Rāghava</s>, and make him your friend,
meeting him before the blazing fire as a pledge against treachery.

children.text: na ca te so 'vamantavyaḥ sugrīvo vānarādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: And you must not slight that <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the <s>vānaras</s>;

children.text: kṛtajñaḥ kāmarūpī ca sahāyārthī ca vīryavān ||
children.translated_text: he is grateful, able to take forms at will, seeking an ally, and valiant.

children.text: śaktau hy adya yuvāṃ kartuṃ kāryaṃ tasya cikīrṣitam
children.translated_text: For today you two are able to accomplish the purpose he wishes to have done;

children.text: kṛtārtho vākṛtārtho vā kṛtyaṃ tava kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: whether his own purpose is fulfilled or unfulfilled, he will do your task.

children.text: sa ṛkṣarajasaḥ putraḥ pampām aṭati śaṅkitaḥ
children.translated_text: That son of <s>Ṛkṣarajas</s> wanders about <s>Pampā</s> in fear,
the bodily son of <s>Bhāskara</s>, one against whom <s>Vālin</s> has committed offense.
Putting aside your weapon quickly, approach the <s>kapi</s> who dwells on <s>Ṛṣyamūka</s>,
and by truth, O <s>Rāghava</s>, make the forest-roaming one your friend.

children.text: sa hi sthānāni sarvāṇi kārtsnyena kapikuñjaraḥ
children.translated_text: For that elephant among <s>kapis</s> knows all places completely,
even in the world of those who eat human flesh, by his skill.

children.text: na tasyāviditaṃ loke kiṃcid asti hi rāghava
children.translated_text: There is nothing in the world unknown to him, O <s>Rāghava</s>,
as far as the thousand-rayed sun shines, O subduer of enemies.

children.text: sa nadīr vipulāñ śailān giridurgāṇi kandarān
children.translated_text: He will search rivers, broad mountains, mountain strongholds, and caves,
and together with the <s>vānaras</s> he will find your wife.
And he will send <s>vānaras</s> of great bodies, O <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: diśo vicetuṃ tāṃ sītāṃ tvadviyogena śocatīm ||
children.translated_text: to search the quarters for that <s>Sītā</s>, grieving from separation from you.

children.text: sa meruśṛṅgāgragatām aninditāṃ praviśya pātālatale 'pi vāśritām
children.translated_text: Whether your blameless beloved has gone to the summit of <s>Meru</s> or has entered and taken refuge even in the floor of <s>Pātāla</s>,

children.text: plavaṃgamānāṃ pravaras tava priyāṃ nihatya rakṣāṃsi punaḥ pradāsyati ||
children.translated_text: the foremost of leapers will slay the <s>rākṣasas</s> and give her back to you.
After thus pointing out the recovery of <s>Sītā</s> for <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: vākyam anvartham arthajñaḥ kabandhaḥ punar abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kabandha</s>, knower of meaning, again spoke an apt speech.

children.text: eṣa rāma śivaḥ panthā yatraite puṣpitā drumāḥ
children.translated_text: This, O <s>Rāma</s>, is the auspicious path where these flowering trees,
stretching toward the western direction, shine delightfully.
Jambū, priyāla, panasa, plakṣa, nyagrodha, and tinduka trees,

children.text: aśvatthāḥ karṇikārāś ca cūtāś cānye ca pādapāḥ ||
children.translated_text: aśvatthas, karṇikāras, mango trees, and other trees as well,

children.text: tān āruhyāthavā bhūmau pātayitvā ca tān balāt
children.translated_text: climbing them, or else forcefully bringing them down to the ground,
you two will eat fruits like nectar as you go.

children.text: caṅkramantau varān deśāñ śailāc chailaṃ vanād vanam
children.translated_text: Wandering through excellent regions, from mountain to mountain and forest to forest,

children.text: tataḥ puṣkariṇīṃ vīrau pampāṃ nāma gamiṣyathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then, heroes, you will reach the lotus-pond called <s>Pampā</s>.
It is free of gravel, unbroken, with even fords, and without moss,
O <s>Rāma</s>, with sandbanks formed, beautiful with lotuses and blue lotuses.

children.text: tatra haṃsāḥ plavāḥ krauñcāḥ kurarāś caiva rāghava
children.translated_text: There swans, water-birds, cranes, and kuraras too, O <s>Rāghava</s>,
cry with charming voices, moving in the waters of <s>Pampā</s>.
They are not frightened on seeing men, beautiful birds unskilled in slaughter;
you will eat those plump twice-born birds, like lumps of ghee.

children.text: rohitān vakratuṇḍāṃś ca nalamīnāṃś ca rāghava
children.translated_text: Rohita fish, curved-snouted fish, and nala fish, O <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: pampāyām iṣubhir matsyāṃs tatra rāma varān hatān ||
children.translated_text: there in <s>Pampā</s>, O <s>Rāma</s>, excellent fish struck down with arrows,
with skin and fins removed, roasted on iron, fat, and having a single bone,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, filled with devotion to you, will hand over to you.

children.text: bhṛśaṃ te khādato matsyān pampāyāḥ puṣpasaṃcaye
children.translated_text: While you are heartily eating fish among the flower-masses of <s>Pampā</s>,
the auspicious water, lotus-scented, pleasantly cool, and free from impurity,
clear, untroubled, and resembling silver and crystal, he will draw up,
and then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> will make you drink it with a lotus leaf.
Large boars, sleeping in mountain caves and roaming in the forest,

children.text: apāṃ lobhād upāvṛttān vṛṣabhān iva nardataḥ
children.translated_text: turned back by desire for water and roaring like bulls,

children.text: rūpānvitāṃś ca pampāyāṃ drakṣyasi tvaṃ narottama ||
children.translated_text: and endowed with beauty, you will see in <s>Pampā</s>, O best of men.
Wandering in the evening, O <s>Rāma</s>, among branching trees wearing garlands,

children.text: śītodakaṃ ca pampāyāṃ dṛṣṭvā śokaṃ vihāsyasi ||
children.translated_text: and seeing the cool water in <s>Pampā</s>, you will cast off sorrow.
There you will see tilaka and naktamālaka trees covered with flowers,

children.text: utpalāni ca phullāni paṅkajāni ca rāghava ||
children.translated_text: and full-blown blue lotuses and lotuses, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: na tāni kaścin mālyāni tatrāropayitā naraḥ
children.translated_text: No man has placed those garlands there;
there were once disciples of <s>Mataṅga</s> there, sages well composed in mind.
As they were wearied by their burdens, carrying forest produce for their guru,

children.text: ye prapetur mahīṃ tūrṇaṃ śarīrāt svedabindavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the drops of sweat that quickly fell from their bodies to the earth,

children.text: tāni mālyāni jātāni munīnāṃ tapasā tadā
children.translated_text: became those garlands then through the austerity of the sages;
born from drops of sweat, they do not perish, O <s>Rāghava</s>.
Even today their attendant is seen right there,
an ascetic woman named <s>Śabarī</s>, long-lived, O <s>Kākutstha</s>.

children.text: tvāṃ tu dharme sthitā nityaṃ sarvabhūtanamaskṛtam
children.translated_text: But after seeing you, O <s>Rāma</s>, ever established in <s>dharma</s> and honored by all beings,
godlike, she will go to the heavenly world.

children.text: tatas tad rāma pampāyās tīram āśritya paścimam
children.translated_text: Then, O <s>Rāma</s>, resorting to the western bank of that <s>Pampā</s>,
you will see an incomparable, hidden hermitage-site, O <s>Kākutstha</s>.

children.text: na tatrākramituṃ nāgāḥ śaknuvanti tam āśramam
children.translated_text: There elephants are not able to enter that hermitage,

children.text: ṛṣes tasya mataṃgasya vidhānāt tac ca kānanam ||
children.translated_text: nor that forest, because of the ordinance of that sage <s>Mataṅga</s>.
In that forest resembling <s>Nandana</s>, like a divine grove,
filled with many kinds of birds, you will delight, O <s>Rāma</s>, at ease.
But <s>Ṛṣyamūka</s>, east of <s>Pampā</s>, is covered with flowering trees;
it is known as very hard to climb and is guarded by śiśunāga serpents,
noble, and fashioned by <s>Brahmā</s> himself in ancient times.

children.text: śayānaḥ puruṣo rāma tasya śailasya mūrdhani
children.translated_text: A man sleeping, O <s>Rāma</s>, on the summit of that mountain,

children.text: yat svapne labhate vittaṃ tat prabuddho 'dhigacchati ||
children.translated_text: whatever wealth he obtains in a dream, obtains when awake.
But a man of crooked conduct, given to evil deeds, does not climb it;

children.text: tatraiva praharanty enaṃ suptam ādāya rākṣasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: there the <s>rākṣasas</s> strike him down as he sleeps, carrying him off.
From there too a great cry of the śiśunāgas is heard.
O <s>Rāma</s>, while those dwelling in <s>Mataṅga</s> forest sport in <s>Pampā</s>,
great elephants, sprinkled with streams of blood after clashing together,
move about separately, scattered, powerful and cloud-colored.

children.text: te tatra pītvā pānīyaṃ vimalaṃ śītam avyayam
children.translated_text: After drinking there the clear, cool, unfailing water,
the forest-ranging creatures turn back and enter the woods again.

children.text: rāma tasya tu śailasya mahatī śobhate guhā
children.translated_text: O <s>Rāma</s>, on that mountain there shines a great cave,
covered by a slab of stone, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, and entry into it is difficult.

children.text: tasyā guhāyāḥ prāgdvāre mahāñ śītodako hradaḥ
children.translated_text: At the eastern door of that cave there is a large pool of cold water,
pleasant, rich in roots and fruits, and surrounded by various trees.

children.text: tasyāṃ vasati sugrīvaś caturbhiḥ saha vānaraiḥ
children.translated_text: In that cave <s>Sugrīva</s> lives with four monkeys;
sometimes he stays on the summit of that mountain.

children.text: kabandhas tv anuśāsyaivaṃ tāv ubhau rāmalakṣmaṇau
children.translated_text: Having instructed the two, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, in this way, <s>Kabandha</s>,
garlanded, shining with the color of the sun, and heroic, blazed forth in the sky.

children.text: taṃ tu khasthaṃ mahābhāgaṃ kabandhaṃ rāmalakṣmaṇau
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, as they were setting out, said at close range

children.text: prasthitau tvaṃ vrajasveti vākyam ūcatur antikāt ||
children.translated_text: to that greatly blessed <s>Kabandha</s> standing in the sky, "Go on."

children.text: gamyatāṃ kāryasiddhyartham iti tāv abravīc ca saḥ
children.translated_text: And he said to the two, "Go, for the accomplishment of your purpose."

children.text: suprītau tāv anujñāpya kabandhaḥ prasthitas tadā ||
children.translated_text: Having dismissed them, both well pleased, <s>Kabandha</s> then departed.

children.text: sa tat kabandhaḥ pratipadya rūpaṃ vṛtaḥ śriyā bhāskaratulyadehaḥ
children.translated_text: That <s>Kabandha</s>, having regained that form, endowed with splendor and with a body equal to the sun,

children.text: nidarśayan rāmam avekṣya khasthaḥ sakhyaṃ kuruṣveti tadābhyuvāca ||
children.translated_text: looked at <s>Rāma</s> from the sky and, pointing the way, then said to him, "Make an alliance."

children.text: tau kabandhena taṃ mārgaṃ pampāyā darśitaṃ vane
children.translated_text: The two princes, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, took the path in the forest
to <s>Pampā</s> that had been shown by <s>Kabandha</s>, taking the western direction.
Looking at the mountain slopes filled with many honey-like fruit trees,
<s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> went on to see <s>Sugrīva</s>.

children.text: kṛtvā ca śailapṛṣṭhe tu tau vāsaṃ raghunandanau
children.translated_text: After the two delights of the <s>Raghu</s> line had spent the night on the mountain slope,
the two <s>Rāghavas</s> approached the western bank of <s>Pampā</s>.

children.text: tau puṣkariṇyāḥ pampāyās tīram āsādya paścimam
children.translated_text: Having reached the western bank of the lotus-filled <s>Pampā</s>,

children.text: apaśyatāṃ tatas tatra śabaryā ramyam āśramam ||
children.translated_text: they then saw there the lovely hermitage of <s>Śabarī</s>.

children.text: tau tam āśramam āsādya drumair bahubhir āvṛtam
children.translated_text: Having come to that hermitage, surrounded by many trees,
and gazing on its great beauty, the two approached <s>Śabarī</s>.

children.text: tau tu dṛṣṭvā tadā siddhā samutthāya kṛtāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: When that perfected woman saw the two, she rose at once with joined palms,

children.text: pādau jagrāha rāmasya lakṣmaṇasya ca dhīmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and grasped the feet of <s>Rāma</s> and of wise <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: tām uvāca tato rāmaḥ śramaṇīṃ saṃśitavratām
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s> spoke to that ascetic woman of sharp vows:

children.text: kaccit te nirjitā vighnāḥ kaccit te vardhate tapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Have your obstacles been overcome? Does your austerity increase?

children.text: kaccit te niyataḥ kopa āhāraś ca tapodhane
children.translated_text: Is your anger controlled, O treasure of asceticism, and is your food regulated?

children.text: kaccit te niyamāḥ prāptāḥ kaccit te manasaḥ sukham
children.translated_text: Have your observances been fulfilled? Is there happiness in your mind?
Has your service to your teachers borne fruit, O fair-spoken one?"

children.text: rāmeṇa tāpasī pṛṣṭā sā siddhā siddhasaṃmatā
children.translated_text: Questioned by <s>Rāma</s>, that perfected ascetic woman, honored by the perfected,
the aged <s>Śabarī</s>, standing before <s>Rāma</s>, reported:
"When you had reached <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, those whom I served

children.text: itas te divam ārūḍhā yān ahaṃ paryacāriṣam ||
children.translated_text: ascended from here to heaven in aerial cars of unequalled splendor.

children.text: taiś cāham uktā dharmajñair mahābhāgair maharṣibhiḥ
children.translated_text: And I was told by those righteous, greatly blessed great seers:

children.text: āgamiṣyati te rāmaḥ supuṇyam imam āśramam ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Rāma</s> will come to this very holy hermitage of yours.
That guest, together with <s>Saumitri</s>, is to be received by you;

children.text: taṃ ca dṛṣṭvā varāṃl lokān akṣayāṃs tvaṃ gamiṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: and after seeing him you will go to the excellent, imperishable worlds."

children.text: mayā tu vividhaṃ vanyaṃ saṃcitaṃ puruṣarṣabha
children.translated_text: Therefore, O bull among men, I have gathered various forest produce
for your sake, O tiger among men, born on the bank of <s>Pampā</s>."

children.text: evam uktaḥ sa dharmātmā śabaryā śabarīm idam
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Śabarī</s>, righteous <s>Rāghava</s>

children.text: rāghavaḥ prāha vijāne tāṃ nityam abahiṣkṛtām ||
children.translated_text: said this to <s>Śabarī</s>: "I know you to be one never cast aside.

children.text: danoḥ sakāśāt tattvena prabhāvaṃ te mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: From <s>Danu</s> I have heard truly of your greatness, noble lady;

children.text: śrutaṃ pratyakṣam icchāmi saṃdraṣṭuṃ yadi manyase ||
children.translated_text: I wish to see it directly, if you think fit."

children.text: etat tu vacanaṃ śrutvā rāmavaktrād viniḥsṛtam
children.translated_text: Hearing this speech issuing from <s>Rāma</s>'s mouth,

children.text: śabarī darśayāmāsa tāv ubhau tad vanaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śabarī</s> showed both of them that great forest.
"Look, O delight of the <s>Raghu</s> line, at this place, dark as a mass of cloud,
filled with deer and birds, famous by the name <s>Mataṅga</s> forest.

children.text: iha te bhāvitātmāno guravo me mahādyute
children.translated_text: Here, O greatly radiant one, my teachers, whose selves were purified,
performed offerings and made a sacred place, honored by mantras as prescribed.

children.text: iyaṃ pratyaksthalī vedī yatra te me susatkṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: This is the western altar-ground where those teachers, highly honored by me,
made offerings of flowers with hands trembling from fatigue.
By the power of their asceticism, see, O best of the <s>Raghus</s>, even today
the altar-grounds, of unequalled splendor, light up all the quarters with their beauty.
When they were unable to go, exhausted and weary from fasting,
see the seven seas, summoned by their thought, gathered here.

children.text: kṛtābhiṣekais tair nyastā valkalāḥ pādapeṣv iha
children.translated_text: After they had performed their ablutions, they placed their bark garments on the trees here;
even today, O delight of the <s>Raghu</s> line, they do not dry up in this place.

children.text: kṛtsnaṃ vanam idaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ śrotavyaṃ ca śrutaṃ tvayā
children.translated_text: You have seen this whole forest, and what was to be heard has been heard by you.

children.text: tad icchāmy abhyanujñātā tyaktum etat kalevaram ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, with your permission, I wish to abandon this body.

children.text: teṣām icchāmy ahaṃ gantuṃ samīpaṃ bhāvitātmanām
children.translated_text: I wish to go into the presence of those purified souls,

children.text: munīnām āśramo yeṣām ahaṃ ca paricāriṇī ||
children.translated_text: the sages whose hermitage this was, and whose attendant I was."

children.text: dharmiṣṭhaṃ tu vacaḥ śrutvā rāghavaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that most righteous speech, <s>Rāghava</s>, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
said with a delighted face, "I permit you. Go."
Permitted by <s>Rāma</s>, she offered herself into the sacrificial fire,
and, shining like a blazing flame, went straight to heaven.
Where those great seers of meritorious souls dwell in delight,
to that holy place <s>Śabarī</s> went through concentration of the self.

children.text: divaṃ tu tasyāṃ yātāyāṃ śabaryāṃ svena karmaṇā
children.translated_text: When <s>Śabarī</s> had gone to heaven through her own merit,
<s>Rāghava</s>, together with his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, began to reflect.

children.text: cintayitvā tu dharmātmā prabhāvaṃ taṃ mahātmanām
children.translated_text: After considering that power of those great-souled ones, the righteous
