<s>Rāghava</s> spoke to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, single-minded and intent on his welfare.
This hermitage has been seen, dear one, full of many wonders and belonging to perfected souls,
where deer and tigers are at ease and which is frequented by many kinds of birds.

children.text: saptānāṃ ca samudrāṇām eṣu tīrtheṣu lakṣmaṇa
children.translated_text: And here, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, at these tīrthas (sacred bathing places) of the seven oceans,

children.text: upaspṛṣṭaṃ ca vidhivat pitaraś cāpi tarpitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: ablution has been performed according to rule, and the ancestors too have been satisfied.

children.text: pranaṣṭam aśubhaṃ yat tat kalyāṇaṃ samupasthitam
children.translated_text: Whatever inauspiciousness there was has vanished; auspiciousness has arisen.

children.text: tena tv etat prahṛṣṭaṃ me mano lakṣmaṇa samprati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, my mind is now delighted by this.
For, tiger among men, something auspicious will become manifest in my heart.

children.text: tad āgaccha gamiṣyāvaḥ pampāṃ tāṃ priyadarśanām ||
children.translated_text: So come; we shall go to that lovely <s>Pampā</s>,
where Mount <s>Ṛśyamūka</s> shines not far away,
on which righteous <s>Sugrīva</s>, son of the radiant one, dwells,

children.text: nityaṃ vālibhayāt trastaś caturbhiḥ saha vānaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: always terrified by fear of <s>Vālin</s>, together with four vānaras (forest-monkeys).

children.text: abhitvare ca taṃ draṣṭuṃ sugrīvaṃ vānararṣabham
children.translated_text: I am eager to see that <s>Sugrīva</s>, bull among vānaras,

children.text: tadadhīnaṃ hi me saumya sītāyāḥ parimārgaṇam ||
children.translated_text: for the search for <s>Sītā</s> depends on him, dear one.

children.text: iti bruvāṇaṃ taṃ rāmaṃ saumitrir idam abravīt
children.translated_text: As <s>Rāma</s> was speaking thus, <s>Saumitri</s> said this to him:

children.text: gacchāvas tvaritaṃ tatra mamāpi tvarate manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let us go there quickly; my own mind too is eager.

children.text: āśramāt tu tatas tasmān niṣkramya sa viśāṃ patiḥ
children.translated_text: Then, setting out from that hermitage, that lord of men
came to <s>Pampā</s> together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, mighty and unconquered.
Gazing at the flower-rich forest, everywhere filled with broad trees,
with koyaṣṭis, arjunakas, śatapatras, and kīcakas,

children.text: etaiś cānyaiś ca vividhair nāditaṃ tad vanaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: and with these and many other kinds, that great forest resounded.

children.text: sa rāmo vividhān vṛkṣān sarāṃsi vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, seeing various trees and various lakes,
tormented by longing, went to the supreme lake.

children.text: sa tām āsādya vai rāmo dūrād udakavāhinīm
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s>, having approached from afar that water-bearing stream,
entered the lake called <s>Mataṅgasaras</s>.
But <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, overcome by grief,

children.text: viveśa nalinīṃ pampāṃ paṅkajaiś ca samāvṛtām ||
children.translated_text: entered the lotus-pond <s>Pampā</s>, covered with lotuses,
shining with tilaka, aśoka, puṃnāga, bakula, and uddālaka trees,
crowded with lovely groves, its waters pressed thick with lotuses,
rich in water like crystal, spread with smooth sand,
crowded with fish and turtles, beautified by trees standing on its banks,
encircled by entwining creepers as if by female companions,
frequented by kiṃnaras, serpents, gandharvas, yakṣas, and rākṣasas,
strewn with many trees and creepers, lovely and full of cool water,
reddish with fragrant lotuses and white with clusters of kumudas,
blue with masses of blue water-lilies, many-colored like a woven coverlet,
possessing aravindas and utpalas, joined with fragrant lotuses,
bordered by flowering mango groves and resounding with the cries of peacocks.

children.text: sa tāṃ dṛṣṭvā tataḥ pampāṃ rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha
children.translated_text: Then, seeing that <s>Pampā</s> together with <s>Saumitri</s>,
the fiery son of <s>Daśaratha</s> lamented out of longing.

children.text: tilakair bījapūraiś ca vaṭaiḥ śukladrumais tathā
children.translated_text: With tilakas, citron trees, banyans, and white trees,

children.text: puṣpitaiḥ karavīraiś ca puṃnāgaiś ca supuṣpitaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: with flowering karavīras and with puṃnāgas in full bloom,
with mālatī and kunda thickets, and with bhaṇḍīras and niculas,
with aśokas, saptaparṇas, ketakas, and atimuktakas,
and with various other trees, it shone like a lovely woman.

children.text: asyās tīre tu pūrvoktaḥ parvato dhātumaṇḍitaḥ
children.translated_text: On its bank is the mountain mentioned before, adorned with minerals,
known as <s>Ṛśyamūka</s>, with forests of variegated flowers.
A hari (vānara), son of that great-souled one named <s>Ṛkṣarajas</s>,

children.text: adhyāste taṃ mahāvīryaḥ sugrīva iti viśrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: great in valor and famous as <s>Sugrīva</s>, dwells upon it.
Go to <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the vānaras, O bull among men,

children.text: ity uvāca punar vākyaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ satyavikramam ||
children.translated_text: he again said this sentence to truthful and valiant <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: tato mahad vartma ca dūrasaṃkramaṃ krameṇa gatvā pravilokayan vanam
children.translated_text: Then, travelling step by step along a great path hard to traverse from afar, while gazing at the forest,
he saw <s>Pampā</s>, whose groves were lovely to behold and crowded with many different birds.
Having gone to that lotus-pond, filled with lotuses, water-lilies, and fish,
<s>Rāma</s>, accompanied by <s>Saumitri</s>, lamented, his senses agitated.

children.text: tasya dṛṣṭvaiva tāṃ harṣād indriyāṇi cakampire
children.translated_text: At the very sight of it, his senses trembled from delight,

children.text: sa kāmavaśam āpannaḥ saumitrim idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: and, fallen under the power of love, he said this to <s>Saumitri</s>:
<s>Saumitri</s>, see the beautiful-looking forest of <s>Pampā</s>,

children.text: yatra rājanti śailābhā drumāḥ saśikharā iva ||
children.translated_text: where the mountain-like trees shine as if they had peaks.

children.text: māṃ tu śokābhisaṃtaptam ādhayaḥ pīḍayanti vai
children.translated_text: But anxieties torment me, scorched as I am by grief,

children.text: bharatasya ca duḥkhena vaidehyā haraṇena ca ||
children.translated_text: because of <s>Bharata</s>'s sorrow and because of the abduction of <s>Vaidehī</s>.

children.text: adhikaṃ pravibhāty etan nīlapītaṃ tu śādvalam
children.translated_text: This blue and yellow grassland shines all the more,
as though covered with spreads of the trees' various flowers.
This breeze is pleasant, <s>Saumitri</s>; the season is rich in passion,
a fragrant, sweet-smelling month, when the trees have put forth flowers and fruit.
See, <s>Saumitri</s>, the forms of the forests rich in flowers,
shedding showers of blossoms like rainclouds pouring water.
And on the lovely tablelands, the various forest trees,
shaken by the force of the wind, scatter the earth with flowers.
The breeze blows pleasantly to the touch, cool as sandalwood,
among the honey-scented woods, with bees humming along.
on the lovely mountain plateaus, charming with flowering trees
The mountains, their peaks joined together, shine with great trees.
And look at these karṇikāra trees all around, their upper branches in flower,
as though covered with gold, like men wearing yellow garments.
This spring, O <s>Saumitri</s>, resounding with many kinds of birds,
inflames my grief, bereft as I am of <s>Sītā</s>.
For desire torments me, overwhelmed as I am by sorrow,
and the delighted cuckoo, calling aloud, seems to summon me.

children.text: eṣa dātyūhako hṛṣṭo ramye māṃ vananirjhare
children.translated_text: This joyful dātyūha bird, beside the lovely forest waterfall,
will make me grieve, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, as it cries out while I am possessed by desire.
The birds, mingled with their males and delighted in their own flocks,
rejoice with the bhṛṅgarāja birds, O <s>Saumitri</s>, and have sweet voices.
For that doe-eyed woman torments me, O <s>Saumitri</s>,
me who am overpowered by anxiety and grief, and so does the cruel wind of the Caitra woods.
The peacocks, surrounded by peahens on the mountain slopes,
increase desire in me, who am wholly overcome by desire.
Look, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>: a peahen dances near the dancing peacock,
she who is afflicted by desire for her husband on the mountain slopes.

children.text: mayūrasya vane nūnaṃ rakṣasā na hṛtā priyā
children.translated_text: Surely the peacock's beloved has not been carried off in the forest by a <s>rākṣasa</s>;

children.text: mama tv ayaṃ vinā vāsaḥ puṣpamāse suduḥsahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but for me, living without her in the month of flowers is very hard to bear.

children.text: paśya lakṣmaṇa puṣpāṇi niṣphalāni bhavanti me
children.translated_text: Look, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>: the flowers become fruitless for me,
in the forests richly laden with masses of blossoms at winter's end.

children.text: vadanti rāvaṃ muditāḥ śakunāḥ saṃghaśaḥ kalam
children.translated_text: The delighted birds utter soft cries in flocks,
as though calling to one another, and they drive me mad with desire.

children.text: nūnaṃ paravaśā sītā sāpi śocaty ahaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: Surely <s>Sītā</s>, subject to another's power, grieves just as I do,

children.text: śyāmā padmapalāśākṣī mṛdubhāṣā ca me priyā ||
children.translated_text: my beloved, dark-hued, lotus-petal-eyed, and soft-spoken.
This wind, carrying flowers, pleasant to the touch and bearing coolness,
is like fire to me as I think of that beloved woman.

children.text: tāṃ vinātha vihaṃgo 'sau pakṣī praṇaditas tadā
children.translated_text: And now, without her, that winged bird, crying out,
a crow perched in a tree, calls aloud in delight.

children.text: eṣa vai tatra vaidehyā vihagaḥ pratihārakaḥ
children.translated_text: This bird here must be a herald from <s>Vaidehī</s> there;

children.text: pakṣī māṃ tu viśālākṣyāḥ samīpam upaneṣyati ||
children.translated_text: this winged one will bring me near the broad-eyed woman.
Look, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, at the sound in the forest, increasing my intoxication,
of the twice-born birds cooing among the trees whose tips are in flower.
O <s>Saumitri</s>, look: in the varied forest-belts of Pampā,
the lotuses shine in the water like the young sun.
This Pampā, with clear water, stretching wide with lotuses and blue lotuses,
is filled with swans and kāraṇḍava ducks and rich in fragrant flowers.
Always accompanied by cakravāka birds, with varied tablelands and forest spaces,
it shines with herds of elephants and deer coming for water.
For my sight thinks the petals of lotus buds
are like the corners of <s>Sītā</s>'s eyes, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Mixed with lotus filaments and issuing from among the trees,

children.text: niḥśvāsa iva sītāyā vāti vāyur manoharaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the lovely wind blows like <s>Sītā</s>'s breath.
O <s>Saumitri</s>, look on the southern mountain slope of Pampā
at the supremely beautiful flowering stem of the karṇikāra tree.
This great mountain, further adorned with mineral colors,
sends forth variegated dust, shaken loose by the force of the wind.
O <s>Saumitri</s>, the mountain tablelands on every side, with all the trees in bloom,

children.text: niṣpattraiḥ sarvato ramyaiḥ pradīpā iva kiṃśukaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and with leafless, lovely kiṃśukas everywhere, are like lamps.
And these trees growing on Pampā's bank, intertwined and honey-fragrant,
are thickets of mālatī and mallikā, and flowering karavīras.

children.text: ketakyaḥ sinduvārāś ca vāsantyaś ca supuṣpitāḥ
children.translated_text: Ketakīs, sinduvāras, and vāsantīs are in full flower,

children.text: mādhavyo gandhapūrṇāś ca kundagulmāś ca sarvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and mādhavīs filled with fragrance, and kunda bushes everywhere.

children.text: ciribilvā madhūkāś ca vañjulā bakulās tathā
children.translated_text: Ciribilvas, madhūkas, vañjulas, and likewise bakulas,

children.text: campakās tilakāś caiva nāgavṛkṣāś ca puṣpitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: campakas, tilakas, and nāga trees are also in flower.

children.text: nīpāś ca varaṇāś caiva kharjūrāś ca supuṣpitāḥ
children.translated_text: Nīpas and varaṇas too, and date palms in full flower,

children.text: aṅkolāś ca kuraṇṭāś ca cūrṇakāḥ pāribhadrakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: aṅkolas, kuraṇṭas, cūrṇakas, and pāribhadrakas,

children.text: cūtāḥ pāṭalayaś caiva kovidārāś ca puṣpitāḥ
children.translated_text: mango trees and pāṭalas, and flowering kovidāras,
as well as mucukundas and arjunas, are seen on the mountain slopes.
Ketakas and uddālakas too, śirīṣas, śiṃśapās, and dhavas,

children.text: śālmalyaḥ kiṃśukāś caiva raktāḥ kurabakās tathā
children.translated_text: śālmalis, kiṃśukas, and likewise red kurabakas,

children.text: tiniśā naktamālāś ca candanāḥ syandanās tathā ||
children.translated_text: tiniśas, naktamālas, sandalwoods, and syandanas as well,

children.text: vividhā vividhaiḥ puṣpais tair eva nagasānuṣu
children.translated_text: various trees with various flowers, on those very mountain slopes,
have made the rocks appear scattered with yellow and red colors, O <s>Saumitri</s>.
At winter's end, O <s>Saumitri</s>, look at the arising of blossoms on the trees;

children.text: puṣpamāse hi taravaḥ saṃgharṣād iva puṣpitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for in the month of flowers the trees have blossomed as though from rubbing against one another.
Look, O <s>Saumitri</s>, at this cool-watered lake filled with lotuses,
traversed by cakravāka birds and frequented by kāraṇḍavas.
Filled with plavas and krauñcas, visited by boars and deer,
Pampā shines still more with the birds crying out.

children.text: dīpayantīva me kāmaṃ vividhā muditā dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: The many delighted birds seem to kindle my desire,
as I remember my beloved, dark-hued, moon-faced, and lotus-eyed.

children.text: paśya sānuṣu citreṣu mṛgībhiḥ sahitān mṛgān
children.translated_text: Look at the stags together with the does on the beautiful slopes,
while I, by contrast, have been separated from doe-eyed <s>Vaidehī</s>.
Thus lamenting there, his mind struck down by grief,
he looked upon auspicious Pampā, beautiful, fair, and flowing with lovely waters.

children.text: nirīkṣamāṇaḥ sahasā mahātmā sarvaṃ vanaṃ nirjharakandaraṃ ca
children.translated_text: Gazing suddenly, the great-souled one beheld the whole forest, with its waterfalls and caves.

children.text: udvignacetāḥ saha lakṣmaṇena vicārya duḥkhopahataḥ pratasthe ||
children.translated_text: With his mind agitated, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, after considering the matter, he set out, stricken by grief.

children.text: tāv ṛṣyamūkaṃ sahitau prayātau sugrīvaśākhāmṛgasevitaṃ tam
children.translated_text: The two went together to that <s>Ṛṣyamūka</s>, frequented by <s>Sugrīva</s>'s branch-roaming monkeys.

children.text: trastās tu dṛṣṭvā harayo babhūvur mahaujasau rāghavalakṣmaṇau tau ||
children.translated_text: But the monkeys, seeing those two mighty ones, <s>Rāghava</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, became terrified.

children.text: tau tu dṛṣṭvā mahātmānau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
children.translated_text: But on seeing those two great-souled brothers, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
the two heroes bearing excellent weapons, <s>Sugrīva</s> became apprehensive.
With his heart agitated, looking over all the quarters,
the bull among vānaras could not stay in any place.

children.text: naiva cakre manaḥ sthāne vīkṣamāṇo mahābalau
children.translated_text: He did not set his mind on any spot as he looked at the two mighty ones;
the mind of that exceedingly frightened monkey sank down.
Having thought it over, that righteous one weighed what was weighty and light;
<s>Sugrīva</s>, greatly agitated, was with all his followers.

children.text: tataḥ sa sacivebhyas tu sugrīvaḥ plavagādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the leaping monkeys, to his counselors,
greatly agitated and looking at <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, spoke.

children.text: etau vanam idaṃ durgaṃ vālipraṇihitau dhruvam
children.translated_text: These two have surely been sent by <s>Vāli</s> into this inaccessible forest;
wearing bark garments as a disguise, they have come here roaming about.
Then the counselors of <s>Sugrīva</s>, seeing the two very powerful bowmen,

children.text: jagmur giritaṭāt tasmād anyac chikharam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: went from that mountain slope to another excellent peak.
Then the herd-leaders, quickly arriving at the bull of their troop,
the monkeys stood near, surrounding the best of vānaras.
Following one single path, leaping from mountain to mountain,
and shaking the peaks of the mountains with their speed.
Then all the powerful branch-animals, leaping,

children.text: babhañjuś ca nagāṃs tatra puṣpitān durgasaṃśritān ||
children.translated_text: broke there the flowering trees that stood in the difficult terrain.
As the excellent monkeys leapt all around that great mountain,
they went then, frightening deer, wildcats, and tigers.
Then <s>Sugrīva</s>'s counselors, having resorted to the lord of mountains,
met with the chief monkey and all stood with joined palms.
Then, to him who was terrified with fear and suspicious of harm from <s>Vāli</s>,
<s>Hanumān</s>, skilled in speech, said these words to <s>Sugrīva</s>.
Since you, O bull among monkeys, are anxious and have fled,

children.text: taṃ krūradarśanaṃ krūraṃ neha paśyāmi vālinam ||
children.translated_text: I do not see here that cruel <s>Vāli</s>, cruel in appearance.

children.text: yasmāt tava bhayaṃ saumya pūrvajāt pāpakarmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Since your fear, gentle one, is of your elder brother of evil deeds,

children.text: sa neha vālī duṣṭātmā na te paśyāmy ahaṃ bhayam ||
children.translated_text: that wicked-souled <s>Vāli</s> is not here; I see no danger for you.

children.text: aho śākhāmṛgatvaṃ te vyaktam eva plavaṃgama
children.translated_text: Ah, your nature as a branch-animal is quite evident, O leaper,
for through lightness of mind you do not steady yourself in judgment.
Endowed with intellect and discernment, do everything by signs;

children.text: na hy abuddhiṃ gato rājā sarvabhūtāni śāsti hi ||
children.translated_text: for a king who has fallen into folly does not rule all beings.

children.text: sugrīvas tu śubhaṃ vākyaṃ śrutvā sarvaṃ hanūmataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s>, having heard the whole auspicious speech of <s>Hanumān</s>,

children.text: tataḥ śubhataraṃ vākyaṃ hanūmantam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: then spoke an even more auspicious word to <s>Hanumān</s>.
Long-armed, broad-eyed, bearing arrows, bows, and swords,

children.text: kasya na syād bhayaṃ dṛṣṭvā etau surasutopamau ||
children.translated_text: whose fear would not arise on seeing these two, who are like sons of the gods?
I suspect that these two best of men have been sent by <s>Vāli</s>;

children.text: rājāno bahumitrāś ca viśvāso nātra hi kṣamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: kings have many allies, and trust is not proper here.
Enemies moving in disguise must be recognized by a man;
for the untrustworthy strike the trusting at vulnerable points.
In matters to be done <s>Vāli</s> is clever; kings are widely experienced;

children.text: bhavanti parahantāras te jñeyāḥ prākṛtair naraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: they can be killers of enemies, and must be recognized by men in ordinary guise.

children.text: tau tvayā prākṛtenaiva gatvā jñeyau plavaṃgama
children.translated_text: Those two, O leaper, should be investigated by you yourself in ordinary form, after going to them,
by their kinds of gestures and by their appearance and speech.
Observe the intention of the two, whether their minds are pleased,

children.text: viśvāsayan praśaṃsābhir iṅgitaiś ca punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: reassuring them with praises and with repeated signs.
Standing facing me, O bull among monkeys, ask
those bow-bearers the purpose of their entry into this forest.

children.text: śuddhātmānau yadi tv etau jānīhi tvaṃ plavaṃgama
children.translated_text: If these two are pure in intention, then know it, O leaper;

children.text: vyābhāṣitair vā rūpair vā vijñeyā duṣṭatānayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: their evil intent, too, is to be known by their words or by their features.
Thus instructed by the king of monkeys, the son of the Wind

children.text: cakāra gamane buddhiṃ yatra tau rāmalakṣmaṇau ||
children.translated_text: formed the intention to go to where <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> were.

children.text: tatheti sampūjya vacas tu tasya kapeḥ subhītasya durāsadasya
children.translated_text: Saying "So be it" and honoring the command of that deeply frightened, unassailable monkey,

children.text: mahānubhāvo hanumān yayau tadā sa yatra rāmo 'tibalaś ca lakṣmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the mighty <s>Hanumān</s> then went to where <s>Rāma</s> and very strong <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> were.
<s>Hanumān</s>, having understood the word of great-souled <s>Sugrīva</s>,

children.text: parvatād ṛśyamūkāt tu pupluve yatra rāghavau ||
children.translated_text: leapt from Mount <s>Ṛṣyamūka</s> to where the two <s>Rāghavas</s> were.

children.text: sa tatra gatvā hanumān balavān vānarottamaḥ
children.translated_text: Having gone there, powerful <s>Hanumān</s>, the best of vānaras,
approached the two with gentle words, he of true valor.
Abandoning his own form, the monkey, in the form of a mendicant,

children.text: ābabhāṣe ca tau vīrau yathāvat praśaśaṃsa ca ||
children.translated_text: addressed the two heroes and duly praised them.
You two ascetics, like royal seers and gods, firm in sharpened vows,

children.text: deśaṃ katham imaṃ prāptau bhavantau varavarṇinau ||
children.translated_text: how have you, fair in form, reached this region?
You frighten the herds of deer and other forest-roaming creatures,
while looking all around at the trees growing on the bank of <s>Pampā</s>.
You mighty ones beautify this river with auspicious water;
steadfast and golden-hued, who are you two wearing bark garments?
Heroes with the gaze of lions, with courage and power surpassing lions,
grasping bows like the bow of <s>Śakra</s> with your broad arms,
splendid, endowed with beauty, with the stride of the best of bulls.
with arms like elephant trunks, radiant, bulls among men.
This lord of mountains has been illuminated by the splendor of you two.
Worthy of kingship and like immortals, how have you come to this region?
Lotus-petal-eyed heroes, wearing masses of matted hair,
two heroes resembling one another, you seem to have come from the world of the gods.
As if arriving by chance, you are like the moon and the sun come down to the earth,
broad-chested heroes, human, yet godlike in form.
Lion-shouldered and mighty in nature, like two strong bulls in rut,

children.text: āyatāś ca suvṛttāś ca bāhavaḥ parighottamāḥ
children.translated_text: your arms are long and well-rounded, like the finest iron clubs.
Worthy to be adorned with every ornament, why are they not adorned?

children.text: ubhau yogyāv ahaṃ manye rakṣituṃ pṛthivīm imām
children.translated_text: I think both of you are fit to protect this earth,
the whole earth with its oceans and forests, adorned by <s>Vindhya</s> and <s>Meru</s>.

children.text: ime ca dhanuṣī citre ślakṣṇe citrānulepane
children.translated_text: And these wonderful bows, smooth and beautifully painted,
shine like <s>Indra</s>'s two thunderbolts adorned with gold.
And your quivers, pleasant to behold, are filled with sharp arrows,
terrible, life-ending, like blazing serpents.
These two swords, large in measure and broad, adorned with refined gold,
gleam like two snakes released from their sloughs.

children.text: evaṃ māṃ paribhāṣantaṃ kasmād vai nābhibhāṣathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As I address you in this way, why do you not speak to me?
There is a certain righteous lord of monkey troops named <s>Sugrīva</s>,

children.text: vīro vinikṛto bhrātrā jagad bhramati duḥkhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a hero wronged by his brother, who wanders the world in sorrow.
I have come here sent by that great-souled <s>Sugrīva</s>,
the king of the foremost monkeys; I am a monkey named <s>Hanumān</s>.

children.text: yuvābhyāṃ saha dharmātmā sugrīvaḥ sakhyam icchati
children.translated_text: The righteous <s>Sugrīva</s> wishes friendship with you two.

children.text: tasya māṃ sacivaṃ vittaṃ vānaraṃ pavanātmajam ||
children.translated_text: Know me to be his minister, a monkey, the son of the Wind.
Disguised under the appearance of a mendicant, out of desire for <s>Sugrīva</s>'s welfare,
I have come here from <s>Ṛśyamūka</s>, able to go where I wish and take whatever form I wish.

children.text: evam uktvā tu hanumāṃs tau vīrau rāmalakṣmaṇau
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to those two heroes, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
<s>Hanumān</s>, expert in expression and skilled in speech, said nothing more.

children.text: etac chrutvā vacas tasya rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt
children.translated_text: Hearing these words of his, <s>Rāma</s> spoke to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
the illustrious one, his face delighted, to his brother standing at his side:
This is the minister of the great-souled <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of monkeys.
He has come into my presence, while I am seeking that very one.
Address him, O <s>Saumitri</s>, this monkey who is <s>Sugrīva</s>'s minister,
this knower of speech, this foe-subduer, with sweet words full of affection.

children.text: tataḥ prahṛṣṭo hanumān kṛtyavān iti tad vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Hanumān</s>, delighted and hearing those words, understood that the matter could be accomplished;
on hearing that sweet address, he turned his mind toward <s>Sugrīva</s>.
The return of kingship for that great-souled <s>Sugrīva</s> is likely,

children.text: yad ayaṃ kṛtyavān prāptaḥ kṛtyaṃ caitad upāgatam ||
children.translated_text: since this capable man has arrived and this business has now appeared.
Then <s>Hanumān</s>, the best of leapers, filled with supreme joy,
replied with these words to <s>Rāma</s>, being skilled in speech:
For what purpose have you come, with your younger brother, to this terrible forest, adorned by the groves of <s>Pampā</s>,
hard to traverse and filled with many kinds of serpents and wild beasts?
Hearing those words of his, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, urged by <s>Rāma</s>,
described the great-souled <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>.
There was a radiant king named <s>Daśaratha</s>, devoted to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order).

children.text: tasyāyaṃ pūrvajaḥ putro rāmo nāma janaiḥ śrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is his elder son, known among people by the name <s>Rāma</s>.
He is a refuge for all beings and one who fully carries out his father's command.
This hero is the most excellent in virtues among <s>Daśaratha</s>'s sons.

children.text: rājyād bhraṣṭo vane vastuṃ mayā sārdham ihāgataḥ
children.translated_text: Removed from the kingdom, he has come here with me to dwell in the forest.
And the self-controlled, greatly radiant one was followed by his wife <s>Sītā</s>,
as the radiant sun at day's end is followed by its light.

children.text: aham asyāvaro bhrātā guṇair dāsyam upāgataḥ
children.translated_text: I am his younger brother, named <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, who through his virtues has come into service
to this grateful and deeply learned man.
He deserves happiness and the highest honor, and his heart is set on the welfare of all beings;
yet he has been deprived of sovereignty and has taken to dwelling in the forest.
His wife was carried off, while he was away, by a shape-shifting <s>rākṣasa</s> (demon),

children.text: tac ca na jñāyate rakṣaḥ patnī yenāsya sā hṛtā ||
children.translated_text: and that <s>rākṣasa</s> by whom his wife was taken is not known.

children.text: danur nāma śriyaḥ putraḥ śāpād rākṣasatāṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: A being named <s>Danu</s>, son of <s>Śrī</s>, had become a <s>rākṣasa</s> through a curse.
By him <s>Sugrīva</s>, the capable lord of monkeys, was pointed out to us.
He, of great valor, will know the abductor of your wife.

children.text: evam uktvā danuḥ svargaṃ bhrājamāno gataḥ sukham ||
children.translated_text: After saying this, <s>Danu</s>, shining brightly, went happily to heaven.

children.text: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yāthātathyena pṛcchataḥ
children.translated_text: All this has been told to you truthfully, since you asked.

children.text: ahaṃ caiva hi rāmaś ca sugrīvaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatau ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, both I and <s>Rāma</s> have gone to <s>Sugrīva</s> for refuge.

children.text: eṣa dattvā ca vittāni prāpya cānuttamaṃ yaśaḥ
children.translated_text: This man, who once gave away riches and obtained unsurpassed fame,

children.text: lokanāthaḥ purā bhūtvā sugrīvaṃ nātham icchati ||
children.translated_text: having formerly been a protector of the world, now seeks <s>Sugrīva</s> as his protector.

children.text: śokābhibhūte rāme tu śokārte śaraṇaṃ gate
children.translated_text: Since <s>Rāma</s> is overcome by grief, afflicted with sorrow, and has come for refuge,

children.text: kartum arhati sugrīvaḥ prasādaṃ saha yūthapaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s>, together with his troop-leaders, ought to show him favor.
As <s>Saumitri</s> spoke thus, piteously, with tears falling,
<s>Hanumān</s>, skilled in speech, replied with these words:
Men such as these, endowed with intelligence, masters of anger and masters of their senses,
should be seen by the lord of monkeys; by good fortune they have come into view.

children.text: sa hi rājyāc ca vibhraṣṭaḥ kṛtavairaś ca vālinā
children.translated_text: For he too has been deprived of his kingdom and has made an enemy of <s>Vālin</s>;

children.text: hṛtadāro vane trasto bhrātrā vinikṛto bhṛśam ||
children.translated_text: his wife has been taken, he is fearful in the forest, and he has been grievously wronged by his brother.
That son of the Sun, <s>Sugrīva</s>, will give help to you two,
together with us, in the search for <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: ity evam uktvā hanumāñ ślakṣṇaṃ madhurayā girā
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Hanumān</s>, in a smooth, sweet voice,
said to <s>Rāghava</s>, 'Let us go to <s>Sugrīva</s>.'

children.text: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ dharmātmā hanūmantaṃ sa lakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: As <s>Hanumān</s> spoke in this way, righteous <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
having duly honored him, said this to <s>Rāghava</s>:
This monkey, this son of the Wind, speaks joyfully in such a way;
he too has come with a purpose. You have achieved your purpose, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: prasannamukhavarṇaś ca vyaktaṃ hṛṣṭaś ca bhāṣate
children.translated_text: His face is bright, and he plainly speaks with joy;
the heroic <s>Hanumān</s>, son of the Wind, will not speak falsely.

children.text: tataḥ sa tu mahāprājño hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the very wise <s>Hanumān</s>, son of the Wind,
went, taking the two heroic <s>Rāghavas</s>, to the king of the monkeys.

children.text: sa tu vipulayaśāḥ kapipravīraḥ pavanasutaḥ kṛtakṛtyavat prahṛṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: That broad-famed chief among monkeys, the son of the Wind, rejoicing like one whose task was done,

children.text: girivaram uruvikramaḥ prayātaḥ sa śubhamatiḥ saha rāmalakṣmaṇābhyām ||
children.translated_text: mighty in stride and auspicious in mind, set out for the excellent mountain with <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: ṛśyamūkāt tu hanumān gatvā taṃ malayaṃ girim
children.translated_text: Then <s>Hanumān</s>, going from <s>Ṛśyamūka</s> to that <s>Malaya</s> mountain,
announced the two heroic <s>Rāghavas</s> to the king of the monkeys.
This is wise <s>Rāma</s>, of firm valor, who has arrived here;
this is <s>Rāma</s> of unfailing valor, together with his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Born in the line of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s>, <s>Rāma</s> is the son of <s>Daśaratha</s>;
he is renowned for <s>dharma</s> and is obedient to his father's command.
While this disciplined, great-souled man was dwelling in the forest,

children.text: rakṣasāpahṛtā bhāryā sa tvāṃ śaraṇam āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: his wife was carried off by a rākṣasa, and he has come to you for refuge.
By him the fire was satisfied with rājasūya and aśvamedha sacrifices,
and gifts were likewise bestowed, cows by the hundreds of thousands.
By austerity and truthful speech the earth was protected by him;

children.text: strīhetos tasya putro 'yaṃ rāmas tvāṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: this <s>Rāma</s>, his son, has come to you for refuge on account of his wife.
The two brothers, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, desire friendship with you;
receive and honor these two, both most worthy of honor.
Hearing <s>Hanumān</s>'s words, <s>Sugrīva</s> was delighted in mind,

children.text: bhayaṃ sa rāghavād ghoraṃ prajahau vigatajvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, freed from distress, he cast off his dreadful fear of <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: sa kṛtvā mānuṣaṃ rūpaṃ sugrīvaḥ plavagādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the monkeys, assuming a human form,
became most pleasing to behold and spoke affectionately to <s>Rāghava</s>:
You are disciplined by <s>dharma</s>, valiant, and kind to all;
the son of the Wind has accurately described your virtues to me.

children.text: tan mamaivaiṣa satkāro lābhaś caivottamaḥ prabho
children.translated_text: Therefore this is indeed an honor for me, and also the highest gain, O lord,

children.text: yat tvam icchasi sauhārdaṃ vānareṇa mayā saha ||
children.translated_text: that you wish for friendship with me, a monkey.

children.text: rocate yadi vā sakhyaṃ bāhur eṣa prasāritaḥ
children.translated_text: If friendship pleases you, this arm is stretched out;

children.text: gṛhyatāṃ pāṇinā pāṇir maryādā badhyatāṃ dhruvā ||
children.translated_text: let hand be clasped with hand, and let a firm covenant be established.

children.text: etat tu vacanaṃ śrutvā sugrīvasya subhāṣitam
children.translated_text: Hearing this well-spoken statement of <s>Sugrīva</s>,
he, delighted in mind, pressed his hand with his own hand,
and, taking hold of heartfelt friendship, embraced him closely.
Then <s>Hanumān</s>, subduer of foes, abandoned his mendicant's form,
and, in his own form, produced fire from two pieces of wood.

children.text: dīpyamānaṃ tato vahniṃ puṣpair abhyarcya satkṛtam
children.translated_text: Then he worshiped the blazing fire with flowers and honored it,

children.text: tayor madhye tu suprīto nidadhe susamāhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, very pleased and composed, placed it between the two of them.

children.text: tato 'gniṃ dīpyamānaṃ tau cakratuś ca pradakṣiṇam
children.translated_text: Then the two of them circumambulated the blazing fire,
and <s>Sugrīva</s> and <s>Rāghava</s> entered into friendship.
Then, their minds greatly pleased, both the monkey and <s>Rāghava</s>,
looking at one another, did not reach satiety.
Then the radiant <s>Sugrīva</s>, single-minded, spoke a sentence

children.text: sugrīvaḥ prāha tejasvī vākyam ekamanās tadā ||
children.translated_text: to <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, who understood every matter:

children.text: ayam ākhyāti me rāma sacivo mantrisattamaḥ
children.translated_text: O <s>Rāma</s>, this minister of mine, <s>Hanumān</s>, the best of counselors, tells me

children.text: hanumān yannimittaṃ tvaṃ nirjanaṃ vanam āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the reason for which you have come to the desolate forest.

children.text: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā vasataś ca vane tava
children.translated_text: While you were dwelling in the forest with your brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
your wife, <s>Maithilī</s>, daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, was carried off by a rākṣasa.

children.text: tvayā viyuktā rudatī lakṣmaṇena ca dhīmatā
children.translated_text: Separated from you and from wise <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, she was crying out,

children.text: antaraṃ prepsunā tena hatvā gṛdhraṃ jaṭāyuṣam ||
children.translated_text: after that rākṣasa, seeking his chance, had killed the vulture <s>Jaṭāyus</s>.
Before long you will be released from the sorrow born of separation from your wife;

children.text: ahaṃ tām ānayiṣyāmi naṣṭāṃ vedaśrutiṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: I shall bring her back, like a lost Vedic revelation.

children.text: rasātale vā vartantīṃ vartantīṃ vā nabhastale
children.translated_text: Whether she is dwelling in <s>Rasātala</s> or dwelling in the sky,

children.text: aham ānīya dāsyāmi tava bhāryām ariṃdama ||
children.translated_text: I will bring your wife and give her to you, O subduer of foes.

children.text: idaṃ tathyaṃ mama vacas tvam avehi ca rāghava
children.translated_text: Know this word of mine to be true, O <s>Rāghava</s>;

children.text: tyaja śokaṃ mahābāho tāṃ kāntām ānayāmi te ||
children.translated_text: abandon grief, mighty-armed one. I shall bring that beloved woman to you.

children.text: anumānāt tu jānāmi maithilī sā na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: From inference I know that she is <s>Maithilī</s>, without doubt;
I saw her being carried away by a rākṣasa of cruel deeds.

children.text: krośantī rāma rāmeti lakṣmaṇeti ca visvaram
children.translated_text: She was crying out loudly, '<s>Rāma</s>, <s>Rāma</s>!' and '<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>!',
trembling in <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s lap like the wife of the lord of serpents.

children.text: ātmanā pañcamaṃ māṃ hi dṛṣṭvā śailataṭe sthitam
children.translated_text: Seeing me standing on the mountain slope as the fifth among five,

children.text: uttarīyaṃ tayā tyaktaṃ śubhāny ābharaṇāni ca ||
children.translated_text: she dropped her upper garment and fine ornaments.

children.text: tāny asmābhir gṛhītāni nihitāni ca rāghava
children.translated_text: We took those things and put them away, O <s>Rāghava</s>;
I shall bring them. You ought to recognize them.

children.text: tam abravīt tato rāmaḥ sugrīvaṃ priyavādinam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s> said to <s>Sugrīva</s>, who spoke pleasingly,
Bring them quickly, my friend. Why are you delaying?

children.text: evam uktas tu sugrīvaḥ śailasya gahanāṃ guhām
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Sugrīva</s> quickly entered
the deep cave of the mountain, from a desire to do what was dear to <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: uttarīyaṃ gṛhītvā tu śubhāny ābharaṇāni ca
children.translated_text: Then, taking the upper garment and the fine ornaments,
the monkey showed them to <s>Rāma</s>, saying, 'Look at this.'

children.text: tato gṛhītvā tadvāsaḥ śubhāny ābharaṇāni ca
children.translated_text: Then, taking that garment and the fine ornaments,
He became choked with tears, like the moon by mist.
But he was stained by tears that had arisen from affection for <s>Sītā</s>;

children.text: hā priyeti rudan dhairyam utsṛjya nyapatat kṣitau ||
children.translated_text: crying, "Ah, beloved!" he abandoned his firmness and fell to the ground.

children.text: hṛdi kṛtvā sa bahuśas tam alaṃkāram uttamam
children.translated_text: Placing that excellent ornament upon his breast again and again,

children.text: niśaśvāsa bhṛśaṃ sarpo bilastha iva roṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he sighed deeply, like an angered serpent in its hole.
With his flow of tears unbroken, he looked at <s>Saumitri</s> beside him,
and <s>Rāma</s>, wretched, began to lament.
Look, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>: this upper garment, cast off by <s>Vaidehī</s> as she was being carried away,

children.text: uttarīyam idaṃ bhūmau śarīrād bhūṣaṇāni ca ||
children.translated_text: and these ornaments from her body lie here upon the ground.
This ornament must surely have been dropped by <s>Sītā</s> as she was being carried away

children.text: utsṛṣṭaṃ bhūṣaṇam idaṃ tathārūpaṃ hi dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: onto the grassy earth; for it is seen here in just such a condition.

children.text: brūhi sugrīva kaṃ deśaṃ hriyantī lakṣitā tvayā
children.translated_text: Tell me, <s>Sugrīva</s>, in what region she was seen by you as she was being carried away,
my beloved, equal to my life, by a rākṣasa of terrible form.

children.text: kva vā vasati tad rakṣo mahad vyasanadaṃ mama
children.translated_text: Or where does that rākṣasa dwell, who brings this great misery upon me,
on whose account I shall destroy all the rākṣasas?

children.text: haratā maithilīṃ yena māṃ ca roṣayatā bhṛśam
children.translated_text: By him who carried off <s>Maithilī</s> and enraged me greatly,
the gate of death has been opened for the ending of his own life.

children.text: mama dayitatamā hṛtā vanād rajanicareṇa vimathya yena sā
children.translated_text: She who is dearest to me was seized from the forest by that night-roamer, after he overpowered her.

children.text: kathaya mama ripuṃ tam adya vai pravagapate yamasaṃnidhiṃ nayāmi ||
children.translated_text: Tell me now of that enemy of mine, lord of monkeys, whom I shall lead to the presence of <s>Yama</s>.

children.text: evam uktas tu sugrīvo rāmeṇārtena vānaraḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the distressed <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Sugrīva</s>, the monkey,
with joined palms and with tears, his voice choked by sobbing, spoke these words:

children.text: na jāne nilayaṃ tasya sarvathā pāparakṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: I do not know in any way the dwelling of that sinful rākṣasa,

children.text: sāmarthyaṃ vikramaṃ vāpi dauṣkuleyasya vā kulam ||
children.translated_text: nor his power, nor his valor, nor the family of that low-born one.

children.text: satyaṃ tu pratijānāmi tyaja śokam ariṃdama
children.translated_text: But I pledge this truth: abandon grief, crusher of foes.

children.text: kariṣyāmi tathā yatnaṃ yathā prāpsyasi maithilīm ||
children.translated_text: I shall make such an effort that you will recover <s>Maithilī</s>.
Having killed <s>Rāvaṇa</s> together with his followers, and satisfying my own valor,

children.text: tathāsmi kartā nacirād yathā prīto bhaviṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: I shall act in such a way that before long you will be pleased.

children.text: alaṃ vaiklavyam ālambya dhairyam ātmagataṃ smara
children.translated_text: Enough of clinging to weakness; remember the courage that is within you.
Such lightness of judgment is not fitting for men like you.
I too have met with a great calamity, born from the abduction of my wife,

children.text: na cāham evaṃ śocāmi na ca dhairyaṃ parityaje ||
children.translated_text: yet I do not grieve like this, nor do I abandon courage.

children.text: nāhaṃ tām anuśocāmi prākṛto vānaro 'pi san
children.translated_text: Though I am only an ordinary monkey, I do not mourn her so;

children.text: mahātmā ca vinītaś ca kiṃ punar dhṛtimān bhavān ||
children.translated_text: how much less should you, who are great-souled, disciplined, and steadfast?

children.text: bāṣpam āpatitaṃ dhairyān nigrahītuṃ tvam arhasi
children.translated_text: You ought, through firmness, to restrain the tears that have come upon you.
You ought not to cast away the steadiness that is the boundary of those endowed with strength.

children.text: vyasane vārthakṛcchre vā bhaye vā jīvitāntage
children.translated_text: In misfortune, in difficulty over wealth, in fear, or when life itself is at an end,

children.text: vimṛśan vai svayā buddhyā dhṛtimān nāvasīdati ||
children.translated_text: a steadfast man, reflecting with his own intelligence, does not sink down.

children.text: bāliśas tu naro nityaṃ vaiklavyaṃ yo 'nuvartate
children.translated_text: But the foolish man who constantly follows after weakness

children.text: sa majjaty avaśaḥ śoke bhārākrānteva naur jale ||
children.translated_text: sinks helplessly in grief, like a boat in water overloaded by its burden.

children.text: eṣo 'ñjalir mayā baddhaḥ praṇayāt tvāṃ prasādaye
children.translated_text: This respectful salutation has been made by me; out of affection I seek to pacify you.

children.text: pauruṣaṃ śraya śokasya nāntaraṃ dātum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: Take refuge in manly strength; you ought not to give grief an opening.

children.text: ye śokam anuvartante na teṣāṃ vidyate sukham
children.translated_text: Those who follow after grief have no happiness.

children.text: tejaś ca kṣīyate teṣāṃ na tvaṃ śocitum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: Their vigor too is diminished; you ought not to grieve.
I speak what is beneficial in the manner of a friend; I am not instructing you.

children.text: vayasyatāṃ pūjayan me na tvaṃ śocitum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: Honoring my friendship, you ought not to grieve.

children.text: madhuraṃ sāntvitas tena sugrīveṇa sa rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Sweetly comforted by that <s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>Rāghava</s>
wiped his face, wet with tears, with the edge of his garment.
Then lord <s>Kākutstha</s>, restored to his natural state by <s>Sugrīva</s>'s words,
embraced <s>Sugrīva</s> and spoke these words:

children.text: kartavyaṃ yad vayasyena snigdhena ca hitena ca
children.translated_text: What should be done by a friend who is affectionate and beneficial,

children.text: anurūpaṃ ca yuktaṃ ca kṛtaṃ sugrīva tat tvayā ||
children.translated_text: that fitting and proper deed has been done by you, <s>Sugrīva</s>.

children.text: eṣa ca prakṛtiṣṭho 'ham anunītas tvayā sakhe
children.translated_text: Here I am, restored to myself after being consoled by you, my friend.

children.text: durlabho hīdṛśo bandhur asmin kāle viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Such a kinsman is hard to obtain, especially at a time like this.

children.text: kiṃ tu yatnas tvayā kāryo maithilyāḥ parimārgaṇe
children.translated_text: But effort must be made by you in the search for <s>Maithilī</s>
and for the wicked <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the terrible rākṣasa.

children.text: mayā ca yad anuṣṭheyaṃ viśrabdhena tad ucyatām
children.translated_text: And whatever I must do, let it be told to me confidently.

children.text: varṣāsv iva ca sukṣetre sarvaṃ saṃpadyate tava ||
children.translated_text: Everything of yours will come to fulfillment, like a good field in the rains.

children.text: mayā ca yad idaṃ vākyam abhimānāt samīritam
children.translated_text: And this word that I have uttered from confidence in myself,

children.text: tat tvayā hariśārdūla tattvam ity upadhāryatām ||
children.translated_text: you should understand, tiger among monkeys, to be the truth.

children.text: anṛtaṃ noktapūrvaṃ me na ca vakṣye kadācana
children.translated_text: I have never before spoken a falsehood, nor shall I ever speak one.

children.text: etat te pratijānāmi satyenaiva śapāmi te ||
children.translated_text: This I promise you; by truth itself I swear to you.

children.text: tataḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ sugrīvo vānaraiḥ sacivaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sugrīva</s>, delighted, together with his monkey ministers,
heard the speech of <s>Rāghava</s>, especially the promise he had made.

children.text: mahānubhāvasya vaco niśamya harir narāṇām ṛṣabhasya tasya
children.translated_text: Hearing the words of that great-souled bull among men,

children.text: kṛtaṃ sa mene harivīramukhyas tadā svakāryaṃ hṛdayena vidvān ||
children.translated_text: the chief of monkey heroes, wise in heart, then considered his own business accomplished.

children.text: parituṣṭas tu sugrīvas tena vākyena vānaraḥ
children.translated_text: Satisfied by that speech, <s>Sugrīva</s>, the monkey,
spoke these words to <s>Rāma</s>, the elder brother of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:
In every way I am surely favored by the gods, without doubt,
since you, endowed with excellent virtues, are my friend.

children.text: śakyaṃ khalu bhaved rāma sahāyena tvayānagha
children.translated_text: With you as an ally, <s>Rāma</s>, sinless lord, it would indeed be possible

children.text: surarājyam api prāptuṃ svarājyaṃ kiṃ punaḥ prabho ||
children.translated_text: to obtain even the sovereignty of the gods, how much more my own kingdom.

children.text: so 'haṃ sabhājyo bandhūnāṃ suhṛdāṃ caiva rāghava
children.translated_text: So I am to be honored by my kinsmen and by my friends, <s>Rāghava</s>,
since I have obtained, with fire as witness, a friend born in the line of <s>Raghu</s>.

children.text: aham apy anurūpas te vayasyo jñāsyase śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: I too am a fitting friend for you; you will know this gradually.

children.text: na tu vaktuṃ samartho 'haṃ svayam ātmagatān guṇān ||
children.translated_text: But I myself am not able to speak of the virtues that belong to me.
Yet among great-souled men, especially among perfected men such as you,

children.text: niścalā bhavati prītir dhairyam ātmavatām iva ||
children.translated_text: affection becomes steady, like firmness in self-possessed men.

children.text: rajataṃ vā suvarṇaṃ vā vastrāṇy ābharaṇāni vā
children.translated_text: Whether silver or gold, or garments or ornaments,
good men understand them as undivided among the good.

children.text: āḍhyo vāpi daridro vā duḥkhitaḥ sukhito 'pi vā
children.translated_text: Whether rich or poor, afflicted or even happy,

children.text: nirdoṣo vā sadoṣo vā vayasyaḥ paramā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether free of fault or with fault, a friend is the highest refuge.
The giving up of wealth, the giving up of happiness, and again even the giving up of the body
come into action for the sake of a friend, when such affection is seen.

children.text: tat tathety abravīd rāmaḥ sugrīvaṃ priyavādinam
children.translated_text: "That is so," said <s>Rāma</s> to <s>Sugrīva</s>, who spoke pleasingly,
before <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, with splendor like that of wise <s>Vāsava</s>.

children.text: tato rāmaṃ sthitaṃ dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahābalam
children.translated_text: Then, seeing <s>Rāma</s> standing there, and also mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: sugrīvaḥ sarvataś cakṣur vane lolam apātayat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s> cast his restless eyes everywhere in the forest.

children.text: sa dadarśa tataḥ sālam avidūre harīśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Then the lord of monkeys saw, not far away, a sāla tree,
in full blossom, somewhat rich in leaves, and adorned by bees.
Breaking off from that sāla one branch thick with leaves and well flowered,
<s>Sugrīva</s> spread it out and sat down on it with <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: tāv āsīnau tato dṛṣṭvā hanūmān api lakṣmaṇam
children.translated_text: Then, seeing those two seated, <s>Hanumān</s> also
uprooted a sāla branch and respectfully seated <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: tataḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ sugrīvaḥ ślakṣṇaṃ madhurayā girā
children.translated_text: Then delighted <s>Sugrīva</s>, with smooth and sweet speech,
spoke to <s>Rāma</s> out of affection, his syllables confused by joy:

children.text: ahaṃ vinikṛto bhrātrā carāmy eṣa bhayārditaḥ
children.translated_text: I have been wronged by my brother, and I wander here tormented by fear,
on the excellent mountain <s>Ṛṣyamūka</s>, deprived of my wife and deeply miserable.

children.text: so 'haṃ trasto bhaye magno vasāmy udbhrāntacetanaḥ
children.translated_text: So I, frightened and sunk in fear, live with an agitated mind,

children.text: vālinā nikṛto bhrātrā kṛtavairaś ca rāghava ||
children.translated_text: wronged by my brother <s>Vāli</s> and made his enemy, O <s>Rāghava</s>.
Since I am afflicted by fear of <s>Vāli</s>, O giver of fearlessness to all the worlds,

children.text: mamāpi tvam anāthasya prasādaṃ kartum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: you ought to show favor even to me, who am without a protector.

children.text: evam uktas tu tejasvī dharmajño dharmavatsalaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, the splendid <s>Kākutstha</s>, knower of <s>dharma</s> and devoted to <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: pratyuvāca sa kākutsthaḥ sugrīvaṃ prahasann iva ||
children.translated_text: answered <s>Sugrīva</s>, as though smiling:
A friend is the fruit of doing help; doing harm is the mark of an enemy.
This very day I shall kill him who has carried off your wife.

children.text: ime hi me mahāvegāḥ pattriṇas tigmatejasaḥ
children.translated_text: For these arrows of mine are very swift, feathered, and keen in brilliance,
born from the grove of <s>Kārttikeya</s> and adorned with gold.
Covered with heron feathers, like the thunderbolt of great <s>Indra</s>,
well jointed and very sharp-pointed, they are like angry serpents.
Look upon <s>Vāli</s>, your enemy bearing the name of brother, who has committed sin,

children.text: śarair vinihataṃ paśya vikīrṇam iva parvatam ||
children.translated_text: struck down by my arrows and scattered like a mountain.
Hearing <s>Rāghava</s>'s words, <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of armies,

children.text: praharṣam atulaṃ lebhe sādhu sādhv iti cābravīt ||
children.translated_text: obtained incomparable joy and said, "Good, good!"
O <s>Rāma</s>, I am overwhelmed by grief; you are the refuge of those afflicted by grief.

children.text: vayasya iti kṛtvā hi tvayy ahaṃ paridevaye ||
children.translated_text: Because I regard you as a friend, I lament before you.
For through the giving of the hand, with fire as witness, you have become my friend,

children.text: kṛtaḥ prāṇair bahumataḥ satyenāpi śapāmy aham ||
children.translated_text: honored by me more than life itself; by truth too I swear this.

children.text: vayasya iti kṛtvā ca viśrabdhaṃ pravadāmy aham
children.translated_text: And because I regard you as a friend, I speak in trust

children.text: duḥkham antargataṃ yan me mano dahati nityaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: of the sorrow within me that constantly burns my mind.
Having spoken this much, his eyes stained with tears,
with a voice choked by tears he could not speak loudly.
But the rush of tears that had suddenly come like the rush of a river
<s>Sugrīva</s> held back with firmness in <s>Rāma</s>'s presence.

children.text: saṃnigṛhya tu taṃ bāṣpaṃ pramṛjya nayane śubhe
children.translated_text: Having restrained those tears and wiped his fair eyes,

children.text: viniḥśvasya ca tejasvī rāghavaṃ punar abravīt ||
children.translated_text: the splendid one sighed and again spoke to <s>Rāghava</s>:

children.text: purāhaṃ vālinā rāma rājyāt svād avaropitaḥ
children.translated_text: In the past, O <s>Rāma</s>, I was cast down by <s>Vāli</s> from my own kingdom,
and after being made to hear harsh words, I was driven away by the stronger one.

children.text: hṛtā bhāryā ca me tena prāṇebhyo 'pi garīyasī
children.translated_text: My wife too, dearer to me than my life, was taken by him,

children.text: suhṛdaś ca madīyā ye saṃyatā bandhaneṣu te ||
children.translated_text: and those friends who are mine have been bound in fetters.
And the very wicked-minded one, O <s>Rāghava</s>, is intent on my destruction.

children.text: bahuśas tat prayuktāś ca vānarā nihatā mayā ||
children.translated_text: Many times monkeys sent by him for that purpose have been killed by me.

children.text: śaṅkayā tv etayā cāhaṃ dṛṣṭvā tvām api rāghava
children.translated_text: And because of this suspicion, O <s>Rāghava</s>, even after seeing you,

children.text: nopasarpāmy ahaṃ bhīto bhaye sarve hi bibhyati ||
children.translated_text: I did not approach you; being afraid, all men fear danger.

children.text: kevalaṃ hi sahāyā me hanumatpramukhās tv ime
children.translated_text: Only these here, headed by <s>Hanumān</s>, are my helpers.

children.text: ato 'haṃ dhārayāmy adya prāṇān kṛcchragato 'pi san ||
children.translated_text: Therefore today, though I am in hardship, I keep myself alive.

children.text: ete hi kapayaḥ snigdhā māṃ rakṣanti samantataḥ
children.translated_text: For these affectionate monkeys guard me on every side,

children.text: saha gacchanti gantavye nityaṃ tiṣṭhanti ca sthite ||
children.translated_text: go with me when I must go, and always stand by me when I stay.

children.text: saṃkṣepas tv eṣa me rāma kim uktvā vistaraṃ hi te
children.translated_text: This, O <s>Rāma</s>, is my account in brief; what need is there to speak of it to you at length?

children.text: sa me jyeṣṭho ripur bhrātā vālī viśrutapauruṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That elder brother of mine, <s>Vālī</s>, famous for his prowess, is my enemy.

children.text: tadvināśāddhi me duḥkhaṃ pranaṣṭaṃ syād anantaram
children.translated_text: From his destruction my sorrow would at once be destroyed,
and my happiness and my life itself depend on his destruction.

children.text: eṣa me rāma śokāntaḥ śokārtena niveditaḥ
children.translated_text: This, O <s>Rāma</s>, is the end of my grief, told by one afflicted with grief.

children.text: duḥkhito 'duḥkhito vāpi sakhyur nityaṃ sakhā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whether in sorrow or not in sorrow, a friend is always the refuge of a friend.

children.text: śrutvaitac ca vaco rāmaḥ sugrīvam idam abravīt
children.translated_text: Hearing this speech, <s>Rāma</s> said this to <s>Sugrīva</s>:

children.text: kiṃnimittam abhūd vairaṃ śrotum icchāmi tattvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: For what reason did this enmity arise? I wish to hear it truly.

children.text: sukhaṃ hi kāraṇaṃ śrutvā vairasya tava vānara
children.translated_text: For, O monkey, after hearing comfortably the cause of your enmity,
I shall bring about the next act, after considering strength and weakness.

children.text: balavān hi mamāmarṣaḥ śrutvā tvām avamānitam
children.translated_text: For my powerful anger, having heard that you have been humiliated,
grows, shaking my heart, like the force of waters in the rainy season.

children.text: hṛṣṭaḥ kathaya viśrabdho yāvad āropyate dhanuḥ
children.translated_text: Tell me gladly and confidently, until the bow is strung;

children.text: sṛṣṭaś ca hi mayā bāṇo nirastaś ca ripus tava ||
children.translated_text: for an arrow has been released by me, and your enemy has been struck down.

children.text: evam uktas tu sugrīvaḥ kākutsthena mahātmanā
children.translated_text: When <s>Sugrīva</s> had been addressed in this way by the great-souled <s>Kākutstha</s>,

children.text: praharṣam atulaṃ lebhe caturbhiḥ saha vānaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: he obtained unequalled joy, together with the four monkeys.
Then, with a delighted face, <s>Sugrīva</s> began
to tell the true cause of the enmity to the elder brother of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: vālī nāma mama bhrātā jyeṣṭhaḥ śatruniṣūdanaḥ
children.translated_text: There is a brother of mine named <s>Vālī</s>, my elder, destroyer of foes,

children.text: pitur bahumato nityaṃ mama cāpi tathā purā ||
children.translated_text: who was always highly regarded by my father, and formerly by me as well.
When our father had passed away, the ministers said, 'He is the eldest,'
and made him lord of the monkeys in the kingdom, with supreme approval.
While he ruled the great kingdom inherited from his father and grandfather,

children.text: ahaṃ sarveṣu kāleṣu praṇataḥ preṣyavat sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I stood at all times obedient to him, bowed down like a servant.

children.text: māyāvī nāma tejasvī pūrvajo dundubheḥ sutaḥ
children.translated_text: There was a powerful demon named <s>Māyāvī</s>, the elder son of <s>Dundubhi</s>.

children.text: tena tasya mahad vairaṃ strīkṛtaṃ viśrutaṃ purā ||
children.translated_text: Between him and <s>Vālī</s> there had long been a great and famous feud, caused by a woman.

children.text: sa tu supte jane rātrau kiṣkindhād vāram āgataḥ
children.translated_text: One night, when the people were asleep, he came to the gate of <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>

children.text: nardati sma susaṃrabdho vālinaṃ cāhvayad raṇe ||
children.translated_text: and roared in great fury, challenging <s>Vālī</s> to battle.

children.text: prasuptas tu mama bhrātā narditaṃ bhairavasvanam
children.translated_text: My brother <s>Vālī</s> was asleep, but when he heard that roaring with its dreadful sound,

children.text: śrutvā na mamṛṣe vālī niṣpapāta javāt tadā ||
children.translated_text: he could not endure it, and at once rushed out swiftly.

children.text: sa tu vai niḥsṛtaḥ krodhāt taṃ hantum asurottamam
children.translated_text: He went out in anger to kill that best of asuras,

children.text: vāryamāṇas tataḥ strībhir mayā ca praṇatātmanā ||
children.translated_text: though he was held back by the women and by me, who had bowed myself before him.

children.text: sa tu nirdhūya sarvānno nirjagāma mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: But that mighty one shook us all off and went out.

children.text: tato 'ham api sauhārdān niḥsṛto vālinā saha ||
children.translated_text: Then I too, out of affection, went out together with <s>Vālī</s>.

children.text: sa tu me bhrātaraṃ dṛṣṭvā māṃ ca dūrād avasthitam
children.translated_text: When that asura saw my brother and me standing at a distance,
he became terrified and then fled away with all speed.

children.text: tasmin dravati saṃtraste hy āvāṃ drutataraṃ gatau
children.translated_text: As he fled in terror, we two went after him still more swiftly,
and the path too was made clear by the rising moon.

children.text: sa tṛṇair āvṛtaṃ durgaṃ dharaṇyā vivaraṃ mahat
children.translated_text: That asura, reaching us, entered with speed a great opening in the earth,
a difficult cave covered with grasses; and we stopped there.

children.text: taṃ praviṣṭaṃ ripuṃ dṛṣṭvā bilaṃ roṣavaśaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that enemy enter the cave, <s>Vālī</s>, overcome by anger,

children.text: mām uvāca tadā vālī vacanaṃ kṣubhitendriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then spoke these words to me, his senses agitated:

children.text: iha tvaṃ tiṣṭha sugrīva biladvāri samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Stay here, <s>Sugrīva</s>, attentive at the mouth of the cave,

children.text: yāvad atra praviśyāhaṃ nihanmi samare ripum ||
children.translated_text: while I enter here and slay the enemy in battle.'

children.text: mayā tv etad vacaḥ śrutvā yācitaḥ sa paraṃtapa
children.translated_text: When I heard this command, scorcher of foes, I pleaded with him;

children.text: śāpayitvā ca māṃ padbhyāṃ praviveśa bilaṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: but after making me swear by his feet, he then entered the cave.

children.text: tasya praviṣṭasya bilaṃ sāgraḥ saṃvatsaro gataḥ
children.translated_text: After he had entered the cave, a full year passed, with some days beyond it,

children.text: sthitasya ca mama dvāri sa kālo vyatyavartata ||
children.translated_text: and that time went by while I remained at the entrance.

children.text: ahaṃ tu naṣṭaṃ taṃ jñātvā snehād āgatasambhramaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, believing him lost, and becoming agitated because of affection,

children.text: bhrātaraṃ na hi paśyāmi pāpaśaṅki ca me manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I did not see my brother, and my mind feared evil.

children.text: atha dīrghasya kālasya bilāt tasmād viniḥsṛtam
children.translated_text: Then, after a long time, I saw blood issuing from that cave,

children.text: saphenaṃ rudhiraṃ raktam ahaṃ dṛṣṭvā suduḥkhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: red and foaming, and I was deeply distressed.

children.text: nardatām asurāṇāṃ ca dhvanir me śrotram āgataḥ
children.translated_text: The sound of roaring asuras reached my ear,

children.text: nirastasya ca saṃgrāme krośato niḥsvano guroḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also the deep cry of my elder brother as he was overthrown in battle.

children.text: ahaṃ tv avagato buddhyā cihnais tair bhrātaraṃ hatam
children.translated_text: By those signs I concluded in my judgment that my brother had been killed.
I closed the cave entrance with a rock the size of a mountain,

children.text: śokārtaś codakaṃ kṛtvā kiṣkindhām āgataḥ sakhe ||
children.translated_text: and, afflicted with grief, having offered water for him, I came to <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, my friend.

children.text: gūhamānasya me tattvaṃ yatnato mantribhiḥ śrutam
children.translated_text: Though I tried hard to conceal the truth, it was learned by the ministers.
Then, when they had assembled together, I was consecrated by them.

children.text: rājyaṃ praśāsatas tasya nyāyato mama rāghava
children.translated_text: While I was ruling that kingdom justly, <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: ājagāma ripuṃ hatvā vālī tam asurottamam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vālī</s> came back after killing that best of asuras, his enemy.

children.text: abhiṣiktaṃ tu māṃ dṛṣṭvā krodhāt saṃraktalocanaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing me consecrated, his eyes red with anger,

children.text: madīyān mantriṇo baddhvā paruṣaṃ vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: he bound my ministers and spoke harsh words.

children.text: nigrahe 'pi samarthasya taṃ pāpaṃ prati rāghava
children.translated_text: Although I was able to restrain that wicked one, <s>Rāghava</s>,
my thought did not turn against him, held back by reverence for my brother.
Honoring that great-souled one, I bowed to him properly;
but no blessings were spoken by him, for he was not satisfied in his heart.
Then, when he had come near, possessed by anger and enraged,
I tried to appease my brother, wishing what was dear to him.

children.text: diṣṭyāsi kuśalī prāpto nihataś ca tvayā ripuḥ
children.translated_text: 'By good fortune you have returned safe, and the enemy has been killed by you.

children.text: anāthasya hi me nāthas tvam eko 'nāthanandanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For me, who was without a protector, you alone are my protector, delighter of the helpless.
Accept this umbrella of yours, with many ribs, risen like the full moon,
together with the yak-tail fan, which has been raised up by me.

children.text: tvam eva rājā mānārhaḥ sadā cāhaṃ yathāpurā
children.translated_text: You alone are the king and worthy of honor; I shall always be as before.

children.text: nyāsabhūtam idaṃ rājyaṃ tava niryātayāmy aham ||
children.translated_text: This kingdom has been held in trust; I now return it to you.

children.text: mā ca roṣaṃ kṛthāḥ saumya mayi śatrunibarhaṇa
children.translated_text: Do not be angry with me, gentle destroyer of enemies.

children.text: yāce tvāṃ śirasā rājan mayā baddho 'yam añjaliḥ ||
children.translated_text: I beg you with my head bowed, O king; these hands of mine are joined in reverence.
I was compelled by force, by the ministers and the townspeople together,
and appointed to kingship from the desire not to leave the land without a ruler.'

children.text: snigdham evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ māṃ sa tu nirbhartsya vānaraḥ
children.translated_text: As I spoke to him affectionately in this way, that monkey rebuked me,

children.text: dhik tvām iti ca mām uktvā bahu tat tad uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: saying, 'Shame on you,' and he said many such things to me.

children.text: prakṛtīś ca samānīya mantriṇaś caiva saṃmatān
children.translated_text: Having summoned the subjects and the approved ministers as well,

children.text: mām āha suhṛdāṃ madhye vākyaṃ paramagarhitam ||
children.translated_text: he spoke to me, in the midst of my friends, words that were utterly blameworthy:

children.text: viditaṃ vo yathā rātrau māyāvī sa mahāsuraḥ
children.translated_text: 'You know how that great asura <s>Māyāvī</s>,
cruel and evil-minded, eager for battle, challenged me in the night.

children.text: tasya tad garjitaṃ śrutvā niḥsṛto 'haṃ nṛpālayāt
children.translated_text: Hearing that roaring of his, I went out from the royal palace.'

children.text: anuyātaś ca māṃ tūrṇam ayaṃ bhrātā sudāruṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And this very fearsome brother quickly followed after me.

children.text: sa tu dṛṣṭvaiva māṃ rātrau sadvitīyaṃ mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: But the mighty one, as soon as he saw me at night accompanied by a second,
ran away, terrified with fear, seeing the two of us pursuing him.
Pursued at speed, he entered a great cave.

children.text: taṃ praviṣṭaṃ viditvā tu sughoraṃ sumahad bilam
children.translated_text: Knowing that he had entered that very terrible, very large cave,

children.text: ayam ukto 'tha me bhrātā mayā tu krūradarśanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I then said this to my brother, who had a fierce appearance:

children.text: ahatvā nāsti me śaktiḥ pratigantum itaḥ purīm
children.translated_text: I have no power to return from here to the city without killing him.

children.text: biladvāri pratīkṣa tvaṃ yāvad enaṃ nihanmy aham ||
children.translated_text: Wait at the mouth of the cave until I kill him.

children.text: sthito 'yam iti matvā tu praviṣṭo 'haṃ durāsadam
children.translated_text: Thinking, 'He is standing here,' I entered that place hard to approach,

children.text: taṃ ca me mārgamāṇasya gataḥ saṃvatsaras tadā ||
children.translated_text: and as I searched for him, a year passed for me then.

children.text: sa tu dṛṣṭo mayā śatrur anirvedād bhayāvahaḥ
children.translated_text: But because I did not lose heart, I saw that fearsome enemy,

children.text: nihataś ca mayā tatra so 'suro bandhubhiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: and there I killed that asura together with his kinsmen.

children.text: tasyāsyāt tu pravṛttena rudhiraugheṇa tad bilam
children.translated_text: Then, from his mouth, with a torrent of blood flowing forth, that cave

children.text: pūrṇam āsīd durākrāmaṃ stanatas tasya bhūtale ||
children.translated_text: was filled and became hard to pass through, while he roared on the ground.

children.text: sūdayitvā tu taṃ śatruṃ vikrāntaṃ dundubheḥ sutam
children.translated_text: Having slain that brave enemy, the son of <s>Dundubhi</s>,

children.text: niṣkrāmann eva paśyāmi bilasya pihitaṃ mukham ||
children.translated_text: as I was coming out I saw the mouth of the cave blocked.

children.text: vikrośamānasya tu me sugrīveti punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Though I cried out again and again, '<s>Sugrīva</s>!'
when there was no answer, I was deeply grieved.

children.text: pādaprahārais tu mayā bahuśas tad vidāritam
children.translated_text: By many blows of my feet I split it open,

children.text: tato 'haṃ tena niṣkramya yathā punar upāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and then, having come out through that, I returned as before.
There I was shut in by this man, who was seeking the kingdom for himself,
by cruel <s>Sugrīva</s>, who had forgotten brotherly affection.

children.text: evam uktvā tu māṃ tatra vastreṇaikena vānaraḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to me there, the monkey
<s>Vālī</s>, free from fear, then banished me with only a single garment.

children.text: tenāham apaviddhaś ca hṛtadāraś ca rāghava
children.translated_text: Cast out by him and deprived of my wife, <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: tadbhayāc ca mahī kṛtsnā krānteyaṃ savanārṇavā ||
children.translated_text: because of fear of him I have wandered over this whole earth, with its forests and oceans.
Grieved by the seizure of my wife, I entered
the excellent mountain <s>Ṛśyamūka</s>, hard to assail, for another reason connected with <s>Vālī</s>.

children.text: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ vairānukathanaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: All this great account of enmity has been told to you.

children.text: anāgasā mayā prāptaṃ vyasanaṃ paśya rāghava ||
children.translated_text: See, <s>Rāghava</s>, the calamity that I have incurred though innocent.
Since I am tormented by fear of <s>Vālī</s>, O giver of fearlessness to all worlds,

children.text: kartum arhasi me vīra prasādaṃ tasya nigrahāt ||
children.translated_text: you ought, hero, to grant me favor by restraining him.

children.text: evam uktaḥ sa tejasvī dharmajño dharmasaṃhitam
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, that fiery one, knower of <s>dharma</s> and joined to <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: vacanaṃ vaktum ārebhe sugrīvaṃ prahasann iva ||
children.translated_text: began to speak a word to <s>Sugrīva</s>, as if smiling:
These sharp arrows of mine, unfailing and bright as the sun,
will fall in anger upon that wicked <s>Vālī</s>.

children.text: yāvat taṃ na hi paśyeyaṃ tava bhāryāpahāriṇam
children.translated_text: Until I see him who has abducted your wife,

children.text: tāvat sa jīvet pāpātmā vālī cāritradūṣakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: let that sinful <s>Vālī</s>, defiler of conduct, live only until then.
By inference from myself I see you sunk in an ocean of grief.

children.text: tvām ahaṃ tārayiṣyāmi kāmaṃ prāpsyasi puṣkalam ||
children.translated_text: I shall carry you across; you will obtain your desire in full.
Hearing <s>Rāma</s>'s words, which increased joy and manly courage,
<s>Sugrīva</s> honored <s>Rāghava</s> and praised him.
Without doubt, with blazing, sharp arrows that pierce vital spots,

children.text: tvaṃ daheḥ kupito lokān yugānta iva bhāskaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: you, when angered, could burn the worlds like the sun at the end of an age.

children.text: vālinaḥ pauruṣaṃ yat tad yac ca vīryaṃ dhṛtiś ca yā
children.translated_text: But what <s>Vālī</s>'s manly power is, and what his strength and firmness are,
hear that from me with one-pointed mind, and then determine what follows.

children.text: samudrāt paścimāt pūrvaṃ dakṣiṇād api cottaram
children.translated_text: From the western ocean to the eastern, and from the southern also to the northern,
<s>Vālī</s> strides before sunrise, free from fatigue.

children.text: agrāṇy āruhya śailānāṃ śikharāṇi mahānty api
children.translated_text: Climbing the foremost peaks of the mountains, even the great summits,
that mighty one hurls them upward with force and catches them again.

children.text: bahavaḥ sāravantaś ca vaneṣu vividhā drumāḥ
children.translated_text: Many trees of solid heartwood and of various kinds in the forests
have been broken by <s>Vālī</s> with force as he displayed his own strength.
There was a buffalo named <s>Dundubhi</s>, shining like the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>.
Mighty in valor, he possessed the strength of a thousand elephants.
Arrogant from the pride of his strength, wicked-minded and deluded by a boon,

children.text: jagāma sa mahākāyaḥ samudraṃ saritāṃ patim ||
children.translated_text: that huge-bodied one went to the ocean, lord of rivers.
Approaching the wave-filled sea, the storehouse of jewels,

children.text: mama yuddhaṃ prayaccheti tam uvāca mahārṇavam ||
children.translated_text: he said to the great ocean, 'Grant me battle.'
Then the righteous ocean, very mighty, rising up,
spoke these words, O king, to the asura driven on by Time:

children.text: samartho nāsmi te dātuṃ yuddhaṃ yuddhaviśārada
children.translated_text: I am not able to give you battle, skilled as you are in war.

children.text: śrūyatām abhidhāsyāmi yas te yuddhaṃ pradāsyati ||
children.translated_text: Listen; I shall tell you who will give you battle.
In the great wilderness there is the king of mountains, the supreme refuge of ascetics,
renowned by the name <s>Himavān</s>, the father-in-law of <s>Śaṃkara</s>.
Endowed with caves, springs, many caverns, and waterfalls,

children.text: sa samarthas tava prītim atulāṃ kartum āhave ||
children.translated_text: he is able to bring you unequalled satisfaction in battle.

children.text: taṃ bhītam iti vijñāya samudram asurottamaḥ
children.translated_text: Recognizing that ocean as afraid, the foremost asura

children.text: himavadvanam āgacchac charaś cāpād iva cyutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: went to the forest of <s>Himavān</s> like an arrow released from a bow.

children.text: tatas tasya gireḥ śvetā gajendravipulāḥ śilāḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Dundubhi</s> hurled that mountain's white rocks, broad as lordly elephants,

children.text: cikṣepa bahudhā bhūmau dundubhir vinanāda ca ||
children.translated_text: in many ways upon the ground, and he roared aloud.
Then <s>Himavān</s>, white as a cloud, gentle and pleasing in form,

children.text: himavān abravīd vākyaṃ sva eva śikhare sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: standing on his own peak, spoke these words:

children.text: kleṣṭum arhasi māṃ na tvaṃ dundubhe dharmavatsala
children.translated_text: You should not trouble me, <s>Dundubhi</s>, lover of <s>dharma</s>.
For I am unskilled in deeds of battle and am a refuge of ascetics.
Hearing that statement of the wise king of mountains,
<s>Dundubhi</s>, his eyes reddened with anger, spoke these words:

children.text: yadi yuddhe 'samarthas tvaṃ madbhayād vā nirudyamaḥ
children.translated_text: If you are unable in battle, or if you make no effort out of fear of me,

children.text: tam ācakṣva pradadyān me yo 'dya yuddhaṃ yuyutsataḥ ||
children.translated_text: then tell me of someone who will give battle to me today, eager as I am to fight.
Hearing this, <s>Himavān</s>, skilled in speech, spoke these words,
words never spoken before, the righteous one speaking in anger to that best of asuras:
There is a very wise monkey named <s>Vālī</s>, equal to <s>Śakra</s> in valor.
That glorious one dwells in <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, whose splendor is unequaled.
He, very wise and skilled in battle, is able

children.text: dvaṃdvayuddhaṃ mahad dātuṃ namucer iva vāsavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: to give you a great single combat, as <s>Vāsava</s> did to <s>Namuci</s>.

children.text: taṃ śīghram abhigaccha tvaṃ yadi yuddham ihecchasi
children.translated_text: Go to him quickly, if you desire battle here.

children.text: sa hi durdharṣaṇo nityaṃ śūraḥ samarakarmaṇi ||
children.translated_text: For he is always hard to assail, a hero in the work of war.

children.text: śrutvā himavato vākyaṃ krodhāviṣṭaḥ sa dundubhiḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing the words of <s>Himavān</s>, that <s>Dundubhi</s>, possessed by anger,

children.text: jagāma tāṃ purīṃ tasya kiṣkindhāṃ vālinas tadā ||
children.translated_text: then went to his city, <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, the city of <s>Vālī</s>.
He took on the form of a buffalo, sharp-horned and terrifying,
like a great cloud in the rainy season, filled with water in the sky.

children.text: tatas tu dvāram āgamya kiṣkindhāyā mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, having come to the gate of <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, the very strong one

children.text: nanarda kampayan bhūmiṃ dundubhir dundubhir yathā ||
children.translated_text: roared, shaking the earth, <s>Dundubhi</s> like a war-drum.

children.text: samīpajān drumān bhañjan vasudhāṃ dārayan khuraiḥ
children.translated_text: Breaking the nearby trees and tearing the ground with his hooves,
he scraped that gate with his horn in pride, like an elephant.
<s>Vālī</s>, who was in the inner palace, heard the sound and, unable to bear it,

children.text: niṣpapāta saha strībhis tārābhir iva candramāḥ ||
children.translated_text: rushed out with the women, like the moon with the stars.

children.text: mitaṃ vyaktākṣarapadaṃ tam uvāca sa dundubhim
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vālī</s>, lord of the monkeys and of all forest-roamers,
spoke to that <s>Dundubhi</s> in measured words with clear syllables and phrases:
For what purpose do you block this city gate and roar?

children.text: dundubhe vidito me 'si rakṣa prāṇān mahābala ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dundubhi</s>, you are known to me; protect your life, mighty one.
Hearing that speech of the wise lord of monkeys,
<s>Dundubhi</s>, his eyes reddened with anger, spoke these words:

children.text: na tvaṃ strīsaṃnidhau vīra vacanaṃ vaktum arhasi
children.translated_text: Hero, you ought not speak words in the presence of women.

children.text: mama yuddhaṃ prayaccha tvaṃ tato jñāsyāmi te balam ||
children.translated_text: Grant me battle, and then I shall know your strength.

children.text: atha vā dhārayiṣyāmi krodham adya niśām imām
children.translated_text: Or else I shall hold back my anger for this night today.
Take your pleasure freely at sunrise among enjoyments of desire, monkey.

children.text: yo hi mattaṃ pramattaṃ vā suptaṃ vā rahitaṃ bhṛśam
children.translated_text: For one who would kill a man intoxicated, careless, asleep, or utterly alone,

children.text: hanyāt sa bhrūṇahā loke tvadvidhaṃ madamohitam ||
