children.translated_text: a man like you, bewildered by intoxication, would be known in the world as a killer of an embryo.

children.text: sa prahasyābravīn mandaṃ krodhāt tam asurottamam
children.translated_text: Then, dismissing all those women headed by <s>Tārā</s>,

children.text: visṛjya tāḥ striyaḥ sarvās tārāprabhṛtikās tadā ||
children.translated_text: he laughed and spoke softly, in anger, to that best of asuras:

children.text: matto 'yam iti mā maṃsthā yady abhīto 'si saṃyuge
children.translated_text: Do not think, 'He is drunk,' if you are fearless in combat.
In this clash let this intoxication be reckoned as the hero's drink.

children.text: tam evam uktvā saṃkruddho mālām utkṣipya kāñcanīm
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to him, the enraged one lifted up his golden garland,
given by his father <s>Mahendra</s>, and took his stand for battle.
Seizing by the two horns that <s>Dundubhi</s>, who was like a mountain,
<s>Vālī</s> threw him down and roared with a great sound.

children.text: yuddhe prāṇahare tasmin niṣpiṣṭo dundubhis tadā
children.translated_text: In that life-taking battle, <s>Dundubhi</s> was crushed then,

children.text: śrotrābhyām atha raktaṃ tu tasya susrāva pātyataḥ
children.translated_text: and as he was being hurled down, blood flowed from his two ears.

children.text: papāta ca mahākāyaḥ kṣitau pañcatvam āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: His great body fell upon the earth, having reached death.
Having weighed with his arms that lifeless, unconscious body,
swift <s>Vālī</s> hurled it with a single force one yojana away.
From the mouth of that body, flung by his speed, drops of blood
fell, carried by the wind, toward the hermitage of <s>Mataṅga</s>.

children.text: tān dṛṣṭvā patitāṃs tatra muniḥ śoṇitavipruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing those drops of blood fallen there, the sage
uttered a great curse against <s>Vālī</s>, the thrower:
He must not enter here; if he enters, death will be his.

children.text: sa maharṣiṃ samāsādya yācate sma kṛtāñjaliḥ ||
children.translated_text: Coming to that great seer, he begged him with joined hands.
Thereafter, frightened by fear of the curse, the monkey

children.text: praveṣṭuṃ necchati harir draṣṭuṃ vāpi nareśvara ||
children.translated_text: does not wish to enter the great mountain <s>Ṛśyamūka</s>, or even to see it, king of men.
Knowing that he cannot enter, <s>Rāma</s>, I roam
through this great forest with my ministers, free from distress.
This heap of bones of that <s>Dundubhi</s> is visible here,
great like a mountain peak, cast away because of the excess of his strength.

children.text: ime ca vipulāḥ sālāḥ sapta śākhāvalambinaḥ
children.translated_text: And these are the seven broad sāla trees, their branches hanging down,
where <s>Vālī</s> is able, with his force, to strip one of its leaves.

children.text: etad asyāsamaṃ vīryaṃ mayā rāma prakāśitam
children.translated_text: This unequaled strength of his has been described by me, <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: kathaṃ taṃ vālinaṃ hantuṃ samare śakṣyase nṛpa ||
children.translated_text: How will you be able to kill that <s>Vālī</s> in battle, O king?

children.text: yadi bhindyād bhavān sālān imāṃs tv ekeṣuṇā tataḥ
children.translated_text: If you were to pierce these sāla trees with a single arrow,

children.text: jānīyāṃ tvāṃ mahābāho samarthaṃ vālino vadhe ||
children.translated_text: then, mighty-armed one, I would know you to be capable of killing <s>Vālī</s>.
Hearing that speech of great-souled <s>Sugrīva</s>,
mighty-armed <s>Rāghava</s> lifted <s>Dundubhi</s>'s body
with his big toe, in play, and hurled it ten yojanas away.

children.text: kṣiptaṃ dṛṣṭvā tataḥ kāyaṃ sugrīvaḥ punar abravīt
children.translated_text: Seeing the body hurled away, <s>Sugrīva</s> then again spoke
these meaningful words to <s>Rāma</s> in the presence of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:

children.text: ārdraḥ samāṃsapratyagraḥ kṣiptaḥ kāyaḥ purā sakhe
children.translated_text: Formerly, my friend, the body was wet, with flesh and freshly killed, when it was hurled.

children.text: laghuḥ samprati nirmāṃsas tṛṇabhūtaś ca rāghava
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Rāghava</s>, it is light, without flesh, and like straw.

children.text: nātra śakyaṃ balaṃ jñātuṃ tava vā tasya vādhikam ||
children.translated_text: It is not possible from this to know whether your strength or his is greater.

children.text: etac ca vacanaṃ śrutvā sugrīveṇa subhāṣitam
children.translated_text: Hearing also this well-spoken statement from <s>Sugrīva</s>,
the greatly radiant <s>Rāma</s> took up his bow in order to give proof.

children.text: sa gṛhītvā dhanur ghoraṃ śaram ekaṃ ca mānadaḥ
children.translated_text: Taking up the dreadful bow and one arrow, the giver of honor

children.text: sālān uddiśya cikṣepa jyāsvanaiḥ pūrayan diśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he aimed at the śāla trees and released it, filling the quarters with the twang of the bowstring.
That arrow, discharged by the mighty one and adorned with gold,

children.text: bhittvā sālān giriprasthe sapta bhūmiṃ viveśa ha ||
children.translated_text: split the seven śāla trees on the mountain slope and entered the earth.

children.text: praviṣṭas tu muhūrtena rasāṃ bhittvā mahājavaḥ
children.translated_text: Having entered, in a moment that very swift arrow pierced the nether region,

children.text: niṣpatya ca punas tūrṇaṃ svatūṇīṃ praviveśa ha ||
children.translated_text: then burst out again quickly and reentered its own quiver.

children.text: tān dṛṣṭvā sapta nirbhinnān sālān vānarapuṃgavaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing those seven śāla trees pierced through by the speed of <s>Rāma</s>'s arrow,
the foremost of monkeys was filled with the highest wonder.
With his ornaments hanging down, he fell with his head to the ground,
and <s>Sugrīva</s>, greatly delighted, stood with joined palms before <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: idaṃ covāca dharmajñaṃ karmaṇā tena harṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: Gladdened by that deed, he said this to the knower of <s>dharma</s>,
to heroic <s>Rāma</s>, who stood there as the best of all who know weapons:

children.text: sendrān api surān sarvāṃs tvaṃ bāṇaiḥ puruṣarṣabha
children.translated_text: Even all the gods together with <s>Indra</s>, O bull among men,

children.text: samarthaḥ samare hantuṃ kiṃ punar vālinaṃ prabho ||
children.translated_text: you are able to kill with your arrows in battle; how much more <s>Vāli</s>, my lord!

children.text: yena sapta mahāsālā girir bhūmiś ca dāritāḥ
children.translated_text: By one arrow, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, seven great śāla trees, the mountain, and the earth were torn open;

children.text: bāṇenaikena kākutstha sthātā te ko raṇāgrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: who could stand before you at the front of battle?

children.text: adya me vigataḥ śokaḥ prītir adya parā mama
children.translated_text: Today my grief has vanished; today my joy is supreme,
because I have obtained you as a friend, one like <s>Mahendra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>.

children.text: tam adyaiva priyārthaṃ me vairiṇaṃ bhrātṛrūpiṇam
children.translated_text: Therefore today, for my dear sake, strike down my enemy in the form of a brother,

children.text: vālinaṃ jahi kākutstha mayā baddho 'yam añjaliḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vāli</s>, O <s>Kākutstha</s>; this gesture of reverence is made by me.
Then wise <s>Rāma</s> embraced handsome <s>Sugrīva</s>
and replied with words approved by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:

children.text: asmād gacchāma kiṣkindhāṃ kṣipraṃ gaccha tvam agrataḥ
children.translated_text: Let us go from here to <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>. Go quickly ahead,
and when you have gone there, O <s>Sugrīva</s>, challenge <s>Vāli</s>, who is only brother-like.

children.text: sarve te tvaritaṃ gatvā kiṣkindhāṃ vālinaḥ purīm
children.translated_text: Then all of them, having quickly gone to <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, <s>Vāli</s>'s city,

children.text: vṛkṣair ātmānam āvṛtya vyatiṣṭhan gahane vane ||
children.translated_text: covered themselves with trees and stood in the dense forest.
For the purpose of summoning <s>Vāli</s>, <s>Sugrīva</s> roared terribly,

children.text: gāḍhaṃ parihito vegān nādair bhindann ivāmbaram ||
children.translated_text: very tightly girded and, with the force of his cries, as though splitting the sky.

children.text: taṃ śrutvā ninadaṃ bhrātuḥ kruddho vālī mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that roar of his brother, mighty <s>Vāli</s>, enraged,
rushed out in great fury, like the sun from the western mountain slope.
Then a very tumultuous battle arose between <s>Vāli</s> and <s>Sugrīva</s>,
like the terrible battle in the sky between the planets <s>Budha</s> and <s>Aṅgāraka</s>.

children.text: talair aśanikalpaiś ca vajrakalpaiś ca muṣṭibhiḥ
children.translated_text: With slaps like thunderbolts and with fists like vajras,
the two brothers, overwhelmed by anger, struck one another in battle.

children.text: tato rāmo dhanuṣpāṇis tāv ubhau samudīkṣya tu
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s>, bow in hand, looked closely at them both,
the two heroic ones resembling each other, both like the twin <s>Aśvins</s>.

children.text: yan nāvagacchat sugrīvaṃ vālinaṃ vāpi rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Since <s>Rāghava</s> could not distinguish <s>Sugrīva</s> from <s>Vāli</s>,

children.text: tato na kṛtavān buddhiṃ moktum antakaraṃ śaram ||
children.translated_text: he did not resolve to release his death-dealing arrow.

children.text: etasminn antare bhagnaḥ sugrīvas tena vālinā
children.translated_text: Meanwhile <s>Sugrīva</s>, broken by that <s>Vāli</s>,
not seeing <s>Rāghava</s> as his protector, fled to <s>Ṛśyamūka</s>.
Exhausted, his limbs drenched with blood and shattered by blows,
he entered the great forest, pursued in anger by <s>Vāli</s>.

children.text: taṃ praviṣṭaṃ vanaṃ dṛṣṭvā vālī śāpabhayāt tataḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing him enter the forest, <s>Vāli</s>, because of fear of the curse,

children.text: mukto hy asi tvam ity uktvā sa nivṛtto mahābalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: said, 'You are released,' and the mighty one turned back.

children.text: rāghavo 'pi saha bhrātrā saha caiva hanūmatā
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> too, together with his brother and with <s>Hanūmat</s>,

children.text: tad eva vanam āgacchat sugrīvo yatra vānaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: came to that very forest where <s>Sugrīva</s> the monkey was.
Seeing <s>Rāma</s> arrive with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
<s>Sugrīva</s>, ashamed, spoke these pitiable words, looking down at the earth:

children.text: āhvayasveti mām uktvā darśayitvā ca vikramam
children.translated_text: After saying to me, 'Challenge him,' and after showing your valor,

children.text: vairiṇā ghātayitvā ca kim idānīṃ tvayā kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: what have you done now by letting me be beaten by my enemy?

children.text: tām eva velāṃ vaktavyaṃ tvayā rāghava tattvataḥ
children.translated_text: At that very time, O <s>Rāghava</s>, you should have told me truthfully,

children.text: vālinaṃ na nihanmīti tato nāham ito vraje ||
children.translated_text: 'I will not kill <s>Vāli</s>'; then I would not have gone from here.
As the great-souled <s>Sugrīva</s> was speaking thus,

children.text: karuṇaṃ dīnayā vācā rāghavaḥ punar abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> again answered in a compassionate and gentle voice:

children.text: sugrīva śrūyatāṃ tāta krodhaś ca vyapanīyatām
children.translated_text: Listen, dear <s>Sugrīva</s>, and let your anger be set aside;

children.text: kāraṇaṃ yena bāṇo 'yaṃ na mayā sa visarjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: hear the reason why this arrow was not released by me.
In ornaments, dress, size, and gait,

children.text: tvaṃ ca sugrīva vālī ca sadṛśau sthaḥ parasparam ||
children.translated_text: you and <s>Vāli</s>, O <s>Sugrīva</s>, are alike to each other.

children.text: svareṇa varcasā caiva prekṣitena ca vānara
children.translated_text: In voice and brilliance too, and in the look of your eyes, O monkey,

children.text: vikrameṇa ca vākyaiś ca vyaktiṃ vāṃ nopalakṣaye ||
children.translated_text: as well as in valor and speech, I could not mark any distinction between you two.
Therefore, confused by the similarity of your forms, O best of monkeys,
I did not let loose the very swift arrow that destroys enemies.

children.text: etanmuhūrte tu mayā paśya vālinam āhave
children.translated_text: But at this very moment, see <s>Vāli</s> in battle, by me,
struck down with a single arrow and writhing on the ground.
Make a distinguishing mark for yourself, O lord of monkeys,
by which I may recognize you when you have entered single combat.
Uproot this blooming gajapuṣpī creeper, auspiciously marked,
O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and place it around the neck of this great-souled <s>Sugrīva</s>.
Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> uprooted that gajapuṣpī, born on the mountain slope and full of flowers,

children.text: lakṣmaṇo gajapuṣpīṃ tāṃ tasya kaṇṭhe vyasarjayat ||
children.translated_text: and placed it around his neck.

children.text: sa tathā śuśubhe śrīmāṃl latayā kaṇṭhasaktayā
children.translated_text: The splendid one, with the creeper fastened around his neck, shone in that way,
like a rain cloud at twilight with a garland of cranes.
Radiant in body and intent on <s>Rāma</s>'s command,
he went with <s>Rāma</s> to <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, protected by <s>Vāli</s>.
From <s>Ṛśyamūka</s>, that righteous elder brother of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>
went together with <s>Sugrīva</s> to <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, protected by <s>Vāli</s>'s prowess.
<s>Rāma</s> raised his great bow, adorned with gold.
Having taken up arrows shining like the sun and able to accomplish battle,

children.text: agratas tu yayau tasya rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: in front of that great-souled <s>Rāghava</s> there went
<s>Sugrīva</s>, firm-necked, and mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: pṛṣṭhato hanumān vīro nalo nīlaś ca vānaraḥ
children.translated_text: Behind him were the heroic <s>Hanumān</s>, and the monkeys <s>Nala</s> and <s>Nīla</s>,
and <s>Tāra</s>, very splendid, together with commanders of monkey troops.
They looked at trees bending under their burden of flowers,
and at rivers with clear-flowing waters, going toward the ocean;

children.text: kandarāṇi ca śailāṃś ca nirdarāṇi guhās tathā
children.translated_text: at mountain caves, mountains, clefts, and caverns too,

children.text: śikharāṇi ca mukhyāni darīś ca priyadarśanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: at prominent peaks and at lovely valleys;
and on the road they saw water-filled ponds, adorned

children.text: śobhitān sajalān mārge taṭākāṃś ca vyalokayan ||
children.translated_text: with leaves clear as vaidūrya gems and with lotuses whose buds were like the sky.
They were resounding with kāraṇḍa ducks, cranes, swans, vañjula birds, and water-hens,
with cakravāka birds and with other birds as well.
They saw forest-ranging deer, fearless and feeding on tender grass-shoots,
moving everywhere and standing on the open grounds.
They also saw enemies of ponds, adorned with white tusks,
terrible, solitary, wild elephants, breakers of riverbanks;

children.text: vane vanacarāṃś cānyān khecarāṃś ca vihaṃgamān
children.translated_text: and in the forest they saw other forest-ranging creatures and sky-ranging birds.
Seeing these, those who were obedient to <s>Sugrīva</s>'s command went on swiftly.

children.text: teṣāṃ tu gacchatāṃ tatra tvaritaṃ raghunandanaḥ
children.translated_text: As they were traveling there quickly, the delight of the <s>Raghu</s> line,

children.text: drumaṣaṇḍaṃ vanaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmaḥ sugrīvam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, seeing a grove of trees, a forest-thicket, said to <s>Sugrīva</s>:
This mass of trees shines like a cloud in the sky,
vast as a gathering of clouds and encircled at its edge by plantains.

children.text: kim etaj jñātum icchāmi sakhe kautūhalaṃ mama
children.translated_text: What is this? I wish to know, my friend; I am curious.
I wish my curiosity to be removed by you.
Hearing that statement of the great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: gacchann evācacakṣe 'tha sugrīvas tan mahad vanam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s>, even as he went, then described that great forest.
This, O <s>Rāghava</s>, is a broad hermitage that removes weariness,
rich in pleasure-groves, with sweet roots, fruits, and water.
Here there were once seven sages named <s>Saptajana</s>, austere in their vows,
seven indeed, with heads downward and constantly lying in water.
Eating only once every seven nights, living in the forest on air,
after seven hundred years they went bodily to heaven.
By the power of those very sages,
this hermitage, enclosed by a rampart of trees, is very hard to assail, even for gods and demons together with <s>Indra</s>.
Birds avoid this place, and so do other forest-dwellers.

children.text: viśanti mohād ye 'py atra nivartante na te punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even those who enter here through delusion do not return again.
Here the sounds of ornaments are heard, clear in every syllable,

children.text: tūryagītasvanāś cāpi gandho divyaś ca rāghava ||
children.translated_text: and also the sounds of instruments and song, and a divine fragrance, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: tretāgnayo 'pi dīpyante dhūmo hy eṣa pradṛśyate
children.translated_text: The three sacred fires too are blazing; for this smoke is seen,
dense, dove-gray and ruddy, as though enveloping the tops of the trees.

children.text: kuru praṇāmaṃ dharmātmaṃs tān samuddiśya rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Offer reverence, righteous one, directing it toward them, O <s>Rāghava</s>,
together with your brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, purified, with controlled and folded hands.

children.text: praṇamanti hi ye teṣām ṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām
children.translated_text: For those who bow to those spiritually perfected seers

children.text: na teṣām aśubhaṃ kiṃcic charīre rāma dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: have nothing inauspicious seen in their bodies, O <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: tato rāmaḥ saha bhrātrā lakṣmaṇena kṛtāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s>, together with his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, joined his palms,
and, directing his reverence to those great-souled seers, saluted them.

children.text: abhivādya ca dharmātmā rāmo bhrātā ca lakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Having saluted them, righteous <s>Rāma</s> and his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
<s>Sugrīva</s> and the monkeys as well went on with delighted minds.

children.text: te gatvā dūram adhvānaṃ tasmāt saptajanāśramāt
children.translated_text: Having gone a long distance from that Saptajana hermitage,
they saw that unassailable <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, ruled by <s>Vāli</s>.

children.text: sarve te tvaritaṃ gatvā kiṣkindhāṃ vālipālitām
children.translated_text: All of them, having quickly reached <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, ruled by <s>Vāli</s>,

children.text: vṛkṣair ātmānam āvṛtya vyatiṣṭhan gahane vane ||
children.translated_text: covered themselves with trees and stood in the dense forest.
Having cast his gaze all around in the woodland, the forest-loving
broad-necked <s>Sugrīva</s> brought forth intense anger.

children.text: tataḥ sa ninadaṃ ghoraṃ kṛtvā yuddhāya cāhvayat
children.translated_text: Then he made a terrible roar and challenged him to battle,
surrounded by his retinues, as though splitting the sky with their cries.
Then <s>Sugrīva</s>, like the young sun and moving with the gait of a proud lion,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā rāmaṃ kriyādakṣaṃ sugrīvo vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: seeing <s>Rāma</s>, skilled in action, spoke these words:
We have reached <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, <s>Vāli</s>'s city, filled with a net of monkeys and having gateways of heated gold,

children.text: prāptāḥ sma dhvajayantrāḍhyāṃ kiṣkindhāṃ vālinaḥ purīm ||
children.translated_text: rich with banners and mechanical devices.

children.text: pratijñā yā tvayā vīra kṛtā vālivadhe purā
children.translated_text: The promise that you made before, O hero, concerning the killing of <s>Vāli</s>,

children.text: saphalāṃ tāṃ kuru kṣipraṃ latāṃ kāla ivāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: make it bear fruit quickly, like the season that has come upon a vine.

children.text: evam uktas tu dharmātmā sugrīveṇa sa rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Sugrīva</s>, that righteous <s>Rāghava</s>,
the destroyer of enemies, then said these words to <s>Sugrīva</s>:
You have been marked with a sign of recognition by this <s>gajasāhvā</s> garland,
like the sun in the sky, as though reversed, by a garland of stars.

children.text: adya vālisamutthaṃ te bhayaṃ vairaṃ ca vānara
children.translated_text: Today, O monkey, the fear and enmity that have arisen for you from <s>Vāli</s>
I shall release with a single discharge of an arrow in battle.
Show me, <s>Sugrīva</s>, your enemy who bears the form of a brother,

children.text: vālī vinihato yāvad vane pāṃsuṣu veṣṭate ||
children.translated_text: so that <s>Vāli</s>, struck down, may roll in the dust in the forest.

children.text: yadi dṛṣṭipathaṃ prāpto jīvan sa vinivartate
children.translated_text: If, having come within the path of my sight, he returns alive,

children.text: tato doṣeṇa mā gacchet sadyo garhec ca mā bhavān ||
children.translated_text: then let blame fall on me, and may you reproach me at once.

children.text: pratyakṣaṃ sapta te sālā mayā bāṇena dāritāḥ
children.translated_text: Before your eyes the seven śāla trees were split by me with one arrow;

children.text: tato vetsi balenādya vālinaṃ nihataṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: therefore, from that strength, know <s>Vāli</s> today as killed by me.

children.text: anṛtaṃ noktapūrvaṃ me vīra kṛcchre 'pi tiṣṭhatā
children.translated_text: Falsehood has never before been spoken by me, O hero, even when I was standing in hardship.
Nor, overcome by concern for <s>dharma</s>, will I speak falsely in any way.

children.text: saphalāṃ ca kariṣyāmi pratijñāṃ jahi sambhramam
children.translated_text: I shall make my promise bear fruit; cast off your confusion.
Just as <s>Śatakratu</s> makes the rice born in a field fruitful by rain.
So, <s>Sugrīva</s>, for the sake of summoning golden-garlanded <s>Vālī</s>,

children.text: sugrīva kuru taṃ śabdaṃ niṣpated yena vānaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: make that sound by which the monkey will come out.
Eager for victory, boastful of victory, and formerly challenged by you,
that <s>Vālī</s>, fond of battle, will come out without hesitation.

children.text: ripūṇāṃ dharṣaṇaṃ śūrā marṣayanti na saṃyuge
children.translated_text: Heroes do not endure provocation by enemies in battle,

children.text: jānantas tu svakaṃ vīryaṃ strīsamakṣaṃ viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: for they know their own valor, especially in the presence of women.

children.text: sa tu rāmavacaḥ śrutvā sugrīvo hemapiṅgalaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Rāma</s>'s words, tawny-golden <s>Sugrīva</s>
roared with a fierce roar, as if splitting the sky apart.

children.text: tasya śabdena vitrastā gāvo yānti hataprabhāḥ
children.translated_text: Terrified by his sound, the cows fled, their splendor gone,
confused like women of good family touched by a king's fault.

children.text: dravanti ca mṛgāḥ śīghraṃ bhagnā iva raṇe hayāḥ
children.translated_text: And the deer ran swiftly, like horses broken in battle,

children.text: patanti ca khagā bhūmau kṣīṇapuṇyā iva grahāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and birds fell to the ground like planets whose merit is exhausted.

children.text: tataḥ sa jīmūtagaṇapraṇādo nādaṃ vyamuñcat tvarayā pratītaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the son of the Sun, confident and swift, released a roar like the rumbling of masses of clouds,
his splendor increased by courage, like the ocean with waves stirred restlessly by the wind.

children.text: atha tasya ninādaṃ taṃ sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vālī</s>, who was intolerant of his brother,
heard the roar of great-souled <s>Sugrīva</s> while he was inside the inner palace.
When he heard that roar, which made all beings tremble,

children.text: madaś caikapade naṣṭaḥ krodhaś cāpatito mahān ||
children.translated_text: his intoxication vanished in an instant, and a great anger came upon him.
With his limbs filled by wrath, <s>Vālī</s>, bright like the glow of sunset,
suddenly lost his radiance, like the sun when eclipsed.
Terrible with his fangs, and like blazing fire from anger, <s>Vālī</s>
shone like a lake with its lotuses torn up, stalks and all.

children.text: śabdaṃ durmarṣaṇaṃ śrutvā niṣpapāta tato hariḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing the unbearable sound, the monkey then sprang out,
as if tearing the earth with the force of his footsteps.

children.text: taṃ tu tārā pariṣvajya snehād darśitasauhṛdā
children.translated_text: But <s>Tārā</s>, embracing him and showing affection out of love,
spoke these words, frightened and agitated, words aimed at his future welfare:

children.text: sādhu krodham imaṃ vīra nadīvegam ivāgatam
children.translated_text: Hero, cast aside this anger, which has arisen like the rush of a river;

children.text: śayanād utthitaḥ kālyaṃ tyaja bhuktām iva srajam ||
children.translated_text: having risen from bed at dawn, cast it off like a garland already worn.

children.text: sahasā tava niṣkrāmo mama tāvan na rocate
children.translated_text: Your rushing out so suddenly does not please me, at least for now.
Listen; I shall tell you the reason why I am holding you back.

children.text: pūrvam āpatitaḥ krodhāt sa tvām āhvayate yudhi
children.translated_text: Previously he came upon you in anger and challenged you to battle;

children.text: niṣpatya ca nirastas te hanyamāno diśo gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: after coming out, he was driven back by you, and, being struck, fled in all directions.
That he, once repulsed by you and especially afflicted,

children.text: ihaitya punar āhvānaṃ śaṅkāṃ janayatīva me ||
children.translated_text: has come here and challenged you again seems to raise suspicion in me.

children.text: darpaś ca vyavasāyaś ca yādṛśas tasya nardataḥ
children.translated_text: The pride and determination shown by him as he roars,

children.text: ninādasya ca saṃrambho naitad alpaṃ hi kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: and the vehemence of his roar: this surely does not have a small cause.

children.text: nāsahāyam ahaṃ manye sugrīvaṃ tam ihāgatam
children.translated_text: I do not think that <s>Sugrīva</s> has come here without help.
He is supported by some helper, relying on whom he roars like this.

children.text: prakṛtyā nipuṇaś caiva buddhimāṃś caiva vānaraḥ
children.translated_text: By nature the monkey is skillful and intelligent,
and <s>Sugrīva</s> would not come with an ally whose strength had not been tested.

children.text: pūrvam eva mayā vīra śrutaṃ kathayato vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Earlier, hero, I heard the words spoken

children.text: aṅgadasya kumārasya vakṣyāmi tvā hitaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by Prince <s>Aṅgada</s>; I shall tell you a word for your welfare.

children.text: tava bhrātur hi vikhyātaḥ sahāyo raṇakarkaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Your brother has a famous helper, harsh in battle:
<s>Rāma</s>, crusher of hostile forces, risen like the fire at the end of an age.
He is a dwelling-tree for the good, the supreme refuge of those in distress,
the shelter of the afflicted, and the sole receptacle of fame.
Endowed with knowledge and discernment, devoted to his father's command,

children.text: dhātūnām iva śailendro guṇānām ākaro mahān ||
children.translated_text: he is, like the lord of mountains for minerals, a great mine of virtues.

children.text: tatkṣamaṃ na virodhas te saha tena mahātmanā
children.translated_text: Therefore it is fitting that there be no opposition between you
and great-souled <s>Rāma</s>, hard to conquer and immeasurable in deeds of war.

children.text: śūra vakṣyāmi te kiṃcin na cecchāmy abhyasūyitum
children.translated_text: Hero, I shall tell you something, and I do not wish to reproach you.

children.text: śrūyatāṃ kriyatāṃ caiva tava vakṣyāmi yaddhitam ||
children.translated_text: Listen, and do what I shall tell you for your welfare.
Quickly and properly consecrate <s>Sugrīva</s> as heir apparent.

children.text: vigrahaṃ mā kṛthā vīra bhrātrā rājan balīyasā ||
children.translated_text: Hero, king, do not make war with your stronger brother.

children.text: ahaṃ hi te kṣamaṃ manye tava rāmeṇa sauhṛdam
children.translated_text: For I think friendship with <s>Rāma</s> is suitable for you,

children.text: sugrīveṇa ca samprītiṃ vairam utsṛjya dūrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and full affection with <s>Sugrīva</s>, after casting enmity far away.

children.text: lālanīyo hi te bhrātā yavīyān eṣa vānaraḥ
children.translated_text: This younger brother, this monkey, should be cherished by you.

children.text: tatra vā sann ihastho vā sarvathā bandhur eva te ||
children.translated_text: Whether he is there or dwelling here, in every way he is your kinsman.

children.text: yadi te matpriyaṃ kāryaṃ yadi cāvaiṣi māṃ hitām
children.translated_text: If what is dear to me is to be done by you, and if you know me to be seeking your welfare,

children.text: yācyamānaḥ prayatnena sādhu vākyaṃ kuruṣva me ||
children.translated_text: then, earnestly entreated, do this good word of mine.
As <s>Tārā</s>, whose face was like the lord of the stars, spoke in this way,
<s>Vālī</s> rebuked her and said these words:

children.text: garjato 'sya ca saṃrambhaṃ bhrātuḥ śatror viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: For what reason should I endure the fury of this roaring brother,
especially when he is an enemy, fair-faced one?
For heroes who cannot be insulted and who do not turn back in battles,
timid one, not enduring insult is greater even than death.

children.text: soḍhuṃ na ca samartho 'haṃ yuddhakāmasya saṃyuge
children.translated_text: I am not able to bear, in battle, the fury
of <s>Sugrīva</s>, who desires war and roars with his wretched neck.

children.text: na ca kāryo viṣādas te rāghavaṃ prati matkṛte
children.translated_text: And you should not grieve on my account regarding <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: dharmajñaś ca kṛtajñaś ca kathaṃ pāpaṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: He knows <s>dharma</s> and is grateful; how could he commit evil?
Turn back with the women; why do you follow me any farther?

children.text: sauhṛdaṃ darśitaṃ tāre mayi bhaktiḥ kṛtā tvayā ||
children.translated_text: You have shown friendship, <s>Tārā</s>; you have shown devotion to me.

children.text: pratiyotsyāmy ahaṃ gatvā sugrīvaṃ jahi sambhramam
children.translated_text: I shall go and fight <s>Sugrīva</s>; cast off your alarm.

children.text: darpaṃ cāsya vineṣyāmi na ca prāṇair vimokṣyate ||
children.translated_text: And I shall take away his pride; he will not escape with his life.

children.text: śāpitāsi mama prāṇair nivartasva jayena ca
children.translated_text: I adjure you by my life and by victory: turn back.

children.text: ahaṃ jitvā nivartiṣye tam alaṃ bhrātaraṃ raṇe ||
children.translated_text: After defeating that brother in battle, I shall return.

children.text: taṃ tu tārā pariṣvajya vālinaṃ priyavādinī
children.translated_text: Then <s>Tārā</s>, speaking affectionately, embraced her beloved <s>Vālī</s>,

children.text: cakāra rudatī mandaṃ dakṣiṇā sā pradakṣiṇam ||
children.translated_text: and, weeping softly, she circumambulated him auspiciously to the right.
Then, having performed a benediction with mantras, wishing him victory,
she entered the inner palace with the women, bewildered by grief.

children.text: praviṣṭāyāṃ tu tārāyāṃ saha strībhiḥ svam ālayam
children.translated_text: When <s>Tārā</s> had entered her own dwelling with the women,

children.text: nagarān niryayau kruddho mahāsarpa iva śvasan ||
children.translated_text: he went out from the city in anger, breathing like a great serpent.
With a deep breath, the immensely swift <s>Vālī</s>, filled with supreme rage,
sent his gaze in every direction, longing to see his enemy.

children.text: sa dadarśa tataḥ śrīmān sugrīvaṃ hemapiṅgalam
children.translated_text: Then the splendid one saw <s>Sugrīva</s>, tawny like gold,
well wrapped and firmly planted, blazing like fire.

children.text: sa taṃ dṛṣṭvā mahāvīryaṃ sugrīvaṃ paryavasthitam
children.translated_text: Seeing mighty <s>Sugrīva</s> standing there before him,
<s>Vālī</s>, in utmost anger, tightened his garment firmly around himself.

children.text: sa vālī gāḍhasaṃvīto muṣṭim udyamya vīryavān
children.translated_text: Thus tightly girded, powerful <s>Vālī</s> raised his fist,
and, resolved upon battle, went straight toward <s>Sugrīva</s> to fight.
With his clenched fist lifted, he came on still more enraged;
<s>Sugrīva</s> too advanced, aiming at golden-garlanded <s>Vālī</s>.
Then <s>Vālī</s>, his eyes copper-red with anger, spoke these words
to <s>Sugrīva</s>, skilled in battle, as he rushed forward with great speed:

children.text: eṣa muṣṭir mayā baddho gāḍhaḥ sunihitāṅguliḥ
children.translated_text: This fist of mine is clenched, tight, with the fingers well set;

children.text: mayā vegavimuktas te prāṇān ādāya yāsyati ||
children.translated_text: released by me with force, it will depart after taking your life.

children.text: evam uktas tu sugrīvaḥ kruddho vālinam abravīt
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, angry <s>Sugrīva</s> said to <s>Vālī</s>:

children.text: tavaiva ca haran prāṇān muṣṭiḥ patatu mūrdhani ||
children.translated_text: Rather, let my fist fall upon your head, taking your own life.
Struck by him, he became enraged and charged forward swiftly;
he began to pour out blood, like a mountain with a stream bursting from it.

children.text: sugrīveṇa tu niḥsaṅgaṃ sālam utpāṭya tejasā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sugrīva</s>, with his force, effortlessly uprooted a sāla tree,
and <s>Vālī</s> was struck on his limbs like a great mountain by a thunderbolt.
But <s>Vālī</s>, shaken and bewildered by the blow of the sāla tree,
became like a boat in the ocean overwhelmed by a heavy load.
Those two, terrible in strength and valor, equal in speed to <s>Suparṇa</s>,
grown mighty and dreadful in form, were like the moon and sun in the sky.
<s>Sugrīva</s>, whose pride had been broken by <s>Vālī</s>, moved with diminished force,
yet, still angry at <s>Vālī</s>, he showed his quickness.
Then, setting on his bow an arrow like a poisonous serpent,
<s>Rāghava</s> sent the great shaft into <s>Vālī</s>'s chest.
Then mighty, radiant <s>Vālī</s>, lord of monkeys, swollen with strength,
struck by that arrow's force, fell down upon the earth.
Then, sprinkled by streams of blood like water, like a richly flowering aśoka shaken by the wind,

children.text: vicetano vāsavasūnur āhave prabhraṃśitendradhvajavat kṣitiṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the son of <s>Vāsava</s>, unconscious in battle, went to the ground like <s>Indra</s>'s banner brought down.
Then, struck by <s>Rāma</s>'s arrow, battle-hardened <s>Vālī</s>

children.text: papāta sahasā vālī nikṛtta iva pādapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: suddenly fell like a tree cut down.
He fell with all his limbs laid upon the ground, adorned with ornaments of heated gold,
like the banner of the king of the gods with its cords loosened.
When that lord of the hosts of monkeys had fallen upon the ground,

children.text: naṣṭacandram iva vyoma na vyarājata bhūtalam ||
children.translated_text: the earth no longer shone, like the sky when its moon is lost.
Even as that great-souled one's body lay fallen on the ground,

children.text: na śrīr jahāti na prāṇā na tejo na parākramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: neither beauty, nor life, nor energy, nor valor abandoned it.
The excellent golden garland, jewel-adorned and given by <s>Śakra</s>,

children.text: dadhāra harimukhyasya prāṇāṃs tejaḥ śriyaṃ ca sā ||
children.translated_text: sustained the chief monkey's life, energy, and splendor.

children.text: sa tayā mālayā vīro haimayā hariyūthapaḥ
children.translated_text: With that golden garland, the heroic leader of the monkey troops
was like a rain cloud whose edges are touched by twilight.

children.text: tasya mālā ca dehaś ca marmaghātī ca yaḥ śaraḥ
children.translated_text: His garland, his body, and the arrow that struck a vital spot,
these three forms of splendor shone even as he lay fallen.
That weapon, opening the hero's path to heaven,
shot from <s>Rāma</s>'s bow, bore him toward the highest state.

children.text: taṃ tathā patitaṃ saṃkhye gatārciṣam ivānalam
children.translated_text: Him fallen thus in battle, like a fire whose flame had gone out,
like <s>Yayāti</s> fallen from the world of the gods when his merit was spent,

children.text: ādityam iva kālena yugānte bhuvi pātitam
children.translated_text: like the sun cast down to earth by Time at the end of an age,

children.text: mahendram iva durdharṣaṃ mahendram iva duḥsaham ||
children.translated_text: like mighty <s>Indra</s>, unassailable, like mighty <s>Indra</s>, hard to withstand,
that fallen <s>Vālī</s>, son of <s>Mahendra</s>, wearing the golden garland,
lion-chested, great-armed, bright-faced, and tawny-eyed,
<s>Rāma</s>, accompanied by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, saw and approached.

children.text: sa dṛṣṭvā rāghavaṃ vālī lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahābalam
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Rāghava</s> and mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
<s>Vālī</s> spoke humble words, harsh yet grounded in <s>dharma</s> (righteous order).

children.text: parāṅmukhavadhaṃ kṛtvā ko nu prāptas tvayā guṇaḥ
children.translated_text: What virtue have you gained by killing one whose face was turned away,

children.text: yad ahaṃ yuddhasaṃrabdhas tvatkṛte nidhanaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: since I, absorbed in battle, have met death because of you?
High-born, endowed with courage, radiant, firm in his vows,

children.text: rāmaḥ karuṇavedī ca prajānāṃ ca hite rataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> knows compassion and is devoted to the welfare of his subjects;
merciful, greatly energetic, a knower of proper agreements, firm in his vow,

children.text: iti te sarvabhūtāni kathayanti yaśo bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: so all beings on earth proclaim your fame.

children.text: tān guṇān sampradhāryāham agryaṃ cābhijanaṃ tava
children.translated_text: Reflecting on those virtues and on your foremost lineage,
though restrained by <s>Tārā</s>, I came to meet <s>Sugrīva</s>.

children.text: na mām anyena saṃrabdhaṃ pramattaṃ veddhum arhasi
children.translated_text: You ought not to have pierced me, unaware and enraged against another,

children.text: iti me buddhir utpannā babhūvādarśane tava ||
children.translated_text: such was the thought that arose in me, since you were out of sight.
I did not know you as one whose very self is ruined, a banner of <s>dharma</s> yet adharmic,
a man of sinful conduct, like a well covered over with grass.

children.text: satāṃ veṣadharaṃ pāpaṃ pracchannam iva pāvakam
children.translated_text: You are a sinner wearing the costume of the good, like a hidden fire;
I do not recognize you, covered over by a cloak of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: viṣaye vā pure vā te yadā nāpakaromy aham
children.translated_text: When I have done you no harm in your territory or in your city,

children.text: na ca tvāṃ pratijāne 'haṃ kasmāt tvaṃ haṃsy akilbiṣam ||
children.translated_text: and I do not acknowledge you as an enemy, why do you kill me, who am blameless?
I am always eating fruits and roots, a monkey who ranges in the forest;
here I was not fighting you, but had met with another.
You are the son of a lord of men, renowned and pleasant to behold;

children.text: liṅgam apy asti te rājan dṛśyate dharmasaṃhitam ||
children.translated_text: and even your outward mark, O king, is seen to be joined with <s>dharma</s>.
Who, born in a kṣatriya family, learned, and free from doubt,
would commit a cruel act while concealed beneath the mark of <s>dharma</s>?

children.text: rāma rājakule jāto dharmavān iti viśrutaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, born in a royal family and famed as righteous,
why do you run about as one unworthy, while wearing a worthy form?

children.text: sāma dānaṃ kṣamā dharmaḥ satyaṃ dhṛtiparākramau
children.translated_text: Conciliation, giving, forbearance, <s>dharma</s>, truth, steadiness, and valor

children.text: pārthivānāṃ guṇā rājan daṇḍaś cāpy apakāriṣu ||
children.translated_text: are the qualities of kings, O king, and also punishment for offenders.
We are forest-roaming creatures, <s>Rāma</s>, animals who eat roots and fruits;

children.text: eṣā prakṛtir asmākaṃ puruṣas tvaṃ nareśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: this is our nature, while you, lord of men, are a human being.

children.text: bhūmir hiraṇyaṃ rūpyaṃ ca nigrahe kāraṇāni ca
children.translated_text: Land, gold, silver, and grounds for restraint

children.text: tatra kas te vane lobho madīyeṣu phaleṣu vā ||
children.translated_text: are the causes there; what greed have you in the forest, or in my fruits?

children.text: nayaś ca vinayaś cobhau nigrahānugrahāv api
children.translated_text: Policy and discipline, both of them, and restraint and favor as well,
make up a king's conduct in unmixed form; kings are not ruled by desire.

children.text: tvaṃ tu kāmapradhānaś ca kopanaś cānavasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: But you are governed chiefly by desire, irascible and unstable,
confused in the practices of kingship, devoted to your bow and arrows.

children.text: na te 'sty apacitir dharme nārthe buddhir avasthitā
children.translated_text: You have no regard for <s>dharma</s>, and your understanding is not fixed on <s>artha</s> (advantage);
being desire-driven by your senses, you are dragged along, lord of men.
After killing me here with an arrow, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, though I had committed no offense,

children.text: kiṃ vakṣyasi satāṃ madhye karma kṛtvā jugupsitam ||
children.translated_text: what will you say among good men, having done a loathsome deed?

children.text: rājahā brahmahā goghnaś coraḥ prāṇivadhe rataḥ
children.translated_text: A king-slayer, a brahman-slayer, a cow-killer, a thief, one delighting in killing living beings,
an atheist, and a parivettṛ (one who improperly marries before an elder brother): all go to hell.

children.text: adhāryaṃ carma me sadbhī romāṇy asthi ca varjitam
children.translated_text: My hide is not to be worn by good men, and my hair and bone are to be avoided;
my flesh too is not to be eaten by practitioners of <s>dharma</s> such as you.
Five five-clawed creatures may be eaten by brahmans and kṣatriyas, O <s>Rāghava</s>:

children.text: śalyakaḥ śvāvidho godhā śaśaḥ kūrmaś ca pañcamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the porcupine, the hedgehog, the monitor lizard, the hare, and the tortoise as the fifth.

children.text: carma cāsthi ca me rājan na spṛśanti manīṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: But wise men do not touch my hide or bone, O king,

children.text: abhakṣyāṇi ca māṃsāni so 'haṃ pañcanakho hataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and my flesh is not to be eaten; yet I, a five-clawed creature, have been killed.

children.text: tvayā nāthena kākutstha na sanāthā vasuṃdharā
children.translated_text: With you as protector, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, the earth is not protected,
like a woman endowed with good character who has fallen to a rogue.
Deceitful, fraudulent, petty, with a mind falsely bent in humility,

children.text: kathaṃ daśarathena tvaṃ jātaḥ pāpo mahātmanā ||
children.translated_text: how were you, evil as you are, born from great-souled <s>Daśaratha</s>?
By one whose boundary of conduct is cut away, who transgresses the <s>dharma</s> of the good,
by the elephant <s>Rāma</s>, who has cast off the goad of <s>dharma</s>, I have been struck down.

children.text: dṛśyamānas tu yudhyethā mayā yudhi nṛpātmaja
children.translated_text: If you had fought me openly, son of a king, in battle,

children.text: adya vaivasvataṃ devaṃ paśyes tvaṃ nihato mayā ||
children.translated_text: today you, struck down by me, would have seen the god <s>Vaivasvata</s>.
But I, hard to assail, have been killed by you while you were unseen in battle,
like a sleeping man under the power of drink killed by a serpent.
Because I was killed by you from a desire to please <s>Sugrīva</s>,

children.text: kaṇṭhe baddhvā pradadyāṃ te 'nihataṃ rāvaṇaṃ raṇe ||
children.translated_text: had I not been killed, I would have bound <s>Rāvaṇa</s> by the neck and handed him over to you in battle.

children.text: nyastāṃ sāgaratoye vā pātāle vāpi maithilīm
children.translated_text: Whether <s>Maithilī</s> had been placed in the waters of the ocean or even in the underworld,
I would have brought her at your command, like a white she-mule.

children.text: yuktaṃ yat prāpnuyād rājyaṃ sugrīvaḥ svargate mayi
children.translated_text: It is proper that <s>Sugrīva</s> should obtain the kingdom when I have gone to heaven;

children.text: ayuktaṃ yad adharmeṇa tvayāhaṃ nihato raṇe ||
children.translated_text: what is improper is that I have been killed by you through adharma in battle.
Indeed the world is assigned by time to such a condition as this;

children.text: kṣamaṃ ced bhavatā prāptam uttaraṃ sādhu cintyatām ||
children.translated_text: if a fitting answer has come to you, let it be carefully considered.

children.text: ity evam uktvā pariśuṣkavaktraḥ śarābhighātād vyathito mahātmā
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, his mouth parched and his great soul pained by the strike of the arrow,
the son of the king of the immortals looked at sun-like <s>Rāma</s> and became silent.

children.text: ity uktaḥ praśritaṃ vākyaṃ dharmārthasahitaṃ hitam
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the slain, bewildered <s>Vālī</s> with a humble speech
that was joined with <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>, beneficial though harsh, <s>Rāma</s>
saw that best of monkeys, dim like the sun and like a cloud emptied of water,
who had spoken his words and was like a fire grown calm.
Then <s>Rāma</s>, reproached by the unsurpassed lord of monkeys,

children.text: adhikṣiptas tadā rāmaḥ paścād vālinam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: who was endowed with the virtues of <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>, afterward spoke to <s>Vālī</s>:

children.text: dharmam arthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca samayaṃ cāpi laukikam
children.translated_text: Without understanding <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and also worldly convention,

children.text: avijñāya kathaṃ bālyān mām ihādya vigarhase ||
children.translated_text: how do you blame me here today out of childishness?
Without questioning wise elders who are honored as teachers,

children.text: saumya vānaracāpalyāt tvaṃ māṃ vaktum ihecchasi ||
children.translated_text: gentle one, out of monkey-fickleness you wish to speak to me here.
This earth belongs to the <s>Ikṣvākus</s>, together with its mountains, forests, and groves,
and so too the restraint and favoring of animals, birds, and human beings.

children.text: tāṃ pālayati dharmātmā bharataḥ satyavāg ṛjuḥ
children.translated_text: Righteous <s>Bharata</s>, truthful in speech and upright, protects it,
knowing the principles of <s>dharma</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>artha</s>, intent on restraint and favor.

children.text: nayaś ca vinayaś cobhau yasmin satyaṃ ca susthitam
children.translated_text: In him policy and discipline are both well established, and truth as well;

children.text: vikramaś ca yathā dṛṣṭaḥ sa rājā deśakālavit ||
children.translated_text: his valor is seen accordingly; he is the king, a knower of place and time.

children.text: tasya dharmakṛtādeśā vayam anye ca pārthivaḥ
children.translated_text: By his command, which acts in accordance with <s>dharma</s>, we and other rulers
move over the whole earth, desiring the continuance of <s>dharma</s>.
When that tiger among kings, <s>Bharata</s>, is devoted to <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: pālayaty akhilāṃ bhūmiṃ kaś cared dharmanigraham ||
children.translated_text: When he protects the whole earth, who could act in defiance of lawful restraint?

children.text: te vayaṃ mārgavibhraṣṭaṃ svadharme parame sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore we, established in our own supreme <s>dharma</s> (duty), restrain the one who has strayed from the path,
placing <s>Bharata</s>'s command before us, according to rule.

children.text: tvaṃ tu saṃkliṣṭadharmā ca karmaṇā ca vigarhitaḥ
children.translated_text: But you are one whose <s>dharma</s> is confused and whose conduct is blameworthy;
you are governed chiefly by desire and are not established in the path of kings.

children.text: jyeṣṭho bhrātā pitā caiva yaś ca vidyāṃ prayacchati
children.translated_text: An elder brother, a father, and also one who gives instruction

children.text: trayas te pitaro jñeyā dharme ca pathi vartinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: are to be known as three fathers, when they walk on the path of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: yavīyān ātmanaḥ putraḥ śiṣyaś cāpi guṇoditaḥ
children.translated_text: One younger than oneself, one's son, and also a pupil distinguished by virtues

children.text: putravat te trayaś cintyā dharmaś ced atra kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: are three whom you should regard like sons, if <s>dharma</s> is the point at issue here.
The <s>dharma</s> of the good is subtle and extremely hard to understand, O monkey;
the self dwelling in the heart of all beings knows good and evil.
Unsteady yourself, with unsteady, undisciplined monkeys,

children.text: jātyandha iva jātyandhair mantrayan drakṣyase nu kim ||
children.translated_text: what will you perceive while deliberating, like one born blind with others born blind?

children.text: ahaṃ tu vyaktatām asya vacanasya bravīmi te
children.translated_text: But I shall speak to you plainly about the meaning of this statement;

children.text: na hi māṃ kevalaṃ roṣāt tvaṃ vigarhitum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: you ought not to denounce me merely from anger.

children.text: tad etat kāraṇaṃ paśya yadarthaṃ tvaṃ mayā hataḥ
children.translated_text: See then this reason for the sake of which you were killed by me:

children.text: bhrātur vartasi bhāryāyāṃ tyaktvā dharmaṃ sanātanam ||
children.translated_text: you have relations with your brother's wife, abandoning eternal <s>dharma</s>.
While this great-souled <s>Sugrīva</s> is still alive,
you, sinner, act from desire toward <s>Rumā</s>, your daughter-in-law by relation.

children.text: tad vyatītasya te dharmāt kāmavṛttasya vānara
children.translated_text: Therefore, O monkey, since you have fallen away from <s>dharma</s> and conduct yourself by desire,
this punishment has been prescribed for this violation of a brother's wife.
For one opposed to <s>dharma</s> and departed from the practice of the world,
I see no restraint other than punishment, O leader of monkey troops.

children.text: aurasīṃ bhaginīṃ vāpi bhāryāṃ vāpy anujasya yaḥ
children.translated_text: If a man from desire should approach his own daughter, or his sister,

children.text: pracareta naraḥ kāmāt tasya daṇḍo vadhaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or the wife of his younger brother, his punishment is declared to be death.

children.text: bharatas tu mahīpālo vayaṃ tv ādeśavartinaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s> is the protector of the earth, and we are obedient to his command;

children.text: tvaṃ ca dharmād atikrāntaḥ kathaṃ śakyam upekṣitum ||
children.translated_text: and you have transgressed <s>dharma</s>. How could you be overlooked?
Wise <s>Bharata</s>, protecting by <s>dharma</s> one who has violated the duty owed to elders,
stands firm in restraining those who act according to desire.

children.text: vayaṃ tu bharatādeśaṃ vidhiṃ kṛtvā harīśvara
children.translated_text: But we, O lord of monkeys, have made <s>Bharata</s>'s command our rule,
and stand ready to control those like you who have broken proper bounds.

children.text: sugrīveṇa ca me sakhyaṃ lakṣmaṇena yathā tathā
children.translated_text: My friendship with <s>Sugrīva</s> is just like my friendship with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>;

children.text: dārarājyanimittaṃ ca niḥśreyasi rataḥ sa me ||
children.translated_text: and, in the matter of wife and kingdom, he is devoted to my highest welfare.

children.text: pratijñā ca mayā dattā tadā vānarasaṃnidhau
children.translated_text: A promise was also given by me then in the presence of the monkeys;
and how could a promise be disregarded by one such as me?

children.text: tad ebhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ sarvair mahadbhir dharmasaṃhitaiḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, for all these great reasons, joined with <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: śāsanaṃ tava yad yuktaṃ tad bhavān anumanyatām ||
children.translated_text: please accept the chastisement that was fitting for you.

children.text: sarvathā dharma ity eva draṣṭavyas tava nigrahaḥ
children.translated_text: In every way your restraint must be regarded precisely as <s>dharma</s>;
one who keeps <s>dharma</s> in view must do good to a friend.

children.text: rājabhir dhṛtadaṇḍās tu kṛtvā pāpāni mānavāḥ
children.translated_text: Men who have committed sins, when punished by kings wielding the rod,

children.text: nirmalāḥ svargam āyānti santaḥ sukṛtino yathā ||
children.translated_text: become stainless and go to heaven, like good men who have done merit.

children.text: āryeṇa mama māndhātrā vyasanaṃ ghoram īpsitam
children.translated_text: By my noble ancestor <s>Māndhātṛ</s>, a terrible penalty was sought

children.text: śramaṇena kṛte pāpe yathā pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ tvayā ||
children.translated_text: when a wandering ascetic had committed a sin, just as the sin committed by you.

children.text: anyair api kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ pramattair vasudhādhipaiḥ
children.translated_text: Even other careless kings have committed sin,

children.text: prāyaścittaṃ ca kurvanti tena tac chāmyate rajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but they perform atonement, and by that the stain is calmed.
Therefore enough of grief. Your death, O tiger among monkeys, was determined according to <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: vadho vānaraśārdūla na vayaṃ svavaśe sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: we do not stand under our own independent will.

children.text: vāgurābhiś ca pāśaiś ca kūṭaiś ca vividhair narāḥ
children.translated_text: With nets, nooses, and many kinds of traps, men catch very many deer,

children.text: praticchannāś ca dṛśyāś ca gṛhṇanti subahūn mṛgān
children.translated_text: whether concealed or in plain sight,
whether they have run away, are terrified, are unsuspecting, or are standing still for too long.

children.text: pramattān apramattān vā narā māṃsārthino bhṛśam
children.translated_text: Men intent on meat shoot them fiercely, whether careless or alert,

children.text: vidhyanti vimukhāṃś cāpi na ca doṣo 'tra vidyate ||
children.translated_text: even when they are turned away, and there is no fault in this.
Royal sages skilled in <s>dharma</s> also go hunting here;

children.text: tasmāt tvaṃ nihato yuddhe mayā bāṇena vānara
children.translated_text: therefore you were killed in battle by me with an arrow, O monkey,

children.text: ayudhyan pratiyudhyan vā yasmāc chākhāmṛgo hy asi ||
children.translated_text: whether you were fighting or not fighting back, since you are indeed a branch-deer.

children.text: durlabhasya ca dharmasya jīvitasya śubhasya ca
children.translated_text: Kings, O best of monkeys, are without doubt the givers
of hard-won <s>dharma</s>, of life, and of auspicious welfare.

children.text: tān na hiṃsyān na cākrośen nākṣipen nāpriyaṃ vadet
children.translated_text: One should not harm them, revile them, reproach them, or speak what is unpleasant to them;
they move upon the earth as gods in human form.

children.text: tvaṃ tu dharmam avijñāya kevalaṃ roṣam āsthitaḥ
children.translated_text: But you, not understanding <s>dharma</s> and taking up only anger,
slander me, though I stand in the <s>dharma</s> of my fathers and grandfathers.

children.text: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa vālī pravyathito bhṛśam
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Vālī</s>, greatly distressed,
then answered <s>Rāma</s>, the lord of monkeys, with folded hands.

children.text: yat tvam āttha naraśreṣṭha tad evaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: What you say, O best of men, is exactly so; there is no doubt about it here.

children.text: prativaktuṃ prakṛṣṭe hi nāpakṛṣṭas tu śaknuyāt ||
children.translated_text: For an inferior person cannot answer back to one who is superior.

children.text: yad ayuktaṃ mayā pūrvaṃ pramādād vākyam apriyam
children.translated_text: Whatever improper and unpleasant word I spoke before through heedlessness,

children.text: tatrāpi khalu me doṣaṃ kartuṃ nārhasi rāghava ||
children.translated_text: even in that matter, O <s>Rāghava</s>, you ought not to hold the fault against me.

children.text: tvaṃ hi dṛṣṭārthatattvajñaḥ prajānāṃ ca hite rataḥ
children.translated_text: For you know the truth of visible affairs and are devoted to the welfare of your subjects;
your clear and unfailing intelligence is established in accomplishing means and ends.
Protect me too, O knower of <s>dharma</s>, with speech joined to <s>dharma</s>,
since I am understood as one who has strayed from <s>dharma</s> and put transgression first.
Then <s>Vālī</s>, his throat choked with tears and his cry full of pain, slowly

children.text: uvāca rāmaṃ samprekṣya paṅkalagna iva dvipaḥ ||
children.translated_text: spoke while looking at <s>Rāma</s>, like an elephant stuck in mud.

children.text: na tv ātmānam ahaṃ śoce na tārāṃ nāpi bāndhavān
children.translated_text: I do not grieve for myself, nor for <s>Tārā</s>, nor even for my kinsmen,
as I grieve for my son <s>Aṅgada</s>, foremost in virtues, wearing golden armlets.

children.text: sa mamādarśanād dīno bālyāt prabhṛti lālitaḥ
children.translated_text: Dejected because he will not see me, cherished from childhood onward,
he will waste away like a pond whose water has been drunk up.

children.text: sugrīve cāṅgade caiva vidhatsva matim uttamām
children.translated_text: Set your best thought upon <s>Sugrīva</s> and upon <s>Aṅgada</s> as well.

children.text: tvaṃ hi śāstā ca goptā ca kāryākāryavidhau sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For you are the ruler and protector, established in deciding what is to be done and what is not to be done.

children.text: yā te narapate vṛttir bharate lakṣmaṇe ca yā
children.translated_text: The conduct that you have toward <s>Bharata</s> and toward <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, O lord of men,

children.text: sugrīve cāṅgade rājaṃs tāṃ cintayitum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: that same conduct, O king, you ought to consider toward <s>Sugrīva</s> and <s>Aṅgada</s>.
So that <s>Sugrīva</s> may not despise that poor <s>Tārā</s>, made faulty by faults caused by me,
you ought to stand firm in such a way.

children.text: tvayā hy anugṛhītena śakyaṃ rājyam upāsitum
children.translated_text: For only when favored by you can the kingdom be attended to,
by one who remains under your control and follows your will.

children.text: sa tam āśvāsayad rāmo vālinaṃ vyaktadarśanam ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s> comforted that clear-sighted <s>Vāli</s>.

children.text: na vayaṃ bhavatā cintyā nāpy ātmā harisattama
children.translated_text: We are not to be worried over by you, nor is your own self, best of monkeys.
We, especially in your case, have made our decision according to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order).

children.text: daṇḍye yaḥ pātayed daṇḍaṃ daṇḍyo yaś cāpi daṇḍyate
children.translated_text: He who imposes punishment on one deserving punishment, and he who is punished when deserving punishment,
both have accomplished the purpose of cause and effect, and neither of them comes to ruin.
Therefore, by contact with this punishment, you, free from sin,

children.text: gataḥ svāṃ prakṛtiṃ dharmyāṃ dharmadṛṣṭena vartmanā ||
children.translated_text: have gone to your own righteous nature by a path viewed through <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: sa tasya vākyaṃ madhuraṃ mahātmanaḥ samāhitaṃ dharmapathānuvartinaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing the sweet, composed words of great-souled <s>Rāma</s>, who followed the path of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: niśamya rāmasya raṇāvamardino vacaḥ suyuktaṃ nijagāda vānaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: the monkey spoke fitting words to <s>Rāma</s>, crusher of foes in battle.

children.text: śarābhitaptena vicetasā mayā pradūṣitas tvaṃ yad ajānatā prabho
children.translated_text: Because, my mind bewildered and scorched by the arrow, I ignorantly maligned you, lord,

children.text: idaṃ mahendropamabhīmavikrama prasāditas tvaṃ kṣama me mahīśvara ||
children.translated_text: now that you are appeased, forgive me, great lord of the earth, whose dreadful valor is like <s>Mahendra</s>'s.
That great king of the monkeys, lying pierced by the arrow,
answered by reasoned words, found no further reply.
His body shattered by stones and violently struck by trees,
and overwhelmed by <s>Rāma</s>'s arrow, he fainted at the end of his life.
His wife <s>Tārā</s> heard that <s>Vāli</s>, tiger among leaping monkeys,
had been slain in battle by the release of the arrow from <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: sā saputrāpriyaṃ śrutvā vadhaṃ bhartuḥ sudāruṇam
children.translated_text: When she, together with her son, heard the terrible and most cruel killing of her husband,
she rushed out, deeply terrified, from various mountain caves.

children.text: ye tv aṅgadaparīvārā vānarā hi mahābalāḥ
children.translated_text: But the mighty monkeys who were <s>Aṅgada</s>'s retinue,

children.text: te sakārmukam ālokya rāmaṃ trastāḥ pradudruvuḥ ||
children.translated_text: seeing <s>Rāma</s> with his bow, fled away in fear.

children.text: sā dadarśa tatas trastān harīn āpatato drutam
children.translated_text: Then she saw the frightened monkeys hastening quickly toward her,
like deer separated from a herd whose herd-leader had been killed.

children.text: tān uvāca samāsādya duḥkhitān duḥkhitā satī
children.translated_text: Approaching those sorrowing ones, herself sorrowful,
she spoke to them all, terrified by <s>Rāma</s>, as though pursued by arrows:
O monkeys, you whose leader was that lion among kings,

children.text: taṃ vihāya suvitrastāḥ kasmād dravata durgatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: why, abandoning him, do you flee so terrified and distressed?

children.text: rājyahetoḥ sa ced bhrātā bhrātā raudreṇa pātitaḥ
children.translated_text: If that brother has been struck down for the sake of the kingdom by his brother,
by <s>Rāma</s>'s dreadful arrows, shot from afar and falling far away,
then the monkeys, able to assume forms at will, hearing the words of the monkey's wife,
spoke to the lady words that were timely and not disconnected from the matter at hand:
Since your son lives, turn back, and protect your son <s>Aṅgada</s>.
Death, in the form of <s>Rāma</s>, has killed <s>Vāli</s> and is carrying him away.

children.text: kṣiptān vṛkṣān samāvidhya vipulāś ca śilās tathā
children.translated_text: After he had hurled thrown trees and also huge rocks,
<s>Vāli</s> was brought down by arrows like thunderbolts, as if by the thunderbolt itself.

children.text: abhidrutam idaṃ sarvaṃ vidrutaṃ prasṛtaṃ balam
children.translated_text: All this army has been attacked, scattered, and put to flight,
now that this tiger among leaping monkeys, equal in splendor to <s>Śakra</s>, has been slain.
Let the city be protected by heroes, and let <s>Aṅgada</s> be consecrated.
The leaping monkeys will follow <s>Vāli</s>'s son when he stands in his father's place.

children.text: atha vā ruciraṃ sthānam iha te rucirānane
children.translated_text: Or else, lovely-faced one, if this place is pleasing to you, remain here;

children.text: āviśanti hi durgāṇi kṣipram adyaiva vānarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for the monkeys are entering the fortresses quickly, this very day.

children.text: abhāryāḥ sahabhāryāś ca santy atra vanacāriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: There are forest-roamers here, some without wives and some with wives.

children.text: lubdhebhyo viprayuktebhyaḥ svebhyo nas tumulaṃ bhayam ||
children.translated_text: We have terrible fear from our own people when they are greedy and separated from order.
Hearing the words of those who had come only a short distance away, the lady,
the lovely-smiling woman, spoke what was fitting for herself:

children.text: putreṇa mama kiṃ kāryaṃ kiṃ rājyena kim ātmanā
children.translated_text: What need have I of a son? What need of a kingdom? What need of myself,
when that great-fortuned lion among monkeys, my husband, is perishing?
I shall go to the foot of that very great-souled one,
who has been struck down by an arrow sent by <s>Rāma</s>.
Having spoken thus, she ran forward, weeping and wasted by grief,

children.text: śiraś coraś ca bāhubhyāṃ duḥkhena samabhighnatī ||
children.translated_text: beating her head and breast with both arms in anguish.
As she came near, she then saw her husband fallen on the ground,
the slayer of lords of demons who never turned back in battles,
the hurler of great mountains, like <s>Vāsava</s> hurling thunderbolts,
sounding like a mass of great clouds filled with a mighty wind,
equal to <s>Śakra</s> in valor, like a rain-cloud that has poured down and ceased,

children.text: nardantaṃ nardatāṃ bhīmaṃ śūraṃ śūreṇa pātitam
children.translated_text: a terrible roarer among roaring warriors, a hero felled by a hero,
like a king of beasts killed by a tiger for the sake of meat.
Honored by all the world, with its banner and altar,
like a shrine torn down by <s>Suparṇa</s> for the sake of a serpent,
she, the auspicious one, saw <s>Rāma</s>, powerful with his bow, standing supported on it,

children.text: rāmaṃ rāmānujaṃ caiva bhartuś caivānujaṃ śubhā ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Rāma</s>'s younger brother, and also her husband's younger brother.

children.text: tān atītya samāsādya bhartāraṃ nihataṃ raṇe
children.translated_text: Passing by them, she approached her husband, slain in battle.

children.text: samīkṣya vyathitā bhūmau saṃbhrāntā nipapāta ha ||
children.translated_text: Seeing him, distressed and bewildered, she fell upon the ground.
Then, rising again as if from sleep, crying, "O noble lord!"

children.text: ruroda sā patiṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃditaṃ mṛtyudāmabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: she wept, seeing her husband bound by the cords of death.

children.text: tām avekṣya tu sugrīvaḥ krośantīṃ kurarīm iva
children.translated_text: But <s>Sugrīva</s>, seeing her crying like an osprey,

children.text: viṣādam agamat kaṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭvā cāṅgadam āgatam ||
children.translated_text: fell into terrible despondency, and also seeing <s>Aṅgada</s> arrived.
By the death-dealing arrow released from <s>Rāma</s>'s bow,
seeing him slain upon the ground, <s>Tārā</s>, whose face was like the moon,
that radiant woman came to her husband and embraced him,
seeing <s>Vālī</s>, elephant-like, struck down by the arrow.
Her mind scorched by grief, seeing the lord of monkeys, like great <s>Indra</s>,
<s>Tārā</s>, afflicted, lamented over him like an uprooted tree.
"O you of terrible prowess in battle, heroic one, best of leapers,

children.text: kiṃ dīnām apurobhāgām adya tvaṃ nābhibhāṣase ||
children.translated_text: why do you not speak to me today, wretched and standing before you?
Rise up, tiger among monkeys; take to a better couch.
Excellent kings do not lie on the ground in such a way.

children.text: atīva khalu te kāntā vasudhā vasudhādhipa
children.translated_text: Surely this earth is very dear to you, O lord of the earth,

children.text: gatāsur api yāṃ gātrair māṃ vihāya niṣevase ||
children.translated_text: since, even with life gone, you touch her with your limbs, abandoning me.

children.text: vyaktam anyā tvayā vīra dharmataḥ sampravartitā
children.translated_text: Clearly, hero, another lovely city has been set in motion by you according to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),
built on the road to heaven, just like the city <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>.

children.text: yāny asmābhis tvayā sārdhaṃ vaneṣu madhugandhiṣu
children.translated_text: Those times that we spent together with you in honey-scented forests,

children.text: vihṛtāni tvayā kāle teṣām uparamaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: sporting with you in due season, have now been brought to an end.
Joyless, hopeless, I am sunk in an ocean of grief,
now that you, great leader of troop-lords, have reached dissolution into the five elements.

children.text: hṛdayaṃ susthiraṃ mahyaṃ dṛṣṭvā vinihataṃ bhuvi
children.translated_text: My heart must be very hard, seeing you slain upon the earth,
because, though scorched by grief, it does not burst today into a thousand pieces.

children.text: sugrīvasya tvayā bhāryā hṛtā sa ca vivāsitaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s>'s wife was taken by you, and he was driven into exile;

children.text: yat tat tasya tvayā vyuṣṭiḥ prāpteyaṃ plavagādhipa ||
children.translated_text: because of that deed, this return from him has come upon you, lord of leapers.
Intent on the highest good, I was rebuked by you in delusion,
when I spoke beneficial words, desiring the welfare of the lord of monkeys.
Without doubt it was Time itself, the ender of your life,
by which you were forcibly brought, helpless, under <s>Sugrīva</s>'s power.
I, a wretched woman, will endure widowhood, the torment of grief, pitiable as I am,
though formerly raised without sorrow, now like one without a protector.
And heroic <s>Aṅgada</s>, cherished, tender, accustomed to comfort,

children.text: vatsyate kām avasthāṃ me pitṛvye krodhamūrchite ||
children.translated_text: what condition will my son live in, with his paternal uncle stupefied by anger?
Son, look well upon your father, devoted to <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty).

children.text: durlabhaṃ darśanaṃ tv asya tava vatsa bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: For seeing him will be difficult for you hereafter, dear child.

children.text: samāśvāsaya putraṃ tvaṃ saṃdeśaṃ saṃdiśasva ca
children.translated_text: Comfort your son, and give him a message.

children.text: mūrdhni cainaṃ samāghrāya pravāsaṃ prasthito hy asi ||
children.translated_text: Smell his head, for you are setting out on a distant journey.

children.text: rāmeṇa hi mahat karma kṛtaṃ tvām abhinighnatā
children.translated_text: Indeed <s>Rāma</s> has done a great deed by striking you down;

children.text: ānṛṇyaṃ tu gataṃ tasya sugrīvasya pratiśrave ||
children.translated_text: he has become free of debt with respect to his promise to <s>Sugrīva</s>.

children.text: sakāmo bhava sugrīva rumāṃ tvaṃ pratipatsyase
children.translated_text: Have your desire fulfilled, <s>Sugrīva</s>; you will recover <s>Rumā</s>.

children.text: bhuṅkṣva rājyam anudvignaḥ śasto bhrātā ripus tava ||
children.translated_text: Enjoy the kingdom without anxiety; your brother, your enemy, has been slain.

children.text: kiṃ mām evaṃ vilapatīṃ premṇā tvaṃ nābhibhāṣase
children.translated_text: Why do you not speak lovingly to me as I lament in this way?

children.text: imāḥ paśya varā bahvīr bhāryās te vānareśvara ||
children.translated_text: Look at these many noble wives of yours, lord of monkeys.

children.text: tasyā vilapitaṃ śrutvā vānaryaḥ sarvataś ca tāḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing her lament, all those monkey-women on every side
took hold of poor <s>Aṅgada</s> and cried out, afflicted with grief.

children.text: kim aṅgadaṃ sāṅgada vīrabāho vihāya yāsy adya cirapravāsam
children.translated_text: O strong-armed hero with armlets, will you go today on a long journey, leaving <s>Aṅgada</s> behind?

children.text: na yuktam evaṃ guṇasaṃnikṛṣṭaṃ vihāya putraṃ priyaputra gantum ||
children.translated_text: It is not right to go, abandoning a son so close to you in virtues, O lover of your son.

children.text: kim apriyaṃ te priyacāruveṣa kṛtaṃ mayā nātha sutena vā te
children.translated_text: What displeasing thing, O lord of lovely and dear form, was done to you by me or by your son,

children.text: sahāyinīm adya vihāya vīra yamakṣayaṃ gacchasi durvinītam ||
children.translated_text: that, leaving your helper today, hero, you go to the hard road of <s>Yama</s>'s abode?

children.text: yady apriyaṃ kiṃcid asaṃpradhārya kṛtaṃ mayā syāt tava dīrghabāho
children.translated_text: If any displeasing thing was done by me without reflection, O long-armed one,

children.text: kṣamasva me taddharivaṃśanātha vrajāmi mūrdhnā tava vīra pādau ||
children.translated_text: forgive me that, lord of the monkey race; hero, I go with my head to your feet.

children.text: tathā tu tārā karuṇaṃ rudantī bhartuḥ samīpe saha vānarībhiḥ
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Tārā</s>, crying piteously near her husband together with the monkey-women,

children.text: vyavasyata prāyam anindyavarṇā upopaveṣṭuṃ bhuvi yatra vālī ||
children.translated_text: the blameless-hued woman resolved to sit down on the ground in a fast to death where <s>Vālī</s> lay.

children.text: tato nipatitāṃ tārāṃ cyutāṃ tārām ivāmbarāt
children.translated_text: Then <s>Hanūmān</s> slowly consoled <s>Tārā</s>, fallen like a star dropped from the sky,
he, the leader of the monkey troops.
"A creature receives what is produced by virtues and faults, caused by the fruit of its own acts;

children.text: avyagras tad avāpnoti sarvaṃ pretya śubhāśubham ||
children.translated_text: unagitated, after death it obtains all of that, auspicious and inauspicious.

children.text: śocyā śocasi kaṃ śocyaṃ dīnaṃ dīnānukampase
children.translated_text: You, worthy of pity, are grieving; for whom, worthy of grief, do you grieve? Pitiful one, you pity the pitiful.
And who is to be mourned by whom in this body, which is like a bubble?
But this young prince <s>Aṅgada</s> must be looked after by you, whose son is alive.

children.text: āyatyā ca vidheyāni samarthāny asya cintaya ||
children.translated_text: With regard to the future, think of measures that will be effective for him.

children.text: jānāsy aniyatām evaṃ bhūtānām āgatiṃ gatim
children.translated_text: You know that the coming and going of beings is uncertain in this way.

children.text: tasmāc chubhaṃ hi kartavyaṃ paṇḍite naihalaukikam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore what is auspicious should be done by a wise person, not merely what belongs to this world.
He in whom thousands of monkeys, tens of thousands and hundreds of millions,
performed their assigned shares, this one has come to his destined end.
Since he saw the matter according to justice and was devoted to conciliation, gifts, and forgiveness,

children.text: gato dharmajitāṃ bhūmiṃ nainaṃ śocitum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: he has gone to the realm won by those who conquer through <s>dharma</s> (righteousness); you should not grieve for him.

children.text: sarve ca hariśārdūlāḥ putraś cāyaṃ tavāṅgadaḥ
children.translated_text: All the tigers among monkeys, and this son of yours, <s>Aṅgada</s>,
and the kingdom of the lords of monkeys and bears, have you as their protector, blameless one.

children.text: tāv imau śokasaṃtaptau śanaiḥ preraya bhāmini
children.translated_text: Gently guide these two, scorched by grief, lovely woman.
Under your care, this <s>Aṅgada</s> should rule the earth."

children.text: saṃtatiś ca yathādṛṣṭā kṛtyaṃ yac cāpi sāmpratam
children.translated_text: And the lineage, as it has been seen, and whatever duty is now at hand,

children.text: rājñas tat kriyatāṃ sarvam eṣa kālasya niścayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: let all that be done for the king; this is the decision required by the time.
But the monkey king should be given his funeral rites, and <s>Aṅgada</s> should be consecrated.
Seeing your son seated on the throne, you will attain peace.
Hearing his words, she, afflicted by the calamity of her husband,
<s>Tārā</s> gave this answer to <s>Hanūmant</s>, who was standing there:
A hundred sons equal to <s>Aṅgada</s> on the one hand,
and on the other, even though this hero has been slain, the embrace of his limbs is better.

children.text: na cāhaṃ harirājasya prabhavāmy aṅgadasya vā
children.translated_text: I have no authority over the monkey king, nor over <s>Aṅgada</s>.
His paternal uncle <s>Sugrīva</s> is next in all matters.

children.text: na hy eṣā buddhir āstheyā hanūmann aṅgadaṃ prati
children.translated_text: For this thought should not be entertained with regard to <s>Aṅgada</s>, O <s>Hanūmant</s>.

children.text: pitā hi bandhuḥ putrasya na mātā harisattama ||
children.translated_text: For the father is the son's kinsman, not the mother, best of monkeys.

children.text: na hi mama harirājasaṃśrayāt kṣamataram asti paratra ceha vā
children.translated_text: For me there is nothing more fitting, in this world or the next, than dependence upon the monkey king:

children.text: abhimukhahatavīrasevitaṃ śayanam idaṃ mama sevituṃ kṣamam ||
children.translated_text: it is fitting for me to occupy this bed attended by a hero slain face to face.

children.text: vīkṣamāṇas tu mandāsuḥ sarvato mandam ucchvasan
children.translated_text: But, with his life-breath faint, looking around and breathing weakly on every side,

children.text: ādāv eva tu sugrīvaṃ dadarśa tv ātmajāgrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: he first saw <s>Sugrīva</s>, with his son awake beside him.
<s>Vāli</s> addressed <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the leaping monkeys, who had gained victory,

children.text: ābhāṣya vyaktayā vācā sasneham idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: and spoke these words to him clearly and with affection:

children.text: sugrīva doṣeṇa na māṃ gantum arhasi kilbiṣāt
children.translated_text: O <s>Sugrīva</s>, you should not regard me as guilty because of a fault,
me who was being dragged along by destiny, forcibly, through delusion of understanding.

children.text: yugapadvihitaṃ tāta na manye sukham āvayoḥ
children.translated_text: Dear one, I do not think happiness was ordained for both of us at the same time.

children.text: sauhārdaṃ bhrātṛyuktaṃ hi tad idaṃ jātam anyathā ||
children.translated_text: For brotherly friendship joined with fraternity has turned otherwise in this case.

children.text: pratipadya tvam adyaiva rājyam eṣāṃ vanaukasām
children.translated_text: Accept today itself the kingdom of these forest-dwellers,

children.text: mām apy adyaiva gacchantaṃ viddhi vaivasvatakṣayam ||
children.translated_text: and know that I too am going today to the abode of <s>Vaivasvata</s>.

children.text: jīvitaṃ ca hi rājyaṃ ca śriyaṃ ca vipulām imām
children.translated_text: Life, kingdom, and this great abundant prosperity,

children.text: prajahāmy eṣa vai tūrṇaṃ mahac cāgarhitaṃ yaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I now swiftly abandon, and also a great and blameless fame.

children.text: asyāṃ tv aham avasthāyāṃ vīra vakṣyāmi yad vacaḥ
children.translated_text: In this condition, hero, I shall say what must be said.

children.text: yady apy asukaraṃ rājan kartum eva tad arhasi ||
children.translated_text: Although it may be difficult to do, O king, you ought indeed to do it.
Look at this boy <s>Aṅgada</s>, worthy of happiness, raised in happiness, still young but not foolish,
his face filled with tears, fallen upon the ground.

children.text: mama prāṇaiḥ priyataraṃ putraṃ putram ivaurasam
children.translated_text: This son, dearer to me than my life, as though he were your own born son,
bereft of me but not bereft of worth, protect him in every way.

children.text: tvam apy asya hi dātā ca paritrātā ca sarvataḥ
children.translated_text: You too are his giver and his protector in every respect,
and the giver of fearlessness in dangers, just as I was, lord of the leaping monkeys.
This glorious son of <s>Tārā</s>, equal to you in valor,

children.text: rakṣasāṃ tu vadhe teṣām agratas te bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: will go before you in the slaughter of those <s>rākṣasas</s>.
Exerting himself in battle, strong in heroic deeds suited to him,
this vigorous young <s>Aṅgada</s>, <s>Tārā</s>'s son, will accomplish them.
And this daughter of <s>Suṣeṇa</s> is thoroughly accomplished in determining subtle matters of policy,
