and in every kind of ominous portent.

children.text: yad eṣā sādhv iti brūyāt kāryaṃ tan muktasaṃśayam
children.translated_text: Whatever she says is good, that should be done without doubt.

children.text: na hi tārāmataṃ kiṃcid anyathā parivartate ||
children.translated_text: For no opinion of <s>Tārā</s> ever turns out otherwise.

children.text: rāghavasya ca te kāryaṃ kartavyam aviśaṅkayā
children.translated_text: And <s>Rāghava</s>'s business must be carried out by you without hesitation.

children.text: syād adharmo hy akaraṇe tvāṃ ca hiṃsyād vimānitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For failure to do it would be <s>adharma</s>, and he, dishonored, would harm you.

children.text: imāṃ ca mālām ādhatsva divyāṃ sugrīva kāñcanīm
children.translated_text: Put on this divine golden garland, O <s>Sugrīva</s>.

children.text: udārā śrīḥ sthitā hy asyāṃ samprajahyān mṛte mayi ||
children.translated_text: For noble royal fortune rests in it; when I am dead, it would abandon me.

children.text: ity evam uktaḥ sugrīvo vālinā bhrātṛsauhṛdāt
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Vāli</s>, out of brotherly affection, <s>Sugrīva</s>

children.text: harṣaṃ tyaktvā punar dīno grahagrasta ivoḍurāṭ ||
children.translated_text: gave up joy and again became despondent, like the moon seized by a planet.

children.text: tad vālivacanāc chāntaḥ kurvan yuktam atandritaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, calmed by <s>Vāli</s>'s words, acting properly and without negligence,

children.text: jagrāha so 'bhyanujñāto mālāṃ tāṃ caiva kāñcanīm ||
children.translated_text: he, permitted by him, took that golden garland.

children.text: tāṃ mālāṃ kāñcanīṃ dattvā vālī dṛṣṭvātmajaṃ sthitam
children.translated_text: After giving that golden garland, <s>Vāli</s>, seeing his son standing there,

children.text: saṃsiddhaḥ pretya bhāvāya snehād aṅgadam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: ready for the state after death, spoke to <s>Aṅgada</s> out of affection:
From now on, attend to place and time, enduring what is pleasant and unpleasant.
Bearing happiness and suffering at the proper time, be subject to <s>Sugrīva</s>.

children.text: yathā hi tvaṃ mahābāho lālitaḥ satataṃ mayā
children.translated_text: For, mighty-armed one, although you were always cherished by me,

children.text: na tathā vartamānaṃ tvāṃ sugrīvo bahu maṃsyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s> will not think highly of you if you behave in that same way.

children.text: māsyāmitrair gataṃ gaccher mā śatrubhir ariṃdama
children.translated_text: Do not follow the path taken by his enemies; do not side with his foes, subduer of enemies.
Self-controlled and intent on your lord's interest, be subject to <s>Sugrīva</s>.
You should not show excessive affection, and you should not be without affection.

children.text: ubhayaṃ hi mahādoṣaṃ tasmād antaradṛg bhava ||
children.translated_text: For both are great faults; therefore be one who sees the middle course.
Having spoken thus, his eyes rolled open, and he was grievously oppressed by the arrow.
With his dreadful teeth exposed, he became one whose life had departed.

children.text: hate tu vīre plavagādhipe tadā plavaṃgamās tatra na śarma lebhire
children.translated_text: When the hero, the lord of the leaping monkeys, had been slain, the monkeys there found no comfort,

children.text: vanecarāḥ siṃhayute mahāvane yathā hi gāvo nihate gavāṃ patau ||
children.translated_text: just as cows in a great forest filled with lions find none when the lord of the herd has been killed.

children.text: tatas tu tārā vyasanārṇavaplutā mṛtasya bhartur vadanaṃ samīkṣya sā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Tārā</s>, plunged in the ocean of calamity, looked upon the face of her dead husband,

children.text: jagāma bhūmiṃ parirabhya vālinaṃ mahādrumaṃ chinnam ivāśritā latā ||
children.translated_text: and fell to the ground, embracing <s>Vāli</s>, like a vine clinging to a great tree that has been cut down.
Then, smelling the face of the monkey king again and again,

children.text: patiṃ lokāc cyutaṃ tārā mṛtaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tārā</s> spoke to her husband, fallen from the world and dead:

children.text: śeṣe tvaṃ viṣame duḥkham akṛtvā vacanaṃ mama
children.translated_text: You lie painfully on uneven ground, hero, without having done what I said,
on this earth's surface, piled with stones, exceedingly painful.

children.text: mattaḥ priyatarā nūnaṃ vānarendra mahī tava
children.translated_text: Surely, lord of monkeys, the earth is dearer to you than I am,

children.text: śeṣe hi tāṃ pariṣvajya māṃ ca na pratibhāṣase ||
children.translated_text: for you lie embracing her and do not answer me.
Only <s>Sugrīva</s> is truly bold, O hero, lover of reckless deeds...
The foremost bears and monkeys attend upon you as a mighty one.

children.text: eṣāṃ vilapitaṃ kṛcchram aṅgadasya ca śocataḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing their painful lamentation, and <s>Aṅgada</s> as he grieves,

children.text: mama cemāṃ giraṃ śrutvā kiṃ tvaṃ na pratibudhyase ||
children.translated_text: and hearing this speech of mine too, why do you not wake up?

children.text: idaṃ tac chūraśayanaṃ yatra śeṣe hato yudhi
children.translated_text: This is that bed of heroes on which you lie, slain in battle,

children.text: śāyitā nihatā yatra tvayaiva ripavaḥ purā ||
children.translated_text: where in former days enemies struck down by you yourself were made to lie.
O you of pure nature and noble birth, lover of battle, my beloved,

children.text: mām anāthāṃ vihāyaikāṃ gatas tvam asi mānada ||
children.translated_text: leaving me helpless and alone, you have gone, O giver of honor.

children.text: śūrāya na pradātavyā kanyā khalu vipaścitā
children.translated_text: Surely a wise man should not give a maiden to a hero.

children.text: śūrabhāryāṃ hatāṃ paśya sadyo māṃ vidhavāṃ kṛtām ||
children.translated_text: Look: a hero's wife is slain; in an instant you have made me a widow.

children.text: avabhagnaś ca me māno bhagnā me śāśvatī gatiḥ
children.translated_text: My honor has been broken, and my lasting refuge has been shattered.
I have sunk in a deep, vast ocean of grief.

children.text: aśmasāramayaṃ nūnam idaṃ me hṛdayaṃ dṛḍham
children.translated_text: Surely this firm heart of mine is made of the essence of stone,

children.text: bhartāraṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā yan nādya śatadhā gatam ||
children.translated_text: since, after seeing my husband slain, it has not today split into a hundred pieces.

children.text: suhṛc caiva hi bhartā ca prakṛtyā ca mama priyaḥ
children.translated_text: For he was my friend, my husband, and by nature dear to me,

children.text: āhave ca parākrāntaḥ śūraḥ pañcatvam āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: valiant in battle, a hero who has gone to the state of the five elements.

children.text: patihīnā tu yā nārī kāmaṃ bhavatu putriṇī
children.translated_text: A woman without a husband may indeed have sons,
and may be filled with wealth and grain, yet the wise call her a widow.
O hero, you lie in a circle of blood that has sprung from your own limbs,
on a bed such as this, amid a spreading redness like swarms of insects.
Your body is covered on every side with dust and blood,
and I cannot embrace you with my arms, O bull among leaping monkeys.
Today <s>Sugrīva</s> has accomplished his purpose in this exceedingly dreadful enmity,
for with one arrow released by <s>Rāma</s> his fear has been taken away.
As the arrow is lodged in your heart, when I look upon you,

children.text: vāryāmi tvāṃ nirīkṣantī tvayi pañcatvam āgate ||
children.translated_text: now that you have gone to death, I am kept from touching your body.

children.text: udbabarha śaraṃ nīlas tasya gātragataṃ tadā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Nīla</s> drew out the arrow lodged in his body,
like a blazing venomous serpent hidden in a mountain cave.

children.text: tasya niṣkṛṣyamāṇasya bāṇasya ca babhau dyutiḥ
children.translated_text: As that arrow was being pulled out, its radiance shone forth,
like a ray of the sun obstructed by a mountain peak at sunset.

children.text: petuḥ kṣatajadhārās tu vraṇebhyas tasya sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Streams of blood then fell from all his wounds,
like torrents from a mountain mixed with copper-red ocher.
Wiping her husband, covered with the dust of battle,
she sprinkled the hero, struck down by the weapon, with tears born from her eyes.
Seeing her husband slain, all his limbs drenched with blood,

children.text: uvāca tārā piṅgākṣaṃ putram aṅgadam aṅganā ||
children.translated_text: the lady <s>Tārā</s> spoke to her tawny-eyed son <s>Aṅgada</s>:

children.text: avasthāṃ paścimāṃ paśya pituḥ putra sudāruṇām
children.translated_text: Look, my son, upon this last and most dreadful state of your father.
Through the sinful deed, the end has come of the enmity that had been joined.
He whose body is like the rising young sun is going to the abode of <s>Yama</s>.
Salute the king, your father, my son, the giver of honor.

children.text: evam uktaḥ samutthāya jagrāha caraṇau pituḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Aṅgada</s> rose and grasped his father's feet
with his two round, full arms, saying, 'It is I, <s>Aṅgada</s>.'
As <s>Aṅgada</s> salutes you, why do you not, as before,
address him and say, 'Live long, my son'?
With my son as my support, I wait upon you, though you are lifeless,

children.text: siṃhena nihataṃ sadyo gauḥ savatseva govṛṣam ||
children.translated_text: like a cow with her calf beside a bull suddenly killed by a lion.
Having sacrificed with the battle-sacrifice whose water was many kinds of weapons,

children.text: asminn avabhṛthe snātaḥ kathaṃ patnyā mayā vinā ||
children.translated_text: how have you bathed in this final bath without me, your wife?

children.text: yā dattā devarājena tava tuṣṭena saṃyuge
children.translated_text: That garland made of refined gold, which the pleased king of gods gave you

children.text: śātakumbhamayīṃ mālāṃ tāṃ te paśyāmi neha kim ||
children.translated_text: in battle, why do I not see it here upon you?

children.text: rājaśrīr na jahāti tvāṃ gatāsum api mānada
children.translated_text: Royal fortune does not abandon you even though your life-breath is gone, O giver of honor,
just as radiance does not leave the king of mountains when the sun has set.

children.text: na me vacaḥ pathyam idaṃ tvayā kṛtaṃ na cāsmi śaktā hi nivāraṇe tava
children.translated_text: You did not act on this wholesome word of mine, and I was not able to restrain you.

children.text: hatā saputrāsmi hatena saṃyuge saha tvayā śrīr vijahāti mām iha ||
children.translated_text: Slain together with my son, I am slain by you slain in battle; together with you, fortune abandons me here.
Then, seeing <s>Vāli</s> lifeless, <s>Rāghava</s>,
the scorcher of foes, spoke humble words to <s>Sugrīva</s>:
One who is dead is not joined with any good by the torment of grief.

children.text: yad atrānantaraṃ kāryaṃ tat samādhātum arhatha ||
children.translated_text: Whatever task comes next here, that you ought to settle.
The custom of the world must be carried out; your shedding of tears is done.

children.text: na kālād uttaraṃ kiṃcit karma śakyam upāsitum ||
children.translated_text: Beyond the proper time, no action can be undertaken.
<s>niyati</s> (destiny) is the cause in the world; <s>niyati</s> is the means by which acts are accomplished.
<s>niyati</s> is the cause here in the appointments of all beings.

children.text: na kartā kasyacit kaścin niyoge cāpi neśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: No one is the maker of anything for anyone, nor is anyone lord over an appointment.

children.text: svabhāve vartate lokas tasya kālaḥ parāyaṇam ||
children.translated_text: The world proceeds according to its own nature, and time is its final resort.

children.text: na kālaḥ kālam atyeti na kālaḥ parihīyate
children.translated_text: Time does not overstep time, nor is time diminished.

children.text: svabhāvaṃ vā samāsādya na kaścid ativartate ||
children.translated_text: Having come upon its own nature, no one passes beyond it.

children.text: na kālasyāsti bandhutvaṃ na hetur na parākramaḥ
children.translated_text: Time has no kinship, no motive, and no valor.
Friendship, family connection, and relation are not its cause, nor is it subject to one's own will.

children.text: kiṃ tu kālaparīṇāmo draṣṭavyaḥ sādhu paśyatā
children.translated_text: Rather, the transformation of time must be regarded by one who sees rightly.

children.text: dharmaś cārthaś ca kāmaś ca kālakramasamāhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>dharma</s> (duty), wealth, and desire are all established in the sequence of time.

children.text: itaḥ svāṃ prakṛtiṃ vālī gataḥ prāptaḥ kriyāphalam
children.translated_text: From here <s>Vāli</s> has gone to his own nature and has obtained the fruit of his deeds,
made pure by the conjunctions of <s>dharma</s>, wealth, and desire, O lord of leaping monkeys.

children.text: svadharmasya ca saṃyogāj jitas tena mahātmanā
children.translated_text: Through union with his own <s>dharma</s>, heaven was won by that great-souled one,
and it was secured by him when he did not protect his own life-breaths.

children.text: eṣā vai niyatiḥ śreṣṭhā yāṃ gato hariyūthapaḥ
children.translated_text: This indeed is the highest destiny to which the leader of the monkey troops has gone.
Therefore enough of this lamentation; attend to what the time has now brought.
But at the end of <s>Rāma</s>'s speech, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, slayer of enemy heroes,
He spoke respectful words to <s>Sugrīva</s>, whose mind was overwhelmed:

children.text: kuru tvam asya sugrīva pretakāryam anantaram
children.translated_text: Perform, <s>Sugrīva</s>, his funeral rites immediately,
together with <s>Tārā</s> and <s>Aṅgada</s>, for the cremation of <s>Vāli</s>.

children.text: samājñāpaya kāṣṭhāni śuṣkāṇi ca bahūni ca
children.translated_text: Have many dry pieces of wood brought together,
and divine sandalwoods too, for the sake of <s>Vāli</s>'s funeral preparation.
And you should console this <s>Aṅgada</s>, whose mind is wretched.

children.text: mā bhūr bāliśabuddhis tvaṃ tvadadhīnam idaṃ puram ||
children.translated_text: Do not be childish in judgment; this city is dependent on you.

children.text: aṅgadas tv ānayen mālyaṃ vastrāṇi vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: But let <s>Aṅgada</s> bring garlands and various garments,

children.text: ghṛtaṃ tailam atho gandhān yac cātra samanantaram ||
children.translated_text: ghee, oil, perfumes, and whatever else is needed here at once.

children.text: tvaṃ tāra śibikāṃ śīghram ādāyāgaccha sambhramāt
children.translated_text: You, <s>Tāra</s>, quickly take up the bier and come in haste.

children.text: tvarā guṇavatī yuktā hy asmin kāle viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: For speed, when joined with good judgment, is especially fitting at this time.
Let the leaping monkeys suited to carrying the bier get ready,
capable and strong; they will carry <s>Vāli</s> out.
Having thus spoken to <s>Sugrīva</s>, the increaser of <s>Sumitrā</s>'s joy,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, slayer of enemy heroes, stood near his brother.
Hearing <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s words, <s>Tāra</s>, his mind agitated,
quickly entered the cave, intent on the bier.

children.text: ādāya śibikāṃ tāraḥ sa tu paryāpatat punaḥ
children.translated_text: Taking the bier, that <s>Tāra</s> returned again,
with it borne by heroic monkeys fit for carrying.

children.text: tato vālinam udyamya sugrīvaḥ śibikāṃ tadā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sugrīva</s>, lifting <s>Vāli</s> at that time,
placed him on the bier, crying aloud, together with <s>Aṅgada</s>.
Having placed lifeless <s>Vāli</s> on the bier,

children.text: alaṃkāraiś ca vividhair mālyair vastraiś ca bhūṣitam ||
children.translated_text: adorned with various ornaments, garlands, and garments,
King <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the leaping monkeys, then gave the order:
Let the obsequies of the noble one be performed fittingly.
Let the monkeys go in front, distributing many various jewels,
and let the bier follow immediately after them.

children.text: rājñām ṛddhiviśeṣā hi dṛśyante bhuvi yādṛśāḥ
children.translated_text: Such special displays of royal prosperity as are seen on earth for kings,
such funeral honors they quickly performed for <s>Vāli</s>.
Taking hold of <s>Aṅgada</s> quickly, <s>Tāra</s> and the others likewise,
all the monkeys, their kinsman slain, went forth crying aloud.
All the monkey-women, beginning with <s>Tārā</s>, whose troop-leader had been killed,
followed their husband, crying out in piteous voices.
By the sound of the weeping of those monkey-women in the forest interior,
all the forests and mountains seemed to cry out everywhere.
On a secluded sandy bank of the mountain river, surrounded by water,
many forest-roaming monkeys built a pyre.
Then, lowering the bier from their shoulders, those fit for carrying it
stood apart, taking a solitary place, all filled with grief.
Then <s>Tārā</s>, seeing her husband lying on the surface of the bier,
placed his head on her lap and lamented, greatly distressed:

children.text: janaṃ ca paśyasīmaṃ tvaṃ kasmāc chokābhipīḍitam
children.translated_text: Why do you not look at this people, oppressed by grief?

children.text: prahṛṣṭam iva te vaktraṃ gatāsor api mānada
children.translated_text: Even though your life-breaths are gone, giver of honor, your face seems joyful,
and is seen, like the color of the setting sun, as if you were alive.

children.text: eṣa tvāṃ rāmarūpeṇa kālaḥ karṣati vānara
children.translated_text: This Death, in the form of <s>Rāma</s>, is dragging you away, O monkey,

children.text: yena sma vidhavāḥ sarvāḥ kṛtā ekeṣuṇā raṇe ||
children.translated_text: by whom all of us have been made widows in battle with a single arrow.

children.text: imās tās tava rājendravānaryo vallabhāḥ sadā
children.translated_text: These are those beloved monkey-women of yours, O king of kings,

children.text: pādair vikṛṣṭam adhvānam āgatāḥ kiṃ na budhyase ||
children.translated_text: who have come along the road with their feet dragging; why do you not notice them?
Surely these wives with moon-like faces were dear to you.
Why now do you not look at <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the leaping monkeys?

children.text: ete hi sacivā rājaṃs tāraprabhṛtayas tava
children.translated_text: Here are your ministers, O king, beginning with <s>Tāra</s>,
and this populace of the city sits surrounding you, blameless one.
Dismiss these mighty ones as is fitting, subduer of foes;
then all of us, excited with wine, shall sport in the forests.
As <s>Tārā</s> was lamenting thus, overwhelmed by grief for her husband,
the monkey-women, themselves wasted by sorrow, then lifted her up.

children.text: sugrīveṇa tataḥ sārdham aṅgadaḥ pitaraṃ rudan
children.translated_text: Then <s>Aṅgada</s>, together with <s>Sugrīva</s>, weeping for his father,
placed him on the pyre, his senses struck down by grief.

children.text: tato 'gniṃ vidhivad dattvā so 'pasavyaṃ cakāra ha
children.translated_text: Then, after duly applying the fire, he made the leftward circuit
around his father, who had set out on the long road, his senses bewildered.

children.text: saṃskṛtya vālinaṃ te tu vidhipūrvaṃ plavaṃgamāḥ
children.translated_text: After those leaping monkeys had cremated <s>Vāli</s> according to rule,

children.text: ājagmur udakaṃ kartuṃ nadīṃ śītajalāṃ śubhām ||
children.translated_text: they went to a beautiful river with cool water to make the water offering.

children.text: tatas te sahitās tatra aṅgadaṃ sthāpya cāgrataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, assembled there and placing <s>Aṅgada</s> in front,
together with <s>Sugrīva</s> and <s>Tārā</s>, they poured water for <s>Vāli</s>.
With sorrowing <s>Sugrīva</s>, the mighty <s>Kākutstha</s> too became sorrowful,
and, sharing the same grief, had the funeral rites performed.
Then the great officers of the branch-roaming monkeys stood around
<s>Sugrīva</s>, scorched by grief, his garments wet.
Approaching mighty-armed <s>Rāma</s>, tireless in action,
all stood with joined palms, like seers before <s>Pitāmaha</s>.
Then, resembling a golden mountain, his face like the young sun,
<s>Hanumān</s>, son of the Wind, spoke these words with joined palms:
By your favor, <s>Sugrīva</s>, my lord, has obtained this great kingdom,

children.text: vānarāṇāṃ suduṣprāpaṃ prāpto rājyam idaṃ prabho ||
children.translated_text: inherited from father and grandfather and very hard for the monkeys to obtain.
Permitted by you, entering the auspicious city,
he, together with his friends, will arrange all affairs.

children.text: snāto 'yaṃ vividhair gandhair auṣadhaiś ca yathāvidhi
children.translated_text: This one has bathed according to rule with various perfumes and medicinal herbs

children.text: arcayiṣyati ratnaiś ca mālyaiś ca tvāṃ viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: He will honor you especially with jewels and garlands.
You ought to go from here to this delightful mountain cave.
Establish the bond with your lord, making the monkeys rejoice.
Thus addressed by <s>Hanumat</s>, <s>Rāghava</s>, the slayer of enemy heroes,
intelligent and skilled in speech, replied to <s>Hanūmant</s>:

children.text: caturdaśasamāḥ saumya grāmaṃ vā yadi vā puram
children.translated_text: For fourteen years, gentle one, whether it be a village or a city,
I shall not enter, <s>Hanuman</s>, as one who keeps his father's command.
Let the heroic <s>Sugrīva</s>, bull among monkeys, enter the prosperous and divine cave,
and quickly be consecrated to the kingdom according to rule.

children.text: evam uktvā hanūmantaṃ rāmaḥ sugrīvam abravīt
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to <s>Hanūmant</s>, <s>Rāma</s> said to <s>Sugrīva</s>:
Hero, consecrate this <s>Aṅgada</s> also as heir apparent.
This first rainy month, <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, the coming of the waters, has arrived;
the four months known as the rains have begun, gentle one.

children.text: nāyam udyogasamayaḥ praviśa tvaṃ purīṃ śubhām
children.translated_text: This is not the time for exertion. Enter the auspicious city,

children.text: asmin vatsyāmy ahaṃ saumya parvate sahalakṣmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: while I, gentle one, shall dwell on this mountain together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
This mountain cave is delightful, spacious, and provided with good air,
with abundant water, gentle one, and abundant lotuses and blue lotuses.
When <s>Kārttika</s> has fully arrived, be intent on the killing of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: eṣa naḥ samayaḥ saumya praviśa tvaṃ svam ālayam
children.translated_text: This is our agreement, gentle one. Enter your own dwelling,
be consecrated in the kingdom, and make your friends rejoice.
Thus permitted by <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Sugrīva</s>, bull among monkeys,
entered the delightful city <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, which had been ruled by <s>Vāli</s>.
When the lord of monkeys had entered, thousands of monkeys,
having bowed to him, joyfully surrounded him on every side.
Then all the subjects, seeing the lord of the monkey hosts,
bowed down with their heads and fell upon the earth, composed in mind.
Mighty <s>Sugrīva</s>, having greeted all the subjects and raised them up,
entered his brother's pleasant inner apartments, he of great strength.
But when <s>Sugrīva</s>, bull among monkeys, had entered and come out again,
his friends consecrated him, as the immortals consecrated thousand-eyed <s>Indra</s>.
They brought him a white parasol adorned with gold,
and two white yak-tail fans with golden handles, bestowers of fame.
Likewise they brought all jewels and all kinds of seeds and herbs,

children.text: sakṣīrāṇāṃ ca vṛkṣāṇāṃ prarohān kusumāni ca ||
children.translated_text: shoots of milk-bearing trees, and flowers.
They brought white garments, white unguent,

children.text: sugandhīni ca mālyāni sthalajāny ambujāni ca ||
children.translated_text: fragrant garlands, both those grown on land and those born in water.

children.text: candanāni ca divyāni gandhāṃś ca vividhān bahūn
children.translated_text: They brought divine sandalwoods and many various perfumes,
unbroken rice, gold, and <s>priyaṅgu</s>, honey, and ghee.

children.text: dadhi carma ca vaiyāghraṃ vārāhī cāpy upānahau
children.translated_text: They brought curds, a tiger skin, and also boar-hide sandals,
taking ointment, yellow pigment, and red arsenic;

children.text: ājagmus tatra muditā varāḥ kanyās tu ṣoḍaśa ||
children.translated_text: and sixteen excellent maidens came there rejoicing.
Then, at the proper time and according to rule, they honored that best of monkeys,

children.text: ratnair vastraiś ca bhakṣyaiś ca toṣayitvā dvijarṣabhān ||
children.translated_text: after satisfying the foremost twice-born men with jewels, garments, and foods.
Then, upon the fire kindled and strewn round with kuśa grass,
the men skilled in mantras made offerings with oblation purified by mantras.
Then on a golden seat, covered with excellent coverings,
on the delightful palace roof, adorned with variegated garlands,
they seated him facing east on an excellent throne with various mantras.
Having gathered water from rivers and streams and from sacred fords on every side,
and having brought it from all the oceans, the bulls among monkeys
placed the pure, auspicious waters in golden pitchers.

children.text: śubhair vṛṣabhaśṛṅgaiś ca kalaśaiś cāpi kāñcanaiḥ
children.translated_text: With auspicious bull horns and also with golden jars,
by the rite seen in the śāstra and prescribed by the great seers,
<s>Gaja</s>, <s>Gavākṣa</s>, <s>Gavaya</s>, <s>Śarabha</s>, and <s>Gandhamādana</s>,

children.text: maindaś ca dvividaś caiva hanūmāñ jāmbavān nalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Mainda</s>, <s>Dvivida</s>, <s>Hanūmān</s>, <s>Jāmbavān</s>, and <s>Nala</s>
consecrated <s>Sugrīva</s> with clear and fragrant water,
as the <s>Vasus</s> consecrated <s>Vāsava</s>, the thousand-eyed one.
When <s>Sugrīva</s> had been consecrated, all the foremost monkeys,
great-souled and delighted, cried out there by the thousands.

children.text: rāmasya tu vacaḥ kurvan sugrīvo haripuṃgavaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sugrīva</s>, foremost of monkeys, carrying out <s>Rāma</s>'s word,
embraced <s>Aṅgada</s> and consecrated him as heir apparent.
When <s>Aṅgada</s> too had been consecrated, the compassionate leaping monkeys,
great-souled, honored <s>Sugrīva</s>, saying, 'Well done, well done!'
Crowded with joyful and well-nourished people and adorned with banners and flags,
the delightful city <s>Kiṣkindhā</s> shone in the mountain cavern.

children.text: nivedya rāmāya tadā mahātmane mahābhiṣekaṃ kapivāhinīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: After reporting the great consecration to the great-souled <s>Rāma</s>, the lord of the monkey army,

children.text: rumāṃ ca bhāryāṃ pratilabhya vīryavān avāpa rājyaṃ tridaśādhipo yathā ||
children.translated_text: having recovered his wife <s>Rumā</s>, the mighty one obtained the kingdom like the lord of the thirty gods.

children.text: abhiṣikte tu sugrīve praviṣṭe vānare guhām
children.translated_text: When <s>Sugrīva</s> had been consecrated and had entered the monkeys' cave,

children.text: ājagāma saha bhrātrā rāmaḥ prasravaṇaṃ girim ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> came with his brother to <s>Prasravaṇa</s> mountain,
filled with the sounds of tigers and deer, surrounded by lions with terrible roars,
covered with many kinds of thickets and creepers, and crowded with many trees.
It was frequented by bears, monkeys, gopucchas, and wild cats,
a mountain like a mass of clouds, always possessing pure water.

children.text: tasya śailasya śikhare mahatīm āyatāṃ guhām
children.translated_text: On the summit of that mountain, <s>Rāma</s>, together with <s>Saumitri</s>, accepted
a great and broad cave as a dwelling place.
There the righteous <s>Rāghava</s> dwelt together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
On that mountain <s>Prasravaṇa</s>, with many visible caves and bowers,
though that mountain was very pleasant and rich in many things,

children.text: vasatas tasya rāmasya ratir alpāpi nābhavat
children.translated_text: there was not even a little delight for <s>Rāma</s> as he lived there,

children.text: hṛtāṃ hi bhāryāṃ smarataḥ prāṇebhyo 'pi garīyasīm ||
children.translated_text: for he remembered his stolen wife, dearer to him even than his life-breaths.
Seeing the moon risen at its rising, and especially the hare-marked moon,

children.text: āviveśa na taṃ nidrā niśāsu śayanaṃ gatam ||
children.translated_text: sleep did not enter him when he had gone to bed at night.
Because of the grief arising from that, his mind was assailed by tears;
to <s>Kākutstha</s>, who was grieving and always given over to sorrow,
his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, sharing equal pain, spoke these consoling words:

children.text: alaṃ vīra vyathāṃ gatvā na tvaṃ śocitum arhasi
children.translated_text: Enough, hero. Having fallen into distress, you ought not to grieve.

children.text: śocato hy avasīdanti sarvārthā viditaṃ hi te ||
children.translated_text: For all aims sink down for one who grieves; this is well known to you.
You are devoted to action in the world; you are devoted to the gods.

children.text: āstiko dharmaśīlaś ca vyavasāyī ca rāghava ||
children.translated_text: You are faithful, righteous in conduct, and resolute, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: na hy avyavasitaḥ śatruṃ rākṣasaṃ taṃ viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: For without resolve you are not able to kill that enemy, especially that <s>rākṣasa</s>,

children.text: samarthas tvaṃ raṇe hantuṃ vikramair jihmakāriṇam ||
children.translated_text: that crooked-working one, in battle by your deeds of valor.

children.text: samunmūlaya śokaṃ tvaṃ vyavasāyaṃ sthiraṃ kuru
children.translated_text: Tear out grief by the root; make your resolve firm.

children.text: tataḥ saparivāraṃ taṃ nirmūlaṃ kuru rākṣasam ||
children.translated_text: Then destroy that <s>rākṣasa</s>, together with his retinue, root and branch.
You are able, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, to overturn even the earth,

children.text: parivartayituṃ śaktaḥ kim aṅga puna rāvaṇam ||
children.translated_text: with its oceans, forests, and mountains; how much more, then, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>?

children.text: ahaṃ tu khalu te vīryaṃ prasuptaṃ pratibodhaye
children.translated_text: As for me, I am indeed awakening that valor of yours which lies asleep,
like fire covered with ashes, awakened in due season by blazing oblations.

children.text: lakṣmaṇasya tu tad vākyaṃ pratipūjya hitaṃ śubham
children.translated_text: Approving that good and beneficial speech of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: rāghavaḥ suhṛdaṃ snigdham idaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> spoke these words to his affectionate, loving friend:

children.text: vācyaṃ yad anuraktena snigdhena ca hitena ca
children.translated_text: What should be said by one who is attached, loving, and concerned for my good,
and who is joined with true valor, that has been said by you, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
This grief, which makes every undertaking sink, has been cast aside.
I now stir up my energy, unobstructed in heroic deeds.
I shall wait for the autumn season; this rainy season has arrived.

children.text: tataḥ sarāṣṭraṃ sagaṇaṃ rākṣasaṃ taṃ nihanmy aham ||
children.translated_text: Then I shall kill that <s>rākṣasa</s>, together with his kingdom and his hosts.

children.text: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā hṛṣṭo rāmasya lakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing those words of <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> rejoiced,
and <s>Saumitri</s>, delighter of his friends, again spoke these words:

children.text: etat te sadṛśaṃ vākyam uktaṃ śatrunibarhaṇa
children.translated_text: This speech you have spoken is worthy of you, destroyer of enemies.

children.text: idānīm asi kākutstha prakṛtiṃ svām upāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, you have returned to your own nature.

children.text: vijñāya hy ātmano vīryaṃ tathyaṃ bhavitum arhasi
children.translated_text: For, knowing your own strength, you ought to become true to yourself.

children.text: etat sadṛśam uktaṃ te śrutasyābhijanasya ca ||
children.translated_text: What you have said is worthy of your learning and your noble birth.
Therefore, tiger among men, while thinking on the destruction of your enemy,
let this rainy season that has come pass by, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: niyamya kopaṃ pratipālyatāṃ śarat kṣamasva māsāṃś caturo mayā saha
children.translated_text: Restrain your anger; wait for autumn. Be patient for four months together with me.
Dwell on this mountain, frequented by lions, increasing your strength and intent on killing your enemy.

children.text: sa tadā vālinaṃ hatvā sugrīvam abhiṣicya ca
children.translated_text: Then, after killing <s>Vāli</s> and consecrating <s>Sugrīva</s>,

children.text: vasan mālyavataḥ pṛṣṭhe rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, living on the summit of <s>Mālyavat</s>, spoke to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:

children.text: ayaṃ sa kālaḥ samprāptaḥ samayo 'dya jalāgamaḥ
children.translated_text: This is that time now arrived; today is the season of the coming of water.

children.text: saṃpaśya tvaṃ nabho meghaiḥ saṃvṛtaṃ girisaṃnibhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Look at the sky covered with clouds that resemble mountains.
Having borne its pregnancy for nine months by the rays of the sun,

children.text: pītvā rasaṃ samudrāṇāṃ dyauḥ prasūte rasāyanam ||
children.translated_text: and having drunk the sap of the oceans, heaven gives birth to life-giving water.
It would be possible to climb the sky by rows of cloud-stairs
and adorn the sun with garlands of <s>kuṭaja</s> and <s>arjuna</s> flowers.
With coppery clouds raised by the redness of twilight, but very pale at the edges,
the sky, wrapped in smooth cloud-cloths, seems like a bandaged wound.
With the slow breathing of the wind, tinted by the sandal of twilight,
and with pale-white clouds, the sky appears like one tormented by desire.
This earth, distressed by heat and flooded with fresh water,
releases tears like <s>Sītā</s>, scorched by grief.
Released from the bellies of the clouds, pleasant and cool as water-lilies,
the winds, fragrant with <s>ketakī</s>, could be drunk with cupped hands.
This mountain, with blooming <s>arjuna</s> trees and perfumed by <s>ketakī</s>,
is being consecrated by streams, like <s>Sugrīva</s> whose enemies are pacified.
Wearing black antelope-skins of cloud and sacred threads of streams,
the mountains, their caves filled by the wind, seem like Brahmin students reciting the Veda.

children.text: kaśābhir iva haimībhir vidyudbhir iva tāḍitam
children.translated_text: As if struck by golden whips, by flashes of lightning,
the sky, with the roar of thunder within it, seems to be in pain.
A lightning-flash, resting on a dark cloud and quivering, appears to me
like poor <s>Vaidehī</s> quivering on the lap of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: imās tā manmathavatāṃ hitāḥ pratihatā diśaḥ
children.translated_text: These quarters, favorable to those who are under love's power, have become blocked,
as if anointed with dense clouds, with the planets and moon lost from sight.
In some places, held back as though by tears, and eager for the coming of the rains,
look, O <s>Saumitri</s>, at the <s>kuṭaja</s> trees flowering on the mountain slopes,
standing there as kindlers of desire for me, who am overcome by grief.

children.text: rajaḥ praśāntaṃ sahimo 'dya vāyur nidāghadoṣaprasarāḥ praśāntāḥ
children.translated_text: The dust has settled; today the wind is cool with mist; the spreading faults of summer heat are quieted.

children.text: sthitā hi yātrā vasudhādhipānāṃ pravāsino yānti narāḥ svadeśān ||
children.translated_text: The marches of kings have stopped, and men living abroad go back to their own countries.
The <s>cakravāka</s> birds, longing to dwell at <s>Mānasa</s>, have now set out, joined with their mates;
on roads cut up by the water of constant rain, vehicles do not proceed.

children.text: kvacit prakāśaṃ kvacid aprakāśaṃ nabhaḥ prakīrṇāmbudharaṃ vibhāti
children.translated_text: In places bright and in places not bright, the sky appears, scattered with rain-bearing clouds.

children.text: kvacit kvacit parvatasaṃniruddhaṃ rūpaṃ yathā śāntamahārṇavasya ||
children.translated_text: Here and there, blocked in by mountains, its form is like that of a calm great ocean.
Fresh water, mixed with flowers of sarja and kadamba and made copper-red by mountain minerals,
the mountain rivers carry swiftly along, accompanied by the cries of peacocks.
The jambu fruit, full of juice and dark like bees, bursts open abundantly,

children.text: anekavarṇaṃ pavanāvadhūtaṃ bhūmau pataty āmraphalaṃ vipakvam ||
children.translated_text: while ripe mango fruit, many-colored and shaken by the wind, falls to the ground.
With lightning as their banners, with rows of cranes as their garlands, and resembling the peaks of great mountains,

children.text: garjanti meghāḥ samudīrṇanādā mattagajendrā iva saṃyugasthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the clouds roar like rutting lordly elephants standing in battle.
A delighted line of cranes, longing for the clouds and flying about, shines forth,
like a hanging garland of fine white lotuses, wind-tossed and arranged in the sky.

children.text: nidrā śanaiḥ keśavam abhyupaiti drutaṃ nadī sāgaram abhyupaiti
children.translated_text: Sleep slowly approaches <s>Keśava</s>; the river swiftly approaches the ocean;

children.text: hṛṣṭā balākā ghanam abhyupaiti kāntā sakāmā priyam abhyupaiti ||
children.translated_text: the delighted crane approaches the cloud, and the eager beloved approaches her lover.

children.text: jātā vanāntāḥ śikhisupranṛttā jātāḥ kadambāḥ sakadambaśākhāḥ
children.translated_text: The forest interiors have become places of splendid dancing peacocks; the kadamba trees have branches full of kadambas;

children.text: jātā vṛṣā goṣu samānakāmā jātā mahī sasyavanābhirāmā ||
children.translated_text: the bulls among the cows are filled with common desire, and the earth has become lovely with crops and woods.

children.text: vahanti varṣanti nadanti bhānti dhyāyanti nṛtyanti samāśvasanti
children.translated_text: They flow, they rain, they trumpet, they shine, they brood, they dance, they take heart:

children.text: nadyo ghanā mattagajā vanāntāḥ priyāvihīnāḥ śikhinaḥ plavaṃgāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the rivers, the clouds, the rutting elephants, the forest interiors, those parted from their beloveds, the peacocks, and the monkeys.
Exhilarated by smelling the fragrance of ketaka flowers, and gladdened among the forest waterfalls,

children.text: prapātaśabdākulitā gajendrāḥ sārdhaṃ mayūraiḥ samadā nadanti ||
children.translated_text: the lordly elephants, amid the tumult of falling waters, trumpet in rut together with the peacocks.
Beaten by the falling streams of rain and clinging to the branches of kadamba trees,

children.text: kṣaṇārjitaṃ puṣparasāvagāḍhaṃ śanair madaṃ ṣaṭcaraṇās tyajanti ||
children.translated_text: the six-footed bees slowly abandon their newly acquired intoxication, sunk in the nectar of flowers.
With fruits resembling heaps of powdered charcoal, rich and filled with excellent juice,

children.text: jambūdrumāṇāṃ pravibhānti śākhā nilīyamānā iva ṣaṭpadaughaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the branches of the jambu trees shine, as though being hidden by swarms of bees.
Adorned with lightning banners and filled with deep, swelling roars,

children.text: vibhānti rūpāṇi balāhakānāṃ raṇodyatānām iva vāraṇānām ||
children.translated_text: the forms of the clouds shine like elephants ready for battle.
A rutting lordly elephant, following the road and moving along the mountain forest, hears the roar of a cloud and sets out;
eager for combat and suspecting a rival elephant, he turns back toward it.

children.text: muktāsakāśaṃ salilaṃ patad vai sunirmalaṃ pattrapuṭeṣu lagnam
children.translated_text: Clear water, like pearls, falls and clings in cups made of leaves;

children.text: hṛṣṭā vivarṇacchadanā vihaṃgāḥ surendradattaṃ tṛṣitāḥ pibanti ||
children.translated_text: delighted, thirsty birds with variegated wings drink what has been given by <s>Surendra</s>.

children.text: nīleṣu nīlā navavāripūrṇā megheṣu meghāḥ pravibhānti saktāḥ
children.translated_text: Blue clouds, full of fresh water, shine as they cling among blue clouds,

children.text: davāgnidagdheṣu davāgnidagdhāḥ śaileṣu śailā iva baddhamūlāḥ ||
children.translated_text: like mountains with fixed roots among mountains burned by forest fire.

children.text: mattā gajendrā muditā gavendrā vaneṣu viśrāntatarā mṛgendrāḥ
children.translated_text: The lordly elephants are rutting, the chief bulls are delighted, and the lions are more deeply at rest in the forests;

children.text: ramyā nagendrā nibhṛtā nagendrāḥ prakrīḍito vāridharaiḥ surendraḥ ||
children.translated_text: the great mountains are lovely, the foremost serpents are withdrawn, and <s>Surendra</s> has sported with the rain clouds.
The campaigns of kings are over, and the army turns back;

children.text: vairāṇi caiva mārgāś ca salilena samīkṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: enmities and roads alike have been leveled by the water.
In the month of <s>Prauṣṭhapada</s>, O holy one, for brahmins wishing to recite,
this season for study, for the singers of the Sāman, has arrived.
Surely <s>Bharata</s>, lord of <s>Kosala</s>, with the places of ritual action now at rest and his stores gathered,
has entered upon the Āṣāḍhī observance.
Surely, as the <s>Sarayū</s> fills, its current increases,

children.text: māṃ samīkṣya samāyāntam ayodhyāyā iva svanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and its sound is like that of <s>Ayodhyā</s> coming to meet me as it sees me approach.

children.text: imāḥ sphītaguṇā varṣāḥ sugrīvaḥ sukham aśnute
children.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s> enjoys these rains, rich in good qualities, in happiness,

children.text: vijitāriḥ sadāraś ca rājye mahati ca sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: his enemy conquered, together with his wife, and established in a great kingdom.

children.text: ahaṃ tu hṛtadāraś ca rājyāc ca mahataś cyutaḥ
children.translated_text: But I, whose wife has been taken and who have fallen from a great kingdom,
am sinking down, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, like the soaked bank of a river.

children.text: śokaś ca mama vistīrṇo varṣāś ca bhṛśadurgamāḥ
children.translated_text: My grief is vast, the rains are extremely hard to cross,

children.text: rāvaṇaś ca mahāñ śatrur apāraṃ pratibhāti me ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, my great enemy, seems to me without a farther shore.

children.text: ayātrāṃ caiva dṛṣṭvemāṃ mārgāṃś ca bhṛśadurgamān
children.translated_text: Seeing this season unfit for marching, and the roads extremely difficult to travel,

children.text: praṇate caiva sugrīve na mayā kiṃcid īritam ||
children.translated_text: and seeing <s>Sugrīva</s> humbly submissive, I have said nothing.
Moreover, he has been much worn down and has met his wife again after a long time;
though my own task is very weighty, I do not wish to speak to the monkey.

children.text: svayam eva hi viśramya jñātvā kālam upāgatam
children.translated_text: For after he himself has rested and has recognized that the time has come,

children.text: upakāraṃ ca sugrīvo vetsyate nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s> will understand the favor he owes; there is no doubt about this.
Therefore I remain waiting for the proper time, O one of auspicious marks,
awaiting the clearing of <s>Sugrīva</s>'s mind and of the rivers.
For a hero is bound by a favor and by the return of that favor;
an ungrateful man, failing to repay it, wounds the minds of the noble.

children.text: athaivam uktaḥ praṇidhāya lakṣmaṇaḥ kṛtāñjalis tat pratipūjya bhāṣitam
children.translated_text: Then, when this had been said, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, taking it to heart, joined his palms and honored that speech;

children.text: uvāca rāmaṃ svabhirāmadarśanaṃ pradarśayan darśanam ātmanaḥ śubham ||
children.translated_text: he spoke to <s>Rāma</s>, whose sight was lovely, showing his own auspicious understanding.

children.text: yathoktam etat tava sarvam īpsitaṃ narendra kartā nacirāddharīśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Everything you desire, O king, is just as you have said; the lord of the monkeys will do it before long.

children.text: śaratpratīkṣaḥ kṣamatām imaṃ bhavāñ jalaprapātaṃ ripunigrahe dhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Waiting for autumn, let your honor endure this downpour, resolute in the subduing of the foe.
Having observed the stainless sky,
with its lightning and clouds gone, filled with the cries of sārasas, and anointed with lovely moonlight,
and <s>Sugrīva</s>, his aim accomplished, but slight in his gathering of dharma and artha,
his mind wholly fixed on the path of the ignoble,
his business completed, his object attained, and always absorbed in women,
having attained all the desires he had wished for, every one of them,

children.text: svāṃ ca patnīm abhipretāṃ tārāṃ cāpi samīpsitām
children.translated_text: and his own desired wife, and <s>Tārā</s> too, whom he had longed for,
sporting day and night, fulfilled and free from feverish distress,
playing like the lord of the gods in <s>Nandana</s> with hosts of Apsarases,
having entrusted affairs to his ministers, and not looking after the ministers,
letting the commands of the kingdom fall into neglect, remaining devoted to pleasure,
<s>Hanumān</s>, whose purpose was settled, who knew the truth of affairs and the distinctions of proper time and duty,
having conciliated him with sweet, reasoned, and pleasing words,
the son of <s>Māruta</s>, skilled in speech, addressed the lord of monkeys, who knew the essence of speech.

children.text: hitaṃ tathyaṃ ca pathyaṃ ca sāmadharmārthanītimat
children.translated_text: The speech was beneficial, true, salutary, and furnished with conciliation, <s>dharma</s> (duty), <s>artha</s> (practical advantage), and policy;
it was joined with affection and love, and formed from a resolve meant to create trust.
Approaching the lord of monkeys, <s>Hanumān</s> spoke these words:

children.text: rājyaṃ prāptaṃ yaśaś caiva kaulī śrīr abhivardhitā
children.translated_text: The kingdom has been obtained, and fame too; your family prosperity has increased.

children.text: mitrāṇāṃ saṃgrahaḥ śeṣas tad bhavān kartum arhati ||
children.translated_text: What remains is the securing of allies; that your honor ought to do.

children.text: yo hi mitreṣu kālajñaḥ satataṃ sādhu vartate
children.translated_text: For the man who knows the right time in matters concerning friends and always acts properly toward them,

children.text: tasya rājyaṃ ca kīrtiś ca pratāpaś cābhivardhate ||
children.translated_text: his kingdom, his fame, and his might all increase.

children.text: yasya kośaś ca daṇḍaś ca mitrāṇy ātmā ca bhūmipa
children.translated_text: He whose treasury, force, allies, and own person, O king,

children.text: samavetāni sarvāṇi sa rājyaṃ mahad aśnute ||
children.translated_text: are all gathered together, enjoys a great kingdom.

children.text: tad bhavān vṛttasampannaḥ sthitaḥ pathi niratyaye
children.translated_text: Therefore, your honor, endowed with good conduct and established on the faultless path,
ought to carry out properly the purpose undertaken for a friend.
But he who lets the proper time pass in matters concerning a friend,

children.text: sa kṛtvā mahato 'py arthān na mitrārthena yujyate ||
children.translated_text: even after accomplishing great aims, is not united with the friend's purpose.
Let this search for <s>Vaidehī</s>, for <s>Rāghava</s>'s sake, be undertaken.

children.text: tad idaṃ vīra kāryaṃ te kālātītam ariṃdama ||
children.translated_text: This task of yours, O hero, has passed its proper time, O subduer of enemies.

children.text: na ca kālam atītaṃ te nivedayati kālavit
children.translated_text: And the knower of time does not inform you that the time has passed,

children.text: tvaramāṇo 'pi san prājñas tava rājan vaśānugaḥ ||
children.translated_text: though he is eager, wise, and obedient to your will, O king.

children.text: kulasya ketuḥ sphītasya dīrghabandhuś ca rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> is the banner of an eminent family and a long-standing kinsman and ally;
his power is immeasurable, and he himself is unequalled in virtues.

children.text: tasya tvaṃ kuru vai kāryaṃ pūrvaṃ tena kṛtaṃ tava
children.translated_text: Do his task, for him who formerly did yours.
O lord of monkeys, you ought to command the best of the monkeys.

children.text: na hi tāvad bhavet kālo vyatītaś codanād ṛte
children.translated_text: For the time would not yet be past so long as there has been no urging;
but once a task has been urged, a passing beyond the proper time would occur.

children.text: akartur api kāryasya bhavān kartā harīśvara
children.translated_text: Even for a task without another doer, you are the doer, O lord of monkeys;

children.text: kiṃ punaḥ pratikartus te rājyena ca dhanena ca ||
children.translated_text: how much more for one to whom repayment is owed by you, with kingdom and wealth.
You are powerful and valiant, O lord of the troops of monkeys and bears.

children.text: kartuṃ dāśaratheḥ prītim ājñāyāṃ kiṃ nu sajjase ||
children.translated_text: Why do you hesitate over carrying out what will please the son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, once it is commanded?
Indeed the son of <s>Daśaratha</s> is able, if he wishes, to bring gods, Asuras, and great serpents

children.text: vaśe dāśarathiḥ kartuṃ tvatpratijñāṃ tu kāṅkṣate ||
children.translated_text: under his control with arrows; but he is waiting for your promise.
A favor was done for you by him with no hesitation even at giving up his life.

children.text: tasya mārgāma vaidehīṃ pṛthivyām api cāmbare ||
children.translated_text: Let us search for his <s>Vaidehī</s> on the earth and also in the sky.

children.text: na devā na ca gandharvā nāsurā na marudgaṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Neither gods nor Gandharvas, nor Asuras nor the hosts of Maruts,

children.text: na ca yakṣā bhayaṃ tasya kuryuḥ kim uta rākṣasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor Yakṣas could cause fear to him; how much less could Rākṣasas?

children.text: tad evaṃ śaktiyuktasya pūrvaṃ priyakṛtas tathā
children.translated_text: Therefore, since <s>Rāma</s> is endowed with such power and has formerly done you a kindness,
O tawny lord, you ought to do what is dear to him with your whole self.

children.text: nādhastād avanau nāpsu gatir nopari cāmbare
children.translated_text: Neither below on the earth, nor in the waters, nor above in the sky
is the movement of any one of us checked, O lord of monkeys, by your command.

children.text: tad ājñāpaya kaḥ kiṃ te kṛte vasatu kutracit
children.translated_text: Therefore command who, appointed to what task by you, should stay anywhere.

children.text: harayo hy apradhṛṣyās te santi koṭyagrato 'nagha ||
children.translated_text: For your monkeys are unassailable, O sinless one, and stand in foremost crores.
Hearing that speech of his, properly presented at the right time,
<s>Sugrīva</s>, endowed with courage, formed an excellent resolve.
He assigned <s>Nīla</s>, always energetic in action, to the task he desired,
the gathering of all the armies in every direction.

children.text: yathā senā samagrā me yūthapālāś ca sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: As my army and all the troop-leaders, everywhere,
may assemble without obstruction, so arrange the foremost divisions of the army.

children.text: ye tv antapālāḥ plavagāḥ śīghragā vyavasāyinaḥ
children.translated_text: Let those frontier-guarding monkeys, swift and energetic,

children.text: samānayantu te sainyaṃ tvaritāḥ śāsanān mama
children.translated_text: quickly bring together the army according to my commands.
And immediately afterward, your honor yourself should inspect the army.

children.text: tripañcarātrād ūrdhvaṃ yaḥ prāpnuyān neha vānaraḥ
children.translated_text: Any monkey who does not arrive here after fifteen nights

children.text: tasya prāṇāntiko daṇḍo nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: shall have death as his punishment; no deliberation is to be made in this matter.

children.text: harīṃś ca vṛddhān upayātu sāṅgado bhavān mamājñām adhikṛtya niścitām
children.translated_text: And you, together with <s>Aṅgada</s>, should go to the elder monkeys, having taken charge of my fixed command.

children.text: iti vyavasthāṃ haripuṃgaveśvaro vidhāya veśma praviveśa vīryavān ||
children.translated_text: Having laid down this arrangement, the valiant lord of the foremost monkeys entered his dwelling.

children.text: guhāṃ praviṣṭe sugrīve vimukte gagane ghanaiḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Sugrīva</s> had entered the cave and the sky had been freed from clouds,
<s>Rāma</s>, who had spent the rainy season there, was oppressed by desire and grief.
Seeing the pale sky and the spotless disk of the moon,
and seeing the autumn night anointed with moonlight,

children.text: kāmavṛttaṃ ca sugrīvaṃ naṣṭāṃ ca janakātmajām
children.translated_text: and knowing <s>Sugrīva</s> to be devoted to pleasure, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s> to be lost,

children.text: buddhvā kālam atītaṃ ca mumoha paramāturaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the proper time to have passed, he fainted, utterly distressed.

children.text: sa tu saṃjñām upāgamya muhūrtān matimān punaḥ
children.translated_text: But after a moment, the wise one regained consciousness again,
and <s>Rāghava</s> thought of <s>Vaidehī</s>, though she already dwelt in his mind.
Seated on the summit of the mountain, adorned with golden minerals,

children.text: śāradaṃ gaganaṃ dṛṣṭvā jagāma manasā priyām ||
children.translated_text: and seeing the autumn sky, he went in his mind to his beloved.
And seeing the clear sky, with lightning and clouds gone,
filled with the cries of sārasas, he lamented in an afflicted voice.
With the sounds of the cries of sārasas, she whose voice sounded like the cry of a sārasa,

children.text: yāśrame ramate bālā sādya me ramate katham ||
children.translated_text: that young woman who delighted in the hermitage: how is she delighting today without me?

children.text: puṣpitāṃś cāsanān dṛṣṭvā kāñcanān iva nirmalān
children.translated_text: Seeing the seats covered with flowers, spotless as if made of gold,

children.text: kathaṃ sā ramate bālā paśyantī mām apaśyatī ||
children.translated_text: how can that young woman take pleasure in them, seeing me and yet not seeing me?
She who formerly, speaking sweetly with a voice like that of royal swans,

children.text: budhyate cārusarvāṅgī sādya me budhyate katham ||
children.translated_text: would wake me, she of lovely limbs, how will she awaken me today?
Hearing the cries of cakravāka birds moving with their mates,
how will this lotus-wide-eyed woman endure?

children.text: sarāṃsi sarito vāpīḥ kānanāni vanāni ca
children.translated_text: Ponds, rivers, reservoirs, groves, and forests,

children.text: tāṃ vinā mṛgaśāvākṣīṃ caran nādya sukhaṃ labhe ||
children.translated_text: wandering among them without that doe-eyed woman, I find no happiness today.

children.text: api tāṃ madviyogāc ca saukumāryāc ca bhāminīm
children.translated_text: May passion, because of separation from me and because of her delicacy,
not afflict that lovely woman too severely, with the qualities of autumn all around.
Thus and in like manner the best of men, the king's son, lamented,
like a sāraṅga bird longing for water from the lord of the gods.
Then, roaming on the lovely mountain slopes in search of fruit,
the fortunate <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, having turned back, saw his elder brother.

children.text: taṃ cintayā duḥsahayā parītaṃ visaṃjñam ekaṃ vijane manasvī
children.translated_text: Seeing him alone in the lonely place, overcome by unbearable anxiety and almost senseless,

children.text: bhrātur viṣādāt paritāpadīnaḥ samīkṣya saumitrir uvāca rāmam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Saumitri</s>, pained and dejected by his brother's grief, addressed <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: kim ārya kāmasya vaśaṃgatena kim ātmapauruṣyaparābhavena
children.translated_text: Why, noble one, should composure always be restrained by one who has fallen under the power of desire, by the defeat of one's own manly strength?

children.text: ayaṃ sadā saṃhriyate samādhiḥ kim atra yogena nivartitena ||
children.translated_text: What use is discipline here if it has been turned away from its purpose?

children.text: kriyābhiyogaṃ manasaḥ prasādaṃ samādhiyogānugataṃ ca kālam
children.translated_text: Make purposeful action, clarity of mind, the proper time joined with collected concentration,

children.text: sahāyasāmarthyam adīnasattva svakarmahetuṃ ca kuruṣva hetum ||
children.translated_text: the strength of allies, your undepressed spirit, and your own deed the grounds of success.

children.text: na jānakī mānavavaṃśanātha tvayā sanāthā sulabhā pareṇa
children.translated_text: O lord of the human race, <s>Jānakī</s>, protected by you, is not easy for another man to obtain;

children.text: na cāgnicūḍāṃ jvalitām upetya na dahyate vīravarārha kaścit ||
children.translated_text: nor does anyone approach a blazing flame crested with fire and escape being burned, O one worthy of the best heroes.

children.text: salakṣmaṇaṃ lakṣmaṇam apradhṛṣyaṃ svabhāvajaṃ vākyam uvāca rāmaḥ
children.translated_text: To <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, endowed with auspicious marks and unassailable, <s>Rāma</s> spoke words born of his own nature,

children.text: hitaṃ ca pathyaṃ ca nayaprasaktaṃ sasāma dharmārthasamāhitaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: beneficial, wholesome, connected with policy, conciliatory, and intent on <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>.

children.text: niḥsaṃśayaṃ kāryam avekṣitavyaṃ kriyāviśeṣo hy anuvartitavyaḥ
children.translated_text: Without doubt the task must be considered, and a specific course of action must be followed;

children.text: nanu pravṛttasya durāsadasya kumārakāryasya phalaṃ na cintyam ||
children.translated_text: surely, once a difficult princely undertaking has begun, its fruit should not be ignored.
Then, thinking of <s>Maithilī</s>, whose eyes were like lotus petals,
<s>Rāma</s> spoke to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> with his mouth dried up.
The thousand-eyed one, having satisfied the earth with water,
and having brought the crops to completion, stands with his work done.
With their deep, smooth rumbling, preceded by mountains and trees,
the clouds, O king's son, have released their water and are weary.
Dark like blue lotus petals, having darkened the ten directions,
the rain-clouds are now calm in force, like elephants whose rut has passed.
Filled with water, of great force, fragrant with kuṭaja and arjuna blossoms,
the rain winds, O gentle one, having ranged forth, have ceased from their onset.

children.text: ghanānāṃ vāraṇānāṃ ca mayūrāṇāṃ ca lakṣmaṇa
children.translated_text: The sound of clouds, elephants, and peacocks, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
and of waterfalls, has suddenly grown quiet, O sinless one.
Washed by great clouds, the mountains with their variegated peaks are stainless;
they shine as though anointed by the moon's rays.
The autumn rivers slowly reveal their sandbanks,
like women, shy from a new union, revealing their hips.
With clear waters, O gentle one, resounding with kurarī birds,
and crowded with flocks of cakravākas, the lakes shine beautifully.
For kings whose hostilities are bound against one another and who wish to conquer, O king's son,
the season for enterprise has arrived, O gentle one.

children.text: iyaṃ sā prathamā yātrā pārthivānāṃ nṛpātmaja
children.translated_text: This is the first march of kings, O king's son,

children.text: na ca paśyāmi sugrīvam udyogaṃ vā tathāvidham ||
children.translated_text: yet I do not see <s>Sugrīva</s>, nor any enterprise of that sort.
The four months of the rains, like a hundred years, have passed
for me, scorched by grief, O gentle one, and not seeing <s>Sītā</s>.
Though I am bereft of my beloved, afflicted by sorrow, deprived of my kingdom, and exiled,

children.text: kṛpāṃ na kurute rājā sugrīvo mayi lakṣmaṇa ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Sugrīva</s> shows no compassion for me, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
'This man is helpless, deprived of his kingdom, violated by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: dīno dūragṛhaḥ kāmī māṃ caiva śaraṇaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: wretched, far from home, longing, and has come to me for refuge'—

children.text: ity etaiḥ kāraṇaiḥ saumya sugrīvasya durātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: for these reasons, O gentle one, by wicked-hearted <s>Sugrīva</s>,
by the king of the monkeys, I have been treated with contempt, O scorcher of foes.
Having counted the time for the search for <s>Sītā</s>,
that foolish man, his purpose accomplished after making an agreement, does not understand it.

children.text: tvaṃ praviśya ca kiṣkindhāṃ brūhi vānarapuṃgavam
children.translated_text: Enter <s>Kiṣkindhā</s> and speak my words to <s>Sugrīva</s>,

children.text: mūrkhaṃ grāmyasukhe saktaṃ sugrīvaṃ vacanān mama ||
children.translated_text: that bull among monkeys, foolish and attached to rustic pleasures.
He who, after promising hope to petitioners who have come to him, especially to those who formerly helped him,

children.text: āśāṃ saṃśrutya yo hanti sa loke puruṣādhamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: destroys that hope is the lowest of men in the world.

children.text: śubhaṃ vā yadi vā pāpaṃ yo hi vākyam udīritam
children.translated_text: Whether good or bad, the man who accepts with truth
a word once uttered is a hero, the best of men.

children.text: kṛtārthā hy akṛtārthānāṃ mitrāṇāṃ na bhavanti ye
children.translated_text: Those who, having achieved their own aim, do not become friends to those whose aim remains unachieved—

children.text: tān mṛtān api kravyādaḥ kṛtaghnān nopabhuñjate ||
children.translated_text: even when dead, flesh-eaters do not consume such ungrateful men.
Surely they wish to see the form of my bow,
with its golden back, drawn in battle by me, like a mass of lightning.
In battle he wishes to hear again the dreadful roar from the string and palm of me when enraged,

children.text: nirghoṣam iva vajrasya punaḥ saṃśrotum icchati ||
children.translated_text: like the crash of the thunderbolt.

children.text: kāmam evaṃ gate 'py asya parijñāte parākrame
children.translated_text: Even though things have come to this, since his valor is known,

children.text: tvatsahāyasya me vīra na cintā syān nṛpātmaja ||
children.translated_text: with you as my helper, O hero, there should be no anxiety for me, O king's son.
For the sake of which this undertaking was begun, O conqueror of enemy cities...
Having achieved his purpose, the lord of the monkeys does not recognize the appointed time.
For although the lord of the monkeys promised, "after the season of the rains,"
he sports away the four months that have passed and does not notice them.
Playing with his ministers and council, he devotes himself only to drinking;
<s>Sugrīva</s> shows no pity toward us, who are wretched with grief.

children.text: ucyatāṃ gaccha sugrīvas tvayā vatsa mahābala
children.translated_text: Go, dear mighty one; <s>Sugrīva</s> must be addressed by you.

children.text: mama roṣasya yadrūpaṃ brūyāś cainam idaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Tell him what form my anger has, and speak these words to him:

children.text: na ca saṃkucitaḥ panthā yena vālī hato gataḥ
children.translated_text: The path by which <s>Vālī</s> went when he was slain is not blocked;

children.text: samaye tiṣṭha sugrīva mā vālipatham anvagāḥ ||
children.translated_text: stand by the agreement, <s>Sugrīva</s>; do not follow <s>Vālī</s>'s path.

children.text: eka eva raṇe vālī śareṇa nihato mayā
children.translated_text: <s>Vālī</s> alone was struck down by me in battle with a single arrow;

children.text: tvāṃ tu satyād atikrāntaṃ haniṣyāmi sabāndhavam ||
children.translated_text: but you, having transgressed truth, I will slay together with your kinsmen.

children.text: tad evaṃ vihite kārye yaddhitaṃ puruṣarṣabha
children.translated_text: Therefore, when the matter has been arranged in this way, whatever is beneficial, O bull among men,

children.text: tat tad brūhi naraśreṣṭha tvara kālavyatikramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: say that, O best of men; hurry, for the appointed time is passing.

children.text: kuruṣva satyaṃ mayi vānareśvara pratiśrutaṃ dharmam avekṣya śāśvatam
children.translated_text: Make true, O lord of monkeys, the promise made to me, considering eternal <s>dharma</s> (right order).

children.text: mā vālinaṃ pretya gato yamakṣayaṃ tvam adya paśyer mama coditaiḥ śaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Do not today, gone after <s>Vālī</s> to <s>Yama</s>'s abode, see him by means of arrows impelled by me.

children.text: sa pūrvajaṃ tīvravivṛddhakopaṃ lālapyamānaṃ prasamīkṣya dīnam
children.translated_text: Seeing his elder brother, whose fierce anger had greatly grown, lamenting and wretched,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, lord of the human line and fierce in splendor, formed a stern resolve concerning the lord of monkeys.

children.text: sa kāminaṃ dīnam adīnasattvaḥ śokābhipannaṃ samudīrṇakopam
children.translated_text: Strong-hearted, he saw him love-stricken, wretched, overcome by grief, and with anger rising;

children.text: narendrasūnur naradevaputraṃ rāmānujaḥ pūrvajam ity uvāca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>'s younger brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, son of a lord of men, spoke thus to his elder brother, the prince:

children.text: na vānaraḥ sthāsyati sādhuvṛtte na maṃsyate kāryaphalānuṣaṅgān
children.translated_text: The monkey will not remain on the path of good conduct; he will not consider the consequences attached to the task.

children.text: na bhakṣyate vānararājyalakṣmīṃ tathā hi nābhikramate 'sya buddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nor should he enjoy the fortune of the monkey kingdom, for his mind does not move toward this task.
Because his judgment has decayed, he is attached to vulgar pleasures, with no thought of requiting your favor;

children.text: hato 'grajaṃ paśyatu vālinaṃ sa na rājyam evaṃ viguṇasya deyam ||
children.translated_text: let him see his elder brother <s>Vālī</s> slain. A kingdom should not be given to one so devoid of virtue.

children.text: na dhāraye kopam udīrṇavegaṃ nihanmi sugrīvam asatyam adya
children.translated_text: I cannot bear this anger of surging force; today I shall slay false <s>Sugrīva</s>.

children.text: haripravīraiḥ saha vāliputro narendrapatnyā vicayaṃ karotu ||
children.translated_text: Let <s>Vālī</s>'s son, together with the foremost monkeys, carry out the search for the king's wife.
As he sprang up, bow and arrows in hand, with the matter thus declared and wrath fierce for battle,

children.text: uvāca rāmaḥ paravīrahantā svavekṣitaṃ sānunayaṃ ca vākyam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, slayer of enemy heroes, spoke to him a speech in accordance with his own judgment and full of conciliation:

children.text: na hi vai tvadvidho loke pāpam evaṃ samācaret
children.translated_text: Surely one such as you in this world should not commit such a sin.

children.text: pāpam āryeṇa yo hanti sa vīraḥ puruṣottamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The hero, O best of men, is one who overcomes wrong by noble conduct.

children.text: nedam adya tvayā grāhyaṃ sādhuvṛttena lakṣmaṇa
children.translated_text: This is not something for you to accept today, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, since you are of virtuous conduct;

children.text: tāṃ prītim anuvartasva pūrvavṛttaṃ ca saṃgatam ||
children.translated_text: follow the affection between us and the bond established before.
With speech accompanied by conciliation, avoiding harsh words,
you should speak to <s>Sugrīva</s>, who has let the appointed time pass.
Then, having been instructed in his purpose by his elder brother just as it should be, that bull among men,
the hero <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, slayer of enemy heroes, entered the city.

children.text: tataḥ śubhamatiḥ prājño bhrātuḥ priyahite rataḥ
children.translated_text: Then wise <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, of auspicious mind, devoted to his brother's dear welfare,
inflamed with anger, went to the monkey's palace.
Taking up his bow, resembling the bow of <s>Śakra</s>, he was like Death at the end of time,
and, with that mountain-peak-like bow, like <s>Mandara</s> with its ridges.
At that time, intent on doing as instructed, <s>Rāma</s>'s younger brother considered the command and the reply with its further implications,
being equal to <s>Bṛhaspati</s> in intelligence.
Enveloped by the fire of his brother's anger, born of desire and wrath,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> then set out like an angry storm wind.
With force he knocked down many śāla, tāla, and aśvakarṇa trees,

children.text: paryasyan girikūṭāni drumān anyāṃś ca vegataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and swiftly hurled aside mountain peaks and other trees.

children.text: śilāś ca śakalīkurvan padbhyāṃ gaja ivāśugaḥ
children.translated_text: Breaking rocks into fragments with his feet, swift like an elephant,

children.text: dūram ekapadaṃ tyaktvā yayau kāryavaśād drutam ||
children.translated_text: he left the long footpath and went quickly under the compulsion of his task.
That tiger of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s>s saw the great city of the monkey king,
formidable <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, crowded with forces and hemmed in by mountains.
With lips quivering from anger toward <s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>
saw fearsome monkeys wandering outside <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>.
Mountain peaks by the hundreds and full-grown great trees
the elephant-like monkeys took up amid the mountains.

children.text: tān gṛhītapraharaṇān harīn dṛṣṭvā tu lakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing those monkeys with weapons in hand,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> became twice as angry, like a fire with abundant fuel.

children.text: taṃ te bhayaparītāṅgāḥ kruddhaṃ dṛṣṭvā plavaṃgamāḥ
children.translated_text: When those monkeys saw him angry, their bodies overcome with fear,
resembling Death and destruction at the end of an age, they fled by the hundreds in all directions.
Then the foremost monkeys entered <s>Sugrīva</s>'s palace
and reported <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s anger and arrival.

children.text: tārayā sahitaḥ kāmī saktaḥ kapivṛṣo rahaḥ
children.translated_text: But the bull among monkeys, lustful and attached in private with <s>Tārā</s>,

children.text: na teṣāṃ kapivīrāṇāṃ śuśrāva vacanaṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: did not hear the words of those monkey heroes at that time.
Then, ordered by the ministers, monkeys that made the hair stand on end,
like mountains, elephants, and clouds, went out from the city.
Terrible, armed with claws and teeth, all frightful to behold,

children.text: sarve śārdūladarpāś ca sarve ca vikṛtānanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all with the pride of tigers and all with distorted faces,
some possessed the strength of ten elephants, and some ten times that;
some were equal in valor to a thousand elephants.

children.text: kṛtsnāṃ hi kapibhir vyāptāṃ drumahastair mahābalaiḥ
children.translated_text: Angry <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> saw that unassailable <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>
entirely filled with very mighty monkeys holding trees in their hands.
Then all those monkeys, from within the wall and moat,
came out, their spirits high, and stood openly revealed.

children.text: sugrīvasya pramādaṃ ca pūrvajaṃ cārtam ātmavān
children.translated_text: Perceiving <s>Sugrīva</s>'s negligence and his elder brother's distress,

children.text: buddhvā kopavaśaṃ vīraḥ punar eva jagāma saḥ ||
children.translated_text: the self-possessed hero, overcome by anger, went again.
With long, hot, mighty sighs and eyes reddened by anger,
that tiger among men became like a fire covered with smoke.
With arrows as his fangs and a quivering arrow-point as his tongue, bearing his bow as his coiling body,
and filled with the poison of his own splendor, he was like a five-mouthed serpent.

children.text: taṃ dīptam iva kālāgniṃ nāgendram iva kopitam
children.translated_text: When <s>Aṅgada</s> approached him, blazing like the fire of Time and like an enraged lord of elephants,
he fell into deep despondency from fear.
Then the greatly renowned one, his eyes copper-red with wrath, instructed <s>Aṅgada</s>:

children.text: sugrīvaḥ kathyatāṃ vatsa mamāgamanam ity uta ||
children.translated_text: "Child, let <s>Sugrīva</s> be told of my arrival."
"This younger brother of <s>Rāma</s>, O subduer of enemies, has come into your presence;
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, afflicted by his brother's suffering, is standing at the door."
Hearing <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s words, <s>Aṅgada</s>, filled with sorrow, spoke

children.text: pituḥ samīpam āgamya saumitrir ayam āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: after coming into his father's presence: "This son of <s>Sumitrā</s> has arrived."
Seeing him, like a great flood and with a sound like the thunderbolt and the lightning-bolt,
they made a lion-roar together near <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
At that great sound the monkey awoke,
his eyes red and unsteady with intoxication, his garland and ornaments disordered.
Then, hearing <s>Aṅgada</s>'s words, two ministers of the lord of monkeys,
who had come there with him, respected and noble in appearance,

children.text: plakṣaś caiva prabhāvaś ca mantriṇāv arthadharmayoḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Plakṣa</s> and <s>Prabhāva</s>, ministers skilled in artha and dharma,

children.text: vaktum uccāvacaṃ prāptaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ tau śaśaṃsatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: announced that <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> had come to speak on matters high and low.
Having appeased <s>Sugrīva</s> with words grounded in conciliation,
the two sat attending on him as the <s>Maruts</s> attend on <s>Śakra</s>.
"The two noble brothers <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> are true to their pledges;
they have entered into friendship with you, are worthy of a kingdom, and have given you a kingdom.

children.text: tayor eko dhanuṣpāṇir dvāri tiṣṭhati lakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: One of them, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, stands at the door with bow in hand;

children.text: yasya bhītāḥ pravepante nādān muñcanti vānarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the monkeys, terrified of him, tremble and utter cries.
This <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, brother of <s>Rāghava</s>, with speech as his charioteer
and resolution as his chariot, has come by that <s>Rāma</s>'s command.

children.text: tasya mūrdhnā praṇamya tvaṃ saputraḥ saha bandhubhiḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, bowing to him with your head, together with your son and kinsmen,
O king, stand by your agreement and be true to your promise."

children.text: aṅgadasya vacaḥ śrutvā sugrīvaḥ sacivaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Aṅgada</s>'s words, <s>Sugrīva</s>, together with his ministers,
and hearing that <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> was angry, the self-possessed one left his seat.
Skilled in counsel, expert in deliberation, and thoroughly grounded in matters of counsel,
he considered what was weighty and what was slight, and spoke these words to his ministers:

children.text: na me durvyāhṛtaṃ kiṃcin nāpi me duranuṣṭhitam
children.translated_text: "I have said nothing improper, nor have I done anything improper.

children.text: lakṣmaṇo rāghavabhrātā kruddhaḥ kim iti cintaye ||
children.translated_text: Why, then, is <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, <s>Rāghava</s>'s brother, angry? So I wonder.
My enemies, hostile men who always look for an opening,
must have made <s>Rāghava</s>'s younger brother hear of faults of mine that do not exist.

children.text: atra tāvad yathābuddhi sarvair eva yathāvidhi
children.translated_text: In this matter, then, all of you, according to your understanding and in due form,

children.text: bhavadbhir niścayas tasya vijñeyo nipuṇaṃ śanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: must carefully and gradually ascertain his decision.

children.text: na khalvasti mama trāso lakṣmaṇānnāpi rāghavāt
children.translated_text: Indeed I have no fear of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, nor of <s>Rāghava</s>;
but a friend angered out of place does cause agitation.
A friend is in every way easy to gain, but hard to maintain;

children.text: anityatvāt tu cittānāṃ prītir alpe 'pi bhidyate ||
children.translated_text: because minds are unstable, affection is broken even by a little thing.
For that reason I am frightened without cause. What has been done for me by great-souled <s>Rāma</s>

children.text: yan mamopakṛtaṃ śakyaṃ pratikartuṃ na tan mayā ||
children.translated_text: is not something I am able to repay."
When <s>Sugrīva</s> had spoken thus, <s>Hanumān</s>, bull among monkeys,
spoke according to his own reasoning in the midst of the monkey ministers:

children.text: sarvathā naitad āścaryaṃ yat tvaṃ harigaṇeśvara
children.translated_text: "It is in no way surprising, O lord of the monkey hosts,
that you do not forget the good, affectionate favor that was done for you.

children.text: rāghaveṇa tu śūreṇa bhayam utsṛjya dūrataḥ
children.translated_text: For brave <s>Rāghava</s>, casting fear far aside,
killed <s>Vālī</s>, equal to <s>Śakra</s> in valor, for the sake of what was dear to you.

children.text: sarvathā praṇayāt kruddho rāghavo nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Certainly <s>Rāghava</s> is angry out of affection; there is no doubt here.
He has sent his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, increaser of prosperity.

children.text: tvaṃ pramatto na jānīṣe kālaṃ kalavidāṃ vara
children.translated_text: You, being negligent, do not recognize the time, O best knower of the proper time.
The auspicious autumn has begun, dark with blossoming saptacchada trees.
The sky is clear, with planets and constellations unobscured, and the clouds have vanished;

children.text: prasannāś ca diśaḥ sarvāḥ saritaś ca sarāṃsi ca ||
children.translated_text: all the quarters are clear, and so are the rivers and lakes.
The time for undertaking action has arrived, but you do not notice it, O bull among monkeys;

children.text: tvaṃ pramatta iti vyaktaṃ lakṣmaṇo 'yam ihāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: it is clear that you are negligent, and for this reason <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> has come here.
You must endure the harsh speech of great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>,
a suffering man whose wife has been taken, even when it comes through another man.

children.text: kṛtāparādhasya hi te nānyat paśyāmy ahaṃ kṣamam
children.translated_text: Since you have committed an offense, I see nothing else proper for you
except appeasing <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> with joined palms.
A king must certainly be told what is beneficial by appointed ministers;

children.text: ata eva bhayaṃ tyaktvā bravīmy avadhṛtaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore, having cast aside fear, I speak this decided word.

children.text: abhikruddhaḥ samartho hi cāpam udyamya rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: For enraged <s>Rāghava</s>, powerful and raising his bow,
is able to bring the world, together with gods, asuras, and gandharvas, under his control.

children.text: na sa kṣamaḥ kopayituṃ yaḥ prasādya punar bhavet
children.translated_text: He is not one who should be angered, for he would have to be appeased again,
especially by a grateful man who remembers his former favor.

children.text: tasya mūrdhnā praṇamya tvaṃ saputraḥ sasuhṛjjanaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, bowing to him with your head, together with your son and friends,

children.text: rājaṃs tiṣṭha svasamaye bhartur bhāryeva tadvaśe ||
children.translated_text: O king, stand by your agreement, under his authority like a wife under her husband's."

children.text: na rāmarāmānujaśāsanaṃ tvayā kapīndrayuktaṃ manasāpy apohitum
children.translated_text: The command of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāma</s>'s younger brother, joined with the lord of monkeys, cannot be set aside by you even in thought;

children.text: mano hi te jñāsyati mānuṣaṃ balaṃ sarāghavasyāsya surendravarcasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for your mind will come to know the human strength of this <s>Rāghava</s>, whose splendor is like <s>Surendra</s>'s.
Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, slayer of enemy heroes, having been instructed in reply,
