entered the terrible cave-city, <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, at <s>Rāma</s>'s command.
The monkeys standing at the gate there, huge-bodied and very strong,

children.text: babhūvur lakṣmaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarve prāñjalayaḥ sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: on seeing <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, all stood with joined palms.

children.text: niḥśvasantaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā kruddhaṃ daśarathātmajam
children.translated_text: But seeing that son of <s>Daśaratha</s> breathing hard in anger,

children.text: babhūvur harayas trastā na cainaṃ paryavārayan ||
children.translated_text: the monkeys became frightened and did not block him.

children.text: sa tāṃ ratnamayīṃ śrīmān divyāṃ puṣpitakānanām
children.translated_text: The glorious one saw that great cave-city, made of jewels, splendid, with flowering groves,
lovely and strewn with jewels.
It was crowded with mansions and palaces, adorned with many kinds of merchandise,
and beautified by flowering trees that bore every desired fruit.
It was adorned with monkeys, sons of gods and gandharvas, able to assume forms at will,
pleasant to behold, wearing heavenly garlands and garments.
Its great roads were made fragrant by the sweet scents of sandal, aloe, and lotuses,
and by the aromas of maireya wines and honeys.
With palaces rising like the expanses of the <s>Vindhya</s> and <s>Meru</s> mountains, many-storied,

children.text: dadarśa girinadyaś ca vimalās tatra rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> also saw clear mountain streams there.

children.text: aṅgadasya gṛhaṃ ramyaṃ maindasya dvividasya ca
children.translated_text: The lovely houses of <s>Aṅgada</s>, of <s>Mainda</s> and <s>Dvivida</s>,
of <s>Gavaya</s>, <s>Gavākṣa</s>, <s>Gaja</s>, and <s>Śarabha</s>,
of <s>Vidyunmālin</s>, <s>Sampāti</s>, <s>Sūryākṣa</s>, and <s>Hanūmat</s>,

children.text: vīrabāhoḥ subāhoś ca nalasya ca mahātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: of <s>Vīrabāhu</s>, <s>Subāhu</s>, and noble <s>Nala</s>,
of <s>Kumuda</s>, <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, <s>Tāra</s>, and <s>Jāmbavat</s>,
of <s>Dadhivaktra</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, <s>Supāṭala</s>, and <s>Sunetra</s>:
on the royal road <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> saw the chief houses
of these noble leaders of the monkeys, massive and excellent.
They shone like white clouds and were adorned with heavenly garlands;
they were full of abundant wealth and grain, and adorned with jewels among women.
Then he saw the lovely house of the lord of monkeys, hard to approach,
surrounded by a white mountain and resembling the dwelling of <s>Mahendra</s>.
It was adorned with white palace-towers like the peaks of <s>Kailāsa</s>,
and with flowering trees that bore every desired fruit.
It was beautified by splendid trees given by <s>Mahendra</s>, resembling dark rain clouds,
with heavenly flowers and fruits, cool shade, and delightful appearance.
Its gate was surrounded by strong monkeys bearing weapons;
it was bright, covered with heavenly garlands, and had gateways of heated gold.
The mighty <s>Saumitri</s> entered <s>Sugrīva</s>'s lovely house,
unhindered, like the sun entering a great cloud.
That righteous one passed through seven courtyards filled with vehicles and seats,
and saw the great inner apartment, vast and well guarded.
It was adorned here and there with many golden and silver couches
and with excellent seats furnished with costly coverings.
As he entered, he constantly heard a sweet sound,
filled with the music of stringed instruments and with words and syllables of choral song.
In <s>Sugrīva</s>'s house the mighty one saw many women of varied appearance,
proud of their beauty and youth.
Having seen those of noble birth, wearing garlands fashioned of variegated flowers,
busy with excellent garlands and adorned with the finest ornaments,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> also observed <s>Sugrīva</s>'s attendants,
neither unsatisfied, nor overly distracted, nor poorly dressed.
Then he saw <s>Sugrīva</s> seated on a supreme golden throne,
furnished with costly coverings and shining like the sun.
His body was adorned with heavenly ornaments; he was handsome, glorious,
wearing heavenly garlands and garments, unconquerable like <s>Mahendra</s>,
and surrounded by women with heavenly ornaments and garlands.

children.text: rumāṃ tu vīraḥ parirabhya gāḍhaṃ varāsanastho varahemavarṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The hero, seated on an excellent seat and of fine golden complexion, tightly embraced <s>Rumā</s>;
wide-eyed, he saw steadfast <s>Saumitri</s>, who also had very broad eyes.
Seeing <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, that best of men, unhindered, angry, and entered within,
<s>Sugrīva</s>'s senses were shaken.

children.text: kruddhaṃ niḥśvasamānaṃ taṃ pradīptam iva tejasā
children.translated_text: Seeing that son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, angry, breathing hard, blazing as if with splendor,
tormented by his brother's distress,
the best of monkeys leapt up, leaving the golden seat,

children.text: mahān mahendrasya yathā svalaṃkṛta iva dhvajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: like <s>Mahendra</s>'s great, well-adorned banner.
As <s>Sugrīva</s> rose, the women beginning with <s>Rumā</s> rose after him,

children.text: sugrīvaṃ gagane pūrṇaṃ candraṃ tārāgaṇā iva ||
children.translated_text: like hosts of stars following the full moon in the sky.
The glorious one, his eyes reddened, moved with joined palms;
he stood there like a great wish-fulfilling tree.
Angry, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> spoke to <s>Sugrīva</s>, who stood among the women with <s>Rumā</s> as his second,

children.text: abravīl lakṣmaṇaḥ kruddhaḥ satāraṃ śaśinaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: like the moon accompanied by <s>Tārā</s>.
A king endowed with strength and noble lineage, compassionate, self-controlled,

children.text: kṛtajñaḥ satyavādī ca rājā loke mahīyate ||
children.translated_text: grateful and truthful, is honored in the world.

children.text: yas tu rājā sthito 'dharme mitrāṇām upakāriṇām
children.translated_text: But the king who stands in unrighteousness and makes a false promise
to friends who have helped him: who is more cruel than he?

children.text: śatam aśvānṛte hanti sahasraṃ tu gavānṛte
children.translated_text: A man kills a hundred by a lie about a horse, and a thousand by a lie about a cow;
by a lie about a man, a person kills himself and his own people.

children.text: pūrvaṃ kṛtārtho mitrāṇāṃ na tat pratikaroti yaḥ
children.translated_text: One who has previously had his purpose accomplished by friends and does not return that service
is ungrateful toward all beings, and he deserves to be killed, O lord of monkeys.
This verse was sung by <s>Brahmā</s>, honored by all the worlds;

children.text: dṛṣṭvā kṛtaghnaṃ kruddhena taṃ nibodha plavaṃgama ||
children.translated_text: learn it, O monkey, as spoken in anger when he saw an ungrateful man.

children.text: brahmaghne ca surāpe ca core bhagnavrate tathā
children.translated_text: For one who kills a brahmin, for one who drinks liquor, for a thief, and also for one who breaks a vow,

children.text: niṣkṛtir vihitā sadbhiḥ kṛtaghne nāsti niṣkṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: atonement has been prescribed by the good; for the ungrateful there is no atonement.

children.text: anāryas tvaṃ kṛtaghnaś ca mithyāvādī ca vānara
children.translated_text: You are ignoble, ungrateful, and a liar, O monkey,

children.text: pūrvaṃ kṛtārtho rāmasya na tat pratikaroṣi yat ||
children.translated_text: because, after having had your purpose accomplished by <s>Rāma</s>, you do not repay that service.

children.text: nanu nāma kṛtārthena tvayā rāmasya vānara
children.translated_text: Surely, O monkey, since your purpose was accomplished,

children.text: sītāyā mārgaṇe yatnaḥ kartavyaḥ kṛtam icchatā ||
children.translated_text: you, wishing to repay what was done by <s>Rāma</s>, ought to make an effort in the search for <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: sa tvaṃ grāmyeṣu bhogeṣu sakto mithyāpratiśravaḥ
children.translated_text: But you, attached to vulgar pleasures and false in your promise,

children.text: na tvāṃ rāmo vijānīte sarpaṃ maṇḍūkarāviṇam ||
children.translated_text: do not understand <s>Rāma</s>, as a frog does not understand the snake that is croaking near it.
By noble <s>Rāma</s>, who feels compassion and is great-souled,

children.text: harīṇāṃ prāpito rājyaṃ tvaṃ durātmā mahātmanā ||
children.translated_text: you, wicked and evil-minded, were brought to the kingship of the monkeys.
If you do not acknowledge what was done by <s>Rāma</s>, whose deeds are unwearied,

children.text: sadyas tvaṃ niśitair bāṇair hato drakṣyasi vālinam ||
children.translated_text: then, struck down at once by sharp arrows, you will see <s>Vālin</s>.

children.text: na ca saṃkucitaḥ panthā yena vālī hato gataḥ
children.translated_text: The path by which <s>Vālin</s>, slain, has gone is not closed;

children.text: samaye tiṣṭha sugrīva mā vālipatham anvagāḥ ||
children.translated_text: stand by the agreement, <s>Sugrīva</s>; do not follow <s>Vālin</s>'s path.

children.text: na nūnam ikṣvākuvarasya kārmukāc cyutāñ śarān paśyasi vajrasaṃnibhān
children.translated_text: Surely you do not see the arrows, like thunderbolts, fallen from the bow of the best of the Ikṣvākus;

children.text: tataḥ sukhaṃ nāma niṣevase sukhī na rāmakāryaṃ manasāpy avekṣase ||
children.translated_text: therefore you enjoy what is called pleasure, happy, and do not even consider <s>Rāma</s>'s business in your mind.

children.text: tathā bruvāṇaṃ saumitriṃ pradīptam iva tejasā
children.translated_text: To <s>Saumitri</s>, speaking thus and blazing as if with splendor,
<s>Tārā</s>, whose face resembled the lord of stars, spoke to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: naivaṃ lakṣmaṇa vaktavyo nāyaṃ paruṣam arhati
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, he should not be spoken to in this way;

children.text: harīṇām īśvaraḥ śrotuṃ tava vaktrād viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the lord of the monkeys does not deserve to hear harsh words, especially from your mouth.

children.text: naivākṛtajñaḥ sugrīvo na śaṭho nāpi dāruṇaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s> is not ungrateful, not deceitful, nor cruel;

children.text: naivānṛtakatho vīra na jihmaś ca kapīśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor, O hero, is the lord of monkeys false in speech or crooked.

children.text: upakāraṃ kṛtaṃ vīro nāpy ayaṃ vismṛtaḥ kapiḥ
children.translated_text: This heroic monkey has not forgotten the service

children.text: rāmeṇa vīra sugrīvo yad anyair duṣkaraṃ raṇe ||
children.translated_text: that heroic <s>Rāma</s> did for <s>Sugrīva</s> in battle, which would be difficult for others to do.

children.text: rāmaprasādāt kīrtiṃ ca kapirājyaṃ ca śāśvatam
children.translated_text: By <s>Rāma</s>'s favor, <s>Sugrīva</s> has obtained fame and the lasting kingdom of the monkeys here,

children.text: prāptavān iha sugrīvo rumāṃ māṃ ca paraṃtapa ||
children.translated_text: as well as <s>Rumā</s> and me, O scorcher of foes.

children.text: suduḥkhaṃ śāyitaḥ pūrvaṃ prāpyedaṃ sukham uttamam
children.translated_text: Having formerly lain in great misery and now attained this supreme happiness,

children.text: prāptakālaṃ na jānīte viśvāmitro yathā muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: he does not know that the proper time has arrived, like the sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>.
For, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, attached to <s>Ghṛtācī</s>,
the righteous great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s> is said to have thought ten years a single day.

children.text: sa hi prāptaṃ na jānīte kālaṃ kālavidāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: He indeed, best of those who know time, did not recognize the time that had arrived,

children.text: viśvāmitro mahātejāḥ kiṃ punar yaḥ pṛthagjanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the very mighty <s>Viśvāmitra</s>; how much less an ordinary person?
Since this one has come under the condition of the body, is weary, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
and is still unsated in pleasures, <s>Rāma</s> ought to forgive him here.

children.text: na ca roṣavaśaṃ tāta gantum arhasi lakṣmaṇa
children.translated_text: And, dear one, you should not fall under the power of anger, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
like an ordinary man acting rashly without understanding the matter for certain.
For men endowed with strength of character, such as you, O bull among men,

children.text: avimṛśya na roṣasya sahasā yānti vaśyatām ||
children.translated_text: do not, without reflection, suddenly come under the control of anger.
Intent upon <s>Sugrīva</s>'s welfare, I beg you, knower of <s>dharma</s> (right conduct);
let this great agitation born of anger be abandoned.

children.text: rumāṃ māṃ kapirājyaṃ ca dhanadhānyavasūni ca
children.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s> would give up <s>Rumā</s>, me, the monkey kingdom, and wealth in grain and goods

children.text: rāmapriyārthaṃ sugrīvas tyajed iti matir mama ||
children.translated_text: for the sake of what is dear to <s>Rāma</s>: such is my opinion.
<s>Sugrīva</s> will bring <s>Rāghava</s> together with <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: śaśāṅkam iva rohiṇyā nihatvā rāvaṇaṃ raṇe ||
children.translated_text: like the moon with <s>Rohiṇī</s>, after killing <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle.
In <s>Laṅkā</s> there are said to be thousands of hundreds of crores of rākṣasas,

children.text: ayutāni ca ṣaṭtriṃśat sahasrāṇi śatāni ca ||
children.translated_text: and thirty-six ayutas, thousands, and hundreds besides.

children.text: ahatvā tāṃś ca durdharṣān rākṣasān kāmarūpiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Without killing those hard-to-subdue rākṣasas, who can take forms at will,

children.text: na śakyo rāvaṇo hantuṃ yena sā maithilī hṛtā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, by whom that <s>Maithilī</s> was carried off, cannot be slain.

children.text: te na śakyā raṇe hantum asahāyena lakṣmaṇa
children.translated_text: They cannot be killed in battle without assistance, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
and cruel-deeded <s>Rāvaṇa</s> especially cannot be killed without <s>Sugrīva</s>.

children.text: evam ākhyātavān vālī sa hy abhijño harīśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Vālin</s> told me; for that lord of monkeys knew the matter well.

children.text: āgamas tu na me vyaktaḥ śravāt tasya bravīmy aham ||
children.translated_text: But the full account is not clear to me; I speak from having heard it from him.
For the purpose of aiding you, the foremost monkeys have been sent
to bring many monkeys, chiefs of monkey troops, for the battle.
Waiting for those valiant and very mighty ones,
the lord of monkeys has not gone out, for the accomplishment of <s>Rāghava</s>'s purpose.

children.text: kṛtā tu saṃsthā saumitre sugrīveṇa yathāpurā
children.translated_text: But an arrangement has been made by <s>Sugrīva</s>, O <s>Saumitri</s>, just as before:

children.text: adya tair vānaraiḥ sarvair āgantavyaṃ mahābalaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: today all those very mighty monkeys are to arrive.
Thousands of crores of bears and hundreds of golāṅgūlas

children.text: adya tvām upayāsyanti jahi kopam ariṃdama
children.translated_text: will come to you today; abandon your anger, O subduer of enemies.
And many crores of monkeys of blazing splendor will come, O <s>Kākutstha</s>.

children.text: tava hi mukham idaṃ nirīkṣya kopāt kṣatajanibhe nayane nirīkṣamāṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing this face of yours, and seeing your eyes, reddened like fresh blood, through anger,

children.text: harivaravanitā na yānti śāntiṃ prathamabhayasya hi śaṅkitāḥ sma sarvāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the women of the best of monkeys cannot become calm; we are all anxious from this first fear.

children.text: ity uktas tārayā vākyaṃ praśritaṃ dharmasaṃhitam
children.translated_text: When <s>Tārā</s> had spoken this humble speech, joined with <s>dharma</s> (right conduct),
the gentle-natured <s>Saumitri</s> accepted her words.
When that speech had been accepted, the lord of the monkey hosts
cast off his great fear of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, like a wet garment.

children.text: tataḥ kaṇṭhagataṃ mālyaṃ citraṃ bahuguṇaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: Then, tearing off the splendid, large, many-stranded garland around his neck,
<s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of monkeys, became free from intoxication.
Then he, the foremost of all monkeys, of terrible strength, turned to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>...
<s>Sugrīva</s>, gladdening him, spoke a humble speech:

children.text: pranaṣṭā śrīś ca kīrtiś ca kapirājyaṃ ca śāśvatam
children.translated_text: My lost prosperity, fame, and lasting kingdom of the monkeys

children.text: rāmaprasādāt saumitre punaḥ prāptam idaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: have been obtained again by me through <s>Rāma</s>'s favor, O <s>Saumitri</s>.

children.text: kaḥ śaktas tasya devasya khyātasya svena karmaṇā
children.translated_text: Who is able to repay that godlike man, famous through his own deeds,
for such valor, O hero, O subduer of foes?

children.text: sītāṃ prāpsyati dharmātmā vadhiṣyati ca rāvaṇam
children.translated_text: The righteous <s>Rāghava</s> will recover <s>Sītā</s> and will kill <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
by his own splendor, with me serving only as an ally.

children.text: sahāyakṛtyaṃ hi tasya yena sapta mahādrumāḥ
children.translated_text: For what service as an ally can be done for him by whom seven great trees,

children.text: śailaś ca vasudhā caiva bāṇenaikena dāritāḥ ||
children.translated_text: a mountain, and the very earth were split by a single arrow?
O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, when he twanged his bow,

children.text: saśailā kampitā bhūmiḥ sahāyais tasya kiṃ nu vai ||
children.translated_text: the earth with its mountains trembled at its sound; what indeed are allies to him?
I shall provide an escort for that lord of men, O bull among men,
as he goes to kill <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, his enemy together with his city.

children.text: yadi kiṃcid atikrāntaṃ viśvāsāt praṇayena vā
children.translated_text: If anything has gone too far through trust or through affection,

children.text: preṣyasya kṣamitavyaṃ me na kaścin nāparādhyati ||
children.translated_text: it should be forgiven in me, your servant; there is no one who does not err.
As the great-souled <s>Sugrīva</s> was speaking thus,

children.text: abhavallakṣmaṇaḥ prītaḥ premṇā cedam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> became pleased, and out of affection he said this:

children.text: sarvathā hi mama bhrātā sanātho vānareśvara
children.translated_text: In every way, O lord of monkeys, my brother has a protector,
with you as his protector, <s>Sugrīva</s>, especially since you are humble.

children.text: yas te prabhāvaḥ sugrīva yac ca te śaucam uttamam
children.translated_text: Such as your power is, <s>Sugrīva</s>, and such as your excellent purity of conduct is,
you deserve to enjoy the unsurpassed fortune of the monkey kingdom.

children.text: sahāyena ca sugrīva tvayā rāmaḥ pratāpavān
children.translated_text: With you as his ally, <s>Sugrīva</s>, the mighty <s>Rāma</s>
will soon kill his enemies in battle; there is no doubt about this.
For one who knows <s>dharma</s>, is grateful, and does not turn back in battles,

children.text: upapannaṃ ca yuktaṃ ca sugrīva tava bhāṣitam ||
children.translated_text: what you have said, <s>Sugrīva</s>, is fitting and proper.

children.text: doṣajñaḥ sati sāmarthye ko 'nyo bhāṣitum arhati
children.translated_text: Who else, knowing faults and possessing the ability, is worthy to speak so,

children.text: varjayitvā mama jyeṣṭhaṃ tvāṃ ca vānarasattama ||
children.translated_text: apart from my elder brother and you, O best of monkeys?

children.text: sadṛśaś cāsi rāmasya vikrameṇa balena ca
children.translated_text: You are equal to <s>Rāma</s> in valor and in strength,
an ally given by the gods for a long time, O foremost of monkeys.

children.text: kiṃ tu śīghram ito vīra niṣkrāma tvaṃ mayā saha
children.translated_text: But now, hero, go out quickly from here with me,
and comfort your friend, who is grieved by the abduction of his wife.

children.text: yac ca śokābhibhūtasya śrutvā rāmasya bhāṣitam
children.translated_text: And because, after hearing the words of grief-stricken <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: mayā tvaṃ paruṣāṇy uktas tac ca tvaṃ kṣantum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: I spoke harsh words to you, you ought to forgive that too.

children.text: evam uktas tu sugrīvo lakṣmaṇena mahātmanā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by great-souled <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: hanumantaṃ sthitaṃ pārśve sacivaṃ vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s> spoke to <s>Hanumān</s>, his minister standing at his side:
Those who are on the peaks of <s>Mahendra</s>, <s>Himavat</s>, <s>Vindhya</s>, and <s>Kailāsa</s>,
and those stationed on <s>Mandara</s>, on the white peak, and among the five mountains,
on mountains colored like the young sun and shining everywhere,

children.text: parvateṣu samudrānte paścimasyāṃ tu ye diśi ||
children.translated_text: and those in the western quarter on mountains at the ocean's edge,
and on the mountain that is the Sun's abode, resembling a twilight cloud,
foremost monkeys who have resorted to the terrible forest of lotuses and palmyras,
those dark like collyrium clouds, with strength like elephants,

children.text: añjane parvate caiva ye vasanti plavaṃgamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the leaping monkeys who live on Mount <s>Añjana</s>,
monkeys living in caves of red arsenic, shining like gold,

children.text: merupārśvagatāś caiva ye ca dhūmragiriṃ śritāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those staying on the flank of <s>Meru</s>, and those who have resorted to <s>Dhūmragiri</s>,
and those on the great red mountain, colored like the young sun,
leaping monkeys of terrible speed, drinking honey-wine and <s>maireya</s> liquor,

children.text: vaneṣu ca suramyeṣu sugandhiṣu mahatsu ca
children.translated_text: and those in lovely, fragrant, and great forests,
and all around in the delightful forest-edges of ascetics,

children.text: tāṃs tāṃs tvam ānaya kṣipraṃ pṛthivyāṃ sarvavānarān
children.translated_text: bring all those monkeys quickly, all the monkeys on earth,
and swiftly dispatch the monkeys by means such as conciliation and gifts.

children.text: preṣitāḥ prathamaṃ ye ca mayā dūtā mahājavāḥ
children.translated_text: Those very swift messengers who were first sent by me

children.text: tvaraṇārthaṃ tu bhūyas tvaṃ harīn saṃpreṣayāparān ||
children.translated_text: for the sake of speed: send still other monkeys after them.

children.text: ye prasaktāś ca kāmeṣu dīrghasūtrāś ca vānarāḥ
children.translated_text: Those monkeys who are attached to pleasures and are procrastinating,

children.text: ihānayasva tān sarvāñ śīghraṃ tu mama śāsanāt ||
children.translated_text: bring them all here quickly by my command.

children.text: ahobhir daśabhir ye ca nāgacchanti mamājñayā
children.translated_text: Those who do not come within ten days at my order
are to be killed, wicked men who violate the king's command.

children.text: śatāny atha sahasrāṇi koṭyaś ca mama śāsanāt
children.translated_text: By my command let hundreds, thousands, and crores

children.text: prayāntu kapisiṃhānāṃ diśo mama mate sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: of lionlike monkeys, standing in accord with my intent, go forth to the quarters.
Let the best monkeys, resembling clouds and mountains, as if covering the sky,
terrible in form, go from here at my command.

children.text: te gatijñā gatiṃ gatvā pṛthivyāṃ sarvavānarāḥ
children.translated_text: Those monkeys who know the routes, having gone their routes over the earth,

children.text: ānayantu harīn sarvāṃs tvaritāḥ śāsanān mama ||
children.translated_text: let them quickly bring all the monkeys by my order.
Having heard the words of that king of monkeys, the son of the Wind
sent out mighty monkeys in all directions.
Those monkeys, moving on paths of birds and stars, on the path once traversed by <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: prayātāḥ prahitā rājñā harayas tatkṣaṇena vai ||
children.translated_text: were dispatched by the king and set out at that very moment.

children.text: te samudreṣu giriṣu vaneṣu ca saritsu ca
children.translated_text: In oceans, on mountains, in forests, and along rivers,
the monkeys urged on all monkeys for <s>Rāma</s>'s sake.
Hearing the command, comparable to the time of death, of the king of kings,
<s>Sugrīva</s>, the monkeys came, seeing the danger of <s>Sugrīva</s>'s anger.
Then from that mountain, dark like collyrium and very swift,

children.text: tisraḥ koṭyaḥ plavaṃgānāṃ niryayur yatra rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: three crores of leaping monkeys went out to where <s>Rāghava</s> was.

children.text: astaṃ gacchati yatrārkas tasmin girivare ratāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who delighted in that excellent mountain where the sun sets:
from there ten crores, shining like heated gold, came down.
And from the peaks of <s>Kailāsa</s>, monkeys with the brilliance of lions' manes...
Then tens of thousands of crores of monkeys arrived,
living on fruits and roots and dwelling near <s>Himavant</s>.
A thousand of those thousands of crores assembled,
terrible, of dreadful deeds, and like burning coals.
Thousands of crores of monkeys swiftly descended from <s>Vindhya</s>,
living on the shore of the milk-ocean and dwelling in tamāla groves,

children.text: nārikelāśanāś caiva teṣāṃ saṃkhyā na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: and eating coconuts; their number is not known.

children.text: vanebhyo gahvarebhyaś ca saridbhyaś ca mahājavāḥ
children.translated_text: From forests, from thickets, and from rivers, very swift,
the monkey army came, as if drinking up the sun.

children.text: ye tu tvarayituṃ yātā vānarāḥ sarvavānarān
children.translated_text: But the monkeys who had gone to hasten all the monkeys,

children.text: te vīrā himavacchailaṃ dadṛśus taṃ mahādrumam ||
children.translated_text: those heroes saw that mountain <s>Himavant</s>, full of great trees.

children.text: tasmin girivare ramye yajño māheśvaraḥ purā
children.translated_text: On that lovely best of mountains, in former times a sacrifice to <s>Maheśvara</s>,
divine, charming, and pleasing to the minds of all the gods, had shone.
There the monkeys saw roots and fruits produced from the outflow of sacrificial food,
having a taste comparable to nectar.

children.text: tad annasambhavaṃ divyaṃ phalaṃ mūlaṃ manoharam
children.translated_text: That divine and lovely fruit and root, produced from that food,

children.text: yaḥ kaścit sakṛd aśnāti māsaṃ bhavati tarpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whoever eats it even once remains satisfied for a month.

children.text: tāni mūlāni divyāni phalāni ca phalāśanāḥ
children.translated_text: Those fruit-eating leaders of monkey troops took those divine roots and fruits,
and divine medicinal herbs as well.

children.text: tasmāc ca yajñāyatanāt puṣpāṇi surabhīṇi ca
children.translated_text: And from that sacrificial ground they took fragrant flowers,
and the monkeys brought them after going, in order to please <s>Sugrīva</s>.

children.text: te tu sarve harivarāḥ pṛthivyāṃ sarvavānarān
children.translated_text: But all those best monkeys, having urged on all the monkeys on earth,
swiftly went at the head of the troops.

children.text: te tu tena muhūrtena yūthapāḥ śīghrakāriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Then in that same muhūrta (brief period), the troop-leaders, quick in action,

children.text: kiṣkindhāṃ tvarayā prāptāḥ sugrīvo yatra vānaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: reached <s>Kiṣkindhā</s> in haste, where the monkey <s>Sugrīva</s> was.

children.text: te gṛhītvauṣadhīḥ sarvāḥ phalaṃ mūlaṃ ca vānarāḥ
children.translated_text: Having taken all the herbs, fruit, and root, the monkeys
presented them to him and spoke this word:

children.text: sarve parigatāḥ śailāḥ samudrāś ca vanāni ca
children.translated_text: All mountains, seas, and forests have been traversed.

children.text: pṛthivyāṃ vānarāḥ sarve śāsanād upayānti te ||
children.translated_text: All the monkeys on earth are coming to you at your command.

children.text: evaṃ śrutvā tato hṛṣṭaḥ sugrīvaḥ plavagādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, hearing this, <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the leapers, was delighted,

children.text: pratijagrāha ca prītas teṣāṃ sarvam upāyanam ||
children.translated_text: and gladly accepted all their gifts.

children.text: pratigṛhya ca tat sarvam upāyanam upāhṛtam
children.translated_text: Having received all that brought offering,

children.text: vānarān sāntvayitvā ca sarvān eva vyasarjayat ||
children.translated_text: and having comforted all the monkeys, he dismissed them all.

children.text: visarjayitvā sa harīñ śūrāṃs tān kṛtakarmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Having dismissed those brave monkeys whose work was done,

children.text: mene kṛtārtham ātmānaṃ rāghavaṃ ca mahābalam ||
children.translated_text: he considered himself and mighty <s>Rāghava</s> to have attained their purpose.
Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> spoke to <s>Sugrīva</s>, of dreadful strength, the best of all monkeys,
a respectful speech, making him very glad:

children.text: kiṣkindhāyā viniṣkrāma yadi te saumya rocate ||
children.translated_text: Come out of <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, gentle one, if that pleases you.
Hearing that well-spoken word of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: sugrīvaḥ paramaprīto vākyam etad uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s>, exceedingly pleased, said this speech:

children.text: evaṃ bhavatu gacchāmaḥ stheyaṃ tvacchāsane mayā
children.translated_text: So be it; we shall go. I must abide by your command.

children.text: tam evam uktvā sugrīvo lakṣmaṇaṃ śubhalakṣmaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> of auspicious marks, <s>Sugrīva</s>

children.text: visarjayāmāsa tadā tārām anyāś ca yoṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: then dismissed <s>Tārā</s> and the other women.
"Come here," <s>Sugrīva</s> called out loudly to the best monkeys.

children.text: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā harayaḥ śīghram āyayuḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that word of his, the monkeys quickly came,
all with joined hollow palms, those who were fit to appear before women.
Then the king, with radiance like the sun, spoke to those who had arrived:
Set my palanquin ready quickly, monkeys.

children.text: śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tasya harayaḥ śīghravikramāḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing his command, the monkeys of swift valor
prepared a lovely palanquin.
Seeing that palanquin set ready, the lord of monkeys
said to <s>Saumitri</s>, "Mount quickly, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>."

children.text: ity uktvā kāñcanaṃ yānaṃ sugrīvaḥ sūryasaṃnibham
children.translated_text: Having said this, <s>Sugrīva</s> mounted the golden vehicle, bright as the sun,
together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and it was borne by great monkeys.
With a white parasol being held over his head,
and with white yak-tail fans being waved on every side,
and saluted by bards amid the sounds of conches and kettledrums,
<s>Sugrīva</s> went out, having attained unsurpassed royal splendor.
Surrounded by many hundreds of fierce monkeys with weapons in hand,

children.text: parikīrṇo yayau tatra yatra rāmo vyavasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he went there where <s>Rāma</s> was stationed.

children.text: sa taṃ deśam anuprāpya śreṣṭhaṃ rāmaniṣevitam
children.translated_text: Having reached that excellent place frequented by <s>Rāma</s>,
the greatly radiant one descended from the palanquin with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Then, approaching <s>Rāma</s>, he stood with joined palms;

children.text: kṛtāñjalau sthite tasmin vānarāś cabhavaṃs tathā ||
children.translated_text: when he stood with joined palms, the monkeys became the same way.

children.text: taṭākam iva tad dṛṣṭvā rāmaḥ kuḍmalapaṅkajam
children.translated_text: Seeing that great army of monkeys like a pond of lotuses in bud,

children.text: vānarāṇāṃ mahat sainyaṃ sugrīve prītimān abhūt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> became pleased with <s>Sugrīva</s>.

children.text: pādayoḥ patitaṃ mūrdhnā tam utthāpya harīśvaram
children.translated_text: When the lord of monkeys had fallen at his feet with his head, <s>Rāghava</s> raised him up
and embraced him with affection and high regard.
After embracing him, the righteous one then said, "Sit down."

children.text: taṃ niṣaṇṇaṃ tato dṛṣṭvā kṣitau rāmo 'bravīd vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, seeing him seated on the ground, <s>Rāma</s> spoke these words:

children.text: dharmam arthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca kāle yas tu niṣevate
children.translated_text: O hero, O best of monkeys, the king who always attends to <s>dharma</s> (duty), <s>artha</s> (advantage), and <s>kāma</s> (desire)

children.text: vibhajya satataṃ vīra sa rājā harisattama ||
children.translated_text: at the proper time, keeping them distinct, is truly a king.

children.text: hitvā dharmaṃ tathārthaṃ ca kāmaṃ yas tu niṣevate
children.translated_text: But he who abandons <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s> and pursues <s>kāma</s>

children.text: sa vṛkṣāgre yathā suptaḥ patitaḥ pratibudhyate ||
children.translated_text: is like one asleep at the top of a tree: only after falling does he awaken.

children.text: amitrāṇāṃ vadhe yukto mitrāṇāṃ saṃgrahe rataḥ
children.translated_text: A king intent on the destruction of enemies and devoted to gathering friends,
and enjoying the fruit of the three aims, is joined with <s>dharma</s>.
The time for undertaking action has now arrived, O destroyer of foes.

children.text: saṃcintyatāṃ hi piṅgeśa haribhiḥ saha mantribhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore deliberate, O lord of the tawny ones, together with the monkeys and your ministers.

children.text: evam uktas tu sugrīvo rāmaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Sugrīva</s> spoke these words to <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: pranaṣṭā śrīś ca kīrtiś ca kapirājyaṃ ca śāśvatam
children.translated_text: Lost prosperity, fame, and the lasting kingdom of the monkeys

children.text: tvatprasādān mahābāho punaḥ prāptam idaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: have now been regained by me through your favor, O mighty-armed one.

children.text: tava deva prasādācca bhrātuś ca jayatāṃ vara
children.translated_text: By your favor, lord, and by that of your brother, O best of the victorious,

children.text: kṛtaṃ na pratikuryād yaḥ puruṣāṇāṃ sa dūṣakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the man who would not repay a kindness done is a disgrace among men.
These foremost monkeys, O destroyer of foes, have arrived by the hundreds,
bringing with them all the powerful monkeys on the earth.

children.text: ṛkṣāś cāvahitāḥ śūrā golāṅgūlāś ca rāghava
children.translated_text: Bears too are attentive, O <s>Rāghava</s>, and brave golāṅgūlas as well,
terrifying to behold and familiar with inaccessible wildernesses, forests, and strongholds.
Monkeys who are sons of gods and gandharvas, able to assume forms at will,

children.text: svaiḥ svaiḥ parivṛtāḥ sainyair vartante pathi rāghava ||
children.translated_text: are on the road, O <s>Rāghava</s>, each surrounded by his own troops.

children.text: śataiḥ śatasahasraiś ca koṭibhiś ca plavaṃgamāḥ
children.translated_text: The leaping monkeys are accompanied by hundreds, hundreds of thousands, and crores,

children.text: ayutaiś cāvṛtā vīrāḥ śaṅkubhiś ca paraṃtapa ||
children.translated_text: and the heroes are surrounded by ayutas and by śaṅkus, O scorcher of foes.

children.text: arbudair arbudaśatair madhyaiś cāntaiś ca vānarāḥ
children.translated_text: The monkeys and monkey troop-lords come in arbudas, hundreds of arbudas, madhyas, and antas,

children.text: samudraiś ca parārdhaiś ca harayo hariyūthapāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and in samudras and parārdhas.
They will come to you, O king, with valor equal to <s>Mahendra</s>'s,
resembling <s>Meru</s> and <s>Mandara</s>, and dwelling in <s>Vindhya</s> and <s>Meru</s>.

children.text: te tvām abhigamiṣyanti rākṣasaṃ ye sabāndhavam
children.translated_text: They will come to you and attack the rākṣasa together with his kinsmen;

children.text: nihatya rāvaṇaṃ saṃkhye hy ānayiṣyanti maithilīm ||
children.translated_text: having slain <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle, they will bring back <s>Maithilī</s>.

children.text: tatas tam udyogam avekṣya buddhimān haripravīrasya nideśavartinaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, seeing that undertaking of the foremost monkey, who followed his command,
the wise prince, whose eyes were like opened blue lotuses, became filled with joy.

children.text: iti bruvāṇaṃ sugrīvaṃ rāmo dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: To <s>Sugrīva</s>, who was speaking thus, <s>Rāma</s>, best of upholders of dharma,
embraced him with both arms and replied as he stood with joined palms.

children.text: yad indro varṣate varṣaṃ na tac citraṃ bhaved bhuvi
children.translated_text: That <s>Indra</s> should rain rain is no wonder on earth,

children.text: ādityo vā sahasrāṃśuḥ kuryād vitimiraṃ nabhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor that the thousand-rayed sun should make the sky free of darkness,

children.text: candramā raśmibhiḥ kuryāt pṛthivīṃ saumya nirmalām
children.translated_text: nor that the moon should make the earth clear and gentle with its rays,
nor that one like you, O scorcher of foes, should repay his friends.

children.text: evaṃ tvayi na tac citraṃ bhaved yat saumya śobhanam
children.translated_text: Therefore, my gentle friend, whatever is noble in you would be no wonder.

children.text: jānāmy ahaṃ tvāṃ sugrīva satataṃ priyavādinam ||
children.translated_text: I know you, <s>Sugrīva</s>, to be ever one who speaks what is pleasing.

children.text: tvatsanāthaḥ sakhe saṃkhye jetāsmi sakalān arīn
children.translated_text: Having you as my protector, friend, I shall conquer all enemies in battle.

children.text: tvam eva me suhṛn mitraṃ sāhāyyaṃ kartum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: You alone are my well-wisher and friend; you ought to give me aid.
The vilest of rākṣasas carried off <s>Vaidehī</s> for his own destruction,

children.text: vañcayitvā tu paulomīm anuhlādo yathā śacīm ||
children.translated_text: just as <s>Anuhlāda</s> deceived <s>Paulomī</s>, <s>Śacī</s>.

children.text: nacirāt taṃ haniṣyāmi rāvaṇaṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
children.translated_text: Before long I shall slay that <s>Rāvaṇa</s> with sharp arrows,
as foe-slaying <s>Śatakratu</s> slew the arrogant father of <s>Paulomī</s>.
At that very moment a cloud of dust began to rise,

children.text: uṣṇāṃ tīvrāṃ sahasrāṃśoś chādayad gagane prabhām ||
children.translated_text: covering in the sky the hot, fierce radiance of the thousand-rayed sun.

children.text: diśaḥ paryākulāś cāsan rajasā tena mūrchitāḥ
children.translated_text: The quarters became confused, overwhelmed by that dust,
and the whole earth shook, together with its mountains, forests, and groves.
Then the entire earth was covered by countless leaping monkeys,
resembling great mountains, with sharp fangs and enormous strength.
In the mere interval of a blink, it was covered by those monkey troop-lords,
shape-shifters attended by retinues of hundreds of crores.

children.text: nādeyaiḥ pārvatīyaiś ca sāmudraiś ca mahābalaiḥ
children.translated_text: There were mighty monkeys from rivers, mountains, and the sea,
with cloudlike roars, and others that wandered in the forests.
There were monkeys of the color of the young sun, and others white as the moon,
others the color of lotus filaments, and white ones dwelling on <s>Meru</s>.
Then the splendid monkey named <s>Śatabali</s>, a hero,
was seen surrounded by ten thousand crores.
Then the valiant father of <s>Tārā</s>, shining like a golden mountain,
was seen with many tens of thousands of crores.
Resembling lotus filaments, with a face like the young sun,
wise <s>Kesarī</s>, the best of monkeys and foremost among all monkeys,
accompanied by many thousands of divisions of monkeys,
the glorious father of <s>Hanumat</s>, was seen.
<s>Gavākṣa</s>, the great king of the golāṅgūlas, of fearsome valor,
was seen surrounded by a thousand crores of monkeys.
<s>Dhūmra</s>, destroyer of foes among the bears of terrifying speed,
advanced surrounded by two thousand crores.
The troop-lord named <s>Panasa</s>, fearsome and like a great mountain,
came, possessed of great valor and surrounded by three crores.
Then the troop-lord named <s>Nīla</s>, like a mass of dark collyrium,
was seen, huge-bodied and surrounded by ten crores.
And mighty <s>Darīmukha</s>, a troop-lord, came near at that time;
surrounded by a thousand crores, he approached <s>Sugrīva</s>.

children.text: maindaś ca dvividaś cobhāv aśviputrau mahābalau
children.translated_text: Both <s>Mainda</s> and <s>Dvivida</s>, mighty sons of the <s>Aśvins</s>,
were seen with a thousand crore-crores of monkeys.
Then <s>Gandhamādana</s> arrived, followed from behind
by monkeys numbering a hundred thousand thousand-crores.
Then prince <s>Aṅgada</s>, surrounded by a thousand padmas and a hundred śaṅkus,
arrived, equal in valor to his father.
Then the monkey <s>Tāra</s>, brilliant as stars and of fearsome valor,
was seen from afar with five crores of monkeys.
The heroic monkey <s>Indrajānu</s>, a troop-leader, was seen,

children.text: ekādaśānāṃ koṭīnām īśvaras taiś ca saṃvṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: lord of eleven crores, surrounded by them.
Then <s>Rambha</s> arrived, resembling the young sun,

children.text: ayutena vṛtaś caiva sahasreṇa śatena ca ||
children.translated_text: attended by ten thousand, and also by a thousand and a hundred.

children.text: tato yūthapatir vīro durmukho nāma vānaraḥ
children.translated_text: Then a heroic troop-leader, a monkey named <s>Durmukha</s>,
mighty and surrounded by two crores, was seen.
With monkeys shaped like the peaks of <s>Kailāsa</s>, of fearsome valor,
<s>Hanumān</s> was seen, surrounded by a thousand crores.
And <s>Nala</s>, of great strength, attended by tree-dwellers,
arrived with a hundred crores, and with a thousand and a hundred.

children.text: śarabhaḥ kumudo vahnir vānaro rambha eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Śarabha</s>, <s>Kumuda</s>, <s>Vahni</s> the monkey, and <s>Rambha</s> as well,

children.text: ete cānye ca bahavo vānarāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: these and many other monkeys, able to assume forms at will,

children.text: āvṛtya pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ parvatāṃś ca vanāni ca
children.translated_text: covering the whole earth, and the mountains and forests too,

children.text: āplavantaḥ plavantaś ca garjantaś ca plavaṃgamāḥ
children.translated_text: leaping, springing, and roaring, those forest-ranging monkeys
came toward <s>Sugrīva</s> like masses of clouds toward the sun.
Making many loud cries, delighted and powerful,
they bowed their heads in submission to <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of monkeys.
Other foremost monkeys, having assembled as was proper,
met with <s>Sugrīva</s> and then stood with joined palms.

children.text: sugrīvas tvarito rāme sarvāṃs tān vānararṣabhān
children.translated_text: The righteous <s>Sugrīva</s>, hastening to <s>Rāma</s>, reported all those bull-like monkeys,
and, standing with joined palms, spoke.

children.text: yathā sukhaṃ parvatanirjhareṣu vaneṣu sarveṣu ca vānarendrāḥ
children.translated_text: After settling the forces duly and comfortably among the mountain streams

children.text: niveśayitvā vidhivad balāni balaṃ balajñaḥ pratipattum īṣṭe ||
children.translated_text: and in all the forests, he who knew the army wished to arrange the force.
Then king <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the forest-goers, whose purpose had prospered,
spoke to <s>Rāma</s>, tiger among men and crusher of enemy forces.
The strong monkey-lords, able to assume forms at will, have arrived and been encamped,
those who dwell in my realm and are equal in splendor to <s>Mahendra</s>.
These fearsome monkeys have come with many thousands
of forest-monkeys of terrible valor, resembling Daityas and Dānavas.
Their deeds and exploits are famous; they are strong and have conquered fatigue,
renowned in acts of courage and foremost in resolute efforts.
They move on earth and in water, O <s>Rāma</s>, and dwell on many mountains;

children.text: koṭyagraśa ime prāptā vānarās tava kiṃkarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: these monkeys, counted by crores, have arrived as your servants.
All follow command; all are devoted to the welfare of their superior;
they will be able to carry out what you desire, O subduer of foes.

children.text: yan manyase naravyāghra prāptakālaṃ tad ucyatām
children.translated_text: What you think timely, O tiger among men, let that be said.

children.text: tat sainyaṃ tvadvaśe yuktam ājñāpayitum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: That army is ready under your control; you should command it.

children.text: kāmam eṣām idaṃ kāryaṃ viditaṃ mama tattvataḥ
children.translated_text: Of course this task of theirs is known to me truly,

children.text: tathāpi tu yathā tattvam ājñāpayitum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: yet you should command according to the truth of the matter.
As <s>Sugrīva</s> spoke thus, <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>,
embraced him with both arms and said these words.

children.text: jñāyatāṃ saumya vaidehī yadi jīvati vā na vā
children.translated_text: Let it be learned, gentle one, whether <s>Vaidehī</s> lives or not,

children.text: sa ca deśo mahāprājña yasmin vasati rāvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also the land, wise one, in which <s>Rāvaṇa</s> dwells.

children.text: adhigamya ca vaidehīṃ nilayaṃ rāvaṇasya ca
children.translated_text: Having found <s>Vaidehī</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s dwelling,

children.text: prāptakālaṃ vidhāsyāmi tasmin kāle saha tvayā ||
children.translated_text: I shall take the timely action at that time together with you.

children.text: nāham asmin prabhuḥ kārye vānareśa na lakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: I am not the master in this matter, O lord of monkeys, nor is <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>;

children.text: tvam asya hetuḥ kāryasya prabhuś ca plavageśvara ||
children.translated_text: you are the cause of this undertaking and its master, O lord of the forest-goers.
You yourself, mighty one, command the decision concerning my task.

children.text: tvaṃ hi jānāsi yat kāryaṃ mama vīra na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For you know what is to be done for me, hero; there is no doubt.
Brave, wise, accompanied by friends, and knowing the proper moment,
you are devoted to our welfare, successful in your own purpose and best of those who know advantage.

children.text: evam uktas tu sugrīvo vinataṃ nāma yūthapam
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Sugrīva</s> spoke to the troop-leader named <s>Vinata</s>,
in the presence of <s>Rāma</s> and wise <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
that lord of forest-goers, like a mountain and rumbling like a cloud.
Together with monkeys born from <s>Soma</s> and <s>Sūrya</s>, O best of monkeys,
skilled in place, time, and policy, and in deciding what should and should not be done,
surrounded by a hundred thousand swift monkeys,
go to the eastern direction, with its mountains, woods, and groves.

children.text: tatra sītāṃ ca vaidehīṃ nilayaṃ rāvaṇasya ca
children.translated_text: There search for <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Vaidehī</s>, and for <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s dwelling,

children.text: mārgadhvaṃ giridurgeṣu vaneṣu ca nadīṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: in mountain fastnesses, forests, and rivers.

children.text: nadīṃ bhāgīrathīṃ ramyāṃ sarayūṃ kauśikīṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Search the lovely river <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>, the <s>Sarayū</s>, and likewise the <s>Kauśikī</s>,

children.text: kālindīṃ yamunāṃ ramyāṃ yāmunaṃ ca mahāgirim ||
children.translated_text: the lovely <s>Kālindī</s>, the <s>Yamunā</s>, and the great <s>Yāmuna</s> mountain,

children.text: sarasvatīṃ ca sindhuṃ ca śoṇaṃ maṇinibhodakam
children.translated_text: the <s>Sarasvatī</s>, the <s>Sindhu</s>, and the <s>Śoṇa</s> with jewel-like waters,
the <s>Mahī</s> and <s>Kālamahī</s> as well, adorned with mountains and forests.
Search the <s>Brahmamālas</s>, the <s>Videhas</s>, the <s>Mālavas</s>, and the <s>Kāśi-Kosalas</s>,

children.text: māgadhāṃś ca mahāgrāmān puṇḍrān vaṅgāṃs tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: the great villages of the <s>Māgadhas</s>, and the <s>Puṇḍras</s> and <s>Vaṅgas</s> as well,
the city of the cocoon-makers and the land that has silver mines;

children.text: sarvam etad vicetavyaṃ mṛgayadbhir tatas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: all this is to be searched everywhere by you as you hunt.
Search for <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Rāma</s>'s beloved wife and <s>Daśaratha</s>'s daughter-in-law,

children.text: samudram avagāḍhāṃś ca parvatān pattanāni ca ||
children.translated_text: and the mountains plunging into the sea and the cities.

children.text: mandarasya ca ye koṭiṃ saṃśritāḥ kecid āyatām
children.translated_text: And search those who have resorted to the long ridge of <s>Mandara</s>, whoever they are,
the <s>Karṇaprāvaraṇas</s>, and also the <s>Oṣṭhakarṇakas</s>,
the dreadful <s>Lohamukhas</s>, the swift one-footed people,
the inexhaustible and powerful men who are man-eaters,
the <s>Kirātas</s>, the <s>Karṇacūḍas</s>, and the golden-limbed, pleasant-looking people;
there are <s>Kirātas</s>, island-dwellers, who eat raw fish,
and dreadful creatures moving under the water, known as man-tigers.
O forest-dwellers, all the abodes of these are to be searched,

children.text: giribhir ye ca gamyante plavanena plavena ca
children.translated_text: and whatever places are reached over mountains, by leaping, and by boat.
Search jewel-rich <s>Yavadvīpa</s>, adorned by seven kingdoms,
and <s>Suvarṇarūpyaka</s>, adorned with mines of gold.
Beyond <s>Yavadvīpa</s> is a mountain named <s>Śiśira</s>;
with its peak it touches heaven, and is frequented by gods and dānavas.
In the mountain fastnesses, precipices, and forests of these places,

children.text: rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyas tatas tataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, together with <s>Vaidehī</s>, must be sought here and there.

children.text: tataḥ samudradvīpāṃś ca subhīmān draṣṭum arhatha ||
children.translated_text: Then you should inspect the very fearsome islands of the ocean.
There huge-bodied asuras constantly seize shadows;
permitted by <s>Brahmā</s>, they have been hungry for a long time.
Approaching that great ocean, resembling a dark cloud and frequented by great serpents,
that roaring great sea, only by a crossing-place,

children.text: tato raktajalaṃ bhīmaṃ lohitaṃ nāma sāgaram
children.translated_text: then, having gone on, you will see the terrible red-watered sea named <s>Lohita</s>.

children.text: gatā drakṣyatha tāṃ caiva bṛhatīṃ kūṭaśālmalīm ||
children.translated_text: There you will also see that great <s>Kūṭaśālmalī</s>,
and the house of <s>Vainateya</s>, adorned with many jewels.
There it stands like <s>Kailāsa</s>, fashioned by <s>Viśvakarman</s>.

children.text: tatra śailanibhā bhīmā mandehā nāma rākṣasāḥ
children.translated_text: There terrible rākṣasas named <s>Mandehas</s>, like mountains,
hang from the mountain peaks, of many forms and frightening.

children.text: te patanti jale nityaṃ sūryasyodayanaṃ prati
children.translated_text: They fall into the water every day at the rising of the sun,

children.text: abhitaptāś ca sūryeṇa lambante sma punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, scorched by the sun, they hang there again and again.
Then, having gone to the sea named <s>Kṣīroda</s>, white as a pale cloud,
O unconquerable ones, you will see it like a pearl necklace with its waves.

children.text: tasya madhye mahāśveta ṛṣabho nāma parvataḥ
children.translated_text: In its middle is a very white mountain named <s>Ṛṣabha</s>,

children.text: divyagandhaiḥ kusumitai rajataiś ca nagair vṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: surrounded by silver trees blossoming with divine fragrances.

children.text: saraś ca rājataiḥ padmair jvalitair hemakesaraiḥ
children.translated_text: There is also a lake with silver lotuses, blazing with golden filaments,
named <s>Sudarśana</s>, crowded with royal swans.
Gods, cāraṇas, yakṣas, kinnaras, together with hosts of apsarases,
joyfully come to that lotus lake, wishing to sport.
Having crossed <s>Kṣīroda</s>, O monkeys, you will then see
<s>Jaloda</s>, best of seas, terrifying to all beings.

children.text: tatra tat kopajaṃ tejaḥ kṛtaṃ hayamukhaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: There that fire born from wrath was made into a great horse-faced form.
They say that all moving and unmoving beings are the food of that mighty, swift one.
There the cry of beings dwelling in the ocean is heard,
the cry of helpless ones as they see that <s>Vaḍavāmukha</s>.
In the region north of the sweet-water sea, for thirteen yojanas,
there is a great golden mountain named <s>Jātarūpaśila</s>.
On the summit of that mountain sits the god <s>Ananta</s>, honored by all beings,
thousand-headed and clad in blue garments.

children.text: triśirāḥ kāñcanaḥ ketus tālas tasya mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: The golden, three-headed palm-banner of that great being
has been set on the mountain top and shines with its altar-platform.

children.text: pūrvasyāṃ diśi nirmāṇaṃ kṛtaṃ tat tridaśeśvaraiḥ
children.translated_text: That construction in the eastern direction was made by the lords of the Thirty.
Beyond that is the splendid golden <s>Udaya</s> mountain.

children.text: tasya koṭir divaṃ spṛṣṭvā śatayojanam āyatā
children.translated_text: Its summit, touching heaven and extending a hundred yojanas,
is divine, made of gold, and shines with an altar-platform.

children.text: sālais tālais tamālaiś ca karṇikāraiś ca puṣpitaiḥ
children.translated_text: With blossoming sālas, tālas, tamālas, and karṇikāras,
divine and made of gold, it shines like the sun.
There is a peak one yojana wide and ten yojanas high,
named <s>Saumanasa</s>, fixed and made of gold.

children.text: tatra pūrvaṃ padaṃ kṛtvā purā viṣṇus trivikrame
children.translated_text: There, in ancient times, <s>Viṣṇu</s> placed his first step in his <s>Trivikrama</s> stride,
and <s>Puruṣottama</s> placed the second on the summit of <s>Meru</s>.
Circling <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> from the north, the sun

children.text: dṛśyo bhavati bhūyiṣṭhaṃ śikharaṃ tan mahocchrayam ||
children.translated_text: becomes most visible upon that very lofty peak.
There the great sages named <s>Vaikhānasas</s>, the <s>Vālakhilyas</s>,
are seen shining, ascetics of the color of the sun.

children.text: ayaṃ sudarśano dvīpaḥ puro yasya prakāśate
children.translated_text: This is the island <s>Sudarśana</s>, before which it shines,

children.text: yasmiṃs tejaś ca cakṣuś ca sarvaprāṇabhṛtām api ||
children.translated_text: and in which are the radiance and sight of all living beings.

children.text: śailasya tasya kuñjeṣu kandareṣu vaneṣu ca
children.translated_text: In the groves, caves, and forests of that mountain,

children.text: rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyas tatas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, together with <s>Vaidehī</s>, must be sought here and there.

children.text: kāñcanasya ca śailasya sūryasya ca mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Filled with the brilliance of the golden mountain and of the great sun,

children.text: āviṣṭā tejasā saṃdhyā pūrvā raktā prakāśate ||
children.translated_text: the eastern twilight appears red and shining.

children.text: tataḥ paramagamyā syād dik pūrvā tridaśāvṛtā
children.translated_text: Beyond that, the eastern direction is impassable, enclosed by the gods,
without moon or sun, invisible, and covered with darkness.

children.text: śaileṣu teṣu sarveṣu kandareṣu vaneṣu ca
children.translated_text: On all those mountains, in their caves and forests,

children.text: ye ca noktā mayā deśā viceyā teṣu jānakī ||
children.translated_text: and in regions not mentioned by me, <s>Jānakī</s> must be searched for.
So far, O foremost monkeys, it is possible for monkeys to go;

children.text: abhāskaram amaryādaṃ na jānīmas tataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: beyond that sunless, limitless region we do not know.

children.text: adhigamya tu vaidehīṃ nilayaṃ rāvaṇasya ca
children.translated_text: But after finding <s>Vaidehī</s> and the dwelling of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: māse pūrṇe nivartadhvam udayaṃ prāpya parvatam ||
children.translated_text: return when the month is complete, after reaching <s>Udaya</s> mountain.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ māsān na vastavyaṃ vasan vadhyo bhaven mama
children.translated_text: You must not stay beyond a month; if one stays, he will be liable to death from me.
Having accomplished your purpose and found <s>Maithilī</s>, return.

children.text: mahendrakāntāṃ vanaṣaṇḍamaṇḍitāṃ diśaṃ caritvā nipuṇena vānarāḥ
children.translated_text: O monkeys, after carefully traversing the direction beloved of <s>Mahendra</s> and adorned with forest thickets,

children.text: avāpya sītāṃ raghuvaṃśajapriyāṃ tato nivṛttāḥ sukhino bhaviṣyatha ||
children.translated_text: and after obtaining <s>Sītā</s>, beloved of the descendant of <s>Raghu</s>, then you will return happy.

children.text: tataḥ prasthāpya sugrīvas tan mahad vānaraṃ balam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sugrīva</s>, having dispatched that great monkey force,
sent chosen monkeys toward the southern direction:

children.text: nīlam agnisutaṃ caiva hanumantaṃ ca vānaram
children.translated_text: <s>Nīla</s>, the son of <s>Agni</s>, and the monkey <s>Hanumat</s>.
and <s>Jāmbavān</s>, son of the grandsire, the great monkey,

children.text: suhotraṃ ca śarāriṃ ca śaragulmaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: and <s>Suhotra</s>, <s>Śarāri</s>, and also <s>Śaragulma</s>,

children.text: gajaṃ gavākṣaṃ gavayaṃ suṣeṇam ṛṣabhaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gaja</s>, <s>Gavākṣa</s>, <s>Gavaya</s>, <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, and likewise <s>Ṛṣabha</s>,

children.text: maindaṃ ca dvividaṃ caiva vijayaṃ gandhamādanam
children.translated_text: and <s>Mainda</s> and <s>Dvivida</s>, <s>Vijaya</s>, and <s>Gandhamādana</s>,
<s>Ulkāmukha</s> and <s>Asaṅga</s>, both sons of <s>Hutāśana</s>,
and the heroes headed by <s>Aṅgada</s>: that heroic lord of the monkey troops,
who knew distinctions, appointed them, endowed with speed and valor.

children.text: teṣām agresaraṃ caiva mahad balam asaṅgagam
children.translated_text: Having arranged a great force of heroic monkeys, impassable and going in front of them,
he directed them toward the southern quarter.

children.text: ye kecana samuddeśās tasyāṃ diśi sudurgamāḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever regions in that direction were very difficult to reach,

children.text: kapīśaḥ kapimukhyānāṃ sa teṣāṃ tān udāharat ||
children.translated_text: that lord of monkeys described all those places to the foremost monkeys.
Look over the thousand-peaked <s>Vindhya</s>, covered with many trees and creepers,
and the hard-to-cross river <s>Narmadā</s>, frequented by great serpents.
Then look over the lovely <s>Godāvarī</s>, the great river <s>Kṛṣṇaveṇī</s>,
and the greatly blessed <s>Varadā</s>, frequented by great serpents.
Look over the <s>Mekhalas</s>, the <s>Utkalas</s>, and the cities of the <s>Daśārṇas</s>,
and <s>Avantī</s> and <s>Abhravantī</s>, all of them without exception.

children.text: vidarbhān ṛṣikāṃś caiva ramyān māhiṣakān api
children.translated_text: Look over the <s>Vidarbhas</s>, the <s>Ṛṣikas</s>, and the delightful <s>Māhiṣakas</s> too,

children.text: tathā vaṅgān kaliṅgāṃś ca kauśikāṃś ca samantataḥ ||
children.translated_text: as well as the <s>Vaṅgas</s>, the <s>Kaliṅgas</s>, and the <s>Kauśikas</s> on every side.
After examining <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest, with its mountains, rivers, and caves,
look over the river <s>Godāvarī</s> too, all of it without exception.

children.text: tathaivāndhrāṃś ca puṇḍrāṃś ca colān pāṇḍyān sakeralān
children.translated_text: Likewise, the <s>Andhras</s>, the <s>Puṇḍras</s>, the <s>Colas</s>, the <s>Pāṇḍyas</s>, and the <s>Keralas</s>,
and <s>Ayomukha</s> mountain, adorned with minerals, must be reached.
That splendid great mountain, with varied peaks and forests bright with many flowers,
with regions of sandalwood groves, must be searched.

children.text: tatas tām āpagāṃ divyāṃ prasannasalilāṃ śivām
children.translated_text: Then there you will see the divine river, auspicious and with clear waters,
the <s>Kāverī</s>, enjoyed by hosts of apsarases.
On the summit of <s>Malaya</s> mountain you will see seated there
the most excellent seer <s>Agastya</s>, of great splendor, shining like the sun.
Then, with the permission of that gracious great-souled one,
you will cross the great river <s>Tāmraparṇī</s>, haunted by crocodiles.
Hidden by divine sandalwood forests and rich in islands,
she enters the sea like a loving young woman approaching her beloved.
Then, when you have gone on, O monkeys, you will see the divine golden gate of the <s>Pāṇḍyas</s>,

children.text: yuktaṃ kavāṭaṃ pāṇḍyānāṃ gatā drakṣyatha vānarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: adorned with pearls and jewels and fitted with doors.
Then, having reached the sea and determined your objective with certainty,
there in the ocean, set in place within it by <s>Agastya</s>,
stands splendid <s>Mahendra</s>, best of mountains, with many kinds of marvelous trees,
glorious, made of gold, and plunging into the great ocean.
It is beautified by blooming trees of many kinds and by creepers,
and frequented by eminent divine seers and yakṣas, and by apsarases.
Scattered with hosts of siddhas and cāraṇas, it is exceedingly charming;

children.text: tam upaiti sahasrākṣaḥ sadā parvasu parvasu ||
children.translated_text: the thousand-eyed one, <s>Indra</s>, visits it always on each sacred day.
Beyond it, on the far shore, is an island one hundred yojanas long,

children.text: agamyo mānuṣair dīptas taṃ mārgadhvaṃ samantataḥ
children.translated_text: inaccessible to men and radiant; search it on every side.
There <s>Sītā</s> must be sought especially, with your whole being.

children.text: sa hi deśas tu vadhyasya rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: For that land is the dwelling of the wicked <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, who is to be slain,
lord of the rākṣasas, equal in brilliance to <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: dakṣiṇasya samudrasya madhye tasya tu rākṣasī
children.translated_text: In the middle of that southern sea is a rākṣasī
well known as <s>Aṅgārakā</s>, who seizes a shadow and feeds on it.
Having passed beyond her, in the sea at a distance of one hundred yojanas,
there is a mountain named <s>Puṣpitaka</s>, prosperous and frequented by siddhas and cāraṇas.
Shining like the rays of the moon and sun and surrounded by ocean waters,

children.text: bhrājate vipulaiḥ śṛṅgair ambaraṃ vilikhann iva ||
children.translated_text: it gleams with broad peaks, as if scratching the sky.

children.text: tasyaikaṃ kāñcanaṃ śṛṅgaṃ sevate yaṃ divākaraḥ
children.translated_text: One golden peak of it is attended by the maker of day, the sun,

children.text: śvetaṃ rājatam ekaṃ ca sevate yaṃ niśākaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and one white silver peak is attended by the maker of night, the moon.

children.text: na taṃ kṛtaghnāḥ paśyanti na nṛśaṃsā na nāstikāḥ
children.translated_text: The ungrateful do not see it, nor the cruel, nor the atheists;

children.text: praṇamya śirasā śailaṃ taṃ vimārgata vānarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: bowing your heads to that mountain, search it, O monkeys.

children.text: tam atikramya durdharṣāḥ sūryavān nāma parvataḥ
children.translated_text: Having passed beyond it, O unassailable ones, there is a mountain named <s>Sūryavān</s>,
fourteen yojanas away along a road hard to traverse.

children.text: tatas tam apy atikramya vaidyuto nāma parvataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, having passed beyond that also, there is a mountain named <s>Vaidyuta</s>,
with trees bearing every desirable fruit and charming in every season.

children.text: tatra bhuktvā varārhāṇi mūlāni ca phalāni ca
children.translated_text: There, after eating excellent roots and fruits

children.text: madhūni pītvā mukhyāni paraṃ gacchata vānarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and drinking the best kinds of honey, go onward, O monkeys.
There is a mountain named <s>Kuñjara</s>, pleasing to the eye and mind,
where <s>Agastya</s>'s dwelling was built by <s>Viśvakarman</s>.
There is a divine golden refuge one yojana wide
and ten yojanas high, adorned with many jewels.

children.text: tatra bhogavatī nāma sarpāṇām ālayaḥ purī
children.translated_text: There is a city named <s>Bhogavatī</s>, abode of the serpents,
with broad roads, unassailable, and protected on every side,
guarded by fearsome serpents with sharp fangs and deadly poison.
In it dwells the exceedingly fearsome serpent-king <s>Vāsuki</s>;

children.text: niryāya mārgitavyā ca sā ca bhogavatī purī ||
children.translated_text: you must go forth and search that city <s>Bhogavatī</s> too.

children.text: taṃ ca deśam atikramya mahān ṛṣabhasaṃsthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Having passed beyond that region, there stands the great, splendid, jewel-made mountain,
named <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, fixed in the form of a bull.

children.text: gośīrṣakaṃ padmakaṃ ca hariśyāmaṃ ca candanam
children.translated_text: There divine sandalwood is produced: <s>gośīrṣaka</s>, <s>padmaka</s>,
and <s>hariśyāma</s>, and it has the brilliance of fire.

children.text: na tu tac candanaṃ dṛṣṭvā spraṣṭavyaṃ ca kadācana
children.translated_text: But that sandalwood, when seen, must never be touched.

children.text: rohitā nāma gandharvā ghorā rakṣanti tad vanam ||
children.translated_text: Fearsome gandharvas named <s>Rohitā</s> guard that forest.
There the lords of the gandharvas, shining like five suns,

children.text: śailūṣo grāmaṇīr bhikṣuḥ śubhro babhrus tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śailūṣa</s>, <s>Grāmaṇī</s>, <s>Bhikṣu</s>, <s>Śubhra</s>, and likewise <s>Babhru</s>,

children.text: ante pṛthivyā durdharṣās tatra svargajitaḥ sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: stand there at the end of the earth, hard to assail, conquerors of heaven.

children.text: tataḥ paraṃ na vaḥ sevyaḥ pitṛlokaḥ sudāruṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Beyond that you must not resort to the very terrible <s>Pitṛloka</s>.
This is the capital of <s>Yama</s>, painfully enveloped in darkness.
Only so far, heroes and foremost monkeys,

children.text: śakyaṃ vicetuṃ gantuṃ vā nāto gatimatāṃ gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: is it possible for you to search or to go; beyond this there is no course for beings that move.

children.text: sarvam etat samālokya yac cānyad api dṛśyate
children.translated_text: Having surveyed all this, and whatever else is seen,
and having learned the whereabouts of <s>Vaidehī</s>, you should return.

children.text: yas tu māsān nivṛtto 'gre dṛṣṭā sīteti vakṣyati
children.translated_text: But whoever, returning first within the month, says, '<s>Sītā</s> has been seen,'
he will enjoy himself happily with wealth and pleasures equal to mine.

children.text: tataḥ priyataro nāsti mama prāṇād viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: There is no one dearer to me than he, dearer especially than my own life.
Even if he has offended me many times, he will be my kinsman.

children.text: amitabalaparākramā bhavanto vipulaguṇeṣu kuleṣu ca prasūtāḥ
children.translated_text: You are endowed with immeasurable strength and valor, and born in families rich in great qualities.

children.text: manujapatisutāṃ yathā labhadhvaṃ tad adhiguṇaṃ puruṣārtham ārabhadhvam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore undertake a surpassing human purpose, so that you may find the daughter of the lord of men.

children.text: tataḥ prasthāpya sugrīvas tān harīn dakṣiṇāṃ diśam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sugrīva</s>, having dispatched those monkeys to the southern direction,
monkeys endowed with intelligence and courage and equal in straight speed to the wind,
then the great-splendored king summoned a troop-leader named <s>Suṣeṇa</s>,
the father of <s>Tārā</s>, his father-in-law, of formidable prowess.

children.text: abravīt prāñjalir vākyam abhigamya praṇamya ca
children.translated_text: Approaching, bowing, and standing with joined palms, he spoke these words:
Give assistance to <s>Rāma</s> in this task that has arisen.
Surrounded by one hundred thousand swift monkeys,

children.text: abhigaccha diśaṃ saumya paścimāṃ vāruṇīṃ prabho ||
children.translated_text: go, gentle lord, to the western direction, the direction of <s>Varuṇa</s>, O master.

children.text: surāṣṭrān saha vāhlīkāñ śūrābhīrāṃs tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Search the <s>Surāṣṭras</s> together with the <s>Vāhlīkas</s>, and likewise the <s>Śūras</s> and <s>Ābhīras</s>,
prosperous and charming countries, and broad cities too.
Search <s>Kukṣi</s>, dense with puṃnāga trees and crowded with many uddālakas,
and likewise the thickets of ketaka, O leaders of monkey troops.

children.text: pratyak srotogamāś caiva nadyaḥ śītajalāḥ śivāḥ
children.translated_text: Search also the rivers flowing westward, with cool and auspicious waters,

children.text: tāpasānām araṇyāni kāntārā girayaś ca ye ||
children.translated_text: the forests of ascetics, the wildernesses, and whatever mountains there are.
Having searched the difficult western direction covered with networks of mountains,

children.text: tataḥ paścimam āsādya samudraṃ draṣṭum arhatha
children.translated_text: then, having reached the western ocean, you should look upon it,
O monkeys, its waters filled with timis and makaras, and impossible to disturb.
Then among the thickets of ketaka and the dense groves of tamāla,
and also in the coconut forests, the monkeys will range.

children.text: tatra sītāṃ ca mārgadhvaṃ nilayaṃ rāvaṇasya ca
children.translated_text: There search for <s>Sītā</s> and for the dwelling of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
and for <s>Marīcipattana</s> too, and charming <s>Jaṭīpura</s>.

children.text: avantīm aṅgalopāṃ ca tathā cālakṣitaṃ vanam
children.translated_text: Search <s>Avantī</s> and <s>Aṅgalopā</s>, and also the unmarked forest,

children.text: rāṣṭrāṇi ca viśālāni pattanāni tatas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the extensive kingdoms and towns, one after another.
There, at the confluence of the <s>Sindhu</s> and the ocean, is a mountain;
a great golden mountain named <s>Hemagiri</s>, with a hundred peaks and great trees.

children.text: tasya prastheṣu ramyeṣu siṃhāḥ pakṣagamāḥ sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: On its pleasant plateaus dwell lions that move by wing.
They carry timi fish and sea-elephants into their nests.

children.text: tāni nīḍāni siṃhānāṃ giriśṛṅgagatāś ca ye
children.translated_text: The nests of those lions are set upon the mountain peaks,
and proud, well-fed elephants, resounding with the sound of rain clouds,
roam over this vast place, filled with water on every side.
Its sky-touching golden peak, with variegated trees,
must all be searched quickly by monkeys who can assume forms at will.

children.text: koṭiṃ tatra samudre tu kāñcanīṃ śatayojanām
children.translated_text: There in the ocean you will see a golden shore one hundred yojanas long,
hard to behold, when you have gone to <s>Pāriyātra</s>, O monkeys.
There dwell twenty-four crores of swift gandharvas,
fire-like, fearsome, and able to assume forms at will.
They must not be approached too closely by monkeys of formidable prowess,

children.text: nādeyaṃ ca phalaṃ tasmād deśāt kiṃcit plavaṃgamaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and no fruit or anything at all should be taken by the leapers from that land.

children.text: durāsadā hi te vīrāḥ sattvavanto mahābalāḥ
children.translated_text: For those heroes are hard to approach, spirited, and very strong.
There, of terrifying prowess, they guard the fruits and roots.

children.text: tatra yatnaś ca kartavyo mārgitavyā ca jānakī
children.translated_text: There effort must be made, and <s>Jānakī</s> must be searched for.

children.text: na hi tebhyo bhayaṃ kiṃcit kapitvam anuvartatām ||
children.translated_text: For there is no fear at all from them for those who keep to monkey conduct.
In a quarter of the ocean is a mountain named <s>Cakravān</s>.
There a wheel with a thousand spokes was fashioned by <s>Viśvakarman</s>.

children.text: tatra pañcajanaṃ hatvā hayagrīvaṃ ca dānavam
children.translated_text: There, after killing <s>Pañcajana</s> and the dānava <s>Hayagrīva</s>,

children.text: ājahāra tataś cakraṃ śaṅkhaṃ ca puruṣottamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the Supreme Person then carried off the discus and the conch.

children.text: tasya sānuṣu citreṣu viśālāsu guhāsu ca
children.translated_text: On its variegated slopes and in its broad caves,

children.text: rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyas tatas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, together with <s>Vaidehī</s>, must be searched for everywhere.
At sixty-four yojanas is a mountain named <s>Varāha</s>,
beautiful, with a golden peak, in the unfathomable abode of <s>Varuṇa</s>.
There is a city named <s>Prāgjyotiṣa</s>, made of gold,

children.text: yasmin vasti duṣṭātmā narako nāma guhāsu ca ||
children.translated_text: in which, and in the caves, dwells the wicked-hearted one named <s>Naraka</s>.

children.text: tasya sānuṣu citreṣu viśālāsu guhāsu ca
children.translated_text: On its variegated slopes and in its broad caves,

children.text: rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyas tatas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, together with <s>Vaidehī</s>, must be searched for everywhere.
Having passed beyond that lord of mountains, there is a mountain with golden inner clefts,
entirely golden and endowed with streams and waterfalls.

children.text: taṃ gajāś ca varāhāś ca siṃhā vyāghrāś ca sarvataḥ
children.translated_text: Elephants, boars, lions, and tigers on every side
roar continually at it, made proud by that sound.
On it is glorious <s>Mahendra</s>, chastiser of <s>Pāka</s>, whose steeds are tawny.

children.text: abhiṣiktaḥ surai rājā meghavān nāma parvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the mountain named <s>Meghavān</s>, consecrated as king by the gods.
Having passed beyond that lord of mountains, protected by <s>Mahendra</s>,
you will go to sixty thousand golden mountains,
colored like the young sun and shining on every side,
adorned with trees made of gold and covered with fine blossoms.

children.text: teṣāṃ madhye sthito rājā merur uttamaparvataḥ
children.translated_text: In the midst of them stands the king, <s>Meru</s>, the highest mountain.
Long ago that mountain received a boon from gracious <s>Āditya</s>.

children.text: tenaivam uktaḥ śailendraḥ sarva eva tvadāśrayāḥ
children.translated_text: That lord of mountains was addressed by him thus: "All who take refuge in you

children.text: matprasādād bhaviṣyanti divā rātrau ca kāñcanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: will, by my favor, be golden by day and by night.
And the gods, gandharvas, and dānavas who dwell upon you

children.text: te bhaviṣyanti raktāś ca prabhayā kāñcanaprabhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: will become ruddy, with a radiance like gold."

children.text: ādityā vasavo rudrā marutaś ca divaukasaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Vasus</s>, <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Maruts</s>, and the heaven-dwellers,
having come to <s>Meru</s>, the highest mountain, at the western twilight,
attend upon <s>Āditya</s>; and honored by them, the sun
goes to the setting mountain, invisible to all beings.
The maker of day traverses those ten thousand yojanas
and quickly reaches that rocky peak within half a muhūrta.

children.text: śṛṅge tasya mahad divyaṃ bhavanaṃ sūryasaṃnibham
children.translated_text: On its summit is a great divine mansion, like the sun,
crowded with excellent palaces, fashioned by <s>Viśvakarman</s>,
adorned with variegated trees and filled with many kinds of birds:
the dwelling of great-souled <s>Varuṇa</s>, who holds the noose in his hand.

children.text: antarā merum astaṃ ca tālo daśaśirā mahān
children.translated_text: Between <s>Meru</s> and <s>Asta</s> stands a great ten-headed palm tree,
splendid, made of gold, shining with a variegated altar.

children.text: teṣu sarveṣu durgeṣu saraḥsu ca saritsu ca
children.translated_text: In all those inaccessible places, in lakes and in rivers,

children.text: rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyas tatas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, together with <s>Vaidehī</s>, must be sought here and there.

children.text: yatra tiṣṭhati dharmātmā tapasā svena bhāvitaḥ
children.translated_text: Where the righteous one dwells, perfected by his own ascetic power,

children.text: merusāvarṇir ity eva khyāto vai brahmaṇā samaḥ ||
children.translated_text: known precisely as <s>Merusāvarṇi</s>, equal to <s>Brahmā</s>,
that great seer <s>Merusāvarṇi</s>, radiant like the sun, should be questioned,

children.text: praṇamya śirasā bhūmau pravṛttiṃ maithilīṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: after bowing with your heads to the ground, about news of <s>Maithilī</s>.
So far extends the world of living beings: at the end of night the sun,

children.text: kṛtvā vitimiraṃ sarvam astaṃ gacchati parvatam ||
children.translated_text: having made everything free of darkness, goes to the setting mountain.
Only so far, O chief monkeys, can the monkeys go;

children.text: abhāskaram amaryādaṃ na jānīmas tataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: beyond that, where there is no sun and no boundary, we do not know.

children.text: adhigamya tu vaidehīṃ nilayaṃ rāvaṇasya ca
children.translated_text: After discovering <s>Vaidehī</s> and the dwelling of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: astaṃ parvatam āsādya pūrṇe māse nivartata ||
children.translated_text: reach <s>Asta</s> mountain and return when the month is complete.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ māsān na vastavyaṃ vasan vadhyo bhaven mama
children.translated_text: You must not stay beyond a month; if anyone stays, he will be liable to death at my hands.

children.text: sahaiva śūro yuṣmābhiḥ śvaśuro me gamiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: The heroic one who is my father-in-law will go together with you.
All of his instructions must be listened to by you, who carry out orders.

children.text: gurur eṣa mahābāhuḥ śvaśuro me mahābalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This mighty-armed, very powerful one is my respected elder and my father-in-law.
You too are valiant and are competent in every task;

children.text: pramāṇam enaṃ saṃsthāpya paśyadhvaṃ paścimāṃ diśam ||
children.translated_text: having set him as the authority, inspect the western quarter.
When the wife of the immeasurably splendid king has been seen,
we shall have accomplished our purpose by repaying what has been done for us.

children.text: ato 'nyad api yat kiṃcit kāryasyāsya hitaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: And whatever else would be beneficial for this undertaking
should be considered by you in relation to place, time, and purpose.

children.text: tataḥ suṣeṇapramukhāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ sugrīvavākyaṃ nipuṇaṃ niśamya
children.translated_text: Then the monkeys led by <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, having carefully heard <s>Sugrīva</s>'s speech,

children.text: āmantrya sarve plavagādhipaṃ te jagmur diśaṃ tāṃ varuṇābhiguptām ||
children.translated_text: took leave of the lord of monkeys and all went to that quarter guarded by <s>Varuṇa</s>.

children.text: tataḥ saṃdiśya sugrīvaḥ śvaśuraṃ paścimāṃ diśam
children.translated_text: Then, after dispatching his father-in-law to the western quarter, <s>Sugrīva</s>,
the bull among monkeys, addressed a heroic monkey named <s>Śatabali</s>.
The king, knower of counsel, spoke a speech

children.text: vākyam ātmahitaṃ caiva rāmasya ca hitaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: for his own good and also for the good of <s>Rāma</s>, approved by all the monkeys.
Surrounded by a hundred thousand forest-dwellers like yourself,
together with the sons of <s>Vaivasvata</s> and your own ministers, set out.
Search thoroughly the mighty northern quarter, crowned by the snowy mountain,
in every direction for the blameless wife of <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: asmin kārye vinivṛtte kṛte dāśaratheḥ priye
children.translated_text: When this task has been accomplished and what is dear to <s>Dāśarathi</s> has been done,
we shall be freed from debt, O foremost of those who understand fulfilled aims.

children.text: kṛtaṃ hi priyam asmākaṃ rāghaveṇa mahātmanā
children.translated_text: For a dear service has been done for us by great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>;
