children.text: tasya cet pratikāro 'sti saphalaṃ jīvitaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: if there is recompense for him, life will become fruitful.

children.text: etāṃ buddhiṃ samāsthāya dṛśyate jānakī yathā
children.translated_text: Adopting this resolve, in whatever way <s>Jānakī</s> may be seen,
that is what you, desiring our welfare and what is dear to us, must do.

children.text: ayaṃ hi sarvabhūtānāṃ mānyas tu narasattamaḥ
children.translated_text: For this best of men is worthy of honor from all beings,
<s>Rāma</s>, conqueror of hostile cities, who has come to love us.
These forest fastnesses, rivers, and mountain interiors
you must search through with the wealth of your intelligence and valor.

children.text: tatra mlecchān pulindāṃś ca śūrasenāṃs tathāiva ca
children.translated_text: There search among the <s>Mlecchas</s>, <s>Pulindas</s>, and <s>Śūrasenas</s>,

children.text: prasthālān bharatāṃś caiva kurūṃś ca saha madrakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and among the <s>Prasthalas</s>, <s>Bharatas</s>, and <s>Kurus</s>, together with the <s>Madrakas</s>;

children.text: kāmbojān yavanāṃś caiva śakān āraṭṭakān api
children.translated_text: among the <s>Kāmbojas</s>, <s>Yavanas</s>, <s>Śakas</s>, and also the <s>Āraṭṭakas</s>,

children.text: vāhlīkān ṛṣikāṃś caiva pauravān atha ṭaṅkaṇān ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Vāhlīkas</s>, <s>Ṛṣikas</s>, <s>Pauravas</s>, and then the <s>Ṭaṅkaṇas</s>;

children.text: cīnān paramacīnāṃś ca nīhārāṃś ca punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: and among the <s>Cīnas</s>, <s>Paramacīnas</s>, and <s>Nīhāras</s>, again and again.
Having searched also the <s>Daradas</s>, investigate <s>Himavant</s>.
In groves of lodhra and padmaka trees and in forests of devadāru,

children.text: rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyas tatas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, together with <s>Vaidehī</s>, must be sought here and there.
Then, having gone to <s>Somāśrama</s>, frequented by gods and gandharvas,

children.text: kālaṃ nāma mahāsānuṃ parvataṃ taṃ gamiṣyatha ||
children.translated_text: you will go to that mountain with the great summit, named <s>Kāla</s>.

children.text: mahatsu tasya śṛṅgeṣu nirdareṣu guhāsu ca
children.translated_text: On its great peaks, in clefts and in caves,
search for the greatly fortunate, renowned wife of <s>Rāma</s>.
Having crossed that lord of mountains, the great mountain <s>Hemavarga</s>,

children.text: tataḥ sudarśanaṃ nāma parvataṃ gantum arhatha ||
children.translated_text: then you should go to the mountain named <s>Sudarśana</s>.
In its forest thickets, clefts, and caves,

children.text: rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyas tatas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s> with <s>Vaidehī</s> must then be sought everywhere.
Having crossed that, there is open space for one hundred yojanas on every side,
without mountains, rivers, or trees, and devoid of all living creatures.

children.text: taṃ tu śīghram atikramya kāntāraṃ romaharṣaṇam
children.translated_text: But quickly crossing that wilderness which makes the hair stand on end,

children.text: kailāsaṃ pāṇḍuraṃ śailaṃ prāpya hṛṣṭā bhaviṣyatha ||
children.translated_text: you will reach the white mountain <s>Kailāsa</s> and will be delighted.
There, resembling a white cloud and adorned with jāmbūnada gold,
is the divine palace of <s>Kubera</s>, built by <s>Viśvakarman</s>.
There is a broad lotus pond, rich in lotuses and blue water-lilies,
filled with haṃsas and kāraṇḍavas, and attended by hosts of apsarases.
There King <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, honored by all beings,

children.text: dhanado ramate śrīmān guhyakaiḥ saha yakṣarāṭ ||
children.translated_text: the splendid <s>Dhanada</s>, lord of yakṣas, delights together with the guhyakas.
In its moonlike mountains and in its caves,

children.text: rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyas tatas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s> with <s>Vaidehī</s> must then be sought everywhere.

children.text: krauñcaṃ tu girim āsādya bilaṃ tasya sudurgamam
children.translated_text: Then, reaching Mount <s>Krauñca</s>, its opening, extremely hard to approach,

children.text: apramattaiḥ praveṣṭavyaṃ duṣpraveśaṃ hi tat smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: must be entered by the vigilant; for it is known as difficult to enter.
For great-souled beings dwell there, equal to the sun in splendor,

children.text: devair apy arcitāḥ samyag devarūpā maharṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: great seers of godlike form, properly worshiped even by the gods.

children.text: krauñcasya tu guhāś cānyāḥ sānūni śikharāṇi ca
children.translated_text: And the other caves of <s>Krauñca</s>, its plateaus and peaks,

children.text: nirdarāś ca nitambāś ca vicetavyās tatas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: its clefts and slopes must be searched everywhere.

children.text: krauñcasya śikharaṃ cāpi nirīkṣya ca tatas tataḥ
children.translated_text: And after inspecting here and there the peak of <s>Krauñca</s>,
also the treeless <s>Kāmaśaila</s> and <s>Mānasa</s>, abode of birds,
there is no access there for beings, gods, dānavas, or rākṣasas;
and that mountain, with its ridges and tablelands, must all be searched.

children.text: krauñcaṃ girim atikramya maināko nāma parvataḥ
children.translated_text: After crossing Mount <s>Krauñca</s>, there is a mountain named <s>Maināka</s>;

children.text: mayasya bhavanaṃ tatra dānavasya svayaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: there stands the dwelling of the dānava <s>Maya</s>, made by himself.
<s>Maināka</s> must be searched, with its ridges, tablelands, and caves;

children.text: strīṇām aśvamukhīnāṃ ca niketās tatra tatra tu ||
children.translated_text: here and there are the dwellings of horse-faced women.
Having passed beyond that region, there is a hermitage attended by siddhas;

children.text: siddhā vaikhānasās tatra vālakhilyāś ca tāpasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: there dwell perfected <s>Vaikhānasa</s>s and <s>Vālakhilya</s> ascetics.

children.text: vandyās te tu tapaḥsiddhās tāpasā vītakalmaṣāḥ
children.translated_text: Those ascetics, perfected by austerity and free from stain, are to be honored,
and, with humility, they should also be asked for news of <s>Sītā</s>.
There is a <s>Vaikhānasa</s> lake covered with golden lotuses,
traversed by auspicious haṃsas resembling the young sun.
<s>Kubera</s>'s riding elephant is remembered as <s>Sārvabhauma</s>;

children.text: gajaḥ paryeti taṃ deśaṃ sadā saha kareṇubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: that elephant always roams that region together with she-elephants.
Having passed beyond that lake, there is a sky where moon and sun have disappeared,
without any host of stars, cloudless, and without beginning.

children.text: gabhastibhir ivārkasya sa tu deśaḥ prakāśate
children.translated_text: Yet that region is illuminated as if by the rays of the sun,
by ascetics perfected through tapas, resting there, godlike and self-luminous.

children.text: taṃ tu deśam atikramya śailodā nāma nimnagā
children.translated_text: Having crossed that region, there is a river named <s>Śailodā</s>,

children.text: ubhayos tīrayor yasyāḥ kīcakā nāma veṇavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: on both of whose banks grow bamboos called kīcakas.

children.text: te nayanti paraṃ tīraṃ siddhān pratyānayanti ca
children.translated_text: They carry the siddhas to the far bank and bring them back again;
there are the <s>Uttara Kurus</s>, radiant with the reward of merit they have earned.
There, by lotus pools filled with golden lotuses,
thousands of rivers are rich with leaves of blue beryl.
And here, adorned with forests of red lotuses and golden growths,
the reservoirs shine there like the young sun.
With priceless jewel-leaves and golden, shining filaments,
that region is surrounded on every side by variegated groves of blue lotuses.

children.text: nistulābhiś ca muktābhir maṇibhiś ca mahādhanaiḥ
children.translated_text: There, with incomparable pearls and precious gems,
the rivers have raised sandbanks made of gold.
They are thick with excellent variegated trees made of every jewel,
and also with trees made of gold, shining like blazing fire.
Here trees, ever bearing flowers and fruit and crowded with birds,
have divine fragrance, taste, and touch, and pour forth every desired thing.
Some excellent trees bear garments of many forms as fruit,
and likewise ornaments variegated with pearls and beryl,

children.text: strīṇāṃ yāny anurūpāṇi puruṣāṇāṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: such as are suitable for women and likewise for men;
other excellent trees bear comforts enjoyable in every season.
Other excellent trees bring forth costly, variegated, golden
beds furnished with richly patterned coverlets.
Other trees here bear garlands pleasing to the mind,

children.text: pānāni ca mahārhāṇi bhakṣyāṇi vividhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: and costly drinks and various foods.
There are women endowed with virtues, marked by beauty and youth;

children.text: gandharvāḥ kiṃnarāḥ siddhā nāgā vidyādharās tathā
children.translated_text: and gandharvas, kinnaras, siddhas, nāgas, and vidyādharas,
bright as the sun, sport there together with those women.
All have performed meritorious deeds; all are devoted to pleasure;
all possess their desired aims and live together with women.
The sound of song and instruments, with the ringing sound of loud laughter,
is heard there constantly, charming to all beings.

children.text: tatra nāmuditaḥ kaścin nāsti kaścid asatpriyaḥ
children.translated_text: There no one is unhappy, and no one is disagreeable.

children.text: ahany ahani vardhante guṇās tatra manoramāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, day after day, delightful excellences increase.

children.text: samatikramya taṃ deśam uttaras payasāṃ nidhiḥ
children.translated_text: Having passed beyond that region, there is the northern ocean,

children.text: tatra somagirir nāma madhye hemamayo mahān ||
children.translated_text: and in its middle is a great golden mountain named <s>Somagiri</s>.

children.text: indralokagatā ye ca brahmalokagatāś ca ye
children.translated_text: Those who have gone to the world of <s>Indra</s>, and those who have gone to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: devās taṃ samavekṣante girirājaṃ divaṃ gatam ||
children.translated_text: the gods behold that king of mountains, reaching up to heaven.

children.text: sa tu deśo visūryo 'pi tasya bhāsā prakāśate
children.translated_text: That region, though without the sun, is illumined by its radiance;
it may be recognized by the splendor of the sun, as if by the blazing sun itself.
There too dwells the blessed <s>Śambhu</s>, the soul of the universe, eleven-formed,
and <s>Brahmā</s>, lord of the gods, surrounded by brahmarṣis.

children.text: na kathaṃcana gantavyaṃ kurūṇām uttareṇa vaḥ
children.translated_text: You must on no account go beyond the northern <s>Kurus</s>;

children.text: anyeṣām api bhūtānāṃ nātikrāmati vai gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the course of other beings too does not pass beyond there.

children.text: sa hi somagirir nāma devānām api durgamaḥ
children.translated_text: For that mountain named <s>Somagiri</s> is hard to reach even for the gods.

children.text: tam ālokya tataḥ kṣipram upāvartitum arhatha ||
children.translated_text: After seeing it, therefore, you should quickly turn back.
So far, O foremost monkeys, can be reached by monkeys.

children.text: abhāskaram amaryādaṃ na jānīmas tataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: Beyond that sunless, limitless region we do not know what lies.

children.text: sarvam etad vicetavyaṃ yan mayā parikīrtitam
children.translated_text: All this that I have described must be searched,

children.text: yad anyad api noktaṃ ca tatrāpi kriyatāṃ matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and whatever else has not been mentioned, apply your minds to that also.

children.text: tataḥ kṛtaṃ dāśarather mahat priyaṃ mahattaraṃ cāpi tato mama priyam
children.translated_text: Then a great service will have been done for <s>Dāśarathi</s>, and a still greater favor, dear to me,

children.text: kṛtaṃ bhaviṣyaty anilānalopamā videhajā darśanajena karmaṇā ||
children.translated_text: will have been accomplished, O you who are like wind and fire, through the act born from seeing the daughter of <s>Videha</s>.

children.text: tataḥ kṛtārthāḥ sahitāḥ sabāndhavā mayārcitāḥ sarvaguṇair manoramaiḥ
children.translated_text: Then, having achieved your purpose, together with your kinsmen, honored by me with every delightful excellence,
you will roam the earth with your enemies pacified and with your beloveds, O earth-ranging monkeys.
But <s>Sugrīva</s> spoke especially with reference to <s>Hanumān</s>;
for in that best of monkeys he was certain of success in accomplishing the task.

children.text: na bhūmau nāntarikṣe vā nāmbare nāmarālaye
children.translated_text: On earth, in midair, in the sky, or in the abode of the immortals,

children.text: nāpsu vā gatisaṃgaṃ te paśyāmi haripuṃgava ||
children.translated_text: or in the waters, I see no obstruction to your movement, O foremost monkey.
All worlds, with asuras, with gandharvas, with nāgas, men, and gods,
together with their oceans and mountains, are known to you.

children.text: gatir vegaś ca tejaś ca lāghavaṃ ca mahākape
children.translated_text: Your power, speed, brilliance, and lightness, O great monkey,

children.text: pitus te sadṛśaṃ vīra mārutasya mahaujasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: are like those of your father, the mighty <s>Māruta</s>, O hero.

children.text: tejasā vāpi te bhūtaṃ samaṃ bhuvi na vidyate
children.translated_text: No being equal to you in brilliance is found on earth.

children.text: tad yathā labhyate sītā tattvam evopapādaya ||
children.translated_text: Therefore devise exactly how <s>Sītā</s> may be found.

children.text: tvayy eva hanumann asti balaṃ buddhiḥ parākramaḥ
children.translated_text: In you alone, O <s>Hanumān</s>, are strength, intelligence, and valor,
and policy suited to place and time, O master of policy.
Then, perceiving the attachment of the task to <s>Hanumān</s>,
and knowing <s>Hanumān</s>, <s>Rāghava</s> reflected.
In every way this lord of monkeys is certain of success through <s>Hanumān</s>,
and <s>Hanumān</s> is even more certain to accomplish the task.
Since he is setting out in this way, recognized through his deeds,
and accepted by his lord, the arising of the fruit of the task is certain.
Seeing that very energetic monkey, whose highest quality was resolve,
he became as if his object were already accomplished, with senses and mind delighted.
Then, pleased, the scorcher of foes gave him
as a token for the princess a signet ring adorned with his own name.
By this sign, O best of monkeys, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>
will look upon you without anxiety as one who has come from my presence.

children.text: vyavasāyaś ca te vīra sattvayuktaś ca vikramaḥ
children.translated_text: Your resolve, O hero, and your valor joined with courage,

children.text: sugrīvasya ca saṃdeśaḥ siddhiṃ kathayatīva me ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Sugrīva</s>'s command seem to proclaim success to me.

children.text: sa tad gṛhya hariśreṣṭhaḥ sthāpya mūrdhni kṛtāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: Taking it, that best of monkeys placed it on his head with joined palms,
bowed to his feet, and the best of leapers set out.

children.text: sa tat prakarṣan hariṇāṃ balaṃ mahad babhūva vīraḥ pavanātmajaḥ kapiḥ
children.translated_text: That heroic monkey, son of the wind, drawing forward the great army of monkeys,
shone like the moon in the cloudless sky, its disk pure and adorned by hosts of stars.

children.text: atibala balam āśritas tavāhaṃ harivaravikrama vikramair analpaiḥ
children.translated_text: O exceedingly strong one, I rely on your strength; O you whose valor is that of the best of monkeys, on your ample acts of valor.

children.text: pavanasuta yathābhigamyate sā janakasutā hanumaṃs tathā kuruṣva ||
children.translated_text: O son of the wind, O <s>Hanumān</s>, act so that the daughter of <s>Janaka</s> may be reached.
Then, understanding the severe command of their master, the foremost monkeys
set out, covering the earth like locusts.
<s>Rāma</s> stayed on that <s>Prasravaṇa</s> together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: pratīkṣamāṇas taṃ māsaṃ yaḥ sītādhigame kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: waiting for that month which had been fixed for the finding of <s>Sītā</s>.
Toward the lovely northern direction, surrounded by kings of mountains,

children.text: pratasthe sahasā vīro hariḥ śatabalis tadā ||
children.translated_text: the heroic monkey <s>Śatabali</s> set out at once.

children.text: pūrvāṃ diśaṃ prati yayau vinato hariyūthapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The monkey troop-leader <s>Vinata</s> went toward the eastern direction.
The leaper, the son of the wind, accompanied by <s>Tārā</s>, <s>Aṅgada</s>, and the others,
as monkey troop-leader, went toward the southern quarter traversed by <s>Agastya</s>.

children.text: paścimāṃ tu diśaṃ ghorāṃ suṣeṇaḥ plavageśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, lord of leapers, that tiger among monkeys, set out
toward the dreadful western direction, strongly guarded by <s>Varuṇa</s>.

children.text: tataḥ sarvā diśo rājā codayitvā yathātatham
children.translated_text: Then, after the king had duly urged on all the directions
and the chief commanders of the monkey army, he rejoiced happily and at ease.
Thus urged on by the king, all the monkey troop-leaders,

children.text: svāṃ svāṃ diśam abhipretya tvaritāḥ sampratasthire ||
children.translated_text: aiming at their own respective directions, quickly set out.

children.text: nadantaś connadantaś ca garjantaś ca plavaṃgamāḥ
children.translated_text: Roaring, bellowing, and thundering, the leapers,
shouting and running, the best of leapers went forth,
saying, "We shall bring back <s>Sītā</s>, and we shall slay <s>Rāvaṇa</s>."

children.text: aham eko haniṣyāmi prāptaṃ rāvaṇam āhave
children.translated_text: "I alone will slay <s>Rāvaṇa</s> when he comes to battle;
then, having crushed him at once, I shall carry off the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>."
You are trembling from fatigue today; remain here, all of you.
I alone will bring <s>Jānakī</s>, even from <s>Pātāla</s>.

children.text: vidhamiṣyāmy ahaṃ vṛkṣān dārayiṣyāmy ahaṃ girīn
children.translated_text: I will shatter the trees; I will split the mountains.
I will tear open the earth and churn up the oceans.
I can leap a distance counted in yojanas; there is no doubt about it here.

children.text: śataṃ yojanasaṃkhyāyāḥ śataṃ samadhikaṃ hy aham ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, I can leap a hundred yojanas, even more than a hundred.

children.text: bhūtale sāgare vāpi śaileṣu ca vaneṣu ca
children.translated_text: On the surface of the earth, in the ocean, on mountains, and in forests,

children.text: pātālasyāpi vā madhye na mamāchidyate gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: or even in the middle of <s>Pātāla</s>, my course cannot be cut off.

children.text: ity ekaikaṃ tadā tatra vānarā baladarpitāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus each one there then, the monkeys proud of their strength,

children.text: ūcuś ca vacanaṃ tasmin harirājasya saṃnidhau ||
children.translated_text: spoke words in the presence of that king of monkeys.
When the monkey-lords had gone, <s>Rāma</s> said to <s>Sugrīva</s>,

children.text: kathaṃ bhavān vijānīte sarvaṃ vai maṇḍalaṃ bhuvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "How do you know the whole circle of the earth?"

children.text: sugrīvas tu tato rāmam uvāca praṇatātmavān
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sugrīva</s>, humbly disposed, said to <s>Rāma</s>,
"Listen; I will tell everything at length, O bull among men.

children.text: yadā tu dundubhiṃ nāma dānavaṃ mahiṣākṛtim
children.translated_text: When <s>Vālī</s> was driving the dānava named <s>Dundubhi</s>, who had the form of a buffalo,
toward Mount <s>Malaya</s>,

children.text: tadā viveśa mahiṣo malayasya guhāṃ prati
children.translated_text: then the buffalo entered a cave of <s>Malaya</s>,
and <s>Vālī</s> entered <s>Malaya</s> there too, wishing to kill him.
Then I was left there at the cave-mouth, obediently keeping watch,

children.text: na ca niṣkramate vālī tadā saṃvatsare gate ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Vālī</s> did not come out, even when a year had passed.
Then the cave was filled with a rush of blood,
and seeing that, I was amazed and tormented by grief for my brother.

children.text: athāhaṃ kṛtabuddhis tu suvyaktaṃ nihato guruḥ
children.translated_text: Then I made up my mind: clearly my elder had been slain.
A rock like a mountain was placed by me at the cave door,
so that, unable to come out, the buffalo would perish.

children.text: tato 'ham āgāṃ kiṣkindhāṃ nirāśas tasya jīvite
children.translated_text: Then I came to <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, despairing of his life.

children.text: rājyaṃ ca sumahat prāptaṃ tārā ca rumayā saha
children.translated_text: The great kingdom came to me, and <s>Tārā</s> together with <s>Rumā</s>,

children.text: mitraiś ca sahitas tatra vasāmi vigatajvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, joined by friends, I lived there free from distress.

children.text: ājagāma tato vālī hatvā taṃ dānavarṣabham
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vālī</s> came back, having killed that bull among dānavas.
Then, from respect and constrained by fear, I gave back the kingdom.

children.text: sa māṃ jighāṃsur duṣṭātmā vālī pravyathitendriyaḥ
children.translated_text: But wicked-souled <s>Vālī</s>, wishing to kill me, his senses agitated,
drove me out in anger as I fled with my ministers.
Then I was pursued by that <s>Vālī</s> together with my followers,

children.text: nadīś ca vividhāḥ paśyan vanāni nagarāṇi ca ||
children.translated_text: while seeing various rivers, forests, and cities.
Then the earth was seen by me like the surface of a mirror,
like a whirling firebrand, and at that time like a cow's hoofprint.

children.text: tataḥ pūrvam ahaṃ gatvā dakṣiṇām aham āśritaḥ
children.translated_text: Then I went east and took refuge in the south;

children.text: diśaṃ ca paścimāṃ bhūyo gato 'smi bhayaśaṅkitaḥ
children.translated_text: again I went to the western quarter, fearful,

children.text: uttarāṃ tu diśaṃ yāntaṃ hanumān mām athābravīt ||
children.translated_text: and as I was going toward the northern quarter, <s>Hanumān</s> then said to me:

children.text: idānīṃ me smṛtaṃ rājan yathā vālī harīśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: "Now I remember, O king, how <s>Vālī</s>, lord of monkeys,

children.text: mataṃgena tadā śapto hy asminn āśramamaṇḍale ||
children.translated_text: was then cursed by <s>Mataṅga</s> in this hermitage district.

children.text: praviśed yadi vā vālī mūrdhāsya śatadhā bhavet
children.translated_text: If <s>Vālī</s> should enter here, his head would split into a hundred pieces;
our dwelling here will be pleasant and free from anxiety."
Then, having reached Mount <s>Ṛśyamūka</s>, O prince,

children.text: na viveśa tadā vālī mataṃgasya bhayāt tadā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vālī</s> did not enter then, because of fear of <s>Mataṅga</s>.

children.text: evaṃ mayā tadā rājan pratyakṣam upalakṣitam
children.translated_text: Thus, O king, I then directly observed

children.text: pṛthivīmaṇḍalaṃ kṛtsnaṃ guhām asmy āgatas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the entire circle of the earth; after that I came to the cave.
For the purpose of seeing <s>Vaidehī</s>, the monkey troop-leaders on every side,
appointed by the monkey-king, went swiftly as instructed.

children.text: sarāṃsi saritaḥ kakṣān ākāśaṃ nagarāṇi ca
children.translated_text: Lakes, rivers, thickets, the sky, and cities,
river-forts as well as mountains, they searched all around.
All the monkey troop-leaders searched the regions
described by <s>Sugrīva</s>, with their mountains, woods, and forests.
Searching through the day, all resolute in finding <s>Sītā</s>,
the monkeys would come together on the earth at night.

children.text: sarvartukāṃś ca deśeṣu vānarāḥ saphalān drumān
children.translated_text: In those regions the monkeys came upon fruitful trees of every season,

children.text: āsādya rajanīṃ śayyāṃ cakruḥ sarveṣv ahaḥsu te ||
children.translated_text: and on all those days they made their beds for the night.

children.text: tad ahaḥ prathamaṃ kṛtvā māse prasravaṇaṃ gatāḥ
children.translated_text: Counting that day as the first, after a month they went to <s>Prasravaṇa</s>,
and the monkey troop-leaders met the monkey-king in despair.

children.text: vicitya tu diśaṃ pūrvāṃ yathoktāṃ sacivaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Having searched the eastern quarter as instructed, together with his counselors,
mighty <s>Vinata</s> returned without having seen <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: uttarāṃ tu diśaṃ sarvāṃ vicitya sa mahākapiḥ
children.translated_text: Having searched the whole northern quarter, that great monkey,

children.text: āgataḥ saha sainyena vīraḥ śatabalis tadā ||
children.translated_text: the hero <s>Śatabali</s>, then came back with his army.

children.text: suṣeṇaḥ paścimām āśāṃ vicitya saha vānaraiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, having searched the western region together with the monkeys,
came back when the month was complete and approached <s>Sugrīva</s>.
Having reached him stationed on the summit of <s>Prasravaṇa</s> and saluted him,

children.text: āsīnaṃ saha rāmeṇa sugrīvam idam abruvan ||
children.translated_text: they spoke these words to <s>Sugrīva</s>, seated with <s>Rāma</s>:

children.text: vicitāḥ parvatāḥ sarve vanāni nagarāṇi ca
children.translated_text: "All mountains have been searched, and forests and cities,

children.text: nimnagāḥ sāgarāntāś ca sarve janapadās tathā ||
children.translated_text: rivers down to the oceans, and all inhabited lands as well.

children.text: guhāś ca vicitāḥ sarvā yās tvayā parikīrtitāḥ
children.translated_text: All the caves that you named have been searched,
and great thickets thickly covered with spreading creepers have been searched.

children.text: gahaneṣu ca deśeṣu durgeṣu viṣameṣu ca
children.translated_text: In dense regions, in inaccessible and uneven places,
creatures of enormous size have been searched out and killed,

children.text: ye caiva gahanā deśā vicitās te punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the difficult regions have been searched again and again.

children.text: udārasattvābhijano mahātmā sa maithilīṃ drakṣyati vānarendraḥ
children.translated_text: That great-souled monkey-lord, of noble courage and birth, will see <s>Maithilī</s>;

children.text: diśaṃ tu yām eva gatā tu sītā tām āsthito vāyusuto hanūmān ||
children.translated_text: for the very direction in which <s>Sītā</s> went has been taken by <s>Hanumān</s>, son of the Wind.

children.text: saha tārāṅgadābhyāṃ tu gatvā sa hanumān kapiḥ
children.translated_text: That monkey <s>Hanumān</s> went together with <s>Tārā</s> and <s>Aṅgada</s>.
He proceeded to the region just as it had been pointed out by <s>Sugrīva</s>.

children.text: sa tu dūram upāgamya sarvais taiḥ kapisattamaiḥ
children.translated_text: But after going a long distance with all those excellent monkeys,

children.text: vicinoti sma vindhyasya guhāś ca gahanāni ca ||
children.translated_text: he searched the caves and dense thickets of <s>Vindhya</s>.
They searched mountain peaks, river-fortresses, broad lakes, and trees,
various clusters of trees and mountains thick with dense woods.

children.text: anveṣamāṇās te sarve vānarāḥ sarvato diśam
children.translated_text: As all those monkeys searched in every direction,

children.text: na sītāṃ dadṛśur vīrā maithilīṃ janakātmajām ||
children.translated_text: the heroes did not see <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Maithilī</s>, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>.

children.text: te bhakṣayanto mūlāni phalāni vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: Eating roots and various fruits,

children.text: anveṣamāṇā durdharṣā nyavasaṃs tatra tatra ha
children.translated_text: those hard-to-subdue ones stayed here and there while searching.

children.text: sa tu deśo duranveṣo guhāgahanavān mahān ||
children.translated_text: But that region was hard to search, great, and full of caves and thickets.

children.text: tyaktvā tu taṃ tadā deśaṃ sarve vai hariyūthapāḥ
children.translated_text: Then all the monkey troop-leaders abandoned that region,
and, fearless on every side, entered another region difficult to assail.
There the trees bore barren fruit, had no flowers, and were stripped of leaves;

children.text: nistoyāḥ sarito yatra mūlaṃ yatra sudurlabham ||
children.translated_text: there the rivers were without water, and roots were very hard to find.

children.text: na santi mahiṣā yatra na mṛgā na ca hastinaḥ
children.translated_text: There were no buffaloes there, no deer, and no elephants,

children.text: śārdūlāḥ pakṣiṇo vāpi ye cānye vanagocarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor tigers or birds, nor any other creatures that range the forest.
There were lotus ponds on the ground with glossy leaves and blooming lotuses,

children.text: prekṣaṇīyāḥ sugandhāś ca bhramaraiś cāpi varjitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: beautiful to look at and fragrant, yet devoid even of bees.
A greatly fortunate sage named <s>Kaṇḍu</s>, truthful in speech and rich in austerity,
was a great seer, intensely wrathful and unassailable by reason of his restraints.

children.text: tasya tasmin vane putro bālako daśavārṣikaḥ
children.translated_text: In that forest his son, a boy ten years old,
had perished, reaching the end of his life; and the great sage became angry there.

children.text: tena dharmātmanā śaptaṃ kṛtsnaṃ tatra mahad vanam
children.translated_text: By that righteous man the whole great forest there was cursed,
made shelterless, hard to approach, and devoid of beasts and birds.

children.text: tasya te kānanāntāṃs tu girīṇāṃ kandarāṇi ca
children.translated_text: With concentrated minds they searched the edges of that forest,
the caves of the mountains, and the sources of the rivers.
But even there those high-souled ones did not see the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,
nor <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, her abductor, those doers of what was dear to <s>Sugrīva</s>.

children.text: te praviśya tu taṃ bhīmaṃ latāgulmasamāvṛtam
children.translated_text: Then, entering that dreadful place covered with creepers and shrubs,
they saw a cruel-working asura, fearless of the gods.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā vanarā ghoraṃ sthitaṃ śailam ivāparam
children.translated_text: Seeing that dreadful one standing like another mountain,

children.text: gāḍhaṃ parihitāḥ sarve dṛṣṭvā taṃ parvatopamam ||
children.translated_text: all the monkeys pressed tightly together when they saw that mountain-like being.

children.text: so 'pi tān vānarān sarvān naṣṭāḥ sthety abravīd balī
children.translated_text: That powerful one too said to all those monkeys, 'You are lost,'
and rushed upon them in anger, raising his clenched fist.
As he suddenly came charging on, <s>Aṅgada</s>, the son of <s>Vāli</s>, then
thinking, 'This is <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,' struck him with his palm.
Struck by the son of <s>Vāli</s>, vomiting blood from his mouth,

children.text: asuro nyapatad bhūmau paryasta iva parvataḥ
children.translated_text: the asura fell to the ground like an overturned mountain.

children.text: te tu tasmin nirucchvāse vānarā jitakāśinaḥ
children.translated_text: When he had stopped breathing, the monkeys, appearing victorious,

children.text: vyacinvan prāyaśas tatra sarvaṃ tad girigahvaram ||
children.translated_text: searched almost all that mountain cave there.

children.text: vicitaṃ tu tataḥ kṛtvā sarve te kānanaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: After completing that search, all of them again
entered another dreadful mountain cave in the forest.

children.text: te vicintya punaḥ khinnā viniṣpatya samāgatāḥ
children.translated_text: Having searched again, weary, they came out and gathered together,
and in a solitary place they sat at the root of a tree, dejected in mind.

children.text: athāṅgadas tadā sarvān vānarān idam abravīt
children.translated_text: Then <s>Aṅgada</s> spoke these words to all the monkeys,
the very wise one, exhausted, gently consoling them with speech:

children.text: vanāni girayo nadyo durgāṇi gahanāni ca
children.translated_text: 'Forests, mountains, rivers, strongholds, and thickets,

children.text: daryo giriguhāś caiva vicitā naḥ samantataḥ ||
children.translated_text: caves and mountain caverns have been searched by us on every side.

children.text: tatra tatra sahāsmābhir jānakī na ca dṛśyate
children.translated_text: Here and there, together with us, <s>Jānakī</s> is still not seen,

children.text: tad vā rakṣo hṛtā yena sītā surasutopamā ||
children.translated_text: nor is that demon by whom <s>Sītā</s>, like a daughter of the gods, was carried off.

children.text: kālaś ca no mahān yātaḥ sugrīvaś cograśāsanaḥ
children.translated_text: A long time has passed for us, and <s>Sugrīva</s> is fierce in command.
Therefore let you all together search on every side.

children.text: vihāya tandrīṃ śokaṃ ca nidrāṃ caiva samutthitām
children.translated_text: Abandoning lassitude, grief, and the sleep that has arisen,
search so that we may see <s>Sītā</s>, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>.

children.text: anirvedaṃ ca dākṣyaṃ ca manasaś cāparājayam
children.translated_text: Freedom from despondency, skill, and the mind's undefeated state

children.text: kāryasiddhikarāṇy āhus tasmād etad bravīmy aham ||
children.translated_text: are said to bring about success in a task; therefore I say this.
Even now, let the forest-dwellers search this difficult forest;

children.text: khedaṃ tyaktvā punaḥ sarvaṃ vanam etad vicīyatām ||
children.translated_text: giving up weariness, let this whole forest be searched again.
For an action that is being carried out, its fruit is surely seen.

children.text: alaṃ nirvedam āgamya na hi no malinaṃ kṣamam ||
children.translated_text: Enough of falling into despair; such dejection is not fitting for us.

children.text: sugrīvaḥ krodhano rājā tīkṣṇadaṇḍaś ca vānarāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s> is an irascible king and sharp in punishment, O monkeys;

children.text: bhetavyaṃ tasya satataṃ rāmasya ca mahātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he is always to be feared, and so too is great-souled <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: hitārtham etad uktaṃ vaḥ kriyatāṃ yadi rocate
children.translated_text: This has been said for your good; let it be done, if it pleases you,

children.text: ucyatāṃ vā kṣamaṃ yan naḥ sarveṣām eva vānarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: or else say what is suitable for all of us, O monkeys.'
Hearing <s>Aṅgada</s>'s speech, <s>Gandhamādana</s>
spoke in a faint voice, worn out by thirst and fatigue:

children.text: sadṛśaṃ khalu vo vākyam aṅgado yad uvāca ha
children.translated_text: 'The speech that <s>Aṅgada</s> has spoken is indeed fitting for you,

children.text: hitaṃ caivānukūlaṃ ca kriyatām asya bhāṣitam ||
children.translated_text: beneficial and favorable; let what he has said be done.

children.text: punar mārgāmahe śailān kandarāṃś ca darīs tathā
children.translated_text: Let us again search the mountains, the mountain caves, and the caverns,
the empty forests and the mountain streams as well.
Let all the forests that have been pointed out by great-souled <s>Sugrīva</s>
and all the mountain fastnesses be searched thoroughly by everyone.'

children.text: tataḥ samutthāya punar vānarās te mahābalāḥ
children.translated_text: Then those very strong monkeys rose up again
and wandered through the southern direction, filled with the forests of <s>Vindhya</s>.
Then the monkeys climbed a splendid silver mountain, resembling an autumn cloud,
possessing peaks and caves.
There they searched the lovely grove of lodhra trees and the forests of saptaparṇa trees,
the foremost monkeys longing for the sight of <s>Sītā</s>.
Having climbed its summit, those broad-striding heroes were weary,

children.text: na paśyanti sma vaidehīṃ rāmasya mahiṣīṃ priyām ||
children.translated_text: and they did not see <s>Vaidehī</s>, the beloved queen of <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: te tu dṛṣṭigataṃ kṛtvā taṃ śailaṃ bahukandaram
children.translated_text: Having taken in with their eyes that mountain full of many caves,
the monkeys descended, looking all around.
Then, having come down to the ground, exhausted and faint in spirit,
they stood there for a moment and then took shelter at the root of a tree.
After they had rested for a while and their fatigue was somewhat broken,

children.text: punar evodyatāḥ kṛtsnāṃ mārgituṃ dakṣiṇāṃ diśam ||
children.translated_text: they again set themselves to search the whole southern direction.
Those bulls among leapers, with <s>Hanumān</s> at their head, set out,

children.text: vindhyam evāditas tāvad vicerus te samantataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and first of all they ranged all around the <s>Vindhya</s> itself.

children.text: saha tārāṅgadābhyāṃ tu saṃgamya hanumān kapiḥ
children.translated_text: Together with <s>Tāra</s> and <s>Aṅgada</s>, <s>Hanumān</s> the monkey assembled with them,

children.text: vicinoti sma vindhyasya guhāś ca gahanāni ca ||
children.translated_text: and he searched the caves and the dense places of the <s>Vindhya</s>.

children.text: siṃhaśārdūlajuṣṭāś ca guhāś ca paritas tathā
children.translated_text: They searched also the caves frequented by lions and tigers all around,
and the difficult places of that lord of mountains, with its great cascades.

children.text: teṣāṃ tatraiva vasatāṃ sa kālo vyatyavartata ||
children.translated_text: While they were dwelling right there, that appointed time passed by for them.

children.text: sa hi deśo duranveṣo guhāgahanavān mahān
children.translated_text: For that country was hard to search, vast, and full of dense caves;

children.text: tatra vāyusutaḥ sarvaṃ vicinoti sma parvatam ||
children.translated_text: there the son of the wind searched the whole mountain.
Separated from one another, yet not far from each other,
were <s>Gaja</s>, <s>Gavākṣa</s>, <s>Gavaya</s>, <s>Śarabha</s>, and <s>Gandhamādana</s>,

children.text: maindaś ca dvividaś caiva hanumāñ jāmbavān api
children.translated_text: and <s>Mainda</s> and <s>Dvivida</s>, and also <s>Hanumān</s> and <s>Jāmbavān</s>,

children.text: aṅgado yuvarājaś ca tāraś ca vanagocaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Aṅgada</s> the crown prince, and <s>Tāra</s>, the forest-roaming monkey.
After searching the southern direction, in regions covered with networks of mountains,
afflicted by hunger and thirst, weary, and seeking water,
they saw a great cavern overgrown with creepers and trees.

children.text: tataḥ krauñcāś ca haṃsāś ca sārasāś cāpi niṣkraman
children.translated_text: Then curlews, swans, and cranes came out from it,
and cakravāka birds, wet with water and their bodies reddened by lotus pollen.

children.text: tatas tad bilam āsādya sugandhi duratikramam
children.translated_text: Then, reaching that fragrant and impassable cavern,
the bulls among monkeys became filled with amazement in their minds.
Those best of leapers, seized by suspicion about that cavern,
approached it joyfully, radiant and very strong.
Then <s>Hanumān</s>, son of <s>Māruta</s>, like a mountain peak,
skilled in wilderness and forest, spoke to all the monkeys:
Having searched the southern direction in regions covered with mountain ranges,

children.text: vayaṃ sarve pariśrāntā na ca paśyāmi maithilīm ||
children.translated_text: we are all exhausted, and I do not see <s>Maithilī</s>.

children.text: asmāccāpi bilāddhaṃsāḥ krauñcāś ca saha sārasaiḥ
children.translated_text: Yet from this cavern swans and curlews, together with cranes,

children.text: jalārdrāś cakravākāś ca niṣpatanti sma sarvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and cakravāka birds wet with water are flying out on every side.

children.text: nūnaṃ salilavān atra kūpo vā yadi vā hradaḥ
children.translated_text: Surely there is water here, either a well or perhaps a lake;

children.text: tathā ceme biladvāre snigdhās tiṣṭhanti pādapāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and likewise these trees stand luxuriant at the mouth of the cavern.

children.text: ity uktās tad bilaṃ sarve viviśus timirāvṛtam
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, all the monkeys entered that cavern covered with darkness,
moonless and sunless, and saw it to be hair-raising.
Then, in that inaccessible cavern, crowded with many kinds of trees,
embracing one another, they went a distance of a yojana.
Their senses lost, thirsty, bewildered, and seeking water,

children.text: paripetur bile tasmin kaṃcit kālam atandritāḥ ||
children.translated_text: they wandered in that cavern for some time without growing slack.
Those heroic leaping monkeys, emaciated, with dejected faces and worn out,

children.text: ālokaṃ dadṛśur vīrā nirāśā jīvite tadā ||
children.translated_text: then saw light, though they had despaired of life.

children.text: tatas taṃ deśam āgamya saumyaṃ vitimiraṃ vanam
children.translated_text: Then, reaching that pleasant, darkness-free region, a forest,
they saw golden trees shining with the radiance of blazing fire,

children.text: sālāṃs tālāṃś ca puṃnāgān kakubhān vañjulān dhavān
children.translated_text: sāla trees, palms, puṃnāgas, kakubhas, vañjulas, dhavas,

children.text: campakān nāgavṛkṣāṃś ca karṇikārāṃś ca puṣpitān ||
children.translated_text: campakas, nāga trees, and flowering karṇikāras,
resembling the young sun and set with platforms made of vaiḍūrya gems,
and lotus ponds, blue like vaiḍūrya, filled with birds.
They saw lotus ponds there, filled with clear water, surrounded by great golden trees
like the young sun, with large fish made of gold and with great turtles,
lotus ponds there endowed with clear water.
They saw golden mansions there, and silver ones as well,
with windows of refined gold and covered with networks of pearls,
with floors of gold and silver, and furnished with vaiḍūrya jewels.
The monkeys saw there principal houses on every side,
and flowering, fruit-bearing trees resembling coral gems,
and golden bees, and honey everywhere.
They saw beds and seats variegated with jewels and gold,

children.text: mahārhāṇi ca yānāni dadṛśus te samantataḥ
children.translated_text: and very costly vehicles on every side,
and heaps of vessels made of gold, silver, and bronze,

children.text: agarūṇāṃ ca divyānāṃ candanānāṃ ca saṃcayān
children.translated_text: and heaps of divine aloeswood and sandalwood,

children.text: śucīny abhyavahāryāṇi mūlāni ca phalāni ca ||
children.translated_text: pure foods, and roots and fruits,

children.text: mahārhāṇi ca pānāni madhūni rasavanti ca
children.translated_text: and costly drinks, and flavorful honey,

children.text: divyānām ambarāṇāṃ ca mahārhāṇāṃ ca saṃcayān
children.translated_text: and heaps of divine garments and of very costly things,

children.text: kambalānāṃ ca citrāṇām ajinānāṃ ca saṃcayān ||
children.translated_text: and heaps of variegated blankets and skins.

children.text: tatra tatra vicinvanto bile tatra mahāprabhāḥ
children.translated_text: Searching here and there in that cavern, those greatly radiant

children.text: dadṛśur vānarāḥ śūrāḥ striyaṃ kāṃcid adūrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: heroic monkeys saw a certain woman not far away.
Seeing her, they were deeply terrified: she was clothed in bark and black antelope skin,
an ascetic woman of regulated diet, blazing as if with radiance.

children.text: tato hanūmān girisaṃnikāśaḥ kṛtāñjalis tām abhivādya vṛddhām
children.translated_text: Then <s>Hanumān</s>, mountain-like, with joined palms, saluted that aged woman.

children.text: papraccha kā tvaṃ bhavanaṃ bilaṃ ca ratnāni cemāni vadasva kasya ||
children.translated_text: He asked, "Who are you? Whose is this dwelling, this cave, and these jewels? Tell me."

children.text: ity uktvā hanumāṃs tatra punaḥ kṛṣṇājināmbarām
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Hanumān</s> there again
addressed that very fortunate ascetic woman, clothed in a black-antelope skin and devoted to <s>dharma</s>.
"We entered this cave suddenly, covered with darkness,
wearied by hunger and thirst, and exhausted in every way.
Thirsty, we entered this great opening in the earth.

children.text: imāṃs tv evaṃvidhān bhāvān vividhān adbhutopamān
children.translated_text: But seeing these varied things of such a kind,
various and resembling marvels, we have become alarmed, confused, and bereft of sense.
Whose are these golden trees, shining like the young sun,

children.text: śucīny abhyavahāryāṇi mūlāni ca phalāni ca ||
children.translated_text: and these pure edible roots and fruits?
Whose are these golden palaces and silver houses,
with refined-gold windows and covered with lattices of jewels?
These trees are flowering and fruit-bearing, blessed and fragrant with sweet scent.
By whose splendor are these trees made of <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold?

children.text: kāñcanāni ca padmāni jātāni vimale jale
children.translated_text: And how have golden lotuses arisen in the clear water?

children.text: kathaṃ matsyāś ca sauvarṇāścaranti saha kacchapaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: How do golden fish move about together with turtles?

children.text: ātmānam anubhāvaṃ ca kasya caitat tapobalam
children.translated_text: Yourself, your power, and whose ascetic might this is,

children.text: ajānatāṃ naḥ sarveṣāṃ sarvam ākhyātum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: you ought to tell us everything, for all of us do not know."
Thus addressed by <s>Hanumān</s>, the ascetic woman devoted to <s>dharma</s>,
delighting in the welfare of all beings, answered <s>Hanumān</s>.
"There was a very brilliant one named <s>Maya</s>, a master of illusion and bull among dānavas.

children.text: tenedaṃ nirmitaṃ sarvaṃ māyayā kāñcanaṃ vanam ||
children.translated_text: By him all this golden forest was fashioned through illusion.
Formerly he was indeed the <s>Viśvakarman</s> of the chief dānavas;
by him this excellent divine golden mansion was fashioned.

children.text: sa tu varṣasahasrāṇi tapas taptvā mahāvane
children.translated_text: After practicing austerity for thousands of years in a great forest,

children.text: pitāmahād varaṃ lebhe sarvam auśanasaṃ dhanam ||
children.translated_text: he obtained from the Grandfather all the wealth of <s>Uśanas</s> as a boon.
Then the mighty one, lord of all objects of desire, arranged everything,

children.text: uvāsa sukhitaḥ kālaṃ kaṃcid asmin mahāvane ||
children.translated_text: and lived happily for some time in this great forest.
When that foremost dānava became attached to the apsaras <s>Hemā</s>,
<s>Indra</s>, lord of cities, attacked, took up his thunderbolt, and slew him.

children.text: idaṃ ca brahmaṇā dattaṃ hemāyai vanam uttamam
children.translated_text: And this excellent forest was given by <s>Brahmā</s> to <s>Hemā</s>,

children.text: śāśvataḥ kāmabhogaś ca gṛhaṃ cedaṃ hiraṇmayam ||
children.translated_text: along with everlasting enjoyment of desires and this golden house.

children.text: duhitā merusāvarṇer ahaṃ tasyāḥ svayaṃ prabhā
children.translated_text: I am the daughter of <s>Merusāvarṇi</s>, and my name is <s>Svayaṃprabhā</s>.
I guard this dwelling of <s>Hemā</s>, O best of monkeys.
My dear friend <s>Hemā</s> is skilled in dance and song.
Having received a boon from her, I guard this excellent mansion.

children.text: kiṃ kāryaṃ kasya vā hetoḥ kāntārāṇi prapadyatha
children.translated_text: For what business, or for what reason, do you enter these wildernesses?

children.text: kathaṃ cedaṃ vanaṃ durgaṃ yuṣmābhir upalakṣitam ||
children.translated_text: And how was this inaccessible forest perceived by you?

children.text: imāny abhyavahāryāṇi mūlāni ca phalāni ca
children.translated_text: After eating these edible roots and fruits,

children.text: bhuktvā pītvā ca pānīyaṃ sarvaṃ me vaktum arhatha ||
children.translated_text: and after drinking water, you ought to tell me everything."

children.text: atha tān abravīt sarvān viśrāntān hariyūthapān
children.translated_text: Then that ascetic woman devoted to <s>dharma</s>, with concentrated mind,
spoke these words to all those rested leaders of monkey troops:

children.text: vānarā yadi vaḥ khedaḥ pranaṣṭaḥ phalabhakṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: "O monkeys, if your fatigue has disappeared through eating fruit,

children.text: yadi caitan mayā śrāvyaṃ śrotum icchāmi kathyatām ||
children.translated_text: and if this may be heard by me, I wish to hear it; let it be told."

children.text: tasyās tad vacanaṃ śrutvā hanumān mārutātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing those words of hers, <s>Hanumān</s>, son of <s>Māruta</s>,
began to tell the truth straightforwardly, just as it was.
"The king of the whole world, equal to great <s>Indra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>,
the glorious <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, entered the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest

children.text: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā vaidehyā cāpi bhāryayā
children.translated_text: together with his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and also with his wife <s>Vaidehī</s>.

children.text: tasya bhāryā janasthānād rāvaṇena hṛtā balāt ||
children.translated_text: His wife was carried off by force from <s>Janasthāna</s> by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: vīras tasya sakhā rājñaḥ sugrīvo nāma vānaraḥ
children.translated_text: The hero's friend is a monkey named <s>Sugrīva</s>, a king,
lord of the foremost monkeys, by whom we have been sent out.
Toward the southern quarter, traversed by <s>Agastya</s> and guarded by <s>Yama</s>,
we have come with these chief monkeys, headed by <s>Aṅgada</s>.
All of us together were instructed, "Search for the rākṣasa <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: sītayā saha vaidehyā mārgadhvam iti coditāḥ ||
children.translated_text: who changes form at will, together with <s>Sītā</s>, the <s>Vaidehī</s>."

children.text: vicitya tu vayaṃ sarve samagrāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ diśam
children.translated_text: After searching the entire southern direction, all of us together,
hungry and exhausted, took shelter at the root of a tree.
All our faces were pale, and all of us were given over to anxious thought.
Sunk in the great ocean of worry, we could not find the further shore.

children.text: cārayantas tataś cakṣur dṛṣṭavanto mahad bilam
children.translated_text: Then, casting our eyes about, we saw a great cave,
covered with creepers and trees and enveloped in darkness.
From it came swans wet with water, their wings sprinkled with drops,
and birds, ospreys and cranes as well, were flying out.

children.text: sādhv atra praviśāmeti mayā tūktāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: I said to the leapers, 'Let us enter here; it is good.'

children.text: teṣām api hi sarveṣām anumānam upāgatam
children.translated_text: For all of them too the same conclusion was reached:
'Let us go; let us enter,' driven by urgency for our master's task.

children.text: tato gāḍhaṃ nipatitā gṛhya hastau parasparam
children.translated_text: Then, firmly holding one another's hands, we fell in deeply,
and suddenly entered this cave covered with darkness.

children.text: etan naḥ kāryam etena kṛtyena vayam āgatāḥ
children.translated_text: This is our task; we have come for this business.
And all of us, distressed and hungry, have come to you.
The roots and fruits given according to the <s>dharma</s> of hospitality
have been eaten by us, who were tormented by hunger.

children.text: yat tvayā rakṣitāḥ sarve mriyamāṇā bubhukṣayā
children.translated_text: Since all of us, dying from hunger, have been protected by you,

children.text: brūhi pratyupakārārthaṃ kiṃ te kurvantu vānarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: tell us, by way of return, what the monkeys should do for you."

children.text: evam uktā tu sarvajñā vānarais taiḥ svayaṃprabhā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by those monkeys, the all-knowing <s>Svayaṃprabhā</s>
then replied with these words to all the leaders of the monkey troops.
I am satisfied with all the swift monkeys,

children.text: carantyā mama dharmeṇa na kāryam iha kenacit ||
children.translated_text: and while I conduct myself according to <s>dharma</s>, nothing needs to be done here by anyone.

children.text: evam uktaḥ śubhaṃ vākyaṃ tāpasyā dharmasaṃhitam
children.translated_text: When he had heard this auspicious speech, joined with the ascetic woman's <s>dharma</s>,
<s>Hanumān</s> spoke these words to her, whose conduct was blameless:

children.text: śaraṇaṃ tvāṃ prapannāḥ smaḥ sarve vai dharmacāriṇi
children.translated_text: We have all taken refuge in you, O follower of <s>dharma</s>.
The time that the great-souled <s>Sugrīva</s> fixed for us

children.text: sa tu kālo vyatikrānto bile ca parivartatām ||
children.translated_text: has passed while we have been wandering about in the cave.

children.text: sā tvam asmād bilād ghorād uttārayitum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: Therefore you should bring us up out of this terrible cave.
Because <s>Sugrīva</s>'s command has been overstepped, our lives are as good as gone.
You should save us all, for we are fearful of <s>Sugrīva</s>.

children.text: mahac ca kāryam asmābhiḥ kartavyaṃ dharmacāriṇi
children.translated_text: And a great task had to be done by us, O follower of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: tac cāpi na kṛtaṃ kāryam asmābhir iha vāsibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: but that task too has not been done by us while dwelling here.

children.text: evam uktā hanumatā tāpasī vākyam abravīt
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Hanumān</s>, the ascetic woman spoke these words:
I think it is difficult for one who has entered to return alive.
But by the power of my austerity, and by the discipline I have acquired,

children.text: sarvān eva bilād asmād uddhariṣyāmi vānarān ||
children.translated_text: I shall bring all these monkeys out of this cave.
Close your eyes, all you bulls among monkeys,
for it is not possible to go out with eyes unclosed.
Then all of them, with their hands and tender fingers,
at once covered their sight, delighted and eager to depart.
Those great-souled monkeys, their faces covered by their hands at that time,
were brought out of the cave by her in the mere interval of a blink.

children.text: tatas tān vānarān sarvāṃs tāpasī dharmacāriṇī
children.translated_text: Then that ascetic woman, a follower of <s>dharma</s>, reassured
all those monkeys who had come out from that difficult place and said this:
This is the splendid <s>Vindhya</s> mountain, furnished with many trees and creepers.
This is <s>Prasravaṇa</s> mountain, and this is the ocean, the great sea.
May all be well with you. I shall go to my dwelling, O bulls among monkeys.

children.text: ity uktvā tad bilaṃ śrīmat praviveśa svayaṃprabhā ||
children.translated_text: Having said this, <s>Svayaṃprabhā</s> entered that splendid cave herself.

children.text: tatas te dadṛśur ghoraṃ sāgaraṃ varuṇālayam
children.translated_text: Then they saw the terrible ocean, the abode of <s>Varuṇa</s>,
boundless, roaring loudly, and agitated by dreadful waves.
As they searched that mountain stronghold fashioned by <s>Maya</s>'s magic,

children.text: teṣāṃ māso vyatikrānto yo rājñā samayaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the month fixed for them by the king had passed.
Then, at the foot of the <s>Vindhya</s> mountain, where the trees were in full bloom,
the greatly fortunate ones sat down and fell into anxiety.
Seeing the springtime trees, their tips heavy with excessive loads of flowers
and covered with hundreds of creepers, they became fearful and apprehensive.
Recognizing to one another that spring had arrived,
and that the time and purpose of their message were lost, they fell to the ground.
Then that monkey, with shoulders like a lion and a bull and with full, long arms,
the very wise crown prince <s>Aṅgada</s>, spoke these words:
By the command of the monkey king we all set out.

children.text: māsaḥ pūrṇo bilasthānāṃ harayaḥ kiṃ na budhyate ||
children.translated_text: O monkeys, does he not know that a month has been completed while we were staying in the cave?

children.text: tasminn atīte kāle tu sugrīveṇa kṛte svayam
children.translated_text: Since that time, fixed by <s>Sugrīva</s> himself, has passed,
fasting to death is fitting for all the forest-dwellers.
<s>Sugrīva</s> is harsh by nature and established in the state of lordship.

children.text: na kṣamiṣyati naḥ sarvān aparādhakṛto gatān ||
children.translated_text: He will not forgive us all when we return as offenders.

children.text: apravṛttau ca sītāyāḥ pāpam eva kariṣyati
children.translated_text: And when there is no news of <s>Sītā</s>, he will certainly commit a sinful act.

children.text: tasmāt kṣamam ihādyaiva prāyopaviśanaṃ hi naḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore it is fitting for us to fast to death here today.

children.text: tyaktvā putrāṃś ca dārāṃś ca dhanāni ca gṛhāṇi ca
children.translated_text: Leaving behind sons, wives, wealth, and homes,

children.text: yāvan na ghātayed rājā sarvān pratigatān itaḥ
children.translated_text: before the king kills all of us after we have returned from here,
death here itself is better for us than an unworthy execution.
And I was not consecrated as crown prince by <s>Sugrīva</s>;
I was consecrated by <s>Rāma</s>, the king of men, whose deeds are unwearied.

children.text: sa pūrvaṃ baddhavairo māṃ rājā dṛṣṭvā vyatikramam
children.translated_text: That king, who earlier held enmity, seeing my transgression,
will have me killed with a severe punishment, firmly resolved.

children.text: kiṃ me suhṛdbhir vyasanaṃ paśyadbhir jīvitāntare
children.translated_text: What use are friends to me, watching my disaster while I still live?
Here itself, on the holy shore of the ocean, I shall sit down to fast until death.
Hearing this speech uttered by the prince, the crown prince,

children.text: sarve te vānaraśreṣṭhāḥ karuṇaṃ vākyam abruvan ||
children.translated_text: all those best of monkeys spoke a piteous word:

children.text: tīkṣṇaḥ prakṛtyā sugrīvaḥ priyāsaktaś ca rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s> is harsh by nature, and <s>Rāghava</s> is attached to his beloved.

children.text: adṛṣṭāyāṃ ca vaidehyāṃ dṛṣṭvāsmāṃś ca samāgatān ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Vaidehī</s> has not been seen and he sees us returned,
for the sake of doing what is dear to <s>Rāghava</s>, he will kill us without doubt.
It is not fitting for offenders to go into the presence of their master.

children.text: plavaṃgamānāṃ tu bhayārditānāṃ śrutvā vacas tāra idaṃ babhāṣe
children.translated_text: Hearing the words of the leapers, who were tormented by fear, <s>Tāra</s> said this:

children.text: alaṃ viṣādena bilaṃ praviśya vasāma sarve yadi rocate vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Enough of despair. Let us enter the cave and all live there, if that pleases you.
For this place, fashioned by magic, is very difficult to reach and has abundant trees, water, food, and drink.

children.text: ihāsti no naiva bhayaṃ puraṃdarān na rāghavād vānararājato 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: Here there is no fear for us from <s>Purandara</s>, nor from <s>Rāghava</s>, nor even from the monkey king.

children.text: śrutvāṅgadasyāpi vaco 'nukūlam ūcuś ca sarve harayaḥ pratītāḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing also <s>Aṅgada</s>'s agreeable speech, all the monkeys, pleased, said:

children.text: yathā na hanyema tathā vidhānam asaktam adyaiva vidhīyatāṃ naḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let an arrangement be made for us today, without delay, by which we may not be killed.
As <s>Tāra</s>, radiant like the lord of stars, was speaking in that way,

children.text: atha mene hṛtaṃ rājyaṃ hanumān aṅgadena tat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hanumān</s> then thought that the kingdom had been seized by <s>Aṅgada</s>.
<s>Hanumān</s> considered the son of <s>Vālin</s> to be endowed with eightfold intelligence,
possessed of the four powers, and furnished with the fourteen qualities,
and ever increasing in brilliance, strength, and valor.
like the moon at the beginning of the bright fortnight, waxing in splendor.
Equal to <s>Bṛhaspati</s> in intelligence and like his father in valor,
attentive to <s>Tāra</s>, as <s>Purandara</s> is to <s>Śukra</s>,
weary from exertion for his master's sake and learned in all the śāstras,
<s>Hanumān</s> then began to win over <s>Aṅgada</s>.
Describing the third of the four expedients,
he split apart all those monkeys by the force of his eloquent speech.
When they had all been divided, he then frightened <s>Aṅgada</s>
with many terrifying words, joined with the expedient of anger.

children.text: tvaṃ samarthataraḥ pitrā yuddhe tāreya vai dhuram
children.translated_text: O son of <s>Tārā</s>, you are more capable than your father in battle of firmly bearing the burden,

children.text: dṛḍhaṃ dhārayituṃ śaktaḥ kapirājyaṃ yathā pitā ||
children.translated_text: and able to hold the monkey kingdom, just as your father did.
For monkeys are always unstable in mind, O bull among monkeys.
Separated from their sons and wives, they will not endure being commanded by you.

children.text: tvāṃ naite hy anuyuñjeyuḥ pratyakṣaṃ pravadāmi te
children.translated_text: They will not follow you. I tell you this plainly,

children.text: yathāyaṃ jāmbavān nīlaḥ suhotraś ca mahākapiḥ ||
children.translated_text: just as this <s>Jāmbavān</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, and the great monkey <s>Suhotra</s> will not.

children.text: na hy ahaṃ ta ime sarve sāmadānādibhir guṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: For neither I nor all these others, by the qualities of conciliation, gifts, and the like,

children.text: daṇḍena na tvayā śakyāḥ sugrīvād apakarṣitum ||
children.translated_text: nor by punishment, can be drawn away by you from <s>Sugrīva</s>.
They say that, when a weaker one is in conflict with a stronger, even sitting still is proper;
therefore, since it protects oneself, the weak should not enter into conflict.

children.text: yāṃ cemāṃ manyase dhātrīm etad bilam iti śrutam
children.translated_text: And as for this support which you think of as this cave that is spoken of,
tearing it open would be only a slight task for <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s arrows.

children.text: svalpaṃ hi kṛtam indreṇa kṣipatā hy aśaniṃ purā
children.translated_text: For <s>Indra</s> did little when he hurled the thunderbolt in ancient times.

children.text: lakṣmaṇo niśitair bāṇair bhindyāt pattrapuṭaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> would split it with sharp arrows as if it were a leaf-cup,

children.text: lakṣmaṇasya ca nārācā bahavaḥ santi tadvidhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> has many such iron arrows.
The very moment you remain fixed in one place, O scorcher of foes,
at that very moment all the monkeys, having made up their minds, will abandon you.
Remembering their sons and wives, constantly anxious and hungry,
worn out by painful beds, they will turn their backs on you.

children.text: sa tvaṃ hīnaḥ suhṛdbhiś ca hitakāmaiś ca bandhubhiḥ
children.translated_text: Then you, deprived of friends and of kinsmen who seek your welfare,
will become more terrified than of a trembling blade of grass.

children.text: na ca jātu na hiṃsyus tvāṃ ghorā lakṣmaṇasāyakāḥ
children.translated_text: Nor would the terrible arrows of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> ever fail to harm you,
hard to withstand, rushing with great speed, and seeking to kill you after you have turned away.

children.text: asmābhis tu gataṃ sārdhaṃ vinītavad upasthitam
children.translated_text: But if you go together with us and stand before him in humble fashion,

children.text: ānupūrvyāt tu sugrīvo rājye tvāṃ sthāpayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s>, in due order, will establish you in the kingdom.
Your father's brother desires <s>dharma</s>, seeks affection, and is firm in his vow;

children.text: śuciḥ satyapratijñaś ca nā tvāṃ jātu jighāṃsati ||
children.translated_text: he is pure and true to his promise, and he will never wish to kill you.

children.text: priyakāmaś ca te mātus tadarthaṃ cāsya jīvitam
children.translated_text: He desires what is dear to your mother, and his life is for her sake.

children.text: tasyāpatyaṃ ca nāsty anyat tasmād aṅgada gamyatām ||
children.translated_text: She has no other child; therefore, <s>Aṅgada</s>, let us go.
Hearing <s>Hanumān</s>'s speech, respectful and joined with <s>dharma</s>,
and accompanied by honor toward his master, <s>Aṅgada</s> spoke these words:
Steadfastness in every respect, purity, compassion, and honesty,

children.text: vikramaiś caiva dhairyaṃ ca sugrīve nopapadyate ||
children.translated_text: as well as courage in exploits and firmness, do not exist in <s>Sugrīva</s>.

children.text: bhrātur jyeṣṭhasya yo bhāryāṃ jīvito mahiṣīṃ priyām
children.translated_text: He who takes to himself the wife of his elder brother, his beloved queen while he was alive,

children.text: dharmeṇa mātaraṃ yas tu svīkaroti jugupsitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: who according to <s>dharma</s> is his mother, is despicable.

children.text: kathaṃ sa dharmaṃ jānīte yena bhrātrā durātmanā
children.translated_text: How does that wicked man know <s>dharma</s>,
that evil-minded brother by whom the mouth of the cave was closed while his brother was engaged for battle?
And he by whom <s>Rāghava</s>, who had clasped his hand in good faith, done his task, and gained great fame,

children.text: vismṛto rāghavo yena sa kasya sukṛtaṃ smaret ||
children.translated_text: was forgotten: whose good deed would such a man remember?
He ordered <s>Sītā</s> to be searched for out of fear of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, not because he feared unrighteousness.

children.text: ādiṣṭā mārgituṃ sītāṃ dharmam asmin kathaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: How can there be <s>dharma</s> in him?

children.text: tasmin pāpe kṛtaghne tu smṛtihīne calātmani
children.translated_text: What noble man, born in that family and wishing to live,

children.text: āryaḥ ko viśvasej jātu tatkulīno jijīviṣuḥ ||
children.translated_text: would ever trust that sinful, ungrateful, forgetful, fickle-minded man?

children.text: rājye putraṃ pratiṣṭhāpya saguṇo nirguṇo 'pi vā
children.translated_text: Having installed his own son in the kingdom, whether qualified or unqualified,
how will <s>Sugrīva</s> let me live, when I am born from an enemy's line?

children.text: bhinnamantro 'parāddhaś ca hīnaśaktiḥ kathaṃ hy aham
children.translated_text: With my plans exposed, guilty, and bereft of strength,

children.text: kiṣkindhāṃ prāpya jīveyam anātha iva durbalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: how could I reach <s>Kiṣkindhā</s> and live there like a helpless weakling?
By a secret punishment he would consign me to imprisonment,

children.text: śaṭhaḥ krūro nṛśaṃsaś ca sugrīvo rājyakāraṇāt ||
children.translated_text: for <s>Sugrīva</s> is deceitful, cruel, and pitiless for the sake of the kingdom.
Better for me than imprisonment and decline is fasting to death.

children.text: anujānīta māṃ sarve gṛhān gacchantu vānarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Permit me, all of you; let the monkeys go home.

children.text: ahaṃ vaḥ pratijānāmi na gamiṣyāmy ahaṃ purīm
children.translated_text: I promise you that I shall not go to the city.

children.text: ihaiva prāyam āsiṣye śreyo maraṇam eva me ||
children.translated_text: Here itself I shall sit down to fast; death itself is better for me.

children.text: abhivādanapūrvaṃ tu rājā kuśalam eva ca
children.translated_text: After first paying homage, the king should be told of my welfare,

children.text: vācyas tato yavīyān me sugrīvo vānareśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: namely <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of monkeys, my younger uncle.

children.text: ārogyapūrvaṃ kuśalaṃ vācyā mātā rumā ca me
children.translated_text: My mother and <s>Rumā</s> should be told of my health and welfare first,

children.text: mātaraṃ caiva me tārām āśvāsayitum arhatha ||
children.translated_text: and you should console my mother <s>Tārā</s>.
By nature she dearly loves her son, and the poor ascetic woman is compassionate.

children.text: vinaṣṭaṃ mām iha śrutvā vyaktaṃ hāsyati jīvitam ||
children.translated_text: Hearing that I am lost here, she will certainly give up her life.

children.text: etāvad uktvā vacanaṃ vṛddhān apy abhivādya ca
children.translated_text: Having said so much and having bowed even to the elders,
<s>Aṅgada</s> lay down on the ground among the darbha grass, weeping and downcast.
As he lay down there, the bulls among monkeys, weeping,

children.text: nayanebhyaḥ pramumucur uṣṇaṃ vai vāri duḥkhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: released hot tears from their eyes in their grief.

children.text: sugrīvaṃ caiva nindantaḥ praśaṃsantaś ca vālinam
children.translated_text: Blaming <s>Sugrīva</s> and praising <s>Vālin</s>,
they all surrounded <s>Aṅgada</s> and resolved to sit down to fast to death.
Having understood that this was the opinion of <s>Vālin</s>'s son, the foremost leapers
Having sipped water, all of them sat down facing east,
on darbha grass whose tips pointed south, resorting to the northern shore.

children.text: sa saṃviśadbhir bahubhir mahīdharo mahādrikūṭapramitaiḥ plavaṃgamaiḥ
children.translated_text: As many monkeys, equal in size to peaks of great mountains, settled upon it,

children.text: babhūva saṃnāditanirjharāntaro bhṛśaṃ nadadbhir jaladair ivolbaṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the mountain, its inner waterfalls resounding, became like fierce clouds roaring loudly.

children.text: upaviṣṭās tu te sarve yasmin prāyaṃ giristhale
children.translated_text: When all the monkeys had sat down to fast unto death on that mountain ground,

children.text: harayo gṛdhrarājaś ca taṃ deśam upacakrame ||
children.translated_text: the king of vultures approached that place where the monkeys were.

children.text: sāmpātir nāma nāmnā tu cirajīvī vihaṃgamaḥ
children.translated_text: There was a long-lived bird named <s>Sampāti</s>,
the splendid brother of <s>Jaṭāyus</s>, renowned for strength and valor.
Coming out from a cave of the great <s>Vindhya</s> mountain,

children.text: upaviṣṭān harīn dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭātmā giram abravīt ||
children.translated_text: he saw the monkeys seated there and, delighted at heart, spoke these words:
Surely fate follows a man in this world according to its own ordinance,

children.text: yathāyaṃ vihito bhakṣyaś cirān mahyam upāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: since this food, assigned to me, has come after a long time.
I shall eat the monkeys one after another, each as he dies.

children.text: uvācaivaṃ vacaḥ pakṣī tān nirīkṣya plavaṃgamān ||
children.translated_text: So the bird spoke, looking at those leaping monkeys.
Hearing that speech of the bird, who was greedy for food,
the utterly distressed <s>Aṅgada</s> then said to <s>Hanumān</s>:
Look: under the pretext of <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Vaivasvata Yama</s> himself
has come to this region for the destruction of the monkeys.

children.text: rāmasya na kṛtaṃ kāryaṃ rājño na ca vacaḥ kṛtam
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>'s task has not been accomplished, and the king's command has not been carried out;
this unforeseen calamity has suddenly come upon the monkeys.
That deed which was done there by <s>Jaṭāyus</s>, the king of vultures,

children.text: gṛdhrarājena yat tatra śrutaṃ vas tad aśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: out of love for <s>Vaidehī</s>, you have heard in full.
So all beings, even those born in animal wombs,

children.text: priyaṃ kurvanti rāmasya tyaktvā prāṇān yathā vayam ||
children.translated_text: do what is dear to <s>Rāma</s>, abandoning their lives, just as we do.
We are exhausted for the sake of <s>Rāghava</s> and have renounced our lives;

children.text: kāntārāṇi prapannāḥ sma na ca paśyāma maithilīm ||
children.translated_text: we have entered wildernesses and still do not see <s>Maithilī</s>.

children.text: sa sukhī gṛdhrarājas tu rāvaṇena hato raṇe
children.translated_text: But that king of vultures is fortunate: killed by <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle,

children.text: muktaś ca sugrīvabhayād gataś ca paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: he was freed from fear of <s>Sugrīva</s> and went to the highest state.
By the death of <s>Jaṭāyus</s>, by the death of king <s>Daśaratha</s>,

children.text: haraṇena ca vaidehyāḥ saṃśayaṃ harayo gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and by the abduction of <s>Vaidehī</s>, the monkeys have fallen into uncertainty.
The dwelling of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> in the forest together with <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: rāghavasya ca bāṇena vālinaś ca tathā vadhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and likewise the killing of <s>Vālin</s> by <s>Rāghava</s>'s arrow,
and the destruction of all the rākṣasas through <s>Rāma</s>'s anger:

children.text: kaikeyyā varadānena idaṃ hi vikṛtaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: all this distortion was brought about by <s>Kaikeyī</s>'s granting of boons.

children.text: tat tu śrutvā tadā vākyam aṅgadasya mukhodgatam
children.translated_text: Then, hearing that speech which had issued from <s>Aṅgada</s>'s mouth,
the sharp-beaked, great-voiced vulture spoke these words:

children.text: ko 'yaṃ girā ghoṣayati prāṇaiḥ priyatarasya me
children.translated_text: Who is this who proclaims, with his voice, the death of my brother <s>Jaṭāyus</s>,

children.text: jaṭāyuṣo vadhaṃ bhrātuḥ kampayann iva me manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: dearer to me than life, as though shaking my mind?
How did the battle between the rākṣasa and the vulture take place in <s>Janasthāna</s>?

children.text: nāmadheyam idaṃ bhrātuś cirasyādya mayā śrutam ||
children.translated_text: After so long, today I have heard this name of my brother.
He was younger, appreciative of virtue, and praiseworthy for his exploits;

children.text: tad iccheyam ahaṃ śrotuṃ vināśaṃ vānararṣabhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: O bulls among monkeys, I wish to hear of his destruction,
the destruction of that brother <s>Jaṭāyus</s>, who dwelt in <s>Janasthāna</s>.

children.text: tasyaiva ca mama bhrātuḥ sakhā daśarathaḥ katham
children.translated_text: And how was king <s>Daśaratha</s> a friend of that very brother of mine,

children.text: yasya rāmaḥ priyaḥ putro jyeṣṭho gurujanapriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whose dear eldest son was <s>Rāma</s>, beloved by his elders?
Because my wings have been burned by the sun's rays, I cannot move about;
O subduers of enemies, I wish to descend from this mountain.

children.text: śokād bhraṣṭasvaram api śrutvā te hariyūthapāḥ
children.translated_text: Although his voice was broken by grief, when those monkey troop-leaders heard him,

children.text: śraddadhur naiva tad vākyaṃ karmaṇā tasya śaṅkitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: they did not trust that statement, being suspicious of his intent.

children.text: te prāyam upaviṣṭās tu dṛṣṭvā gṛdhraṃ plavaṃgamāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing the vulture while they sat fasting unto death, the leaping monkeys

children.text: cakrur buddhiṃ tadā raudrāṃ sarvān no bhakṣayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: formed a grim thought then: 'He will eat us all.'

children.text: sarvathā prāyam āsīnān yadi no bhakṣayiṣyati
children.translated_text: If he will eat us in every way as we sit fasting unto death,

children.text: kṛtakṛtyā bhaviṣyāmaḥ kṣipraṃ siddhim ito gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: we shall have accomplished our purpose and quickly attained success from here.

children.text: etāṃ buddhiṃ tataś cakruḥ sarve te vānararṣabhāḥ
children.translated_text: Then all those bulls among monkeys formed this resolution.

children.text: avatārya gireḥ śṛṅgād gṛdhram āhāṅgadas tadā ||
children.translated_text: Having brought the vulture down from the mountain peak, <s>Aṅgada</s> then said:
There was a mighty king of monkeys named <s>Ṛkṣarajas</s>,

children.text: mamāryaḥ pārthivaḥ pakṣin dhārmikau tasya cātmajau ||
children.translated_text: my noble lord and king, O bird; his two sons were righteous.

children.text: sugrīvaś caiva vālī ca putrāv oghabalāv ubhau
children.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s> and <s>Vālin</s> were his two sons, both of flood-like strength;

children.text: loke viśrutakarmābhūd rājā vālī pitā mama ||
children.translated_text: king <s>Vālin</s>, my father, was renowned in the world for his deeds.
The glorious <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, a great chariot-warrior king
of the whole world of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s>, entered the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest,

children.text: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā vaidehyā cāpi bhāryayā
children.translated_text: with his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and also with his wife <s>Vaidehī</s>,
intent on his father's command and having taken the righteous path.

children.text: tasya bhāryā janasthānād rāvaṇena hṛtā balāt ||
children.translated_text: His wife was carried off by force from <s>Janasthāna</s> by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: rāmasya ca pitur mitraṃ jaṭāyur nāma gṛdhrarāṭ
children.translated_text: A king of vultures named <s>Jaṭāyus</s>, a friend of <s>Rāma</s>'s father,
saw <s>Sītā Vaidehī</s> being carried away through the sky.

children.text: rāvaṇaṃ virathaṃ kṛtvā sthāpayitvā ca maithilīm
children.translated_text: After making <s>Rāvaṇa</s> chariotless and stopping <s>Maithilī</s>,

children.text: pariśrāntaś ca vṛddhaś ca rāvaṇena hato raṇe ||
children.translated_text: he, exhausted and old, was killed by <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle.

children.text: evaṃ gṛdhro hatas tena rāvaṇena balīyasā
children.translated_text: Thus that vulture was slain by the stronger <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: saṃskṛtaś cāpi rāmeṇa gataś ca gatim uttamām ||
children.translated_text: but he was honored with funeral rites by <s>Rāma</s> and went to the highest state.
Then <s>Rāghava</s> made friendship with my paternal uncle,

children.text: cakāra rāghavaḥ sakhyaṃ so 'vadhīt pitaraṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: the great-souled <s>Sugrīva</s>, and he killed my father.

children.text: mama pitrā viruddho hi sugrīvaḥ sacivaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: For <s>Sugrīva</s>, together with his ministers, had been opposed by my father;

children.text: nihatya vālinaṃ rāmas tatas tam abhiṣecayat ||
children.translated_text: after killing <s>Vālin</s>, <s>Rāma</s> then consecrated him.

children.text: sa rājye sthāpitas tena sugrīvo vānareśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: That monkey-lord <s>Sugrīva</s> was established in the kingdom by him.
the king of the chief monkeys, by whom we were sent forth.

children.text: evaṃ rāmaprayuktās tu mārgamāṇās tatas tataḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, sent by <s>Rāma</s>, searching here and there,
we do not find <s>Vaidehī</s>, like the radiance of the sun at night.
We, having searched the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest with full attention,

children.text: ajñānāt tu praviṣṭāḥ sma dharaṇyā vivṛtaṃ bilam ||
children.translated_text: out of ignorance entered a cavern, an opening in the earth.

children.text: mayasya māyāvihitaṃ tad bilaṃ ca vicinvatām
children.translated_text: As we searched that cavern fashioned by <s>Maya</s>'s magic,

children.text: vyatītas tatra no māso yo rājñā samayaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there our month passed, the time that the king had fixed.
We all carry out the command of the monkey king,

children.text: kṛtāṃ saṃsthām atikrāntā bhayāt prāyam upāsmahe ||
children.translated_text: but we have exceeded the appointed limit, and from fear we sit down to fast to death.

children.text: kruddhe tasmiṃs tu kākutsthe sugrīve ca salakṣmaṇe
children.translated_text: When that <s>Kākutstha</s>, and <s>Sugrīva</s> together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, are angry,

children.text: gatānām api sarveṣāṃ tatra no nāsti jīvitam ||
children.translated_text: even if all of us go there, there will be no life for us.

children.text: ity uktaḥ karuṇaṃ vākyaṃ vānarais tyaktajīvitaiḥ
children.translated_text: When this piteous speech had been spoken by the monkeys who had abandoned hope of life,
the tearful vulture answered the monkeys in a great voice.

children.text: yavīyān mama sa bhrātā jaṭāyur nāma vānarāḥ
children.translated_text: That younger brother of mine is named <s>Jaṭāyus</s>, O monkeys,
whom you have reported slain in battle by mighty <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
