children.text: vṛddhabhāvād apakṣatvāc chṛṇvaṃs tad api marṣaye
children.translated_text: Because of old age and because I am without wings, even hearing that, I must endure it;

children.text: na hi me śaktir adyāsti bhrātur vairavimokṣaṇe ||
children.translated_text: for today I have no power to avenge my brother's enmity.

children.text: purā vṛtravadhe vṛtte sa cāhaṃ ca jayaiṣiṇau
children.translated_text: Long ago, when the slaying of <s>Vṛtra</s> had taken place, he and I, seeking victory,
approached the blazing sun, garlanded with rays.
Covering the path of the sky, we went with great speed,

children.text: madhyaṃ prāpte ca sūrye ca jaṭāyur avasīdati ||
children.translated_text: and when the sun had reached the middle of the sky, <s>Jaṭāyus</s> began to sink.

children.text: tam ahaṃ bhrātaraṃ dṛṣṭvā sūryaraśmibhir arditam
children.translated_text: Seeing that brother of mine afflicted by the sun's rays,
I covered him with my wings, deeply overwhelmed by affection.
With my wings burnt away I fell on the <s>Vindhya</s>, O best of monkeys,

children.text: aham asmin vasan bhrātuḥ pravṛttiṃ nopalakṣaye ||
children.translated_text: and while living here I did not learn any news of my brother.

children.text: jaṭāyuṣas tv evam ukto bhrātrā saṃpātinā tadā
children.translated_text: When <s>Jaṭāyus</s> had thus been spoken of then by his brother <s>Saṃpāti</s>,
the very wise crown prince <s>Aṅgada</s> then replied:

children.text: jaṭāyuṣo yadi bhrātā śrutaṃ te gaditaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: If you are <s>Jaṭāyus</s>'s brother, you have heard what I have told;

children.text: ākhyāhi yadi jānāsi nilayaṃ tasya rakṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: tell us, if you know it, the dwelling of that demon.
That short-sighted <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the lord of demons,

children.text: antike yadi vā dūre yadi jānāsi śaṃsa naḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether he is near or far, if you know, tell us.
Then the mighty elder brother of <s>Jaṭāyus</s> spoke,
uttering words worthy of himself and gladdening the monkeys:
I am a vulture with burnt wings, my strength gone, O leapers,

children.text: vāṅmātreṇa tu rāmasya kariṣye sāhyam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: but by speech alone I shall render the highest aid to <s>Rāma</s>.
I know the worlds of <s>Varuṇa</s>, and even the three strides of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
the clashes of gods and demons, and the churning for nectar.

children.text: rāmasya yad idaṃ kāryaṃ kartavyaṃ prathamaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: This task of <s>Rāma</s> ought first to be done by me,

children.text: jarayā ca hṛtaṃ tejaḥ prāṇāś ca śithilā mama ||
children.translated_text: but my splendor has been taken away by old age, and my life-breaths are slack.
A young woman, endowed with beauty and adorned with every ornament,
was seen by me as she was being carried away by evil-minded <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: krośantī rāma rāmeti lakṣmaṇeti ca bhāminī
children.translated_text: The lovely woman was crying, "<s>Rāma</s>, <s>Rāma</s>!" and "<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>!"
throwing down her ornaments and shaking her limbs.
Like sunlight on a mountain peak, her excellent silk garment

children.text: asite rākṣase bhāti yathā vā taḍidambude ||
children.translated_text: shone against the dark demon as lightning shines in a cloud.

children.text: tāṃ tu sītām ahaṃ manye rāmasya parikīrtanāt
children.translated_text: I think that she was <s>Sītā</s>, because she was proclaiming <s>Rāma</s>'s name;

children.text: śrūyatāṃ me kathayato nilayaṃ tasya rakṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: listen as I tell the dwelling of that demon.

children.text: putro viśravasaḥ sākṣād bhrātā vaiśravaṇasya ca
children.translated_text: The direct son of <s>Viśravas</s> and the brother of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>,

children.text: adhyāste nagarīṃ laṅkāṃ rāvaṇo nāma rākṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a demon named <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, dwells in the city <s>Laṅkā</s>.
From here, on an island in the ocean, a full hundred <s>yojanas</s> away,

children.text: tasmiṃl laṅkā purī ramyā nirmitā viśvakarmaṇā ||
children.translated_text: there is that lovely city <s>Laṅkā</s>, built by <s>Viśvakarman</s>.
In it <s>Vaidehī</s> dwells, miserable and clothed in silk,
confined in <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s inner palace and well guarded by demonesses.
In that city you will see <s>Maithilī</s>, the daughter of King <s>Janaka</s>,
there in <s>Laṅkā</s>, guarded on every side by the sea.
Reaching the far end of the ocean, a full hundred <s>yojanas</s>,

children.text: āsādya dakṣiṇaṃ kūlaṃ tato drakṣyatha rāvaṇam ||
children.translated_text: and attaining the southern shore, then you will see <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
There, swiftly and quickly, exert your valor, O leapers;
for by my knowledge I see that, after seeing her, you will return.

children.text: ādyaḥ panthāḥ kuliṅgānāṃ ye cānye dhānyajīvinaḥ
children.translated_text: The first path belongs to kuliṅga birds and to others that live on grain;
the second belongs to those that eat offerings and to those that eat the fruit of trees.

children.text: bhāsās tṛtīyaṃ gacchanti krauñcāś ca kuraraiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Bhāsas go on the third, and krauñcas together with kuraras;

children.text: śyenāś caturthaṃ gacchanti gṛdhrā gacchanti pañcamam ||
children.translated_text: hawks go on the fourth, and vultures go on the fifth.
For those endowed with strength and valor, and possessed of beauty and youth,

children.text: ṣaṣṭhas tu panthā haṃsānāṃ vainateyagatiḥ parā
children.translated_text: the sixth path is that of the haṃsas; the highest course is that of <s>Vainateya</s>,

children.text: vainateyāc ca no janma sarveṣāṃ vānararṣabhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and from <s>Vainateya</s> comes the birth of all of us, O bulls among monkeys.

children.text: garhitaṃ tu kṛtaṃ karma yena sma piśitāśanāḥ
children.translated_text: But a blameworthy deed was done, by which we became eaters of flesh.
Stationed here, I perceive <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and <s>Jānakī</s> as well.

children.text: asmākam api sauvarṇaṃ divyaṃ cakṣurbalaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: We too have golden, divine eyesight and strength;
therefore, by the power of food and by nature, O monkeys,

children.text: ā yojanaśatāt sāgrād vayaṃ paśyāma nityaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: we constantly see from somewhat more than a hundred <s>yojanas</s> away.

children.text: asmākaṃ vihitā vṛttir nisargeṇa ca dūrataḥ
children.translated_text: Our livelihood has by nature been ordained from afar,
but the livelihood of those who fight with their feet is ordained at the foot of things.
Let some means be found for crossing the salt water;
after approaching <s>Vaidehī</s>, you will depart with your purpose accomplished.
I wish to be led by you to the ocean, the abode of <s>Varuṇa</s>.
I shall offer water to my high-souled brother, who has gone to heaven.

children.text: tato nītvā tu taṃ deśaṃ tīre nadanadīpateḥ
children.translated_text: Then they led him to that place on the bank of the lord of rivers,
the mighty monkeys leading wing-burned <s>Saṃpāti</s> there.

children.text: punaḥ pratyānayitvā vai taṃ deśaṃ patageśvaram
children.translated_text: And after bringing that lord of birds back again to that place,

children.text: babhūvur vānarā hṛṣṭāḥ pravṛttim upalabhya te ||
children.translated_text: the monkeys became delighted, having obtained news.
Then that speech, with the taste of nectar, spoken by the king of vultures,
those bulls among leapers heard as he spoke, and they rejoiced.

children.text: jāmbavān vai hariśreṣṭhaḥ saha sarvaiḥ plavaṃgamaiḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Jāmbavān</s>, the best of monkeys, together with all the leapers,
rose suddenly from the ground and spoke to the king of vultures:

children.text: kva sītā kena vā dṛṣṭā ko vā harati maithilīm
children.translated_text: Where is <s>Sītā</s>? By whom was she seen? Who is carrying off <s>Maithilī</s>?

children.text: tad ākhyātu bhavān sarvaṃ gatir bhava vanaukasām ||
children.translated_text: Let your honor tell all that. Be the refuge of the forest-dwellers.
Who would not take thought of the valor of <s>Dāśarathi</s>'s arrows,

children.text: svayaṃ lakṣmaṇam uktānāṃ na cintayati vikramam ||
children.translated_text: falling with the speed of thunderbolts, and of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> himself when roused?
Then, pleased, he again reassured the monkeys, who were full of joy

children.text: punar āśvāsayan prīta idaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: and intent on hearing of <s>Sītā</s>, and spoke these words:

children.text: śrūyatām iha vaidehyā yathā me haraṇaṃ śrutam
children.translated_text: Hear here how I heard of the abduction of <s>Vaidehī</s>,
and by whom it was told to me, and where the wide-eyed one is.

children.text: aham asmin girau durge bahuyojanam āyate
children.translated_text: On this difficult mountain, extending for many yojanas,
I have long lain fallen, old, with my life and courage diminished.

children.text: taṃ mām evaṃgataṃ putraḥ supārśvo nāma nāmataḥ
children.translated_text: My son, known by the name <s>Supārśva</s>, supports me in this condition,
O best of birds, with food at the proper time.
The <s>Gandharvas</s> are keen in passion, serpents keen in anger,

children.text: mṛgāṇāṃ tu bhayaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ tatastīkṣṇakṣudhā vayam ||
children.translated_text: deer are keen in fear, and therefore we are keen in hunger.
Once, when I was tormented by hunger and longing for food,
my son came to me after sunset, without meat.
Because of my old age and anger, I rebuked him,
the young best of birds, while I was overcome by hunger and thirst.
He, pained by having obstructed my food, he who increases my joy,
conciliated me and then spoke these words truthfully:

children.text: ahaṃ tāta yathākālam āmiṣārthī kham āplutaḥ
children.translated_text: Father, at the proper time I flew up into the sky in search of meat,

children.text: mahendrasya girer dvāram āvṛtya ca samāsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and stationed myself blocking the gateway of mount <s>Mahendra</s>.
There, facing downward, I alone resolved to block the path
of thousands of creatures moving through the midst of the ocean.
There I saw someone, dark like a mass of split collyrium,
going along carrying a woman whose splendor was like sunrise.
Desiring food, when I saw those two, I made up my mind.
But he humbly and gently asked me for passage.

children.text: na hi sāmopapannānāṃ prahartā vidyate kvacit
children.translated_text: For nowhere is there found anyone who strikes those who come with conciliation,

children.text: nīceṣvapi janaḥ kaścit kim aṅga bata madvidhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even among base people; how much less, indeed, one such as I.

children.text: sa yātastejasā vyoma saṃkṣipann iva vegataḥ
children.translated_text: He went on, seeming to compress the sky by his brilliance and speed.
Then beings who move in the sky approached me and honored me.
The great seers said to me, 'By good fortune you live, dear one.
Somehow he has gone past you together with the woman; without doubt, may there be well-being.'
Thus addressed by those exceedingly splendid siddhas,

children.text: sa ca me rāvaṇo rājā rakṣasāṃ prativeditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I was informed that he was <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, king of the <s>Rākṣasas</s>,
carrying off the wife of <s>Rāma</s> <s>Dāśarathi</s>, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,
her ornaments and silk garments slipped away, overcome by the force of grief,
crying the names of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, with her hair loosened.
This, then, is how the delay occurred, O best of those skilled in speech.

children.text: etam arthaṃ samagraṃ me supārśvaḥ pratyavedayat
children.translated_text: <s>Supārśva</s> reported this whole matter to me completely.

children.text: tacchrutvāpi hi me buddhir nāsīt kācit parākrame ||
children.translated_text: Yet even after hearing it, I had no thought at all of heroic action.

children.text: apakṣo hi kathaṃ pakṣī karma kiṃcid upakramet
children.translated_text: For how could a bird without wings undertake any deed?

children.text: yat tu śakyaṃ mayā kartuṃ vāgbuddhiguṇavartinā ||
children.translated_text: But hear what I can do, since I still possess the virtues of speech and understanding.
I shall tell that to you, founded on your own manly effort.

children.text: vāṅmatibhyāṃ hi sarveṣāṃ kariṣyāmi priyaṃ hi vaḥ
children.translated_text: For with speech and thought I shall do what is pleasing for you all.

children.text: yaddhi dāśaratheḥ kāryaṃ mama tannātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever is the task of <s>Dāśarathi</s> is mine as well; there is no doubt here.
You are best in counsel, strong, and high-spirited,
and, united with the monkey king, unassailable even by the gods.
And the sharp, heron-feathered arrows of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>
are sufficient in all the three worlds for protection and punishment.
Granted, <s>Daśagrīva</s> is endowed with brilliance and strength;

children.text: bhavatāṃ tu samarthānāṃ na kiṃcid api duṣkaram ||
children.translated_text: but for capable ones such as you nothing at all is difficult.
Therefore enough of wasting time. Let a firm decision be made.

children.text: na hi karmasu sajjante buddhimanto bhavadvidhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For wise men such as you do not become stuck in their undertakings.

children.text: tataḥ kṛtodakaṃ snātaṃ taṃ gṛdhraṃ hariyūthapāḥ
children.translated_text: Then the leaders of the monkey troops, after he had offered water and bathed,
sat down around that vulture on the difficult mountain on every side.

children.text: tam aṅgadam upāsīnaṃ taiḥ sarvair haribhir vṛtam
children.translated_text: To <s>Aṅgada</s>, who was sitting near him and surrounded by all those monkeys,
<s>Saṃpāti</s>, his confidence born, again spoke out of joy:

children.text: kṛtvā niḥśabdam ekāgrāḥ śṛṇvantu harayo mama
children.translated_text: Let the monkeys become silent and one-pointed; let them hear from me.
I shall proclaim the truth, as I know it, about <s>Maithilī</s>.

children.text: asya vindhyasya śikhare patito 'smi purā vane
children.translated_text: Long ago I fell on the peak of this <s>Vindhya</s>, in the forest,
my limbs overcome by the heat of the sun, burned by the sun's rays.
After six nights I regained consciousness, helpless and as if bewildered.
Looking at all the directions, I did not recognize anything.

children.text: tatastu sāgarāñ śailānnadīḥ sarvāḥ sarāṃsi ca
children.translated_text: Then, after I had surveyed the oceans, mountains, all the rivers and lakes,
and the forests and woodland regions, my understanding returned.
Crowded with flocks of delighted birds and possessing peaks within its caves,
this is certainly the <s>Vindhya</s>, on the shore of the southern ocean.
And here there was a holy hermitage, highly honored even by the gods,
in which a seer named <s>Niśākara</s> had performed fierce austerity.
For eight thousand years, without that seer,

children.text: vasato mama dharmajñāḥ svargate tu niśākare ||
children.translated_text: I lived here, O knowers of <s>dharma</s>, after <s>Niśākara</s> had gone to heaven.
Descending from the summit of <s>Vindhya</s>, with difficulty and slowly from the rugged place,
I came again, painfully, to the earth covered with sharp darbha grass.
I wished to see that seer, and I came to him in great distress;

children.text: jaṭāyuṣā mayā caiva bahuśo 'bhigato hi saḥ ||
children.translated_text: for he had often been approached by <s>Jaṭāyus</s> and by me.
Near the grounds of his hermitage fragrant winds blew,

children.text: vṛkṣo nāpuṣpitaḥ kaścid aphalo vā na dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: and no tree was seen that was without flowers or without fruit.
Having reached the holy hermitage, I took shelter at the root of a tree,
and, wishing to see the venerable <s>Niśākara</s>, I waited.
Then I saw the seer not far away, blazing with splendor,
bathed, irresistible, and turned back facing north.

children.text: tam ṛkṣāḥ sṛmarā vyāghrāḥ siṃhā nāgāḥ sarīsṛpāḥ
children.translated_text: Bears, antelopes, tigers, lions, elephants, and reptiles
came up around him, as living beings approach a giver.

children.text: tataḥ prāptam ṛṣiṃ jñātvā tāni sattvāni vai yayuḥ
children.translated_text: Then, when they knew that the seer had arrived, those creatures went away,

children.text: praviṣṭe rājani yathā sarvaṃ sāmātyakaṃ balam ||
children.translated_text: as the whole army with its ministers withdraws when the king has entered.

children.text: ṛṣistu dṛṣṭvā māṃ tuṣṭaḥ praviṣṭaścāśramaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: But the seer, seeing me, was pleased; and after he had entered the hermitage again,
he came out after only a moment and then asked my business.

children.text: saumya vaikalyatāṃ dṛṣṭvā romṇāṃ te nāvagamyate
children.translated_text: Dear one, seeing the disfigurement of your plumage, you cannot be recognized.

children.text: agnidagdhāvimau pakṣau tvak caiva vraṇitā tava ||
children.translated_text: These two wings of yours are burned by fire, and your skin is wounded.

children.text: dvau gṛdhrau dṛṣṭapūrvau me mātariśvasamau jave
children.translated_text: I have seen before two vultures, equal to <s>Mātariśvan</s> in speed,
kings of the vultures, brothers, able to assume any form they wished.

children.text: jyeṣṭhastvaṃ tu ca saṃpātir jaṭāyur anujastava
children.translated_text: You are the elder, <s>Saṃpāti</s>, and <s>Jaṭāyus</s> is your younger brother;

children.text: mānuṣaṃ rūpam āsthāya gṛhṇītāṃ caraṇau mama ||
children.translated_text: taking on human form, you two would clasp my feet.

children.text: kiṃ te vyādhisamutthānaṃ pakṣayoḥ patanaṃ katham
children.translated_text: What is the origin of this affliction of yours? How did your wings fall away?

children.text: daṇḍo vāyaṃ dhṛtaḥ kena sarvam ākhyāhi pṛcchataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or by whom was this punishment inflicted? Tell me everything, since I ask.

children.text: tatastad dāruṇaṃ karma duṣkaraṃ sāhasāt kṛtam
children.translated_text: Then I told the sage all about that dreadful deed,
hard to perform and rashly done, and also about following the sun.
Venerable sir, because I am wounded and because shame has overwhelmed my senses,
I am exhausted and cannot speak my words fully.
I and <s>Jaṭāyus</s>, driven by rivalry and deluded by pride,
flew into the sky like two heroes, eager to display our prowess.
On the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>, before the sages, we made a wager:

children.text: raviḥ syād anuyātavyo yāvad astaṃ mahāgirim ||
children.translated_text: the sun was to be followed until it set at the great mountain.
Then, having risen at the same time, we looked down on the earth below,
and saw cities here and there, each the size of a chariot wheel.
In some places we heard the sounds of instruments and the sounds of Vedic recitation,
and we saw many women singing, dressed in red garments.
Swiftly flying up into the sky and taking to the path of the sun,
we looked down on that forest standing amid grassy ground.

children.text: upalair iva saṃchannā dṛśyate bhūḥ śiloccayaiḥ
children.translated_text: The earth, covered with heaps of rock, appeared as if strewn with pebbles,
and the land, encircled by rivers, looked as if wrapped with threads.
<s>Himavat</s>, <s>Vindhya</s>, and <s>Meru</s>, that very great mountain,
shone on the surface of the earth like elephants in a pool of water.
Then intense sweat, exhaustion, and fear came upon us both,
and delusion entered us, and from delusion came terrible fainting.

children.text: na dig vijñāyate yāmyā nāgneyā na ca vāruṇī
children.translated_text: The southern direction was no longer known, nor the southeastern, nor the western;

children.text: yugānte niyato loko hato dagdha ivāgninā ||
children.translated_text: the world seemed fixed at the end of an age, struck down and burned by fire.
With great effort the sun was looked at again,
and the radiant one appeared to us equal in measure to the earth.

children.text: jaṭāyur mām anāpṛcchya nipapāta mahīṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Jaṭāyus</s>, without consulting me, fell down to the earth;

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā tūrṇam ākāśād ātmānaṃ muktavān aham ||
children.translated_text: seeing him, I swiftly released myself from the sky.

children.text: pakṣibhyāṃ ca mayā gupto jaṭāyur na pradahyata
children.translated_text: Protected by my two wings, <s>Jaṭāyus</s> was not burned,

children.text: pramādāt tatra nirdagdhaḥ patan vāyupathād aham ||
children.translated_text: but through heedlessness I was burned there as I fell from the path of the wind.
I suppose that <s>Jaṭāyus</s> fell in <s>Janasthāna</s>;

children.text: ahaṃ tu patito vindhye dagdhapakṣo jaḍīkṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but I fell on <s>Vindhya</s>, my wings burned and my senses numbed.

children.text: rājyena hīno bhrātrā ca pakṣābhyāṃ vikrameṇa ca
children.translated_text: Bereft of kingdom, of brother, of wings, and of valor,

children.text: sarvathā martum evecchan patiṣye śikharād gireḥ ||
children.translated_text: wishing in every way only to die, I shall cast myself from the mountain peak.

children.text: evam uktvā muniśreṣṭham arudaṃ duḥkhito bhṛśam
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to the best of sages, I wept, greatly distressed;

children.text: atha dhyātvā muhūrtaṃ tu bhagavān idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: then the venerable one, after meditating for a moment, said this:

children.text: pakṣau ca te prapakṣau ca punar anyau bhaviṣyataḥ
children.translated_text: Your wings and your outer pinions will grow again, different and new,

children.text: cakṣuṣī caiva prāṇāśca vikramaśca balaṃ ca te ||
children.translated_text: and your eyes, life-breaths, vigor, and strength will also be yours.

children.text: purāṇe sumahat kāryaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ hi mayā śrutam
children.translated_text: For I have heard in ancient lore of a very great deed that is to come,

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ me tapasā caiva śrutvā ca viditaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: and I have seen it by austerity; having heard it, it is known to me.
There will be a king named <s>Daśaratha</s>, a delight of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> line;

children.text: tasya putro mahātejā rāmo nāma bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: his son, of great brilliance, will be named <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: araṇyaṃ ca saha bhrātrā lakṣmaṇena gamiṣyati
children.translated_text: Together with his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, he will go to the forest,

children.text: tasminn arthe niyuktaḥ san pitrā satyaparākramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: appointed to that purpose by his father, he whose valor is true.

children.text: nairṛto rāvaṇo nāma tasyā bhāryāṃ hariṣyati
children.translated_text: A Rākṣasa named <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, belonging to the southwest, will carry off his wife;
that lord of Rākṣasas, invulnerable to gods and Dānavas, will take her from <s>Janasthāna</s>.

children.text: sā ca kāmaiḥ pralobhyantī bhakṣyair bhojyaiśca maithilī
children.translated_text: And she, <s>Maithilī</s>, though tempted with desires and with foods to be eaten and enjoyed,
will not eat, that illustrious and greatly fortunate woman, sunk in sorrow.

children.text: paramānnaṃ tu vaidehyā jñātvā dāsyati vāsavaḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Vāsava</s>, recognizing <s>Vaidehī</s>, will give her the choicest food,

children.text: yad annam amṛtaprakhyaṃ surāṇām api durlabham ||
children.translated_text: food like nectar, difficult even for the gods to obtain.

children.text: tad annaṃ maithilī prāpya vijñāyendrād idaṃ tviti
children.translated_text: Having received that food, <s>Maithilī</s>, understanding, 'This is from <s>Indra</s>,'
will lift out the first portion and place it on the ground as an offering for <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: yadi jīvati me bhartā lakṣmaṇena saha prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: 'If my lord husband lives together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: devatvaṃ gatayor vāpi tayor annam idaṃ tviti ||
children.translated_text: or even if those two have attained divine state, this food is for them.'
The searchers for her will come, the leaping messengers of <s>Rāma</s>;
you, O bird, must tell them about <s>Rāma</s>'s queen.

children.text: sarvathā tu na gantavyam īdṛśaḥ kva gamiṣyasi
children.translated_text: In every way you must not go; where could you go in such a condition?
Wait for the proper place and time; you will regain your wings.

children.text: utsaheyam ahaṃ kartum adyaiva tvāṃ sapakṣakam
children.translated_text: I could make you winged even today,

children.text: ihasthastvaṃ tu lokānāṃ hitaṃ kāryaṃ kariṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: but while staying here you will accomplish a deed beneficial to the worlds.

children.text: tvayāpi khalu tat kāryaṃ tayośca nṛpaputrayoḥ
children.translated_text: That deed is surely to be done by you also, for those two princes,

children.text: brāhmaṇānāṃ surāṇāṃ ca munīnāṃ vāsavasya ca ||
children.translated_text: and for the Brahmins, the gods, the sages, and <s>Vāsava</s>.
I too wish to see the brothers <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>;
I do not wish to hold my life for long; I shall abandon the body.
With these and many other words, that expert in speech

children.text: māṃ praśasyābhyanujñāpya praviṣṭaḥ sa svam āśramam ||
children.translated_text: praised me, gave me permission, and entered his own hermitage.

children.text: kandarāt tu visarpitvā parvatasya śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: Creeping out slowly from the mountain cave,
I climbed <s>Vindhya</s> and have been waiting for you.

children.text: adya tvetasya kālasya sāgraṃ varṣaśataṃ gatam
children.translated_text: Today more than a full hundred years of this time have passed,
and I have been waiting for the proper place and time, keeping the sage's words in my heart.
But when <s>Niśākara</s> attained the great departure and went to heaven,

children.text: māṃ nirdahati saṃtāpo vitarkair bahubhir vṛtam ||
children.translated_text: grief burned me, surrounded as I was by many anxious thoughts.
I restrain the thought that rises toward death by means of the sage's words.

children.text: buddhir yā tena me dattā prāṇasaṃrakṣaṇāya tu
children.translated_text: That understanding which he gave me for the protection of my life
drives away my sorrow like a blazing flame of fire driving away darkness.

children.text: budhyatā ca mayā vīryaṃ rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: And when I perceived the power of wicked <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: putraḥ saṃtarjito vāgbhir na trātā maithilī katham ||
children.translated_text: why was <s>Maithilī</s> not rescued by my son, after he had merely threatened him with words?

children.text: tasyā vilapitaṃ śrutvā tau ca sītāvinākṛtau
children.translated_text: Hearing her lament, and seeing those two deprived of <s>Sītā</s>,
my son produced no pleasure for me, because of my affection for <s>Daśaratha</s>.

children.text: tasya tvevaṃ bruvāṇasya saṃpāter vānaraiḥ saha
children.translated_text: While <s>Saṃpāti</s> was speaking thus with the monkeys,
then his two wings sprang up before the eyes of the forest-dwellers.

children.text: sa dṛṣṭvā svāṃ tanuṃ pakṣair udgatair aruṇacchadaiḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing his own body with wings grown forth, with reddish feathers,
he gained incomparable delight and said this to the monkeys:
By the power of the great sage <s>Niśākara</s>, immeasurable in spirit,
my wings, burned by the sun's rays, have risen again.
The valor which I had when I was in youth,

children.text: tam evādyāvagacchāmi balaṃ pauruṣam eva ca ||
children.translated_text: that very strength and manliness I now recognize again today.
By all means let effort be made; you will find <s>Sītā</s>.
This gaining of wings by me is a cause of confidence in your success.

children.text: ityuktvā tān harīn sarvān saṃpātiḥ patatāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to all those monkeys, <s>Saṃpāti</s>, best of flying beings,
flew up from the mountain peak, wishing to test a bird's course.
Hearing that speech of his, their minds gladdened and thrilled,
the tiger-like monkeys became intent on the rise of their valor.
Then the best of leapers, equal to the wind in prowess and with their manliness restored,
went toward the quarter of <s>Abhijit</s>, intent on searching for <s>Janaka</s>'s daughter.
Having been informed by the vulture-king, the leapers rose up
and came together, joined in joy, roaring, lion-like in prowess.
Hearing <s>Saṃpāti</s>'s words, the monkeys, eager for <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s destruction,
joyfully came to the ocean, longing to see <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: abhikramya tu taṃ deśaṃ dadṛśur bhīmavikramāḥ
children.translated_text: Advancing to that region, those terrible in valor saw

children.text: kṛtsnaṃ lokasya mahataḥ pratibimbam iva sthitam ||
children.translated_text: what stood like a reflection of the whole great world.
Having reached the northern side of the southern ocean,
the best of monkeys then made camp together.

children.text: sattvair mahadbhir vikṛtaiḥ krīḍadbhir vividhair jale
children.translated_text: It was crowded with great, misshapen beings of many kinds, playing in the water,
with gaping mouths and huge bodies, and it was thronged with waves.

children.text: prasuptam iva cānyatra krīḍantam iva cānyataḥ
children.translated_text: In one place it seemed asleep, and in another as if playing,
somewhere covered with masses of water the size of mountains.
Crowded also with lords of <s>Dānavas</s> dwelling on the floor of <s>Pātāla</s>,
the monkey chiefs, seeing it hair-raising, became despondent.

children.text: ākāśam iva duṣpāraṃ sāgaraṃ prekṣya vānarāḥ
children.translated_text: Beholding the ocean, hard to cross like the sky, the monkeys

children.text: viṣeduḥ sahasā sarve kathaṃ kāryam iti bruvan ||
children.translated_text: all at once became despondent, saying, 'How can the task be done?'
Seeing the army despondent from looking at the ocean,
the best of monkeys comforted the frightened monkeys.

children.text: na niṣādena naḥ kāryaṃ viṣādo doṣavattaraḥ
children.translated_text: We have no business with dejection; dejection is deeply blameworthy.

children.text: viṣādo hanti puruṣaṃ bālaṃ kruddha ivoragaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Dejection destroys a man like an angry serpent destroying a child.
This dejection overpowers one when valor is close at hand;

children.text: tejasā tasya hīnasya puruṣārtho na sidhyati ||
children.translated_text: for a man deprived of its energy, the human goal is not accomplished.

children.text: tasyāṃ rātryāṃ vyatītāyām aṅgado vānaraiḥ saha
children.translated_text: When that night had passed, <s>Aṅgada</s>, together with the monkeys,
met with the elders of the monkeys and again held counsel.
That army of monkeys shone, surrounding <s>Aṅgada</s>,
like the host of the <s>Maruts</s> standing around <s>Vāsava</s>.

children.text: ko 'nyastāṃ vānarīṃ senāṃ śaktaḥ stambhayituṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Who else could be able to hold back that monkey army,
apart from the son of <s>Vāli</s>, and apart from <s>Hanūmat</s>?
Then, after honoring those elder monkeys and that army, the subduer of foes,
the illustrious <s>Aṅgada</s> spoke a meaningful speech.
Who now, O very splendid ones, will leap across the ocean?
Who will make <s>Sugrīva</s>, truthful in his pledge and subduer of foes, successful?
What hero, O monkeys, could leap a hundred yojanas?
And who could free all these troop-leaders from great danger?

children.text: kasya prasādād dārāṃśca putrāṃścaiva gṛhāṇi ca
children.translated_text: By whose favor, having returned from here with our purpose accomplished,

children.text: ito nivṛttāḥ paśyema siddhārthāḥ sukhino vayam ||
children.translated_text: may we happily see our wives, sons, and homes?

children.text: kasya prasādād rāmaṃ ca lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahābalam
children.translated_text: By whose favor may we go joyfully to mighty <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
and also to mighty <s>Sugrīva</s>?

children.text: yadi kaścit samartho vaḥ sāgaraplavane hariḥ
children.translated_text: If any monkey among you is able to leap across the ocean,

children.text: sa dadātviha naḥ śīghraṃ puṇyām abhayadakṣiṇām ||
children.translated_text: let him quickly give us here the blessed gift of fearlessness.

children.text: aṅgadasya vacaḥ śrutvā na kaścit kiṃcid abravīt
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Aṅgada</s>'s words, no one said anything at all.
The whole monkey host there became as if motionless.

children.text: punar evāṅgadaḥ prāha tān harīn harisattamaḥ
children.translated_text: Again <s>Aṅgada</s>, best of monkeys, spoke to those monkeys:
All of you are foremost among the strong and firm in valor.
You were born in distinguished families and are constantly honored.

children.text: na hi vo gamane saṃgaḥ kadācid api kasyacit ||
children.translated_text: Surely there is never any impediment at all for any of you in going.

children.text: bruvadhvaṃ yasya yā śaktir gamane plavagarṣabhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Tell, O bulls among leaping monkeys, what each one's capacity is for going.
Then, hearing <s>Aṅgada</s>'s words, all those best of monkeys

children.text: svaṃ svaṃ gatau samutsāham āhustatra yathākramam ||
children.translated_text: declared in order their own eagerness for the journey.
<s>Gaja</s>, <s>Gavākṣa</s>, <s>Gavaya</s>, <s>Śarabha</s>, <s>Gandhamādana</s>,
and <s>Mainda</s>, <s>Dvivida</s>, <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, and <s>Jāmbavān</s> as well spoke.
There <s>Gaja</s> said, I can leap ten yojanas.
<s>Gavākṣa</s> said, I shall go twenty yojanas.
There the monkey <s>Gavaya</s> said to those monkeys,
O leaping monkeys, I shall go thirty yojanas.
There the monkey <s>Śarabha</s> said to those monkeys,
I shall go forty yojanas, without doubt.
The very splendid <s>Gandhamādana</s> said to the monkeys,

children.text: yojanānāṃ gamiṣyāmi pañcāśat tu na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall go fifty yojanas, without doubt.
There the monkey <s>Mainda</s> said to those monkeys,

children.text: yojanānāṃ paraṃ ṣaṣṭim ahaṃ plavitum utsahe ||
children.translated_text: I am able to leap as far as sixty yojanas.
Then the very splendid <s>Dvivida</s> replied there,
Without doubt, I shall go seventy yojanas.
<s>Suṣeṇa</s>, best of monkeys, said to the excellent monkeys,
O bulls among leaping monkeys, I could leap eighty yojanas.

children.text: teṣāṃ kathayatāṃ tatra sarvāṃstān anumānya ca
children.translated_text: When they had spoken there, and after having acknowledged them all,
then <s>Jāmbavān</s>, the eldest of them, replied:
Formerly we too possessed a certain vigor in movement,

children.text: te vayaṃ vayasaḥ pāram anuprāptāḥ sma sāmpratam ||
children.translated_text: but now we have reached the far limit of age.

children.text: kiṃ tu naivaṃ gate śakyam idaṃ kāryam upekṣitum
children.translated_text: Even so, when matters stand thus, this task cannot be neglected,
for the sake of which both the monkey king and <s>Rāma</s> have formed their resolve.
Now hear what speed remains to me with the change brought by time:

children.text: navatiṃ yojanānāṃ tu gamiṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall go ninety yojanas, without doubt.

children.text: tāṃśca sarvān hariśreṣṭhāñ jāmbavān punar abravīt
children.translated_text: <s>Jāmbavān</s> again addressed all those best of monkeys:

children.text: na khalvetāvad evāsīd gamane me parākramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: My prowess in going was certainly not only this much.
By me and by the very mighty ones, eternal <s>Viṣṇu</s>
was formerly circumambulated at the sacrifice as he strode forth as <s>Trivikrama</s>.

children.text: sa idānīm ahaṃ vṛddhaḥ plavane mandavikramaḥ
children.translated_text: That I am now old, slow in prowess for leaping.

children.text: yauvane ca tadāsīnme balam apratimaṃ paraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: In youth, however, my strength then was unmatched by others.
At present I judge my capacity for going to be just so much.
And with that much, the accomplishment of this task will not come about.
Then wise <s>Aṅgada</s>, after honoring the great monkey <s>Jāmbavān</s>,
spoke a further reply, noble in meaning.

children.text: aham etad gamiṣyāmi yojanānāṃ śataṃ mahat
children.translated_text: I shall go this great distance of a hundred yojanas.

children.text: nivartane tu me śaktiḥ syānna veti na niścitam ||
children.translated_text: But whether or not I have the power to return is not certain.
The best of monkeys, <s>Jāmbavān</s>, skilled in speech, said to him:
Your power for going is known, O best of monkeys and bears.

children.text: kāmaṃ śatasahasraṃ vā na hyeṣa vidhir ucyate
children.translated_text: Indeed, your honor is able to go and return
even a hundred thousand yojanas, if you wish; yet this is not called the proper rule.

children.text: na hi preṣayitā tāta svāmī preṣyaḥ kathaṃcana
children.translated_text: For the sender, dear one, the master, is never to be sent by any means.
This whole company is to be sent by you, O best of leaping monkeys.
You are our protected household, established in the position of lord.

children.text: svāmī kalatraṃ sainyasya gatir eṣā paraṃtapa ||
children.translated_text: The lord is the protected household of the army; this is the rule, O scorcher of foes.

children.text: tasmāt kalatravat tāta pratipālyaḥ sadā bhavān
children.translated_text: Therefore, dear one, you must always be guarded like a household.
Moreover, your honor is the root of this task, O subduer of foes.

children.text: mūlam arthasya saṃrakṣyam eṣa kāryavidāṃ nayaḥ
children.translated_text: The root of a matter must be protected; this is the policy of those who know how tasks are done.

children.text: mūle hi sati sidhyanti guṇāḥ puṣpaphalādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For when the root exists, the qualities, flowers, fruits, and the rest come to perfection.

children.text: tad bhavān asyā kāryasya sādhane satyavikramaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore your honor, true in valor, in accomplishing this task
is the cause here, endowed with wisdom and courage, O scorcher of foes.

children.text: guruśca guruputraśca tvaṃ hi naḥ kapisattama
children.translated_text: You are our elder and the son of our elder, O excellent monkey.
Depending on you, we are indeed capable of achieving the objective.
When the great monkey <s>Jāmbavān</s>, very wise, had spoken these words,
<s>Aṅgada</s>, son of <s>Vāli</s>, then answered him with a further speech:
If I do not go, no other bull among monkeys will...
Again, surely, we must undertake this fasting unto death.

children.text: na hyakṛtvā haripateḥ saṃdeśaṃ tasya dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: For without carrying out the command of that wise lord of the monkeys,
even if we go there, I do not see any preservation of our lives.

children.text: sa hi prasāde cātyarthaṃ kope ca harir īśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: For that monkey lord has full power both in favor and in anger;

children.text: atītya tasya saṃdeśaṃ vināśo gamane bhavet ||
children.translated_text: if we pass beyond his command, destruction would come from going back.

children.text: tad yathā hyasya kāryasya na bhavatyanyathā gatiḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, since there is no other course for this task,

children.text: tad bhavān eva dṛṣṭārthaḥ saṃcintayitum arhati ||
children.translated_text: you yourself, who have seen the matter, ought to consider it.
When the heroic bull among leaping monkeys was thus answered by <s>Aṅgada</s>,
<s>Jāmbavān</s> then spoke this further word to <s>Aṅgada</s>:

children.text: asya te vīra kāryasya na kiṃcit parihīyate
children.translated_text: O hero, nothing at all is lacking in this undertaking of yours.
I shall now urge on this one, who will accomplish the task.

children.text: tataḥ pratītaṃ plavatāṃ variṣṭham ekāntam āśritya sukhopaviṣṭam
children.translated_text: Then, approaching apart the most eminent of leapers, confident and seated at ease,
the heroic monkey urged on that very heroic monkey, <s>Hanumān</s>.
Seeing the monkey army, many hundreds of thousands strong, sunk in despair,
<s>Jāmbavān</s> then spoke thus to <s>Hanumān</s>:
O hero of the monkey world, versed in every śāstra,

children.text: tūṣṇīm ekāntam āśritya hanuman kiṃ na jalpasi ||
children.translated_text: why, <s>Hanumān</s>, do you sit silently apart and say nothing?
For, <s>Hanumān</s>, you are equal to <s>Sugrīva</s>, king of the monkeys,
and also to <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> in splendor and in strength.
The mighty <s>Garutmān</s>, <s>Vainateya</s>, son of <s>Ariṣṭanemi</s>,
is famed as the highest among all birds.

children.text: bahuśo hi mayā dṛṣṭaḥ sāgare sa mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: I have often seen that mighty bird in the ocean,
of great speed and great fame, carrying off serpents.

children.text: pakṣayor yad balaṃ tasya tāvad bhujabalaṃ tava
children.translated_text: As much strength as there is in his two wings, so much strength is there in your arms;
and in prowess and speed you are not inferior to him.

children.text: balaṃ buddhiśca tejaśca sattvaṃ ca harisattama
children.translated_text: Strength, intelligence, splendor, and courage are yours, best of monkeys,

children.text: viśiṣṭaṃ sarvabhūteṣu kim ātmānaṃ na budhyase ||
children.translated_text: surpassing those of all beings; why do you not recognize yourself?
Among the apsarases there was a foremost apsaras, famous as <s>Puñjikasthalā</s>,
renowned as <s>Añjanā</s>, the wife of the monkey <s>Kesari</s>.
Because of a curse, dear one, she became a monkey-woman, able to assume any form,
the daughter of the great-souled monkey lord <s>Kuñjara</s>.
While in monkey form, lovely in every limb, and able at times to take any shape,
she assumed a human body, endowed with the fullness of youth,
and wandered on the peak of a mountain that resembled a rain cloud,
wearing varied garlands and ornaments and garments of costly linen.

children.text: tasyā vastraṃ viśālākṣyāḥ pītaṃ raktadaśaṃ śubham
children.translated_text: As she stood on the mountain peak, broad-eyed, her auspicious yellow garment with red border
was slowly carried away by the wind.
Then he saw her rounded, well-formed thighs,

children.text: stanau ca pīnau sahitau sujātaṃ cāru cānanam ||
children.translated_text: her full breasts close together, and her handsome, lovely face.
Seeing that illustrious woman, broad and wide in the hips, slender in the waist,
auspicious in every limb, <s>Pavana</s> was overcome by desire.

children.text: sa tāṃ bhujābhyāṃ pīnābhyāṃ paryaṣvajata mārutaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Māruta</s> embraced that blameless woman with his strong arms,
his whole body possessed by passion, his self-control gone.

children.text: sā tu tatraiva saṃbhrāntā suvṛttā vākyam abravīt
children.translated_text: But there, startled, that well-formed woman spoke these words:
Who wishes to destroy this vow of mine to one husband?
Hearing <s>Añjanā</s>'s words, <s>Māruta</s> answered:

children.text: na tvāṃ hiṃsāmi suśroṇi mā bhūt te subhage bhayam ||
children.translated_text: I do not violate you, fair-hipped one; let there be no fear for you, fortunate lady.

children.text: manasāsmi gato yat tvāṃ pariṣvajya yaśasvini
children.translated_text: Since I have approached you in thought, embracing you, illustrious woman,
a son will be born to you, mighty and endowed with intelligence.

children.text: abhyutthitaṃ tataḥ sūryaṃ bālo dṛṣṭvā mahāvane
children.translated_text: Then, as a child in the great forest, seeing the sun risen,
you thought, 'It is a fruit,' and, wishing to seize it, leapt up and flew into the sky.
After you had gone three hundred yojanas, great monkey,

children.text: tejasā tasya nirdhūto na viṣādaṃ tato gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: though blasted by its brilliance, you did not fall into despondency.
As you were swiftly rushing through the midair, great monkey,

children.text: kṣiptam indreṇa te vajraṃ krodhāviṣṭena dhīmatā ||
children.translated_text: the thunderbolt was hurled at you by wise <s>Indra</s>, who was filled with anger.
Then, on the summit of a mountain peak, your left jaw was broken;

children.text: tato hi nāmadheyaṃ te hanumān iti kīrtyate ||
children.translated_text: therefore your name is celebrated as <s>Hanumān</s>.

children.text: tatastvāṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā vāyur gandhavahaḥ svayam
children.translated_text: Then, seeing you struck down, <s>Vāyu</s>, the bearer of fragrance himself,

children.text: trailokye bhṛśasaṃkruddho na vavau vai prabhañjanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: became fiercely angry throughout the three worlds, and the wind did not blow.

children.text: saṃbhrāntāśca surāḥ sarve trailokye kṣubhite sati
children.translated_text: All the gods were alarmed when the three worlds were thrown into agitation,
and the lords of beings sought to appease the angered <s>Māruta</s>.

children.text: prasādite ca pavane brahmā tubhyaṃ varaṃ dadau
children.translated_text: When <s>Pavana</s> had been appeased, <s>Brahmā</s> gave you a boon:
that you would not be slain by weapons in battle, dear one of true valor.

children.text: vajrasya ca nipātena virujaṃ tvāṃ samīkṣya ca
children.translated_text: And seeing you free from pain after the fall of the thunderbolt,

children.text: sahasranetraḥ prītātmā dadau te varam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: the Thousand-eyed one, pleased in heart, gave you an excellent boon:

children.text: svacchandataśca maraṇaṃ te bhūyād iti vai prabho
children.translated_text: that your death should occur only at your own will, O lord.

children.text: sa tvaṃ kesariṇaḥ putraḥ kṣetrajo bhīmavikramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus you are the kṣetra-born son of <s>Kesari</s>, terrible in valor,
and the natural son of <s>Māruta</s>, equal to him in splendor.

children.text: tvaṃ hi vāyusuto vatsa plavane cāpi tatsamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: You are indeed the son of <s>Vāyu</s>, child, and equal to him also in leaping.

children.text: vayam adya gataprāṇā bhavān asmāsu sāmpratam
children.translated_text: Today we are as if our lives are gone; you are now among us,
endowed with skill and prowess, like another king of birds.
At the time of <s>Trivikrama</s>, dear one, I circled the earth, with its mountains, forests, and groves,
three times seven times in clockwise course.
Then herbs were gathered by us at the command of the gods,
by which the nectar was prepared; at that time my strength was very great.
But now I am old, my valor diminished.
At this present time, you, endowed with every virtue, are our refuge.

children.text: tad vijṛmbhasva vikrāntaḥ plavatām uttamo hyasi
children.translated_text: Therefore expand yourself, mighty one; for you are the best of those who leap.
This whole monkey army longs to see your valor.
Rise up, tiger among monkeys, and leap across the great ocean.

children.text: parā hi sarvabhūtānāṃ hanuman yā gatistava ||
children.translated_text: For, <s>Hanumān</s>, the course that is yours is beyond that of all beings.

children.text: viṣaṇṇā harayaḥ sarve hanuman kim upekṣase
children.translated_text: All the monkeys are despondent; <s>Hanumān</s>, why do you remain indifferent?
Show your might, you of great speed, like <s>Viṣṇu</s> with his three strides.

children.text: tatastu vai jāmbavatābhicoditaḥ pratītavegaḥ pavanātmajaḥ kapiḥ
children.translated_text: Then the monkey, son of the Wind, his speed awakened when urged by <s>Jāmbavān</s>,

children.text: praharṣayaṃstāṃ harivīra vāhinīṃ cakāra rūpaṃ mahad ātmanastadā ||
children.translated_text: gladdening that army of monkey heroes, made his own form immense.
Praised by them, mighty <s>Hanumān</s> grew larger,

children.text: samāvidhya ca lāṅgūlaṃ harṣācca balam eyivān ||
children.translated_text: and, having swung his tail around, he gained strength from joy.
As he was being praised by all the foremost monkeys,
and as he was filled with splendor, his form became unsurpassed.
As a lion, grown huge in a mountain cave, stretches and expands,
so now the true son of <s>Māruta</s> stretched and expanded.
The face of that wise one, as he opened it wide, shone brilliantly,
like a glowing fire-pit, like smokeless fire.
Rising from the midst of the monkeys, with the hair of his body thrilled with joy,

children.text: abhivādya harīn vṛddhān hanumān idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hanumān</s> bowed to the elder monkeys and said this:
The wind, friend of fire, moves in the sky, breaking the peaks of mountains;
he is powerful and immeasurable, coursing through the heavens.
I am the true son of that swift-speeding, quickly moving, great-souled

children.text: mārutasyaurasaḥ putraḥ plavane nāsti me samaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Māruta</s>; in leaping there is no equal to me.
I would be able, without hindrance, to go around the broad mountain <s>Meru</s>
a thousand times, as though tracing the sky.
With the ocean driven on by the force of my arms, I would be able
to flood the world together with its mountains, rivers, and lakes.
By the speed of my thighs and shanks, the ocean, abode of <s>Varuṇa</s>,
will be lifted up, its great sea-monsters thrown into confusion.
In the sky, I am able to circle a thousand times around <s>Vainateya</s>,
the eater of serpents, as he flies, attended by birds.
I am fully able to approach the radiant <s>Āditya</s>, garlanded with rays,
even after he has set forth from sunrise and before he has set.

children.text: tato bhūmim asaṃspṛśya punar āgantum utsahe
children.translated_text: Then, without touching the earth, I am able to return again
with that very great and fearsome speed, bulls among leapers.
I would be able to overtake all beings that move through the sky;
I shall churn the ocean and split the earth.
As I leap, O leaping monkeys, I shall shake the mountains,
and as I leap, I shall carry off the great ocean with the vast speed of my thighs.

children.text: latānāṃ vīrudhāṃ puṣpaṃ pādapānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: The blossoms of vines, creepers, and all trees
will follow me today as I leap through the air.

children.text: bhaviṣyati hi me panthāḥ svāteḥ panthā ivāmbare ||
children.translated_text: For my path in the sky will be like the path of <s>Svāti</s> in the heavens.

children.text: carantaṃ ghoram ākāśam utpatiṣyantam eva ca
children.translated_text: All beings, O monkeys, will see me moving through the dreadful sky,
springing upward and also descending.
You will see me, O leaping monkeys, resembling great <s>Meru</s>,
going while covering the sky, as if swallowing the heavens.
I shall scatter the clouds and make the mountains tremble;
as I leap, composed in mind, I shall churn the ocean.

children.text: vainateyasya vā śaktir mama vā mārutasya vā
children.translated_text: Either <s>Vainateya</s>'s power, or mine, or <s>Māruta</s>'s,
apart from the king of birds or mighty <s>Māruta</s>,

children.text: na hi bhūtaṃ prapaśyāmi yo māṃ plutam anuvrajet ||
children.translated_text: I see no being who could follow me once I have leapt.
In no more than the interval of a blink, through the unsupported sky,
I shall suddenly descend, like lightning rising from a cloud.

children.text: bhaviṣyati hi me rūpaṃ plavamānasya sāgaram
children.translated_text: As I leap over the ocean, my form will then be

children.text: viṣṇoḥ prakramamāṇasya tadā trīn vikramān iva ||
children.translated_text: like that of <s>Viṣṇu</s> when he strode his three strides.

children.text: buddhyā cāhaṃ prapaśyāmi manaśceṣṭā ca me tathā
children.translated_text: And by my understanding I already see it, and so too by the effort of my mind:
I shall see <s>Vaidehī</s>; rejoice, O leaping monkeys.

children.text: mārutasya samo vege garuḍasya samo jave
children.translated_text: Equal to <s>Māruta</s> in speed and equal to <s>Garuḍa</s> in swiftness,

children.text: ayutaṃ yojanānāṃ tu gamiṣyāmīti me matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: I believe I can go ten thousand yojanas.
From the hand of <s>Vāsava</s> with his thunderbolt, or of self-born <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: vikramya sahasā hastād amṛtaṃ tad ihānaye
children.translated_text: I could, with a sudden act of valor, bring that nectar here;

children.text: laṅkāṃ vāpi samutkṣipya gaccheyam iti me matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: or I could even uproot <s>Laṅkā</s> and go with it, so I believe.
To that best of monkeys, roaring in this way, of immeasurable energy,
the greatly delighted <s>Jāmbavān</s>, finest of monkeys, said:
Hero, son of <s>Keśarin</s>, swift son of <s>Māruta</s>,
dear child, you have destroyed the great sorrow of your kinsmen.
The chief monkeys, whose hearts are set on your welfare, have gathered;
with concentrated minds they will perform an auspicious rite for the success of the mission.
By the grace of the sages, by the judgment of the elder monkeys,

children.text: gurūṇāṃ ca prasādena plavasva tvaṃ mahārṇavam ||
children.translated_text: and by the grace of your teachers, leap across the great ocean.
We shall stand on one foot until your return,
and the lives of all the forest-dwellers depend upon you.
Then the tiger among monkeys said to those forest-dwellers:

children.text: neyaṃ mama mahī vegaṃ plavane dhārayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: This earth will not be able to bear my speed as I leap.
But these peaks of this mountain <s>Mahendra</s>, full of masses of rock,

children.text: śikharāṇi mahendrasya sthirāṇi ca mahānti ca ||
children.translated_text: are firm and great.

children.text: etāni mama niṣpeṣaṃ pādayoḥ patatāṃ varāḥ
children.translated_text: These, O best of those who leap, will bear the crushing pressure of my feet
as I leap from here for a hundred yojanas.
Then that monkey, like the wind, the son of the Wind,
the crusher of enemies, climbed <s>Mahendra</s>, the best of mountains.
It was surrounded by trees of many kinds, its grassy slopes frequented by deer,
crowded with creepers and flowers, and bearing trees always in blossom and fruit.
Lions and tigers roamed there, and rutting elephants resorted to it;
it resounded with flocks of excited birds and was crowded with outbursts of water.

children.text: mahadbhir ucchritaṃ śṛṅgair mahendraṃ sa mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: That best of monkeys, mighty in strength and equal in valor to <s>Mahendra</s>,
wandered over great <s>Mahendra</s>, raised high with its lofty peaks.
Pressed by the feet of that great-souled one,
the great mountain roared like a huge rutting elephant struck by a lion.
It released jets of water, its masses of rock scattered about,
its deer and elephants frightened, and its great trees shaken.
With many pairs of <s>Gandharvas</s>, made rough by their drinking revelry,
and with birds flying up, and also with hosts of <s>Vidyādharas</s>,
its broad heights being abandoned and its great serpents hiding away,
that great mountain then had its peaks and rocks struck loose.
With those serpents then hissing, half emerged,
that holder of the earth appeared as if furnished with banners.
The heap of rocks, abandoned by sages terrified and bewildered,
was like a traveler sinking in a great wilderness, deprived of his caravan.
That swift one, his mind gathered into speed, the heroic monkey, the slayer of enemy heroes,

children.text: manaḥ samādhāya mahānubhāvo jagāma laṅkāṃ manasā manasvī ||
children.translated_text: the high-souled and resolute one, fixed his mind and went to <s>Laṅkā</s> in thought.
Then the crusher of foes wished to trace the path
of <s>Sītā</s>, carried away by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, along the way traveled by the <s>Cāraṇas</s>.
Then the mighty and steadfast one wandered at ease
over grassy places blue-green like beryl and resembling water.

children.text: dvijān vitrāsayan dhīmān urasā pādapān haran
children.translated_text: The wise one frightened birds, tore down trees with his chest,

children.text: mṛgāṃśca subahūn nighnan pravṛddha iva kesarī ||
children.translated_text: and struck down very many deer, like a full-grown lion.
It was adorned with natural, variegated mineral ores
blue, red, madder-colored, lotus-hued, white, and black.
It was constantly inhabited by shape-shifting beings with their retinues,
by <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and godlike serpents.
There, at the foot of that best of mountains, filled with excellent elephants,
the best of monkeys stood and shone like an elephant in a lake.
He made reverent añjali to the Sun, to <s>Mahendra</s>, to the Wind, to the Self-born,
and to all beings, and set his mind on going.
Facing east, he made añjali to the Wind, his own source,

children.text: tato hi vavṛdhe gantuṃ dakṣiṇo dakṣiṇāṃ diśam ||
children.translated_text: and then, capable and strong, he increased himself in order to go to the southern quarter.
Seen by the foremost monkeys, resolved upon the leap,
he grew for the increase of <s>Rāma</s>'s cause, like the ocean on the lunar days.
Becoming immeasurable in body and wishing to cross the sea,
he pressed the mountain with his arms and with his feet.
That lovely immovable mountain, pressed by the monkey, trembled for a moment,
and shook down every blossom from the trees whose tips were in flower.
By that fragrant mass of flowers released from the trees,

children.text: sarvataḥ saṃvṛtaḥ śailo babhau puṣpamayo yathā ||
children.translated_text: the mountain, covered on all sides, shone as if made of flowers.
Pressed by him of unsurpassed valor, that mountain

children.text: salilaṃ samprasusrāva madaṃ matta iva dvipaḥ ||
children.translated_text: poured forth water like a rutting elephant pouring out ichor.
Pressed by that powerful one, Mount <s>Mahendra</s>
brought forth streams of gold, collyrium-black ore, and silver,

children.text: mumoca ca śilāḥ śailo viśālāḥ samanaḥśilāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the mountain released huge rocks together with realgar.
As the mountain was pressed, all the beings
dwelling in its caves cried out with distorted voices.
That great roar of living creatures, born from the mountain's compression,
filled the earth, the directions, and the groves.
Serpents with broad heads, marked plainly with svastika signs,

children.text: vamantaḥ pāvakaṃ ghoraṃ dadaṃśur daśanaiḥ śilāḥ ||
children.translated_text: vomiting dreadful fire, bit the rocks with their fangs.
Then those great rocks, bitten by those enraged venomous serpents,
blazed, kindled by fire, and split into a thousand pieces.
Even the masses of medicinal herbs born on that mountain,

children.text: viṣaghnānyapi nāgānāṃ na śekuḥ śamituṃ viṣam ||
children.translated_text: though able to counter poison, could not quell the serpents' venom.

children.text: bhidyate 'yaṃ girir bhūtair iti matvā tapasvinaḥ
children.translated_text: Thinking, 'This mountain is being split apart by beings,'
the terrified <s>Vidyādharas</s> flew up from it together with groups of women.
They abandoned the golden seats and vessels lying in the drinking ground,
as well as very costly bowls and golden pitchers.
They left foods to be licked, edibles of many kinds, and various meats,
as well as bull hides and swords with golden hilts.
Wearing strings around their necks, drunk, adorned with red garlands and unguents,
red-eyed and lotus-eyed, they took to the sky.
Women wearing necklaces, anklets, armlets, and upper ornaments,
amazed and smiling, stood in the sky with their lovers.
The great <s>Vidyādhara</s> sages, displaying their great knowledge,
stood together in the sky and looked upon the mountain.
Then they heard the sound of the sages of disciplined minds,
and of the <s>Cāraṇas</s> and <s>Siddhas</s> standing in the stainless sky:
'This is <s>Hanūmān</s>, son of the Wind, resembling a mountain,
who wishes to cross the mighty ocean, the abode of makaras,

children.text: rāmārthaṃ vānarārthaṃ ca cikīrṣan karma duṣkaram
children.translated_text: seeking to perform a difficult deed for the sake of <s>Rāma</s> and for the sake of the monkeys.'

children.text: samudrasya paraṃ pāraṃ duṣprāpaṃ prāptum icchati ||
children.translated_text: He wishes to reach the further shore of the ocean, a shore difficult to attain.

children.text: dudhuve ca sa romāṇi cakampe cācalopamaḥ
children.translated_text: He shook his hair, and he trembled like an immovable mountain.

children.text: nanāda ca mahānādaṃ sumahān iva toyadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And he roared a great roar, like a very great rain-cloud.
Then, in order, his rounded tail, covered with hair,
as he was about to leap, he tossed about like the king of birds tossing a serpent.
His tail, coiled behind him as he moved with extreme speed,
appeared like a great serpent being carried off by <s>Garuḍa</s>.
He braced his two arms, which resembled great iron bars,

children.text: sasāda ca kapiḥ kaṭyāṃ caraṇau saṃcukoca ca ||
children.translated_text: and the monkey crouched at the waist and drew in his feet.

children.text: saṃhṛtya ca bhujau śrīmāṃstathaiva ca śirodharām
children.translated_text: Drawing in his arms, glorious as he was, and likewise his neck,

children.text: tejaḥ sattvaṃ tathā vīryam āviveśa sa vīryavān ||
children.translated_text: that mighty one gathered into himself brilliance, firmness, and strength.
Looking at the path from afar, with his eyes fixed upward,
he held his breaths in his heart while gazing at the sky.

children.text: padbhyāṃ dṛḍham avasthānaṃ kṛtvā sa kapikuñjaraḥ
children.translated_text: Having made a firm stance with his two feet, that elephant among monkeys,
<s>Hanumān</s>, mighty in strength, folded back his ears as he was about to spring up,
and that best of monkeys spoke these words to the monkeys:
Just as an arrow released by <s>Rāghava</s>, with the swiftness of the wind,
would go, so shall I go to <s>Laṅkā</s>, ruled by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: na hi drakṣyāmi yadi tāṃ laṅkāyāṃ janakātmajām
children.translated_text: For if I do not see that daughter of <s>Janaka</s> in <s>Laṅkā</s>,
then with this very speed I shall go to the abode of the gods.

children.text: yadi vā tridive sītāṃ na drakṣyāmi kṛtaśramaḥ
children.translated_text: Or if, after making the effort, I do not see <s>Sītā</s> in the third heaven,
I shall bind <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, king of the rākṣasas, and bring him back.
In every way I shall return with the task accomplished, together with <s>Sītā</s>,
or I shall uproot <s>Laṅkā</s>, along with <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, and bring it back.

children.text: evam uktvā tu hanumān vānarān vānarottamaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to the monkeys, <s>Hanumān</s>, the foremost monkey,
then sprang up with speed, swift as he was, without hesitation.
But as he leapt up with force, the trees growing on that mountain,
drawing in all their branches, rose up on every side.
He carried along the flowering trees, frequented by intoxicated birds,
and went through the clear sky with the speed of his thighs.
The trees, shaken up by the speed of his thighs, followed the monkey for a moment,

children.text: prasthitaṃ dīrgham adhvānaṃ svabandhum iva bāndhavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: as he set out on the long road, like kinsmen following their own kinsman.
Those sāla trees and other excellent trees, churned by the speed of his thighs,
followed <s>Hanumān</s> like armies following a king.
Accompanied by many trees with tips in full blossom,
<s>Hanumān</s>, the monkey who had the form of a mountain, became wondrous to behold.
Then the solid, heavy trees sank in the salt water,
like mountains in the ocean, as if from fear of <s>Mahendra</s>.
That monkey, covered with many flowers and with shoots and buds,
shone, cloud-like, like a mountain covered with fireflies.

children.text: vimuktāstasya vegena muktvā puṣpāṇi te drumāḥ
children.translated_text: Released by his speed, those trees, after letting go their flowers,
fell apart in the water like friends turning back.
That varied, light mass fell into the ocean,
the many-colored flowers of the trees, stirred by the monkey's wind.
Encircled by a stream of flowers of many colors,
the monkey shone like a rising cloud adorned with clusters of lightning.
Because of the flowers produced by his speed, the water appeared
like the sky with lovely stars risen in it.
As he moved through the sky, his two extended arms were seen
like two five-headed serpents emerging from a mountain peak.

children.text: pibann iva babhau cāpi sormijālaṃ mahārṇavam
children.translated_text: He shone as if drinking the great ocean together with its network of waves,

children.text: pipāsur iva cākāśaṃ dadṛśe sa mahākapiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and that great monkey appeared as if thirsty for the sky.
As he followed the path of the wind, his eyes, bright like lightning,
shone forth like two fires standing on a mountain.
The great, round, tawny eyes of that tawny-eyed chief
shone like the moon and sun stationed there.

children.text: mukhaṃ nāsikayā tasya tāmrayā tāmram ābabhau
children.translated_text: His face, coppery with his copper-colored nose, shone red,
like the disk of the sun touched by twilight.
The coiled tail of the son of the Wind, as he flew, shone
in the sky like the raised banner of <s>Śakra</s>.
With the circle of his tail, the great, wise son of the Wind, white-fanged,
shone like the sun surrounded by a halo.
That great monkey gleamed with his reddish haunch-region,
like a mountain split open by a great vein of red ochre.
As that lion among monkeys was leaping over the ocean,
the wind caught under his armpits roared like a cloud.
As a meteor, fallen from the northern quarter, is seen in the sky

children.text: dṛśyate sānubandhā ca tathā sa kapikuñjaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: with a trailing path, so appeared that elephant among monkeys.
The monkey, stretched out, shone like a falling winged creature,
like a full-grown elephant being bound with a girth.
With his body above and with his deep shadow below,

children.text: sāgare mārutāviṣṭā naur ivāsīt tadā kapiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the monkey then seemed upon the ocean like a boat driven by the wind.

children.text: yaṃ yaṃ deśaṃ samudrasya jagāma sa mahākapiḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever region of the ocean that great monkey reached,

children.text: sa sa tasyāṅgavegena sonmāda iva lakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: that region seemed driven mad by the speed of his limbs.
With his chest he struck the masses of the ocean's waves, whose bodies were like mountains,
and that great monkey leapt on with tremendous speed.
The powerful wind of the monkey and the wind issuing from the clouds
shook the ocean greatly, with its terrible roar.
Dragging great masses of waves through the salt water,
With great speed he crossed the waves, as if counting them.
Then the serpents dwelling in the ocean, seeing him leaping,

children.text: vyomni taṃ kapiśārdūlaṃ suparṇam iti menire ||
children.translated_text: thought that tiger among monkeys in the sky to be <s>Suparṇa</s>.
Ten yojanas wide and thirty yojanas long,
the shadow of the lion among monkeys appeared very beautiful in the water.
Like a dense row of white clouds, following the son of the wind,

children.text: tasya sā śuśubhe chāyā vitatā lavaṇāmbhasi ||
children.translated_text: that outspread shadow of his shone upon the salt water.

children.text: plavamānaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā plavagaṃ tvaritaṃ tadā
children.translated_text: Seeing that leaping monkey leaping swiftly then,
the gods, gandharvas, and dānavas showered down showers of flowers.

children.text: tatāpa na hi taṃ sūryaḥ plavantaṃ vānareśvaram
children.translated_text: The sun did not scorch that lord of monkeys as he leapt,
and the wind served him then for the accomplishment of <s>Rāma</s>'s task.
The sages praised him as he leapt through the sky,
and the divine gandharvas sang, praising the one of great splendor.

children.text: nāgāśca tuṣṭuvur yakṣā rakṣāṃsi vibudhāḥ khagāḥ
children.translated_text: Nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, gods, and birds praised him,
when they saw the best of monkeys in the sky, suddenly free from weariness.
As that tiger among leapers, <s>Hanūmān</s>, was leaping,
the ocean, desiring honor for the house of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, reflected:
If I do not render assistance to the monkey lord <s>Hanūmān</s>,
I shall become blameworthy to all who may speak of it.
I was enlarged by <s>Sagara</s>, lord of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s>;
and this one is an ally of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s>; he does not deserve to sink down.

children.text: tathā mayā vidhātavyaṃ viśrameta yathā kapiḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore I must arrange it so that the monkey may rest,
and, having rested upon me, he will easily cross what remains.

children.text: iti kṛtvā matiṃ sādhvīṃ samudraśchannam ambhasi
children.translated_text: Having formed this good intention, the ocean, concealed in the waters,
addressed golden-naveled <s>Maināka</s>, the best of mountains:
You have been stationed here, for the hosts of asuras
who dwell in the nether region, as a barrier by the king of the gods, O best of mountains.
You stand blocking the gate of immeasurable <s>Pātāla</s>
against these beings of known strength, should they rise up again.

children.text: tiryag ūrdhvam adhaścaiva śaktiste śaila vardhitum
children.translated_text: Your power, O mountain, is to grow sideways, upward, and downward;
therefore I urge you: rise up, O best of mountains.
This tiger among monkeys, the mighty <s>Hanūmān</s>, is passing above you,
having leapt into the sky for <s>Rāma</s>'s task, terrible in deed.
I must give assistance to him who belongs to the line of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>.
The <s>Ikṣvākus</s> are venerable to me, and supremely venerable to you.

children.text: kuru sācivyam asmākaṃ na naḥ kāryam atikramet
children.translated_text: Act as our helper; let our purpose not pass us by.

children.text: kartavyam akṛtaṃ kāryaṃ satāṃ manyum udīrayet ||
children.translated_text: A duty left undone, though it ought to be done, stirs the anger of the good.
Rise up above the water; let this monkey stand upon you.
He is our guest, and worthy of honor, the best of leapers.
O one with a great golden navel, attended by gods and gandharvas,
<s>Hanūmān</s>, having rested upon you, will then go the rest of the way.
Considering the compassion of <s>Kākutstha</s> and the exile of <s>Maithilī</s>,
and the fatigue of the lord of leapers, you ought to rise.
Golden-naveled <s>Maināka</s>, hearing the words of the salt ocean,
rose swiftly from the water, covered with great trees and creepers.
Splitting the ocean water, he stood very high then,
like the sun with blazing rays splitting a cloud.
With peaks made of fine gold, inhabited by kinnaras and great serpents,
resembling the rising sun and seeming to scratch the sky,
with the mountain's uplifted peaks of jāmbūnada gold,
the sky became golden-bright, gleaming like weapons.
With peaks made of gold, blazing and self-luminous,
that best of mountains became like a hundred suns.

children.text: tam utthitam asaṃgena hanūmān agrataḥ sthitam
children.translated_text: <s>Hanūmān</s>, moving without obstruction, saw him risen and standing before him
in the middle of the salt water, and decided, "This is an obstacle."

children.text: sa tam ucchritam atyarthaṃ mahāvego mahākapiḥ
children.translated_text: That great monkey, possessed of great speed, struck the mountain,
which was raised up exceedingly high, with his chest, as the wind strikes a cloud.
Then that best of mountains, struck down by the monkey,

children.text: buddhvā tasya kaper vegaṃ jaharṣa ca nananda ca ||
children.translated_text: recognized the monkey's speed and rejoiced and was delighted.
The mountain, pleased and glad at heart, spoke to that hero who was moving in the sky

children.text: prīto hṛṣṭamanā vākyam abravīt parvataḥ kapim
children.translated_text: and standing in the sky, addressing the monkey with these words,

children.text: mānuṣaṃ dhārayan rūpam ātmanaḥ śikhare sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: while bearing a human form and standing upon his own peak:

children.text: duṣkaraṃ kṛtavān karma tvam idaṃ vānarottama
children.translated_text: You have performed this difficult deed, O best of monkeys.
Alight upon my peaks and rest as happily as you wish.
The ocean was enlarged by those born in the family of <s>Rāghava</s>;

children.text: sa tvāṃ rāmahite yuktaṃ pratyarcayati sāgaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore the ocean honors you, who are engaged in <s>Rāma</s>'s welfare.

children.text: kṛte ca pratikartavyam eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
children.translated_text: When a favor has been done, it should be repaid; this is eternal <s>dharma</s>.
Thus, seeking to repay that favor, he deserves honor from you.
For your sake I have been urged by him out of respect:

children.text: yojanānāṃ śataṃ cāpi kapir eṣa samāplutaḥ
children.translated_text: "This monkey has leapt even a hundred yojanas;

children.text: tava sānuṣu viśrāntaḥ śeṣaṃ prakramatām iti ||
children.translated_text: having rested on your slopes, let him set out for the rest."

children.text: tiṣṭha tvaṃ hariśārdūla mayi viśramya gamyatām
children.translated_text: Stay, O tiger among monkeys; rest upon me and then go on.

children.text: tad idaṃ gandhavat svādu kandamūlaphalaṃ bahu
children.translated_text: Here are abundant fragrant and sweet tubers, roots, and fruits;
having tasted them, O best of monkeys, you will proceed refreshed.
O chief of monkeys, we too indeed have a connection with you,
one famous in the three worlds and joined with great virtues.
Among the leaping monkeys who leap with speed, O son of the wind,

children.text: teṣāṃ mukhyatamaṃ manye tvām ahaṃ kapikuñjara ||
children.translated_text: I consider you the foremost of them, O elephant among monkeys.
A guest, indeed, is worthy of honor, even if ordinary, by one who understands,

children.text: dharmaṃ jijñāsamānena kiṃ punar yādṛśo bhavān ||
children.translated_text: and who seeks to know <s>dharma</s> (righteous order); how much more one such as you.
For you are the son of the great-souled <s>Māruta</s>,
the best of gods, and equal to him in speed, O elephant among monkeys.

children.text: pūjite tvayi dharmajña pūjāṃ prāpnoti mārutaḥ
children.translated_text: When you are honored, O knower of <s>dharma</s>, <s>Māruta</s> receives honor,

children.text: tasmāt tvaṃ pūjanīyo me śṛṇu cāpyatra kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: therefore you are to be honored by me; hear also the reason for this.
Formerly, dear one, in the <s>Kṛta</s> age, mountains had wings,
and they too went in every direction, swift as <s>Garuḍa</s> and the wind.
Then, when they were moving about, the hosts of gods together with the sages,
and all beings became afraid, fearing that they might fall.
Then the thousand-eyed <s>Śatakratu</s>, angered,
cut off the wings of the mountains here and there by the thousands with his thunderbolt.

children.text: sa mām upagataḥ kruddho vajram udyamya devarāṭ
children.translated_text: The king of the gods came at me in anger, raising his thunderbolt,
but then I was suddenly hurled away by the great-souled Wind.
And into this salt water I was cast, O best of leapers,
with my wings hidden, whole, and protected by your father.

children.text: tato 'haṃ mānayāmi tvāṃ mānyo hi mama mārutaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore I honor you, for <s>Māruta</s> is worthy of honor to me;

children.text: tvayā me hyeṣa saṃbandhaḥ kapimukhya mahāguṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: through you I have this excellent bond, O chief of monkeys, great in virtue.

children.text: asminn evaṃgate kārye sāgarasya mamaiva ca
children.translated_text: Since this matter concerns both <s>Sāgara</s> and me in this way,

children.text: prītiṃ prītamanāḥ kartuṃ tvam arhasi mahākape ||
children.translated_text: you should, with pleased mind, do what is pleasing, O great monkey.

children.text: śramaṃ mokṣaya pūjāṃ ca gṛhāṇa kapisattama
children.translated_text: Release your fatigue and accept my honor, O best of monkeys;

children.text: prītiṃ ca bahu manyasva prīto 'smi tava darśanāt ||
children.translated_text: esteem this affection highly, for I am pleased at seeing you.
Thus addressed, the best of monkeys said to that excellent mountain,
I am pleased; hospitality has been performed. Let this concern be put aside.
The time for my task is pressing, and the day too is passing away;

children.text: pratijñā ca mayā dattā na sthātavyam ihāntarā ||
children.translated_text: and I have given a pledge that I must not stop here on the way.
Having spoken thus, the bull among monkeys touched the mountain with his hand,
and, entering the sky, the valiant one went on, as if laughing.
The son of the Wind, regarded with honor by the mountain and the ocean,
and worshiped with fitting blessings,
then sprang far upward, leaving the mountain and the great ocean,
and, taking to his father's path, went through the stainless sky.
Again gaining an upward course, while looking back at that mountain,
the son of <s>Vāyu</s> went through the stainless sky without support.

children.text: tad dvitīyaṃ hanumato dṛṣṭvā karma suduṣkaram
children.translated_text: Seeing that second exceedingly difficult deed of <s>Hanumān</s>,
all the gods, the <s>Siddhas</s>, and the great seers praised him.
The deities standing there were delighted by his deed,
and so too the thousand-eyed <s>Vāsava</s> with golden <s>Sunābha</s>.
The wise one, with voice faltering from satisfaction, spoke these words,
the lord of <s>Śacī</s> himself, to <s>Sunābha</s>, best of mountains:
O <s>Hiraṇyanābha</s>, lord of mountains, I am deeply pleased with you;

children.text: abhayaṃ te prayacchāmi tiṣṭha saumya yathāsukham ||
children.translated_text: I grant you fearlessness; stay, gentle one, as you please.

children.text: sāhyaṃ kṛtaṃ te sumahad vikrāntasya hanūmataḥ
children.translated_text: You have rendered very great aid to the mighty <s>Hanumān</s>,
who was striding a hundred <s>yojanas</s>, fearless though there was danger.

children.text: rāmasyaiṣa hi dautyena yāti dāśarather hariḥ
children.translated_text: For this monkey is going as a messenger of <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>;

children.text: satkriyāṃ kurvatā śaktyā toṣito 'smi dṛḍhaṃ tvayā ||
children.translated_text: by doing him honor according to your power, you have firmly satisfied me.
Then the excellent mountain obtained vast joy,
seeing the lord of the gods, <s>Śatakratu</s>, pleased.
That mountain, having been granted a boon, then remained steady,
and <s>Hanumān</s> in a moment crossed beyond the ocean.
Then the gods, together with the <s>Gandharvas</s>, and the <s>Siddhas</s> and great seers,
spoke to <s>Surasā</s>, the mother of serpents, who shone like the sun:
This glorious son of the Wind is leaping over the ocean;

children.text: hanūmānnāma tasya tvaṃ muhūrtaṃ vighnam ācara ||
children.translated_text: his name is <s>Hanumān</s>. Create an obstacle for him for a moment.
Assuming a very dreadful, mountain-like <s>rākṣasa</s> form,
with terrible tusks, tawny eyes, and a mouth touching the sky,
we wish to know his strength and also his further prowess;
whether he will overcome you by stratagem or fall into despondency.

children.text: evam uktā tu sā devī daivatair abhisatkṛtā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed and honored by the deities,
that goddess <s>Surasā</s>, in the middle of the ocean, bearing a <s>rākṣasa</s> body,

children.text: vikṛtaṃ ca virūpaṃ ca sarvasya ca bhayāvaham
children.translated_text: deformed, ugly, and terrifying to everyone,
covered <s>Hanumān</s> as he was flying and said this:
You have been assigned to me as food by the lords, O bull among monkeys;
I shall eat you; enter this mouth of mine.
Thus addressed by <s>Surasā</s>, the bull among monkeys, with joined palms,
glorious and with a delighted face, spoke these words:
<s>Rāma</s>, named the son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, entered the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest,

children.text: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā vaidehyā cāpi bhāryayā ||
children.translated_text: with his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and also with his wife <s>Vaidehī</s>.
While he was absorbed in his task and had made enmity with the <s>rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: tasya sītā hṛtā bhāryā rāvaṇena yaśasvinī ||
