children.translated_text: his famous wife <s>Sītā</s> was carried off by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
I am going as his messenger into her presence, by <s>Rāma</s>'s command;
you should render aid to <s>Rāma</s>, O dweller in this region.

children.text: atha vā maithilīṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmaṃ cākliṣṭakāriṇam
children.translated_text: Or else, after seeing <s>Maithilī</s> and <s>Rāma</s>, performer of untroubled deeds,

children.text: āgamiṣyāmi te vaktraṃ satyaṃ pratiśṛṇomi te ||
children.translated_text: I shall come to your mouth; I truly promise you this.
Thus addressed by <s>Hanumān</s>, <s>Surasā</s>, who could assume any form,
said, No one shall pass beyond me; this is my boon.
Thus addressed by <s>Surasā</s>, the foremost monkey became angry

children.text: abravīt kuru vai vaktraṃ yena māṃ viṣahiṣyase ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Make your mouth one with which you will be able to contain me."
Having spoken thus to <s>Surasā</s>, the angry <s>Hanūmān</s>
then became ten yojanas long and ten yojanas broad.
Seeing him, cloud-like, ten yojanas in extent,
<s>Surasā</s> too made her mouth twenty yojanas wide.
Then the angry <s>Hanūmān</s> became thirty yojanas long,
and <s>Surasā</s> made her mouth forty yojanas high.
The heroic <s>Hanūmān</s> became fifty yojanas high,
and <s>Surasā</s> made her mouth sixty yojanas wide.
In the same way the heroic <s>Hanūmān</s> became seventy yojanas high,
and <s>Surasā</s> made her mouth eighty yojanas wide.
<s>Hanūmān</s>, like an immovable mountain, became ninety yojanas high,
and <s>Surasā</s> made her mouth one hundred yojanas wide.

children.text: tad dṛṣṭvā vyāditaṃ tvāsyaṃ vāyuputraḥ sa buddhimān
children.translated_text: Seeing that mouth opened wide by <s>Surasā</s>, the wise son of the Wind,
with its long tongue, very terrible and like hell,

children.text: sa saṃkṣipyātmanaḥ kāyaṃ jīmūta iva mārutiḥ
children.translated_text: contracted his own body, <s>Māruti</s> becoming like a cloud,
and in that instant <s>Hanūmān</s> became the size of a thumb.

children.text: so 'bhipatyāśu tad vaktraṃ niṣpatya ca mahājavaḥ
children.translated_text: Swiftly rushing into that mouth and coming out again, he of great speed,

children.text: antarikṣe sthitaḥ śrīmān idaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: the splendid one standing in the sky, spoke these words:

children.text: praviṣṭo 'smi hi te vaktraṃ dākṣāyaṇi namo 'stu te
children.translated_text: "I have indeed entered your mouth, O <s>Dākṣāyaṇī</s>; homage to you.

children.text: gamiṣye yatra vaidehī satyaṃ cāstu vacastava ||
children.translated_text: I shall go where <s>Vaidehī</s> is. Let your word too be true."

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā vadanānmuktaṃ candraṃ rāhumukhād iva
children.translated_text: Seeing the monkey freed from her mouth, like the moon from the mouth of <s>Rāhu</s>,

children.text: abravīt surasā devī svena rūpeṇa vānaram ||
children.translated_text: the goddess <s>Surasā</s>, in her own form, said to him:
"Go, best of monkeys, gentle one, at ease, for the accomplishment of your purpose.
Bring <s>Vaidehī</s> together with the great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>."

children.text: tat tṛtīyaṃ hanumato dṛṣṭvā karma suduṣkaram
children.translated_text: Seeing that third very difficult deed of <s>Hanūmān</s>,
the beings then praised the monkey, saying, "Well done, well done!"
He approached the unassailable ocean, the abode of <s>Varuṇa</s>,
and, entering the sky, went with the speed of <s>Garuḍa</s>.
In that sky, frequented by rain-bearing clouds and attended by birds,
traveled by the <s>Kaiśika</s> teachers and frequented by <s>Airāvata</s>,
adorned with lions, elephants, tigers, birds, serpents, and vehicles,
and with spotless aerial cars flying together,
made splendid by thunderbolt and lightning strikes and by fires,
adorned by highly fortunate merit-makers who had won heaven,
served constantly by <s>Citrabhānu</s>, who carries oblations,
ornamented with hosts of planets, lunar mansions, the moon, the sun, and stars,
crowded with hosts of great seers, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, and <s>Yakṣas</s>,
secluded, stainless, universal, and frequented by <s>Viśvāvasu</s>,
trodden by the elephant of the king of the gods, auspicious as the path of the moon and sun,
the broad canopy of the living world, fashioned by <s>Brahmā</s>,
often frequented by heroes and by excellent hosts of <s>Vidyādharas</s>,
great clouds, drawn along by the monkey, shone brightly.
Entering masses of clouds and coming out again and again,
he shone then like the moon in the rainy season, emerging and entering.

children.text: plavamānaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā siṃhikā nāma rākṣasī
children.translated_text: Seeing him leaping along, a rākṣasī named <s>Siṃhikā</s>,
grown large and able to assume any form at will, thought in her mind:
"Today, after a long time, I shall have a meal.

children.text: idaṃ hi me mahat sattvaṃ cirasya vaśam āgatam ||
children.translated_text: For this great being has come under my power after so long."

children.text: iti saṃcintya manasā chāyām asya samakṣipat
children.translated_text: Thinking this in her mind, she seized his shadow.
When his shadow had been grasped, the monkey thought:
"I have suddenly been pulled back, my prowess made helpless,
like a great ship in the ocean by a contrary wind."
Then, looking sideways, upward, and downward,
the monkey saw a great being risen up in the salt water.
"The wondrous-looking being described by the king of monkeys,

children.text: chāyāgrāhi mahāvīryaṃ tad idaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: mighty and shadow-grasping, is this very one; there is no doubt here."

children.text: sa tāṃ buddhvārthatattvena siṃhikāṃ matimān kapiḥ
children.translated_text: The intelligent monkey, having understood that <s>Siṃhikā</s> according to the truth of the matter,
expanded his great body like a rain cloud.

children.text: tasya sā kāyam udvīkṣya vardhamānaṃ mahākapeḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing the body of that great monkey increasing,
she stretched out her mouth, resembling the underworld and the sky.

children.text: sa dadarśa tatastasyā vikṛtaṃ sumahan mukham
children.translated_text: Then the wise great monkey saw her distorted, very huge mouth,

children.text: kāyamātraṃ ca medhāvī marmāṇi ca mahākapiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the measure of her body, and her vital points.

children.text: sa tasyā vivṛte vaktre vajrasaṃhananaḥ kapiḥ
children.translated_text: When her mouth was opened, the thunderbolt-limbed monkey
again contracted himself and leapt out with great strength.
The <s>Siddhas</s> and <s>Cāraṇas</s> saw him sinking into her mouth,

children.text: grasyamānaṃ yathā candraṃ pūrṇaṃ parvaṇi rāhuṇā ||
children.translated_text: being swallowed like the full moon by <s>Rāhu</s> on the day of conjunction.
Then, tearing out her vital points with his sharp nails, the monkey
sprang up with speed, his power swift as the mind.

children.text: tāṃ hatāṃ vānareṇāśu patitāṃ vīkṣya siṃhikām
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Siṃhikā</s>, slain by the monkey and quickly fallen,
the sky-moving beings said to that bull among leapers:

children.text: bhīmam adya kṛtaṃ karma mahat sattvaṃ tvayā hatam
children.translated_text: "A dreadful deed has been done today; a great being has been slain by you.
Accomplish your intended purpose unharmed, best of leapers.

children.text: yasya tvetāni catvāri vānarendra yathā tava
children.translated_text: O lord of monkeys, he in whom these four qualities exist, as they do in you,

children.text: dhṛtir dṛṣṭir matir dākṣyaṃ sa karmasu na sīdati ||
children.translated_text: steadfastness, insight, intelligence, and skill, does not fail in undertakings."
Honored by them, venerable, and committed to his purpose,
the monkey entered the sky and went like <s>Garuḍa</s>.
Having almost reached the farther shore, he looked around on every side
At the end of a hundred yojanas he saw a line of forest.
And even as he descended, he saw it adorned with various trees:
the island, the best of branch-roaming monkeys saw, and the groves of <s>Malaya</s>.
He looked upon the ocean, the ocean's shores, and the trees born on the ocean's shores,
and even the mouths of the ocean's consorts.
Seeing his own body, like a great cloud,
as though blocking the sky, the wise one formed a thought in his mind:

children.text: kāyavṛddhiṃ pravegaṃ ca mama dṛṣṭvaiva rākṣasāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Seeing the increase of my body and my great speed, the rākṣasas

children.text: mayi kautūhalaṃ kuryur iti mene mahākapiḥ ||
children.translated_text: will surely become curious about me,' thought the great monkey.
Then, contracting that body of his, which had been like a great mountain,
he returned again to his natural form, like a self-possessed man freed from delusion.
He, able to assume many beautiful forms, having reached the far shore of the sea,
with a form impossible for others to attain, having examined himself and considered his purpose,

children.text: tataḥ sa lambasya gireḥ samṛddhe vicitrakūṭe nipapāta kūṭe
children.translated_text: then fell upon a peak of <s>Lamba</s> mountain, prosperous and varied in its summits,
covered with ketaka, uddālaka, and coconut trees, that great-souled one like the peak of a great mountain.

children.text: sa sāgaraṃ dānavapannagāyutaṃ balena vikramya mahormimālinam
children.translated_text: Having crossed by his strength the ocean filled with dānavas and serpents, garlanded with great waves,

children.text: nipatya tīre ca mahodadhestadā dadarśa laṅkām amarāvatīm iva ||
children.translated_text: and having landed then on the shore of the great ocean, he saw <s>Laṅkā</s>, like <s>Amarāvatī</s>.
That very mighty one, having crossed the unassailable ocean,

children.text: trikūṭaśikhare laṅkāṃ sthitāṃ svastho dadarśa ha ||
children.translated_text: stood composed and saw <s>Laṅkā</s> situated on the peak of <s>Trikūṭa</s>.
Then, showered with a rain of flowers released from the trees, the heroic one
stood there and shone as though made of flowers.
The glorious monkey of supreme valor, though he had crossed a hundred yojanas,
did not pant there and did not suffer fatigue.
'I could stride across many hundreds of yojanas as well;
how much more the measured limit of the ocean, a hundred yojanas?'

children.text: sa tu vīryavatāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ plavatām api cottamaḥ
children.translated_text: He, the best of the powerful and the foremost even among leapers,
went swiftly to <s>Laṅkā</s>, having leapt across the great ocean.

children.text: śādvalāni ca nīlāni gandhavanti vanāni ca
children.translated_text: Through blue grassy places, fragrant forests,

children.text: gaṇḍavanti ca madhyena jagāma nagavanti ca ||
children.translated_text: and through places with slopes in the middle and with mountains, he went.
Mountains covered with trees and flowering rows of forest
the splendid <s>Hanumān</s>, bull among leapers, passed over.

children.text: sa tasminn acale tiṣṭhan vanānyupavanāni ca
children.translated_text: Standing on that mountain, the son of the Wind saw forests and pleasure groves,

children.text: sa nagāgre ca tāṃ laṅkāṃ dadarśa pavanātmajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and from the mountain's summit he saw that <s>Laṅkā</s>.
He saw sarala trees, karṇikāras, and well-flowered date-palms,
priyālas, muculindas, kuṭajas, and ketakas too;
fragrant priyaṅgus, nīpas, and saptacchadas as well,
asanas, kovidāras, and flowering karavīras;
trees weighed down by masses of flowers and others still in bud,
trees filled with birds and with their tops shaken by the wind;
ponds filled with haṃsas and kāraṇḍavas, furnished with lotuses and blue lotuses,
various charming playgrounds and many kinds of reservoirs;
and gardens spread with various trees, bearing fruits and flowers in every season,
lovely pleasure gardens the elephant among monkeys saw.
Having reached splendid <s>Laṅkā</s>, ruled by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
adorned with moats full of lotuses and blue lotuses,
well guarded by <s>Rāvaṇa</s> because of the abduction of <s>Sītā</s>,
and by rākṣasas moving about on every side, armed with fierce bows,
that lovely great city covered with a golden rampart,
filled with hundreds of watchtowers and garlanded with banners and flags,
with divine golden gateways variegated by rows of creepers,

children.text: dadarśa hanumāṃl laṅkāṃ divi devapurīm iva ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hanumān</s> saw <s>Laṅkā</s>, like a city of the gods in heaven.

children.text: girimūrdhni sthitāṃ laṅkāṃ pāṇḍurair bhavanaiḥ śubhaiḥ
children.translated_text: The glorious monkey saw <s>Laṅkā</s> standing on the mountain-top, with auspicious white buildings,

children.text: dadarśa sa kapiḥ śrīmān puram ākāśagaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: like a city moving in the sky.
Guarded by the lord of the rākṣasas and fashioned by <s>Viśvakarman</s>,
<s>Hanumān</s> saw the city as though floating in the sky.

children.text: sampūrṇāṃ rākṣasair ghorair nāgair bhogavatīm iva
children.translated_text: Filled with terrible rākṣasas, like <s>Bhogavatī</s> with serpents,
inconceivable, well made, clearly laid out, formerly inhabited by <s>Kubera</s>,
guarded by many brave tusked rākṣasas with spears and paṭṭiśas in hand,

children.text: rakṣitāṃ rākṣasair ghorair guhām āśīviṣair api ||
children.translated_text: terrible rākṣasas like a cave guarded even by venomous serpents,
with rampart and wall as its hips, with broad waters as its new garment,
with śataghnīs and spears as the ends of its hair, and watchtowers as its ornaments,
the monkey reached the northern gate and began to think.
It was like the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>, as though scratching the sky,
as though the sky were being held up by its lofty, excellent buildings.

children.text: tasyāśca mahatīṃ guptiṃ sāgaraṃ ca nirīkṣya saḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing its great protection and the ocean,

children.text: rāvaṇaṃ ca ripuṃ ghoraṃ cintayāmāsa vānaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the terrible enemy, the monkey began to reflect:
'Even if the monkeys come here, they will be useless;

children.text: na hi yuddhena vai laṅkā śakyā jetuṃ surair api ||
children.translated_text: for <s>Laṅkā</s> cannot be conquered in battle even by the gods.

children.text: imāṃ tu viṣamāṃ durgāṃ laṅkāṃ rāvaṇapālitām
children.translated_text: Having reached this difficult and rugged fortress, <s>Laṅkā</s>, ruled by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: prāpyāpi sa mahābāhuḥ kiṃ kariṣyati rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: what will mighty-armed <s>Rāghava</s> do?
No opportunity for conciliation is found among the rākṣasas;

children.text: na dānasya na bhedasya naiva yuddhasya dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: none is seen for gifts, for division, or even for war.

children.text: caturṇām eva hi gatir vānarāṇāṃ mahātmanām
children.translated_text: Indeed there is a way only for four great-souled monkeys:
for the son of <s>Vālin</s>, for <s>Nīla</s>, for me, and for the wise king.

children.text: yāvajjānāmi vaidehīṃ yadi jīvati vā na vā
children.translated_text: Until I learn whether <s>Vaidehī</s> is alive or not,
I shall deliberate right there, after seeing that daughter of <s>Janaka</s>.'
Then that elephant among monkeys reflected for a moment,
standing on that mountain peak, intent on the success of <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: anena rūpeṇa mayā na śakyā rakṣasāṃ purī
children.translated_text: With this form of mine, I cannot enter the city of the <s>rakṣasas</s>,
guarded as it is by cruel <s>rākṣasas</s> endowed with strength.
The <s>rākṣasas</s> are fierce in splendor, greatly heroic, and powerful;
I must deceive them all while I search for <s>Jānakī</s>.

children.text: lakṣyālakṣyeṇa rūpeṇa rātrau laṅkā purī mayā
children.translated_text: In a form partly seen and partly unseen, by night, the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>

children.text: praveṣṭuṃ prāptakālaṃ me kṛtyaṃ sādhayituṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: is now ready for me to enter, in order to accomplish my great task.

children.text: tāṃ purīṃ tādṛśīṃ dṛṣṭvā durādharṣāṃ surāsuraiḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that city as it was, hard for gods and asuras to assail,
<s>Hanūmān</s> reflected, sighing again and again.
By what means may I see <s>Maithilī</s>, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,
without being seen by the evil-minded <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>?

children.text: na vinaśyet kathaṃ kāryaṃ rāmasya viditātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: How may the mission of wise <s>Rāma</s> not be ruined?
And how may I, alone, see the solitary daughter of <s>Janaka</s> in a deserted place?
Matters already undertaken come to grief when they are opposed to proper place and time,

children.text: viklavaṃ dūtam āsādya tamaḥ sūryodaye yathā ||
children.translated_text: when they meet with a confused messenger, like darkness at sunrise.
Even a settled plan does not prosper when the mind moves from purpose into misfortune;
for messengers who think themselves learned destroy undertakings.

children.text: na vinaśyet kathaṃ kāryaṃ vaiklavyaṃ na kathaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: How may the mission not be ruined, and how may there be no confusion?

children.text: laṅghanaṃ ca samudrasya kathaṃ nu na vṛthā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: And how indeed may the crossing of the ocean not become fruitless?

children.text: mayi dṛṣṭe tu rakṣobhī rāmasya viditātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: But if I am seen by the <s>rākṣasas</s>, this mission of wise <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: bhaved vyartham idaṃ kāryaṃ rāvaṇānartham icchataḥ ||
children.translated_text: who seeks <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s ruin, would become futile.

children.text: na hi śakyaṃ kvacit sthātum avijñātena rākṣasaiḥ
children.translated_text: For it is not possible to remain anywhere without being discovered by the <s>rākṣasas</s>,
even in the form of a <s>rākṣasa</s>, much less in any other form.

children.text: vāyur apyatra nājñātaścared iti matir mama
children.translated_text: Even the wind could not move here unknown; such is my thought.
For nothing is unknown to these very powerful <s>rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: ihāhaṃ yadi tiṣṭhāmi svena rūpeṇa saṃvṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: If I remain here concealed in my own form,
I will meet destruction, and my master's purpose will fail.

children.text: tad ahaṃ svena rūpeṇa rajanyāṃ hrasvatāṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the night, having made my own form small,
I will enter <s>Laṅkā</s> for the accomplishment of <s>Rāghava</s>'s purpose.
Entering by night the city of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, very hard to approach,
I shall search every building and see the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>.
Having thus reflected, <s>Hanūmān</s>, the monkey hero,
then waited for the setting of the sun, eager for the sight of <s>Vaidehī</s>.
Becoming only the size of a small cat, he was wondrous to behold.
At twilight, mighty <s>Hanūmān</s> quickly leapt up
and entered the lovely city, with its great roads well laid out.
It was spread with rows of mansions and with pillars of gold and silver,
with latticed windows made of refined gold, like a city of the gandharvas.
He saw that great city with seven- and eight-storied buildings,
their floors filled with crystal and adorned with gold.
Those buildings of the <s>rākṣasas</s> shone there with floors
variegated with vaidūrya gems and adorned with networks of pearls.
The <s>rākṣasas</s>' golden, many-colored gateways
lit up <s>Laṅkā</s>, adorned on every side.
Seeing <s>Laṅkā</s>, inconceivable and wondrous in form,
the great monkey became both dejected and delighted, eager for the sight of <s>Vaidehī</s>.
He saw the city garlanded with pale, lofty mansions and with costly gates and lattices of jāmbūnada gold,
protected by the arms of glorious <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and surrounded by night-roaming beings of terrible strength.

children.text: candro 'pi sācivyam ivāsya kurvaṃs tārāgaṇair madhyagato virājan
children.translated_text: The moon too, as if assisting him, shone forth amid the host of stars,
spreading the world with a canopy of moonlight as the many-thousand-rayed one rose.
That foremost monkey saw the moon rising and shining forth,

children.text: dadarśa candraṃ sa kapipravīraḥ poplūyamānaṃ sarasīva haṃsam ||
children.translated_text: white as a conch, milk, and lotus fiber, like a swan gliding in a lake.
On a long, pendant peak, resembling a hanging raincloud,
the wise <s>Hanūmān</s>, son of the wind, gathered his courage.
At night that great-souled elephant among monkeys entered <s>Laṅkā</s>,
the city ruled by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, rich in lovely groves and waters.
It was beautified by buildings like autumn clouds,
resounding like the ocean and served by the ocean wind.
It was well guarded by a well-nourished force, like a city full of branching trees,
with beautiful gateways and projecting turrets, and with pale gates and portals.
Guarded and fair, like <s>Bhogavatī</s> traversed by serpents,
that city was thick with clouds flashing with lightning and frequented by the path of lights.
It roared with fierce winds, like <s>Amarāvatī</s> of <s>Indra</s>,
and was encircled by a great rampart of refined gold.
Adorned with banners whose networks of little bells rang out,
he reached it suddenly, rejoiced, and went up to the rampart.
His heart filled with wonder as he looked at the city on every side,
with gates made of jāmbūnada gold and platforms made of vaidūrya,
with jeweled pavements adorned by gems, crystal, and pearls,
with projections of heated gold, silvery and spotless white,
with stairways floored in vaidūrya and with inner dustings of crystal,
beautiful, fitted with lovely covered walks, as if they had flown up into the sky,
resounding with flocks of curlews and peacocks, and frequented by royal swans,
echoing everywhere with the sounds of instruments and ornaments,
then, having surveyed the city, comparable to the dwelling of the Vasus,

children.text: kham ivotpatitāṃ laṅkāṃ jaharṣa hanumān kapiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The monkey <s>Hanumān</s> rejoiced at <s>Laṅkā</s>, as though it had sprung up into the sky.

children.text: tāṃ samīkṣya purīṃ laṅkāṃ rākṣasādhipateḥ śubhām
children.translated_text: Seeing that beautiful city of <s>Laṅkā</s>, belonging to the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>,
incomparable and endowed with prosperity, the heroic one reflected.

children.text: neyam anyena nagarī śakyā dharṣayituṃ balāt
children.translated_text: "This city cannot be assaulted by force by anyone else,
guarded as it is by the forces of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, bearing weapons held ready.
This ground might perhaps be accessible to <s>Kumuda</s> or <s>Aṅgada</s>, or to the great monkey <s>Suṣeṇa</s>,
and it might be renowned even for <s>Mainda</s> and <s>Dvivida</s>.
It might be a course for the son of <s>Vivasvat</s>, for the monkey <s>Kuśaparvaṇ</s>,

children.text: ṛkṣasya ketumālasya mama caiva gatir bhavet ||
children.translated_text: for the bear <s>Ketumāla</s>, and for me as well."
But considering the prowess of mighty-armed <s>Rāghava</s>

children.text: lakṣmaṇasya ca vikrāntam abhavat prītimān kapiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the valor of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the monkey became glad.
The great monkey saw that city of the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, rich with jewels and garments,
adorned with storehouses, with arsenals as its breasts, prosperous like an ornamented woman,
with darkness dispelled by lamps and by shining great mansions,
that city of the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>.
The son of the Wind, endowed with courage, entered by night,
and took the great road, shining with pearls and flowers.
With sounds of laughter and loud cries, preceded by the noise of instruments,
and with houses like thunderbolts and elephant-goads, adorned with diamond lattices,

children.text: gṛhamedhaiḥ purī ramyā babhāse dyaur ivāmbudaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the lovely city shone like the sky with clouds.
Then <s>Laṅkā</s> blazed with the splendid houses of the hosts of <s>rākṣasas</s>,
variegated and resembling white clouds, set in forms of lotuses and svastikas,
and with prospering houses everywhere richly adorned.
That glorious monkey, acting for the welfare of the king of monkeys,

children.text: rāghavārthaṃ carañ śrīmān dadarśa ca nananda ca ||
children.translated_text: wandering for <s>Rāghava</s>'s sake, saw that city decked with bright garlands and ornaments, and rejoiced.
He heard the sweet singing of women rich with intoxication,
adorned with the tones of the three registers, like <s>apsarases</s> in heaven.
He heard the jingling of girdles and the sound of anklets,
and also the sounds of stairways in the mansions of the great,
as well as sounds of clapping and cries from here and there.
He saw <s>yātudhānas</s> intent on recitation,
and <s>rākṣasas</s> roaring, accompanied by praises of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
He saw a great <s>rākṣasa</s> force stationed there, occupying the royal road,

children.text: dadarśa madhyame gulme rākṣasasya carān bahūn ||
children.translated_text: and many scouts of the <s>rākṣasa</s> in the central guard-post.
He saw consecrated ones, matted-haired ones, shaven-headed ones, and those wearing cowhide garments,
some with fistfuls of darbha grass as weapons and others with fire-pits as weapons.
There were men with deceptive clubs in hand, and others bearing staffs as weapons,
one-eyed and many-eared beings, and those with swaying, pendulous breasts.
There were grim ones, crooked-faced ones, monstrous ones, and dwarfish ones,
bowmen and swordsmen, armed with śataghnīs and pestles,
and others with excellent iron clubs in their hands, gleaming in variegated armor.
He saw beings neither too fat nor too thin, neither too tall nor too short,
misshapen, many-formed, beautiful, and splendid in radiance.
He saw warriors armed with spears and trees, and wielders of paṭṭiśas and thunderbolts,
with throwing-weapons and nooses in their hands.
He saw garlanded and anointed ones, adorned with excellent ornaments,
and mighty ones bearing sharp spears and thunderbolt weapons.
The monkey saw an undisturbed central guard, a hundred thousand strong,
completely enclosed by a rampart; the great monkey saw it.
He entered the house of the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, divine and like heaven,
resounding with heavenly sounds, filled with the neighing of horses and with the noise of ornaments,

children.text: rathair yānair vimānaiśca tathā gajahayaiḥ śubhaiḥ
children.translated_text: adorned with chariots, vehicles, aerial cars, and with fine elephants and horses,
and with four-tusked elephants like masses of white clouds,
beautifully gated, adorned, and filled with intoxicated animals and birds,
guarded as it was by the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: tataḥ sa madhyaṃ gatam aṃśumantaṃ jyotsnāvitānaṃ mahad udvamantam
children.translated_text: Then the wise one saw the radiant moon standing in mid-sky, pouring forth a great expanse of moonlight,

children.text: dadarśa dhīmān divi bhānumantaṃ goṣṭhe vṛṣaṃ mattam iva bhramantam ||
children.translated_text: shining in heaven like a rutting bull roaming in a cowshed.

children.text: lokasya pāpāni vināśayantaṃ mahodadhiṃ cāpi samedhayantam
children.translated_text: He saw the cool-rayed moon approaching, destroying the sins of the world,

children.text: bhūtāni sarvāṇi virājayantaṃ dadarśa śītāṃśum athābhiyāntam ||
children.translated_text: swelling even the great ocean, and making all beings shine.

children.text: yā bhāti lakṣmīr bhuvi mandarasthā tathā pradoṣeṣu ca sāgarasthā
children.translated_text: The beauty that shines on earth when set on <s>Mandara</s>, and likewise at twilight when set in the ocean,

children.text: tathaiva toyeṣu ca puṣkarasthā rarāja sā cāruniśākarasthā ||
children.translated_text: and similarly in waters when set on a lotus, that beauty shone when set in the lovely moon.

children.text: haṃso yathā rājatapañjarasthaḥ siṃho yathā mandarakandarasthaḥ
children.translated_text: As a goose shines in a silver cage, as a lion in a cave of <s>Mandara</s>,

children.text: vīro yathā garvitakuñjarasthaś candro 'pi babhrāja tathāmbarasthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and as a hero mounted on a proud elephant, so too the moon shone in the sky.

children.text: sthitaḥ kakudmān iva tīkṣṇaśṛṅgo mahācalaḥ śveta ivoccaśṛṅgaḥ
children.translated_text: Like a humped bull standing with sharp horns, like a great white mountain with high peaks,
like an elephant with its tusks bound in gold, the moon shone with its horns full.
Blessed nightfall shone like heaven, its darkness destroyed by the bright moonrise,
though marked by the fault of the growing flesh-eating <s>rākṣasas</s>, and by minds stirred by lovely women.

children.text: tantrīsvanāḥ karṇasukhāḥ pravṛttāḥ svapanti nāryaḥ patibhiḥ suvṛttāḥ
children.translated_text: Stringed sounds, pleasant to the ear, began; well-conducted women slept with their husbands,
and the night-wanderers also set out to roam, their conduct wondrous and terrible.
The wise monkey saw families confused with drunken and heedless people,

children.text: vīraśriyā cāpi samākulāni dadarśa dhīmān sa kapiḥ kulāni ||
children.translated_text: crowded with chariots, horses, and noble seats, and crowded too with heroic splendor.

children.text: parasparaṃ cādhikam ākṣipanti bhujāṃśca pīnān adhivikṣipanti
children.translated_text: They challenge one another still more, and fling about their stout arms.
They pour out drunken babble, and, intoxicated, revile one another.

children.text: rakṣāṃsi vakṣāṃsi ca vikṣipanti gātrāṇi kāntāsu ca vikṣipanti
children.translated_text: The <s>rākṣasas</s> toss their chests about and cast their limbs upon their beloved women.

children.text: dadarśa kāntāśca samālapanti tathāparāstatra punaḥ svapanti ||
children.translated_text: He saw beloved women conversing there, and others again sleeping there.

children.text: mahāgajaiś cāpi tathā nadadbhiḥ supūjitaiś cāpi tathā susadbhiḥ
children.translated_text: With great elephants trumpeting there, and likewise with honored, well-seated ones,

children.text: rarāja vīraiśca viniḥśvasadbhir hrado bhujaṅgair iva niḥśvasadbhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: it shone with heroes breathing deeply, like a lake with hissing serpents.
He saw there in that city <s>yātudhānas</s>, foremost in intelligence, pleasant in speech, confident, chiefs of the world,

children.text: nānāvidhānān rucirābhidhānān dadarśa tasyāṃ puri yātudhānān ||
children.translated_text: of many kinds and fair names.

children.text: nananda dṛṣṭvā sa ca tān surūpān nānāguṇān ātmaguṇānurūpān
children.translated_text: Seeing those handsome beings, endowed with many qualities suited to their own nature, he rejoiced;

children.text: vidyotamānān sa ca tān surūpān dadarśa kāṃścic ca punar virūpān ||
children.translated_text: and he saw some of them handsome and shining, and others again deformed.

children.text: tato varārhāḥ suviśuddhabhāvās teṣāṃ striyastatra mahānubhāvāḥ
children.translated_text: Then he saw there the worthy wives of those powerful ones, pure in disposition,

children.text: priyeṣu pāneṣu ca saktabhāvā dadarśa tārā iva suprabhāvāḥ ||
children.translated_text: attached to their beloveds and to drinking, shining brightly like stars.
He saw some blazing with beauty, embraced by modesty, and, in the dead of night, embraced by their lovers;

children.text: dadarśa kāścit pramadopagūḍhā yathā vihaṃgāḥ kusumopagūḍhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: some were embraced by delight, like birds enfolded in flowers.

children.text: anyāḥ punar harmyatalopaviṣṭās tatra priyāṅkeṣu sukhopaviṣṭāḥ
children.translated_text: Others again were seated on palace terraces there, happily seated in the laps of their beloveds;

children.text: bhartuḥ priyā dharmaparā niviṣṭā dadarśa dhīmān madanābhiviṣṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wise one saw them, dear to their husbands, intent on <s>dharma</s>, settled there, and overcome by desire.
Some were uncovered, with the color of streaks of gold; others were excellent, with the hue of refined gold.
And again some, whose lovely limbs were the color of the moon's mark, were bereft of their lovers.

children.text: tataḥ priyān prāpya mano'bhirāmān suprītiyuktāḥ prasamīkṣya rāmāḥ
children.translated_text: Then, having obtained beloved men who delighted the mind, the women, filled with great affection and gazing at them,

children.text: gṛheṣu hṛṣṭāḥ paramābhirāmā haripravīraḥ sa dadarśa rāmāḥ ||
children.translated_text: were joyful in their houses and supremely lovely; the foremost monkey saw those women.
He saw garlands of faces bright as the moon, with curved eyes and lashes, and rows of lovely eyes;

children.text: vibhūṣaṇānāṃ ca dadarśa mālāḥ śatahradānām iva cārumālāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and he saw garlands of ornaments, lovely as garlands of lightning flashes.

children.text: na tveva sītāṃ paramābhijātāṃ pathi sthite rājakule prajātām
children.translated_text: But he did not see <s>Sītā</s>, nobly born, born in a royal line, standing on the path,

children.text: latāṃ praphullām iva sādhujātāṃ dadarśa tanvīṃ manasābhijātām ||
children.translated_text: slender and noble-minded, like a well-born creeper in full bloom.

children.text: sanātane vartmani saṃniviṣṭāṃ rāmekṣaṇīṃ tāṃ madanābhiviṣṭām
children.translated_text: She was established in the ancient path, with her gaze fixed on <s>Rāma</s>, overcome by love,

children.text: bhartur manaḥ śrīmad anupraviṣṭāṃ strībhyo varābhyaśca sadā viśiṣṭām ||
children.translated_text: having entered the glorious heart of her husband, and always distinguished above the best of women.
She was afflicted by heat, her throat wet with streams of tears, who once had worn an excellent and costly necklace;

children.text: sujātapakṣmām abhiraktakaṇṭhīṃ vane pravṛttām iva nīlakaṇṭhīm ||
children.translated_text: with beautiful lashes and a lovely throat, like a peahen gone into the forest.

children.text: avyaktalekhām iva candralekhāṃ pāṃsupradigdhām iva hemalekhām
children.translated_text: She was like a crescent moon with its line indistinct, like a streak of gold smeared with dust,

children.text: kṣataprarūḍhām iva bāṇalekhāṃ vāyuprabhinnām iva meghalekhām ||
children.translated_text: like the mark of a wound healed from an arrow, like a streak of cloud broken by the wind.

children.text: sītām apaśyanmanujeśvarasya rāmasya patnīṃ vadatāṃ varasya
children.translated_text: Not seeing <s>Sītā</s>, the wife of <s>Rāma</s>, lord of men and best of speakers,
the monkey was struck by grief after so long a time, as though suddenly become dispirited.
Then, moving wherever he wished among those mansions and taking any form he desired,
the monkey, endowed with lightness, ranged through <s>Laṅkā</s>.
Then the fortunate one reached the residence of the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>,
enclosed by a shining rampart the color of the sun.

children.text: rakṣitaṃ rākṣasair bhīmaiḥ siṃhair iva mahad vanam
children.translated_text: It was guarded by terrible <s>rākṣasas</s>, like a great forest by lions;
as he inspected the building, the elephant among monkeys shone forth.
It was surrounded by ornate gateways inlaid with silver and adorned with gold,
by varied courts and by beautiful doors.
It was attended by brave, tireless mahouts mounted on elephants,
and by irresistible horses that drew chariots.
It was constantly traversed by resounding, splendid chariots, their coverings marked with lions and tigers,
and with well-tamed steeds adorned with gold and silver.
It was strewn with many jewels and held costly seats and vessels;
it was the dwelling of great chariot-warriors and had great seats for great warriors.
It was filled on every side with those supremely noble and visible creatures,
with many thousands of various beasts and birds.
It was well guarded by disciplined gatekeepers and by <s>rākṣasas</s>,
and it was filled on every side with chief and excellent women.
The residence of the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s> held joyous jewels among women,
and with the clamor of fine ornaments it sounded like the roar of the ocean.
That palace, endowed with royal excellence and with the finest sandalwood,
resounded with drums and mṛdaṅgas and rang with the sound of conches.
It was worshiped daily, honored by the <s>rākṣasas</s> at all times, and received offerings on festival days;

children.text: samudram iva gambhīraṃ samudram iva niḥsvanam ||
children.translated_text: it was deep as the ocean and sounded like the ocean.
The great monkey saw the great dwelling of the great-souled one, furnished with great jewels,
and crowded with many people.
It shone with its own beauty and was thronged with elephants, horses, and chariots;
the great monkey considered it the very ornament of <s>Laṅkā</s>.

children.text: gṛhād gṛhaṃ rākṣasānām udyānāni ca vānaraḥ
children.translated_text: Fearless, the monkey went from house to house of the <s>rākṣasas</s>,
examining gardens and palaces as he moved about.
Leaping down with great speed into the residence of <s>Prahasta</s>,
the mighty one then sprang to another mansion, that of <s>Mahāpārśva</s>.
Then he came to the residence of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, which resembled a cloud.

children.text: vibhīṣaṇasya ca tathā pupluve sa mahākapiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And likewise the great monkey leapt to the house of <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>.

children.text: mahodarasya ca tathā virūpākṣasya caiva hi
children.translated_text: And likewise to that of <s>Mahodara</s>, and also indeed to that of <s>Virūpākṣa</s>;
to the dwelling of <s>Vidyujjihva</s>, and likewise to that of <s>Vidyunmālin</s>;

children.text: vajradaṃṣṭrasya ca tathā pupluve sa mahākapiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and likewise the great monkey leapt to that of <s>Vajradaṃṣṭra</s>.

children.text: śukasya ca mahāvegaḥ sāraṇasya ca dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: With great speed he went to the house of <s>Śuka</s> and of wise <s>Sāraṇa</s>;
and then the lord of monkey troops went to the mansion of <s>Indrajit</s>.
The lord of monkey troops went to the houses of <s>Jambumāli</s> and <s>Sumāli</s>,
to the dwelling of <s>Raśmiketu</s>, and likewise to that of <s>Sūryaśatru</s>.
The son of the wind went to the dwelling of <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s> and <s>Saṃpāti</s>,
and to those of <s>Vidyudrūpa</s>, <s>Bhīma</s>, <s>Ghana</s>, and <s>Vighana</s>;
of <s>Śukanābha</s>, <s>Vakra</s>, <s>Śaṭha</s>, and <s>Vikaṭa</s>;
and of the rākṣasas <s>Hrasvakarṇa</s>, <s>Daṃṣṭra</s>, and <s>Romaśa</s>.
Then, in order, he passed those of <s>Yuddhonmatta</s>, <s>Matta</s>, <s>Dhvajagrīva</s>, and <s>Nādin</s>,
and likewise those of <s>Vidyujjihva</s>, <s>Indrajihva</s>, and <s>Hastimukha</s>;
and indeed those of <s>Karāla</s>, <s>Piśāca</s>, and <s>Śoṇitākṣa</s>.
Thus <s>Hanūmān</s>, the son of the wind, advanced step by step.
In those very costly mansions, one after another,

children.text: teṣām ṛddhimatām ṛddhiṃ dadarśa sa mahākapiḥ ||
children.translated_text: that famous great monkey saw the prosperity of those prosperous beings.
Passing on every side beyond the houses of them all,
the fortunate one then reached the residence of the lord of the rākṣasas.
The best of monkeys saw the female attendants who slept near <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Moving about, the tiger among monkeys saw rākṣasī women with distorted eyes,
holding spears and clubs in their hands, and carrying lances and javelins.
He saw many kinds of guard-posts in the house of that lord of rākṣasas.
He saw red, white, and pale horses, and also bay ones, of great speed,
well-bred, handsome elephants, crushers of enemy elephants,
trained in elephant-riding and equal to <s>Airāvata</s> in battle,

children.text: nihantṝn parasainyānāṃ gṛhe tasmin dadarśa saḥ ||
children.translated_text: slayers of hostile armies; he saw them in that house.

children.text: kṣarataśca yathā meghān sravataśca yathā girīn
children.translated_text: Like clouds pouring down, and like mountains streaming forth,
with a roar like the thunder of clouds, impossible for enemies to withstand in battle,
he saw there a thousand processional chariots plated with jāmbūnada gold,
covered throughout with golden networks, resembling the young sun.
In the residence of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of rākṣasas,
that monkey, the son of the wind, saw litters of many forms.
He saw charming vine-bowers and picture-gallery houses,
pleasure houses of other kinds as well, and wooden artificial mountains.

children.text: kāmasya gṛhakaṃ ramyaṃ divāgṛhakam eva ca
children.translated_text: In the residence of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of rākṣasas,
he saw a delightful house of love, and also a daytime pavilion.
He saw that best of buildings, like the slope of <s>Mandara</s>, crowded with places for peacocks,
and filled with banner-staffs.
It had an endless mass of jewels and a network of treasures everywhere,
and its work had been firmly completed; it was like the house of the lord of beings.
With the rays of its jewels and with the splendor of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: virarājātha tad veśma raśmimān iva raśmibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: that mansion then shone like the sun with his rays.
The lord of monkey troops saw beds and seats made of jāmbūnada gold,
and bright vessels as well.
Moistened by honey and wine, crowded with jeweled vessels,
charming and spacious, it was like the dwelling of <s>Kubera</s>.

children.text: nūpurāṇāṃ ca ghoṣeṇa kāñcīnāṃ ninadena ca
children.translated_text: It resounded with the sound of anklets and with the ringing of girdles,
and with the loud beats of drums and cymbals.
Endowed with groups of palaces and crowded with hundreds of jewel-like women,
<s>Hanūmān</s> entered the great house, whose inner courts were well arranged.
Strong <s>Hanūmān</s> saw the network of mansions, covered with lattices of vaidūrya and gold,

children.text: yathā mahat prāvṛṣi meghajālaṃ vidyutpinaddhaṃ savihaṃgajālam ||
children.translated_text: like a vast mass of clouds in the rainy season, bound with lightning and filled with flocks of birds.
He saw various halls among the residences: chief halls for conches, weapons, and bows,

children.text: manoharāścāpi punar viśālā dadarśa veśmādriṣu candraśālāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and again, on the mansion-peaks, charming, spacious moon-chambers.
The monkey saw houses adorned with various riches, honored even by gods and asuras,

children.text: sarvaiśca doṣaiḥ parivarjitāni kapir dadarśa svabalārjitāni ||
children.translated_text: free from every defect and won by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s own power.

children.text: tāni prayatnābhisamāhitāni mayena sākṣād iva nirmitāni
children.translated_text: He saw the houses of the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, carefully planned and composed,
as if built by <s>Maya</s> himself, surpassing all qualities upon the earth.
Then he saw the highest house, shaped like a lofty cloud, delightful, and beautiful with gold,
suited to the strength of the lord of rākṣasas and of an incomparable form.

children.text: mahītale svargam iva prakīrṇaṃ śriyā jvalantaṃ bahuratnakīrṇam
children.translated_text: It was like heaven spread upon the earth, blazing with splendor and strewn with many jewels,
scattered with flowers from various trees, like a mountain peak covered with pollen.

children.text: nārīpravekair iva dīpyamānaṃ taḍidbhir ambhodavad arcyamānam
children.translated_text: It shone as if with foremost women, and was adored like a raincloud by lightning flashes;

children.text: haṃsapravekair iva vāhyamānaṃ śriyā yutaṃ khe sukṛtāṃ vimānam ||
children.translated_text: as if borne by excellent swans, it was a sky-going palace of the meritorious, endowed with beauty.

children.text: yathā nagāgraṃ bahudhātucitraṃ yathā nabhaśca grahacandracitram
children.translated_text: As a mountain peak is variegated with many minerals, and as the sky is variegated with planets and the moon,
he saw that jewel among aerial palaces, variegated with arranged cloud-like designs and many gems.

children.text: mahī kṛtā parvatarājipūrṇā śailāḥ kṛtā vṛkṣavitānapūrṇāḥ
children.translated_text: The earth had been fashioned full of rows of mountains; the mountains had been fashioned full of spreading trees;

children.text: vṛkṣāḥ kṛtāḥ puṣpavitānapūrṇāḥ puṣpaṃ kṛtaṃ kesarapatrapūrṇam ||
children.translated_text: the trees had been fashioned full of masses of flowers; each flower had been fashioned full of filaments and petals.

children.text: kṛtāni veśmāni ca pāṇḍurāṇi tathā supuṣpā api puṣkariṇyaḥ
children.translated_text: White mansions too had been made, and likewise ponds full of fine flowers;

children.text: punaśca padmāni sakesarāṇi dhanyāni citrāṇi tathā vanāni ||
children.translated_text: and again lotuses with their filaments, and rich, colorful groves had been fashioned.
There, the great monkey saw a great <s>vimāna</s> (aerial palace) named <s>Puṣpaka</s>, splendid and enhanced by the radiance of jewels,
rising even above the finest mansions.

children.text: kṛtāśca vaidūryamayā vihaṃgā rūpyapravālaiśca tathā vihaṃgāḥ
children.translated_text: There were birds made of vaidūrya, and likewise birds made with silver and coral;
variegated serpents of many precious materials, and handsome horses fashioned according to their breeds.
The crafted birds had wings of coral, jāmbūnada gold, and flowers, with gracefully bent, curving pinions;

children.text: kāmasya sākṣād iva bhānti pakṣāḥ kṛtā vihaṃgāḥ sumukhāḥ supakṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: with beautiful faces and fine wings, they shone like the very wings of <s>Kāma</s> himself.
There were well-trunked elephants as if being harnessed, maned, and holding lotus leaves in their trunks;

children.text: babhūva devī ca kṛtā suhastā lakṣmīstathā padmini padmahastā ||
children.translated_text: and the goddess <s>Lakṣmī</s> too had been fashioned there, fair-handed, lotus-born and lotus-handed.

children.text: itīva tad gṛham abhigamya śobhanaṃ savismayo nagam iva cāruśobhanam
children.translated_text: Thus, having approached that beautiful palace, he was filled with wonder, as if before a lovely mountain;

children.text: punaśca tat paramasugandhi sundaraṃ himātyaye nagam iva cārukandaram ||
children.translated_text: and again it seemed supremely fragrant and beautiful, like a mountain with lovely caves at winter's end.

children.text: tataḥ sa tāṃ kapir abhipatya pūjitāṃ caran purīṃ daśamukhabāhupālitām
children.translated_text: Then that monkey ranged through the honored city protected by the arms of the ten-headed one,

children.text: adṛśya tāṃ janakasutāṃ supūjitāṃ suduḥkhitāṃ patiguṇaveganirjitām ||
children.translated_text: but he did not see the honored daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, deeply distressed and overcome by the force of her husband's virtues.
Then, for that self-controlled and accomplished great soul, whose mind reflected in many ways,

children.text: apaśyato 'bhavad atiduḥkhitaṃ manaḥ sucakṣuṣaḥ pravicarato mahātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: his mind became exceedingly sorrowful when, though keen-eyed and wandering about, he did not see the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>.
In the middle of that foremost residence, broad and long,
<s>Hanūmān</s>, son of the wind, saw the finest of buildings.
That building of the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s> was half a yojana wide
and a yojana long, crowded with many palaces.
Searching for the wide-eyed <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Vaidehī</s>,
<s>Hanūmān</s>, destroyer of foes, went all around on every side.
It was surrounded by four-tusked elephants and likewise by three-tusked ones,
spacious and unobstructed, guarded by warriors with raised weapons.
The dwelling of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> was encircled by his <s>rākṣasī</s> wives,
and by princesses who had been carried off by force.
It was like the ocean, filled with crocodiles and makaras, crowded with timiṅgilas and fish,
shaken by the speed of the wind and full of serpents.

children.text: yā hi vaiśravaṇe lakṣmīr yā cendre harivāhane
children.translated_text: Whatever splendor belongs to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, and whatever belongs to <s>Indra</s> of the bay horses,
all of that dwelt constantly in <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s house and never departed.

children.text: yā ca rājñaḥ kuberasya yamasya varuṇasya ca
children.translated_text: And whatever wealth belongs to king <s>Kubera</s>, to <s>Yama</s>, and to <s>Varuṇa</s>,
such prosperity, or even greater, was here in the houses of the <s>rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: tasya harmyasya madhyasthaṃ veśma cānyat sunirmitam
children.translated_text: In the middle of that palace, the son of the wind saw another well-built mansion,
crowded with many projecting pavilions.

children.text: brahmaṇo 'rthe kṛtaṃ divyaṃ divi yad viśvakarmaṇā
children.translated_text: It was the divine <s>vimāna</s> named <s>Puṣpaka</s>, adorned with every jewel,
which <s>Viśvakarman</s> had made in heaven for the sake of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: pareṇa tapasā lebhe yat kuberaḥ pitāmahāt
children.translated_text: By supreme austerity <s>Kubera</s> had obtained it from the grandsire;

children.text: kuberam ojasā jitvā lebhe tad rākṣaseśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, having conquered <s>Kubera</s> by his might, obtained it.
It was furnished with artificial beasts and with well-made pillars

children.text: sukṛtair ācitaṃ stambhaiḥ pradīptam iva ca śriyā ||
children.translated_text: of refined gold, and it seemed to blaze with splendor.
It was adorned on every side with fine upper chambers shaped like <s>Meru</s> and <s>Mandara</s>,
as though they were scraping the sky.
That <s>vimāna</s>, made well by <s>Viśvakarman</s>, shone like fire and sun;
it had golden stairways and a lovely, excellent dais.
It was fitted with golden and crystal latticed windows,
and with a splendid dais of indranīla and great nīla gems;
the great monkey climbed that divine <s>Puṣpaka</s> <s>vimāna</s>.
Standing there, he smelled a divine, mingled fragrance
arising from drink, delicacies, and cooked food, like wind made visible.

children.text: sa gandhastaṃ mahāsattvaṃ bandhur bandhum ivottamam
children.translated_text: That fragrance spoke, as it were, to that great being like the dearest friend to a friend:

children.text: ita ehītyuvāceva tatra yatra sa rāvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Come here,' to the place where <s>Rāvaṇa</s> was.

children.text: tatastāṃ prasthitaḥ śālāṃ dadarśa mahatīṃ śubhām
children.translated_text: Then, setting out toward that hall, he saw it, great and splendid,
dear to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s heart, like a lovely and excellent woman.
It was fashioned with jeweled stairways, shining with golden latticework,
its floor covered with crystal and its forms inlaid with ivory.
It was adorned with pearls, corals, silver, and gold,
and embellished with jewel pillars and very many other pillars.
With even, straight, very high pillars, beautifully ornamented all around,

children.text: stambhaiḥ pakṣair ivātyuccair divaṃ samprasthitām iva ||
children.translated_text: it seemed to set out toward heaven, as if on lofty wings.
It was spread with a great carpet marked with the features of the earth,
and looked as broad as the earth, with its kingdoms and rows of houses.
It resounded with intoxicated birds and was scented with divine fragrances;
it had supremely precious coverings and was attended by the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>.
It was darkened by aloe-wood incense, yet spotless and white as a swan;
variegated with offerings of flowers, it was bright though mottled.
It brought delight to the mind and even made one's complexion clear;

children.text: tāṃ śokanāśinīṃ divyāṃ śriyaḥ saṃjananīm iva ||
children.translated_text: divine, dispelling grief, it seemed to generate prosperity itself.
Then that hall guarded by <s>Rāvaṇa</s> satisfied the five senses
with the five excellent objects of the senses, like a mother.
'This is heaven; this is the world of the gods; this must be <s>Indra</s>'s city,

children.text: siddhir veyaṃ parā hi syād ityamanyata mārutiḥ ||
children.translated_text: or else this is supreme attainment itself,' thought <s>Māruti</s>.
There he saw golden lamps that seemed to be brooding in thought,
like cheats defeated at dice by greater cheats.

children.text: dīpānāṃ ca prakāśena tejasā rāvaṇasya ca
children.translated_text: By the brightness of the lamps and by the splendor of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>
and, from the radiance of the ornaments too, he thought it was blazing.
Then he saw, seated on rugs, with garments and garlands of many colors,
a thousand choice women, adorned with many kinds of dress and ornament.
When half the night had passed, overcome by drinking and sleep,
after they had sported and ceased in the night, that powerful company slept soundly then.
That sleeping hall shone, its inner ornaments silent,
like a great lotus-wood where swans and bees are silent.
<s>Māruti</s> saw the faces of those lovely women, with teeth covered and eyes closed,
fragrant like lotuses.
At the end of night, becoming like lotuses awakened,
then again, at night, they appeared with their petals closed.
These lotus-faces, surely, intoxicated six-footed bees
seek again and again as if they were blossoming water-lotuses.
Thus the glorious great monkey reasoned by inference,
for he thought them, in their qualities, equal to water-born lotuses.

children.text: sā tasya śuśubhe śālā tābhiḥ strībhir virājitā
children.translated_text: That hall of his, adorned with those women, shone
like the clear autumn sky made beautiful by stars.

children.text: sa ca tābhiḥ parivṛtaḥ śuśubhe rākṣasādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: And the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, surrounded by them, shone
just as the splendid lord of the stars is surrounded by stars.
The stars that fall from the sky when their store of merit is exhausted,

children.text: imāstāḥ saṃgatāḥ kṛtsnā iti mene haristadā ||
children.translated_text: all those, gathered here, are these women, so the monkey thought then.
Like the radiance, color, and clearness of great stars
with auspicious rays, the women there shone distinctly.
Their heavy, full garlands had slipped aside, and their fine ornaments were scattered;
at times of drinking and exercise, sleep had stolen away their minds.
Some had their tilakas displaced, and some had anklets gone astray;
some lovely women had necklaces slipped to the side.
Others were encircled with pearl necklaces; some had garments fallen loose;
their girdle-bands were disordered, like young mares after being driven.
Others wore fine earrings and had garlands torn and crushed,
like flowering creepers in a great forest crushed by a lordly elephant.
The high necklaces of some women, shining like rays of moonlight,

children.text: haṃsā iva babhuḥ suptāḥ stanamadhyeṣu yoṣitām ||
children.translated_text: appeared as sleeping swans between the breasts of the women.

children.text: aparāsāṃ ca vaidūryāḥ kādambā iva pakṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: For others, vaidūrya gems were like kādamba birds,
and the golden cords of others looked like cakravākas.
Filled with swans and kāraṇḍava birds and beautified by cakravākas,

children.text: āpagā iva tā rejur jaghanaiḥ pulinair iva ||
children.translated_text: they shone like rivers, with their hips like sandy banks.
Resembling nets of little bells, with broad golden lotuses,
with feeling as their crocodiles and fame as their banks, they appeared like sleeping rivers.
On the soft limbs of some, and resting on the tips of their breasts,
beautiful rows of ornaments became like ornaments upon ornaments.
The lovely ends of the garments of some, stirred by the breath from their mouths,
were blown again and again above their faces.
Raised like banners, those bright-hued cloths of the wives
shone at the bases of their faces, made of many colors and gold.
Here the earrings of some lovely women, bright with auspicious rays,
fluttered very gently from contact with the breath of their mouths.
The breath from their faces, scented with sugar-liquor, naturally fragrant and pleasant,
attended upon <s>Rāvaṇa</s> then.
Some of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s women, suspecting the face of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: mukhāni sma sapatnīnām upājighran punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: kept smelling again and again the faces of their co-wives.
Those excellent women, their minds excessively attached to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
not independent, then did only what was dear to their co-wives.
Other young women, adorned with encircling ornaments, laid down their arms
and their beautiful garments there.

children.text: anyā vakṣasi cānyasyāstasyāḥ kācit punar bhujam
children.translated_text: One woman lay on another's breast, and another again on her arm;
another was on the lap of another, and yet another on her two arms.
Relying on one another's thighs, sides, waists, and backs,
their limbs placed upon one another, they were subject to the power of intoxication and affection.
Delighting in the touch of one another's limbs, the slender-waisted women
all slept there with their arms made into one interlaced mass.
That garland of women, strung together by the thread of one another's arms,
shone like a garland strung on a thread and filled with intoxicated bees.
Like blossoming vines in the month of Mādhava, served by the wind,
their clusters of flowers were interwoven in mutual garlands and clinging together.
With lovely trunks twined around one another and thronged by one another's bees,

children.text: āsīd vanam ivoddhūtaṃ strīvanaṃ rāvaṇasya tat ||
children.translated_text: that forest of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s women was like a forest stirred by the wind.

children.text: uciteṣvapi suvyaktaṃ na tāsāṃ yoṣitāṃ tadā
children.translated_text: Even among things well known to belong to each, plainly, at that time
it was impossible to make a distinction among those women's ornaments, limbs, garments, and garlands.
While <s>Rāvaṇa</s> was lying comfortably, those women, of varied splendor,
were watched by blazing golden lamps, as if the lamps were unwinking.
The wives of royal seers, ancestors, daityas, and gandharvas,
and the maidens of <s>rākṣasas</s>, had come under his power of desire.

children.text: na tatra kācit pramadā prasahya vīryopapannena guṇena labdhā
children.translated_text: There was no woman there won by force by his valor, power, or virtue;

children.text: na cānyakāmāpi na cānyapūrvā vinā varārhāṃ janakātmajāṃ tu ||
children.translated_text: nor was there any who loved another, nor any formerly belonging to another, except the worthy daughter of <s>Janaka</s>.

children.text: na cākulīnā na ca hīnarūpā nādakṣiṇā nānupacārayuktā
children.translated_text: No wife of his was of low family, nor poor in beauty, nor unskilled, nor lacking in courteous service;

children.text: bhāryābhavat tasya na hīnasattvā na cāpi kāntasya na kāmanīyā ||
children.translated_text: none became his wife who was low in spirit, nor unlovely to her beloved, nor undesirable.
But the thought arose in the lord of monkeys: if <s>Rāghava</s>'s lawful wife were of such a kind,

children.text: imā yathā rākṣasarājabhāryāḥ sujātam asyeti hi sādhubuddheḥ ||
children.translated_text: as these wives of the king of the <s>rākṣasas</s> are, then his judgment would indeed be noble and well born.

children.text: punaśca so 'cintayad ārtarūpo dhruvaṃ viśiṣṭā guṇato hi sītā
children.translated_text: And again, afflicted in appearance, he thought: surely <s>Sītā</s> is especially distinguished in virtues;

children.text: athāyam asyāṃ kṛtavānmahātmā laṅkeśvaraḥ kaṣṭam anāryakarma ||
children.translated_text: for this great-souled lord of <s>Laṅkā</s> has done a harsh and ignoble deed with regard to her.
There, looking around, <s>Hanumān</s> saw a foremost couch,
divine in appearance, made of crystal, and adorned with jewels.
And in one part of it he saw a white parasol,
adorned with excellent garlands and resembling the lord of the stars, the moon.
It was being fanned on every side by women holding chowries,
filled with many kinds of fragrances and perfumed with excellent incense.
It was spread with the finest coverings and covered with woolen skins,
and all around it was made splendid by strings of excellent garlands.
On that couch he saw one like a rain cloud, with excellent earrings blazing,
red-eyed, great-armed, and wearing a great silvery garment;
his limbs were anointed with fragrant red sandalwood,
like a cloud in the sky reddened by twilight and streaked with lightning.
Surrounded by divine ornaments, handsome, and able to assume forms at will,
he seemed like <s>Mandara</s> asleep, rich with trees, woods, and thickets.
Having sported in the night and then ceased, he was adorned with excellent ornaments,
dear to the <s>rākṣasa</s> maidens and a giver of pleasure to the <s>rākṣasas</s>.
After drinking too and then stopping, the great monkey saw him,
the heroic lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, asleep on a brilliant bed.
The best of monkeys, having come upon <s>Rāvaṇa</s> breathing like a serpent,
became extremely agitated and drew back, as if very afraid.
Then, reaching an ascent and taking his place on another platform,
the great monkey gazed at the sleeping tiger among <s>rākṣasas</s>.
The excellent bed of the sleeping lord of <s>rākṣasas</s> shone,
like a great cascade when a rutting elephant has entered it.
And the noble monkey saw the two arms of the lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>,
bound with golden armlets and flung out, like the standards of <s>Indra</s>.
They bore wounds made by the pressure of the tips of <s>Airāvata</s>'s tusks,
their massive shoulders scratched by the thunderbolt and marked by <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s discus.
They were full, with well-formed equal shoulders, joined and endowed with strength,
with auspicious nails and thumbs, and marked on the palms and fingers.
Compact, shaped like iron bars, rounded, and like elephant trunks,
they lay spread out on the white bed like two five-headed serpents.
They were well anointed and well adorned with the finest sandalwood,
cool and fragrant, with a hue like fresh blood.
Rubbed by the finest women and attended by the best perfumes,
they were arms before which <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>pannagas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, gods, and <s>dānavas</s> had cried out.
The monkey saw those two arms of his lying on the bed,
like two great enraged serpents asleep within <s>Mandara</s>.
With those two full arms, the lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>,
mountain-like, shone like <s>Mandara</s> with its two peaks.
Fragrant with mango and puṃnāga blossoms and joined with finest bakula scent,
mixed with the flavor of rich food and preceded by the smell of drink,
a great breath came forth from the mouth of that lion among <s>rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: śayānasya viniḥśvāsaḥ pūrayann iva tad gṛham ||
children.translated_text: as he lay asleep, as though filling that whole house.
His face was lit by earrings and by a golden, shining crown,
variegated with pearls and gems, which had slipped aside.
He was bright with a broad, deep, and expansive chest,
anointed with red sandalwood and adorned with a shining necklace.
With pale fine linen cast aside and with blood-red eyes,
he was well wrapped in a costly, excellent yellow garment.
Dark like a heap of black gram and breathing like a serpent,
he seemed like an elephant asleep on the broad bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
By four golden lamps blazing in the four directions,
all his limbs were made visible, like a cloud by clusters of lightning.
At the feet of that very mighty lord in the house of the ruler of <s>rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: patnīḥ sa priyabhāryasya tasya rakṣaḥpater gṛhe ||
children.translated_text: he also saw the wives of him who was dear to his beloved women.
The leader of the monkey hosts saw women with faces bright as the moon,
adorned with excellent earrings and with garlands and ornaments unfaded.
Skilled in dancing and instrumental music, resting within the embrace of the lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>' arms,
and wearing the finest ornaments, those women were seen by the monkey as they sat there.
At the ends of the women's ears he saw golden earrings,
with diamonds and vaidūrya gems set within them, and bracelets as well.
With their lovely moon-like faces and graceful earrings,
that aerial palace shone like the sky with its host of stars.
Exhausted by intoxication and exertion, those women of the lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>,
slender-waisted, slept in those various places.
One woman slept clasping a vīṇā, and shone there,
like a lotus plant scattered by a great river and clinging to a boat.
Another dark-eyed woman slept with a maḍḍuka drum tucked under her arm,
and the lovely woman appeared like a tender mother with her little child.
A woman of beautiful limbs and lovely breasts slept pressing a paṭaha drum to herself,
like a passionate woman embracing a lover obtained after a long time.
Some lotus-eyed woman slept embracing a shoulder,
overcome by sleep, like a lovely woman together with her beloved.
Another woman, with limbs like gold, soft, full, and charming,
clasping a mṛdaṅga with her body, slept, her eyes intoxicated.
With a paṇava lying between her arm and side, tucked at her armpit,
a blameless slender-waisted woman slept with it, wearied by intoxication.
Another, taking up a ḍiṇḍima, likewise clung to the ḍiṇḍima,
and slept like a lovely woman embracing a young calf.
One lotus-petal-eyed woman, having made an āḍambara drum pressed in the embrace of her arms,
slept, bewildered by intoxication.
Another lovely woman, having set aside a kalaśī, slept and shone
like a flower-variegated garland in spring, smoothed out.
One young woman clasped her breasts, like golden jars, with her two hands,
and slept, overcome by the force of sleep.
Another lotus-petal-eyed woman, her face like the full moon,
embraced another woman, beautiful-hipped, and slept, overwhelmed by intoxication.
The excellent women embraced the various musical instruments

children.text: nipīḍya ca kucaiḥ suptāḥ kāminyaḥ kāmukān iva ||
children.translated_text: and, pressing them with their breasts, slept like lovers embracing beloved men.
On a fine bed set apart from those women lying there,

children.text: dadarśa rūpasampannām aparāṃ sa kapiḥ striyam ||
children.translated_text: the monkey saw another woman endowed with beauty.
She was beautifully adorned with ornaments set with pearls and gems,
and seemed to adorn the excellent palace by her own splendor.
Fair, shining with a golden hue, beloved, the mistress of the inner palace,
there the monkey saw <s>Mandodarī</s>, of lovely form, lying asleep.

children.text: sa tāṃ dṛṣṭvā mahābāhur bhūṣitāṃ mārutātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing her adorned in that way, the great-armed son of the Wind
reasoned from her perfection of beauty and youth that she was <s>Sītā</s>;
filled with great joy, the leader of the monkeys rejoiced.

children.text: āsphoṭayāmāsa cucumba pucchaṃ nananda cikrīḍa jagau jagāma
children.translated_text: He slapped his arms, kissed his tail, rejoiced, played, sang, and moved about;

children.text: stambhān arohannipapāta bhūmau nidarśayan svāṃ prakṛtiṃ kapīnām ||
children.translated_text: climbing the pillars and falling to the ground, he displayed his own monkey nature.
Then, shaking off that idea, he became composed,

children.text: jagāma cāparāṃ cintāṃ sītāṃ prati mahākapiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the great monkey turned to another reflection concerning <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: na rāmeṇa viyuktā sā svaptum arhati bhāminī
children.translated_text: That lovely woman, separated from <s>Rāma</s>, would not be able to sleep,

children.text: na bhoktuṃ nāpyalaṃkartuṃ na pānam upasevitum ||
children.translated_text: nor to eat, nor adorn herself, nor partake of drink.

children.text: nānyaṃ naram upasthātuṃ surāṇām api ceśvaram
children.translated_text: Nor would she attend upon another man, even if he were the lord of the gods;

children.text: na hi rāmasamaḥ kaścid vidyate tridaśeṣvapi
children.translated_text: for no one equal to <s>Rāma</s> exists even among the Thirty Gods.

children.text: anyeyam iti niścitya pānabhūmau cacāra saḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having decided, "This is another woman," he moved through the drinking hall.

children.text: krīḍitenāparāḥ klāntā gītena ca tathā parāḥ
children.translated_text: Some were tired by play, and others likewise by song;
others were tired by dancing and likewise overcome by drinking.
Some women were settled on murajas, mṛdaṅgas, and stools,
and other women had lain down on the finest couches.
With a thousand women adorned with ornaments,
of beautiful form, skilled in conversation, and speaking words joined with song and meaning,
skilled in place and time and uttering appropriate sentences,
the leader of the monkeys saw him asleep after pleasure and enjoyment.
In their midst the great-armed lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s> shone

children.text: goṣṭhe mahati mukhyānāṃ gavāṃ madhye yathā vṛṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: like a bull among the chief cows in a great herd.

children.text: sa rākṣasendraḥ śuśubhe tābhiḥ parivṛtaḥ svayam
children.translated_text: That lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s> himself shone, surrounded by them,
like a great elephant surrounded in the forest by cow elephants.
The tiger among monkeys saw the drinking hall of the great-souled one,
furnished with every object of desire, in the house of that lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: mṛgāṇāṃ mahiṣāṇāṃ ca varāhāṇāṃ ca bhāgaśaḥ
children.translated_text: There in the drinking hall he saw meats laid out in portions

children.text: tatra nyastāni māṃsāni pānabhūmau dadarśa saḥ ||
children.translated_text: from deer, buffaloes, and boars.
In broad golden vessels, partly eaten,
the tiger among monkeys saw peacocks and fowl as well.
He inspected boars and vārdhrāṇasaka meat, prepared with curds and sauvarcala salt,
and porcupines, deer, and peacocks; <s>Hanūmān</s> looked them over.
He saw various cooked kṛkara birds and half-eaten cakoras,
buffaloes, whole-spitted animals, and goats cooked to completion,

children.text: lekhyam uccāvacaṃ peyaṃ bhojyāni vividhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: lickable foods of high and low kinds, drinks, and various foods to be eaten.
With various sour and salty relishes and different sauces,
with costly necklaces, anklets, and armlets cast aside,
with fruits of many kinds scattered from drinking vessels,
the floor, with flower offerings made upon it, displayed even greater splendor.

children.text: tatra tatra ca vinyastaiḥ suśliṣṭaiḥ śayanāsanaiḥ
children.translated_text: Here and there, with well-arranged beds and seats laid out close together,
the drinking hall appeared as if blazing, though without fire.
With many kinds of varied meats, prepared with excellent seasonings,
set separately in the drinking hall and skillfully combined,

children.text: divyāḥ prasannā vividhāḥ surāḥ kṛtasurā api
children.translated_text: and with various clear divine liquors, as well as prepared liquors,
sugar-cane spirits, mādhvīka honey-liquors, flower-liquors, and fruit-liquors,
each separately perfumed with various fragrant powders,
the floor, covered with many garlands spread about, shone,
strewn with golden pitchers and crystal vessels,
and covered with other pitchers made of Jāmbūnada gold.
In silver jars and in jars made of Jāmbūnada gold,

children.text: pānaśreṣṭhaṃ tadā bhūri kapistatra dadarśa ha ||
children.translated_text: the monkey there saw abundant excellent drink.
The great monkey saw vessels for sīdhu liquor made of śātakumbha gold and of jewels,
and silver vessels too, all full.
In some places the drinks were half remaining; in some they had been drunk completely.

children.text: kvacin naiva prapītāni pānāni sa dadarśa ha ||
children.translated_text: In some places they had not been drunk at all; he saw those drinks there.

children.text: kvacid bhakṣyāṃśca vividhān kvacit pānāni bhāgaśaḥ
children.translated_text: In some places he saw various foods to be eaten, and in some, portions of drink.

children.text: kvacid annāvaśeṣāṇi paśyan vai vicacāra ha ||
children.translated_text: In some places, seeing remnants of food, he wandered about.

children.text: kvacit prabhinnaiḥ karakaiḥ kvacid āloḍitair ghaṭaiḥ
children.translated_text: In some places there were broken cups, and in some places jars that had been stirred about.

children.text: kvacit saṃpṛktamālyāni jalāni ca phalāni ca ||
children.translated_text: In some places garlands, water, and fruits were mixed together.
Elsewhere the beds of women were empty in many different ways.
Some excellent women slept embracing one another.

children.text: kācic ca vastram anyasyā apahṛtyopaguhya ca
children.translated_text: One woman, having taken another's garment and clasped it to herself,
came near and slept helplessly, overcome by the power of sleep.

children.text: tāsām ucchvāsavātena vastraṃ mālyaṃ ca gātrajam
children.translated_text: From the wind of their breathing, the cloth and garland upon their bodies

children.text: nātyarthaṃ spandate citraṃ prāpya mandam ivānilam ||
children.translated_text: moved only a little, wondrously, as if touched by a gentle breeze.

children.text: candanasya ca śītasya sīdhor madhurasasya ca
children.translated_text: Of cool sandalwood and of sweet-tasting <s>sīdhu</s> wine,

children.text: vividhasya ca mālyasya puṣpasya vividhasya ca ||
children.translated_text: and of varied garlands and many kinds of flowers,
the breeze there carried a manifold fragrance in many ways.

children.text: snānānāṃ candanānāṃ ca dhūpānāṃ caiva mūrchitaḥ
children.translated_text: Mingled with the scents of baths, sandal-pastes, and incenses,

children.text: pravavau surabhir gandho vimāne puṣpake tadā ||
children.translated_text: a fragrant odor then wafted through the <s>Puṣpaka</s> palace.
There were other women there, dark and fair, and some black, excellent-limbed women;
some women in the <s>rākṣasa</s> dwelling had limbs the color of gold.
Because they were under the power of sleep and bewildered by passion,

children.text: padminīnāṃ prasuptānāṃ rūpam āsīd yathaiva hi ||
children.translated_text: the appearance of those women was just like that of sleeping lotus-beds.
Thus the monkey of very great splendor saw all of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s inner palace

children.text: dadarśa sumahātejā na dadarśa ca jānakīm ||
children.translated_text: entirely and without remainder, but he did not see <s>Jānakī</s>.
Then, as that great monkey looked at those women,
he entered into great anxiety, troubled by fear concerning <s>dharma</s>.
This looking upon the sleeping enclosure of another's wives
will surely bring about a very great loss of <s>dharma</s> for me.

children.text: na hi me paradārāṇāṃ dṛṣṭir viṣayavartinī
children.translated_text: For my sight has not turned toward another's wives as objects of sense-desire,
yet here I have seen the possession of another's wives.
Then another thought arose in the mind of that wise one,
whose mind was fixed on one sole aim and who saw clearly the certainty of his task.

children.text: kāmaṃ dṛṣṭvā mayā sarvā viśvastā rāvaṇastriyaḥ
children.translated_text: Granted, I have seen all the women of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> lying trustingly asleep,

children.text: na tu me manasaḥ kiṃcid vaikṛtyam upapadyate ||
children.translated_text: but no alteration at all has arisen in my mind.

children.text: mano hi hetuḥ sarveṣām indriyāṇāṃ pravartate
children.translated_text: The mind indeed is the cause that sets all the senses in motion
in auspicious and inauspicious conditions, and that mind of mine is well controlled.

children.text: nānyatra hi mayā śakyā vaidehī parimārgitum
children.translated_text: <s>Vaidehī</s> cannot be sought by me anywhere else,

children.text: striyo hi strīṣu dṛśyante sadā samparimārgaṇe ||
children.translated_text: for when a search is being made, women are always found among women.

children.text: yasya sattvasya yā yonistasyāṃ tat parimārgyate
children.translated_text: Whatever the class of birth of a being is, it is searched for in that class;

children.text: na śakyaṃ pramadā naṣṭā mṛgīṣu parimārgitum ||
children.translated_text: a lost woman cannot be sought among does.

children.text: tad idaṃ mārgitaṃ tāvacchuddhena manasā mayā
children.translated_text: Therefore this whole inner palace of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> has now been searched by me

children.text: rāvaṇāntaḥpuraṃ sarvaṃ dṛśyate na ca jānakī ||
children.translated_text: with a pure mind; it is seen, but <s>Jānakī</s> is not.
Valiant <s>Hanumān</s>, looking over daughters of gods and gandharvas
and daughters of nāgas, still did not see <s>Jānakī</s>.
Not seeing her there, while seeing other excellent women,
the heroic monkey then withdrew and began to brood.

children.text: sa tasya madhye bhavanasya vānaro latāgṛhāṃścitragṛhānniśāgṛhān
children.translated_text: In the middle of that palace the <s>vānara</s>, eager for the sight of <s>Sītā</s>, went to vine-bowers, picture-halls, and night-chambers,

children.text: jagāma sītāṃ prati darśanotsuko na caiva tāṃ paśyati cārudarśanām ||
children.translated_text: yet he still did not see that lovely-looking woman.

children.text: sa cintayāmāsa tato mahākapiḥ priyām apaśyan raghunandanasya tām
children.translated_text: Then the great monkey, not seeing that beloved wife of <s>Raghunandana</s>, thought:

children.text: dhruvaṃ nu sītā mriyate yathā na me vicinvato darśanam eti maithilī ||
children.translated_text: Surely <s>Sītā</s> is dying, since <s>Maithilī</s> does not come into my sight as I search.

children.text: sā rākṣasānāṃ pravareṇa bālā svaśīlasaṃrakṣaṇatatparā satī
children.translated_text: That young virtuous woman, intent on protecting her own character,

children.text: anena nūnaṃ pratiduṣṭakarmaṇā hatā bhaved āryapathe pare sthitā ||
children.translated_text: has surely been killed by that evildoer, the foremost of <s>rākṣasas</s>, though she stood on the highest noble path.
Seeing the wives of the <s>rākṣasa</s> king, ugly, deformed, lusterless, huge-mouthed, and long and hideous to behold,

children.text: samīkṣya sā rākṣasarājayoṣito bhayād vinaṣṭā janakeśvarātmajā ||
children.translated_text: that daughter of King <s>Janaka</s> has perished from fear.

children.text: sītām adṛṣṭvā hyanavāpya pauruṣaṃ vihṛtya kālaṃ saha vānaraiściram
children.translated_text: Having failed to see <s>Sītā</s> and having achieved no success, after spending a long time with the <s>vānaras</s>,

children.text: na me 'sti sugrīvasamīpagā gatiḥ sutīkṣṇadaṇḍo balavāṃśca vānaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: there is no way for me to go near <s>Sugrīva</s>, for that powerful <s>vānara</s> has a very sharp punishment.
The whole inner palace has been seen, and <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s women have been seen;

children.text: na sītā dṛśyate sādhvī vṛthā jāto mama śramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but virtuous <s>Sītā</s> is not seen, and my labor has been born in vain.

children.text: kiṃ nu māṃ vānarāḥ sarve gataṃ vakṣyanti saṃgatāḥ
children.translated_text: What indeed will all the assembled <s>vānaras</s> say to me when I have returned?

children.text: gatvā tatra tvayā vīra kiṃ kṛtaṃ tad vadasva naḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having gone there, hero, what was done by you? Tell us that.

children.text: adṛṣṭvā kiṃ pravakṣyāmi tām ahaṃ janakātmajām
children.translated_text: Without having seen that daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, what shall I say?
Surely they will undertake a fast unto death when the appointed time has passed.

children.text: kiṃ vā vakṣyati vṛddhaśca jāmbavān aṅgadaśca saḥ
children.translated_text: Or what will aged <s>Jāmbavān</s> say, and that <s>Aṅgada</s>,
and the gathered <s>vānaras</s>, after I have crossed to the far shore of the ocean?

children.text: anirvedaḥ śriyo mūlam anirvedaḥ paraṃ sukham
children.translated_text: Non-despondency is the root of prosperity; non-despondency is the highest happiness.

children.text: bhūyastāvad viceṣyāmi na yatra vicayaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore I shall search again in the places where no search has been made.
For non-despondency is always the impeller in every undertaking;

children.text: karoti saphalaṃ jantoḥ karma yacca karoti saḥ ||
children.translated_text: it makes fruitful whatever action a creature performs.
