Therefore I will exert the utmost effort produced by non-despondency,
and I will search the unseen regions ruled by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Drinking halls have been searched, and so too flower-houses;
picture galleries have been searched, and again pleasure-houses.
Garden enclosures, inner lanes, and aerial mansions have been searched in every way.
Having thought thus, he again began to search.
He searched underground chambers, shrine-houses, and even rooms beyond rooms,
leaping up and dropping down, standing still, and sometimes going on again,
opening doors and pushing against their panels.
Entering and coming out, falling down and springing up as well,
that great monkey moved through every available space.
There was not even a space of four fingers' breadth

children.text: rāvaṇāntaḥpure tasmin yaṃ kapir na jagāma saḥ ||
children.translated_text: in that inner palace of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> where the monkey did not go.
The roads between the ramparts, the platforms, and the shrines,
the pits and lotus-ponds too, were all inspected by him.
Female <s>rākṣasas</s> of various forms, misshapen and distorted,

children.text: dṛṣṭā hanūmatā tatra na tu sā janakātmajā ||
children.translated_text: were seen there by <s>Hanūmat</s>, but not that daughter of <s>Janaka</s>.
Excellent women of the <s>vidyādharas</s>, unequalled in beauty in the world,

children.text: dṛṣṭā hanūmatā tatra na tu rāghavanandinī ||
children.translated_text: were seen there by <s>Hanūmat</s>, but not the delight of <s>Rāghava</s>.
Daughters of the <s>nāgas</s>, with fine hips and faces like the full moon,

children.text: dṛṣṭā hanūmatā tatra na tu sītā sumadhyamā ||
children.translated_text: were seen there by <s>Hanūmat</s>, but not slender-waisted <s>Sītā</s>.
Daughters of the <s>nāgas</s>, violently seized and carried off by the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: dṛṣṭā hanūmatā tatra na sā janakanandinī ||
children.translated_text: were seen there by <s>Hanūmat</s>, but not that delight of <s>Janaka</s>.
Not seeing her, though seeing other excellent women, the mighty-armed one,
the mighty-armed <s>Hanūmān</s>, son of the Wind, sank into despondency.
Seeing the effort of the monkey chiefs and the crossing of the ocean
as futile, the son of the Wind again fell into anxious thought.
Having descended from the aerial palace, <s>Hanūmān</s>, son of the Wind,
then fell into thought, his mind stricken by sorrow.
But after crossing down from the aerial palace to the rampart, the leader of the monkey troop,
swift <s>Hanūmān</s>, stood like lightning amid clouds.
Having gone all around the dwellings of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: adṛṣṭvā jānakīṃ sītām abravīd vacanaṃ kapiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and not having seen <s>Jānakī</s>, <s>Sītā</s>, the monkey spoke these words:

children.text: bhūyiṣṭhaṃ loḍitā laṅkā rāmasya caratā priyam
children.translated_text: Most of <s>Laṅkā</s> has been searched by me as I worked for <s>Rāma</s>'s good,

children.text: na hi paśyāmi vaidehīṃ sītāṃ sarvāṅgaśobhanām ||
children.translated_text: but I do not see <s>Vaidehī</s>, <s>Sītā</s>, beautiful in every limb.
Pools, tanks, lakes, and rivers too,
rivers, marshy forest regions, strongholds, and mountains,

children.text: loḍitā vasudhā sarvā na ca paśyāmi jānakīm ||
children.translated_text: the whole earth has been searched, yet I do not see <s>Jānakī</s>.
Here in <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s dwelling <s>Sītā</s> was reported by <s>Sampāti</s>,

children.text: ākhyātā gṛdhrarājena na ca paśyāmi tām aham ||
children.translated_text: the king of vultures, and yet I do not see her.

children.text: kiṃ nu sītātha vaidehī maithilī janakātmajā
children.translated_text: Can it be that <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Vaidehī</s>, <s>Maithilī</s>, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,
helplessly serves <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, whose conduct is wicked?

children.text: kṣipram utpatato manye sītām ādāya rakṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: I think that when the <s>rākṣasa</s> quickly flew up, carrying <s>Sītā</s>,
fearful of <s>Rāma</s>'s arrows, she may have fallen on the way.
Or, while she was being carried away along the path frequented by perfected beings,

children.text: manye patitam āryāyā hṛdayaṃ prekṣya sāgaram ||
children.translated_text: I think the noble lady's heart may have failed on seeing the ocean.
Through <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s terrible speed and through being crushed by his arms,

children.text: tayā manye viśālākṣyā tyaktaṃ jīvitam āryayā ||
children.translated_text: I think that wide-eyed noble lady gave up her life.
Or surely, as he then crossed over and over the ocean,
the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, struggling, fell into the sea.

children.text: āho kṣudreṇa cānena rakṣantī śīlam ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Alas, perhaps the ascetic <s>Sītā</s>, guarding her own chastity,
was eaten by this vile <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, with no kinsman to protect her.
Or else, the dark-eyed, innocent lady
may have been eaten by the wives of the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, whose hearts are wicked.
Meditating on <s>Rāma</s>'s face, resembling the full moon,

children.text: rāmasya dhyāyatī vaktraṃ pañcatvaṃ kṛpaṇā gatā ||
children.translated_text: with eyes like lotus petals, the pitiable woman has perhaps gone to death.

children.text: hā rāma lakṣmaṇetyeva hāyodhyeti ca maithilī
children.translated_text: Crying, 'Ah <s>Rāma</s>! <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>!' and 'Ah <s>Ayodhyā</s>!'
<s>Maithilī</s>, <s>Vaidehī</s>, after much lamentation, may have laid down her body.
Or else I think she has been placed somewhere in <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s dwelling;
surely she laments softly, like a mynah bird in a cage.
Born in the family of <s>Janaka</s>, the slender-waisted wife of <s>Rāma</s>,
how could the lotus-petal-eyed woman come under <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s power?

children.text: vinaṣṭā vā pranaṣṭā vā mṛtā vā janakātmajā
children.translated_text: Whether the daughter of <s>Janaka</s> is destroyed, lost, or dead,
it is not fitting to report this to <s>Rāma</s>, whose beloved wife she is.

children.text: nivedyamāne doṣaḥ syād doṣaḥ syād anivedane
children.translated_text: There would be fault if it is reported; there would be fault if it is not reported.

children.text: kathaṃ nu khalu kartavyaṃ viṣamaṃ pratibhāti me ||
children.translated_text: What, indeed, should be done? This appears to me a difficult matter.

children.text: asminn evaṃgate kārye prāptakālaṃ kṣamaṃ ca kim
children.translated_text: When the task has come to such a pass, what would be timely and proper?

children.text: bhaved iti matiṃ bhūyo hanumān pravicārayan ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hanūmān</s> considered the matter again in his mind.
If I go from here to the city of the monkey king

children.text: gamiṣyāmi tataḥ ko me puruṣārtho bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: without having seen <s>Sītā</s>, then what achievement will there be for me?
This crossing of the ocean by me will have been futile,
as will my entrance into <s>Laṅkā</s> and my sight of the <s>rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: kiṃ vā vakṣyati sugrīvo harayo vā samāgatāḥ
children.translated_text: What will <s>Sugrīva</s> say, or the assembled monkeys,
and what will the two sons of <s>Daśaratha</s> say when they have reached <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>?

children.text: gatvā tu yadi kākutsthaṃ vakṣyāmi param apriyam
children.translated_text: But if, after going to <s>Kākutstha</s>, I tell him the most unpleasant news,

children.text: na dṛṣṭeti mayā sītā tatastyakṣyanti jīvitam ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Sītā</s> was not seen by me,' then they will give up their lives.
On hearing that harsh, dreadful, cruel, piercing word, tormenting the senses,

children.text: sītānimittaṃ durvākyaṃ śrutvā sa na bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: the evil report concerning <s>Sītā</s>, he will not survive.
Seeing him in distress, his mind set upon death,
wise <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, deeply attached to him, will not survive.
Hearing that the two brothers have perished, <s>Bharata</s> too will die;

children.text: bharataṃ ca mṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā śatrughno na bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: and seeing <s>Bharata</s> dead, <s>Śatrughna</s> will not survive.
Then, seeing their sons dead, the mothers will not survive:

children.text: kausalyā ca sumitrā ca kaikeyī ca na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kausalyā</s>, <s>Sumitrā</s>, and <s>Kaikeyī</s>, without doubt.
Grateful and true to his promise, <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the monkeys,

children.text: rāmaṃ tathā gataṃ dṛṣṭvā tatastyakṣyanti jīvitam ||
children.translated_text: seeing <s>Rāma</s> in such a state, will then give up his life.
Downcast, afflicted, miserable, joyless, and suffering,
Afflicted by grief for her husband, <s>Rumā</s> will give up her life.
And <s>Tārā</s>, afflicted by sorrow and worn down by grief connected with <s>Vālin</s>,
will not survive when the king goes to the state of the five elements.
With the loss of his mother and father, and with <s>Sugrīva</s>'s calamity as well,
why would even Prince <s>Aṅgada</s> continue to sustain his life?
Overcome by grief for their lord, the forest-dwellers
will strike their heads with the palms of their hands and with their fists.
The vānaras, cherished by the glorious monkey-king
with conciliation, generous gifts, and honor, will abandon their lives.

children.text: na vaneṣu na śaileṣu na nirodheṣu vā punaḥ
children.translated_text: Neither in forests, nor on mountains, nor again in caverns
will the lordly monkeys enjoy sport after gathering together.
Oppressed by the disaster to their master, with sons, wives, and ministers,
they will gather and fall from mountain peaks onto rugged places.

children.text: viṣam udbandhanaṃ vāpi praveśaṃ jvalanasya vā
children.translated_text: Poison, hanging, entering the blazing fire,
fasting, or the weapon: the vānaras will resort to these.

children.text: ghoram ārodanaṃ manye gate mayi bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: I think there will be terrible lamentation when I am gone,
and the destruction of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> lineage, and also the destruction of the forest-dwellers.

children.text: so 'haṃ naiva gamiṣyāmi kiṣkindhāṃ nagarīm itaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore I will not go from here to the city of <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>.

children.text: na hi śakṣyāmyahaṃ draṣṭuṃ sugrīvaṃ maithilīṃ vinā ||
children.translated_text: For I will not be able to look upon <s>Sugrīva</s> without <s>Maithilī</s>.
But if I do not go and remain here, those two righteous great warriors
and the high-minded vānaras will sustain themselves on hope.
Restrained, eating what is taken by hand and mouth, living on roots at the foot of trees,
I will become a forest-dwelling ascetic, without having seen the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>.
In a region near the ocean, rich in roots, fruits, and water,
I will build a pyre and enter the kindled fire born from the araṇi sticks.
Or, while I sit, rightly undertaking the ascetic discipline and its marks,
crows and wild beasts will devour my body.

children.text: idam apy ṛṣibhir dṛṣṭaṃ niryāṇam iti me matiḥ
children.translated_text: This too has been seen by the seers as a way of departure; so I think.

children.text: samyag āpaḥ pravekṣyāmi na cet paśyāmi jānakīm ||
children.translated_text: I will properly enter the waters, if I do not see <s>Jānakī</s>.
For me, not seeing <s>Sītā</s>, this long night has shattered
a fair, noble-rooted, fortunate, famous garland of renown.
Or I will become a restrained ascetic, living on roots at the foot of trees;
I will not return from here without having seen that dark-eyed woman.
If I return from here without finding that <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: aṅgadaḥ sahitaiḥ sarvair vānarair na bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aṅgada</s>, together with all the vānaras, will cease to exist.

children.text: vināśe bahavo doṣā jīvan prāpnoti bhadrakam
children.translated_text: There are many faults in destruction; by living one obtains what is good.

children.text: tasmāt prāṇān dhariṣyāmi dhruvo jīvati saṃgamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore I will preserve my life, for union is certain for one who lives.
Holding such many-sided grief again and again in his mind,
the lordly monkey then found no far shore of his sorrow.
Or I will kill <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the mighty ten-necked one.

children.text: kāmam astu hṛtā sītā pratyācīrṇaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Let it be that <s>Sītā</s> has been carried off; retribution will have been made.
Or, having lifted him up and carried him over the ocean,
I will present him to <s>Rāma</s>, like a sacrificial animal to <s>Paśupati</s>.
Thus overwhelmed by thought, not having found that <s>Sītā</s>,
the vānara, his self encompassed by meditation and sorrow, reflected.

children.text: yāvat sītāṃ na paśyāmi rāmapatnīṃ yaśasvinīm
children.translated_text: Until I see <s>Sītā</s>, the glorious wife of <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: tāvad etāṃ purīṃ laṅkāṃ vicinomi punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I will search this city, <s>Laṅkā</s>, again and again.
And if, on <s>Sampāti</s>'s word, I bring <s>Rāma</s> here,
<s>Rāghava</s>, not seeing his wife, would burn up all the vānaras.
I will live right here, with regulated food and restrained senses,

children.text: na matkṛte vinaśyeyuḥ sarve te naravānarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: so that all those men and vānaras may not perish because of me.
And here is this great Aśoka grove, filled with great trees.

children.text: imām abhigamiṣyāmi na hīyaṃ vicitā mayā ||
children.translated_text: I will go into it, for it has not yet been searched by me.
Having bowed to the <s>Vasus</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, the <s>Ādityas</s>, the two <s>Aśvins</s>, and also the <s>Maruts</s>,
I will go as one who increases the sorrow of the rākṣasas.
Having conquered the rākṣasas, I will hand over the goddess, the delight of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> line,
to the ascetic <s>Rāma</s>, once success has been achieved.
After meditating for a moment, his senses loosened by anxiety,
the great-armed <s>Hanumān</s>, son of <s>Māruta</s>, stood up.

children.text: namo 'stu rāmāya salakṣmaṇāya devyai ca tasyai janakātmajāyai
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Rāma</s> together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and to that goddess, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>.
Homage to <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Yama</s>, and <s>Anila</s>; homage to the moon, the sun, and the hosts of <s>Maruts</s>.

children.text: sa tebhyastu namaskṛtvā sugrīvāya ca mārutiḥ
children.translated_text: Having bowed to them, and also to <s>Sugrīva</s>, the son of <s>Marut</s>
looked over all the directions and turned toward the Aśoka grove.

children.text: sa gatvā manasā pūrvam aśokavanikāṃ śubhām
children.translated_text: Having first gone in his mind to the auspicious Aśoka grove,
the vānara, son of <s>Māruta</s>, thought about what came next.
Surely it will be full of rākṣasas and crowded with woodland;
the Aśoka grove, adorned with every refinement, must be approached with care.
And guards appointed here surely protect the trees.
Even the blessed, all-pervading wind does not blow there with too much disturbance.

children.text: saṃkṣipto 'yaṃ mayātmā ca rāmārthe rāvaṇasya ca
children.translated_text: I have made this body of mine small for <s>Rāma</s>'s purpose and with regard to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Here the gods, together with the hosts of seers, will arrange success for me.

children.text: brahmā svayambhūr bhagavān devāścaiva diśantu me
children.translated_text: May the blessed self-born <s>Brahmā</s> himself, and the gods, grant me
success, and <s>Agni</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, and the much-invoked wielder of the thunderbolt.
May <s>Varuṇa</s>, with noose in hand, and <s>Soma</s> and <s>Āditya</s> likewise,

children.text: aśvinau ca mahātmānau marutaḥ sarva eva ca ||
children.translated_text: and the two great-souled <s>Aśvins</s>, and all the <s>Maruts</s>, grant it.

children.text: siddhiṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāni bhūtānāṃ caiva yaḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: All beings, and he who is lord of beings,

children.text: dāsyanti mama ye cānye adṛṣṭāḥ pathi gocarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and whatever others, unseen, move upon the path, will grant me success.

children.text: tad unnasaṃ pāṇḍuradantam avraṇaṃ śucismitaṃ padmapalāśalocanam
children.translated_text: That face, with raised nose, white teeth, without blemish, with a pure smile and eyes like lotus petals,

children.text: drakṣye tad āryāvadanaṃ kadā nvahaṃ prasannatārādhipatulyadarśanam ||
children.translated_text: when indeed shall I see that noble face, whose sight is like the clear lord of the stars?
By a vile, sinful one, doer of cruel deeds, wearing a very terrible ornamented disguise,

children.text: balābhibhūtā abalā tapasvinī kathaṃ nu me dṛṣṭapathe 'dya sā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: overpowered by force, helpless, ascetic woman that she is, how may she come within my sight today?

children.text: sa muhūrtam iva dhyātvā manasā cādhigamya tām
children.translated_text: Having pondered for a moment and having found her in his mind,
the greatly radiant one leapt down upon the rampart of that mansion.
Then the great monkey, every limb thrilled with joy, standing on the rampart,
saw various trees with flowering tops at the beginning of spring:
sāla trees, aśokas, splendid ones, and well-flowered campakas,
uddālakas, nāga-trees, mangoes, and kapimukhas too.
Then, into one covered with a mango grove and surrounded by hundreds of creepers,
he leapt like an arrow released from a bowstring into the tree garden.

children.text: sa praviśya vicitrāṃ tāṃ vihagair abhināditām
children.translated_text: Entering that wondrous place, resounding with birds,
surrounded everywhere by silver and golden trees,
varied with flocks of birds and herds of deer, a grove of many colors,
<s>Hanumān</s> the monkey saw it shining like the risen sun.
It was enclosed by many kinds of trees, bearing flowers and bearing fruit,
and constantly frequented by intoxicated cuckoos and royal bees.
At a season that gladdened people, crowded with deer and birds,
loud with companies of intoxicated peacocks, filled with many flocks of twice-born birds,
searching for the fair-hipped, blameless princess,
the monkey woke the birds that had fallen happily asleep.
Struck by the wings of the flocks of birds flying up,
the sāla trees, of many colors and kinds, released showers of flowers.
Covered with scattered flowers, <s>Hanumān</s>, son of the Wind, shone
in the midst of the Aśoka grove like a mountain made of flowers.
Seeing the monkey rushing through all quarters in the thickets of trees,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā sarvāṇi bhūtāni vasanta iti menire ||
children.translated_text: all beings thought, 'It is spring.'
With flowers of many kinds fallen from the trees and strewn about,
the earth there shone like a woman adorned for pleasure.
Those trees, shaken forcefully by the swift one,
then let fall their many-colored blossoms because of the monkey.
With their leaves and tops shaken off, their flowers and fruits fallen,
the trees looked like defeated rogues who had cast away their garments and ornaments.
Shaken by swift <s>Hanumān</s>, those excellent trees,
rich in flowers, quickly dropped flowers, leaves, and fruits.
Deprived of their flocks of birds, with only their trunks and branches remaining,
all the trees became hard to approach, as if shaken by the wind.
As a young woman with her hair disheveled, her cosmetic color rubbed away,
her lovely teeth and lips drained of beauty, scratched by nails and teeth,
so too, crushed by tail and hands and by feet,
the Aśoka grove became one whose fine trees were broken.
The monkey violently scattered the garlands of great creepers,
as the wind scatters masses of clouds over the <s>Vindhya</s> in the rainy season.
There the monkey, wandering, saw jewel pavements,
lovely silver pavements, and likewise golden pavements.
And here and there he saw ponds of various shapes, filled with excellent water,
furnished with costly stairways of jewels,
with floors inlaid with pearls, coral sand, and crystal,
beautified on their banks by variegated golden trees.
Their beds of blooming lotuses and blue lotuses were called over by cakravākas,
resounded with the cries of waterfowl, and filled with the calls of geese and cranes.
On every side they were adorned with long rivers accompanied by trees,
auspicious, prepared with waters like nectar.
They were covered with hundreds of creepers and overgrown with santānaka plants,
their groves enclosed by many shrubs, with spaces made by oleanders.
Then he saw a mountain like a rain cloud, with high peaks,
having varied summits and surrounded on all sides by peaks,
spread with stone houses and covered with many trees;
the tiger among monkeys saw that lovely mountain in the world.

children.text: dadarśa ca nagāt tasmānnadīṃ nipatitāṃ kapiḥ
children.translated_text: The monkey also saw a river falling from that mountain,

children.text: aṅkād iva samutpatya priyasya patitāṃ priyām ||
children.translated_text: like a beloved woman fallen from the lap of her beloved after springing up.
It was beautified by trees whose tips had fallen into the water,
like an angry woman being restrained by her dear kinsmen.

children.text: punar āvṛttatoyāṃ ca dadarśa sa mahākapiḥ
children.translated_text: The great monkey saw its water turning back again,

children.text: prasannām iva kāntasya kāntāṃ punar upasthitām ||
children.translated_text: like a beloved woman, now gracious, returning again to her lover.
Not far from it, the tiger among monkeys, <s>Hanumān</s>, son of the Wind,
saw lotus ponds filled with many flocks of birds.

children.text: kṛtrimāṃ dīrghikāṃ cāpi pūrṇāṃ śītena vāriṇā
children.translated_text: He also saw an artificial long pond filled with cool water,
with excellent jewel stairways and shining with pearl sand,
varied with herds of many kinds of deer, a grove of many colors,
and adorned on every side with very great mansions built by <s>Viśvakarman</s>,
and with artificial groves as well.
Whatever trees were there, bearing flowers and bearing fruit,
all had parasols and platforms, and all had golden altars.
Covered with many spreading creepers and many leaves,

children.text: kāñcanīṃ śiṃśupām ekāṃ dadarśa sa mahākapiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the great monkey saw one golden śiṃśupā tree.
He saw stretches of ground, hollows, and springs,
and he saw other golden trees, resembling flames.

children.text: teṣāṃ drumāṇāṃ prabhayā meror iva mahākapiḥ
children.translated_text: By the radiance of those trees, the great monkey, as if on <s>Meru</s>,
the heroic monkey then thought, "I am golden."
Seeing that grove stirred by the wind among masses of golden trees,
resounding with the jingling of hundreds of bells, he was filled with wonder.
With flowering tips, beautiful, and furnished with fresh sprouts and leaves,
the very swift one climbed that śiṃśapā tree covered with foliage.
"From here I shall see <s>Vaidehī</s>, longing for the sight of <s>Rāma</s>,
distressed with grief, moving about here and there by chance.
This aśoka grove of the wicked one is indeed delightful,
adorned with campakas and sandalwoods, and also with bakulas.
And this lovely lotus pond is frequented by flocks of birds;

children.text: imāṃ sā rāmamahiṣī nūnam eṣyati jānakī ||
children.translated_text: surely <s>Jānakī</s>, <s>Rāma</s>'s queen, will come to it.

children.text: sā rāmā rāmamahiṣī rāghavasya priyā sadā
children.translated_text: <s>Jānakī</s>, that lovely woman, <s>Rāma</s>'s queen, always dear to <s>Rāghava</s>,
skilled in roaming forests, will surely come here.
Or else the doe-eyed woman, knowing this grove well,
will come to this grove here, emaciated by thoughts of <s>Rāma</s>.
Scorched by grief for <s>Rāma</s>, that lovely-eyed noble lady,
always delighting in forest dwelling, will come here as a forest-roaming woman.
Surely she has long yearned constantly for the creatures that move in the forest,

children.text: rāmasya dayitā bhāryā janakasya sutā satī ||
children.translated_text: the beloved wife of <s>Rāma</s>, the chaste daughter of <s>Janaka</s>.
Dark in complexion and mindful of the twilight hour, <s>Jānakī</s> will surely come,
the fair woman, to this river of auspicious water for the twilight rite.
And this auspicious aśoka grove is suitable for her,

children.text: śubhā yā pārthivendrasya patnī rāmasya saṃmitā ||
children.translated_text: the auspicious wife of the lord of kings, well matched with <s>Rāma</s>.
If that noble lady, whose face is like the lord of stars, is alive,
then she will certainly come to this river of auspicious water."

children.text: evaṃ tu matvā hanumānmahātmā pratīkṣamāṇo manujendrapatnīm
children.translated_text: Thinking thus, great-souled <s>Hanumān</s>, waiting for the wife of the lord of men,

children.text: avekṣamāṇaśca dadarśa sarvaṃ supuṣpite parṇaghane nilīnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and looking about, saw everything while hidden in the tree dense with flowers and leaves.
Standing there, watching and searching for <s>Maithilī</s>,
and looking about, he surveyed all that ground.
It was adorned with santānaka creepers and trees,
filled with divine scents and juices, and decorated on every side.
He saw it resembling <s>Nandana</s>, filled with animals and birds,
crowded with mansions and palaces, resounding with the cries of many cuckoos,
adorned with tanks containing golden lotuses and lotuses,
provided with many seats and rugs, and furnished with many multi-storied houses,
with lovely flowers of every season and with fruit-bearing trees,
and, through the splendor of the flowering aśokas, bright as sunrise.
<s>Māruti</s>, standing there, beheld it as though blazing,
as birds repeatedly seemed to make its branches stripped of leaves,
with hundreds of variegated flower-clusters flying off.
It had aśokas, destroyers of sorrow, heaped with flowers from the root upward,
and, overburdened by the weight of blossoms, seeming to touch the earth.
With blooming karṇikāras and fully flowering kiṃśukas,

children.text: sa deśaḥ prabhayā teṣāṃ pradīpta iva sarvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: that place, through their radiance, seemed ablaze everywhere.
Puṃnāgas, saptaparṇas, campakas, and uddālakas too,
many of them with fully grown roots, shone there in full bloom.
Some aśokas there were like refined gold, some like tongues of fire,
and some like dark collyrium, in their thousands.
Like <s>Nandana</s>, a varied garden, and like the wondrous <s>Caitraratha</s>,

children.text: ativṛttam ivācintyaṃ divyaṃ ramyaṃ śriyā vṛtam ||
children.translated_text: it seemed to exceed all measure, inconceivable, divine, lovely, and endowed with splendor.
Like a second sky, filled with hosts of flower-lights,
variegated with hundreds of flower-jewels, it was like a fifth ocean.
The delightful garden was filled with flowers of every season, with honey-scented trees,
and with herds of deer and birds making many sounds.
It carried many fragrances, had a holy scent, and was pleasing to the mind,
like the lord of mountains rich in fragrance, a second <s>Gandhamādana</s>.
There in that aśoka grove, the foremost of monkeys
saw nearby a lofty caitya-palace,
standing in the middle with a thousand pillars, white as <s>Kailāsa</s>,
with stairways made of coral and a terrace of molten gold,

children.text: muṣṇantam iva cakṣūṃṣi dyotamānam iva śriyā
children.translated_text: as though stealing the eyes, as though shining with splendor,
pure, and because of its great height, as though scraping the sky.
Then he saw her, clothed in soiled garments and surrounded by <s>rākṣasī</s> women,
emaciated by fasting, wretched, and sighing again and again,
spotless like the crescent moon at the beginning of the bright fortnight.
Her beautiful radiance was dimly visible through her form,
like a flame of fire enveloped by a net of smoke.
She was wrapped in a single yellow, excellent garment, now worn and soiled,
mud-stained, without ornaments, like a lotus pond bereft of lotuses.
She was ashamed, scorched by sorrow, withered, and pitiable,
like <s>Rohiṇī</s> afflicted by the planet <s>Aṅgāraka</s>.
Her face was full of tears; she was wretched and thin also from fasting,
intent on grief and brooding, miserable, ever given over to sorrow,
not seeing her beloved one, seeing only the troop of <s>rākṣasī</s> women,
like a doe separated from her own herd and surrounded by a pack of hounds.
with a single braid, dark as a black serpent, reaching down to her hips,
fit for happiness, yet scorched by sorrow, unskilled in calamities.

children.text: tāṃ samīkṣya viśālākṣīm adhikaṃ malināṃ kṛśām
children.translated_text: Seeing her, wide-eyed, excessively soiled and thin,
he reasoned, on the basis of fitting causes, that she was <s>Sītā</s>.
When she was being carried away by that rākṣasa who could assume any form,

children.text: yathārūpā hi dṛṣṭā vai tathārūpeyam aṅganā ||
children.translated_text: just as she had then been seen in appearance, so was this woman in appearance.
Her face was like the full moon, her brows fair, her breasts beautifully rounded,

children.text: kurvantīṃ prabhayā devīṃ sarvā vitimirā diśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the goddess making all the quarters free from darkness with her radiance.
That dark-haired, bimba-lipped woman, slender-waisted and well-formed,
was <s>Sītā</s>, lotus-petal-eyed, like <s>Rati</s> herself to <s>Manmatha</s>.
Beloved of the whole world, like the radiance of the full moon,

children.text: bhūmau sutanum āsīnāṃ niyatām iva tāpasīm ||
children.translated_text: she sat on the ground, delicate-limbed, restrained like an ascetic woman.
Breathing many sighs, timid, like the mate of a lordly serpent,
she did not shine, wrapped in a great, spreading net of grief.
Like a flame of fire enveloped by a mass of smoke,

children.text: tāṃ smṛtīm iva saṃdigdhām ṛddhiṃ nipatitām iva ||
children.translated_text: like memory grown doubtful, like prosperity fallen down,

children.text: vihatām iva ca śraddhām āśāṃ pratihatām iva
children.translated_text: like faith obstructed, like hope frustrated,

children.text: sopasargāṃ yathā siddhiṃ buddhiṃ sakaluṣām iva ||
children.translated_text: like success beset by obstacles, like understanding made turbid,
like fame fallen through a false slander,
she was pained by <s>Rāma</s>'s confinement and emaciated by the rākṣasa's abduction.
Powerless, with eyes like a young doe's, looking this way and that,
with her dark face and eyelashes around eyes filled with waters of tears,
with an unhappy face, she sighed again and again.
Bearing dirt and mire, wretched, worthy of adornment yet unadorned,
she was like the light of the lord of stars veiled by black clouds.

children.text: tasya saṃdidihe buddhir muhuḥ sītāṃ nirīkṣya tu
children.translated_text: His mind wavered repeatedly as he looked upon <s>Sītā</s>,
like sacred knowledge grown slack through the improper recitation of the Vedas.
With difficulty <s>Hanumān</s> recognized the unadorned <s>Sītā</s>,
as one recognizes speech that, lacking refinement, has gone into another meaning.
Seeing that wide-eyed, blameless princess,
he reasoned, establishing it by causes, that she was <s>Sītā</s>.
Those ornaments on <s>Vaidehī</s>'s limbs which <s>Rāma</s> had then described,
he noticed as networks of ornaments shining on her body.

children.text: sukṛtau karṇaveṣṭau ca śvadaṃṣṭrau ca susaṃsthitau
children.translated_text: The finely made ear-ornaments and the well-set dog-tooth-shaped ornaments,
and the ornaments on her hands, variegated with jewels and coral,
darkened because they had long been worn, yet still retaining their shapes,
these very ones, I think, are those which <s>Rāma</s> described.
Those which were lost there I do not perceive,
but those of hers which were not lost are these, without doubt.

children.text: pītaṃ kanakapaṭṭābhaṃ srastaṃ tad vasanaṃ śubham
children.translated_text: That auspicious yellow garment, like a strip of gold, had slipped down,
and the upper cloth, caught on the mountain, was seen then by the vānaras.
And the chief ornaments were seen on the ground,
large and ringing, cast away by this very woman.
Because it has been worn for a long time, this garment is rather soiled,

children.text: tathā hi nūnaṃ tad varṇaṃ tathā śrīmad yathetarat ||
children.translated_text: yet surely it has that color and that beauty, just like the other one.
This golden-limbed woman is the beloved queen of <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: pranaṣṭāpi satī yasya manaso na praṇaśyati ||
children.translated_text: who, though lost, does not disappear from his mind.
This is she for whose sake <s>Rāma</s> is tormented in four ways:
by compassion, by kindness, by grief, and by love.
Out of compassion because a woman is lost, out of kindness because she sought refuge,

children.text: patnī naṣṭeti śokena priyeti madanena ca ||
children.translated_text: out of grief because his wife is lost, and out of love because she is dear.
As is the beauty of this goddess, and the grace of each limb and sub-limb,
and as is <s>Rāma</s>'s own beauty, this dark-eyed woman is worthy of him.
This goddess's mind is fixed on him, and his on her;

children.text: teneyaṃ sa ca dharmātmā muhūrtam api jīvati ||
children.translated_text: therefore she and that righteous one live even for a moment.

children.text: duṣkaraṃ kurute rāmo ya imāṃ mattakāśinīm
children.translated_text: Great-armed <s>Rāma</s> performs a hard deed, living even for a moment

children.text: sītāṃ vinā mahābāhur muhūrtam api jīvati ||
children.translated_text: without this <s>Sītā</s>, whose glance is like that of an intoxicated woman.

children.text: evaṃ sītāṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭaḥ pavanasaṃbhavaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, having then seen <s>Sītā</s>, the son of the Wind was delighted,

children.text: jagāma manasā rāmaṃ praśaśaṃsa ca taṃ prabhum ||
children.translated_text: went in his mind to <s>Rāma</s>, and praised that lord.

children.text: praśasya tu praśastavyāṃ sītāṃ tāṃ haripuṃgavaḥ
children.translated_text: After praising <s>Sītā</s>, worthy of praise, the foremost of monkeys
and also <s>Rāma</s>, delightful through his virtues, again became absorbed in thought.
After meditating for a moment, his eyes filled with confused tears,

children.text: sītām āśritya tejasvī hanumān vilalāpa ha ||
children.translated_text: the radiant <s>Hanumān</s> lamented, taking <s>Sītā</s> as his theme.
She is honored by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, who is trained in respect for elders, and dear to his revered elder;

children.text: yadi sītāpi duḥkhārtā kālo hi duratikramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: if even <s>Sītā</s> is afflicted by sorrow, time is indeed hard to overcome.
Knowing <s>Rāma</s>'s resolve and that of wise <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
the goddess is not excessively shaken, like the <s>Gaṅgā</s> at the coming of the clouds.
Equal in character, age, conduct, noble birth, and marks,
<s>Rāghava</s> deserves <s>Vaidehī</s>, and this dark-eyed woman deserves him.

children.text: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā navahemābhāṃ lokakāntām iva śriyam
children.translated_text: Seeing her, shining like fresh gold and beautiful as the world's own fortune,

children.text: jagāma manasā rāmaṃ vacanaṃ cedam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: he went in his mind to <s>Rāma</s> and spoke these words:

children.text: asyā hetor viśālākṣyā hato vālī mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: For the sake of this wide-eyed woman, mighty <s>Vālī</s> was slain,
and <s>Kabandha</s>, equal to <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in valor, was struck down.
And <s>Virādha</s>, a rākṣasa of terrible prowess, was slain in battle,
overpowered in the forest by <s>Rāma</s>, as <s>Śambara</s> was by great <s>Indra</s>.
Fourteen thousand rākṣasas of dreadful deeds
were killed in <s>Janasthāna</s> by arrows like flames of fire.
And <s>Khara</s> was slain in battle, and <s>Triśiras</s> was struck down,
and mighty, radiant <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> by <s>Rāma</s>, who knows the self.
And the sovereignty of the vānaras, difficult to obtain and guarded by <s>Vāli</s>,
<s>Sugrīva</s> obtained for her sake, honored by the world.
And the glorious ocean, lord of rivers and streams, was crossed by me

children.text: asyā hetor viśālākṣyāḥ purī ceyaṃ nirīkṣitā ||
children.translated_text: for the sake of this broad-eyed woman, and this city has been inspected.
If <s>Rāma</s> were to overturn the earth as far as the ocean's end

children.text: asyāḥ kṛte jagaccāpi yuktam ityeva me matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: for her sake, even that, I think, would be fitting.

children.text: rājyaṃ vā triṣu lokeṣu sītā vā janakātmajā
children.translated_text: The kingdom in the three worlds, or <s>Sītā</s>, daughter of <s>Janaka</s>:
the entire sovereignty of the three worlds would not equal even a fraction of <s>Sītā</s>.
This is that daughter of the great-souled <s>Maithila</s>, whose nature is righteous,
<s>Sītā</s>, daughter of king <s>Janaka</s>, firm in her vow toward her husband.
She rose up after breaking through the earth, in a field cut by the point of a plough,
covered with auspicious field-dust resembling lotus pollen.
She is the daughter-in-law of <s>Daśaratha</s>, of valiant and noble character,
who never turned back in battles, the famous king's eldest daughter-in-law.
This is that beloved wife of <s>Rāma</s>, knower of <s>dharma</s>, grateful, and self-aware,

children.text: iyaṃ sā dayitā bhāryā rākṣasīvaśam āgatā ||
children.translated_text: who has fallen under the power of rākṣasīs.
Abandoning all pleasures, compelled by the strength of love for her husband,
and disregarding hardships, she entered the lonely forest.
Content with fruit and roots, devoted to serving her husband,

children.text: yā parāṃ bhajate prītiṃ vane 'pi bhavane yathā ||
children.translated_text: she experienced supreme joy even in the forest, as if in a palace.
This same woman, with limbs the color of gold and always speaking with a gentle smile,
endures this torment, though she has no share in these misfortunes.

children.text: imāṃ tu śīlasampannāṃ draṣṭum icchati rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> longs to see this woman, endowed with good character,
crushed by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, like a thirsty man longing for a water-station.

children.text: asyā nūnaṃ punar lābhād rāghavaḥ prītim eṣyati
children.translated_text: Surely from recovering her, <s>Rāghava</s> will gain joy again,
like a king, deprived of his kingdom, on obtaining the earth once more.
Separated from enjoyments of desire and deprived of her kinsfolk,
she sustains her own body, longing for union with him.
She does not see these rākṣasīs, nor these trees rich in flowers and fruit;
with her heart fixed on one place, surely she sees only <s>Rāma</s> before her.

children.text: bhartā nāma paraṃ nāryā bhūṣaṇaṃ bhūṣaṇād api
children.translated_text: A husband is indeed a woman's highest ornament, beyond ornaments themselves;

children.text: eṣā hi rahitā tena śobhanārhā na śobhate ||
children.translated_text: for she, worthy of beauty, does not shine when deprived of him.

children.text: duṣkaraṃ kurute rāmo hīno yad anayā prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, the lord, performs a difficult feat in that, though separated from her,
he sustains his own body and does not sink down through sorrow.
Seeing her, with ends of hair dark-black and eyes like hundred-petalled lotuses,

children.text: sukhārhāṃ duḥkhitāṃ dṛṣṭvā mamāpi vyathitaṃ manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: worthy of happiness but now distressed, even my mind is pained.
She, patient as the earth and lotus-eyed, who was protected by <s>Rāghava</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: sā rākṣasībhir vikṛtekṣaṇābhiḥ saṃrakṣyate saṃprati vṛkṣamūle ||
children.translated_text: is now guarded at the foot of a tree by rākṣasīs with deformed eyes.
Like a lotus-bed struck by frost, its beauty destroyed, oppressed by a chain of calamities,

children.text: sahacararahiteva cakravākī janakasutā kṛpaṇāṃ daśāṃ prapannā ||
children.translated_text: like a cakravākī bird bereft of her mate, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s> has fallen into a pitiable state.

children.text: asyā hi puṣpāvanatāgraśākhāḥ śokaṃ dṛḍhaṃ vai janayantyaśokāḥ
children.translated_text: For her, these Aśoka trees, their top branches bent down with flowers, surely produce deep sorrow,
and with the frost departed the thousand-rayed sun has risen, its rays gentle.

children.text: ityevam arthaṃ kapir anvavekṣya sīteyam ityeva niviṣṭabuddhiḥ
children.translated_text: Considering the matter in just this way, the monkey fixed his mind on the thought, 'This is <s>Sītā</s>,'

children.text: saṃśritya tasminniṣasāda vṛkṣe balī harīṇām ṛṣabhastarasvī ||
children.translated_text: and, taking refuge in that tree, the strong and swift bull among vānaras sat down.
Then the moon, itself stainless, resembling a cluster of white lotuses,
moved through the clear sky like a swan through blue water.

children.text: sācivyam iva kurvan sa prabhayā nirmalaprabhaḥ
children.translated_text: As if acting as an adviser, that moon of spotless radiance,
with its cool rays, served the son of <s>Pavana</s> by its light.
Then he saw <s>Sītā</s>, her face resembling the full moon,

children.text: śokabhārair iva nyastāṃ bhārair nāvam ivāmbhasi ||
children.translated_text: as if weighed down by masses of grief, like a boat by loads in water.
<s>Hanumān</s>, son of <s>Māruta</s>, wishing to see <s>Vaidehī</s>,
then saw nearby rākṣasīs of terrible appearance.
One-eyed, one-eared, and others with ears as coverings,
earless, spike-eared, and with nostrils rising up on their heads;
with oversized bodies and heads, and with thin, long necks,
with ruined hair, hairless, and wearing hair as a blanket;
with hanging ears and foreheads, and with hanging bellies and breasts,
with hanging lips, lips at the chin, hanging mouths, and hanging knees;

children.text: hrasvāṃ dīrghāṃ ca kubjāṃ ca vikaṭāṃ vāmanāṃ tathā
children.translated_text: short, tall, hunchbacked, misshapen, and dwarf,
grim-faced, with twisted garments, tawny-eyed, and deformed-faced;
deformed, tawny, black, wrathful, fond of quarrels,
bearing great iron spears, mallets, and hammers;
with faces of boars, deer, tigers, buffaloes, goats, and jackals,
and others with feet of elephants, camels, and horses, and with heads sunk low;
with one hand and one foot, with donkey ears and horse ears,
cow-eared, elephant-eared, and others with lion-like ears;
noseless, over-nosed, with crooked noses, and without noses,
with noses like elephants, and with nostrils rising upon the forehead;
with elephant feet, huge feet, cow feet, and hair growing on their feet,
with excessively large heads and necks, and excessively large breasts and bellies;
with excessively large mouths and eyes, and with long tongues and nails,
goat-faced, elephant-faced, cow-faced, and pig-faced;
with mouths of horses, camels, and donkeys, rākṣasīs of terrible appearance,
with spears and clubs in hand, wrathful and fond of quarrels;
grim, smoke-haired rākṣasīs with deformed faces,
drinking liquor constantly and always fond of meat and wine.
with limbs smeared with flesh and blood, feeding on flesh and blood,
the best of monkeys saw those whose appearance made the hair stand on end.
They were sitting around a tree with great boughs, surrounding it,
and beneath it he saw that goddess, the blameless princess.
The illustrious <s>Hanumān</s> recognized the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,
dimmed in radiance, scorched by grief, her hair matted with dirt.

children.text: kṣīṇapuṇyāṃ cyutāṃ bhūmau tārāṃ nipatitām iva
children.translated_text: She was like a star whose merit had waned, fallen down upon the earth,
rich in the reputation of chastity, brought low by not seeing her husband.
She was deprived of excellent ornaments, adorned only by devotion to her husband,
confined by the lord of the rākṣasas and separated from her kinsmen.
She was like a female elephant parted from her herd and held fast by a lion,
like a crescent moon at the end of the rainy season covered by autumn clouds.
Her form was afflicted; from being untouched, she was like a lute out of tune.

children.text: sītāṃ bhartṛhite yuktām ayuktāṃ rakṣasāṃ vaśe ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s> was devoted to her husband's welfare, yet ill-suited to the power of the rākṣasas.
In the middle of the Aśoka grove she was plunged into an ocean of sorrow,

children.text: tābhiḥ parivṛtāṃ tatra sagrahām iva rohiṇīm ||
children.translated_text: surrounded there by those women like <s>Rohiṇī</s> beset by planets.

children.text: dadarśa hanumān devīṃ latām akusumām iva
children.translated_text: <s>Hanumān</s> saw the goddess like a creeper without flowers.

children.text: sā malena ca digdhāṅgī vapuṣā cāpyalaṃkṛtā ||
children.translated_text: Her body was smeared with dirt, yet she was still adorned by her own beauty.

children.text: mṛṇālī paṅkadigdheva vibhāti ca na bhāti ca
children.translated_text: Like a lotus fiber smeared with mud, she both shone and did not shine.
In a soiled and worn-out garment,
the monkey <s>Hanumān</s> saw the doe-eyed lady covered.
He saw that goddess with a piteous face, yet not abject because of her husband's splendor,
dark-eyed <s>Sītā</s>, protected by her own virtue.
Seeing <s>Sītā</s>, whose eyes were like those of a fawn,
frightened like a young doe and looking about on every side,
as though burning the leaf-bearing trees with her sighs,
like a mass of griefs, like a wave of suffering risen up,
emaciated, with finely proportioned limbs, beautiful even without ornaments,

children.text: praharṣam atulaṃ lebhe mārutiḥ prekṣya maithilīm
children.translated_text: <s>Māruti</s> gained incomparable joy on seeing <s>Maithilī</s>.

children.text: harṣajāni ca so 'śrūṇi tāṃ dṛṣṭvā madirekṣaṇām ||
children.translated_text: Seeing that wine-eyed woman, he shed tears born of joy.
<s>Hanumān</s> let them fall there and bowed to <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: namaskṛtvā ca rāmāya lakṣmaṇāya ca vīryavān ||
children.translated_text: Having bowed to <s>Rāma</s> and to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the heroic one,
<s>Hanumān</s>, delighted by the sight of <s>Sītā</s>, remained hidden.
As he was looking over the forest with its flowering trees,
and searching for <s>Vaidehī</s>, only a little of the night remained.
Of those learned in the Veda with its six auxiliaries, sacrificers of the foremost rites,
he heard the brahman-sounds of the Brahma-rākṣasas in the latter part of the night.
Then, with auspicious instruments and sounds pleasing to the ear,
the great-armed, mighty ten-necked one was awakened.
Having awakened at the proper time, the powerful lord of the rākṣasas,
with his garlands and garments slipped loose, thought of <s>Vaidehī</s>.
Strongly fixed on her and swollen with passion, overcome by <s>Madana</s>,

children.text: na sa taṃ rākṣasaḥ kāmaṃ śaśākātmani gūhitum ||
children.translated_text: that rākṣasa could not hide that desire within himself.
Adorned with every ornament and bearing unsurpassed splendor,
he approached that grove, frequented by many kinds of trees and supplied with every flower and fruit,
encircled by lotus ponds and adorned with many kinds of blossoms,
varied and most wonderful with birds ever in rutting intoxication,
and surrounded by many kinds of marvelous deer pleasing to the eye.
Gazing at avenues with gateways of jewel and gold,
crowded with herds of many deer and strewn with fallen fruits,
he entered that very Aśoka grove, thick with continuous trees.
About a hundred women followed him as he went,
as women of gods and gandharvas might follow <s>Mahendra</s>, so they followed <s>Paulastya</s>.
Some women there took up golden lamps,
others had yak-tail fans in hand, and others held palm-leaf fans.

children.text: kāñcanair api bhṛṅgārair jahruḥ salilam agrataḥ
children.translated_text: With golden pitchers they carried water before him,
and others, taking round-tipped swords, went behind.

children.text: kācid ratnamayīṃ pātrīṃ pūrṇāṃ pānasya bhāminī
children.translated_text: One beautiful woman took a jeweled vessel full of drink,
dexterously, then, in her right hand.
Another took a royal parasol like a swan, shining like the full moon,
with a golden staff, and followed behind him.
The finest women of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, their eyes overcome by sleep and intoxication,

children.text: anujagmuḥ patiṃ vīraṃ ghanaṃ vidyullatā iva ||
children.translated_text: followed their heroic lord like streaks of lightning following a cloud.

children.text: tataḥ kāñcīninādaṃ ca nūpurāṇāṃ ca niḥsvanam
children.translated_text: Then the son of <s>Māruta</s>, the monkey, heard the sound of girdles
and the ringing of the anklets of those supreme women.
The monkey <s>Hanumān</s> saw him, incomparable in deeds and of inconceivable strength and manliness,
as he reached the entrance.
He was illuminated on every side by many lamps,
anointed with fragrant oil and carried before him.
He was possessed by lust, arrogance, and intoxication, with crooked, coppery, elongated eyes,
like <s>Kandarpa</s> himself before one's eyes, his bow cast aside.
His excellent garment, white like the foam of churned nectar and free from dust,
had slipped loose and caught on his armlet as he drew it along playfully.
Hidden in a leafy bough, densely covered with leaves and flowers,
he began to observe him as he came near.
Then, watching, the elephant among monkeys saw
the choice women of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, endowed with beauty and youth.
The greatly renowned king was surrounded by those lovely women.
He entered that pleasure-garden, resounding with deer and birds.
Intoxicated, adorned with varied ornaments, with pointed ears, and very strong,

children.text: tena viśravasaḥ putraḥ sa dṛṣṭo rākṣasādhipaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there that son of <s>Viśravas</s>, the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, was seen by him.
He was surrounded by supreme women, like the moon by stars.
The great monkey, mighty in splendor, saw that powerful one.
Thinking, "This is <s>Rāvaṇa</s> of mighty arms," the monkey
of great splendor, <s>Hanumān</s>, son of the wind, sprang down.
Yet, though he himself was of fierce splendor, shaken by that one's radiance,
<s>Hanumān</s> clung within the hidden space among the leaves and became concealed.
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, wishing to see that woman whose hair-ends were black, with beautiful hips and close-set breasts,
and whose side-glances were dark, turned toward her.

children.text: tasminn eva tataḥ kāle rājaputrī tvaninditā
children.translated_text: Then at that very time the blameless princess
saw the lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, endowed with beauty and youth and adorned with the finest ornaments.
As soon as <s>Vaidehī</s> saw him,
the lovely-waisted woman trembled like a plantain tree in the wind.

children.text: ūrubhyām udaraṃ chādya bāhubhyāṃ ca payodharau
children.translated_text: Covering her belly with her thighs and her breasts with her arms,
the wide-eyed, beautiful woman sat there weeping.
But <s>Daśagrīva</s> saw <s>Vaidehī</s>, guarded by groups of <s>rākṣasī</s> women,

children.text: dadarśa dīnāṃ duḥkhārtaṃ nāvaṃ sannām ivārṇave ||
children.translated_text: wretched and afflicted with sorrow, like a ship foundering in the ocean.
She sat on the bare ground, firm in her vows,

children.text: chinnāṃ prapatitāṃ bhūmau śākhām iva vanaspateḥ
children.translated_text: like a branch cut off from a tree and fallen to the earth,
her limbs smeared with dirt as ornament, though she deserved ornaments and had none.
She seemed to be going near the lion among kings, <s>Rāma</s>, whose self was known,
by chariots of thought yoked with horses of resolve.
Drying up, weeping, alone, wholly given over to brooding and grief,
not seeing an end to sorrow, <s>Rāmā</s> remained devoted to <s>Rāma</s>.
She writhed as though seized, like the wife of a great serpent,
and seemed smoked over by a planet, like <s>Rohiṇī</s> by a comet.
Born in a family of good conduct, upright custom, and <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),

children.text: punaḥ saṃskāram āpannāṃ jātām iva ca duṣkule ||
children.translated_text: she seemed, as though after a new transformation, to have been born in a bad family.

children.text: sannām iva mahākīrtiṃ śraddhām iva vimānitām
children.translated_text: She was like great fame bowed down, like faith dishonored,

children.text: prajñām iva parikṣīṇām āśāṃ pratihatām iva ||
children.translated_text: like wisdom exhausted, like hope beaten back.

children.text: āyatīm iva vidhvastām ājñāṃ pratihatām iva
children.translated_text: She was like future fortune destroyed, like a command obstructed,

children.text: dīptām iva diśaṃ kāle pūjām apahṛtām iva ||
children.translated_text: like a blazing direction at the destined time, like worship carried away.

children.text: padminīm iva vidhvastāṃ hataśūrāṃ camūm iva
children.translated_text: She was like a lotus-pond ravaged, like an army whose heroes had been slain,
like radiance ruined by heat, like a river diminished.

children.text: vedīm iva parāmṛṣṭāṃ śāntām agniśikhām iva
children.translated_text: She was like an altar defiled, like a flame of fire grown calm,
like a full-moon night whose moon-disc has been seized by <s>Rāhu</s>.
She was like a lotus-pond with leaves and lotuses torn up and birds frightened away,
confused after being swept by an elephant's trunk.
Afflicted by sorrow for her husband and withered, she was like a river drained dry,

children.text: parayā mṛjayā hīnāṃ kṛṣṇapakṣe niśām iva ||
children.translated_text: like a night in the dark fortnight deprived of its highest cleansing brightness.
Delicate, with well-born limbs, fit for a jewel-filled inner chamber,
she seemed like a lotus-fiber, freshly pulled up, being scorched by heat.
Held fast, bound to a post, and separated from her herd-leader,
sighing and deeply afflicted with sorrow, she was like the mate of a lordly elephant.
She shone without effort by a single long braid,
like the earth with a dark line of forest when the clouds have passed away.

children.text: upavāsena śokena dhyānena ca bhayena ca
children.translated_text: Through fasting, grief, brooding, and fear,
she was wasted, thin, wretched, eating little, and rich only in austerity.
Sorrow-stricken and begging with joined palms, like a goddess,
she was contemplating in her heart the defeat of <s>Daśagrīva</s> by the chief of the <s>Raghus</s>.
As she looked on, weeping, blameless, with lovely-lashed, coppery, wide, white eyes,

children.text: anuvratāṃ rāmam atīva maithilīṃ pralobhayāmāsa vadhāya rāvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, to his own destruction, tried to entice <s>Maithilī</s>, who was utterly devoted to <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: sa tāṃ parivṛtāṃ dīnāṃ nirānandāṃ tapasvinīm
children.translated_text: Seeing her surrounded, wretched, joyless, and ascetic,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> addressed her with expressive gestures and sweet words.
"Seeing me, you hide your breasts and belly with your elephant-trunk-like thighs,
and out of fear you wish to make yourself as if invisible.

children.text: kāmaye tvāṃ viśālākṣi bahu manyasva māṃ priye
children.translated_text: I desire you, wide-eyed one. Esteem me highly, beloved,
perfect in the qualities of every limb and enchanting to all the worlds.

children.text: neha kecin manuṣyā vā rākṣasāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: There are no humans here, nor <s>rākṣasas</s> who change form at will.

children.text: vyapasarpatu te sīte bhayaṃ mattaḥ samutthitam ||
children.translated_text: Let the fear arisen from me depart from you, <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: svadharme rakṣasāṃ bhīru sarvathaiṣa na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Timid one, this is entirely the proper nature of <s>rākṣasas</s>; there is no doubt:

children.text: gamanaṃ vā parastrīṇāṃ haraṇaṃ sampramathya vā ||
children.translated_text: approaching other men's wives, or carrying them off after overpowering them.

children.text: evaṃ caitad akāmāṃ ca na tvāṃ sprakṣyāmi maithili
children.translated_text: Yet even so, <s>Maithilī</s>, unwilling as you are, I shall not touch you.

children.text: kāmaṃ kāmaḥ śarīre me yathākāmaṃ pravartatām ||
children.translated_text: Let desire in my body proceed as it wishes.

children.text: devi neha bhayaṃ kāryaṃ mayi viśvasihi priye
children.translated_text: Lady, no fear should be felt here. Trust me, beloved,

children.text: praṇayasva ca tattvena maivaṃ bhūḥ śokalālasā ||
children.translated_text: and accept my affection truly; do not remain so attached to sorrow.
A single braid, a bed on the ground, brooding, soiled clothing,
and fasting in an improper place: these are not fitting for you.
Variegated garlands, sandal-pastes and aloes,
various garments and heavenly ornaments,

children.text: mahārhāṇi ca pānāni yānāni śayanāni ca
children.translated_text: costly drinks, vehicles, and couches,

children.text: gītaṃ nṛttaṃ ca vādyaṃ ca labha māṃ prāpya maithili ||
children.translated_text: song, dance, and music: obtain them by accepting me, <s>Maithilī</s>.

children.text: strīratnam asi maivaṃ bhūḥ kuru gātreṣu bhūṣaṇam
children.translated_text: You are a jewel among women; do not be like this. Put ornaments on your limbs.

children.text: māṃ prāpya tu kathaṃ hi syāstvam anarhā suvigrahe ||
children.translated_text: Having obtained me, how could you, lovely-bodied one, remain in a state unworthy of you?
This youth of yours, beautifully born, is passing away.

children.text: yad atītaṃ punar naiti srotaḥ śīghram apām iva ||
children.translated_text: What has passed does not return, like the swift current of waters."

children.text: tvāṃ kṛtvoparato manye rūpakartā sa viśvakṛt
children.translated_text: Having made you, I think, the fashioner of forms, the maker of the universe, ceased from his work;

children.text: na hi rūpopamā tvanyā tavāsti śubhadarśane ||
children.translated_text: for there is no other beauty comparable to your form, O auspicious-looking one.
Having attained you, O <s>Vaidehī</s>, endowed with beauty and youth,

children.text: kaḥ pumān ativarteta sākṣād api pitāmahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: what man could pass you by, even <s>Pitāmaha</s> himself in person?

children.text: yad yat paśyāmi te gātraṃ śītāṃśusadṛśānane
children.translated_text: Whatever limb of yours I see, O moon-faced one,
on each and every one, O broad-hipped woman, my eye is fixed.

children.text: bhava maithili bhāryā me moham enaṃ visarjaya
children.translated_text: Become my wife, O <s>Maithilī</s>; cast off this delusion.
Become my chief queen among my many excellent women.
Whatever jewels I have seized and brought from the worlds,

children.text: tāni te bhīru sarvāṇi rājyaṃ caitad ahaṃ ca te ||
children.translated_text: all those are yours, timid one, and this kingdom, and I myself am yours.
Having conquered the whole earth, garlanded with many cities,
I will give it to <s>Janaka</s> for your sake, O playful one.

children.text: neha paśyāmi loke 'nyaṃ yo me pratibalo bhavet
children.translated_text: I do not see here in the world any other who could be a match for me.

children.text: paśya me sumahad vīryam apratidvandvam āhave ||
children.translated_text: Behold my very great valor, without rival in battle.
Many times in combat the devas and asuras, their standards crushed, have been broken by me,
unable to stand in the opposing ranks before me.

children.text: iccha māṃ kriyatām adya pratikarma tavottamam
children.translated_text: Desire me; let the finest adornment be done for you today.
Let ornaments, bright with radiance, hang upon your limbs,

children.text: sādhu paśyāmi te rūpaṃ saṃyuktaṃ pratikarmaṇā ||
children.translated_text: so that I may duly see your form joined with adornment.
Adorned with embellishment and with graciousness, O fair-faced one,

children.text: bhuṅkṣva bhogān yathākāmaṃ piba bhīru ramasva ca
children.translated_text: enjoy pleasures as you wish; drink, timid one, and take your delight.

children.text: yatheṣṭaṃ ca prayaccha tvaṃ pṛthivīṃ vā dhanāni ca ||
children.translated_text: Give away as you like, whether the earth or wealth.

children.text: lalasva mayi viśrabdhā dhṛṣṭam ājñāpayasva ca
children.translated_text: Long for me with confidence, and command me boldly.
By my power, while you take your pleasure, let your kinsmen take theirs.

children.text: ṛddhiṃ mamānupaśya tvaṃ śriyaṃ bhadre yaśaśca me
children.translated_text: Look upon my prosperity, my splendor, O blessed lady, and my fame.
What will you do with <s>Rāma</s>, fortunate one, clad in bark-garments?
<s>Rāma</s>, whose victory is cast away, whose splendor is gone, roams the forest,

children.text: vratī sthaṇḍilaśāyī ca śaṅke jīvati vā na vā ||
children.translated_text: observing vows and sleeping on bare ground; I doubt whether he is alive or not.

children.text: na hi vaidehi rāmastvāṃ draṣṭuṃ vāpyupalapsyate
children.translated_text: For <s>Rāma</s> will not even obtain the chance to see you, O <s>Vaidehī</s>,

children.text: puro balākair asitair meghair jyotsnām ivāvṛtām ||
children.translated_text: like moonlight covered by dark clouds with cranes before them.

children.text: na cāpi mama hastāt tvāṃ prāptum arhati rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Nor can <s>Rāghava</s> recover you from my hand,
as <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> could not recover fame that had gone into <s>Indra</s>'s hand.
O lovely-smiling, lovely-toothed, lovely-eyed, playful one,

children.text: mano harasi me bhīru suparṇaḥ pannagaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: you steal my mind, timid one, as <s>Suparṇa</s> steals a serpent.
Having seen you, slender, wearing distressed silk garments and even unadorned,

children.text: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā sveṣu dāreṣu ratiṃ nopalabhāmyaham ||
children.translated_text: I find no delight among my own wives.
The women dwelling in my inner palace, endowed with every virtue,

children.text: yāvantyo mama sarvāsām aiśvaryaṃ kuru jānaki ||
children.translated_text: as many as there are, exercise sovereignty over all of them, O <s>Jānakī</s>.
For among my women, O dark-haired one, the foremost women of the three worlds
will attend upon you, as apsarases attend upon <s>Śrī</s>.

children.text: yāni vaiśravaṇe subhru ratnāni ca dhanāni ca
children.translated_text: The jewels and wealth that belong to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, O fine-browed one,

children.text: tāni lokāṃśca suśroṇi māṃ ca bhuṅkṣva yathāsukham ||
children.translated_text: enjoy those, and the worlds, and me, O fair-hipped one, as happily as you wish.

children.text: na rāmastapasā devi na balena na vikramaiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> is not equal to me, goddess, in austerity, nor in strength, nor in valor,

children.text: na dhanena mayā tulyastejasā yaśasāpi vā ||
children.translated_text: nor in wealth, nor in majesty, nor even in fame.

children.text: piba vihara ramasva bhuṅkṣva bhogān dhananicayaṃ pradiśāmi medinīṃ ca
children.translated_text: Drink, wander, take your pleasure, enjoy pleasures; I assign you heaps of wealth and the earth.

children.text: mayi lala lalane yathāsukhaṃ tvaṃ tvayi ca sametya lalantu bāndhavāste ||
children.translated_text: Long for me, O lovely woman, as happily as you wish, and, having come together with you, let your kinsmen delight.
In groves along the seashore, covered with networks of flowering trees and filled with bees,

children.text: kanakavimalahārabhūṣitāṅgī vihara mayā saha bhīru kānanāni ||
children.translated_text: your limbs adorned with spotless golden garlands, roam with me, timid one.

children.text: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sītā raudrasya rakṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing those words of that dreadful <s>rākṣasa</s>,

children.text: ārtā dīnasvarā dīnaṃ pratyuvāca śanair vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s>, afflicted, with a pitiable voice, slowly replied with pitiable words.
<s>Sītā</s>, afflicted with grief, weeping, trembling, the ascetic woman,
the lovely-hipped devoted wife, thinking only of her husband.
Putting a blade of grass between them, the pure-smiling one replied:

children.text: nivartaya mano mattaḥ svajane kriyatāṃ manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Turn your mind away from me; let your mind be placed upon your own people.

children.text: na māṃ prārthayituṃ yuktastvaṃ siddhim iva pāpakṛt
children.translated_text: It is not fitting for you to seek me, as an evildoer seeks spiritual success.

children.text: akāryaṃ na mayā kāryam ekapatnyā vigarhitam
children.translated_text: What is wrong, condemned for a woman devoted to one husband, must not be done by me,

children.text: kulaṃ samprāptayā puṇyaṃ kule mahati jātayā ||
children.translated_text: who have entered a virtuous family and was born in a great family.

children.text: evam uktvā tu vaidehī rāvaṇaṃ taṃ yaśasvinī
children.translated_text: Having thus addressed that <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the illustrious <s>Vaidehī</s>

children.text: rākṣasaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā bhūyo vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: turned her back on the <s>rākṣasa</s> and spoke these further words:

children.text: nāham aupayikī bhāryā parabhāryā satī tava
children.translated_text: I, being another's wife and faithful, am not a suitable wife for you.

children.text: sādhu dharmam avekṣasva sādhu sādhuvrataṃ cara ||
children.translated_text: Look properly to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order); properly practice a good vow.

children.text: yathā tava tathānyeṣāṃ rakṣyā dārā niśācara
children.translated_text: As your wives are to you, so the wives of others are to be protected, night-roamer.

children.text: ātmānam upamāṃ kṛtvā sveṣu dāreṣu ramyatām ||
children.translated_text: Taking yourself as the comparison, take delight in your own wives.
Other men's wives lead to ruin a man unsatisfied among his own wives,
fickle, with wavering senses and a deceitful mind.

children.text: iha santo na vā santi sato vā nānuvartase
children.translated_text: Either good men do not exist here, or, though they exist, you do not follow

children.text: vaco mithyā praṇītātmā pathyam uktaṃ vicakṣaṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wholesome counsel spoken by the wise, for your self is wrongly directed.
On attaining a king who has not mastered himself and delights in misconduct,
prosperous kingdoms and cities perish.
So too this <s>Laṅkā</s>, thronged with floods of jewels, having come under you,
will soon perish through the fault of you alone.
When <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lacking foresight, is being destroyed by his own deeds,
beings will rejoice at the destruction of the evildoer.

children.text: evaṃ tvāṃ pāpakarmāṇaṃ vakṣyanti nikṛtā janāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, when you, a doer of evil, are ruined, people you have wronged will say of you,

children.text: diṣṭyaitad vyasanaṃ prāpto raudra ityeva harṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Fortunately this violent one has fallen into this calamity," and they will rejoice.

children.text: śakyā lobhayituṃ nāham aiśvaryeṇa dhanena vā
children.translated_text: I cannot be tempted by sovereignty or by wealth;
I am inseparable from <s>Rāghava</s>, as radiance is from the sun.
Having laid down the honored arm of that lord of the world,
how could I ever lay down the arm of anyone else?
I am the proper wife of that king of the earth alone,
like knowledge suited to a twice-born man who has bathed after his vow and knows himself.

children.text: sādhu rāvaṇa rāmeṇa māṃ samānaya duḥkhitām
children.translated_text: Do well, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>: bring me, miserable as I am, together with <s>Rāma</s>,
as one would bring a she-elephant dwelling in the forest together with the lord of elephants.

children.text: mitram aupayikaṃ kartuṃ rāmaḥ sthānaṃ parīpsatā
children.translated_text: If you seek a secure place and do not wish for a terrible death,
you should make that <s>Rāma</s>, bull among men, a fitting friend.
One might avoid a hurled thunderbolt; one might long avoid Death;

children.text: tvadvidhaṃ na tu saṃkruddho lokanāthaḥ sa rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but a man like you cannot avoid that angered <s>Rāghava</s>, lord of the world.

children.text: rāmasya dhanuṣaḥ śabdaṃ śroṣyasi tvaṃ mahāsvanam
children.translated_text: You will hear the great sound of <s>Rāma</s>'s bow,
like the crash of a thunderbolt discharged by <s>Śatakratu</s>.
Here, very soon, arrows like serpents with blazing mouths and fine joints,
marked with the signs of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, will fall.
As they strike down the rākṣasas all around this city,
the feathered arrows, clad in heron plumes, will make it impossible to move about.
That great <s>Rāma</s>, a mighty <s>Garuḍa</s>,
will swiftly tear away the great serpent-like lords of the rākṣasas, as <s>Vainateya</s> tears away serpents.

children.text: apaneṣyati māṃ bhartā tvattaḥ śīghram ariṃdamaḥ
children.translated_text: My husband, the subduer of enemies, will quickly take me away from you,

children.text: asurebhyaḥ śriyaṃ dīptāṃ viṣṇustribhir iva kramaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: as <s>Viṣṇu</s> took blazing fortune from the asuras with his three strides.
When the place of slaughter, <s>Janasthāna</s>, had been emptied and the army of rākṣasas destroyed,

children.text: aśaktena tvayā rakṣaḥ kṛtam etad asādhu vai ||
children.translated_text: this wicked deed was done by you, powerless rākṣasa.

children.text: āśramaṃ tu tayoḥ śūnyaṃ praviśya narasiṃhayoḥ
children.translated_text: Entering the empty hermitage of those two lions among men,
when the two brothers had gone within range of their quarry, you carried me off, base man.
For after merely smelling the scent of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: śakyaṃ saṃdarśane sthātuṃ śunā śārdūlayor iva ||
children.translated_text: you could not stand in their sight, like a dog before two tigers.

children.text: tasya te vigrahe tābhyāṃ yugagrahaṇam asthiram
children.translated_text: Your conflict with those two is as unstable as the seizing of a yoke;
it is like the restraint of one arm of <s>Vṛtra</s> by the arms of <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: kṣipraṃ tava sa nātho me rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha
children.translated_text: Quickly, that <s>Rāma</s>, my lord, together with <s>Saumitri</s>,

children.text: toyam alpam ivādityaḥ prāṇān ādāsyate śaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: will take away your life with arrows, as the sun takes up a little water.

children.text: giriṃ kuberasya gato 'thavālayaṃ sabhāṃ gato vā varuṇasya rājñaḥ
children.translated_text: Whether you go to <s>Kubera</s>'s mountain, or to the abode, or to the court of king <s>Varuṇa</s>,

children.text: asaṃśayaṃ dāśarather na mokṣyase mahādrumaḥ kālahato 'śaner iva ||
children.translated_text: without doubt you will not escape <s>Dāśarathi</s>, like a great tree struck down by Time, from a thunderbolt.
Hearing <s>Sītā</s>'s harsh words, the lord of the rākṣasas
then answered lovely <s>Sītā</s> with words displeasing to her.

children.text: yathā yathā sāntvayitā vaśyaḥ strīṇāṃ tathā tathā
children.translated_text: The more a man consoles women, the more he becomes subject to them;

children.text: yathā yathā priyaṃ vaktā paribhūtastathā tathā ||
children.translated_text: the more he speaks pleasantly, the more he is despised.

children.text: saṃniyacchati me krodhaṃ tvayi kāmaḥ samutthitaḥ
children.translated_text: The passion that has arisen in me for you restrains my anger,

children.text: dravato mārgam āsādya hayān iva susārathiḥ ||
children.translated_text: like a skilled charioteer restraining horses when they have come upon the road as they run.

children.text: vāmaḥ kāmo manuṣyāṇāṃ yasmin kila nibadhyate
children.translated_text: Perverse desire, so they say, when it becomes fixed on someone among human beings,
then compassion and affection arise toward that person.
For this reason, fair-faced woman, I do not kill you,
though you deserve death and contempt, delighting in that false ascetic.

children.text: paruṣāṇi hi vākyāni yāni yāni bravīṣi mām
children.translated_text: For whatever harsh words you speak to me,

children.text: teṣu teṣu vadho yuktastava maithili dāruṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for each of them, <s>Maithilī</s>, a dreadful death would be fitting for you.

children.text: evam uktvā tu vaidehīṃ rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to <s>Vaidehī</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas,
filled with anger and agitation, spoke further to <s>Sītā</s>:

children.text: dvau māsau rakṣitavyau me yo 'vadhiste mayā kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Two months are to be guarded for me; that is the limit I have set for you.

children.text: tataḥ śayanam āroha mama tvaṃ varavarṇini ||
children.translated_text: After that, beautiful woman, you must mount my bed.

children.text: dvābhyām ūrdhvaṃ tu māsābhyāṃ bhartāraṃ mām anicchatīm
children.translated_text: But after two months, if you still do not desire me as your husband,
they will prepare you in my kitchen for my morning meal.
Seeing <s>Jānakī</s> being threatened by the lord of the rākṣasas,
those broad-eyed maidens of the gods and gandharvas were distressed.
Some, with gestures of their lips, and others with their eyes and faces,
comforted <s>Sītā</s>, who had been threatened by that rākṣasa.
Comforted by them, <s>Sītā</s> addressed <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas,
with words beneficial to herself, proud in their upright courage.

children.text: nūnaṃ na te janaḥ kaścid asti niḥśreyase sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Surely there is no one among your people who is established in what is best for you,

children.text: nivārayati yo na tvāṃ karmaṇo 'smād vigarhitāt ||
children.translated_text: someone who would restrain you from this blameworthy act.

children.text: māṃ hi dharmātmanaḥ patnīṃ śacīm iva śacīpateḥ
children.translated_text: For who in the three worlds, apart from you, would even in thought desire me,
the wife of righteous <s>Rāma</s>, like <s>Śacī</s>, wife of the lord of <s>Śacī</s>?
Lowest of rākṣasas, since you have uttered this sinful speech about the wife of immeasurably splendid <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: uktavān asi yat pāpaṃ kva gatastasya mokṣyase ||
children.translated_text: where will you go and escape from him?

children.text: yathā dṛptaśca mātaṅgaḥ śaśaśca sahitau vane
children.translated_text: As a proud elephant and a hare might be together in the forest,

children.text: tathā dviradavad rāmastvaṃ nīca śaśavat smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so <s>Rāma</s> is known as like the elephant, while you, base man, are like the hare.

children.text: sa tvam ikṣvākunāthaṃ vai kṣipann iha na lajjase
children.translated_text: And you, reviling the lord of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s> here, are not ashamed,

children.text: cakṣuṣo viṣayaṃ tasya na tāvad upagacchasi ||
children.translated_text: though you have not yet come within the range of his eyes.

children.text: ime te nayane krūre virūpe kṛṣṇapiṅgale
children.translated_text: These cruel, misshapen eyes of yours, black and tawny,
why have they not fallen to the ground as you gaze upon me, ignoble man?

children.text: tasya dharmātmanaḥ patnīṃ snuṣāṃ daśarathasya ca
children.translated_text: As you speak to me, the wife of that righteous one and the daughter-in-law of <s>Daśaratha</s>,

children.text: kathaṃ vyāharato māṃ te na jihvā pāpa śīryate ||
children.translated_text: why does your tongue not split apart, sinful man?
Only because I have no command from <s>Rāma</s>, and because I preserve my ascetic discipline,

children.text: na tvāṃ kurmi daśagrīva bhasma bhasmārhatejasā ||
children.translated_text: I do not reduce you to ashes, <s>Daśagrīva</s>, with my splendor that could burn one fit to be ash.

children.text: nāpahartum ahaṃ śakyā tasya rāmasya dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: I cannot be carried away from that wise <s>Rāma</s>
Your fate has been ordained for the sake of your death; there is no doubt about this.
Though you are heroic, the brother of <s>Dhanada</s>, and accompanied by assembled forces,

children.text: apohya rāmaṃ kasmāddhi dāracauryaṃ tvayā kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: why did you commit the theft of another's wife, avoiding <s>Rāma</s>?
Hearing <s>Sītā</s>'s words, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas,
opened his cruel eyes wide and looked upon <s>Jānakī</s>.
Dark like a blue rain cloud, with mighty arms, heads, and neck,
moving with the gait and spirit of a lion, splendid, with blazing tongue and fierce eyes,
tall, with the tip of his crown trembling, adorned with variegated garlands and unguents,
wearing red garlands and garments, and ornamented with heated gold armlets,
well covered by a great dark girdle-string at his hips,
like <s>Mandara</s> bound round by the serpent when the nectar was produced,
adorned with two earrings the color of the young sun,
like a mountain adorned by two aśoka trees with red shoots and flowers,
gazing at <s>Vaidehī</s> with eyes reddened by anger,

children.text: uvāca rāvaṇaḥ sītāṃ bhujaṃga iva niḥśvasan ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s> spoke to <s>Sītā</s>, hissing like a serpent:
"O devoted woman, possessed by improper conduct and devoid of sense,

children.text: nāśayāmyaham adya tvāṃ sūryaḥ saṃdhyām ivaujasā ||
children.translated_text: I shall destroy you today with my power, as the sun destroys twilight."
Having spoken thus to <s>Maithilī</s>, King <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, crusher of enemies,
then gave orders to all the rākṣasīs of dreadful appearance:
to the one-eyed and one-eared, and likewise to the one whose ears served as coverings,
to the cow-eared, the elephant-eared, the long-eared, and the earless,
to the elephant-footed and horse-footed, the cow-footed and the hair-footed,
to the one-eyed, the one-footed, the broad-footed, and the footless,
to those with overlarge heads and necks, and with overlarge breasts and bellies,
to those with overlarge mouths and eyes, with long tongues, and without tongues,
to the noseless, the lion-faced, the cow-faced, and the boar-faced.

children.text: yathā madvaśagā sītā kṣipraṃ bhavati jānakī
children.translated_text: "In whatever way <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Jānakī</s>, may quickly become subject to my will,

children.text: tathā kuruta rākṣasyaḥ sarvāḥ kṣipraṃ sametya ca ||
children.translated_text: do that, rākṣasīs, all of you gathered together quickly.
By contrary and agreeable means, by conciliation, gifts, and the other methods of division,
turn <s>Vaidehī</s> around, and also by raising punishment against her."
Having commanded them again and again in this way, the lord of rākṣasas,
his self overcome by desire and anger, repeatedly threatened <s>Jānakī</s>.
Then the rākṣasī <s>Dhānyamālinī</s> quickly approached,
embraced <s>Daśagrīva</s>, and spoke these words:
"Sport with me, great king. What is this <s>Sītā</s> to you?
The body of one who desires an unwilling woman is tormented;
when one desires a woman who desires him, beautiful pleasure arises."
Thus addressed by the rākṣasī, the powerful one, then lifted up,
entered his dwelling, bright like the blazing sun.
The daughters of gods and gandharvas, and the daughters of nāgas, then
surrounded <s>Daśagrīva</s> and entered that excellent house.

children.text: sa maithilīṃ dharmaparām avasthitāṃ pravepamānāṃ paribhartsya rāvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: After reviling <s>Maithilī</s>, who was fixed on dharma, trembling, and standing firm, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: vihāya sītāṃ madanena mohitaḥ svam eva veśma praviveśa bhāsvaram ||
children.translated_text: abandoning <s>Sītā</s> and deluded by passion, entered his own shining palace.
Having spoken thus to <s>Maithilī</s>, King <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, crusher of enemies,

children.text: saṃdiśya ca tataḥ sarvā rākṣasīr nirjagāma ha ||
children.translated_text: and having instructed all the rākṣasīs, then went out.

children.text: niṣkrānte rākṣasendre tu punar antaḥpuraṃ gate
children.translated_text: When the lord of rākṣasas had gone out and returned again to the inner apartments,
those rākṣasīs of terrible form rushed upon <s>Sītā</s>.
Then, approaching <s>Sītā</s>, the rākṣasīs, faint with anger,

children.text: paraṃ paruṣayā vācā vaidehīm idam abruvan ||
children.translated_text: spoke these words to <s>Vaidehī</s> in exceedingly harsh speech:
