"O <s>Sītā</s>, do you not think much of becoming the wife of the great-souled <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: daśagrīvasya bhāryātvaṃ sīte na bahu manyase ||
children.translated_text: the foremost descendant of <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Daśagrīva</s>?"
Then a rākṣasī named <s>Ekajaṭā</s> spoke a sentence,
addressing <s>Sītā</s>, the slender-waisted one, while her eyes were red with anger:

children.text: prajāpatīnāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ tu caturtho yaḥ prajāpatiḥ
children.translated_text: "Among the six <s>Prajāpatis</s>, the one who is the fourth <s>Prajāpati</s>,

children.text: mānaso brahmaṇaḥ putraḥ pulastya iti viśrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a mind-born son of <s>Brahmā</s>, is famed as <s>Pulastya</s>.

children.text: pulastyasya tu tejasvī maharṣir mānasaḥ sutaḥ
children.translated_text: Of <s>Pulastya</s>, the radiant great seer, the mind-born son,
is named <s>Viśravas</s>, equal in splendor to a <s>Prajāpati</s>.
His son, O wide-eyed one, is <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, crusher of enemies.

children.text: tasya tvaṃ rākṣasendrasya bhāryā bhavitum arhasi
children.translated_text: You ought to become the wife of that lord of rākṣasas.
O woman lovely in every limb, why do you not approve the words I have spoken?"

children.text: tato harijaṭā nāma rākṣasī vākyam abravīt
children.translated_text: Then a rākṣasī named <s>Harijaṭā</s> spoke a sentence,
opening wide her eyes from anger, her gaze like a cat's:
"The thirty-three gods, and the king of the gods, were conquered by him.

children.text: tasya tvaṃ rākṣasendrasya bhāryā bhavitum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: You ought to become the wife of that lord of rākṣasas.
Why will you not obtain wifehood with that hero, proud of his valor,

children.text: balino vīryayuktasya bhāryātvaṃ kiṃ na lapsyase ||
children.translated_text: who does not turn back in battles, who is strong and endowed with might?

children.text: priyāṃ bahumatāṃ bhāryāṃ tyaktvā rājā mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: The mighty king <s>Rāvaṇa</s> will abandon his beloved and highly honored wife,

children.text: sarvāsāṃ ca mahābhāgāṃ tvām upaiṣyati rāvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: greatly fortunate among all women, and come to you.
Abandoning his inner palace, prosperous with a thousand women
and adorned with many jewels, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> will come to you.
The gods, nāgas, gandharvas, and dānavas have often

children.text: nirjitāḥ samare yena sa te pārśvam upāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: been conquered in battle by him; he has come to your side.
Why do you not desire wifehood with that <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
the great-souled lord of rākṣasas, possessed of every prosperity, O base woman?

children.text: yasya sūryo na tapati bhīto yasya ca mārutaḥ
children.translated_text: The sun does not shine on him, out of fear, and the wind

children.text: na vāti smāyatāpāṅge kiṃ tvaṃ tasya na tiṣṭhasi ||
children.translated_text: does not blow before him, O woman with smiling sidelong glances. Why do you not stand with him?

children.text: puṣpavṛṣṭiṃ ca taravo mumucur yasya vai bhayāt
children.translated_text: The trees send down a rain of flowers because of fear of him.
and mountains, fine-browed one, and water, and rain-clouds, and whatever he desires.
For that king of the <s>Nairṛtas</s>, that king of kings, O lovely woman,

children.text: kiṃ tvaṃ na kuruṣe buddhiṃ bhāryārthe rāvaṇasya hi ||
children.translated_text: why do you not set your mind upon being the wife of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>?

children.text: sādhu te tattvato devi kathitaṃ sādhu bhāmini
children.translated_text: Good counsel, O goddess, has been truthfully spoken to you; good counsel, O lovely woman.

children.text: gṛhāṇa susmite vākyam anyathā na bhaviṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: Accept this word, O sweet-smiling one; otherwise you will not live.
Then the <s>rākṣasī</s> women, with distorted faces, approached <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: paruṣaṃ paruṣā nārya ūcustā vākyam apriyam ||
children.translated_text: and those harsh women spoke harsh, unpleasant words.
Why, <s>Sītā</s>, do you not consent to dwell in the inner palace,
delighting all beings and furnished with costly couches?
You, a human woman, think highly of being the wife of a mere human.

children.text: pratyāhara mano rāmānna tvaṃ jātu bhaviṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: Withdraw your mind from <s>Rāma</s>; you will never belong to him.

children.text: mānuṣī mānuṣaṃ taṃ tu rāmam icchasi śobhane
children.translated_text: A human woman desires that human <s>Rāma</s>, O lovely one,

children.text: rājyād bhraṣṭam asiddhārthaṃ viklavaṃ tam anindite ||
children.translated_text: fallen from his kingdom, unsuccessful in his purpose, and helpless, O blameless one.
Hearing the words of the <s>rākṣasīs</s>, lotus-eyed <s>Sītā</s>
spoke these words with both eyes filled with tears.
This thing that you, gathered together, are saying is hated by the world.
That sinful speech does not settle in my mind.

children.text: na mānuṣī rākṣasasya bhāryā bhavitum arhati
children.translated_text: A human woman ought not become the wife of a <s>rākṣasa</s>.

children.text: kāmaṃ khādata māṃ sarvā na kariṣyāmi vo vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Eat me, all of you, if you wish; I will not do what you say.

children.text: dīno vā rājyahīno vā yo me bhartā sa me guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whether wretched or deprived of his kingdom, the one who is my husband is my lord.
Hearing <s>Sītā</s>'s words, the <s>rākṣasīs</s>, overwhelmed with anger,
began to threaten her with harsh words, urged on by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Hidden in the śiṃśapā tree, silent and speechless, <s>Hanumān</s>,
the monkey, heard those <s>rākṣasīs</s> terrifying <s>Sītā</s>.
Advancing upon her in rage, while she trembled on every side,
they licked their blazing, pendulous lips with great intensity.
And, extremely angry, they spoke, quickly seizing axes:
This woman does not deserve <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, as a husband.
Threatened by the dreadful <s>rākṣasīs</s>, that beautiful-faced woman

children.text: sā bāṣpam apamārjantī śiṃśapāṃ tām upāgamat ||
children.translated_text: wiped away her tears and went to that śiṃśapā tree.
Then <s>Sītā</s>, surrounded by the <s>rākṣasīs</s>,
approached that śiṃśapā tree and stood there, wide-eyed and overwhelmed with grief.
Thin, with a wretched face, and wearing soiled garments,
she was threatened on every side by those dreadful <s>rākṣasīs</s>.
Then a <s>rākṣasī</s> named <s>Vinatā</s>, terrible to behold,
with an angry appearance, frightful and hollow-bellied, said:
<s>Sītā</s>, enough; this much love for your husband has been shown.
Excess in everything, good lady, tends toward misfortune.

children.text: parituṣṭāsmi bhadraṃ te mānuṣaste kṛto vidhiḥ
children.translated_text: I am satisfied; good fortune to you. A human woman's duty has been performed by you.

children.text: mamāpi tu vacaḥ pathyaṃ bruvantyāḥ kuru maithili ||
children.translated_text: But now, <s>Maithilī</s>, heed my beneficial words as I speak.
Take <s>Rāvaṇa</s> as your husband, the husband of all <s>rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: vikrāntaṃ rūpavantaṃ ca sureśam iva vāsavam ||
children.translated_text: valiant and handsome, like <s>Vāsava</s>, lord of the gods.
He is courteous, liberal by nature, and speaks pleasantly to everyone.

children.text: mānuṣaṃ kṛpaṇaṃ rāmaṃ tyaktvā rāvaṇam āśraya ||
children.translated_text: Abandon miserable human <s>Rāma</s> and take refuge in <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Anointed with divine unguents, O <s>Vaidehī</s>, adorned with divine ornaments,

children.text: adya prabhṛti sarveṣāṃ lokānām īśvarī bhava
children.translated_text: from this day onward become mistress of all the worlds,

children.text: agneḥ svāhā yathā devī śacīvendrasya śobhane ||
children.translated_text: as the goddess <s>Svāhā</s> is of <s>Agni</s>, and as <s>Śacī</s> is of <s>Indra</s>, O lovely one.

children.text: kiṃ te rāmeṇa vaidehi kṛpaṇena gatāyuṣā ||
children.translated_text: What use have you, O <s>Vaidehī</s>, for miserable <s>Rāma</s>, whose life is spent?

children.text: etad uktaṃ ca me vākyaṃ yadi tvaṃ na kariṣyasi
children.translated_text: And if you will not do this word that I have spoken,
we shall all devour you at this very moment.
But another, named <s>Vikaṭā</s>, with hanging breasts,

children.text: abravīt kupitā sītāṃ muṣṭim udyamya garjatī ||
children.translated_text: angrily said to <s>Sītā</s>, raising her fist and roaring:
Many improper words, wicked-minded one,
have been endured from you, O <s>Maithilī</s>, because of pity and gentleness.

children.text: na ca naḥ kuruṣe vākyaṃ hitaṃ kālapuraskṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Yet you do not obey our words, which are beneficial and suited to the time.
You have been brought to the far shore of the ocean, inaccessible to others,
and you have entered <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s dreadful inner palace, O <s>Maithilī</s>.
Shut up in <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s house and closely guarded by us,

children.text: na tvāṃ śaktaḥ paritrātum api sākṣāt puraṃdaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: not even <s>Puraṃdara</s> himself is able to rescue you.
Do the word of me who speaks for your welfare, O <s>Maithilī</s>.
Enough with this fall of tears; abandon useless grief.

children.text: bhaja prītiṃ praharṣaṃ ca tyajaitāṃ nityadainyatām
children.translated_text: Embrace affection and delight; give up this constant misery.
<s>Sītā</s>, sport as you please with the king of the <s>rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: jānāsi hi yathā bhīru strīṇāṃ yauvanam adhruvam
children.translated_text: For you know, timid one, that women's youth is impermanent.

children.text: yāvanna te vyatikrāmet tāvat sukham avāpnuhi ||
children.translated_text: Before it passes away from you, obtain pleasure.
Wander through lovely gardens and mountain groves
together with the king of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, O wine-eyed one.

children.text: strīsahasrāṇi te sapta vaśe sthāsyanti sundari
children.translated_text: Seven thousand women, beautiful one, will stand under your command.
Take <s>Rāvaṇa</s> as your husband, the husband of all <s>rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: utpāṭya vā te hṛdayaṃ bhakṣayiṣyāmi maithili
children.translated_text: Or, tearing out your heart, I shall eat it, O <s>Maithilī</s>,

children.text: yadi me vyāhṛtaṃ vākyaṃ na yathāvat kariṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: if you do not duly carry out the word I have uttered.
Then a <s>rākṣasī</s> named <s>Caṇḍodarī</s>, cruel to behold,
brandishing a great spear, spoke these words:
Seeing this woman with eyes restless like a deer's, her breasts trembling with terror,

children.text: rāvaṇena hṛtāṃ dṛṣṭvā daurhṛdo me mahān abhūt ||
children.translated_text: carried off by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, a great craving has arisen in me.
Her liver, spleen, and lungs, her heart together with its attachments,

children.text: antrāṇyapi tathā śīrṣaṃ khādeyam iti me matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and likewise her entrails and head too: my thought is that I would eat them.

children.text: tatastu praghasā nāma rākṣasī vākyam abravīt
children.translated_text: Then the rākṣasī named <s>Praghasā</s> spoke these words:

children.text: kaṇṭham asyā nṛśaṃsāyāḥ pīḍayāmaḥ kim āsyate ||
children.translated_text: "Let us squeeze the throat of this wicked woman; why sit here?

children.text: nivedyatāṃ tato rājñe mānuṣī sā mṛteti ha
children.translated_text: Then let it be reported to the king: 'That human woman is dead.'

children.text: nātra kaścana saṃdehaḥ khādateti sa vakṣyati ||
children.translated_text: There is no doubt about it; he will say, 'Eat her.'"
Then the rākṣasī named <s>Ajāmukhī</s> spoke these words:

children.text: viśasyemāṃ tataḥ sarvān samān kuruta pīlukān ||
children.translated_text: "Cut her up; then make equal portions for everyone.

children.text: vibhajāma tataḥ sarvā vivādo me na rocate
children.translated_text: Then we shall all divide her; I do not like quarrelling.

children.text: peyam ānīyatāṃ kṣipraṃ mālyaṃ ca vividhaṃ bahu ||
children.translated_text: Let drink be brought quickly, and many garlands of various kinds."

children.text: tataḥ śūrpaṇakhā nāma rākṣasī vākyam abravīt
children.translated_text: Then the rākṣasī named <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s> spoke these words:

children.text: ajāmukhyā yad uktaṃ hi tad eva mama rocate ||
children.translated_text: "What <s>Ajāmukhī</s> has said is exactly what pleases me.
Let liquor too be brought quickly, the destroyer of every sorrow.
Having obtained human flesh, let us dance at <s>Nikumbhilā</s>."
Thus threatened, <s>Sītā</s>, like a daughter of the gods,
wept, abandoning courage, before those exceedingly dreadful rākṣasīs.

children.text: tathā tāsāṃ vadantīnāṃ paruṣaṃ dāruṇaṃ bahu
children.translated_text: While those grim rākṣasīs were speaking in that way,
uttering many harsh and terrible words, <s>Janaka</s>'s daughter wept.

children.text: evam uktā tu vaidehī rākṣasībhir manasvinī
children.translated_text: But <s>Vaidehī</s>, high-minded though she was, thus addressed by the rākṣasīs,
spoke in utter terror, with a voice choked by tears:

children.text: na mānuṣī rākṣasasya bhāryā bhavitum arhati
children.translated_text: "A human woman ought not to become the wife of a rākṣasa.

children.text: kāmaṃ khādata māṃ sarvā na kariṣyāmi vo vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Eat me, all of you, as you please; I will not do what you say."
<s>Sītā</s>, like a daughter of the gods, standing amid the rākṣasīs,

children.text: na śarma lebhe duḥkhārtā rāvaṇena ca tarjitā ||
children.translated_text: found no comfort, afflicted by sorrow and threatened by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
<s>Sītā</s> trembled all the more, as if shrinking into her own body,
like a doe lost from the herd in the forest and harried by predators.

children.text: sā tvaśokasya vipulāṃ śākhām ālambya puṣpitām
children.translated_text: Grasping a broad flowering branch of the aśoka tree,
she thought of her husband, her mind broken by grief.
Bathing her broad breasts with streams of water from her eyes,
she kept thinking and at that time could not reach the end of her grief.

children.text: sā vepamānā patitā pravāte kadalī yathā
children.translated_text: Trembling and fallen like a plantain tree in a strong wind,
terrified by the rākṣasīs, she became pale-faced.

children.text: tasyāḥ sā dīrghavipulā vepantyāḥ sītayā tadā
children.translated_text: Then, as that <s>Sītā</s> trembled, her long and heavy
braid was seen quivering, like a serpent creeping about.
Sighing, afflicted by sorrow, her mind overwhelmed by grief,

children.text: ārtā vyasṛjad aśrūṇi maithilī vilalāpa ha ||
children.translated_text: distressed <s>Maithilī</s> shed tears and lamented:

children.text: hā rāmeti ca duḥkhārtā punar hā lakṣmaṇeti ca
children.translated_text: "Ah, <s>Rāma</s>!" she cried in sorrow, and again, "Ah, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>!"

children.text: hā śvaśru mama kausalye hā sumitreti bhāvini ||
children.translated_text: "Ah, my mother-in-law <s>Kausalyā</s>! Ah, <s>Sumitrā</s>, noble lady!"
"This common saying, declared by the wise, is true:

children.text: akāle durlabho mṛtyuḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā ||
children.translated_text: death is hard to obtain before its time, for a woman or for a man.
For here I am tormented by these cruel rākṣasīs,

children.text: jīvāmi hīnā rāmeṇa muhūrtam api duḥkhitā ||
children.translated_text: yet I live, bereft of <s>Rāma</s>, miserable even for a moment.
I, poor and of little merit, shall perish like one without a protector,
like a laden ship in the middle of the ocean struck by violent winds.
Not seeing that husband of mine, having fallen under the rākṣasīs' power,

children.text: sīdāmi khalu śokena kūlaṃ toyahataṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: I truly sink with grief, like a riverbank battered by water.
Blessed are those who see my lord, lotus-petal-eyed,

children.text: dhanyāḥ paśyanti me nāthaṃ kṛtajñaṃ priyavādinam ||
children.translated_text: moving with a lion's stride, grateful, and sweet-spoken.
For me, wholly deprived of that <s>Rāma</s>, knower of himself,

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ viṣam ivāsvādya durlabhaṃ mama jīvitam ||
children.translated_text: life is hard to sustain, as if I had tasted sharp poison.

children.text: kīdṛśaṃ tu mayā pāpaṃ purā dehāntare kṛtam
children.translated_text: What sort of sin did I commit long ago in another body,

children.text: yenedaṃ prāpyate duḥkhaṃ mayā ghoraṃ sudāruṇam ||
children.translated_text: through which this dreadful, most terrible suffering is now obtained by me?

children.text: jīvitaṃ tyaktum icchāmi śokena mahatā vṛtā
children.translated_text: Surrounded by great grief, I wish to abandon life;
but with the rākṣasīs guarding me, <s>Rāma</s> cannot be reached by me.

children.text: dhig astu khalu mānuṣyaṃ dhig astu paravaśyatām
children.translated_text: Fie upon human birth indeed; fie upon dependence on another,

children.text: na śakyaṃ yat parityaktum ātmacchandena jīvitam ||
children.translated_text: since life cannot be given up according to one's own will.
Thus speaking, <s>Janaka</s>'s daughter, her face streaming with tears,
the young woman, her face bent downward, began to lament.
Grieving like one mad, like one intoxicated, like one whose mind is bewildered,
she writhed on the ground like a young mare turned back.
From vigilant <s>Rāghava</s>, by the shape-shifting rākṣasa,
by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, I was violently seized and carried off by force while crying out.
Having fallen under the rākṣasīs' power and being most terribly threatened,
thinking on all this and afflicted by great sorrow, I cannot bear to live.

children.text: na hi me jīvitenārtho naivārthair na ca bhūṣaṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: For I have no use for life, nor for wealth, nor for ornaments,
while dwelling among rākṣasīs without <s>Rāma</s>, the great chariot-warrior.

children.text: dhiṅ mām anāryām asatīṃ yāhaṃ tena vinā kṛtā
children.translated_text: Fie on me, ignoble and unfaithful, that I, separated from him,
protect this sinful life even for a single moment.

children.text: kā ca me jīvite śraddhā sukhe vā taṃ priyaṃ vinā
children.translated_text: What concern have I with life, or with happiness, without that beloved one,
my sweet-speaking husband, dear to the earth bounded by the ocean?
Let this body be split apart or eaten; I give it up.

children.text: na cāpyahaṃ ciraṃ duḥkhaṃ saheyaṃ priyavarjitā ||
children.translated_text: And bereft of my beloved, I could not endure sorrow for long.
I would not touch the night-roaming <s>Rāvaṇa</s> even with my left foot;

children.text: rāvaṇaṃ kiṃ punar ahaṃ kāmayeyaṃ vigarhitam ||
children.translated_text: how then could I desire that contemptible one?

children.text: pratyākhyātaṃ na jānāti nātmānaṃ nātmanaḥ kulam
children.translated_text: He does not understand that he has been rejected, nor does he know himself or his own family,
he who, by his cruel nature, wishes to court me.

children.text: chinnā bhinnā vibhaktā vā dīpte vāgnau pradīpitā
children.translated_text: Cut, broken, divided, or set blazing in a blazing fire,
I would not attend upon <s>Rāvaṇa</s>; what is the use of your long prattle?
<s>Rāghava</s> is renowned as wise, grateful, compassionate,
and righteous; yet, through the exhaustion of my fortune, I suspect he has become pitiless.
The fourteen thousand rākṣasas in <s>Janasthāna</s>,

children.text: yenaikena nirastāni sa māṃ kiṃ nābhipadyate ||
children.translated_text: who were cast down by him alone: why does he not come to me?
I have been imprisoned by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, a rākṣasa of little strength.

children.text: samarthaḥ khalu me bhartā rāvaṇaṃ hantum āhave ||
children.translated_text: Surely my husband is capable of killing <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle.
That foremost of rākṣasas, <s>Virādha</s>, in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest,

children.text: raṇe rāmeṇa nihataḥ sa māṃ kiṃ nābhipadyate ||
children.translated_text: was slain in battle by <s>Rāma</s>; why does he not come to me?
Granted, this <s>Laṅkā</s>, in the middle of the ocean, is hard to assault,

children.text: na tu rāghavabāṇānāṃ gatirodhī ha vidyate ||
children.translated_text: but there is no obstruction to the course of <s>Rāghava</s>'s arrows.

children.text: kiṃ nu tat kāraṇaṃ yena rāmo dṛḍhaparākramaḥ
children.translated_text: What indeed is the reason that <s>Rāma</s>, firm in valor,
does not recover his beloved wife, carried off by a rākṣasa?

children.text: ihasthāṃ māṃ na jānīte śaṅke lakṣmaṇapūrvajaḥ
children.translated_text: I suspect that <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s elder brother does not know that I am here;

children.text: jānann api hi tejasvī dharṣaṇāṃ marṣayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: for if he knew, would that fiery one endure this outrage?
The king of vultures, who, having learned that I was taken, would have reported it to <s>Rāghava</s>,
even he was struck down in battle by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: kṛtaṃ karma mahat tena māṃ tadābhyavapadyatā
children.translated_text: A great deed was done by him when he came to my aid then,
by <s>Jaṭāyus</s>, though old, as he stood against <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in combat.

children.text: yadi mām iha jānīyād vartamānāṃ sa rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: If that <s>Rāghava</s> knew that I am staying here,

children.text: adya bāṇair abhikruddhaḥ kuryāl lokam arākṣasam ||
children.translated_text: today, enraged, he would make the world free of rākṣasas with his arrows.
He would shatter the city of <s>Laṅkā</s> and dry up the great ocean,

children.text: rāvaṇasya ca nīcasya kīrtiṃ nāma ca nāśayet ||
children.translated_text: and he would destroy the fame and name of base <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Then, in house after house, for the rākṣasīs whose lords had been slain,

children.text: yathāham evaṃ rudatī tathā bhūyo na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: there would be still more weeping, just as I am weeping; there is no doubt.

children.text: anviṣya rakṣasāṃ laṅkāṃ kuryād rāmaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, would search the rākṣasas' <s>Laṅkā</s> and do this.

children.text: na hi tābhyāṃ ripur dṛṣṭo muhūrtam api jīvati
children.translated_text: For no enemy seen by those two lives even for a muhūrta.
With its roads filled with the smoke of funeral pyres and crowded with flocks of vultures,
this <s>Laṅkā</s> would soon become like a cremation ground.
In a short time I shall surely obtain my desire.
This evil portent announces the downfall of all of you.

children.text: yādṛśāni tu dṛśyante laṅkāyām aśubhāni tu
children.translated_text: Such inauspicious signs as are seen in <s>Laṅkā</s>
mean that before long it will be stripped of its splendor.

children.text: nūnaṃ laṅkā hate pāpe rāvaṇe rākṣasādhipe
children.translated_text: Surely, when sinful <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of rākṣasas, is slain,

children.text: śoṣaṃ yāsyati durdharṣā pramadā vidhavā yathā ||
children.translated_text: unassailable <s>Laṅkā</s> will wither away like a widow.
Though prosperous with Puṣya festivals, bereft of its lord and together with its rākṣasas,
the city of <s>Laṅkā</s> will become like a woman whose husband is lost.
Surely, before long, in house after house,

children.text: śroṣyāmi nacirād eva duḥkhārtānām iha dhvanim ||
children.translated_text: I shall hear here the cries of rākṣasa maidens weeping and afflicted with grief.
Darkened, its brightness destroyed, and its foremost rākṣasas slain,
the city of <s>Laṅkā</s> will be burned by <s>Rāma</s>'s arrows.

children.text: yadi nāma sa śūro māṃ rāmo raktāntalocanaḥ
children.translated_text: If indeed that hero <s>Rāma</s>, whose eyes are red at the corners,
should know that I am staying in <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s dwelling,
then the time that this cruel, base <s>Rāvaṇa</s>
has fixed for me has now arrived.

children.text: akāryaṃ ye na jānanti nairṛtāḥ pāpakāriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: These wicked nairṛtas, doers of evil, do not know what must not be done.

children.text: adharmāt tu mahotpāto bhaviṣyati hi sāmpratam ||
children.translated_text: From adharma (unrighteousness), a great calamity will now arise.
These flesh-eating rākṣasas do not understand dharma (righteous order).
Surely the rākṣasa will have me prepared for his morning meal.

children.text: sāhaṃ kathaṃ kariṣyāmi taṃ vinā priyadarśanam
children.translated_text: How shall I go on without that beloved one, beautiful to behold,
without seeing <s>Rāma</s>, whose eyes are red at the corners, I who am deeply afflicted?

children.text: yadi kaścit pradātā me viṣasyādya bhaved iha
children.translated_text: If there were anyone here today who would give me poison,

children.text: kṣipraṃ vaivasvataṃ devaṃ paśyeyaṃ patinā vinā ||
children.translated_text: then, without my husband, I would quickly see the god <s>Vaivasvata</s>.
<s>Rāma</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s elder brother, does not know that I am alive.

children.text: jānantau tau na kuryātāṃ norvyāṃ hi mama mārgaṇam ||
children.translated_text: If those two knew, they would not fail to search for me on the earth.

children.text: nūnaṃ mamaiva śokena sa vīro lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ
children.translated_text: Surely because of grief for me, that hero, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s elder brother,
has gone from here to the world of the gods, abandoning his body on the earth.
Blessed are the gods together with the gandharvas, the siddhas, and the supreme seers,

children.text: mama paśyanti ye nāthaṃ rāmaṃ rājīvalocanam ||
children.translated_text: who behold my lord <s>Rāma</s>, lotus-eyed.

children.text: atha vā na hi tasyārthe dharmakāmasya dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: Or perhaps, for that wise one devoted to dharma,
for <s>Rāma</s>, the royal seer and great-souled one, I as his wife have no purpose.
Affection may exist when one is seen; for one unseen there is no friendship.
Only the ungrateful destroy it; <s>Rāma</s> will not destroy it.

children.text: kiṃ nu me na guṇāḥ kecit kiṃ vā bhāgyakṣayo hi me
children.translated_text: Have I no good qualities at all, or has my fortune indeed come to an end,

children.text: yāhaṃ sītā varārheṇa hīnā rāmeṇa bhāminī ||
children.translated_text: that I, <s>Sītā</s>, a radiant woman, am separated from worthy <s>Rāma</s>?

children.text: śreyo me jīvitānmartuṃ vihīnā yā mahātmanā
children.translated_text: Better for me to die than to live, separated as I am from that great-souled one,
from <s>Rāma</s>, of unblemished conduct, heroic and a crusher of enemies.
Or perhaps those two have laid down their weapons in the forest and eat roots and fruits,
the two brothers, best of men, moving through the forest ranges.
Or perhaps by the evil-minded <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of rākṣasas,
the two heroic brothers, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, have been slain by deceit.

children.text: sāham evaṃgate kāle martum icchāmi sarvathā
children.translated_text: With things having come to this, I wish in every way to die.

children.text: na ca me vihito mṛtyur asmin duḥkhe 'pi vartati ||
children.translated_text: Yet death has not been ordained for me, even while I remain in this sorrow.
Blessed indeed are the great-souled sages, honored for truth,

children.text: jitātmāno mahābhāgā yeṣāṃ na staḥ priyāpriye ||
children.translated_text: self-controlled and greatly fortunate, for whom there is neither dear nor hateful.

children.text: priyānna sambhaved duḥkham apriyād adhikaṃ bhayam
children.translated_text: From the dear arises sorrow, and from the hateful greater fear.

children.text: tābhyāṃ hi ye viyujyante namasteṣāṃ mahātmanām ||
children.translated_text: Homage to those great-souled ones who are separated from both.
I, abandoned here by beloved <s>Rāma</s>, who knows the self,
having fallen into the power of sinful <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, shall give up my life.
Thus spoken to by <s>Sītā</s>, the terrible rākṣasīs were overcome with anger.
Some went to report that to the swift <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Then the rākṣasīs, terrible to behold, approached <s>Sītā</s>,
and again spoke harshly, with a single purpose, for a harmful end.
"Now, O ignoble <s>Sītā</s>, resolved upon evil,
the rākṣasīs will eat this flesh of yours as they please."

children.text: sītāṃ tābhir anāryābhir dṛṣṭvā saṃtarjitāṃ tadā
children.translated_text: Then, seeing <s>Sītā</s> threatened by those ignoble women,

children.text: rākṣasī trijaṭā vṛddhā śayānā vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: the aged rākṣasī <s>Trijaṭā</s>, lying there, spoke these words:
"Eat yourselves, ignoble women; you will not eat <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: janakasya sutām iṣṭāṃ snuṣāṃ daśarathasya ca ||
children.translated_text: the beloved daughter of <s>Janaka</s> and daughter-in-law of <s>Daśaratha</s>.

children.text: svapno hyadya mayā dṛṣṭo dāruṇo romaharṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: For today I saw a dreadful dream, making the hair stand on end,

children.text: rākṣasānām abhāvāya bhartur asyā bhavāya ca ||
children.translated_text: for the destruction of the rākṣasas and for the prosperity of her husband.
Thus addressed by <s>Trijaṭā</s>, the rākṣasīs, overcome with anger,

children.text: sarvā evābruvan bhītāstrijaṭāṃ tām idaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: all of them terrified, spoke these words to that <s>Trijaṭā</s>:

children.text: kathayasva tvayā dṛṣṭaḥ svapno 'yaṃ kīdṛśo niśi ||
children.translated_text: "Tell us what sort of dream you saw in the night."

children.text: tāsāṃ śrutvā tu vacanaṃ rākṣasīnāṃ mukhodgatam
children.translated_text: Hearing the words that had come from the mouths of those rākṣasīs,
<s>Trijaṭā</s>, at the proper time, spoke words concerning the dream:
"A divine litter made of ivory, moving through the sky,
yoked with a thousand horses, was mounted by <s>Rāghava</s> himself.

children.text: svapne cādya mayā dṛṣṭā sītā śuklāmbarāvṛtā
children.translated_text: And in my dream today I saw <s>Sītā</s> covered in white garments,
standing on a white mountain encircled by the ocean;

children.text: rāmeṇa saṃgatā sītā bhāskareṇa prabhā yathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s> was united with <s>Rāma</s>, like radiance with the sun.
And I saw <s>Rāghava</s> mounted on a great four-tusked elephant,
resembling a mountain, moving about together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Then those two tigers among men, blazing with their own splendor,
wearing white garlands and garments, came near <s>Jānakī</s>.
Then, on the top of that elephant, mountain-like and standing in the sky,
<s>Jānakī</s>, received by her husband, rested upon his shoulder.
Then, springing up from her husband's lap, the lotus-eyed woman
was seen by me wiping the moon and the sun with her hands.
Then that best of elephants, mounted by those two princes

children.text: sītayā ca viśālākṣyā laṅkāyā upari sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and by wide-eyed <s>Sītā</s>, stood above <s>Laṅkā</s>.
In a chariot yoked with eight pale bulls,
wearing white garlands and garments, joined by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā sītayā saha bhāryayā ||
children.translated_text: with his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and with <s>Sītā</s>, his wife.

children.text: vimānāt puṣpakād adya rāvaṇaḥ patito bhuvi
children.translated_text: Today I saw <s>Rāvaṇa</s> fallen from the Puṣpaka aerial car to the ground,

children.text: kṛṣyamāṇaḥ striyā dṛṣṭo muṇḍaḥ kṛṣṇāmbaraḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: being dragged by a woman, shaven-headed and again dressed in black.
In a chariot yoked with donkeys, wearing red garlands and unguents,

children.text: prayāto dakṣiṇām āśāṃ praviṣṭaḥ kardamaṃ hradam ||
children.translated_text: he went toward the southern quarter and entered a muddy lake.
Having bound <s>Daśagrīva</s> by the neck, a woman dressed in red,
black, with limbs smeared with mud, drags him toward the southern quarter.
<s>Daśagrīva</s> went by a boar, <s>Indrajit</s> by a śiṃśumāra,
and <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> by a camel, toward the southern direction.
And a great gathering took place, with the sound of songs and instruments,
of rākṣasas drinking, wearing red garlands and red garments.
And this beautiful city <s>Laṅkā</s>, crowded with horses and chariots,
was seen fallen into the ocean, its gateways and arches broken.
Having drunk oil, all the rākṣasa women danced and laughed with loud noise
in <s>Laṅkā</s>, which was harsh and dry with ashes.
And these foremost rākṣasas, <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> and the others, all of them,
putting on red clothing, entered a pool of cow-dung.
Go away; perish! <s>Rāghava</s> is obtaining <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: ghātayet paramāmarṣī sarvaiḥ sārdhaṃ hi rākṣasaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: That supremely wrathful one will slay you together with all the rākṣasas.
His beloved and highly honored wife, who followed him into forest exile,
<s>Rāghava</s> will not tolerate as having been reviled or threatened.

children.text: tad alaṃ krūravākyair vaḥ sāntvam evābhidhīyatām
children.translated_text: Therefore enough of your cruel words; let only conciliation be spoken.
Let us entreat <s>Vaidehī</s>; for this is what seems right to me.
For when such a dream appears to a woman in sorrow,

children.text: sā duḥkhair bahubhir muktā priyaṃ prāpnotyanuttamam ||
children.translated_text: she, freed from many sorrows, obtains unsurpassed joy.

children.text: bhartsitām api yācadhvaṃ rākṣasyaḥ kiṃ vivakṣayā
children.translated_text: Though you have threatened her, beg her, rākṣasīs; what more need be said?
For a terrible fear from <s>Rāghava</s> has come upon the rākṣasas.
For <s>Maithilī</s>, <s>Janaka</s>'s daughter, pleased by prostration,

children.text: alam eṣā paritrātuṃ rākṣasyo mahato bhayāt ||
children.translated_text: is able to protect you rākṣasīs from great fear.

children.text: api cāsyā viśālākṣyā na kiṃcid upalakṣaye
children.translated_text: Moreover, I perceive nothing at all in the limbs of this wide-eyed woman,

children.text: viruddham api cāṅgeṣu susūkṣmam api lakṣmaṇam ||
children.translated_text: no hostile sign, even one exceedingly subtle.
I suspect only a defect in her complexion, from the sorrow that has come upon
this queen, undeserving of sorrow, who has come to be under the open sky.
But I see the accomplishment of <s>Vaidehī</s>'s purpose at hand,
and the destruction of the king of rākṣasas and the victory of <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: nimittabhūtam etat tu śrotum asyā mahat priyam
children.translated_text: This is an omen that she is to hear something greatly dear,
and her long eye, like a lotus petal, is seen throbbing.
And her left arm, not the right, is slightly thrilled;

children.text: akasmād eva vaidehyā bāhur ekaḥ prakampate ||
children.translated_text: one arm of <s>Vaidehī</s> suddenly trembles.
And her excellent left thigh, like the trunk of a cow-elephant,
trembling, seems to indicate <s>Rāghava</s> standing before her.

children.text: pakṣī ca śākhānilayaṃ praviṣṭaḥ punaḥ punaścottamasāntvavādī
children.translated_text: And a bird, entering its dwelling on a branch, repeatedly speaking the best consoling words,

children.text: sukhāgatāṃ vācam udīrayāṇaḥ punaḥ punaścodayatīva hṛṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: uttering a welcome cry of happy arrival, seems again and again to urge her on, delighted."

children.text: sā rākṣasendrasya vaco niśamya tad rāvaṇasyāpriyam apriyārtā
children.translated_text: Hearing that unwelcome speech of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of rākṣasas, she, afflicted by what was hateful,

children.text: sītā vitatrāsa yathā vanānte siṃhābhipannā gajarājakanyā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s> trembled like a young daughter of an elephant king in the forest depths, assailed by a lion.

children.text: sā rākṣasīmadhyagatā ca bhīrur vāgbhir bhṛśaṃ rāvaṇatarjitā ca
children.translated_text: Timid and surrounded by rākṣasīs, and harshly threatened by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s words,

children.text: kāntāramadhye vijane visṛṣṭā bāleva kanyā vilalāpa sītā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s> wailed like a little girl abandoned in the middle of a lonely wilderness.

children.text: satyaṃ batedaṃ pravadanti loke nākālamṛtyur bhavatīti santaḥ
children.translated_text: 'True indeed is what good people say in the world: there is no death before its time,

children.text: yatrāham evaṃ paribhartsyamānā jīvāmi kiṃcit kṣaṇam apyapuṇyā ||
children.translated_text: since I, wretched and sinful, live even for some moment while being abused in this way.

children.text: sukhād vihīnaṃ bahuduḥkhapūrṇam idaṃ tu nūnaṃ hṛdayaṃ sthiraṃ me
children.translated_text: Surely this heart of mine, deprived of happiness and filled with many sorrows, is firm,

children.text: vidīryate yanna sahasradhādya vajrāhataṃ śṛṅgam ivācalasya ||
children.translated_text: for it does not split today into a thousand pieces, like a mountain peak struck by a thunderbolt.

children.text: naivāsti nūnaṃ mama doṣam atra vadhyāham asyāpriyadarśanasya
children.translated_text: Surely there is no fault of mine in this; yet I am fit to be killed by this hateful-looking one,

children.text: bhāvaṃ na cāsyāham anupradātum alaṃ dvijo mantram ivādvijāya ||
children.translated_text: for I cannot return his desire, as a <s>dvija</s> cannot give a mantra to one who is not a <s>dvija</s>.

children.text: nūnaṃ mamāṅgānyacirād anāryaḥ śastraiḥ śitaiśchetsyati rākṣasendraḥ
children.translated_text: Surely before long that ignoble lord of rākṣasas will cut my limbs with sharp weapons,

children.text: tasminn anāgacchati lokanāthe garbhasthajantor iva śalyakṛntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: while the lord of the world does not come, like a cutter of the flesh of a creature in the womb.

children.text: duḥkhaṃ batedaṃ mama duḥkhitāyā māsau cirāyābhigamiṣyato dvau
children.translated_text: Alas, this is misery for miserable me: the two months that are to come will pass slowly,

children.text: baddhasya vadhyasya yathā niśānte rājāparādhād iva taskarasya ||
children.translated_text: like the night for a bound thief condemned to death at dawn for an offense against the king.

children.text: hā rāma hā lakṣmaṇa hā sumitre hā rāma mātaḥ saha me jananyā
children.translated_text: Alas, <s>Rāma</s>! Alas, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>! Alas, <s>Sumitrā</s>! Alas, mother of <s>Rāma</s>, together with my own mother!

children.text: eṣā vipadyāmyaham alpabhāgyā mahārṇave naur iva mūḍhavātā ||
children.translated_text: I, ill-fated, am perishing here like a boat in the great ocean, driven by a confused wind.

children.text: tarasvinau dhārayatā mṛgasya sattvena rūpaṃ manujendraputrau
children.translated_text: Those two sons of a lord of men, swift and powerful, because of the being who assumed a deer's form,

children.text: nūnaṃ viśastau mama kāraṇāt tau siṃharṣabhau dvāviva vaidyutena ||
children.translated_text: have surely been slaughtered on my account, those two like a lion and a bull struck by lightning.

children.text: nūnaṃ sa kālo mṛgarūpadhārī mām alpabhāgyāṃ lulubhe tadānīm
children.translated_text: Surely that Time itself, wearing the form of a deer, lured me, ill-fated, then,

children.text: yatrāryaputraṃ visasarja mūḍhā rāmānujaṃ lakṣmaṇapūrvakaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: when, foolish, I sent away my noble lord, and also <s>Rāma</s>'s younger brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> after him.

children.text: hā rāma satyavrata dīrghabāho hā pūrṇacandrapratimānavaktra
children.translated_text: Alas, <s>Rāma</s>, true to your vow, long-armed one! Alas, face resembling the full moon!

children.text: hā jīvalokasya hitaḥ priyaśca vadhyāṃ na māṃ vetsi hi rākṣasānām ||
children.translated_text: Alas, you who are beneficial and dear to the living world, you do not know that I am condemned to death by the rākṣasas.

children.text: ananyadevatvam iyaṃ kṣamā ca bhūmau ca śayyā niyamaśca dharme
children.translated_text: My having no deity but you, this forbearance, sleeping on the ground, and restraint in <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: pativratātvaṃ viphalaṃ mamedaṃ kṛtaṃ kṛtaghneṣviva mānuṣāṇām ||
children.translated_text: this devotion to my husband has become fruitless, like service done for ungrateful people.

children.text: mogho hi dharmaścarito mamāyaṃ tathaikapatnītvam idaṃ nirartham
children.translated_text: This <s>dharma</s> practiced by me is vain, and this single-spouse fidelity is likewise meaningless,

children.text: yā tvāṃ na paśyāmi kṛśā vivarṇā hīnā tvayā saṃgamane nirāśā ||
children.translated_text: since I, emaciated, pale, bereft of you and without hope of union, do not see you.
Having duly fulfilled your father's command, returned from the forest, and completed your vow,

children.text: strībhistu manye vipulekṣaṇābhiḥ saṃraṃsyase vītabhayaḥ kṛtārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I suppose you, fearless and fulfilled, will take pleasure with wide-eyed women.

children.text: ahaṃ tu rāma tvayi jātakāmā ciraṃ vināśāya nibaddhabhāvā
children.translated_text: But I, <s>Rāma</s>, whose love has arisen for you and whose heart has long been bound for destruction,

children.text: moghaṃ caritvātha tapovrataṃ ca tyakṣyāmi dhig jīvitam alpabhāgyā ||
children.translated_text: having practiced austerity and vows in vain, shall abandon this life. Shame on life, ill-fated as I am!

children.text: sā jīvitaṃ kṣipram ahaṃ tyajeyaṃ viṣeṇa śastreṇa śitena vāpi
children.translated_text: I would quickly give up life by poison or by a sharp weapon,

children.text: viṣasya dātā na tu me 'sti kaścic chastrasya vā veśmani rākṣasasya ||
children.translated_text: but there is no one here to give me poison or a weapon in the rākṣasa's house.

children.text: śokābhitaptā bahudhā vicintya sītātha veṇyudgrathanaṃ gṛhītvā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sītā</s>, scorched by grief, thinking in many ways and taking hold of the tie of her braid,

children.text: udbadhya veṇyudgrathanena śīghram ahaṃ gamiṣyāmi yamasya mūlam ||
children.translated_text: thought, 'Binding myself quickly with this braid-tie, I shall go to <s>Yama</s>'s abode.'

children.text: itīva sītā bahudhā vilapya sarvātmanā rāmam anusmarantī
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Sītā</s>, lamenting in many ways and remembering <s>Rāma</s> with her whole self,
trembling and with her face dried up, approached a foremost flowering tree.

children.text: upasthitā sā mṛdusarvagātrī śākhāṃ gṛhītvātha nagasya tasya
children.translated_text: She, soft in every limb, stood near it and then took hold of a branch of that tree.

children.text: tasyāstu rāmaṃ pravicintayantyā rāmānujaṃ svaṃ ca kulaṃ śubhāṅgyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But as that fair-limbed woman was thinking of <s>Rāma</s>, of <s>Rāma</s>'s younger brother, and of her own family,

children.text: śokānimittāni tadā bahūni dhairyārjitāni pravarāṇi loke
children.translated_text: many excellent omens then appeared, renowned in the world and won by her steadiness,
omens that had already proved auspicious before and were recognized as signs.

children.text: tathāgatāṃ tāṃ vyathitām aninditāṃ vyapetaharṣāṃ paridīnamānasām
children.translated_text: For her who had come there, distressed, blameless, bereft of joy, and with a wretched mind,

children.text: śubhāṃ nimittāni śubhāni bhejire naraṃ śriyā juṣṭam ivopajīvinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: auspicious omens attended that auspicious woman, like servants attending a man possessed by prosperity.

children.text: tasyāḥ śubhaṃ vāmam arālapakṣma rājīvṛtaṃ kṛṣṇaviśālaśuklam
children.translated_text: One auspicious left eye of the lovely-haired woman, with curling lashes, lotus-like, black at the pupil and wide in the white,

children.text: prāspandataikaṃ nayanaṃ sukeśyā mīnāhataṃ padmam ivābhitāmram ||
children.translated_text: twitched, reddish like a lotus struck by a fish.
And her left arm, beautiful, curved, full and round, worthy of the finest black aloe and sandal paste,
which had once been occupied by her incomparable beloved, quickly trembled after a long time.

children.text: gajendrahastapratimaśca pīnas tayor dvayoḥ saṃhatayoḥ sujātaḥ
children.translated_text: And her thigh, full and resembling the trunk of a lordly elephant, well formed where the two thighs were joined,

children.text: praspandamānaḥ punar ūrur asyā rāmaṃ purastāt sthitam ācacakṣe ||
children.translated_text: trembling again, announced <s>Rāma</s> standing before her.
Again the bright-eyed woman's auspicious garment, golden in color and as if lightly dust-stained,

children.text: vāsaḥ sthitāyāḥ śikharāgradantyāḥ kiṃcit parisraṃsata cārugātryāḥ ||
children.translated_text: as she stood there, she of fine pointed teeth and lovely limbs, slipped down a little.

children.text: etair nimittair aparaiśca subhrūḥ saṃbodhitā prāg api sādhusiddhaiḥ
children.translated_text: Awakened by these and other omens, already well proven before, the fair-browed woman

children.text: vātātapaklāntam iva pranaṣṭaṃ varṣeṇa bījaṃ pratisaṃjaharṣa ||
children.translated_text: rejoiced again, like a seed withered by wind and sun and almost lost, revived by rain.
Her face, with lips like bimba fruit, beautiful eyes and brows, hair at its edge, and curling lashes,

children.text: vaktraṃ babhāse sitaśukladaṃṣṭraṃ rāhor mukhāccandra iva pramuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: shone with bright white teeth, like the moon released from the mouth of <s>Rāhu</s>.
Freed from grief, with drowsiness gone, fever calmed, and her spirit awakened by joy,

children.text: aśobhatāryā vadanena śukle śītāṃśunā rātrir ivoditena ||
children.translated_text: that noble lady shone with her bright face like night with the risen moon.

children.text: hanumān api vikrāntaḥ sarvaṃ śuśrāva tattvataḥ
children.translated_text: The mighty <s>Hanumān</s> also heard everything truly:
the threatening of <s>Sītā</s> by <s>Trijaṭā</s> and by the <s>rākṣasīs</s>.
Looking upon that lady, like a goddess in <s>Nandana</s>,
the monkey then pondered many kinds of thoughts.
She whom many thousands and tens of thousands of monkeys

children.text: dikṣu sarvāsu mārgante seyam āsāditā mayā ||
children.translated_text: are searching for in all directions has been found by me.

children.text: cāreṇa tu suyuktena śatroḥ śaktim avekṣatā
children.translated_text: By a spy well employed, observing the enemy's strength,

children.text: gūḍhena caratā tāvad avekṣitam idaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: moving secretly, all this has now been observed by me.
The special character of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, and this city too, have been observed,
as well as the power of this lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
It is proper, for that immeasurable one who has compassion for all beings,
to console his wife, who longs to see her husband.
I shall console this woman, whose face resembles the full moon,
who had never seen suffering and who now does not reach the end of suffering.
For if I go away without consoling this lady,
whose mind is struck down by grief, my departure would be blameworthy.

children.text: gate hi mayi tatreyaṃ rājaputrī yaśasvinī
children.translated_text: For when I have gone there, this glorious princess,
<s>Jānakī</s>, finding no deliverance, would abandon her life.
And it is right that by me that great-armed one, whose face resembles the full moon,
should be reassured, since he longs for the sight of <s>Sītā</s>.
But speaking to her in the presence of the night-roaming women is not permissible.

children.text: kathaṃ nu khalu kartavyam idaṃ kṛcchragato hyaham ||
children.translated_text: How indeed is this to be done? For I have fallen into difficulty.
If she is not reassured by me during what remains of the night,
then without any doubt at all she will abandon her life.

children.text: rāmaśca yadi pṛcchenmāṃ kiṃ māṃ sītābravīd vacaḥ
children.translated_text: And if <s>Rāma</s> asks me, 'What words did <s>Sītā</s> speak to me?'

children.text: kim ahaṃ taṃ pratibrūyām asambhāṣya sumadhyamām ||
children.translated_text: what shall I answer him, having not conversed with the woman of slender waist?
If I go from here in haste, without a message from <s>Sītā</s>,
the angry <s>Kākutstha</s> might burn me up with his fierce eye.
And if I bring her husband here on <s>Rāma</s>'s account,
his coming with his army will be in vain.

children.text: antaraṃ tvaham āsādya rākṣasīnām iha sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Having found an interval among the <s>rākṣasīs</s>, while remaining here,
I shall gently console this woman, who is full of anguish.
For I am extremely small in form, and particularly a monkey;
yet I shall utter here a human speech, in Sanskrit.

children.text: yadi vācaṃ pradāsyāmi dvijātir iva saṃskṛtām
children.translated_text: If I use refined speech, like a twice-born man,

children.text: rāvaṇaṃ manyamānā māṃ sītā bhītā bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s>, thinking me to be <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, will become frightened.

children.text: avaśyam eva vaktavyaṃ mānuṣaṃ vākyam arthavat
children.translated_text: Nevertheless I must speak meaningful words in human language.
Only so can this blameless woman be comforted by me, and not otherwise.

children.text: seyam ālokya me rūpaṃ jānakī bhāṣitaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: This <s>Jānakī</s>, seeing my form and likewise hearing my speech,
having already been terrified by the <s>rākṣasas</s>, will become still more terrified.
Then, seized by terror, that high-minded woman might cry out,
the wide-eyed woman knowing <s>Rāvaṇa</s> to be one who can assume any form he desires.

children.text: sītayā ca kṛte śabde sahasā rākṣasīgaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: And when a cry has been made by <s>Sītā</s>, the troop of <s>rākṣasīs</s>,
terrible and bearing many kinds of weapons, would suddenly gather like death itself.
Then, surrounding me on every side, those women with distorted faces

children.text: vadhe ca grahaṇe caiva kuryur yatnaṃ yathābalam ||
children.translated_text: would make every effort according to their strength either to kill or to seize me.
Seeing me running about among the branches, sub-branches,
and trunks of the best trees, they would become fearful and alarmed.

children.text: mama rūpaṃ ca samprekṣya vanaṃ vicarato mahat
children.translated_text: And seeing my form as I range through the great grove,
the <s>rākṣasīs</s>, with distorted faces, would become frightened with fear.

children.text: tataḥ kuryuḥ samāhvānaṃ rākṣasyo rakṣasām api
children.translated_text: Then the <s>rākṣasīs</s> would summon even the <s>rākṣasas</s>,
those appointed by the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s> in the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>' residence.
They, holding spears, arrows, swords, and various weapons,
would rush into this struggle swiftly, causing terror.
If, enraged, I were to scatter the forces of the <s>rākṣasas</s> all around,

children.text: śaknuyāṃ na tu samprāptuṃ paraṃ pāraṃ mahodadheḥ ||
children.translated_text: I might not then be able to reach the far shore of the great ocean.

children.text: māṃ vā gṛhṇīyur āplutya bahavaḥ śīghrakāriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Or many of them, swift in action, might leap up and seize me.

children.text: syād iyaṃ cāgṛhītārthā mama ca grahaṇaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Then this mission's aim would not be obtained, and I too would be captured.
Delighting in violence, they might harm this daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,

children.text: vipannaṃ syāt tataḥ kāryaṃ rāmasugrīvayor idam ||
children.translated_text: and then this work of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Sugrīva</s> would fail.
<s>Jānakī</s> dwells in this place where the way is lost,
surrounded by <s>rākṣasas</s>, encircled by the ocean, and guarded.

children.text: viśaste vā gṛhīte vā rakṣobhir mayi saṃyuge
children.translated_text: If I were slain or seized by the <s>rākṣasas</s> in battle,
I see no other helper for <s>Rāma</s> in accomplishing the task.

children.text: vimṛśaṃśca na paśyāmi yo hate mayi vānaraḥ
children.translated_text: Reflecting, I do not see any monkey who, if I were killed,
could leap across the great ocean, a hundred yojanas wide.
Granted, I am able to kill even thousands of <s>rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: na tu śakṣyāmi samprāptuṃ paraṃ pāraṃ mahodadheḥ ||
children.translated_text: but I shall not be able to reach the far shore of the great ocean.

children.text: asatyāni ca yuddhāni saṃśayo me na rocate
children.translated_text: Battles are uncertain, and uncertainty does not please me.

children.text: kaśca niḥsaṃśayaṃ kāryaṃ kuryāt prājñaḥ sasaṃśayam ||
children.translated_text: What wise man would make a certain task doubtful?

children.text: eṣa doṣo mahān hi syānmama sītābhibhāṣaṇe
children.translated_text: This indeed would be a great fault in my speaking to <s>Sītā</s>,
while <s>Vaidehī</s>'s abandoning of life would result from not speaking to her.
Accomplished aims perish when they are opposed to place and time,

children.text: viklavaṃ dūtam āsādya tamaḥ sūryodaye yathā ||
children.translated_text: when they meet with a bewildered messenger, just as darkness perishes at sunrise.
Even a settled plan does not shine when its judgment lies between benefit and harm,
for messengers who think themselves learned destroy undertakings.

children.text: na vinaśyet kathaṃ kāryaṃ vaiklavyaṃ na kathaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: How can the undertaking not be ruined, and how can bewilderment not arise?

children.text: laṅghanaṃ ca samudrasya kathaṃ nu na vṛthā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: And how might the crossing of the ocean not be in vain?

children.text: kathaṃ nu khalu vākyaṃ me śṛṇuyānnodvijeta ca
children.translated_text: How indeed might she hear my words and not be alarmed?
Thinking thus, wise <s>Hanumān</s> formed his resolve.
Praising <s>Rāma</s>, whose deeds are unwearied, her own beloved kinsman,
I shall not alarm her, whose mind is fixed on her bond with him.
Presenting the auspicious and <s>dharma</s>-joined words of <s>Rāma</s>,
the best of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s>s, whose self is well known,
I shall make her hear them all, speaking in a sweet voice.

children.text: śraddhāsyati yathā hīyaṃ tathā sarvaṃ samādadhe ||
children.translated_text: I have arranged everything in such a way that she will trust it.

children.text: iti sa bahuvidhaṃ mahānubhāvo jagatipateḥ pramadām avekṣamāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus the great-souled one, looking upon the wife of the lord of the earth after much thought,

children.text: madhuram avitathaṃ jagāda vākyaṃ drumaviṭapāntaram āsthito hanūmān ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hanūmān</s>, stationed among the branches of the tree, spoke words that were sweet and true.
After the great monkey had reflected on many kinds of thoughts in this way,

children.text: saṃśrave madhuraṃ vākyaṃ vaidehyā vyājahāra ha ||
children.translated_text: he then uttered sweet words within hearing of <s>Vaidehī</s>.
There was a king named <s>Daśaratha</s>, lord of chariots, elephants, and horses,
virtuous in conduct, greatly famed, upright, and of great renown,
born in a family of universal emperors and equal to <s>Purandara</s> in strength.
He delighted in non-injury, was not petty, was compassionate, and had truth as his valor;
he was the chief of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> lineage, possessed of fortune and increasing fortune.
Endowed with the marks of a king, broad in splendor, a bull among kings,
he was famous on the four-ended earth, a giver of happiness and himself happy.
His beloved eldest son, whose face was like the lord of the stars,
was named <s>Rāma</s>, discerning in distinctions and the best of all bowmen.
He protects his own conduct and also protects his own people;
that scorcher of foes protects the world of living beings and <s>dharma</s> as well.
At the word of his aged father, who was intent on truth,

children.text: sabhāryaḥ saha ca bhrātrā vīraḥ pravrajito vanam ||
children.translated_text: that hero went forth to the forest with his wife and with his brother.
While he was there in the great forest, running about in pursuit of game,
and after the slaughter at <s>Janasthāna</s> was heard of, and <s>Khara</s> and <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> had been killed,
then <s>Jānakī</s> was carried off by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, seized by anger.
Her exact form, her exact complexion, and her exact marks of beauty were known to me
as those of <s>Rāghava</s>'s lady; this is she, now found by me.
Having spoken thus, that bull among monkeys ceased his speech,

children.text: jānakī cāpi tacchrutvā vismayaṃ paramaṃ gatā ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Jānakī</s>, hearing it, was filled with the greatest wonder.
Then she, whose hair curved at its ends, lovely-haired and covered with hair,
timidly lifted up her face and looked at the <s>śiṃśapā</s> tree.

children.text: sā tiryag ūrdhvaṃ ca tathāpyadhastān nirīkṣamāṇā tam acintyabuddhim
children.translated_text: Looking sideways, upward, and also downward,

children.text: dadarśa piṅgādhipater amātyaṃ vātātmajaṃ sūryam ivodayastham ||
children.translated_text: she saw the son of the Wind, the minister of the lord of tawny monkeys, of inconceivable intelligence, like the sun rising.
Then, seeing him hidden among the branches, her mind became unsettled,

children.text: sā dadarśa kapiṃ tatra praśritaṃ priyavādinam ||
children.translated_text: and there she saw the monkey, humble and speaking pleasantly.

children.text: sā tu dṛṣṭvā hariśreṣṭhaṃ vinītavad upasthitam
children.translated_text: But when <s>Maithilī</s> saw the best of monkeys standing there as if respectfully,
that lovely woman thought, 'This is a dream.'

children.text: sā taṃ samīkṣyaiva bhṛśaṃ visaṃjñā gatāsukalpeva babhūva sītā
children.translated_text: As soon as <s>Sītā</s> saw him closely, she became greatly insensible, almost as if her life had gone.

children.text: cireṇa saṃjñāṃ pratilabhya caiva vicintayāmāsa viśālanetrā ||
children.translated_text: After a long while, regaining consciousness, the wide-eyed woman reflected:

children.text: svapno mayāyaṃ vikṛto 'dya dṛṣṭaḥ śākhāmṛgaḥ śāstragaṇair niṣiddhaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Today I have seen this strange dream; a branch-animal is condemned by groups of scriptures.

children.text: svastyastu rāmāya salakṣmaṇāya tathā pitur me janakasya rājñaḥ ||
children.translated_text: May there be welfare for <s>Rāma</s> together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and for my father, King <s>Janaka</s>.

children.text: svapno 'pi nāyaṃ na hi me 'sti nidrā śokena duḥkhena ca pīḍitāyāḥ
children.translated_text: Yet this is not a dream, for I have no sleep while I am afflicted by grief and sorrow.

children.text: sukhaṃ hi me nāsti yato 'smi hīnā tenendupūrṇapratimānanena ||
children.translated_text: I have no happiness, since I am separated from him whose face is like the full moon.

children.text: ahaṃ hi tasyādya manobhavena saṃpīḍitā tadgatasarvabhāvā
children.translated_text: Today I am oppressed by love for him, with all my being directed toward him.

children.text: vicintayantī satataṃ tam eva tathaiva paśyāmi tathā śṛṇomi ||
children.translated_text: Thinking of him constantly, I see him in just that way and hear him in just that way.

children.text: manorathaḥ syād iti cintayāmi tathāpi buddhyā ca vitarkayāmi
children.translated_text: I think, "This may be a wish of my mind," yet I also reason with my understanding:

children.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ tasya hi nāsti rūpaṃ suvyaktarūpaśca vadatyayaṃ mām ||
children.translated_text: what is the reason? For that wish has no form, but this one, with a very clear form, speaks to me.

children.text: namo 'stu vācaspataye savajriṇe svayambhuve caiva hutāśanāya
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Vācaspati</s>, to him who bears the thunderbolt, to <s>Svayambhū</s>, and to <s>Hutāśana</s>.

children.text: anena coktaṃ yad idaṃ mamāgrato vanaukasā tacca tathāstu nānyathā ||
children.translated_text: And whatever has been said here before me by this forest-dweller, may that be so, and not otherwise.'
Then mighty <s>Hanūmān</s>, son of the Wind, addressed her,
placing his joined palms upon his head and speaking to <s>Sītā</s> in a sweet voice:
'Who are you, lotus-petal-eyed one, wearing distressed silk garments,

children.text: drumasya śākhām ālambya tiṣṭhasi tvam aninditā ||
children.translated_text: standing, blameless lady, holding onto the branch of a tree?

children.text: kimarthaṃ tava netrābhyāṃ vāri sravati śokajam
children.translated_text: Why does water born of grief flow from your two eyes,
like water scattered from two lotus petals?
Of gods and asuras, nāgas, gandharvas, and rākṣasas,

children.text: yakṣāṇāṃ kiṃnarāṇāṃ ca kā tvaṃ bhavasi śobhane ||
children.translated_text: of yakṣas and kinnaras, who are you, beautiful one?

children.text: kā tvaṃ bhavasi rudrāṇāṃ marutāṃ vā varānane
children.translated_text: Who are you among the <s>Rudra</s>s, or among the <s>Marut</s>s, fair-faced lady,

children.text: vasūnāṃ vā varārohe devatā pratibhāsi me ||
children.translated_text: or among the <s>Vasu</s>s, lovely-hipped one? You appear to me to be a goddess.

children.text: kiṃ nu candramasā hīnā patitā vibudhālayāt
children.translated_text: Are you <s>Rohiṇī</s>, best of the stars, endowed with every excellence,
fallen from the abode of the gods, deprived of the moon?

children.text: kopād vā yadi vā mohād bhartāram asitekṣaṇā
children.translated_text: Or, dark-eyed auspicious lady, whether from anger or delusion,
are you not <s>Arundhatī</s>, having angered your venerable husband <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>?

children.text: ko nau putraḥ pitā bhrātā bhartā vā te sumadhyame
children.translated_text: What son, father, brother, or husband of yours, slender-waisted one,

children.text: asmāl lokād amuṃ lokaṃ gataṃ tvam anuśocasi ||
children.translated_text: has gone from this world to the other world, so that you grieve for him?

children.text: vyañjanāni hi te yāni lakṣaṇāni ca lakṣaye
children.translated_text: For from the marks and characteristics of yours that I observe,
I think you are the chief queen of a ruler of the earth, a king's daughter.'
If you are <s>Sītā</s>, forcibly abducted from <s>Janasthāna</s> by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: sītā tvam asi bhadraṃ te tanmamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ ||
children.translated_text: may it be well with you; then tell me this, as I ask.
Hearing his words, delighted by the mention of <s>Rāma</s>,
<s>Vaidehī</s> spoke this sentence to <s>Hanūmān</s>, who was resting in the tree.
I am the daughter of great-souled <s>Janaka</s>, the <s>Vaideha</s> king,

children.text: sītā ca nāma nāmnāhaṃ bhāryā rāmasya dhīmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and by name I am called <s>Sītā</s>; I am the wife of wise <s>Rāma</s>.
For twelve years there, in <s>Rāghava</s>'s dwelling,
I enjoyed human pleasures, endowed with the abundance of every desire.
Then in the thirteenth year the king, together with his priest,
set about consecrating the delight of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> line to the kingdom.
But while that consecration of <s>Rāghava</s> was being prepared,

children.text: kaikeyī nāma bhartāraṃ devī vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: the queen named <s>Kaikeyī</s> spoke these words to her husband:

children.text: na pibeyaṃ na khādeyaṃ pratyahaṃ mama bhojanam
children.translated_text: 'I shall not drink, nor shall I eat my daily food;
this will be the end of my life, if <s>Rāma</s> is consecrated.

children.text: yat tad uktaṃ tvayā vākyaṃ prītyā nṛpatisattama
children.translated_text: That word which you once spoke out of affection, best of kings,

children.text: tac cen na vitathaṃ kāryaṃ vanaṃ gacchatu rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: if it is not to be made false, let <s>Rāghava</s> go to the forest.'

children.text: sa rājā satyavāg devyā varadānam anusmaran
children.translated_text: Then the king, true to his word and remembering the granting of the boon to the queen,

children.text: mumoha vacanaṃ śrutvā kaikeyyāḥ krūram apriyam ||
children.translated_text: fainted when he heard <s>Kaikeyī</s>'s cruel and unwelcome speech.
Then the aged king, established in the <s>dharma</s> of truth,

children.text: jyeṣṭhaṃ yaśasvinaṃ putraṃ rudan rājyam ayācata ||
children.translated_text: weeping, begged his eldest and renowned son concerning the kingdom.

children.text: sa pitur vacanaṃ śrīmān abhiṣekāt paraṃ priyam
children.translated_text: The illustrious one, having first accepted in his mind his father's command,
which was dearer than the consecration, then accepted it with his words.
<s>Rāma</s>, of true valor, would give and would not receive,
nor would he say anything displeasing, even for the sake of his life.
The greatly renowned one put aside his very costly upper garments,

children.text: visṛjya manasā rājyaṃ jananyai māṃ samādiśat ||
children.translated_text: renounced the kingdom in his mind, and assigned me to his mother.
But I quickly set out before him, resolved to roam the forest,

children.text: na hi me tena hīnāyā vāsaḥ svarge 'pi rocate ||
children.translated_text: for, separated from him, even dwelling in heaven would not please me.

children.text: prāg eva tu mahābhāgaḥ saumitrir mitranandanaḥ
children.translated_text: And beforehand the great-fortuned <s>Saumitri</s>, delighter of his friends,
adorned himself with bark garments for the purpose of accompanying his elder brother.

children.text: te vayaṃ bhartur ādeśaṃ bahu mānya dṛḍhavratāḥ
children.translated_text: We, firm in our vows and highly honoring my husband's command,
entered the forest, never seen before and deep in aspect.
While that immeasurably powerful one was dwelling in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest,
I, his wife, was abducted by the evil-souled <s>rākṣasa</s> <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: dvau māsau tena me kālo jīvitānugrahaḥ kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: A span of two months has been granted to me by him as a favor to my life;

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ dvābhyāṃ tu māsābhyāṃ tatastyakṣyāmi jīvitam ||
children.translated_text: but after those two months I shall give up my life.
Hearing those words of hers, <s>Hanūmān</s>, leader of monkey troops,
spoke in reply a consolation to her who was overcome by sorrow upon sorrow:
O queen, I have come to you as a messenger by <s>Rāma</s>'s command;

children.text: vaidehi kuśalī rāmastvāṃ ca kauśalam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Vaidehī</s>, <s>Rāma</s> is well, and he asks about your welfare.

children.text: yo brāhmam astraṃ vedāṃśca veda vedavidāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: He who knows the <s>brāhma</s> weapon and the <s>Vedas</s>, the best of those who know the <s>Veda</s>,

children.text: sa tvāṃ dāśarathī rāmo devi kauśalam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: that son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, O queen, asks about your welfare.
And mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the beloved follower of your husband,
tormented by grief, has made obeisance to you with his head.

children.text: sā tayoḥ kuśalaṃ devī niśamya narasiṃhayoḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing of the welfare of those two lion-like men, the queen
with every limb thrilled by joy then spoke to <s>Hanūmān</s>:

children.text: kalyāṇī bata gātheyaṃ laukikī pratibhāti me
children.translated_text: Auspicious indeed this common saying seems to me:
'Joy comes to a living man, even after a hundred years.'
At that meeting between the two, a wondrous joy arose,
and, trusting one another, the two began conversation with each other.
Hearing those words of hers, <s>Hanūmān</s>, leader of monkey troops,
approached near to <s>Sītā</s>, who was wretched with grief.

children.text: yathā yathā samīpaṃ sa hanūmān upasarpati
children.translated_text: But the nearer <s>Hanūmān</s> drew toward her,

children.text: tathā tathā rāvaṇaṃ sā taṃ sītā pariśaṅkate ||
children.translated_text: the more <s>Sītā</s> suspected him to be <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: aho dhig dhik kṛtam idaṃ kathitaṃ hi yad asya me
children.translated_text: Ah, shame, shame on this act of mine, that I spoke to him;

children.text: rūpāntaram upāgamya sa evāyaṃ hi rāvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for this is that very <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, having assumed another form.

children.text: tām aśokasya śākhāṃ sā vimuktvā śokakarśitā
children.translated_text: Worn down by sorrow, she let go of that branch of the <s>aśoka</s> tree,
and the faultless-limbed woman sat down right there on the ground.
Then the mighty-armed one bowed to that daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,
but she, terrified with fear, did not look up at him again.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā vandamānaṃ tu sītā śaśinibhānanā
children.translated_text: Seeing him bowing, <s>Sītā</s>, whose face was like the moon,
sighed deeply and spoke to the monkey in a sweet voice:

children.text: māyāṃ praviṣṭo māyāvī yadi tvaṃ rāvaṇaḥ svayam
children.translated_text: If you are <s>Rāvaṇa</s> himself, a trickster resorting to illusion,

children.text: utpādayasi me bhūyaḥ saṃtāpaṃ tanna śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: and you are producing further anguish for me, that is not fitting.
You who abandoned your own form and assumed the form of a wandering ascetic,

children.text: janasthāne mayā dṛṣṭastvaṃ sa evāsi rāvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: you were seen by me in <s>Janasthāna</s>; you are that very <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
O night-roamer who takes whatever form he wishes, you torment me again,

children.text: saṃtāpayasi māṃ bhūyaḥ saṃtāpaṃ tanna śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: wretched and emaciated by fasting; that torment is not fitting.

children.text: yadi rāmasya dūtastvam āgato bhadram astu te
children.translated_text: If you have come as <s>Rāma</s>'s messenger, may it be well with you;

children.text: pṛcchāmi tvāṃ hariśreṣṭha priyā rāmakathā hi me ||
children.translated_text: I ask you, best of monkeys, for talk of <s>Rāma</s> is dear to me.

children.text: guṇān rāmasya kathaya priyasya mama vānara
children.translated_text: Tell me the virtues of <s>Rāma</s>, my beloved, O monkey;

children.text: cittaṃ harasi me saumya nadīkūlaṃ yathā rayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: gentle one, you carry away my mind as a current carries away a riverbank.

children.text: aho svapnasya sukhatā yāham evaṃ cirāhṛtā
children.translated_text: Ah, the happiness of a dream, if I, abducted so long ago,
am seeing a forest-dweller supposedly sent by <s>Rāghava</s>.
If even in a dream I were to see heroic <s>Rāghava</s> together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
I would not sink down; yet even a dream is jealous of me.

children.text: nāhaṃ svapnam imaṃ manye svapne dṛṣṭvā hi vānaram
children.translated_text: I do not think this is a dream; for, after seeing a monkey in a dream,
A good outcome is impossible to obtain, and yet a good outcome has come to me.
What indeed is this confusion of mind? Or might this be a derangement of wind?

children.text: unmādajo vikāro vā syād iyaṃ mṛgatṛṣṇikā ||
children.translated_text: Or is it a disturbance born of madness, or is this a mirage?
Or else this is not madness; even delusion has the marks of madness.

children.text: saṃbudhye cāham ātmānam imaṃ cāpi vanaukasam ||
children.translated_text: For I am aware of myself, and also of this forest-dweller.
Thus <s>Sītā</s>, after considering strength and weakness in many ways,
because <s>rākṣasas</s> can assume forms at will, thought him to be the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: etāṃ buddhiṃ tadā kṛtvā sītā sā tanumadhyamā
children.translated_text: Having then formed this judgment, that slender-waisted <s>Sītā</s>
the daughter of <s>Janaka</s> did not answer the monkey in return.
Understanding what <s>Sītā</s> had thought, <s>Hanūmān</s>, son of the Wind,
then gladdened her with words pleasing to the ear.

children.text: āditya iva tejasvī lokakāntaḥ śaśī yathā
children.translated_text: Splendid like the sun, beloved of the world as the moon is,

children.text: rājā sarvasya lokasya devo vaiśravaṇo yathā ||
children.translated_text: a king over all the world, like the god <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>,
endowed with valor, like the greatly renowned <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
truth-speaking, sweet-spoken, like the god <s>Vācaspati</s>,

children.text: rūpavān subhagaḥ śrīmān kandarpa iva mūrtimān
children.translated_text: handsome, fortunate, prosperous, like <s>Kandarpa</s> embodied,
one who strikes when anger is fitting, the best great chariot-warrior in the world,
that great-souled one beneath the shadow of whose arms the world rests:
after drawing <s>Rāghava</s> away from the hermitage in the form of a deer,

children.text: śūnye yenāpanītāsi tasya drakṣyasi yat phalam ||
children.translated_text: the one by whom you were carried off when it was empty: you will see the fruit that comes to him.

children.text: nacirād rāvaṇaṃ saṃkhye yo vadhiṣyati vīryavān
children.translated_text: Before long, that mighty one will slay <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle
with arrows released in wrath, blazing like fires.
Sent by him as a messenger, I have come here into your presence.

children.text: tvadviyogena duḥkhārtaḥ sa tvāṃ kauśalam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Afflicted by sorrow through separation from you, he asked after your welfare.
And mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, increaser of <s>Sumitrā</s>'s joy,
the long-armed one, having bowed, also asked after your welfare.

children.text: rāmasya ca sakhā devi sugrīvo nāma vānaraḥ
children.translated_text: O lady, <s>Rāma</s>'s friend, a monkey named <s>Sugrīva</s>,

children.text: rājā vānaramukhyānāṃ sa tvāṃ kauśalam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: king of the chief monkeys, also asked after your welfare.
Together with <s>Sugrīva</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, <s>Rāma</s> remembers you always.
By good fortune you are alive, O <s>Vaidehī</s>, though you have come under the power of <s>rākṣasīs</s>.

children.text: nacirād drakṣyase rāmaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahāratham
children.translated_text: Before long you will see <s>Rāma</s> and the great chariot-warrior <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
and <s>Sugrīva</s> of immeasurable splendor amid crores of monkeys.
I am <s>Hanūmān</s>, a monkey, minister of <s>Sugrīva</s>;
having leapt across the great ocean, I entered the city <s>Laṅkā</s>.
Having set my foot on the head of wicked <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
I have come to see you, relying on my valor.

children.text: nāham asmi tathā devi yathā mām avagacchasi
children.translated_text: I am not such, O lady, as you understand me to be;

children.text: viśaṅkā tyajyatām eṣā śraddhatsva vadato mama ||
children.translated_text: let this suspicion be abandoned; trust me as I speak.

children.text: tāṃ tu rāmakathāṃ śrutvā vaidehī vānararṣabhāt
children.translated_text: But having heard that story of <s>Rāma</s> from the bull among monkeys, <s>Vaidehī</s>

children.text: uvāca vacanaṃ sāntvam idaṃ madhurayā girā ||
children.translated_text: spoke these comforting words in a sweet voice.

children.text: kva te rāmeṇa saṃsargaḥ kathaṃ jānāsi lakṣmaṇam
children.translated_text: How did your association with <s>Rāma</s> come about? How do you know <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>?

children.text: vānarāṇāṃ narāṇāṃ ca katham āsīt samāgamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: How did the meeting of monkeys and men take place?

children.text: yāni rāmasya liṅgāni lakṣmaṇasya ca vānara
children.translated_text: The marks that belong to <s>Rāma</s>, and those of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, O monkey,

children.text: tāni bhūyaḥ samācakṣva na māṃ śokaḥ samāviśet ||
children.translated_text: tell them to me again, so that sorrow may not enter me.

children.text: kīdṛśaṃ tasya saṃsthānaṃ rūpaṃ rāmasya kīdṛśam
children.translated_text: What is his bodily build like? What is <s>Rāma</s>'s appearance like?

children.text: katham ūrū kathaṃ bāhū lakṣmaṇasya ca śaṃsa me ||
children.translated_text: Tell me what his thighs are like, what his arms are like, and also <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s.
When <s>Vaidehī</s> had spoken thus, <s>Hanūmān</s>, son of the Wind,
then began to describe <s>Rāma</s> exactly as he is.

children.text: jānantī bata diṣṭyā māṃ vaidehi paripṛcchasi
children.translated_text: Since, by good fortune, you know me, O <s>Vaidehī</s>, you ask me,
lotus-eyed one, for the description of your husband and of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: yāni rāmasya cihnāni lakṣmaṇasya ca yāni vai
children.translated_text: Those marks of <s>Rāma</s>, and those indeed of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: lakṣitāni viśālākṣi vadataḥ śṛṇu tāni me ||
children.translated_text: which have been observed, O wide-eyed one, hear them from me as I speak.
<s>Rāma</s> has eyes like lotus petals and enchants all beings;
he is endowed with beauty and courtesy, nobly born, O daughter of <s>Janaka</s>.
In splendor he resembles the sun; in patience he is equal to the earth.
In intelligence he is equal to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>; in fame he is like <s>Vāsava</s>.
He is the protector of the world of living beings and the protector of his own people;

children.text: rakṣitā svasya vṛttasya dharmasya ca paraṃtapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that scorcher of foes is the protector of his own conduct and of <s>dharma</s>.
O lovely woman, <s>Rāma</s> is the protector of the world's four <s>varṇas</s>;

children.text: maryādānāṃ ca lokasya kartā kārayitā ca saḥ ||
children.translated_text: he is the maker and enforcer of the world's boundaries.
Radiant and exceedingly honored, he is established in the vow of <s>brahmacarya</s>;
he knows the services rendered by good men and understands the proper course of actions.
He is trained in royal science and attends upon <s>brāhmaṇas</s>;
learned, endowed with character, disciplined, and a scorcher of foes.
He is trained in the <s>Yajurveda</s> and is well honored by knowers of the Veda;

children.text: dhanurvede ca vede ca vedāṅgeṣu ca niṣṭhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he is grounded in the <s>Dhanurveda</s>, in the Veda, and in the <s>Vedāṅgas</s>.
Broad-shouldered, long-armed, conch-necked, and fair-faced,

children.text: gūḍhajatruḥ sutāmrākṣo rāmo devi janaiḥ śrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, O lady, is known among people as having hidden collarbones and reddish eyes.
His voice has the deep sound of a kettledrum; he is smooth in complexion and majestic.
He is symmetrical, with limbs evenly proportioned, and his color is dark.
Three parts of him are firm, three are long, three are even, and three are raised;
he has three folds, three lowered parts, four distinguished limbs, and a threefold head-mark.
He has four measures, four lines, four cubits, and four equal parts;
he has fourteen pairs alike, four prominent teeth, and four kinds of gait.
His lips, jaw, and nose are large; five parts are smooth, and he has an eightfold frame.
Ten parts are lotus-like, ten are large, three extend fully, and two are white;
six are elevated, nine are slender, and by three measures <s>Rāghava</s> fills out his form.
Splendid and devoted to truth and <s>dharma</s> (righteous conduct), he is intent on restraint and favor.
He knows the divisions of place and time, and he speaks words pleasing to all people.

children.text: bhrātā ca tasya dvaimātraḥ saumitrir aparājitaḥ
children.translated_text: And his brother by a different mother is the unconquered <s>Saumitri</s>,
equal to him in affection, beauty, and virtues.

children.text: tvām eva mārgamāṇau tau vicarantau vasuṃdharām
children.translated_text: Those two, searching for you alone, as they wandered over the earth,
saw the lord of deer, cast down by his elder brother.
On the slope of <s>Rsyamuka</s>, crowded with many trees,
they saw handsome <s>Sugriva</s> sitting there, distressed over his brother's wife, cast down by his elder brother.

children.text: vayaṃ tu harirājaṃ taṃ sugrīvaṃ satyasaṃgaram
children.translated_text: We, for our part, serve that monkey-king <s>Sugriva</s>, true to his agreements,
who had been cast out of his kingdom by his elder brother.
Then those two, clothed in bark garments and holding excellent bows in their hands,
came to a lovely region of <s>Rsyamuka</s> mountain.

children.text: sa tau dṛṣṭvā naravyāghrau dhanvinau vānararṣabhaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing those two tiger-like men, bowmen, that bull among monkeys
leapt up to the peak of that mountain, bewildered with fear.

children.text: tataḥ sa śikhare tasmin vānarendro vyavasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, standing on that peak, the lord of monkeys

children.text: tayoḥ samīpaṃ mām eva preṣayāmāsa satvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: quickly sent me myself near those two.
At <s>Sugriva</s>'s command I approached those two tiger-like men, those lords,
endowed with beauty and auspicious marks, with folded hands.
After I had discerned the true meaning of their purpose, I, filled with affection,
