children.text: pṛṣṭham āropya taṃ deśaṃ prāpitau puruṣarṣabhau ||
children.translated_text: placed those excellent men on my back and brought them to that place.
They were accurately introduced by me to the great-souled <s>Sugriva</s>,
and from their mutual conversation great affection arose.
There the two renowned ones, the lord of monkeys and the lord of men,
gave one another confidence by recounting what had happened before.
Then <s>Rama</s>, elder brother of <s>Laksmana</s>, consoled <s>Sugriva</s>,
who, because of a woman, had been driven out by his brother <s>Valin</s> of vast might.
Then <s>Laksmana</s> reported to the lord of monkeys, <s>Sugriva</s>,
the grief of unwearied <s>Rama</s> caused by your disappearance.
When that lord of monkeys heard the words spoken by <s>Laksmana</s>,
he became then exceedingly dim, like the radiant sun seized by an eclipse.
Then the clusters of ornaments that adorned your limbs,
which, as you were being carried off by the <s>raksasa</s>, had been dropped on the ground,
all those the monkey troop-leaders brought to <s>Rama</s>,

children.text: saṃhṛṣṭā darśayāmāsur gatiṃ tu na vidustava ||
children.translated_text: and joyfully showed them to him, though they did not know your course.
Those were given to <s>Rama</s>, brought forward by me myself,
jingling and scattered, while his mind was stricken.
After placing those lovely ornaments in his lap,
that godlike radiant lord lamented in many ways.
As he looked at them, wept, and grew faint again and again,
they kindled the fire of grief in the son of <s>Dasaratha</s>.

children.text: śayitaṃ ca ciraṃ tena duḥkhārtena mahātmanā
children.translated_text: Long did that great-souled one, afflicted with sorrow, lie there;

children.text: mayāpi vividhair vākyaiḥ kṛcchrād utthāpitaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: with various words I too raised him up again with difficulty.

children.text: tāni dṛṣṭvā mahārhāṇi darśayitvā muhur muhuḥ
children.translated_text: Having seen those very precious ornaments and having shown them again and again,
<s>Raghava</s>, together with <s>Saumitri</s>, entrusted the matter to <s>Sugriva</s>.
Because he does not see you, noble lady, that <s>Raghava</s> burns with anguish,
like a volcano with a great blazing fire at all times.

children.text: tvatkṛte tam anidrā ca śokaścintā ca rāghavam
children.translated_text: For your sake sleeplessness, grief, and anxiety
torment the great-souled <s>Raghava</s>, as fires torment a house of fire.
By the sorrow of not seeing you, <s>Raghava</s> is shaken,
like a great mountain mass by a mighty earthquake.
As he wanders through very lovely forests, rivers, and waterfalls,
he finds no delight, not seeing you, princess.

children.text: sa tvāṃ manujaśārdūlaḥ kṣipraṃ prāpsyati rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: That tiger among men, <s>Raghava</s>, will quickly reach you,
after killing <s>Ravana</s> together with his friends and kinsmen, daughter of <s>Janaka</s>.
Then <s>Rama</s> and <s>Sugriva</s> together made an agreement,

children.text: samayaṃ vālinaṃ hantuṃ tava cānveṣaṇaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: to kill <s>Valin</s> and likewise to search for you.

children.text: tato nihatya tarasā rāmo vālinam āhave
children.translated_text: Thereafter <s>Rama</s>, having swiftly slain <s>Valin</s> in battle,
made <s>Sugriva</s> lord of all the hosts of bears and monkeys.
Thus, O lady, the alliance of <s>Rama</s> and <s>Sugriva</s> came about;

children.text: hanūmantaṃ ca māṃ viddhi tayor dūtam ihāgatam ||
children.translated_text: and know me, <s>Hanumat</s>, to be the messenger of those two, come here.
Having regained his own kingdom, <s>Sugriva</s> assembled the great monkeys
and sent mighty ones to the ten directions for your sake.
Commanded by the monkey-lord <s>Sugriva</s> of great splendor,
they, resembling kings of mountains, set out over the earth on every side.
A glorious one named <s>Angada</s>, the very strong son of <s>Valin</s>,
a tiger among monkeys, set out accompanied by a third of the army.
As we had lost our way on <s>Vindhya</s>, that best of mountains,
and were deeply overcome by grief, many days and nights passed.
Then, from despair over the task and because time had passed,
and from fear of the monkey-king, we resolved to give up our lives.
Having searched the forest fastnesses and the mountain waterfalls,
and not having found the lady's trace, we resolved to give up our lives.
Sunk deep in an ocean of grief, <s>Angada</s> lamented,

children.text: tava nāśaṃ ca vaidehi vālinaśca tathā vadham
children.translated_text: about your loss, O <s>Vaidehi</s>, and likewise the death of <s>Valin</s>,
about our fasting unto death and the death of <s>Jatayus</s>.
To us, despairing and wishing to die because of our master's command,
there came, as if for the sake of the task, a great mighty bird.
He was the uterine brother of the king of vultures, a vulture-king named <s>Sampati</s>.

children.text: śrutvā bhrātṛvadhaṃ kopād idaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Hearing of his brother's death, he angrily spoke these words.

children.text: yavīyān kena me bhrātā hataḥ kva ca vināśitaḥ
children.translated_text: By whom was my younger brother slain, and where was he destroyed?
I wish this to be told by you, O best of monkeys.
<s>Aṅgada</s> told him of the great killing in <s>Janasthāna</s>,
by the fearsome <s>rākṣasa</s>, on your account, just as it had happened.
Hearing of <s>Jaṭāyus</s>' death, that son of <s>Aruṇa</s> was grieved,

children.text: tvām āha sa varārohe vasantīṃ rāvaṇālaye ||
children.translated_text: and he spoke of you, O lovely-waisted lady, as dwelling in <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s abode.
Hearing that word of <s>Sampāti</s>, which increased our joy,
we all, headed by <s>Aṅgada</s>, then set out,
monkeys delighted and pleased, filled with zeal by the prospect of seeing you.
Then, seeing the monkey army despondent before the ocean,

children.text: vyavadhūya bhayaṃ tīvraṃ yojanānāṃ śataṃ plutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shook off intense fear and leapt a hundred yojanas.

children.text: laṅkā cāpi mayā rātrau praviṣṭā rākṣasākulā
children.translated_text: And <s>Laṅkā</s>, full of <s>rākṣasas</s>, was entered by me at night;
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> was seen by me, and you too, oppressed by grief.

children.text: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yathāvṛttam anindite
children.translated_text: All this has been told to you, O blameless lady, just as it occurred.

children.text: abhibhāṣasva māṃ devi dūto dāśarather aham ||
children.translated_text: Speak with me, O goddess; I am the messenger of <s>Dāśarathi</s>.
Know me as one engaged in <s>Rāma</s>'s task, come here for your sake,
O goddess, as <s>Sugrīva</s>'s minister, the son of <s>Pavana</s>.
Your <s>Kākutstha</s> is well, the best of all who bear weapons,
and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, endowed with fine marks, is intent upon serving his elder.

children.text: tasya vīryavato devi bhartustava hite rataḥ
children.translated_text: For the sake of that powerful husband of yours, O goddess, devoted to your welfare,
I alone have come here by <s>Sugrīva</s>'s command.
As I wandered alone, able to assume any form at will,
the southern quarter was traversed by me while I sought to discover your path.
By good fortune, for the monkey armies grieving over your disappearance,
I shall remove their anguish by announcing that I have reached you.

children.text: diṣṭyā hi na mama vyarthaṃ devi sāgaralaṅghanam
children.translated_text: By good fortune, O goddess, my crossing of the ocean has not been in vain;
by good fortune I shall gain this fame produced by seeing you.
And mighty <s>Rāghava</s> will quickly come to you,
after killing <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, together with his friends and kinsmen.

children.text: kaurajo nāma vaidehi girīṇām uttamo giriḥ
children.translated_text: O <s>Vaidehī</s>, there is a mountain named <s>Kauraja</s>, the best of mountains;

children.text: tato gacchati gokarṇaṃ parvataṃ kesarī hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: from there the monkey <s>Kesarī</s> goes to the mountain <s>Gokarṇa</s>.

children.text: sa ca devarṣibhir dṛṣṭaḥ pitā mama mahākapiḥ
children.translated_text: And he, my father, the great monkey, was seen by divine seers,
when at the holy ford of the lord of rivers he overthrew <s>Śambasādana</s>.

children.text: tasyāhaṃ hariṇaḥ kṣetre jāto vātena maithili
children.translated_text: In that monkey's field I was born through <s>Vāta</s>, O <s>Maithilī</s>;

children.text: hanūmān iti vikhyāto loke svenaiva karmaṇā
children.translated_text: I am known in the world as <s>Hanumān</s> by my own deed.

children.text: viśvāsārthaṃ tu vaidehi bhartur uktā mayā guṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the sake of trust, O <s>Vaidehī</s>, I have told you of your husband's virtues.
Thus convinced by these fitting reasons, <s>Sītā</s>, wasted by grief,
understands him to be the messenger by the recognition tokens he has supplied.

children.text: atulaṃ ca gatā harṣaṃ praharṣeṇa tu jānakī
children.translated_text: And <s>Jānakī</s> came to incomparable joy through that gladness,
and from her eyes with curved lashes she shed tears born of delight.
That lovely face of hers, with long eyes coppery at the corners and white within,
shone, for the wide-eyed lady, like the moon released from <s>Rāhu</s>'s mouth.

children.text: hanūmantaṃ kapiṃ vyaktaṃ manyate nānyatheti sā ||
children.translated_text: She plainly thought the monkey to be <s>Hanumān</s>, and not otherwise.
Then <s>Hanumān</s> spoke a reply to that lovely-looking lady.
When the asura <s>Śambasādana</s> had been slain in battle by the foremost monkey at the urging of great seers,

children.text: tato 'smi vāyuprabhavo hi maithili prabhāvatastatpratimaśca vānaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: then indeed I was born from <s>Vāyu</s>, O <s>Maithilī</s>, and by power I am a monkey equal to him.
Again the greatly radiant <s>Hanumān</s>, son of <s>Māruta</s>,
spoke a humble word in order to create confidence in <s>Sītā</s>.
I am a monkey, O highly fortunate lady, the messenger of wise <s>Rāma</s>.
Look, O goddess, at this ring marked with <s>Rāma</s>'s name.
Take heart; may it be well with you, for the fruit of your sorrow is now exhausted.
Taking and examining the ornament from her husband's hand,
<s>Jānakī</s> became joyful, as though she had come into her husband's presence.
That lovely face of hers, with long eyes coppery at the corners and white within,
became raised up with joy, like the moon released from <s>Rāhu</s>.

children.text: tataḥ sā hrīmatī bālā bhartuḥ saṃdeśaharṣitā
children.translated_text: Then that modest young woman, delighted by her husband's message,
satisfied on hearing what was dear to her, praised the great monkey.
You are valiant, you are capable, you are wise, O best of monkeys,
since this seat of the <s>rākṣasas</s> has been assailed by you alone.
The ocean, a hundred yojanas broad and the abode of sea-monsters,
has been made like a cow's hoofprint by you as you crossed with praiseworthy valor.

children.text: na hi tvāṃ prākṛtaṃ manye vānaraṃ vānararṣabha
children.translated_text: For I do not think you an ordinary monkey, O bull among monkeys,

children.text: yasya te nāsti saṃtrāso rāvaṇānnāpi saṃbhramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: since you have no terror of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, nor even agitation before him.
And you deserve, O best of monkeys, to be addressed by me,
if you have been sent by that self-knowing <s>Rāma</s>.
For the unassailable <s>Rāma</s> would not send someone untested,
especially into my presence, without knowing his valor.

children.text: diṣṭyā ca kuśalī rāmo dharmātmā dharmavatsalaḥ
children.translated_text: By good fortune righteous <s>Rāma</s>, devoted to <s>dharma</s>, is well,
and so too mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, increaser of <s>Sumitrā</s>'s joy.

children.text: kuśalī yadi kākutsthaḥ kiṃ nu sāgaramekhalām
children.translated_text: If <s>Kākutstha</s> is well, why does he not burn the earth girdled by the ocean,
rising in anger like the fire at the end of an age?

children.text: atha vā śaktimantau tau surāṇām api nigrahe
children.translated_text: Or rather, those two are powerful enough to subdue even the gods;

children.text: mamaiva tu na duḥkhānām asti manye viparyayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I think only my sorrows have no reversal.
Does <s>Rāma</s> suffer? Does he not burn with grief?
And does that best of men undertake the further tasks?

children.text: kaccinna dīnaḥ saṃbhrāntaḥ kāryeṣu ca na muhyati
children.translated_text: Is he not despondent or bewildered, and does he not lose his way in his duties?
Does the king's son carry out the deeds proper to a man?
Does he who desires victory employ a twofold and threefold policy, and its means as well,
as a scorcher of foes toward his friends and among his allies?
Does he gain allies, and is he also approached by allies?
Is he one who has good friends, and is he honored by his allies?
Does the prince hope for the favor of the gods?

children.text: kaccit puruṣakāraṃ ca daivaṃ ca pratipadyate ||
children.translated_text: Does he rely on both human effort and fate?
Has <s>Rāghava</s>, because of dwelling away from home, not lost his affection for me?
Will the monkey free me from this calamity?
He is always accustomed to comforts and unaccustomed to hardships;

children.text: duḥkham uttaram āsādya kaccid rāmo na sīdati ||
children.translated_text: having reached this extreme sorrow, I hope <s>Rāma</s> does not sink down.
Is good news of <s>Kausalyā</s> and likewise of <s>Sumitrā</s>

children.text: abhīkṣṇaṃ śrūyate kaccit kuśalaṃ bharatasya ca ||
children.translated_text: and also of <s>Bharata</s> heard again and again?
For my sake, is the honorable <s>Rāghava</s> overcome with grief?
Is <s>Rāma</s> not thinking of another? Will he carry me across?
Will brother-loving <s>Bharata</s> send a terrible akṣauhiṇī army,
a bannered force guarded by ministers, for my sake?
Will the illustrious lord of monkeys, <s>Sugrīva</s>, come
for my sake, surrounded by heroic monkeys armed with teeth and nails?
And will valiant <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, who increases <s>Sumitrā</s>'s joy,
skilled in weapons, scatter the rākṣasas with a net of arrows?

children.text: raudreṇa kaccid astreṇa rāmeṇa nihataṃ raṇe
children.translated_text: Will I, in a short time, see <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, together with his friends and kinsmen,
slain in battle by <s>Rāma</s> with a terrible missile?
I hope that face of his, equal in color to gold and lotus-like in fragrance,

children.text: mayā vinā śuṣyati śokadīnaṃ jalakṣaye padmam ivātapena ||
children.translated_text: does not, without me, wither away, wretched with grief, like a lotus in the sun when the water is gone.

children.text: dharmāpadeśāt tyajataśca rājyaṃ māṃ cāpyaraṇyaṃ nayataḥ padātim
children.translated_text: When he abandoned the kingdom under the pretext of <s>dharma</s> and led me on foot into the forest,

children.text: nāsīd vyathā yasya na bhīr na śokaḥ kaccit sa dhairyaṃ hṛdaye karoti ||
children.translated_text: he felt no distress, no fear, and no sorrow; I hope he holds that firmness in his heart.

children.text: na cāsya mātā na pitā na cānyaḥ snehād viśiṣṭo 'sti mayā samo vā
children.translated_text: No mother, no father, and no one else is dearer to him than I am, or even equal to me;

children.text: tāvaddhyahaṃ dūta jijīviṣeyaṃ yāvat pravṛttiṃ śṛṇuyāṃ priyasya ||
children.translated_text: therefore, messenger, I would live only so long as I hear news of my beloved.

children.text: itīva devī vacanaṃ mahārthaṃ taṃ vānarendraṃ madhurārtham uktvā
children.translated_text: After the lady had thus spoken that weighty speech, sweet in meaning, to the lord of monkeys,

children.text: śrotuṃ punastasya vaco 'bhirāmaṃ rāmārthayuktaṃ virarāma rāmā ||
children.translated_text: the fair <s>Sītā</s> ceased, wishing to hear again his lovely words concerned with <s>Rāma</s>.
Hearing <s>Sītā</s>'s words, the son of the Wind, of fearsome valor,
placed his joined palms on his head and spoke this answer:

children.text: na tvām ihasthāṃ jānīte rāmaḥ kamalalocanaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, the lotus-eyed one, does not know that you are here;

children.text: śrutvaiva tu vaco mahyaṃ kṣipram eṣyati rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but as soon as he hears my words, <s>Rāghava</s> will come quickly.
Drawing on a great army crowded with troops of monkeys and bears,
and damming the unshakable ocean with floods of arrows,
<s>Kākutstha</s> will make the city of <s>Laṅkā</s> emptied of rākṣasas.

children.text: tatra yadyantarā mṛtyur yadi devāḥ sahāsurāḥ
children.translated_text: If Death stands in his way there, or even the gods together with the asuras,

children.text: sthāsyanti pathi rāmasya sa tān api vadhiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: on <s>Rāma</s>'s path, he will slay them too.
Noble lady, he is overwhelmed by the grief born from not seeing you;

children.text: na śarma labhate rāmaḥ siṃhārdita iva dvipaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> finds no comfort, like an elephant harried by a lion.

children.text: dardareṇa ca te devi śape mūlaphalena ca
children.translated_text: I swear to you, lady, by <s>Dardara</s> and by roots and fruits,

children.text: malayena ca vindhyena meruṇā mandareṇa ca ||
children.translated_text: by <s>Malaya</s>, <s>Vindhya</s>, <s>Meru</s>, and <s>Mandara</s>:
you will see <s>Rāma</s>'s handsome face, with beautiful eyes, charming, with bimba-like lips and lovely earrings,
like the full moon risen.

children.text: kṣipraṃ drakṣyasi vaidehi rāmaṃ prasravaṇe girau
children.translated_text: Soon, <s>Vaidehī</s>, you will see <s>Rāma</s> on Mount <s>Prasravaṇa</s>,
seated like <s>Śatakratu</s> on the summit of heaven.

children.text: na māṃsaṃ rāghavo bhuṅkte na cāpi madhu sevate
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> eats no meat, nor does he partake of honey;

children.text: vanyaṃ suvihitaṃ nityaṃ bhaktam aśnāti pañcamam ||
children.translated_text: he always eats a well-prepared woodland meal, only a fifth portion.
<s>Rāghava</s>, his inner self fixed on you, does not brush from his body
gadflies, mosquitoes, insects, or creeping things.
<s>Rāma</s> is always intent on meditation, always given over to grief;

children.text: nānyaccintayate kiṃcit sa tu kāmavaśaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: he thinks of nothing else, for he has fallen under the power of love.

children.text: anidraḥ satataṃ rāmaḥ supto 'pi ca narottamaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, best of men, is constantly sleepless; even when asleep,
he wakes up uttering the sweet word, '<s>Sītā</s>.'

children.text: dṛṣṭvā phalaṃ vā puṣpaṃ vā yaccānyat strīmanoharam
children.translated_text: Seeing a fruit or a flower, or anything else that delights women,
he sighs and addresses you again and again, saying, 'Ah, beloved!'

children.text: sa devi nityaṃ paritapyamānas tvām eva sītetyabhibhāṣamāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Lady, he is constantly tormented, speaking only of you as '<s>Sītā</s>';

children.text: dhṛtavrato rājasuto mahātmā tavaiva lābhāya kṛtaprayatnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that great-souled prince, firm in his vow, has made every effort solely to win you back.
The daughter of <s>Videha</s>, freed from grief by the praise of <s>Rāma</s> yet sharing <s>Rāma</s>'s sorrow,
became like a night at the onset of autumn, when the moon is freed from the last clouds.
Hearing that speech, <s>Sītā</s>, whose face was like the full moon,
spoke these words to <s>Hanūmān</s>, joined with <s>dharma</s> and purpose:
Monkey, what you have said is nectar mixed with poison:
that <s>Rāma</s> thinks of no one else, and that he is wholly given over to grief.

children.text: aiśvarye vā suvistīrṇe vyasane vā sudāruṇe
children.translated_text: Whether in vast sovereignty or in very terrible calamity,
Fate binds a man as if with a rope and drags him along.
Surely destiny is irresistible for living beings, best of leapers;

children.text: saumitriṃ māṃ ca rāmaṃ ca vyasanaiḥ paśya mohitān ||
children.translated_text: see <s>Saumitri</s>, me, and <s>Rāma</s> bewildered by misfortunes.
When will <s>Rāghava</s> reach the far shore of this grief,
like an exhausted swimmer in the ocean whose boat is wrecked?

children.text: rākṣasānāṃ kṣayaṃ kṛtvā sūdayitvā ca rāvaṇam
children.translated_text: after bringing about the destruction of the rākṣasas and slaying <s>Rāvaṇa</s>

children.text: laṅkām unmūlitāṃ kṛtvā kadā drakṣyati māṃ patiḥ ||
children.translated_text: When will my husband see me, after having uprooted <s>Laṅkā</s>?

children.text: sa vācyaḥ saṃtvarasveti yāvad eva na pūryate
children.translated_text: He should be told, "Make haste," so long as it is not yet fulfilled,
for this year is the limit; so long only is my life.

children.text: vartate daśamo māso dvau tu śeṣau plavaṃgama
children.translated_text: The tenth month is passing, O monkey; two remain

children.text: rāvaṇena nṛśaṃsena samayo yaḥ kṛto mama ||
children.translated_text: of the time that was set for me by cruel <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: vibhīṣaṇena ca bhrātrā mama niryātanaṃ prati
children.translated_text: And by his brother <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, regarding my release,

children.text: anunītaḥ prayatnena na ca tat kurute matim ||
children.translated_text: he was earnestly entreated, but he does not turn his mind to that.

children.text: mama pratipradānaṃ hi rāvaṇasya na rocate
children.translated_text: For returning me is not pleasing to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>;

children.text: rāvaṇaṃ mārgate saṃkhye mṛtyuḥ kālavaśaṃ gatam ||
children.translated_text: death seeks <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle, as one who has fallen under Time's power.
O monkey, the eldest daughter, named <s>Analā</s>, daughter of <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,

children.text: tayā mamaitad ākhyātaṃ mātrā prahitayā svayam ||
children.translated_text: told me this herself, sent by her mother.
There is a wise one named <s>Avindhya</s>, learned, foremost among <s>rākṣasas</s>,
steadfast, virtuous, aged, and highly respected by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
He warned him of the destruction of the <s>rākṣasas</s> that would come from <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: na ca tasyāpi duṣṭātmā śṛṇoti vacanaṃ hitam ||
children.translated_text: but that evil-minded one does not listen even to his beneficial words.

children.text: āśaṃseti hariśreṣṭha kṣipraṃ māṃ prāpsyate patiḥ
children.translated_text: Hope, O best of monkeys, that my husband will quickly reach me;

children.text: antarātmā hi me śuddhastasmiṃśca bahavo guṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for my heart is pure, and in him there are many virtues.
Energy, manliness, strength, kindness, gratitude,
valor, and majesty are present in <s>Rāghava</s>, O monkey.
He who slew fourteen thousand <s>rākṣasas</s>

children.text: janasthāne vinā bhrātrā śatruḥ kastasya nodvijet ||
children.translated_text: in <s>Janasthāna</s> without his brother--what enemy would not tremble before him?
That bull among men cannot be measured by calamities;
I know his power, as <s>Pulomajā</s> knows <s>Śakra</s>'s.
O monkey, heroic <s>Rāma</s>, a sun whose rays are nets of arrows,
will bring to dryness the water made of enemy <s>rākṣasas</s>.
As she was speaking thus, emaciated by grief on <s>Rāma</s>'s account,
her face filled with tears, <s>Hanumān</s> the monkey said to her:

children.text: śrutvaiva tu vaco mahyaṃ kṣipram eṣyati rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: As soon as he hears my word, <s>Rāghava</s> will come quickly,
leading a great army crowded with hosts of monkeys and bears.

children.text: athavā mocayiṣyāmi tām adyaiva hi rākṣasāt
children.translated_text: Or else I myself will free you from the <s>rākṣasa</s> this very day;

children.text: asmād duḥkhād upāroha mama pṛṣṭham anindite ||
children.translated_text: climb onto my back out of this suffering, O blameless lady.

children.text: tvāṃ hi pṛṣṭhagatāṃ kṛtvā saṃtariṣyāmi sāgaram
children.translated_text: For, having placed you on my back, I will cross the ocean;

children.text: śaktir asti hi me voḍhuṃ laṅkām api sarāvaṇām ||
children.translated_text: I have the strength to carry even <s>Laṅkā</s> together with <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
O <s>Maithilī</s>, today I will bring you to <s>Rāghava</s>, who is staying on <s>Prasravaṇa</s>,
as fire brings the offered oblation to <s>Śakra</s>.
This very day, O <s>Vaidehī</s>, you shall see <s>Rāghava</s> together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
endowed with resolve, like <s>Viṣṇu</s> at the slaughter of demons.
Greatly strong, dwelling at the hermitage, with his zeal aroused by the sight of you,
seated like <s>Purandara</s> on the head of the king of elephants.

children.text: pṛṣṭham āroha me devi mā vikāṅkṣasva śobhane
children.translated_text: Mount my back, O goddess; do not hesitate, O lovely one.
Seek union with <s>Rāma</s>, like <s>Rohiṇī</s> with the moon.
Like <s>Suvarcalā</s> with the sun, as though conversing with the moon,
having mounted my back, you shall cross the great ocean of the starry sky.

children.text: na hi me samprayātasya tvām ito nayato 'ṅgane
children.translated_text: For when I have set out, carrying you away from here, O lady,
all the inhabitants of <s>Laṅkā</s> will not be able to follow my course.
Just as I came here, so without doubt

children.text: yāsyāmi paśya vaidehi tvām udyamya vihāyasam ||
children.translated_text: I shall go, behold, O <s>Vaidehī</s>, lifting you through the sky.
But <s>Maithilī</s>, having heard the wondrous speech of the best of monkeys,
with all her limbs thrilled and amazed, then said to <s>Hanumān</s>:

children.text: hanūman dūram adhvānaṃ kathaṃ māṃ voḍhum icchasi
children.translated_text: O <s>Hanumān</s>, how do you wish to carry me over so long a road?

children.text: tad eva khalu te manye kapitvaṃ hariyūthapa ||
children.translated_text: That indeed, I think, is just your monkey nature, O leader of monkey troops.

children.text: kathaṃ vālpaśarīrastvaṃ mām ito netum icchasi
children.translated_text: How, with so small a body, do you wish to take me from here
to the presence of my husband, lord of men, O bull among leapers?
Hearing <s>Sītā</s>'s words, <s>Hanumān</s>, son of <s>Māruta</s>,
the glorious one, thought that a fresh slight had been made.

children.text: na me jānāti sattvaṃ vā prabhāvaṃ vāsitekṣaṇā
children.translated_text: This wide-eyed lady does not know my strength or my power;

children.text: tasmāt paśyatu vaidehī yad rūpaṃ mama kāmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore let <s>Vaidehī</s> see whatever form of mine I desire.
Having thought thus, <s>Hanumān</s>, the best of leapers, then
showed <s>Vaidehī</s> his own form, the crusher of foes.

children.text: sa tasmāt pādapād dhīmān āplutya plavagarṣabhaḥ
children.translated_text: The wise bull among leapers sprang away from that tree,
and then began to grow for the sake of winning <s>Sītā</s>'s confidence.
Like <s>Meru</s> and <s>Mandara</s>, he shone with the radiance of blazing fire,
and the bull among monkeys stood before <s>Sītā</s>.
The monkey, mountain-like, copper-faced, and very strong,
terrible with thunderbolt-like teeth and nails, said this to <s>Vaidehī</s>:
This <s>Laṅkā</s>, together with its mountains, forests, ramparts, walls, and gateways,

children.text: laṅkām imāṃ sanāthāṃ vā nayituṃ śaktir asti me ||
children.translated_text: even with its lord, I have the strength to carry away.
Therefore let your judgment be settled; enough of hesitation, O goddess.
Make <s>Rāghava</s>, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, free from sorrow, O <s>Vaidehī</s>.
Seeing him like a mountain, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,
wide-eyed like lotus petals, spoke to the own son of <s>Māruta</s>:

children.text: tava sattvaṃ balaṃ caiva vijānāmi mahākape
children.translated_text: I know your courage and your strength, O great monkey,

children.text: vāyor iva gatiṃ cāpi tejaścāgnir ivādbhutam ||
children.translated_text: and also your speed like the wind, and your wondrous splendor like fire.

children.text: prākṛto 'nyaḥ kathaṃ cemāṃ bhūmim āgantum arhati
children.translated_text: How could another, an ordinary being, be fit to come to this land,
to the far shore of the immeasurable ocean, O foremost monkey?

children.text: jānāmi gamane śaktiṃ nayane cāpi te mama
children.translated_text: I know your power in going, and also in carrying me,
but the accomplishment of our purpose here must certainly be considered at once.

children.text: ayuktaṃ tu kapiśreṣṭha mayā gantuṃ tvayā saha
children.translated_text: But, best of monkeys, it is not proper for me to go with you.
Your speed, whose rush is like the speed of the Wind, would bewilder me.
While suspended in the sky, high above the ocean,

children.text: prapateyaṃ hi te pṛṣṭhād bhayād vegena gacchataḥ ||
children.translated_text: I would fall from your back out of fear as you traveled at speed.
And if I fell into the ocean crowded with timi fish, makaras, and jhaṣa fish,

children.text: bhaveyam āśu vivaśā yādasām annam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: I would quickly become helpless, the finest food for aquatic creatures.

children.text: na ca śakṣye tvayā sārdhaṃ gantuṃ śatruvināśana
children.translated_text: Nor will I be able to go together with you, destroyer of enemies;
there would certainly be danger for you too, since you would have a woman with you.

children.text: hriyamāṇāṃ tu māṃ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasā bhīmavikramāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing me being carried away, the rākṣasas of terrible valor
would pursue, ordered by the evil-souled <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Surrounded by those brave warriors, with spears and clubs in their hands,

children.text: bhavestvaṃ saṃśayaṃ prāpto mayā vīra kalatravān ||
children.translated_text: you would fall into danger, hero, because of me, burdened with a woman.
The rākṣasas would be many and armed in the sky, while you would be unarmed;

children.text: kathaṃ śakṣyasi saṃyātuṃ māṃ caiva parirakṣitum ||
children.translated_text: how will you be able to fight and also protect me?
While you were fighting those rākṣasas of cruel deeds,

children.text: prapateyaṃ hi te pṛṣṭhād bhayārtā kapisattama ||
children.translated_text: I, distressed by fear, would fall from your back, best of monkeys.

children.text: atha rakṣāṃsi bhīmāni mahānti balavanti ca
children.translated_text: Or the rākṣasas, fearsome, huge, and powerful,
might somehow conquer you in battle, best of monkeys.
Or, while you were fighting and your face was turned away, I might fall;

children.text: patitāṃ ca gṛhītvā māṃ nayeyuḥ pāparākṣasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the sinful rākṣasas might seize me after I had fallen and carry me away.

children.text: māṃ vā hareyustvaddhastād viśaseyur athāpi vā
children.translated_text: They might snatch me from your hand, or even kill me;
for victory and defeat in battle are both seen to be uncertain.
Or I might perish, threatened by the rākṣasas;
then your effort, best of monkeys, would be entirely fruitless.

children.text: kāmaṃ tvam api paryāpto nihantuṃ sarvarākṣasān
children.translated_text: Of course you are capable enough to destroy all the rākṣasas;

children.text: rāghavasya yaśo hīyet tvayā śastaistu rākṣasaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: but if the rākṣasas were slain by you, <s>Rāghava</s>'s fame would diminish.

children.text: athavādāya rakṣāṃsi nyasyeyuḥ saṃvṛte hi mām
children.translated_text: Or the rākṣasas might carry me off and hide me in a concealed place,

children.text: yatra te nābhijānīyur harayo nāpi rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: where neither the monkeys nor <s>Rāghava</s> would know of me.
Then this undertaking for my sake would become useless for you;

children.text: tvayā hi saha rāmasya mahān āgamane guṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for there is great advantage in <s>Rāma</s>'s coming together with you.
The life of great-souled <s>Rāghava</s> depends upon me,

children.text: bhrātṝṇāṃ ca mahābāho tava rājakulasya ca ||
children.translated_text: and that of his brothers, mighty-armed one, and of your royal house as well.
If those two, losing hope because of me and wasted by the burning pain of grief,
would abandon their hold on life together with all the bears and monkeys.

children.text: bhartur bhaktiṃ puraskṛtya rāmād anyasya vānara
children.translated_text: Putting devotion to my husband first, monkey,

children.text: nāhaṃ spraṣṭuṃ padā gātram iccheyaṃ vānarottama ||
children.translated_text: I would not wish even to touch with my foot the body of anyone other than <s>Rāma</s>, best of monkeys.

children.text: yad ahaṃ gātrasaṃsparśaṃ rāvaṇasya gatā balāt
children.translated_text: As for the bodily contact with <s>Rāvaṇa</s> that I underwent by force,

children.text: anīśā kiṃ kariṣyāmi vināthā vivaśā satī ||
children.translated_text: being powerless, unprotected, and helpless, what could I do?

children.text: yadi rāmo daśagrīvam iha hatvā sarākṣasam
children.translated_text: If <s>Rāma</s>, after killing the Ten-necked one here together with the rākṣasas,

children.text: mām ito gṛhya gaccheta tat tasya sadṛśaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: were to take me from here and go, that would be worthy of him.

children.text: śrutā hi dṛṣṭāśca mayā parākramā mahātmanastasya raṇāvamardinaḥ
children.translated_text: For I have heard and seen the exploits in battle of that great-souled crusher of armies;

children.text: na devagandharvabhujaṃgarākṣasā bhavanti rāmeṇa samā hi saṃyuge ||
children.translated_text: neither gods, gandharvas, serpents, nor rākṣasas are equal to <s>Rāma</s> in combat.

children.text: samīkṣya taṃ saṃyati citrakārmukaṃ mahābalaṃ vāsavatulyavikramam
children.translated_text: Having seen that mighty <s>Rāghava</s> in battle, with his wondrous bow and valor equal to <s>Vāsava</s>,

children.text: salakṣmaṇaṃ ko viṣaheta rāghavaṃ hutāśanaṃ dīptam ivānileritam ||
children.translated_text: who could withstand him together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, like blazing fire fanned by the wind?

children.text: salakṣmaṇaṃ rāghavam ājimardanaṃ diśāgajaṃ mattam iva vyavasthitam
children.translated_text: Who, chief of monkeys, could endure in battle <s>Rāghava</s> together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, crusher of armies,

children.text: saheta ko vānaramukhya saṃyuge yugāntasūryapratimaṃ śarārciṣam ||
children.translated_text: standing like an intoxicated elephant of the quarter, like the sun at the end of the age, with arrows as his flames?

children.text: sa me hariśreṣṭha salakṣmaṇaṃ patiṃ sayūthapaṃ kṣipram ihopapādaya
children.translated_text: Therefore, best of monkeys, quickly bring here my husband together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and the troop-leaders.

children.text: cirāya rāmaṃ prati śokakarśitāṃ kuruṣva māṃ vānaramukhya harṣitām ||
children.translated_text: Long wasted by grief for <s>Rāma</s>, make me happy, chief of monkeys.
Then that tiger among monkeys, delighted by that speech,
having heard <s>Sītā</s>'s words, spoke to her, being skilled in speech:
Lady, fair one, what you have said is fitting in form,
worthy of the nature of women and of the modesty of virtuous wives.

children.text: strītvaṃ na tu samarthaṃ hi sāgaraṃ vyativartitum
children.translated_text: Indeed, as a woman you are not able to cross
the vast ocean, a hundred yojanas in extent, mounted upon me.
And the second reason that you state, modest one,

children.text: rāmād anyasya nārhāmi saṃsparśam iti jānaki ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Jānakī</s>, saying, 'I am not fit for contact from anyone other than <s>Rāma</s>,'

children.text: etat te devi sadṛśaṃ patnyāstasya mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: that, lady, is fitting for the wife of that great-souled man.

children.text: kā hyanyā tvām ṛte devi brūyād vacanam īdṛśam ||
children.translated_text: For what other woman except you, lady, would speak such a word?
<s>Kākutstha</s> will hear, completely and without omission,

children.text: ceṣṭitaṃ yat tvayā devi bhāṣitaṃ mama cāgrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: everything that you have done and said before me, lady.
Lady, for many reasons, desiring to do what is dear to <s>Rāma</s>,
and with my mind overflowing with affection, I said this.
Because <s>Laṅkā</s> is hard to enter, because the great ocean is hard to cross,
and because of my own power, I stated this.
I wished to bring you together with the kinsman of <s>Raghu</s> this very day;

children.text: gurusnehena bhaktyā ca nānyathā tad udāhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: it was said out of deep affection and devotion, and not otherwise.

children.text: yadi notsahase yātuṃ mayā sārdham anindite
children.translated_text: If you do not dare to go with me, blameless one,

children.text: abhijñānaṃ prayaccha tvaṃ jānīyād rāghavo hi yat ||
children.translated_text: give a token of recognition by which <s>Rāghava</s> may know.
Thus addressed by <s>Hanumān</s>, <s>Sītā</s>, like a daughter of the gods,
spoke a gentle speech whose syllables were choked by tears:

children.text: idaṃ śreṣṭham abhijñānaṃ brūyāstvaṃ tu mama priyam
children.translated_text: Then tell my beloved this best token of recognition:
at the northeastern foot of Mount <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, at that time,
when I was dwelling in the hermitage of ascetics, where roots, fruits, and water were abundant...
In that land of <s>Siddhāśrama</s>, not far from the <s>Mandākinī</s>,
among its groves, fragrant with many kinds of flowers,
after wandering about, wet with water, I sat down in your lap.
Then, in your turn, O elder brother of <s>Bharata</s>, you too fell asleep in my lap.
Then a crow, drawn by flesh, began pecking at me all around;

children.text: tam ahaṃ loṣṭam udyamya vārayāmi sma vāyasam ||
children.translated_text: I picked up a clod and kept warding off that crow.

children.text: dārayan sa ca māṃ kākastatraiva parilīyate
children.translated_text: But as that crow tore at me, it hid right there;
and, seeking food, the eater of offerings did not desist from my flesh.

children.text: utkarṣantyāṃ ca raśanāṃ kruddhāyāṃ mayi pakṣiṇe
children.translated_text: As I angrily pulled at my girdle against the bird,

children.text: sraṃsamāne ca vasane tato dṛṣṭā tvayā hyaham ||
children.translated_text: and as my garment was slipping, then indeed I was seen by you.

children.text: tvayā vihasitā cāhaṃ kruddhā saṃlajjitā tadā
children.translated_text: You laughed at me, and I, angry and embarrassed then,

children.text: bhakṣya gṛddhena kālena dāritā tvām upāgatā ||
children.translated_text: torn by that bird greedy for food, came to you.

children.text: āsīnasya ca te śrāntā punar utsaṅgam āviśam
children.translated_text: Exhausted, I again entered your lap as you sat there,
and as I was angry, you, delighted, comforted me.
With my face full of tears, slowly wiping my eyes,
I was observed by you, lord, provoked by the crow.

children.text: āśīviṣa iva kruddhaḥ śvasan vākyam abhāṣathāḥ
children.translated_text: Angry like a poisonous serpent, breathing hard, you spoke these words:

children.text: kena te nāganāsoru vikṣataṃ vai stanāntaram
children.translated_text: 'Who has wounded the space between your breasts, O lady whose thighs are like an elephant's trunk?
Who is playing angrily with a five-mouthed serpent?'
Then, looking around, you saw that crow,

children.text: nakhaiḥ sarudhirais tīkṣṇair mām evābhimukhaṃ sthitam ||
children.translated_text: standing facing me, with sharp blood-stained claws.

children.text: putraḥ kila sa śakrasya vāyasaḥ patatāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: That crow, they say, was the son of <s>Śakra</s>, best of birds,
swift, moving through the mid-air, equal to the wind in speed.
Then, mighty-armed one, your eyes rolling with anger,

children.text: vāyase kṛtavān krūrāṃ matiṃ matimatāṃ vara ||
children.translated_text: you, best of the wise, formed a cruel resolve against that crow.
Taking a blade of darbha from the darbha bedding, you charged it with <s>Brahmā</s>'s missile;

children.text: sa dīpta iva kālāgnir jajvālābhimukho dvijam ||
children.translated_text: it blazed, facing the bird, like the flaming fire at the end of time.

children.text: cikṣepitha pradīptāṃ tām iṣīkāṃ vāyasaṃ prati
children.translated_text: You hurled that blazing reed-stalk at the crow;
pursued then by Death itself, he went in many directions,

children.text: trāṇakāma imaṃ lokaṃ sarvaṃ vai vicacāra ha ||
children.translated_text: seeking protection, and indeed he roamed through this whole world.

children.text: sa pitrā ca parityaktaḥ suraiḥ sarvair maharṣibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Abandoned by his father and by all the gods and great sages,

children.text: trīṃl lokān samparikramya tvām eva śaraṇaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: after traversing the three worlds, he came to you alone for refuge.

children.text: taṃ tvaṃ nipatitaṃ bhūmau śaraṇyaḥ śaraṇāgatam
children.translated_text: When he had fallen on the ground, seeking refuge, you, giver of refuge,
protected him out of compassion, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, though he deserved death;

children.text: na śarma labdhvā lokeṣu tvām eva śaraṇaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: finding no safety in the worlds, he came to you alone for refuge.

children.text: paridyūnaṃ viṣaṇṇaṃ ca sa tvam āyāntam uktavān
children.translated_text: As he came exhausted and despondent, you addressed him:

children.text: moghaṃ kartuṃ na śakyaṃ tu brāhmam astraṃ tad ucyatām ||
children.translated_text: 'This <s>brahmāstra</s> (Brahmā missile) cannot be made fruitless; tell me what is to be done.'

children.text: tatastasyākṣi kākasya hinasti sma sa dakṣiṇam ||
children.translated_text: Then that missile destroyed the crow's right eye.

children.text: sa te tadā namaskṛtvā rājñe daśarathāya ca
children.translated_text: Then, having bowed to you and to King <s>Daśaratha</s>,

children.text: tvayā vīra visṛṣṭastu pratipede svam ālayam ||
children.translated_text: released by you, hero, he went back to his own dwelling.
For my sake a <s>brahmāstra</s> (Brahmā missile) was loosed even against a mere crow;

children.text: kasmād yo māṃ harat tvattaḥ kṣamase taṃ mahīpate ||
children.translated_text: why, lord of the earth, do you pardon the one who carried me away from you?

children.text: sa kuruṣva mahotsāhaṃ kṛpāṃ mayi nararṣabha
children.translated_text: So summon up great energy; show compassion to me, bull among men.

children.text: ānṛśaṃsyaṃ paro dharmastvatta eva mayā śrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I have heard from you yourself that gentleness is the highest <s>dharma</s> (sacred duty).
I know you to be of great valor, great energy, and great strength,
boundless beyond bounds, unshakable, and like the ocean in depth,
the lord of the earth girdled by the ocean, equal to <s>Vāsava</s>.

children.text: evam astravidāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ sattvavān balavān api
children.translated_text: Though you are thus the foremost knower of missiles, steadfast and powerful,

children.text: kimartham astraṃ rakṣaḥsu na yojayasi rāghava ||
children.translated_text: why, <s>Rāghava</s>, do you not employ a missile against the rākṣasas?

children.text: na nāgā nāpi gandharvā nāsurā na marudgaṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Neither nāgas, nor gandharvas, nor asuras, nor the hosts of <s>Maruts</s>,
are able to withstand <s>Rāma</s>'s force in battle.

children.text: tasya vīryavataḥ kaścid yadyasti mayi saṃbhramaḥ
children.translated_text: If he, so heroic, has any concern for me,

children.text: kimarthaṃ na śaraistīkṣṇaiḥ kṣayaṃ nayati rākṣasān ||
children.translated_text: why does he not bring the rākṣasas to destruction with sharp arrows?

children.text: bhrātur ādeśam ādāya lakṣmaṇo vā paraṃtapaḥ
children.translated_text: Or why does <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, scorcher of foes, taking his brother's command,

children.text: kasya hetor na māṃ vīraḥ paritrāti mahābalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: not protect me, that mighty hero of great strength?
If those two tigers among men, equal in splendor to Wind and <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: surāṇām api durdharṣau kimarthaṃ mām upekṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: are hard for even the gods to assail, why do they neglect me?

children.text: mamaiva duṣkṛtaṃ kiṃcin mahad asti na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: There is surely some great misdeed of my own, no doubt,
since those two scorchers of foes, though capable, do not look after me.
The high-minded <s>Kausalyā</s> gave birth to him, the sustainer of the worlds;

children.text: taṃ mamārthe sukhaṃ pṛccha śirasā cābhivādaya ||
children.translated_text: ask after his welfare for my sake, and bow to him with your head.
Garlands and all jewels, and beloved excellent women,

children.text: aiśvaryaṃ ca viśālāyāṃ pṛthivyām api durlabham ||
children.translated_text: and sovereignty, hard to obtain even over the broad earth,
having honored and won the favor of his father and mother,
he, by whom <s>Rāma</s> was followed into exile, made <s>Sumitrā</s> the mother of a noble son;
that righteous one, favorably disposed, abandoned unsurpassed comfort.
He follows <s>Kākutstha</s>, guarding his brother in the forest,
lion-shouldered, mighty-armed, high-minded, pleasant to look upon.
He behaves toward <s>Rāma</s> as toward a father, and treats me as a mother;

children.text: hriyamāṇāṃ tadā vīro na tu māṃ veda lakṣmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but the hero <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> did not know when I was being carried away.
He serves his elders, is endowed with fortune, capable, and not talkative;
the prince, foremost among dear ones, is a match for my father-in-law.

children.text: mattaḥ priyataro nityaṃ bhrātā rāmasya lakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, <s>Rāma</s>'s brother, is always dearer to me than my own self;

children.text: niyukto dhuri yasyāṃ tu tām udvahati vīryavān ||
children.translated_text: the burden to which he is appointed he bears with valor.

children.text: yaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāghavo naiva vṛddham āryam anusmarat
children.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Rāghava</s> did not even remember his aged noble father;
he should be asked after his welfare for my sake, on my word.

children.text: mṛdur nityaṃ śucir dakṣaḥ priyo rāmasya lakṣmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> is gentle, always pure, capable, and dear to <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: idaṃ brūyāśca me nāthaṃ śūraṃ rāmaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: And again and again you should say this from me to my lord, the heroic <s>Rāma</s>:
I shall sustain my life for one month, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>;

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ māsānna jīveyaṃ satyenāhaṃ bravīmi te ||
children.translated_text: beyond a month I would not live. I tell you this truly.
I am confined by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, through deceit, by that evil-doer;

children.text: trātum arhasi vīra tvaṃ pātālād iva kauśikīm ||
children.translated_text: you ought to rescue me, hero, as <s>Kauśikī</s> was rescued from the netherworld.

children.text: tato vastragataṃ muktvā divyaṃ cūḍāmaṇiṃ śubham
children.translated_text: Then, unfastening the auspicious divine cūḍāmaṇi (crest-jewel) from her garment,
<s>Sītā</s> gave it to <s>Hanumān</s>, saying, 'This is to be given to <s>Rāghava</s>.'
Then the hero, receiving that unsurpassed jewel among gems,

children.text: aṅgulyā yojayāmāsa na hyasya prābhavad bhujaḥ ||
children.translated_text: placed it on his finger, for his arm was not able to hold it.
The best of monkeys, having received the jewel among gems and bowed respectfully,

children.text: sītāṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā praṇataḥ pārśvataḥ sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: circumambulated <s>Sītā</s> clockwise and stood at her side with head bowed.
Filled with great joy born from the sight of <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: hṛdayena gato rāmaṃ śarīreṇa tu viṣṭhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he had gone to <s>Rāma</s> in his heart, though with his body he remained there.

children.text: maṇivaram upagṛhya taṃ mahārhaṃ janakanṛpātmajayā dhṛtaṃ prabhāvāt
children.translated_text: Taking up that excellent, very precious jewel, borne in splendor by the daughter of King <s>Janaka</s>,
he, happy in mind, set out on the return path, like a great mountain freed after being shaken by the wind.

children.text: maṇiṃ dattvā tataḥ sītā hanūmantam athābravīt
children.translated_text: Then, after giving the jewel, <s>Sītā</s> said to <s>Hanūmān</s>:
This is a token truly known to <s>Rāma</s> as a sign of recognition.

children.text: maṇiṃ tu dṛṣṭvā rāmo vai trayāṇāṃ saṃsmariṣyati
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāma</s> sees the jewel, the hero will remember three people:

children.text: vīro jananyā mama ca rājño daśarathasya ca ||
children.translated_text: his mother, me, and King <s>Daśaratha</s>.
So once more, stirred to zeal, best of monkeys,
consider what comes next in the undertaking of this task.
In the accomplishment of this task, you are the authority, best of monkeys;

children.text: tasya cintaya yo yatno duḥkhakṣayakaro bhavet ||
children.translated_text: think of the effort that would bring about the end of his sorrow.
<s>Māruti</s>, of fearsome valor, promised, 'So be it,'
bowed with his head to <s>Vaidehī</s>, and prepared to depart.
Knowing that the monkey, the son of the Wind, was setting out, the lady,
<s>Maithilī</s>, spoke these words in a voice choked with tears:
<s>Hanumān</s>, report the welfare of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> together,

children.text: sugrīvaṃ ca sahāmātyaṃ vṛddhān sarvāṃśca vānarān ||
children.translated_text: and of <s>Sugrīva</s> with his ministers, and of all the elder monkeys.

children.text: yathā ca sa mahābāhur māṃ tārayati rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: And as to how mighty-armed <s>Rāghava</s> may carry me across
from this confinement in the waters of sorrow, you ought to arrange that.

children.text: jīvantīṃ māṃ yathā rāmaḥ saṃbhāvayati kīrtimān
children.translated_text: You must tell it so that renowned <s>Rāma</s>

children.text: tat tvayā hanuman vācyaṃ vācā dharmam avāpnuhi ||
children.translated_text: may think of me as still living, <s>Hanumān</s>; gain <s>dharma</s> through your speech.
Hearing the words uttered by me, words always joined with encouragement,
the manliness of <s>Dāśarathi</s> will increase for the purpose of gaining me back.
Hearing from you words furnished with my message, <s>Rāghava</s>
the hero, will duly set in order the course of his valor.
Hearing that speech of <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Hanumān</s>, the son of the Wind,
placed his joined palms upon his head and spoke this answer:
<s>Kākutstha</s> will come quickly, surrounded by the foremost monkeys and bears;
he will conquer your enemies in battle and remove your sorrow.

children.text: na hi paśyāmi martyeṣu nāmareṣvasureṣu vā
children.translated_text: For I see no one among mortals, immortals, or asuras
who could dare stand before him as he pours forth arrows.

children.text: apyarkam api parjanyam api vaivasvataṃ yamam
children.translated_text: Even the sun, even <s>Parjanya</s>, even <s>Yama</s> son of <s>Vivasvat</s>,

children.text: sa hi soḍhuṃ raṇe śaktas tava hetor viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: he is able to withstand in battle, especially for your sake.

children.text: sa hi sāgaraparyantāṃ mahīṃ śāsitum īhate
children.translated_text: For he is fit to rule the earth as far as the ocean's boundary;
<s>Rāma</s>'s victory, daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, has you as its cause.

children.text: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā samyak satyaṃ subhāṣitam
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech of his, correct, true, and well spoken,

children.text: jānakī bahu mene 'tha vacanaṃ cedam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jānakī</s> valued it highly, and then spoke these words:

children.text: tatastaṃ prasthitaṃ sītā vīkṣamāṇā punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sītā</s>, looking again and again at him as he was departing,
out of affection, addressed him with a speech filled with love for her husband:

children.text: yadi vā manyase vīra vasaikāham ariṃdama
children.translated_text: Or, if you think it best, hero, subduer of foes, stay for one day

children.text: kasmiṃścit saṃvṛte deśe viśrāntaḥ śvo gamiṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: in some hidden place; rested, you will go tomorrow.

children.text: mama ced alpabhāgyāyāḥ sāṃnidhyāt tava vīryavān
children.translated_text: Mighty one, for me of little fortune, through your nearness,

children.text: asya śokasya mahato muhūrtaṃ mokṣaṇaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: there might be a moment's release from this great sorrow.
For when you have gone, tiger among monkeys, before your return,

children.text: prāṇānām api saṃdeho mama syānnātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there would be doubt even about my life-breaths; of this there is no doubt.
The grief born from not seeing you would scorch me again,
monkey, as though inflaming me, already touched by sorrow upon sorrow.
And this doubt, hero, seems to stand before me,
a very great one concerning your helpers, the monkeys and bears, lord of monkeys.

children.text: kathaṃ nu khalu duṣpāraṃ tariṣyanti mahodadhim
children.translated_text: How indeed will those armies of monkeys and bears cross
the great ocean, so hard to cross, or those two best princes of men?
For only three beings here have the power

children.text: śaktiḥ syād vainateyasya tava vā mārutasya vā ||
children.translated_text: to leap across the ocean: <s>Vainateya</s>, you, or the Wind.
Therefore, in carrying out this task, hero, so hard to overcome,

children.text: kiṃ paśyasi samādhānaṃ tvaṃ hi kāryavidāṃ varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: what solution do you see? For you are the best of those who know what must be done.

children.text: kāmam asya tvam evaikaḥ kāryasya parisādhane
children.translated_text: Indeed, you alone are sufficient for accomplishing this task,
slayer of enemy heroes; glorious is the manifestation of your strength.

children.text: balaiḥ samagrair yadi māṃ rāvaṇaṃ jitya saṃyuge
children.translated_text: But if, with all his forces, after defeating <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle,

children.text: vijayī svapuraṃ yāyāt tat tu me syād yaśaskaram ||
children.translated_text: the victorious one should lead me to his own city, that would be honorable for me.
But if <s>Kākutstha</s>, destroyer of enemy forces, filling <s>Laṅkā</s> with troops,

children.text: māṃ nayed yadi kākutsthastat tasya sadṛśaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: should take me away, then that would be fitting for him.

children.text: tad yathā tasya vikrāntam anurūpaṃ mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, in whatever way is suitable to the valor of that great-souled one...
Act in such a way that it would be worthy of a hero in battle.
Hearing that speech, placed for her purpose, coherent and furnished with reasons,

children.text: niśamya hanumāñ śeṣaṃ vākyam uttaram abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hanūmān</s> spoke the remaining words in reply:
Lady, the lord of the armies of monkeys and bears, the best of leapers,
<s>Sugrīva</s>, endowed with spirit, has firmly resolved upon your cause.
He, surrounded by tens of millions of thousands of monkeys,
will come quickly, <s>Vaidehī</s>, to destroy the rākṣasas.
His monkeys, rich in valor, spirited, and very mighty,
swift as the flight of thought, stand under his command.

children.text: yeṣāṃ nopari nādhastānna tiryak sajjate gatiḥ
children.translated_text: For them no movement is obstructed above, below, or sideways;
and in great undertakings they do not falter, measureless in splendor.
By those high-spirited ones, more than once, the earth with its oceans and mountains
has been circumambulated, as they followed the path of the wind.
There are forest-dwellers there superior to me and equal to me;
in <s>Sugrīva</s>'s presence there is no one inferior to me.

children.text: ahaṃ tāvad iha prāptaḥ kiṃ punaste mahābalāḥ
children.translated_text: I, for my part, have reached this place; how much more those mighty ones?

children.text: na hi prakṛṣṭāḥ preṣyante preṣyante hītare janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the foremost are not sent as messengers; lesser men indeed are sent.

children.text: tad alaṃ paritāpena devi śoko vyapaitu te
children.translated_text: Therefore enough of despair, lady; let your sorrow pass away.
With a single leap the leaders of the monkey troops will come to your <s>Laṅkā</s>.
And those two, riding on my back, like the moon and sun arisen,
the two great-souled lion-like men, will come into your presence.

children.text: tau hi vīrau naravarau sahitau rāmalakṣmaṇau
children.translated_text: For those two heroes, the best of men, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> together,
will come to the city of <s>Laṅkā</s> and shatter it with arrows.
Having killed <s>Rāvaṇa</s> together with his followers, <s>Rāghava</s>, delight of <s>Raghu</s>'s line,
will take you, fair-hipped lady, and return to his own city.

children.text: tad āśvasihi bhadraṃ te bhava tvaṃ kālakāṅkṣiṇī
children.translated_text: So take heart; may it be well with you. Wait for the proper time.
Before long you will see <s>Rāma</s>, blazing like fire.
And when the lord of rākṣasas has been slain together with his sons, ministers, and kinsmen,
you will unite with <s>Rāma</s> as <s>Rohiṇī</s> with the moon.

children.text: kṣipraṃ tvaṃ devi śokasya pāraṃ yāsyasi maithili
children.translated_text: Soon, lady <s>Maithilī</s>, you will go beyond sorrow;
and before long you will see <s>Rāvaṇa</s> slain by <s>Rāma</s>.
Having thus reassured <s>Vaidehī</s>, <s>Hanūmān</s>, son of the Wind,

children.text: gamanāya matiṃ kṛtvā vaidehīṃ punar abravīt ||
children.translated_text: set his mind on departure and again spoke to <s>Vaidehī</s>:

children.text: tam arighnaṃ kṛtātmānaṃ kṣipraṃ drakṣyasi rāghavam
children.translated_text: You will quickly see <s>Rāghava</s>, slayer of foes and master of himself,
and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, bow in hand, standing at the gate of <s>Laṅkā</s>.
You will quickly see heroic monkeys, whose claws and teeth are weapons and whose valor is like that of lions and tigers,
assembled there, resembling lordly elephants.
On the <s>Malaya</s> peaks of <s>Laṅkā</s>, like mountains and clouds in appearance,
you will see many troops of chief monkeys roaring, noble lady.

children.text: sa tu marmaṇi ghoreṇa tāḍito manmatheṣuṇā
children.translated_text: But <s>Rāma</s>, struck in a vital spot by the terrible arrow of Love,

children.text: na śarma labhate rāmaḥ siṃhārdita iva dvipaḥ ||
children.translated_text: finds no comfort, like an elephant oppressed by a lion.

children.text: mā rudo devi śokena mā bhūt te manaso 'priyam
children.translated_text: Do not weep from grief, lady; let there be nothing distressing in your mind.

children.text: śacīva pathyā śakreṇa bhartrā nāthavatī hyasi ||
children.translated_text: Like <s>Śacī</s> with <s>Śakra</s>, you have a husband as your protector.

children.text: rāmād viśiṣṭaḥ ko 'nyo 'sti kaścit saumitriṇā samaḥ
children.translated_text: Who else is superior to <s>Rāma</s>? Who is equal to <s>Saumitri</s>?
Those two brothers, like Fire and Wind, are your refuge.

children.text: nāsmiṃściraṃ vatsyasi devi deśe rakṣogaṇair adhyuṣite 'tiraudre
children.translated_text: Lady, you will not dwell long in this land, exceedingly terrible and inhabited by hosts of rākṣasas.

children.text: na te cirād āgamanaṃ priyasya kṣamasva matsaṃgamakālamātram ||
children.translated_text: Your beloved will come before long; endure only the interval until my meeting with him.

children.text: śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tasya vāyusūnor mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing the words of the great-souled son of the Wind,
<s>Sītā</s>, like a daughter of the gods, spoke words for her own welfare:
Seeing you, monkey, a speaker of pleasing words, I rejoice,
like the earth with half-grown crops when it has received rain.
As I would touch that tiger among men with limbs wasted by grief,

children.text: saṃspṛśeyaṃ sakāmāhaṃ tathā kuru dayāṃ mayi ||
children.translated_text: fulfilled in my desire, so show compassion to me.
And the recognition token for <s>Rāma</s> has been given, best of the monkey hosts:
the reed cast at the crow in anger, which destroyed one eye.
The mark of red arsenic placed on the side of my cheek,

children.text: tvayā pranaṣṭe tilake taṃ kila smartum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: when my tilaka had been lost, you indeed should remember that.

children.text: sa vīryavān kathaṃ sītāṃ hṛtāṃ samanumanyase
children.translated_text: How can that heroic one tolerate <s>Sītā</s>, abducted,
dwelling among rākṣasas, O one equal to <s>Mahendra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>?
This divine crest jewel, carefully guarded by me,

children.text: etaṃ dṛṣṭvā prahṛṣyāmi vyasane tvām ivānagha ||
children.translated_text: when I see it in distress, I rejoice as if seeing you, faultless one.
This splendid jewel, born from the waters, has been handed over by me to you;

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ na śakṣyāmi jīvituṃ śokalālasā ||
children.translated_text: after this I will not be able to live, longing in grief.
Unbearable sorrows and heart-rending words
from the very terrible rākṣasī women I endure for your sake.
I will sustain my life for one month, slayer of foes;

children.text: māsād ūrdhvaṃ na jīviṣye tvayā hīnā nṛpātmaja ||
children.translated_text: beyond a month I shall not live, deprived of you, prince.

children.text: ghoro rākṣasarājo 'yaṃ dṛṣṭiśca na sukhā mayi
children.translated_text: This fierce king of rākṣasas is terrible, and his gaze upon me brings no happiness;

children.text: tvāṃ ca śrutvā vipadyantaṃ na jīveyam ahaṃ kṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: and if I heard that you had fallen into danger, I would not live for a moment.
Hearing <s>Vaidehī</s>'s compassionate words, spoken with tears,
then mighty <s>Hanūmān</s>, son of the Wind, replied:

children.text: tvacchokavimukho rāmo devi satyena te śape
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> is turned away from joy because of your grief, lady; by truth I swear to you.
And when <s>Rāma</s> is overwhelmed by grief, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> too is greatly tormented.

children.text: dṛṣṭā kathaṃcid bhavatī na kālaḥ pariśocitum
children.translated_text: Now that you have somehow been seen, this is no time for lamenting;

children.text: imaṃ muhūrtaṃ duḥkhānām antaṃ drakṣyasi bhāmini ||
children.translated_text: this very moment you will see the end of your sorrows, beautiful lady.
Those two faultless princes, the two tigers among men,
With the zeal produced by seeing you, they will reduce <s>Laṅkā</s> to ashes.

children.text: hatvā tu samare krūraṃ rāvaṇaṃ sahabāndhavam
children.translated_text: And after killing cruel <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle, together with his kinsmen,

children.text: rāghavau tvāṃ viśālākṣi svāṃ purīṃ prāpayiṣyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the two <s>Rāghavas</s> will bring you, O wide-eyed lady, to their own city.

children.text: yat tu rāmo vijānīyād abhijñānam anindite
children.translated_text: But whatever token <s>Rāma</s> might recognize, O blameless one,
and which would produce joy in him, that you ought to give again.
She said, 'The excellent token has already been given here by me.

children.text: etad eva hi rāmasya dṛṣṭvā matkeśabhūṣaṇam
children.translated_text: For when <s>Rāma</s> sees this very ornament from my hair,

children.text: śraddheyaṃ hanuman vākyaṃ tava vīra bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: your word, O valiant <s>Hanumān</s>, will become credible.'

children.text: sa taṃ maṇivaraṃ gṛhya śrīmān plavagasattamaḥ
children.translated_text: Taking that finest jewel, the glorious best of leapers
bowed his head to the lady and began to set out.
Seeing that bull among monkeys, his zeal aroused for a bold exploit,
growing in tremendous speed, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s> spoke,
downcast, her face full of tears, in a voice choked with sobs.
'<s>Hanumān</s>, tell the lion-like brothers <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: sugrīvaṃ ca sahāmātyaṃ sarvān brūyā anāmayam ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Sugrīva</s> with his ministers, and all the others, that I am safe.

children.text: yathā ca sa mahābāhur māṃ tārayati rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: And you ought to arrange how mighty-armed <s>Rāghava</s>
may rescue me from this confinement in an ocean of sorrow.

children.text: imaṃ ca tīvraṃ mama śokavegaṃ rakṣobhir ebhiḥ paribhartsanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Tell <s>Rāma</s>, when you have gone into his presence, of this fierce surge of my grief and of the intimidation by these <s>rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: brūyāstu rāmasya gataḥ samīpaṃ śivaśca te 'dhvāstu haripravīra ||
children.translated_text: And may your road be auspicious, O best of monkey heroes.'

children.text: sa rājaputryā prativeditārthaḥ kapiḥ kṛtārthaḥ parihṛṣṭacetāḥ
children.translated_text: The monkey, to whom the princess had communicated the matter, his purpose accomplished and his heart delighted,

children.text: tad alpaśeṣaṃ prasamīkṣya kāryaṃ diśaṃ hyudīcīṃ manasā jagāma ||
children.translated_text: seeing that only a little of the task remained, directed his mind toward the northern quarter.

children.text: sa ca vāgbhiḥ praśastābhir gamiṣyan pūjitastayā
children.translated_text: Then, honored by her with words of praise as he was about to go,
the monkey withdrew from that place and reflected.
'This task has only a little left; this dark-eyed lady has been seen.

children.text: trīn upāyān atikramya caturtha iha dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: Having passed over the three stratagems, the fourth is visible here.

children.text: na sāma rakṣaḥsu guṇāya kalpate na dānam arthopaciteṣu vartate
children.translated_text: Conciliation is not suited to success among <s>rākṣasas</s>; gifts do not work among those rich in possessions.

children.text: na bhedasādhyā baladarpitā janāḥ parākramastveṣa mameha rocate ||
children.translated_text: People arrogant with strength cannot be managed by division; but valor is what pleases me here.

children.text: na cāsya kāryasya parākramād ṛte viniścayaḥ kaścid ihopapadyate
children.translated_text: Apart from valor, no certain resolution of this matter is possible here.

children.text: hṛtapravīrāstu raṇe hi rākṣasāḥ kathaṃcid īyur yad ihādya mārdavam ||
children.translated_text: For if their foremost fighters are taken from them in battle, the <s>rākṣasas</s> might somehow come to mildness here today.

children.text: kārye karmaṇi nirdiṣṭo yo bahūnyapi sādhayet
children.translated_text: One who is assigned to a task and can accomplish many other things too,
without contradicting the prior task, is fit to carry out that task.

children.text: na hyekaḥ sādhako hetuḥ svalpasyāpīha karmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: For one means alone does not accomplish even a small deed here.

children.text: yo hyarthaṃ bahudhā veda sa samartho 'rthasādhane ||
children.translated_text: One who understands an objective in many ways is capable in accomplishing that objective.

children.text: ihaiva tāvat kṛtaniścayo hyahaṃ yadi vrajeyaṃ plavageśvarālayam
children.translated_text: If, having made my decision here for now, I were to go to the abode of the lord of leapers,
then, as one who knows the true nature of the special crushing of the enemy and myself, my master's command would be fulfilled.

children.text: kathaṃ nu khalvadya bhavet sukhāgataṃ prasahya yuddhaṃ mama rākṣasaiḥ
children.translated_text: How indeed today might a forced battle with the <s>rākṣasas</s> come about successfully for me?

children.text: tathaiva khalvātmabalaṃ ca sāravat samānayenmāṃ ca raṇe daśānanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And likewise how might <s>Daśānana</s> bring his substantial own strength against me in battle?
This excellent grove of that cruel one, like <s>Nandana</s>,
is charming to the eye and mind and filled with many trees and creepers.
I will destroy it as fire destroys a dry forest.

children.text: asmin bhagne tataḥ kopaṃ kariṣyati sa rāvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When this is broken, then <s>Rāvaṇa</s> will become angry.

children.text: tato mahat sāśvamahārathadvipaṃ balaṃ samāneṣyati rākṣasādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the lord of <s>rākṣasas</s> will bring a great army with horses, great chariots, and elephants,

children.text: triśūlakālāyasapaṭṭiśāyudhaṃ tato mahad yuddham idaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: armed with tridents and iron pikes; then this great battle will take place.

children.text: ahaṃ tu taiḥ saṃyati caṇḍavikramaiḥ sametya rakṣobhir asaṃgavikramaḥ
children.translated_text: But I, meeting in battle those <s>rākṣasas</s> of fierce valor, my prowess unimpeded,

children.text: nihatya tad rāvaṇacoditaṃ balaṃ sukhaṃ gamiṣyāmi kapīśvarālayam ||
children.translated_text: after slaying that force dispatched by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, will go happily to the abode of the lord of monkeys.'
Then, enraged like the wind, <s>Māruti</s>, terrible in prowess,
began to hurl trees with the great force of his thighs.
Then that hero <s>Hanumān</s> broke the pleasure grove,
which resounded with intoxicated birds and was filled with many trees and creepers.

children.text: tad vanaṃ mathitair vṛkṣair bhinnaiśca salilāśayaiḥ
children.translated_text: That grove, with trees churned up and ponds broken,
and with mountain peaks crushed, became unpleasant to look at.
With vine-houses and painted houses destroyed, and with great serpents and dangerous beasts shaken out,

children.text: śilāgṛhair unmathitaistathā gṛhaiḥ pranaṣṭarūpaṃ tad abhūnmahad vanam ||
children.translated_text: with stone houses and other buildings torn up, that great grove lost its form.

children.text: sa tasya kṛtvārthapater mahākapir mahad vyalīkaṃ manaso mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Having done a great offense against the mind of that noble, wealthy lord, the great monkey

children.text: yuyutsur eko bahubhir mahābalaiḥ śriyā jvalaṃstoraṇam āśritaḥ kapiḥ ||
children.translated_text: wishing to fight alone against many very strong warriors, blazing with splendor, took position at the gateway.
Then, by the cries of birds and by the sound of breaking trees,
all the inhabitants of <s>Laṅkā</s> became terrified and confused.
The beasts and birds, fleeing and fear-stricken, cried out,
and cruel omens appeared among the <s>rākṣasas</s>.
Then, when sleep had gone, the <s>rākṣasīs</s> of misshapen faces

children.text: tad vanaṃ dadṛśur bhagnaṃ taṃ ca vīraṃ mahākapim ||
children.translated_text: saw that grove broken and that heroic great monkey.

children.text: sa tā dṛṣṭvā mahābāhur mahāsattvo mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing them, that great-armed, great-hearted, mighty one
made an enormous form, terrifying to the <s>rākṣasīs</s>.
Then, seeing that monkey like a mountain, huge-bodied and very strong,
the <s>rākṣasīs</s> questioned the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>.

children.text: ko 'yaṃ kasya kuto vāyaṃ kiṃnimittam ihāgataḥ
children.translated_text: 'Who is this? Whose is he, and from where? For what reason has he come here?

children.text: kathaṃ tvayā sahānena saṃvādaḥ kṛta ityuta ||
children.translated_text: And how was a conversation held by you with him?'

children.text: ācakṣva no viśālākṣi mā bhūt te subhage bhayam
children.translated_text: 'Tell us, O wide-eyed one; may there be no fear for you, blessed lady.'

children.text: saṃvādam asitāpāṅge tvayā kiṃ kṛtavān ayam ||
children.translated_text: What conversation has this one had with you, O dark-eyed lady?
Then the virtuous <s>Sītā</s>, beautiful in every limb, spoke at that time:

children.text: rakṣasāṃ kāmarūpāṇāṃ vijñāne mama kā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: "What capacity have I to know <s>rākṣasas</s> who can assume forms at will?

children.text: yūyam evāsya jānīta yo 'yaṃ yad vā kariṣyati
children.translated_text: You yourselves know who this is, or what he will do.

children.text: ahir eva aheḥ pādān vijānāti na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A serpent alone knows the feet of a serpent; there is no doubt.

children.text: aham apyasya bhītāsmi nainaṃ jānāmi konvayam
children.translated_text: I too am afraid of him. I do not know who this is.
I know only that he is a <s>rākṣasa</s> who can assume forms at will and has come here."

children.text: vaidehyā vacanaṃ śrutvā rākṣasyo vidrutā drutam
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Vaidehī</s>'s words, the <s>rākṣasīs</s> quickly ran off in haste.

children.text: sthitāḥ kāścid gatāḥ kāścid rāvaṇāya niveditum ||
children.translated_text: Some stayed there, and some went to report to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Then, in <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s presence, the <s>rākṣasīs</s> of distorted faces
began to report the misshapen, terrifying monkey.
"O king, in the middle of the Aśoka grove there is a monkey of frightening body,
of immeasurable prowess, who has held conversation with <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: na ca taṃ jānakī sītā hariṃ hariṇalocanā
children.translated_text: And <s>Jānakī</s> <s>Sītā</s>, the doe-eyed lady, though questioned by us in many ways,
does not wish to tell us about that monkey.

children.text: vāsavasya bhaved dūto dūto vaiśravaṇasya vā
children.translated_text: He may be a messenger of <s>Vāsava</s>, or a messenger of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>,
or he may have been sent by <s>Rāma</s> with the desire of searching for <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: tena tvadbhutarūpeṇa yat tat tava manoharam
children.translated_text: By that one of wondrous form, that charming grove of yours,
carefully tended and filled with many herds of animals, the pleasure grove,

children.text: na tatra kaścid uddeśo yastena na vināśitaḥ
children.translated_text: has been laid waste. There is no place there that has not been destroyed by him,

children.text: yatra sā jānakī sītā sa tena na vināśitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: except the place where <s>Jānakī</s> <s>Sītā</s> was; that was not destroyed by him.
Whether for the protection of <s>Jānakī</s>, or from weariness, we do not know.
Or else, what weariness could there be for him? She herself was protected by him.
The flourishing śiṃśapā tree, rich with lovely shoots and leaves, which <s>Sītā</s> herself had occupied,
was also protected by him.
You ought to command a terrible punishment for that one of terrible form,

children.text: sītā saṃbhāṣitā yena tad vanaṃ ca vināśitam ||
children.translated_text: by whom <s>Sītā</s> was addressed and that grove was destroyed.
O lord of the hosts of <s>rākṣasas</s>, who would address <s>Sītā</s>, whom you have taken into your heart,

children.text: kaḥ sītām abhibhāṣeta yo na syāt tyaktajīvitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: unless he had already abandoned his life?"
Hearing the words of the <s>rākṣasīs</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>,
blazed like a sacrificial fire, his eyes rolling with anger.
The greatly radiant one ordered brave <s>rākṣasas</s>, equal to himself, called <s>Kiṃkaras</s>,
for the purpose of restraining <s>Hanūmat</s>.
Eighty thousand of those swift <s>Kiṃkaras</s>,
holding hammers and clubs, went out from that palace.
They were huge-bellied, great-fanged, terrifying in form, and very strong.
All were intent on battle and eager to seize <s>Hanūmat</s>.

children.text: te kapiṃ taṃ samāsādya toraṇastham avasthitam
children.translated_text: Having approached that monkey standing at the gateway,
they rushed upon him with great speed, like moths upon a fire.
With varied maces, iron bars, and golden armlets,
they struck the best of monkeys with arrows resembling the sun.
But <s>Hanūmān</s>, radiant, splendid, and resembling a mountain,
struck his tail upon the ground and roared with a great sound.
At the sound of his roar they became fearful and anxious,
and they saw <s>Hanūmat</s> towering like an evening cloud.
Then those <s>rākṣasas</s>, confident in their master's command, attacked the monkey
from every side with varied and dreadful weapons.

children.text: sa taiḥ parivṛtaḥ śūraiḥ sarvataḥ sa mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: Surrounded on every side by those brave warriors, that mighty one
came upon a dreadful iron bar resting by the gateway.

children.text: sa taṃ parigham ādāya jaghāna rajanīcarān ||
children.translated_text: Taking up that bar, he struck down the night-roamers.
Like the son of <s>Vinatā</s> taking up a writhing serpent,
the heroic son of the Wind moved through the sky, holding that bar.
After slaying the heroic <s>rākṣasas</s>, the <s>Kiṃkaras</s>, <s>Mārutātmaja</s>,
still eager for battle, again took his place at the gateway.
Then a few <s>rākṣasas</s> there, freed from that fear,
reported to <s>Rāvaṇa</s> that all the <s>Kiṃkaras</s> had been slain.

children.text: sa rākṣasānāṃ nihataṃ mahābalaṃ niśamya rājā parivṛttalocanaḥ
children.translated_text: When the king heard that the mighty force of the <s>rākṣasas</s> had been slain, his eyes rolled,
and he commanded the son of <s>Prahasta</s>, matchless in valor and very hard to conquer in battle.

children.text: tataḥ sa kiṃkarān hatvā hanūmān dhyānam āsthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after killing the <s>Kiṃkaras</s>, <s>Hanūmān</s> entered into reflection:

children.text: vanaṃ bhagnaṃ mayā caityaprāsādo na vināśitaḥ
children.translated_text: "The grove has been broken by me, but the caitya-prāsāda has not been destroyed.
Therefore I shall demolish this palace as well, just in this way."
Having thus considered, <s>Hanumān</s>, resolving in his mind to display his strength,
leapt upon the caitya-prāsāda, lofty like the peak of <s>Meru</s>,
and <s>Hanūmān</s>, best of monkeys and son of the Wind, climbed it.
Having violently shaken the lofty and hard-to-assail caitya-prāsāda,
<s>Hanūmān</s>, blazing with splendor, became like <s>Pāriyātra</s>.
Then <s>Hanūmān</s>, the son of the Wind, assumed a huge body
and struck his arms defiantly, filling <s>Laṅkā</s> with the sound.
At the great, ear-splitting sound of his arm-slap,
birds fell from the sky, and he loudly proclaimed this:
"Victorious is mighty <s>Rāma</s>, and mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> too!
Victorious is king <s>Sugrīva</s>, protected by <s>Rāghava</s>!
I am the servant of <s>Rāma</s>, lord of <s>Kosala</s>, whose action is unwearied;
<s>Hanūmān</s>, son of the Wind, destroyer of enemy armies.

children.text: na rāvaṇasahasraṃ me yuddhe pratibalaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Not even a thousand <s>Rāvaṇas</s> would be a match for me in battle
as I strike with stones and with trees by the thousand.

children.text: ardayitvā purīṃ laṅkām abhivādya ca maithilīm
children.translated_text: Having crushed the city of <s>Laṅkā</s> and paid homage to <s>Maithilī</s>,
I shall go, my purpose accomplished, while all the <s>rākṣasas</s> look on.
Having spoken thus, the foremost of monkeys, standing in the aerial palace at the shrine,
roared with a terrifying sound, producing fear among the <s>rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: tena śabdena mahatā caityapālāḥ śataṃ yayuḥ
children.translated_text: At that great sound a hundred guardians of the shrine rushed forth.

children.text: gṛhītvā vividhān astrān prāsān khaḍgān paraśvadhān
children.translated_text: Taking various weapons, spears, swords, and battle-axes,
the great-bodied ones, hurling them, surrounded <s>Māruti</s>.
Like a vast, great whirlpool of the water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: parikṣipya hariśreṣṭhaṃ sa babhau rakṣasāṃ gaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the troop of <s>rākṣasas</s>, encircling the best of monkeys, appeared splendid.
Then the son of the Wind, enraged, assumed a terrible form.
From that great palace, a great pillar adorned with gold,
<s>Hanūmān</s>, the son of the Wind, uprooted with force,
and then that very strong one whirled it, with its hundred edges.
Having slain the hundred <s>rākṣasas</s>, as <s>Indra</s> slew the <s>asuras</s> with the thunderbolt,
the glorious one, standing in the sky, spoke these words:
"Thousands of great-hearted ones like me have been dispatched,
strong lords of monkeys who act under <s>Sugrīva</s>'s command.
With hundreds, with hundreds of thousands, with crores and even tens of thousands,
<s>Sugrīva</s> will come as the destroyer of you all.

children.text: neyam asti purī laṅkā na yūyaṃ na ca rāvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: This city <s>Laṅkā</s> will not exist, nor will you, nor will <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
because the great lord of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s> has made enmity with you."
