Commanded by the lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>, the strong son of <s>Prahasta</s>,
<s>Jambumālī</s>, with great fangs and bearing a bow, went forth.
Wearing red garlands and garments, garlanded, with beautiful earrings,
huge, with wide-open eyes, fierce, and hard to defeat in battle,
he swiftly drew a great bow resembling <s>Śakra</s>'s bow, fitted with beautiful arrows,
with a sound like the thunderbolt and the crash of lightning.
By the great twanging roar of his bow,
the quarters, the intermediate quarters, and the sky itself were suddenly filled.

children.text: rathena kharayuktena tam āgatam udīkṣya saḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing him arrive in a chariot yoked with donkeys,

children.text: hanūmān vegasampanno jaharṣa ca nanāda ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hanūmān</s>, endowed with speed, rejoiced and roared.
At <s>Hanūmān</s>, the great monkey standing on the archway turret,
the long-armed <s>Jambumālī</s> shot sharp arrows.
With a crescent-headed arrow he struck him in the face, and with one barbed arrow on the head;
with ten iron arrows he pierced the lord of monkeys in both arms.
His copper-colored face, struck by that arrow, shone beautifully,
like a blossoming lotus in autumn pierced by a ray of the sun.
The great monkey, struck by arrows, grew angry at the <s>rākṣasa</s>.
Then nearby he saw an exceedingly broad, great rock.

children.text: tarasā tāṃ samutpāṭya cikṣepa balavad balī
children.translated_text: With force the strong one uprooted it and hurled it powerfully.
The enraged <s>rākṣasa</s> struck it with ten arrows.
Seeing that effort ruined, <s>Hanūmān</s>, fierce in valor,
uprooted a great śāla tree and, full of strength, whirled it.
Seeing the very strong monkey whirling the śāla tree,
the mighty <s>Jambumālī</s> discharged very many arrows.
With four he cut apart the śāla tree; with five he struck the monkey on the arms,
with one arrow in the chest, and with ten between the breasts.

children.text: sa śaraiḥ pūritatanuḥ krodhena mahatā vṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: His body filled with arrows, enveloped by great anger,

children.text: tam eva parighaṃ gṛhya bhrāmayāmāsa vegitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he seized that same iron bar and swiftly whirled it.
Exceedingly swift and terrible in strength, he whirled it with extreme speed,
and brought the iron bar down upon <s>Jambumālī</s>'s great chest.

children.text: tasya caiva śiro nāsti na bāhū na ca jānunī
children.translated_text: There was no head of his, nor arms, nor knees;

children.text: na dhanur na ratho nāśvāstatrādṛśyanta neṣavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: no bow, no chariot, no horses, and no arrows were seen there.
Thus <s>Jambumālī</s>, the great chariot-warrior, was slain at once by him,
and, killed, fell to the ground with limbs and ornaments crushed.
Hearing that <s>Jambumālī</s> and the mighty kiṃkaras had been killed,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> became angry, his eyes reddened with wrath.
With coppery eyes rolled by fury at the death of <s>Prahasta</s>'s mighty son,
the lord of night-roamers quickly commanded the ministers' sons, men of surpassing courage and prowess.
Then, urged on by the lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>, those ministers' sons
went out from that palace, seven of them, with the splendor of the seven flames.
Surrounded by very strong retinues, bowmen and themselves very strong,
trained in weapons, foremost among those who know missiles, and each seeking victory over the others,
with great chariots adorned with golden netting, bearing standards and banners,
yoked with horses and rumbling with a sound like thunderclouds,
those of immeasurable prowess joyfully drew their bows, bright with refined gold,
like clouds accompanied by lightning.
Then their mothers, learning that the kiṃkaras had been killed,
became confused with grief, together with their kinsmen, relatives, and friends.
Those warriors, clashing against one another and adorned with refined gold,
rushed upon <s>Hanūmān</s>, who stood stationed on the archway.
Letting loose a rain of arrows, with the rumbling sound of their chariots,
those foremost <s>rākṣasas</s> moved about like rain-bearing clouds.
Then <s>Hanūmān</s>, covered by those showers of arrows,
became hidden in form, like the king of mountains by rains.

children.text: sa śarān vañcayāmāsa teṣām āśucaraḥ kapiḥ
children.translated_text: That swift-moving monkey eluded their arrows,
and the speed of the heroes' chariots, as he moved in the stainless sky.

children.text: sa taiḥ krīḍan dhanuṣmadbhir vyomni vīraḥ prakāśate
children.translated_text: Playing with those bowmen in the sky, the hero shone forth.

children.text: dhanuṣmadbhir yathā meghair mārutaḥ prabhur ambare ||
children.translated_text: as the wind is master in the sky among clouds armed, as it were, with bows.

children.text: sa kṛtvā ninadaṃ ghoraṃ trāsayaṃstāṃ mahācamūm
children.translated_text: Having made a terrible roar and terrifying that great army,

children.text: cakāra hanumān vegaṃ teṣu rakṣaḥsu vīryavān ||
children.translated_text: the mighty <s>Hanumān</s> rushed violently among those <s>rākṣasas</s>.
The scorcher of foes struck some with his palm and some with his feet;
he struck some with his fist and tore others apart with his nails.
The monkey crushed some with his chest and others with his thighs,

children.text: kecit tasyaiva nādena tatraiva patitā bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: and some, by his roar alone, fell there on the ground.
Then, when they had been struck down and had fallen to the earth,

children.text: tat sainyam agamat sarvaṃ diśo daśa bhayārditam ||
children.translated_text: that whole army, afflicted with fear, fled to the ten directions.

children.text: vinedur visvaraṃ nāgā nipetur bhuvi vājinaḥ
children.translated_text: Elephants trumpeted discordantly, and horses fell to the ground;
the earth was strewn with chariots whose seats, standards, and parasols were broken.

children.text: sa tān pravṛddhān vinihatya rākṣasān mahābalaścaṇḍaparākramaḥ kapiḥ
children.translated_text: Having slain those swollen-with-pride <s>rākṣasas</s>, the very powerful monkey of fierce valor

children.text: yuyutsur anyaiḥ punar eva rākṣasais tad eva vīro 'bhijagāma toraṇam ||
children.translated_text: again approached that same gateway, the hero eager to fight with other <s>rākṣasas</s>.
Learning that the ministers' sons had been slain by the great-souled monkey,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, concealing his outward expression, formed an excellent plan.
The Ten-necked one appointed <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, <s>Yūpākṣa</s>, and the <s>rākṣasa</s> <s>Durdhara</s>,
as well as <s>Praghasa</s> and <s>Bhāsakarṇa</s>, five foremost leaders of armies,
heroes skilled in policy,
intent on seizing <s>Hanumān</s> and equal to the wind in speed in battle.
'Go, all of you foremost leaders of the army, with your great forces,
with horses, chariots, and elephants; let that monkey be punished.'

children.text: yat taiśca khalu bhāvyaṃ syāt tam āsādya vanālayam
children.translated_text: 'And whatever should be considered by you after reaching that forest-dweller,
that deed must be carried out with due regard to place and time.'

children.text: na hyahaṃ taṃ kapiṃ manye karmaṇā pratitarkayan
children.translated_text: 'For, judging by his deed, I do not think that monkey
is in every respect an ordinary being; he is a great creature, possessed of immense strength.

children.text: bhaved indreṇa vā sṛṣṭam asmadarthaṃ tapobalāt ||
children.translated_text: Perhaps he was created by <s>Indra</s> through the power of austerity for our sake.'
'The gods, <s>asuras</s>, great seers, and those together with serpents, <s>yakṣas</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s>

children.text: yuṣmābhiḥ sahitaiḥ sarvair mayā saha vinirjitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: have all been conquered by you together, and by me as well.'

children.text: tair avaśyaṃ vidhātavyaṃ vyalīkaṃ kiṃcid eva naḥ
children.translated_text: 'By them some wrong must surely be devised against us;

children.text: tad eva nātra saṃdehaḥ prasahya parigṛhyatām ||
children.translated_text: therefore, without any doubt here, he must be forcibly captured.'
'And you must not underrate the monkey, whose valor is cruel;

children.text: dṛṣṭā hi harayaḥ śīghrā mayā vipulavikramāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for I have seen monkeys swift and possessed of vast prowess.'
'There is <s>Vālī</s>, together with <s>Sugrīva</s>, and the very mighty <s>Jāmbavān</s>,
and <s>Nīla</s> the commander, and others beginning with <s>Dvivida</s>.'

children.text: naiva teṣāṃ gatir bhīmā na tejo na parākramaḥ
children.translated_text: 'But among them there is not such fearsome movement, nor splendor, nor valor,

children.text: na matir na balotsāho na rūpaparikalpanam ||
children.translated_text: nor such intelligence, nor strength and energy, nor such power of assuming forms.'

children.text: mahat sattvam idaṃ jñeyaṃ kapirūpaṃ vyavasthitam
children.translated_text: 'This should be known as some great being, established in the form of a monkey;

children.text: prayatnaṃ mahad āsthāya kriyatām asya nigrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: making a great effort, bring about his restraint.'
'Though indeed the three worlds, with <s>Indra</s>, with gods, <s>asuras</s>, and men,

children.text: bhavatām agrataḥ sthātuṃ na paryāptā raṇājire ||
children.translated_text: would not be sufficient to stand before you on the battlefield,

children.text: tathāpi tu nayajñena jayam ākāṅkṣatā raṇe
children.translated_text: nevertheless, by one who knows policy and desires victory in battle,

children.text: ātmā rakṣyaḥ prayatnena yuddhasiddhir hi cañcalā ||
children.translated_text: one's own self must be protected with effort, for success in war is unstable.'
All those warriors of great vigor accepted their master's command,
and sprang up with great speed, equal in splendor to sacrificial fire.
With chariots, with intoxicated elephants, and with very swift horses,
with various sharp weapons, and all furnished with forces,
those heroes then saw the great monkey blazing,
like the rising sun, ray-bearing and garlanded with rays of his own splendor.
He stood at the gateway, immensely swift, great in being, very strong,
great in mind, great in energy, huge-bodied, and very powerful.

children.text: taṃ samīkṣyaiva te sarve dikṣu sarvāsvavasthitāḥ
children.translated_text: As soon as they beheld him, all of them took positions in every direction,
and from every side attacked him with their various terrible weapons.
Five sharp iron arrows, white and yellow-tipped,
resembling blue-lotus petals at their heads, were shot by <s>Durdhara</s> at his head.

children.text: sa taiḥ pañcabhir āviddhaḥ śaraiḥ śirasi vānaraḥ
children.translated_text: Pierced in the head by those five arrows, the monkey

children.text: utpapāta nadan vyomni diśo daśa vinādayan ||
children.translated_text: leapt up roaring into the sky, making the ten directions resound.
Then the heroic <s>Durdhara</s>, in his chariot and with his bow strung,
rushed against the mighty one, scattering many hundreds of arrows.

children.text: sa kapir vārayāmāsa taṃ vyomni śaravarṣiṇam
children.translated_text: The monkey checked him as he poured down arrows in the sky,
as the wind checks a rain-laden cloud at the end of the rainy season.
Then, being assailed by <s>Durdhara</s>, the son of the Wind

children.text: cakāra ninadaṃ bhūyo vyavardhata ca vegavān ||
children.translated_text: roared again and, full of speed, increased in size.

children.text: sa dūraṃ sahasotpatya durdharasya rathe hariḥ
children.translated_text: Suddenly leaping far away, the monkey, with tremendous speed,
fell upon <s>Durdhara</s>'s chariot like a mass of lightning on a mountain.
Then <s>Durdhara</s>, his eight horses crushed and his chariot with axle and pole broken,
abandoned that chariot and fell to the ground, his life gone.
Seeing him fallen on the earth, <s>Virūpākṣa</s> and <s>Yūpākṣa</s>,
angered and unassailable, sprang up, those two subduers of foes.
The monkey, having suddenly leapt up and stationed himself in the clear sky,
was struck on the chest with two clubs by those two swift, great-armed warriors.
Having checked the rush of those two impetuous warriors, the very powerful one,
whose valor equaled <s>Suparṇa</s>'s, fell back again to the ground.

children.text: sa sālavṛkṣam āsādya samutpāṭya ca vānaraḥ
children.translated_text: Then the monkey reached a <s>sāla</s> tree and tore it up,
and the son of the Wind slew both those heroic <s>rākṣasas</s>.
Then, knowing that those three had been slain by the forceful monkey,
the very swift <s>Praghasa</s> attacked the monkey forcibly.
<s>Bhāsakarṇa</s> too, enraged and powerful, took up a spear,
and the two stood on either side of the illustrious tiger among monkeys.
<s>Praghasa</s> struck him with a sharp-pointed paṭṭiśa,
and <s>Bhāsakarṇa</s>, the <s>rākṣasa</s>, struck the best of monkeys with his spear.
With his limbs wounded by those two, and the hair of his body smeared with blood,
the monkey became enraged, shining like the young sun.
Tearing up a mountain peak along with deer, beasts, and trees,
the heroic <s>Hanumān</s>, elephant among monkeys, killed the two <s>rākṣasas</s>.
Then, when those five commanders had fallen,

children.text: balaṃ tad avaśeṣaṃ tu nāśayāmāsa vānaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: the monkey destroyed the rest of that army.

children.text: aśvair aśvān gajair nāgān yodhair yodhān rathai rathān
children.translated_text: With horses he destroyed horses, with elephants elephants, with warriors warriors, and with chariots chariots;
that monkey destroyed them as <s>Sahasrākṣa</s> destroyed the <s>asuras</s>.
With elephants slain, with horses slain, and with great chariots whose axles were broken,
and with <s>rākṣasas</s> slain, the earth was blocked on every side.

children.text: tataḥ kapistān dhvajinīpatīn raṇe nihatya vīrān sabalān savāhanān
children.translated_text: Then, having slain in battle those heroic lords of armies together with their forces and vehicles,

children.text: tad eva vīraḥ parigṛhya toraṇaṃ kṛtakṣaṇaḥ kāla iva prajākṣaye ||
children.translated_text: the hero grasped that same gateway arch and, having found his moment, stood like Time at the destruction of creatures.

children.text: senāpatīn pañca sa tu pramāpitān hanūmatā sānucarān savāhanān
children.translated_text: Seeing the five commanders killed by <s>Hanumān</s>, together with their attendants and vehicles,

children.text: samīkṣya rājā samaroddhatonmukhaṃ kumāram akṣaṃ prasamaikṣatākṣatam ||
children.translated_text: the king looked intently at the unharmed prince <s>Akṣa</s>, whose face was turned toward the swelling battle.
Impelled by the casting of his gaze, the valiant one with a bow variegated with gold
then leapt up, urged by the assembly, like fire kindled by the chief twice-born for the oblation.
Then, mounting a great chariot shining like the young sun, covered with a lattice of heated jāmbūnada gold,

children.text: rathaṃ samāsthāya yayau sa vīryavān mahāhariṃ taṃ prati nairṛtarṣabhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that valiant bull among <s>rākṣasas</s> went toward the great monkey.
Then there was the chariot, won by the accumulated store gathered through ascetic power, adorned with a lattice of heated jāmbūnada gold,
bearing standards, with a jewel-adorned banner, well yoked with eight excellent horses swift as thought,
unassailable by gods and <s>asuras</s>, moving unobstructed, sun-bright, sky-going, and steady,
equipped with a quiver, beautiful with eight swords fastened on, and with śaktis and tomaras set in order.
It shone with its full equipment, with golden garlands, and with the brilliance of moon and sun;
then, mounted on that sunlike chariot, he of godlike prowess went forth.

children.text: sa pūrayan khaṃ ca mahīṃ ca sācalāṃ turaṃgamataṅgamahārathasvanaiḥ
children.translated_text: Filling the sky and the earth with its mountains with the sound of horses, elephants, and great chariots,

children.text: balaiḥ sametaiḥ sa hi toraṇasthitaṃ samartham āsīnam upāgamat kapim ||
children.translated_text: he approached with assembled forces the capable monkey seated at the gateway.

children.text: sa taṃ samāsādya hariṃ harīkṣaṇo yugāntakālāgnim iva prajākṣaye
children.translated_text: Coming up to that monkey as he stood like the fire of the end of the age at the destruction of creatures,
the tawny-eyed <s>Akṣa</s>, filled with wonder and agitation, gazed at him with eyes of respect.

children.text: sa tasya vegaṃ ca kaper mahātmanaḥ parākramaṃ cāriṣu pārthivātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: The mighty prince considered the speed of that great-souled monkey and his prowess against enemies,

children.text: vicārayan khaṃ ca balaṃ mahābalo himakṣaye sūrya ivābhivardhate ||
children.translated_text: and, mighty in strength, he grew in the sky and in power like the sun when winter comes to an end.

children.text: sa jātamanyuḥ prasamīkṣya vikramaṃ sthiraḥ sthitaḥ saṃyati durnivāraṇam
children.translated_text: His anger arose; seeing that irresistible valor, he stood firm in battle,

children.text: samāhitātmā hanumantam āhave pracodayāmāsa śaraistribhiḥ śitaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and with composed mind he drove three sharp arrows against <s>Hanumān</s> in the fight.

children.text: tataḥ kapiṃ taṃ prasamīkṣya garvitaṃ jitaśramaṃ śatruparājayorjitam
children.translated_text: Then, seeing that monkey proud, free from fatigue, and energized by the defeat of his foes,
<s>Akṣa</s>, his spirit aroused, looked on with arrow in hand and bow grasped.
Adorned with golden niṣkas, armlets, and fine earrings, swift in valor, he approached the monkey,

children.text: tayor babhūvāpratimaḥ samāgamaḥ surāsurāṇām api saṃbhramapradaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and between those two there arose an incomparable meeting, causing alarm even among gods and <s>asuras</s>.

children.text: rarāsa bhūmir na tatāpa bhānumān vavau na vāyuḥ pracacāla cācalaḥ
children.translated_text: The earth roared, the sun gave no heat, the wind did not blow, and the immovable mountain shook;

children.text: kapeḥ kumārasya ca vīkṣya saṃyugaṃ nanāda ca dyaur udadhiśca cukṣubhe ||
children.translated_text: seeing the combat of the monkey and the prince, heaven resounded and the ocean was disturbed.

children.text: tataḥ sa vīraḥ sumukhān patatriṇaḥ suvarṇapuṅkhān saviṣān ivoragān
children.translated_text: Then that hero loosed handsome feathered arrows, with golden tails, like venomous serpents,
and, knowing the truth of concentration, joining, and release, he dropped three arrows upon the monkey's head.

children.text: sa taiḥ śarair mūrdhni samaṃ nipātitaiḥ kṣarann asṛgdigdhavivṛttalocanaḥ
children.translated_text: With those arrows fallen together on his head, streaming blood and with blood-smeared rolling eyes,
he shone like the newly risen sun, bearing arrow-rays, like the sun garlanded with beams.

children.text: tataḥ sa piṅgādhipamantrisattamaḥ samīkṣya taṃ rājavarātmajaṃ raṇe
children.translated_text: Then that best minister of the lord of tawny monkeys, seeing that royal prince in battle,
with lofty, wondrous weapons and a variegated bow, rejoiced and swelled up, eager for combat.
Like the ray-bearing sun standing on the peak of <s>Mandara</s>, he, his anger grown and endowed with strength and valor,

children.text: kumāram akṣaṃ sabalaṃ savāhanaṃ dadāha netrāgnimarīcibhistadā ||
children.translated_text: then burned prince <s>Akṣa</s>, with his forces and vehicles, by the rays of the fire of his eyes.

children.text: tataḥ sa bāṇāsanaśakrakārmukaḥ śarapravarṣo yudhi rākṣasāmbudaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the <s>rākṣasa</s> cloud in battle, whose bow was like <s>Indra</s>'s bow and whose shower was arrows,
quickly released arrows at the mountain that was the lord of monkeys, as a raincloud releases rain upon the finest mountain.
Then the monkey, seeing in combat prince <s>Akṣa</s>, fierce in battle, whose arrows grew in splendor, strength, and valor,

children.text: kumāram akṣaṃ prasamīkṣya saṃyuge nanāda harṣād ghanatulyavikramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: roared with joy, his prowess like that of a thundercloud.

children.text: sa bālabhāvād yudhi vīryadarpitaḥ pravṛddhamanyuḥ kṣatajopamekṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Through his youthful nature, proud of his valor in battle, his anger increased and his eyes resembling blood,

children.text: samāsasādāpratimaṃ raṇe kapiṃ gajo mahākūpam ivāvṛtaṃ tṛṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: he approached the peerless monkey in battle like an elephant approaching a great pit covered with grass.

children.text: sa tena bāṇaiḥ prasabhaṃ nipātitaiś cakāra nādaṃ ghananādaniḥsvanaḥ
children.translated_text: Struck forcibly by those arrows as they fell, he gave a roar with the sound of a thundercloud,
and <s>Māruti</s> quickly sprang up into the sky, terrible to behold with the tossing of his arms and thighs.

children.text: samutpatantaṃ samabhidravad balī sa rākṣasānāṃ pravaraḥ pratāpavān
children.translated_text: As he leapt up, the strong and mighty foremost one among the <s>rākṣasas</s> rushed against him,

children.text: rathī rathaśreṣṭhatamaḥ kirañ śaraiḥ payodharaḥ śailam ivāśmavṛṣṭibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: a chariot-warrior, best of excellent chariot-fighters, scattering arrows like a cloud showering stones upon a mountain.

children.text: sa tāñ śarāṃstasya vimokṣayan kapiś cacāra vīraḥ pathi vāyusevite
children.translated_text: Loosing himself from those arrows of his, the heroic monkey moved along the path traveled by the wind,

children.text: śarāntare mārutavad viniṣpatan manojavaḥ saṃyati caṇḍavikramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: darting out between the arrows like the wind, swift as thought and fierce in valor in battle.

children.text: tam āttabāṇāsanam āhavonmukhaṃ kham āstṛṇantaṃ vividhaiḥ śarottamaiḥ
children.translated_text: The son of the Wind saw <s>Akṣa</s>, bow and arrows in hand, facing battle, covering the sky with various excellent arrows,

children.text: avaikṣatākṣaṃ bahumānacakṣuṣā jagāma cintāṃ ca sa mārutātmajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and he looked upon him with eyes of respect and fell into thought.

children.text: tataḥ śarair bhinnabhujāntaraḥ kapiḥ kumāravaryeṇa mahātmanā nadan
children.translated_text: Then the monkey, pierced in the chest by arrows from that noble young prince, roared aloud,
and the great-armed one, knowing the true nature of exceptional deeds, reflected on his prowess in battle.
"Though he is a boy, this greatly powerful one does not act like a boy; shining like the young sun, he performs a great deed.

children.text: na cāsya sarvāhavakarmaśobhinaḥ pramāpaṇe me matir atra jāyate ||
children.translated_text: And here no thought arises in me to kill this one, who is splendid in every action of battle.

children.text: ayaṃ mahātmā ca mahāṃśca vīryataḥ samāhitaścātisahaśca saṃyuge
children.translated_text: This great-souled one is great in heroism, collected, and exceedingly capable in combat.

children.text: asaṃśayaṃ karmaguṇodayād ayaṃ sanāgayakṣair munibhiśca pūjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Without doubt, by the rise of his deeds and virtues, he is honored by serpents, <s>yakṣas</s>, and sages.
His mind enlarged by valor and energy, he stands before me and watches me face to face.

children.text: parākramo hyasya manāṃsi kampayet surāsurāṇām api śīghrakāriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For his swiftly acting prowess would shake even the minds of gods and <s>asuras</s>.

children.text: na khalvayaṃ nābhibhaved upekṣitaḥ parākramo hyasya raṇe vivardhate
children.translated_text: Surely this one, if disregarded, would not fail to overpower me; for his prowess grows in battle.

children.text: pramāpaṇaṃ tveva mamāsya rocate na vardhamāno 'gnir upekṣituṃ kṣamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore killing him is what pleases me; a fire that is increasing cannot be disregarded."

children.text: iti pravegaṃ tu parasya tarkayan svakarmayogaṃ ca vidhāya vīryavān
children.translated_text: Thus judging the rush of his opponent and setting his own proper action in order, the heroic one

children.text: cakāra vegaṃ tu mahābalastadā matiṃ ca cakre 'sya vadhe mahākapiḥ ||
children.translated_text: then put on speed, and the mighty great monkey resolved upon his death.

children.text: sa tasya tān aṣṭahayānmahājavān samāhitān bhārasahān vivartane
children.translated_text: The heroic monkey, the son of the Wind, struck down his eight very swift horses, well-trained, able to bear burdens and turn about,

children.text: jaghāna vīraḥ pathi vāyusevite talaprahāraiḥ pavanātmajaḥ kapiḥ ||
children.translated_text: with blows from his palms on the path traveled by the wind.
Then that great chariot of his, struck by the palm and destroyed by the minister of the tawny lord,

children.text: sa bhagnanīḍaḥ parimuktakūbaraḥ papāta bhūmau hatavājir ambarāt ||
children.translated_text: its body broken and its yoke-pole cast loose, fell from the sky to the earth, its horses slain.

children.text: sa taṃ parityajya mahāratho rathaṃ sakārmukaḥ khaḍgadharaḥ kham utpatat
children.translated_text: Leaving that chariot, the great chariot-warrior, still with his bow and holding his sword, leapt into the sky,

children.text: tapo'bhiyogād ṛṣir ugravīryavān vihāya dehaṃ marutām ivālayam ||
children.translated_text: like a sage of fierce power, through the discipline of austerity, leaving the body for the abode of the <s>Maruts</s>.
Then the monkey came upon him as he moved in the sky, on the path frequented by the king of birds, the wind, and the <s>siddhas</s>,

children.text: sametya taṃ mārutavegavikramaḥ krameṇa jagrāha ca pādayor dṛḍham ||
children.translated_text: and, with prowess as swift as the wind, firmly seized him by both feet.

children.text: sa taṃ samāvidhya sahasraśaḥ kapir mahoragaṃ gṛhya ivāṇḍajeśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Swinging him around thousands of times, like <s>Garuḍa</s>, lord of birds, seizing a great serpent,

children.text: mumoca vegāt pitṛtulyavikramo mahītale saṃyati vānarottamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the best of monkeys, equal in prowess to his father, hurled him forcefully to the earth in battle.
With arms, thighs, hips, and neck broken, streaming blood, with bones and eyes crushed,

children.text: sa bhinnasaṃdhiḥ pravikīrṇabandhano hataḥ kṣitau vāyusutena rākṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: with joints split and sinews scattered, the <s>rākṣasa</s> lay slain on the ground by the son of the Wind.

children.text: mahākapir bhūmitale nipīḍya taṃ cakāra rakṣo'dhipater mahad bhayam ||
children.translated_text: Crushing him on the surface of the earth, the great monkey caused great fear in the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>.
When the prince had been slain, that monkey was watched by great-vowed great sages who move through the sky, by beings together with <s>yakṣas</s> and serpents,

children.text: suraiśca sendrair bhṛśajātavismayair hate kumāre sa kapir nirīkṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and by the gods with <s>Indra</s>, all filled with intense astonishment.

children.text: nihatya taṃ vajrisutopamaprabhaṃ kumāram akṣaṃ kṣatajopamekṣaṇam
children.translated_text: After slaying prince <s>Akṣa</s>, whose splendor was like that of the son of the thunderbolt-bearer and whose eyes were like blood,

children.text: tad eva vīro 'bhijagāma toraṇaṃ kṛtakṣaṇaḥ kāla iva prajākṣaye ||
children.translated_text: the hero went back to that very gateway, having made his moment, like <s>Kāla</s> at the destruction of creatures.

children.text: tatastu rakṣo'dhipatir mahātmā hanūmatākṣe nihate kumāre
children.translated_text: Then the great-souled lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, when prince <s>Akṣa</s> had been slain by <s>Hanumān</s>,

children.text: manaḥ samādhāya tadendrakalpaṃ samādideśendrajitaṃ sa roṣāt ||
children.translated_text: composed his mind and, in anger, commanded <s>Indrajit</s>, who was like <s>Indra</s>:

children.text: tvam astravicchastrabhṛtāṃ variṣṭhaḥ surāsurāṇām api śokadātā
children.translated_text: "You know the missiles; you are foremost among bearers of weapons, a giver of grief even to gods and <s>asuras</s>.
Your deeds have been seen among the gods together with <s>Indra</s>; your missiles have been amassed through worship of the Grandfather <s>Brahmā</s>.
Having encountered the strength of your missiles, neither the <s>asuras</s> nor the hosts of <s>Maruts</s>,

children.text: na kaścit triṣu lokeṣu saṃyuge na gataśramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor anyone in the three worlds, has failed to grow weary in battle.
Guarded by the heroism of your arms and protected by austerity,
you know the divisions of place and time; you alone are best in judgment.

children.text: na te 'styaśakyaṃ samareṣu karmaṇā na te 'styakāryaṃ matipūrvamantraṇe
children.translated_text: There is no deed impossible for you in battles; there is no course beyond you in counsel preceded by thought.

children.text: na so 'sti kaścit triṣu saṃgraheṣu vai na veda yaste 'strabalaṃ balaṃ ca te ||
children.translated_text: There is no one at all in the threefold conflicts who does not know your missile-power and your strength.

children.text: mamānurūpaṃ tapaso balaṃ ca te parākramaścāstrabalaṃ ca saṃyuge
children.translated_text: Your power of austerity, strength, prowess, and missile-power in battle are equal to mine.

children.text: na tvāṃ samāsādya raṇāvamarde manaḥ śramaṃ gacchati niścitārtham ||
children.translated_text: When my mind has reached you in the crushing press of battle, fixed upon its goal, it does not grow weary.

children.text: nihatāḥ kiṃkarāḥ sarve jambumālī ca rākṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: All the <s>kiṃkaras</s> have been slain, and the <s>rākṣasa</s> <s>Jambumālī</s> too,
as well as the heroic sons of ministers, and the five who went at the head of the army.
Your beloved brother, prince <s>Akṣa</s>, has been killed,

children.text: na tu teṣveva me sāro yastvayyariniṣūdana ||
children.translated_text: but my true reliance was not in them as it is in you, O crusher of enemies.

children.text: idaṃ hi dṛṣṭvā matimanmahad balaṃ kapeḥ prabhāvaṃ ca parākramaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Therefore, O wise one, seeing this great strength of the monkey, and his might and prowess,

children.text: tvam ātmanaścāpi samīkṣya sāraṃ kuruṣva vegaṃ svabalānurūpam ||
children.translated_text: and also considering the substance of your own power, act swiftly in a way suited to your strength.

children.text: balāvamardastvayi saṃnikṛṣṭe yathā gate śāmyati śāntaśatrau
children.translated_text: When you are close at hand and have gone forth, the crushing of our force subsides, O one whose enemies are pacified.

children.text: tathā samīkṣyātmabalaṃ paraṃ ca samārabhasvāstravidāṃ variṣṭha ||
children.translated_text: So, having weighed your own strength and that of the enemy, begin, O foremost knower of missiles.

children.text: na khalviyaṃ matiḥ śreṣṭhā yat tvāṃ saṃpreṣayāmyaham
children.translated_text: Yet this is certainly not the best judgment, that I am sending you."

children.text: iyaṃ ca rājadharmāṇāṃ kṣatrasya ca matir matā ||
children.translated_text: And this is regarded as the proper understanding of royal duties and of the warrior estate:
skill with many kinds of weapons in battle, O subduer of foes,

children.text: avaśyam eva boddhavyaṃ kāmyaśca vijayo raṇe ||
children.translated_text: must certainly be learned, and victory in war must be desired.

children.text: tataḥ pitustad vacanaṃ niśamya pradakṣiṇaṃ dakṣasutaprabhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, hearing those words of his father, the hero of unfailing spirit, endowed with mighty prowess,

children.text: cakāra bhartāram adīnasattvo raṇāya vīraḥ pratipannabuddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: circumambulated his lord, having fixed his mind on battle.
Then <s>Indrajit</s>, honored by those dear troops of his own,
his zeal raised high for combat, entered upon the battle.
The glorious, lotus-petal-eyed son of the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>,
of great splendor, went forth like the ocean on the days of its swelling tides.
<s>Indrajit</s>, equal to <s>Indra</s>, mounted a chariot yoked with four fierce beasts
whose speed was like that of the king of birds, white, sharp-fanged, and moving with unhindered swiftness.

children.text: sa rathī dhanvināṃ śreṣṭhaḥ śastrajño 'stravidāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: That chariot-warrior, the best of bowmen, expert in weapons and foremost among those who know missiles,
quickly advanced by chariot to the place where <s>Hanumān</s> was.

children.text: sa tasya rathanirghoṣaṃ jyāsvanaṃ kārmukasya ca
children.translated_text: Hearing the roar of his chariot and the twang of his bowstring and bow,
that heroic monkey became still more delighted.
Taking up a very great bow and arrows with sharp points,
the master of battle went forth with <s>Hanumān</s> in mind.

children.text: tasmiṃstataḥ saṃyati jātaharṣe raṇāya nirgacchati bāṇapāṇau
children.translated_text: Then, as he went out to fight, delighted in battle, arrow in hand,

children.text: diśaśca sarvāḥ kaluṣā babhūvur mṛgāśca raudrā bahudhā vineduḥ ||
children.translated_text: all the quarters became turbid, and dreadful beasts cried out in many ways.
Nāgas, yakṣas, great seers, siddhas moving in their circles,

children.text: nabhaḥ samāvṛtya ca pakṣisaṃghā vinedur uccaiḥ paramaprahṛṣṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and flocks of birds gathered there, covering the sky, and cried out loudly in great delight.

children.text: āyantaṃ sarathaṃ dṛṣṭvā tūrṇam indrajitaṃ kapiḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Indrajit</s> coming swiftly with his chariot, the monkey
uttered a great roar and, full of speed, grew in size.
But <s>Indrajit</s>, mounted on his divine chariot and bearing a variegated bow,
made his bow resound with a noise powerful as thunder.
Then the two met, exceedingly swift, very strong, and fearless in battle:
the monkey and the son of the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, like the lords of gods and <s>asuras</s> locked in enmity.

children.text: sa tasya vīrasya mahārathasya dhanuṣmataḥ saṃyati saṃmatasya
children.translated_text: In that fight he frustrated the arrow-speed of that heroic, great chariot-warrior,

children.text: śarapravegaṃ vyahanat pravṛddhaś cacāra mārge pitur aprameyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: renowned in battle and armed with a bow; grown large, he moved immeasurably in his father's path.
Then the hero, the slayer of enemy heroes, released arrows
long, sharp-pointed, well feathered, with shafts marked in gold, well joined together and swift as falling thunderbolts.

children.text: sa tasya tat syandananiḥsvanaṃ ca mṛdaṅgabherīpaṭahasvanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Hearing the noise of his chariot, the sounds of mṛdaṅgas, bherīs, and paṭahas,

children.text: vikṛṣyamāṇasya ca kārmukasya niśamya ghoṣaṃ punar utpapāta ||
children.translated_text: and the twang of the bow as it was drawn, he leapt up again.
The great monkey quickly moved among the spaces between the arrows,
and though he was the target, the monkey made him lose his grasp of the target.
Again he turned about before the points of his arrows;
stretching out his hands, <s>Hanumān</s>, the son of the Wind, leapt up.
Those two, both endowed with speed and skilled in the work of battle,
performed a supreme combat that seized the minds of all beings.

children.text: hanūmato veda na rākṣaso 'ntaraṃ na mārutistasya mahātmano 'ntaram
children.translated_text: The <s>rākṣasa</s> found no opening in <s>Hanumān</s>, nor did <s>Māruti</s> find an opening in that great-souled one;

children.text: parasparaṃ nirviṣahau babhūvatuḥ sametya tau devasamānavikramau ||
children.translated_text: meeting one another, those two of godlike prowess became unable to overcome each other.

children.text: tatastu lakṣye sa vihanyamāne śareṣu mogheṣu ca saṃpatatsu
children.translated_text: Then, when the target was being thwarted and the arrows were falling in vain,
the great-souled one fell into deep thought, his mind concentrated through the discipline of collected attention.

children.text: tato matiṃ rākṣasarājasūnuś cakāra tasmin harivīramukhye
children.translated_text: Then the son of the king of <s>rākṣasas</s> formed a plan regarding that foremost heroic monkey:

children.text: avadhyatāṃ tasya kapeḥ samīkṣya kathaṃ nigacched iti nigrahārtham ||
children.translated_text: having observed that the monkey could not be killed, he considered how he might be brought under control.

children.text: tataḥ paitāmahaṃ vīraḥ so 'stram astravidāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: Then that hero, foremost among those who know missiles and very mighty in splendor,
set the weapon of <s>Pitāmaha</s> against that best of monkeys.
Knowing, 'This one cannot be slain,' <s>Indrajit</s>, who knew the truth of missiles,
restrained the son of the Wind with that weapon, he of mighty arms.
Then the monkey, bound by that weapon by the <s>rākṣasa</s>,
became motionless and fell upon the ground.

children.text: tato 'tha buddhvā sa tadāstrabandhaṃ prabhoḥ prabhāvād vigatālpavegaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, understanding that bond of the weapon and that a little of his speed had departed through the lord's power,
the heroic monkey reflected on <s>Pitāmaha</s>'s favor toward him.
<s>Hanumān</s> thought about the <s>Brahmāstra</s>, empowered by svāyambhuva mantras,
and about the boon granted by <s>Pitāmaha</s>.

children.text: na me 'strabandhasya ca śaktir asti vimokṣaṇe lokaguroḥ prabhāvāt
children.translated_text: 'I have no power to free myself from the bond of this weapon, because of the power of the teacher of the worlds;
therefore, bound by this weapon in this way, I must obey the Self-born one.'

children.text: sa vīryam astrasya kapir vicārya pitāmahānugraham ātmanaśca
children.translated_text: Having considered the power of the weapon, and <s>Pitāmaha</s>'s favor toward him,
and having reflected on his power of release, the monkey obeyed <s>Pitāmaha</s>'s command.

children.text: astreṇāpi hi baddhasya bhayaṃ mama na jāyate
children.translated_text: 'Even while bound by the weapon, no fear arises in me,
for I am protected by <s>Pitāmaha</s> and <s>Mahendra</s>, and by the Wind.
And in being seized by the <s>rākṣasas</s>, I see a great advantage:
there will be conversation with the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>; therefore let the enemies seize me.'
Resolved in purpose, slayer of enemy heroes, acting after careful thought, he ceased from movement;

children.text: paraiḥ prasahyābhigatair nigṛhya nanāda taistaiḥ paribhartsyamānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when enemies came upon him violently and seized him, he roared as they threatened him in many ways.
Then the <s>rākṣasas</s>, seeing that subduer of foes motionless...
They bound him with hempen fibers and with tightly gathered strips of tree-bark.

children.text: sa rocayāmāsa paraiśca bandhanaṃ prasahya vīrair abhinigrahaṃ ca
children.translated_text: He approved of that binding by his enemies, and of being forcibly seized by the heroes,

children.text: kautūhalānmāṃ yadi rākṣasendro draṣṭuṃ vyavasyed iti niścitārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: having fixed his purpose: "Perhaps, out of curiosity, the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s> will decide to see me."
Bound by that bark, the mighty one was released from the weapon's bond;

children.text: astrabandhaḥ sa cānyaṃ hi na bandham anuvartate ||
children.translated_text: for a bond made by an <s>astra</s> does not continue when there is another bond.

children.text: athendrajit taṃ drumacīrabandhaṃ vicārya vīraḥ kapisattamaṃ tam
children.translated_text: Then heroic <s>Indrajit</s>, considering that best of monkeys bound with strips of tree-bark,

children.text: vimuktam astreṇa jagāma cintām anyena baddho hyanuvartate 'stram ||
children.translated_text: became anxious, seeing him released from the <s>astra</s>; for one bound by another bond no longer remains under the weapon.

children.text: aho mahat karma kṛtaṃ nirarthakaṃ na rākṣasair mantragatir vimṛṣṭā
children.translated_text: "Alas, a great deed has been made useless; the <s>rākṣasas</s> did not reflect on the way of counsel.

children.text: punaśca nāstre vihate 'stram anyat pravartate saṃśayitāḥ sma sarve ||
children.translated_text: And once an <s>astra</s> has been thwarted, another <s>astra</s> cannot be set in motion; now we are all in doubt."
<s>Hanumān</s>, released by the <s>astra</s>, did not reveal his own condition;
but, being dragged by the <s>rākṣasas</s> and pressed by those bonds,
then, as he was struck by cruel <s>rākṣasas</s> with sticks and fists,
that monkey was dragged near the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: athendrajit taṃ prasamīkṣya muktam astreṇa baddhaṃ drumacīrasūtraiḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Indrajit</s>, seeing him released from the <s>astra</s> but bound with tree-bark cords,

children.text: vyadarśayat tatra mahābalaṃ taṃ haripravīraṃ sagaṇāya rājñe ||
children.translated_text: displayed that mighty champion of the monkeys there to the king together with his retinue.

children.text: taṃ mattam iva mātaṅgaṃ baddhaṃ kapivarottamam
children.translated_text: The <s>rākṣasas</s> reported to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>,
that foremost of excellent monkeys, bound like an intoxicated elephant.

children.text: ko 'yaṃ kasya kuto vāpi kiṃ kāryaṃ ko vyapāśrayaḥ
children.translated_text: "Who is this? Whose is he? From where has he come? What is his purpose? On whom does he rely?"
Such talks arose there among the <s>rākṣasa</s> heroes.

children.text: hanyatāṃ dahyatāṃ vāpi bhakṣyatām iti cāpare
children.translated_text: "Let him be killed, or burned, or eaten,"
other angry <s>rākṣasas</s> there said then to one another.

children.text: atītya mārgaṃ sahasā mahātmā sa tatra rakṣo'dhipapādamūle
children.translated_text: After swiftly passing along the way, that great-souled one came there to the foot of the lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: dadarśa rājñaḥ paricāravṛddhān gṛhaṃ mahāratnavibhūṣitaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: and saw the king's aged attendants and the palace adorned with great jewels.
The glorious <s>Rāvaṇa</s> saw that best of monkeys,
dragged this way and that by <s>rākṣasas</s> of distorted forms.
And that best of monkeys also saw the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>,
endowed with brilliance and strength, blazing like the sun.
Then ten-faced <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, his coppery eyes rolled with anger, looked over that monkey,

children.text: athopaviṣṭān kulaśīlavṛddhān samādiśat taṃ prati mantramukhyān ||
children.translated_text: and ordered his chief ministers, seated there, elders in family and conduct, regarding him.

children.text: yathākramaṃ taiḥ sa kapiśca pṛṣṭaḥ kāryārtham arthasya ca mūlam ādau
children.translated_text: Questioned in order by them, the monkey first explained the purpose of his mission and the root of the matter:

children.text: nivedayāmāsa harīśvarasya dūtaḥ sakāśād aham āgato 'smi ||
children.translated_text: "I have come from the presence of the lord of the monkeys as his messenger."

children.text: tataḥ sa karmaṇā tasya vismito bhīmavikramaḥ
children.translated_text: Then mighty <s>Hanumān</s>, terrible in valor, amazed by his power,
looked upon the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s> with eyes reddened by anger.
He was shining with a very costly golden crown, gleaming brightly,
covered with a net of pearls and of great splendor;
with golden ornaments, marvelous as if fashioned by thought,
made with priceless jewels joined together with diamonds;
clothed in very costly linen, reddened with red sandalwood,
well anointed with many varied and beautiful markings;
with broad, handsome eyes, red and fearsome to behold,
with great fangs blazing and sharp, and with long coverings over his teeth;
heroic, blazing, of great energy, with ten heads,
like <s>Mandara</s> with its peaks crowded with many serpents;
resembling a mass of dark collyrium, with a necklace shining on his chest,
and with a face like the full moon, like a cloud accompanied by cranes;
with stout arms fitted with armlets and reddened with the finest sandalwood,
shining with bracelets, like five-headed serpents;
seated on a great, variegated crystal throne,
inlaid with jewels and spread with the finest coverings;
served nearby on every side by exceedingly adorned women,
holding yak-tail fans in their hands;
with irresistible <s>Prahasta</s>, with <s>Mahāpārśva</s> the <s>rākṣasa</s>,
and with <s>Nikumbha</s> the minister, all ministers who knew the essence of counsel;
seated near him were four <s>rākṣasas</s> proud of their strength,

children.text: kṛtsnaiḥ parivṛtaṃ lokaṃ caturbhir iva sāgaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: as though the whole world were encircled by the four oceans;
and he was attended by ministers who knew the essence of counsel,
and by other advisers of auspicious understanding, like the lord of gods attended by the gods.
<s>Hanumān</s> beheld the exceedingly brilliant lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>,
set there like a water-filled cloud on the peak of <s>Meru</s>.
Though he was being pressed by those <s>rākṣasas</s> of fearsome valor,
he reached the highest astonishment and gazed at the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>.
Then, seeing the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s> blazing,
<s>Hanumān</s>, bewildered by his splendor, reflected in his mind:

children.text: aho rūpam aho dhairyam aho sattvam aho dyutiḥ
children.translated_text: "Ah, what beauty! Ah, what firmness! Ah, what strength! Ah, what radiance!
Ah, how the king of <s>rākṣasas</s> is endowed with every auspicious mark!

children.text: yadyadharmo na balavān syād ayaṃ rākṣaseśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: If <s>adharma</s> were not powerful in this lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>,
he would be the protector even of the world of the gods together with <s>Śakra</s>.
For that reason the worlds, with gods and <s>dānavas</s>, truly fear him;

children.text: ayaṃ hyutsahate kruddhaḥ kartum ekārṇavaṃ jagat ||
children.translated_text: for, when angered, he is capable of making the world into a single ocean."
Thus the wise monkey formed many kinds of thoughts,
after seeing the majesty of the <s>rākṣasa</s> king of immeasurable energy.

children.text: tam udvīkṣya mahābāhuḥ piṅgākṣaṃ purataḥ sthitam
children.translated_text: Seeing him, the mighty-armed <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, terror of the worlds, whose eyes were tawny, standing before him,
was possessed by great anger.
That king, his eyes copper-red with rage, addressed <s>Prahasta</s>, the best of ministers,
with these broad, meaningful words suited to the moment:

children.text: durātmā pṛcchyatām eṣa kutaḥ kiṃ vāsya kāraṇam
children.translated_text: 'Let this wicked-souled one be questioned: from where has he come, and what is his purpose?

children.text: vanabhaṅge ca ko 'syārtho rākṣasīnāṃ ca tarjane ||
children.translated_text: What aim has he in breaking the grove and in threatening the <s>rākṣasīs</s>?'

children.text: rāvaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā prahasto vākyam abravīt
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s words, <s>Prahasta</s> spoke this sentence:

children.text: samāśvasihi bhadraṃ te na bhīḥ kāryā tvayā kape ||
children.translated_text: 'Take heart. May it be well with you. You need not be afraid, monkey.

children.text: yadi tāvat tvam indreṇa preṣito rāvaṇālayam
children.translated_text: If you have indeed been sent by <s>Indra</s> to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s palace,

children.text: tattvam ākhyāhi mā te bhūd bhayaṃ vānara mokṣyase ||
children.translated_text: tell the truth; let there be no fear for you, monkey, and you shall be released.

children.text: yadi vaiśravaṇasya tvaṃ yamasya varuṇasya ca
children.translated_text: Or if you belong to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, or to <s>Yama</s> or <s>Varuṇa</s>,

children.text: cāru rūpam idaṃ kṛtvā yamasya varuṇasya ca ||
children.translated_text: having assumed this charming form, or to <s>Yama</s> or <s>Varuṇa</s>,
or if you are a messenger sent by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who seeks victory,

children.text: na hi te vānaraṃ tejo rūpamātraṃ tu vānaram ||
children.translated_text: for your splendor is not that of a monkey; only your form is that of a monkey.
Tell the truth fully today; then, monkey, you shall be released.
But if you speak falsely, your life will be hard to keep.
Or else tell for what reason you entered <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s palace.'
Thus addressed, the best of monkeys then spoke to the lord of the hosts of <s>rākṣasas</s>:
'I am not <s>Śakra</s>'s, nor <s>Yama</s>'s, nor <s>Varuṇa</s>'s.

children.text: dhanadena na me sakhyaṃ viṣṇunā nāsmi coditaḥ
children.translated_text: I have no friendship with the giver of wealth, nor have I been prompted by <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: jātir eva mama tveṣā vānaro 'ham ihāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: This indeed is my birth-species: I am a monkey, and I have come here.

children.text: darśane rākṣasendrasya durlabhe tad idaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: Since seeing the lord of <s>rākṣasas</s> is difficult,
I destroyed the grove of the king of <s>rākṣasas</s> for the sake of obtaining that audience.
Then your powerful <s>rākṣasas</s>, desiring battle, came upon me,

children.text: rakṣaṇārthaṃ ca dehasya pratiyuddhā mayā raṇe ||
children.translated_text: and for the protection of my body I fought them back in combat.

children.text: astrapāśair na śakyo 'haṃ baddhuṃ devāsurair api
children.translated_text: I cannot be bound with weapon-nooses even by gods and <s>asuras</s>;
this boon too was granted to me by the Grandfather.
Because I wished to see the king, I submitted to the missile.
Released by the missile, I was nevertheless greatly harassed by the <s>rākṣasas</s>.
Know me to be the messenger of <s>Rāghava</s>, whose power is immeasurable.

children.text: śrūyatāṃ cāpi vacanaṃ mama pathyam idaṃ prabho ||
children.translated_text: Hear also this beneficial word of mine, lord.
That best of monkeys, full of courage, looking upon that great being,
spoke to ten-faced <s>Rāvaṇa</s> a meaningful sentence, unperturbed:
'At <s>Sugrīva</s>'s command I have come here to your palace.
O lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>, the lord of monkeys, your brother, inquired after your welfare.
Hear the instruction of your brother, the great-souled <s>Sugrīva</s>,

children.text: dharmārthopahitaṃ vākyam iha cāmutra ca kṣamam ||
children.translated_text: a word joined with <s>dharma</s> (right order) and advantage, suitable both here and hereafter.
There was a king named <s>Daśaratha</s>, possessing chariots, elephants, and horses,
a father-like kinsman of the world, equal in brilliance to the lord of the gods.
His eldest son, mighty-armed, dear to him, and lordly,
went forth at his father's command and entered the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest.

children.text: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā sītayā cāpi bhāryayā
children.translated_text: Together with his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and with his wife <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: rāmo nāma mahātejā dharmyaṃ panthānam āśritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that greatly radiant one named <s>Rāma</s> followed the path of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: tasya bhāryā vane naṣṭā sītā patim anuvratā
children.translated_text: His wife, <s>Sītā</s>, devoted to her husband, was lost in the forest,
the daughter of the noble king <s>Janaka</s> of <s>Videha</s>.
Searching for that lady, the prince, together with his younger brother,
came to <s>Ṛśyamūka</s> and met with <s>Sugrīva</s>.
By him the search for <s>Sītā</s> was promised,
and by <s>Rāma</s> the kingdom of the monkeys was pledged to <s>Sugrīva</s>.
Then, after that prince slew <s>Vālin</s> in battle,
<s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the hosts of monkeys and bears, was established in the kingdom.
Intent on the search for <s>Sītā</s>, true to his compact,
<s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of monkeys, sent monkeys into all directions.

children.text: tāṃ harīṇāṃ sahasrāṇi śatāni niyutāni ca
children.translated_text: Thousands, hundreds, and countless hosts of those monkeys
are searching in all directions, below, above, and in the sky.
Some are equal to <s>Vainateya</s>, and some there are like the wind,
unobstructed in movement, swift, heroic monkeys of great strength.
I, however, am named <s>Hanumān</s>, the own son of the Wind.
For <s>Sītā</s>'s sake, swiftly, over a hundred yojanas in extent,
having crossed the ocean, I came here desiring to see her.
Therefore you, who have seen <s>dharma</s> and advantage and who have undertaken ascetic discipline,
ought not, great wise one, to confine another man's wife.
For wise men such as you do not attach themselves to deeds opposed to <s>dharma</s>,
full of many dangers and cutting at the very root.
And who, even among gods and <s>asuras</s>, is able to stand before
the arrows released by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, following upon <s>Rāma</s>'s wrath?

children.text: na cāpi triṣu lokeṣu rājan vidyeta kaścana
children.translated_text: Nor, king, is anyone found in the three worlds

children.text: rāghavasya vyalīkaṃ yaḥ kṛtvā sukham avāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: who, after doing wrong to <s>Rāghava</s>, could attain happiness.

children.text: tat trikālahitaṃ vākyaṃ dharmyam arthānubandhi ca
children.translated_text: Therefore consider this word, beneficial in all three times, righteous and linked with advantage:
let <s>Jānakī</s> be returned to the lord among men.

children.text: dṛṣṭā hīyaṃ mayā devī labdhaṃ yad iha durlabham
children.translated_text: For this lady has been seen by me; what was difficult to obtain here has been obtained.

children.text: uttaraṃ karma yaccheṣaṃ nimittaṃ tatra rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As for the further task that remains, <s>Rāghava</s> will be the cause there.
This <s>Sītā</s> has been found by me, and she is wholly given over to grief.

children.text: gṛhya yāṃ nābhijānāsi pañcāsyām iva pannagīm ||
children.translated_text: Having seized her, you do not recognize her as a five-headed serpent, as it were.

children.text: neyaṃ jarayituṃ śakyā sāsurair amarair api
children.translated_text: She cannot be digested even by the immortals together with the <s>asuras</s>,
like food greatly mixed with poison when eaten by a powerful man.
This possession of <s>dharma</s> of yours, gained through the heat of ascetic practice,
That which is bound up with one's own life should not rightly be destroyed.
As for the inviolability which you perceive for yourself through austerities,
even against the gods together with the <s>asuras</s>, there is this great reason in that matter too.

children.text: sugrīvo na hi devo 'yaṃ nāsuro na ca mānuṣaḥ
children.translated_text: For this <s>Sugrīva</s> is not a god, nor an <s>asura</s>, nor a human being;

children.text: na rākṣaso na gandharvo na yakṣo na ca pannagaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he is not a <s>rākṣasa</s>, nor a <s>gandharva</s>, nor a <s>yakṣa</s>, nor a serpent.
The <s>Rāghava</s> is a human, O king, and <s>Sugrīva</s> is lord of the monkeys.
Therefore how, O king, will you preserve your life?
Dharma does not come to an end joined with the fruit of adharma;
that very fruit follows, and dharma is the destroyer of adharma.

children.text: prāptaṃ dharmaphalaṃ tāvad bhavatā nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: So far you have obtained the fruit of dharma; about this there is no doubt.
But you will very soon meet the fruit of this adharma as well.
Knowing the slaughter at <s>Janasthāna</s>, and knowing likewise the killing of <s>Vālin</s>,
and the friendship of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Sugrīva</s>, understand what is good for yourself.
Indeed, if I wished, I too, alone, could destroy <s>Laṅkā</s>, with its horses, chariots, and elephants;
but that is his fixed decision.
For <s>Rāma</s> has vowed, in the presence of the hosts of monkeys and bears,
the uprooting of the enemies by whom <s>Sītā</s> was assaulted.

children.text: apakurvan hi rāmasya sākṣād api puraṃdaraḥ
children.translated_text: Even <s>Purandara</s> himself, if he were to wrong <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: na sukhaṃ prāpnuyād anyaḥ kiṃ punastvadvidho janaḥ ||
children.translated_text: would not obtain happiness; how much less some person such as you.

children.text: yāṃ sītetyabhijānāsi yeyaṃ tiṣṭhati te vaśe
children.translated_text: She whom you know as <s>Sītā</s>, this woman who stands under your control,
know her to be <s>Kālarātrī</s>, the night of death, destroyer of all <s>Laṅkā</s>.
Enough, then, with this noose of Time, taking the embodied form of <s>Sītā</s>,
fastened by yourself upon your own neck; let what is fitting for yourself be considered.
Burned by the splendor of <s>Sītā</s> and crushed by the anger of <s>Rāma</s>,
behold this city blazing, with its watchtowers and gateways.

children.text: sa sauṣṭhavopetam adīnavādinaḥ kaper niśamyāpratimo 'priyaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing the unwelcome speech of that incomparable monkey, endowed with eloquence and speaking without dejection,

children.text: daśānanaḥ kopavivṛttalocanaḥ samādiśat tasya vadhaṃ mahākapeḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Daśānana</s>, his eyes rolling with anger, ordered the killing of that great monkey.
Having heard that speech of the great-souled monkey,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, overcome with anger, commanded that he be killed.
When his killing had been ordered by the evil-minded <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> did not approve the killing of one who had delivered a message as an envoy.

children.text: taṃ rakṣo'dhipatiṃ kruddhaṃ tacca kāryam upasthitam
children.translated_text: Knowing the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s> to be angry and that matter to be at hand,
he reflected on what should be done, standing firm in the proper procedure for action.
Then, having decided the matter and having respectfully appeased with conciliation his elder brother, the conqueror of enemies,
that skilled speaker uttered a speech that was exceedingly beneficial.
"O king, the killing of this monkey is opposed to dharma and condemned by worldly custom,

children.text: tava cāsadṛśaṃ vīra kaper asya pramāpaṇam ||
children.translated_text: and it is unworthy of you, O hero.

children.text: asaṃśayaṃ śatrur ayaṃ pravṛddhaḥ kṛtaṃ hyanenāpriyam aprameyam
children.translated_text: Without doubt this enemy has grown strong, and by him an immeasurable injury has been done.

children.text: na dūtavadhyāṃ pravadanti santo dūtasya dṛṣṭā bahavo hi daṇḍāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But the good do not declare a messenger killable; many punishments for a messenger are observed.

children.text: vairūpyam aṅgeṣu kaśābhighāto mauṇḍyaṃ tathā lakṣaṇasaṃnipātaḥ
children.translated_text: Disfigurement of the limbs, a blow with a whip, shaving of the head, and also branding with marks:

children.text: etān hi dūte pravadanti daṇḍān vadhastu dūtasya na naḥ śruto 'pi ||
children.translated_text: these indeed they declare to be punishments for a messenger, but we have not even heard of killing a messenger.
How could one like you, whose intellect is trained in dharma and policy, whose conclusions are fixed by knowledge of high and low matters,

children.text: bhavadvidhaḥ kopavaśe hi tiṣṭhet kopaṃ niyacchanti hi sattvavantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: stand under the power of anger? For men of strength restrain anger.

children.text: na dharmavāde na ca lokavṛtte na śāstrabuddhigrahaṇeṣu vāpi
children.translated_text: In discourse on dharma, in worldly conduct, and in grasp of scriptural understanding,

children.text: vidyeta kaścit tava vīra tulyas tvaṃ hyuttamaḥ sarvasurāsurāṇām ||
children.translated_text: no one equal to you is to be found, O hero; for you are foremost among all gods and <s>asuras</s>.

children.text: na cāpyasya kaper ghāte kaṃcit paśyāmyahaṃ guṇam
children.translated_text: Nor do I see any benefit at all in the killing of this monkey.

children.text: teṣvayaṃ pātyatāṃ daṇḍo yair ayaṃ preṣitaḥ kapiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let punishment be made to fall upon those by whom this monkey was sent.

children.text: sādhur vā yadi vāsādhuḥ parair eṣa samarpitaḥ
children.translated_text: Whether good or not good, this one has been dispatched by others;

children.text: bruvan parārthaṃ paravānna dūto vadham arhati ||
children.translated_text: speaking another's purpose and dependent on another, a messenger does not deserve death.

children.text: api cāsmin hate rājannānyaṃ paśyāmi khecaram
children.translated_text: Moreover, if this one is killed, O king, I see no other sky-goer

children.text: iha yaḥ punar āgacchet paraṃ pāraṃ mahodadhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: who would come here again across the far shore of the great ocean.
Therefore no effort should be made to kill him, O conqueror of enemy cities.

children.text: bhavān sendreṣu deveṣu yatnam āsthātum arhati ||
children.translated_text: You ought rather to direct your effort against the gods together with <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: asmin vinaṣṭe na hi dūtam anyaṃ paśyāmi yastau nararājaputrau
children.translated_text: If this one is destroyed, I see no other envoy who would stir up those two princes,
fond of battle and ill-restrained, blocked by the long road, for war.
Since you are high-minded in valor and energy, and hard to conquer even for gods and <s>asuras</s>,

children.text: tvayā manonandana nairṛtānāṃ yuddhāyatir nāśayituṃ na yuktā ||
children.translated_text: O delighter of the minds of the <s>Nairṛtas</s>, it is not fitting for you to destroy the opportunity for battle.

children.text: hitāśca śūrāśca samāhitāśca kuleṣu jātāśca mahāguṇeṣu
children.translated_text: Your warriors are loyal, brave, collected, and born in families of great virtues;

children.text: manasvinaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ variṣṭhāḥ koṭyagraśaste subhṛtāśca yodhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: high-spirited, foremost among bearers of weapons, counted by tens of millions, and well maintained.

children.text: tad ekadeśena balasya tāvat kecit tavādeśakṛto 'payāntu
children.translated_text: Therefore let some of them, at least one part of your army, go forth, carrying out your command,

children.text: tau rājaputrau vinigṛhya mūḍhau pareṣu te bhāvayituṃ prabhāvam ||
children.translated_text: to seize those two foolish princes and to make your power manifest among your enemies."
Hearing that speech of his, the mighty <s>Daśagrīva</s>
replied to his brother with words beneficial and suited to place and time:

children.text: samyag uktaṃ hi bhavatā dūtavadhyā vigarhitā
children.translated_text: "You have spoken rightly; the killing of a messenger is censured.

children.text: avaśyaṃ tu vadhād anyaḥ kriyatām asya nigrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But some restraint other than death must certainly be imposed on this one.

children.text: kapīnāṃ kila lāṅgūlam iṣṭaṃ bhavati bhūṣaṇam
children.translated_text: The tail of monkeys, they say, is a cherished ornament.

children.text: tad asya dīpyatāṃ śīghraṃ tena dagdhena gacchatu ||
children.translated_text: Let that be quickly set ablaze; with it burned, let him go.
Then let all his friends, kinsmen, relatives,
and well-wishers see him wretched, wasted by the disfigurement of his limb."
The lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s> gave command about the whole city, including its squares:
"Let him be led around by the <s>rākṣasas</s> with his tail set ablaze."
Having heard that command of his, the <s>rākṣasas</s>, harsh with anger,

children.text: veṣṭante tasya lāṅgūlaṃ jīrṇaiḥ kārpāsikaiḥ paṭaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: wound his tail around with old cotton cloths.
As his tail was being wrapped, the great monkey grew larger,
like fire in the woods when it has reached dry fuel.
Then, after soaking it with oil, they set fire to it there.
With his tail ablaze, he made those <s>rākṣasas</s> fall,
his self filled with anger and indignation, his face like the young sun.

children.text: sa bhūyaḥ saṃgataiḥ krūrai rākṣasair harisattamaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, when the cruel <s>rākṣasas</s> had gathered again, that best of monkeys
was bound, but the hero formed a thought suited to that moment.

children.text: kāmaṃ khalu na me śaktā nibaddhasyāpi rākṣasāḥ
children.translated_text: "Of course these <s>rākṣasas</s> are not able to overpower me, even though I am bound.

children.text: chittvā pāśān samutpatya hanyām aham imān punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Cutting the bonds and leaping up, I could kill these men again.

children.text: sarveṣām eva paryāpto rākṣasānām ahaṃ yudhi
children.translated_text: I alone am enough for all the <s>rākṣasas</s> in battle;

children.text: kiṃ tu rāmasya prītyarthaṃ viṣahiṣye 'ham īdṛśam ||
children.translated_text: but, for the sake of <s>Rāma</s>'s pleasure, I will endure such treatment.

children.text: laṅkā cārayitavyā me punar eva bhaved iti
children.translated_text: <s>Laṅkā</s> must be surveyed by me again, as may now happen;

children.text: rātrau na hi sudṛṣṭā me durgakarmavidhānataḥ
children.translated_text: for at night I did not see her well with respect to the arrangement of her fortifications.

children.text: avaśyam eva draṣṭavyā mayā laṅkā niśākṣaye ||
children.translated_text: At daybreak I must certainly see <s>Laṅkā</s>.

children.text: kāmaṃ bandhaiśca me bhūyaḥ pucchasyoddīpanena ca
children.translated_text: Let the <s>rākṣasas</s> cause me pain as much as they wish with these bonds and with the setting alight of my tail;

children.text: pīḍāṃ kurvantu rakṣāṃsi na me 'sti manasaḥ śramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there is no weariness in my mind."
Then those <s>rākṣasas</s> seized the great monkey, whose form was concealed and who was full of strength,
and happily led away that elephant among monkeys.
Proclaiming him with the sounds of conches and drums, through their own actions,
the <s>rākṣasas</s> of cruel deeds paraded him through that city.
And <s>Hanumān</s> caused himself to be led through the great city of the <s>rākṣasas</s>;
then the great monkey saw marvelous aerial palaces,
enclosed plots of ground and well-laid-out squares,
streets crowded with houses, and crossroads.
In the squares, at four-way crossings, and likewise on the royal road,

children.text: ghoṣayanti kapiṃ sarve cārīka iti rākṣasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all the <s>rākṣasas</s> proclaimed the monkey, "He is a spy."
Then, when the tip of <s>Hanumān</s>'s tail was blazing,
those misshapen-eyed <s>rākṣasī</s> women told the goddess that unwelcome news:
"That copper-faced monkey with whom you conversed, O <s>Sītā</s>,
is now being led around with his tail set aflame."
Hearing that cruel word, like the stealing away of her own self,
<s>Vaidehī</s>, scorched by grief, approached the fire.
Then she, intent on an auspicious outcome for that great monkey,
the wide-eyed one, purified, worshipped the carrier of oblations.
"If there is service to my husband, if there is austerity I have practiced,
and if there is fidelity to one husband, be cool for <s>Hanumān</s>.
If that wise one has any compassion for me,

children.text: yadi vā bhāgyaśeṣaṃ me śīto bhava hanūmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: or if any remnant of good fortune is mine, be cool for <s>Hanumān</s>.
If that righteous one knows me to be endowed with good conduct and longing for reunion with him,

children.text: sa vijānāti dharmātmā śīto bhava hanūmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: be cool for <s>Hanumān</s>.
If noble <s>Sugrīva</s>, true to his pledge,
the great-armed one, will carry me across from this suffering, be cool for <s>Hanumān</s>."
Then the fire, sharp-flamed yet steady, with its flame turning to the right,

children.text: jajvāla mṛgaśāvākṣyāḥ śaṃsann iva śivaṃ kapeḥ ||
children.translated_text: blazed as if announcing good fortune for the monkey to the fawn-eyed woman.
And as his tail was burning, the monkey reflected:

children.text: pradīpto 'gnir ayaṃ kasmānna māṃ dahati sarvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Why does this blazing fire not burn me on every side?

children.text: dṛśyate ca mahājvālaḥ karoti ca na me rujam
children.translated_text: It is seen with great flames, yet it causes me no pain;
it rests on the tip of my tail like a fall of coolness.

children.text: athavā tad idaṃ vyaktaṃ yad dṛṣṭaṃ plavatā mayā
children.translated_text: Or rather, this is clearly like that marvel which I saw while leaping,
when, by <s>Rāma</s>'s power, the mountain appeared in the lord of rivers.

children.text: yadi tāvat samudrasya mainākasya ca dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: If there was such eager concern, for <s>Rāma</s>'s sake, in the ocean and in wise <s>Maināka</s>,

children.text: rāmārthaṃ saṃbhramastādṛk kim agnir na kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: what will fire not do?
Through <s>Sītā</s>'s compassion, through <s>Rāghava</s>'s splendor,

children.text: pituśca mama sakhyena na māṃ dahati pāvakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and through my father's friendship, the purifying fire does not burn me."
Again that elephant among monkeys reflected for a moment;
then the great monkey leapt up with speed and roared.
Then the splendid son of the Wind approached the city gate,
lofty like a mountain peak and crowded with ranks of <s>rākṣasa</s> guards.

children.text: sa bhūtvā śailasaṃkāśaḥ kṣaṇena punar ātmavān
children.translated_text: Becoming like a mountain, and then in a moment self-possessed
attaining the utmost smallness, he shook off the bonds.
Freed, the splendid one again became like a mountain,
and, looking about, saw an iron-fitted bar resting against the gateway arch.
The great-armed <s>Māruti</s> seized it, dark with iron fittings,
and once again slew all those guards.

children.text: sa tānnihatvā raṇacaṇḍavikramaḥ samīkṣamāṇaḥ punar eva laṅkām
children.translated_text: Having killed them, his valor fierce in battle, he looked once more at <s>Laṅkā</s>;
garlanded with flames made by his blazing tail, he shone like the sun with its rays.
Then, looking over <s>Laṅkā</s>, the monkey, his purpose accomplished,
with his enthusiasm increasing, thought about the remaining task.

children.text: kiṃ nu khalvavaśiṣṭaṃ me kartavyam iha sāmpratam
children.translated_text: "What indeed remains for me to do here now,

children.text: yad eṣāṃ rakṣasāṃ bhūyaḥ saṃtāpajananaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: that would again create torment for these <s>rākṣasas</s>?

children.text: vanaṃ tāvat pramathitaṃ prakṛṣṭā rākṣasā hatāḥ
children.translated_text: The grove has already been crushed; eminent <s>rākṣasas</s> have been slain;
a portion of the army has been destroyed; what remains is the destruction of the fortress.
When the fortress has been destroyed, the labor of the mission will have become easy."
With little effort, my labor in this matter would become fruitful.

children.text: yo hyayaṃ mama lāṅgūle dīpyate havyavāhanaḥ
children.translated_text: For this bearer of oblations, which is blazing on my tail,

children.text: asya saṃtarpaṇaṃ nyāyyaṃ kartum ebhir gṛhottamaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: it is proper to satisfy it with these finest houses.
Then, his tail blazing, like a cloud with lightning,
the great monkey moved about on the tops of the houses of <s>Laṅkā</s>.
<s>Hanumān</s> released the fire, resembling the flame of the fire at the end of time.
And from contact with the wind, the fire, very swift and mighty,
blazed and grew like the fire of time.
The wind drove the blazing fire through those mansions.
Those houses, with golden latticework and made of pearls and gems,
great and filled with jewels, collapsed.
Those mansions, their aerial pavilions broken, fell to the surface of the earth,
like dwellings of <s>siddhas</s> from the sky when their merit is exhausted.
Those varied materials, composed of diamond, coral, beryl, pearls, and silver,

children.text: vicitrān bhavanād dhātūn syandamānān dadarśa saḥ ||
children.translated_text: streaming from the mansions, he saw.

children.text: nāgnistṛpyati kāṣṭhānāṃ tṛṇānāṃ ca yathā tathā
children.translated_text: As fire is not satisfied with wood and grass in that way,

children.text: hanūmān rākṣasendrāṇāṃ vadhe kiṃcin na tṛpyati ||
children.translated_text: so <s>Hanumān</s> was not at all satisfied in killing the lords of the <s>rākṣasas</s>.
Enveloped in flames of fire, with her champions slain and her warriors turned back,
<s>Laṅkā</s>, overwhelmed by the force of <s>Hanumān</s>'s anger, became as if struck by a curse.
Full of <s>rākṣasas</s> who were agitated, frightened, and dejected, and marked by blazing flames of fire,
the high-minded <s>Hanumān</s> saw <s>Laṅkā</s> like the earth struck by the anger of <s>Svayambhū</s>.

children.text: sa rākṣasāṃstān subahūṃśca hatvā vanaṃ ca bhaṅktvā bahupādapaṃ tat
children.translated_text: Having killed those many <s>rākṣasas</s> and broken that grove with its many trees,

children.text: visṛjya rakṣobhavaneṣu cāgniṃ jagāma rāmaṃ manasā mahātmā ||
children.translated_text: and having cast fire into the dwellings of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, the great-souled one turned in his mind to <s>Rāma</s>.
Having set all <s>Laṅkā</s> ablaze, the great monkey
then extinguished the fire of his tail in the ocean, that best of monkeys.
Looking upon the city blazing, devastated, and filled with terrified hosts of <s>rākṣasas</s>,
<s>Hanumān</s> the monkey surveyed <s>Laṅkā</s> and reflected.
A very great terror arose in him, and self-reproach was born:

children.text: laṅkāṃ pradahatā karma kiṃsvit kṛtam idaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: 'In burning <s>Laṅkā</s>, what deed have I done?

children.text: dhanyāste puruṣaśreṣṭhā ye buddhyā kopam utthitam
children.translated_text: Blessed are those best of men who, by intelligence,
restrain anger that has arisen, like blazing fire with water.

children.text: yadi dagdhā tviyaṃ laṅkā nūnam āryāpi jānakī
children.translated_text: But if this <s>Laṅkā</s> has been burned, surely noble <s>Jānakī</s> too

children.text: dagdhā tena mayā bhartur hataṃ kāryam ajānatā ||
children.translated_text: has been burned; through that, I, not knowing, have ruined my master's task.
The task for whose sake this undertaking began has been brought to ruin;

children.text: mayā hi dahatā laṅkāṃ na sītā parirakṣitā ||
children.translated_text: for while burning <s>Laṅkā</s>, I did not protect <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: īṣatkāryam idaṃ kāryaṃ kṛtam āsīnna saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: This undertaking had nearly been accomplished, without doubt;
but, overcome by anger, I have destroyed its very root.

children.text: vinaṣṭā jānakī vyaktaṃ na hyadagdhaḥ pradṛśyate
children.translated_text: <s>Jānakī</s> has plainly perished, for no part of <s>Laṅkā</s>

children.text: laṅkāyāḥ kaścid uddeśaḥ sarvā bhasmīkṛtā purī ||
children.translated_text: is seen unburned; the whole city has been reduced to ashes.

children.text: yadi tad vihataṃ kāryaṃ mayā prajñāviparyayāt
children.translated_text: If that task has been ruined by me through a reversal of judgment,
then even the laying down of my life here itself is highly pleasing to me.
Shall I throw myself into fire today, or perhaps into the mouth of the submarine fire,
or shall I give my body to the beings dwelling in the ocean?

children.text: kathaṃ hi jīvatā śakyo mayā draṣṭuṃ harīśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: For how can I, while living, see <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the monkeys,
or those two tigers among men, when I have destroyed the whole task?

children.text: mayā khalu tad evedaṃ roṣadoṣāt pradarśitam
children.translated_text: Indeed, because of the fault of wrath, I have displayed this very thing:
the monkey nature, unstable and famed in the three worlds.

children.text: dhig astu rājasaṃ bhāvam anīśam anavasthitam
children.translated_text: Shame on this passionate disposition, powerless and unsteady,

children.text: īśvareṇāpi yad rāgānmayā sītā na rakṣitā ||
children.translated_text: since, through passion, I, though capable, did not protect <s>Sītā</s>.
But when <s>Sītā</s> is lost, those two both will perish;
when they perish, <s>Sugrīva</s>, together with his kinsmen, will perish.

children.text: etad eva vacaḥ śrutvā bharato bhrātṛvatsalaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing this very report, how will <s>Bharata</s>, loving his brother,
righteous and together with <s>Śatrughna</s>, be able to live?
When the most righteous <s>Ikṣvāku</s> lineage has surely gone to destruction,
all the subjects will be afflicted by grief and torment.
Therefore I, bereft of fortune, having lost the gathering of <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>,
my self overcome by the fault of wrath, am plainly a destroyer of the worlds.'
As he was thinking thus, omens appeared to him,
the very ones perceived before; he again considered them directly.
'Or perhaps the blessed lady of lovely limbs, protected by her own splendor,

children.text: na naśiṣyati kalyāṇī nāgnir agnau pravartate ||
children.translated_text: will not perish; fire does not act upon fire.
For the fire ought not to touch the wife of that immeasurably radiant, righteous man,
protected as she is by her own conduct.
Surely by <s>Rāma</s>'s power and by <s>Vaidehī</s>'s good deed,
this bearer of oblations, though engaged in burning, did not burn me.

children.text: trayāṇāṃ bharatādīnāṃ bhrātṝṇāṃ devatā ca yā
children.translated_text: She who is the deity of the three brothers beginning with <s>Bharata</s>,

children.text: rāmasya ca manaḥkāntā sā kathaṃ vinaśiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: and dear to <s>Rāma</s>'s heart, how could she perish?

children.text: yad vā dahanakarmāyaṃ sarvatra prabhur avyayaḥ
children.translated_text: Or if this fire, imperishable and powerful everywhere, is the agent of burning,

children.text: na me dahati lāṅgūlaṃ katham āryāṃ pradhakṣyati ||
children.translated_text: yet it does not burn my tail; how will it burn the noble lady?
By her austerity, truth-speaking, and exclusive devotion to her husband,

children.text: api sā nirdahed agniṃ na tām agniḥ pradhakṣyati ||
children.translated_text: she might even burn fire itself; fire will not burn her.'
While he was thus considering there the goddess's possession of <s>dharma</s>,
<s>Hanumān</s> heard the words of the great-souled <s>Cāraṇas</s>:

children.text: aho khalu kṛtaṃ karma durviṣahyaṃ hanūmatā
children.translated_text: 'Ah, what a deed, truly hard to endure, has been done by <s>Hanumān</s>,
as he repeatedly released terrible fire among the dwellings of the <s>rākṣasas</s>!'
This city <s>Laṅkā</s>, with its towers, ramparts, and gateways, has been burned,

children.text: jānakī na ca dagdheti vismayo 'dbhuta eva naḥ ||
children.translated_text: but <s>Jānakī</s> has not been burned: this is truly a wondrous marvel to us.
By omens, by manifest signs, by causes, and by great virtues,
and by the words of seers, <s>Hanumān</s> became glad at heart.

children.text: tataḥ kapiḥ prāptamanorathārthas tām akṣatāṃ rājasutāṃ viditvā
children.translated_text: Then the monkey, having attained the purpose of his wish and knowing the king's daughter to be unharmed,

children.text: pratyakṣatastāṃ punar eva dṛṣṭvā pratiprayāṇāya matiṃ cakāra ||
children.translated_text: after seeing her again directly, resolved on the return journey.
Then, at the foot of the śiṃśapā tree, to <s>Jānakī</s> who remained there,
having bowed, he said, "By good fortune, I see you here unharmed."

children.text: tatastaṃ prasthitaṃ sītā vīkṣamāṇā punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sītā</s>, watching him as he set out again and again,
spoke to <s>Hanumān</s> a word filled with affection for her husband:

children.text: kāmam asya tvam evaikaḥ kāryasya parisādhane
children.translated_text: "Indeed you alone are sufficient for accomplishing this task,
O slayer of enemy heroes; the rise of your strength is glorious.
But if <s>Kākutstha</s>, the crusher of enemy forces, making <s>Laṅkā</s> crowded with his troops,

children.text: māṃ nayed yadi kākutsthastasya tat sadṛśaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: were to lead me away, that would be worthy of him.

children.text: tad yathā tasya vikrāntam anurūpaṃ mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, in such a way as may be fitting for the valor of that great-souled one,
for him who is heroic in battle, bring that very matter to fulfillment."
Having heard her speech, furnished with purpose,
