humble and joined with reasons, <s>Hanumān</s> spoke this reply:
"<s>Kākutstha</s> will come swiftly, surrounded by the foremost monkeys and bears,
and after conquering your enemies in battle, he will drive away your grief."
Thus having comforted <s>Vaidehī</s>, <s>Hanumān</s>, the son of the Wind,
having resolved to depart, bowed to <s>Vaidehī</s>.
Then that tiger among monkeys, eager to see his lord,
the crusher of foes, climbed the excellent mountain <s>Ariṣṭa</s>.
It was enclosed by blue rows of forest, frequented by lofty padmaka trees,
and covered with sāla, tāla, aśvakarṇa trees, and many bamboos.
It was adorned with spreading canopies of flowering creepers,
thronged by herds of many kinds of animals and ornamented by flowing mineral streams.
It was provided with many waterfalls and difficult because of masses of rock,
inhabited by great seers, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Kiṃnaras</s>, and serpents.
It was crowded with creepers and trees, its caves filled with lions,
filled with troops of tigers, and bearing trees with sweet roots and fruits.
The exceedingly strong best of leapers climbed that mountain,
impelled by delight at the thought of soon seeing <s>Rāma</s>.
Then, on the lovely mountain slopes trampled by the soles of his feet,
the rocks, resounding, split apart, crushed to powder.

children.text: sa tam āruhya śailendraṃ vyavardhata mahākapiḥ
children.translated_text: Having climbed that lord of mountains, the great monkey expanded,
seeking the northern shore of the salt sea from the southern one.
Then the heroic son of the Wind, having ascended the mountain,
saw the terrifying ocean, inhabited by fish and serpents.
The tiger among monkeys, born from the Wind,
entered the sky like the wind, going from the south toward the north.
Then that best of mountains, oppressed by that monkey,

children.text: rarāsa saha tair bhūtaiḥ prāviśad vasudhātalam
children.translated_text: roared together with those beings and sank into the earth,

children.text: kampamānaiśca śikharaiḥ patadbhir api ca drumaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: with its peaks shaking and its trees falling.
The flowering trees, churned by his great speed,
fell broken onto the ground, like trees struck by <s>Śakra</s>'s weapon.
From the mighty lions dwelling in the interiors of caves, oppressed,

children.text: siṃhānāṃ ninado bhīmo nabho bhindan sa śuśruve ||
children.translated_text: a terrible roar was heard, splitting the sky.
Their garments slipped and whirled away, their ornaments thrown into disorder,
the <s>Vidyādhara</s> women suddenly sprang up from the mountain.
Enormous, strong, blazing-tongued, and very venomous,
great serpents, their heads and necks crushed, writhed about.
<s>Kiṃnaras</s>, serpents, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Vidyādharas</s> likewise,

children.text: pīḍitaṃ taṃ nagavaraṃ tyaktvā gaganam āsthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: leaving that oppressed best of mountains, took to the sky.

children.text: sa ca bhūmidharaḥ śrīmān balinā tena pīḍitaḥ
children.translated_text: And that splendid mountain, oppressed by that strong one,
with trees and lofty peaks, entered the subterranean region.
The mountain, ten yojanas wide and thirty yojanas high,

children.text: dharaṇyāṃ samatāṃ yātaḥ sa babhūva dharādharaḥ ||
children.translated_text: became level with the earth; such did that mountain become.
The lovely, auspicious sky had the moon as its white lotus and the sun as its kāraṇḍava bird,
with <s>Tiṣya</s> and <s>Śravaṇa</s> as its flocks, and clouds as its duckweed and grassy banks.
It had <s>Punarvasu</s> as a great fish and <s>Lohitāṅga</s> as a great sea-monster,
<s>Airāvata</s> as a great island, and was stirred by the swan <s>Svātī</s>.
Its waves were born from masses of wind, and its waters were cool with moonbeams.
It had serpents, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Gandharvas</s> as its awakened lotuses and blue lotuses.
As though swallowing the sky, as though licking the lord of stars,
as though carrying off heaven with its stars and the disk of the sun,
the splendid great sky-going monkey <s>Hanumān</s>, moving through the abode of the Wind,
went on, as though dragging along the masses of clouds.
Great clouds shone white and red, blue and madder-colored,
and green and ruddy in hue.
Entering into masses of clouds and coming out again and again,
he was seen hidden and visible, like the moon.
Roaring with a great roar, with a great sound like thunderclouds,
the very radiant one came again through the middle of the ocean.
And having touched the excellent mountain <s>Sunābha</s>, the mighty one,
approached at great speed, like an iron arrow released from a bowstring.
Having come somewhat nearer, he looked at the great mountain.
The foremost monkey roared, resembling a cloud over <s>Mahendra</s>.
Hearing the sound of his roar, the monkeys on every side
all became eager, longing to see their friend.
That best of monkeys, <s>Jāmbavān</s>, his mind thrilled with joy,

children.text: upāmantrya harīn sarvān idaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: addressed all the monkeys and spoke these words:
In every way this <s>Hanumān</s> has accomplished the task; there is no doubt here.
For such a roar as this would not belong to one whose task was unaccomplished.

children.text: tasya bāhūruvegaṃ ca ninādaṃ ca mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing the force of the arms and thighs of that great-souled one, and his roar,
the monkeys, delighted, sprang up here and there.
From tree-top to tree-top, and from summit to summit,
they joyfully went, wishing to see <s>Hanumān</s>.

children.text: te prītāḥ pādapāgreṣu gṛhya śākhāḥ supuṣpitāḥ
children.translated_text: Those monkeys, delighted, grasped well-flowered branches on the tops of trees
and waved the bright branches as if they were garments.
Seeing that great monkey, like a dense mass of cloud, rushing toward them,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā te vānarāḥ sarve tasthuḥ prāñjalayastadā ||
children.translated_text: all those monkeys then stood with joined palms.
Then that swift monkey, mountain-like himself,
fell upon the tree-covered summit of Mount <s>Mahendra</s>.
Then all the foremost monkeys, with joyful minds,
surrounded the great-souled <s>Hanumān</s> and stood attending him.

children.text: parivārya ca te sarve parāṃ prītim upāgatāḥ
children.translated_text: Having surrounded him, they all attained supreme joy,
all with delighted faces, since he had returned unharmed.

children.text: upāyanāni cādāya mūlāni ca phalāni ca
children.translated_text: Taking offerings, roots, and fruits,
the monkeys honored the best of monkeys, the son of the Wind.

children.text: vinedur muditāḥ kecic cakruḥ kilakilāṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Some cried out joyfully, and likewise some made a chattering cry;
delighted, the bull-like monkeys brought branches of trees.
But <s>Hanumān</s>, the great monkey, then bowed to the honored elders,
headed by <s>Jāmbavān</s>, and also to prince <s>Aṅgada</s>.

children.text: sa tābhyāṃ pūjitaḥ pūjyaḥ kapibhiśca prasāditaḥ
children.translated_text: Honored by those two, and respectfully received by the monkeys,
the heroic one briefly reported, "The goddess has been seen."

children.text: niṣasāda ca hastena gṛhītvā vālinaḥ sutam
children.translated_text: And, taking the son of <s>Vālin</s> by the hand, he sat down
in a charming woodland place on Mount <s>Mahendra</s>.
<s>Hanumān</s>, delighted, then spoke to those bull-like monkeys:
"The daughter of <s>Janaka</s> has been seen, dwelling in the <s>Aśoka</s> grove.
She is guarded by very terrible <s>rākṣasīs</s>, blameless,
a young woman wearing a single braid and longing for the sight of <s>Rāma</s>,
wearied by fasting, soiled, with matted hair, and thin."
Then, hearing the words "She has been seen," weighty in meaning and like nectar,
all the monkeys became joyful at the son of the Wind's report.
Some powerful ones shouted, others roared, and others bellowed;
some made chattering cries, and others answered with roars.
Some elephant-like monkeys, delighted, raised their tails high
and waved their curved, outstretched, long tails.
But other monkeys, rejoicing, leapt down from mountain peaks
and touched <s>Hanumān</s>, who was like an elephant.
Then <s>Aṅgada</s> spoke an unsurpassed word to <s>Hanumān</s>, who had spoken,
in the midst of all the monkey heroes:

children.text: sattve vīrye na te kaścit samo vānara vidyate
children.translated_text: "In energy and strength no monkey is found equal to you,

children.text: yad avaplutya vistīrṇaṃ sāgaraṃ punar āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: since you leapt across the vast ocean and returned again.

children.text: diṣṭyā dṛṣṭā tvayā devī rāmapatnī yaśasvinī
children.translated_text: Fortunately the glorious goddess, <s>Rāma</s>'s wife, has been seen by you.
Fortunately <s>Kākutstha</s> will abandon the grief born of separation from <s>Sītā</s>."
Then the monkeys, surrounding <s>Aṅgada</s>, <s>Hanumān</s>,
and <s>Jāmbavān</s>, rejoiced and occupied broad rocks.
The best of monkeys, wishing to hear of the crossing of the ocean,

children.text: darśanaṃ cāpi laṅkāyāḥ sītāyā rāvaṇasya ca
children.translated_text: and also the sight of <s>Laṅkā</s>, of <s>Sītā</s>, and of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
all stood with joined palms, their faces turned toward <s>Hanumān</s>'s face.

children.text: tasthau tatrāṅgadaḥ śrīmān vānarair bahubhir vṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The illustrious <s>Aṅgada</s> stood there, surrounded by many monkeys,
like the lord of the gods in heaven being attended by the gods.
With famous and glorious <s>Hanumān</s>, and with <s>Aṅgada</s>, whose arm was adorned with an armlet,

children.text: mudā tadādhyāsitam unnataṃ mahan mahīdharāgraṃ jvalitaṃ śriyābhavat ||
children.translated_text: that lofty, great mountain-top, then joyfully occupied, blazed with splendor.
Then on the summit of that mountain, the mighty <s>Mahendra</s>,
the monkeys headed by <s>Hanumān</s> attained supreme joy.
Then <s>Jāmbavān</s>, greatly thrilled, asked that joyful great monkey,
the son of the Wind, about the course of the mission:

children.text: kathaṃ dṛṣṭā tvayā devī kathaṃ vā tatra vartate
children.translated_text: "How was the goddess seen by you? And how does she remain there?

children.text: tasyāṃ vā sa kathaṃ vṛttaḥ krūrakarmā daśānanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And how has the ten-faced one, of cruel deeds, behaved toward her?

children.text: tattvataḥ sarvam etannaḥ prabrūhi tvaṃ mahākape
children.translated_text: Tell us all this truthfully, great monkey.
When we have heard the matter, we shall consider further the decision about the task.
And what message must be spoken there by us when we have gone, self-possessed one,

children.text: rakṣitavyaṃ ca yat tatra tad bhavān vyākarotu naḥ ||
children.translated_text: and what must be protected there: please explain that to us."
Then, appointed by him, with the hairs of his body bristling with joy,
he bowed his head to the goddess <s>Sītā</s> and replied:

children.text: pratyakṣam eva bhavatāṃ mahendrāgrāt kham āplutaḥ
children.translated_text: "Before your very eyes, from the top of <s>Mahendra</s>, I leapt into the sky,
intent on reaching the southern shore of the ocean.

children.text: gacchataśca hi me ghoraṃ vighnarūpam ivābhavat
children.translated_text: As I was going, there appeared to me, as if in the form of a dreadful obstacle,
a divine golden peak, exceedingly charming.

children.text: sthitaṃ panthānam āvṛtya mene vighnaṃ ca taṃ nagam ||
children.translated_text: Standing there and blocking the path, that mountain seemed to me an obstacle."
Having approached that divine, golden, best of mountains,

children.text: kṛtā me manasā buddhir bhettavyo 'yaṃ mayeti ca ||
children.translated_text: I formed a resolve in my mind: "This one must be broken through by me."

children.text: prahataṃ ca mayā tasya lāṅgūlena mahāgireḥ
children.translated_text: And when I struck that great mountain with my tail,
its peak, bright as the sun, shattered into a thousand pieces.

children.text: vyavasāyaṃ ca me buddhvā sa hovāca mahāgiriḥ
children.translated_text: Understanding my resolve, that great mountain said to me,
"Son," in a sweet voice, as if delighting my heart:

children.text: pitṛvyaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi sakhāyaṃ mātariśvanaḥ
children.translated_text: "Know me too as your paternal uncle, a friend of <s>Mātariśvan</s>,
known as <s>Maināka</s>, dwelling in the great ocean.
Formerly, son, the foremost mountains had wings;
at will they moved over the earth, afflicting it on every side.
Hearing of the conduct of the mountains, great <s>Mahendra</s>, chastiser of <s>Pāka</s>,
cut off their wings by the thousands with his thunderbolt.

children.text: ahaṃ tu mokṣitastasmāt tava pitrā mahātmanā
children.translated_text: But I was freed from that by your great-souled father;
by <s>Māruta</s>, dear child, I was then cast into the great ocean.

children.text: rāmasya ca mayā sāhye vartitavyam ariṃdama
children.translated_text: And I must render help to <s>Rāma</s>, subduer of foes;
<s>Rāma</s> is the best of upholders of <s>dharma</s> (normative order), equal in valor to great <s>Indra</s>."
Hearing this from that great-souled <s>Maināka</s>,

children.text: kāryam āvedya tu girer uddhataṃ ca mano mama ||
children.translated_text: I told the mountain my task, while my mind was uplifted.
Then, permitted by that great-souled <s>Maināka</s>,

children.text: uttamaṃ javam āsthāya śeṣam adhvānam āsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I assumed the highest speed and set out on the rest of the road.
Then for a very long time I went along the path with speed;
then I saw the goddess <s>Surasā</s>, mother of the <s>nāgas</s>.

children.text: samudramadhye sā devī vacanaṃ mām abhāṣata
children.translated_text: In the middle of the ocean that goddess spoke to me:
"You have been assigned to me as food by the immortals, best of monkeys;
therefore I will eat you, for you have long been allotted to me."

children.text: evam uktaḥ surasayā prāñjaliḥ praṇataḥ sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Surasā</s>, I stood with joined palms, bowed down;
becoming pale-faced, I uttered these words:
"Splendid <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, entered the Daṇḍaka forest,

children.text: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā sītayā ca paraṃtapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the scorcher of foes, together with his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and with <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: tasya sītā hṛtā bhāryā rāvaṇena durātmanā
children.translated_text: His wife <s>Sītā</s> was carried off by wicked <s>Rāvaṇa</s>;
I am going as a messenger to her presence at <s>Rāma</s>'s command.
You ought to help <s>Rāma</s>, O dweller in this region.
Then, after seeing <s>Maithilī</s> and <s>Rāma</s>, whose actions are unwearied,

children.text: āgamiṣyāmi te vaktraṃ satyaṃ pratiśṛṇoti me ||
children.translated_text: I will come into your mouth; hear my truthful promise."

children.text: evam uktā mayā sā tu surasā kāmarūpiṇī
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by me, that shape-changing <s>Surasā</s>
said, "No one may pass beyond me; this is my boon."
Thus addressed by <s>Surasā</s>, I became ten yojanas long,
and in a moment I became half that in breadth.
And she opened that mouth in proportion to my measure;

children.text: tad dṛṣṭvā vyāditaṃ tvāsyaṃ hrasvaṃ hyakaravaṃ vapuḥ ||
children.translated_text: seeing her mouth opened wide, I made my body small.
At that very moment I again became the size of a thumb;

children.text: abhipatyāśu tad vaktraṃ nirgato 'haṃ tataḥ kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: quickly entering that mouth, I came out again in an instant.

children.text: abravīt surasā devī svena rūpeṇa māṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: The goddess <s>Surasā</s>, in her own form, spoke to me again:
"Go, gentle best of monkeys, happily, for the accomplishment of your purpose.
Bring <s>Vaidehī</s> together with great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>;

children.text: sukhī bhava mahābāho prītāsmi tava vānara ||
children.translated_text: be happy, mighty-armed monkey; I am pleased with you."
Then, praised by all beings with "Well done, well done!",
I leapt into the wide sky like <s>Garuḍa</s>.

children.text: chāyā me nigṛhītā ca na ca paśyāmi kiṃcana
children.translated_text: Then my shadow was seized, and I could see nothing.
With my speed gone, looking over the ten directions,

children.text: na kiṃcit tatra paśyāmi yena me 'pahṛtā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: I saw nothing there by which my movement had been taken away.

children.text: tato me buddhir utpannā kiṃ nāma gamane mama
children.translated_text: Then this thought arose in me: "What sort of obstacle

children.text: īdṛśo vighna utpanno rūpaṃ yatra na dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: has arisen in my journey, where no form is seen?"

children.text: adhobhāgena me dṛṣṭiḥ śocatā pātitā mayā
children.translated_text: In distress I cast my gaze downward;

children.text: tato 'drākṣam ahaṃ bhīmāṃ rākṣasīṃ salile śayām ||
children.translated_text: then I saw a terrible <s>rākṣasī</s> lying in the water.

children.text: prahasya ca mahānādam ukto 'haṃ bhīmayā tayā
children.translated_text: Laughing with a great roar, I was addressed by that terrible one,
as I remained steady and unalarmed, with these ugly words:
"Where will you go, great-bodied one, you who are desired by hungry me?

children.text: bhakṣaḥ prīṇaya me dehaṃ ciram āhāravarjitam ||
children.translated_text: Become my food; satisfy my body, long deprived of nourishment."

children.text: bāḍham ityeva tāṃ vāṇīṃ pratyagṛhṇām ahaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Then I accepted her words simply by saying, "So be it,"
and filled her body beyond the measure of her mouth.

children.text: tasyāścāsyaṃ mahad bhīmaṃ vardhate mama bhakṣaṇe
children.translated_text: Her great, terrible mouth grew larger in order to eat me,

children.text: na ca māṃ sā tu bubudhe mama vā vikṛtaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: but she did not understand me or the alteration I had made.
Then, reducing my vast form in the blink of an eye,
I seized her heart and shot forth into the sky.
That terrible one, her arms flung out, fell into the salt ocean,
her heart cut out by me, large as a mountain.

children.text: śṛṇomi khagatānāṃ ca siddhānāṃ cāraṇaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: And I heard the sky-goers and the siddhas together with the cāraṇas saying:

children.text: rākṣasī siṃhikā bhīmā kṣipraṃ hanumatā hṛtā ||
children.translated_text: "The terrible <s>rākṣasī</s> <s>Siṃhikā</s> has quickly been slain by <s>Hanumān</s>."

children.text: tāṃ hatvā punar evāhaṃ kṛtyam ātyayikaṃ smaran
children.translated_text: Having killed her, I again remembered the urgent task;
after traveling a great distance, I saw, adorned with mountains,

children.text: dakṣiṇaṃ tīram udadher laṅkā yatra ca sā purī ||
children.translated_text: the southern shore of the ocean, where that city <s>Laṅkā</s> stood.

children.text: astaṃ dinakare yāte rakṣasāṃ nilayaṃ purīm
children.translated_text: When the sun had set, I entered the city, the abode of the <s>rākṣasas</s>,
unknown to the <s>rākṣasas</s> of terrible valor.
There, searching all night for the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,
I went into <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s inner apartments but did not see the slender-waisted woman.
Then, when I did not see <s>Sītā</s> in <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s residence,
Having reached an ocean of grief, I could not perceive its far shore.

children.text: śocatā ca mayā dṛṣṭaṃ prākāreṇa samāvṛtam
children.translated_text: And as I grieved, I saw an excellent house-garden enclosed by a rampart,
a splendid one, with an extended golden wall.
Leaping over that rampart, I saw a place filled with many trees.
In the middle of the aśoka grove there was a great śiṃśapā tree;

children.text: tam āruhya ca paśyāmi kāñcanaṃ kadalīvanam ||
children.translated_text: climbing it, I saw a golden grove of plantain trees.
Not far from the śiṃśapā tree I saw a woman of lovely complexion,
dark, lotus-petal-eyed, her face made thin by fasting.
She was surrounded by ugly and cruel <s>rākṣasī</s> women,
eaters of flesh and blood, like a doe surrounded by tigresses.

children.text: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā tādṛśīṃ nārīṃ rāmapatnīm aninditām
children.translated_text: Seeing that woman in such a state, the blameless wife of <s>Rāma</s>,
I remained right there in the śiṃśapā tree, watching.
Then I heard a tumultuous sound mixed with the noise of girdles and anklets,
very deep, from <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s residence.
Then, greatly alarmed, I drew in my own form,

children.text: ahaṃ ca śiṃśapāvṛkṣe pakṣīva gahane sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and I stayed in the śiṃśapā tree like a bird in a thicket.
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s wives and mighty <s>Rāvaṇa</s> himself

children.text: taṃ deśaṃ samanuprāptā yatra sītābhavat sthitā ||
children.translated_text: came to the place where <s>Sītā</s> was standing.
When the fair-hipped <s>Sītā</s> saw him, the lord of the <s>rākṣasa</s> hosts,

children.text: saṃkucyorū stanau pīnau bāhubhyāṃ parirabhya ca ||
children.translated_text: she drew in her thighs and clasped her full breasts with her arms.
The ten-necked one spoke to <s>Sītā</s>, who was in the deepest distress:

children.text: avākśirāḥ prapatito bahu manyasva mām iti ||
children.translated_text: 'With head bowed, I have fallen before you; hold me in high regard.'

children.text: yadi cet tvaṃ tu māṃ darpānnābhinandasi garvite
children.translated_text: 'But if, out of pride, you do not welcome me, arrogant woman,
after two months, O <s>Sītā</s>, I shall drink your blood.'
Hearing this speech of wicked-souled <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
<s>Sītā</s>, extremely angry, spoke an excellent reply.
'Lowest of <s>rākṣasas</s>, as I am the wife of <s>Rāma</s> of immeasurable splendor,
the lord of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> line, and the daughter-in-law of <s>Daśaratha</s>,

children.text: avācyaṃ vadato jihvā kathaṃ na patitā tava ||
children.translated_text: how has your tongue not fallen out while you speak what should not be spoken?'

children.text: kiṃsvid vīryaṃ tavānārya yo māṃ bhartur asaṃnidhau
children.translated_text: 'What power is yours, ignoble one, you who, while my husband was absent,
abducted me and came away, sinful one, unseen by that great-souled man?'

children.text: na tvaṃ rāmasya sadṛśo dāsye 'pyasya na yujyase
children.translated_text: 'You are not equal to <s>Rāma</s>; you are not fit even for servitude to him.

children.text: yajñīyaḥ satyavāk caiva raṇaślāghī ca rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> is worthy of sacrifice, truthful in speech, and praised in battle.'

children.text: jānakyā paruṣaṃ vākyam evam ukto daśānanaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Jānakī</s> with harsh words, the ten-faced one
suddenly blazed up in anger like a fire standing on a funeral pyre.

children.text: vivṛtya nayane krūre muṣṭim udyamya dakṣiṇam
children.translated_text: Rolling open his cruel eyes and raising his right fist,

children.text: maithilīṃ hantum ārabdhaḥ strībhir hāhākṛtaṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: he began to strike <s>Maithilī</s>; then the women cried out in alarm.

children.text: strīṇāṃ madhyāt samutpatya tasya bhāryā durātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Springing up from among the women, the wife of that wicked one,

children.text: varā mandodarī nāma tayā sa pratiṣedhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the excellent lady named <s>Mandodarī</s>, restrained him.

children.text: uktaśca madhurāṃ vāṇīṃ tayā sa madanārditaḥ
children.translated_text: And he, tormented by passion, was addressed by her in sweet speech:
'What business have you with <s>Sītā</s>, you whose valor equals great <s>Indra</s>'s?

children.text: mayā saha ramasvādya madviśiṣṭā na jānakī ||
children.translated_text: Sport with me today; <s>Jānakī</s> is not superior to me.'
'With daughters of gods and gandharvas, and with daughters of yakṣas too,

children.text: sārdhaṃ prabho ramasveha sītayā kiṃ kariṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: sport here, my lord; what will you do with <s>Sītā</s>?'
Then that mighty night-roamer, together with those assembled women,

children.text: utthāpya sahasā nīto bhavanaṃ svaṃ niśācaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: was suddenly raised up and led to his own palace.
When the ten-necked one had gone, the <s>rākṣasī</s> women of distorted faces
rebuked <s>Sītā</s> with cruel and exceedingly harsh words.
<s>Jānakī</s> counted their speech as no more than grass,

children.text: tarjitaṃ ca tadā tāsāṃ sītāṃ prāpya nirarthakam ||
children.translated_text: and then their threats against <s>Sītā</s> came to nothing.
Those flesh-eating <s>rākṣasī</s> women, whose roaring was futile and whose effort had failed,
reported to <s>Rāvaṇa</s> <s>Sītā</s>'s firm and noble resolve.
Then all of them together, their hopes frustrated and their effort spent,
surrounded her on every side and fell under the power of sleep.

children.text: tāsu caiva prasuptāsu sītā bhartṛhite ratā
children.translated_text: And when those women had fallen asleep, <s>Sītā</s>, devoted to her husband's welfare,
lamented piteously and, miserable, grieved in great sorrow.

children.text: tāṃ cāhaṃ tādṛśīṃ dṛṣṭvā sītāyā dāruṇāṃ daśām
children.translated_text: Seeing her in such a state, and seeing <s>Sītā</s>'s terrible condition,

children.text: cintayāmāsa viśrānto na ca me nirvṛtaṃ manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I thought while resting there, and my mind found no peace.
For the sake of speaking with <s>Jānakī</s>, a method was considered by me,
and then I placed before her the lineage of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> family.
Hearing the speech I uttered, honored by companies of royal sages,
the goddess answered me, her eyes covered with tears.

children.text: kastvaṃ kena kathaṃ ceha prāpto vānarapuṃgava
children.translated_text: 'Who are you? By whom, and how, have you reached this place, foremost of monkeys?

children.text: kā ca rāmeṇa te prītistanme śaṃsitum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: And what friendship do you have with <s>Rāma</s>? You ought to tell me that.'
Hearing that speech of hers, I too spoke these words:
'Goddess, your husband <s>Rāma</s> has an ally of fearsome valor,
a heroic monkey-king named <s>Sugrīva</s>, mighty in strength.'

children.text: tasya māṃ viddhi bhṛtyaṃ tvaṃ hanūmantam ihāgatam
children.translated_text: 'Know me to be his servant, <s>Hanumān</s>, who has come here.
I have been sent to you by your husband, <s>Rāma</s> of unwearied action.'

children.text: idaṃ ca puruṣavyāghraḥ śrīmān dāśarathiḥ svayam
children.translated_text: 'And this ring, a token of recognition, the illustrious son of <s>Daśaratha</s> himself, that tiger among men,
gave for you, O renowned lady.'

children.text: tad icchāmi tvayājñaptaṃ devi kiṃ karavāṇyaham
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, commanded by you, goddess, I wish to know what I should do.

children.text: rāmalakṣmaṇayoḥ pārśvaṃ nayāmi tvāṃ kim uttaram ||
children.translated_text: Shall I take you to the side of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, or what reply shall I bring?'
Hearing and recognizing this, <s>Sītā</s>, daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,

children.text: āha rāvaṇam utsādya rāghavo māṃ nayatviti ||
children.translated_text: said, 'Let <s>Rāghava</s> destroy <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and take me away.'

children.text: praṇamya śirasā devīm aham āryām aninditām
children.translated_text: Bowing my head to the goddess, the noble and blameless lady,
I asked for a token of recognition that would gladden <s>Rāghava</s>'s mind.
Thus addressed, the fair-hipped lady produced the excellent, finest jewel.

children.text: prāyacchat paramodvignā vācā māṃ saṃdideśa ha ||
children.translated_text: Very distressed, she gave it to me and instructed me with these words.
Then, having bowed to that princess, I, composed in mind,
circumambulated her respectfully and set my mind on returning here.

children.text: uttaraṃ punar evāha niścitya manasā tadā
children.translated_text: Then, having resolved it in her mind, she spoke again this reply:
"<s>Hanumān</s>, you must tell my condition to <s>Rāghava</s>.
Act in such a way that, merely on hearing it, before long those two heroes, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
together with <s>Sugrīva</s>, may come here.

children.text: yadyanyathā bhaved etad dvau māsau jīvitaṃ mama
children.translated_text: If this should happen otherwise, my life will last two months;

children.text: na māṃ drakṣyati kākutstho mriye sāham anāthavat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kākutstha</s> will not see me, for I shall die like one without a protector."

children.text: tacchrutvā karuṇaṃ vākyaṃ krodho mām abhyavartata
children.translated_text: Hearing that pitiable speech, anger came over me,

children.text: uttaraṃ ca mayā dṛṣṭaṃ kāryaśeṣam anantaram ||
children.translated_text: and immediately I saw that some remainder of the task still had to be done.
Then my body grew, then, like a mountain,
and, longing for battle, I began to destroy that grove.
When that mass of grove had been broken, and its beasts and birds were bewildered and frightened,
the <s>rākṣasīs</s> with hideous faces awoke and looked about.

children.text: māṃ ca dṛṣṭvā vane tasmin samāgamya tatastataḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing me in that grove, they came together from every side,
and those who had assembled quickly reported it to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>:

children.text: rājan vanam idaṃ durgaṃ tava bhagnaṃ durātmanā
children.translated_text: "O king, this inaccessible grove of yours has been broken by an evil-minded one,
by a monkey, O mighty one, without knowing your valor.
O lord of kings, quickly command the killing of that wicked-minded one,

children.text: vadham ājñāpaya kṣipraṃ yathāsau vilayaṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: who has acted against your pleasure, so that he may go to destruction."
Hearing this, the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s> sent out exceedingly hard-to-conquer
<s>rākṣasas</s> called Kiṃkaras, obedient to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s will.
Eighty thousand of them, with spears and clubs in their hands,
were slain by me in that part of the grove with an iron bar.

children.text: teṣāṃ tu hataśeṣā ye te gatā laghuvikramāḥ
children.translated_text: Those of them who survived the slaughter, swift in movement,
went and reported to <s>Rāvaṇa</s> that the army had been killed by me.

children.text: tato me buddhir utpannā caityaprāsādam ākramam ||
children.translated_text: Then this thought arose in me: I should attack the palace shrine.

children.text: tatrasthān rākṣasān hatvā śataṃ stambhena vai punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having killed a hundred <s>rākṣasas</s> stationed there, again with a pillar,
I angrily destroyed what was the ornament of <s>Laṅkā</s>.
Then he ordered <s>Jambumālin</s>, the son of <s>Prahasta</s>.
That strong <s>rākṣasa</s>, skilled in battle,
I struck down, together with his followers, with an exceedingly dreadful iron bar.
Hearing this, the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, sent
the mighty sons of his ministers, supplied with infantry forces.
With that very iron bar I sent them all to the abode of <s>Yama</s>.
When he heard that the sons of his ministers, swift in battle, had been killed,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> sent five heroic army commanders,

children.text: tān ahaṃ saha sainyān vai sarvān evābhyasūdayam ||
children.translated_text: and I slew all of them together with their armies.

children.text: tataḥ punar daśagrīvaḥ putram akṣaṃ mahābalam
children.translated_text: Then once more the ten-necked one sent his mighty son <s>Akṣa</s>
into battle together with many <s>rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: taṃ tu mandodarī putraṃ kumāraṃ raṇapaṇḍitam
children.translated_text: But that prince, <s>Mandodarī</s>'s son, learned in battle,
as he suddenly sprang up into the sky, I seized by the feet,
and after whirling him a hundred times, with his shield and sword, I crushed him.

children.text: tam akṣam āgataṃ bhagnaṃ niśamya sa daśānanaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that <s>Akṣa</s> had come to ruin and been broken, the ten-faced one

children.text: tata indrajitaṃ nāma dvitīyaṃ rāvaṇaḥ sutam
children.translated_text: then, enraged, assigned <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s second son,
named <s>Indrajit</s>, strong and arrogant in battle.

children.text: tasyāpyahaṃ balaṃ sarvaṃ taṃ ca rākṣasapuṃgavam
children.translated_text: Having drained the energy of all his force, and of that foremost <s>rākṣasa</s> himself,

children.text: naṣṭaujasaṃ raṇe kṛtvā paraṃ harṣam upāgamam ||
children.translated_text: in battle, I attained the highest joy.
For that mighty-armed, very strong one, with great confidence,
had been sent by <s>Rāvaṇa</s> together with proud heroes.
But with the Brahmā weapon he bound me at great speed,

children.text: rajjūbhir abhibadhnanti tato māṃ tatra rākṣasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and then the <s>rākṣasas</s> bound me there with ropes.

children.text: rāvaṇasya samīpaṃ ca gṛhītvā mām upānayan
children.translated_text: Taking hold of me, they brought me into <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s presence,
and after seeing me, wicked <s>Rāvaṇa</s> spoke with me.
He asked about my coming to <s>Laṅkā</s> and about that killing of the <s>rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: tat sarvaṃ ca mayā tatra sītārtham iti jalpitam ||
children.translated_text: and all of that was explained there by me as being for <s>Sītā</s>'s sake.
"Desiring to see her, I have come to your palace, O lord.
I am <s>Hanumān</s>, a monkey, the legitimate son of the Wind.

children.text: rāmadūtaṃ ca māṃ viddhi sugrīvasacivaṃ kapim
children.translated_text: Know me to be <s>Rāma</s>'s messenger, a monkey and minister of <s>Sugrīva</s>.
I have come here into your presence on <s>Rāma</s>'s embassy.

children.text: śṛṇu cāpi samādeśaṃ yad ahaṃ prabravīmi te
children.translated_text: Hear also the command that I speak to you:
O lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>, the lord of the monkeys speaks to you this collected speech,
joined with <s>dharma</s> (right order), advantage, and desire, wholesome like suitable food.
While I was living on Mount <s>Ṛṣyamūka</s>, rich in broad trees,
<s>Rāghava</s>, valiant in battle, entered into friendship with me.

children.text: tena me kathitaṃ rājan bhāryā me rakṣasā hṛtā
children.translated_text: He told me, O king, 'My wife has been carried off by a <s>rākṣasa</s>.

children.text: tatra sāhāyyahetor me samayaṃ kartum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: For the sake of helping in that matter, you should make an agreement with me.'
With <s>Sugrīva</s>, whose kingdom had been taken by <s>Vālin</s>, the lord,
<s>Rāghava</s>, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, made a friendship witnessed by fire.
By him <s>Vālin</s> was struck down with a single arrow in battle,
and <s>Sugrīva</s> was made the great king of the monkeys, lord of those who leap.

children.text: tasya sāhāyyam asmābhiḥ kāryaṃ sarvātmanā tviha
children.translated_text: His aid is to be rendered here by us with our whole being.
Therefore, in accordance with <s>dharma</s> (right conduct), I have been sent here into your presence.

children.text: kṣipram ānīyatāṃ sītā dīyatāṃ rāghavasya ca
children.translated_text: Let <s>Sītā</s> be brought quickly and given to <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: yāvanna harayo vīrā vidhamanti balaṃ tava ||
children.translated_text: before the heroic monkeys destroy your army.

children.text: vānarāṇāṃ prabhavo hi na kena viditaḥ purā
children.translated_text: For who has not known before the power of the monkeys?"

children.text: devatānāṃ sakāśaṃ ca ye gacchanti nimantritāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and those who, when invited, go into the presence of the gods.
When I had said, "Thus the monkey-king speaks to you,"

children.text: mām aikṣata tato ruṣṭaścakṣuṣā pradahann iva ||
children.translated_text: he then looked at me angrily, as if burning me with his eye.
By that <s>rākṣasa</s> of terrible deeds I was ordered to be killed.

children.text: tato vibhīṣaṇo nāma tasya bhrātā mahāmatiḥ
children.translated_text: Then his brother, named <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, a man of great wisdom,
pleaded with that king of <s>rākṣasas</s> on my behalf:

children.text: dūtavadhyā na dṛṣṭā hi rājaśāstreṣu rākṣasa
children.translated_text: "The killing of envoys is not seen in the royal treatises, O <s>rākṣasa</s>;
and the facts should be reported by an envoy who speaks for another's welfare.
Even when there is a very great offense, O you of incomparable valor,
mutilation of an envoy is recognized, but there is no killing here according to śāstra."
Thus addressed by <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> gave orders to those

children.text: rākṣasān etad evādya lāṅgūlaṃ dahyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: <s>rākṣasas</s>: "Today this very tail is to be burned."

children.text: tatastasya vacaḥ śrutvā mama pucchaṃ samantataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after hearing his command, all around my tail
they wrapped hempen bark-cloth and also cotton cloths.
Those fierce and powerful <s>rākṣasas</s>, fully equipped,

children.text: tad ādīpyanta me pucchaṃ hanantaḥ kāṣṭhamuṣṭibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: then set my tail on fire, striking me with sticks and fists.

children.text: baddhasya bahubhiḥ pāśair yantritasya ca rākṣasaiḥ
children.translated_text: Though I was bound with many nooses and restrained by the <s>rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: na me pīḍā bhavet kācid didṛkṣor nagarīṃ divā ||
children.translated_text: no pain at all arose in me, since I wished to see the city by daylight.

children.text: tataste rākṣasāḥ śūrā baddhaṃ mām agnisaṃvṛtam
children.translated_text: Then those heroic <s>rākṣasas</s>, with me bound and enveloped in fire,
proclaimed me along the royal road, having reached the city gate.

children.text: tato 'haṃ sumahad rūpaṃ saṃkṣipya punar ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Then I greatly contracted my own form again,

children.text: vimocayitvā taṃ bandhaṃ prakṛtiṣṭhaḥ sthitaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: freed myself from that bondage, and stood once more in my natural size.
Taking an iron club, I slew those <s>rākṣasas</s>;
then with speed I leapt upon that city gate.

children.text: pucchena ca pradīptena tāṃ purīṃ sāṭṭagopurām
children.translated_text: With my blazing tail, that city with its watchtowers and gates
I burned, unalarmed, like the fire at the end of an age burning creatures.

children.text: dagdhvā laṅkāṃ punaścaiva śaṅkā mām abhyavartata
children.translated_text: After burning <s>Laṅkā</s>, doubt again came over me:

children.text: dahatā ca mayā laṅkāṃ dagdhā sītā na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "While I was burning <s>Laṅkā</s>, <s>Sītā</s> has surely been burned."
Then I heard the auspicious words of the <s>Cāraṇas</s>,
who, speaking a wondrous report, said that <s>Jānakī</s> had not been burned.

children.text: tato me buddhir utpannā śrutvā tām adbhutāṃ giram
children.translated_text: Then, having heard that marvelous speech, an idea arose in me,

children.text: punar dṛṣṭā ca vaidehī visṛṣṭaśca tayā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Vaidehī</s> was seen again and I was again dismissed by her.
By the power of <s>Rāghava</s> and by your own splendor,

children.text: sugrīvasya ca kāryārthaṃ mayā sarvam anuṣṭhitam ||
children.translated_text: and for the purpose of <s>Sugrīva</s>'s mission, everything has been accomplished by me.

children.text: etat sarvaṃ mayā tatra yathāvad upapāditam
children.translated_text: All this was duly carried out by me there.

children.text: atra yanna kṛtaṃ śeṣaṃ tat sarvaṃ kriyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Whatever remains undone in this matter, let all that now be done."
<s>Hanumān</s>, son of the Wind, told that whole account,
and then began again to speak further words:
"<s>Rāghava</s>'s effort and <s>Sugrīva</s>'s urgency have borne fruit,

children.text: śīlam āsādya sītāyā mama ca plavanaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: through the virtue of <s>Sītā</s> and through my great leap.
Such is the virtue of noble <s>Sītā</s>, O bulls among leapers,

children.text: tapasā dhārayel lokān kruddhā vā nirdahed api ||
children.translated_text: that by her austerity she could sustain the worlds, or, if angered, could burn them up.
In every way that <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>, must be greatly favored,

children.text: yasya tāṃ spṛśato gātraṃ tapasā na vināśitam ||
children.translated_text: since, when he touched her, his body was not destroyed by her austerity.

children.text: na tad agniśikhā kuryāt saṃspṛṣṭā pāṇinā satī
children.translated_text: What a flame of fire, touched by the hand, might not do,
the daughter of <s>Janaka</s> would do, if she were made impure by anger.
In the midst of the <s>Aśoka</s> grove of wicked <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
beneath a śiṃśapā tree, the virtuous lady remained in pitiable distress.
Surrounded by <s>rākṣasīs</s>, emaciated by the torment of grief,
she was like a dim crescent moon surrounded by streaks of cloud.
<s>Vaidehī</s> gave no thought to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, arrogant in his strength;

children.text: pativratā ca suśroṇī avaṣṭabdhā ca jānakī ||
children.translated_text: the fair-hipped, devoted wife <s>Jānakī</s> remained resolute.

children.text: anuraktā hi vaidehī rāmaṃ sarvātmanā śubhā
children.translated_text: For auspicious <s>Vaidehī</s> is attached to <s>Rāma</s> with her whole self,
and her mind is fixed on <s>Rāma</s> alone, like <s>Paulomī</s> on <s>Purandara</s>.
Clad in that single garment, and covered with dust as well,
<s>Sītā</s>, her body wretched from the torment of grief, was intent on her husband's welfare.

children.text: sā mayā rākṣasīmadhye tarjyamānā muhur muhuḥ
children.translated_text: I saw that woman in the grove, among the <s>rākṣasīs</s>,

children.text: rākṣasībhir virūpābhir dṛṣṭā hi pramadā vane ||
children.translated_text: being threatened again and again by hideous <s>rākṣasīs</s>.
She wore a single braid, was miserable, wholly absorbed in thoughts of her husband,
lying on the ground, her limbs discolored, like a lotus at the coming of frost.
Having turned away from <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s purpose, resolved on dying,
the doe-eyed lady was somehow brought to trust me.

children.text: tataḥ saṃbhāṣitā caiva sarvam arthaṃ ca darśitā
children.translated_text: Then she was spoken to, and the whole matter was explained to her;
hearing of the alliance between <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Sugrīva</s>, she became joyful.
Her conduct is controlled, and her devotion to her husband is supreme.

children.text: yanna hanti daśagrīvaṃ sa mahātmā daśānanaḥ
children.translated_text: If that great-souled lady does not herself kill the ten-necked, ten-faced <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
<s>Rāma</s> will become only the instrument in his death.
Thus the highly fortunate <s>Sītā</s> remains, absorbed in grief.

children.text: yad atra pratikartavyaṃ tat sarvam upapādyatām ||
children.translated_text: Whatever must be done in this matter, let all that be arranged."
Hearing those words of his, the son of <s>Vālin</s> spoke,
after taking leave of all the great monkeys headed by <s>Jāmbavān</s>:

children.text: asminn evaṃgate kārye bhavatāṃ ca nivedite
children.translated_text: "Since the mission stands thus, and since it has been reported to you,

children.text: nyāyyaṃ sma saha vaidehyā draṣṭuṃ tau pārthivātmajau ||
children.translated_text: it is proper that we see those two royal sons together with <s>Vaidehī</s>.
Even I alone am sufficient, with force, to destroy that city,

children.text: tāṃ laṅkāṃ tarasā hantuṃ rāvaṇaṃ ca mahābalam ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Laṅkā</s> with its hosts of <s>rākṣasas</s>, and mighty <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: kiṃ punaḥ sahito vīrair balavadbhiḥ kṛtātmabhiḥ
children.translated_text: How much more when joined by heroic, powerful, self-controlled,
weapon-trained, capable leapers such as you, who desire victory."

children.text: ahaṃ tu rāvaṇaṃ yuddhe sasainyaṃ sapuraḥsaram
children.translated_text: But in battle I shall shatter <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, together with his army and those who stand before him,
together with his sons and joined with his brothers in combat.

children.text: brāhmam aindraṃ ca raudraṃ ca vāyavyaṃ vāruṇaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: The brahma, aindra, raudra, vāyavya, and likewise vāruṇa weapons,
if they are <s>Śakrajit</s>'s weapons, hard to look upon in battle,
I shall destroy them; I shall slay the <s>rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: bhavatām abhyanujñāto vikramo me ruṇaddhi tam ||
children.translated_text: With your permission, my valor will check him.
For a ceaseless shower of rocks, unequaled when released by me,

children.text: devān api raṇe hanyāt kiṃ punastānniśācarān ||
children.translated_text: would slay even the gods in battle; how much more those night-roamers?
The ocean might overstep its shore, and <s>Mandara</s> might move,
but an enemy army would not shake <s>Jāmbavān</s> in battle.
Of all the hosts of <s>rākṣasas</s>, and of those <s>rākṣasas</s> who came before,

children.text: alam eko vināśāya vīro vāyusutaḥ kapiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the heroic monkey, the son of <s>Vāyu</s>, is alone enough for their destruction.
By the immense speed of <s>Panasa</s> and of great-souled <s>Nīla</s>,
even <s>Mandara</s> would be shattered; how much more the <s>rākṣasas</s> in battle?
In wars involving gods and asuras, among gandharvas, serpents, and birds,
name an opponent for <s>Mainda</s>, or for <s>Dvivida</s>.
These two swiftest, best of leaping monkeys are sons of the <s>Aśvins</s>,
and, elated by the boon of the Grandfather, they have assumed supreme pride.
For the sake of honoring the <s>Aśvins</s>, the Grandfather of all worlds
formerly gave these two incomparable invulnerability to all beings.

children.text: varotsekena mattau ca pramathya mahatīṃ camūm
children.translated_text: And, intoxicated by confidence in that boon, after crushing a great army,
the two heroic monkeys drank the gods' nectar.
These very two, when enraged, are able to destroy <s>Laṅkā</s>,

children.text: laṅkāṃ nāśayituṃ śaktau sarve tiṣṭhantu vānarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: with its horses, chariots, and elephants; let all the other vānaras stand aside.

children.text: ayuktaṃ tu vinā devīṃ dṛṣṭavadbhiḥ plavaṃgamāḥ
children.translated_text: But, O leaping monkeys, for us who have seen the lady, it is not proper, without her,
to go near the great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭā devī na cānītā iti tatra nivedanam
children.translated_text: To report there, 'The lady has been seen but not brought back,'
seems to me improper for you, whose valor is renowned.

children.text: na hi vaḥ plavane kaścin nāpi kaścit parākrame
children.translated_text: For there is no one equal to you in leaping, nor anyone in prowess,
among the worlds with gods and daityas, O best of monkeys.
When those heroic <s>rākṣasas</s> have been slain in this way by <s>Hanumān</s>,

children.text: kim anyad atra kartavyaṃ gṛhītvā yāma jānakīm ||
children.translated_text: what else remains to be done here? Let us seize <s>Jānakī</s> and go.
To him, resolved in this way, <s>Jāmbavān</s>, the best of monkeys,
being very pleased, spoke meaningful words, for he knew what was fitting.

children.text: na tāvad eṣā matir akṣamā no yathā bhavān paśyati rājaputra
children.translated_text: So far, prince, this thought of ours is not incapable, just as you see it;

children.text: yathā tu rāmasya matir niviṣṭā tathā bhavān paśyatu kāryasiddhim ||
children.translated_text: but you should see the accomplishment of the task in the way that <s>Rāma</s>'s intention is fixed.
Then the forest-dwellers accepted <s>Jāmbavān</s>'s words,
the heroes headed by <s>Aṅgada</s>, and <s>Hanumān</s>, the great monkey.
Then all of them, joyful, with the son of <s>Vāyu</s> at their head,
the bulls among leaping monkeys, left the summit of <s>Mahendra</s> and sprang away.
Like <s>Meru</s> and <s>Mandara</s>, like intoxicated great elephants,
they were huge-bodied and mighty, seeming to cover the sky.
As though carrying with their eyes that self-possessed, mighty <s>Hanumān</s>,
who was being honored by living beings, the very swift and powerful one,
having fixed in mind the fulfillment of <s>Rāghava</s>'s purpose and the supreme fame of their lord,
their aim accomplished, they were exalted by the success of their deed.
All were eager to announce welcome news, all delighted in battle,
all high-minded and firmly resolved on service to <s>Rāma</s>.
Then those forest-dwellers, leaping and crossing through the sky,
reached a forest like <s>Nandana</s>, filled with trees and creepers.
That was the grove called Madhuvana, protected by <s>Sugrīva</s>,
unassailable to all beings and charming to every creature.

children.text: yad rakṣati mahāvīryaḥ sadā dadhimukhaḥ kapiḥ
children.translated_text: The monkey of great valor named <s>Dadhimukha</s> always guards it,
the maternal uncle of great-souled <s>Sugrīva</s>, chief of the monkeys.

children.text: te tad vanam upāgamya babhūvuḥ paramotkaṭāḥ
children.translated_text: Having come to that grove, those vānaras became exceedingly excited,
seeing the great grove dearest to the monkey-king's heart.

children.text: tataste vānarā hṛṣṭā dṛṣṭvā madhuvanaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: Then the delighted vānaras, seeing the great Madhuvana,
their bodies tawny with honey, begged the prince for the honey.
Then the prince, after honoring those elder monkeys headed by <s>Jāmbavān</s>,
granted them free leave to eat the honey.
Then, with permission given, all the forest-dwellers were overjoyed,
and, delighted, they began dancing here and there.

children.text: gāyanti kecit praṇamanti kecin nṛtyanti kecit prahasanti kecit
children.translated_text: Some sang, some bowed down, some danced, some laughed,

children.text: patanti kecid vicaranti kecit plavanti kecit pralapanti kecit ||
children.translated_text: some fell down, some roamed about, some leapt, and some babbled.

children.text: parasparaṃ kecid upāśrayante parasparaṃ kecid atibruvante
children.translated_text: Some leaned upon one another; some shouted over one another;

children.text: drumād drumaṃ kecid abhiplavante kṣitau nagāgrānnipatanti kecit ||
children.translated_text: some leapt from tree to tree, and some fell from tree-tops to the ground.
Some, with surging speed from the surface of the earth, rushed up to the tops of great trees;

children.text: gāyantam anyaḥ prahasann upaiti hasantam anyaḥ prahasann upaiti ||
children.translated_text: one came laughing up to another who was singing, and another came laughing up to one who was laughing.

children.text: rudantam anyaḥ prarudann upaiti nudantam anyaḥ praṇudann upaiti
children.translated_text: One came weeping up to one who was weeping, and another came pushing up to one who was pushing.
That monkey army became confused, its beings' movements made wild by drinking honey,

children.text: na cātra kaścin na babhūva matto na cātra kaścin na babhūva tṛptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and there was no one there who was not intoxicated, and no one there who was not satisfied.

children.text: tato vanaṃ tat paribhakṣyamāṇaṃ drumāṃśca vidhvaṃsitapatrapuṣpān
children.translated_text: Then, seeing that grove being consumed and the trees stripped of leaves and flowers,

children.text: samīkṣya kopād dadhivaktranāmā nivārayāmāsa kapiḥ kapīṃstān ||
children.translated_text: the monkey named <s>Dadhivaktra</s>, in anger, restrained those monkeys.

children.text: sa taiḥ pravṛddhaiḥ paribhartsyamāno vanasya goptā harivīravṛddhaḥ
children.translated_text: Being rebuked by those grown powerful, the aged monkey-hero, the guardian of the grove,

children.text: cakāra bhūyo matim ugratejā vanasya rakṣāṃ prati vānarebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: fierce in splendor, again formed the intention of protecting the grove from the monkeys.

children.text: uvāca kāṃścit paruṣāṇi dhṛṣṭam asaktam anyāṃśca talair jaghāna
children.translated_text: He spoke harsh words boldly to some; he ineffectively struck others with slaps.

children.text: sametya kaiścit kalahaṃ cakāra tathaiva sāmnopajagāma kāṃścit ||
children.translated_text: With some he joined in quarrels, and others he approached with conciliatory words.
But by those monkeys, whose speed could not be checked because of intoxication, and who could not be restrained by his strength,
he was assaulted by them as they gathered without fear, and he was dragged about, with no regard for the fault.

children.text: nakhaistudanto daśanair daśantas talaiśca pādaiśca samāpnuvantaḥ
children.translated_text: Piercing him with their nails, biting him with their teeth, and striking him with palms and feet,

children.text: madāt kapiṃ taṃ kapayaḥ samagrā mahāvanaṃ nirviṣayaṃ ca cakruḥ ||
children.translated_text: all the monkeys, drunk with honey, ruined that monkey and made the great grove desolate.
Then <s>Hanumān</s>, best of monkeys, a bull among vānaras, said to them:
"Monkeys, with undisturbed minds, enjoy the honey."
Hearing <s>Hanumān</s>'s words, <s>Aṅgada</s>, foremost of the monkeys,
answered with a pleased heart, "Let the monkeys drink the honey.
Since the task has certainly been accomplished, <s>Hanumān</s>'s word

children.text: akāryam api kartavyaṃ kim aṅga punar īdṛśam ||
children.translated_text: must be carried out by me even if it were improper; how much more when it is such as this."
Hearing the words from <s>Aṅgada</s>'s mouth, the bulls among vānaras,
delighted, honored him in reply, saying, "Good, good!"
After all the monkeys had honored <s>Aṅgada</s>, that bull among vānaras,

children.text: jagmur madhuvanaṃ yatra nadīvega iva drutam ||
children.translated_text: they went swiftly, like the current of a river, to where <s>Madhuvana</s> was.

children.text: te prahṛṣṭā madhuvanaṃ pālān ākramya vīryataḥ
children.translated_text: Those delighted ones forcefully overran the guards in <s>Madhuvana</s>,

children.text: atisargācca paṭavo dṛṣṭvā śrutvā ca maithilīm ||
children.translated_text: bold because of the permission, and because they had seen and heard of <s>Maithilī</s>.

children.text: utpatya ca tataḥ sarve vanapālān samāgatāḥ
children.translated_text: Then all of them sprang up, and when the assembled grove-guards came,
they beat them by the hundreds as they clung to <s>Madhuvana</s> at that time.
Taking honeycombs the size of troughs in their arms,

children.text: ghnanti sma sahitāḥ sarve bhakṣayanti tathāpare ||
children.translated_text: they all together smashed them, while others ate.
Some, tawny with honey, drank the honey and threw it away.

children.text: madhūcchiṣṭena kecic ca jaghnur anyonyam utkaṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Others, wild, struck one another with the leavings of honey.
Others stood at the roots of trees, holding branches,
and, utterly weary from intoxication, spread leaves and lay down.
The leapers became like madmen, drunk with honey and full of joy.
Some threw one another about, and others stumbled.

children.text: kecit kṣveḍān prakurvanti kecit kūjanti hṛṣṭavat
children.translated_text: Some made roaring cries; some cooed joyfully.

children.text: harayo madhunā mattāḥ kecit suptā mahītale ||
children.translated_text: The monkeys, drunk with honey, lay asleep on the ground, some of them.

children.text: ye 'pyatra madhupālāḥ syuḥ preṣyā dadhimukhasya tu
children.translated_text: Whatever honey-guards were there, servants of <s>Dadhimukha</s>,

children.text: te 'pi tair vānarair bhīmaiḥ pratiṣiddhā diśo gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: they too, opposed by those terrible monkeys, fled in all directions.
Dragged by the knees and shown the heavenly road,
they went, deeply distressed, and spoke these words to <s>Dadhimukha</s>:
"By those to whom <s>Hanumān</s> has granted permission, <s>Madhuvana</s> has been violently destroyed.

children.text: vayaṃ ca jānubhiḥ kṛṣṭā devamārgaṃ ca darśitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: We have been dragged by the knees and shown the heavenly road."
Then the monkey <s>Dadhimukha</s>, the grove-guardian there, became angry.

children.text: hataṃ madhuvanaṃ śrutvā sāntvayāmāsa tān harīn ||
children.translated_text: Hearing that <s>Madhuvana</s> had been destroyed, he consoled those monkeys.
"Come, come. Let us go; by force we shall restrain
the monkeys who are over-proud and eating the honey."
Hearing these words of <s>Dadhimukha</s>, the bulls among vānaras,

children.text: punar vīrā madhuvanaṃ tenaiva sahitā yayuḥ ||
children.translated_text: those heroes went again to <s>Madhuvana</s> together with him.
In their midst <s>Dadhimukha</s>, taking hold of a very great tree,

children.text: samabhyadhāvad vegena te ca sarve plavaṃgamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: rushed forward at speed, and so did all those leapers.
Those monkeys, in anger, took up rocks, trees,
and stones as well, and advanced to where those elephantine monkeys were.
Placing that command of their master in their hearts, those heroes
rushed swiftly forward, armed with sāla trees, palms, and rocks.
The heroic guards there, by the thousands, attacked
the monkeys standing in trees and on the ground, those who were arrogant with strength.
Then, seeing <s>Dadhimukha</s> angry, the foremost monkeys,
headed by <s>Hanumān</s>, rushed forward at speed at that time.
As that mighty-armed, very strong one came on, tree in hand,
the enraged <s>Aṅgada</s> struck that venerable elder there with both arms.

children.text: madāndhaśca na vedainam āryako 'yaṃ mameti saḥ
children.translated_text: Blinded by intoxication, he did not recognize him as, "This is my elder."
Then he quickly crushed him forcefully to the ground.
With his arm broken, his face turned away, bewildered, and sprinkled with blood,
the heroic elephant among monkeys suddenly fainted for a moment.
Somehow freed from those monkeys, that bull among vānaras
went aside and spoke to the servants who had come to him:

children.text: ete tiṣṭhantu gacchāmo bhartā no yatra vānaraḥ
children.translated_text: "Let these remain here. Let us go to where our lord, the monkey
<s>Sugrīva</s> of broad neck, stands together with <s>Rāma</s>.
I shall report all the blame concerning <s>Aṅgada</s> to the king.
When that intolerant one hears the report, he will have the monkeys killed.
For this <s>Madhuvana</s> is dear to the great-souled <s>Sugrīva</s>,
divine, inherited from his fathers and grandfathers, and hard even for the gods to approach.
By punishment <s>Sugrīva</s> will have all these monkeys killed,
greedy for honey and whose lives are spent, together with their friends.
For these wicked ones, who have despised the king's command, deserve death.
Our anger, born from indignation, will bear fruit."
Having spoken thus, mighty <s>Dadhimukha</s> addressed the grove-guards.
He suddenly sprang up and went, accompanied by the forest-guards.
For in only the space of a wink he reached the forest dwelling
where wise <s>Sugrīva</s>, the monkey son of the thousand-rayed Sun, was.

children.text: rāmaṃ ca lakṣmaṇaṃ caiva dṛṣṭvā sugrīvam eva ca
children.translated_text: Having seen <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and also <s>Sugrīva</s> himself,
he dropped down from the sky onto the level earth.
When he had fallen, the very powerful one, surrounded by all those
forest-guards, the monkey <s>Dadhimukha</s>, supreme lord of the guards,

children.text: sa dīnavadano bhūtvā kṛtvā śirasi cāñjalim
children.translated_text: with a dejected face, placing his joined palms on his head,
pressed <s>Sugrīva</s>'s two auspicious feet with his head.
Then, seeing the monkey fallen with his head
the bull among monkeys, his heart alarmed, spoke these words:

children.text: uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha kasmāt tvaṃ pādayoḥ patito mama
children.translated_text: "Get up, get up. Why have you fallen at my feet?

children.text: abhayaṃ te bhaved vīra satyam evābhidhīyatām ||
children.translated_text: Let there be safety for you, hero; let the truth be told."
Then, reassured by that great-souled <s>Sugrīva</s>,
the very wise <s>Dadhimukha</s> rose and spoke this speech:
"Neither by <s>Ṛkṣarajas</s>, O king, nor by you, nor by <s>Vālin</s>,

children.text: vanaṃ nisṛṣṭapūrvaṃ hi bhakṣitaṃ tat tu vānaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: was the grove ever before released for use; but it has now been consumed by monkeys.
They also assaulted us when they were restrained by the forest-guards;
paying no heed to us, they eat and drink the honey.
What is left here they throw away, while others go on eating;

children.text: nivāryamāṇāste sarve bhruvau vai darśayanti hi ||
children.translated_text: and when they are all restrained, they merely show their brows in anger.
These guards, more and more enraged, were likewise overpowered by them
while trying to drive them from that grove, by the angry foremost monkeys.
Then by those many heroic monkeys, O bull among monkeys,
with eyes reddened in anger, the forest-guards were violently shaken.

children.text: pāṇibhir nihatāḥ kecit kecij jānubhir āhatāḥ
children.translated_text: Some were struck with hands; others were hit with knees;
they were dragged about at will and shown the path of the gods.

children.text: evam ete hatāḥ śūrāstvayi tiṣṭhati bhartari
children.translated_text: Thus these brave ones have been beaten, while you, their lord, are alive,

children.text: kṛtsnaṃ madhuvanaṃ caiva prakāmaṃ taiḥ prabhakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: and the whole <s>Madhuvana</s> is being freely devoured by them."
As <s>Sugrīva</s>, the bull among monkeys, was being informed in this way,
the very wise <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, slayer of enemy heroes, asked him:

children.text: kim ayaṃ vānaro rājan vanapaḥ pratyupasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: "What has this monkey, O king, this forest-keeper who has come here,

children.text: kaṃ cārtham abhinirdiśya duḥkhito vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: indicated as his purpose, and why did he speak sorrowfully?"
Thus addressed by great-souled <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
<s>Sugrīva</s>, skilled in speech, replied to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> with these words:

children.text: ārya lakṣmaṇa saṃprāha vīro dadhimukhaḥ kapiḥ
children.translated_text: "Noble <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the heroic monkey <s>Dadhimukha</s> reports
that the honey has been consumed by the monkeys, heroes headed by <s>Aṅgada</s>.
Such a proceeding would not belong to them if they had not accomplished their task;

children.text: vanaṃ yathābhipannaṃ taiḥ sādhitaṃ karma vānaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: since they have attacked the grove in this way, the mission has been accomplished by the monkeys.

children.text: dṛṣṭā devī na saṃdeho na cānyena hanūmatā
children.translated_text: The lady has been seen; there is no doubt. And by none other than <s>Hanumān</s>;

children.text: na hyanyaḥ sādhane hetuḥ karmaṇo 'sya hanūmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: for no one other than <s>Hanumān</s> is the cause of accomplishing this mission.
Success in the task, and intelligence in <s>Hanumān</s>, the foremost monkey,

children.text: vyavasāyaśca vīryaṃ ca śrutaṃ cāpi pratiṣṭhitam ||
children.translated_text: as well as resolution, strength, and learning, are firmly established.

children.text: jāmbavān yatra netā syād aṅgadasya baleśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Where <s>Jāmbavān</s> is the leader and <s>Aṅgada</s> the lord of the troop,
and <s>Hanumān</s> too is the guide, its outcome cannot be otherwise.
The heroes headed by <s>Aṅgada</s> have indeed destroyed <s>Madhuvana</s>,
the foremost monkeys who had searched the southern quarter and returned.

children.text: āgataiśca praviṣṭaṃ tad yathā madhuvanaṃ hi taiḥ
children.translated_text: And since, having returned, they entered <s>Madhuvana</s> in that way,

children.text: dharṣitaṃ ca vanaṃ kṛtsnam upayuktaṃ ca vānaraiḥ
children.translated_text: and the whole grove has been assaulted and used up by the monkeys,
and the assembled guards were stopped and struck with knees,

children.text: etadartham ayaṃ prāpto vaktuṃ madhuravāg iha
children.translated_text: for this reason this sweet-speaking one has come here to speak,
the monkey named <s>Dadhimukha</s>, famed for valor.

children.text: dṛṣṭā sītā mahābāho saumitre paśya tattvataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s> has been seen, mighty-armed <s>Saumitri</s>; see this truly,

children.text: abhigamya yathā sarve pibanti madhu vānarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: from the way all the monkeys approach and drink the honey.
For without having seen <s>Vaidehī</s>, O renowned bull among men,
the forest-dwellers would not ravage the divine grove granted as a boon."
Then righteous <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, together with <s>Rāghava</s>, became delighted,
hearing the speech pleasant to the ear that had fallen from <s>Sugrīva</s>'s mouth.
<s>Rāma</s> rejoiced greatly, and so did <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> of great fame.
Having heard this from <s>Dadhimukha</s>, <s>Sugrīva</s> also rejoiced,
and <s>Sugrīva</s> again addressed the forest-keeper with these words:

children.text: prīto 'smi saumya yad bhuktaṃ vanaṃ taiḥ kṛtakarmabhiḥ
children.translated_text: "I am pleased, gentle one, that the grove has been consumed by those who have accomplished their task.
The conduct of those who have done their work is pardoned, and deserves pardon.
I wish quickly to see those branch-roaming monkeys, with <s>Hanumān</s> at their head, proud as the king of beasts,

children.text: draṣṭuṃ kṛtārthān saha rāghavābhyāṃ śrotuṃ ca sītādhigame prayatnam ||
children.translated_text: who have achieved their purpose, together with the two <s>Rāghavas</s>, and to hear about the effort by which <s>Sītā</s> was found."
Thus addressed by <s>Sugrīva</s>, the monkey <s>Dadhimukha</s> was delighted;
he saluted <s>Rāghava</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and <s>Sugrīva</s>.

children.text: sa praṇamya ca sugrīvaṃ rāghavau ca mahābalau
children.translated_text: Having bowed to <s>Sugrīva</s> and to the two mighty <s>Rāghavas</s>,

children.text: vānaraiḥ sahitaiḥ śūrair divam evotpapāta ha ||
children.translated_text: he sprang straight up into the sky with the assembled heroic monkeys.

children.text: sa yathaivāgataḥ pūrvaṃ tathaiva tvarito gataḥ
children.translated_text: As he had come before, so he went back quickly;

children.text: nipatya gaganād bhūmau tad vanaṃ praviveśa ha ||
children.translated_text: dropping from the sky to the earth, he entered that grove.
Having entered <s>Madhuvana</s>, he saw the monkey troop-leaders,
all intoxicated, excited, and urinating honey-water.

children.text: sa tān upāgamad vīro baddhvā karapuṭāñjalim
children.translated_text: The hero approached them, joining his hollowed hands in <s>añjali</s>.

children.text: uvāca vacanaṃ ślakṣṇam idaṃ hṛṣṭavad aṅgadam ||
children.translated_text: he spoke these gentle words to delighted <s>Aṅgada</s>:

children.text: saumya roṣo na kartavyo yad ebhir abhivāritaḥ
children.translated_text: "Gentle one, you should not be angry because these men stopped you.
Through ignorance and anger, the guards kept you back.
You are the crown prince and the lord of this forest, mighty one.

children.text: maurkhyāt pūrvaṃ kṛto doṣastad bhavān kṣantum arhati ||
children.translated_text: The fault was committed earlier through foolishness; therefore you ought to forgive it.

children.text: yathaiva hi pitā te 'bhūt pūrvaṃ harigaṇeśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: For just as your father formerly was lord of the hosts of monkeys,

children.text: tathā tvam api sugrīvo nānyastu harisattama ||
children.translated_text: so too are you, and so is <s>Sugrīva</s>; there is no other, best of monkeys.

children.text: ākhyātaṃ hi mayā gatvā pitṛvyasya tavānagha
children.translated_text: Going to your uncle, sinless one, I have already reported
the arrival here of all these forest-ranging monkeys.
When he heard of your coming, together with these monkey troop-leaders,

children.text: prahṛṣṭo na tu ruṣṭo 'sau vanaṃ śrutvā pradharṣitam ||
children.translated_text: he was delighted, not angry, on hearing that the grove had been ravaged.
Your uncle, <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the monkeys, was delighted with me,

children.text: śīghraṃ preṣaya sarvāṃstān iti hovāca pārthivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the king said, 'Send them all quickly.'
Hearing this gentle speech of <s>Dadhimukha</s>, <s>Aṅgada</s>,
the best of monkeys, skilled in speech, spoke these words to those monkeys:
"I think this event has been heard by <s>Rāma</s>, O leaders of monkey troops.

children.text: tat kṣamaṃ neha naḥ sthātuṃ kṛte kārye paraṃtapāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore it is proper for us not to stay here, since the task has been accomplished, scorcher of foes.
Having drunk honey as we wished and rested, O forest-rangers,

children.text: kiṃ śeṣaṃ gamanaṃ tatra sugrīvo yatra me guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: what remains except to go there, where <s>Sugrīva</s>, my elder, is?

children.text: sarve yathā māṃ vakṣyanti sametya hariyūthapāḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever all the monkey troop-leaders say to me when they have assembled,

children.text: tathāsmi kartā kartavye bhavadbhiḥ paravān aham ||
children.translated_text: that I shall do in the matter to be done; I am dependent on you.
I am not able to command you, although I am crown prince.
Since you have accomplished the mission, it would not be proper for me to constrain you."
When <s>Aṅgada</s> had spoken thus, hearing his unfailing words,
the forest-dwellers, delighted in mind, said these words:

children.text: evaṃ vakṣyati ko rājan prabhuḥ san vānararṣabha
children.translated_text: "Who, O king, would speak in this way while being the lord, bull among monkeys?
Everyone intoxicated by the pride of power thinks, 'I alone am everything.'

children.text: tava cedaṃ susadṛśaṃ vākyaṃ nānyasya kasyacit
children.translated_text: But this speech is entirely worthy of you, and of no one else.
For your humility declares your future good fortune.

children.text: sarve vayam api prāptāstatra gantuṃ kṛtakṣaṇāḥ
children.translated_text: We too have all reached the moment for going there,

children.text: sa yatra harivīrāṇāṃ sugrīvaḥ patir avyayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: where <s>Sugrīva</s>, unfailing lord of the monkey heroes, is.

children.text: tvayā hyanuktair haribhir naiva śakyaṃ padāt padam
children.translated_text: Without being directed by you, the monkeys cannot take even one step

children.text: kvacid gantuṃ hariśreṣṭha brūmaḥ satyam idaṃ tu te ||
children.translated_text: to go anywhere, best of monkeys; this truth we tell you."

children.text: evaṃ tu vadatāṃ teṣām aṅgadaḥ pratyabhāṣata
children.translated_text: As they were speaking in this way, <s>Aṅgada</s> answered them,
and saying, 'Very well, let us go,' he sprang up from the earth.
As he sprang up, all those monkey troop-leaders sprang up after him,
filling the sky so that no empty sky remained, like fires flung upward in sacrifice.
Those swift leaping monkeys suddenly rose into the air,
roaring with a great sound like clouds driven by the wind.
When <s>Aṅgada</s> had not yet arrived, <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the monkeys,
spoke to lotus-eyed <s>Rāma</s>, who was stricken with grief:

children.text: samāśvasihi bhadraṃ te dṛṣṭā devī na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: "Take heart; good fortune to you. The lady has been seen, without doubt.

children.text: nāgantum iha śakyaṃ tair atīte samaye hi naḥ ||
children.translated_text: For otherwise it would not be possible for them to come here after our appointed time had passed.

children.text: na matsakāśam āgacchet kṛtye hi vinipātite
children.translated_text: The crown prince, mighty-armed <s>Aṅgada</s>, foremost of leapers,
would not come near me if the task had miscarried.
If such conduct belonged to men who had not accomplished their task,
he would have a downcast face and a mind confused and shaken.
This Madhuvana is my paternal and ancestral possession, protected by those before me.

children.text: na me madhuvanaṃ hanyād ahṛṣṭaḥ plavageśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The lord of leapers would not damage it unless he were delighted.
O <s>Rāma</s>, noble son of <s>Kausalyā</s>, take heart, steadfast one.

children.text: dṛṣṭā devī na saṃdeho na cānyena hanūmatā
children.translated_text: The lady has been seen, no doubt, and by none other than <s>Hanumān</s>.

children.text: na hyanyaḥ karmaṇo hetuḥ sādhane tadvidho bhavet ||
children.translated_text: For no other cause of success in this undertaking could be of that kind.
In <s>Hanumān</s>, best of the intelligent, there are success and intelligence,

children.text: vyavasāyaśca vīryaṃ ca sūrye teja iva dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: resolution and valor, as radiance is certainly in the sun.

children.text: jāmbavān yatra netā syād aṅgadaśca baleśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Where <s>Jāmbavān</s> is the guide, <s>Aṅgada</s> lord of strength,
and <s>Hanumān</s> too the one who presides, its outcome cannot be otherwise.
Do not be beset by anxiety now, you of immeasurable valor."
Then he heard a chattering cry nearby in the sky,
of the forest-dwellers roaring, proud of <s>Hanumān</s>'s deed,
as they came to <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, seeming to proclaim their success.

children.text: tataḥ śrutvā ninādaṃ taṃ kapīnāṃ kapisattamaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, hearing that roar of the monkeys, the best of monkeys
became joyful in mind, with his long tail curled upward.
Those monkeys also arrived, eager to see <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: aṅgadaṃ purataḥ kṛtvā hanūmantaṃ ca vānaram ||
children.translated_text: placing <s>Aṅgada</s> in front, and the monkey <s>Hanumān</s> as well.
Those heroes headed by <s>Aṅgada</s>, delighted and filled with joy,
alighted near the monkey king and <s>Rāghava</s>.
Then mighty-armed <s>Hanumān</s>, bowing with his head,
reported to <s>Rāghava</s> that the lady was self-controlled and unharmed.
When the goal was certain through that son of the Wind,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, pleased, looked with honor upon delighted <s>Sugrīva</s>.
Then <s>Rāghava</s>, destroyer of enemy heroes, rejoicing with affection,
looked upon <s>Hanumān</s> with great esteem.

children.text: tataḥ prasravaṇaṃ śailaṃ te gatvā citrakānanam
children.translated_text: Then, having gone to Mount <s>Prasravaṇa</s>, with its variegated groves,

children.text: praṇamya śirasā rāmaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahābalam ||
children.translated_text: and having bowed with their heads to <s>Rāma</s> and mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
placing the crown prince before them and saluting <s>Sugrīva</s>,
they then began to tell the news of <s>Sītā</s>.
Her confinement in <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s inner quarters and the threats made by the <s>rākṣasīs</s>,

children.text: rāme samanurāgaṃ ca yaścāpi samayaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: her deep love for <s>Rāma</s>, and also the time limit that had been fixed;

children.text: etad ākhyānti te sarve harayo rāmasaṃnidhau
children.translated_text: all the monkeys reported this in <s>Rāma</s>'s presence.
Hearing that <s>Vaidehī</s> was unharmed, <s>Rāma</s> then spoke further:

children.text: kva sītā vartate devī kathaṃ ca mayi vartate
children.translated_text: "Where is the goddess <s>Sītā</s> staying, and how does she feel toward me?

children.text: etanme sarvam ākhyāta vaidehīṃ prati vānarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Tell me all this concerning <s>Vaidehī</s>, O <s>vānaras</s>."
Hearing <s>Rāma</s>'s words, the monkeys in <s>Rāma</s>'s presence
urged <s>Hanumān</s>, who knew the full account of <s>Sītā</s>.
Then, hearing their words, <s>Hanumān</s>, son of the Wind,

children.text: uvāca vākyaṃ vākyajñaḥ sītāyā darśanaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: skilled in speech, told the story of how he had seen <s>Sītā</s>:
"After crossing the ocean, a hundred yojanas wide,
I went in search of <s>Jānakī</s> <s>Sītā</s>, wishing to see her.
There, on the southern shore of the southern ocean,
stands the city called <s>Laṅkā</s>, belonging to wicked <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: tatra dṛṣṭā mayā sītā rāvaṇāntaḥpure satī
children.translated_text: There I saw <s>Sītā</s>, the virtuous woman, in <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s inner quarters,

children.text: saṃnyasya tvayi jīvantī rāmā rāma manoratham ||
children.translated_text: living with her desire fixed on you, O <s>Rāma</s>, and placing her hope in <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭā me rākṣasīmadhye tarjyamānā muhur muhuḥ
children.translated_text: I saw her among the <s>rākṣasīs</s>, threatened again and again,
guarded in the pleasure grove by hideous <s>rākṣasīs</s>.
The goddess, though worthy of no sorrow through you, is falling into misery,
confined in <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s inner quarters and closely guarded by <s>rākṣasīs</s>.
She wears a single braid, is miserable, and is wholly absorbed in thought of you,
lying on the ground, her limbs discolored, like a lotus at the coming of frost.
Rejecting <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s purpose and resolved on death,

children.text: devī kathaṃcit kākutstha tvanmanā mārgitā mayā ||
children.translated_text: the goddess, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, was somehow found by me, her mind fixed on you.
O sinless one, as I slowly recited the fame of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> line,
I brought her to trust me, O tiger among men.

children.text: tataḥ saṃbhāṣitā devī sarvam arthaṃ ca darśitā
children.translated_text: Then the goddess was addressed, and the whole matter was explained to her;
hearing of the friendship between <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Sugrīva</s>, she became joyful.
Her conduct is restrained, and so too is her devotion to you.
Thus, O greatly fortunate one, I saw the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,
joined with fierce austerity through devotion to you, O bull among men.

children.text: abhijñānaṃ ca me dattaṃ yathāvṛttaṃ tavāntike
children.translated_text: She gave me a token of recognition, the incident as it occurred in your presence,
on <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, O wise <s>Rāghava</s>, concerning the crow.
'<s>Rāma</s>, the tiger among men, must be informed by you, O son of the Wind,

children.text: akhileneha yad dṛṣṭam iti mām āha jānakī ||
children.translated_text: of everything, fully, that has been seen here,' so <s>Jānakī</s> said to me.
'And this, carefully preserved with effort, is to be given to him,
while these words are spoken in <s>Sugrīva</s>'s hearing.
This splendid crest-jewel has been carefully guarded by me for you;
and remember the tilaka of red arsenic,' she said.
'This splendid jewel, born of water, has been sent out by me to you.

children.text: etaṃ dṛṣṭvā pramodiṣye vyasane tvām ivānagha ||
children.translated_text: Seeing this in misfortune, I shall rejoice as if seeing you, O sinless one.
I shall sustain my life for one month, O son of <s>Daśaratha</s>;

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ māsānna jīveyaṃ rakṣasāṃ vaśam āgatā ||
children.translated_text: after a month I shall not live, having fallen under the power of the <s>rākṣasas</s>.'

children.text: iti mām abravīt sītā kṛśāṅgī dharmacāriṇī
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Sītā</s>, emaciated and devoted to <s>dharma</s>, spoke to me,
confined in <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s inner quarters, with eyes wide like a frightened doe.

children.text: etad eva mayākhyātaṃ sarvaṃ rāghava yad yathā
children.translated_text: All this, O <s>Rāghava</s>, has been told by me exactly as it happened.
By every means, let a crossing over the waters of the ocean now be arranged."

children.text: tau jātāśvāsau rājaputrau viditvā taccābhijñānaṃ rāghavāya pradāya
children.translated_text: When the two princes had regained hope, he gave that token of recognition to <s>Rāghava</s>;

children.text: devyā cākhyātaṃ sarvam evānupūrvyād vācā sampūrṇaṃ vāyuputraḥ śaśaṃsa ||
children.translated_text: the son of the Wind fully related in speech everything told by the goddess, in proper order.
Thus addressed by <s>Hanumān</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>,

children.text: taṃ maṇiṃ hṛdaye kṛtvā praruroda salakṣmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: placed the jewel against his heart and, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, burst into tears.

children.text: taṃ tu dṛṣṭvā maṇiśreṣṭhaṃ rāghavaḥ śokakarśitaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that best of jewels, <s>Rāghava</s>, wasted by grief,
with both eyes filled with tears, said this to <s>Sugrīva</s>:

children.text: yathaiva dhenuḥ sravati snehād vatsasya vatsalā
