children.translated_text: "Just as an affectionate cow lets milk flow out of love for her calf,
so too my heart melts at the sight of this jewel.

children.text: maṇiratnam idaṃ dattaṃ vaidehyāḥ śvaśureṇa me
children.translated_text: This jewel was given to <s>Vaidehī</s> by my father-in-law;

children.text: vadhūkāle yathā baddham adhikaṃ mūrdhni śobhate ||
children.translated_text: when fastened on her head at the time of marriage, it shone surpassingly.
For this jewel, born of water and honored as excellent,
was given by wise <s>Śakra</s>, who was supremely pleased at a sacrifice.

children.text: imaṃ dṛṣṭvā maṇiśreṣṭhaṃ tathā tātasya darśanam
children.translated_text: Seeing this best of jewels, dear one, today I feel as though I have seen my father,
and also the mighty lord of <s>Vaideha</s>.

children.text: ayaṃ hi śobhate tasyāḥ priyāyā mūrdhni me maṇiḥ
children.translated_text: For this jewel shines on the head of that beloved woman of mine;

children.text: adyāsya darśanenāhaṃ prāptāṃ tām iva cintaye ||
children.translated_text: by seeing it today, I imagine that I have obtained her.

children.text: kim āha sītā vaidehī brūhi saumya punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: What did <s>Sītā</s> <s>Vaidehī</s> say? Tell me again and again, dear one,
sprinkling me, as if I were lifeless, with the water of her words.

children.text: itastu kiṃ duḥkhataraṃ yad imaṃ vārisaṃbhavam
children.translated_text: What could be more painful than this, O <s>Saumitri</s>,

children.text: maṇiṃ paśyāmi saumitre vaidehīm āgataṃ vinā ||
children.translated_text: that I see this water-born jewel come here without <s>Vaidehī</s>?

children.text: ciraṃ jīvati vaidehī yadi māsaṃ dhariṣyati
children.translated_text: <s>Vaidehī</s> will be living long indeed if she can hold out for a month;

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ saumya na jīveyaṃ vinā tām asitekṣaṇām ||
children.translated_text: I, dear one, would not live for a moment without that dark-eyed woman.

children.text: naya mām api taṃ deśaṃ yatra dṛṣṭā mama priyā
children.translated_text: Take me also to that place where my beloved was seen.

children.text: na tiṣṭheyaṃ kṣaṇam api pravṛttim upalabhya ca ||
children.translated_text: Having learned this news, I could not remain here even for a moment.

children.text: kathaṃ sā mama suśroṇī bhīrubhīruḥ satī tadā
children.translated_text: How is my fair-hipped one, timid among the timid and virtuous, then
standing amid those dreadful, terrifying <s>rākṣasas</s>?
Surely, like the autumn moon facing darkness and covered by clouds,

children.text: āvṛtaṃ vadanaṃ tasyā na virājati rākṣasaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: her face, covered by <s>rākṣasas</s>, does not shine.

children.text: kim āha sītā hanumaṃstattvataḥ kathayasva me
children.translated_text: What did <s>Sītā</s> say, <s>Hanumān</s>? Tell me truly.
By this I shall live, like a sick man by medicine."

children.text: madhurā madhurālāpā kim āha mama bhāminī
children.translated_text: What did my sweet, sweet-speaking beloved say,
that fair-hipped lady separated from me? Tell me, <s>Hanumān</s>.

children.text: duḥkhād duḥkhataraṃ prāpya kathaṃ jīvati jānakī ||
children.translated_text: Having reached a sorrow still more grievous than sorrow, how does <s>Jānakī</s> live?
Thus addressed by the great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>, <s>Hanumān</s>
reported to <s>Rāghava</s> everything spoken by <s>Sītā</s>.
The lady <s>Jānakī</s>, O bull among men, said this:
a token of recognition from a former event at <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, just as it happened.

children.text: sukhasuptā tvayā sārdhaṃ jānakī pūrvam utthitā
children.translated_text: When <s>Jānakī</s>, who had slept happily with you before, had risen first,
a crow suddenly flew up and scratched her between the breasts.
Then, in turn, you slept in the lady's lap, O elder brother of <s>Bharata</s>,

children.text: punaśca kila pakṣī sa devyā janayati vyathām ||
children.translated_text: and again, so it was, that bird caused pain to the lady.

children.text: tataḥ punar upāgamya virarāda bhṛśaṃ kila
children.translated_text: Then it came back again and, indeed, scratched her violently;
then you were awakened by her, sprinkled with blood.
By that same crow she was continually being tormented,
and you, sleeping happily, O scorcher of foes, were awakened by the lady.

children.text: tāṃ tu dṛṣṭvā mahābāho rāditāṃ ca stanāntare
children.translated_text: Seeing her then, O mighty-armed one, scratched between the breasts,
you spoke, breathing hard in anger like a venomous serpent:

children.text: nakhāgraiḥ kena te bhīru dāritaṃ tu stanāntaram
children.translated_text: 'By whom, timid one, has the space between your breasts been torn with the tips of nails?
Who is playing with an angry five-mouthed serpent?'
Looking around, you suddenly saw the crow,

children.text: nakhaiḥ sarudhirais tīkṣṇair mām evābhimukhaṃ sthitam ||
children.translated_text: standing facing me with sharp nails stained with blood.

children.text: sutaḥ kila sa śakrasya vāyasaḥ patatāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: That crow, they say, was the son of <s>Śakra</s>, the best of birds,
a swift mover through the regions of the earth, equal to the wind in speed.
Then, O mighty-armed one, your eyes rolling with anger toward him,

children.text: vāyase tvaṃ kṛthāḥ krūrāṃ matiṃ matimatāṃ vara ||
children.translated_text: you formed a cruel resolve against the crow, O best of the wise.

children.text: sa darbhaṃ saṃstarād gṛhya brahmāstreṇa nyayojayaḥ
children.translated_text: Taking a blade of darbha-grass from the bedding, you charged it with the <s>brahmāstra</s> (Brahmā-weapon).

children.text: sa dīpta iva kālāgnir jajvālābhimukhaḥ khagam ||
children.translated_text: Blazing like the fire of time, it flamed forth toward the bird.

children.text: sa tvaṃ pradīptaṃ cikṣepa darbhaṃ taṃ vāyasaṃ prati
children.translated_text: Then you hurled that blazing blade of grass at the crow,

children.text: tatastu vāyasaṃ dīptaḥ sa darbho 'nujagāma ha ||
children.translated_text: and that blazing darbha pursued the crow.

children.text: sa pitrā ca parityaktaḥ suraiḥ sarvair maharṣibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Abandoned by his father, by all the gods, and by the great seers,
he went around the three worlds and found no protector.

children.text: taṃ tvaṃ nipatitaṃ bhūmau śaraṇyaḥ śaraṇāgatam
children.translated_text: When he fell to the ground before you, seeking refuge, you, who give refuge,
O <s>Kākutstha</s>, protected him out of compassion, though he deserved death.

children.text: mogham astraṃ na śakyaṃ tu kartum ityeva rāghava
children.translated_text: But, O <s>Rāghava</s>, the weapon could not be made fruitless;

children.text: tatastasyākṣi kākasya hinasti sma sa dakṣiṇam ||
children.translated_text: therefore it struck out that crow's right eye.

children.text: rāma tvāṃ sa namaskṛtvā rājño daśarathasya ca
children.translated_text: Then, after bowing to you, <s>Rāma</s>, and to king <s>Daśaratha</s>,

children.text: visṛṣṭastu tadā kākaḥ pratipede kham ālayam ||
children.translated_text: the crow was released and returned to his dwelling in the sky.

children.text: evam astravidāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ sattvavāñ śīlavān api
children.translated_text: Being thus the foremost knower of weapons, and also strong and virtuous,

children.text: kimartham astraṃ rakṣaḥsu na yojayasi rāghava ||
children.translated_text: why, O <s>Rāghava</s>, do you not employ a weapon against the <s>rākṣasas</s>?

children.text: na nāgā nāpi gandharvā nāsurā na marudgaṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Neither nāgas, nor gandharvas, nor asuras, nor hosts of Maruts,

children.text: tava rāma mukhe sthātuṃ śaktāḥ pratisamādhitum ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Rāma</s>, are able to stand before your face in opposition.
If there is concern for me in you, who are mighty in valor,

children.text: kṣipraṃ suniśitair bāṇair hanyatāṃ yudhi rāvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: let <s>Rāvaṇa</s> quickly be slain in battle with well-sharpened arrows.

children.text: bhrātur ādeśam ādāya lakṣmaṇo vā paraṃtapaḥ
children.translated_text: Or why does <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, taking his brother's command, O scorcher of foes,

children.text: sa kimarthaṃ naravaro na māṃ rakṣati rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that best of men, not protect me, O <s>Rāghava</s>?
Those two tigers among men are powerful, equal in splendor to wind and fire,

children.text: surāṇām api durdharṣau kimarthaṃ mām upekṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: unassailable even by the gods; why do they neglect me?

children.text: mamaiva duṣkṛtaṃ kiṃcin mahad asti na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: There must be some great wrongdoing of my own, no doubt,
since the two scorchers of foes, though able and together, take no notice of me.
Having heard <s>Vaidehī</s>'s piteous words, spoken with tears,

children.text: punar apyaham āryāṃ tām idaṃ vacanam abruvam ||
children.translated_text: I again said these words to that noble lady:

children.text: tvacchokavimukho rāmo devi satyena te śape
children.translated_text: 'Lady, <s>Rāma</s> has turned his whole mind toward grief for you; by truth I swear this to you.
And when <s>Rāma</s> is overwhelmed by sorrow, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> too is tormented.

children.text: kathaṃcid bhavatī dṛṣṭā na kālaḥ pariśocitum
children.translated_text: Somehow you have been seen; this is no time for lamentation.

children.text: imaṃ muhūrtaṃ duḥkhānām antaṃ drakṣyasi bhāmini ||
children.translated_text: In this very moment you will see the end of your sorrows, O lovely lady.
Those two tigers among men, the princes, conquerors of enemies,
made eager by the sight of you, will burn <s>Laṅkā</s> to ashes.

children.text: hatvā ca samare raudraṃ rāvaṇaṃ sahabāndhavam
children.translated_text: And after slaying fierce <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle together with his kinsmen,

children.text: rāghavastvāṃ mahābāhuḥ svāṃ purīṃ nayate dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: the mighty-armed <s>Rāghava</s> will surely take you to his own city.

children.text: yat tu rāmo vijānīyād abhijñānam anindite
children.translated_text: But, blameless lady, whatever token of recognition <s>Rāma</s> may know,
one that will produce joy in him, you ought to give that truly.'
She looked in every direction, loosened the excellent fastening of her braid,

children.text: muktvā vastrād dadau mahyaṃ maṇim etaṃ mahābala ||
children.translated_text: and, taking this jewel from her garment, gave it to me, O mighty one.

children.text: pratigṛhya maṇiṃ divyaṃ tava heto raghūttama
children.translated_text: Receiving the divine jewel for your sake, O best of the <s>Raghus</s>,
I bowed to her with my head and hastened to depart.
Seeing me eager to go, that lovely-complexioned lady,

children.text: vivardhamānaṃ ca hi mām uvāca janakātmajā
children.translated_text: the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, spoke to me as I was increasing in size,
her face full of tears, distressed, and her speech choked with sobs:
'<s>Hanumān</s>, to those two lion-like ones, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: sugrīvaṃ ca sahāmātyaṃ sarvān brūyā anāmayam ||
children.translated_text: and to <s>Sugrīva</s> with his ministers, tell all of them that I am unharmed.

children.text: yathā ca sa mahābāhur māṃ tārayati rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: And as that mighty-armed <s>Rāghava</s> may carry me across
from this confinement in the waters of sorrow, you must arrange that.

children.text: imaṃ ca tīvraṃ mama śokavegaṃ rakṣobhir ebhiḥ paribhartsanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: And when you have gone near <s>Rāma</s>, tell him of this fierce rush of my grief and of the threatening by these <s>rākṣasas</s>;

children.text: brūyāstu rāmasya gataḥ samīpaṃ śivaśca te 'dhvāstu haripravīra ||
children.translated_text: and may your road be auspicious, O heroic chief of monkeys.'

children.text: etat tavāryā nṛparājasiṃha sītā vacaḥ prāha viṣādapūrvam
children.translated_text: This, O noble lion among kings, was the sorrowful speech that <s>Sītā</s> spoke to you.

children.text: etacca buddhvā gaditaṃ mayā tvaṃ śraddhatsva sītāṃ kuśalāṃ samagrām ||
children.translated_text: Knowing this too, which has been told by me, trust that <s>Sītā</s> is safe and whole.

children.text: athāham uttaraṃ devyā punar uktaḥ sasaṃbhramam
children.translated_text: Then I was again addressed by the goddess in reply, with agitation:

children.text: tava snehān naravyāghra sauhārdād anumānya ca ||
children.translated_text: "Out of your affection for me, O tiger among men, and because of your friendship, having considered it fitting,
<s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, must be addressed in many ways by you,

children.text: yathā mām āpnuyācchīghraṃ hatvā rāvaṇam āhave ||
children.translated_text: so that, having slain <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle, he may quickly reach me.

children.text: yadi vā manyase vīra vasaikāham ariṃdama
children.translated_text: Or, if you think it best, O hero, O subduer of foes, stay for one day

children.text: kasmiṃścit saṃvṛte deśe viśrāntaḥ śvo gamiṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: in some hidden place, and, rested, you will go tomorrow.
For me too, ill-fated as I am, O vānara, from your nearness
there would be release for a moment from the ripening of this grief.

children.text: gate hi tvayi vikrānte punarāgamanāya vai
children.translated_text: For when you, mighty one, have gone to return again,

children.text: prāṇānām api saṃdeho mama syān nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there would be uncertainty even about my life-breaths; of this there is no doubt.
The grief born from not seeing you would burn me still more,
overcome by sorrow upon sorrow, fallen into misery, and allotted only suffering.
But this heroic doubt stands, as it were, before me,
a very great one concerning your helpers, the vānaras and bears, without doubt.

children.text: kathaṃ nu khalu duṣpāraṃ tariṣyanti mahodadhim
children.translated_text: How indeed will those vānara and bear armies cross
the great ocean, so hard to cross, or those two best princes?
Among beings, only three would have power

children.text: śaktiḥ syād vainateyasya vāyor vā tava vānagha ||
children.translated_text: to leap across this ocean: <s>Vainateya</s>, or <s>Vāyu</s>, or you, O sinless vānara.
Therefore, in this assignment of the task, O hero, so hard to overcome,

children.text: kiṃ paśyasi samādhānaṃ brūhi kāryavidāṃ vara ||
children.translated_text: what solution do you see? Tell me, best of those who understand affairs.

children.text: kāmam asya tvam evaikaḥ kāryasya parisādhane
children.translated_text: To be sure, you alone are sufficient
to accomplish this task, O slayer of enemy heroes; the rise of your strength is glorious.

children.text: balaiḥ samagrair yadi māṃ hatvā rāvaṇam āhave
children.translated_text: But if, with all his forces, after killing <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle,

children.text: vijayī svāṃ purīṃ rāmo nayet tat syād yaśaskaram ||
children.translated_text: victorious <s>Rāma</s> were to take me to his own city, that would be glorious.

children.text: yathāhaṃ tasya vīrasya vanād upadhinā hṛtā
children.translated_text: As I was carried off from the forest from that hero

children.text: rakṣasā tadbhayād eva tathā nārhati rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by a rākṣasa through deception, so, for fear of that very reproach, <s>Rāghava</s> ought not act.

children.text: balais tu saṃkulāṃ kṛtvā laṅkāṃ parabalārdanaḥ
children.translated_text: But if <s>Kākutstha</s>, destroyer of enemy forces, making <s>Laṅkā</s> crowded with his troops,

children.text: māṃ nayed yadi kākutsthas tat tasya sadṛśaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: were to lead me away, that would be worthy of him.

children.text: tad yathā tasya vikrāntam anurūpaṃ mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, in whatever way it may be fitting for that great-souled hero's valor,
for him who is brave in battle, arrange it so.
After hearing that meaningful speech, modest and joined with reasoning,

children.text: niśamyāhaṃ tataḥ śeṣaṃ vākyam uttaram abruvam ||
children.translated_text: I then spoke the remaining words in answer:
"O goddess, the lord of the armies of vānaras and bears, the best of leapers,
<s>Sugrīva</s>, endowed with courage, is firmly resolved for your sake.
Under his command stand vānaras endowed with prowess, courageous and very strong,
who move with the speed of thought and intention.

children.text: yeṣāṃ nopari nādhastān na tiryak sajjate gatiḥ
children.translated_text: For them their movement is obstructed neither above, nor below, nor sideways,

children.text: na ca karmasu sīdanti mahatsv amitatejasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and in great tasks those of immeasurable splendor do not sink down in failure.
Many times by those greatly fortunate vānaras, endowed with strength,
the earth has been circled, following the path of the wind.

children.text: madviśiṣṭāś ca tulyāś ca santi tatra vanaukasaḥ
children.translated_text: There are forest-dwellers there superior to me and equal to me;
there is no one inferior to me in <s>Sugrīva</s>'s presence.

children.text: ahaṃ tāvad iha prāptaḥ kiṃ punas te mahābalāḥ
children.translated_text: I, for my part, have come here; how much more those very powerful ones?

children.text: na hi prakṛṣṭāḥ preṣyante preṣyante hītare janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the foremost are not sent out; rather, other persons are sent.

children.text: tad alaṃ paritāpena devi manyur vyapaitu te
children.translated_text: Therefore enough of this distress, O goddess; let your anger and sorrow depart.
With a single leap the leaders of the vānara troops will come to <s>Laṅkā</s> for you.

children.text: mama pṛṣṭhagatau tau ca candrasūryāv ivoditau
children.translated_text: And those two, riding on my back, like the moon and sun risen together,
will come to your presence, O greatly fortunate one, like two lions among men.
You will soon see <s>Rāghava</s>, slayer of foes, like a lion,
and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, bow in hand, standing at the gate of <s>Laṅkā</s>.
You will soon see assembled heroic vānaras, armed with claws and teeth,
with the valor of lions and tigers, resembling the lords of vānaras.
On the slopes of <s>Laṅkā</s> and <s>Malaya</s> you will before long hear
the roar of the chief monkeys, who are like mountains and clouds.
You will soon see <s>Rāghava</s>, subduer of foes, returned from forest exile,
together with you, consecrated as king in <s>Ayodhyā</s>."

children.text: tato mayā vāgbhir adīnabhāṣiṇī śivābhir iṣṭābhir abhiprasāditā
children.translated_text: Then, by my auspicious, desired, and comforting words,

children.text: jagāma śāntiṃ mama maithilātmajā tavāpi śokena tathābhipīḍitā ||
children.translated_text: the daughter of <s>Maithila</s>, speaking without dejection, found peace, though she was also oppressed by grief for you.
Hearing <s>Hanumān</s>'s speech, spoken just as it was,
<s>Rāma</s>, filled with joy, spoke these words in reply:

children.text: kṛtaṃ hanumatā kāryaṃ sumahad bhuvi duṣkaram
children.translated_text: "By <s>Hanumān</s> a very great task has been accomplished, hard to do on earth,

children.text: manasāpi yad anyena na śakyaṃ dharaṇītale ||
children.translated_text: one that could not be done by another even in thought on the surface of the earth.

children.text: na hi taṃ paripaśyāmi yastareta mahārṇavam
children.translated_text: For I do not see anyone who could cross the great ocean,

children.text: anyatra garuḍād vāyor anyatra ca hanūmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: apart from <s>Garuḍa</s>, apart from <s>Vāyu</s>, and apart from <s>Hanumān</s>.
Who, relying on courage, could enter <s>Laṅkā</s>, the city unassailable
to gods, dānavas, yakṣas, gandharvas, serpents, and rākṣasas, and well guarded by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: praviṣṭaḥ sattvam āśritya jīvan ko nāma niṣkramet
children.translated_text: and come out alive?
Who could enter that city, very hard to assail and well guarded by rākṣasas,
if he were not equal to <s>Hanumān</s>, endowed with heroism and strength?
By <s>Hanumān</s> a great servant's duty for <s>Sugrīva</s> has been done,

children.text: evaṃ vidhāya svabalaṃ sadṛśaṃ vikramasya ca ||
children.translated_text: in this way displaying his own strength, fitting his valor.

children.text: yo hi bhṛtyo niyuktaḥ san bhartrā karmaṇi duṣkare
children.translated_text: For a servant who, when assigned by his master to a difficult task,
does it through devotion to him, they call that man the best of persons.

children.text: niyukto nṛpateḥ kāryaṃ na kuryād yaḥ samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: But he who, appointed to the king's task, does not perform it attentively

children.text: bhṛtyo yuktaḥ samarthaśca tam āhuḥ puruṣādhamam ||
children.translated_text: They call him the lowest of men: a servant who is entrusted with a charge and capable of carrying it out.
The task assigned in that commission has been accomplished by <s>Hanumān</s>;

children.text: na cātmā laghutāṃ nītaḥ sugrīvaścāpi toṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he has not brought himself into contempt, and <s>Sugrīva</s> too has been satisfied.
I, the lineage of <s>Raghu</s>, and mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>
have today, through the sight of <s>Vaidehī</s>, been preserved in accordance with <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: idaṃ tu mama dīnasya mano bhūyaḥ prakarṣati
children.translated_text: But this again distresses the mind of me, who am wretched:

children.text: yad ihāsya priyākhyātur na kurmi sadṛśaṃ priyam ||
children.translated_text: that here I do not do a fitting kindness for this teller of dear news.
This embrace, however, which is all that I possess, is for <s>Hanumān</s>;

children.text: mayā kālam imaṃ prāpya dattastasya mahātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: having reached this moment, I give it to that great-souled one.
In every way, the search for <s>Sītā</s> has indeed been well accomplished for now;

children.text: sāgaraṃ tu samāsādya punar naṣṭaṃ mano mama ||
children.translated_text: but, having come to the ocean, my mind is lost again.
How indeed will the <s>haris</s> (monkey warriors), composed and intent,
go to the southern shore of this ocean, hard to cross and filled with great waters?

children.text: yadyapyeṣa tu vṛttānto vaidehyā gadito mama
children.translated_text: Although this account of <s>Vaidehī</s> has been told to me,
what further answer can there be concerning the <s>haris</s>' crossing beyond the ocean?
Having spoken thus, <s>Rāma</s>, the destroyer of foes, bewildered by grief,
then fell into thought after addressing mighty-armed <s>Hanumān</s>.
Then the illustrious <s>Sugrīva</s> spoke a grief-dispelling word
to <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, who was overcome with sorrow.

children.text: kiṃ tvaṃ saṃtapyase vīra yathānyaḥ prākṛtastathā
children.translated_text: Why are you grieving, hero, like some ordinary man?

children.text: maivaṃ bhūstyaja saṃtāpaṃ kṛtaghna iva sauhṛdam ||
children.translated_text: Do not be so; cast off distress, as an ungrateful man casts off friendship.

children.text: saṃtāpasya ca te sthānaṃ na hi paśyāmi rāghava
children.translated_text: I see no proper ground for your distress, O <s>Rāghava</s>,
when news has been obtained and the enemy's dwelling is known.
You are steadfast, learned in the śāstras, wise, and discerning, O <s>Rāghava</s>;
abandon this sinful thought, which, like a wrong against oneself, ruins one's purpose.
Having crossed the ocean, thronged with great sea-monsters,
we shall scale <s>Laṅkā</s> and kill your enemy.
For one who is without energy, dejected, and whose mind is overwhelmed by grief,
all purposes collapse, and he falls into calamity.

children.text: ime śūrāḥ samarthāśca sarve no hariyūthapāḥ
children.translated_text: These leaders of monkey troops of ours are all brave and capable;
for the sake of what is dear to you, they are eager even to enter fire.

children.text: eṣāṃ harṣeṇa jānāmi tarkaścāsmin dṛḍho mama
children.translated_text: From their joy I know this, and my reasoning about it is firm:

children.text: vikrameṇa samāneṣye sītāṃ hatvā yathā ripum ||
children.translated_text: by valor I shall bring back <s>Sītā</s>, having slain the enemy as required.

children.text: setur atra yathā badhyed yathā paśyema tāṃ purīm
children.translated_text: Act here, O <s>Rāghava</s>, in such a way that a bridge may be built

children.text: tasya rākṣasarājasya tathā tvaṃ kuru rāghava ||
children.translated_text: and that we may see the city of that king of the <s>rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tāṃ hi purīṃ laṅkāṃ trikūṭaśikhare sthitām
children.translated_text: For when you have seen that city, <s>Laṅkā</s>, standing on the peak of <s>Trikūṭa</s>,

children.text: hataṃ ca rāvaṇaṃ yuddhe darśanād upadhāraya ||
children.translated_text: understand from that very sight that <s>Rāvaṇa</s> has been slain in battle.
When the bridge has been built in the ocean up to the vicinity of <s>Laṅkā</s>

children.text: sarvaṃ tīrṇaṃ ca vai sainyaṃ jitam ityupadhāryatām ||
children.translated_text: and the whole army has crossed, consider that everything has been won.

children.text: ime hi samare śūrā harayaḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: For these <s>haris</s>, brave in battle, can assume forms at will;

children.text: tad alaṃ viklavā buddhī rājan sarvārthanāśanī ||
children.translated_text: therefore enough of this wavering thought, O king, which destroys every aim.
For in this world grief diminishes a man's courage.

children.text: yat tu kāryaṃ manuṣyeṇa śauṇḍīryam avalambatā
children.translated_text: But whatever task must be done by a man relying on boldness,
at this time, greatly wise one, take up strength with energy.
For brave men, great-souled ones such as you,

children.text: vinaṣṭe vā pranaṣṭe vā śokaḥ sarvārthanāśanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: grief over what is destroyed or lost destroys every aim.
But you are the best of the intelligent, versed in the meaning of all śāstras;

children.text: madvidhaiḥ sacivaiḥ sārdham ariṃ jetum ihārhasi ||
children.translated_text: together with counselors like me, you ought here to conquer the enemy.

children.text: na hi paśyāmyahaṃ kaṃcit triṣu lokeṣu rāghava
children.translated_text: For I do not see anyone in the three worlds, O <s>Rāghava</s>,
who could stand facing you in battle when you have taken up your bow.

children.text: vānareṣu samāsaktaṃ na te kāryaṃ vipatsyate
children.translated_text: With the <s>vānaras</s> engaged, your purpose will not come to disaster;

children.text: acirād drakṣyase sītāṃ tīrtvā sāgaram akṣayam ||
children.translated_text: before long you will see <s>Sītā</s>, after crossing the inexhaustible ocean.

children.text: tad alaṃ śokam ālambya krodham ālamba bhūpate
children.translated_text: Therefore enough of clinging to grief; cling to anger, O king.

children.text: niśceṣṭāḥ kṣatriyā mandāḥ sarve caṇḍasya bibhyati ||
children.translated_text: Inactive kṣatriyas are feeble; everyone fears the fierce man.
For the sake of crossing the dreadful ocean, lord of rivers,
consider carefully with subtle intelligence, joined here together with us.

children.text: ime hi samare śūrā harayaḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: For these <s>haris</s>, brave in battle and able to assume forms at will,
will scatter those enemies with showers of rocks and trees.
Somehow we shall survey for you this abode of <s>Varuṇa</s>.

children.text: kim uktvā bahudhā cāpi sarvathā vijayī bhavān ||
children.translated_text: Why speak at length? In every way you will be victorious.
Hearing <s>Sugrīva</s>'s reasoned words, <s>Kākutstha</s>, who knew the highest truth,
accepted them, and then he spoke to <s>Hanumān</s>.
By force, by building a bridge, or by drying up the ocean,
in every way I am fully capable of crossing this ocean.

children.text: kati durgāṇi durgāyā laṅkāyāstad bravīhi me
children.translated_text: Tell me how many strong defenses belong to difficult <s>Laṅkā</s>;

children.text: jñātum icchāmi tat sarvaṃ darśanād iva vānara ||
children.translated_text: I wish to know all that, as if from direct sight, O <s>vānara</s>.
Tell me also the measure of its army and the arrangements of its gates and fortifications,

children.text: guptikarma ca laṅkāyā rakṣasāṃ sadanāni ca ||
children.translated_text: the work of guarding <s>Laṅkā</s> and the dwellings of the <s>rākṣasas</s>.
You saw <s>Laṅkā</s> at leisure and exactly as it is;

children.text: sarvam ācakṣva tattvena sarvathā kuśalo hyasi ||
children.translated_text: tell everything truly, for you are skilled in every respect.
Hearing <s>Rāma</s>'s words, <s>Hanumān</s>, son of the Wind,

children.text: vākyaṃ vākyavidāṃ śreṣṭho rāmaṃ punar athābravīt ||
children.translated_text: best of those who know speech, then again spoke this sentence to <s>Rāma</s>.
Listen; I shall describe everything according to the arrangement of its fortifications:

children.text: guptā purī yathā laṅkā rakṣitā ca yathā balaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: how the city of <s>Laṅkā</s> is guarded and how it is protected by forces.

children.text: parāṃ samṛddhiṃ laṅkāyāḥ sāgarasya ca bhīmatām
children.translated_text: the surpassing prosperity of <s>Laṅkā</s> and the dreadfulness of the ocean,

children.text: vibhāgaṃ ca balaughasya nirdeśaṃ vāhanasya ca ||
children.translated_text: the division of the massed army and the description of its vehicles.
<s>Laṅkā</s> is exultant and joyful, crowded with rutting elephants,
great, filled with chariots, and crowded with hosts of <s>rākṣasas</s>.
Its gates have firmly fastened doors and great bars,
four broad entrances, all very large.
On the ramparts there are powerful and massive stone-casting engines;
by them an approaching enemy army is repelled there.
At the gates, dreadful, well-made, sharp, iron

children.text: śataśo rocitā vīraiḥ śataghnyo rakṣasāṃ gaṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>śataghnīs</s> (hundred-slaying engines) have been set up by the hundreds by the heroic hosts of <s>rākṣasas</s>.
Her great golden rampart is hard to assault,
its spaces adorned with jewels, coral, beryl, and pearls.
All around are very terrible, excellent moats with cold water,
unfathomable, filled with crocodiles, and frequented by fish.
At their gates there are four very long causeways,
furnished with many great machines and strongly joined fastenings.
Those causeways protect the place when an enemy army arrives;
by those machines they are cast down all around into the moats.
But one causeway is immovable, strong, and exceedingly firm,
adorned with many golden pillars and platforms.
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> himself, O <s>Rāma</s>, is endowed with resources and eager for battle,
alert and vigilant in the inspection of his forces.
The city <s>Laṅkā</s> is isolated, a divine fortress, and terrifying,

children.text: nādeyaṃ pārvataṃ vanyaṃ kṛtrimaṃ ca caturvidham ||
children.translated_text: fourfold: protected by water, mountain, forest, and artificial works.
It stands on the far shore of the hard-to-cross ocean, O <s>Rāghava</s>,
and there is no boat route here, with no landmark anywhere around.

children.text: śailāgre racitā durgā sā pūr devapuropamā
children.translated_text: That fortress-city, built on a mountain peak, is like the city of the gods;
<s>Laṅkā</s>, filled with horses and elephants, is supremely hard to conquer.
Bars, <s>śataghnīs</s>, and various machines
adorn the city <s>Laṅkā</s> of wicked <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Ten thousand <s>rākṣasas</s> here occupy the western gate,
spear in hand, hard to attack, all foremost fighters with the sword.
A hundred thousand <s>rākṣasas</s> here occupy the southern gate,
with a fourfold army; there too the warriors are unsurpassed.
A million <s>rākṣasas</s> here occupy the eastern gate,
all bearing shields and swords and skilled in every weapon.
An <s>arbuda</s> of <s>rākṣasas</s> here occupies the northern gate,
chariot-fighters and horsemen, noble-born and highly honored.
A hundred hundred-thousands have taken position in the central division,
<s>yātudhānas</s> hard to assault, and more than a crore of <s>rākṣasas</s>.
Those causeways were broken by me, and the moats were filled in;
the city <s>Laṅkā</s> was burned, and the ramparts were battered down.

children.text: yena kena tu mārgeṇa tarāma varuṇālayam
children.translated_text: By whatever route we can, let us cross the abode of <s>Varuṇa</s>.
Let the city <s>Laṅkā</s> be regarded as already destroyed by the <s>vānaras</s>.

children.text: aṅgado dvivido maindo jāmbavān panaso nalaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Aṅgada</s>, <s>Dvivida</s>, <s>Mainda</s>, <s>Jāmbavān</s>, <s>Panasa</s>, and <s>Nala</s>,
and <s>Nīla</s> the general as well: what need have you of the rest of the army?

children.text: plavamānā hi gatvā tāṃ rāvaṇasya mahāpurīm
children.translated_text: For, leaping there to that great city of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
they will bring back <s>Maithilī</s>, together with its ramparts and palaces.
Therefore quickly order the full mustering of the forces,
and choose departure at a proper auspicious moment.
Having heard <s>Hanumān</s>'s speech duly and in sequence,
then mighty <s>Rāma</s>, true in valor, spoke:

children.text: yāṃ nivedayase laṅkāṃ purīṃ bhīmasya rakṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: "The city <s>Laṅkā</s> of the fearsome <s>rākṣasa</s>, which you report,

children.text: kṣipram enāṃ vadhiṣyāmi satyam etad bravīmi te ||
children.translated_text: I shall swiftly destroy; this I tell you truly.
At this very moment, <s>Sugrīva</s>, I approve the march.

children.text: yukto muhūrto vijayaḥ prāpto madhyaṃ divākaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The favorable <s>Vijaya</s> moment has arrived; the sun has reached midday.
Today is <s>Uttarā Phalgunī</s>; tomorrow it will be joined with <s>Hasta</s>.
Let us set out, <s>Sugrīva</s>, surrounded by the whole army.

children.text: nimittāni ca dhanyāni yāni prādurbhavanti me
children.translated_text: The auspicious omens that appear to me
show that, after slaying <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, I shall bring back <s>Sītā Jānakī</s>.
For this eye of mine, twitching above,
seems to announce victory achieved and my heart's desire fulfilled.

children.text: agre yātu balasyāsya nīlo mārgam avekṣitum
children.translated_text: Let <s>Nīla</s> go at the front of this army to inspect the road,
surrounded by a hundred thousand swift <s>vānaras</s>.
O <s>Nīla</s>, along a road with fruit and roots, cool groves and water,

children.text: pathā madhumatā cāśu senāṃ senāpate naya ||
children.translated_text: and rich with honey, quickly lead the army, commander.
The wicked <s>rākṣasas</s> might spoil the roots, fruits, and water along the road;
be constantly alert and protect them from those foes.
In low ground, in forest strongholds, and in forests, let the forest-dwellers
leap ahead and inspect the enemy's deployed force.
Let the mighty lion-like monkeys draw forward the fearsome vanguard, like a flood of the sea,
by hundreds and then by thousands.
Let <s>Gaja</s>, mountain-like, and mighty <s>Gavaya</s>,
and <s>Gavākṣa</s> go in front, like proud bulls among cattle.
Let the <s>vānara</s>, lord of leapers, go with the monkey army,
<s>Ṛṣabha</s>, bull among <s>vānaras</s>, guarding the right flank.
Irresistible like an elephant in rut and swift, <s>Gandhamādana</s>
should go posted on the left flank of the <s>vānara</s> army.
I myself shall go in the middle of the army, gladdening the mass of forces,
mounted on <s>Hanumān</s>, as the lord of the gods on <s>Airāvata</s>.
And let <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, resembling <s>Antaka</s>, go together with <s>Aṅgada</s>.
as the lord of beings, the lord of wealth, is guarded by a universal sovereign.
And <s>Jāmbavān</s>, <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, and the monkey <s>Vegadarśī</s>,

children.text: ṛkṣarājo mahāsattvaḥ kukṣiṃ rakṣantu te trayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king of bears, great in spirit, let those three guard your flank.
Hearing the word of <s>Rāghava</s>, <s>Sugrīva</s>, commander of the army,
the bull among monkeys, ordered the very mighty monkeys.
Then all those troops of monkeys, leaping up and eager to fight,
quickly sprang at that time from caves and from mountain peaks.
Then, honored by the king of monkeys and by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: jagāma rāmo dharmātmā sasainyo dakṣiṇāṃ diśam ||
children.translated_text: righteous <s>Rāma</s> went with his army toward the southern quarter.
With hundreds, hundred-thousands, crores, and even tens of thousands,
he went then surrounded by elephant-like monkeys.

children.text: taṃ yāntam anuyāti sma mahatī harivāhinī ||
children.translated_text: As he went, a great monkey army followed him.
All were delighted and overjoyed, protected by <s>Sugrīva</s>;
leaping, bounding, and roaring, the monkeys,

children.text: kṣveḍanto ninadantaśca jagmur vai dakṣiṇāṃ diśam ||
children.translated_text: shouting and making loud cries, went indeed toward the southern quarter.

children.text: bhakṣayantaḥ sugandhīni madhūni ca phalāni ca
children.translated_text: Eating fragrant honey and fruits,
and carrying great trees that bore clusters of blossoms,

children.text: anyonyaṃ sahasā dṛptā nirvahanti kṣipanti ca
children.translated_text: proud and impetuous, they carried and hurled one another,
while some fell and sprang up, and others made others fall.

children.text: rāvaṇo no nihantavyaḥ sarve ca rajanīcarāḥ
children.translated_text: "<s>Rāvaṇa</s> must be slain by us, and all the night-roamers too,"
so the monkeys roared near <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: purastād ṛṣabho vīro nīlaḥ kumuda eva ca
children.translated_text: In front, the heroes <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, and <s>Kumuda</s>

children.text: panthānaṃ śodhayanti sma vānarair bahubhiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: cleared the road with many monkeys.

children.text: madhye tu rājā sugrīvo rāmo lakṣmaṇa eva ca
children.translated_text: But in the middle were king <s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
the destroyers of enemies, surrounded by many strong and terrible warriors.

children.text: hariḥ śatabalir vīraḥ koṭībhir daśabhir vṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The heroic monkey <s>Śatabali</s>, surrounded by ten crores,
alone supported and guarded the whole monkey army on every side.
<s>Kesarī</s>, <s>Panasa</s>, <s>Gaja</s>, and the exceedingly strong <s>Arka</s>, each with a retinue of a hundred crores,
protected one side of that army.
<s>Suṣeṇa</s> and <s>Jāmbavān</s>, surrounded by many bears,
kept <s>Sugrīva</s> in front and carefully guarded the rear.
Their commander, the heroic <s>Nīla</s>, bull among monkeys,
moving and leaping, the best among those who leap, watched over that army.
<s>Darīmukha</s>, <s>Prajaṅgha</s>, <s>Jambha</s>, and then the monkey <s>Rabhasa</s>
went everywhere as heroes, urging on the monkeys.
Thus those tigers among monkeys, as they went, exulting in their strength,
saw the excellent mountain <s>Sahya</s>, covered with trees and creepers.
That great monkey force, terrible and like a flood of the ocean,
poured forth with a mighty roar, like the sea with dreadful speed.
Beside that son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, those heroic elephant-like monkeys

children.text: tūrṇam āpupluvuḥ sarve sadaśvā iva coditāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all leapt swiftly, like well-bred horses when urged on.
Carried by two monkeys, those two bulls among men shone,
like the moon and the sun touched by two mighty seizing planets.

children.text: tam aṅgadagato rāmaṃ lakṣmaṇaḥ śubhayā girā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, mounted on <s>Aṅgada</s>, addressed that <s>Rāma</s>
with auspicious speech, full in meaning, mindful and eloquent:

children.text: hṛtām avāpya vaidehīṃ kṣipraṃ hatvā ca rāvaṇam
children.translated_text: "Having recovered <s>Vaidehī</s> after quickly slaying <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
you will return to prosperous <s>Ayodhyā</s>, your purpose fulfilled and her prosperity restored.

children.text: mahānti ca nimittāni divi bhūmau ca rāghava
children.translated_text: Great omens, O <s>Rāghava</s>, in heaven and on earth,
all auspicious, I see for the accomplishment of your every aim.

children.text: anu vāti śubho vāyuḥ senāṃ mṛduhitaḥ sukhaḥ
children.translated_text: A favorable wind blows after the army, gentle, beneficial, and pleasant;
and these animals and birds cry out with full and lovely voices.
All the quarters are clear, and the sun is spotless;

children.text: uśanā ca prasannārcir anu tvāṃ bhārgavo gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Uśanas</s>, the <s>Bhārgava</s>, with clear rays, has gone along behind you.
The constellation of <s>Brahmā</s> is pure, and the great seers too are clear;
all shining brightly, they appear to the right of <s>Dhruva</s>.
The royal seer <s>Triśaṅku</s> shines spotless together with his priest,
the excellent forefather of us, the great-souled <s>Ikṣvākus</s>.
The two <s>Viśākhās</s> also shine clear and free from affliction,
the supreme <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion) of us, the great-souled <s>Ikṣvākus</s>.
But the <s>nakṣatra</s> of the <s>Nairṛtas</s> and of the <s>nairṛtas</s> is being oppressed;
<s>Mūla</s>, touched by one having a root-like tail, is made smoky by a comet.
All this has arisen for the destruction of the <s>rākṣasas</s>,
when the star of those seized by Time is oppressed by a planet at the proper time.
The waters are clear and pleasant-tasting, and the forests are full of fruit;
the trees, with flowers in season, waft forth fragrances in abundance.
The monkey armies, drawn up in formation, shine all the more, my lord,
like the armies of the gods in the battle with <s>Tārakā</s>.

children.text: evam ārya samīkṣyaitān prīto bhavitum arhasi
children.translated_text: Thus, noble one, seeing these signs, you ought to be pleased."

children.text: iti bhrātaram āśvāsya hṛṣṭaḥ saumitrir abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Having reassured his brother in this way, the delighted <s>Saumitri</s> spoke.

children.text: athāvṛtya mahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ jagāma mahatī camūḥ
children.translated_text: Then the great army, covering the whole earth, went on,
surrounded by tigers among bears and monkeys, whose weapons were claws and teeth.
The dust raised by the monkeys with the tips of their hands and feet

children.text: bhaumam antardadhe lokaṃ nivārya savituḥ prabhām ||
children.translated_text: hid the earthly world, blocking the light of the sun.

children.text: sā sma yāti divārātraṃ mahatī harivāhinī
children.translated_text: That great monkey army kept moving by day and night,
a force delighted and overjoyed, protected by <s>Sugrīva</s>.
All the monkeys, delighting in battle, hurried onward,
wishing to free <s>Sītā</s>; they did not rest anywhere even for a moment.
Then they came to a place crowded with trees and filled with many kinds of animals,
to the <s>Sahya</s> mountain and also to <s>Malaya</s>, the great mountain.
As he went, <s>Rāma</s> looked upon the varied forests

children.text: paśyann api yayau rāmaḥ sahyasya malayasya ca ||
children.translated_text: and the rivers and waterfalls of <s>Sahya</s> and <s>Malaya</s>.
The monkeys broke campaka trees, tilakas, mango trees, aśokas, and sinduvārakas,
as well as karavīras and timiśas.
There the powerful monkeys ate the fruits fragrant like nectar,
and the roots and flowers of the trees.
The monkeys went on joyfully drinking honey-combs
hanging down, as large in measure as a droṇa, their bodies tawny with honey.
Breaking down trees and dragging away creepers,
the bulls among monkeys went on, shaking the excellent mountains.
Some monkeys, intoxicated with honey, roared from the trees,
some climbed upon trees, and others even fell down.
The earth became filled with those foremost monkeys,
as though the ground were covered with fields of ripe lotuses.
Then, having reached <s>Mahendra</s>, lotus-eyed <s>Rāma</s>,
the mighty-armed one, climbed its peak adorned with trees.
Then, having climbed the peak, <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>,
saw the reservoir of waters, crowded with turtles and fish.

children.text: te sahyaṃ samatikramya malayaṃ ca mahāgirim
children.translated_text: Having passed beyond <s>Sahya</s> and the great mountain <s>Malaya</s>,
they reached in due order the ocean with its terrible roar.
Having descended, <s>Rāma</s>, the best of those who give delight, quickly went
to the unsurpassed shore-forest, together with <s>Sugrīva</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Then, reaching the broad shore whose rocky ground was washed

children.text: velām āsādya vipulāṃ rāmo vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: by masses of water suddenly rising up, <s>Rāma</s> spoke these words:
"Here we have arrived, <s>Sugrīva</s>, at the abode of <s>Varuṇa</s>.

children.text: ihedānīṃ vicintā sā yā na pūrvaṃ samutthitā ||
children.translated_text: Now, here, that problem has arisen which had not arisen before.
Beyond this lies the far shore; this ocean is the lord of rivers.
And this sea cannot be crossed without a means.

children.text: tad ihaiva niveśo 'stu mantraḥ prastūyatām iha
children.translated_text: Therefore let the encampment be right here, and let counsel be begun here,
so that this monkey army may reach the far shore."
Thus the mighty-armed <s>Rāma</s>, worn down by <s>Sītā</s>'s abduction,

children.text: rāmaḥ sāgaram āsādya vāsam ājñāpayat tadā ||
children.translated_text: having reached the ocean, then ordered a halt.
"The time for our counsel has arrived here concerning the crossing of the ocean.

children.text: svāṃ svāṃ senāṃ samutsṛjya mā ca kaścit kuto vrajet
children.translated_text: Let no one go anywhere after leaving his own division of the army.

children.text: gacchantu vānarāḥ śūrā jñeyaṃ channaṃ bhayaṃ ca naḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let brave monkeys go out; our hidden danger must be learned."
Having heard <s>Rāma</s>'s command, <s>Sugrīva</s>, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
encamped the army on the tree-filled shore of the ocean.

children.text: virarāja samīpasthaṃ sāgarasya tu tad balam
children.translated_text: That army, standing close to the ocean, shone forth
like a second splendid ocean, its mass pale-yellow like honey-water.
Then those foremost monkeys came to the shore-forest
and settled there, longing for the far shore of the great ocean.
That joyful monkey host, having reached the great sea,
gazed upon the great ocean, stirred by the speed of the wind.
Seeing the abode of <s>Varuṇa</s>, whose far shore was distant and unobstructed,
and which was frequented by bands of <s>rākṣasas</s>, the monkey chiefs sat down.
At the onset of night, at the close of day, it was dreadful, full of fierce crocodiles and sea-monsters;
at moonrise it was shaken and crowded with reflected moons.
The abode of <s>Varuṇa</s> was filled with mighty creatures, fierce winds, whales, and timingilas,
as if crowded with serpents whose hoods were blazing.
It was plunged into by great beings and filled with many rocks,

children.text: durgaṃ durgam amārgaṃ tam agādham asurālayam ||
children.translated_text: hard to approach, hard to cross, pathless, unfathomable, and an abode of asuras.
Entered by makaras and by the coils of serpents, and tossed by the wind,
the swollen masses of water rose up and fell down.
It was as though strewn with powdered fire, with shining waters and great serpents,
a terrible realm of the enemies of the gods, always uneven like <s>Pātāla</s>.
The ocean appeared like the sky, and the sky like the ocean;
as ocean and sky, they seemed without distinction.

children.text: saṃpṛktaṃ nabhasā hyambhaḥ saṃpṛktaṃ ca nabho 'mbhasā
children.translated_text: For the water was mingled with the sky, and the sky was mingled with the water;
they were seen in just such a form, filled with stars and jewels.
Between the sea, with its rows of waves, and the sky with clouds rising up,

children.text: viśeṣo na dvayor āsīt sāgarasyāmbarasya ca ||
children.translated_text: there was no difference between the two.
The waves of the king of rivers, striking one another and clinging together,
roared with a terrible sound like great war-drums in battle.
It resounded with masses of jewels and waters, as if seized by the wind,
as if leaping upward in anger, crowded with hosts of aquatic creatures.
Those great-souled ones saw that water-mass beaten by the wind,
as if frisking in the sky with its waves stirred up by the gale,
the ocean restless, with the roar of its swirling waves and waters.

children.text: sā tu nīlena vidhivat svārakṣā susamāhitā
children.translated_text: That army, with its own protection properly arranged by <s>Nīla</s>, was well ordered;
it was duly encamped on the northern shore of the ocean.
And both <s>Mainda</s> and <s>Dvivida</s>, those foremost monkeys,
went about that army in every direction for the sake of protection.
When the army had encamped on the shore of the lord of rivers and streams,

children.text: pārśvasthaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmo vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, seeing <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> standing nearby, spoke these words:
"They say that grief passes away with the passing of time;
but for me, as I do not see my beloved, it increases day by day.

children.text: na me duḥkhaṃ priyā dūre na me duḥkhaṃ hṛteti ca
children.translated_text: My grief is not that my beloved is far away, nor is my grief simply that she has been carried off.
This very thing I grieve over: her youth is passing away.

children.text: vāhi vāta yataḥ kanyā tāṃ spṛṣṭvā mām api spṛśa
children.translated_text: Blow, O wind, from the place where the maiden is; after touching her, touch me too.
In you I have the touch of her limbs, and in the moon the meeting of my sight with hers.

children.text: tanme dahati gātrāṇi viṣaṃ pītam ivāśaye
children.translated_text: That burns my limbs like poison drunk within.

children.text: hā nātheti priyā sā māṃ hriyamāṇā yad abravīt ||
children.translated_text: When that beloved, while being carried away, said to me, "Ah, lord!"
with that separation as its fuel and with the thought of her as its wide flames,

children.text: rātriṃ divaṃ śarīraṃ me dahyate madanāgninā ||
children.translated_text: day and night my body is burned by the fire of love.
I shall plunge into the ocean and sleep, O <s>Saumitri</s>, without you;

children.text: kathaṃcit prajvalan kāmaḥ samāsuptaṃ jale dahet ||
children.translated_text: perhaps blazing desire will somehow burn me as I lie asleep in the water.
For one who longs so greatly, it is possible to live by this,

children.text: yad ahaṃ sā ca vāmorūr ekāṃ dharaṇim āśritau ||
children.translated_text: that I and she of lovely thighs are both resting on one and the same earth.
Like a waterless field beside a field that has water,
I live by a seepage of moisture, because I hear that she is alive.
But when indeed shall I see the fair-hipped one, whose eyes are long like lotuses,

children.text: vijitya śatrūn drakṣyāmi sītāṃ sphītām iva śriyam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s>, after conquering my enemies, like prosperity grown abundant?

children.text: kadā nu cārubimbauṣṭhaṃ tasyāḥ padmam ivānanam
children.translated_text: When, slightly raising her lotus-like face with its lovely bimba-fruit lips,
shall I drink it in like a sick man drinking an elixir?

children.text: tau tasyāḥ saṃhatau pīnau stanau tālaphalopamau
children.translated_text: Those two close-set, full breasts of hers, like palmyra fruits,

children.text: kadā nu khalu sotkampau hasantyā māṃ bhajiṣyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: when indeed, trembling as she laughs, will they come to me?
Surely that dark-cornered-eyed, faithful woman, standing among the <s>rākṣasas</s>,
though I am her lord, like one without a lord, finds no protector.
When will she, after throwing the <s>rākṣasas</s> into turmoil, shake them off and rise forth,
like a crescent moon in autumn shaking off dark clouds?
Naturally slender, surely <s>Sītā</s>, through grief and fasting,
has become still thinner because of the reversal of place and circumstance.
When, after planting arrows in the chest of the lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>,
shall I bring <s>Sītā</s> back and cast off the grief in my mind?

children.text: kadā nu khalu māṃ sādhvī sītāmarasutopamā
children.translated_text: When indeed will the virtuous <s>Sītā</s>, like a daughter of the immortals,
longing, clasp my neck and shed tears born of joy?
When shall I suddenly cast off this terrible grief born from separation from <s>Maithilī</s>,
as one casts off a garment that is no longer white?
As wise <s>Rāma</s> lamented in this way there,
the sun, its form grown dim at day's end, went to its setting.
Comforted by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, <s>Rāma</s> performed the twilight worship,
remembering lotus-petal-eyed <s>Sītā</s>, overcome by sorrow.

children.text: laṅkāyāṃ tu kṛtaṃ karma ghoraṃ dṛṣṭvā bhayāvaham
children.translated_text: But seeing the dreadful, fear-inspiring deed done in <s>Laṅkā</s>
by high-souled <s>Hanumān</s>, as if by <s>Śakra</s>,

children.text: abravīd rākṣasān sarvān hriyā kiṃcid avāṅmukhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>, somewhat downcast with shame, addressed all the <s>rākṣasas</s>:

children.text: dharṣitā ca praviṣṭā ca laṅkā duṣprasahā purī
children.translated_text: "The hard-to-assail city <s>Laṅkā</s> has been violated and entered,

children.text: tena vānaramātreṇa dṛṣṭā sītā ca jānakī ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Sītā Jānakī</s> has been seen by that mere <s>vānara</s>.
The palace and the shrine have been violated; foremost <s>rākṣasas</s> have been killed,

children.text: āvilā ca purī laṅkā sarvā hanumatā kṛtā ||
children.translated_text: and the whole city <s>Laṅkā</s> has been thrown into confusion by <s>Hanumān</s>.

children.text: kiṃ kariṣyāmi bhadraṃ vaḥ kiṃ vā yuktam anantaram
children.translated_text: What shall I do, good sirs? Or what is fitting next?

children.text: ucyatāṃ naḥ samarthaṃ yat kṛtaṃ ca sukṛtaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Tell us what would be effective and, once done, would be well done.

children.text: mantramūlaṃ hi vijayaṃ prāhur āryā manasvinaḥ
children.translated_text: For the noble and thoughtful say that victory has counsel as its root;

children.text: tasmād vai rocaye mantraṃ rāmaṃ prati mahābalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore, mighty ones, I approve counsel concerning <s>Rāma</s>.
In the world men are of three kinds: best, lowest, and middling;
I shall state the qualities and faults of those when they come together.
He who, with ministers joined to his welfare and capable in deciding counsel,

children.text: mitrair vāpi samānārthair bāndhavair api vā hitaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: or with friends of equal interest, or with well-wishing kinsmen,
having consulted together, sets undertakings in motion,

children.text: daive ca kurute yatnaṃ tam āhuḥ puruṣottamam ||
children.translated_text: and also makes effort with regard to fate: him they call the best man.

children.text: eko 'rthaṃ vimṛśed eko dharme prakurute manaḥ
children.translated_text: He who considers a matter alone, alone sets his mind on <s>dharma</s> (right order),

children.text: ekaḥ kāryāṇi kurute tam āhur madhyamaṃ naram ||
children.translated_text: and alone performs actions: him they call a middling man.
He who, without determining merits and faults and abandoning reliance on fate,

children.text: kariṣyāmīti yaḥ kāryam upekṣet sa narādhamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: neglects the task merely saying, "I will do it": he is the lowest man.
Just as these men are always best, lowest, and middling,
so too counsel is to be understood as best, lowest, and middling.
Where ministers, having reached unanimity through the eye taught by <s>śāstra</s> (authoritative teaching),

children.text: mantriṇo yatra nirastāstam āhur mantram uttamam ||
children.translated_text: are free from dissension, that they call the best counsel.
Where, though the ministers have gone through many opinions in deciding the matter,

children.text: punar yatraikatāṃ prāptaḥ sa mantro madhyamaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: they again arrive at unity, that counsel is remembered as middling.
Where each relies on another's opinion and discussion goes on,

children.text: na caikamatye śreyo 'sti mantraḥ so 'dhama ucyate ||
children.translated_text: and there is no good unanimity, that counsel is called inferior.
Therefore, excellent ministers, having deliberated well and properly,
undertake this task of mine, the most urgent of all.
For <s>Rāma</s>, surrounded by thousands of heroic <s>vānaras</s>,
is approaching the city <s>Laṅkā</s> to besiege us.

children.text: tariṣyati ca suvyaktaṃ rāghavaḥ sāgaraṃ sukham
children.translated_text: And it is quite clear that <s>Rāghava</s> will easily cross the ocean,
with fitting force, together with his younger brother and followed by his army.

children.text: asminn evaṃgate kārye viruddhe vānaraiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Since this matter has reached such a state, involving conflict with the <s>vānaras</s>,

children.text: hitaṃ pure ca sainye ca sarvaṃ saṃmantryatāṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: let everything beneficial for my city and army be fully deliberated for me.
Thus addressed by the lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>, those mighty <s>rākṣasas</s>
all spoke with joined palms to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>:
"O king, when your very great army is crowded with iron clubs, spears, lances, tridents, and broadswords,

children.text: sumahanno balaṃ kasmād viṣādaṃ bhajate bhavān ||
children.translated_text: why does Your Majesty fall into despondency?
He who dwells on the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>, surrounded by many <s>yakṣas</s>...

children.text: sumahat kadanaṃ kṛtvā vaśyaste dhanadaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After causing very great slaughter, you made the lord of wealth subject to you.
Boasting of his friendship with <s>Maheśvara</s>, O lord,
that mighty world-protector was conquered by you in battle, in anger.

children.text: vinihatya ca yakṣaughān vikṣobhya ca vigṛhya ca
children.translated_text: After slaying hosts of <s>yakṣas</s>, shaking them, and engaging them in battle,
this aerial car was brought by you from the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>.
By <s>Maya</s>, lord of the <s>dānavas</s>, who desired friendship out of fear of you,
his daughter was given to you as a wife, O bull among <s>rākṣasas</s>.
A lord of the <s>dānavas</s> named <s>Madhu</s>, swollen with valor and hard to assail,
was brought under control after being fought, bringing happiness to <s>Kumbhīnasī</s>.
The <s>nāgas</s> were conquered by you, O mighty-armed one, when you went to <s>Rasātala</s>;

children.text: vāsukistakṣakaḥ śaṅkho jaṭī ca vaśam āhṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vāsuki</s>, <s>Takṣaka</s>, <s>Śaṅkha</s>, and <s>Jaṭī</s> were brought under control.
The <s>dānavas</s>, inexhaustible, powerful, brave, and again possessed of boons,

children.text: tvayā saṃvatsaraṃ yuddhvā samare dānavā vibho ||
children.translated_text: after you had fought them for a year in battle, O lord,
were brought under control by you, crusher of foes, relying on your own strength,
and many magical powers were acquired there, O lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>.
The brave and powerful sons of <s>Varuṇa</s>, followed by four kinds of forces in battle,
were conquered by you, O mighty-armed one.
O king, you plunged into <s>Yama</s>'s ocean of forces, whose great crocodile was the death-rod,
and which was adorned with the island of <s>Śālmali</s>.
A vast victory was won, and death itself was checked;

children.text: suyuddhena ca te sarve lokāstatra sutoṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and by your good battle all the worlds there were greatly pleased.
The earth was filled with many heroic <s>kṣatriyas</s>, equal to <s>Śakra</s> in valor,

children.text: āsīd vasumatī pūrṇā mahadbhir iva pādapaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: as if it were filled with great trees.

children.text: teṣāṃ vīryaguṇotsāhair na samo rāghavo raṇe
children.translated_text: In battle there was no <s>Rāghava</s> equal to them in valor, qualities, and energy;

children.text: prasahya te tvayā rājan hatāḥ paramadurjayāḥ ||
children.translated_text: yet those most hard-to-conquer men were forcibly slain by you, O king.
O king, this misfortune has come from a common person and is unworthy of you;

children.text: hṛdi naiva tvayā kāryā tvaṃ vadhiṣyasi rāghavam ||
children.translated_text: you should not take it to heart at all. You will kill <s>Rāghava</s>.
Then a <s>rākṣasa</s> named <s>Prahasta</s>, dark as a blue cloud,
a brave commander, spoke these words then with joined palms:
Gods, <s>dānavas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, birds, and serpents

children.text: na tvāṃ dharṣayituṃ śaktāḥ kiṃ punar vānarā raṇe ||
children.translated_text: are not able to attack you; how much less can monkeys do so in battle?

children.text: sarve pramattā viśvastā vañcitāḥ sma hanūmatā
children.translated_text: All of us, heedless and trusting, were deceived by <s>Hanūmat</s>.

children.text: na hi me jīvato gacchejjīvan sa vanagocaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: If I were alive, that forest-roaming creature would not go away alive.
Let your majesty command me, and I shall make the whole earth, as far as the ocean,
with its mountains, woods, and groves, free of monkeys.
And I shall arrange protection from the monkey, O night-roamer;
no suffering born from your own fault will come upon you.
Then a <s>rākṣasa</s> named <s>Durmukha</s>, greatly enraged, said:

children.text: idaṃ na kṣamaṇīyaṃ hi sarveṣāṃ naḥ pradharṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: This outrage against all of us is not to be endured.
This is a further insult to the city and the inner apartments:
the assault by the lord of monkeys upon the glorious lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>.
At this very moment I alone shall kill the monkeys and return,

children.text: praviṣṭān sāgaraṃ bhīmam ambaraṃ vā rasātalam ||
children.translated_text: whether they have entered the dreadful ocean, the sky, or <s>Rasātala</s>.
Then mighty <s>Vajradaṃṣṭra</s>, greatly enraged, spoke,
grasping a terrible iron club smeared with flesh and blood:

children.text: kiṃ vo hanumatā kāryaṃ kṛpaṇena tapasvinā
children.translated_text: What business have you with that wretched ascetic <s>Hanūmat</s>,
when invincible <s>Rāma</s> stands there with <s>Sugrīva</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>?
Today, after I alone have struck down <s>Rāma</s> with <s>Sugrīva</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> by means of this club,
and have thrown the monkey army into confusion, I shall come back.
Then the heroic and powerful <s>Nikumbha</s>, son of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>,
spoke in extreme anger to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, who made the worlds cry out:
Let all of you remain here together with the great king;
I alone shall kill <s>Rāghava</s> together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Then a mountain-like <s>rākṣasa</s> named <s>Vajrahanu</s>,

children.text: kruddhaḥ parilihan vaktraṃ jihvayā vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: angry and licking his mouth with his tongue, spoke these words:
Let all of you freely attend to your affairs, free from anxiety;
I alone shall devour all those monkey troop-leaders.
Let them play at ease, without worry, and drink honey-wine;
I alone shall kill <s>Sugrīva</s> together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: sāṅgadaṃ ca hanūmantaṃ rāmaṃ ca raṇakuñjaram ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Hanūmat</s> together with <s>Aṅgada</s>, and <s>Rāma</s>, the elephant of battle.
Then <s>Nikumbha</s>, <s>Rabhasa</s>, <s>Sūryaśatru</s> the mighty,
<s>Suptaghna</s>, <s>Yajñakopa</s>, <s>Mahāpārśva</s>, and <s>Mahodara</s>,
<s>Agniketu</s> the invincible, and the <s>rākṣasa</s> <s>Raśmiketu</s>,
and <s>Indrajit</s>, the mighty and powerful son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
<s>Prahasta</s>, <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, mighty <s>Vajradaṃṣṭra</s>,
<s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>, <s>Atikāya</s>, and the <s>rākṣasa</s> <s>Durmukha</s>,
taking up iron clubs, battle-axes, spears, darts, tridents, axes,

children.text: cāpāni ca sabāṇāni khaḍgāṃśca vipulāñ śitān ||
children.translated_text: bows with arrows, and broad, sharp swords,
those <s>rākṣasas</s>, supremely enraged, sprang up

children.text: abruvan rāvaṇaṃ sarve pradīptā iva tejasā ||
children.translated_text: and all spoke to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, blazing as if with splendor:

children.text: adya rāmaṃ vadhiṣyāmaḥ sugrīvaṃ ca salakṣmaṇam
children.translated_text: Today we shall kill <s>Rāma</s>, and <s>Sugrīva</s> with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: kṛpaṇaṃ ca hanūmantaṃ laṅkā yena pradharṣitā ||
children.translated_text: and that wretched <s>Hanūmat</s> by whom <s>Laṅkā</s> was assaulted.
Having restrained all those men who had taken up weapons, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>

children.text: abravīt prāñjalir vākyaṃ punaḥ pratyupaveśya tān ||
children.translated_text: spoke again with joined palms, after making them sit down once more:
Dear one, when an objective cannot be attained by the three expedients,
the wise say that the proper times for valor are then appropriate for that objective.
When people are heedless, under attack, and struck down by fate,
Exploits, dear father, succeed when they are undertaken after examination and according to rule.

children.text: apramattaṃ kathaṃ taṃ tu vijigīṣuṃ bale sthitam
children.translated_text: But how do you wish to assail him who is vigilant, desirous of victory, and stationed in his strength,
who has conquered anger and is hard to overpower?
After crossing the dreadful ocean, the lord of rivers and streams,

children.text: kṛtaṃ hanumatā karma duṣkaraṃ tarkayeta kaḥ ||
children.translated_text: who could have imagined the difficult deed accomplished by <s>Hanumān</s>?
O <s>rākṣasas</s>, the forces and powers of enemies are immeasurable;
contempt for others must never be shown rashly in any way.
And what wrong had <s>Rāma</s> previously done to the king of the <s>rākṣasas</s>,
whose illustrious wife he carried away from <s>Janasthāna</s>?
If <s>Khara</s> had overstepped, he was killed by <s>Rāma</s> in battle;

children.text: avaśyaṃ prāṇināṃ prāṇā rakṣitavyā yathā balam ||
children.translated_text: for living beings must protect their lives as far as they are able.

children.text: etannimittaṃ vaidehī bhayaṃ naḥ sumahad bhavet
children.translated_text: Because of this <s>Vaidehī</s>, a very great danger may befall us.

children.text: āhṛtā sā parityājyā kalahārthe kṛte na kim ||
children.translated_text: She who was carried off should be given up; what was not done by creating a cause for quarrel?

children.text: na naḥ kṣamaṃ vīryavatā tena dharmānuvartinā
children.translated_text: It is not fitting for us to make a useless enmity

children.text: vairaṃ nirarthakaṃ kartuṃ dīyatām asya maithilī ||
children.translated_text: with that mighty follower of <s>dharma</s>; let <s>Maithilī</s> be given to him.
Before he tears apart this city, with its elephants and horses,

children.text: purīṃ dārayate bāṇair dīyatām asya maithilī ||
children.translated_text: crowded with many jewels, by his arrows, let <s>Maithilī</s> be given to him.
Before the very dreadful, great, irresistible army of monkeys

children.text: nāvaskandati no laṅkāṃ tāvat sītā pradīyatām ||
children.translated_text: falls upon our <s>Laṅkā</s>, let <s>Sītā</s> be given back.

children.text: vinaśyeddhi purī laṅkā śūrāḥ sarve ca rākṣasāḥ
children.translated_text: For the city of <s>Laṅkā</s> would perish, and all the brave <s>rākṣasas</s> too,

children.text: rāmasya dayitā patnī na svayaṃ yadi dīyate ||
children.translated_text: if <s>Rāma</s>'s beloved wife is not given back of your own accord.

children.text: prasādaye tvāṃ bandhutvāt kuruṣva vacanaṃ mama
children.translated_text: Because I am your kinsman, I entreat you: do what I say.

children.text: hitaṃ pathyaṃ tvahaṃ brūmi dīyatām asya maithilī ||
children.translated_text: I speak what is beneficial and wholesome; let <s>Maithilī</s> be given to him.
Before the prince releases, for your destruction, unfailing arrows like the rays of the autumn sun,

children.text: sṛjatyamoghān viśikhān vadhāya te pradīyatāṃ dāśarathāya maithilī ||
children.translated_text: with fresh points and feathers and very firm shafts, let <s>Maithilī</s> be given to <s>Dāśarathi</s>.

children.text: tyajasva kopaṃ sukhadharmanāśanaṃ bhajasva dharmaṃ ratikīrtivardhanam
children.translated_text: Abandon anger, which destroys happiness and <s>dharma</s>; embrace <s>dharma</s>, which increases delight and fame.

children.text: prasīda jīvema saputrabāndhavāḥ pradīyatāṃ dāśarathāya maithilī ||
children.translated_text: Be gracious; may we live with sons and kinsmen. Let <s>Maithilī</s> be given to <s>Dāśarathi</s>.
When <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> had spoken this well-founded, beneficial speech,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, driven on by Time, spoke a harsh word.
One may live together with an angry enemy, or even with a venomous serpent,
but one should not live with one who is a friend in name while serving the enemy.
O <s>rākṣasa</s>, I know the character of kinsmen in all the worlds:
kinsmen always rejoice in the misfortunes of their kin.

children.text: pradhānaṃ sādhakaṃ vaidyaṃ dharmaśīlaṃ ca rākṣasa
children.translated_text: O <s>rākṣasa</s>, kinsmen despise a foremost man, one who succeeds, one who is learned, and one whose nature is righteous;
they also insult a hero.
Always delighted with one another in others' calamities, assailants in misfortune,
with hidden hearts and terrible, kinsmen are fearsome.

children.text: śrūyante hastibhir gītāḥ ślokāḥ padmavane kvacit
children.translated_text: There are verses once heard sung by elephants in a lotus grove,

children.text: pāśahastānnarān dṛṣṭvā śṛṇu tān gadato mama ||
children.translated_text: when they saw men with nooses in their hands; listen as I recite them.

children.text: nāgnir nānyāni śastrāṇi na naḥ pāśā bhayāvahāḥ
children.translated_text: Neither fire, nor other weapons, nor nooses are fearsome to us;
but terrible kinsmen, intent on their own interest, are fearsome to us.

children.text: upāyam ete vakṣyanti grahaṇe nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: They will tell the means for capturing us; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: kṛtsnād bhayājjñātibhayaṃ sukaṣṭaṃ viditaṃ ca naḥ ||
children.translated_text: Of all fears, fear from kinsmen is very painful, and it is known to us.

children.text: vidyate goṣu sampannaṃ vidyate brāhmaṇe damaḥ
children.translated_text: Prosperity is found among cows; self-restraint is found in a Brahmin.

children.text: vidyate strīṣu cāpalyaṃ vidyate jñātito bhayam ||
children.translated_text: Fickleness is found among women; danger is found from kinsmen.

children.text: tato neṣṭam idaṃ saumya yad ahaṃ lokasatkṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore this, gentle one, is not pleasing to you: that I am honored by the world,

children.text: aiśvaryam abhijātaśca ripūṇāṃ mūrdhni ca sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: born to sovereignty, and standing upon the heads of my enemies.
If another night-roamer were to speak such a speech as this,

children.text: asminmuhūrte na bhavet tvāṃ tu dhik kulapāṃsanam ||
children.translated_text: he would not exist at this very moment; but shame on you, disgrace of the family!
Thus addressed with harsh speech, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, speaker of what is just,
leapt up, mace in hand, together with four <s>rākṣasas</s>.
Then <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, anger arisen in him, spoke these words,
standing in the air, glorious, to his brother, the lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>:

children.text: sa tvaṃ bhrātāsi me rājan brūhi māṃ yad yad icchasi
children.translated_text: You are my brother, O king; say to me whatever you wish.

children.text: idaṃ tu paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ na kṣamāmyanṛtaṃ tava ||
children.translated_text: But I do not tolerate this harsh, untrue word of yours.
A well-guided and beneficial word has been spoken by one who seeks your good, O ten-faced one;
but those without self-mastery, come under the sway of Time, do not accept it.
O king, men who always speak what is pleasant are easy to find,

children.text: apriyasya tu pathyasya vaktā śrotā ca durlabhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but one who speaks what is unpleasant yet wholesome, and one who listens to it, are hard to find.
Bound by the noose of Time, which carries off all beings,

children.text: na naśyantam upekṣeyaṃ pradīptaṃ śaraṇaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: I would not neglect you as you perish, like a shelter set on fire.
I do not wish to see you killed by <s>Rāma</s> with arrows

children.text: na tvām icchāmyahaṃ draṣṭuṃ rāmeṇa nihataṃ śaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: blazing like flaming fire, sharp, and adorned with gold.
Heroes who are strong and skilled in weapons on the battlefield,
when overtaken by Time, sink down like bridges of sand.

children.text: ātmānaṃ sarvathā rakṣa purīṃ cemāṃ sarākṣasām
children.translated_text: Protect yourself in every way, and this city together with its <s>rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: svasti te 'stu gamiṣyāmi sukhī bhava mayā vinā ||
children.translated_text: May it be well with you; I shall go. Be happy without me.

children.text: nivāryamāṇasya mayā hitaiṣiṇā na rocate te vacanaṃ niśācara
children.translated_text: Though I, desiring your welfare, try to restrain you, my word does not please you, O night-roamer.

children.text: parītakālā hi gatāyuṣo narā hitaṃ na gṛhṇanti suhṛdbhir īritam ||
children.translated_text: For men whose time has closed in and whose life is spent do not accept beneficial advice spoken by friends.
Having thus spoken a harsh word to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s younger brother
came in a moment to where <s>Rāma</s> was, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
The monkey lords standing on the earth saw him in the sky, shaped like a peak of <s>Meru</s>,
like a blazing lightning flash.
Seeing him with himself as the fifth, <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the monkeys...
The wise and hard-to-assail one pondered together with the <s>vānaras</s>.

children.text: cintayitvā muhūrtaṃ tu vānarāṃstān uvāca ha
children.translated_text: After thinking for a moment, he addressed those <s>vānaras</s>,
all headed by <s>Hanūmān</s>, with these excellent words:
"Look, this <s>rākṣasa</s>, equipped with every weapon and accompanied by four <s>rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: rākṣaso 'bhyeti paśyadhvam asmān hantuṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is coming toward us, no doubt to kill us."

children.text: sugrīvasya vacaḥ śrutvā sarve te vānarottamāḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Sugrīva</s>'s words, all those best of <s>vānaras</s>,

children.text: sālān udyamya śailāṃśca idaṃ vacanam abruvan ||
children.translated_text: lifting up sāla trees and rocks, spoke these words:

children.text: śīghraṃ vyādiśa no rājan vadhāyaiṣāṃ durātmanām
children.translated_text: "Command us quickly, O king, for the slaughter of these evil-minded ones.
Let these short-lived creatures fall to the ground, slain."
While they were speaking with one another, that <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,

children.text: uttaraṃ tīram āsādya khastha eva vyatiṣṭhata ||
children.translated_text: having reached the northern shore, remained standing in the sky itself.

children.text: uvāca ca mahāprājñaḥ svareṇa mahatā mahān
children.translated_text: And the great, very wise <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> spoke in a loud voice,

children.text: sugrīvaṃ tāṃśca samprekṣya khastha eva vibhīṣaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: looking at <s>Sugrīva</s> and those others, while still standing in the sky:
"There is an ill-conducted <s>rākṣasa</s> named <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: tasyāham anujo bhrātā vibhīṣaṇa iti śrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I am his younger brother, known by the name <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>.
By him <s>Sītā</s> was carried off from <s>Janasthāna</s> after he had killed <s>Jaṭāyus</s>,

children.text: ruddhvā ca vivaśā dīnā rākṣasībhiḥ surakṣitā ||
children.translated_text: and she is held captive, helpless and wretched, guarded closely by <s>rākṣasīs</s>.

children.text: tam ahaṃ hetubhir vākyair vividhaiśca nyadarśayam
children.translated_text: With reasoned words and many arguments I pointed out to him,

children.text: sādhu niryātyatāṃ sītā rāmāyeti punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: again and again, 'Let <s>Sītā</s> be duly returned to <s>Rāma</s>.'

children.text: sa ca na pratijagrāha rāvaṇaḥ kālacoditaḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, driven by death, did not accept it,
though a beneficial word was being spoken, like one perversely rejecting medicine.
So I, reviled by him and insulted like a slave,

children.text: tyaktvā putrāṃśca dārāṃśca rāghavaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: have abandoned sons and wife and come to <s>Rāghava</s> for refuge.
Quickly announce me, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, who has arrived,
to high-souled <s>Rāghava</s>, the refuge of all worlds."

children.text: etat tu vacanaṃ śrutvā sugrīvo laghuvikramaḥ
children.translated_text: But hearing this speech, <s>Sugrīva</s> of swift valor,
agitated, spoke these words to <s>Rāma</s> in front of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:
"The younger brother of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, known as <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,

children.text: caturbhiḥ saha rakṣobhir bhavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: has come to Your Majesty for refuge, together with four <s>rākṣasas</s>.
Know this <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> to have been sent by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: tasyāhaṃ nigrahaṃ manye kṣamaṃ kṣamavatāṃ vara ||
children.translated_text: I think it proper to restrain him, O best of the forbearing.
This <s>rākṣasa</s> has come here, ordered with crooked intention,

children.text: prahartuṃ māyayā channo viśvaste tvayi rāghava ||
children.translated_text: hidden by deceit so as to strike when you trust him, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: badhyatām eṣa tīvreṇa daṇḍena sacivaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Let him be punished with severe punishment, together with his ministers,
for this <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> is the brother of cruel <s>Rāvaṇa</s>."

children.text: evam uktvā tu taṃ rāmaṃ saṃrabdho vāhinīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus addressed <s>Rāma</s>, the commander of the army, still agitated,
a knower of speech, then fell silent before him who was skilled in speech.

children.text: sugrīvasya tu tad vākyaṃ śrutvā rāmo mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: But mighty <s>Rāma</s>, hearing that statement of <s>Sugrīva</s>,
spoke as follows to the <s>haris</s> standing nearby, headed by <s>Hanūmān</s>:
"What has been said by the monkey-king concerning <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s younger brother

children.text: vākyaṃ hetumad atyarthaṃ bhavadbhir api tacchrutam ||
children.translated_text: is a very well-reasoned statement, and you too have heard it.
For in difficulties of purpose it is fitting for a wise and good friend,
even one capable himself, to give counsel when he desires lasting prosperity.

children.text: ityevaṃ paripṛṣṭāste svaṃ svaṃ matam atandritāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus questioned, they then, alert and wishing to do what was beneficial,
each stated his own opinion to <s>Rāma</s> with due courtesy.

children.text: ajñātaṃ nāsti te kiṃcit triṣu lokeṣu rāghava
children.translated_text: "Nothing at all is unknown to you in the three worlds, O <s>Rāghava</s>.
O <s>Rāma</s>, honoring us, you ask us out of friendship.

children.text: tvaṃ hi satyavrataḥ śūro dhārmiko dṛḍhavikramaḥ
children.translated_text: For you are true to your vow, heroic, righteous, and firm in valor,
one who acts after examination, mindful, and open-hearted toward friends.
Therefore let your ministers, one by one, speak first,
again and again, with reasons, being possessed of judgment and competence."
When this had been said to <s>Rāghava</s>, wise <s>Aṅgada</s>, standing in front,
the <s>hari</s>, spoke these words for the purpose of testing <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>:

children.text: śatroḥ sakāśāt samprāptaḥ sarvathā śaṅkya eva hi
children.translated_text: "One who has come from the presence of an enemy is surely to be suspected in every way.
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> should not suddenly be made worthy of trust.
For men of deceitful mind move about concealing their true nature,

children.text: praharanti ca randhreṣu so 'narthaḥ sumahān bhavet ||
children.translated_text: and they strike at vulnerable points; that would become a very great disaster.
