Having determined advantage and disadvantage, one should take a firm course.
One should accept him on account of merits, but dismiss him on account of faults.
If there is a great fault in him, let him be abandoned without hesitation.

children.text: guṇān vāpi bahūñ jñātvā saṃgrahaḥ kriyatāṃ nṛpa ||
children.translated_text: Or, knowing many merits, let him be accepted, O king."
Then <s>Śarabha</s>, having decided, spoke a meaningful word:
"Quickly, O tiger among men, let a spy be appointed concerning this man.
For after setting a subtle-minded spy on him,

children.text: parīkṣya ca tataḥ kāryo yathānyāyaṃ parigrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and examining him properly, he should then be accepted according to rule."
Then discerning <s>Jāmbavān</s>, looking on with understanding grounded in <s>śāstra</s> (authoritative teaching),
made known a statement endowed with merits and free from faults:
"<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> has come from the wicked lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>, with whom enmity is fixed,
at an improper place and time; in every way this man should be suspected."
Then <s>Mainda</s>, skilled in policy and impolicy, after considering,
spoke a still more reasoned statement, being eloquent in speech:
"This <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> is said to be connected with that <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Let him be questioned gently and slowly, O lord of the best of men.

children.text: bhāvam asya tu vijñāya tatastattvaṃ kariṣyasi
children.translated_text: Having learned his disposition, then you will determine the truth,

children.text: yadi dṛṣṭo na duṣṭo vā buddhipūrvaṃ nararṣabha ||
children.translated_text: whether he is seen to be corrupt or not, deliberately, O bull among men."
Then <s>Hanūmān</s>, endowed with refinement and the best of ministers,
He spoke words that were polished, meaningful, sweet, and concise.

children.text: na bhavantaṃ matiśreṣṭhaṃ samarthaṃ vadatāṃ varam
children.translated_text: Not even <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, while speaking, would be able to surpass you,
O best in judgment, capable one, foremost among speakers.
It is not from argument, nor from contention, nor from superiority, nor from desire
that I shall speak, O king, but truthfully, out of respect for <s>Rāma</s>.
As for what your ministers have said, with advantage and disadvantage as its ground,

children.text: tatra doṣaṃ prapaśyāmi kriyā na hyupapadyate ||
children.translated_text: I see a fault there, for that course of action is not appropriate.

children.text: ṛte niyogāt sāmarthyam avaboddhuṃ na śakyate
children.translated_text: Apart from an assigned charge, a person’s capacity cannot be known;

children.text: sahasā viniyogo hi doṣavān pratibhāti me ||
children.translated_text: sudden employment seems to me to be full of fault.
As for the placing of spies, which your ministers proposed,
because the aim cannot be accomplished there, the reason does not apply.
As to the claim that this <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> has arrived at an improper place and time,

children.text: vivakṣā cātra me 'stīyaṃ tāṃ nibodha yathāmati ||
children.translated_text: I have something to say on this point; hear it according to my judgment.

children.text: sa eṣa deśaḥ kālaśca bhavatīha yathā tathā
children.translated_text: This same place and time become suitable here in whatever way they do,
when they come from one person to another; so too do faults and virtues.

children.text: daurātmyaṃ rāvaṇe dṛṣṭvā vikramaṃ ca tathā tvayi
children.translated_text: Seeing wickedness in <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and likewise prowess in you,

children.text: yuktam āgamanaṃ tasya sadṛśaṃ tasya buddhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: his coming is fitting and consistent with his intelligence.

children.text: ajñātarūpaiḥ puruṣaiḥ sa rājan pṛcchyatām iti
children.translated_text: As for what was said here, O king, “Let him be questioned by men of unknown appearance,”

children.text: yad uktam atra me prekṣā kācid asti samīkṣitā ||
children.translated_text: I have a certain considered view about that.
Being questioned, he, being wise, might at once mistrust the words;

children.text: tatra mitraṃ praduṣyeta mithyā pṛṣṭaṃ sukhāgatam ||
children.translated_text: then a friend, falsely questioned after happily arriving, might be alienated.

children.text: aśakyaḥ sahasā rājan bhāvo vettuṃ parasya vai
children.translated_text: O king, the disposition of another person cannot be known all at once;

children.text: antaḥ svabhāvair gītaistair naipuṇyaṃ paśyatā bhṛśam ||
children.translated_text: one must look very carefully at skill through those signs of inner nature.

children.text: na tvasya bruvato jātu lakṣyate duṣṭabhāvatā
children.translated_text: But no evil intention is ever perceived while he is speaking,

children.text: prasannaṃ vadanaṃ cāpi tasmānme nāsti saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and his face too is clear; therefore I have no doubt.
With an unsuspecting mind, self-possessed, and not deceitful, he does not move furtively,

children.text: na cāsya duṣṭā vāk cāpi tasmānnāstīha saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor is his speech evil; therefore there is no doubt here.
Even when outward form is being concealed, it cannot be fully hidden;
by force it reveals the inward feeling of human beings.
O best of those who know what should be done, a task suited to place and time,
when intended and put into execution, quickly makes its result fruitful.

children.text: udyogaṃ tava samprekṣya mithyāvṛttaṃ ca rāvaṇam
children.translated_text: Observing your effort, the false conduct of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
and hearing of <s>Vālin</s>’s death and of <s>Sugrīva</s> being consecrated,
he has come here deliberately, desiring the kingdom.

children.text: etāvat tu puraskṛtya yujyate tvasya saṃgrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Taking just this into account, his acceptance is appropriate.
According to my ability I have spoken regarding the honesty of the <s>rākṣasa</s>;

children.text: tvaṃ pramāṇaṃ tu śeṣasya śrutvā buddhimatāṃ vara ||
children.translated_text: but you are the authority for the rest, after hearing, O best of the wise.

children.text: atha rāmaḥ prasannātmā śrutvā vāyusutasya ha
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s>, serene in spirit, after hearing the son of <s>Vāyu</s>,
the unassailable and learned one, replied with what was settled in his own mind.

children.text: mamāpi tu vivakṣāsti kācit prati vibhīṣaṇam
children.translated_text: I too have something to say regarding <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>;

children.text: śrutam icchāmi tat sarvaṃ bhavadbhiḥ śreyasi sthitaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: I wish all of it to be heard by you, who stand in what is best.
One who has come in the spirit of friendship I would not abandon in any way;

children.text: doṣo yadyapi tasya syāt satām etad agarhitam ||
children.translated_text: even if he had some fault, this is not censured among good people.
Hearing <s>Rāma</s>’s words, <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the <s>vānaras</s>,
urged on by affection, replied to <s>Kākutstha</s>.
What wonder is there in this, O knower of <s>dharma</s>, crest-jewel of the world’s protectors,

children.text: yat tvam āryaṃ prabhāṣethāḥ sattvavān satpathe sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that you, noble, strong in character, and standing on the good path, should speak nobly?
My own inner self also knows <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> to be pure,
well examined from inference, from his disposition, and from every side.
Therefore, O <s>Rāghava</s>, let him quickly become equal with us,
and let very wise <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> enter into friendship with us.

children.text: sa sugrīvasya tad vākyaṃ rāmaḥ śrutvā vimṛśya ca
children.translated_text: After <s>Rāma</s> heard that statement of <s>Sugrīva</s> and reflected on it,
he then spoke words still more auspicious to the foremost of <s>vānaras</s>.

children.text: suduṣṭo vāpyaduṣṭo vā kim eṣa rajanīcaraḥ
children.translated_text: Whether this night-roaming being is very wicked or not wicked,
he is in no way able to do me even the slightest harm.

children.text: piśācān dānavān yakṣān pṛthivyāṃ caiva rākṣasān
children.translated_text: The <s>piśācas</s>, <s>dānavas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and <s>rākṣasas</s> on earth,
I could kill them with the tip of my finger if I wished, O lord of the monkey hosts.

children.text: śrūyate hi kapotena śatruḥ śaraṇam āgataḥ
children.translated_text: For it is heard that by a pigeon an enemy who had come for refuge
was honored according to rule and invited with its own flesh.

children.text: sa hi taṃ pratijagrāha bhāryā hartāram āgatam
children.translated_text: For that pigeon received the one who had come, the abductor of his wife;

children.text: kapoto vānaraśreṣṭha kiṃ punar madvidho janaḥ ||
children.translated_text: how much more should a person like me do so, O best of <s>vānaras</s>?
Hear the ancient verse, most righteous, formerly sung by

children.text: śṛṇu gāthāṃ purā gītāṃ dharmiṣṭhāṃ satyavādinā ||
children.translated_text: the truth-speaking great seer <s>Kaṇḍu</s>, son of the seer <s>Kaṇva</s>.
One should not kill, for the sake of non-cruelty, even an enemy

children.text: na hanyād ānṛśaṃsyārtham api śatruṃ paraṃtapa ||
children.translated_text: who has come for refuge, wretched and begging with hands folded, O scorcher of foes.

children.text: ārto vā yadi vā dṛptaḥ pareṣāṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: Whether distressed or proud, if an enemy has gone to another’s refuge,
he must be protected by a self-controlled man, even at the cost of his life.

children.text: sa ced bhayād vā mohād vā kāmād vāpi na rakṣati
children.translated_text: If, from fear, delusion, or desire, he does not protect him

children.text: svayā śaktyā yathātattvaṃ tat pāpaṃ lokagarhitam ||
children.translated_text: to the full extent of his own power and in truth, that sin is condemned by the world.
If one who has come for refuge perishes while his protector looks on,

children.text: ādāya sukṛtaṃ tasya sarvaṃ gacched arakṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: unprotected, he goes away taking all that protector’s merit.

children.text: evaṃ doṣo mahān atra prapannānām arakṣaṇe
children.translated_text: Thus there is great fault here in failing to protect those who have surrendered;
it does not lead to heaven, brings infamy, and destroys strength and valor.

children.text: kariṣyāmi yathārthaṃ tu kaṇḍor vacanam uttamam
children.translated_text: I shall act rightly according to the excellent saying of <s>Kaṇḍu</s>;

children.text: dharmiṣṭhaṃ ca yaśasyaṃ ca svargyaṃ syāt tu phalodaye ||
children.translated_text: when its fruit arises, it will be most righteous, famous, and leading to heaven.

children.text: sakṛd eva prapannāya tavāsmīti ca yācate
children.translated_text: To one who has come for refuge even once and asks, saying, "I am yours,"
I grant fearlessness from all beings; this is my vow.
Bring him here, best of the <s>vānaras</s>; protection has been granted to him by me,

children.text: vibhīṣaṇo vā sugrīva yadi vā rāvaṇaḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: whether he is <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, <s>Sugrīva</s>, or even <s>Rāvaṇa</s> himself.
Then the lord of men, hearing the words of <s>Sugrīva</s> spoken by that lord of the <s>haris</s>,

children.text: vibhīṣaṇenāśu jagāma saṃgamaṃ patatrirājena yathā puraṃdaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: quickly went to a meeting with <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, like <s>Puraṃdara</s> with the king of birds.
When <s>Rāghava</s> had granted fearlessness, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s younger brother bowed low,

children.text: khāt papātāvaniṃ hṛṣṭo bhaktair anucaraiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: and fell joyfully from the sky to the ground, together with his loyal attendants.

children.text: sa tu rāmasya dharmātmā nipapāta vibhīṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: That righteous <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> then fell down
at <s>Rāma</s>'s feet, seeking refuge, together with four <s>rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: abravīcca tadā rāmaṃ vākyaṃ tatra vibhīṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: And then <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> spoke these words to <s>Rāma</s> there,

children.text: dharmayuktaṃ ca yuktaṃ ca sāmprataṃ saṃpraharṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: righteous, fitting, timely, and gladdening.
"I am the younger brother of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, and I have been insulted by him.
I have come for refuge to you, the refuge of all beings.

children.text: parityaktā mayā laṅkā mitrāṇi ca dhanāni ca
children.translated_text: <s>Laṅkā</s> has been abandoned by me, along with friends and wealth;

children.text: bhavadgataṃ me rājyaṃ ca jīvitaṃ ca sukhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: my kingdom, my life, and my pleasures are now placed in you.
In killing the <s>rākṣasas</s> and storming <s>Laṅkā</s>,
I shall give aid to the extent of my life, and I shall enter the army."
As he was speaking thus, <s>Rāma</s> embraced <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,
and, pleased, said to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, "Bring water from the ocean.
With it quickly consecrate this very wise <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>

children.text: rājānaṃ rakṣasāṃ kṣipraṃ prasanne mayi mānada ||
children.translated_text: as king of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, now that I am gracious, giver of honor."
Thus addressed, <s>Saumitri</s> consecrated <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>
as king in the midst of the chiefs of the <s>vānaras</s>, by <s>Rāma</s>'s command.

children.text: taṃ prasādaṃ tu rāmasya dṛṣṭvā sadyaḥ plavaṃgamāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that favor of <s>Rāma</s>, the <s>plavaṃgamas</s> at once
shouted great cries and said, "Good, good!"
Then <s>Hanumān</s> and <s>Sugrīva</s> said to <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,
"How shall we cross the unshakable ocean, the abode of <s>Varuṇa</s>?
By what means shall we approach the lord of rivers and streams
so that all of us, with the army, may swiftly cross the abode of <s>Varuṇa</s>?"
Thus addressed, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, knower of <s>dharma</s> (right order), replied,

children.text: samudraṃ rāghavo rājā śaraṇaṃ gantum arhati ||
children.translated_text: "King <s>Rāghava</s> ought to seek refuge with the ocean.
This immeasurable great ocean was dug by <s>Sagara</s>;

children.text: kartum arhati rāmasya jñāteḥ kāryaṃ mahodadhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the great ocean ought to do the task of its kinsman <s>Rāma</s>."
When the wise <s>rākṣasa</s> <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> had spoken thus,
it pleased <s>Rāghava</s> too, who was by nature devoted to <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: sa lakṣmaṇaṃ mahātejāḥ sugrīvaṃ ca harīśvaram
children.translated_text: Mighty <s>Rāma</s>, skilled in action, then addressed <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>
and <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the <s>haris</s>, with a smile, for the sake of proper action:
"This counsel of <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> pleases me, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Speak, you together with <s>Sugrīva</s>, if it pleases you also.
<s>Sugrīva</s> is always learned, and you are skilled in counsel;

children.text: ubhābhyāṃ sampradhāryāryaṃ rocate yat tad ucyatām ||
children.translated_text: after both of you have deliberated, noble one, say what seems good."

children.text: evam uktau tu tau vīrāvubhau sugrīvalakṣmaṇau
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, those two heroes, <s>Sugrīva</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
spoke these words, joined with proper courtesy:

children.text: kimarthaṃ no naravyāghra na rociṣyati rāghava
children.translated_text: "Why should what <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> has said not please us, tiger among men, <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: vibhīṣaṇena yat tūktam asmin kāle sukhāvaham ||
children.translated_text: since it brings welfare at this time?
Without building a bridge over this dreadful sea, the abode of <s>Varuṇa</s>,

children.text: laṅkā nāsādituṃ śakyā sendrair api surāsuraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Laṅkā</s> cannot be reached even by gods and <s>asuras</s> together with <s>Indra</s>.
Let the words of heroic <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> be carried out exactly;
enough of spending time: let this ocean be set to the task."
Thus addressed, on the shore of the lord of rivers and streams, spread with <s>kuśa</s> grass,

children.text: saṃviveśa tadā rāmo vedyām iva hutāśanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> then lay down like fire on an altar.
As <s>Rāma</s> lay on the ground spread with <s>kuśa</s> grass,
vigilant in his observance, three nights passed.

children.text: na ca darśayate mandastadā rāmasya sāgaraḥ
children.translated_text: But the dull ocean did not then show himself to <s>Rāma</s>,
though he had been duly honored by <s>Rāma</s>, who had made the effort.
Then <s>Rāma</s>, angry at the ocean, his eyes red at the corners,
spoke these words to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, marked with auspicious signs, who stood nearby:
"Just see, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the arrogance of this ignoble ocean, though it is being worshiped,

children.text: avalepaṃ samudrasya na darśayati yat svayam ||
children.translated_text: in that it does not show itself.
Calmness, forbearance, straightforwardness, and pleasant speech:
these virtues of good men bear fruit among the worthless as mere incapacity.
A self-praising, wicked, insolent man, rushing perversely about,
and wielding punishment everywhere, is honored by the world.

children.text: na sāmnā śakyate kīrtir na sāmnā śakyate yaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Fame cannot be obtained by conciliation, nor can renown be obtained by conciliation,

children.text: prāptuṃ lakṣmaṇa loke 'smiñ jayo vā raṇamūrdhani ||
children.translated_text: nor victory at the front of battle in this world, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Today, with <s>makaras</s> pierced by my arrows,
see the abode of <s>makaras</s>, O <s>Saumitri</s>, its waters obstructed by creatures floating everywhere.

children.text: mahābhogāni matsyānāṃ kariṇāṃ ca karān iha
children.translated_text: See here the great bodies of fish and the trunks of elephants,

children.text: bhogāṃśca paśya nāgānāṃ mayā bhinnāni lakṣmaṇa ||
children.translated_text: and the coils of <s>nāgas</s>, split apart by me, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
With arrows, along with its masses of conches and shells, its fish and <s>makaras</s>,
today, by a great battle, I shall dry up the ocean.

children.text: kṣamayā hi samāyuktaṃ mām ayaṃ makarālayaḥ
children.translated_text: For this abode of <s>makaras</s> thinks that I, endowed with forbearance,

children.text: asamarthaṃ vijānāti dhik kṣamām īdṛśe jane ||
children.translated_text: am powerless. Shame on forbearance toward such a person!
Bring the bow, <s>Saumitri</s>, and arrows like venomous serpents;
today, enraged, I shall shake even the unshakable ocean."
Though its boundary had been fixed at the shores and it was filled with thousands of waves,
I shall make the abode of <s>Varuṇa</s> overstep its bounds with my arrows.
Having spoken thus, bow in hand, his eyes widened with anger,

children.text: babhūva rāmo durdharṣo yugāntāgnir iva jvalan ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> became unassailable, blazing like the fire at the end of an age.

children.text: saṃpīḍya ca dhanur ghoraṃ kampayitvā śarair jagat
children.translated_text: Pressing down his dreadful bow and shaking the world with his arrows,
he released fierce shafts, like thunderbolts from <s>Śatakratu</s>.
Those best of arrows, blazing, very swift, and full of brilliance,
entered the water of the ocean, frightening the serpents.
Then there arose a great surge of the ocean, filled with crocodiles and makaras,
exceedingly terrible, with a roar like the wind.
Spread out with garlands of great waves and filled with conchs and shells,
the great ocean suddenly had waves that whirled as if amid smoke.
The serpents were distressed, with blazing mouths and blazing eyes,
as were the very powerful <s>Dānavas</s> who dwell at the bottom of the netherworld.
Then the waves of the king of rivers, filled with crocodiles and makaras,
leapt up in thousands, resembling <s>Vindhya</s> and <s>Mandara</s>.
With masses of waves thrown into turmoil, and with serpents and <s>rākṣasas</s> bewildered,
the watery expanse became one in which great sea-creatures were churned up.

children.text: tato madhyāt samudrasya sāgaraḥ svayam utthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then from the middle of the ocean <s>Sāgara</s> himself arose,
like the sun rising up from the great mountain <s>Meru</s>;
the ocean appeared together with serpents whose mouths were blazing.
He shone like smooth vaidūrya and was adorned with jāmbūnada gold,
wearing red garlands and garments, with eyes like lotus petals.
Mighty <s>Sāgara</s>, coming forward, first addressed him,
and with joined palms spoke these words to <s>Rāghava</s>, who held arrows in his hand.

children.text: pṛthivī vāyur ākāśam āpo jyotiśca rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Earth, wind, space, water, and light, O <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: svabhāve saumya tiṣṭhanti śāśvataṃ mārgam āśritāḥ ||
children.translated_text: abide in their own nature, gentle one, resorting to the eternal course.
This too is my own nature: that I am unfathomable and cannot be crossed by swimming.

children.text: vikārastu bhaved gādha etat te pravadāmyaham ||
children.translated_text: If there were alteration, I would become fordable; this I tell you.

children.text: na kāmānna ca lobhād vā na bhayāt pārthivātmaja
children.translated_text: Not from desire, nor from greed, nor from fear, O son of a king,
could I in any way make still my waters, crowded with sea-monsters.

children.text: vidhāsye rāma yenāpi viṣahiṣye hyahaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: I shall make such an arrangement, O <s>Rāma</s>, by which I will endure it in that way:

children.text: grāhā na prahariṣyanti yāvat senā tariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: the sea-creatures will not attack while the army is crossing.

children.text: ayaṃ saumya nalo nāma tanujo viśvakarmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Here, gentle one, is one named <s>Nala</s>, the son of <s>Viśvakarma</s>,
splendid, granted a boon by his father, and equal to <s>Viśvakarma</s>.

children.text: eṣa setuṃ mahotsāhaḥ karotu mayi vānaraḥ
children.translated_text: Let this greatly energetic <s>vānara</s> (monkey warrior) build the bridge upon me;

children.text: tam ahaṃ dhārayiṣyāmi tathā hyeṣa yathā pitā ||
children.translated_text: I shall support him, for he is just like his father.
Having spoken thus, the ocean vanished; then <s>Nala</s>, rising up,
the best of the vānaras, spoke these words to mighty <s>Rāma</s>:
I shall make a bridge over the broad abode of <s>Varuṇa</s>,

children.text: pituḥ sāmarthyam āsthāya tattvam āha mahodadhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: relying on my father's skill. The great ocean has spoken the truth.

children.text: mama mātur varo datto mandare viśvakarmaṇā
children.translated_text: A boon was given to my mother on <s>Mandara</s> by <s>Viśvakarma</s>:
I am his own son, resembling <s>Viśvakarma</s>.

children.text: na cāpyaham anukto vai prabrūyām ātmano guṇān
children.translated_text: Yet, unasked, I would not indeed proclaim my own virtues.
Let the foremost vānaras now build the bridge, as they wish.
Then the monkey-chiefs, sent out by <s>Rāma</s> in every direction,
joyfully rushed into the great forest by the hundreds of thousands.
There the mountain-like vānaras, bulls among the bands of tree-ranging monkeys,
broke trees and dragged them toward the ocean.
The vānaras, with śāla, aśvakarṇa, dhava, and bamboo trees,
and also with kuṭaja, arjuna, tāla, tilaka, and timiśa trees,
with bilvaka and saptaparṇa trees, and with flowering karṇikāras,
and with mango and aśoka trees, filled the ocean.
The best of the monkeys took trees, some with roots and some uprooted,
and, lifting them up like <s>Indra</s>'s standards, the monkeys carried the trees away.
As mountains were hurled in, the water was suddenly stirred up,
rose up to the sky, and then flowed away in every direction.
Ten yojanas wide and a hundred yojanas long,
<s>Nala</s> made the great bridge in the middle of the lord of rivers and streams.
As rocks were being thrown and mountains were being dropped there,
a tumultuous sound arose then in that great ocean.

children.text: sa nalena kṛtaḥ setuḥ sāgare makarālaye
children.translated_text: That bridge, made by <s>Nala</s> on the ocean, the abode of makaras,
shone, lovely and splendid, like the path of <s>Svāti</s> in the sky.
Then the gods, together with the <s>Gandharvas</s>, the <s>Siddhas</s>, and the supreme seers,
and the leaping, jumping, and roaring vānaras,

children.text: tam acintyam asahyaṃ ca adbhutaṃ lomaharṣaṇam
children.translated_text: beheld that inconceivable, irresistible, wonderful, hair-raising sight:
all beings saw the binding of the bridge in the ocean.
Those many thousands of crores of very powerful vānaras,

children.text: badhnantaḥ sāgare setuṃ jagmuḥ pāraṃ mahodadheḥ ||
children.translated_text: while building the bridge in the ocean, went across to the far shore of the great sea.
Broad, well-made, splendid, with good footing and well-set,
the great bridge shone like a parting-line in the ocean.
Then on the far shore of the ocean, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, mace in hand,
stood with his ministers for the purpose of striking the enemies.
At the front of that army, glorious <s>Rāma</s> with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
the righteous-souled archer, went on, accompanied by <s>Sugrīva</s>.
Some of the monkeys went through the middle; others, moving along the sides,

children.text: salile prapatantyanye mārgam anye na lebhire
children.translated_text: some fell into the water, and others found no path.
Some, going through the air, flew like <s>Suparṇas</s>.
With its great roar,
the fearsome army of monkeys, as it crossed, drowned out the terrible, rising roar of the ocean.

children.text: vānarāṇāṃ hi sā tīrṇā vāhinī nalasetunā
children.translated_text: For that army of monkeys, having crossed by <s>Nala</s>'s bridge,
encamped by the king on the shore, where there were many roots, fruits, and waters.

children.text: tad adbhutaṃ rāghavakarma duṣkaraṃ samīkṣya devāḥ saha siddhacāraṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that marvelous and difficult deed of <s>Rāghava</s>, the gods together with the <s>siddhas</s> and <s>cāraṇas</s>

children.text: upetya rāmaṃ sahitā maharṣibhiḥ samabhyaṣiñcan suśubhair jalaiḥ pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: approached <s>Rāma</s> along with the great seers and, each in turn, sprinkled him with auspicious waters.

children.text: jayasva śatrūnnaradeva medinīṃ sasāgarāṃ pālaya śāśvatīḥ samāḥ
children.translated_text: "Conquer your enemies, O lord of men; rule the earth, girdled by the ocean, for endless years."

children.text: itīva rāmaṃ naradevasatkṛtaṃ śubhair vacobhir vividhair apūjayan ||
children.translated_text: Thus, with many auspicious words, they honored <s>Rāma</s>, who was honored as a lord of men.
When <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, had crossed the ocean with his army,
the glorious <s>Rāvaṇa</s> spoke to his two ministers, <s>Śuka</s> and <s>Sāraṇa</s>.

children.text: samagraṃ sāgaraṃ tīrṇaṃ dustaraṃ vānaraṃ balam
children.translated_text: "The whole monkey force has crossed the ocean, hard to cross.
The building of a bridge in the ocean by <s>Rāma</s> is something never seen before.

children.text: sāgare setubandhaṃ tu na śraddadhyāṃ kathaṃcana
children.translated_text: I could never in any way have believed in the building of a bridge in the sea;

children.text: avaśyaṃ cāpi saṃkhyeyaṃ tanmayā vānaraṃ balam ||
children.translated_text: and yet that monkey force must certainly be counted by me.
You two should enter the monkey army unnoticed,

children.text: parimāṇaṃ ca vīryaṃ ca ye ca mukhyāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and learn its size and strength, and who the chief leaping monkeys are;

children.text: mantriṇo ye ca rāmasya sugrīvasya ca saṃmatāḥ
children.translated_text: who are <s>Rāma</s>'s ministers and those approved by <s>Sugrīva</s>,

children.text: ye pūrvam abhivartante ye ca śūrāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: who go in front, and which leaping monkeys are heroes;

children.text: sa ca setur yathā baddhaḥ sāgare salilārṇave
children.translated_text: how that bridge was built in the watery sea,
and what the encampment of those great-souled monkeys is like.

children.text: rāmasya vyavasāyaṃ ca vīryaṃ praharaṇāni ca
children.translated_text: You ought to know truly <s>Rāma</s>'s purpose, his valor, and his weapons,

children.text: lakṣmaṇasya ca vīrasya tattvato jñātum arhatha ||
children.translated_text: and also those of the heroic <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
And who is the commander of those mighty monkeys?
Having learned this exactly, you should return quickly."
Thus instructed, the two <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>Śuka</s> and <s>Sāraṇa</s>,
brave and wearing the forms of monkeys, entered the monkey force.
Then, at that time, <s>Śuka</s> and <s>Sāraṇa</s> could not manage
to count that monkey army, inconceivable and hair-raising.

children.text: tat sthitaṃ parvatāgreṣu nirdareṣu guhāsu ca
children.translated_text: It was stationed on mountain peaks, in clefts, and in caves,
and on the shores of the ocean, in forests and groves.

children.text: taramāṇaṃ ca tīrṇaṃ ca tartukāmaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Everywhere some were crossing, some had crossed, and some wished to cross;
some were encamped and some were still encamping, making a terrible roar and possessing great strength.

children.text: tau dadarśa mahātejāḥ pracchannau ca vibhīṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The greatly radiant <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> saw those two as they were hidden,
and then, seizing <s>Śuka</s> and <s>Sāraṇa</s>, he reported to <s>Rāma</s>:
"These two spies, subduers of enemy cities, have come here from <s>Laṅkā</s>."

children.text: tau dṛṣṭvā vyathitau rāmaṃ nirāśau jīvite tadā
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Rāma</s>, they were distressed and at that moment despaired of life;
frightened and with their palms joined in reverence, they spoke these words:
"Gentle lord, we two have come here, both sent by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
to learn this entire force of yours, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>."
Hearing that statement of theirs, <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>,
who delighted in the welfare of all beings, spoke these words with a laugh:

children.text: yadi dṛṣṭaṃ balaṃ kṛtsnaṃ vayaṃ vā susamīkṣitāḥ
children.translated_text: "If you have seen the whole army, or if we have been well inspected,

children.text: yathoktaṃ vā kṛtaṃ kāryaṃ chandataḥ pratigamyatām ||
children.translated_text: or if the task has been carried out as ordered, then go back at your pleasure.
After entering the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>, you two should tell the younger brother of <s>Dhanada</s>,

children.text: vaktavyo rakṣasāṃ rājā yathoktaṃ vacanaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: the king of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, exactly these words of mine:

children.text: yad balaṃ ca samāśritya sītāṃ me hṛtavān asi
children.translated_text: 'That strength relying on which you carried off my <s>Sītā</s>,
show it as you wish, together with your army and your kinsmen.

children.text: śvaḥ kāle nagarīṃ laṅkāṃ saprākārāṃ satoraṇām
children.translated_text: Tomorrow, at the proper time, behold the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>, with its ramparts and gateways,

children.text: rākṣasaṃ ca balaṃ paśya śarair vidhvaṃsitaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: and the <s>rākṣasa</s> force shattered by my arrows.

children.text: ghoraṃ roṣam ahaṃ mokṣye balaṃ dhāraya rāvaṇa
children.translated_text: I shall release a terrible anger; muster your army, O <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Tomorrow I shall be like thunderbolt-bearing <s>Vāsava</s> hurling the thunderbolt among the <s>dānavas</s>.'"
Thus instructed, the two <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>Śuka</s> and <s>Sāraṇa</s>,
came to the city of <s>Laṅkā</s> and spoke to the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>.
"Seized by <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> and deserving death, O lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>,
after we had been seen, we were released by righteous <s>Rāma</s> of immeasurable splendor.
There, gathered in one place, were four bulls among men,
heroes like the guardians of the worlds, masters of weapons and firm in valor:
glorious <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,
and greatly radiant <s>Sugrīva</s>, equal in prowess to great <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: ete śaktāḥ purīṃ laṅkāṃ saprākārāṃ satoraṇām
children.translated_text: They are able to uproot the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>, with its ramparts and gateways,
and carry it away, while all the monkeys stand aside.

children.text: yādṛśaṃ tasya rāmasya rūpaṃ praharaṇāni ca
children.translated_text: Such are that <s>Rāma</s>'s form and weapons

children.text: vadhiṣyati purīṃ laṅkām ekastiṣṭhantu te trayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that he alone will destroy the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>, while those three stand aside.
That army, protected by <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and by <s>Sugrīva</s>,
became still harder to assail, even for all the gods and <s>asuras</s>.

children.text: prahṛṣṭarūpā dhvajinī vanaukasāṃ mahātmanāṃ saṃprati yoddhum icchatām
children.translated_text: The army of the forest-dwellers, great-souled and joyful in form, now wishes to fight.

children.text: alaṃ virodhena śamo vidhīyatāṃ pradīyatāṃ dāśarathāya maithilī ||
children.translated_text: Enough of hostility; let peace be made. Let <s>Maithilī</s> be given to the son of <s>Daśaratha</s>."
Hearing that salutary and forthright speech spoken by <s>Sāraṇa</s>,
King <s>Rāvaṇa</s> replied to <s>Sāraṇa</s>.
"Even if gods, <s>gandharvas</s>, and <s>dānavas</s> were to attack me,
I would not give back <s>Sītā</s>, even from fear of all the worlds.

children.text: tvaṃ tu saumya paritrasto haribhir nirjito bhṛśam
children.translated_text: But you, gentle one, are terrified and utterly defeated by the monkeys;
therefore today itself you think the return of <s>Sītā</s> is good.

children.text: ko hi nāma sapatno māṃ samare jetum arhati ||
children.translated_text: For what rival indeed is able to conquer me in battle?"
Having spoken this harsh speech, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>,
then climbed, in his splendor, a palace white as snow,
many palm-trees high; <s>Rāvaṇa</s> did so from a desire to see.
Together with those two spies, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, overcome by anger,

children.text: paśyamānaḥ samudraṃ ca parvatāṃśca vanāni ca
children.translated_text: looking at the ocean, the mountains, and the forests,
saw the region of the earth completely filled with monkeys.

children.text: tad apāram asaṃkhyeyaṃ vānarāṇāṃ mahad balam
children.translated_text: Seeing that great force of monkeys, boundless and innumerable,
King <s>Rāvaṇa</s> questioned <s>Sāraṇa</s>.

children.text: eṣāṃ vānaramukhyānāṃ ke śūrāḥ ke mahābalāḥ
children.translated_text: "Among these leading monkeys, who are the heroes, who are the mighty ones?
Who are advancing in front on every side with great energy?

children.text: keṣāṃ śṛṇoti sugrīvaḥ ke vā yūthapayūthapāḥ
children.translated_text: Whose counsel does <s>Sugrīva</s> hear, and who are commanders of commanders?

children.text: sāraṇācakṣva me sarvaṃ ke pradhānāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sāraṇa</s>, tell me everything: who are the foremost among the leaping monkeys?"
<s>Sāraṇa</s>, knowledgeable about the leaders, then explained to the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>,
as he kept asking, those foremost dwellers in the forest.
"This monkey who stands facing <s>Laṅkā</s> and roaring,
surrounded by a hundred thousand troop-commanders,
by whose great roar the whole of <s>Laṅkā</s>, with its ramparts and gateways,
trembles, together with its mountains, woods, and groves,
stands at the head of the army of great-souled <s>Sugrīva</s>,

children.text: balāgre tiṣṭhate vīro nīlo nāmaiṣa yūthapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: lord of all the branch-roaming beasts; this heroic troop-leader is named <s>Nīla</s>.

children.text: bāhū pragṛhya yaḥ padbhyāṃ mahīṃ gacchati vīryavān
children.translated_text: That powerful one who stretches out his arms and moves over the earth on his feet,

children.text: laṅkām abhimukhaḥ kopād abhīkṣṇaṃ ca vijṛmbhate ||
children.translated_text: facing <s>Laṅkā</s>, and in anger repeatedly yawns wide,
who resembles a mountain peak and is like the filaments of a lotus,
violently lashes his tail again and again in fury.
At the sound of his tail, the ten directions seem to resound.
This one, consecrated as crown prince by the monkey-king <s>Sugrīva</s>,
is named <s>Aṅgada</s>; he challenges you to battle.

children.text: ye tu viṣṭabhya gātrāṇi kṣveḍayanti nadanti ca
children.translated_text: Those foremost monkeys who brace their limbs, shout, and roar,
and who rise up and yawn wide in anger,
are unassailable, terrible, fierce, and fierce in valor.
Eight hundred-thousands and ten hundred crores
of heroes dwelling on <s>Candana</s> follow him.
He hopes to crush <s>Laṅkā</s> with his own army.
The monkey <s>Śveta</s>, shining like silver, with his force, is of fearsome prowess;
wise and heroic, he is renowned in the three worlds.

children.text: tūrṇaṃ sugrīvam āgamya punar gacchati vānaraḥ
children.translated_text: Swiftly coming to <s>Sugrīva</s>, that monkey goes back again,
dividing the monkey army and cheering the battle lines.

children.text: yaḥ purā gomatītīre ramyaṃ paryeti parvatam
children.translated_text: He who formerly ranged around the lovely mountain on the bank of the <s>Gomatī</s>,
a mountain named <s>Saṃkocana</s>, furnished with various trees,

children.text: tatra rājyaṃ praśāstyeṣa kumudo nāma yūthapaḥ
children.translated_text: there this troop-leader named <s>Kumuda</s> rules his kingdom,
he who draws after him a thousand hundred-thousands.
His followers have hair spread over many fathoms and attached to long tails;

children.text: tāmrāḥ pītāḥ sitāḥ śvetāḥ prakīrṇā ghorakarmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: coppery, yellow, pale, and white, they are scattered about and terrible in action.
Undaunted, irascible, and fierce, he longs for battle.
He too hopes to crush <s>Laṅkā</s> with his own army.
But this one who is lion-like, tawny, and long-maned,

children.text: nibhṛtaḥ prekṣate laṅkāṃ didhakṣann iva cakṣuṣā ||
children.translated_text: quietly gazes at <s>Laṅkā</s>, as if wishing to burn it with his eyes.

children.text: vindhyaṃ kṛṣṇagiriṃ sahyaṃ parvataṃ ca sudarśanam
children.translated_text: O king, he constantly dwells on <s>Vindhya</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇagiri</s>, <s>Sahya</s>,

children.text: rājan satatam adhyāste rambho nāmaiṣa yūthapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the mountain <s>Sudarśana</s>; this troop-leader is named <s>Rambha</s>.
A hundred hundred-thousands and thirty monkey troop-leaders
surround and follow him, intending to crush <s>Laṅkā</s> with their might.

children.text: yastu karṇau vivṛṇute jṛmbhate ca punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: But he who opens his ears wide and yawns again and again,

children.text: na ca saṃvijate mṛtyor na ca yūthād vidhāvati ||
children.translated_text: who does not tremble before death and does not run away from his troop,
the mighty, fearless one constantly dwells, O king,

children.text: rājan satatam adhyāste śarabho nāma yūthapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: on the lovely <s>Sālveya</s> mountain; he is the troop-leader named <s>Śarabha</s>.

children.text: etasya balinaḥ sarve vihārā nāma yūthapāḥ
children.translated_text: All the troop-commanders of this mighty one are named <s>Vihāras</s>;
O king, they are forty hundred-thousands in number.

children.text: yastu megha ivākāśaṃ mahān āvṛtya tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: But he who, huge, stands covering the sky like a cloud,
in the midst of the monkey heroes like <s>Vāsava</s> among the gods,

children.text: bherīṇām iva saṃnādo yasyaiṣa śrūyate mahān
children.translated_text: whose great sound is heard like the booming of kettledrums,
terrible among the lords of branch-roaming beasts who long for battle,
he dwells on the unsurpassed mountain <s>Pāriyātra</s>;

children.text: yuddhe duṣprasaho nityaṃ panaso nāma yūthapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: always hard to withstand in battle, he is the troop-leader named <s>Panasa</s>.
Fifty hundred-thousands attend upon him,
troop-commanders upon that best of troop-commanders, whose troops are arranged by divisions.

children.text: yastu bhīmāṃ pravalgantīṃ camūṃ tiṣṭhati śobhayan
children.translated_text: But he who stands adorning the fearsome, bounding army,

children.text: sthitāṃ tīre samudrasya dvitīya iva sāgaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: stationed on the ocean shore like a second ocean,
this one, like <s>Dardara</s>, is the troop-leader named <s>Vinata</s>;
he roams drinking from <s>Parṇāśā</s>, best of rivers.
Sixty hundred-thousands of leaping monkeys are his force.

children.text: tvām āhvayati yuddhāya krathano nāma yūthapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The troop-leader named <s>Krathana</s> challenges you to battle.
But the monkey who nourishes a body gleaming with the color of red ochre,

children.text: gavayo nāma tejasvī tvāṃ krodhād abhivartate ||
children.translated_text: the radiant one named <s>Gavaya</s>, advances against you in anger.
Seventy hundred-thousands attend upon him.
He hopes to crush <s>Laṅkā</s> with his own army.
These unassailable, terrible, mighty ones, able to assume forms at will,

children.text: yūthapā yūthapaśreṣṭhā yeṣāṃ saṃkhyā na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: are troop-commanders, the best of troop-commanders, whose number cannot be known.
I shall describe those troop-commanders to you as you look on.

children.text: rāghavārthe parākrāntā ye na rakṣanti jīvitam ||
children.translated_text: who have exerted themselves for <s>Rāghava</s>'s sake and do not guard their lives.

children.text: snigdhā yasya bahuśyāmā vālā lāṅgūlam āśritāḥ
children.translated_text: The many glossy, very dark hairs of his tail are attached to it;

children.text: tāmrāḥ pītāḥ sitāḥ śvetāḥ prakīrṇā ghorakarmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: copper-colored, yellow, pale, and white, scattered over that terrible doer of deeds,
when raised up, they shine like the rays of the sun,
and they are dragged along the earth. This troop-leader is named <s>Hara</s>.
Those who follow behind him in hundreds and in thousands,
raising trees, are united and intent on climbing <s>Laṅkā</s>.
This one, with a thousand crores of mighty <s>vānaras</s>,
desires to defeat you in battle, O conqueror of hostile cities.
Those whom you see standing like great dark-blue clouds,
resembling black collyrium, whose valor in battle is true,
heroes whose weapons are claws and fangs, sharp-tempered and fearsome,
innumerable and indescribable, like the farthest shore of the ocean,

children.text: parvateṣu ca ye kecid viṣameṣu nadīṣu ca
children.translated_text: and all those who dwell on mountains, in difficult places, and by rivers:

children.text: ete tvām abhivartante rājann ṛkṣāḥ sudāruṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: these most dreadful <s>ṛkṣas</s>, O king, are advancing upon you.

children.text: eṣāṃ madhye sthito rājan bhīmākṣo bhīmadarśanaḥ
children.translated_text: Standing in their midst, O king, with terrible eyes and a terrible appearance,
surrounded on every side like <s>Parjanya</s> by rain-clouds,
dwelling on <s>Ṛkṣavant</s>, best of mountains, and drinking from the <s>Narmadā</s>,
is the lord of all the <s>ṛkṣas</s>; this troop-leader is named <s>Dhūmra</s>.

children.text: yavīyān asya tu bhrātā paśyainaṃ parvatopamam
children.translated_text: But look at this younger brother of his, resembling a mountain,
equal to his brother in form, yet superior in valor.
He is the one named <s>Jāmbavān</s>, a troop-leader of great troop-leaders,
calm and obedient to his elders, yet intolerant of insult in battles.

children.text: etena sāhyaṃ sumahat kṛtaṃ śakrasya dhīmatā
children.translated_text: By this wise <s>Jāmbavān</s> very great aid was given to <s>Śakra</s>,
and in the war of the gods and <s>asuras</s> many boons were obtained by him.
Climbing onto the peaks of mountains, they release boulders

children.text: muñcanti vipulākārā na mṛtyor udvijanti ca ||
children.translated_text: broad as great clouds and vast in size, and they do not tremble before death.

children.text: rākṣasānāṃ ca sadṛśāḥ piśācānāṃ ca romaśāḥ
children.translated_text: Like <s>rākṣasas</s> and like <s>piśācas</s>, shaggy,
many in his army roam about with the splendor of fire.

children.text: yaṃ tvenam abhisaṃrabdhaṃ plavamānam iva sthitam
children.translated_text: All the <s>vānaras</s> look upon this one, enraged,
standing as if about to leap, a troop-leader of troop-leaders.
This lord of <s>haris</s>, O king, attends upon the thousand-eyed god;
endowed with strength by his strength, this troop-leader is named <s>Rambha</s>.

children.text: yaḥ sthitaṃ yojane śailaṃ gacchan pārśvena sevate
children.translated_text: As he goes beside a mountain standing a <s>yojana</s> high, he brushes it with his flank;

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ tathaiva kāyena gataḥ prāpnoti yojanam ||
children.translated_text: and when he stretches upward with his body, he likewise reaches a <s>yojana</s>.
He than whom no greater form is found among quadrupeds
is known as <s>Saṃnādana</s>, the grandsire of the <s>vānaras</s>.

children.text: yena yuddhaṃ tadā dattaṃ raṇe śakrasya dhīmatā
children.translated_text: By that wise one battle was once offered to <s>Śakra</s> in combat,
and defeat was not suffered; this is that troop-leader of troop-leaders,
whose prowess, when he strides forth, is like the prowess of <s>Śakra</s>.
This one was born from a <s>gandharva</s> maiden by <s>Kṛṣṇavartman</s>,
long ago in the war of gods and <s>asuras</s>, to aid the dwellers in heaven.
Where king <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> resorts to the <s>jambū</s> tree,
which is king of the best mountains, served by many <s>kiṃnaras</s>,
and always gives pleasure in recreation to your brother, O lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>,
there dwells this illustrious and powerful bull among <s>vānaras</s>,
a troop-leader named <s>Krathana</s>, who never boasts in battles.
Surrounded by a thousand crores of <s>haris</s>, standing ready,
he too hopes to crush <s>Laṅkā</s> with his own army.

children.text: yo gaṅgām anu paryeti trāsayan hastiyūthapān
children.translated_text: He who ranges along the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, terrifying the leaders of elephant herds,
remembering the old hostility between elephants and <s>vānaras</s>,
this troop-lord and leader, whose dwelling is in mountain caves as he goes,
is chief of the army of <s>haris</s> along the Himalayan river.
Taking refuge at <s>Uśīrabīja</s>, a mountain like <s>Mandara</s>,

children.text: ramate vānaraśreṣṭho divi śakra iva svayam ||
children.translated_text: that best of <s>vānaras</s> delights there like <s>Śakra</s> himself in heaven.
A thousand hundreds of thousands are advancing with him;

children.text: eṣa durmarṣaṇo rājan pramāthī nāma yūthapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this hard-to-endure one, O king, is the troop-leader named <s>Pramāthī</s>.
That one whom you see like a cloud tossed up by the wind,
turning about again and again where this thick dust rises:
these dreadful black-faced, long-tailed ones of great strength,
a hundred hundred-thousands, having seen the bridge being built,
surround the very swift long-tailed troop-leader named <s>Gavākṣa</s>
and advance to crush <s>Laṅkā</s> with their might.
Where there are trees yielding every desired fruit, frequented by bees,
and where they move around a mountain whose color is like the sun,

children.text: yasya bhāsā sadā bhānti tadvarṇā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: by whose radiance the animals and birds of that same color always shine,

children.text: yasya prasthaṃ mahātmāno na tyajanti maharṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and whose plateau great seers of lofty spirit never abandon:
there this one delights, O king, on the lovely golden mountain,
chief of the foremost <s>vānaras</s>, the troop-leader named <s>Kesarī</s>.
There are sixty thousand lovely golden mountains;
among them is the best of mountains, as you, sinless one, are among the <s>rākṣasas</s>.
There these tawny, white, copper-faced, honey-brown ones
live on that highest mountain, their sharp fangs and claws serving as weapons.

children.text: siṃhā iva caturdaṃṣṭrā vyāghrā iva durāsadāḥ
children.translated_text: Like lions with four fangs, like tigers difficult to assail,
all are equal to fire, like blazing venomous serpents.
Their tails are very long and curved, and they resemble rutting elephants;
they are like great mountains and have the roar of great rain-clouds.

children.text: eṣa caiṣām adhipatir madhye tiṣṭhati vīryavān
children.translated_text: And this powerful one stands in the midst of them as their lord.

children.text: nāmnā pṛthivyāṃ vikhyāto rājañ śatabalīti yaḥ
children.translated_text: Known by name on earth, O king, is the one called <s>Śatabali</s>;
this very one hopes to crush <s>Laṅkā</s> with his own army.

children.text: gajo gavākṣo gavayo nalo nīlaśca vānaraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Gaja</s>, <s>Gavākṣa</s>, <s>Gavaya</s>, <s>Nala</s>, and the vānara <s>Nīla</s>:

children.text: ekaika eva yūthānāṃ koṭibhir daśabhir vṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: each one of them is surrounded by ten crores of troops.
Likewise there are other foremost vānaras dwelling on Mount <s>Vindhya</s>;

children.text: na śakyante bahutvāt tu saṃkhyātuṃ laghuvikramāḥ ||
children.translated_text: because of their multitude they cannot be counted, swift though they are in valor.
All of them, great king, are of immense power; all have bodies like great mountains.

children.text: sarve samarthāḥ pṛthivīṃ kṣaṇena kartuṃ pravidhvastavikīrṇaśailām ||
children.translated_text: All are capable, in a moment, of making the earth a place where the mountains are shattered and scattered.
After hearing the words of <s>Sāraṇa</s> to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: balam ālokayan sarvaṃ śuko vākyam athābravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śuka</s>, surveying the whole army, then spoke these words.

children.text: sthitān paśyasi yān etānmattān iva mahādvipān
children.translated_text: You see those standing there like rutting great elephants,

children.text: nyagrodhān iva gāṅgeyān sālān haimavatān iva ||
children.translated_text: like banyans along the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, like śāla trees of the <s>Himavat</s>.
These, O king, are hard to withstand, strong, and able to assume forms at will;
they resemble <s>daityas</s> and <s>dānavas</s>, and in battle they have the valor of gods.

children.text: eṣāṃ koṭisahasrāṇi nava pañca ca sapta ca
children.translated_text: Of these there are nine, five, and seven thousand crores,
and likewise thousands of śaṅkhas, and hundreds of vṛndas too.
These are ministers of <s>Sugrīva</s>, always dwelling in <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>;
they are monkeys, born from gods and <s>gandharvas</s>, able to assume forms at will.

children.text: yau tau paśyasi tiṣṭhantau kumārau devarūpiṇau
children.translated_text: Those two princes of divine appearance whom you see standing there,

children.text: maindaśca dvividaścobhau tābhyāṃ nāsti samo yudhi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mainda</s> and <s>Dvivida</s>, both of them: there is no one equal to them in battle.
Both were permitted by <s>Brahmā</s> and have drunk amṛta (nectar of immortality);

children.text: āśaṃsete yudhā laṅkām etau marditum ojasā ||
children.translated_text: these two hope to crush <s>Laṅkā</s> in battle by their energy.
Those two who stand beside them, resembling mountains,
are <s>Sumukha</s> and <s>Vimukha</s>, sons of <s>Mṛtyu</s>, equal to their father.

children.text: yaṃ tu paśyasi tiṣṭhantaṃ prabhinnam iva kuñjaram
children.translated_text: But the one whom you see standing like an elephant with streaming temples,

children.text: yo balāt kṣobhayet kruddhaḥ samudram api vānaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: the vānara who, when angered, could by force agitate even the ocean:
this one was the visitor to <s>Laṅkā</s>, to <s>Vaidehī</s>, and to you, lord.

children.text: enaṃ paśya purā dṛṣṭaṃ vānaraṃ punar āgatam ||
children.translated_text: Look at this vānara, seen before, now come again.

children.text: jyeṣṭhaḥ kesariṇaḥ putro vātātmaja iti śrutaḥ
children.translated_text: He is the eldest son of <s>Kesarī</s>, known as the son of the Wind;

children.text: hanūmān iti vikhyāto laṅghito yena sāgaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: he is famed as <s>Hanūmān</s>, by whom the ocean was leapt across.
He can assume forms at will, is the best of monkeys, and is endowed with strength and beauty;
his course cannot be checked, like that of the lord who ever moves.

children.text: udyantaṃ bhāskaraṃ dṛṣṭvā bālaḥ kila pipāsitaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing the rising sun, when as a child he was eager and hungry,
and having traversed a distance of three thousand yojanas,

children.text: ādityam āhariṣyāmi na me kṣut pratiyāsyati
children.translated_text: "I shall seize the sun; my hunger will not come back,"
so this one, long ago, thought in his mind, proud of his strength.
Before he could reach the god most unassailable even by gods, seers, and <s>dānavas</s>,
he fell upon the mountain at the place of the sun's rising.

children.text: patitasya kaper asya hanur ekā śilātale
children.translated_text: When this monkey had fallen, one jaw of his struck the rocky surface

children.text: kiṃcid bhinnā dṛḍhahanor hanūmān eṣa tena vai ||
children.translated_text: and was slightly broken; because he has a firm jaw, he is indeed <s>Hanūmān</s> for that reason.
By true traditional knowledge this monkey is known to me.

children.text: nāsya śakyaṃ balaṃ rūpaṃ prabhāvo vānubhāṣitum
children.translated_text: It is not possible to describe his strength, form, or power.

children.text: eṣa āśaṃsate laṅkām eko marditum ojasā ||
children.translated_text: This one alone hopes to crush <s>Laṅkā</s> by his energy.
And this heroic one next to him, dark, with eyes like lotuses,
is a great chariot-warrior of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s>, whose manliness is famous in the world.

children.text: yasminna calate dharmo yo dharmaṃ nātivartate
children.translated_text: In him <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) does not waver, and he does not transgress <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: yo brāhmam astraṃ vedāṃśca veda vedavidāṃ varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He knows the brahma-weapon and the Vedas, best among those who know the Veda.

children.text: yo bhindyād gaganaṃ bāṇaiḥ parvatāṃścāpi dārayet
children.translated_text: He could split the sky with arrows and tear apart mountains as well;

children.text: yasya mṛtyor iva krodhaḥ śakrasyeva parākramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: his anger is like Death, and his prowess like that of <s>Śakra</s>.
His wife <s>Sītā</s> was carried off by you from <s>Janasthāna</s>;

children.text: sa eṣa rāmastvāṃ yoddhuṃ rājan samabhivartate ||
children.translated_text: this is that <s>Rāma</s>, O king, advancing to fight you.
And this one on his right side, with the brilliance of pure refined gold,
broad-chested, copper-eyed, and with dark curling hair,

children.text: eṣo 'sya lakṣmaṇo nāma bhrātā prāṇasamaḥ priyaḥ
children.translated_text: is his brother named <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, dear to him as life itself.
He is skilled in policy and in war, and versed in every śāstra (treatise).

children.text: amarṣī durjayo jetā vikrānto buddhimān balī
children.translated_text: Impatient of insult, hard to conquer, victorious, bold, wise, and strong,

children.text: rāmasya dakṣiṇo bāhur nityaṃ prāṇo bahiścaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: he is always <s>Rāma</s>'s right arm, his life moving outside his body.
For <s>Rāghava</s>'s sake this one does not guard his own life;
he himself hopes to slay all the <s>rākṣasas</s> in battle.

children.text: yastu savyam asau pakṣaṃ rāmasyāśritya tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: But the one standing there on <s>Rāma</s>'s left flank, relying on him,
surrounded by hosts of <s>rākṣasas</s>, is king <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>.
He has been consecrated in <s>Laṅkā</s> by the glorious king of kings;
enraged against you alone, he advances for battle.

children.text: yaṃ tu paśyasi tiṣṭhantaṃ madhye girim ivācalam
children.translated_text: But the one whom you see standing in the middle, unmoving like a mountain,
is the undefeated lord of all the chiefs of the tree-ranging monkeys.
By brilliance, fame, intelligence, knowledge, and noble birth,

children.text: yaḥ kapīn ati babhrāja himavān iva parvatān ||
children.translated_text: he outshines the monkeys as <s>Himavān</s> outshines mountains.
He rules <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, a cave dense with thick trees,
a fortress set amid mountain fastnesses, together with his chief troop-leaders.
This golden garland of his, with a hundred lotuses, shines forth;
dear to gods and humans, prosperity is established in it.

children.text: etāṃ ca mālāṃ tārāṃ ca kapirājyaṃ ca śāśvatam
children.translated_text: This garland, and <s>Tārā</s>, and the lasting kingship of the monkeys
were bestowed on <s>Sugrīva</s> by <s>Rāma</s> after he had killed <s>Vālin</s>.

children.text: evaṃ koṭisahasreṇa śaṅkūnāṃ ca śatena ca
children.translated_text: Thus, with a thousand crores and with a hundred śaṅkus,
<s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the vānaras, advances against you for the sake of battle.

children.text: imāṃ mahārāja samīkṣya vāhinīm upasthitāṃ prajvalitagrahopamām
children.translated_text: Having surveyed this army, great king, which has arrived and is like blazing planets...

children.text: tataḥ prayatnaḥ paramo vidhīyatāṃ yathā jayaḥ syānna paraiḥ parājayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the greatest effort should be made, so that victory may be won and there may be no defeat at the hands of enemies.
But when he had seen those monkey troop-leaders described by <s>Śuka</s>,

children.text: samīpasthaṃ ca rāmasya bhrātaraṃ svaṃ vibhīṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: and his own brother <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> standing near <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahāvīryaṃ bhujaṃ rāmasya dakṣiṇam
children.translated_text: and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, of great valor, the right arm of <s>Rāma</s>,
and <s>Sugrīva</s>, king of all the monkeys, of terrifying prowess,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> became somewhat troubled at heart and grew angry,
and, at the end of their account, he rebuked the two heroes, <s>Śuka</s> and <s>Sāraṇa</s>.
As the two, <s>Śuka</s> and <s>Sāraṇa</s>, bowed with downcast faces, he said
a harsh speech, enraged, in a voice choked with anger.

children.text: na tāvat sadṛśaṃ nāma sacivair upajīvibhiḥ
children.translated_text: It is surely not fitting for ministers who live in dependence
to say what is displeasing to a king, a lord of punishment and favor.
When hostile enemies are advancing for the sake of battle,

children.text: ubhābhyāṃ sadṛśaṃ nāma vaktum aprastave stavam ||
children.translated_text: how fitting indeed it is for you two to utter praise at an improper time!

children.text: ācāryā guravo vṛddhā vṛthā vāṃ paryupāsitāḥ
children.translated_text: Teachers, gurus, and elders have been attended by you two in vain,

children.text: sāraṃ yad rājaśāstrāṇām anujīvyaṃ na gṛhyate ||
children.translated_text: since the essence of the sciences of kingship, by which a dependent should live, has not been grasped.

children.text: gṛhīto vā na vijñāto bhāro jñānasya vohyate
children.translated_text: Or, if it was grasped, it was not understood; you carry the burden of knowledge.

children.text: īdṛśaiḥ sacivair yukto mūrkhair diṣṭyā dharāmyaham ||
children.translated_text: Joined with such foolish ministers as you, by good fortune I still survive.

children.text: kiṃ nu mṛtyor bhayaṃ nāsti māṃ vaktuṃ paruṣaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Have you no fear of death, that you speak harsh words to me,

children.text: yasya me śāsato jihvā prayacchati śubhāśubham ||
children.translated_text: when my tongue, as I command, grants good and evil?

children.text: apyeva dahanaṃ spṛṣṭvā vane tiṣṭhanti pādapāḥ
children.translated_text: Trees may remain standing in a forest even after touching fire,
but offenders touched by a king's wrath do not remain standing.
I would kill these two sinners, these praisers of the enemy's side,

children.text: yadi pūrvopakārair me na krodho mṛdutāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: if my anger did not become softened by their former services to me.
Be gone; go away from here, away from my presence.

children.text: na hi vāṃ hantum icchāmi smarann upakṛtāni vām
children.translated_text: I do not wish to kill you two, remembering the services you have done for me.
Yet, ungrateful and turned away from affection for me, you two are as good as killed.

children.text: evam uktau tu savrīḍau tāvubhau śukasāraṇau
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, both <s>Śuka</s> and <s>Sāraṇa</s> were ashamed,
and, acclaiming <s>Rāvaṇa</s> with a cry of victory, they went out.
Then the ten-necked one spoke to <s>Mahodara</s>, who was standing nearby:
Bring before me quickly spies who are skilled in policy.
Then the spies, hastening at the king's command, arrived,
and stood present with joined palms after honoring him with blessings of victory.

children.text: tān abravīt tato vākyaṃ rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, spoke this command to them,
to the spies, trustworthy, heroic, devoted, and free from fear:
Go from here and examine <s>Rāma</s>'s plan.
Learn who are admitted to his counsels and have gathered with him out of affection.

children.text: kathaṃ svapiti jāgarti kim anyacca kariṣyati
children.translated_text: How does he sleep? How does he keep watch? What else will he do?
Having learned everything carefully and completely, you must return without omission.
An enemy known through a spy by wise rulers of the earth
can be approached in battle and driven away with little effort.
The spies said, 'So be it,' and, delighted, circumambulated the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: kṛtvā pradakṣiṇaṃ jagmur yatra rāmaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and went to where <s>Rāma</s> was with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Going near Mount <s>Suvela</s>, they saw <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>
hidden, together with <s>Sugrīva</s> and <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>.

children.text: te tu dharmātmanā dṛṣṭā rākṣasendreṇa rākṣasāḥ
children.translated_text: But those <s>rākṣasas</s>, present there, were seen by the righteous lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>,
and were seized there by <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> by chance.
Harried by the monkeys, who were bold and swift in valor,
they reached <s>Laṅkā</s> again, panting and with their senses lost.

children.text: tato daśagrīvam upasthitāste cārā bahirnityacarā niśācarāḥ
children.translated_text: Then those spies, night-roamers who always ranged outside, came before <s>Daśagrīva</s>,

children.text: gireḥ suvelasya samīpavāsinaṃ nyavedayan bhīmabalaṃ mahābalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, mighty though they were, reported the fearsome army dwelling near Mount <s>Suvela</s>.
Then the spies reported that unshakable force to the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>,
and <s>Rāghava</s> encamped on Mount <s>Suvela</s>.

children.text: cārāṇāṃ rāvaṇaḥ śrutvā prāptaṃ rāmaṃ mahābalam
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāvaṇa</s> heard from the spies that mighty <s>Rāma</s> had arrived,
he became somewhat agitated and spoke these words to <s>Śārdūla</s>:
Your color is not as it should be, and you are downcast, O night-roamer.

children.text: nāsi kaccid amitrāṇāṃ kruddhānāṃ vaśam āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Surely you have not fallen under the power of the angry enemies?
Thus questioned by him, <s>Śārdūla</s>, bewildered with fear,
uttered a faint speech to that tiger among <s>rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: na te cārayituṃ śakyā rājan vānarapuṃgavāḥ
children.translated_text: Those foremost monkeys cannot be spied upon by you, O king;
they are bold and powerful, and they are protected by <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: nāpi saṃbhāṣituṃ śakyāḥ sampraśno 'tra na labhyate
children.translated_text: Nor can they be spoken to; no questioning is possible there.
Every path is guarded on all sides by monkeys like mountains.
As soon as I entered that army, before it could be reconnoitered, I was discovered.
I was seized forcibly by many and torn in many ways.
I was struck violently with knees, fists, teeth, and palms,
and was dragged around by mighty, intolerant monkeys.
After dragging me everywhere, they led me to <s>Rāma</s>'s assembly,
all my limbs smeared with blood, bewildered, and my senses shaken.
While I was being beaten by the monkeys and was begging with joined palms,
I was protected by <s>Rāghava</s>; by chance I am still alive.
This <s>Rāma</s>, having filled the great ocean with mountains and rocks,
stands armed, having taken his position at the gate of <s>Laṅkā</s>.
Having assumed the <s>garuḍavyūha</s> formation and being surrounded on all sides by monkeys,
the greatly radiant one has released me and is advancing directly against <s>Laṅkā</s>.

children.text: purā prākāram āyāti kṣipram ekataraṃ kuru
children.translated_text: Before he reaches the rampart, quickly do one of the two alternatives.

children.text: sītāṃ cāsmai prayacchāśu suyuddhaṃ vā pradīyatām ||
children.translated_text: And quickly give <s>Sītā</s> to him, or let a fair battle be offered.
Then, on hearing that, the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s> burned inwardly in his mind.

children.text: śārdūlasya mahad vākyam athovāca sa rāvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After the weighty speech of <s>Śārdūla</s>, that <s>Rāvaṇa</s> then said:
"Even if gods, <s>gandharvas</s>, and <s>dānavas</s> were to fight against me,
I would not give back <s>Sītā</s>, even out of fear of all the worlds.

children.text: evam uktvā mahātejā rāvaṇaḥ punar abravīt
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the greatly radiant <s>Rāvaṇa</s> spoke again:

children.text: cāritā bhavatā senā ke 'tra śūrāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "The army has been observed by you. Which monkeys here are heroes?
What are those hard-to-approach monkeys like, and what is their power?

children.text: kasya putrāśca pautrāśca tattvam ākhyāhi rākṣasa ||
children.translated_text: Whose sons and grandsons are they? Tell me the truth, O <s>rākṣasa</s>.
Then, having learned the strength and weakness of these men, I shall decide here.
A reckoning of forces must certainly be made by one who desires battle."
Then, thus addressed by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, <s>Śārdūla</s>, the best of spies,
began to speak these words in <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s presence:
"Then there is the son of <s>Ṛkṣarajas</s>, O king, very hard to conquer in battle,
and here is the son of <s>Gadgada</s>, famed as <s>Jāmbavān</s>.
There is also another son of <s>Gadgada</s>, a son of the preceptor of <s>Śatakratu</s>;

children.text: kadanaṃ yasya putreṇa kṛtam ekena rakṣasām ||
children.translated_text: by his son alone destruction was wrought among the <s>rākṣasas</s>.
And <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, righteous and heroic, is the son of <s>Dharma</s>.
Here too, O king, is the gentle monkey <s>Dadhimukha</s>, son of <s>Soma</s>.
Here are the monkeys <s>Sumukha</s>, <s>Durmukha</s>, and <s>Vegadarśin</s>.
Surely Death himself was created by <s>Svayambhū</s> in monkey form.
Then there is <s>Nīla</s>, son of the fire-bearer, himself the commander of the army,

children.text: anilasya ca putro 'tra hanūmān iti viśrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and here is the son of the Wind, famed as <s>Hanūmān</s>.

children.text: naptā śakrasya durdharṣo balavān aṅgado yuvā
children.translated_text: The young <s>Aṅgada</s>, powerful and hard to assail, is <s>Śakra</s>'s grandson,
and <s>Mainda</s> and <s>Dvivida</s>, both mighty, are born from the <s>Aśvins</s>.
Here are five sons of <s>Vaivasvata</s>, resembling destroyers at the end of time:
<s>Gaja</s>, <s>Gavākṣa</s>, <s>Gavaya</s>, <s>Śarabha</s>, and <s>Gandhamādana</s>.
Here too are <s>Śveta</s> and <s>Jyotirmukha</s>, born from <s>Bhāskara</s> himself,
and then <s>Hemakūṭa</s>, the monkey son of <s>Varuṇa</s>.
<s>Nala</s>, heroic son of <s>Viśvakarman</s>, is the best of leaping monkeys.
Here too is a valiant, swift, and very hard-to-withstand son of the <s>Vasus</s>.
As for the ten crores of monkeys, brave and eager for battle,
the remaining glorious sons of gods, I do not dare to describe them.
This is the young son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, with the build of a lion;
by him <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> was killed, and so were <s>Khara</s> and <s>Triśiras</s>.

children.text: nāsti rāmasya sadṛśo vikrame bhuvi kaścana
children.translated_text: There is no one on earth equal to <s>Rāma</s> in valor.
By him <s>Virādha</s> was killed, and <s>Kabandha</s>, who was like Death.

children.text: vaktuṃ na śakto rāmasya naraḥ kaścid guṇān kṣitau
children.translated_text: No man on earth is able to speak fully of <s>Rāma</s>'s virtues.
By him so many <s>rākṣasas</s> who had gone to <s>Janasthāna</s> were killed.
And here is righteous <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, like a bull among elephants.

children.text: yasya bāṇapathaṃ prāpya na jīved api vāsavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having reached the path of his arrows, even <s>Vāsava</s> would not live.
And your brother <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, foremost among <s>rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: parigṛhya purīṃ laṅkāṃ rāghavasya hite rataḥ ||
children.translated_text: has accepted the city of <s>Laṅkā</s> and is devoted to <s>Rāghava</s>'s welfare.

children.text: iti sarvaṃ samākhyātaṃ tavedaṃ vānaraṃ balam
children.translated_text: Thus this entire monkey force of yours has been fully described.
It is stationed on <s>Suvela</s> mountain; in the remaining task, you are the authority."
Then the king's spies in <s>Laṅkā</s> reported to him about that unshakable force,
and about <s>Rāghava</s>, stationed on <s>Suvela</s> mountain.

children.text: cārāṇāṃ rāvaṇaḥ śrutvā prāptaṃ rāmaṃ mahābalam
children.translated_text: Hearing from the spies that mighty <s>Rāma</s> had arrived,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> became somewhat anxious and said this to his ministers:

children.text: mantriṇaḥ śīghram āyāntu sarve vai susamāhitāḥ
children.translated_text: "Let all the ministers come quickly, fully composed.

children.text: ayaṃ no mantrakālo hi samprāpta iva rākṣasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the time for our counsel has now arrived, O <s>rākṣasas</s>."
Hearing that command of his, the ministers came swiftly.
Then he took counsel together with his <s>rākṣasa</s> ministers.

children.text: mantrayitvā sa durdharṣaḥ kṣamaṃ yat samanantaram
children.translated_text: Having deliberated, that hard-to-assail one dismissed his ministers immediately afterward,
when what was suitable had been settled, and entered his own residence.
Then, summoning the mighty <s>rākṣasa</s> <s>Vidyujjihva</s>,
the great deceiver went to the place where <s>Maithilī</s> was.
The lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s> said to <s>Vidyujjihva</s>, skilled in illusion:
"We shall bewilder <s>Sītā</s>, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, by illusion.
Taking a head of <s>Rāghava</s> made by magic, O night-roamer,

children.text: māṃ tvaṃ samupatiṣṭhasva mahacca saśaraṃ dhanuḥ ||
children.translated_text: come to attend me, and bring also a great bow together with arrows."
Thus addressed, the night-roamer <s>Vidyujjihva</s> said, "So be it."

children.text: tasya tuṣṭo 'bhavad rājā pradadau ca vibhūṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: The king was pleased with him and gave him an ornament.
Then the mighty one entered the <s>Aśoka</s> grove.
There the younger brother of <s>Dhanada</s> saw her, wretched though undeserving of misery,
seated on the ground with her face cast down and given over to grief.
She had gone to the <s>Aśoka</s> grove, meditating only on her husband,
and was being watched from nearby by dreadful <s>rākṣasīs</s>.

children.text: upasṛtya tataḥ sītāṃ praharṣan nāma kīrtayan
children.translated_text: Then, approaching <s>Sītā</s>, feigning delight and calling her by name,

children.text: idaṃ ca vacanaṃ dhṛṣṭam uvāca janakātmajām ||
children.translated_text: he spoke these bold words to the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>:

children.text: sāntvyamānā mayā bhadre yam upāśritya valgase
children.translated_text: "Good lady, while I have been conciliating you, the one relying on whom you exult,

children.text: kharahantā sa te bhartā rāghavaḥ samare hataḥ ||
children.translated_text: that husband of yours, <s>Rāghava</s>, the slayer of <s>Khara</s>, has been killed in battle.

children.text: chinnaṃ te sarvato mūlaṃ darpaste nihato mayā
children.translated_text: Your root has been cut off on every side; your pride has been destroyed by me.
Through your own misfortune, O <s>Sītā</s>, you will become my wife.
O woman of little merit, whose purpose is lost, foolish though thinking yourself wise,

children.text: śṛṇu bhartṛvadhaṃ sīte ghoraṃ vṛtravadhaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: listen, O <s>Sītā</s>, to the dreadful killing of your husband, like the slaying of <s>Vṛtra</s>.

children.text: samāyātaḥ samudrāntaṃ māṃ hantuṃ kila rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s>, it seems, had come to the edge of the ocean to kill me.
surrounded by a great army led by the lord of the <s>vānaras</s>,
he encamped after reaching the southern shore of the ocean.
<s>Rāma</s>, with his great army, was advancing when the sun had set.
Then, at midnight, when the army was halted on the road, weary from the journey,
and sleeping comfortably, after it had first been tracked by spies,
that army of his, where <s>Rāma</s> was together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: balam asya hataṃ rātrau yatra rāmaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: was struck down at night by my great force led by <s>Prahasta</s>.
Broad-bladed weapons, iron clubs, swords, discuses, and massive iron staffs,
networks of arrows, spears, and shining heavy hammers,
staves, javelins, lances, wheels, and pestles too,
were raised again and again by the <s>rākṣasas</s> and hurled down upon the <s>vānaras</s>.
Then, while <s>Rāma</s> was asleep, by the crushing <s>Prahasta</s>,
skilled of hand, his head was cut off without hindrance by a great sword.
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, springing up, was seized by chance,

children.text: diśaḥ pravrājitaḥ sarvair lakṣmaṇaḥ plavagaiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, together with all the leaping monkeys, was driven off to the quarters.
<s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the leaping monkeys, lies with his neck broken;
<s>Hanūmān</s>, his jaw smashed, lies slain by the <s>rākṣasas</s>.
Then <s>Jāmbavān</s>, rising up on his knees, was killed in battle,
cut apart by many broad blades, chopped down like a tree.
Both <s>Mainda</s> and <s>Dvivida</s>, those bulls among <s>vānaras</s>, were slain,
sighing and weeping, drenched with blood.
<s>Panasa</s>, destroyer of enemies, struck by a sword and cut through the middle,
groans on the earth like a panasa tree.
<s>Darīmukha</s>, pierced by many iron arrows, lies in a ravine;
and mighty-radiant <s>Kumuda</s>, groaning, was slain by arrows.
<s>Aṅgada</s>, cut by many arrows when the <s>rākṣasas</s> reached him,
was cast down, vomiting blood; <s>Aṅgada</s> fell upon the ground.
Some monkeys were crushed by elephants, and others by masses of chariots;
there they were laid low and trampled, like clouds by storm winds.
Still others fled in terror and were being struck from behind;
the <s>rākṣasas</s> charged them like lions charging great elephants.

children.text: sāgare patitāḥ kecit kecid gaganam āśritāḥ
children.translated_text: Some fell into the ocean, and some took to the sky;
bears climbed trees, mingled together with the <s>vānaras</s>.

children.text: sāgarasya ca tīreṣu śaileṣu ca vaneṣu ca
children.translated_text: On the shores of the ocean, on the mountains, and in the forests,
many of those tawny-eyed ones were slain by many hideous-eyed foes.

children.text: evaṃ tava hato bhartā sasainyo mama senayā
children.translated_text: Thus your husband has been killed, together with his army, by my army;
and this blood-wet, dust-covered head of his has been brought here.
Then the exceedingly unassailable <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>,
while <s>Sītā</s> was listening, said this to a <s>rākṣasī</s>:
Bring the cruel-acting <s>rākṣasa</s> <s>Vidyujjihva</s>,

children.text: yena tad rāghavaśiraḥ saṃgrāmāt svayam āhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: by whom that head of <s>Rāghava</s> was himself brought from the battle.
Then <s>Vidyujjihva</s>, taking that head together with the bow,
made obeisance with his head and stood before <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: tam abravīt tato rājā rāvaṇo rākṣasaṃ sthitam
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Rāvaṇa</s> spoke to that <s>rākṣasa</s> standing there,
to <s>Vidyujjihva</s>, great-tongued and moving close at hand:

children.text: agrataḥ kuru sītāyāḥ śīghraṃ dāśaratheḥ śiraḥ
children.translated_text: Place the head of <s>Dāśarathi</s> quickly before <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: avasthāṃ paścimāṃ bhartuḥ kṛpaṇā sādhu paśyatu ||
children.translated_text: so that the wretched woman may properly see her husband's final state.

children.text: evam uktaṃ tu tad rakṣaḥ śirastat priyadarśanam
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, that <s>rākṣasa</s> quickly set down
that handsome head near <s>Sītā</s> and disappeared.
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> too tossed down the great shining bow,

children.text: triṣu lokeṣu vikhyātaṃ sītām idam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: famed in the three worlds, and said this to <s>Sītā</s>:

children.text: idaṃ tat tava rāmasya kārmukaṃ jyāsamanvitam
children.translated_text: This is that bow of your <s>Rāma</s>, furnished with its bowstring;

children.text: iha prahastenānītaṃ hatvā taṃ niśi mānuṣam ||
children.translated_text: it was brought here by <s>Prahasta</s>, after he slew that mortal in the night.

children.text: sa vidyujjihvena sahaiva tacchiro dhanuśca bhūmau vinikīrya rāvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Having scattered that head and bow on the ground, together with <s>Vidyujjihva</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>

children.text: videharājasya sutāṃ yaśasvinīṃ tato 'bravīt tāṃ bhava me vaśānugā ||
children.translated_text: then said to the glorious daughter of the king of <s>Videha</s>, Become subject to my will.

children.text: sā sītā tacchiro dṛṣṭvā tacca kārmukam uttamam
children.translated_text: When <s>Sītā</s> saw that head and that excellent bow,
and the connection with <s>Sugrīva</s> that had been described by <s>Hanūmān</s>,

children.text: nayane mukhavarṇaṃ ca bhartustat sadṛśaṃ mukham
children.translated_text: the eyes, the complexion of the face, and that face resembling her husband's,

children.text: keśān keśāntadeśaṃ ca taṃ ca cūḍāmaṇiṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: the hair, the edge of the hairline, and that auspicious crest-jewel,
recognizing him by all these tokens, she became deeply afflicted
and then reviled <s>Kaikeyī</s>, crying out like a female osprey.
Be satisfied, <s>Kaikeyī</s>; this joy of his house has been killed.
The entire family has been destroyed by you, quarrelsome woman.

children.text: āryeṇa kiṃ nu kaikeyyāḥ kṛtaṃ rāmeṇa vipriyam
children.translated_text: What offense, pray, did noble <s>Rāma</s> do to <s>Kaikeyī</s>,
that by her he was sent from home to the forest, clothed in bark?

children.text: evam uktvā tu vaidehī vepamānā tapasvinī
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, trembling, the ascetic <s>Vaidehī</s>,

children.text: jagāma jagatīṃ bālā chinnā tu kadalī yathā ||
children.translated_text: young and helpless, went down to the ground like a cut plantain tree.

children.text: sā muhūrtāt samāśvasya pratilabhya ca cetanām
children.translated_text: After a moment she recovered her breath and regained consciousness;
then, smelling that head, the wide-eyed woman lamented.
Alas, I am slain, O mighty-armed one, I who followed your heroic vow.

children.text: imāṃ te paścimāvasthāṃ gatāsmi vidhavā kṛtā ||
children.translated_text: I have come to this final state of yours, made a widow.

children.text: prathamaṃ maraṇaṃ nāryā bhartur vaiguṇyam ucyate
children.translated_text: A husband's calamity is said to be a woman's first death;
you, noble in conduct, have met it before me, though I was faithful in conduct.
For me, who had fallen from sorrow into sorrow and sunk in the ocean of grief,

children.text: yo hi mām udyatastrātuṃ so 'pi tvaṃ vinipātitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: you, who were preparing to rescue me, have yourself been cast down.
