children.text: sā śvaśrūr mama kausalyā tvayā putreṇa rāghava
children.translated_text: That mother-in-law of mine, Kausalyā>, with you as her son, O Rāghava...

children.text: vatseneva yathā dhenur vivatsā vatsalā kṛtā ||
children.translated_text: like a cow bereft of her calf but made tender again by a calf.
Those by whom a long life was ordained for you, O one of inconceivable valor,

children.text: anṛtaṃ vacanaṃ teṣām alpāyur asi rāghava ||
children.translated_text: their words were false; you are short-lived, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: atha vā naśyati prajñā prājñasyāpi satastava
children.translated_text: Or else even your wisdom, though you are wise, is being destroyed;

children.text: pacatyenaṃ tathā kālo bhūtānāṃ prabhavo hyayam ||
children.translated_text: for time cooks this being in just this way, since it is the origin and lord of creatures.

children.text: adṛṣṭaṃ mṛtyum āpannaḥ kasmāt tvaṃ nayaśāstravit
children.translated_text: Having met death unseen, why, though you know the science of policy,
and though you know the remedies for misfortunes and are skilled at avoiding them, did you fall thus?
Thus, after embracing you, I have been torn away by cruel, exceedingly pitiless
night-of-death, and you, lotus-eyed one, have been taken from me.
You lie here, mighty-armed one, leaving me, the wretched ascetic woman, behind,

children.text: priyām iva śubhāṃ nārīṃ pṛthivīṃ puruṣarṣabha ||
children.translated_text: as if leaving the auspicious earth, your beloved woman, O bull among men.

children.text: arcitaṃ satataṃ yatnād gandhamālyair mayā tava
children.translated_text: This bow of yours, hero, dear to me, adorned with gold,

children.text: idaṃ te matpriyaṃ vīra dhanuḥ kāñcanabhūṣitam ||
children.translated_text: was always worshiped by me with effort, with perfumes and garlands.
Surely, sinless one, you have now met in heaven with your father <s>Daśaratha</s>, my father-in-law,

children.text: pūrvaiśca pitṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ nūnaṃ svarge samāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: together with your former ancestors.

children.text: divi nakṣatrabhūtastvaṃ mahat karma kṛtaṃ priyam
children.translated_text: Having become a star in the sky, and having done a great and beloved deed,
you now look upon your own pure lineage of royal seers.

children.text: kiṃ māṃ na prekṣase rājan kiṃ māṃ na pratibhāṣase
children.translated_text: Why do you not look at me, king? Why do you not speak back to me,

children.text: bālāṃ bālena samprāptāṃ bhāryāṃ māṃ sahacāriṇīm ||
children.translated_text: me, your young wife and companion, obtained by you while you too were young?

children.text: saṃśrutaṃ gṛhṇatā pāṇiṃ cariṣyāmīti yat tvayā
children.translated_text: Remember what you promised when taking my hand, <s>Kākutstha</s>, saying, 'I shall walk with you,'

children.text: smara tanmama kākutstha naya mām api duḥkhitām ||
children.translated_text: and take me too, afflicted as I am.

children.text: kasmānmām apahāya tvaṃ gato gatimatāṃ vara
children.translated_text: Why have you abandoned me and gone, O best of those who attain the goal,

children.text: asmāl lokād amuṃ lokaṃ tyaktvā mām iha duḥkhitām ||
children.translated_text: from this world to that other world, leaving me here in sorrow?

children.text: kalyāṇair ucitaṃ yat tat pariṣvaktaṃ mayaiva tu
children.translated_text: That body of yours, which was fit for auspicious embraces and was embraced only by me,
is surely now being dragged about by flesh-eaters.
You performed sacrifices such as the <s>agniṣṭoma</s>, with proper gifts to the priests;

children.text: agnihotreṇa saṃskāraṃ kena tvaṃ tu na lapsyase ||
children.translated_text: but through what consecration by the sacred fire will you now not be attained?
Of the three who went forth to the forest, only one will have returned;
<s>Kausalyā</s>, craving through grief, will question <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> closely.

children.text: sa tasyāḥ paripṛcchantyā vadhaṃ mitrabalasya te
children.translated_text: And as she questions him, he will surely tell her of the killing of your ally's army,

children.text: tava cākhyāsyate nūnaṃ niśāyāṃ rākṣasair vadham ||
children.translated_text: and of your own killing by <s>rākṣasas</s> in the night.

children.text: sā tvāṃ suptaṃ hataṃ śrutvā māṃ ca rakṣogṛhaṃ gatām
children.translated_text: When she hears that you were killed while sleeping, and that I have gone to a <s>rākṣasa</s>'s house,
she will not live, O <s>Rāghava</s>, her heart split apart.

children.text: sādhu pātaya māṃ kṣipraṃ rāmasyopari rāvaṇa
children.translated_text: Good, quickly cast me down upon <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>;

children.text: samānaya patiṃ patnyā kuru kalyāṇam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: bring the husband together with his wife, and perform the highest good deed.

children.text: śirasā me śiraścāsya kāyaṃ kāyena yojaya
children.translated_text: Join my head with his head, and my body with his body.
I shall follow, O <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the path of my great-souled husband;
I do not wish to live even for a moment with a sinful life.

children.text: śrutaṃ mayā vedavidāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ pitur gṛhe
children.translated_text: I heard in my father's house from brāhmaṇas who know the Veda

children.text: yāsāṃ strīṇāṃ priyo bhartā tāsāṃ lokā mahodayāḥ ||
children.translated_text: that for those women whose husband is dear, their worlds are greatly exalted.

children.text: kṣamā yasmin damastyāgaḥ satyaṃ dharmaḥ kṛtajñatā
children.translated_text: In whom there was patience, self-restraint, generosity, truth, <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), gratitude,

children.text: ahiṃsā caiva bhūtānāṃ tam ṛte kā gatir mama ||
children.translated_text: and non-injury toward living beings: apart from him, what path is there for me?
Thus she, the wide-eyed daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, scorched by sorrow, lamented there,
gazing at her husband's head and bow.
While <s>Sītā</s> was lamenting in this way there, a <s>rākṣasa</s>,
standing in the army, approached his lord with folded hands.
After saluting him and placating him with the words, 'Be victorious, noble prince,'
he reported that <s>Prahasta</s>, the commander of the army, had arrived.
'<s>Prahasta</s> has come, accompanied by all the ministers;

children.text: kiṃcid ātyayikaṃ kāryaṃ teṣāṃ tvaṃ darśanaṃ kuru ||
children.translated_text: they have some urgent business. Grant them an audience.'
Hearing this report from the <s>rākṣasa</s>, <s>Daśagrīva</s>
left the <s>Aśoka</s> grove and went to see his ministers.

children.text: sa tu sarvaṃ samarthyaiva mantribhiḥ kṛtyam ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, having fully considered with his ministers everything that concerned his own business,
he entered the assembly and made his arrangements, knowing <s>Rāma</s>'s valor.

children.text: antardhānaṃ tu tacchīrṣaṃ tacca kārmukam uttamam
children.translated_text: But that head and that excellent bow vanished
immediately after <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s departure.
Then the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, together with those ministers of terrible valor,
deliberated on the decision to be made in the matter of <s>Rāma</s>.
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, like Time itself, spoke to all the commanders nearby,
strong and well-disposed as they were:
'Quickly, by the sound of the war drum struck loudly at its rim,

children.text: samānayadhvaṃ sainyāni vaktavyaṃ ca na kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: assemble my armies, and the reason is not to be announced.'

children.text: tatastatheti pratigṛhya tad vaco balādhipāste mahad ātmano balam
children.translated_text: Then the commanders accepted that order, saying, 'So be it,' and assembled his great army;

children.text: samānayaṃścaiva samāgataṃ ca te nyavedayan bhartari yuddhakāṅkṣiṇi ||
children.translated_text: when it had gathered, they reported it to their lord, who was eager for battle.

children.text: sītāṃ tu mohitāṃ dṛṣṭvā saramā nāma rākṣasī
children.translated_text: But seeing <s>Sītā</s> bewildered, a <s>rākṣasī</s> named <s>Saramā</s>,
her dear, affectionate friend, quickly approached <s>Vaidehī</s>.

children.text: sā hi tatra kṛtā mitraṃ sītayā rakṣyamāṇayā
children.translated_text: For there, while <s>Sītā</s> was being guarded, <s>Saramā</s> had made friendship with her,
protecting her from <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, beloved, compassionate, and firm in her vow.

children.text: sā dadarśa sakhīṃ sītāṃ saramā naṣṭacetanām
children.translated_text: That friend <s>Saramā</s> saw her friend <s>Sītā</s> bereft of consciousness,
turned aside, risen up, and ruined, like a mare in the dust.
Her virtuous friend consoled her with affection, saying,

children.text: uktā yad rāvaṇena tvaṃ pratyuktaṃ ca svayaṃ tvayā ||
children.translated_text: 'What <s>Rāvaṇa</s> said to you, and what you yourself replied,

children.text: sakhīsnehena tad bhīru mayā sarvaṃ pratiśrutam
children.translated_text: all that, timid one, I heard out of a friend's affection,

children.text: līnayā gahane śūnye bhayam utsṛjya rāvaṇāt
children.translated_text: while hidden in the empty thicket, having cast away fear of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: tava hetor viśālākṣi na hi me jīvitaṃ priyam ||
children.translated_text: for your sake, wide-eyed one; for my own life is not dear to me.'
For the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, on whose account he had gone out in agitation,

children.text: tacca me viditaṃ sarvam abhiniṣkramya maithili ||
children.translated_text: that whole matter is known to me, O <s>Maithilī</s>, since I went out.

children.text: na śakyaṃ sauptikaṃ kartuṃ rāmasya viditātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: It is not possible to carry out a sleeping attack against <s>Rāma</s>, whose self is known to him;
and the killing of that tiger among men is fitting only in his own presence.

children.text: na caiva vānarā hantuṃ śakyāḥ pādapayodhinaḥ
children.translated_text: Nor can the monkeys, who fight with trees, be killed,
for they are well protected by <s>Rāma</s>, like the gods by the bull among gods.
His arms are long and rounded; he is glorious, broad-chested, and powerful,
a bowman, compact in frame, righteous in soul, and renowned on earth.

children.text: vikrānto rakṣitā nityam ātmanaśca parasya ca
children.translated_text: Heroic, always the protector of himself and of others,
he is safe with his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, skilled in the science of policy.
The slayer of floods of hostile armies, with inconceivable strength and manly valor,

children.text: na hato rāghavaḥ śrīmān sīte śatrunibarhaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the glorious <s>Rāghava</s>, destroyer of enemies, has not been killed, O <s>Sītā</s>.
By one whose thought and action are improper, who is hostile to all beings,

children.text: iyaṃ prayuktā raudreṇa māyā māyāvidā tvayi ||
children.translated_text: this terrible illusion has been used against you by that master of illusion.

children.text: śokaste vigataḥ sarvaḥ kalyāṇaṃ tvām upasthitam
children.translated_text: Let all your grief be gone; good fortune has come upon you.

children.text: dhruvaṃ tvāṃ bhajate lakṣmīḥ priyaṃ prītikaraṃ śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: Surely prosperity attends you. Hear what is dear and pleasing.
<s>Rāma</s>, having crossed the ocean together with the monkey army,
has encamped on reaching the southern shore of the sea.
I have seen <s>Kākutstha</s>, his purpose fulfilled, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Protected by forces gathered at the edge of the ocean, he stands firm.

children.text: anena preṣitā ye ca rākṣasā laghuvikramāḥ
children.translated_text: And the swift-moving <s>rākṣasas</s> who were sent by him
have brought here the report that <s>Rāghava</s> has crossed over.

children.text: sa tāṃ śrutvā viśālākṣi pravṛttiṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that report, O wide-eyed one, the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: eṣa mantrayate sarvaiḥ sacivaiḥ saha rāvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, is now taking counsel with all his ministers.

children.text: iti bruvāṇā saramā rākṣasī sītayā saha
children.translated_text: As the <s>rākṣasī</s> <s>Saramā</s> was speaking thus with <s>Sītā</s>,
she heard the dreadful sound of the armies with all their preparations.
Hearing the great blast of a drum resounding like the fall of a staff,
sweet-speaking <s>Saramā</s> said this to <s>Sītā</s>:
This fearsome war-drum, O timid one, summons men to put on armor.
Listen to the deep sound of the kettledrum, like the roar of a rain-cloud.
Rut-maddened elephants are being made ready, and chariot horses are being yoked;

children.text: tatra tatra ca saṃnaddhāḥ saṃpatanti padātayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: here and there infantrymen, fully armed, are rushing together.
The royal roads are filling with armies of wondrous appearance,
swift and roaring, like the ocean with rushing floods of water.

children.text: śāstrāṇāṃ ca prasannānāṃ carmaṇāṃ varmaṇāṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Look at the radiance rising in many colors from bright weapons,
from shields and armor, from chariots, horses, and elephants, and from adorned <s>rākṣasas</s>,
as they send forth their splendor.
It is like the form of fire in the hot season as it burns a forest.

children.text: ghaṇṭānāṃ śṛṇu nirghoṣaṃ rathānāṃ śṛṇu nisvanam
children.translated_text: Listen to the clamor of bells; listen to the rumbling of chariots;
listen to the neighing of horses and to the sound of war-instruments.
This is the tumult of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, with weapons raised in their hands,
following the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, noisy and making the hair stand on end.

children.text: śrīstvāṃ bhajati śokaghnī rakṣasāṃ bhayam āgatam
children.translated_text: Fortune that destroys grief attends you; fear has come upon the <s>rākṣasas</s>
from <s>Rāma</s>, O lotus-petal-eyed one, as upon the daityas from <s>Vāsava</s>.
Your husband, having conquered that inconceivably mighty one and mastered his anger,
will kill <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle and regain you.
Your husband, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, will show his prowess among the <s>rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: yathā śatruṣu śatrughno viṣṇunā saha vāsavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as enemy-slaying <s>Vāsava</s> did among his foes together with <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: āgatasya hi rāmasya kṣipram aṅkagatāṃ satīm
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāma</s> has come, I shall soon see you, your aim accomplished,

children.text: ahaṃ drakṣyāmi siddhārthāṃ tvāṃ śatrau vinipātite ||
children.translated_text: as a virtuous woman held in his lap, when the enemy has been struck down.
You will shed tears born of joy, O lovely one,
when you meet him and are embraced upon the broad chest of that broad-chested man.

children.text: acirānmokṣyate sīte devi te jaghanaṃ gatām
children.translated_text: Soon, O divine <s>Sītā</s>, mighty <s>Rāma</s> will loosen this braid of yours,

children.text: dhṛtām etāṃ bahūnmāsān veṇīṃ rāmo mahābalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: which has reached your hips and has been worn for many months.

children.text: tasya dṛṣṭvā mukhaṃ devi pūrṇacandram ivoditam
children.translated_text: Seeing his face, O lady, risen like the full moon,

children.text: mokṣyase śokajaṃ vāri nirmokam iva pannagī ||
children.translated_text: you will cast off the water born of grief, like a female serpent her slough.

children.text: rāvaṇaṃ samare hatvā nacirād eva maithili
children.translated_text: After killing <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle, O <s>Maithilī</s>, before long

children.text: tvayā samagraṃ priyayā sukhārho lapsyate sukham ||
children.translated_text: he, worthy of happiness, will obtain complete happiness with you, his beloved.
Reunited with great-souled <s>Rāma</s>, you will rejoice,
as the earth rejoices when joined with crops after good rain.

children.text: girivaram abhito 'nuvartamāno haya iva maṇḍalam āśu yaḥ karoti
children.translated_text: The one who, moving around the great mountain, swiftly makes his circuit like a horse,

children.text: tam iha śaraṇam abhyupehi devi divasakaraṃ prabhavo hyayaṃ prajānām ||
children.translated_text: take refuge in that sun here, O lady; for he is the source of creatures.

children.text: atha tāṃ jātasaṃtāpāṃ tena vākyena mohitām
children.translated_text: Then <s>Saramā</s> refreshed her, who had become tormented
and bewildered by that speech, as the sky refreshes the earth with water.
Then, wishing to do what was beneficial for her friend, the friend spoke words
at the proper time, knowing the time, with a smile before she spoke.
I would be able, O dark-eyed one, to go, report your words
and your welfare to <s>Rāma</s>, and return unseen.

children.text: na hi me kramamāṇāyā nirālambe vihāyasi
children.translated_text: For while I move through the unsupported sky,

children.text: samartho gatim anvetuṃ pavano garuḍo 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: neither the wind nor even <s>Garuḍa</s> is able to follow my course.

children.text: evaṃ bruvāṇāṃ tāṃ sītā saramāṃ punar abravīt
children.translated_text: When she had spoken thus, <s>Sītā</s> again addressed <s>Saramā</s>
in a sweet, gentle voice, still afflicted by her former grief:

children.text: samarthā gaganaṃ gantum api vā tvaṃ rasātalam
children.translated_text: I know that you are able to go to the sky, or even to the underworld,
but I understand that what you have to do is not that; there is another task concerning me.

children.text: matpriyaṃ yadi kartavyaṃ yadi buddhiḥ sthirā tava
children.translated_text: If what is dear to me is to be done, and if your resolve is firm,

children.text: jñātum icchāmi taṃ gatvā kiṃ karotīti rāvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I wish to know: go to him and learn what <s>Rāvaṇa</s> is doing.

children.text: sa hi māyābalaḥ krūro rāvaṇaḥ śatrurāvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: For that cruel <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, powerful through illusion and a tormentor of enemies,
that wicked-souled one bewilders me, like <s>Vāruṇī</s> liquor as soon as it is drunk.
He has me threatened constantly and reviled again and again

children.text: rākṣasībhiḥ sughorābhir yā māṃ rakṣanti nityaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by very dreadful <s>rākṣasīs</s> who guard me at all times.

children.text: udvignā śaṅkitā cāsmi na ca svasthaṃ mano mama
children.translated_text: I am agitated and fearful, and my mind is not at ease;
agitated by fear of him, I have come to the <s>Aśoka</s> grove.

children.text: yadi nāma kathā tasya niścitaṃ vāpi yad bhavet
children.translated_text: If there is any talk of him, or whatever decision may have been made,

children.text: nivedayethāḥ sarvaṃ tat paro me syād anugrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: please report all of that; it would be the greatest favor to me.

children.text: sā tvevaṃ bruvatīṃ sītāṃ saramā valgubhāṣiṇī
children.translated_text: As <s>Sītā</s> was speaking in this way, sweet-spoken <s>Saramā</s>
spoke these words to her, touching her as she was overcome with tears:
"If this is your intention, then I will go, O <s>Jānakī</s>.

children.text: gṛhya śatror abhiprāyam upāvṛttāṃ ca paśya mām ||
children.translated_text: After grasping the enemy's intention, see me returned again."

children.text: evam uktvā tato gatvā samīpaṃ tasya rakṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, she then went near that <s>rākṣasa</s>
and heard what <s>Rāvaṇa</s> was saying together with his ministers.

children.text: sā śrutvā niścayaṃ tasya niścayajñā durātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard the decision of that evil-minded one, she who understood his decision
quickly came back again then to the <s>Aśoka</s> grove.
Entering there once more, she saw the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>

children.text: pratīkṣamāṇāṃ svām eva bhraṣṭapadmām iva śriyam ||
children.translated_text: waiting for her, like <s>Śrī</s> bereft of her lotus.

children.text: tāṃ tu sītā punaḥ prāptāṃ saramāṃ valgubhāṣiṇīm
children.translated_text: When <s>Sītā</s> saw sweet-spoken <s>Saramā</s> come back again,

children.text: pariṣvajya ca susnigdhaṃ dadau ca svayam āsanam ||
children.translated_text: she embraced her very affectionately and herself gave her a seat.

children.text: ihāsīnā sukhaṃ sarvam ākhyāhi mama tattvataḥ
children.translated_text: "Sit here comfortably and tell me everything exactly:
the decision of that cruel, evil-minded <s>Rāvaṇa</s>."

children.text: evam uktā tu saramā sītayā vepamānayā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by trembling <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Saramā</s>
told everything that <s>Rāvaṇa</s> had said together with his ministers.
"The lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s> was indeed admonished by his mother, with weighty words, for the sake of your release,
and also, O <s>Vaidehī</s>, by an unshaken elder minister.
'Let <s>Maithilī</s> be given respectfully to the lord of men.

children.text: nidarśanaṃ te paryāptaṃ janasthāne yad adbhutam ||
children.translated_text: The extraordinary event at <s>Janasthāna</s> is sufficient proof for you.

children.text: laṅghanaṃ ca samudrasya darśanaṃ ca hanūmataḥ
children.translated_text: The crossing of the ocean and the appearance of <s>Hanūmat</s>,

children.text: vadhaṃ ca rakṣasāṃ yuddhe kaḥ kuryānmānuṣo bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: and the slaughter of <s>rākṣasas</s> in battle: what human being on earth could do these things?

children.text: evaṃ sa mantrivṛddhaiśca mātrā ca bahu bhāṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: Though he was addressed at length in this way by the elder ministers and by his mother,

children.text: na tvām utsahate moktum artham arthaparo yathā ||
children.translated_text: he is not willing to release you, as a man intent on wealth is not willing to give up wealth.

children.text: notsahatyamṛto moktuṃ yuddhe tvām iti maithili
children.translated_text: He is not willing to release you while he lives in battle, O <s>Maithilī</s>;
this is the settled decision of that cruel one together with his ministers.

children.text: tad eṣā susthirā buddhir mṛtyulobhād upasthitā
children.translated_text: This firm resolve has arisen in him from a longing that leads to death;
out of fear, he is unable to release you unless he is first overthrown in battle,

children.text: rākṣasānāṃ ca sarveṣām ātmanaśca vadhena hi ||
children.translated_text: through the death of all the <s>rākṣasas</s> and of himself.

children.text: nihatya rāvaṇaṃ saṃkhye sarvathā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
children.translated_text: After slaying <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle in every way with sharp arrows,
<s>Rāma</s> will bring you back to <s>Ayodhyā</s>, O dark-eyed one."
Meanwhile a sound filled with drums and conches
was heard from all the armies, shaking the surface of the earth.

children.text: śrutvā tu taṃ vānarasainyaśabdaṃ laṅkāgatā rākṣasarājabhṛtyāḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that sound of the monkey army, the servants of the <s>rākṣasa</s> king who were in <s>Laṅkā</s>

children.text: naṣṭaujaso dainyaparītaceṣṭāḥ śreyo na paśyanti nṛpasya doṣaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: lost their vigor, their actions overcome by misery, and, because of the king's faults, they saw no good outcome.
With that sound of drums mixed with conches, <s>Rāghava</s>,
mighty-armed <s>Rāma</s>, conqueror of enemy cities, had arrived.
Then, hearing that roar, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>,
entered into thought for a moment and looked toward his counselors.

children.text: atha tān sacivāṃstatra sarvān ābhāṣya rāvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s> addressed all those counselors there,
and, filling the whole assembly hall with his voice, the mighty one spoke thus:
"What you have said about <s>Rāma</s>'s crossing of the ocean, his valor, and the gathering of his forces,
that I have heard;
and I also know your true courage in battle.
Then a very wise <s>rākṣasa</s> named <s>Mālyavān</s>,
the maternal grandfather of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s mother, having heard <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s words, spoke:
"A king, O king, who is well trained in the sciences and follows the principles of policy

children.text: sa śāsti ciram aiśvaryam arīṃśca kurute vaśe ||
children.translated_text: rules his sovereignty for a long time and brings his enemies under control.
Making peace at the proper time and also waging war against enemies,
while strengthening his own side, he obtains great sovereignty.

children.text: hīyamānena kartavyo rājñā saṃdhiḥ samena ca
children.translated_text: A king who is declining, and one who is equal, should make peace;

children.text: na śatrum avamanyeta jyāyān kurvīta vigraham ||
children.translated_text: he should not despise an enemy, and when stronger he should wage war.

children.text: tanmahyaṃ rocate saṃdhiḥ saha rāmeṇa rāvaṇa
children.translated_text: Therefore peace with <s>Rāma</s>, O <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, seems best to me.

children.text: yadartham abhiyuktāḥ sma sītā tasmai pradīyatām ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s>, for whose sake we have been attacked, should be given back to him.
All the divine seers and <s>gandharvas</s> desire his victory.

children.text: virodhaṃ mā gamastena saṃdhiste tena rocatām ||
children.translated_text: Do not enter into conflict with him; let peace with him be pleasing to you.

children.text: asṛjad bhagavān pakṣau dvāveva hi pitāmahaḥ
children.translated_text: The blessed <s>Pitāmaha</s> created only two sides:
that of the gods and that of the asuras, with dharma and adharma resting upon them.

children.text: dharmo hi śrūyate pakṣaḥ surāṇāṃ ca mahātmanām
children.translated_text: Dharma is said to be the side of the great-souled gods;

children.text: adharmo rakṣasāṃ pakṣo hyasurāṇāṃ ca rāvaṇa ||
children.translated_text: adharma is the side of the <s>rākṣasas</s> and asuras, O <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: dharmo vai grasate 'dharmaṃ tataḥ kṛtam abhūd yugam
children.translated_text: Dharma indeed devours adharma; then the <s>Kṛta</s> age comes into being.
Adharma devours dharma; then the <s>Tiṣya</s> age begins.

children.text: tat tvayā caratā lokān dharmo vinihato mahān
children.translated_text: Because you have roamed through the worlds, great dharma has been destroyed by you,
and adharma has been seized upon; therefore our enemies are stronger than we are.

children.text: sa pramādād vivṛddhaste 'dharmo 'hir grasate hi naḥ
children.translated_text: That adharma, grown through your negligence, is swallowing us like a serpent,
and, fostering the gods, it increases the side of the gods.
Because you are attached to the objects of sense and act however you please...
Great agitation was produced among the sages, who were like fires;

children.text: teṣāṃ prabhāvo durdharṣaḥ pradīpta iva pāvakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: their power is hard to assail, like a blazing flame.
Their selves purified by austerity, devoted to the favoring of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),

children.text: mukhyair yajñair yajantyete nityaṃ taistair dvijātayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: these twice-born men constantly sacrifice with various principal sacrifices.
They offer oblations into the fires according to rule and recite the Vedas aloud;
overpowering the <s>rākṣasas</s>, they send forth the sound of sacred recitation,
and all the quarters are driven into flight, as by thunder in the hot season.
The smoke arisen from the agnihotra of the sages, who are like fires,

children.text: ādatte rakṣasāṃ tejo dhūmo vyāpya diśo daśa ||
children.translated_text: takes away the splendor of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, pervading the ten directions.

children.text: teṣu teṣu ca deśeṣu puṇyeṣu ca dṛḍhavrataiḥ
children.translated_text: In each of those sacred regions, by men firm in their vows,
the severe austerity being practiced scorches the <s>rākṣasas</s>.
Seeing various portents, dreadful and of many kinds,
I foresee the destruction of all the <s>rākṣasas</s>.
Terrible clouds, rumbling harshly and causing fear,
rain hot blood on <s>Laṅkā</s> from every side.
Tear-drops fall from the crying mounts;

children.text: dhvajā dhvastā vivarṇāśca na prabhānti yathāpuram ||
children.translated_text: the banners are broken and discolored, and they no longer shine as before.

children.text: vyālā gomāyavo gṛdhrā vāśanti ca subhairavam
children.translated_text: Serpents, jackals, and vultures cry out very fearfully,
entering <s>Laṅkā</s> constantly and forming gatherings.
Dark goddesses with pale teeth stand before us laughing;

children.text: striyaḥ svapneṣu muṣṇantyo gṛhāṇi pratibhāṣya ca ||
children.translated_text: in dreams, women steal away houses after addressing them.
Dogs consume the household offerings made to the dwellings;

children.text: kharā goṣu prajāyante mūṣikā nakulaiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: donkeys are born among cows, and mice together with mongooses.

children.text: mārjārā dvīpibhiḥ sārdhaṃ sūkarāḥ śunakaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Cats come together with panthers, and pigs with dogs;
kinnaras, <s>rākṣasas</s>, and humans also mingle together.
Pale birds with red feet, driven on by Time,
and pigeons move about for the destruction of the <s>rākṣasas</s>.
Mynah birds, standing in the houses, cry 'cīcīkūcī';
though bound together, they fall down, defeated, eager for quarrel.
A terrifying, misshapen, bald man, dark and tawny,
Time himself, at intervals, inspects everyone's houses.
These and other evil omens arise.

children.text: viṣṇuṃ manyāmahe rāmaṃ mānuṣaṃ deham āsthitam
children.translated_text: We think <s>Rāma</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, having assumed a human body;
for that steadfastly valiant <s>Rāghava</s> is not a mere human being.

children.text: yena baddhaḥ samudrasya sa setuḥ paramādbhutaḥ
children.translated_text: By him that bridge over the ocean was built, exceedingly marvelous.
Make peace, O <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, with <s>Rāma</s>, the king among men.

children.text: idaṃ vacastatra nigadya mālyavān parīkṣya rakṣo'dhipater manaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken this speech there, <s>Mālyavān</s> again examined the mind of the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>;

children.text: anuttameṣūttamapauruṣo balī babhūva tūṣṇīṃ samavekṣya rāvaṇam ||
children.translated_text: then that strong man, supreme in valor among the unsurpassed, became silent, watching <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: tat tu mālyavato vākyaṃ hitam uktaṃ daśānanaḥ
children.translated_text: But ten-necked <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, evil-souled and come under the power of Time,

children.text: na marṣayati duṣṭātmā kālasya vaśam āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: could not endure that beneficial speech spoken by <s>Mālyavān</s>.

children.text: sa baddhvā bhrukuṭiṃ vaktre krodhasya vaśam āgataḥ
children.translated_text: He knit a frown upon his face, overcome by anger;
his eyes rolling from resentment, he then spoke to <s>Mālyavān</s>:

children.text: hitabuddhyā yad ahitaṃ vacaḥ paruṣam ucyate
children.translated_text: "This hostile and harsh speech, though spoken with the thought of benefit,
as if entering the side of the enemy, has not entered my ears.
By what reasoning do you consider wretched <s>Rāma</s>, a mere human, alone, dependent on branch-animals,

children.text: samarthaṃ manyase kena tyaktaṃ pitrā vanālayam ||
children.translated_text: cast off by his father and dwelling in the forest, to be capable?

children.text: rakṣasām īśvaraṃ māṃ ca devatānāṃ bhayaṃkaram
children.translated_text: And by what reasoning do you consider me, lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, terrifying to the gods,

children.text: hīnaṃ māṃ manyase kena ahīnaṃ sarvavikramaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: to be inferior, though I am not lacking in any valor?

children.text: vīradveṣeṇa vā śaṅke pakṣapātena vā ripoḥ
children.translated_text: I suspect that through hatred of heroes, or partiality toward the enemy,
or through encouragement from another side, you have spoken harsh words to me.
For who, being learned and knowing the truth of the śāstras, would speak harshly
to one who is powerful and established in his position, without encouragement from an enemy?

children.text: ānīya ca vanāt sītāṃ padmahīnām iva śriyam
children.translated_text: Having brought <s>Sītā</s> from the forest, like <s>Śrī</s> bereft of her lotus,
why should I give her back out of fear of <s>Rāghava</s>?
In a few days you shall see <s>Rāghava</s>, surrounded by crores of monkeys,

children.text: paśya kaiścid ahobhistvaṃ rāghavaṃ nihataṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: together with <s>Sugrīva</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, slain by me.

children.text: dvandve yasya na tiṣṭhanti daivatānyapi saṃyuge
children.translated_text: When even the gods do not stand before him in single combat in battle,

children.text: sa kasmād rāvaṇo yuddhe bhayam āhārayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: why should that <s>Rāvaṇa</s> bring fear upon himself in war?

children.text: dvidhā bhajyeyam apyevaṃ na nameyaṃ tu kasyacit
children.translated_text: I might be split in two in this way, but I would not bow to anyone;

children.text: eṣa me sahajo doṣaḥ svabhāvo duratikramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this is my innate fault, and one's nature is hard to overcome.

children.text: yadi tāvat samudre tu setur baddho yadṛcchayā
children.translated_text: If indeed a bridge over the ocean was built by <s>Rāma</s> by chance,

children.text: rāmeṇa vismayaḥ ko 'tra yena te bhayam āgatam ||
children.translated_text: what wonder is there in that, because of which fear has come upon you?

children.text: sa tu tīrtvārṇavaṃ rāmaḥ saha vānarasenayā
children.translated_text: But when <s>Rāma</s> has crossed the ocean with the army of monkeys,

children.text: pratijānāmi te satyaṃ na jīvan pratiyāsyati ||
children.translated_text: I truly promise you that he will not return alive."

children.text: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ saṃrabdhaṃ ruṣṭaṃ vijñāya rāvaṇam
children.translated_text: Knowing <s>Rāvaṇa</s> to be enraged and furious as he spoke in this way,
ashamed, <s>Mālyavān</s> made no reply to his words.
After duly increasing the king's fortune with a blessing for victory,
<s>Mālyavān</s>, dismissed, went to his own residence.
But <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, together with his ministers, having counseled and deliberated,
caused an incomparable guard to be established in <s>Laṅkā</s>.

children.text: vyādideśa ca pūrvasyāṃ prahastaṃ dvāri rākṣasam
children.translated_text: He assigned the <s>rākṣasa</s> <s>Prahasta</s> to the eastern gate,
and to the southern gate the two mighty heroes <s>Mahāpārśva</s> and <s>Mahodara</s>.

children.text: paścimāyām atho dvāri putram indrajitaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Then at the western gate he assigned his son <s>Indrajit</s>,
great in magic, surrounded by many <s>rākṣasas</s>.
Having assigned <s>Śuka</s> and <s>Sāraṇa</s> to the northern city gate,

children.text: svayaṃ cātra bhaviṣyāmi mantriṇastān uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: he told those ministers, "I myself shall be here."
But the <s>rākṣasa</s> <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, of great valor and prowess,
he stationed in the middle division, together with many <s>rākṣasas</s>.
Having made such an arrangement in <s>Laṅkā</s>, the foremost of <s>rākṣasas</s>
thought himself to have accomplished his aim, though he had come under the power of fate.

children.text: visarjayāmāsa tataḥ sa mantriṇo vidhānam ājñāpya purasya puṣkalam
children.translated_text: Then, after ordering the extensive disposition of the city, he dismissed his ministers;

children.text: jayāśiṣā mantragaṇena pūjito viveśa so 'ntaḥpuram ṛddhimanmahat ||
children.translated_text: honored by the company of ministers with blessings for victory, he entered his great, prosperous inner palace.

children.text: naravānararājau tau sa ca vāyusutaḥ kapiḥ
children.translated_text: The two kings, of men and of vānaras, and that monkey, the son of the Wind,
and <s>Jāmbavān</s>, king of the bears, and the <s>rākṣasa</s> <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,
<s>Aṅgada</s>, son of <s>Vālin</s>, <s>Saumitri</s>, and the monkey <s>Śarabha</s>,

children.text: suṣeṇaḥ sahadāyādo maindo dvivida eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Suṣeṇa</s> with his kinsmen, and likewise <s>Mainda</s> and <s>Dvivida</s>,
<s>Gaja</s>, <s>Gavākṣa</s>, <s>Kumuda</s>, <s>Nala</s>, and also <s>Panasa</s>,
having reached the enemy's territory, assembled and deliberated.

children.text: iyaṃ sā lakṣyate laṅkā purī rāvaṇapālitā
children.translated_text: "This is seen to be that city <s>Laṅkā</s>, protected by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
hard to conquer even for immortals, together with asuras, serpents, and gandharvas.
Keeping the accomplishment of the task before you, deliberate toward a decision;
for <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, is always present here."
While they were speaking thus, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, the younger brother of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
spoke words free from vulgar expression and rich in meaning.
"<s>Anala</s>, <s>Śarabha</s>, <s>Saṃpāti</s>, and likewise <s>Praghasa</s>,

children.text: gatvā laṅkāṃ mamāmātyāḥ purīṃ punar ihāgatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: my ministers, went to the city <s>Laṅkā</s> and have returned here again.

children.text: bhūtvā śakunayaḥ sarve praviṣṭāśca ripor balam
children.translated_text: All of them became birds and entered the enemy's army;

children.text: vidhānaṃ vihitaṃ yacca tad dṛṣṭvā samupasthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: having seen the arrangement that had been made there, they have come back.
As they reported the disposition of wicked <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: rāma tad bruvataḥ sarvaṃ yathātathyena me śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: hear all that from me, <s>Rāma</s>, exactly as it is.

children.text: pūrvaṃ prahastaḥ sabalo dvāram āsādya tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: First, <s>Prahasta</s> stands at the eastern gate with his army;
and at the southern gate stand the two mighty warriors <s>Mahāpārśva</s> and <s>Mahodara</s>.
<s>Indrajit</s>, surrounded by many <s>rākṣasas</s>, holds the western gate,
with men bearing spears, swords, and bows, and with spears and clubs in hand.
The son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> is surrounded by heroes with various weapons,
by many thousands of <s>rākṣasas</s> with weapons in hand.
Fully arrayed and very much on guard, surrounded by many <s>rākṣasas</s>,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> himself has taken his place at the northern city gate.
But <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, with a great force bearing spears, swords, and bows,

children.text: balena rākṣasaiḥ sārdhaṃ madhyamaṃ gulmam āsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: has taken his place in the middle division together with <s>rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: etān evaṃvidhān gulmāṃl laṅkāyāṃ samudīkṣya te
children.translated_text: Having observed these divisions of such a kind in <s>Laṅkā</s>,

children.text: māmakāḥ sacivāḥ sarve śīghraṃ punar ihāgatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all my counselors quickly returned here again.

children.text: gajānāṃ ca sahasraṃ ca rathānām ayutaṃ pure
children.translated_text: In the city there are a thousand elephants and ten thousand chariots,

children.text: hayānām ayute dve ca sāgrakoṭī ca rakṣasām ||
children.translated_text: twenty thousand horses and more than a crore of <s>rākṣasas</s>.
Valiant, powerful, and aggressive in battles,
these night-roamers are always dear to the king of the <s>rākṣasas</s>.
For each <s>rākṣasa</s> here in battle, O lord of men,
a retinue of a thousand thousands stands in attendance.
After <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> had told this report about <s>Laṅkā</s>, as spoken by his ministers,
he then spoke this further reply to lotus-petal-eyed <s>Rāma</s>:

children.text: kuberaṃ tu yadā rāma rāvaṇaḥ pratyayudhyata
children.translated_text: "When <s>Rāvaṇa</s> fought against <s>Kubera</s>, O <s>Rāma</s>,
sixty hundred-thousands of <s>rākṣasas</s> marched out at that time,
who, in prowess, strength, brilliance, and weight of spirit,
were equal in arrogance to wicked <s>Rāvaṇa</s> here.

children.text: atra manyur na kartavyo roṣaye tvāṃ na bhīṣaye
children.translated_text: No anger should be felt at this; I do not provoke you or frighten you,

children.text: samartho hyasi vīryeṇa surāṇām api nigrahe ||
children.translated_text: for by your valor you are capable even of restraining the gods.
Therefore, surrounded by a great fourfold army,
array this host of vānaras, and you will crush <s>Rāvaṇa</s>."
When the younger brother of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> had spoken these words, <s>Rāghava</s>,
for the purpose of striking back at his enemies, spoke these words:
"At the eastern gate of <s>Laṅkā</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, foremost of vānaras,

children.text: prahastaṃ pratiyoddhā syād vānarair bahubhir vṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: surrounded by many vānaras, shall be the opponent of <s>Prahasta</s>.
But <s>Aṅgada</s>, son of <s>Vālin</s>, surrounded by a great force,
shall harass <s>Mahāpārśva</s> and <s>Mahodara</s> at the southern gate.
<s>Hanūmān</s>, the son of the Wind, pressing hard upon the western gate,
let that immeasurable-souled one enter, surrounded by many monkeys.
As for the low one, fond of wronging hosts of daityas and dānavas
and the great-souled seers, empowered by the strength of boons,

children.text: parikrāmati yaḥ sarvāṃl lokān saṃtāpayan prajāḥ
children.translated_text: who ranges through all the worlds, tormenting creatures,

children.text: tasyāhaṃ rākṣasendrasya svayam eva vadhe dhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I myself am resolved upon the killing of that lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>.
I, together with <s>Saumitri</s>, will press upon the northern city gate
and enter it, where <s>Rāvaṇa</s> stands with his army.
Let the powerful lord of the vānaras, and <s>Jāmbavān</s>, king of the bears,
and the younger brother of the lord of <s>rākṣasas</s> be in the middle division.

children.text: na caiva mānuṣaṃ rūpaṃ kāryaṃ haribhir āhave
children.translated_text: No human form is to be assumed by the monkeys in battle;

children.text: eṣā bhavatu naḥ saṃjñā yuddhe 'smin vānare bale ||
children.translated_text: let this be our signal in this battle among the vānara army.
Vānaras alone will be our mark among our own people here;

children.text: vayaṃ tu mānuṣeṇaiva sapta yotsyāmahe parān ||
children.translated_text: but we seven will fight the enemy in human form.

children.text: aham eva saha bhrātrā lakṣmaṇena mahaujasā
children.translated_text: I myself, together with my brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> of great splendor,
and this friend of mine, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, fifth with his own companions,

children.text: sa rāmaḥ kāryasiddhyartham evam uktvā vibhīṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Thus, for the accomplishment of the task, that wise <s>Rāma</s>, having spoken to <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,
fixed his thought and intention on ascending <s>Suvela</s>.

children.text: tatastu rāmo mahatā balena pracchādya sarvāṃ pṛthivīṃ mahātmā
children.translated_text: Then the great-souled <s>Rāma</s>, with a mighty army, covering the whole earth,

children.text: prahṛṣṭarūpo 'bhijagāma laṅkāṃ kṛtvā matiṃ so 'rivadhe mahātmā ||
children.translated_text: joyful in appearance, advanced toward <s>Laṅkā</s>, having resolved upon the slaying of his enemy.

children.text: sa tu kṛtvā suvelasya matim ārohaṇaṃ prati
children.translated_text: Having formed his decision about ascending <s>Suvela</s>,
<s>Rāma</s>, followed by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, spoke these words to <s>Sugrīva</s>,
and to righteous <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, the devoted night-roamer,

children.text: mantrajñaṃ ca vidhijñaṃ ca ślakṣṇayā parayā girā ||
children.translated_text: who knew counsel and proper procedure, in a very gentle voice:
"Let us all climb this noble lord of mountains, <s>Suvela</s>, adorned with hundreds of minerals;
we shall spend this night here.
And we shall look upon <s>Laṅkā</s>, the dwelling of that <s>rākṣasa</s>,

children.text: yena me maraṇāntāya hṛtā bhāryā durātmanā ||
children.translated_text: by whom, evil-souled as he is, my wife was carried off, bringing me to the verge of death.

children.text: yena dharmo na vijñāto na vṛttaṃ na kulaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: By whom <s>dharma</s> was not recognized, nor conduct, nor family lineage,

children.text: rākṣasyā nīcayā buddhyā yena tad garhitaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: by whom that blameworthy deed was done with a base <s>rākṣasa</s> understanding.
At the mention of whom my anger increases, that vilest of <s>rākṣasas</s>,
and because of whose offense, base as he is, I shall see the slaughter of the <s>rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: eko hi kurute pāpaṃ kālapāśavaśaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: For one man, come under the power of the noose of Time, does evil;
through his low misconduct, the family is destroyed by him."

children.text: evaṃ saṃmantrayann eva sakrodho rāvaṇaṃ prati
children.translated_text: While speaking in counsel in this way, still angry toward <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
<s>Rāma</s> climbed <s>Suvela</s>, with its varied peaks, to dwell there.
Behind him <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> followed attentively,

children.text: saśaraṃ cāpam udyamya sumahad vikrame rataḥ ||
children.translated_text: raising his bow with arrows, intent upon very great valor.
<s>Sugrīva</s> climbed after him with his ministers and with <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>;

children.text: hanūmān aṅgado nīlo maindo dvivida eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hanūmān</s>, <s>Aṅgada</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, <s>Mainda</s>, and <s>Dvivida</s> as well;
<s>Gaja</s>, <s>Gavākṣa</s>, <s>Gavaya</s>, <s>Śarabha</s>, and <s>Gandhamādana</s>;
<s>Panasa</s>, <s>Kumuda</s>, <s>Hara</s>, and <s>Rambha</s>, the troop-leaders.

children.text: ete cānye ca bahavo vānarāḥ śīghragāminaḥ
children.translated_text: These and many other swift-moving monkeys,
those mountain-roamers, inclined to the speed of the wind,
climbed <s>Suvela</s> by the hundreds, where <s>Rāghava</s> was.

children.text: te tvadīrgheṇa kālena girim āruhya sarvataḥ
children.translated_text: After no long time, having climbed the mountain on every side,

children.text: dadṛśuḥ śikhare tasya viṣaktām iva khe purīm ||
children.translated_text: they saw on its summit the city, as if suspended in the sky.
The monkey troop-leaders saw that splendid <s>Laṅkā</s>, with excellent gates,
shining with fine ramparts and filled with <s>rākṣasas</s>.
And because of the dark night-roamers stationed in masses upon the ramparts,
those best of monkeys saw as though another rampart had been made.

children.text: te dṛṣṭvā vānarāḥ sarve rākṣasān yuddhakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing all the <s>rākṣasas</s> eager for battle,
the monkeys released great roars there as <s>Rāma</s> watched.
Then the sun set, reddened by twilight,
and night came on, lit by the full moon.

children.text: tataḥ sa rāmo harivāhinīpatir vibhīṣaṇena pratinandya satkṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Then that <s>Rāma</s>, lord of the monkey army, welcomed and honored by <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,
together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and surrounded by groups of troop-leaders, dwelt comfortably on the back of <s>Suvela</s>.
Having passed that night there on <s>Suvela</s>, the foremost monkeys
saw the forests and pleasure groves in <s>Laṅkā</s>.
They were level and pleasant, charming, broad, and extensive;
seeing them delightful to the eye, the monkeys became filled with wonder.
Thick with campaka, aśoka, punnāga, sāla, and tāla trees,
covered with tamāla groves and encircled with nāgamālā plants,
with flowering hintāla, arjuna, nīpa, and saptaparṇa trees,
and everywhere with tilaka, karṇikāra, and pāṭala trees,
<s>Laṅkā</s> shone with trees whose tops were in flower and which were embraced by creepers,
with many kinds of divine growths, like <s>Indra</s>'s <s>Amarāvatī</s>.
With varied flowers and red, tender shoots,
with green lawns and with variegated rows of forests,
there the trees bore fragrant and delightful flowers and fruits,
like human beings bearing ornaments.
That charming forest, like <s>Caitraratha</s> and resembling <s>Nandana</s>,
lovely in every season and filled with bees, shone.
With nātyūha birds and yaṣṭibhakas, and with peacocks dancing,
and the cry of cuckoos was heard at the forest waterfall.
With birds constantly intoxicated, and frequented by bees,
with thickets crowded by cuckoos and resounding with birds,
sung over by bhṛṅgarāja birds and attended by bees,
echoing with koṇālaka birds and resounding with cranes,
then those heroes entered those forests and pleasure groves,
the monkeys, rejoicing and delighted, able to assume forms at will.
As those mighty monkeys were entering there,
a breeze blew, fragrant from contact with flowers and pleasant to the smell.
But other troop-leaders among the monkey heroes, coming out from their troops,
with <s>Sugrīva</s>'s permission, went toward bannered <s>Laṅkā</s>,
frightening the birds and terrifying the deer and elephants,

children.text: kampayantaśca tāṃ laṅkāṃ nādaiḥ svair nadatāṃ varāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and shaking that <s>Laṅkā</s> with their roars, best among those who roar.
As those very swift ones made the earth trampled by their feet,
dust raised by their feet suddenly went upward.

children.text: ṛkṣāḥ siṃhā varāhāśca mahiṣā vāraṇā mṛgāḥ
children.translated_text: Bears, lions, boars, buffaloes, elephants, and deer,

children.text: tena śabdena vitrastā jagmur bhītā diśo daśa ||
children.translated_text: frightened by that sound, went in fear to the ten directions.

children.text: śikharaṃ tu trikūṭasya prāṃśu caikaṃ divispṛśam
children.translated_text: But one lofty peak of <s>Trikūṭa</s>, high and touching the sky,
covered with flowers on every side and resembling great silver,
was a hundred yojanas broad, spotless, and lovely to behold.
smooth, splendid, and great, hard to reach even for birds;

children.text: manasāpi durārohaṃ kiṃ punaḥ karmaṇā janaiḥ
children.translated_text: hard to climb even in thought, how much more by bodily effort for men.
On that peak stood <s>Laṅkā</s>, guarded by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
That city, with lofty gateways, was like white clouds,

children.text: kāñcanena ca sālena rājatena ca śobhitā ||
children.translated_text: and shone with a golden rampart and a silver one.
<s>Laṅkā</s> was supremely adorned with palaces and aerial mansions,
like the middle station of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, cloud-filled when the heat has passed.
In it a palace ornamented with a thousand pillars
was seen, shaped like the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>, as though scraping the sky.
That shrine of the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s> was the ornament of the city,

children.text: śatena rakṣasāṃ nityaṃ yaḥ samagreṇa rakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: and it was always guarded by a full hundred <s>rākṣasas</s>.
Prosperous and having attained his purpose, <s>Rāma</s>, the elder brother of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: rāvaṇasya purīṃ rāmo dadarśa saha vānaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: saw that prosperous city of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> together with the monkeys.

children.text: tāṃ ratnapūrṇāṃ bahusaṃvidhānāṃ prāsādamālābhir alaṃkṛtāṃ ca
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, with his great army, saw that city filled with jewels, furnished in many ways, and adorned with rows of palaces,

children.text: purīṃ mahāyantrakavāṭamukhyāṃ dadarśa rāmo mahatā balena ||
children.translated_text: a city whose chief features were great mechanical gate-doors.
Then, seeing the omens there, the elder brother of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>
spoke these words to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, who was endowed with fortune:
Taking possession of cool water and fruit-bearing woods,
let us divide this mass of troops, array it, and stand firm, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
I see close at hand a terrible danger that brings destruction to the world,
the annihilation of foremost heroes among bears, monkeys, and <s>rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: vātāśca paruṣaṃ vānti kampate ca vasuṃdharā
children.translated_text: The winds blow harshly, and the earth trembles;
the mountain summits shake, and mountains fall down.
Clouds, harsh and harsh-sounding, resembling flesh-eaters,
cruelly rain down a dreadful shower mixed with drops of blood.
The twilight, like red sandalwood, is exceedingly dreadful,
and this blazing disk of fire falls from the sun.
Terrible, inauspicious beasts and birds, wretched and with wretched cries,
howl toward the sun, producing great fear.
At night the moon, without brightness, causes distress,
with its rays ending in black and red, as at the destruction of the world.
A small, dry, inauspicious, and very red halo
is seen in the sun's disk, and a dark mark too, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
The constellations are not seen properly, and they move in disorder;

children.text: yugāntam iva lokasya paśya lakṣmaṇa śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: see, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, it foretells the end of the world.

children.text: kākāḥ śyenāstathā gṛdhrā nīcaiḥ paripatanti ca
children.translated_text: Crows, hawks, and vultures fly about low to the ground,
and jackals utter inauspicious cries with loud voices.
Today, quickly and with speed, let us attack the hard-to-assail city guarded by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
surrounded on all sides by the monkeys.

children.text: ityevaṃ tu vadan vīro lakṣmaṇaṃ lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus speaking to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the hero, the elder brother of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
the mighty one quickly descended from that mountain peak.

children.text: avatīrya tu dharmātmā tasmācchailāt sa rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Having descended from that mountain, that righteous <s>Rāghava</s>
saw his own army, exceedingly hard for enemies to withstand.
Then, together with <s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>Rāghava</s> arrayed the great army of the monkey king,
and, knowing the proper time, at that time urged it on to battle.

children.text: tataḥ kāle mahābāhur balena mahatā vṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, at the appointed time, the great-armed archer, surrounded by a great force,

children.text: prasthitaḥ purato dhanvī laṅkām abhimukhaḥ purīm ||
children.translated_text: set out in front, facing the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>.
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, <s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>Hanūmān</s>, <s>Jāmbavān</s>, and <s>Nala</s>
followed him then, as did the bear-king, <s>Nīla</s>, and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Then behind him a very great army of bears and forest-dwellers,

children.text: pracchādya mahatīṃ bhūmim anuyāti sma rāghavam ||
children.translated_text: covering the broad earth, followed <s>Rāghava</s>.
The monkeys, like elephants and repellers of foes, took up hundreds of mountain peaks
and great trees that had grown tall.
In no long time those two enemy-subduing brothers, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
reached <s>Laṅkā</s>, the city of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
It was beautiful, garlanded with banners, splendid with gardens and groves,
with varied ramparts, very hard to reach, and with high walls and gateways.
Urged by <s>Rāma</s>'s command, the forest-dwellers pressed in upon that city,
unassailable even by the gods, and took up positions according to his instructions.
The northern gate of <s>Laṅkā</s>, lofty like a mountain peak,

children.text: rāmaḥ sahānujo dhanvī jugopa ca rurodha ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, bow in hand and with his younger brother, guarded and blockaded.
Having encamped against <s>Laṅkā</s>, the brave <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>,
accompanied by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, stood before the city guarded by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
He reached the northern gate, where <s>Rāvaṇa</s> was stationed;

children.text: nānyo rāmāddhi tad dvāraṃ samarthaḥ parirakṣitum ||
children.translated_text: for no one other than <s>Rāma</s> was able to hold that gate.
It was terrible, occupied by <s>Rāvaṇa</s> like the ocean by <s>Varuṇa</s>,
guarded all around by dreadful armed <s>rākṣasas</s>,
and a source of terror to the weak, like <s>Pātāla</s> with its <s>Dānavas</s>.

children.text: vinyastāni ca yodhānāṃ bahūni vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: He saw many various arrays of the warriors' weapons
and likewise networks of weapons and coats of armor.

children.text: pūrvaṃ tu dvāram āsādya nīlo haricamūpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Having reached the eastern gate, <s>Nīla</s>, the valiant lord of the monkey army,

children.text: atiṣṭhat saha maindena dvividena ca vīryavān ||
children.translated_text: stood there with <s>Mainda</s> and <s>Dvivida</s>.
Mighty <s>Aṅgada</s> took the southern gate,
together with <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Gavākṣa</s>, <s>Gaja</s>, and <s>Gavaya</s>.
The powerful monkey <s>Hanūmān</s> guarded the western gate,
joined by <s>Pramāthi</s>, <s>Praghasa</s>, and other heroes.

children.text: madhyame ca svayaṃ gulme sugrīvaḥ samatiṣṭhata
children.translated_text: And <s>Sugrīva</s> himself took his stand in the central division.
together with all the foremost monkeys, like <s>Suparṇa</s> and the wind.
Now thirty-six crores of the monkeys, renowned troop leaders,
pressed close together and encamped where <s>Sugrīva</s> the monkey was.
Then, by <s>Rāma</s>'s command, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, together with <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,

children.text: dvāre dvāre harīṇāṃ tu koṭiṃ koṭiṃ nyaveśayat ||
children.translated_text: stationed a crore of monkeys at each and every gate.
To the west of <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Sugrīva</s> together with <s>Jāmbavān</s>,
not far away, stood in the middle division, followed by a great force.

children.text: te tu vānaraśārdūlāḥ śārdūlā iva daṃṣṭriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: But those tiger-like monkeys, like fanged tigers,
took up trees and mountain peaks and stood delighted for battle.
All had distorted tails; all had teeth and nails as weapons.
All had strange and mottled limbs, and all had distorted faces.
Some had the strength of ten elephants, and some had ten times more;
some were equal in valor to a thousand elephants.
Some had the strength of a flood, and some had a hundred times more;
and other monkey troop-lords there were of immeasurable strength.
Their gathering was wonderful and varied;
there was an uprising there of the monkey armies like a swarm of locusts.
The sky seemed filled, and the earth seemed covered,
by the monkeys who had encamped around <s>Laṅkā</s> and were rushing in.
Separate hundreds of hundred-thousands of bears and forest-dwellers
came up to the gates of <s>Laṅkā</s>, while others came to fight on every side.

children.text: āvṛtaḥ sa giriḥ sarvaistaiḥ samantāt plavaṃgamaiḥ
children.translated_text: That whole mountain was surrounded on every side by all those leaping monkeys,

children.text: ayutānāṃ sahasraṃ ca purīṃ tām abhyavartata ||
children.translated_text: and a thousand ten-thousands advanced upon that city.
With powerful monkeys bearing trees in their hands,
<s>Laṅkā</s>, hard to enter even for the wind, was enclosed on every side.
The <s>rākṣasas</s>, suddenly hard-pressed, were struck with amazement
by monkeys resembling clouds and equal to <s>Śakra</s> in valor.
A great noise arose there as the mass of the army advanced,
like the roar of water from the ocean when it has been broken open.
By that great sound, with her ramparts and gateways,
all <s>Laṅkā</s> shook, together with its mountains, woods, and groves.
That army, protected by <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and by <s>Sugrīva</s>,
became harder to assail even for all the gods and <s>asuras</s>.

children.text: rāghavaḥ saṃniveśyaivaṃ sainyaṃ svaṃ rakṣasāṃ vadhe
children.translated_text: Having deployed his own army in this way for the slaughter of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: saṃmantrya mantribhiḥ sārdhaṃ niścitya ca punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: after counseling with his ministers and deciding again and again,
desiring immediate action and knowing the truth of proper sequence and order,
with <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>'s consent, remembering royal duty,
summoned <s>Aṅgada</s>, son of <s>Vālin</s>, and spoke these words:

children.text: gatvā saumya daśagrīvaṃ brūhi madvacanāt kape
children.translated_text: "Go, gentle monkey, and speak to ten-necked <s>Rāvaṇa</s> on my behalf,

children.text: laṅghayitvā purīṃ laṅkāṃ bhayaṃ tyaktvā gatavyathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: after leaping into the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>, fearless and free from distress:
'You whose splendor has fallen, whose sovereignty is gone, who are about to die, whose mind is lost,
O night-roamer, whatever sin against seers, gods, Gandharvas and Apsarases,

children.text: nāgānām atha yakṣāṇāṃ rājñāṃ ca rajanīcara
children.translated_text: and against Nāgas, Yakṣas, and kings,

children.text: yacca pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ mohād avaliptena rākṣasa ||
children.translated_text: you, an arrogant <s>rākṣasa</s>, have committed through delusion,
surely today the pride born from <s>Svayambhū</s>'s boon has departed,
for I am the bearer of punishment for you, worn by the abduction of my wife,
standing at the gate of <s>Laṅkā</s> while holding that punishment.

children.text: padavīṃ devatānāṃ ca maharṣīṇāṃ ca rākṣasa
children.translated_text: O <s>rākṣasa</s>, to the path of the gods and of the great seers,

children.text: rājarṣīṇāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ gamiṣyasi mayā hataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and of all the royal seers, you will go, slain by me.

children.text: balena yena vai sītāṃ māyayā rākṣasādhama
children.translated_text: With that power by which, O lowest of <s>rākṣasas</s>, by illusion,
you carried off <s>Sītā</s> after outwitting me, show it now.

children.text: arākṣasam imaṃ lokaṃ kartāsmi niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
children.translated_text: I shall make this world free of <s>rākṣasas</s> with sharp arrows,

children.text: na ceccharaṇam abhyeṣi mām upādāya maithilīm ||
children.translated_text: if you do not seek refuge in me, bringing <s>Maithilī</s> with you.
This righteous <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, best of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, has come to me;
this illustrious one will surely obtain the lordship of <s>Laṅkā</s>, free from obstacles.

children.text: na hi rājyam adharmeṇa bhoktuṃ kṣaṇam api tvayā
children.translated_text: For a kingdom cannot be enjoyed by you even for a moment through unrighteousness,
with foolish allies, sinful and unconquered in yourself.

children.text: yudhyasva vā dhṛtiṃ kṛtvā śauryam ālambya rākṣasa
children.translated_text: Or fight, gathering firmness and relying on valor, O <s>rākṣasa</s>;
quieted in battle by my arrows, you will then become purified.
Even if you enter the three worlds, becoming a bird with the speed of thought,

children.text: mama cakṣuṣpathaṃ prāpya na jīvan pratiyāsyasi ||
children.translated_text: once you come within the path of my sight, you will not return alive.

children.text: bravīmi tvāṃ hitaṃ vākyaṃ kriyatām aurdhvadehikam
children.translated_text: I tell you a beneficial word: let the rites after death be performed;

children.text: sudṛṣṭā kriyatāṃ laṅkā jīvitaṃ te mayi sthitam ||
children.translated_text: take a good look at <s>Laṅkā</s>, for your life rests in me.'"
Thus addressed by tireless <s>Rāma</s>, that son of <s>Tārā</s>
entered the sky and went, like the Fire-god embodied.
In a moment, passing swiftly on, the illustrious one saw <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s palace,
and <s>Rāvaṇa</s> seated undisturbed together with his ministers.
Then, landing not far from him, that bull among monkeys,
<s>Aṅgada</s> with golden armlets stood like a blazing fire.
All that excellent speech of <s>Rāma</s>, with nothing lacking or added,
he caused <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and his ministers to hear, after announcing himself in person.
"I am the messenger of the lord of <s>Kosala</s>, of <s>Rāma</s>, tireless in action;

children.text: vāliputro 'ṅgado nāma yadi te śrotram āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: I am named <s>Aṅgada</s>, son of <s>Vālin</s>, if that has come to your ears.
<s>Rāghava</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, increaser of <s>Kausalyā</s>'s joy, says this to you:
'Come out and fight back, cruel one, lowest of men.
I will kill you together with your ministers, sons, kinsmen, and relatives;
when you are slain, the three worlds will be free from anxiety.'"
Today I shall uproot the enemy of the gods, <s>dānavas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, serpents, and <s>rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: śatrum adyoddhariṣyāmi tvām ṛṣīṇāṃ ca kaṇṭakam ||
children.translated_text: you, the thorn of the sages.
And lordship will belong to <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> when you have been slain,

children.text: na cet satkṛtya vaidehīṃ praṇipatya pradāsyasi ||
children.translated_text: unless you honor <s>Vaidehī</s>, bow down, and give her back.
As the foremost monkey was speaking such harsh words,
the lord of the night-roaming host came under the sway of anger.
Then, his eyes copper-red with rage, he commanded his ministers at that time,

children.text: gṛhyatām eṣa durmedhā vadhyatām iti cāsakṛt ||
children.translated_text: again and again saying, "Seize this foolish one; let him be killed."
Hearing the command of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, whose splendor was like blazing fire,
four terrible night-roamers then seized him.
The son of <s>Tārā</s>, the hero, of his own accord allowed himself to be seized,
in order then to show his strength to the host of <s>rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: sa tān bāhudvaye saktān ādāya patagān iva
children.translated_text: Taking those who clung to his two arms, as if they were birds,
<s>Aṅgada</s> then leapt up onto a palace that resembled a mountain.
Shaken off from midair by his speed, those <s>rākṣasas</s>
all fell to the ground as the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s> watched.
Then the palace pinnacle, lofty like a mountain peak,
split apart when he trampled it, as ten-necked <s>Rāvaṇa</s> looked on.
Having broken the palace pinnacle and proclaimed his own name,
he roared a very great roar and sprang up into the sky.
But <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, because of the assault on his palace, conceived the highest anger;
seeing his own destruction, he became absorbed in heavy sighing.
But <s>Rāma</s>, surrounded by many delighted, roaring monkeys,
eager to slay the enemy, advanced solely for battle.
<s>Suṣeṇa</s>, a monkey of great valor, like a mountain peak,
was surrounded there by many monkeys who could assume forms at will.
At <s>Sugrīva</s>'s command the formidable monkey
went around all four gates, like the moon among the stars.
Seeing hundreds of <s>akṣauhiṇīs</s> of those forest-dwellers,
who had encamped around <s>Laṅkā</s> after crossing the ocean,
the <s>rākṣasas</s> were struck with wonder; others were seized with terror,
while still others, from the excitement of battle, felt only joy.
For the whole space between wall and moat was filled with monkeys;
the dejected <s>rākṣasas</s> saw the rampart made into a mass of monkeys.
When that greatly terrifying tumult had begun in the capital of the <s>rākṣasa</s> king,

children.text: pragṛhya rakṣāṃsi mahāyudhāni yugāntavātā iva saṃviceruḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>rākṣasas</s>, taking up great weapons, moved about like winds at the end of an age.
Then those <s>rākṣasas</s> went there to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s palace

children.text: nyavedayan purīṃ ruddhāṃ rāmeṇa saha vānaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and reported that the city was blockaded by <s>Rāma</s> together with the monkeys.

children.text: ruddhāṃ tu nagarīṃ śrutvā jātakrodho niśācaraḥ
children.translated_text: But hearing that the city was blockaded, the night-roamer grew angry;
hearing of the doubled arrangement, he climbed the palace.
He saw <s>Laṅkā</s>, with its mountains, groves, and forests, surrounded
on every side by countless monkey troops eager for battle.

children.text: sa dṛṣṭvā vānaraiḥ sarvāṃ vasudhāṃ kavalīkṛtām
children.translated_text: Seeing the whole earth swallowed up by monkeys,
he became intent on the thought, "How can they be destroyed?"

children.text: sa cintayitvā suciraṃ dhairyam ālambya rāvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: After thinking for a long time and taking hold of courage, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
the wide-eyed one, looked at <s>Rāghava</s> and the monkey troops.
As the lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s> watched, those divisions of the army, part by part,
then mounted <s>Laṅkā</s> for the sake of what was dear to <s>Rāghava</s>.
Copper-faced and golden in color, having abandoned their lives for <s>Rāma</s>'s sake,
they advanced upon <s>Laṅkā</s> itself, armed with śāla trees, palm trees, and rocks.
Those leaping monkeys, with trees, mountain peaks, and fists,
churned up the high tops of palaces and the gateways.
The monkeys filled the moats, which were full of clear water,
with dust, mountain peaks, grass, and wood.
Then troop-lords with thousands of troops, and others with crores of troops,
and still others accompanied by hundreds of crores, mounted <s>Laṅkā</s> at that time.
The leaping monkeys crushed the golden gateways
and shattered gate-towers resembling the peaks of <s>Kailāsa</s>.
Leaping down, leaping across, and roaring, the monkeys,
resembling great elephants, advanced upon that <s>Laṅkā</s>.
"Victorious is mighty <s>Rāma</s>, and mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> too;
victorious is King <s>Sugrīva</s>, protected by <s>Rāghava</s>."
Thus shouting and roaring, the monkeys,
able to assume forms at will, rushed against the rampart of <s>Laṅkā</s>.
<s>Vīrabāhu</s>, <s>Subāhu</s>, and <s>Nala</s>, the forest-roamer,
pressed close and settled upon the rampart, those monkey troop-lords.
Meanwhile they made an encampment for the army.

children.text: pūrvadvāraṃ tu kumudaḥ koṭibhir daśabhir vṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: At the eastern gate <s>Kumuda</s>, surrounded by ten crores,
strong and encircled by monkeys of victorious splendor, stood blocking it.
Coming to the southern gate, the heroic monkey <s>Śatabali</s>,
strong and surrounded by twenty crores, stood blocking it.
<s>Suṣeṇa</s>, the father of <s>Tārā</s>, went to the western gate;
strong and surrounded by sixty crores, he stood blocking it.
Having reached the northern gate, <s>Rāma</s> together with <s>Saumitri</s>,
and <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the monkeys, stood there strongly blocking it.
<s>Gavākṣa</s>, the large-bodied long-tailed monkey, terrible to behold,
of great valor and surrounded by a crore, stood at <s>Rāma</s>'s side.
<s>Dhūmra</s>, destroyer of enemies, surrounded by bears of terrible speed,
stood at <s>Rāma</s>'s side with a crore of very mighty ones.
And very mighty <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, armed and holding a mace in his hand,
stood there, powerful, surrounded by those ministers of his.
<s>Gaja</s>, <s>Gavākṣa</s>, <s>Gavaya</s>, <s>Śarabha</s>, and <s>Gandhamādana</s>,
running about on every side, guarded the army of the vānaras.
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas, his heart overcome by anger,
at that moment ordered the rapid march-out of all his troops.
Then the armies, delighted and urged on by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, rushed forth,
like the surges of the great ocean when it is swelling at its season.
At that interval a dreadful battle arose

children.text: rakṣasāṃ vānarāṇāṃ ca yathā devāsure purā ||
children.translated_text: between the rākṣasas and the vānaras, like that between the gods and asuras in ancient times.
Those terrible ones, proclaiming their own valor, with blazing maces, spears, tridents, and axes,
struck down the vānaras.
Likewise the great-bodied vānaras, with trees and mountain peaks,
struck down those rākṣasas, rushing on with nails and teeth.
Other fierce rākṣasas, standing on the ramparts, attacked those on the ground
and tore them apart with bhiṇḍipāla missiles, swords, and spears.
The enraged vānaras too, leaping up from the ground,
made the rākṣasas standing on the ramparts fall down.
That tumultuous hand-to-hand fight, muddy with flesh and blood,
arose between the rākṣasas and the vānaras, wondrous in appearance.
Then, as those great-souled vānaras were fighting,
a most dreadful surge of force and fury arose among the rākṣasas.
With horses wearing golden headpieces, with standards like flames of fire,
with chariots shining like the sun, and with splendid armor,
the tiger-like rākṣasas marched out, making the ten directions resound,
rākṣasas of dreadful deeds, eager for <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s victory.

children.text: vānarāṇām api camūr mahatī jayam icchatām
children.translated_text: The great army of the vānaras too, desiring victory,
rushed against that army of shape-shifting rākṣasas.
At that interval, as they rushed at one another,
single combats began between the rākṣasas and the vānaras.
The mighty rākṣasa <s>Indrajit</s> fought with <s>Aṅgada</s>, son of <s>Vālin</s>,
just as <s>Andhaka</s> once fought with three-eyed <s>Tryambaka</s>.

children.text: prajaṅghena ca saṃpātir nityaṃ durmarṣaṇo raṇe
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃpāti</s>, always hard to withstand in battle, fought with <s>Prajaṅgha</s>;
and the vānara <s>Hanūmān</s> engaged <s>Jambūmālin</s>.
The rākṣasa younger brother of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, filled with very great anger,
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, met in battle with swift-moving <s>Mitraghna</s>.
Powerful <s>Gaja</s> fought together with the rākṣasa <s>Tapana</s>,
and brilliant <s>Nīla</s> likewise fought with <s>Nikumbha</s>.
The lord of the vānaras, <s>Sugrīva</s>, met with <s>Praghasa</s>,
and glorious <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> met in battle with <s>Virūpākṣa</s>.
The unconquerable rākṣasa <s>Agniketu</s>, and <s>Raśmiketu</s>,
<s>Suptaghna</s>, and <s>Yajñakopa</s> encountered <s>Rāma</s>.
<s>Vajramuṣṭi</s> met with <s>Mainda</s>, and <s>Aśaniprabha</s> with <s>Dvivida</s>;
the two foremost monkeys came together with those two very dreadful rākṣasas.
The fierce rākṣasa hero <s>Pratapana</s>, hard to withstand in battle,
fought in combat with sharp speed against <s>Nala</s>.

children.text: dharmasya putro balavān suṣeṇa iti viśrutaḥ
children.translated_text: The powerful son of <s>Dharma</s>, famous as <s>Suṣeṇa</s>,
that great monkey fought with <s>Vidyunmālin</s>.
And other terrifying vānaras with other rākṣasas

children.text: dvandvaṃ samīyur bahudhā yuddhāya bahubhiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: met in many ways, many against many, for single combat.
There arose there a very great battle, tumultuous and hair-raising,

children.text: rakṣasāṃ vānarāṇāṃ ca vīrāṇāṃ jayam icchatām ||
children.translated_text: between the rākṣasas and the vānaras, heroes eager for victory.
From the bodies of vānaras and rākṣasas streamed rivers of blood, grassy with hair,
bearing along masses of bodies.
Angry <s>Indrajit</s>, like hundred-sacrificing <s>Śatakratu</s> with the thunderbolt,
struck the hero <s>Aṅgada</s>, splitter of enemy armies, with his mace.
In battle, swift-moving and glorious <s>Aṅgada</s> smashed

children.text: jaghāna samare śrīmān aṅgado vegavān kapiḥ ||
children.translated_text: his gold-adorned chariot, together with its horses and charioteer.
<s>Saṃpāti</s>, struck by <s>Prajaṅgha</s> with three arrows,
killed <s>Prajaṅgha</s> at the battle-front with an aśvakarṇa tree.
But powerful <s>Jambūmālin</s>, standing on his chariot,
angrily pierced <s>Hanūmān</s> in the chest in battle with a chariot-spear.
<s>Hanūmān</s>, son of the Wind, mounted that chariot of his
and quickly crushed it with his palm, together with that very rākṣasa.
His limbs pierced by the sharp arrows of the quick-handed rākṣasa,
<s>Gaja</s> struck <s>Tapana</s> with a mountain peak and with his fist.
As <s>Praghasa</s> seemed to be devouring the armies,
<s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the vānaras, pierced him with a saptaparṇa tree and killed him.
Having crushed the fearsome-looking rākṣasa with a shower of arrows,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> killed <s>Virūpākṣa</s> with a single arrow.
The unconquerable <s>Agniketu</s>, and the rākṣasa <s>Raśmiketu</s>,
<s>Suptaghna</s>, and <s>Yajñakopa</s> pierced <s>Rāma</s> with arrows.

children.text: teṣāṃ caturṇāṃ rāmastu śirāṃsi samare śaraiḥ
children.translated_text: But in battle angry <s>Rāma</s> cut off the heads of those four
with four terrible arrows like flames of fire.
<s>Vajramuṣṭi</s> was killed in battle by <s>Mainda</s> with his fist.

children.text: papāta sarathaḥ sāśvaḥ purāṭṭa iva bhūtale ||
children.translated_text: He fell to the ground with his chariot and horses, like a mansion from a city.
<s>Dvivida</s> too, whose touch was like a thunderbolt and lightning,
struck <s>Aśaniprabha</s> with a mountain peak, while all the <s>rākṣasas</s> looked on.
But <s>Aśaniprabha</s>, in battle, pierced the monkey lord <s>Dvivida</s>,
who fought with trees, with arrows resembling lightning.
With his limbs deeply pierced by arrows, <s>Dvivida</s>, overcome with anger,
struck down <s>Aśaniprabha</s>, together with his chariot and horses, with a śāla tree.
And in battle <s>Nikumbha</s> pierced <s>Nīla</s>, whose splendor was like a mass of dark collyrium,
with sharp arrows, as the sun pierces a cloud with its rays.
Then again the night-roamer <s>Nikumbha</s>, swift-handed,

children.text: bibheda samare nīlaṃ nikumbhaḥ prajahāsa ca ||
children.translated_text: pierced <s>Nīla</s> in battle with a hundred arrows and laughed aloud.
But <s>Nīla</s>, like <s>Viṣṇu</s> in battle, with the wheel of that very chariot,
cut off the head of <s>Nikumbha</s>'s charioteer in the fight.
But <s>Vidyunmālī</s>, standing in his chariot, with arrows adorned with gold,

children.text: suṣeṇaṃ tāḍayāmāsa nanāda ca muhur muhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: struck <s>Suṣeṇa</s> and roared again and again.

children.text: taṃ rathastham atho dṛṣṭvā suṣeṇo vānarottamaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, seeing him stationed in his chariot, <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, best of monkeys,
quickly hurled down the chariot with a great mountain peak.
But the night-roamer <s>Vidyunmālī</s>, endowed with agility,

children.text: apakramya rathāt tūrṇaṃ gadāpāṇiḥ kṣitau sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: leapt swiftly away from the chariot and stood on the ground, mace in hand.
Then <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, foremost of monkeys, filled with anger,
took up a very great rock and rushed at the night-roamer.
As he came on, the night-roamer <s>Vidyunmālī</s>, with his mace,
quickly struck <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, best of monkeys, on the chest.
Disregarding that terrible blow of the mace, the best of leapers
dropped that rock upon his chest in the great battle.
Struck by the blow of the rock, the night-roamer <s>Vidyunmālī</s>,
his heart crushed, fell lifeless to the ground.

children.text: evaṃ tair vānaraiḥ śūraiḥ śūrāste rajanīcarāḥ
children.translated_text: In this way, by those heroic monkeys, those heroic night-roamers
were crushed there in single combats, like Daityas by the gods.
With darts, swords, maces, spears, lances, and paṭṭasa weapons,
with battle-chariots and horses cast aside and broken,
with slain rutting elephants, and likewise with monkeys and <s>rākṣasas</s>,
and with wheels, axles, yokes, and poles shattered and lying on the ground,
the dreadful battlefield became a haunt of packs of jackals.
Headless trunks of monkeys and <s>rākṣasas</s> sprang up in every direction
in that tumultuous clash, like a battle of gods and Asuras.
Being torn apart at that time by the foremost monkeys, the night-roamers, their bodies smeared with blood,
again took refuge in fierce fighting with force, longing for the setting of the sun.

children.text: yudhyatām eva teṣāṃ tu tadā vānararakṣasām
children.translated_text: While those monkeys and <s>rākṣasas</s> were still fighting,

children.text: ravir astaṃ gato rātriḥ pravṛttā prāṇahāriṇī ||
children.translated_text: the sun set, and a life-destroying night began.
For those terrible warriors, bound by mutual enmity and desiring victory,
a night battle between the monkeys and <s>rākṣasas</s> then began.
The monkeys cried, 'You are a <s>rākṣasa</s>!' and the <s>rākṣasas</s>, 'You are a monkey!'
and in that dreadful darkness they struck one another in battle.

children.text: jahi dāraya caihīti kathaṃ vidravasīti ca
children.translated_text: 'Strike! Tear him apart! Come here! Why are you running away?'
Such a very tumultuous sound was heard in that darkness.
Black, but clad in golden armor, the <s>rākṣasas</s> in that darkness
appeared like great mountains with forests of shining herbs.
In that darkness, difficult to cross, the <s>rākṣasas</s>, overcome with anger,
rushed about with great speed, devouring the leaping monkeys.
They leapt upon horses with golden headpieces and upon banners like flames of fire,
and, furious with terrible anger, tore them apart with their sharp teeth.
Elephants, elephant-riders, and chariots bearing flags and standards
they dragged and bit with their teeth, overcome with anger.
And <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and <s>Rāma</s>, with arrows resembling poisonous serpents,
struck down the foremost <s>rākṣasas</s>, both visible and invisible.
The dust of the earth, kicked up by horses' hooves and raised by chariot rims,
blocked the ears and eyes of those who were fighting.
