As that dreadful battle, making the hair stand on end, went on,
swift rivers of blood flowed there.
Then the sound of kettledrums, mṛdaṅgas, and paṇavas,
mingled with the sound of conches and flutes, became wondrous beyond compare.
The sound of the slain and the groaning, and the cries of the <s>rākṣasas</s>,
and of weapons and monkeys, became exceedingly terrible.
There the battlefield was strewn with weapons as flowers and offerings;
it was hard to discern and hard to enter, muddy with streams of blood.
That night became terrible, destructive of monkeys and <s>rākṣasas</s>,
like the night of Time for all beings, impossible to pass beyond.
Then those <s>rākṣasas</s> there, in that dreadful darkness,
joyfully rushed straight upon <s>Rāma</s> through showers of arrows.
The sound of those angry attackers roaring as they advanced

children.text: udvarta iva saptānāṃ samudrāṇām abhūt svanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: was like the roar of seven oceans surging upward.

children.text: teṣāṃ rāmaḥ śaraiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ ṣaḍ jaghāna niśācarān
children.translated_text: With six arrows <s>Rāma</s> killed six night-roamers
in the mere span of a blink, with sharp arrows like flames of fire.
<s>Yajñaśatru</s>, the hard-to-assail one, <s>Mahāpārśva</s> and <s>Mahodara</s>,
<s>Vajradaṃṣṭra</s>, <s>Mahākāya</s>, and those two, <s>Śuka</s> and <s>Sāraṇa</s>,

children.text: te tu rāmeṇa bāṇaughaiḥ sarvamarmasu tāḍitāḥ
children.translated_text: they, struck by <s>Rāma</s> with floods of arrows in all their vital points,
Those who withdrew from the battle there survived with the remainder of their lives.
Then, with arrows whose golden-decorated bodies
were like tongues of fire, the mighty one made the quarters and intermediate quarters clear.

children.text: ye tvanye rākṣasā vīrā rāmasyābhimukhe sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: But those other heroic <s>rākṣasas</s> who stood facing <s>Rāma</s>

children.text: te 'pi naṣṭāḥ samāsādya pataṃgā iva pāvakam ||
children.translated_text: also perished when they met him, like moths approaching a fire.
With gold-feathered arrows flying down in thousands,

children.text: babhūva rajanī citrā khadyotair iva śāradī ||
children.translated_text: the night became variegated, like an autumn night with fireflies.

children.text: rākṣasānāṃ ca ninadair harīṇāṃ cāpi garjitaiḥ
children.translated_text: With the cries of the <s>rākṣasas</s> and the roars of the monkeys as well,

children.text: sā babhūva niśā ghorā bhūyo ghoratarā tadā ||
children.translated_text: that night, already terrible, then became still more terrible.
By that great sound, swelling on every side,
<s>Trikūṭa</s>, the mountain filled with caves, seemed to roar in response.
The great-bodied <s>golāṅgūlas</s>, equal to darkness in their hue,
embraced the night-roamers with their arms and devoured them.
But <s>Aṅgada</s>, coming forward in battle to kill his enemy,

children.text: rāvaṇer nijaghānāśu sārathiṃ ca hayān api ||
children.translated_text: quickly slew the charioteer and the horses of <s>Rāvaṇi</s> as well.

children.text: indrajit tu rathaṃ tyaktvā hatāśvo hatasārathiḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Indrajit</s>, abandoning his chariot, his horses and charioteer slain,
that master of great illusion, disappeared there because of <s>Aṅgada</s>.
That wicked <s>Rāvaṇi</s>, harsh in battle, having entered invisibility,
the heroic <s>Rāvaṇi</s>, possessed of a boon granted by <s>Brahmā</s> and overwhelmed by anger,
released sharp arrows, invisible, with the brilliance of thunderbolts.

children.text: sa rāmaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ caiva ghorair nāgamayaiḥ śaraiḥ
children.translated_text: In battle that <s>rākṣasa</s>, enraged, pierced <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>
in every limb with terrible serpent-made arrows.

children.text: sa tasya gatim anvicchan rājaputraḥ pratāpavān
children.translated_text: Searching for his path, the powerful prince,
mighty <s>Rāma</s>, directed ten monkey troop-leaders.

children.text: dvau suṣeṇasya dāyādau nīlaṃ ca plavagarṣabham
children.translated_text: He assigned the two heirs of <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, and <s>Nīla</s>, bull among the leaping monkeys,

children.text: aṅgadaṃ vāliputraṃ ca śarabhaṃ ca tarasvinam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aṅgada</s>, son of <s>Vālin</s>, and swift <s>Śarabha</s>.
He also assigned <s>Vinata</s>, <s>Jāmbavat</s>, mighty <s>Sānuprastha</s>,
and <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, whose shoulders were like a bull's; the scorcher of foes gave the order.

children.text: te samprahṛṣṭā harayo bhīmān udyamya pādapān
children.translated_text: Those monkeys, greatly delighted, raised up fearsome trees,

children.text: ākāśaṃ viviśuḥ sarve mārgamāṇā diśo daśa ||
children.translated_text: and all entered the sky, searching the ten directions.
With arrows swifter than the speed of those swift ones,
<s>Rāvaṇi</s>, skilled in weapons, checked their speed with a supreme missile.
Those monkeys of terrible speed, torn and mangled by iron arrows,

children.text: andhakāre na dadṛśur meghaiḥ sūryam ivāvṛtam ||
children.translated_text: could not see him in the darkness, as the sun is hidden by clouds.
<s>Rāvaṇi</s>, conqueror in battle, drove arrows that pierced every vital point
deep into <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> alone.
The two heroic brothers, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, their bodies covered without a gap,
were struck by the enraged <s>Indrajit</s> with serpents that had taken the form of arrows.
Through the channels of their wounds much blood flowed from them,
and those two shone like flowering <s>kiṃśuka</s> trees.
Then <s>Rāvaṇi</s>, his eyes red at the edges and dark like a mass of split collyrium,
spoke these words to the brothers while remaining invisible.
"Even <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the thirty gods, cannot see me

children.text: draṣṭum āsādituṃ vāpi na śaktaḥ kiṃ punar yuvām ||
children.translated_text: or reach me when I fight unseen; how much less can you two?
Covered with a net of arrows feathered with heron plumes, O <s>Rāghavas</s>,
I, my mind enveloped in fury, will now take you to <s>Yama</s>'s abode."

children.text: evam uktvā tu dharmajñau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, he pierced the two brothers, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, who knew <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: nirbibheda śitair bāṇaiḥ prajaharṣa nanāda ca ||
children.translated_text: with sharp arrows; he rejoiced and roared.
Dark like a heap of split collyrium, he stretched his great bow,

children.text: bhūyo bhūyaḥ śarān ghorān visasarja mahāmṛdhe ||
children.translated_text: and again and again in the great battle he discharged terrible arrows.
Then the hero, knowing the vital points, sank sharp arrows into the vital points

children.text: rāmalakṣmaṇayor vīro nanāda ca muhur muhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and roared again and again.
Bound by the bonds of arrows, those two at the front of battle
could not even look up for the mere interval of a blink.
Then both, with every limb pierced and heaped over with arrow-shafts,
were like <s>Mahendra</s>'s banners trembling after their ropes had been loosened.
Those two heroes, great archers and lords of the earth, staggered,
wasted by wounds to their vital parts, and fell upon the ground.
Those two heroes lay on a hero's bed, sprinkled with blood,
their whole bodies wrapped in arrows, distressed and deeply afflicted.

children.text: na hyaviddhaṃ tayor gātraṃ babhūvāṅgulam antaram
children.translated_text: For there was not the space of a finger on their bodies that was unwounded,

children.text: nānirbhinnaṃ na cāstabdham ā karāgrād ajihmagaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: not unpierced, not pinned fast, from their fingertips onward, by straight arrows.

children.text: tau tu krūreṇa nihatau rakṣasā kāmarūpiṇā
children.translated_text: Struck down by that cruel <s>rākṣasa</s> who could assume any form at will,
the two poured forth blood violently, like springs pouring water.

children.text: papāta prathamaṃ rāmo viddho marmasu mārgaṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> fell first, pierced in the vital points by shafts,

children.text: krodhād indrajitā yena purā śakro vinirjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by <s>Indrajit</s> in anger, by whom <s>Śakra</s> had formerly been conquered.
With long iron arrows, half-arrows, broad-headed shafts, and añjalika arrows,
and also with calf-tooth, lion-fang, and razor-headed arrows, he pierced him.

children.text: sa vīraśayane śiśye vijyam ādāya kārmukam
children.translated_text: He lay on a hero's bed, holding his bow with its string loosened,
its grip's girth broken, bent in three places, and adorned with gold.
Seeing <s>Rāma</s>, bull among men, fallen there between the flights of arrows,

children.text: sa tatra lakṣmaṇo dṛṣṭvā nirāśo jīvite 'bhavat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> became hopeless of life.

children.text: baddhau tu vīrau patitau śayānau tau vānarāḥ saṃparivārya tasthuḥ
children.translated_text: But the monkeys stood surrounding the two heroes, bound and fallen, as they lay there;

children.text: samāgatā vāyusutapramukhyā viṣādam ārtāḥ paramaṃ ca jagmuḥ ||
children.translated_text: those who had gathered, with the son of <s>Vāyu</s> at their head, were afflicted and fell into deepest grief.

children.text: tato dyāṃ pṛthivīṃ caiva vīkṣamāṇā vanaukasaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the forest-dwellers, looking up to the sky and down to the earth,
saw the brothers <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> covered continuously with arrows.
When the <s>rākṣasa</s> had done his work, like the god after raining and ceasing,
Then <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, together with <s>Sugrīva</s>, came to that place.
And <s>Nīla</s>, <s>Dvivida</s>, <s>Mainda</s>, <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, <s>Sumukha</s>, and <s>Aṅgada</s>,
quickly, together with <s>Hanūmān</s>, grieved over the two <s>Rāghavas</s>.
They were motionless, breathing faintly, and drenched in a flood of blood,
covered with a net of arrows, rigid, lying upon beds of arrows.
Breathing like serpents, motionless, their strength slackened,
their limbs smeared with flowing blood, they were like two golden banners.
Those two heroes lay on a hero's couch, moving only faintly,
surrounded by those troop-leaders whose eyes were troubled with tears.
Seeing the fallen <s>Rāghavas</s> covered by a net of arrows,
all the vānaras, along with <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, became distressed.
The vānaras searched the sky and all the directions,

children.text: na cainaṃ māyayā channaṃ dadṛśū rāvaṇiṃ raṇe ||
children.translated_text: but they did not see <s>Rāvaṇi</s> in the battle, hidden by magic.
But <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, looking by means of magic itself at that one concealed by magic,
then saw his brother's son standing there.
That hero of incomparable deeds, unrivalled in combat,
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> saw him hidden, by virtue of a boon.

children.text: indrajit tvātmanaḥ karma tau śayānau samīkṣya ca
children.translated_text: But <s>Indrajit</s>, seeing his own deed and the two lying there,
spoke, exceedingly pleased, gladdening all the rākṣasas.

children.text: dūṣaṇasya ca hantārau kharasya ca mahābalau
children.translated_text: "The slayers of <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> and mighty <s>Khara</s>,
the brothers <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, have been laid low by my arrows.
These two cannot be released from this bondage of arrows,
even if all the hosts of seers, gods, and asuras were to assemble together.
He for whose sake my father broods, afflicted with grief,
so that the night passes without his limbs touching his bed,
he for whose sake all this <s>Laṅkā</s> is disturbed like a river in the rains,
that calamity, uprooting the very root of all, has now been slain by me.
Of <s>Rāma</s>, of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and of all the forest-dwellers,

children.text: vikramā niṣphalāḥ sarve yathā śaradi toyadāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all their valor is fruitless, like clouds in autumn."

children.text: evam uktvā tu tān sarvān rākṣasān paripārśvagān
children.translated_text: Having thus addressed all those rākṣasas standing around him,
<s>Rāvaṇi</s> struck all those troop-leaders as well.
Having tormented them with streams of arrows and terrified the vānaras,
the mighty-armed one laughed loudly and spoke these words:
"By this dreadful binding of arrows I have bound these two at the head of the army,
these two brothers together; behold them, rākṣasas."

children.text: evam uktāstu te sarve rākṣasāḥ kūṭayodhinaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, all those rākṣasas who fought by deceit

children.text: paraṃ vismayam ājagmuḥ karmaṇā tena toṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: fell into supreme wonder, pleased by that deed.
All those cloud-like ones roared great roars,

children.text: hato rāma iti jñātvā rāvaṇiṃ samapūjayan ||
children.translated_text: and, thinking <s>Rāma</s> slain, they honored <s>Rāvaṇi</s>.

children.text: niṣpandau tu tadā dṛṣṭvā tāvubhau rāmalakṣmaṇau
children.translated_text: Then, seeing both <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> motionless,
breathless upon the earth, he supposed that they had been killed.
Filled with joy, <s>Indrajit</s>, conqueror in battle,
entered the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>, gladdening all the rākṣasas.
Seeing the bodies of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> covered with arrows,
and every limb and minor limb pierced, fear entered <s>Sugrīva</s>.
To the terrified king of the vānaras <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> spoke,
as his face was wet with tears, wretched, and his eyes bewildered by grief:
"Enough of fear, <s>Sugrīva</s>; let this rush of tears be restrained.
Battles are often of this kind; victory is never absolutely fixed.
If, hero, some remnant of good fortune will remain for us,
these two brothers, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, will cast off their stupor.
Steady yourself, O vānara, and me too, for I am without support.
For those devoted to truth and <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), there is no fear caused by death."
Having spoken thus, then with his hand moistened with water,
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> wiped the auspicious eyes of <s>Sugrīva</s>.
After wiping the face of that wise king of the monkeys,
he spoke these timely words, without agitation:
"This is not the time, O lord of monkey-kings, to give way to weakness.
Even excessive affection at this untimely moment conduces to death.
Therefore, abandoning weakness, which destroys every undertaking,
let the welfare of the armies led by <s>Rāma</s> be considered.
Or else <s>Rāma</s> must be protected so long as his consciousness is disordered.

children.text: labdhasaṃjñau tu kākutsthau bhayaṃ no vyapaneṣyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: But when the two <s>Kākutsthas</s> have regained consciousness, they will remove our fear.

children.text: naitat kiṃcana rāmasya na ca rāmo mumūrṣati
children.translated_text: This is nothing at all for <s>Rāma</s>, and <s>Rāma</s> is not about to die.

children.text: na hyenaṃ hāsyate lakṣmīr durlabhā yā gatāyuṣām ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Lakṣmī</s> will not abandon him, she who is hard to obtain for those whose lifespan is spent.
Therefore reassure yourself, and reassure your own army,
while I restore all the troops to order.
For these monkeys, their eyes wide open, overcome by alarm from fear,
have been whispering from ear to ear, O foremost of monkeys.

children.text: māṃ tu dṛṣṭvā pradhāvantam anīkaṃ sampraharṣitum
children.translated_text: But when they see me running forward to encourage the army,
let the monkeys cast off fear like a garland already worn."
Having reassured <s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, lord of rākṣasas,
again reassured that vānara army which had fled.
But <s>Indrajit</s>, master of great magic, surrounded by his entire army,
entered the city of <s>Laṅkā</s> and approached his father.
There, bowing with joined palms to <s>Rāvaṇa</s> as he sat,
he reported to his father the welcome news that <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> had been slain.

children.text: utpapāta tato hṛṣṭaḥ putraṃ ca pariṣasvaje
children.translated_text: Then, delighted, he sprang up and embraced his son,

children.text: rāvaṇo rakṣasāṃ madhye śrutvā śatrū nipātitau ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, in the midst of the rākṣasas, after hearing that his enemies had been laid low.
Smelling his head, he questioned him with a pleased mind;

children.text: pṛcchate ca yathāvṛttaṃ pitre sarvaṃ nyavedayat ||
children.translated_text: and when his father asked, he reported everything just as it had happened.
His inner being carried along by a rush of joy, hearing the words of that great chariot-warrior,

children.text: jahau jvaraṃ dāśaratheḥ samutthitaṃ prahṛṣya vācābhinananda putram ||
children.translated_text: he cast off the fever that had arisen from <s>Daśaratha</s>'s son, and, rejoicing, praised his son with words.
But when the son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, having accomplished his purpose, had re-entered <s>Laṅkā</s>,
the foremost vānaras, distressed, surrounded <s>Rāghava</s> and guarded him.

children.text: hanūmān aṅgado nīlaḥ suṣeṇaḥ kumudo nalaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Hanūmān</s>, <s>Aṅgada</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, <s>Kumuda</s>, <s>Nala</s>,
<s>Gaja</s>, <s>Gavākṣa</s>, <s>Gavaya</s>, <s>Śarabha</s>, and <s>Gandhamādana</s>,

children.text: jāmbavān ṛṣabhaḥ sundo rambhaḥ śatabaliḥ pṛthuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Jāmbavān</s>, <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Sunda</s>, <s>Rambha</s>, <s>Śatabali</s>, and <s>Pṛthu</s>,
with their battle lines arrayed and alert, took up trees on every side.

children.text: vīkṣamāṇā diśaḥ sarvāstiryag ūrdhvaṃ ca vānarāḥ
children.translated_text: Looking toward all the quarters, sideways and upward, the vānaras

children.text: tṛṇeṣvapi ca ceṣṭatsu rākṣasā iti menire ||
children.translated_text: thought even grasses that stirred to be rākṣasas.
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> too, greatly delighted, dismissed his son <s>Indrajit</s>,
and then summoned the rākṣasī women who guarded <s>Sītā</s>.
The rākṣasīs, and <s>Trijaṭā</s> also, came before him at his command;

children.text: tā uvāca tato hṛṣṭo rākṣasī rākṣaseśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: then the lord of rākṣasas, delighted, said to those rākṣasīs:
"<s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> have been killed, as <s>Indrajit</s> has reported to <s>Vaidehī</s>;

children.text: puṣpakaṃ ca samāropya darśayadhvaṃ hatau raṇe ||
children.translated_text: put her aboard the <s>Puṣpaka</s> and show her the two killed in battle.
Depending on whom, supported by whom, this woman does not come to me,

children.text: so 'syā bhartā saha bhrātrā nirasto raṇamūrdhani ||
children.translated_text: that husband of hers, together with his brother, has been cast down at the head of battle.
Free from doubt, free from fear, and free from expectation, <s>Maithilī</s>,
<s>Sītā</s>, adorned with every ornament, will come to me.

children.text: adya kālavaśaṃ prāptaṃ raṇe rāmaṃ salakṣmaṇam
children.translated_text: Today, seeing <s>Rāma</s> together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> come under the power of death in battle,
her hope turned back and seeing no other refuge, she will come."
Hearing that speech of wicked-souled <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
those rākṣasīs said, "So be it," and went to where the <s>Puṣpaka</s> was.
Then, taking the <s>Puṣpaka</s> at <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s command,
the rākṣasīs brought that <s>Maithilī</s>, who was staying in the <s>Aśoka</s> grove.
Having taken <s>Sītā</s>, wholly given over to grief for her husband,
the rākṣasīs then made her mount that aerial car, the <s>Puṣpaka</s>.

children.text: tataḥ puṣpakam āropya sītāṃ trijaṭayā saha
children.translated_text: Then, having placed <s>Sītā</s> on the <s>Puṣpaka</s> together with <s>Trijaṭā</s>,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> had <s>Laṅkā</s> adorned with banners and flags.
And the lord of rākṣasas, delighted, caused it to be proclaimed in <s>Laṅkā</s>:
"<s>Rāghava</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> have been killed by <s>Indrajit</s> in battle."

children.text: vimānenāpi sītā tu gatvā trijaṭayā saha
children.translated_text: But <s>Sītā</s>, going in the aerial car together with <s>Trijaṭā</s>,

children.text: dadarśa vānarāṇāṃ tu sarvaṃ sainyaṃ nipātitam ||
children.translated_text: saw the whole army of the vānaras laid low.
She also saw the flesh-eaters with minds delighted,
and the vānaras afflicted with grief beside <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Then <s>Sītā</s> saw both of them lying on beds of arrows,

children.text: lakṣmaṇaṃ caiva rāmaṃ ca visaṃjñau śarapīḍitau ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and <s>Rāma</s>, unconscious and tormented by arrows.
The two heroes had their armor shattered and their bows flung aside;
all their limbs were cut by shafts, and they lay on the ground as if made of pillars of arrows.

children.text: tau dṛṣṭvā bhrātarau tatra vīrau sā puruṣarṣabhau
children.translated_text: Seeing those two brothers there, those heroes, those best of men,

children.text: duḥkhārtā subhṛśaṃ sītā karuṇaṃ vilalāpa ha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s>, deeply afflicted with grief, lamented piteously.

children.text: sā bāṣpaśokābhihatā samīkṣya tau bhrātarau devasamaprabhāvau
children.translated_text: Struck down by tears and sorrow, looking at those two brothers, equal in might to the gods,

children.text: vitarkayantī nidhanaṃ tayoḥ sā duḥkhānvitā vākyam idaṃ jagāda ||
children.translated_text: and imagining their death, she, filled with grief, spoke these words:

children.text: bhartāraṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahābalam
children.translated_text: Seeing her husband slain, and mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> too,
<s>Sītā</s>, wasted by sorrow, lamented greatly and piteously.

children.text: ūcur lakṣaṇikā ye māṃ putriṇyavidhaveti ca
children.translated_text: "Those interpreters of bodily marks who told me, 'You will have sons and will not be widowed,'
all of them, now that <s>Rāma</s> is killed, are ignorant speakers of falsehood.

children.text: yajvano mahiṣīṃ ye mām ūcuḥ patnīṃ ca sattriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Those who called me the chief queen of a sacrificer and the wife of one who performs sacrificial sessions,
all of them, now that <s>Rāma</s> is killed, are ignorant speakers of falsehood.

children.text: vīrapārthivapatnī tvaṃ ye dhanyeti ca māṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: Those who understood me as blessed, saying, 'You are the wife of a heroic king,'
all of them, now that <s>Rāma</s> is killed, are ignorant speakers of falsehood.

children.text: ūcuḥ saṃśravaṇe ye māṃ dvijāḥ kārtāntikāḥ śubhām
children.translated_text: Those twice-born astrologers who, in a gathering for hearing omens, called me auspicious,
all of them, now that <s>Rāma</s> is killed, are ignorant speakers of falsehood.

children.text: imāni khalu padmāni pādayor yaiḥ kila striyaḥ
children.translated_text: These lotus signs on the feet, by which, indeed, women
are consecrated to sovereignty together with their royal husbands,
and those inauspicious marks by which women, deprived of fortune, go to widowhood,
I do not see those on myself, though I now see myself as one whose auspicious marks are destroyed.
Surely these lotus signs have been declared true in the science of women's marks;

children.text: tānyadya nihate rāme vitathāni bhavanti me ||
children.translated_text: today, with <s>Rāma</s> killed, they have become false for me.

children.text: keśāḥ sūkṣmāḥ samā nīlā bhruvau cāsaṃgate mama
children.translated_text: My hair is fine, even, and dark-blue, and my eyebrows do not meet;
my shanks are rounded and hairless, and my teeth are not set far apart.

children.text: śaṅkhe netre karau pādau gulphāvūrū ca me citau
children.translated_text: My temples, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, and thighs are well-formed;
my nails are rounded, smooth, and even, and so are my fingers.
These two breasts of mine are close-set and full, with nipples sunk in;

children.text: magnā cotsaṅginī nābhiḥ pārśvoraskaṃ ca me citam ||
children.translated_text: my navel too is deep and broad, and my sides and chest are well-formed.
My complexion is like a jewel, and the hairs on my body are soft;
they declared me, by twelve established marks, to be auspiciously marked.
The palms and soles of my hands and feet are complete like barley grains, unbroken, and well-colored;
and the interpreters of maidenly marks knew me as one with a gentle smile.
The consecration to sovereignty for me, together with my husband, was proclaimed by the brahmins
All that was said by those skilled in destiny has been made false.
After he had scoured <s>Janasthāna</s> and obtained news of her,

children.text: tīrtvā sāgaram akṣobhyaṃ bhrātarau goṣpade hatau ||
children.translated_text: after crossing the unshakable ocean, the two brothers have been slain as if in a cow's hoofprint.

children.text: nanu vāruṇam āgneyam aindraṃ vāyavyam eva ca
children.translated_text: Surely the <s>Vāruṇa</s>, the <s>Āgneya</s>, the <s>Aindra</s>, and likewise the <s>Vāyavya</s> missiles,
and the <s>Brahmaśiras</s> weapon too, had been obtained by the two <s>Rāghavas</s>.
By one who was unseen in battle, through illusion, those two who were like <s>Vāsava</s>
have been killed, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, my protectors when I am without a protector.

children.text: na hi dṛṣṭipathaṃ prāpya rāghavasya raṇe ripuḥ
children.translated_text: For an enemy, once he had come within the range of <s>Rāghava</s>'s sight in battle,
would not return alive, even if he were as swift as the mind.
There is no excessive burden for Time, and Death is very hard to conquer,

children.text: yatra rāmaḥ saha bhrātrā śete yudhi nipātitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: since <s>Rāma</s>, together with his brother, lies struck down in battle.

children.text: nāhaṃ śocāmi bhartāraṃ nihataṃ na ca lakṣmaṇam
children.translated_text: I do not grieve so much for my husband slain, nor for <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: nātmānaṃ jananīṃ cāpi yathā śvaśrūṃ tapasvinīm ||
children.translated_text: nor for myself or even for my mother, as I grieve for my ascetic mother-in-law.

children.text: sā hi cintayate nityaṃ samāptavratam āgatam
children.translated_text: For she is always thinking of him as having fulfilled his vow and returned:

children.text: kadā drakṣyāmi sītāṃ ca rāmaṃ ca sahalakṣmaṇam ||
children.translated_text: 'When shall I see <s>Sītā</s>, and <s>Rāma</s> together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>?'
As she was lamenting, the <s>rākṣasī</s> <s>Trijaṭā</s> said to her,

children.text: mā viṣādaṃ kṛthā devi bhartāyaṃ tava jīvati ||
children.translated_text: 'Do not give way to despair, lady; this husband of yours is alive.

children.text: kāraṇāni ca vakṣyāmi mahānti sadṛśāni ca
children.translated_text: I shall tell you weighty and fitting reasons,
by which, lady, these two brothers, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, are known to be alive.
When a lord has been slain, the faces of warriors in battle

children.text: bhavanti yudhi yodhānāṃ mukhāni nihate patau ||
children.translated_text: are not filled with anger and restless with eagerness for joy.

children.text: idaṃ vimānaṃ vaidehi puṣpakaṃ nāma nāmataḥ
children.translated_text: This aerial car, <s>Vaidehī</s>, is called <s>Puṣpaka</s> by name;
being divine, it would not carry you if these two had lost their lives.
For an army whose chief heroes are slain is dispirited and without effort;

children.text: senā bhramati saṃkhyeṣu hatakarṇeva naur jale ||
children.translated_text: it wanders in battles like a boat in water with its helmsman lost.
But this army is unconfused, undisturbed, and full of force;

children.text: senā rakṣati kākutsthau māyayā nirjitau raṇe ||
children.translated_text: it protects the two <s>Kākutsthas</s>, who have been overcome by illusion in battle.

children.text: sā tvaṃ bhava suvisrabdhā anumānaiḥ sukhodayaiḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore be quite confident, from these happy signs;

children.text: ahatau paśya kākutsthau snehād etad bravīmi te ||
children.translated_text: see that the two <s>Kākutsthas</s> are unhurt. Out of affection I say this to you.

children.text: anṛtaṃ noktapūrvaṃ me na ca vakṣye kadācana
children.translated_text: I have never before spoken an untruth, nor shall I ever speak one.
Because of the happiness and goodness of your character, you have entered my heart.

children.text: nemau śakyau raṇe jetuṃ sendrair api surāsuraiḥ
children.translated_text: These two cannot be conquered in battle even by gods and asuras together with <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: etayor ānanaṃ dṛṣṭvā mayā cāveditaṃ tava ||
children.translated_text: Having seen their faces, I have made this known to you.

children.text: idaṃ ca sumahaccihnaṃ śanaiḥ paśyasva maithili
children.translated_text: And this is a very great sign; look carefully, <s>Maithilī</s>:
although both of them are unconscious, their splendor has not departed at all.
Usually, when men have lost their strength and their life is gone,
a supreme distortion appears in their visible faces.

children.text: tyaja śokaṃ ca duḥkhaṃ ca mohaṃ ca janakātmaje
children.translated_text: Abandon grief, pain, and delusion, daughter of <s>Janaka</s>;
as for <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, they cannot be lifeless today.'

children.text: śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tasyāḥ sītā surasutopamā
children.translated_text: Having heard her words, <s>Sītā</s>, like a daughter of the gods,
joined her palms and said, 'May it be so,' she, the <s>Maithilī</s>.

children.text: vimānaṃ puṣpakaṃ tat tu saṃnivartya manojavam
children.translated_text: Then that aerial car <s>Puṣpaka</s>, swift as thought, was turned back,

children.text: dīnā trijaṭayā sītā laṅkām eva praveśitā ||
children.translated_text: and the wretched <s>Sītā</s>, accompanied by <s>Trijaṭā</s>, was brought back into <s>Laṅkā</s> itself.
Then, descending from <s>Puṣpaka</s> together with <s>Trijaṭā</s>,
she was led by the <s>rākṣasīs</s> into the <s>Aśokavanikā</s> itself.

children.text: praviśya sītā bahuvṛkṣaṣaṇḍāṃ tāṃ rākṣasendrasya vihārabhūmim
children.translated_text: Entering that grove with its many clusters of trees, the pleasure-ground of the lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: samprekṣya saṃcintya ca rājaputrau paraṃ viṣādaṃ samupājagāma ||
children.translated_text: and looking about and thinking of the two princes, <s>Sītā</s> fell into deepest despair.
The two sons of <s>Daśaratha</s> were bound by a terrible mass of arrows,
lying there covered with blood, breathing like serpents.
All those foremost <s>vānaras</s>, together with mighty <s>Sugrīva</s>,
stood around the two great-souled ones, overwhelmed with grief.
At that moment heroic <s>Rāma</s> regained consciousness,
because of his firmness and strength of spirit, though he was bound fast by arrows.

children.text: tato dṛṣṭvā sarudhiraṃ viṣaṇṇaṃ gāḍham arpitam
children.translated_text: Then, seeing his brother bloody, despondent, and deeply pierced,
with a wretched face, he lamented in anguish.

children.text: kiṃ nu me sītayā kāryaṃ kiṃ kāryaṃ jīvitena vā
children.translated_text: What use have I for <s>Sītā</s>, or what use for life,

children.text: śayānaṃ yo 'dya paśyāmi bhrātaraṃ yudhi nirjitam ||
children.translated_text: when today I see my brother lying defeated in battle?

children.text: śakyā sītāsamā nārī prāptuṃ loke vicinvatā
children.translated_text: A woman equal to <s>Sītā</s> may be found in the world by one who searches,
but there is no brother equal to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, no counselor for a crisis.
I shall give up my life while the <s>vānaras</s> look on,
if the increaser of <s>Sumitrā</s>'s joy has passed into the five elements.

children.text: kiṃ nu vakṣyāmi kausalyāṃ mātaraṃ kiṃ nu kaikayīm
children.translated_text: What shall I say to my mother <s>Kauśalyā</s>, and what to <s>Kaikeyī</s>?
And how shall I speak to mother <s>Sumitrā</s>, longing for the sight of her son?

children.text: vivatsāṃ vepamānāṃ ca krośantīṃ kurarīm iva
children.translated_text: Bereft of her child, trembling, crying out like a kurarī bird,

children.text: katham āśvāsayiṣyāmi yadi yāsyāmi taṃ vinā ||
children.translated_text: how shall I console her if I return without him?

children.text: kathaṃ vakṣyāmi śatrughnaṃ bharataṃ ca yaśasvinam
children.translated_text: How shall I tell glorious <s>Śatrughna</s> and <s>Bharata</s>

children.text: mayā saha vanaṃ yāto vinā tenāgataḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that he went to the forest with me, but I have come back without him?

children.text: upālambhaṃ na śakṣyāmi soḍhuṃ bata sumitrayā
children.translated_text: I shall not be able to endure reproach from <s>Sumitrā</s>; alas,

children.text: ihaiva dehaṃ tyakṣyāmi na hi jīvitum utsahe ||
children.translated_text: I shall give up my body here itself, for I cannot bear to live.

children.text: dhiṅ māṃ duṣkṛtakarmāṇam anāryaṃ yatkṛte hyasau
children.translated_text: Shame on me, evil in deed and ignoble, for whose sake this
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> lies fallen on a bed of arrows, as if his life-breath were gone.

children.text: tvaṃ nityaṃ suviṣaṇṇaṃ mām āśvāsayasi lakṣmaṇa
children.translated_text: You always used to console me when I was deeply despondent, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: gatāsur nādya śaknoṣi mām ārtam abhibhāṣitum ||
children.translated_text: Now, as if lifeless, you cannot speak to me in my distress.

children.text: yenādya bahavo yuddhe rākṣasā nihatāḥ kṣitau
children.translated_text: He by whom many <s>rākṣasas</s> were today slain on the ground in battle,

children.text: tasyām eva kṣitau vīraḥ sa śete nihataḥ paraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: that hero himself lies on that very ground, struck down by enemies,
lying on this bed of arrows, drenched with his own blood.
Covered with nets of arrows, he shines like the sun going to its setting.
Because his vital parts have been struck by arrows, he is unable to look up;
and the redness of his eyes reveals the pain of him as he cannot speak.

children.text: yathaiva māṃ vanaṃ yāntam anuyāto mahādyutiḥ
children.translated_text: Just as this greatly radiant one followed me when I was going to the forest,
so I too shall follow him to the abode of <s>Yama</s>.

children.text: iṣṭabandhujano nityaṃ māṃ ca nityam anuvrataḥ
children.translated_text: Always devoted to his beloved kinsmen and constantly faithful to me,
he has today come to this state through the bad policy of me, ignoble as I am.
I do not remember that the heroic <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, even when deeply angered,

children.text: paruṣaṃ vipriyaṃ vāpi śrāvitaṃ na kadācana ||
children.translated_text: ever made me hear a harsh or displeasing word.
He who released five hundred arrows with a single impulse,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> is superior to him and even to <s>Kārtavīrya</s> in the science of archery.
He who could strike down even the great-souled <s>Śakra</s>'s weapons with weapons,
that very one lies slain upon the earth, though fit for a costly bed.

children.text: tacca mithyā pralaptaṃ māṃ pradhakṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: And that empty utterance of mine will burn me, without doubt:

children.text: yanmayā na kṛto rājā rākṣasānāṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> was not made king of the <s>rākṣasas</s> by me.
At this moment, <s>Sugrīva</s>, you should return from here.

children.text: matvā hīnaṃ mayā rājan rāvaṇo 'bhidraved balī ||
children.translated_text: Thinking me bereft, O king, the mighty <s>Rāvaṇa</s> will attack.
Putting <s>Aṅgada</s> in front, together with your army and your friends,
cross the ocean, <s>Sugrīva</s>, again by that very bridge.

children.text: kṛtaṃ hanumatā kāryaṃ yad anyair duṣkaraṃ raṇe
children.translated_text: The deed that was hard for others to do in battle has been done by <s>Hanumat</s>;
and I am pleased with the king of the bears and with the lord of the <s>golāṅgūlas</s>.

children.text: aṅgadena kṛtaṃ karma maindena dvividena ca
children.translated_text: The deed has been done by <s>Aṅgada</s>, and by <s>Mainda</s> and <s>Dvivida</s>;

children.text: yuddhaṃ kesariṇā saṃkhye ghoraṃ saṃpātinā kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: a terrible battle has been fought in combat by <s>Kesarī</s> and <s>Saṃpāti</s>.
And by <s>Gavaya</s>, <s>Gavākṣa</s>, <s>Śarabha</s>, and <s>Gaja</s>,
and by other monkeys who abandoned their lives for my sake, battle has been fought.

children.text: na cātikramituṃ śakyaṃ daivaṃ sugrīva mānuṣaiḥ
children.translated_text: Fate, <s>Sugrīva</s>, cannot be overstepped by human beings.

children.text: yat tu śakyaṃ vayasyena suhṛdā vā paraṃtapa
children.translated_text: But whatever can be done by a companion or a friend, O scorcher of foes,
all that has been done by you, <s>Sugrīva</s>, who fear <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness).
This service to a friend has been done by you, O bulls among monkeys.

children.text: anujñātā mayā sarve yatheṣṭaṃ gantum arhatha ||
children.translated_text: All of you, with my permission, may go as you wish.
All those monkeys heard his lamentation,
and shed tears from their black-and-white eyes.
Then, after stationing all the armies, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,
club in hand, hurried to the place where <s>Rāghava</s> was.
Seeing him coming swiftly, like a mass of dark collyrium,
all the monkeys fled, thinking he was <s>Rāvaṇi</s>.
Then the greatly radiant and mighty king of the monkeys said,

children.text: kim iyaṃ vyathitā senā mūḍhavāteva naur jale ||
children.translated_text: Why is this army distressed, like a bewildered boat in the water?
Hearing <s>Sugrīva</s>'s words, <s>Aṅgada</s>, the son of <s>Vālin</s>, said,

children.text: na tvaṃ paśyasi rāmaṃ ca lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahābalam ||
children.translated_text: Do you not see mighty <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>?
The two heroic sons of <s>Daśaratha</s> are covered with a mass of arrows,
the two great-souled ones lying on a bed of arrows, sprinkled with blood.
Then <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of monkeys, said to his son <s>Aṅgada</s>,

children.text: nānimittam idaṃ manye bhavitavyaṃ bhayena tu ||
children.translated_text: I do not think this is without cause; rather, it must be because of fear.
For these monkeys, their faces despondent and their weapons abandoned,
are fleeing in all directions from terror, their eyes wide open.

children.text: anyonyasya na lajjante na nirīkṣanti pṛṣṭhataḥ
children.translated_text: They feel no shame before one another and do not look back;
they drag one another away and leap over those who have fallen.
Meanwhile the hero <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, club in hand,
greeted <s>Sugrīva</s> and looked upon <s>Rāghava</s>.
Seeing that <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, terrifying to the monkeys,
<s>Sugrīva</s> spoke to the nearby king of the bears, <s>Jāmbavat</s>:
This is <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> who has arrived; seeing him, O bull among monkeys,
the monkeys run away in terror, suspecting him to be the son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Quickly steady these greatly frightened ones, who have scattered in many directions,
and tell them that <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> has arrived.
Thus addressed by <s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>Jāmbavān</s>, the bear-king,
comforted the monkeys and turned back those who were running away.
Then all the monkeys turned back again, their panic gone,

children.text: ṛkṣarājavacaḥ śrutvā taṃ ca dṛṣṭvā vibhīṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: when they heard the words of the bear-king and saw <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>.
But righteous <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, seeing <s>Rāma</s>'s body covered with arrows,
and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s as well, became shaken in his senses.

children.text: jalaklinnena hastena tayor netre pramṛjya ca
children.translated_text: Wiping the eyes of the two with a hand wet with water,
his mind oppressed by grief, he wept and lamented.
These two, endowed with strength, heroic, and dear to battle,
have been brought to this state by <s>rākṣasas</s> who fight by deceit.

children.text: bhrātuḥ putreṇa me tena duṣputreṇa durātmanā
children.translated_text: By that son of my brother, a bad son and evil-minded,
with crooked <s>rākṣasa</s> intelligence, these two of straightforward valor have been deceived.
These two, pierced all over with arrows and soaked with blood,
are seen sleeping on the earth like two porcupines.

children.text: yayor vīryam upāśritya pratiṣṭhā kāṅkṣitā mayā
children.translated_text: Relying on the valor of those two, I desired secure establishment;
those two bulls among men are now both asleep, to the destruction of my body.
Though living today, I am ruined, my hope for kingship destroyed;
and the enemy <s>Rāvaṇa</s> has achieved his vow and been made one whose desire is fulfilled.
As he was lamenting in this way, <s>Sugrīva</s>, endowed with strength,
embraced <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, and the monkey-king said this:

children.text: rājyaṃ prāpsyasi dharmajña laṅkāyāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: You will obtain the kingdom in <s>Laṅkā</s>, O knower of <s>dharma</s>; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: rāvaṇaḥ saha putreṇa sa rājyaṃ neha lapsyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, together with his son, will not obtain the kingdom here.
These two, <s>Rāghava</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, though pressed hard by arrows,

children.text: tyaktvā mohaṃ vadhiṣyete sagaṇaṃ rāvaṇaṃ raṇe ||
children.translated_text: will cast off their stupor and slay <s>Rāvaṇa</s> with his troops in battle.

children.text: tam evaṃ sāntvayitvā tu samāśvāsya ca rākṣasam
children.translated_text: Having thus comforted and reassured that <s>rākṣasa</s>,

children.text: suṣeṇaṃ śvaśuraṃ pārśve sugrīvastam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s> then spoke to <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, his father-in-law, who was at his side.
Together with brave companies of monkeys, when the two subduers of foes have regained consciousness,

children.text: gaccha tvaṃ bhrātarau gṛhya kiṣkindhāṃ rāmalakṣmaṇau ||
children.translated_text: go, taking the brothers <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, to <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>.

children.text: ahaṃ tu rāvaṇaṃ hatvā saputraṃ sahabāndhavam
children.translated_text: But I, after killing <s>Rāvaṇa</s> with his son and kinsmen,

children.text: maithilīm ānayiṣyāmi śakro naṣṭām iva śriyam ||
children.translated_text: will bring back <s>Maithilī</s>, as <s>Śakra</s> brought back lost prosperity.
Hearing this speech of the lord of the monkeys, <s>Suṣeṇa</s> said:
A very terrible great war between the gods and the asuras was once experienced.
Then the dānavas, skilled in the touch of arrows,
kept striking down the gods, who were skilled in weapons, covering them again and again.
Those who were afflicted, unconscious, and bereft of life, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>
treated with sciences joined to mantras and with herbs.
To bring those herbs, let the monkeys go swiftly and quickly
to the ocean <s>Kṣīroda</s>, <s>Sampāti</s>, <s>Panasa</s>, and the others.
For the monkeys know those two great herbs on the mountain,
the divine <s>Saṃjīvakaraṇī</s> and <s>Viśalyā</s>, fashioned by the gods.
The mountains named <s>Candra</s> and <s>Droṇa</s> stand in the excellent ocean,

children.text: amṛtaṃ yatra mathitaṃ tatra te paramauṣadhī ||
children.translated_text: where the nectar was churned; there are those supreme herbs.

children.text: te tatra nihite devaiḥ parvate paramauṣadhī
children.translated_text: Since those two supreme herbs were placed there on the mountain by the gods,
let this son of <s>Vāyu</s>, O king, <s>Hanūmān</s>, go there.
At that moment the wind, driving along clouds with lightning,

children.text: paryasyan sāgare toyaṃ kampayann iva parvatān ||
children.translated_text: and scattering water upon the ocean, seemed to shake the mountains.
By the mighty wind of his wings, all the great trees of the islands
fell into the salt water, their branches broken and their roots torn up.
The serpents dwelling there, the hooded ones, became terrified,
and all the aquatic creatures quickly fled through the salt ocean.
Then, after a moment, all the monkeys saw <s>Garuḍa</s>, <s>Vainateya</s>, mighty in strength,

children.text: vānarā dadṛśuḥ sarve jvalantam iva pāvakam ||
children.translated_text: blazing like fire.
Seeing him arrive, those nāgas fled in all directions,
by whom, in the form of arrows, those two mighty noble men had been bound.

children.text: tataḥ suparṇaḥ kākutsthau dṛṣṭvā pratyabhinandya ca
children.translated_text: Then <s>Suparṇa</s>, seeing the two <s>Kākutsthas</s> and greeting them,
stroked with his hands their faces, which shone like the moon.
When the two were touched by <s>Vainateya</s>, their wounds healed,

children.text: suvarṇe ca tanū snigdhe tayor āśu babhūvatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: and their bodies quickly became golden-hued and smooth.

children.text: tejo vīryaṃ balaṃ cauja utsāhaśca mahāguṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Their splendor, prowess, strength, energy, courage, and great qualities,

children.text: pradarśanaṃ ca buddhiśca smṛtiśca dviguṇaṃ tayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: and their beauty, intelligence, and memory became twice as great.
Raising up the two great heroes, <s>Garuḍa</s>, equal to <s>Vāsava</s>,

children.text: ubhau tau sasvaje hṛṣṭau rāmaścainam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: embraced them both with delight; and <s>Rāma</s> said to him:
Through your favor, the great calamity caused by <s>Rāvaṇi</s>

children.text: āvām iha vyatikrāntau śīghraṃ ca balinau kṛtau ||
children.translated_text: has been overcome by us here, and we have quickly been made strong.

children.text: yathā tātaṃ daśarathaṃ yathājaṃ ca pitāmaham
children.translated_text: As when I meet father <s>Daśaratha</s> or grandfather <s>Aja</s>,

children.text: tathā bhavantam āsādya hṛdayaṃ me prasīdati ||
children.translated_text: so, on coming to you, my heart is pleased.
Who are you, endowed with beauty, wearing divine garlands and unguents,
clothed in stainless garments and adorned with divine ornaments?
Then <s>Vainateya</s>, great in splendor and mighty in strength,
the king of birds, joyful in spirit, his eyes overwhelmed with delight, said to him:

children.text: ahaṃ sakhā te kākutstha priyaḥ prāṇo bahiścaraḥ
children.translated_text: I am your friend, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, dear to you, your life moving outside your body;
<s>Garutmān</s> has come here to help you both.

children.text: asurā vā mahāvīryā dānavā vā mahābalāḥ
children.translated_text: Neither asuras of great prowess nor dānavas of great strength,
nor even the gods together with the gandharvas, with <s>Śatakratu</s> before them,
would be able to release this very terrible arrow-bond,
created by the power of illusion by cruel-working <s>Indrajit</s>.
These are nāgas, sons of <s>Kadrū</s>, sharp-fanged and terrible with poison,
who, through the power of <s>rākṣasa</s> magic, became arrows and attached themselves to you.
You are fortunate, O <s>Rāma</s>, knower of <s>dharma</s>, whose valor is true,
together with your brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the slayer of enemies in battle.

children.text: imaṃ śrutvā tu vṛttāntaṃ tvaramāṇo 'ham āgataḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing of this event, I came in haste,
suddenly, out of affection for you both and in keeping with our friendship.
You two have been released from this extremely dreadful bond of arrows,

children.text: apramādaśca kartavyo yuvābhyāṃ nityam eva hi ||
children.translated_text: but vigilance must always be exercised by you both.
By nature all <s>rākṣasas</s> are deceitful fighters in battle;
for heroes of pure intention such as you, straightforwardness is strength.
Therefore you must not trust the <s>rākṣasas</s> on the battlefield;
from this very example, the <s>rākṣasas</s> are always crooked.

children.text: evam uktvā tato rāmaṃ suparṇaḥ sumahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken to <s>Rāma</s>, the very mighty <s>Suparṇa</s>
embraced him with friendly affection and began to take leave.

children.text: sakhe rāghava dharmajña ripūṇām api vatsala
children.translated_text: Friend <s>Rāghava</s>, knower of <s>dharma</s>, kind even to enemies,
I wish to be permitted; I shall go as I came.
After making <s>Laṅkā</s>, by waves of arrows, a city with only children and old men left,

children.text: rāvaṇaṃ ca ripuṃ hatvā sītāṃ samupalapsyase ||
children.translated_text: and after killing your enemy <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, you will regain <s>Sītā</s>.
Having spoken this speech, swift-striding <s>Suparṇa</s>,

children.text: rāmaṃ ca virujaṃ kṛtvā madhye teṣāṃ vanaukasām ||
children.translated_text: after making <s>Rāma</s> free from wounds in the midst of those forest-dwellers,

children.text: pradakṣiṇaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā pariṣvajya ca vīryavān
children.translated_text: then circumambulated him and, valiant as he was, embraced him,
entered the sky and went away like the wind.
Then, seeing the two <s>Rāghavas</s> free from injury, the vānaras' troop-leaders
roared lion-roars and shook their tails.
Then they beat the kettledrums and sounded the mṛdaṅgas;
delighted, they blew conches and also shouted as before.
The valiant vānaras, warriors with trees, slapped their arms again and again,
and, having uprooted many kinds of trees, stood there by the hundreds of thousands.
Sending forth great cries and frightening the night-roamers,
the leaping vānaras, eager to fight, approached the gates of <s>Laṅkā</s>.
Then a fearful, tumultuous roar arose from the troop-leaders of the branch-roaming vānaras,

children.text: kṣaye nidāghasya yathā ghanānāṃ nādaḥ subhīmo nadatāṃ niśīthe ||
children.translated_text: like the exceedingly terrible sound of clouds thundering at midnight at the end of the hot season.
At that time <s>Rāvaṇa</s> heard the very tumultuous sound

children.text: nardatāṃ rākṣasaiḥ sārdhaṃ tadā śuśrāva rāvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: of those forceful vānaras roaring together with the rākṣasas.
Hearing that smooth, deep resonance very clearly,
he then spoke these words in the midst of those ministers:
"Since this very great roar has arisen from the delighted vānaras,
from many of them, like the roaring of thunderclouds,

children.text: vyaktaṃ sumahatī prītir eteṣāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: clearly there is very great joy among them; there is no doubt about this.
For the abode of <s>Varuṇa</s>, the ocean, is shaken by their vast cries.

children.text: tau tu baddhau śaraistīkṣṇair bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
children.translated_text: But those two brothers, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, were bound by sharp arrows,

children.text: ayaṃ ca sumahān nādaḥ śaṅkāṃ janayatīva me ||
children.translated_text: and this very great roar seems to raise a suspicion in me."

children.text: etat tu vacanaṃ coktvā mantriṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken these words, the lord of the rākṣasas
addressed the nearby rākṣasas who were moving about there:
"Quickly find out the cause of joy that has arisen
among all these forest-roamers at a time when grief should have come upon them."
Thus instructed by him, they climbed the rampart in alarm
and saw the army protected by great-souled <s>Sugrīva</s>.

children.text: tau ca muktau sughoreṇa śarabandhena rāghavau
children.translated_text: Seeing the two <s>Rāghavas</s> freed from the very terrible bond of arrows,
risen up and greatly blessed, the rākṣasas sank into despair.
All of them, with terrified hearts, descended from the rampart;
all with dejected faces, they came before the lord of rākṣasas.
Those night-roamers, downcast in face, reported to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>
that whole unwelcome matter exactly, being skilled in speech:
"Those two brothers, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, whom <s>Indrajit</s> in battle
bound with a bond of arrows and made motionless in their arms,
are seen freed from the arrow-bond in the battlefield,
like two elephants that have cut their nooses, equal in valor to lordly elephants."
Hearing their speech, the mighty lord of the rākṣasas,
overcome by anxiety and grief, spoke with a dejected face:
"They were bound in battle by <s>Indrajit</s> after being struck down with dreadful, boon-given arrows
that were like venomous serpents, unfailing, and shining like the sun.

children.text: tam astrabandham āsādya yadi muktau ripū mama
children.translated_text: If my enemies have escaped after coming under that weapon-bond,
I see this whole army of mine as standing in uncertainty.
Surely the arrows with the splendor of <s>Vāsuki</s> have become fruitless,

children.text: ādattaṃ yaistu saṃgrāme ripūṇāṃ mama jīvitam ||
children.translated_text: those by which the life of my enemies was seized in battle."

children.text: evam uktvā tu saṃkruddho niśvasann urago yathā
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, enraged and breathing like a serpent,

children.text: abravīd rakṣasāṃ madhye dhūmrākṣaṃ nāma rākṣasam ||
children.translated_text: he spoke among the rākṣasas to a rākṣasa named <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>:
"Joined with a great force of rākṣasas of dreadful deeds,
go forth for the killing of <s>Rāma</s> together with the vānaras."
Thus addressed by the wise lord of rākṣasas, <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>
made obeisance and, delighted, went out from the king's palace.
Having gone out through that gate, he said to the commander of the forces:

children.text: tvarayasva balaṃ tūrṇaṃ kiṃ cireṇa yuyutsataḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Hasten the army quickly. Why delay, when they are eager to fight?"
Hearing <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>'s words, the commander, accompanied by the troops,
quickly mobilized the army at <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s command.
Those strong, dreadful-looking night-roamers, with bells fastened on them,
roaring and delighted, surrounded <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>.
With many kinds of weapons in hand, holding spears and maces,

children.text: gadābhiḥ paṭṭasair daṇḍair āyasair musalair bhṛśam ||
children.translated_text: and with clubs, paṭṭisas, iron staffs, and pestles in abundance,
with iron bars, bhiṇḍipālas, javelins, darts, and battle-axes,

children.text: niryayū rākṣasā ghorā nardanto jaladā yathā ||
children.translated_text: the dreadful rākṣasas went forth roaring like clouds.
Others, armored and mounted on chariots adorned with banners
and fitted with golden latticework, went out with asses of many faces.
With exceedingly swift horses and with lordly elephants furious in rut,
the tiger-like rākṣasas went out, hard to assail, like tigers.
<s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>, whose sound was like that of an ass, mounted a divine chariot
yoked with asses that had faces like wolves and lions and were adorned with gold.

children.text: sa niryāto mahāvīryo dhūmrākṣo rākṣasair vṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: That very mighty <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>, surrounded by rākṣasas, went out,
laughing, toward the western gate, where <s>Hanūmān</s> was troop-leader.
As the very terrible rākṣasa of frightful appearance advanced,
cruel birds moving through the sky barred his way.
A very dreadful vulture fell upon the top of his chariot,
and corpse-eating birds, entangled at the tip of the banner, fell down.

children.text: rudhirārdro mahāñ śvetaḥ kabandhaḥ patito bhuvi
children.translated_text: A huge, pale, blood-wet headless trunk fell upon the ground,
uttering a harsh, discordant cry near <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>.

children.text: vavarṣa rudhiraṃ devaḥ saṃcacāla ca medinī
children.translated_text: The sky rained blood, and the earth shook.
The wind blew against them, with a sound like thunderbolts.
There the quarters, covered by masses of darkness, did not shine.
Then, seeing those portents, terrifying to the rākṣasas,
and very dreadful as they appeared, <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s> became distressed.

children.text: tataḥ subhīmo bahubhir niśācarair vṛto 'bhiniṣkramya raṇotsuko balī
children.translated_text: Then, very fearsome, surrounded by many night-wanderers, mighty and eager for battle, he went out

children.text: dadarśa tāṃ rāghavabāhupālitāṃ samudrakalpāṃ bahuvānarīṃ camūm ||
children.translated_text: and saw that vast army of many vānaras, like the ocean and protected by <s>Rāghava</s>'s arm.
Seeing <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>, the rākṣasa of dreadful roar, coming forth,
all the vānaras roared, delighted and longing for battle.

children.text: teṣāṃ tu tumulaṃ yuddhaṃ saṃjajñe harirakṣasām
children.translated_text: Then there arose a tumultuous battle between the vānaras and rākṣasas,
as they struck one another with dreadful trees, spears, and clubs.
The dreadful vānaras were cut down all around by the rākṣasas,
and the rākṣasas too were leveled to the ground by the vānaras with trees.
The enraged rākṣasas, with sharp arrows,
pierced the vānaras with dreadful-looking, straight shafts feathered with kaṅka-plumes.
With frightful maces, paṭṭasas, spiked clubs,
dreadful iron bars of many kinds, and sharpened tridents,
those mighty vānaras, being torn apart by the rākṣasas,
roused to exultation by anger, performed deeds as if fearless.
Though their bodies were split by arrows and their limbs pierced by spears,
the leaders of the vānara troops seized trees and rocks there.
Those terrifying vānaras, rushing with fearful speed and roaring on every side,
crushed the fearsome rākṣasas and shouted out their names.
That wondrous, dreadful battle of the vānaras and rākṣasas took place,
with various rocks and many-branched trees.
Some rākṣasas were crushed by the vānaras, who shone in victory,
and some of the blood-eating ones poured blood from their mouths.

children.text: pārśveṣu dāritāḥ kecit kecid rāśīkṛtā drumaiḥ
children.translated_text: Some were split open in their sides; some were heaped up by trees.
Some were crushed by rocks, and some were torn apart with teeth.
With standards battered and broken, with donkeys fallen down,
with chariots shattered, and with night-wanderers fallen,
the rākṣasas, by the vānaras of dreadful prowess as they leapt again and again in their speed,
were slashed on their faces with sharp nails.
Their faces discolored and their hair scattered loose,
stupefied by the smell of blood, they fell upon the surface of the earth.
But other rākṣasas, greatly enraged and of dreadful valor,
rushed at the vānaras with their palms alone, equal in touch to thunderbolts.
As they charged, they were outsped by the still swifter vānaras
and were battered with fists, feet, teeth, and trees.

children.text: sainyaṃ tu vidrutaṃ dṛṣṭvā dhūmrākṣo rākṣasarṣabhaḥ
children.translated_text: But seeing his army routed, <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>, bull among rākṣasas,
in anger wrought slaughter among the vānaras who wished to fight.
Some vānaras, streaming blood, were crushed by prāsas,
and some, struck by clubs, fell on the surface of the earth.
Some were crushed by iron bars and torn open by bhiṇḍipālas,
and some, struck by paṭṭasas, reeled and lost their lives.
Some forest-dwellers were slain on the ground, soaked with blood,

children.text: kecid vidrāvitā naṣṭāḥ saṃkruddhai rākṣasair yudhi ||
children.translated_text: and some were driven away and fled in battle by the enraged rākṣasas.
Some, their hearts split open, lay on one side,
and some, torn by tridents, had their entrails spilled out.
That very dreadful, great battle, thronged with vānaras and rākṣasas,
full of weapons and crowded with rocks and trees, shone forth.
Its sweet music was the twanging string of bow-cords, accompanied by the rhythm of hiccuping gasps,
and with deep thunder as song, it appeared as a battle-gāndharva.
But <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>, bow in hand, at the front of battle,
laughing, drove those vānaras in all directions with showers of arrows.
Seeing the army tormented and shaken by <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>, <s>Māruti</s>
turned upon him in anger, seizing a huge rock.
His eyes doubly copper-red from wrath, and his valor equal to his father's,

children.text: śilāṃ tāṃ pātayāmāsa dhūmrākṣasya rathaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: he hurled that rock at <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>'s chariot.

children.text: āpatantīṃ śilāṃ dṛṣṭvā gadām udyamya saṃbhramāt
children.translated_text: Seeing the rock falling toward him, he raised his mace in alarm,
leapt swiftly from the chariot, and stood upon the earth.

children.text: sā pramathya rathaṃ tasya nipapāta śilā bhuvi
children.translated_text: That rock, after smashing his chariot, fell upon the ground,
with its wheels and yoke, its horses, its standard, and its bow.

children.text: sa bhaṅktvā tu rathaṃ tasya hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: After breaking his chariot, <s>Hanūmān</s>, son of the Wind,
wrought slaughter among the rākṣasas with trees bearing trunks and branches.
The rākṣasas, their heads split open and sprinkled with blood,
and others crushed by trees, fell upon the surface of the earth.
Having routed the rākṣasa army, <s>Hanūmān</s>, son of the Wind,
took up a mountain peak and rushed upon <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>.

children.text: tam āpatantaṃ dhūmrākṣo gadām udyamya vīryavān
children.translated_text: As he came rushing on, the valiant <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>, raising his mace,
roared aloud and suddenly ran at <s>Hanūmān</s>.

children.text: tataḥ kruddhastu vegena gadāṃ tāṃ bahukaṇṭakām
children.translated_text: Then the enraged <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>, with force,
brought that many-spiked mace down upon <s>Hanūmān</s>'s head.

children.text: tāḍitaḥ sa tayā tatra gadayā bhīmarūpayā
children.translated_text: Struck there by that mace of dreadful form,
that monkey, possessing the Wind's strength, paid no heed to the blow.
he hurled a mountain peak onto the middle of <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>'s head.
Struck by the mountain peak, with all his limbs bewildered,

children.text: papāta sahasā bhūmau vikīrṇa iva parvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: he suddenly fell to the ground like a mountain scattered apart.
Seeing <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s> slain, the remaining night-roamers,
terrified and being struck down by the monkeys, entered <s>Laṅkā</s>.

children.text: sa tu pavanasuto nihatya śatruṃ kṣatajavahāḥ saritaśca saṃvikīrya
children.translated_text: But the son of the Wind, having slain the enemy and scattered rivers bearing streams of blood,

children.text: ripuvadhajanitaśramo mahātmā mudam agamat kapibhiśca pūjyamānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that great-souled one, wearied by the slaughter of the foe, rejoiced as he was honored by the monkeys.
Hearing that <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s> had been killed, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas,
spoke these words to the commander of the army, who stood before him with joined palms:
Let the unconquerable rākṣasas of terrible valor quickly march out,
placing <s>Akampana</s>, skilled in every weapon, at their head.
Then the chief rākṣasas, bearing many kinds of weapons, fierce-eyed and terrible to behold,
rushed out, urged on by the commander of the army.
Mounting a huge chariot, wearing earrings of refined gold,
then <s>Akampana</s> went forth, surrounded by dreadful rākṣasas.

children.text: na hi kampayituṃ śakyaḥ surair api mahāmṛdhe
children.translated_text: For even the gods could not shake him in a great battle;
therefore he was <s>Akampana</s>, Unshakable, among them, like the sun in splendor.
As he was rushing forward, inflamed with eagerness to fight,
suddenly dejection came upon the horses that drew his chariot.
The left eye of that lover of battle throbbed,
the color of his face turned pale, and his voice became choked.
Even on a fair day there arose foul weather with a harsh wind,

children.text: ūcuḥ khagā mṛgāḥ sarve vācaḥ krūrā bhayāvahāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and all the birds and beasts uttered cruel, fearsome cries.
He, whose shoulders were full like a lion's and whose valor was equal to a tiger's,
paid no heed to those portents and went out to the battlefield.
Then, as that rākṣasa went forth together with the rākṣasas,
there arose a very great roar, as if shaking the ocean.
Terrified by that sound, the great army of monkeys,
armed with trees and rocks, stood ready to fight.
A battle of great ferocity arose between the monkeys and rākṣasas,
who had all but abandoned their lives for the sake of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
All were exceedingly strong heroes, all like mountains,
the monkeys and the rākṣasas alike, eager to kill one another.
As they roared in battle, those of tremendous speed,
a very great sound was heard from their wrathful bellowing at one another.
Dust, red in hue, became exceedingly frightful,
raised up by the monkeys and rākṣasas, and it blocked all ten directions.
Covered by that dust, pale like shaken silk,

children.text: saṃvṛtāni ca bhūtāni dadṛśur na raṇājire ||
children.translated_text: the beings in the battlefield did not see one another.

children.text: na dhvajo na patākā vā varma vā turago 'pi vā
children.translated_text: Neither standard nor banner, nor armor, nor even horse,

children.text: āyudhaṃ syandanaṃ vāpi dadṛśe tena reṇunā ||
children.translated_text: nor weapon nor chariot could be seen because of that dust.
A very great noise of them roaring and charging

children.text: śrūyate tumule yuddhe na rūpāṇi cakāśire ||
children.translated_text: was heard in the tumultuous battle, but their forms did not appear.

children.text: harīn eva susaṃkruddhā harayo jaghnur āhave
children.translated_text: In the clash, the monkeys, greatly enraged, struck down monkeys themselves,
and the rākṣasas too slew rākṣasas in that darkness.
Killing both others and their own, the monkeys and rākṣasas
then made the earth wet with blood and smeared with mire.
Then the dust, sprinkled by the flood of blood, disappeared,
and the earth became strewn with bodies and corpses.
With trees, spears, stones, lances, maces, iron clubs, and javelins,
the monkeys and rākṣasas swiftly struck one another with force.
Fighting with arms shaped like iron clubs, mountain-like,
the monkeys of terrible deeds struck down the rākṣasas in battle.
The rākṣasas too, enraged and holding lances and javelins in their hands,
there slew the monkeys with weapons of extreme cruelty.
But the monkeys also, with great trees and great stones,
charged forward and tore apart the rākṣasas, snatching away their weapons by their valor.

children.text: etasminn antare vīrā harayaḥ kumudo nalaḥ
children.translated_text: At that moment the heroic monkeys <s>Kumuda</s>, <s>Nala</s>,
and <s>Mainda</s>, extremely enraged, put forth unsurpassed speed.

children.text: te tu vṛkṣair mahāvegā rākṣasānāṃ camūmukhe
children.translated_text: Those monkey chiefs, of great speed, with trees in the front of the rākṣasa army,
made a very great slaughter with ease.

children.text: tad dṛṣṭvā sumahat karma kṛtaṃ vānarasattamaiḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that very great deed done by the best of the monkeys,
<s>Akampana</s> summoned up fierce anger in battle.
His form overcome by anger, brandishing his excellent bow,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tu karma śatrūṇāṃ sārathiṃ vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: and seeing the action of his enemies, he spoke a sentence to his charioteer:

children.text: tatraiva tāvat tvaritaṃ rathaṃ prāpaya sārathe
children.translated_text: Drive the chariot there at once, quickly, O charioteer;

children.text: ete 'tra bahavo ghnanti subahūn rākṣasān raṇe ||
children.translated_text: for here these many are killing very many rākṣasas in battle.
Here these mighty monkeys, with terrible bodies,
armed with trees and rocks, stand before me.
I wish to kill them; for I am one who takes pride in battle.

children.text: etaiḥ pramathitaṃ sarvaṃ dṛśyate rākṣasaṃ balam ||
children.translated_text: All the rākṣasa army is seen to have been crushed by them.
Then the best of chariot-warriors, in a chariot with fast-running horses,
<s>Akampana</s> struck the monkeys in anger with nets of arrows.

children.text: na sthātuṃ vānarāḥ śekuḥ kiṃ punar yoddhum āhave
children.translated_text: The monkeys could not stand firm; how much less could they fight in battle?
Broken by <s>Akampana</s>'s arrows, every one of them fled away.
Those who had fallen under the sway of death and come under <s>Akampana</s>'s power
Having looked over his kinsmen, mighty <s>Hanumān</s> took his stand near them.
Seeing that great leaping monkey, all the leaders of the monkey troops
came together in the battle, and the heroes surrounded him in a body.
When those leaders of the monkey troops saw <s>Hanumān</s> standing firm,
they became strong indeed, for they had taken refuge with one who was strong.
But <s>Akampana</s>, seeing <s>Hanumān</s> standing there like a mountain,

children.text: mahendra iva dhārābhiḥ śarair abhivavarṣa ha ||
children.translated_text: showered him with arrows, as <s>Mahendra</s> showers a mountain with torrents of rain.
Paying no heed to the masses of sharp arrows that had fallen upon his body,
the mighty one set his mind on killing <s>Akampana</s>.
Then, laughing, the greatly radiant <s>Hanumān</s>, son of the Wind,

children.text: abhidudrāva tad rakṣaḥ kampayann iva medinīm ||
children.translated_text: rushed at that <s>rākṣasa</s>, as if making the earth tremble.
As he roared and blazed with energy,
his form became unassailable, like that of a flaming fire.
Knowing himself to be without a weapon, and filled with anger,
the foremost of monkeys swiftly uprooted a mountain.
Taking that great mountain in one hand, <s>Māruti</s>,
valiant as he was, roared a tremendous roar and whirled it about.
Then he rushed upon <s>Akampana</s>, lord of the rākṣasas,

children.text: yathā hi namuciṃ saṃkhye vajreṇeva puraṃdaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: just as <s>Purandara</s> once rushed upon <s>Namuci</s> in battle with his thunderbolt.
But <s>Akampana</s>, seeing that mountain peak lifted up,
split it apart from a distance with great crescent-headed arrows.
Seeing that mountain peak, torn apart in the sky by the rākṣasa's arrows,
scattered and fallen, <s>Hanumān</s> was overcome with anger.
Then the monkey, filled with fury and pride, came upon an aśvakarṇa tree
and quickly uprooted it, tall as a great mountain.
Taking that great-trunked, splendid aśvakarṇa tree,
he laughed and, with supreme delight, whirled it in the battle.
Running forward with immense speed and violently breaking trees,
the utterly enraged <s>Hanumān</s> tore the earth with his feet.
Elephants together with their riders, chariots with their charioteers,
and also the foot-soldier rākṣasas were struck down by wise <s>Hanumān</s>.

children.text: tam antakam iva kruddhaṃ samare prāṇahāriṇam
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Hanumān</s> in the battle, enraged like Death and taking lives,
the rākṣasas fled in all directions.
The heroic <s>Akampana</s> saw him advancing in fury,
terrifying the rākṣasas, and he grew angry and roared.
With fourteen sharp arrows that tore into the body,
the mighty <s>Akampana</s> pierced the greatly valiant <s>Hanumān</s>.
Though struck in that way by many showers of arrows,

children.text: hanūmān dadṛśe vīraḥ prarūḍha iva sānumān ||
children.translated_text: the heroic <s>Hanumān</s> appeared like a mountain covered with sprouting shoots.

children.text: tato 'nyaṃ vṛkṣam utpāṭya kṛtvā vegam anuttamam
children.translated_text: Then, uprooting another tree and putting on matchless speed,
he quickly struck <s>Akampana</s>, lord of the rākṣasas, on the head.
Hit by that tree wielded by the wrathful great-souled one,

children.text: rākṣaso vānarendreṇa papāta sa mamāra ca ||
children.translated_text: the rākṣasa fell under the monkey lord's blow and died.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā nihataṃ bhūmau rākṣasendram akampanam
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Akampana</s>, lord of the rākṣasas, slain on the ground,

children.text: vyathitā rākṣasāḥ sarve kṣitikampa iva drumāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all the rākṣasas shook with distress like trees in an earthquake.
All those rākṣasas, defeated and abandoning their weapons,
fled in terror toward <s>Laṅkā</s>, pursued by those monkeys.
With hair loosened, bewildered, their pride broken, and defeated,
their limbs streaming with sweat, they fled away, panting.
They crushed one another and entered the city out of fear,
utterly confused and looking back again and again behind them.
When the rākṣasas had entered <s>Laṅkā</s>, all the mighty monkeys
came together and honored <s>Hanumān</s>.
He too, delighted, honored all those monkeys in return,
<s>Hanumān</s>, endowed with courage, doing so fittingly and kindly.
The monkeys, showing signs of victory, roared according to their strength,
and there once more they dragged off rākṣasas who were still alive.

children.text: sa vīraśobhām abhajanmahākapiḥ sametya rakṣāṃsi nihatya mārutiḥ
children.translated_text: The great monkey <s>Māruti</s> gained heroic splendor after coming together with the rākṣasas and killing them,

children.text: mahāsuraṃ bhīmam amitranāśanaṃ yathaiva viṣṇur balinaṃ camūmukhe ||
children.translated_text: just as <s>Viṣṇu</s>, destroyer of foes, gained it after killing the terrible great asura <s>Bali</s> at the head of battle.

children.text: apūjayan devagaṇāstadā kapiṃ svayaṃ ca rāmo 'tibalaśca lakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the hosts of gods honored the monkey, as did <s>Rāma</s> himself and the exceedingly mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
and likewise the monkeys headed by <s>Sugrīva</s>, and the very mighty <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>.
Hearing of <s>Akampana</s>'s death, the lord of the rākṣasas grew angry,
and, with his face somewhat downcast, looked at those ministers.

children.text: sa tu dhyātvā muhūrtaṃ tu mantribhiḥ saṃvicārya ca
children.translated_text: After reflecting for a moment and consulting with his ministers,

children.text: purīṃ pariyayau laṅkāṃ sarvān gulmān avekṣitum ||
children.translated_text: he went around the city of <s>Laṅkā</s> to inspect all the military posts.

children.text: tāṃ rākṣasagaṇair guptāṃ gulmair bahubhir āvṛtām
children.translated_text: He saw the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>, guarded by hosts of rākṣasas, surrounded by many troops,
and garlanded with banners and flags.

children.text: ruddhāṃ tu nagarīṃ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing the city blockaded, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas,
spoke, at the proper time, in anger to <s>Prahasta</s>, skilled in war:
For a city besieged and suddenly hard pressed,
I see no deliverance other than battle, O expert in war.

children.text: ahaṃ vā kumbhakarṇo vā tvaṃ vā senāpatir mama
children.translated_text: I, or <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, or you, my general,

children.text: indrajid vā nikumbho vā vaheyur bhāram īdṛśam ||
children.translated_text: or <s>Indrajit</s> or <s>Nikumbha</s>, could bear such a burden.

children.text: sa tvaṃ balam itaḥ śīghram ādāya parigṛhya ca
children.translated_text: Therefore quickly take and gather an army from here,
and march out for victory to the place where all the forest-dwellers are.

children.text: niryāṇād eva te nūnaṃ capalā harivāhinī
children.translated_text: At your very setting out, surely, that fickle army of vānaras
will run away when it hears the roar of the roaring lords of rākṣasas.
For the vānaras are fickle, undisciplined, and unsteady in mind;

children.text: na sahiṣyanti te nādaṃ siṃhanādam iva dvipāḥ ||
children.translated_text: they will not endure your roar, as elephants do not endure a lion's roar.

children.text: vidrute ca bale tasmin rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha
children.translated_text: And when that army has fled, <s>Rāma</s>, together with <s>Saumitri</s>,
helpless and without support, will come under <s>Prahasta</s>'s power.
In danger, what is uncertain may still be best; here nothing has been made certain.

children.text: pratilomānulomaṃ vā yad vā no manyase hitam ||
children.translated_text: Whether contrary or agreeable, tell us whatever you think is beneficial.
But when <s>Rāvaṇa</s> had spoken thus, <s>Prahasta</s>, commander of the army,
spoke these words to the lord of rākṣasas, as <s>Uśanas</s> would to the lord of asuras:
O king, we consulted before with skilled ministers,
and a debate also took place among us as we examined one another's views.

children.text: pradānena tu sītāyāḥ śreyo vyavasitaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: By giving back <s>Sītā</s>, the better course was resolved upon by me;

children.text: apradāne punar yuddhaṃ dṛṣṭam etat tathaiva naḥ ||
children.translated_text: but if she were not given back, then war was seen; this was also our view.
I have constantly been honored by you with gifts and respect,

children.text: sāntvaiśca vividhaiḥ kāle kiṃ na kuryāṃ priyaṃ tava ||
children.translated_text: and with various conciliatory words at the proper time; what dear service would I not do for you?

children.text: na hi me jīvitaṃ rakṣyaṃ putradāradhanāni vā
children.translated_text: For neither my life, nor my sons, wives, or wealth, must be protected by me.

children.text: tvaṃ paśya māṃ juhūṣantaṃ tvadarthe jīvitaṃ yudhi ||
children.translated_text: See me offering up my life in battle for your sake.

children.text: evam uktvā tu bhartāraṃ rāvaṇaṃ vāhinīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken to his lord, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the commander of the army said,

children.text: samānayata me śīghraṃ rākṣasānāṃ mahad balam ||
children.translated_text: "Bring me quickly the great army of the rākṣasas.
Today, in the courtyard of battle, with the speed of my arrows like thunderbolts,
let the birds be sated with the flesh of the slain forest-dwellers."
Thus addressed by <s>Prahasta</s>, the officers of the army, making haste,
began to ready the army in that palace of the rākṣasas.
Within a moment, with sharp weapons of many kinds,
<s>Laṅkā</s> was filled with those rākṣasa heroes, as if crowded with elephants.
As they satisfied the sacred fire and paid homage to the brahmins,
a fragrant breeze blew, carrying the smell of ghee.
They took up garlands of various forms, consecrated with mantras;
then the rākṣasas, delighted and ready for battle, wore them.
Armed with bows and clad in armor, the rākṣasas leapt up swiftly,
and, seeing king <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, surrounded <s>Prahasta</s>.

children.text: athāmantrya ca rājānaṃ bherīm āhatya bhairavām
children.translated_text: Then, after taking leave of the king and striking a terrifying drum,
<s>Prahasta</s> mounted a divine chariot, fully equipped and prepared.
It was yoked with very swift horses and properly fitted with an excellent charioteer,
resounding like a great rain-cloud and shining like the moon and sun in person.
With a serpent-banner, unassailable, with fine defenses and excellent fittings,
joined with golden latticework, it seemed to laugh with splendor.
Then, mounting that chariot, with command entrusted to him by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: laṅkāyā niryayau tūrṇaṃ balena mahatā vṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he quickly went out from <s>Laṅkā</s>, surrounded by a great army.
Then, as the commander of the army set forth, the roar of kettledrums,
like the rumbling of rain-clouds, was heard, and also the sound of conches.

children.text: ninadantaḥ svarān ghorān rākṣasā jagmur agrataḥ
children.translated_text: Uttering dreadful cries, the rākṣasas went in front,
terrible in form, huge in body, marching before <s>Prahasta</s>.
With his forces arrayed in a very dreadful formation, he went out by the eastern gate,
surrounded by a great army resembling a herd of elephants.
Surrounded by that army, whose surge was like the sea,
<s>Prahasta</s> went out quickly, enraged and like <s>Kālāntaka</s>.
At the noise of his departure and of the roaring rākṣasas,
all beings in <s>Laṅkā</s> cried out with distorted voices.
Entering the cloudless sky, birds that feed on flesh and blood
made counterclockwise circles around his chariot.
Terrible jackals, vomiting flames of fire, howled.
A meteor fell from the sky, and a harsh wind blew;
the planets, hostile to one another, did not shine.
They rained blood upon him and sprinkled those marching in front;
a vulture settled on the top of his standard, facing south.
And as he repeatedly plunged into battle, from the charioteer's hand
the goad fell from the hand of the driver who guided the horses.
The splendor of his departure, bright and very hard to attain,

children.text: sā nanāśa muhūrtena same ca skhalitā hayāḥ ||
children.translated_text: vanished in a moment, and the horses stumbled even on level ground.
As <s>Prahasta</s> marched out, renowned for strength and manliness,
the vānar army, armed with many weapons, advanced against him in battle.
Then a very tumultuous roar arose among the vānaras,
as they tore up trees and seized heavy rocks.
Both armies, the hosts of rākṣasas and forest-dwellers, rejoiced;
they were swift, capable, and eager to kill one another.
As they challenged one another, a great din was heard.
