children.text: tataḥ prahastaḥ kapirājavāhinīm abhipratasthe vijayāya durmatiḥ
children.translated_text: Then the foolish <s>Prahasta</s> advanced against the army of the monkey king to win victory,

children.text: vivṛddhavegāṃ ca viveśa tāṃ camūṃ yathā mumūrṣuḥ śalabho vibhāvasum ||
children.translated_text: and entered that force of increasing speed, like a moth about to die entering a fire.
Then, as <s>Prahasta</s> marched out, terrible and of terrible valor,
roaring, very huge in body, and surrounded by rākṣasas,
the great army of the powerful vānaras saw him;
with their anger greatly aroused, they roared at <s>Prahasta</s>.
Swords, spears, javelins, arrows,
tridents, clubs, maces, iron bars, prāsas, and various axes,
and the varied bows of the rākṣasas who sought victory
Taken up, they shone in the hands of those rushing upon the vānaras.
And the bull-like vānaras seized flowering trees,
and broad, long rocks, for the leaping warriors wished to fight.

children.text: teṣām anyonyam āsādya saṃgrāmaḥ sumahān abhūt
children.translated_text: When they met one another, a very great battle arose among them,

children.text: bahūnām aśmavṛṣṭiṃ ca śaravṛṣṭiṃ ca varṣatām ||
children.translated_text: with many raining down a shower of stones and a shower of arrows.
In battle many rākṣasas struck down many leaders of monkey troops,
and many vānaras likewise struck down many rākṣasas.

children.text: śūlaiḥ pramathitāḥ kecit kecit tu paramāyudhaiḥ
children.translated_text: Some were crushed by spears, and some by supreme weapons;

children.text: parighair āhatāḥ kecit kecic chinnāḥ paraśvadhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: some were struck by iron clubs, and some were cut apart by axes.
Again, some lay fallen on the surface of the earth, no longer breathing;
some had their hearts split open, pierced by volleys of arrows.

children.text: kecid dvidhākṛtāḥ khaḍgaiḥ sphurantaḥ patitā bhuvi
children.translated_text: Some, cut in two by swords, fell twitching on the ground;
the vānaras were torn open in the sides by the rākṣasas' spears.
And on every side, by the enraged vānaras, the masses of rākṣasas
were crushed upon the earth with trees and mountain peaks.
Struck violently by palms hard as thunderbolts and by fists,
with teeth and eyes shattered, they vomited blood from their mouths.

children.text: ārtasvaraṃ ca svanatāṃ siṃhanādaṃ ca nardatām
children.translated_text: Of those groaning with cries of pain and of those roaring lion-roars,

children.text: babhūva tumulaḥ śabdo harīṇāṃ rakṣasāṃ yudhi ||
children.translated_text: a tumultuous sound arose in battle among the vānaras and rākṣasas.
The angry vānaras and rākṣasas, following the path of heroes,
with rolling eyes and cruel aspect, performed deeds as if without fear.
<s>Narāntaka</s>, <s>Kumbhahanu</s>, <s>Mahānāda</s>, and <s>Samunnata</s>,
these ministers of <s>Prahasta</s>, all struck down the forest-dwellers.

children.text: teṣām āpatatāṃ śīghraṃ nighnatāṃ cāpi vānarān
children.translated_text: As they charged swiftly and kept killing the vānaras,
<s>Dvivida</s> struck one of them, <s>Narāntaka</s>, with a mountain peak.

children.text: durmukhaḥ punar utpāṭya kapiḥ sa vipuladrumam
children.translated_text: Then the monkey <s>Durmukha</s>, uprooting a huge tree,
with quick hands crushed the rākṣasa <s>Samunnata</s>.
But the very enraged <s>Jāmbavān</s>, seizing a great rock,
the glorious one hurled it upon <s>Mahānāda</s>'s chest.
Then the valiant <s>Kumbhahanu</s> there, encountered by <s>Tāra</s>,
was struck on the head with a tree, and the rākṣasa gave up his life.
Unable to endure that deed, <s>Prahasta</s>, mounted on his chariot,
with bow in hand wrought dreadful slaughter among the forest-dwellers.
Then there arose, as it were, a whirlpool in both armies,
and a roar like that of the immeasurable ocean when it is stirred up.
For with a great mass of arrows <s>Prahasta</s>, skilled in war,
enraged, tormented the vānaras in that supreme battle.
With the bodies of vānaras and rākṣasas

children.text: babhūva nicitā ghorā patitair iva parvataiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the dreadful earth became covered, as if with fallen mountains.
That earth, covered with a flood of blood, shone forth

children.text: saṃchannā mādhave māsi palāśair iva puṣpitaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: like land covered with flowering palāśas in the month of Mādhava.
Its banks were masses of slain heroes, and its great trees were broken weapons;
its great water was streams of blood, and it flowed toward the ocean of <s>Yama</s>.
Its great mud was liver and spleen, and its water-plants were scattered entrails;
its fish were broken bodies and heads, and its grass was limbs and parts of limbs.
It was filled with flocks of vultures as with swans, and frequented by kaṅkas as by cranes;
it was covered with foam of fat, and it resounded with cries of distress.
That river made of the battlefield, hard for cowards to cross,
was like a river after the clouds have passed, frequented by swans and cranes.
The rākṣasas and the foremost monkeys crossed that hard-to-cross river
as herd-leading elephants cross a lotus pond dusted with lotus pollen.

children.text: tataḥ sṛjantaṃ bāṇaughān prahastaṃ syandane sthitam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Nīla</s> saw <s>Prahasta</s>, standing in his chariot, releasing streams of arrows
and swiftly striking down the leaping warriors.
The mighty monkey, seeing that utterly unassailable <s>Prahasta</s> rushing on,
struck him, valiant as he was, with an uprooted tree.
Struck by it, the foremost rākṣasa, angered and roaring,
rained showers of arrows upon the commander of the leapers' army.
Unable to ward them off, he received them with eyes shut,

children.text: yathaiva govṛṣo varṣaṃ śāradaṃ śīghram āgatam ||
children.translated_text: just as a bull receives a sudden autumn rain when it comes quickly.
In just this way <s>Nīla</s>, with eyes closed, suddenly endured
<s>Prahasta</s>'s unapproachable and very dreadful shower of arrows.
Great <s>Nīla</s>, enraged by that shower of arrows, with a huge sāla tree
struck <s>Prahasta</s>'s horses, swift as thought.
Made bowless by him, <s>Prahasta</s>, commander of the army,
seized a dreadful club and leapt down from the chariot.
Those two chiefs of armies, both quick and born to anger,
stood with limbs smeared in blood, like two rutting elephants.
Scraping one another with very sharp tusks,
they were like a lion and a tiger, acting like a lion and a tiger.
Heroic in their valor and victory, never turning back in battles,
both longing to win fame, they were equal to <s>Vṛtra</s> and <s>Vāsava</s>.

children.text: ājaghāna tadā nīlaṃ lalāṭe musalena saḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Prahasta</s>, greatly exerted, struck <s>Nīla</s> on the forehead
with his club, and blood flowed from him.
Then, his body smeared with blood, the mighty monkey angrily seized
a very great tree and hurled it at <s>Prahasta</s>'s chest.

children.text: tam acintya prahāraṃ sa pragṛhya musalaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: Disregarding that inconceivable blow, he seized his great club
and, strong himself, ran at the powerful leaping warrior <s>Nīla</s>.
As that mighty monkey saw him rushing on with fierce speed, enraged,
Then, looking closely, the very swift one seized a great rock.
As <s>Prahasta</s>, eager for battle, fought in combat with his mace,

children.text: prahastasya śilāṃ nīlo mūrdhni tūrṇam apātayat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nīla</s> quickly dropped the rock upon <s>Prahasta</s>'s head.

children.text: sā tena kapimukhyena vimuktā mahatī śilā
children.translated_text: That huge and terrible rock, hurled by the foremost monkey,
then shattered <s>Prahasta</s>'s head into many pieces.
Lifeless, bereft of splendor, strength, and senses,

children.text: papāta sahasā bhūmau chinnamūla iva drumaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he suddenly fell to the ground like a tree with its root cut off.
From him, whose head had been split open, much blood flowed,

children.text: śarīrād api susrāva gireḥ prasravaṇaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: and it poured from his body as a spring pours from a mountain.

children.text: hate prahaste nīlena tad akampyaṃ mahad balam
children.translated_text: When <s>Prahasta</s> had been slain by <s>Nīla</s>, that great, once-unshakable force
of dispirited rākṣasas made its way back to <s>Laṅkā</s>.
They could not remain in formation after their commander had been killed,
like water scattered apart when it reaches a bridge or dam.
When that leader of the army was slain, those rākṣasas lost all resolve,
and, going to the lord of the rākṣasas' palace, fell into brooding silence.

children.text: tatastu nīlo vijayī mahābalaḥ praśasyamānaḥ svakṛtena karmaṇā
children.translated_text: Then victorious <s>Nīla</s>, mighty in strength and praised for his own deed,

children.text: sametya rāmeṇa salakṣmaṇena prahṛṣṭarūpastu babhūva yūthapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: met with <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and the troop-leader became joyful in appearance.

children.text: tasmin hate rākṣasasainyapāle plavaṃgamānām ṛṣabheṇa yuddhe
children.translated_text: When the guardian of the rākṣasa army had been killed in battle by the bull among the monkeys,
the army of the rākṣasa king, with terrible weapons and speed like the ocean, fled away.

children.text: gatvā tu rakṣo'dhipateḥ śaśaṃsuḥ senāpatiṃ pāvakasūnuśastam
children.translated_text: Going to the lord of the rākṣasas, they reported that the commander had been slain by the son of Fire,

children.text: taccāpi teṣāṃ vacanaṃ niśamya rakṣo'dhipaḥ krodhavaśaṃ jagāma ||
children.translated_text: and hearing those words of theirs, the lord of the rākṣasas came under the power of anger.

children.text: saṃkhye prahastaṃ nihataṃ niśamya śokārditaḥ krodhaparītacetāḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that <s>Prahasta</s> had been killed in battle, afflicted with grief and his mind filled with anger,
he spoke to those chief warriors of the rākṣasas as <s>Indra</s> speaks to the chief warriors of the immortals:
No contempt should be shown toward an enemy by whom the destroyer of <s>Indra</s>'s army,
my army-guardian, has been slain together with his followers and elephants.
Therefore I myself, intent on destroying the enemy and winning victory,

children.text: svayam eva gamiṣyāmi raṇaśīrṣaṃ tad adbhutam ||
children.translated_text: will go, without further deliberation, to that astonishing front of battle.

children.text: adya tad vānarānīkaṃ rāmaṃ ca sahalakṣmaṇam
children.translated_text: Today I shall burn up that host of monkeys, and <s>Rāma</s> together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
with floods of arrows, as one burns a forest with blazing fires.

children.text: sa evam uktvā jvalanaprakāśaṃ rathaṃ turaṃgottamarājiyuktam
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the enemy of the king of the immortals mounted a chariot bright as fire,
yoked with rows of excellent horses, shining and blazing with its splendor.
With the sounds of conches, kettledrums, and war-drums, with clapping, shouts, and lion-roars,
and honored with auspicious praises, that foremost rākṣasa king then set out.
Surrounded by flesh-eaters whose forms resembled mountains and rain-clouds, and whose eyes blazed like fire,

children.text: babhau vṛto rākṣasarājamukhyair bhūtair vṛto rudra ivāmareśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he shone among the foremost rākṣasa chiefs like lord <s>Rudra</s> surrounded by spirits.

children.text: tato nagaryāḥ sahasā mahaujā niṣkramya tad vānarasainyam ugram
children.translated_text: Then the mighty one suddenly went out from the city and saw that fierce army of monkeys,
roaring like the great ocean and clouds, with trees and mountains lifted in their hands.

children.text: tad rākṣasānīkam atipracaṇḍam ālokya rāmo bhujagendrabāhuḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that exceedingly fierce rākṣasa army, <s>Rāma</s>, whose arms were like great serpents,

children.text: vibhīṣaṇaṃ śastrabhṛtāṃ variṣṭham uvāca senānugataḥ pṛthuśrīḥ ||
children.translated_text: broad in splendor and accompanied by his army, spoke to <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, best of weapon-bearers:
Whose unshakable army is this, filled with many banners, standards, and weapons, with spears, swords, tridents, missiles, and discus-weapons,
filled with elephants like lordly mountains, and filled with fearless warriors?

children.text: tatastu rāmasya niśamya vākyaṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ śakrasamānavīryaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, hearing <s>Rāma</s>'s words, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, equal to <s>Śakra</s> in valor,
pointed out to <s>Rāma</s> the excellent strength of the great-souled rākṣasa champions.
That great-souled one there, mounted on an elephant's shoulder, with a coppery face like the newly risen sun,

children.text: prakampayannāgaśiro 'bhyupaiti hy akampanaṃ tvenam avehi rājan ||
children.translated_text: comes forward shaking the elephant's head; know him, O king, as <s>Akampana</s>.

children.text: yo 'sau rathastho mṛgarājaketur dhūnvan dhanuḥ śakradhanuḥprakāśam
children.translated_text: That one there standing in a chariot, with a lion on his banner, shaking a bow shining like <s>Indra</s>'s bow,
gleams like an elephant with terrible, gaping tusks; he is named <s>Indrajit</s>, chief among the boon-favored.
And this one, like the Vindhya, the setting mountain, and Mahendra, a bowman in a chariot, a great chariot-warrior of exceeding valor,
twanging his unequalled bow, is named <s>Atikāya</s>, because his body is exceedingly huge.
That one there, with copper-red eyes like a newly risen sun, having mounted an elephant resounding with bells,

children.text: gajaṃ kharaṃ garjati vai mahātmā mahodaro nāma sa eṣa vīraḥ ||
children.translated_text: roars harshly; that hero of great soul is named <s>Mahodara</s>.
That one there, mounted on a horse with golden, variegated trappings, gleaming like an evening cloud over a mountain,
raises a spear bound with rays; this piśāca-like warrior has the speed of a thunderbolt.

children.text: yaścaiṣa śūlaṃ niśitaṃ pragṛhya vidyutprabhaṃ kiṃkaravajravegam
children.translated_text: And this famous one, grasping a sharpened trident bright as lightning and swift as a servant's thunderbolt,

children.text: vṛṣendram āsthāya giriprakāśam āyāti so 'sau triśirā yaśasvī ||
children.translated_text: comes mounted on a great bull that shines like a mountain; that is <s>Triśiras</s>.
And that one, cloudlike in form, is <s>Kumbha</s>, with a broad, well-developed chest,

children.text: samāhitaḥ pannagarājaketur visphārayan bhāti dhanur vidhūnvan ||
children.translated_text: composed, with a serpent-king on his banner; he shines as he twangs and shakes his bow.

children.text: yaścaiṣa jāmbūnadavajrajuṣṭaṃ dīptaṃ sadhūmaṃ parighaṃ pragṛhya
children.translated_text: And this one, grasping a blazing, smoke-wreathed iron club adorned with gold and diamonds,
comes as the banner of the rākṣasa host; that is <s>Nikumbha</s>, wondrous and terrible in his deeds.
And this proud one, mounted on a chariot bearing bows, swords, and streams of arrows, bannered and blazing like fire,
shines forth; that is <s>Narāntaka</s>, a fighter with mountain peaks.
And this one, with various terrifying forms, with faces of tiger, camel, lordly elephant, and lion,

children.text: bhūtair vṛto bhāti vivṛttanetraiḥ so 'sau surāṇām api darpahantā ||
children.translated_text: Surrounded by beings with wide-open eyes, that one shines, the humbler of even the gods' pride.

children.text: yatraitad indupratimaṃ vibhāti chattraṃ sitaṃ sūkṣmaśalākam agryam
children.translated_text: Where that excellent white umbrella shines, moonlike and fitted with fine ribs,

children.text: atraiṣa rakṣo'dhipatir mahātmā bhūtair vṛto rudra ivāvabhāti ||
children.translated_text: there this great-souled lord of the rākṣasas, surrounded by beings, appears like <s>Rudra</s>.
There he is, crowned, his face framed by swinging earrings, his terrifying body like the lord of serpents or <s>Vindhya</s> mountain.
The lord of the rākṣasas, humbler of the pride of <s>Mahendra</s> and <s>Vaivasvata</s>, shines like the sun.
Then <s>Rāma</s> replied to <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, the subduer of enemies:
Ah, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas, is blazing and greatly radiant.

children.text: āditya iva duṣprekṣyo raśmibhir bhāti rāvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Like the sun, hard to look upon, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> shines with rays.
I can clearly perceive his form, enveloped in splendor.
The bodies of heroes among gods and dānavas would not be of such a kind
as this body of the lord of rākṣasas that now shines forth.
All his warriors are like mountains, and all fight like mountains.
All the warriors of that greatly powerful one bear blazing weapons.
That king of the rākṣasas shines, surrounded by fierce, blazing warriors,
as if he were embodied <s>Antaka</s> surrounded by sharp beings.

children.text: evam uktvā tato rāmo dhanur ādāya vīryavān
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, mighty <s>Rāma</s> then took up his bow
and stood with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> at his side, drawing out his best arrow.

children.text: tataḥ sa rakṣo'dhipatir mahātmā rakṣāṃsi tānyāha mahābalāni
children.translated_text: Then that great-souled lord of rākṣasas addressed those very powerful rākṣasas:
Stand well prepared and without fear at the gates, patrol houses, and city towers.

children.text: visarjayitvā sahasā tatastān gateṣu rakṣaḥsu yathāniyogam
children.translated_text: Then, after quickly sending them away, when the rākṣasas had gone according to their assignments,
he tore through the ocean-flood of monkeys like a great fish through a full flood of the sea.

children.text: tam āpatantaṃ sahasā samīkṣya dīpteṣucāpaṃ yudhi rākṣasendram
children.translated_text: Seeing the lord of rākṣasas suddenly rushing upon him in battle with blazing arrows and bow,

children.text: mahat samutpāṭya mahīdharāgraṃ dudrāva rakṣo'dhipatiṃ harīśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the lord of monkeys uprooted a great mountain peak and ran at the lord of rākṣasas.
Grasping that mountain summit, with its many trees and ridges, he hurled it at the night-roamer.

children.text: tam āpatantaṃ sahasā samīkṣya bibheda bāṇaistapanīyapuṅkhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing it suddenly rushing toward him, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> split it apart with gold-feathered arrows.

children.text: tasmin pravṛddhottamasānuvṛkṣe śṛṅge vikīrṇe patite pṛthivyām
children.translated_text: When that peak, grown thick with noble ridges and trees, was shattered and had fallen to the earth,
the lord of the rākṣasa world took up an arrow like a great serpent and resembling death.
Taking that arrow, swift as the wind, gleaming like fire with sparks,
and moving with the speed of <s>Mahendra</s>'s thunderbolt, he angrily hurled it to kill <s>Sugrīva</s>.
That shaft, released from <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s arm, sharp-pointed and with a form like <s>Śakra</s>'s thunderbolt,

children.text: sugrīvam āsādya bibheda vegād guheritā krauñcam ivograśaktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: struck <s>Sugrīva</s> and pierced him with force, like the fierce spear hurled by <s>Guha</s> at <s>Krauñca</s>.

children.text: sa sāyakārto viparītacetāḥ kūjan pṛthivyāṃ nipapāta vīraḥ
children.translated_text: Tormented by the shaft and his mind overturned, the hero cried out and fell to the earth.

children.text: taṃ prekṣya bhūmau patitaṃ visaṃjñaṃ neduḥ prahṛṣṭā yudhi yātudhānāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing him fallen on the ground unconscious, the yātudhānas roared in battle, delighted.

children.text: tato gavākṣo gavayaḥ sudaṃṣṭras tatharṣabho jyotimukho nalaśca
children.translated_text: Then <s>Gavākṣa</s>, <s>Gavaya</s>, <s>Sudaṃṣṭra</s>, likewise <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Jyotimukha</s>, and <s>Nala</s>,

children.text: śailān samudyamya vivṛddhakāyāḥ pradudruvustaṃ prati rākṣasendram ||
children.translated_text: their bodies expanded, raised mountains and rushed toward that lord of rākṣasas.

children.text: teṣāṃ prahārān sa cakāra meghān rakṣo'dhipo bāṇagaṇaiḥ śitāgraiḥ
children.translated_text: The lord of rākṣasas rendered their blows futile with masses of sharp-pointed arrows.

children.text: tān vānarendrān api bāṇajālair bibheda jāmbūnadacitrapuṅkhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He pierced those monkey chiefs too with nets of arrows, bright with variegated gold shafts.

children.text: te vānarendrāstridaśāribāṇair bhinnā nipetur bhuvi bhīmarūpāḥ
children.translated_text: Those monkey chiefs, split by the arrows of the enemy of the gods, fell upon the earth in terrible forms.

children.text: tatastu tad vānarasainyam ugraṃ pracchādayāmāsa sa bāṇajālaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he covered that fierce monkey army with nets of arrows.
As they were being struck down, their foremost heroes fallen, roaring in many ways and pierced by the barb of fear,

children.text: śākhāmṛgā rāvaṇasāyakārtā jagmuḥ śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ sma rāmam ||
children.translated_text: the tree-ranging monkeys, tormented by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s arrows, went for refuge to <s>Rāma</s>, the protector.

children.text: tato mahātmā sa dhanur dhanuṣmān ādāya rāmaḥ sahasā jagāma
children.translated_text: Then great-souled <s>Rāma</s>, bow in hand, took up his bow and suddenly advanced.

children.text: taṃ lakṣmaṇaḥ prāñjalir abhyupetya uvāca vākyaṃ paramārthayuktam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> approached him with joined palms and spoke a speech full of highest meaning:
My noble lord is certainly fully capable of killing this wicked one,
but I shall destroy the base man; permit me, my lord.
Greatly radiant <s>Rāma</s>, whose valor is true, said to him:
Go, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and be intent on effort in the battle.
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> is very powerful, and in battle his valor is astonishing.
When enraged, he cannot be withstood even by the three worlds; there is no doubt.

children.text: tasya chidrāṇi mārgasva svacchidrāṇi ca gopaya
children.translated_text: Seek out his openings, and guard your own openings.
With eye and bow, carefully and composed, protect yourself.

children.text: rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā sampariṣvajya pūjya ca
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Rāghava</s>'s words, and having embraced and honored him,

children.text: abhivādya tato rāmaṃ yayau saumitrir āhavam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Saumitri</s> then bowed to <s>Rāma</s> and went to the battle.
He saw <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, whose arms were like an elephant's trunk, holding up a blazing, terrible bow,
covering those monkeys, whose bodies were pierced and scattered, with nets of showers of arrows.
Seeing him, the greatly radiant <s>Hanūmān</s>, son of the wind,
warded off the nets of arrows and rushed at <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: rathaṃ tasya samāsādya bhujam udyamya dakṣiṇam
children.translated_text: Reaching his chariot and raising his right arm,

children.text: trāsayan rāvaṇaṃ dhīmān hanūmān vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: wise <s>Hanūmān</s>, terrifying <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, spoke these words:
Gods, dānavas, gandharvas, yakṣas, and rākṣasas together

children.text: avadhyatvāt tvayā bhagnā vānarebhyastu te bhayam ||
children.translated_text: have been crushed by you because of your immunity from being slain; but from monkeys there is danger for you.

children.text: eṣa me dakṣiṇo bāhuḥ pañcaśākhaḥ samudyataḥ
children.translated_text: This right arm of mine, raised with its five branches,
will drive from your body the life-spirit that has dwelt there long.
Hearing <s>Hanūmān</s>'s words, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> of terrible valor,
his eyes reddened with anger, spoke these words.

children.text: kṣipraṃ prahara niḥśaṅkaṃ sthirāṃ kīrtim avāpnuhi
children.translated_text: Strike quickly and without hesitation, and gain lasting fame.
Then I shall destroy you, O monkey, you who are renowned among your kin.
Hearing <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s words, the son of the Wind spoke these words:

children.text: prahṛtaṃ hi mayā pūrvam akṣaṃ smara sutaṃ tava ||
children.translated_text: Remember that your son <s>Akṣa</s> was already struck down by me.
Thus addressed, the great-splendored <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas,
powerful as he was, struck the son of the Wind on the chest with his palm.

children.text: sa talābhihatastena cacāla ca muhur muhuḥ
children.translated_text: Struck by that palm, he staggered again and again,
and, thoroughly enraged, he struck the foe of the immortals with his own palm.
Then, struck by the palm of the great-souled monkey,
the Ten-necked one was shaken like a mountain in an earthquake.

children.text: saṃgrāme taṃ tathā dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇaṃ talatāḍitam
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Rāvaṇa</s> struck by a palm in that way in battle,

children.text: ṛṣayo vānarāḥ siddhā nedur devāḥ sahāsurāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the seers, monkeys, siddhas, gods, and asuras cried out.
Then, recovering himself, the great-splendored <s>Rāvaṇa</s> spoke these words:

children.text: sādhu vānara vīryeṇa ślāghanīyo 'si me ripuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Well done, monkey; through your valor you are an enemy worthy of my praise.
When <s>Rāvaṇa</s> had spoken thus, <s>Māruti</s> spoke these words:

children.text: dhig astu mama vīryaṃ tu yat tvaṃ jīvasi rāvaṇa ||
children.translated_text: Shame on my strength, since you are still alive, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: sakṛt tu praharedānīṃ durbuddhe kiṃ vikatthase
children.translated_text: Now strike just once, evil-minded one; why do you boast?
Then my fist will send you to the abode of <s>Yama</s>.
Then, at <s>Māruti</s>'s words, his anger blazed up.
With blood-red eyes, he forcefully raised his right fist,
and the powerful one brought it down swiftly on the monkey's chest.

children.text: hanūmān vakṣasi vyūḍhe saṃcacāla hataḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hanumān</s>, hit again on his broad chest, staggered.

children.text: vihvalaṃ taṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā hanūmantaṃ mahābalam
children.translated_text: Seeing the mighty <s>Hanumān</s> reeling then,
that great chariot-warrior quickly went in his chariot toward <s>Nīla</s>.
With terrible arrows like serpents, piercing the most vital spots,
he set <s>Nīla</s>, commander of the monkey army, aflame.
Distressed by the mass of arrows, <s>Nīla</s>, lord of the monkey troops,
hurled a mountain peak at the lord of the rākṣasas with one hand.
The radiant, great-minded <s>Hanumān</s> too had recovered himself,
and, watching and eager for battle, said this in anger:
Since <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas, is engaged with <s>Nīla</s>,
it is not proper to rush against someone who is fighting with another.
But the great-splendored <s>Rāvaṇa</s> struck that peak with seven arrows,
sharp-pointed and keen, and it fell shattered to pieces.

children.text: tad vikīrṇaṃ gireḥ śṛṅgaṃ dṛṣṭvā haricamūpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that mountain peak shattered, the commander of the monkey army,
a destroyer of enemy heroes, blazed with anger like the fire of Time.
Then <s>Nīla</s> threw aśvakarṇa trees, dhava trees, sāla trees, and flowering mango trees,
as well as various other trees, in the battle.

children.text: sa tān vṛkṣān samāsādya praticicheda rāvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s> met those trees and cut them apart,
and he rained a most terrible shower of arrows upon the son of Fire.
Showered by that mass of arrows like a great mountain by a cloud,

children.text: hrasvaṃ kṛtvā tadā rūpaṃ dhvajāgre nipapāta ha ||
children.translated_text: he made his form small and alighted on the tip of the banner.
Seeing the son of Fire stationed on the tip of the banner,

children.text: jajvāla rāvaṇaḥ krodhāt tato nīlo nanāda ha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s> blazed with anger, and then <s>Nīla</s> roared.

children.text: dhvajāgre dhanuṣaścāgre kirīṭāgre ca taṃ harim
children.translated_text: On the tip of the banner, the tip of the bow, and the tip of the crown, that monkey
was seen by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, <s>Hanumān</s>, and <s>Rāma</s>, and they were astonished.
The great-splendored <s>Rāvaṇa</s> too, amazed at the monkey's agility,
summoned the blazing, wondrous āgneya weapon.
Then those leaping monkeys cried out in delight, finding their mark,
when they saw <s>Rāvaṇa</s> bewildered by <s>Nīla</s>'s agility in battle.
And then, enraged by the clamor of the monkeys, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>
with his heart seized by confusion, could not understand anything.
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s> took an arrow joined with the āgneya weapon,
and the night-wanderer looked at <s>Nīla</s> standing on the banner's top.
Then the great-splendored <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas, said:
Monkey, you are endowed with agility by this supreme magic.

children.text: jīvitaṃ khalu rakṣasva yadi śaknoṣi vānara
children.translated_text: Protect your life, if you can, O monkey.
Again and again you create all those forms of yourself.
Even so, this arrow released by me and empowered with a weapon
will deprive you of life while you are trying to preserve your life.
Having spoken thus, the great-armed <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas,
fitted the arrow with the weapon and struck the commander of the army.
<s>Nīla</s>, struck on the chest by that weapon-charged arrow,
fell suddenly to the ground, as though being burned.
Because of the greatness of his father and also because of his own fiery energy,

children.text: jānubhyām apatad bhūmau na ca prāṇair vyayujyata ||
children.translated_text: he fell to the ground on his knees, but he was not separated from life.
Seeing the monkey unconscious, the Ten-necked one, eager for battle,
rushed in his cloud-roaring chariot toward <s>Saumitri</s>.

children.text: tam āha saumitrir adīnasattvo visphārayantaṃ dhanur aprameyam
children.translated_text: As he twanged his immeasurable bow, steadfast <s>Saumitri</s> said to him:

children.text: anvehi mām eva niśācarendra na vānarāṃstvaṃ prati yoddhum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: Come after me alone, lord of the night-wanderers; you ought not fight the monkeys.

children.text: sa tasya vākyaṃ paripūrṇaghoṣaṃ jyāśabdam ugraṃ ca niśamya rājā
children.translated_text: Hearing his full-resounding speech and the fierce sound of the bowstring, the king,

children.text: āsādya saumitrim avasthitaṃ taṃ kopānvitaṃ vākyam uvāca rakṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the rākṣasa, approached <s>Saumitri</s> as he stood there and, filled with anger, spoke these words:

children.text: diṣṭyāsi me rāghava dṛṣṭimārgaṃ prāpto 'ntagāmī viparītabuddhiḥ
children.translated_text: By good fortune you have come within range of my sight, O <s>Rāghava</s>, destined for your end and perverse in mind.

children.text: asmin kṣaṇe yāsyasi mṛtyudeśaṃ saṃsādyamāno mama bāṇajālaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: At this very moment you will go to the realm of death, overwhelmed by my nets of arrows.

children.text: tam āha saumitrir avismayāno garjantam udvṛttasitāgradaṃṣṭram
children.translated_text: Unastonished, <s>Saumitri</s> said to him as he roared, his white-tipped fangs protruding upward:

children.text: rājanna garjanti mahāprabhāvā vikatthase pāpakṛtāṃ variṣṭha ||
children.translated_text: O king, those of great power roar; you boast idly, foremost among evil-doers.

children.text: jānāmi vīryaṃ tava rākṣasendra balaṃ pratāpaṃ ca parākramaṃ ca
children.translated_text: I know your heroism, lord of rākṣasas, your strength, your fiery might, and your valor.
I stand here with arrows and bow in hand. Come. What is the use of empty boasting?

children.text: sa evam uktaḥ kupitaḥ sasarja rakṣo'dhipaḥ saptaśarān supuṅkhān
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, the enraged lord of rākṣasas released seven well-feathered arrows.

children.text: tāṃl lakṣmaṇaḥ kāñcanacitrapuṅkhaiś cicheda bāṇair niśitāgradhāraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> cut them apart with sharp-pointed arrows whose beautiful feathers were adorned with gold.

children.text: tān prekṣamāṇaḥ sahasā nikṛttān nikṛttabhogān iva pannagendrān
children.translated_text: Seeing them suddenly severed, like great serpents with their coils cut off,

children.text: laṅkeśvaraḥ krodhavaśaṃ jagāma sasarja cānyānniśitān pṛṣatkān ||
children.translated_text: the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s> came under the sway of anger and released other sharp shafts.

children.text: sa bāṇavarṣaṃ tu vavarṣa tīvraṃ rāmānujaḥ kārmukasamprayuktam
children.translated_text: But <s>Rāma</s>'s younger brother rained down a fierce shower of arrows, set upon his bow,

children.text: kṣurārdhacandrottamakarṇibhallaiḥ śarāṃśca cicheda na cukṣubhe ca ||
children.translated_text: and with razor-headed, crescent-headed, fine-eared, and broad-headed shafts he cut down those arrows and did not tremble.
Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> quickly fitted sharp-pointed arrows, equal in speed to <s>Mahendra</s>'s thunderbolt and lightning,

children.text: saṃdhāya cāpe jvalanaprakāśān sasarja rakṣo'dhipater vadhāya ||
children.translated_text: bright as fire, upon his bow, and released them to slay the lord of rākṣasas.

children.text: sa tān pracicheda hi rākṣasendraś chittvā ca tāṃl lakṣmaṇam ājaghāna
children.translated_text: The king of rākṣasas cut those apart; and, after cutting them, he struck <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>
on the forehead with an arrow given by <s>Svayambhū</s>, its splendor like the fire at the end of time.

children.text: sa lakṣmaṇo rāvaṇasāyakārtaś cacāla cāpaṃ śithilaṃ pragṛhya
children.translated_text: Tormented by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s arrow, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> reeled, holding his bow loosened in his grasp.

children.text: punaśca saṃjñāṃ pratilabhya kṛcchrāccicheda cāpaṃ tridaśendraśatroḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, regaining consciousness with difficulty, he cut apart the bow of the enemy of the Thirty Gods.

children.text: nikṛttacāpaṃ tribhir ājaghāna bāṇaistadā dāśarathiḥ śitāgraiḥ
children.translated_text: When his bow had been cut, <s>Dāśarathi</s> struck him then with three sharp-pointed arrows.

children.text: sa sāyakārto vicacāla rājā kṛcchrācca saṃjñāṃ punar āsasāda ||
children.translated_text: Tormented by those shafts, the king staggered, and with difficulty regained consciousness again.
His bow cut, struck by arrows, his body wet with sweat and drenched in blood,

children.text: jagrāha śaktiṃ samudagraśaktiḥ svayambhudattāṃ yudhi devaśatruḥ ||
children.translated_text: the enemy of the gods, powerful in battle, seized a spear given by <s>Svayambhū</s>.
The lord of the rākṣasa realm hurled that spear, blazing, like smokeless fire,

children.text: cikṣepa śaktiṃ tarasā jvalantīṃ saumitraye rākṣasarāṣṭranāthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: terrifying to the armies of vānaras, swiftly at <s>Saumitri</s>.

children.text: tām āpatantīṃ bharatānujo 'strair jaghāna bāṇaiśca hutāgnikalpaiḥ
children.translated_text: As it came on, <s>Bharata</s>'s younger brother struck it with missiles and with arrows like sacrificial fire.

children.text: tathāpi sā tasya viveśa śaktir bhujāntaraṃ dāśarather viśālam ||
children.translated_text: Even so, that spear entered the broad space between the arms of <s>Dāśarathi</s>.
Struck by that Brahmā-given spear in the middle of the chest, <s>Saumitri</s>

children.text: viṣṇor acintyaṃ svaṃ bhāgam ātmānaṃ pratyanusmarat ||
children.translated_text: recalled himself as his own inconceivable portion of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Then the tormentor of the gods, having pressed <s>Saumitri</s>, crusher of the pride of dānavas,
with both his arms, was unable to lift him.
<s>Himavān</s>, <s>Mandara</s>, <s>Meru</s>, or the three worlds together with the immortals

children.text: śakyaṃ bhujābhyām uddhartuṃ na saṃkhye bharatānujaḥ ||
children.translated_text: could be lifted up with the arms in battle, but not <s>Bharata</s>'s younger brother.

children.text: athainaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ bhāgaṃ mānuṣaṃ deham āsthitam
children.translated_text: Then, seeing <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, that Vaiṣṇava portion established in a human body,
lying unconscious, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> was astonished.
Then the son of the Wind, enraged, rushed upon <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Angry, he struck him on the chest with a fist like a thunderbolt.
By that blow of the fist, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of rākṣasas,

children.text: jānubhyām apatad bhūmau cacāla ca papāta ca ||
children.translated_text: fell to the ground on his knees; he shook and collapsed.
Seeing the unconscious <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, terrible in valor, in battle,
the seers, the vānaras, and the gods together with <s>Vāsava</s> roared aloud.
Then the radiant <s>Hanūmān</s> took <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, oppressed by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
near to <s>Rāghava</s>, clasping him in both arms.

children.text: vāyusūnoḥ suhṛttvena bhaktyā paramayā ca saḥ
children.translated_text: Because of the friendship and supreme devotion of the son of the Wind, he,
though unshakable by enemies, became light for the monkey.

children.text: taṃ samutsṛjya sā śaktiḥ saumitriṃ yudhi durjayam
children.translated_text: That spear, having released <s>Saumitri</s>, hard to conquer in battle,

children.text: rāvaṇasya rathe tasmin sthānaṃ punar upāgamat ||
children.translated_text: returned again to its place on that chariot of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Mighty <s>Rāvaṇa</s> too, having regained consciousness in the great battle,

children.text: ādade niśitān bāṇāñ jagrāha ca mahad dhanuḥ ||
children.translated_text: took up sharp arrows and grasped a great bow.
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, slayer of foes, was restored and freed from the arrow wound,
remembering himself as the immeasurable portion of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
But <s>Rāghava</s>, seeing the great army of vānaras in battle, its great heroes cast down,
rushed upon <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Then <s>Hanūmān</s> approached him and said these words:

children.text: mama pṛṣṭhaṃ samāruhya rākṣasaṃ śāstum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: 'Mount upon my back, and you should chastise the rākṣasa.'
Hearing that speech spoken by the son of the Wind,
heroic <s>Rāghava</s> quickly mounted <s>Hanūmān</s>, the great monkey.
The lord of men saw <s>Rāvaṇa</s> standing in his chariot in battle.

children.text: tam ālokya mahātejāḥ pradudrāva sa rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Looking upon him, that greatly radiant <s>Rāghava</s> rushed forward,
like angry <s>Viṣṇu</s>, weapon raised, advancing against <s>Vairocana</s>.
He made a fierce sound with his bowstring, like the crash of a thunderbolt,

children.text: girā gambhīrayā rāmo rākṣasendram uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Rāma</s> spoke to the lord of rākṣasas in a deep voice:

children.text: tiṣṭha tiṣṭha mama tvaṃ hi kṛtvā vipriyam īdṛśam
children.translated_text: 'Stand, stand! After doing such wrong to me,

children.text: kva nu rākṣasaśārdūla gato mokṣam avāpsyasi ||
children.translated_text: where now, tiger among rākṣasas, will you go and obtain release?
If you go to <s>Indra</s>, <s>Vaivasvata</s>, <s>Bhāskara</s>, <s>Svayambhū</s>, <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, or <s>Śaṃkara</s>,

children.text: gamiṣyasi tvaṃ daśa vā diśo vā tathāpi me nādya gato vimokṣyase ||
children.translated_text: or even to the ten directions, still today, once gone from me, you will not be freed.
And this one, struck today by your spear and suddenly brought to distress though he desired battle,

children.text: sa eṣa rakṣogaṇarāja mṛtyuḥ saputradārasya tavādya yuddhe ||
children.translated_text: he, O king of the hosts of rākṣasas, is death for you today in battle, together with your sons and wives.'
Hearing <s>Rāghava</s>'s words, the lord of rākṣasas struck the great monkey
with sharp arrows resembling the flames of the fire at the end of time.
In the battle with the rākṣasas, even when he had been struck with arrows,
his splendor, joined with its own natural brilliance, increased still more.
Then mighty <s>Rāma</s>, seeing the tiger among the leapers
wounded by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, came under the power of anger.
Advancing against his chariot, with its wheels, horses, banner, umbrella, and great standard,

children.text: sasārathiṃ sāśaniśūlakhaḍgaṃ rāmaḥ pracicheda śaraiḥ supuṅkhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> cut it apart with well-feathered arrows, together with its charioteer, thunderbolt, spear, and sword.
Then he forcefully struck the enemy of <s>Indra</s> with an arrow resembling a thunderbolt and lightning,

children.text: bhujāntare vyūḍhasujātarūpe vajreṇa meruṃ bhagavān ivendraḥ ||
children.translated_text: between his arms, on his broad and well-shaped chest, as blessed <s>Indra</s> once struck <s>Meru</s> with the thunderbolt.

children.text: yo vajrapātāśanisaṃnipātān na cukṣubhe nāpi cacāla rājā
children.translated_text: The king who had not trembled or shaken at the fall of thunderbolts and lightning

children.text: sa rāmabāṇābhihato bhṛśārtaś cacāla cāpaṃ ca mumoca vīraḥ ||
children.translated_text: was struck by <s>Rāma</s>'s arrow; greatly pained, the hero trembled and let go of his bow.

children.text: taṃ vihvalantaṃ prasamīkṣya rāmaḥ samādade dīptam athārdhacandram
children.translated_text: Seeing him reeling, <s>Rāma</s> then set a blazing crescent-headed arrow to his bow,

children.text: tenārkavarṇaṃ sahasā kirīṭaṃ cicheda rakṣo'dhipater mahātmā ||
children.translated_text: and with it the great-souled one suddenly cut off the sun-colored crown of the lord of rākṣasas.
Like a serpent without venom, like the sun with its rays extinguished, without radiance,

children.text: gataśriyaṃ kṛttakirīṭakūṭam uvāca rāmo yudhi rākṣasendram ||
children.translated_text: with his glory gone and the crest of his crown cut away, <s>Rāma</s> addressed the lord of rākṣasas in battle.

children.text: kṛtaṃ tvayā karma mahat subhīmaṃ hatapravīraśca kṛtastvayāham
children.translated_text: You have done a great and very dreadful deed, and by you I have been made bereft of slain foremost heroes.

children.text: tasmāt pariśrānta iti vyavasya na tvāṃ śarair mṛtyuvaśaṃ nayāmi ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, judging that you are exhausted, I do not bring you under the power of death with my arrows.

children.text: sa evam ukto hatadarpaharṣo nikṛttacāpaḥ sa hatāśvasūtaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, with his pride and joy destroyed, his bow cut away, and his horses and charioteer slain,

children.text: śarārditaḥ kṛttamahākirīṭo viveśa laṅkāṃ sahasā sma rājā ||
children.translated_text: tormented by arrows and with his great crown cut off, the king at once entered <s>Laṅkā</s>.
When that lord of night-roamers had entered, the mighty enemy of Dānavas and gods,

children.text: harīn viśalyān saha lakṣmaṇena cakāra rāmaḥ paramāhavāgre ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, freed the monkeys from arrows at the front of the supreme battle.

children.text: tasmin prabhagne tridaśendraśatrau surāsurā bhūtagaṇā diśaśca
children.translated_text: When that enemy of the lord of the thirty gods had been routed, the gods, asuras, hosts of beings, and the quarters,
together with the oceans, the sages, and the great serpents, and likewise the creatures of land and water, rejoiced.
Having entered the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>, afflicted by fear of <s>Rāma</s>'s arrows,
the king, his pride broken, then became distressed in his senses.
Like an elephant overcome by a lion, like a serpent overcome by <s>Garuḍa</s>,
the king had been overpowered by the great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>.
Remembering the arrows of <s>Rāghava</s>, shining like the rod of <s>Brahmā</s>
and having a brilliance like lightning, the lord of rākṣasas trembled.
Taking his seat on a divine golden throne,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, looking around at the rākṣasas, spoke these words:

children.text: sarvaṃ tat khalu me moghaṃ yat taptaṃ paramaṃ tapaḥ
children.translated_text: All that supreme austerity which I practiced has indeed proved fruitless,
since I, who am equal to great <s>Indra</s>, have been conquered by a human.

children.text: idaṃ tad brahmaṇo ghoraṃ vākyaṃ mām abhyupasthitam
children.translated_text: This dreadful word of <s>Brahmā</s> has now come upon me,

children.text: mānuṣebhyo vijānīhi bhayaṃ tvam iti tat tathā ||
children.translated_text: that I should know danger for myself from humans; and that is true.
From gods, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, rākṣasas, and serpents

children.text: avadhyatvaṃ mayā prāptaṃ mānuṣebhyo na yācitam ||
children.translated_text: I obtained invulnerability; from humans I did not ask it.
Accepting this very fact, you ought to make an effort here,
and the rākṣasas should stand on the tops of the ramparts and gate-towers.
And that <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, incomparable and unfathomably deep, destroyer of the pride of gods and Dānavas,
but overpowered by <s>Brahmā</s>'s curse, must be awakened.

children.text: sa parājitam ātmānaṃ prahastaṃ ca niṣūditam
children.translated_text: Knowing himself defeated and <s>Prahasta</s> slain,
the mighty one gave commands to the dreadful rākṣasa force.
Let care be taken at the gates; let the ramparts be mounted.
Let <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, who is possessed by the power of sleep, be awakened.

children.text: nava ṣaṭ sapta cāṣṭau ca māsān svapiti rākṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: The rākṣasa sleeps for nine, six, seven, and eight months.

children.text: taṃ tu bodhayata kṣipraṃ kumbhakarṇaṃ mahābalam ||
children.translated_text: Wake that mighty <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> quickly.

children.text: sa hi saṃkhye mahābāhuḥ kakudaṃ sarvarakṣasām
children.translated_text: For in battle that great-armed one is the chief strength of all rākṣasas,

children.text: vānarān rājaputrau ca kṣipram eva vadhiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: and he will very quickly kill the vānaras and the two princes.

children.text: kumbhakarṇaḥ sadā śete mūḍho grāmyasukhe rataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> is always asleep, foolish, and devoted to coarse pleasures.
In this very dreadful battle, when I have been driven back by <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: bhaviṣyati na me śokaḥ kumbhakarṇe vibodhite
children.translated_text: there will be no grief for me once <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> is awakened.
For what shall I do with him, though his strength is equal to <s>Śakra</s>'s,

children.text: īdṛśe vyasane prāpte yo na sāhyāya kalpate
children.translated_text: if, when such a disaster has arisen, he is not fit to come to my aid?

children.text: te tu tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rākṣasendrasya rākṣasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But those rākṣasas, hearing that word of the lord of rākṣasas,
went in the utmost agitation to <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>'s dwelling.
Those eaters of flesh and blood, commanded by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
took perfumes, garlands, and foods, and quickly went.
Entering that cave with great doors, a yojana in extent on every side,
the pleasant cave of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, through which every fragrance flowed,
as they made their way, they entered the cave with difficulty and effort.

children.text: tāṃ praviśya guhāṃ ramyāṃ śubhāṃ kāñcanakuṭṭimām
children.translated_text: Having entered that lovely and splendid cave with a golden floor,
they saw the tiger among rākṣasas lying there, dreadful to behold.

children.text: te tu taṃ vikṛtaṃ suptaṃ vikīrṇam iva parvatam
children.translated_text: All together they awakened that misshapen sleeper, like a mountain spread out,
<s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, sunk in great sleep.
His body had its hairs bristling upward, and he breathed like a serpent,
terrifying them with his great breaths as he lay there, dreadful to behold.
They saw him with terrible nostrils and a mouth as vast as the underworld,
the tiger among rākṣasas, mighty <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>.
Then those great-souled ones at that time placed before <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>
a supremely satisfying heap of meats resembling <s>Meru</s>,

children.text: mṛgāṇāṃ mahiṣāṇāṃ ca varāhāṇāṃ ca saṃcayān
children.translated_text: and piles of deer, buffaloes, and boars.
The tigers among the Nairṛtas made a wondrous heap of food.
Then pots of blood and various liquors
the enemies of the thirty gods placed before <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>.
They anointed the scorcher of foes with very costly sandal paste
and covered him with divine garlands and fragrant perfumes.
They released fragrant incense and praised the scorcher of foes,
and the yātudhānas roared in thousands like clouds.
They blew conches bright as the moon,
and all at once, in fury, they also cried out tumultuously.
Those night-wanderers roared, clapped their arms, and shouted,
making a vast sound in order to awaken <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>.
With the din of conches, bherīs, and paṭahas, with the noise of arm-clapping, cries, and lion-roars,

children.text: diśo dravantastridivaṃ kirantaḥ śrutvā vihaṃgāḥ sahasā nipetuḥ ||
children.translated_text: birds, hearing it, suddenly fell down, fleeing through the quarters and scattering through the sky.

children.text: yadā bhṛśaṃ tair ninadair mahātmā na kumbhakarṇo bubudhe prasuptaḥ
children.translated_text: When, though deeply asleep, the great-souled <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> did not wake from those sounds,

children.text: tato bhuśuṇḍīmusalāni sarve rakṣogaṇāste jagṛhur gadāśca ||
children.translated_text: then all those hosts of rākṣasas took up clubs, pestles, and maces.

children.text: taṃ śailaśṛṅgair musalair gadābhir vṛkṣaistalair mudgaramuṣṭibhiśca
children.translated_text: With mountain peaks, pestles, maces, trees, palms, hammers, and fists,

children.text: sukhaprasuptaṃ bhuvi kumbhakarṇaṃ rakṣāṃsyudagrāṇi tadā nijaghnuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the fierce rākṣasas then struck <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, who was sleeping comfortably on the ground.
Because of the wind of the breath of that rākṣasa <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>,
even the powerful rākṣasas could not stand before him.
Then before him the rākṣasas of terrible valor, forcefully
played mṛdaṅgas, paṇavas, bherīs, and groups of conches and jars,
ten thousand rākṣasas sounding them all at once.
They tried to wake him, whose form was like a mass of blue-black collyrium,

children.text: abhighnanto nadantaśca naiva saṃvivide tu saḥ ||
children.translated_text: striking him and roaring, but he did not perceive anything at all.

children.text: yadā cainaṃ na śekuste pratibodhayituṃ tadā
children.translated_text: And when they could not wake him,
then they began a still heavier and terrible effort.
They beat horses, camels, donkeys, and elephants with sticks, goads, and hooks,
and with all their breath they sounded bherīs, conches, and mṛdaṅgas.
They struck his limbs with great logs and clubs,
and with hammers and pestles, exerting all their strength.
With that great noise <s>Laṅkā</s> was completely filled,
mountains and forests and all; yet even then he did not wake.
Then a thousand bherīs were beaten all at once,
their rims of polished gold, placed everywhere around him.
When even thus the one sunk in excessive sleep did not wake,
being subject to the power of the curse, then the night-wanderers became angry.
All filled with great wrath and of terrible prowess,
intending to wake that rākṣasa, some made another effort.

children.text: anye bherīḥ samājaghnur anye cakrur mahāsvanam
children.translated_text: Some struck bherīs, others made a great noise,

children.text: keśān anye pralulupuḥ karṇāvanye daśanti ca
children.translated_text: some pulled his hair, and others bit his ears;
but <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, gone under the power of great sleep, did not stir.
And other strong ones, holding iron mallets in their hands,
dropped those iron mallets on his head, chest, and limbs.
Bound with ropes and with śataghnīs on every side,
the huge-bodied rākṣasa, though being struck, did not awaken.
But when a thousand elephants were driven over his body,
then <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, awakened, became aware of the supreme touch.

children.text: sa pātyamānair giriśṛṅgavṛkṣair acintayaṃstān vipulān prahārān
children.translated_text: Disregarding those mighty blows from falling mountain peaks and trees,
and tormented by hunger after his sleep was spent, he suddenly leapt up, yawning.
Throwing out his arms, like elephant coils and mountain peaks, solid as mountain ridges,

children.text: vivṛtya vaktraṃ vaḍavāmukhābhaṃ niśācaro 'sau vikṛtaṃ jajṛmbhe ||
children.translated_text: that night-wanderer opened his mouth, like the mouth of the submarine fire, and yawned hideously.
As he yawned, his mouth, resembling the underworld,
was seen like the sun risen over the peak of <s>Meru</s>.
As the exceedingly strong night-wanderer yawned after awakening,
his breath arose like wind from a mountain.
The form of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> as he stood up shone then
like a cloud with cranes at the end of the hot season as it pours down rain.
His two great eyes, blazing like kindled fire and bright like lightning,
were seen like two blazing great planets.
Hungry, he ate meat; thirsty, he drank blood.

children.text: medaḥkumbhaṃ ca madyaṃ ca papau śakraripustadā ||
children.translated_text: Then the enemy of <s>Śakra</s> drank jars of fat and liquor too.
Then, knowing that he was satisfied, the night-wanderers sprang up,
bowed to him with their heads, and surrounded him on every side.
That bull among the Nairṛtas comforted all the Nairṛtas,
and, astonished at his awakening, said this to the rākṣasas:
For what reason have you struck me and awakened me?

children.text: kaccit sukuśalaṃ rājño bhayaṃ vā neha kiṃcana ||
children.translated_text: Surely all is well with the king, and there is no danger here?

children.text: athavā dhruvam anyebhyo bhayaṃ param upasthitam
children.translated_text: Or rather, surely some supreme danger has arisen from others,
for the sake of which you have quickly awakened me.
Today I shall uproot the fear of the king of the rākṣasas.
I shall cast down <s>Mahendra</s>, or likewise shatter <s>Anala</s>.

children.text: na hyalpakāraṇe suptaṃ bodhayiṣyati māṃ bhṛśam
children.translated_text: For they would not so urgently awaken me from sleep for a small reason.
Therefore tell me truly the reason for awakening me.
As <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, subduer of foes, was speaking thus in fury,

children.text: yūpākṣaḥ sacivo rājñaḥ kṛtāñjalir uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yūpākṣa</s>, the king's minister, with joined palms, said:

children.text: na no devakṛtaṃ kiṃcid bhayam asti kadācana
children.translated_text: We have no fear at any time from anything caused by the gods,

children.text: na daityadānavebhyo vā bhayam asti hi tādṛśam
children.translated_text: nor is there such fear from daityas or dānavas

children.text: yādṛśaṃ mānuṣaṃ rājan bhayam asmān upasthitam ||
children.translated_text: as the human danger, O king, that now confronts us.
This <s>Laṅkā</s> has been surrounded by monkeys shaped like mountains;
from <s>Rāma</s>, tormented by the abduction of <s>Sītā</s>, there is a tremendous danger to us.
Formerly this great city was burned by a single monkey,
and prince <s>Akṣa</s> was slain, together with his retinue and elephants.
Even the lord of the rākṣasas himself, the <s>Paulastya</s>, tormentor of the gods,
was released in battle by <s>Rāma</s>, radiant as the sun, as though he were dead.

children.text: yanna devaiḥ kṛto rājā nāpi daityair na dānavaiḥ
children.translated_text: What was not done to the king by the gods, nor by daityas or dānavas,

children.text: kṛtaḥ sa iha rāmeṇa vimuktaḥ prāṇasaṃśayāt ||
children.translated_text: that was done here by <s>Rāma</s>; he was released from danger to his life.

children.text: sa yūpākṣavacaḥ śrutvā bhrātur yudhi parājayam
children.translated_text: Hearing this speech of <s>Yūpākṣa</s> about his brother's defeat in battle,
<s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, his eyes rolling, said this to <s>Yūpākṣa</s>:
Today itself, <s>Yūpākṣa</s>, after killing the whole monkey army, along with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: rāghavaṃ ca raṇe hatvā paścād drakṣyāmi rāvaṇam ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Rāghava</s> too in battle, I shall afterward see <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
I shall satisfy the rākṣasas with the flesh and blood of the monkeys,
and I myself shall drink the blood of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> as well.

children.text: tat tasya vākyaṃ bruvato niśamya sagarvitaṃ roṣavivṛddhadoṣam
children.translated_text: Hearing that boastful speech of his as he spoke, its fault increased by anger,

children.text: mahodaro nairṛtayodhamukhyaḥ kṛtāñjalir vākyam idaṃ babhāṣe ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mahodara</s>, chief of the rākṣasa warriors, joined his palms and spoke these words:

children.text: rāvaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā guṇadoṣau vimṛśya ca
children.translated_text: After hearing <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s word and considering its merits and faults,

children.text: paścād api mahābāho śatrūn yudhi vijeṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: then afterward too, great-armed one, you will conquer the enemies in battle.
Hearing <s>Mahodara</s>'s speech, surrounded by rākṣasas,
the mighty and very powerful <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> set out.
Having roused that fearsome-eyed one, terrible in form and valor,
the rākṣasas quickly went to the dwelling of the Ten-necked one.
Then, having gone to the Ten-necked one, who was seated on a supreme throne,
all the night-wanderers spoke, their joined palms cupped:
This <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, your brother, has awakened, bull among rākṣasas.

children.text: kathaṃ tatraiva niryātu drakṣyase tam ihāgatam ||
children.translated_text: Should he set out from there itself, or will you see him when he has come here?
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, delighted, said to those rākṣasas who stood near:

children.text: draṣṭum enam ihecchāmi yathānyāyaṃ ca pūjitam ||
children.translated_text: I wish to see him here, honored according to proper form.

children.text: tathetyuktvā tu te sarve punar āgamya rākṣasāḥ
children.translated_text: Saying 'So be it,' all those rākṣasas returned again
and, urged by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, said this speech to <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>:
The king, foremost of all rākṣasas, desires to see you.
Make up your mind to go; gladden your brother.
But invincible <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, having learned his brother's command,
said 'So be it,' and, mighty in valor, sprang up from his bed.
Having washed his face, delighted, bathed, and adorned with supreme ornaments,
he was thirsty and hastened them to bring drink that would stir his strength.
Then, hurried by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s command, those rākṣasas
quickly brought him wine and various foods.
After drinking a thousand jars, he began to set out.
Slightly excited, intoxicated, and endowed with splendor and strength,
<s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> shone joyfully, like <s>Yama</s> at the end of time.
Going to his brother's palace, accompanied by a force of rākṣasas,
<s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> made the earth tremble with his footsteps.

children.text: sa rājamārgaṃ vapuṣā prakāśayan sahasraraśmir dharaṇīm ivāṃśubhiḥ
children.translated_text: Illuminating the royal road with his body, as the thousand-rayed sun lights the earth with its rays,

children.text: jagāma tatrāñjalimālayā vṛtaḥ śatakratur geham iva svayambhuvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he went there, surrounded by a garland of joined palms, like <s>Śatakratu</s> going to the house of <s>Svayambhū</s>.

children.text: kecic charaṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ sma rāmaṃ vrajanti kecid vyathitāḥ patanti
children.translated_text: Some, distressed, went to <s>Rāma</s> as refuge and shelter; some fell down;

children.text: kecid diśaḥ sma vyathitāḥ prayānti kecid bhayārtā bhuvi śerate sma ||
children.translated_text: some fled in terror to the quarters, and some, afflicted by fear, lay on the ground.

children.text: tam adriśṛṅgapratimaṃ kirīṭinaṃ spṛśantam ādityam ivātmatejasā
children.translated_text: Seeing him, crowned and like a mountain peak, seeming to touch the sun with his own brilliance,

children.text: vanaukasaḥ prekṣya vivṛddham adbhutaṃ bhayārditā dudruvire tatastataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the forest-dwellers, beholding that huge and wondrous being, ran away in every direction, stricken with fear.

children.text: tato rāmo mahātejā dhanur ādāya vīryavān
children.translated_text: Then mighty <s>Rāma</s>, powerful and taking up his bow,
saw crowned, enormous <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>.
Seeing that best of rākṣasas, appearing like a mountain,
as if he were the ancient lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> striding across the sky,
resembling a rain-filled cloud and adorned with golden armlets,
the great army of monkeys again fled away.

children.text: vidrutāṃ vāhinīṃ dṛṣṭvā vardhamānaṃ ca rākṣasam
children.translated_text: Seeing the army routed and the rākṣasa growing greater,

children.text: savismayam idaṃ rāmo vibhīṣaṇam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, filled with amazement, said this to <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>:
Who is that hero, mountain-like, crowned, and tawny-eyed,

children.text: laṅkāyāṃ dṛśyate vīraḥ savidyud iva toyadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: who is seen in <s>Laṅkā</s> like a rain cloud with lightning?
That single great one is seen here as if he were the banner of the earth;

children.text: yaṃ dṛṣṭvā vānarāḥ sarve vidravanti tatastataḥ ||
children.translated_text: on seeing him all the monkeys run in every direction.

children.text: ācakṣva me mahān ko 'sau rakṣo vā yadi vāsuraḥ
children.translated_text: Tell me who that great one is, whether he is a rākṣasa or perhaps an asura.
Never before have I seen any being of such a kind.
Questioned by prince <s>Rāma</s>, whose acts are unwearied,
the very wise <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> said this to the <s>Kākutstha</s>:
He by whom <s>Vaivasvata</s> and <s>Vāsava</s> were defeated in battle,
this is that powerful <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, son of <s>Viśravas</s>.

children.text: etena devā yudhi dānavāśca yakṣā bhujaṃgāḥ piśitāśanāśca
children.translated_text: By him, in battle, the gods, the dānavas, the yakṣas, the serpents, and the flesh-eaters...
Gandharvas, Vidyādharas, and Kiṃnaras too were routed by the thousands, O <s>Rāghava</s>.
The Thirty Gods, deluded and thinking, "This is Time itself,"

children.text: hantuṃ na śekustridaśāḥ kālo 'yam iti mohitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: could not kill mighty <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, trident in hand and misshapen-eyed.
For by nature this mighty <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> is full of fiery power;
the strength of the other lords of rākṣasas was produced by the granting of boons.
By this great-souled one, as soon as he was born and tormented by hunger,
many thousands of creatures were devoured.
While they were being eaten up, the beings, oppressed by fear,

children.text: yānti sma śaraṇaṃ śakraṃ tam apyarthaṃ nyavedayan ||
children.translated_text: went to <s>Śakra</s> for refuge and reported that matter to him.

children.text: sa kumbhakarṇaṃ kupito mahendro jaghāna vajreṇa śitena vajrī
children.translated_text: Then angry great <s>Indra</s>, the wielder of the thunderbolt, struck <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> with his sharp thunderbolt;

children.text: sa śakravajrābhihato mahātmā cacāla kopācca bhṛśaṃ nanāda ||
children.translated_text: struck by <s>Śakra</s>'s thunderbolt, the great-souled one staggered and, in anger, roared terribly.
When wise <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> was roaring so,

children.text: śrutvā ninādaṃ vitrastā bhūyo bhūmir vitatrase ||
children.translated_text: the earth, hearing his roar and terrified, trembled again.
Then mighty <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, enraged at great <s>Indra</s>,
tore a tusk from <s>Airāvata</s> and struck <s>Vāsava</s> in the chest.
Hurt by <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>'s blow, <s>Vāsava</s> reeled;
then gods, brahmarṣis, and Dānavas at once sank into despair.

children.text: prajābhiḥ saha śakraśca yayau sthānaṃ svayambhuvaḥ
children.translated_text: Together with the creatures, <s>Śakra</s> went to the abode of <s>Svayambhū</s>.
They told <s>Prajāpati</s> of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>'s wickedness,

children.text: prajānāṃ bhakṣaṇaṃ cāpi devānāṃ cāpi dharṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: of his devouring of creatures and also of his assault upon the gods.

children.text: evaṃ prajā yadi tveṣa bhakṣayiṣyati nityaśaḥ
children.translated_text: If this one keeps devouring creatures in this way every day,
then in a very short time the world will become empty.
Hearing <s>Vāsava</s>'s words, the grandsire of all worlds
summoned the rākṣasas and saw <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>.
As soon as he looked upon <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s> was terrified;

children.text: dṛṣṭvā niśvasya caivedaṃ svayambhūr idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: seeing him, and sighing, <s>Svayambhū</s> spoke these words:
Surely you were fashioned by the <s>Paulastya</s> for the destruction of the worlds;

children.text: tasmāt tvam adya prabhṛti mṛtakalpaḥ śayiṣyasi
children.translated_text: therefore, from today onward you shall sleep as though dead.
Then, overpowered by <s>Brahmā</s>'s curse, he fell down before the lord.
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, greatly agitated, spoke these words:
A golden tree, grown tall, is cut down just when it is about to bear fruit.

children.text: na naptāraṃ svakaṃ nyāyyaṃ śaptum evaṃ prajāpate
children.translated_text: It is not right, O <s>Prajāpati</s>, to curse your own grandson in this way.

children.text: na mithyāvacanaśca tvaṃ svapsyatyeṣa na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Nor can your word be false; he will sleep, there is no doubt.

children.text: kālastu kriyatām asya śayane jāgare tathā ||
children.translated_text: But let a fixed time be appointed for his sleeping and likewise for his waking.

children.text: rāvaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā svayambhūr idam abravīt
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s words, <s>Svayambhū</s> said this:

children.text: śayitā hyeṣa ṣaṇ māsān ekāhaṃ jāgariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: He shall sleep for six months, and for one day he shall remain awake.
But in a single day that hero, roaming the earth while hungry,

children.text: vyāttāsyo bhakṣayel lokān saṃkruddha iva pāvakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: would devour the worlds with gaping mouth, like a raging fire.
That king <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, fallen into calamity, has awakened this <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>,
and at present he is afraid of your valor.

children.text: sa eṣa nirgato vīraḥ śibirād bhīmavikramaḥ
children.translated_text: This hero of terrible prowess has come out from the camp,
and, furiously enraged, he is running about devouring the vānaras.
At the mere sight of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, the monkeys have fled in all directions.

children.text: katham enaṃ raṇe kruddhaṃ vārayiṣyanti vānarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: How will the vānaras hold him back in battle when he is enraged?

children.text: ucyantāṃ vānarāḥ sarve yantram etat samucchritam
children.translated_text: Let all the vānaras be told, "This is a great engine raised up."
Knowing this, the monkeys here will become fearless.
Hearing <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>'s reasonable words, spoken from his fair mouth,

children.text: uvāca rāghavo vākyaṃ nīlaṃ senāpatiṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> then spoke to <s>Nīla</s>, the commander of the army:

children.text: gaccha sainyāni sarvāṇi vyūhya tiṣṭhasva pāvake
children.translated_text: Go, arrange all the forces, and stand ready, O <s>Pāvaka</s>;
take control of the gates of <s>Laṅkā</s>, and also the patrol routes and crossings.
Let all the vānaras gather mountain peaks, trees,
and stones too, and stand armed, with mountains in their hands.
Thus instructed by <s>Rāghava</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, lord of the monkey host,
that elephant among monkeys, commanded the vānara army properly.

children.text: tato gavākṣaḥ śarabho hanumān aṅgado nalaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Gavākṣa</s>, <s>Śarabha</s>, <s>Hanumān</s>, <s>Aṅgada</s>, and <s>Nala</s>,
mountain-like themselves, took up mountain peaks and went to the gate.

children.text: tato harīṇāṃ tad anīkam ugraṃ rarāja śailodyatavṛkṣahastam
children.translated_text: Then that fierce army of monkeys shone, with mountains raised and trees in hand,
just like a vast and dreadful mass of great rain clouds gathered near a mountain.
But that tiger among rākṣasas, confused with the intoxication of sleep,
went along the royal road, attended by splendor, with his vast stride.
Surrounded by thousands of rākṣasas, utterly hard to conquer,
he went on while showers of flowers were scattered from the houses.
He saw the broad, lovely dwelling of the lord of rākṣasas,
covered with golden latticework and shining with the brilliance of the sun.

children.text: sa tat tadā sūrya ivābhrajālaṃ praviśya rakṣo'dhipater niveśanam
children.translated_text: Then, entering the lord of rākṣasas' dwelling like the sun entering a bank of clouds,

children.text: dadarśa dūre 'grajam āsanasthaṃ svayambhuvaṃ śakra ivāsanastham ||
children.translated_text: he saw his elder brother far off, seated on a throne like <s>Svayambhū</s> or <s>Śakra</s> seated on his throne.

children.text: so 'bhigamya gṛhaṃ bhrātuḥ kakṣyām abhivigāhya ca
children.translated_text: Having approached his brother's house and passed into its inner court,
he saw his honored elder seated, anxious, in the <s>Puṣpaka</s> aerial palace.
Then, seeing <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> standing before him, <s>Daśagrīva</s>
quickly rose up in delight and drew him near.
Then mighty <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, seated on the couch,

children.text: bhrātur vavande caraṇau kiṃ kṛtyam iti cābravīt
children.translated_text: bowed to his brother's feet and said, "What is to be done?"
Joyful, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> sprang up and embraced him.
Embraced by his brother and duly greeted,
<s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> took his seat on a beautiful, divine, excellent throne.
Having settled on that seat, mighty <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>,
his eyes reddened with anger, spoke these words to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>:

children.text: kimartham aham ādṛtya tvayā rājan prabodhitaḥ
children.translated_text: For what purpose, O king, have you awakened me with such urgency?

children.text: śaṃsa kasmād bhayaṃ te 'sti ko 'dya preto bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Tell me why you are afraid. Who is to become a corpse today?
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> addressed his brother <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, who stood there enraged,

children.text: īṣat tu parivṛttābhyāṃ netrābhyāṃ vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: with his two eyes turned slightly aside, and said these words:

children.text: adya te sumahān kālaḥ śayānasya mahābala
children.translated_text: O mighty one, while you have been sleeping, a very great length of time has passed for you.

children.text: sukhitastvaṃ na jānīṣe mama rāmakṛtaṃ bhayam ||
children.translated_text: You have been at ease and do not know the fear caused to me by <s>Rāma</s>.
This powerful <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, together with <s>Sugrīva</s>,
has crossed the ocean with his army and is cutting away our root.
Come, look at the woods and pleasure-groves of <s>Laṅkā</s>.
Having come easily by means of a bridge, they have made them into one ocean of vānaras.

children.text: ye rākṣasā mukhyatamā hatāste vānarair yudhi
children.translated_text: Those foremost rākṣasas who were the very chief among us have been killed by vānaras in battle,

children.text: vānarāṇāṃ kṣayaṃ yuddhe na paśyāmi kadācana ||
children.translated_text: yet I never see any destruction of the vānaras in the fight.

children.text: sarvakṣapitakośaṃ ca sa tvam abhyavapadya mām
children.translated_text: Therefore come to my aid, now that my entire treasury has been exhausted,
and save this city, <s>Laṅkā</s>, in which only children and old men remain.

children.text: bhrātur arthe mahābāho kuru karma suduṣkaram
children.translated_text: For your brother's sake, O great-armed one, perform a deed very hard to accomplish.

children.text: mayaivaṃ noktapūrvo hi kaścid bhrātaḥ paraṃtapa
children.translated_text: Never before has anyone been addressed by me in this way, brother, O scorcher of foes.

children.text: tvayyasti mama ca snehaḥ parā saṃbhāvanā ca me ||
children.translated_text: For I have affection for you, and my regard for you is supreme.
In clashes between gods and asuras, O bull among rākṣasas,
you have often routed the gods, and the asuras too have been conquered by you in battle.

children.text: na hi te sarvabhūteṣu dṛśyate sadṛśo balī ||
children.translated_text: Among all beings no warrior equal to you in strength is seen.

children.text: kuruṣva me priyahitam etad uttamaṃ yathāpriyaṃ priyaraṇa bāndhavapriya
children.translated_text: Do for me this highest act, dear and beneficial, just as is pleasing, O lover of battle and dear to your kinsmen.

children.text: svatejasā vidhama sapatnavāhinīṃ śaradghanaṃ pavana ivodyato mahān ||
children.translated_text: By your own might scatter the enemy army, as a great rising wind scatters an autumn cloud.
Hearing the lamentation of that king of rākṣasas,
<s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> then spoke a word and laughed aloud:

children.text: dṛṣṭo doṣo hi yo 'smābhiḥ purā mantravinirṇaye
children.translated_text: The fault that we saw before, at the time when counsel was being decided,
has now been reached by you, because you were not intent on what was beneficial.

children.text: śīghraṃ khalvabhyupetaṃ tvāṃ phalaṃ pāpasya karmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The fruit of sinful action has indeed come upon you quickly,
just as falling into hells comes upon a doer of evil deeds.

children.text: prathamaṃ vai mahārāja kṛtyam etad acintitam
children.translated_text: At the outset, great king, this matter was not considered by you.
Acting only from the pride of valor, you did not examine the consequence.

children.text: yaḥ paścāt pūrvakāryāṇi kuryād aiśvaryam āsthitaḥ
children.translated_text: A man established in power who does earlier tasks afterward,

children.text: pūrvaṃ cottarakāryāṇi na sa veda nayānayau ||
children.translated_text: and later tasks beforehand, does not know policy from impolicy.
Actions that lack proper place and time, and are done as if reversed,
come to ruin, like oblations offered among those who are ritually impure.

children.text: trayāṇāṃ pañcadhā yogaṃ karmaṇāṃ yaḥ prapaśyati
children.translated_text: He who sees the fivefold application of the three kinds of action,

children.text: sacivaiḥ samayaṃ kṛtvā sa sabhye vartate pathi ||
children.translated_text: and makes agreement with his ministers, proceeds on the proper path in council.

children.text: yathāgamaṃ ca yo rājā samayaṃ vicikīrṣati
children.translated_text: And a king who wishes to make a decision according to rule
understands his ministers by his intelligence and also observes his friends.

children.text: dharmam arthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca sarvān vā rakṣasāṃ pate
children.translated_text: A man, O lord of rākṣasas, attends in due time to <s>dharma</s> (right order), <s>artha</s> (advantage), and <s>kāma</s> (desire),

children.text: bhajate puruṣaḥ kāle trīṇi dvandvāni vā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or to all three, or again to the three pairs formed from them.
But if, after hearing what is best among these three, one does not understand it,

children.text: rājā vā rājamātro vā vyarthaṃ tasya bahuśrutam ||
children.translated_text: whether he is a king or merely one connected with a king, his great learning is useless.

children.text: upapradānaṃ sāntvaṃ vā bhedaṃ kāle ca vikramam
children.translated_text: Gift, conciliation, division, and force at the proper time,

children.text: yogaṃ ca rakṣasāṃ śreṣṭha tāvubhau ca nayānayau ||
children.translated_text: and the application of policy, O best of rākṣasas: these two are policy and impolicy.

children.text: kāle dharmārthakāmān yaḥ saṃmantrya sacivaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: One who is self-controlled and, in time, deliberates with ministers and pursues <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s>

children.text: niṣevetātmavāṃl loke na sa vyasanam āpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: does not meet with calamity in the world.
Having considered what is to his own benefit and what should or should not be done here,
a king lives together with ministers who know the true nature of advantage.
Men of animal-like understanding, not knowing the meanings of the treatises,
desire, from mere boldness, to speak when they have been admitted into councils.

children.text: aśāstraviduṣāṃ teṣāṃ na kāryam ahitaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Their harmful speech should not be acted on, for they do not know the treatises
and are ignorant of the science of polity, though they desire vast prosperity.

children.text: ahitaṃ ca hitākāraṃ dhārṣṭyājjalpanti ye narāḥ
children.translated_text: Those men who, from insolence, babble what is harmful while it has the appearance of benefit
should, when recognized, be kept outside counsel as spoilers of affairs.
Ministers allied with clever enemies, destroying their master,
cause wrong-headed undertakings to be carried out here.
In decisions of counsel, the master should recognize those ministers who look like friends
but are enemies standing close by, through their conduct.
When a fickle man rushes after tasks in haste here,

children.text: chidram anye prapadyante krauñcasya kham iva dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: others find an opening, like birds finding the hollow of a krauñca mountain.

children.text: yo hi śatrum avajñāya nātmānam abhirakṣati
children.translated_text: For one who despises an enemy and does not protect himself
incurs misfortunes and is removed from his position.

children.text: tat tu śrutvā daśagrīvaḥ kumbhakarṇasya bhāṣitam
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, <s>Daśagrīva</s>

children.text: bhrukuṭiṃ caiva saṃcakre kruddhaścainam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: knitted his brow and, angered, said to him:

children.text: mānyo gurur ivācāryaḥ kiṃ māṃ tvam anuśāsasi
children.translated_text: Why do you instruct me like a venerable elder, a teacher?

children.text: kim evaṃ vākśramaṃ kṛtvā kāle yuktaṃ vidhīyatām ||
children.translated_text: What use is such labor of speech? Let what suits the present moment be done.
Whether through confusion, delusion of mind, or reliance on strength and valor,

children.text: nābhipannam idānīṃ yad vyarthāstasya punaḥ kṛthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: what has not been properly undertaken until now is useless for you to bring up again.

children.text: asmin kāle tu yad yuktaṃ tad idānīṃ vidhīyatām
children.translated_text: But what is fitting at this time, let that now be done.
By your prowess set right the fault born of my bad policy.

children.text: yadi khalvasti me sneho bhrātṛtvaṃ vāvagacchasi
children.translated_text: If indeed there is affection for me in you, or if you understand the bond of brotherhood,

children.text: yadi vā kāryam etat te hṛdi kāryatamaṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: or if this undertaking of mine is thought by you in your heart to be most urgent,

children.text: sa suhṛd yo vipannārthaṃ dīnam abhyavapadyate
children.translated_text: He is a friend who comes to the aid of one whose fortunes have failed and who is wretched;
he is a kinsman who stands ready to help when others have withdrawn.

children.text: tam athaivaṃ bruvāṇaṃ tu vacanaṃ dhīradāruṇam
children.translated_text: Then, as he was speaking in this way, with words both firm and harsh,

children.text: ruṣṭo 'yam iti vijñāya śanaiḥ ślakṣṇam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: knowing, "He is angry," he spoke slowly and gently.
For, observing that his brother's senses were greatly agitated,
<s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> slowly spoke these words, seeking to calm him:
Enough, lord of rākṣasa kings; it is not fitting for you to fall into distress.

children.text: roṣaṃ ca samparityajya svastho bhavitum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: Abandon anger as well, and you should become composed.
This should not be held in your mind while I am alive, O king.
I shall destroy the one on account of whom you are grieving.

children.text: avaśyaṃ tu hitaṃ vācyaṃ sarvāvasthaṃ mayā tava
children.translated_text: But in every condition I must speak what is beneficial to you;
what I have said was spoken from the feeling of kinship and from brotherly affection, O king.

children.text: sadṛśaṃ yat tu kāle 'smin kartuṃ snigdhena bandhunā
children.translated_text: But what is fitting now for an affectionate kinsman to do,

children.text: śatrūṇāṃ kadanaṃ paśya kriyamāṇaṃ mayā raṇe ||
children.translated_text: behold that being done by me in battle: the slaughter of the enemies.
Today, mighty-armed one, behold on the front of battle

children.text: hate rāme saha bhrātrā dravantīṃ harivāhinīm ||
children.translated_text: the monkey army fleeing when <s>Rāma</s> has been killed by me together with his brother.

children.text: adya rāmasya tad dṛṣṭvā mayānītaṃ raṇācchiraḥ
