children.translated_text: Today, when you see <s>Rāma</s>'s head brought by me from the battlefield,
be happy, mighty-armed one, and let <s>Sītā</s> be sorrowful.

children.text: adya rāmasya paśyantu nidhanaṃ sumahat priyam
children.translated_text: Today let all the rākṣasas in <s>Laṅkā</s>,

children.text: laṅkāyāṃ rākṣasāḥ sarve ye te nihatabāndhavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those whose kinsmen have been slain, see the greatly desired death of <s>Rāma</s>.
Today, for those overcome with grief because of the killing of their own kinsmen,
I shall wipe away their tears by destroying the enemy in battle.
Today behold <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the monkeys, mountain-like,
scattered in battle like a cloud with the sun.
No other man need be sent by you to battle, O warrior of unequalled valor.
I shall exterminate your enemies, mighty one.

children.text: yadi śakro yadi yamo yadi pāvakamārutau
children.translated_text: Whether it is <s>Śakra</s>, whether <s>Yama</s>, whether <s>Pāvaka</s> and <s>Māruta</s>,
I shall fight them, and <s>Kubera</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> too.
Of me, whose body is the size of a mountain and who carries a sharp spear,
roaring and sharp-fanged, even <s>Purandara</s> would be afraid.
Or, casting weapons aside and swiftly trampling my enemies,

children.text: na me pratimukhe kaścicchaktaḥ sthātuṃ jijīviṣuḥ ||
children.translated_text: no one who wishes to live can stand before my face.

children.text: naiva śaktyā na gadayā nāsinā na śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
children.translated_text: Not with spear, not with mace, not with sword, not with sharp arrows,
but enraged, with my two hands alone, I shall kill even <s>Vajrin</s>.

children.text: yadi me muṣṭivegaṃ sa rāghavo 'dya sahiṣyati
children.translated_text: If that <s>Rāghava</s> withstands the force of my fist today,

children.text: tataḥ pāsyanti bāṇaughā rudhiraṃ rāghavasya te ||
children.translated_text: then those floods of arrows will drink <s>Rāghava</s>'s blood.

children.text: cintayā bādhyase rājan kimarthaṃ mayi tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: Why are you oppressed by worry, O king, while I stand here?
I am ready to go out for the destruction of your enemy.

children.text: muñca rāmād bhayaṃ rājan haniṣyāmīha saṃyuge
children.translated_text: Give up fear of <s>Rāma</s>, O king; I shall kill here in battle

children.text: rāghavaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ caiva sugrīvaṃ ca mahābalam
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and mighty <s>Sugrīva</s> too.

children.text: asādhāraṇam icchāmi tava dātuṃ mahad yaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I wish to give you great glory beyond the common lot.

children.text: vadhena te dāśaratheḥ sukhāvahaṃ sukhaṃ samāhartum ahaṃ vrajāmi
children.translated_text: I go to gather for you the happiness that brings comfort through the killing of <s>Dāśarathi</s>.

children.text: nihatya rāmaṃ saha lakṣmaṇena khādāmi sarvān hariyūthamukhyān ||
children.translated_text: After killing <s>Rāma</s> together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, I shall eat all the chiefs of the monkey troops.

children.text: ramasva kāmaṃ piba cāgryavāruṇīṃ kuruṣva kṛtyāni vinīyatāṃ jvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Enjoy yourself as you wish; drink the finest vāruṇī liquor; perform your duties, and let your fever be driven away.

children.text: mayādya rāme gamite yamakṣayaṃ cirāya sītā vaśagā bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāma</s> has today been sent by me to <s>Yama</s>'s abode, <s>Sītā</s> will be subject to you for a long time.
Having heard that speech of the huge-bodied, strong, mighty-armed
<s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, <s>Mahodara</s> spoke:
Though born in the line of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, you are insolent and of common understanding.

children.text: avalipto na śaknoṣi kṛtyaṃ sarvatra veditum ||
children.translated_text: Puffed up, you are not able to understand what should be done in every situation.

children.text: na hi rājā na jānīte kumbhakarṇa nayānayau
children.translated_text: Surely the king does know policy and impolicy, <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>;

children.text: tvaṃ tu kaiśorakāddhṛṣṭaḥ kevalaṃ vaktum icchasi ||
children.translated_text: but you, insolent from childishness, merely wish to speak.

children.text: sthānaṃ vṛddhiṃ ca hāniṃ ca deśakālavibhāgavit
children.translated_text: One who knows the divisions of place and time understands position, growth, and decline,
both of himself and of others, bull among rākṣasas.

children.text: yat tu śakyaṃ balavatā kartuṃ prākṛtabuddhinā
children.translated_text: But what wise man would do such a thing, possible for a strong man of crude intellect,
who has not attended upon elders?
As for the <s>dharma</s> (right order), <s>artha</s> (advantage), and <s>kāma</s> (desire) of which you speak as having separate foundations,

children.text: anuboddhuṃ svabhāvena na hi lakṣaṇam asti te ||
children.translated_text: there is no sign in you, by nature, that you can understand them.

children.text: karma caiva hi sarveṣāṃ kāraṇānāṃ prayojanam
children.translated_text: Action itself is the purpose of all causes,

children.text: śreyaḥ pāpīyasāṃ cātra phalaṃ bhavati karmaṇām ||
children.translated_text: and here action has better or worse fruit.
<s>Dharma</s> and <s>artha</s> have the highest good as their fruit, as do the others also when rightly pursued;
but the attainment of <s>adharma</s> and ruin has a fruit that turns back in harm.
Action bearing on this world and the next is practiced by men;

children.text: karmāṇyapi tu kalpyāni labhate kāmam āsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but one who is set on desire obtains actions only as they are contrived.

children.text: tatra kﾱptam idaṃ rājñā hṛdi kāryaṃ mataṃ ca naḥ
children.translated_text: In this matter, this plan has been arranged by the king and is our considered opinion in the heart.

children.text: śatrau hi sāhasaṃ yat syāt kim ivātrāpanīyate ||
children.translated_text: For if there is boldness against the enemy, what objection is to be removed here?
But as to the reason you have put forward for a single man's expedition,

children.text: tatrāpyanupapannaṃ te vakṣyāmi yad asādhu ca ||
children.translated_text: there too I shall tell you what is untenable in you and what is unsound.
How will you alone conquer that <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: rākṣasā rāghavaṃ taṃ tvaṃ katham eko jayiṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: by whom many very powerful rākṣasas were formerly killed in <s>Janasthāna</s>?
Those mighty rākṣasas who were conquered by him long ago in <s>Janasthāna</s>,

children.text: rākṣasāṃstān pure sarvān bhītān adyāpi paśyasi ||
children.translated_text: you still see them all afraid in the city today.

children.text: taṃ siṃham iva saṃkruddhaṃ rāmaṃ daśarathātmajam
children.translated_text: You wish, in your folly, to awaken <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>,
enraged like a lion, like a sleeping serpent.

children.text: jvalantaṃ tejasā nityaṃ krodhena ca durāsadam
children.translated_text: Blazing always with energy and hard to approach in anger,
who deserves to encounter him, unbearable like death?
This whole matter is doubtful when confronting the enemy;

children.text: ekasya gamanaṃ tatra na hi me rocate tava ||
children.translated_text: your going there alone does not please me.

children.text: hīnārthastu samṛddhārthaṃ ko ripuṃ prākṛto yathā
children.translated_text: For what ordinary man, having small means, would wish to bring a prosperous enemy under his control,
when he has resolved upon the abandonment of his own life?
O best of rākṣasas, he has no equal among men;
how do you expect to fight him as an equal of <s>Indra</s> and <s>Vivasvat</s>?

children.text: evam uktvā tu saṃrabdhaṃ kumbhakarṇaṃ mahodaraḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken to the enraged <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, <s>Mahodara</s>
spoke in the midst of the rākṣasas to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, who makes the worlds cry out:

children.text: labdhvā punastāṃ vaidehīṃ kimarthaṃ tvaṃ prajalpasi
children.translated_text: After obtaining that <s>Vaidehī</s> again, why are you talking so much?

children.text: yadecchasi tadā sītā vaśagā te bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: When you desire it, then <s>Sītā</s> will become subject to your will.
I have seen a certain stratagem that will bring about <s>Sītā</s>'s attendance upon you;

children.text: rucitaścet svayā buddhyā rākṣaseśvara taṃ śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: if it is pleasing to your own judgment, lord of rākṣasas, hear it.
Proclaim this: 'I, <s>Dvijihva</s>, <s>Saṃhrādī</s>, <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, and <s>Vitardana</s>,
these five, are setting out to kill <s>Rāma</s>.'

children.text: tato gatvā vayaṃ yuddhaṃ dāsyāmastasya yatnataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, having gone, we shall carefully offer battle to him.

children.text: jeṣyāmo yadi te śatrūnnopāyaiḥ kṛtyam asti naḥ ||
children.translated_text: If we conquer your enemies, we have no need of stratagems.

children.text: atha jīvati naḥ śatrur vayaṃ ca kṛtasaṃyugāḥ
children.translated_text: But if our enemy is still alive, and we too have fought the battle,
then we shall carry out what is to be considered in our minds.
We shall come back here from the battle sprinkled with blood,
having torn our own bodies with sharp arrows marked with <s>Rāma</s>'s name.
Saying, '<s>Rāghava</s> has been devoured by us, and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> too,'

children.text: tava pādau grahīṣyāmastvaṃ naḥ kāmaṃ prapūraya ||
children.translated_text: we shall grasp your feet; you should fulfill our desire.
Then, O king, have it proclaimed everywhere in the city from the shoulder of an elephant:

children.text: hato rāmaḥ saha bhrātrā sasainya iti sarvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Rāma</s> has been slain together with his brother and his army.'

children.text: prīto nāma tato bhūtvā bhṛtyānāṃ tvam ariṃdama
children.translated_text: Then, appearing pleased, O subduer of enemies,
give wealth, enjoyments, retinues, and pleasures to your servants.
Then give garlands, garments, and unguents suited to heroes,

children.text: peyaṃ ca bahu yodhebhyaḥ svayaṃ ca muditaḥ piba ||
children.translated_text: and abundant drink to the warriors; and drink yourself, delighted.
Then, when this rumor has become widespread and has gone everywhere,

children.text: praviśyāśvāsya cāpi tvaṃ sītāṃ rahasi sāntvaya
children.translated_text: enter, reassure <s>Sītā</s>, and conciliate her in private,
and tempt her with wealth, grain, pleasures, and jewels.
By this trick, O king, attended by fear and grief,
unwilling <s>Sītā</s>, bereft of her protector, will come under your control.

children.text: rañjanīyaṃ hi bhartāraṃ vinaṣṭam avagamya sā
children.translated_text: For, knowing her husband, whom she ought to delight, to have perished,
through despair and through the frailty of a woman she will submit to your will.
She, formerly raised in comfort, deserving comfort, and now worn down by sorrow,
knowing that happiness depends on you, will by every means come to you.

children.text: etat sunītaṃ mama darśanena rāmaṃ hi dṛṣṭvaiva bhaved anarthaḥ
children.translated_text: In my view this is good policy; for merely seeing <s>Rāma</s> would bring disaster.

children.text: ihaiva te setsyati motsuko bhūr mahān ayuddhena sukhasya lābhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Your aim will succeed right here; do not be anxious. There will be a great gain of happiness without battle.

children.text: anaṣṭasainyo hyanavāptasaṃśayo ripūn ayuddhena jayañ janādhipa
children.translated_text: For a king who has not lost his army, who has not incurred uncertainty, and who conquers his enemies without battle,

children.text: yaśaśca puṇyaṃ ca mahanmahīpate śriyaṃ ca kīrtiṃ ca ciraṃ samaśnute ||
children.translated_text: long enjoys great fame and merit, O great king, as well as prosperity and renown.
But when he had been addressed in that way, <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> rebuked <s>Mahodara</s>
and then spoke to his brother <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the foremost of rākṣasas:

children.text: so 'haṃ tava bhayaṃ ghoraṃ vadhāt tasya durātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: I myself today will wipe away your terrible fear arising from the killing power
of that evil-minded <s>Rāma</s>; be free from enmity and happy.

children.text: garjanti na vṛthā śūrā nirjalā iva toyadāḥ
children.translated_text: Heroes do not roar in vain like clouds without water;

children.text: paśya saṃpādyamānaṃ tu garjitaṃ yudhi karmaṇā ||
children.translated_text: watch this roar being made good in battle by action.
A hero does not vaunt himself or think highly of himself;
without displaying themselves beforehand, heroes perform deeds difficult to do.
While faint-hearted, foolish kings who think themselves wise,
kings like you, <s>Mahodara</s>, listen from the beginning to such counsel,
by cowards in war, by men like you who always speak pleasing words
and follow the king, this necessary business has been ruined.

children.text: rājaśeṣā kṛtā laṅkā kṣīṇaḥ kośo balaṃ hatam
children.translated_text: <s>Laṅkā</s> has been reduced to the king alone; the treasury is exhausted, the army destroyed,
because this king has fallen in with a false friend bearing the marks of a well-wisher.
Now I go out to battle, intent on conquering the enemy,
to set right today in the great fight the bad policy of you all.
When wise <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> had spoken this speech,
the lord of rākṣasas then replied, laughing:

children.text: mahodaro 'yaṃ rāmāt tu paritrasto na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: This <s>Mahodara</s> is terrified of <s>Rāma</s>, no doubt;

children.text: na hi rocayate tāta yuddhaṃ yuddhaviśārada ||
children.translated_text: for, dear one skilled in battle, he does not approve of fighting.

children.text: kaścinme tvatsamo nāsti sauhṛdena balena ca
children.translated_text: There is no one equal to you in friendship toward me or in strength;

children.text: gaccha śatruvadhāya tvaṃ kumbhakarṇa jayāya ca ||
children.translated_text: go, <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, to slay the enemy and to win victory.
The destroyer of enemies quickly took up a sharp spear,
made entirely of black iron, blazing, and adorned with heated gold,
terrible like <s>Indra</s>'s thunderbolt and heavy as a vajra,
capable of destroying gods, dānavas, gandharvas, yakṣas, and kinnaras,
wreathed with great red garlands and issuing fire of itself.
Taking up that sharp spear, stained with the blood of enemies,
mighty <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, of great splendor, spoke this speech to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>:
I shall go alone; let the great army remain here.

children.text: adya tān kṣudhitaḥ kruddho bhakṣayiṣyāmi vānarān ||
children.translated_text: Today, hungry and enraged, I shall devour those monkeys.
Hearing <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>'s words, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> spoke this speech:
Go surrounded by troops bearing spears and clubs.
For the great-souled monkeys are swift and resolute.

children.text: ekākinaṃ pramattaṃ vā nayeyur daśanaiḥ kṣayam ||
children.translated_text: or, if he were alone or heedless, they would bring him to destruction with their teeth.
Therefore go surrounded by armies most difficult to assail,
and destroy the whole enemy faction, hostile to the rākṣasas.
Then, springing up from his seat, he took a garland interspersed with jewels,
and mighty <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, of great splendor, fastened it upon <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>.
Armlets, finger-rings, and excellent ornaments,
and a necklace shining like the moon he fastened on the great-souled one.
And <s>Rāvaṇa</s> put on him divine, fragrant wreaths of garlands,
and he attached splendid earrings to his ears.
With golden armlets and bracelets, adorned with niṣka-ornaments,
<s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, of great ears, shone like a well-kindled fire.
He was resplendent with a great black girdle at his hips,
like Mount <s>Mandara</s> bound by the serpent at the churning of the nectar.

children.text: sa kāñcanaṃ bhārasahaṃ nivātaṃ vidyutprabhaṃ dīptam ivātmabhāsā
children.translated_text: As the golden armor, able to bear great weight, windproof, and blazing with lightning-like radiance and its own brilliance,
was being fastened on him, he shone like the king of mountains wrapped in evening cloud.
That rākṣasa, all his limbs bound with ornaments and with a spear in his hand,
appeared like <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, filled with the zeal of the three strides.
He embraced his brother and also circumambulated him,
bowed his head to him, and the mighty one set out;
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> sent him forth with noble blessings.
With the sounds of conches and kettledrums, and with troops bearing excellent weapons,
with elephants, horses, and chariots roaring like clouds,
chariot-warriors followed that great-souled one, the best of chariot-warriors.
With serpents, camels, donkeys, horses, lions, elephants, beasts, and birds,
they followed that terrible and mighty <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>.
Strewn with flowers of many colors, holding a parasol, and with a sharp spear in hand,
wild with rut and maddened by the scent of blood, the enemy of Dānavas and gods went out.
Many foot soldiers too, loud-roaring and very strong,
fearsome rākṣasas with dreadful eyes and weapons in hand, followed him.
Red-eyed, of enormous bodies, like masses of dark collyrium,
they raised spears, swords, and sharp axes,
and broad throwing weapons many fathoms long, hard to withstand,
and huge palm trunks, missiles hard to withstand.
Then, taking on another form, dreadful and making the hair stand on end,
the mighty, very splendid <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> rushed forth.
He measured a hundred bows in girth and rose six hundred bows high,
terrible, with eyes like cartwheels, resembling a great mountain.
Coming together with the rākṣasas, huge like a burned mountain,
<s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, great-mouthed, laughed and said this:
Today, portion by portion, the troops of the chief vānaras
I shall burn up in fury, like fire burning locusts.
The forest-roaming vānaras have not really offended me;
that race is an adornment of the pleasure-groves for beings such as us.
But the root of the siege of the city is <s>Rāghava</s> together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>;

children.text: hate tasmin hataṃ sarvaṃ taṃ vadhiṣyāmi saṃyuge ||
children.translated_text: when he is killed, everything is killed. I shall slay him in battle.
As <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> was speaking thus, the rākṣasas
made a most dreadful roar, as if shaking the ocean.
As wise <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> was going forth swiftly,
terrifying omens arose everywhere.
Clouds joined with meteors and thunderbolts roared most terribly,
and the earth, together with ocean and forest, shook.
Jackals of dreadful form howled, with fiery morsels in their mouths,
and birds formed circles to the left.

children.text: niṣpapāta ca gṛdhro 'sya śūle vai pathi gacchataḥ
children.translated_text: A vulture alighted on his spear as he was going along the road,
and his eye twitched, and his left arm trembled.
Then a blazing meteor fell with a terrifying sound,
and the sun became dim; no pleasant wind blew.
Disregarding the great portents that had arisen, making the hair stand on end,
<s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> went out, driven by the power of Death.
Having crossed the rampart on foot, mountain-like,
he saw the marvelous army of vānaras, resembling a mass of rain-clouds.
Seeing the foremost rākṣasa, like a mountain,

children.text: vāyununnā iva ghanā yayuḥ sarvā diśastadā ||
children.translated_text: the vānaras, like clouds driven by wind, went then in every direction.

children.text: tad vānarānīkam atipracaṇḍaṃ diśo dravad bhinnam ivābhrajālam
children.translated_text: Seeing that extremely fierce army of vānaras running to the directions, broken like a mass of clouds,

children.text: sa kumbhakarṇaḥ samavekṣya harṣān nanāda bhūyo ghanavad ghanābhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: cloud-dark <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> roared again with delight, like a cloud.

children.text: te tasya ghoraṃ ninadaṃ niśamya yathā ninādaṃ divi vāridasya
children.translated_text: Hearing that dreadful roar of his, like the roar of a rain-cloud in the sky,

children.text: petur dharaṇyāṃ bahavaḥ plavaṃgā nikṛttamūlā iva sālavṛkṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: many leaping vānaras fell to the ground like śāla trees cut off at the roots.

children.text: vipulaparighavān sa kumbhakarṇo ripunidhanāya viniḥsṛto mahātmā
children.translated_text: Mighty <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, bearing a huge iron club, had gone out for the destruction of his enemies,

children.text: kapigaṇabhayam ādadat subhīmaṃ prabhur iva kiṃkaradaṇḍavān yugānte ||
children.translated_text: bringing terrible fear upon the troops of monkeys, like the lord of death at the end of the age, staff-bearing and attended by servants.
He roared a mighty roar, making the ocean resound,

children.text: janayann iva nirghātān vidhamann iva parvatān ||
children.translated_text: as if producing thunderclaps and shattering mountains.

children.text: tam avadhyaṃ maghavatā yamena varuṇena ca
children.translated_text: Seeing him, invulnerable to <s>Maghavat</s>, <s>Yama</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s>,
approaching with dreadful eyes, the vānaras scattered in flight.
But seeing them fleeing, <s>Aṅgada</s>, the son of <s>Vāli</s>, said:

children.text: nalaṃ nīlaṃ gavākṣaṃ ca kumudaṃ ca mahābalam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nala</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, <s>Gavākṣa</s>, and mighty <s>Kumuda</s>!
Forgetting yourselves here, and your heroic deeds and noble lineages,

children.text: kva gacchata bhayatrastāḥ prākṛtā harayo yathā ||
children.translated_text: where are you going, terrified with fear, like ordinary monkeys?

children.text: sādhu saumyā nivartadhvaṃ kiṃ prāṇān parirakṣatha
children.translated_text: Good sirs, gentle ones, turn back. Why are you trying to preserve your lives?

children.text: nālaṃ yuddhāya vai rakṣo mahatīyaṃ vibhīṣikā ||
children.translated_text: The rākṣasa is not equal to battle; this is only a great terror.
This great terror of the rākṣasas that has arisen,
we shall scatter by our valor. Turn back, O leaping ones.

children.text: kṛcchreṇa tu samāśvāsya saṃgamya ca tatastataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after being reassured with difficulty and gathering from here and there,
the monkeys, with trees and mountain-peaks in their hands, set out for the battlefield.

children.text: te nivṛtya tu saṃkruddhāḥ kumbhakarṇaṃ vanaukasaḥ
children.translated_text: But turning back in fury, the forest-dwellers
struck <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, exceedingly enraged, like rutting elephants,
with lofty mountain-peaks and stones, mighty as they were.
Though struck with trees whose tops were in flower, he did not tremble.

children.text: tasya gātreṣu patitā bhidyante śataśaḥ śilāḥ
children.translated_text: The stones that fell on his body shattered by the hundreds,
and the flowering-topped trees broke and fell upon the ground.
He too, enraged, crushed the armies of the powerful vānaras,
fully exerting himself, like a fire rising through forests.
Many bull-like vānaras, wet with blood, lay there,

children.text: nirastāḥ patitā bhūmau tāmrapuṣpā iva drumāḥ ||
children.translated_text: hurled down and fallen on the earth, like trees with copper-red blossoms.
The vānaras, leaping and running, did not look back.

children.text: kecit samudre patitāḥ kecid gaganam āśritāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Some fell into the ocean; some took refuge in the sky.
As those heroes were being slain by the very strong rākṣasa,

children.text: sāgaraṃ yena te tīrṇāḥ pathā tenaiva dudruvuḥ ||
children.translated_text: they ran back by the very path by which they had crossed the ocean.

children.text: te sthalāni tathā nimnaṃ viṣaṇṇavadanā bhayāt
children.translated_text: Over level places and low ground, their faces dejected from fear,

children.text: ṛkṣā vṛkṣān samārūḍhāḥ kecit parvatam āśritāḥ ||
children.translated_text: some bears climbed trees, and some took refuge on a mountain.

children.text: mamajjur arṇave kecid guhāḥ kecit samāśritāḥ
children.translated_text: Some plunged into the sea; some entered caves.
Some leaping monkeys sat down, while others did not stand firm at all.

children.text: tān samīkṣyāṅgado bhagnān vānarān idam abravīt
children.translated_text: Seeing those vānaras broken, <s>Aṅgada</s> said this:
Stand firm. Let us fight. Turn back, O leaping ones.

children.text: bhagnānāṃ vo na paśyāmi parigamya mahīm imām
children.translated_text: For you who are broken, after roaming over this earth,

children.text: sthānaṃ sarve nivartadhvaṃ kiṃ prāṇān parirakṣatha ||
children.translated_text: I see no place of safety. All of you turn back. Why are you trying to preserve your lives?
If you flee unarmed, with your course and manhood disordered,

children.text: dārā hyapahasiṣyanti sa vai ghātastu jīvatām ||
children.translated_text: your wives will surely laugh at you; that indeed is death for the living.

children.text: kuleṣu jātāḥ sarve sma vistīrṇeṣu mahatsu ca
children.translated_text: We have all been born in broad and great families.

children.text: anāryāḥ khalu yad bhītāstyaktvā vīryaṃ pradhāvata ||
children.translated_text: You are surely ignoble, since, frightened, you run away after abandoning valor.

children.text: vikatthanāni vo yāni yadā vai janasaṃsadi
children.translated_text: Those boastful words of yours, which you spoke in the assembly of men,

children.text: tāni vaḥ kva ca yatāni sodagrāṇi mahānti ca ||
children.translated_text: where have those proud and mighty words of yours gone?
The reproach of cowardice is heard against a man who lives in disgrace.

children.text: mārgaḥ satpuruṣair juṣṭaḥ sevyatāṃ tyajyatāṃ bhayam ||
children.translated_text: Follow the path practiced by good men; abandon fear.
Either, with our lives brief, we shall lie slain upon the earth,

children.text: duṣprāpaṃ brahmalokaṃ vā prāpnumo yudhi sūditāḥ
children.translated_text: or, struck down in battle, we shall attain the hard-to-reach world of <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: samprāpnuyāmaḥ kīrtiṃ vā nihatya śatrum āhave ||
children.translated_text: or we shall gain fame by killing the enemy in combat.

children.text: na kumbhakarṇaḥ kākutsthaṃ dṛṣṭvā jīvan gamiṣyati
children.translated_text: <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> will not go away alive after seeing <s>Kākutstha</s>,
just as a moth, coming upon a blazing fire, does not survive.
Known for flight, we are trying to save our lives;

children.text: ekena bahavo bhagnā yaśo nāśaṃ gamiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: many broken by one alone: our fame will go to ruin.

children.text: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ taṃ śūram aṅgadaṃ kanakāṅgadam
children.translated_text: As the heroic <s>Aṅgada</s>, wearing a golden armlet, spoke thus,
the fleeing ones then spoke words condemned by heroes:

children.text: kṛtaṃ naḥ kadanaṃ ghoraṃ kumbhakarṇena rakṣasā
children.translated_text: A dreadful slaughter has been made of us by the rākṣasa <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>.

children.text: na sthānakālo gacchāmo dayitaṃ jīvitaṃ hi naḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is no time to stand. Let us go, for life is dear to us.

children.text: etāvad uktvā vacanaṃ sarve te bhejire diśaḥ
children.translated_text: Having said only this statement, all of them scattered to the quarters,
when the leaders of the vānaras saw the fearsome, terrible-eyed one coming.
But as those monkey-faced heroes were running away,
they were all turned back by <s>Aṅgada</s> with consolations and honors.
<s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Śarabha</s>, <s>Mainda</s>, <s>Dhūmra</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, <s>Kumuda</s>, <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, <s>Gavākṣa</s>, <s>Rambha</s>, and <s>Tārā</s>,
with <s>Dvivida</s>, <s>Panasa</s>, and the chief son of <s>Vāyu</s> among them, went very swiftly toward the battle.
Those great-bodied ones, having turned back when they heard <s>Aṅgada</s>'s words,
adopted a firm resolve, all of them eager for battle.
Their valor was stirred up and their prowess lifted high;
the monkey-faced warriors were steadied by <s>Aṅgada</s>'s words.
They advanced and became joyful, having resolved upon death.
The vānaras, abandoning their lives, made a very tumultuous battle.
Then the great-bodied vānaras quickly raised up trees
and very great mountain ridges, and rushed against <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>.

children.text: sa kumbhakarṇaḥ saṃkruddho gadām udyamya vīryavān
children.translated_text: That powerful <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, enraged, lifted his mace,
and, huge-bodied, crushed and scattered his enemies on every side.

children.text: śatāni sapta cāṣṭau ca sahasrāṇi ca vānarāḥ
children.translated_text: Seven hundreds and eight thousands of vānaras
lay scattered on the ground, struck down by <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>.

children.text: ṣoḍaśāṣṭau ca daśa ca viṃśat triṃśat tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Sixteen, eight, ten, twenty, and thirty at a time,
he enclosed them with his two arms and ran about eating them.
Very enraged, he devoured them like <s>Garuḍa</s> devouring serpents.
<s>Hanumān</s>, stationed in the sky, sent down mountain-peaks
and many various trees upon <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>'s head.

children.text: tāni parvataśṛṅgāṇi śūlena tu bibheda ha
children.translated_text: But he split those mountain-peaks with his spear,
and mighty <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> shattered the rain of trees.

children.text: tato harīṇāṃ tad anīkam ugraṃ dudrāva śūlaṃ niśitaṃ pragṛhya
children.translated_text: Then that fierce army of the monkeys ran away, while he grasped a sharp spear.

children.text: tasthau tato 'syāpatataḥ purastān mahīdharāgraṃ hanumān pragṛhya ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Hanumān</s>, seizing the peak of a mountain, stood before him as he came rushing on.

children.text: sa kumbhakarṇaṃ kupito jaghāna vegena śailottamabhīmakāyam
children.translated_text: Angered, he struck <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, whose terrible body was like the best of mountains, with force.

children.text: sa cukṣubhe tena tadābhibhūto medārdragātro rudhirāvasiktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Overwhelmed by that blow, he shook, his limbs wet with fat and drenched in blood.

children.text: sa śūlam āvidhya taḍitprakāśaṃ giriṃ yathā prajvalitāgraśṛṅgam
children.translated_text: Then, brandishing his lightning-bright spear, like a mountain with its summit blazing,

children.text: bāhvantare mārutim ājaghāna guho 'calaṃ krauñcam ivograśaktyā ||
children.translated_text: he struck <s>Māruti</s> between the arms, as <s>Guha</s> struck the <s>Krauñca</s> mountain with his fierce lance.
<s>Hanumān</s>, his great space between the arms pierced by the spear, reeled and vomited blood from his mouth;
in the great battle he roared terribly, with a sound like the thunder of a cloud at the end of an age.

children.text: tato vineduḥ sahasā prahṛṣṭā rakṣogaṇāstaṃ vyathitaṃ samīkṣya
children.translated_text: Then the hosts of rākṣasas suddenly shouted with joy when they saw him wounded,

children.text: plavaṃgamāstu vyathitā bhayārtāḥ pradudruvuḥ saṃyati kumbhakarṇāt ||
children.translated_text: while the leaping monkeys, distressed and terrified, fled from <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> in the battle.
<s>Nīla</s> hurled a mountain peak at wise <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>;
seeing it falling upon him, he struck it with his fist.
That mountain peak, struck by the blow of his fist, shattered;
with sparks and flames it fell to the earth.
<s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Śarabha</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, <s>Gavākṣa</s>, and <s>Gandhamādana</s>,
five tiger-like chiefs of the monkeys, rushed upon <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>.
Mighty as they were, with rocks, trees, palms, feet, and fists,
they struck huge-bodied <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> on every side.

children.text: sparśān iva prahārāṃstān vedayāno na vivyathe
children.translated_text: Feeling those blows as mere touches, he was not shaken;
but he clasped swift <s>Ṛṣabha</s> with both arms.
Crushed by the arms of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, that bull among monkeys,
the terrible <s>Ṛṣabha</s> fell down, blood coming from his face.

children.text: muṣṭinā śarabhaṃ hatvā jānunā nīlam āhave
children.translated_text: After striking <s>Śarabha</s> with his fist and <s>Nīla</s> with his knee in the battle,
that enemy of <s>Indra</s> then struck <s>Gavākṣa</s> with his palm.
Tormented by the blows he had delivered and sprinkled with blood, they fainted;

children.text: nipetuste tu medinyāṃ nikṛttā iva kiṃśukāḥ ||
children.translated_text: they fell on the ground like severed kiṃśuka trees.
When those great-souled chief monkeys had fallen,
thousands of monkeys ran at <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>.

children.text: taṃ śailam iva śailābhāḥ sarve tu plavagarṣabhāḥ
children.translated_text: All those bull-like leapers, mountain-like themselves, climbed upon him as upon a mountain;
springing up, the mighty ones bit him too.
With nails and teeth, and likewise with fists and knees,
those bull-like leapers struck huge-bodied <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>.
Covered by those thousands of monkeys, he, who was like a mountain,
the tiger among rākṣasas, shone like a mountain covered with trees grown from itself.

children.text: bāhubhyāṃ vānarān sarvān pragṛhya sa mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: Seizing all the monkeys with his two arms, that mighty one,
in fury devoured them like <s>Garuḍa</s> devouring serpents.
Thrown by <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> into his mouth, which resembled the underworld,
the monkeys came out through his nostrils and also through his ears.
Devouring the monkeys in great fury, that rākṣasa, mountain-like in form,
that foremost rākṣasa, enraged, crushed all the monkeys.
Making the ground muddy with flesh and blood, that rākṣasa
moved among the monkey troops like the fire of time run wild.
Like <s>Śakra</s> with the thunderbolt in his hand, like <s>Antaka</s> with the noose in his hand,
mighty <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> appeared there with the spear in his hand.
As fire burns dry forests in summer,
so <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> was consuming the monkey armies.
Then the monkeys, being slaughtered, their troop-leaders slain, without commanders,
and shaken with fear, cried out loudly with discordant voices.
Being slain again and again by <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, the monkeys,
distressed and weary in mind, went to <s>Rāghava</s> for refuge.
Seeing mighty <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> rushing on,
the heroic monkey-king <s>Sugrīva</s> then leapt up.
Lifting up a mountain peak and whirling it about, the great monkey
rushed swiftly against mighty <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>.
Seeing that leaper coming upon him, <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>
stood with all his limbs laid open, facing the lord of monkeys.
Seeing <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> standing there, his limbs smeared with monkey blood and devouring great monkeys,

children.text: kumbhakarṇaṃ sthitaṃ dṛṣṭvā sugrīvo vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s> spoke these words:

children.text: pātitāśca tvayā vīrāḥ kṛtaṃ karma suduṣkaram
children.translated_text: Heroes have been felled by you, and a very difficult deed has been done;

children.text: bhakṣitāni ca sainyāni prāptaṃ te paramaṃ yaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the armies have been devoured, and supreme fame has come to you.

children.text: tyaja tad vānarānīkaṃ prākṛtaiḥ kiṃ kariṣyasi
children.translated_text: Leave that monkey army. What will you do with common creatures?
Endure this one fall of my mountain, O rākṣasa.
Hearing that speech of the monkey king, endowed with spirit and firmness,
<s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, the tiger among rākṣasas, spoke these words:
You are the grandson of <s>Prajāpati</s>, and likewise the son of <s>Ṛkṣarajas</s>;
you are endowed with renowned valor, and therefore you roar, O monkey.

children.text: sa kumbhakarṇasya vaco niśamya vyāvidhya śailaṃ sahasā mumoca
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>'s words, he suddenly whirled the mountain and let it fly;
with that mountain, resembling a thunderbolt or lightning-flash, he struck <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> on the chest.

children.text: tacchailaśṛṅgaṃ sahasā vikīrṇaṃ bhujāntare tasya tadā viśāle
children.translated_text: That mountain peak was suddenly shattered then on the broad space between his arms;

children.text: tato viṣeduḥ sahasā plavaṃgamā rakṣogaṇāścāpi mudā vineduḥ ||
children.translated_text: thereupon the leaping monkeys suddenly became despondent, while the hosts of rākṣasas shouted with joy.

children.text: sa śailaśṛṅgābhihataścukopa nanāda kopācca vivṛtya vaktram
children.translated_text: Struck by the mountain peak, he grew angry and, from anger, roared with his mouth wide open.

children.text: vyāvidhya śūlaṃ ca taḍitprakāśaṃ cikṣepa haryṛkṣapater vadhāya ||
children.translated_text: Brandishing his spear, flashing like lightning, he hurled it to kill the lord of the monkeys and bears.

children.text: tat kumbhakarṇasya bhujapraviddhaṃ śūlaṃ śitaṃ kāñcanadāmajuṣṭam
children.translated_text: That sharp spear, hurled from <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>'s arm and adorned with bands of gold,

children.text: kṣipraṃ samutpatya nigṛhya dorbhyāṃ babhañja vegena suto 'nilasya ||
children.translated_text: the son of the Wind swiftly leapt up, seized with both arms, and broke by his force.
That great spear of black iron, made to weigh a thousand bhāras,
the delighted bull among leapers set upon his knee and broke.

children.text: sa tat tadā bhagnam avekṣya śūlaṃ cukopa rakṣo'dhipatir mahātmā
children.translated_text: Seeing that spear broken then, the great-souled lord of rākṣasas became enraged;

children.text: utpāṭya laṅkāmalayāt sa śṛṅgaṃ jaghāna sugrīvam upetya tena ||
children.translated_text: uprooting a peak from <s>Laṅkā</s>'s <s>Malaya</s>, he approached <s>Sugrīva</s> and struck him with it.

children.text: sa śailaśṛṅgābhihato visaṃjñaḥ papāta bhūmau yudhi vānarendraḥ
children.translated_text: Struck by the mountain peak, the king of monkeys lost consciousness and fell to the ground in battle;

children.text: taṃ prekṣya bhūmau patitaṃ visaṃjñaṃ neduḥ prahṛṣṭā yudhi yātudhānāḥ ||
children.translated_text: seeing him lying senseless on the ground, the yātudhānas roared joyfully in the fight.

children.text: tam abhyupetyādbhutaghoravīryaṃ sa kumbhakarṇo yudhi vānarendram
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> approached that monkey-king, whose valor was wondrous and terrible, in battle;

children.text: jahāra sugrīvam abhipragṛhya yathānilo megham atipracaṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: seizing <s>Sugrīva</s> firmly, he carried him off, as an exceedingly violent wind carries a cloud.

children.text: sa taṃ mahāmeghanikāśarūpam utpāṭya gacchan yudhi kumbhakarṇaḥ
children.translated_text: As <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, whose form was like a great cloud, went along in battle carrying him away,
he, with a form resembling <s>Meru</s>, shone like <s>Meru</s> with its lofty and terrible peaks.

children.text: tataḥ samutpāṭya jagāma vīraḥ saṃstūyamāno yudhi rākṣasendraiḥ
children.translated_text: Then the hero went on, lifting him up, while he was praised in battle by the lords of the rākṣasas,
and while he heard the roar of the dwellers in the gods' abodes, amazed at the capture of the king of leapers.

children.text: tatastam ādāya tadā sa mene harīndram indropamam indravīryaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, holding him at that time, that enemy of <s>Indra</s>, with <s>Indra</s>'s valor, regarded the lord of monkeys as equal to <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: asmin hṛte sarvam idaṃ hṛtaṃ syāt sarāghavaṃ sainyam itīndraśatruḥ ||
children.translated_text: thinking, 'When this one has been carried off, this whole army, together with <s>Rāghava</s>, will have been carried off.'
Seeing the army of monkeys fleeing in every direction,
and seeing <s>Sugrīva</s>, the monkey, seized by <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>,
thoughtful <s>Hanūmān</s>, the son of the Wind, reflected:

children.text: evaṃ gṛhīte sugrīve kiṃ kartavyaṃ mayā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: 'When <s>Sugrīva</s> has been seized like this, what ought to be done by me?

children.text: yad vai nyāyyaṃ mayā kartuṃ tat kariṣyāmi sarvathā
children.translated_text: Whatever is right for me to do, that I shall do in every way;
becoming like a mountain, I shall destroy this rākṣasa.

children.text: mayā hate saṃyati kumbhakarṇe mahābale muṣṭiviśīrṇadehe
children.translated_text: When mighty <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> has been slain by me in battle, his body shattered by my fists,

children.text: vimocite vānarapārthive ca bhavantu hṛṣṭāḥ plavagāḥ samagrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and when the monkey-king has been freed, let all the leapers together be glad.

children.text: athavā svayam apyeṣa mokṣaṃ prāpsyati pārthivaḥ
children.translated_text: Or else this king himself will obtain release,
even if he were seized by the gods together with asuras and serpents.

children.text: manye na tāvad ātmānaṃ budhyate vānarādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: I think the lord of monkeys is not yet aware of himself,
having been struck in battle by <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>'s blow with the mountain.
In a moment this <s>Sugrīva</s>, having regained consciousness in the great battle,

children.text: ātmano vānarāṇāṃ ca yat pathyaṃ tat kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: will do what is beneficial for himself and for the monkeys.
But if this great-souled <s>Sugrīva</s> were released by me,
there would be painful displeasure for him and everlasting loss of fame.
Therefore I shall wait a moment for the valor of our king;
meanwhile I shall reassure the broken monkey army.'
Having reflected in this way, <s>Hanūmān</s>, the son of the Wind,
again steadied the great army of monkeys.

children.text: sa kumbhakarṇo 'tha viveśa laṅkāṃ sphurantam ādāya mahāhariṃ tam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> entered <s>Laṅkā</s>, carrying that great monkey as he writhed,
while he was sprinkled with showers of the finest flowers by those stationed on aerial palaces, mansions, and gateways.

children.text: tataḥ sa saṃjñām upalabhya kṛcchrād balīyasastasya bhujāntarasthaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, with difficulty, the great-souled one regained consciousness as he lay between the arms of that stronger warrior,
and, looking at the royal road of the city, he reflected again and again:

children.text: evaṃ gṛhītena kathaṃ nu nāma śakyaṃ mayā saṃprati kartum adya
children.translated_text: 'Being seized in this way, how indeed can anything be done by me now, today?

children.text: tathā kariṣyāmi yathā harīṇāṃ bhaviṣyatīṣṭaṃ ca hitaṃ ca kāryam ||
children.translated_text: I shall act so that the task will become both desired and beneficial for the monkeys.'

children.text: tataḥ karāgraiḥ sahasā sametya rājā harīṇām amarendraśatroḥ
children.translated_text: Then the king of the monkeys suddenly attacked the enemy of the lord of the immortals with the tips of his hands;

children.text: nakhaiśca karṇau daśanaiśca nāsāṃ dadaṃśa pārśveṣu ca kumbhakarṇam ||
children.translated_text: with his nails he tore at his ears, with his teeth at his nose, and bit <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> on the sides.
<s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, robbed of ears and nose, torn by him and battered,

children.text: roṣābhibhūtaḥ kṣatajārdragātraḥ sugrīvam āvidhya pipeṣa bhūmau ||
children.translated_text: overcome with anger and his limbs wet with blood, whirled <s>Sugrīva</s> about and crushed him on the ground.
Crushed on the ground by that fearsome strength and being struck by those enemies of the gods,

children.text: jagāma khaṃ vegavad abhyupetya punaśca rāmeṇa samājagāma ||
children.translated_text: he swiftly rose into the sky and then returned to <s>Rāma</s>.
Mighty <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, deprived of ears and nose,
shone drenched with blood like a mountain with streams flowing down it.

children.text: tataḥ sa puryāḥ sahasā mahātmā niṣkramya tad vānarasainyam ugram
children.translated_text: Then that great-souled rākṣasa suddenly came out of the city and into the fierce monkey army;

children.text: babhakṣa rakṣo yudhi kumbhakarṇaḥ prajā yugāntāgnir iva pradīptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> devoured creatures in battle like the blazing fire at the end of an age.

children.text: bubhukṣitaḥ śoṇitamāṃsagṛdhnuḥ praviśya tad vānarasainyam ugram
children.translated_text: Hungry and greedy for blood and flesh, he entered that fierce monkey army,

children.text: cakhāda rakṣāṃsi harīn piśācān ṛkṣāṃśca mohād yudhi kumbhakarṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and in his confusion <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> ate rākṣasas, monkeys, piśācas, and bears in battle.

children.text: ekaṃ dvau trīn bahūn kruddho vānarān saha rākṣasaiḥ
children.translated_text: One, two, three, and many enraged monkeys, together with rākṣasas,
he took up in one hand and quickly threw into his mouth.
Then fat and blood streamed from that mighty one,
and, even while being struck by the peaks of great mountains, he kept devouring monkeys.

children.text: te bhakṣyamāṇā harayo rāmaṃ jagmustadā gatim ||
children.translated_text: Those monkeys, as they were being eaten, then went to <s>Rāma</s> as their refuge.
At that time <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the son of <s>Sumitrā</s> and destroyer of enemy forces,
angry and conquering enemy cities, engaged in battle.

children.text: sa kumbhakarṇasya śarāñ śarīre sapta vīryavān
children.translated_text: The valiant <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> planted seven arrows in <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>'s body,
then took up others and released them.
And passing beyond <s>Saumitri</s>, mighty <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>
rushed straight at <s>Rāma</s>, as though tearing open the earth.

children.text: atha dāśarathī rāmo raudram astraṃ prayojayan
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, set in motion the raudra weapon
and released sharp arrows into <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>'s heart.
As he was pierced by <s>Rāma</s> and suddenly charged onward,
flames mixed with embers issued from his angry mouth.
The arrows, feathered with peacock plumes, sank into his chest,
and from his hand his great mace slipped and fell to the earth.

children.text: sa nirāyudham ātmānaṃ yadā mene mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: When the mighty one realized that he was unarmed,

children.text: muṣṭibhyāṃ cāraṇābhyāṃ ca cakāra kadanaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: he wrought great slaughter with his fists and feet.
His limbs deeply pierced by arrows and drenched with blood,
he streamed blood like a mountain with waterfalls.

children.text: sa tīvreṇa ca kopena rudhireṇa ca mūrchitaḥ
children.translated_text: Overwhelmed by fierce anger and by blood,
he ran about devouring monkeys, rākṣasas, and bears.

children.text: tasmin kāle sa dharmātmā lakṣmaṇo rāmam abravīt
children.translated_text: At that time righteous <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> spoke to <s>Rāma</s>,
intent on <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>'s killing and considering many stratagems.
This one, O king, no longer distinguishes monkeys from rākṣasas;
maddened by the smell of blood, he eats both his own men and the enemy.
Let the foremost monkeys climb upon him from every side,
and let the troop-leaders, each according to rank, stand all around him.
Perhaps this evil-minded rākṣasa, oppressed at the right moment by their heavy weight,

children.text: prapatan rākṣaso bhūmau nānyān hanyāt plavaṃgamān ||
children.translated_text: will fall to the ground and not kill other leapers.
Hearing that speech of the wise prince,
the leapers joyfully climbed upon <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>.
But <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, enraged as the leapers had climbed on him,
shook them off violently, like a vicious elephant shaking off its riders.

children.text: tān dṛṣṭvā nirdhūtān rāmo ruṣṭo 'yam iti rākṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing them shaken off, <s>Rāma</s>, angered at the rākṣasa,
sprang up swiftly and took up his excellent bow.

children.text: sa cāpam ādāya bhujaṃgakalpaṃ dṛḍhajyam ugraṃ tapanīyacitram
children.translated_text: Taking that bow, serpent-like, firm-strung, fierce, and bright with gold,
<s>Rāma</s>, reassuring the monkeys, leapt forward with arrows fixed in his excellent quiver.
Surrounded by those hosts of monkeys, he was exceedingly hard to conquer;
mighty <s>Rāma</s>, with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> following him, set forth.
The great-souled one saw mighty <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, crowned and subduer of foes,
with all his limbs drenched in blood.
He was rushing at all of them like an enraged elephant of the quarters,
angrily seeking out the monkeys and surrounded by rākṣasas.
He resembled <s>Vindhya</s> and <s>Mandara</s> and was adorned with golden armlets;
blood poured from his mouth like a rising rain-cloud.
Blood-sprinkled, licking up blood with his tongue,
he crushed the monkey army, resembling <s>Yama</s> the ender at the end of time.
Seeing that foremost rākṣasa, whose splendor was like blazing fire,
the bull among men then twanged his bow.
At the sound of his bow, the bull among the nairṛtas became enraged,
and, unable to endure that noise, charged at <s>Rāghava</s>.
Then, as he came on like a cloud driven by the wind, with arms like the coils of a great serpent king,

children.text: tam āpatantaṃ dharaṇīdharābham uvāca rāmo yudhi kumbhakarṇam ||
children.translated_text: and resembling a mountain, <s>Rāma</s> addressed <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> in battle:

children.text: āgaccha rakṣo'dhipa mā viṣādam avasthito 'haṃ pragṛhītacāpaḥ
children.translated_text: Come, lord of rākṣasas; do not despair. I stand here with my bow grasped.

children.text: avehi māṃ śakrasapatna rāmam ayaṃ muhūrtād bhavitā vicetāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Know me to be <s>Rāma</s>, O enemy of <s>Śakra</s>; in a moment you will be senseless.
Recognizing, This is <s>Rāma</s>, he laughed with a distorted sound,
as though making the hearts of all the forest-dwellers fall.
Having laughed a dreadful, distorted laugh like the thunder of a cloud,
the greatly radiant <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> spoke these words to <s>Rāghava</s>:

children.text: nāhaṃ virādho vijñeyo na kabandhaḥ kharo na ca
children.translated_text: I am not to be taken for <s>Virādha</s>, nor for <s>Kabandha</s>, nor for <s>Khara</s>,

children.text: na vālī na ca mārīcaḥ kumbhakarṇo 'ham āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor for <s>Vālī</s>, nor for <s>Mārīca</s>; I am <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, come here.

children.text: paśya me mudgaraṃ ghoraṃ sarvakālāyasaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: Look at my dreadful hammer, great and made wholly of black iron.

children.text: anena nirjitā devā dānavāśca mayā purā ||
children.translated_text: With this I formerly conquered the gods and dānavas.

children.text: vikarṇanāsa iti māṃ nāvajñātuṃ tvam arhasi
children.translated_text: You should not despise me as one whose ears and nose are mutilated;

children.text: svalpāpi hi na me pīḍā karṇanāsāvināśanāt ||
children.translated_text: for there is not even slight pain for me from the destruction of my ears and nose.
Show your valor quickly upon my limbs, O tiger of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s>s;
then, after seeing your manly prowess and might, I shall devour you.

children.text: sa kumbhakarṇasya vaco niśamya rāmaḥ supuṅkhān visasarja bāṇān
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>'s words, <s>Rāma</s> released well-feathered arrows.

children.text: tair āhato vajrasamapravegair na cukṣubhe na vyathate surāriḥ ||
children.translated_text: Struck by them, whose force equaled the thunderbolt, the enemy of the gods neither trembled nor felt pain.

children.text: yaiḥ sāyakaiḥ sālavarā nikṛttā vālī hato vānarapuṃgavaśca
children.translated_text: Those arrows by which the finest sāla trees had been cut down, and by which <s>Vālī</s>, the bull among monkeys, was slain,

children.text: te kumbhakarṇasya tadā śarīraṃ vajropamā na vyathayāṃpracakruḥ ||
children.translated_text: those thunderbolt-like arrows then did not pain <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>'s body.

children.text: sa vāridhārā iva sāyakāṃstān pibañ śarīreṇa mahendraśatruḥ
children.translated_text: Drinking those arrows with his body as though they were streams of rain, the enemy of <s>Mahendra</s>

children.text: jaghāna rāmasya śarapravegaṃ vyāvidhya taṃ mudgaram ugravegam ||
children.translated_text: checked the rush of <s>Rāma</s>'s arrows by whirling that hammer of terrible speed.
Then that rākṣasa, smeared with blood, the terror of the great armies of the gods,

children.text: vyāvidhya taṃ mudgaram ugravegaṃ vidrāvayāmāsa camūṃ harīṇām ||
children.translated_text: whirling that hammer of terrible speed, put the army of monkeys to flight.

children.text: vāyavyam ādāya tato varāstraṃ rāmaḥ pracikṣepa niśācarāya
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s> took up the excellent vāyavya weapon and hurled it at the night-roamer.

children.text: samudgaraṃ tena jahāra bāhuṃ sa kṛttabāhustumulaṃ nanāda ||
children.translated_text: With it he tore away the arm along with the hammer; and he, his arm cut off, roared tumultuously.

children.text: sa tasya bāhur giriśṛṅgakalpaḥ samudgaro rāghavabāṇakṛttaḥ
children.translated_text: That arm of his, like a mountain peak, together with the hammer and cut off by <s>Rāghava</s>'s arrow,

children.text: papāta tasmin harirājasainye jaghāna tāṃ vānaravāhinīṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: It fell among that army of the king of monkeys and struck that monkey host.

children.text: te vānarā bhagnahatāvaśeṣāḥ paryantam āśritya tadā viṣaṇṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Those monkeys, broken and slain, with only remnants left, then took refuge at the edge, despondent.
With limbs trembling, they beheld the very terrible encounter between the human king and the lord of the rākṣasas.
Great <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, his arm cut off by the weapon, was like a lordly mountain whose summit had been cut away.

children.text: utpāṭayāmāsa kareṇa vṛkṣaṃ tato 'bhidudrāva raṇe narendram ||
children.translated_text: He tore up a tree with his hand and then rushed in battle against the king of men.

children.text: taṃ tasya bāhuṃ saha sālavṛkṣaṃ samudyataṃ pannagabhogakalpam
children.translated_text: That arm of his, raised together with the sāla tree and resembling the coil of a serpent,
<s>Rāma</s> cut away with an arrow marked with gold and joined to the weapon of <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: sa kumbhakarṇasya bhujo nikṛttaḥ papāta bhūmau girisaṃnikāśaḥ
children.translated_text: That severed arm of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, mountain-like, fell upon the ground.

children.text: viveṣṭamāno nijaghāna vṛkṣāñ śailāñ śilā vānararākṣasāṃśca ||
children.translated_text: Writhing, it crushed trees, mountains, rocks, monkeys, and rākṣasas.

children.text: taṃ chinnabāhuṃ samavekṣya rāmaḥ samāpatantaṃ sahasā nadantam
children.translated_text: Seeing him with his arm cut off, as he came rushing suddenly with a roar, <s>Rāma</s>

children.text: dvāvardhacandrau niśitau pragṛhya cicheda pādau yudhi rākṣasasya ||
children.translated_text: took up two sharp crescent-headed arrows and cut off the rākṣasa's feet in battle.
His arms cut off and his feet cut away, he opened wide his mouth, like the mouth of the submarine fire,

children.text: dudrāva rāmaṃ sahasābhigarjan rāhur yathā candram ivāntarikṣe ||
children.translated_text: and suddenly rushed at <s>Rāma</s>, roaring, like <s>Rāhu</s> at the moon in the sky.

children.text: apūrayat tasya mukhaṃ śitāgrai rāmaḥ śarair hemapinaddhapuṅkhaiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> filled his mouth with sharp-pointed arrows whose shafts were bound with gold.

children.text: sa pūrṇavaktro na śaśāka vaktuṃ cukūja kṛcchreṇa mumoha cāpi ||
children.translated_text: With his mouth filled, he could not speak; with difficulty he gave a cry, and he also fainted.
Then <s>Rāma</s> took up an unfailing, keen, well-feathered arrow of <s>Indra</s>, like the rays of the sun,

children.text: ariṣṭam aindraṃ niśitaṃ supuṅkhaṃ rāmaḥ śaraṃ mārutatulyavegam ||
children.translated_text: like <s>Brahmā</s>'s rod, like <s>Antaka</s>, like time, and equal in speed to the wind.
That arrow, with a beautiful shaft of thunderbolt and gold, shining with the blaze of a flaming sun,
and equal in speed to the thunderbolt and lightning of great <s>Indra</s>, <s>Rāma</s> hurled at the night-roamer.

children.text: sa sāyako rāghavabāhucodito diśaḥ svabhāsā daśa saṃprakāśayan
children.translated_text: That missile, driven by <s>Rāghava</s>'s arm, lighting up the ten directions with its radiance,
went forth, appearing like smokeless blazing fire and possessing the might of <s>Śakra</s>'s thunderbolt.
Then, as <s>Purandara</s> once cut off <s>Vṛtra</s>'s head, it cut off the head of the lord of rākṣasas,

children.text: cakarta rakṣo'dhipateḥ śirastadā yathaiva vṛtrasya purā puraṃdaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: which resembled the peak of a great mountain, with gaping fangs and beautiful swinging earrings.
That rākṣasa head, struck by <s>Rāma</s>'s arrow and resembling a mountain, fell down.

children.text: babhañja caryāgṛhagopurāṇi prākāram uccaṃ tam apātayacca ||
children.translated_text: It shattered houses, gateways, and towers, and it knocked down the high rampart.
Then that huge-bodied rākṣasa, shining like <s>Himavat</s>, fell into the ocean.

children.text: grāhānmahāmīnacayān bhujaṃgamān mamarda bhūmiṃ ca tathā viveśa ||
children.translated_text: He crushed crocodiles, shoals of great fish, and serpents, and likewise entered into the earth.

children.text: tasmin hate brāhmaṇadevaśatrau mahābale saṃyati kumbhakarṇe
children.translated_text: When the mighty <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, enemy of brahmins and gods, had been killed in battle,

children.text: cacāla bhūr bhūmidharāśca sarve harṣācca devāstumulaṃ praṇeduḥ ||
children.translated_text: the earth shook, as did all the mountains, and the gods thundered tumultuously with joy.
Then the divine seers, great seers, serpents, gods, beings, suparṇas, and guhyakas,
together with hosts of yakṣas and gandharvas, standing in the sky, were delighted by <s>Rāma</s>'s valor.

children.text: praharṣam īyur bahavastu vānarāḥ prabuddhapadmapratimair ivānanaiḥ
children.translated_text: Many monkeys rejoiced, their faces like awakened lotuses,

children.text: apūjayan rāghavam iṣṭabhāginaṃ hate ripau bhīmabale durāsade ||
children.translated_text: and they honored fortunate <s>Rāghava</s> when the terrifying, mighty, unassailable enemy had been killed.
Having slain <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, crusher of the armies of the gods, whose exertion was unconquered in great battles,

children.text: nananda hatvā bharatāgrajo raṇe mahāsuraṃ vṛtram ivāmarādhipaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the elder brother of <s>Bharata</s> rejoiced in the fight, like the lord of the immortals after killing the great asura <s>Vṛtra</s>.
Seeing <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> slain by great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>,
the rākṣasas reported it to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, king of the rākṣasas.
Hearing that mighty <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> had been killed in battle,

children.text: rāvaṇaḥ śokasaṃtapto mumoha ca papāta ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, scorched by grief, fainted and fell down.
On hearing that their paternal uncle had been killed, <s>Devāntaka</s> and <s>Narāntaka</s>,
and <s>Triśiras</s> and <s>Atikāya</s>, wept, oppressed by grief.
Hearing that his brother had been killed by <s>Rāma</s>, whose deeds are unwearied,
<s>Mahodara</s> and <s>Mahāpārśva</s> became overwhelmed with grief.
Then the foremost rākṣasa, regaining consciousness with difficulty,
wretched because of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>'s death, that <s>Rāvaṇa</s> lamented.
Ah, hero, destroyer of the enemy's pride, mighty <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>!

children.text: śatrusainyaṃ pratāpyaikaḥ kva māṃ saṃtyajya gacchasi ||
children.translated_text: Having burned the enemy army all alone, where are you going, abandoning me?

children.text: idānīṃ khalvahaṃ nāsmi yasya me patito bhujaḥ
children.translated_text: Now indeed I am no more, since that right arm of mine has fallen,

children.text: dakṣiṇo yaṃ samāśritya na bibhemi surāsurān ||
children.translated_text: relying on which I did not fear gods or asuras.
How has such a hero, a destroyer of the pride of gods and dānavas,
like the fire of time, today been slain in battle by <s>Rāghava</s>?

children.text: yasya te vajraniṣpeṣo na kuryād vyasanaṃ sadā
children.translated_text: When the blow of a thunderbolt would never cause you distress,
how do you lie asleep on the earth, pained by <s>Rāma</s>'s arrow?

children.text: ete devagaṇāḥ sārdham ṛṣibhir gagane sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: These hosts of gods, together with the seers, stand in the sky,

children.text: nihataṃ tvāṃ raṇe dṛṣṭvā ninadanti praharṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and seeing you slain in battle, they shout with joy.
Surely today the leapers, delighted and having attained their goal,
will climb here over the fortifications and all the gates of <s>Laṅkā</s>.

children.text: rājyena nāsti me kāryaṃ kiṃ kariṣyāmi sītayā
children.translated_text: I have no use for kingship; what shall I do with <s>Sītā</s>?
Without <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, I have no delight in life.

children.text: yadyahaṃ bhrātṛhantāraṃ na hanmi yudhi rāghavam
children.translated_text: If I do not kill <s>Rāghava</s>, the slayer of my brother, in battle,

children.text: nanu me maraṇaṃ śreyo na cedaṃ vyarthajīvitam ||
children.translated_text: then death is better for me, not this useless life.

children.text: adyaiva taṃ gamiṣyāmi deśaṃ yatrānujo mama
children.translated_text: Today itself I shall go to that place where my younger brother is.

children.text: na hi bhrātṝn samutsṛjya kṣaṇaṃ jīvitum utsahe ||
children.translated_text: For I cannot bear to live even for a moment after abandoning my brothers.

children.text: devā hi māṃ hasiṣyanti dṛṣṭvā pūrvāpakāriṇam
children.translated_text: For the gods will laugh at me when they see me, who first did them harm.

children.text: katham indraṃ jayiṣyāmi kumbhakarṇa hate tvayi ||
children.translated_text: How shall I conquer <s>Indra</s>, when you, <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, have been slain?

children.text: tad idaṃ mām anuprāptaṃ vibhīṣaṇavacaḥ śubham
children.translated_text: Therefore this good word of <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> has now come upon me,

children.text: yad ajñānānmayā tasya na gṛhītaṃ mahātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: which, through ignorance, I did not accept from that great-souled one.
As long as <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>'s words, together with the destruction of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> and <s>Prahasta</s>,
have now come to pass, this terrible thing fills me with shame.

children.text: tasyāyaṃ karmaṇaḥ prāto vipāko mama śokadaḥ
children.translated_text: This result of that deed has come to maturity for me, bringing sorrow,

children.text: yanmayā dhārmikaḥ śrīmān sa nirasto vibhīṣaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: because I drove away that righteous and illustrious <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>.

children.text: iti bahuvidham ākulāntarātmā kṛpaṇam atīva vilapya kumbhakarṇam
children.translated_text: Thus, with his inner self deeply agitated, after lamenting most piteously over <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> in many ways,

children.text: nyapatad atha daśānano bhṛśārtas tam anujam indraripuṃ hataṃ viditvā ||
children.translated_text: the ten-faced one, deeply afflicted, fell down, knowing that his younger brother, the enemy of <s>Indra</s>, had been slain.
As evil-minded <s>Rāvaṇa</s> was lamenting in this way,
burning with grief, <s>Triśiras</s>, hearing him, spoke these words.

children.text: evam eva mahāvīryo hato nastāta madhyamaḥ
children.translated_text: Indeed, father, our middle brother, of great valor, has been slain in this way;

children.text: na tu satpuruṣā rājan vilapanti yathā bhavān ||
children.translated_text: but good men, O king, do not lament as you do.
Surely you are sufficient even for the three worlds, my lord.

children.text: sa kasmāt prākṛta iva śokasyātmānam īdṛśam ||
children.translated_text: Why then, like an ordinary man, do you subject yourself to such grief?

children.text: brahmadattāsti te śaktiḥ kavacaḥ sāyako dhanuḥ
children.translated_text: You possess the power given by <s>Brahmā</s>, armor, arrows, and a bow,
and a chariot yoked with a thousand mules, sounding like a cloud.
More than once, even unarmed, you have destroyed gods and dānavas.
Equipped with every weapon, you ought to chastise <s>Rāghava</s>.
Remain here as you wish, great king; I will go out to battle.

children.text: uddhariṣyāmi te śatrūn garuḍaḥ pannagān iha ||
children.translated_text: Here I shall tear out your enemies, as <s>Garuḍa</s> tears out serpents.
As <s>Śambara</s> was laid low by the king of the gods, and <s>Naraka</s> by <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: tathādya śayitā rāmo mayā yudhi nipātitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so today <s>Rāma</s>, struck down by me in battle, will lie on the ground.
Hearing the words of <s>Triśiras</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas,
driven on by Time, considered himself as though born again.
Hearing the words of <s>Triśiras</s>, <s>Devāntaka</s> and <s>Narāntaka</s>,
and radiant <s>Atikāya</s>, became eager for battle.
Then, roaring, "I, I!" those bulls among the night-roaming rākṣasas,
the heroic sons of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, equal to <s>Śakra</s> in prowess,
all moving through the sky, all skilled in illusion,
all destroyers of the pride of the thirty gods, and all wildly arrogant in battle,
all endowed with the strength of weapons, all of far-reaching fame,

children.text: sarve samaram āsādya na śrūyante sma nirjitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all, when they had entered battle, had never been heard of as defeated.
All were heroic masters of missiles, all skilled in warfare,
all possessed of excellent knowledge, and all likewise had obtained boons.

children.text: sa taistathā bhāskaratulyavarcasaiḥ sutair vṛtaḥ śatrubalapramardanaiḥ
children.translated_text: Surrounded by those sons, whose splendor was equal to the sun and who crushed enemy forces,

children.text: rarāja rājā maghavān yathāmarair vṛto mahādānavadarpanāśanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king shone like <s>Maghavan</s> surrounded by immortals who destroy the pride of mighty dānavas.

children.text: sa putrān sampariṣvajya bhūṣayitvā ca bhūṣaṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: He embraced his sons, adorned them with ornaments,
and, with excellent blessings, sent them into battle.
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> also sent his brothers <s>Mahodara</s> and <s>Mahāpārśva</s>
into battle for the protection of the princes.
Having bowed to the great-souled <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, who made his enemies cry out,
and having circumambulated him, those huge-bodied warriors set out.
Anointed with all herbs and fragrances, those mighty ones,
those six foremost night-roaming rākṣasas, went out, longing for battle.
Then <s>Mahodara</s> mounted an elephant named <s>Sudarśana</s>,
born in the line of <s>Airāvata</s> and resembling a dark blue raincloud.
It was furnished with every weapon and adorned with quivers;
mounted on that elephant, he shone like the sun over the summit of the setting mountain.
<s>Triśiras</s>, son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, mounted an excellent chariot,
yoked with the finest horses and crowded with every weapon.
Standing on the chariot, bow in hand, <s>Triśiras</s> shone forth
like a cloud with lightning, meteors, flame, and <s>Indra</s>'s bow.
With three crowns, <s>Triśiras</s> looked splendid on that excellent chariot,
like <s>Himavān</s>, lord of mountains, with three golden peaks.
Then radiant <s>Atikāya</s>, son of the lord of rākṣasas,
himself the best of all bowmen, mounted an excellent chariot.
It had fine wheels and axles, was well harnessed, with a rear platform and yoke-pole,
and it blazed with quivers, arrows, and seats, crowded with spears, swords, and iron clubs.
With a shining crown variegated with gold,

children.text: bhūṣaṇaiśca babhau meruḥ prabhābhir iva bhāsvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and with ornaments, he gleamed like <s>Meru</s> radiant with its rays.

children.text: sa rarāja rathe tasmin rājasūnur mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: That mighty prince shone on that chariot,
surrounded by tiger-like rākṣasas, like <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> surrounded by immortals.
<s>Narāntaka</s> mounted a white horse, adorned with gold,
huge-bodied, swift as thought, and resembling <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s>.
Taking up a spear like a meteor, <s>Narāntaka</s> shone forth,
radiant like <s>Guha</s> taking up his lance against enemies in battle.
<s>Devāntaka</s>, taking up a mace adorned like a thunderbolt,

children.text: parigṛhya giriṃ dorbhyāṃ vapur viṣṇor viḍambayan ||
children.translated_text: seemed to mock the form of <s>Viṣṇu</s> holding a mountain in his arms.
Mighty-armed and very radiant <s>Mahāpārśva</s>, taking up a mace,
shone in battle, mace in hand, like <s>Kubera</s>.

children.text: te pratasthur mahātmāno balair apratimair vṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Those great-souled ones set out, surrounded by matchless forces,
like gods in <s>Amarāvatī</s>, surrounded by matchless forces.
After them followed great-souled rākṣasas with elephants, horses,
and chariots rumbling like clouds, bearing excellent weapons.
Those great-souled princes, radiant as the sun, shone forth.

children.text: kirīṭinaḥ śriyā juṣṭā grahā dīptā ivāmbare ||
children.translated_text: The crowned warriors, attended by splendor, shone like blazing planets in the sky.

children.text: pragṛhītā babhau teṣāṃ chatrāṇām āvaliḥ sitā
children.translated_text: The white row of parasols held aloft over them shone
like a line of swans in the sky, resembling autumn clouds.

children.text: maraṇaṃ vāpi niścitya śatrūṇāṃ vā parājayam
children.translated_text: Having resolved either on death or on the defeat of their enemies,

children.text: iti kṛtvā matiṃ vīrā nirjagmuḥ saṃyugārthinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and having formed that intention, the heroes went out, eager for battle.
They roared, shouted, and also discharged arrows;
and the great-souled ones rejoiced as they set out, wild with the fury of battle.
With the noise of cries and slapping arms the earth seemed to tremble,
and with the lion-roars of the rākṣasas the sky then seemed to burst.
Those mighty rākṣasa lords, joyous after marching out,
saw the monkey army with rocks and trees raised up.
The great-souled monkeys too saw the rākṣasa force,
crowded with elephants, horses, and chariots, and sounding with hundreds of tinkling bells.
It was dark like a blue rain cloud, with great weapons lifted up,
and surrounded everywhere by rākṣasas resembling blazing fire and the sun.

children.text: tad dṛṣṭvā balam āyāntaṃ labdhalakṣyāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that army approaching, the leapers had their targets in sight;
raising great mountains, they roared again and again.
Then, hearing the loud uproar of the monkey troop-leaders,

children.text: amṛṣyamāṇāḥ paraharṣam ugraṃ mahābalā bhīmataraṃ vineduḥ ||
children.translated_text: the mighty hosts of rākṣasas, unable to bear the enemies’ fierce joy, roared more terribly.
The monkey troop-leaders entered that dreadful rākṣasa army,

children.text: vicerur udyataiḥ śailair nagāḥ śikhariṇo yathā ||
children.translated_text: and with mountains raised they moved about like peaked mountains.

children.text: kecid ākāśam āviśya kecid urvyāṃ plavaṃgamāḥ
children.translated_text: Some leapers entered the sky, and some moved upon the earth;
angry and armed with trees and rocks, they ranged through the rākṣasa armies.
With trees, rocks, and mountains they made an unsurpassed shower,
though the fierce-valored monkeys were being checked by floods of arrows.
The rākṣasas and monkeys uttered lion-roars in battle,
and the leapers crushed the yātudhānas with rocks.
Angry in the battle, they struck down those covered with armor and ornaments,
some heroes mounted on chariots, and also on elephants and horses.
Suddenly leaping up, the monkeys struck down the yātudhānas,
and at the fall of mountain peaks and blows from fists, their eyes were forced out;
there the foremost rākṣasas staggered, fell, and roared.
Then, by mountains and swords hurled by monkeys and rākṣasas,
in a moment the earth became covered and flooded with blood.
The rākṣasas, crushers of foes, lay scattered in mountain-like heaps,
hurled and being hurled by the monkeys, with their spears broken.
Those night-roamers struck down monkeys with monkeys themselves;

children.text: rākṣasān rākṣasair eva jaghnuste vānarā api ||
children.translated_text: and the monkeys too struck down rākṣasas with rākṣasas themselves.

children.text: ākṣipya ca śilāsteṣāṃ nijaghnū rākṣasā harīn
children.translated_text: The rākṣasas seized the monkeys’ rocks and struck down the monkeys;

children.text: teṣāṃ cācchidya śastrāṇi jaghnū rakṣāṃsi vānarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the monkeys, cutting away their weapons, struck down the rākṣasas.
With mountains, spears, and missiles they struck and split one another,
and monkeys and rākṣasas uttered lion-roars in battle.
The rākṣasas whose armor and mail had been cut were slain by the monkeys;
there they streamed blood like trees pouring out their sap.

children.text: rathena ca rathaṃ cāpi vāraṇena ca vāraṇam
children.translated_text: With chariot against chariot and elephant against elephant,

children.text: hayena ca hayaṃ kecin nijaghnur vānarā raṇe ||
children.translated_text: and horse against horse, some monkeys struck them down in battle.
With razor-headed arrows, crescent-headed arrows, bhallas, and sharp shafts,
the rākṣasas cut down the trees and rocks of the monkey lords.
With mountain tops scattered and trees cut down in the battle,
and with slain monkeys and rākṣasas, the earth became hard to traverse.

children.text: tasmin pravṛtte tumule vimarde prahṛṣyamāṇeṣu valīmukheṣu
children.translated_text: When that tumultuous crushing had begun, while the monkeys were exulting,

children.text: nipātyamāneṣu ca rākṣaseṣu maharṣayo devagaṇāśca neduḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the rākṣasas were being felled, the great seers and hosts of gods cried out.

children.text: tato hayaṃ mārutatulyavegam āruhya śaktiṃ niśitāṃ pragṛhya
children.translated_text: Then, mounting a horse swift as the wind and seizing a sharpened spear,
<s>Narāntaka</s> entered the army of the monkey king like a fish entering the great ocean.

children.text: sa vānarān saptaśatāni vīraḥ prāsena dīptena vinirbibheda
children.translated_text: That hero pierced seven hundred monkeys with his blazing lance;

children.text: ekaḥ kṣaṇenendraripur mahātmā jaghāna sainyaṃ haripuṃgavānām ||
children.translated_text: alone, in a moment, that great-souled enemy of <s>Indra</s> slew the army of the foremost monkeys.
The Vidyādharas and great seers saw that great-souled one
standing on the horse’s back and moving among the monkey army.
His path appeared as mud of flesh and blood,
covered with fallen monkeys as huge as mountains.
As soon as the foremost leapers formed the intention to show their valor,
<s>Narāntaka</s> had already passed beyond them and pierced them.
At the edge of the battle, raising his blazing spear, <s>Narāntaka</s>
burned the monkey armies like fire burning forests.
As soon as the forest-dwellers uprooted trees and mountains,
they fell, struck by the spear, like mountains cut down by a thunderbolt.
The mighty <s>Narāntaka</s> ranged in all directions,
crushing everyone on every side in battle, like the wind in the rainy season.

children.text: na śekur dhāvituṃ vīrā na sthātuṃ spandituṃ kutaḥ
children.translated_text: The heroes could not run, nor stand; how could they even stir?

children.text: utpatantaṃ sthitaṃ yāntaṃ sarvān vivyādha vīryavān ||
children.translated_text: The mighty one pierced them all, whether leaping up, standing still, or going away.
By a single death-like spear, radiant as the sun,
the shattered monkey armies fell upon the surface of the earth.
The monkeys could not endure the impact of the spear,

children.text: na śekur vānarāḥ soḍhuṃ te vinedur mahāsvanam ||
children.translated_text: which was like the crushing blow of a thunderbolt; they uttered a great cry.
The forms of the falling monkey heroes shone forth
like falling mountains whose foremost peaks had been split by a thunderbolt.

children.text: ye tu pūrvaṃ mahātmānaḥ kumbhakarṇena pātitāḥ
children.translated_text: But those great-souled ones who had earlier been felled by <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>,
those distressed foremost monkeys came up to <s>Sugrīva</s>.
Looking about, <s>Sugrīva</s> saw the monkey army,
terrified by fear of <s>Narāntaka</s> and fleeing here and there.

children.text: vidrutāṃ vāhinīṃ dṛṣṭvā sa dadarśa narāntakam
children.translated_text: Seeing the army in flight, he saw <s>Narāntaka</s>,
approaching with spear in hand, established on the back of a horse.
Then the greatly radiant <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the monkeys,
spoke to the heroic prince <s>Aṅgada</s>, whose valor was equal to <s>Śakra</s>'s:

children.text: gacchainaṃ rākṣasaṃ vīra yo 'sau turagam āsthitaḥ
children.translated_text: "Go, hero, and quickly separate from life
that rākṣasa there, who is mounted on a horse and is agitating the monkey force."
Hearing his lord's command, <s>Aṅgada</s> then sprang forth
from the cloud-like ranks, like the sun from a mass of clouds.
<s>Aṅgada</s>, best of the monkeys, resembling a mass of mountains,
shone, adorned with armlets, like a mountain rich with minerals.
Unarmed, greatly radiant, equipped only with nails and teeth,
the son of <s>Vālin</s> approached <s>Narāntaka</s> and spoke these words:

children.text: tiṣṭha kiṃ prākṛtair ebhir haribhistvaṃ kariṣyasi
children.translated_text: "Stand fast. What will you do with these ordinary monkeys?
Hurl your spear at my chest, whose touch is like a thunderbolt."
Hearing <s>Aṅgada</s>'s words, <s>Narāntaka</s> became enraged;

children.text: saṃdaśya daśanair oṣṭhaṃ niśvasya ca bhujaṃgavat ||
children.translated_text: biting his lip with his teeth and hissing like a serpent,

children.text: sa prāsam āvidhya tadāṅgadāya samujjvalantaṃ sahasotsasarja
children.translated_text: he whirled the blazing spear and suddenly hurled it at <s>Aṅgada</s>.

children.text: sa vāliputrorasi vajrakalpe babhūva bhagno nyapatacca bhūmau ||
children.translated_text: It broke upon the thunderbolt-like chest of the son of <s>Vālin</s> and fell to the ground.

children.text: taṃ prāsam ālokya tadā vibhagnaṃ suparṇakṛttoragabhogakalpam
children.translated_text: Then, seeing that spear broken, like a serpent's coil cut by <s>Suparṇa</s>,

children.text: talaṃ samudyamya sa vāliputras turaṃgamasyābhijaghāna mūrdhni ||
children.translated_text: the son of <s>Vālin</s> raised his palm and struck the horse on the head.
Its feet sank down, the pupils of its eyes burst, its tongue came out, and it was like a mountain;

children.text: sa tasya vājī nipapāta bhūmau talaprahāreṇa vikīrṇamūrdhā ||
children.translated_text: that horse of his fell to the ground, its head shattered by the slap.

children.text: narāntakaḥ krodhavaśaṃ jagāma hataṃ turagaṃ patitaṃ nirīkṣya
children.translated_text: <s>Narāntaka</s> fell under the power of anger when he saw his horse killed and fallen.

children.text: sa muṣṭim udyamya mahāprabhāvo jaghāna śīrṣe yudhi vāliputram ||
children.translated_text: Raising his fist, the mighty one struck the son of <s>Vālin</s> on the head in battle.

children.text: athāṅgado muṣṭivibhinnamūrdhā susrāva tīvraṃ rudhiraṃ bhṛśoṣṇam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Aṅgada</s>, his head split by the fist, poured out intensely hot blood.

children.text: muhur vijajvāla mumoha cāpi saṃjñāṃ samāsādya visiṣmiye ca ||
children.translated_text: Again and again he flared up and fainted; regaining consciousness, he was astonished.
Then the great-souled son of <s>Vālin</s> clenched a fist
with the force of a thunderbolt and like a mountain peak, and brought it down on <s>Narāntaka</s>'s chest.
With his chest crushed and split by the fist, vomiting flame, his body smeared with blood,
<s>Narāntaka</s> fell on the surface of the earth like a mountain broken by the fall of a thunderbolt.
Then in the sky there arose a great roar from the foremost gods
and from the forest-dwellers, when that foremost hero <s>Narāntaka</s> had been slain in battle by the son of <s>Vālin</s>.

children.text: athāṅgado rāmamanaḥpraharṣaṇaṃ suduṣkaraṃ taṃ kṛtavān hi vikramam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Aṅgada</s> had performed that very difficult feat, one that gladdened <s>Rāma</s>'s heart.

children.text: visiṣmiye so 'pyativīryavikramaḥ punaśca yuddhe sa babhūva harṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He too, of exceedingly heroic valor, was amazed, and again he rejoiced in battle.
Seeing <s>Narāntaka</s> slain, the bulls among the rākṣasas cried out:
<s>Devāntaka</s>, <s>Triśiras</s>, and the descendant of <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Mahodara</s>.
