Mounted on a lordly elephant resembling a cloud, <s>Mahodara</s>,
a mighty hero, rushed against the very powerful son of <s>Vālin</s>.
Then powerful <s>Devāntaka</s>, tormented by his brother's calamity,
took up a blazing iron club and charged at <s>Aṅgada</s>.
The hero <s>Triśiras</s>, mounting a chariot shining like the sun,
yoked with excellent horses, then advanced against the son of <s>Vālin</s>.
Assailed by those three lordly rākṣasas who crushed the pride of the gods,
<s>Aṅgada</s> uprooted a tree with great branches.
The hero <s>Aṅgada</s> suddenly hurled that great tree at <s>Devāntaka</s>,
a great tree with great branches, as <s>Śakra</s> hurls a blazing thunderbolt.
<s>Triśiras</s> cut it apart with arrows like venomous serpents.

children.text: sa vṛkṣaṃ kṛttam ālokya utpapāta tato 'ṅgadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing the tree cut down, <s>Aṅgada</s> then leapt up.

children.text: sa vavarṣa tato vṛkṣāñ śilāśca kapikuñjaraḥ
children.translated_text: Then that elephant among monkeys showered trees and rocks,
but angry <s>Triśiras</s> cut them apart with sharp arrows.

children.text: parighāgreṇa tān vṛkṣān babhañja ca surāntakaḥ
children.translated_text: And <s>Devāntaka</s> shattered those trees with the tip of his iron club,
while <s>Triśiras</s> rushed at the heroic <s>Aṅgada</s> with arrows.
Charging on his elephant at the son of <s>Vālin</s>, <s>Mahodara</s>,
enraged, struck him in the chest with javelins like thunderbolts.
And enraged <s>Devāntaka</s> then approached <s>Aṅgada</s>
and, after swiftly striking him with his iron club, withdrew at speed.
Assailed at the same time by the three foremost rākṣasas,
the greatly radiant, majestic son of <s>Vālin</s> did not tremble.
Leaping up fiercely, he struck <s>Mahodara</s>'s great elephant with his palm;

children.text: petatur locane tasya vinanāda sa vāraṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: its eyes fell out, and that elephant roared.
The very strong son of <s>Vālin</s> pulled out its tusk,
rushed at <s>Devāntaka</s>, and struck him in the battle.
With all his limbs reeling, like a tree shaken by the wind,
he poured blood from his mouth, red as lac dye.
Then the powerful, greatly radiant <s>Devāntaka</s>, recovering with difficulty,
whirled his dreadful iron club and then struck <s>Aṅgada</s>.
And then, though struck by the iron club, the son of the lord of the vānaras,

children.text: jānubhyāṃ patito bhūmau punar evotpapāta ha ||
children.translated_text: having fallen to the ground on his knees, immediately sprang up again.
As he was leaping up, <s>Triśiras</s> struck the son of the lord of the monkeys
on the forehead with three terrible arrows resembling venomous snakes.
Then <s>Hanūmān</s>, and also <s>Nīla</s>, perceiving that <s>Aṅgada</s>
was surrounded by the three foremost nairṛtas, advanced.
Then <s>Nīla</s> hurled the peak of a mountain at <s>Triśiras</s>,

children.text: tad rāvaṇasuto dhīmān bibheda niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: but the wise son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> split it apart with sharp arrows.
That mountain peak, pierced by a hundred arrows, with its rocky surface torn open,
fell down with sparks and flames.
Then, seeing that opening, <s>Devāntaka</s>, exulting,
rushed in battle upon the son of the Wind with an iron club.
As he came charging on, <s>Hanūmān</s>, the son of the Wind, leapt up
and struck him on the head with his fist, with the force of a thunderbolt.
With his head crushed and scattered by the fist, his teeth and eyes knocked out, and his tongue hanging loose,

children.text: devāntako rākṣasarājasūnur gatāsur urvyāṃ sahasā papāta ||
children.translated_text: <s>Devāntaka</s>, son of the rākṣasa king, lifeless, suddenly fell upon the earth.

children.text: tasmin hate rākṣasayodhamukhye mahābale saṃyati devaśatrau
children.translated_text: When that foremost rākṣasa warrior, the mighty enemy of the gods, had been slain in battle,

children.text: kruddhastrimūrdhā niśitāgram ugraṃ vavarṣa nīlorasi bāṇavarṣam ||
children.translated_text: the enraged three-headed one rained a fierce shower of sharp-pointed arrows upon <s>Nīla</s>'s chest.

children.text: sa taiḥ śaraughair abhivarṣyamāṇo vibhinnagātraḥ kapisainyapālaḥ
children.translated_text: Pelted by those floods of arrows, his body pierced through, the guardian of the monkey army,
<s>Nīla</s>, his limbs slackened, became stunned by that mighty warrior.

children.text: tatastu nīlaḥ pratilabhya saṃjñāṃ śailaṃ samutpāṭya savṛkṣaṣaṇḍam
children.translated_text: But then <s>Nīla</s>, regaining consciousness, uprooted a mountain together with its clumps of trees,

children.text: tataḥ samutpatya bhṛśogravego mahodaraṃ tena jaghāna mūrdhni ||
children.translated_text: and, leaping up with exceedingly terrible speed, struck <s>Mahodara</s> on the head with it.

children.text: tataḥ sa śailābhinipātabhagno mahodarastena saha dvipena
children.translated_text: Then <s>Mahodara</s>, crushed by the fall of that mountain, together with his elephant,

children.text: vipothito bhūmitale gatāsuḥ papāta vajrābhihato yathādriḥ ||
children.translated_text: was pulverized on the ground, lifeless, and fell like a mountain struck by a thunderbolt.
Seeing his father's brother slain, <s>Triśiras</s> took up his bow,

children.text: hanūmantaṃ ca saṃkruddho vivyādha niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and in rage pierced <s>Hanūmān</s> with sharp arrows.
But <s>Hanūmān</s>, leaping up then, enraged, tore apart

children.text: vidadāra nakhaiḥ kruddho gajendraṃ mṛgarāḍ iva ||
children.translated_text: the horses of <s>Triśiras</s> with his nails, as a lion tears apart a lordly elephant.
Then <s>Triśiras</s>, son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, taking up a spear like Death in the form of the night of doom,
hurled it at the son of the Wind.

children.text: divi kṣiptām ivolkāṃ tāṃ śaktiṃ kṣiptām asaṃgatām
children.translated_text: The tiger among monkeys caught that spear, hurled without missing,

children.text: gṛhītvā hariśārdūlo babhañja ca nanāda ca ||
children.translated_text: as though it were a meteor thrown in the sky, broke it, and roared.

children.text: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā ghorasaṃkāśāṃ śaktiṃ bhagnāṃ hanūmatā
children.translated_text: Seeing that dreadful-looking spear broken by <s>Hanūmān</s>,
the hosts of vānaras rejoiced and roared like rain clouds.
Then <s>Triśiras</s>, best of rākṣasas, raised his sword
and angrily buried it in the chest of the lord of the vānaras.
Struck by the blow of the sword, <s>Hanūmān</s>, son of the Wind,
the powerful one, struck the three-headed warrior on the chest with his palm.
Struck by that palm-blow, with his hands and garment slipping loose,
the greatly radiant <s>Triśiras</s> fell unconscious to the ground.

children.text: sa tasya patataḥ khaḍgaṃ samāchidya mahākapiḥ
children.translated_text: As he was falling, the great monkey snatched away his sword,
and, mountain-like, roared, terrifying all the nairṛtas.
Unable to endure that cry, the night-roamer sprang up,
and, leaping up, struck <s>Hanūmān</s> with his fist.
At that blow of the fist the great monkey became enraged,
and, angered, seized the bull among rākṣasas by his diadem.

children.text: sa tasya śīrṣāṇyasinā śitena kirīṭajuṣṭāni sakuṇḍalāni
children.translated_text: With his sharp sword the enraged son of the Wind cut off his heads,

children.text: kruddhaḥ pracicheda suto 'nilasya tvaṣṭuḥ sutasyeva śirāṃsi śakraḥ ||
children.translated_text: adorned with diadems and earrings, as <s>Śakra</s> cut off the heads of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>'s son.
Those broad-eyed heads, mountain-like, with eyes blazing like fire,

children.text: petuḥ śirāṃsīndraripor dharaṇyāṃ jyotīṃṣi muktāni yathārkamārgāt ||
children.translated_text: fell to the earth from the enemy of <s>Indra</s>, like lights loosed from the path of the sun.

children.text: tasmin hate devaripau triśīrṣe hanūmatā śakraparākrameṇa
children.translated_text: When that three-headed enemy of the gods had been slain by <s>Hanūmān</s>, whose valor was like <s>Śakra</s>'s,

children.text: neduḥ plavaṃgāḥ pracacāla bhūmī rakṣāṃsyatho dudruvire samantāt ||
children.translated_text: the leapers roared, the earth shook, and then the rākṣasas fled on every side.

children.text: hataṃ triśirasaṃ dṛṣṭvā tathaiva ca mahodaram
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Triśiras</s> slain, and likewise <s>Mahodara</s>,
and seeing the hard-to-assail <s>Devāntaka</s> and <s>Narāntaka</s> slain,
the exceedingly wrathful, very mighty <s>Mahāpārśva</s> grew furious,
and seized a splendid all-iron mace, blazing with light.
It was bound with bands of gold, smeared with flesh and blood,
shining with its form and reddened by the blood of enemies.
Its tip blazed with radiance, and it was adorned with red garlands,
bringing terror to <s>Airāvata</s>, <s>Mahāpadma</s>, and <s>Sārvabhauma</s>.
Taking up that mace, the enraged and very mighty <s>Mahāpārśva</s>
rushed upon the monkeys, blazing like the fire at the end of an age.
Then the powerful vānara <s>Ṛṣabha</s> leapt up
and, approaching <s>Mahāpārśva</s>, the younger brother of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, stood before him.

children.text: taṃ purastāt sthitaṃ dṛṣṭvā vānaraṃ parvatopamam
children.translated_text: Seeing that mountain-like vānara standing before him,
he angrily struck him on the chest with his mace, which was like a thunderbolt.
Struck by him with that mace, the bull among vānaras,
his chest split and his body shaken, poured forth much blood.

children.text: sa samprāpya cirāt saṃjñām ṛṣabho vānararṣabhaḥ
children.translated_text: After a long time <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, bull among vānaras, regained consciousness;
angry, his lips quivering, he looked upon <s>Mahāpārśva</s>.

children.text: tāṃ gṛhītvā gadāṃ bhīmām āvidhya ca punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Grasping that terrible mace and whirling it again and again,
he struck the intoxicated-elephant-like <s>Mahāpārśva</s> at the forefront of battle.
He, shattered by his own mace, with his teeth and eyes scattered,
<s>Mahāpārśva</s> fell like a mountain struck by a thunderbolt.

children.text: tasmin hate bhrātari rāvaṇasya tannairṛtānāṃ balam arṇavābham
children.translated_text: When that brother of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> had been killed, the ocean-like army of the Nairṛtas
threw away its weapons and, seeking only to preserve life, fled like a shattered ocean.
Seeing his own force shaken, in a tumult that made the hair stand on end,
and seeing his brothers slain, who were equal to <s>Śakra</s> in valor,
and also seeing his two paternal uncles cut down in battle,
<s>Mahodara</s> and <s>Mahāpārśva</s>, the two brothers, bulls among rākṣasas,
the greatly radiant one, who had received a boon from <s>Brahmā</s>, became furious in the battle,
<s>Atikāya</s>, mountain-like and a crusher of the pride of gods and Dānavas.
Mounting a chariot that shone like the massed light of a thousand suns,
that enemy of <s>Śakra</s> rushed upon the monkeys.
Stretching his great bow, crowned and wearing polished earrings,
he proclaimed his name and roared with a mighty sound.
With that lion-roar, with the proclamation of his name,
and with the terrible sound of his bowstring, he terrified the monkeys.

children.text: te tasya rūpam ālokya yathā viṣṇostrivikrame
children.translated_text: Beholding his form, as if it were <s>Viṣṇu</s> at the triple stride,

children.text: bhayārtā vānarāḥ sarve vidravanti diśo daśa ||
children.translated_text: all the fear-stricken monkeys fled to the ten directions.
The monkeys, their minds bewildered on encountering <s>Atikāya</s>,
went in battle for refuge to the refuge-giving elder brother of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Then <s>Kākutstha</s> saw <s>Atikāya</s> on his chariot, mountain-like,
armed with a bow, roaring from afar like a black cloud.

children.text: sa taṃ dṛṣṭvā mahātmānaṃ rāghavastu suvismitaḥ
children.translated_text: When the great-souled <s>Rāghava</s> saw him, he was greatly astonished,

children.text: vānarān sāntvayitvā tu vibhīṣaṇam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: and, after comforting the monkeys, he spoke to <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>.
Who is that one, like a mountain, bow in hand, with tawny eyes,
standing in a vast chariot yoked with a thousand horses?

children.text: ya eṣa niśitaiḥ śūlaiḥ sutīkṣṇaiḥ prāsatomaraiḥ
children.translated_text: He is surrounded by sharp lances, very keen prāsas and tomaras,

children.text: arciṣmadbhir vṛto bhāti bhūtair iva maheśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, shining with flame, he appears like <s>Maheśvara</s> surrounded by beings.
He gleams with weapons shining like the tongues of Time,
surrounded by chariot-spears like a rain-cloud by lightning.
His strung bows, gold-backed on every side,
adorn that excellent chariot like the fall of <s>Śakra</s>'s bolt in the sky.
Who is this tiger among rākṣasas, making the battlefield shine,
approaching, the best of chariot-warriors, in a chariot radiant as the sun?
He is adorned by <s>Rāhu</s> set upon the peak of his banner,
and he lights up the ten directions with arrows bright as sunbeams.
His bow, thrice-bent, roaring like a cloud, gold-backed and adorned,
shines like the bow of <s>Śatakratu</s>.
That great chariot, with standard, with banners, and with its rear-dragging gear,
joined with four horsemen, has the sound of a thundering cloud.

children.text: viṃśatir daśa cāṣṭau ca tūṇīrā ratham āsthitāḥ
children.translated_text: Twenty, ten, and eight quivers are mounted on the chariot,
along with fearsome bows and bowstrings tawny like gold.

children.text: dvau ca khaḍgau rathagatau pārśvasthau pārśvaśobhinau
children.translated_text: Two swords rest on the chariot, one on each side, beautifying the sides,
with hilts measured at four hands and blades visibly extending ten hands.
Steadfast, with a red neck-cord, resembling a great mountain,
he is like Death with the great mouth of Time, like the sun standing within a cloud.
He shines with his two arms bound by golden armlets,
like <s>Himavān</s>, best of mountains, with two lofty peaks.

children.text: kuṇḍalābhyāṃ tu yasyaitad bhāti vaktraṃ śubhekṣaṇam
children.translated_text: His handsome-eyed face shines with those two earrings,
like the full orb of the moon set between the two <s>Punarvasus</s>.

children.text: ācakṣva me mahābāho tvam enaṃ rākṣasottamam
children.translated_text: Tell me, mighty-armed one, who this best of rākṣasas is,

children.text: yaṃ dṛṣṭvā vānarāḥ sarve bhayārtā vidrutā diśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: at the sight of whom all the monkeys, stricken with fear, have fled in all directions.
Questioned by <s>Rāma</s>, the immeasurably radiant prince,
the greatly radiant <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> explained it to <s>Rāghava</s>.
There is the ten-necked, greatly radiant king, the younger brother of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas, terrible in deeds and great in energy.
He had a valiant son, equal to <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle,
one who served his elders, retained what he heard, and was the best of all who knew weapons.

children.text: aśvapṛṣṭhe rathe nāge khaḍge dhanuṣi karṣaṇe
children.translated_text: He was esteemed in riding horse, chariot, and elephant, in sword, bow, and drawing the bow,

children.text: bhede sāntve ca dāne ca naye mantre ca saṃmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and in division, conciliation, gift, policy, and counsel.

children.text: yasya bāhuṃ samāśritya laṅkā bhavati nirbhayā
children.translated_text: Leaning on whose arm, <s>Laṅkā</s> becomes fearless,
they know this <s>Atikāya</s> as the son of <s>Dhānyamālinī</s>.
By him <s>Brahmā</s> was propitiated through austerity, his self made pure;
weapons too were obtained, and enemies were defeated.
Invulnerability against gods and Asuras was granted to him by <s>Svayambhū</s> himself,
as well as this divine armor and this sun-bright chariot.
By him gods and Dānavas were defeated by the hundreds,
rākṣasas were protected, and Yakṣas too were cut down.

children.text: vajraṃ viṣṭambhitaṃ yena bāṇair indrasya dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: By him the thunderbolt of wise <s>Indra</s> was checked with arrows,
and likewise the noose of the lord of waters was repelled in battle.
This is powerful <s>Atikāya</s>, bull among rākṣasas,
the wise son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, crusher of the pride of gods and Dānavas.

children.text: tad asmin kriyatāṃ yatnaḥ kṣipraṃ puruṣapuṃgava
children.translated_text: Therefore effort should be made against him quickly, best of men,
before he brings the monkey armies to destruction with his arrows.
Then powerful <s>Atikāya</s>, entering the army of monkeys,

children.text: visphārayāmāsa dhanur nanāda ca punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: stretched his bow and roared again and again.

children.text: taṃ bhīmavapuṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā rathasthaṃ rathināṃ varam
children.translated_text: Seeing him of dreadful form, standing on his chariot, the best of chariot-warriors,
the great-souled chief monkeys rushed upon him.

children.text: kumudo dvivido maindo nīlaḥ śarabha eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Kumuda</s>, <s>Dvivida</s>, <s>Mainda</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, and also <s>Śarabha</s>
rushed upon him all at once with trees and mountain peaks.
Their trees and rocks
the greatly radiant <s>Atikāya</s>, foremost of those skilled in missiles, cut apart with gold-adorned arrows.

children.text: tāṃścaiva sarvān sa harīñ śaraiḥ sarvāyasair balī
children.translated_text: And all those monkeys the mighty night-roamer, huge in body,
pierced in battle with all-iron arrows as they faced him.
Tormented by the shower of arrows, their limbs split open, those leapers
were unable to retaliate against <s>Atikāya</s> in the great battle.
That rākṣasa terrified the army of monkey heroes,

children.text: mṛgayūtham iva kruddho harir yauvanam āsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: like an enraged lion in its prime terrifying a herd of deer.

children.text: sa rākṣasendro harisainyamadhye nāyudhyamānaṃ nijaghāna kaṃcit
children.translated_text: That lord of rākṣasas, standing amid the monkey army, did not kill anyone who was not fighting;

children.text: upetya rāmaṃ sadhanuḥkalāpī sagarvitaṃ vākyam idaṃ babhāṣe ||
children.translated_text: he approached <s>Rāma</s>, equipped with bow and quiver, and spoke these proud words:

children.text: rathe sthito 'haṃ śaracāpapāṇir na prākṛtaṃ kaṃcana yodhayāmi
children.translated_text: 'Standing on my chariot with arrows and bow in hand, I do not fight with any common man.

children.text: yasyāsti śaktir vyavasāyayuktā dadātu me kṣipram ihādya yuddham ||
children.translated_text: Let the one who has strength joined with resolve give me battle here today at once.'

children.text: tat tasya vākyaṃ bruvato niśamya cukopa saumitrir amitrahantā
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech as he uttered it, <s>Saumitri</s>, slayer of foes, became enraged;

children.text: amṛṣyamāṇaśca samutpapāta jagrāha cāpaṃ ca tataḥ smayitvā ||
children.translated_text: unable to endure it, he sprang up and then, smiling, took his bow.

children.text: kruddhaḥ saumitrir utpatya tūṇād ākṣipya sāyakam
children.translated_text: Angry <s>Saumitri</s> leapt up, drew an arrow from his quiver,
and before <s>Atikāya</s> pulled his great bow.

children.text: pūrayan sa mahīṃ śailān ākāśaṃ sāgaraṃ diśaḥ
children.translated_text: Filling the earth, the mountains, the sky, the ocean, and the quarters,
the fierce twang of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s bowstring terrified the night-roamers.
Hearing then the fearsome roar of <s>Saumitri</s>'s bow,
the mighty, greatly radiant son of the lord of rākṣasas was amazed.
Then <s>Atikāya</s>, angered on seeing <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> risen up,

children.text: ādāya niśitaṃ bāṇam idaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: took a sharpened arrow and spoke these words:
'You are a boy, <s>Saumitri</s>, unskilled in feats of valor.

children.text: gaccha kiṃ kālasadṛśaṃ māṃ yodhayitum icchasi ||
children.translated_text: Go away. Why do you wish to fight me, who am like Death?

children.text: na hi madbāhusṛṣṭānām astrāṇāṃ himavān api
children.translated_text: For even <s>Himavān</s> is not able to withstand the force

children.text: soḍhum utsahate vegam antarikṣam atho mahī ||
children.translated_text: of the missiles released by my arms, nor are the sky or the earth.
You wish to awaken a dozing fire of time.

children.text: nyasya cāpaṃ nivartasva mā prāṇāñ jahi madgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Lay down your bow and turn back; do not give up your life by coming to me.

children.text: athavā tvaṃ pratiṣṭabdho na nivartitum icchasi
children.translated_text: But if you are stubborn and do not wish to turn back,
stand here; abandoning your life, you will go to the house of <s>Yama</s>.
Behold my sharp arrows, crushers of the pride of enemies,
like the weapons of the Lord, adorned with heated gold.

children.text: eṣa te sarpasaṃkāśo bāṇaḥ pāsyati śoṇitam
children.translated_text: This arrow of mine, like a serpent, will drink your blood,
as an angry lion drinks the blood of a lordly elephant.'

children.text: śrutvātikāyasya vacaḥ saroṣaṃ sagarvitaṃ saṃyati rājaputraḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Atikāya</s>'s angry and proud words in the fight, the prince

children.text: sa saṃcukopātibalo bṛhacchrīr uvāca vākyaṃ ca tato mahārtham ||
children.translated_text: became enraged, mighty and splendid, and then spoke words of great meaning:

children.text: na vākyamātreṇa bhavān pradhāno na katthanāt satpuruṣā bhavanti
children.translated_text: 'You are not foremost by words alone, and good men are not made by boasting.

children.text: mayi sthite dhanvini bāṇapāṇau vidarśayasvātmabalaṃ durātman ||
children.translated_text: Since I stand here as an archer with arrow in hand, show your own strength, evil-minded one.
Reveal yourself by action; you should not boast.

children.text: pauruṣeṇa tu yo yuktaḥ sa tu śūra iti smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But one who is endowed with valor is remembered as a hero.
Equipped with every weapon, you are an archer mounted on a chariot;

children.text: śarair vā yadi vāpyastrair darśayasva parākramam ||
children.translated_text: whether with arrows or with missiles, show your prowess.
Then with sharp arrows I shall make your head fall,
as the wind makes a palm fruit, ripened by time, fall from its stalk.
Today my arrows, adorned with heated gold,
will drink the blood rising from within your limbs around the arrow wounds.

children.text: bālo 'yam iti vijñāya na māvajñātum arhasi
children.translated_text: Knowing, "He is a boy," you should not despise me.

children.text: bālo vā yadi vā vṛddho mṛtyuṃ jānīhi saṃyuge ||
children.translated_text: Whether one is a boy or an old man, know death in battle.'
Hearing <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s reasoned and deeply meaningful words,
<s>Atikāya</s> became very angry and took up an excellent arrow.

children.text: tato vidyādharā bhūtā devā daityā maharṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: Then Vidyādharas, spirits, gods, daityas, and great seers,
and great-souled Guhyakas, watched that battle then.
Then angry <s>Atikāya</s> set an arrow on his bow,
and hurled it at <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, as though contracting the sky.
As that sharp arrow, like a venomous serpent, came flying on,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, slayer of enemy heroes, cut it with a crescent-headed arrow.

children.text: taṃ nikṛttaṃ śaraṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛttabhogam ivoragam
children.translated_text: Seeing that arrow cut apart like a serpent with its hood severed,
<s>Atikāya</s>, greatly enraged, took up five arrows.
The night-roamer hurled those arrows at <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>;
before they reached him, <s>Bharata</s>'s younger brother cut them apart with sharp arrows.
Having cut them apart with sharp arrows, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, slayer of enemy heroes,

children.text: ādade niśitaṃ bāṇaṃ jvalantam iva tejasā ||
children.translated_text: took up a sharp arrow blazing, as it were, with splendor.
Taking it, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> set it on his excellent bow,

children.text: vicakarṣa ca vegena visasarja ca sāyakam ||
children.translated_text: drew it swiftly, and released the shaft.
With that arrow, fully drawn and released, straight at every joint,
that hero struck the foremost rākṣasa on the forehead.

children.text: sa lalāṭe śaro magnastasya bhīmasya rakṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: The arrow sunk into the forehead of that terrible rākṣasa,
smeared with blood, looked like a lordly serpent in battle.
The rākṣasa, shaken by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s arrow, trembled,
like the dreadful gate-tower of <s>Tripura</s> struck by <s>Rudra</s>'s arrow.
Then, regaining his breath, that mighty one reflected and considered,
'Well done. By that arrow-strike you are worthy of praise from me, my enemy.'
Having thus deliberated, he bowed his face and bent both his arms;

children.text: sa rathopastham āsthāya rathena pracacāra ha ||
children.translated_text: then he mounted the seat of the chariot and drove forth in the chariot.

children.text: ekaṃ trīn pañca sapteti sāyakān rākṣasarṣabhaḥ
children.translated_text: One, three, five, seven: the bull among rākṣasas took up arrows,
set them to the bow as well, drew it back, and released them.
Those arrows, resembling death, loosed from the bow of the lord of rākṣasas,
with golden feathers and shining like the sun, made the sky seem blazing.
Then the younger brother of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, unshaken, cut apart those torrents of arrows
released by the rākṣasa, with many sharp shafts.

children.text: tāñ śarān yudhi samprekṣya nikṛttān rāvaṇātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing those arrows cut down in battle, the son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
the enemy of the lord of the Thirty Gods, became angry and seized a sharp arrow.
That greatly radiant one set it to the bow and suddenly released that arrow;
then he struck <s>Saumitri</s> as he advanced, between the breasts.
Struck by <s>Atikāya</s> in battle on the chest, <s>Saumitri</s>

children.text: susrāva rudhiraṃ tīvraṃ madaṃ matta iva dvipaḥ ||
children.translated_text: poured out fierce blood, like an intoxicated elephant pouring out rut-fluid.

children.text: sa cakāra tadātmānaṃ viśalyaṃ sahasā vibhuḥ
children.translated_text: Then the powerful one at once made himself free of the arrow,

children.text: jagrāha ca śaraṃ tīkṣṇam astreṇāpi samādadhe ||
children.translated_text: took up a sharp shaft, and fitted it with a weapon.
He joined that arrow with the <s>Āgneya</s> weapon;

children.text: sa jajvāla tadā bāṇo dhanuścāsya mahātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then the arrow blazed, as did the bow of that great-souled hero.
The exceedingly radiant <s>Atikāya</s> took up the solar weapon,
and with it he joined an arrow like a serpent, with golden feathers.

children.text: tatastaṃ jvalitaṃ ghoraṃ lakṣmaṇaḥ śaram āhitam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> hurled that blazing, terrible arrow, set upon the bow,
at <s>Atikāya</s>, like <s>Antaka</s> hurling the staff of death.
Seeing the arrow joined with the <s>Āgneya</s> weapon, the night-roamer
then released a blazing arrow joined with the solar weapon.
Both arrows struck one another in the sky,
their tips blazing with splendor, like two angry serpents.
Having burned one another up, those two excellent arrows fell to the surface of the earth;
their flames gone and reduced to ash, they no longer shone.
Then <s>Atikāya</s>, enraged, released the <s>Aiṣīka</s> weapon;

children.text: tat pracicheda saumitrir astram aindreṇa vīryavān ||
children.translated_text: the valiant <s>Saumitri</s> cut that weapon apart with the <s>Aindra</s> weapon.
Seeing the <s>Aiṣīka</s> destroyed, the prince, the son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
angrily joined an arrow with the <s>Yāmya</s> weapon.
Then the night-roamer hurled that weapon at <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>;

children.text: vāyavyena tad astraṃ tu nijaghāna sa lakṣmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> struck down that weapon with the <s>Vāyavya</s> weapon.
Then, like a raincloud with streams of water,
the enraged <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> showered the son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> with streams of arrows.
Those arrows, reaching <s>Atikāya</s>'s armor adorned with diamonds,
fell at once to the earth, their tips and barbs broken.
Seeing those arrows rendered useless, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, slayer of enemy heroes,
the greatly renowned one, showered him with a thousand arrows.
Though being rained upon by floods of arrows, mighty <s>Atikāya</s>,
a rākṣasa whose armor was invulnerable in battle, was not pained at all.

children.text: na śaśāka rujaṃ kartuṃ yudhi tasya narottamaḥ
children.translated_text: That best of men could not cause him pain in battle;

children.text: athainam abhyupāgamya vāyur vākyam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: then <s>Vāyu</s> approached him and spoke these words.
This one has a boon granted by <s>Brahmā</s> and is covered by invulnerable armor;

children.text: brāhmeṇāstreṇa bhinddhyenam eṣa vadhyo hi nānyathā ||
children.translated_text: pierce him with the <s>Brāhma</s> weapon, for he can be killed by this and not otherwise.

children.text: tataḥ sa vāyor vacanaṃ niśamya saumitrir indrapratimānavīryaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, hearing the word of <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Saumitri</s>, whose valor equaled <s>Indra</s>'s,

children.text: samādade bāṇam amoghavegaṃ tad brāhmam astraṃ sahasā niyojya ||
children.translated_text: took up an arrow of unfailing speed, quickly applying to it that <s>Brāhma</s> weapon.

children.text: tasmin varāstre tu niyujyamāne saumitriṇā bāṇavare śitāgre
children.translated_text: As that excellent weapon was being applied by <s>Saumitri</s> to the sharp-tipped best of arrows,

children.text: diśaḥ sacandrārkamahāgrahāśca nabhaśca tatrāsa rarāsa corvī ||
children.translated_text: the quarters, with moon, sun, and great planets, trembled, and the sky and earth roared.

children.text: taṃ brahmaṇo 'streṇa niyujya cāpe śaraṃ supuṅkhaṃ yamadūtakalpam
children.translated_text: Having applied <s>Brahmā</s>'s weapon to the bow, that well-feathered arrow resembling a messenger of <s>Yama</s>,

children.text: saumitrir indrārisutasya tasya sasarja bāṇaṃ yudhi vajrakalpam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Saumitri</s> released in battle against that son of <s>Indra</s>'s enemy an arrow like the thunderbolt.
<s>Atikāya</s> then saw that arrow released by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, of unfailing speed,
falling upon him, shining like fire, with splendid feathers marked by gold and the finest diamond.

children.text: taṃ prekṣamāṇaḥ sahasātikāyo jaghāna bāṇair niśitair anekaiḥ
children.translated_text: As <s>Atikāya</s> watched it, he suddenly struck it with many sharp arrows;

children.text: sa sāyakastasya suparṇavegas tadātivegena jagāma pārśvam ||
children.translated_text: but that shaft, with the speed of <s>Suparṇa</s>, went to his side with tremendous force.

children.text: tam āgataṃ prekṣya tadātikāyo bāṇaṃ pradīptāntakakālakalpam
children.translated_text: Seeing that arrow come on, blazing and like <s>Antaka</s> and Time,
<s>Atikāya</s>, with his effort unshaken, struck it with spears, javelins, maces, axes, tridents, and ploughshares.
Having made those weapons of wondrous form futile, that fire-blazing arrow

children.text: prasahya tasyaiva kirīṭajuṣṭaṃ tadātikāyasya śiro jahāra ||
children.translated_text: forcibly carried away the head of that very <s>Atikāya</s>, adorned with a diadem.
That head, together with its helmet, crushed by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s arrow,

children.text: papāta sahasā bhūmau śṛṅgaṃ himavato yathā ||
children.translated_text: suddenly fell to the ground like a peak of <s>Himavat</s>.
Then many monkeys, filled with delight and with faces like opened lotuses,

children.text: apūjayaṃllakṣmaṇam iṣṭabhāginaṃ hate ripau bhīmabale durāsade ||
children.translated_text: honored fortunate <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> when the terrible, mighty, unassailable foe had been slain.
Then the surviving hosts of rākṣasas there quickly reported to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>

children.text: rakṣogaṇāstatra hatāvaśiṣṭās te rāvaṇāya tvaritaṃ śaśaṃsuḥ ||
children.translated_text: that those foremost rākṣasas had been slain: <s>Devāntaka</s> and the others, <s>Triśiras</s> and <s>Atikāya</s>.

children.text: tato hatāṃstān sahasā niśamya rājā mumohāśrupariplutākṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, hearing suddenly that they had been killed, the king fainted, his eyes flooded with tears;

children.text: putrakṣayaṃ bhrātṛvadhaṃ ca ghoraṃ vicintya rājā vipulaṃ pradadhyau ||
children.translated_text: thinking of the loss of his sons and the dreadful killing of his brothers, the king sank into deep brooding.

children.text: tatastu rājānam udīkṣya dīnaṃ śokārṇave saṃparipupluvānam
children.translated_text: Then, seeing the king wretched and completely drowning in an ocean of grief,

children.text: atharṣabho rākṣasarājasūnur athendrajid vākyam idaṃ babhāṣe ||
children.translated_text: Then the bull among them, the son of the rākṣasa king, <s>Indrajit</s>, spoke these words:

children.text: na tāta mohaṃ pratigantum arhasi yatrendrajijjīvati rākṣasendra
children.translated_text: Father, you should not fall into delusion, so long as <s>Indrajit</s> lives, O lord of rākṣasas.

children.text: nendrāribāṇābhihato hi kaścit prāṇān samarthaḥ samare 'bhidhartum ||
children.translated_text: For no one struck by the arrows of <s>Indrajit</s>, the foe of <s>Indra</s>, is able to hold on to his life in battle.
Today you shall see <s>Rāma</s>, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, his body pierced and torn apart by my arrows,

children.text: gatāyuṣaṃ bhūmitale śayānaṃ śaraiḥ śitair ācitasarvagātram ||
children.translated_text: his life gone, lying on the ground, every limb covered with sharp shafts.

children.text: imāṃ pratijñāṃ śṛṇu śakraśatroḥ suniścitāṃ pauruṣadaivayuktām
children.translated_text: Hear this firm vow of the enemy of <s>Śakra</s>, joined with manly strength and divine power:

children.text: adyaiva rāmaṃ saha lakṣmaṇena saṃtāpayiṣyāmi śarair amoghaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: this very day I shall torment <s>Rāma</s>, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, with unfailing arrows.
Today <s>Indra</s>, <s>Vaivasvata</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, the <s>Sādhyas</s>, the <s>Aśvins</s>, <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, the moon, and the sun

children.text: drakṣyanti me vikramam aprameyaṃ viṣṇor ivograṃ baliyajñavāṭe ||
children.translated_text: will behold my immeasurable valor, fierce like that of <s>Viṣṇu</s> at the sacrificial ground of <s>Bali</s>.

children.text: sa evam uktvā tridaśendraśatrur āpṛcchya rājānam adīnasattvaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the enemy of the lord of the gods, whose spirit was not low, took leave of the king
and mounted a chariot swift as the wind, yoked with the best of mules.
Mounting that chariot, the very splendid subduer of enemies, like the chariot of <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: jagāma sahasā tatra yatra yuddham ariṃdamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: went swiftly to the place where the battle was.
Many warriors of great strength followed that great-souled one as he set out,
exulting, with excellent bows in their hands.
Some were mounted on the shoulders of elephants, and some on excellent horses,
bearing spears, mallets, swords, axes, battle-axes, and maces.

children.text: sa śaṅkhaninadair bhīmair bherīṇāṃ ca mahāsvanaiḥ
children.translated_text: With the terrible blare of conches and the great din of kettledrums,
the enemy of the lord of the gods went forth, praised by the night-roamers.
That slayer of foes shone beneath a full parasol white as a conch and the moon,
like the sky with the full moon.
Then the hero was fanned with golden chowries adorned with gold,
the foremost of all bowmen, with the finest beautiful fly-whisks.
Then <s>Laṅkā</s>, through <s>Indrajit</s>, whose splendor was equal to the sun's,
and whose valor was unmatched, shone like the heaven through the radiant sun.

children.text: sa tu dṛṣṭvā viniryāntaṃ balena mahatā vṛtam
children.translated_text: Seeing him going out surrounded by a great army,
the glorious lord of rākṣasas, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, spoke to his son:

children.text: tvam apratirathaḥ putra jitaste yudhi vāsavaḥ
children.translated_text: Son, you have no rival in the chariot-fight; <s>Vāsava</s> has been conquered by you in battle.

children.text: kiṃ punar mānuṣaṃ dhṛṣyaṃ na vadhiṣyasi rāghavam ||
children.translated_text: How then will you not kill the vulnerable human <s>Rāghava</s>?
So addressed by the lord of rākṣasas, and having received his great blessing,
the hero quickly went by his horse-yoked chariot to <s>Nikumbhilā</s>.
When that very splendid subduer of enemies reached the battlefield,
he stationed the rākṣasas all around his chariot as guards.
Then the foremost rākṣasa, whose radiance was like that of the fire-eater,
offered oblations to the eater of oblations, with mantras and according to rule.
With preparations of offerings, preceded by garlands and fragrances,
that mighty lord of rākṣasas offered there to the purifying fire.
Weapons, arrow-feathers, and fuel-sticks of vibhītaka wood,

children.text: lohitāni ca vāsāṃsi sruvaṃ kārṣṇāyasaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: red garments too, and a ladle of black iron were there.
Having spread the fire there with arrow-feathers and javelins,
he seized the throat of a wholly black goat while it was still alive.
At once, when the fire had been kindled, smokeless and with great flames,
those signs appeared which indicated victory.
The purifying fire, its flame turning clockwise and resembling heated gold,
rose up by itself and accepted that oblation.
Then he, the best of those who know weapons, caused the <s>Brāhma</s> weapon to be brought,
and consecrated the bow, his own chariot, and everything there with mantras.
While that weapon was being invoked and the fire was being offered to,
the vault of heaven, with sun, planets, moon, and stars, trembled.
Having sacrificed to the fire, he whose fiery splendor blazed like fire and whose might was equal to great <s>Indra</s>'s,
together with bow, arrows, sword, chariot, horses, and charioteer, concealed his inconceivable form in the sky.

children.text: sa sainyam utsṛjya sametya tūrṇaṃ mahāraṇe vānaravāhinīṣu
children.translated_text: Leaving his army, he quickly came together in the great battle against the vānaras' hosts,

children.text: adṛśyamānaḥ śarajālam ugraṃ vavarṣa nīlāmbudharo yathāmbu ||
children.translated_text: and, unseen, poured down a fierce net of arrows, like a dark cloud pouring water.
Their bodies shattered by the arrows of the conqueror of <s>Śakra</s>, struck down by his māyā, crying out in discordant voices,
the monkey warriors fell in battle, massive as mountains, like great mountains struck by <s>Indra</s>'s thunderbolt.

children.text: te kevalaṃ saṃdadṛśuḥ śitāgrān bāṇān raṇe vānaravāhinīṣu
children.translated_text: In the battle, among the vānaras' troops, they saw only the sharp-tipped arrows,

children.text: māyānigūḍhaṃ ca surendraśatruṃ na cātra taṃ rākṣasam abhyapaśyan ||
children.translated_text: and the enemy of the lord of the gods hidden by māyā; but they did not see that rākṣasa there.

children.text: tataḥ sa rakṣo'dhipatir mahātmā sarvā diśo bāṇagaṇaiḥ śitāgraiḥ
children.translated_text: Then that great-souled lord of rākṣasas covered all the quarters with masses of sharp-tipped arrows,
bright as sunlight, and cast the chiefs of the vānaras into despair.
Whirling spears, swords, and axes, blazing like kindled fire,
flaming with sparks like burning fires, he poured them fiercely upon the army of the lords of the leapers.
Then the leaders of the monkey troops, struck by the sharp arrows of the conqueror of <s>Śakra</s>, blazing like fire,
looked like blooming kiṃśuka trees.
Rushing against one another and crying out in discordant voices,
the bull-like vānaras, pierced by the weapon of the lord of rākṣasas, fell down.
Some, looking up at the sky, were struck in the eyes;
pierced by arrows, they ran into one another and fell upon the earth.
And <s>Hanumān</s>, <s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>Aṅgada</s>, <s>Gandhamādana</s>,

children.text: jāmbavantaṃ suṣeṇaṃ ca vegadarśinam eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jāmbavān</s>, <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, and <s>Vegadarśin</s> as well

children.text: maindaṃ ca dvividaṃ nīlaṃ gavākṣaṃ gajagomukhau
children.translated_text: <s>Mainda</s>, <s>Dvivida</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, <s>Gavākṣa</s>, <s>Gaja</s>, and <s>Gomukha</s>,
<s>Kesari</s>, <s>Hariloman</s>, and the vānara <s>Vidyuddaṃṣṭra</s>,
<s>Sūryānana</s>, <s>Jyotimukha</s>, and likewise the hari <s>Dadhimukha</s>,

children.text: pāvakākṣaṃ nalaṃ caiva kumudaṃ caiva vānaram ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pāvakākṣa</s>, <s>Nala</s>, and also the vānara <s>Kumuda</s>,
with javelins, spears, and sharp arrows charged with <s>Indrajit</s>'s mantras,
that best of rākṣasas pierced all those tiger-like haris.

children.text: sa vai gadābhir hariyūthamukhyān nirbhidya bāṇaistapanīyapuṅkhaiḥ
children.translated_text: Having shattered the foremost leaders of the hari troops with maces and arrows with golden shafts,
he rained upon <s>Rāma</s>, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, networks of showers of arrows like rays of the sun.

children.text: sa bāṇavarṣair abhivarṣyamāṇo dhārānipātān iva tān vicintya
children.translated_text: Being showered over with those showers of arrows, and considering them like falling streams of rain,
<s>Rāma</s>, of supremely wondrous splendor, looked on and then said this to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:

children.text: asau punar lakṣmaṇa rākṣasendro brahmāstram āśritya surendraśatruḥ
children.translated_text: "<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, that lord of rākṣasas, the enemy of the lord of the gods, has again taken refuge in the <s>Brahmāstra</s>.

children.text: nipātayitvā harisainyam ugram asmāñ śarair ardayati prasaktam ||
children.translated_text: Having struck down the fierce army of haris, he continually torments us with arrows.
The great-souled one has obtained a boon from <s>Svayambhū</s>; he stands in the sky, invisible, his dreadful body hidden.

children.text: kathaṃ nu śakyo yudhi naṣṭadeho nihantum adyendrajid udyatāstraḥ ||
children.translated_text: How can <s>Indrajit</s>, whose body has disappeared in battle and whose weapon is raised, be slain today?

children.text: manye svayambhūr bhagavān acintyo yasyaitad astraṃ prabhavaśca yo 'sya
children.translated_text: I think the inconceivable Blessed <s>Svayambhū</s>, whose weapon this is and who is its source, is present here.

children.text: bāṇāvapātāṃstvam ihādya dhīman mayā sahāvyagramanāḥ sahasva ||
children.translated_text: Wise one, with an undistracted mind, endure today these falls of arrows here together with me.

children.text: pracchādayatyeṣa hi rākṣasendraḥ sarvā diśaḥ sāyakavṛṣṭijālaiḥ
children.translated_text: For this lord of rākṣasas is covering all the directions with networks of showers of arrows,

children.text: etacca sarvaṃ patitāgryavīraṃ na bhrājate vānararājasainyam ||
children.translated_text: and this whole army of the vānara king, with its foremost heroes fallen, no longer shines.

children.text: āvāṃ tu dṛṣṭvā patitau visaṃjñau nivṛttayuddhau hataroṣaharṣau
children.translated_text: But when he sees us two fallen, unconscious, withdrawn from battle, our anger and joy destroyed,
he will surely enter the dwelling of the foes of the immortals, carrying off the fortune of the forefront of battle."
Then the two of them there at that time were mangled by <s>Indrajit</s>'s net of weapons,

children.text: sa cāpi tau tatra viṣādayitvā nanāda harṣād yudhi rākṣasendraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and that lord of rākṣasas too, having cast them into despondency there, roared in battle out of joy.

children.text: sa tat tadā vānararājasainyaṃ rāmaṃ ca saṃkhye saha lakṣmaṇena
children.translated_text: Having cast into despondency that army of the vānara king and <s>Rāma</s> in battle together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
he suddenly entered the city protected by the arms of <s>Daśagrīva</s>.

children.text: tayostadā sāditayo raṇāgre mumoha sainyaṃ hariyūthapānām
children.translated_text: When those two had been laid low at the forefront of battle, the army of the hari troop-leaders was stupefied,

children.text: sugrīvanīlāṅgadajāmbavanto na cāpi kiṃcit pratipedire te ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, <s>Aṅgada</s>, and <s>Jāmbavān</s> could make out nothing at all.

children.text: tato viṣaṇṇaṃ samavekṣya sainyaṃ vibhīṣaṇo buddhimatāṃ variṣṭhaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, seeing the army dispirited, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, foremost of the intelligent,
spoke to the heroic leaders of the branch-roamers, reassuring them with incomparable words:

children.text: mā bhaiṣṭa nāstyatra viṣādakālo yad āryaputrāvavaśau viṣaṇṇau
children.translated_text: "Do not be afraid. This is no time for despair, because the noble princes lie helpless and dejected,
bearing out the word of <s>Svayambhū</s>, since they have been laid low by <s>Indrajit</s>'s net of weapons.

children.text: tasmai tu dattaṃ paramāstram etat svayambhuvā brāhmam amoghavegam
children.translated_text: This supreme weapon, the unfailing and swift <s>Brahmāstra</s>, was given to him by <s>Svayambhū</s>.

children.text: tanmānayantau yadi rājaputrau nipātitau ko 'tra viṣādakālaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If the princes, honoring it, have fallen down, what occasion for despair is there?"

children.text: brāhmam astraṃ tadā dhīmānmānayitvā tu mārutiḥ
children.translated_text: Then wise <s>Hanūmān</s>, honoring that <s>Brahmāstra</s>,
heard <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>'s words and then said this to him:
"In this slaughtered army of the swift vānaras,

children.text: yo yo dhārayate prāṇāṃstaṃ tam āśvāsayāvahe ||
children.translated_text: let us reassure each one who still sustains his life."
Then those two heroes together, <s>Hanūmān</s> and the best of rākṣasas,
with torches in hand, moved about at night over the battlefield.
With tails, hands, thighs, feet, fingers, heads, and necks cut off,
with bodies streaming blood from wounds and flowing on every side,
crowded with fallen vānaras, mountain-like in form,
and with fallen blazing weapons, they saw the earth.
<s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>Aṅgada</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, <s>Śarabha</s>, <s>Gandhamādana</s>,
<s>Jāmbavān</s>, <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, <s>Vegadarśana</s>, and <s>Āhuka</s>,

children.text: maindaṃ nalaṃ jyotimukhaṃ dvividaṃ panasaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Mainda</s>, <s>Nala</s>, <s>Jyotimukha</s>, <s>Dvivida</s>, and likewise <s>Panasa</s>,
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> and <s>Hanūmān</s> saw them struck down in battle.
Sixty-seven crores of the swift vānaras had been slain
in the remaining fifth part of the day by the favorite of <s>Svayambhū</s>.
Seeing the dreadful force, like a flood of the ocean, tormented by arrows,
<s>Hanūmān</s>, together with <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, searched for <s>Jāmbavān</s>.
He was aged with natural old age and covered with hundreds of arrows,
the heroic son of <s>Prajāpati</s>, like a fire growing calm.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tam upasaṃgamya paulastyo vākyam abravīt
children.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Paulastya</s> approached and spoke these words:

children.text: kaccid ārya śaraistīkṣṇair na prāṇā dhvaṃsitāstava ||
children.translated_text: "Noble sir, I hope your vital breaths have not been destroyed by the sharp arrows."
Hearing <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>'s words, <s>Jāmbavān</s>, bull among bears,

children.text: kṛcchrād abhyudgiran vākyam idaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: with difficulty brought forth speech and uttered these words:
"Greatly heroic lord of the nairṛtas, I recognize you by your voice.

children.text: pīḍyamānaḥ śitair bāṇair na tvāṃ paśyāmi cakṣuṣā ||
children.translated_text: Tormented by sharp arrows, I cannot see you with my eyes.

children.text: añjanā suprajā yena mātariśvā ca nairṛta
children.translated_text: O nairṛta, does the best of vānaras, <s>Hanūmān</s>, for whom <s>Añjanā</s> was a blessed mother
and <s>Mātariśvan</s> a blessed father, still sustain his life somewhere?"
Hearing <s>Jāmbavān</s>'s words, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> said this:
"Passing over the noble princes, why do you ask about <s>Māruti</s>?

children.text: naiva rājani sugrīve nāṅgade nāpi rāghave
children.translated_text: Not toward King <s>Sugrīva</s>, nor toward <s>Aṅgada</s>, nor even toward <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: ārya saṃdarśitaḥ sneho yathā vāyusute paraḥ ||
children.translated_text: noble sir, have you shown such affection as you have particularly toward the son of <s>Vāyu</s>."
Hearing <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>'s words, <s>Jāmbavān</s> spoke these words:
"Listen, tiger among nairṛtas, to why I ask about <s>Māruti</s>."

children.text: tasmiñ jīvati vīre tu hatam apyahataṃ balam
children.translated_text: But while that hero is alive, the army, though slain, is not slain;
if <s>Hanūmān</s> has given up his life, then we, though living, are slain.
Dear one, if <s>Māruti</s>, equal to the wind, still holds on to life,
and is like <s>Vaiśvānara</s> in energy, then there would be hope of life.
Then, approaching the elder, he duly bowed down,
and <s>Hanūmān</s>, son of the wind, took hold of <s>Jāmbavān</s>'s feet.
Hearing <s>Hanūmān</s>'s words, though his senses were still distressed,
that bull among bears considered himself as if born again.
Then the greatly radiant <s>Jāmbavān</s> said to <s>Hanūmān</s>,
"Come, tiger among the haris; you must save the vānaras.
No one else is equal to this exertion; you are their supreme friend.
This is the time for your valor; I do not see anyone else at all.
Gladden the ranks of the heroic bears and vānaras,
and make these two, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, who have been laid low, free from their arrows.
Having gone a very great distance, high above the ocean,
<s>Hanūmān</s>, you must go to <s>Himavat</s>, the best of mountains.
Then, destroyer of enemies, you will see the golden, very terrible <s>Ṛṣabha</s>,
the excellent mountain, and also the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>.
Between those two peaks, hero, you will see the herb mountain,
blazing with unequalled radiance and filled with every medicinal plant.
On its summit, tiger among vānaras, you will see four herbs born there,

children.text: drakṣyasy oṣadhayo dīptā dīpayantyo diśo daśa ||
children.translated_text: shining brightly and lighting up the ten directions.
They are <s>Mṛtasaṃjīvanī</s>, and also <s>Viśalyakaraṇī</s>,
as well as <s>Sauvarṇakaraṇī</s> and the great herb <s>Saṃdhānī</s>.

children.text: tāḥ sarvā hanuman gṛhya kṣipram āgantum arhasi
children.translated_text: Taking all of them, <s>Hanūmān</s>, you must come back quickly.
Son of the scent-bearing wind, restore heart to the haris by joining them again with their life-breaths."
Hearing the words of <s>Jāmbavān</s>, <s>Hanūmān</s>, bull among the haris,
was filled with surges of rising strength, like the ocean with rushing waters.
Standing on the edge of the mountain slope and pressing down that best of mountains,

children.text: hanūmān dṛśyate vīro dvitīya iva parvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the heroic <s>Hanūmān</s> appeared like a second mountain.
Split apart by the hari's feet, that mountain sank down;
heavily compressed, it could not bear itself then.

children.text: tasya petur nagā bhūmau harivegācca jajvaluḥ
children.translated_text: Its trees fell to the ground, and because of the hari's speed they burst into flame;
and the peaks of the mountain, pressed by <s>Hanūmān</s>, were scattered about.
While that excellent mountain was being crushed, with its trees and rocky slopes broken,

children.text: na śekur vānarāḥ sthātuṃ ghūrṇamāne nagottame ||
children.translated_text: the vānaras could not stand upon it as it reeled.
With its great gates shaken and its houses and gateways shattered,
<s>Laṅkā</s>, panic-stricken at night, then seemed as if it were dancing.
The son of the wind, resembling a holder of the earth, pressed down the mountain,
and shook the earth together with the oceans.
Pressing the mountain with his two feet and opening his fierce mouth like the mouth of the submarine fire,
he roared loudly, as if terrifying the rākṣasas.
Hearing the wondrous roar as he roared,

children.text: laṅkāsthā rākṣasāḥ sarve na śekuḥ spandituṃ bhayāt ||
children.translated_text: all the rākṣasas dwelling in <s>Laṅkā</s> could not stir because of fear.
Then, having bowed to <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Māruti</s> of terrible prowess,
scorcher of foes, undertook a supreme deed for <s>Rāghava</s>'s sake.

children.text: sa puccham udyamya bhujaṃgakalpaṃ vinamya pṛṣṭhaṃ śravaṇe nikuñcya
children.translated_text: Raising his tail like a serpent, bending his back, and drawing in his ears,

children.text: vivṛtya vaktraṃ vaḍavāmukhābham āpupluve vyomni sa caṇḍavegaḥ ||
children.translated_text: opening his mouth like the mouth of the submarine fire, he leapt into the sky with fierce speed.

children.text: sa vṛkṣaṣaṇḍāṃstarasā jahāra śailāñ śilāḥ prākṛtavānarāṃśca
children.translated_text: By his force he carried away clusters of trees, mountains, rocks, and ordinary vānaras;
hurled onward by the speed of his arms and thighs, they fell into the water when their speed was spent.
Stretching out those two arms like the coils of serpents, with strength like the enemy of serpents,

children.text: jagāma meruṃ nagarājam agryaṃ diśaḥ prakarṣann iva vāyusūnuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the son of the wind went toward <s>Meru</s>, the foremost king of mountains, as if dragging the directions after him.

children.text: sa sāgaraṃ ghūrṇitavīcimālaṃ tadā bhṛśaṃ bhrāmitasarvasattvam
children.translated_text: Looking upon the ocean, with its garlands of waves whirling and all its creatures violently tossed,

children.text: samīkṣamāṇaḥ sahasā jagāma cakraṃ yathā viṣṇukarāgramuktam ||
children.translated_text: he went suddenly, like the discus released from the tip of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s hand.

children.text: sa parvatān vṛkṣagaṇān sarāṃsi nadīstaṭākāni purottamāni
children.translated_text: He saw mountains, groups of trees, lakes, rivers, ponds, and excellent cities,

children.text: sphītāñjanāṃstān api samprapaśyañ jagāma vegāt pitṛtulyavegaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and even those flourishing peoples or regions, as he went with a speed equal to his father's.
Taking the path of the sun, he went on without weariness;
that best of haris saw <s>Himavat</s>, the excellent mountain.
It was furnished with many waterfalls, with many caves and cascades,
and with lovely peaks resembling masses of white clouds.
Reaching that great lord of mountains, with its exceedingly high and dreadful peaks,
he saw holy great hermitages served by the finest hosts of divine seers.

children.text: sa brahmakośaṃ rajatālayaṃ ca śakrālayaṃ rudraśarapramokṣam
children.translated_text: He saw <s>Brahmakośa</s>, <s>Rajatālaya</s>, <s>Śakrālaya</s>, the place where <s>Rudra</s>'s arrow was released,
<s>Hayānana</s>, the blazing <s>Brahmaśiras</s>, and the attendants of <s>Vaivasvata</s>.

children.text: vajrālayaṃ vaiśravaṇālayaṃ ca sūryaprabhaṃ sūryanibandhanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: He saw <s>Vajrālaya</s>, <s>Vaiśravaṇālaya</s>, <s>Sūryaprabha</s>, and <s>Sūryanibandhana</s>,

children.text: brahmāsanaṃ śaṃkarakārmukaṃ ca dadarśa nābhiṃ ca vasuṃdharāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmāsana</s>, <s>Śaṃkara</s>'s bow, and the navel of the earth.

children.text: kailāsam agryaṃ himavacchilāṃ ca tatharṣabhaṃ kāñcanaśailam agryam
children.translated_text: He saw foremost <s>Kailāsa</s>, the snowy rock, and <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, the foremost golden mountain,
and the lord of all herb mountains, blazing with every shining medicinal plant.
Seeing that mountain blazing with rays like fire, the son of <s>Vāsava</s>'s messenger was amazed;

children.text: āplutya taṃ cauṣadhiparvatendraṃ tatrauṣadhīnāṃ vicayaṃ cakāra ||
children.translated_text: having leapt onto that lord of herb mountains, he began there to search for the herbs.
The great monkey, having passed over thousands of yojanas,
The son of <s>Māruta</s> ranged over the mountain that bore the divine herbs.
But all those great herbs on that best of mountains,
knowing that a seeker had come, then went out of sight.

children.text: sa tā mahātmā hanumān apaśyaṃś cukopa kopācca bhṛśaṃ nanāda
children.translated_text: The great-souled <s>Hanumān</s>, not seeing them, grew angry, and in anger roared violently.
Unable to endure it, with eyes like fire, he spoke this word to that lord of mountains:

children.text: kim etad evaṃ suviniścitaṃ te yad rāghave nāsi kṛtānukampaḥ
children.translated_text: What is this decision of yours, that you show no compassion toward <s>Rāghava</s>?

children.text: paśyādya madbāhubalābhibhūto vikīrṇam ātmānam atho nagendra ||
children.translated_text: See yourself today, O king of mountains, shattered by the strength of my arms.

children.text: sa tasya śṛṅgaṃ sanagaṃ sanāgaṃ sakāñcanaṃ dhātusahasrajuṣṭam
children.translated_text: He seized its peak, with its trees and serpents, golden and filled with a thousand minerals,
with its ridges scattered and its upper slopes shaken, and with force he suddenly tore it up.

children.text: sa taṃ samutpāṭya kham utpapāta vitrāsya lokān sasurān surendrān
children.translated_text: Having uprooted it, he leapt into the sky, terrifying the worlds along with the gods and <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: saṃstūyamānaḥ khacarair anekair jagāma vegād garuḍogravīryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, praised by many sky-ranging beings, he went swiftly, mighty in valor like fierce <s>Garuḍa</s>.

children.text: sa bhāskarādhvānam anuprapannas tad bhāskarābhaṃ śikharaṃ pragṛhya
children.translated_text: Following the path of the sun, carrying that sun-bright peak,

children.text: babhau tadā bhāskarasaṃnikāśo raveḥ samīpe pratibhāskarābhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he then shone, himself like the sun, near the sun and with the splendor of a second sun.

children.text: sa tena śailena bhṛśaṃ rarāja śailopamo gandhavahātmajastu
children.translated_text: With that mountain the son of the wind-bearer shone greatly, himself like a mountain,

children.text: sahasradhāreṇa sapāvakena cakreṇa khe viṣṇur ivoddhṛtena ||
children.translated_text: like <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the sky with the lifted discus of a thousand spokes and fire.

children.text: taṃ vānarāḥ prekṣya tadā vineduḥ sa tān api prekṣya mudā nanāda
children.translated_text: Seeing him then, the monkeys shouted; and seeing them too, he roared with joy.

children.text: teṣāṃ samudghuṣṭaravaṃ niśamya laṅkālayā bhīmataraṃ vineduḥ ||
children.translated_text: Hearing the loud cry raised by them, the dwellers in <s>Laṅkā</s> cried out still more terribly.

children.text: tato mahātmā nipapāta tasmiñ śailottame vānarasainyamadhye
children.translated_text: Then the great-souled one descended with that excellent mountain in the midst of the monkey army.

children.text: haryuttamebhyaḥ śirasābhivādya vibhīṣaṇaṃ tatra ca sasvaje saḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having bowed with his head to the foremost monkeys, he also embraced <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> there.

children.text: tāvapyubhau mānuṣarājaputrau taṃ gandham āghrāya mahauṣadhīnām
children.translated_text: And those two princes, sons of a human king, smelling the fragrance of the great herbs,

children.text: babhūvatustatra tadā viśalyāvuttasthur anye ca haripravīrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: then became freed from their arrows there, and the other foremost monkey heroes also rose up.

children.text: tato harir gandhavahātmajastu tam oṣadhīśailam udagravīryaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the monkey, the son of the wind-bearer, of lofty valor,

children.text: nināya vegāddhimavantam eva punaśca rāmeṇa samājagāma ||
children.translated_text: swiftly took that herb-mountain back to <s>Himavant</s> itself, and again came to <s>Rāma</s>.
Then mighty <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the monkeys, spoke,
making an urgent request to powerful <s>Hanumān</s>:
Since <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> has been slain and the princes have been struck down,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> should not now be given any withdrawal.

children.text: ye ye mahābalāḥ santi laghavaśca plavaṃgamāḥ
children.translated_text: Let all those strong and swift monkeys who are present,
the bulls among leapers, quickly leap upon <s>Laṅkā</s>, taking up firebrands.
Then, when the sun had set, at that fierce onset of night,
those bulls among leapers went toward <s>Laṅkā</s> with their firebrands.
Assailed from every side by troops of monkeys with firebrands in their hands,
the misshapen-eyed rākṣasas at the guard-posts suddenly fled in confusion.
At the gateways, watchtowers, lanes, and various passages,
and in the palaces, they joyfully set fire.
Then the fire consumed thousands of their houses,
and the dwellings of the rākṣasas, of all the householders.
Of those whose armor was variegated with gold, who wore garlands, wreaths, and garments,
whose eyes rolled from drinking liquor, and whose gait was unsteady with intoxication,
whose garments were held by their beloved women, whose anger had arisen against the enemy,
who held maces, spears, and swords in their hands, even while they were eating and drinking,
who slept on costly beds together with their beloveds,

children.text: trastānāṃ gacchatāṃ tūrṇaṃ putrān ādāya sarvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and who, terrified, hurried everywhere carrying their sons,
of those inhabitants of <s>Laṅkā</s>, thousands of houses

children.text: adahat pāvakastatra jajvāla ca punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the fire burned there then, and it blazed up again and again.
The rich and very costly mansions, deep and full of fine qualities,
with golden moons and half-moons, and lofty moon-pavilions,
with jewel-inlaid latticed windows and foundations throughout,
variegated with gems and coral and seeming to touch the sun,
resounding with the sounds of curlews, peacocks, vīṇās,
and ornaments, those houses, like mountains, the fire burned.
The gateways surrounded by flame gleamed,
like masses of clouds bound with lightning in the hot season.
And noble women asleep in the aerial palaces, as they were being burned,
their ornaments cast off, cried loudly, 'Alas! Alas!'
There, even the buildings encircled by fire fell down,
like the peaks of a great mountain struck by the thunderbolt of the wielder of the thunderbolt.
As they were being burned, those buildings shone from afar,
like peaks of <s>Himavat</s> and forests of blazing herbs.
With the tops of mansions burning and blazing with flames,

children.text: rātrau sā dṛśyate laṅkā puṣpitair iva kiṃśukaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Laṅkā</s> was seen at night as if covered with flowering kiṃśukas.

children.text: hastyadhyakṣair gajair muktair muktaiśca turagair api
children.translated_text: With elephant keepers and elephants set loose, and with horses also set loose,
<s>Laṅkā</s> became, at the end of the world, like an ocean in which sea-monsters wandered bewildered.

children.text: aśvaṃ muktaṃ gajo dṛṣṭvā kaccid bhīto 'pasarpati
children.translated_text: Seeing a horse set loose, an elephant, frightened, would sometimes move away;

children.text: bhīto bhītaṃ gajaṃ dṛṣṭvā kvacid aśvo nivartate ||
children.translated_text: and seeing a frightened elephant, a frightened horse would sometimes turn back.

children.text: sā babhūva muhūrtena haribhir dīpitā purī
children.translated_text: In a moment that city, set on fire by the monkeys, became
like the earth ablaze at the terrible destruction of this world.
The sound of the women, enveloped in smoke and crying loudly,
tormented by the burning fire, was heard for ten yojanas.
Then other rākṣasas, their bodies burned, came out outside,
and the monkeys, eager to fight, suddenly leapt upon them.

children.text: udghuṣṭaṃ vānarāṇāṃ ca rākṣasānāṃ ca nisvanaḥ
children.translated_text: The shouting of the vānaras and the roar of the rākṣasas

children.text: diśo daśa samudraṃ ca pṛthivīṃ cānvanādayat ||
children.translated_text: made the ten directions, the ocean, and the earth resound.
But those two great-souled ones, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, freed of their wounds,
both took up their excellent bows without agitation.
Then, as <s>Rāma</s> twanged his supreme bow,
there arose a tumultuous sound that brought fear to the rākṣasas.
At that time <s>Rāma</s>, twanging his great bow, shone forth

children.text: bhagavān iva saṃkruddho bhavo vedamayaṃ dhanuḥ ||
children.translated_text: like the blessed, enraged <s>Bhava</s> with the Veda-made bow.
The shouted cry raised by the vānaras, the roar of the rākṣasas,

children.text: jyāśabdaścāpi rāmasya trayaṃ vyāpa diśo daśa ||
children.translated_text: and also the sound of <s>Rāma</s>'s bowstring: these three filled the ten directions.
And by the arrows released from his bow, the gate-tower of that city,
resembling a peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>, was shattered and fell to the ground.

children.text: tato rāmaśarān dṛṣṭvā vimāneṣu gṛheṣu ca
children.translated_text: Then, seeing <s>Rāma</s>'s arrows in their aerial cars and houses,
a tumultuous arming of the rākṣasa lords took place.
As they were arming themselves and uttering lion-roars,
the night of the rākṣasa lords became as if dreadful.
Those chiefs of the vānaras, commanded by great-souled <s>Sugrīva</s>,
having come near the gate, said, "Fight, bulls among leapers!"

children.text: yaśca vo vitathaṃ kuryāt tatra tatra vyavasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: "And whoever among you, stationed here and there, should act falsely,
he is to be leapt upon and slain as one who corrupts the king's command."
When those foremost vānaras stood by the gate, their hands blazing bright with burning brands,

children.text: sthiteṣu dvāram āsādya rāvaṇaṃ manyur āviśat ||
children.translated_text: anger entered <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: tasya jṛmbhitavikṣepād vyāmiśrā vai diśo daśa
children.translated_text: Because of the agitation caused by his gaping and tossing about, all ten directions became confused;
anger, as if taking the very form of <s>Rudra</s>, appeared in his limbs.

children.text: sa nikumbhaṃ ca kumbhaṃ ca kumbhakarṇātmajāvubhau
children.translated_text: Enraged, he sent <s>Nikumbha</s> and <s>Kumbha</s>,
the two sons of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, together with many rākṣasas.

children.text: śaśāsa caiva tān sarvān rākṣasān rākṣaseśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: And the lord of the rākṣasas gave orders to all those rākṣasas:
"Rākṣasas, go forth right here, making the lion-roar resound!"
Then, urged on by him, the heroic rākṣasas with blazing weapons

children.text: laṅkāyā niryayur vīrāḥ praṇadantaḥ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: went out from <s>Laṅkā</s>, roaring again and again.
That terrible rākṣasa army, crowded with dreadful horses, chariots, elephants,
and many foot-soldiers, with blazing spears, maces, swords, lances, javelins, and bows,
that dreadful rākṣasa force, terrible in valor and manly strength,
was seen with blazing lances and with hundreds of small bells ringing.
Its arms were overlaid with golden mail; it was encircled with axes,
brandishing great weapons, and its bows were set with arrows.
The mighty wind was made fragrant by the abundance of scents, garlands, and wine,
and the army was dreadful, thronged with brave men, and sounded like a great mass of clouds.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā balam āyāntaṃ rākṣasānāṃ sudāruṇam
children.translated_text: Seeing that exceedingly terrible army of rākṣasas coming on,

children.text: saṃcacāla plavaṃgānāṃ balam uccair nanāda ca ||
children.translated_text: the army of the leapers trembled and roared aloud.
Then, leaping with speed, that great force of rākṣasas
advanced against the hostile army like a moth into a fire.
With its clubs and thunderbolt-like weapons rubbed by the contact of their arms,
the excellent army of the rākṣasas shone even more brightly.
Likewise, some of those dreadful-looking night-roamers
struck down the heroic vānaras on every side with sharp swords.
One struck another who was striking; another brought down one who was bringing someone down.
One reviled another who was reviling him; another bit one who was biting.
One said, "Give it!" another said, "I am giving it!" and another in turn said,
"Why do you trouble me? Stand still!" Thus they spoke to one another there.
A very dreadful battle of vānaras and rākṣasas began,
crowded with great uplifted lances, fists, spears, and swords.
The rākṣasas threw down vānaras by tens and sevens;

children.text: rākṣasān daśa sapteti vānarā jaghnur āhave ||
children.translated_text: the vānaras slew rākṣasas by tens and sevens in the fight.
With hair and girdles loosened, with armor and banners cast off,
the vānaras surrounded the rākṣasa army, laying hold of it.
When that confused and dreadful battle, destructive of heroic men, had begun,
<s>Aṅgada</s>, eager for combat, encountered the heroic <s>Kampana</s>.
Calling out to <s>Aṅgada</s>, <s>Kampana</s>, in anger and with speed,

children.text: gadayā kampanaḥ pūrvaṃ sa cacāla bhṛśāhataḥ ||
children.translated_text: first struck him with a mace; and he staggered, badly hit.

children.text: sa saṃjñāṃ prāpya tejasvī cikṣepa śikharaṃ gireḥ
children.translated_text: Regaining consciousness, the fiery hero hurled a mountain peak;
crushed by the blow, <s>Kampana</s> fell to the ground.
Then the army of the rākṣasa lord, distressed because its foremost heroes had been slain,
moved toward the place where the son of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> was.
And as that army rushed on with speed, <s>Kumbha</s> calmed it.

children.text: sa dhanur dhanvināṃ śreṣṭhaḥ pragṛhya susamāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: That best of archers, taking up his bow with perfect composure,
released serpent-like arrows that tore bodies apart.

children.text: tasya tacchuśubhe bhūyaḥ saśaraṃ dhanur uttamam
children.translated_text: His excellent bow, furnished with arrows, shone still more
like a second bow of <s>Indra</s>, radiant with lightning and <s>Airāvata</s>.
Then with a feathered arrow, drawn to the ear and released,
with a golden shaft and feathered dress, he struck <s>Dvivida</s>.
Suddenly struck by it, losing his footing and trembling,
that best of leapers, bewildered and like a mountain peak, fell down.

children.text: maindastu bhrātaraṃ dṛṣṭvā bhagnaṃ tatra mahāhave
children.translated_text: But <s>Mainda</s>, seeing his brother broken there in the great battle,
rushed forward swiftly, seizing a great rock.

children.text: tāṃ śilāṃ tu pracikṣepa rākṣasāya mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: The mighty one hurled that rock at the rākṣasa,

children.text: bibheda tāṃ śilāṃ kumbhaḥ prasannaiḥ pañcabhiḥ śaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: but <s>Kumbha</s> split that rock with five clear-flying arrows.
And fitting another handsome arrow, like a venomous serpent,
the mighty one struck <s>Mainda</s>, <s>Dvivida</s>'s elder brother, in the chest.

children.text: sa tu tena prahāreṇa maindo vānarayūthapaḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Mainda</s>, leader of the vānara troops, by that blow
was struck by him in a vital spot and fell unconscious upon the ground.

children.text: aṅgado mātulau dṛṣṭvā patitau tau mahābalau
children.translated_text: Seeing those two mighty maternal uncles fallen, <s>Aṅgada</s>
rushed swiftly at <s>Kumbha</s>, who had raised his bow.

children.text: tam āpatantaṃ vivyādha kumbhaḥ pañcabhir āyasaiḥ
children.translated_text: As he came on, <s>Kumbha</s> pierced him with five iron arrows

children.text: tribhiścānyaiḥ śitair bāṇair mātaṃgam iva tomaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and with three other sharp arrows, like an elephant with lances.

children.text: so 'ṅgadaṃ vividhair bāṇaiḥ kumbho vivyādha vīryavān
children.translated_text: The valiant <s>Kumbha</s> pierced <s>Aṅgada</s> with many kinds of arrows,
sharp, keen, unblunted in edge, and adorned with gold.
Though his limbs were pierced, <s>Aṅgada</s>, son of <s>Vāli</s>, did not tremble;
he rained showers of rocks and trees upon his head.

children.text: sa pracicheda tān sarvān bibheda ca punaḥ śilāḥ
children.translated_text: He cut all those down and again split the rocks,
the splendid son of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, hurled by the son of <s>Vāli</s>.
Seeing the vānara troop-leader rushing upon him,

children.text: bhruvor vivyādha bāṇābhyām ulkābhyām iva kuñjaram ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kumbha</s> pierced him between the brows with two arrows, like an elephant with two firebrands.
<s>Aṅgada</s> covered his eyes, which were smeared with blood, with one hand,
and with one hand seized a nearby sāla tree.
That tree was like <s>Indra</s>'s banner and resembled <s>Mandara</s>;
as he hurled it with speed, while all the rākṣasas looked on,

children.text: sa cicheda śitair bāṇaiḥ saptabhiḥ kāyabhedanaiḥ
children.translated_text: he cut it down with seven sharp arrows that pierced the body.

children.text: aṅgado vivyathe 'bhīkṣṇaṃ sasāda ca mumoha ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aṅgada</s> suffered greatly again and again, sank down, and fell senseless.

children.text: aṅgadaṃ vyathitaṃ dṛṣṭvā sīdantam iva sāgare
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Aṅgada</s> distressed, as if sinking in the ocean,
the hard-to-assail foremost vānaras reported it to <s>Rāghava</s>.
When <s>Rāma</s> heard that the son of <s>Vāli</s> was distressed in the great battle,
he then ordered the foremost vānaras headed by <s>Jāmbavat</s>.

children.text: te tu vānaraśārdūlāḥ śrutvā rāmasya śāsanam
children.translated_text: Those tiger-like vānaras, hearing <s>Rāma</s>'s command,
rushed on in great anger against <s>Kumbha</s>, who had raised his bow.
Then, with trees and rocks in their hands and eyes reddened by anger,
the bull-like vānaras rushed forward, wishing to protect <s>Aṅgada</s>.
<s>Jāmbavat</s>, <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, and the vānara <s>Vegadarśin</s>
ran in anger against the heroic son of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>.
Seeing those mighty vānara lords rushing upon him,
he blocked them with a flood of arrows, as a mountain blocks a lake.

children.text: tasya bāṇacayaṃ prāpya na śekur ativartitum
children.translated_text: Reaching that mass of his arrows, they could not pass beyond it,
those great-souled vānara lords, as the great ocean cannot pass the shore.
Seeing those troops of monkeys tormented by showers of arrows,
and putting his nephew <s>Aṅgada</s> behind him, the lord of the leapers,
<s>Sugrīva</s>, rushed swiftly at <s>Kumbha</s> in battle,
like a swift lion at an elephant moving along mountain slopes.

children.text: utpāṭya ca mahāśailān aśvakarṇān dhavān bahūn
children.translated_text: Uprooting great mountain peaks, many aśvakarṇa and dhava trees,
and various other trees, the mighty one hurled them.
That hard-to-withstand shower of trees, covering the sky,
the splendid son of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> cut down with sharp arrows.
Pierced by <s>Kumbha</s>'s well-aimed, fierce, sharp arrows,

children.text: ācitāste drumā rejur yathā ghorāḥ śataghnayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: those trees shone like dreadful śataghnīs.

children.text: drumavarṣaṃ tu tacchinnaṃ dṛṣṭvā kumbhena vīryavān
children.translated_text: Seeing that shower of trees cut apart by <s>Kumbha</s>,
the splendid lord of the vānaras, mighty in spirit, was not shaken.
Though suddenly pierced through, and though he endured those arrows,
he snatched away <s>Kumbha</s>'s bow and broke it, bright as <s>Indra</s>'s bow.

children.text: avaplutya tataḥ śīghraṃ kṛtvā karma suduṣkaram
children.translated_text: Then, quickly leaping down after doing that most difficult deed,

children.text: abravīt kupitaḥ kumbhaṃ bhagnaśṛṅgam iva dvipam ||
children.translated_text: he angrily spoke to <s>Kumbha</s>, who was like an elephant with broken tusk:

children.text: nikumbhāgraja vīryaṃ te bāṇavegaṃ tad adbhutam
children.translated_text: O elder brother of <s>Nikumbha</s>, your valor and the speed of your arrows are wondrous;

children.text: saṃnatiśca prabhāvaśca tava vā rāvaṇasya vā ||
children.translated_text: so too your composure and power, whether they are yours or <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s.
O you who are like <s>Prahrāda</s>, <s>Bali</s>, <s>Vṛtraghna</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s>,
you alone have taken after your father, even stronger than he.
You alone, mighty-armed, spear in hand, crusher of enemies,
the thirty gods cannot overcome, as afflictions cannot overcome one who has mastered the senses.
By the power of a boon your uncle withstands gods and dānavas,
but <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, by valor, withstands gods and asuras.
In the bow you are equal to <s>Indrajit</s>, and in majesty to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>;

children.text: tvam adya rakṣasāṃ loke śreṣṭho 'si balavīryataḥ ||
children.translated_text: today, in the world of rākṣasas, you are supreme in strength and valor.
Let all beings today behold your wondrous great clash with me in battle,
like that of <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Śambara</s>.
An incomparable deed has been done, and skill in weapons has been displayed;
these monkey heroes of terrible prowess have been felled by you.
And from fear of reproach, hero, you have not been slain by me,

children.text: kṛtakarmā pariśrānto viśrāntaḥ paśya me balam ||
children.translated_text: for you had done your deed and were exhausted; now, rested, behold my strength.
By that contemptuous speech of <s>Sugrīva</s>, with which he was nevertheless honored,
his energy grew like that of a fire into which ghee has been poured.

children.text: tataḥ kumbhaḥ samutpatya sugrīvam abhipadya ca
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kumbha</s> sprang up and, attacking <s>Sugrīva</s>,
angrily struck him in the chest with a fist moving at thunderbolt speed.

children.text: tasya carma ca pusphoṭa saṃjajñe cāsya śoṇitam
children.translated_text: His skin burst open, and blood appeared from him;
and that fist, moving with great force, rebounded against the plate of bone.

children.text: tadā vegena tatrāsīt tejaḥ prajvālitaṃ muhuḥ
children.translated_text: Then, from that force, a blaze flared up there again and again,
like flame produced by the crushing stroke of a thunderbolt on Mount <s>Meru</s>.
Struck there by him, <s>Sugrīva</s>, bull among vānaras,
the mighty one clenched a fist like a thunderbolt.
With a thousand rays spread open, shining like the orb of the sun,
the mighty one brought his fist down upon <s>Kumbha</s>'s chest.
Struck by that fist, the rākṣasa quickly fell,
like a red-bodied, blazing-rayed luminary falling by chance from the sky.
As <s>Kumbha</s> fell, his form, with his chest shattered by the fist,

children.text: babhau rudrābhipannasya yathā rūpaṃ gavāṃ pateḥ ||
children.translated_text: shone like the form of the lord of cattle when assailed by <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: tasmin hate bhīmaparākrameṇa plavaṃgamānām ṛṣabheṇa yuddhe
children.translated_text: When he had been slain in battle by that bull among the leapers, terrible in valor,

children.text: mahī saśailā savanā cacāla bhayaṃ ca rakṣāṃsyadhikaṃ viveśa ||
children.translated_text: the earth with its mountains and forests shook, and greater fear entered the rākṣasas.
Seeing his brother struck down by <s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>Nikumbha</s>
looked at the lord of the vānaras as though burning him with anger.
Then the hero took up a splendid iron club, bound with a garland-wreath and marked with five finger-spans,
like the peak of a great mountain.
It was encircled with bands of gold and adorned with diamonds and coral,
dreadful like the staff of <s>Yama</s>, and dispelling the fear of the rākṣasas.
Whirling it in battle, the greatly radiant <s>Nikumbha</s>, equal to <s>Śakra</s>'s banner,
roared with his mouth opened wide, terrible in prowess.
With the necklace resting on his chest, and with armlets on his arms,

children.text: kuṇḍalābhyāṃ ca mṛṣṭābhyāṃ mālayā ca vicitrayā ||
children.translated_text: with polished earrings and with a variegated garland,

children.text: nikumbho bhūṣaṇair bhāti tena sma parigheṇa ca
children.translated_text: <s>Nikumbha</s> shone with his ornaments and with that iron club,
as a cloud shines with <s>Indra</s>'s bow, with lightning and thunder.
At the tip of the club a knot of wind burst for that great-souled one,
and it blazed with a roar, like smokeless fire.
Together with the city <s>Viṭapāvatī</s>, with its excellent Gandharva mansions,
and together with <s>Amarāvatī</s> and all its buildings,
