with its hosts of stars and asterisms, with the moon and the great planets,
the vault of heaven seemed to whirl, spun by <s>Nikumbha</s>'s club.
He became hard to approach, radiant with the adornment of his club;
the fire that was <s>Nikumbha</s>, fueled by anger, rose like the fire at the end of an age.

children.text: rākṣasā vānarāścāpi na śekuḥ spandituṃ bhayāt
children.translated_text: The rākṣasas and the vānaras alike could not move because of fear,
but mighty <s>Hanūmān</s>, opening his chest wide, stood facing him.
Then the strong one, whose arms were like iron clubs, took that sun-bright club
and brought it down upon the chest of that mighty hero.

children.text: sthire tasyorasi vyūḍhe parighaḥ śatadhā kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: On his firm, broad chest the iron club was shattered into a hundred pieces,
breaking apart suddenly like a hundred meteors in the sky.

children.text: sa tu tena prahāreṇa cacāla ca mahākapiḥ
children.translated_text: But from that blow the great ape trembled,
shaken by the iron club as a mountain is shaken in an earthquake.
Thus struck by him, <s>Hanūmān</s>, the best of leapers,
drew up his fist with force, though he was already exceedingly strong.
Raising it, the mighty and greatly radiant hero aimed it at <s>Nikumbha</s>'s chest,
and, swift and possessing the force of the wind, hurled it with speed.

children.text: tataḥ pusphoṭa carmāsya prasusrāva ca śoṇitam
children.translated_text: Then his skin burst open and blood streamed forth;

children.text: muṣṭinā tena saṃjajñe jvālā vidyud ivotthitā ||
children.translated_text: from that fist-blow a flame arose like lightning.

children.text: sa tu tena prahāreṇa nikumbho vicacāla ha
children.translated_text: From that blow <s>Nikumbha</s> indeed staggered,
yet, steadying himself, he seized mighty <s>Hanūmān</s>.
Then the inhabitants of <s>Laṅkā</s> cried out terribly in the battle,
seeing mighty <s>Hanūmān</s> lifted up by <s>Nikumbha</s>.
But even while he was being carried away in that way by the son of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>,
the son of the Wind struck him with a fist having the speed of a thunderbolt.
Then, freeing himself, he dropped down to the ground,
and <s>Hanūmān</s>, son of the Wind, quickly crushed <s>Nikumbha</s>.
Throwing <s>Nikumbha</s> down with utmost effort, he crushed him,
and springing up with force, the mighty hero fell upon his chest.
Seizing his neck with both arms and twisting it around,
he tore off the great, dreadful head as <s>Nikumbha</s> roared.

children.text: atha vinadati sādite nikumbhe pavanasutena raṇe babhūva yuddham
children.translated_text: Then, when <s>Nikumbha</s> had been laid low in battle by the son of the Wind, there arose, as he cried out,
a much more terrible battle between the armies of <s>Daśaratha</s>'s son and the lord of rākṣasas, both filled with anger.

children.text: nikumbhaṃ ca hataṃ śrutvā kumbhaṃ ca vinipātitam
children.translated_text: Hearing that <s>Nikumbha</s> had been slain and that <s>Kumbha</s> had been struck down,
the exceedingly wrathful <s>Rāvaṇa</s> blazed up like fire.
The rākṣasa, overwhelmed by both anger and grief,
urged on wide-eyed <s>Makarākṣa</s>, the son of <s>Khara</s>.
'Go, my son, commanded by me and accompanied by force;

children.text: rāghavaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ caiva jahi tau savanaukasau ||
children.translated_text: slay <s>Rāghava</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, those two forest-dwellers.'

children.text: rāvaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā śūro mānī kharātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s words, the heroic and proud son of <s>Khara</s>,
the night-roaming <s>Makarākṣa</s>, gladly said, 'So be it.'
He bowed to the Ten-necked one and circumambulated him,
then the strong one went out from <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s bright palace at his command.
The son of <s>Khara</s> said this to the commander standing nearby:

children.text: ratham ānīyatāṃ śīghraṃ sainyaṃ cānīyatāṃ tvarāt ||
children.translated_text: 'Let a chariot be brought quickly, and let the army be brought at once.'
Hearing that command of his, the night-roaming commander

children.text: syandanaṃ ca balaṃ caiva samīpaṃ pratyapādayat ||
children.translated_text: brought the chariot and the army into his presence.
The night-roamer circumambulated the chariot and mounted it,

children.text: sūtaṃ saṃcodayāmāsa śīghraṃ me ratham āvaha ||
children.translated_text: and urged the charioteer, 'Drive my chariot quickly.'
Then <s>Makarākṣa</s> said this to all those rākṣasas:
'All of you rākṣasas, fight in front of me.
I have been commanded by great-souled <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, king of the rākṣasas,
to kill those two, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, in battle.'

children.text: adya rāmaṃ vadhiṣyāmi lakṣmaṇaṃ ca niśācarāḥ
children.translated_text: Today, O night-roamers, I shall kill <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
and also the branch-animal <s>Sugrīva</s> and the vānaras, with the finest arrows.
Today, with the fall of my spears, I shall burn up the great army of the vānaras
that has come here, as fire burns dry fuel.
Hearing that speech of <s>Makarākṣa</s>, those night-roamers,
all strong, intent, and equipped with many kinds of weapons,
those heroic shape-shifters, tusked and tawny-eyed,
roaring like elephants, with disheveled hair and terrible forms,
surrounded the huge-bodied son of <s>Khara</s>, himself huge-bodied,
and then advanced joyfully, shaking the earth.
Then, from thousands of conches and kettledrums beaten on every side,

children.text: kṣveḍitāsphoṭitānāṃ ca tataḥ śabdo mahān abhūt ||
children.translated_text: and from roars and slaps of defiance, a great sound arose.
Then the goad slipped from the hand of his charioteer,

children.text: papāta sahasā caiva dhvajastasya ca rakṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and suddenly the banner of that rākṣasa also fell down.
The horses yoked to his chariot, bereft of vigor,

children.text: caraṇair ākulair gatvā dīnāḥ sāsramukhā yayuḥ ||
children.translated_text: went on with confused steps, dejected and with tearful faces.
At the departure of that fierce, evil-minded <s>Makarākṣa</s>,
a wind blew against him, dusty, harsh, and terrible.
Seeing those omens, the most valorous rākṣasas

children.text: acintya nirgatāḥ sarve yatra tau rāmalakṣmaṇau ||
children.translated_text: gave them no thought and all went out to where <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> were.
Dark as clouds, elephants, or buffaloes, and often cut by maces and swords in the front of battle,

children.text: aham aham iti yuddhakauśalāste rajanicarāḥ paribabhramur nadantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: those night-roamers, skilled in war and crying 'I, I!', ranged about, roaring.
When the foremost vānaras saw <s>Makarākṣa</s> coming out,
they all sprang up at once and stood ready, eager to fight.

children.text: tataḥ pravṛttaṃ sumahat tad yuddhaṃ lomaharṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Then that very great battle began, making the hair stand on end,
between the night-roamers and the leapers, like the battle of the gods with the dānavas.
With the casting down of trees and spears, and the hurling of rocks and iron clubs,
the vānaras and night-roamers then crushed one another.
With lances, spears, maces, swords, and javelins, the night-roamers,
and on every side with broad-bladed weapons, bhindipālas, and falling arrows,
and also with nooses, hammers, clubs, thunderbolt-like blows, and other weapons,
those night-roamers made slaughter among the lion-like vānaras.
Tormented by floods of arrows from the son of <s>Khara</s>, the vānaras,
their minds bewildered, all fled, oppressed by fear.

children.text: tān dṛṣṭvā rākṣasāḥ sarve dravamāṇān vanaukasaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing those forest-dwellers running away, all the rākṣasas,
exultant and appearing victorious, roared like lions.
Then, as those vānaras were fleeing on every side,
<s>Rāma</s> checked those rākṣasas with a shower of arrows.
Seeing the rākṣasas checked, the night-roamer <s>Makarākṣa</s>,
filled with the fire of anger, spoke these words:

children.text: tiṣṭha rāma mayā sārdhaṃ dvandvayuddhaṃ dadāmi te
children.translated_text: Stand, <s>Rāma</s>; I offer you single combat with me.

children.text: tyājayiṣyāmi te prāṇān dhanurmuktaiḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: With sharp arrows released from my bow, I shall make you give up your life.
When in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest you killed my father,
who stood before me, intent on his own deed, remembering that, my rage grows.
My limbs burn fiercely, wicked <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: yanmayāsi na dṛṣṭastvaṃ tasmin kāle mahāvane ||
children.translated_text: because I did not see you at that time in the great forest.

children.text: diṣṭyāsi darśanaṃ rāma mama tvaṃ prāptavān iha
children.translated_text: By good fortune, <s>Rāma</s>, you have now come here within my sight.
You are longed for by me as another animal is by a hungry lion.
Today, carried by the force of my arrows to the realm of the lord of the dead,

children.text: ye tvayā nihatāḥ śūrāḥ saha taistvaṃ sameṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: you shall join those heroes who were slain by you.

children.text: bahunātra kim uktena śṛṇu rāma vaco mama
children.translated_text: What need is there of much speech here? Hear my word, <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: paśyantu sakalā lokāstvāṃ māṃ caiva raṇājire ||
children.translated_text: Let all the worlds behold you and me in the battlefield.

children.text: astrair vā gadayā vāpi bāhubhyāṃ vā mahāhave
children.translated_text: Whether with missiles, or with a mace, or with our two arms in this great battle,

children.text: abhyastaṃ yena vā rāma tena vā vartatāṃ yudhi ||
children.translated_text: or by whatever you have practiced, <s>Rāma</s>, by that let the fight proceed.
Hearing the words of <s>Makarākṣa</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>,
laughed and spoke a reply to him who was answering again and again:
Fourteen thousand rākṣasas, and your father too,
as well as <s>Triśiras</s> and <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>, were slain by me in <s>Daṇḍaka</s>.
Today, sinner, vultures, jackals, and crows,
with sharp beaks, claws, and hooked talons, will be well fed on your flesh.
Thus addressed by <s>Rāma</s>, the night-roamer son of <s>Khara</s>
released floods of arrows at that <s>Rāghava</s> in the battlefield.
But <s>Rāma</s>, with a shower of arrows, cut those arrows apart in many pieces;

children.text: nipetur bhuvi te chinnā rukmapuṅkhāḥ sahasraśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: cut off, they fell on the ground by thousands, with golden shafts.

children.text: tad yuddham abhavat tatra sametyānyonyam ojasā
children.translated_text: There arose then that battle, as they met one another with force,
between the son of the rākṣasa <s>Khara</s> and the son of <s>Daśaratha</s>.
Like two clouds in the sky, the sound of their bowstrings then,
loud from arrows released from their bows, was heard in the battlefield.
The gods, dānavas, gandharvas, kinnaras, and great serpents,
all standing in the sky, wished to see that wonder.
As they were wounded in each other's limbs, their strength grew twofold;
the two of them made blow and counterblow against one another in the battlefield.
The rākṣasa cut off the floods of arrows released by <s>Rāma</s> in the battle,
and <s>Rāma</s> likewise cut apart in many pieces with arrows those released by the rākṣasa.
All the quarters and intermediate quarters were spread over with floods of arrows,
and the earth too was covered all around and no longer shone forth.
Then the mighty-armed one, angered, cut the rākṣasa's bow;

children.text: aṣṭābhir atha nārācaiḥ sūtaṃ vivyādha rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: and then <s>Rāghava</s> struck the charioteer with eight nārācas.

children.text: bhittvā śarai rathaṃ rāmo rathāśvān samapātayat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, piercing the chariot with arrows, brought down the horses of the chariot.
The night-roaming <s>Makarākṣa</s>, deprived of his chariot, stood on the earth.

children.text: atiṣṭhad vasudhāṃ rakṣaḥ śūlaṃ jagrāha pāṇinā
children.translated_text: Standing on the earth, the rākṣasa took up a spear in his hand,
terrifying to all beings and equal in splendor to the fire at the end of an age.
Brandishing that great blazing spear, the night-roamer,

children.text: sa krodhāt prāhiṇot tasmai rāghavāya mahāhave ||
children.translated_text: in anger, hurled it at that <s>Rāghava</s> in the great battle.
As that blazing spear, loosed from the hand of the son of <s>Khara</s>, came rushing on,

children.text: bāṇaistu tribhir ākāśe śūlaṃ cicheda rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> cut it apart in the sky with three arrows.
Cut into many pieces, that spear adorned with divine gold
was shattered on the ground like a great meteor, struck by <s>Rāma</s>'s arrows.
Seeing that spear destroyed by <s>Rāma</s> of wondrous deeds,
the beings in the sky cried out, "Well done, well done!"

children.text: tad dṛṣṭvā nihataṃ śūlaṃ makarākṣo niśācaraḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that spear destroyed, the night-roaming <s>Makarākṣa</s>

children.text: muṣṭim udyamya kākutsthaṃ tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt ||
children.translated_text: raised his fist against <s>Kākutstha</s> and said, "Stand, stand!"

children.text: sa taṃ dṛṣṭvā patantaṃ vai prahasya raghunandanaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing him rushing upon him, <s>Raghunandana</s> laughed,
and then <s>Rāma</s> fitted the fire-missile to his own bow.

children.text: tenāstreṇa hataṃ rakṣaḥ kākutsthena tadā raṇe
children.translated_text: Struck in battle then by that missile of <s>Kākutstha</s>, the rākṣasa,

children.text: saṃchinnahṛdayaṃ tatra papāta ca mamāra ca ||
children.translated_text: his heart cut open, fell there and died.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā te rākṣasāḥ sarve makarākṣasya pātanam
children.translated_text: Seeing the fall of <s>Makarākṣa</s>, all those rākṣasas,
tormented by <s>Rāma</s>'s arrows, then ran straight back to <s>Laṅkā</s>.
The delighted gods then saw that night-roamer, the son of <s>Khara</s>, slain by the force of the arrows of the son of king <s>Daśaratha</s>,

children.text: dadṛśur atha ca devatāḥ prahṛṣṭā girim iva vajrahataṃ yathā viśīrṇam ||
children.translated_text: as one sees a mountain split apart after being struck by the thunderbolt.
Hearing that <s>Makarākṣa</s> had been slain, victorious-in-battle <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
then enraged, ordered his son <s>Indrajit</s> to battle.
"Slay, hero, those two of great valor, the brothers <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: adṛśyo dṛśyamāno vā sarvathā tvaṃ balādhikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whether invisible or visible, in every way you are superior in strength.
You defeat <s>Indra</s>, whose deeds are unequaled, in battle;

children.text: kiṃ punar mānuṣau dṛṣṭvā na vadhiṣyasi saṃyuge ||
children.translated_text: how much more, seeing two human beings, will you not kill them in battle?"
Thus addressed by the lord of the rākṣasas, accepting his father's word,
<s>Indrajit</s> duly offered oblations to the fire on the sacrificial ground.
While he was offering into the fire there, women wearing red turbans,
rākṣasīs, came there in agitation to where <s>Rāvaṇi</s> was.
Weapons, arrowheads, and, for fuel, vibhītaka wood,

children.text: lohitāni ca vāsāṃsi sruvaṃ kārṣṇāyasaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: red garments also, and likewise a ladle made of black iron,
having strewn these all around the fire on every side with arrowheads,
he grasped the throat of a wholly black goat while it was alive.
When the fire had been kindled by the oblation of cooked offering, smokeless and with great flames,
those signs appeared, showing victory.
With its flame curling to the right and resembling heated gold,
the fire, rising up by itself, accepted that oblation.
Having offered into the fire and then satisfied the gods, dānavas, and rākṣasas,
he mounted the best of chariots, auspicious and able to become invisible.
Together with four horses and sharp arrows,
with a great bow set upon it, he shone on that excellent chariot.
Blazing with his body and furnished with golden equipment,
that chariot was adorned with arrows of crescent and half-moon shape.
The great golden conch-shaped banner of <s>Indrajit</s>,
like a blazing fire and adorned with beryl, came into being.
Protected by that Brahmā-missile, equal to the sun,
<s>Rāvaṇi</s>, of very great strength, became unassailable.
Then <s>Indrajit</s>, victorious in battle, went out from the city,
and, after offering to the fire with rākṣasa mantras, spoke while invisible:

children.text: adya hatvāhave yau tau mithyā pravrajitau vane
children.translated_text: "Today, having slain in battle those two who are falsely gone forth in the forest,
I shall give my father <s>Rāvaṇa</s> victory, supreme in war.

children.text: kṛtvā nirvānarām urvīṃ hatvā rāmaṃ salakṣmaṇam
children.translated_text: Having made the earth empty of <s>Rāma</s>, and having killed <s>Rāma</s> together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
I shall bring about the greatest joy." Having said this, he vanished.
Then, enraged and urged on by <s>Daśagrīva</s>,
that fierce enemy of <s>Indra</s> rushed into battle with sharp bows and nārācas.
He saw the two heroes of great valor, like two three-hooded serpents,
sending forth nets of arrows, heroic, standing among the vānaras.

children.text: imau tāviti saṃcintya sajyaṃ kṛtvā ca kārmukam
children.translated_text: Thinking, "These are those two," and stringing his bow,
he spread out streams of arrows like a rain-bearing cloud.

children.text: sa tu vaihāyasaṃ prāpya saratho rāmalakṣmaṇau
children.translated_text: Reaching the sky with his chariot, he attacked <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
standing beyond the range of their sight, with sharp arrows.
Surrounded by the force of his arrows, the two, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: dhanuṣī saśare kṛtvā divyam astraṃ pracakratuḥ ||
children.translated_text: took up their bows with arrows and began to use a divine missile.
Covering the sky with nets of arrows, the two mighty ones,

children.text: tam astraiḥ surasaṃkāśau naiva pasparśatuḥ śaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: though resembling gods, did not touch him with their arrows or missiles.

children.text: sa hi dhūmāndhakāraṃ ca cakre pracchādayannabhaḥ
children.translated_text: For that splendid one, covering the sky, made smoke and darkness,
and the quarters disappeared, enveloped in mist and gloom.
Neither the twang of his bowstring nor the sound of rim or hoof

children.text: śuśruve caratastasya na ca rūpaṃ prakāśate ||
children.translated_text: was heard as he moved about, nor did his form appear.
In the dense, dark gloom, wondrously, like a rain of arrows,
that mighty-armed one poured down showers of nārāca arrows.

children.text: sa rāmaṃ sūryasaṃkāśaiḥ śarair dattavaro bhṛśam
children.translated_text: The enraged, boon-gifted son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, in battle, pierced <s>Rāma</s> fiercely
on all his limbs with arrows shining like the sun.

children.text: tau hanyamānau nārācair dhārābhir iva parvatau
children.translated_text: As those two tiger-like men were being struck by iron arrows, like mountains by torrents,
they released sharp arrows with golden shafts.
Those bird-like arrows, furnished with heron-feather flights, reached the sky toward <s>Rāvaṇi</s>,
but, cut apart, they fell to the ground, sprinkled with blood.
As the two best of men were oppressed beyond measure by a flood of arrows,

children.text: tān iṣūn patato bhallair anekair nicakartatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: they cut apart those falling shafts with many broad-headed arrows.

children.text: yato hi dadṛśāte tau śarānnipatitāñ śitān
children.translated_text: From whatever direction those two saw sharp arrows falling down,
from that very direction the sons of <s>Daśaratha</s> released excellent missiles.
But <s>Rāvaṇi</s>, a mighty chariot-warrior, ranging through all the quarters in his chariot,

children.text: vivyādha tau dāśarathī laghvastro niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: swift with weapons, pierced the two sons of <s>Daśaratha</s> with sharp arrows.
Those two heroes, excessively pierced by him with well-joined, gold-shafted arrows,
the sons of <s>Daśaratha</s>, became like flowering kiṃśuka trees.

children.text: nāsya veda gatiṃ kaścin na ca rūpaṃ dhanuḥ śarān
children.translated_text: No one knew his course, nor his form, nor his bow or arrows;
nothing at all was perceived, as of the sun when clouds have gathered.
And the vānaras pierced by him, struck down and lifeless,
fell there by the hundreds upon the surface of the earth.
Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, greatly enraged, spoke these words to his brother:
"I shall employ the Brahmā weapon for the destruction of all the rākṣasas."

children.text: tam uvāca tato rāmo lakṣmaṇaṃ śubhalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s> said to that auspiciously marked <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:

children.text: naikasya heto rakṣāṃsi pṛthivyāṃ hantum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: "For the sake of one alone, you ought not to kill the rākṣasas on earth.
One who is not fighting, one who is concealed, one with joined palms, one who has sought refuge,

children.text: palāyantaṃ pramattaṃ vā na tvaṃ hantum ihārhasi ||
children.translated_text: one who is fleeing, or one who is heedless: such a person you ought not to kill here.

children.text: asyaiva tu vadhe yatnaṃ kariṣyāvo mahābala
children.translated_text: Mighty one, we shall make our effort toward killing this one alone,
and we shall command swift missiles, like venomous serpents.

children.text: tam enaṃ māyinaṃ kṣudram antarhitarathaṃ balāt
children.translated_text: When the leaders of the vānara troops see this low, magic-working rākṣasa,
whose chariot is hidden, they will kill him by force.

children.text: yadyeṣa bhūmiṃ viśate divaṃ vā rasātalaṃ vāpi nabhastalaṃ vā
children.translated_text: Whether he enters the earth, or heaven, or even the underworld, or the sky,

children.text: evaṃ nigūḍho 'pi mamāstradagdhaḥ patiṣyate bhūmitale gatāsuḥ ||
children.translated_text: even so concealed, burned by my missile, he will fall lifeless upon the ground."

children.text: ityevam uktvā vacanaṃ mahātmā raghupravīraḥ plavagarṣabhair vṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken such words, the great-souled hero of the <s>Raghus</s>, surrounded by the bull-like vānaras,

children.text: vadhāya raudrasya nṛśaṃsakarmaṇas tadā mahātmā tvaritaṃ nirīkṣate ||
children.translated_text: then swiftly looked about for the killing of that fierce one of cruel deeds.
But when he understood the mind of that great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>,
he withdrew from that battle and then entered the city.
Remembering the slaughter of those forceful rākṣasas,
that hero of great splendor, his eyes reddened by anger, came forth.

children.text: sa paścimena dvāreṇa niryayau rākṣasair vṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Surrounded by rākṣasas, he went out through the western gate,
<s>Indrajit</s>, the mighty descendant of <s>Pulastya</s>, tormentor of the gods.

children.text: indrajit tu tato dṛṣṭvā bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
children.translated_text: Then <s>Indrajit</s>, seeing the brothers <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
the two heroes risen up for battle, produced an illusion at that time.

children.text: indrajit tu rathe sthāpya sītāṃ māyāmayīṃ tadā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Indrajit</s> placed a magically fashioned <s>Sītā</s> on his chariot,
surrounded her with a great force, and made her killing appear.

children.text: mohanārthaṃ tu sarveṣāṃ buddhiṃ kṛtvā sudurmatiḥ
children.translated_text: The wicked-minded one, having formed this intention to bewilder them all,
resolved to kill <s>Sītā</s> and went facing the vānaras.
Seeing him coming out from the city, the forest-dwellers
sprang up enraged, stones in hand, eager to fight.
<s>Hanūmān</s>, the elephant among monkeys, went at their head,
holding up a very great and unassailable peak of a mountain.

children.text: sa dadarśa hatānandāṃ sītām indrajito rathe
children.translated_text: He saw joyless <s>Sītā</s> on <s>Indrajit</s>'s chariot,
wearing a single braid, wretched, her face thin from fasting,
clad in one soiled garment, unwashed, the beloved of <s>Rāghava</s>,
that noble woman with all her limbs smeared with dust and dirt.

children.text: tāṃ nirīkṣya muhūrtaṃ tu maithilīm adhyavasya ca
children.translated_text: Having looked for a moment at that <s>Maithilī</s> and having determined who she was,
<s>Hanūmān</s>, his face clouded with tears, was distressed.

children.text: abravīt tāṃ tu śokārtāṃ nirānandāṃ tapasvinīm
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Sītā</s> standing on the chariot, stricken with grief, joyless, and ascetic in suffering,
under the power of the son of the lord of rākṣasas, he spoke to her.

children.text: kiṃ samarthitam asyeti cintayan sa mahākapiḥ
children.translated_text: Thinking, "What has he contrived?" that great monkey
rushed at <s>Rāvaṇi</s> together with those foremost vānaras.
Seeing that vānara army, <s>Rāvaṇi</s>, overcome with anger,

children.text: kṛtvā vikośaṃ nistriṃśaṃ mūrdhni sītāṃ parāmṛśat ||
children.translated_text: unsheathed his sword and seized <s>Sītā</s> by the head.

children.text: tāṃ striyaṃ paśyatāṃ teṣāṃ tāḍayāmāsa rāvaṇiḥ
children.translated_text: As they looked on, <s>Rāvaṇi</s> struck that woman,

children.text: krośantīṃ rāma rāmeti māyayā yojitāṃ rathe ||
children.translated_text: who cried, "<s>Rāma</s>! <s>Rāma</s>!", placed on the chariot by magic.
Seeing her seized by the hair, <s>Hanūmān</s> was overcome with wretchedness,
and, shedding from his eyes water born of grief, the son of the Wind
spoke harsh words in anger to the son of the lord of rākṣasas:
"Evil-minded one, for your own destruction you lay hold of her hair.

children.text: brahmarṣīṇāṃ kule jāto rākṣasīṃ yonim āśritaḥ
children.translated_text: Born in the lineage of brahmarṣis, yet resorting to a rākṣasa womb,

children.text: dhik tvāṃ pāpasamācāraṃ yasya te matir īdṛśī ||
children.translated_text: shame on you, of sinful conduct, whose intention is such as this!
Cruel, ignoble, ill-conducted, low, whose valor is sinful,

children.text: anāryasyedṛśaṃ karma ghṛṇā te nāsti nirghṛṇa ||
children.translated_text: this is the deed of an ignoble man; you have no pity, pitiless one.
<s>Maithilī</s> has fallen from her home, from her kingdom, and from <s>Rāma</s>'s hand.

children.text: kiṃ tavaiṣāparāddhā hi yad enāṃ hantum icchasi ||
children.translated_text: What offense has she committed against you, that you wish to kill her?

children.text: sītāṃ ca hatvā na ciraṃ jīviṣyasi kathaṃcana
children.translated_text: And after killing <s>Sītā</s>, you will in no way live for long;
by this deed worthy of death, you have indeed come into my hands."

children.text: ye ca strīghātināṃ lokā lokavadhyaiśca kutsitāḥ
children.translated_text: Those worlds that belong to killers of women, and the despised worlds of those who slaughter people,

children.text: iha jīvitam utsṛjya pretya tān pratilapsyase ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned your life here, you will obtain them after death.

children.text: iti bruvāṇo hanumān sāyudhair haribhir vṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Speaking thus, <s>Hanumān</s>, surrounded by armed vānaras,
rushed forward in anger toward the son of the lord of the rākṣasas.
That army of forest-dwellers, attacking with great valor,
he checked with an army of rākṣasas of terrible speed.
Having thrown that vānara army into confusion with a thousand arrows,
<s>Indrajit</s> then addressed <s>Hanūmant</s>, the best of vānaras:
The <s>Vaidehī</s> for whose sake <s>Sugrīva</s>, you, and <s>Rāma</s> have come here,

children.text: tāṃ haniṣyāmi vaidehīm adyaiva tava paśyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall kill her today itself, while you look on.

children.text: imāṃ hatvā tato rāmaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ tvāṃ ca vānara
children.translated_text: After killing her, then <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and you, O vānara,

children.text: sugrīvaṃ ca vadhiṣyāmi taṃ cānāryaṃ vibhīṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Sugrīva</s> too, and that ignoble <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, I shall slay.

children.text: na hantavyāḥ striyaśceti yad bravīṣi plavaṃgama
children.translated_text: As for what you say, 'Women must not be killed,' O leaper,

children.text: pīḍākaram amitrāṇāṃ yat syāt kartavyam eva tat ||
children.translated_text: whatever would bring pain to enemies, that indeed must be done.

children.text: tam evam uktvā rudatīṃ sītāṃ māyāmayīṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to him, then <s>Indrajit</s> himself
struck the weeping, māyā-made <s>Sītā</s> with a sharp-edged sword.
Cut by him along the line of the sacred thread, that ascetic lady,
broad-hipped and lovely to behold, fell to the earth.

children.text: tām indrajitstriyaṃ hatvā hanūmantam uvāca ha
children.translated_text: Having killed that woman, <s>Indrajit</s> said to <s>Hanūmant</s>:

children.text: mayā rāmasya paśyemāṃ kopena ca niṣūditām ||
children.translated_text: Behold this woman of <s>Rāma</s>, struck down by me in anger.

children.text: tataḥ khaḍgena mahatā hatvā tām indrajit svayam
children.translated_text: Then, after killing her himself with his great sword,

children.text: hṛṣṭaḥ sa ratham āsthāya vinanāda mahāsvanam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indrajit</s>, exultant, mounted his chariot and roared with a mighty sound.
The vānaras, standing not far away, heard the sound
of him roaring with gaping mouth, while he occupied that stronghold.

children.text: tathā tu sītāṃ vinihatya durmatiḥ prahṛṣṭacetāḥ sa babhūva rāvaṇiḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus slain <s>Sītā</s>, the evil-minded son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> became joyful in heart;

children.text: taṃ hṛṣṭarūpaṃ samudīkṣya vānarā viṣaṇṇarūpāḥ samabhipradudruvuḥ ||
children.translated_text: seeing him so exultant, the vānaras became downcast and fled away.
Hearing that dreadful roar, equal in sound to <s>Śakra</s>'s thunderbolt,
the bull-like vānaras, looking in every direction, ran away.
Then <s>Hanūmān</s>, son of the wind, spoke to all those
who were downcast in face, miserable, terrified, and fleeing separately:
Why are your faces downcast? Why are you running away, O leaping vānaras?

children.text: tyaktayuddhasamutsāhāḥ śūratvaṃ kva nu vo gatam ||
children.translated_text: You have abandoned your eagerness for battle; where has your heroism gone?
Follow behind me as I go in front into the battle;
for heroes endowed with noble birth, turning back is improper.
Thus addressed by the wise son of the wind, they became greatly enraged
and, joyful in mind, seized mountain peaks and trees.
The bull-like vānaras charged at the rākṣasas with roars,
and, surrounding <s>Hanūmant</s>, followed him in the great battle.

children.text: sa tair vānaramukhyaistu hanūmān sarvato vṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Surrounded on every side by those chief vānaras,
<s>Hanūmān</s>, blazing like fire, burned the enemy army.
That great monkey made slaughter among the rākṣasas,
surrounded by the vānara army, like <s>Yama</s> the ender at the end of time.

children.text: sa tu śokena cāviṣṭaḥ krodhena ca mahākapiḥ
children.translated_text: But the great monkey <s>Hanūmān</s>, possessed by grief and anger,
hurled a great rock at the chariot of <s>Rāvaṇi</s>.

children.text: tām āpatantīṃ dṛṣṭvaiva rathaḥ sārathinā tadā
children.translated_text: As soon as he saw it falling, the chariot, then
yoked with obedient horses, was driven far away by the charioteer.
Not reaching <s>Indrajit</s>, who stood in the chariot with his charioteer,

children.text: viveśa dharaṇīṃ bhittvā sā śilā vyartham udyatā ||
children.translated_text: that rock, raised in vain, split the ground and entered the earth.

children.text: patitāyāṃ śilāyāṃ tu rakṣasāṃ vyathitā camūḥ
children.translated_text: When the rock had fallen, the army of the rākṣasas was shaken;
the forest-dwellers rushed at him by hundreds, roaring.
Those huge-bodied, terribly valiant vānaras lifted up trees
and mountain peaks and hurled them into the midst of their enemies.
The night-roamers, dreadful in form, struck by those mighty vānaras
with trees by the force of their valor, writhed on the battlefield.
Then, seeing his own army oppressed by the vānaras, <s>Indrajit</s>,
angry and with weapon grasped, went forward to face his foes.
Releasing floods of arrows, surrounded by his own army,
the warrior of proven valor killed many tiger-like monkeys.
And with spears, thunderbolt-like missiles, swords, paṭṭasas, spiked clubs, and hammers,
the vānaras too slew his attendants in the battle.
With śāla trees bearing branches and trunks, and with rocks, by his great strength,
<s>Hanūmān</s> made slaughter among the rākṣasas of terrible deeds.

children.text: sa nivārya parānīkam abravīt tān vanaukasaḥ
children.translated_text: Having checked the enemy army, <s>Hanūmān</s> said to those forest-dwellers:

children.text: hanūmān saṃnivartadhvaṃ na naḥ sādhyam idaṃ balam ||
children.translated_text: Turn back; this force is not conquerable by us.
We are struggling, giving up our lives, wishing to do what is dear to <s>Rāma</s>;

children.text: yannimittaṃ hi yudhyāmo hatā sā janakātmajā ||
children.translated_text: but she for whose sake we fight, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, has been killed.

children.text: imam arthaṃ hi vijñāpya rāmaṃ sugrīvam eva ca
children.translated_text: After reporting this matter to <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Sugrīva</s>,

children.text: tau yat pratividhāsyete tat kariṣyāmahe vayam ||
children.translated_text: whatever those two decide, that we shall do.
Having spoken thus, the best of vānaras, restraining all the vānaras,

children.text: śanaiḥ śanair asaṃtrastaḥ sabalaḥ sa nyavartata ||
children.translated_text: slowly and without fear withdrew with his force.

children.text: sa tu prekṣya hanūmantaṃ vrajantaṃ yatra rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: But seeing <s>Hanūmant</s> going to where <s>Rāghava</s> was,
<s>Indrajit</s>, taking his station at <s>Nikumbhilā</s>, offered into the fire.
In the sacrificial ground, according to rule, the fire,
being fed by that rākṣasa, blazed up then, consuming the blood of the oblation.
Satisfied with the blood of the oblation, it appeared enveloped in flames.
That fierce fire rose up like the sun at twilight.

children.text: athendrajid rākṣasabhūtaye tu juhāva havyaṃ vidhinā vidhānavat
children.translated_text: Then <s>Indrajit</s> offered the oblation according to rule and proper ordinance, for the welfare of the rākṣasas.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā vyatiṣṭhanta ca rākṣasāste mahāsamūheṣu nayānayajñāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing it, those rākṣasas, skilled in policy and impolicy, took their stations in great companies.
And <s>Rāghava</s>, hearing that vast battle-roar
of the rākṣasas and forest-dwellers, spoke to <s>Jāmbavant</s>:

children.text: saumya nūnaṃ hanumatā kṛtaṃ karma suduṣkaram
children.translated_text: "Gentle one, surely a very difficult deed has been done by <s>Hanumat</s>;

children.text: śrūyate hi yathā bhīmaḥ sumahān āyudhasvanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for a terrifying and very great clash of weapons is heard.
Therefore go quickly, lord of bears, surrounded by your own force,
and give aid to that best of vānaras as he fights."
The king of bears said, "So be it," and, surrounded by his own army,
came to the western gate, where the vānara <s>Hanumān</s> was.
Then on the road the lord of bears saw <s>Hanumān</s> approaching,
surrounded by vānaras who had fought in battle and were breathing hard.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā pathi hanūmāṃśca tad ṛkṣabalam udyatam
children.translated_text: And seeing on the road that bear-force drawn up,
dark like a blue cloud and terrible, <s>Hanumān</s> checked it and turned back.
With that army of monkeys, the greatly renowned one

children.text: śīghram āgamya rāmāya duḥkhito vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: quickly came near <s>Rāma</s> and, distressed, spoke these words:

children.text: samare yudhyamānānām asmākaṃ prekṣatāṃ ca saḥ
children.translated_text: "While we were fighting in the battle, and while we were watching,
<s>Indrajit</s>, son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, killed the weeping <s>Sītā</s>.
My mind was shaken when I saw her, and I was despondent, subduer of foes;

children.text: tad ahaṃ bhavato vṛttaṃ vijñāpayitum āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore I have come to inform you of what happened."
Hearing those words of his, <s>Rāghava</s>, overcome by grief,

children.text: nipapāta tadā bhūmau chinnamūla iva drumaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then fell to the ground like a tree whose root has been cut.

children.text: taṃ bhūmau devasaṃkāśaṃ patitaṃ dṛśya rāghavam
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Rāghava</s>, godlike, fallen on the ground,
the best of the monkeys leapt up and rushed to him from every side.
They sprinkled him with waters fragrant with lotuses and blue lotuses,
as he burned unbearably, like a sudden fire risen up.
Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, deeply distressed, embraced with both arms
<s>Rāma</s>, who was unwell, and spoke words joined with reasoning and meaning:
"You stand on the auspicious path, noble one, conqueror of the senses;

children.text: anarthebhyo na śaknoti trātuṃ dharmo nirarthakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: yet useless <s>dharma</s> cannot protect you from misfortunes.

children.text: bhūtānāṃ sthāvarāṇāṃ ca jaṅgamānāṃ ca darśanam
children.translated_text: The appearance of beings, both stationary and moving,

children.text: yathāsti na tathā dharmastena nāstīti me matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: exists as it is; <s>dharma</s> is not so, and therefore I think it does not exist.

children.text: yathaiva sthāvaraṃ vyaktaṃ jaṅgamaṃ ca tathāvidham
children.translated_text: Just as what is stationary is manifest, and what moves is manifest in the same way,
this matter is not fitting in that way; one like you should not fall into calamity.

children.text: yadyadharmo bhaved bhūto rāvaṇo narakaṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: If <s>adharma</s> were real, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> would go to hell,
and you, joined with <s>dharma</s>, would not meet such a disaster.

children.text: tasya ca vyasanābhāvād vyasanaṃ ca gate tvayi
children.translated_text: From the absence of disaster for him, and from disaster having come to you,
one would recognize <s>dharma</s> by <s>dharma</s>, and <s>adharma</s> also by <s>adharma</s>.
If people delighting in <s>adharma</s> were joined with <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: dharmeṇa caratāṃ dharmastathā caiṣāṃ phalaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: then <s>dharma</s> and its fruit would belong to those who practice <s>dharma</s>.
Since prosperity increases for those in whom <s>adharma</s> is established,
and those whose character is <s>dharma</s> are tormented, therefore these two are useless.
If evil-doers are killed by <s>adharma</s>, <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: vadhakarmahato dharmaḥ sa hataḥ kaṃ vadhiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: then <s>dharma</s>, struck down by the act of killing, is itself destroyed; whom will it kill?

children.text: athavā vihitenāyaṃ hanyate hanti vā param
children.translated_text: Or else, if this man is killed by what is ordained, or kills another,

children.text: vidhir ālipyate tena na sa pāpena karmaṇā ||
children.translated_text: then fate is implicated by that, not he by the sinful act.
By something unseen, without visible remedy, unmanifest, unreal or real,
how can the highest goal be attained through <s>dharma</s>, tormentor of enemies?

children.text: yadi sat syāt satāṃ mukhya nāsat syāt tava kiṃcana
children.translated_text: If the real truly existed, best of the good, there would be nothing unreal for you;
since such a thing has befallen you, therefore the real is not established.
Or else <s>dharma</s> is weak and impotent, and follows strength;

children.text: durbalo hṛtamaryādo na sevya iti me matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: being weak and stripped of its bounds, it is not to be served: this is my view.

children.text: balasya yadi ced dharmo guṇabhūtaḥ parākrame
children.translated_text: But if <s>dharma</s> is a subordinate quality of strength in heroic power,

children.text: dharmam utsṛjya vartasva yathā dharme tathā bale ||
children.translated_text: then abandon <s>dharma</s> and conduct yourself toward strength just as you did toward <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: atha cet satyavacanaṃ dharmaḥ kila paraṃtapa
children.translated_text: And if truth-speaking is indeed <s>dharma</s>, scorcher of foes,
why did you not bind your father, who spoke falsely and was unmerciful toward you?

children.text: yadi dharmo bhaved bhūta adharmo vā paraṃtapa
children.translated_text: If <s>dharma</s> or <s>adharma</s> were real, scorcher of foes,

children.text: na sma hatvā muniṃ vajrī kuryād ijyāṃ śatakratuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vajrin</s>, <s>Śatakratu</s>, would not have performed sacrifice after killing a sage.
<s>Dharma</s> resting on <s>adharma</s> brings destruction, <s>Rāghava</s>;

children.text: sarvam etad yathākāmaṃ kākutstha kurute naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: a man does all this, <s>Kākutstha</s>, according to his desire.

children.text: mama cedaṃ mataṃ tāta dharmo 'yam iti rāghava
children.translated_text: And this is my opinion, dear one, <s>Rāghava</s>: if this is <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: dharmamūlaṃ tvayā chinnaṃ rājyam utsṛjatā tadā ||
children.translated_text: then its root, the kingdom, was cut off by you when you abandoned it then.
For from goods that have grown and increased on every side
all actions proceed, as rivers flow from mountains.
For a man of little energy who is separated from <s>artha</s>,

children.text: vyucchidyante kriyāḥ sarvā grīṣme kusarito yathā ||
children.translated_text: all undertakings are cut off, like small streams in summer.
So this man, abandoning <s>artha</s>, desiring pleasure and set on comfort,

children.text: pāpam ārabhate kartuṃ tathā doṣaḥ pravartate ||
children.translated_text: begins to commit evil; thus fault comes into being.
He who has <s>artha</s> has friends; he who has <s>artha</s> has kinsmen.

children.text: yasyārthāḥ sa pumāṃl loke yasyārthāḥ sa ca paṇḍitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He who has <s>artha</s> is a man in the world; he who has <s>artha</s> is learned.

children.text: yasyārthāḥ sa ca vikrānto yasyārthāḥ sa ca buddhimān
children.translated_text: He who has <s>artha</s> is valiant; he who has <s>artha</s> is intelligent.

children.text: yasyārthāḥ sa mahābhāgo yasyārthāḥ sa mahāguṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He who has <s>artha</s> is greatly fortunate; he who has <s>artha</s> possesses great virtues."
These faults in the abandonment of <s>artha</s> (material power) have been fully declared by me,

children.text: rājyam utsṛjatā vīra yena buddhistvayā kṛtā ||
children.translated_text: O hero, when you gave up the kingdom according to the judgment you had made.
For one who has wealth, <s>dharma</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>artha</s> all turn favorably;
but for one without wealth, though he desires wealth and searches for it, the goal cannot be achieved.

children.text: harṣaḥ kāmaśca darpaśca dharmaḥ krodhaḥ śamo damaḥ
children.translated_text: Joy, desire, pride, <s>dharma</s>, anger, tranquility, and self-restraint,
all these arise from <s>artha</s>, O lord of men.
Those aims, by which this world is not lost for men who live in <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: te 'rthāstvayi na dṛśyante durdineṣu yathā grahāḥ ||
children.translated_text: are not seen in you, as planets are not seen on cloudy days.

children.text: tvayi pravrajite vīra gurośca vacane sthite
children.translated_text: When you, O hero, went into exile and stood firm in your father's command,
your wife, dearer to you than life, was carried off by a rākṣasa.

children.text: tad adya vipulaṃ vīra duḥkham indrajitā kṛtam
children.translated_text: Therefore today, O hero, this great sorrow caused by <s>Indrajit</s>
I shall remove by action; therefore rise, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: ayam anagha tavoditaḥ priyārthaṃ janakasutānidhanaṃ nirīkṣya ruṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: O blameless one, angry on seeing the reported killing of the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, and acting for your dear purpose,

children.text: sahayagajarathāṃ sarākṣasendrāṃ bhṛśam iṣubhir vinipātayāmi laṅkām ||
children.translated_text: I shall utterly cast down <s>Laṅkā</s>, together with its horses, elephants, chariots, and lord of the rākṣasas, with my arrows.
While <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, loving his brother, was thus consoling <s>Rāma</s>,
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, having stationed the troops in their proper places, came there.
He was surrounded by four brave ministers carrying various weapons,
dark like heaps of blue-black collyrium, as a lord of a herd is surrounded by elephants.
Approaching the great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>, languishing in grief,
he saw the vānaras too, their eyes confused and full of tears.
And he saw the great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>, joy of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> line,
fallen into stupor and resting in <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s lap.
Seeing <s>Rāma</s> ashamed and scorched by grief, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,

children.text: antarduḥkhena dīnātmā kim etad iti so 'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: miserable at heart with inner pain, said, "What is this?"
Looking at <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>'s face, at <s>Sugrīva</s>, and at those vānaras,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, overwhelmed with tears, spoke these words:

children.text: hatām indrajitā sītām iha śrutvaiva rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing here that <s>Sītā</s> had been slain by <s>Indrajit</s>, <s>Rāghava</s>,
from the words of <s>Hanūmat</s>, gentle one, then fell into stupor.
But <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> checked <s>Saumitri</s> as he was speaking,

children.text: puṣkalārtham idaṃ vākyaṃ visaṃjñaṃ rāmam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: and addressed this meaningful speech to the unconscious <s>Rāma</s>:
O lord of men, what was reported to you by <s>Hanūmat</s> in his distressed state,

children.text: tad ayuktam ahaṃ manye sāgarasyeva śoṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: I think that is impossible, like the drying up of the ocean.
But I know the intention of wicked <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: sītāṃ prati mahābāho na ca ghātaṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: and regarding <s>Sītā</s>, O mighty-armed one, he will not kill her.
Though I, wishing his welfare, begged him many times,

children.text: vaidehīm utsṛjasveti na ca tat kṛtavān vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: saying, "Release <s>Vaidehī</s>," he did not carry out that word.

children.text: naiva sāmnā na bhedena na dānena kuto yudhā
children.translated_text: Not by conciliation, not by division, not by gifts, and how much less by war,

children.text: sā draṣṭum api śakyeta naiva cānyena kenacit ||
children.translated_text: could she even be seen; nor could she be seen by anyone else.
Having deluded the vānaras, that rākṣasa has gone back

children.text: caityaṃ nikumbhilāṃ nāma yatra homaṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: to the sanctuary called <s>Nikumbhilā</s>, where he will perform a fire-offering.

children.text: hutavān upayāto hi devair api savāsavaiḥ
children.translated_text: For when he has offered the oblation and set out, this son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>
becomes hard to assail in battle even for the gods together with <s>Vāsava</s>.

children.text: tena mohayatā nūnam eṣā māyā prayojitā
children.translated_text: Surely this illusion was employed by him while he was deceiving them,
seeking to obstruct, dear one, the valor of the vānaras.
Let us go there with the army before that rite is completed.
Cast off this false distress that has come upon you, tiger among men;

children.text: sīdate hi balaṃ sarvaṃ dṛṣṭvā tvāṃ śokakarśitam ||
children.translated_text: for the whole army sinks when it sees you wasted by grief.
Remain here with a steady heart, raised up by courage,
and send <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> with us, along with the leaders of the army.

children.text: eṣa taṃ naraśārdūlo rāvaṇiṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
children.translated_text: This tiger among men will force <s>Rāvaṇi</s> to abandon that rite

children.text: tyājayiṣyati tat karma tato vadhyo bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: with sharp arrows; then he will become one who can be killed.
These keen, sharp arrows of his, feather-winged and swift,
dreadful like birds of prey, will drink blood.
Therefore command the auspicious-marked <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, O mighty-armed one,
for the destruction of the rākṣasa, as the wielder of the thunderbolt commands the thunderbolt.

children.text: manujavara na kālaviprakarṣo ripunidhanaṃ prati yat kṣamo 'dya kartum
children.translated_text: Best of men, there should be no delay in regard to the enemy's destruction, when it can be done today.

children.text: tvam atisṛja ripor vadhāya vāṇīm asurapuronmathane yathā mahendraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Send forth your command for the foe's death, as great <s>Indra</s> did for the overthrow of the asura cities.

children.text: samāptakarmā hi sa rākṣasendro bhavatyadṛśyaḥ samare surāsuraiḥ
children.translated_text: For when that lord of rākṣasas has completed his rite, he becomes invisible in battle to gods and asuras;

children.text: yuyutsatā tena samāptakarmaṇā bhavet surāṇām api saṃśayo mahān ||
children.translated_text: and if he fights after completing that rite, even the gods would face great uncertainty.
Hearing that speech of his, <s>Rāghava</s>, wasted by grief,

children.text: nopadhārayate vyaktaṃ yad uktaṃ tena rakṣasā ||
children.translated_text: did not clearly grasp what had been said by that rākṣasa.
Then, taking hold of courage, <s>Rāma</s>, conqueror of enemy cities,
spoke to <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> as he sat nearby, in the presence of the vānaras:

children.text: nairṛtādhipate vākyaṃ yad uktaṃ te vibhīṣaṇa
children.translated_text: Lord of the night-roamers, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, the speech that you have spoken,

children.text: bhūyastacchrotum icchāmi brūhi yat te vivakṣitam ||
children.translated_text: I wish to hear it again; tell me what you intend to say.
Hearing <s>Rāghava</s>'s words, skilled in speech as he was,

children.text: yat tat punar idaṃ vākyaṃ babhāṣe sa vibhīṣaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> then spoke these words again:
O mighty-armed hero, the stationing of the troops as ordered by you
has been carried out just so, immediately after your command.
All those forces have been divided on every side,
and the troop-leaders have been placed properly, each in his own division.
But I have something further to inform you of; hear it, O greatly renowned one.
When you are tormented without cause, our hearts are tormented too.

children.text: tyaja rājann imaṃ śokaṃ mithyā saṃtāpam āgatam
children.translated_text: Abandon this grief, O king, this false distress that has come upon you.
Therefore let this worry, which increases the enemy's joy, be abandoned.
Make an effort, hero; take up glad confidence.

children.text: prāptavyā yadi te sītā hantavyāśca niśācarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: If <s>Sītā</s> is to be obtained by you, the night-roamers must be killed.

children.text: raghunandana vakṣyāmi śrūyatāṃ me hitaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>, I shall speak; listen to my beneficial word.

children.text: sādhvayaṃ yātu saumitrir balena mahatā vṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Let this <s>Saumitri</s> go, surrounded by a great force,
and, reaching <s>Nikumbhilā</s>, let him kill <s>Rāvaṇi</s> in battle.
With arrows released from the circle of his bow, like the poison of venomous serpents,
the great archer, conqueror in combat, should kill <s>Rāvaṇi</s>.
Through austerity and by the boon of the Self-born, that hero
obtained the <s>Brahmaśiras</s> weapon and horses that go wherever he wishes.

children.text: nikumbhilām asaṃprāptam ahutāgniṃ ca yo ripuḥ
children.translated_text: If an enemy should strike you, O foe of <s>Indra</s>, before you have reached <s>Nikumbhilā</s>

children.text: tvām ātatāyinaṃ hanyād indraśatro sa te vadhaḥ
children.translated_text: and before the fire-oblation has been offered, that attacker would be your death.
Thus, O king, the death of that wise one himself has been ordained.
O <s>Rāma</s>, assign that mighty one to the killing of <s>Indrajit</s>.

children.text: hate tasmin hataṃ viddhi rāvaṇaṃ sasuhṛjjanam ||
children.translated_text: When he is killed, know <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, together with his friends and followers, to be killed.
Having heard <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>'s words, <s>Rāma</s> then spoke this sentence:
I know the <s>māyā</s> of that terrible one, whose valor is true.

children.text: sa hi brahmāstravit prājño mahāmāyo mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: For he knows the <s>Brahmāstra</s>, is wise, powerful in <s>māyā</s>, and very mighty.
In battle he renders even the gods, together with <s>Varuṇa</s>, unconscious.
When he moves through the sky in his chariot, O greatly famous hero,
his course is not known, like that of the sun in a mass of clouds.
But <s>Rāghava</s>, knowing the evil-minded enemy's power of <s>māyā</s>,
spoke these words to glorious <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:

children.text: yad vānarendrasya balaṃ tena sarveṇa saṃvṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Surrounded by all the force of the lord of the monkeys,
and with the troop-leaders headed by <s>Hanūmat</s>, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
surrounded by the army together with <s>Jāmbavān</s>, lord of the bears,
kill that son of the rākṣasa, skilled in the power of <s>māyā</s>.

children.text: ayaṃ tvāṃ sacivaiḥ sārdhaṃ mahātmā rajanīcaraḥ
children.translated_text: This noble night-roamer, together with his ministers,
knowing that place, will follow behind you.
Hearing <s>Rāghava</s>'s word, mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, with <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,
took up an excellent bow, one suited to his fearsome valor.

children.text: saṃnaddhaḥ kavacī khaḍgī sa śarī hemacāpadhṛk
children.translated_text: Fastened in armor, bearing a sword and arrows, and holding a golden bow,
<s>Saumitri</s>, delighted, touched <s>Rāma</s>'s feet and said:
Today the arrows launched from my bow, after piercing <s>Rāvaṇi</s>,
will descend upon <s>Laṅkā</s> like swans upon a lotus pond.

children.text: adyaiva tasya raudrasya śarīraṃ māmakāḥ śarāḥ
children.translated_text: Today my arrows will scatter the body of that terrible one,
loosed from the string of my great bow, after killing him.

children.text: sa evam uktvā dyutimān vacanaṃ bhrātur agrataḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken that shining speech before his brother,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, eager for <s>Rāvaṇi</s>'s death, went swiftly.

children.text: so 'bhivādya guroḥ pādau kṛtvā cāpi pradakṣiṇam
children.translated_text: Having bowed to the feet of his elder and also circumambulated him,
he went to <s>Nikumbhilā</s>, the sanctuary guarded by <s>Rāvaṇi</s>.
The glorious prince, accompanied by <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, for whom his brother had performed auspicious rites, went swiftly.
<s>Hanūmān</s>, surrounded by many thousands of monkeys,
and <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> with his ministers then followed <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Surrounded on every side by a great and swift monkey army,
he saw on the road the force of the bear-king stationed there.

children.text: sa gatvā dūram adhvānaṃ saumitrir mitranandanaḥ
children.translated_text: Having gone a long way, <s>Saumitri</s>, delighter of his friends,
saw from afar the army of the lord of rākṣasas drawn up in formation.
Having reached that enemy joined to <s>māyā</s>, bow in hand, O subduer of foes,
he stood, according to the ordinance of <s>Brahmā</s>, to conquer, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>.

children.text: vividham amalaśastrabhāsvaraṃ tad dhvajagahanaṃ vipulaṃ mahārathaiśca
children.translated_text: That enemy force was varied, gleaming with spotless weapons, dense with standards, and vast with great charioteers;

children.text: pratibhayatamam aprameyavegaṃ timiram iva dviṣatāṃ balaṃ viveśa ||
children.translated_text: he entered it, most terrifying and of immeasurable speed, like darkness itself.
Then, while he was in that situation, the younger brother of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>
spoke to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> a word harmful to the foes and effective for the aim.
Strive, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, to break this great army.
When it is broken here, the son of the lord of rākṣasas will become visible.

children.text: sa tvam indrāśaniprakhyaiḥ śarair avakiran parān
children.translated_text: Therefore, scattering the enemies with arrows like <s>Indra</s>'s thunderbolt,

children.text: abhidravāśu yāvad vai naitat karma samāpyate ||
children.translated_text: rush quickly, before this rite is completed.
Kill, hero, the evil-minded, <s>māyā</s>-devoted, unrighteous one,
<s>Rāvaṇi</s>, cruel in deed and a source of fear to all the worlds.
Hearing <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>'s words, auspicious-marked <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>
poured showers of arrows against the son of the lord of rākṣasas.
The bears and the branch-ranging monkeys, fighting with trees and mountain peaks,
rushed together against that army standing in formation.
The rākṣasas, with sharpened arrows, swords, spears, and lances,
advanced with weapons raised, desiring to kill the monkey army.
A tumultuous battle arose between the monkeys and the rākṣasas,

children.text: śabdena mahatā laṅkāṃ nādayan vai samantataḥ ||
children.translated_text: making all <s>Laṅkā</s> resound with a great noise.
With weapons of many forms, with sharp arrows, and with trees
and dreadful mountain peaks raised up, the sky was covered.
Those rākṣasas, with misshapen faces and arms,
plunging their weapons into the monkeys, created very great terror.
Likewise, with whole trees and with mountain peaks, the monkeys
struck and slew the foremost rākṣasas in battle.
and by the chief bears and monkeys, great-bodied and very mighty,
Great fear arose among the rākṣasas as they were being slain.

children.text: svam anīkaṃ viṣaṇṇaṃ tu śrutvā śatrubhir arditam
children.translated_text: But when the hard-to-subdue one heard that his own army was despondent and pressed by enemies,
he rose up while that rite remained unperformed.
Emerging from the darkness of the trees, that son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> became enraged,

children.text: āruroha rathaṃ sajjaṃ pūrvayuktaṃ sa rākṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the rākṣasa mounted his ready chariot, already yoked before.
With a terrible bow and arrows, resembling a mass of black collyrium,
cruel, with red mouth and eyes, he shone like Death, the ender.

children.text: dṛṣṭvaiva tu rathasthaṃ taṃ paryavartata tad balam
children.translated_text: As soon as that force saw him standing on the chariot, it turned back,
the army of rākṣasas of fearful speed, eager to fight with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: tasmin kāle tu hanumān udyamya sudurāsadam
children.translated_text: At that time <s>Hanumān</s>, subduer of foes, lifted up a very hard-to-resist
great tree, while he himself was like a mountain.

children.text: sa rākṣasānāṃ tat sainyaṃ kālāgnir iva nirdahan
children.translated_text: Burning down that army of rākṣasas like the fire at the end of time,

children.text: cakāra bahubhir vṛkṣair niḥsaṃjñaṃ yudhi vānaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: the monkey made it senseless in battle with many trees.
Seeing the son of the Wind destroying them with force,
thousands of rākṣasas showered weapons upon <s>Hanūmant</s>.
Those who held sharp tridents attacked with tridents, and sword-bearers with swords;
those with spears in hand attacked with spears, and those armed with paṭṭasas with paṭṭasas.
With iron bars, with clubs, and with handsome javelins,
and by the hundred with śataghnīs and with iron hammers,
with dreadful axes and with bhiṇḍipālas, the rākṣasas attacked,
and with fists swift as thunderbolts and palms like lightning-strikes.
Coming upon the one who was like a mountain, they struck him on every side,

children.text: teṣām api ca saṃkruddhaścakāra kadanaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: but, enraged, he made a great slaughter of them as well.
<s>Indrajit</s> saw the best of monkeys, like an immovable mountain,
the son of the Wind, slayer of foes, cutting down his enemies.

children.text: sa sārathim uvācedaṃ yāhi yatraiṣa vānaraḥ
children.translated_text: He said this to his charioteer: 'Go where this monkey is.

children.text: kṣayam eva hi naḥ kuryād rākṣasānām upekṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If ignored, he would surely bring about the destruction of us rākṣasas.'

children.text: ityuktaḥ sārathistena yayau yatra sa mārutiḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by him, the charioteer went where <s>Māruti</s> was,
carrying <s>Indrajit</s>, supremely hard to withstand, standing in the chariot.
Approaching, that hard-to-subdue rākṣasa, with arrows, swords, paṭṭasas, blades, and axes,
showered them upon the monkey's head.

children.text: tāni śastrāṇi ghorāṇi pratigṛhya sa mārutiḥ
children.translated_text: Receiving those dreadful weapons, <s>Māruti</s>,

children.text: roṣeṇa mahatāviṣṭo vākyaṃ cedam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: filled with great anger, then spoke these words:
'Fight, if you are a hero, evil-minded son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Having met the son of the Wind, you will not go back alive.

children.text: bāhubhyāṃ samprayudhyasva yadi me dvandvam āhave
children.translated_text: Fight with your arms, if you seek a duel with me in battle.

children.text: vegaṃ sahasva durbuddhe tatastvaṃ rakṣasāṃ varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Endure my speed, foolish one; then you will be the best of rākṣasas.'
As the son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, bow raised, wished to kill <s>Hanūmant</s>,
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> pointed him out to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
'He who conquered <s>Vāsava</s>, born from <s>Rāvaṇa</s> himself,

children.text: sa eṣa ratham āsthāya hanūmantaṃ jighāṃsati ||
children.translated_text: this is he, mounted on a chariot, wishing to kill <s>Hanūmant</s>.
With incomparable arrows that tear enemies apart,
dreadful arrows that end life, kill <s>Rāvaṇi</s>, O <s>Saumitri</s>.'
Thus addressed then by great-souled <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, terror of enemies,

children.text: dadarśa taṃ parvatasaṃnikāśaṃ rathasthitaṃ bhīmabalaṃ durāsadam ||
children.translated_text: he saw him, mountain-like, standing in his chariot, of dreadful strength and hard to approach.

children.text: evam uktvā tu saumitriṃ jātaharṣo vibhīṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken to <s>Saumitri</s>, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, filled with joy,
took the bow-armed prince and went swiftly.

children.text: avidūraṃ tato gatvā praviśya ca mahad vanam
children.translated_text: After going no great distance and entering a great forest,
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> showed that rite to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
A banyan, dark as a blue rain-cloud and terrible to behold,
was pointed out to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> by the radiant brother of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
'Here the powerful son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> presents an offering to the beings,
and only afterward turns toward battle.
Then the rākṣasa becomes invisible to all beings,

children.text: nihanti samare śatrūn badhnāti ca śarottamaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: kills enemies in battle, and binds them with the finest arrows.
Before the mighty son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> enters the banyan,
destroy him with sharp arrows, together with his chariot, horses, and charioteer.'
Saying, 'So be it,' the greatly radiant <s>Saumitri</s>, delighter of his friends,
stood there, twanging his splendid bow.
Then the powerful son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, on a fire-colored chariot,
<s>Indrajit</s>, armored, sword in hand, and bearing his banner, appeared.
The greatly radiant one addressed the undefeated <s>Paulastya</s>:

children.text: samāhvaye tvāṃ samare samyag yuddhaṃ prayaccha me ||
children.translated_text: 'I challenge you in battle. Grant me a proper fight.'
Thus addressed, the greatly radiant and spirited son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: abravīt paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ tatra dṛṣṭvā vibhīṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: seeing <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> there, spoke harsh words:

children.text: iha tvaṃ jātasaṃvṛddhaḥ sākṣād bhrātā pitur mama
children.translated_text: 'Here you were born and raised, the direct brother of my father.

children.text: kathaṃ druhyasi putrasya pitṛvyo mama rākṣasa ||
children.translated_text: How do you betray his son, my paternal uncle, rākṣasa?

children.text: na jñātitvaṃ na sauhārdaṃ na jātistava durmate
children.translated_text: Neither kinship, nor friendship, nor birth has authority for you, evil-minded one,

children.text: pramāṇaṃ na ca sodaryaṃ na dharmo dharmadūṣaṇa ||
children.translated_text: nor common blood, nor <s>dharma</s>, corrupter of <s>dharma</s>.
You are pitiable, foolish one, and blameworthy before good people,
since you have abandoned your own people and come into service under another.

children.text: naitacchithilayā buddhyā tvaṃ vetsi mahad antaram
children.translated_text: With this feeble understanding you do not perceive the great difference:

children.text: kva ca svajanasaṃvāsaḥ kva ca nīcaparāśrayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: where is life among one's own people, and where is base dependence on another?

children.text: guṇavān vā parajanaḥ svajano nirguṇo 'pi vā
children.translated_text: Whether an outsider is virtuous, or one's own man is without virtue,

children.text: nirguṇaḥ svajanaḥ śreyān yaḥ paraḥ para eva saḥ ||
children.translated_text: one's own man, even without virtue, is better; one who is other remains only other.'
And this heartlessness of yours is of such a kind, night-roaming one,
that harsh speech toward your own kin is possible for you, O younger brother of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Thus addressed by his brother's son, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> replied:

children.text: ajānann iva macchīlaṃ kiṃ rākṣasa vikatthase ||
children.translated_text: "O rākṣasa, why do you boast as though you did not know my character?
Unworthy son of the lord of rākṣasas, abandon harshness out of respect.
Although I was born in a family of rākṣasas whose deeds are cruel,

children.text: guṇo 'yaṃ prathamo nṝṇāṃ tanme śīlam arākṣasam ||
children.translated_text: this is the foremost virtue of men; that character of mine is not rākṣasa-like.

children.text: na rame dāruṇenāhaṃ na cādharmeṇa vai rame
children.translated_text: I do not delight in cruelty, nor indeed do I delight in <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness).
How should a brother not reject a brother whose nature is perverse?
Taking the property of others, touching the wives of others,

children.text: suhṛdām atiśaṅkā ca trayo doṣāḥ kṣayāvahāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and excessive suspicion of friends: these three faults bring destruction.
The terrible killing of great seers, conflict with all the gods,
pride, anger, enmity, and opposition:
these faults of my brother, destroyers of life and sovereignty,
covered over his virtues like rainclouds covering mountains.

children.text: doṣair etaiḥ parityakto mayā bhrātā pitā tava
children.translated_text: Because of these faults, my brother, your father, was abandoned by me.

children.text: neyam asti purī laṅkā na ca tvaṃ na ca te pitā ||
children.translated_text: For me there is no city <s>Laṅkā</s>, nor you, nor your father.
You are arrogant, childish, and ill-disciplined, O rākṣasa.

children.text: baddhastvaṃ kālapāśena brūhi māṃ yad yad icchasi ||
children.translated_text: You are bound by the noose of Time; say to me whatever you wish.

children.text: adya te vyasanaṃ prāptaṃ kim iha tvaṃ tu vakṣyasi
children.translated_text: Today ruin has reached you. What will you say here?

children.text: praveṣṭuṃ na tvayā śakyo nyagrodho rākṣasādhama ||
children.translated_text: You will not be able to enter the banyan tree, vilest of rākṣasas.

children.text: dharṣayitvā tu kākutsthau na śakyaṃ jīvituṃ tvayā
children.translated_text: Having attacked the two <s>Kākutsthas</s>, you cannot live.
Fight in battle with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the prince.
When slain, you will accomplish the task of the gods in <s>Yama</s>'s abode.
Show forth your own strength raised for battle; make full expenditure of every weapon and arrow.

children.text: na lakṣmaṇasyaitya hi bāṇagocaraṃ tvam adya jīvan sabalo gamiṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: For once you have come into the range of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s arrows, you will not today go away alive with your army."
Hearing the words of <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s son, overcome by anger,
spoke a harsh utterance and sprang up swiftly.
With weapon and sword raised, standing on his ornamented chariot,
great and yoked with black horses, he stood like Death at the end of time.
Lifting up a great, broad, swift, and firm bow,
and grasping that dreadful bow and arrows that destroy enemies,
he said, fully roused, to <s>Saumitri</s> together with <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,
and to those tiger-like monkeys: "Behold my valor.
Today the hard-to-withstand shower of arrows released from my bow,
set loose in the sky like rain, you will have to ward off in battle.
Today my arrows, issued from my great bow,
will scatter your limbs as fire scatters a heap of cotton.
Pierced by sharp shafts, and by tridents, javelins, spears, and lances,

children.text: adya vo gamayiṣyāmi sarvān eva yamakṣayam ||
children.translated_text: today I will send all of you to <s>Yama</s>'s abode.
When I, swift-handed in battle, hurl showers of arrows,
roaring like a cloud, who will stand before me?"
Hearing then that roar of the lord of rākṣasas,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, fearless in face and angry, said to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s son:

children.text: uktaśca durgamaḥ pāraḥ kāryāṇāṃ rākṣasa tvayā
children.translated_text: "The far shore of undertakings, O rākṣasa, has been called hard to reach by you;

children.text: kāryāṇāṃ karmaṇā pāraṃ yo gacchati sa buddhimān ||
children.translated_text: but the wise man is he who reaches the far shore of undertakings by action.

children.text: sa tvam arthasya hīnārtho duravāpasya kenacit
children.translated_text: Yet you, empty of the very purpose that is hard for anyone to attain,
think, after uttering words, 'I have accomplished my aim,' O fool.
That conduct which you practiced then in battle while hidden from sight
is a path practiced by thieves; it is not one followed by heroes.

children.text: yathā bāṇapathaṃ prāpya sthito 'haṃ tava rākṣasa
children.translated_text: Since I stand here, O rākṣasa, having reached the path of your arrows,

children.text: darśayasvādya tat tejo vācā tvaṃ kiṃ vikatthase ||
children.translated_text: show that energy of yours today. Why do you boast with words?"

children.text: evam ukto dhanur bhīmaṃ parāmṛśya mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, the mighty one grasped his dreadful bow,
and <s>Indrajit</s>, conqueror in battle, released sharpened arrows.
Those arrows, discharged with great speed and like serpent poison,

children.text: samprāpya lakṣmaṇaṃ petuḥ śvasanta iva pannagāḥ ||
children.translated_text: reached <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and fell upon him like hissing serpents.
With arrows of exceedingly great speed, the swift son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
<s>Indrajit</s>, pierced handsome <s>Saumitri</s> in battle.
His limbs deeply pierced by arrows and drenched with blood,

children.text: śuśubhe lakṣmaṇaḥ śrīmān vidhūma iva pāvakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the glorious <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> shone like a smokeless fire.
Then <s>Indrajit</s>, seeing and recognizing his own deed,
roared a very great roar and spoke these words:
"These feathered arrows with sharp edges, loosed from my bow,
will take your life today, <s>Saumitri</s>, as bringers of life's end.
Today, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, let packs of jackals and flocks of hawks,

children.text: gṛdhrāśca nipatantu tvāṃ gatāsuṃ nihataṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: and vultures, descend upon you, lifeless and slain by me.
That mere kṣatriya by birth, ever ignoble <s>Rāma</s>, of utterly evil mind,

children.text: bhaktaṃ bhrātaram adyaiva tvāṃ drakṣyati mayā hatam ||
children.translated_text: will see you, his devoted brother, killed by me this very day.
With your armor cut apart and your bow cast away on the ground,

children.text: hṛtottamāṅgaṃ saumitre tvām adya nihataṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: your noble head torn off, <s>Saumitri</s>, you will today lie slain by me."
To <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s son, who was speaking thus, enraged and harshly,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> replied with a very reasoned speech:

children.text: akṛtvā katthase karma kimartham iha rākṣasa
children.translated_text: "Without doing the deed, why do you boast here, O rākṣasa?

children.text: kuru tat karma yenāhaṃ śraddadhyāṃ tava katthanam ||
children.translated_text: Do that deed by which I may believe your boasting.
Without speaking any harsh word, without disparaging anything at all,
and without boasting, I will kill you. Watch, O man-eater."
Having spoken thus, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> planted five nārāca arrows, drawn back to the ear,
with tremendous speed in the breast of the rākṣasa.
Struck by him with those well-aimed arrows, the son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, angered,
in return pierced <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> with three arrows.
Then there arose a most terrible clash in battle
between the lion among men and the lion among rākṣasas, both seeking to kill each other.
For both were endowed with strength, both possessed of valor,
both exceedingly heroic and skilled in every weapon and missile.
Both were supremely hard to conquer, unequaled in strength and splendor,
and the two great heroes fought like planets moving through the sky.

children.text: balavṛtrāviva hi tau yudhi vai duṣpradharṣaṇau
children.translated_text: Like <s>Bala</s> and <s>Vṛtra</s>, hard to assail in battle,
those two great-souled warriors fought then like two lions.
Standing firm while releasing many floods of arrows,
the lion among men and the lion among rākṣasas fought on with delight.
The two foremost ones, man and rākṣasa, greatly exultant, desirous of victory, and bearing arrows and bows,

children.text: parasparaṃ tau pravavarṣatur bhṛśaṃ śaraughavarṣeṇa balāhakāviva ||
children.translated_text: poured down upon each other a heavy rain of arrow-showers, like clouds.
Then the son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, tormentor of enemies, set an arrow on the string,

children.text: sasarja rākṣasendrāya kruddhaḥ sarpa iva śvasan ||
children.translated_text: and, enraged and breathing like a serpent, released it at the lord of rākṣasas.
When the son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> heard the twang and roar of his bowstring,
his face grew pale, and he looked closely at <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Seeing that rākṣasa, the son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, with a dejected face,
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> spoke to <s>Saumitri</s>, who was absorbed in battle:
"I observe omens in this son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: tvara tena mahābāho bhagna eṣa na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so make haste, mighty-armed one; he is broken, without doubt."
Then <s>Saumitri</s> fitted arrows like tongues of fire,
and released them all at him, sharp and fierce with venom as it were.
Struck by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s arrows, whose touch was like <s>Śakra</s>'s thunderbolt,
for a moment he became stupefied, all his senses shaken.
Recovering consciousness after a moment, with his senses returned,
the hero saw the heroic son of <s>Daśaratha</s> standing before him.
His eyes reddened with rage, he advanced upon <s>Saumitri</s>,

children.text: abravīccainam āsādya punaḥ sa paruṣaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, coming up to him, again spoke harsh words:

children.text: kiṃ na smarasi tad yuddhe prathame matparākramam
children.translated_text: "Do you not remember my prowess in that first battle,

children.text: nibaddhastvaṃ saha bhrātrā yadā yudhi viceṣṭase ||
children.translated_text: when, bound along with your brother, you writhed in the fight?
In that great battle, with arrows equal to <s>Śakra</s>'s thunderbolt,
you two young men, together with your vanguard, lay at first on the ground unconscious.

children.text: smṛtir vā nāsti te manye vyaktaṃ vā yamasādanam
children.translated_text: I think either your memory is gone, or plainly you wish

children.text: gantum icchasi yasmāt tvaṃ māṃ dharṣayitum icchasi ||
children.translated_text: to go to <s>Yama</s>'s abode, since you wish to attack me.

children.text: yadi te prathame yuddhe na dṛṣṭo matparākramaḥ
children.translated_text: If in the first battle you did not see my prowess,
today I shall show it to you. Stand now, firmly prepared."
Having said this, he pierced <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> with seven arrows,
and <s>Hanūmat</s> with ten excellent arrows of sharp edges.
Then that valiant one, doubly enraged through anger,
pierced <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> with a hundred well-aimed arrows.
When <s>Rāma</s>'s younger brother saw that deed done by <s>Indrajit</s>,
he disregarded it, laughing and saying, "This is nothing."

children.text: mumoca sa śarān ghorān saṃgṛhya narapuṃgavaḥ
children.translated_text: Then that bull among men, gathering up terrible arrows, released them,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, fearless-faced and enraged, at the son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle.
"Heroes who have entered battle do not strike in this way, night-roamer.
These arrows of yours are light, weak in force, and easy to bear.
Heroes desiring victory in combat do not fight like this."
While speaking to him in this way, he covered him with showers of arrows.
Shattered by his arrows, the rākṣasa's armor, adorned with gold,
broke apart on the floor of the chariot like a net of stars falling from the sky.
With his armor shaken off and wounded by nārāca arrows,

children.text: indrajit samare śūraḥ prarūḍha iva sānumān ||
children.translated_text: heroic <s>Indrajit</s> in battle looked like a mountain peak with trees grown upon it.

children.text: abhīkṣṇaṃ niśvasantau hi yudhyetāṃ tumulaṃ yudhi
children.translated_text: Breathing heavily again and again, the two fought a tumultuous battle,
all their limbs cut by arrows and smeared everywhere with blood.
The two best knowers of missiles repeatedly displayed missiles,
and bound arrows of many different shapes in the air.

children.text: vyapetadoṣam asyantau laghucitraṃ ca suṣṭhu ca
children.translated_text: Hurling them faultlessly, swiftly, variously, and skillfully,

children.text: ubhau tu tumulaṃ ghoraṃ cakratur nararākṣasau ||
children.translated_text: the two, man and rākṣasa, made a fierce and tumultuous battle.
Separately from each of the two there was heard the dreadful sound of their bowstrings,
like the thunder of two very terrible clouds roaring in the sky.

children.text: te gātrayor nipatitā rukmapuṅkhāḥ śarā yudhi
children.translated_text: The gold-feathered arrows that had fallen upon their bodies in battle,
smeared with blood, flew out and entered the surface of the earth.
With other very sharp weapons their arrows collided in the sky,
and by thousands they broke and cut one another apart.
In that battle there arose a terrible heap made of their arrows,
like a heap of kuśa grass in a sacrifice beside two blazing fires.
The wounded bodies of those two great-souled ones shone brightly,
like leafless śālmalī and kiṃśuka trees in the forest, yet covered with flowers.
Again and again they made a fierce, terrible, tumultuous encounter,
<s>Indrajit</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, each seeking victory over the other.
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> struck the son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle, and the son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> likewise struck <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Striking one another, the two did not become weary.
With nets of arrows lodged deep in their bodies, the two powerful ones
shone, those great heroes, like two mountains overgrown with shoots.
Their limbs, drenched with blood and thickly covered with arrows,
blazed on every side like flaming fires.

children.text: tayor atha mahān kālo vyatīyād yudhyamānayoḥ
children.translated_text: Then, as the two fought, a long time passed,

children.text: na ca tau yuddhavaimukhyaṃ śramaṃ vāpyupajagmatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: yet neither turned away from battle nor succumbed to weariness.
Then, to remove the battle-fatigue of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, undefeated in the battle-fronts,
mighty <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, providing what was dear and beneficial, came to the battle and took his stand.

children.text: yudhyamānau tu tau dṛṣṭvā prasaktau nararākṣasau
