children.translated_text: Seeing the man and the rākṣasa fighting, both intent upon the duel,
that heroic brother of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> stood at the head of the battle.
Then, standing firm, he twanged his great bow,
and released great arrows with sharp points against the rākṣasas.
Those arrows, like blazing fire, falling with careful aim,
tore the rākṣasas apart like thunderbolts striking great mountains.
The followers of <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> too, with spears, swords, and paṭṭasas,
cut down heroic rākṣasas in battle, those foremost of rākṣasas.

children.text: rākṣasaistaiḥ parivṛtaḥ sa tadā tu vibhīṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Surrounded by those rākṣasas, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> then

children.text: babhau madhye prahṛṣṭānāṃ kalabhānām iva dvipaḥ ||
children.translated_text: shone among the delighted ones like an elephant amid young elephants.
Then, urging on the monkeys, who delighted in war with the rākṣasas,

children.text: uvāca vacanaṃ kāle kālajño rakṣasāṃ varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that best of rākṣasas, knowing the proper time, spoke these words at the right moment:
This one alone stands as though he were the final refuge of the lord of rākṣasas.

children.text: etaccheṣaṃ balaṃ tasya kiṃ tiṣṭhata harīśvarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is the remainder of his army. Why do you stand still, lords of the monkeys?
When this evil rākṣasa has been slain at the head of battle,

children.text: rāvaṇaṃ varjayitvā tu śeṣam asya balaṃ hatam ||
children.translated_text: apart from <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the rest of his army will have been destroyed.
The hero <s>Prahasta</s> has been killed, and mighty <s>Nikumbha</s>,
<s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, <s>Kumbha</s>, and the night-roamer <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>;
<s>Akampana</s>, <s>Supārśva</s>, and the rākṣasa <s>Cakramālī</s>,
<s>Kampana</s>, and the valiant <s>Devāntaka</s> and <s>Narāntaka</s>.
Having slain these and many other exceedingly strong foremost rākṣasas,

children.text: bāhubhyāṃ sāgaraṃ tīrtvā laṅghyatāṃ goṣpadaṃ laghu ||
children.translated_text: you who crossed the ocean with your arms should leap over this small cow's hoofprint.

children.text: etāvad iha śeṣaṃ vo jetavyam iha vānarāḥ
children.translated_text: Only this much remains here for you to conquer, monkeys;
all the rākṣasas, arrogant in strength, have been slain after coming together.

children.text: ayuktaṃ nidhanaṃ kartuṃ putrasya janitur mama
children.translated_text: It is not fitting for me to bring about the death of my own brother's son;

children.text: ghṛṇām apāsya rāmārthe nihanyāṃ bhrātur ātmajam ||
children.translated_text: yet, casting aside pity for <s>Rāma</s>'s sake, I would kill my brother's son.
As I desire to kill him, tears and my very eyes obstruct me.
Therefore this mighty-armed <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> will put him down,

children.text: vānarā ghnantuṃ sambhūya bhṛtyān asya samīpagān ||
children.translated_text: while the monkeys, gathered together, should kill his servants standing near him.
Thus urged on by that exceedingly famous rākṣasa,
the monkey-lords rejoiced and shook their tails.
Then those tiger-like monkeys, roaring again and again,
uttered various cries, like peacocks on seeing clouds.

children.text: jāmbavān api taiḥ sarvaiḥ svayūthair abhisaṃvṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Jāmbavān</s> too, surrounded by all his own troops,
struck the rākṣasas with stones, claws, and teeth.
Those very mighty rākṣasas, seeing the lord of bears killing them,
surrounded him, having cast off fear, armed with many kinds of weapons.
With arrows, sharp axes, paṭṭasas, staffs, and javelins,

children.text: jāmbavantaṃ mṛdhe jaghnur nighnantaṃ rākṣasīṃ camūm ||
children.translated_text: they struck <s>Jāmbavān</s> in the battle as he was destroying the rākṣasa army.
That tumultuous clash arose between monkeys and rākṣasas,
like the dreadful, great-sounding battle of the enraged gods and asuras.

children.text: hanūmān api saṃkruddhaḥ sālam utpāṭya parvatāt
children.translated_text: <s>Hanūmān</s> too, enraged, uprooted a śāla tree from the mountain,
and, reaching the rākṣasas, made slaughter of them by the thousands.

children.text: sa dattvā tumulaṃ yuddhaṃ pitṛvyasyendrajid yudhi
children.translated_text: After giving fierce battle to his paternal uncle in combat, <s>Indrajit</s>
again rushed upon <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the slayer of enemy heroes.

children.text: tau prayuddhau tadā vīrau mṛdhe lakṣmaṇarākṣasau
children.translated_text: Then those two heroes, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and the rākṣasa, fought in battle,
and, pouring down floods of arrows, struck one another.
The two mighty ones continually hid each other with nets of arrows,
like the moon and sun at the end of the hot season hidden by powerful clouds.

children.text: na hyādānaṃ na saṃdhānaṃ dhanuṣo vā parigrahaḥ
children.translated_text: Neither the taking up, nor the fitting to the string, nor the grasping of the bow,

children.text: na vipramokṣo bāṇānāṃ na vikarṣo na vigrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor the release of arrows, nor the drawing back, nor the movement in combat,
nor the joining of fist to bowstring, nor the aiming at the target
could be seen there as the two fought, because of the lightness of their hands.
And with nets of arrows released by the speed of their bows on every side,
when the sky was covered over, no forms shone forth.

children.text: tamasā pihitaṃ sarvam āsīd bhīmataraṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: Everything was enveloped in darkness, great and still more terrible.

children.text: na tadānīṃ vavau vāyur na jajvāla ca pāvakaḥ
children.translated_text: At that moment the wind did not blow, nor did fire burn;
and the great seers muttered, "May there be welfare for the worlds,"
and the gandharvas who had come there gathered together with the cāraṇas.
Then the four black horses, adorned with gold, of that lion among rākṣasas
<s>Saumitri</s> pierced with four arrows.
Then, with another bhalla arrow, as the charioteer was moving about,

children.text: lāghavād rāghavaḥ śrīmāñ śiraḥ kāyād apāharat ||
children.translated_text: the glorious <s>Rāghava</s>, with quickness, severed his head from his body.
Seeing his charioteer slain in battle, the son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>

children.text: prajahau samaroddharṣaṃ viṣaṇṇaḥ sa babhūva ha ||
children.translated_text: lost his exultation in battle and became despondent.
Seeing the rākṣasa with a despondent face, the leaders of the monkey troops
Then, greatly delighted, they also honored <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Then <s>Pramāthī</s>, <s>Śarabha</s>, <s>Rabhasa</s>, and <s>Gandhamādana</s>,
four lordly vānaras, unable to endure it, made a swift charge.

children.text: te cāsya hayamukhyeṣu tūrṇam utpatya vānarāḥ
children.translated_text: Those vānaras, swiftly leaping up onto his foremost horses,
the four of very great valor, fell upon the four with terrible force.
When those mountain-like vānaras had mounted upon them,
blood visibly flowed from the mouths of the horses.

children.text: te nihatya hayāṃstasya pramathya ca mahāratham
children.translated_text: After killing his horses and crushing his great chariot,
they leapt back again with speed and stood at <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s side.
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s son, leaping down from the chariot whose horses had been killed and whose charioteer was crushed,
rushed at <s>Saumitri</s> with a shower of arrows.

children.text: tato mahendrapratimaḥ sa lakṣmaṇaḥ padātinaṃ taṃ niśitaiḥ śarottamaiḥ
children.translated_text: Then that <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, like great <s>Indra</s>, checked with sharp excellent arrows

children.text: sṛjantam ādau niśitāñ śarottamān bhṛśaṃ tadā bāṇagaṇair nyavārayat ||
children.translated_text: the foot-soldier as he first released sharp, excellent shafts, stopping him then with hosts of arrows.
His horses slain, the mighty, brilliant night-roamer stood upon the ground;
<s>Indrajit</s>, exceedingly enraged, blazed with his splendor.
The two bowmen, each wishing to kill the other fiercely with arrows,
had gone forth for victory like two rutting lordly elephants in the forest.
As the rākṣasas and forest-dwellers struck one another down,
they did not abandon their lords in battle, rushing here and there.

children.text: sa lakṣmaṇaṃ samuddiśya paraṃ lāghavam āsthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Aiming at <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, he assumed the utmost quickness
and rained showers of arrows as <s>Purandara</s> rains down rains.

children.text: muktam indrajitā tat tu śaravarṣam ariṃdamaḥ
children.translated_text: That shower of arrows released by <s>Indrajit</s>
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, subduer of foes, unconfused, warded off though it was very hard to withstand.
Thinking <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s armor impossible to pierce, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s son,
<s>Indrajit</s>, with three well-feathered arrows struck <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> in the forehead,
exceedingly enraged and displaying a swift missile.
With those arrows fixed in his forehead, the delight of the <s>Raghu</s> line shone
at the front of battle, proud in combat, like a mountain with three peaks.
Though thus wounded by arrows from the rākṣasa in the great battle,

children.text: tam āśu prativivyādha lakṣmaṇaḥ pañcabhiḥ śaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> swiftly pierced him in return with five arrows.
The two heroes, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and <s>Indrajit</s>, mighty in strength and bow,
struck one another with arrows, with terrible-flying shafts.
Approaching one another, the two bowmen pierced each other
in every limb with dreadful arrows, both resolved upon victory.
Against him whose horses had been slain, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, more firmly enraged,
released five arrows into his chest, their touch like the thunderbolt.

children.text: te tasya kāyaṃ nirbhidya rukmapuṅkhā nimittagāḥ
children.translated_text: Piercing his body, those gold-feathered shafts found their mark
and, smeared with blood, became like great red serpents.
Angered at his father's brother, mighty <s>Indrajit</s> took up an arrow,
excellent among the rākṣasas, bestowed by <s>Yama</s>.

children.text: taṃ samīkṣya mahātejā maheṣuṃ tena saṃhitam
children.translated_text: Seeing that great, brilliant, mighty arrow fitted by him,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> too, of terrible prowess, took up another arrow,

children.text: kubereṇa svayaṃ svapne yad dattam amitātmanā
children.translated_text: which the immeasurable-souled <s>Kubera</s> himself had given in a dream,

children.text: durjayaṃ durviṣahyaṃ ca sendrair api surāsuraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: unconquerable and unbearable even for the gods and asuras together with <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: tābhyāṃ tau dhanuṣi śreṣṭhe saṃhitau sāyakottamau
children.translated_text: Those two excellent shafts, fitted to the two finest bows,
as they were drawn by the two heroes, blazed greatly with splendor.
Those two arrows, illuminating the sky, were loosed from the bows;
striking face against face, they collided with force.
Like two great planets, after colliding with one another
in the battle, they broke into a hundred pieces and fell upon the earth.
Seeing those two arrows repelled at the head of the battle,
both <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and <s>Indrajit</s> were ashamed and filled with anger.
Then the highly enraged <s>Saumitri</s> took up the Vāruṇa missile;

children.text: raudraṃ mahendrajid yuddhe vyasṛjad yudhi viṣṭhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mahendrajit</s>, standing firm in battle, released the Raudra missile in the fight.
Between them there arose a very tumultuous battle, resembling a wonder;
the beings stationed in the sky surrounded <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
In the terrible battle of vānaras and rākṣasas, filled with frightful cries,

children.text: bhūtair bahubhir ākāśaṃ vismitair āvṛtaṃ babhau ||
children.translated_text: the sky appeared covered with many amazed beings.
Seers, ancestors, gods, gandharvas, garuḍas, and serpents,
placing <s>Śatakratu</s> at their head, protected <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> in battle.
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s younger brother fitted another best of shafts,
with a touch like fire, terrible to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s son:
well-feathered, with a straight body, well-jointed and well-set,
wrought with gold, a heroic arrow that would end the body,
hard to ward off, hard to endure, bringing fear to the rākṣasas,
like the venom of a poisonous serpent, honored by hosts of gods,

children.text: yena śakro mahātejā dānavān ajayat prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: with which mighty, lordly <s>Śakra</s>, the powerful one borne by bay steeds,
formerly conquered the dānavas in the war between gods and asuras.
That Aindra missile, undefeated in battles, <s>Saumitri</s>, best of men,
fitted as the finest arrow to the finest bow.
Having fitted that crusher of enemies, he drew the bow,

children.text: sajyam āyamya durdharṣaḥ kālo lokakṣaye yathā ||
children.translated_text: stretching the strung weapon, hard to assail, like Time at the destruction of the worlds.

children.text: saṃdhāya dhanuṣi śreṣṭhe vikarṣann idam abravīt
children.translated_text: Having set it upon the excellent bow, and drawing it back,
glorious <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> spoke these words, effective for accomplishing his purpose.
If <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, is righteous and true to his promise,
and if he is unrivaled in manly valor, then by that truth slay this son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: ityuktvā bāṇam ā karṇaṃ vikṛṣya tam ajihmagam
children.translated_text: Having said this, and drawing that straight-flying arrow back to his ear,
heroic <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> released it in battle against <s>Indrajit</s>,
joining it with the Aindra weapon, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the slayer of enemy heroes.
His head, with its helmet and splendid blazing earrings,
was torn from <s>Indrajit</s>'s body and fell upon the ground.
That great head of the rākṣasa prince, severed from its shoulders,
gold-like and sprinkled with blood, was seen upon the earth.
Slain, the son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> quickly fell upon the earth,
with armor and helmet, shattered, together with his bow.
Then all the monkeys, together with <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, cried out,

children.text: hṛṣyanto nihate tasmin devā vṛtravadhe yathā ||
children.translated_text: rejoicing when he had been slain, as the gods did at the slaying of <s>Vṛtra</s>.
Then in the sky a clamor arose among beings and great-souled seers,
and also among gandharvas and apsarases.
Recognizing that he had fallen, that great rākṣasa army,
being struck down by the triumphant monkeys, scattered into the quarters.
Those rākṣasas, being killed by the monkeys, threw away their weapons,
and all ran toward <s>Laṅkā</s>, their senses lost.

children.text: dudruvur bahudhā bhītā rākṣasāḥ śataśo diśaḥ
children.translated_text: Terrified rākṣasas fled in many ways, by hundreds, into the quarters,
all abandoning their weapons: spears, swords, and axes.
Some, terrified and tormented by the monkeys, entered <s>Laṅkā</s>;

children.text: samudre patitāḥ kecit kecit parvatam āśritāḥ ||
children.translated_text: some fell into the sea, and some took refuge on the mountain.
Seeing <s>Indrajit</s> slain, lying on the battlefield,
among the thousands of rākṣasas not one could be seen.
As, when the sun has set, its rays do not remain,
so, when he had fallen, those rākṣasas went off into the quarters.
Like the sun with its rays stilled, like a fire extinguished,
that great-bright one became lifeless, his life gone.
With its many afflictions quieted, its enemy destroyed, and filled with joy,
the world became so then, when the son of the rākṣasa king had fallen.

children.text: harṣaṃ ca śakro bhagavān saha sarvaiḥ surarṣabhaiḥ
children.translated_text: Lord <s>Śakra</s>, together with all the best of the gods,
felt joy when that sinful rākṣasa had been slain.
The waters and the sky became clear, and the daityas and dānavas rejoiced;
they came when that terror of all the worlds had fallen.
All the gods, gandharvas, and dānavas together said,
"Let the brāhmaṇas move about free from fever and with their impurity calmed."
Then, overjoyed, the monkey troop-leaders congratulated him in the battle,
seeing that matchless chief of the rākṣasas slain.
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, <s>Hanūmat</s>, and <s>Jāmbavān</s>, leader of the bear troops,
congratulating him on the victory, also praised <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Shouting, roaring, and bellowing, the leaping monkeys,
having achieved their aim, surrounded and stood beside the son of <s>Raghu</s>.
Brandishing their tails and making slapping sounds, the monkeys
then made heard the words, "<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> is victorious!"
Embracing one another, the monkeys, their minds delighted,
told many kinds of stories born from reliance on the <s>Rāghavas</s>.

children.text: tad asukaram athābhivīkṣya hṛṣṭāḥ priyasuhṛdo yudhi lakṣmaṇasya karma
children.translated_text: Then, joyfully beholding that deed of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> in battle, hard to accomplish, his dear friends

children.text: paramam upalabhanmanaḥpraharṣaṃ vinihatam indraripuṃ niśamya devāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the gods, hearing that <s>Indra</s>'s enemy had been slain, attained supreme delight of mind.
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, whose limbs were wet with blood and whose marks were auspicious,
became joyful after killing in battle the conqueror of <s>Śakra</s>.

children.text: tataḥ sa jāmbavantaṃ ca hanūmantaṃ ca vīryavān
children.translated_text: Then that valiant, greatly radiant one turned back <s>Jāmbavān</s>,
and <s>Hanūmat</s>, and all those forest-dwellers,
and then quickly went to where <s>Sugrīva</s> and <s>Rāghava</s> were,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> leaning on <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> and <s>Hanūmat</s>.

children.text: tato rāmam abhikramya saumitrir abhivādya ca
children.translated_text: Then <s>Saumitri</s> approached <s>Rāma</s> and bowed to him,
and stood near his brother, like the younger brother of <s>Śakra</s> beside <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: ācacakṣe tadā vīro ghoram indrajito vadham ||
children.translated_text: The hero then recounted the terrible slaying of <s>Indrajit</s>.
And <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, rejoicing, reported to <s>Rāma</s>
that the head of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s son had been severed by great-souled <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Seating him on his lap and embracing him though he was sorely wounded,

children.text: mūrdhni cainam upāghrāya bhūyaḥ saṃspṛśya ca tvaran
children.translated_text: smelling his head and again touching him quickly,
that bull among men comforted <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and spoke these words:
"A deed of supreme blessing has been done by you, who do what is hard to do.
Today I have been made free of enemies, for <s>Rāvaṇa</s> will come out
with a great battle-array when he hears that his son has been struck down.
As that lord of rākṣasas comes out, burned by grief at his son's death,
I shall surround him with a great army and slay the unconquerable one.

children.text: tvayā lakṣmaṇa nāthena sītā ca pṛthivī ca me
children.translated_text: With you, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, as my protector, <s>Sītā</s> and the earth

children.text: na duṣprāpā hate tvadya śakrajetari cāhave ||
children.translated_text: are not difficult for me to obtain, now that the conqueror of <s>Śakra</s> has been slain by you today in battle."

children.text: sa taṃ bhrātaram āśvāsya pariṣvajya ca rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: After consoling and embracing that brother, <s>Rāghava</s>,
<s>Rāma</s> joyfully addressed <s>Suṣeṇa</s> and said this:
"This <s>Saumitri</s>, deeply wise and affectionate to his friends, still has arrows lodged in him;
treat him so that he becomes completely well.
Let <s>Saumitri</s>, together with <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, quickly be freed from the darts."
of the bear-and-monkey armies, of the brave warriors who fight with trees

children.text: ye cānye 'tra ca yudhyantaḥ saśalyā vraṇinastathā
children.translated_text: and whatever others are fighting here, with arrows still lodged in them and wounded likewise,
let all of them too be made well by you with care.

children.text: evam uktaḥ sa rāmeṇa mahātmā hariyūthapaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Rāma</s>, that great-souled leader of the monkey troops,
<s>Suṣeṇa</s> administered the supreme medicine to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> through the nose.

children.text: sa tasya gandham āghrāya viśalyaḥ samapadyata
children.translated_text: After smelling its fragrance, he became free of the arrows,
and then free from pain, with his wounds healed over.
At <s>Rāghava</s>'s command, for his friends headed by <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,
he then performed treatment for all the chief monkeys.
Then, restored to his natural state, with the arrows removed and his pain gone,
<s>Saumitri</s> was delighted there, free from fever in a moment.
Likewise <s>Rāma</s>, the lord of the leapers, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, and <s>Jāmbavān</s>, lord of the bears,

children.text: avekṣya saumitrim arogam utthitaṃ mudā sasainyaḥ suciraṃ jaharṣire ||
children.translated_text: seeing <s>Saumitri</s> risen and healthy, rejoiced in gladness for a long time together with the army.

children.text: apūjayat karma sa lakṣmaṇasya suduṣkaraṃ dāśarathir mahātmā
children.translated_text: The great-souled son of <s>Daśaratha</s> praised the deed of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, so very hard to accomplish,

children.text: hṛṣṭā babhūvur yudhi yūthapendrā niśamya taṃ śakrajitaṃ nipātitam ||
children.translated_text: and the leaders of the monkey troops were delighted on hearing that <s>Śakrajit</s> had been struck down in battle.
Then the ministers of the descendant of <s>Paulastya</s>, hearing that <s>Indrajit</s> had been killed,
ascertained it and reported it, distressed, to the ten-necked one.
"In battle, great king, your son has been killed by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
with <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> as his helper, while we looked on, O greatly radiant one.
A hero, meeting a hero, unconquered in battles,
your heroic son, conqueror of the lord of the gods, has been killed by heroic <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>."

children.text: sa taṃ pratibhayaṃ śrutvā vadhaṃ putrasya dāruṇam
children.translated_text: Hearing that terrifying and dreadful death of his son,
the terrible death of <s>Indrajit</s> in battle, he entered a great faintness.
After a long time the king, bull among rākṣasas, regained consciousness,
and, afflicted by grief for his son, wretched, lamented with his senses distraught.
"Ah, foremost of the rākṣasa army, my child, great chariot-warrior,

children.text: jitvendraṃ katham adya tvaṃ lakṣmaṇasya vaśaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: having conquered <s>Indra</s>, how have you today come under <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s power?

children.text: nanu tvam iṣubhiḥ kruddho bhindyāḥ kālāntakāvapi
children.translated_text: Surely, enraged, you could split even <s>Kāla</s> and <s>Antaka</s> with your arrows,

children.text: mandarasyāpi śṛṅgāṇi kiṃ punar lakṣmaṇaṃ raṇe ||
children.translated_text: even the peaks of <s>Mandara</s>; how much more <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> in battle?

children.text: adya vaivasvato rājā bhūyo bahumato mama
children.translated_text: Today king <s>Vaivasvata</s> is again highly honored by me,
since today you, mighty-armed one, have been joined to the law of death.
This is the path of good warriors, even among all the hosts of immortals:

children.text: yaḥ kṛte hanyate bhartuḥ sa pumān svargam ṛcchati ||
children.translated_text: the man who is slain for the sake of his lord reaches heaven.
Today all the hosts of gods, the guardians of the worlds, and the seers too,

children.text: hatam indrajitaṃ dṛṣṭvā sukhaṃ svapsyanti nirbhayāḥ ||
children.translated_text: seeing <s>Indrajit</s> slain, will sleep happily and without fear.

children.text: adya lokāstrayaḥ kṛtsnāḥ pṛthivī ca sakānanā
children.translated_text: Today all the three worlds, and the earth with its forests,
bereft of the one <s>Indrajit</s>, appears empty to me.
Today in the inner palace I shall hear the cry of the daughters of the <s>Nairṛtas</s>,
like the trumpeting of a herd of female elephants in a mountain cave.

children.text: yauvarājyaṃ ca laṅkāṃ ca rakṣāṃsi ca paraṃtapa
children.translated_text: The heirship, <s>Laṅkā</s>, the rākṣasas, O scorcher of foes,

children.text: mātaraṃ māṃ ca bhāryāṃ ca kva gato 'si vihāya naḥ ||
children.translated_text: your mother, me, and your wife: where have you gone, abandoning us?

children.text: mama nāma tvayā vīra gatasya yamasādanam
children.translated_text: For me, hero, when I had gone to <s>Yama</s>'s abode,
the funeral rites should have been performed by you; for the opposite has happened.

children.text: sa tvaṃ jīvati sugrīve rāghave ca salakṣmaṇe
children.translated_text: While <s>Sugrīva</s> is alive, and <s>Rāghava</s> with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: mama śalyam anuddhṛtya kva gato 'si vihāya naḥ ||
children.translated_text: where have you gone, abandoning us, without drawing out my thorn of grief?"
As <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of rākṣasas, was tormented by laments of this kind,
a great anger, born from the calamity of his son, entered him.

children.text: ghoraṃ prakṛtyā rūpaṃ tat tasya krodhāgnimūrchitam
children.translated_text: That form of his, terrible by nature, became overwhelmed by the fire of anger,
like the form of enraged <s>Rudra</s>, unapproachable.
From the eyes of that enraged one, drops of tears fell,
like drops of oil with flames from two blazing lamps.
As he gnashed his teeth, the sound of his teeth was heard,
like that of a great machine being turned by dānavas.

children.text: kālāgnir iva saṃkruddho yāṃ yāṃ diśam avaikṣata
children.translated_text: Like the fire at the end of time, enraged, whichever direction he looked,
in that very direction the rākṣasas, terrified with fear, hid themselves.
As he, like <s>Antaka</s> enraged and eager to devour moving and unmoving beings,
gazed at all the directions, the rākṣasas did not approach him.
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of rākṣasas, utterly enraged,
spoke in the midst of the rākṣasas, wishing to steady them in battle:
"For thousands of years I practiced austerity that is hard to practice,
and in those various places <s>Svayambhū</s> was pleased.
By the fruition of that very austerity and by the favor of <s>Svayambhū</s>,

children.text: nāsurebhyo na devebhyo bhayaṃ mama kadācana ||
children.translated_text: I never have any fear from asuras or from gods.
The armor given to me by <s>Brahmā</s>, bright as the sun,
has not been split in battles between gods and asuras, even by thunderbolts and spears.

children.text: tena mām adya saṃyuktaṃ rathastham iha saṃyuge
children.translated_text: Equipped with that today, standing on my chariot here in battle,

children.text: pratīyāt ko 'dya mām ājau sākṣād api puraṃdaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: who would oppose me today in combat, even <s>Purandara</s> himself?
And that great bow with its arrows,
which was given to me by <s>Svayambhū</s> when he was gracious in the battles between gods and asuras,

children.text: adya tūryaśatair bhīmaṃ dhanur utthāpyatāṃ mahat
children.translated_text: today let that great, terrible bow be lifted up with hundreds of war instruments sounding,
for the killing of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> themselves in the supreme battle."
Tormented by the death of his son, the hero came under the sway of anger,

children.text: samīkṣya rāvaṇo buddhyā sītāṃ hantuṃ vyavasyata ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, reflecting with his mind, resolved to kill <s>Sītā</s>.
But the copper-eyed, very terrible one, looking over all those night-roamers,
dreadful to behold, dejected, and speaking in dejected voices, said to them:
"By illusion, for the purpose of deceiving the forest-dwellers, my child...

children.text: kiṃcid eva hataṃ tatra sīteyam iti darśitam ||
children.translated_text: Only a little was slain there; this <s>Sītā</s> was shown as such.

children.text: tad idaṃ satyam evāhaṃ kariṣye priyam ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore I shall now make this true, a thing dear to myself:
I shall destroy <s>Vaidehī</s>, who is devoted to that mere kṣatriya.

children.text: ityevam uktvā sacivān khaḍgam āśu parāmṛśat ||
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, he quickly took hold of his sword before his ministers.
Drawing out that excellent sword, whose brilliance was like a spotless garment,

children.text: niṣpapāta sa vegena sabhāyāḥ sacivair vṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he rushed out swiftly from the assembly, surrounded by his ministers.
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, his mind deeply agitated by grief for his son,

children.text: saṃkruddhaḥ khaḍgam ādāya sahasā yatra maithilī ||
children.translated_text: became enraged, seized his sword, and suddenly went to where <s>Maithilī</s> was.
Seeing the rākṣasa going forth, they cried out with lion-roars,
and, embracing one another as they saw the enraged rākṣasa, the rākṣasas said:
Today, when those two brothers see this one, they will both tremble greatly.
For the four guardians of the world were conquered by this man when he was angry,
and many other enemies too were struck down in battles.
While they were speaking among themselves, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> came to the Aśoka grove,
and, overcome with anger, rushed upon <s>Vaidehī</s>.
Though restrained by well-meaning friends of good counsel, he was violently enraged;

children.text: abhyadhāvata saṃkruddhaḥ khe graho rohiṇīm iva ||
children.translated_text: enraged, he ran at her like a planet in the sky attacking <s>Rohiṇī</s>.
But faultless <s>Maithilī</s>, guarded by rākṣasī women,
saw the angry rākṣasa bearing an excellent sword.
When <s>Janaka</s>'s daughter perceived him with his sword, she was terrified,
as he was repeatedly restrained by his friends but would not turn back.
Since this man, enraged at me, is himself rushing straight upon me,

children.text: vadhiṣyati sanāthāṃ mām anāthām iva durmatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wicked-minded one will kill me, though I have a protector, as if I were helpless.
Many times he urged me, devoted as I am to my husband,
saying, 'Become my wife; take pleasure with me,' but he was rejected by me.

children.text: so 'yaṃ mām anupasthānād vyaktaṃ nairāśyam āgataḥ
children.translated_text: Now, because I would not attend on him, he has plainly fallen into despair,
and, possessed by anger and delusion, has risen up to kill me.
Or else those two tigers among men, the brothers <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
have today been felled in battle by that ignoble one on my account.
Ah, shame on this destruction of the two princes caused by me!

children.text: hanūmato hi tadvākyaṃ na kṛtaṃ kṣudrayā mayā
children.translated_text: For I, petty woman that I am, did not do what <s>Hanūmat</s> said.
If I, faultless one, had then gone on his back,
I would not be grieving like this today, but would be resting in my husband's lap.

children.text: manye tu hṛdayaṃ tasyāḥ kausalyāyāḥ phaliṣyati
children.translated_text: But I think the heart of <s>Kauśalyā</s>

children.text: ekaputrā yadā putraṃ vinaṣṭaṃ śroṣyate yudhi ||
children.translated_text: will break when, she who has one son, hears that her son has perished in battle.

children.text: sā hi janma ca bālyaṃ ca yauvanaṃ ca mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: For, weeping, she will remember the birth, childhood, and youth
of the great-souled one, his works of dharma, and his beauty.

children.text: nirāśā nihate putre dattvā śrāddham acetanā
children.translated_text: Hopeless when her son has been killed, after offering the śrāddha rites, senseless with grief,

children.text: agnim ārokṣyate nūnam apo vāpi pravekṣyati ||
children.translated_text: she will surely mount the fire or else enter the waters.

children.text: dhig astu kubjām asatīṃ mantharāṃ pāpaniścayām
children.translated_text: Shame on the hunchbacked, unchaste <s>Mantharā</s>, fixed on evil,
because of whom <s>Kauśalyā</s> will meet with this sorrow.
Seeing <s>Maithilī</s>, the suffering woman, lamenting in this way,

children.text: rohiṇīm iva candreṇa vinā grahavaśaṃ gatām ||
children.translated_text: like <s>Rohiṇī</s> deprived of the moon and fallen under the power of a planet,
the wise one named <s>Supārśva</s> addressed <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of rākṣasas,
who was being restrained by his ministers, with these words:
How, O ten-necked one, direct younger brother of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>,

children.text: hantum icchasi vaidehīṃ krodhād dharmam apāsya hi ||
children.translated_text: do you wish, from anger and having cast aside dharma, to kill <s>Vaidehī</s>?
You are versed in Vedic knowledge, purified by vows, and always devoted to your own dharma;

children.text: striyāḥ kasmād vadhaṃ vīra manyase rākṣaseśvara ||
children.translated_text: why, hero, lord of rākṣasas, do you think of killing a woman?
Look upon <s>Maithilī</s>, endowed with beauty, O king;

children.text: tvam eva tu sahāsmābhī rāghave krodham utsṛja ||
children.translated_text: but you yourself, together with us, should direct your anger against <s>Rāghava</s>.
Make your preparation today, on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight,
and set out on the new-moon day, surrounded by your forces, for victory.

children.text: śūro dhīmān rathī khaḍgī rathapravaram āsthitaḥ
children.translated_text: A hero, wise, a chariot-warrior and swordsman, mounted on the finest chariot,

children.text: hatvā dāśarathiṃ rāmaṃ bhavān prāpsyati maithilīm ||
children.translated_text: your majesty will obtain <s>Maithilī</s> after killing <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>.

children.text: sa tad durātmā suhṛdā niveditaṃ vacaḥ sudharmyaṃ pratigṛhya rāvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: That evil-souled but mighty <s>Rāvaṇa</s> accepted the very righteous speech presented by his friend,

children.text: gṛhaṃ jagāmātha tataśca vīryavān punaḥ sabhāṃ ca prayayau suhṛdvṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then went to his house and afterward returned to the assembly, surrounded by his friends.

children.text: sa praviśya sabhāṃ rājā dīnaḥ paramaduḥkhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Entering the assembly, the king, dejected and afflicted by supreme sorrow,

children.text: niṣasādāsane mukhye siṃhaḥ kruddha iva śvasan ||
children.translated_text: sat down on the chief seat, breathing like an angry lion.
Then mighty <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, wasted by the calamity of his son,
spoke these words to all the chiefs of the army, who stood with joined palms:
Let all of you go forth, all surrounded by elephants and horses,
and adorned with masses of chariots and foot-soldiers.

children.text: ekaṃ rāmaṃ parikṣipya samare hantum arhatha
children.translated_text: Having surrounded <s>Rāma</s> alone in battle, you must kill him,
delighted, with showers of arrows like clouds in the rainy season.
Or else tomorrow in the great battle, with sharp arrows,

children.text: bhavadbhiḥ śvo nihantāsmi rāmaṃ lokasya paśyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: I myself, before the eyes of the world, will kill <s>Rāma</s>, his limbs pierced by you.
Having received this command of the lord of rākṣasas, the rākṣasas
set out swiftly in chariots, surrounded also by elephant divisions.
At the rising of the sun that battle, exceedingly terrible,
arose in tumult between the rākṣasas and the vānaras.

children.text: te gadābhir vicitrābhiḥ prāsaiḥ khaḍgaiḥ paraśvadhaiḥ
children.translated_text: Then in battle the vānaras and rākṣasas struck one another
with varied maces, spears, swords, and axes.
Elephants and chariots were its banks, horses its fish, and banners its trees.
Rivers of blood, carrying masses of bodies, flowed forth.
Standards, armor, chariots, horses, and various weapons too,
the monkey-chiefs, leaping again and again in battle, smashed apart.
Hair, ears, foreheads, and noses of the rākṣasas
the monkeys cut away with sharp teeth and also with their nails.
In battle a hundred foremost vānaras ran at each single rākṣasa,
as birds rush upon a fruit-bearing tree.

children.text: tathā gadābhir gurvībhiḥ prāsaiḥ khaḍgaiḥ paraśvadhaiḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise, with heavy maces, spears, swords, and axes,
mountain-like rākṣasas struck down the terrible vānaras.
As the vānaras were being slain by the rākṣasas, their great army
went for refuge to <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, the refuge-giver.

children.text: tato rāmo mahātejā dhanur ādāya vīryavān
children.translated_text: Then mighty <s>Rāma</s>, full of great splendor and valor, took up his bow,

children.text: praviśya rākṣasaṃ sainyaṃ śaravarṣaṃ vavarṣa ha ||
children.translated_text: entered the rākṣasa army, and poured down a rain of arrows.

children.text: praviṣṭaṃ tu tadā rāmaṃ meghāḥ sūryam ivāmbare
children.translated_text: But when <s>Rāma</s> had entered then, the terribly fierce ones did not approach him,
like clouds that do not approach the sun in the sky, as he burned them with the fire of his arrows.
The night-roamers saw only the dreadful deeds already done by <s>Rāma</s>,
and the deeds of <s>Rāma</s> in battle that were hard to accomplish.
They saw him shaking the great army and scattering the great chariot-warriors,

children.text: dadṛśuste na vai rāmaṃ vātaṃ vanagataṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: but they did not see <s>Rāma</s>, just as one does not see the wind moving through a forest.

children.text: chinnaṃ bhinnaṃ śarair dagdhaṃ prabhagnaṃ śastrapīḍitam
children.translated_text: They saw the army cut, broken, burned by arrows, crushed, and oppressed by weapons,

children.text: balaṃ rāmeṇa dadṛśur na rāmaṃ śīghrakāriṇam ||
children.translated_text: but not <s>Rāma</s>, swift in action.

children.text: praharantaṃ śarīreṣu na te paśyanti rāghavam
children.translated_text: They did not see <s>Rāghava</s> as he struck their bodies,
just as creatures do not see the inner self abiding among the objects of the senses.

children.text: eṣa hanti gajānīkam eṣa hanti mahārathān
children.translated_text: 'This one is killing the elephant division; this one is killing the great chariot-warriors;

children.text: eṣa hanti śaraistīkṣṇaiḥ padātīn vājibhiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: this one is killing foot-soldiers together with horsemen by means of sharp arrows.'

children.text: iti te rākṣasāḥ sarve rāmasya sadṛśān raṇe
children.translated_text: Thus all those rākṣasas, seeing forms like <s>Rāma</s> in battle,
struck one another in anger, because of their likeness to <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: na te dadṛśire rāmaṃ dahantam arivāhinīm
children.translated_text: They did not see <s>Rāma</s> burning the enemy army,
for they were bewildered by the great-souled one's supreme Gāndharva weapon.

children.text: te tu rāmasahasrāṇi raṇe paśyanti rākṣasāḥ
children.translated_text: Those rākṣasas saw thousands of forms of <s>Rāma</s> in battle,

children.text: punaḥ paśyanti kākutstham ekam eva mahāhave ||
children.translated_text: and then again in the great conflict they saw <s>Kākutstha</s> alone.
They saw the golden tip of the great-souled one's bow whirling,
like a circle of firebrands, but not <s>Rāghava</s>.
Its hub was bodies, its flame was living beings, its spokes were arrows, and its rim was the bow;
it had the sound of the bowstring and the slap of the hand, and shone with the qualities of energy and intelligence.
Bounded by the power of divine weapons and slaying rākṣasas in battle,

children.text: dadṛśū rāmacakraṃ tat kālacakram iva prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: they saw that wheel of <s>Rāma</s> as creatures see the wheel of Time.
An army of ten thousand chariots, swift as the wind,
and eighteen thousand powerful elephants,
and fourteen thousand horses with their riders,
and a full two hundred thousand rākṣasa foot-soldiers,
in the eighth part of the day, by arrows like flames of fire,
were slain among the form-changing rākṣasas by <s>Rāma</s> alone.
With their horses killed and their chariots destroyed, exhausted and with their standards shattered,
the night-roamers who survived fled back to the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>.
With slain elephants, foot-soldiers, and horses, that battlefield became
like the playground of angry <s>Rudra</s>, the bearer of the <s>Pināka</s> bow.
Then the gods, together with the Gandharvas, the Siddhas, and the supreme seers,

children.text: sādhu sādhviti rāmasya tat karma samapūjayan ||
children.translated_text: honored that deed of <s>Rāma</s>, saying, 'Well done, well done!'
And then <s>Rāma</s> spoke next to <s>Sugrīva</s>:

children.text: etad astrabalaṃ divyaṃ mama vā tryambakasya vā ||
children.translated_text: 'This is the divine power of weapons, either mine or that of <s>Tryambaka</s>.'

children.text: nihatya tāṃ rākṣasavāhinīṃ tu rāmastadā śakrasamo mahātmā
children.translated_text: Having destroyed that rākṣasa host, <s>Rāma</s>, the great-souled one equal to <s>Śakra</s>,

children.text: astreṣu śastreṣu jitaklamaśca saṃstūyate devagaṇaiḥ prahṛṣṭaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: unwearied in missiles and weapons, was praised by the delighted hosts of gods.
Those thousands of elephants and of horses with their riders,
and thousands of fire-colored chariots with their standards,
and thousands of rākṣasas fighting with maces and iron clubs,
heroic, able to change form at will, and bright with golden standards,
were slain by sharp arrows adorned with heated gold,
though they had been sent forth by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, by <s>Rāma</s> of effortless action.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā śrutvā ca saṃbhrāntā hataśeṣā niśācarāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing and hearing this, the surviving night-roamers were terrified,
and the rākṣasī women gathered together, miserable and overwhelmed by anxiety.
Widowed, bereft of sons, crying out, and bereft of kinsmen,
the rākṣasīs assembled together and, afflicted with sorrow, lamented.
'How did aged <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>, hideous and hollow-bellied,

children.text: āsasāda vane rāmaṃ kandarpam iva rūpiṇam ||
children.translated_text: come upon <s>Rāma</s> in the forest, beautiful in form like <s>Kandarpa</s>?
Seeing him tender, great-souled, and devoted to the welfare of all beings,

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā lokavadhyā sā hīnarūpā prakāmitā ||
children.translated_text: that ill-formed woman, worthy of the world's condemnation, was seized by desire.
How did that rākṣasī, lacking all virtues, ugly-faced,
desire <s>Rāma</s>, who possessed virtues, great splendor, and a beautiful face?
Because of the poor fortune of this people, that grey-haired, white-headed woman
did an improper and ridiculous deed, condemned by the whole world.
For the destruction of the rākṣasas and of <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> and <s>Khara</s>,
that misshapen woman committed an unseemly assault against <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: tannimittam idaṃ vairaṃ rāvaṇena kṛtaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: Because of that, this great hostility was made by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>;

children.text: vadhāya nītā sā sītā daśagrīveṇa rakṣasā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s> was carried off by the ten-necked rākṣasa for his own destruction.

children.text: na ca sītāṃ daśagrīvaḥ prāpnoti janakātmajām
children.translated_text: And the ten-necked one does not obtain <s>Sītā</s>, daughter of <s>Janaka</s>;

children.text: baddhaṃ balavatā vairam akṣayaṃ rāghaveṇa ha ||
children.translated_text: a powerful and inexhaustible enmity has been bound with <s>Rāghava</s>.'

children.text: vaidehīṃ prārthayānaṃ taṃ virādhaṃ prekṣya rākṣasaṃ
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāma</s> alone killed the rākṣasa <s>Virādha</s>, who was seeking <s>Vaidehī</s>,
that is sufficient evidence.
Fourteen thousand rākṣasas of dreadful deeds
were slain in <s>Janasthāna</s> by arrows like tongues of fire.
<s>Khara</s> too was killed in battle, and <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> and <s>Triśiras</s> likewise,
by arrows shining like the sun; that is sufficient evidence.
The blood-eating <s>Kabandha</s>, with arms a yojana long, was slain,
as he roared in the pain of anger; that is sufficient evidence.
<s>Rāma</s> killed the mighty <s>Vālin</s>, son of the thousand-eyed god,
who was like a cloud; that is sufficient evidence.
While <s>Sugrīva</s> was living miserably on Mount <s>Ṛśyamūka</s>, his hopes broken,
he was established in the kingdom; that is sufficient evidence.
A fitting speech, joined with dharma and advantage and beneficial to all the rākṣasas,

children.text: yuktaṃ vibhīṣaṇenoktaṃ mohāt tasya na rocate ||
children.translated_text: was spoken by <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, but through delusion it did not please him.
If the younger brother of <s>Dhanada</s> had followed <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>'s words,

children.text: śmaśānabhūtā duḥkhārtā neyaṃ laṅkā purī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: this city <s>Laṅkā</s> would not have become like a cremation ground, afflicted with sorrow.
Having heard that mighty <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> had been killed by <s>Rāghava</s>,
and that his beloved son <s>Indrajit</s> was dead, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> still does not understand.

children.text: mama putro mama bhrātā mama bhartā raṇe hataḥ
children.translated_text: 'My son, my brother, my husband has been killed in battle,'

children.text: ityevaṃ śrūyate śabdo rākṣasānāṃ kule kule ||
children.translated_text: such a cry is heard in every family of the rākṣasas.
Chariots, horses, and elephants have been slain by the hundreds of thousands,
and so have rākṣasas fighting on foot, by heroic <s>Rāma</s> in battle.

children.text: rudro vā yadi vā viṣṇur mahendro vā śatakratuḥ
children.translated_text: Whether it is <s>Rudra</s>, or <s>Viṣṇu</s>, or great <s>Indra</s> of a hundred sacrifices,

children.text: hanti no rāmarūpeṇa yadi vā svayam antakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or Death himself, he is killing us in the form of <s>Rāma</s>.
Our foremost heroes have been slain by <s>Rāma</s>; we despair of life.
Seeing no end to our fear, helpless, we lament.
Though the ten-necked one is a hero who has received boons, he does not understand
that this very great and terrible danger has arisen in battle from <s>Rāma</s>'s hand.

children.text: na devā na ca gandharvā na piśācā na rākṣasāḥ
children.translated_text: Neither gods, nor gandharvas, nor piśācas, nor rākṣasas
are able to save anyone attacked by <s>Rāma</s> in combat.
Omens too are seen for <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle after battle;
they will foretell <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s destruction by <s>Rāma</s>.
When the grandsire was pleased, immunity from gods, dānavas, and rākṣasas
was granted to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>; he did not ask it from human beings.

children.text: tad idaṃ mānuṣānmanye prāptaṃ niḥsaṃśayaṃ bhayam
children.translated_text: Therefore I think this danger has undoubtedly come from a human being,
terrible and bringing an end to the life of the rākṣasas and of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Oppressed by the powerful rākṣasa through the gift of boons,
the gods, with blazing austerities, worshipped the grandsire.
For the welfare of the deities, the great-souled grandsire,

children.text: uvāca devatāḥ sarvā idaṃ tuṣṭo mahad vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: pleased, spoke this great word to all the gods:
'From this day forward, in the three worlds, all dānavas and rākṣasas,
wrapped in fear, will wander forever and always.'
Then, having gathered with all the gods led by <s>Indra</s>,
they propitiated <s>Mahādeva</s>, the bull-bannered destroyer of <s>Tripura</s>.
When <s>Mahādeva</s> was pleased, he spoke these words to the gods:
'For your welfare a woman will arise, bringing about the destruction of the rākṣasas.'

children.text: eṣā devaiḥ prayuktā tu kṣud yathā dānavān purā
children.translated_text: Just as Hunger, set in motion by the gods, once devoured the dānavas,
so <s>Sītā</s>, slayer of rākṣasas, will devour us together with <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Through the misconduct of ill-disciplined, evil-minded <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
this dreadful final blow has come upon us, overwhelmed with grief.

children.text: taṃ na paśyāmahe loke yo naḥ śaraṇado bhavet
children.translated_text: In the world we see no one who could give us refuge,
when we have been attacked by <s>Rāghava</s>, as though by Time at the destruction of an age.

children.text: itīva sarvā rajanīcarastriyaḥ parasparaṃ samparirabhya bāhubhiḥ
children.translated_text: Thus all the night-roaming women, embracing one another with their arms,

children.text: viṣedur ārtātibhayābhipīḍitā vinedur uccaiśca tadā sudāruṇam ||
children.translated_text: sank down, afflicted by pain and extreme fear, and then wailed loudly and terribly.

children.text: ārtānāṃ rākṣasīnāṃ tu laṅkāyāṃ vai kule kule
children.translated_text: In <s>Laṅkā</s>, in every household, from the suffering rākṣasī women,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> heard a pitiful sound of lamentation.

children.text: sa tu dīrghaṃ viniśvasya muhūrtaṃ dhyānam āsthitaḥ
children.translated_text: He sighed deeply and remained absorbed in thought for a moment;
then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, terrible to behold, became exceedingly enraged.
Biting his lip with his teeth, his eyes reddened with anger,

children.text: rākṣasair api durdarśaḥ kālāgnir iva mūrchitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: hard even for rākṣasas to look upon, he seemed like the blazing fire of the end-time.
The lord of rākṣasas then spoke to the rākṣasas standing near him,
who were speaking indistinctly from fear, as though burning them with his eyes:
'<s>Mahodara</s>, <s>Mahāpārśva</s>, and the rākṣasa <s>Virūpākṣa</s>,
quickly tell the armies to march out by my command.'
Hearing that order of his, those rākṣasas, stricken with fear,
urged on those rākṣasas, who were not dismayed, according to the king's command.

children.text: te tu sarve tathetyuktvā rākṣasā ghoradarśanāḥ
children.translated_text: Then all those rākṣasas, terrible to behold, said, 'So be it,'
and, after all had performed auspicious rites, they went before <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Those great chariot-warriors duly honored <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
and all stood with joined palms, desiring their master's victory.
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, overwhelmed with anger, laughed and spoke to them,
to <s>Mahodara</s>, <s>Mahāpārśva</s>, and the rākṣasa <s>Virūpākṣa</s>:
'Today, with arrows released from my bow and resembling the suns at the end of an age,
I shall send <s>Rāghava</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> to the abode of <s>Yama</s>.
Today, by slaying the enemy, I shall make requital
for <s>Khara</s>, <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, <s>Prahasta</s>, and likewise <s>Indrajit</s>.'

children.text: naivāntarikṣaṃ na diśo na nadyo nāpi sāgaraḥ
children.translated_text: Neither the sky, nor the quarters, nor the rivers, nor even the ocean,
covered by the clouds of my arrows, will come into visibility.
Today, in separate divisions, those companies of the vānara hosts
I will churn with waves of arrows arising from the ocean of my bow.
Today, like an elephant, I will crush the troop-ponds
whose circles are opened lotuses and whose splendor is like lotus filaments.
Today in battle the leaders of the vānara troops, with faces pierced by arrows,
will adorn the earth like lotuses together with their stalks.
Today, of the battle-fierce monkeys who fight with trees,
I will pierce hundreds upon hundreds in battle with a single released arrow.

children.text: hato bhartā hato bhrātā yāsāṃ ca tanayā hatāḥ
children.translated_text: For those whose husband has been killed, whose brother has been killed, and whose sons have been killed,
today, by the killing of the enemy, I will wipe away their tears.
Today, with vānaras split open by my arrows, scattered and bereft of consciousness,
I will make the earth in battle such that its surface can be seen only with effort.

children.text: adya gomāyavo gṛdhrā ye ca māṃsāśino 'pare
children.translated_text: Today I will satisfy the jackals, the vultures,
and all the other flesh-eaters with the arrow-tormented flesh of my enemies.

children.text: kalpyatāṃ me rathaḥ śīghraṃ kṣipram ānīyatāṃ dhanuḥ
children.translated_text: Let my chariot be made ready quickly; let my bow be brought at once.
Let those night-roamers who remain follow me into battle.
Having heard that speech of his, <s>Mahāpārśva</s> spoke these words
to the army officers standing there: 'Let the army be hastened.'
Then the army officers, enraged and swift in valor, went around <s>Laṅkā</s>,
urging on those rākṣasas from house to house.
Then, after a short while, rākṣasas of terrible valor rushed out,
roaring, with terrifying faces and with arms bearing many kinds of weapons:

children.text: asibhiḥ paṭṭasaiḥ śūlair gadābhir musalair halaiḥ
children.translated_text: with swords, paṭṭasas, spears, maces, clubs, and plough-weapons,
with sharp-edged śaktis and great spiked hammers,
with staffs, bright discuses, and sharpened axes,
with bhiṇḍipālas, śataghnīs, and other excellent weapons as well.
Then, at <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s command, four army officers quickly brought
a chariot joined with its charioteer and yoked with eight horses.
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> mounted the divine chariot, blazing with its own splendor,
as if splitting the earth by the depth of his might.
With <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s permission, <s>Mahāpārśva</s>, <s>Mahodara</s>,
and the hard-to-assail <s>Virūpākṣa</s> then mounted their chariots.

children.text: te tu hṛṣṭā vinardanto bhindata iva medinīm
children.translated_text: They, delighted and roaring, as if cleaving the earth,
set out seeking victory and letting loose a terrible sound.
Then the powerful one, surrounded by the forces of rākṣasa hosts,
went forth for battle with bow raised, like <s>Yama</s> the ender at the end of time.
Then that great chariot-warrior, in a chariot with swift-running horses,

children.text: dvāreṇa niryayau tena yatra tau rāmalakṣmaṇau ||
children.translated_text: went out through the gate where those two, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, were.
Then the sun lost its radiance, and the quarters were covered with darkness;

children.text: dvijāśca nedur ghorāśca saṃcacāla ca medinī ||
children.translated_text: birds cried dreadfully, and the earth shook.
The god rained blood, and the horses stumbled;
a vulture fell on the tip of the banner, and inauspicious jackals howled.

children.text: nayanaṃ cāsphurad vāmaṃ savyo bāhur akampata
children.translated_text: His left eye twitched, and his left arm trembled;
his face became discolored, and his voice faltered somewhat.
Thus, as the rākṣasa <s>Daśagrīva</s> was rushing out to battle,
these forms arose in the fight, proclaiming his death.
A meteor fell from the sky, with a crash like a thunderbolt;
vultures, answered by crows, cried inauspiciously.
Disregarding these dreadful portents that had appeared,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, deluded, went forth, seeking his own death and driven on by Time.
But at the chariot-noise of those great-souled rākṣasas,
the army of the vānaras also advanced only for battle.
A very tumultuous battle then arose between the monkeys and the rākṣasas,
as they challenged one another, enraged and desiring victory.
Then the enraged <s>Daśagrīva</s>, with arrows adorned with gold,
made a great slaughter among the battle-lines of the vānaras.
Some monkeys had their heads cut off by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>;

children.text: nirucchvāsā hatāḥ kecit kecit pārśveṣu dāritāḥ
children.translated_text: some were killed, breathless, and some were torn open in their sides;
some had their heads split apart, and some were deprived of their eyes.

children.text: daśānanaḥ krodhavivṛttanetro yato yato 'bhyeti rathena saṃkhye
children.translated_text: Wherever the ten-faced one, his eyes rolling with anger, approached in battle with his chariot,

children.text: tatastatastasya śarapravegaṃ soḍhuṃ na śekur hariyūthapāste ||
children.translated_text: there and there those leaders of the monkey hosts could not bear the force of his arrows.
Thus, with their limbs cut by the shafts of <s>Daśagrīva</s>,

children.text: babhūva vasudhā tatra prakīrṇā haribhir vṛtā ||
children.translated_text: the earth there became strewn about and covered with monkeys.
They could not endure, on any side, that irresistible

children.text: na śekuḥ sahituṃ dīptaṃ pataṃgā iva pāvakam ||
children.translated_text: blazing shower of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s arrows, like moths unable to endure fire.
Afflicted by the sharp arrows, they cried out and fled in all directions,
like elephants being burned when engulfed by flames of fire.
In that battle <s>Rāvaṇa</s> scattered the armies of the leaping monkeys with arrows,

children.text: sa yayau samare tasmin vidhaman rāvaṇaḥ śaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: as the wind scatters great clouds.
Having swiftly made a slaughter of the forest-dwellers,
the lord of rākṣasas then hurriedly approached <s>Rāghava</s> in battle.

children.text: sugrīvastān kapīn dṛṣṭvā bhagnān vidravato raṇe
children.translated_text: Seeing those monkeys broken and fleeing in battle,

children.text: gulme suṣeṇaṃ nikṣipya cakre yuddhe drutaṃ manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s>, after stationing <s>Suṣeṇa</s> in the troop, quickly set his mind on battle.

children.text: ātmanaḥ sadṛśaṃ vīraṃ sa taṃ nikṣipya vānaram
children.translated_text: Having stationed that heroic vānara, equal to himself,
<s>Sugrīva</s>, facing the enemy, advanced with a tree as his weapon.
At his sides and behind him, all the troop-leaders themselves
carried along great rocks and various huge trees.

children.text: sa nadan yudhi sugrīvaḥ svareṇa mahatā mahān
children.translated_text: Mighty <s>Sugrīva</s>, great in battle, roaring with a mighty voice,
struck down various others and slew the foremost rākṣasas.
The lord of the vānaras, huge-bodied, crushed the rākṣasas,
as the wind at the end of an age crushes full-grown trees.
Upon the armies of the rākṣasas he rained a shower of rocks,
as a cloud rains a shower of stones upon flocks of birds in the forest.
By those showers of rocks released by the king of the monkeys, the rākṣasas,
their heads shattered, fell like mountains cut down.
Then, when the rākṣasas were being destroyed on every side,
broken by <s>Sugrīva</s>, falling and roaring aloud,

children.text: virūpākṣaḥ svakaṃ nāma dhanvī viśrāvya rākṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: the rākṣasa <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, a bowman, proclaiming his own name,
unassailable, leapt from his chariot and mounted the shoulder of an elephant.

children.text: sa taṃ dviradam āruhya virūpākṣo mahārathaḥ
children.translated_text: Having mounted that elephant, <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, the great chariot-warrior,
rushed upon the vānaras, shouting with a terrible roar.

children.text: sugrīve sa śarān ghorān visasarja camūmukhe
children.translated_text: At the head of the army he discharged dreadful arrows at <s>Sugrīva</s>,
and he steadied the frightened rākṣasas, gladdening them.
Deeply pierced by sharp arrows from that rākṣasa, the lord of the monkeys

children.text: cukrodha ca mahākrodho vadhe cāsya mano dadhe ||
children.translated_text: became furious, and in great anger set his mind on killing him.

children.text: tataḥ pādapam uddhṛtya śūraḥ saṃpradhane hariḥ
children.translated_text: Then the heroic vānara, pulling up a tree in the battle,
rushed forward and struck that great elephant on the front of its face.
That great elephant, struck by <s>Sugrīva</s>'s blow,
moved back the length of a bow, sank down, and bellowed.

children.text: gajāt tu mathitāt tūrṇam apakramya sa vīryavān
children.translated_text: Quickly stepping away from the battered elephant, that powerful
rākṣasa went forward to meet his enemy, the monkey, face to face.
Taking up a bull-hide shield and a sword, swift in movement,
he approached <s>Sugrīva</s>, who stood firm, as if threatening him.

children.text: sa hi tasyābhisaṃkruddhaḥ pragṛhya mahatīṃ śilām
children.translated_text: Enraged at him, that vānara <s>Sugrīva</s> seized a great rock,
cloud-like, and hurled it at <s>Virūpākṣa</s>.

children.text: sa tāṃ śilām āpatantīṃ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasapuṃgavaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that rock falling upon him, the chief of the rākṣasas,
very valiant, stepped aside and then struck with his sword.
Angry, with that sword, in front of the army, he made <s>Sugrīva</s>'s
armor fall; struck by the sword, <s>Sugrīva</s> fell down.
Having fallen, the monkey rose up and launched at him
a palm-blow, equal to a thunderbolt, with a terrible sound.
That rākṣasa, by skill, escaped the palm-blow
raised by <s>Sugrīva</s>, and struck him on the chest with his fist.
Then <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the vānaras, became still more enraged,

children.text: mokṣitaṃ cātmano dṛṣṭvā prahāraṃ tena rakṣasā ||
children.translated_text: when he saw that his own blow had been evaded by that rākṣasa.
The vānara saw an opening in that <s>Virūpākṣa</s>,
and then, in anger, brought down a great palm-blow on the region of his temple.
Struck to the ground by that palm, like <s>Mahendra</s>'s thunderbolt,
he fell, soaked with blood and vomiting blood.
With his eyes rolled wide from rage, drenched with foaming blood,
they saw <s>Virūpākṣa</s> made still more hideous-eyed.
The monkeys saw their enemy twitching, rolling on his side, smeared with blood,

children.text: karuṇaṃ ca vinardantaṃ dadṛśuḥ kapayo ripum ||
children.translated_text: and roaring piteously.

children.text: tathā tu tau saṃyati samprayuktau tarasvinau vānararākṣasānām
children.translated_text: Thus those two, energetic warriors of the vānaras and rākṣasas, joined in combat,

children.text: balārṇavau sasvanatuḥ sabhīmaṃ mahārṇavau dvāviva bhinnavelau ||
children.translated_text: and the two oceans of armies roared terribly, like two great oceans whose shores had burst.

children.text: vināśitaṃ prekṣya virūpanetraṃ mahābalaṃ taṃ haripārthivena
children.translated_text: Seeing that mighty <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, the misshapen-eyed one, destroyed by the monkey king,
the whole army of monkeys and rākṣasas became like the maddened <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

children.text: hanyamāne bale tūrṇam anyonyaṃ te mahāmṛdhe
children.translated_text: As the forces in that great battle were swiftly killing one another,
the two armies became greatly diminished, like lakes in the great heat.
Because of the ruin of his own army and the killing of <s>Virūpākṣa</s>,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas, became twice as angry.

children.text: prakṣīṇaṃ tu balaṃ dṛṣṭvā vadhyamānaṃ valīmukhaiḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing his army wasted and being slain by the monkey-faced ones,
he felt distress in the battle, perceiving the reversal of fate.
And he spoke to <s>Mahodara</s>, the subduer of enemies, who stood nearby:

children.text: asmin kāle mahābāho jayāśā tvayi me sthitā ||
children.translated_text: At this time, mighty-armed one, my hope of victory rests in you.
Slay the enemy army, hero; show your prowess today.
This is the time to repay your lord's bread; let the good fight well.
Thus addressed, <s>Mahodara</s> said, 'So be it,' to the lord of the rākṣasas,
and entered the enemy army like a moth entering fire.

children.text: tataḥ sa kadanaṃ cakre vānarāṇāṃ mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the greatly powerful one wrought slaughter among the vānaras,
the fiery warrior urged on by his lord's command and by his own valor.
Seeing the great army of the vānaras broken in battle,
<s>Sugrīva</s> at once rushed upon <s>Mahodara</s>.
Seizing a broad, terrible rock, equal to a mountain,
the mighty lord of the monkeys hurled it in order to kill him.

children.text: tām āpatantīṃ sahasā śilāṃ dṛṣṭvā mahodaraḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that rock suddenly falling upon him, <s>Mahodara</s>,
unconfused, then pierced that unassailable rock with arrows.

children.text: rakṣasā tena bāṇaughair nikṛttā sā sahasradhā
children.translated_text: Cut apart by that rākṣasa with torrents of arrows, that rock
fell to the ground in a thousand pieces, like a confused circle of vultures.

children.text: tāṃ tu bhinnāṃ śilāṃ dṛṣṭvā sugrīvaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ
children.translated_text: But seeing that boulder split apart, <s>Sugrīva</s>, overcome with anger,
uprooted a sāla tree and hurled it at the rākṣasa in the forefront of battle.
And the brave conqueror of enemy cities tore him with arrows.

children.text: sa dadarśa tataḥ kruddhaḥ parighaṃ patitaṃ bhuvi
children.translated_text: Then, enraged, he saw an iron club lying on the ground.

children.text: āvidhya tu sa taṃ dīptaṃ parighaṃ tasya darśayan
children.translated_text: Whirling that blazing iron club and displaying it to him,
with the tip of the club he struck down his excellent horses with speed.
From that great chariot whose horses had been slain, the hero leapt down,
and then <s>Mahodara</s>, the rākṣasa, enraged, seized a mace.
Those two heroes, one with mace and one with iron club in hand, met in battle,
roaring like bulls, like two clouds filled with lightning.
The lord of the monkeys struck his mace with the iron club,
and his iron club, broken by the mace, fell to the ground.
Then the radiant <s>Sugrīva</s> took up from the surface of the earth
a terrible iron pestle, adorned with gold on every side.

children.text: taṃ samudyamya cikṣepa so 'pyanyāṃ vyākṣipad gadām
children.translated_text: Raising it up, he hurled it, and he too flung another mace.
Broken when they met one another, the two weapons fell on the ground.
Then, their weapons shattered, the two met with their fists,
filled with energy and strength, blazing like two sacrificial fires.
At that time they struck each other and roared again and again.
And after striking one another with their palms, they fell on the ground.
Then they sprang up quickly and struck each other again.
The two unconquered heroes also threw one another with their arms.
Then the rākṣasa <s>Mahodara</s>, of great speed, took up a sword
lying not far away, together with a shield.

children.text: tathaiva ca mahākhaḍgaṃ carmaṇā patitaṃ saha
children.translated_text: In the same way <s>Sugrīva</s>, best of vānaras, even swifter,
seized a great sword that had fallen together with a shield.
With their bodies enveloped by rage, the two ran at each other roaring,
delighted in combat, their swords raised, both skilled in weapons in battle.

children.text: dakṣiṇaṃ maṇḍalaṃ cobhau tau tūrṇaṃ saṃparīyatuḥ
children.translated_text: Both of them quickly circled to the right in a mandala movement,
furious at one another and both intent on victory.

children.text: sa tu śūro mahāvego vīryaślāghī mahodaraḥ
children.translated_text: But the heroic, very swift <s>Mahodara</s>, proud of his valor,
evil-minded, brought that sword down upon the great shield.
As he was drawing out the stuck sword, the elephant among monkeys, with his own sword,
took off his head, together with its helmet and adorned with earrings.
Seeing him lying on the ground with his head cut off,

children.text: tad balaṃ rākṣasendrasya dṛṣṭvā tatra na tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: the army of the lord of rākṣasas did not remain there.

children.text: hatvā taṃ vānaraiḥ sārdhaṃ nanāda mudito hariḥ
children.translated_text: Having slain him, the monkey roared joyfully together with the vānaras.

children.text: cukrodha ca daśagrīvo babhau hṛṣṭaśca rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Daśagrīva</s> became angry, while <s>Rāghava</s> shone with delight.
When <s>Mahodara</s> had been killed, mighty <s>Mahāpārśva</s>, great in strength,
shook the terrible army of <s>Aṅgada</s> with arrows.
He made the heads of the foremost vānaras on every side
fall from their bodies, as the wind makes fruit fall from its stalk.
With arrows the rākṣasa cut off the arms and shoulders of some;
greatly enraged, he tore open the sides of some vānaras.
Afflicted by the shower of arrows from <s>Mahāpārśva</s>, those vānaras
all became despondent, turned away, and bereft of sense.
Seeing the army agitated and tormented by the rākṣasa,

children.text: vegaṃ cakre mahābāhuḥ samudra iva parvaṇi ||
children.translated_text: mighty-armed <s>Aṅgada</s> surged forward like the ocean at the lunar change.
Taking up an iron club whose radiance was equal to the rays of the sun,
the best of vānaras brought it down upon <s>Mahāpārśva</s> in battle.

children.text: sa tu tena prahāreṇa mahāpārśvo vicetanaḥ
children.translated_text: By that blow <s>Mahāpārśva</s> lost consciousness,

children.text: sasūtaḥ syandanāt tasmād visaṃjñaḥ prāpatad bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: and, together with his charioteer, fell senseless from that chariot to the ground.
But the radiant king of bears, resembling a mass of dark collyrium,
of very great valor, sprang out from his own troop, which was like a cloud.

children.text: pragṛhya giriśṛṅgābhāṃ kruddhaḥ sa vipulāṃ śilām
children.translated_text: Enraged, seizing a great rock like a mountain peak,

children.text: aśvāñ jaghāna tarasā syandanaṃ ca babhañja tam ||
children.translated_text: he swiftly killed the horses and shattered that chariot.
But after a moment mighty <s>Mahāpārśva</s>, great in strength, regained consciousness,
and again pierced <s>Aṅgada</s> with many arrows.
He struck <s>Jāmbavān</s> in the chest with three arrows,

children.text: ṛkṣarājaṃ gavākṣaṃ ca jaghāna bahubhiḥ śaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and he struck the king of bears and <s>Gavākṣa</s> with many arrows.

children.text: gavākṣaṃ jāmbavantaṃ ca sa dṛṣṭvā śarapīḍitau
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Gavākṣa</s> and <s>Jāmbavān</s> tormented by arrows,
<s>Aṅgada</s>, overcome with anger, seized a terrible iron club.
Enraged, <s>Aṅgada</s> took up that iron club
of the rākṣasa standing far away, shining like the rays of the sun.

children.text: dvābhyāṃ bhujābhyāṃ saṃgṛhya bhrāmayitvā ca vegavān
children.translated_text: Grasping it with both arms and whirling it, the swift one,
<s>Vāli</s>'s son, hurled it at <s>Mahāpārśva</s> in order to kill him.

children.text: sa tu kṣipto balavatā parighastasya rakṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: That club, hurled by the strong one at the rākṣasa,
knocked from his hand his bow with its arrows, and also his helmet.
Reaching him swiftly, the powerful son of <s>Vāli</s>,
in anger struck him with his palm at the root of the ear, together with the earring.

children.text: sa tu kruddho mahāvego mahāpārśvo mahādyutiḥ
children.translated_text: But the angry, very swift, greatly radiant <s>Mahāpārśva</s>
seized with one hand a very great battle-axe.
Oil-washed, spotless, firm, and made of the essence of the mountain,
the intensely enraged rākṣasa brought it down upon <s>Vāli</s>'s son.
When that battle-axe had fallen heavily upon his left shoulder-blade,
<s>Aṅgada</s>, enraged, freed himself from it.

children.text: sa vīro vajrasaṃkāśam aṅgado muṣṭim ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: That hero <s>Aṅgada</s>, whose fist was like a thunderbolt,
rolling up his own fist, greatly enraged and equal to his father in valor,
knowing the vital points, aimed at the rākṣasa's heart near his breast
and brought down that fist, whose touch was like <s>Indra</s>'s thunderbolt.
By the fall of that blow, in the great battle,

children.text: paphāla hṛdayaṃ cāśu sa papāta hato bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: the rākṣasa's heart quickly burst, and he fell to the ground slain.
When he had fallen upon the earth, that army was thrown into confusion,

children.text: abhavacca mahān krodhaḥ samare rāvaṇasya tu ||
children.translated_text: and in the battle great anger arose in <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Seeing the two rākṣasas <s>Mahodara</s> and <s>Mahāpārśva</s> slain,
and that heroic, mighty <s>Virūpākṣa</s> also killed,

children.text: āviveśa mahān krodho rāvaṇaṃ tu mahāmṛdhe
children.translated_text: great anger entered <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in the great battle,

children.text: sūtaṃ saṃcodayāmāsa vākyaṃ cedam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: and he urged on his charioteer and spoke these words:
For my ministers who have been slain and for the city that is besieged,
I shall remove this grief by killing those two, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
In battle I shall cut down the tree that is <s>Rāma</s>, bearing <s>Sītā</s> as flower and fruit,

children.text: praśākhā yasya sugrīvo jāmbavān kumudo nalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whose spreading branches are <s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>Jāmbavān</s>, <s>Kumuda</s>, and <s>Nala</s>.

children.text: sa diśo daśa ghoṣeṇa rathasyātiratho mahān
children.translated_text: Then the great chariot-warrior, with the roar of his chariot
making the ten directions resound, quickly set out and advanced upon <s>Rāghava</s>.
Filled with that sound, together with its rivers, mountains, and forests,
the whole earth shook, with its boars, deer, and elephants.
He employed a very terrible and exceedingly dreadful tāmasa weapon;
it burned up all the monkeys, and they fell on every side.
Seeing the many armies shattered by hundreds
by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s excellent arrows, <s>Rāghava</s> stood firm.

children.text: sa dadarśa tato rāmaṃ tiṣṭhantam aparājitam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s> saw <s>Rāma</s> standing undefeated,

children.text: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā viṣṇunā vāsavaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: together with his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, like <s>Vāsava</s> with <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
He seemed to be drawing lines upon the sky as he held his great bow,
wide-eyed like lotus petals, long-armed, and a subduer of enemies.

children.text: vānarāṃśca raṇe bhagnān āpatantaṃ ca rāvaṇam
children.translated_text: Seeing the vānaras broken in battle and <s>Rāvaṇa</s> rushing on,

children.text: samīkṣya rāghavo hṛṣṭo madhye jagrāha kārmukam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s>, rejoicing, took up his bow in their midst.

children.text: visphārayitum ārebhe tataḥ sa dhanur uttamam
children.translated_text: Then he began to draw that excellent bow,
mighty in force and loud in sound, as though splitting the earth.
Entering the arrow-range of the two princes,

children.text: sa babhūva yathā rāhuḥ samīpe śaśisūryayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s> became like <s>Rāhu</s> near the moon and the sun.
Then, by the floods of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s arrows and by the sound
made by <s>Rāma</s>'s drawn bow, rākṣasas fell by hundreds.

children.text: tam icchan prathamaṃ yoddhuṃ lakṣmaṇo niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
children.translated_text: Wishing to fight him first, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, drawing his bow,
released sharp arrows like tongues of fire.
As soon as those arrows had been released into the sky by bow-bearing <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
the greatly radiant <s>Rāvaṇa</s> warded off the arrows with arrows.

children.text: ekam ekena bāṇena tribhistrīn daśabhir daśa
children.translated_text: One with one arrow, three with three, and ten with ten,
he cut off <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s shafts, displaying the lightness of his hand.
Passing beyond <s>Saumitri</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, victorious in battle,

children.text: āsasāda tato rāmaṃ sthitaṃ śailam ivācalam ||
children.translated_text: then approached <s>Rāma</s>, who stood unmoving like a mountain.
Reaching <s>Rāma</s> in battle, his eyes reddened with anger,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> poured showers of arrows upon <s>Rāghava</s>.
When <s>Rāma</s> saw the streams of arrows loosed from <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s bow
falling swiftly, he quickly took up crescent-headed shafts.
Then with sharp bhallas <s>Rāghava</s> cut apart those masses of arrows,
blazing, very swift, like enraged venomous serpents.

children.text: rāghavo rāvaṇaṃ tūrṇaṃ rāvaṇo rāghavaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> swiftly showered <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, and <s>Rāvaṇa</s> likewise showered <s>Rāghava</s>,
each covering the other with various sharp arrows.
For a long time the two moved in a wondrous circle, to left and right,
watching the speed of the arrows, both undefeated in battles.
Creatures trembled as the two fought at the same time,
terrible, releasing missiles, resembling <s>Yama</s> and <s>Antaka</s>.

children.text: saṃtataṃ vividhair bāṇair babhūva gaganaṃ tadā
children.translated_text: Then the sky became continuously filled with various arrows,
like clouds at the end of the heat, tangled with garlands of lightning.
The sky seemed latticed by showers of arrows,
very swift, with extremely sharp points, well-feathered with vulture plumes.

children.text: śarāndhakāraṃ tau bhīmaṃ cakratuḥ paramaṃ tadā
children.translated_text: Then those two made a supreme and dreadful darkness of arrows,
like two great clouds risen even after the sun had set.
A tumultuous battle arose between the two, each desiring the other's death,
unapproachable and inconceivable, like that of <s>Vṛtra</s> and <s>Vāsava</s>.
For both were supreme archers, both skilled in weapons,
both foremost among those who know missiles, and both moved about in battle.

children.text: ubhau hi yena vrajatastena tena śarormayaḥ
children.translated_text: Whichever way the two went, that same way the waves of arrows

children.text: ūrmayo vāyunā viddhā jagmuḥ sāgarayor iva ||
children.translated_text: went, like waves of two oceans driven by the wind.
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, who made the worlds cry out, his hand joined to his bowstring,
sent a garland of iron arrows against <s>Rāma</s>'s forehead.
Though that garland, discharged from the terrible bow, had the gleam of blue lotus petals,

children.text: śirasā dhārayan rāmo na vyathāṃ pratyapadyata ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> bore it upon his head and did not feel distress.

children.text: atha mantrān api japan raudram astram udīrayan
children.translated_text: Then, reciting mantras and raising the terrible missile,
<s>Rāma</s>, filled with anger, again took up arrows.
The greatly radiant and heroic one released them, drawing his bow,
and, his own shafts unbroken, hurled those arrows at the lord of rākṣasas.
Those arrows fell upon the armor of the lord of rākṣasas,
which was like a great cloud and invulnerable, and at that time they caused no distress.

children.text: punar evātha taṃ rāmo rathasthaṃ rākṣasādhipam
children.translated_text: Then again <s>Rāma</s>, skilled in every weapon, struck that lord of rākṣasas,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, as he stood in his chariot, on the forehead with a supreme missile.
Those arrows, having split apart into arrow-forms, like five-headed serpents,
hissing, entered the earth, having been thwarted by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
After destroying <s>Rāghava</s>'s weapon, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, overwhelmed by anger,
took up another weapon, an asura missile, very great and terrible.
He released sharp arrows, some with the faces of lions and tigers, and others with the faces of herons and crows,
and with the faces of vultures and hawks, and likewise with the faces of jackals;
others with the faces of wolves, with mouths gaping, frightening,
and five-mouthed ones licking with their tongues.
He released other arrows with the faces of asses, and some formed with boar-faces,
and others with the mouths of dogs and cocks, and the faces of makaras and venomous serpents.
These and many others, with his powers of illusion, the great-radiant one sent forth as sharp arrows,

children.text: rāmaṃ prati mahātejāḥ kruddhaḥ sarpa iva śvasan ||
children.translated_text: against <s>Rāma</s>, angry and hissing like a serpent.
Assailed by that asura weapon, the descendant of <s>Raghu</s>,
of great energy and like fire itself, released a fiery weapon.
He released sharp arrows with faces blazing like fire, and also with faces like the sun,
with faces like the moon and the half-moon, and with faces like comets,
colored like planets and stars, and shaped with faces like great meteors,
and others like lightning-tongues.
Those terrible arrows of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, struck by <s>Rāghava</s>'s weapon,
perished in the sky and went away by the thousands.
Seeing that weapon destroyed by <s>Rāma</s>, whose action is unwearied,
all the shape-shifting vānaras then joyfully roared.
But when that weapon had been repelled, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas,

children.text: krodhaṃ ca dviguṇaṃ cakre krodhāccāstram anantaram ||
children.translated_text: doubled his anger, and from anger took up another weapon after it.

children.text: mayena vihitaṃ raudram anyad astraṃ mahādyutiḥ
children.translated_text: The greatly radiant <s>Rāvaṇa</s> began to discharge against <s>Rāghava</s>
another terrible weapon, a fierce one fashioned by <s>Maya</s>.

children.text: tataḥ śūlāni niścerur gadāśca musalāni ca
children.translated_text: Then spears, maces, and pestles issued forth
from his bow, blazing on all sides and hard as thunderbolts.
Clubs, hammers, nooses, and blazing thunderbolts as well
flew out, various and sharp, like winds at the destruction of an age.

children.text: tad astraṃ rāghavaḥ śrīmān uttamāstravidāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: But glorious <s>Rāghava</s>, the radiant best of those who know the highest weapons,
struck down that weapon with a supreme Gandharva missile.
