When that weapon had been repelled by great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, his eyes red with anger, sent forth a solar weapon.
Then great shining disks flew forth
from the bow of wise <s>Daśagrīva</s>, whose speed was dreadful.

children.text: tair āsīd gaganaṃ dīptaṃ saṃpatadbhir itastataḥ
children.translated_text: The sky was lit by them as they rushed together here and there,
and the quarters were bright with them as they fell, like moons, suns, and planets.

children.text: tāni cicheda bāṇaughaiścakrāṇi tu sa rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: But that <s>Rāghava</s> cut apart those disks with streams of arrows,
those wondrous weapons of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, before the army.

children.text: tad astraṃ tu hataṃ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that weapon destroyed, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas,

children.text: vivyādha daśabhir bāṇai rāmaṃ sarveṣu marmasu ||
children.translated_text: pierced <s>Rāma</s> in all his vital points with ten arrows.
Pierced by ten arrows shot from the great bow
by the very radiant <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, <s>Rāghava</s> did not tremble.
Then <s>Rāghava</s>, conqueror in battle, greatly enraged,
pierced <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in every limb with many arrows.
At that moment <s>Rāghava</s>'s strong younger brother, angered,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, slayer of enemy heroes, took up seven arrows.
With those very swift arrows, the greatly radiant <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>

children.text: dhvajaṃ manuṣyaśīrṣaṃ tu tasya cicheda naikadhā ||
children.translated_text: cut <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s human-headed banner into many pieces.
And with an arrow glorious, mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>
took off the charioteer's head, blazing with earrings, from the powerful rākṣasa.
With his arrows <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> also cut apart the bow of the lord of rākṣasas,
which was like an elephant's trunk, with five sharp arrows.
And <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, leaping up with his mace, killed <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s excellent horses,
dark as blue clouds and like mountains.
Swift <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, from his horseless chariot, quickly sprang down from that great car

children.text: krodham āhārayat tīvraṃ bhrātaraṃ prati rāvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and directed fierce anger toward his brother.

children.text: tataḥ śaktiṃ mahāśaktir dīptāṃ dīptāśanīm iva
children.translated_text: Then the powerful, majestic lord of rākṣasas hurled at <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>
a spear, blazing like a flaming thunderbolt.
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> cut that spear apart with three arrows before it reached him,
and then a shout arose among the vānaras in the battle.

children.text: sā papāta tridhā chinnā śaktiḥ kāñcanamālinī
children.translated_text: That gold-wreathed spear, cut into three pieces, fell,
blazing and sending out sparks, like a great meteor fallen from heaven.
Then he took up a broad spear, still more formidable,
hard to withstand even for <s>Kāla</s>, blazing with its own brilliance.
That spear, held by swift, powerful, evil-minded <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
blazed, exceedingly terrible, equal in splendor to <s>Śakra</s>'s thunderbolt.
At that moment the heroic <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> quickly went up to that <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,
who had fallen into peril of his life.
To free him, heroic <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> drew his bow
and showered that <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, spear in hand, with torrents of arrows.
Covered by the flood of arrows released by the great-souled one,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> did not set his mind on striking, his valor turned away.

children.text: mokṣitaṃ bhrātaraṃ dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇena sa rāvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing his brother freed by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, that <s>Rāvaṇa</s>
Standing facing <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, he spoke these words:
Since, boaster of strength, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> has been released by you in this way,
this <s>śakti</s> (spear), sparing the rākṣasa, is being hurled down upon you.

children.text: eṣā te hṛdayaṃ bhittvā śaktir lohitalakṣaṇā
children.translated_text: This blood-marked <s>śakti</s> will pierce your heart,
and, released from the iron bar of my arm, will go off taking your life-breaths.

children.text: ityevam uktvā tāṃ śaktim aṣṭaghaṇṭāṃ mahāsvanām
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, he took that <s>śakti</s>, fitted with eight bells and making a great sound,
fashioned by <s>Maya</s> through magic, unfailing, and slaying enemies,
and, aiming it at <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, blazing as if with splendor,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, exceedingly enraged, hurled it and roared.
Hurled with dreadful speed and sounding like <s>Śakra</s>'s thunderbolt,
the <s>śakti</s> rushed swiftly upon <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> at the head of the battle.
<s>Rāghava</s> addressed that falling <s>śakti</s> as it came on:
'May there be welfare for <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>; become fruitless, your undertaking destroyed.'
With great speed it fell upon <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s broad chest,
shining with great brilliance like the tongue of the king of serpents.
Then, by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s force, with it sunk very far in,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, his heart pierced by the <s>śakti</s>, fell to the ground.
Seeing <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> in that condition nearby, <s>Rāghava</s>,
greatly radiant, became downcast at heart from brotherly affection.
After reflecting for a moment, his eyes clouded with tears,
he became still more enraged, like fire at the end of an age.

children.text: na viṣādasya kālo 'yam iti saṃcintya rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Thinking, 'This is not the time for despair,' <s>Rāghava</s>

children.text: cakre sutumulaṃ yuddhaṃ rāvaṇasya vadhe dhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: made a very tumultuous battle, resolved on the killing of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: sa dadarśa tato rāmaḥ śaktyā bhinnaṃ mahāhave
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s> saw <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, pierced by the <s>śakti</s> in the great battle,
smeared with blood, like a mountain with a serpent upon it.

children.text: tām api prahitāṃ śaktiṃ rāvaṇena balīyasā
children.translated_text: Even that <s>śakti</s>, sent forth by mighty <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
the best of the monkeys, despite their effort, were not able to crush,
for they were being battered by streams of arrows from the quick-handed rākṣasa.
Having pierced <s>Saumitri</s>, it entered the surface of the earth.

children.text: tāṃ karābhyāṃ parāmṛśya rāmaḥ śaktiṃ bhayāvahām
children.translated_text: Taking hold with both hands of that terrifying <s>śakti</s>,

children.text: babhañja samare kruddho balavad vicakarṣa ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, enraged in battle, broke it and forcefully drew it out.
As he was drawing out the <s>śakti</s>, mighty <s>Rāvaṇa</s>
sent arrows onto all his limbs, piercing the vital points.

children.text: acintayitvā tān bāṇān samāśliṣya ca lakṣmaṇam
children.translated_text: Paying no heed to those arrows and embracing <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
<s>Rāghava</s> spoke to <s>Hanūmant</s> and also to <s>Sugrīva</s>:
'Stand here, best of vānaras, surrounding <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
The time for my valor, long desired, has now arrived.
This evil-souled <s>Daśagrīva</s>, fixed in evil, must be slain,
like the sight of a cloud at summer's end for a thirsty cātaka.
At this very moment, before long, I truly promise you:

children.text: arāvaṇam arāmaṃ vā jagad drakṣyatha vānarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: O vānaras, you will see the world either without <s>Rāvaṇa</s> or without <s>Rāma</s>.
The loss of my kingdom, the dwelling in the forest, the roaming through <s>Daṇḍaka</s>,
the laying of hands upon <s>Vaidehī</s>, and the encounter with the rākṣasas,

children.text: prāptaṃ duḥkhaṃ mahad ghoraṃ kleśaṃ ca nirayopamam
children.translated_text: the great, terrible sorrow I have undergone, and the torment like hell,

children.text: adya sarvam ahaṃ tyakṣye hatvā taṃ rāvaṇaṃ raṇe ||
children.translated_text: today I shall cast all of it away by killing that <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle.

children.text: yadarthaṃ vānaraṃ sainyaṃ samānītam idaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: For the sake of which I assembled this army of vānaras,

children.text: sugrīvaśca kṛto rājye nihatvā vālinaṃ raṇe ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Sugrīva</s> was established in the kingdom after I killed <s>Vālin</s> in battle,

children.text: yadarthaṃ sāgaraḥ krāntaḥ setur baddhaśca sāgare
children.translated_text: for the sake of which the ocean was crossed and a bridge was built in the sea,
that sinner has today come within range of my eyes in battle.
Having come within range of my eyes, this one does not deserve to live,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> being to me like one who has met the gaze of a sight-poisoning serpent.
Watch calmly, unconquerable bulls among vānaras,
seated on the mountain peaks, this battle of mine and <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s.

children.text: adya rāmasya rāmatvaṃ paśyantu mama saṃyuge
children.translated_text: Today, in combat, let them see <s>Rāma</s>'s very Rāma-ness in me:
the three worlds, with Gandharvas, with gods, with seers and Cāraṇas.
Today I shall do a deed which the worlds, moving and unmoving,
together with the gods, will tell of as long as the earth endures.'
Having spoken thus, with sharp arrows adorned with heated gold,
<s>Rāma</s>, composed in battle, struck <s>Daśagrīva</s>.
Then with blazing iron arrows, and also with clubs, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>

children.text: abhyavarṣat tadā rāmaṃ dhārābhir iva toyadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: showered <s>Rāma</s> then, like a rain-cloud with streams of water.
Of the arrows released by <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, striking one another,

children.text: śarāṇāṃ ca śarāṇāṃ ca babhūva tumulaḥ svanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: of arrows against arrows, there arose a tumultuous sound.
Those arrows of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, split and scattered,
fell from the sky to the surface of the earth, their tips blazing.
The great twang of bowstrings and slap of palms from <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s>
became terrifying to all beings and wondrous in appearance.
Being covered with showers of nets of arrows and harried by the great-souled one with blazing bow,

children.text: bhayāt pradudrāva sametya rāvaṇo yathānilenābhihato balāhakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, having confronted him, fled in fear, like a cloud struck by the wind.

children.text: sa dattvā tumulaṃ yuddhaṃ rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: After giving dreadful battle to evil-minded <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: visṛjan eva bāṇaughān suṣeṇaṃ vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: while still releasing streams of arrows, he spoke these words to <s>Suṣeṇa</s>:
'This <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, struck by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s force, has fallen on the ground.

children.text: sarpavad veṣṭate vīro mama śokam udīrayan ||
children.translated_text: The hero writhes like a serpent, heightening my grief.

children.text: śoṇitārdram imaṃ vīraṃ prāṇair iṣṭataraṃ mama
children.translated_text: While I look upon this hero, wet with blood and dearer to me than life,

children.text: paśyato mama kā śaktir yoddhuṃ paryākulātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: what power have I to fight, with my self thrown into confusion?

children.text: ayaṃ sa samaraślāghī bhrātā me śubhalakṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: This is that brother of mine, praised in battle and marked with auspicious signs,

children.text: yadi pañcatvam āpannaḥ prāṇair me kiṃ sukhena vā ||
children.translated_text: If he has met death, what use are my life-breaths to me, or happiness?

children.text: lajjatīva hi me vīryaṃ bhraśyatīva karād dhanuḥ
children.translated_text: My valor seems ashamed, and my bow seems to slip from my hand.
My arrows sink down, and my sight has come under the sway of tears.

children.text: cintā me vardhate tīvrā mumūrṣā copajāyate ||
children.translated_text: My sharp anxiety grows, and a desire to die arises in me.
Seeing his brother struck down by evil-minded <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
he fell into the deepest despair and wailed, his senses overcome.

children.text: na hi yuddhena me kāryaṃ naiva prāṇair na sītayā
children.translated_text: I have no purpose in battle, nor indeed in life, nor in <s>Sītā</s>,
after seeing my brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> struck down in the dust of battle.

children.text: kiṃ me rājyena kiṃ prāṇair yuddhe kāryaṃ na vidyate
children.translated_text: What is kingship to me? What are my life-breaths? I have no purpose in battle,
when this <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> lies slain on the front of the battlefield.

children.text: rāmam āśvāsayan vīraḥ suṣeṇo vākyam abravīt
children.translated_text: Consoling <s>Rāma</s>, the heroic <s>Suṣeṇa</s> spoke these words:
This mighty-armed <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, increaser of good fortune, is not dead.

children.text: na cāsya vikṛtaṃ vaktraṃ nāpi śyāmaṃ na niṣprabham
children.translated_text: His face is not altered, nor is it dark, nor without luster.

children.text: suprabhaṃ ca prasannaṃ ca mukham asyābhilakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: His face is seen to be bright and clear.
His hands have palms red as lotuses, and his eyes are very clear.

children.text: evaṃ na vidyate rūpaṃ gatāsūnāṃ viśāṃ pate
children.translated_text: Such an appearance is not found in those whose life-breaths have departed, O lord of men.

children.text: mā viṣādaṃ kṛtvā vīra saprāṇo 'yam ariṃdama ||
children.translated_text: Do not fall into grief, hero; this subduer of foes is alive.
Of him lying on the ground as though asleep, with limbs slackened,

children.text: socchvāsaṃ hṛdayaṃ vīra kampamānaṃ muhur muhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the heart is known, O hero, to be breathing and trembling again and again.

children.text: evam uktvā tu vākyajñaḥ suṣeṇo rāghavaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken these words, <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, who knew how to speak,
then hurriedly said this to <s>Hanūmant</s>, who was standing nearby:

children.text: saumya śīghram ito gatvā śailam oṣadhiparvatam
children.translated_text: Gentle one, go quickly from here to the mountain, the herb-bearing peak,

children.text: pūrvaṃ hi kathito yo 'sau vīra jāmbavatā śubhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that auspicious one which, hero, was previously described by <s>Jāmbavān</s>.

children.text: dakṣiṇe śikhare tasya jātām oṣadhim ānaya
children.translated_text: Bring the herb born on its southern summit,
the auspicious <s>Viśalyakaraṇī</s> by name, the remover of darts.
And also <s>Sauvarṇakaraṇī</s>, and likewise <s>Saṃjīvanī</s>,
and <s>Saṃdhānakaraṇī</s> too; go and bring them here quickly,
for the reviving of noble, heroic <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Thus addressed, <s>Hanumān</s> went to the mountain of herbs,
but the glorious one became anxious, not recognizing those great herbs.
Then a thought arose in the son of the Wind, of boundless might:

children.text: idam eva gamiṣyāmi gṛhītvā śikharaṃ gireḥ ||
children.translated_text: I will go back carrying this very peak of the mountain.
If I go without taking <s>Viśalyakaraṇī</s>,

children.text: kālātyayena doṣaḥ syād vaiklavyaṃ ca mahad bhavet ||
children.translated_text: there will be harm from the loss of time, and great distress would result.

children.text: iti saṃcintya hanumān gatvā kṣipraṃ mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: Having thought this through, mighty <s>Hanumān</s> went swiftly,
and <s>Hanumān</s> leapt up, carrying the mountain peak.
I do not recognize the herbs, O foremost of monkeys;

children.text: tad idaṃ śikharaṃ kṛtsnaṃ girestasyāhṛtaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: therefore I have brought this whole peak of that mountain.
As the son of the Wind was saying this, <s>Suṣeṇa</s> praised him,
and <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, best of monkeys, plucked out and took the herbs.
Then the splendid monkey <s>Suṣeṇa</s> crushed that herb,
and placed it at <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s nose, blazing with great radiance.
Though still pierced by the dart, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, slayer of enemy heroes, smelled it,
and, freed from the dart and from pain, quickly rose up from the ground.

children.text: samutthitaṃ te harayo bhūtalāt prekṣya lakṣmaṇam
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> risen from the earth, those monkeys,
greatly delighted, honored <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, saying, 'Well done, well done!'
'Come, come,' said <s>Rāma</s> to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, slayer of enemy heroes,
and he embraced him tightly with affection, his eyes overcome with tears.
Then <s>Rāghava</s>, embracing <s>Saumitri</s>, said:

children.text: diṣṭyā tvāṃ vīra paśyāmi maraṇāt punar āgatam ||
children.translated_text: By good fortune, hero, I see you returned again from death.

children.text: na hi me jīvitenārthaḥ sītayā ca jayena vā
children.translated_text: For I have no purpose in living, nor in <s>Sītā</s>, nor in victory.

children.text: ko hi me jīvitenārthastvayi pañcatvam āgate ||
children.translated_text: What use would life be to me, if you had met death?
As noble <s>Rāghava</s> was speaking in this way,

children.text: khinnaḥ śithilayā vācā lakṣmaṇo vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, weary, spoke these words in a weakened voice:
Having once made that vow, O you whose valor is true,

children.text: laghuḥ kaścid ivāsattvo naivaṃ vaktum ihārhasi ||
children.translated_text: you ought not speak so here, like some light and spiritless man.

children.text: na pratijñāṃ hi kurvanti vitathāṃ sādhavo 'nagha
children.translated_text: For good men, sinless one, do not make a false vow.
Keeping a vow is indeed a great mark of such a man.

children.text: nairāśyam upagantuṃ te tad alaṃ matkṛte 'nagha
children.translated_text: Enough, then, of giving way to despair on my account, sinless one.
Today fulfill your vow by killing <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: na jīvan yāsyate śatrustava bāṇapathaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: The enemy, once he has entered the path of your arrows, will not go away alive,
like a great elephant before a roaring lion with sharp fangs.

children.text: ahaṃ tu vadham icchāmi śīghram asya durātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: But I wish for the quick death of this evil-minded one,

children.text: yāvad astaṃ na yātyeṣa kṛtakarmā divākaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: before this sun, its work done, goes to its setting.

children.text: lakṣmaṇena tu tadvākyam uktaṃ śrutvā sa rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech spoken by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, <s>Rāghava</s>
loosed terrible arrows at <s>Rāvaṇa</s> at the head of the army.
But ten-necked <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, standing on his chariot, struck <s>Rāma</s>
with very dreadful arrows like thunderbolts, as a rain cloud strikes with streams of water.
With arrows like blazing fire and adorned with gold,
focused <s>Rāma</s> pierced ten-necked <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle.
The gods, gandharvas, and dānavas said that the fighting was unequal
between <s>Rāma</s> standing on the ground and the rākṣasa standing on a chariot.
Then, with its body patterned in gold and adorned with hundreds of little bells,
resembling the young sun and having a pole made of vaidūrya gems,
yoked with excellent horses wearing golden head-ornaments and white chowries,
with tawny steeds resembling the sun and adorned with nets of gold,
The splendid, excellent chariot of the king of the gods, with golden shafts and banner,
came near to <s>Kākutstha</s>, having descended from heaven.

children.text: abravīcca tadā rāmaṃ sapratodo rathe sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, standing in the chariot with his goad, he spoke to <s>Rāma</s>;
with joined palms <s>Mātali</s>, the charioteer of the thousand-eyed god, said these words:
"O <s>Kākutstha</s>, this chariot has been given to you by <s>Sahasrākṣa</s> for victory,
O great-hearted one, splendid destroyer of enemies.
Here is the great bow of <s>Indra</s>, and armor shining like fire,
arrows bright as the sun, and a spotless, sharp spear.

children.text: āruhyemaṃ rathaṃ vīra rākṣasaṃ jahi rāvaṇam
children.translated_text: Mount this chariot, hero, and kill the rākṣasa <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: mayā sārathinā rāma mahendra iva dānavān ||
children.translated_text: with me as your charioteer, <s>Rāma</s>, as great <s>Indra</s> slew the dānavas."

children.text: ityuktaḥ sa parikramya rathaṃ tam abhivādya ca
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, he circumambulated that chariot and honored it,
and then <s>Rāma</s> mounted it, illuminating the worlds with his splendor.
Then there arose a marvelous duel between two chariots, making the hair stand on end,

children.text: rāmasya ca mahābāho rāvaṇasya ca rakṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: between mighty-armed <s>Rāma</s> and the rākṣasa <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: sa gāndharveṇa gāndharvaṃ daivaṃ daivena rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s>, supreme knower of missiles, countered the gandharva missile with a gandharva one, and the divine with a divine one,
striking down the weapon of the king of rākṣasas.

children.text: astraṃ tu paramaṃ ghoraṃ rākṣasaṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: But the rākṣasa lord, that night-roamer, extremely enraged,
again discharged a supreme and terrible rākṣasa missile.
Those arrows released from <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s bow, adorned with gold,
came toward <s>Kākutstha</s>, becoming serpents full of deadly poison.

children.text: te dīptavadanā dīptaṃ vamanto jvalanaṃ mukhaiḥ
children.translated_text: With blazing faces, vomiting blazing fire from their mouths,
they came straight at <s>Rāma</s>, fearsome, with gaping jaws.
By those great-poisoned serpents, with the touch of <s>Vāsuki</s> and blazing coils,
all the quarters and intermediate quarters were filled and covered.

children.text: tān dṛṣṭvā pannagān rāmaḥ samāpatata āhave
children.translated_text: Seeing those snakes rushing down upon him in battle, <s>Rāma</s>
brought forth the dreadful and fearsome <s>Garuḍa</s> missile.
Released from <s>Rāghava</s>'s bow, those gold-feathered arrows, bright as fire,
became golden suparṇas, enemies of serpents, and moved about.
Those arrows of <s>Rāma</s>, taking the form of suparṇas and assuming forms at will,
destroyed all those swift arrows that had taken serpent form.
When his missile had been repelled, the rākṣasa lord <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, enraged,
then showered <s>Rāma</s> with terrible rains of arrows.
Then, after tormenting <s>Rāma</s>, whose deeds were unfailing, with a thousand arrows,
he struck <s>Mātali</s> too with a flood of shafts.

children.text: pātayitvā rathopasthe rathāt ketuṃ ca kāñcanam
children.translated_text: After knocking the golden banner down from the top of the chariot,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> struck <s>Indra</s>'s horses with a net of arrows.
The gods and gandharvas, together with dānavas and cāraṇas, became despondent,

children.text: rāmam ārtaṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā siddhāśca paramarṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as did the siddhas and great seers, seeing <s>Rāma</s> then distressed.
The lords of the vānaras, together with <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, were shaken,
seeing moon-like <s>Rāma</s> seized by <s>Rāvaṇa</s> as by <s>Rāhu</s>.

children.text: prājāpatyaṃ ca nakṣatraṃ rohiṇīṃ śaśinaḥ priyām
children.translated_text: <s>Budha</s> stood upon <s>Rohiṇī</s>, the Prajāpati constellation dear to the moon,
bringing misfortune to living beings.
The ocean, its waves rolling with smoke around them, blazing as if aflame,

children.text: utpapāta tadā kruddhaḥ spṛśann iva divākaram ||
children.translated_text: then leapt up in anger, as though touching the sun.
The sun appeared harsh, weapon-colored, and dim-rayed,
its disk like a headless trunk and joined with a comet.
The constellation of the <s>Kosalas</s>, clearly having <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> as its deities,
was occupied by <s>Aṅgāraka</s>, who stood in the sky upon <s>Viśākhā</s>.
Ten-faced, twenty-armed, and holding his bow ready,
<s>Daśagrīva</s> appeared like <s>Maināka</s> mountain.
But <s>Rāma</s>, assailed by the rākṣasa <s>Daśagrīva</s>,
could not set his arrows upon their targets at the front of battle.

children.text: sa kṛtvā bhrukuṭīṃ kruddhaḥ kiṃcit saṃraktalocanaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, knitting his brows in anger, his eyes somewhat reddened,
he passed into immense wrath, as if burning everything with his gaze.

children.text: tasya kruddhasya vadanaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmasya dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing the face of wise <s>Rāma</s> when he was enraged,
all beings trembled, and the earth shook.
The mountain, with its lions and tigers, shook together with its immovable trees,

children.text: babhūva cāpi kṣubhitaḥ samudraḥ saritāṃ patiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the ocean too, lord of rivers, became agitated.
Birds in the sky, with harsh cries and rough voices,
circled all around, shrieking as portents.
Seeing <s>Rāma</s> deeply enraged and the very dreadful portents,
all beings trembled, and fear entered <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Then the gods stationed in aerial cars, the gandharvas, and the great serpents,
the seers, dānavas, daityas, garutmants, and sky-goers,
watched that battle, which stood like the destruction of the worlds,
as the two heroes fought each other with many dreadful weapons.

children.text: ūcuḥ surāsurāḥ sarve tadā vigraham āgatāḥ
children.translated_text: Then all the gods and asuras, arrayed on opposite sides,
watching the great battle, joyfully uttered words with devotion.
The assembled asuras said, "Victory to <s>Daśagrīva</s>!"

children.text: devā rāmam athocuste tvaṃ jayeti punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: while the gods again and again said to <s>Rāma</s>, "May you be victorious!"

children.text: etasminn antare krodhād rāghavasya sa rāvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, out of anger, that wicked-souled <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
wishing to strike <s>Rāghava</s>, touched a great weapon,
hard as a thunderbolt, loud-roaring, and destructive of every enemy,
studded with knobs like mountain peaks and terrifying to behold,
smoky, sharp-pointed, and like a mass of fire at the end of an age,
exceedingly terrible, unassailable, hard even for Time to approach,
frightening to all beings, tearing and splitting them apart.

children.text: pradīpta iva roṣeṇa śūlaṃ jagrāha rāvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, as if blazing with anger, seized a spear.
The very angry, mighty one grasped that spear in its middle,
surrounded in battle by many brave rākṣasas.
Raising it, the huge-bodied one roared dreadfully in battle,
his eyes blood-red from anger, gladdening his own army.
The earth, the mid-air, the quarters, and likewise the intermediate quarters
were shaken then by the dreadful sound of the lord of rākṣasas.
At that roar of the evil-minded one, who roared beyond measure,
all beings trembled, and the ocean was stirred.

children.text: sa gṛhītvā mahāvīryaḥ śūlaṃ tad rāvaṇo mahat
children.translated_text: Then the great-heroic <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, taking up that great spear,
roared a tremendous roar and spoke harshly to <s>Rāma</s>:
This spear, hard as a thunderbolt, has been raised by me in anger, <s>Rāma</s>;
it will at once take the lives of you, together with your brother and helpers.
To the heroic rākṣasas who today have been killed at the head of the army,

children.text: tvāṃ nihatya raṇaślāghin karomi tarasā samam ||
children.translated_text: I shall, after killing you, O boaster in battle, quickly make you equal.

children.text: tiṣṭhedānīṃ nihanmi tvām eṣa śūlena rāghava
children.translated_text: Stand now, <s>Rāghava</s>; I am going to kill you with this spear.

children.text: evam uktvā sa cikṣepa tacchūlaṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the lord of rākṣasas hurled that spear.
<s>Rāghava</s> checked it as it came on with a flood of arrows,
as <s>Vāsava</s> checks a rising end-of-age fire with floods of water.
But <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s great spear burned up those arrows released from <s>Rāma</s>'s bow,
as fire burns up moths.
Seeing those arrows in the air, reduced to ash and crushed by contact with the spear,
<s>Rāghava</s> became angry.
Then <s>Rāghava</s>, delight of the <s>Raghu</s> line, very angry,
took up that śakti (dart), made by <s>Vāsava</s> and brought by <s>Mātali</s>.
That dart, brandished by the mighty one and sounding like bells,
lit up the sky with its radiance like an end-of-age meteor.

children.text: sā kṣiptā rākṣasendrasya tasmiñ śūle papāta ha
children.translated_text: Hurled, it struck that spear of the lord of rākṣasas,
and the great spear, split by the dart, fell down with its brilliance gone.

children.text: nirbibheda tato bāṇair hayān asya mahājavān
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s> pierced his very swift horses
with sharp, high-speed, whetted arrows, like thunderbolts.
Then he pierced <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in the chest with sharp arrows;
<s>Rāghava</s>, supremely intent, pierced him in the forehead with three feathered shafts.
The lord of rākṣasas, all his limbs pierced by arrows and blood streaming from his body,
appeared amid the host like a blossoming aśoka tree.
The lord of night-roamers, his body deeply pierced by <s>Rāma</s>'s arrows, his limbs wet with blood,

children.text: jagāma khedaṃ ca samājamadhye krodhaṃ ca cakre subhṛśaṃ tadānīm ||
children.translated_text: grew weary in the midst of the assembly, and then became exceedingly angry.

children.text: sa tu tena tadā krodhāt kākutsthenārdito raṇe
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, tormented in battle by that <s>Kākutstha</s> in anger,
proud of war, entered into great fury.
With blazing eyes from wrath, the mighty one drew his bow,
and, greatly enraged, pressed hard against <s>Rāghava</s> in the supreme battle.
With thousands of streams of arrows, like a rain-cloud from the sky,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> filled <s>Rāghava</s> with arrows as one fills a pond.
Filled in battle by the net of arrows released from the bow,
<s>Kākutstha</s>, unshakable like a great mountain, did not tremble.

children.text: sa śaraiḥ śarajālāni vārayan samare sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Standing in battle, warding off the nets of arrows with arrows,
the mighty one received them as if they were rays of the sun.
Then the night-roamer, quick-handed and angry,
struck thousands of arrows into the chest of noble <s>Rāghava</s>.
Covered with blood in battle, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s elder brother
was seen like a great kiṃśuka tree blooming in the forest.
Enraged by the blows of arrows, he too seized arrows,
<s>Kākutstha</s>, of very great splendor, with the brilliance of the end-of-age sun.
Then both <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, greatly enraged with each other,
could not be seen at that time in battle, because of the darkness made by arrows.
Then the heroic <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, possessed by anger,

children.text: uvāca rāvaṇaṃ vīraḥ prahasya paruṣaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: laughed and spoke harsh words to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>:
Because, O lowest rākṣasa, you carried off my wife from <s>Janasthāna</s> while I was unaware,

children.text: hṛtā te vivaśā yasmāt tasmāt tvaṃ nāsi vīryavān ||
children.translated_text: and she was helpless in your power, for that reason you are no man of valor.
While she was separated from me, wretched and living in the great forest,

children.text: vaidehīṃ prasabhaṃ hṛtvā śūro 'ham iti manyase ||
children.translated_text: you forcibly abducted <s>Vaidehī</s> and think, "I am a hero."
A hero among women without protectors, violator of another's wife,

children.text: kṛtvā kāpuruṣaṃ karma śūro 'ham iti manyase ||
children.translated_text: having done a coward's deed, you think, "I am a hero."
Breaker of bounds, shameless one, unstable in conduct,
through arrogance you have brought death upon yourself, and yet you think, "I am a hero."
By you, brave brother of <s>Dhanada</s>, assembled with your forces,

children.text: ślāghanīyaṃ yaśasyaṃ ca kṛtaṃ karma mahat tvayā ||
children.translated_text: a great deed has indeed been done, praiseworthy and glorious.
Of that act, committed by one seized with arrogance, blameworthy and harmful,
now receive today its very great fruit.
You understand yourself to be "a hero," O fool,

children.text: naiva lajjāsti te sītāṃ coravad vyapakarṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: but you had no shame while dragging <s>Sītā</s> away like a thief.

children.text: yadi matsaṃnidhau sītā dharṣitā syāt tvayā balāt
children.translated_text: If <s>Sītā</s> had been assaulted by you by force in my presence,

children.text: bhrātaraṃ tu kharaṃ paśyestadā matsāyakair hataḥ ||
children.translated_text: then you would have seen your brother <s>Khara</s>, slain by my arrows.
By fortune, evil-minded one, you have come within range of my sight.
Today I shall send you with sharp arrows to the abode of <s>Yama</s>.
Today let flesh-eaters drag away your head, cut off by my arrows,
with its blazing earrings, scattered in the dust of battle.
Let vultures alight on your breast, O <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, when you have been hurled to the ground,
and in their thirst drink the blood that rises from within the wounds made by arrow-points.
Today, when you have been split by my arrows, lifeless and fallen,
let the birds drag out your entrails, as <s>Garuḍas</s> drag out serpents.

children.text: ityevaṃ sa vadan vīro rāmaḥ śatrunibarhaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: As the hero <s>Rāma</s>, destroyer of enemies, was speaking in this way,
he showered the nearby lord of rākṣasas with torrents of arrows.

children.text: babhūva dviguṇaṃ vīryaṃ balaṃ harṣaśca saṃyuge
children.translated_text: In the battle, the valor, strength, and joy of <s>Rāma</s> became doubled,
as did the power of his weapons, for he longed for the enemy's destruction.
All the weapons appeared for him, whose self was fully aware,
and from exultation the greatly radiant one became still quicker with his hands.
Recognizing these auspicious signs that had arisen within himself,
<s>Rāma</s>, destroyer of the rākṣasas, again afflicted <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Struck by the volleys of stones from the monkeys and by the showers of arrows from <s>Rāghava</s>,
ten-necked <s>Rāvaṇa</s> became unsteady at heart.

children.text: yadā ca śastraṃ nārebhe na vyakarṣaccharāsanam
children.translated_text: When he no longer took up a weapon and did not draw his bow,
his courage gave him no response, for his inner mind was bewildered.
Even the arrows he had loosed, and the various weapons too,
did not serve the purpose of battle as the time of death drew near.
But his charioteer, the driver of his chariot, seeing him in that condition,
calmly and without panic drove his chariot slowly away from the battle.
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, confused, greatly enraged, and driven by the power of death,
with eyes reddened by anger, spoke to the charioteer:
As though I were lacking in valor, powerless, and bereft of manliness,

children.text: bhīruṃ laghum ivāsattvaṃ vihīnam iva tejasā ||
children.translated_text: as though I were cowardly, contemptible, without strength, and deprived of splendor,

children.text: vimuktam iva māyābhir astrair iva bahiṣkṛtam
children.translated_text: as though abandoned by my māyās (illusive powers) and shut out from my weapons,

children.text: mām avajñāya durbuddhe svayā buddhyā viceṣṭase ||
children.translated_text: you disregard me, fool, and act according to your own judgment.

children.text: kimarthaṃ mām avajñāya macchandam anavekṣya ca
children.translated_text: Why have you disregarded me and ignored my will?
Why has this chariot of mine been driven away by you in the enemy's presence?
Today, ignoble man, you have destroyed what I won over a long time:

children.text: yaśo vīryaṃ ca tejaśca pratyayaśca vināśitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: my fame, my valor, my splendor, and my reputation.
In the sight of an enemy famed for his valor and worthy of being pleased by feats of prowess,
you have made me, eager for battle, into a coward.

children.text: yastvaṃ ratham imaṃ mohānna codvahasi durmate
children.translated_text: Since, in your delusion, you do not drive this chariot on, evil-minded one,

children.text: satyo 'yaṃ pratitarko me pareṇa tvam upaskṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this suspicion of mine is true: you have been suborned by another.

children.text: na hīdaṃ vidyate karma suhṛdo hitakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: For this is not the act of a friend who desires my welfare;
rather, it resembles the act of enemies, and this has not been well done by you.

children.text: nivartaya rathaṃ śīghraṃ yāvannāpaiti me ripuḥ
children.translated_text: Turn the chariot back quickly, before my enemy goes away,

children.text: yadi vāpyuṣito 'si tvaṃ smaryante yadi vā guṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: if indeed you have lived with me, or if my favors are remembered.
Thus harshly addressed by the senseless one, the charioteer, whose mind was set on his welfare,

children.text: abravīd rāvaṇaṃ sūto hitaṃ sānunayaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: spoke to <s>Rāvaṇa</s> words that were beneficial and conciliatory:

children.text: na bhīto 'smi na mūḍho 'smi nopajapto 'smi śatrubhiḥ
children.translated_text: I am not afraid, I am not deluded, nor have I been incited by enemies.

children.text: na pramatto na niḥsneho vismṛtā na ca satkriyā ||
children.translated_text: I am not careless, not without affection, nor have proper honors been forgotten.
By me, who desired your welfare and was protecting your fame,
with a heart overflowing with affection, this unpleasant thing was done as something dear to you.

children.text: nāsminn arthe mahārāja tvaṃ māṃ priyahite ratam
children.translated_text: In this matter, great king, you should not regard me,
who am devoted to what is dear and beneficial to you, as blameworthy, like some low and ignoble man.
Listen, and I will tell you the reason why the chariot
was turned back by me in battle, like waters by the current of a river.
I perceive your fatigue from the great labor of battle;

children.text: na hi te vīra saumukhyaṃ praharṣaṃ vopadhāraye ||
children.translated_text: for I do not observe in you, hero, either readiness to face the foe or exultation.
And these horses of your chariot are exhausted from drawing the chariot;
they are downcast and worn out by heat, like cows beaten by rain.

children.text: nimittāni ca bhūyiṣṭhaṃ yāni prādurbhavanti naḥ
children.translated_text: And among the many omens that are appearing to us,
as each occurs, I mark it as unfavorable.
Place and time must be understood, as well as marks and gestures,
dejection, joy, fatigue, and the strength and weakness of the warrior in the chariot.
The low and high places of the ground, and its even and uneven stretches,
the time for battle, and the perception of an opening in the opponent, must be known.
Advance and withdrawal, standing firm and retreating:
all this must be known by the chariot-warrior's attendant who stands on the chariot.
For the sake of your rest, and also that of these chariot-horses,

children.text: raudraṃ varjayatā khedaṃ kṣamaṃ kṛtam idaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: I did what was proper, while trying to avoid fierce exhaustion.

children.text: na mayā svecchayā vīra ratho 'yam apavāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: It was not by my own wish, hero, that this chariot was driven away;
what I did, lord, was done by me because I was filled with affection for my master.
Command me truly, O slayer of enemies, as you will speak;
that I shall do, hero, with a mind that has discharged its debt.
Satisfied with that speech of his charioteer, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
eager for battle, praised him in many ways and said this:

children.text: rathaṃ śīghram imaṃ sūta rāghavābhimukhaṃ kuru
children.translated_text: Quickly turn this chariot, charioteer, toward <s>Rāghava</s>.
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> will not turn back from battle without killing his enemies.
Having said this, then, pleased, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas,

children.text: dadau tasya śubhaṃ hyekaṃ hastābharaṇam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: gave him a splendid and excellent hand-ornament.

children.text: tato drutaṃ rāvaṇavākyacoditaḥ pracodayāmāsa hayān sa sārathiḥ
children.translated_text: Then, urged on by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s words, that charioteer swiftly drove the horses forward,

children.text: sa rākṣasendrasya tato mahārathaḥ kṣaṇena rāmasya raṇāgrato 'bhavat ||
children.translated_text: and in an instant the great chariot of the lord of rākṣasas stood before <s>Rāma</s> at the front of battle.
The king of men saw that chariot of the rākṣasa king, rushing upon him suddenly, resounding, with a great banner,
yes, he saw it as it came on.
yoked with black horses, endowed with terrible splendor,
dense with lightning-like banners, displaying a weapon like <s>Indra</s>'s bow,
releasing streams of arrows, like a rain cloud pouring down a torrent of water.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā meghasaṃkāśam āpatantaṃ rathaṃ ripoḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that enemy's chariot, cloud-like and rushing onward,
with a sound like a mountain splitting when struck by a thunderbolt,
<s>Rāma</s> spoke to <s>Mātali</s>, the charioteer of the thousand-eyed one:

children.text: mātale paśya saṃrabdham āpatantaṃ rathaṃ ripoḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Mātali</s>, look at the enemy's chariot rushing on in fury.
As it comes again in a counterclockwise course with great speed,

children.text: samare hantum ātmānaṃ tathānena kṛtā matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: so he has formed the intention of bringing death upon himself in battle.

children.text: tad apramādam ātiṣṭha pratyudgaccha rathaṃ ripoḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore keep to careful attention; go forward to meet the enemy's chariot.
I wish to shatter it, as the wind shatters a risen cloud.
Without faltering, without confusion, with heart and eyes undistracted,
drive the chariot swiftly, keeping the movement of the reins controlled.
Indeed, you need no instruction, accustomed as you are to <s>Purandara</s>'s chariot.

children.text: yuyutsur aham ekāgraḥ smāraye tvāṃ na śikṣaye ||
children.translated_text: I am eager for battle and single-minded; I remind you, I do not teach you.

children.text: parituṣṭaḥ sa rāmasya tena vākyena mātaliḥ
children.translated_text: Pleased by that speech of <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Mātali</s>,
the best of divine charioteers, urged the chariot on.
Then, making <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s great chariot pass to the left,
he shook <s>Rāvaṇa</s> with the dust thrown up by the wheels.
Then ten-necked <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, enraged, his coppery eyes wide open,
showered arrows upon <s>Rāma</s>, who was facing his chariot.
<s>Rāma</s>, angered by the attack, letting wrath overrun composure,
took up in battle <s>Indra</s>'s bow of very great force,
and the greatly radiant one took arrows shining like rays of the sun.
Then the great battle was joined between the two who longed to kill one another,
facing each other like two proud lions.
Then the gods, together with the gandharvas, the siddhas, and the great seers,
assembled to see the chariot duel, wishing for <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s destruction.
Then dreadful portents arose, making the hair stand on end,
for the destruction of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and for the victory of <s>Rāghava</s>.
The god rained blood over <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s chariot,
and fierce whirling winds began to move counterclockwise.
A great flock of vultures, wheeling in the sky,

children.text: yena yena ratho yāti tena tena pradhāvati ||
children.translated_text: rushed after him wherever his chariot went.
<s>Laṅkā</s> was covered by a twilight resembling hibiscus flowers,
and even by day the earth appeared as if set ablaze.
Thunderclaps and great meteors, making a mighty roar, moved about,
disheartening the rākṣasas and then turned against <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Wherever <s>Rāvaṇa</s> moved there, the earth trembled,

children.text: rakṣasāṃ ca praharatāṃ gṛhītā iva bāhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the arms of the striking rākṣasas seemed as if seized fast.

children.text: tāmrāḥ pītāḥ sitāḥ śvetāḥ patitāḥ sūryaraśmayaḥ
children.translated_text: Coppery, yellow, pale, and white rays of the sun fell down,
and were seen on <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s body like ores on a mountain.
Jackals, followed by vultures and vomiting fire from their mouths,

children.text: praṇedur mukham īkṣantyaḥ saṃrabdham aśivaṃ śivāḥ ||
children.translated_text: looked at his face and howled a fierce, inauspicious howl.

children.text: pratikūlaṃ vavau vāyū raṇe pāṃsūn samutkiran
children.translated_text: An adverse wind blew in the battle, throwing up dust,
and causing the sight of that king of rākṣasas to fail.
<s>Indra</s>'s thunderbolts fell all around in his army,
terrible and unbearable in sound, though no rain cloud sounded.
All the directions and intermediate directions became covered in darkness,
and the sky became hard to see because of a great rain of dust.
Mynas, making a dreadful quarrel toward that chariot,
fell there by the hundreds, dreadful and dreadful in cry.
From their hind parts came sparks, and from their eyes constant tears;

children.text: mumucustasya turagāstulyam agniṃ ca vāri ca ||
children.translated_text: his horses emitted fire and water alike.
Many fearful portents of this kind,
terrible ones, arose for <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s destruction.

children.text: rāmasyāpi nimittāni saumyāni ca śivāni ca
children.translated_text: For <s>Rāma</s> too, gentle and auspicious signs,
announcing victory, appeared everywhere.

children.text: tato nirīkṣyātmagatāni rāghavo raṇe nimittāni nimittakovidaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāghava</s>, skilled in omens, observed in battle the signs concerning himself,

children.text: jagāma harṣaṃ ca parāṃ ca nirvṛtiṃ cakāra yuddhe 'bhyadhikaṃ ca vikramam ||
children.translated_text: and reached joy and supreme relief, and showed still greater valor in the fight.
Then at that time there began between <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s>
a very great and very cruel chariot duel, terrifying all the worlds.

children.text: tato rākṣasasainyaṃ ca harīṇāṃ ca mahad balam
children.translated_text: Then the army of rākṣasas and the great force of the monkeys,
weapons gripped in hand, stood motionless.
Seeing the mighty man and rākṣasa fighting together,
all had their hearts thrown into confusion and reached the highest amazement.
With their arms busy with many kinds of weapons, their minds astonished,

children.text: tasthuḥ prekṣya ca saṃgrāmaṃ nābhijaghnuḥ parasparam ||
children.translated_text: they stood watching the battle and did not strike one another.

children.text: rakṣasāṃ rāvaṇaṃ cāpi vānarāṇāṃ ca rāghavam
children.translated_text: As the rākṣasas watched <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and the monkeys watched <s>Rāghava</s>,
the army, its eyes full of wonder, appeared like a painted picture.

children.text: tau tu tatra nimittāni dṛṣṭvā rāghavarāvaṇau
children.translated_text: But there, after seeing those omens, <s>Rāghava</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
their minds resolved and their fury firm, fought without fear.

children.text: jetavyam iti kākutstho martavyam iti rāvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: 'He must be conquered,' thought <s>Kākutstha</s>; 'I must die,' thought <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Resolute, they then displayed all their own valor in battle.

children.text: tataḥ krodhād daśagrīvaḥ śarān saṃdhāya vīryavān
children.translated_text: Then ten-necked <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, mighty and enraged, set arrows on the string,

children.text: mumoca dhvajam uddiśya rāghavasya rathe sthitam ||
children.translated_text: and released them at the banner standing on <s>Rāghava</s>'s chariot.
Those arrows, not reaching the banner on <s>Purandara</s>'s chariot,
touched the supreme red spear and fell upon the surface of the earth.
Then mighty <s>Rāma</s>, greatly enraged, drew his bow,
and in his mind began to set about making return for what had been done.
Aiming at <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s banner, he released a sharpened arrow,
unendurable like a great serpent, blazing with its own radiance.

children.text: jagāma sa mahīṃ bhittvā daśagrīvadhvajaṃ śaraḥ
children.translated_text: That arrow went, cutting through the earth, to the banner of the ten-necked one;
and <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s chariot-banner, cut down, fell upon the ground.
Seeing the overthrow of his banner, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, of very great strength,
became, in battle, as though kindled by the fire born of anger.

children.text: sa roṣavaśam āpannaḥ śaravarṣaṃ mahad vaman
children.translated_text: Overcome by fury and vomiting forth a great shower of arrows,

children.text: rāmasya turagān divyāñ śarair vivyādha rāvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s> pierced <s>Rāma</s>'s divine horses with arrows.
Though pierced, those tawny horses of his did not stumble or become confused;
they remained steady-hearted, as if struck with lotus-stalks.
Seeing then the lack of agitation in those steeds,

children.text: bhūya eva susaṃkruddhaḥ śaravarṣaṃ mumoca ha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, even more enraged, released another shower of arrows.
Maces, iron clubs, discus-weapons, and pestles,
mountain peaks and trees, and likewise spears and axes,
this magically produced rain of weapons he made fall,
along with arrows by the thousand, his heart and effort unwearied.
Tumultuous, terrifying, dreadful, and dreadfully resounding,
that great mass of many weapons became hard to withstand in battle.
Leaving aside <s>Rāghava</s>'s chariot and turning all around upon the monkey army,
he quickly made the sky uninterrupted with shafts,
and the ten-necked one released them with a mind free from hesitation.

children.text: vyāyacchamānaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā tatparaṃ rāvaṇaṃ raṇe
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Rāvaṇa</s> exerting himself in battle, intent on that alone,

children.text: prahasann iva kākutsthaḥ saṃdadhe sāyakāñ śitān ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kākutstha</s>, as if smiling, fitted sharp arrows to his bow.

children.text: sa mumoca tato bāṇān raṇe śatasahasraśaḥ
children.translated_text: Then in battle he released arrows by the hundreds of thousands;

children.text: tān dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇaścakre svaśaraiḥ khaṃ nirantaram ||
children.translated_text: seeing them, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> made the sky unbroken with his own arrows.
Then, with the shining showers of arrows discharged by those two,
a second bright sky seemed to appear, bound together by arrows.
No arrow was without purpose, none failed to pierce fully, none was fruitless,
as <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s> kept releasing arrows in the fight.
They fought without interruption, shooting to left and right,
and with floods of arrows the two made the sky seem unable to breathe.

children.text: rāvaṇasya hayān rāmo hayān rāmasya rāvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> struck <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s horses, and <s>Rāvaṇa</s> struck <s>Rāma</s>'s horses;
then those two, each answering the other's act, attacked one another.

children.text: tau tathā yudhyamānau tu samare rāmarāvaṇau
children.translated_text: As <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s> were fighting in that way in battle,
all beings watched them with amazement in their hearts.
Harassing the two in battle, those two excellent chariots of theirs,
intent on each other's destruction, became terrible in form.
Circles, lanes, advances and retreats,
the two charioteers displayed many kinds of movement born of charioteering skill.

children.text: ardayan rāvaṇaṃ rāmo rāghavaṃ cāpi rāvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> harassing <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, and <s>Rāvaṇa</s> harassing <s>Rāghava</s>,
they reached full speed of movement in advancing and turning back.
As those two hurled nets of arrows, their two excellent chariots
moved over the battlefield like two rain-clouds pouring down showers.

children.text: darśayitvā tadā tau tu gatiṃ bahuvidhāṃ raṇe
children.translated_text: After displaying then many kinds of movement in battle,
they again stood facing one another.

children.text: dhuraṃ dhureṇa rathayor vaktraṃ vaktreṇa vājinām
children.translated_text: The yoke of one chariot met the other's yoke, and the horses' mouths met mouth to mouth;
as they stood there, the banners met the banners.

children.text: rāvaṇasya tato rāmo dhanurmuktaiḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s>, with four sharp arrows released from his bow,
drove back the four blazing horses of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
The night-roamer, overcome by anger at the withdrawal of his horses,
released sharpened arrows at <s>Rāghava</s>.
Though deeply pierced by mighty ten-necked <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: jagāma na vikāraṃ ca na cāpi vyathito 'bhavat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> underwent no change and was not distressed.
And again the night-roamer shot arrows with the crash of falling thunderbolts,
aiming at the charioteer of the wielder of the thunderbolt.
The arrows of great speed fell upon <s>Mātali</s>'s body,

children.text: na sūkṣmam api saṃmohaṃ vyathāṃ vā pradadur yudhi ||
children.translated_text: but in battle they caused him not even the slightest bewilderment or pain.

children.text: tayā dharṣaṇayā kruddho mātaler na tathātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Angered by that assault on <s>Mātali</s>, more than by one on himself,
<s>Rāghava</s>, with a net of arrows, made his enemy turn away.
Twenty, thirty, sixty, then by the hundreds and thousands,

children.text: mumoca rāghavo vīraḥ sāyakān syandane ripoḥ ||
children.translated_text: heroic <s>Rāghava</s> released shafts upon the enemy's chariot.

children.text: gadānāṃ musalānāṃ ca parighāṇāṃ ca nisvanaiḥ
children.translated_text: By the sounds of maces, pestles, and iron clubs,
and by the winds from the feathered ends of arrows, the seven oceans were shaken.
And when the oceans were shaken, all the serpents dwelling in the depths of <s>Pātāla</s>
were terrified, as were dānavas by the thousands.
The entire earth, with its mountains, forests, and groves, trembled;
the sun became devoid of splendor, and the wind did not blow.
Then the gods together with the gandharvas, the siddhas, and the supreme seers,
all, along with kinnaras and great serpents, fell into anxiety.
May there be welfare for cows and brahmins; may the worlds stand forever.
May <s>Rāghava</s> win in battle over <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas.
Then the long-armed <s>Rāma</s>, enhancer of the fame of the <s>Raghus</s>, became angry,
and, setting upon his bow a razor-edged arrow like a venomous serpent,
He cut off <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s head, adorned with splendid blazing earrings.
Then that head, fallen on the ground, was seen at that time by the three worlds,
and another head of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, exactly like it, rose up.
That too, quickly, by quick-handed <s>Rāma</s>, swift in action,
the second head of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> was cut off in battle with arrows.

children.text: chinnamātraṃ ca tacchīrṣaṃ punar anyat sma dṛśyate
children.translated_text: And as soon as that head was cut off, yet another was seen again;
that too was cut off by <s>Rāma</s> with arrows resembling thunderbolts.

children.text: evam eva śataṃ chinnaṃ śirasāṃ tulyavarcasām
children.translated_text: In this very way a hundred heads, equal in splendor, were cut off,
and yet no end of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> was seen in the loss of his life.
Then the heroic knower of all weapons, increaser of <s>Kausalyā</s>'s joy,
<s>Rāghava</s>, furnished with many shafts, reflected:

children.text: mārīco nihato yaistu kharo yaistu sudūṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: "These arrows by which <s>Mārīca</s> was killed, and by which <s>Khara</s> and <s>Sudūṣaṇa</s> were killed,
and <s>Virādha</s> in the <s>Krauñca</s> forest, and <s>Kabandha</s> in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest,

children.text: ta ime sāyakāḥ sarve yuddhe pratyayikā mama
children.translated_text: all these shafts are reliable for me in battle.

children.text: kiṃ nu tat kāraṇaṃ yena rāvaṇe mandatejasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What, then, is that cause by which, in the case of dull-splendored <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, this is so?"
Thinking thus, he was intent on thought and yet alert in the battle;
<s>Rāghava</s> rained showers of arrows upon <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s chest.
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s> too, angered, the lord of rākṣasas standing on his chariot,
harassed <s>Rāma</s> in battle with a shower of maces and clubs.
While gods, dānavas, yakṣas, piśācas, serpents, and rākṣasas
looked on, that great battle went on through the whole night.

children.text: naiva rātriṃ na divasaṃ na muhūrtaṃ na ca kṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Neither night nor day, nor a muhūrta nor a moment,
did the battle of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s> come to a halt.
Then <s>Mātali</s> at that time reminded <s>Rāghava</s>:

children.text: ajānann iva kiṃ vīra tvam enam anuvartase ||
children.translated_text: "Hero, as if not knowing, why do you merely follow him?

children.text: visṛjāsmai vadhāya tvam astraṃ paitāmahaṃ prabho
children.translated_text: My lord, release against him, for his death, <s>Brahmā</s>'s weapon;

children.text: vināśakālaḥ kathito yaḥ suraiḥ so 'dya vartate ||
children.translated_text: the time of destruction which the gods foretold is occurring today."
Then <s>Rāma</s>, reminded by that speech of <s>Mātali</s>,

children.text: jagrāha sa śaraṃ dīptaṃ niśvasantam ivoragam ||
children.translated_text: took up a blazing arrow, as if it were a hissing serpent,

children.text: yam asmai prathamaṃ prādād agastyo bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
children.translated_text: which the blessed seer <s>Agastya</s> had first given to him,
a great unfailing arrow given by <s>Brahmā</s>, mighty in battle.
It had formerly been fashioned by immeasurably powerful <s>Brahmā</s> for <s>Indra</s>'s sake,
and had formerly been given to the lord of the gods, who desired victory over the three worlds.
In its feathers was the wind; in its point were fire and the sun;
its body was made of space; in weight it had <s>Meru</s> and <s>Mandara</s>.
Blazing in its form, well-feathered, adorned with gold,
it was made from the energy of all beings and had the brilliance of the sun.

children.text: sadhūmam iva kālāgniṃ dīptam āśīviṣaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: Like the fire at the end of time with smoke, like a blazing venomous serpent,
it could pierce hosts of chariots, elephants, and horses and acted swiftly.

children.text: dvārāṇāṃ parighāṇāṃ ca girīṇām api bhedanam
children.translated_text: It could pierce gates and bars, and even mountains;
its body was smeared with various blood and anointed with fat, exceedingly terrible.
Hard as a thunderbolt, loud-roaring, dreadful in many battles,
terrible, frightening all creatures, breathing like a serpent,
for flocks of kaṅkas and vultures, and for packs of jackals and rākṣasas,
it always provided food in battle, deathlike and fear-bringing.
It was the delight of the chiefs of the monkeys and the oppressor of the rākṣasas,
furnished with various bright and variegated feathers of <s>Garuḍa</s>.
That supreme arrow of the worlds, destroyer of the fear of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s>,
robber of the fame of enemies and producer of joy for himself,
then mighty <s>Rāma</s> consecrated that great arrow
by the procedure proclaimed in the Veda and set it on his bow.

children.text: sa rāvaṇāya saṃkruddho bhṛśam āyamya kārmukam
children.translated_text: Furious at <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, he drew the bow very far,
and, with supreme concentration, hurled that vital-piercing arrow.
Like a thunderbolt, unassailable, released from arms like thunderbolts,
and like Death irresistible, it fell upon <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s chest.
That arrow, released with great speed and bringing the body's end,
pierced the heart of wicked <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Blood-stained, that life-ending arrow, with its force,
took away <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s breaths and entered the earth.
Having killed <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, that arrow, its appearance made wet with blood,
its deed done, quietly entered again into its own quiver.
From the hand of the slain one, immediately, that bow together with its arrows
fell, along with his breaths, as he was slipping away from life.
The great-splendored lord of the nairṛtas, terrible in speed, his life gone,

children.text: papāta syandanād bhūmau vṛtro vajrahato yathā ||
children.translated_text: fell from the chariot to the ground like <s>Vṛtra</s> struck by the thunderbolt.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā patitaṃ bhūmau hataśeṣā niśācarāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing him fallen on the ground, the surviving night-roamers,
their lord slain and terrified with fear, fled in every direction.
Roaring, the tree-fighting monkeys rushed upon them,
having seen the killing of <s>Daśagrīva</s> and <s>Rāghava</s>'s victory.

children.text: arditā vānarair hṛṣṭair laṅkām abhyapatan bhayāt
children.translated_text: Harried by the delighted monkeys, they fled in fear toward <s>Laṅkā</s>,
because their refuge had been slain, with piteous faces streaming with tears.
Then the monkeys, rejoicing and shining with victory, cried aloud,

children.text: vadanto rāghavajayaṃ rāvaṇasya ca taṃ vadham ||
children.translated_text: proclaiming <s>Rāghava</s>'s victory and that killing of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Then in the sky the gentle kettledrum of the thirty gods sounded forth,
and there a very pleasant wind bearing divine fragrance blew.
And from the sky a rain of flowers fell then upon the earth,
unattainable and delightful, scattering over <s>Rāghava</s>'s chariot.
Joined with praise of <s>Rāghava</s>, there was heard in the sky

children.text: sādhu sādhviti vāg agryā devatānāṃ mahātmanām ||
children.translated_text: the excellent speech of the great-souled gods: "Well done, well done!"

children.text: āviveśa mahān harṣo devānāṃ cāraṇaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Great joy entered the gods, together with the cāraṇas,
when fierce <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, who had caused fear to all worlds, had been slain.

children.text: tataḥ sakāmaṃ sugrīvam aṅgadaṃ ca mahābalam
children.translated_text: Then the delighted <s>Rāghava</s>, after killing the foremost rākṣasa,
made <s>Sugrīva</s> and mighty <s>Aṅgada</s> fulfilled in their desire.

children.text: tataḥ prajagmuḥ praśamaṃ marudgaṇā diśaḥ prasedur vimalaṃ nabho'bhavat
children.translated_text: Then the hosts of winds became calm, the directions grew clear, and the sky became spotless;

children.text: mahī cakampe na ca mārutā vavuḥ sthiraprabhaścāpyabhavad divākaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: the earth trembled, the winds did not blow, and the sun too became steady in its light.
Then <s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, and the others, his special friends, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: sametya hṛṣṭā vijayena rāghavaṃ raṇe 'bhirāmaṃ vidhinābhyapūjayan ||
children.translated_text: gathered joyfully and duly honored <s>Rāghava</s>, lovely in battle, because of the victory.

children.text: sa tu nihataripuḥ sthirapratijñaḥ svajanabalābhivṛto raṇe rarāja
children.translated_text: He, with his enemy slain, firm in his vow, surrounded in battle by the strength of his own people, shone forth,
the mighty joy of the kings of <s>Raghu</s>'s line, as <s>Indra</s> surrounded by the hosts of the Thirty gods.
Hearing that <s>Rāvaṇa</s> had been slain by the great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>,
the rākṣasa women, wasted by grief, rushed out from the inner palace.
Though repeatedly restrained, rolling in the dust of the ground,
with hair loosened and afflicted by sorrow, they were like cows whose calves had been killed.
Going out by the northern gate together with the rākṣasas,
they entered the terrible battlefield, searching for their slain husband.

children.text: āryaputreti vādinyo hā nātheti ca sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Crying on every side, "Noble lord!" and "Ah, protector!",
they fell upon the earth, strewn with headless trunks and muddy with blood.
Those women, their eyes filled with tears and overcome by grief for their husband,
wailed like female elephants trumpeting when their herd-leader has been killed.
They saw great-bodied, very heroic, greatly radiant
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> lying slain on the ground, like a mass of dark collyrium.

children.text: tāḥ patiṃ sahasā dṛṣṭvā śayānaṃ raṇapāṃsuṣu
children.translated_text: Seeing their husband suddenly lying in the dust of battle,
they fell upon his limbs like forest creepers that had been cut down.

children.text: bahumānāt pariṣvajya kācid enaṃ ruroda ha
children.translated_text: One, out of reverence, embraced him and wept;

children.text: caraṇau kācid āliṅgya kācit kaṇṭhe 'valambya ca ||
children.translated_text: one clasped his feet, and another clung to his neck.

children.text: uddhṛtya ca bhujau kācid bhūmau sma parivartate
children.translated_text: One lifted up his arms and rolled about on the ground;
one, seeing the face of the slain man, fell into a swoon.

children.text: kācid aṅke śiraḥ kṛtvā ruroda mukham īkṣatī
children.translated_text: One placed his head in her lap and wept while gazing at his face,
bathing his face with tears, as if sprinkling a lotus with dewdrops.

children.text: evam ārtāḥ patiṃ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇaṃ nihataṃ bhuvi
children.translated_text: Thus, distressed after seeing their husband <s>Rāvaṇa</s> slain on the earth,
they cried out in many ways from grief, and again they lamented further.

children.text: yena vitrāsitaḥ śakro yena vitrāsito yamaḥ
children.translated_text: "He by whom <s>Śakra</s> was terrified, he by whom <s>Yama</s> was terrified,
he by whom King <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> was deprived of <s>Puṣpaka</s>,

children.text: gandharvāṇām ṛṣīṇāṃ ca surāṇāṃ ca mahātmanām
children.translated_text: he by whom great fear was given to the gandharvas, the seers,

children.text: bhayaṃ yena mahad dattaṃ so 'yaṃ śete raṇe hataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the great-souled gods, that very man lies slain in battle.

children.text: asurebhyaḥ surebhyo vā pannagebhyo 'pi vā tathā
children.translated_text: He who knew no fear from asuras, or gods,

children.text: na bhayaṃ yo vijānāti tasyedaṃ mānuṣād bhayam ||
children.translated_text: or even from serpents as well, for him this fear has come from a human.
He who could not be slain by the gods, nor likewise by dānavas and rākṣasas,

children.text: hataḥ so 'yaṃ raṇe śete mānuṣeṇa padātinā ||
children.translated_text: that same one lies slain in battle by a human foot-soldier.

children.text: yo na śakyaḥ surair hantuṃ na yakṣair nāsuraistathā
children.translated_text: He who could not be killed by gods, nor by yakṣas, nor likewise by asuras,

children.text: so 'yaṃ kaścid ivāsattvo mṛtyuṃ martyena lambhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that same one, as if he were some powerless man, has met death through a mortal.

children.text: evaṃ vadantyo bahudhā rurudustasya tāḥ striyaḥ
children.translated_text: Speaking in many ways like this, those women of his wept,

children.text: bhūya eva ca duḥkhārtā vilepuśca punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, afflicted by sorrow yet again, lamented again and again.
"Because you did not listen to friends who constantly spoke for your welfare,

children.text: etāḥ samam idānīṃ te vayam ātmā ca pātitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: now we, along with yourself and your own person, have been brought down.

children.text: bruvāṇo 'pi hitaṃ vākyam iṣṭo bhrātā vibhīṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Even though beloved brother <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> spoke words for your welfare,
he was rashly and harshly insulted by you in delusion, as you sought your own death.

children.text: yadi niryātitā te syāt sītā rāmāya maithilī
children.translated_text: If <s>Sītā</s>, the <s>Maithilī</s>, had been handed over by you to <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: na naḥ syād vyasanaṃ ghoram idaṃ mūlaharaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: this terrible, great calamity, uprooting us at the root, would not have befallen us.

children.text: vṛttakāmo bhaved bhrātā rāmo mitrakulaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Your brother would have had his desire fulfilled, <s>Rāma</s> would have become a friendly family,

children.text: vayaṃ cāvidhavāḥ sarvāḥ sakāmā na ca śatravaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and all of us would not be widows; we would have had our desires fulfilled, and there would have been no enemies.

children.text: tvayā punar nṛśaṃsena sītāṃ saṃrundhatā balāt
children.translated_text: But by you, cruel man, who forcibly confined <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: rākṣasā vayam ātmā ca trayaṃ tulyaṃ nipātitam ||
children.translated_text: we rākṣasas, ourselves, and you too: all three alike have been cast down.

children.text: na kāmakāraḥ kāmaṃ vā tava rākṣasapuṃgava
children.translated_text: It was not the wilful act of desire, nor desire itself, for you, foremost of rākṣasas;

children.text: daivaṃ ceṣṭayate sarvaṃ hataṃ daivena hanyate ||
children.translated_text: fate impels everything; one struck down by fate is slain.

children.text: vānarāṇāṃ vināśo 'yaṃ rākṣasānāṃ ca te raṇe
children.translated_text: This destruction of the monkeys and of your rākṣasas in battle,
and of you yourself, mighty-armed one, has come about through the conjunction of fate.

children.text: naivārthena na kāmena vikrameṇa na cājñayā
children.translated_text: By wealth, by desire, by valor, or by command,
the course of fate, once set in motion in the world, cannot be turned back.
Thus the wretched wives of the lord of rākṣasas lamented,
distressed like ospreys, their eyes overwhelmed with tears.
As those rākṣasa women were lamenting in that way,

children.text: jyeṣṭhā patnī priyā dīnā bhartāraṃ samudaikṣata ||
children.translated_text: his eldest wife, beloved and wretched, looked upon her husband.
Seeing ten-necked <s>Daśagrīva</s>, her husband, slain by <s>Rāma</s> of inconceivable deeds,
there the pitiable <s>Mandodarī</s> lamented.
"Surely, mighty-armed one, younger brother of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>,
when you were angry even <s>Purandara</s> trembled to stand before you.
Surely the seers, the earth-gods, and the famous gandharvas,
and the cāraṇas too, out of fear of you, fled to the directions.

children.text: sa tvaṃ mānuṣamātreṇa rāmeṇa yudhi nirjitaḥ
children.translated_text: Yet you have been conquered in battle by <s>Rāma</s>, a mere human.

children.text: na vyapatrapase rājan kim idaṃ rākṣasarṣabha ||
children.translated_text: Are you not ashamed, O king? What is this, bull among rākṣasas?

children.text: kathaṃ trailokyam ākramya śriyā vīryeṇa cānvitam
children.translated_text: How, after overrunning the three worlds, endowed with splendor and valor...
A forest-ranging human has struck you down, though you were unassailable.
For you, who moved in a sphere beyond human reach and could assume any form,
destruction by <s>Rāma</s> in battle does not seem fitting.

children.text: na caitat karma rāmasya śraddadhāmi camūmukhe
children.translated_text: Nor do I believe this deed of <s>Rāma</s> in the face of the army,
that he could have laid hands on you, furnished as you were on every side.

children.text: indriyāṇi purā jitvā jitaṃ tribhuvanaṃ tvayā
children.translated_text: Long ago, after conquering your senses, you conquered the three worlds;

children.text: smaradbhir iva tad vairam indriyair eva nirjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but now, as though they remembered that enmity, you have been conquered by those very senses.

children.text: atha vā rāmarūpeṇa vāsavaḥ svayam āgataḥ
children.translated_text: Or perhaps <s>Vāsava</s> himself came in the form of <s>Rāma</s>,
having devised an inconceivable illusion for your destruction.

children.text: yadaiva hi janasthāne rākṣasair bahubhir vṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: For when, in <s>Janasthāna</s>, surrounded by many rākṣasas,

children.text: kharastava hato bhrātā tadaivāsau na mānuṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: your brother <s>Khara</s> was killed, even then this one was no human.

children.text: yadaiva nagarīṃ laṅkāṃ duṣpraveśāṃ surair api
children.translated_text: And when mighty <s>Hanumān</s> entered the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>,

children.text: praviṣṭo hanumān vīryāt tadaiva vyathitā vayam ||
children.translated_text: hard to enter even for the gods, even then we were shaken.
When I said, 'Let there be no hostility with <s>Rāghava</s>,'

children.text: ucyamāno na gṛhṇāsi tasyeyaṃ vyuṣṭir āgatā ||
children.translated_text: you would not accept it; now the result of that has arrived.
And without cause you lusted after <s>Sītā</s>, O foremost of rākṣasas,
for the destruction of your sovereignty, your body, and your own people.
By violating that honorable <s>Sītā</s>, superior to <s>Arundhatī</s>

children.text: sītāṃ dharṣayatā mānyāṃ tvayā hyasadṛśaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and even to <s>Rohiṇī</s>, O evil-minded one, you did what was unworthy of you.

children.text: na kulena na rūpeṇa na dākṣiṇyena maithilī
children.translated_text: <s>Maithilī</s> is not superior to me, nor even equal, in lineage,

children.text: mayādhikā vā tulyā vā tvaṃ tu mohānna budhyase ||
children.translated_text: nor in beauty or graciousness; but through delusion you did not understand.
In every way, for all beings, there is no death without a sign;
for you, then, this death bears <s>Maithilī</s> as its sign.
<s>Maithilī</s>, free from sorrow, will sport together with <s>Rāma</s>,
but I, of little merit, have fallen into a terrible ocean of grief.

children.text: kailāse mandare merau tathā caitrarathe vane
children.translated_text: On <s>Kailāsa</s>, on <s>Mandara</s>, on <s>Meru</s>, and in the grove of <s>Caitraratha</s>,
after sporting together with you in all the gardens of the gods,
as I traveled in a fitting aerial car with incomparable splendor,
seeing many different lands, wearing varied garlands and garments,
I have now been cast down from pleasures of desire by your death, O hero.

children.text: satyavāk sa mahābhāgo devaro me yad abravīt
children.translated_text: Truthful was that blessed brother-in-law of mine in what he said:
'This destruction of the chiefs of the rākṣasas has drawn near.'
Through a ruinous attachment arising from desire and anger,

children.text: tvayā kṛtam idaṃ sarvam anāthaṃ rakṣasāṃ kulam ||
children.translated_text: you have made this whole race of rākṣasas helpless.

children.text: na hi tvaṃ śocitavyo me prakhyātabalapauruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Indeed, you should not be mourned by me, famed as you were for strength and manliness;

children.text: strīsvabhāvāt tu me buddhiḥ kāruṇye parivartate ||
children.translated_text: yet because of a woman's nature my mind turns toward pity.

children.text: sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ ca tvaṃ gṛhītvā svāṃ gatiṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: Taking up your good and evil deeds, you have gone to your own destiny;
I mourn for myself, distressed by separation from you.
Dark like a blue rain-cloud, wearing yellow garments and bright armlets,
why do you lie with all your limbs flung out, drenched in blood?

children.text: prasupta iva śokārtāṃ kiṃ māṃ na pratibhāṣase ||
children.translated_text: As if asleep, why do you not speak to me, afflicted with grief?
You of great valor, skillful, never fleeing in battles,

children.text: yātudhānasya dauhitrīṃ kiṃ tvaṃ māṃ nābhyudīkṣase ||
children.translated_text: why do you not look upon me, the granddaughter of a yātudhāna?
That weapon with which you slew enemies in battle, radiant like the sun,
like the thunderbolt of the wielder of the thunderbolt, this one always honored by you,
your iron club, adorned with a golden net and smiting enemies in battle,
lies scattered, cut by arrows into a thousand pieces.

children.text: dhig astu hṛdayaṃ yasyā mamedaṃ na sahasradhā
children.translated_text: Shame on this heart of mine, that it does not split into a thousand pieces
when you have reached death and it is tormented by grief.

children.text: etasminn antare rāmo vibhīṣaṇam uvāca ha
children.translated_text: At that moment <s>Rāma</s> said to <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>:
'Let your brother's funeral rite be performed, and send these women away.'

children.text: taṃ praśritas tato rāmaṃ śrutavākyo vibhīṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, having heard <s>Rāma</s>'s words, bowed respectfully to him;
knowing <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty), he reflected with his intellect on speech joined with <s>dharma</s> and practical purpose,
and, precisely in order to comply with <s>Rāma</s>, he gave this reply:
'I am not fit to perform the rites for one who abandoned the vow of <s>dharma</s>, who was cruel,
ruthless, false, and a violator of another's wife.

children.text: bhrātṛrūpo hi me śatrur eṣa sarvāhite rataḥ
children.translated_text: This <s>Rāvaṇa</s> was an enemy in the form of a brother, intent on harm to all;
he does not deserve honor, though as an elder he would otherwise be worthy of respect.

children.text: nṛśaṃsa iti māṃ rāma vakṣyanti manujā bhuvi
children.translated_text: People on earth, O <s>Rāma</s>, will call me cruel;

children.text: śrutvā tasya guṇān sarve vakṣyanti sukṛtaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but when they hear all his qualities, they will again say that it was well done.'
Hearing that, <s>Rāma</s>, best of those who uphold <s>dharma</s>, was greatly pleased,
and, skilled in speech, said this to <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, who was expert in speech:

children.text: tavāpi me priyaṃ kāryaṃ tvatprabhavācca me jitam
children.translated_text: 'Your wish too must be carried out by me, and through you my victory has been won;

children.text: avaśyaṃ tu kṣamaṃ vācyo mayā tvaṃ rākṣaseśvara ||
children.translated_text: but still, O lord of rākṣasas, I must speak a fitting word to you.
Granted, this night-roamer was joined with unrighteousness and falsehood,

children.text: tejasvī balavāñ śūraḥ saṃgrāmeṣu ca nityaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: yet he was energetic, strong, and heroic always in battles.
It is said that he was not defeated by the gods headed by <s>Śatakratu</s>;
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the terror of the worlds, was great-souled and endowed with strength.
Hostilities end with death; our purpose has been accomplished.

children.text: kriyatām asya saṃskāro mamāpyeṣa yathā tava ||
children.translated_text: Let his funeral rite be performed. He is mine as much as yours.
From you, O mighty-armed one, he deserves the rite performed according to rule;

children.text: kṣipram arhati dharmajña tvaṃ yaśobhāg bhaviṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: quickly, <s>dharma</s>-knower, you will become a sharer in fame.'
Hearing <s>Rāghava</s>'s words, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> hastened
and arranged <s>Rāvaṇa</s> with a funeral rite appropriate to him.

children.text: sa dadau pāvakaṃ tasya vidhiyuktaṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> gave the fire for him in accordance with the prescribed rule,

children.text: tāḥ striyo 'nunayāmāsa sāntvam uktvā punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and again and again he consoled those women, speaking gentle words.
And when all the rākṣasī women had entered, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>...
He approached <s>Rāma</s>'s side and then stood there humbly.
<s>Rāma</s> too, together with the army, with <s>Sugrīva</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: harṣaṃ lebhe ripuṃ hatvā yathā vṛtraṃ śatakratuḥ ||
children.translated_text: rejoiced after killing the enemy, as <s>Śatakratu</s> did after <s>Vṛtra</s>.
Having seen the killing of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the gods, gandharvas, and dānavas

children.text: jagmustaistair vimānaiḥ svaiḥ kathayantaḥ śubhāḥ kathāḥ ||
children.translated_text: went in their own various aerial cars, telling auspicious tales.
They spoke of the terrible killing of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, of <s>Rāghava</s>'s valor,

children.text: suyuddhaṃ vānarāṇāṃ ca sugrīvasya ca mantritam ||
children.translated_text: of the excellent battle of the vānaras and of <s>Sugrīva</s>'s counsel,

children.text: anurāgaṃ ca vīryaṃ ca saumitrer lakṣmaṇasya ca
children.translated_text: and of the affection and heroism of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, son of <s>Sumitrā</s>;
telling these things, the noble ones went joyfully back the way they had come.
But blessed <s>Rāghava</s> dismissed the divine chariot given by <s>Indra</s>, bright as fire,
and honored <s>Mātali</s>.
Permitted to depart by <s>Rāghava</s>, <s>Mātali</s>, <s>Śakra</s>'s charioteer,

children.text: divyaṃ taṃ ratham āsthāya divam evāruroha saḥ ||
children.translated_text: mounted that divine chariot and ascended straight to heaven.
When that best of heavenly charioteers had ascended to heaven,
<s>Rāghava</s>, filled with supreme joy, embraced <s>Sugrīva</s>.
After embracing <s>Sugrīva</s>, and greeted respectfully by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
he, honored by the best of the monkeys, went to the army camp.
Then <s>Rāma</s> spoke to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
the son of <s>Sumitrā</s>, endowed with courage and blazing in splendor, who was staying nearby:
"Gentle one, consecrate this <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> in <s>Laṅkā</s>,
