children.text: anuraktaṃ ca bhaktaṃ ca mama caivopakāriṇam ||
children.translated_text: who is devoted, loyal, and has rendered service to me.

children.text: eṣa me paramaḥ kāmo yad imaṃ rāvaṇānujam
children.translated_text: This is my highest desire: that I should see this <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, the younger brother of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
gentle one, consecrated in <s>Laṅkā</s>."
Thus addressed by great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, son of <s>Sumitrā</s>,

children.text: tathetyuktvā tu saṃhṛṣṭaḥ sauvarṇaṃ ghaṭam ādade ||
children.translated_text: gladly said, "So be it," and took up a golden jar.
With that jar <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, son of <s>Sumitrā</s>, consecrated <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,
as king in <s>Laṅkā</s>, in the midst of the rākṣasas, by <s>Rāma</s>'s command.
That righteous one consecrated pure-souled <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>;

children.text: tasyāmātyā jahṛṣire bhaktā ye cāsya rākṣasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: his ministers rejoiced, as did the rākṣasas devoted to him.
Seeing <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas, consecrated in <s>Laṅkā</s>,
<s>Rāghava</s>, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, felt the greatest joy.

children.text: sa tad rājyaṃ mahat prāpya rāmadattaṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Having obtained that great kingdom, given by <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>

children.text: prakṛtīḥ sāntvayitvā ca tato rāmam upāgamat ||
children.translated_text: comforted the subjects and then approached <s>Rāma</s>.
Then the delighted night-roaming citizens brought unhusked rice, sweetmeats, parched grain,
and divine flowers for him.

children.text: sa tān gṛhītvā durdharṣo rāghavāya nyavedayat
children.translated_text: The unconquerable, heroic one accepted them and presented

children.text: maṅgalyaṃ maṅgalaṃ sarvaṃ lakṣmaṇāya ca vīryavān ||
children.translated_text: all those auspicious and propitious offerings to <s>Rāghava</s> and to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Seeing <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> successful in his task and prospering in his aim,
<s>Rāma</s> accepted it all, wishing to please him.

children.text: tataḥ śailopamaṃ vīraṃ prāñjaliṃ pārśvataḥ sthitam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāghava</s> spoke these words to the heroic <s>Hanūmān</s>,
who stood nearby with joined palms and was like a mountain,
"After honoring this great king <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, gentle one,
enter <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s house and approach with humility.
Tell <s>Vaidehī</s> that I am well, together with <s>Sugrīva</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: ācakṣva jayatāṃ śreṣṭha rāvaṇaṃ ca mayā hatam ||
children.translated_text: O best of victors, and that <s>Rāvaṇa</s> has been slain by me.
Having told this welcome news to <s>Maithilī</s>, O lord of monkeys,
you should receive her message and return."
Thus commanded, <s>Hanūmān</s>, son of the Wind,
entered the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>, honored by the night-roamers.
Having entered <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s dwelling, the greatly radiant one

children.text: dadarśa śaśinā hīnāṃ sātaṅkām iva rohiṇīm ||
children.translated_text: saw her like <s>Rohiṇī</s>, anxious and bereft of the moon.
Restrained, bowed, and humble, he approached, saluted her,
and began to report all of <s>Rāma</s>'s words.
"<s>Vaidehī</s>, <s>Rāma</s> is well, together with <s>Sugrīva</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>;
having achieved his purpose and slain his enemy, the subduer of foes asks after your welfare.
With the help of <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, by <s>Rāma</s> together with the monkeys,

children.text: nihato rāvaṇo devi lakṣmaṇasya nayena ca ||
children.translated_text: and through <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s strategy, O lady, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> has been slain.

children.text: pṛṣṭvā ca kuśalaṃ rāmo vīrastvāṃ raghunandanaḥ
children.translated_text: After asking of your welfare, heroic <s>Rāma</s>, delight of the <s>Raghus</s>,
spoke to you, supremely pleased in his heart because his purpose was fulfilled.

children.text: priyam ākhyāmi te devi tvāṃ tu bhūyaḥ sabhājaye
children.translated_text: I tell you welcome news, O lady, and I honor you once more:

children.text: diṣṭyā jīvasi dharmajñe jayena mama saṃyuge ||
children.translated_text: by good fortune you live, knower of <s>dharma</s> (righteous conduct), through my victory in battle.

children.text: labdho no vijayaḥ sīte svasthā bhava gatavyathā
children.translated_text: We have won victory, <s>Sītā</s>; be at ease, your pain gone.

children.text: rāvaṇaḥ sa hataḥ śatrur laṅkā ceyaṃ vaśe sthitā ||
children.translated_text: That enemy <s>Rāvaṇa</s> has been slain, and this <s>Laṅkā</s> stands under our control.
For I, sleepless and firmly resolved to recover you,
have carried this vow through, after building a bridge over the great ocean.
You should feel no alarm while living in <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s palace,
for the lordship of <s>Laṅkā</s> has been placed under <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>'s authority.
So take heart; trusting, you move about in your own house.
And he is coming here delighted, eager to see you."
When she had been addressed in this way, moon-faced <s>Sītā</s> sprang up,
but, choked by joy, she said nothing at all.
Then the best of monkeys spoke to <s>Sītā</s>, who did not answer:

children.text: kiṃ tvaṃ cintayase devi kiṃ ca māṃ nābhibhāṣase ||
children.translated_text: "What are you thinking of, O lady? Why do you not speak to me?"

children.text: evam uktā hanumatā sītā dharme vyavasthitā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Hanūmān</s>, <s>Sītā</s>, steadfast in <s>dharma</s> (righteous conduct),
answered, supremely pleased, in a voice choked with joy:
"Hearing this welcome news, resting on my husband's victory,
Having fallen under the power of great joy, I am speechless for a moment.

children.text: na hi paśyāmi sadṛśaṃ cintayantī plavaṃgama
children.translated_text: For, as I reflect, O <s>plavaṃgama</s> (monkey), I do not see
any fitting thanks here for you, who have brought news dear to me.

children.text: na ca paśyāmi tat saumya pṛthivyām api vānara
children.translated_text: And I do not see, O gentle monkey, even on the earth,

children.text: sadṛśaṃ matpriyākhyāne tava dātuṃ bhavet samam ||
children.translated_text: anything equal that could be given to you, fitting for this dear news of mine.

children.text: hiraṇyaṃ vā suvarṇaṃ vā ratnāni vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: Gold, or refined gold, or various jewels,

children.text: rājyaṃ vā triṣu lokeṣu naitad arhati bhāṣitum ||
children.translated_text: or sovereignty in the three worlds: none of this deserves to be spoken of.
Thus addressed by <s>Vaidehī</s>, the monkey replied,
standing before <s>Sītā</s> with joined palms uplifted, with these words:
You are devoted to your husband's dear welfare and desire your husband's victory;

children.text: snigdham evaṃvidhaṃ vākyaṃ tvam evārhasi bhāṣitum ||
children.translated_text: you alone are worthy to speak such affectionate words.

children.text: tavaitad vacanaṃ saumye sāravat snigdham eva ca
children.translated_text: This speech of yours, O gentle lady, is full of substance and affection,
and surpasses even a flood of various jewels and the sovereignty of the gods.
In meaning, the excellences beginning with divine sovereignty have been obtained by me,

children.text: hataśatruṃ vijayinaṃ rāmaṃ paśyāmi yat sthitam ||
children.translated_text: since I see <s>Rāma</s> standing victorious, his enemy slain.

children.text: imāstu khalu rākṣasyo yadi tvam anumanyase
children.translated_text: But these rākṣasī women, if you approve,

children.text: hantum icchāmyahaṃ sarvā yābhistvaṃ tarjitā purā ||
children.translated_text: I wish to kill all of them, by whom you were formerly threatened.
When you had gone to the <s>Aśoka</s> grove, suffering, devoted to your husband as your deity,
they were terrifying in form and conduct, cruel, and still more cruel in their glances.

children.text: rākṣasyo dāruṇakathā varam etaṃ prayaccha me
children.translated_text: The rākṣasī women spoke harsh words; grant me this boon.

children.text: icchāmi vividhair ghātair hantum etāḥ sudāruṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: I wish to kill these exceedingly cruel women with various kinds of slaughter.
With fists, with hands, and with feet, O beautiful one,
with dreadful blows of the knees, and with the knocking out of their teeth,
with biting off ears and noses, and likewise with tearing out hair,
with their mouths made terribly dry, and with harsh tramplings and blows,
with many such kinds of insults and injuries, O illustrious lady,
I wish to kill these women who have sinned against you, O goddess.
Thus addressed by <s>Hanumān</s>, <s>Vaidehī</s>, daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,
the illustrious lady spoke to <s>Hanumān</s> words joined with <s>dharma</s> (righteousness):
Who would be angry, O best of monkeys, at women subject to royal authority,

children.text: vidheyānāṃ ca dāsīnāṃ kaḥ kupyed vānarottama ||
children.translated_text: acting under another's command, obedient slave-women as they are?
Through the conjunction of unequal fortune, and through former misconduct,
all this is being experienced by me; indeed one enjoys the fruit of one's own act.
It is certain that this was to be attained by me through the turn of my condition.
Weak as I am here, I forgive the slave-women of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Ordered by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, these rākṣasī women threatened me;

children.text: hate tasminna kuryur hi tarjanaṃ vānarottama ||
children.translated_text: when he is slain, O best of monkeys, they would not make such threats.
There is an old verse, joined with <s>dharma</s> (righteous teaching),

children.text: ṛkṣeṇa gītaḥ śloko me taṃ nibodha plavaṃgama ||
children.translated_text: sung by a bear near a tiger; learn it from me, O monkey.

children.text: na paraḥ pāpam ādatte pareṣāṃ pāpakarmaṇām
children.translated_text: One person does not take on the sin
of the sinful deeds of others; an agreement must be kept, and the good are adorned by conduct.

children.text: pāpānāṃ vā śubhānāṃ vā vadhārhāṇāṃ plavaṃgama
children.translated_text: Toward the wicked or the good, toward those who deserve death, O monkey,
compassion must be shown by a noble person; there is no one who does not offend.
Even toward rākṣasas who roam about harming the world, who can assume forms at will,

children.text: kurvatām api pāpāni naiva kāryam aśobhanam ||
children.translated_text: and who commit sins, an unseemly act should not be done.
Thus addressed by <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Hanumān</s>, skilled in speech,
then replied to <s>Sītā</s>, the illustrious wife of <s>Rāma</s>:
You are truly the illustrious lawful wife of <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: pratisaṃdiśa māṃ devi gamiṣye yatra rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Give me your message, O goddess; I shall go where <s>Rāghava</s> is.
Thus addressed by <s>Hanumān</s>, <s>Vaidehī</s>, daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,
said, I wish to see my husband, O best of monkeys.
Hearing that statement of hers, <s>Hanumān</s>, son of the Wind,
gladdening <s>Maithilī</s>, the greatly radiant one spoke these words:
O noble lady, you will see <s>Rāma</s>, whose face is like the full moon, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
firm in friendship and with his enemy slain, like <s>Śacī</s> seeing the lord of the thirty gods.

children.text: tām evam uktvā rājantīṃ sītāṃ sākṣād iva śriyam
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken to shining <s>Sītā</s>, who was like fortune itself in visible form,
swift <s>Hanumān</s> went to where <s>Rāghava</s> was.
Approaching <s>Rāma</s>, the very wise monkey,
who understood meaning, spoke a word to that best of all bowmen:
That goddess, for whose sake this undertaking was made and the fruit of deeds has arisen,

children.text: tāṃ devīṃ śokasaṃtaptāṃ maithilīṃ draṣṭum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Maithilī</s>, scorched by grief, you ought to see.
For <s>Maithilī</s>, filled with sorrow and with eyes clouded by tears,

children.text: maithilī vijayaṃ śrutvā tava harṣam upāgamat ||
children.translated_text: on hearing of your victory, came to joy.
And because of the trust from before, she, having confidence in me, said:
I wish to see my husband, his purpose accomplished, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: evam ukto hanumatā rāmo dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Hanumān</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, best of those who uphold <s>dharma</s> (righteousness),
suddenly fell into thought and was flooded with tears.

children.text: dīrgham uṣṇaṃ ca niśvasya medinīm avalokayan
children.translated_text: Sighing long and hotly, and looking down at the earth,
he spoke to <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, who stood nearby and resembled a cloud:
Bring <s>Vaidehī</s>, <s>Sītā</s>, here at once, bathed from head to foot,
anointed with divine cosmetics and adorned with divine ornaments.
Thus addressed by <s>Rāma</s>, the hurried <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>
entered the inner apartments and urged <s>Sītā</s> through his own women:
O <s>Vaidehī</s>, anointed with divine cosmetics and adorned with divine ornaments,

children.text: yānam āroha bhadraṃ te bhartā tvāṃ draṣṭum icchati ||
children.translated_text: mount the vehicle; good fortune to you. Your husband wishes to see you.

children.text: evam uktā tu vaidehī pratyuvāca vibhīṣaṇam
children.translated_text: But thus addressed, <s>Vaidehī</s> replied to <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>:
Unbathed, O lord of rākṣasas, I wish to see my husband.
Having heard those words of hers, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> replied:

children.text: yathāhaṃ rāmo bhartā te tat tathā kartum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: "As <s>Rāma</s>, your husband, has said, so you should do."
Hearing that speech of his, <s>Maithilī</s>, who regarded her husband's brother as a deity,
virtuous and vowed to devotion to her husband, replied, "So be it."
Then <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> brought <s>Sītā</s>, bathed from the head and adorned by young women,
furnished with very costly ornaments and wearing very costly garments,
having placed her in a shining palanquin covered with most precious cloth,
and guarded by many rākṣasas.
Approaching the great-souled one, and knowing that he was absorbed in thought,
he bowed down, rejoiced, and announced that <s>Sītā</s> had arrived.
Hearing that she had come, after dwelling long in a rākṣasa's house,

children.text: harṣo dainyaṃ ca roṣaśca trayaṃ rāghavam āviśat ||
children.translated_text: joy, dejection, and anger, all three, entered <s>Rāghava</s>.
Then, seeing <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> standing at his side, <s>Rāghava</s>, reflecting and considering,
not rejoicing, spoke this word to him:
"Gentle lord of rākṣasas, ever intent on my victory,
let <s>Vaidehī</s> quickly come near me."
Understanding that command of <s>Rāghava</s>, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>
at once caused an effort to be made everywhere to clear the way.
There men in tunics and turbans, holding staffs and rattling canes,
went about on every side, driving people away.

children.text: ṛkṣāṇāṃ vānarāṇāṃ ca rākṣasānāṃ ca sarvataḥ
children.translated_text: From every side the groups of bears, vānaras, and rākṣasas,
as they were being driven off, then withdrew far away.
As all of them were being driven away, a sound arose,
like the roar of the ocean being stirred up by the wind.
Seeing them being driven away on every side and thrown into confusion,
<s>Rāghava</s>, out of courtesy and out of indignation at that, restrained them.
Angered, <s>Rāma</s> spoke, as if burning with his eyes,
this reproachful word to the very wise <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>:

children.text: kimarthaṃ mām anādṛtya kliśyate 'yaṃ tvayā janaḥ
children.translated_text: "Why, disregarding me, are these people being troubled by you?
Stop this undertaking; these people are my own people.

children.text: na gṛhāṇi na vastrāṇi na prākārāstiraskriyāḥ
children.translated_text: Not houses, nor garments, nor ramparts, nor acts of concealment,
nor such royal honors as these are a woman's covering; conduct is her covering.

children.text: vyasaneṣu na kṛcchreṣu na yuddhe na svayaṃvare
children.translated_text: In calamities, in hardships, in battle, at a svayaṃvara (self-choice of a husband),

children.text: na kratau no vivāhe ca darśanaṃ duṣyate striyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: at a sacrifice, and at a wedding, the sight of a woman is not blameworthy.

children.text: saiṣā yuddhagatā caiva kṛcchre mahati ca sthitā
children.translated_text: This woman has come from war itself and stands in great hardship;
there should be no fault in seeing her, especially in my presence.

children.text: tad ānaya samīpaṃ me śīghram enāṃ vibhīṣaṇa
children.translated_text: Therefore bring her near me quickly, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>.

children.text: sītā paśyatu mām eṣā suhṛdgaṇavṛtaṃ sthitam ||
children.translated_text: Let this <s>Sītā</s> see me standing surrounded by a circle of friends."
Thus addressed by <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, after reflection,
brought <s>Sītā</s> near to <s>Rāma</s>, modestly and obediently.
Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and <s>Sugrīva</s>, and <s>Hanūmān</s> the vāṇara,

children.text: niśamya vākyaṃ rāmasya babhūvur vyathitā bhṛśam ||
children.translated_text: hearing <s>Rāma</s>'s words, became deeply distressed.
From his harsh gestures, as though indifferent to his wife,

children.text: aprītam iva sītāyāṃ tarkayanti sma rāghavam ||
children.translated_text: they began to suppose that <s>Rāghava</s> was displeased with <s>Sītā</s>.
But <s>Maithilī</s>, shrinking into her own limbs from shame,
followed by <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, approached her husband.
With her face covered by her garment, out of shame in the public assembly,
she wept as she came to her husband, saying, "Noble prince."
Lamenting from astonishment, great joy, and affection,
she, whose face was yet more gentle, looked up at her husband's gentle face.

children.text: atha samapanudanmanaḥklamaṃ sā suciram adṛṣṭam udīkṣya vai priyasya
children.translated_text: Then, seeing the face of her beloved, unseen for a very long time,
she cast off the weariness of her mind and became like one whose face resembled a spotless moon with the beauty of the risen full moon.

children.text: tāṃ tu pārśve sthitāṃ prahvāṃ rāmaḥ samprekṣya maithilīm
children.translated_text: But when <s>Rāma</s> looked at <s>Maithilī</s> standing at his side, bent forward,
with anger hidden inside his heart, he began to speak.

children.text: eṣāsi nirjitā bhadre śatruṃ jitvā mayā raṇe
children.translated_text: "Here you are, won back, noble lady, after I defeated the enemy in battle.

children.text: pauruṣād yad anuṣṭheyaṃ tad etad upapāditam ||
children.translated_text: What had to be accomplished by manly valor has now been accomplished.
I have reached the limit of my indignation; the outrage has been wiped away.
Dishonor and the enemy have been uprooted by me at the same time.

children.text: adya me pauruṣaṃ dṛṣṭam adya me saphalaḥ śramaḥ
children.translated_text: Today my valor has been seen; today my labor has borne fruit.
Today, because my vow has been fulfilled, I am master of myself here.

children.text: yā tvaṃ virahitā nītā calacittena rakṣasā
children.translated_text: You, separated from me, were carried off by a rākṣasa of fickle mind;
the fault brought about by fate has been conquered by me, a man.
When a man does not wipe away the dishonor that has befallen him by his energy,
what purpose of manhood is there for that man of little spirit?
The crossing of the ocean and the crushing of <s>Laṅkā</s>:

children.text: saphalaṃ tasya tacchlāghyam adya karma hanūmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: that praiseworthy deed of <s>Hanūmān</s> is today fruitful.
The labor of <s>Sugrīva</s>, together with his army,
as he fought bravely in battle and gave counsel for my good, is today fruitful.

children.text: nirguṇaṃ bhrātaraṃ tyaktvā yo māṃ svayam upasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: For <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, my devoted follower, who abandoned his worthless brother
and came to me of his own accord, the labor is today fruitful.
As <s>Rāma</s> spoke that speech in this way, <s>Sītā</s>
became flooded with tears, her eyes opened wide like those of a doe.
But as <s>Rāma</s> looked at her, anger came over him again,
like a blazing fire drenched with abundant ghee.
He knit a frown upon his face, with eyes glancing askance,
he spoke harshly to <s>Sītā</s> in the midst of the vānaras and rākṣasas:
"Whatever should be done by a man wiping away an outrage,

children.text: tat kṛtaṃ sakalaṃ sīte śatruhastād amarṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: all of that has been done, <s>Sītā</s>, from indignation at your being in the enemy's hand.
You have been won back, as the living world's southern quarter was subdued
by the sage <s>Agastya</s>, hard to assail and with his self purified by austerity.
And let it be known, welfare to you, that this toil of battle

children.text: sa tīrṇaḥ suhṛdāṃ vīryānna tvadarthaṃ mayā kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: has been crossed through the valor of friends; it was not undertaken by me for your sake.

children.text: rakṣatā tu mayā vṛttam apavādaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Rather, it was done by me while guarding my own conduct and removing public reproach in every way,
and while wiping away disgrace from my renowned family line.
Standing before me with your character now fallen under suspicion,
you are firmly repugnant to me, like a lamp to a man diseased in the eyes.
Therefore go, permitted by me, wherever you wish, daughter of <s>Janaka</s>.

children.text: etā daśa diśo bhadre kāryam asti na me tvayā ||
children.translated_text: These ten directions are open to you, good lady; I have no use for you.

children.text: kaḥ pumān hi kule jātaḥ striyaṃ paragṛhoṣitām
children.translated_text: For what man born in a noble family, a man of spirit, would take back a woman
who had lived in another's house, merely with a heart moved by affection?
You have slipped from <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s lap and have been seen by his wicked eye;
how could I take you back again while claiming a great lineage?

children.text: tadarthaṃ nirjitā me tvaṃ yaśaḥ pratyāhṛtaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: It was for that purpose that you were won back by me; my fame has been recovered by me.

children.text: nāsti me tvayyabhiṣvaṅgo yatheṣṭaṃ gamyatām itaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I have no attachment to you; go from here as you wish.
Thus, good lady, this has been said by me with a fixed resolve.

children.text: lakṣmaṇe bharate vā tvaṃ kuru buddhiṃ yathāsukham ||
children.translated_text: Set your mind as you please on <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> or on <s>Bharata</s>,
or on <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the vānaras, or on <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas;

children.text: niveśaya manaḥ sīte yathā vā sukham ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: place your heart, <s>Sītā</s>, wherever it may be agreeable to yourself.

children.text: na hi tvāṃ rāvaṇo dṛṣṭvā divyarūpāṃ manoramām
children.translated_text: For <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, seeing you of divine beauty and lovely form,
would not have endured for long, <s>Sītā</s>, your moving about within his own house."

children.text: tataḥ priyārhaśravaṇā tad apriyaṃ priyād upaśrutya cirasya maithilī
children.translated_text: Then <s>Maithilī</s>, whose ears deserved dear words, hearing after so long that unwelcome speech from her beloved,

children.text: mumoca bāṣpaṃ subhṛśaṃ pravepitā gajendrahastābhihateva vallarī ||
children.translated_text: trembled and let fall abundant tears, like a creeper struck by the trunk of a lordly elephant.

children.text: evam uktā tu vaidehī paruṣaṃ lomaharṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Rāghava</s> in harsh, hair-raising words,
<s>Vaidehī</s> became deeply distressed under his anger.

children.text: sā tad aśrutapūrvaṃ hi jane mahati maithilī
children.translated_text: In that great assembly, <s>Maithilī</s>, hearing for the first time
the rough words of her husband, became ashamed and abashed.
The daughter of <s>Janaka</s> seemed to shrink into her very own limbs,
and, as if pierced by those arrow-like words, she shed tears in abundance.
Then, wiping her own face, which was drenched with tears,

children.text: śanair gadgadayā vācā bhartāram idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: she slowly said this to her husband in a voice choked with sobs:

children.text: kiṃ mām asadṛśaṃ vākyam īdṛśaṃ śrotradāruṇam
children.translated_text: "Why do you make me hear such unfitting words,

children.text: rūkṣaṃ śrāvayase vīra prākṛtaḥ prākṛtām iva ||
children.translated_text: harsh and cruel to the ear, O hero, as a common man would address a common woman?

children.text: na tathāsmi mahābāho yathā tvam avagacchasi
children.translated_text: I am not as you understand me to be, O mighty-armed one.

children.text: pratyayaṃ gaccha me svena cāritreṇaiva te śape ||
children.translated_text: Put trust in me through my own conduct; by that very conduct I swear to you.

children.text: pṛthak strīṇāṃ pracāreṇa jātiṃ tvaṃ pariśaṅkase
children.translated_text: By the behavior of women in general you suspect the whole class of women;

children.text: parityajemāṃ śaṅkāṃ tu yadi te 'haṃ parīkṣitā ||
children.translated_text: but abandon this suspicion if I have been tested by you.
If I came into contact with another's body helplessly, my lord,

children.text: kāmakāro na me tatra daivaṃ tatrāparādhyati ||
children.translated_text: there was no act of desire on my part in that; fate is at fault there.

children.text: madadhīnaṃ tu yat tanme hṛdayaṃ tvayi vartate
children.translated_text: But what is under my control, that heart of mine, remains fixed on you.
What can I do, powerless as I am, about limbs that are under another's control?
Because of affection grown up through living together, and because of our intimacy, O giver of honor,

children.text: yadyahaṃ te na vijñātā hatā tenāsmi śāśvatam ||
children.translated_text: if I am not known by you, then by that I am destroyed forever.
When the brave <s>Hanūmān</s> was sent by you as a scout,

children.text: laṅkāsthāhaṃ tvayā vīra kiṃ tadā na visarjitā ||
children.translated_text: while I was in <s>Laṅkā</s>, O hero, why was I not abandoned by you then?
In the very presence of the lord of the vānaras, immediately after your message,

children.text: tvayā saṃtyaktayā vīra tyaktaṃ syājjīvitaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: if I had been rejected by you, O hero, I would have given up my life.

children.text: na vṛthā te śramo 'yaṃ syāt saṃśaye nyasya jīvitam
children.translated_text: This labor of yours would not have been in vain, with life placed in uncertainty,
nor would this distress of your friends have been fruitless.
But you, tiger among men, following anger alone,
have set my womanhood foremost, like a petty man.
My derivation from <s>Janaka</s> is only by designation; my true birth was from the surface of the earth.

children.text: mama vṛttaṃ ca vṛttajña bahu te na puraskṛtam ||
children.translated_text: And my conduct too, O knower of conduct, has not been given much weight by you.

children.text: na pramāṇīkṛtaḥ pāṇir bālye bālena pīḍitaḥ
children.translated_text: The hand taken by you in childhood, when you too were a boy, has not been treated as proof;

children.text: mama bhaktiśca śīlaṃ ca sarvaṃ te pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: my devotion and my character, all of it, have been cast behind your back."
Speaking thus, weeping, and talking in a voice choked with tears,

children.text: abravīl lakṣmaṇaṃ sītā dīnaṃ dhyānaparaṃ sthitam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s> addressed <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, who stood there wretched and absorbed in thought:

children.text: citāṃ me kuru saumitre vyasanasyāsya bheṣajam
children.translated_text: "Build me a pyre, <s>Saumitri</s>, as a remedy for this calamity.
Struck down by false reproach, I cannot bear to live.
Abandoned in the public assembly by a husband not pleased with my virtues,

children.text: yā kṣamā me gatir gantuṃ pravekṣye havyavāhanam ||
children.translated_text: I shall enter the fire, the carrier of oblations; that is the fitting path for me to go."
When <s>Vaidehī</s> had spoken thus, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, slayer of enemy heroes,
overcome by indignation, looked toward <s>Rāghava</s>'s face.
Understanding the inclination of <s>Rāma</s>'s mind, signaled by his expression,

children.text: citāṃ cakāra saumitrir mate rāmasya vīryavān ||
children.translated_text: the valiant <s>Saumitri</s> made a pyre in accordance with <s>Rāma</s>'s intention.

children.text: adhomukhaṃ tato rāmaṃ śanaiḥ kṛtvā pradakṣiṇam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vaidehī</s> slowly circumambulated <s>Rāma</s>, who had lowered his face,
and approached the blazing fire.
Having bowed to the deities and to the brāhmaṇas, <s>Maithilī</s>,
with her hollowed palms joined, spoke this near the fire:

children.text: yathā me hṛdayaṃ nityaṃ nāpasarpati rāghavāt
children.translated_text: "As my heart never turns away from <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: tathā lokasya sākṣī māṃ sarvataḥ pātu pāvakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so may <s>Pāvaka</s>, witness of the world, protect me on every side."

children.text: evam uktvā tu vaidehī parikramya hutāśanam
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Vaidehī</s>, after circumambulating the fire,
She entered the blazing fire with an inward self free from attachment.
There, that very great crowd, filled with children and elders,
saw <s>Maithilī</s> there as she entered the fire-oblation bearer.

children.text: tasyām agniṃ viśantyāṃ tu hāheti vipulaḥ svanaḥ
children.translated_text: But as she was entering the fire, a vast cry of "Alas! alas!"
arose among the rākṣasas and the vānaras, like something wondrous.
Then King <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, and <s>Yama</s>, crusher of enemies,
and the thousand-eyed great <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s>, scorcher of foes,
and the blessed <s>Mahādeva</s>, bull-bannered, with three eyes,

children.text: kartā sarvasya lokasya brahmā brahmavidāṃ varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Brahmā</s>, maker of the whole world, best of knowers of brahman,
all these, gathering together in aerial cars like the sun,
came to the city of <s>Laṅkā</s> and approached <s>Rāghava</s>.
Then, raising their broad arms adorned with bracelets,
the best of the thirty gods spoke to <s>Rāghava</s>, who stood with joined palms:

children.text: kartā sarvasya lokasya śreṣṭho jñānavatāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: "You are the maker of the whole world, the foremost, best of those who possess knowledge.
How can you disregard <s>Sītā</s> as she falls into the carrier of oblations?
How do you not recognize yourself as the best of the hosts of gods?

children.text: ṛtadhāmā vasuḥ pūrvaṃ vasūnāṃ ca prajāpatiḥ
children.translated_text: You were formerly <s>Ṛtadhāman</s>, a <s>Vasu</s>, and lord of the <s>Vasus</s>;

children.text: tvaṃ trayāṇāṃ hi lokānām ādikartā svayamprabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: for you are the prime creator of the three worlds, self-luminous.

children.text: rudrāṇām aṣṭamo rudraḥ sādhyānām api pañcamaḥ
children.translated_text: Among the <s>Rudras</s> you are the eighth <s>Rudra</s>, and among the <s>Sādhyas</s> the fifth.

children.text: aśvinau cāpi te karṇau candrasūryau ca cakṣuṣī ||
children.translated_text: The two <s>Aśvins</s> are your ears, and the moon and sun are your eyes.

children.text: ante cādau ca lokānāṃ dṛśyase tvaṃ paraṃtapa
children.translated_text: At the end and at the beginning of worlds you are seen, scorcher of foes,

children.text: upekṣase ca vaidehīṃ mānuṣaḥ prākṛto yathā ||
children.translated_text: and yet you disregard <s>Vaidehī</s> like an ordinary human being.
Thus addressed by those world-protectors, <s>Rāghava</s>, lord of the world,
<s>Rāma</s>, best of those who uphold <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), spoke to the best of the thirty gods:
"I consider myself a human being, <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>.

children.text: yo 'haṃ yasya yataścāhaṃ bhagavāṃstad bravītu me ||
children.translated_text: Who I am, whose I am, and whence I am, let the blessed one tell me that."

children.text: iti bruvāṇaṃ kākutsthaṃ brahmā brahmavidāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: To <s>Kākutstha</s>, speaking thus, <s>Brahmā</s>, best of knowers of brahman,
said, "Hear from me the truth, <s>Rāma</s>, you whose valor is true.
You are the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the blessed, all-pervading one armed with the discus.
You are the one-tusked <s>Varāha</s>, conqueror of enemies past and future.

children.text: akṣaraṃ brahmasatyaṃ ca madhye cānte ca rāghava
children.translated_text: You are the imperishable, brahman, and truth, in the middle and at the end, <s>Rāghava</s>.
You are the supreme <s>dharma</s> (cosmic order) of the worlds, <s>Viṣvaksena</s>, four-armed.
You bear the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow; you are <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, the Person, the supreme Person.
You are unconquered, sword-bearing <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and also <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> of great strength.

children.text: senānīr grāmaṇīśca tvaṃ buddhiḥ sattvaṃ kṣamā damaḥ
children.translated_text: You are the general and the leader; you are intelligence, being, patience, and self-restraint.
You are both origin and dissolution, <s>Upendra</s>, slayer of <s>Madhu</s>.
You perform <s>Indra</s>'s deeds; you are great <s>Indra</s>, <s>Padmanābha</s>, maker of an end to battle.

children.text: śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ ca tvām āhur divyā maharṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The divine great seers call you refuge and the one worthy of refuge.
You are thousand-horned, whose self is the Veda, hundred-tongued, great bull.
You are the sacrifice, you are the vaṣaṭ-call, you are the oṃ-syllable, scorcher of foes.

children.text: prabhavaṃ nidhanaṃ vā te na viduḥ ko bhavān iti
children.translated_text: They do not know your origin or your end, nor who you are.

children.text: dṛśyase sarvabhūteṣu brāhmaṇeṣu ca goṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: You are seen in all beings, and among brahmins and cows.

children.text: dikṣu sarvāsu gagane parvateṣu vaneṣu ca
children.translated_text: In all directions, in the sky, on mountains, and in forests,
you are thousand-footed, blessed, hundred-headed, thousand-bearing.

children.text: tvaṃ dhārayasi bhūtāni vasudhāṃ ca saparvatām
children.translated_text: You support beings, and the earth together with its mountains.

children.text: ante pṛthivyāḥ salile dṛśyase tvaṃ mahoragaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the end of the earth, in the waters, you are seen as the great serpent.
You support the three worlds, <s>Rāma</s>, together with gods, gandharvas, and dānavas.

children.text: ahaṃ te hṛdayaṃ rāma jihvā devī sarasvatī ||
children.translated_text: I am your heart, <s>Rāma</s>; the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> is your tongue.

children.text: devā gātreṣu lomāni nirmitā brahmaṇā prabho
children.translated_text: The gods are the hairs on your limbs, created by <s>Brahmā</s>, lord.
The closing of your eyes became night; the opening of your eyes became day.

children.text: saṃskārāste 'bhavan vedā na tad asti tvayā vinā
children.translated_text: The <s>saṃskāras</s> (sacred rites) became the Vedas; there is nothing apart from you.

children.text: jagat sarvaṃ śarīraṃ te sthairyaṃ te vasudhātalam ||
children.translated_text: The whole universe is your body; the solid earth is your stability.
Fire is your anger, and <s>Soma</s> your grace, you who bear the mark of <s>Śrīvatsa</s>.
By you the three worlds were formerly traversed in three strides.

children.text: mahendraśca kṛto rājā baliṃ baddhvā mahāsuram
children.translated_text: And great <s>Indra</s> was made king after you bound the great asura <s>Bali</s>.

children.text: sītā lakṣmīr bhavān viṣṇur devaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ prajāpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s> is <s>Lakṣmī</s>; you are <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the god <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, lord of creatures.
For the purpose of killing <s>Rāvaṇa</s> here you entered a human body.

children.text: tad idaṃ naḥ kṛtaṃ kāryaṃ tvayā dharmabhṛtāṃ vara ||
children.translated_text: Therefore this task of ours has been accomplished by you, best of those who uphold <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: nihato rāvaṇo rāma prahṛṣṭo divam ākrama
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s> has been slain, <s>Rāma</s>; rejoice and ascend to heaven.
Your strength and heroism are unfailing; your prowess is unfailing.
And those men who are devoted to you will be unfailing.

children.text: ye tvāṃ devaṃ dhruvaṃ bhaktāḥ purāṇaṃ puruṣottamam
children.translated_text: Those people who are steadfast devotees of you, the god, the ancient supreme Person,

children.text: ye narāḥ kīrtayiṣyanti nāsti teṣāṃ parābhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and who will praise you, there is no defeat for them."
Having heard this auspicious speech uttered by the grandfather,
the fire, taking <s>Vaidehī</s> in his lap, rose up.
She shone like the young sun, adorned with refined gold ornaments,
wearing red garments, young, with dark curling hair.
Her garlands and ornaments were unwithered; she was just as before, high-minded.

children.text: dadau rāmāya vaidehīm aṅke kṛtvā vibhāvasuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Taking <s>Vaidehī</s> on his lap, the fire gave her to <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: abravīcca tadā rāmaṃ sākṣī lokasya pāvakaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Pāvaka</s>, witness of the world, spoke to <s>Rāma</s>:

children.text: eṣā te rāma vaidehī pāpam asyā na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: "This is your <s>Vaidehī</s>, <s>Rāma</s>; there is no sin in her.

children.text: naiva vācā na manasā nānudhyānānna cakṣuṣā
children.translated_text: Not by speech, nor by mind, nor by thought, nor by sight,

children.text: suvṛttā vṛttaśauṇḍīrā na tvām aticacāra ha ||
children.translated_text: has this woman of good conduct, skilled in virtue, ever transgressed against you.
She was carried off by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, that rākṣasa arrogant in his strength,

children.text: tvayā virahitā dīnā vivaśā nirjanād vanāt ||
children.translated_text: helpless, wretched, separated from you, from the lonely forest.
Confined and guarded in the inner apartments, she kept her mind on you and was devoted to you."
She was guarded by bands of rākṣasī women, deformed and terrible to behold.
<s>Maithilī</s>, though tempted in various ways and also threatened,
did not think of that rākṣasa, for her inner self was fixed on you.
Accept her, <s>Rāghava</s>, whose disposition is pure and who is sinless.

children.text: na kiṃcid abhidhātavyam aham ājñāpayāmi te ||
children.translated_text: Nothing more need be said; I command you.
Thus addressed, the greatly radiant, steadfast, firmly valorous
<s>Rāma</s>, the best of upholders of <s>dharma</s>, spoke to the chief of the thirty gods.

children.text: avaśyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu sītā pāvanam arhati
children.translated_text: Certainly, in the three worlds, <s>Sītā</s> deserves purification,
for this auspicious woman has dwelt for a long time in <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s inner palace.
'<s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, is indeed childish and ruled by desire,'

children.text: iti vakṣyanti māṃ santo jānakīm aviśodhya hi ||
children.translated_text: so good people would say of me, if I did not test <s>Jānakī</s>.
I also know <s>Maithilī</s>, daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,
to have an undivided heart, devoted, and guarded by her thought of me.
But for the sake of assurance to the three worlds, I, who take refuge in truth,
even disregarded <s>Vaidehī</s> as she entered the fire.

children.text: imām api viśālākṣīṃ rakṣitāṃ svena tejasā
children.translated_text: Even this wide-eyed woman, protected by her own splendor,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> could not transgress, just as the great ocean cannot cross its shore.

children.text: na hi śaktaḥ sa duṣṭātmā manasāpi hi maithilīm
children.translated_text: For that wicked-souled one was not able even in thought
to violate unattainable <s>Maithilī</s>, like a blazing tongue of fire.
This auspicious woman does not belong to lordship in <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s inner palace.

children.text: ananyā hi mayā sītāṃ bhāskareṇa prabhā yathā ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Sītā</s> is not other than I, as light is not other than the sun.
<s>Maithilī</s>, daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, is pure in the three worlds.

children.text: na hi hātum iyaṃ śakyā kīrtir ātmavatā yathā ||
children.translated_text: She cannot be abandoned, just as fame cannot be abandoned by a self-possessed man.

children.text: avaśyaṃ ca mayā kāryaṃ sarveṣāṃ vo vaco hitam
children.translated_text: And I must necessarily do what is beneficial, the word of all of you,

children.text: snigdhānāṃ lokamānyānām evaṃ ca bruvatāṃ hitam ||
children.translated_text: who are affectionate, honored by the world, and speaking what is beneficial in this way.

children.text: itīdam uktvā vacanaṃ mahābalaiḥ praśasyamānaḥ svakṛtena karmaṇā
children.translated_text: Having spoken this speech, <s>Rāma</s>, praised by the mighty for the deed he had done,

children.text: sametya rāmaḥ priyayā mahābalaḥ sukhaṃ sukhārho 'nubabhūva rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: joined with his beloved, and mighty <s>Rāghava</s>, worthy of happiness, enjoyed happiness.
Hearing this auspicious speech, well spoken by <s>Rāghava</s>,
<s>Maheśvara</s> uttered this still more auspicious speech.
Lotus-eyed one, great-armed one, broad-chested scorcher of foes,

children.text: diṣṭyā kṛtam idaṃ karma tvayā śastrabhṛtāṃ vara ||
children.translated_text: fortunately this deed has been done by you, best of weapon-bearers.

children.text: diṣṭyā sarvasya lokasya pravṛddhaṃ dāruṇaṃ tamaḥ
children.translated_text: Fortunately the fierce, greatly increased darkness over the whole world,

children.text: apāvṛttaṃ tvayā saṃkhye rāma rāvaṇajaṃ bhayam ||
children.translated_text: the fear born from <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, has been uncovered and removed by you in battle, <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: āśvāsya bharataṃ dīnaṃ kausalyāṃ ca yaśasvinīm
children.translated_text: Having reassured distressed <s>Bharata</s>, and illustrious <s>Kausalyā</s>,

children.text: kaikeyīṃ ca sumitrāṃ ca dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇamātaram ||
children.translated_text: and having seen <s>Kaikeyī</s> and <s>Sumitrā</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s mother,
having obtained the kingship in <s>Ayodhyā</s> and delighted your friends,
and having established the lineage in the family of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s>, great-armed one,
having sacrificed with the horse-sacrifice and obtained unsurpassed fame,

children.text: brāhmaṇebhyo dhanaṃ dattvā tridivaṃ gantum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: and having given wealth to the brāhmaṇas, you may go to heaven.
This king, standing in the aerial car, is your father <s>Daśaratha</s>,
your greatly renowned elder in the human world, <s>Kākutstha</s>.
The glorious one has gone to <s>Indra</s>'s world and has been saved by you, his son.

children.text: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā tvam enam abhivādaya ||
children.translated_text: Together with your brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, pay homage to him.
Hearing <s>Mahādeva</s>'s words, <s>Kākutstha</s>, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
made obeisance to his father, who stood on the summit of the aerial car.
Shining with his own splendor, wearing spotless garments,

children.text: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā dadarśa pitaraṃ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the lord saw his father, together with his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Filled with great joy, the lord of the earth, standing in the aerial car,
then <s>Daśaratha</s> saw his son, dearer than life.
The great-armed lord, seated on an excellent seat, took him onto his lap,
embraced him with both arms, and then began a speech.

children.text: na me svargo bahumataḥ saṃmānaśca surarṣibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Heaven is not highly valued by me, nor honor from the divine seers,

children.text: tvayā rāma vihīnasya satyaṃ pratiśṛṇomi te ||
children.translated_text: when I am separated from you, <s>Rāma</s>; I truly promise you this.

children.text: kaikeyyā yāni coktāni vākyāni vadatāṃ vara
children.translated_text: Those words which were spoken by <s>Kaikeyī</s>, best of speakers,
for the sake of sending you into exile, have remained in my heart.

children.text: tvāṃ tu dṛṣṭvā kuśalinaṃ pariṣvajya salakṣmaṇam
children.translated_text: But seeing you well and embracing you together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: adya duḥkhād vimukto 'smi nīhārād iva bhāskaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: today I am freed from sorrow, like the sun from mist.
I have been saved by you, my son, by a noble son of great spirit,
just as the righteous brāhmaṇa was saved by <s>Aṣṭāvakra</s>.

children.text: idānīṃ ca vijānāmi yathā saumya sureśvaraiḥ
children.translated_text: And now, gentle one, I know how, by the lords of the gods,
the supreme person was appointed here for the killing of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: siddhārthā khalu kausalyā yā tvāṃ rāma gṛhaṃ gatam
children.translated_text: Surely <s>Kausalyā</s> has accomplished her aim, for she, overjoyed, will see you, <s>Rāma</s>,
returned home, come back from the forest, destroyer of foes.

children.text: siddhārthāḥ khalu te rāma narā ye tvāṃ purīṃ gatam
children.translated_text: Surely those men have accomplished their aim, <s>Rāma</s>, who will see you
entered into the city, wet with consecration water, and lord of the earth.
I would wish to see you met with <s>Bharata</s>,

children.text: iccheyaṃ tvām ahaṃ draṣṭuṃ bharatena samāgatam ||
children.translated_text: who is devoted, strong, pure, and walks according to <s>dharma</s>.
Fourteen years, gentle one, have been spent by you in the forest,

children.text: vasatā sītayā sārdhaṃ lakṣmaṇena ca dhīmatā ||
children.translated_text: dwelling with <s>Sītā</s> and with wise <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
You have completed your forest-dwelling; the promise has been made fruitful.

children.text: rāvaṇaṃ ca raṇe hatvā devāste paritoṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And having killed <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle, the gods have been satisfied by you.

children.text: kṛtaṃ karma yaśaḥ ślāghyaṃ prāptaṃ te śatrusūdana
children.translated_text: The deed has been done, and praiseworthy fame has been obtained by you, destroyer of foes.

children.text: bhrātṛbhiḥ saha rājyastho dīrgham āyur avāpnuhi ||
children.translated_text: Established in kingship together with your brothers, obtain a long life.

children.text: iti bruvāṇaṃ rājānaṃ rāmaḥ prāñjalir abravīt
children.translated_text: To the king speaking thus, <s>Rāma</s> spoke with joined palms:

children.text: kuru prasādaṃ dharmajña kaikeyyā bharatasya ca ||
children.translated_text: Show favor, knower of <s>dharma</s>, toward <s>Kaikeyī</s> and <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: saputrāṃ tvāṃ tyajāmīti yad uktā kaikayī tvayā
children.translated_text: What was said by you to <s>Kaikeyī</s>, "I abandon you together with your son,"

children.text: sa śāpaḥ kaikayīṃ ghoraḥ saputrāṃ na spṛśet prabho ||
children.translated_text: may that terrible curse, O lord, not touch <s>Kaikeyī</s> together with her son.

children.text: sa tatheti mahārājo rāmam uktvā kṛtāñjalim
children.translated_text: Saying "So be it" to <s>Rāma</s>, who stood with joined palms, the great king

children.text: lakṣmaṇaṃ ca pariṣvajya punar vākyam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: embraced <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> too, and then spoke again.

children.text: rāmaṃ śuśrūṣatā bhaktyā vaidehyā saha sītayā
children.translated_text: By serving <s>Rāma</s> with devotion, together with <s>Vaidehī</s>, <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: kṛtā mama mahāprītiḥ prāptaṃ dharmaphalaṃ ca te ||
children.translated_text: you have given me great joy, and the fruit of <s>dharma</s> has been obtained by you.

children.text: dharmaṃ prāpsyasi dharmajña yaśaśca vipulaṃ bhuvi
children.translated_text: You will obtain <s>dharma</s>, knower of <s>dharma</s>, and abundant fame on earth;

children.text: rāme prasanne svargaṃ ca mahimānaṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: when <s>Rāma</s> is pleased, you will obtain heaven and likewise greatness.
Serve <s>Rāma</s>; welfare to you, increaser of <s>Sumitrā</s>'s joy.
<s>Rāma</s> is always devoted to the welfare of the whole world.
These three worlds together with <s>Indra</s>, and the siddhas and supreme seers,
approach that great-souled supreme person and worship him.

children.text: etat tad uktam avyaktam akṣaraṃ brahmanirmitam
children.translated_text: He is that unmanifest, imperishable principle spoken of, fashioned by brahman;

children.text: devānāṃ hṛdayaṃ saumya guhyaṃ rāmaḥ paraṃtapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: gentle one, <s>Rāma</s>, scorcher of foes, is the secret and supreme heart of the gods.
The practice of <s>dharma</s> and abundant fame have been obtained by you

children.text: rāmaṃ śuśrūṣatā bhaktyā vaidehyā saha sītayā ||
children.translated_text: through serving <s>Rāma</s> with devotion, together with <s>Vaidehī</s>, <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: sa tathoktvā mahābāhur lakṣmaṇaṃ prāñjaliṃ sthitam
children.translated_text: After speaking thus to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the long-armed king, righteous in soul,

children.text: uvāca rājā dharmātmā vaidehīṃ vacanaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: who stood with joined palms, spoke an auspicious word to <s>Vaidehī</s>.

children.text: kartavyo na tu vaidehi manyustyāgam imaṃ prati
children.translated_text: No anger, O <s>Vaidehī</s>, should be felt with regard to this abandonment;
this was done by <s>Rāma</s>, who sought your welfare, for the sake of proving your purity.

children.text: na tvaṃ subhru samādheyā patiśuśrūṣaṇaṃ prati
children.translated_text: You, fair-browed lady, do not need to be instructed about service to your husband;

children.text: avaśyaṃ tu mayā vācyam eṣa te daivataṃ param ||
children.translated_text: yet I must say this: he is your supreme deity.

children.text: iti pratisamādiśya putrau sītāṃ tathā snuṣām
children.translated_text: Having thus instructed his sons and <s>Sītā</s>, his daughter-in-law,
<s>Daśaratha</s>, blazing, went by aerial car to the world of <s>Indra</s>.
When <s>Kākutstha</s> had departed again, mighty <s>Indra</s>, chastiser of <s>Pāka</s>,
greatly pleased, spoke to <s>Rāghava</s>, who stood with joined palms:
O <s>Rāma</s>, scorcher of foes, your sight of us is not fruitless;
I am joined with affection. Therefore say what your mind desires.
Thus addressed, <s>Kākutstha</s>, with joined palms, replied,

children.text: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā sītayā cāpi bhāryayā ||
children.translated_text: together with his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and also with his wife <s>Sītā</s>:
If affection has arisen for me, O lord of all the gods,

children.text: vakṣyāmi kuru me satyaṃ vacanaṃ vadatāṃ vara ||
children.translated_text: I shall speak; make my word true, best of speakers.

children.text: mama hetoḥ parākrāntā ye gatā yamasādanam
children.translated_text: Those who, striving for my sake, have gone to the abode of <s>Yama</s>,

children.text: te sarve jīvitaṃ prāpya samuttiṣṭhantu vānarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: let all those vānaras regain life and rise up.
They were devoted to what was dear to me and did not reckon death;

children.text: tvatprasādāt sameyuste varam etad ahaṃ vṛṇe ||
children.translated_text: by your favor let them be reunited. This is the boon I choose.
Free from disease and free from wounds, endowed with strength and manly valor,
I wish to see the long-tailed vānaras and likewise the bears, O giver of honor.

children.text: akāle cāpi mukhyāni mūlāni ca phalāni ca
children.translated_text: And even out of season, let choice roots and fruits
and clear rivers remain wherever the vānaras are.

children.text: śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tasya rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech of the great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>,
mighty <s>Indra</s> replied with these words marked by affection:
This is a great boon, dear child, that you have spoken, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>.
The monkeys shall rise up as sleepers do when sleep has ended.
With friends, kinsmen, relatives, and their own people,

children.text: sarva eva sameṣyanti saṃyuktāḥ parayā mudā ||
children.translated_text: all of them shall come together, joined with supreme joy.
Out of season the trees shall be variegated with flowers and laden with fruit,
O great archer, and the rivers shall be filled with water.

children.text: savraṇaiḥ prathamaṃ gātraiḥ saṃvṛtair nirvraṇaiḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: At first with wounded limbs, and then with them covered over and unwounded again,

children.text: babhūvur vānarāḥ sarve kim etad iti vismitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all the vānaras came to be, amazed and asking, "What is this?"
Seeing <s>Kākutstha</s> with his purpose fully accomplished, all the best of the gods,
after first praising him who was worthy of praise, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, said:

children.text: gacchāyodhyām ito vīra visarjaya ca vānarān
children.translated_text: Go from here to <s>Ayodhyā</s>, hero, and dismiss the vānaras.
Console this <s>Maithilī</s>, the ascetic lady who is devoted to you.
See your brother <s>Bharata</s>, who practices vows because of grief for you;
have yourself consecrated, and, after going there, gladden the citizens.

children.text: evam uktvā tam āmantrya rāmaṃ saumitriṇā saha
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus and taken leave of <s>Rāma</s> together with <s>Saumitri</s>,

children.text: vimānaiḥ sūryasaṃkāśair hṛṣṭā jagmuḥ surā divam ||
children.translated_text: the gods, delighted, went to heaven in aerial cars bright as the sun.
After bowing to all those best of the thirty gods, <s>Kākutstha</s>,

children.text: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā vāsam ājñāpayat tadā ||
children.translated_text: together with his brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, then ordered a halt for the night.

children.text: tatastu sā lakṣmaṇarāmapālitā mahācamūr hṛṣṭajanā yaśasvinī
children.translated_text: Then that great army, protected by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and <s>Rāma</s>, with its people rejoicing and famous,

children.text: śriyā jvalantī virarāja sarvato niśāpraṇīteva hi śītaraśminā ||
children.translated_text: blazing with splendor, shone on every side like night led by the cool-rayed moon.

children.text: tāṃ rātrim uṣitaṃ rāmaṃ sukhotthitam ariṃdamam
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāma</s>, subduer of enemies, had spent that night and risen happily,

children.text: abravīt prāñjalir vākyaṃ jayaṃ pṛṣṭvā vibhīṣaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, with joined palms, asked about his victory and spoke these words:
Baths, unguents, garments, and ornaments,

children.text: candanāni ca divyāni mālyāni vividhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: divine sandal pastes and various garlands,
and these women skilled in adornment, with eyes like lotuses,
are present; they will bathe you according to rule, O <s>Rāghava</s>.
Thus addressed, <s>Kākutstha</s> replied to <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>:
Invite the vānaras, with <s>Sugrīva</s> at their head, to bathe.

children.text: sa tu tāmyati dharmātmā mama hetoḥ sukhocitaḥ
children.translated_text: For that righteous one, accustomed to comfort, is wasting away for my sake,
the delicate, long-armed prince, faithful to his promise.
Without him, <s>Bharata</s>, the son of <s>Kaikeyī</s>, who practices <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: na me snānaṃ bahumataṃ vastrāṇyābharaṇāni ca ||
children.translated_text: bathing, garments, and ornaments are not highly valued by me.

children.text: ita eva pathā kṣipraṃ pratigacchāma tāṃ purīm
children.translated_text: From here, by this very road, let us quickly return to that city.
For this road leading to <s>Ayodhyā</s> is extremely difficult.
When this had been said, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> replied to <s>Kākutstha</s>:

children.text: ahnā tvāṃ prāpayiṣyāmi tāṃ purīṃ pārthivātmaja ||
children.translated_text: "Son of a king, I shall bring you to that city in a single day.

children.text: puṣpakaṃ nāma bhadraṃ te vimānaṃ sūryasaṃnibham
children.translated_text: Blessings on you; there is an aircraft named <s>Puṣpaka</s>, resembling the sun.
It belonged to my brother <s>Kubera</s>, and was taken by force by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: tad idaṃ meghasaṃkāśaṃ vimānam iha tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: That aircraft, resembling a cloud, stands here now.

children.text: tena yāsyasi yānena tvam ayodhyāṃ gatajvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: By that conveyance you will go to <s>Ayodhyā</s>, free from distress.

children.text: ahaṃ te yadyanugrāhyo yadi smarasi me guṇān
children.translated_text: If I am worthy of favor from you, and if you remember my virtues,

children.text: vasa tāvad iha prājña yadyasti mayi sauhṛdam ||
children.translated_text: then stay here for a while, wise one, if there is friendship toward me.

children.text: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā vaidehyā cāpi bhāryayā
children.translated_text: Together with your brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and with your wife <s>Vaidehī</s>,
honored with every desired object, then, <s>Rāma</s>, you shall depart.
With affection for me, <s>Rāma</s>, along with your army and your circle of friends,

children.text: satkriyāṃ vihitāṃ tāvad gṛhāṇa tvaṃ mayodyatām ||
children.translated_text: accept for a while the hospitality that I have arranged and made ready.
Out of affection, respect, and friendship, <s>Rāghava</s>,
I seek your favor; I am your servant, and I certainly do not command you."
Then <s>Rāma</s>, thus addressed, replied to <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>
while all the rākṣasas and vānaras were listening:
"Hero, scorcher of foes, I have been honored by you through your counsel,
and with your whole self, by your efforts, and by the highest friendship.

children.text: na khalvetanna kuryāṃ te vacanaṃ rākṣaseśvara
children.translated_text: Lord of rākṣasas, it is certainly not that I would not do this word of yours;

children.text: taṃ tu me bhrātaraṃ draṣṭuṃ bharataṃ tvarate manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but my mind is hastening to see my brother <s>Bharata</s>.
He came to <s>Citrakūṭa</s> in order to turn me back,

children.text: śirasā yācato yasya vacanaṃ na kṛtaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: and I did not carry out the word of him who entreated me with his head bowed.

children.text: kausalyāṃ ca sumitrāṃ ca kaikeyīṃ ca yaśasvinīm
children.translated_text: And I must see glorious <s>Kausalyā</s>, <s>Sumitrā</s>, and <s>Kaikeyī</s>,
my elders and friends, and the citizens together with their children.
Quickly bring the aircraft before me, lord of rākṣasas.

children.text: kṛtakāryasya me vāsaḥ kathaṃcid iha saṃmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: How could any stay here be agreeable to me, now that my task is accomplished?
Permit me to go, gentle <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>; I have been honored.
You must not feel anger; in my haste I ask your leave."
Then the aircraft, its body adorned with gold and its platform made of beryl gems,
encircled by lofty chambers and shining everywhere like silver,
decorated with white pennants and flags,
beautiful with golden mansions and adorned with golden lotuses,
covered with networks of small bells and fitted with windows of pearls and jewels,
surrounded by rows of bells, sweet-sounding on every side,
shaped like the peak of <s>Meru</s> and fashioned by <s>Viśvakarman</s>,
adorned with many mansions resembling pearls and silver,
with floors whose surfaces were bright with crystal and with excellent beryl seats,
furnished with very costly coverings and supplied with great wealth,
that unassailable aircraft, swift as thought, stood ready.
Having announced it to <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> stood there.

children.text: upasthitaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā puṣpakaṃ puṣpabhūṣitam
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Puṣpaka</s>, adorned with flowers, standing ready,
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> spoke to <s>Rāma</s>, who was standing not far away.

children.text: sa tu baddhāñjaliḥ prahvo vinīto rākṣaseśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: The lord of rākṣasas, with joined palms, bowed, humble,
and, filled with urgency, said to <s>Rāghava</s>, "What shall I do?"
The greatly radiant <s>Rāghava</s>, while <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> listened,
considered the matter and spoke these words full of affection:
"<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, the forest-dwellers have performed deeds requiring great effort.
Honor them with jewels, wealth of various kinds, and ornaments.
Together with these men, <s>Laṅkā</s> was battered and conquered, lord of rākṣasas,
by joyful warriors who had cast aside fear for their lives and never turned back in battles.
Thus honored by you, a grateful man, these leaders of the monkey troops,
who deserve honor and bestow honor, will be content.
Because they know you to be generous, one who wins people over, compassionate, and famous,
therefore I remind you of this."
Thus addressed by <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>
honored all those vānaras with a distribution of jewels and wealth.

children.text: tatastān pūjitān dṛṣṭvā ratnair arthaiśca yūthapān
children.translated_text: Then, seeing those troop leaders honored with jewels and wealth,
<s>Rāma</s> mounted that unsurpassed aircraft.
Taking bashful, glorious <s>Vaidehī</s> onto his lap,
together with his valiant bow-bearing brother <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
<s>Kākutstha</s>, standing in the aircraft, spoke to all the vānaras,

children.text: sugrīvaṃ ca mahāvīryaṃ rākṣasaṃ ca vibhīṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: and also to mighty <s>Sugrīva</s> and to the rākṣasa <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>:
"Best of vānaras, this service to a friend has been performed by you.
All of you have my permission; return wherever you wish.

children.text: yat tu kāryaṃ vayasyena suhṛdā vā paraṃtapa
children.translated_text: Whatever should be done by a companion or a friend, scorcher of foes,

children.text: kṛtaṃ sugrīva tat sarvaṃ bhavatā dharmabhīruṇā
children.translated_text: all that has been done by you, <s>Sugrīva</s>, who are mindful of <s>dharma</s>.
Go back at once to <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, surrounded by your own army.

children.text: svarājye vasa laṅkāyāṃ mayā datte vibhīṣaṇa
children.translated_text: Dwell in <s>Laṅkā</s> in your own kingdom, given by me, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>.

children.text: na tvāṃ dharṣayituṃ śaktāḥ sendrā api divaukasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even the gods, together with <s>Indra</s>, will not be able to overpower you.
I shall go back to <s>Ayodhyā</s>, my father's capital.
I wish to take leave; I bid farewell to you all."
When <s>Rāma</s> had spoken thus, those mighty vānaras,
with joined palms, and the rākṣasa <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, said to <s>Rāma</s>:

children.text: ayodhyāṃ gantum icchāmaḥ sarvānnayatu no bhavān ||
children.translated_text: "We wish to go to <s>Ayodhyā</s>; may your lordship take us all.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tvām abhiṣekārdraṃ kausalyām abhivādya ca
children.translated_text: After seeing you wet from the consecration and after saluting <s>Kausalyā</s>,
O son of the king, before long we shall come to our own homes.
But when the righteous one had been addressed thus by the vānaras together with <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,
the splendid <s>Rāghava</s> spoke to them, along with <s>Sugrīva</s> and <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>:

children.text: priyāt priyataraṃ labdhaṃ yad ahaṃ sasuhṛjjanaḥ
children.translated_text: "Dearer than what is dear has been obtained, since I, together with my friends,

children.text: sarvair bhavadbhiḥ sahitaḥ prītiṃ lapsye purīṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: shall gain joy when I have reached the city in the company of all of you.

children.text: kṣipram āroha sugrīva vimānaṃ vānaraiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Quickly mount the aerial car, <s>Sugrīva</s>, together with the vānaras.
And you, lord of rākṣasas, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, mount it with your ministers."

children.text: tatastat puṣpakaṃ divyaṃ sugrīvaḥ saha senayā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sugrīva</s>, together with his army, quickly and eagerly
mounted that divine <s>Puṣpaka</s>, and <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> too mounted it with his ministers.
When all of them had mounted that supreme seat belonging to <s>Kubera</s>,
it rose up into the sky, with <s>Rāghava</s>'s permission.
In that shining aerial car, yoked with swans, he went on;
and <s>Rāma</s>, delighted and confident, shone like <s>Kubera</s>.

children.text: anujñātaṃ tu rāmeṇa tad vimānam anuttamam
children.translated_text: Then that unsurpassed aerial car, permitted by <s>Rāma</s>,
rose up like a great cloud driven onward by the wind.
Then, casting his eyes in every direction, the delight of the <s>Raghu</s> line,
<s>Rāma</s>, spoke to <s>Sītā</s> of <s>Mithilā</s>, whose face was like the moon:
"Look, O <s>Vaidehī</s>, at <s>Laṅkā</s>, standing on the summit of <s>Trikūṭa</s>,
like the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>, fashioned by <s>Viśvakarman</s>.
See this battlefield, muddied with flesh and blood,

children.text: harīṇāṃ rākṣasānāṃ ca sīte viśasanaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Sītā</s>, the great slaughter-place of the vānaras and rākṣasas.

children.text: tava hetor viśālākṣi rāvaṇo nihato mayā
children.translated_text: For your sake, wide-eyed one, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> was slain by me;
here <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> was slain, and <s>Prahasta</s>, the night-roaming rākṣasa.
Here in battle <s>Indrajit</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s son, was slain by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
as were terrible <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, <s>Mahāpārśva</s>, and <s>Mahodara</s>.
<s>Akampana</s> was slain, and other mighty rākṣasas too,
as were <s>Triśiras</s>, <s>Atikāya</s>, <s>Devāntaka</s>, and <s>Narāntaka</s>.

children.text: atra mandodarī nāma bhāryā taṃ paryadevayat
children.translated_text: Here his wife named <s>Mandodarī</s> lamented for him,
surrounded, with tears, by a thousand co-wives.

children.text: etat tu dṛśyate tīrthaṃ samudrasya varānane
children.translated_text: This ford of the ocean is seen here, beautiful-faced one,

children.text: yatra sāgaram uttīrya tāṃ rātrim uṣitā vayam ||
children.translated_text: where, after crossing the sea, we spent that night.

children.text: eṣa setur mayā baddhaḥ sāgare salilārṇave
children.translated_text: This bridge was built by me over the sea, the flood of waters,
for your sake, wide-eyed one: <s>Nala</s>'s bridge, very hard to accomplish.
Look at the unshakable ocean, O <s>Vaidehī</s>, the abode of <s>Varuṇa</s>,
boundless, roaring, and frequented by conches and shellfish.
Look, O <s>Maithilī</s>, at that golden, gold-naveled lord of mountains,
risen from the ocean after splitting it, for <s>Hanūmān</s>'s rest.
Here this king of rākṣasas, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, came to me.

children.text: eṣā sā dṛśyate sīte kiṣkindhā citrakānanā
children.translated_text: This is that <s>Kiṣkindhā</s> which is seen, O <s>Sītā</s>, with its varied groves,

children.text: sugrīvasya purī ramyā yatra vālī mayā hataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the lovely city of <s>Sugrīva</s>, where <s>Vālī</s> was slain by me.

children.text: dṛśyate 'sau mahān sīte savidyud iva toyadaḥ
children.translated_text: That great one is seen there, O <s>Sītā</s>, like a raincloud with lightning:
<s>Ṛśyamūka</s>, best of mountains, covered with golden minerals.
Here I met with <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the vānaras,

children.text: samayaśca kṛtaḥ sīte vadhārthaṃ vālino mayā ||
children.translated_text: and here, O <s>Sītā</s>, I made an agreement for the killing of <s>Vālī</s>.

children.text: eṣā sā dṛśyate pampā nalinī citrakānanā
children.translated_text: This is that <s>Pampā</s> which is seen, a lotus-pond with varied groves,
where, bereft of you, I lamented in great sorrow.
On its bank I saw <s>Śabarī</s>, a woman ascetic devoted to dharma;
and here long-armed <s>Kabandha</s> was slain by me.
That splendid tree is seen there in <s>Janasthāna</s>, O <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: yatra yuddhaṃ mahad vṛttaṃ tava hetor vilāsini
children.translated_text: where a great battle took place for your sake, charming one,
between cruel <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and great-souled <s>Jaṭāyus</s>.
<s>Khara</s> was slain in battle, and <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> was struck down,
and mighty <s>Triśiras</s> too, by me with straight-flying arrows.
The lovely leaf-hut is also seen there, beautiful one,

children.text: yatra tvaṃ rākṣasendreṇa rāvaṇena hṛtā balāt ||
children.translated_text: where you were carried off by force by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of rākṣasas.
This is the lovely <s>Godāvarī</s>, clear-watered and auspicious;
and this is <s>Agastya</s>'s hermitage, visible here. Look, O <s>Maithilī</s>.
O <s>Vaidehī</s>, the great hermitage of <s>Śarabhaṅga</s> is seen here,
where thousand-eyed <s>Śakra</s>, the fortress-breaker, came.
These dwellings of ascetics are seen, slender-waisted one,
where <s>Atri</s>, the head of the family, shines with the radiance of sun and fire.

children.text: atra sīte tvayā dṛṣṭā tāpasī dharmacāriṇī ||
children.translated_text: Here, O <s>Sītā</s>, you saw the woman ascetic devoted to dharma.

children.text: asmin deśe mahākāyo virādho nihato mayā ||
children.translated_text: In this region huge-bodied <s>Virādha</s> was slain by me.
That lordly mountain shines forth there, fair-limbed one: <s>Citrakūṭa</s>,
where the son of <s>Kaikeyī</s> came to conciliate me.

children.text: eṣā sā yamunā dūrād dṛśyate citrakānanā
children.translated_text: This is that <s>Yamunā</s>, seen from afar, with its varied groves,
where this splendid hermitage of <s>Bharadvāja</s> shines forth.
This is the three-pathed <s>Gaṅgā</s>, seen here, excellent-complexioned one,
and this is <s>Śṛṅgaverapura</s>, where <s>Guha</s> met me.

children.text: eṣā sā dṛśyate 'yodhyā rājadhānī pitur mama
children.translated_text: This is that <s>Ayodhyā</s>, seen here, the capital of my father.

children.text: ayodhyāṃ kuru vaidehi praṇāmaṃ punar āgatā ||
children.translated_text: Bow to <s>Ayodhyā</s>, O <s>Vaidehī</s>, now that you have returned."
Then all those vānaras, and <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> the rākṣasa,
leaping up again and again, looked upon that beautiful city.
Then the leaping vānaras saw that city <s>Ayodhyā</s>, garlanded with white mansions, with spacious courtyards, crowded with elephants and horses,

children.text: purīm ayodhyāṃ dadṛśuḥ plavaṃgamāḥ purīṃ mahendrasya yathāmarāvatīm ||
children.translated_text: a city like <s>Amarāvatī</s>, the city of great <s>Indra</s>.
When the fourteenth year was complete, the elder brother of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, together with five others,
reached <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s hermitage and, self-controlled, bowed to the sage.
Having bowed to the ascetic wealthy in austerity, he asked <s>Bharadvāja</s>
Do you hear, blessed one, that there is prosperity and health in the city?

children.text: kaccicca yukto bharato jīvantyapi ca mātaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Is <s>Bharata</s> properly devoted to his task, and are the mothers still alive?
Thus addressed by <s>Rāma</s>, the great sage <s>Bharadvāja</s>
replied to the best of the <s>Raghus</s>, first smiling and seeming delighted:
<s>Bharata</s>, smeared with mud and wearing matted hair, is waiting for you,

children.text: pāduke te puraskṛtya sarvaṃ ca kuśalaṃ gṛhe ||
children.translated_text: placing your sandals before him; and all is well at home.
Formerly, when I saw you entering the great forest in bark garments,

children.text: strītṛtīyaṃ cyutaṃ rājyād dharmakāmaṃ ca kevalam ||
children.translated_text: with your wife and brother as your only companions, fallen from the kingdom and devoted only to <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty),
going on foot, having given up all possessions, carrying out your father's word,
deprived of heavenly enjoyments, like an immortal fallen from heaven,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tu karuṇā pūrvaṃ mamāsīt samitiṃjaya
children.translated_text: compassion arose in me first when I saw you, conqueror in battle,
bound by <s>Kaikeyī</s>'s word and eating forest roots and fruits.
But now, seeing you with your purpose richly fulfilled, together with hosts of friends and kinsmen,

children.text: samīkṣya vijitāriṃ tvāṃ mama prītir anuttamā ||
children.translated_text: and with your enemies conquered, my joy is unsurpassed.

children.text: sarvaṃ ca sukhaduḥkhaṃ te viditaṃ mama rāghava
children.translated_text: All your happiness and suffering is known to me, <s>Rāghava</s>,
the great ordeal that you underwent, beginning with the slaughter at <s>Janasthāna</s>.
While you were charged with the cause of the brahmins and protecting all the ascetics,
there was the encounter with <s>Mārīca</s> and also the abduction of <s>Sītā</s>.
There was also the encounter with <s>Kabandha</s>, and likewise your going to <s>Pampā</s>,

children.text: sugrīveṇa ca te sakhyaṃ yacca vālī hatastvayā ||
children.translated_text: your friendship with <s>Sugrīva</s>, and the fact that <s>Vālī</s> was slain by you.

children.text: mārgaṇaṃ caiva vaidehyāḥ karma vātātmajasya ca
children.translated_text: There was the search for <s>Vaidehī</s> and the deed of the son of the Wind,

children.text: viditāyāṃ ca vaidehyāṃ nalasetur yathā kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: and, when <s>Vaidehī</s> had been found, how <s>Nala</s>'s bridge was made,

children.text: yathā ca dīpitā laṅkā prahṛṣṭair hariyūthapaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and how <s>Laṅkā</s> was set ablaze by the exultant leaders of the vānaras.
With his sons, kinsmen, ministers, army, and vehicles,

children.text: yathā ca nihataḥ saṃkhye rāvaṇo devakaṇṭakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: how <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, tormentor of the gods, was slain in battle,

children.text: samāgamaśca tridaśair yathā dattaśca te varaḥ
children.translated_text: how there was a meeting with the thirty gods, and how a boon was granted to you,
all this is known to me through austerity, lover of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: aham apyatra te dadmi varaṃ śastrabhṛtāṃ vara
children.translated_text: I too grant you a boon here, best of weapon-bearers.
Accept this arghya; tomorrow you will go to <s>Ayodhyā</s>.
Accepting that speech of his with his head bowed, the prince,

children.text: bāḍham ityeva saṃhṛṣṭaḥ śrīmān varam ayācata ||
children.translated_text: glorious and delighted, said, 'So be it,' and asked for a boon:
May all the trees bear fruit out of season, and may they drip honey,

children.text: bhavantu mārge bhagavann ayodhyāṃ prati gacchataḥ ||
children.translated_text: blessed one, along the road of those going toward <s>Ayodhyā</s>.
The fruitless trees became fruitful, and those without blossoms became rich in blossoms;
the dry trees had their full foliage, and the trees dripped honey.
Then, looking toward <s>Ayodhyā</s>, <s>Rāghava</s> reflected,
and after reflecting he cast his glance upon the vānaras.
Desiring what was dear, the wise and radiant <s>Rāma</s> then
spoke to <s>Hanūmān</s>, the swiftly valorous leaper:

children.text: ayodhyāṃ tvarito gaccha kṣipraṃ tvaṃ plavagottama
children.translated_text: Go quickly to <s>Ayodhyā</s>, best of leapers; go at once,
and learn whether the people in the king's palace are well.
After reaching <s>Śṛṅgaverapura</s>, speak to <s>Guha</s>, whose range is the thickets,
the lord of the niṣādas, of my welfare by my word.

children.text: śrutvā tu māṃ kuśalinam arogaṃ vigatajvaram
children.translated_text: Hearing that I am well, free from sickness and fever,

children.text: bhaviṣyati guhaḥ prītaḥ sa mamātmasamaḥ sakhā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Guha</s> will be pleased, for he is a friend equal to my own self.

children.text: ayodhyāyāśca te mārgaṃ pravṛttiṃ bharatasya ca
children.translated_text: The niṣāda lord <s>Guha</s>, pleased, will tell you
the road to <s>Ayodhyā</s> and the news of <s>Bharata</s>.
But <s>Bharata</s> must be told by you of my welfare by my word.

children.text: siddhārthaṃ śaṃsa māṃ tasmai sabhāryaṃ sahalakṣmaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Tell him that I have fulfilled my purpose, together with my wife and with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
Tell of the carrying off of <s>Vaidehī</s> by mighty <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: sugrīveṇa ca saṃvādaṃ vālinaśca vadhaṃ raṇe ||
children.translated_text: of the alliance with <s>Sugrīva</s>, and of <s>Vālī</s>'s death in battle;
of the search for <s>Maithilī</s>, and how she was found by you
after you had leapt across the great water, the imperishable lord of rivers;
of the approach to the ocean and the sight of the sea,

children.text: yathā ca kāritaḥ setū rāvaṇaśca yathā hataḥ ||
children.translated_text: how the bridge was caused to be built, and how <s>Rāvaṇa</s> was killed;
of the bestowal of boons by great <s>Indra</s>, by <s>Brahmā</s>, and by <s>Varuṇa</s>,
and, through the grace of <s>Mahādeva</s>, of my meeting with my father.

children.text: jitvā śatrugaṇān rāmaḥ prāpya cānuttamaṃ yaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Say: '<s>Rāma</s>, having conquered the hosts of enemies and gained unsurpassed fame,
comes near with his purpose fulfilled, together with his friends, mighty in strength.'
Having heard this, whatever disposition <s>Bharata</s> then assumes

children.text: sa ca te veditavyaḥ syāt sarvaṃ yaccāpi māṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: must be known by you, as well as everything concerning me.

children.text: jñeyāḥ sarve ca vṛttāntā bharatasyeṅgitāni ca
children.translated_text: All the circumstances and the gestures of <s>Bharata</s> must be discerned
accurately from the color of his face, his look, and his speech.
For whose mind would a kingdom, rich in every desire, crowded with elephants, horses, and chariots,
inherited from father and grandfather, not turn back?

children.text: saṃgatyā bharataḥ śrīmān rājyenārthī svayaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: If, through attachment, glorious <s>Bharata</s> himself should desire the kingship,
let the delight of the <s>Raghus</s> rule the whole earth entire.

children.text: tasya buddhiṃ ca vijñāya vyavasāyaṃ ca vānara
children.translated_text: Having learned his intention and his resolve, vāṇara,

children.text: yāvanna dūraṃ yātāḥ smaḥ kṣipram āgantum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: you should quickly come back before we have gone far.
Thus instructed, <s>Hanūmān</s>, son of the Wind,

children.text: mānuṣaṃ dhārayan rūpam ayodhyāṃ tvarito yayau ||
children.translated_text: assuming a human form, quickly went to <s>Ayodhyā</s>.
Having crossed the path of the Fathers and the auspicious abode of the serpent-lords,
and having passed beyond the dreadful confluence of <s>Gaṅgā</s> and <s>Yamunā</s>,
he reached <s>Śṛṅgaverapura</s> and met <s>Guha</s>, the mighty one.

children.text: sa vācā śubhayā hṛṣṭo hanūmān idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Joyful, <s>Hanūmān</s> addressed him with auspicious speech, saying this:

children.text: sakhā tu tava kākutstho rāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ
children.translated_text: Your friend <s>Kākutstha</s>, <s>Rāma</s> of unfailing valor,

children.text: sasītaḥ saha saumitriḥ sa tvāṃ kuśalam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Together with <s>Sītā</s> and with <s>Saumitri</s>, he asked after your welfare.
After spending this fifth night today, at the sage's word,
you will see <s>Rāghava</s> this very day, with <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s permission.
Having spoken thus, the greatly radiant one, the hairs on his body thrilled with joy,
sprang up with great speed; swift as he was, he did not hesitate.

children.text: so 'paśyad rāmatīrthaṃ ca nadīṃ vālukinīṃ tathā
children.translated_text: He saw <s>Rāmatīrtha</s>, and likewise the river <s>Vālukinī</s>;

children.text: gomatīṃ tāṃ ca so 'paśyad bhīmaṃ sālavanaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: he also saw that <s>Gomatī</s> and the fearsome sāla forest.

children.text: sa gatvā dūram adhvānaṃ tvaritaḥ kapikuñjaraḥ
children.translated_text: After traveling a long road in haste, that bull among vānaras
came upon flowering trees growing near <s>Nandigrāma</s>.
About a krośa from <s>Ayodhyā</s>, wearing garments of bark and black antelope skin,
he saw <s>Bharata</s>, wretched and thin, living in a hermitage.
His hair was matted, his body was smeared with dirt, and he was worn down by distress for his brother;
he ate fruits and roots, was self-controlled, an ascetic, and one who walked in <s>dharma</s>.
His mass of matted hair was piled high, and he wore bark and antelope skin;
he was disciplined, inwardly cultivated, and equal in splendor to a brahmin seer.

children.text: pāduke te puraskṛtya śāsantaṃ vai vasuṃdharām
children.translated_text: Placing your sandals before him, he governed the earth,
protecting the people of the four varṇas from fear on every side.
He was attended by ministers, by pure priests,
and by chief officers of the army, all capable men wearing ocher garments.

children.text: na hi te rājaputraṃ taṃ cīrakṛṣṇājināmbaram
