children.translated_text: For the citizens, devoted to <s>dharma</s>, did not wish to let that prince,
wearing bark and black antelope skin, abandon his vow.

children.text: taṃ dharmam iva dharmajñaṃ devavantam ivāparam
children.translated_text: To him, who knew <s>dharma</s> and seemed like <s>Dharma</s> embodied, like another god,
<s>Hanūmān</s>, son of the Wind, spoke with joined palms.
The <s>Kākutstha</s> whom you mourn, who lived in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest, wearing bark and matted hair,

children.text: anuśocasi kākutsthaṃ sa tvā kuśalam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: has asked after your welfare.

children.text: priyam ākhyāmi te deva śokaṃ tyakṣyasi dāruṇam
children.translated_text: I tell you welcome news, lord; you will cast off your terrible grief.

children.text: asminmuhūrte bhrātrā tvaṃ rāmeṇa saha saṃgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: At this very moment you will be reunited with your brother <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: nihatya rāvaṇaṃ rāmaḥ pratilabhya ca maithilīm
children.translated_text: After killing <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and recovering <s>Maithilī</s>,
<s>Rāma</s> is approaching, his purpose fulfilled, together with mighty friends.
And greatly radiant <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and illustrious <s>Vaidehī</s>,

children.text: sītā samagrā rāmeṇa mahendreṇa śacī yathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s>, safe and whole, are with <s>Rāma</s>, as <s>Śacī</s> is with great <s>Indra</s>.
When <s>Bharata</s>, son of <s>Kaikeyī</s>, had been addressed in this way by <s>Hanūmān</s>,

children.text: papāta sahasā hṛṣṭo harṣānmohaṃ jagāma ha ||
children.translated_text: he suddenly fell down, delighted, and from joy passed into a swoon.

children.text: tato muhūrtād utthāya pratyāśvasya ca rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Then after a moment <s>Rāghava</s>, <s>Bharata</s>, rose and regained his composure,
and spoke these words to <s>Hanūmān</s>, the bearer of welcome speech.
Embracing the vānara in his agitation, with tears born of the end of sorrow and full of affection,
glorious <s>Bharata</s> bathed him with great drops of tears.

children.text: devo vā mānuṣo vā tvam anukrośād ihāgataḥ
children.translated_text: Whether you are a god or a human being, you have come here out of compassion.

children.text: priyākhyānasya te saumya dadāmi bruvataḥ priyam ||
children.translated_text: Gentle one, as you speak this beloved message, I shall give you a beloved reward.

children.text: gavāṃ śatasahasraṃ ca grāmāṇāṃ ca śataṃ param
children.translated_text: I give you a hundred thousand cows and a further hundred villages,
and sixteen maidens as wives, with earrings and of good conduct.
They are golden in complexion, with lovely noses and thighs, their faces gentle as the moon,
women furnished with every ornament and endowed with noble families and birth.
Having heard of <s>Rāma</s>'s arrival, the prince, hearing that wondrous report from the foremost vānara,

children.text: praharṣito rāmadidṛkṣayābhavat punaśca harṣād idam abravīd vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: was filled with joy and with desire to see <s>Rāma</s>; and again, from joy, he spoke these words.

children.text: bahūni nāma varṣāṇi gatasya sumahad vanam
children.translated_text: Many years indeed have passed since he went to the very great forest;
now I hear the joy-bringing praise of my lord.

children.text: kalyāṇī bata gātheyaṃ laukikī pratibhāti me
children.translated_text: This auspicious worldly saying now seems true to me:

children.text: eti jīvantam ānando naraṃ varṣaśatād api ||
children.translated_text: joy comes to a living man even after a hundred years.

children.text: rāghavasya harīṇāṃ ca katham āsīt samāgamaḥ
children.translated_text: How did the meeting of <s>Rāghava</s> and the vānaras come about?

children.text: kasmin deśe kim āśritya tat tvam ākhyāhi pṛcchataḥ ||
children.translated_text: In what region, and relying on what, did it happen? Tell that to me as I ask.
Asked by the prince and seated upon a seat,

children.text: ācacakṣe tataḥ sarvaṃ rāmasya caritaṃ vane ||
children.translated_text: he then related the whole story of <s>Rāma</s>'s conduct in the forest:

children.text: yathā pravrajito rāmo mātur datte vare tava
children.translated_text: how <s>Rāma</s> went into exile because of the boon given to your mother,

children.text: yathā ca putraśokena rājā daśaratho mṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and how King <s>Daśaratha</s> died from grief for his son;
how you, lord, were quickly brought by messengers from <s>Rājagṛha</s>,

children.text: tvayāyodhyāṃ praviṣṭena yathā rājyaṃ na cepsitam ||
children.translated_text: and how, when you entered <s>Ayodhyā</s>, you did not desire the kingdom;
how, after going to Mount <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, you, scorcher of foes,
invited your brother to accept the kingdom, while you yourself practiced the <s>dharma</s> of the good;

children.text: sthitena rājño vacane yathā rājyaṃ visarjitam
children.translated_text: how, standing by the king's word, the kingdom was relinquished,

children.text: āryasya pāduke gṛhya yathāsi punar āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and how, taking the noble one's sandals, you returned again.
All this, mighty-armed one, is known to you just as it happened;

children.text: tvayi pratiprayāte tu yad vṛttaṃ tannibodha me ||
children.translated_text: but now hear from me what occurred after you had gone back.
When you had departed, he then entered the vast, lonely <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest,
where deer and birds were thrown into alarm.

children.text: teṣāṃ purastād balavān gacchatāṃ gahane vane
children.translated_text: As they were going through the dense forest, the powerful one before them,
<s>Virādha</s>, appeared, roaring with a very great roar.
They lifted up that loudly roaring one, his arms raised and his head downward,

children.text: nikhāte prakṣipanti sma nadantam iva kuñjaram ||
children.translated_text: and threw him into a pit, as he bellowed like an elephant.

children.text: tat kṛtvā duṣkaraṃ karma bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
children.translated_text: Having performed that difficult deed, the two brothers <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>
went in the evening to the lovely hermitage of <s>Śarabhaṅga</s>.
When <s>Śarabhaṅga</s> had gone to heaven, <s>Rāma</s>, true in valor,
saluted all the sages and went to <s>Janasthāna</s>.
Fourteen thousand rākṣasas of fearsome deeds
were slain there by great-souled <s>Rāghava</s> while he was dwelling there.
Then afterward <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s> came to <s>Rāma</s>'s side.
Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, instructed by <s>Rāma</s>, rose up at once.
Taking up his sword, the mighty one cut off her ears and nose.
Then the woman, tormented by him, went to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
A terrible rākṣasa, an attendant of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, named <s>Mārīca</s>,
enticed <s>Vaidehī</s> by becoming a deer made of jewels.

children.text: sā rāmam abravīd dṛṣṭvā vaidehī gṛhyatām iti
children.translated_text: When <s>Vaidehī</s> saw it, she said to <s>Rāma</s>, "Let it be caught."

children.text: aho manoharaḥ kānta āśrame no bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: "Ah, charming and lovely, it will be at our hermitage."
Then <s>Rāma</s>, bow in hand, pursued it as it ran.
He struck it while it was running with a straight-jointed arrow.

children.text: atha saumya daśagrīvo mṛgaṃ yāte tu rāghave
children.translated_text: Then, gentle one, when <s>Rāghava</s> had gone after the deer, the ten-necked one,
and when <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> too had gone out, entered the hermitage at that time.

children.text: jagrāha tarasā sītāṃ grahaḥ khe rohiṇīm iva ||
children.translated_text: He seized <s>Sītā</s> suddenly, like <s>Graha</s> seizing <s>Rohiṇī</s> in the sky.

children.text: trātukāmaṃ tato yuddhe hatvā gṛdhraṃ jaṭāyuṣam
children.translated_text: Then, after killing the vulture <s>Jaṭāyus</s> in battle as he wished to rescue her,

children.text: pragṛhya sītāṃ sahasā jagāmāśu sa rāvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Rāvaṇa</s> seized <s>Sītā</s> and swiftly went away at once.
Then, wondrous in appearance, standing on a mountain peak,
the vānaras, mountain-like themselves, saw him carrying <s>Sītā</s> away,
and stood amazed there at <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas.
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, who made the worlds cry out, entered <s>Laṅkā</s>.
Into a lovely, great mansion encircled with gold,
having brought <s>Maithilī</s> inside, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> tried to soothe her with words.
As <s>Kākutstha</s> was returning, he saw the vulture and was deeply distressed.

children.text: gṛdhraṃ hataṃ tadā dagdhvā rāmaḥ priyasakhaṃ pituḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s> cremated the slain vulture, his father's dear friend,
and, wandering along the <s>Godāvarī</s> and through flowering forest tracts,
the two came upon a rākṣasa named <s>Kabandha</s> in the great forest.
Then, following <s>Kabandha</s>'s words, <s>Rāma</s>, whose valor is true,
went to Mount <s>Ṛśyamūka</s> and met with <s>Sugrīva</s>.

children.text: tayoḥ samāgamaḥ pūrvaṃ prītyā hārdo vyajāyata
children.translated_text: At their first meeting, a heartfelt bond arose through affection,
and through mutual conversation their friendship became deep.
By the strength of his own arms, <s>Rāma</s> restored him to his kingdom,
after killing <s>Vālin</s>, huge-bodied and very mighty, in battle.
<s>Sugrīva</s>, established in the kingship together with all the vānaras,
promised <s>Rāma</s> that he would search for the princess.
Commanded by the great-souled <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the vānaras,
ten crores of leapers were sent out in every direction.
For us, lost on the <s>Vindhya</s>, best of mountains,
and intensely afflicted with grief, a long time passed by.

children.text: bhrātā tu gṛdhrarājasya saṃpātir nāma vīryavān
children.translated_text: But the powerful brother of the king of vultures, named <s>Saṃpāti</s>,
told us of <s>Sītā</s>'s dwelling in <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s abode.
So I, removing the sorrow of my kinsmen who were overcome with sorrow,
relied on my own strength and leapt a hundred yojanas.
There I saw her alone, having gone into an <s>Aśoka</s> grove,
wearing a silk garment, soiled, joyless, and firm in her vow.

children.text: tayā sametya vidhivat pṛṣṭvā sarvam aninditām
children.translated_text: After meeting that blameless woman properly and asking her everything,
I received a jewel as a token and came back with my purpose fulfilled.
And when I returned again to <s>Rāma</s>, whose acts are unwearied,

children.text: abhijñānaṃ mayā dattam arciṣmān sa mahāmaṇiḥ ||
children.translated_text: I gave him the token, that radiant great jewel.

children.text: śrutvā tāṃ maithilīṃ hṛṣṭastvāśaśaṃse sa jīvitam
children.translated_text: Hearing of <s>Maithilī</s>, he rejoiced and hoped for life,
like a sick man who has reached life's end after drinking nectar.
Preparing to set the enterprise in motion, he fixed his mind on the destruction of <s>Laṅkā</s>,
like <s>Vibhāvasu</s> wishing to destroy all those worlds.

children.text: tataḥ samudram āsādya nalaṃ setum akārayat
children.translated_text: Then, reaching the ocean, he had <s>Nala</s> build a bridge.
The army of vānara heroes crossed over by means of that bridge.
<s>Nīla</s> killed <s>Prahasta</s>; <s>Rāghava</s>, for his part, killed <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>.
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> killed <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s son, and <s>Rāma</s> himself killed <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: sa śakreṇa samāgamya yamena varuṇena ca
children.translated_text: Meeting with <s>Śakra</s>, with <s>Yama</s>, and with <s>Varuṇa</s>,
and with the divine seers, <s>Kākutstha</s>, scorcher of foes, received boons.

children.text: sa tu dattavaraḥ prītyā vānaraiśca samāgataḥ
children.translated_text: Granted boons and joyfully joined by the vānaras,
he came to <s>Kiṣkindhā</s> in the aerial car <s>Puṣpaka</s>.

children.text: taṃ gaṅgāṃ punar āsādya vasantaṃ munisaṃnidhau
children.translated_text: Having again reached the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, he is staying in the presence of the sage;

children.text: avighnaṃ puṣyayogena śvo rāmaṃ draṣṭum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: tomorrow, under the conjunction of <s>Puṣya</s>, you should see <s>Rāma</s> without hindrance.

children.text: tataḥ sa satyaṃ hanumadvaco mahan niśamya hṛṣṭo bharataḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Bharata</s>, hearing <s>Hanumān</s>'s great and truthful speech, rejoiced and joined his palms,

children.text: uvāca vāṇīṃ manasaḥ praharṣiṇīṃ cirasya pūrṇaḥ khalu me manorathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and uttered words that delighted his mind: "After so long, my desire is indeed fulfilled."

children.text: śrutvā tu param ānandaṃ bharataḥ satyavikramaḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard that supreme joy, <s>Bharata</s>, whose valor is true,
joyfully gave orders to <s>Śatrughna</s>, slayer of enemy heroes.

children.text: daivatāni ca sarvāṇi caityāni nagarasya ca
children.translated_text: "Let all the deities and the city's sacred shrines
be worshipped by pure men with fragrant garlands and musical instruments.
Let the royal women, the ministers, the soldiers, the army divisions, and the women
go out to see <s>Rāma</s>'s face, which is like the moon.
Hearing <s>Bharata</s>'s words, valiant <s>Śatrughna</s>, slayer of enemy heroes,
set many thousands of work gangs in motion.
"Make the low places even, and make the uneven places level;

children.text: sthānāni ca nirasyantāṃ nandigrāmād itaḥ param ||
children.translated_text: and from here onward from <s>Nandigrāma</s>, let the places be cleared.
Let them sprinkle the whole earth with water cold as snow."
Then others scattered parched grain and flowers everywhere.
Let the roads in the excellent city have raised banners,
and let them adorn the houses facing the sunrise."
With garlands, loose flowers, and fragrant blossoms of five colors,
let hundreds of men scatter them over the broad, unobstructed royal road.
With thousands of intoxicated elephants adorned with gold,
and others with female elephants, together with their elephants, fitted with golden girths,
great chariot-warriors went out in haste, mounted on chariots.
Then all the wives of <s>Daśaratha</s>, mounted on vehicles,

children.text: kausalyāṃ pramukhe kṛtvā sumitrāṃ cāpi niryayuḥ ||
children.translated_text: went forth, placing <s>Kausalyā</s> at their head, and <s>Sumitrā</s> too.
At the sound of the horses' hooves and the rumbling of chariot wheels,
and at the blare of conches and kettledrums, the earth seemed to shake.

children.text: kṛtsnaṃ ca nagaraṃ tat tu nandigrāmam upāgamat
children.translated_text: And that whole city went to <s>Nandigrāma</s>,
together with the foremost twice-born men, the righteous one, the chiefs of guilds, and the townsmen.
Surrounded by ministers holding garlands and sweetmeats in their hands, <s>Bharata</s>
was praised by bards amid the sounds of conches and drums.
The knower of <s>dharma</s>, taking the noble one's sandals upon his head,
and taking up the white parasol, adorned with white garlands,
and the two white yak-tail fans, worthy of a king and ornamented with gold,
emaciated by fasting, sorrowful, and wearing bark-cloth and black antelope skin,

children.text: bhrātur āgamanaṃ śrutvā tat pūrvaṃ harṣam āgataḥ
children.translated_text: having heard of his brother's arrival, was first filled with joy,

children.text: pratyudyayau tadā rāmaṃ mahātmā sacivaiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: and then the great-souled one went out to meet <s>Rāma</s>, together with his counselors.
Looking around, <s>Bharata</s> spoke this word to the son of the Wind:
"Surely, monkey, you are not indulging in a fickleness natural to monkeys?

children.text: na hi paśyāmi kākutsthaṃ rāmam āryaṃ paraṃtapam ||
children.translated_text: For I do not see <s>Kākutstha</s>, noble <s>Rāma</s>, the scorcher of foes."

children.text: athaivam ukte vacane hanūmān idam abravīt
children.translated_text: When these words had been spoken, <s>Hanūmān</s> said this,
as he explained the matter to <s>Bharata</s>, whose valor was true:
"Having reached trees always fruitful, flowering, and dripping honey,
humming with intoxicated bees through the favor of <s>Bharadvāja</s>,

children.text: tasya caiṣa varo datto vāsavena paraṃtapa
children.translated_text: and this boon was granted to him by <s>Vāsava</s>, scorcher of foes:
hospitality was offered there to the army, complete with every excellence.
A dreadful roar of the delighted forest-dwellers is being heard;

children.text: manye vānarasenā sā nadīṃ tarati gomatīm ||
children.translated_text: I think that vānaras' army is crossing the <s>Gomatī</s> river.
Look at the shower of dust that has arisen toward the <s>Vālukinī</s>;
I think the leaping monkeys are shaking the lovely śāla forest.

children.text: tad etad dṛśyate dūrād vimalaṃ candrasaṃnibham
children.translated_text: And there, visible from afar, pure and like the moon,
is the divine <s>Puṣpaka</s> aircraft, created by <s>Brahmā</s> through his mind.

children.text: rāvaṇaṃ bāndhavaiḥ sārdhaṃ hatvā labdhaṃ mahātmanā
children.translated_text: After slaying <s>Rāvaṇa</s> together with his kinsmen, it was obtained by the great-souled one;
by the favor of the lord of wealth, this divine craft moves as swift as thought.

children.text: etasmin bhrātarau vīrau vaidehyā saha rāghavau
children.translated_text: In it are the two heroic brothers, the <s>Rāghavas</s>, together with <s>Vaidehī</s>,
and mighty <s>Sugrīva</s> and <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas."
Then a roar born of joy touched the sky,
raised by women, children, youths, and elders, crying, "This is <s>Rāma</s>!"
Having dismounted from chariots, elephants, and horses, they came to the ground;
the men saw him standing in the aircraft, like the moon in the sky.
<s>Bharata</s>, with joined palms, joyful and facing <s>Rāghava</s>,
then honored <s>Rāma</s> with a proper welcome.
In the aircraft created by <s>Brahmā</s> through his mind, the elder brother of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
broad and long-eyed, shone like another wielder of the thunderbolt.
Then <s>Bharata</s>, bowing low, at that time saluted his brother <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: vavande praṇato rāmaṃ merustham iva bhāskaram ||
children.translated_text: who was at the front of the aircraft, like the sun stationed on <s>Meru</s>.
<s>Bharata</s>, whose valor was true, was brought up into that aircraft;
having reached <s>Rāma</s>, joyful, he bowed again.
<s>Kākutstha</s> raised him up, since after a long time he had come within sight,
and, taking <s>Bharata</s> onto his lap, joyfully embraced him.

children.text: tato lakṣmaṇam āsādya vaidehīṃ ca paraṃtapaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, approaching <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and <s>Vaidehī</s>, the scorcher of foes,
<s>Bharata</s> saluted them with affection and spoke his name.
The son of <s>Kaikeyī</s> embraced <s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>Jāmbavān</s>, and likewise <s>Aṅgada</s>,

children.text: maindaṃ ca dvividaṃ nīlam ṛṣabhaṃ caiva sasvaje ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Mainda</s>, <s>Dvivida</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, and <s>Ṛṣabha</s> as well.

children.text: te kṛtvā mānuṣaṃ rūpaṃ vānarāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Those vānaras, able to assume any form at will, took on human form,
and, delighted, asked <s>Bharata</s> then about his welfare.

children.text: vibhīṣaṇaṃ ca bharataḥ sāntvayan vākyam abravīt
children.translated_text: And <s>Bharata</s>, consoling <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, said these words:

children.text: diṣṭyā tvayā sahāyena kṛtaṃ karma suduṣkaram ||
children.translated_text: "By good fortune, with you as an ally, a very difficult deed has been accomplished."
Then <s>Śatrughna</s> saluted <s>Rāma</s> together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
and afterward, endowed with humility, bowed to <s>Sītā</s>'s feet.
<s>Rāma</s>, approaching his mother, despondent and wasted by grief,

children.text: jagrāha praṇataḥ pādau mano mātuḥ prasādayan ||
children.translated_text: bowed down and grasped her feet, soothing his mother's mind.

children.text: abhivādya sumitrāṃ ca kaikeyīṃ ca yaśasvinīm
children.translated_text: After saluting <s>Sumitrā</s> and illustrious <s>Kaikeyī</s>,

children.text: sa mātṝśca tadā sarvāḥ purohitam upāgamat ||
children.translated_text: and all his mothers at that time, he approached the family priest.
"Welcome to you, mighty-armed one, increaser of <s>Kausalyā</s>'s joy,"

children.text: iti prāñjalayaḥ sarve nāgarā rāmam abruvan ||
children.translated_text: all the citizens said to <s>Rāma</s> with joined palms.
The elder brother of <s>Bharata</s> saw those thousands of joined palms
raised by the citizens, like lotuses crying out.

children.text: pāduke te tu rāmasya gṛhītvā bharataḥ svayam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Bharata</s> himself took those sandals of <s>Rāma</s>,
and, knowing <s>dharma</s>, placed them on the feet of the king of men.

children.text: abravīcca tadā rāmaṃ bharataḥ sa kṛtāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Bharata</s>, with joined palms, said to <s>Rāma</s>:

children.text: etat te rakṣitaṃ rājan rājyaṃ niryātitaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: "This kingdom of yours, O king, has been guarded and handed back by me.

children.text: adya janma kṛtārthaṃ me saṃvṛttaśca manorathaḥ
children.translated_text: Today my birth has become fruitful, and my wish has been fulfilled,

children.text: yastvāṃ paśyāmi rājānam ayodhyāṃ punar āgatam ||
children.translated_text: since I see you, the king, returned again to <s>Ayodhyā</s>.

children.text: avekṣatāṃ bhavān kośaṃ koṣṭhāgāraṃ puraṃ balam
children.translated_text: Let your majesty inspect the treasury, the granary, the city, and the army."
Through your majesty I have made all this tenfold.

children.text: tathā bruvāṇaṃ bharataṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ bhrātṛvatsalam
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Bharata</s> speaking thus, affectionate toward his brother,
the vānaras and <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> the rākṣasa shed tears.

children.text: tataḥ praharṣād bharatam aṅkam āropya rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, in great joy, <s>Rāghava</s> lifted <s>Bharata</s> into his embrace,
and, together with his army, went in that vimāna to <s>Bharata</s>'s hermitage.
When <s>Rāghava</s>, together with his army, reached <s>Bharata</s>'s hermitage then,
he descended from the front of the vimāna and stood upon the earth.
Then <s>Rāma</s> said to that unsurpassed vimāna,
"Carry the god <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>; I release you. Go."
Then that unsurpassed vimāna, permitted by <s>Rāma</s>,
went toward the northern direction, to the abode of <s>Dhanada</s>.
<s>Rāghava</s>, like <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the immortals, before <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, pressed the feet of his priest, who was equal to himself,

children.text: nipīḍya pādau pṛthag āsane śubhe sahaiva tenopaviveśa vīryavān ||
children.translated_text: and the heroic one sat down together with him on a separate auspicious seat.
The son of <s>Kaikeyī</s>, increaser of her joy, placed his joined hands upon his head,
and <s>Bharata</s> spoke to his elder brother <s>Rāma</s>, whose valor is true.

children.text: pūjitā māmikā mātā dattaṃ rājyam idaṃ mama
children.translated_text: "My mother has been honored, and this kingdom was given to me;

children.text: tad dadāmi punas tubhyaṃ yathā tvam adadā mama ||
children.translated_text: I give it back to you, just as you gave it to me.
This yoke, placed on me alone by a stronger bull,

children.text: kiśoravad guruṃ bhāraṃ na voḍhum aham utsahe ||
children.translated_text: this heavy burden, I cannot bear, like a young calf.

children.text: vārivegena mahatā bhinnaḥ setur iva kṣaran
children.translated_text: Like a bridge broken and leaking under a great rush of water,
I think this breach in the kingdom, left uncovered, is hard to dam.

children.text: gatiṃ khara ivāśvasya haṃsasyeva ca vāyasaḥ
children.translated_text: As a donkey cannot follow the gait of a horse, or a crow that of a swan,

children.text: nānvetum utsahe deva tava mārgam ariṃdama ||
children.translated_text: I cannot follow your path, lord, tamer of enemies.

children.text: yathā ca ropito vṛkṣo jātaś cāntarniveśane
children.translated_text: And just as a tree that has been planted and has grown inside a courtyard,
large, very hard to climb, with a great trunk and many branches,

children.text: śīryeta puṣpito bhūtvā na phalāni pradarśayet
children.translated_text: might wither after flowering and not show its fruits,

children.text: tasya nānubhaved arthaṃ yasya hetoḥ sa ropyate ||
children.translated_text: so it would not fulfill the purpose for which it was planted.

children.text: eṣopamā mahābāho tvam arthaṃ vettum arhasi
children.translated_text: This is the simile, mighty-armed one; you should understand its meaning,

children.text: yady asmān manujendra tvaṃ bhaktān bhṛtyān na śādhi hi ||
children.translated_text: if, king among men, you do not rule us, your devoted servants.
Let the world today behold you consecrated everywhere,
blazing like the sun at midday, radiant with shining majesty.
With the resounding roar of gathered instruments, with the jingling of girdles and anklets,

children.text: madhurair gītaśabdaiś ca pratibudhyasva śeṣva ca ||
children.translated_text: and with sweet sounds of song, wake and sleep.

children.text: yāvad āvartate cakraṃ yāvatī ca vasuṃdharā
children.translated_text: As long as the wheel turns, and as far as the earth extends,

children.text: tāvat tvam iha sarvasya svāmitvam abhivartaya ||
children.translated_text: so long maintain lordship here over all.
Hearing <s>Bharata</s>'s words, <s>Rāma</s>, conqueror of enemy cities,
accepted them, saying, "So be it," and sat down on the auspicious seat.
Then, at <s>Śatrughna</s>'s command, skillful barbers,
with gentle hands and very swift, attended upon <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: pūrvaṃ tu bharate snāte lakṣmaṇe ca mahābale
children.translated_text: But first, when <s>Bharata</s> had bathed, and mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
and <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the vānaras, and <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas,
<s>Rāma</s>, his matted locks cleansed away, bathed, adorned with bright garlands and unguents,
and furnished with very costly garments, stood there blazing with splendor.
The valiant one had <s>Rāma</s>'s grooming performed,
and also <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s, that fortunate increaser of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> line.
And all the wives of <s>Daśaratha</s>, high-minded and charming,
then themselves performed <s>Sītā</s>'s adornment.
Then joyful <s>Kausalyā</s>, affectionate toward her son,
carefully performed the beautiful adornment of all the wives of the <s>Rāghavas</s>.
Then, at <s>Śatrughna</s>'s command, the charioteer named <s>Sumantra</s>,
having yoked the chariot, approached with it, splendid in every part.
Seeing the divine chariot standing there, resembling the disk of the sun,
mighty-armed <s>Rāma</s>, whose valor is true, mounted it.

children.text: ayodhyāyāṃ tu sacivā rājño daśarathasya ye
children.translated_text: But in <s>Ayodhyā</s>, those ministers of King <s>Daśaratha</s>,
placing the priest at their head, deliberated purposefully.
As they deliberated for <s>Rāma</s>'s prosperity and for the livelihood of the city,
all that was for the consecration of that great-souled one worthy of victory,

children.text: kartum arhatha rāmasya yad yan maṅgalapūrvakam ||
children.translated_text: whatever was preceded by auspicious rites, they said, should be done for <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: iti te mantriṇaḥ sarve saṃdiśya tu purohitam
children.translated_text: Having thus instructed the priest, all those ministers
went quickly out from the city, intent on seeing <s>Rāma</s>.
Sinless <s>Rāma</s>, like thousand-eyed <s>Indra</s> in a chariot yoked with bay horses,

children.text: prayayau ratham āsthāya rāmo nagaram uttamam ||
children.translated_text: set out for the excellent city, having mounted the chariot.

children.text: jagrāha bharato raśmīñ śatrughnaś chatram ādade
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s> grasped the reins; <s>Śatrughna</s> took up the parasol;
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> fanned above his head with a fan.
<s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the vānaras, held a white yak-tail fan,
and <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas, held another, shining like the moon.
As <s>Rāma</s> was praised then in the sky by assemblies of seers
and by the gods together with the hosts of <s>Maruts</s>, a sweet sound was heard.
Then <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the vānaras, mounted
the elephant named <s>Śatruṃjaya</s>, mountain-like and very radiant.
The vānaras went mounted on nine thousand elephants,
having assumed human forms and all adorned with ornaments.
With the resounding blasts of conches and the sounds of kettledrums,
the tiger among men set out for that city garlanded with mansions.
They saw <s>Rāghava</s>, foremost in the procession, coming toward them,
radiant in body, an eminent chariot-warrior upon his chariot then.
After those men had greeted <s>Kākutstha</s> and had been welcomed in return by <s>Rāma</s>,
they followed the great-souled one, who was surrounded by his brothers.

children.text: amātyair brāhmaṇaiś caiva tathā prakṛtibhir vṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Surrounded by ministers and brāhmaṇas, and likewise by the citizens and officers of state,

children.text: śriyā viruruce rāmo nakṣatrair iva candramāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> shone with splendor like the moon among the stars.
With musical instruments going before him, and with delighted men holding cymbals and auspicious emblems,
proclaiming blessings aloud, he went on, surrounded by them.

children.text: akṣataṃ jātarūpaṃ ca gāvaḥ kanyās tathā dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: Unbroken rice, gold, cows, maidens, and brāhmaṇas,

children.text: narā modakahastāś ca rāmasya purato yayuḥ ||
children.translated_text: and men carrying sweetmeats in their hands went before <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: sakhyaṃ ca rāmaḥ sugrīve prabhāvaṃ cānilātmaje
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s> explained to his ministers his friendship with <s>Sugrīva</s>,

children.text: vānarāṇāṃ ca tat karma vyācacakṣe 'tha mantriṇām
children.translated_text: the power of the son of the Wind, and the deed of the vānaras;
and when the residents of <s>Ayodhyā</s> heard it, they were filled with wonder.
Having related this, radiant <s>Rāma</s>, surrounded by the vānaras,
entered <s>Ayodhyā</s>, crowded with people who were joyful and thriving.

children.text: tato hy abhyucchrayan paurāḥ patākās te gṛhe gṛhe
children.translated_text: Then the citizens raised banners at every house,
and he reached the lovely palace of his father, occupied by the descendants of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>.

children.text: pitur bhavanam āsādya praviśya ca mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Having reached the palace of his great-souled father and entered it,

children.text: kausalyāṃ ca sumitrāṃ ca kaikeyīṃ cābhyavādayat ||
children.translated_text: he paid homage to <s>Kausalyā</s>, <s>Sumitrā</s>, and <s>Kaikeyī</s>.
Then the prince, delight of the <s>Raghus</s>, spoke to <s>Bharata</s>,
best of the righteous, in gentle and sweet words:

children.text: yac ca madbhavanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sāśokavanikaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: "That excellent and great residence of mine, together with its <s>Aśoka</s> grove,
strewn with pearls and vaidūrya gems, assign it to <s>Sugrīva</s>."
Hearing that command of his, truth-valorous <s>Bharata</s>

children.text: pāṇau gṛhītvā sugrīvaṃ praviveśa tam ālayam ||
children.translated_text: took <s>Sugrīva</s> by the hand and entered that dwelling.
Then, taking oil lamps and couch-coverings,
men quickly entered, urged on by <s>Śatrughna</s>.
The greatly radiant younger brother of <s>Rāghava</s> said to <s>Sugrīva</s>:
"Lord, command messengers for <s>Rāma</s>'s consecration.
For the four lords of the vānaras he gave four golden jars,
quickly, all adorned with jewels.
"At daybreak, with full jars of water from the four oceans,

children.text: pūrṇair ghaṭaiḥ pratīkṣadhvaṃ tathā kuruta vānarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: stand ready. Do this, vānaras."
Thus addressed, the great-souled vānaras, like elephants,

children.text: utpetur gaganaṃ śīghraṃ garuḍā iva śīghragāḥ ||
children.translated_text: sprang swiftly into the sky, like swift-flying <s>Garuḍas</s>.

children.text: jāmbavāṃś ca hanūmāṃś ca vegadarśī ca vānaraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Jāmbavān</s>, <s>Hanūmān</s>, the vānara <s>Vegadarśin</s>,
and <s>Ṛṣabha</s> then brought jars filled with water,
carrying water in vessels from five hundred rivers.
From the eastern ocean <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, endowed with strength, then brought
a water-filled jar, adorned with every jewel.
<s>Ṛṣabha</s> swiftly brought water from the southern ocean.
A golden jar covered with red sandal and camphor
<s>Gavaya</s> brought with water from the western great ocean.
With a great jeweled vessel, the one whose valor was like the wind brought cool water,
swiftly from the north, moving with the speed of <s>Garuḍa</s> and the Wind.
For <s>Rāma</s>'s consecration, <s>Śatrughna</s>, together with the ministers,
presented it to the excellent family priest and to the friends.

children.text: tataḥ sa prayato vṛddho vasiṣṭho brāhmaṇaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Then the aged <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, purified and intent, together with brāhmaṇas,
seated <s>Rāma</s> with <s>Sītā</s> on a jeweled throne.

children.text: vasiṣṭho vāmadevaś ca jābālir atha kāśyapaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, <s>Jābāli</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>,

children.text: kātyāyanaḥ suyajñaś ca gautamo vijayas tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kātyāyana</s>, <s>Suyajña</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, and <s>Vijaya</s> likewise
consecrated the tiger among men with clear, fragrant water,
as the <s>Vasus</s> consecrate thousand-eyed <s>Vāsava</s>.

children.text: ṛtvigbhir brāhmaṇaiḥ pūrvaṃ kanyābhir mantribhis tathā
children.translated_text: First the officiating priests and brāhmaṇas, then maidens and ministers,
and warriors too, together with the guildsmen, consecrated him, all overjoyed.
With the essences of all healing herbs, and by the deities standing in the sky,

children.text: caturbhir lokapālaiś ca sarvair devaiś ca saṃgataiḥ ||
children.translated_text: by the four world-protectors and by all the assembled gods, he was consecrated.

children.text: chatraṃ tasya ca jagrāha śatrughnaḥ pāṇḍuraṃ śubham
children.translated_text: <s>Śatrughna</s> took up for him a fair white parasol,
and <s>Sugrīva</s>, lord of the vānaras, took a white yak-tail fan;
another, moon-bright one was taken by <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas.
A golden garland, blazing with its beauty and set with a hundred lotuses,
the Wind, urged by <s>Vāsava</s>, gave to <s>Rāghava</s>.
A pearl necklace, joined with every kind of jewel and adorned with precious gems,
he gave to the king of men, impelled by <s>Śakra</s>.
The divine gandharvas sang, and hosts of apsarases danced
at the consecration then of wise <s>Rāma</s>, who was worthy of it.

children.text: bhūmiḥ sasyavatī caiva phalavantaś ca pādapāḥ
children.translated_text: At <s>Rāghava</s>'s festival the earth became rich in crops,
the trees bore fruit, and the flowers became fragrant.

children.text: sahasraśatam aśvānāṃ dhenūnāṃ ca gavāṃ tathā
children.translated_text: The bull among men first gave a hundred thousand horses,

children.text: dadau śataṃ vṛṣān pūrvaṃ dvijebhyo manujarṣabhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and cows and cattle as well, and a hundred bulls, to the brāhmaṇas.
Again <s>Rāghava</s> gave thirty crores of gold to the brāhmaṇas,
and various ornaments and garments of great value.
The bull among men presented to <s>Sugrīva</s> a divine golden garland,
shining like the rays of the sun and fashioned with gems.
To <s>Aṅgada</s>, son of <s>Vāli</s>, the steadfast one gave armlets
variegated with vaidūrya gems and adorned with diamonds and jewels.
And to <s>Sītā</s> <s>Rāma</s> gave an unsurpassed pearl necklace,
set with the finest gems and gleaming like rays of the moon.

children.text: araje vāsasī divye śubhāny ābharaṇāni ca
children.translated_text: The radiant <s>Vaidehī</s>, looking at the heavenly, spotless garments
and the auspicious ornaments, gave them to the son of <s>Vāyu</s>.
Loosening the necklace from her own neck, the delight of <s>Janaka</s>

children.text: avaikṣata harīn sarvān bhartāraṃ ca muhur muhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: looked again and again at all the haris and at her husband.
Seeing her, the knower of signs addressed the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>:

children.text: pradehi subhage hāraṃ yasya tuṣṭāsi bhāmini ||
children.translated_text: "Give the necklace, lovely one, to the one with whom you are pleased, fair lady."

children.text: pauruṣaṃ vikramo buddhir yasminn etāni nityadā
children.translated_text: In him manliness, valor, and intelligence are always present;

children.text: dadau sā vāyuputrāya taṃ hāram asitekṣaṇā ||
children.translated_text: the dark-eyed woman gave that necklace to the son of <s>Vāyu</s>.
<s>Hanūmān</s>, the bull among vānaras, shone with that necklace,
white as a mass of moonbeams, like a mountain with a white cloud.
Then the scorcher of foes, the lord of the earth, considering every desirable excellence,
gave gifts to <s>Dvivida</s>, <s>Mainda</s>, and <s>Nīla</s>.
All the elder vānaras and the other lords of vānaras
were honored, each according to his worth, with garments and ornaments.

children.text: yathārhaṃ pūjitāḥ sarve kāmai ratnaiś ca puṣkalaiḥ
children.translated_text: All of them, honored as was fitting with pleasures and abundant jewels,
went away just as they had come, all with delighted hearts.
The most generous <s>Rāghava</s>, with supreme joy, gave his command;
<s>Rāma</s> spoke to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, knower of <s>dharma</s> and devoted to <s>dharma</s>:

children.text: ātiṣṭha dharmajña mayā sahemāṃ gāṃ pūrvarājādhyuṣitāṃ balena
children.translated_text: "Take your place, knower of <s>dharma</s>, together with me, over this earth once inhabited by former kings and held by power.

children.text: tulyaṃ mayā tvaṃ pitṛbhir dhṛtā yā tāṃ yauvarājye dhuram udvahasva ||
children.translated_text: Bear equally with me, in the office of heir-apparent, the burden which was borne by our fathers."

children.text: sarvātmanā paryanunīyamāno yadā na saumitrir upaiti yogam
children.translated_text: When <s>Saumitri</s>, though entreated with his whole heart, would not consent

children.text: niyujyamāno bhuvi yauvarājye tato 'bhyaṣiñcad bharataṃ mahātmā ||
children.translated_text: to being appointed heir-apparent on earth, then the great-souled one anointed <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: rāghavaś cāpi dharmātmā prāpya rājyam anuttamam
children.translated_text: And righteous <s>Rāghava</s>, having obtained the unsurpassed kingdom,
performed many kinds of sacrifices together with his friends, brothers, and kinsmen.
The bull among kings sacrificed repeatedly with the <s>Pauṇḍarīka</s>, the <s>Aśvamedha</s>,

children.text: anyaiś ca vividhair yajñair ayajat pārthivarṣabhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Vājapeya</s>, and with various other sacrifices.
<s>Rāghava</s>, having obtained the kingdom for ten thousand years,
undertook a hundred horse-sacrifices, with excellent horses and abundant gifts.
With arms hanging down to his knees, great shoulders, and mighty splendor,
<s>Rāma</s>, attended by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, ruled the earth.

children.text: na paryadevan vidhavā na ca vyālakṛtaṃ bhayam
children.translated_text: No widows lamented, and there was no fear caused by wild beasts,

children.text: na vyādhijaṃ bhayaṃ vāpi rāme rājyaṃ praśāsati ||
children.translated_text: nor any fear born of disease, while <s>Rāma</s> governed the kingdom.
The world became free from bandits; no misfortune touched anyone.

children.text: na ca sma vṛddhā bālānāṃ pretakāryāṇi kurvate ||
children.translated_text: Nor did elders have to perform funeral rites for children.
Everything was joyful, and everyone was intent on <s>dharma</s>.
Looking only to <s>Rāma</s>, people did not harm one another.
While <s>Rāma</s> governed the kingdom, people lived for thousands of years

children.text: nirāmayā viśokāś ca rāme rājyaṃ praśāsati ||
children.translated_text: and had thousands of sons, free from illness and sorrow.
Trees were always in flower, always bearing fruit, with widely spreading boughs.

children.text: kālavarṣī ca parjanyaḥ sukhasparśaś ca mārutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The rain-cloud rained in season, and the wind was pleasant to the touch.

children.text: svakarmasu pravartante tuṣṭāḥ svair eva karmabhiḥ
children.translated_text: People devoted themselves to their own duties, content with their own work.

children.text: āsan prajā dharmaparā rāme śāsati nānṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: While <s>Rāma</s> ruled, his subjects were devoted to <s>dharma</s> and free from falsehood.
All were endowed with auspicious marks; all were devoted to <s>dharma</s>.
<s>Rāma</s> caused the kingdom to be ruled for ten thousand years.
When <s>Rāma</s> had obtained the kingdom and the rākṣasas had been slain,
all the sages came to congratulate <s>Rāghava</s>.
<s>Kauśika</s>, then <s>Yavakrīta</s>, <s>Raibhya</s>, and <s>Cyavana</s>,

children.text: kaṇvo medhātitheḥ putraḥ pūrvasyāṃ diśi ye śritāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Kaṇva</s>, son of <s>Medhātithi</s>, were those who dwelt in the eastern quarter.
The blessed <s>Svastyātreya</s>, <s>Namuci</s>, and <s>Pramucu</s> likewise

children.text: ājagmuste sahāgastyā ye śritā dakṣiṇāṃ diśam ||
children.translated_text: came together with <s>Agastya</s>, those who dwelt in the southern quarter.

children.text: pṛṣadguḥ kavaṣo dhaumyo raudreyaśca mahān ṛṣiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Pṛṣadgu</s>, <s>Kavaṣa</s>, <s>Dhaumya</s>, and <s>Raudreya</s>, the great sage,

children.text: te 'pyājagmuḥ saśiṣyā vai ye śritāḥ paścimāṃ diśam ||
children.translated_text: also came with their disciples, those who dwelt in the western quarter.
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Kaśyapa</s>, then <s>Atri</s>, <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, then <s>Gautama</s>,
<s>Jamadagni</s>, and <s>Bharadvāja</s> also were the seven great seers.
Those great-souled ones, having reached <s>Rāghava</s>'s residence,
stood there, radiant like fire, waiting for admission.
Then the doorkeeper, quickly, at <s>Agastya</s>'s word,
swiftly entered the presence of the great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>.
Seeing <s>Rāma</s> at once, shining like the full moon,
he announced that <s>Agastya</s> had arrived together with the sages.
Hearing that those sages, radiant like the young sun, had arrived,
the king then said to the doorkeeper, "Let them enter at their pleasure."
Seeing that those sages had arrived, <s>Rāma</s> rose, joined his palms,
saluted them reverently, and assigned them seats.
On those golden-decorated seats, well-spread and comfortable,
the foremost of sages sat down according to their rank.
Asked by <s>Rāma</s> about their welfare, together with their disciples and leaders,
the great seers, knowers of the Veda, spoke these words to <s>Rāma</s>:
"We are well everywhere, mighty-armed delight of the <s>Raghus</s>.

children.text: tvāṃ tu diṣṭyā kuśalinaṃ paśyāmo hataśātravam ||
children.translated_text: And by good fortune we see you well, your enemies slain.

children.text: na hi bhāraḥ sa te rāma rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: For <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas, was no heavy burden for you, <s>Rāma</s>;

children.text: sadhanustvaṃ hi lokāṃstrīn vijayethā na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: armed with your bow, you could conquer the three worlds, without doubt.

children.text: diṣṭyā tvayā hato rāma rāvaṇaḥ putrapautravān
children.translated_text: By good fortune <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, with sons and grandsons, was slain by you, <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: diṣṭyā vijayinaṃ tvādya paśyāmaḥ saha bhāryayā ||
children.translated_text: By good fortune today we see you victorious, together with your wife.
By good fortune <s>Prahasta</s>, <s>Vikaṭa</s>, <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, and <s>Mahodara</s>...
And <s>Akampana</s> and the unassailable <s>Durdharṣa</s>, those night-roamers, have been slain.

children.text: yasya pramāṇād vipulaṃ pramāṇaṃ neha vidyate
children.translated_text: He whose vast size has no equal measure here,

children.text: diṣṭyā te samare rāma kumbhakarṇo nipātitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by good fortune, <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> has been felled by you in battle.
By good fortune you came into single combat with the lord of the rākṣasas,
who was invulnerable to the gods, and you obtained victory.

children.text: saṃkhye tasya na kiṃcit tu rāvaṇasya parābhavaḥ
children.translated_text: In battle there was indeed no defeat at all for that <s>Rāvaṇa</s>;

children.text: dvandvayuddham anuprāpto diṣṭyā te rāvaṇir hataḥ ||
children.translated_text: by good fortune <s>Rāvaṇi</s>, who had met you in single combat, was slain.
By good fortune, mighty-armed hero, from him as he rushed upon you like Time itself,
from that enemy of the gods, you were released, and victory was gained by you.
This is a wonder to us, gentle one, hearing that <s>Indrajit</s> has been slain,
for in battle he bore mighty illusion and was invulnerable to all beings.

children.text: dattvā puṇyām imāṃ vīra saumyām abhayadakṣiṇām
children.translated_text: Having given this auspicious, gentle gift of fearlessness, O hero,
by good fortune you prosper through victory, <s>Kākutstha</s>, scorcher of foes.

children.text: śrutvā tu vacanaṃ teṣām ṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām
children.translated_text: But hearing the words of those seers whose selves were disciplined,

children.text: vismayaṃ paramaṃ gatvā rāmaḥ prāñjalir abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, filled with the highest wonder, spoke with joined palms.

children.text: bhavantaḥ kumbhakarṇaṃ ca rāvaṇaṃ ca niśācaram
children.translated_text: Sirs, passing over <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s> the night-roamer,
both of mighty prowess, why do you praise <s>Rāvaṇi</s>?

children.text: mahodaraṃ prahastaṃ ca virūpākṣaṃ ca rākṣasaṃ
children.translated_text: Passing over <s>Mahodara</s>, <s>Prahasta</s>, and <s>Virūpākṣa</s> the rākṣasa,
all of mighty prowess, why do you praise <s>Rāvaṇi</s>?

children.text: kīdṛśo vai prabhāvo 'sya kiṃ balaṃ kaḥ parākramaḥ
children.translated_text: What indeed is his power? What is his strength? What is his valor?
For what reason does he surpass <s>Rāvaṇa</s>?

children.text: śakyaṃ yadi mayā śrotuṃ na khalvājñāpayāmi vaḥ
children.translated_text: If it is possible for me to hear it, I certainly do not command you;

children.text: yadi guhyaṃ na ced vaktuṃ śrotum icchāmi kathyatām
children.translated_text: if it is not too secret to tell, I wish to hear it; let it be told.

children.text: kathaṃ śakro jitastena kathaṃ labdhavaraśca saḥ ||
children.translated_text: How was <s>Śakra</s> conquered by him, and how did he obtain his boon?
Hearing that speech of the great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: kumbhayonir mahātejā vākyam etad uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: the very radiant <s>Kumbhayoni</s> spoke this statement.

children.text: śṛṇu rājan yathāvṛttaṃ yasya tejobalaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: Listen, O king, to the matter as it happened, concerning him whose splendor and strength were great,

children.text: jaghāna ca ripūn yuddhe yathāvadhyaśca śatrubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: how he slew enemies in battle, and how he became invulnerable to foes.

children.text: ahaṃ te rāvaṇasyedaṃ kulaṃ janma ca rāghava
children.translated_text: I shall tell you this: <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s family and birth, O <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: varapradānaṃ ca tathā tasmai dattaṃ bravīmi te ||
children.translated_text: and also the granting of the boon that was given to him.
Long ago, in the <s>Kṛtayuga</s>, O <s>Rāma</s>, there was a powerful son of <s>Prajāpati</s>,

children.text: pulastyo nāma brahmarṣiḥ sākṣād iva pitāmahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a brahmarṣi named <s>Pulastya</s>, like <s>Pitāmaha</s> himself.
His virtues, in respect of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) and likewise of character, cannot be fully recounted;

children.text: prajāpateḥ putra iti vaktuṃ śakyaṃ hi nāmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: it is possible only to name him as the son of <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: sa tu dharmaprasaṅgena meroḥ pārśve mahāgireḥ
children.translated_text: He, in connection with sacred duty, went to the hermitage of <s>Tṛṇabindu</s>,
on the slope of the great mountain <s>Meru</s>, and that foremost sage dwelt there.
That righteous one practiced austerity, disciplined in Vedic recitation and with senses restrained;
but maidens would come to his hermitage grounds and disturb him.
Daughters of gods and pannagas, and daughters of royal seers,
as well as apsarases at play, came to that place.
Because the forest was delightful and enjoyable in every season,

children.text: nityaśastāstu taṃ deśaṃ gatvā krīḍanti kanyakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those maidens would constantly go to that place and play there.
Then the very radiant great sage, angered, uttered these words:

children.text: yā me darśanam āgacchet sā garbhaṃ dhārayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: "Whichever woman comes within my sight will conceive a child."

children.text: tāstu sarvāḥ pratigatāḥ śrutvā vākyaṃ mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing the words of that great-souled one, they all went back,
frightened by fear of a brahmanical curse, and they did not approach that place.
But the daughter of the royal seer <s>Tṛṇabindu</s> did not hear it;
having gone to his hermitage grounds, she wandered about quite fearlessly.

children.text: tasminn eva tu kāle sa prājāpatyo mahān ṛṣiḥ
children.translated_text: At that very time that great seer, the son of <s>Prajāpati</s>,
was performing Vedic recitation there, his radiance made bright by austerity.

children.text: sā tu vedadhvaniṃ śrutvā dṛṣṭvā caiva tapodhanam
children.translated_text: Hearing the sound of the Veda and seeing that treasure of austerity,
she became pale in body, with the signs arising in her body clearly manifest.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā paramasaṃvignā sā tu tadrūpam ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that condition of herself, she was deeply alarmed,

children.text: idaṃ me kiṃ nviti jñātvā pitur gatvāgrataḥ sthitā ||
children.translated_text: and, wondering, "What is this with me?" she went and stood before her father.

children.text: tāṃ tu dṛṣṭvā tathābhūtāṃ tṛṇabindur athābravīt
children.translated_text: Seeing her in such a state, <s>Tṛṇabindu</s> then said:

children.text: kiṃ tvam etat tvasadṛśaṃ dhārayasyātmano vapuḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Why do you bear this body of yours, so unlike yourself?"

children.text: sā tu kṛtvāñjaliṃ dīnā kanyovāca tapodhanam
children.translated_text: Then the distressed maiden made añjali (a gesture of reverence) and spoke to that ascetic:

children.text: na jāne kāraṇaṃ tāta yena me rūpam īdṛśam ||
children.translated_text: "I do not know the cause, father, by which my appearance is like this.

children.text: kiṃ tu pūrvaṃ gatāsmyekā maharṣer bhāvitātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: But earlier I went alone to the divine hermitage of the great-souled sage,
<s>Pulastya</s>, to search for my own companions.

children.text: na ca paśyāmyahaṃ tatra kāṃcid apyāgatāṃ sakhīm
children.translated_text: And there I did not see even one friend who had come,

children.text: rūpasya tu viparyāsaṃ dṛṣṭvā cāham ihāgatā ||
children.translated_text: and, seeing the alteration in my appearance, I came here."
Then the royal seer <s>Tṛṇabindu</s>, his radiance bright with austerity,
entered meditation and saw that this too had arisen from the sage's act.

children.text: sa tu vijñāya taṃ śāpaṃ maharṣer bhāvitātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Having understood the curse of the great-souled sage,

children.text: gṛhītvā tanayāṃ gatvā pulastyam idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: he took his daughter, went to <s>Pulastya</s>, and said this:

children.text: bhagavaṃstanayāṃ me tvaṃ guṇaiḥ svair eva bhūṣitām
children.translated_text: "Blessed lord, accept this daughter of mine, adorned with her own virtues,
as alms, O great seer, offered here of her own accord.
For you, who are devoted to the practice of austerity and whose senses are wearied,
she will always be intent on service; there is no doubt."

children.text: taṃ bruvāṇaṃ tu tadvākyaṃ rājarṣiṃ dhārmikaṃ tadā
children.translated_text: To the righteous royal seer as he spoke those words then,

children.text: jighṛkṣur abravīt kanyāṃ bāḍham ityeva sa dvijaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the twice-born one, wishing to accept the maiden, said simply, "So be it."

children.text: dattvā tu sa gato rājā svam āśramapadaṃ tadā
children.translated_text: Having given her, the king then went to his own hermitage grounds.

children.text: sāpi tatrāvasat kanyā toṣayantī patiṃ guṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: She too dwelt there, pleasing her husband with her virtues,

children.text: prītaḥ sa tu mahātejā vākyam etad uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: and that very radiant one, pleased, spoke this statement.

children.text: parituṣṭo 'smi bhadraṃ te guṇānāṃ saṃpadā bhṛśam
children.translated_text: I am greatly pleased with the abundance of your virtues; may there be welfare for you.

children.text: tasmāt te viramāmyadya putram ātmasamaṃ guṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore today I shall give you a son equal to myself in virtues,
a maker of both lineages, renowned as <s>Paulastya</s>.
And since the Veda was heard by you here while I was reciting it,

children.text: tasmāt sa viśravā nāma bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore he will without doubt have the name <s>Viśravas</s>.

children.text: evam uktā tu sā kanyā prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, that maiden, delighted in her heart,
after only a short time gave birth to a son, <s>Viśravas</s>.
He, famous in the three worlds and endowed with purity and <s>dharma</s> (righteous conduct),
was, like his father, devoted to austerity: <s>Viśravas</s>, foremost of sages.
Then <s>Viśravas</s>, the son of <s>Pulastya</s>, foremost of sages,
after only a short time stood firm in austerity, like his father.
He was truthful, virtuous, capable, devoted to Vedic study, and pure,
unattached to all enjoyments and always intent on <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: jñātvā tasya tu tadvṛttaṃ bharadvājo mahān ṛṣiḥ
children.translated_text: Knowing that conduct of his, the great seer <s>Bharadvāja</s>

children.text: dadau viśravase bhāryāṃ svāṃ sutāṃ devavarṇinīm ||
children.translated_text: gave to <s>Viśravas</s> as wife his own daughter, <s>Devavarṇinī</s>.
Having duly accepted the daughter of <s>Bharadvāja</s> then,
<s>Viśravas</s>, foremost of sages, was filled with supreme joy.
With her the righteous-souled one begot a mighty child, wondrous in the highest degree,
endowed with all brahmanical qualities.

children.text: tasmiñ jāte tu saṃhṛṣṭaḥ sa babhūva pitāmahaḥ
children.translated_text: When he was born, the grandsire became delighted,
and, pleased, gave him a name then together with the divine seers.
Since he is the offspring of <s>Viśravas</s> and, by likeness, is as if another <s>Viśravas</s>,
therefore he will become renowned by the name <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>.
Then that <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, dwelling there in the ascetic grove,
grew in great splendor like a fire fed by oblations.
While that great-souled one was living in the hermitage, this thought arose in him:

children.text: cariṣye niyato dharmaṃ dharmo hi paramā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: "I shall practice <s>dharma</s> with self-restraint, for <s>dharma</s> is the supreme goal."
He performed austerities for thousands of years in the great forest,

children.text: pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu taṃ taṃ vidhim avartata ||
children.translated_text: and, when each thousand years was complete, he observed one discipline after another.
He lived on water, on air, and then with no food at all;
in this way those thousands of years passed as if they were only years.

children.text: atha prīto mahātejāḥ sendraiḥ suragaṇaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Then the greatly splendid <s>Brahmā</s>, pleased and accompanied by the hosts of gods with <s>Indra</s>,
went to his hermitage and spoke these words:
"I am pleased with you, child, by this act of yours, O firm-vowed one.

children.text: varaṃ vṛṇīṣva bhadraṃ te varārhastvaṃ hi me mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Choose a boon; welfare to you, for I consider you worthy of a boon."
Then <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> spoke to the grandsire who stood before him:
"Lord, I would desire guardianship of the worlds and the protection of wealth."
Then, with a delighted mind, <s>Brahmā</s>

children.text: brahmā suragaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ bāḍham ityeva hṛṣṭavat ||
children.translated_text: said joyfully to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, together with the hosts of gods, "So be it."

children.text: ahaṃ hi lokapālānāṃ caturthaṃ sraṣṭum udyataḥ
children.translated_text: "For I am intent on creating a fourth among the guardians of the worlds,

children.text: yamendravaruṇānāṃ hi padaṃ yat tava cepsitam ||
children.translated_text: the office of <s>Yama</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s>, which you have desired.
That has been done. Go, knower of <s>dharma</s>; obtain lordship over wealth.
Today you shall be the fourth beside <s>Yama</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s>.
And accept this aircraft named <s>Puṣpaka</s>, resembling the sun,
for your vehicle; attain equality with the thirty gods.

children.text: svasti te 'stu gamiṣyāmaḥ sarva eva yathāgatam
children.translated_text: May it be well with you. We shall all go just as we came.

children.text: kṛtakṛtyā vayaṃ tāta dattvā tava mahāvaram ||
children.translated_text: Dear child, we have accomplished our purpose by granting you this great boon."
When the gods, with <s>Brahmā</s> at their head, had gone to the sky,

children.text: dhaneśaḥ pitaraṃ prāha vinayāt praṇato vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the lord of wealth bowed humbly and spoke these words to his father:
"Lord, I have received a boon from the lotus-born one,

children.text: nivāsaṃ na tu me devo vidadhe sa prajāpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: but that god, the lord of creatures, did not appoint a dwelling for me.

children.text: tat paśya bhagavan kaṃcid deśaṃ vāsāya naḥ prabho
children.translated_text: Therefore, lord, please consider some region as a residence for us, O master,

children.text: na ca pīḍā bhaved yatra prāṇino yasya kasyacit ||
children.translated_text: where there would be no oppression of any living being at all."
Thus addressed by his son, <s>Viśravas</s>, foremost of sages,

children.text: vacanaṃ prāha dharmajña śrūyatām iti dharmavit ||
children.translated_text: knower of <s>dharma</s>, spoke this word: "Listen," said that knower of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: laṅkā nāma purī ramyā nirmitā viśvakarmaṇā
children.translated_text: "There is a lovely city named <s>Laṅkā</s>, built by <s>Viśvakarman</s>,
as a residence for the rākṣasas, like <s>Amarāvatī</s> for <s>Indra</s>.
That city is delightful, with gateways of gold and vaidūrya gems.
Long ago it was abandoned by the rākṣasas, afflicted by fear of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
and emptied of all hosts of rākṣasas, who went to the depths of <s>Rasātala</s>.

children.text: sa tvaṃ tatra nivāsāya rocayasva matiṃ svakām
children.translated_text: So set your own mind on dwelling there.

children.text: nirdoṣastatra te vāso na ca bādhāsti kasyacit ||
children.translated_text: Your residence there will be blameless, and there is no injury to anyone."

children.text: etacchrutvā tu dharmātmā dharmiṣṭhaṃ vacanaṃ pituḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard this righteous word of his father,
that righteous-souled one then settled in <s>Laṅkā</s> on the summit of the mountain.
With thousands of delighted and ever-joyful Nairṛtas,
it was quickly filled all at once by his command.
Then the righteous-souled lord of the Nairṛtas, the son of <s>Viśravas</s>,
dwelt there happily in <s>Laṅkā</s>, girdled by the sea.
At proper times, with disciplined mind, the lord of wealth

children.text: abhyagacchat susaṃhṛṣṭaḥ pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca saḥ ||
children.translated_text: joyfully visited his father and mother in the <s>Puṣpaka</s>.

children.text: sa devagandharvagaṇair abhiṣṭutas tathaiva siddhaiḥ saha cāraṇair api
children.translated_text: Praised by hosts of gods and gandharvas, and likewise by siddhas together with cāraṇas,

children.text: gabhastibhiḥ sūrya ivaujasā vṛtaḥ pituḥ samīpaṃ prayayau śriyā vṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: surrounded by splendor as the sun is by rays, he went near his father, attended by prosperity.
Hearing the speech uttered by <s>Agastya</s>, <s>Rāma</s> was filled with wonder:

children.text: pūrvam āsīt tu laṅkāyāṃ rakṣasām iti saṃbhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "So this was the former origin of the rākṣasas in <s>Laṅkā</s>."
Then, shaking his head, he whose form was equal to the three sacred fires
Looking again and again at <s>Agastya</s>, he addressed him with a smile.
Blessed lord, even before this, <s>Laṅkā</s> belonged to flesh-eaters;

children.text: itīdaṃ bhavataḥ śrutvā vismayo janito mama ||
children.translated_text: having heard this from you, wonder has arisen in me.

children.text: pulastyavaṃśād udbhūtā rākṣasā iti naḥ śrutam
children.translated_text: We have heard that the rākṣasas arose from the line of <s>Pulastya</s>;
now another origin too has been recounted by you.
Than <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, <s>Prahasta</s>, and even <s>Vikaṭa</s>,

children.text: rāvaṇasya ca putrebhyaḥ kiṃ nu te balavattarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and than the sons of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, were they perhaps stronger?

children.text: ka eṣāṃ pūrvako brahman kiṃnāmā kiṃtapobalaḥ
children.translated_text: Who was the ancestor of these, O brahman? What was his name? What was the power of his austerity?

children.text: aparādhaṃ ca kaṃ prāpya viṣṇunā drāvitāḥ purā ||
children.translated_text: And what offense did they incur, when long ago they were put to flight by <s>Viṣṇu</s>?
Tell me all this in full, O sinless one;

children.text: kautūhalaṃ kṛtaṃ mahyaṃ nuda bhānur yathā tamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: dispel the curiosity that has been produced in me, as the sun dispels darkness.
Hearing that speech of <s>Rāghava</s>, adorned with refinement,
<s>Agastya</s>, slightly amazed, spoke to that <s>Rāghava</s>.
Long ago <s>Prajāpati</s>, the lotus-born, born from the waters, having created the waters,
created beings for the guarding of those waters, he who was born from the lotus.
Those beings approached the maker of beings humbly,
saying, "What shall we do?" afflicted by hunger, thirst, and fear.
Then <s>Prajāpati</s>, as if laughing, said to those beings,

children.text: ābhāṣya vācā yatnena rakṣadhvam iti mānadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: addressing them carefully with speech, "Protect them," O giver of honor.
There some said, "We shall protect," and others likewise, "We shall worship";
when this had been said by those who were hungry and not hungry, the maker of beings then said to them:

children.text: rakṣāma iti yair uktaṃ rākṣasāste bhavantu vaḥ
children.translated_text: "Those by whom it was said, 'We shall protect,' shall be rākṣasas among you;

children.text: yakṣāma iti yair uktaṃ te vai yakṣā bhavantu vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: those by whom it was said, 'We shall worship,' shall indeed be yakṣas among you."
There <s>Heti</s> and <s>Praheti</s>, two brothers, bulls among rākṣasas,
like <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, became subduers of enemies.
<s>Praheti</s> was righteous there, and he did not desire wives;

children.text: hetir dārakriyārthaṃ tu yatnaṃ param athākarot ||
children.translated_text: but <s>Heti</s> then made the utmost effort for the sake of marriage.

children.text: sa kālabhaginīṃ kanyāṃ bhayāṃ nāma bhayāvahām
children.translated_text: He, immeasurable in spirit and very wise, married <s>Bhayā</s>, the fearsome maiden,
the sister of <s>Kāla</s>, by himself.
In her <s>Heti</s>, the foremost of rākṣasas, begot

children.text: putraṃ putravatāṃ śreṣṭho vidyutkeśa iti śrutam ||
children.translated_text: a son, the best of those who have sons, known as <s>Vidyutkeśa</s>.
<s>Vidyutkeśa</s>, the son of <s>Heti</s>, had a splendor equal to blazing fire;
that very radiant one grew like a lotus in the midst of water.

children.text: sa yadā yauvanaṃ bhadram anuprāpto niśācaraḥ
children.translated_text: When that night-roamer reached auspicious youth,

children.text: tato dārakriyāṃ tasya kartuṃ vyavasitaḥ pitā ||
children.translated_text: his father then resolved to arrange his marriage.
Then <s>Heti</s>, the foremost rākṣasa, chose for his son
the daughter of <s>Saṃdhyā</s>, equal to <s>Saṃdhyā</s> in majesty.

children.text: avaśyam eva dātavyā parasmai seti saṃdhyayā
children.translated_text: Thinking, "She must certainly be given to another," <s>Saṃdhyā</s>
gave her daughter to <s>Vidyutkeśa</s>, O <s>Rāghava</s>.
Having obtained the daughter of <s>Saṃdhyā</s>, <s>Vidyutkeśa</s> the night-roamer

children.text: ramate sa tayā sārdhaṃ paulomyā maghavān iva ||
children.translated_text: delighted with her, as <s>Maghavan</s> delights with <s>Paulomī</s>.
Then after some time, O <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Sālakaṭaṅkaṭā</s>
conceived from <s>Vidyutkeśa</s>, like a bank of clouds from the ocean.
Then that rākṣasī, having gone to <s>Mandara</s>, gave birth to a child

children.text: prasūtā mandaraṃ gatvā gaṅgā garbham ivāgnijam ||
children.translated_text: shining like a cloud-filled mass, as <s>Gaṅgā</s> gave birth to the fire-born embryo.

children.text: tam utsṛjya tu sā garbhaṃ vidyutkeśād ratārthinī
children.translated_text: But casting aside that child born from <s>Vidyutkeśa</s>, desirous of pleasure,

children.text: reme sā patinā sārdhaṃ vismṛtya sutam ātmajam ||
children.translated_text: she sported with her husband, forgetting her own son.
Abandoned by her, that infant, equal in brilliance to the autumn sun,

children.text: pāṇim āsye samādhāya ruroda ghanarāḍ iva ||
children.translated_text: put his hand in his mouth and cried like the lord of clouds.

children.text: athopariṣṭād gacchan vai vṛṣabhastho haraḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: Then above, as lord <s>Hara</s> was passing by, mounted on his bull,
he saw, together with <s>Umā</s>, the weeping son of the rākṣasa.
Then, out of <s>Pārvatī</s>'s feeling of compassion, <s>Bhava</s>, the destroyer of <s>Tripura</s>,

children.text: taṃ rākṣasātmajaṃ cakre mātur eva vayaḥsamam ||
children.translated_text: made that rākṣasa child equal in age to his mother.
And making him immortal, inexhaustible and undecaying, great god <s>Mahādeva</s>
gave him a city moving through the sky, out of the wish to please <s>Pārvatī</s>.
A boon too was given by <s>Umā</s> to rākṣasī women, O prince:

children.text: sadya upalabdhir garbhasya prasūtiḥ sadya eva ca
children.translated_text: the immediate obtaining of pregnancy, and delivery immediately as well,

children.text: sadya eva vayaḥprāptir mātur eva vayaḥsamam ||
children.translated_text: and immediate attainment of youth, equal in age to the mother.

children.text: tataḥ sukeśo varadānagarvitaḥ śriyaṃ prabhoḥ prāpya harasya pārśvataḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sukeśa</s>, proud because of the granted boon, having obtained the lordly prosperity of <s>Hara</s>'s favor,

children.text: cacāra sarvatra mahāmatiḥ khagaḥ khagaṃ puraṃ prāpya puraṃdaro yathā ||
children.translated_text: that very wise sky-goer moved everywhere after obtaining a sky-going city, like <s>Purandara</s>.

children.text: sukeśaṃ dhārmikaṃ dṛṣṭvā varalabdhaṃ ca rākṣasaṃ
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Sukeśa</s>, a righteous rākṣasa who had received a boon,
a gandharva named <s>Grāmaṇī</s>, equal in splendor to <s>Viśvāvasu</s>,

children.text: tasya devavatī nāma dvitīyā śrīr ivātmajā
children.translated_text: had a daughter named <s>Devavatī</s>, like a second <s>Śrī</s>;

children.text: tāṃ sukeśāya dharmeṇa dadau dakṣaḥ śriyaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: he gave her lawfully to <s>Sukeśa</s>, as the capable <s>Dakṣa</s> gave <s>Śrī</s>.

children.text: varadānakṛtaiśvaryaṃ sā taṃ prāpya patiṃ priyam
children.translated_text: Having obtained as her beloved husband that one whose sovereignty was made by the granted boon,

children.text: āsīd devavatī tuṣṭā dhanaṃ prāpyeva nirdhanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Devavatī</s> was pleased, like a poor person obtaining wealth.

children.text: sa tayā saha saṃyukto rarāja rajanīcaraḥ
children.translated_text: United with her, that night-roamer shone,
like a great elephant with a cow-elephant, come forth from <s>Añjana</s>.
And in <s>Devavatī</s>, O <s>Rāghava</s>, <s>Sukeśa</s> begot
three rākṣasa sons equal to the three-eyed god, that lord of rākṣasas:

children.text: mālyavantaṃ sumāliṃ ca māliṃ ca balināṃ varam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mālyavat</s>, <s>Sumāli</s>, and <s>Māli</s>, the best of the strong.
They were like the three worlds, undisturbed; like the three fires standing firm;
like the three mantras, exceedingly fierce; like three dreadful diseases.
The three sons of <s>Sukeśa</s>, equal in splendor to the three sacred fires,
grew there like diseases left unattended.

children.text: varaprāptiṃ pituste tu jñātvaiśvaryaṃ tato mahat
children.translated_text: But when those brothers learned of their father's gaining a boon and of his great lordship thereafter,
they went to <s>Meru</s>, firmly resolved to practice austerity.
Taking on terrible vows, the rākṣasas, O best of kings,
performed a dreadful austerity, one that brought fear to all beings.
With austerities hard to perform on earth, endowed with truth, uprightness, and self-control,
they scorched the three worlds, together with gods, asuras, and human beings.
Then the mighty four-faced lord, seated in an excellent aerial car,
addressed the sons of <s>Sukeśa</s> and said, "I am the giver of boons."

children.text: brahmāṇaṃ varadaṃ jñātvā sendrair devagaṇair vṛtam
children.translated_text: Knowing <s>Brahmā</s> to be a giver of boons, surrounded by hosts of gods together with <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: ūcuḥ prāñjalayaḥ sarve vepamānā iva drumāḥ ||
children.translated_text: they all spoke with folded hands, trembling like trees.

children.text: tapasārādhito deva yadi no diśase varam
children.translated_text: "O god, if, pleased by our austerity, you grant us a boon,
may we be unconquerable, slayers of enemies, and likewise long-lived;
may we be powerful," they said, "and devoted to one another."
Saying, "So it shall be," the lord spoke to the sons of <s>Sukeśa</s>;
and <s>Brahmā</s>, affectionate toward brahmans, went away to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: varaṃ labdhvā tataḥ sarve rāma rātriṃcarāstadā
children.translated_text: Then, O <s>Rāma</s>, after they had obtained the boon, all those night-roamers
began to harass gods and asuras, made utterly fearless by the granting of the boon.
The thirty gods, with groups of seers and cāraṇas, being struck down by them,
could find no protector, like men who are in hell.

children.text: atha te viśvakarmāṇaṃ śilpināṃ varam avyayam
children.translated_text: Then those rākṣasas assembled and, delighted, addressed <s>Viśvakarman</s>,
the imperishable best of craftsmen, O best of the <s>Raghus</s>.
"You alone are the maker of dwellings for the gods, fulfilling what is desired in their hearts;

children.text: asmākam api tāvat tvaṃ gṛhaṃ kuru mahāmate ||
children.translated_text: therefore, O great-minded one, make a dwelling for us as well.

children.text: himavantaṃ samāśritya meruṃ mandaram eva vā
children.translated_text: Taking support from <s>Himavant</s>, or <s>Meru</s>, or <s>Mandara</s>,
let a great dwelling, like the house of <s>Maheśvara</s>, be made for us."
Then <s>Viśvakarman</s> told those great-armed rākṣasas
of a residence like <s>Amarāvatī</s>, the city of <s>Śakra</s>.
"On the shore of the southern ocean there is a mountain named <s>Trikūṭa</s>;
on the middle peak of that mountain, which resembles a cloud,
hard for even birds to reach, with its four sides cut by chisels,
thirty yojanas wide, with golden ramparts and gateways,
stands a city named <s>Laṅkā</s>, built by me at <s>Śakra</s>'s command.
Dwell in that city, O unassailable best of rākṣasas,
like the dwellers in heaven together with <s>Indra</s> when they have reached <s>Amarāvatī</s>.
Having reached the fortress of <s>Laṅkā</s>, surrounded by many rākṣasas,
you will be hard for enemies to assail, O destroyers of enemies."
Hearing the words of <s>Viśvakarman</s>, those rākṣasas then, O <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: sahasrānucarā gatvā laṅkāṃ tām avasan purīm ||
children.translated_text: went with thousands of attendants and inhabited that city <s>Laṅkā</s>.
Having obtained <s>Laṅkā</s>, with firm ramparts and moats and surrounded by hundreds of golden houses,

children.text: laṅkām avāpya te hṛṣṭā viharanti niśācarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those night-roamers rejoiced and sported there.
There was a gandharvī named <s>Narmadā</s>, enriched with many virtues;
she had three daughters, equal in splendor to wisdom, fortune, and fame.
In order of seniority, she, though no rākṣasī herself, joyfully gave
those maidens, whose faces were like the full moon, to those rākṣasas.
The three gandharva maidens, highly blessed, were given to the three rākṣasa lords
by their mother under the constellation whose deity is <s>Bhaga</s>.
Having taken wives, O <s>Rāma</s>, the sons of <s>Sukeśa</s>, O lord,
sported with their wives like immortals with apsarases.

children.text: tatra mālyavato bhāryā sundarī nāma sundarī
children.translated_text: Among them, <s>Mālyavat</s>'s wife was a beautiful woman named <s>Sundarī</s>;

children.text: sa tasyāṃ janayāmāsa yad apatyaṃ nibodha tat ||
children.translated_text: now hear of the offspring that he begot in her.
<s>Vajramuṣṭi</s>, <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, and the rākṣasa <s>Durmukha</s>,
<s>Suptaghna</s>, <s>Yajñakopa</s>, and likewise <s>Matta</s> and <s>Unmatta</s>,

children.text: analā cābhavat kanyā sundaryāṃ rāma sundarī ||
children.translated_text: and a beautiful daughter, <s>Analā</s>, were born from <s>Sundarī</s>, O <s>Rāma</s>.
<s>Sumāli</s>'s wife too had a face like the full moon;
she was named <s>Ketumatī</s> and was dearer to him than life itself.
The night-roamer <s>Sumāli</s> begot offspring
in <s>Ketumatī</s>, O great king; hear of them from me in order.
<s>Prahasta</s>, <s>Akampana</s>, <s>Vikaṭa</s>, and <s>Kālakārmuka</s>,
then <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>, <s>Daṇḍa</s>, and mighty <s>Supārśva</s>,
<s>Saṃhrādi</s>, <s>Praghasa</s>, and the rākṣasa <s>Bhāsakarṇa</s>,

children.text: rākā puṣpotkaṭā caiva kaikasī ca śucismitā
children.translated_text: <s>Rākā</s>, <s>Puṣpotkaṭā</s>, <s>Kaikasī</s> of the pure smile,

children.text: kumbhīnasī ca ityete sumāleḥ prasavāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Kumbhīnasī</s>: these are remembered as <s>Sumāli</s>'s children.
<s>Māli</s>'s wife was a gandharvī named <s>Vasudā</s>, endowed with beauty,
lotus-petal-eyed and fair-eyed, like the finest yakṣī.
O lord, hear now as I tell you of the offspring

children.text: apatyaṃ kathyamānaṃ tanmayā tvaṃ śṛṇu rāghava ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Sumāli</s>'s younger brother begot in her, O <s>Rāghava</s>.
<s>Anala</s>, <s>Anila</s>, <s>Hara</s>, and <s>Saṃpāti</s>:
these night-roamers, the sons of <s>Māli</s>, were <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>'s ministers.

children.text: tatastu te rākṣasapuṃgavāstrayo niśācaraiḥ putraśataiśca saṃvṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Then those three bulls among rākṣasas, surrounded by night-roamers and hundreds of sons,

children.text: surān sahendrān ṛṣināgadānavān babādhire te balavīryadarpitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: proud of their strength and valor, oppressed the gods together with <s>Indra</s>, and the seers, nāgas, and dānavas.

children.text: jagad bhramanto 'nilavad durāsadā raṇe ca mṛtyupratimāḥ samāhitāḥ
children.translated_text: Roaming the world like the wind, hard to approach, and in battle like Death, they were intent and composed;

children.text: varapradānād abhigarvitā bhṛśaṃ kratukriyāṇāṃ praśamaṃkarāḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: greatly arrogant because of the granted boon, they always brought sacrificial rites to a halt.
Struck down by them, the gods and the seers rich in austerity
went in fear to <s>Maheśvara</s>, the god of gods, for refuge.

children.text: te sametya tu kāmāriṃ tripurāriṃ trilocanam
children.translated_text: Assembling before the foe of <s>Kāma</s>, the foe of <s>Tripura</s>, the three-eyed one,
the gods spoke with folded hands, their voices choked by fear.
O blessed lord, by the sons of <s>Sukeśa</s>, grown arrogant through the boon of <s>Pitāmaha</s>,
O lord of creatures, O subduer of enemies, all creatures are being oppressed.
Places of refuge and places that were no refuge have alike been made into hermitages for us,

children.text: svargācca cyāvitaḥ śakraḥ svarge krīḍanti śakravat ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Śakra</s> has been driven down from heaven, while they sport in heaven like <s>Śakra</s> himself.

children.text: ahaṃ viṣṇur ahaṃ rudro brahmāhaṃ devarāḍ aham
children.translated_text: "I am <s>Viṣṇu</s>, I am <s>Rudra</s>, I am <s>Brahmā</s>, I am the king of the gods;
I am <s>Yama</s>, I am <s>Varuṇa</s>, I am the moon, and I am the sun as well."

children.text: iti te rākṣasā deva varadānena darpitāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, O god, those rākṣasas, made proud by the granting of the boon,

children.text: bādhante samaroddharṣā ye ca teṣāṃ puraḥsarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and those who go at their head, exultant in battle, oppress us.

children.text: tanno deva bhayārtānām abhayaṃ dātum arhasi
children.translated_text: Therefore, O god, you ought to grant fearlessness to us, who are stricken with fear.
Assuming an inauspicious form, kill those thorns of the gods.
When all the gods had spoken thus, the matted-haired, blue-red lord,

children.text: sukeśaṃ prati sāpekṣa āha devagaṇān prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: with regard for <s>Sukeśa</s>, spoke to the hosts of gods.
I shall not kill them; those asuras are not to be slain by me.

children.text: kiṃ tu mantraṃ pradāsyāmi yo vai tānnihaniṣyati ||
children.translated_text: But I shall give you counsel about the one who will indeed kill them.
With this very effort placed before you, O bulls among the gods,

children.text: gacchantu śaraṇaṃ viṣṇuṃ haniṣyati sa tān prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: go for refuge to <s>Viṣṇu</s>; that lord will kill them.
Then, acclaiming <s>Maheśvara</s> with cries of victory,
they went to <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s presence, afflicted by fear of the night-roamers.

children.text: śaṅkhacakradharaṃ devaṃ praṇamya bahu mānya ca
children.translated_text: Bowing to the god who bears the conch and discus, and honoring him greatly,
they spoke these agitated words, distressed by the sons of <s>Sukeśa</s>:
O god, by the three sons of <s>Sukeśa</s>, who are like the three sacred fires,
our stations have been overrun and taken away through the power of the boon.

children.text: laṅkā nāma purī durgā trikūṭaśikhare sthitā
children.translated_text: There is a difficult city named <s>Laṅkā</s>, standing on the peak of <s>Trikūṭa</s>;
stationed there, the night-roamers greatly oppress us all.

children.text: sa tvam asmatpriyārthaṃ tu jahi tānmadhusūdana
children.translated_text: So, for our welfare, slay them, O <s>Madhusūdana</s>;
send to <s>Yama</s> those whose lotus-like faces have been cut by the discus.
In dangers you are the giver of fearlessness to us; there is no other equal to you.

children.text: nuda tvaṃ no bhayaṃ deva nīhāram iva bhāskaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Dispel our fear, O god, as the sun dispels mist.
Thus addressed by the deities, <s>Janārdana</s>, the god of gods,

children.text: abhayaṃ bhayado 'rīṇāṃ dattvā devān uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: the giver of fear to enemies, granted fearlessness and spoke to the gods.
I know the rākṣasa <s>Sukeśa</s>, made proud by the boon from <s>Īśāna</s>,
