children.text: tāṃścāsya tanayāñ jāne yeṣāṃ jyeṣṭhaḥ sa mālyavān ||
children.translated_text: and I know his sons too, of whom the eldest is <s>Mālyavān</s>.
Those base rākṣasas who have overstepped all bounds
I shall destroy in battle. Gods, be free from feverish fear.
Thus addressed by mighty <s>Viṣṇu</s>, all those gods

children.text: yathā vāsaṃ yayur hṛṣṭāḥ praśaṃsanto janārdanam ||
children.translated_text: went joyfully to their own dwellings, praising <s>Janārdana</s>.
The night-roamer <s>Mālyavān</s>, hearing of the gods' undertaking,

children.text: śrutvā tau bhrātarau vīrāvidaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: spoke these words to his two heroic brothers:
The immortals and the seers, gathering to <s>Śaṃkara</s>,
are said to have sought our death and to have spoken this to the three-eyed god:
"O god, the sons of <s>Sukeśa</s>, arrogant through the strength of boons,
terrible in form and fully prepared, oppress us at every step.

children.text: rākṣasair abhibhūtāḥ sma na śaktāḥ sma umāpate
children.translated_text: We are overcome by the rākṣasas, O husband of <s>Umā</s>, and are unable

children.text: sveṣu veśmasu saṃsthātuṃ bhayāt teṣāṃ durātmanām ||
children.translated_text: to remain in our own homes because of fear of those wicked ones.

children.text: tad asmākaṃ hitārthe tvaṃ jahi tāṃstāṃstrilocana
children.translated_text: Therefore, for our welfare, kill those rākṣasas, O three-eyed god;
burn the rākṣasas with a mere hum, O best of those who burn."
Hearing himself addressed in this way by the Thirty, the slayer of <s>Andhaka</s>

children.text: śiraḥ karaṃ ca dhunvāna idaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: shook his head and hand and spoke these words:

children.text: avadhyā mama te devāḥ sukeśatanayā raṇe
children.translated_text: The sons of <s>Sukeśa</s> are not to be slain by me in battle, O gods;

children.text: mantraṃ tu vaḥ pradāsyāmi yo vai tānnihaniṣyati ||
children.translated_text: but I shall give you counsel about the one who will indeed kill them.
He who has discus and mace in hand, the yellow-robed <s>Janārdana</s>,

children.text: haniṣyati sa tān yuddhe śaraṇaṃ taṃ prapadyatha ||
children.translated_text: will kill them in battle; take refuge in him.

children.text: harānnāvāpya te kāmaṃ kāmārim abhivādya ca
children.translated_text: Having failed to obtain their wish from <s>Hara</s>, and having bowed to the enemy of <s>Kāma</s>,
they reached <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>'s abode and reported everything to him.
Then the gods, with <s>Indra</s> at their head, were told by <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>:
"I shall destroy the enemies of the gods. Gods, be free from feverish fear."
For the gods, terrified with fear, <s>Hari</s> has promised our death,
O bulls among rākṣasas; consider what is proper in this matter.
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the death of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> and of other enemies of the gods,

children.text: duḥkhaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ jetuṃ yo no hantum abhīpsati ||
children.translated_text: is hard to conquer, and he seeks to kill us.

children.text: tataḥ sumālī mālī ca śrutvā mālyavato vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sumālī</s> and <s>Mālī</s>, hearing <s>Mālyavān</s>'s words,
spoke to their eldest brother, like two shares of splendor addressing <s>Vāsava</s>:

children.text: svadhītaṃ dattam iṣṭaṃ ca aiśvaryaṃ paripālitam
children.translated_text: Sacred study has been completed, gifts have been given, sacrifice has been performed, and sovereignty has been protected;

children.text: āyur nirāmayaṃ prāptaṃ svadharmaḥ sthāpitaśca naḥ ||
children.translated_text: a life free from illness has been gained, and our own <s>dharma</s> (proper order) has been established.
Having plunged with floods of weapons into the unshakable ocean of the gods,

children.text: jitā devā raṇe nityaṃ na no mṛtyukṛtaṃ bhayam ||
children.translated_text: we have constantly conquered the gods in battle; we have no fear caused by death.
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, and <s>Yama</s> as well,

children.text: asmākaṃ pramukhe sthātuṃ sarva eva hi bibhyati ||
children.translated_text: all fear to stand in front of us.
There is no fault of <s>Viṣṇu</s> in this matter, O lord of rākṣasas;

children.text: devānām eva doṣeṇa viṣṇoḥ pracalitaṃ manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: only through the fault of the gods has <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s mind been stirred.
Therefore today, fully prepared and surrounded by all our army,

children.text: devān eva jighāṃsāmo yebhyo doṣaḥ samutthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: let us seek to kill the gods themselves, from whom the offense has arisen.

children.text: iti mālī sumālī ca mālyavān agrajaḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Mālī</s>, <s>Sumālī</s>, and the elder <s>Mālyavān</s>, their lord,

children.text: udyogaṃ ghoṣayitvātha rākṣasāḥ sarva eva te
children.translated_text: proclaimed the mobilization, and then all those rākṣasas,
angry, went out to battle like the forces of <s>Jambha</s> and <s>Vṛtra</s>.
With chariots, with lordly elephants, and with horses like mountains...
With asses, cattle, camels, śiṃśumāras, and serpents,
with makaras, tortoises, fish, and birds resembling <s>Garuḍa</s>,
with lions, tigers, boars, sṛmaras, and camarīs as well,

children.text: tyaktvā laṅkāṃ tataḥ sarve rākṣasā balagarvitāḥ
children.translated_text: then all the rākṣasas, proud of their strength, abandoned <s>Laṅkā</s>
and set out for the world of the gods, the enemies of the deities going to fight.
Seeing the overturning of <s>Laṅkā</s>, those beings dwelling in <s>Laṅkā</s>
were filled with fear and altogether despondent.
Then fearful portents, on the earth and in the midair, commanded by Time,
quickly arose for the destruction of the lords of the rākṣasas.

children.text: asthīni meghā varṣanti uṣṇaṃ śoṇitam eva ca
children.translated_text: Clouds rained down bones, and also hot blood;
the ocean too crossed its shore, and the greatest mountains shook.
Releasing bursts of loud laughter, with sounds like the thunder of clouds,
spirits fell all around in their thousands, dancing.
A great circle of vultures too, with mouths belching fire,
wheeled above the rākṣasas like the wheel of Time.
Disregarding those inconceivable great portents, the rākṣasas, proud of their strength,
kept going and did not turn back, bound fast by the nooses of death.

children.text: mālyavāṃśca sumālī ca mālī ca rajanīcarāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Mālyavān</s>, <s>Sumālī</s>, and <s>Mālī</s>, night-roamers,
were their leaders, like fires at the head of sacrificial rites.

children.text: mālyavantaṃ tu te sarve mālyavantam ivācalam
children.translated_text: All those night-roamers took refuge in <s>Mālyavān</s>, like the immovable mountain <s>Mālyavat</s>,
as embodied beings take refuge in the Creator.
That army of the rākṣasa lords, sounding like a mass of great clouds,
went to the world of the gods in desire for victory, standing under <s>Mālī</s>'s command.

children.text: rākṣasānāṃ samudyogaṃ taṃ tu nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: But lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, hearing from the messenger of the gods

children.text: devadūtād upaśrutya dadhre yuddhe tato manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: of that undertaking of the rākṣasas, then fixed his mind on battle.
Praised in song by gods, siddhas, seers, great serpents, chief gandharvas, and apsarases,
bearing the discus, sword, ploughshare, and other excellent weapons, he approached the army of the immortals' enemies.
Its flanks driven by the wind from <s>Suparṇa</s>'s wings, its banners whirling, its weapons scattered,

children.text: cacāla tad rākṣasarājasainyaṃ calopalo nīla ivācalendraḥ ||
children.translated_text: that army of the rākṣasa kings moved like a blue lord of mountains with loose boulders rolling.
Then, with sharp weapons stained by blood and flesh and having forms like the fire of the end of the age,

children.text: niśācarāḥ saṃparivārya mādhavaṃ varāyudhair nirbibhiduḥ sahasraśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the night-roamers surrounded <s>Mādhava</s> in the great battle and pierced him by the thousands with excellent weapons.
Roaring, those rākṣasa-clouds rained upon the mountain <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>
with a shower of arrows, as clouds rain upon a mountain with rain.
Dark and bright <s>Viṣṇu</s>, surrounded by those dark foremost night-roamers,
was like a collyrium mountain encircled by raining clouds.

children.text: śalabhā iva kedāraṃ maśakā iva parvatam
children.translated_text: As locusts enter a field, as mosquitoes enter a mountain,
as living beings enter a jar of nectar, and as makaras enter the ocean,
so arrows released from rākṣasa bows, swift as thunderbolt, wind, and thought,

children.text: hariṃ viśanti sma śarā lokāstam iva paryaye ||
children.translated_text: entered <s>Hari</s>, as worlds enter him at the dissolution.
Chariot-warriors on chariots, elephant-riders on the backs of elephants,
horsemen on fine horses, foot-soldiers, and those who moved in the sky,
the rākṣasa lords, mountain-like, with arrows, javelins, spears, and tomaras,

children.text: nirucchvāsaṃ hariṃ cakruḥ prāṇāyāma iva dvijam ||
children.translated_text: made <s>Hari</s> breathless, as breath-control makes a twice-born man still.
Being struck by the night-roamers like a great whale by fish,
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, drawing <s>Śārṅga</s>, in the great battle,
with arrows fully drawn and released, thunderbolt-faced and swift as thought,
cut the bodies of the rākṣasas into pieces, by hundreds and then by thousands.

children.text: vidrāvya śaravarṣaṃ taṃ varṣaṃ vāyur ivotthitam
children.translated_text: Having scattered that shower of arrows as the wind scatters rain that has risen up,
<s>Puruṣottama</s> blew the great conch <s>Pāñcajanya</s>.
That lotus-born king of conches, blown by <s>Hari</s> with all his breath,
roared with a terrible sound like a cloud at the end of the age.
Then that roar of the king of conches terrified the rākṣasas,
as the king of beasts terrifies rutting elephants in the forest.

children.text: na śekur aśvāḥ saṃsthātuṃ vimadāḥ kuñjarābhavan
children.translated_text: The horses could not stand firm, and the elephants lost their rut;
warriors fell from their chariots, weakened by the roar of the conch.
Arrows released from the bow <s>Śārṅga</s>, with points like thunderbolts,

children.text: vidārya tāni rakṣāṃsi supuṅkhā viviśuḥ kṣitim ||
children.translated_text: split those rākṣasas and, well-feathered, entered the earth.
Others too, being pierced by arrows fallen from <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>'s bow,

children.text: nipetū rākṣasā bhīmāḥ śailā vajrahatā iva ||
children.translated_text: terrible rākṣasas, fell like mountains struck by the thunderbolt.
From wounds produced by <s>Adhokṣaja</s>'s arrows, wounds made by the enemy's wound-makers,
they poured blood in streams, like mountains pouring streams of gold.
The roar of the king of conches, the twang of the bow <s>Śārṅga</s>,
and the cries of the rākṣasas too were swallowed by the sound of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: sūryād iva karā ghorā ūrmayaḥ sāgarād iva
children.translated_text: As terrible rays go forth from the sun, as waves from the ocean,

children.text: parvatād iva nāgendrā vāryoghā iva cāmbudāt ||
children.translated_text: as lordly elephants from a mountain, and as floods of water from a cloud,
so arrows released from <s>Śārṅga</s> and impelled by <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>
ran out swiftly, by hundreds and then by thousands.

children.text: śarabheṇa yathā siṃhāḥ siṃhena dviradā yathā
children.translated_text: As lions are overpowered by a śarabha, as elephants by a lion,

children.text: dviradena yathā vyāghrā vyāghreṇa dvīpino yathā ||
children.translated_text: as tigers by an elephant, and as leopards by a tiger,

children.text: dvīpinā ca yathā śvānaḥ śunā mārjārakā yathā
children.translated_text: as dogs by a leopard, as cats by a dog,

children.text: mārjāreṇa yathā sarpāḥ sarpeṇa ca yathākhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as snakes by a cat, and as mice by a snake,

children.text: tathā te rākṣasā yuddhe viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā
children.translated_text: so those rākṣasas in battle were overpowered by mighty <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
and they fled, were driven away, and were laid low on the ground.
Having slain thousands of rākṣasas, <s>Madhusūdana</s>
made the water-born conch resound, as the king of the gods makes a rain-cloud sound.
Struck by the arrows of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and utterly bewildered by the sound of the conch,

children.text: yayau laṅkām abhimukhaṃ prabhagnaṃ rākṣasaṃ balam ||
children.translated_text: the shattered rākṣasa army went toward <s>Laṅkā</s>.
When the rākṣasa army had been broken, struck by <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>'s arrows,
<s>Sumālī</s>, with a shower of arrows, hemmed in <s>Hari</s> in battle.

children.text: utkṣipya hemābharaṇaṃ karaṃ karam iva dvipaḥ
children.translated_text: Raising his hand adorned with gold ornaments, like an elephant raising its trunk,

children.text: rarāsa rākṣaso harṣāt sataḍit toyado yathā ||
children.translated_text: the rākṣasa roared in delight, like a rain cloud streaked with lightning.
As that <s>Sumālī</s> roared, <s>Hari</s> cut off the head of his charioteer, blazing with earrings,

children.text: cicheda yantur aśvāśca bhrāntāstasya tu rakṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the horses of that rākṣasa became bewildered.

children.text: tair aśvair bhrāmyate bhrāntaiḥ sumālī rākṣaseśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: With those bewildered horses, <s>Sumālī</s>, lord of rākṣasas, was whirled about,

children.text: indriyāśvair yathā bhrāntair dhṛtihīno yathā naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: like a man bereft of steadiness, driven astray by the horses of the senses.

children.text: mālī cābhyadravad yuddhe pragṛhya saśaraṃ dhanuḥ
children.translated_text: And <s>Mālī</s> rushed forward in battle, grasping a bow with its arrows.
The arrows loosed from <s>Mālī</s>'s bow, adorned with refined gold,

children.text: viviśur harim āsādya krauñcaṃ patrarathā iva ||
children.translated_text: entered <s>Hari</s> when they reached him, like birds entering Mount <s>Krauñca</s>.
Then, tormented by the thousands of arrows released by <s>Mālī</s>,

children.text: cukṣubhe na raṇe viṣṇur jitendriya ivādhibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> did not tremble in battle, like one who has mastered his senses amid afflictions.
Then the blessed lord, creator of beings, made the bowstring resound,
and, bearing sword and mace, released floods of arrows against <s>Mālī</s>.
Those arrows, brilliant like thunderbolts and lightning, reached <s>Mālī</s>'s body

children.text: pibanti rudhiraṃ tasya nāgā iva purāmṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and drank his blood, like serpents drinking the nectar of old.

children.text: mālinaṃ vimukhaṃ kṛtvā mālimauliṃ harir balāt
children.translated_text: Forcing <s>Mālī</s> to turn away, <s>Hari</s> struck down by force <s>Mālī</s>'s crest,

children.text: rathaṃ ca sadhvajaṃ cāpaṃ vājinaśca nyapātayat ||
children.translated_text: his chariot with its banner, his bow, and his horses.
Deprived of his chariot, <s>Mālī</s>, foremost of night-roamers, took up a mace;
mace in hand, he leapt up like a lion from a mountain peak.

children.text: sa tayā garuḍaṃ saṃkhye īśānam iva cāntakaḥ
children.translated_text: With it he struck <s>Garuḍa</s> in the battle, as <s>Antaka</s> might strike <s>Īśāna</s>,
on the region of the forehead, as <s>Indra</s> strikes a mountain with the thunderbolt.
Struck hard with the mace by that <s>Mālī</s>, <s>Garuḍa</s>,
distressed by pain, made the god turn away from the battle.

children.text: parāṅmukhe kṛte deve mālinā garuḍena vai
children.translated_text: When the god with <s>Garuḍa</s> had been turned away by <s>Mālī</s>,
a great shout arose from the rākṣasas as they roared aloud.
Hearing the clamor of the roaring rākṣasas, the younger brother of <s>Indra</s>,
though turned away, released the discus with the desire to kill <s>Mālī</s>.
That discus, shining like the disk of the sun and lighting the sky with its own radiance,
a discus like the wheel of Time, cut off <s>Mālī</s>'s head.
That fearsome head of the rākṣasa lord, severed by the discus,
fell gushing blood, like <s>Rāhu</s>'s head in ancient times.
Then from the gods, greatly delighted and stirred with all their life-breath,
there burst forth a lion-roar, as they cried, 'Well done, O god!'

children.text: mālinaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā sumālī mālyavān api
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Mālī</s> slain, <s>Sumālī</s> and <s>Mālyavān</s> too,
both with their forces, scorched by grief, fled toward <s>Laṅkā</s>.
But <s>Garuḍa</s>, recovered and turning back, great-minded,
angrily drove the rākṣasas away with the wind of his wings.
And <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, with excellent arrows like thunderbolts released from his bow, tore apart
the night-roamers, their hair loosened and shaken, as great <s>Indra</s>, accompanied by lightning, tears clouds apart with thunderbolts.
With parasols broken, weapons falling, bodies shattered and torn apart by arrows,

children.text: viniḥsṛtāntraṃ bhayalolanetraṃ balaṃ tad unmattanibhaṃ babhūva ||
children.translated_text: entrails spilling out and eyes rolling with fear, that army became like a mad thing.

children.text: siṃhārditānām iva kuñjarāṇāṃ niśācarāṇāṃ saha kuñjarāṇām
children.translated_text: The cries and rushes of the night-roamers, together with their elephants,

children.text: ravāśca vegāśca samaṃ babhūvuḥ purāṇasiṃhena vimarditānām ||
children.translated_text: became like those of elephants tormented by a lion, crushed by an ancient lion.
Covered over by the nets of <s>Hari</s>'s arrows, while releasing their own nets of arrows,
the night-roaming dark clouds ran like dark clouds driven on by the wind.
Their heads cut off by blows of the discus, their limbs crushed by blows of the mace,

children.text: asiprahārair bahudhā vibhaktāḥ patanti śailā iva rākṣasendrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and split in many ways by blows of the sword, the rākṣasa lords fell like mountains.
Their lotus-like faces were cut by the discus, their chests crushed by the mace,
their necks battered by the plough, and their heads split by pestles.
Some were cut down by the sword, and others likewise struck by arrows;
the rākṣasas fell swiftly from the sky into the waters of the ocean.
Then the sky, filled without gap by night-roamers like dark clouds, their necklaces and earrings slipping away,

children.text: nipātyamānair dadṛśe nirantaraṃ nipātyamānair iva nīlaparvataiḥ ||
children.translated_text: as they were being struck down, looked as though blue mountains were being cast down.
As that army was being struck from behind by lotus-naveled <s>Padmanābha</s>,
<s>Mālyavān</s> then turned back, like the ocean passing beyond its shore.
His eyes reddened, his crown shaking with anger, the night-roamer

children.text: padmanābham idaṃ prāha vacanaṃ paruṣaṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: then spoke these harsh words to <s>Padmanābha</s>:
'<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, you do not know the eternal <s>kṣatradharma</s> (warrior code),
since you kill us, broken and not intent on fighting, like any ordinary man.
O lord of the gods, he who commits the sin of killing those who have turned away

children.text: sa hantā na gataḥ svargaṃ labhate puṇyakarmaṇām ||
children.translated_text: does not obtain the heaven of men of meritorious deeds as his killer's reward.
Or, if you have eagerness for battle, O bearer of conch, discus, and mace,

children.text: ahaṃ sthito 'smi paśyāmi balaṃ darśaya yat tava ||
children.translated_text: I am standing here and watching; show the strength that is yours.'
The mighty younger brother of the king of the gods spoke to that lord of rākṣasas:
'I have given freedom from fear to the gods, who were terrified by fear of you,
in the form of the destruction of the rākṣasas, and that promise is now being upheld.

children.text: prāṇair api priyaṃ kāryaṃ devānāṃ hi sadā mayā
children.translated_text: Even with my life, I must always do what is dear to the gods;
therefore I shall kill you, even if you have gone down to <s>Rasātala</s>.'
But as the god, whose eyes were red lotuses, was speaking thus,

children.text: śaktyā bibheda saṃkruddho rākṣasendro rarāsa ca ||
children.translated_text: The enraged lord of the rākṣasas pierced him with a spear and roared.
The spear released from <s>Mālyavān</s>'s arm, making a sound like a bell,
shone on <s>Hari</s>'s chest like lightning in a cloud.
Then lotus-eyed <s>Hari</s>, beloved of the spear-bearing god, pulled out that very spear,
and hurled it, aiming at <s>Mālyavān</s>.
That spear, going forth from <s>Govinda</s>'s hand as if released by <s>Skanda</s>,
went toward the rākṣasa eagerly, like a great meteor toward a mountain of collyrium.
It fell on the broad chest of that lord of rākṣasas,
brightened by the gleam of his necklace, like a thunderbolt on a mountain peak.
His armor split by it, <s>Mālyavān</s> entered a great darkness;
then, recovering again, he stood firm like an unmoving mountain.
Then, taking up a black-iron spear covered with many spikes,
he struck the god hard between the breasts.
Still blood-maddened in battle, the night-roamer struck the younger brother of <s>Vāsava</s> with his fist,
and then withdrew by the length of a bow.

children.text: tato 'mbare mahāñ śabdaḥ sādhu sādhviti cotthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then a great cry arose in the sky, saying, "Well done, well done!"
After striking <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the rākṣasa struck <s>Garuḍa</s> as well.
Then <s>Vainateya</s>, enraged, with the wind from his wings
drove away the rākṣasa, as a powerful wind drives a heap of dry leaves.
Seeing his elder brother driven off by the wing-wind of the king of birds,

children.text: sumālī svabalaiḥ sārdhaṃ laṅkām abhimukho yayau ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sumālī</s>, together with his forces, went toward <s>Laṅkā</s>.
The rākṣasa <s>Mālyavān</s> too, blown away by the force of the wing-wind,

children.text: svabalena samāgamya yayau laṅkāṃ hriyā vṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: rejoined his own army and went to <s>Laṅkā</s>, covered with shame.

children.text: evaṃ te rākṣasā rāma hariṇā kamalekṣaṇa
children.translated_text: Thus, O lotus-eyed <s>Rāma</s>, those rākṣasas
were broken many times in battle by <s>Hari</s>, their foremost leaders slain.
Unable to fight against <s>Viṣṇu</s> and tormented by fear,

children.text: tyaktvā laṅkāṃ gatā vastuṃ pātālaṃ sahapatnayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: they abandoned <s>Laṅkā</s> and went to dwell in <s>Pātāla</s> with their wives.
Having reached the rākṣasa <s>Sumālī</s>, O delight of the <s>Raghu</s> line,
those famed heroes remained in the line of <s>Sālakaṭaṃkaṭa</s>.

children.text: ye tvayā nihatāste vai paulastyā nāma rākṣasāḥ
children.translated_text: Those whom you slew were indeed the rākṣasas called <s>Paulastyas</s>:

children.text: sumālī mālyavānmālī ye ca teṣāṃ puraḥsarāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sumālī</s>, <s>Mālyavān</s>, <s>Mālī</s>, and those who were their leaders before them.
All these, O greatly fortunate one, were stronger than <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: na cānyo rakṣasāṃ hantā sureṣvapi puraṃjaya
children.translated_text: And there was no other slayer of the rākṣasas even among the gods, O conqueror of cities,
apart from the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, bearer of conch, discus, and mace.
You are the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, four-armed and eternal,
born to slay the rākṣasas, unconquerable, sovereign, and imperishable.

children.text: kasyacit tvatha kālasya sumālī nāma rākṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after some time, a rākṣasa named <s>Sumālī</s>
wandered over the whole mortal world from <s>Rasātala</s>.
He was like a dark rain-cloud, with earrings of heated gold,

children.text: kanyāṃ duhitaraṃ gṛhya vinā padmam iva śriyam
children.translated_text: and he took with him his maiden daughter, like <s>Śrī</s> without her lotus.
Then he saw the lord of wealth going in the <s>Puṣpaka</s>.
Seeing him going along, like an immortal and like blazing fire,

children.text: athābravīt sutāṃ rakṣaḥ kaikasīṃ nāma nāmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the rākṣasa then spoke to his daughter, named <s>Kaikasī</s> by name:
"Daughter, this is the time for giving you away; your youth is passing by.

children.text: tvatkṛte ca vayaṃ sarve yantritā dharmabuddhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And because of you, all of us, though mindful of dharma, are constrained.

children.text: tvaṃ hi sarvaguṇopetā śrīḥ sapadmeva putrike
children.translated_text: For you are endowed with every virtue, little daughter, like <s>Śrī</s> together with her lotus.
Yet suitors, afraid of being rejected, do not accept you.
Fatherhood of a daughter is painful for all who desire honor,

children.text: na jñāyate ca kaḥ kanyāṃ varayed iti putrike ||
children.translated_text: for it is not known who will choose the maiden, little daughter.

children.text: mātuḥ kulaṃ pitṛkulaṃ yatra caiva pradīyate
children.translated_text: The mother's family, the father's family, and the family to which she is given:

children.text: kulatrayaṃ sadā kanyā saṃśaye sthāpya tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: a maiden always keeps these three families in uncertainty.
Therefore go, daughter, to <s>Viśravas</s>, best of excellent sages,

children.text: gaccha viśravasaṃ putri paulastyaṃ varaya svayam ||
children.translated_text: born in the line of <s>Prajāpati</s>, a <s>Paulastya</s>, and choose him yourself.

children.text: īdṛśāste bhaviṣyanti putrāḥ putri na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Such sons will be yours, daughter, without doubt,
equal in splendor to the sun, like this lord of wealth."
In the meantime, O <s>Rāma</s>, the twice-born son of <s>Pulastya</s>
was attending to the agnihotra, like a fourth fire.

children.text: sā tu tāṃ dāruṇāṃ velām acintya pitṛgauravāt
children.translated_text: But she, not considering that terrible hour, out of regard for her father's authority,
approached and stood before him, her face lowered toward his feet.

children.text: sa tu tāṃ vīkṣya suśroṇīṃ pūrṇacandranibhānanām
children.translated_text: Seeing her, with beautiful hips and a face like the full moon,
that most noble sage, blazing as it were with energy, said:

children.text: bhadre kasyāsi duhitā kuto vā tvam ihāgatā
children.translated_text: "Good lady, whose daughter are you, and from where have you come here?

children.text: kiṃ kāryaṃ kasya vā hetostattvato brūhi śobhane ||
children.translated_text: What is your business, and for what reason? Tell me truly, beautiful one."

children.text: evam uktā tu sā kanyā kṛtāñjalir athābravīt
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, the maiden then spoke with joined palms:

children.text: ātmaprabhāvena mune jñātum arhasi me matam ||
children.translated_text: "By your own power, O sage, you should know my intention.

children.text: kiṃ tu viddhi hi māṃ brahmañśāsanāt pitur āgatām
children.translated_text: But know me, O brahman, to have come at my father's command.

children.text: kaikasī nāma nāmnāhaṃ śeṣaṃ tvaṃ jñātum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: By name I am called <s>Kaikasī</s>; the rest you should know."

children.text: sa tu gatvā munir dhyānaṃ vākyam etad uvāca ha
children.translated_text: Then the sage entered meditation and spoke these words:

children.text: vijñātaṃ te mayā bhadre kāraṇaṃ yanmanogatam ||
children.translated_text: "I have understood, good lady, the cause that lay in your mind.

children.text: dāruṇāyāṃ tu velāyāṃ yasmāt tvaṃ mām upasthitā
children.translated_text: Since you have approached me at a terrible hour,
therefore hear, good lady, what kind of sons you will bear.
Terrible, terrible in form, and fond of terrible lineage,
you will give birth, beautiful-hipped one, to rākṣasas of cruel deeds."

children.text: sā tu tadvacanaṃ śrutvā praṇipatyābravīd vacaḥ
children.translated_text: But she, hearing that statement, bowed down and spoke these words:
"Lord, such sons are not fitting from you, whose source is <s>Brahmā</s>."
Then the sage said there, "The youngest son of yours
will be suited to my lineage and will be righteous."

children.text: evam uktā tu sā kanyā rāma kālena kenacit
children.translated_text: When she had been thus addressed, that maiden, O <s>Rāma</s>, after some time
gave birth to a hideous being of rākṣasa form, exceedingly terrible.
He had ten heads and great fangs, and was like a mass of blue-black collyrium;
his lips were coppery, he had twenty arms, a huge mouth, and blazing hair.
Then, as soon as he was born, jackals with flames in their mouths
and flesh-eaters made counterclockwise circles.
The sky rained blood, and the clouds had a harsh roar;

children.text: prababhau na ca khe sūryo maholkāścāpatan bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: the sun did not shine in the sky, and great meteors fell to the earth.
Then his father, equal to the Grandsire, gave him a name:
"Since this one has been born with ten heads, he will be <s>Daśagrīva</s>."
After him was born <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, mighty in strength;

children.text: pramāṇād yasya vipulaṃ pramāṇaṃ neha vidyate ||
children.translated_text: no measure exists here by which the vastness of his size could be measured.
Then one named <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>, with a deformed face, was born,
and righteous-souled <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> was the youngest son of <s>Kaikasī</s>.

children.text: te tu tatra mahāraṇye vavṛdhuḥ sumahaujasaḥ
children.translated_text: They grew there in the great forest, very powerful;
among them cruel <s>Daśagrīva</s> became a cause of terror to the worlds.
Reckless <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, wickedly devouring great seers devoted to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),

children.text: trailokyaṃ trāsayan duṣṭo bhakṣayan vicacāra ha ||
children.translated_text: wandered about terrifying the three worlds.
But righteous-souled <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, always established on the path of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),
lived with his senses restrained, observant of sacred recitation and a regulated diet.
Then, after some time, the god who was lord of wealth
came in the <s>Puṣpaka</s> to see his greatly powerful father.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā kaikasī tatra jvalantam iva tejasā
children.translated_text: Seeing him there, blazing as if with splendor,

children.text: āsthāya rākṣasīṃ buddhiṃ daśagrīvam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kaikasī</s>, adopting a rākṣasī intention, spoke to <s>Daśagrīva</s>:

children.text: putra vaiśravaṇaṃ paśya bhrātaraṃ tejasā vṛtam
children.translated_text: "Son, behold <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, your brother, surrounded by splendor;

children.text: bhrātṛbhāve same cāpi paśyātmānaṃ tvam īdṛśam ||
children.translated_text: though the state of brotherhood is the same, look at yourself, such as you are.
O <s>Daśagrīva</s>, of immeasurable valor, make such an effort

children.text: yathā bhavasi me putra śīghraṃ vaiśravaṇopamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that you, my son, may quickly become like <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>."
Hearing that speech of his mother, mighty <s>Daśagrīva</s>

children.text: amarṣam atulaṃ lebhe pratijñāṃ cākarot tadā ||
children.translated_text: felt incomparable resentment and then made a vow:

children.text: satyaṃ te pratijānāmi tulyo bhrātrādhiko 'pi vā
children.translated_text: "I truly promise you: I shall soon be equal to my brother, or even superior,
Mother; abandon the grief lodged in your heart."
Then through that very anger, <s>Daśagrīva</s>, together with his younger brothers,

children.text: prāpsyāmi tapasā kāmam iti kṛtvādhyavasya ca
children.translated_text: formed the resolve, "I shall attain my desire through austerity,"
and came to the holy hermitage of <s>Gokarṇa</s> for the attainment of his aim.

children.text: athābravīd dvijaṃ rāmaḥ kathaṃ te bhrātaro vane
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s> said to the twice-born sage, "How, in the forest, did those brothers,
those great-vowed men, practice austerity then, O brahmin sage?"
<s>Agastya</s> then spoke to <s>Rāma</s>, whose mind was attentive:
"Those brothers there entered upon various prescribed rules of <s>dharma</s> (sacred discipline).
Then <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, exerting himself and always devoted to <s>dharma</s> (sacred discipline),
performed austerity in the hot season, standing amid the five fires.
In the rainy season, drenched by cloud-water, he practiced the heroic posture,
and always in the cold season he took refuge in the midst of water.
Thus ten thousand years passed for him,
as he strove in <s>dharma</s> (religious discipline) and remained fixed on the good path.
But righteous-souled <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, always devoted to <s>dharma</s> and pure,
stood on one foot for five thousand years.
When his observance was completed, hosts of apsarases danced,
a shower of flowers fell, and the deities too were stirred.
For five thousand years he also followed the sun,
and stood with head and arms raised, his mind held firm by sacred recitation.
Thus for self-restrained <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> also
ten thousand years passed, as if he were dwelling in <s>Nandana</s> in heaven.
But <s>Daśānana</s> remained without food for ten thousand years;

children.text: pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu śiraścāgnau juhāva saḥ ||
children.translated_text: at the completion of each thousand years he offered a head into the fire.
Thus nine thousand years passed for him,
and nine of his heads had entered the sacrificial fire.

children.text: atha varṣasahasre tu daśame daśamaṃ śiraḥ
children.translated_text: Then, in the tenth thousand years, when he wished to cut off the tenth head,
the righteous-souled Grandsire arrived there.
The Grandsire, greatly pleased, appeared together with the gods
and addressed him: "Child, child, <s>Daśagrīva</s>, I am pleased.
Quickly choose a boon, knower of <s>dharma</s>, the boon that you desire;

children.text: kiṃ te kāmaṃ karomyadya na vṛthā te pariśramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: what wish of yours shall I grant today? Your toil shall not be fruitless."
Then <s>Daśagrīva</s>, delighted in his inner self,
bowed his head to the god and, with a voice faltering from joy, said:

children.text: bhagavan prāṇināṃ nityaṃ nānyatra maraṇād bhayam
children.translated_text: "Lord, for living beings there is always no fear apart from death;

children.text: nāsti mṛtyusamaḥ śatrur amaratvam ato vṛṇe ||
children.translated_text: there is no enemy equal to death; therefore I choose immortality.
Against <s>Suparṇa</s>, nāgas, yakṣas, daityas, dānavas, and rākṣasas,

children.text: avadhyaḥ syāṃ prajādhyakṣa devatānāṃ ca śāśvatam ||
children.translated_text: and against the gods forever, O lord of creatures, may I be invulnerable.
I have no concern about other living beings, O you honored by the immortals;

children.text: tṛṇabhūtā hi me sarve prāṇino mānuṣādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for all creatures, humans and the rest, are like blades of grass to me."
Thus addressed by the rākṣasa <s>Daśagrīva</s>, the righteous-souled

children.text: uvāca vacanaṃ rāma saha devaiḥ pitāmahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Grandsire, together with the gods, spoke these words, O <s>Rāma</s>:
"So indeed shall this be for you, foremost of rākṣasas;

children.text: śṛṇu cāpi vaco bhūyaḥ prītasyeha śubhaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: and now hear further this auspicious word of mine, for I am pleased.

children.text: hutāni yāni śīrṣāṇi pūrvam agnau tvayānagha
children.translated_text: The heads that previously were offered by you into the fire, faultless one,
those too shall again become yours in just the same way, O rākṣasa."
Thus, as the grandfather had said, of the rākṣasa <s>Daśagrīva</s>

children.text: agnau hutāni śīrṣāṇi yāni tānyutthitāni vai ||
children.translated_text: the heads that had been offered into the fire indeed arose again.

children.text: evam uktvā tu taṃ rāma daśagrīvaṃ prajāpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to that <s>Daśagrīva</s>, O <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>
then the grandfather of the worlds spoke this word to <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>.
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, my child, by you, whose mind is joined with <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),
I am pleased, O knower of <s>dharma</s>; choose a boon, O one of good vows.
Then righteous <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> spoke the words with joined palms,

children.text: vṛtaḥ sarvaguṇair nityaṃ candramā iva raśmibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: ever endowed with all virtues, like the moon with its rays.
Lord, I am one whose purpose is fulfilled, since the teacher of the world himself

children.text: prīto yadi tvaṃ dātavyaṃ varaṃ me śṛṇu suvrata ||
children.translated_text: is pleased. If you would grant me a boon, hear it from me, O one of good vows.

children.text: yā yā me jāyate buddhir yeṣu yeṣvāśrameṣviha
children.translated_text: Whatever understanding arises in me, in whatever states of life here,

children.text: sā sā bhavatu dharmiṣṭhā taṃ taṃ dharmaṃ ca pālaye ||
children.translated_text: may each of those be most righteous, and may I preserve that <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: eṣa me paramodāra varaḥ paramako mataḥ
children.translated_text: This is my supremely noble boon, considered the highest one,

children.text: na hi dharmābhiraktānāṃ loke kiṃcana durlabham ||
children.translated_text: for nothing in the world is difficult for those devoted to <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: atha prajāpatiḥ prīto vibhīṣaṇam uvāca ha
children.translated_text: Then <s>Prajāpati</s>, being pleased, said to <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>:

children.text: dharmiṣṭhastvaṃ yathā vatsa tathā caitad bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: As you are most righteous, my child, so indeed this shall be.
Since, though born in a rākṣasa womb, O subduer of foes,

children.text: nādharme jāyate buddhir amaratvaṃ dadāmi te ||
children.translated_text: your mind does not arise in unrighteousness, I grant you immortality.
But as he was granting a boon to <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, O subduer of enemies,
all the gods, with joined palms, spoke these words to <s>Prajāpati</s>.
A boon must not yet be granted by you to <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>,
for you know how this wicked-minded one terrifies the worlds.
In <s>Nandana</s>, seven apsarases and ten attendants of great <s>Indra</s>
have been eaten by him, O <s>Brahmā</s>, and likewise seers and human beings.
Under the pretext of a boon, let delusion be given to him, O immeasurably radiant one,

children.text: lokānāṃ svasti caiva syād bhaved asya ca saṃnatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and there would be welfare for the worlds, and he would be brought low.
Thus addressed by the gods, <s>Brahmā</s>, the lotus-born, reflected,
and, as he thought, the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> stood near at his side.

children.text: prāñjaliḥ sā tu pārśvasthā prāha vākyaṃ sarasvatī
children.translated_text: Standing beside him with joined palms, <s>Sarasvatī</s> spoke this word:

children.text: iyam asmyāgatā deva kiṃ kāryaṃ karavāṇyaham ||
children.translated_text: I have come here, O god; what work shall I do?

children.text: prajāpatistu tāṃ prāptāṃ prāha vākyaṃ sarasvatīm
children.translated_text: Then <s>Prajāpati</s> spoke this word to <s>Sarasvatī</s>, who had come:

children.text: vāṇi tvaṃ rākṣasendrasya bhava yā devatepsitā ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Vāṇī</s>, become the speech of the lord of the rākṣasas, as the gods desire.
Saying, "So be it," she entered him; then <s>Prajāpati</s> said:

children.text: kumbhakarṇa mahābāho varaṃ varaya yo mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, mighty-armed one, choose the boon that you desire.

children.text: kumbhakarṇastu tad vākyaṃ śrutvā vacanam abravīt
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, hearing that statement, uttered these words:
To sleep for many years, O god of gods, is what I desire.

children.text: evam astviti taṃ coktvā saha devaiḥ pitāmahaḥ
children.translated_text: Saying to him, "So be it," the grandfather, together with the gods,

children.text: devī sarasvatī caiva muktvā taṃ prayayau divam ||
children.translated_text: and the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>, after releasing him, went to heaven.
But evil-minded <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, distressed, thought:

children.text: kīdṛśaṃ kiṃ nvidaṃ vākyaṃ mamādya vadanāccyutam ||
children.translated_text: What sort of word, what indeed, has fallen today from my mouth?
All the brothers, having obtained boons and blazing with splendor,

children.text: śleṣmātakavanaṃ gatvā tatra te nyavasan sukham ||
children.translated_text: went to the <s>Śleṣmātaka</s> forest and dwelt there happily.

children.text: sumālī varalabdhāṃstu jñātvā tān vai niśācarān
children.translated_text: <s>Sumālī</s>, learning that those night-roamers had obtained boons,

children.text: udatiṣṭhad bhayaṃ tyaktvā sānugaḥ sa rasātalāt ||
children.translated_text: rose up with his followers from <s>Rasātala</s>, casting off fear.
<s>Mārīca</s>, <s>Prahasta</s>, <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, and <s>Mahodara</s>
the ministers of that rākṣasa, rose up in great excitement.

children.text: sumālī caiva taiḥ sarvair vṛto rākṣasapuṃgavaiḥ
children.translated_text: And <s>Sumālī</s>, surrounded by all those foremost rākṣasas,
approached <s>Daśagrīva</s>, embraced him, and said this:
By good fortune, son, this wish you had contemplated has been achieved,
that you have obtained such a boon from the foremost being in the three worlds.

children.text: yatkṛte ca vayaṃ laṅkāṃ tyaktvā yātā rasātalam
children.translated_text: For the sake of which we abandoned <s>Laṅkā</s> and went to <s>Rasātala</s>,

children.text: tad gataṃ no mahābāho mahad viṣṇukṛtaṃ bhayam ||
children.translated_text: that great fear of ours caused by <s>Viṣṇu</s> has gone, mighty-armed one.

children.text: asakṛt tena bhagnā hi parityajya svam ālayam
children.translated_text: For we were repeatedly broken by him and, abandoning our own abode,

children.text: vidrutāḥ sahitāḥ sarve praviṣṭāḥ sma rasātalam ||
children.translated_text: all fled together and entered <s>Rasātala</s>.
And this city <s>Laṅkā</s>, ours and inhabited by rākṣasas,
has been settled by your brother, the wise lord of wealth.

children.text: yadi nāmātra śakyaṃ syāt sāmnā dānena vānagha
children.translated_text: If it should be possible here by conciliation or by gifts, O sinless one,

children.text: tarasā vā mahābāho pratyānetuṃ kṛtaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: or by force, mighty-armed one, it ought to be brought back.

children.text: tvaṃ ca laṅkeśvarastāta bhaviṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: And you, dear one, will be lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>; there is no doubt,
and you will be the master of us all, mighty one.
Then <s>Daśagrīva</s> said to his maternal grandfather who stood nearby:
The lord of wealth is our elder; you ought not speak thus.
When <s>Daśagrīva</s> had spoken these words thus, the night-roamer

children.text: prahastaḥ praśritaṃ vākyam idam āha sakāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prahasta</s> spoke this respectful and reasoned word.
<s>Daśagrīva</s>, mighty-armed one, you should not speak like this.

children.text: saubhrātraṃ nāsti śūrāṇāṃ śṛṇu cedaṃ vaco mama ||
children.translated_text: Brotherhood does not exist among heroes; listen to this word of mine.
<s>Aditi</s> and <s>Diti</s> were indeed two sisters together,
the wives of <s>Prajāpati</s> <s>Kaśyapa</s>, of surpassing beauty.
<s>Aditi</s> gave birth to the gods, lords of the three worlds,
while <s>Diti</s> gave birth to the daityas, <s>Kaśyapa</s>'s own offspring.
Indeed, O knower of <s>dharma</s>, in the past this earth, together with forests and oceans,
with its mountains, belonged to the daityas, O hero; they were the powerful ones.
But after mighty <s>Viṣṇu</s> slew them in battle,

children.text: devānāṃ vaśam ānītaṃ trailokyam idam avyayam ||
children.translated_text: this imperishable triple world was brought under the power of the gods.

children.text: naitad eko bhavān eva kariṣyati viparyayam
children.translated_text: You alone will not be the only one to make such a reversal;

children.text: surair ācaritaṃ pūrvaṃ kuruṣvaitad vaco mama ||
children.translated_text: do what was formerly practiced by the gods; heed this word of mine.
Thus addressed by the evil-minded <s>Daśagrīva</s> by <s>Prahasta</s>,

children.text: cintayitvā muhūrtaṃ vai bāḍham ityeva so 'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: he thought for a moment and then said, "Very well."

children.text: sa tu tenaiva harṣeṇa tasminn ahani vīryavān
children.translated_text: Then, in that very joy, on that day the mighty <s>Daśagrīva</s>

children.text: vanaṃ gato daśagrīvaḥ saha taiḥ kṣaṇadācaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: went to the forest together with those night-roamers.

children.text: trikūṭasthaḥ sa tu tadā daśagrīvo niśācaraḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Daśagrīva</s>, the night-roaming rākṣasa, stationed on <s>Trikūṭa</s>,
sent <s>Prahasta</s>, skilled in speech, as an envoy.

children.text: prahasta śīghraṃ gatvā tvaṃ brūhi nairṛtapuṃgavam
children.translated_text: "<s>Prahasta</s>, go quickly and speak to the foremost of the nairṛtas;
by my word, speak this conciliatory speech to the lord of wealth:

children.text: iyaṃ laṅkā purī rājan rākṣasānāṃ mahātmanām
children.translated_text: 'This city <s>Laṅkā</s>, O king, belongs to the great-souled rākṣasas.

children.text: tvayā niveśitā saumya naitad yuktaṃ tavānagha ||
children.translated_text: It has been settled by you, gentle one; this is not proper for you, sinless one.

children.text: tad bhavān yadi sāmnaitāṃ dadyād atulavikrama
children.translated_text: Therefore, if your honor, of incomparable valor, would give it by conciliation,
my pleasure would be accomplished, and <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) would also be upheld.'"

children.text: ityuktaḥ sa tadā gatvā prahasto vākyakovidaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus instructed, <s>Prahasta</s>, skilled in speech, went then
and reported all of <s>Daśagrīva</s>'s words to the lord of wealth.

children.text: prahastād api saṃśrutya devo vaiśravaṇo vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard the speech from <s>Prahasta</s>, the god <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>,
expert in speech, replied to that <s>Prahasta</s> with these words:

children.text: brūhi gaccha daśagrīvaṃ purī rājyaṃ ca yanmama
children.translated_text: "Go and tell <s>Daśagrīva</s>: 'The city and kingdom that are mine
are yours too, mighty-armed one. Enjoy this realm whose thorns are destroyed.

children.text: sarvaṃ kartāsmi bhadraṃ te rākṣaseśa vaco 'cirāt
children.translated_text: I shall soon do all your bidding, lord of rākṣasas; good fortune to you.

children.text: kiṃ tu tāvat pratīkṣasva pitur yāvannivedaye ||
children.translated_text: But wait just until I inform my father.'"

children.text: evam uktvā dhanādhyakṣo jagāma pitur antikam
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the lord of wealth went to his father's presence;
he bowed to his teacher and told him what <s>Rāvaṇa</s> desired.
"Father, this <s>Daśagrīva</s> has sent a messenger to me:
'Let the city <s>Laṅkā</s>, formerly inhabited by hosts of rākṣasas, be given.'
Tell me, virtuous one, what I should do in this matter."
When he had been addressed in this way, the brahmarṣi <s>Viśravas</s>, best of sages,

children.text: uvāca dhanadaṃ vākyaṃ śṛṇu putra vaco mama ||
children.translated_text: spoke these words to the giver of wealth: "Listen, my son, to my word.
Mighty-armed <s>Daśagrīva</s> spoke in this way in my presence also;
he was reproached by me, and that very wicked-minded one was admonished in many ways.

children.text: sa krodhena mayā cokto dhvaṃsasveti punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: In anger I repeatedly said to him, 'Fall away!'

children.text: śreyo'bhiyuktaṃ dharmyaṃ ca śṛṇu putra vaco mama ||
children.translated_text: Now hear, my son, my word, directed to your welfare and in accord with <s>dharma</s>.
Bewildered by the granting of boons, that wicked-minded one does not know

children.text: na vetti mama śāpācca prakṛtiṃ dāruṇāṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: what is worthy and unworthy, and because of my curse he has come to a dreadful nature.
Therefore go, mighty-armed one, to <s>Kailāsa</s>, the mountain-holder;
settle there for your residence, and abandon <s>Laṅkā</s> together with your followers.

children.text: tatra mandākinī ramyā nadīnāṃ pravarā nadī
children.translated_text: There is charming <s>Mandākinī</s>, the foremost river among rivers,
its waters covered with golden lotuses shining like the sun.

children.text: na hi kṣamaṃ tvayā tena vairaṃ dhanada rakṣasā
children.translated_text: For you, O giver of wealth, enmity with that rākṣasa is not suitable,

children.text: jānīṣe hi yathānena labdhaḥ paramako varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for you know what supreme boon he has obtained."

children.text: evam ukto gṛhītvā tu tad vacaḥ pitṛgauravāt
children.translated_text: Thus instructed, accepting that word out of respect for his father,
he departed with wife, townsmen, ministers, vehicles, and wealth.
But <s>Prahasta</s> went to <s>Daśagrīva</s> and reported everything:

children.text: śūnyā sā nagarī laṅkā triṃśadyojanam āyatā
children.translated_text: "That city <s>Laṅkā</s>, thirty yojanas in extent, is empty.

children.text: praviśya tāṃ sahāsmābhiḥ svadharmaṃ tatra pālaya ||
children.translated_text: Enter it with us and uphold your own rule there."
Thus addressed by <s>Prahasta</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the rākṣasa, then
entered the city <s>Laṅkā</s> with his brothers and his strong following.

children.text: sa cābhiṣiktaḥ kṣaṇadācaraistadā niveśayāmāsa purīṃ daśānanaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, consecrated by the night-roamers, the ten-faced one settled the city;

children.text: nikāmapūrṇā ca babhūva sā purī niśācarair nīlabalāhakopamaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and that city became filled to desire with night-roamers resembling dark clouds.
Then the lord of wealth, out of respect for his father's command, established
on the moon-bright mountain a city adorned with well-decorated excellent mansions, like <s>Amarāvatī</s> of <s>Purandara</s>.
The lord of rākṣasas, having been consecrated, together with his brothers then
next considered the giving away of his rākṣasī sister.
He gave that rākṣasī, his sister named <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>,
to <s>Vidyujjihva</s> by name, a lord of dānavas, a <s>Kālakeya</s>.

children.text: atha dattvā svasāraṃ sa mṛgayāṃ paryaṭannṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after giving away his sister, that king wandered about hunting.

children.text: tatrāpaśyat tato rāma mayaṃ nāma diteḥ sutam ||
children.translated_text: There then, O <s>Rāma</s>, he saw a son of <s>Diti</s> named <s>Maya</s>.
Seeing him accompanied by a maiden, <s>Daśagrīva</s>, the night-roamer,

children.text: apṛcchat ko bhavān eko nirmanuṣyamṛge vane ||
children.translated_text: asked, "Who are you, alone in this forest empty of men and beasts?"
Then <s>Maya</s>, O <s>Rāma</s>, spoke to that questioning night-roamer:

children.text: śrūyatāṃ sarvam ākhyāsye yathāvṛttam idaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: "Listen; I shall tell you everything, just as this matter happened to me.
There is an apsaras named <s>Hemā</s>, dear sir, if you have heard of her before.

children.text: daivatair mama sā dattā paulomīva śatakratoḥ ||
children.translated_text: She was given to me by the gods, as <s>Paulomī</s> was given to <s>Śatakratu</s>.
With my mind attached to her, dear sir, I spent five hundred years;

children.text: sā ca daivatakāryeṇa gatā varṣaṃ caturdaśam ||
children.translated_text: and she, on account of a divine duty, went away for the fourteenth year.

children.text: tasyāḥ kṛte ca hemāyāḥ sarvaṃ hemapuraṃ mayā
children.translated_text: For the sake of that <s>Hemā</s>, the whole golden city was made by me then,
variegated with diamond and vaidūrya, through my magic power.
There, deprived of her and greatly sorrowing, I found no delight;

children.text: tasmāt purād duhitaraṃ gṛhītvā vanam āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore I came from that city to the forest, taking my daughter with me.
This is my own daughter, O king, grown in her womb.

children.text: bhartāram anayā sārdham asyāḥ prāpto 'smi mārgitum ||
children.translated_text: Together with her I have come to seek a husband for her.
For men who desire honor, the state of being a maiden's father is painful;

children.text: kanyā hi dve kule nityaṃ saṃśaye sthāpya tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: for a maiden always stands placing two families in uncertainty.

children.text: dvau sutau tu mama tvasyāṃ bhāryāyāṃ saṃbabhūvatuḥ
children.translated_text: And two sons were born to me from that wife:
<s>Māyāvī</s> first, dear sir, and <s>Dundubhi</s> after him."

children.text: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yāthātathyena pṛcchataḥ
children.translated_text: All this has been related to you truthfully, since you asked.

children.text: tvām idānīṃ kathaṃ tāta jānīyāṃ ko bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: Now, dear one, how may I know you, and who you are?

children.text: evam ukto rākṣasendro vinītam idam abravīt
children.translated_text: When he had been addressed in this way, the lord of rākṣasas spoke these humble words:
I am the son of <s>Pulastya</s>, and by name I am <s>Daśagrīva</s>.

children.text: brahmarṣestaṃ sutaṃ jñātvā mayo harṣam upāgataḥ
children.translated_text: Knowing him to be the son of a brahmarṣi, <s>Maya</s> became delighted,

children.text: dātuṃ duhitaraṃ tasya rocayāmāsa tatra vai ||
children.translated_text: and there he chose to give his daughter to him.

children.text: prahasan prāha daityendro rākṣasendram idaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Laughing, the lord of daityas spoke these words to the lord of rākṣasas:
This is my own daughter, O king, borne by the apsaras <s>Hemā</s>.
She is a maiden named <s>Mandodarī</s>; accept her for the purpose of being your wife.
<s>Daśagrīva</s>, O <s>Rāma</s>, answered him simply, 'So be it,'
and, after kindling the sacred fire there, he performed the taking of her hand.

children.text: na hi tasya mayo rāma śāpābhijñastapodhanāt
children.translated_text: For <s>Maya</s>, O <s>Rāma</s>, did not know of the curse upon him from the rich-in-austerity sage;

children.text: viditvā tena sā dattā tasya paitāmahaṃ kulam ||
children.translated_text: knowing his ancestral family, he gave her to him.

children.text: amoghāṃ tasya śaktiṃ ca pradadau paramādbhutām
children.translated_text: He also gave him that unfailing spear, most wondrous,
obtained through supreme austerity, with which he struck <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ sa kṛtadāro vai laṅkāyām īśvaraḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, having taken a wife, the powerful lord and ruler of <s>Laṅkā</s>

children.text: gatvā tu nagaraṃ bhārye bhrātṛbhyāṃ samudāvahat ||
children.translated_text: went to the city and brought wives for his two brothers.
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> brought <s>Vajrajvālā</s>, so named, the daughter's daughter of <s>Virocana</s>,
as the wife of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>.
The righteous <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> obtained as his wife <s>Saramā</s>,

children.text: saramā nāma dharmajño lebhe bhāryāṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the daughter of the great-souled <s>Śailūṣa</s>, king of the gandharvas.

children.text: tīre tu sarasaḥ sā vai saṃjajñe mānasasya ca
children.translated_text: She was born on the shore of the lake <s>Mānasa</s>,
and the lake <s>Mānasa</s>, dear one, swelled when the rains came.

children.text: mātrā tu tasyāḥ kanyāyāḥ snehanākranditaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the mother of that maiden, crying out words of affection,

children.text: saro mā vardhatetyuktaṃ tataḥ sā saramābhavat ||
children.translated_text: said, 'Lake, do not grow'; from that she became <s>Saramā</s>.

children.text: evaṃ te kṛtadārā vai remire tatra rākṣasāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus those rākṣasas, having taken wives, delighted there,

children.text: svāṃ svāṃ bhāryām upādāya gandharvā iva nandane ||
children.translated_text: each with his own wife, like gandharvas in <s>Nandana</s>.
Then <s>Mandodarī</s> gave birth to a son, <s>Meghanāda</s>;
he is the one called <s>Indrajit</s> by you.
Formerly, as soon as he was born, that son of a rākṣasa,
while crying, released a very great sound like that of a rain cloud.

children.text: jaḍīkṛtāyāṃ laṅkāyāṃ tena nādena tasya vai
children.translated_text: When <s>Laṅkā</s> had been stunned by that sound of his,
his father himself gave him the name <s>Meghanāda</s>.
He then grew up, O <s>Rāma</s>, in <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s splendid inner palace,
guarded by excellent women, hidden like fire by pieces of wood.
Then, at some later time, a fierce embodied Sleep, sent forth by the lord of the world,
came upon <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> there.
Then <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> spoke to his brother as he sat there:

children.text: nidrā māṃ bādhate rājan kārayasva mamālayam ||
children.translated_text: Sleep oppresses me, O king; have a dwelling made for me.
Then craftsmen appointed by the king, like <s>Viśvakarman</s>,
made for <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> a dwelling equal to <s>Kailāsa</s>.

children.text: vistīrṇaṃ yojanaṃ śubhraṃ tato dviguṇam āyatam
children.translated_text: They made it one yojana broad, bright, and twice as long,
beautiful to behold and free from obstruction, for <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>.
Everywhere it was adorned with variegated crystal and golden pillars,
made splendid with vaidūrya stones, and with lattices of little bells as well.
It was furnished with ivory archways and with platforms of diamond and crystal,

children.text: sarvartusukhadaṃ nityaṃ meroḥ puṇyāṃ guhām iva ||
children.translated_text: always giving comfort in every season, like a holy cave of <s>Meru</s>.
There the night-roaming <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, overcome by sleep,
lay for many thousands of years and did not wake.
But when <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> was overcome by sleep, <s>Daśānana</s>
constantly harassed devarṣis, yakṣas, and gandharvas.
Going in great anger to the marvelous gardens,

children.text: tāni gatvā susaṃkruddho bhinatti sma daśānanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: including <s>Nandana</s> and the others, <s>Daśānana</s> would destroy them.

children.text: nadīṃ gaja iva krīḍan vṛkṣān vāyur iva kṣipan
children.translated_text: Playing like an elephant in a river, casting down trees like the wind,

children.text: nagān vajra iva sṛṣṭo vidhvaṃsayati nityaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he continually shattered mountains like a thunderbolt that had been hurled.
When <s>Dhaneśvara</s> learned of <s>Daśagrīva</s>'s conduct in this way,
he, knowing <s>dharma</s> and remembering conduct suited to his family and to himself,
<s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> then sent a messenger to <s>Laṅkā</s>
for the sake of showing brotherly feeling, and for <s>Daśagrīva</s>'s welfare.

children.text: sa gatvā nagarīṃ laṅkām āsasāda vibhīṣaṇam
children.translated_text: He went to the city of <s>Laṅkā</s> and approached <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>;
honored by him according to <s>dharma</s>, he was asked about the reason for his arrival.

children.text: pṛṣṭvā ca kuśalaṃ rājño jñātīn api ca bāndhavān
children.translated_text: After inquiring about the welfare of the king, and also of his kinsmen and relatives,
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> showed him <s>Daśānana</s>, sitting in the assembly.

children.text: sa dṛṣṭvā tatra rājānaṃ dīpyamānaṃ svatejasā
children.translated_text: Seeing the king there, blazing with his own splendor,
and honoring him with a salutation of victory, he sat silent for a moment.
When a couch covered with fine spreads had been brought for him,
the messenger sat down and then addressed <s>Daśagrīva</s> with these words:

children.text: rājan vadāmi te sarvaṃ bhrātā tava yad abravīt
children.translated_text: O king, I shall tell you everything that your brother said,

children.text: ubhayoḥ sadṛśaṃ saumya vṛttasya ca kulasya ca ||
children.translated_text: O gentle one, which is fitting for both your conduct and your lineage.
Good; enough of this. A full account of your conduct has been gathered.

children.text: sādhu dharme vyavasthānaṃ kriyatāṃ yadi śakyate ||
children.translated_text: Good; let firm standing in <s>dharma</s> be undertaken, if it can be done.

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ me nandanaṃ bhagnam ṛṣayo nihatāḥ śrutāḥ
children.translated_text: I have seen <s>Nandana</s> broken, and I have heard that ṛṣis have been slain.

children.text: devānāṃ tu samudyogastvatto rājañ śrutaśca me ||
children.translated_text: I have also heard, O king, of the gods' mobilization because of you.
You have disregarded me many times, O lord of rākṣasas;
yet one's own kinsmen, though they have offended through childishness, are to be protected.

children.text: ahaṃ tu himavatpṛṣṭhaṃ gato dharmam upāsitum
children.translated_text: I, however, have gone to the slopes of <s>Himavat</s> to practice <s>dharma</s>,
having undertaken a fierce vow, disciplined and with my senses restrained.

children.text: tatra devo mayā dṛṣṭaḥ saha devyomayā prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: There I saw the god, the lord, together with the goddess <s>Umā</s>.

children.text: savyaṃ cakṣur mayā caiva tatra devyāṃ nipātitam ||
children.translated_text: And there my left eye fell upon that goddess.

children.text: kā nviyaṃ syād iti śubhā na khalvanyena hetunā
children.translated_text: "Who indeed might this auspicious woman be?" It was certainly from no other motive;

children.text: rūpaṃ hyanupamaṃ kṛtvā tatra krīḍati pārvatī ||
children.translated_text: for <s>Pārvatī</s>, having assumed an incomparable form, was sporting there.

children.text: tato devyāḥ prabhāvena dagdhaṃ savyaṃ mamekṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Then, through the power of the goddess, my left eye was burned;
like a light covered with dust, it became tawny.

children.text: tato 'ham anyad vistīrṇaṃ gatvā tasya girestaṭam
children.translated_text: Then I went to another broad slope of that mountain
and for a full eight hundred years undertook a great vow.
When that observance was completed, there the god <s>Maheśvara</s>,

children.text: prītaḥ prītena manasā prāha vākyam idaṃ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: pleased and with a pleased mind, the lord spoke these words:
"I am pleased with you, knower of <s>dharma</s>, by this austerity, O firm-vowed one.

children.text: mayā caitad vrataṃ cīrṇaṃ tvayā caiva dhanādhipa ||
children.translated_text: This vow has been performed by me, and by you also, O lord of wealth.

children.text: tṛtīyaḥ puruṣo nāsti yaścared vratam īdṛśam
children.translated_text: There is no third person who could perform such a vow;
for this very difficult vow was created by me in ancient times.

children.text: tat sakhitvaṃ mayā sārdhaṃ rocayasva dhaneśvara
children.translated_text: Therefore choose friendship together with me, O lord of wealth;
since you have conquered me by austerity, become my friend, faultless one.

children.text: devyā dagdhaṃ prabhāvena yacca savyaṃ tavekṣaṇam
children.translated_text: And because your left eye was burned by the power of the goddess,
the name <s>Ekākṣipiṅgala</s> shall remain forever."

children.text: evaṃ tena sakhitvaṃ ca prāpyānujñāṃ ca śaṃkarāt
children.translated_text: Thus, having obtained friendship with him and permission from <s>Śaṃkara</s>,

children.text: āgamya ca śruto 'yaṃ me tava pāpaviniścayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I came here, and this wicked resolve of yours has been heard by me.
Therefore turn back from joining in this most unrighteous act, corrupter of your family;
for the means of your death is being considered by hosts of seers and by the gods.
Thus addressed, <s>Daśagrīva</s>, angry and with blood-red eyes,

children.text: hastān dantāṃśca saṃpīḍya vākyam etad uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: clenching his hands and teeth, spoke this word:

children.text: vijñātaṃ te mayā dūta vākyaṃ yat tvaṃ prabhāṣase
children.translated_text: "Your message that you speak has been understood by me, envoy.

children.text: naiva tvam asi naivāsau bhrātrā yenāsi preṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: You are no true envoy, nor is he a brother by whom you have been sent.

children.text: hitaṃ na sa mamaitaddhi bravīti dhanarakṣakaḥ
children.translated_text: That guardian of wealth does not speak this for my good;
yet you, fool, proclaim his friendship with <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: na hantavyo gurur jyeṣṭho mamāyam iti manyate
children.translated_text: He thinks, 'This elder brother, my guru, must not be killed.'

children.text: tasya tvidānīṃ śrutvā me vākyam eṣā kṛtā matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: But now, hear my words: this is the decision I have made about him.
Relying on the strength of my arms, I shall conquer even the three worlds.

children.text: etanmuhūrtam eṣo 'haṃ tasyaikasya kṛte ca vai
children.translated_text: At this very moment, for the sake of that one alone,
I shall lead those four guardians of the worlds to the abode of <s>Yama</s>."

children.text: evam uktvā tu laṅkeśo dūtaṃ khaḍgena jaghnivān
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Laṅkeśa</s> struck down the envoy with his sword
and gave him to the wicked-minded rākṣasas to be eaten.
Then, after auspicious rites had been performed, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> mounted his chariot;
desiring conquest of the three worlds, he went to where the lord of wealth was.

children.text: tataḥ sa sacivaiḥ sārdhaṃ ṣaḍbhir nityaṃ balotkaṭaiḥ
children.translated_text: Then, together with his six ministers, always fierce in strength,
with <s>Mahodara</s> and <s>Prahasta</s>, with <s>Mārīca</s>, <s>Śuka</s>, and <s>Sāraṇa</s>,
and with heroic <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>, ever greedy for battle,

children.text: vṛtaḥ samprayayau śrīmān krodhāllokān dahann iva ||
children.translated_text: the glorious one, surrounded by them, set out, as if burning the worlds in anger.

children.text: purāṇi sa nadīḥ śailān vanānyupavanāni ca
children.translated_text: Passing over cities, rivers, mountains, forests, and groves
in a moment, he entered Mount <s>Kailāsa</s>.

children.text: taṃ niviṣṭaṃ girau tasmin rākṣasendraṃ niśamya tu
children.translated_text: When they heard that the lord of rākṣasas had encamped on that mountain,

children.text: rājño bhrātāyam ityuktvā gatā yatra dhaneśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: saying, "This is the king's brother," they went to where the lord of wealth was.

children.text: gatvā tu sarvam ācakhyur bhrātustasya viniścayam
children.translated_text: Having gone, they reported in full that brother's resolve;
and, permitted by the giver of wealth, they then went to battle.
Then the tumult of the lord of the nairṛtas' army swelled
like the rising ocean, as if shaking the mountain.
Then a battle arose, crowded with yakṣas and rākṣasas,
and there that rākṣasa's ministers became hard pressed.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā tādṛśaṃ sainyaṃ daśagrīvo niśācaraḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing such an army, the night-roaming <s>Daśagrīva</s>
then roared out of joy and advanced in fury.

children.text: ye tu te rākṣasendrasya sacivā ghoravikramāḥ
children.translated_text: But those ministers of the lord of rākṣasas, terrible in valor,
each fought against a thousand thousands.
Then, while he was being struck with maces, iron bars, swords, spears, and javelins,
<s>Daśagrīva</s> plunged into that army.
There, struck by them as if left breathless, <s>Daśānana</s>
was hemmed in by the yakṣa chiefs, like by clouds pouring rain.
That wicked one, raising a mace like the staff of Time,

children.text: praviveśa tataḥ sainyaṃ nayan yakṣān yamakṣayam ||
children.translated_text: then entered the army, sending yakṣas to the abode of <s>Yama</s>.
Like a fire driven by the wind burning a wide thicket
filled with dry fuel, he burned that dreadful army.
But by his ministers in battle, <s>Mahodara</s>, <s>Śuka</s>, and the others,
those yakṣas were made few in number, like clouds by winds.
Some, their limbs broken by weapons, had fallen on the battlefield;
cast down upon the earth, they bit their lips with their sharp teeth.
Out of fear, embracing one another, their weapons fallen in the arena of battle,

children.text: niṣeduste tadā yakṣāḥ kūlā jalahatā iva ||
children.translated_text: those yakṣas then sank down like riverbanks battered by water.
Among those slain and standing in heaven, those fighting on the surface of the earth,
and the hosts of seers looking on, there was no empty space in the sky.
At this interval, O <s>Rāma</s>, with a vast force and vehicles,
there came a very great yakṣa named <s>Saṃyodhakaṇṭaka</s>.
By that yakṣa, <s>Mārīca</s> was struck down as if by <s>Viṣṇu</s>;
fallen, he reached the earth from the sky, like one whose merit was exhausted.
Having regained consciousness within a moment and having rested, the night-roamer

children.text: taṃ yakṣaṃ yodhayāmāsa sa ca bhagnaḥ pradudruve ||
children.translated_text: fought with that yakṣa, and he, broken, fled away.
Then, variegated with gold and inlaid with vaidūrya and silver,
he entered that gateway arch, the guarded limit of the doorkeepers.
Then, O <s>Rāma</s>, as the night-roamer <s>Daśagrīva</s> was entering,
the doorkeeper known as <s>Sūryabhānu</s> stopped him.
Then that yakṣa tore up the gateway arch and struck him;
the rākṣasa was smitten by the gateway hurled by the yakṣa,

children.text: na kṣitiṃ prayayau rāma varāt salilayoninaḥ ||
children.translated_text: yet, O <s>Rāma</s>, because of the boon from the water-born one, he did not fall to the earth.

children.text: sa tu tenaiva taṃ yakṣaṃ toraṇena samāhanat
children.translated_text: But with that very gateway arch he struck that yakṣa,

children.text: nādṛśyata tadā yakṣo bhasma tena kṛtastu saḥ ||
children.translated_text: and then the yakṣa was no longer seen; by it he was reduced to ash.

children.text: tataḥ pradudruvuḥ sarve yakṣā dṛṣṭvā parākramam
children.translated_text: Then all the yakṣas fled when they saw his valor,
and, pressed by fear, they entered rivers and caves.
Then, seeing those yakṣas fleeing by hundreds of thousands,

children.text: svayam eva dhanādhyakṣo nirjagāma raṇaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: the lord of wealth himself went out toward battle.
There a yakṣa named <s>Māṇicāra</s>, exceedingly hard to conquer,
surrounded by four thousand yakṣas, joined battle.
With clubs, pestles, spears, javelins, lances, and hammers,
the yakṣas, striking in battle, rushed against the rākṣasas.

children.text: tataḥ prahastena tadā sahasraṃ nihataṃ raṇe
children.translated_text: Then at that time a thousand were slain by <s>Prahasta</s> in battle,
and another thousand were slain by <s>Mahodara</s> with his mace.

children.text: kruddhena ca tadā rāma mārīcena durātmanā
children.translated_text: And then, O <s>Rāma</s>, by the enraged and wicked <s>Mārīca</s>,
in the space of only a blink, two thousand were struck down.
When <s>Māṇibhadra</s> met <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s> in the great battle,

children.text: musalenorasi krodhāt tāḍito na ca kampitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he was struck on the chest in anger with a pestle, but did not tremble.
Then, when <s>Māṇibhadra</s> brandished his mace, the rākṣasa
<s>Dhūmrākṣa</s> was struck on the head; dazed, he fell down.
Seeing <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s> struck, fallen, and sprinkled with blood,
the ten-faced one, greatly enraged, ran at <s>Māṇibhadra</s>.
As he angrily rushed on, rising like the fire at the end of an age,
the foremost yakṣa struck him with three spears.
Then, by the king of the rākṣasas, he was struck with a mace in battle;

children.text: tasya tena prahāreṇa mukuṭaḥ pārśvam āgataḥ
children.translated_text: from that blow his diadem slipped to one side,

children.text: tadā prabhṛti yakṣo 'sau pārśvamaulir iti smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and from then on that yakṣa was remembered as <s>Pārśvamauli</s>.
When that great-souled yakṣa <s>Māṇibhadra</s> had turned away,
a very great uproar, O <s>Rāma</s>, increased on that mountain.
Then from afar the mace-bearing lord of wealth was seen,
surrounded by <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Proṣṭhapada</s>, and by <s>Śaṅkha</s> and <s>Padma</s>.

children.text: sa dṛṣṭvā bhrātaraṃ saṃkhye śāpād vibhraṣṭagauravam
children.translated_text: Seeing his brother in battle, his glory fallen away because of the curse,

children.text: uvāca vacanaṃ dhīmān yuktaṃ paitāmahe kule ||
children.translated_text: the wise one spoke words fitting the family descended from the grandsire.
Though you were being restrained by me, wicked-minded one, you do not understand;

children.text: paścād asya phalaṃ prāpya jñāsyase nirayaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: later, after receiving its fruit, you will know it when you have gone to hell.

children.text: yo hi mohād viṣaṃ pītvā nāvagacchati mānavaḥ
children.translated_text: For a man who, through delusion, drinks poison and does not understand it

children.text: pariṇāme sa vimūḍho jānīte karmaṇaḥ phalam ||
children.translated_text: knows, bewildered, at the end the fruit of the act.
For the deities rejoice in anyone who is joined with <s>dharma</s> (righteous order);

children.text: yena tvam īdṛśaṃ bhāvaṃ nītastacca na budhyase ||
children.translated_text: and you do not understand that by this you have been brought to such a state.

children.text: yo hi mātṝḥ pitṝn bhrātṝn ācāryāṃścāvamanyate
children.translated_text: For one who disdains mothers, fathers, brothers, and teachers

children.text: sa paśyati phalaṃ tasya pretarājavaśaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: sees the fruit of that when he has come under the power of the king of the dead.

children.text: adhruve hi śarīre yo na karoti tapo'rjanam
children.translated_text: He who, while the body is unstable, does not acquire austerity,

children.text: sa paścāt tapyate mūḍho mṛto dṛṣṭvātmano gatim ||
children.translated_text: afterward grieves, foolish, when dead and seeing his own fate.
For no understanding arises according to the wish of someone whose intellect is bad;

children.text: yādṛśaṃ kurute karma tādṛśaṃ phalam aśnute ||
children.translated_text: as a person performs an act, so he experiences its fruit.

children.text: buddhiṃ rūpaṃ balaṃ vittaṃ putrānmāhātmyam eva ca
children.translated_text: Understanding, beauty, strength, wealth, sons, and greatness too,
men obtain all through their own former deeds.

children.text: evaṃ nirayagāmī tvaṃ yasya te matir īdṛśī
children.translated_text: Thus you are bound for hell, since your thought is such;
I will not speak to you; this is the judgment regarding one of evil conduct.
Having spoken thus, then his ministers were struck by him;
all of them, with <s>Mārīca</s> at their head, turned away and fled in confusion.
Then by that great-souled lord of the yakṣas, <s>Daśagrīva</s>

children.text: gadayābhihato mūrdhni na ca sthānād vyakampata ||
children.translated_text: was struck on the head with a mace, but did not move from his place.
Then the two, O <s>Rāma</s>, striking each other in the supreme battle,

children.text: na vihvalau na ca śrāntau babhūvatur amarṣaṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: became neither dazed nor tired, both full of wrath.

children.text: āgneyam astraṃ sa tato mumoca dhanado raṇe
children.translated_text: Then <s>Dhanada</s> released the Āgneya weapon in battle;
<s>Daśagrīva</s> countered that weapon with the Vāruṇa.

children.text: tato māyāṃ praviṣṭaḥ sa rākṣasīṃ rākṣaseśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Then the lord of rākṣasas entered a rākṣasa illusion,

children.text: jaghāna mūrdhni dhanadaṃ vyāvidhya mahatīṃ gadām ||
children.translated_text: and struck <s>Dhanada</s> on the head, brandishing a great mace.
Thus struck by him, dazed and sprinkled with blood,
the lord of wealth fell like an aśoka tree cut at the root.
Then there, by <s>Padma</s> and the other treasures, the lord of wealth
<s>Dhanada</s> was brought to the <s>Nandana</s> grove, and then restored to breath.

children.text: tato nirjitya taṃ rāma dhanadaṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, O <s>Rāma</s>, having defeated him, <s>Dhanada</s>, the lord of rākṣasas
took his <s>Puṣpaka</s> vimāna, the mark of victory.
It was surrounded by golden pillars and had gateways of vaidūrya gems,
covered with nets of pearls, and furnished with trees yielding every desired fruit.

children.text: tat tu rājā samāruhya kāmagaṃ vīryanirjitam
children.translated_text: Mounting that, the king, going at will and won by his valor,
having conquered the god <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, descended from <s>Kailāsa</s>.

children.text: sa jitvā bhrātaraṃ rāma dhanadaṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: That lord of rākṣasas, O <s>Rāma</s>, having conquered his brother <s>Dhanada</s>,
Then he went to <s>Śaravaṇa</s>, the birthplace of <s>Mahāsena</s>.
Then <s>Daśagrīva</s> saw that golden <s>Śaravaṇa</s>,
wrapped in a net of rays, like a second sun.
Having reached a mountain with a charming woodland in its interior,

children.text: apaśyat puṣpakaṃ tatra rāma viṣṭambhitaṃ divi ||
children.translated_text: he saw the <s>Puṣpaka</s> there, O <s>Rāma</s>, checked in the sky.

children.text: viṣṭabdhaṃ puṣpakaṃ dṛṣṭvā kāmagaṃ hyagamaṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: Seeing the <s>Puṣpaka</s> checked, made unable to go though it moved at will,
the rākṣasa, surrounded by those ministers, began to think:

children.text: kim idaṃ yannimittaṃ me na ca gacchati puṣpakam
children.translated_text: "What is this? For what reason does my <s>Puṣpaka</s> not go?
Whose deed could this be, while it stands above the mountain?"
Then <s>Mārīca</s>, skilled in judgment, said to <s>Daśagrīva</s>,
"This is not without cause, O king; this <s>Puṣpaka</s> does not go."
Then the powerful attendant of <s>Bhava</s> came to his side,
and <s>Nandīśvara</s>, fearless, said this to the lord of rākṣasas:
"Turn back, <s>Daśagrīva</s>; <s>Śaṃkara</s> is sporting on the mountain.
For suparṇas, nāgas, yakṣas, daityas, dānavas, and rākṣasas,

children.text: prāṇinām eva sarveṣām agamyaḥ parvataḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and indeed for all living beings, the mountain has been made inaccessible."

children.text: sa roṣāt tāmranayanaḥ puṣpakād avaruhya ca
children.translated_text: Red-eyed with anger, he dismounted from the <s>Puṣpaka</s>,
and saying, "Who is this <s>Śaṃkara</s>?" he went to the foot of the mountain.
Then he saw the lord <s>Nandīśvara</s> standing not far away,

children.text: dīptaṃ śūlam avaṣṭabhya dvitīyam iva śaṃkaram ||
children.translated_text: blazing, leaning on his trident, like a second <s>Śaṃkara</s>.

children.text: sa vānaramukhaṃ dṛṣṭvā tam avajñāya rākṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing him with a monkey's face and despising him, the rākṣasa,

children.text: prahāsaṃ mumuce maurkhyāt satoya iva toyadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: through folly, let out a laugh like a raincloud heavy with water.
The blessed <s>Nandī</s>, another form of <s>Śaṃkara</s>, became enraged,
and spoke there to the rākṣasa <s>Daśagrīva</s>, who stood before him:

children.text: yasmād vānaramūrtiṃ māṃ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasa durmate
children.translated_text: "Because, O wicked-minded rākṣasa, seeing me with a monkey's form,

children.text: maurkhyāt tvam avajānīṣe parihāsaṃ ca muñcasi ||
children.translated_text: you despise me through folly and also give way to laughter,
therefore monkeys endowed with my form, equal to me in strength and splendor,

children.text: utpatsyante vadhārthaṃ hi kulasya tava vānarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: will arise for the destruction of your lineage.

children.text: kiṃ tvidānīṃ mayā śakyaṃ kartuṃ yat tvāṃ niśācara
children.translated_text: But what can now be done by me to you, O night-roamer?

children.text: na hantavyo hatastvaṃ hi pūrvam eva svakarmabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: You are not to be killed by me, for you have already been slain by your own deeds."
Without considering <s>Nandī</s>'s words then, the night-roamer

children.text: parvataṃ taṃ samāsādya vākyam etad uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: approached that mountain and spoke these words:
"Since, because of this, the movement of my <s>Puṣpaka</s> has been cut off as it was going,

children.text: tad etacchailam unmūlaṃ karomi tava gopate ||
children.translated_text: I shall tear up this mountain by the roots, O lord of bulls.
By what power does <s>Bhava</s> sport there like a king?
