You do not understand that a place of danger has come near and must be recognized."

children.text: evam uktvā tato rājan bhujān prakṣipya parvate
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, O king, he thrust his arms into the mountain
and shook that mountain, together with its deer, wild beasts, and trees.

children.text: tato rāma mahādevaḥ prahasan vīkṣya tatkṛtam
children.translated_text: Then, O <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>, laughing as he saw what he had done,
pressed that mountain down playfully with his big toe.
Then his arms, crushed beneath that mountain,
were pinned down, and that rākṣasa's ministers were astonished there.

children.text: rakṣasā tena roṣācca bhujānāṃ pīḍanāt tathā
children.translated_text: From that rākṣasa, because of anger and the crushing of his arms,
there issued a very great roar by which the three worlds were filled.
Men, terrified by the sound, thought that the worlds were being destroyed,
and the deities too were shaken, disturbed in their own duties.
Then <s>Mahādeva</s>, pleased and standing on the mountain peak,

children.text: muktvā tasya bhujān rājan prāha vākyaṃ daśānanam ||
children.translated_text: released his arms, O king, and spoke these words to <s>Daśānana</s>:
"I am pleased with your strength and boldness, O night-roamer.
As you roared, a supremely terrible voice was released from pain.
Because this threefold world, overcome by fear, has been made to cry out by you,

children.text: tasmāt tvaṃ rāvaṇo nāma nāmnā tena bhaviṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: therefore you shall be called <s>Rāvaṇa</s> by that name.

children.text: devatā mānuṣā yakṣā ye cānye jagatītale
children.translated_text: The gods, humans, yakṣas, and whatever others are on the earth
will address you in this way as <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the roarer of the worlds.

children.text: gaccha paulastya viśrabdhaḥ pathā yena tvam icchasi
children.translated_text: Go, <s>Paulastya</s>, confident, by whatever path you wish.
You have been permitted by me, lord of rākṣasas; depart."
Thus named by <s>Maheśvara</s> himself, that <s>Rāvaṇa</s>
bowed to <s>Mahādeva</s> and mounted that aerial car.
Then, O <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> roamed over the earth,
oppressing mighty <s>kṣatriya</s>s here and there.
Then, O king, as the mighty-armed <s>Rāvaṇa</s> wandered the earth,
he reached a forest of <s>Himavat</s> and roamed about.
There he saw a maiden wearing black antelope-skin and matted hair,

children.text: ārṣeṇa vidhinā yuktāṃ tapantīṃ devatām iva ||
children.translated_text: engaged in the manner of the seers, practicing austerity like a deity.

children.text: sa dṛṣṭvā rūpasampannāṃ kanyāṃ tāṃ sumahāvratām
children.translated_text: Seeing that beautiful maiden of very great vows,
his self overcome by the delusion of desire, he asked her, as if laughing:

children.text: kim idaṃ vartase bhadre viruddhaṃ yauvanasya te
children.translated_text: "What is this, fair one, that you are doing, contrary to your youth?

children.text: na hi yuktā tavaitasya rūpasyeyaṃ pratikriyā ||
children.translated_text: This practice is not suited to such beauty as yours.

children.text: kasyāsi duhitā bhadre ko vā bhartā tavānaghe
children.translated_text: Whose daughter are you, fair one? Or who is your husband, blameless one?

children.text: pṛcchataḥ śaṃsa me śīghraṃ ko vā hetustapo'rjane ||
children.translated_text: Tell me quickly as I ask: what is the reason for undertaking <s>tapas</s> (austerity)?"

children.text: evam uktā tu sā kanyā tenānāryeṇa rakṣasā
children.translated_text: Addressed in this way by that ignoble rākṣasa,
the ascetic maiden, having duly offered him hospitality, said:

children.text: kuśadhvajo nāma pitā brahmarṣir mama dhārmikaḥ
children.translated_text: "My father is named <s>Kuśadhvaja</s>, a righteous <s>brahmarṣi</s> (brahman-sage),
the glorious son of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, equal to <s>Bṛhaspati</s> in intelligence.
As that great-souled one was constantly engaged in study of the <s>Veda</s>,

children.text: sambhūtā vāṅmayī kanyā nāmnā vedavatī smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: I was born as a maiden made of speech, remembered by the name <s>Vedavatī</s>.
Then the gods, together with gandharvas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and pannagas...

children.text: te cāpi gatvā pitaraṃ varaṇaṃ rocayanti me ||
children.translated_text: And they too, having gone to my father, urge him to choose me for them.

children.text: na ca māṃ sa pitā tebhyo dattavān rākṣaseśvara
children.translated_text: But that father of mine did not give me to them, O lord of rākṣasas.
I shall tell you the reason for that; listen, mighty-armed one.

children.text: pitustu mama jāmātā viṣṇuḥ kila surottamaḥ
children.translated_text: For <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the best of the gods, the lord of the three worlds, was intended as my father's son-in-law, so it is said.
Therefore my righteous father does not wish to give me to anyone else.
Hearing that, and proud of his strength,

children.text: śambhur nāma tato rājā daityānāṃ kupito 'bhavat
children.translated_text: a king of the daityas named <s>Śambhu</s> then became angry.

children.text: tena rātrau prasupto me pitā pāpena hiṃsitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By that sinful one my father was killed at night while he slept.

children.text: tato me jananī dīnā taccharīraṃ pitur mama
children.translated_text: Then my wretched mother, that most noble lady, embraced the body of my father,
and entered the fire together with him.

children.text: tato manorathaṃ satyaṃ pitur nārāyaṇaṃ prati
children.translated_text: Thereafter the wish of my father concerning <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> should be made true,

children.text: karomīti mamecchā ca hṛdaye sādhu viṣṭhitā ||
children.translated_text: and this desire has been firmly established in my heart.
Even though my father has gone among the dead, I shall fulfill what he longed for.

children.text: iti pratijñām āruhya carāmi vipulaṃ tapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having taken up this vow, I practice great austerity.

children.text: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ mayā rākṣasapuṃgava
children.translated_text: All this has been told to you by me, O foremost of rākṣasas.
Know that I have taken refuge in <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), desiring <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as my husband.

children.text: vijñātastvaṃ hi me rājan gaccha paulastyanandana
children.translated_text: I know who you are, O king; go, delight of <s>Paulastya</s>'s line.

children.text: jānāmi tapasā sarvaṃ trailokye yaddhi vartate ||
children.translated_text: Through austerity I know everything that takes place in the three worlds.
Thereupon <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, afflicted by the arrows of <s>Kandarpa</s>, spoke to that maiden of great vows,
after descending from the top of his aerial chariot.
You are arrogant, fair-hipped one, since such is your intention.
Doe-eyed one, the accumulation of <s>dharma</s> is splendid among the old.
You, endowed with every virtue, do not deserve to do such a thing,
O timid beauty of the three worlds, imposing an old person's rule upon youth.

children.text: kaśca tāvad asau yaṃ tvaṃ viṣṇur ityabhibhāṣase
children.translated_text: And who, after all, is this man whom you call <s>Viṣṇu</s>?

children.text: vīryeṇa tapasā caiva bhogena ca balena ca
children.translated_text: In valor, in austerity, in enjoyment, and in strength,

children.text: na mayāsau samo bhadre yaṃ tvaṃ kāmayase 'ṅgane ||
children.translated_text: he is not equal to me, good lady, this man whom you desire, O woman.

children.text: mā maivam iti sā kanyā tam uvāca niśācaram
children.translated_text: 'Do not, do not speak so,' that maiden said to the night-roamer,

children.text: mūrdhajeṣu ca tāṃ rakṣaḥ karāgreṇa parāmṛśat ||
children.translated_text: but the rākṣasa touched her on the hair with the tip of his hand.

children.text: tato vedavatī kruddhā keśān hastena sāchinat
children.translated_text: Then the enraged <s>Vedavatī</s> cut off her hair with her hand,
and, composing herself for the fire and hastening toward death, she spoke:
'Since I have been violated by you, ignoble one, my life is now no life at all.
Therefore, rākṣasa, while you look on, I shall enter the sacrificial fire.

children.text: yasmāt tu dharṣitā cāham apāpā cāpyanāthavat
children.translated_text: But because I, though sinless, have been violated by you like one without a protector,

children.text: tasmāt tava vadhārthaṃ vai samutpatsyāmyahaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore I shall be born again for the sake of your death.

children.text: na hi śakyaḥ striyā pāpa hantuṃ tvaṃ tu viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: For you cannot be killed by a woman, evil one, and you especially cannot be killed so.

children.text: śāpe tvayi mayotsṛṣṭe tapasaśca vyayo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: If I were to cast a curse upon you, there would be a wasting of my austerity.

children.text: yadi tvasti mayā kiṃcit kṛtaṃ dattaṃ hutaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: If there is anything that has been done, given, or offered by me,

children.text: tena hyayonijā sādhvī bhaveyaṃ dharmiṇaḥ sutā ||
children.translated_text: then by that may I become a virtuous woman, not born from a womb, the daughter of a righteous man.'

children.text: evam uktvā praviṣṭā sā jvalantaṃ vai hutāśanam
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, she entered the blazing sacrificial fire,

children.text: papāta ca divo divyā puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ samantataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and a divine shower of flowers fell from heaven on every side.
That enemy, struck down before by her anger, was killed by you,
after she had taken refuge in your superhuman valor, mountain-like in force.
Thus this most blessed woman is born again among mortals,
in a field furrowed by the point of a plough, on the altar-ground, like a flame of fire.

children.text: eṣā vedavatī nāma pūrvam āsīt kṛte yuge
children.translated_text: This woman was formerly named <s>Vedavatī</s> in the <s>Kṛta</s> age.
Having reached the <s>Tretā</s> age, for the sake of that rākṣasa's death,
she is this <s>Sītā</s>, again called by men '<s>Sītā</s> born from the furrow.'

children.text: praviṣṭāyāṃ hutāśaṃ tu vedavatyāṃ sa rāvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Vedavatī</s> had entered the sacrificial fire, that <s>Rāvaṇa</s>
mounted the <s>Puṣpaka</s> and roamed over the earth.

children.text: tato maruttaṃ nṛpatiṃ yajantaṃ saha daivataiḥ
children.translated_text: Then he saw King <s>Marutta</s> performing sacrifice together with the gods,

children.text: uśīrabījam āsādya dadarśa sa tu rākṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: after that rākṣasa had reached <s>Uśīrabīja</s>.

children.text: saṃvarto nāma brahmarṣir bhrātā sākṣād bṛhaspateḥ
children.translated_text: A brahmarṣi named <s>Saṃvarta</s>, the direct brother of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,
righteous and surrounded by all the hosts of brahmans, officiated as his priest.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā devāstu tad rakṣo varadānena durjayam
children.translated_text: But when the gods saw that rākṣasa, unconquerable because of the granted boon,
they assumed various births, afraid of being overpowered by him.
<s>Indra</s> became a peacock, and <s>Dharmarāja</s> became a crow.
The lord of wealth became a chameleon, and <s>Varuṇa</s> became a swan.

children.text: taṃ ca rājānam āsādya rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: Approaching that king, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of rākṣasas,

children.text: prāha yuddhaṃ prayaccheti nirjito 'smīti vā vada ||
children.translated_text: said, 'Give me battle, or say, "I have been conquered."'

children.text: tato marutto nṛpatiḥ ko bhavān ityuvāca tam
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Marutta</s> said to him, 'Who are you?'

children.text: avahāsaṃ tato muktvā rākṣaso vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Thereupon the rākṣasa broke into laughter and spoke these words:
'Because of your lack of curiosity, O earthly king, I am pleased with you,
since you do not recognize me, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the younger brother of the lord of wealth.

children.text: triṣu lokeṣu kaḥ so 'sti yo na jānāti me balam
children.translated_text: Who is there in the three worlds who does not know my strength,

children.text: bhrātaraṃ yena nirjitya vimānam idam āhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: I by whom my brother was conquered and this aerial chariot taken away?'
Then King <s>Marutta</s> spoke to that rākṣasa:

children.text: dhanyaḥ khalu bhavān yena jyeṣṭho bhrātā raṇe jitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Blessed indeed are you, since your elder brother was defeated in battle.
Having done a wicked deed, not joined with <s>dharma</s> and not approved by the world,
you boast of the conquest of your brother.

children.text: kiṃ tvaṃ prāk kevalaṃ dharmaṃ caritvā labdhavān varam
children.translated_text: Or did you first practice only <s>dharma</s> and so obtain a boon?

children.text: śrutapūrvaṃ hi na mayā yādṛśaṃ bhāṣase svayam ||
children.translated_text: For I have never before heard such a thing as you yourself proclaim.'

children.text: tataḥ śarāsanaṃ gṛhya sāyakāṃśca sa pārthivaḥ
children.translated_text: Then that earthly king took up his bow and arrows,

children.text: raṇāya niryayau kruddhaḥ saṃvarto mārgam āvṛṇot ||
children.translated_text: and went forth in anger for battle, but <s>Saṃvarta</s> blocked his path.

children.text: so 'bravīt snehasaṃyuktaṃ maruttaṃ taṃ mahān ṛṣiḥ
children.translated_text: That great seer spoke to <s>Marutta</s> with affection,

children.text: śrotavyaṃ yadi madvākyaṃ saṃprahāro na te kṣamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'If my word is to be heard, a fight is not proper for you.'

children.text: māheśvaram idaṃ satram asamāptaṃ kulaṃ dahet
children.translated_text: This sacrificial session for <s>Maheśvara</s>, if unfinished, would burn up the family.

children.text: dīkṣitasya kuto yuddhaṃ krūratvaṃ dīkṣite kutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: How can there be fighting for one who has been consecrated? How can cruelty be in one consecrated?
And in battle there is always uncertainty; this rākṣasa is difficult to conquer.
So <s>Marutta</s>, lord of the earth, turned back because of his guru's words;
putting aside his bow with its arrow, he became composed and intent upon the sacrifice.

children.text: tatastaṃ nirjitaṃ matvā ghoṣayāmāsa vai śukaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śuka</s>, thinking him defeated, proclaimed aloud:
"<s>Rāvaṇa</s> has conquered," and in joy he let out a cry.
Having devoured the great seers who were standing there, who had come to the sacrifice,
and being sated with their blood, he again went over the earth.

children.text: rāvaṇe tu gate devāḥ sendrāścaiva divaukasaḥ
children.translated_text: But when <s>Rāvaṇa</s> had gone, the gods, together with <s>Indra</s>, the sky-dwellers,

children.text: tataḥ svāṃ yonim āsādya tāni sattvānyathābruvan ||
children.translated_text: then, having regained their own forms, spoke to those creatures.
Then <s>Indra</s>, out of joy, spoke to the peacock with blue tail-feathers:
"I am pleased with your service, O bird who knows <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: mama netrasahasraṃ yat tat te barhe bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: That thousand eyes of mine will be on your tail-feathers;
when I rain, you will obtain joy as the sign of my pleasure.

children.text: nīlāḥ kila purā barhā mayūrāṇāṃ narādhipa
children.translated_text: Formerly, O lord of men, the tail-feathers of peacocks were indeed blue;

children.text: surādhipād varaṃ prāpya gatāḥ sarve vicitratām ||
children.translated_text: having received the boon from the lord of the gods, they all became variegated.
O <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Dharmarāja</s> spoke to the crow standing in the eastern hall:

children.text: pakṣiṃstavāsmi suprītaḥ prītasya ca vacaḥ śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: "O bird, I am very pleased with you; hear the words of one who is pleased.

children.text: yathānye vividhai rogaiḥ pīḍyante prāṇino mayā
children.translated_text: As other living beings are afflicted by me with various diseases,

children.text: te na te prabhaviṣyanti mayi prīte na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: they will not prevail over you, when I am pleased; there is no doubt.
You have no fear from death, O bird, because of my boon;

children.text: yāvat tvāṃ na vadhiṣyanti narāstāvad bhaviṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: as long as men do not kill you, so long will you live.
And those humans who belong to my realm and are afflicted by hunger,

children.text: tvayi bhukte tu tṛptāste bhaviṣyanti sabāndhavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: when food is eaten by you, they and their kinsmen will become satisfied.
But <s>Varuṇa</s> spoke to the swan moving in the waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>:
"Let my words, joined with affection, be heard, O lord of winged chariots.
A color beautiful and gentle, resembling the disk of the moon,
will be splendid for you, shining like white foam.
Having approached my body, you will always be lovely;
and you will obtain incomparable joy: this is the sign of my pleasure.

children.text: haṃsānāṃ hi purā rāma na varṇaḥ sarvapāṇḍuraḥ
children.translated_text: For formerly, O <s>Rāma</s>, swans were not wholly white in color;
their wings were covered with blue tips, and their breasts were pure like tips of grass.
Then <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> spoke to the chameleon standing on the mountain:
"I bestow a golden color; you too have my favor.

children.text: sadravyaṃ ca śiro nityaṃ bhaviṣyati tavākṣayam
children.translated_text: Your head, always furnished with that substance, will be undecaying;

children.text: eṣa kāñcanako varṇo matprītyā te bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: this golden color will be yours because of my pleasure.
Having thus given boons to them at that sacrificial festival, the gods,

children.text: nivṛtte saha rājñā vai punaḥ svabhavanaṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: when it had ended, together with the king, returned to their own abodes.

children.text: atha jitvā maruttaṃ sa prayayau rākṣasādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, having conquered <s>Marutta</s>, the lord of rākṣasas set out,
<s>Daśānana</s>, desiring battle, toward the cities of kings.
Approaching royal lords comparable to <s>Mahendra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>,

children.text: abravīd rākṣasendrastu yuddhaṃ me dīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: the lord of rākṣasas said, "Give me battle."

children.text: nirjitāḥ smeti vā brūta eṣo hi mama niścayaḥ
children.translated_text: "Or say, 'We have been conquered.' This is my fixed resolve;

children.text: anyathā kurvatām evaṃ mokṣo vo nopapadyate ||
children.translated_text: for those who do otherwise, release for you is not possible.
Then many wise earthly kings, certain in <s>dharma</s>,
said, "We have been conquered," knowing the enemy's strength from his boon.

children.text: duṣyantaḥ suratho gādhir gayo rājā purūravāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Duṣyanta</s>, <s>Suratha</s>, <s>Gādhi</s>, King <s>Gaya</s>, and <s>Purūravas</s>:
all these kings, dear one, said, "We have been conquered."
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the lord of rākṣasas, reached <s>Ayodhyā</s>,
well guarded by <s>Anaraṇya</s>, like <s>Amarāvatī</s> by <s>Śakra</s>.

children.text: prāha rājānam āsādya yuddhaṃ me sampradīyatām
children.translated_text: Approaching the king, he said, "Let battle be given to me,

children.text: nirjito 'smīti vā brūhi mamaitad iha śāsanam ||
children.translated_text: or say, 'I am conquered.' This is my command here."
<s>Anaraṇya</s>, greatly enraged, then spoke to the lord of rākṣasas:
"I give you single combat, O lord of rākṣasas."

children.text: atha pūrvaṃ śrutārthena sajjitaṃ sumahaddhi yat
children.translated_text: Then that very great army of the king, previously equipped because the matter had been heard,
came forth, intent on killing the rākṣasa.
Many thousands of elephants and ten thousand horses,
together with infantry and chariots, came out at once, covering the earth.

children.text: tad rāvaṇabalaṃ prāpya balaṃ tasya mahīpateḥ
children.translated_text: When that army of the earth-lord reached <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s force,

children.text: prāṇaśyata tadā rājan havyaṃ hutam ivānale ||
children.translated_text: then, O king, it perished like an oblation poured into fire.
The king saw his great army being destroyed,
like the water of five rivers on reaching the great ocean.
Then, making his bow like <s>Śakra</s>'s rainbow resound,
the king, overcome with anger, approached that <s>Rāvaṇa</s> himself.
Then the delight of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>'s line caused eight hundred arrows
to fall upon the head of that king of rākṣasas.

children.text: tasya bāṇāḥ patantaste cakrire na kṣataṃ kvacit
children.translated_text: But those arrows, as they fell on him, made no wound anywhere,
like streams of water falling from clouds upon a mountain peak.
Then the king was struck on the head by the enraged king of rākṣasas
with his palm, and he fell from his chariot.

children.text: sa rājā patito bhūmau vihvalāṅgaḥ pravepitaḥ
children.translated_text: That king fell on the ground, his limbs bewildered, trembling,
like a great śāla tree in the forest, burned by a thunderbolt, fallen down.
Laughing at him, the rākṣasa spoke to the <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, lord of the earth:

children.text: kim idānīṃ tvayā prāptaṃ phalaṃ māṃ prati yudhyatā ||
children.translated_text: "What result have you now obtained by fighting against me?"

children.text: trailokye nāsti yo dvandvaṃ mama dadyānnarādhipa
children.translated_text: There is no one in the three worlds, O lord of men, who could give me single combat.

children.text: śaṅke pramatto bhogeṣu na śṛṇoṣi balaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: I suspect that, heedless amid enjoyments, you have not heard of my strength.

children.text: tasyaivaṃ bruvato rājā mandāsur vākyam abravīt
children.translated_text: As he spoke thus, the king, his vital breaths failing, said this reply:

children.text: kiṃ śakyam iha kartuṃ vai yat kālo duratikramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "What can be done here, when Time is indeed hard to overstep?
For I have not been defeated by you, O rākṣasa, self-praising as you are;
I have met disaster here through Time, while you are only the instrumental cause for me.

children.text: kiṃ tvidānīṃ mayā śakyaṃ kartuṃ prāṇaparikṣaye
children.translated_text: But what can now be done by me when my life-breaths are at their end?
Because I have been sustained by the line of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, I shall speak a word, O rākṣasa.

children.text: yadi dattaṃ yadi hutaṃ yadi me sukṛtaṃ tapaḥ
children.translated_text: If anything has been given by me, if anything has been offered in sacrifice, if my austerity has been meritorious,

children.text: yadi guptāḥ prajāḥ samyak tathā satyaṃ vaco 'stu me ||
children.translated_text: if my subjects have been properly protected, then let this word of mine be true:
In this line of the great-souled <s>Ikṣvāku</s>s there will be born
a king of supreme splendor who will take away your life."
Then a divine drum, lofty as a rain cloud, was struck,
when that curse had been pronounced, and a rain of flowers fell from the sky.

children.text: tataḥ sa rājā rājendra gataḥ sthānaṃ triviṣṭapam
children.translated_text: Then that king, O king of kings, went to the abode, <s>Triviṣṭapa</s>,

children.text: svargate ca nṛpe rāma rākṣasaḥ sa nyavartata ||
children.translated_text: and when the ruler had gone to heaven, O <s>Rāma</s>, that rākṣasa turned back.
Then, terrifying mortals on the earth, the lord of rākṣasas
encountered in that dense cloud the excellent sage <s>Nārada</s>.
But <s>Nārada</s>, great in splendor, the divine seer of immeasurable radiance,
standing on the back of a cloud, spoke to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, who was standing in the <s>Puṣpaka</s>.
"Lord of rākṣasas, gentle one, stop, son of <s>Viśravas</s>.
I am pleased, noble-born one, by your mighty exploits.
By <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s slayings of the Daityas and by <s>Tārkṣya</s>'s harassment of serpents,
and by your crushings in battle, I am deeply satisfied.

children.text: kiṃcid vakṣyāmi tāvat te śrotavyaṃ śroṣyase yadi
children.translated_text: I shall tell you something now; you should listen to it, if you will hear.
And after hearing it, O bull among rākṣasas, you should act at once.
Why is this world being slain by you, who cannot be slain by the gods?

children.text: hata eva hyayaṃ loko yadā mṛtyuvaśaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: For this world is already slain, since it has come under the power of Death.
Look, O mighty-armed lord of rākṣasas, at this human

children.text: lokam enaṃ vicitrārthaṃ yasya na jñāyate gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: world of varied concerns, whose course is not understood.
In one place music and dances are enjoyed by delighted people;
in another there is weeping by the afflicted, their eyes and faces pouring streams of tears.
Through attachment to mother, father, sons, wives, and charming kinsmen,

children.text: mohenāyaṃ jano dhvastaḥ kleśaṃ svaṃ nāvabudhyate ||
children.translated_text: this people is ruined by delusion and does not perceive its own suffering.

children.text: tat kim evaṃ parikliśya lokaṃ mohanirākṛtam
children.translated_text: So why distress in this way a world consumed by delusion?

children.text: jita eva tvayā saumya martyaloko na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The mortal world has already been conquered by you, gentle one; there is no doubt."
When <s>Laṅkeśa</s>, blazing as if with energy, was thus addressed,
he laughed, saluted <s>Nārada</s> there, and said:
"Great seer, lover of battle, whose haunts are those of gods and gandharvas,
I am in fact setting out, eager for victory, to go to <s>Rasātala</s>.

children.text: tato lokatrayaṃ jitvā sthāpya nāgān surān vaśe
children.translated_text: Then, having conquered the three worlds and placed the nāgas and gods under my control,
I shall churn the ocean, the abode of waters, for the sake of amṛta.
Then the venerable sage <s>Nārada</s> said to <s>Daśagrīva</s>:
"By what route, then, will you go now along this path?

children.text: ayaṃ khalu sudurgamyaḥ pitṛrājñaḥ puraṃ prati
children.translated_text: This path, hard to travel and difficult to assail, goes indeed
toward the city of the king of the ancestors, of <s>Yama</s>, scorcher of foes."

children.text: sa tu śāradameghābhaṃ muktvā hāsaṃ daśānanaḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Daśānana</s>, giving a laugh like an autumn cloud,

children.text: uvāca kṛtam ityeva vacanaṃ cedam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: said, "It is done," and then spoke these words:
"Therefore, O great brahman, intent on slaying <s>Vaivasvata</s>,

children.text: gacchāmi dakṣiṇām āśāṃ yatra sūryātmajo nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I am going to the southern quarter, where the king, the son of the Sun, is.

children.text: mayā hi bhagavan krodhāt pratijñātaṃ raṇārthinā
children.translated_text: For, holy sir, in anger and desiring battle, I have vowed:
'I shall subdue the four guardians of the worlds,' O lord.
For that reason I have set out toward the city of the king of the ancestors;
I shall yoke with death the maker of suffering for living beings."

children.text: evam uktvā daśagrīvo muniṃ tam abhivādya ca
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Daśagrīva</s> saluted that sage

children.text: prayayau dakṣiṇām āśāṃ prahṛṣṭaiḥ saha mantribhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and went to the southern quarter with his delighted ministers.
But <s>Nārada</s>, great in splendor, entered meditation for a moment,
and the best of brahmans reflected, like a smokeless fire:
"By him the three worlds, together with <s>Indra</s> and with moving and unmoving beings, are afflicted;

children.text: kṣīṇe cāyuṣi dharme ca sa kālo hiṃsyate katham ||
children.translated_text: when lifespan and <s>dharma</s> are exhausted, how can that Time be harmed?

children.text: yasya nityaṃ trayo lokā vidravanti bhayārditāḥ
children.translated_text: He from whom the three worlds always flee, distressed by fear,
how is that lord of rākṣasas himself approaching him?

children.text: yo vidhātā ca dhātā ca sukṛte duṣkṛte yathā
children.translated_text: He who is the ordainer and the disposer of good and evil deeds as they are,

children.text: trailokyaṃ vijitaṃ yena taṃ kathaṃ nu vijeṣyati ||
children.translated_text: by whom the three worlds have been conquered--how indeed will he conquer him?

children.text: aparaṃ kiṃ nu kṛtvaivaṃ vidhānaṃ saṃvidhāsyati
children.translated_text: What further arrangement will he make after doing this?
Curiosity has arisen; I shall go to <s>Yama</s>'s abode."
Having reflected thus, the best of brahmans went with swift stride

children.text: ākhyātuṃ tad yathāvṛttaṃ yamasya sadanaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: toward <s>Yama</s>'s abode to report what had happened exactly.

children.text: apaśyat sa yamaṃ tatra devam agnipuraskṛtam
children.translated_text: There he saw the god <s>Yama</s>, with Fire before him,
attending to the dispensation appropriate to each creature.

children.text: sa tu dṛṣṭvā yamaḥ prāptaṃ maharṣiṃ tatra nāradam
children.translated_text: When <s>Yama</s> saw the great seer <s>Nārada</s> arrived there,

children.text: abravīt sukham āsīnam arghyam āvedya dharmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: he offered him arghya according to rule and spoke as he sat comfortably:

children.text: kaccit kṣemaṃ nu devarṣe kaccid dharmo na naśyati
children.translated_text: "Is all well, divine seer? Is <s>dharma</s> not perishing?
What business has brought you here, you who are attended by gods and gandharvas?"

children.text: abravīt tu tadā vākyaṃ nārado bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
children.translated_text: Then the venerable sage <s>Nārada</s> spoke these words:
"Listen; I shall tell it, and let the proper measure be taken."
This night-roamer named <s>Daśagrīva</s>, O king of the Pitṛs,
is approaching to bring under his control you, who are very hard to conquer, by his exploits.
For this reason I have come in haste, O lord;
what indeed will your staff-weapon do today?
In the meantime, from afar, like the sun arisen,

children.text: dadṛśe divyam āyāntaṃ vimānaṃ tasya rakṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the divine aerial car of that rākṣasa was seen approaching.

children.text: taṃ deśaṃ prabhayā tasya puṣpakasya mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: By the radiance of that <s>Puṣpaka</s>, the mighty one
made that whole region free of darkness and drew near.
Then the great-armed <s>Daśagrīva</s> looked here and there
and saw living beings enjoying the fruits of good deeds and also of evil deeds.
Then those who were being punished by their own evil deeds
the strong <s>Rāvaṇa</s> freed by force, through his prowess.
When the departed spirits were being released by the powerful rākṣasa,
the guardians of the dead, greatly enraged, rushed at the lord of rākṣasas.

children.text: te prāsaiḥ parighaiḥ śūlair mudgaraiḥ śaktitomaraiḥ
children.translated_text: With spears, iron clubs, tridents, maces, javelins, and lances,
heroic hundreds of thousands showered the <s>Puṣpaka</s>.
Its seats, mansions, terraces, and coverings,
those warriors quickly shattered, like bees swarming over it.
That aerial car <s>Puṣpaka</s>, which had become an abode of gods, in battle,
though being broken in that way, remained imperishable through <s>Brahmā</s>'s power.
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s ministers, according to their desire and according to their strength,

children.text: ayudhyanta mahāvīryāḥ sa ca rājā daśānanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: fought, those of great valor, and so did King <s>Daśānana</s>.
Their limbs smeared with blood, struck by every kind of weapon,
the ministers of the lord of rākṣasas made a great battle.

children.text: anyonyaṃ ca mahābhāgā jaghnuḥ praharaṇair yudhi
children.translated_text: In the fight, those illustrious ones struck one another with weapons:

children.text: yamasya ca mahat sainyaṃ rākṣasasya ca mantriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s>'s great army and the rākṣasa's counselors.
But abandoning the ministers of the rākṣasa of great power,
they rushed upon <s>Daśānana</s> himself with showers of tridents.
Then, his limbs smeared with blood and shattered by blows,
the best of rākṣasas shone in the aerial car like a flowering aśoka tree.
Spears, maces, barbed darts, javelins, lances, arrows,
clubs, stones, and trees the strong one discharged by the power of his missile.

children.text: tāṃstu sarvān samākṣipya tad astram apahatya ca
children.translated_text: But they knocked all of those aside and repelled that missile;
then the hundred thousand struck that one dreadful rākṣasa.

children.text: parivārya ca taṃ sarve śailaṃ meghotkarā iva
children.translated_text: Surrounding him all together, like masses of clouds surrounding a mountain,
with bhindipālas and tridents they left him breathless.
With his armor cast off, enraged, and drenched by streams of blood,
he abandoned the <s>Puṣpaka</s> and stood upon the earth.

children.text: tataḥ sa kārmukī bāṇī pṛthivyāṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the lord of rākṣasas, armed with bow and arrows on the ground,
having regained consciousness after a moment, stood angry like <s>Antaka</s>.

children.text: tataḥ pāśupataṃ divyam astraṃ saṃdhāya kārmuke
children.translated_text: Then, fitting the divine <s>Pāśupata</s> weapon to his bow,

children.text: tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti tān uktvā taccāpaṃ vyapakarṣata ||
children.translated_text: he said to them, 'Stand! Stand!' and drew that bow.

children.text: jvālāmālī sa tu śaraḥ kravyādānugato raṇe
children.translated_text: That arrow, wreathed in flames and followed in battle by flesh-eaters,

children.text: mukto gulmān drumāṃścaiva bhasma kṛtvā pradhāvati ||
children.translated_text: once released, rushed onward, reducing thickets and trees to ash.

children.text: te tasya tejasā dagdhāḥ sainyā vaivasvatasya tu
children.translated_text: Burned by its brilliance, the soldiers of <s>Vaivasvata</s>
fell in that battle like trees burned by a forest fire.

children.text: tataḥ sa sacivaiḥ sārdhaṃ rākṣaso bhīmavikramaḥ
children.translated_text: Then that rākṣasa of dreadful prowess, together with his counselors,
uttered a very great roar, as if shaking the earth.

children.text: sa tu tasya mahānādaṃ śrutvā vaivasvato yamaḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Yama Vaivasvata</s>, hearing that great roar of his,

children.text: śatruṃ vijayinaṃ mene svabalasya ca saṃkṣayam ||
children.translated_text: considered the enemy victorious and his own force destroyed.
Thinking his warriors slain, his eyes agitated with anger,
he quickly said to his charioteer, 'Let the chariot be brought near.'

children.text: tasya sūto rathaṃ divyam upasthāpya mahāsvanam
children.translated_text: His charioteer brought up the divine chariot with its great sound,

children.text: sthitaḥ sa ca mahātejā āruroha mahāratham ||
children.translated_text: and that greatly splendid one, standing there, mounted the great chariot.
<s>Mṛtyu</s>, holding a noose and club in his hands, stood before him,
by whom this whole triple world, with moving and unmoving beings, is drawn together to its end.
And the <s>kāladaṇḍa</s>, the staff of Time, personified, stood beside him in the chariot,
<s>Yama</s>'s divine weapon, blazing as if with splendor.
Then the three worlds were terrified, and the dwellers in heaven trembled,
when they saw angry <s>Kāla</s>, bringing fear to the three worlds.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tu te taṃ vikṛtaṃ rathaṃ mṛtyusamanvitam
children.translated_text: Seeing that misshapen chariot, accompanied by <s>Mṛtyu</s>,
bringing fear to all worlds, the counselors of the lord of rākṣasas
all, through weakness of spirit, lost consciousness and were afflicted with fear;

children.text: nātra yoddhuṃ samarthāḥ sma ityuktvā vipradudruvuḥ ||
children.translated_text: saying, 'We are not able to fight here,' they fled away in panic.

children.text: sa tu taṃ tādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvā rathaṃ lokabhayāvaham
children.translated_text: But when that rākṣasa saw such a chariot, bringing fear to the worlds,

children.text: nākṣubhyata tadā rakṣo vyathā caivāsya nābhavat ||
children.translated_text: he was not shaken then, nor did distress arise in him.
Then <s>Yama</s>, reaching <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and releasing javelins and lances,
angrily cut into the vital points of the rākṣasa.

children.text: rāvaṇastu sthitaḥ svasthaḥ śaravarṣaṃ mumoca ha
children.translated_text: But <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, standing composed, poured forth a shower of arrows
upon that chariot of <s>Vaivasvata</s>, like a cloud pouring rain.
Then, as hundreds of great javelins fell upon his broad chest,
the rākṣasa, tormented by darts, was unable to retaliate.
Thus, by many kinds of weapons from <s>Yama</s>, crusher of foes,

children.text: saptarātraṃ kṛte saṃkhye na bhagno vijito 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: in a battle fought for seven nights, he was neither broken nor conquered.
Then again there was battle between <s>Yama</s> and the rākṣasa,
both desiring victory there, neither turning back in combats.
Then the gods, together with the gandharvas, and the siddhas and supreme seers,
placing <s>Prajāpati</s> at their head, saw that battlefield.
The battle of those two became like the destruction of the worlds:

children.text: rākṣasānāṃ ca mukhyasya pretānām īśvarasya ca ||
children.translated_text: that of the chief of the rākṣasas and of the lord of the dead.
Then the lord of rākṣasas, enraged, drew his bow in the battle
and released arrows, making the sky seem completely filled.

children.text: mṛtyuṃ caturbhir viśikhaiḥ sūtaṃ saptabhir ardayat
children.translated_text: With four sharp arrows he afflicted <s>Mṛtyu</s>, and with seven the charioteer;
with a thousand arrows he quickly struck <s>Yama</s> in his vital points.
Then, suddenly, from enraged <s>Yama</s>
there issued from his mouth a breath wreathed in flames, the fire of anger.
Then the gods, dānavas, and rākṣasas saw a wonder there:

children.text: krodhajaṃ pāvakaṃ dīptaṃ didhakṣantaṃ ripor balam ||
children.translated_text: a blazing fire born of wrath, eager to burn up the enemy's army.
But <s>Mṛtyu</s>, exceedingly enraged, then said to <s>Vaivasvata</s>:

children.text: muñca māṃ deva śīghraṃ tvaṃ nihanmi samare ripum ||
children.translated_text: "Release me quickly, O god; I will kill the enemy in battle.

children.text: narakaḥ śambaro vṛtraḥ śambhuḥ kārttasvaro balī
children.translated_text: <s>Naraka</s>, <s>Śambara</s>, <s>Vṛtra</s>, <s>Śambhu</s>, mighty <s>Kārttasvara</s>,
<s>Namuci</s> and <s>Virocana</s>, and those two, <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s>,

children.text: ete cānye ca bahavo balavanto durāsadāḥ
children.translated_text: these and many others, powerful and hard to assail,
I have seen fallen by me. What concern is there over this night-roamer?

children.text: muñca māṃ sādhu dharmajña yāvad enaṃ nihanmyaham
children.translated_text: Release me, good sir, knower of <s>dharma</s>, until I kill him.

children.text: na hi kaścinmayā dṛṣṭo muhūrtam api jīvati ||
children.translated_text: For I have seen no one live even for a moment when met by me.
This is not merely my strength; this is the natural boundary:

children.text: saṃspṛṣṭo hi mayā kaścinna jīved iti niścayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the certainty is that one touched by me does not live."

children.text: etat tu vacanaṃ śrutvā dharmarājaḥ pratāpavān
children.translated_text: Hearing these words, the majestic king of <s>dharma</s>

children.text: abravīt tatra taṃ mṛtyumayam enaṃ nihanmyaham ||
children.translated_text: said there to <s>Mṛtyu</s>, "I myself will kill him."
Then the lord <s>Vaivasvata</s>, his eyes reddened and enraged,
weighed in his hand that unfailing <s>kāladaṇḍa</s>.
At its sides the snares of Time were fixed without gaps,
and a mace stood embodied there, like the touch of fire.

children.text: darśanād eva yaḥ prāṇān prāṇinām uparudhyati
children.translated_text: By the very sight of it, it obstructs the life-breaths of living beings;

children.text: kiṃ punastāḍanād vāpi pīḍanād vāpi dehinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: how much more by striking or crushing the embodied creature.
Surrounded by flames, as if drinking up the night-roamer,
that staff, touched by the hand of the mighty one, became enraged and terribly fearsome.
Then all beings fled from that battlefield,
and the gods were shaken when they saw <s>Yama</s> raising the <s>kāladaṇḍa</s>.

children.text: tasmin prahartukāme tu daṇḍam udyamya rāvaṇam
children.translated_text: But when he was about to strike <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, having lifted the staff,
<s>Pitāmaha</s> himself appeared to <s>Yama</s> and said this:
"O mighty-armed <s>Vaivasvata</s>, whose valor is unequalled,
you must not strike this night-roamer with that staff.
A boon was indeed given to him by me, O foremost of the Thirty Gods;

children.text: tat tvayā nānṛtaṃ kāryaṃ yanmayā vyāhṛtaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore the word I have spoken must not be made false by you.
For this <s>kāladaṇḍa</s>, created by me long ago with <s>Mṛtyu</s> at its head,
is unfailing in the destruction of all creatures.

children.text: tanna khalveṣa te saumya pātyo rākṣasamūrdhani
children.translated_text: Therefore, gentle one, it must not be made to fall on the rākṣasa's head.

children.text: na hyasmin patite kaścinmuhūrtam api jīvati ||
children.translated_text: For when it has fallen, no one lives even for a moment.
If, when it fell upon him, this rākṣasa did not die,
or if <s>Daśagrīva</s> did die, in either case there would be falsehood.
Restrain this staff, now raised for slaughter, from the lord of rākṣasas.

children.text: satyaṃ mama kuruṣvedaṃ lokāṃstvaṃ samavekṣya ca ||
children.translated_text: Make this word of mine true, and consider the worlds as well."
Thus addressed, righteous <s>Yama</s> then replied:

children.text: eṣa vyāvartito daṇḍaḥ prabhaviṣṇur bhavān hi naḥ ||
children.translated_text: "This staff has been turned back; for you are our lord.

children.text: kiṃ tvidānīṃ mayā śakyaṃ kartuṃ raṇagatena hi
children.translated_text: But what can now be done by me, standing in battle,
since this rākṣasa, made arrogant by his boon, is not to be killed by me?

children.text: eṣa tasmāt praṇaśyāmi darśanād asya rakṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore I now disappear from the sight of this rākṣasa."
Having said this, he vanished there together with his chariot and horses.

children.text: daśagrīvastu taṃ jitvā nāma viśrāvya cātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Daśagrīva</s>, having conquered him and made his own name famous,
departed joyfully from <s>Yama</s>'s abode in the <s>Puṣpaka</s>.
Then <s>Vaivasvata</s>, together with the gods led by <s>Brahmā</s>,
went gladly to heaven, as did the great sage <s>Nārada</s>.

children.text: sa tu jitvā daśagrīvo yamaṃ tridaśapuṃgavam
children.translated_text: Having conquered <s>Yama</s>, foremost among the Thirty Gods,
<s>Daśagrīva</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, boasting of victory, saw his own companions.
Then, congratulating those headed by <s>Mārīca</s> on the victory,

children.text: puṣpakaṃ bhejire sarve sāntvitā rāvaṇena ha ||
children.translated_text: all of them, comforted by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, resorted to the <s>Puṣpaka</s>.

children.text: tato rasātalaṃ hṛṣṭaḥ praviṣṭaḥ payaso nidhim
children.translated_text: Then, delighted, he entered <s>Rasātala</s>, the ocean's depths,
inhabited by hosts of daityas and serpents and well protected by <s>Varuṇa</s>.

children.text: sa tu bhogavatīṃ gatvā purīṃ vāsukipālitām
children.translated_text: Having gone to <s>Bhogavatī</s>, the city guarded by <s>Vāsuki</s>,

children.text: sthāpya nāgān vaśe kṛtvā yayau maṇimatīṃ purīm ||
children.translated_text: and having established the nāgas under his control, he went to the city <s>Maṇimatī</s>.
There dwelt the <s>Nivātakavaca</s> daityas, who had obtained boons.
The rākṣasa approached them and challenged them to battle.

children.text: te tu sarve suvikrāntā daiteyā balaśālinaḥ
children.translated_text: All those daityas were very valiant and strong in power;
there, armed with many kinds of weapons, they fought, maddened by battle.

children.text: teṣāṃ tu yudhyamānānāṃ sāgraḥ saṃvatsaro gataḥ
children.translated_text: As they fought, a full year with its surplus passed,

children.text: na cānyatarayostatra vijayo vā kṣayo 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: and neither side there had victory or destruction.
Then <s>Pitāmaha</s>, the imperishable god and refuge of the three worlds,
quickly came there, mounted on an excellent aerial car.
After stopping the battle-work of the <s>Nivātakavacas</s>,
the aged <s>Pitāmaha</s> spoke a word full of understood meaning:

children.text: na hyayaṃ rāvaṇo yuddhe śakyo jetuṃ surāsuraiḥ
children.translated_text: "For this <s>Rāvaṇa</s> cannot be conquered in battle by gods or asuras."

children.text: na bhavantaḥ kṣayaṃ netuṃ śakyāḥ sendraiḥ surāsuraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: You cannot be brought to destruction even by gods and asuras together with <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: rākṣasasya sakhitvaṃ vai bhavadbhiḥ saha rocate
children.translated_text: Indeed, friendship between this rākṣasa and you is pleasing.

children.text: avibhaktā hi sarvārthāḥ suhṛdāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For among friends all interests are undivided; there is no doubt about this.
Then there <s>Rāvaṇa</s> made a friendship witnessed by fire,
and at that time he became pleased in company with the <s>Nivātakavacas</s>.
Honored by them according to rule, he lived there happily for a year,
and <s>Daśānana</s> received worship no different from that in his own city.

children.text: sa tūpadhārya māyānāṃ śatam ekonam ātmavān
children.translated_text: Then that self-possessed one, having learned ninety-nine magical arts,
wandered through <s>Rasātala</s>, searching for the city of the lord of the waters.
Then there was a city named <s>Aśmanagara</s>, protected by the <s>Kālakeyas</s>;
having conquered it in a moment, he slew four hundred daityas.
Then the lord of rākṣasas saw the divine abode of <s>Varuṇa</s>,
standing like <s>Kailāsa</s>, resembling a pale white cloud.

children.text: kṣarantīṃ ca payo nityaṃ surabhiṃ gām avasthitām
children.translated_text: There he saw the cow <s>Surabhi</s> standing, constantly streaming milk,
from the outflow of whose milk there is the ocean named <s>Kṣīroda</s>.
From it the cool-rayed moon, benefactor of creatures, comes forth;
and by reaching it the supreme seers who drink foam live on.

children.text: amṛtaṃ yatra cotpannaṃ surā cāpi surāśinām ||
children.translated_text: There too amṛta was produced, and also surā for the gods who partake of it.

children.text: yāṃ bruvanti narā loke surabhiṃ nāma nāmataḥ
children.translated_text: People in the world call her by the name <s>Surabhi</s>.

children.text: pradakṣiṇaṃ tu tāṃ kṛtvā rāvaṇaḥ paramādbhutām
children.translated_text: Having circumambulated that supremely wondrous one, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>
entered a very terrible place, guarded by many kinds of forces.
Then, covered with hundreds of streams and resembling an autumn cloud,
he saw the finest house of <s>Varuṇa</s>, ever full of delight.

children.text: tato hatvā balādhyakṣān samare taiśca tāḍitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after killing the commanders and being struck by them in battle,

children.text: abravīt kva gato yo vo rājā śīghraṃ nivedyatām ||
children.translated_text: he said, "Where has your king gone? Report it quickly.
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> has come seeking battle; let battle be given to him.

children.text: vada vā na bhayaṃ te 'sti nirjito 'smīti sāñjaliḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or, with folded hands, say, 'I have been conquered; there is no fear for you.'"
At this point, the enraged sons and grandsons of great-souled <s>Varuṇa</s>

children.text: putrāḥ pautrāśca niṣkrāman gauśca puṣkara eva ca ||
children.translated_text: came out, including <s>Gau</s> and <s>Puṣkara</s>.

children.text: te tu vīryaguṇopetā balaiḥ parivṛtāḥ svakaiḥ
children.translated_text: Endowed with valor and excellence, surrounded by their own forces,
they yoked desire-moving chariots with the splendor of the rising sun.
Then a dreadful, hair-raising battle arose
between the sons of the lord of waters and <s>Rāvaṇa</s> the rākṣasa.
But by the very mighty ministers of the rākṣasa <s>Daśagrīva</s>,

children.text: vāruṇaṃ tad balaṃ kṛtsnaṃ kṣaṇena vinipātitam ||
children.translated_text: that whole force of <s>Varuṇa</s> was struck down in an instant.
Seeing their own force in battle then, the sons of <s>Varuṇa</s>,
afflicted by a net of arrows, withdrew from the work of battle.
But when those who had come down to the earth saw <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in the <s>Puṣpaka</s>,
they quickly entered the sky in swift-moving chariots.

children.text: mahad āsīt tatasteṣāṃ tulyaṃ sthānam avāpya tat
children.translated_text: Then, after they had reached the same level, there arose a great
tumultuous aerial battle, like one between gods and dānavas.
Then in battle they turned <s>Rāvaṇa</s> back
with arrows resembling fire, and, delighted, uttered various roars.

children.text: tato mahodaraḥ kruddho rājānaṃ dṛśya dharṣitam
children.translated_text: Then angry <s>Mahodara</s>, seeing the king assailed,
abandoned fear of death and, as a hero longing for battle, looked about.

children.text: tena teṣāṃ hayā ye ca kāmagāḥ pavanopamāḥ
children.translated_text: The horses of theirs that moved at will and were like the wind
were struck by <s>Mahodara</s> with his mace and went down to the earth.

children.text: teṣāṃ varuṇasūnūnāṃ hatvā yodhān hayāṃśca tān
children.translated_text: Having slain the warriors of those sons of <s>Varuṇa</s>, and those horses too,

children.text: mumocāśu mahānādaṃ virathān prekṣya tān sthitān ||
children.translated_text: he quickly released a great roar on seeing them standing without chariots.

children.text: te tu teṣāṃ rathāḥ sāśvāḥ saha sārathibhir varaiḥ
children.translated_text: Their chariots, together with the horses and with the excellent charioteers,
were slain by <s>Mahodara</s> and fell upon the surface of the earth.

children.text: te tu tyaktvā rathān putrā varuṇasya mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: But the heroic sons of great-souled <s>Varuṇa</s>, abandoning their chariots,
stood in the sky and, by their own power, were not shaken.
Stringing their bows and piercing <s>Mahodara</s>,
they angrily rushed together at <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle.

children.text: tataḥ kruddho daśagrīvaḥ kālāgnir iva viṣṭhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then angry <s>Daśagrīva</s>, standing like the fire at the end of time,
sent a very swift shower of arrows down upon their vital points.
Then various pestles, and hundreds of bhalla-arrows,
paṭṭasas, spears, śataghnīs, and javelins as well,
that hard-to-assail one, standing above them, caused to fall upon them.

children.text: atha viddhāstu te vīrā viniṣpetuḥ padātayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, pierced, those heroes fell down as foot-soldiers.

children.text: tato rakṣo mahānādaṃ muktvā hanti sma vāruṇān
children.translated_text: Then the rākṣasa released a great roar and struck the followers of <s>Varuṇa</s>
with many kinds of terrible weapons, like a cloud with downpours of rain.
Then all of them, turned back and fallen on the earth,
were quickly led from the battlefield by their own men into their houses.

children.text: tān abravīt tato rakṣo varuṇāya nivedyatām
children.translated_text: Then the rākṣasa said to them, "Let this be reported to <s>Varuṇa</s>."
And a minister of <s>Varuṇa</s> named <s>Prabhāsa</s> spoke to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>:
"The lord of waters, of great splendor, has indeed gone to <s>Brahmaloka</s>;

children.text: gāndharvaṃ varuṇaḥ śrotuṃ yaṃ tvam āhvayase yudhi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Varuṇa</s>, whom you challenge in battle, has gone to hear gandharva music.

children.text: tat kiṃ tava vṛthā vīra pariśrāmya gate nṛpe
children.translated_text: So why, hero, do you weary yourself in vain when the king has gone away?

children.text: ye tu saṃnihitā vīrāḥ kumārāste parājitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But the heroes who were present here, the princes, have been defeated."
Hearing that, the lord of rākṣasas made his own name proclaimed,
and, releasing a roar from joy, went out from <s>Varuṇa</s>'s abode.

children.text: āgatastu pathā yena tenaiva vinivṛtya saḥ
children.translated_text: Having come by the path by which he had arrived, he turned back by that very path;
the rākṣasa went through the sky, facing toward <s>Laṅkā</s>.
As he was returning, that evil-minded <s>Rāvaṇa</s> was delighted.
On the road he carried off maidens of kings, sages, gods, and gandharvas.

children.text: darśanīyāṃ hi yāṃ rakṣaḥ kanyāṃ strīṃ vātha paśyati
children.translated_text: For whatever beautiful rākṣasa maiden, girl, or woman he saw,
after killing her kinsmen, he placed her in the aerial car.
There, from among pannagas, yakṣas, humans, and rākṣasas,

children.text: daityānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca kanyā jagrāha rāvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s> seized the daughters of daityas and dānavas as well.
They were long-haired, very lovely-limbed, with faces like the full moon;
all were young, overcome by grief, and bent by the weight of their breasts.
There, like flames of fire, born from the fire of grief and fear,
trembling and afflicted with sorrow, they shed water born of tears.
As they sighed, by the breaths of those women
the <s>Puṣpaka</s>, with fire shut within, shone like an agnihotra fire.

children.text: kācid dadhyau suduḥkhārtā hanyād api hi mām ayam
children.translated_text: One woman, deeply afflicted with sorrow, thought, "This man may even kill me."

children.text: smṛtvā mātṝḥ pitṝn bhrātṝn putrān vai śvaśurān api
children.translated_text: Remembering their mothers, fathers, brothers, sons, and even fathers-in-law,
the women, filled with grief and sorrow, lamented together.

children.text: kathaṃ nu khalu me putraḥ kariṣyati mayā vinā
children.translated_text: "How indeed will my son fare without me?

children.text: kathaṃ mātā kathaṃ bhrātā nimagnāḥ śokasāgare ||
children.translated_text: How will my mother, how will my brother, sunk in the ocean of grief?

children.text: hā kathaṃ nu kariṣyāmi bhartāraṃ daivataṃ vinā
children.translated_text: Ah, how indeed shall I live without my husband, my divinity?

children.text: mṛtyo prasīda yāce tvāṃ naya māṃ yamasādanam ||
children.translated_text: O Death, be gracious; I beg you, take me to the abode of <s>Yama</s>.

children.text: kiṃ nu me duṣkṛtaṃ karma kṛtaṃ dehāntare purā
children.translated_text: What evil deed did I do before in another body,
that I have now been violated by this man and fallen into an ocean of grief?
Now I see no end here to my own suffering.
Alas, shame on human worlds; surely there is nothing lower.

children.text: yad durbalā balavatā bāndhavā rāvaṇena me
children.translated_text: For my weak kinsmen were destroyed by the strong <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
like stars by the sun as soon as it has risen.
Alas, the very powerful rākṣasa delights in methods of killing.

children.text: aho durvṛttam ātmānaṃ svayam eva na budhyate ||
children.translated_text: Alas, he does not himself understand his own wicked self.
In every way the valor of this evil-minded one is at least fitting;
but this act, the touching of another's wives, is unfitting.

children.text: yasmād eṣa parakyāsu strīṣu rajyati durmatiḥ
children.translated_text: Since this evil-minded one delights in other men's women,
therefore <s>Rāvaṇa</s> will meet death through a woman alone."

children.text: śaptaḥ strībhiḥ sa tu tadā hatatejāḥ suniṣprabhaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, cursed by the women, he became bereft of splendor and very dim,
cursed by chaste and virtuous wives who stood on the path of virtue.
While they were lamenting in this way, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of rākṣasas,
entered the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>, honored by the night-wanderers.
Then the sister of the king of rākṣasas, deeply distressed,
fell at his feet and began to speak.
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s> raised up his sister and, consoling her,

children.text: abravīt kim idaṃ bhadre vaktum arhasi me drutam ||
children.translated_text: said, "What is this, good lady? You should tell me quickly."
She, the rākṣasī, with eyes choked by tears, spoke these words:
"I am slain, O king; I have been made a widow by you, the mighty one.

children.text: ete vīryāt tvayā rājan daityā vinihatā raṇe
children.translated_text: By your valor, O king, these daityas have been slain in battle,
known as the <s>Kālakaeyas</s>, of great strength and prowess.

children.text: tatra me nihato bhartā garīyāñjīvitād api
children.translated_text: There my husband, dearer even than life, was killed,

children.text: sa tvayā dayitastatra bhrātrā śatrusamena vai ||
children.translated_text: that beloved one, by you there, by a brother who was like an enemy.

children.text: yā tvayāsmi hatā rājan svayam eveha bandhunā
children.translated_text: I, O king, have been killed by you, here by my own kinsman;

children.text: duḥkhaṃ vaidhavyaśabdaṃ ca dattaṃ bhokṣyāmyahaṃ tvayā ||
children.translated_text: by you I have been given sorrow and the name of widowhood to endure.

children.text: nanu nāma tvayā rakṣyo jāmātā samareṣvapi
children.translated_text: Surely your son-in-law should have been protected by you, even in battles.

children.text: taṃ nihatya raṇe rājan svayam eva na lajjase ||
children.translated_text: Having killed him in battle, O king, are you not ashamed of yourself?"
Thus addressed by his sister, who was crying out, the rākṣasa

children.text: abravīt sāntvayitvā tāṃ sāmapūrvam idaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: spoke this conciliatory speech to her after comforting her:

children.text: alaṃ vatse viṣādena na bhetavyaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: "Enough, child, with grief; there is no need to fear in any way.
I will always satisfy you with special honors and gifts.
In battle I was careless, distracted, longing for victory, and shooting arrows;

children.text: nāvagacchāmi yuddheṣu svān parān vāpyahaṃ śubhe
children.translated_text: in battles, good lady, I do not recognize my own people or enemies.

children.text: tenāsau nihataḥ saṃkhye mayā bhartā tava svasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For that reason your husband, sister, was killed by me in combat.

children.text: asmin kāle tu yat prāptaṃ tat kariṣyāmi te hitam
children.translated_text: But at this time I shall do for you whatever good is possible.
Stay beside <s>Khara</s>, your brother, established in sovereignty.
Your brother will be lord over fourteen thousand

children.text: prabhuḥ prayāṇe dāne ca rākṣasānāṃ mahaujasām ||
children.translated_text: rākṣasas of great energy, in expeditions and distributions.

children.text: tatra mātṛṣvasuḥ putro bhrātā tava kharaḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: There your kinsman, your brother <s>Khara</s>, as lord,

children.text: bhaviṣyati sadā kurvan yad vakṣyasi vacaḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: will always carry out whatever command you yourself speak.
Let this hero go quickly to protect the <s>Daṇḍakas</s>;
the very mighty <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> will be his commander of forces.

children.text: sa hi śapto vanoddeśaḥ kruddhenośanasā purā
children.translated_text: For that region of forest was cursed long ago by angry <s>Uśanas</s>;

children.text: rākṣasānām ayaṃ vāso bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: it will, without doubt, become the dwelling place of rākṣasas."

children.text: evam uktvā daśagrīvaḥ sainyaṃ tasyādideśa ha
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Daśagrīva</s> then assigned his army to him:
fourteen thousand rākṣasas who could assume forms at will.

children.text: sa taiḥ sarvaiḥ parivṛto rākṣasair ghoradarśanaiḥ
children.translated_text: Surrounded by all those rākṣasas of dreadful appearance,
<s>Khara</s> quickly set out for the <s>Daṇḍakas</s>, fearing nothing.
There he made the kingdom free of enemies,

children.text: sā ca śūrpaṇakhā prītā nyavasad daṇḍakāvane ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>, pleased, dwelt in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest.

children.text: sa tu dattvā daśagrīvo vanaṃ ghoraṃ kharasya tat
children.translated_text: But <s>Daśagrīva</s>, having given that dreadful forest to <s>Khara</s>,
and having reassured his sister, became glad and more at ease.

children.text: tato nikumbhilā nāma laṅkāyāḥ kānanaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: Then there was a great grove of <s>Laṅkā</s> named <s>Nikumbhilā</s>;
the great-souled lord of rākṣasas entered it with his attendants.
There it was strewn with hundreds of sacrificial posts and adorned with pleasant shrines

children.text: dadarśa viṣṭhitaṃ yajñaṃ saṃpradīptam iva śriyā ||
children.translated_text: He saw the sacrifice spread out, as if blazing with splendor.
Then, wearing a black antelope skin and marked by water-pot, topknot, and banner,
he saw his own son there, <s>Meghanāda</s>, the subduer of enemies.
The lord of the rākṣasas approached him and embraced him with his arms,

children.text: abravīt kim idaṃ vatsa vartate tad bravīhi me ||
children.translated_text: and said, "What is this, child, that is going on? Tell me that."
But there <s>Uśanas</s>, the teacher, spoke for the success of the sacrifice
to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, best of rākṣasas; that best of twice-born sages was greatly austere.

children.text: aham ākhyāmi te rājañśrūyatāṃ sarvam eva ca
children.translated_text: "I shall explain it to you, king; let everything be heard in full.
Seven sacrifices, very extensive, have been accomplished by your son.
The <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, the <s>Aśvamedha</s>, and the sacrifice rich in much gold,
the <s>Rājasūya</s> sacrifice, likewise the <s>Gomedha</s>, and the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>.

children.text: māheśvare pravṛtte tu yajñe puṃbhiḥ sudurlabhe
children.translated_text: And when the <s>Māheśvara</s> sacrifice, very hard for men to attain, had begun,

children.text: varāṃste labdhavān putraḥ sākṣāt paśupater iha ||
children.translated_text: your son received boons here directly from <s>Paśupati</s> himself.
A divine chariot that moves at will, surely traveling through the mid-air,

children.text: māyāṃ ca tāmasīṃ nāma yayā sampadyate tamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and a magic power named <s>Tāmasī</s>, by which darkness comes into being.
By this magic power, lord of rākṣasas, in battle,

children.text: prayuddhasya gatiḥ śakyā na hi jñātuṃ surāsuraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the course of one who is fighting cannot be known by gods or asuras.
Inexhaustible quivers with arrows, and a bow very hard to conquer,

children.text: astraṃ ca balavat saumya śatruvidhvaṃsanaṃ raṇe ||
children.translated_text: and a powerful missile, gentle one, that destroys enemies in battle.
Having obtained all these boons, this son of yours, <s>Daśānana</s>,
today, at the completion of the sacrifice, stood waiting for you."

children.text: tato 'bravīd daśagrīvo na śobhanam idaṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Daśagrīva</s> said, "This has not been well done,
since enemies, with <s>Indra</s> foremost, have been honored with sacrificial substances.

children.text: ehīdānīṃ kṛtaṃ yaddhi tad akartuṃ na śakyate
children.translated_text: Come now. What has been done cannot be made undone.

children.text: āgaccha saumya gacchāmaḥ svam eva bhavanaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: Come, gentle one; let us go to our own palace."
Then <s>Daśagrīva</s>, going there with his son and with <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,
caused all those women, overwhelmed by tears, to alight.
They were lovely, jewels among the gods, dānavas, and rākṣasas,
endowed with many ornaments and blazing with their own radiance.
But righteous <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, seeing those women overcome with grief,

children.text: tasya tāṃ ca matiṃ jñātvā dharmātmā vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: and knowing that intention of his, spoke these words:
"By such conduct as this, destructive of fame, wealth, and family,
you act according to your own whim after inflicting violation upon living beings.
After dishonoring kinswomen, these excellent women have been brought by you;

children.text: tvām atikramya madhunā rājan kumbhīnasī hṛtā ||
children.translated_text: but, king, <s>Kumbhīnasī</s> has been carried off by <s>Madhu</s>, overstepping you.
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s> spoke these words: "I do not understand what this is.

children.text: ko vāyaṃ yastvayākhyāto madhur ityeva nāmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Who is this one whom you have named simply <s>Madhu</s>?"
But <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, angered, spoke these words to his brother:

children.text: śrūyatām asya pāpasya karmaṇaḥ phalam āgatam ||
children.translated_text: "Listen; the fruit of this sinner's deed has come upon us.
There is the eldest brother of our maternal grandfather, of <s>Sumālin</s>,
a night-wanderer famed as <s>Mālyavān</s>, old and wise.
Being older than our father and our mother, he was our venerable elder.
He had a daughter's daughter named <s>Kumbhīnasī</s>.
That maiden, born from <s>Anala</s>, was the daughter of our maternal aunt,

children.text: bhavatyasmākam eṣā vai bhrātṝṇāṃ dharmataḥ svasā ||
children.translated_text: and by <s>dharma</s> she is indeed the sister of us brothers.

children.text: sā hṛtā madhunā rājan rākṣasena balīyasā
children.translated_text: She has been carried off, king, by the powerful rākṣasa <s>Madhu</s>,
while your son was engaged in sacrifice and while I was staying within the water.
After killing the foremost rākṣasas, your trusted ministers,

children.text: dharṣayitvā hṛtā rājan guptā hyantaḥpure tava ||
children.translated_text: she was seized and carried off, king, though guarded in your inner palace.

children.text: śrutvā tvetanmahārāja kṣāntam eva hato na saḥ
children.translated_text: On hearing this, great king, it was merely endured; he was not killed,

children.text: yasmād avaśyaṃ dātavyā kanyā bhartre hi dātṛbhiḥ
children.translated_text: because a maiden must necessarily be given by her givers to her husband.

children.text: asminn evābhisamprāptaṃ loke viditam astu te ||
children.translated_text: Let it be known to you that this is the accepted rule in this world."
Then <s>Daśagrīva</s>, enraged, his eyes reddened, said,

children.text: kalpyatāṃ me rathaḥ śīghraṃ śūrāḥ sajjībhavantu ca ||
children.translated_text: "Let my chariot be made ready quickly, and let the heroes arm themselves.

children.text: bhrātā me kumbhakarṇaśca ye ca mukhyā niśācarāḥ
children.translated_text: Let my brother <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> and the chief night-wanderers
mount their vehicles, bearing weapons and arms of many kinds.

children.text: adya taṃ samare hatvā madhuṃ rāvaṇanirbhayam
children.translated_text: Today, after killing that <s>Madhu</s>, who has no fear of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, in battle,
I shall go to <s>Indraloka</s>, longing for war and surrounded by my friends.

children.text: tato vijitya tridivaṃ vaśe sthāpya puraṃdaram
children.translated_text: Then, having conquered heaven and brought <s>Puraṃdara</s> under my control,
I shall sport in contentment, splendid with sovereignty over the three worlds."
Four thousand fierce akṣauhiṇīs of rākṣasas,
bearing weapons of many kinds, swiftly set out, longing for battle.

children.text: indrajit tvagrataḥ sainyaṃ sainikān parigṛhya ca
children.translated_text: <s>Indrajit</s> was at the front of the army, taking the soldiers with him;
heroic <s>Rāvaṇa</s> was in the middle, and <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> at the rear.
But righteous <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> remained in <s>Laṅkā</s>, practicing <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: te tu sarve mahābhāgā yayur madhupuraṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: All those great-souled ones went toward <s>Madhupura</s>.

children.text: rathair nāgaiḥ kharair uṣṭrair hayair dīptair mahoragaiḥ
children.translated_text: With chariots, elephants, asses, camels, shining horses, and great serpents,
all the rākṣasas went, making the sky without any gap.
And hundreds of daityas there, who had made enmity with the gods,
seeing <s>Rāvaṇa</s> going, followed after him from behind.

children.text: sa tu gatvā madhupuraṃ praviśya ca daśānanaḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Daśānana</s>, having gone to <s>Madhupura</s> and entered it,

children.text: na dadarśa madhuṃ tatra bhaginīṃ tatra dṛṣṭavān ||
children.translated_text: did not see <s>Madhu</s> there; he saw his sister there.

children.text: sā prahvā prāñjalir bhūtvā śirasā pādayor gatā
children.translated_text: She became bowed down, with joined palms, and went with her head to the feet
of that king of rākṣasas: his sister <s>Kumbhīnasī</s>, terrified.

children.text: tāṃ samutthāpayāmāsa na bhetavyam iti bruvan
children.translated_text: He raised her up, saying, "You must not be afraid."

children.text: rāvaṇo rākṣasaśreṣṭhaḥ kiṃ cāpi karavāṇi te ||
children.translated_text: I am <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, best of the rākṣasas. What may I do for you?

children.text: sābravīd yadi me rājan prasannastvaṃ mahābala
children.translated_text: She said, "If you are pleased with me, O king, mighty one,

children.text: bhartāraṃ na mamehādya hantum arhasi mānada ||
children.translated_text: you ought not to kill my husband here today, giver of honor.

children.text: satyavāg bhava rājendra mām avekṣasva yācatīm
children.translated_text: Be true to your word, king of kings; look upon me as I beg.

children.text: tvayā hyuktaṃ mahābāho na bhetavyam iti svayam ||
children.translated_text: For you yourself, mighty-armed one, have said, 'There is no need to be afraid.'"
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s> boldly said to his sister, who was standing there,

children.text: kva cāsau tava bhartā vai mama śīghraṃ nivedyatām ||
children.translated_text: "Where is that husband of yours? Let him be quickly pointed out to me.

children.text: saha tena gamiṣyāmi suralokaṃ jayāya vai
children.translated_text: Together with him I shall go to conquer the world of the gods.
Out of compassion and affection for you, I have turned back from killing <s>Madhu</s>."

children.text: ityuktā sā prasuptaṃ taṃ samutthāpya niśācaram
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, she woke that night-ranging one from sleep
and, as though greatly delighted, the rākṣasī spoke to the very wise one:

children.text: eṣa prāpto daśagrīvo mama bhrātā niśācaraḥ
children.translated_text: "This <s>Daśagrīva</s>, my brother, the night-ranger, has arrived.
Desiring to conquer the world of the gods, he also chooses you as an ally.

children.text: tad asya tvaṃ sahāyārthaṃ sabandhur gaccha rākṣasa
children.translated_text: Therefore, rākṣasa, go with your kinsmen for the sake of helping him.
It is fitting to act for the benefit of one who is affectionate and seeks your alliance."

children.text: tasyāstad vacanaṃ śrutvā tathetyāha madhur vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing those words of hers, <s>Madhu</s> answered, "So be it."
Approaching according to propriety, he saw the best of the rākṣasas.
He duly honored <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the lord of the rākṣasas.
The powerful <s>Daśagrīva</s>, having received honor in <s>Madhu</s>'s house,
stayed there for one night and then began to depart.
Then, reaching <s>Kailāsa</s>, the mountain abode of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>,
the lord of the rākṣasas, like <s>Mahendra</s>, encamped his army.

children.text: sa tu tatra daśagrīvaḥ saha sainyena vīryavān
children.translated_text: There the powerful <s>Daśagrīva</s>, together with his army,
when the sun had set, arranged a resting place.
When the spotless moon had risen, with a splendor like that of a mountain,
he saw the beauties there, adorned by the moon's rays:
divine groves of karṇikāra trees and dense kadamba thickets,
blooming lotus-ponds, and the waters of the <s>Mandākinī</s>.
A sweet sound was heard, like the ringing of bells,
from companies of apsarases singing in the abode of <s>Dhanada</s>.
The trees, shaken by the wind and releasing showers of flowers,
seemed to perfume that mountain with the scents of spring and early summer.
Taking up an abundant fragrance mingled with the pollen of spring flowers,
a pleasant wind blew, increasing <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s desire.

children.text: geyāt puṣpasamṛddhyā ca śaityād vāyor guṇair gireḥ
children.translated_text: Because of the singing, the abundance of flowers, the coolness of the wind, and the qualities of the mountain,
and because night had begun and the moon had risen,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, of very great valor, came under the power of the arrows of <s>Kāma</s>.
Sighing again and again, he gazed at the moon.
At that moment, adorned there with divine flowers,
<s>Rambhā</s>, foremost among all the apsarases, with a face like the full moon,
wearing fresh ornaments and festive flowers of the six seasons,
and wrapped in a blue garment resembling a rain-laden cloud,

children.text: yasyā vaktraṃ śaśinibhaṃ bhruvau cāpanibhe śubhe
children.translated_text: whose face was like the moon and whose two lovely eyebrows were like bows,
whose thighs had the form of elephants' trunks and whose hands were soft as young shoots,
was noticed by <s>Rāvaṇa</s> as she passed through the middle of the army.
Rising up, the lord of rākṣasas, tormented by the force of <s>Kāma</s>'s arrows,
seized her hand as she was going and, smiling, addressed her:

children.text: kva gacchasi varārohe kāṃ siddhiṃ bhajase svayam
children.translated_text: "Where are you going, lovely-hipped one? What fulfillment do you seek for yourself?
Whose time of good fortune has now arrived, he who will enjoy you?
Of the nectar of your mouth today, fragrant with lotus and blue lotus,
like the immortal sweetness of ambrosia, who today will attain satisfaction?
O timid one, these two full, beautiful breasts of yours, like golden jars and set close together,
will grant contact with the chest of whom?
Who today will mount your broad, gold-girdled
heaven embodied in your hips, resembling a golden disk?

children.text: madviśiṣṭaḥ pumān ko 'nyaḥ śakro viṣṇur athāśvinau
children.translated_text: What other man is superior to me: <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, or the <s>Aśvins</s>?

children.text: mām atītya hi yasya tvaṃ yāsi bhīru na śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: It is not fitting, timid one, that you go to someone else after passing me by.

children.text: viśrama tvaṃ pṛthuśroṇi śilātalam idaṃ śubham
children.translated_text: Rest, broad-hipped one; this stone slab is lovely.

children.text: trailokye yaḥ prabhuścaiva tulyo mama na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: In the three worlds there is no lord equal to me.

children.text: tad eṣa prāñjaliḥ prahvo yācate tvāṃ daśānanaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore this <s>Daśānana</s>, with joined palms and bowed low, begs you.

children.text: yaḥ prabhuścāpi bhartā ca trailokyasya bhajasva mām ||
children.translated_text: Choose me, who am both lord and master of the three worlds."
Thus addressed, <s>Rambhā</s>, trembling and with joined palms, said,

children.text: prasīda nārhase vaktum īdṛśaṃ tvaṃ hi me guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Be gracious. You ought not to speak in this way, for you are my elder.

children.text: anyebhyo 'pi tvayā rakṣyā prāpnuyāṃ dharṣaṇaṃ yadi
children.translated_text: I should be protected by you even from others, if I were to suffer assault.

children.text: dharmataśca snuṣā te 'haṃ tattvam etad bravīmi te ||
children.translated_text: And according to dharma I am your daughter-in-law; I tell you this truth."
<s>Daśagrīva</s> spoke to her as she stood with her face lowered toward his feet:

children.text: sutasya yadi me bhāryā tatastvaṃ me snuṣā bhaveḥ ||
children.translated_text: "If you were my son's wife, then you would be my daughter-in-law."

children.text: bāḍham ityeva sā rambhā prāha rāvaṇam uttaram
children.translated_text: <s>Rambhā</s> answered <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, saying emphatically, "Indeed so.
According to dharma I am your son's wife, bull among rākṣasas.

children.text: putraḥ priyataraḥ prāṇair bhrātur vaiśravaṇasya te
children.translated_text: The son, dearer than life, of your brother <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>,
who is famed in the three worlds as <s>Nalakūbara</s>,

children.text: dharmato yo bhaved vipraḥ kṣatriyo vīryato bhavet
children.translated_text: who by dharma would be a brahmin and by valor would be a kṣatriya,

children.text: krodhād yaśca bhaved agniḥ kṣāntyā ca vasudhāsamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: who by wrath would be fire and by patience equal to the earth,
to him, the son of a world-protector, I have been pledged by arrangement.

children.text: tam uddiśya ca me sarvaṃ vibhūṣaṇam idaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: And with him in mind all this adornment of mine has been made."

children.text: yasya tasya hi nānyasya bhāvo māṃ prati tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: For my feeling is fixed toward him, and toward no one else.
By that truth, O king, subduer of enemies, you ought to release me.

children.text: sa hi tiṣṭhati dharmātmā sāmprataṃ matsamutsukaḥ
children.translated_text: He, righteous-souled, is even now waiting, longing for me.

children.text: tanna vighnaṃ sutasyeha kartum arhasi muñca mām ||
children.translated_text: Therefore you should not make an obstacle here for your son; release me.
Follow the path practiced by the good, O foremost of rākṣasas.

children.text: mānanīyo mayā hi tvaṃ lālanīyā tathāsmi te ||
children.translated_text: For you are to be honored by me, and likewise I am to be cherished by you.

children.text: evaṃ bruvāṇāṃ rambhāṃ tāṃ dharmārthasahitaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: As <s>Rambhā</s> spoke these words, joined with <s>dharma</s> and purpose,

children.text: nirbhartsya rākṣaso mohāt pratigṛhya balād balī
children.translated_text: the powerful rākṣasa, from delusion, reviled her and seized her by force.
Enraged by the delusion of desire, he set about sexual assault.
Then <s>Rambhā</s>, released by him, with her garlands and ornaments fallen away,
became distressed like a river churned up by the sport of lordly elephants.
Trembling, ashamed, frightened, and with hands joined in supplication,
she approached <s>Nalakūbara</s> and fell down at his feet.

children.text: tadavasthāṃ ca tāṃ dṛṣṭvā mahātmā nalakūbaraḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing her in that condition, the great-souled <s>Nalakūbara</s>

children.text: abravīt kim idaṃ bhadre pādayoḥ patitāsi me ||
children.translated_text: said, What is this, good lady? Why have you fallen at my feet?

children.text: sā tu niśvasamānā ca vepamānātha sāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: Then she, sighing, trembling, and with folded hands,
began to tell him everything exactly as it had happened.

children.text: eṣa deva daśagrīvaḥ prāpto gantuṃ triviṣṭapam
children.translated_text: Lord, this <s>Daśagrīva</s> has arrived, intending to go to <s>Triviṣṭapa</s>.
With the support of his army, he is passing the night here.
As I was coming toward your presence, O subduer of enemies, I was seen by him.

children.text: gṛhītvā tena pṛṣṭāsmi kasya tvam iti rakṣasā ||
children.translated_text: He seized me, and I was asked by that rākṣasa, Whose are you?

children.text: mayā tu sarvaṃ yat satyaṃ taddhi tasmai niveditam
children.translated_text: I told him all that was true, all of it,
but, his mind overcome by the delusion of desire, he did not listen to my words.

children.text: yācyamāno mayā deva snuṣā te 'ham iti prabho
children.translated_text: Though I begged him, lord, saying, I am your daughter-in-law, master,

children.text: tat sarvaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā balāt tenāsmi dharṣitā ||
children.translated_text: he put all that behind him, and by force I was violated by him.

children.text: evaṃ tvam aparādhaṃ me kṣantum arhasi mānada
children.translated_text: Thus you ought to forgive this offense of mine, giver of honor.

children.text: na hi tulyaṃ balaṃ saumya striyāśca puruṣasya ca ||
children.translated_text: For, gentle one, the strength of a woman and of a man is not equal.
Hearing this, the son of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> then became enraged.

children.text: dharṣaṇāṃ tāṃ parāṃ śrutvā dhyānaṃ sampraviveśa ha ||
children.translated_text: Hearing of that supreme violation, he entered into meditation.

children.text: tasya tat karma vijñāya tadā vaiśravaṇātmajaḥ
