children.translated_text: Then the son of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, having learned of that act of his,
after a moment, his eyes copper-red with anger, took water in his hand.
Taking the divine water and sipping it according to rule,
he then pronounced a terrible curse against the lord of rākṣasas.

children.text: akāmā tena yasmāt tvaṃ balād bhadre pradharṣitā
children.translated_text: Because, good lady, you were unwilling and were violated by him by force,

children.text: tasmāt sa yuvatīm anyāṃ nākāmām upayāsyati ||
children.translated_text: therefore he shall not approach any other unwilling young woman.
Whenever, maddened by desire, he violates an unwilling woman,

children.text: mūrdhā tu saptadhā tasya śakalībhavitā tadā ||
children.translated_text: at that very time his head shall split into seven pieces.
When that curse, bright as blazing fire, had been uttered,
the divine drums sounded, and a shower of flowers fell from the sky.
All the gods, with <s>Prajāpati</s> at their head, rejoiced,

children.text: jñātvā lokagatiṃ sarvāṃ tasya mṛtyuṃ ca rakṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: knowing the whole course of the world and the death of that rākṣasa.

children.text: śrutvā tu sa daśagrīvastaṃ śāpaṃ romaharṣaṇam
children.translated_text: But when <s>Daśagrīva</s> heard that hair-raising curse,
he no longer found pleasure in sexual intent toward unwilling women.
Then <s>Daśagrīva</s>, together with the rākṣasas, crossed <s>Kailāsa</s>.
The night-wanderer of great splendor reached <s>Indraloka</s>.
As that army of rākṣasas approached from every side,
a sound like a breaking ocean went up to the world of the gods.

children.text: śrutvā tu rāvaṇaṃ prāptam indraḥ saṃcalitāsanaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that <s>Rāvaṇa</s> had arrived, <s>Indra</s>, his seat shaken,

children.text: abravīt tatra tān devān sarvān eva samāgatān ||
children.translated_text: spoke there to all those gods who had assembled.
To the <s>Ādityas</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, the <s>Viśvas</s>, the <s>Sādhyas</s>, and the hosts of <s>Maruts</s>, he said,
Arm yourselves for battle against evil-minded <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: evam uktāstu śakreṇa devāḥ śakrasamā yudhi
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Śakra</s>, the gods, equal to <s>Śakra</s> in battle,
those great beings, eager for war, put on their armor.

children.text: sa tu dīnaḥ paritrasto mahendro rāvaṇaṃ prati
children.translated_text: But <s>Mahendra</s>, distressed and terrified on account of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: viṣṇoḥ samīpam āgatya vākyam etad uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: came near to <s>Viṣṇu</s> and spoke this statement.
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, what shall we do, O one of great strength and valor?

children.text: asau hi balavān rakṣo yuddhārtham abhivartate ||
children.translated_text: For that powerful rākṣasa is advancing for battle.
He is powerful because of the granting of a boon, not indeed for any other reason.

children.text: tacca satyaṃ hi kartavyaṃ vākyaṃ deva prajāpateḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that word of <s>Prajāpati</s>, O god, must indeed be made true.

children.text: tad yathā namucir vṛtro balir narakaśambarau
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as <s>Namuci</s>, <s>Vṛtra</s>, <s>Bali</s>, <s>Naraka</s>, and <s>Śambara</s>
were burned up by relying on your counsel, so do the same now.

children.text: na hyanyo deva devānām āpatsu sumahābala
children.translated_text: For, O god, O very mighty one, there is no other refuge

children.text: gatiḥ parāyaṇaṃ vāsti tvām ṛte puruṣottama ||
children.translated_text: or supreme resort for the gods in calamities apart from you, O highest person.

children.text: tvaṃ hi nārāyaṇaḥ śrīmān padmanābhaḥ sanātanaḥ
children.translated_text: For you are glorious <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, eternal <s>Padmanābha</s>,
and by you I have been established in the eternal kingship of the gods.

children.text: tad ākhyāhi yathātattvaṃ devadeva mama svayam
children.translated_text: Therefore tell me yourself, O god of gods, according to the truth,
whether you, with sword and discus as aids, will fight the enemy in battle.

children.text: evam uktaḥ sa śakreṇa devo nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Śakra</s> had spoken thus, the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the lord,

children.text: abravīnna paritrāsaḥ kāryaste śrūyatāṃ ca me ||
children.translated_text: said, You should not be afraid; listen to me.

children.text: na tāvad eṣa durvṛttaḥ śakyo daivatadānavaiḥ
children.translated_text: For now this wicked one cannot be slain by gods or dānavas,
when met in battle, since he is hard to conquer because of the granting of the boon.

children.text: sarvathā tu mahat karma kariṣyati balotkaṭaḥ
children.translated_text: Yet in every way this rākṣasa, swollen with strength, will perform a great deed.
With his son as ally, such is seen to be his very nature.

children.text: bravīṣi yat tu māṃ śakra saṃyuge yotsyasīti ha
children.translated_text: But as for what you say to me, <s>Śakra</s>, that I should fight in battle,
I shall certainly not fight that <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the overlord of rākṣasas.

children.text: anihatya ripuṃ viṣṇur na hi pratinivartate
children.translated_text: For <s>Viṣṇu</s> does not turn back without killing his enemy.
This wish is hard to accomplish now, since the rākṣasa has obtained a boon.
Yet I promise before you, O <s>Devendra</s>, O <s>Śatakratu</s>:
I myself shall become the cause of this rākṣasa's death.

children.text: aham enaṃ vadhiṣyāmi rāvaṇaṃ sasutaṃ yudhi
children.translated_text: I shall slay this <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, together with his son, in battle,
and I shall satisfy the deities when I know that the time has arrived.
Meanwhile, at the close of night, a roar was heard
from that army of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> fighting on every side.
Then at that time a battle arose between the gods and the rākṣasas,
terrible, with a tumultuous din, and full of many missiles and weapons.
Meanwhile, heroic rākṣasas, dreadful to behold,
rushed forward for battle at the command of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s ministers:
<s>Mārīca</s>, <s>Prahasta</s>, <s>Mahāpārśva</s>, and <s>Mahodara</s>,

children.text: akampano nikumbhaśca śukaḥ sāraṇa eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Akampana</s>, <s>Nikumbha</s>, <s>Śuka</s>, and <s>Sāraṇa</s>,
<s>Saṃhrādi</s>, <s>Dhūmaketu</s>, <s>Mahādaṃṣṭra</s>, and <s>Mahāmukha</s>,
<s>Jambumālī</s>, <s>Mahāmālī</s>, and the rākṣasa <s>Virūpākṣa</s>.
Surrounded by all these warriors of great valor,
<s>Sumālī</s>, the grandfather of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and foremost of rākṣasas, entered the army.
For he, enraged, with sharp weapons of many kinds,
was destroying all the hosts of gods together with those night-roamers.

children.text: etasminn antare śūro vasūnām aṣṭamo vasuḥ
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, a hero, the eighth Vasu among the Vasus,
renowned as <s>Sāvitra</s>, entered the great battle.

children.text: tato yuddhaṃ samabhavat surāṇāṃ rākṣasaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Then a battle took place between the gods and the rākṣasas,
against the enraged rākṣasas, famed as men who never turned back in fights.

children.text: tataste rākṣasāḥ śūrā devāṃstān samare sthitān
children.translated_text: Then those heroic rākṣasas struck the gods who stood in battle
by the hundreds of thousands with their various dreadful weapons.
But the gods, by their own splendor, sent the dreadful, mighty rākṣasas
to <s>Yama</s>'s abode in battle with various weapons.

children.text: etasminn antare śūraḥ sumālī nāma rākṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, a heroic rākṣasa named <s>Sumālī</s>,
enraged and bearing many kinds of weapons, advanced straight into the battle.

children.text: devānāṃ tad balaṃ sarvaṃ nānāpraharaṇaiḥ śitaiḥ
children.translated_text: Enraged, with sharp weapons of many kinds, he destroyed
the whole force of the gods, as wind destroys clouds.
Tormented by great showers of arrows, by spears, and by dreadful lances,

children.text: pīḍyamānāḥ surāḥ sarve na vyatiṣṭhan samāhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all the gods could not stand firm and composed.
Then, as the thirty gods were being routed by <s>Sumālī</s>,
the god <s>Sāvitra</s>, the eighth of the Vasus, stood his ground.
With his own troops around him, the greatly radiant one, by his valor,
checked in battle the night-roamer who was attacking.
Between those two, both fiercely exultant, there was a very terrible battle in the world,
between <s>Sumālī</s> and the Vasu, both men who never turned back in fights.
Then, by the great arrows of that high-souled Vasu,
his great serpent-yoked chariot was brought down in an instant.

children.text: hatvā tu saṃyuge tasya rathaṃ bāṇaśataiḥ śitaiḥ
children.translated_text: After destroying his chariot in battle with hundreds of sharp arrows,

children.text: gadāṃ tasya vadhārthāya vasur jagrāha pāṇinā ||
children.translated_text: the Vasu took a mace in his hand in order to kill him.
Quickly raising that blazing, auspicious mace, like the staff of Time,
<s>Sāvitra</s> brought it down upon <s>Sumālī</s>'s head.

children.text: tasya mūrdhani solkābhā patantī ca tadā babhau
children.translated_text: As it fell then upon his head, blazing like a meteor,
it shone like a great thunderbolt hurled by the thousand-eyed god upon a mountain.

children.text: tasya naivāsthi kāyo vā na māṃsaṃ dadṛśe tadā
children.translated_text: Then neither his bones, nor his body, nor his flesh could be seen;
struck down in that battle, he had been reduced to ashes by the mace.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā nihataṃ saṃkhye rākṣasāste samantataḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing him slain in combat, those rākṣasas on every side
all fled together, crying out with a mighty noise.
Having seen <s>Sumālī</s> slain and reduced to ashes by the Vasu,

children.text: vidrutaṃ cāpi svaṃ sainyaṃ lakṣayitvārditaṃ śaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and noticing that his own army too had fled, afflicted by arrows,

children.text: tataḥ sa balavān kruddho rāvaṇasya suto yudhi
children.translated_text: then the powerful son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, enraged in battle,
<s>Meghanāda</s> turned back all the rākṣasas and took his stand.
That great chariot-warrior, in a fire-colored chariot that moved at will,

children.text: abhidudrāva senāṃ tāṃ vanānyagnir iva jvalan ||
children.translated_text: charged at that army, blazing like fire rushing upon forests.
Then, as he entered bearing various weapons,

children.text: vidudruvur diśaḥ sarvā devāstasya ca darśanāt ||
children.translated_text: all the gods scattered in every direction at the sight of him.

children.text: na tatrāvasthitaḥ kaścid raṇe tasya yuyutsataḥ
children.translated_text: No one stood there in battle when he desired to fight.
Seeing them all scattered and terrified, <s>Śakra</s> addressed them:

children.text: na bhetavyaṃ na gantavyaṃ nivartadhvaṃ raṇaṃ prati
children.translated_text: "Do not be afraid; do not go. Turn back toward the battle.

children.text: eṣa gacchati me putro yuddhārtham aparājitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This unconquered son of mine is going forth to fight."

children.text: tataḥ śakrasuto devo jayanta iti viśrutaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the god, son of <s>Śakra</s>, renowned as <s>Jayanta</s>,
advanced to the battle in a chariot of wondrous design.
Then all those thirty gods, surrounding the son of <s>Śacī</s>,
came upon the son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle and took their stand.

children.text: teṣāṃ yuddhaṃ mahad abhūt sadṛśaṃ devarakṣasām
children.translated_text: A great battle of the gods and rākṣasas arose between them,
on behalf of the son of great <s>Indra</s> and the son of the lord of rākṣasas.
Then the rākṣasa's son loosed golden-adorned arrows
at <s>Gomukha</s>, son of <s>Mātali</s>, who was serving as charioteer.
And <s>Jayanta</s>, son of <s>Śacī</s>, likewise, enraged,

children.text: taṃ caiva rāvaṇiṃ kruddhaḥ pratyavidhyad raṇājire ||
children.translated_text: struck his charioteer and that very <s>Rāvaṇi</s> on the field of battle.
Then the rākṣasa, greatly radiant, enraged, with eyes wide open,
<s>Rāvaṇi</s> covered that son of <s>Śakra</s> with showers of arrows.

children.text: tataḥ pragṛhya śastrāṇi sāravanti mahānti ca
children.translated_text: Then, taking up weapons both solid and great,
he took śataghnīs, javelins, lances, maces, swords, and axes.
<s>Rāvaṇi</s> made very great mountain peaks fall.

children.text: tataḥ pravyathitā lokāḥ saṃjajñe ca tamo mahat
children.translated_text: Then the worlds trembled, and a great darkness arose
while that son of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> was striking down his enemies.
Then that army of the gods, on every side around that son of <s>Śacī</s>,

children.text: bahuprakāram asvasthaṃ tatra tatra sma dhāvati ||
children.translated_text: being disordered in many ways, ran here and there.
At that time they did not recognize one another, whether enemies or gods,
as they were overturned here and there and running about on every side.

children.text: etasminn antare śūraḥ pulomā nāma vīryavān
children.translated_text: Meanwhile a heroic and powerful daiteya named <s>Pulomā</s>
seized the son of <s>Śacī</s> and carried him away.

children.text: gṛhītvā taṃ tu naptāraṃ praviṣṭaḥ sa mahodadhim
children.translated_text: Having taken that grandson, he entered the great ocean,
his maternal grandfather, the venerable one through whom <s>Śacī</s> is called <s>Paulomī</s>.
Seeing the exceedingly terrible disappearance of <s>Jayanta</s>,
the gods, distressed and joyless, fled in every direction.
Then <s>Rāvaṇi</s>, delighted and surrounded by his own forces,
charged at those gods and let out a mighty roar.
Seeing the disappearance of his son and the valor of <s>Rāvaṇi</s>,
the lord of the gods said to <s>Mātali</s>, "Let the chariot be brought near."

children.text: sa tu divyo mahābhīmaḥ sajja eva mahārathaḥ
children.translated_text: That divine, very fearsome, great chariot was already prepared,
and it stood ready, driven by <s>Mātali</s>, swift as thought.
Then clouds with lightning and mighty thunder, on that chariot,
going before it and swift as wind, roared aloud at that time.
Many kinds of instruments were played, and hymns were intoned with concentration,
and companies of apsarases danced as <s>Vāsava</s> set out for battle.
Surrounded by <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Vasus</s>, <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Sādhyas</s>, and hosts of <s>Maruts</s>,
the lord of the thirty gods went forth with many kinds of weapons.
As <s>Śakra</s> went out, a harsh wind blew,
the sun became dim, and great meteors fell.
Meanwhile the heroic and mighty <s>Daśagrīva</s>
mounted a divine chariot made by <s>Viśvakarman</s>.
It was encircled by huge-bodied serpents that made the hair stand on end,
by the wind of whose breath the battle seemed to be set ablaze.
Surrounded by heroic daityas and night-roaming rākṣasas,
that divine chariot, facing battle, advanced toward great <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: putraṃ taṃ vārayitvāsau svayam eva vyavasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Having restrained that son, he himself took his position;
and <s>Rāvaṇi</s> too withdrew from the battle and sat down.

children.text: tato yuddhaṃ pravṛttaṃ tu surāṇāṃ rākṣasaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Then battle began between the gods and the rākṣasas,
a terrible showering of weapons, like clouds in combat.
But wicked-souled <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, raising many kinds of weapons,
could not be recognized in battle as fighting with anyone in particular.
With his teeth, his arms, and his feet, and with spears, javelins, and arrows,
enraged, he struck the gods with whatever came to hand.
Then the night-roamer fought with the greatly fortunate <s>Rudras</s>
together with the <s>Ādityas</s>, and in battle he was continually cut by their weapons.
Then that whole rākṣasa army, by the thirty gods together with the hosts of <s>Maruts</s>,
was put to flight in battle with various sharp weapons.

children.text: kecid vinihatāḥ śastrair veṣṭanti sma mahītale
children.translated_text: Some, slain by weapons, writhed on the ground,
while others, stuck fast on their mounts, remained standing in the battle.
Chariots, elephants, donkeys, camels, serpents, horses,
śiṃśumāras, boars, and beings with the faces of piśācas:

children.text: tān samāliṅgya bāhubhyāṃ viṣṭabdhāḥ kecid ucchritāḥ
children.translated_text: embracing these with their arms, some stood rigid and upright,
and the night-roamers, pierced through by the gods' weapons, died.
That turmoil of battle among them appeared like a painted scene,
with the slain and maddened rākṣasas lying on the ground.
Pouring streams of blood as its water and crowded with herons and vultures,
a river with weapons for crocodiles began to flow at the front of battle.
Meanwhile the heroic and mighty <s>Daśagrīva</s>, enraged,

children.text: nirīkṣya tad balaṃ sarvaṃ daivatair vinipātitam ||
children.translated_text: saw that whole army being struck down by the gods.
He swiftly plunged into that swelling ocean of troops,
and, slaying the thirty gods in battle, advanced directly toward <s>Śakra</s>.
Then <s>Śakra</s> drew his great bow with a tremendous sound,

children.text: yasya visphāraghoṣeṇa svananti sma diśo daśa ||
children.translated_text: by the twang of which the ten directions resounded.
Drawing that great bow, <s>Indra</s> loosed arrows onto <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s head,
arrows with the brilliance of fire and the sun.
Likewise mighty-armed <s>Daśagrīva</s> stood firm
and covered <s>Śakra</s> with showers of arrows released from his bow.
As those two fought, with showers of arrows on every side,

children.text: nājñāyata tadā kiṃcit sarvaṃ hi tamasā vṛtam ||
children.translated_text: nothing at all could be discerned then, for everything was covered with darkness.
Then, when that darkness had arisen, the rākṣasas along with the gods,
mad with strength, fought on, slaughtering one another.
Then, by the army of the gods, the great force of the rākṣasas

children.text: daśāṃśaṃ sthāpitaṃ yuddhe śeṣaṃ nītaṃ yamakṣayam ||
children.translated_text: was reduced in battle to a tenth, while the rest was sent to destruction in <s>Yama</s>'s realm.

children.text: tasmiṃstu tamasā naddhe sarve te devarākṣasāḥ
children.translated_text: But when all those gods and rākṣasas were bound in darkness,
they did not recognize one another as they fought each other.
<s>Indra</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, and mighty <s>Rāvaṇi</s>

children.text: tasmiṃstamojālavṛte moham īyur na te trayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: all three fell into bewilderment in that net of darkness.

children.text: sa tu dṛṣṭvā balaṃ sarvaṃ nihataṃ rāvaṇo raṇe
children.translated_text: But when <s>Rāvaṇa</s> saw that the whole army had been slain in battle,

children.text: krodham abhyāgamat tīvraṃ mahānādaṃ ca muktavān ||
children.translated_text: He fell into fierce anger and let loose a great roar.

children.text: krodhāt sūtaṃ ca durdharṣaḥ syandanastham uvāca ha
children.translated_text: In anger the unassailable one then spoke to his charioteer, who was standing in the chariot:
"Drive me through the middle of the enemy army, as far as its farthest end.
Today in battle I myself, by my heroic might,
will destroy all these Thirty gods from the sky with many kinds of powerful weapons.

children.text: aham indraṃ vadhiṣyāmi varuṇaṃ dhanadaṃ yamam
children.translated_text: I shall slay <s>Indra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Dhanada</s>, and <s>Yama</s>;
and after swiftly killing the Thirty gods, I myself will stand above them.

children.text: viṣādo na ca kartavyaḥ śīghraṃ vāhaya me ratham
children.translated_text: You must not give way to despair. Drive my chariot quickly.

children.text: dviḥ khalu tvāṃ bravīmyadya yāvadantaṃ nayasva mām ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, I tell you twice today: take me as far as the end."

children.text: ayaṃ sa nandanoddeśo yatra vartāmahe vayam
children.translated_text: "This is that region of <s>Nandana</s> where we now are.

children.text: naya mām adya tatra tvam udayo yatra parvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Take me there today, where Mount <s>Udaya</s> stands."

children.text: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā turagān sa manojavān
children.translated_text: Having heard that command of his,
the charioteer then directed the mind-swift horses right through the midst of the enemies.

children.text: tasya taṃ niścayaṃ jñātvā śakro deveśvarastadā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, knowing that resolve of his,
while standing in his chariot, addressed these gods who were stationed for battle:

children.text: surāḥ śṛṇuta madvākyaṃ yat tāvanmama rocate
children.translated_text: "Gods, hear my word, what seems best to me for the moment.

children.text: jīvann eva daśagrīvaḥ sādhu rakṣo nigṛhyatām ||
children.translated_text: While <s>Daśagrīva</s> is still alive, it is good that this rākṣasa should be captured.
For this one, very strong, with a chariot whose force is like the wind,
will move through the army like the ocean when its waves are swollen at the full moon.

children.text: na hyeṣa hantuṃ śakyo 'dya varadānāt sunirbhayaḥ
children.translated_text: Because of the boon he received, this fearless one cannot be killed today.

children.text: tad grahīṣyāmahe rakṣo yattā bhavata saṃyuge ||
children.translated_text: Therefore we shall seize the rākṣasa. Be vigilant in the battle.

children.text: yathā baliṃ nigṛhyaitat trailokyaṃ bhujyate mayā
children.translated_text: Just as, after restraining <s>Bali</s>, this triple world is enjoyed by me,

children.text: evam etasya pāpasya nigraho mama rocate ||
children.translated_text: so the restraint of this evil one seems best to me."

children.text: tato 'nyaṃ deśam āsthāya śakraḥ saṃtyajya rāvaṇam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, taking up another position and leaving <s>Rāvaṇa</s> aside,
fought with great brilliance, destroying rākṣasas in battle.
<s>Daśagrīva</s>, unchecked, entered from the north,
while <s>Śatakratu</s> entered from the southern side.
Then the lord of rākṣasas, having penetrated for a hundred yojanas,
covered the whole army of the gods with showers of arrows.

children.text: tataḥ śakro nirīkṣyātha praviṣṭaṃ taṃ balaṃ svakam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, seeing that he had entered his own force,
turned back without confusion and encircled <s>Daśānana</s>.
At that moment a cry was released by the dānavas and rākṣasas:

children.text: hā hatāḥ smeti taṃ dṛṣṭvā grastaṃ śakreṇa rāvaṇam ||
children.translated_text: "Alas, we are slain!" when they saw <s>Rāvaṇa</s> caught by <s>Śakra</s>.
Then <s>Rāvaṇi</s>, mounted on his chariot and faint with anger,
entered that exceedingly terrible army, enraged beyond measure.

children.text: sa tāṃ praviśya māyāṃ tu dattāṃ gopatinā purā
children.translated_text: Entering into that māyā (power of illusion) once granted by the lord of cows,
he became invisible to all beings and scattered that army.

children.text: tataḥ sa devān saṃtyajya śakram evābhyayād drutam
children.translated_text: Then, leaving the gods aside, he rushed swiftly upon <s>Śakra</s> himself,

children.text: mahendraśca mahātejā na dadarśa sutaṃ ripoḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the very brilliant <s>Mahendra</s> did not see the son of his enemy.
Striking <s>Mātali</s> and the horses with excellent arrows,
he, swift-handed, covered <s>Mahendra</s> with a shower of arrows.

children.text: tataḥ śakro rathaṃ tyaktvā visṛjya ca sa mātalim
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, leaving his chariot and releasing <s>Mātali</s>,
mounted <s>Airāvata</s> and searched for <s>Rāvaṇi</s>.

children.text: sa tu māyābalād rakṣaḥ saṃgrāme nābhyadṛśyata
children.translated_text: But that rākṣasa, by the power of māyā, was not seen in the battle,
as he showered mighty <s>Mahendra</s> with a mass of arrows.

children.text: sa taṃ yadā pariśrāntam indraṃ mene 'tha rāvaṇiḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāvaṇi</s> then thought that <s>Indra</s> was exhausted,
he bound him by māyā and led him away toward his own army.
Then, seeing <s>Mahendra</s> carried off by force in that battle through māyā,

children.text: mahendram amarāḥ sarve kiṃ nvetad iti cukruśuḥ
children.translated_text: all the immortals cried out, "What can this be?"

children.text: na hi dṛśyati vidyāvānmāyayā yena nīyate ||
children.translated_text: For the possessor of knowledge, by whose māyā he was being led away, could not be seen.
At that same moment, all the hosts of gods then,
greatly enraged, rushed upon <s>Rāvaṇa</s> with showers of weapons.
But <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, encountering the hosts of Vasus, Ādityas, and Maruts,

children.text: na śaśāka raṇe sthātuṃ na yoddhuṃ śastrapīḍitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: could not stand in battle or fight, oppressed by their weapons.

children.text: taṃ tu dṛṣṭvā pariśrāntaṃ prahārair jarjaracchavim
children.translated_text: Seeing him exhausted, his appearance shattered by blows,
<s>Rāvaṇi</s>, standing invisible, spoke this to his father in battle:

children.text: āgaccha tāta gacchāvo nivṛttaṃ raṇakarma tat
children.translated_text: "Come, father. Let us go. This work of battle has turned back.

children.text: jitaṃ te viditaṃ bho 'stu svastho bhava gatajvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Know that victory is yours. Be at ease and free from fever.

children.text: ayaṃ hi surasainyasya trailokyasya ca yaḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: For this <s>Śakra</s>, who is lord of the army of gods and of the triple world,

children.text: sa gṛhīto mayā śakro bhagnamānāḥ surāḥ kṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: has been seized by me, and the gods have been made broken in pride.

children.text: yatheṣṭaṃ bhuṅkṣva trailokyaṃ nigṛhya ripum ojasā
children.translated_text: Enjoy the triple world as you wish, after subduing your enemy by force.

children.text: vṛthā te kiṃ śramaṃ kṛtvā yuddhaṃ hi tava niṣphalam ||
children.translated_text: Why make useless exertion? For your battle is now without purpose."
By the power of fate, he withdrew from that work of battle;
and hearing the words of <s>Rāvaṇi</s>, <s>Daśānana</s> became calm in mind.

children.text: atha raṇavigatajvaraḥ prabhur vijayam avāpya niśācarādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the lord, the ruler of the night-roamers, his battle-fever gone and victory obtained,

children.text: bhavanam abhi tato jagāma hṛṣṭaḥ svasutam avāpya ca vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: went joyfully to his dwelling; and after reaching his son, he spoke these words:
"By these feats of valor, matching your immense strength,
the honor of my family has been increased, since, equal in prowess to the immortals, you have conquered the lord of the Thirty gods and the Thirty gods themselves.

children.text: tvaritam upanayasva vāsavaṃ nagaram ito vraja sainyasaṃvṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Quickly bring <s>Vāsava</s> here. Go to the city, surrounded by the army.

children.text: aham api tava gacchato drutaṃ saha sacivair anuyāmi pṛṣṭhataḥ ||
children.translated_text: As you go swiftly, I too will follow behind you with my ministers."

children.text: atha sa balavṛtaḥ savāhanas tridaśapatiṃ parigṛhya rāvaṇiḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāvaṇi</s>, surrounded by his force and with his vehicles, seized the lord of the Thirty gods,

children.text: svabhavanam upagamya rākṣaso muditamanā visasarja rākṣasān ||
children.translated_text: and the rākṣasa, having reached his own dwelling, glad at heart, dismissed the rākṣasas.
When the very mighty <s>Mahendra</s> had indeed been conquered by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s son,
the gods, placing <s>Prajāpati</s> at their head, then went to <s>Laṅkā</s>.
Having approached that <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, who was surrounded by his sons and brothers,
<s>Prajāpati</s>, standing in the sky, spoke with words first meant to conciliate him.

children.text: vatsa rāvaṇa tuṣṭo 'smi tava putrasya saṃyuge
children.translated_text: Child <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, I am pleased with your son in battle.
Ah, what valor and nobility are his; he is equal to you, or even greater.

children.text: jitaṃ hi bhavatā sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ svena tejasā
children.translated_text: For the whole threefold world has been conquered by you through your own splendor.

children.text: kṛtā pratijñā saphalā prīto 'smi svasutena vai ||
children.translated_text: Your vow has been made fruitful; indeed I am pleased with your own son.
And this exceedingly strong son of yours, O <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, this <s>Rāvaṇi</s>,
will be renowned in the world as <s>Indrajit</s>.
This powerful rākṣasa will be a conqueror of enemies,

children.text: yam āśritya tvayā rājan sthāpitāstridaśā vaśe ||
children.translated_text: by relying on whom, O king, you have brought the Thirty Gods under your control.
Therefore let the great-armed <s>Mahendra</s>, the chastiser of <s>Pāka</s>, be released.
And what will the dwellers in heaven give for the sake of his release?
Then the very splendid <s>Indrajit</s>, victorious in battle, spoke:
God, I choose immortality here in return for releasing him.

children.text: abravīt tu tadā devo rāvaṇiṃ kamalodbhavaḥ
children.translated_text: But then the lotus-born god spoke to <s>Rāvaṇi</s>:

children.text: nāsti sarvāmaratvaṃ hi keṣāṃcit prāṇināṃ bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: For no living beings at all on earth possess complete immortality.
Then <s>Indrajit</s> spoke to the lotus-born one standing there:
Let it be heard what success may be mine in releasing <s>Śatakratu</s>.

children.text: mameṣṭaṃ nityaśo deva havyaiḥ sampūjya pāvakam
children.translated_text: It is my wish always, O god, after honoring the fire with oblations,
to enter battle while desiring the conquest of enemies.
But if, before that recitation and fire-offering to <s>Vibhāvasu</s> is completed,

children.text: yudhyeyaṃ deva saṃgrāme tadā me syād vināśanam ||
children.translated_text: I should fight in battle, O god, then let my destruction take place.

children.text: sarvo hi tapasā caiva vṛṇotyamaratāṃ pumān
children.translated_text: For every man chooses immortality through tapas (austerity),
but by my valor this immortality has been set in motion.

children.text: evam astviti taṃ prāha vākyaṃ devaḥ prajāpatiḥ
children.translated_text: So be it, the god <s>Prajāpati</s> said that word to him.
And <s>Śakra</s> was released by <s>Indrajit</s>, and the gods went to heaven.
Meanwhile <s>Śakra</s>, dejected, with his garment and garland fallen away,
O <s>Rāma</s>, his mind filled with anxiety, became intent on meditation.

children.text: taṃ tu dṛṣṭvā tathābhūtaṃ prāha devaḥ prajāpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing him in such a state, the god <s>Prajāpati</s> said:

children.text: śatakrato kim utkaṇṭhāṃ karoṣi smara duṣkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Śatakratu</s>, why do you feel distress? Remember the wrong you did.

children.text: amarendra mayā bahvyaḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭāḥ purā prabho
children.translated_text: O king of the immortals, lord, long ago I created many creatures,
all of one color, of the same speech, and entirely of one form.

children.text: tāsāṃ nāsti viśeṣo hi darśane lakṣaṇe 'pi vā
children.translated_text: Among them there was no distinction at all in appearance or even in marks.
Then, with concentrated mind, I reflected upon those creatures.

children.text: so 'haṃ tāsāṃ viśeṣārthaṃ striyam ekāṃ vinirmame
children.translated_text: So, for the sake of making a distinction among them, I fashioned one woman,

children.text: yad yat prajānāṃ pratyaṅgaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ tat tad uddhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: taking out whatever was excellent in each limb of the creatures.

children.text: tato mayā rūpaguṇair ahalyā strī vinirmitā
children.translated_text: Then by me the woman <s>Ahalyā</s> was fashioned with beauty and virtues,

children.text: ahalyetyeva ca mayā tasyā nāma pravartitam ||
children.translated_text: and by me the name <s>Ahalyā</s> itself was given to her.

children.text: nirmitāyāṃ tu devendra tasyāṃ nāryāṃ surarṣabha
children.translated_text: But when that woman had been fashioned, O divine <s>Indra</s>, bull among gods,
the thought arose in me: To whom will she belong?

children.text: tvaṃ tu śakra tadā nārīṃ jānīṣe manasā prabho
children.translated_text: But you, O <s>Śakra</s>, O lord, then knew that woman in your mind,
thinking, Because of my superior station, this one is my wife, O <s>Purandara</s>.

children.text: sā mayā nyāsabhūtā tu gautamasya mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: But she, being like a trust of mine, was entrusted to great-souled <s>Gautama</s>.

children.text: nyastā bahūni varṣāṇi tena niryātitā ca sā ||
children.translated_text: She was left with him for many years, and he returned her.
Then, after I had recognized the steadiness of that great sage

children.text: jñātvā tapasi siddhiṃ ca patnyarthaṃ sparśitā tadā ||
children.translated_text: and had known his perfection in tapas, she was then given to him as a wife.

children.text: sa tayā saha dharmātmā ramate sma mahāmuniḥ
children.translated_text: That righteous great sage delighted with her,
but the gods became disappointed when she had been given to <s>Gautama</s>.

children.text: tvaṃ kruddhastviha kāmātmā gatvā tasyāśramaṃ muneḥ
children.translated_text: But you, angry and full of desire, went here to that sage's hermitage,

children.text: dṛṣṭavāṃśca tadā tāṃ strīṃ dīptām agniśikhām iva ||
children.translated_text: and then saw that woman, blazing like a flame of fire.

children.text: sā tvayā dharṣitā śakra kāmārtena samanyunā
children.translated_text: She was violated by you, O <s>Śakra</s>, when you were afflicted by desire and anger,

children.text: dṛṣṭastvaṃ ca tadā tena āśrame paramarṣiṇā ||
children.translated_text: and at that time you were seen by that supreme seer in the hermitage.
Then, in anger, you were cursed by that sage of supreme splendor,
by which, O divine <s>Indra</s>, you underwent a reversal into a state of disgrace.

children.text: yasmānme dharṣitā patnī tvayā vāsava nirbhayam
children.translated_text: Because my wife was violated by you fearlessly, O <s>Vāsava</s>,
therefore, O king, you will fall into an enemy's hands in battle.

children.text: ayaṃ tu bhāvo durbuddhe yastvayeha pravartitaḥ
children.translated_text: And this disposition, fool, which has been set in motion by you here,
will also exist among all human beings, without doubt.
There, a very powerful and great <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) will arise.

children.text: tatrārdhaṃ tasya yaḥ kartā tvayyardhaṃ nipatiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: There half of it will fall on the one who commits it, and half on you.

children.text: na ca te sthāvaraṃ sthānaṃ bhaviṣyati puraṃdara
children.translated_text: And you, O <s>Purandara</s>, will have no fixed station,
because of this connection with <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) that you have begun here.

children.text: yaśca yaśca surendraḥ syād dhruvaḥ sa na bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: And whichever one becomes lord of the gods will not be permanent.

children.text: eṣa śāpo mayā mukta ityasau tvāṃ tadābravīt ||
children.translated_text: This curse has been released by me, he said to you then.

children.text: tāṃ tu bhāryāṃ vinirbhartsya so 'bravīt sumahātapāḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after rebuking that wife, the greatly ascetic one said:
Ill-conducted woman, vanish from the vicinity of my hermitage.
Since, though endowed with beauty and youth, you were unsteady,

children.text: tasmād rūpavatī loke na tvam ekā bhaviṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: therefore you alone will not be the beautiful woman in the world.

children.text: rūpaṃ ca tat prajāḥ sarvā gamiṣyanti sudurlabham
children.translated_text: And all creatures will obtain that very beauty, so hard to acquire,
by relying on which this bewilderment of yours has arisen.
From that time onward most creatures became endowed with beauty.
All this came about from the sending forth of that sage's curse.

children.text: tat smara tvaṃ mahābāho duṣkṛtaṃ yat tvayā kṛtam
children.translated_text: Therefore remember, great-armed one, the wrong that was done by you.

children.text: yena tvaṃ grahaṇaṃ śatror gato nānyena vāsava ||
children.translated_text: By that one, O <s>Vāsava</s>, you fell into the enemy's grasp, and by no other.

children.text: śīghraṃ yajasva yajñaṃ tvaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ susamāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Quickly perform a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> sacrifice, you yourself being well composed.
Purified by that sacrifice, you will then go to the third heaven.

children.text: putraśca tava devendra na vinaṣṭo mahāraṇe
children.translated_text: And your son, O <s>Devendra</s>, has not perished in the great battle.
He has been taken away and kept nearby by <s>Aryaka</s> in the great ocean.

children.text: etacchrutvā mahendrastu yajñam iṣṭvā ca vaiṣṇavam
children.translated_text: Hearing this, great <s>Indra</s> performed the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> sacrifice,
and again ascended to the third heaven and ruled over the gods.

children.text: etad indrajito rāma balaṃ yat kīrtitaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: This, O <s>Rāma</s>, is the strength of <s>Indrajit</s> that I have recounted:

children.text: nirjitastena devendraḥ prāṇino 'nye ca kiṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by him <s>Devendra</s> was conquered; what then of other living beings?

children.text: tato rāmo mahātejā vismayāt punar eva hi
children.translated_text: Then mighty-spirited <s>Rāma</s>, once again in astonishment,
bowed and spoke these words to <s>Agastya</s>, best of seers:

children.text: bhagavan kiṃ tadā lokāḥ śūnyā āsan dvijottama
children.translated_text: "Blessed lord, were the worlds empty then, O best of twice-born men,

children.text: dharṣaṇāṃ yatra na prāpto rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: so that <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of rākṣasas, met with no humiliation?
Or had those lords of earth become deficient in valor?
Were many kings deprived of excellent weapons and conquered?"

children.text: rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā agastyo bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing the words of <s>Rāghava</s>, the blessed seer <s>Agastya</s>
spoke to <s>Rāma</s> with a smile, as the grandsire might speak to the lord:
"While thus oppressing kings, O bull among rulers,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, O <s>Rāma</s>, roamed over the earth, O lord of the earth.
Then he reached a city named <s>Māhiṣmatī</s>, radiant like the city of heaven,
where the supreme presence of <s>Vasuretas</s> was found.
Its king, by his majesty, was equal to <s>Vasuretas</s>,

children.text: arjuno nāma yasyāgniḥ śarakuṇḍe śayaḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: a ruler named <s>Arjuna</s>, whose fire always lay in the arrow-pit.

children.text: tam eva divasaṃ so 'tha haihayādhipatir balī
children.translated_text: On that very day, that strong lord of the <s>Haihaya</s>s,

children.text: arjuno narmadāṃ rantuṃ gataḥ strībhiḥ saheśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Arjuna</s>, had gone with women and retainers to sport in the <s>Narmadā</s>.
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of rākṣasas, questioned his ministers there:

children.text: kvārjuno vo nṛpaḥ so 'dya śīghram ākhyātum arhatha ||
children.translated_text: 'Where is your king <s>Arjuna</s> today? You ought to tell me quickly.
I, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, have arrived, desiring battle with that best of kings.
You, unperturbed, must report my arrival.'
Thus addressed by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, those very wise ministers
told the lord of rākṣasas that the king was not present.

children.text: śrutvā viśravasaḥ putraḥ paurāṇām arjunaṃ gatam
children.translated_text: Hearing from the townspeople that <s>Arjuna</s> had gone, the son of <s>Viśravas</s>
withdrew and came to the <s>Vindhya</s>, a mountain like <s>Himavat</s>.

children.text: sa tam abhram ivāviṣṭam udbhrāntam iva medinīm
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s> saw that <s>Vindhya</s>, as if filled with clouds, as if the earth had risen up,
as if scraping the sky.
It had a thousand peaks and caves inhabited by lions,
and, with cool waters fallen from cascades, it seemed to laugh aloud.
With gods, dānavas, gandharvas, hosts of apsarases, and kinnaras,
all sporting with women, that great height had become like heaven.
With rivers flowing down, its waters were matchless in their course,
and with bright, moving tongues it seemed to be pouring them forth.
Seeing the <s>Vindhya</s>, a mountain with meteors and caves, resembling <s>Himavat</s>,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> then went to the <s>Narmadā</s>.
Its sacred waters moved over shifting stones, and it flowed toward the western ocean.
Its pools were churned by buffaloes, deer, lions, tigers, bears, and noble elephants,
all scorched by heat and thirsty.
It was covered with cakravākas, kāraṇḍava ducks, swans, and waterfowl,
and with cranes, ever excited and crying aloud.
Blossoming trees formed its crest-ornament, and pairs of cakravākas were its breasts;
its broad sandbanks were its hips, and rows of swans its fair girdle.
Its limbs were smeared with flower-pollen, and the pure foam of the water was its garment;
the touch of entering its water was its embrace, and its lovely eyes were blooming lotuses.
Swiftly descending from the <s>Puṣpaka</s>, <s>Daśānana</s>

children.text: iṣṭām iva varāṃ nārīm avagāhya daśānanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: entered the <s>Narmadā</s>, best of rivers, as one might embrace a beloved and excellent woman.
On her charming bank, adorned with many kinds of flowers,
that foremost rākṣasa sat down together with his ministers,
and the lord of rākṣasas obtained delight born from the sight of the <s>Narmadā</s>.
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of rākṣasas, laughing playfully there,
spoke to his ministers, <s>Mārīca</s>, <s>Śuka</s>, and <s>Sāraṇa</s>:
'This sun, making the world golden, as it were, with a thousand rays,
the maker of fierce heat, has taken his place in the middle of the sky;
yet, knowing that I am seated here, the day-maker becomes moonlike.
And this wind, cooled by the water of the <s>Narmadā</s>, fragrant, and destroying fatigue,
blows here well restrained out of fear of me.
And this best of rivers, the <s>Narmadā</s>, increaser of delight,
stands like a frightened woman, with its fish, birds, and waves hidden.

children.text: tad bhavantaḥ kṣatāḥ śastrair nṛpair indrasamair yudhi
children.translated_text: Therefore you, wounded by weapons in battle by kings equal to <s>Indra</s>,
and sprinkled with blood as if with the juice of sandalwood,

children.text: te yūyam avagāhadhvaṃ narmadāṃ śarmadāṃ nṛṇām
children.translated_text: enter the <s>Narmadā</s>, giver of comfort to men,
like intoxicated great elephants, with lotus-like faces, entering the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
Having bathed in this great river, you will cast off sin.
I too, here on this bank, bright as the autumn moon,
will slowly make an offering of flowers to the lord of <s>Umā</s>.'
Thus addressed by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, <s>Mārīca</s>, <s>Śuka</s>, and <s>Sāraṇa</s>,
together with <s>Mahodara</s> and <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>, entered the <s>Narmadā</s>.
By those elephant-like lords of rākṣasas the river <s>Narmadā</s> was agitated,
as the <s>Gaṅgā</s> is by great elephants such as <s>Vāmana</s>, <s>Añjana</s>, and <s>Padma</s>.
Then those rākṣasas, having bathed in the excellent water of the <s>Narmadā</s>,
Having crossed over, they brought flowers for the offering to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
On the lovely sandy bank of the <s>Narmadā</s>, shining like a pure white cloud,
a mountain made of flowers was made in a moment by the lords of the rākṣasas.
When the flowers had been brought as offerings, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas,

children.text: avatīrṇo nadīṃ snātuṃ gaṅgām iva mahāgajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: descended into the river to bathe, like a great elephant into the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

children.text: tatra snātvā ca vidhivajjaptvā japyam anuttamam
children.translated_text: After bathing there according to rule and muttering the unsurpassed mantra to be muttered,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> rose up from that water of the <s>Narmadā</s>.
Seven rākṣasas followed <s>Rāvaṇa</s> as he went with joined palms.

children.text: yatra yatra sa yāti sma rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: Wherever <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas, went,

children.text: jāmbūnadamayaṃ liṅgaṃ tatra tatra sma nīyate ||
children.translated_text: there and there the <s>liṅga</s> made of jāmbūnada gold was carried.
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, setting that <s>liṅga</s> in the middle of an altar of sand,
worshipped it with perfumes and with flowers fragrant like nectar.

children.text: tataḥ satām ārtiharaṃ haraṃ paraṃ varapradaṃ candramayūkhabhūṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Then, having worshipped <s>Hara</s>, remover of the distress of the good, supreme, bestower of boons, adorned with moonbeams,

children.text: samarcayitvā sa niśācaro jagau prasārya hastān praṇanarta cāyatān ||
children.translated_text: that night-roamer sang and, stretching out his long arms, danced reverently.
At the place on the bank of the <s>Narmadā</s> where that lord of rākṣasas, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
was making his flower-offering, not far from that region,

children.text: arjuno jayatāṃ śreṣṭho māhiṣmatyāḥ patiḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Arjuna</s>, best of conquerors, lord and ruler of <s>Māhiṣmatī</s>,
was sporting with women, standing in the water of the <s>Narmadā</s>.

children.text: tāsāṃ madhyagato rājā rarāja sa tato 'rjunaḥ
children.translated_text: Standing among them, King <s>Arjuna</s> then shone
like a tusker standing among a thousand cow elephants.

children.text: jijñāsuḥ sa tu bāhūnāṃ sahasrasyottamaṃ balam
children.translated_text: Wishing to test the supreme strength of his thousand arms,
that <s>Arjuna</s> then blocked the current of the <s>Narmadā</s> with his arms.
Reaching the barrier made by the arms of <s>Kārtavīrya</s>, that clear water,
tearing away the banks, ran back against the current.
Filled with fish, water-monsters, and makaras, and strewn with flowers and kuśa grass,
that rush of <s>Narmadā</s> water appeared like the rainy season.
That rush of water, as if sent forward by <s>Kārtavīrya</s>,

children.text: puṣpopahāraṃ tat sarvaṃ rāvaṇasya jahāra ha ||
children.translated_text: carried away all that flower-offering of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, leaving that observance half completed,

children.text: narmadāṃ paśyate kāntāṃ pratikūlāṃ yathā priyām ||
children.translated_text: looked at the lovely <s>Narmadā</s>, flowing contrary like a beloved woman turned against him.
Seeing in the west that swelling rush of water,

children.text: vardhantam ambhaso vegaṃ pūrvām āśāṃ praviśya tu ||
children.translated_text: resembling the ocean's surge, entering the eastern quarter,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> then looked at the river, whose birds were not startled,
standing in its highest natural state and appearing like an unchanged woman.
With a loud sound made by the fingers of his left hand, <s>Daśānana</s>
ordered <s>Śuka</s> and <s>Sāraṇa</s> to seek out the source of the current.
Those two brothers, <s>Śuka</s> and <s>Sāraṇa</s>, commanded by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
heroic wanderers through the spaces of the sky, set out facing west.

children.text: ardhayojanamātraṃ tu gatvā tau tu niśācarau
children.translated_text: After going about half a yojana, those two night-roamers
saw a man in the water, sporting with women.
He was like a great śāla tree, his hair disordered by the water,
his eyes red at the corners with intoxication, and his radiance like that of <s>Madana</s>.
He, crusher of enemies, was blocking the river with a thousand arms,
as if a mountain with a thousand feet were blocking the earth.
Surrounded by a thousand young and excellent women,
he was like a tusker among a thousand rutting cow elephants.
Seeing that most wondrous man, the two rākṣasas <s>Śuka</s> and <s>Sāraṇa</s>
turned back, approached <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, and then said to him:
"O lord of rākṣasas, some man there, like a great śāla tree,
has blocked the <s>Narmadā</s> as if by a dam and is making the women sport.
With the river's water completely blocked by his thousand arms,
it repeatedly sends forth surges like the ocean's outpourings.
Hearing <s>Śuka</s> and <s>Sāraṇa</s> speaking in this way,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, saying "It is <s>Arjuna</s>," rose up, eager for battle.
When the lord of rākṣasas set out facing <s>Arjuna</s>,

children.text: sakṛd eva kṛto rāvaḥ saraktaḥ preṣito ghanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: a single roar, bloody in tone, was sent forth by the clouds.
Surrounded by <s>Mahodara</s>, <s>Mahāpārśva</s>, <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>, <s>Śuka</s>, and <s>Sāraṇa</s>,
the lord of rākṣasas went there where that <s>Arjuna</s> was.

children.text: nātidīrgheṇa kālena sa tato rākṣaso balī
children.translated_text: In no long time, that powerful rākṣasa,
dark as collyrium, came to that dreadful pool of the <s>Narmadā</s>.

children.text: sa tatra strīparivṛtaṃ vāśitābhir iva dvipam
children.translated_text: There the king of the rākṣasas saw that king, <s>Arjuna</s>, surrounded by women,
like an elephant surrounded by cow elephants.
Red-eyed with anger and swollen with strength, the lord of rākṣasas
spoke thus in a deep voice to <s>Arjuna</s>'s ministers:

children.text: amātyāḥ kṣipram ākhyāta haihayasya nṛpasya vai
children.translated_text: "Ministers, quickly announce to the king of the <s>Haihaya</s>:
'One named <s>Rāvaṇa</s> has arrived for the purpose of battle.'"
Hearing <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s words, those ministers of <s>Arjuna</s>

children.text: uttasthuḥ sāyudhāstaṃ ca rāvaṇaṃ vākyam abruvan ||
children.translated_text: rose up with weapons in hand and spoke this statement to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>:

children.text: yuddhasya kālo vijñātaḥ sādhu bhoḥ sādhu rāvaṇa
children.translated_text: "The time for battle is understood. Good, sir, good, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: yaḥ kṣībaṃ strīvṛtaṃ caiva yoddhum icchasi no nṛpam
children.translated_text: that you wish to fight our king when he is drunk and surrounded by women,
like a tiger wishing to fight a rutting elephant among cow elephants.
Be patient today, <s>Daśagrīva</s>; let the night be spent by you here.
But if you have eagerness for battle, tomorrow, dear sir, you shall meet <s>Arjuna</s> in combat.
Or if there is urgency for you, if you are overcome by thirst for battle,
then, after killing us, you will come to battle with <s>Arjuna</s>."
Then, by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s ministers, however, the ministers of the king...
And in the battle they too were slain, and were devoured by the hungry ones.
Then a tumultuous cry arose on the bank of the <s>Narmadā</s>
from the attendants of <s>Arjuna</s> and from the ministers of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
With arrows, javelins, spears, and thunderbolt-like weapons fitted with hooks,
they rushed in from every side, tormenting those who were with <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
The onrush of the warriors of the lord of the <s>Haihayas</s> was extremely dreadful,
like the roar of an ocean filled with crocodiles, fish, and makaras.
But <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s ministers, <s>Prahasta</s>, <s>Śuka</s>, and <s>Sāraṇa</s>,
angrily burned through <s>Kārtavīrya</s>'s army, blazing with the splendor of fire.

children.text: arjunāya tu tat karma rāvaṇasya samantriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: But that deed of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> together with his ministers
was reported to <s>Arjuna</s>, while he was sporting, by men who guarded the gates.

children.text: uktvā na bhetavyam iti strījanaṃ sa tato 'rjunaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Arjuna</s>, after telling the women, 'There is nothing to fear,'
came up out of that water, like dark collyrium from the water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
Then, his eyes stained by anger, that fire-like <s>Arjuna</s>
blazed up, very terrible, like the fire at the end of an age.
Very quickly, wearing excellent golden armlets, he took up his mace
and charged at the rākṣasas like the sun at darkness.
Raising the great mace that made his arms swing wide,
and taking on the speed of <s>Garuḍa</s>, that <s>Arjuna</s> seemed to swoop down.
Blocking his path, like the <s>Vindhya</s> mountain blocking the sun's path,
stood <s>Prahasta</s>, armed with a club, immovable like <s>Vindhya</s> itself.
Then <s>Prahasta</s>, enraged and swollen with pride, launched at him

children.text: prahastaḥ preṣayan kruddho rarāsa ca yathāmbudaḥ ||
children.translated_text: his terrible iron-bound club, and roared like a cloud.
At the front of that club there was fire, like a cluster of aśoka blossoms,
as it flew from <s>Prahasta</s>'s hand, seeming to burn everything.
As the club rushed toward him, <s>Kārtavīrya Arjuna</s>,
mace in hand and moving like an elephant, skillfully dodged it.
Then the lord of the <s>Haihayas</s> charged at <s>Prahasta</s>,
whirling his heavy mace, which rose to five hundred arm-lengths.
Struck then with tremendous force by that mace, <s>Prahasta</s>
fell like a standing mountain struck by <s>Indra</s>'s thunderbolt.
Seeing <s>Prahasta</s> fallen, <s>Mārīca</s>, <s>Śuka</s>, and <s>Sāraṇa</s>,
together with <s>Mahodara</s> and <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>, withdrew from the battlefield.
When the ministers had retreated and <s>Prahasta</s> had been struck down,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> swiftly attacked <s>Arjuna</s>, the best of kings.
Then that dreadful battle of the thousand-armed one and the twenty-armed one,
of the king and the rākṣasa, began there, making the hair stand on end.
They were like two oceans in turmoil, like two mountains with their roots shaking,
like two suns endowed with splendor, like two fires burning.

children.text: baloddhatau yathā nāgau vāśitārthe yathā vṛṣau
children.translated_text: They were like two serpents swollen with strength, like two bulls fighting for a cow,
like two roaring clouds, like two lions in the fullness of their strength.
Thus those two, the rākṣasa and <s>Arjuna</s>, enraged like <s>Rudra</s> and <s>Kāla</s>,
struck each other fiercely with their maces.
As mountains endure terrible blows from the thunderbolt,
so those two, the man and the rākṣasa, endured the blows of the maces.
Just as an echo arises from the roar of thunderbolts,

children.text: tathā tābhyāṃ gadāpātair diśaḥ sarvāḥ pratiśrutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: so all the quarters resounded from the falls of their maces.
That mace of <s>Arjuna</s>, as it was hurled against his enemy's chest,
made the sky shine with golden radiance, like a flash of lightning.
Likewise, as it was hurled again and again by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
the mace shone on <s>Arjuna</s>'s chest like a fiery meteor on a great mountain.
Neither <s>Arjuna</s> grew weary, nor did the lord of the rākṣasa hosts.

children.text: samam āsīt tayor yuddhaṃ yathā pūrvaṃ balīndrayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: Their battle was even, like the former battle of <s>Bali</s> and <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: śṛṅgair maharṣabhau yadvad dantāgrair iva kuñjarau
children.translated_text: Like two great bulls with their horns, or like two elephants with the tips of their tusks,
the best of the man and the rākṣasa battered each other.
Then by the enraged <s>Arjuna</s>, with all his strength, that mace
was released between <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s breasts in the great battle.
On <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s chest, protected by the granting of boons, that mace
split in two and fell to the ground like a weak army.
But from the mace-blow released by <s>Arjuna</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>
moved back a bow's length and sank down, groaning.

children.text: sa vihvalaṃ tad ālakṣya daśagrīvaṃ tato 'rjunaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Arjuna</s>, perceiving the ten-necked <s>Rāvaṇa</s> to be dazed,
suddenly seized him, like <s>Garuḍa</s> seizing a serpent.

children.text: sa taṃ bāhusahasreṇa balād gṛhya daśānanam
children.translated_text: That mighty king, grasping the ten-faced one by force with his thousand arms,

children.text: babandha balavān rājā baliṃ nārāyaṇo yathā ||
children.translated_text: bound him, just as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> bound <s>Bali</s>.
As the ten-necked one was being bound, siddhas, cāraṇas, and deities,
saying 'Well done!', scattered flowers upon <s>Arjuna</s>'s head.

children.text: vyāghro mṛgam ivādāya siṃharāḍ iva dantinam
children.translated_text: Taking him as a tiger takes a deer, or as the king of lions takes an elephant,
the <s>Haihaya</s> king roared again and again from joy, like a cloud.
But <s>Prahasta</s>, having recovered, saw the ten-faced one bound,
and, angry, together with those rākṣasas, charged at the king.
The rush of those night-roamers as they came on
appeared wondrous, like the swelling of the oceans when the heat has passed away.
Crying 'Release him, release him!' and repeatedly 'Stand, stand!',
they hurled clubs and spears then at <s>Arjuna</s>.
Before those weapons could reach him, that <s>Arjuna</s>, unshaken,
the slayer of foes, quickly seized the weapons of the enemies of the immortals.
Then, with those very irresistible, foremost weapons, against the rākṣasas...
Having broken through them, he drove them away, as the wind drives clouds.
Then, after terrifying the rākṣasas, <s>Kārtavīryārjuna</s>
seized <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and entered the city, surrounded by his friends.

children.text: sa kīryamāṇaḥ kusumākṣatotkarair dvijaiḥ sapauraiḥ puruhūtasaṃnibhaḥ
children.translated_text: Showered with masses of flowers and unbroken grains by the twice-born and the townspeople, like <s>Puruhūta</s>,

children.text: tadārjunaḥ sampraviveśa tāṃ purīṃ baliṃ nigṛhyeva sahasralocanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Arjuna</s> entered that city, as the thousand-eyed one entered after subduing <s>Bali</s>.
But that capture of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, resembling the capture of the wind,

children.text: ṛṣiḥ pulastyaḥ śuśrāva kathitaṃ divi daivataiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the sage <s>Pulastya</s> heard, as it was told in heaven by the gods.
Then, trembling from love for his grandson, the very steadfast one
came, the great sage, to see the lord of <s>Māhiṣmatī</s>.
Taking the path of the wind, that twice-born one, moving with the speed of the wind,
reached the city <s>Māhiṣmatī</s>, his resolve stirred by mental anguish.
He entered the city, resembling <s>Amarāvatī</s> and filled with joyful, thriving people,
as <s>Brahmā</s> might enter <s>Indra</s>'s <s>Amarāvatī</s>.
Seeing him coming forth like the sun walking on foot, very hard to behold,
they then recognized him and reported it to <s>Arjuna</s>.

children.text: pulastya iti taṃ śrutvā vacanaṃ haihayādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing the words, '<s>Pulastya</s>,' the lord of the <s>Haihayas</s>
raised his joined palms to his head and went out to meet the best of twice-borns.
His priest, taking the arghya (honor-offering) and likewise the madhuparka (welcome offering),
went before the king, like <s>Bṛhaspati</s> before <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: tatastam ṛṣim āyāntam udyantam iva bhāskaram
children.translated_text: Then, seeing that sage coming like the rising sun,
<s>Arjuna</s>, when he had arrived, bowed to him as <s>Indra</s> bows to <s>Īśvara</s>.

children.text: sa tasya madhuparkaṃ ca pādyam arghyaṃ ca dāpayan
children.translated_text: He had madhuparka, pādya (water for the feet), and arghya given to him,
and the king of kings addressed <s>Pulastya</s> in a voice choked with joy:
Today this <s>Māhiṣmatī</s> has been made equal to <s>Amarāvatī</s>,

children.text: adyāhaṃ tu dvijendrendra yasmāt paśyāmi durdṛśam ||
children.translated_text: because today, O foremost lord of twice-borns, I see one who is hard to behold.

children.text: adya me kuśalaṃ deva adya me kulam uddhṛtam
children.translated_text: Today all is well with me, lord; today my lineage has been raised up,

children.text: yat te devagaṇair vandyau vande 'haṃ caraṇāvimau ||
children.translated_text: since I bow to these two feet of yours, which are honored by hosts of gods.

children.text: idaṃ rājyam ime putrā ime dārā ime vayam
children.translated_text: This kingdom, these sons, these wives, and we ourselves are here;

children.text: brahman kiṃ kurma kiṃ kāryam ājñāpayatu no bhavān ||
children.translated_text: O Brahman, what shall we do, what is to be done? Let your honor command us.

children.text: taṃ dharme 'gniṣu bhṛtyeṣu śivaṃ pṛṣṭvātha pārthivam
children.translated_text: After asking the king about welfare in dharma, the sacred fires, and his servants,
<s>Pulastya</s> then spoke to that <s>Arjuna</s>, king of the <s>Haihayas</s>:
O king of kings, with spotless lotus-eyes and a face like the full moon,

children.text: atulaṃ te balaṃ yena daśagrīvastvayā jitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: matchless is your strength, by which <s>Daśagrīva</s> has been conquered by you.
He from fear of whom the ocean and the wind would stand motionless,

children.text: so 'yam adya tvayā baddhaḥ pautro me 'tīvadurjayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this one, my grandson, exceedingly hard to conquer, has today been bound by you.

children.text: tat putraka yaśaḥ sphītaṃ nāma viśrāvitaṃ tvayā
children.translated_text: Therefore, child, abundant fame and a renowned name have been won by you;
being entreated today by my word, dear child, release <s>Daśānana</s>.
Then <s>Arjuna</s>, accepting <s>Pulastya</s>'s command without any contrary word,
that supreme king of kings gladly released the lord of rākṣasas.

children.text: sa taṃ pramuktvā tridaśārim arjunaḥ prapūjya divyābharaṇasragambaraiḥ
children.translated_text: After releasing that enemy of the Thirty gods, <s>Arjuna</s> honored him with heavenly ornaments, garlands, and garments,

children.text: ahiṃsakaṃ sakhyam upetya sāgnikaṃ praṇamya sa brahmasutaṃ gṛhaṃ yayau ||
children.translated_text: formed a harmless friendship before the sacred fire, bowed to the son of <s>Brahmā</s>, and went home.
After meeting with <s>Pulastya</s>, the mighty lord of rākṣasas
was embraced, received as a guest, and, ashamed, was dismissed.
And <s>Pulastya</s>, son of the grandfather <s>Brahmā</s> and best of sages,
having freed <s>Daśagrīva</s>, went to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: evaṃ sa rāvaṇaḥ prāptaḥ kārtavīryāt tu dharṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: Thus that <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, after suffering humiliation from <s>Kārtavīrya</s>,
and also through <s>Pulastya</s>'s words, obtained release again.
Thus, O descendant of <s>Rāghava</s>, there are stronger men than the strong;

children.text: nāvajñā parataḥ kāryā ya icchecchreya ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one who wishes his own welfare should not show contempt for another.

children.text: tataḥ sa rājā piśitāśanānāṃ sahasrabāhor upalabhya maitrīm
children.translated_text: Then that king of flesh-eaters, having gained the friendship of the thousand-armed one,

children.text: punar narāṇāṃ kadanaṃ cakāra cacāra sarvāṃ pṛthivīṃ ca darpāt ||
children.translated_text: again made slaughter among men and roamed the whole earth in arrogance.
But <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of rākṣasas, released by <s>Arjuna</s>,
wandered over the whole earth, not disheartened by what had happened.

children.text: rākṣasaṃ vā manuṣyaṃ vā śṛṇute yaṃ balādhikam
children.translated_text: Whatever rākṣasa or human being he heard was stronger,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, proud, approached him and challenged him in battle.
Then once he went to the city <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, ruled by <s>Vālin</s>,
and challenged golden-garlanded <s>Vālin</s> to battle.
Then <s>Tāra</s>, a monkey minister, lord and father of <s>Tārā</s>,
spoke these words to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, who had come seeking battle:

children.text: rākṣasendra gato vālī yaste pratibalo bhavet
children.translated_text: O lord of rākṣasas, <s>Vālin</s>, who would be a match for you, has gone away;

children.text: nānyaḥ pramukhataḥ sthātuṃ tava śaktaḥ plavaṃgamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: no other monkey is able to stand before you face to face.
After observing his twilight worship at the four oceans, O <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: imaṃ muhūrtam āyāti vālī tiṣṭha muhūrtakam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vālin</s> will come this very moment; wait a little while.

children.text: etān asthicayān paśya ya ete śaṅkhapāṇḍurāḥ
children.translated_text: Look at these heaps of bones, which are white as conch shells;
O king, these belonged to those seeking battle, through the power of the monkey-lord.
Either you have drunk the nectar of immortality, O <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, rākṣasa,

children.text: tathā vālinam āsādya tadantaṃ tava jīvitam ||
children.translated_text: or, having approached <s>Vālin</s>, your life will come to that end.
But if you are hastening to die, go to the southern ocean;

children.text: vālinaṃ drakṣyase tatra bhūmiṣṭham iva bhāskaram ||
children.translated_text: there you will see <s>Vālin</s>, like the sun standing on the earth.

children.text: sa tu tāraṃ vinirbhartsya rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of rākṣasas, rebuked <s>Tāra</s>,
and, mounting that <s>Puṣpaka</s>, set out for the southern ocean.
There, like a golden mountain, with a face like the young sun,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> saw <s>Vālin</s> intent upon twilight worship.
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, black as collyrium, descended from <s>Puṣpaka</s>.
He quickly ran up with silent steps to seize <s>Vālī</s>.
But <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, even as <s>Vālī</s> happened to open his eyes,
was seen with evil intent, and <s>Vālī</s> did not become alarmed.

children.text: śaśam ālakṣya siṃho vā pannagaṃ garuḍo yathā
children.translated_text: Just as a lion, seeing a hare, or <s>Garuḍa</s>, seeing a serpent,

children.text: na cintayati taṃ vālī rāvaṇaṃ pāpaniścayam ||
children.translated_text: so <s>Vālī</s> gave no thought to that <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, fixed upon evil.
"Desiring to seize this evil-minded <s>Rāvaṇa</s> today,
I shall make him hang from my armpit and go to the great oceans.
They will see my enemy placed in my lap, with thighs, arms, and garment slipping,
<s>Daśagrīva</s> hanging down like a serpent in <s>Garuḍa</s>'s grasp."

children.text: ityevaṃ matim āsthāya vālī karṇam upāśritaḥ
children.translated_text: Having settled upon this thought, <s>Vālī</s>, with his ear attentive,
stood there reciting the Vedic mantras, like the king of mountains.
Those two kings, the monkey and the rākṣasa, each desiring to seize the other,
both intent and proud of their strength, strove for that deed.

children.text: hastagrāhyaṃ tu taṃ matvā pādaśabdena rāvaṇam
children.translated_text: But thinking <s>Rāvaṇa</s> within reach of his hand from the sound of his feet,
<s>Vālī</s>, though facing away, seized him, as a bird seizes a serpent.

children.text: grahītukāmaṃ taṃ gṛhya rakṣasām īśvaraṃ hariḥ
children.translated_text: Having seized that lord of the rākṣasas who wished to seize him, the monkey
sprang swiftly into the sky, making him hang from his armpit.

children.text: sa taṃ pīḍayamānastu vitudantaṃ nakhair muhuḥ
children.translated_text: Though <s>Rāvaṇa</s> kept tormenting him and repeatedly piercing him with his nails,
<s>Vālī</s> carried <s>Rāvaṇa</s> off as the wind carries a cloud.
Then, as <s>Daśānana</s> was being carried away, those fierce rākṣasa ministers,
wishing to free him, ran after him, roaring.
Followed by them, <s>Vālī</s>, moving in the middle of the sky, shone forth
like the sun standing in the sky and followed by masses of clouds.
Those foremost rākṣasas could not overtake <s>Vālī</s> once he had gone ahead,
and, exhausted by the speed of his arms and thighs, they fell down.
Even great mountains drew aside from <s>Vālī</s>'s path as he went.
The monkey-king, of very great speed, whose flight birds could not match,
in due order revered all the oceans at twilight time.
Honored by beings moving in the sky, the sky-going monkey
<s>Vālī</s> came to the western ocean together with <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: tatra saṃdhyām upāsitvā snātvā japtvā ca vānaraḥ
children.translated_text: There, after performing the twilight rite, bathing, and reciting prayers, the monkey
went to the northern ocean, carrying <s>Daśānana</s>.
Having performed the twilight rite at the northern ocean,
<s>Vālī</s>, still carrying <s>Daśānana</s>, went to the eastern great reservoir of waters.

children.text: tatrāpi saṃdhyām anvāsya vāsaviḥ sa harīśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: After observing the twilight rite there as well, that son of <s>Vāsava</s>, lord of monkeys,
again returned, holding <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, toward <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>.
After observing twilight worship at all four oceans, the monkey,
wearied from carrying <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, descended in the grove near <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>.
Then the best of monkeys released <s>Rāvaṇa</s> from his armpit

children.text: kutastvam iti covāca prahasan rāvaṇaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: and, laughing, said to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, "Where have you come from?"
Then the lord of rākṣasas, filled with great amazement and looking about in exhaustion,

children.text: rākṣaseśo harīśaṃ tam idaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: spoke these words to that lord of monkeys:
"O king of monkeys, equal to <s>Mahendra</s>, I am <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, king of rākṣasas.
I came here desiring battle, and today I have been encountered by you.

children.text: aho balam aho vīryam aho gambhīratā ca te
children.translated_text: Ah, your strength! Ah, your heroism! Ah, your depth of spirit!
By it I was seized like a beast and whirled around the four oceans.

children.text: evam aśrāntavad vīra śīghram eva ca vānara
children.translated_text: O hero, O monkey, while seeming unwearied and very swift,
what other hero could stride on while carrying me?

children.text: trayāṇām eva bhūtānāṃ gatir eṣā plavaṃgama
children.translated_text: O leaper, this is the course only of three beings,
of mind, wind, and <s>Suparṇa</s>, or else of you; of this there is no doubt.
Therefore, having seen your strength, O bull among monkeys,

children.text: tvayā saha ciraṃ sakhyaṃ susnigdhaṃ pāvakāgrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: I wish for lasting and most affectionate friendship with you before the fire.
Wives, sons, city, kingdom, pleasures, clothing, and food,
all shall be undivided between us, O lord of monkeys."
Then, after kindling the fire, those two, monkey and rākṣasa,
embraced each other and entered into brotherhood.
Then those two, the monkey and the rākṣasa, with hands clasped around each other,

children.text: kiṣkindhāṃ viśatur hṛṣṭau siṃhau giriguhām iva ||
children.translated_text: entered <s>Kiṣkindhā</s> joyfully, like two lions entering a mountain cave.

children.text: sa tatra māsam uṣitaḥ sugrīva iva rāvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: There <s>Rāvaṇa</s> stayed for a month, as if he were <s>Sugrīva</s>,
along with the low ministers who had come, intent on destroying the three worlds.

children.text: evam etat purāvṛttaṃ vālinā rāvaṇaḥ prabho
children.translated_text: "Thus, my lord, this happened long ago: <s>Rāvaṇa</s> was subdued by <s>Vālī</s>
and also made his brother in the presence of the fire.
O <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Vālī</s> possessed unsurpassed and supreme strength,

children.text: so 'pi tvayā vinirdagdhaḥ śalabho vahninā yathā ||
children.translated_text: yet even he was burned up by you, like a moth by fire."
Then <s>Rāma</s>, with joined palms and full of humility,
asked the sage who had his dwelling in the southern quarter, speaking these meaningful words:

children.text: atulaṃ balam etābhyāṃ vālino rāvaṇasya ca
children.translated_text: "The strength of these two, <s>Vālī</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, was incomparable;

children.text: na tvetau hanumadvīryaiḥ samāviti matir mama ||
children.translated_text: but my thought is that these two were not equal to <s>Hanumān</s> in valor.

children.text: śauryaṃ dākṣyaṃ balaṃ dhairyaṃ prājñatā nayasādhanam
children.translated_text: Heroism, skill, strength, firmness, wisdom, success in policy,
prowess, and power have made their abode in <s>Hanumān</s>.
Seeing this monkey army despondent before the ocean,

children.text: samāśvāsya kapīn bhūyo yojanānāṃ śataṃ plutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he encouraged the monkeys and then leapt a hundred yojanas.
After assaulting the city of <s>Laṅkā</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s inner palace,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā saṃbhāṣitā cāpi sītā viśvāsitā tathā ||
children.translated_text: he saw <s>Sītā</s>, spoke with her, and reassured her.
The commanders of the army, the ministers' sons, the servants, and <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s son:
these were struck down there by <s>Hanumān</s> alone.
Again, freed from bondage, after speaking with <s>Daśānana</s>,
<s>Laṅkā</s> was reduced to ashes by him, like the earth by fire.

children.text: na kālasya na śakrasya na viṣṇor vittapasya ca
children.translated_text: Neither of Time, nor of <s>Śakra</s>, nor of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, nor of the lord of wealth

children.text: karmāṇi tāni śrūyante yāni yuddhe hanūmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: are deeds heard of like those which were <s>Hanūmat</s>'s in battle.

children.text: etasya bāhuvīryeṇa laṅkā sītā ca lakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: By the heroic strength of this one's arms, <s>Laṅkā</s>, <s>Sītā</s>, and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>

children.text: prāpto mayā jayaścaiva rājyaṃ mitrāṇi bāndhavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: were gained by me, and victory too, my kingdom, my friends, and my kinsmen.

children.text: hanūmān yadi me na syād vānarādhipateḥ sakhā
children.translated_text: If <s>Hanūmān</s>, the friend of the lord of the monkeys, had not been mine,

children.text: pravṛttam api ko vettuṃ jānakyāḥ śaktimān bhavet ||
children.translated_text: who would have been able even to learn the news of <s>Jānakī</s>?
For what reason, then, when enmity arose at that time, was <s>Vālī</s> not burned by him,

children.text: tadā vaire samutpanne na dagdho vīrudho yathā ||
children.translated_text: out of desire to do what was dear to <s>Sugrīva</s>, as a creeper is burned?

children.text: na hi veditavānmanye hanūmān ātmano balam
children.translated_text: For I think <s>Hanūmān</s> did not know his own strength,
since he saw the monkey-lord, dearer than life, being afflicted.
All this about <s>Hanūmat</s>, revered sir, O great sage,
tell me in full and in its true nature, O you who are honored by the immortals.
Having heard <s>Rāghava</s>'s reasoned speech, the seer then,

children.text: hanūmataḥ samakṣaṃ tam idaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: in <s>Hanūmat</s>'s presence, spoke these words to him:

children.text: satyam etad raghuśreṣṭha yad bravīṣi hanūmataḥ
children.translated_text: This is true, best of the <s>Raghus</s>, what you say about <s>Hanūmat</s>.

children.text: na bale vidyate tulyo na gatau na matau paraḥ ||
children.translated_text: In strength there is none equal to him; in speed and understanding there is none superior.
But a curse was once given to him by sages whose curses never fail,

children.text: na veditā balaṃ yena balī sann arimardanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by which, though strong, he did not know his strength, O crusher of enemies.

children.text: bālye 'pyetena yat karma kṛtaṃ rāma mahābala
children.translated_text: Even in childhood, O mighty <s>Rāma</s>, the deed done by him
cannot be fully described to you, because of its extreme childishness.
But if you have the wish to hear that, O <s>Rāghava</s>,
compose your mind, <s>Rāma</s>, and listen; I shall tell it.
There is a mountain named <s>Sumeru</s>, golden through a boon given by the sun,

children.text: yatra rājyaṃ praśāstyasya kesarī nāma vai pitā ||
children.translated_text: where his father, named <s>Kesarī</s>, indeed ruled a kingdom.
His beloved wife became renowned as <s>Añjanā</s>,

children.text: janayāmāsa tasyāṃ vai vāyur ātmajam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: and in her <s>Vāyu</s> begot an excellent son of his own.
Then <s>Añjanā</s> gave birth to this one, shining like a rice awn,
and, wishing to bring fruits, she went out into the forest thicket.

children.text: eṣa mātur viyogācca kṣudhayā ca bhṛśārditaḥ
children.translated_text: Because of separation from his mother and because he was greatly afflicted by hunger,

children.text: ruroda śiśur atyarthaṃ śiśuḥ śarabharāḍ iva ||
children.translated_text: the child cried exceedingly, a child like a young śarabha.
Then he saw the rising <s>Vivasvant</s>, resembling a mass of hibiscus flowers,
and, from desire for fruit, he leapt up toward the sun.
The child, facing the young sun, himself like the young sun embodied,
wishing to seize the young sun, sprang through the middle of the sky.
As <s>Hanūmat</s>, still in his infant state, was leaping in this way,
a very great amazement arose among gods, demons, and siddhas.

children.text: nāpyevaṃ vegavān vāyur garuḍo na manastathā
children.translated_text: Neither the wind, nor <s>Garuḍa</s>, nor the mind is so swift
as this son of <s>Vāyu</s> moves through the highest sky.
If such are the speed and stride of this child even now,

children.text: yauvanaṃ balam āsādya kathaṃ vego bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: when he has reached youth and strength, what will his velocity be?

children.text: tam anuplavate vāyuḥ plavantaṃ putram ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vāyu</s> followed his own son as he leapt,
protecting him from fear of the sun's burning heat, cool as a mass of frost.
Then he crossed many thousands of yojanas through the sky,
and by his father's strength and by childishness came near <s>Bhāskara</s>.

children.text: śiśur eṣa tvadoṣajña iti matvā divākaraḥ
children.translated_text: Thinking, "This is a child who does not know fault," the day-maker

children.text: kāryaṃ cātra samāyattam ityevaṃ na dadāha saḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also, "A task depends on this matter," did not burn him.

children.text: yam eva divasaṃ hyeṣa grahītuṃ bhāskaraṃ plutaḥ
children.translated_text: On the very day when he leapt to seize <s>Bhāskara</s>,

children.text: tam eva divasaṃ rāhur jighṛkṣati divākaram ||
children.translated_text: on that same day <s>Rāhu</s> was wishing to seize the day-maker.
And touched by this one, <s>Rāma</s>, upon the chariot of the sun,
<s>Rāhu</s>, crusher of moon and sun, drew back in fear.
Going to <s>Indra</s>'s palace, the angry son of <s>Siṃhikā</s>

children.text: abravīd bhrukuṭīṃ kṛtvā devaṃ devagaṇair vṛtam ||
children.translated_text: knitted his brow and spoke to the god, surrounded by hosts of gods:
After giving me the removal of my hunger in the moon and sun, O <s>Vāsava</s>,

children.text: kim idaṃ tat tvayā dattam anyasya balavṛtrahan ||
children.translated_text: why has that which you gave been given to another, O mighty slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>?

children.text: adyāhaṃ parvakāle tu jighṛkṣuḥ sūryam āgataḥ
children.translated_text: Today, at the appointed time, I came wishing to seize the sun,

children.text: athānyo rāhur āsādya jagrāha sahasā ravim ||
children.translated_text: but another <s>Rāhu</s> approached and suddenly seized the sun.

children.text: sa rāhor vacanaṃ śrutvā vāsavaḥ saṃbhramānvitaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Rāhu</s>'s words, <s>Vāsava</s>, filled with alarm,
sprang up, leaving his seat and lifting his golden garland.
Then, upon the four-tusked one, resembling a peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>, streaming with rut,
lofty, adorned, and laughing aloud with golden bells,

children.text: indraḥ karīndram āruhya rāhuṃ kṛtvā puraḥsaram
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> mounted the lord of elephants, set <s>Rāhu</s> in front,
and went to where the sun was, together with this <s>Hanūmat</s>.
Then <s>Rāhu</s>, leaving <s>Vāsava</s>, went with excessive haste,

children.text: anena ca sa vai dṛṣṭa ādhāvañśailakūṭavat ||
children.translated_text: and this one saw him rushing like a mountain peak.

children.text: tataḥ sūryaṃ samutsṛjya rāhum evam avekṣya ca
children.translated_text: Then, giving up the sun and looking at <s>Rāhu</s> in this way,
he leapt again into the sky to seize the son of <s>Siṃhikā</s>.
Seeing the monkey rushing, having abandoned the sun, O <s>Rāma</s>,
<s>Rāhu</s> turned back, with only his mouth remaining toward him, and fled away.
The son of <s>Siṃhikā</s>, hoping for <s>Indra</s> as his protector,
cried again and again in terror, "<s>Indra</s>! <s>Indra</s>!"
Hearing the voice of <s>Rāhu</s> as he cried out, recognized even before he was seen,

children.text: śrutvendrovāca mā bhaiṣīr ayam enaṃ nihanmyaham ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> said, "Do not fear. I shall strike this one down."

children.text: airāvataṃ tato dṛṣṭvā mahat tad idam ityapi
