children.translated_text: Then, seeing <s>Airāvata</s>, and thinking, "This too is a great fruit,"
<s>Māruti</s> rushed at that king of elephants.
At that time, as he ran in his desire to seize <s>Airāvata</s>,

children.text: muhūrtam abhavad ghoram indrāgnyor iva bhāsvaram ||
children.translated_text: his form for a moment became dreadful, brilliant like <s>Indra</s> and fire.
But as he rushed in this way, the lord of <s>Śacī</s>, not greatly angered,
with the thunderbolt, hurled violently from the end of his hand.
Then this child fell upon the mountain, struck by <s>Indra</s>'s thunderbolt;
and as he fell, his left jaw was broken.
But when the child had fallen there, stunned by the blow of the thunderbolt,
<s>Pavana</s> grew angry at <s>Indra</s>, and for the misfortune of creatures.
The mighty lord, entering within living beings, closed up the channels of excrement and urine,
and he obstructed all beings, as <s>Vāsava</s> may hold back the rains for years.
Because of <s>Vāyu</s>'s wrath, beings everywhere became without breath;
their joints breaking, they became like pieces of wood.
Without svadhā offerings, without vaṣaṭ-calls, without rites, and deprived of dharma,
the three worlds, because of <s>Vāyu</s>'s wrath, appeared as though placed in hell.
Then the creatures, together with gandharvas, gods, asuras, and humans,
ran to <s>Prajāpati</s>, afflicted by pain and seeking relief.
The gods, with joined palms and bellies like mere hollows, said:

children.text: tvayā sma bhagavan sṛṣṭāḥ prajānātha caturvidhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: By you, blessed lord, lord of creatures, we four kinds of beings were created.

children.text: tvayā datto 'yam asmākam āyuṣaḥ pavanaḥ patiḥ
children.translated_text: By you this <s>Pavana</s>, lord of life, was given to us;

children.text: so 'smān prāṇeśvaro bhūtvā kasmād eṣo 'dya sattama ||
children.translated_text: so why has he, having become our lord of breath, O best of beings,

children.text: rurodha duḥkhaṃ janayann antaḥpura iva striyaḥ
children.translated_text: obstructed us today, producing suffering, like women in an inner chamber?

children.text: tasmāt tvāṃ śaraṇaṃ prāptā vāyunopahatā vibho ||
children.translated_text: Therefore we have come to you for refuge, O mighty one, stricken by <s>Vāyu</s>.

children.text: vāyusaṃrodhajaṃ duḥkham idaṃ no nuda śatruhan ||
children.translated_text: Remove this pain of ours, born from the obstruction of <s>Vāyu</s>, O destroyer of enemies.

children.text: etat prajānāṃ śrutvā tu prajānāthaḥ prajāpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing this statement of the creatures, <s>Prajāpati</s>, lord of creatures,

children.text: kāraṇād iti tān uktvā prajāḥ punar abhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: said to them, 'It is for a cause,' and then spoke again to the creatures:

children.text: yasmin vaḥ kāraṇe vāyuścukrodha ca rurodha ca
children.translated_text: Hear fully that reason on account of which <s>Vāyu</s> became angry with you and obstructed you,

children.text: prajāḥ śṛṇudhvaṃ tat sarvaṃ śrotavyaṃ cātmanaḥ kṣamam ||
children.translated_text: and which it is proper for your own sake to hear.
His son has today been struck down by <s>Indra</s>, lord of the immortals;

children.text: rāhor vacanam ājñāya rājñā vaḥ kopito 'nilaḥ ||
children.translated_text: hearing <s>Rāhu</s>'s words, O people, the king has angered <s>Anila</s>.
Bodiless <s>Vāyu</s> moves within bodies, protecting them;

children.text: śarīraṃ hi vinā vāyuṃ samatāṃ yāti reṇubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: for without <s>Vāyu</s>, a body becomes equal to dust.

children.text: vāyuḥ prāṇāḥ sukhaṃ vāyur vāyuḥ sarvam idaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: <s>Vāyu</s> is the breaths; <s>Vāyu</s> is happiness; <s>Vāyu</s> is this whole world.

children.text: vāyunā samparityaktaṃ na sukhaṃ vindate jagat ||
children.translated_text: When abandoned by <s>Vāyu</s>, the world does not find happiness.

children.text: adyaiva ca parityaktaṃ vāyunā jagad āyuṣā
children.translated_text: Today this world has indeed been abandoned by <s>Vāyu</s>, its life;
today these beings stand breathless, like wood and walls.

children.text: tad yāmastatra yatrāste māruto rukprado hi vaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore let us go there where <s>Māruta</s> is staying, for he is causing you pain;
let us not go to destruction without appeasing the son of <s>Aditi</s>.
Then <s>Prajāpati</s>, together with the creatures and with gods, gandharvas, serpents, and guhyakas,

children.text: jagāma tatrāsyati yatra mārutaḥ sutaṃ surendrābhihataṃ pragṛhya saḥ ||
children.translated_text: went to the place where <s>Māruta</s> was, holding his son who had been struck by the lord of gods.
Then the four-faced one saw the son of <s>Sadāgati</s>, lying in his lap and shining like the sun, fire, and gold,
and, together with gods, siddhas, seers, serpents, and rākṣasas, he felt compassion.
Then <s>Vāyu</s>, distressed by the slaying of his son, saw the grandsire;

children.text: śiśukaṃ taṃ samādāya uttasthau dhātur agrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: taking up that little child, he stood before the Creator.
Adorned with moving earrings, a diadem, garlands, and ornaments of refined gold,
<s>Vāyu</s> fell at the feet of <s>Vedhas</s>, bowing three times.
Then the first knower of the Veda, splendid with dangling ornaments,

children.text: vāyum utthāpya hastena śiśuṃ taṃ parimṛṣṭavān ||
children.translated_text: raised <s>Vāyu</s> with his hand and stroked that child.
Thereupon, merely touched with ease by the lotus-born god,

children.text: jalasiktaṃ yathā sasyaṃ punar jīvitam āptavān ||
children.translated_text: he regained life, like a crop sprinkled with water.

children.text: prāṇavantam imaṃ dṛṣṭvā prāṇo gandhavaho mudā
children.translated_text: Seeing him full of breath, <s>Prāṇa</s>, the bearer of fragrance, joyfully
moved again through all beings, as before, after having been restrained.
Freed from the disorder caused by the wind, the creatures became joyful,
like lotus-ponds with their lotuses freed from a cold wind.
Then the deity <s>Brahmā</s>, triple in form, three-peaked, three-aboded, and worshiped by the gods,
spoke out of a desire to please <s>Māruta</s>.
O <s>Mahendra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Dhaneśvara</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>,

children.text: jānatām api tat sarvaṃ hitaṃ vakṣyāmi śrūyatām ||
children.translated_text: though you already know all this, I shall speak what is beneficial; listen.

children.text: anena śiśunā kāryaṃ kartavyaṃ vo bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: A task will have to be accomplished for you by this child;
all of you must give him boons that will bring satisfaction to this <s>Māruta</s>.
Then the thousand-eyed one, his auspicious face flushed with affection,
lifted up a garland made of lotuses and said this:
Since this child's jaw was injured by the thunderbolt released from my hand,
this tiger among monkeys will by name become <s>Hanumān</s>.

children.text: aham evāsya dāsyāmi paramaṃ varam uttamam
children.translated_text: I myself shall give him a supreme and excellent boon:
from this time onward he will be invulnerable to my thunderbolt.
Then the blessed <s>Mārtaṇḍa</s>, remover of darkness, spoke there:
I give him a hundredth portion of my own radiance.

children.text: yadā tu śāstrāṇyadhyetuṃ śaktir asya bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: When he becomes capable of studying the śāstras,

children.text: tadāsya śāstraṃ dāsyāmi yena vāgmī bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: then I shall give him knowledge of śāstra, by which he will become eloquent.
And <s>Varuṇa</s> granted a boon: death shall not befall him,
even after a hundred myriads of years, from my noose or from water.
<s>Yama</s> too, well pleased, grants him invulnerability to the rod and constant freedom from disease,
and also freedom from despondency in battle.
This mace of mine shall not kill him in battles,
so spoke the boon-giving tawny one-eyed god at that time.

children.text: matto madāyudhānāṃ ca na vadhyo 'yaṃ bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: He will not be killable by me or by my weapons;
thus also was a supreme boon given to him by <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
He will be invulnerable to all the rods of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: dīrghāyuśca mahātmā ca iti brahmābravīd vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Long-lived and great-souled," <s>Brahmā</s> spoke these words.
But <s>Viśvakarman</s>, seeing this child like the young sun,

children.text: śilpināṃ pravaraḥ prāha varam asya mahāmatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the foremost of craftsmen, wise-minded, declared a boon for him:
"Whatever weapons of the gods have been fashioned here,
in battle-time he shall be invulnerable to those."

children.text: tataḥ surāṇāṃ tu varair dṛṣṭvā hyenam alaṃkṛtam
children.translated_text: Then, seeing him adorned with the boons of the gods,
the four-faced world-teacher, with a pleased face, spoke to <s>Vāyu</s>:
"A terror to enemies and a giver of fearlessness to friends,

children.text: ajeyo bhavitā te 'tra putro māruta mārutiḥ ||
children.translated_text: your son here, O <s>Māruta</s>, <s>Māruti</s>, shall be unconquerable.
For the destruction of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and for the delight of <s>Rāma</s>,
he will perform hair-raising deeds in battle."

children.text: evam uktvā tam āmantrya mārutaṃ te 'maraiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus and taken leave of <s>Māruta</s>, those immortals,
with the Grandfather at their head, all went away as they had come.

children.text: so 'pi gandhavahaḥ putraṃ pragṛhya gṛham ānayat
children.translated_text: The bearer of fragrances also took his son and brought him home;
after telling <s>Añjanā</s> of the boon that had been given, he departed.
Having obtained boons, O <s>Rāma</s>, this one, endowed with the strength of those gifts,
was filled by the power settled in himself, like the ocean.
As this foremost of monkeys was being filled with strength,
he fearlessly committed offenses in the hermitages of the great seers.

children.text: srugbhāṇḍān agnihotraṃ ca valkalānāṃ ca saṃcayān
children.translated_text: Sacrificial ladles, vessels, the agnihotra, and heaps of bark garments,
he made broken, torn apart, and ruined, though they belonged to men of perfect calm.
Knowing that <s>Brahmā</s> had made him invulnerable to all brahma-staffs,

children.text: jānanta ṛṣayastaṃ vai kṣamante tasya nityaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the seers always endured him.

children.text: yadā kesariṇā tveṣa vāyunā sāñjanena ca
children.translated_text: But when this monkey, though restrained by <s>Kesarin</s>, by <s>Vāyu</s>,
and by <s>Añjanā</s>, kept overstepping the proper bounds,
then the great seers of the lineages of <s>Bhṛgu</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s>, angry,
cursed him, O best of the <s>Raghus</s>, though their anger was not excessive.

children.text: bādhase yat samāśritya balam asmān plavaṃgama
children.translated_text: "Because, O leaping one, you harass us by relying on your strength,
for a long time you shall not know that strength, deluded by our curse."
Then his force and vigor were taken away by the power of the great seers' words,
and, moving with a gentle disposition, he no longer trespassed in the hermitages.
Now there was one named <s>Ṛkṣarajas</s>, father of <s>Vālin</s> and <s>Sugrīva</s>;
he was king of all the monkeys, like the sun in splendor.

children.text: sa tu rājyaṃ ciraṃ kṛtvā vānarāṇāṃ harīśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: After ruling the monkeys for a long time, that lord of monkeys,
the one named <s>Ṛkṣarajas</s>, then met the law of time.
When he had set, <s>Vālin</s> was made king in his father's seat

children.text: pitrye pade kṛto rājā sugrīvo vālinaḥ pade ||
children.translated_text: by ministers skilled in counsel, and <s>Sugrīva</s> was placed in <s>Vālin</s>'s former position.
His friendship with <s>Sugrīva</s> was without division, without defect,
and impossible to take away, like the friendship of wind with fire.

children.text: eṣa śāpavaśād eva na veda balam ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: It is because of the curse itself that this one does not know his own strength,
when the enmity of <s>Vālin</s> and <s>Sugrīva</s> arose because of <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: na hyeṣa rāma sugrīvo bhrāmyamāṇo 'pi vālinā
children.translated_text: For even when <s>Sugrīva</s>, O <s>Rāma</s>, was being driven about by <s>Vālin</s>,

children.text: vedayāno na ca hyeṣa balam ātmani mārutiḥ ||
children.translated_text: this <s>Māruti</s> did not recognize the strength within himself.
In prowess, energy, intelligence, majesty, good nature, sweetness, and policy,
in depth, cleverness, excellent heroism, and courage, who in the world is superior to <s>Hanūmat</s>?

children.text: asau purā vyākaraṇaṃ grahīṣyan sūryonmukhaḥ pṛṣṭhagamaḥ kapīndraḥ
children.translated_text: In former times, wishing to learn grammar, the monkey-lord faced the sun and went backward;

children.text: udyadgirer astagiriṃ jagāma granthaṃ mahad dhārayad aprameyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: from the mountain of sunrise to the mountain of sunset he went, retaining a great, immeasurable treatise.

children.text: pravīvikṣor iva sāgarasya lokān didhakṣor iva pāvakasya
children.translated_text: Who will stand before <s>Hanūmat</s>, who is like the ocean wishing to overflow,

children.text: lokakṣayeṣveva yathāntakasya hanūmataḥ sthāsyati kaḥ purastāt ||
children.translated_text: like fire wishing to burn the worlds, like <s>Antaka</s> at the destruction of the worlds?

children.text: eṣo 'pi cānye ca mahākapīndrāḥ sugrīvamaindadvividāḥ sanīlāḥ
children.translated_text: This one too, and other great monkey-lords, <s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>Mainda</s>, <s>Dvivida</s>, and <s>Nīla</s>,

children.text: satāratāreyanalāḥ sarambhās tvatkāraṇād rāma surair hi sṛṣṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: together with <s>Tārā</s>, <s>Tāreya</s>, <s>Nala</s>, and <s>Sarambha</s>, were created by the gods for your sake, O <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: tad etat kathitaṃ sarvaṃ yanmāṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi
children.translated_text: Thus all this that you ask me has been told;
this deed of <s>Hanūmat</s> in his childhood has been recounted by me.
You have been seen and spoken with, O <s>Rāma</s>; we shall go now."

children.text: evam uktvā gatāḥ sarve ṛṣayaste yathāgatam ||
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, all those seers went away as they had come.

children.text: vimṛśya ca tato rāmo vayasyam akutobhayam
children.translated_text: Then, after reflecting, <s>Rāma</s> embraced his fearless friend,
<s>Pratardana</s>, lord of <s>Kāśi</s>, and said this:

children.text: darśitā bhavatā prītir darśitaṃ sauhṛdaṃ param
children.translated_text: "Affection has been shown by you; supreme goodwill has been shown;

children.text: udyogaśca kṛto rājan bharatena tvayā saha ||
children.translated_text: and effort has been made, O king, by you together with <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: tad bhavān adya kāśeyīṃ purīṃ vārāṇasīṃ vraja
children.translated_text: Therefore let your majesty now go to the Kāśi city, <s>Vārāṇasī</s>,
charming, guarded by you, with fine ramparts and fine gateways."
Having said this much, <s>Kākutstha</s> rose from his excellent seat,
and the righteous one closely embraced him against his chest.

children.text: visṛjya taṃ vayasyaṃ sa svāgatān pṛthivīpatīn
children.translated_text: After dismissing that friend and the kings who had come to welcome him,
<s>Rāghava</s>, smiling, spoke words sweet in syllables:
"Your untroubled affection has been protected by your splendor;

children.text: dharmaśca niyato nityaṃ satyaṃ ca bhavatāṃ sadā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> is always fixed among you, and truth is always yours.

children.text: yuṣmākaṃ ca prabhāvena tejasā ca mahātmanām
children.translated_text: By the power and splendor of you great-souled ones,
the evil-minded, wicked-souled <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of rākṣasas, was slain.

children.text: hetumātram ahaṃ tatra bhavatāṃ tejasāṃ hataḥ
children.translated_text: I was merely the instrumental cause there; through your splendor
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, with his host, his sons, and his kinsmen, was slain in battle.
You were brought together by great-souled <s>Bharata</s>,
after he heard that the daughter of king <s>Janaka</s> had been carried off in the forest.
For all the great-souled kings who were ready for action,

children.text: kālo hyatītaḥ sumahān gamane rocatāṃ matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: a very long time has passed; let your minds now be pleased with departure."
And the kings, filled with great joy, answered him:

children.text: diṣṭyā tvaṃ vijayī rāma rājyaṃ cāpi pratiṣṭhitam ||
children.translated_text: "By good fortune you are victorious, O <s>Rāma</s>, and the kingdom too has been established.

children.text: diṣṭyā pratyāhṛtā sītā diṣṭyā śatruḥ parājitaḥ
children.translated_text: By good fortune <s>Sītā</s> has been brought back; by good fortune the enemy has been defeated.

children.text: eṣa naḥ paramaḥ kāma eṣā naḥ kīrtir uttamā ||
children.translated_text: This is our highest desire; this is our supreme glory,

children.text: yat tvāṃ vijayinaṃ rāma paśyāmo hataśātravam
children.translated_text: that we see you victorious, O <s>Rāma</s>, with your enemies slain.

children.text: upapannaṃ ca kākutstha yat tvam asmān praśaṃsasi ||
children.translated_text: And it is fitting, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, that you praise us,

children.text: praśaṃsārhā hi jānanti praśaṃsāṃ vaktum īdṛśīm
children.translated_text: for those who are worthy of praise know how to utter such praise.

children.text: āpṛcchāmo gamiṣyāmo hṛdistho naḥ sadā bhavān
children.translated_text: We ask your leave and shall go; may you always dwell in our hearts,

children.text: bhavecca te mahārāja prītir asmāsu nityadā ||
children.translated_text: and may your affection for us, great king, remain forever."

children.text: te prayātā mahātmānaḥ pārthivāḥ sarvato diśam
children.translated_text: Those high-souled, heroic kings set out in every direction,
shaking the earth as they joyfully went to their own cities.
With thousands of <s>akṣauhiṇī</s>s (vast army divisions), assembled in many groups,
all those who had gathered for <s>Rāghava</s>'s sake returned, delighted.
And the rulers of the earth, endowed with pride in their armies, said:

children.text: na nāma rāvaṇaṃ yuddhe paśyāmaḥ purataḥ sthitam ||
children.translated_text: "We did not, alas, see <s>Rāvaṇa</s> standing before us in battle.
We were summoned afterward by <s>Bharata</s> to no purpose.

children.text: hatā hi rākṣasāstatra pārthivaiḥ syur na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the rākṣasas there would certainly have been slain by the kings; there is no doubt.
Protected by the strength of <s>Rāma</s>'s arms and by that of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
we would have fought happily, free from anxiety, on the far shore of the ocean."
Telling these and thousands of other tales there, the kings,
great chariot-warriors, entered their own realms.

children.text: yathāpurāṇi te gatvā ratnāni vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: When they had gone to their respective cities, the kings gave various jewels
and offerings to <s>Rāma</s>, wishing to do what was dear to him.
They gave horses, jewels, garments, and elephants fierce with rut,
as well as divine sandalwoods and divine ornaments.
<s>Bharata</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and the great chariot-warrior <s>Śatrughna</s>

children.text: ādāya tāni ratnāni ayodhyām agaman punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: took those jewels and went again to <s>Ayodhyā</s>.
When those bulls among men had reached the lovely city <s>Ayodhyā</s>,
they gave all the jewels to the high-souled <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: pratigṛhya ca tat sarvaṃ prītiyuktaḥ sa rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Receiving all that, <s>Rāghava</s>, filled with affection,
gave all those things to the high-souled <s>Sugrīva</s>.

children.text: vibhīṣaṇāya ca dadau ye cānye ṛkṣavānarāḥ
children.translated_text: He gave them also to <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> and to the other bears and monkeys,
the heroes headed by <s>Hanūmat</s>, and to the mighty rākṣasas.
Then all of them, their minds delighted, received those gifts bestowed by <s>Rāma</s>
and, mighty as they were, bore them upon their heads and arms.
They also drank fragrant honey-wines of various kinds,
ate well-prepared meats, and tasted fruits.

children.text: evaṃ teṣāṃ nivasatāṃ māsaḥ sāgro gatastadā
children.translated_text: As they were staying there in this way, more than a month then passed,

children.text: muhūrtam iva tat sarvaṃ rāmabhaktyā samarthayan ||
children.translated_text: yet through devotion to <s>Rāma</s> they regarded it all as but a moment.

children.text: reme rāmaḥ sa taiḥ sārdhaṃ vānaraiḥ kāmarūpibhiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> took pleasure together with those shape-shifting monkeys,
with the kings of great valor, and with the mighty rākṣasas.

children.text: evaṃ teṣāṃ yayau māso dvitīyaḥ śaiśiraḥ sukham
children.translated_text: Thus a second winter month passed happily
for all the delighted monkeys and rākṣasas.
Then, while those bears, monkeys, and rākṣasas were dwelling there,
the greatly radiant <s>Rāghava</s> said this to <s>Sugrīva</s>:
"Go, gentle one, to <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, unassailable by gods and asuras,
and rule the kingdom, with your ministers, its thorns removed.
With the highest affection, O mighty-armed one, look after <s>Aṅgada</s>,

children.text: paśya tvaṃ hanumantaṃ ca nalaṃ ca sumahābalam ||
children.translated_text: and also <s>Hanūmat</s> and the very mighty <s>Nala</s>.

children.text: suṣeṇaṃ śvaśuraṃ śūraṃ tāraṃ ca balināṃ varam
children.translated_text: Look after your brave father-in-law <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, <s>Tāra</s>, best of the strong,

children.text: kumudaṃ caiva durdharṣaṃ nīlaṃ ca sumahābalam ||
children.translated_text: and invincible <s>Kumuda</s> and the very mighty <s>Nīla</s>.

children.text: vīraṃ śatabaliṃ caiva maindaṃ dvividam eva ca
children.translated_text: Look after the hero <s>Śatabali</s>, and also <s>Mainda</s> and <s>Dvivida</s>,

children.text: gajaṃ gavākṣaṃ gavayaṃ śarabhaṃ ca mahābalam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gaja</s>, <s>Gavākṣa</s>, <s>Gavaya</s>, and the mighty <s>Śarabha</s>.
Look after the invincible king of the bears, the mighty <s>Jāmbavant</s>,
and <s>Gandhamādana</s> too, with affection.
And whatever other high-souled ones have given up their lives for my sake,

children.text: paśya tvaṃ prītisaṃyukto mā caiṣāṃ vipriyaṃ kṛthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: look after them with affection, and do not do anything displeasing to them."

children.text: evam uktvā ca sugrīvaṃ praśasya ca punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to <s>Sugrīva</s> and praised him again and again,
<s>Rāma</s> then addressed <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> in a sweet voice:

children.text: laṅkāṃ praśādhi dharmeṇa saṃmato hyasi pārthiva
children.translated_text: "Rule <s>Laṅkā</s> according to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), for you are accepted as king

children.text: purasya rākṣasānāṃ ca bhrātur vaiśravaṇasya ca ||
children.translated_text: by the city, by the rākṣasas, and by your brother <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>.

children.text: mā ca buddhim adharme tvaṃ kuryā rājan kathaṃcana
children.translated_text: And do not, O king, ever set your mind upon <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) in any way.

children.text: buddhimanto hi rājāno dhruvam aśnanti medinīm ||
children.translated_text: For wise kings surely enjoy the earth.
And I, O king, together with <s>Sugrīva</s>, should always be remembered by you

children.text: smartavyaḥ parayā prītyā gaccha tvaṃ vigatajvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: with supreme affection. Go now, free from anxiety."
Hearing <s>Rāma</s>'s speech, the bears, monkeys, and rākṣasas

children.text: sādhu sādhviti kākutsthaṃ praśaśaṃsuḥ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: praised <s>Kākutstha</s> again and again, saying, "Good! Good!"

children.text: tava buddhir mahābāho vīryam adbhutam eva ca
children.translated_text: "Your wisdom, O mighty-armed one, and your valor are truly wondrous,

children.text: mādhuryaṃ paramaṃ rāma svayambhor iva nityadā ||
children.translated_text: and your supreme sweetness, O <s>Rāma</s>, is always like that of <s>Svayambhū</s>."

children.text: teṣām evaṃ bruvāṇānāṃ vānarāṇāṃ ca rakṣasām
children.translated_text: As the monkeys and rākṣasas were speaking in this way,

children.text: hanūmān praṇato bhūtvā rāghavaṃ vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hanūmat</s>, having bowed down, spoke these words to <s>Rāghava</s>:

children.text: sneho me paramo rājaṃstvayi nityaṃ pratiṣṭhitaḥ
children.translated_text: "My supreme affection, O king, is always fixed upon you,

children.text: bhaktiśca niyatā vīra bhāvo nānyatra gacchati ||
children.translated_text: and my devotion is constant, O hero; my feeling goes nowhere else.
As long as I shall hear the story of <s>Rāma</s>, O hero, upon the surface of the earth,

children.text: tāvaccharīre vatsyantu mama prāṇā na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so long shall the breaths of life remain in my body; there is no doubt."
As he was speaking thus, the king of kings then rose from his seat toward <s>Hanūmat</s>

children.text: utthāya ca pariṣvajya vākyam etad uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: And rising up and embracing him, he spoke these words:

children.text: evam etat kapiśreṣṭha bhavitā nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: "So it will be, best of monkeys; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: lokā hi yāvat sthāsyanti tāvat sthāsyati me kathā ||
children.translated_text: For as long as the worlds shall stand, so long shall my story stand.

children.text: cariṣyati kathā yāvallokān eṣā hi māmikā
children.translated_text: As long as this story of mine shall move through the worlds,
so long shall your life-breaths dwell in your body, child; there is no doubt."

children.text: tato 'sya hāraṃ candrābhaṃ mucya kaṇṭhāt sa rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāghava</s>, taking from his neck a necklace bright as the moon,
glittering with vaidūrya gems, fastened it affectionately on <s>Hanūmat</s>.
With that necklace fastened on his breast, that great monkey
shone like a lordly golden mountain with the moon resting on its summit.
But when they had heard this from <s>Rāghava</s>, the monkeys rose up again and again,
bowed with their heads to his feet, and departed, those mighty ones.
And mighty-armed <s>Sugrīva</s> too was embraced by <s>Rāma</s>,
and righteous <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> was held close against his breast.

children.text: sarve ca te bāṣpagalāḥ sāśrunetrā vicetasaḥ
children.translated_text: All of them, their throats choked with tears, their eyes tearful, and their minds bewildered,

children.text: saṃmūḍhā iva duḥkhena tyajante rāghavaṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: then left <s>Rāghava</s>, as though stunned by grief.
After dismissing the bears, monkeys, and rākṣasas, the great-armed

children.text: bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito rāmaḥ pramumoda sukhī sukham ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, together with his brothers, rejoiced happily in his happiness.
Then, in the afternoon, <s>Rāghava</s>, together with his brothers,
heard a sweet voice speaking from the sky:

children.text: saumya rāma nirīkṣasva saumyena vadanena mām
children.translated_text: "Gentle <s>Rāma</s>, look upon me with a gentle face.

children.text: kailāsaśikharāt prāptaṃ viddhi māṃ puṣpakaṃ prabho ||
children.translated_text: Know me, lord, as <s>Puṣpaka</s>, come from the summit of <s>Kailāsa</s>.

children.text: tava śāsanam ājñāya gato 'smi dhanadaṃ prati
children.translated_text: Having obeyed your command, I went to <s>Dhanada</s>,

children.text: upasthātuṃ naraśreṣṭha sa ca māṃ pratyabhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: best of men, to attend upon him; and he spoke to me:
'You have been conquered by the king, the great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>,
after he slew in battle the invincible <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas.

children.text: mamāpi paramā prītir hate tasmin durātmani
children.translated_text: I too have supreme delight now that that evil-minded one has been slain,
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, together with his host, his sons, ministers, and kinsmen.

children.text: sa tvaṃ rāmeṇa laṅkāyāṃ nirjitaḥ paramātmanā
children.translated_text: Since you were won in <s>Laṅkā</s> by <s>Rāma</s>, the supreme-souled one,

children.text: vaha saumya tam eva tvam aham ājñāpayāmi te ||
children.translated_text: carry that very same one, gentle one; I command you.

children.text: eṣa me paramaḥ kāmo yat tvaṃ rāghavanandanam
children.translated_text: This is my highest desire: that you should carry the delight of the <s>Raghus</s>,
the conveyance for the world. Go, free from distress.'
Knowing that command of great-souled <s>Dhanada</s>,

children.text: tvatsakāśaṃ punaḥ prāptaḥ sa evaṃ pratigṛhṇa mām ||
children.translated_text: I have returned again to your presence. Therefore receive me as I am."
Saying simply, "Very well," <s>Kākutstha</s> honored <s>Puṣpaka</s>
with parched grain, unbroken rice, flowers, and very fragrant perfumes.

children.text: gamyatāṃ ca yathākāmam āgacchestvaṃ yadā smare
children.translated_text: "Go as you wish, and come whenever I remember you."

children.text: evam astviti rāmeṇa visṛṣṭaḥ puṣpakaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Dismissed by <s>Rāma</s> with the words "So be it," <s>Puṣpaka</s> again
went toward the direction it desired, <s>Puṣpaka</s> adorned with flowers.
When that manifold <s>Puṣpaka</s> had disappeared in this way,
<s>Bharata</s>, with joined palms, spoke these words to the delight of the <s>Raghus</s>:
"Most wonderful things are seen while you rule the kingdom;
the utterances of non-human beings are heard again and again.

children.text: anāmayācca martyānāṃ sāgro māso gato hyayam
children.translated_text: More than a month has now passed with mortals free from illness,

children.text: jīrṇānām api sattvānāṃ mṛtyur nāyāti rāghava ||
children.translated_text: and death does not come even to aged beings, <s>Rāghava</s>.
Women give birth to sons, and men are handsome in form;
and there is an even greater joy among the people dwelling in the city, O king.
In due season <s>Vāsava</s> sends down rain like nectar,
and the winds too blow, pleasant to the touch and giving happiness.
'May such a king be ours for a long time,' O lord of men:

children.text: kathayanti pure paurā janā janapadeṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: so the citizens in the city and the people in the countryside say."
Hearing these very sweet words

children.text: śrutvā rāmo mudā yuktaḥ pramumoda sukhī sukham ||
children.translated_text: spoken by <s>Bharata</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, filled with joy, rejoiced happily in happiness.

children.text: sa visṛjya tato rāmaḥ puṣpakaṃ hemabhūṣitam
children.translated_text: Then, after dismissing gold-adorned <s>Puṣpaka</s>,
the great-armed <s>Rāma</s> entered the Aśoka grove at that time.
It was adorned on every side with sandal, aloe, mango,
lofty kāleyaka trees, and also groves of devadāru.
It was covered with priyaṅgu trees, kadambas, and also kurabakas,
with jambū trees, pāṭalīs, and kovidāras.
It was always charming with lovely flowers and delightful fruit-bearing trees,
rich in beautiful shoots and blossoms, and thronged with intoxicated bees.
It was adorned with cuckoos, bhṛṅgarāja birds, and birds of many colors,
with hundreds of variegated mango trees as its ornaments.
Some trees there resembled refined gold, some were like flames of fire,
and others shone like dark collyrium.
There were ponds of various shapes, filled with excellent water,
with costly jewel stairways and inner pavements of crystal.
They had groves of blooming lotuses and blue lotuses and were adorned by cakravāka birds,
and they were beautified by walls of various forms and by stone slabs.
Here and there in the regions of the grove were lawns like vaidūrya gems,
most richly furnished and joined with flowering trees.

children.text: nandanaṃ hi yathendrasya brāhmaṃ caitrarathaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: As <s>Indra</s>'s <s>Nandana</s> is, and as <s>Caitraratha</s> of <s>Brahmā</s> is,
so was that garden of <s>Rāma</s> laid out in form.
It was furnished with many sitting-houses and surrounded by vine-bowers.
Having entered the flourishing Aśoka grove, the delight of the <s>Raghus</s>
sat down on an auspicious seat adorned with clusters of flowers,
covered with a carpet and spread with cushions.
Taking <s>Sītā</s> in his two arms, with excellent honeyed maireya wine...
<s>Kākutstha</s> made her drink, just as <s>Indra</s> gives <s>Śacī</s> ambrosia to drink.

children.text: māṃsāni ca vicitrāṇi phalāni vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: And meats of many kinds, and fruits of various sorts,
the attendants quickly brought for <s>Rāma</s>'s eating.
Women skilled in dancing and song danced attendance upon the king,
young, beautiful women who had come under the influence of drink.

children.text: evaṃ rāmo mudā yuktā sītāṃ surucirānanām
children.translated_text: In this way <s>Rāma</s>, filled with joy, delighted <s>Sītā</s>, whose face was very lovely,
entertaining <s>Vaidehī</s> day after day like a god.

children.text: tathā tu ramamāṇasya tasyaivaṃ śiśiraḥ śubhaḥ
children.translated_text: As that great-souled king, <s>Rāghava</s>, was thus enjoying himself,
the auspicious winter passed by for him.
In the forenoon, after performing the duties toward the citizens according to <s>dharma</s>, he who knew <s>dharma</s>
spent the remaining half of the day inside the inner apartments.

children.text: sītā ca devakāryāṇi kṛtvā paurvāhṇikāni tu
children.translated_text: And <s>Sītā</s>, after performing the morning rites for the gods,
stood with folded hands before all her mothers-in-law without distinction.
Then, adorned with many varied ornaments, she approached <s>Rāma</s>,
as <s>Śacī</s> approaches the thousand-eyed one seated in <s>Triviṣṭapa</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tu rāghavaḥ patnīṃ kalyāṇena samanvitām
children.translated_text: Seeing his wife endowed with auspiciousness, <s>Rāghava</s>

children.text: praharṣam atulaṃ lebhe sādhu sādhviti cābravīt ||
children.translated_text: felt incomparable delight and said, 'Good, good.'
'The gaining of offspring has now come to me, O <s>Vaidehī</s>.

children.text: kim icchasi hi tad brūhi kaḥ kāmaḥ kriyatāṃ tava ||
children.translated_text: Tell me what you desire; what wish of yours should be fulfilled?'

children.text: prahasantī tu vaidehī rāmaṃ vākyam athābravīt
children.translated_text: Then smiling <s>Vaidehī</s> spoke this sentence to <s>Rāma</s>:
'I wish to see the holy hermitage groves, O <s>Rāghava</s>,
situated on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, belonging to sages of holy deeds,
and to stay at the feet of those who eat fruits and roots, O hero.
This is my highest desire, O <s>Kākutstha</s>: among those who live on roots and fruits,
among those blessed ones, I would dwell even for one night.'
'So be it,' was promised by <s>Rāma</s>, whose acts were unwearied:
'Be at ease, O <s>Vaidehī</s>; tomorrow you shall go, without doubt.'

children.text: evam uktvā tu kākutstho maithilīṃ janakātmajām
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to <s>Maithilī</s>, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,
<s>Rāma</s>, <s>Kākutstha</s>, went out to the middle chamber, surrounded by friends.
There, as the king sat, clever men attended upon him,
jesters telling many kinds of stories on every side.
<s>Vijaya</s>, <s>Madhumatta</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Piṅgala</s>, <s>Kuśa</s>,
<s>Surāji</s>, <s>Kāliya</s>, <s>Bhadra</s>, <s>Dantavakra</s>, and <s>Samāgadha</s> were assembled.
These men, delighted, told many kinds of stories,
mixed with jokes, to the great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>.
Then, during one particular story, <s>Rāghava</s> spoke:

children.text: kāḥ kathā nagare bhadra vartante viṣayeṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: 'What stories, good <s>Bhadra</s>, are current in the city and in the provinces?
What do the townsmen and country people say concerning me?

children.text: kiṃ ca sītāṃ samāśritya bharataṃ kiṃ nu lakṣmaṇam ||
children.translated_text: And what concerning <s>Sītā</s>? What about <s>Bharata</s>, or <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>?

children.text: kiṃ nu śatrughnam āśritya kaikeyīṃ mātaraṃ ca me
children.translated_text: What about <s>Śatrughna</s>, and about <s>Kaikeyī</s>, my mother?

children.text: vaktavyatāṃ ca rājāno nave rājye vrajanti hi ||
children.translated_text: For kings in a new kingdom come to be spoken about.'

children.text: evam ukte tu rāmeṇa bhadraḥ prāñjalir abravīt
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāma</s> had spoken thus, <s>Bhadra</s>, with folded hands, said:

children.text: sthitāḥ kathāḥ śubhā rājan vartante puravāsinām ||
children.translated_text: 'Auspicious stories, O king, are current among the city dwellers.
But this victory, gentle one, concerning the slaying of the ten-necked one,
is told of most of all by the citizens in your own city, O bull among men.'

children.text: evam uktastu bhadreṇa rāghavo vākyam abravīt
children.translated_text: When <s>Bhadra</s> had spoken thus, <s>Rāghava</s> said these words:
'Tell everything exactly as it is, without anything omitted.
The auspicious and inauspicious words that the city dwellers say,

children.text: śrutvedānīṃ śubhaṃ kuryāṃ na kuryām aśubhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: having heard them now, I shall do what is good and not do what is bad.
Speak confidently, without fear and without anxiety;

children.text: kathayante yathā paurā janā janapadeṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: tell how the citizens and the people in the provinces talk.'
Thus addressed by <s>Rāghava</s>, <s>Bhadra</s>, with folded hands and composed mind,
replied to the long-armed one with well-pleasing speech:

children.text: śṛṇu rājan yathā paurāḥ kathayanti śubhāśubham
children.translated_text: 'Hear, O king, how the citizens speak good and bad
in crossroads, shops, and streets, and in forests and groves.
<s>Rāma</s> has done a hard thing, building a bridge over the ocean,

children.text: akṛtaṃ pūrvakaiḥ kaiścid devair api sadānavaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: something not done by any of the ancients, even by the gods together with the demons.
And hard-to-assail <s>Rāvaṇa</s> has been killed, together with his forces and vehicles;

children.text: vānarāśca vaśaṃ nītā ṛkṣāśca saha rākṣasaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the monkeys too have been brought under control, and the bears along with the rākṣasas.

children.text: hatvā ca rāvaṇaṃ yuddhe sītām āhṛtya rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: After killing <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle and recovering <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: amarṣaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā svaveśma punar ānayat ||
children.translated_text: putting resentment behind him, brought her back again to his own house.
What sort of pleasure born of union with <s>Sītā</s> is in his heart,

children.text: aṅkam āropya hi purā rāvaṇena balāddhṛtām ||
children.translated_text: since she was formerly placed on <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s lap and carried off by force?

children.text: laṅkām api punar nītām aśokavanikāṃ gatām
children.translated_text: She was even taken again to <s>Laṅkā</s> and went to the <s>Aśoka</s> grove;

children.text: rakṣasāṃ vaśam āpannāṃ kathaṃ rāmo na kutsate ||
children.translated_text: having fallen under the power of rākṣasas, how does <s>Rāma</s> not despise her?
The same will become tolerable even with regard to our own wives,

children.text: yathā hi kurute rājā prajā tam anuvartate ||
children.translated_text: for as the king acts, his subjects follow him.'
'In this way the city dwellers speak many kinds of words,
in all the cities and in the provinces too, O king.'
Hearing that speech, <s>Rāghava</s>, as if deeply afflicted,
said to all his friends, 'How is this report to be stated?'

children.text: sarve tu śirasā bhūmāvabhivādya praṇamya ca
children.translated_text: But all of them, bowing with their heads to the ground and prostrating,

children.text: pratyūcū rāghavaṃ dīnam evam etanna saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: answered the sorrowing <s>Rāghava</s>, 'It is just so; there is no doubt.'

children.text: śrutvā tu vākyaṃ kākutsthaḥ sarveṣāṃ samudīritam
children.translated_text: Hearing the statement uttered by all of them, <s>Kākutstha</s>,
the tormentor of enemies, then dismissed them all.

children.text: visṛjya tu suhṛdvargaṃ buddhyā niścitya rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: After dismissing the circle of his friends and resolving in his mind, <s>Rāghava</s>

children.text: samīpe dvāḥstham āsīnam idaṃ vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: spoke these words to the doorkeeper seated nearby:
'Quickly bring <s>Saumitri</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> of auspicious marks.'
and <s>Bharata</s>, the mighty-armed one, and unconquered <s>Śatrughna</s>.

children.text: rāmasya bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā dvāḥstho mūrdhni kṛtāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard <s>Rāma</s>'s words, the doorkeeper, with joined palms held to his head,
went to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s house and entered unhindered.

children.text: uvāca ca tadā vākyaṃ vardhayitvā kṛtāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after greeting him respectfully with joined palms, he spoke this sentence:

children.text: draṣṭum icchasi rājā tvāṃ gamyatāṃ tatra māciram ||
children.translated_text: "The king wishes to see you. Go there without delay."
"So be it," said <s>Saumitri</s>; and hearing <s>Rāghava</s>'s command,
he quickly mounted a chariot and hurried to <s>Rāghava</s>'s residence.

children.text: prayāntaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā dvāḥstho bharatam antikāt
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> setting out, the doorkeeper went near <s>Bharata</s>

children.text: uvāca prāñjalir vākyaṃ rājā tvāṃ draṣṭum icchati ||
children.translated_text: and, with joined palms, spoke this sentence: "The king wishes to see you."
But <s>Bharata</s>, hearing from the doorkeeper the words uttered by <s>Rāma</s>,
sprang up at once from his seat and then went on foot alone.
Seeing <s>Bharata</s> going in haste, the doorkeeper hurried on with joined palms,

children.text: śatrughnabhavanaṃ gatvā tato vākyaṃ jagāda ha ||
children.translated_text: went to <s>Śatrughna</s>'s palace, and then spoke this sentence:

children.text: ehyāgaccha raghuśreṣṭha rājā tvāṃ draṣṭum icchati
children.translated_text: "Come, come here, best of the <s>Raghus</s>; the king wishes to see you.

children.text: gato hi lakṣmaṇaḥ pūrvaṃ bharataśca mahāyaśāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> has gone before, and so has the greatly renowned <s>Bharata</s>."

children.text: śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tasya śatrughno rāmaśāsanam
children.translated_text: Hearing his words, <s>Śatrughna</s> understood <s>Rāma</s>'s command,

children.text: śirasā vandya dharaṇīṃ prayayau yatra rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: bowed his head to the ground, and set out for the place where <s>Rāghava</s> was.
Hearing that the princes had arrived, his senses troubled by anxiety,
with head bent down and mind dejected, he said this word to the doorkeeper:
"Bring the princes in quickly to my presence.

children.text: eteṣu jīvitaṃ mahyam ete prāṇā bahiścarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In them is my life; they are my life-breaths moving outside my body."
Ordered by the lord of men, the princes, dressed in white garments,
bowed low, stood with joined palms, and entered with collected minds.

children.text: te tu dṛṣṭvā mukhaṃ tasya sagrahaṃ śaśinaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: They saw his face like the moon under eclipse,
like the sun at evening, deprived of its radiance;

children.text: bāṣpapūrṇe ca nayane dṛṣṭvā rāmasya dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: and seeing the wise <s>Rāma</s>'s eyes filled with tears,

children.text: hataśobhaṃ yathā padmaṃ mukhaṃ vīkṣya ca tasya te ||
children.translated_text: and looking upon his face, its beauty struck down like a lotus,
they quickly saluted <s>Rāma</s>'s feet with their heads.
They all stood composed, and <s>Rāma</s> let his tears flow.

children.text: tān pariṣvajya bāhubhyām utthāpya ca mahābhujaḥ
children.translated_text: Embracing them with his arms and raising them up, the mighty-armed one

children.text: āsaneṣvādhvam ityuktvā tato vākyaṃ jagāda ha ||
children.translated_text: said, "Sit down on the seats," and then spoke this sentence:

children.text: bhavanto mama sarvasvaṃ bhavanto mama jīvitam
children.translated_text: "You are my whole possession; you are my life.
With you, O kings, I protect the kingdom that has been established.
You understand the meaning of the śāstras and are firmly settled in judgment;
therefore, coming together, this matter of mine must be considered, O kings."
When all of them had sat down, their minds dejected,
<s>Kākutstha</s> spoke these words with a mouth grown dry:

children.text: sarve śṛṇuta bhadraṃ vo mā kurudhvaṃ mano 'nyathā
children.translated_text: "All of you listen. May good be yours. Do not set your minds otherwise.

children.text: paurāṇāṃ mama sītāyāṃ yādṛśī vartate kathā ||
children.translated_text: What kind of talk exists among the citizens regarding my <s>Sītā</s>,
and what great reproach among the townspeople and countryside too,

children.text: vartate mayi bībhatsaḥ sa me marmāṇi kṛntati ||
children.translated_text: a loathsome one, exists against me: that cuts my vital parts.

children.text: ahaṃ kila kule jāta ikṣvākūṇāṃ mahātmanām
children.translated_text: 'Born, indeed, in the family of the great-souled <s>Ikṣvākus</s>,
how could I bring <s>Sītā</s>, one of sinful conduct, into the city?'

children.text: jānāsi hi yathā saumya daṇḍake vijane vane
children.translated_text: You know, gentle one, how in the lonely forest of <s>Daṇḍaka</s>

children.text: rāvaṇena hṛtā sītā sa ca vidhvaṃsito mayā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s> was carried off by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, and how he was destroyed by me.
In your presence, O <s>Saumitri</s>, <s>Havyavāhana</s> himself,
and <s>Vāyu</s>, moving through the sky, declared the <s>Maithilī</s> sinless.

children.text: candrādityau ca śaṃsete surāṇāṃ saṃnidhau purā
children.translated_text: The moon and the sun also testified long ago in the presence of the gods,
and all the seers likewise declared <s>Janaka</s>'s daughter sinless.
Thus, pure in conduct, in the presence of gods and gandharvas,
on the island of <s>Laṅkā</s>, she was placed into my hand by <s>Mahendra</s>.

children.text: antarātmā ca me vetti sītāṃ śuddhāṃ yaśasvinīm
children.translated_text: My inner self too knows the renowned <s>Sītā</s> to be pure;

children.text: tato gṛhītvā vaidehīm ayodhyām aham āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore, taking <s>Vaidehī</s>, I came back to <s>Ayodhyā</s>.

children.text: ayaṃ tu me mahān vādaḥ śokaśca hṛdi vartate
children.translated_text: But this great controversy and this grief remain in my heart:
the very great reproach of the citizens and of the countryside too.

children.text: akīrtir yasya gīyeta loke bhūtasya kasyacit
children.translated_text: For any being whose ill fame is proclaimed in the world
falls down indeed into the lowest worlds as long as that report is spoken.

children.text: akīrtir nindyate daivaiḥ kīrtir deveṣu pūjyate
children.translated_text: Ill fame is condemned by the gods; fame is honored among the gods.

children.text: kīrtyarthaṃ ca samārambhaḥ sarva eva mahātmanām ||
children.translated_text: And every undertaking of great-souled men is for the sake of fame.

children.text: apyahaṃ jīvitaṃ jahyāṃ yuṣmān vā puruṣarṣabhāḥ
children.translated_text: I would abandon even my life, or you, O bulls among men,
terrified by fear of reproach; how much more, then, <s>Janaka</s>'s daughter.
Therefore see me fallen into an ocean of grief.

children.text: na hi paśyāmyahaṃ bhūyaḥ kiṃcid duḥkham ato 'dhikam ||
children.translated_text: For I see no suffering greater than this any longer.
Tomorrow at daybreak, O <s>Saumitri</s>, mount the chariot managed by <s>Sumantra</s>,
place <s>Sītā</s> on it, and leave her at the border of the realm.
On the farther bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> is the āśrama of great-souled <s>Vālmīki</s>,
shining like heaven, situated on the bank of the <s>Tamasā</s>.
There, in a secluded thicket, leave her, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>,

children.text: śīghram āgaccha saumitre kuruṣva vacanaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: and come back quickly, O <s>Saumitri</s>. Carry out my word.

children.text: na cāsmi prativaktavyaḥ sītāṃ prati kathaṃcana
children.translated_text: And I must not be answered back in any way with regard to <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: aprītiḥ paramā mahyaṃ bhavet tu prativārite ||
children.translated_text: If I am opposed, the utmost displeasure will arise in me.

children.text: śāpitāśca mayā yūyaṃ bhujābhyāṃ jīvitena ca
children.translated_text: And you have been put under oath by me, by my two arms and by my life:

children.text: ye māṃ vākyāntare brūyur anunetuṃ kathaṃcana ||
children.translated_text: whoever should speak another word to me in any way in order to conciliate me,

children.text: mānayantu bhavanto māṃ yadi macchāsane sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: let you all honor me, if you stand by my command.

children.text: ito 'dya nīyatāṃ sītā kuruṣva vacanaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: Let <s>Sītā</s> be taken away from here today. Carry out my word."
"Formerly I was told by her about the great hermitages on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>..."

children.text: paśyeyam iti tasyāśca kāmaḥ saṃvartyatām ayam ||
children.translated_text: and let this desire of hers, "May I see them," be fulfilled.

children.text: evam uktvā tu kākutstho bāṣpeṇa pihitekṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Kākutstha</s>, his eyes covered with tears,
the righteous one, surrounded by his brothers, entered within.
Then, when the night had passed, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, downcast in mind,
spoke these words to <s>Sumantra</s> with his mouth gone dry:
"Charioteer, quickly yoke the horses to the excellent chariot,
with a fair, well-spread seat for <s>Sītā</s> from the royal palace.
For <s>Sītā</s> must be taken by me from the royal palace to the hermitage

children.text: mayā neyā maharṣīṇāṃ śīghram ānīyatāṃ rathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: of the great seers of holy deeds. Let the chariot be brought quickly."
And <s>Sumantra</s>, saying "So be it," took a chariot yoked with the finest horses,
lovely in appearance and well spread with a comfortable couch,
and said to <s>Saumitri</s>, the increaser of his friends' joy:

children.text: ratho 'yaṃ samanuprāpto yat kāryaṃ kriyatāṃ prabho ||
children.translated_text: "This chariot has arrived; let what must be done be done, my lord."

children.text: evam uktaḥ sumantreṇa rājaveśma sa lakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Sumantra</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, bull among men,
entered the royal residence, approached <s>Sītā</s>, and spoke:

children.text: gaṅgātīre mayā devi munīnām āśrame śubhe
children.translated_text: "O goddess, by the command of our king you are to go quickly with me
and be brought to the auspicious hermitage of the sages on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>."

children.text: evam uktā tu vaidehī lakṣmaṇena mahātmanā
children.translated_text: When <s>Vaidehī</s> was thus addressed by the great-souled <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
she felt immeasurable joy and approved the journey.

children.text: vāsāṃsi ca mahārhāṇi ratnāni vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: Taking very costly garments and various jewels,
<s>Vaidehī</s> made ready to depart.
"I shall give these ornaments to the wives of the sages."
<s>Saumitri</s>, saying "So be it," placed <s>Maithilī</s> on the chariot,
and set out with swift horses, remembering <s>Rāma</s>'s command.
Then <s>Sītā</s> said to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the increaser of prosperity:
"Today I see many inauspicious omens, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>.
My eye is twitching today, and trembling arises in my limbs;

children.text: hṛdayaṃ caiva saumitre asvastham iva lakṣaye ||
children.translated_text: and, O <s>Saumitri</s>, I perceive my heart as if unwell.

children.text: autsukyaṃ paramaṃ cāpi adhṛtiśca parā mama
children.translated_text: I also have the utmost anxiety and a supreme loss of composure,

children.text: śūnyām iva ca paśyāmi pṛthivīṃ pṛthulocana ||
children.translated_text: and, wide-eyed one, I see the earth as if empty.

children.text: api svasti bhavet tasya bhrātuste bhrātṛbhiḥ saha
children.translated_text: May all be well with that brother of yours, together with his brothers,

children.text: śvaśrūṇāṃ caiva me vīra sarvāsām aviśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and with all my mothers-in-law without exception, O hero.

children.text: pure janapade caiva kuśalaṃ prāṇinām api
children.translated_text: May there also be welfare in the city and the countryside, and among living beings."
Thus <s>Sītā</s>, with folded hands, implored the deities.

children.text: lakṣmaṇo 'rthaṃ tu taṃ śrutvā śirasā vandya maithilīm
children.translated_text: Hearing that meaning, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> bowed his head to <s>Maithilī</s>
and, outwardly bold while his heart was drying up, said, "May there be good fortune."
Then, reaching a lodging at an hermitage on the bank of the <s>Gomatī</s>,

children.text: prabhāte punar utthāya saumitriḥ sūtam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Saumitri</s> rose again at dawn and said to the charioteer:
"Yoke the chariot quickly. Today I shall bear the water of the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>
upon my head, as <s>Tryambaka</s> does upon the mountain."
After quickly examining the horses and yoking the swift-as-thought steeds to the chariot,
the charioteer, with folded hands, said to <s>Vaidehī</s>, "Please mount."

children.text: sā tu sūtasya vacanād āruroha rathottamam
children.translated_text: At the charioteer's words she mounted the excellent chariot,

children.text: sītā saumitriṇā sārdhaṃ sumitreṇa ca dhīmatā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s> together with <s>Saumitri</s> and the wise <s>Sumantra</s>.
Then, after half the day had passed, seeing the waters of the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>,
the sorrowful <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> burst into loud weeping.

children.text: sītā tu paramāyattā dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇam āturam
children.translated_text: But <s>Sītā</s>, deeply concerned, seeing <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> distressed,

children.text: uvāca vākyaṃ dharmajña kim idaṃ rudyate tvayā ||
children.translated_text: said these words: "Knower of <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty), why are you weeping?
Having reached the bank of the <s>Jāhnavī</s>, long desired by me,

children.text: harṣakāle kim arthaṃ māṃ viṣādayasi lakṣmaṇa ||
children.translated_text: why do you make me grieve at a time of joy, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>?
You always remain at <s>Rāma</s>'s feet, O bull among men.

children.text: kaccid vinā kṛtastena dvirātre śokam āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Have you, being separated from him for two nights, fallen into grief?
<s>Rāma</s> too is dearer to me than life itself, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>;

children.text: na cāham evaṃ śocāmi maivaṃ tvaṃ bāliśo bhava ||
children.translated_text: yet I do not grieve in this way. Do not be so childish.

children.text: tārayasva ca māṃ gaṅgāṃ darśayasva ca tāpasān
children.translated_text: Take me across the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and show me the ascetics;
then I shall give wealth, garments, and ornaments.
After duly saluting the great seers there,

children.text: tatra caikāṃ niśām uṣya yāsyāmastāṃ purīṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and staying there for one night, we shall go back again to that city."

children.text: tasyāstad vacanaṃ śrutvā pramṛjya nayane śubhe
children.translated_text: Hearing those words of hers, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, wiping his lovely eyes,

children.text: titīrṣur lakṣmaṇo gaṅgāṃ śubhāṃ nāvam upāharat ||
children.translated_text: wishing to cross the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, brought a fine boat.
Then the younger brother of <s>Rāghava</s> boarded a very broad boat of the Niṣādas,
well equipped, after first placing <s>Maithilī</s> aboard.

children.text: sumantraṃ caiva sarathaṃ sthīyatām iti lakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: And <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, afflicted with grief, said to <s>Sumantra</s> with the chariot,
"Stay here," and to the boatman, "Go on."
Then, reaching the bank of the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>
spoke these words to <s>Maithilī</s>, with folded hands and a voice choked by tears:

children.text: hṛdgataṃ me mahacchalyaṃ yad asmyāryeṇa dhīmatā
children.translated_text: "A great thorn has entered my heart, because I, O <s>Vaidehī</s>,
have been made blameworthy in the eyes of the world by my wise noble brother in this matter.

children.text: śreyo hi maraṇaṃ me 'dya mṛtyor vā yat paraṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Death would be better for me today, or whatever may lie beyond death;

children.text: na cāsminn īdṛśe kārye niyojyo lokanindite ||
children.translated_text: I should not have been appointed to such a deed, condemned by the world.

children.text: prasīda na ca me roṣaṃ kartum arhasi suvrate
children.translated_text: Be gracious, virtuous lady, and you should not be angry with me."
Thus <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, with folded hands, fell down upon the ground.

children.text: rudantaṃ prāñjaliṃ dṛṣṭvā kāṅkṣantaṃ mṛtyum ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing him weeping with folded hands and wishing for his own death,
<s>Maithilī</s>, greatly agitated, spoke these words to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:

children.text: kim idaṃ nāvagacchāmi brūhi tattvena lakṣmaṇa
children.translated_text: "What is this? I do not understand. Tell me the truth, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: paśyāmi tvāṃ ca na svastham api kṣemaṃ mahīpateḥ ||
children.translated_text: I see that you are unwell. Is the king safe?

children.text: śāpito 'si narendreṇa yat tvaṃ saṃtāpam ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Have you been bound by an oath by the lord of men, that you bring such anguish upon yourself?"

children.text: tad brūyāḥ saṃnidhau mahyam aham ājñāpayāmi te ||
children.translated_text: Tell that in my presence; I command you.
But <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, urged on by <s>Vaidehī</s>, his mind dejected,

children.text: avāṅmukho bāṣpagalo vākyam etad uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: with his face cast down and his throat choked with tears, spoke these words:
"Having heard, in the midst of the assembly, a terribly harsh reproach,
both in the city and in the countryside, on your account, O daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,

children.text: na tāni vacanīyāni mayā devi tavāgrataḥ
children.translated_text: those things, O goddess, are not to be spoken by me in your presence,

children.text: yāni rājñā hṛdi nyastānyamarṣaḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: which the king has placed in his heart, setting anger behind him.

children.text: sā tvaṃ tyaktā nṛpatinā nirdoṣā mama saṃnidhau
children.translated_text: Therefore, though innocent, you have been abandoned by the king in my presence,
because he fears the reproach of the townspeople; O goddess, you must not understand this otherwise.

children.text: āśramānteṣu ca mayā tyaktavyā tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi
children.translated_text: And by me you are to be left at the edges of the hermitages,

children.text: rājñaḥ śāsanam ājñāya tavaivaṃ kila daurhṛdam ||
children.translated_text: knowing the king's command, since such indeed was said to be your pregnancy-longing.
So here on the bank of the <s>Jāhnavī</s> is the ascetic grove of brahmarṣis,

children.text: puṇyaṃ ca ramaṇīyaṃ ca mā viṣādaṃ kṛthāḥ śubhe ||
children.translated_text: holy and delightful; do not grieve, auspicious one.
This foremost sage, the supreme brahmin <s>Vālmīki</s> of very great fame,
is a friend of my father, king <s>Daśaratha</s>.
Having gone to the shade of the feet of that great-souled one,
live there happily, intent only on fasting vows, O daughter of <s>Janaka</s>.

children.text: pativratātvam āsthāya rāmaṃ kṛtvā sadā hṛdi
children.translated_text: Taking your stand in devotion to your husband and always keeping <s>Rāma</s> in your heart,

children.text: śreyaste paramaṃ devi tathā kṛtvā bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: your highest good, O goddess, will come about by doing so."
Hearing <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s cruel words, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,

children.text: paraṃ viṣādam āgamya vaidehī nipapāta ha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vaidehī</s>, falling into utter despair, collapsed.
For a moment she was as if unconscious, her eyes clouded with tears;
the daughter of <s>Janaka</s> spoke to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> in a piteous voice:

children.text: māmikeyaṃ tanur nūnaṃ sṛṣṭā duḥkhāya lakṣmaṇa
children.translated_text: "Surely this body of mine was created for suffering, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
by the Creator, since today its very form appears to me as misery.

children.text: kiṃ nu pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ ko vā dārair viyojitaḥ
children.translated_text: What sin was committed before, or who was separated from his wife,
that I, of pure conduct and faithful, have been abandoned by the king?
Formerly, while following <s>Rāma</s>'s feet, I lived in the hermitage,
even though constrained, O <s>Saumitri</s>, turning about in hardship.

children.text: sā kathaṃ hyāśrame saumya vatsyāmi vijanīkṛtā
children.translated_text: How then, gentle <s>Saumitri</s>, shall I live in a hermitage, made solitary?
And to whom shall I, given over to sorrow, tell my sorrow?

children.text: kiṃ ca vakṣyāmi muniṣu kiṃ mayāpakṛtaṃ nṛpe
children.translated_text: And what shall I say among the sages? What offense have I committed against the king?

children.text: kasmin vā kāraṇe tyaktā rāghaveṇa mahātmanā ||
children.translated_text: For what reason have I been abandoned by the great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>?
Certainly today itself, O <s>Saumitri</s>, I would give up my life in the waters of the <s>Jāhnavī</s>,
but then the royal line of my husband would be mocked.

children.text: yathājñāṃ kuru saumitre tyaja māṃ duḥkhabhāginīm
children.translated_text: Carry out the command, O <s>Saumitri</s>; abandon me, a woman who shares in suffering.

children.text: nideśe sthīyatāṃ rājñaḥ śṛṇu cedaṃ vaco mama ||
children.translated_text: Let the king's order be obeyed, and hear this word of mine:
Without distinction among my mothers-in-law, with joined palms and with reverence,

children.text: śirasā vandya caraṇau kuśalaṃ brūhi pārthivam ||
children.translated_text: bowing your head at their feet, speak of my welfare to the king.
As you behave toward your brothers, so should you always behave toward the townspeople;

children.text: paramo hyeṣa dharmaḥ syād eṣā kīrtir anuttamā ||
children.translated_text: for this would be the highest <s>dharma</s> (duty), and this the unsurpassed fame.

children.text: yat tvaṃ paurajanaṃ rājan dharmeṇa samavāpnuyāḥ
children.translated_text: May you, O king, win over the people of the city through <s>dharma</s> (righteous rule).
I do not grieve for my own body, O bull among men,
as I grieve for the slander spoken by the townspeople, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>."
As <s>Sītā</s> was speaking thus, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, his mind dejected,

children.text: śirasā dharaṇīṃ gatvā vyāhartuṃ na śaśāka ha ||
children.translated_text: brought his head to the ground and was unable to speak.

children.text: pradakṣiṇaṃ ca kṛtvā sa rudann eva mahāsvanam
children.translated_text: After circumambulating her, weeping with a great cry,
he mounted the boat again and urged on the boatman.
Having gone to the northern bank, burdened with grief,

children.text: saṃmūḍha iva duḥkhena ratham adhyāruhad drutam ||
children.translated_text: as if bewildered by sorrow, he quickly mounted the chariot.

children.text: muhur muhur apāvṛtya dṛṣṭvā sītām anāthavat
children.translated_text: Again and again turning back and looking at <s>Sītā</s>, who was like one without a protector,
writhing on the further bank, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> then departed.

children.text: dūrasthaṃ ratham ālokya lakṣmaṇaṃ ca muhur muhuḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing the chariot far away and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> again and again,
as she watched in distress, grief entered <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: sā duḥkhabhārāvanatā tapasvinī yaśodharā nātham apaśyatī satī
children.translated_text: Bent down by the weight of sorrow, the ascetic woman, the faithful wife whose fame she bore, not seeing her lord,

children.text: ruroda sā barhiṇanādite vane mahāsvanaṃ duḥkhaparāyaṇā satī ||
children.translated_text: wept in that forest resounding with peacocks, the faithful one given over to sorrow crying loudly.

children.text: sītāṃ tu rudatīṃ dṛṣṭvā ye tatra munidārakāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Sītā</s> weeping, the young sons of sages who were there

children.text: prādravan yatra bhagavān āste vālmīkir agryadhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: ran to where the blessed <s>Vālmīki</s>, foremost in wisdom, was sitting.
Having bowed to the sage's feet, the sons of the sages
all reported to the great seer the sound of her weeping:
"Blessed one, this woman, never seen before, seems to be the wife of some great-souled man;

children.text: patnī śrīr iva saṃmohād virauti vikṛtasvarā ||
children.translated_text: like <s>Śrī</s> herself, from bewilderment she cries out in a changed voice.

children.text: bhagavan sādhu paśyemāṃ devatām iva khāccyutām
children.translated_text: Blessed one, please look upon this woman, like a goddess fallen from the sky.

children.text: na hyenāṃ mānuṣīṃ vidmaḥ satkriyāsyāḥ prayujyatām ||
children.translated_text: We do not think her human; let hospitality be offered to her."

children.text: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā buddhyā niścitya dharmavit
children.translated_text: Hearing that word of theirs, the knower of <s>dharma</s>, discerning it with his understanding,
and possessing sight gained through austerity, ran to where <s>Maithilī</s> was.

children.text: taṃ tu deśam abhipretya kiṃcit padbhyāṃ mahāmuniḥ
children.translated_text: When the great sage had approached that place a little on foot,
taking a splendid arghya and reaching the bank of the <s>Jāhnavī</s>,
he saw <s>Sītā</s>, beloved wife of <s>Rāghava</s>, like one without a protector.
Seeing that <s>Sītā</s> afflicted by the burden of grief, <s>Vālmīki</s>, foremost of sages,

children.text: uvāca madhurāṃ vāṇīṃ hlādayann iva tejasā ||
children.translated_text: spoke sweet speech to her, as if gladdening her with his radiance:

children.text: snuṣā daśarathasya tvaṃ rāmasya mahiṣī satī
children.translated_text: "You are the daughter-in-law of <s>Daśaratha</s>, the faithful queen of <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: janakasya sutā rājñaḥ svāgataṃ te pativrate ||
children.translated_text: and the daughter of king <s>Janaka</s>; welcome to you, devoted wife.
Even as you were coming, you were known by me through concentration on <s>dharma</s>,
and the whole reason has been perceived by me in my heart.

children.text: apāpāṃ vedmi sīte tvāṃ tapolabdhena cakṣuṣā
children.translated_text: I know you, O <s>Sītā</s>, to be sinless, by the sight gained through austerity."
Pure in disposition, <s>Vaidehī</s>, you are now staying with me.
Not far from my hermitage there are female ascetics, established in ascetic practice.

children.text: tāstvāṃ vatse yathā vatsaṃ pālayiṣyanti nityaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They, child, will constantly protect you as one protects a young calf.

children.text: idam arghyaṃ pratīccha tvaṃ viśrabdhā vigatajvarā
children.translated_text: Accept this arghya, trusting and free from anxiety.

children.text: yathā svagṛham abhyetya viṣādaṃ caiva mā kṛthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: As though you had come to your own home, do not give way to sorrow.

children.text: śrutvā tu bhāṣitaṃ sītā muneḥ paramam adbhutam
children.translated_text: When <s>Sītā</s> heard the sage's most wondrous speech,
she bowed to his feet with her head and, with folded hands, said, 'So be it.'

children.text: taṃ prayāntaṃ muniṃ sītā prāñjaliḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nvagāt
children.translated_text: As the sage set out, <s>Sītā</s> followed behind him with folded hands,
and he led her to where the female ascetics, constant in <s>dharma</s> and composed, were dwelling.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā munim āyāntaṃ vaidehyānugataṃ tadā
children.translated_text: When they saw the sage approaching then, followed by <s>Vaidehī</s>,

children.text: upājagmur mudā yuktā vacanaṃ cedam abruvan ||
children.translated_text: they came forward joyfully and spoke these words:
Welcome to you, best of sages; it has been long since you came, lord.

children.text: abhivādayāmaḥ sarvāstvām ucyatāṃ kiṃ ca kurmahe ||
children.translated_text: We all bow to you. Tell us what we should do.

children.text: tāsāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā vālmīkir idam abravīt
children.translated_text: Hearing those words of theirs, <s>Vālmīki</s> said this:
This <s>Sītā</s> has come here, the wife of wise <s>Rāma</s>.
She is the daughter-in-law of <s>Daśaratha</s>, the faithful daughter of <s>Janaka</s>.

children.text: apāpā patinā tyaktā paripālyā mayā sadā ||
children.translated_text: Sinless though she is, she has been abandoned by her husband; she must always be protected under my care.

children.text: imāṃ bhavatyaḥ paśyantu snehena parameṇa ha
children.translated_text: Let your reverences look upon her with supreme affection.
Out of respect for my word, let her be especially honored by you.
Again and again the greatly renowned sage consoled <s>Vaidehī</s>,
and then the great ascetic, surrounded by his disciples, returned to his own hermitage.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tu maithilīṃ sītām āśramaṃ saṃpraveśitām
children.translated_text: But when he saw <s>Maithilī</s>, <s>Sītā</s>, brought into the hermitage,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, his heart miserable, fell into terrible anguish.
The very powerful one spoke to <s>Sumantra</s>, the counsellor and charioteer:
Behold the sorrow of wise <s>Rāma</s>, born from <s>Sītā</s>'s distress.

children.text: ato duḥkhataraṃ kiṃ nu rāghavasya bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: What could be more painful than this for <s>Rāghava</s>,
after sending away his wife, <s>Janaka</s>'s daughter, whose conduct is pure?

children.text: vyaktaṃ daivād ahaṃ manye rāghavasya vinābhavam
children.translated_text: Clearly, charioteer, I think <s>Rāghava</s>'s separation

children.text: vaidehyā sārathe sārdhaṃ daivaṃ hi duratikramam ||
children.translated_text: from <s>Vaidehī</s> is due to fate; fate is indeed hard to overcome.

children.text: yo hi devān sagandharvān asurān saha rākṣasaiḥ
children.translated_text: For <s>Rāghava</s>, when angered, could slay the gods together with the gandharvas,

children.text: nihanyād rāghavaḥ kruddhaḥ sa daivam anuvartate ||
children.translated_text: and the asuras along with the rākṣasas, yet he follows fate.

children.text: purā mama pitur vākyair daṇḍake vijane vane
children.translated_text: Formerly, because of my father's words, he lived in the deserted <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest,
that very dreadful place, for nine years and five more besides.
Again, more painful than that is <s>Sītā</s>'s banishment.

children.text: paurāṇāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā nṛśaṃsaṃ pratibhāti me ||
children.translated_text: After hearing the words of the citizens, it seems cruel to me.

children.text: ko nu dharmāśrayaḥ sūta karmaṇyasmin yaśohare
children.translated_text: What support in <s>dharma</s>, charioteer, is there in this fame-destroying deed
toward <s>Maithilī</s>, brought about by townsmen whose statements are base?
Hearing these many kinds of words spoken by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: sumantraḥ prāñjalir bhūtvā vākyam etad uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sumantra</s>, with folded hands, then spoke this sentence:

children.text: na saṃtāpastvayā kāryaḥ saumitre maithilīṃ prati
children.translated_text: You should not grieve over <s>Maithilī</s>, <s>Saumitri</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭam etat purā vipraiḥ pituste lakṣmaṇāgrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: This was foreseen long ago by brahmins in the presence of your father, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
It was certain that <s>Rāma</s> would become one whose life is mostly sorrow, with little happiness,

children.text: tvāṃ caiva maithilīṃ caiva śatrughnabharatau tathā
children.translated_text: and that the great, righteous man would, in time, abandon you too, and <s>Maithilī</s>,
as well as <s>Śatrughna</s> and <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: na tvidaṃ tvayi vaktavyaṃ saumitre bharate 'pi vā
children.translated_text: But this was not to be told to you, <s>Saumitri</s>, nor even to <s>Bharata</s>:

children.text: rājñā vo 'vyāhṛtaṃ vākyaṃ durvāsā yad uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: the statement concerning you which <s>Durvāsā</s> uttered, and which the king forbade us to repeat.
In the presence of the great king, and of me too, bull among men,

children.text: ṛṣiṇā vyāhṛtaṃ vākyaṃ vasiṣṭhasya ca saṃnidhau ||
children.translated_text: that statement was spoken by the sage in <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s presence.

children.text: ṛṣestu vacanaṃ śrutvā mām āha puruṣarṣabhaḥ
children.translated_text: When he had heard the seer's words, the best of men said to me:

children.text: sūta na kvacid evaṃ te vaktavyaṃ janasaṃnidhau ||
children.translated_text: Charioteer, this must never be told by you anywhere in the presence of people.
I, fully composed, would never make false

children.text: naiva jātvanṛtaṃ kuryām iti me saumya darśanam ||
children.translated_text: the word of that guardian of the world; such is my view, gentle one.
Yet there is, in every way, nothing that I may not tell in your presence, gentle one.

children.text: yadi te śravaṇe śraddhā śrūyatāṃ raghunandana ||
children.translated_text: If you have faith enough to hear it, listen, delight of the <s>Raghus</s>.
Although long ago I was made to hear this secret by the king,
I shall relate that too; fate is indeed hard to overcome.
Hearing that great speech of his, whose words held a profound meaning,

children.text: tathyaṃ brūhīti saumitriḥ sūtaṃ vākyam athābravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Saumitri</s> then said to the charioteer, 'Tell it truthfully.'
Thus urged by great-souled <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: tad vākyam ṛṣiṇā proktaṃ vyāhartum upacakrame ||
children.translated_text: the charioteer began to utter that statement spoken by the sage.

children.text: purā nāmnā hi durvāsā atreḥ putro mahāmuniḥ
children.translated_text: Long ago the great sage named <s>Durvāsā</s>, son of <s>Atri</s>,

children.text: vasiṣṭhasyāśrame puṇye sa vārṣikyam uvāsa ha ||
children.translated_text: spent the rainy season in the holy hermitage of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.

children.text: tam āśramaṃ mahātejāḥ pitā te sumahāyaśāḥ
children.translated_text: Your father, very famous and full of splendor,
went himself to that hermitage, wishing to see the great-souled family priest.

children.text: sa dṛṣṭvā sūryasaṃkāśaṃ jvalantam iva tejasā
children.translated_text: He saw the great sage, bright as the sun and blazing as if with radiance,
seated on <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s left side,
and he humbly bowed to those two sages, the best of ascetics.

children.text: sa tābhyāṃ pūjito rājā svāgatenāsanena ca
children.translated_text: Honored by those two with welcome, a seat,
water for his feet, fruits, and roots, the king too sat with the sages.
While they sat there, various very sweet stories
were told among the supreme seers when the day had reached midday.

children.text: tataḥ kathāyāṃ kasyāṃcit prāñjaliḥ pragraho nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, during one such story, the restrained king, with folded hands,

children.text: uvāca taṃ mahātmānam atreḥ putraṃ tapodhanam ||
children.translated_text: spoke to that great-souled ascetic, the son of <s>Atri</s>:

children.text: bhagavan kiṃ pramāṇena mama vaṃśo bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Lord, by what measure will my lineage endure?

children.text: kimāyuśca hi me rāmaḥ putrāścānye kimāyuṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And what lifespan will my <s>Rāma</s> have, and what lifespan my other sons?

children.text: rāmasya ca sutā ye syusteṣām āyuḥ kiyad bhavet
children.translated_text: And those who would be sons of <s>Rāma</s>: how long would their life be?

children.text: kāmyayā bhagavan brūhi vaṃśasyāsya gatiṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: Holy one, please tell me, as I desire to know, the course of this lineage of mine.

children.text: tacchrutvā vyāhṛtaṃ vākyaṃ rājño daśarathasya tu
children.translated_text: Having heard the words spoken by King <s>Daśaratha</s>,
the greatly radiant <s>Durvāsas</s> began to speak.
<s>Rāma</s> will be lord of <s>Ayodhyā</s> for a long time,
and his younger brothers will be happy and prosperous.

children.text: kasmiṃścit kāraṇe tvāṃ ca maithilīṃ ca yaśasvinīm
children.translated_text: For some reason, after a long time, you and the renowned <s>Maithilī</s>
will be abandoned, it is said, by that righteous-souled one.
For ten thousand years and ten hundred years
<s>Rāma</s> will attend to the kingdom and then go to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
After sacrificing with rich horse sacrifices, the conqueror of enemy cities,
<s>Kākutstha</s> will establish many royal lineages.

children.text: sa sarvam akhilaṃ rājño vaṃśasyāsya gatāgatam
children.translated_text: Having told the king, in full and without omission, the coming and going
of this entire lineage, that greatly radiant, splendid one sat silent.
When that sage had become silent, King <s>Daśaratha</s> then
bowed to the two great-souled ones and returned again to the excellent city.

children.text: etad vaco mayā tatra muninā vyāhṛtaṃ purā
children.translated_text: Those words, uttered there long ago by the sage, were heard by me

children.text: śrutaṃ hṛdi ca nikṣiptaṃ nānyathā tad bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: and placed in my heart; it will not be otherwise.

children.text: evaṃgate na saṃtāpaṃ gantum arhasi rāghava
children.translated_text: Since this is so, you should not fall into grief, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: sītārthe rāghavārthe vā dṛḍho bhava narottama ||
children.translated_text: Be firm, best of men, whether for <s>Sītā</s>'s sake or for <s>Rāghava</s>'s sake.
Hearing those supremely wondrous words spoken by the charioteer,

children.text: praharṣam atulaṃ lebhe sādhu sādhviti cābravīt ||
children.translated_text: he obtained immeasurable joy and said, "Well done, well done."
As the charioteer and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> were conversing in this way on the road,

children.text: astam arko gato vāsaṃ gomatyāṃ tāvathoṣatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the sun set, and then the two stayed by the <s>Gomatī</s>.

children.text: tatra tāṃ rajanīm uṣya gomatyāṃ raghunandanaḥ
children.translated_text: After spending that night there by the <s>Gomatī</s>, the delight of the <s>Raghus</s>,

children.text: prabhāte punar utthāya lakṣmaṇaḥ prayayau tadā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, rising again at dawn, set out then.
Then, when half the day had arrived, the great chariot-warrior entered
<s>Ayodhyā</s>, full of jewels and thronged with happy, well-nourished people.
But <s>Saumitri</s>, though very wise, sank into extreme dejection:

children.text: rāmapādau samāsādya vakṣyāmi kim ahaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Having gone back to <s>Rāma</s>'s feet, what shall I say?"
As he was thinking thus, the moonlike palace
of the king, exceedingly noble, appeared before him.
At the doorway of the king's palace that best of men descended
and, with face downcast and mind dejected, entered unhindered.

children.text: sa dṛṣṭvā rāghavaṃ dīnam āsīnaṃ paramāsane
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Rāghava</s> sitting sorrowfully on the highest seat,
with both eyes filled with tears, he beheld his elder brother before him.
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, dejected in mind, grasped his feet
and, with folded hands and fully composed, spoke in a sorrowful voice:
"Having placed my noble lord's command first and having released <s>Janaka</s>'s daughter
on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, at the auspicious hermitage of <s>Vālmīki</s>, as directed,
I have returned again, hero, to attend upon the base of your feet.

children.text: mā śucaḥ puruṣavyāghra kālasya gatir īdṛśī
children.translated_text: Do not grieve, tiger among men; such is the course of time.

children.text: tvadvidhā na hi śocanti sattvavanto manasvinaḥ ||
