children.translated_text: Those like you, strong in character and thoughtful, do not grieve.
All accumulations end in decay; all elevations end in falling.
Unions end in separation, and life ends in death.
You are able to conquer yourself by yourself, indeed by the mind alone,

children.text: lokān sarvāṃśca kākutstha kiṃ punar duḥkham īdṛśam ||
children.translated_text: and all the worlds as well, O <s>Kākutstha</s>; how much more this kind of sorrow?
Men like you do not become bewildered in such matters, bull among men,
O king, since <s>Maithilī</s> was abandoned out of fear of public reproach.
Therefore, tiger among men, composed with courage,

children.text: tyajemāṃ durbalāṃ buddhiṃ saṃtāpaṃ mā kuruṣva ha ||
children.translated_text: abandon this weak thought; do not make grief for yourself."
Thus addressed by the great-souled <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, <s>Kākutstha</s>
spoke with the highest affection to <s>Saumitri</s>, who was loving as a friend:
"It is just as you say, best of men, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
And I am satisfied, hero, with your guidance concerning my duty.
Relief has been brought about, gentle one, and grief has been removed.
By your very sweet words I have been conciliated, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>."
Then <s>Sumantra</s> came and spoke these words to <s>Rāghava</s>:

children.text: ete nivāritā rājan dvāri tiṣṭhanti tāpasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "These ascetics, O king, have been held back and are standing at the door.
The great seers, placing the <s>Bhārgava</s> named <s>Cyavana</s> at their head,
are urgently requesting an audience with you, great king,
well-disposed, tiger among men, and dwelling on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>."

children.text: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rāmaḥ provāca dharmavit
children.translated_text: Hearing that statement of his, <s>Rāma</s>, knower of dharma, said:
"Let the great-souled twice-born men, headed by the <s>Bhārgava</s>, be brought in."
Putting the king's command first, the doorkeeper, with folded hands raised to his head,
then brought in the many honored ascetics.
More than a hundred were there, blazing with their own splendor;
the great-souled ascetics entered the royal palace.
Those twice-born men, with full jars honored with water from all sacred fords,
and taking fruits and roots, brought many offerings to <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: pratigṛhya tu tat sarvaṃ rāmaḥ prītipuraskṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Receiving all that with affection, <s>Rāma</s> accepted
all the sacred-ford waters and the various fruits.

children.text: uvāca ca mahābāhuḥ sarvān eva mahāmunīn
children.translated_text: And the long-armed one said to all the great sages:
"Let each of you sit, as is proper, on these excellent seats."

children.text: rāmasya bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā sarva eva maharṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Rāma</s>'s speech, all those great seers
sat down on beautiful golden seats.
Seeing the seers seated there, the conqueror of enemy cities

children.text: prayataḥ prāñjalir bhūtvā rāghavo vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Having become attentive and standing with folded hands, <s>Rāghava</s> spoke these words:

children.text: kim āgamanakāryaṃ vaḥ kiṃ karomi tapodhanāḥ
children.translated_text: "What is the purpose of your coming? What shall I do, treasures of austerity?
I am at the command of the great seers, ready to accomplish every desire happily.

children.text: idaṃ rājyaṃ ca sakalaṃ jīvitaṃ ca hṛdi sthitam
children.translated_text: This entire kingdom, and the life fixed in my heart,

children.text: sarvam etad dvijārthaṃ me satyam etad bravīmi vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: all this is for the sake of the twice-born. I tell you this truthfully."

children.text: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sādhuvādo mahān abhūt
children.translated_text: When they heard that speech of his, there arose a great cry of approval
among those fierce-austeritied seers who dwelt on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>.
And those great-souled ones, filled with great joy, said:
"This is fitting, best of men, for you alone upon the earth, and for no one else.
Many powerful earthly kings have passed by, O king,
but, having heard the gravity of the task, they did not approve the pledge.

children.text: tvayā punar brāhmaṇagauravād iyaṃ kṛtvā pratijñā hyanavekṣya kāraṇam
children.translated_text: But you, out of regard for brāhmaṇas, have made this pledge without considering the reason.

children.text: kuruṣva kartā hyasi nātra saṃśayo mahābhayāt trātum ṛṣīṃstvam arhasi ||
children.translated_text: Carry it out; you are the one to do it, there is no doubt here. You ought to save the seers from great fear."

children.text: bruvadbhir evam ṛṣibhiḥ kākutstho vākyam abravīt
children.translated_text: As the seers spoke in this way, <s>Kākutstha</s> said these words:

children.text: kiṃ kāryaṃ brūta bhavatāṃ bhayaṃ nāśayitāsmi vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Tell me what your task is. I shall destroy your fear."

children.text: tathā vadati kākutsthe bhārgavo vākyam abravīt
children.translated_text: When <s>Kākutstha</s> had spoken thus, a descendant of <s>Bhṛgu</s> said these words:

children.text: bhayaṃ naḥ śṛṇu yanmūlaṃ deśasya ca nareśvara ||
children.translated_text: "Hear the root of our fear, O lord of men, and of the fear of the country.
Formerly, in the <s>Kṛtayuga</s>, O <s>Rāma</s>, there was a very powerful Daitya,
the eldest son of <s>Lolā</s>, a great Asura named <s>Madhu</s>.
He honored brāhmaṇas, offered refuge, and was firmly settled in understanding,
and he had matchless friendship with the supremely noble gods.

children.text: sa madhur vīryasampanno dharme ca susamāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: That <s>Madhu</s>, endowed with valor and well composed in <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),
received from <s>Rudra</s>, out of his regard, a wondrous boon.
Drawing forth from his own trident a trident of great power and great radiance,

children.text: dadau mahātmā suprīto vākyaṃ caitad uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: the delighted great-souled one gave it to him and spoke these words:

children.text: tvayāyam atulo dharmo matprasādāt kṛtaḥ śubhaḥ
children.translated_text: "By my favor you have performed this matchless and auspicious <s>dharma</s> (righteous conduct).
Joined with the highest affection, I give you this supreme weapon.

children.text: yāvat suraiśca vipraiśca na virudhyer mahāsura
children.translated_text: As long as you do not act hostilely toward the gods and the Brahmins, great Asura,

children.text: tāvacchūlaṃ tavedaṃ syād anyathā nāśam āpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: so long this trident shall be yours; otherwise it will meet destruction.
And whoever, free from anxiety, attacks you for battle,

children.text: taṃ śūlaṃ bhasmasāt kṛtvā punar eṣyati te karam ||
children.translated_text: this trident, having reduced him to ashes, will return again to your hand."

children.text: evaṃ rudrād varaṃ labdhvā bhūya eva mahāsuraḥ
children.translated_text: Having received such a boon from <s>Rudra</s>, that great Asura once again

children.text: praṇipatya mahādevaṃ vākyam etad uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: bowed down to <s>Mahādeva</s> and spoke these words:
"Blessed lord, may this unsurpassed trident belong always

children.text: bhavet tu satataṃ deva surāṇām īśvaro hyasi ||
children.translated_text: to my lineage, O god, for you are indeed the lord of the gods."

children.text: taṃ bruvāṇaṃ madhuṃ devaḥ sarvabhūtapatiḥ śivaḥ
children.translated_text: To <s>Madhu</s> as he spoke thus, the god <s>Śiva</s>, lord of all beings,
<s>Mahādeva</s>, replied: "This will not be so.

children.text: mā bhūt te viphalā vāṇī matprāsādakṛtā śubhā
children.translated_text: Yet let your auspicious speech, made through my favor, not be fruitless:

children.text: bhavataḥ putram ekaṃ tu śūlam etad gamiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: this trident will pass to one son of yours.

children.text: yāvat karasthaḥ śūlo 'yaṃ bhaviṣyati sutasya te
children.translated_text: As long as this trident is in your son's hand,
with the trident in hand he will be invulnerable to all beings."

children.text: evaṃ madhuvaraṃ labdhvā devāt sumahad adbhutam
children.translated_text: After receiving this very great and wondrous boon for <s>Madhu</s> from the god,
the best of Asuras had a splendid dwelling built.

children.text: tasya patnī mahābhāgā priyā kumbhīnasī hi yā
children.translated_text: His wife, greatly fortunate and dear to him, was <s>Kumbhīnasī</s>,
a brilliant daughter of <s>Viśvāvasu</s> by <s>Analā</s>.

children.text: tasyāḥ putro mahāvīryo lavaṇo nāma dāruṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Her son was a very powerful and terrible one named <s>Lavaṇa</s>,
who, from childhood onward, being wicked-souled, performed only evil deeds.

children.text: taṃ putraṃ durvinītaṃ tu dṛṣṭvā duḥkhasamanvitaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that ill-disciplined son, <s>Madhu</s> was filled with grief,

children.text: madhuḥ sa śokam āpede na cainaṃ kiṃcid abravīt ||
children.translated_text: and he fell into sorrow, but said nothing at all to him.

children.text: sa vihāya imaṃ lokaṃ praviṣṭo varuṇālayam
children.translated_text: Leaving this world, he entered the abode of <s>Varuṇa</s>,

children.text: śūlaṃ niveśya lavaṇe varaṃ tasmai nyavedayat ||
children.translated_text: having placed the trident with <s>Lavaṇa</s> and having told him of the boon.
By the power of the trident, and also by the wickedness of his own nature,
he torments the three worlds, and especially the ascetics.
Such is <s>Lavaṇa</s>'s power, and such is that trident.

children.text: śrutvā pramāṇaṃ kākutstha tvaṃ hi naḥ paramā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having heard the full account, <s>Kākutstha</s>, you are our highest refuge.

children.text: bahavaḥ pārthivā rāma bhayārtair ṛṣibhiḥ purā
children.translated_text: Many earthly kings, O <s>Rāma</s>, were formerly asked for safety

children.text: abhayaṃ yācitā vīra trātāraṃ na ca vidmahe ||
children.translated_text: by fear-stricken seers, O hero, but we have found no protector.

children.text: te vayaṃ rāvaṇaṃ śrutvā hataṃ sabalavāhanam
children.translated_text: But when we heard that <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, together with his forces and vehicles, had been slain,

children.text: trātāraṃ vidmahe rāma nānyaṃ bhuvi narādhipam
children.translated_text: we knew you, O <s>Rāma</s>, to be the protector, and no other lord of men on earth.
Therefore, afflicted by fear of <s>Lavaṇa</s>, we wish to be protected."

children.text: tathokte tān ṛṣīn rāmaḥ pratyuvāca kṛtāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: When this had been said, <s>Rāma</s> answered those seers with folded hands:

children.text: kimāhāraḥ kimācāro lavaṇaḥ kva ca vartate ||
children.translated_text: "What is <s>Lavaṇa</s>'s food? What is his conduct? And where does he live?"

children.text: rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā ṛṣayaḥ sarva eva te
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Rāghava</s>'s words, all those seers
then reported how <s>Lavaṇa</s> had grown up.
"His food is all living beings, and especially ascetics.

children.text: ācāro raudratā nityaṃ vāso madhuvane sadā ||
children.translated_text: His conduct is constant ferocity, and his dwelling is always in <s>Madhuvana</s>.
After killing ten thousands of lions, tigers, deer, and elephants,
and human beings as well, he makes them his daily meal.
Then that mighty one devours other beings too,
like Death with gaping mouth when the time of destruction has arrived."

children.text: tacchrutvā rāghavo vākyam uvāca sa mahāmunīn
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech, <s>Rāghava</s> said to the great sages:

children.text: ghātayiṣyāmi tad rakṣo vyapagacchatu vo bhayam ||
children.translated_text: "I shall have that Rakṣas killed. Let your fear depart."
Having made that promise to those sages of fierce splendor,

children.text: sa bhrātṝn sahitān sarvān uvāca raghunandanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the delight of the <s>Raghus</s> addressed all his assembled brothers:

children.text: ko hantā lavaṇaṃ vīrāḥ kasyāṃśaḥ sa vidhīyatām
children.translated_text: "Heroes, who will be the slayer of <s>Lavaṇa</s>? To whose share shall he be assigned?"
of mighty-armed <s>Bharata</s>, or else again of <s>Śatrughna</s>?
But when <s>Rāghava</s> had spoken thus, <s>Bharata</s> said this speech:

children.text: aham enaṃ vadhiṣyāmi mamāṃśaḥ sa vidhīyatām ||
children.translated_text: "I shall kill him; let that share be assigned to me."
Hearing <s>Bharata</s>'s words, endowed with courage and valor,
the younger brother of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> stood up, leaving the golden seat.
Then <s>Śatrughna</s>, bowing down to the lord of men, spoke these words:
"The mighty-armed middle son, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>, has fulfilled his duty.

children.text: āryeṇa hi purā śūnyā ayodhyā rakṣitā purī
children.translated_text: For the noble one formerly guarded the city of <s>Ayodhyā</s> when it was empty,
keeping anguish in his heart as he awaited the noble one's return.
And many sufferings have been endured here, O king,
as that great-souled one lay on beds of sorrow in <s>Nandigrāma</s>,
living on fruits and roots, and wearing matted hair and bark garments.
This delight of the <s>Rāghavas</s> has endured such sorrow;

children.text: preṣye mayi sthite rājanna bhūyaḥ kleśam āpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: while I stand here as your servant, O king, he should not incur hardship again."

children.text: tathā bruvati śatrughne rāghavaḥ punar abravīt
children.translated_text: As <s>Śatrughna</s> spoke in this way, <s>Rāghava</s> again said:

children.text: evaṃ bhavatu kākutstha kriyatāṃ mama śāsanam ||
children.translated_text: "So be it, O <s>Kākutstha</s>. Let my command be carried out.

children.text: rājye tvām abhiṣekṣyāmi madhostu nagare śubhe
children.translated_text: I shall consecrate you to kingship in the auspicious city of <s>Madhu</s>.
O mighty-armed one, take up your residence there, if you have regard for <s>Bharata</s>.
You are brave, trained in knowledge, and capable in settlement and governance
of the city once inhabited by <s>Madhu</s>, and likewise of the splendid districts.

children.text: yo hi vaṃśaṃ samutpāṭya pārthivasya punaḥ kṣaye
children.translated_text: For a man who uproots a royal lineage and then, when that ruler is destroyed,

children.text: na vidhatte nṛpaṃ tatra narakaṃ sa nigacchati ||
children.translated_text: does not establish a king there, goes to hell.

children.text: sa tvaṃ hatvā madhusutaṃ lavaṇaṃ pāpaniścayam
children.translated_text: Therefore, after killing <s>Lavaṇa</s>, <s>Madhu</s>'s son, whose resolve is evil,

children.text: rājyaṃ praśādhi dharmeṇa vākyaṃ me yadyavekṣase ||
children.translated_text: rule the kingdom according to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), if you have regard for my word.

children.text: uttaraṃ ca na vaktavyaṃ śūra vākyāntare mama
children.translated_text: And no answer is to be spoken, O hero, in interruption of my command.
The younger must carry out the elder brother's order; there is no doubt about this.
Receive from me the consecration that has been prepared, O <s>Kākutstha</s>,
with the Brahmins headed by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, preceded by the rite and the mantras."

children.text: evam uktastu rāmeṇa parāṃ vrīḍām upāgataḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Śatrughna</s> was overcome with deep embarrassment,

children.text: śatrughno vīryasampanno mandaṃ mandam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: and, though full of valor, spoke very softly:
"Your command must indeed be carried out, O bull among men,
and your command, great lord, is not to be transgressed.
O king, O bull among men, I am yours, one who acts according to your wish."

children.text: evam ukte tu śūreṇa śatrughnena mahātmanā
children.translated_text: When the heroic, great-souled <s>Śatrughna</s> had spoken thus,

children.text: uvāca rāmaḥ saṃhṛṣṭo lakṣmaṇaṃ bharataṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: the delighted <s>Rāma</s> spoke to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and also to <s>Bharata</s>:
"Bring the materials for the consecration, with focused minds.
Today itself I shall consecrate this unconquerable tiger among men.
And, O <s>Kākutsthas</s>, bring the household priest, the townsmen, and the officiating priests,
and also all my ministers, by my command."
Having learned the king's command, the great warriors did accordingly.
Putting the household priest at the head of the consecration undertaking,
they entered the royal palace, which was like the house of <s>Purandara</s>.
Then the consecration of great-souled <s>Śatrughna</s> proceeded,
splendid and bringing great joy to <s>Rāghava</s> and to the city.
Then <s>Rāghava</s> placed the consecrated <s>Śatrughna</s> on his lap
and spoke sweet words, filling his own splendor into him:
"This arrow of yours is unfailing, divine, and a conqueror of enemy cities.
With this, gentle son of the <s>Raghus</s>, you shall kill <s>Lavaṇa</s>.

children.text: sṛṣṭaḥ śaro 'yaṃ kākutstha yadā śete mahārṇave
children.translated_text: This arrow was created, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, when the self-born, unconquered god

children.text: svayambhūr ajito devo yaṃ nāpaśyan surāsurāḥ ||
children.translated_text: lay in the great ocean, unseen by gods and asuras.
Because he was invisible to all beings, this best of arrows
was created by him when he was overcome by anger, for the destruction of the wicked ones,
of <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, O hero, who were engaged in obstruction.
Desiring to create the three worlds, he slew those two with this in battle,
and with this chief of arrows he then made the worlds.

children.text: nāyaṃ mayā śaraḥ pūrvaṃ rāvaṇasya vadhārthinā
children.translated_text: I did not previously release this arrow for the purpose of killing <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: muktaḥ śatrughna bhūtānāṃ mahāṃstrāso bhaved iti ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Śatrughna</s>, thinking that there would be great terror among beings.
And that great trident of his, given by great-souled <s>Tryambaka</s>
for the destruction of enemies, is the supreme weapon of <s>Madhu</s>.

children.text: tat saṃnikṣipya bhavane pūjyamānaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having placed it in his house, where it is worshiped again and again,
he surveys all the quarters and obtains his own food.

children.text: yadā tu yuddham ākāṅkṣan kaścid enaṃ samāhvayet
children.translated_text: But when someone, desiring battle, challenges him,

children.text: tadā śūlaṃ gṛhītvā tad bhasma rakṣaḥ karoti tam ||
children.translated_text: then the rākṣasa takes that trident and reduces him to ashes.
Therefore you, tiger among men, should stand at the gate, weapon in hand,
before he has entered the city and while he is without that weapon.
Before he has entered his house, O bull among men,
challenge him to battle, mighty-armed one; then you will kill the rākṣasa.

children.text: anyathā kriyamāṇe tu avadhyaḥ sa bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: If it is done otherwise, he will be invincible;

children.text: yadi tvevaṃ kṛte vīra vināśam upayāsyati ||
children.translated_text: but if it is done in this way, O hero, he will meet destruction.

children.text: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ śūlasya ca viparyayam
children.translated_text: All this has been explained to you, including the reversal of the trident's advantage,
for the act of glorious <s>Śitikaṇṭha</s> is hard to overcome."

children.text: evam uktvā tu kākutsthaṃ praśasya ca punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to the <s>Kākutstha</s> and praised him again and again,
the delight of the <s>Raghus</s> again spoke another speech:
"These four thousand horses, O bull among men,

children.text: rathānāṃ ca sahasre dve gajānāṃ śatam eva ca ||
children.translated_text: and two thousand chariots, and one hundred elephants,
and market-streets adorned with many kinds of goods,
and likewise actors and dancers, should accompany you, <s>Śatrughna</s>."
Take ten thousand pieces of gold and fine gold, O bull among men,
and go, O <s>Śatrughna</s>, supplied with adequate wealth and vehicles.

children.text: balaṃ ca subhṛtaṃ vīra hṛṣṭapuṣṭam anuttamam
children.translated_text: And address your well-maintained army, hero, cheerful, well-nourished, and unsurpassed;
gladden it with gifts, O best of men.

children.text: na hyarthāstatra tiṣṭhanti na dārā na ca bāndhavāḥ
children.translated_text: For wealth does not stay there, nor wives, nor kinsmen,
but a very pleased body of servants does remain, O <s>Rāghava</s>.
Therefore, having sent forth a great army crowded with joyful men,

children.text: eka eva dhanuṣpāṇistad gaccha tvaṃ madhor vanam ||
children.translated_text: go alone, bow in hand, to that forest of <s>Madhu</s>.

children.text: yathā tvāṃ na prajānāti gacchantaṃ yuddhakāṅkṣiṇam
children.translated_text: So that <s>Lavaṇa</s>, son of <s>Madhu</s>, does not recognize you
as you go desiring battle, go in that way, unsuspected.

children.text: na tasya mṛtyur anyo 'sti kaściddhi puruṣarṣabha
children.translated_text: There is no other death for him at all, O bull among men;

children.text: darśanaṃ yo 'bhigaccheta sa vadhyo lavaṇena hi ||
children.translated_text: whoever comes within his sight is indeed to be killed by <s>Lavaṇa</s>.

children.text: sa grīṣme vyapayāte tu varṣarātra upasthite
children.translated_text: But when summer has passed and the rainy season has arrived,

children.text: hanyāstvaṃ lavaṇaṃ saumya sa hi kālo 'sya durmateḥ ||
children.translated_text: then kill <s>Lavaṇa</s>, gentle one; that is the time for that evil-minded one.
Let your soldiers set out with the great seers placed at their head,
so that, at the end of summer, they may cross the water of the <s>Jāhnavī</s>.

children.text: tataḥ sthāpya balaṃ sarvaṃ nadītīre samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, having stationed the whole army on the riverbank, composed,

children.text: agrato dhanuṣā sārdhaṃ gaccha tvaṃ laghuvikrama ||
children.translated_text: go ahead with your bow, you whose stride is swift.
Thus addressed by <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Śatrughna</s>

children.text: senāmukhyān samānīya tato vākyam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: summoned those mighty leaders of the army and then spoke these words:

children.text: ete vo gaṇitā vāsā yatra yatra nivatsyatha
children.translated_text: These dwelling places have been assigned for you, wherever you are to stay;

children.text: sthātavyaṃ cāvirodhena yathā bādhā na kasyacit ||
children.translated_text: you must stay without conflict, so that there is no trouble for anyone.

children.text: tathā tāṃstu samājñāpya niryāpya ca mahad balam
children.translated_text: After giving them such orders and sending forth the great army,

children.text: kausalyāṃ ca sumitrāṃ ca kaikeyīṃ cābhyavādayat ||
children.translated_text: he paid homage to <s>Kausalyā</s>, <s>Sumitrā</s>, and <s>Kaikeyī</s>.
Having circumambulated <s>Rāma</s> and bowed down with his head,
<s>Śatrughna</s>, scorcher of enemies, was given leave by <s>Rāma</s>.
With folded hands he bowed down to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and <s>Bharata</s>,
and also to the family priest <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>; self-controlled <s>Śatrughna</s>,
after circumambulating them, went out, mighty as he was.

children.text: prasthāpya tad balaṃ sarvaṃ māsamātroṣitaḥ pathi
children.translated_text: Having dispatched that whole army, after staying on the road for about a month,
<s>Śatrughna</s> then went on swiftly by himself, in haste.
The hero, delight of the <s>Rāghavas</s>, after staying two nights on the way,

children.text: vālmīker āśramaṃ puṇyam agacchad vāsam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: came to the holy hermitage of <s>Vālmīki</s>, an excellent lodging.
He paid homage to the great-souled <s>Vālmīki</s>, best of sages,

children.text: kṛtāñjalir atho bhūtvā vākyam etad uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: and then, standing with folded hands, spoke these words:

children.text: bhagavan vastum icchāmi guroḥ kṛtyād ihāgataḥ
children.translated_text: Revered sir, I wish to stay here; I have come on my elder's business.

children.text: śvaḥ prabhāte gamiṣyāmi pratīcīṃ vāruṇīṃ diśam ||
children.translated_text: Tomorrow at daybreak I shall go to the western, <s>Vāruṇī</s>, direction.
Hearing <s>Śatrughna</s>'s words, the bull among sages smiled
and replied to the great-souled one, Welcome to you, greatly renowned one.

children.text: svam āśramam idaṃ saumya rāghavāṇāṃ kulasya ha
children.translated_text: This hermitage is your own, gentle one, belonging indeed to the family of the <s>Rāghavas</s>.

children.text: āsanaṃ pādyam arghyaṃ ca nirviśaṅkaḥ pratīccha me ||
children.translated_text: Accept from me, without hesitation, a seat, water for your feet, and an arghya offering.

children.text: pratigṛhya tataḥ pūjāṃ phalamūlaṃ ca bhojanam
children.translated_text: Then, accepting the honor, and a meal of fruits and roots,
the <s>Kākutstha</s> ate and reached the highest satisfaction.

children.text: sa tu bhuktvā mahābāhur maharṣiṃ tam uvāca ha
children.translated_text: When he had eaten, the long-armed one spoke to that great seer:
Formerly, near whose hermitage was this sacrificial splendor?

children.text: tasya tadbhāṣitaṃ śrutvā vālmīkir vākyam abravīt
children.translated_text: Hearing that statement of his, <s>Vālmīki</s> spoke a reply:
Listen, <s>Śatrughna</s>, to whom this place belonged long ago.
There was an earlier king of yours, son of the great-souled <s>Sudāsa</s>,
named <s>Mitrasaha</s>, mighty and exceedingly righteous.

children.text: sa bāla eva saudāso mṛgayām upacakrame
children.translated_text: While still young, that <s>Saudāsa</s> set out on a hunt;
that hero saw a pair of rākṣasas roaming about.
Terrible, in tiger form, they were devouring animals by the many thousands,
not satisfied and not reaching satiety.

children.text: sa tu tau rākṣasau dṛṣṭvā nirmṛgaṃ ca vanaṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: Seeing those two rākṣasas and the forest made empty of animals,
he was seized by great anger and killed one with a great arrow.

children.text: vinipātya tam ekaṃ tu saudāsaḥ puruṣarṣabhaḥ
children.translated_text: Having struck down that one, <s>Saudāsa</s>, bull among men,
free from fever and with his anger gone, looked upon the slain rākṣasa.
Seeing him looking on, the companion of that rākṣasa

children.text: saṃtāpam akarod ghoraṃ saudāsaṃ cedam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: felt terrible anguish and said this to <s>Saudāsa</s>:

children.text: yasmād anaparāddhaṃ tvaṃ sahāyaṃ mama jaghnivān
children.translated_text: Because you have killed my companion when he had done no wrong,
therefore I too, most sinful one, will give you requital.
Having spoken thus, that rākṣasa vanished there itself.
In the course of time, King <s>Mitrasaha</s> came to be.
The king too performed a sacrifice near that hermitage,
a great <s>aśvamedha</s> sacrifice, and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> supervised it.
There the great sacrifice lasted for many groups of years,
prosperous with supreme splendor, like a sacrifice of the gods.
Then, at the conclusion of the sacrifice, remembering his old enmity,
the rākṣasa, in the form of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, spoke thus to the king:
Today, at the very end of the sacrifice, a meal with meat

children.text: dīyatām iti śīghraṃ vai nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: must be given to me quickly; no deliberation is to be made here.
Hearing that uttered speech from the shape-shifting rākṣasa,
the lord of the earth addressed one skilled in preparing food:

children.text: haviṣyaṃ sāmiṣaṃ svādu yathā bhavati bhojanam
children.translated_text: Make a savory oblation with meat into a meal

children.text: tathā kuruṣva śīghraṃ vai parituṣyed yathā guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: quickly, so that the guru may be satisfied.
At the command of the lord of kings, the cook, his mind bewildered,

children.text: sa ca rakṣaḥ punastatra sūdaveṣam athākarot ||
children.translated_text: And that <s>rākṣasa</s> there again assumed the guise of a cook.

children.text: sa mānuṣam atho māṃsaṃ pārthivāya nyavedayat
children.translated_text: Then he presented human flesh to the king.

children.text: idaṃ svāduhaviṣyaṃ ca sāmiṣaṃ cānnam āhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: "This tasty sacrificial food, and this meal with meat, has been brought."

children.text: sa bhojanaṃ vasiṣṭhāya patnyā sārdham upāharat
children.translated_text: He brought the food to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> together with his wife,
O tiger among men, the meat-containing food brought by the <s>rākṣasa</s>, with <s>Madayantī</s>.
When the Brahmin knew that the meat brought for the meal was human,
he was seized by great anger and began to speak.

children.text: yasmāt tvaṃ bhojanaṃ rājanmamaitad dātum icchasi
children.translated_text: "Because you wish to give me this meal, O king,

children.text: tasmād bhojanam etat te bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore this food will become yours; there is no doubt."

children.text: sa rājā saha patnyā vai praṇipatya muhur muhuḥ
children.translated_text: Then the king, together with his wife, bowed down again and again

children.text: punar vasiṣṭhaṃ provāca yad uktaṃ brahmarūpiṇā ||
children.translated_text: and spoke once more to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> about what had been said by the one in a Brahmin's form.

children.text: tacchrutvā pārthivendrasya rakṣasā vikṛtaṃ ca tat
children.translated_text: Hearing that from the lord of the earth, and that it had been distorted by the <s>rākṣasa</s>,
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s> again addressed the king, that bull among men.

children.text: mayā roṣaparītena yad idaṃ vyāhṛtaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: "This word which I uttered while overcome by anger

children.text: naitacchakyaṃ vṛthā kartuṃ pradāsyāmi ca te varam ||
children.translated_text: cannot be made false; but I shall grant you a boon.
The term of this curse will be twelve years,
and by my grace, great king, when it has passed you will not remember it."

children.text: evaṃ sa rājā taṃ śāpam upabhujyārimardanaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus that king, crusher of foes, endured the curse,
then recovered his kingdom again and protected his subjects.
This is the auspicious place of the sacrifice of that <s>Kalmāṣapāda</s>,
near this hermitage, about which you ask, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: tasya tāṃ pārthivendrasya kathāṃ śrutvā sudāruṇām
children.translated_text: Having heard that very terrible tale of that lord of kings,
he entered the leaf-hut after saluting the great seer.

children.text: yām eva rātriṃ śatrughnaḥ parṇaśālāṃ samāviśat
children.translated_text: On the very night when <s>Śatrughna</s> entered the leaf-hut,

children.text: tām eva rātriṃ sītāpi prasūtā dārakadvayam ||
children.translated_text: on that same night <s>Sītā</s> too gave birth to two boys.
Then, at midnight, the young sons of the sages

children.text: vālmīkeḥ priyam ācakhyuḥ sītāyāḥ prasavaṃ śubham
children.translated_text: told <s>Vālmīki</s> the dear news of <s>Sītā</s>'s auspicious delivery:
"Greatly radiant one, perform a protection for them that destroys spirits."

children.text: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā munir harṣam upāgamat
children.translated_text: Hearing their words, the sage was filled with joy,
and he made for the two a spirit-killing protection, destructive of <s>rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: kuśamuṣṭim upādāya lavaṃ caiva tu sa dvijaḥ
children.translated_text: Taking up a handful of kuśa grass and also small clippings, that twice-born one,
<s>Vālmīki</s>, gave the two a protection that destroys spirits.

children.text: yastayoḥ pūrvajo jātaḥ sa kuśair mantrasaṃskṛtaiḥ
children.translated_text: "The one born first of the two should be wiped clean
with kuśa grasses consecrated by mantra; from that his name will be <s>Kuśa</s>.
And the other of the two should be carefully wiped clean
by the elder women with the clippings; by name he will be <s>Lava</s>.
Thus, by the names <s>Kuśa</s> and <s>Lava</s>, these two twin-born boys
will become famous through the names bestowed by me."

children.text: te rakṣāṃ jagṛhustāṃ ca munihastāt samāhitāḥ
children.translated_text: They received that protective rite from the sage's hand with concentration,
and then, free from stain, they performed the protection for the two boys.

children.text: tathā tāṃ kriyamāṇāṃ tu rakṣāṃ gotraṃ ca nāma ca
children.translated_text: While that protection was being performed, and their lineage and names

children.text: saṃkīrtanaṃ ca rāmasya sītāyāḥ prasavau śubhau ||
children.translated_text: were being proclaimed, along with <s>Rāma</s>'s name and <s>Sītā</s>'s auspicious births,

children.text: ardharātre tu śatrughnaḥ śuśrāva sumahat priyam
children.translated_text: at midnight <s>Śatrughna</s> heard that very great happy news.

children.text: parṇaśālāṃ gato rātrau diṣṭyā diṣṭyeti cābravīt ||
children.translated_text: Having gone to the leaf-hut in the night, he said, "By good fortune, by good fortune!"
And while the great-souled <s>Śatrughna</s> was thus delighted,
that rainy-season night of Śrāvaṇa passed swiftly.

children.text: prabhāte tu mahāvīryaḥ kṛtvā paurvāhṇikaṃ kramam
children.translated_text: At dawn, the very mighty one performed the morning rite,

children.text: muniṃ prāñjalir āmantrya prāyāt paścānmukhaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: took leave of the sage with folded hands, and set out again westward.
Going to the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, after spending seven nights on the road,
he came to stay in the hermitage of sages of holy renown.

children.text: sa tatra munibhiḥ sārdhaṃ bhārgavapramukhair nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: There the king of great fame, together with sages headed by the <s>Bhārgavas</s>,
spent his stay in many kinds of conversation.
Then, when night had begun, <s>Śatrughna</s>
asked the Brahmin <s>Cyavana</s>, descendant of <s>Bhṛgu</s>, about <s>Lavaṇa</s>'s strength and weakness:

children.text: śūlasya ca balaṃ brahman ke ca pūrvaṃ nipātitāḥ
children.translated_text: "And what is the power of the spear, Brahmin? Who in former times were struck down
by that spear-point when they came into single combat?"
Hearing that speech of the great-souled <s>Śatrughna</s>,
the greatly radiant <s>Cyavana</s> replied to the descendant of <s>Raghu</s>:
"Countless are the deeds of this one, O bull among men.
Hear from me what happened, O scion of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> line.
In <s>Ayodhyā</s> in former times there was a mighty king, son of <s>Yuvanāśva</s>,
renowned as <s>Māndhātā</s>, valiant in the three worlds.

children.text: sa kṛtvā pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ śāsane pṛthivīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: That lord of the earth, having brought the whole earth under his rule,
then made an effort to conquer the world of the gods.

children.text: indrasya tu bhayaṃ tīvraṃ surāṇāṃ ca mahātmanām
children.translated_text: A severe fear arose for <s>Indra</s> and for the great-souled gods
when <s>Māndhātā</s> had undertaken his effort, desiring to conquer the world of the gods.
With half of <s>Śakra</s>'s seat and half of his sovereignty, O king,
while being honored by the hosts of gods, he ascended to his vow.
Knowing his sinful intention, <s>Pākaśāsana</s>
spoke these words, preceded by conciliation, to the son of <s>Yuvanāśva</s>:

children.text: rājā tvaṃ mānuṣe loke na tāvat puruṣarṣabha
children.translated_text: "You are king in the human world, O bull among men;
without yet making the earth obedient, you desire the gods' kingdom here.

children.text: yadi vīra samagrā te medinī nikhilā vaśe
children.translated_text: If, hero, the entire earth is wholly under your control,
then rule the gods' kingdom here, together with servants, army, and vehicles."

children.text: indram evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ tu māndhātā vākyam abravīt
children.translated_text: When <s>Indra</s> had spoken thus, <s>Māndhātā</s> uttered this reply:

children.text: kva me śakra pratihataṃ śāsanaṃ pṛthivītale ||
children.translated_text: "Where, O <s>Śakra</s>, has my command been checked on the surface of the earth?"

children.text: tam uvāca sahasrākṣo lavaṇo nāma rākṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: The thousand-eyed one said to him, "A rākṣasa named <s>Lavaṇa</s>,
son of <s>Madhu</s>, in <s>Madhuvana</s>, does not obey your command, sinless one."
Hearing that dreadful and unwelcome statement spoken by the thousand-eyed one,

children.text: vrīḍito 'vāṅmukho rājā vyāhartuṃ na śaśāka ha ||
children.translated_text: the king, ashamed and with face cast down, was unable to speak.

children.text: āmantrya tu sahasrākṣaṃ hriyā kiṃcid avāṅmukhaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after taking leave of the thousand-eyed one, with his face somewhat lowered in shame,
that illustrious lord of men returned again to this world.
Harboring resentment in his heart, together with his servants, army, and vehicles,

children.text: ājagāma madhoḥ putraṃ vaśe kartum aninditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the blameless one came to bring <s>Madhu</s>'s son under his control.
That bull among men, desiring battle with <s>Lavaṇa</s>,
sent a messenger to <s>Lavaṇa</s>'s presence.

children.text: sa gatvā vipriyāṇyāha bahūni madhunaḥ sutam
children.translated_text: Having gone there, he said many unpleasant things to <s>Madhu</s>'s son;

children.text: vadantam evaṃ taṃ dūtaṃ bhakṣayāmāsa rākṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and while that messenger was speaking thus, the rākṣasa ate him.
When the messenger was delayed, the king, filled with anger,
assailed that rākṣasa on every side with a shower of arrows.

children.text: tataḥ prahasya lavaṇaḥ śūlaṃ jagrāha pāṇinā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Lavaṇa</s>, laughing, took a spear in his hand
and released that supreme weapon to kill him together with his followers.
That blazing spear, after reducing to ashes the king
together with his servants, army, and vehicles, returned again to <s>Lavaṇa</s>'s hand.

children.text: evaṃ sa rājā sumahān hataḥ sabalavāhanaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus that very great king was slain together with his army and vehicles;

children.text: śūlasya ca balaṃ vīra aprameyam anuttamam ||
children.translated_text: and the power of that spear, hero, is immeasurable and unsurpassed.

children.text: śvaḥ prabhāte tu lavaṇaṃ vadhiṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: But at daybreak tomorrow you will kill <s>Lavaṇa</s>, without doubt,
quickly, when he has not taken up his weapon; your victory is certain.

children.text: kathāṃ kathayatāṃ teṣāṃ jayaṃ cākāṅkṣatāṃ śubham
children.translated_text: As they told these tales and wished for auspicious victory,
the night of great-souled <s>Śatrughna</s> quickly passed.

children.text: tataḥ prabhāte vimale tasmin kāle sa rākṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, in the clear morning at that time, that heroic rākṣasa
went out from the city, driven by the need to obtain food for eating.

children.text: etasminn antare śūraḥ śatrughno yamunāṃ nadīm
children.translated_text: Meanwhile the brave <s>Śatrughna</s> crossed the river <s>Yamunā</s>
and stood at the gate of <s>Madhupura</s>, bow in hand.
Then, when midday had arrived, that rākṣasa of cruel deeds
came carrying a load of many thousands of living creatures.

children.text: tato dadarśa śatrughnaṃ sthitaṃ dvāri dhṛtāyudham
children.translated_text: Then he saw <s>Śatrughna</s> standing at the gate with weapon in hand,

children.text: tam uvāca tato rakṣaḥ kim anena kariṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: and the rākṣasa then said to him, "What will you do with this?
Thousands like you, armed men, lowest of men,

children.text: bhakṣitāni mayā roṣāt kālam ākāṅkṣase nu kim ||
children.translated_text: have been eaten by me in anger. Are you waiting for your appointed time?
And this meal of mine is still not complete, lowest of men.

children.text: svayaṃ praviṣṭo nu mukhaṃ katham āsādya durmate ||
children.translated_text: How is it, fool, that after coming here you have entered my mouth of your own accord?"
As he was speaking in this way and laughing again and again,
valorous <s>Śatrughna</s> shed tears out of anger.
From every limb of great-souled <s>Śatrughna</s>, overwhelmed by anger,
radiant rays made of splendor streamed forth.
And the greatly enraged <s>Śatrughna</s> said to that night-roamer,

children.text: yoddhum icchāmi durbuddhe dvandvayuddhaṃ tvayā saha ||
children.translated_text: "Evil-minded one, I wish to fight a duel with you.
I am the son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, brother of wise <s>Rāma</s>;
I am named <s>Śatrughna</s>, slayer of foes, and I have come desiring your death.
Grant me, who desire battle, a duel.

children.text: śatrustvaṃ sarvajīvānāṃ na me jīvan gamiṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: You are the enemy of all living beings; you will not depart alive from me."

children.text: tasmiṃstathā bruvāṇe tu rākṣasaḥ prahasann iva
children.translated_text: When he had spoken thus, the rākṣasa, as if laughing,
replied to that best of men, "By good fortune you have arrived, fool.

children.text: mama mātṛṣvasur bhrātā rāvaṇo nāma rākṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: The rākṣasa named <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the brother of my mother's sister,
was slain by <s>Rāma</s>, evil-minded lowest of men, for the sake of a woman.

children.text: tacca sarvaṃ mayā kṣāntaṃ rāvaṇasya kulakṣayam
children.translated_text: I endured all that destruction of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s family,

children.text: avajñāṃ purataḥ kṛtvā mayā yūyaṃ viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: setting you all, especially, before me as beneath contempt.

children.text: na hatāśca hi me sarve paribhūtāstṛṇaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: You all were not killed by me because you were despised like grass,
both those already born and those yet to be, and you too, lowest of men.

children.text: tasya te yuddhakāmasya yuddhaṃ dāsyāmi durmate
children.translated_text: For you, who desire battle, I will give battle, fool,

children.text: īpsitaṃ yādṛśaṃ tubhyaṃ sajjaye yāvad āyudham ||
children.translated_text: just as you wish, as soon as I arm myself."

children.text: tam uvācātha śatrughnaḥ kva me jīvan gamiṣyasi
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śatrughna</s> said to him, "Where will you go while still alive from me?
Even a weak enemy, once he has come, should not be released by one who is resolute.

children.text: yo hi viklavayā buddhyā prasaraṃ śatrave dadau
children.translated_text: For the man who, with a cowardly mind, gives his enemy an opening
is killed through dull-wittedness, just like an unmanly coward.
Hearing that statement of great-souled <s>Śatrughna</s>,

children.text: krodham āhārayat tīvraṃ tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt ||
children.translated_text: he summoned up fierce anger and said, 'Stand! Stand!'

children.text: pāṇau pāṇiṃ viniṣpiṣya dantān kaṭakaṭāyya ca
children.translated_text: Crushing one hand in the other and gnashing his teeth,
<s>Lavaṇa</s> repeatedly challenged the tiger of the <s>Raghu</s>s.

children.text: taṃ bruvāṇaṃ tathā vākyaṃ lavaṇaṃ ghoravikramam
children.translated_text: To <s>Lavaṇa</s>, of dreadful valor, speaking such words,
<s>Śatrughna</s>, slayer of the enemies of the gods, spoke this word:

children.text: śatrughno na tadā jāto yadānye nirjitāstvayā
children.translated_text: "<s>Śatrughna</s> had not yet been born when the others were conquered by you;

children.text: tad adya bāṇābhihato vraja tvaṃ yamasādanam ||
children.translated_text: therefore today, struck by my arrows, go to the abode of <s>Yama</s>.
Today let the seers too, evil-souled one, and the learned brahmins,
see you slain by me in battle, as the gods saw <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
When you, night-roamer, are burned by my arrows and have fallen today,

children.text: puraṃ janapadaṃ cāpi kṣemam etad bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: this city and countryside will be secure.
Today an arrow, loosed from my arm, with a head like the thunderbolt,

children.text: pravekṣyate te hṛdayaṃ padmam aṃśur ivārkajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: will enter your heart as a ray born of the sun enters a lotus."
Thus addressed, <s>Lavaṇa</s>, faint with anger, hurled a great tree
at <s>Śatrughna</s>'s breast, and the hero cut it into a hundred pieces.

children.text: tad dṛṣṭvā viphalaṃ karma rākṣasaḥ punar eva tu
children.translated_text: Seeing that his action had failed, the powerful rākṣasa again

children.text: pādapān subahūn gṛhya śatrughne vyasṛjad balī ||
children.translated_text: seized many trees and hurled them at <s>Śatrughna</s>.
And radiant <s>Śatrughna</s>, as the many trees came flying toward him,
cut each one apart with three or four bent-jointed arrows.
Then <s>Śatrughna</s>, endowed with valor, released a shower made of arrows

children.text: śatrughno vīryasampanno vivyathe na ca rākṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: against the rākṣasa's chest, but the rākṣasa was not distressed.

children.text: tataḥ prahasya lavaṇo vṛkṣam utpāṭya līlayā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Lavaṇa</s>, laughing, casually uprooted a tree
and struck the hero on the head; his limbs slackened and he fainted.
When that hero had fallen, a great cry of alarm arose
among the sages, the hosts of gods, and also the gandharvas and apsarases.

children.text: tam avajñāya tu hataṃ śatrughnaṃ bhuvi pātitam
children.translated_text: Disregarding <s>Śatrughna</s> as slain and fallen on the ground,

children.text: rakṣo labdhāntaram api na viveśa svam ālayam ||
children.translated_text: the rākṣasa, though he had gained his opportunity, did not enter his own dwelling.

children.text: nāpi śūlaṃ prajagrāha taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhuvi pātitam
children.translated_text: Nor did he take up the trident, seeing him fallen on the ground;

children.text: tato hata iti jñātvā tān bhakṣān samudāvahat ||
children.translated_text: then, knowing him to be dead, he brought out those foods.
But after a moment, having regained consciousness, <s>Śatrughna</s> again stood there with his weapon ready,
at the rākṣasa's gate, honored by the sages.

children.text: tato divyam amoghaṃ taṃ jagrāha śaram uttamam
children.translated_text: Then he took up that excellent divine arrow, unfailing,

children.text: jvalantaṃ tejasā ghoraṃ pūrayantaṃ diśo daśa ||
children.translated_text: blazing with terrible splendor and filling the ten directions.
It had a thunderbolt-like point and thunderbolt-like speed, with the weight of <s>Meru</s> and <s>Mandara</s>,
bent at every joint and unconquered in battles.
Its body was smeared with blood and sandal, it had beautiful feathers, and it flew straight,
terrible to the lords of dānavas, to the chiefs of mountains, and to the asuras.

children.text: taṃ dīptam iva kālāgniṃ yugānte samupasthite
children.translated_text: Seeing it blazing like the fire of Time appearing at the end of an age,
all beings were overcome with terror.
Indeed the whole world, together with gods, asuras, gandharvas, sages,
and hosts of apsarases, became disturbed and approached the Grandfather.
They said to the lord of gods, the giver of boons, the great-grandfather:

children.text: kaccil lokakṣayo deva prāpto vā yugasaṃkṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Has the destruction of the worlds arrived, O god, or the end of the age?

children.text: nedṛśaṃ dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ na śrutaṃ vā prapitāmaha
children.translated_text: Such a thing has never before been seen or even heard of, O great-grandfather:
confusion from fear among the gods, and destruction of the worlds, O lord."

children.text: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing those words of theirs, <s>Brahmā</s>, the Grandfather of the worlds,
explained the cause of the fear to the gods, while giving them reassurance:
"For the slaying of <s>Lavaṇa</s> in battle, the arrow is held by <s>Śatrughna</s>;

children.text: tejasā yasya sarve sma saṃmūḍhāḥ surasattamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: by its splendor we have all been bewildered, O best of the gods.

children.text: eṣo hi pūrvaṃ devasya lokakartuḥ sanātanaḥ
children.translated_text: This, dear ones, is the former arrow of the eternal god, the maker of the worlds,

children.text: śarastejomayo vatsā yena vai bhayam āgatam ||
children.translated_text: made of splendor, because of which fear has arisen.
This great arrow was fashioned by that great-souled one
for the sake of <s>Kaiṭabha</s> and <s>Madhu</s>, for the destruction of those two daityas.
Know this, then, as the splendor-filled arrow of <s>Viṣṇu</s>;

children.text: eṣā caiva tanuḥ pūrvā viṣṇostasya mahātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and this is the former body of that great-souled <s>Viṣṇu</s> himself.
Go from here and behold <s>Lavaṇa</s>, the foremost rākṣasa, being slain
by the great-souled hero, the younger brother of <s>Rāma</s>."

children.text: tasya te devadevasya niśamya madhurāṃ giram
children.translated_text: Hearing that sweet speech of the god of gods,
they went to the place where <s>Śatrughna</s> and <s>Lavaṇa</s> were both fighting.
All beings saw that arrow, shining like a divine thing,
held in <s>Śatrughna</s>'s hand, as if the fire at the end of the age had arisen.

children.text: ākāśam āvṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā devair hi raghunandanaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing the sky covered by the gods, the delight of the <s>Raghus</s>

children.text: siṃhanādaṃ muhuḥ kṛtvā dadarśa lavaṇaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: roared like a lion again and again, and then looked once more at <s>Lavaṇa</s>.
Then, summoned by that great-souled <s>Śatrughna</s>,
<s>Lavaṇa</s>, filled with anger, came forward for battle.

children.text: ā karṇāt sa vikṛṣyātha tad dhanur dhanvināṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: Then that best of bowmen drew the bow back to his ear
and released the great arrow into <s>Lavaṇa</s>'s broad chest.
Quickly tearing open his chest, it entered the netherworld.
After going to the divine netherworld, the arrow honored by the gods
swiftly returned again to the delight of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> line.
Pierced by <s>Śatrughna</s>'s arrow, that night-roaming <s>Lavaṇa</s>
suddenly fell to the earth like a mountain struck by a thunderbolt.
And when the rākṣasa <s>Lavaṇa</s> had been slain, that great divine trident,
while all beings looked on, passed back under <s>Rudra</s>'s control.
Having destroyed the fear of these three worlds by the fall of a single arrow, the heroic scion of <s>Raghu</s>,
with bow and arrow raised, shone forth like the thousand-rayed sun after dispelling darkness.

children.text: hate tu lavaṇe devāḥ sendrāḥ sāgnipurogamāḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Lavaṇa</s> had been slain, the gods, together with <s>Indra</s> and with <s>Agni</s> at their head,
spoke very sweet words to <s>Śatrughna</s>, scorcher of enemies:

children.text: diṣṭyā te vijayo vatsa diṣṭyā lavaṇarākṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: "By good fortune victory is yours, dear one; by good fortune the rākṣasa <s>Lavaṇa</s>
has been slain, tiger among men. Choose a boon, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: varadāḥ sma mahābāho sarva eva samāgatāḥ
children.translated_text: We have all come together as givers of boons, mighty-armed one,
desiring victory for you, for our appearance is not fruitless."

children.text: devānāṃ bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā śūro mūrdhni kṛtāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing the speech of the gods, the heroic, mighty-armed <s>Śatrughna</s>,
with joined palms raised to his head and with self-control, replied:
"May I quickly obtain this lovely city of <s>Madhu</s>,

children.text: niveśaṃ prāpnuyāṃ śīghram eṣa me 'stu varo mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the charming <s>Madhurā</s>, built by the gods, as a settlement; let this be the boon I choose."

children.text: taṃ devāḥ prītamanaso bāḍham ityeva rāghavam
children.translated_text: The gods, pleased in mind, said to that <s>Rāghava</s>, "So be it."

children.text: bhaviṣyati purī ramyā śūrasenā na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "It shall without doubt be the lovely city called <s>Śūrasenā</s>."
Having spoken thus, those great-souled ones then ascended to heaven,
and greatly radiant <s>Śatrughna</s> also brought that army near.
That army came quickly when it heard <s>Śatrughna</s>'s command,
and <s>Śatrughna</s>, by command, began the settlement.

children.text: sā purī divyasaṃkāśā varṣe dvādaśame śubhā
children.translated_text: That auspicious city, resembling a divine one, in the twelfth year
was established in the territory of the <s>Śūrasenas</s>, wholly free from fear.
The fields were rich with crops; <s>Vāsava</s> rained at the proper time.
Its heroic men were free from illness, protected by the arm of <s>Śatrughna</s>.
It shone like a half-moon, beautified by the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>;
it was adorned with foremost houses, and adorned with crossroads and marketplaces.

children.text: yacca tena mahacchūnyaṃ lavaṇena kṛtaṃ purā
children.translated_text: And that great empty place which <s>Lavaṇa</s> had formerly made
the hero beautified with prosperity in many kinds of merchandise.
When prosperous <s>Śatrughna</s>, the younger brother of <s>Bharata</s>, saw that city
prosperous and filled with wealth, he was exceedingly pleased and attained supreme joy.

children.text: tasya buddhiḥ samutpannā niveśya madhurāṃ purīm
children.translated_text: Then this thought arose in him: "Having established the city of <s>Madhurā</s>,
in the auspicious twelfth year I should look upon the feet of <s>Rāma</s>."
Then in the twelfth year <s>Śatrughna</s> desired to go
to <s>Ayodhyā</s>, ruled by <s>Rāma</s>, accompanied by a small force of attendants.
Having sent back the ministers, the chief officers of the army, and the household priest,
he went in an excellent shining chariot yoked with horses.

children.text: sa gatvā gaṇitān vāsān saptāṣṭau raghunandanaḥ
children.translated_text: After spending seven or eight counted nights on the road, that delight of the <s>Raghus</s>
quickly reached <s>Ayodhyā</s>, eager for the sight of <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: sa praviśya purīṃ ramyāṃ śrīmān ikṣvākunandanaḥ
children.translated_text: Entering the lovely city, the illustrious delight of the <s>Ikṣvākus</s>,
the mighty-armed one entered the place where <s>Rāma</s> of great splendor was.
Having bowed to the great-souled one, who blazed as if with majesty,
he stood with joined palms and spoke to <s>Rāma</s>, whose valor is true:

children.text: yad ājñaptaṃ mahārāja sarvaṃ tat kṛtavān aham
children.translated_text: "Whatever was commanded, great king, I have done all of it.

children.text: hataḥ sa lavaṇaḥ pāpaḥ purī sā ca niveśitā ||
children.translated_text: That sinful <s>Lavaṇa</s> has been slain, and that city has been established.

children.text: dvādaśaṃ ca gataṃ varṣaṃ tvāṃ vinā raghunandana
children.translated_text: The twelfth year too has passed without you, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>.

children.text: notsaheyam ahaṃ vastuṃ tvayā virahito nṛpa ||
children.translated_text: I cannot bear to live separated from you, O king.
Therefore show me favor, O <s>Kākutstha</s> of immeasurable valor.
Like a calf without its mother, I live away from home without you."
As <s>Śatrughna</s> was speaking thus, <s>Rāma</s> embraced him and said this:

children.text: mā viṣādaṃ kṛthā vīra naitat kṣatriyaceṣṭitam ||
children.translated_text: "Do not give way to sorrow, hero; this is not the conduct of a <s>kṣatriya</s>.
Kings do not sink down in despondency during separations, O <s>Rāghava</s>.
Subjects must be protected according to <s>kṣatradharma</s> (the duty of rulership), O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: kāle kāle ca māṃ vīra ayodhyām avalokitum
children.translated_text: From time to time, hero, come to <s>Ayodhyā</s>

children.text: āgaccha tvaṃ naraśreṣṭha gantāsi ca puraṃ tava ||
children.translated_text: to see me, best of men; and you shall return to your own city.

children.text: mamāpi tvaṃ sudayitaḥ prāṇair api na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: You too are very dear to me, even dearer than life, without doubt.
But the protection of the kingdom must necessarily be carried out.

children.text: tasmāt tvaṃ vasa kākutstha pañcarātraṃ mayā saha
children.translated_text: Therefore, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, stay with me for five nights;
afterwards you shall go to <s>Madhurā</s> with your attendants, army, and vehicles."
Hearing this righteous and pleasing speech of <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: śatrughno dīnayā vācā bāḍham ityeva cābravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śatrughna</s> answered in a humble voice, "So be it."
That <s>Kākutstha</s>, the great archer, stayed there for five nights
according to <s>Rāghava</s>'s command, and then prepared for departure.
Taking leave of great-souled <s>Rāma</s>, whose valor is true,
and of <s>Bharata</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, he mounted his great chariot.
Accompanied for a long distance by those two, by great-souled <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>

children.text: bharatena ca śatrughno jagāmāśu purīṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: and by <s>Bharata</s>, <s>Śatrughna</s> then quickly went to his city.

children.text: prasthāpya tu sa śatrughnaṃ bhrātṛbhyāṃ saha rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: After sending <s>Śatrughna</s> off together with his brothers, <s>Rāghava</s>
rejoiced, happy as he protected the kingdom according to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order).
Then, after some days, an aged twice-born man from the countryside
took up the corpse of a child and came to the royal gate.
Weeping, with many kinds of words filled with the syllables of affection,

children.text: asakṛt putra putreti vākyam etad uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: again and again he uttered this cry: "My son! My son!"

children.text: kiṃ nu me duṣkṛtaṃ karma pūrvaṃ dehāntare kṛtam
children.translated_text: "What evil deed of mine was done before, in another body,

children.text: yad ahaṃ putram ekaṃ tvāṃ paśyāmi nidhanaṃ gatam ||
children.translated_text: that I see you, my only son, gone to death?
You were a child not yet come to youth, only five years old,

children.text: akāle kālam āpannaṃ duḥkhāya mama putraka ||
children.translated_text: overtaken by death before your time, to my grief, my little son.

children.text: alpair ahobhir nidhanaṃ gamiṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: In a few days I too shall go to death, without doubt,

children.text: ahaṃ ca jananī caiva tava śokena putraka ||
children.translated_text: and so will your mother, through sorrow for you, my son.

children.text: na smarāmyanṛtaṃ hyuktaṃ na ca hiṃsāṃ smarāmyaham
children.translated_text: I do not remember ever speaking an untruth, nor do I remember doing violence.

children.text: kena me duṣkṛtenādya bāla eva mamātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: By what evil deed of mine has my own son now, while still only a child,
been led to the abode of <s>Vaivasvata</s> without performing the rites owed to his father?

children.text: nedṛśaṃ dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ me śrutaṃ vā ghoradarśanam
children.translated_text: Such a terrible sight has never before been seen by me, nor even heard of:
the death of those whose time had not yet come, as now in the realm of <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: rāmasya duṣkṛtaṃ kiṃcinmahad asti na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: There must be some great wrongdoing of <s>Rāma</s>; there is no doubt.
O king, restore this child who has fallen under the power of death.

children.text: bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito rājan dīrgham āyur avāpnuhi
children.translated_text: Together with your brothers, O king, may you obtain a long life.

children.text: uṣitāḥ sma sukhaṃ rājye tavāsmin sumahābala ||
children.translated_text: We have lived happily in this kingdom of yours, O very mighty one.
But now the realm of the great-souled <s>Ikṣvākus</s> is without a protector,
having found here as its protector <s>Rāma</s>, a king who has caused the death of a child.
For subjects perish through the faults of a king when they are not protected according to rule.
When the ruler is of improper conduct, people die before their time.
When people in cities and in the countryside

children.text: kurvate na ca rakṣāsti tadākālakṛtaṃ bhayam ||
children.translated_text: commit improper acts and there is no protection, then fear arises from untimely death.
Clearly this will be a fault of the king; there is no doubt.

children.text: pure janapade vāpi tadā bālavadho hyayam ||
children.translated_text: Whether in the city or in the countryside, this is therefore the killing of a child.

children.text: evaṃ bahuvidhair vākyair nindayāno muhur muhuḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, with many kinds of words, denouncing him again and again,
the man, scorched by grief, embraced that son of his.

children.text: tathā tu karuṇaṃ tasya dvijasya paridevitam
children.translated_text: When that lamentation of the twice-born man was so pitiful
<s>Rāghava</s> heard the whole matter, filled with sorrow and grief.
Deeply scorched by sorrow, he summoned his ministers,
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and <s>Vāmadeva</s>, and his brothers together with the townsmen.

children.text: tato dvijā vasiṣṭhena sārdham aṣṭau praveśitāḥ
children.translated_text: Then eight twice-born men were brought in together with <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.
They said to the king, who was like a god, "May you prosper."
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, then <s>Maudgalya</s>, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, and <s>Kāśyapa</s>,
then <s>Kātyāyana</s>, <s>Jābāli</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, and also <s>Nārada</s>:
all these bulls among the twice-born were seated on seats,
and so too the ministers and townsmen, each suitably and in fitting order.
When all of them, blazing with splendor, had sat down,

children.text: raghavaḥ sarvam ācaṣṭe dvijo yasmāt praroditi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> told them everything, the reason why the twice-born man was weeping.

children.text: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rājño dīnasya nāradaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that statement of the dejected king, <s>Nārada</s>

children.text: pratyuvāca śubhaṃ vākyam ṛṣīṇāṃ saṃnidhau nṛpam ||
children.translated_text: addressed the ruler with an auspicious speech in the presence of the seers.
"Listen, O king, how this destruction of the child has come at its proper time.
After hearing what is to be done, hero, do it, delight of the <s>Raghu</s>s.

children.text: purā kṛtayuge rāma brāhmaṇā vai tapasvinaḥ
children.translated_text: Formerly, in the <s>Kṛta</s> age, O <s>Rāma</s>, brahmins alone were ascetics;
at that time, O king, no non-brahmin was in any way an ascetic.
In that age, radiant, wholly brahman-like, and uncovered,
all were then born free from death and far-seeing.
Then came the age called <s>Tretā</s> among embodied human beings,
in which kṣatriyas are born, endowed with austerity from before.
In former birth they were superior through valor and austerity,
the great-souled human beings in that <s>Tretā</s> age.

children.text: brahmakṣatraṃ tu tat sarvaṃ yat pūrvam aparaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: All that brahman and kṣatra, both what was earlier and what was later,
in the two ages was endowed with equal power.

children.text: apaśyantastu te sarve viśeṣam adhikaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: But when all of them saw afterward a greater distinction,
they everywhere established the fourfold system of varṇas.

children.text: adharmaḥ pādam ekaṃ tu pātayat pṛthivītale
children.translated_text: <s>Adharma</s> (unrighteousness) set one foot down upon the earth,
and because they were joined with <s>adharma</s>, the twice-born became diminished.
Then for the first time a fixed limit of lifespan became manifest.
People still practiced only auspicious deeds, devoted to truth and <s>dharma</s>.
In the <s>Tretā</s> age, the brahmins and kṣatriyas who lived then

children.text: tapo 'tapyanta te sarve śuśrūṣām apare janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all practiced austerity, while the other people gave service.
That supreme <s>dharma</s> of theirs then came to the vaiśyas and śūdras.
The śūdras in particular performed reverence toward all the varṇas.
Then <s>adharma</s> brought down its second foot,
and thereafter the condition called the <s>Dvāpara</s> age arose.
While that state called <s>Dvāpara</s> was taking place at the decline of the age,
<s>adharma</s> and falsehood increased, bull among men.
In that condition called <s>Dvāpara</s>, austerity entered the vaiśyas.

children.text: na śūdro labhate dharmam ugraṃ taptaṃ nararṣabha ||
children.translated_text: A śūdra does not obtain the <s>dharma</s> of severe austerity, bull among men.
Yet, best of men, a man of a lower varṇa is practicing very great austerity.

children.text: bhaviṣyā śūdrayonyāṃ hi tapaścaryā kalau yuge ||
children.translated_text: For in the future, in the Kali age, ascetic practice will belong even among those born as śūdras.
O <s>Rāma</s>, this is supreme <s>adharma</s> in the <s>Dvāpara</s>, upheld by a śūdra.
Indeed, at the edge of your realm, O king, a man of great austerity,
a foolish śūdra, is practicing austerity; therefore this killing of the child has occurred.

children.text: yo hyadharmam akāryaṃ vā viṣaye pārthivasya hi
children.translated_text: Whoever, in a king's territory, does what is <s>adharma</s> or what ought not to be done,

children.text: karoti rājaśārdūla pure vā durmatir naraḥ
children.translated_text: whether in the city or elsewhere, tiger among kings, that evil-minded man

children.text: kṣipraṃ hi narakaṃ yāti sa ca rājā na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: quickly goes to hell, and so does the king, without doubt.

children.text: sa tvaṃ puruṣaśārdūla mārgasva viṣayaṃ svakam
children.translated_text: Therefore, tiger among men, search your own realm.
Wherever you may see an evil deed, there apply your effort.
In this way there will be an increase of <s>dharma</s> for you, and a lengthening of men's lives,
best of men, and there will also be life for this child."

children.text: nāradasya tu tad vākyaṃ śrutvāmṛtamayaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech of <s>Nārada</s>, which was like nectar,

children.text: praharṣam atulaṃ lebhe lakṣmaṇaṃ cedam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: he obtained incomparable joy and said this to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:
"Go, gentle one, console the best of the twice-born, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: bālasya ca śarīraṃ tat tailadroṇyāṃ nidhāpaya ||
children.translated_text: and place the child's body in a trough of oil.
With the most excellent perfumes and with very fragrant oils,

children.text: yathā na kṣīyate bālastathā saumya vidhīyatām ||
children.translated_text: gentle one, arrange it so that the child does not decay.
See that no destruction or splitting apart occurs

children.text: vipattiḥ paribhedo vā bhavenna ca tathā kuru ||
children.translated_text: in the guarded body of the child of unblemished deeds; act in that way."
Having thus instructed <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> of auspicious marks,
the greatly renowned <s>Kākutstha</s> thought in his mind of <s>Puṣpaka</s>, saying, "Come."

children.text: iṅgitaṃ sa tu vijñāya puṣpako hemabhūṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: Perceiving his intention, the gold-adorned <s>Puṣpaka</s>
came in a moment near to <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: so 'bravīt praṇato bhūtvā ayam asmi narādhipa
children.translated_text: Bowing down, it said, "Here I am, lord of men,
obedient to you, mighty-armed one; your servant stands ready."
Hearing the pleasing speech of <s>Puṣpaka</s>, the lord of men
honored those great seers and mounted the aerial car.

children.text: dhanur gṛhītvā tūṇīṃ ca khaḍgaṃ ca ruciraprabham
children.translated_text: Taking his bow, quiver, and sword of beautiful brilliance,
and leaving the two heroes, <s>Saumitri</s> and <s>Bharata</s>, in the city,

children.text: prāyāt pratīcīṃ sa marūn vicinvaṃśca samantataḥ
children.translated_text: he set out toward the west, searching everywhere through the deserts,
and the glorious one went to the northern direction, covered by the <s>Himavat</s>.
Not seeing there even the slightest evil deed,
the lord of men then also inspected the whole eastern direction.
Then the descendant of royal seers entered the southern direction.
On the northern side of <s>Śaivala</s> he saw a very great lake.

children.text: tasmin sarasi tapyantaṃ tāpasaṃ sumahat tapaḥ
children.translated_text: In that lake, practicing a very great austerity,
the illustrious <s>Rāghava</s> saw an ascetic hanging head downward.
Then, approaching him as he practiced that supreme austerity,

children.text: uvāca rāghavo vākyaṃ dhanyastvam asi suvrata ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> spoke these words: "Blessed are you, observant of good vows.
In what birth-class, grown great in austerity, do you abide, firm in valor?

children.text: kautūhalāt tvāṃ pṛcchāmi rāmo dāśarathir hyaham ||
children.translated_text: Out of curiosity I ask you; for I am <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>.
What desired aim is yours? Is it the winning of heaven, refuge of the excellent?

children.text: yam āśritya tapastaptaṃ śrotum icchāmi tāpasa ||
children.translated_text: Relying on which aim have you practiced this austerity? I wish to hear it, ascetic.

children.text: brāhmaṇo vāsi bhadraṃ te kṣatriyo vāsi durjayaḥ
children.translated_text: Are you a brahmin? Welfare to you. Or are you a kṣatriya, unconquerable one?

children.text: vaiśyo vā yadi vā śūdraḥ satyam etad bravīhi me ||
children.translated_text: Or are you a vaiśya, or else a śūdra? Tell me this truthfully."
Hearing that speech of <s>Rāma</s>, whose acts were unwearied,
he, with his head downward and remaining just so, spoke these words:
"I was born in a śūdra womb and have undertaken fierce austerity.
I seek godhood, O <s>Rāma</s> of great fame, with this very body.
I do not speak falsely, O king, from a desire to conquer the world of the gods.

children.text: śūdraṃ māṃ viddhi kākutstha śambūkaṃ nāma nāmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Know me, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, to be a śūdra, named by name <s>Śambūka</s>."
While that śūdra was speaking, <s>Rāghava</s> drew from its sheath
a spotless sword, beautifully shining, and cut off his head.
At that very moment that boy was joined again with life.
Then lotus-eyed <s>Rāma</s> went to the hermitage of <s>Agastya</s>,

children.text: sa gatvā vinayenaiva taṃ natvā mumude sukhī ||
children.translated_text: and, having gone there, bowed to him with humility and rejoiced happily.
After saluting the great-souled one, who blazed as if with splendor,
the lord of men received supreme hospitality and sat down.
The very splendid one, born from a jar and great in austerity, said to him:

children.text: svāgataṃ te naraśreṣṭha diṣṭyā prāpto 'si rāghava ||
children.translated_text: "Welcome to you, best of men. By good fortune you have arrived, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: tvaṃ me bahumato rāma guṇair bahubhir uttamaiḥ
children.translated_text: You are highly honored by me, O <s>Rāma</s>, because of your many excellent virtues;

children.text: atithiḥ pūjanīyaśca mama rājan hṛdi sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as a guest you are to be worshiped, O king, and you are established in my heart.

children.text: surā hi kathayanti tvām āgataṃ śūdraghātinam
children.translated_text: For the gods speak of you as having come, the slayer of a śūdra;

children.text: brāhmaṇasya tu dharmeṇa tvayā jīvāpitaḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and by your adherence to <s>dharma</s>, the brahmin's son has been brought back to life.

children.text: uṣyatāṃ ceha rajanīṃ sakāśe mama rāghava
children.translated_text: Spend this night here in my presence, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: prabhāte puṣpakeṇa tvaṃ gantā svapuram eva hi ||
children.translated_text: At dawn you will go by the <s>Puṣpaka</s> to your own city.
And this ornament, gentle one, fashioned by <s>Viśvakarman</s>,
divine, shining by its own splendor with a divine form,
accept it, O <s>Kākutstha</s>; do what is dear to me, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: dattasya hi punar dānaṃ sumahat phalam ucyate
children.translated_text: For the giving again of what has been given is said to have a very great fruit.

children.text: tasmāt pradāsye vidhivat tat pratīccha nararṣabha ||
children.translated_text: Therefore I shall give it in due form; accept it, bull among men."
Then <s>Rāma</s> accepted from that great-souled sage

children.text: divyam ābharaṇaṃ citraṃ pradīptam iva bhāskaram ||
children.translated_text: the wonderful divine ornament, blazing like the sun.
Having accepted that excellent ornament,
<s>Rāma</s> then began to ask about the origin of that divine object:

children.text: atyadbhutam idaṃ brahman vapuṣā yuktam uttamam
children.translated_text: "This is exceedingly wondrous, O brahmin, excellent and endowed with beauty.

children.text: kathaṃ bhagavatā prāptaṃ kuto vā kena vāhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: How was it obtained by your reverence, and from where, and by whom was it brought?
Out of curiosity, O brahmin of great fame, I ask you.

children.text: āścaryāṇāṃ bahūnāṃ hi nidhiḥ paramako bhavān ||
children.translated_text: For you are the supreme treasury of many wonders."

children.text: evaṃ bruvati kākutsthe munir vākyam athābravīt
children.translated_text: When <s>Kākutstha</s> had spoken thus, the sage then said these words:

children.text: śṛṇu rāma yathāvṛttaṃ purā tretāyuge gate ||
children.translated_text: "Hear, O <s>Rāma</s>, what happened in the past, when the <s>Tretā</s> age had gone by.
Formerly, indeed, in the <s>Tretā</s> age, there was a very extensive forest,
a hundred yojanas all around, without deer and devoid of birds.
In that uninhabited forest, intending to practice supreme austerity,

children.text: aham ākramituṃ saumya tad araṇyam upāgamam ||
children.translated_text: I came, gentle one, to enter that forest.

children.text: tasya rūpam araṇyasya nirdeṣṭuṃ na śaśāka ha
children.translated_text: He could not fully describe the appearance of that forest,
with pleasant-tasting fruits and roots and with trees of many forms.

children.text: tasyāraṇyasya madhye tu saro yojanam āyatam
children.translated_text: But in the middle of that forest there was a lake a yojana long,
covered with lotuses and blue water lilies, with moss grown beyond measure.
It was utterly like a wonder, unsurpassed in pleasant savor,
free from dust, unshaken, and filled with splendid flocks of birds.

children.text: tasmin saraḥsamīpe tu mahad adbhutam āśramam
children.translated_text: Near that lake there was a great and wondrous hermitage,
ancient and exceedingly holy, but devoid of ascetics.
There I spent a summer night, bull among men,
and in the morning, rising at daybreak, I approached that lake.

children.text: athāpaśyaṃ śavaṃ tatra supuṣṭam ajaraṃ kvacit
children.translated_text: Then there I saw a corpse somewhere, well-nourished and undecayed,
standing in that body of water with supreme beauty, O king.

children.text: tam arthaṃ cintayāno 'haṃ muhūrtaṃ tatra rāghava
children.translated_text: Thinking about that matter for a moment there, O <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: viṣṭhito 'smi sarastīre kiṃ nvidaṃ syād iti prabho ||
children.translated_text: I stood on the bank of the lake, wondering, 'What could this be, lord?'
Then after a moment I saw something divine and wonderful to behold:
a supremely noble aerial car, yoked with swans and swift as the mind.
There in the aerial car, O delight of the <s>Raghu</s>s, was an exceedingly heavenly being,
attended, O hero, by a thousand apsarases adorned with divine ornaments.
Some sang lovely songs, and others played instruments.

children.text: paśyato me tadā rāma vimānād avaruhya ca
children.translated_text: While I was watching, O <s>Rāma</s>, that heavenly one descended from the aerial car

children.text: taṃ śavaṃ bhakṣayāmāsa sa svargī raghunandana ||
children.translated_text: and ate that corpse, O delight of the <s>Raghu</s>s.

children.text: tato bhuktvā yathākāmaṃ māṃsaṃ bahu ca suṣṭhu ca
children.translated_text: Then, after eating as much as he wished, a great quantity of flesh and very well,
the heavenly one descended into the lake and began to wash himself.
Having sipped water according to rule, O bull among men, that heavenly one
began to mount the excellent aerial car."

children.text: tam ahaṃ devasaṃkāśam ārohantam udīkṣya vai
children.translated_text: Having seen that godlike one ascending,

children.text: athāham abruvaṃ vākyaṃ tam eva puruṣarṣabha ||
children.translated_text: I then spoke these words to that very man, O bull among men:
"Who are you, godlike one? And this food is blameworthy;

children.text: tvayāyaṃ bhujyate saumya kimarthaṃ vaktum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: why is it being eaten by you, gentle sir? You ought to tell me."
"Such a condition is wondrous: radiant and honored by the gods,

children.text: āhāro garhitaḥ saumya śrotum icchāmi tattvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: yet the food is blameworthy, gentle sir. I wish to hear the truth."

children.text: śrutvā tu bhāṣitaṃ vākyaṃ mama rāma śubhākṣaram
children.translated_text: Having heard my well-spoken words, O <s>Rāma</s>,
that heavenly one, with joined palms, replied as follows, O <s>Raghunandana</s>:
"Hear, O brahman, exactly how this matter of my happiness and misery occurred,

children.text: duratikramaṇīyaṃ hi yathā pṛcchasi māṃ dvija ||
children.translated_text: for what you ask me about, O twice-born one, is hard to overcome.

children.text: purā vaidarbhako rājā pitā mama mahāyaśāḥ
children.translated_text: Long ago there was a king of Vidarbha, my father, greatly renowned,
known as <s>Sudeva</s>, mighty in the three worlds.

children.text: tasya putradvayaṃ brahman dvābhyāṃ strībhyām ajāyata
children.translated_text: To him, O brahman, two sons were born from two wives;

children.text: ahaṃ śveta iti khyāto yavīyān suratho 'bhavat ||
children.translated_text: I was known as <s>Śveta</s>, and the younger was <s>Suratha</s>.

children.text: tataḥ pitari svaryāte paurā mām abhyaṣecayan
children.translated_text: Then, when my father had gone to heaven, the citizens consecrated me,
and there I ruled the kingdom according to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), fully composed.
Thus thousands of years passed, O you of good vows,

children.text: rājyaṃ kārayato brahman prajā dharmeṇa rakṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: while I governed the kingdom, O brahman, protecting the people according to <s>dharma</s>.
Then, from some sign, O best of the twice-born, I understood my lifespan,

children.text: kāladharmaṃ hṛdi nyasya tato vanam upāgamam ||
children.translated_text: set the law of time in my heart, and went to the forest.
I entered this difficult forest, devoid of animals and birds,
near this beautiful lake, in order to practice <s>tapas</s> (austerity).
After consecrating my brother <s>Suratha</s> as king in the realm,

children.text: idaṃ saraḥ samāsādya tapastaptaṃ mayā ciram ||
children.translated_text: I came to this lake and practiced <s>tapas</s> for a long time.
For three thousand years, O great sage,
having practiced exceedingly difficult <s>tapas</s>, I attained unsurpassed <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: tato māṃ svargasaṃsthaṃ vai kṣutpipāse dvijottama
children.translated_text: Then, while I was established in heaven, O best of the twice-born, hunger and thirst
afflicted me, most noble one, and so my senses were distressed.
Going to <s>Pitāmaha</s>, the foremost of the three worlds, I said:
'Lord, this <s>Brahmaloka</s> is free from hunger and thirst.
As I am under the power of hunger and thirst, from what deed has this result come?

children.text: āhāraḥ kaśca me deva tanme brūhi pitāmaha ||
children.translated_text: And what is my food, O god? Tell me that, <s>Pitāmaha</s>.'
Then <s>Pitāmaha</s> said to me, 'O son of <s>Sudeva</s>, your food

children.text: svādūni svāni māṃsāni tāni bhakṣaya nityaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is your own tasty flesh; eat that constantly.

children.text: svaśarīraṃ tvayā puṣṭaṃ kurvatā tapa uttamam
children.translated_text: Your own body was nourished by you while performing excellent <s>tapas</s>;
what has not been sown never grows, O <s>Śveta</s>, O wise one.

children.text: dattaṃ na te 'sti sūkṣmo 'pi vane sattvaniṣevite
children.translated_text: Not even the slightest gift has been given by you in the forest frequented by beings;
therefore, child, though gone to heaven, you are afflicted by hunger and thirst.
