children.text: sa tvaṃ supuṣṭam āhāraiḥ svaśarīram anuttamam
children.translated_text: So eat your own unsurpassed body, well nourished with foods;
it has the taste of nectar, and that will be your satisfaction.

children.text: yadā tu tad vanaṃ śveta agastyaḥ sumahān ṛṣiḥ
children.translated_text: But when that forest, O <s>Śveta</s>, is entered by the very great sage
<s>Agastya</s>, hard to withstand, then you will be freed from this hardship.

children.text: sa hi tārayituṃ saumya śaktaḥ suragaṇān api
children.translated_text: For he, gentle sir, is able to rescue even the hosts of the gods;
how much more you, mighty-armed one, who have fallen under the power of hunger and thirst.'
Having heard the decision of the blessed lord, the god of gods,
I perform this blameworthy feeding on my own body, O best of the twice-born.

children.text: bahūn varṣagaṇān brahman bhujyamānam idaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: For many groups of years, O brahman, though this body has been eaten by me,
it does not diminish, O brahmarṣi, and my satisfaction too is supreme.

children.text: tasya me kṛcchrabhūtasya kṛcchrād asmād vimokṣaya
children.translated_text: Therefore free me, who am reduced to distress, from this distress,

children.text: anyeṣām agatir hyatra kumbhayonim ṛte dvijam ||
children.translated_text: for here there is no refuge in another except the twice-born <s>Kumbhayoni</s>.
This ornament, gentle sir, O best of the twice-born, is for my rescue;
accept it, O brahmarṣi. You ought to show me favor."
Hearing the words of that heavenly one, filled with sorrow,
I accepted that excellent ornament for his rescue.

children.text: mayā pratigṛhīte tu tasminn ābharaṇe śubhe
children.translated_text: And when that splendid ornament had been accepted by me,

children.text: mānuṣaḥ pūrvako deho rājarṣeḥ sa nanāśa ha ||
children.translated_text: the former human body of that royal sage vanished.

children.text: pranaṣṭe tu śarīre 'sau rājarṣiḥ parayā mudā
children.translated_text: When the body had disappeared, that royal sage, with great joy,

children.text: tṛptaḥ pramudito rājā jagāma tridivaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: satisfied and delighted, the king went again to the third heaven.
For that reason this divine ornament, from that one equal to <s>Śakra</s>,
was given to me, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, wondrous to behold."
After hearing that most wondrous speech of <s>Agastya</s>, <s>Rāghava</s>
began, out of respect and amazement, to ask further:

children.text: bhagavaṃstad vanaṃ ghoraṃ tapastapyati yatra saḥ
children.translated_text: "Lord, that terrible forest where he practiced <s>tapas</s>,

children.text: śveto vaidarbhako rājā kathaṃ tad amṛgadvijam ||
children.translated_text: that King <s>Śveta</s> of Vidarbha, how was it without animals and birds?

children.text: niḥsattvaṃ ca vanaṃ jātaṃ śūnyaṃ manujavarjitam
children.translated_text: And how did the forest become lifeless, empty, devoid of human beings,

children.text: tapaścartuṃ praviṣṭaḥ sa śrotum icchāmi tattvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: when he entered it to practice <s>tapas</s>? I wish to hear the truth."
Hearing <s>Rāma</s>'s speech, filled with curiosity,
the exceedingly splendid one began to speak these words:

children.text: purā kṛtayuge rāma manur daṇḍadharaḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: "Formerly, in the Kṛta age, O <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Manu</s>, the powerful bearer of <s>daṇḍa</s> (punitive authority),

children.text: tasya putro mahān āsīd ikṣvākuḥ kulavardhanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: had a great son, <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, increaser of his lineage.

children.text: taṃ putraṃ pūrvake rājye nikṣipya bhuvi durjayam
children.translated_text: Installing that unconquerable son in the ancestral kingdom on earth,
he said, 'Be the founder of royal lineages upon the earth.'

children.text: tatheti ca pratijñātaṃ pituḥ putreṇa rāghava
children.translated_text: 'So be it,' the son promised his father, O <s>Rāghava</s>;

children.text: tataḥ paramasaṃhṛṣṭo manuḥ punar uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: then <s>Manu</s>, greatly delighted, spoke again:
'I am pleased, most noble one; you will indeed be the doer, without doubt.

children.text: daṇḍena ca prajā rakṣa mā ca daṇḍam akāraṇe ||
children.translated_text: Protect the subjects with <s>daṇḍa</s> (punishment), but do not apply <s>daṇḍa</s> without cause.'"

children.text: aparādhiṣu yo daṇḍaḥ pātyate mānaveṣu vai
children.translated_text: The punishment that is indeed inflicted upon offending men,

children.text: sa daṇḍo vidhivanmuktaḥ svargaṃ nayati pārthivam ||
children.translated_text: that punishment, released according to rule, leads the king to heaven.

children.text: tasmād daṇḍe mahābāho yatnavān bhava putraka
children.translated_text: Therefore, O mighty-armed son, be diligent in punishment;

children.text: dharmo hi paramo loke kurvataste bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: for <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) will be supreme in the world for you as you act.

children.text: iti taṃ bahu saṃdiśya manuḥ putraṃ samādhinā
children.translated_text: Having thus instructed his son at length and with concentration, <s>Manu</s>
went joyfully to the third heaven, to the unsurpassed world of <s>Brahmā</s>.
When he had gone to heaven, the boundlessly radiant <s>Ikṣvāku</s>
became absorbed in thought: "How shall I beget sons?"
Through many kinds of rites, each in its proper form, that son of <s>Manu</s>,
righteous-souled, begot a hundred sons like sons of the gods.
The youngest of them all, dear one, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>,
was foolish and untrained in proper conduct, and he would not serve his elder brothers.

children.text: nāma tasya ca daṇḍeti pitā cakre 'lpatejasaḥ
children.translated_text: His father gave that weak-spirited one the name <s>Daṇḍa</s>,
saying, "Punishment must surely fall upon his body."

children.text: sa paśyamānastaṃ doṣaṃ ghoraṃ putrasya rāghava
children.translated_text: Seeing that terrible fault in his son, O <s>Rāghava</s>,
the subduer of foes gave him a kingdom between <s>Vindhya</s> and <s>Śaivala</s>.
There <s>Daṇḍa</s> became king on that lovely mountain slope,
and, O <s>Rāma</s>, he founded an incomparable and unsurpassed city.
He gave the city the name <s>Madhumanta</s>, O lord,
and chose the well-vowed <s>Uśanas</s> as his purohita (royal priest).

children.text: evaṃ sa rājā tad rājyaṃ kārayat sapurohitaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus that king, together with his purohita, governed that kingdom,
crowded with delighted people, like the kingdom of the king of the gods in heaven.
After telling this to <s>Rāma</s>, the great sage <s>Kumbhasaṃbhava</s>
began another statement within this very story.
Then, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, that <s>Daṇḍa</s>, for many thousands of years,
ruled there, dull-souled though he was, with all thorns removed.

children.text: atha kāle tu kasmiṃścid rājā bhārgavam āśramam
children.translated_text: Then at a certain time the king approached the hermitage of <s>Bhārgava</s>,
which was delightful, in the charming month of <s>Caitra</s>.
There <s>Daṇḍa</s> saw <s>Bhārgava</s>'s daughter, unsurpassed on earth in beauty,
wandering in a part of the forest, peerless.
On seeing her, that very foolish man, pierced by the arrows of <s>Anaṅga</s>,
approached in great agitation and spoke these words to the maiden:

children.text: kutastvam asi suśroṇi kasya vāsi sutā śubhe
children.translated_text: "Where are you from, fair-hipped one? Whose daughter are you, auspicious one?
I am tormented by <s>Anaṅga</s>; I ask you, slender-waisted one."
To him, speaking in this way, crazed by delusion and desire,
the <s>Bhārgava</s> maiden replied with these conciliatory words to the king:
"Know me, O king of kings, as the daughter of <s>Bhārgava</s>, the divine one of unwearied deeds,
named <s>Arajā</s>, his eldest daughter, dwelling in the hermitage.

children.text: guruḥ pitā me rājendra tvaṃ ca śiṣyo mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: My father is your guru, O king of kings, and you are the disciple of that great-souled one.

children.text: vyasanaṃ sumahat kruddhaḥ sa te dadyānmahātapāḥ ||
children.translated_text: If angered, that great ascetic would bring a very great calamity upon you.

children.text: yadi vātra mayā kāryaṃ dharmadṛṣṭena satpathā
children.translated_text: But if anything is to be done with me here by a righteous and proper path,

children.text: varayasva nṛpa śreṣṭha pitaraṃ me mahādyutim ||
children.translated_text: then, best of kings, ask my greatly radiant father for me.

children.text: anyathā tu phalaṃ tubhyaṃ bhaved ghorābhisaṃhitam
children.translated_text: Otherwise the result for you would be directed toward something dreadful;

children.text: krodhena hi pitā me 'sau trailokyam api nirdahet ||
children.translated_text: for in anger that father of mine could burn even the three worlds."
To <s>Arajā</s>, who was speaking thus, <s>Daṇḍa</s>, afflicted by the arrows of desire,
answered, drunk with passion, placing his joined palms upon his head:

children.text: prasādaṃ kuru suśroṇi na kālaṃ kṣeptum arhasi
children.translated_text: "Show favor, fair-hipped one; you should not let time pass.

children.text: tvatkṛte hi mama prāṇā vidīryante śubhānane ||
children.translated_text: For on account of you my vital breaths are splitting apart, fair-faced one.

children.text: tvāṃ prāpya hi vadho vāpi pāpaṃ vāpi sudāruṇam
children.translated_text: Having obtained you, whether death or even a most terrible sin should come,

children.text: bhaktaṃ bhajasva māṃ bhīru bhajamānaṃ suvihvalam ||
children.translated_text: love me, your devoted servant, timid one, as I love you, utterly distraught."

children.text: evam uktvā tu tāṃ kanyāṃ dorbhyāṃ gṛhya balād balī
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to the maiden, the strong man seized her forcibly with both arms,
and, as she struggled, he proceeded as he desired to intercourse.

children.text: tam anarthaṃ mahāghoraṃ daṇḍaḥ kṛtvā sudāruṇam
children.translated_text: After <s>Daṇḍa</s> had committed that terrible, utterly dreadful outrage,
he quickly went to the unsurpassed city <s>Madhumanta</s>.
But <s>Arajā</s>, weeping and very frightened,
waited not far from the hermitage for her godlike father.
After a short while, having heard of it, the godlike sage of boundless radiance,
hungry and surrounded by disciples, returned to his own hermitage.
He saw poor <s>Arajā</s>, covered with dust,
like moonlight overwhelmed by the red dawn at daybreak, no longer shining.
His anger arose, especially because he was hungry,

children.text: nirdahann iva lokāṃstrīñ śiṣyāṃścedam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: and, as though burning the three worlds, he said this to his disciples:
"Behold the ruin of perverse <s>Daṇḍa</s>, who does not know himself,
terrible in appearance, like an enraged flame of fire.
Destruction has come for this evil-minded, wicked man, together with his followers,

children.text: yaḥ pradīptāṃ hutāśasya śikhāṃ vai spraṣṭum icchati ||
children.translated_text: who wishes to touch the blazing flame of a sacrificial fire.

children.text: yasmāt sa kṛtavān pāpam īdṛśaṃ ghoradarśanam
children.translated_text: Because this foolish man has committed a sin of such dreadful appearance,

children.text: tasmāt prāpsyati durmedhāḥ phalaṃ pāpasya karmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore he shall receive the fruit of his sinful act.
Within seven nights that king, along with his servants, army, and vehicles,
that evil-minded man whose conduct is sinful, shall meet destruction.
And all around, for a hundred yojanas, the territory of that foolish man
<s>Pākaśāsana</s> will burn with a great rain of dust.
All living beings here, both stationary and moving,
will be utterly destroyed by the great rain of dust.
As far as <s>Daṇḍa</s>'s territory extends, to that extent every raised thing
will after seven nights become as if made of dust, unseen."
Having spoken thus, heated with anger, he said to those hermitage-dwelling
people, "Stay at the borders of the country."

children.text: śrutvā tūśanaso vākyaṃ sa āśramāvasatho janaḥ
children.translated_text: But hearing the words of <s>Ūśanas</s>, that community living in the hermitage

children.text: niṣkrānto viṣayāt tasya sthānaṃ cakre 'tha bāhyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: went out from his realm and then made its dwelling outside.

children.text: sa tathoktvā munijanam arajām idam abravīt
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to the ascetic folk, he said this to <s>Arajā</s>:
"Dull-minded one, remain right here in the hermitage, fully composed.
This lake, extending for a yojana and shining with beautiful splendor,
enjoy here, <s>Arajā</s>, free from fever; and let the appointed time be awaited here.

children.text: tvatsamīpe tu ye sattvā vāsam eṣyanti tāṃ niśām
children.translated_text: But whatever beings come to dwell near you on that night
will forever become immune to the shower of dust."
Having spoken thus, the <s>Bhārgava</s> began to take up residence elsewhere.
After seven days, as had been stated by the speaker of <s>brahman</s>, it had become reduced to ashes.
That territory of <s>Daṇḍa</s>, on the slopes of the <s>Vindhya</s> and <s>Śaivala</s> mountains,

children.text: śapto brahmarṣiṇā tena purā vaidharmake kṛte ||
children.translated_text: was cursed by that brahmarṣi in ancient times because an unrighteous act had been done.
From then onward, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, it is called <s>Daṇḍakāraṇya</s>;
and where ascetics settled, it then became known as <s>Janasthāna</s>.

children.text: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yanmāṃ pṛcchasi rāghava
children.translated_text: All this has been told to you, O <s>Rāghava</s>, what you asked me about.
The time for attending to the twilight rite, hero, is now passing by.
All these great seers on every side, with full water jars,
having performed the water rite, O tiger among men, are worshiping the sun.

children.text: sa tair ṛṣibhir abhyastaḥ sahitair brahmasattamaiḥ
children.translated_text: Practiced by those assembled seers, the foremost knowers of <s>brahman</s>,

children.text: ravir astaṃ gato rāma gacchodakam upaspṛśa ||
children.translated_text: the sun has set, O <s>Rāma</s>; go, sip the water for purification."

children.text: ṛṣer vacanam ājñāya rāmaḥ saṃdhyām upāsitum
children.translated_text: Accepting the seer's command, <s>Rāma</s> began to attend to the twilight rite,
approaching the holy lake frequented by apsarases.
There, having sipped the water and performed the western twilight observance,
<s>Rāma</s> entered the hermitage of the great-souled <s>Kumbhayoni</s>.
For him <s>Agastya</s> prepared abundant fruits and roots, as well as medicinal herbs,
and pure vegetables for his meal.
That best of men ate that food, which was like nectar,
and, delighted and fully satisfied, spent that night there.
At daybreak in the morning, rising and performing his daily rites, the subduer of foes,
the best of the <s>Raghu</s>s, approached the seer in order to depart.
Having saluted him, <s>Rāma</s> said to the great seer born from the jar:

children.text: āpṛcche tvāṃ gamiṣyāmi mām anujñātum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: "I ask your leave; I shall go. You should permit me.
I am blessed; I have been favored by the sight of the great-souled one.
And I shall come here again to see you, for the purification of myself."
When <s>Kākutstha</s> was speaking that wondrously pleasing speech,
the wealth of austerity, the guide of <s>dharma</s>, being supremely pleased, said:

children.text: atyadbhutam idaṃ vākyaṃ tava rāma śubhākṣaram
children.translated_text: "This speech of yours, O <s>Rāma</s>, with auspicious syllables, is most wondrous.
You yourself are the purifier of all worlds, O delight of the <s>Raghu</s>s.

children.text: muhūrtam api rāma tvāṃ ye nu paśyanti kecana
children.translated_text: Whoever sees you, O <s>Rāma</s>, even for a moment,
is purified, becomes as one fit for heaven, and is honored in heaven by the gods.

children.text: ye ca tvāṃ ghoracakṣurbhir īkṣante prāṇino bhuvi
children.translated_text: And those creatures on earth who look upon you with terrible eyes
are struck down by <s>Yama</s>'s rod and at once go to hell.
Go unharmed and undisturbed along a road free from fear on every side.

children.text: praśādhi rājyaṃ dharmeṇa gatir hi jagato bhavān ||
children.translated_text: Rule the kingdom with <s>dharma</s>; for you are the course and refuge of the world."

children.text: evam uktastu muninā prāñjaliḥ pragraho nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the sage, the wise king, with joined palms and self-control,
bowed down to that seer of meritorious conduct.
Having saluted the best of sages and all those wealthy in austerity,
he calmly mounted the <s>Puṣpaka</s>, adorned with gold.
As he was departing, the groups of sages, with blessings on every side,
honored him, who was like <s>Mahendra</s>, as the immortals honor the thousand-eyed one.

children.text: svasthaḥ sa dadṛśe rāmaḥ puṣpake hemabhūṣite
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, at ease in the gold-adorned <s>Puṣpaka</s>, appeared
like the moon standing near a cloud at the coming of the rainy season.
Then, when half the day had arrived, being honored on every side,
<s>Kākutstha</s> reached <s>Ayodhyā</s> and descended from the aerial car.
Then, after dismissing the beautiful <s>Puṣpaka</s>, which went wherever one wished,
<s>Rāma</s> spoke these words to the doorkeeper stationed in the inner court:

children.text: lakṣmaṇaṃ bharataṃ caiva gatvā tau laghuvikramau
children.translated_text: "Go to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and <s>Bharata</s>, those two of swift valor,

children.text: mamāgamanam ākhyāya śabdāpaya ca māṃ ciram ||
children.translated_text: announce my arrival, and quickly summon them to me."
Hearing that speech of <s>Rāma</s>, whose deeds are effortless,
the doorkeeper summoned the princes and reported it to <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tu rāghavaḥ prāptau priyau bharatalakṣmaṇau
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāghava</s> saw his dear <s>Bharata</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> arrived,

children.text: pariṣvajya tato rāmo vākyam etad uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> embraced them and then spoke this statement:
"I have done, exactly as it should be done, the unsurpassed task of the twice-born man.
Further, O <s>Rāghava</s>s, I wish to perform the making of a bridge of <s>dharma</s>.
Together with you two, who are like my very self, I wish to sacrifice

children.text: sahito yaṣṭum icchāmi tatra dharmo hi śāśvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: with the unsurpassed <s>rājasūya</s>; for in that there is eternal <s>dharma</s>.
After sacrificing with the <s>rājasūya</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, the destroyer of enemies,
through that well-offered and well-performed sacrifice attained the state of <s>Varuṇa</s>.
And <s>Soma</s>, knower of <s>dharma</s>, having sacrificed with the <s>rājasūya</s> according to <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: prāptaśca sarvalokānāṃ kīrtiṃ sthānaṃ ca śāśvatam ||
children.translated_text: attained fame among all worlds and an eternal station.
What is best on this day, consider that together with me.

children.text: hitaṃ cāyatiyuktaṃ ca prayatau vaktum arhathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Being composed, you should speak what is beneficial and joined with future welfare."
But hearing this speech of <s>Rāghava</s>, the skilled speaker

children.text: bharataḥ prāñjalir bhūtvā vākyam etad uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s>, with joined palms, spoke this statement.

children.text: tvayi dharmaḥ paraḥ sādho tvayi sarvā vasuṃdharā
children.translated_text: In you, O righteous good man, the highest <s>dharma</s> abides; in you the whole earth
is established, O mighty-armed one, and so is fame, O hero of immeasurable valor.
All the protectors of the earth, great-souled as they are, look to you as the immortals look to <s>Prajāpati</s>,
as to the lord of the world, just as we do.

children.text: prajāśca pitṛvad rājan paśyanti tvāṃ mahābala
children.translated_text: The subjects, O king, O mighty one, look upon you as upon a father;
on earth you have become the refuge even of living beings, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: sa tvam evaṃvidhaṃ yajñam āhartāsi kathaṃ nṛpa
children.translated_text: How then, O king, can you undertake such a sacrifice,
in which the destruction of the royal lineages on earth is seen?

children.text: pṛthivyāṃ ye ca puruṣā rājan pauruṣam āgatāḥ
children.translated_text: And whatever men on earth, O king, have attained manly prowess,
there the destruction of them all will come, like the ender of all things.
Therefore you, tiger among men, of unequaled valor through your virtues,

children.text: pṛthivīṃ nārhase hantuṃ vaśe hi tava vartate ||
children.translated_text: ought not to destroy the earth, for it is under your control.

children.text: bharatasya tu tad vākyaṃ śrutvāmṛtamayaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech of <s>Bharata</s>, as if made of nectar,
<s>Rāma</s>, whose valor was true, obtained incomparable joy.

children.text: uvāca ca śubhāṃ vāṇīṃ kaikeyyā nandivardhanam
children.translated_text: And he spoke these auspicious words to the increaser of <s>Kaikeyī</s>'s delight:
'I am pleased; I am fully satisfied today by your speech.
This manly statement, intent on <s>dharma</s>,
has been uttered by you, tiger among men, for the protection of the earth.
Therefore, because of that intention, from the rājasūya, the best of sacrifices,
I turn back, O knower of <s>dharma</s>, through your well-spoken word.

children.text: prajānāṃ pālanaṃ dharmo rājñāṃ yajñena saṃmitaḥ
children.translated_text: The guarding of subjects is the <s>dharma</s> of kings, equal in worth to sacrifice;
therefore I heed your speech, well said and well considered.'

children.text: tathoktavati rāme tu bharate ca mahātmani
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāma</s> had spoken thus, and great-souled <s>Bharata</s> also,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> too spoke auspicious words to the delight of the <s>Raghus</s>.
'The aśvamedha is a great sacrifice, purifier of all sins;
let that purifier, hard to withstand, the foremost of sacrifices, please you.
For an ancient event is heard concerning the very great-souled <s>Vāsava</s>:
<s>Śakra</s>, covered by the sin of brahmahatyā, was purified by the horse sacrifice.
Formerly, mighty-armed one, in a meeting of gods and asuras,

children.text: vṛtro nāma mahān āsīd daiteyo lokasaṃmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: there was a great Daitya named <s>Vṛtra</s>, honored by the world.
He extended for a hundred yojanas, and rose three times as high as that;
with affection and love he looked upon the three worlds everywhere.
He knew <s>dharma</s>, was grateful, and was fully settled in understanding;
well composed, he ruled the whole earth according to <s>dharma</s>.
While he was ruling then, the earth yielded every desired thing;

children.text: rasavanti prasūtāni mūlāni ca phalāni ca ||
children.translated_text: juicy produce was born, roots and fruits as well.
For that great-souled one, the earth ripened crops without ploughing and was richly endowed;

children.text: sa rājyaṃ tādṛśaṃ bhuṅkte sphītam adbhutadarśanam ||
children.translated_text: he enjoyed such a flourishing kingdom, wondrous to behold.

children.text: tasya buddhiḥ samutpannā tapaḥ kuryām anuttamam
children.translated_text: Then the thought arose in him: "I should perform unsurpassed <s>tapas</s> (austerity);

children.text: tapo hi paramaṃ śreyastapo hi paramaṃ sukham ||
children.translated_text: for <s>tapas</s> is the highest good, and <s>tapas</s> is the highest happiness."

children.text: sa nikṣipya sutaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ paureṣu parameśvaram
children.translated_text: Placing his eldest son among the citizens as supreme ruler,
he undertook fierce <s>tapas</s>, heating all the gods.
But while <s>Vṛtra</s> was practicing <s>tapas</s>, <s>Vāsava</s>, deeply distressed,

children.text: viṣṇuṃ samupasaṃkramya vākyam etad uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: approached <s>Viṣṇu</s> and spoke these words:
"The worlds have been conquered by mighty-armed <s>Vṛtra</s> as he practices <s>tapas</s>;

children.text: balavān sa hi dharmātmā nainaṃ śakṣyāmi bādhitum ||
children.translated_text: for he is powerful and righteous, and I will not be able to oppress him.

children.text: yadyasau tapa ātiṣṭhed bhūya eva sureśvara
children.translated_text: If he should undertake <s>tapas</s> still further, O lord of the gods,
as long as the worlds endure, so long will they follow his will.
And you, O greatly powerful one, disregard this supremely noble being;

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ hi na bhaved vṛtraḥ kruddhe tvayi sureśvara ||
children.translated_text: if you were angered, O lord of the gods, <s>Vṛtra</s> would not last a moment.

children.text: yadā hi prītisaṃyogaṃ tvayā viṣṇo samāgataḥ
children.translated_text: For when he came into a bond of affection with you, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
from that time onward he gained lordship over the worlds.

children.text: sa tvaṃ prasādaṃ lokānāṃ kuruṣva sumahāyaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore show favor to the worlds, O greatly renowned one;

children.text: tvatkṛtena hi sarvaṃ syāt praśāntam ajaraṃ jagat ||
children.translated_text: for through your act this whole ageless world would become peaceful.

children.text: ime hi sarve viṣṇo tvāṃ nirīkṣante divaukasaḥ
children.translated_text: All these dwellers in heaven, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, are looking to you;

children.text: vṛtraghātena mahatā eṣāṃ sāhyaṃ kuruṣva ha ||
children.translated_text: with the great slaying of <s>Vṛtra</s>, give them help.

children.text: tvayā hi nityaśaḥ sāhyaṃ kṛtam eṣāṃ mahātmanām
children.translated_text: For you have always given help to these great-souled ones;

children.text: asahyam idam anyeṣām agatīnāṃ gatir bhavān ||
children.translated_text: this burden is unbearable for others. You are the refuge of those without refuge."

children.text: lakṣmaṇasya tu tad vākyaṃ śrutvā śatrunibarhaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the destroyer of enemies
said to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, "Tell the slaying of <s>Vṛtra</s> in full."
Thus addressed by <s>Rāghava</s>, the increaser of <s>Sumitrā</s>'s joy,

children.text: bhūya eva kathāṃ divyāṃ kathayāmāsa lakṣmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> again related the divine tale.
Hearing the words of the thousand-eyed one and of all the dwellers in heaven,
<s>Viṣṇu</s> spoke this to all the gods, with <s>Indra</s> at their head:
"Previously I was bound by friendship with the very great-souled <s>Vṛtra</s>;

children.text: tena yuṣmatpriyārthaṃ vai nāhaṃ hanmi mahāsuram ||
children.translated_text: therefore, even for the sake of your welfare, I will not kill the great asura.

children.text: avaśyaṃ karaṇīyaṃ ca bhavatāṃ sukham uttamam
children.translated_text: Yet your highest happiness must certainly be brought about;

children.text: tasmād upāyam ākhyāsye yena vṛtraṃ haniṣyatha ||
children.translated_text: therefore I shall tell you the means by which you will slay <s>Vṛtra</s>.
I shall make myself threefold, O best of gods;

children.text: tena vṛtraṃ sahasrākṣo haniṣyati na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by that, the thousand-eyed one will slay <s>Vṛtra</s>, without doubt.

children.text: eko 'ṃśo vāsavaṃ yātu dvitīyo vajram eva tu
children.translated_text: Let one portion go to <s>Vāsava</s>, the second to the thunderbolt itself,
and the third to the earth; then <s>Śakra</s> will slay <s>Vṛtra</s>."

children.text: tathā bruvati deveśe devā vākyam athābruvan
children.translated_text: When the lord of gods had spoken thus, the gods then said these words:

children.text: evam etanna saṃdeho yathā vadasi daityahan ||
children.translated_text: "So it is, without doubt, just as you say, O slayer of Daityas.
May there be welfare for you. We shall go, desiring the killing of the asura <s>Vṛtra</s>;
O supremely noble one, enter <s>Vāsava</s> with your own splendor."
Then all those great-souled ones, with the thousand-eyed one at their head,

children.text: tad araṇyam upākrāman yatra vṛtro mahāsuraḥ ||
children.translated_text: They entered that forest where the great asura <s>Vṛtra</s> was.
They saw the best of asuras, blazing with splendor,
as if drinking up the three worlds, as if burning the sky.
At the mere sight of that foremost asura, the gods were seized by terror.

children.text: katham enaṃ vadhiṣyāmaḥ kathaṃ na syāt parājayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "How shall we kill him? How can there be no defeat for us?"
While they were considering this there, the thousand-eyed <s>Puraṃdara</s>
grasped the thunderbolt in both arms and hurled it at <s>Vṛtra</s>'s head.
Like the fire of time, terrible and blazing with great flame,
when it struck <s>Vṛtra</s>'s head, the whole world fell into terror.
The glorious lord of the gods, pondering that impossible killing
of <s>Vṛtra</s>, quickly went to the end of the world.
As <s>Indra</s> went away, <s>Brahmahatyā</s> (the sin of brahmin-murder) at once followed him,

children.text: apataccāsya gātreṣu tam indraṃ duḥkham āviśat ||
children.translated_text: and it fell upon his limbs; suffering entered that <s>Indra</s>.
With their enemy slain but with <s>Indra</s> lost, the gods, led by <s>Agni</s>,
again and again worshiped <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the best of the three worlds.

children.text: tvaṃ gatiḥ paramā deva pūrvajo jagataḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: "You are the supreme refuge, O god, the first-born, lord of the world.
For the protection of all beings you have assumed the state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: hataścāyaṃ tvayā vṛtro brahmahatyā ca vāsavam
children.translated_text: This <s>Vṛtra</s> has been slain by you, and <s>Brahmahatyā</s> afflicts <s>Vāsava</s>,
O tiger among gods; declare the means of release for him."

children.text: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā devānāṃ viṣṇur abravīt
children.translated_text: Hearing those words of the gods, <s>Viṣṇu</s> said:

children.text: mām eva yajatāṃ śakraḥ pāvayiṣyāmi vajriṇam ||
children.translated_text: "Let <s>Śakra</s> sacrifice to me alone; I shall purify the wielder of the thunderbolt.
Having worshiped me with the meritorious <s>hayamedha</s> (horse sacrifice), <s>Pākaśāsana</s>
will again attain the rank of <s>Indra</s> among the gods, free from fear on every side."

children.text: evaṃ saṃdiśya devānāṃ tāṃ vāṇīm amṛtopamām
children.translated_text: Having thus instructed the gods with that nectar-like speech,
the lordly god <s>Viṣṇu</s>, praised by them, went to heaven.

children.text: tathā vṛtravadhaṃ sarvam akhilena sa lakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, having related in full the whole slaying of <s>Vṛtra</s>,
that best of men began the remainder of the tale.
Then, when mighty <s>Vṛtra</s>, terror of the gods, had been slain,

children.text: brahmahatyāvṛtaḥ śakraḥ saṃjñāṃ lebhe na vṛtrahā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s>, enveloped by <s>Brahmahatyā</s>, the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, did not regain consciousness.
Taking refuge at the end of the worlds, bereft of consciousness and senseless,
he stayed there for some time, writhing like a serpent.
Then, when the thousand-eyed one had disappeared, the world became distressed.
The earth appeared ruined, sapless, and with its forests dried up.
The clouds had no streams, and so too the lakes and rivers were dry,
and there was disturbance among living beings caused by lack of rain.
As this world was wasting away, the gods, their minds agitated,

children.text: yad uktaṃ viṣṇunā pūrvaṃ taṃ yajñaṃ samupānayan ||
children.translated_text: undertook that sacrifice which <s>Viṣṇu</s> had formerly prescribed.
Then all the hosts of gods, with their preceptors and with the seers,

children.text: taṃ deśaṃ sahitā jagmur yatrendro bhayamohitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: went together to that place where <s>Indra</s> was bewildered by fear.

children.text: te tu dṛṣṭvā sahasrākṣaṃ mohitaṃ brahmahatyayā
children.translated_text: Seeing the thousand-eyed one deluded by <s>Brahmahatyā</s>,
they placed the lord of the gods before them and performed the <s>aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice).
Then the great <s>aśvamedha</s> of great-souled <s>Mahendra</s>
proceeded, O king, for the purpose of purifying him from <s>Brahmahatyā</s>.
Then at the completion of the sacrifice, <s>Brahmahatyā</s> approached

children.text: abhigamyābravīd vākyaṃ kva me sthānaṃ vidhāsyatha ||
children.translated_text: the great-souled one and said these words: "Where will you assign my place?"
Then the gods, satisfied and filled with joy, said to her:
"Divide yourself into four parts by your own power, O hard-to-assail one."
Hearing the words spoken by those great-souled gods,
<s>Brahmahatyā</s>, difficult to dwell with, chose another place in their presence.
"With one part I shall dwell in rivers whose waters are full,

children.text: dvitīyena tu vṛkṣeṣu satyam etad bravīmi vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and with a second in trees; I tell you this truly.
That third part of mine shall dwell among young women
for three nights when they are filled with passion, striking down their pride.

children.text: hantāro brāhmaṇān ye tu prekṣāpūrvam adūṣakān
children.translated_text: And those who knowingly kill innocent brahmins,
I shall take refuge in them with my fourth part, O bulls among gods."

children.text: pratyūcustāṃ tato devā yathā vadasi durvase
children.translated_text: Then the gods answered her: "As you say, O hard-to-dwell-with one,

children.text: tathā bhavatu tat sarvaṃ sādhayasva yathepsitam ||
children.translated_text: so let all that be. Accomplish it as you desire."
Then the gods, filled with gladness, bowed to the thousand-eyed one,
and <s>Vāsava</s> became free from fever and purified of sin.

children.text: praśāntaṃ ca jagat sarvaṃ sahasrākṣe pratiṣṭhite
children.translated_text: And when the thousand-eyed one had been restored, the whole world became calm,
and then <s>Śakra</s> honored that sacrifice, wondrous in appearance.
Such indeed is the power of the <s>aśvamedha</s>, O delight of the <s>Raghu</s> line.
Therefore, O very fortunate king, sacrifice with the <s>hayamedha</s> (horse sacrifice).
Hearing that speech spoken by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the eloquent
greatly radiant <s>Rāghava</s> replied with a smile:
"It is exactly so, O best of men, as you say, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
regarding the slaying of <s>Vṛtra</s> in full and the fruit of the <s>vājimedha</s> (horse sacrifice).

children.text: śrūyate hi purā saumya kardamasya prajāpateḥ
children.translated_text: For it is heard that in ancient times, gentle one, <s>Kardama</s> <s>Prajāpati</s>

children.text: putro bāhlīśvaraḥ śrīmān ilo nāma sudhārmikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: had a splendid, very righteous son, lord of <s>Bāhlī</s>, named <s>Ila</s>.

children.text: sa rājā pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ vaśe kṛtvā mahāyaśāḥ
children.translated_text: That king, having brought the whole earth under his control, O tiger among men,
guarded his kingdom as one would guard a son.
By the supremely noble gods and by the mighty asuras among the daityas,
by nāgas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, and by very great yakṣas,
he was constantly honored, gentle one, O delight of the <s>Raghu</s> line, by those afflicted with fear,
and the three worlds feared that great-souled one when he was angry.

children.text: sa rājā tādṛśo hyāsīd dharme vīrye ca niṣṭhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Such indeed was that king, established in <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) and valor."
and in wisdom he was supremely noble, the greatly renowned lord of the <s>Bāhlīka</s>s.

children.text: sa pracakre mahābāhur mṛgayāṃ rucire vane
children.translated_text: That mighty-armed one began a hunt in a lovely forest,
in the delightful month of <s>Caitra</s>, together with his servants, army, and mounts.
That king slew deer in the wilderness by hundreds of thousands,
yet even after killing them, that great-souled king had no satisfaction.
While a myriad of various animals was being slain by that great-souled one,
he approached the region where <s>Mahāsena</s> had been born.
But there <s>Hara</s>, the lord of the gods and god of gods, with the daughter of the mountain-king,
was sporting together with all his irresistible attendants.
The lord of <s>Umā</s>, whose banner bears the bull, had made himself female,
wishing to do what was pleasing to the goddess, there by a mountain cascade.

children.text: ye ca tatra vanoddeśe sattvāḥ puruṣavādinaḥ
children.translated_text: And whatever beings in that forest region were called male,

children.text: yacca kiṃcana tat sarvaṃ nārīsaṃjñaṃ babhūva ha ||
children.translated_text: whatever there was, all of it became designated as female.

children.text: etasminn antare rājā sa ilaḥ kardamātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: Meanwhile that king <s>Ila</s>, son of <s>Kardama</s>,
approached that region while striking down thousands of deer.
Seeing everything made female, including serpents, deer, and birds,
and seeing himself and his followers likewise become female, O delight of the <s>Raghu</s>s,

children.text: tasya duḥkhaṃ mahat tvāsīd dṛṣṭvātmānaṃ tathāgatam
children.translated_text: great grief arose in him when he saw himself in that condition,

children.text: umāpateśca tat karma jñātvā trāsam upāgamat ||
children.translated_text: and, knowing that this was the act of <s>Umāpati</s>, he became terrified.
Then the king, with his servants, army, and mounts,
sought refuge with the great-souled god, the blue-throated, matted-haired one.

children.text: tataḥ prahasya varadaḥ saha devyā mahāyaśāḥ
children.translated_text: Then the boon-giver, greatly renowned, laughing together with the goddess,
himself spoke these words as a boon-giver to the son of <s>Prajāpati</s>:
'Rise, rise, royal sage, mighty son of <s>Kardama</s>.

children.text: puruṣatvam ṛte saumya varaṃ varaya suvrata ||
children.translated_text: Choose a boon, gentle one of good vow, except for manhood.'

children.text: tataḥ sa rājā śokārtāḥ pratyākhyāto mahātmanā
children.translated_text: Then that king, afflicted with grief and refused by the great-souled one,

children.text: na sa jagrāha strībhūto varam anyaṃ surottamāt ||
children.translated_text: being made female, accepted no other boon from the best of gods.
Then the king, in great sorrow, to the daughter of the mountain-king,
bowed down to the great goddess with his whole inner being.

children.text: īśe varāṇāṃ varade lokānām asi bhāmini
children.translated_text: 'You are mistress of boons, boon-giving lady, mistress of the worlds, O beautiful one.

children.text: amoghadarśane devi bhaje saumye namo 'stu te ||
children.translated_text: O goddess whose sight is unfailing, I approach you, gentle one; homage to you.'
Knowing what was in that royal sage's heart in the presence of <s>Hara</s>,

children.text: pratyuvāca śubhaṃ vākyaṃ devī rudrasya saṃmatā ||
children.translated_text: the goddess, approved by <s>Rudra</s>, replied with auspicious words:

children.text: ardhasya devo varado varārdhasya tathā hyaham
children.translated_text: 'The god is the giver of half the boon, and I likewise of the other half of the boon.

children.text: tasmād ardhaṃ gṛhāṇa tvaṃ strīpuṃsor yāvad icchasi ||
children.translated_text: Therefore take half, as much as you desire, of female and male states.'

children.text: tad adbhutatamaṃ śrutvā devyā varam anuttamam
children.translated_text: Hearing that most wonderful, unsurpassed boon from the goddess,
the king became delighted in mind and then spoke these words:

children.text: yadi devi prasannā me rūpeṇāpratimā bhuvi
children.translated_text: 'If, O goddess, you are gracious to me, you whose form is unequaled on earth,

children.text: māsaṃ strītvam upāsitvā māsaṃ syāṃ puruṣaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: after dwelling for a month in womanhood, may I again be a man for a month.'
Knowing his wish, the goddess of lovely face

children.text: pratyuvāca śubhaṃ vākyam evam etad bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: replied with auspicious words: 'So shall it be.'
'O king, when you have become male, you will not remember the female state,
and when you have become female for the following month, you will not remember manhood.'

children.text: evaṃ sa rājā puruṣo māsaṃ bhūtvātha kārdamiḥ
children.translated_text: Thus that king, <s>Kārdami</s>, after being a man for a month,
became <s>Ilā</s>, a woman beautiful in the three worlds, for one month.
Hearing that story connected with <s>Ila</s>, told by <s>Rāma</s>,
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and <s>Bharata</s> were filled with the highest wonder.

children.text: tau rāmaṃ prāñjalībhūtvā tasya rājño mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, with joined palms, the two asked <s>Rāma</s> again

children.text: vistaraṃ tasya bhāvasya tadā papracchatuḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: about the full extent of that condition of that great-souled king:

children.text: kathaṃ sa rājā strībhūto vartayāmāsa durgatim
children.translated_text: 'How did that king, having become a woman, endure that misfortune?

children.text: puruṣo vā yadā bhūtaḥ kāṃ vṛttiṃ vartayatyasau ||
children.translated_text: Or when he became a man, what mode of life did he follow?'
Hearing that speech of theirs, filled with curiosity,
<s>Kākutstha</s> related what happened to that king.

children.text: tam eva prathamaṃ māsaṃ strībhūtvā lokasundarī
children.translated_text: In that very first month, having become a woman beautiful to the world,

children.text: tābhiḥ parivṛtā strībhir ye 'sya pūrvaṃ padānugāḥ ||
children.translated_text: surrounded by those women who had formerly been his attendants,
that beauty of the world quickly entered that forest and sported there,
walking with her feet through trees, shrubs, and creepers, lotus-petal-eyed as she was.

children.text: vāhanāni ca sarvāṇi saṃtyaktvā vai samantataḥ
children.translated_text: Abandoning all the mounts on every side,
<s>Ilā</s> then delighted there in the hollow of the mountain slope.
Then in that forest region, not far from the mountain,
there was a lake of very lovely appearance, filled with flocks of many birds.

children.text: dadarśa sā ilā tasmin budhaṃ somasutaṃ tadā
children.translated_text: There <s>Ilā</s> saw <s>Budha</s>, son of <s>Soma</s>,

children.text: jvalantaṃ svena vapuṣā pūrṇaṃ somam ivoditam ||
children.translated_text: shining with his own body like the full moon risen.
He was practicing intense austerity in the midst of the water, hard to approach,
bestowing fame, able to go at will, and established in youth.

children.text: sā taṃ jalāśayaṃ sarvaṃ kṣobhayāmāsa vismitā
children.translated_text: Amazed, she disturbed that whole body of water,
together with those former men who had become women, O delight of the <s>Raghu</s>s.
But <s>Budha</s>, as soon as he saw her, tormented by the arrows of desire,
could not compose himself then, and he trembled in those waters.
As he gazed at <s>Ilā</s>, auspicious and surpassing the three worlds in beauty,
he fell into thought: 'Who indeed is this woman, more than divine?

children.text: na devīṣu na nāgīṣu nāsurīṣvapsaraḥsu ca
children.translated_text: Among goddesses, serpent-maidens, demonesses, and apsarases,
I have never before seen anyone adorned with such beauty.
She would be suited to me, if she belongs to no one else.'

children.text: iti buddhiṃ samāsthāya jalāt sthalam upāgamat ||
children.translated_text: Having fixed upon this thought, he came from the water to dry land.
Having approached the hermitage, that righteous one then summoned four young women,
and they bowed to him.

children.text: sa tāḥ papraccha dharmātmā kasyaiṣā lokasundarī
children.translated_text: That righteous one asked those women, "Whose is this beauty of the world?

children.text: kimartham āgatā ceha satyam ākhyāta māciram ||
children.translated_text: For what purpose has she come here? Tell the truth without delay."

children.text: śubhaṃ tu tasya tadvākyaṃ madhuraṃ madhurākṣaram
children.translated_text: Hearing that auspicious speech of his, sweet and made of sweet syllables,

children.text: śrutvā tu tāḥ striyaḥ sarvā ūcur madhurayā girā ||
children.translated_text: all those women then spoke in a sweet voice.

children.text: asmākam eṣā suśroṇī prabhutve vartate sadā
children.translated_text: "This fine-hipped woman always lives as our mistress,
and, without a husband, she wanders with us at the edges of the forest."

children.text: tad vākyam avyaktapadaṃ tāsāṃ strīṇāṃ niśamya tu
children.translated_text: But hearing that speech of those women, whose words were indistinct,

children.text: vidyām āvartanīṃ puṇyām āvartayata sa dvijaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the twice-born man recited the holy returning spell.

children.text: so 'rthaṃ viditvā nikhilaṃ tasya rājño yathāgatam
children.translated_text: Knowing the whole matter of that king just as it had occurred,
that foremost sage spoke to all those women.
"Did any men dwell here, O blessed ones, on the slope of the mountain?
You will live on this mountain; let a place be assigned.
All of you will always subsist on roots, leaves, and fruits,
and you women will obtain husbands called <s>kimpuruṣa</s>s."
Hearing the words of the son of <s>Soma</s>, those women, made into <s>kimpuruṣī</s>s,
then resorted to that mountain, many as they were, in many places.
Hearing the origin of the <s>kimpuruṣa</s>s, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and <s>Bharata</s> then

children.text: āścaryam iti cābrūtām ubhau rāmaṃ janeśvaram ||
children.translated_text: both said to <s>Rāma</s>, lord of men, "This is wondrous."

children.text: atha rāmaḥ kathām etāṃ bhūya eva mahāyaśāḥ
children.translated_text: Then the righteous and greatly renowned <s>Rāma</s>
again told this story of the son of <s>Prajāpati</s>.
When the best of sages saw all those <s>kinnarī</s>s scattered in flight,

children.text: uvāca rūpasampannāṃ tāṃ striyaṃ prahasann iva ||
children.translated_text: he spoke, as if smiling, to that woman endowed with beauty.
"O lovely-faced one, I am the very dear son of <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: bhajasva māṃ varārohe bhaktyā snigdhena cakṣuṣā ||
children.translated_text: Choose me, O fair-hipped woman, with devotion and with a tender glance."
Hearing that speech of his, alone and bereft of her own people,
<s>Ilā</s> answered the great planet, who had a most charming appearance.
"O gentle one, I will do as you desire; I am under your control.

children.text: praśādhi māṃ somasuta yathecchasi tathā kuru ||
children.translated_text: Command me, son of <s>Soma</s>; do with me whatever you wish."
Hearing that wondrous reply of hers, filled with delight,

children.text: sa vai kāmī saha tayā reme candramasaḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the passionate son of the Moon sported with her.
For <s>Budha</s>, while he delighted that lovely-faced <s>Ilā</s>
exceedingly, the month of <s>Mādhava</s> passed like a moment.
Then, when the month was complete, the glorious son of <s>Prajāpati</s>,
whose face was like the full moon, awoke on the bed.
There he saw the son of <s>Soma</s> practicing austerity in a pool,
with arms raised, without support; the king addressed him.
"Lord, I entered this difficult mountain together with my retinue,

children.text: na ca paśyāmi tat sainyaṃ kva nu te māmakā gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: but I do not see that army. Where indeed have my people gone?"
Hearing the speech of that royal sage whose awareness had been lost,

children.text: pratyuvāca śubhaṃ vākyaṃ sāntvayan parayā girā ||
children.translated_text: he replied with auspicious words, consoling him in a supreme voice.
"Your servants were struck down by a great shower of stones,
and you slept in the hermitage, afflicted by fear of wind and rain.
Take heart; may it be well with you. Be fearless and free from distress.
O hero, live here as you please, eating fruits and roots."

children.text: sa rājā tena vākyena pratyāśvasto mahāyaśāḥ
children.translated_text: The greatly renowned king, reassured by that speech,
answered with auspicious words, sorrowful over the destruction of his servants.

children.text: tyakṣyāmyahaṃ svakaṃ rājyaṃ nāhaṃ bhṛtyair vinākṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: "I shall abandon my own kingdom. Bereft of my servants,
I could not live for a moment, O brahman. You should grant me permission.
O brahman, my eldest son, intent on <s>dharma</s>, is greatly renowned,

children.text: śaśabindur iti khyātaḥ sa me rājyaṃ prapatsyate ||
children.translated_text: known as <s>Śaśabindu</s>; he will receive my kingdom.

children.text: na hi śakṣyāmyahaṃ gatvā bhṛtyadārān sukhānvitān
children.translated_text: For I will not be able to go back and tell the wives of my servants,
who are happy, even the slightest inauspicious word, O greatly radiant one."

children.text: tathā bruvati rājendre budhaḥ paramam adbhutam
children.translated_text: As the lord of kings was speaking thus, <s>Budha</s>, most wondrous,
then said, with words preceded by consolation, "Let dwelling here please you.
You should not grieve, O mighty <s>Kārdameya</s>.
When you have lived here for a year, I shall bring about your welfare."
Hearing that speech of tireless-working <s>Budha</s>,

children.text: vāsāya vidadhe buddhiṃ yad uktaṃ brahmavādinā ||
children.translated_text: he resolved to stay, as the speaker of sacred knowledge had said.

children.text: māsaṃ sa strī tadā bhūtvā ramayatyaniśaṃ śubhā
children.translated_text: For a month, becoming a woman, that beautiful one delighted him day and night;
for a month, in the state of a man, he set his mind on <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: tataḥ sa navame māsi ilā somasutātmajam
children.translated_text: Then, in the ninth month, fine-hipped <s>Ilā</s>
gave birth to <s>Purūravas</s>, son of the son of <s>Soma</s>, as her own son.

children.text: jātamātraṃ tu suśroṇī pitur haste nyaveśayat
children.translated_text: As soon as he was born, the fine-hipped woman placed
the mighty son of <s>Ilā</s>, equal in complexion to <s>Budha</s>, in his father's hands.
<s>Budha</s> too, after reassuring the lord of men when he had become male,
self-possessed, entertained him with stories joined with <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: tathoktavati rāme tu tasya janma tad adbhutam
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāma</s> had thus told of that wondrous birth,
greatly renowned <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and <s>Bharata</s> again spoke.
"After that beloved of the son of <s>Soma</s> had lived there for a year,

children.text: akarot kiṃ naraśreṣṭha tat tvaṃ śaṃsitum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: what did she do, O best of men? You should tell us that."
Hearing the sweetness of the words of those two as they questioned him,
<s>Rāma</s> again told this story about the son of <s>Prajāpati</s>.
"When the hero had attained manhood, supremely wise <s>Budha</s>,
greatly renowned, summoned the most noble <s>Saṃvarta</s>,
and <s>Cyavana</s>, son of <s>Bhṛgu</s>, and the sage <s>Ariṣṭanemi</s>,
<s>Pramodana</s>, <s>Modakara</s>, and then the sage <s>Durvāsas</s>."
Having gathered all these friends, who knew how to speak and saw the truth,
he addressed them all, steady and fully composed in courage.

children.text: ayaṃ rājā mahābāhuḥ kardamasya ilaḥ sutaḥ
children.translated_text: This mighty-armed king is <s>Ila</s>, the son of <s>Kardama</s>.
Know him as he truly is, and let what is best for him be prescribed.

children.text: teṣāṃ saṃvadatām eva tam āśramam upāgamat
children.translated_text: While they were still speaking together, <s>Kardama</s>,
of very great splendor, came to that hermitage with great-souled brahmins.
<s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Kratu</s>, <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s>, and also
the greatly radiant <s>Oṃkāra</s> came to that hermitage.
All of them, their minds delighted at meeting one another,
then spoke separate words as well-wishers of the lord of <s>Bāhlī</s>.
But <s>Kardama</s> spoke words of supreme benefit for his son:

children.text: dvijāḥ śṛṇuta madvākyaṃ yacchreyaḥ pārthivasya hi ||
children.translated_text: "Brahmins, hear my speech, for it concerns the king's welfare.
I see no other remedy apart from <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s>.
There is no sacrifice higher than the <s>aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice), and it is dear to that great-souled one.
Therefore let us all sacrifice, for the king's sake, to that hard-to-approach lord."
When <s>Kardama</s> had spoken thus, all those best of brahmin sages

children.text: rocayanti sma taṃ yajñaṃ rudrasyārādhanaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: approved that sacrifice for the propitiation of <s>Rudra</s>.
The royal sage, the conqueror of hostile cities, disciple of <s>Saṃvarta</s>,
famous as <s>Marutta</s>, undertook that sacrifice.
Then a great sacrifice took place near the hermitage of <s>Budha</s>,
and the highly renowned <s>Rudra</s> came to the highest satisfaction.

children.text: atha yajñasamāptau tu prītaḥ paramayā mudā
children.translated_text: Then, at the completion of the sacrifice, pleased with supreme joy,

children.text: umāpatir dvijān sarvān uvācedam ilāṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Umāpati</s> said this to all the brahmins concerning <s>Ilā</s>:
"I am pleased by the <s>hayamedha</s> (horse sacrifice) and by your devotion, O best of brahmins.

children.text: asya bāhlipateścaiva kiṃ karomi priyaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: What pleasing and auspicious favor shall I do for this lord of <s>Bāhlī</s>?"
When the lord of the gods had spoken so, those brahmins, fully composed,
propitiated the lord of the gods so that <s>Ilā</s> might become a man.

children.text: tataḥ prītamanā rudraḥ puruṣatvaṃ dadau punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rudra</s>, delighted in mind, gave manhood back again
to the greatly radiant <s>Ilā</s>, and, having given it, disappeared.

children.text: nivṛtte hayamedhe tu gate cādarśanaṃ hare
children.translated_text: When the <s>hayamedha</s> (horse sacrifice) had ended and <s>Hara</s> had vanished,
all the far-seeing brahmins went away as they had come.

children.text: rājā tu bāhlim utsṛjya madhyadeśe hyanuttamam
children.translated_text: But the king, leaving <s>Bāhlī</s>, in the unsurpassed middle country
founded the renowned city of <s>Pratiṣṭhāna</s>.
<s>Śaśabindu</s>, conqueror of hostile cities, became king in <s>Bāhlī</s>,
while the strong king <s>Ila</s>, son of <s>Prajāpati</s>, ruled in <s>Pratiṣṭhāna</s>.

children.text: sa kāle prāptavāṃl lokam ilo brāhmam anuttamam
children.translated_text: In time <s>Ila</s> attained the unsurpassed world of <s>Brahmā</s>,
and king <s>Purūravas</s>, the descendant of <s>Ila</s>, obtained <s>Pratiṣṭhāna</s>.
Such is the power of the <s>aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice), O bulls among men:

children.text: strībhūtaḥ pauruṣaṃ lebhe yaccānyad api durlabham ||
children.translated_text: having become a woman, he regained manhood and whatever else is difficult to obtain.
Having related this, the immeasurably radiant <s>Kākutstha</s>

children.text: lakṣmaṇaṃ punar evāha dharmayuktam idaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: again spoke to his brothers and to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> these words joined with <s>dharma</s> (righteous order):

children.text: vasiṣṭhaṃ vāmadevaṃ ca jābālim atha kaśyapam
children.translated_text: "<s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, <s>Jābāli</s>, and <s>Kaśyapa</s>,
and all the foremost brahmins, with the <s>aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice) placed first,

children.text: etān sarvān samāhūya mantrayitvā ca lakṣmaṇa
children.translated_text: summon all these, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and after consulting with them,
I shall release, with collected mind, a horse endowed with auspicious marks."
Hearing that speech spoken by <s>Rāghava</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, swift in valor,
summoned all the brahmins and showed them to <s>Rāghava</s>.
Seeing <s>Rāghava</s>, who was like a god, difficult to assail,
after he had bowed at their feet, they honored him with blessings.
Then <s>Rāghava</s>, standing with joined palms before the best of brahmins,
spoke words in accord with <s>dharma</s> concerning the <s>aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice).
Then, having heard the wonderful counsel of those chief brahmins
concerning the <s>aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice), he became deeply pleased at that time.

children.text: vijñāya tu mataṃ teṣāṃ rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt
children.translated_text: Knowing their opinion, <s>Rāma</s> said to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:
"Mighty-armed one, send word to the great-souled <s>Sugrīva</s>.
May he quickly come, together with many great vānaras and his numerous followers,

children.text: sārdham āgaccha bhadraṃ te anubhoktuṃ makhottamam ||
children.translated_text: blessings on you, to partake in this supreme sacrifice.
And let mighty-armed <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, surrounded by many desire-roaming rākṣasas,
swift in valor, come to the <s>aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice).
And, tiger among men, let those kings who wish to do what is dear to me
come quickly with their retinues to the unsurpassed sacrificial ground.
Invite all those brahmins devoted to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order)
who dwell in distant lands, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, for the <s>aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice).
And, mighty-armed one, let the sages rich in austerity be summoned,
as well as the great seers who dwell in distant lands, together with their wives.
Let a very great sacrificial enclosure be ordered in <s>Naimiṣa</s> forest on the <s>Gomatī</s>,
mighty-armed one, for that place is unsurpassed in holiness.
Let one hundred thousand loads of excellent rice
and ten thousand loads of sesame and mung beans go in front, mighty one.
Let many crores of gold, more than a hundred measures of bullion,
be placed in front by <s>Bharata</s>; let that great-minded one go ahead.
Let temporary market streets and all actors and dancers,
guildsmen, children and elders, and well-composed brahmins,
skilled workmen and learned craftsmen,
all my mothers, the princes, and the inner apartments,

children.text: kāñcanīṃ mama patnīṃ ca dīkṣārhāṃ yajñakarmaṇi
children.translated_text: and the golden image of my wife, fit for consecration in the sacrificial rite,
be placed in front by <s>Bharata</s>; let that great-minded one go ahead."
After quickly sending all that off completely, <s>Bharata</s>'s elder brother
released the horse, marked like a black antelope and furnished with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: ṛtvigbhir lakṣmaṇaṃ sārdham aśve ca viniyujya saḥ
children.translated_text: Having appointed <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> together with the officiating priests to attend the horse,
then <s>Kākutstha</s> went with his army to <s>Naimiṣa</s>.
Seeing the sacrificial enclosure, most wonderful to behold, the mighty-armed,

children.text: praharṣam atulaṃ lebhe śrīmān iti ca so 'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: glorious one obtained incomparable joy, and said, "Splendid!"
While he was dwelling at <s>Naimiṣa</s>, all the kings
came from every realm, and <s>Rāma</s> duly honored them.
For the great-souled kings, along with their retinues, that best of men,
of great splendor, assigned exceedingly valuable lodgings.
Food, drink, and garments for those great-souled men and their attendants
<s>Bharata</s>, together with <s>Śatrughna</s>, then quickly provided.
And the great-souled monkeys, together with <s>Sugrīva</s>, at that time
all bowed down to the brahmins and performed the serving of food.
And <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, surrounded by many rākṣasas wearing garlands,
stood in attendance as a servant of the sages of fierce austerity.
Thus well arranged, the sacrifice, the <s>hayamedha</s> (horse sacrifice), went forward,
and the course of the horse, guarded by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, was set in motion.
No other sound arose there at the great-souled king's <s>hayamedha</s>

children.text: chandato dehi viśrabdho yāvat tuṣyanti yācakāḥ
children.translated_text: than, "Give as you wish, freely, until the petitioners are satisfied."
So long as they wished, it was seen that gifts were indeed being given by the monkeys and rākṣasas.

children.text: na kaścinmalinastatra dīno vāpyatha vā kṛśaḥ
children.translated_text: There was no one there who was dirty, wretched, or thin,
at that excellent sacrifice of the king, surrounded by people joyful and well nourished.
And the great-souled, long-lived sages who were there
did not remember any such sacrifice, adorned with floods of gifts.
Of silver, gold, jewels, and garments,
being given constantly, no end was seen.

children.text: na śakrasya na somasya yamasya varuṇasya vā
children.translated_text: Not even of <s>Śakra</s>, nor of <s>Soma</s>, nor of <s>Yama</s> or <s>Varuṇa</s>,
had such a sacrifice been seen before; so said the ascetics rich in austerity.
Everywhere the monkeys stood, and everywhere also the rākṣasas;

children.text: vāso dhanāni kāmibhyaḥ pūrṇahastā dadur bhṛśam ||
children.translated_text: with hands full, they gave clothing and wealth in abundance to those who desired them.
Such was the sacrifice of the lion among kings, endowed with every excellence;

children.text: saṃvatsaram atho sāgraṃ vartate na ca hīyate ||
children.translated_text: it continued for more than a year and did not diminish.
While that supreme and wondrous sacrifice was proceeding in that way,
the foremost of sages, <s>Vālmīki</s>, quickly arrived with his pupils.
Seeing the sacrifice, shining like something divine and wondrous to behold,
he made auspicious huts in a secluded part of the sages' encampments.
Joyfully he said to his two pupils, "Go, both of you, composed in mind,

children.text: kṛtsnaṃ rāmāyaṇaṃ kāvyaṃ gāyatāṃ parayā mudā ||
children.translated_text: and sing the whole poem of the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s> with supreme delight.
In the holy encampments of the sages and in the dwellings of the brahmins,
in the streets, on the royal roads, and in the houses of the kings,

children.text: rāmasya bhavanadvāri yatra karma ca vartate
children.translated_text: at the doorway of <s>Rāma</s>'s residence, and wherever the rite is going on,
and especially before the officiating priests, there it should be sung.

children.text: imāni ca phalānyatra svādūni vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: Here too are these various sweet fruits,
grown on mountain peaks; tasting them again and again, you should sing.

children.text: na yāsyathaḥ śramaṃ vatsau bhakṣayitvā phalāni vai
children.translated_text: You will not grow weary, my children, after eating the fruits,
and the well-prepared roots; you will keep away from the city.
If the lord of the earth, <s>Rāma</s>, should summon you for hearing it,
then, when the sages have taken their seats, let the singing begin.

children.text: divase viṃśatiḥ sargā geyā vai parayā mudā
children.translated_text: Twenty cantos are to be sung each day with supreme delight,
in many measures there, just as I indicated before.
And no greed at all should be shown, not even a little, through desire for wealth;
what need have forest hermits, who live on fruits and roots, of wealth?

children.text: yadi pṛcchet sa kākutstho yuvāṃ kasyeti dārakau
children.translated_text: If that <s>Kākutstha</s> asks, 'Whose boys are you?',

children.text: vālmīker atha śiṣyau hi brūtām evaṃ narādhipam ||
children.translated_text: then tell the king this: 'We are indeed pupils of <s>Vālmīki</s>.'
Taking up these very sweet stringed instruments, and the pitch shown beforehand,
raise the melody and sing very sweetly, free from anxiety.
It should be sung from the beginning, and the king must not be treated with disrespect,

children.text: pitā hi sarvabhūtānāṃ rājā bhavati dharmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: for by <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) the king is the father of all beings.

children.text: tad yuvāṃ hṛṣṭamanasau śvaḥ prabhāte samādhinā
children.translated_text: Therefore, with joyful minds, tomorrow at daybreak, in concentration,
sing the sweet song, furnished with the rhythm of the strings."
Having instructed them repeatedly in this way, the sage, son of <s>Pracetas</s>, then,
the most noble and greatly famed <s>Vālmīki</s>, sat silent.

children.text: tām adbhutāṃ tau hṛdaye kumārau niveśya vāṇīm ṛṣibhāṣitāṃ śubhām
children.translated_text: Placing in their hearts that wondrous, auspicious speech spoken by the sage, the two boys,

children.text: samutsukau tau sukham ūṣatur niśāṃ yathāśvinau bhārgavanītisaṃskṛtau ||
children.translated_text: eager, spent the night happily, like the two <s>Aśvins</s> trained in the discipline of <s>Bhārgava</s>.
When the night had become morning, the two had bathed and offered into the sacred fire;
as the sage had instructed before, they sang here and there.

children.text: tāṃ sa śuśrāva kākutsthaḥ pūrvacaryāṃ tatastataḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kākutstha</s> heard that ancient course of conduct from place to place,
and an unprecedented style of recitation, adorned with song.
Bound in many measures and joined with the rhythm of stringed instruments,
<s>Rāghava</s>, hearing it from the two boys, became filled with curiosity.
Then, during an interval in the rite, the king, having summoned the great sages,
the tiger among men also summoned the kings, learned men, and merchants,
the reciters of ancient lore, experts in words, and those elderly twice-born men who were there;
having summoned all these, he seated the two singers.
The hosts of sages there were delighted, and so were the kings of great might.

children.text: pibanta iva cakṣurbhyāṃ rājānaṃ gāyakau ca tau ||
children.translated_text: as if drinking in the king and the two singers with their eyes.

children.text: parasparam athocuste sarva eva samaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Then all of them together said to one another,

children.text: ubhau rāmasya sadṛśau bimbād bimbam ivoddhṛtau ||
children.translated_text: "The two are both like <s>Rāma</s>, as if one image had been drawn out from another.

children.text: jaṭilau yadi na syātāṃ na valkaladharau yadi
children.translated_text: If they did not have matted hair, if they did not wear bark garments,
we would not perceive any difference between the two who sing and <s>Rāghava</s>."
While the listeners were speaking thus among themselves, increasing their delight,
the two sons of the sage began the song there.
Then the sweet <s>gāndharva</s> (musical performance), more than human, began,

children.text: na ca tṛptiṃ yayuḥ sarve śrotāro geyasaṃpadā ||
children.translated_text: and all the listeners found no satiety in the excellence of the song.
Beginning from the start, from the cantos that follow the vision of <s>Nārada</s>,
from there onward they sang the cantos, up to twenty.
Then, in the afternoon, <s>Rāghava</s>,
having heard those twenty cantos, spoke to <s>Bharata</s>, who loved his brother:
"Quickly give eighteen thousand pieces of gold

children.text: dadasva śīghraṃ kākutstha bālayor mā vṛthā śramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: to these two great-souled boys, O <s>Kākutstha</s>; let their effort not be in vain."
The two <s>Kuśīlavas</s> did not accept that gold as it was being given,
and the two great-souled ones, astonished, said, "What use is this?"
"We two forest-dwellers delight in wild fruits and roots;
what shall we do in the forest with gold and wealth?"
As the two spoke in that way, the listeners, filled with curiosity,
and <s>Rāma</s> himself, all became greatly astonished.

children.text: tasya caivāgamaṃ rāmaḥ kāvyasya śrotum utsukaḥ
children.translated_text: Eager to hear the origin of that poem,
the very radiant <s>Rāma</s> questioned those two sons of the sage:

children.text: kiṃpramāṇam idaṃ kāvyaṃ kā pratiṣṭhā mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: "What is the extent of this poem? What is the foundation of the great-souled one?

children.text: kartā kāvyasya mahataḥ ko vāsau munipuṃgavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Who is the maker of this great poem, that bull among sages?"
To <s>Rāghava</s> as he asked this question, the two sons of the sage said:
"Blessed <s>Vālmīki</s> is the maker; he has come to the vicinity of the sacrifice,
he by whom this whole story of yours has been shown in full.
From the beginning onward, O king of kings, there are five hundred cantos,
and the foundation, O king, is your life, so long as it lasts, both auspicious and inauspicious.
If you have resolved, O king, O great chariot-warrior, to hear it,
then, when there is a moment between ritual duties, listen to it together with your younger brothers."
"Very well," said <s>Rāma</s>; and after taking leave of <s>Rāghava</s>,
the two, delighted, went to the dwelling where that bull among sages was.
<s>Rāma</s> too, together with the sages and the great-souled kings,
having heard the sweetness of that song, went to the sacrificial hall.
For many days indeed <s>Rāma</s> listened to that supremely wondrous song,

children.text: śuśrāva munibhiḥ sārdhaṃ rājabhiḥ saha vānaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: together with the sages, with kings, and with the vānaras.

children.text: tasmin gīte tu vijñāya sītāputrau kuśīlavau
children.translated_text: But when <s>Rāma</s> learned from that song that the two <s>Kuśīlavas</s> were sons of <s>Sītā</s>,

children.text: tasyāḥ pariṣado madhye rāmo vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: he spoke these words in the midst of that assembly:
"Repeat my words and go to the presence of the blessed one.
If she is pure in conduct, if she is free from stain,
let her, with the great sage's permission, make a purification of herself here.
Having learned the sage's wish and the thought in <s>Sītā</s>'s mind,
if she desires to give proof, then tell me quickly.

children.text: śvaḥ prabhāte tu śapathaṃ maithilī janakātmajā
children.translated_text: Tomorrow morning let <s>Maithilī</s>, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, make an oath
in the midst of the assembly, for the sake of purification for me as well."

children.text: śrutvā tu rāghavasyaitad vacaḥ paramam adbhutam
children.translated_text: Having heard this supremely wondrous speech of <s>Rāghava</s>,
the messengers went to the enclosure where the bull among sages was staying.
They bowed to the great-souled one, blazing with boundless radiance,
and spoke <s>Rāma</s>'s words, gentle and sweet.

children.text: teṣāṃ tad bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā rāmasya ca manogatam
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech of theirs and understanding <s>Rāma</s>'s intention,
the sage of very great radiance then spoke these words:

children.text: evaṃ bhavatu bhadraṃ vo yathā tuṣyati rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: "So be it. Good fortune to you. Just as <s>Rāghava</s> is pleased,

children.text: tathā kariṣyate sītā daivataṃ hi patiḥ striyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: so <s>Sītā</s> will act, for a husband is a woman's deity."
Thus addressed by the sage, all the mighty messengers of <s>Rāma</s>
returned and reported the sage's words to <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: tataḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ kākutsthaḥ śrutvā vākyaṃ mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kākutstha</s>, delighted after hearing the great-souled sage's words,
addressed the assembled seers there and the kings as well:
"Let the blessed ones, together with their disciples, and the lords of men with their followers,
witness <s>Sītā</s>'s oath, and whoever else desires to do so."
Hearing that statement of great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>,
there arose a great cry of approval from all the foremost seers.
And the great-souled kings praised <s>Rāghava</s>:
"This is fitting in you alone, O best of men, and in no other on earth."

children.text: evaṃ viniścayaṃ kṛtvā śvobhūta iti rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Having made this decision, <s>Rāghava</s>, the destroyer of foes, said, "It will be tomorrow,"
and then dismissed all those people.
When that night had passed, the king, gone to the sacrificial enclosure,
the very radiant <s>Rāghava</s>, had all the seers summoned.
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, <s>Jābāli</s>, and then <s>Kāśyapa</s>,
<s>Viśvāmitra</s>, long in austerity, and <s>Durvāsas</s>, great in austerity,
then <s>Agastya</s>, likewise <s>Śakti</s>, and <s>Bhārgava</s> and <s>Vāmana</s>,
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, long-lived, and <s>Maudgalya</s>, great in austerity,
<s>Bhārgava</s> <s>Cyavana</s> also, and <s>Śatānanda</s>, knower of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),
and radiant <s>Bharadvāja</s>, and <s>Suprabha</s>, son of <s>Agni</s>;

children.text: ete cānye ca munayo bahavaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ
children.translated_text: these and many other sages, firm in their vows,
And kings, tigers among men, all gathered there,
and rākṣasas of great valor and vānaras of great strength,
all those great-souled ones came together out of curiosity.
Kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and also śūdras by the thousands,
all assembled in order to witness <s>Sītā</s>'s oath.
Hearing that all had assembled there, motionless as if turned to stone,
the best of sages quickly came up, together with <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: tam ṛṣiṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ sītā sānvagacchad avāṅmukhī
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s> followed behind that seer, her face cast down,
with joined palms, her voice choked with tears, having placed <s>Rāma</s> in her mind.

children.text: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā śrīm ivāyāntīṃ brahmāṇam anugāminīm
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Sītā</s> coming behind <s>Vālmīki</s>, like prosperity itself approaching, following <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: vālmīkeḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ sītāṃ sādhukāro mahān abhūt ||
children.translated_text: a great cry of approval arose.

children.text: tato halahalā śabdaḥ sarveṣām evam ābabhau
children.translated_text: Then a confused tumultuous sound arose from them all,
whose hearts were agitated by a vast grief born of sorrow.

children.text: sādhu sīteti kecit tu sādhu rāmeti cāpare
children.translated_text: Some said, "Well done, <s>Sītā</s>!" while others said, "Well done, <s>Rāma</s>!"

children.text: ubhāveva tu tatrānye sādhu sādhviti cābruvan ||
children.translated_text: and still others there said of both of them, "Well done, well done!"
Then the foremost sage entered the middle of the mass of people,
and <s>Vālmīki</s>, with <s>Sītā</s> beside him, spoke thus to <s>Rāghava</s>:
"O son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, this is <s>Sītā</s>, firm in vows and walking in <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),
sinless, though abandoned by you, from the neighborhood of my hermitage.
O <s>Rāma</s> of great vows, because you feared the reproach of the world,

children.text: pratyayaṃ dāsyate sītā tām anujñātum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sītā</s> will give you assurance; you ought to permit her to do so.

children.text: imau ca jānakī putrāvubhau ca yamajātakau
children.translated_text: And these two are <s>Jānakī</s>'s sons, both born as twins;

children.text: sutau tavaiva durdharṣau satyam etad bravīmi te ||
children.translated_text: they are your own unconquerable sons. I tell you this truth.
O delight of the <s>Rāghavas</s>, I am the tenth son of <s>Pracetas</s>;

children.text: na smarāmyanṛtaṃ vākyaṃ tathemau tava putrakau ||
children.translated_text: I do not remember ever speaking an untrue word; so too these two are your sons.
For many thousands of years austerity has been practiced by me;

children.text: tasyāḥ phalam upāśnīyām apāpā maithilī yathā ||
children.translated_text: may I enjoy its fruit if <s>Maithilī</s> is sinless.
O <s>Rāghava</s>, having considered <s>Sītā</s> in relation to the five elements, with the mind as the sixth,
I took her in, judging her pure, beside the forest stream.
This woman is pure in conduct, sinless, and devoted to her husband as to a deity;
for you, who feared the reproach of the world, she will give assurance."
When <s>Vālmīki</s> had spoken thus, <s>Rāghava</s> replied,

children.text: prāñjalir jagato madhye dṛṣṭvā tāṃ devavarṇinīm ||
children.translated_text: standing with joined palms in the midst of the world, after seeing her, who had the complexion of a goddess:
"So it is, great-fortuned one, just as you say, knower of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: pratyayo hi mama brahmaṃstava vākyair akalmaṣaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For I have confidence, O brahman, in your stainless words.

children.text: pratyayo hi purā datto vaidehyā surasaṃnidhau
children.translated_text: Indeed, assurance was formerly given by <s>Vaidehī</s> in the presence of the gods;
yet, O brahman, though I knew she was sinless,

children.text: parityaktā mayā sītā tad bhavān kṣantum arhati ||
children.translated_text: this <s>Sītā</s> was abandoned by me out of fear of the world. Therefore you ought to forgive me.

children.text: jānāmi cemau putrau me yamajātau kuśīlavau
children.translated_text: And I know that these two, <s>Kuśa</s> and <s>Lava</s>, born as twins, are my sons.

children.text: śuddhāyāṃ jagato madhye maithilyāṃ prītir astu me ||
children.translated_text: May I have affection for <s>Maithilī</s>, who is pure, in the midst of the world."
But the best of gods, understanding <s>Rāma</s>'s intention,
all assembled there, placing the grandsire before them:

children.text: ādityā vasavo rudrā viśve devā marudgaṇāḥ
children.translated_text: the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Viśve Devas, the hosts of Maruts,
the two Aśvins, sages and gandharvas, and hosts of apsarases,

children.text: sādhyāśca devāḥ sarve te sarve ca paramarṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the Sādhyas and all the gods, and all the supreme seers.

children.text: tato vāyuḥ śubhaḥ puṇyo divyagandho manoramaḥ
children.translated_text: Then an auspicious, holy wind, fragrant with divine scent and delightful,
gladdened that mass of people on every side, by the power of the best of gods.
People from all the kingdoms gazed intently at that event,
marvelous and inconceivable, as people had done formerly in the Kṛta age.
Seeing all who had assembled, <s>Sītā</s>, dressed in ocher garments,
spoke these words with joined palms, eyes lowered and face cast down:

children.text: yathāhaṃ rāghavād anyaṃ manasāpi na cintaye
children.translated_text: "As I have not thought of anyone other than <s>Rāghava</s>, even in my mind,

children.text: tathā me mādhavī devī vivaraṃ dātum arhati ||
children.translated_text: so may the goddess <s>Mādhavī</s> grant me an opening."

children.text: tathā śapantyāṃ vaidehyāṃ prādurāsīt tad adbhutam
children.translated_text: As <s>Vaidehī</s> was swearing thus, that wonder appeared:
a divine and unsurpassed throne rose up from the surface of the earth,
borne upon the heads of nāgas of immeasurable might,
divine, adorned with divine beauty and decorated with every jewel.

children.text: tasmiṃstu dharaṇī devī bāhubhyāṃ gṛhya maithilīm
children.translated_text: On it the goddess Earth took <s>Maithilī</s> with both arms,
welcomed her with honor, and seated her upon the seat.
Seeing her seated on the throne and entering the netherworld,
an unbroken divine shower of flowers rained down upon <s>Sītā</s>.
And a very great cry of approval suddenly arose from the gods:

children.text: sādhu sādhviti vai sīte yasyāste śīlam īdṛśam ||
children.translated_text: "Well done, well done, <s>Sītā</s>, whose character is such as this!"
In many such ways the delighted gods who stood in the sky
uttered words when they saw <s>Sītā</s>'s entry.

children.text: yajñavāṭagatāś cāpi munayaḥ sarva eva te
children.translated_text: And all the sages who had come to the sacrificial enclosure,
and the kings, tigers among men, could not cease from wonder.

children.text: antarikṣe ca bhūmau ca sarve sthāvarajaṅgamāḥ
children.translated_text: In the sky and on the earth, all moving and unmoving beings,
the great-bodied dānavas and the lords of serpents in the netherworld,
some cried out in delight, some were absorbed in meditation,

children.text: kecid rāmaṃ nirīkṣante kecit sītām acetanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: some looked at <s>Rāma</s>, and some, unconscious, looked at <s>Sītā</s>.
Seeing <s>Sītā</s>'s entry, that assembly of theirs remained

children.text: taṃ muhūrtam ivātyarthaṃ sarvaṃ saṃmohitaṃ jagat ||
children.translated_text: as if, for that moment, the whole world had been utterly bewildered.
Then, at the close of the sacrifice, <s>Rāma</s>, exceedingly downcast,

children.text: apaśyamāno vaidehīṃ mene śūnyam idaṃ jagat
