children.translated_text: not seeing <s>Vaidehī</s>, thought this world empty,
and, utterly overcome by grief, he found no peace in his mind.
Having dismissed all the earthly kings, the bears, vānaras, and rākṣasas,
he dismissed the crowd of people headed by brahmans, after honoring them with wealth.

children.text: tato visṛjya tān sarvān rāmo rājīvalocanaḥ
children.translated_text: Then lotus-eyed <s>Rāma</s>, having dismissed all of them,

children.text: hṛdi kṛtvā tadā sītām ayodhyāṃ praviveśa saḥ ||
children.translated_text: placed <s>Sītā</s> in his heart at that time and entered <s>Ayodhyā</s>.

children.text: na sītāyāḥ parāṃ bhāryāṃ vavre sa raghunandanaḥ
children.translated_text: That delight of the <s>Raghu</s> line chose no wife beyond <s>Sītā</s>;

children.text: yajñe yajñe ca patnyarthaṃ jānakī kāñcanī bhavat ||
children.translated_text: and at every sacrifice a golden <s>Jānakī</s> served in the place of his wife.
For ten thousand years he undertook the <s>Vājimedha</s> sacrifice,
and <s>Vājapeya</s> rites ten times as many, and also many <s>Bahusuvarṇaka</s> rites.
With <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> and <s>Atirātra</s>, and with <s>Gosava</s> rites rich in great wealth,

children.text: īje kratubhir anyaiśca sa śrīmān āptadakṣiṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: that glorious one sacrificed with other rites as well, supplied with full priestly gifts.

children.text: evaṃ sa kālaḥ sumahān rājyasthasya mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus a very long time passed for the high-souled one established in kingship,
for <s>Rāghava</s>, who was striving in <s>dharma</s> (righteous order).
Bears, monkeys, and <s>rākṣasas</s> remained under <s>Rāma</s>'s command;
and kings became devoted to <s>Rāghava</s> day after day.

children.text: kāle varṣati parjanyaḥ subhikṣaṃ vimalā diśaḥ
children.translated_text: Rain fell in season, there was abundant food, and the quarters were clear;
the city and the countryside were filled with people who were joyful and well nourished.

children.text: nākāle mriyate kaścinna vyādhiḥ prāṇināṃ tadā
children.translated_text: No one died out of season, and at that time there was no disease among living beings;
nor did any unrighteousness arise while <s>Rāma</s> governed the kingdom.
Then, after a long time, <s>Rāma</s>'s illustrious mother,
surrounded by sons and grandsons, came under the law of time.
Illustrious <s>Sumitrā</s> also followed, and <s>Kaikeyī</s> too;
having performed <s>dharma</s> in many forms, they came to dwell in the third heaven.

children.text: sarvāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ svarge rājñā daśarathena ca
children.translated_text: All those greatly fortunate women were established in heaven,

children.text: samāgatā mahābhāgāḥ saha dharmaṃ ca lebhire ||
children.translated_text: reunited with King <s>Daśaratha</s>, and they attained the reward of <s>dharma</s> together.

children.text: tāsāṃ rāmo mahādānaṃ kāle kāle prayacchati
children.translated_text: At proper times <s>Rāma</s> made great gifts on their behalf,
without distinction among his mothers, to brahmans and ascetics.
The righteous <s>Rāma</s> performed ancestral rites rich in many jewels,

children.text: cakāra rāmo dharmātmā pitṝn devān vivardhayan ||
children.translated_text: and sacrifices exceedingly hard to accomplish, increasing the fathers and the gods.
Then, after some time, <s>Yudhājit</s>, king of the <s>Kekayas</s>,
sent his own preceptor to the high-souled <s>Rāghava</s>.
He sent <s>Gārgya</s>, son of <s>Aṅgiras</s>, a brahmarṣi of immeasurable splendor,
and ten thousand horses as an unsurpassed gift of affection.
The king also gave blankets, jewels, and excellent variegated cloth,
and many ornaments to <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: śrutvā tu rāghavo gārgyaṃ maharṣiṃ samupāgatam
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāghava</s> heard that the great seer <s>Gārgya</s> had arrived,
that a dear messenger from his maternal uncle <s>Aśvapati</s> had come,
<s>Kākutstha</s>, together with his attendants, went out to meet him for about a krośa,

children.text: gārgyaṃ saṃpūjayāmāsa dhanaṃ tat pratigṛhya ca ||
children.translated_text: honored <s>Gārgya</s>, and accepted that wealth.

children.text: pṛṣṭvā ca prītidaṃ sarvaṃ kuśalaṃ mātulasya ca
children.translated_text: After asking about the whole gift of affection and about his maternal uncle's welfare,
<s>Rāma</s> began to question the greatly fortunate one when he was seated.

children.text: kim āha mātulo vākyaṃ yadarthaṃ bhagavān iha
children.translated_text: "What message has my maternal uncle spoken, for the sake of which, venerable sir,

children.text: prāpto vākyavidāṃ śreṣṭha sākṣād iva bṛhaspatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: you have come here, O best of those skilled in speech, like <s>Bṛhaspati</s> himself?"
Hearing <s>Rāma</s>'s words, the brahmarṣi began
to tell <s>Rāghava</s> the full matter, wondrous in appearance.
"Your maternal uncle, O mighty-armed one, O bull among men,
<s>Yudhājit</s>, speaks this affectionate message. Hear it, if it pleases you.
This region of the <s>Gandharvas</s>, adorned with fruits and roots,
is a supremely beautiful country on both banks of the <s>Sindhu</s>.

children.text: taṃ ca rakṣanti gandharvāḥ sāyudhā yuddhakovidāḥ
children.translated_text: Armed <s>Gandharvas</s>, skilled in war, guard it,
heroic sons of <s>Śailūṣa</s>, three crores in number, very mighty.
Conquer them, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, and in the auspicious <s>Gandharva</s> region,
O mighty-armed one, carefully establish two cities.
No one else has access there, and this country is very beautiful.

children.text: rocatāṃ te mahābāho nāhaṃ tvām anṛtaṃ vade ||
children.translated_text: Let it please you, O mighty-armed one; I am not speaking falsely to you."
Hearing that, <s>Rāghava</s> was pleased with the great seer and with his maternal uncle,
and said, "Very well," and then looked toward <s>Bharata</s>.
Pleased, <s>Rāghava</s> spoke to the twice-born man, holding his joined palms:

children.text: imau kumārau taṃ deśaṃ brahmarṣe vijayiṣyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: "These two princes, O brahmarṣi, will conquer that country.

children.text: bharatasyātmajau vīrau takṣaḥ puṣkala eva ca
children.translated_text: They are <s>Bharata</s>'s heroic sons, <s>Takṣa</s> and <s>Puṣkala</s>;

children.text: mātulena suguptau tau dharmeṇa ca samāhitau ||
children.translated_text: well protected by their maternal uncle, the two are firmly established in <s>dharma</s>.
Putting <s>Bharata</s> in front, the two princes, followed by their forces,
will slay the sons of the <s>Gandharvas</s> and divide the land into two cities.

children.text: niveśya te puravare ātmajau saṃniveśya ca
children.translated_text: After founding those excellent cities and settling his own sons there,
the exceedingly righteous one will come again into my presence."

children.text: brahmarṣim evam uktvā tu bharataṃ sabalānugam
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to the brahmarṣi, he then commanded
<s>Bharata</s> together with his accompanying army, and consecrated the two princes.
Under an auspicious gentle constellation, placing the son of <s>Aṅgiras</s> in front,

children.text: bharataḥ saha sainyena kumārābhyāṃ ca niryayau ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s> set out with the army and with the two princes.
Then that army went out from the city as if joined with <s>Śakra</s>,
followed far by <s>Rāghava</s>, hard for gods and asuras to assail.

children.text: māṃsāśīni ca sattvāni rakṣāṃsi sumahānti ca
children.translated_text: Flesh-eating beings and very great <s>rākṣasas</s>
followed <s>Bharata</s>, thirsting for blood.
And many hosts of beings, very dreadful flesh-eaters,
by the thousands, desired to eat the flesh of the <s>Gandharva</s> sons.
Of lions, tigers, jackals, and birds moving in the sky,

children.text: bahūni vai sahasrāṇi senāyā yayur agrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: many thousands indeed went in front of the army.
The army spent a month and a half on the road, free from sickness,
filled with joyful and well-nourished people, and reached <s>Kekaya</s>.
Hearing that the army commander <s>Bharata</s> had arrived, the lord of the <s>Kekayas</s>,
<s>Yudhājit</s>, together with <s>Gārgya</s>, felt supreme delight.
The lord of the <s>Kekayas</s> set out with a great multitude of people,
and, hurrying, advanced against the <s>Gandharvas</s>, who had the form of gods.
<s>Bharata</s> and <s>Yudhājit</s>, both swift in valor, assembled together,
and reached the city of the <s>Gandharvas</s>, with their armies and foot-followers.

children.text: śrutvā tu bharataṃ prāptaṃ gandharvāste samāgatāḥ
children.translated_text: But hearing that <s>Bharata</s> had arrived, those <s>Gandharvas</s> gathered,
desiring battle, of great heroism, roaring on every side.
Then a tumultuous battle arose, making the hair stand on end,
very terrible for seven nights, and there was victory for neither side.
Then <s>Bharata</s>, the younger brother of <s>Rāma</s>, enraged, took up <s>Kāla</s>'s dreadful weapon,
named <s>Saṃvarta</s>, and deployed it against the <s>Gandharvas</s>.
Bound by the noose of <s>Kāla</s> and torn apart by <s>Saṃvarta</s>,
three crores of them were struck down there in a moment by the great-souled one.

children.text: taṃ ghātaṃ ghorasaṃkāśaṃ na smaranti divaukasaḥ
children.translated_text: The dwellers in heaven do not remember such a slaughter, terrible in appearance,
of such great-souled beings, within the mere span of a blink.
When those heroes had been slain, <s>Bharata</s>, son of <s>Kaikeyī</s>,
then established two excellent cities there, prosperous ones:
<s>Takṣa</s> in <s>Takṣaśilā</s>, and <s>Puṣkara</s> in <s>Puṣkarāvatī</s>.
That lovely country of the <s>Gandharvas</s>, that region of <s>Gāndhāra</s>,
within five years was filled with territories and with city-dwellers.
The two were full of streams of wealth and jewels, and adorned with groves,
and, through rivalry with each other, produced the widening of their qualities in competition.
Both were like splendid cities of the gods, with transactions free from stain,
surrounded by masses of parks and conveyances, and with well-divided inner markets.
Both excellent cities were charming and adorned with broad expanses,
with beautiful principal houses and aerial mansions of matching color.
They were adorned with beautiful and extensive temples of the gods.
Having established them over five years, <s>Bharata</s>, the younger brother of <s>Rāghava</s>,
the mighty-armed son of <s>Kaikeyī</s>, returned again to <s>Ayodhyā</s>.
The illustrious <s>Bharata</s> bowed to the great-souled <s>Rāghava</s>,

children.text: rāghavaṃ bharataḥ śrīmān brahmāṇam iva vāsavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: who was like <s>Dharma</s> itself in another form, as <s>Vāsava</s> bows to <s>Brahmā</s>.
He reported just as it had happened the excellent slaughter of the <s>Gandharvas</s>,

children.text: niveśanaṃ ca deśasya śrutvā prīto 'sya rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the settlement of the country; hearing this, <s>Rāghava</s> was pleased with him.

children.text: tacchrutvā harṣam āpede rāghavo bhrātṛbhiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Having heard that, <s>Rāghava</s>, together with his brothers, was filled with joy,
and <s>Rāghava</s> spoke to his brothers words that seemed wondrous:
"These two princes, O son of <s>Sumitrā</s>, your sons skilled in <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),
<s>Aṅgada</s> and <s>Candraketu</s>, strong bowmen, are worthy of kingship.
I shall consecrate these two to kingship; let a country be duly arranged,
for it should be lovely and uncrowded, where the two bowmen may delight.

children.text: na rājñāṃ yatra pīḍā syānnāśramāṇāṃ vināśanam
children.translated_text: Let there be no oppression of kings there, nor destruction of hermitages.

children.text: sa deśo dṛśyatāṃ saumya nāparādhyāmahe yathā ||
children.translated_text: Look for such a country, gentle one, so that we may not commit an offense."

children.text: tathoktavati rāme tu bharataḥ pratyuvāca ha
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāma</s> had spoken thus, <s>Bharata</s> replied:
"This land of <s>Kārāpatha</s> is very delightful and free from disease.
Let a city be established there for great-souled <s>Aṅgada</s>,
and for <s>Candraketu</s> a lovely, disease-free city named <s>Candrakāntā</s>."
<s>Rāghava</s> accepted that statement spoken by <s>Bharata</s>,

children.text: taṃ ca kṛtvā vaśe deśam aṅgadasya nyaveśayat ||
children.translated_text: and, after bringing that country under control, he settled it for <s>Aṅgada</s>.
The charming city <s>Aṅgadīyā</s> was established for <s>Aṅgada</s>,
delightful and well guarded, by <s>Rāma</s>, whose actions were unwearied.
For the wrestler-like <s>Candraketu</s>, in <s>Mallabhūmi</s>, a city was established,
renowned as <s>Candrakāntā</s>, divine like a city of heaven.

children.text: tato rāmaḥ parāṃ prītiṃ bharato lakṣmaṇastathā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Bharata</s>, and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> likewise

children.text: yayur yudhi durādharṣā abhiṣekaṃ ca cakrire ||
children.translated_text: attained supreme joy, irresistible in battle, and they performed the consecration.
Having consecrated the two princes and sent them forth with armies and followers,
they sent <s>Aṅgada</s> to the western land and <s>Candraketu</s> facing north.
<s>Saumitri</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, followed <s>Aṅgada</s> as well,
while <s>Bharata</s> became the rear-guard of <s>Candraketu</s>.
Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, having stayed for a year in <s>Aṅgadīyā</s>,

children.text: putre sthite durādharṣe ayodhyāṃ punar āgamat ||
children.translated_text: when his unconquerable son was established, returned again to <s>Ayodhyā</s>.
<s>Bharata</s> too, having likewise stayed for a year and somewhat more,
came again to <s>Ayodhyā</s> and approached <s>Rāma</s>'s feet.
Both <s>Saumitri</s> and <s>Bharata</s>, devoted to <s>Rāma</s>'s feet,
being exceedingly righteous, out of affection did not perceive even the passage of time.
In this way ten thousand years then passed for them,
as they strove in <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) and constantly in the affairs of the citizens.

children.text: vihṛtya kālaṃ paripūrṇamānasāḥ śriyā vṛtā dharmapathe pare sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: Having passed the full measure of time with fulfilled minds, surrounded by prosperity, and established on the supreme path of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),

children.text: trayaḥ samiddhā iva dīptatejasā hutāgnayaḥ sādhu mahādhvare trayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the three, blazing with radiant splendor, were like three well-kindled sacrificial fires in a great rite.
Then, after some time, while <s>Rāma</s> stood on the path of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),
<s>Kāla</s>, in the form of an ascetic, came to the royal gate.
He spoke these words to steadfast and renowned <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:
"Announce me to <s>Rāma</s>; I have arrived because of the weightiness of my mission.
For I am the messenger of a very powerful great sage of immeasurable splendor,

children.text: rāmaṃ didṛkṣur āyātaḥ kāryeṇa hi mahābala ||
children.translated_text: and I have come wishing to see <s>Rāma</s>, for a matter, O mighty one."
Hearing that statement of his, <s>Saumitri</s>, filled with haste,
reported to <s>Rāma</s> what the ascetic wished to say.

children.text: jayasva rājan dharmeṇa ubhau lokau mahādyute
children.translated_text: "May you conquer through <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), O king, both worlds, O greatly radiant one.
An ascetic messenger, bright as the sun, has come to see you."

children.text: tad vākyaṃ lakṣmaṇenoktaṃ śrutvā rāma uvāca ha
children.translated_text: Having heard those words spoken by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, <s>Rāma</s> said:
"Dear one, let the sage of great power, the bearer of his message, be admitted."
<s>Saumitri</s>, saying, "So be it," admitted that sage,
who was as if blazing with splendors and burning with rays.
Approaching the best of the <s>Raghus</s>, who shone with his own radiance,
the seer said to <s>Rāghava</s>, in a sweet voice, "May you prosper."
To him the very radiant <s>Rāma</s> gave worship preceded by arghya,
and calmly began to ask about his welfare.

children.text: pṛṣṭaśca kuśalaṃ tena rāmeṇa vadatāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: Asked about his welfare by <s>Rāma</s>, that best of speakers,
the greatly renowned one sat down on a splendid golden seat.

children.text: tam uvāca tato rāmaḥ svāgataṃ te mahāmune
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāma</s> said to him, "Welcome to you, great sage.

children.text: prāpayasva ca vākyāni yato dūtastvam āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Deliver the words for whose sake you have come as a messenger."
Urged by that lion among kings, the sage uttered this speech:

children.text: dvandvam etat pravaktavyaṃ na ca cakṣurhataṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "This matter is to be spoken in private; the words must not be exposed to anyone's eyes.

children.text: yaḥ śṛṇoti nirīkṣed vā sa vadhyastava rāghava
children.translated_text: Whoever hears or looks on is to be put to death by you, O <s>Rāghava</s>,
if you are willing to observe the command of the foremost sage."

children.text: tatheti ca pratijñāya rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt
children.translated_text: Agreeing, "So be it," <s>Rāma</s> said to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:
"Stand at the doorway, mighty-armed one; dismiss the doorkeeper.

children.text: sa me vadhyaḥ khalu bhavet kathāṃ dvandvasamīritām
children.translated_text: Surely that person would be liable to death at my hands,

children.text: ṛṣer mama ca saumitre paśyed vā śṛṇuyācca yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: who either saw or heard the private conversation between the seer and me, O <s>Saumitri</s>."
Then <s>Kākutstha</s>, placing <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> in charge of the door,

children.text: tam uvāca muniṃ vākyaṃ kathayasveti rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: said to that sage, "Speak," said <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: yat te manīṣitaṃ vākyaṃ yena vāsi samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: "The message that is in your mind, or the matter for which you have come intent upon it,
tell it without hesitation; it is in my heart also."

children.text: śṛṇu rāma mahābāho yadartham aham āgataḥ
children.translated_text: "Listen, O mighty-armed <s>Rāma</s>, to the purpose for which I have come.
I have been sent by the divine Grandsire, mighty one.
In your former state, O conqueror of enemy cities, I was your son,
O hero, brought into being by your māyā (creative power): I am <s>Kāla</s>, gatherer of all.
And the blessed Grandsire, the lord and ruler of the worlds, said:
"The time has come for you, mighty-armed one, to protect the heavenly worlds.

children.text: saṃkṣipya ca purā lokānmāyayā svayam eva hi
children.translated_text: Long ago, having contracted the worlds by your māyā (creative power), you yourself,

children.text: mahārṇave śayāno 'psu māṃ tvaṃ pūrvam ajījanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: lying in the waters of the great ocean, first generated me.

children.text: bhogavantaṃ tato nāgam anantam udake śayam
children.translated_text: Then, by your māyā (creative power), you created the serpent <s>Ananta</s>, with coils, lying in the water,

children.text: māyayā janayitvā tvaṃ dvau ca sattvau mahābalau ||
children.translated_text: and two mighty beings as well,

children.text: madhuṃ ca kaiṭabhaṃ caiva yayor asthicayair vṛtā
children.translated_text: namely <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, with whose heaps of bones
this earth, crowded with mountains, was covered and became the earth.

children.text: padme divyārkasaṃkāśe nābhyām utpādya mām api
children.translated_text: Bringing me too forth from your navel, in a lotus shining like the divine sun,

children.text: prājāpatyaṃ tvayā karma sarvaṃ mayi niveśitam ||
children.translated_text: you placed the whole work of creation in me.

children.text: so 'haṃ saṃnyastabhāro hi tvām upāse jagatpatim
children.translated_text: Thus, with my burden laid aside, I attend upon you, lord of the world;

children.text: rakṣāṃ vidhatsva bhūteṣu mama tejaskaro bhavān ||
children.translated_text: establish protection among beings; you are the one who strengthens my power.
Then you too, unassailable, from that eternal state,
for the protection of all beings, assumed the condition of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Born from <s>Aditi</s> as a valiant son, increasing the joy of your brothers,
you are fitted to aid the worlds when tasks arise.

children.text: sa tvaṃ vitrāsyamānāsu prajāsu jagatāṃ vara
children.translated_text: You, best of the worlds, when creatures were being terrified,
desiring <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s death, set your mind on birth among human beings.
Long ago you yourself fixed the limit of your dwelling

children.text: kṛtvā vāsasya niyatiṃ svayam evātmanaḥ purā ||
children.translated_text: as ten thousand years and ten hundred years.

children.text: sa tvaṃ manomayaḥ putraḥ pūrṇāyur mānuṣeṣviha
children.translated_text: You, a mind-born son, have now completed your lifespan here among humans;
the time, O best of excellent men, has come near.
If, great king, you wish to continue attending to your subjects,

children.text: vasa vā vīra bhadraṃ te evam āha pitāmahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then dwell here, hero; blessed be you. Thus said the Grandsire.

children.text: atha vā vijigīṣā te suralokāya rāghava
children.translated_text: Or, if your desire is conquest toward the world of the gods, O <s>Rāghava</s>,
let the gods, having <s>Viṣṇu</s> as their protector, become free from distress."
Having heard the speech uttered by <s>Kāla</s> and spoken by the Grandsire,
<s>Rāghava</s>, smiling, spoke to <s>Kāla</s>, the ender of all:

children.text: śrutaṃ me devadevasya vākyaṃ paramam adbhutam
children.translated_text: "I have heard the supreme, wondrous word of the god of gods.
Great joy has arisen from your coming.

children.text: bhadraṃ te 'stu gamiṣyāmi yata evāham āgataḥ
children.translated_text: May it be well with you. I shall go back to the place from which I came.

children.text: hṛdgato hyasi samprāpto na me 'styatra vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: You have come as one already present in my heart; there is no deliberation for me here.
For in all the tasks of the gods, who depend on me,
I must act at the universal dissolution just as the Grandsire has said."

children.text: tathā tayoḥ kathayator durvāsā bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
children.translated_text: While the two were speaking thus, the blessed seer <s>Durvāsas</s>
came to the royal gate, desiring to see <s>Rāma</s>.
Approaching <s>Saumitri</s>, that best of seers said,

children.text: rāmaṃ darśaya me śīghraṃ purā me 'rtho 'tivartate ||
children.translated_text: "Show me <s>Rāma</s> quickly, before my business passes beyond reach."
Hearing the sage's words, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, slayer of enemy heroes,

children.text: abhivādya mahātmānaṃ vākyam etad uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: bowed to the great-souled one and spoke these words:

children.text: kiṃ kāryaṃ brūhi bhagavan ko vārthaḥ kiṃ karomyaham
children.translated_text: "Tell me, blessed one, what is to be done, what the matter is, and what I should do.

children.text: vyagro hi rāghavo brahmanmuhūrtaṃ vā pratīkṣatām ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> is occupied, brahmin; please wait for a moment."
Hearing that, the tiger among seers, made turbid with anger,

children.text: uvāca lakṣmaṇaṃ vākyaṃ nirdahann iva cakṣuṣā ||
children.translated_text: spoke to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, as if burning him with his eyes:

children.text: asmin kṣaṇe māṃ saumitre rāmāya prativedaya
children.translated_text: "This very instant, <s>Saumitri</s>, announce me to <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: viṣayaṃ tvāṃ puraṃ caiva śapiṣye rāghavaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: I shall curse your realm and city, and <s>Rāghava</s> as well,

children.text: bharataṃ caiva saumitre yuṣmākaṃ yā ca saṃtatiḥ
children.translated_text: and <s>Bharata</s> too, <s>Saumitri</s>, and whatever offspring you have;

children.text: na hi śakṣyāmyahaṃ bhūyo manyuṃ dhārayituṃ hṛdi ||
children.translated_text: for I can no longer hold the anger in my heart."
Hearing that dreadful-looking speech of that great-souled one,
He considered in his mind the firm conclusion of that statement:

children.text: ekasya maraṇaṃ me 'stu mā bhūt sarvavināśanam
children.translated_text: "Let there be the death of one person, namely me; let there not be the destruction of all."
Having decided thus in his judgment, he reported it to <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: lakṣmaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā rāmaḥ kālaṃ visṛjya ca
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s words, <s>Rāma</s> dismissed <s>Kāla</s>,

children.text: niṣpatya tvaritaṃ rājā atreḥ putraṃ dadarśa ha ||
children.translated_text: and the king, quickly going out, saw the son of <s>Atri</s>.
Having greeted the great-souled one, who was blazing as if with splendor,

children.text: kiṃ kāryam iti kākutsthaḥ kṛtāñjalir abhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kākutstha</s>, with joined palms, said, "What is to be done?"

children.text: tad vākyaṃ rāghaveṇoktaṃ śrutvā munivaraḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that statement spoken by <s>Rāghava</s>, the lordly best of sages,
<s>Durvāsas</s>, replied to <s>Rāma</s>, "Listen, O lover of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order).
Today, O <s>Rāghava</s>, a thousand years of mine have been completed.
Therefore I desire food, as it is ready, from you, O blameless one."
Hearing that speech, <s>Rāma</s>, filled with great joy,
brought food, as it was ready, for the chief of sages.

children.text: sa tu bhuktvā muniśreṣṭhastad annam amṛtopamam
children.translated_text: Then that best of sages, having eaten that food like nectar,

children.text: sādhu rāmeti sambhāṣya svam āśramam upāgamat ||
children.translated_text: addressed him, saying, "Well done, <s>Rāma</s>," and went to his own hermitage.
When he had gone, the greatly radiant <s>Rāghava</s>, pleased at heart,
then remembered the words of <s>Kāla</s> and fell into grief.

children.text: duḥkhena ca susaṃtaptaḥ smṛtvā tad ghoradarśanam
children.translated_text: Deeply scorched by sorrow, remembering that dreadful sight,

children.text: avāṅmukho dīnamanā vyāhartuṃ na śaśāka ha ||
children.translated_text: he became downcast and dejected, and could not speak.
Then <s>Rāghava</s>, having resolved in his mind the words of <s>Kāla</s>,

children.text: naitad astīti coktvā sa tūṣṇīm āsīnmahāyaśāḥ ||
children.translated_text: said, "This cannot be," and the greatly famous one sat in silence.

children.text: avāṅmukham atho dīnaṃ dṛṣṭvā somam ivāplutam
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Rāghava</s> downcast and wretched, like the moon submerged,

children.text: rāghavaṃ lakṣmaṇo vākyaṃ hṛṣṭo madhuram abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, glad in spirit, spoke a sweet word to him:

children.text: na saṃtāpaṃ mahābāho madarthaṃ kartum arhasi
children.translated_text: "O mighty-armed one, you should not feel anguish for my sake.
For such is the course of <s>Kāla</s> (Time), bound by what was ordained before.

children.text: jahi māṃ saumya viśrabdhaḥ pratijñāṃ paripālaya
children.translated_text: Slay me, gentle one, with confidence; preserve your vow.
Men whose vows are broken, O <s>Kākutstha</s>, go to hell.
If there is affection, great king, and if I am worthy of favor from you,

children.text: jahi māṃ nirviśaṅkastvaṃ dharmaṃ vardhaya rāghava ||
children.translated_text: slay me without hesitation, O <s>Rāghava</s>; increase <s>dharma</s> (righteous order)."
When <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> had spoken thus, <s>Rāma</s>, his senses shaken,
summoned his ministers and also the household priest.
The lord of men told them, in their midst, exactly what had happened:
the coming of <s>Durvāsas</s> and the vow of the ascetic.
Hearing that, all the ministers, together with the preceptors, sat down.

children.text: vasiṣṭhastu mahātejā vākyam etad uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: Then the greatly radiant <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> spoke this word:
"This has been foreseen, O mighty-armed one: your terrible, hair-raising destruction,
and your separation from <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, O greatly famous <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: tyajainaṃ balavān kālo mā pratijñāṃ vṛthā kṛthāḥ
children.translated_text: Abandon him; <s>Kāla</s> is powerful. Do not make your vow fruitless.

children.text: vinaṣṭāyāṃ pratijñāyāṃ dharmo hi vilayaṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: For when a vow is destroyed, <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) goes to dissolution.

children.text: tato dharme vinaṣṭe tu trailokyaṃ sacarācaram
children.translated_text: And when <s>dharma</s> is destroyed, the three worlds, with moving and unmoving beings,
all together with the hosts of gods and seers, would perish; there is no doubt.
Therefore, O tiger among men, for the protection of the three worlds,

children.text: lakṣmaṇasya vadhenādya jagat svasthaṃ kuruṣva ha ||
children.translated_text: by the killing of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> today, make the world well and secure."
Hearing that statement of theirs, assembled together, joined with <s>dharma</s> and practical purpose,

children.text: śrutvā pariṣado madhye rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, in the midst of the council, spoke to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>:

children.text: visarjaye tvāṃ saumitre mā bhūd dharmaviparyayaḥ
children.translated_text: "I dismiss you, O <s>Saumitri</s>; let there be no reversal of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: tyāgo vadho vā vihitaḥ sādhūnām ubhayaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: For good men, abandonment or killing is prescribed; the two are equal."
When that word had been spoken by <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, his eyes troubled with tears,

children.text: lakṣmaṇastvaritaḥ prāyāt svagṛhaṃ na viveśa ha ||
children.translated_text: quickly departed; he did not enter his own house.
Going to the bank of the <s>Sarayū</s>, sipping water, and standing with joined palms,

children.text: nigṛhya sarvasrotāṃsi niḥśvāsaṃ na mumoca ha ||
children.translated_text: he restrained all his channels of breath and did not release an exhalation.
As he stood joined in yoga, not breathing, the gods, together with <s>Śakra</s> and the hosts of apsarases,
and all the gods with the hosts of seers, showered him with flowers then.
Invisible to all his younger brothers, <s>Śakra</s> took mighty <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, bodily,

children.text: pragṛhya lakṣmaṇaṃ śakro divaṃ sampraviveśa ha ||
children.translated_text: and entered heaven.
Then all the best of gods joyfully and gladly worshiped,
together with the seers, the fourth part of <s>Viṣṇu</s> that had come.
Having dismissed <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, filled with pain and grief,
spoke these words to the household priest, the ministers, and the citizens:
"Today I shall consecrate <s>Bharata</s>, devoted to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), in the kingdom,

children.text: ayodhyāyāṃ patiṃ vīraṃ tato yāsyāmyahaṃ vanam ||
children.translated_text: as the heroic lord in <s>Ayodhyā</s>; then I shall go to the forest.
Bring in the consecration materials, so that there may be no passing of the proper time.
This very day I shall go on the path that <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> has gone."
Hearing what had been spoken by <s>Rāghava</s>, all the subjects, greatly distressed,
bowed their heads to the ground and became as if bereft of life.
And <s>Bharata</s> became unconscious on hearing <s>Rāma</s>'s speech.
He denounced the kingdom and spoke this to <s>Rāghava</s>:

children.text: satyena hi śape rājan svargaloke na caiva hi
children.translated_text: "By truth I swear, O king, and by the heavenly world as well,

children.text: na kāmaye yathā rājyaṃ tvāṃ vinā raghunandana ||
children.translated_text: that I do not desire the kingdom without you, O delight of the <s>Raghus</s>.
Consecrate these two, <s>Kuśa</s> and <s>Lava</s>, O king, O lord of men:

children.text: kosaleṣu kuśaṃ vīram uttareṣu tathā lavam ||
children.translated_text: the heroic <s>Kuśa</s> among the <s>Kosalas</s>, and likewise <s>Lava</s> among the northern people.
And let messengers of swift valor go to <s>Śatrughna</s>.
Let them quickly announce this journey of ours toward heaven."
Hearing what had been spoken by <s>Bharata</s>, and seeing the townspeople also downcast,

children.text: paurān duḥkhena saṃtaptān vasiṣṭho vākyam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: tormented with grief, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> spoke a word.

children.text: vatsa rāma imāḥ paśya dharaṇīṃ prakṛtīr gatāḥ
children.translated_text: Dear child <s>Rāma</s>, look at these subjects, fallen upon the ground.

children.text: jñātvaiṣām īpsitaṃ kāryaṃ mā caiṣāṃ vipriyaṃ kṛthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Knowing the purpose they desire, do not do anything displeasing to them.
Then, at <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s word, <s>Kākutstha</s> raised up the people of the realm,

children.text: kiṃ karomīti kākutsthaḥ sarvān vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: and said to them all, "What shall I do?"

children.text: tataḥ sarvāḥ prakṛtayo rāmaṃ vacanam abruvan
children.translated_text: Then all the subjects spoke these words to <s>Rāma</s>:
"As you go, <s>Rāma</s>, we will follow wherever you will go.

children.text: eṣā naḥ paramā prītir eṣa dharmaḥ paro mataḥ
children.translated_text: This is our highest joy; this is regarded as the highest <s>dharma</s> (sacred duty).
The satisfaction fixed in our hearts is always firm in following you.

children.text: paureṣu yadi te prītir yadi sneho hyanuttamaḥ
children.translated_text: If you have affection for the townspeople, if your love is indeed unsurpassed,
then, <s>Kākutstha</s>, with our sons and wives let us go together on the good path.

children.text: tapovanaṃ vā durgaṃ vā nadīm ambhonidhiṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Whether to a grove of ascetics, a difficult place, a river, or the ocean,

children.text: vayaṃ te yadi na tyājyāḥ sarvānno naya īśvara ||
children.translated_text: if we are not to be abandoned by you, lord, lead all of us there."

children.text: sa teṣāṃ niścayaṃ jñātvā kṛtāntaṃ ca nirīkṣya ca
children.translated_text: Knowing their fixed resolve and seeing the decree of destiny,

children.text: paurāṇāṃ dṛḍhabhaktiṃ ca bāḍham ityeva so 'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: and seeing the firm devotion of the townspeople, he said only, "So be it."

children.text: evaṃ viniścayaṃ kṛtvā tasminn ahani rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: Having made this decision on that day, <s>Rāghava</s>

children.text: kosaleṣu kuśaṃ vīram uttareṣu tathā lavam ||
children.translated_text: installed the heroic <s>Kuśa</s> among the <s>Kosalas</s> and likewise <s>Lava</s> among the northern people,
both high-souled and noble in conduct.

children.text: rathānāṃ tu sahasrāṇi trīṇi nāgāyutāni ca ||
children.translated_text: He gave each of them three thousand chariots and thirty thousand elephants,
and ten thousand horses as wealth for each.
The two were rich in many jewels and much wealth, surrounded by joyful and well-nourished people.

children.text: abhiṣicya tu tau vīrau prasthāpya svapure tathā
children.translated_text: After consecrating those two heroes and sending them likewise to their own cities,
he dispatched messengers to the high-souled <s>Śatrughna</s>.
Those messengers, urged on by <s>Rāma</s>'s command and swift in movement,

children.text: prajagmur madhurāṃ śīghraṃ cakrur vāsaṃ na cādhvani ||
children.translated_text: went quickly to <s>Madhurā</s> and made no halt on the road.
Then, after reaching <s>Madhurā</s> in three days and nights,

children.text: śatrughnāya yathāvṛttam ācakhyuḥ sarvam eva tat ||
children.translated_text: they reported to <s>Śatrughna</s> everything exactly as it had happened:
the abandonment of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and <s>Rāghava</s>'s vow,
the consecration of the two sons and the following of the townspeople.
The lovely city of <s>Kuśa</s> was on the slope of the <s>Vindhya</s> mountain;

children.text: kuśāvatīti nāmnā sā kṛtā rāmeṇa dhīmatā ||
children.translated_text: that city, named <s>Kuśāvatī</s>, had been made by wise <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: śrāvitā ca purī ramyā śrāvatīti lavasya ca
children.translated_text: And the lovely city assigned to <s>Lava</s> was called <s>Śrāvatī</s>;
<s>Ayodhyā</s> was deserted, and <s>Bharata</s> was following <s>Rāghava</s>.
Having quickly reported all this to the high-souled <s>Śatrughna</s>,

children.text: viremuste tato dūtāstvara rājann iti bruvan ||
children.translated_text: the messengers then fell silent, saying, "Make haste, O king."
Hearing that the destruction of the family, dreadful in appearance, was at hand,
he assembled the subjects and <s>Kāñcana</s> the priest.
The delight of the <s>Raghus</s> told them all exactly as it had happened,
and also his own coming change, together with his brothers.
Then the heroic king consecrated his two sons:

children.text: subāhur madhurāṃ lebhe śatrughātī ca vaidiśam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Subāhu</s> received <s>Madhurā</s>, and <s>Śatrughātī</s> received <s>Vaidiśa</s>.

children.text: dvidhākṛtvā tu tāṃ senāṃ mādhurīṃ putrayor dvayoḥ
children.translated_text: Dividing that army of <s>Madhurā</s> into two parts for his two sons,
he established the two princes, furnished with wealth and grain.
Then, after sending the king <s>Śatrughātin</s> to <s>Vaidiśa</s>,
<s>Rāghava</s> hurried to <s>Ayodhyā</s> in a single chariot.

children.text: sa dadarśa mahātmānaṃ jvalantam iva pāvakam
children.translated_text: He saw the high-souled one blazing like fire,
wearing fine linen garments and accompanied by imperishable sages.
Then he bowed to <s>Rāma</s>, stood with joined palms and controlled senses,
and, knowing <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty), spoke these words while thinking only of <s>dharma</s>:
"I have performed the consecration of my two sons, properly supplied with wealth.
Know me, O king, to be firmly resolved on following you.

children.text: na cānyad atra vaktavyaṃ dustaraṃ tava śāsanam
children.translated_text: Nothing else is to be said here; your command is hard to cross.

children.text: tyaktuṃ nārhasi māṃ vīra bhaktimantaṃ viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: You should not abandon me, hero, especially when I am devoted to you."

children.text: tasya tāṃ buddhim aklībāṃ vijñāya raghunandanaḥ
children.translated_text: Recognizing that fearless resolve of his, the delight of the <s>Raghus</s>,

children.text: bāḍham ityeva śatrughnaṃ rāmo vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, said to <s>Śatrughna</s> only these words: "So be it."
At the end of his speech, vānaras able to take any form they wished
and many groups of bears and rākṣasas arrived.
Sons of gods, sons of seers, and sons of gandharvas as well,

children.text: rāmakṣayaṃ viditvā te sarva eva samāgatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all came there, having learned of <s>Rāma</s>'s departure.

children.text: te rāmam abhivādyāhuḥ sarva eva samāgatāḥ
children.translated_text: They all bowed to <s>Rāma</s> and said, having all assembled,
"Greatly famed king, we have come to follow you.
If, <s>Rāma</s>, bull among men, you were to go without us,
we would be struck down by you as though you had raised the staff of <s>Yama</s>."
Hearing these words of the bears, vānaras, and rākṣasas,
he then spoke sweetly to <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> in a gentle voice:

children.text: yāvat prajā dhariṣyanti tāvat tvaṃ vai vibhīṣaṇa
children.translated_text: "So long as living beings endure, so long you, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,
greatly powerful lord of rākṣasas, shall remain in <s>Laṅkā</s> and maintain your own realm.

children.text: prajāḥ saṃrakṣa dharmeṇa nottaraṃ vaktum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: Protect the people according to <s>dharma</s> (righteous rule); you should say nothing further."

children.text: tam evam uktvā kākutstho hanūmantam athābravīt
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to him, <s>Kākutstha</s> then said to <s>Hanūmat</s>:
"You have fixed your mind on life; do not break your promise.
As long as my stories circulate in the world, lord of monkeys,

children.text: tāvat tvaṃ dhārayan prāṇān pratijñām anupālaya ||
children.translated_text: so long preserve your life-breaths and keep your promise."
Having spoken in the same way, <s>Kākutstha</s> addressed all those bears and vānaras:

children.text: mayā sārdhaṃ prayāteti tadā tān rāghavo 'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: "Set out together with me," <s>Rāghava</s> then said to them.
When the night had passed into dawn, the broad-chested, greatly famed
lotus-petal-eyed <s>Rāma</s> then said to his household priest:
"Let the agnihotra go in front, with the ghee and the blazing sacrificial fire."
and the parasol of the <s>Vājapeya</s> sacrifice, making the great road shine.
Then radiant <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, without omitting anything,
performed according to rule the righteous rite for the great departure.
Then, wearing linen garments and reciting the supreme <s>brahman</s>,
he took kuśa grass in both hands, set it forth, and then departed.
Speaking nothing at all anywhere, motionless and devoid of worldly pleasure on the road,
he went out from that house, blazing like the sun.

children.text: rāmasya pārśve savye tu padmā śrīḥ susamāhitā
children.translated_text: At <s>Rāma</s>'s left side was <s>Śrī</s>, lotus-born fortune, perfectly composed;
on his right was wide-eyed <s>Hrī</s> (modesty), and in front was Resolve.
Arrows of many kinds, and the bow with its long form,
all followed <s>Kākutstha</s>, having assumed human bodies.
The <s>Vedas</s> in the form of brahmins, <s>Sāvitrī</s> the protector of all,
the syllable Oṃ and the exclamation Vaṣaṭ, all were devoted to <s>Rāma</s> and followed him.
And the great-souled seers, all the earth-gods,
followed <s>Kākutstha</s> as he approached the gate of heaven.

children.text: taṃ yāntam anuyānti sma antaḥpuracarāḥ striyaḥ
children.translated_text: As he went, the women who moved within the inner apartments followed him,
together with old people, children, maidservants, aged servants, and attendants.
<s>Bharata</s>, with the inner household and accompanied by <s>Śatrughna</s>, went too;
having taken up <s>Rāma</s>'s vow, they were devoted followers of <s>Rāghava</s>.
Then the great-souled brahmins, composed and with their agnihotra fires,
followed the wise <s>Kākutstha</s>, together with their sons and wives.
The ministers and the class of servants, with their sons and kinsmen,
all followed <s>Rāghava</s> with their attendants, as if filled with joy.
Then all the citizens, surrounded by glad and well-nourished people,
followed <s>Rāghava</s> as he went forth, delighted by his virtues.
Everything was bathed and joyful, incomparable and bright with rejoicing flowers;
exultant with cries of delight, everything was devoted to <s>Rāma</s> and followed him.

children.text: na tatra kaścid dīno 'bhūd vrīḍito vāpi duḥkhitaḥ
children.translated_text: There no one was dejected, ashamed, or sorrowful;
everything became glad and delighted, supremely wondrous.
Then the country people, wishing to see the king's departure,

children.text: samprāptaḥ so 'pi dṛṣṭvaiva saha sarvair anuvrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: arrived there too, and at the mere sight of him followed along with everyone else.
The bears, monkeys, rākṣasas, and the people dwelling in the city
went behind him with supreme devotion, perfectly composed.
After going a yojana and a half, <s>Raghunandana</s> saw the river
<s>Sarayū</s>, whose waters are holy, lying to the west.

children.text: atha tasmin muhūrte tu brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ
children.translated_text: Then at that very moment <s>Brahmā</s>, the grandsire and father of the worlds,
surrounded by all the gods and by the great-souled seers,
came to the place where <s>Kākutstha</s> had arrived for heaven,
enveloped by hundreds of crores of divine aerial chariots.
A shower of flowers fell, released by the wind, like a great flood.
In that place filled with hundreds of instruments and crowded with <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Apsarases</s>,
<s>Rāma</s> stepped with his feet into the waters of the <s>Sarayū</s>.
Then the grandsire spoke these words from the sky:

children.text: āgaccha viṣṇo bhadraṃ te diṣṭyā prāpto 'si rāghava ||
children.translated_text: "Come, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>; blessings to you. By good fortune you have arrived, O <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: bhrātṛbhiḥ saha devābhaiḥ praviśasva svakāṃ tanum
children.translated_text: Together with your brothers, who shine like gods, enter your own body,

children.text: vaiṣṇavīṃ tāṃ mahātejas tad ākāśaṃ sanātanam ||
children.translated_text: that body of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O greatly radiant one, that eternal expanse of heaven.

children.text: tvaṃ hi lokagatir deva na tvāṃ kecit prajānate
children.translated_text: For you are the course of the worlds, O god; none truly know you,
except through your former consort, wide-eyed <s>Māyā</s>.

children.text: tvam acintyaṃ mahad bhūtam akṣayaṃ sarvasaṃgraham
children.translated_text: You are the inconceivable great being, imperishable and containing all;

children.text: yām icchasi mahātejas tāṃ tanuṃ praviśa svayam ||
children.translated_text: enter by yourself whatever body you desire, O greatly radiant one."
Hearing the grandsire's words, the great-minded one made his decision,
and, together with his younger brothers and still embodied, entered the radiance of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: tato viṣṇugataṃ devaṃ pūjayanti sma devatāḥ
children.translated_text: Then the deities worshiped the god who had gone into <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
the <s>Sādhyas</s> and hosts of <s>Maruts</s>, together with <s>Indra</s> and with <s>Agni</s> at their head,

children.text: ye ca divyā ṛṣigaṇā gandharvāpsarasaśca yāḥ
children.translated_text: and the hosts of divine seers, the <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Apsarases</s>,
the <s>Suparṇas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, and <s>Yakṣas</s>, and the <s>Daityas</s>, <s>Dānavas</s>, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>.
Everything was glad and delighted; everything had its desire fulfilled.

children.text: sādhu sādhviti tat sarvaṃ tridivaṃ gatakalmaṣam ||
children.translated_text: All the sinless heaven cried, "Well done, well done!"

children.text: atha viṣṇur mahātejāḥ pitāmaham uvāca ha
children.translated_text: Then mighty-radiant <s>Viṣṇu</s> spoke to the grandsire:
"O true-vowed one, you should grant worlds to these floods of people.

children.text: ime hi sarve snehān mām anuyātā manasvinaḥ
children.translated_text: For all these high-minded ones have followed me out of affection;
they are devotees, worthy of a share, and have abandoned themselves for my sake."
Hearing that speech of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, the lord and teacher of the worlds, said:
"These who have assembled will go to the worlds called <s>Sāṃtānika</s>.
And whatever creature of animal birth has meditated only on <s>Rāma</s>

children.text: prāṇāṃs tyakṣyati bhaktyā vai saṃtāne tu nivatsyati
children.translated_text: and gives up its life through devotion will dwell in <s>Sāṃtāna</s>,

children.text: sarvair eva guṇair yukte brahmalokād anantare ||
children.translated_text: endowed with every virtue, immediately below <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: vānarāśca svakāṃ yonim ṛkṣāścaiva tathā yayuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The monkeys and likewise the bears will go to their own sources of birth.

children.text: yebhyo viniḥsṛtā ye ye surādibhyaḥ susaṃbhavāḥ
children.translated_text: Whichever of them issued from whichever gods and other beings, being well-born from them,
from seers, <s>Nāgas</s>, or <s>Yakṣas</s>, to those very beings they will return."
When the lord of gods had spoken thus, they came to <s>Gopratāra</s>,
and all entered the <s>Sarayū</s>, overcome with tears filled with joy.

children.text: avagāhya jalaṃ yo yaḥ prāṇī hyāsīt prahṛṣṭavat
children.translated_text: Whatever living being there was, joyfully plunging into the water,
abandoned its human body and mounted an aerial chariot.
And those who had been born in animal wombs, on reaching the water of the <s>Sarayū</s>,

children.text: divyā divyena vapuṣā devā dīptā ivābhavan ||
children.translated_text: became divine, with divine bodies, shining like radiant gods.

children.text: gatvā tu sarayūtoyaṃ sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca
children.translated_text: Having gone to the water of the <s>Sarayū</s>, both the stationary beings and the moving ones,
and having received the moistening of that water, went to the world of the gods.

children.text: devānāṃ yasya yā yonir vānarā ṛkṣarākṣasāḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever divine birth belonged to each of the <s>Vānaras</s>, bears, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: tām eva viviśuḥ sarve dehān nikṣipya cāmbhasi ||
children.translated_text: all of them entered that very birth, casting off their bodies in the waters.

children.text: tathā svargagataṃ sarvaṃ kṛtvā lokagurur divam
children.translated_text: Having thus caused all to go to heaven, the teacher of the world,

children.text: jagāma tridaśaiḥ sārdhaṃ hṛṣṭair hṛṣṭo mahāmatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the great-minded one, himself delighted, went to heaven together with the delighted thirty gods.
